Industrial systems—such as supply chains, production networks, and service operations—increasingly face dynamic disruptions, stochastic demand, and multi-objective trade-offs. Traditional optimization methods struggle with the combinatorial complexity and high-dimensional parameter spaces inherent to these systems, particularly when modeling interdependencies between human, material, and informational flows. The research will focus on integrating stochastic programming, agent-based simulation, and parallelizable decomposition algorithms to enable large-scale, near-optimal solutions. Key computational challenges include solving mixed-integer nonlinear programs with time-dependent constraints, managing asynchronous simulations for scenario exploration, and optimizing hyperparameters for ensemble machine learning models that predict system behaviors. HPC resources will be critical for distributed memory parallelism to partition problem instances, GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo sampling for uncertainty propagation, and in-memory data processing for real-time feedback loops. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for adaptive resource allocation, validated through case studies in semiconductor manufacturing and hospital logistics. These applications will quantify trade-offs between system resilience, cost, and sustainability metrics under varying disruption scenarios. The project aims to advance methodological rigor in industrial and systems engineering by bridging gaps between theoretical optimization, computational scalability, and practical implementation. Results will be disseminated as open-source code to support reproducibility, alongside performance benchmarks demonstrating HPC-driven reductions in solution times for billion-variable problem instances. This work will provide foundational insights into designing agile, data-driven systems capable of operating efficiently in uncertain environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Combines instruction in industrial and systems engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize sustainable textile waste reduction in wholesale fashion merchandising through dynamic pricing and inventory strategies, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, multi-agent supply chain ecosystems. The fashion industry faces escalating pressure to mitigate overproduction and textile waste, particularly at the wholesale level, where mismatches between bulk orders and retailer demand lead to unsold inventory and environmental harm. Current strategies rely on static pricing or heuristic demand forecasting, which fail to adapt to real-time shifts in consumer trends, supplier constraints, or geopolitical disruptions. To address this, we propose an interdisciplinary computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), reinforcement learning (RL), and large-scale sentiment analysis of social media and economic datasets. HPC resources will enable simulations of thousands of wholesale buyers, suppliers, and retailers operating under dynamic conditions, including climate policy shocks and viral trend cycles. The ABM component will capture heterogeneous decision-making behaviors, while RL algorithms will train adaptive pricing agents to balance profitability with waste reduction. Sentiment data, scraped from platforms like Instagram and TikTok, will inform demand predictions at granular regional and demographic levels. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU clusters, we aim to identify pricing-inventory policies that reduce overstock by ≥30% in simulated wholesale environments while maintaining profit margins. Outcomes will provide actionable strategies for wholesalers to align purchasing contracts with emerging sustainability regulations and volatile consumer preferences. This research bridges computational social science, operations research, and environmental management, advancing both business efficiency and circular economy objectives in a critically understudied domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote product lines/brands, and organize promotional campaigns, at the wholesale level to attract retailer interest, wholesale purchasing, and supply contracts. Includes instruction in wholesaling, wholesale advertising, selling, and customer relations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision metal fabrication processes in machine shop applications by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize machining dynamics. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to toolpath planning, cutting parameter selection, and thermal management in subtractive manufacturing often lead to material waste, tool wear, and suboptimal surface finishes. To address these challenges, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate multi-physics interactions during machining operations. High-fidelity models will analyze stress distributions, heat generation, and material deformation for common alloys (e.g., steel, titanium) under varying spindle speeds, feed rates, and coolant conditions. ML algorithms will process experimental sensor data (vibration, temperature, force) from CNC machines to validate and refine simulations. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these resource-intensive simulations across thousands of parameter combinations and enabling real-time predictive analytics. Expected outcomes include optimized machining parameter sets to minimize tool wear and energy consumption, predictive models for surface integrity, and a publicly accessible database of simulation results. This work will directly support small-scale manufacturing enterprises and vocational training programs by providing data-driven guidelines to improve machining efficiency and part quality. The integration of computational modeling into machine shop workflows represents a novel cross-disciplinary advance, bridging traditional manufacturing practices with Industry 4.0 methodologies. All developed tools and datasets will be disseminated through partnerships with regional technical colleges to enhance curriculum development in machine shop technology programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and modify metal parts in support of other manufacturing, repair or design activities, or as an independent business.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an AI-driven decision support system to optimize personalized meal planning for individuals with complex dietary needs, such as chronic metabolic disorders, rare allergies, or multi-morbidity conditions. Current manual approaches to meal design by dietetic professionals are time-intensive and often fail to dynamically integrate real-time patient data, evolving nutritional guidelines, and sensory preferences. The proposed system will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve combinatorial optimization challenges inherent in balancing dozens of nutritional, medical, and logistical constraints while maximizing patient adherence. A hybrid machine learning architecture will be implemented, combining transformer-based natural language processing for automated analysis of clinical records and dietary preferences with constrained reinforcement learning to iteratively refine meal plans. Multi-objective optimization algorithms will simultaneously minimize nutrient deficits, allergen risks, and ingredient costs while incorporating patient feedback loops. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, biomolecular food databases, and longitudinal patient satisfaction metrics. By simulating thousands of meal permutations under variable constraints, the HPC environment will enable rapid prototyping of context-aware dietary solutions. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for adaptive meal planning that reduces dietitian workload by 40–60% in preliminary trials while improving adherence rates among patients with intersecting dietary restrictions. The computational models and datasets produced will be made available to the clinical nutrition community, offering a foundation for future research in precision dietetics. This work bridges gaps between computational systems biology and applied nutritional sciences, addressing a critical need for scalable tools in personalized dietary care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying dance therapy’s therapeutic effects on individuals with trauma-related anxiety disorders. Despite empirical evidence supporting dance therapy’s efficacy, the dynamic interplay between movement patterns, autonomic nervous system responses, and neural plasticity remains poorly quantified. Current clinical evaluations rely on subjective metrics, limiting personalization and mechanistic insights. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating motion capture data, biometric sensor outputs (heart rate variability, galvanic skin response), and functional neuroimaging to model how structured dance interventions modulate stress responses and cortical activation patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multimodal datasets spanning terabytes of kinematic, physiological, and fMRI data, as well as training machine learning models to identify predictive movement signatures tied to therapeutic outcomes. Computational workflows will include parallelized preprocessing pipelines for noise reduction and temporal alignment of heterogeneous data streams, GPU-accelerated neural networks for classifying movement quality and emotional valence, and agent-based simulations of stress response dynamics during improvisational dance sequences. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework linking specific movement parameters (e.g., symmetry, fluidity, spatial complexity) to quantifiable neurophysiological changes and (2) open-source tools enabling therapists to design individualized interventions based on predictive biomarkers. By elucidating the biomechanical and neural correlates of dance therapy, this work aims to establish a data-driven foundation for optimizing clinical protocols, advancing evidence-based practices in a field traditionally reliant on qualitative assessment.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use the therapeutic application of creative dance movement to assist in promoting client rehabilitation and physical, emotional, and mental health. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, personality development, movement and motor behavior, psychology, dance, creative expression modalities, improvisation, group psychology and leadership, client evaluation and supervision, dance therapy practice, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern computing systems, particularly in edge computing and IoT applications, demands efficient hardware-software co-design strategies to optimize performance, energy efficiency, and scalability. Current methodologies for prototyping hybrid architectures—such as systems integrating reconfigurable field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) with parallelized GPU accelerators—face significant computational bottlenecks. Traditional simulation tools struggle to model large-scale, heterogeneous systems in reasonable timeframes, limiting the exploration of design trade-offs and real-time optimization. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable rapid, high-fidelity simulations of next-generation embedded computing architectures. The research will focus on developing a scalable computational framework to model the interplay between hardware reconfiguration, task scheduling, and power dynamics in FPGA-GPU hybrid systems. Computational methods will include parallelized discrete-event simulations using MPI and OpenMP to emulate multi-core interactions, machine learning-driven optimization of task allocation, and finite-element analysis for thermal and power characterization. By utilizing HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce simulation times for large-scale systems (10,000+ logic elements and 100+ parallel threads) from weeks to hours, enabling iterative design refinement and real-time adaptive control algorithms. Expected outcomes include a publicly available simulation toolkit for hybrid architecture prototyping, empirically validated design guidelines for energy-latency trade-offs in edge computing devices, and novel hardware-aware scheduling algorithms. These contributions will directly support the development of efficient, reconfigurable systems for applications such as autonomous robotics, smart sensor networks, and low-power AI inference engines. The project will also serve as a platform for training undergraduate researchers in HPC-aided co-design methodologies, bridging gaps between theoretical computer engineering principles and practical large-scale system implementation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize resource allocation strategies for complex, multi-stakeholder R&D programs through computational modeling of dynamic project management scenarios. A critical challenge in R&D management lies in balancing competing priorities—such as budget constraints, technical uncertainty, and interdisciplinary team coordination—while maintaining agility in rapidly evolving research environments. Traditional static allocation models often fail to account for stochastic variables like shifting project timelines, emergent risks, or variable resource yields from partnerships. To address this gap, we propose developing an adaptive decision-support framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate large-scale R&D portfolios under diverse constraints. Agent-based modeling will capture interactions between heterogeneous stakeholders (research teams, funding bodies, regulatory entities), while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes across thousands of scenario permutations. Machine learning techniques will then identify allocation patterns that maximize research output metrics while minimizing systemic risks. The computational workload requires HPC resources due to the need for simultaneous optimization of nonlinear variables across multiple temporal and organizational scales, with individual simulations involving >10^6 decision nodes. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for real-time resource reallocation in R&D programs, quantitative risk propagation models for multi-project systems, and scalability benchmarks for managing distributed innovation networks. This work will advance evidence-based practices in research administration by enabling data-driven tradeoff analyses between short-term operational efficiency and long-term strategic investment in scientific enterprises. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation modules and case studies demonstrating computational gains over conventional project management tools in pharmaceutical development and clean energy consortium contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage projects, programs and organizations involving basic and applied research, or specialized technology applications, in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in all aspects of business management applied to the leadership and control of scientific, clinical, engineering and social scientific enterprises; the management of related operational, security and logistical issues; and technical competence in one or more research disciplines.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for real-time, multi-agent simulation of decentralized accounting ecosystems. The focus lies in modeling emergent behaviors within blockchain-enabled accounting networks, where autonomous agents—representing firms, auditors, and regulatory nodes—interact under smart contract governance. Traditional accounting research struggles to capture the nonlinear dynamics of such systems, particularly as cryptographic consensus mechanisms, tokenized incentives, and automated compliance protocols introduce unprecedented complexity. The proposed approach combines agent-based modeling with game-theoretic reinforcement learning, implemented through parallelized simulations on GPU clusters. Each agent will employ deep Q-networks to adapt strategies in response to evolving network states, while distributed ledger transactions are simulated at scale using cryptographic primitives optimized for massively parallel architectures. Key challenges include maintaining temporal consistency across asynchronous agent interactions and validating emergent network properties against real-world accounting governance frameworks. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable simulation platform for stress-testing decentralized accounting protocols under adversarial conditions, (2) quantitative insights into incentive alignment failures in automated audit systems, and (3) novel metrics for measuring systemic trust in algorithmically governed financial reporting environments. This work bridges distributed systems engineering with accounting theory, addressing critical gaps in understanding how next-generation accounting infrastructures might stabilize or destabilize financial ecosystems. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the required simulation fidelity across millions of concurrent agents while maintaining sub-second resolution of micro-level accounting events.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in accounting, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Marine transportation systems face increasing demands for efficiency, safety, and environmental sustainability, yet computational tools to model complex maritime operations at scale remain underdeveloped. This project proposes to address critical gaps in optimizing vessel routing, port logistics, and emissions mitigation through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations. The research focuses on three interconnected challenges: (1) simulating multi-vessel interactions in dynamic coastal environments under variable weather and traffic conditions, (2) optimizing global shipping routes considering real-time fuel consumption patterns and emission regulations, and (3) predicting infrastructure strain under climate-driven extreme weather scenarios. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, hydrodynamic simulations, and machine learning techniques to create a coupled simulation framework. High-fidelity vessel performance models will be developed using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to quantify energy use and emissions, while reinforcement learning algorithms will train adaptive routing systems on historical Automatic Identification System (AIS) data encompassing 500 million vessel positions. Port operations will be simulated through discrete-event models incorporating container handling robotics and tidal energy harvesting systems. The HPC resources will enable parallel execution of 10,000+ scenario variations across climate models and economic parameters, requiring petascale processing of coupled ocean-atmosphere data. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing bunker fuel consumption in regulated emission control areas, risk maps for coastal infrastructure resilience, and open-source algorithms for collision avoidance systems. By advancing computational methods specific to maritime operations, this work aims to provide actionable insights for decarbonization pathways in global shipping while establishing benchmark datasets for vessel-environment interaction modeling. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the non-linear system dynamics and spatiotemporal scales inherent to marine transportation challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in water transportation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of high-performance computing (HPC) resources into dermatopathology research is critical to advancing the analysis of complex, multidimensional datasets generated in the study of skin diseases. Current diagnostic workflows for conditions such as cutaneous lymphomas, autoimmune blistering disorders, and melanocytic neoplasms rely heavily on histopathological interpretation, yet emerging technologies—including whole-slide imaging, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplexed immunohistochemistry—produce vast, heterogeneous datasets that exceed the processing capacity of conventional computational tools. This project proposes to address this bottleneck by leveraging HPC infrastructure to develop and optimize machine learning (ML) models for automated feature extraction, pattern recognition, and predictive analytics in dermatopathology. The research will focus on two parallel objectives: (1) training deep neural networks to classify high-resolution histopathological images with subcellular precision, integrating clinical metadata and genomic data where available, and (2) creating scalable pipelines for multi-omics data fusion to identify molecular signatures associated with diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic relevance. Computational workflows will utilize containerized environments for reproducibility, with GPU-accelerated nodes employed for model training and inference. Validation will involve retrospective analysis of annotated case cohorts from institutional biorepositories, benchmarking against gold-standard pathologist interpretations. Anticipated outcomes include the generation of open-source tools for quantitative dermatopathology analysis, novel biomarkers for disease stratification, and frameworks to reduce interobserver variability in challenging diagnoses. By enabling rapid processing of terabyte-scale datasets, this work aims to establish a computational foundation for precision dermatopathology, directly supporting translational research in personalized treatment strategies and enhancing the scalability of digital pathology initiatives in clinical laboratories. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage memory-intensive workloads and ensure iterative model refinement within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical and microscopic diagnosis and analysis of skin diseases and disorders. May included related research in laboratory administration and the supervision and training of support personnel.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of biopsychosocial mechanisms underlying chronic pain management by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic interactions between psychological, behavioral, and physiological variables. Chronic pain conditions present complex challenges where traditional linear models fail to capture recursive relationships between cognitive-emotional processes, social determinants, and neurobiological adaptations. We propose developing a multilevel computational framework integrating individual patient data from electronic health records (EHRs), ecological momentary assessments (EMAs), and wearable biosensors with population-level behavioral trends. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate how variations in coping strategies, social support networks, and stress reactivity influence long-term pain trajectories. Machine learning pipelines will process multimodal data to identify risk profiles predictive of opioid misuse or treatment nonadherence. Computational demands include large-scale parameter space exploration for ABM calibration, federated learning across decentralized EHR datasets, and real-time optimization of personalized intervention strategies. HPC resources are essential to handle the iterative nature of these analyses, which involve millions of agent interactions per simulation epoch and high-dimensional optimization across 50+ psychosocial variables. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model of biobehavioral feedback loops in pain chronicity, (2) predictive algorithms for matching patients to cognitive-behavioral or mindfulness-based interventions, and (3) open-source tools for simulating community-level impacts of stigma reduction campaigns. By elucidating nonlinear pathways through which health beliefs and social inequities modulate physiological stress responses, this work will inform scalable, culturally attuned counseling approaches while maintaining strict privacy standards for sensitive health data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological study of health and illness, and recovery, from the perspective that these phenomena arise from a combination of physical, behavioral, and social conditions. Includes instruction in abnormal and social psychology, psychophysiology, psychopharmacology, learning processes, clinical and behavioral therapies, biopsychosocial modeling, clinical procedures and assessment, preventive education, psychotherapy, rehabilitation processes, and research methods.

abstract: Vocational rehabilitation counseling aims to optimize outcomes for individuals with disabilities through personalized, evidence-based interventions. However, current practices face challenges in integrating complex, multidimensional data—including medical histories, psychosocial factors, vocational assessments, and longitudinal employment outcomes—to predict intervention efficacy or tailor counseling strategies. Traditional analytical methods struggle to model nonlinear interactions among these variables at scale, limiting the field’s ability to identify critical predictors of success or dynamically adapt interventions. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulation frameworks that enhance decision-making in vocational rehabilitation. The research will utilize machine learning (ML) algorithms, including ensemble methods and neural networks, to analyze anonymized longitudinal datasets from state vocational rehabilitation agencies, healthcare systems, and community partners. These datasets encompass diverse variables such as disability type, service utilization patterns, employer engagement metrics, and post-intervention employment stability. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle high-dimensional data and perform sensitivity analyses on hypothetical intervention scenarios. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to unstructured case notes and client-counselor interactions to extract latent themes influencing outcomes. The project will validate models through cross-agency replication and real-time feedback loops with practicing counselors. Expected outcomes include the identification of modifiable risk factors for vocational disengagement, predictive tools to prioritize resource allocation, and a simulation platform for testing intervention combinations across demographic subgroups. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with clinical expertise, this work aims to advance personalized rehabilitation planning, reduce disparities in service access, and establish scalable computational methodologies for the health professions. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and training modules to empower counselors in adopting data-enhanced practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel and assist disabled individuals and recovering patients in order to achieve their greatest physical, mental, social, educational, and vocational potential. Includes instruction in patient evaluation and testing, rehabilitation program planning, patient support services and referral, job analysis, adjustment psychology, rehabilitation services provision, patient counseling and education, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are critical for biodiversity, carbon sequestration, and hydrological regulation, yet their resilience to climate-driven stressors remains poorly quantified at landscape scales. This project seeks to advance predictive understanding of forest resilience by integrating high-resolution remote sensing data, species-specific physiological thresholds, and dynamic climate projections. The primary challenge lies in modeling spatially explicit forest responses to compound stressors—such as drought, heatwaves, and pest outbreaks—across heterogeneous terrains, which demands computationally intensive simulations of biotic-abiotic feedbacks. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement an agent-based modeling framework that simulates individual tree growth, mortality, and regeneration under varying climate scenarios. The model will integrate multi-scale datasets, including LiDAR-derived canopy structure, soil moisture dynamics from distributed sensor networks, and species trait databases, to parameterize interactions between forest composition, microclimate, and disturbance regimes. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will be employed to quantify uncertainty in resilience thresholds across 10^4 simulated forest stands, each representing unique combinations of species mixes, topography, and historical disturbance legacies. Additionally, machine learning pipelines will be developed to assimilate real-time satellite imagery into model calibration, reducing predictive biases. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of forest types most vulnerable to near-term climate extremes in the study region (Pacific Northwest, USA), (2) quantification of silvicultural interventions that enhance adaptive capacity, and (3) open-source tools for scenario-based forest management planning. By enabling fine-grained, process-based simulations across decadal timescales, this HPC-driven approach will provide actionable insights for conserving forest biodiversity and ecosystem services under rapidly changing environmental conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of one or more forest-related sciences to the study of environmental factors affecting forests and the growth and management of forest resources. Includes instruction in forest biology, forest hydrology, forest mensuration, silviculture, forest soils, water resources, environmental science, forest resources management, and wood science.

abstract: The growing complexity of computational workflows in commercial photography, driven by ultra-high-resolution imaging (8K+), multi-spectral capture, and AI-enhanced post-processing, has exposed critical limitations in conventional computing infrastructure. This project addresses the challenge of processing terabyte-scale visual datasets while maintaining artistic fidelity and meeting industry turnaround expectations. Current methods for tasks such as neural style transfer, computational lighting simulation, and batch processing of RAW files become prohibitively slow when handling modern medium-format digital captures or frame-accurate video sequences. We propose deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a hybrid pipeline combining distributed GPU rendering, containerized machine learning workflows, and memory-optimized preprocessing nodes. The research will focus on three key areas: 1) Parallel implementation of non-destructive editing operations across massive image stacks using PyTorch and OpenCL, 2) Photorealistic virtual staging through real-time ray tracing accelerated by multi-GPU architectures, and 3) Semantic segmentation of commercial product imagery at scale using vision transformers fine-tuned on proprietary datasets. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce processing times for complex compositing workflows by 70-90% compared to desktop workstations while enabling previously impractical techniques like iterative generative AI refinement across 10,000+ image campaigns. Outcomes will include optimized algorithms for photographic applications, performance benchmarks for heterogeneous computing clusters in visual media production, and a reproducible framework for cloud-native photography workflows. This work advances the integration of computational arts methodologies within commercial practice, providing artists with tools to push creative boundaries while maintaining technical feasibility for client-driven projects. The resource allocation will directly support both algorithmic development and large-scale testing using real-world datasets from active industry collaborations.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences, and recording events and people, via digital, film, still and video photography. Includes instruction in specialized camera and equipment operation and maintenance, applications to commercial and industrial needs, and photography business operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the intergenerational transmission of Indigenous ecological knowledge (IEK) among Pacific Islander communities, with a focus on how digital storytelling archives can illuminate patterns of cultural resilience and adaptation. While existing studies have qualitatively explored IEK, large-scale computational analysis of oral narratives, genealogical records, and environmental interaction data remains limited. The research problem centers on mapping nonlinear relationships between story content, linguistic markers of ecological practices, and historical environmental shifts across decentralized Pacific communities. A computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis will be applied to a corpus of over 20,000 digitized oral histories, ethnographic records, and colonial-era documents from Aotearoa (New Zealand), Vanuatu, and Hawaiʻi. Custom transformer models will be trained to identify place-based knowledge references, kinship-linked stewardship practices, and adaptive narratives in Indigenous languages and creoles. Concurrently, temporal graph networks will model the diffusion and transformation of ecological practices pre- and post-contact. HPC resources are critical for processing low-resource Pacific languages, running parallelized semantic analyses across multilingual texts, and simulating knowledge network evolution over 15 generations. Expected outcomes include 1) a geotemporal database linking narrative motifs to documented environmental changes, 2) quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural-ecological interdependencies in Pacific Studies, and 3) open-access tools for communities to analyze their own archival materials. By computationally bridging scales of individual storytelling and regional ecological knowledge systems, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in Indigenous-led area studies while informing contemporary climate adaptation strategies rooted in Pacific epistemologies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Australasia and the Pacific Ocean, related island groups and bordering coastal regions, and including pre- and post-colonial migration patterns.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding the evolutionary and ecological dynamics of ancient ecosystems through computational paleontology. A central challenge in paleobiological research lies in integrating large, heterogeneous datasets—including fossil occurrence records, geochemical proxies, and stratigraphic data—to model species interactions, biogeographic patterns, and responses to environmental perturbations across deep time. Current computational limitations restrict the scalability of probabilistic models and simulations, particularly when analyzing high-resolution, continent-scale datasets spanning millions of years. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-tiered computational approach. First, Bayesian hierarchical models will be implemented to quantify uncertainties in fossil preservation biases and temporal correlations among extinction events. Second, agent-based simulations will reconstruct paleocommunity dynamics under varying climatic and tectonic scenarios, parameterized by geochemical and lithostratigraphic data. These simulations will integrate GPU-accelerated algorithms to handle complex spatial interactions among species and abiotic factors. Third, machine learning workflows will classify microfossil assemblages from 3D µCT scan datasets, automating taxonomic identifications while accounting for taphonomic distortion. The requested HPC resources will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets, reduce runtime for iterative model testing, and support high-dimensional visualization of paleoecological networks. Anticipated outcomes include novel frameworks for quantifying extinction selectivity in mass extinction intervals, spatially explicit models of Mesozoic vertebrate dispersal, and open-source tools for microfossil data processing. By resolving computational bottlenecks, this work will advance predictive capacity for ecosystem resilience under anthropogenic climate change while establishing scalable methods for synthesizing paleontological and geological data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of extinct life forms and associated fossil remains, and the reconstruction and analysis of ancient life forms, ecosystems, and geologic processes. Includes instruction in sedimentation and fossilization processes, fossil chemistry, evolutionary biology, paleoecology, paleoclimatology, trace fossils, micropaleontology, invertebrate paleontology, vertebrate paleontology, paleobotany, field research methods, and laboratory research and conservation methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of personalizing cosmetic treatments while minimizing damage to hair and skin, a persistent issue in cosmetology due to the biological and structural diversity of clients. Current approaches rely heavily on generalized product formulations and heuristic techniques, often resulting in suboptimal outcomes or unintended harm. To bridge this gap, the research proposes a computational framework integrating high-fidelity biophysical modeling, machine learning (ML), and large-scale data analytics to predict hyper-personalized treatment plans. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will simulate molecular interactions between common cosmetic agents (e.g., dyes, relaxers) and keratin structures across diverse hair types, informed by spectroscopic and microscopic datasets. Concurrently, a convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on 3D-scanned hair and skin samples to classify texture, porosity, and damage levels, enabling real-time recommendations during client consultations. A parallelized optimization algorithm will then iteratively refine treatment parameters (e.g., chemical concentrations, exposure times) to balance efficacy with safety thresholds. The computational pipeline will be validated against empirical data from partnered salons, incorporating feedback loops to enhance model accuracy. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive tool for licensed cosmetologists, reducing trial-and-error practices and fostering evidence-based decision-making. By elucidating microstructure-level dynamics of cosmetic interventions, the project also aims to establish foundational datasets for understudied hair types, addressing biases in existing beauty technology. The scalability of the models will further support future research into sustainable formulation design and virtual training environments, advancing both the scientific rigor and ethical standards of cosmetology practice.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to cut, trim, and style scalp, facial, and body hair; apply cosmetic preparations; perform manicures and pedicures; massage the head and extremities; and prepare for practice as licensed cosmetologists in specialized or full-service salons.  Includes instruction in hair cutting and styling, manicuring, pedicuring, facial treatments, shampooing, chemical applications, esthetics, shop management, sanitation and safety, customer service, and applicable professional and labor laws and regulations.

abstract: Sleep disorders present complex diagnostic challenges due to the multidimensional nature of polysomnographic data, which includes electroencephalographic (EEG), electrooculographic (EOG), electromyographic (EMG), and cardiorespiratory signals. Current clinical workflows rely on manual scoring of sleep stages and events, a time-intensive process prone to inter-rater variability and limited in its capacity to detect subtle physiological patterns predictive of disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy, or parasomnias. This project proposes the development of automated, high-resolution analysis pipelines leveraging machine learning (ML) and signal processing to improve the accuracy and efficiency of sleep disorder diagnostics. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on large-scale polysomnography datasets, encompassing diverse patient demographics and pathologies. Computational workflows will integrate time-frequency analysis for noise reduction, feature extraction from multichannel biosignals, and ensemble modeling to classify sleep stages and pathological events. A key innovation involves the synthesis of spatially resolved EEG dynamics with cardiorespiratory variability metrics to identify novel biomarkers of sleep disruption. HPC capabilities are critical for managing the computational load of processing terabytes of high-density physiological data, optimizing hyperparameters for convolutional and recurrent neural networks, and conducting large-scale validation across heterogeneous cohorts. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated polysomnography scoring, validated ML models with clinical interpretability, and new insights into the physiological signatures of understudied sleep disorders. By enhancing the granularity and reproducibility of sleep data analysis, this work aims to advance personalized treatment strategies, reduce diagnostic latency, and establish scalable infrastructure for translational sleep research. The requested resources will directly support iterative model training, real-time simulation of biosignal processing pipelines, and benchmarking against gold-standard clinical assessments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for electromagnetic (EM) wave interactions with complex biological systems, a critical challenge in applied physics with direct applications to medical imaging and therapeutic technologies. Current analytical and numerical approaches struggle to resolve the multi-scale, nonlinear dynamics of EM fields in heterogeneous biological tissues, particularly at cellular and subcellular levels. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for macroscale wave propagation with stochastic Monte Carlo simulations for microscale energy deposition. This approach will enable coupled modeling of EM field distributions, thermal effects, and biochemical responses across spatial scales spanning meters to nanometers. The computational demands of this multi-physics problem are substantial, requiring iterative 3D simulations with adaptive mesh refinement and statistical sampling of stochastic processes. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the necessary resolution and parameter space exploration within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include validated models of EM-tissue interactions under varying physiological conditions, which will inform the design of next-generation, non-invasive medical devices for conditions such as cardiac arrhythmias and neurological disorders. These models will also provide mechanistic insights into safety thresholds for emerging high-frequency EM technologies. By bridging gaps between classical electrodynamics, statistical biophysics, and computational engineering, this work will establish a scalable platform for interdisciplinary research at the physics-biology interface. The requested computing resources will directly support the parallelization of FDTD solvers, optimization of GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo algorithms, and large-scale data analysis, ensuring robust validation against experimental measurements from collaborative biomedical partners.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics to a technical discipline or with the interface between physics and other disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale digital humanities investigation into the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in Ukraine, with emphasis on underrepresented regional and gender perspectives. The research problem centers on analyzing vast, unstructured datasets—including digitized folklore archives, Soviet-era periodicals, post-independence media, and contemporary social media—to identify patterns in how cultural symbols, linguistic markers, and collective memory have been negotiated across Ukraine’s contested historical landscapes. Current methodologies in cultural studies lack scalable tools to systematically process multimodal Ukrainian-language materials spanning five centuries while accounting for dialectal diversity, shifting political terminologies, and erasures in archival records. Our computational approach integrates transformer-based language models fine-tuned on historical Ukrainian texts, geospatial network analysis of cultural production centers, and semi-supervised clustering algorithms to map discursive continuities and fractures across time, space, and sociocultural groups. The workflow requires parallelized processing of 12TB of text and image data, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for graph-based analyses of regional cultural networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of persistent subnational narrative frameworks in border regions like Slobozhanshchyna and Bukovyna; (2) quantitative models tracing the impact of 20th-century state policies on gendered representations in folk traditions; (3) an open-access annotated corpus of Ukrainian cultural discourse from 1600–2023. By enabling computationally intensive analysis at unprecedented temporal and geographical granularity, this project will provide new empirical foundations for understanding cultural resilience and adaptation in Ukraine while developing transferable pipelines for non-Anglocentric digital humanities research. The requested resources directly address the computational barriers that have historically constrained large-scope cultural studies in under-resourced linguistic contexts.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Ukraine and its inhabitants, and related border regions, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity simulations of radiation transport in advanced nuclear reactor systems to optimize shielding designs and improve operational safety protocols. Current models for neutron and gamma-ray propagation rely on simplified geometric approximations or homogenized material properties, limiting their accuracy in predicting localized radiation hotspots and dose distributions in complex, heterogeneous reactor environments. To address this, we propose a computational workflow combining deterministic transport methods (e.g., discrete ordinates solvers) with Monte Carlo-based stochastic sampling, implemented through the OpenMC and Shift frameworks. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform full-core, 3D simulations at unprecedented spatial resolutions (<1 mm voxel size) while incorporating real-time thermal-hydraulic feedback from coupled multiphysics models. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive cross-section libraries for hundreds of isotopic species and achieving scalable parallelism across 10,000+ CPU cores to reduce wall-clock time for iterative design optimization. Expected outcomes include validated benchmarks for next-generation reactor shielding configurations, reducing conservatism in safety margins by 15-20% compared to legacy systems, and an open-source toolset for automated variance reduction in hybrid deterministic-stochastic simulations. This work directly supports the development of compact, inherently safe reactor designs by enabling rapid virtual prototyping of radiation management strategies. Successful implementation will advance regulatory compliance frameworks by providing high-confidence dose prediction capabilities for non-standard reactor geometries, with additional applications in nuclear waste storage optimization and medical isotope production facilities. The requested HPC allocation will enable month-long parametric studies equivalent to 2.8 million CPU-hours, including sensitivity analyses of novel shielding composites under transient accident scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering, knowledge and technical skills in support of engineer and other professionals operating nuclear facilities and engaged in nuclear applications and safety procedures. Includes instruction in physics, nuclear science, nuclear systems, nuclear plant and systems design, radiological safety, radiological applications, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision manufacturing processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize complex fabrication workflows. Precision production trades rely on intricate material interactions, toolpath planning, and thermal-mechanical dynamics, yet current simulation tools often lack the resolution or computational scalability to capture multi-physics phenomena at production-relevant scales. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing high-fidelity computational models that integrate technical illustration data, material science parameters, and real-time sensor feedback to predict outcomes in subtractive and additive manufacturing processes. Key computational methods include finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain modeling during machining, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for heat distribution in laser-based systems, and machine learning algorithms to correlate process variables with product quality metrics. These workflows demand parallelized computing architectures to handle large datasets from 3D technical drawings, material databases, and in-situ monitoring systems. The requested HPC resources will enable parametric studies of tool geometry, feed rates, and energy inputs across thousands of simulated production scenarios, reducing reliance on physical prototyping. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for minimizing material waste, optimizing surface finish quality, and preventing tool failure in CNC machining and laser cutting applications. By coupling HPC-driven insights with precision tradecraft principles, this work aims to establish a framework for adaptive manufacturing systems that dynamically adjust process parameters based on computational forecasts. The results will directly benefit industries requiring micron-level precision, such as aerospace component fabrication and medical device production, while providing educational case studies for integrating computational tools into technical trades curricula.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in creating products using precision crafting and technical illustration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic population modeling under rapidly shifting demographic conditions, with a focus on multi-level interactions between individual behaviors, household dynamics, and regional migration patterns. Traditional demographic models often struggle to integrate real-time, high-resolution data streams—such as longitudinal surveys, geospatial mobility traces, and administrative records—while accounting for complex feedback loops between fertility, mortality, and migration. This limitation hinders accurate projections in contexts like urbanization surges, climate-driven displacement, or post-pandemic population recovery. The proposed research will develop a scalable computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with Bayesian hierarchical techniques to simulate population systems at granular spatiotemporal scales. By parallelizing stochastic simulations across HPC nodes, the framework will assimilate heterogeneous data sources (e.g., census microdata, satellite-derived settlement layers) to quantify uncertainties in demographic transitions. Key objectives include (1) modeling decision-making processes underlying migration in response to environmental and socioeconomic stressors, (2) estimating localized fertility-rate dependencies on education access and healthcare infrastructure, and (3) validating projections against historical demographic crises. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive datasets, optimizing parameter calibration via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, and running ensemble simulations to assess policy interventions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive population forecasting, peer-reviewed insights into resilience factors for aging populations, and evidence-based scenarios to guide regional planning. This work will address methodological gaps in capturing non-linear demographic interactions while providing a replicable computational architecture for interdisciplinary social science research.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of population models and population phenomena, and related problems of social structure and behavior. Includes instruction in population growth, spatial distribution, mortality and fertility factors, migration, dynamic population modeling, population estimation and projection, mathematical and statistical analysis of population data, population policy studies, and applications to problems in economics and government planning.

abstract: The fabrication of high-precision ophthalmic lenses requires addressing complex optical challenges influenced by individual patient anatomy, material properties, and environmental factors. Current lens design and testing workflows rely on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-consuming, resource-intensive, and limited in accounting for real-world variability in ocular biomechanics and wearer-specific conditions. This project proposes a computational approach to optimize lens manufacturing by developing physics-informed machine learning models that simulate light propagation, material stress, and patient-specific visual outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train deep neural networks on multi-modal datasets, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans, lens material databases, and dynamic eye movement recordings. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution in progressive and multifocal lenses under mechanical and thermal processing conditions, while Monte Carlo ray-tracing simulations will evaluate optical performance across diverse pupil sizes and illumination scenarios. By integrating these computational pipelines, the project aims to predict optimal lens curvature, thickness, and coating parameters that minimize aberrations and maximize durability. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for virtual lens prototyping, reducing physical trial iterations by ≥50% and improving edge thickness consistency in high-index lenses. The computational tools developed will also enable rapid customization of lenses for patients with irregular corneal topography or post-surgical ocular geometries. This work aligns with advancements in precision ophthalmics, offering labs a pathway to adopt data-driven manufacturing practices while maintaining compliance with ANSI Z80.1 safety standards. Successful implementation will enhance the scalability of personalized eyewear production and inform educational modules on computational optics for ophthalmic technologists.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the cascading impacts of climate-driven migration on transnational governance systems, an urgent yet understudied nexus of environmental, socio-political, and economic dynamics. Current migration models often isolate environmental stressors from institutional responses, neglecting feedback loops between displaced populations, shifting resource availability, and multilateral policy frameworks. Our research addresses this gap by integrating geospatial climate projections, agent-based demographic simulations, and network analyses of international legal architectures. The computational approach combines climate data (CMIP6 ensembles) with stochastic agent models to simulate migration decision-making under variable drought and sea-level rise scenarios, scaled across six geopolitically critical regions. These outputs will feed into a dynamic network model that maps strain on international governance systems, including trade agreements, refugee protocols, and disaster response treaties. By iteratively coupling environmental and institutional layers, the framework will identify tipping points where existing governance structures risk failure and propose adaptive policy pathways. HPC resources are essential to process petabyte-scale climate datasets, run high-resolution simulations across diverse socioecological contexts, and optimize multi-objective governance strategies via machine learning. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for anticipatory governance, peer-reviewed insights into resilience bottlenecks in international frameworks, and policy briefs targeting UN climate adaptation platforms. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges climatology, computational social science, and international relations, offering a novel paradigm to analyze emergent risks in global systems under ecological stress. The project aligns with UNESCO’s priorities in climate justice while advancing methodological innovation in data-driven globalization studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on global and international issues from the perspective of the social sciences, social services, and related fields.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical need for advanced computational tools in enhancing pedagogical strategies for Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) teacher education. Current methods for training FCS educators lack robust frameworks to model the complex, dynamic interactions between instructional techniques, student engagement, and learning outcomes in home economics contexts, such as nutrition science, textile design, and household resource management. Traditional experimental or observational approaches struggle to account for the multivariate nature of these educational environments, limiting the scalability and generalizability of teacher training programs. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate diverse classroom scenarios, incorporating variables such as student demographics, socio-economic backgrounds, and differentiated learning styles. Machine learning algorithms will analyze historical datasets of student performance and teaching evaluations to identify patterns in effective instructional strategies. The computational models will further test hypothetical interventions, such as virtual labs for culinary arts or adaptive learning modules for financial literacy education, to predict their efficacy across varied educational settings. By integrating these computational outputs with empirical data from partner FCS teacher training programs, the project aims to generate evidence-based guidelines for optimizing curriculum design and instructional delivery. The anticipated outcomes include a scalable, open-access toolkit for FCS educators to simulate and refine teaching practices, thereby improving preparedness for real-world classroom challenges. This work aligns with national priorities to modernize vocational education through data-driven innovation, ultimately contributing to a more skilled workforce in home economics disciplines. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required computational throughput for parallelized simulations and large-scale data analytics, enabling real-time feedback loops for iterative model refinement.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Home Economics Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational home economics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance osteopathic medicine research by elucidating the biomechanical and molecular mechanisms underlying osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT). Despite the widespread clinical use of OMT to address musculoskeletal dysfunction and systemic health, the precise biophysical interactions between manual interventions, tissue response, and physiological outcomes remain poorly characterized. This gap limits evidence-based optimization of OMT protocols and hinders the integration of osteopathic principles into broader precision medicine frameworks. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational modeling approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) of musculoskeletal dynamics with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of mechanotransduction pathways activated by OMT. FEA will simulate tissue deformation, strain distribution, and fluid flow in anatomically accurate 3D models derived from patient-specific MRI/CT data. Concurrently, MD simulations will explore how mechanical forces alter ion channel conformations, extracellular matrix protein interactions, and downstream signaling cascades linked to anti-inflammatory or regenerative responses. Machine learning models will integrate these datasets to predict patient-specific OMT outcomes based on biomechanical, genomic, and clinical variables. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of multiscale simulations, large-scale medical image processing, and iterative training of predictive algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for mechanistically linking OMT techniques to physiological effects, identification of biomarkers for treatment responsiveness, and open-access tools for simulating osteopathic interventions in diverse patient populations. This work will strengthen the evidence base for osteopathic medicine, enable data-driven refinement of manipulative therapies, and foster interdisciplinary collaborations bridging clinical practice, systems biology, and computational biomechanics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of osteopathic medicine, involving a combination of medical principles and procedures and osteopathic principles of holistic medicine and the relationship of the musculoskeletal system to general health. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, preventive medicine, family and community medicine, medical informatics, disease systems, organ and physiologic systems, osteopathic principles and practice, osteopathic manipulative treatment, musculoskeletal and skin systems, clinical specialty rotations, medical ethics, and professional standards and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize irrigation and nutrient delivery systems for ornamental landscapes, addressing inefficiencies in current practices that lead to water waste, plant stress, and operational costs. While modern landscaping prioritizes sustainability, dynamic interactions between soil heterogeneity, plant species-specific water requirements, and microclimate variability complicate manual or rule-based irrigation scheduling. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach integrating soil moisture sensor data, real-time weather forecasts, and plant physiological models to predict irrigation demands at fine spatial and temporal scales. Agent-based modeling will simulate water transport in root zones across diverse soil compositions, while machine learning algorithms trained on historical sensor data will identify patterns in turfgrass and ornamental plant responses to drought and nutrient deficits. The HPC environment is critical for running ensemble simulations that account for uncertainty in precipitation forecasts and soil properties, enabling adaptive irrigation strategies tailored to site-specific conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that recommends optimized watering schedules, reducing water use by an estimated 20–35% compared to conventional systems without compromising plant health. Additionally, the project will generate a curated dataset linking plant performance metrics to environmental stressors, supporting future research in drought-resistant landscaping species. By leveraging scalable computational resources, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical horticultural principles and data-driven grounds management practices, offering actionable insights for commercial landscaping operations, urban planners, and agricultural extension services.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: Radiation therapy is a cornerstone of modern oncology, requiring precise delivery of therapeutic doses to tumor targets while minimizing exposure to surrounding healthy tissues. Current treatment planning systems rely on deterministic algorithms that approximate radiation transport, introducing uncertainties in complex anatomical scenarios. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, Monte Carlo-based computational framework for radiation dose calculation and treatment optimization, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the limitations of conventional methods. The primary research problem centers on the computational cost of Monte Carlo simulations, which traditionally limit their clinical utility despite superior accuracy in modeling radiation interactions. By implementing GPU-accelerated, parallelized algorithms on HPC infrastructure, we aim to reduce simulation times from hours to minutes, enabling real-time, patient-specific treatment planning. The computational approach integrates three-dimensional patient imaging data, radiation source modeling, and machine learning techniques to iteratively optimize beam parameters and dose distributions. Key objectives include validating simulated dose profiles against physical phantom measurements and clinical patient data, as well as developing predictive models for normal tissue toxicity. The project’s outcomes are expected to advance adaptive radiotherapy workflows, particularly for heterogeneous tumor geometries such as lung and head-and-neck cancers, where tissue density variations significantly impact dose deposition. Successful implementation will provide a scalable platform for exploring novel treatment modalities, including flash radiotherapy and combined photon-electron beam techniques. By bridging the gap between computational precision and clinical feasibility, this work has the potential to reduce treatment-related complications, improve local tumor control, and establish best practices for HPC-driven innovation in radiologic science. Resource allocation will support GPU node utilization, large-scale data storage for patient cohorts, and the development of open-source tools to disseminate findings to the medical physics community.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in commercial meat processing workflows, with a focus on optimizing yield, reducing waste, and enhancing food safety through advanced computational modeling. The meat-cutting industry faces persistent challenges in balancing manual expertise with scalable precision, particularly in predicting optimal cutting patterns for diverse animal anatomies, minimizing pathogen risks during processing, and adhering to dynamic regulatory standards. Traditional approaches rely heavily on experiential knowledge, which limits standardization and adaptability to variable inputs such as animal size, muscle composition, and market demand. To bridge this gap, this research proposes the development of a multi-modal computational framework integrating three core components: (1) biomechanical simulations of tissue separation under varying blade geometries and cutting forces, validated against empirical data from sensor-equipped tools; (2) machine learning models trained on hyperspectral imaging datasets to predict microbial contamination hotspots in real time; and (3) generative algorithms for adaptive cutting-path optimization that account for carcass-specific morphology and real-time yield targets. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution 3D scans from livestock imaging systems, finite element analysis of tissue mechanics at micron-level granularity, and ensemble modeling of contamination risk factors across heterogeneous environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of dynamically adjusting cutting protocols to maximize product value while ensuring compliance with food safety regulations. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of butchering expertise, this work aims to establish computational tools that preserve artisanal craftsmanship while introducing data-driven scalability—a critical advancement for an industry navigating labor shortages and sustainability pressures. The resulting models will be disseminated through collaborative partnerships with vocational training programs and meat processing facilities, fostering innovation in a traditionally low-tech sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, cut, and package animal meat products in commercial establishments and to function as licensed meat cutters/butchers.  Includes instruction in product recognition for beef, veal, lamb, pork, poultry, and fancy and smoked meats; retail and wholesale cutting and specialty cuts; packaging and counter display; shop safety; meat sanitation, storage and rotation; quality control; meat handling laws and regulations; and customer service.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in animal populations pose critical threats to veterinary and human public health, with complex transmission dynamics influenced by interspecies interactions, environmental factors, and heterogeneous management practices. Current epidemiological models often lack the resolution to capture these multi-scale dynamics, limiting the design of targeted interventions. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, multi-agent computational framework to simulate AMR transmission across livestock, wildlife, and environmental reservoirs in agricultural ecosystems. The research will integrate genomic, epidemiological, and environmental data to model resistance gene transfer, host mobility, and pathogen persistence under varying husbandry practices and climate conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute spatially explicit, individual-based simulations at scale, incorporating millions of agents representing animals, vectors, and microbial communities. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will be used to quantify uncertainty in transmission pathways, while machine learning algorithms will analyze large metagenomic datasets to identify AMR hotspot signatures. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU acceleration for real-time parameter optimization during scenario testing, such as evaluating the impact of vaccination schedules or feed additive policies. Outcomes will include predictive maps of AMR emergence risks, validated against field surveillance data from partner veterinary networks, and a publicly accessible decision-support tool for optimizing antimicrobial stewardship programs. By elucidating context-specific drivers of resistance spread, this work aims to advance preventive strategies in veterinary medicine, reduce reliance on empirical treatment protocols, and inform One Health policies bridging animal and human health sectors. The scalable computational framework will also provide a foundation for future studies on zoonotic disease dynamics and resilience planning in agroecosystems.
cip_definition: Research focused on the investigation of and intervention in health and disease problems of animal and related human communities, comparative medicine, and animal public health. May included related research in biostatistics, epidemiology, environmental control, toxicology and the planning and administration of animal health programs and services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the creation and analysis of large-scale generative visual art and immersive digital installations, addressing the growing computational demands of contemporary visual arts practice. As algorithmic and data-driven art methodologies expand, artists and researchers increasingly require robust computational infrastructure to develop, simulate, and render complex multimedia works. Current limitations in local computing capacity restrict experimentation with high-resolution 3D environments, real-time interactive systems, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on terabyte-scale visual datasets. The proposed research will employ parallelized rendering pipelines and distributed machine learning frameworks to optimize the production of dynamic, algorithmically generated artworks. Key computational tasks include training custom vision models on heterogeneous cultural image corpora, simulating particle-based visual effects across GPU clusters, and implementing real-time viewer interaction protocols for large-scale installations. By utilizing HPC resources, the project aims to overcome latency and scalability barriers in processing 4K/8K visual outputs while enabling iterative refinement of generative systems through rapid prototyping. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible repository of optimized computational art workflows, benchmarking data on HPC-driven creative processes, and three experimental installations premiered at interdisciplinary arts venues. This work will establish new methodological frameworks for integrating advanced computing into visual arts research, offering scalable solutions for data-intensive digital humanities projects while expanding the technical lexicon of contemporary artistic practice. The results will directly inform curriculum development in computational media design, bridging gaps between artistic experimentation and high-performance technical infrastructures.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the visual and performing arts and that may prepare individuals in any of the visual artistic media or performing disciplines.
