abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine through the integration of multi-omics data and clinical patient records. A central challenge in modern medicine lies in understanding the molecular and phenotypic heterogeneity of complex diseases, such as cancer, cardiovascular disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions, which often lead to variable treatment responses. Traditional approaches struggle to synthesize high-dimensional genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets with clinical variables, limiting the development of personalized therapeutic strategies. To address this, we propose a computational framework employing machine learning (ML) and network analysis to identify predictive biomarkers, disease subtypes, and therapeutic targets. Large-scale genomic sequencing data from public repositories (e.g., TCGA, UK Biobank) and institutional electronic health records will be harmonized, followed by feature selection using dimensionality reduction techniques. Deep neural networks will model nonlinear interactions between molecular profiles and clinical outcomes, while graph-based algorithms will map disease-associated protein interaction networks. These analyses demand significant computational power due to the volume of data (>1 PB), iterative model training, and parallelized simulations of biological pathways. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid processing of these tasks, reducing runtime from months to days. Expected outcomes include validated ML models for predicting patient-specific treatment responses, novel biomarkers for early disease detection, and open-source tools for scalable multi-omics integration. This work will directly inform clinical trial design and therapeutic decision-making, bridging gaps between computational research and bedside application. By elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment resistance and comorbidity patterns, the project aims to improve patient stratification and reduce healthcare costs. The resulting datasets and pipelines will be shared with the broader research community, fostering collaboration in computational medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of illnesses, injuries, and other disorders of the human body. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, clinical medicine, examination and diagnosis, patient communications, medical ethics and law, professional standards, and rotations in specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, orthopedics, neurology, ophthalmology, radiology, clinical pathology, anesthesiology, family medicine, and psychiatry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven framework to model and optimize pedagogical strategies in STEM teacher training programs using high-performance computing (HPC). Despite advancements in educational theory, teacher professional development often relies on qualitative assessments and small-scale studies, limiting the scalability of evidence-based practices. This work addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing large, multimodal datasets—including classroom video recordings, student performance metrics, and teacher reflections—to identify patterns in effective instructional techniques. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) to evaluate teacher-student discourse, computer vision algorithms to assess classroom engagement dynamics, and agent-based modeling to simulate the impact of pedagogical interventions across diverse educational contexts. These methods require HPC resources due to the scale of data (10,000+ hours of video from 200 classrooms) and the complexity of training deep learning models for real-time feedback systems. By parallelizing tasks such as feature extraction from video streams and optimizing hyperparameters for ensemble models, HPC will enable rapid iteration of simulations testing how variations in lesson pacing, questioning strategies, and differentiation practices affect student outcomes. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for quantifying teaching effectiveness, personalized recommendations for teacher professional development, and generative models that propose context-aware instructional adaptations. This work will directly inform the design of competency-based training modules for pre-service and in-service STEM teachers, with broader implications for reducing disparities in subject-specific pedagogical training. The resource request prioritizes GPU nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale simulations of classroom interaction networks.
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Subject Areas, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education, specific academic and vocational programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how large-scale digital communication patterns within organizations shape decision-making, conflict resolution, and power dynamics, with a focus on the role of asynchronous and algorithm-mediated interactions. As organizations increasingly rely on distributed teams and digital platforms, understanding the computational traces of these interactions—such as email threads, project management tool logs, and intra-organizational social media data—is critical to addressing inefficiencies in collaboration and employee engagement. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable frameworks to analyze complex, temporally layered communication data and model its relationship to organizational outcomes. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), temporal network analysis, and agent-based modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabytes of multi-modal communication data, training transformer-based models to detect latent power dynamics and conflict markers in text, and simulating how micro-level interactions scale to macro-level organizational phenomena. Network analysis will map information flow bottlenecks and coalition formation, while agent-based models will test hypotheses about how communication policies (e.g., feedback latency rules, platform affordances) affect emergent outcomes like consensus-building speed. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel taxonomy of digitally mediated organizational communication patterns correlated with performance metrics, (2) open-source tools for real-time detection of systemic miscommunication risks, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for designing communication protocols in hybrid work environments. This work bridges computational social science with organizational communication theory, offering empirically grounded insights into how algorithmic systems mediate workplace relationships. The requested resources will enable parsing of context-specific language use at scale—a previously intractable challenge for qualitative-dominated disciplinary methods—while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for human-centric HPC applications.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on general communication processes and dynamics within organizations. Includes instruction in the development and maintenance of interpersonal group relations within organizations; decision-making and conflict management; the use of symbols to create and maintain organizational images, missions, and values; power and politics within organizations; human interaction with computer technology; and how communications socializes and supports employees and team members.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze ethical decision-making processes in complex, real-world professional environments, with a focus on identifying and mitigating systemic biases in organizational policies. Despite advances in ethical theory, practical applications often struggle to account for dynamic, multi-stakeholder scenarios where competing values and power imbalances complicate outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model large-scale simulations of ethical dilemmas across healthcare, corporate governance, and environmental policy contexts. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be used to represent diverse actors (e.g., professionals, institutions, communities) and their interactions under varying ethical frameworks (utilitarian, deontological, care ethics). Machine learning techniques will then identify patterns in emergent ethical conflicts and evaluate the efficacy of intervention strategies. A key innovation is the integration of empirical datasets—such as historical case law, public health records, and corporate ethics reports—to ground simulations in observed behavior. The computational demands of this approach are significant: ABM scalability requires parallel processing to manage thousands of concurrent agents, while NLP-driven analysis of unstructured ethical case texts necessitates GPU-accelerated transformers. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated ethical scenarios with annotated decision trees, (2) quantitative metrics for assessing bias and fairness in organizational ethics protocols, and (3) predictive models to guide policy redesign in high-stakes domains like AI governance and crisis triage systems. By bridging normative ethics with data-driven systems analysis, this work aims to equip practitioners with tools to navigate increasingly granular ethical trade-offs in sociotechnical systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the required computational depth and real-world validation at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of ethical issues in the workplace and public life, and the application of ethical decision-making to the practical problems of society and the professions. Includes instruction in ethical theory; history of ethics; contemporary social dilemmas; methods in applied ethics; and applications including medical ethics, legal ethics, business ethics, environmental ethics, and criminal justice ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of manufacturing components in tool and die applications demands advanced computational tools to optimize design, material behavior, and production efficiency. Current challenges include high costs of iterative physical prototyping, unpredictable material deformation during forming processes, and inefficiencies in toolpath generation for multi-axis machining. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address these limitations through large-scale simulations and machine learning-driven optimization. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) finite element analysis (FEA) of metal flow and stress distribution in progressive die systems under dynamic thermal-mechanical conditions, (2) generative design algorithms for lightweight yet durable jig and fixture configurations, and (3) physics-informed neural networks to predict tool wear patterns across diverse workpiece materials. By parallelizing these computationally intensive workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, the team aims to reduce simulation times for complex stamping operations from weeks to days while maintaining micron-level accuracy. The HPC environment will enable parametric studies examining the interplay between alloy microstructure, forming speeds, and die geometry at scales impractical for physical experimentation. Anticipated outcomes include open-source computational models for tool life prediction, optimized die designs for high-strength alloys, and adaptive toolpath strategies that minimize energy consumption in CNC machining. These results will directly benefit small-to-medium tooling enterprises by lowering R&D barriers and improving process sustainability. The project will also create curriculum modules integrating HPC workflows into tool and die technician training, preparing students for emerging demands in smart manufacturing. Resource allocation will support iterative model validation using real-world case studies from automotive stamping applications, ensuring practical relevance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate machine tools used in the forming of metal components, as well as the fabrication of special tools, dies, jigs and fixtures used in cutting, working and finishing metal components.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics and textual analysis within Ukrainian language studies. The Ukrainian language exhibits significant dialectal diversity and historical linguistic shifts, yet large-scale quantitative studies of its structural patterns, regional variations, and literary evolution remain underdeveloped due to the computational demands of processing vast textual corpora. This project addresses this gap by employing machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze digitized Ukrainian texts spanning five centuries, including vernacular sources, literary works, and dialectal records. The primary research objectives include (1) modeling phonological and morphological variation across dialects using neural networks, (2) identifying stylistic and thematic trends in 19th- and 20th-century Ukrainian literature through semantic clustering, and (3) reconstructing proto-forms of underdocumented historical dialects via comparative algorithms. The computational workflow involves training transformer-based models (e.g., BERT) on curated Ukrainian corpora, parallelizing feature extraction across multiple nodes, and running iterative simulations to map linguistic change. HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s scale—over 10TB of text data—and for optimizing complex tasks such as attention mechanism training and high-dimensional vector space modeling. Expected outcomes include the first open-access digital atlas of Ukrainian dialect boundaries, an annotated corpus of historical linguistic features, and publicly deployable NLP tools tailored to Ukrainian philology. These resources will enable novel interdisciplinary research in language preservation, literary analysis, and educational technology while strengthening computational infrastructure for Ukrainian studies globally. By integrating HPC-driven methods with traditional humanities scholarship, this project aims to redefine the methodological possibilities for research in Slavic linguistics and digital literary studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Ukrainian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Clinical and translational research increasingly relies on the integration of multi-dimensional biomedical data to uncover disease mechanisms and advance precision medicine. However, the volume and complexity of multi-omics datasets (e.g., genomics, proteomics, metabolomics), coupled with high-resolution clinical imaging and electronic health records (EHR), present significant computational challenges. Current analytical pipelines lack the scalability to process these heterogeneous data types efficiently, limiting the ability to model disease pathways or predict patient outcomes in real time. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to address these bottlenecks, focusing on scalable machine learning models and dynamic simulations of disease progression. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures to integrate multi-omics data with longitudinal clinical outcomes, identifying biomarkers predictive of treatment response in autoimmune disorders. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate immune cell interactions at single-cell resolution, informed by spatially resolved transcriptomic data from patient biopsies. These computational workflows require parallel processing, large-memory nodes, and distributed storage systems to handle datasets exceeding 500 TB, including raw sequencing files, 3D medical imaging, and federated EHR data from multi-institutional cohorts. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for autoimmune flare-ups, mechanistic insights into cell-level disease drivers, and open-source tools for reproducible clinical data analysis. By enabling rapid, large-scale data synthesis, this project will directly inform the design of targeted therapeutic trials and personalized treatment strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming latency and scalability barriers in current infrastructure, ensuring clinically actionable results within feasible timeframes. This work bridges computational innovation with translational impact, advancing a data-driven paradigm for clinical research.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated clinical science program that prepares clinicians to conduct clinical and translational research in various areas. Note: programs that prepare clinicians to conduct research in specific scientific fields should report under the relevant CIP code series (e.g., Series 26 Biological and Biomedical Sciences).

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural production and transnational identity formation of Latinx communities in the U.S., with a focus on Mexican-American/Chicano and Puerto Rican diasporic narratives. The research problem centers on analyzing large-scale, multilingual textual and audiovisual archives—including community newspapers, oral histories, digital media, and literature—to identify patterns of cultural resilience, hybridity, and resistance across generational and geographic divides. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these datasets, which span decades and incorporate code-switching, vernacular expressions, and non-standardized Spanish-English dialects. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) tailored for mixed-language corpora, network analysis to map thematic and discursive connections across communities, and machine learning models to trace evolving representations of identity in creative works. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on custom Latinx linguistic datasets, parallel processing of multimedia files, and visualizing dynamic cultural networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated materials, computational tools optimized for Latinx cultural analytics, and new interdisciplinary frameworks for studying intersectional identity in diasporic contexts. By bridging computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to amplify underrepresented narratives, inform culturally responsive pedagogy, and empower community-driven research partnerships. The work aligns with the program’s mission to center Latinx epistemologies while innovating methodologies for preserving and interpreting cultural heritage in the digital age.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Hispanic-American, Puerto Rican, Latinx, and Mexican-American/ Chicano Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic American immigrant populations within the U.S. and Canada, including Mexican-American Studies, Cuban American Studies, Puerto Rican Studies, and others.

abstract: The development of advanced biopharmaceutical processes and biomolecular systems requires precise molecular-level understanding of dynamic interactions between engineered proteins, metabolic pathways, and reactor environments. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve the timescales and complexity of these systems, particularly when optimizing enzymatic activity, drug delivery mechanisms, or metabolic fluxes in industrial-scale bioreactors. This project seeks to address these challenges through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multi-scale modeling to accelerate the rational design of protein-based therapeutics and sustainable biomanufacturing processes. We propose a computational framework integrating atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, coarse-grained enzyme-substrate binding analyses, and genome-scale metabolic network modeling. MD simulations will investigate conformational dynamics of engineered enzymes under process-relevant conditions (e.g., non-aqueous solvents, shear stress), while machine learning algorithms will predict mutation hotspots to enhance catalytic efficiency. Concurrently, constraint-based metabolic models will optimize carbon flux in microbial systems for target metabolite overproduction, informed by kinetic parameters derived from quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations of rate-limiting enzymatic steps. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of these compute-intensive tasks, including long-timescale MD trajectories (>100 μs aggregate sampling), high-throughput virtual screening of mutant enzyme libraries (>10^5 variants), and genome-scale flux balance analyses under dynamic reactor conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for (1) solvent-stable enzyme variants for continuous bioprocessing, (2) optimized metabolic chassis strains for antibody conjugate production, and (3) multi-physics correlations between molecular-scale protein behavior and reactor-scale mass transfer phenomena. This work will directly support the development of efficient, scalable biomanufacturing platforms for next-generation biologics, reducing reliance on empirical trial-and-error approaches in industrial chemical and biomolecular engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems at the interface of chemical engineering and biology, with an emphasis at the molecular level, such as biopharmaceutical processes, protein engineering, metabolic engineering, gene therapy, biomaterials, cell and tissue engineering, and drug delivery. Includes instruction in chemical engineering, thermodynamics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, momentum and heat transfer, cellular and molecular biotechnology, process design, and chemical reactor design.

abstract: Sheet metal forming processes are critical to manufacturing industries, yet optimizing these techniques for complex geometries and advanced materials remains a significant challenge. Traditional empirical approaches often lead to material waste, excessive energy consumption, and suboptimal product performance due to insufficient understanding of nonlinear deformation mechanics, anisotropic material behavior, and dynamic tool-workpiece interactions. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-stage sheet metal forming processes with unprecedented fidelity. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) simulations using explicit dynamics solvers to capture localized strain distributions, springback effects, and residual stress formation across aluminum, stainless steel, and advanced composite materials. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to predict optimal toolpath parameters, bending sequences, and force profiles through iterative simulation workflows. Validation will occur via parallel experimental studies using digital image correlation (DIC) metrology on physical forming equipment. The computational demand arises from the need to resolve microstructural interactions at mesoscale (10-100 µm) while maintaining macroscale part dimensions (1-10 m), requiring coupled multi-physics simulations with >10^8 degrees of freedom. HPC resources are essential to achieve practical simulation timescales through massively parallel computation and GPU-accelerated solver algorithms. Expected outcomes include predictive models for defect minimization in high-curvature forming operations, energy-optimized forming sequences for sustainable manufacturing, and a publicly accessible database of material-formability indices. This work will advance precision in sheet metal fabrication technologies while reducing prototyping costs by 30-50% in aerospace and automotive applications. The resulting computational toolkit will be disseminated through open-source plugins for industry-standard CAD/CAM platforms, directly enhancing workforce training capabilities in sheet metal technology programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to form, shape, bend and fold extruded metals, including the creation of new products, using hand tools and machines such as cornice brakes, forming rolls, and squaring shears.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interactions between urban park design, visitor behavior, and community well-being—an underexplored nexus within Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Studies. Traditional approaches to park planning rely on static demographic data and qualitative surveys, which lack the granularity to capture real-time decision-making patterns or predict emergent outcomes of design choices. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework simulating how diverse populations interact with park features under varying spatial configurations, seasonal conditions, and programmatic offerings. The model integrates geospatial data, anonymized mobility traces, and psychometric profiles derived from longitudinal leisure preference surveys to generate synthetic populations with heterogeneous needs. Computational challenges include scaling the ABM to simulate millions of agent-park interactions across probabilistic scenarios, processing high-resolution LiDAR scans of proposed park layouts, and training machine learning classifiers to detect behavioral patterns from simulated activity sequences. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo iterations, optimizing spatial network analyses, and managing memory-intensive datasets linking environmental variables to behavioral outcomes. Anticipated outputs include a validated decision-support tool for municipal planners, identifying design elements that maximize equitable access, social connectivity, and adaptive reuse of recreational spaces. By quantifying trade-offs between aesthetic, functional, and inclusivity priorities, this work advances evidence-based frameworks for leisure infrastructure investment while contributing methodological innovations to computational social science. Results will be disseminated through open-source model repositories and partnerships with the National Recreation and Park Association, ensuring translational impact for communities navigating urbanization pressures.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles underlying recreational and leisure activities, and the practices involved in providing indoor and outdoor recreational facilities and services for the general public.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research at the intersection of historiography, linguistics, and literary analysis. The core research problem centers on tracing the evolution of cultural narratives across multilingual historical texts from 16th- to 19th-century Europe, with a focus on how political upheavals influenced linguistic shifts and literary production in contested border regions. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to systematically analyze the scale and complexity of these materials, which include digitized manuscripts, print archives in six languages, and regional dialect corpora spanning four centuries. The project proposes a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), historical network analysis, and semantic modeling to 1) identify patterns of lexical borrowing across political boundaries, 2) map the diffusion of narrative tropes through time and space, and 3) correlate linguistic changes with sociopolitical events documented in parallel historical records. Key computational challenges include processing non-standardized orthographies in early modern texts, aligning multilingual embeddings for cross-linguistic comparison, and training transformer models on heterogenous, low-resource historical languages. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of over 50TB of textual data, iterative model training using graph neural networks to represent evolving semantic relationships, and dynamic visualization of multidimensional cultural networks. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital archive of annotated texts, computational workflows adaptable to other multilingual historical studies, and new interdisciplinary insights into how language ideologies shaped collective memory in transitional societies. By bridging computational scalability with humanistic interpretability, this project aims to establish reproducible methods for analyzing cultural change at previously unmanageable temporal and linguistic scales.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in historiography; historical research methods; linguistics; literature, philology; and studies of specific periods, issues and cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to optimize equitable and sustainable transportation infrastructure investments under climate uncertainty. Current planning models often struggle to account for dynamic interactions between socioeconomic disparities, shifting mobility patterns, and environmental risks at regional scales. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-agent simulation system coupled with machine learning-driven scenario analysis. The computational model will synthesize high-resolution spatial datasets—including census demographics, transportation network topologies, climate projections, and land-use patterns—to evaluate infrastructure adaptation strategies across multiple time horizons. Agent-based modeling will simulate individual and commercial travel behaviors under various policy interventions, while Monte Carlo methods assess risks from extreme weather events. Graph neural networks will be trained to identify vulnerable network segments and predict cascading failure impacts on accessibility. By parallelizing these computationally intensive simulations across thousands of cores, we aim to quantify trade-offs between equity metrics, fiscal constraints, and emissions targets at unprecedented spatial granularity. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support toolkit for transportation planners, validated through case studies of mid-sized metropolitan regions. This work will advance methodological integration of GIS, complex systems theory, and climate resilience analytics in public infrastructure planning. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling terabyte-scale urban datasets and achieving policy-relevant simulation timescales, directly supporting evidence-based investments in transportation systems that balance efficiency, environmental justice, and adaptive capacity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the economic, social, spatial, and environmental aspects of transportation and infrastructure planning. Includes instruction in economics, environmental analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, risk analysis, transportation economics, transportation evaluation, transportation planning, transportation policy, and urban transportation planning.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution of legal reasoning within judicial decisions across common law jurisdictions. The study addresses a critical gap in computational legal research: the lack of scalable frameworks for tracing doctrinal shifts and their sociopolitical drivers in large, unstructured corpora of case law. By integrating natural language processing (NLP), temporal network analysis, and agent-based modeling, the project will map relationships between legal concepts, judicial citations, and external sociodemographic variables over a 50-year period. The computational approach involves training domain-specific language models on a curated dataset of 10 million judicial opinions from U.S. federal courts and selected Commonwealth jurisdictions, followed by dynamic network simulations to model the propagation of legal arguments. Key technical challenges include developing hybrid architectures to process legalese semantics at scale and implementing graph neural networks capable of handling sparse temporal connections in citation networks. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for longitudinal legal pattern detection, 2) quantitative evidence of feedback loops between judicial decision-making and legislative activity, and 3) novel metrics for measuring legal stability in complex systems. This work bridges computational social science and jurisprudential theory, offering methodological innovations for studying law as a complex adaptive system while providing practical tools to enhance judicial analytics. The requested HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on terabyte-scale legal texts and running iterative simulations of doctrinal evolution across multiple parallel scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of law, for taking state and national bar examinations, and for advanced research in jurisprudence. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of the legal system, including the statutory, administrative, and judicial components of civil and criminal law.

abstract: Ensuring microbial safety while preserving nutritional and sensory quality in processed foods remains a critical challenge in food technology. Traditional thermal processing methods often rely on empirical models that inadequately balance energy efficiency, nutrient retention, and pathogen inactivation, particularly in heterogeneous food matrices. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to optimize thermal processing and packaging design for plant-based food products. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with kinetic models of microbial inactivation, nutrient degradation, and heat transfer to predict system behavior under varying processing conditions. A parallelized finite element approach will model heat distribution in complex food geometries, while machine learning algorithms will analyze large datasets to identify energy-efficient processing parameters that maximize safety and quality. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will assess gas diffusion properties of novel biodegradable packaging materials to extend shelf life. The computational intensity of these multi-physics models—requiring millions of processor hours for parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and 3D visualization—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for optimizing industrial-scale retort systems, data-driven packaging material design guidelines, and reduced energy consumption in food processing. This work will advance precision engineering in food manufacturing, directly supporting the development of sustainable, nutrient-dense food products while addressing global food safety challenges. Results will be disseminated through open-source models and collaborations with food processors to bridge academic research and industry innovation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the development and implementation of manufacturing, packaging, storage, and distribution technologies and processes for food products. Includes instruction in food engineering, food preservation and handling, food preparation, food packaging and display, food storage and shipment, and related equipment and facilities design, operation, and maintenance.

abstract: The integration of decentralized renewable energy sources into existing power grids presents a critical challenge for achieving net-zero emissions targets, particularly as distributed generation and storage systems scale in complexity and heterogeneity. Current simulation tools lack the capability to model dynamic, multi-domain interactions between thousands of geographically dispersed assets—including solar arrays, small-scale wind turbines, and heterogeneous battery systems—while accounting for real-time grid stability metrics and stochastic demand patterns. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for optimizing the design and operation of hyper-localized energy networks through coupled electro-thermal-storage modeling. By leveraging GPU-accelerated finite element analysis and graph neural networks, the proposed methodology will resolve multi-physics interactions across temporal scales (nanosecond transients to seasonal storage cycles) and spatial resolutions (component-level degradation to regional power flow). The computational workflow will integrate real-world weather datasets, demand profiles, and hardware telemetry to train surrogate models for rapid scenario testing, enabling predictive maintenance scheduling and adaptive power routing under uncertainty. Key innovations include a novel topology optimization algorithm for hybrid AC/DC microgrids and a digital twin platform capable of emulating grid-edge device behaviors at unprecedented scale. Anticipated outcomes include validated protocols for minimizing curtailment losses in renewables-rich networks, a benchmark dataset for decentralized energy system interoperability, and open-source tools to aid utilities in transitioning infrastructure toward modular, resilient architectures. This research directly addresses the computational bottleneck in designing next-generation energy systems, where traditional sequential optimization methods fail to capture emergent phenomena in distributed, nonlinear networks. Successful implementation will provide policymakers and grid operators with actionable insights for accelerating decarbonization while maintaining reliability in evolving energy ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of energy generation, storage, conversion, and distribution systems. Includes instruction in conventional and alternative/renewable energy systems, electrical power systems, and electrical system design.

abstract: Pediatric critical care involves complex, dynamic decision-making to manage life-threatening organ failure and support vital physiological functions in children. Current approaches to predicting clinical deterioration or optimizing treatment strategies often rely on static models that inadequately capture the interdependencies between organ systems, evolving patient trajectories, and heterogeneous responses to therapies. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating multi-organ physiological modeling, high-resolution clinical data, and machine learning to address these limitations. The primary research problem centers on improving real-time predictive capabilities for critically ill children by characterizing nonlinear interactions between cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, and neurological systems during acute crises. We will leverage a de-identified dataset encompassing 12,000+ pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, including high-frequency vital sign streams, electronic health record data, and multimodal biomarker measurements. Computational challenges include processing temporal data at multiple scales (seconds to days), managing sparse clinical observations, and simulating coupled physiological systems. The project requires high-performance computing resources for three core tasks: 1) Parallelized training of ensemble neural networks to predict hemodynamic instability from multivariate time-series data 2) Multi-scale agent-based modeling of systemic inflammatory responses interacting with organ function 3) Bayesian optimization of simulated treatment protocols across diverse virtual patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for clinical deterioration, mechanistic insights into cross-organ failure pathways in sepsis and trauma, and computational tools for personalized resuscitation strategy testing. This work will establish a platform for in silico clinical trials to evaluate life support interventions while addressing ethical and practical barriers to experimental studies in critically ill children. The requested computing resources are essential given the need for massive parameter space exploration in physiological models, iterative refinement of deep learning architectures, and probabilistic integration of heterogeneous clinical data streams at scale. Successful implementation could transform precision monitoring and decision support in PICUs worldwide.
cip_definition: Research focused on advanced life support for children, from the term or near-term neonate to the adolescent. This includes critical care management of life-threatening organ system failure in both medical and surgical patients and support of vital physiological functions.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical operational and decision-making challenges in correctional facility management through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Correctional systems face complex, dynamic problems, including overcrowding, resource allocation inefficiencies, and risk prediction for inmate behavior, yet traditional analytical tools often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between institutional policies, environmental factors, and human dynamics. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution agent-based simulation framework to model facility operations, inmate population dynamics, and staff-inmate interactions. The framework will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including historical incident reports, staffing patterns, and facility infrastructure metrics—to simulate scenarios such as contagion spread during health crises, resource strain during intake surges, and the cascading effects of policy changes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps, optimize hyperparameters for machine learning components embedded in agent decision trees, and validate models against real-world operational data. Computational outcomes will be paired with interpretability algorithms to identify leverage points for improving safety, reducing costs, and mitigating systemic risks. Expected deliverables include an open-source simulation toolkit tailored for corrections administrators, predictive models for incident hot-spot mapping, and evidence-based recommendations for adaptive staffing protocols. By bridging computational social science, operations research, and correctional theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven corrections management while adhering to ethical guidelines for algorithmic transparency and bias mitigation. The project’s computational demands—particularly its need for parallelized simulations across thousands of agents and multi-year temporal horizons—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve practical scalability and real-world relevance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study the theories and principles, of correctional science and to function as professional corrections officers and other workers in public and/or private incarceration facilities.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face increasing pressure to optimize crop yields and resilience amid climate variability and resource constraints. Traditional approaches to crop improvement and management often rely on field trials that are time-intensive, spatially limited, and unable to fully account for complex genotype-environment-management (G×E×M) interactions. This project proposes to address these challenges by developing a high-throughput computational framework integrating genomic, phenomic, and environmental data to predict optimal crop varieties and management practices for diverse agricultural landscapes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct machine learning models trained on multi-year datasets encompassing crop genotype information, hyperspectral imagery, soil chemistry profiles, and micrometeorological records. These models will simulate crop growth dynamics under varying climate scenarios and input regimes, enabling genome-to-phenome predictions at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Key computational tasks include parallelized processing of terabyte-scale remote sensing data, Bayesian optimization of management parameters, and ensemble modeling of genotype performance across heterogeneous environments. The project will focus on staple crops critical to regional food security, with validation through targeted field experiments. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide precision breeding programs, site-specific management recommendations to reduce input waste, and risk-assessment frameworks for climate adaptation planning. By elucidating complex G×E×M relationships at scale, this research aims to accelerate the development of climate-resilient agricultural systems while maintaining computational reproducibility through containerized workflows. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive genomic analyses, iterative model training across parameter spaces, and large-scale spatial simulations that cannot feasibly run on local infrastructure.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural production operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) represent critical challenges in hepatology, with disease mechanisms influenced by complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, and microenvironmental factors. Current clinical strategies for risk stratification and therapeutic targeting remain inadequate due to limitations in modeling these multi-scale interactions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative computational models that bridge genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial proteomic data from patient cohorts, thereby identifying novel drivers of disease progression and treatment resistance. A key focus is the creation of a multi-omics pipeline to analyze bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from 500+ patients with NAFLD-associated HCC, integrated with clinical outcomes and histopathology imaging. Machine learning approaches, including graph neural networks, will be applied to infer cell-cell communication networks within the tumor microenvironment and predict context-specific drug responses. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate the impact of metabolic stressors on hepatocyte-stellate cell crosstalk during fibrogenesis, parameterized by longitudinal metabolomic datasets. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration to manage datasets exceeding 100 TB and to execute millions of stochastic simulations for robustness testing. Expected outcomes include the identification of combinatorial biomarkers for early HCC detection, predictive models of therapeutic resistance, and candidate targets for disrupting pro-fibrotic signaling. By elucidating mechanisms linking NAFLD progression to HCC, this work aims to advance precision hepatology tools for risk prediction and tailored interventions. The requested HPC allocation will enable scaling of analyses to population-level biobanks and foster the development of open-source tools for liver disease research, directly addressing unmet clinical needs in hepatology.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hepatology

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize emergency medical service (EMS) decision-making in pre-hospital care scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in real-time patient prioritization, ambulance routing, and resource allocation. Emergency care attendants (ECAs) operate in highly dynamic environments where rapid decisions impact patient survival and outcomes. However, current protocols for triage, route planning, and equipment deployment often rely on static guidelines that do not account for real-time variables such as traffic patterns, fluctuating resource availability, or concurrent multi-patient emergencies. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven simulation platform integrating geospatial data, historical EMS call records, and machine learning models to generate adaptive decision-support tools. The computational approach will involve agent-based modeling to simulate urban emergency scenarios, Monte Carlo methods to evaluate probabilistic outcomes, and reinforcement learning to iteratively refine response strategies under constraints. HPC resources are essential to process large-scale datasets (e.g., city-wide traffic feeds, electronic patient care records) and execute parallelized simulations that capture the complexity of real-world emergencies. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimal ambulance dispatch routing, dynamic triage protocols tailored to evolving incident severity, and evidence-based recommendations for allocating on-board medical equipment. By quantifying the impact of computational optimization on response times and patient outcomes, this research aims to directly enhance ECA training curricula and operational standards. The project will provide open-access tools to EMS agencies, fostering scalable improvements in pre-hospital care efficiency and equity, particularly in underserved regions with limited emergency infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist licensed EMTs, under the supervision of a physician, to prepare and transport ill or injured patients, and to operate emergency vehicles and equipment such as life support units. Includes instruction in first aid and emergency medicine field techniques, patient stabilization and care, medical field communications, equipment operation and maintenance, emergency vehicle operation, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT) is a cornerstone of osteopathic medicine, yet its biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely characterized, limiting evidence-based optimization of clinical protocols. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets and simulate OMT’s effects on neuromusculoskeletal systems. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the integration of high-resolution imaging, motion-capture biomechanics, electrophysiological signals, and patient-reported outcomes—key to modeling the complex, dynamic interactions underlying OMT efficacy. We propose a computational framework combining finite element modeling (FEM), machine learning (ML), and network analysis to quantify how OMT-induced mechanical forces propagate through tissue structures, modulate neural signaling, and correlate with clinical outcomes. FEM will simulate real-time tissue deformation and stress distribution during OMT maneuvers, informed by 3D musculoskeletal anatomy derived from patient-specific MRI/CT data. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify predictive patterns in heterogeneous clinical datasets (n=850 retrospective cases; prospective n=120), including electromyography, gait analysis, and inflammatory biomarkers. Graph-based network models will map functional connectivity shifts in sensorimotor and autonomic pathways post-OMT. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses: biomechanical simulations require parallelized solvers for ultra-high-resolution meshes (>10^6 elements), while ML workflows demand GPU acceleration to train deep neural networks on terabyte-scale multimodal data. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into OMT’s impact on proprioceptive feedback loops, validated predictive models for treatment personalization, and open-source computational tools for the osteopathic research community. By bridging clinical observations with multiscale computational modeling, this work aims to establish a robust framework for advancing OMT research, ultimately enhancing therapeutic precision in neuromusculoskeletal care.
cip_definition: Research focused on osteopathic neuromusculoskeletal diagnosis and Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT).

abstract: The biological effects of ionizing radiation are mediated through complex interactions between physical energy deposition, molecular damage, and cellular repair processes. A critical unresolved challenge in radiobiology is the mechanistic understanding of how radiation-induced DNA damage—particularly clustered lesions and cross-linked macromolecular complexes—evades canonical repair pathways, leading to persistent genomic instability. Current experimental methods lack the spatiotemporal resolution to characterize these highly localized, multi-scale processes. This project proposes an integrative computational framework combining atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) modeling, and kinetic network analyses to map the structural and energetic determinants of irreparable DNA-protein cross-link (DPC) formation following irradiation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate radiation-induced radical cascades in explicit solvent environments, model DPC dynamics at microsecond timescales, and screen repair enzyme binding affinities across conformational ensembles. Initial benchmarks using GPU-accelerated AMBER simulations have quantified lesion-dependent distortions in DNA topology, but scaling to biologically representative systems (e.g., chromatin fibers with histones) requires parallelized workflows across multi-node architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of lesion recognition by base excision repair (BER) proteins, (2) free energy landscapes for DPC resolvase activity, and (3) a biophysical database linking radiation quality (LET, particle type) to repair pathway efficiency. These results will advance targeted radiotherapy approaches by identifying molecular signatures of radiation sensitivity and inform next-gen radioprotectant design. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster with GPU support will enable statistically robust sampling across radiation scenarios, directly addressing a critical bottleneck in translating physical dosimetry to biological effect prediction.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the effects of radiation on organisms and biological systems. Includes instruction in particle physics, ionization, and biophysics of radiation perturbations, cellular and organismic repair systems, genetic and pathological effects of radiation, and the measurement of radiation dosages.

abstract: Environmental health research faces growing challenges in assessing the complex interactions between environmental contaminants, exposure pathways, and population-level health outcomes. Traditional risk assessment models often lack the resolution to account for dynamic environmental variables, heterogeneous exposure patterns, and multi-scale biological responses. This project seeks to advance environmental health risk prediction by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating geospatial exposure modeling, toxicokinetic/toxicodynamic simulations, and machine learning-driven epidemiological analysis. The research will focus on two priority areas: (1) modeling airborne particulate matter (PM2.5) and industrial chemical dispersion patterns in urban environments using coupled atmospheric transport and fluid dynamics simulations, and (2) predicting dose-response relationships for emerging contaminants through parallelized toxicological simulations across diverse demographic cohorts. Computational workflows will process multi-source data including satellite imagery, environmental sensor networks, electronic health records, and biomonitoring datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable spatial-temporal modeling at meter-scale resolution across metropolitan regions, coupled with population pharmacokinetic simulations at individual and community levels. Expected outcomes include novel exposure-risk matrices for environmental policy development, identification of high-risk exposure corridors, and predictive models for chemical prioritization under climate change scenarios. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this work will overcome current limitations in processing latency and model granularity that hinder real-time risk assessment capabilities. The resource allocation will directly support public health objectives in environmental emergency response, regulatory decision-making, and targeted intervention strategies for vulnerable populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of environmental sciences, public health, the biomedical sciences, and environmental toxicology to the study of environmental factors affecting human health, safety, and related ecological issues, and prepares individuals to function as professional environmental health specialists. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, toxicology, public policy analysis, public management, risk assessment, communications, environmental law, occupational health and safety emergency response, and applications such as air quality, food protection, radiation protection, solid and hazardous waste management, water quality, soil quality, noise abatement, housing quality, and environmental control of recreational areas.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are critical for biodiversity conservation and carbon sequestration, yet their resilience is increasingly threatened by climate change and anthropogenic disturbances. Current predictive models often lack the spatial resolution and computational complexity needed to integrate multi-scale environmental data, limiting actionable insights for adaptive management. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-resolution, mechanistic model to simulate forest ecosystem dynamics under varying climate scenarios and land-use patterns. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of LiDAR-derived canopy structure data, satellite-based phenology records, and spatially explicit climate projections. Computational workflows will employ parallelized agent-based modeling to simulate tree species interactions, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict shifts in habitat suitability for keystone species. Sensitivity analyses will quantify uncertainties in climate drivers and disturbance regimes, while GPU-accelerated raster operations will enable fine-scale (10m²) mapping of carbon stocks and biodiversity hotspots across regional landscapes. The outcomes will advance understanding of threshold behaviors in forest ecosystems, such as tipping points in species composition under drought stress, and inform prioritization of conservation corridors. By integrating heterogeneous datasets at unprecedented scales, this work will generate open-access tools for simulating forest resilience, supporting stakeholders in aligning reforestation efforts with climate adaptation goals. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive processing of 3D forest structure data and reduce runtime for ensemble simulations, which are computationally prohibitive on local clusters. This project bridges ecological theory and computational innovation, providing a framework to optimize forest management in the face of rapid environmental change.
cip_definition: Any program in forestry, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between urban spatial configurations and emergent pedestrian movement patterns to model how micro-scale human behaviors influence macro-scale accessibility and equity in cities. While urban mobility is often studied through transportation networks or economic frameworks, this research adopts a novel computational social science lens, focusing on pedestrian decision-making as a driver of spatial segregation, resource access, and neighborhood vitality. The core challenge lies in simulating millions of individual agents with heterogeneous preferences (e.g., safety, convenience, social ties) across high-resolution urban environments while capturing feedback loops between mobility choices and evolving neighborhood conditions. We propose an adaptive agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrating real-time geospatial data streams (street-view imagery, pedestrian sensors, crowdsourced place perceptions) with machine learning to calibrate agent behavior rules. High-performance computing resources are essential to parallelize simulations across 20+ urban case studies, each requiring 10^5-10^6 agents interacting over dynamic graph representations of street networks and land use. The computational workflow leverages GPU-accelerated spatial kernels for pathfinding and graph updates, paired with Bayesian optimization to iteratively refine parameters against ground-truth mobility datasets. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) identification of critical inflection points where pedestrian behavior amplifies or mitigates spatial inequalities, (2) a scalable urban simulation toolkit for testing equity-focused interventions (e.g., pedestrian infrastructure investments), and (3) synthetic population mobility datasets to support policymaking in underserved cities lacking traditional survey infrastructure. By bridging computational scalability with behavioral realism, this work advances methodological frontiers in urban social science while providing actionable insights for designing cities that prioritize human-centered accessibility over purely efficiency-driven models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of social science principles to the study of urban institutions and the forces influencing urban social and political life. Includes instruction in urban theory, the development and evolution of urban areas, urban sociology, principles of urban and social planning, and the politics and economics of urban government and services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational literary analysis within the field of creative writing, specifically exploring how large-scale textual datasets and machine learning can illuminate patterns in narrative construction, stylistic innovation, and genre evolution. While traditional literary scholarship often focuses on close reading of individual texts, this study proposes a macroanalytic approach to interrogate how linguistic and structural features correlate with reader engagement, aesthetic impact, and market success across diverse literary corpora. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models and semantic network analysis, we will process and analyze over 100,000 contemporary short stories, novels, and poetry collections from both published and peer-reviewed unpublished works. The computational pipeline will identify latent patterns in syntax, metaphor density, narrative pacing, and character interaction, while reinforcement learning models will simulate reader responses to stylistic variations. A key innovation involves training genre-specific generative models to probabilistically map "narrative pathways," enabling systematic testing of how compositional choices affect textual outcomes. This work addresses critical gaps in empirically grounded creative writing pedagogy by generating actionable insights into craft techniques, while also developing open-source tools for writers to computationally analyze and iteratively refine their work. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing multi-terabyte text corpora, fine-tuning large language models, and running parallelized simulations of narrative decision trees. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of stylometric features linked to critical and commercial success metrics, as well as novel methodologies for bridging computational analysis with humanistic inquiry. By integrating HPC-driven research into creative writing practice, this project aims to foster data-informed approaches to literary craft while preserving the irreducible complexities of artistic expression.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process and techniques of original composition in various literary forms such as the short story, poetry, the novel, and others. Includes instruction in technical and editorial skills, criticism, and the marketing of finished manuscripts.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing sustainability and operational efficiency in large-scale resort ecosystems through advanced computational modeling. Resorts face increasing pressure to reduce environmental impact while maintaining profitability and guest satisfaction, yet existing decision-making frameworks often rely on static, siloed data that fails to account for dynamic interactions between energy systems, guest behavior, and environmental conditions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation platform that integrates real-time data streams from IoT sensors, weather forecasts, and guest activity patterns to model resort-wide resource flows. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate guest decision-making with Monte Carlo methods to assess uncertainty in energy demand and renewable generation. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical datasets to predict peak resource utilization, while multi-objective optimization techniques will balance trade-offs between carbon emissions, operational costs, and service quality. High-performance computing resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets from participating resorts, run parallelized simulations of alternative sustainability strategies, and optimize complex systems encompassing water treatment, waste management, and smart grid integration. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that enables resort operators to test circular economy interventions—such as adaptive pricing for off-peak renewable energy use or AI-driven waste sorting systems—before physical implementation. The project will generate novel insights into the scalability of green technologies in hospitality contexts, with particular significance for island resorts facing climate vulnerabilities. By creating a computational framework that quantifies both environmental and business impacts of sustainability initiatives, this research aims to establish new standards for data-driven resource allocation in the $300 billion global resort industry while advancing methodological integration of complex systems theory in hospitality analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market comprehensive vacation facilities and services and related products. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, hotel/motel management, restaurant and food services management, facilities planning, leisure studies, recreation administration, marketing, recreation equipment and grounds operations and maintenance, business finance, insurance and taxation, event management and guest services, personnel management, travel and logistics management, safety and health services, professional standards and ethics, and applications to specific vacation types and locations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to enhance the precision and scalability of 3D biomedical visualizations, addressing critical bottlenecks in processing complex anatomical datasets for medical education and clinical applications. Current methods for reconstructing high-fidelity anatomical models from medical imaging data (e.g., MRI, CT, histology) are limited by the computational demands of integrating multi-modal datasets, rendering dynamic physiological processes, and automating segmentation of intricate structures like neural pathways or vascular networks. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines for automated tissue segmentation, multi-scale biomechanical simulations, and real-time interactive visualization platforms. Key computational steps include training deep learning architectures (e.g., 3D U-Nets) on annotated clinical imaging datasets to improve segmentation accuracy, employing finite element analysis to simulate soft tissue mechanics in surgical scenarios, and optimizing ray-tracing algorithms for photorealistic rendering of microscopic anatomical features. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce model generation times from days to hours, and support collaborative visualization via cloud-based interfaces. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating patient-specific anatomical models with submillimeter accuracy, dynamic simulations of disease progression for educational modules, and interactive 3D atlases of embryological development. These resources will directly benefit medical illustrators, educators, and clinicians by providing tools to create more effective visual narratives of complex biomedical processes. The project will also establish benchmarks for computational efficiency in medical visualization workflows, bridging gaps between data-rich biomedical research and accessible visual communication. By integrating HPC capabilities with medical illustration principles, this work aims to advance the reproducibility and clinical relevance of biomedical visualizations while reducing development barriers for resource-intensive projects in the health professions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles and techniques of art and computer-assisted imaging, graphics, and animation to create visual materials to facilitate the recording and dissemination of biomedical knowledge for educational, research, and clinical purposes. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, histology, embryology, neuroanatomy, medical terminology, artistic media and techniques, illustration techniques, three-dimensional modeling, prosthetics, data display design, exhibit design and production, medical photography, multimedia, computer graphics and animation, digital imaging, business management, production technology, and instructional design.

abstract: Public policy interventions increasingly target complex, interconnected systems where outcomes depend on dynamic interactions between institutional actors, infrastructure, and populations. However, existing analytical tools often fail to capture the emergent behaviors and nonlinear feedback loops inherent in these systems, leading to suboptimal or unintended policy consequences. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational model to simulate the impacts of multi-sector policy interventions in urban environments, with a focus on public health service accessibility and infrastructure resilience. The research problem centers on identifying leverage points for policy efficacy under conditions of resource scarcity and demographic heterogeneity. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with network analysis to represent decision-making processes at individual, organizational, and municipal levels. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the model’s scale, which simulates over 10 million agent interactions across layered spatial and temporal domains while incorporating real-world datasets on service utilization, mobility patterns, and infrastructure capacity. Parallelized simulations will test policy scenarios varying funding allocation rules, interagency coordination protocols, and crisis response timelines. Sensitivity analyses will quantify robustness to demographic and environmental uncertainties. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for evaluating trade-offs between equity, efficiency, and sustainability in policy design, (2) actionable insights into optimal resource allocation strategies for concurrent public health and infrastructure challenges, and (3) open-source tools enabling policymakers to visualize cascading impacts of interventions. By advancing computational methods tailored to policy analysis, this work aims to establish reproducible practices for evidence-based decision-making in complex governance contexts, directly addressing the program’s focus on innovative approaches to public policy challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public policy analysis, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Home health aides (HHAs) face complex challenges in managing dynamic, real-time risks for homebound patients, including falls, medication errors, and environmental hazards. Current protocols rely on static checklists and retrospective reporting, which lack predictive capacity to avert adverse events. This project proposes the development of an adaptive risk-prediction framework using multimodal data integration and machine learning to empower HHAs with proactive decision-support tools. Leveraging anonymized datasets from wearable sensors (accelerometry, heart rate variability), environmental IoT devices (room temperature, motion patterns), and electronic care logs from 12,000+ home care episodes, we will train temporal graph neural networks to model interdependencies between caregiver actions, patient biometrics, and environmental states. Computational challenges include handling irregularly sampled time series from heterogeneous devices, imbalanced event classes, and privacy-preserving federated learning across decentralized care agencies. High-performance computing resources are required for hyperparameter optimization of attention-based architectures, simulation of intervention scenarios through digital twin modeling, and real-time inference testing via edge computing benchmarks. Anticipated outcomes include: 1) A validated ensemble model predicting 85%+ of preventable adverse events in cross-validation testing, 2) An open-source toolkit for adaptive retraining on limited HHA-reported data, and 3) Prototype dashboards optimizing task prioritization based on evolving risk profiles. This computational infrastructure will establish a novel paradigm for precision home care, bridging gaps between biomedical informatics, human-computer interaction, and operational research in community health settings. Successful implementation could reduce emergency hospital transfers by an estimated 22% in pilot populations while providing foundational architecture for AI-assisted home care ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and support services for homebound disabled, recovering, or elderly people. Includes instruction in basic nutrition, home sanitation, infection control, first aid, taking vital signs, personal hygiene, interpersonal communication skills, supervised home management, emergency recognition and referral, geriatric care, and legal and ethical responsibilities.

abstract: The global apparel industry faces mounting challenges in balancing aesthetic innovation with environmental sustainability, particularly regarding textile waste generated by fast fashion cycles. Current approaches to sustainable design often lack the computational tools necessary to model complex interactions between consumer behavior, material innovation, and supply chain logistics. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate and optimize textile reuse pathways, integrating spatially explicit consumer disposal patterns, material degradation dynamics, and regional recycling infrastructure constraints. By leveraging agent-based modeling and generative adversarial networks (GANs), the research will simulate how localized design interventions—such as modular garment architectures or region-specific fiber blends—could reduce landfill deposition while maintaining commercial viability. The computational workflow will process multi-source datasets, including geospatial disposal metrics, textile physicochemical properties, and consumer preference surveys, to generate probabilistic maps of waste diversion outcomes under varying design and policy scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for designers and policymakers to visualize the lifecycle impacts of textile choices, as well as a ranked portfolio of design strategies optimized for scalability across socioeconomic contexts. This work bridges gaps between computational social science, environmental systems analysis, and apparel design—a niche not adequately addressed by traditional engineering or policy-focused sustainability research. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of globalized textile flows and enabling real-time interactive simulations that inform both creative practice and circular economy infrastructure planning.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in apparel and textiles, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the safety, efficacy, and innovation of nail care practices through computational modeling and data-driven analysis.
