While nail technology is traditionally a hands-on field, emerging challenges—such as optimizing sterilization protocols, predicting allergenicity of novel cosmetic formulations, and modeling the biomechanical interactions between nail products and natural nail structures—require sophisticated computational approaches. Current training and practice rely heavily on empirical knowledge, with limited tools to systematically evaluate risks or design evidence-based solutions. This research addresses gaps in understanding microbial persistence under salon conditions, chemical stability of hybrid gel polishes, and stress distribution in artificial nail extensions. Computational methods will include finite element analysis to simulate mechanical forces on nail architectures, molecular dynamics to study polymer-curing processes, and machine learning models trained on microbial genomic data to predict pathogen survival post-sterilization. Additionally, agent-based models will evaluate contamination risks in salon workflows. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to generate actionable insights for improving sanitization standards, reducing occupational hazards, and guiding product development. Outcomes will include open-access datasets on material properties and microbial thresholds, predictive tools for allergy risk assessment, and simulation frameworks for training nail technicians in virtual environments. This work bridges the technical-artisanal divide, positioning computational research as a transformative force in a field where empirical tradition and modern scientific rigor intersect.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shape fingernails and toenails, remove unwanted skin and blemishes, apply polish and cosmetics to nails, and function as licensed manicurists or nail technicians/specialists.  Includes instruction in manicuring theory; skin anatomy; nail growth, irregularities, and diseases; sterilization and sanitation; equipment and table maintenance; cuticle, blemish, and rough skin removal; nail filing, shaping, and polishing; cream application and extremity massage; nail sculpture and design art; product storage and use; customer service; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing personalized rehabilitation protocols in patients with neuromotor impairments resulting from stroke or traumatic brain injury. Current rehabilitation strategies often rely on generalized guidelines, leading to variable patient outcomes due to heterogeneous pathophysiology, individual biomechanical constraints, and dynamic neuroplastic responses. The research addresses this gap by integrating multimodal data—including high-resolution motion capture, electromyography, and real-time neuroimaging—to model patient-specific motor recovery trajectories. A key challenge lies in processing and analyzing these large, temporally dense datasets to identify individualized intervention parameters. The computational approach combines biomechanical simulations, Bayesian optimization, and reinforcement learning to iteratively adapt therapeutic regimens based on evolving patient performance and physiological feedback. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses, enabling parallel execution of computationally intensive tasks such as finite element modeling of musculoskeletal stress, stochastic optimization of intervention sequences, and ensemble forecasting of long-term recovery outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for adaptive rehabilitation planning, validated against clinical data from a cohort of 120 patients undergoing upper-limb therapy. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and clinical practice, offering a paradigm shift from static to dynamic, data-driven rehabilitation protocols. Success would provide allied health professionals with actionable tools to personalize interventions in real time, potentially accelerating functional recovery, reducing secondary complications, and lowering healthcare costs. The project further contributes methodological advances in interpretable machine learning for time-series health data, with applications extending to other neuromotor disorders and sensorimotor rehabilitation domains.
cip_title: Allied Health Diagnostic, Intervention, and Treatment Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health diagnostic, intervention, and treatment professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of histologic data, driven by high-resolution digital microscopy and multiplex staining techniques, presents significant challenges in efficiently analyzing tissue samples for diagnostic and research purposes. Current manual and semi-automated methods for quantifying histologic features—such as cellular morphology, staining intensity, and spatial relationships—are time-intensive, prone to variability, and ill-suited for large-scale datasets. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing an open-source computational pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to automate the analysis of histologic images. Using a repository of digitized tissue samples from clinical partnerships, we will train deep learning models to segment tissue structures, classify staining patterns, and quantify biomarkers across diverse specimen types. The computational workflow will integrate convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image feature extraction, graph-based algorithms for analyzing cellular networks, and statistical frameworks to correlate histologic patterns with clinical metadata. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of whole-slide images, optimizing hyperparameters for model generalizability across tissue fixation and staining protocols, and enabling rapid iteration of ensemble learning approaches. Expected outcomes include a scalable, containerized toolset validated against gold-standard manual annotations, with performance benchmarks targeting >95% accuracy in routine diagnostic tasks (e.g., tumor margin identification). The pipeline will be designed for integration with clinical laboratory information systems, reducing turnaround times for complex cases. By democratizing access to advanced computational histology, this work aims to enhance the precision of tissue-based diagnostics, support technician training through AI-assisted quality control modules, and establish a framework for collaborative reproducibility studies across histopathology laboratories. Results and tools will be disseminated through academic pathology networks and integrated into competency-based curricula for histotechnician trainees.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance developmental education pedagogy by modeling the efficacy of adaptive instructional strategies for underprepared college learners. Despite decades of research, persistent equity gaps in postsecondary outcomes highlight the need for scalable, data-driven approaches to personalize academic support. Current studies often rely on small-scale qualitative analyses or linear statistical models, limiting insights into complex interactions between pedagogical interventions, student behaviors, and institutional contexts. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating virtual classrooms of 10,000+ heterogeneous learners, parameterized using anonymized institutional data on demographics, prior academic performance, and engagement patterns. The ABM will test hypotheses about how combinations of andragogical strategies—such as flipped classrooms, metacognitive scaffolding, and real-time formative feedback—affect emergent outcomes like course completion rates and critical thinking skill development. Machine learning pipelines will analyze multimodal data (discussion forum text, syllabus designs, LMS interaction logs) to identify predictive features of successful interventions. HPC resources are critical for running computationally intensive parameter sweeps across diverse virtual cohorts and optimizing neural networks for natural language processing of open-response assessments. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation framework for prototyping developmental education strategies, evidence-based design principles for hybrid learning environments, and predictive tools to flag at-risk students earlier in the term. By quantifying how non-linear interactions between instructional practices and learner traits influence outcomes, this work aims to equip educators with actionable models for reducing systemic barriers in postsecondary access.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach educational strategies for assisting students who are perceived as underprepared for the academic rigor of college-level coursework at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing supply chain resilience and resource allocation under dynamic disruptions, such as those caused by geopolitical shifts, climate events, or demand volatility. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the complexity of modern global supply networks, which involve multi-echelon inventory systems, interdependent transportation routes, and stochastic supplier reliability. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and multi-objective optimization. The computational model will simulate large-scale supply chain networks with thousands of nodes, incorporating real-world data on lead times, carbon emissions, inventory costs, and supplier risk profiles. Machine learning algorithms will predict disruption probabilities and supplier performance, while parallelized optimization routines will dynamically allocate resources to minimize costs, reduce waste, and maintain service levels. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing petabytes of historical transaction data, running Monte Carlo simulations to stress-test scenarios, and solving non-linear budgetary constraints across decentralized decision-making units. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for evaluating trade-offs between just-in-time efficiency and redundancy buffers, identifying optimal contingency sourcing strategies, and quantifying the financial impact of sustainability initiatives. This research will provide actionable insights for enterprises navigating volatile markets while advancing computational methodologies in logistics management. Results will be validated through partnerships with automotive and pharmaceutical industries, where supply chain agility directly impacts operational viability. The project aligns with the program’s focus on integrating technological innovation with strategic resource allocation, offering a paradigm shift in adaptive supply chain design.
cip_title: Logistics, Materials, and Supply Chain Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and coordinate all logistical functions in an enterprise, ranging from acquisitions to receiving and handling, through internal allocation of resources to operations units, to the handling and delivery of output. Includes instruction in acquisitions and purchasing, inventory control, storage and handling, just-in-time manufacturing, logistics planning, shipping and delivery management, transportation, quality control, resource estimation and allocation, and budgeting.

abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of histopathological data in clinical diagnostics present challenges in timely and accurate disease characterization. Manual analysis of whole-slide images (WSIs) remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability, particularly in rare or morphologically ambiguous pathologies. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging deep learning to enhance diagnostic precision and efficiency in surgical pathology workflows. We propose to train multimodal neural networks integrating WSIs with associated clinical metadata and molecular profiles to predict histological subtypes, prognostic markers, and therapeutic responses. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing high-resolution slide scans (up to 100,000x100,000 pixels per image), implementing attention-based architectures for feature extraction, and developing uncertainty quantification metrics to flag cases requiring expert review. High-performance computing resources are essential for distributed training across multiple GPU nodes, hyperparameter optimization through large-scale grid searches, and validation against multi-institutional datasets comprising over 50,000 annotated cases. Expected outcomes include validated diagnostic decision-support tools that maintain pathologist-level accuracy while reducing analysis time by 40-60%, as well as novel feature discovery through gradient-based interpretability methods. The developed models will be deployed as modular components within existing laboratory information systems, directly supporting pathology assistants in specimen prioritization, quality control, and preliminary report generation. This research aligns with emerging needs in precision pathology by creating scalable computational infrastructure to handle next-generation diagnostic data streams while preserving clinician-in-the-loop verification processes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of fire evacuation dynamics in complex urban high-rise environments, with a focus on integrating human behavioral data, real-time hazard propagation, and architectural variability. Current evacuation models often rely on oversimplified assumptions about occupant decision-making, static building layouts, and uniform fire-spread patterns, limiting their utility in designing adaptive safety protocols for modern structures. The research problem centers on addressing these gaps by developing a scalable, agent-based simulation framework that captures heterogeneous occupant behaviors (e.g., mobility constraints, group dynamics, stress responses), coupled with dynamic fire and smoke propagation models informed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The computational approach will involve parallelized simulations using modified versions of the FDS (Fire Dynamics Simulator) and social force models, optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters to handle the high-dimensional parameter space of multi-story buildings with diverse occupancy profiles. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate behavioral parameters against empirical data from evacuation drills and post-incident reports. Key outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for scenario testing, validated against historical high-rise fire case studies, and probabilistic risk assessments quantifying the impact of design variables (e.g., stairwell placement, signage visibility) on evacuation efficiency. The project’s significance lies in its potential to inform next-generation fire safety standards, particularly for aging infrastructure retrofits and smart building systems integrating IoT-based emergency guidance. By bridging fire science, behavioral psychology, and computational engineering within a non-traditional safety technology context, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven, occupant-centric fire prevention strategies that transcend conventional prescriptive codes.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science and technology to problems of reducing fire risk, limiting loss, supervising substance removal, conducting safety inspections and investigations, and advising on matters of safety procedures and fire prevention policy. Includes instruction in fire behavior, fire simulation, structural risk assessment, materials analysis, detection and suppression systems, smoke management, supply and evacuation, public education, legal aspects of fire prevention, and related research and communications methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in women’s health by investigating the molecular and clinical heterogeneity of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a complex endocrine disorder affecting 10% of reproductive-aged women globally. Despite its prevalence, PCOS remains poorly understood, with heterogeneous presentation, unclear etiology, and limited targeted therapies. The research problem centers on integrating multi-omic datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic) with longitudinal clinical data to identify subtype-specific biomarkers and mechanistic drivers of PCOS. This requires large-scale computational workflows to harmonize heterogeneous data from 5,000+ participants across international cohorts, perform dimensionality reduction, and apply unsupervised machine learning for patient stratification. HPC resources are critical to support parallelized processing of whole-genome sequencing data, GPU-accelerated deep learning for feature extraction from electronic health records, and dynamic network modeling of endocrine-metabolic pathways. The computational pipeline will integrate Python-based tools (e.g., PyTorch, Scanpy) with R packages for multivariate survival analysis, enabling discovery of genetic variants, gene co-expression modules, and metabolic signatures predictive of PCOS progression and treatment response. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated classification framework for PCOS subtypes, (2) mechanistic insights into ovarian follicle dysregulation and insulin resistance, and (3) open-source software for reproducible analysis of women’s health multi-omics data. By elucidating molecular drivers of PCOS heterogeneity, this work aims to inform targeted interventions, reduce diagnostic delays, and address critical gaps in clinical management for a understudied condition disproportionately impacting women’s lifelong health. The scale of data integration and computational demands necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve statistically robust, translatable findings within project timelines.
cip_definition: Research focused on Women's Health

abstract: Health system pharmacy administration faces challenges in optimizing medication therapy management across diverse patient populations, particularly in balancing efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness. Current approaches often rely on retrospective analyses or simplified models that inadequately capture the complexity of real-world clinical, genomic, and operational data. This project proposes the development of a predictive computational framework to model patient-specific therapeutic outcomes and system-wide resource allocation strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-source data—including electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacogenomic profiles, drug utilization patterns, and institutional workflow logs—to train ensemble machine learning models. These models will predict individual patient responses to therapies while accounting for variables such as polypharmacy risks, drug-drug interactions, and institutional formulary constraints. A parallel computational workflow will simulate large-scale intervention scenarios, employing agent-based modeling to evaluate the impact of proposed policy changes on medication safety, staffing efficiency, and supply chain dynamics. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters for high-dimensional models, and running stochastic simulations necessitate distributed computing architectures and GPU-accelerated processing. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for personalized dosing protocols, risk stratification tools for adverse drug events, and data-driven recommendations for formulary management. By enabling real-time analysis of complex, heterogeneous datasets, this project aims to advance precision pharmacy practices, reduce preventable medication-related hospitalizations, and improve operational decision-making in health systems. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will provide a scalable template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into pharmacy administration research and practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on Health System Pharmacy Administration

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize construction site management by integrating high-performance computing (HPC) with dynamic risk prediction and resource allocation models. Construction projects are inherently complex, involving interdependent variables such as labor productivity, equipment availability, material logistics, and environmental factors, which traditional static scheduling tools often fail to adapt to in real time. This research addresses the critical challenge of minimizing delays, rework, and safety incidents through predictive analytics and scenario-based simulations. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES) to create a hybrid digital twin of construction sites, capable of ingesting real-time data from IoT sensors, weather APIs, and workforce tracking systems. Machine learning models, trained on historical accident reports and project timelines, will identify risk patterns and predict bottlenecks or safety hazards. HPC resources are essential to parallelize simulations across thousands of scenarios, enabling rapid evaluation of mitigation strategies, such as reallocating labor or adjusting equipment schedules under constraints like diversity training compliance or union regulations. The expected outcomes include an open-source tool that provides site managers with actionable recommendations for resource distribution, contingency planning, and accident prevention. By quantifying the impact of variables like crew diversity, communication protocols, and subcontractor coordination on project efficiency, this research aims to reduce average project overruns by 15–20% and lower incident rates through proactive risk management. The results will advance the integration of computational decision-support systems in construction education and practice, aligning with industry demands for data-driven, adaptive management strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise, manage, and inspect construction sites, buildings, and associated facilities. Includes instruction in site safety, personnel supervision, labor relations, diversity training, construction documentation, scheduling, resource and cost control, bid strategies, rework prevention, construction insurance and bonding, accident management and investigation, applicable law and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of legal reasoning in transnational human rights jurisprudence, with a focus on identifying latent patterns in judicial decision-making that reflect shifting sociopolitical values. While legal scholarship traditionally relies on qualitative case analysis, this study adopts an interdisciplinary computational approach, integrating natural language processing (NLP), temporal network analysis, and agent-based modeling to quantify how precedents interact across jurisdictions and time. The core research problem centers on the lack of scalable frameworks for tracing the diffusion of normative principles—such as proportionality or dignity—through millions of pages of case law from supranational courts (e.g., ECtHR, IACtHR) and domestic systems. By training transformer-based models on a curated multilingual corpus of legal texts (1945–present), we aim to reconstruct conceptual networks that map the transmission and adaptation of legal arguments. Computational challenges include managing semantic ambiguity in cross-linguistic legal terminology, handling sparse data from understudied jurisdictions, and simulating feedback loops between judicial decisions and public sentiment. The HPC environment is critical for running large-scale parallelized simulations of precedent cascades and optimizing dynamic topic models that account for temporal drift in legal concepts. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel taxonomy of legal argument migration pathways, 2) predictive insights into how emerging technologies (e.g., AI governance claims) are reshaping rights frameworks, and 3) open-access tools for visualizing citation dynamics in legal ecosystems. This work bridges computational social science and doctrinal analysis, offering a replicable methodology for studying law as a complex adaptive system while informing strategic litigation efforts and judicial training programs.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on law and legal issues from the perspective of the social sciences and humanities.

abstract: Hearing loss rehabilitation through hearing aids requires precise alignment between device parameters and individual neurophysiological profiles, yet current fitting protocols rely on generalized thresholds that fail to account for the dynamic interplay of cochlear mechanics, neural plasticity, and real-world auditory environments. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating biophysical cochlear modeling, machine learning–driven signal processing, and individualized neural adaptation simulations to optimize hearing aid personalization. The research will address two interconnected challenges: (1) modeling nonlinear cochlear responses to amplified speech signals under varying degrees of hair cell degeneration and synaptic loss, and (2) predicting long-term cortical reorganization patterns resulting from altered auditory input. High-performance computing resources will enable large-scale finite element simulations of basilar membrane mechanics across 10,000+ anatomically variable cochlear geometries, coupled with deep neural networks trained on electroencephalographic (EEG) data from hearing aid users. Multiphysics simulations will resolve wave propagation in three-dimensional cochlear models with patient-specific tonotopic damage profiles, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively adjust gain-frequency responses to maximize speech intelligibility metrics derived from cortical auditory evoked potentials. The computational pipeline will incorporate real-world noise environments through generative adversarial networks trained on binaural acoustic datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for hearing aid parameter optimization, an open-source toolbox for simulating neuro-auditory adaptation, and quantitative biomarkers linking cochleosynaptic health to optimal device configurations. This work bridges gaps between auditory neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and computational linguistics, offering a paradigm shift from threshold-based fittings to dynamic, physiology-guided hearing rehabilitation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to test the hearing of, and to select, fit and dispense appropriate hearing aids for, patients. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of the ear, hearing testing, hearing aid fitting and technology, health promotion and rehabilitation, counseling and communication, business management, and professional ethics.

abstract: The increasing stringency of vehicle emissions regulations necessitates advanced diagnostic and predictive tools to ensure compliance while minimizing economic burdens on vehicle owners. Current inspection and maintenance (I/M) protocols rely heavily on static thresholds and periodic testing, which fail to account for dynamic driving conditions, evolving engine performance, and complex after-treatment system behaviors. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model real-world emission profiles, optimize I/M procedures, and predict system degradation in diverse vehicle fleets. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement large-scale simulations integrating engine performance data, exhaust after-treatment dynamics, and machine learning-driven anomaly detection. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will be coupled with chemical kinetic solvers to simulate particulate filter and catalytic converter efficiency under variable load cycles, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will analyze onboard diagnostic (OBD) telemetry streams to identify pre-failure conditions. The research will utilize anonymized datasets from state I/M programs, comprising over 10 million vehicle inspection records, paired with real-world driving data from connected vehicles. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across HPC nodes, we will quantify uncertainty in emission estimates and optimize test cycle designs for improved regulatory compliance. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for adaptive inspection scheduling, predictive maintenance algorithms for emission control systems, and validated models correlating short-term test results with long-term environmental impact. These outputs will directly inform next-generation I/M program designs, reduce false failure rates in emissions testing, and provide technician training platforms for emerging diagnostics technologies. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scalability in analyzing heterogeneous vehicle populations, bridging gaps between laboratory-grade emission models and field-deployable technical solutions.
cip_title: Vehicle Emissions Inspection and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to test, repair, service, and maintain vehicle emission systems in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.

abstract: Clinical genetics faces a critical challenge in efficiently interpreting genomic variants of uncertain significance (VUS), which account for ~30% of findings in diagnostic sequencing. Resolving VUS requires integrating population-scale genomic data, functional assays, and phenotypic correlations—a task hindered by the computational complexity of multi-omics analyses and the lack of scalable frameworks for clinical variant prioritization. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a machine learning platform that unifies heterogeneous genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic datasets to improve VUS classification and risk prediction. The computational workflow will leverage graph neural networks to model variant interactions across biological networks and transformer-based architectures to interpret non-coding regulatory elements in rare disease contexts. Population-level simulations using coalescent models will assess the impact of ancestral diversity on variant pathogenicity estimates, addressing biases in existing clinical databases. A key innovation involves federated learning approaches to securely aggregate data from multiple clinical genomics centers while preserving patient confidentiality. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of >500,000 whole genomes, high-throughput functional genomics datasets (e.g., CRISPR screens, single-cell ATAC-seq), and real-time updates from public repositories such as ClinVar and gnomAD. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline reducing VUS rates by ≥40% in tested cohorts, (2) open-access tools for dynamic reclassification of variants using longitudinal clinical data, and (3) population-adjusted pathogenicity scores to minimize disparities in genetic diagnosis across ancestries. By enabling rapid, evidence-based variant interpretation at scale, this work directly supports the program’s mission to advance diagnostic precision and personalized management for genetic disorders. The computational framework will be deployed as a cloud-enabled resource for clinical genetics laboratories, enhancing collaborative research and translational applications.
cip_definition: Research on how to provide comprehensive diagnostic, management, and counseling services for individuals and families at risk for clinical disorders with a genetic basis.

abstract: The design and optimization of next-generation aerospace vehicles require high-fidelity simulations to address complex multi-physics challenges, such as turbulent hypersonic flows, coupled thermal-structural response during atmospheric re-entry, and propulsion system performance in extreme environments. Traditional computational approaches are limited by inadequate resolution of critical phenomena, leading to conservative designs and incomplete understanding of operational limits. This project seeks advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) methods, and finite element analysis (FEA) for multi-disciplinary aerospace systems. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) resolving hypersonic boundary layer transition mechanisms under real-gas effects using adaptive mesh refinement and reactive flow solvers, (2) modeling ablation and thermal degradation of ceramic composite materials in re-entry vehicles through coupled CFD-FEA frameworks, and (3) simulating plasma dynamics in advanced air-breathing propulsion systems for sustained hypersonic flight. These simulations demand petascale computational capabilities due to the need for three-dimensional, time-accurate solutions with billions of grid points and microsecond-scale temporal resolution. The proposed work leverages GPU-accelerated solvers and hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization to optimize resource utilization. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for aerodynamic heating, material failure thresholds, and combustion instability mitigation strategies, directly addressing critical gaps in current design methodologies. By enabling unprecedented resolution of multi-physics interactions, this research will advance the development of robust thermal protection systems, efficient propulsion architectures, and high-speed vehicle control algorithms, with applications to orbital launch systems, planetary entry vehicles, and hypersonic platforms. The computational datasets and open-source tools generated will provide foundational resources for the aerospace engineering community.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering, general
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their systems; applied research on flight and orbital characteristics; and the development of systems and procedures for the launching, guidance, and control of air and space vehicles.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biological systems and biotechnological processes necessitates advanced computational tools to model, optimize, and predict outcomes in experimental and industrial workflows. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in microbial fermentation and protein engineering, two pillars of biotechnology with broad applications in therapeutic development, sustainable manufacturing, and bioenergy. Current limitations in simulating large-scale metabolic networks, protein folding dynamics, and bioreactor heterogeneity restrict the precision of strain optimization and enzyme design, leading to costly trial-and-error experimentation. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating genome-scale metabolic modeling (GMM), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to predict strain behavior under industrial fermentation conditions and engineer proteins with enhanced stability and activity. GMMs will map metabolic fluxes across microbial populations, while MD simulations will resolve atomic-level interactions in engineered enzymes under varying physicochemical conditions. CFD models will simulate mass transfer, nutrient gradients, and shear stress in bioreactors, enabling the design of scalable fermentation systems. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing, large memory nodes, and GPU acceleration to manage datasets spanning terabytes of omics data, high-resolution temporal-spatial simulations, and iterative machine learning-driven parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive models for strain performance, validated enzyme designs with improved catalytic efficiency, and bioreactor configurations that maximize product yield. By bridging computational predictions with experimental validation, this work will accelerate the development of robust bioprocesses and biologics, reducing time-to-market for bio-based products. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these simulations, which cannot feasibly be executed on local clusters. This project aligns with national priorities in sustainable biotechnology and precision bioengineering, offering transformative tools for academic and industrial research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of biologists and biotechnologists in research, industrial, and government settings. Includes instruction in fermentation technology, cell culturing, protein purification, biologic synthesis, assaying and testing, quality control, industrial microbiology, bioprocessing, chromatography and bioseparation, genetic technology, laboratory and hazardous materials safety, and computer applications.

abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a critical role in mediating dietary impacts on metabolic health, yet the mechanisms underlying its interaction with host physiology in diverse populations remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting personalized nutritional responses by integrating multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and proteomic) with clinical biomarkers to model host-microbiome-diet interactions. A key barrier is the computational complexity of simulating dynamic, multi-scale biological systems that span microbial community ecology, molecular nutrient metabolism, and systemic physiological outcomes. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining agent-based modeling of microbial ecosystems with machine learning-driven analysis of longitudinal human cohort data. Agent-based simulations will capture stochastic microbial interactions under varying nutrient conditions, while neural networks trained on clinical trial datasets will identify predictive signatures linking dietary patterns to metabolic outcomes. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these resource-intensive simulations across thousands of microbial taxa and optimizing models using hyperparameter tuning on high-dimensional omics data (>10^6 features). Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for simulating personalized nutrient metabolism and validated predictive models of glycemic response variability across ethnic and metabolic health subgroups. This work will advance precision nutrition by enabling mechanistic insights into how individual differences in microbial ecology and host molecular networks modulate dietary impacts, with direct applications for designing equitable, population-specific dietary guidelines. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source resources to support interdisciplinary research at the intersection of nutritional biochemistry, systems biology, and public health.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the utilization of food for human growth and metabolism, in both normal and dysfunctional states, from the interdisciplinary perspective of the agricultural, human, biological, and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in food science, biochemistry, physiology, dietetics, food and nutrition studies, biotechnology, biophysics, and the clinical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model complex, multi-party dispute resolution dynamics and evaluate intervention strategies in real-world conflict scenarios. Dispute resolution processes often involve intricate interactions among stakeholders with divergent priorities, cultural backgrounds, and power asymmetries, yet existing analytical tools struggle to account for the nonlinear behavioral patterns and contextual variables inherent in these systems. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build agent-based simulations that integrate behavioral economics, game theory, and psychosocial datasets. The computational model will parameterize variables such as communication styles, concession patterns, and third-party mediator efficacy across diverse dispute contexts (e.g., labor negotiations, cross-border commercial conflicts). Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical arbitration case data to identify latent predictors of successful resolutions, while Monte Carlo methods will test the robustness of proposed mediation protocols under stochastic conditions. The scale of required simulations—encompassing thousands of agent permutations, temporal iterations, and scenario branches—necessitates parallelized computing architectures to achieve practical runtimes. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models that quantify the impact of specific negotiation tactics on resolution likelihood, optimized intervention templates for mediator training programs, and a novel framework for stress-testing dispute resolution policies in silico before real-world implementation. By bridging computational social science with conflict resolution praxis, this work aims to advance evidence-based methodologies for reducing escalatory behaviors and improving equitable outcomes in legal, organizational, and cross-cultural disputes. The resulting tools will be disseminated through open-source simulation platforms designed for adaptability across academic, governmental, and NGO applications.
cip_definition: A program that provides individuals with skills in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration, that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive educational technologies tailored to students with multiple disabilities. Current challenges in special education include the heterogeneity of learner needs, the complexity of integrating multisensory inputs, and the lack of scalable tools to personalize instruction in real time. Traditional methods for designing individualized education plans (IEPs) rely on manual, time-intensive assessments, limiting educators’ capacity to address dynamic student requirements. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework that combines machine learning (ML) and multimodal data analysis to model student interactions, predict learning barriers, and generate actionable feedback for educators. The project will process diverse datasets—including eye-tracking, gesture recognition, speech patterns, and physiological signals—to identify behavioral and cognitive correlates of engagement and comprehension in students with co-occurring sensory, motor, and intellectual disabilities. HPC resources are essential to train large-scale neural networks on these high-dimensional datasets, simulate virtual learning environments for hypothesis testing, and optimize real-time adaptive algorithms. Key outcomes include (1) a predictive model linking specific disability profiles to effective instructional strategies, (2) an open-source platform for simulating and testing assistive technologies, and (3) empirically validated guidelines for integrating computational tools into IEP development. By enabling rapid iteration of complex simulations and data-driven insights, this work aims to reduce the latency between pedagogical innovation and classroom implementation, ultimately empowering educators to deliver more responsive, equitable instruction. The project aligns with national priorities in inclusive education and bridges a critical gap between special education research and computational scalability.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Multiple Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with multiple disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with multiple disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with multiple handicaps, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) protocols by developing predictive computational models of tissue oxygenation dynamics under varying hyperbaric conditions. Despite widespread clinical use for conditions such as chronic non-healing wounds and radiation injury, HBOT efficacy remains inconsistent, with poor mechanistic understanding of how patient-specific factors (e.g., vascular anatomy, metabolic demand) interact with pressure-dosing schedules. Current trial-and-error approaches to protocol design limit outcomes and safety. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating fluid dynamics, oxygen transport modeling, and tissue-level metabolic responses to simulate HBOT effects across diverse physiological scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 1) 3D simulations of oxygen diffusion in heterogeneous tissues using finite element analysis, informed by patient-specific vascular imaging data, and 2) ensemble modeling of systemic physiological responses through coupled ordinary differential equation systems representing cardiovascular, respiratory, and cellular adaptations to hyperbaric exposure. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify critical parameter thresholds linking simulated oxygenation patterns to clinical outcomes using retrospective patient data. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro oxygenation measurements from tissue-engineered models exposed to controlled hyperbaric conditions. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for personalizing pressure profiles and session durations, identification of biomarkers for treatment responsiveness, and mechanistic insights into HBOT-related risks such as oxidative stress. This interdisciplinary approach bridges clinical hyperbaric medicine with computational physiology, addressing a critical gap in protocol optimization while advancing fundamental knowledge of gas transport under hyperbaric conditions. The requested HPC resources are essential given the computational intensity of multi-physics simulations and the need to process high-resolution imaging datasets across large patient cohorts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to operate hyperbaric (recompression) chambers for the treatment of disease. Includes instruction in patient assessment and management, hyperbaric safety, physics of hyperbaric and hypobaric exposures, physiology, hyperbaric chamber operation, and air decompression procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive maintenance frameworks for industrial machinery using high-performance computing (HPC) to address the challenge of unplanned downtime in manufacturing and processing systems. Industrial equipment such as pumps, conveyor systems, and steam propulsion systems are subject to complex wear patterns influenced by mechanical stress, thermal cycling, and material degradation. Traditional maintenance models often rely on oversimplified failure thresholds or static schedules, leading to inefficient resource use or catastrophic failures. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational approach integrating multi-physics simulations, sensor data analytics, and machine learning (ML) to predict failure modes with higher accuracy. HPC resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distributions in critical components under dynamic operational conditions, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to assess thermal and fluid-driven wear. These simulations will generate synthetic training datasets to augment real-world sensor data from vibration, temperature, and pressure sensors. ML models, including graph neural networks (GNNs) tailored for mechanical systems, will be trained on HPC clusters to identify early failure signatures from heterogeneous data streams. The project will validate models against experimental datasets from collaborating industry partners, including turbine degradation profiles and bearing failure cases. Expected outcomes include optimized maintenance scheduling algorithms, a digital twin framework for real-time equipment health monitoring, and open-source tools for industrial mechanics training programs. By reducing unplanned downtime by an estimated 15–30% in target systems, this work aims to lower operational costs and enhance safety in sectors reliant on complex machinery, while advancing computational methodologies for maintenance technology education.
cip_title: Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair and maintain industrial machinery and equipment such as cranes, pumps, engines and motors, pneumatic tools, conveyor systems, production machinery, marine deck machinery, and steam propulsion, refinery, and pipeline-distribution systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize real-time monitoring and mitigation of airborne pollutants in urban environments, where complex interactions between emission sources, meteorological factors, and built infrastructure challenge existing pollution control systems. Current sensor networks often lack the spatial resolution and predictive capacity to inform timely interventions, while static maintenance schedules for monitoring equipment risk operational inefficiencies. To address these gaps, we propose integrating high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with machine learning (ML) models to predict pollutant dispersion patterns and dynamically optimize sensor placement, calibration, and maintenance protocols. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve large-scale 3D urban airflow simulations at meter-scale resolution, capturing turbulence and pollutant transport mechanisms across diverse weather scenarios. Parallelized CFD outputs will train ML algorithms to correlate real-time sensor data with predicted emission hotspots, enabling adaptive network reconfiguration. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulations will assess failure risks across sensor nodes under varying environmental conditions, informing predictive maintenance schedules to minimize downtime. The computational pipeline will be validated against field data from pilot sites, including particulate matter and NO2 measurements. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolset for municipalities to enhance monitoring accuracy, reduce operational costs, and prioritize mitigation efforts in high-impact zones. By bridging high-fidelity environmental modeling with infrastructure management strategies, this work aims to advance resilient pollution control systems that proactively address public health risks while maintaining compliance with evolving air quality standards. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the iterative simulation workloads, ML training processes, and uncertainty quantification analyses central to this effort.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using indoor and outdoor environmental pollution control systems. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of software ecosystems demands innovative approaches to optimize code maintenance and adaptability in heterogeneous computing environments. This project addresses the challenge of automating context-aware program refactoring for legacy systems operating across hybrid architectures (CPU/GPU/FPGA). Traditional static analysis tools struggle to account for dynamic runtime behaviors and hardware-specific performance characteristics, particularly when scaling to large codebases. We propose developing a machine learning-driven framework that integrates execution trace analysis, hardware telemetry, and semantic code pattern recognition to recommend optimized code transformations. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model interprocedural code dependencies with reinforcement learning agents trained on performance outcome simulations. High-performance computing resources are critical for two components: (1) parallel processing of terabyte-scale execution traces from distributed instrumentation nodes, and (2) simultaneous training of multiple architecture-specific optimization models through hyperparameter-optimized ensemble learning. Our methodology employs containerized microservices to process diverse data streams, including low-level hardware performance counters and abstract syntax tree representations. The expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit capable of suggesting context-sensitive code modifications that preserve functional equivalence while improving energy efficiency by 15-30% across target architectures. This research bridges gaps between conventional program optimization techniques and emerging requirements for adaptive computing infrastructure, particularly in edge computing scenarios where hardware heterogeneity and resource constraints complicate traditional maintenance paradigms. Success metrics will evaluate both computational efficiency gains in the refactoring pipeline itself and downstream performance improvements in transformed applications. The results aim to establish new methodologies for sustainable software evolution in increasingly complex computing environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general writing and implementation of generic and customized programs to drive operating systems and that generally prepares individuals to apply the methods and procedures of software design and programming to software installation and maintenance. Includes instruction in software design, low- and high-level languages and program writing; program customization and linking; prototype testing; troubleshooting; and related aspects of operating systems and networks.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting developmental trajectories in children with neuropsychiatric disorders by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multimodal datasets. Clinical child psychology research faces limitations in integrating large-scale neuroimaging, behavioral, and genetic data to model dynamic interactions between biological and environmental factors. Current approaches often rely on static, small-sample analyses, which fail to capture the heterogeneity of disorders such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or early-onset anxiety. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining longitudinal machine learning models and biophysically informed neural network simulations. The project will utilize HPC resources to process high-resolution fMRI and EEG data from a multi-site cohort of 800 children (ages 3–12), integrate these with behavioral assessments and family environmental measures, and train ensemble models to identify critical developmental windows for intervention. Graph-based algorithms will map functional connectivity changes, while parallelized Bayesian inference methods will quantify uncertainty in individual trajectory predictions. This approach requires significant memory allocation and GPU acceleration to handle the petabyte-scale data and computationally intensive simulations. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of transdiagnostic biomarkers predictive of treatment response and the development of open-source tools for personalized risk stratification. By enabling rapid iteration of complex models across diverse developmental pathways, HPC resources will directly advance clinical applications, such as tailoring early interventions to neurodevelopmental subtypes. The project aligns with clinical child psychology’s emphasis on developmental mechanisms and ethical practice by creating scalable, evidence-based resources to reduce diagnostic delays and improve access to precision mental health care for pediatric populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the developmental processes of children and associated disorders and that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical child psychology. Includes instruction in developmental neuropsychology, child psychopathology, testing of children and adolescents, pediatric psychology, psychosocial variables in child development, clinical skills, family therapy, behavioral assessment and intervention, clinical skills, consultation, professional standards and ethics, and applications to topics such as infancy, childhood, and adolescence.

abstract: Cardiovascular diagnostics rely heavily on high-resolution imaging and hemodynamic data, yet current methods to integrate multimodal datasets for predicting acute events—such as aortic dissection or ischemic cascades—remain computationally constrained. This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework capable of synthesizing real-time 4D flow MRI, intravascular ultrasound, and wearable sensor data to model microvascular dysfunction and predict rupture-risk in patients with undiagnosed cardiovascular anomalies. The primary challenge lies in processing terabyte-scale spatiotemporal datasets while preserving clinically relevant features across disparate modalities. We propose a hybrid computational approach leveraging GPU-accelerated dimensionality reduction (via non-negative tensor factorization) and physics-informed neural networks to simulate blood flow dynamics under variable physiological conditions. High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized training of ensemble models on anonymized datasets from 1,200 retrospective cases, followed by validation against prospective clinical outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable pipeline for identifying subclinical precursors of cardiovascular crises, reducing diagnostic latency by automating the detection of nonlinear hemodynamic patterns. This work bridges gaps between cardiovascular technology and computational biomechanics, offering a platform for personalized risk stratification without reliance on traditional, symptom-driven diagnostic pathways. Success will provide open-source tools for real-time analysis of complex cardiovascular data, advancing the integration of high-fidelity imaging with predictive analytics in clinical practice. Resource allocation will specifically support the deployment of containerized workflows on clustered nodes, optimizing memory bandwidth for large-scale tensor operations and reducing inference latency to meet clinical decision-making timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform invasive, noninvasive, and peripheral examinations of the cardiovascular system at the request of physicians to aid in diagnoses and therapeutic treatments. Includes instruction in reviewing and recording patient histories and clinical data, patient care, investigative and examination procedures, diagnostic procedures, data analysis and documentation, physician consultation, equipment operation and monitoring, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and fabrication of complex wooden structures through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations. Traditional woodworking practices rely heavily on empirical knowledge and iterative physical prototyping, which limits the exploration of innovative geometries, material efficiencies, and performance under dynamic environmental conditions. The research problem centers on overcoming these constraints by modeling the anisotropic behavior of wood, stress distribution in advanced joinery systems, and the effects of humidity and temperature fluctuations on structural integrity. A multi-scale computational approach will be implemented, combining finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical behavior, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for moisture diffusion modeling, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict warping and cracking risks in diverse wood species. These simulations require HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of parametric design spaces, the non-linear interactions between environmental factors and material properties, and the need for real-time feedback in generative design workflows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for failure thresholds in custom joints, optimized cutting patterns to minimize waste, and a digital twin framework for testing virtual prototypes under simulated environmental stressors. The project aims to advance sustainable woodworking practices by reducing material waste and energy consumption in fabrication, while enabling the creation of structurally resilient, aesthetically novel designs that push the boundaries of traditional craftsmanship. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools tailored for woodworking education, fostering integration of computational methods into technical training programs.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to lay out and shape stock; assemble wooden articles or subassemblies; mark, bind, saw, carve, and sand wooden products; repair wooden articles, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of specific learning disabilities (SLDs) necessitates the development of adaptive, evidence-based instructional strategies tailored to individual learner profiles. However, current approaches to designing educational interventions often rely on static frameworks that inadequately account for the dynamic interplay between cognitive, behavioral, and environmental factors influencing learning outcomes. This project proposes to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate the efficacy of personalized teaching strategies for students with SLDs. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets of student performance, demographic information, and intervention records, we will employ machine learning techniques to identify patterns in learning trajectories and predict responsiveness to specific pedagogical approaches. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments with heterogeneous learner profiles, enabling the systematic testing of intervention scenarios under varied conditions. Computational demands arise from the need to process multimodal educational data (e.g., text, sensor-based engagement metrics, and assessment results) at scale, as well as to run thousands of parallel simulations optimizing parameters such as instructional pacing, scaffolding methods, and feedback timing. Outcomes will include a validated computational framework for generating individualized education plans (IEPs) that dynamically adapt to student progress, reducing the trial-and-error period often associated with SLD interventions. Additionally, the project will produce open-source tools for educators to visualize learning patterns and simulate intervention impacts within their own classrooms. By integrating computational modeling with educational theory, this work aims to advance precision teaching practices, directly supporting educators in delivering targeted, data-informed instruction for students with SLDs. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary computational throughput for large-scale parameter optimization and real-world validation, which cannot be feasibly conducted on local infrastructure.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Specific Learning Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with specific learning disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with specific learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with specific learning disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized fitness program design by analyzing the interplay between biomechanical variability, metabolic responses, and behavioral adherence patterns. Current fitness programming often relies on generalized protocols that inadequately address individual differences in mobility, recovery capacity, and physiological adaptation thresholds, leading to suboptimal outcomes and increased injury risk. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets from wearable sensors, 3D motion capture systems, and longitudinal client performance records. Machine learning models will identify latent patterns in biomechanical efficiency across diverse population cohorts, while agent-based simulations will test the emergent effects of program variables (e.g., exercise sequencing, load progression) on long-term adherence and physiological adaptation. The computational pipeline will integrate musculoskeletal modeling with reinforcement learning algorithms to generate adaptive training prescriptions that dynamically adjust to real-time biometric feedback. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support system for fitness technicians that quantifies injury probability surfaces and predicts individual response curves for specific exercise modalities. This resource-intensive modeling requires parallel processing capabilities to handle high-dimensional data from heterogeneous sources, including time-series biomechanics (sampled at 100Hz+) and multi-omics profiles related to metabolic flexibility. The resulting framework aims to establish evidence-based thresholds for personalized load progression while accounting for psychosocial factors influencing program compliance. By bridging computational modeling with practical fitness implementation, this work could redefine precision in client-specific program design while reducing trial-and-error approaches in fitness service delivery.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in health and fitness clubs, wellness centers, public and private recreation facilities, hospitals and corporate fitness programs where they will perform a variety of instructional and administrative duties. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, fitness techniques, exercise science, personal training, nutrition, and customer service.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing demand for computationally intensive typographic design processes in digital media production. Current software tools for dynamic text composition—particularly for high-resolution, multi-platform publishing—struggle to efficiently render complex layouts integrating variable fonts, adaptive kerning, and real-time accessibility adjustments (e.g., dyslexia-friendly formatting). The project proposes developing a GPU-accelerated framework for optimizing automated typographic workflows, leveraging high-performance computing resources to overcome latency and scalability barriers in existing composition systems. Using parallelized layout engines and machine learning models trained on typographic design patterns, we aim to simulate and evaluate text composition scenarios at production-scale resolutions (8K+), accounting for diverse output devices and user interaction parameters. Methods will include benchmarking existing CPU-bound composition pipelines, prototyping OpenCL-optimized rendering modules, and training transformer-based models on a corpus of 50,000 professionally designed publication layouts to predict context-aware formatting adjustments. The computational workload requires access to GPU clusters capable of processing terabyte-scale font datasets and simultaneous rendering tasks across multiple virtualized design environments. Expected outcomes include a quantifiable reduction in layout computation times for complex documents (targeting 60-75% improvement over industry-standard tools), as well as novel metrics for evaluating typographic accessibility in dynamic content. Results will directly benefit digital publishing workflows and open-source design tools, while advancing pedagogical resources for next-generation typography operators working with AI-assisted composition systems. This work bridges critical gaps between traditional graphic design principles and modern computational demands, ensuring robust typographic practices can scale alongside emerging immersive media formats.
cip_title: Computer Typography and Composition Equipment Operator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to design and execute page formats, layouts and text composition, and to make typographical selections using computer graphics and other computer-assisted design programs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, installation, and maintenance of next-generation hybrid fiber-coaxial (HFC) and wireless communication systems. As modern networks grow in complexity—driven by 5G integration, IoT proliferation, and escalating bandwidth demands—traditional empirical approaches to system testing and fault diagnosis are becoming insufficient. The research problem centers on addressing signal integrity degradation, electromagnetic interference (EMI), and latency bottlenecks in heterogeneous communication infrastructures, which require high-fidelity simulations to resolve. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to model large-scale network topologies, simulate multi-physics interactions (electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical stressors), and analyze real-world telemetry datasets from field deployments. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) for EMI prediction, machine learning (ML)-driven anomaly detection in time-series network performance data, and Monte Carlo simulations to assess failure probabilities under variable environmental conditions. The project will also leverage GPU-accelerated ray tracing to optimize signal propagation in dense urban environments. Outcomes will include predictive maintenance frameworks, validated installation protocols to minimize signal loss, and open-source simulation tools tailored for technician training programs. By integrating HPC-driven insights with hands-on repair methodologies, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical diagnostics and practical field operations, ultimately enhancing the reliability and scalability of communication infrastructures. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of network configurations, reduce simulation turnaround times from weeks to hours, and support the development of AI-assisted decision systems for technicians. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and integrated into the academic curriculum to advance workforce preparedness for emerging smart grid and broadband access challenges.
cip_title: Communications Systems Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair one- and two- way communications equipment and systems, including television cable systems and mobile or stationary communication devices. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of communications systems.

abstract: Orthopedic conditions, particularly those affecting load-bearing joints, present complex biomechanical challenges that are difficult to model using conventional experimental methods. Current limitations in predicting long-term outcomes of surgical interventions or implant performance stem from an incomplete understanding of multiscale tissue mechanics and patient-specific variability. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate musculoskeletal dynamics, bone remodeling, and implant-tissue interactions under physiologically realistic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) and agent-based modeling to capture mechanobiological processes across spatial scales, from cellular responses to whole-joint biomechanics. Patient-specific anatomical data, including CT and MRI-derived geometries, will inform model parametrization, while machine learning techniques will optimize computational efficiency by identifying reduced-order representations of high-dimensional datasets. The proposed simulations will quantify stress-shielding effects in orthopedic implants, predict bone adaptation patterns post-surgery, and evaluate the biomechanical consequences of anatomical variations across diverse patient populations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for implant failure risk, data-driven guidelines for personalized surgical planning, and mechanistic insights into osteoarthritis progression. The computational demands of this work necessitate HPC infrastructure due to the requirement for parallel processing of large-scale multiphysics simulations (10^6-10^7 elements per model), ensemble runs for population-level analysis, and iterative optimization of machine learning architectures. Successful implementation will provide clinical researchers with an open-source simulation platform to test intervention strategies in silico, potentially reducing costly postoperative complications and accelerating the development of next-generation orthopedic treatments.
cip_definition: Research focused on Orthopedic

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of psychodynamic processes in therapeutic interactions through computational modeling and large-scale natural language processing (NLP). Traditional psychoanalytic research has relied on qualitative case studies and manual coding of clinical sessions, limiting scalability and reproducibility. The proposed research addresses this gap by developing computational frameworks to analyze longitudinal therapy transcripts, quantify patterns in transference-countertransference dynamics, and model the emergence of unconscious conflict resolution during treatment. Using anonymized datasets comprising over 10,000 hours of psychotherapy session transcripts across diverse clinical populations, we will implement neural language models to identify latent linguistic markers of defense mechanisms, emotional valence shifts, and therapeutic alliance fluctuations. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate dyadic patient-therapist interactions under varying psychodynamic principles to test hypotheses about optimal intervention timing. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-dimensional text data, training transformer-based architectures on therapeutic dialogue, and running parallelized simulations of complex interpersonal dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated NLP pipeline for automated detection of clinically relevant psychodynamic phenomena, (2) computational evidence linking specific interaction patterns to treatment outcomes, and (3) open-source tools enabling real-time analysis of therapeutic process variables. By bridging psychoanalytic theory with computational psychiatry methods, this work aims to establish quantitative foundations for psychodynamic research while providing clinicians with data-driven insights into intervention efficacy. The project represents a novel convergence of depth psychology and artificial intelligence, addressing core challenges in mental health care personalization and mechanistic understanding of psychotherapy.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the provision of psychoanalytic counseling to individuals and groups based on the psychodynamic principles evolved from authorities such as Freud, Adler, and Jung.
