Includes instruction in self-analysis, personality theory, dream analysis, free association and transference theory and techniques, psychodynamic theory, developmental processes, applications to specific clinical conditions, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational approach to analyzing the cross-cultural evolution of symbolic systems and ethical frameworks within religious and philosophical traditions. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically tracing how core concepts—such as justice, purity, or transcendence—are semantically constructed, transmitted, and transformed across diverse textual corpora spanning multiple languages, historical periods, and cultural contexts. Traditional hermeneutic methods struggle to manage the scale and complexity of these interdependent processes, particularly when analyzing non-linear influences between traditions (e.g., comparative studies of Abrahamic and Dharmic symbolic networks). The project will employ computational text analysis, including transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for ancient and sacred texts, to map conceptual relationships and semantic shifts at scale. Network analysis algorithms will identify structural patterns in symbolic systems, while agent-based modeling will simulate the diffusion of ethical principles through hypothetical historical-cultural scenarios. These methods require HPC capabilities to process multilingual corpora (Sanskrit, Classical Arabic, Koine Greek, etc.), run parallelized semantic clustering algorithms, and iteratively train models on philosophically annotated datasets. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for quantifying phenomenological patterns in religious symbolism, 2) computational evidence addressing debates about universal versus culturally contingent ethics, and 3) open-access tools for interdisciplinary religion-philosophy research. By enabling large-scale comparative analysis of how abstract concepts emerge and interact within belief systems, this work aims to provide new empirical grounding for theories in the philosophy of religion while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources for humanistic inquiry.
cip_definition: A general program that combines the study of philosophy and religious studies. Includes instruction in logic; ethics; epistemology; symbolism; phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature, and art of religion; and world religions.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in modeling large-scale, heterogeneous educational datasets to identify nuanced predictors of student outcomes. Educational research increasingly relies on high-dimensional data from longitudinal assessments, digital learning platforms, and multi-institutional studies. Traditional statistical approaches often struggle to account for nested data structures (e.g., students within schools, districts, or regions), temporal dependencies, and complex interaction effects while maintaining computational feasibility. The proposed research will develop and validate advanced multilevel structural equation models with Bayesian inference to simultaneously model latent constructs, hierarchical dependencies, and time-varying covariates across diverse educational contexts. These models require iterative sampling techniques (e.g., Hamiltonian Monte Carlo) and intensive matrix operations that scale cubically with the number of latent variables—a computational barrier for standard workstations when applied to datasets with millions of observations from national education surveys. The requested high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized parameter estimation across multiple chains, distributed memory architectures for massive matrix computations, and GPU-accelerated gradient evaluations. Additionally, the project will implement machine learning ensemble methods to compare predictive accuracy against traditional psychometric models, leveraging HPC capabilities for hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation across stratified subsamples. Anticipated outcomes include (1) optimized algorithms for detecting cross-level mediation effects in educational interventions, (2) scalable methods for handling missing data in longitudinal educational assessments, and (3) open-source computational tools for reproducible education research. This work will directly inform evidence-based strategies for addressing achievement gaps by identifying context-specific predictors of learning outcomes while advancing methodological frameworks for complex educational data analysis. The computational infrastructure will support both proposed analyses of the National Educational Longitudinal Study (N=25,000 students, 15,000 variables) and ongoing simulations of intervention scenarios through agent-based modeling.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the analysis and solution of educational research problems, and the development of technical designs for research studies. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, research design, computer applications, instrument design, research methodologies, and applications to research problems in specific education subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the structural integrity, thermal performance, and material efficiency of modern and historical masonry systems. Traditional masonry design relies on empirical methods and standardized codes, which often overlook complex interactions between heterogeneous materials, environmental stressors, and long-term degradation patterns. To address these limitations, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze the micro- and macro-scale behavior of masonry assemblies under dynamic loads, moisture ingress, and thermal cycling. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution across brick-mortar interfaces, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate moisture transport and freeze-thaw effects in porous masonry materials. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and experimental datasets to predict crack propagation and identify failure thresholds in decorative and load-bearing elements. Additionally, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will investigate the nano-scale adhesion properties of novel sustainable mortars to reduce carbon footprints. The HPC environment is critical for managing the high-resolution 3D meshes, transient multiphysics couplings, and large parameter spaces inherent to these simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for enhancing masonry durability in extreme climates, data-driven guidelines for retrofitting historic structures, and optimized material compositions for next-generation masonry systems. By integrating computational insights with traditional craftsmanship, this research will advance pedagogical resources for masonry education and provide actionable strategies to improve energy efficiency and safety in construction practices. The requested computing resources will enable the execution of parallelized simulations at unprecedented scales, directly supporting innovation in a field foundational to global infrastructure resilience.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the laying and/or setting of exterior brick, concrete block, hard tile, marble and related materials, using trowels, levels, hammers, chisels, and other hand tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, blueprint reading, structural masonry, decorative masonry, foundations, reinforcement, mortar preparation, cutting and finishing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize multimodal cross-border freight routing under dynamic regulatory constraints using high-performance computing (HPC) to address systemic inefficiencies in customs-triggered logistics delays. Current routing models inadequately integrate real-time updates to tariffs, trade agreements, and inspection protocols, resulting in cascading delays that cost global supply chains an estimated $140 billion annually. We propose developing a simulation framework that models freight movement across air, maritime, and terrestrial networks while dynamically incorporating jurisdictional policy changes, automated customs documentation validation, and carrier capacity constraints. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation with transformer-based natural language processing to parse regulatory texts from 190+ customs jurisdictions, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively optimize routing decisions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 1) high-resolution geotemporal traffic data, 2) multilingual regulatory updates scraped from government portals, and 3) multi-agent simulations evaluating over 10^6 potential route permutations per shipment corridor. Expected outcomes include a predictive routing engine that reduces customs clearance times by 18-22% in simulated scenarios while maintaining compliance accuracy above 99.4%, benchmarked against historical shipment data from EU and ASEAN trade corridors. The computational toolkit will be designed for integration with existing transportation management systems, providing actionable recommendations for fleet dispatchers and customs brokers. This research fills a critical gap in adaptive logistics planning at the intersection of computational trade compliance and transportation operations, offering scalability benefits for both public customs authorities and private-sector freight forwarders navigating increasingly complex transnational regulatory environments.
cip_title: Traffic, Customs, and Transportation Clerk/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform duties associated with managing revenue-based customs, traffic, or transportation services, such as control of domestic and international traffic, toll roads and waterways, and to assist in the dispatch and control of fleet-based traffic for businesses and public services. Includes instruction in record-keeping; preparation of customs and transportation documentation; operation of communications equipment; basic transportation operations management; tariffs, rates and fares; revenue collection and change-making; and interpretation of customs or transportation regulations and related legislation, policies, and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to analyze the efficacy of multimodal communication strategies in secondary education classrooms, with a focus on improving pedagogical training for pre-service Communication Arts and Literature teachers. A critical challenge in teacher education is understanding how diverse instructional techniques—such as interactive storytelling, debate facilitation, and peer review workflows—impact student engagement and learning outcomes across varied demographic contexts. While qualitative studies dominate this field, the scale and complexity of classroom interaction data (e.g., transcribed dialogues, written feedback, and multimedia artifacts) require advanced computational methods to identify patterns and predictors of successful teaching practices. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to process and analyze large datasets comprising audio/video recordings of classroom activities, student writing samples, and teacher feedback logs from 50+ partner schools. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for sentiment analysis and discourse structure identification, will be applied to evaluate linguistic and paralinguistic features of teacher-student interactions. Concurrently, network analysis will map the relationship between specific instructional approaches (e.g., scaffolded writing exercises) and longitudinal student performance metrics. The computational pipeline will integrate these multimodal inputs to generate adaptive simulations of classroom scenarios, enabling pre-service teachers to virtually test and refine communication strategies in diverse simulated environments. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for quantifying the impact of rhetorical choices on learning outcomes, (2) evidence-based recommendations for personalizing communication pedagogy, and (3) open-access training modules incorporating computational insights into existing teacher education curricula. By bridging computational linguistics with classroom praxis, this work aims to equip educators with data-driven tools to address evolving challenges in literacy education and intercultural communication.
cip_title: Communication Arts and Literature Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to teach oral expression, literature, and writing to students at various education levels. Includes instruction in interpersonal communication, intercultural communication, language learning, listening instructional techniques, public speaking, reading instructional techniques, writing instructional techniques, and practical teaching experience.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary framework for modeling the cascading impacts of climate-driven landscape changes on ecological systems and human health outcomes. Traditional approaches to studying disease vector dynamics, ecological shifts, and public health risks often operate in disciplinary silos, limiting predictive capacity for complex, feedback-driven systems. We propose a novel integration of geospatial, ecological, and epidemiological data streams—including high-resolution satellite imagery, species distribution records, and anonymized healthcare datasets—to develop a coupled modeling system. The computational workflow combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for real-time land cover classification, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map habitat connectivity for disease vectors, and agent-based models (ABMs) simulating human exposure scenarios. Key challenges include scaling spatiotemporal alignment of heterogeneous datasets (10^7+ georeferenced data points across 15+ years) and optimizing memory-intensive Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification in cross-system interactions. HPC resources are critical for parallel processing of multi-terabyte remote sensing archives, training deep learning models with dynamic spatial dependencies, and running ensemble projections under 20+ climate and land-use scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational platform for identifying high-risk zones where microclimatic shifts amplify vector-borne disease transmission, validated against historical outbreak patterns in three ecoregions. This work bridges gaps between landscape ecology, climate science, and public health preparedness, offering a template for data-driven resilience planning in underserved regions facing rapid environmental change. The resource allocation will directly support 4.2 million core-hours for model development, sensitivity analyses, and the generation of risk projection maps at 100m resolution for stakeholder use.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis of large scale data sources from the interdisciplinary perspectives of applied statistics, computer science, data storage, data representation, data modeling, mathematics, and statistics. Includes instruction in computer algorithms, computer programming, data management, data mining, information policy, information retrieval, mathematical modeling, quantitative analysis, statistics, trend spotting, and visual analytics.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address critical challenges in urologic oncology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multi-modal datasets for improved prostate cancer stratification. Prostate cancer exhibits significant heterogeneity in progression and treatment response, yet existing clinical tools inadequately predict outcomes, leading to overtreatment or delayed interventions. This project will develop computational models integrating genomic, radiomic, and electronic health record (EHR) data from 3,500+ patients across six institutions to identify novel biomarkers and predictive signatures. The computational approach employs deep learning architectures (3D convolutional neural networks for MRI analysis, transformer models for temporal EHR patterns) combined with Bayesian hierarchical frameworks to account for multi-center data variability. Genome-scale metabolic modeling will be performed using constraint-based reconstruction and analysis (COBRA) tools to map tumor-specific metabolic vulnerabilities. Due to the scale of whole-genome sequencing data (>50 TB), radiomic feature extraction from multiparametric MRI, and iterative model training requirements, HPC resources are essential for parallelized processing, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale in silico simulations of treatment response. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for biochemical recurrence risk with superior accuracy to existing clinical nomograms (target AUC >0.85 vs current 0.70-0.75), (2) identification of metabolic pathways associated with castration resistance, and (3) open-source computational workflows for multimodal data integration in urologic malignancies. This resource will enable clinically actionable risk stratification, inform targeted therapy development, and establish a framework for computational urology that could be extended to bladder and kidney cancers. The requested HPC allocation will directly support data-intensive tasks including neural network training on GPU clusters, genome assembly via distributed memory systems, and population-level metabolic flux simulations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Urology

abstract: The increasing complexity of dynamic edge computing environments in precision agriculture demands resilient, low-latency networks capable of adapting to variable terrains, intermittent connectivity, and resource constraints. Traditional static network architectures struggle to optimize data flows from distributed IoT sensors (e.g., soil moisture monitors, autonomous drones) under rapidly changing conditions, leading to inefficiencies in real-time decision-making for resource allocation. This project proposes the development of a bio-inspired, adaptive networking framework that leverages decentralized reinforcement learning (RL) to autonomously reconfigure topology and routing protocols in response to environmental perturbations. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale agricultural networks (>10,000 nodes) across diverse geospatial models, incorporating stochastic weather patterns, equipment mobility, and heterogeneous communication protocols (LoRaWAN, 5G-NR). Computational experiments will train multi-agent RL models using federated learning techniques to preserve data locality, while graph neural networks will predict congestion hotspots and prioritize critical agroinformatics streams. Key challenges include minimizing energy consumption in resource-constrained edge devices and maintaining synchronization across asynchronous learning cycles. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for self-organizing agricultural networks, validated through digital twin simulations, that reduces median packet loss by ≥40% compared to current SDN-based approaches. The work bridges telecommunications engineering and agricultural informatics, advancing cyber-physical system design principles for non-uniform deployment environments. Successful implementation will directly support sustainable farming practices through enhanced edge analytics capabilities, with methodological extensions applicable to disaster response networks and remote infrastructure monitoring. HPC resources are essential for scaling emulation of hybrid network architectures and accelerating RL training cycles across parameterized environmental scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of linked systems of computers, peripherals, and associated software to maximize efficiency and productivity, and that prepares individuals to function as network specialists and managers at various levels. Includes instruction in operating systems and applications; systems design and analysis; networking theory and solutions; types of networks; network management and control; network and flow optimization; security; configuring; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in legal document analysis and compliance verification by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop scalable natural language processing (NLP) tools tailored to legal support services. Legal professionals routinely navigate vast repositories of unstructured text—including contracts, regulatory filings, and case law—where manual review is time-intensive, error-prone, and inaccessible to smaller firms. While computational methods hold promise, existing tools lack domain-specific optimization for legal semantics, jurisdictional nuance, and evolving regulatory frameworks. This research proposes a novel computational pipeline combining transformer-based language models, graph-based citation networks, and automated compliance-checking algorithms to identify critical clauses, cross-reference legal precedents, and flag discrepancies in real time. The project will train and fine-tune models on a curated corpus of legal texts, including anonymized court records, legislative documents, and standardized contracts, using distributed deep learning frameworks to handle the scale and complexity of legal language. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets, dynamic graph traversal of legal citation networks, and iterative model training to accommodate regional legal variations. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for semantic search, anomaly detection, and summarization of legal documents, validated through partnerships with legal aid organizations and corporate compliance teams. By automating routine tasks, this work aims to reduce bottlenecks in legal workflows, lower costs for under-resourced entities, and improve consistency in regulatory adherence. The project also contributes methodologically to computational legal studies by establishing benchmarks for model interpretability and ethical AI use in sensitive legal contexts, setting a foundation for future interdisciplinary innovations at the intersection of law and advanced computing.
cip_definition: Any program in legal support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Hospice and palliative care patients often experience complex, dynamic symptom burdens and heterogeneous trajectories of functional decline, yet existing prognostic tools lack precision for individualized care planning. This project seeks to develop computational models that integrate multimodal clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), patient-reported outcomes, and wearable sensor metrics—to predict symptom exacerbation, functional decline, and survival in patients with advanced serious illnesses. A key challenge lies in analyzing high-dimensional, temporally irregular datasets while accounting for interactions between biological, psychological, and social determinants of outcomes. To address this, we propose a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble models combining recurrent neural networks, transformer architectures for clinical note analysis, and Bayesian survival models. Computational workflows will process structured EHR data (medications, lab values, diagnoses) alongside unstructured clinician notes (processed via natural language processing) and continuous wearable data (activity levels, vital signs). The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory CPU nodes for large-scale survival analysis. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for 30- and 90-day trajectories of pain, dyspnea, and functional status, (2) identification of modifiable risk factors for acute care utilization in hospice populations, and (3) open-source tools for temporal fusion of palliative care datasets. By enabling real-time analysis of longitudinal data from 15,000+ patients across three health systems, this HPC-supported approach aims to advance personalized goal-concordant care while addressing computational bottlenecks in palliative care research. The resource allocation will directly support model training at scale, sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups, and simulation studies to evaluate clinical implementation scenarios.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hospice and Palliative Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to advance the optimization of industrial-scale chemical production processes through high-fidelity computational modeling of multiphase reactor systems, with an emphasis on catalytic conversion efficiency and environmental impact reduction. Current empirical approaches to reactor design and process scaling in chemical manufacturing suffer from high experimental costs, limited resolution of localized reaction dynamics, and challenges in predicting byproduct formation under transient operating conditions. To address these limitations, we propose developing a multiscale computational framework integrating quantum mechanical calculations of catalytic surface interactions, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of reactor-scale transport phenomena, and machine learning-assisted parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parallelized simulations of turbulent multiphase flows with coupled heterogeneous reactions, particularly for modeling industrially relevant geometries and timescales. The computational workflow will leverage open-source simulation packages (OpenFOAM, LAMMPS) alongside custom Python-based optimization algorithms to iteratively refine reactor configurations and operating parameters. Expected outcomes include predictive models for reaction yield improvement in Fischer-Tropsch-type systems, identification of optimal catalyst bed geometries to minimize pressure drop, and quantitative assessments of thermal management strategies to prevent catalyst deactivation. Successful implementation will provide actionable insights for reducing energy intensity in continuous-flow chemical processes while maintaining compliance with evolving environmental regulations. The resulting datasets and validated simulation protocols will be disseminated through industry partnerships and integrated into the Chemical Engineering Technology curriculum, enhancing workforce training in computational process design. This work directly supports regional chemical manufacturers transitioning to sustainable production methods by offering a virtual testing platform for process innovations without interrupting active operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize the design and operational efficiency of wind turbine arrays in complex terrain using high-fidelity computational modeling, a critical challenge in expanding wind energy adoption. Current industry tools for wind farm layout optimization rely on simplified wake models and static atmospheric data, limiting their accuracy in predicting energy losses due to turbulent interactions in non-uniform landscapes. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework combining large-eddy simulation (LES) for microscale turbulence analysis with mesoscale weather model data to capture site-specific atmospheric dynamics. The computational workflow will integrate open-source computational fluid dynamics (CFD) software (e.g., OpenFOAM) with custom Python-based optimization algorithms to evaluate turbine placement configurations under varying wind regimes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve turbulent flow structures at meter-scale resolutions across multi-kilometer domains while iterating through thousands of potential layouts. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for wake-induced power losses in topographically diverse regions and a decision-support tool that balances energy output with infrastructure costs. This work directly supports regional wind energy developers aiming to site projects in underserved mountainous areas, where poor layout choices can reduce array efficiency by 15–25%. By leveraging HPC capabilities to account for real-world complexity, the project aims to reduce levelized energy costs through improved capacity factors while providing students in Wind Energy Technology with hands-on experience in cutting-edge computational methods. The resulting datasets and workflow templates will be shared through public repositories to advance collaborative research in renewable energy systems integration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing wind-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in wind energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling and optimization of power plant operations, with a focus on improving energy efficiency, reducing emissions, and enhancing operational stability in aging infrastructure. Power plants face growing challenges due to fluctuating energy demands, integration of renewable energy sources, and stringent environmental regulations. Traditional operational models struggle to account for real-time dynamic interactions between mechanical, thermal, and chemical systems, particularly in legacy coal, natural gas, and nuclear facilities. To address this, the research will employ multiphysics computational simulations integrating thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and corrosion kinetics to model turbine performance, heat exchanger efficiency, and combustion dynamics under variable load conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical operational data and simulation outputs to identify optimal control strategies for minimizing fuel consumption and pollutant emissions (e.g., NOx, CO2) while maintaining grid reliability. Key computational tasks include large-scale parallelized simulations of reactor coolant systems, finite element analysis of turbine blade stress under thermal cycling, and Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification for corrosion rates in high-temperature components. These workflows require HPC resources due to the high resolution of 3D mesh geometries, iterative solver demands for nonlinear systems, and the need for rapid parameter sweeps across multi-objective optimization frameworks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for proactive maintenance scheduling, a digital twin framework for real-time operational decision support, and scalable emission-reduction strategies adaptable to diverse power plant configurations. By bridging gaps between theoretical models and real-world operational constraints, this work aims to provide actionable insights for extending the lifespan of existing infrastructure, reducing downtime, and supporting the transition to low-carbon energy systems. The computational tools developed will also serve as educational resources for training power plant technicians in advanced simulation-based diagnostics and control optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the precision and efficiency of postmortem tissue analysis in forensic and clinical pathology through automated histomorphometric feature extraction and machine learning-driven pattern recognition. Pathologist Assistants (PAs) routinely process complex tissue specimens for diagnostic evaluation, yet current workflows rely heavily on manual microscopic assessment, which is time-intensive and subject to interobserver variability. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating scalable tools to quantify subtle morphological patterns in digitized histopathology slides, particularly in cases of ambiguous cause-of-death determination or early-stage disease. The computational approach integrates high-throughput image analysis pipelines with deep learning models (e.g., convolutional neural networks) trained on annotated datasets of postmortem tissues from diverse etiologies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale whole-slide imaging data, optimization of three-dimensional reconstructions from serial tissue sections, and parallelized model training to detect microarchitectural anomalies predictive of specific pathologies. Methods include validation against gold-standard autopsy reports and clinical histories, with iterative feedback from practicing PAs to ensure clinical relevance. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated tissue classification, anomaly detection algorithms optimized for postmortem artifacts, and quantitative biomarkers linking morphological signatures to molecular autopsy findings. This work aims to augment PA decision-making in complex cases, reduce diagnostic turnaround times, and establish a foundation for data-driven forensic pathology. The HPC infrastructure is critical given the computational demands of multi-scale image analysis and the need for robust generalizability across heterogeneous tissue types and staining protocols. Successful implementation could transform autopsy workflows while advancing the integration of computational pathology into PA education and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a cross-linguistic analysis of narrative structures in 20th-century Francophone and Lusophone African novels, alongside their Arabic and indigenous language literary counterparts. While comparative literary scholarship has long recognized the interplay between colonial languages and local storytelling traditions in these works, existing studies remain limited by manual close-reading methods, which struggle to systematically map stylistic and thematic convergences across vast multilingual corpora. The proposed research addresses this gap by employing computational text analysis to identify patterns in narrative voice, metaphor usage, and temporal representation within a corpus of 500+ novels digitized in French, Portuguese, Arabic, and Bambara. Key computational methods include multilingual sentence embeddings for cross-lingual semantic alignment, transformer-based models for detecting code-switching phenomena, and graph-theoretical approaches to trace character network evolution across texts. These analyses require HPC capabilities due to the scale of parallel processing needed for training language-specific models, the memory-intensive nature of aligning heterogeneous textual representations, and the iterative optimization of comparative metrics across four linguistic systems. Anticipated outcomes include a computational framework for quantifying cross-cultural narrative adaptation, a publicly accessible database of annotated literary features, and new theoretical insights into how postcolonial authors reconfigure European literary forms through indigenous aesthetic practices. By enabling systematic comparisons at unprecedented scale, this project aims to redefine methodological paradigms in multilingual literary studies while contributing open-source tools for computational humanities research in under-resourced languages.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on two or more literary traditions in the original languages or in translation. Includes instruction in comparative linguistics; applicable foreign languages; English/French language and literature; literary criticism; and applications to genre, period, national, and textual studies as well as literary forms such as poetry, prose, and drama.

abstract: Mental health disorders represent a significant global burden, yet their underlying biological and environmental mechanisms remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address critical gaps in psychiatric research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex, multi-modal datasets spanning genomics, neuroimaging, and electronic health records (EHRs). A key challenge in psychiatric research is the integration of heterogeneous data types to identify predictive biomarkers, elucidate disease pathways, and model interactions between genetic risk factors and environmental stressors. Traditional analytical approaches are insufficient for handling the scale and dimensionality of these datasets, which often include millions of genetic variants, high-resolution neuroimaging voxels, and longitudinal clinical outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework combining machine learning, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and network-based neuroimaging analysis to uncover multi-scale patterns in psychiatric disorders such as major depressive disorder and schizophrenia. Custom pipelines will be developed to harmonize EHR-derived symptom trajectories with functional MRI data, while deep learning models will prioritize genetic variants associated with treatment resistance. Large-scale simulations will model gene-environment interactions using agent-based approaches, requiring parallelized computation to iteratively test hypotheses across parameter spaces. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid processing of petabyte-scale datasets, reduce runtime for iterative model training, and support the deployment of containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel transdiagnostic biomarkers, predictive models of treatment response, and mechanistic insights into stress-related neural circuitry. By advancing computational psychiatry, this work aims to bridge the gap between molecular discoveries and clinical applications, ultimately informing personalized intervention strategies. The scalability of the proposed methods will also provide a template for future studies addressing complex psychiatric phenotypes, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational domains.
cip_definition: Research focused on Psychiatric/Mental Health

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing the control and dynamic behavior of autonomous robotic systems operating in unstructured environments. A critical challenge in mechatronics and automation lies in designing robots that can adaptively respond to real-world uncertainties—such as variable terrain, dynamic obstacles, and sensor noise—while maintaining energy efficiency and operational safety. Traditional control strategies and physics-based models often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between electromechanical components, environmental forces, and embedded decision-making algorithms, limiting system reliability. To address this, we propose a multi-physics computational approach integrating rigid-body dynamics, soft-body deformation modeling, and data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) to co-optimize mechanical design parameters and control policies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of simulating distributed sensor-actuator networks, training deep RL agents in parallelized virtual environments, and solving coupled mechanical-electrical-thermal systems at millisecond timescales. The proposed workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated finite element analysis for structural integrity prediction, MPI-based distributed computing for multi-agent collaboration scenarios, and containerized workflows to streamline heterogeneous simulations. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for rapid prototyping of adaptive robotic systems, validated against experimental data from a quadrupedal inspection robot case study. This work will advance the integration of computational mechanics and machine learning in mechatronics, enabling next-generation robots with enhanced autonomy in industrial maintenance and disaster response applications. The requested resources will directly support large-scale parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and validation of probabilistic control frameworks, which are infeasible on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer controlled electro-mechanical systems and products with embedded electronics, sensors, and actuators; and which includes, but is not limited to, automata, robots and automation systems. Includes instruction in mechanical engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, computer and software engineering, and control engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance geoarchaeological research focused on reconstructing human-environment interactions in semi-arid regions during the mid-to-late Holocene. Traditional geoarchaeological methods struggle to integrate multi-scalar datasets—such as sediment micromorphology, geochemical proxies, and high-resolution paleoclimatic models—into cohesive simulations of landscape evolution and anthropogenic impact. The research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework that couples agent-based modeling (ABM) with geospatial machine learning to simulate sediment deposition, erosion, and anthropogenic modification processes across archaeological sites in Anatolia and the Levant. The core challenge lies in resolving the nonlinear feedbacks between localized human activities (e.g., agriculture, settlement construction) and regional hydroclimatic variability at decadal to centennial scales. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of LiDAR-derived topographic data, hyperspectral sediment profiles, and paleoenvironmental proxies (δ¹⁸O, charcoal microparticles) to parameterize stochastic models of site formation and taphonomic alteration. A hybrid approach will be employed, combining finite element methods for sediment transport modeling with graph neural networks to identify spatial-temporal patterns in anthropogenic sediment disturbances. Expected outcomes include the first open-source toolkit for simulating coupled human-landscape dynamics in geoarchaeology, validated against stratigraphic sequences from three key Neolithic-to-Bronze Age sites. The project will generate new hypotheses about thresholds of environmental resilience in early agricultural societies and provide a replicable computational methodology for quantifying uncertainty in paleoenvironmental reconstructions. By bridging geoscience, archaeology, and high-performance computational analytics, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-intensive investigations of long-term human adaptation to environmental stress.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of analytical techniques, concepts, and field methods from the earth sciences to solve archaeological questions related to human settlement, artifacts, site taphonomy, and paleoenvironments. Includes instruction in anthropology, ancient civilizations, archeology, geology, paleoclimatic reconstruction, sedimentology, and site taphonomic research.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the digital reconstruction and predictive conservation of at-risk vernacular architecture in Southeast Asia, a domain that intersects architectural history, computational modeling, and cultural heritage preservation. Traditional methods of documenting and analyzing vernacular structures—such as hand-drawn surveys, photogrammetry, and qualitative risk assessments—struggle to address the scale and complexity of environmental, social, and material degradation faced by these sites. This research proposes a computational framework integrating 3D laser scan datasets, environmental sensor data, and agent-based modeling to simulate multi-decadal decay patterns under varying climate and anthropogenic scenarios. The core challenge lies in processing terabytes of high-resolution spatial data to generate probabilistic models of structural vulnerability while accounting for regional material heterogeneity and informal construction practices. HPC resources are critical for running finite element analysis (FEA) on composite organic materials (e.g., bamboo, thatch, untreated timber) and parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations that test conservation interventions across thousands of stochastic environmental futures. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool for prioritizing conservation efforts, a geolocated database of material performance metrics under tropical conditions, and novel visualizations of temporal decay processes for pedagogical use. By bridging computational engineering methods with humanities-driven conservation ethics, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for safeguarding non-monumental architectural heritage—a chronically understudied yet vital component of cultural memory and community resilience. The project’s computational demands necessitate GPU-accelerated rendering, distributed memory architectures for large-scale spatial analysis, and high-throughput storage for archiving iterative simulation results, all of which exceed the capacity of local institutional infrastructure.
cip_title: Architectural History, Criticism, and Conservation, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural history, criticism, and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing personalized curriculum design through large-scale analysis of learning interactions and educational content. Current approaches to curriculum development often rely on generalized frameworks or static models that inadequately account for the dynamic, nonlinear relationships between instructional materials, learner behaviors, and educational outcomes. The computational complexity of modeling these multidimensional interactions—particularly across diverse student populations and rapidly evolving digital learning environments—exceeds the capabilities of conventional analytical tools. To address this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework to simulate curriculum efficacy under variable conditions. The project will utilize agent-based modeling to represent heterogeneous learner trajectories, coupled with natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze textual and multimodal instructional resources. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of neural networks on longitudinal educational datasets (e.g., student response patterns, engagement metrics, and assessment histories) while maintaining necessary privacy-preserving safeguards. Key computational challenges include optimizing graph-based representations of curricular dependencies and implementing ensemble methods to account for contextual factors in learning sciences. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for evaluating curriculum designs against simulated learner outcomes, 2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive sequencing of instructional content, and 3) open-source tools for visualizing curriculum coherence across learning objectives. This work will provide novel insights into how computational modeling can inform the design of responsive, equity-oriented curricula while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of education research and data science. The requested resources are critical for handling the project's memory-intensive NLP tasks and the concurrent execution of multiple simulation scenarios required for robust validation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the curriculum and related instructional processes and tools, and that may prepare individuals to serve as professional curriculum specialists. Includes instruction in curriculum theory, curriculum design and planning, instructional material design and evaluation, curriculum evaluation, and applications to specific subject matter, programs or educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary study at the intersection of archaeology, computational social science, and digital heritage. The research focuses on reconstructing and simulating social dynamics in ancient urban centers through the integration of fragmented archaeological datasets, including settlement patterns, artifact distributions, and epigraphic records. A persistent challenge in archaeological research is the synthesis of sparse, heterogeneous data to model complex social behaviors such as trade networks, resource allocation, or collective decision-making in pre-literate societies. To address this, we propose a multi-layered computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), spatial network analysis, and machine learning techniques. The ABM component will simulate interactions between households, craft specialists, and regional elites under varying environmental and economic constraints, calibrated using archaeological evidence from the Late Bronze Age Aegean (1600–1100 BCE). Network analysis will map inferred connectivity between settlements based on shared material culture and resource provenance data, while machine learning pipelines will classify artifact assemblages to identify socio-economic stratification patterns. HPC resources are critical for scaling stochastic simulations across plausible parameter spaces, optimizing spatial networks with high-resolution geographic data, and training deep learning models on imbalanced, incomplete datasets. Expected outcomes include novel methodologies for quantifying social complexity in antiquity, open-source tools for integrating archaeological and computational workflows, and empirically grounded insights into how early urban systems balanced cooperation and competition. By bridging archaeological theory with data-driven computational social science, this project aims to demonstrate how HPC can transform the study of past human behavior, offering scalable frameworks applicable to under-documented societies worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of extinct societies, and the past of living societies, via the excavation, analysis and interpretation of their artifactual, human, and associated remains. Includes instruction in archeological theory, field methods, dating methods, conservation and museum studies, cultural and physical evolution, and the study of specific selected past cultures with a focus on the humanistic aspects of archaeology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and optimize scalable algorithms for solving high-dimensional combinatorial optimization problems, with applications in network design, resource distribution, and machine learning model training. Combinatorial optimization lies at the intersection of mathematics and computer science, requiring advanced graph theory, linear algebra, and stochastic methods. Current approaches struggle with scalability in high-dimensional spaces due to exponential growth in computational complexity, limiting their utility in modern data-driven applications. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), quantum-inspired annealing, and distributed gradient-based optimization. This framework will leverage parallelization across high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to manage memory-intensive operations and enable real-time heuristic updates across problem subspaces. Key computational challenges include designing fault-tolerant task distribution protocols, minimizing inter-node communication overhead during stochastic sampling, and implementing adaptive load-balancing for irregular workloads. The project will validate the approach using two case studies: (1) optimizing energy-aware routing in large-scale wireless sensor networks, modeled as a dynamic Steiner tree problem with time-varying constraints, and (2) accelerating hyperparameter optimization for deep reinforcement learning architectures through dimension-aware pruning strategies. Expected outcomes include novel convergence guarantees for hybrid optimization algorithms in high-dimensional spaces, open-source parallel computing libraries for combinatorial mathematics, and quantitative benchmarks comparing classical and quantum-inspired methods on shared memory architectures. Successful implementation will provide mathematical insights into the tractability of NP-hard problems under parallel computation models while delivering practical tools for computational scientists working on optimization-intensive applications. The requested HPC resources are critical for scaling experiments beyond prototype stages, particularly for distributed memory systems handling terabyte-scale graph instances and GPU-accelerated neural architecture search tasks.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and computer science or a specialization which draws from mathematics and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models for optimizing individualized education program (IEP) design in special education settings. A persistent challenge in the field is the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to tailor instructional strategies for students with diverse and intersecting learning needs, particularly in under-resourced schools where manual IEP development strains educator capacity. The research will analyze multi-modal datasets—including longitudinal academic performance records, behavioral observation logs, speech-language therapy transcripts, and assistive technology usage metrics—to identify patterns in effective intervention strategies across neurodevelopmental conditions (e.g., autism spectrum disorder, specific learning disabilities). Using natural language processing and reinforcement learning techniques, the team will train models to simulate student responses to different pedagogical approaches under varying resource constraints. These simulations will inform the creation of an adaptive recommendation system that proposes evidence-based IEP components while accounting for classroom-level variables such as student-teacher ratios and available technologies. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to handle sensitive student data securely within federated learning frameworks, as well as GPU acceleration for real-time optimization of multi-objective models balancing academic progress, social-emotional development, and practical implementation feasibility. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for generating IEP prototypes, validated against historical success metrics from urban and rural school districts. By reducing trial-and-error in intervention design, this work aims to empower special education teachers with AI-assisted planning tools while maintaining human oversight in decision-making. The project will contribute novel methodologies for applying HPC to equity-focused educational challenges, with implications for teacher training programs seeking to integrate computational literacy into special education curricula.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in special education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The dynamics of energy transduction in biological macromolecular complexes remain poorly understood despite their critical role in cellular function. This project seeks to elucidate the mechanistic principles governing energy transfer in two structurally resolved but dynamically uncharacterized systems: a photosynthetic supercomplex from extremophilic algae and a redox-driven transmembrane ATP synthase. A key challenge lies in modeling the interplay between conformational fluctuations, proton-coupled electron transfer, and electrostatic interactions across microsecond-to-millisecond timescales. To address this, we propose an integrated computational strategy leveraging all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enhanced by adaptive sampling algorithms, combined with hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) free energy calculations. The MD simulations will employ explicit solvent models with polarizable force fields to capture dielectric heterogeneity, while the QM/MM framework will parameterize redox potentials and protonation states at critical cofactors. These simulations demand high-performance computing resources due to system sizes exceeding 1.5 million atoms, necessitating sustained multi-node GPU acceleration for achieving sufficient sampling. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of metastable conformational states linked to energy transduction efficiency, (2) quantification of electrostatic coupling between electron transfer chains and rotary ATPase domains, and (3) predictive models for how evolutionary variations in supramolecular architecture optimize energy capture under extreme environmental conditions. The results will advance fundamental understanding of bioenergetic nanomachines while providing a computational framework to guide experimental studies on engineered photosynthetic systems and ATP synthase inhibitors. Successful completion requires dedicated allocation of 250,000 node-hours on a Tier 2 HPC cluster with GPU-optimized architecture, enabling concurrent execution of enhanced sampling trajectories and QM/MM parametric scans.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the dynamics and interactions of macromolecules and other three-dimensional ultrastructures, the architecture of supramolecular structures, and energy transfer in biomolecular systems. Includes instruction in energy transduction, structural dynamics, mechanisms of electron and proton transfer in biological systems, bioinformatics, automated analysis, and specialized research techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of non-perturbative electron correlation effects in multi-electron atomic and molecular systems, a critical challenge in quantum many-body physics. While density functional theory and coupled-cluster methods have provided insights into weakly correlated regimes, systems with strong electron interactions—such as transition-metal complexes, highly charged ions, or molecules in intense laser fields—exhibit emergent phenomena that defy conventional approximations. Current computational approaches struggle to resolve the interplay of dynamic, static, and relativistic correlations at scale, limiting predictive accuracy for spectroscopic properties and reaction dynamics. We propose to develop and apply ab initio variational quantum Monte Carlo (VQMC) methods combined with explicitly correlated basis sets to address these limitations. The research will implement parallelized algorithms for optimizing Jastrow-Slater wavefunctions, enabling systematic treatment of correlation energies while maintaining scalability across distributed-memory architectures. Key innovations include adaptive sampling techniques to reduce stochastic noise in high-dimensional integrals and GPU-accelerated evaluation of relativistic corrections. These methods will be deployed to investigate two paradigmatic systems: (1) the electronic structure of lanthanide atoms, where competing correlation and relativistic effects complicate interpretation of hyperfine splitting measurements, and (2) the time-dependent electron dynamics of diatomic molecules in ultra-short intense laser pulses, probing correlated multielectron responses during non-adiabatic ionization. The requested high-performance computing resources will support large-scale wavefunction optimizations (requiring >10^4 CPU-core hours per system) and real-time propagation simulations with explicit electron-electron terms. Successful execution will yield benchmark-quality data for validating next-generation quantum chemistry models, insights into correlation-driven processes in extreme environments, and open-source computational tools for the atomic physics community. Outcomes are anticipated to impact precision spectroscopy, attosecond science, and the design of correlated quantum materials.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior of matter-energy phenomena at the level of atoms and molecules. Includes instruction in chemical physics, atomic forces and structure, molecular orbital theory, magnetic resonance, molecular bonding, phase equilibria, quantum theory of solids, and applications to the study of specific elements and higher compounds.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic resource allocation in tertiary care hospitals using high-performance computing (HPC) to model real-time operational workflows and predict systemic bottlenecks. Current hospital administration strategies rely on static scheduling and retrospective data, limiting responsiveness to emergent patient influxes, equipment failures, or staff shortages. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to simulate multi-departmental interactions under variable conditions. The model will ingest real-time data streams—including patient triage levels, staff availability, equipment utilization rates, and facility throughput metrics—to generate adaptive resource allocation strategies. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations across parallelized scenarios, enabling rapid evaluation of contingency plans for rare but high-impact events such as mass casualty incidents or supply chain disruptions. Machine learning components will be trained on synthetic datasets generated through these simulations, augmented with historical operational data from partner hospitals. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for administrators to proactively balance competing priorities (e.g., surgical suite utilization vs. emergency department overcrowding) while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory constraints. The project will deliver open-source optimization algorithms tailored for healthcare management, validated against real-world metrics such as patient wait-time reduction and critical resource idle-time minimization. By bridging computational systems engineering and healthcare operations, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven resilience in hospital administration.
cip_title: Hospital and Health Care Facilities Administration/ Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, and other health care facilities. Includes instruction in facilities planning, building and operations management, business management, financial management and insurance, fund-raising and marketing, public relations, human resources management and labor relations, health care facilities operations, principles of health care delivery, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the ecological and molecular drivers of tripartite interactions between entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs), their symbiotic bacteria, and invasive insect vectors under climate-induced thermal stress. EPNs are critical biocontrol agents, but their efficacy varies unpredictably in warming ecosystems, particularly against invasive species like the red imported fire ant (Solenopsis invicta) and Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri). Current models fail to integrate nematode behavioral plasticity, bacterial toxin production dynamics, and host immune responses across temperature gradients, limiting predictive capacity for biocontrol optimization. This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multi-scale simulations that couple 1) agent-based modeling of nematode foraging strategies under thermal constraints, 2) genome-resolved metagenomic analysis of symbiont virulence gene expression, and 3) machine learning-driven predictions of host-pathogen coevolution. Customizable thermal gradient datasets from microcosm experiments (5-40°C) will parameterize stochastic models of nematode-bacteria-insect interactions across >10^6 possible environmental scenarios. Parallelized genomic pipelines will process tera-scale sequencing data from time-series transcriptomics of nematode-bacteria symbioses, identifying thermally sensitive regulatory networks controlling nematode motility and bacterial toxin biosynthesis. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for predicting EPN biocontrol efficiency under climate variability, identification of thermally robust nematode-bacteria partnerships, and actionable metrics for field deployment strategies. The HPC resources are essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of multi-trophic interactions, enabling real-time parameter optimization in 4D ecological models, and processing high-throughput functional genomics data. This work bridges entomology, thermal biology, and computational ecology to address critical gaps in sustainable pest management, with direct applications in agriculture and ecosystem conservation under global change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) and insect species/populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the intersection of legal reasoning and computational pattern recognition within Pre-Law Studies, focusing on the emergent niche of algorithmic modeling of judicial decision-making frameworks. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational tools to systematically evaluate how non-doctrinal factors—such as sociocultural context, rhetorical framing, and temporal trends—influence judicial outcomes in appellate courts. Traditional legal analysis often prioritizes doctrinal coherence, yet emerging scholarship suggests that implicit biases and contextual variables play understudied roles in shaping legal arguments and verdicts. To address this gap, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based analytics to process a corpus of 20th-century U.S. appellate court opinions, dissents, and amicus briefs. Computational methods will include transformer-based models for semantic similarity analysis, community detection algorithms to map citation networks, and temporal clustering to identify shifts in legal reasoning paradigms. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the project aims to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in handling terabyte-scale legal text datasets. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying the impact of non-legal factors on judicial logic, as well as open-source tools to visualize latent patterns in legal argumentation. This research will advance Pre-Law education by providing data-driven pedagogical resources that bridge traditional case law analysis with computational literacy, preparing students to critically engage with increasingly complex, data-rich legal environments. The findings may also inform policy discussions on transparency in judicial decision-making processes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional study of law at the post-baccalaureate level.

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of nonlinear wave propagation in architectured granular crystals, a class of metamaterials with tunable dynamic properties, through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale simulations. Granular systems present unique engineering challenges due to their discrete nature, where macroscopic wave phenomena emerge from complex particle-scale interactions governed by Hertzian contact mechanics, dissipation, and geometric arrangement. Current analytical models struggle to capture the interplay between transient wave localization, energy redistribution, and material disorder across scales—limiting the design of metamaterials for impact mitigation, signal processing, or energy harvesting applications. We propose a hybrid computational framework integrating discrete element method (DEM) simulations of particle ensembles with continuum-level finite element (FEM) wave propagation analysis, bridged by machine learning surrogates trained on HPC-generated datasets. The research will employ GPU-accelerated DEM codes to resolve micromechanical interactions in 3D granular lattices (10^4–10^6 particles) under dynamic loading, coupled with spectral FEM solvers to model emergent wave modes. Machine learning models will then correlate particle-scale parameters (contact stiffness, damping, packing topology) to macroscopic dispersion relationships and attenuation spectra. Sensitivity analysis and topology optimization routines will identify robust designs for target wave manipulation functionalities. The HPC implementation will leverage distributed memory parallelism for large-scale DEM-FEM coupling and automated workflow management across heterogeneous architectures. Expected outcomes include validated multiscale models for granular metamaterial design, open-source simulation tools for wave-structure interaction analysis, and fundamental insights into how mesoscale disorder influences energy transport in discrete media. This work will establish computational strategies to engineer granular systems for next-generation wave control applications while advancing numerical methods for multiscale problems in engineering mechanics.
cip_definition: A program with a general focus on the application of the mathematical and scientific principles of classical mechanics to the analysis and evaluation of the behavior of structures, forces and materials in engineering problems. Includes instruction in statics, kinetics, dynamics, kinematics, celestial mechanics, stress and failure, and electromagnetism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the empirical understanding of dance movement therapy (DMT) by modeling the dynamic interplay between creative movement, neuroanatomical activation, and psychosocial outcomes. Despite growing clinical adoption of DMT, mechanistic insights into how movement patterns influence emotional regulation, cognitive processing, and interpersonal coordination remain understudied due to the complexity of analyzing multidimensional biomechanical, physiological, and behavioral data. Our research integrates motion capture systems, wearable biosensors, and patient-reported outcomes to capture real-time movement signatures during therapeutic interventions. Computational challenges include processing high-resolution kinematic data (500 Hz sampling rates), synchronizing multimodal datasets (motion, EEG, heart rate variability), and training machine learning models to classify movement patterns predictive of therapeutic progress. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of motor control networks using neuroanatomical models, as well as graph-theoretical analyses of group therapy dynamics to quantify emergent social coordination. A key innovation involves developing generative AI models to simulate patient-specific movement trajectories, allowing therapists to predict individualized intervention adjustments. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework linking specific movement qualities (e.g., fluidity, symmetry) to neural activation patterns and emotional states, (2) predictive algorithms for optimizing session plans based on real-time biometric feedback, and (3) open-source tools for quantifying therapeutic alliance through dyadic movement synchrony metrics. By bridging embodied therapeutic practices with computational neuroscience methodologies, this work will establish empirically grounded protocols to enhance DMT efficacy, particularly for populations with motor impairments or trauma-related disorders. The requested resources directly address the computational demands of analyzing terabyte-scale movement datasets while ensuring ethical data governance through encrypted processing pipelines compliant with healthcare privacy standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use the therapeutic application of creative dance movement to assist in promoting client rehabilitation and physical, emotional, and mental health. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, personality development, movement and motor behavior, psychology, dance, creative expression modalities, improvisation, group psychology and leadership, client evaluation and supervision, dance therapy practice, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale literary corpora, advancing methodological innovations in computational literary studies. While traditional close reading remains foundational to literary analysis, the scale and complexity of available digitized texts—spanning centuries, genres, and cultural contexts—present challenges for manual examination. This research addresses the need for scalable, systematic approaches to identify macro-level patterns in literary production, such as shifts in narrative structure, thematic recurrence, or stylistic evolution across time. The primary computational focus involves developing and refining natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to process and analyze heterogeneous literary datasets, including novels, poetry, and drama from the 18th century to the present. Key tasks include training transformer-based models for context-aware semantic analysis, implementing graph-based algorithms to map intertextual networks, and applying unsupervised clustering techniques to detect latent stylistic or thematic groupings. A pilot study on 19th-century British novels demonstrated preliminary success in tracing the diffusion of Gothic tropes, but scaling this to multi-genre, transnational corpora requires HPC capabilities for distributed storage, parallel processing, and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a reusable computational framework for diachronic literary analysis, (2) empirical insights into genre hybridity and canon formation, and (3) public datasets annotated with computational metadata to support reproducibility. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to bridge methodological divides in literary scholarship, offering new tools to interrogate the relationships between form, content, and cultural change at scale. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale text collections, reduce runtime for iterative model training, and facilitate high-dimensional visualization of literary networks—tasks infeasible on standard institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on literature from one or more genres, cultures or traditions. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and studies of various types of literary text.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dialectal variation and historical linguistic shifts in Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian (BSH) languages using advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The research addresses a critical gap in BSH studies: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to systematically map dialect continua, track lexical and morphosyntactic changes across time, and quantify mutual intelligibility between regional varieties. Current methodologies rely heavily on manual analysis of limited text samples, which restricts the scope and reproducibility of findings. To overcome these limitations, we propose training transformer-based language models on a curated corpus of over 10 million words spanning contemporary and historical texts (19th–21st centuries), including novels, newspapers, oral histories, and social media. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing this heterogeneous dataset, which requires distributed training across multiple GPU nodes to handle memory-intensive tasks such as contextual embedding generation and diachronic semantic shift detection. Computational experiments will include dialect classification using attention mechanisms, phonetic alignment of regional speech variants, and graph-based network analysis to model lexical borrowing patterns. The project will also develop open-source tools for low-resource Slavic language processing, including a BSH-specific tokenizer and a web interface for visualizing dialect boundaries. Expected outcomes include new insights into the dynamic interplay between standard languages and regional varieties in post-Yugoslav contexts, with applications in language preservation, educational resource development, and cross-cultural NLP systems.
