By leveraging parallel computing architectures to manage the computational complexity of multilingual and multidialectal modeling, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for computational humanities research in understudied language communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian Languages and Literatures
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bosnian, Serbian and/or Croatian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the empirical understanding of somatic interventions in counseling and applied psychology. While somatic practices such as yoga, Tai Chi, and authentic movement are increasingly integrated into therapeutic settings, the mechanisms underlying their efficacy remain understudied due to the complexity of body-mind interactions and the multidimensional nature of psychological outcomes. Current methodologies lack the capacity to process large-scale, multimodal datasets—including biometric data, motion-capture sequences, and self-reported psychological states—in a unified analytical framework. This research aims to address this gap by developing computational models that quantify the dynamic relationships between somatic practices, physiological responses, and therapeutic outcomes. The project will employ machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks and time-series analysis, to identify patterns in synchronized datasets collected from wearable sensors, video recordings of movement sessions, and participant surveys. High-resolution simulations of body-mind integration processes will be conducted using dynamical systems modeling to explore how specific somatic techniques modulate stress, emotional regulation, and interpersonal attunement. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project will achieve the scalability required to analyze heterogeneous data from diverse participant cohorts. Expected outcomes include the creation of predictive frameworks to optimize somatic intervention protocols for individualized counseling, as well as validated computational tools for assessing body-mind alignment in real time. This work will directly contribute to evidence-based practices in somatic psychology, offering novel insights into how embodied techniques can be systematically tailored to address interpersonal and psychological challenges. The computational infrastructure will also establish a replicable pipeline for future interdisciplinary research at the intersection of movement sciences, biometrics, and applied psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on a holistic approach to solving interpersonal issues and psychological problems. Includes instruction in authentic movement, body-mind balance and integration, contact improvisation, dance, Pilates, Tai Chi, relaxation techniques, and Yoga.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a computational framework to enhance the design and evaluation of competency-based training modules in Trade and Industrial Teacher Education (TITE). A critical challenge in vocational education is ensuring that instructional strategies align with the dynamic technical and pedagogical demands of modern industrial environments. While existing curricula emphasize hands-on skill development, there is a lack of scalable tools to simulate complex trade scenarios, model learner progression, and optimize teaching methods for diverse student cohorts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build adaptive simulation environments and predictive analytics models. The research will focus on three interconnected computational tasks: (1) developing physics-based simulations of industrial tasks (e.g., mechatronic systems troubleshooting, precision machining) using finite element analysis and discrete event modeling; (2) training machine learning classifiers to identify patterns in learner performance data from virtual labs; and (3) implementing multi-agent reinforcement learning systems to model classroom interactions and pedagogical decision-making. These methods require parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale datasets of student interactions, high-fidelity equipment simulations, and stochastic modeling of educational outcomes. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of training scenarios across variables such as class size, skill heterogeneity, and resource availability. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for generating evidence-based teaching recommendations, predictive models of skill acquisition timelines, and optimized virtual training environments that mirror real-world trade workplaces. By computationally bridging the gap between industrial practice and teacher preparation, this work aims to elevate the precision and scalability of vocational educator training while maintaining strict alignment with industry standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational trades and industries programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and optimize the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into administrative workflows, specifically within the context of evolving organizational communication and task management systems. As administrative roles increasingly intersect with AI-driven platforms—such as automated scheduling, intelligent document processing, and real-time multilingual translation—there remains a critical gap in understanding how these tools interact with human decision-making under high-volume, time-sensitive conditions. Traditional studies in Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science have focused on manual or semi-automated workflows, but the computational complexity of modern AI-augmented systems demands advanced simulation and modeling capabilities. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate hybrid human-AI administrative teams, coupled with natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze communication efficiency in multi-stakeholder environments. Large-scale datasets of real-world administrative tasks—including email correspondence, meeting minutes, and workflow logs—will be processed to train probabilistic models predicting bottlenecks in AI-human collaboration. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of over 10,000 workflow permutations, assessing variables such as task urgency, tool reliability, and user adaptability. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying AI tool efficacy in administrative settings, predictive metrics for workflow optimization, and actionable insights into training protocols that bridge technical and interpersonal skill gaps. This work will contribute to the emerging interdisciplinary field of computational organizational support, advancing both theoretical models of human-AI symbiosis and practical strategies for deploying scalable, ethical automation in business environments.
cip_title: Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform the duties of administrative assistants and/or secretaries and stenographers. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, word processing and data entry, office machines operation and maintenance, office procedures, public relations, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the spatial and temporal dynamics of ancient trade networks in the Maya Lowlands, integrating large-scale archaeological datasets with environmental and epigraphic records. Traditional methods struggle to synthesize disparate data types—such as settlement patterns, ceramic distributions, isotopic sourcing, and hieroglyphic trade references—into a unified analytical framework. The research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) and network analyses that simulate trade interactions under variable climatic and socio-political conditions between 300–900 CE. Computational challenges include processing high-resolution LiDAR-derived terrain data, managing uncertainty in artifact provenance, and scaling simulations to regional levels while preserving localized detail. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo iterations to test competing hypotheses about trade route stability, resource access inequities, and the role of elite control versus decentralized exchange. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of latent network structures connecting coastal and inland sites, (2) quantification of climate change impacts on trade resilience, and (3) open-source tools for archaeological network analytics. By bridging computational archaeology and complexity science, this work advances methodological innovation in reconstructing premodern economies while providing empirical insights into how past societies navigated environmental and political risks. The project’s datasets and models will be archived for reuse, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between archaeologists, data scientists, and climate historians. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, geospatial data processing, and machine learning workflows to classify trade-related iconography in digitized artifact corpora, enabling pattern detection at scales unfeasible through manual analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of extinct societies, and the past of living societies, via the excavation, analysis and interpretation of their artifactual, human, and associated remains. Includes instruction in archeological theory, field methods, dating methods, conservation and museum studies, cultural and physical evolution, and the study of specific selected past cultures.

abstract: Dental materials must meet stringent biocompatibility, mechanical, and functional requirements to ensure long-term success in restorative and prosthetic applications. However, the development of next-generation materials is hindered by the complex interplay between microstructural properties, interfacial interactions, and dynamic oral environments, which are difficult to model experimentally. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the multiscale computational design of novel dental composites and bioactive coatings. The research will focus on two primary challenges: (1) predicting the long-term degradation behavior of ceramic-polymer composites under cyclic mechanical loading and enzymatic activity, and (2) optimizing the interfacial bonding between bioactive glass coatings and titanium implant surfaces under simulated physiological conditions. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize atomic-scale interactions at material-tissue interfaces, while finite element analysis will model stress distribution and fatigue failure in heterogeneous composite structures. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to analyze large datasets linking processing parameters to mechanical performance and biological response. The computational workflow will integrate multiphysics models accounting for time-dependent changes in pH, temperature, and salivary composition. By establishing predictive frameworks for material behavior, this work aims to reduce reliance on iterative physical prototyping and accelerate the development of materials with enhanced durability, osseointegration capacity, and resistance to biofilm formation. Outcomes will directly inform the design of patient-specific prostheses and minimally invasive restorations, addressing critical needs in implantology and caries management. The requested HPC resources are essential due to the computational intensity of simulating multiphase systems across relevant spatial (nanometer to millimeter) and temporal (microsecond to year) scales, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of cores. Results will be validated against experimental data from collaborating dental biomaterials laboratories, ensuring translational relevance. This project will advance fundamental understanding of structure-property relationships in dental materials while providing a computational toolkit for data-driven material innovation in oral healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for simulating and visualizing hyperdimensional deformable materials in immersive environments, a challenge at the intersection of computer graphics, applied topology, and materials science. Traditional deformable body simulations are constrained by three-dimensional Euclidean representations, limiting their ability to model complex materials exhibiting non-linear stress-strain relationships or dynamic topological changes, such as self-healing polymers or metamorphic architectural composites. The research problem centers on extending real-time physics-based simulation methods to n-dimensional manifolds while maintaining computational tractability for interactive visualization. The proposed approach combines discrete exterior calculus (DEC) with adaptive mesh refinement techniques to model high-dimensional material behaviors, then projects these dynamics into 3D renderable representations through dimensionally-reduced spectral embeddings. High-performance computing resources are critical for two components: 1) parallel solving of sparse linear systems arising from DEC formulations across irregular meshes, and 2) training neural operators to approximate dimension reduction mappings using gradient-based optimization on manifolds. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for hyperdimensional material simulation and novel rendering pipelines that preserve topological features during dimensional projection. This work will enable new applications in computational material design, medical simulation for multifractal biological tissues, and educational visualization of abstract mathematical structures. The computational demands—particularly memory bandwidth for handling high-dimensional adjacency matrices and GPU acceleration for real-time neural operator inference—necessitate cluster-scale resources with mixed-precision capabilities. Successful implementation will establish foundational methods for bridging abstract mathematical material models with practical computer graphics applications, advancing both simulation science and interactive visualization paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the software, hardware, and mathematical tools used to represent, display, and manipulate topological, two-, and three-dimensional objects on a computer screen and that prepares individuals to function as computer graphics specialists. Includes instruction in graphics software and systems; digital multimedia; graphic design; graphics devices, processors, and standards; attributes and transformations; projections; surface identification and rendering; color theory and application; and applicable geometry and algorithms.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for reconstructing fragmented or degraded cultural heritage artifacts using machine learning and multimodal data fusion. While digital heritage preservation intersects with computer vision and graphics, it remains an under-resourced interdisciplinary niche requiring specialized tools beyond conventional 3D modeling. The primary challenge lies in automating the alignment and semantic interpretation of irregular artifact fragments—often digitized as high-resolution LiDAR scans, spectral images, or crowdsourced photographs—amidst noise, missing regions, and ambiguous geometric features. Existing software frameworks lack adaptive architectures to handle the combinatorial complexity of multi-material artifacts or the integration of non-geometric data (e.g., historical texts, pigment chemistry) critical for context-aware reconstruction. We propose a hybrid graph neural network (GNN) and transformer model optimized for parallel processing, trained on a novel corpus of synthetically degraded artifacts paired with archaeologically validated reconstructions. The workflow will integrate differentiable rendering, physics-based material simulation, and uncertainty quantification to prioritize plausible reconstructions while preserving interpretability for domain experts. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the petascale datasets involved, accelerate hyperparameter optimization across multimodal fusion strategies, and enable real-time interactive refinement of results via a web-based visualization portal. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source pipeline for artifact reconstruction, a benchmark dataset for computational archaeology applications, and new metrics for evaluating preservation authenticity in algorithmic outputs. By bridging gaps between cultural heritage practices and scalable computational infrastructure, this work aims to establish reproducible standards for ethically aligned digital conservation tools while advancing foundational methods in non-Euclidean data processing.
cip_title: Computer Software and Media Applications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer software and media applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of groundwater contaminant transport in heterogeneous geological systems, a critical challenge in environmental geoscience. Current models struggle to resolve fine-scale geological variability and dynamic biogeochemical interactions at watershed scales, limiting their utility for informing sustainable resource management and remediation strategies. We propose to develop a coupled hydrogeochemical simulation framework integrating high-resolution geological datasets, fluid flow dynamics, and reactive transport processes. The computational approach will utilize parallelized finite element methods to solve 3D multiphase flow equations, coupled with machine learning-assisted parameterization of spatially variable hydraulic and geochemical properties derived from field measurements. Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in contaminant dispersal under varying climate and land-use scenarios. The HPC environment is essential for managing the computational intensity of these multiscale, stochastic simulations, which require iterative runs across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 combinations. Anticipated outcomes include improved predictive capacity for contaminant migration timelines, identification of high-risk zones in aquifer systems, and optimized mitigation strategies for stakeholders. This work directly addresses gaps in environmental policy implementation by providing scalable tools to assess compliance with groundwater quality standards under evolving regulatory frameworks. By elucidating links between subsurface heterogeneity and contaminant persistence, the project will contribute foundational insights into sustainable water resource management while advancing computational methodologies for geoscience applications. The requested resources will support the parallel processing and large memory allocation needed to achieve spatiotemporal resolutions necessary for actionable decision-making at the interface of geological processes and human environmental impacts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the environmental implications of geological processes and human activities on Earth. Includes instruction in environmental/natural resource management, geographic information systems (GIS), geology, hydrology, regulatory agency compliance, hazard identification and mitigation, environmental law, environmental policy, and sustainability studies.

abstract: Congenital anomalies of the genitourinary tract represent a leading cause of pediatric morbidity, with surgical outcomes varying significantly due to anatomical complexity, heterogeneity in disease presentation, and limited predictive models for postoperative complications. Current clinical decision-making relies on retrospective analyses and population-level data, which inadequately address individual patient variability. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating patient-specific anatomical modeling, longitudinal clinical data, and biomechanical simulations to predict surgical outcomes and optimize intervention strategies for children with complex urological conditions, including posterior urethral valves, bladder exstrophy, and neurogenic bladder. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process high-resolution imaging data (MRI/CT) to construct 3D organ reconstructions, simulate tissue biomechanics under surgical modification scenarios, and train machine learning models on multi-modal datasets encompassing genomic, urodynamic, and long-term follow-up data. Computational workflows will parallelize finite element analysis for tissue stress-strain modeling and employ deep learning architectures to identify prognostic biomarkers from imaging and electronic health records. The scale of data—terabytes of imaging, thousands of patient trajectories, and iterative simulation testing—necessitates HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime and storage. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for postoperative renal function, bladder capacity, and complication risks, validated against a prospective cohort of 200 patients. This work will establish a paradigm for precision surgical planning in pediatric urology, reducing revision surgeries and improving quality of life. By open-sourcing validated models, we aim to catalyze collaborative innovation in pediatric surgical research while addressing critical gaps in data-driven care standards for rare congenital anomalies.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals in the study, prevention, and management of congenital, childhood-acquired, and overlapping adolescent anomalies of the genitourinary tract, including problems, diseases, tumors, and traumas.

abstract: The increasing complexity of air transportation systems demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in airspace management, flight efficiency, and environmental sustainability. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing dynamic air traffic flow management (ATFM) under stochastic operational constraints, including weather disruptions, variable demand, and evolving emissions regulations. Current ATFM models struggle to balance real-time adaptability with computational tractability, particularly when scaling to continental airspace networks. To overcome these limitations, the proposed research will implement a hybrid computational architecture combining agent-based modeling, graph neural networks (GNNs), and multi-objective reinforcement learning. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training GNNs on historical flight trajectory datasets (10+ TB), running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of weather-impact scenarios, and solving fleet-level optimization problems with 10^6+ decision variables. The framework will integrate real-time data streams from ADS-B, weather satellites, and airline scheduling systems through a distributed memory paradigm. Key innovations include a physics-informed machine learning layer to predict sector congestion under convective weather and a carbon-aware routing module that minimizes contrail formation alongside fuel burn. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms capable of reducing average flight delays by 15-20% in simulated National Airspace System stress scenarios, (2) quantitative trade-off analyses between fuel efficiency and climate impacts, and (3) open-source tools for air traffic management stakeholders. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance decision-support systems for next-generation aviation infrastructure while providing a template for large-scale transportation network optimization. The computational requirements necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory CPUs for running 1000+ concurrent simulation instances during parameter sensitivity studies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in aviation and air transportation services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on the historical evolution and regional variation of the Polish language. The primary research problem centers on analyzing large-scale textual corpora spanning six centuries (14th–20th centuries) to trace phonological, morphological, and lexical changes across Polish dialects. Traditional manual methods for dialectology and philological analysis struggle to process the scale and complexity of these datasets, which include digitized manuscripts, printed texts, and transcribed oral histories from regional archives. Our computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted for historical Polish with machine learning models to identify patterns of linguistic change. Key tasks include developing a unified pipeline for automated morphological tagging of archaic and dialectal forms, training transformer-based models on historical texts to detect semantic shifts, and implementing geospatial clustering algorithms to map regional linguistic features. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of unstructured text data, running parallelized comparative analyses across temporal and geographic dimensions, and training domain-specific language models. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Polish dialect evolution, quantitative models of language contact effects between Polish and neighboring languages, and open-access tools for computational historical linguistics. This research will significantly enhance understanding of Polish language development while providing methodological frameworks applicable to other under-resourced Slavic languages. The computational resources requested will directly support the creation of publicly available datasets and models, fostering collaboration across linguistics, digital humanities, and cultural heritage preservation initiatives.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing precision agriculture technologies, with a focus on algorithmic decision-making systems in farming operations. As advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), sensor networks, and automated machinery reshape agricultural practices, legal doctrines addressing liability, data ownership, and environmental compliance face unprecedented challenges. The project aims to systematically model interactions between heterogeneous legal domains—including intellectual property, tort law, and environmental regulations—and computationally intensive agricultural systems. By developing agent-based simulations of farm operations under varying regulatory regimes, the research will quantify how legal uncertainty impacts the adoption rates of precision agriculture technologies. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be deployed to analyze case law, policy documents, and contractual agreements across jurisdictions, identifying emergent patterns in liability disputes and regulatory enforcement. Graph neural networks will map the interdependencies between multi-scale legal constraints (local, national, international) and technology diffusion pathways. The computational framework will integrate stochastic optimization models to propose adaptive policy mechanisms capable of balancing innovation incentives with environmental and equity concerns. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated legal corpora specific to agricultural technology, predictive models of litigation risk for AI-driven farming systems, and scenario analyses informing the design of interoperable regulatory standards. By bridging computational social science methodologies with legal informatics, this project addresses a critical gap in governance strategies for 21st-century agricultural systems while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources in non-traditional, policy-relevant research domains.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in food and agriculture.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in modern manufacturing quality control by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models for real-time defect detection and process optimization. Traditional quality control systems often struggle to manage the growing complexity of multi-stage production environments, where high-dimensional sensor data, material variability, and dynamic operating conditions create bottlenecks in defect identification and root-cause analysis. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) with physics-based simulations. The first phase will employ HPC resources to train ensemble ML models on terabyte-scale datasets of historical production metrics, inline sensor readings, and non-destructive testing imagery. Parallelized finite element analysis simulations will concurrently model stress distributions, thermal effects, and material behaviors under diverse manufacturing scenarios. In the second phase, these components will be coupled via surrogate modeling techniques to enable adaptive real-time quality prediction. The computational workflow will optimize statistical process control algorithms through distributed parameter sweeps, evaluating millions of potential control strategies under uncertainty quantification frameworks. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive quality monitoring system capable of identifying substandard components with 99.5% accuracy at production-line speeds, reducing material waste by an estimated 15-20% in target aerospace composite manufacturing use cases. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing memory-intensive simulation ensembles and enabling rapid retraining of ML models as production environments evolve. This work will provide an open-source computational toolkit to help small and medium manufacturers adopt AI-driven quality control systems, advancing the broader integration of smart manufacturing technologies while maintaining rigorous compliance with international quality standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining consistent manufacturing and construction standards. Includes instruction in quality control systems management principles, technical standards applicable to specific engineering and manufacturing projects, testing procedures, inspection procedures, related instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets of classroom interactions and instructional practices in STEM teacher education. A critical challenge in teacher professional development is the lack of scalable tools to evaluate how novice educators implement evidence-based pedagogical strategies in real-world settings. Current manual observation protocols are resource-intensive and fail to capture longitudinal patterns across diverse teaching contexts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model video recordings, audio transcripts, and digital lesson artifacts from 500+ classroom sessions involving pre-service science and mathematics teachers. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to automatically code instructional moves (e.g., questioning techniques, formative assessment practices) using transformer-based NLP models and computer vision algorithms trained on established observation rubrics. Graph neural networks will then analyze temporal relationships between teaching behaviors and student engagement metrics derived from multimodal signals. The computational demands of processing 40+ terabytes of video data, training domain-specific large language models on educational discourse, and running iterative simulations of pedagogical scenario outcomes necessitate GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed storage systems. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for automated teacher practice analysis, 2) evidence-based insights into high-leverage teaching competencies that predict early-career effectiveness, and 3) synthetic training modules generated through agent-based modeling of classroom dynamics. By enabling unprecedented scalability in pedagogical analytics, this work aims to transform how teacher preparation programs diagnose skill gaps and personalize professional learning trajectories, ultimately strengthening STEM instruction in secondary education.
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Subject Areas, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education, specific academic and vocational programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The genetic architecture of complex traits in domesticated and wild animal populations remains poorly understood, particularly regarding the interplay between regulatory variation, epigenetic modification, and selection history. This project seeks to address critical gaps in characterizing non-coding regulatory elements influencing production traits in livestock species and adaptive variation in endangered populations, using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in data integration and evolutionary genomics. Our research will develop novel computational workflows to analyze whole-genome sequencing, chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and histone modification data from cattle (Bos taurus) and threatened wolf populations (Canis lupus), integrating these multi-omics datasets with phased haplotype information and ancient DNA references. Key computational challenges include implementing graph-based genome representations for structural variant analysis, training deep learning models to predict enhancer-promoter interactions across tissues, and performing phylogenetically aware scans for convergent selection signals. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these analyses across terabase-scale datasets, enabling comparative chromatin state annotation in 12 tissues, demographic inference under complex migration models, and Bayesian estimation of selection coefficients. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of conserved regulatory modules underlying milk production traits in bovids, 2) characterization of epigenetic adaptation signatures in wolves recolonizing human-modified habitats, and 3) open-source pipelines for joint analysis of selective sweeps and regulatory evolution. This work will directly inform precision breeding strategies while advancing conservation genomics methodologies, bridging a critical gap between molecular quantitative genetics and population-level evolutionary processes. The requested resources will support containerized workflow execution, large-memory genome assembly tasks, and GPU-accelerated neural network training, substantially accelerating discovery in non-model animal systems where genetic improvement and adaptive potential are urgent agricultural and ecological concerns.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of multicellular animal life forms from the experimental, comparative, and clinical (veterinary and medical) viewpoints. Includes instruction in molecular genetics, gene expression, gene regulation, genomics, epigenetic phenomena, DNA recombination and repair, genetic interactions at the microbial and higher levels, and molecular evolution.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and analyze large-scale simulations of classroom dynamics across multiple educational levels (K-12), with the goal of identifying instructional strategies that optimize student engagement and learning outcomes in diverse, multi-age educational settings. A critical challenge in teacher education is preparing educators to adapt pedagogical techniques to varying developmental stages, particularly in classrooms or programs that serve students spanning early childhood through adolescence. Current research lacks computational models that integrate behavioral, cognitive, and socio-emotional data across age groups to test hypothetical teaching approaches in silico. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling framework that simulates teacher-student interactions under varying curricular structures, classroom compositions, and instructional methods. The model will incorporate empirical data from classroom observations, student performance metrics, and developmental psychology studies to parameterize agents representing teachers and learners. HPC resources are essential to run thousands of parallelized simulations, systematically varying parameters such as class size, age distribution, lesson pacing, and feedback mechanisms. Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to detect patterns in effective cross-level teaching practices. Expected outcomes include evidence-based guidelines for designing teacher training modules that emphasize flexibility in instructional delivery, differentiation strategies, and real-time decision-making in heterogeneous classrooms. By quantifying how specific pedagogical choices propagate across student subgroups, this work aims to advance the preparation of educators for multi-level teaching contexts while providing a scalable computational toolkit for iterative, data-driven improvements in teacher education programs.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at more than one educational level, such as a combined program in elementary/secondary, early childhood/elementary, elementary/middle school, or junior high/high school teacher education.

abstract: The emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens underscores the urgent need to elucidate mechanisms of host-pathogen interaction and immune evasion. This project seeks to investigate the molecular basis of Clostridioides difficile virulence and host immune recognition using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. C. difficile infection (CDI) causes severe gastrointestinal disease, yet the structural dynamics of its toxin-mediated disruption of intestinal epithelial barriers and concurrent modulation of host T-cell responses remain poorly characterized. We propose to integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of toxin-receptor binding, agent-based modeling of immune cell signaling, and comparative genomic analyses of hypervirulent C. difficile strains. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of toxin B (TcdB) interactions with host Frizzled receptors, leveraging cryo-EM structural data to model conformational changes during receptor engagement. Concurrently, spatial stochastic models will simulate neutrophil and T-cell recruitment dynamics in response to toxin-induced tissue damage, incorporating single-cell RNA-seq data from murine CDI models. These computational workflows will be validated through iterative collaboration with experimental labs performing mutagenesis and functional assays. Expected outcomes include identifying critical residues in TcdB responsible for immune evasion, mapping signaling nodes that regulate ineffective anti-CD4+ T-cell responses, and stratifying strain-specific virulence factors. By bridging microbial pathogenesis and immunology through multiscale computational modeling, this work will advance targeted therapeutic strategies, including toxoid vaccines and host-directed immunomodulators. The scale of these simulations—requiring millions of core-hours for ensemble sampling of flexible toxin domains and stochastic immune population modeling—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve biologically relevant timescales and system sizes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microorganisms that cause disease and the host immune response to them. Includes instruction in microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, pathogenic bacteriology, disease mechanisms, immunology, immunogenetics, autoimmunity, and bioinformatics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing water supply systems through advanced computational modeling, with a focus on improving the efficiency, sustainability, and resilience of plumbing infrastructure in urban environments. Aging water supply networks, increasing demand due to population growth, and climate-induced stressors such as fluctuating water availability and pipe corrosion necessitate innovative approaches to system design and maintenance. Traditional empirical methods for analyzing fluid dynamics, pipe material degradation, and network performance lack the resolution to account for complex, interdependent variables at scale. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning, and network optimization algorithms. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate transient flow behaviors, pressure fluctuations, and sediment transport in piping systems under varying operational conditions, while coupled corrosion models will assess material degradation rates based on water chemistry and environmental factors. Machine learning techniques will analyze historical failure data and real-time sensor inputs to predict vulnerabilities and prioritize maintenance interventions. Agent-based modeling will further evaluate the impact of user behavior on water demand patterns. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources to achieve the spatial and temporal resolution necessary for actionable insights, particularly when scaling from individual building systems to municipal networks. The outcomes will include predictive tools for optimizing pipe material selection, reducing non-revenue water losses, and extending infrastructure lifespans. This work is expected to advance the field of plumbing and water supply services by providing a scalable, data-driven framework for infrastructure planning, directly contributing to sustainable urban development goals. Collaboration with municipal water authorities and plumbing engineering firms will ensure practical validation and deployment of the models, bridging gaps between academic research and industry application.
cip_title: Plumbing and Related Water Supply Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plumbing and related water supply services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate decision-making processes in asymmetric hybrid warfare scenarios, where traditional kinetic operations intersect with cyber, information, and psychological domains. The increasing complexity of modern conflicts—characterized by rapid information dissemination, decentralized command structures, and adaptive adversarial tactics—requires advanced tools to evaluate the cascading effects of multi-domain interventions. Current analytical models lack the dynamic resolution to account for real-time feedback loops between physical operations, digital infrastructure disruptions, and sociocultural perception shifts. To address this gap, the project proposes a hybrid agent-based and system dynamics model leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational architecture will integrate heterogeneous agents (military units, civilian populations, cyber networks) with probabilistic threat propagation algorithms and natural language processing modules to simulate adversarial influence campaigns. Large-scale parameter sweeps will assess resilience thresholds across varying operational tempos and resource constraints, while machine learning components will identify emergent patterns in simulated escalation pathways. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for evaluating trade-offs between preemptive actions, countermessaging strategies, and infrastructure hardening measures in contested environments. By enabling parallelized scenario testing at unprecedented granularity, this work aims to advance decision-support capabilities for planners operating in dynamically evolving threat landscapes. The computational demands of modeling millions of agent interactions across coupled physical-digital domains necessitate access to distributed memory systems and GPU-accelerated analytics frameworks, which form the basis of this resource allocation request.
cip_title: Military Technologies and Applied Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military technologies and applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The pulp and paper industry faces significant challenges in optimizing energy efficiency and reducing environmental impact during manufacturing processes, particularly in pulping, bleaching, and fiber network formation. Current experimental approaches to improve these processes are limited by the cost and scalability of physical trials, while existing computational models lack the resolution to capture multiscale interactions between chemical reactions, fluid dynamics, and fiber morphology. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity simulations of key papermaking processes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to bridge this gap. The research will employ multiphysics modeling techniques, integrating molecular dynamics (MD) to study lignin-cellulose interactions during pulping, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to analyze fiber suspension flows in headboxes, and finite element analysis (FEA) to predict mechanical properties of paper sheets under varying coating formulations. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to accelerate parameter optimization across these models. Simulations will be validated against experimental data from laboratory-scale pulping reactors and pilot paper machines. The computational demands of resolving nanoscale fiber surface chemistry while maintaining macroscale process flows necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with parallelized solvers and large memory nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive models for energy-efficient pulping conditions, optimized coating formulations to reduce material waste, and a framework for virtual testing of novel fiber modification strategies. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing carbon emissions in paper manufacturing while maintaining product performance, addressing critical sustainability goals. The resulting open-source simulation tools will advance computational capabilities in paper science, enabling future research into bio-based materials and circular economy solutions for the industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and manufacturing of pulp and paper products. Includes instruction in pulp and paper science, pulping and bleaching processes, paper structure and processes, pulp and paper manufacturing, coating technology, surface and colloid science, and fibers.

abstract: The growing complexity of immunologic diseases, such as autoimmune disorders and transplant rejection, demands advanced computational frameworks to decipher multi-dimensional data and optimize therapeutic strategies. Current limitations in analyzing high-throughput genomic, proteomic, and clinical datasets hinder the identification of robust biomarkers and predictive models for patient-specific immunotherapy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrated computational platform for analyzing immune system dynamics, treatment responses, and molecular heterogeneity in immunopathology. The research will focus on three aims: (1) constructing predictive models of immune cell interactions and cytokine networks in autoimmune diseases using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics data, (2) simulating host-pathogen dynamics in post-transplant infections to optimize immunosuppressive regimens, and (3) applying deep learning to histopathology images and flow cytometry data to refine diagnostic classification of immune-mediated diseases. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian network inference, agent-based modeling, and convolutional neural networks, requiring parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps for model optimization, real-time integration of multi-omics data from collaborating clinical sites, and validation against longitudinal patient outcomes. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets for rheumatoid arthritis and lupus, predictive algorithms for graft-versus-host disease risk stratification, and a cloud-accessible toolset for clinical pathologists to interpret complex immune profiles. By bridging computational immunology with translational medicine, this work aims to accelerate the development of precision immunotherapy protocols while reducing reliance on trial-and-error treatment approaches. The requested resources will directly support 8 active clinical trials and 15 collaborative studies on immune dysregulation, advancing both mechanistic understanding and patient care in immunopathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment and laboratory management of immunologic diseases. Includes instruction in diagnostic surgical pathology, management of organ transplantation and immunotherapy.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in human-centric text composition workflows by investigating adaptive, context-aware word processing systems optimized for cognitive ergonomics. Traditional word processors employ static interfaces and linear input models, which fail to account for individual differences in user behavior, such as variable typing rhythms, task-switching patterns, or context-dependent error profiles. We propose a computational framework that leverages real-time biometric feedback (keystroke dynamics, eye tracking, and EEG-derived cognitive load metrics) to dynamically reconfigure interface elements, predictive text suggestions, and error correction algorithms. The research will employ high-performance computing resources to train multimodal transformer architectures on a novel corpus combining text entry logs, physiological sensor data, and document semantic structures from 10,000+ writing sessions. Computational challenges include parallel processing of heterogeneous temporal data streams at millisecond resolution and maintaining low-latency inference for real-time interface adaptations across GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated cognitive efficiency metric quantifying the relationship between interface adaptations and writing quality/productivity, (2) open-source libraries for resource-optimized biodynamic typing analysis, and (3) prototype architectures demonstrating ≥40% reduction in cognitive load metrics compared to conventional word processors. This work bridges human-computer interaction, psycholinguistics, and distributed systems engineering to pioneer a new paradigm in writing assistance technologies, with particular significance for accessibility applications and high-stakes professional writing environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in medical office administration by developing computational tools to optimize patient scheduling, electronic health record (EHR) management, and workflow prioritization in clinical environments. Medical offices face growing challenges due to increasing patient volumes, complex insurance protocols, and fragmented data systems, leading to delays, errors, and staff burnout. While existing software solutions provide partial support, they often lack adaptive capabilities to handle dynamic, context-sensitive scenarios common in multi-specialty practices. This research proposes a machine learning (ML) framework to analyze historical and real-time operational data—including appointment patterns, EHR metadata, and staff interaction logs—to model and predict workflow bottlenecks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training deep reinforcement learning models on large-scale, heterogeneous datasets spanning anonymized patient records, administrative metadata, and temporal variables (e.g., seasonal demand shifts). The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing to extract unstructured data from clinical notes and insurance documents, coupled with simulation tools to test scheduling policies under diverse scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating personalized workflow recommendations, reducing no-show rates via predictive patient reminders, and automating prior authorization tasks. By leveraging HPC to process millions of simulated scheduling permutations and EHR interactions, this work aims to provide scalable solutions that enhance operational efficiency while maintaining compliance with healthcare privacy standards. Results will directly inform curriculum updates for medical office assistant training programs, emphasizing data-driven decision-making in healthcare administration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers and other professionals, to perform routine administrative duties in a medical, clinical, or health care facility/system office environment. Includes instruction in general office skills, data processing, office equipment operation, principles of medical record-keeping and business regulations, medical/clinical office procedures, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in predictive modeling of radioactive material dispersion in complex environments, a challenge central to radiation safety protocols and emergency response planning. Current models often rely on simplified atmospheric and topographical assumptions, limiting their accuracy in real-world scenarios such as urban settings, uneven terrain, or mixed indoor-outdoor contamination events. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity computational framework that integrates 3D radiation transport simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven uncertainty quantification. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute parallelized Monte Carlo N-Particle (MCNP) simulations coupled with weather-resolved CFD models, enabling millimeter-scale resolution of particle deposition patterns under diverse environmental conditions. A key innovation involves training neural networks on simulated and historical contamination datasets to predict radiation field evolution in near-real time, accounting for dynamic variables such as wind shear, precipitation, and structural shielding effects. The computational workload necessitates large-scale GPU-accelerated nodes for particle transport calculations and distributed memory clusters for ensemble modeling of probabilistic exposure scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit validated against experimental data from radioisotope tracer studies, which will directly inform improvements in radioactive waste storage guidelines, decontamination workflow optimization, and technician training modules for radiation field mapping. By bridging the gap between theoretical health physics principles and practical computational decision support, this work aims to establish new best practices for radiation risk assessment in occupational and environmental settings while enhancing the technical capabilities of future radiation protection professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health physicists, occupational safety and health specialists, and public health officials, to monitor and control radiation exposure and implement preventive measures in health care, work, and natural environments. Includes instruction in radiation physics, environmental radioactivity, radiological instrumentation, electronics of radiation detection equipment, radioactive waste management and control, safety and handling procedures, decontamination procedures, radioactivity testing and analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in dermatology by analyzing complex, multi-modal datasets to elucidate mechanisms underlying inflammatory skin diseases, such as atopic dermatitis and psoriasis. Despite advances in targeted therapies, disease heterogeneity and incomplete understanding of molecular drivers limit treatment efficacy. Our research addresses this gap by integrating genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and microbiome data from patient cohorts to identify disease endotypes and predictive biomarkers. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional datasets (whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics) and modeling non-linear interactions between genetic variants, immune pathways, and microbial communities. We will develop machine learning pipelines to cluster patients by molecular profiles, prioritize causal pathways via network analysis, and predict therapeutic responses using neural networks. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across terabytes of data, optimizing hyperparameters in combinatorial search spaces, and running ensemble models to ensure robustness. Additionally, we will simulate skin barrier dynamics via finite element modeling to assess how genetic variants in filaggrin and other structural proteins influence biomechanical properties and disease susceptibility. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel therapeutic targets, stratification biomarkers for clinical trials, and open-source tools for dermatological data integration. This work will provide a computational framework for translating multi-omics insights into personalized treatment strategies, directly addressing unmet needs in managing chronic, relapsing skin diseases. By coupling scalable analytics with clinical datasets, the project aims to accelerate innovation in diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for diverse patient populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on diseases of the skin, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May also include research on dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, sexually transmitted diseases, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the impacts of climate change and anthropogenic stressors on critical watershed systems, with a focus on predicting future water availability and ecosystem health. The research addresses a pressing gap in regional-scale conservation planning: the integration of dynamic hydrological, biogeochemical, and socioecological data into unified predictive frameworks. Current models often oversimplify interactions between snowpack dynamics, groundwater recharge, land-use changes, and aquatic biodiversity, limiting their utility for adaptive management. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-model coupling approach that combines a high-resolution hydrologic model (WRF-Hydro) with machine learning algorithms trained on historical and projected climate data (CMIP6), remote sensing-derived land cover maps, and in-situ water quality measurements. The computational workflow will require parallel processing to manage large spatiotemporal datasets (10+ TB) spanning multiple decades at 100m spatial resolution, with iterative parameter optimization to account for regional variability in soil permeability, vegetation cover, and precipitation patterns. By simulating thousands of scenarios under varying climate trajectories and management policies, this work will quantify trade-offs between water allocation for human use, riparian habitat preservation, and long-term watershed resilience. Expected outcomes include publicly accessible risk maps identifying priority zones for conservation easements, predictive metrics for aquatic species vulnerability, and decision-support tools for balancing ecological and agricultural water demands. The HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary scale and resolution for actionable insights, as local hydrologic responses to global change exhibit nonlinear behaviors that cannot be captured through conventional modeling approaches. Results will directly inform state and tribal natural resource agencies in their efforts to mitigate biodiversity loss while maintaining water security in rapidly changing environments.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the studies and activities relating to the natural environment and its conservation, use, and improvement. Includes instruction in subjects such as climate, air, soil, water, land, fish and wildlife, and plant resources; in the basic principles of environmental science and natural resources management; and the recreational and economic uses of renewable and nonrenewable natural resources.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions of polyherbal Ayurvedic formulations, a critical yet underexplored area in integrative health sciences. Ayurvedic medicine employs complex herbal synergies, but the absence of mechanistic data on multi-compound interactions limits evidence-based validation and global integration. Traditional reductionist approaches struggle to address the combinatorial complexity of these formulations, which may involve hundreds of bioactive compounds acting on multiple biological targets. We propose a computational systems biology framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning-driven network pharmacology, and quantum chemical calculations to map compound-target-pathway relationships in three classical Ayurvedic formulations (Triphala, Ashwagandharishta, and Brahma Rasayana). Molecular docking simulations will prioritize ligand-receptor interactions using GPU-accelerated algorithms, while ensemble-based free energy perturbation methods will quantify binding affinities. Concurrently, generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on phytochemical databases will predict novel synergistic combinations. A multi-omics layer incorporating metabolomic and transcriptomic data from ongoing in vitro studies will validate computational predictions of anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the scale of these simulations, which involve ~10^6 compound-target pairs and require parallelized workflows across CPU-GPU architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of herb-herb interaction mechanisms, (2) identification of lead compounds for downstream experimental validation, and (3) an open-access database correlating Ayurvedic therapeutic claims with computational biomarker profiles. By bridging ancient empirical knowledge with modern computational biology, this work aims to establish a quantitative framework for evaluating traditional pharmacopeias, potentially informing personalized Ayurvedic treatment protocols while addressing safety and efficacy concerns critical to interdisciplinary healthcare integration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize blasting efficiency and ore fragmentation in open-pit mining operations, addressing a critical gap in current mineral extraction systems. Fragmentation outcomes directly influence downstream processing costs, energy consumption, and environmental impacts, yet existing predictive tools struggle to account for the complex interplay of rock heterogeneity, blast design parameters, and dynamic fracture propagation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework integrating discrete element modeling (DEM), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve 3D rock mass structures at millimeter-scale resolution while capturing mine-scale blast dynamics, requiring parallelized simulations across millions of particles and fluid cells. The DEM module will simulate fracture initiation and propagation in heterogeneous ore bodies using GPU-accelerated contact mechanics algorithms, while CFD models track dust dispersion and gas flow interactions. ML surrogate models, trained on simulation outputs and sensor data from field trials, will identify optimal blast patterns that balance fragmentation targets with minimized energy use and environmental footprint. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin system capable of predicting fragmentation distributions with <15% error relative to optical sizing measurements, reducing processing energy intensity by an estimated 20-30%. The computational toolkit will enable real-time adjustment of blasting parameters based on geologic variability, advancing sustainable mining practices through reduced waste and emissions. Successful implementation requires access to HPC clusters with dedicated GPU nodes for DEM-CFD coupling and distributed memory architectures for ensemble ML training. This work directly supports national priorities for resource-efficient mineral extraction and aligns with industry roadmaps for decarbonizing mining operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of mineral extraction, processing and refining systems, including open pit and shaft mines, prospecting and site analysis equipment and instruments, environmental and safety systems, mine equipment and facilities, mineral processing and refining methods and systems, and logistics and communications systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in the creation and analysis of large-scale generative visual art. Generative methods in visual arts increasingly rely on iterative, data-driven processes—such as neural style transfer, 3D procedural modeling, and agent-based simulation—to produce complex, dynamic artworks. However, scaling these techniques to high-resolution formats or real-time interactive installations requires significant computational power beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The project focuses on optimizing generative algorithms for parallel processing, enabling the synthesis of ultra-high-definition visual outputs (e.g., 8K+ resolution) and the integration of real-time viewer interaction data into evolving artworks. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated training of custom generative adversarial networks (GANs) tailored to artistic datasets, distributed rendering of fractal-based 3D environments, and agent-based simulations modeling emergent visual patterns. A key innovation involves coupling these methods with motion-capture data streams to create responsive installations that adapt to audience movement. Outcomes will advance methodological frameworks for computationally intensive art practices, reduce latency in interactive systems, and enable the production of artworks at unprecedented scales. The research will also contribute open-source tools for artists working with HPC infrastructure, bridging gaps between technical scalability and creative intent. By demonstrating how advanced computing resources can expand the boundaries of generative art, this project aims to establish new interdisciplinary benchmarks for computational creativity while addressing practical challenges in rendering, interactivity, and data synthesis unique to visual arts research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the visual and performing arts and that may prepare individuals in any of the visual artistic media or performing disciplines.

abstract: The translational gap between preclinical animal studies and human clinical outcomes remains a critical challenge in biomedical research, with high failure rates in drug development often attributed to interspecies physiological differences and limitations in conventional experimental designs. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that improve the predictive validity of laboratory animal studies, specifically focusing on murine and porcine models of cardiovascular disease and metabolic disorders. By integrating multi-omics datasets (genomics, proteomics, metabolomics) with high-resolution physiological monitoring data, we aim to construct species-specific digital twins capable of simulating disease progression and therapeutic responses under varying genetic and environmental conditions. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms to identify conserved pathways across species, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate cellular and molecular interactions within tissue microenvironments. A parallel focus will optimize experimental design through in silico trials, reducing animal use while maintaining statistical power. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing petascale datasets from next-generation sequencing, dynamic imaging, and real-time biosensor outputs, as well as for running computationally intensive simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks to prioritize translational animal models for specific disease contexts, (2) open-access algorithms for cross-species data harmonization, and (3) validated protocols for virtual cohort generation to minimize redundant animal trials. This work directly addresses NIH priorities for refining animal research and aligns with AAALAC’s emphasis on computational alternatives in laboratory animal science. By establishing quantitative links between model organism biology and human pathobiology, the project will enhance the ethical and scientific value of comparative medical research while providing training in computational approaches for veterinary scientists.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) by modeling and simulating complex, large-scale interactions between users and emerging technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and AI-driven adaptive interfaces. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how these technologies influence collective human behavior, cognitive load, and social dynamics in real-world scenarios. Current methods for analyzing such interactions are constrained by the scale of data, the need for real-time processing of multimodal inputs (e.g., eye tracking, gesture recognition, physiological sensors), and the computational demands of simulating diverse user populations. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and immersive environment simulations. Agent-based models will represent heterogeneous user behaviors and decision-making patterns derived from empirical studies in cognitive psychology and sociology. Deep learning techniques will process multimodal interaction data to predict user responses and adapt system interfaces dynamically. Large-scale simulations will replicate socio-technical ecosystems, enabling the study of emergent group behaviors and long-term societal impacts, such as shifts in communication norms or accessibility disparities. HPC resources are essential to train these models on massive datasets, run parallelized simulations across thousands of virtual users, and optimize interface designs through iterative reinforcement learning. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based frameworks for designing equitable, cognitively sustainable technologies, (2) predictive models of technology adoption and societal impact, and (3) open-source tools for simulating HCI scenarios at scale. This work directly supports the interdisciplinary mission of HCI by integrating computational innovation with behavioral science insights, ultimately advancing the responsible development of technologies that align with human needs and societal values.
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of the interaction between people and technology and how that technology impacts society, and combines disciplines within the fields of computing and information science (information systems, software engineering, artificial intelligence and design), engineering, and the behavior sciences (cognitive science, cognitive psychology, sociology, organizational psychology, and social psychology). Includes instruction in information technology, cognitive and behavioral sciences, and systems design.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation for public sector decision-making under complex, multi-dimensional constraints—a critical issue in public policy analysis. Current approaches to modeling policy interventions often rely on simplified assumptions that fail to capture the dynamic interactions between socioeconomic variables, institutional capacities, and geographic disparities. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-resolution simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational model will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with system dynamics to evaluate the cascading effects of policy choices across education, healthcare, and infrastructure systems in heterogeneous urban environments. By incorporating real-world datasets spanning 10+ years of municipal service records, demographic shifts, and budgetary constraints, the simulations will enable granular scenario testing at scale. Key computational tasks include parallelized Monte Carlo sampling to quantify uncertainty in policy outcomes, machine learning-driven sensitivity analysis to identify leverage points, and network optimization algorithms to balance equity-efficiency trade-offs. The HPC environment is essential for handling the model’s scale: preliminary tests on local clusters suggest that simulating a mid-sized city’s 5-year policy horizon requires processing over 50 million agent interactions per iteration. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support toolkit for municipal administrators, validated through partnerships with three regional planning agencies. This work advances public administration scholarship by introducing scalable computational methods to evaluate polycentric governance challenges, while directly addressing gaps in evidence-based policy design. Results will inform best practices for integrating predictive analytics into participatory budgeting processes and multi-stakeholder policy formulation.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Policy and Public Administration with an emphasis on issues related to public policy. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, principles of public administration; the management of public policy; and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: The management of acutely life-threatening conditions in veterinary patients, such as multi-organ failure, sepsis, or traumatic injury, requires rapid, data-driven decisions to optimize outcomes.
