However, clinical heterogeneity, dynamic disease progression, and the lack of validated predictive models for animal-specific physiology limit the development of personalized treatment protocols. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex, multi-modal datasets from veterinary critical care units and develop computational tools for real-time decision support. The research will integrate electronic health records, continuous vital sign monitoring, biomarker data, and imaging studies from canine and feline patients treated for life-threatening conditions. Machine learning models, including recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to predict organ dysfunction trajectories, identify early warning signals for clinical deterioration, and simulate responses to fluid resuscitation, vasopressor therapy, and other interventions. Agent-based modeling will further test hypothetical treatment protocols under diverse physiological scenarios. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (projected >10 TB across 5,000+ cases), the complexity of time-series analyses, and the need for parallel processing to optimize hyperparameters across multiple model architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for multi-organ failure risk stratification, validated against retrospective clinical outcomes; (2) computational frameworks for comparing emergency intervention strategies in silico; and (3) open-source tools to assist clinicians in tailoring hemodynamic support and monitoring plans. By advancing data integration and predictive analytics in veterinary critical care, this work aims to reduce mortality rates, improve resource allocation in emergency units, and establish scalable methodologies for translational research at the human-animal medicine interface. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, veterinary critical care consortiums, and modular software packages designed for adaptive reuse in related clinical domains.
cip_title: Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Medicine
cip_definition: Research focused on the emergency treatment and management of care for animals with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. May included related research in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures, and long-term care of critically diseased animals.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in clinical esthetics through data-driven modeling of skin response dynamics to multi-modal treatments. Despite the growing demand for personalized, evidence-based aesthetic interventions, the field lacks robust computational frameworks to predict how combinations of chemical, mechanical, and manual therapies interact with heterogeneous skin biomes. Current protocols rely on generalized guidelines, which inadequately account for individual variations in skin physiology, microbiome composition, and post-treatment recovery patterns. The proposed research will develop machine learning (ML) models trained on multi-omics datasets—including longitudinal skin microbiome sequencing, hyperspectral imaging of tissue response, and patient-reported outcomes—to simulate treatment efficacy across diverse demographic and dermatological profiles. Computational workflows will integrate finite element modeling of dermal absorption kinetics for topical agents, agent-based simulations of inflammatory cascades, and reinforcement learning to optimize treatment sequences. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across variables such as peel concentration gradients, microdermabrasion intensity-frequency tradeoffs, and post-procedure microbiome restoration timelines. Anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms to guide practitioner decisions in medical esthetic settings, particularly for high-risk populations (e.g., immunocompromised or post-operative patients), and a validated simulation environment for virtual treatment testing. The project bridges clinical esthetics with computational biology and AI, establishing a novel framework to reduce adverse events while enhancing therapeutic personalization. By mapping complex interactions between esthetic interventions and skin ecosystems, this work aims to elevate industry standards through quantitatively grounded protocols, ultimately supporting safer, more effective integration of advanced esthetic technologies in dermatological care pathways.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and body with advanced chemical and cosmetic preparations and esthetic medical treatments, and to function as licensed master or medical estheticians in dermatologists' and plastic surgeons' offices as well as in salons and spas. Includes instruction in advanced anatomy and physiology, skin properties and disorders, sanitation and infection control, advanced facial treatments, spa body treatments, advanced extractions, corrective makeup, chemical peels, microdermabrasion, lymphatic drainage and advanced massage techniques, pre- and post-operative esthetic skin care, client/patient evaluation and care, applicable laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the optimization of cross-platform advertising campaigns in dynamic media environments. Contemporary advertising involves analyzing vast datasets from social media, streaming platforms, and programmatic ad exchanges to predict consumer behavior and allocate budgets effectively. However, the computational demands of processing multimodal data (text, images, video) in real time, coupled with the need for rapid A/B testing of ad variants, exceed the capabilities of standard workstations. The proposed research will develop machine learning models to simulate consumer engagement patterns across heterogeneous media channels, using neural networks trained on historical campaign data enriched with real-time sentiment analysis and attention-tracking metrics. Computational methods will include natural language processing for ad copy evaluation, computer vision techniques for visual ad element optimization, and reinforcement learning to iteratively refine media buying strategies. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to reduce model training times from weeks to days and enable granular, large-scale simulations of audience responses under varying market conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to guide adaptive budget allocation, identify high-impact creative elements, and mitigate biases in ad targeting algorithms. This work will directly support the development of evidence-based practices for ethical, data-driven advertising in fragmented media landscapes, while providing students and researchers with hands-on experience in applying computational tools to strategic communication challenges. The requested resources are critical to handling terabyte-scale datasets and ensuring reproducibility in testing campaign scenarios across diverse demographic and cultural contexts.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creation, execution, transmission, and evaluation of commercial messages in various media intended to promote and sell products, services, and brands; and that prepares individuals to function as advertising assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in advertising theory, marketing strategy, advertising design and production methods, campaign methods and techniques, media management, related principles of business management, and applicable technical and equipment skills.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance geography education by developing computational tools to model and analyze complex geospatial datasets for classroom integration, addressing a critical gap in accessible, data-driven pedagogical resources. Despite the growing availability of geospatial data from satellites, sensors, and citizen science platforms, K-12 educators often lack the technical capacity to process these datasets into meaningful lesson materials. The research problem centers on bridging this divide by creating scalable methods to transform raw spatial data into interactive, curriculum-aligned visualizations and simulations. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets using parallelized workflows in Python and R, integrating machine learning (e.g., convolutional neural networks) to identify pedagogically relevant spatial patterns in land-use change, climate variability, and urban dynamics. Agent-based modeling frameworks (e.g., NetLogo) will simulate student interactions with geospatial interfaces to optimize usability across diverse learning environments. Proposed work includes benchmarking computational efficiency of data downsampling algorithms, training predictive models to flag region-specific geographic phenomena for lesson customization, and generating synthetic datasets to represent underrepresented locales. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of computationally preprocessed geospatial teaching modules, validated through partnerships with 15 teacher-training programs. By reducing computational barriers to real-world data integration, this project aims to empower educators to foster spatial literacy and evidence-based reasoning skills. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling memory-intensive geoprocessing tasks and large-scale parameter testing of educational simulation models, which would be infeasible on standard academic computing systems. Results will advance geography teacher education by demonstrating scalable intersections between computational earth science and classroom practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach geography at various grade levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize the design of urban green spaces for equitable public access and ecological resilience. While parks and recreational facilities are critical to community well-being, current planning frameworks often rely on static demographic data and generalized ecological thresholds, failing to account for dynamic human behavior patterns, climate variability, and evolving urban landscapes. The research problem centers on developing a predictive computational model that integrates real-time mobility data, climate projections, and socio-cultural preferences to simulate how diverse populations interact with green spaces under varying environmental and infrastructural conditions. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate visitor behavior with geospatial machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets, including anonymized mobile device location traces, vegetation health indices from satellite imagery, and public survey responses on leisure preferences. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these datasets, which require parallel processing for ABM scenario testing across thousands of simulated agents and high-resolution spatial analyses at city-wide scales. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that enables municipal planners to (1) prioritize park upgrades in underserved neighborhoods, (2) forecast visitor demand under heatwave or precipitation extremes, and (3) balance recreational use with biodiversity conservation goals. By bridging computational social science, landscape ecology, and urban design, this work advances an interdisciplinary methodology for data-driven leisure space planning while addressing gaps in traditional Parks and Recreation studies that lack integration with real-time behavioral analytics and climate adaptation frameworks. The project’s computational outputs will be validated through partnerships with three city parks departments, ensuring translational impact on equitable public resource allocation.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles underlying recreational and leisure activities, and the practices involved in providing indoor and outdoor recreational facilities and services for the general public.

abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) remain a critical challenge in modern operating rooms (ORs), with contamination risks persisting despite adherence to standardized aseptic protocols. This project proposes a computational study to model and optimize dynamic OR workflows, focusing on the interplay between surgical technologist movements, equipment handling, and airborne particle dispersion. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop agent-based simulations that integrate real-time sensor data from robotic surgical systems, environmental monitoring devices, and personnel tracking tools. The computational framework will employ discrete event simulation to map procedural workflows, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model airborne pathogen spread under varying OR ventilation configurations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify high-risk temporal and spatial patterns in contamination pathways during complex multi-instrument procedures. Validation will utilize anonymized datasets from 12 academic medical centers, encompassing 23,000+ surgical cases with corresponding infection outcome records. Expected outcomes include predictive models for contamination risk stratification, evidence-based recommendations for instrument tray placement optimization, and dynamic workflow adjustments to minimize breaks in sterility. This research addresses a critical gap in surgical technology by quantifying previously intangible risks in aseptic practice, with potential to reduce SSI rates by an estimated 15-20% in robot-assisted procedures. The computational approach directly supports surgical technologists’ decision-making in real-time equipment management while advancing OR safety analytics through large-scale spatiotemporal pattern recognition. Successful implementation will establish a novel paradigm for data-driven sterility protocol design in next-generation hybrid OR environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and surgical nurses, to maintain, monitor, and enforce the sterile field and adherence to aseptic technique by preoperative, surgical team, and postoperative personnel. Includes instruction in instrument and equipment sterilization and handling, surgical supplies management, wound exposure and closure, surgical computer and robot operation and monitoring, maintenance of hemostasis, and patient and team scrubbing.

abstract: Healthcare systems face escalating demands for efficient resource allocation amidst dynamic patient needs, workforce variability, and financial constraints. Traditional decision-making frameworks often rely on static models, which inadequately capture the complexity and uncertainty inherent in healthcare operations. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation and optimization platform to model multi-faceted healthcare delivery systems, with the goal of improving resource allocation strategies across hospitals and integrated care networks. The research will integrate agent-based modeling to simulate patient flow, staff scheduling, equipment utilization, and facility operations under diverse scenarios, including surge events and policy changes. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be employed to dynamically optimize real-time decisions, such as bed allocation, elective surgery scheduling, and cross-facility resource sharing, while accounting for financial viability and regulatory compliance. The computational framework will process large-scale datasets, including electronic health records, staffing logs, and cost structures, to identify inefficiencies and predict outcomes of intervention strategies. By leveraging parallel computing, the project will scale simulations to regional healthcare networks, enabling system-level analysis of trade-offs between cost, wait times, and clinical outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for administrators to balance operational budgets with service quality, evidence-based policy recommendations for crisis resource management, and open-source algorithmic modules adaptable to diverse healthcare settings. This work addresses critical gaps in computational health management by providing data-driven methodologies to enhance equity, resilience, and sustainability in healthcare delivery systems, directly supporting the program’s focus on operational excellence in health administration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, plan, and manage health care operations and services within health care facilities and across health care systems. Includes instruction in planning, business management, financial management, public relations, human resources management, health care systems operation and management, health care resource allocation and policy making, health law and regulations, and applications to specific types of health care services.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing wine recommendation systems and enhancing precision in food-wine pairing strategies, specifically tailored to the needs of professional sommeliers and hospitality programs. The challenge lies in the multidimensional nature of wine selection, which integrates sensory data (e.g., flavor profiles, tannin structure), regional production variables (e.g., terroir, climate trends), and dynamic consumer preferences—a dataset too complex for traditional analytical methods. Current approaches in wine program management rely heavily on heuristic expertise, lacking scalable tools to synthesize global wine databases, historical vintage performance, and real-time market trends. This project proposes a machine learning pipeline to model nonlinear relationships between wine attributes, contextual dining scenarios, and sensory outcomes. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) of sommelier notes and consumer reviews, geospatial analysis of vineyard microclimates using satellite data, and neural networks trained on chemical composition datasets (e.g., volatile organic compounds, phenolic content). By simulating pairing scenarios across diverse culinary traditions and dietary trends, the framework will generate adaptive recommendations for inventory management and service design. HPC resources are critical for handling large-scale, heterogeneous datasets (e.g., global wine certifications, hospitality industry sales metrics) and iteratively training models with cross-disciplinary inputs. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access decision-support tool for wine educators and sommeliers, validated through partnerships with hospitality training programs. This work bridges computational analytics and enological practice, offering a novel methodology to address evolving challenges in gastronomic tourism and luxury service industries. The results aim to elevate empirical rigor in sommelier education while fostering data-driven innovations in wine program sustainability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage wine selection, purchasing, storage, sales, and service for a variety of establishments in the hospitality industry. Includes instruction in wine production, wine regions of the world, wine tasting, food and wine matching, service techniques, and wine program management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Deaf Studies through large-scale computational analysis of American Sign Language (ASL) linguistic patterns and historical-cultural datasets. The central research problem involves understanding how ASL evolves in response to sociocultural shifts within the U.S. deaf community, particularly in the context of technological advancements (e.g., video relay services, social media) and civil rights milestones. Traditional qualitative methods in Deaf Studies face scalability limitations when analyzing decades of ASL media archives, educational materials, and community publications, which are critical to tracing linguistic change and cultural identity formation. This project proposes a hybrid computational approach, combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted for ASL gloss annotations, network analysis of intergenerational transmission patterns, and machine learning-driven topic modeling of deaf-led advocacy texts from 1970–present. Datasets include digitized records from deaf newspapers, ASL lecture transcripts, and metadata from 15,000+ video entries in the National Deaf Digital Library. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multimodal data (text, video timestamps, sign metadata) and training of custom transformer models to detect syntactic innovations in ASL usage across regions and age cohorts. Expected outcomes include: (1) the first longitudinal map of lexical-semantic shifts in ASL tied to specific historical events, (2) identification of understudied sociolinguistic barriers in deaf education policy, and (3) open-access tools for annotating ASL corpus data. By computationally bridging linguistic analysis with cultural history, this work aims to inform inclusive pedagogical frameworks and provide empirical support for deaf community-led language preservation initiatives. The scale and complexity of these analyses require HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-level datasets and computationally intensive NLP pipelines, which are beyond the scope of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the sociological, historical and linguistic aspects of the deaf and hearing impaired, and that prepares individuals to work with the deaf and hearing impaired. Includes instruction in American Sign Language, deaf studies, American deaf culture, structure of American Sign Language, history of the American deaf community, and civil rights of deaf people.

abstract: Higher education instructors face increasing demands to adopt evidence-based teaching practices that promote engagement, critical thinking, and equitable outcomes across diverse student populations. However, existing studies on instructional effectiveness often rely on small-scale datasets or simplified models, limiting their applicability to complex, real-world classroom dynamics. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models that simulate postsecondary learning environments at scale, enabling the systematic exploration of how pedagogical strategies interact with student variables to influence academic success. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will construct agent-based simulations incorporating heterogeneous learner profiles (e.g., prior knowledge, motivation levels, demographic factors) and varying instructional conditions (e.g., flipped classrooms, active learning modules, technology-enhanced assessment). Concurrently, machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze multimodal educational datasets—including LMS interaction logs, discussion forum texts, and assessment results—from six institutions to identify patterns linking teaching approaches to student outcomes. The computational demands of simulating thousands of virtual classrooms while processing terabytes of unstructured data necessitate distributed computing architectures and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for predicting the efficacy of syllabus designs under different demographic conditions, (2) actionable guidelines for optimizing asynchronous discussion prompts to foster critical thinking, and (3) open-source tools enabling educators to model course redesign impacts prior to implementation. By bridging computational modeling with andragogical theory, this work aims to provide empirically grounded strategies that enhance teaching practices while maintaining scalability across diverse institutional contexts.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: The optimization of food processing techniques to enhance nutritional quality, safety, and shelf-life remains a critical challenge due to the complex, multi-scale interactions between biochemical, thermal, and mechanical factors. Traditional experimental approaches often struggle to capture these dynamic processes across molecular, cellular, and industrial scales. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models that bridge molecular-level phenomena with macroscopic food processing dynamics. Key focus areas include simulating protein denaturation and starch gelatinization during thermal treatments using molecular dynamics, analyzing heat and mass transfer in industrial-scale equipment via computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and predicting microbial inactivation kinetics under varying processing parameters. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be employed to correlate processing conditions with physicochemical stability during storage, enabling predictive optimization of shelf-life. The integration of these computational approaches will generate actionable insights into time-temperature thresholds for pathogen reduction, energy-efficient processing protocols, and packaging configurations that minimize quality degradation. By elucidating the fundamental mechanisms governing food matrix behavior, this research aims to establish a computational framework for accelerating the design of novel processing technologies. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the large-scale simulations, iterative parameter optimization, and high-dimensional data analysis inherent to this work. Outcomes will advance food science by providing quantitative tools to reduce waste, improve safety, and tailor functional properties of processed foods, with direct benefits to both industry practices and public health initiatives.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of converting raw agricultural products into processed forms suitable for direct human consumption, and the storage of such products. Includes instruction in applicable aspects of the agricultural sciences, human physiology and nutrition, food chemistry, agricultural products processing, food additives, food preparation and packaging, food storage and shipment, and related aspects of human health and safety including toxicology and pathology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular interactions between traditional herbal compounds and neuroinflammatory pathways implicated in chronic pain disorders. Despite growing interest in plant-based therapies as adjuncts to conventional pain management, the mechanistic basis of many traditional remedies remains poorly characterized, limiting their integration into evidence-based care. Using an interdisciplinary approach blending ethnobotanical data, cheminformatics, and systems biology, we aim to map the polypharmacological effects of 50 prioritized plant-derived compounds on glial cell signaling networks. The computational workflow will involve three phases: (1) molecular docking simulations to predict binding affinities between phytochemicals and 27 validated protein targets in neuroinflammation, (2) machine learning-driven network pharmacology models to identify synergistic compound combinations, and (3) comparative molecular dynamics simulations of top candidate complexes under physiological membrane conditions. The scale of these analyses requires HPC capabilities to manage ~200,000 docking simulations, train predictive models on multi-omics datasets (including scRNA-seq from human microglia), and perform nanosecond-scale simulations across multiple binding states. Expected outcomes include the identification of 3-5 high-priority phytochemical complexes with predicted blood-brain barrier permeability and multimodal anti-inflammatory activity, accompanied by mechanistic hypotheses for preclinical validation. This work will establish a computational framework for evaluating traditional medicine bioactivity at unprecedented resolution while addressing critical gaps in understanding how complex herbal formulations may modulate neuroimmune crosstalk. Results will be disseminated through open-access databases and collaborations with clinical researchers exploring integrative approaches for refractory pain syndromes. By bridging computational biology and traditional knowledge systems, the project aims to advance rigorous, data-driven methodologies for studying alternative therapeutic paradigms.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medical Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medical support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in optimizing dynamic theatrical environments for live performances. Technical theatre design—encompassing lighting, sound, set construction, and spatial acoustics—increasingly relies on predictive modeling to balance artistic vision with physical and logistical constraints. However, real-time simulation of complex variables, such as interactive light-scattering effects in multidimensional stage geometries or acoustic propagation in adaptive performance spaces, remains computationally prohibitive using standard tools. This limits the precision and scalability of pre-production workflows, particularly for large venues or productions requiring rapid iterative adjustments. Our research proposes a computational framework combining ray-tracing algorithms, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization to model these systems at high fidelity. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of lighting rigs with thousands of adjustable parameters, coupled with wave-based acoustic models that account for audience movement, set reconfigurations, and material properties. Additionally, we will develop a reinforcement learning pipeline to automate design trade-offs between aesthetic goals (e.g., shadow sharpness, sound clarity) and practical constraints (e.g., energy consumption, structural load limits). By validating these models against empirical data from partner theatres, we aim to create open-source tools that reduce reliance on physical prototyping and enable real-time adjustments during technical rehearsals. The outcomes will directly enhance the efficiency and creative potential of theatre production teams, while advancing computational methodologies for live performance design—a domain underexplored in HPC applications. This work will also establish benchmarks for integrating sensory feedback systems into adaptive theatrical environments, with implications for immersive entertainment and experiential education in the performing arts.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Technical Theatre/ Theatre Design and Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic, technical and dramatic principles and techniques to the communication of dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through technical theatre methods. Includes instruction in set design, lighting design, sound effects, theatre acoustics, scene painting, property management, costume design, and technical direction and production and use of computer applications to support these functions.

abstract: Chronic disease management in family practice settings presents complex challenges due to the interplay of biological, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors influencing patient outcomes. Current clinical decision-making tools often lack the granularity to account for this multidimensional variability, particularly in underserved populations. This project proposes to develop a computational framework for optimizing personalized care plans by analyzing heterogeneous health data from electronic health records (EHRs), patient-reported outcomes, and community health surveys. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train machine learning models to identify risk stratification patterns, predict intervention efficacy, and simulate long-term health trajectories across diverse family structures. The computational approach integrates natural language processing for unstructured clinical notes, graph neural networks to model family relational dynamics, and agent-based simulations to test care coordination strategies under resource constraints. Key innovations include the synthesis of household-level social determinants of health with individual biometric data, enabling family practice nurses to evaluate how care plans interact with familial support systems. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source predictive tool for identifying high-risk patients requiring tailored interventions, (2) simulation-backed recommendations for redistributing clinical resources in rural health systems, and (3) quantitative evidence linking family-centered care models to reduced hospital readmissions. The scale of analysis—spanning 500,000+ de-identified patient records from regional health networks—necessitates HPC capabilities for distributed data processing, hyperparameter optimization across GPU nodes, and parallel execution of Monte Carlo simulations. By mapping how household-level variables mediate chronic disease outcomes, this work aims to advance evidence-based practice in family nursing while providing a computational model adaptable to other primary care contexts. Results will directly inform curriculum updates for family nurse practitioner programs regarding data-driven intervention design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the biophysical mechanisms underlying energy-based therapies, specifically Qi Gong and Therapeutic Touch, which are hypothesized to modulate cellular stress responses through non-invasive bioenergetic interactions. Despite anecdotal and preliminary clinical evidence of efficacy, the lack of mechanistic understanding limits their integration into evidence-based care. The central challenge lies in modeling the complex, multiscale interactions between hypothesized bioenergetic fields (e.g., electromagnetic or quantum-vibrational phenomena) and cellular systems, particularly under oxidative stress conditions. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining molecular dynamics simulations of redox-sensitive proteins (e.g., thioredoxin, Nrf2) with finite element modeling of electromagnetic field propagation in biological tissues. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the integration of quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulations to assess field-induced electronic perturbations in protein active sites, alongside macroscopic tissue-level field distributions. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze multi-omics datasets from in vitro models exposed to controlled bioenergetic interventions, identifying potential biomarkers of response. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from partner labs using impedance spectroscopy and single-cell redox imaging. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of bioenergetic field interactions with cellular components, (2) identification of putative molecular targets for energy-based modulation of oxidative stress, and (3) a scalable computational platform for optimizing therapeutic parameters (frequency, intensity, spatial targeting). This work bridges biophysics, systems biology, and complementary medicine, providing quantitative insights into a poorly understood class of therapies while advancing computational methods for analyzing subtle energy-matter interactions in biological systems. Successful implementation could inform clinical trial design for energy therapies and contribute foundational knowledge to the emerging field of biofield science.
cip_title: Energy and Biologically Based Therapies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative, complementary, and somatic health and therapeutic services not elsewhere classified (bioenergetics, cranio-sacral therapy, Therapeutic Touch, Qi Gong, and others).

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the multi-dimensional impacts of transnational policy frameworks on human security outcomes in fragile and conflict-affected regions. The research addresses a critical gap in public policy analysis: the lack of scalable, data-driven methodologies to evaluate how overlapping international agreements—ranging from climate adaptation pledges to arms control treaties—interact dynamically to influence displacement risks, resource access, and governance stability. Traditional policy evaluation tools struggle to account for the non-linear feedback loops, time-lagged effects, and spatial interdependencies inherent in these systems. To overcome these limitations, the project will develop an adaptive computational framework integrating three components: (1) natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to systematically codify treaty obligations and compliance reports from 150+ multilateral agreements; (2) agent-based models simulating how policy-induced resource allocation changes propagate through local socioeconomic networks; and (3) geospatial-temporal analyses linking satellite-derived conflict indicators with policy implementation timelines. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing unstructured multilingual policy documents at scale, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across diverse conflict scenarios, and maintaining high-resolution spatial datasets spanning 40+ at-risk regions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible policy interaction matrix identifying leverage points for reducing unintended consequences, along with machine learning models capable of forecasting second-order governance impacts when novel agreements are proposed. By quantifying how discrete policy instruments collectively shape human security trajectories, this work aims to advance evidence-based frameworks for designing coherent international policy portfolios while mitigating fragmentation risks in multilateral systems. The computational tools developed will be shared with UN policy coordination units to strengthen scenario-testing capacities in crisis response planning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to relationships among nations and among governments and non-governmental entities. Includes instruction in international politics, governance, financial policy, and security affairs; globalization; economic and social policies of developing nations; and applications to specific public policy topics such as labor and employment, immigration, and human rights.

abstract: The increasing complexity of computational workloads in modern high-performance computing (HPC) systems necessitates adaptive resource management strategies that harmonize software efficiency with hardware capabilities. This project addresses the challenge of optimizing resource allocation in heterogeneous computing environments, where diverse architectures—such as CPUs, GPUs, and emerging accelerators—must be dynamically coordinated to meet evolving computational demands. Traditional static allocation methods often lead to underutilization, energy inefficiency, and latency in task scheduling, particularly in interdisciplinary applications spanning simulation, machine learning, and large-scale data analysis. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid approach integrating reinforcement learning (RL) with real-time performance modeling to enable intelligent, context-aware resource distribution. Computational experiments will involve developing and training RL agents on simulated HPC clusters, leveraging historical workload data to predict resource needs and environmental constraints. These agents will be validated on physical HPC infrastructure, where they will autonomously adjust allocations based on live system metrics, workload priorities, and hardware health. The project requires access to HPC resources with diverse architectures to test scalability, including multi-node GPU clusters for RL training and CPU-FPGA hybrid systems for latency-sensitive task evaluation. Expected outcomes include a framework that reduces idle resource time by at least 30% compared to conventional schedulers while maintaining QoS guarantees, as well as generalized benchmarks for cross-architecture performance prediction. This work bridges computer science principles in algorithmic design and machine learning with computer engineering expertise in hardware-aware optimization, offering a scalable solution for scientific computing, cloud infrastructure, and edge computing systems. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated openly to advance interdisciplinary research in efficient computing.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of computer science and computer engineering principles or a specialization which includes expertise in both computer engineering and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive workplace design in response to dynamic organizational needs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between spatial configurations, occupant behavior, and operational efficiency. Traditional facility planning methods rely on static benchmarks or heuristic evaluations, which struggle to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating occupancy patterns, evolving health and safety protocols, and heterogeneous employee preferences. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate environmental psychology principles, real-time sensor data, and multi-objective optimization to generate workspace layouts that balance productivity, well-being, and resource efficiency. Using agent-based modeling and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, the project will analyze how spatial parameters (e.g., desk density, circulation pathways, shared amenities) interact with human factors (e.g., collaboration frequency, noise sensitivity) and environmental conditions (e.g., air quality, thermal comfort). HPC resources are critical to scaling these simulations across thousands of hypothetical scenarios, enabling probabilistic assessments of design resilience under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., energy use vs. social connectivity) and identifies Pareto-optimal solutions for facility managers. This work bridges gaps between data science, behavioral economics, and architectural design, offering a novel methodology for post-pandemic workspace strategy. By advancing computational approaches to facility planning, the project aims to establish evidence-based standards for adaptive environments while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional, policy-adjacent domains. Results will be validated against empirical data from partner organizations, with open-source model components to encourage broader adoption in workplace innovation research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on strategic workplace and facility planning and that prepares individuals to function as facility and event managers and workplace consultants. Includes instruction in the principles of aesthetic and functional design, environmental psychology and organizational behavior, real estate planning, principles of occupational health and safety, event planning and management, operations management, and applicable regulatory and policy issues.

abstract: Landscape architecture faces growing challenges in addressing dynamic environmental systems under climate change, yet traditional design methods often rely on static, historical data or simplified models. This project seeks to develop a computational framework that integrates real-time environmental data, predictive ecological modeling, and human behavioral patterns to simulate landscape performance across multiple temporal and spatial scales. The research problem centers on the inability of conventional tools to account for the complex feedback loops between microclimatic conditions, vegetative adaptation, and public space utilization in rapidly urbanizing areas. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement a coupled modeling system combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for wind and thermal analysis, agent-based modeling (ABM) for pedestrian movement simulations, and machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal ecological datasets. These components will be spatially synchronized through GPU-accelerated raster processing and validated against sensor data from three pilot sites undergoing climate-adaptive redesign. The computational approach addresses scalability challenges in rendering high-resolution 3D terrain models while maintaining real-time interactivity for scenario testing. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform that quantifies trade-offs between ecological resilience, thermal comfort, and social equity in landscape interventions. By enabling probabilistic forecasting of plant community succession under varying management strategies and climate scenarios, this work aims to advance evidence-based design protocols that transcend current horticultural databases and static zoning paradigms. The requested computing resources will specifically support the parallel processing of LiDAR-derived point clouds, calibration of neural networks for phenology prediction, and multi-objective optimization routines balancing carbon sequestration potential with recreational carrying capacity. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges gaps between landscape architecture, urban ecology, and computational social science while operating outside traditional STEM domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of landscape architecture and research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; soils, groundcovers, and horticultural elements; project and site planning; landscape design, history, and theory; environmental design; applicable law and regulations; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how rapid environmental change alters species interactions and evolutionary trajectories in fragmented ecosystems, with a focus on host-pathogen coevolution in plant-pollinator networks. As climate shifts and habitat loss disrupt ecological communities, traditional models struggle to predict emergent evolutionary dynamics due to nonlinear feedbacks between species behavior, population structure, and selection pressures. We propose developing an agent-based simulation framework integrating spatially explicit landscape data, trait-mediated interaction networks, and adaptive evolutionary processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multi-scale interactions across 10^4–10^6 individual agents representing plants, pollinators, and pathogens, while tracking genomic regions associated with resistance and virulence traits over 100–500 generations. The model will parameterize using empirical data from long-term montane ecosystem studies, incorporating realistic dispersal constraints, phenological mismatches, and thermal tolerance curves. Parallelized simulations will assess how varying rates of environmental warming and habitat fragmentation alter coevolutionary outcomes, including the spatial distribution of adaptive alleles and network robustness to cascading extinctions. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of tipping points in eco-evolutionary dynamics under combined stressors, (2) predictive metrics for prioritizing habitat corridors to maintain coadaptation potential, and (3) open-source tools for coupling genomic architecture models with community-level interaction networks. This work addresses critical gaps in forecasting biodiversity responses to anthropogenic change while advancing computational methods for scaling evolutionary theory to realistic landscape contexts. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration across 50+ scenario combinations, each requiring ~10,000 core-hours to complete stochastic replicates and sensitivity analyses.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_title: Ecology, Evolution, Systematics and Population Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ecology, evolution, and systematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of biomedical imaging data, particularly in dynamic cellular processes, presents a critical bottleneck in understanding disease mechanisms at subcellular resolutions. Current methods for analyzing time-resolved 3D microscopy datasets—essential for studying phenomena like organelle interactions in neurodegenerative diseases or tumor microenvironment remodeling—rely on fragmented computational workflows that inadequately integrate spatial, temporal, and biophysical parameters. This project proposes a novel computational framework to unify multiscale modeling, deep learning, and real-time adaptive imaging control for high-content cellular dynamics studies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop a GPU-optimized pipeline to process terabyte-scale 4D (x,y,z,t) volumetric imaging datasets, integrating convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for organelle segmentation, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model inter-organelle interaction networks, and physics-informed reinforcement learning to optimize experimental imaging parameters during live-cell experiments. The computational workflow will be validated against ground-truth datasets from CRISPR-tagged organelles in glioblastoma and Parkinson’s disease cell models, with iterative feedback between experimental and computational teams. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive operations for 4D data registration, scaling GNN training to capture rare interaction events, and reducing latency for real-time experimental steering. Successful implementation will enable unprecedented resolution of subcellular event cascades, directly informing mechanistic studies of disease-associated cellular dysfunction. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive microscopy control, a curated repository of annotated 4D cellular dynamics datasets, and new biomarkers for organelle-level dysfunction in neurodegenerative and oncological contexts. This work bridges computational scalability gaps in biomedical imaging informatics, advancing both methodology and translational applications through tight integration of HPC-driven analytics with experimental biomedical research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to health and/or biomedical research,  and the development of advanced database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in biomedical and/or health sciences; information science and technology; social and behavioral sciences; biomedical/health information science and technology; human factors and socio-technical systems;  applied social, behavioral, and information science and technology; and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of next-generation molten salt reactors (MSRs) requires precise modeling of coupled thermohydraulic and neutronic phenomena under dynamic conditions. Current simulation tools struggle to resolve the complex, multiphysics interactions between turbulent fluoride salt flows, delayed neutron precursor transport, and spatially varying power distributions—a critical gap given MSRs’ inherent integration of fuel and coolant. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to analyze these interdependencies at unprecedented resolution, enabling predictive assessments of MSR transient behavior. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a tightly coupled multiphysics model combining Monte Carlo neutron transport (via OpenMC) with large-eddy simulation computational fluid dynamics (LES-CFD) in a custom workflow. The approach will extend existing neutronic codes to handle time-dependent solute transport in circulating fuels while integrating real-time thermal feedback mechanisms. Validation against experimental datasets from molten salt loops and zero-power reactor facilities will constrain model uncertainties. Key computational challenges include managing scale-resolving turbulence simulations across geometrically complex reactor domains, optimizing parallelization strategies for hybrid CPU-GPU architectures, and minimizing latency in multiphysics data exchange. Successful implementation will yield the first open-source tool capable of resolving sub-second transients in MSR systems with three-dimensional fidelity, addressing a critical need for regulatory acceptance of advanced reactor designs. Anticipated outcomes include optimized flow channel geometries to mitigate localized power spikes, improved safety case methodologies for license applications, and foundational insights into salt chemistry effects on reactivity control. This work directly supports the deployment of inherently safer nuclear energy systems while advancing computational methods for multiphysics reactor analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling and manipulating nuclear energy, including nuclear power plant design, fission reactor design, fusion reactor design, reactor control and safety systems design, power transfer systems, containment vessels and structures design; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as fission and fusion processes, human and environmental factors, construction, and operational considerations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel adaptive programming framework for optimizing computational workflows in heterogeneous edge computing environments, where traditional resource allocation strategies struggle to balance latency, energy efficiency, and device heterogeneity. As edge networks expand to support applications in smart infrastructure, distributed robotics, and IoT ecosystems, programmers face challenges in dynamically partitioning tasks across devices with varying computational capabilities, energy constraints, and intermittent connectivity. Current approaches rely on static partitioning or centralized orchestration, which fail to adapt to real-time resource fluctuations. To address this gap, we propose a decentralized, machine learning-enhanced runtime system that autonomously redistributes computational subroutines across edge nodes based on live performance telemetry and predictive resource modeling. The core innovation lies in embedding lightweight decision-making agents directly within program binaries, enabling localized adaptation without centralized control. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate large-scale edge networks with thousands of nodes under diverse operational scenarios, including urban mobility patterns and industrial sensor deployments. Using agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations, we will test adaptive algorithms against stochastically generated workloads and failure modes. Benchmarks will evaluate latency reduction, energy savings, and fault tolerance relative to existing edge computing paradigms. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for programming adaptive edge applications and empirical guidelines for resource-aware code partitioning. This work bridges gaps between distributed systems programming and autonomous decision-making architectures, offering new methodologies for developers operating in resource-constrained, dynamic environments. The results will directly inform emerging standards for edge computing in 5G/6G networks and distributed AI deployments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general writing and implementation of generic and customized programs to drive operating systems and that generally prepares individuals to apply the methods and procedures of software design and programming to software installation and maintenance. Includes instruction in software design, low- and high-level languages and program writing; program customization and linking; prototype testing; troubleshooting; and related aspects of operating systems and networks.

abstract: Veterinary dermatology faces significant challenges in diagnosing and managing complex, multifactorial skin diseases in diverse animal species, particularly as clinical heterogeneity and overlapping presentations complicate traditional diagnostic approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for analyzing large-scale dermatologic datasets, including histopathology images, genomic sequences, and electronic health records, to identify novel biomarkers and optimize therapeutic strategies. A central focus is the development of machine learning models trained on multispecies dermatologic data to classify inflammatory, autoimmune, and neoplastic skin disorders with higher accuracy than conventional methods. Computational pipelines will integrate whole-genome sequencing data from companion animals with cutaneous lymphoma to identify somatic mutations and clonal evolution patterns predictive of treatment resistance. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between emerging biologic therapies and species-specific immune receptors to refine drug design for allergic dermatitis. The scale of data—encompassing high-resolution whole-slide imaging (20,000+ samples), longitudinal clinical metadata, and terabase-scale sequencing—necessitates distributed computing architectures for efficient processing. Expected outcomes include open-source diagnostic algorithms validated across 15 animal species, a genomic atlas of cutaneous malignancies in veterinary patients, and predictive frameworks for personalizing immunomodulatory therapies. By enabling rapid analysis of cross-species dermatologic data, this work aims to address critical gaps in translational veterinary medicine, particularly for rare or refractory conditions lacking evidence-based guidelines. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale genomic variant calling, and parallelized simulation workloads, directly contributing to advancements in both veterinary clinical practice and comparative dermatology research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: Critical infrastructure systems, such as power grids, transportation networks, and communication systems, face escalating threats from adversarial cyber-physical attacks and cascading failures exacerbated by interdependencies. Current risk assessment models often oversimplify these interdependencies or lack the computational capacity to simulate large-scale, dynamic scenarios, limiting their utility in real-world mitigation planning. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model and analyze multi-sector infrastructure vulnerabilities under hybrid cyber-physical threat scenarios. The research will integrate agent-based modeling, network dynamics simulations, and machine learning techniques to capture the nonlinear interactions between physical infrastructure components, cyber control systems, and human operator responses. Computational workflows will simulate coordinated attacks on interdependent systems, incorporating stochastic threat vectors, adaptive adversary behaviors, and cascading failure pathways. The HPC environment will enable parallelized scenario testing across thousands of parameter combinations, including climate stressors, infrastructure age profiles, and regional interdependency configurations. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for quantifying systemic risks, identifying critical failure cascades, and evaluating the resilience of redundancy configurations. The project will also produce AI-driven threat detection modules capable of processing real-time operational data streams from supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems. By leveraging HPC resources to overcome scale limitations in existing methods, this work aims to advance evidence-based infrastructure protection strategies, providing policymakers and operators with actionable insights for hardening nationally significant assets. The resulting computational framework will be adaptable to emerging threat landscapes and support the development of standardized resilience metrics for cross-sector infrastructure governance.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the design, planning and management of systems and procedures for protecting critical national physical and cyber infrastructure from external threats, including terrorism. Includes instruction in homeland security policy, critical infrastructure policy, information security, matrix vulnerability assessment, threat assessment, physical security, personnel security, operational security, contingency planning, case analyses of specific industries and systems, redundancy planning, emergency and disaster planning, security systems, and intelligence operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of groundwater depletion dynamics in anthropogenically stressed aquifers. Rapid population growth and agricultural intensification have disrupted natural recharge cycles in critical aquifer systems, yet current models inadequately resolve the coupled hydrogeological, geochemical, and land-use processes governing long-term groundwater resilience. We propose to develop a multi-physics framework integrating 3D heterogeneous subsurface flow simulations with reactive transport modeling and stochastic uncertainty quantification. The computational workflow will assimilate high-resolution datasets, including InSAR-derived land subsidence, electrical resistivity tomography, and decadal-scale geochemical monitoring, to constrain parameters governing aquifer compaction and contaminant mobilization risks. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated ensembles to enable probabilistic forecasting under diverse climate and extraction scenarios. The project’s computational demands arise from high-resolution discretization of complex stratigraphy (10^8+ grid cells), iterative Bayesian inversion of multi-modal datasets, and ensemble simulations spanning 50+ years at daily timesteps. Memory-intensive tasks include parallelized solving of coupled flow-transport equations with adaptive mesh refinement and deep learning architectures for pattern recognition in time-series outputs. Anticipated outcomes include (1) an open-source codebase for coupled groundwater-geomechanical modeling, (2) uncertainty-bounded projections of depletion tipping points for major agricultural basins, and (3) optimized monitoring network designs informed by sensitivity analysis. These results will directly inform state agencies in revising sustainable yield estimates and contamination mitigation strategies. The HPC allocation is critical for achieving the spatiotemporal resolution required to resolve nonlinear feedbacks between pumping regimes, subsidence-induced permeability changes, and legacy pollutant transport—a computational challenge intractable on local cluster resources.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on earth, its environments, human activities, and the linkages between them. Includes instruction biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, pollution control and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in semi-automated data entry workflows by developing adaptive computational models that optimize human-machine collaboration in microcomputer-based environments. Traditional data entry systems rely on static software interfaces and rigid workflows, which struggle to accommodate variability in input formats, user skill levels, or real-time error correction needs. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble machine learning models that dynamically adjust interface parameters, predictive text suggestions, and error detection thresholds based on continuous analysis of user interaction patterns. Using distributed computing frameworks, we will process terabyte-scale datasets of keystroke dynamics, cursor movements, and correction patterns collected from diverse microcomputer applications (spreadsheets, database interfaces, legacy systems). The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing for context-aware field prioritization and computer vision techniques for layout recognition in semi-structured documents. A key innovation involves developing GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning agents that simulate human decision-making processes during data validation tasks, enabling proactive workflow adjustments without disrupting user attention. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive data entry systems that reduces repetitive strain injuries by 18-25% through ergonomic interface adaptations, decreases procedural errors by 30% via real-time anomaly detection, and improves throughput by 15% in heterogeneous input environments. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of modeling individualized user profiles while maintaining sub-200ms latency requirements for responsive interface adjustments. This work bridges gaps between human-computer interaction research and practical microcomputer applications, offering scalable solutions for industries reliant on legacy data entry systems undergoing digital transformation.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform basic data and text entry using standard and customized software products. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, personal computer and work station operation, reading draft texts and raw data forms, audio and tape dictation, and various interactive software programs used for tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, databases, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the physicochemical evolution of silicate mineral assemblages under extreme pressure-temperature regimes using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate metamorphic processes in subduction zones and continental collision settings. A critical gap persists in modeling the coupled geochemical and geomechanical behavior of silicate systems at scales bridging atomic-level mineral reactions (1–10 nm) and regional tectonic deformation (10–100 km). Current limitations arise from insufficient computational resolution to capture strain localization in polymineralic aggregates while simultaneously tracking element redistribution through fluid-mediated reactions. Our team will employ a multiscale modeling framework integrating quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT) calculations of mineral surface energetics with continuum-scale finite element models of rock rheology. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of (1) dislocation dynamics in olivine-pyroxene-garnet systems under mantle-relevant conditions using molecular dynamics (LAMMPS), and (2) coupled chemo-mechanical evolution of subducting slabs through adaptive mesh refinement in Abaqus/Standard. The computational workflow requires 500,000+ core-hours to handle 3D models with >10^8 elements incorporating experimentally derived kinetic parameters for 15 major silicate phases. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) quantitative maps of strain partitioning in heterogeneous lithologies during eclogitization, (2) predictive models of rare earth element mobility along reaction-enhanced shear zones, and (3) open-source code modules for coupling reactive transport with anisotropic plasticity. These results will advance fundamental understanding of how atomic-scale mineral transformations influence orogenic processes, with applications to metamorphic petrology, tectonic reconstruction, and critical mineral exploration. The requested allocation supports time-sensitive simulations aligned with ongoing NSF-funded experimental studies of subduction interface rheology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the silicates and other substances formed by chemical and physical geomorphological processes.

abstract: Environmental control systems in agricultural and industrial settings face challenges in balancing operational efficiency with sustainability goals. Current methodologies for optimizing parameters such as temperature, humidity, and airflow often rely on simplified models that fail to capture the complex, nonlinear interactions between environmental variables and system performance. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and optimize multi-domain environmental control technologies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with data-driven machine learning models to analyze dynamic interactions within controlled environments. The simulations will account for real-world variability in external conditions and internal load demands, enabling the identification of adaptive control strategies that minimize energy consumption while maintaining stringent environmental targets. Key deliverables include an open-source simulation toolkit tailored for environmental control applications and a series of case studies demonstrating performance improvements in prototype systems. The outcomes aim to advance the design of next-generation environmental control technologies by providing scalable, evidence-based optimization tools that reduce carbon footprints and operational costs across multiple industries. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to manage the computational burden of parallelized CFD solvers and large-scale parameter optimization, which exceed the capabilities of local computing resources. This project bridges gaps in current environmental control methodologies by addressing system-wide interdependencies, offering transformative potential for sustainable industrial and agricultural practices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental control technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling large-scale, dynamic communication patterns in digital public relations and advertising campaigns, where traditional computational tools struggle to process real-time, multi-platform data at the speed and scale required for actionable insights. The research problem centers on the inability of existing frameworks to predict emergent audience behaviors or optimize cross-channel messaging strategies in environments characterized by high-volume, unstructured data (e.g., social media, streaming platforms, and interactive ad exchanges). To overcome these limitations, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling simulations and machine learning pipelines tailored to analyze terabytes of heterogeneous communication data. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment and thematic analysis of user-generated content, graph neural networks to map information diffusion across networks, and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate adaptive audience responses under varying campaign conditions. By leveraging parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated model training, the project aims to identify patterns in engagement dynamics, predict viral messaging thresholds, and test crisis communication strategies in synthetic yet realistic scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework for real-time campaign optimization, validated against historical case studies from corporate and nonprofit communication contexts. The findings will advance theoretical understanding of nonlinear communication effects in digital ecosystems while providing practitioners with evidence-based tools to allocate resources efficiently, mitigate reputational risks, and maximize message resonance in increasingly fragmented media landscapes. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in addressing complex, data-driven challenges unique to modern organizational communication research.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in organizational communication, public relations, and advertising, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational model of multigenerational family resilience under systemic stressors. While family systems theory has long emphasized dynamic interactions among individuals and environments, existing studies rely heavily on qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods, limiting insights into nonlinear, time-dependent processes shaping resilience. The project addresses this gap by developing an agent-based simulation framework to model how cultural, socioeconomic, and interpersonal variables interact across generations during prolonged crises such as climate migration or economic collapse. Agents will be parameterized using longitudinal datasets spanning 30 years of family development records, integrating psychometric scales, economic behaviors, and health outcomes. Computational challenges include optimizing Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic decision trees governing intergenerational support patterns and parallelizing neural networks that analyze emergent communication dynamics from simulated dialogue corpora. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical leverage points in family networks that predict adaptive capacity, (2) validation of intervention strategies through counterfactual scenario testing, and (3) open-source tools for simulating culturally specific resilience pathways. By bridging developmental theory with computational social science, this work aims to create predictive models that inform policy and clinical practices while establishing methodological frameworks for HPC applications in understudied domains of human development research. The requested resources will enable scaling to population-level simulations (>100,000 agent households) with real-time adaptation algorithms, substantially exceeding the capacity of existing psychosocial research infrastructures.
cip_title: Human Development, Family Studies, and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in human development, family studies, and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for analyzing the structural and sociolinguistic evolution of Romanian dialects, particularly in underdocumented regions such as rural Transylvania, Banat, and Moldova. While Romanian philology has a rich tradition of qualitative analysis, the increasing volume of digitized historical texts, contemporary speech corpora, and ethnographic recordings necessitates advanced computational methods to detect patterns across time, space, and social strata. The primary research problem involves modeling dialectal variation at scale, including phonetic shifts, lexical borrowing, and syntactic innovations influenced by contact with neighboring languages and digital communication trends. To achieve this, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for Romanian’s morphological complexity, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on historical and modern texts, dialect-specific speech recognition systems, and geospatial visualization tools. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on heterogeneous datasets (spanning 16th-century manuscripts to social media corpora) and running parallelized comparative analyses across millions of tokens. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible digital atlas of Romanian dialects with dynamic visualization layers; (2) open-source tools for automated dialect classification and historical text normalization; and (3) quantitative evidence informing debates on language standardization policies. The computational infrastructure will enable the first large-scale synthesis of Romania’s linguistic diversity, with applications in education, cultural preservation, and technology localization. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological expertise, this project aims to establish a replicable framework for under-resourced language research while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies in the humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Romanian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.
