abstract: Agricultural and Extension Education Services face increasing demands to address complex challenges in modern agriculture, including dynamic pest pressures, climate variability, and the need for data-driven decision support systems. Current approaches often rely on static models or localized datasets, limiting their ability to predict system-wide outcomes or deliver timely, scalable solutions to diverse agricultural stakeholders. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive frameworks integrating multi-scale agricultural data, enabling real-time analysis and adaptive management strategies. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate pest population dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes, machine learning algorithms to optimize irrigation and nutrient application under variable climate conditions, and network analysis to evaluate the efficacy of extension education campaigns. Computational workflows will process spatially explicit datasets from remote sensing, soil sensors, and regional pest monitoring networks, requiring parallelized processing for large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include open-access decision support tools that quantify trade-offs between agricultural productivity, input costs, and environmental impacts, tailored for use by extension educators and producers. By coupling these computational models with participatory feedback systems, the project will advance precision agriculture education while maintaining practical relevance to small-scale operations. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the stochasticity inherent in biological systems and the high-dimensional data generated by IoT devices in smart farming applications. Successful implementation will provide extension services with evidence-based protocols for sustainable pest management, climate resilience training modules, and metrics to assess technology adoption rates across diverse farming communities. This work bridges computational agriculture with adult education methodologies, creating a novel paradigm for translating complex models into actionable guidance through cooperative extension networks.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide referral, consulting, technical assistance, and educational services to gardeners, farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and other organizations. Includes instruction in basic agricultural sciences, agricultural business operations, pest control, adult education methods, public relations, applicable state laws and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address operational inefficiencies in food service management, focusing on the optimization of dining room workflows, staff allocation, and customer satisfaction. Despite advances in hospitality technology, many restaurants struggle to balance dynamic variables such as fluctuating customer demand, real-time staff performance, and post-pandemic sanitation protocols. Traditional manual or rule-based approaches often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these factors, leading to suboptimal resource use, prolonged wait times, and inconsistent service quality. To resolve this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), discrete-event simulation (DES), and reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate and analyze complex dining room ecosystems. The ABM component will model customer behavior, including arrival patterns, seating preferences, and meal duration variability, while DES will map staff movements, table turnover, and sanitation workflows. RL algorithms will then iteratively optimize staff-task assignments and seating policies under constraints such as labor costs and hygiene compliance. By scaling these simulations across HPC clusters, we will generate granular insights into high-efficiency service configurations under diverse scenarios (e.g., peak hours, special events). Expected outcomes include a predictive decision-support tool capable of recommending adaptive staffing levels, table layouts, and workflow prioritization in real time. This tool will be validated against empirical data from partner restaurants, with success metrics including reduced customer wait times (target: 15–20%), improved staff utilization rates, and enhanced compliance with safety protocols. The project bridges computational modeling and hospitality management, offering a novel application of HPC to a non-traditional domain while advancing operational sustainability in food service industries.
cip_title: Food Service, Waiter/Waitress, and Dining Room Management/Manager.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve food to customers in formal or informal settings.  Includes instruction in the nutritional, sensory, and functional properties of food and its ingredients; food services principles; table and counter services; dining room operations and procedures; service personnel supervision and management; communication skills; business math; safety; and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize customer service operations in high-volume call centers through advanced computational modeling of real-time agent-customer interaction dynamics. While traditional approaches focus on process engineering or workforce management, this research addresses a critical gap: the inability to predict and adapt to emergent conversational patterns that drive customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose developing a multimodal machine learning framework to analyze terabyte-scale datasets encompassing voice recordings, sentiment markers, CRM metadata, and agent assist tool usage logs from a multinational teleservice provider. The computational methodology combines transformer-based natural language processing for real-time dialogue analysis, graph neural networks to map knowledge base utilization patterns, and multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate optimal response pathways under varying workload conditions. Key technical challenges include processing 50,000+ concurrent voice streams with <200ms latency, maintaining temporal coherence across asynchronous customer journeys, and scaling recommendation systems across 15+ language domains. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model identifying at-risk interactions 40% earlier than current threshold-based systems, (2) dynamic resource allocation algorithms that reduce average handle time by 18% while maintaining quality metrics, and (3) an open-source framework for ethical AI-assisted coaching in customer-facing roles. This work bridges computational linguistics, operations research, and human-computer interaction, offering novel insights into the cognitive ergonomics of hybrid human-AI service teams. Successful implementation could transform $350B+ global customer experience markets by enabling real-time adaptive systems that balance economic constraints with complex psychosocial interaction requirements.
cip_title: Customer Service Support/ Call Center/ Teleservice Operation
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist customers with inquiries and problems in frontline call centers, help desks, teleservice centers, and online. Includes instruction in user interfaces and user behavior, principles of hardware and software systems operation, customer interaction skills, telephone and e-mailing skills, data entry, and database and Internet searching and retrieval.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the theoretical and practical understanding of computational complexity in automated verification, with a focus on developing scalable algorithms for model checking temporal logic formulas. The core challenge lies in the exponential growth of state spaces for concurrent and distributed systems, which limits the applicability of existing verification tools to real-world systems. Traditional sequential algorithms for evaluating linear temporal logic (LTL) and computation tree logic (CTL) properties struggle with systems exceeding 10^6 states, necessitating new approaches that leverage parallel architectures. We propose a hybrid methodology combining symbolic model checking with distributed graph traversal techniques, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) developing a partitioned representation of transition systems using binary decision diagrams (BDDs) to minimize inter-node communication, (2) implementing asynchronous counterexample search algorithms across GPU and CPU clusters, and (3) creating adaptive heuristics that dynamically allocate resources based on formula structure and state space topology. The project will utilize MPI for distributed memory management and CUDA for GPU acceleration, with rigorous complexity analysis to quantify speedup factors under different scaling regimes. Expected outcomes include open-source implementations of the proposed algorithms, theoretical bounds on parallel verification complexity classes, and practical benchmarks demonstrating verification of systems with 10^8+ states. This work will directly contribute to foundational knowledge in computational logic while addressing critical bottlenecks in formal methods for safety-critical systems. Successful completion could enable new applications in automated reasoning for large-scale distributed protocols, biological system modeling, and AI safety verification, bridging theoretical computer science with practical engineering challenges. Resource requests emphasize GPU node allocation and large-memory systems for BDD manipulation, with an estimated need for 500,000 core-hours across the project timeline.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical techniques underlying computing, including the theory of computation, and logic in computer science and artificial intelligence.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges of modeling emergent phenomena in multi-component, non-equilibrium systems, which are critical to advancing next-generation technologies in energy storage, catalytic materials, and bio-inspired sensors. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve the dynamic interplay of quantum, molecular, and mesoscale interactions in these systems, while existing computational methods lack the scalability to capture spatially heterogeneous and temporally evolving behaviors across multiple physical scales. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC), and finite element analysis (FEA), coupled with machine learning-driven parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations across disparate time and length scales, manage the combinatorial complexity of material configurations, and train surrogate models on terabytes of multi-fidelity data. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for DFT calculations, distributed-memory architectures for ensemble kMC sampling, and in-memory databases for real-time data integration. Expected outcomes include predictive models for designing metastable materials with tailored electronic and catalytic properties, open-source software tools for cross-scale simulation workflows, and validated protocols for embedding machine learning into multi-physics frameworks. By enabling the systematic exploration of non-equilibrium phase spaces, this work will accelerate the discovery of functional materials for sustainable energy applications while advancing computational methodologies in underrepresented areas of science-related technologies. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster will support 18 months of simulations, including validation against synchrotron X-ray diffraction and in situ microscopy data from collaborating experimental groups.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in science technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Educational leaders face complex challenges in optimizing institutional decision-making processes, particularly when balancing resource allocation, policy implementation, and student outcomes across dynamic school systems. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the multidimensional interactions between administrative strategies, stakeholder behaviors, and systemic inequities. This project proposes the development of an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate district-level decision-making processes and evaluate the longitudinal impacts of leadership policies on organizational efficiency and equity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will model large-scale educational ecosystems comprising thousands of autonomous agents representing administrators, teachers, students, and community members. The computational framework will integrate machine learning techniques with institutional datasets (e.g., budget allocations, staffing patterns, student performance metrics) to parameterize decision pathways and emergent behaviors. Parallel computing architectures will enable simultaneous testing of multiple policy scenarios, including interventions targeting resource distribution models, professional development frameworks, and equity-focused initiatives. Sensitivity analyses will identify critical leverage points in leadership practices that disproportionately influence educational access and institutional resilience. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to help administrators visualize policy consequences, optimize resource deployment, and mitigate unintended disparities. By quantifying how micro-level decisions propagate through complex educational systems, this work aims to advance evidence-based leadership practices while establishing computational social science methodologies within educational administration research. The HPC component is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of interacting variables across temporal, spatial, and organizational scales inherent in district-level simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and techniques of administering a wide variety of schools and other educational organizations and facilities, supervising educational personnel at the school or staff level, and that may prepare individuals as general administrators and supervisors.

abstract: Agricultural extension services face growing challenges in delivering timely, scalable, and evidence-based recommendations to farmers, particularly in optimizing integrated pest management (IPM) strategies that balance economic viability, crop yield, and environmental sustainability. Current approaches often rely on static models or localized field trials, which struggle to account for dynamic interactions between pest populations, crop genetics, climate variability, and management practices across diverse agroecosystems. This project seeks to develop a predictive computational framework to simulate pest-crop-environment interactions at scale, enabling extension professionals to generate region-specific IPM guidance. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models that integrate multi-year pest surveillance data, genomic traits of resistant crop cultivars, and high-resolution climate projections. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to identify patterns in pest population dynamics under varying management scenarios, while sensitivity analyses will quantify the relative impacts of biological, chemical, and cultural control methods. The computational workflow will process terabytes of heterogeneous agricultural datasets, including geospatial layers of farm operations, real-time sensor networks from partner cooperatives, and historical outbreak records. By parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, this approach will enable rapid scenario testing unachievable with conventional computing infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access decision support toolkit that extension agents can use to customize IPM strategies for specific crops, regions, and farm scales. This research directly enhances the precision and responsiveness of agricultural education services while reducing reliance on blanket pesticide recommendations. The computational framework will also provide a template for addressing analogous challenges in livestock disease management and precision agriculture, strengthening the scientific foundation of extension programming nationally.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and metabolic determinants of personalized exercise adherence in sedentary populations, a critical yet understudied factor in long-term health outcomes. While public health frameworks broadly address physical activity promotion, individual variability in biomechanics, neuromuscular efficiency, and metabolic response remains a barrier to designing universally effective exercise regimens. We aim to develop a computational model integrating motion capture data, physiological biomarkers, and psychological self-reports to predict optimal exercise modalities for sustaining adherence. The research problem centers on resolving how idiosyncratic physiological constraints interact with behavioral preferences to influence compliance, particularly in populations with obesity or early-stage metabolic syndrome. Using HPC clusters, we will process high-resolution biomechanical datasets from wearable sensors (sampled at 200 Hz) and merge these with metabolomic profiles derived from mass spectrometry. Machine learning pipelines will train on these multimodal datasets to identify latent patterns linking biomechanical efficiency, perceived exertion, and biochemical markers of exercise adaptation. Agent-based modeling will then simulate long-term adherence scenarios under varying exercise prescriptions. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for tailoring exercise interventions to individual biomechanical and metabolic phenotypes, with potential applications in workplace wellness programs and community health initiatives. By quantifying previously intangible interactions between physiology and behavior, this work could redefine how health systems operationalize "personalized" exercise guidance, moving beyond generic recommendations toward computationally optimized prescriptions. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the terabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing complex simulations, and iterating neural network architectures within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to assume roles as health/wellness professionals in private business and industry, community organizations, and health care settings. Includes instruction in personal health, community health and welfare, nutrition, epidemiology, disease prevention, fitness and exercise, and health behaviors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model the dynamic interactions between dietary compounds, gut microbiota, and host metabolic pathways in the context of personalized nutrition. Current understanding of diet-microbiome-host tripartite relationships remains fragmented due to the complexity of multivariate interactions, individual variability in microbial composition, and nonlinear metabolic responses. Traditional reductionist approaches fail to capture the emergent properties of these systems, limiting the translation of nutritional science into precision dietary interventions. To address this gap, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of microbial communities, genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction, and probabilistic machine learning to simulate how personalized dietary patterns modulate microbiota functionality and host health outcomes. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across simulated gut ecosystems, integrating multi-omic datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and host transcriptomic) from clinical cohorts to refine model accuracy. Key computational challenges include resolving time-dependent metabolic flux distributions at microbial population scales, optimizing hybrid ABM–ODE systems for host-microbe metabolite exchange, and training neural networks on sparse longitudinal nutritional data. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying dietary strategies to stabilize dysbiotic states in metabolic syndrome, (2) a publicly accessible simulation platform for testing hypotheses about microbiota-nutrient interactions, and (3) biomarkers linking specific microbial metabolic functions to dietary responsiveness. By bridging computational systems biology with nutritional epidemiology, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of diet-host-microbiome dynamics while providing a foundation for data-driven personalized nutrition recommendations. The requested resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of microbial communities, scaling metabolomic network analyses, and achieving sufficient statistical power in individual-level simulations.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the utilization of food for human growth and metabolism, in both normal and dysfunctional states, from the interdisciplinary perspective of the agricultural, human, biological, and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in food science, biochemistry, physiology, dietetics, food and nutrition studies, biotechnology, biophysics, and the clinical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of digital community formation and spiritual engagement among adolescents within youth ministry contexts. While youth ministries increasingly integrate digital platforms for outreach, mentorship, and worship, there is limited empirical understanding of how online interactions correlate with long-term spiritual development or psychosocial well-being. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in digital communication—such as social media engagement, virtual small group interactions, and multimedia content consumption—that predict meaningful spiritual growth or disengagement among youth. Using anonymized datasets from partner organizations (including text, video analytics, and longitudinal survey responses), the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) to classify emotional and theological themes in youth-generated content, network analysis to map relational dynamics within digital communities, and agent-based modeling to simulate the long-term impacts of varying ministry strategies. Computational challenges include processing large volumes of unstructured text and video data, training custom NLP models sensitive to religious vernacular, and simulating nonlinear behavioral outcomes across diverse demographic cohorts. Outcomes will provide youth ministry practitioners with evidence-based frameworks for optimizing digital outreach, mitigating risks of alienation in hybrid (online/in-person) environments, and fostering inclusive communities that align with developmental needs. By integrating computational social science methods with theological anthropology, this interdisciplinary work advances Humanities scholarship at the intersection of technology, spirituality, and adolescent development—a niche underexplored by traditional disciplines. The requested HPC resources are critical for scaling analyses beyond pilot datasets and ensuring robust, generalizable insights for faith-based organizations serving youth globally.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to children, adolescents, and young adults. Includes instruction in child and adolescent psychology, human growth and development, family studies, communication skills, religious education, youth counseling, small group leadership, planning and organizing youth activities, volunteer supervision, and youth evangelism and worship.

abstract: Entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) are critical biocontrol agents against agricultural insect pests, yet their efficacy under variable environmental conditions remains unpredictable. This project seeks to model the tripartite interactions between EPNs (Steinernema spp. and Heterorhabditis spp.), their symbiotic bacteria (Xenorhabdus spp. and Photorhabdus spp.), and target insect hosts under spatially heterogeneous soil ecosystems. The research problem centers on identifying nonlinear thresholds in soil moisture, temperature, and microbial competition that disrupt nematode-host localization and symbiont-mediated insect immunosuppression. Current gap analyses lack integration of 3D soil microstructure data with population-genetic dynamics of nematode-bacteria mutualism, limiting predictive models for field applications. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC) framework combining discrete element method (DEM) simulations of soil particle dynamics, agent-based modeling of nematode foraging behavior, and genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions of bacterial symbionts. Multi-layered environmental datasets from mesocosm experiments will parameterize Monte Carlo simulations examining resilience to drought-induced lipid depletion in nematodes and phage-driven shifts in bacterial virulence factors. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods for pore-scale hydrology and parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling for Bayesian inference of host infection probabilities. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive atlas of EPN performance across soil typologies, (2) identification of conserved metabolic bottlenecks in nematode-symbiont resource exchange, and (3) optimization algorithms for spatiotemporal biocontrol deployment. By resolving how microscale environmental gradients mediate macroscale pest suppression, this work will establish computational pipelines for translating laboratory findings into climate-resilient agricultural management strategies. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale combinatorial simulations spanning molecular interactions to ecosystem-level emergent properties.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) and insect species/populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: Advances in clinical laboratory science increasingly rely on integrating complex, multi-modal datasets to address challenges in diagnostics, biomarker discovery, and precision medicine. However, the analysis of high-dimensional data—such as genomic sequences, proteomic profiles, and digital pathology images—exceeds the capacity of standard computational infrastructure. This project proposes the development of a scalable computational framework to analyze heterogeneous clinical laboratory datasets using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The primary research problem involves overcoming bottlenecks in processing speed, data integration, and model training that currently limit the translation of large-scale biomedical data into actionable clinical insights. Our approach combines parallelized bioinformatics pipelines for genomic variant calling, deep learning models for image-based phenotyping, and graph-based algorithms to map correlations between molecular signatures and patient outcomes. These workflows will be optimized for GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures to handle datasets exceeding 100 TB in size, including whole-genome sequences from 10,000 patients and high-resolution histopathology images. Key deliverables include open-source tools for federated learning across multi-institutional datasets and a predictive model linking microbial metagenomic profiles to sepsis risk in critically ill patients. The expected significance lies in enabling real-time analysis of emerging clinical data during hospital outbreaks or therapeutic trials, directly supporting rapid diagnostic decision-making. By leveraging HPC resources, this work aims to establish a reproducible pipeline for integrating research-grade omics data into routine laboratory workflows, bridging a critical gap between translational research and clinical practice. Successful implementation will provide a template for resource-constrained laboratories to adopt advanced computational methods without compromising data security or regulatory compliance.
cip_title: Clinical/ Medical Laboratory Science and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in clinical/medical laboratory science and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for high-fidelity real-time animation and interactive visual effects in media production presents significant computational challenges, particularly in rendering complex simulations and maintaining interactivity in immersive environments. Current workflows often struggle with the processing requirements for physics-based dynamics, detailed 3D models, and AI-driven content generation, leading to bottlenecks in creativity and production efficiency. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable computational pipelines for advanced animation and special effects. The research will focus on parallelizing rendering tasks using GPU clusters to accelerate ray tracing and photon mapping techniques, enabling real-time visualization of intricate scenes. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be implemented on distributed systems to automate texture synthesis and character animation, reducing manual labor while enhancing artistic control. High-fidelity fluid and particle simulations, critical for realistic environmental effects, will be optimized through adaptive mesh refinement and hybrid CPU-GPU architectures. The integration of these computational methods aims to push the boundaries of interactive storytelling and virtual production, particularly in applications such as augmented reality journalism and educational simulations. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-source tools that democratize access to high-end visual effects workflows, a framework for real-time collaborative editing in virtual environments, and novel techniques for balancing computational efficiency with artistic intent. By providing insights into optimizing resource allocation for creative processes, this project will contribute to both the technical and artistic advancement of digital media, fostering innovation in communication strategies across entertainment, journalism, and experiential learning platforms.
cip_title: Animation, Interactive Technology, Video Graphics, and Special Effects
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use computer applications and related visual and sound imaging techniques to manipulate images and information originating as film, video, still photographs, digital copy, soundtracks, and physical objects in order to communicate messages simulating real-world content. Includes instruction in specialized camerawork and equipment operation and maintenance, image capture, computer programming, dubbing, CAD applications, and applications to specific commercial, industrial, and entertainment needs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing computational demands of advanced digital media creation and algorithmic design processes in commercial and advertising art. As the field increasingly integrates high-resolution 3D modeling, real-time rendering, and AI-driven generative tools, traditional local workstations face limitations in processing complex visual datasets, simulating dynamic advertising environments, and optimizing iterative design workflows. The research problem centers on overcoming these bottlenecks to enable scalable, efficient production of multimedia content while exploring novel computational methods for artistic innovation. Proposed work includes parallelized rendering of ultra-high-definition visual assets, training machine learning models for generative design applications (e.g., automated layout optimization, style transfer, and audience-targeted visual customization), and large-scale simulations of consumer interaction patterns with digital advertisements. Computational methods will utilize GPU-accelerated frameworks for neural style transfer and GAN-based asset generation, distributed rendering pipelines for collaborative projects, and agent-based modeling to simulate viewer engagement metrics across diverse demographic datasets. By implementing these approaches on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to reduce processing times for 4K/8K multimedia projects by 60-75%, enable real-time iteration on complex design variants, and produce empirically validated insights into computational aesthetics for advertising efficacy. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for HPC-accelerated commercial art workflows, a dataset linking computational design parameters to consumer engagement metrics, and case studies demonstrating scalable pipelines for immersive advertising media. This research will advance the integration of computational methods in visual communication disciplines, offering new methodologies for data-driven artistic practice while addressing industry needs for rapid, large-scale content production. The requested resources directly support both technical experimentation and pedagogical initiatives, ensuring students gain proficiency in cutting-edge computational art techniques that bridge creative and technological domains.

Includes instruction in concept design, layout, paste-up, and techniques such as engraving, etching, silkscreen, lithography, offset, drawing and cartooning, painting, collage, and computer graphics.

abstract: The rapid evolution of consumer behavior and supply chain dynamics has created a critical gap in merchandising decision-making tools, particularly in optimizing product assortment and inventory allocation under volatile demand. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computational framework to simulate and predict the cascading effects of real-time consumer sentiment, supply chain disruptions, and competitive pricing actions on retail buying outcomes. Traditional merchandising models rely on historical sales data and static trend analysis, which fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between social media-driven demand shifts, supplier lead time variability, and perishability constraints in fast-moving consumer goods. Using agent-based modeling and graph neural networks, we will construct a dynamic simulation environment that maps multi-echelon retail networks, incorporating heterogeneous consumer segments, vendor negotiation parameters, and product lifecycle trajectories. The computational architecture will require parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate probabilistic scenarios for product substitution effects, markdown optimization, and deadstock risk across 10,000+ SKUs. By integrating live social media sentiment data and supplier API feeds, the model will iteratively retrain to adapt to emerging trends. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies the resilience of buying strategies under stochastic disruptions, reducing excess inventory costs by an estimated 12–18% in simulated retail environments. This work bridges computational social science and operations research, advancing the use of adaptive AI in merchandising while addressing sustainability challenges through waste reduction. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential to handle the memory-intensive graph computations and hyperparameter tuning across multi-terabyte datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional buyers of resale products and product lines for stores, chains, and other retail enterprises. Includes instruction in product evaluation, merchandising, applicable aspects of brand and consumer research, principles of purchasing, and negotiation skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inequities in consumer-facing algorithmic systems by developing computational tools to audit and mitigate bias in automated recommendation platforms used across retail, financial services, and healthcare sectors. While such systems increasingly influence consumer access to credit, healthcare options, and fair pricing, their proprietary nature and computational complexity create barriers for independent oversight. Our research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to reverse-engineer algorithmic behavior through large-scale simulations of consumer interaction patterns, enabling systematic analysis of disparate impacts across demographic groups. Using synthetically generated datasets reflecting diverse socioeconomic profiles, we will train surrogate models to approximate black-box commercial systems while preserving privacy constraints. Computational workflows will combine graph neural networks to map recommendation ecosystems, Monte Carlo methods to simulate decision cascades, and adversarial machine learning techniques to identify vulnerability points where biases amplify. The project’s hybrid approach—blending consumer protection frameworks with computational social science methodologies—requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale interaction logs and millions of synthetic agent simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source benchmarking toolkit for quantifying algorithmic fairness in consumer services, validated through partnerships with advocacy organizations. By enabling granular analysis of how automated systems disproportionately steer vulnerable populations toward suboptimal financial products or restricted healthcare options, this work aims to establish reproducible standards for third-party algorithmic audits while advancing computational methods tailored to consumer protection research. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive graph computations and iterative model training cycles that exceed the capacity of local academic computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on providing end-use advice and representational services to individuals and groups within a variety of settings, and the analytical and research techniques needed to protect consumers from unsafe, unreliable, and/or unhealthy products and services. Includes instruction in consumer advocacy, family management systems, ecological impacts of consumption practices, and analyzing and testing product quality and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of audience engagement in fragmented digital media environments by developing a computational model to optimize real-time communication strategies for public relations and advertising campaigns. Current approaches to audience segmentation and message tailoring rely on static demographic data or coarse-grained behavioral metrics, limiting their adaptability to rapidly shifting online discourse dynamics. To bridge this gap, we propose implementing natural language processing (NLP) architectures and network analysis tools on high-performance computing (HPC) systems to process multi-platform social media data at scale. The computational workflow will integrate transformer-based models for sentiment and topic detection across multilingual user-generated content, coupled with temporal graph analysis to map information diffusion patterns among overlapping audience clusters. By leveraging GPU-accelerated training and distributed memory parallelism, the system will analyze terabytes of streaming data from platforms including X (Twitter), TikTok, and Reddit, while maintaining the low-latency processing required for responsive campaign adjustments. Expected outcomes include a framework for simulating audience response to proposed messaging strategies before deployment, significantly reducing risks in crisis communication scenarios. The research will additionally produce open-source tools for ethical audience analytics, addressing concerns about privacy-preserving data aggregation in organizational communication. Results will advance theoretical understanding of cross-platform narrative convergence while providing practitioners with evidence-based methods to enhance message resonance in increasingly polarized digital spaces. This work requires HPC resources due to the concurrent demands of training large language models on heterogeneous text corpora, maintaining real-time inference pipelines across multiple data streams, and executing complex network simulations with millions of node-edge interactions.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance early childhood education research by modeling the interplay between instructional strategies, classroom environments, and developmental outcomes in preschool-aged children. A critical challenge in kindergarten and preschool education is the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to evaluate how dynamic, multimodal interactions—between teachers, students, and learning materials—affect skill acquisition in foundational domains such as literacy, numeracy, and social-emotional development. Traditional observational methods are limited in capturing the complexity of these interactions at scale, particularly across diverse classroom settings. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate classroom dynamics using real-world datasets from video observations, student assessments, and teacher logs. The ABM framework will parameterize individual learner behaviors, teacher intervention patterns, and environmental factors (e.g., activity schedules, resource availability), while ML techniques will analyze longitudinal data to identify predictors of optimal learning trajectories. HPC resources are essential to handle the high dimensionality of multimodal data (e.g., speech, gaze, and motion tracking) and to run large-scale simulations testing hypothetical teaching strategies under varying constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated computational model to predict how specific instructional choices—such as play-based versus structured activities—correlate with developmental gains, as well as actionable insights for designing teacher training modules. This work will provide a novel, scalable tool for educators to iteratively refine pedagogical practices, ultimately supporting equitable, evidence-based early learning experiences. By integrating computational rigor with developmental theory, the project bridges a critical gap in teacher education, empowering preschool educators with data-driven strategies tailored to the heterogeneous needs of young learners.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in formal settings prior to beginning regular elementary school, usually ranging in age from three to six years (or grade one), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation strategies in multi-unit hospitality ecosystems under volatile demand conditions. The hospitality industry faces increasing complexity due to fluctuating traveler preferences, climate-related disruptions, and supply chain interdependencies across lodging, transportation, and experience-based services. Existing pricing models often fail to account for real-time cross-domain variables such as localized weather impacts, event-driven demand spikes, and sustainability-linked operational constraints. We propose an adaptive machine learning architecture leveraging transformer-based neural networks and multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate system-wide decision-making across geographically distributed hospitality assets. The computational approach will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including IoT sensor networks from smart facilities, social sentiment analysis, and environmental impact metrics—to generate predictive models capable of hour-ahead resource optimization. High-performance computing resources are required to train ensemble models on historical operational datasets (5+ TB of transactional, meteorological, and customer behavior data) and run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations evaluating 10,000+ scenario permutations for risk-aware pricing strategies. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that reduces revenue volatility by 12-18% in simulated crisis scenarios while maintaining carbon emission targets, as well as novel metrics for quantifying resilience trade-offs in hospitality resource networks. This work bridges computational economics and operational sustainability in tourism ecosystems, offering a template for data-driven governance of complex service industry interdependencies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as general managers and directors of hospitality operations on a system-wide basis, including both travel arrangements and promotion and the provision of traveler facilities. Includes instruction in principles of operations in the travel and tourism, hotel and lodging facilities, food services, and recreation facilities industries; hospitality marketing strategies; hospitality planning; management and coordination of franchise and unit operations; business management; accounting and financial management; hospitality transportation and logistics; and hospitality industry policies and regulations.

abstract: The development of advanced metal alloys capable of withstanding extreme thermo-mechanical conditions remains a critical challenge in metallurgical engineering. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize microstructural properties and processing parameters are often time-intensive and limited in resolving multiscale phenomena. This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to establish a predictive framework for microstructure evolution in nickel-based superalloys during additive manufacturing and high-temperature service. Computational methods will integrate molecular dynamics simulations to model atomic-scale defect dynamics, phase-field modeling for mesoscale grain growth and precipitation behavior, and machine learning algorithms to accelerate parameter space exploration. These multiscale simulations will explicitly couple thermal gradients, solidification kinetics, and stress accumulation effects, enabling the quantification of process-structure-property relationships across spatial and temporal domains. The research aims to identify alloy compositions and heat treatment protocols that minimize creep deformation while maintaining fracture toughness under cyclic loading. Successful implementation will provide fundamental insights into dislocation-precipitate interactions, pore formation mechanisms, and thermal stability limits in next-generation superalloys. By correlating virtual experiments with physical validation data, the project will deliver optimized processing guidelines and open-source simulation tools for the metallurgy community. The anticipated outcomes directly address industry needs for durable materials in energy generation and transportation systems, supporting technological advancements through computationally driven alloy design. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the high computational cost of billion-atom molecular dynamics systems, multiphase phase-field models, and data-intensive machine learning workflows, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and metallurgical principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of metal components of structural, load-bearing, power, transmission, and moving systems; and the analysis of engineering problems such as stress, creep, failure, alloy behavior, environmental fluctuations, stability, electromagnetic and thermodynamic characteristics, optimal manufacturing processes, and related design considerations.

abstract: The growing complexity of patient care in practical nursing settings necessitates advanced tools to optimize clinical decision-making and workforce allocation. Current approaches to predicting patient outcomes and staffing needs often rely on static guidelines, which fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff skill mix, and real-time resource availability. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework for simulating patient care scenarios and modeling risk stratification in real time. Leveraging anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), staffing logs, and sensor-derived patient mobility data from three regional healthcare networks, we will train machine learning models to predict adverse events (e.g., falls, medication errors) and simulate staffing configurations using agent-based modeling. The computational demands of processing multi-terabyte datasets, coupled with the need for parallelized execution of thousands of simulated care scenarios, require dedicated HPC resources to achieve practical runtime thresholds. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive tool for identifying high-risk patients, (2) evidence-based staffing algorithms that dynamically adjust to unit-level demands, and (3) a validated simulation environment for nursing education programs. By integrating these computational tools into vocational nursing curricula and clinical practice guidelines, this research aims to enhance care quality while reducing preventable adverse events by an estimated 15–20% in participating facilities. The project will also establish a replicable methodology for applying HPC resources to workforce optimization challenges in frontline healthcare delivery, directly supporting the training of nursing professionals in data-informed care strategies. This work bridges a critical gap between computational innovation and practical nursing applications, offering scalable solutions to improve patient outcomes and operational efficiency in diverse healthcare settings.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in textual studies, focusing on the computational analysis of large-scale textual corpora spanning print, manuscript, and digital formats. The core research problem centers on reconstructing historical textual lineages and identifying patterns of transmission, adaptation, and cultural influence across premodern to modern works. Traditional manual collation and stemmatological methods struggle to address the scale and complexity of multilingual, multiformat datasets, which include digitized manuscripts, early printed books, and born-digital texts. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a hybrid computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), phylogenetic modeling, and graph-based network analysis. Customized algorithms will be developed to automate collation, detect textual variants, and model relationships between versions of texts across time and media. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on non-standard historical languages, processing high-resolution manuscript images via computer vision techniques, and simulating probabilistic stemma reconstructions at scale. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for textual scholars, new empirical insights into textual transmission networks in three case studies (medieval legal codices, early modern scientific correspondence, and 20th-century avant-garde periodicals), and methodological frameworks for integrating material book history with linguistic analysis. By enabling the systematic study of textual variance and cultural context across previously intractable datasets, this work aims to redefine interdisciplinary boundaries in textual scholarship while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources for humanities research. The project will also generate annotated training datasets and reproducible workflows to support future computational textual studies, fostering collaboration between literary scholars, digital archivists, and computational researchers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interconnected histories of digital or print texts and manuscripts for cultural and literary study. Includes instruction in archiving texts, bibliography, book and literary history, cultural studies, codicology, paleography, stemmatology, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing multi-echelon supply chain networks under uncertainty, with applications to business operations in logistics, manufacturing, and retail. Traditional methods for supply chain optimization often struggle with dynamic demand fluctuations, supplier disruptions, and complex interdependencies between inventory, production, and distribution nodes. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach integrating stochastic optimization, Monte Carlo simulation, and reinforcement learning. The research will model supply chain networks as Markov decision processes with time-dependent constraints, using parallelized scenario generation to evaluate risk and resilience metrics across thousands of simulated operational scenarios. Key computational challenges include solving large-scale mixed-integer linear programs with chance constraints and training adaptive reinforcement learning policies for real-time decision support. The project will implement decomposition algorithms (e.g., L-shaped method) accelerated via distributed computing, coupled with deep reinforcement learning architectures (e.g., proximal policy optimization) to handle state spaces with over 10^5 dimensions. By leveraging GPU-accelerated optimization and asynchronous parameter servers, we aim to reduce solution times for industry-scale problems from days to hours. Expected outcomes include (1) decision-support tools for robust resource allocation under uncertainty, (2) benchmark datasets comparing computational strategies for supply chain optimization, and (3) open-source implementations of hybrid simulation-optimization workflows. The HPC resources requested are critical for managing memory-intensive scenario trees, parallelizing hyperparameter tuning, and validating models against real-world business datasets with >1 million transaction records. This work will advance computational operations research methodologies while providing actionable insights for enterprises managing complex, globalized supply chains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems. These programs have a focus on business operations or applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the genetic and environmental determinants of complex diseases in diverse populations, with a focus on advancing equity in public health genetics. Genetic research increasingly highlights polygenic risk scores (PRS) and gene-environment interactions as critical drivers of disease susceptibility, yet existing models often lack generalizability across ancestrally diverse cohorts, perpetuating health disparities. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS), multi-omic data (genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic), and environmental exposure datasets from public biobanks. Machine learning models will be trained to identify population-specific risk variants and optimize PRS calibration while accounting for structural biases in genomic datasets. The scale of data—spanning millions of genetic variants, electronic health records, and geospatial environmental variables—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallelized processing, large-memory simulations, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include (1) validated, ancestry-informed risk prediction tools for conditions such as cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes, (2) mechanistic insights into gene-environment interplay in understudied populations, and (3) open-access computational pipelines to support ethical translation of genetic findings into public health practice. By elucidating genetic risk architectures within diverse social and environmental contexts, this work aims to directly inform equitable screening guidelines, precision prevention strategies, and policy discussions on the ethical use of polygenic risk tools. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome computational bottlenecks in handling multi-terabyte datasets and enable reproducible, large-scale analyses that bridge genetic discovery and population health implementation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to respond to the complex social, legal, ethical, and public health policy implications generated by genetic research. Includes instruction in biochemical genetics of complex diseases, bioethics, chromosomes and human disease, genetic counseling, genetic epidemiology, gene mapping, human population genetics, and the molecular basis of human inherited disease.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing autonomous vehicle (AV) deployment across multimodal transportation networks. While existing scholarship in transportation law focuses on doctrinal or policy-based critiques, this research addresses a computational gap: modeling how heterogeneous legal regimes—spanning municipal, state, federal, and international jurisdictions—interact dynamically with rapidly advancing AV technologies. The complexity arises from (1) the scale of interconnected regulations (e.g., liability statutes, data privacy mandates, infrastructure standards) and (2) the need to simulate how emergent case law and regulatory amendments propagate uncertainty across transportation systems. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will develop a graph-based computational model to map regulatory dependencies and conflicts, paired with agent-based simulations to evaluate how hypothetical legal scenarios influence AV adoption rates and operational risk profiles. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will process over 10,000 legal documents (statutes, court opinions, administrative rulings) to extract relational features, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in liability attribution under varying regulatory conditions. The HPC environment is critical for scaling graph traversals across multi-jurisdictional legal networks and running high-fidelity simulations incorporating real-world transportation data. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital toolkit for policymakers to stress-test proposed regulations and a taxonomy of "legal friction points" that impede cross-jurisdictional AV interoperability. By integrating computational social science with transportation law, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for analyzing complex legal systems as dynamic, data-driven networks, offering novel insights into the governance of emerging technologies in non-science/engineering domains.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting land, sea, air, and space transportation.

abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of aromatherapy relies on the complex interactions of bioactive compounds within essential oil blends, yet the molecular mechanisms underpinning their synergistic effects remain poorly characterized. Traditional approaches to blend formulation often depend on empirical observations, which lack the precision needed to optimize therapeutic outcomes and ensure safety. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to systematically model the physicochemical and pharmacological interactions of essential oil components at scale. Using molecular dynamics simulations and machine learning algorithms, we will analyze the binding affinities, diffusion kinetics, and metabolic pathways of key terpenes, phenols, and esters across biological targets relevant to aromatherapy applications. Computational models will integrate data from gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) profiles, pharmacokinetic databases, and cytotoxicity assays to predict optimal blending ratios while accounting for individual variability in absorption and sensitivity. The anticipated outcomes include a validated predictive framework for rational essential oil formulation, an open-access database of compound interaction networks, and evidence-based safety protocols for topical and olfactory administration. By elucidating structure-function relationships in aromatherapeutic blends, this research aims to advance clinical practice guidelines, support personalized treatment planning, and establish computational chemistry as a cornerstone of modern aromatherapy education and practice. The scale of multi-omic data integration and the combinatorial complexity of blend permutations necessitate HPC capabilities to achieve statistically robust results within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide therapeutic care through the preparation and application of extracted essential oils from plants, including flowers (botanicals), roots, berries, and bark. Includes instruction in aromatherapy history and theory, basic physiology of absorption, aromachemistry, organic chemistry, botanical taxonomy, carrier oils, essential oils, extraction methods, blending techniques, application methods, safety, client consultation and treatment planning, business management, professional standards and ethics, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for the study of Catalan linguistic diversity and its historical evolution. Despite Catalan’s rich dialectal variation and its significance across cultural, educational, and technological domains, scalable computational tools for analyzing its regional and historical forms remain underdeveloped. The research aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale textual and speech corpora spanning medieval manuscripts to contemporary digital sources, enabling systematic investigations into phonetic, syntactic, and lexical shifts across dialects and time periods. The primary computational challenge involves processing heterogeneous data—including digitized archives, transcribed oral histories, and modern social media—while accounting for orthographic inconsistencies, non-standardized regional forms, and code-switching phenomena. Machine learning models, particularly transformer-based architectures, will be trained to automate dialect classification, identify diachronic linguistic patterns, and reconstruct unattested intermediate forms. Concurrently, phonetic analysis pipelines will utilize signal processing tools to map prosodic features in spoken Catalan, correlating these with geographic and sociolinguistic variables. By integrating these approaches, the project will generate dynamic dialectometric maps and a publicly accessible database of annotated linguistic features, providing scholars, educators, and developers with resources to advance Catalan language technologies, such as regionally adaptive speech recognition systems and educational tools. The computational demands—large-scale parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training, and complex spatial-temporal visualizations—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve feasible runtime and accuracy. Outcomes will directly contribute to preserving linguistic heritage, inform policy on language standardization, and enhance cross-disciplinary applications in NLP-driven fields, reinforcing Catalan’s vitality in global digital contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Catalan language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Critical care nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to manage patients with life-threatening conditions, yet current clinical tools often lack the precision to predict dynamic patient trajectories or optimize interventions in real time. This project addresses the challenge of integrating heterogeneous, high-frequency physiological data—such as vital signs, ventilator outputs, and electronic health records—into predictive models that can guide critical care nursing practice. We propose developing a machine learning framework to analyze multi-modal patient data from intensive care units (ICUs), with the goal of identifying early warning signs of clinical deterioration, sepsis, or organ failure. The computational approach will involve training deep neural networks on retrospective ICU datasets to recognize patterns preceding adverse events, validated against prospective data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of time-series data, manage complex feature extraction across disparate data streams (e.g., waveform vitals, laboratory results, nursing notes), and iteratively optimize model architectures through hyperparameter tuning. Additionally, we will simulate intervention scenarios using agent-based modeling to evaluate how predictive alerts could be integrated into nursing workflows without contributing to alarm fatigue. Expected outcomes include deployable algorithms for real-time risk stratification, validated against clinical outcomes such as mortality, length of stay, and complication rates. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance evidence-based protocols for critical care nurses, enabling proactive management of unstable patients. The results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits tailored for healthcare environments, ensuring scalability across ICU settings. This project directly aligns with nursing science priorities by bridging computational innovation with bedside practice, ultimately enhancing the precision and timeliness of life-saving interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide specialized care to patients with life-threatening problems, including those in intensive care facilities and on life support. Includes instruction in adult, neonatal, and pediatric critical care; technical skills; patient monitoring and assessment; normal and abnormal readings; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of labor negotiation outcomes in hybrid and gig economy workforces, an understudied area within Labor and Industrial Relations. Traditional labor frameworks struggle to account for the rapid evolution of decentralized work structures, algorithmic management, and shifting worker preferences. The research problem centers on quantifying how these factors influence bargaining power, dispute resolution efficiency, and the viability of collective action in non-traditional employment contexts. Using agent-based modeling (ABM), we will simulate multi-stakeholder interactions across heterogeneous labor markets, incorporating real-world data on gig platform policies, worker mobility patterns, and historical arbitration cases. The computational approach requires parallelized simulations of up to 10^6 autonomous agents with dynamic utility functions, trained via reinforcement learning to adapt their negotiation strategies under constraints imposed by AI-driven scheduling systems and variable regulatory environments. Bayesian network analysis will be applied to identify critical thresholds where small changes in workforce composition or platform incentives lead to disproportionate shifts in negotiation outcomes. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for assessing labor policy impacts in emerging work arrangements and empirically grounded recommendations for updating grievance resolution protocols in algorithmically managed workplaces. The computational intensity arises from iterative parameter optimization across high-dimensional spaces (e.g., varying union density, platform fee structures, and legal jurisdiction overlap), necessitating GPU-accelerated workloads and large-memory nodes. By bridging computational social science with industrial relations theory, this work aims to establish scalable methods for analyzing 21st-century labor dynamics while providing stakeholders with evidence-based tools to mitigate systemic disputes in evolving labor ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on employee-management interactions and the management of issues and disputes regarding working conditions and worker benefit packages, and that may prepare individuals to function as labor or personnel relations specialists. Includes instruction in labor history, policies and strategies of the labor movement, union organization, labor-management negotiation, labor law and contract interpretation, labor economics, welfare and benefit packages, grievance procedures, and labor policy studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Japanese cultural narratives through large-scale textual and visual datasets spanning the Edo period to the present. While prior studies have relied on manual close readings or limited samples, this research addresses the challenge of systematically identifying patterns in cultural expression—such as shifts in literary motifs, iconography in ukiyo-e prints, or regional folklore variations—across centuries of material. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for classical and modern Japanese texts, computer vision techniques for image corpus analysis, and geospatial mapping tools to trace the dissemination of cultural themes. Key methodologies include training custom transformer models on premodern Japanese literature (e.g., gesaku works and Edo-era diaries) to detect semantic shifts in concepts like "nature" or "urbanity," as well as employing convolutional neural networks to classify recurring visual symbols in woodblock prints and modern manga. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing over 10 TB of multilingual primary sources (digitized manuscripts, museum collections, oral history transcripts) and running iterative machine learning experiments at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database linking temporal, geographic, and medium-specific trends in Japanese cultural production, 2) quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric periodization frameworks in cultural studies, and 3) new computational workflows adaptable to under-resourced premodern Japanese language datasets. By bridging digital humanities and area studies, this work aims to redefine how cultural continuity and change are analyzed in non-Western contexts, with implications for preserving intangible cultural heritage and informing contemporary artistic practices in Japan.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Japan, and related island groups and coastal neighbors.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address unresolved questions about the interplay between human biological adaptation and cultural evolution across deep time. A critical challenge in anthropology lies in integrating disparate datasets—genomic, archaeological, and environmental—to model how hominin populations adapted to shifting climates and resource landscapes during key transitions, such as the Pleistocene-Holocene boundary. Current limitations in processing power restrict the scale of spatiotemporal simulations, hindering efforts to test hypotheses about gene-culture coevolution and migration dynamics. This project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and Bayesian phylogenetic inference to simulate population interactions, tool-use transmission, and adaptive responses to environmental stressors over millennial scales. Computational workflows will integrate high-resolution paleoclimate data, ancient DNA datasets, and ethnographic records to parameterize models. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing thousands of simulation iterations across variable parameters, enabling robust sensitivity analyses and likelihood comparisons. Expected outcomes include (1) novel frameworks for quantifying cultural resilience in past societies, (2) refined chronologies for hominin dispersals in understudied regions like Sundaland and the Sahul, and (3) open-source tools for cross-disciplinary data fusion in evolutionary anthropology. By resolving computational bottlenecks, this work will advance methodological synergies between quantitative archaeology and paleogenomics while providing training infrastructure for computational anthropology. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated phylogenetic reconstructions and memory-intensive analyses of 3D-scanned lithic assemblages, which are currently infeasible on local clusters. Results will contribute to international efforts to digitally preserve endangered archaeological heritage, with implications for understanding modern human responses to rapid environmental change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human beings, their antecedents and related primates, and their cultural behavior and institutions, in comparative perspective. Includes instruction in biological/physical anthropology, primatology, human paleontology and prehistoric archeology, hominid evolution, anthropological linguistics, ethnography, ethnology, ethnohistory, socio-cultural anthropology, psychological anthropology, research methods, and applications to areas such as medicine, forensic pathology, museum studies, and international affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interactions between neuropeptide signaling and neural circuit activity in modulating affective states, a critical yet underexplored nexus in biopsychology. While prior studies have independently mapped neurochemical pathways or characterized neural correlates of emotion, the bidirectional mechanisms linking molecular-scale neuropeptide dynamics (e.g., oxytocin, corticotropin-releasing hormone) to macroscale brain network reconfigurations remain poorly resolved. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations of receptor-ligand interactions with whole-brain neural mass modeling. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of neuropeptide diffusion and binding kinetics across spatially resolved synaptic environments, parameterized by empirical data from fMRI and positron emission tomography. These outputs will feed into a hierarchical neural network model to predict how receptor-level perturbations propagate to alter functional connectivity patterns associated with stress resilience or vulnerability. Machine learning pipelines will then identify candidate biomarkers linking simulated neurochemical shifts to behavioral phenotypes derived from longitudinal human cohort data. This approach directly addresses the computational bottleneck of cross-scale integration in biopsychology, where traditional methods lack the resolution to reconcile molecular, neural, and behavioral timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive models of neuropeptide-mediated circuit plasticity, validated against electrophysiological and psychometric datasets, and a novel computational toolkit for simulating intervention effects on affective dysregulation. By bridging biophysical, systems neuroscience, and clinical psychology domains, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of neuropsychiatric disorders while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC-driven multiscale modeling in interdisciplinary biopsychology research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological and psychological linkages, especially the linkages between biochemical and biophysical activity and the functioning of the central nervous system.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling and simulation in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS), addressing critical challenges in patient-specific surgical planning and postoperative outcome prediction. Current approaches to complex procedures—such as mandibular reconstruction, orthognathic surgery, and prosthetic implantation—often rely on static imaging and generalized biomechanical assumptions, limiting precision in predicting tissue responses, implant stability, and long-term functional outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating patient-specific anatomical data from cone-beam CT and intraoral scans with dynamic biomechanical modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive analytics. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution 3D datasets, simulate real-time mechanical stresses during mastication and speech, and model biological processes such as osseointegration and soft tissue healing under diverse physiological conditions.
