The computational pipeline will employ GPU-accelerated solvers for FEA, agent-based modeling for cellular responses to surgical interventions, and ensemble ML algorithms trained on retrospective clinical data to identify risk factors for complications such as nonunion, infection, or implant failure. By enabling granular analysis of biomechanical interactions and tissue adaptation, this work aims to generate predictive tools for optimizing surgical techniques, implant designs, and postoperative care protocols. Successful implementation will provide clinicians with actionable insights to reduce revision surgeries, improve functional and aesthetic outcomes, and personalize treatment strategies for pathologies including traumatic injuries, congenital defects, and oncologic resections. The project will also establish an open-source computational toolkit adaptable to broader OMFS research, fostering innovation in a field where advanced modeling remains underrepresented despite its transformative potential for patient care.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the diagnosis and intrusive and adjunctive treatment of diseases, injuries, and defects of the oral and maxillofacial regions, including functional and aesthetic aspects. Includes instruction in pharmacology, analgesia, anesthesia, anxiety control, surgical procedures and techniques, surgical instrumentation, exodontia, oral diseases and malfunctions, soft and hard tissue pathology, dentoalveolar surgery, infection management, and prosthetic implantation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the intersection of cultural identity and transnational media networks in 20th-century Latin American and Caribbean diasporic communities. The research problem centers on gaps in understanding how marginalized groups—particularly Afro-Caribbean and Indigenous populations—negotiated cultural belonging through media production and consumption amid political upheavals and migration waves. Traditional archival methods struggle to analyze the scale and multilingual diversity of primary sources, including digitized newspapers, radio broadcasts, and community newsletters scattered across repositories in over 15 countries. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, geospatial mapping, and network modeling. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to analyze Spanish, French, Portuguese, and Creole texts for thematic patterns, sentiment, and discursive strategies related to identity formation. Geospatial tools will visualize the circulation of media artifacts across migration corridors, while network graphs will map connections between publishers, writers, and audiences. These methods require HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train multilingual NLP models, and run iterative simulations of cultural diffusion dynamics. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated media corpora, interactive visualizations of transnational cultural networks, and a methodological framework for computational analysis of diasporic cultural production. The findings will contribute to interdisciplinary debates on decolonial epistemologies and offer scalable tools for scholars studying identity in underrepresented communities. By integrating computational rigor with area studies expertise, this project aims to redefine how cultural resilience is analyzed in contexts of displacement, providing a model for resource-conscious, ethically informed digital humanities research in Global South contexts.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for analyzing the structural and semantic evolution of legal systems across jurisdictions. The research addresses a critical gap in comparative law: the inability to systematically map large-scale legal text corpora to trace the diffusion of legal concepts, identify latent doctrinal conflicts, and quantify convergence/divergence patterns between civil law, common law, and hybrid systems. While traditional comparative legal analysis relies on manual case law review and doctrinal synthesis, this project develops machine learning models to process multilingual legal documents—including statutes, judicial opinions, and legislative histories—from over 50 jurisdictions spanning 2000–2023. The computational approach integrates transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for cross-lingual semantic alignment, graph neural networks to model citation networks and precedent hierarchies, and time-series analysis to detect phase transitions in legal reasoning. Key technical challenges include scaling heterogeneous document parsing (PDFs, scanned texts, XML), managing concept drift in legal terminology, and ensuring interpretability of model outputs for legal scholars. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific language models on terabyte-scale legal corpora, running distributed simulations of normative system interactions, and generating 3D visualizations of multi-jurisdictional legal topology. Expected outcomes include an open-access platform for dynamic comparative law analysis, a quantitative typology of legal system interoperability, and predictive metrics for identifying areas of transnational legal friction. By enabling data-driven comparative jurisprudence at unprecedented scale, this work aims to inform legal harmonization efforts, treaty design, and transnational dispute resolution mechanisms while establishing computational methods as a transformative paradigm in legal research.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of legal systems and philosophies in comparative perspective.

abstract: Poultry production systems face critical challenges in optimizing animal health, feed efficiency, and disease resilience, which are essential for sustainable food security. Current limitations in predicting pathogen dynamics, understanding host-microbiome interactions, and tailoring nutritional strategies hinder progress in these areas. This project seeks to address these gaps through advanced computational modeling and large-scale genomic analyses, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) simulating molecular interactions between poultry pathogens (e.g., Salmonella, Avian Influenza viruses) and host immune proteins using all-atom molecular dynamics to identify virulence mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets; (2) applying machine learning to integrate multi-omics datasets (genomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic) from poultry gut microbiomes to model nutrient absorption efficiency and predict optimal feed formulations; and (3) developing agent-based epidemiological models to assess transmission risks of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens in commercial poultry operations. These computationally intensive workflows require parallel processing capabilities for molecular simulations with millisecond-scale sampling, training of deep neural networks on terabyte-scale omics datasets, and stochastic modeling of disease spread across complex production networks. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and validation against experimental data from collaborating poultry research centers. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for mitigating antimicrobial resistance, genetically informed feeding strategies to reduce environmental footprints, and mechanistic insights into host-pathogen interactions that could inform vaccine development. By bridging computational biology and poultry science, this work aims to generate translational tools for enhancing poultry welfare, productivity, and food safety while reducing reliance on antibiotics. The resulting models and datasets will be shared with the agricultural research community to accelerate innovation in sustainable poultry production.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of poultry animals and the production and handling of poultry products. Includes instruction in avian sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, hatchery design, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: Nursing practice faces a critical translational gap between research evidence and real-world clinical implementation, particularly in managing complex health conditions influenced by multi-dimensional patient data. This project addresses the challenge of integrating high-dimensional datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic biomarkers, and real-time patient monitoring streams—into actionable clinical decision-support tools for nurses. Traditional computing methods lack the capacity to process these heterogeneous data streams efficiently, limiting the scalability of predictive models and simulations of clinical outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models and agent-based simulations (ABS) that optimize evidence-based intervention strategies. The computational workflow includes preprocessing terabyte-scale EHR data to identify patterns in patient deterioration, training ensemble ML models to predict sepsis and hospital-acquired pressure injuries, and simulating the impact of nurse staffing ratios on intervention efficacy using ABS. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing model training across thousands of parameters, conducting Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in clinical scenarios, and analyzing genomic-epigenomic interactions influencing patient responses to nursing interventions. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for early risk detection, validated simulation frameworks to guide staffing and policy decisions, and scalable pipelines for integrating multi-omics data into nursing practice. By enabling rapid analysis of billion-row datasets and computationally intensive simulations, this project will advance precision nursing interventions, reduce unwarranted clinical variation, and provide a replicable computational infrastructure for future nursing research. The findings will be disseminated through interoperable clinical dashboards and training modules for nursing leaders, directly supporting the program’s mission to translate research into practice through innovation.
cip_definition: A practice-focused program that prepares registered nurses for increasingly complex evidence-based nursing practice, including translating research into practice, evaluating evidence, applying research in decision-making, and implementing viable clinical innovations to change practice. Includes instruction in healthcare delivery systems, health economics and finance, health policy, research methods, translating evidence into practice, concepts in population health, and nursing leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize hybrid manufacturing processes that integrate additive and subtractive technologies, addressing critical inefficiencies in multi-stage production systems. Current industrial workflows struggle with dynamic resource allocation, thermal distortion management, and toolpath synchronization, particularly when processing high-strength alloys used in specialized tooling and prototyping. To overcome these challenges, the research will employ high-fidelity finite element modeling (FEM) to simulate coupled thermo-mechanical effects during layered deposition and machining cycles, paired with multi-objective optimization algorithms to balance production time, material waste, and energy consumption. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the computationally intensive, transient simulations of 3D printing and milling interactions at industrially relevant scales, with model domains exceeding 10^8 mesh elements. The computational workflow will integrate machine learning surrogates trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate parameter space exploration, enabling real-time adaptive control strategies for in-situ process adjustments. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for hybrid process planning, validated against experimental data from collaborative industry partners, and generalized guidelines for minimizing post-processing in low-volume, high-complexity part manufacturing. By addressing the computational bottlenecks in simulating integrated production systems, this work aims to advance digital twin capabilities for small-to-medium enterprises adopting hybrid manufacturing, ultimately supporting energy-efficient transitions to on-demand production models. The requested resources will directly enable parametric studies across 50+ material-toolpair configurations, reducing simulation wall-clock time from weeks to days while maintaining the resolution required to capture critical edge-case failures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in industrial production technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced predictive framework for optimizing credit risk mitigation strategies in decentralized financial ecosystems. Traditional credit management models often struggle to account for the nonlinear interdependencies between borrower behavior, collateral valuation dynamics, and macroeconomic shocks in distributed lending environments. The study addresses this gap by proposing a multi-agent reinforcement learning system that simulates complex credit networks at scale, integrating real-time asset price volatility, cross-chain collateralization patterns, and regulatory constraint propagation. Computational challenges arise from modeling thousands of interacting agents with heterogeneous risk preferences while processing high-frequency financial data streams from decentralized ledger platforms. The proposed methodology combines graph neural networks for mapping evolving credit relationships with quantum-inspired optimization algorithms to identify robust risk allocation policies under uncertainty. Key innovations include developing adaptive collateral haircut models using generative adversarial networks trained on synthetic crisis scenarios and implementing privacy-preserving federated learning techniques to aggregate sensitive credit data across institutional boundaries. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational architecture for stress testing decentralized credit protocols, quantitative insights into systemic risk contagion pathways, and empirically validated heuristics for dynamic credit limit adjustments in volatile markets. The HPC implementation will utilize GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations and distributed tensor computations to handle the combinatorial complexity of multi-jurisdictional regulatory environments. By bridging computational finance, cryptographic verification mechanisms, and behavioral credit analytics, this research aims to advance next-generation credit management infrastructure for hybrid centralized-decentralized financial systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and/or manage operations concerning personal and corporate credit, collateral, loan processing, and related financial agency communications. Includes instruction in general finance and banking principles, insurance, real estate, taxation, business law and regulations, quantitative methods, financial computer systems applications, database management, communications skills, business and office management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Pediatric rheumatic diseases, such as juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and pediatric lupus, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their heterogeneity, complex pathophysiology, and variable treatment responses. Current clinical approaches often rely on imprecise diagnostic criteria and generalized treatment protocols, leading to delayed interventions and suboptimal outcomes. This project aims to address these limitations by integrating multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic) with longitudinal clinical and imaging datasets to identify disease-specific biomarkers, stratify patients into molecular subtypes, and predict treatment responses. The scale and complexity of these datasets—encompassing thousands of patients from international registries and high-resolution imaging repositories—necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable efficient data processing, storage, and analysis. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms (e.g., unsupervised clustering, deep neural networks) to classify disease subtypes and Bayesian network modeling to map dynamic interactions between genetic variants, immune pathways, and environmental triggers. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate how specific mutations alter protein structures implicated in autoimmune responses. These analyses require parallelized computing architectures to manage terabyte-scale datasets and perform millions of stochastic simulations within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive models for early diagnosis, personalized therapeutic targets, and a publicly accessible computational framework for pediatric rheumatology research. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project will advance precision medicine in a clinical population with high unmet need, reducing diagnostic delays and improving long-term musculoskeletal outcomes for children and young adults. The tools and pipelines generated will also serve as a template for computational research in other pediatric chronic diseases.
cip_definition: Research on how to diagnose and treat diseases of joints, muscle, bones, and tendons in children and young adults, including arthritis, back pain, muscle strains, common athletic injuries, and collagen diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize resource allocation and environmental management in commercial plant nurseries, addressing challenges posed by dynamic climate conditions and operational scalability. Current nursery practices often rely on generalized protocols for irrigation, fertilization, and climate control, leading to inefficiencies in water use, energy consumption, and plant health during propagation. To resolve this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating real-time sensor data, plant physiological models, and machine learning to predict species-specific growth responses under variable nursery conditions. Multi-agent simulations will model individual plant interactions with microenvironments, while parallelized optimization algorithms will iteratively refine irrigation schedules, substrate compositions, and thermal regimes across production zones. The computational pipeline will process hyperspectral imaging data to detect stress biomarkers and correlate these with growth outcomes using convolutional neural networks. By leveraging GPU-accelerated clusters, the system will simulate thousands of operational scenarios to identify cost-effective strategies balancing productivity, resource use, and labor constraints. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for customizing cultivation protocols across diverse species, reducing water and nutrient waste by an estimated 20–35%, and improving seedling survival rates during transplantation. This work will provide nursery operators with scalable decision-support systems adaptable to shifting market demands and climate variability, directly enhancing the economic and environmental sustainability of nursery operations. The resulting datasets and models will be disseminated through an open-access portal to support industry adoption and further research in precision horticulture.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage outdoor plant farms, tree and shrub nurseries, and related facilities that develop domesticated plant products for propagation, harvesting, and transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science, farm and business management, nursery operations, equipment operation and maintenance, safety procedures, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of Catholic theological and philosophical texts, with a focus on tracing the evolution of key doctrinal and ethical concepts across historical contexts. The research problem centers on the challenges of synthesizing vast, multilingual corpora—including works in Latin, Biblical Greek, and Hebrew—that underpin Catholic intellectual tradition. Traditional manual methods struggle to systematically identify patterns in theological argumentation, semantic shifts in doctrinal language, or correlations between scriptural interpretation and developments in Catholic social thought. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and network analysis to analyze digitized manuscripts, conciliar documents, and theological treatises. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of text datasets spanning 15 centuries, training transformer-based models for ancient language semantic similarity tasks, and constructing dynamic knowledge graphs to map relationships between philosophical concepts, ethical frameworks, and sociocultural influences. Expected outcomes include identifying previously unrecognized doctrinal inflection points in church history, quantifying the influence of Thomistic philosophy on bioethical discourse, and visualizing how Catholic social teaching adapts to technological modernity. The computational pipelines developed will be made available to the broader Catholic Studies community, fostering interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of theology, digital humanities, and computational social science. By enabling scalable analysis of primary sources, this project aims to deepen understanding of how Catholic tradition dynamically engages with philosophical inquiry while maintaining doctrinal continuity—a contribution with implications for both academic scholarship and contemporary faith practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Catholic thought, culture, and how Catholic tradition informs theology, culture, institutions, and identity. Includes instruction in Biblical Greek, Biblical Hebrew, Catholic bioethics, Catholic social thought, church history, Latin, philosophy, and theology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between economic narratives in multilingual literature and their influence on regional trade policy formation, focusing on understudied linguistic regions in Southeast Asia and East Africa. The research problem centers on the lack of quantitative frameworks to analyze how literary representations of economic concepts—embedded in postcolonial texts, government white papers, and trade union archives—shape policymakers’ perceptions of comparative advantage and trade reciprocity. Current methodologies in economic textual analysis remain siloed by language barriers and fail to account for culturally specific metaphors in fiscal discourse. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline combining semantic analysis of multilingual corpora (Burmese, Swahili, and English texts) with econometric modeling of historical trade data. High-performance computing resources will enable (1) large-scale parallel processing of digitized literature and economic documents using transformer-based language models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, (2) network analysis of concept diffusion across literary and policy genres, and (3) agent-based simulations of how localized narrative patterns correlate with measurable shifts in bilateral trade agreements (1990–2020). The workflow requires GPU-accelerated training of custom embeddings that capture economic semantics across linguistic systems, coupled with distributed memory architectures for cross-regional comparative simulations. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of narrative-driven economic decision-making and an open-access repository linking literary motifs to trade elasticity metrics. This interdisciplinary approach advances computational humanities by creating transferable methods for analyzing non-Western economic discourses while providing development economists with culture-aware models of policy adoption. The resource-intensive nature of processing rare language datasets and running high-dimensional cultural-econometric simulations necessitates the requested computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in comparative economic systems, econometrics, economic theory, money and banking systems, international economics, international trade, linguistics, philology, and translation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of personalized nutrition, food systems optimization, and behavioral health analytics—a niche within Foods, Nutrition, and Wellness Studies that integrates computational modeling with human-centered health outcomes. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how dynamic, individualized dietary patterns interact with socioeconomic, cultural, and physiological variables to influence long-term wellness. Traditional nutrition studies often rely on static dietary assessments or small-sample trials, limiting their ability to model complex, nonlinear relationships between food intake, metabolic responses, and lifestyle factors at scale. To overcome this, we propose developing a machine learning framework to analyze multi-modal datasets, including longitudinal dietary logs, biometric sensor data, regional food supply chain metrics, and psychosocial surveys. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional time-series data, training ensemble models to predict nutrient absorption variability across demographic subgroups, and simulating the public health impacts of culturally tailored dietary interventions under diverse socioeconomic scenarios. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter optimization for neural networks, parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of intervention efficacy, and real-time integration of heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive toolkit for personalized meal planning that accounts for user-specific constraints (e.g., budget, food accessibility), (2) evidence-based models linking localized food production practices to community health disparities, and (3) novel metrics for evaluating nutrition interventions across temporal and biological scales. By bridging computational scalability with human-factors complexity, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven wellness policy while advancing methodological innovation in non-traditional HPC applications. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, storage of petabyte-scale nutritional databases, and collaborative visualization of multidimensional wellness landscapes.
cip_title: Foods, Nutrition, and Wellness Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the role of foods and nutrition in human health and wellness. Includes instruction in nutritional care and education, the planning and provision of food services, the development of consumable food products, life-span nutrition and wellness, the principles of nutritional assessment, and food safety and food composition.

abstract: This project seeks to address disparities in educational outcomes for culturally and linguistically diverse learners by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop adaptive, data-driven instructional strategies. Current approaches to multicultural education often rely on generalized frameworks that struggle to account for the intersectional identities of students, including language proficiency, cultural background, and socioeconomic factors. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study analyzing large-scale, multilingual datasets from K-12 and adult education programs to identify patterns in student engagement, content accessibility, and learning outcomes across diverse populations. The research will employ machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures, to process natural language data from student-teacher interactions, multilingual assignments, and community feedback. These models will be trained to predict instructional interventions that align with culturally responsive pedagogy, such as personalized resource recommendations and dynamic curriculum adjustments. Agent-based simulations will further model classroom ecosystems under varying pedagogical strategies, enabling the testing of hypothetical scenarios without real-world risks. By integrating these computational approaches, the project aims to generate actionable insights into optimizing instructional design for underrepresented groups, particularly emergent multilingual students and learners from non-dominant cultural backgrounds. The outcomes will include open-access predictive tools for educators, a repository of simulated teaching strategies, and evidence-based guidelines for deploying adaptive educational technologies in multicultural settings. This work directly supports the advancement of equitable, scalable solutions in teacher education by translating complex sociocultural dynamics into computationally tractable models, thereby empowering educators to address systemic barriers with precision.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, and implementation of instructional and advising services for culturally diverse learning populations. Includes instruction in cultural diversity, at-risk populations, multilingual and ESL education, program and curriculum design, instructional technology, information resources, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling and communicating with multicultural populations, law and regulations, and applications to specific cultural groups, educational services, and research issues.

abstract: This project seeks to address the persistent challenge of personalizing literacy instruction for adult learners with diverse linguistic, cognitive, and socioeconomic backgrounds by leveraging advanced computational modeling. Adult literacy programs often struggle to adapt instructional strategies in real time to learners’ evolving needs, particularly in settings with limited resources. Traditional methods rely on static curricula or manual assessments, which fail to account for the dynamic interplay between learner engagement, neurocognitive processing, and sociocultural factors. To bridge this gap, we propose developing an adaptive learning framework powered by machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to optimize instructional interventions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training deep neural networks on multimodal datasets—including eye-tracking data, writing samples, and biometric feedback—collected from adult learners during literacy tasks. These models will simulate individualized learning trajectories, predict skill acquisition bottlenecks, and recommend targeted pedagogical adjustments. The computational workflow involves three phases: (1) preprocessing and fusion of heterogeneous data streams using GPU-accelerated pipelines, (2) reinforcement learning to iteratively refine instructional decision-making algorithms, and (3) large-scale validation through agent-based simulations of virtual classrooms with varying learner demographics. By integrating cognitive science, sociolinguistics, and educational technology, this research aims to produce an open-source toolset for dynamically tailoring literacy instruction. Expected outcomes include empirically validated strategies for mitigating skill plateaus in adult learners and a computational framework that generalizes to other competency-based adult education domains. The project’s reliance on HPC stems from the need to process terabytes of temporal interaction data and execute parallelized simulations to model diverse learner populations, tasks infeasible on standard infrastructure. Findings will advance both the science of adult learning and the practical scalability of data-driven educational technologies in underserved communities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as instructors and mentors for adults in basic or functional literacy programs in school, institutional, community, and private settings.

abstract: The discovery and characterization of bioactive natural products remain a critical yet resource-intensive endeavor in drug development. Traditional approaches to isolate and screen compounds from complex biological matrices are limited by low yields, time-consuming processes, and challenges in predicting bioactivity. This project seeks to address these bottlenecks by integrating computational chemistry and machine learning to prioritize high-potential compounds from ethnobotanically relevant plant species, thereby streamlining the discovery pipeline. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will perform large-scale virtual screening of phytochemical libraries against therapeutic targets implicated in antimicrobial resistance and cancer. Molecular docking simulations will assess binding affinities to target proteins (e.g., bacterial efflux pumps, kinase enzymes), while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will evaluate complex stability and conformational dynamics over biologically relevant timescales. Concurrently, we will train graph neural networks on structural and bioassay data to predict compound bioactivity and pharmacokinetic properties, enabling iterative refinement of candidate selection. These computational workflows will be validated experimentally through collaboration with wet-lab researchers, who will test prioritized compounds using bioassays and LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics. The HPC environment is essential to manage the project’s computational demands, including quantum mechanical calculations for electronic structure analysis, parallelized MD simulations, and processing of high-dimensional spectral datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel scaffolds with validated bioactivity, structural insights into target-ligand interactions, and an open-access predictive model for natural product prioritization. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error isolation, this work aims to accelerate the translation of natural products into drug leads while advancing computational methodologies in pharmacognosy. The requested resources will directly support 12–18 months of intensive simulations, data integration, and model training, with results contributing to both therapeutic innovation and the sustainable utilization of biodiversity.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to enhance the accuracy and interpretability of electrocardiogram (ECG) signal analysis, with a focus on detecting subtle arrhythmias and improving diagnostic workflows in clinical settings. Despite advances in automated ECG interpretation, existing algorithms often struggle with rare arrhythmias, noisy signals, and patient-specific variability, leading to missed diagnoses or false alarms. To address this, we propose training deep learning models on a large, diverse dataset of ECG waveforms—including 12-lead recordings, patient metadata, and clinician annotations—to improve generalization across demographic and pathological subgroups. The computational approach involves preprocessing raw ECG signals using wavelet transforms to isolate cardiac cycles and suppress noise, followed by a hybrid convolutional-recurrent neural network architecture to capture spatial and temporal dependencies. Hyperparameter optimization and model validation will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the scale of data (over 500,000 annotated ECG traces from multi-center databases) and the complexity of training ensemble models. Key outcomes include an open-source arrhythmia classification tool optimized for integration with hospital ECG devices, a quantitative assessment of model robustness across patient ages and comorbidities, and a clinician-facing dashboard to visualize model confidence and salient waveform features. The project’s significance lies in its potential to reduce diagnostic delays for conditions like atrial fibrillation and conduction disorders while maintaining alignment with clinical interpretability standards. By utilizing HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge the gap between computational research and real-world ECG technology applications, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance patient care through innovative diagnostic tools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to administer EKG and ECG diagnostic examinations and report results to the treatment team. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, the cardiovascular system, medical terminology, cardiovascular medications and effects, patient care, EKG and ECG administration, equipment operation and maintenance, interpretation of cardiac rhythm, patient record management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize evidence-based teaching strategies for secondary education classrooms, with a focus on addressing heterogeneous student learning needs. A persistent challenge in teacher education is designing adaptable instructional approaches that respond dynamically to variations in student prior knowledge, engagement levels, and cognitive processing styles. Current manual analysis methods limit educators’ capacity to anticipate how pedagogical interventions will scale across diverse classroom compositions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate classroom learning dynamics through agent-based modeling (ABM). The computational framework will parameterize student agents using empirical data from anonymized K-12 learning analytics, incorporating variables such as foundational skill mastery, attention patterns, and social learning behaviors. Parallelized simulations will test how different instructional sequences—including differentiated scaffolding, peer learning configurations, and formative assessment timing—affect predicted learning outcomes across 10,000+ synthetic classroom configurations. Machine learning techniques will then identify high-efficacy teaching strategies under specific student demographic and competency distributions. The models will be validated against real-world classroom observation datasets from partner school districts. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible simulation engine to help pre-service teachers visualize intervention impacts during training programs, and (2) evidence-based frameworks for personalizing instruction in mixed-ability secondary classrooms. By enabling large-scale synthetic experimentation, this HPC-driven approach aims to equip educators with actionable strategies for reducing achievement gaps while maintaining curricular rigor—a critical need in teacher preparation programs. Resource requirements include GPU-accelerated nodes for ABM parallelization and 50TB of storage for multidimensional simulation outputs and validation datasets.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the secondary grades, which may include grades seven through twelve, depending on the school system or state regulations. May include preparation to teach a comprehensive curriculum or specific subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural religious syncretism through computational analysis of textual and ritual data spanning multiple traditions. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of adaptation and synthesis in religious practices and narratives, particularly in contexts of cultural exchange, which are difficult to trace using conventional qualitative methods due to the scale and complexity of the data. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze a corpus of digitized primary sources—including liturgical texts, oral tradition transcripts, and ethnographic records—from three understudied syncretic traditions in Southeast Asia, the Caribbean, and East Africa. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) techniques for semantic network analysis to map conceptual overlaps, as well as machine learning models (e.g., topic modeling, clustering algorithms) to detect latent thematic and structural parallels across traditions. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate the diffusion of ritual practices under varying sociopolitical conditions. The scale of data (over 10 million words across six languages and 15,000 annotated ritual descriptions) necessitates parallelized processing and large-memory nodes to manage multilingual tokenization, entity recognition, and network graph generation. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying syncretic processes, visualizations of belief-system hybridization, and a public dataset of annotated texts. This work will advance methodological innovation in religious studies by demonstrating how computational approaches can reveal macro-scale patterns in religious change, offering new insights into the mechanisms of cultural resilience and adaptation. The results will be disseminated through open-access tools tailored for humanities researchers, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue on computational hermeneutics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religion/religious studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of pollution control systems, driven by stringent environmental regulations and the need for energy-efficient solutions, requires advanced tools to optimize system design and operation. Current approaches often rely on oversimplified models or costly physical prototyping, limiting the ability to account for dynamic environmental variables, heterogeneous pollutant sources, and multi-scale interactions in indoor and outdoor settings. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize hybrid mechanical-biological filtration systems for industrial air quality management. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and reactive transport models to resolve turbulent airflow patterns, particulate deposition kinetics, and biodegradation processes in three-dimensional reactor geometries. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify optimal operational parameters under variable pollutant loads and humidity conditions. The models will be validated against experimental data from pilot-scale bioreactor trials, including real-time sensor measurements of particulate matter, volatile organic compounds, and microbial activity. By enabling rapid scenario testing across diverse environmental conditions, this computational approach will reduce the iterative costs of system prototyping by an estimated 40-60%. Anticipated outcomes include novel design guidelines for modular filtration units, predictive maintenance protocols based on simulated performance degradation, and an open-source toolkit for environmental technicians to assess system resilience to emerging contaminants. The project directly aligns with the program’s focus on applied engineering technologies by bridging laboratory-scale data with field-scale implementation strategies, ultimately advancing the development of adaptive pollution control infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using indoor and outdoor environmental pollution control systems. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and calibration of industrial measurement and control systems, addressing the growing complexity of modern instrumentation in high-demand environments. Current methodologies for designing multi-sensor networks and adaptive control systems face limitations in scalability and precision, particularly when accounting for dynamic variables such as thermal fluctuations, signal interference, and real-time data throughput. To overcome these challenges, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), agent-based modeling, and machine learning (ML) to simulate and optimize instrumentation performance under heterogeneous operational conditions. The computational workflow will parallelize sensor network simulations to evaluate millions of parameter combinations, including material properties, geometric configurations, and environmental stressors, while ML algorithms will iteratively refine calibration protocols. A key innovation involves coupling real-time data assimilation from prototype systems with digital twin models to reduce calibration drift in predictive scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale sensitivity analyses to identify failure thresholds and resilience metrics for instrumentation deployed in extreme environments, such as high-vibration manufacturing systems or chemically corrosive processes. Expected outcomes include validated models for designing fault-tolerant sensor arrays, automated calibration pipelines to reduce manual tuning by 40–60%, and open-source tools for simulating industrial control systems with variable latency constraints. This work will directly enhance the precision and reliability of next-generation instrumentation technologies, with applications in energy production, advanced manufacturing, and automated quality assurance. By leveraging HPC resources, the project bridges critical gaps between theoretical instrumentation design and practical implementation, accelerating the development of robust, adaptive measurement systems for Industry 4.0 infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing control and measurement systems and procedures. Includes instruction in instrumentation design and maintenance, calibration, design and production testing and scheduling, automated equipment functions, applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: The study of polymer physics presents unique challenges due to the complex interplay of molecular interactions, topological constraints, and non-equilibrium dynamics that govern polymer behavior across melt, solution, and solid-state phases. While existing analytical models provide foundational insights, they often fail to predict emergent phenomena in industrially relevant regimes, such as extreme deformation rates, high monomer densities, or heterogeneous confinement. This project seeks to address these limitations through large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and coarse-grained Monte Carlo (MC) simulations to unravel the physics of entangled polymer systems under non-equilibrium conditions. The primary research objectives include elucidating the role of topological constraints in stress relaxation, quantifying the coupling between chain orientation and transport properties in shear-thinning melts, and characterizing glass transition dynamics in polydisperse systems with tunable monomer architectures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate systems spanning 10^4–10^5 polymer chains at atomistic and mesoscopic resolutions, capturing timescales from picosecond-scale segmental motions to millisecond-scale reptation dynamics. GPU-accelerated MD simulations using optimized force fields will probe strain-rate-dependent viscosity and normal stress differences, while hybrid MC-MD workflows will map phase diagrams for disordered systems near the glass transition. The computational framework integrates open-source packages (LAMMPS, HOOMD-blue) with custom algorithms for analyzing entanglement networks and stress propagation. Expected outcomes include predictive relationships between molecular architecture, entanglement density, and nonlinear viscoelasticity, which will refine continuum-scale constitutive models. These results will advance fundamental understanding of polymer physics by bridging gaps between theory, simulation, and experimental observations, with broader implications for optimizing polymer processing in manufacturing contexts. The scale of the simulations necessitates access to parallelized computing architectures capable of handling ~10^6 core-hours, including large memory nodes for trajectory analysis and machine-learning-assisted post-processing of structural datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanical, optical, and transport properties of polymers with respect to the underlying physics and physical chemistry of polymers in melt, solution, and solid state

abstract: The increasing complexity of clinical laboratory workflows, driven by advances in diagnostic technologies and higher testing volumes, has amplified risks of pre-analytical and analytical errors that compromise patient safety. While laboratory automation has improved precision, human-machine interactions during sample handling, instrument calibration, and data validation remain critical failure points, particularly in settings utilizing waived testing systems. This project proposes a computational investigation of error propagation patterns in clinical laboratory workflows to develop predictive models for risk mitigation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze multimodal datasets encompassing procedural logs, sensor outputs from laboratory equipment, and annotated error reports from 12 regional laboratories. Machine learning approaches, including graph neural networks (GNNs) and time-series anomaly detection models, will be applied to map temporal and spatial relationships between operator actions, environmental variables, and error outcomes. A novel agent-based simulation framework will model interactions between laboratory personnel, automated systems, and specimen workflows under varying operational constraints. The computational pipeline will integrate real-world data from phlebotomy quality metrics, reagent lot variability records, and equipment maintenance logs to identify latent risk factors. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive dashboard for error-prone workflow segments, (2) optimized procedural checkpoints tailored to waived testing environments, and (3) AI-generated training modules targeting high-risk operator-instrument interactions. By bridging computational modeling with clinical laboratory operations, this work aims to establish a framework for preemptive error reduction in non-specialized laboratory settings, ultimately enhancing diagnostic reliability while maintaining cost-effectiveness in resource-constrained healthcare systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians or laboratory scientists or technologists, to perform waived testing procedures (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988), phlebotomy, and other duties in support of laboratory teams. Includes instruction in clinical procedures, various laboratory tests, laboratory mathematics, computer technology, equipment operation and maintenance, sterilization and safety, communications skills, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: The preservation of historic built environments demands innovative approaches to address the complex interplay of material degradation, environmental stressors, and evolving conservation ethics. Current methods for predicting structural vulnerabilities in heritage buildings often rely on generalized environmental models or localized material testing, which fail to capture the multiscale, dynamic interactions between aging materials and microclimatic conditions. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate decay mechanisms in historic masonry and timber structures under fluctuating environmental loads. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will model coupled hygrothermal-mechanical processes at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, integrating heterogeneous datasets ranging from micromaterial characterization to regional climate projections. The computational workflow combines finite element analysis (FEA) for stress propagation, lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) for moisture transport, and machine learning algorithms trained on spectral imaging data from 12 case-study monuments. By implementing parallelized multi-physics simulations across GPU clusters, the project aims to identify critical thresholds for material failure while accounting for cyclical loading patterns over decadal timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive risk maps for prioritized conservation interventions and a decision-support tool for adaptive reuse scenarios. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—requiring teraflop-scale processing for stochastic environmental scenario testing—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation beyond conventional workstation capabilities. This work will establish a new paradigm for evidence-based conservation planning, enabling proactive stewardship of cultural heritage assets while addressing the computational challenges inherent in modeling historic materials’ nonlinear behavior. The resulting methodologies could inform international conservation standards and provide transferable insights for analyzing complex material-environment interactions in other non-engineering contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the architectural design principles and building techniques used in historic structures and environments, and the process of saving and restoring old buildings and districts for contemporary use and enjoyment. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation techniques, and material conservation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of preparing educators to effectively teach across multiple grade levels by leveraging computational modeling to analyze pedagogical strategies and their impact on diverse student populations. Teacher education programs for multi-level licensure must balance the developmental, curricular, and socioemotional variability inherent in teaching different age groups, yet evidence-based frameworks for optimizing such training remain underdeveloped. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale datasets from classroom observations, student performance metrics, and teacher reflection journals across K-12 environments. Machine learning algorithms, including transformer-based natural language processing and hierarchical clustering, will identify patterns in instructional effectiveness tied to specific grade-level transitions (e.g., elementary to middle school). Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom interactions under varying teaching strategies to predict outcomes for hypothetical student cohorts. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing due to the volume of multimodal data (≥50TB) and the complexity of simulating heterogeneous educational ecosystems. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for tailoring teacher training interventions to address competency gaps in cross-level pedagogy, as well as open-source tools for visualizing developmental trajectories in teacher decision-making. This work will directly inform the design of adaptive curricula for multi-level teacher certification programs, with implications for reducing teacher attrition and improving equity in classrooms serving students at critical transitional stages. By quantifying previously qualitative aspects of cross-grade instructional adaptability, the project aims to establish scalable computational methods for strengthening teacher preparation in an increasingly interdisciplinary educational landscape.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at more than one educational level, such as a combined program in elementary/secondary, early childhood/elementary, elementary/middle school, or junior high/high school teacher education.

abstract: Institutional researchers in higher education face the challenge of synthesizing increasingly large, heterogeneous datasets—spanning student outcomes, enrollment trends, and institutional operations—to inform equity-centered decision-making. While existing tools support basic descriptive analytics, the scale and complexity of modern educational data, including unstructured text from student feedback and high-dimensional administrative records, demand advanced computational methods. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to multi-modal institutional data from a network of public universities. The research will focus on two interconnected problems: (1) identifying patterns in attrition risks among underrepresented student populations by integrating longitudinal academic performance, demographic, and socio-economic data; and (2) automating the analysis of qualitative student experience narratives to detect systemic barriers to success. Computational workflows will employ distributed computing frameworks (e.g., Apache Spark) for scalable data integration, GPU-accelerated deep learning models (Transformer architectures) for NLP tasks, and interpretable ML methods to ensure actionable results. The project will leverage existing institutional datasets spanning 500,000+ student records and 1.2 million course evaluations. HPC resources are critical for training complex models on this scale while maintaining privacy-preserving data protocols. Expected outcomes include open-source pipelines for ethical educational data mining, validated predictive models of student persistence, and evidence-based recommendations for targeted interventions. By advancing computational methods tailored to institutional research needs, this work aims to establish replicable practices for leveraging HPC in education research while directly addressing equity gaps in postsecondary outcomes.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares an individual to be an institutional researcher at a postsecondary educational institution. Includes instruction in data analysis, data-driven decision-making, data mining, higher education administration and organization, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: Livestock diseases pose significant threats to agricultural productivity, food security, and public health, yet predicting outbreaks and optimizing interventions remains challenging due to the complex interplay of pathogen genetics, host immunity, and environmental factors. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling the spread of high-consequence viral pathogens in cattle populations, with a focus on bovine respiratory disease (BRD)—a leading cause of economic loss in the beef industry. We will integrate genomic data from circulating pathogens, host metagenomic and transcriptomic datasets, and spatially explicit environmental variables to identify drivers of transmission and predict outbreak trajectories. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support large-scale agent-based epidemiological simulations, Bayesian phylodynamic analyses of viral evolution, and machine learning models linking microbial community dynamics to disease susceptibility. These multi-modal datasets, which include millions of pathogen sequences, longitudinal health records from 50,000 cattle, and geospatial climate data, require distributed-memory parallelization and GPU-accelerated neural network training. The project will produce predictive tools to identify herds at elevated risk of BRD outbreaks, classify viral strains with heightened zoonotic potential, and evaluate the efficacy of vaccine protocols under shifting climate conditions. Outcomes will directly inform management strategies to reduce antibiotic use, improve vaccine deployment, and mitigate economic losses for producers. By advancing computational methods tailored to agricultural animal systems, this work will establish a template for addressing complex disease challenges in livestock populations while adhering to the One Health paradigm.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the study, prevention, and control of diseases in agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in environmental science, pharmacology, animal population studies, genetics, animal physiology and diet, disease prevention, treatment methodologies, and laboratory and testing procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the study of Norwegian linguistic evolution and literary innovation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale textual and dialectal datasets. Current research on Norwegian dialects and literature is constrained by the limited scalability of traditional methods, particularly when handling multi-regional historical texts, modern speech corpora, and metadata-rich literary works. The primary research problem centers on identifying patterns of linguistic change across time, space, and literary genres, as well as quantifying the sociocultural factors influencing these shifts. To overcome computational bottlenecks, this project will employ NLP pipelines optimized for parallel processing to conduct syntactic, morphological, and lexical analyses of digitized manuscripts, contemporary novels, and dialect recordings. Deep learning models, trained on HPC clusters, will classify dialect features in literary texts and correlate them with sociolinguistic variables such as urbanization and migration. Additionally, spectral clustering algorithms will map phonetic and grammatical divergence across regions using datasets exceeding 10 TB, requiring distributed storage and GPU-accelerated computation. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive diachronic atlas of Norwegian dialects, a computational framework for detecting literary dialect stylization, and publicly accessible tools for corpus-based philological research. These resources will advance scholarly understanding of language variation in Norway while supporting language preservation initiatives and applications in speech technology. The project’s computational demands—including multi-node processing of unstructured text, memory-intensive phylogenetic modeling, and large-scale hyperparameter tuning—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve rigorous, reproducible results within feasible timeframes. By integrating computational linguistics with literary studies, this work aims to redefine methodological paradigms in Scandinavian philology.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Norwegian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize drywall installation processes by simulating material performance, environmental interactions, and labor efficiency in diverse construction scenarios. While modern drywall installation relies on empirical methods and standardized practices, emerging challenges—including climate-driven material degradation, demand for energy-efficient buildings, and labor shortages—require data-driven strategies to improve precision and sustainability. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive models to evaluate how variables such as humidity, thermal cycling, and installation techniques influence long-term structural integrity and resource efficiency. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), discrete event simulation (DES), and machine learning (ML) to model drywall systems at multiple scales. FEA will simulate stress distribution, crack propagation, and moisture absorption in drywall panels under dynamic environmental conditions. Concurrently, DES will model workflow efficiency across job sites, incorporating variables like crew size, tool availability, and spatial constraints. ML algorithms trained on historical installation data will predict optimal material cutting patterns and labor allocation to minimize waste and time. These modules will be coupled to create a digital twin platform for virtual testing of drywall strategies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for resolving high-resolution, multiphysics simulations and iterating ML models across large parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for contractors to preemptively identify failure risks, reduce material waste by up to 20%, and improve compliance with energy codes. By bridging computational engineering and construction trades, this work aims to advance technical education in drywall installation, enabling trainees to engage with predictive analytics and sustainable practices. The resulting datasets and models will be disseminated through open-source repositories and integrated into vocational training curricula.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, tape, and plaster drywall installations in interior and exterior construction jobs. Includes instruction in drywall handling and transport, cutting and mounting, taping and spackling, finishing, job analysis and estimation, site safety, tool operation and maintenance, blueprint and specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The increasing complexity of commercial vehicle operations necessitates advanced computational approaches to enhance safety, efficiency, and training outcomes. Traditional driver instruction and operational planning methods often struggle to account for dynamic variables such as real-time traffic, cargo load dynamics, and environmental conditions. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale simulation and optimization platform tailored for commercial vehicle operations. The research will integrate high-fidelity vehicle dynamics models, machine learning algorithms, and large-scale traffic datasets to simulate realistic driving scenarios, optimize route planning under uncertainty, and analyze driver decision-making processes. Computational workflows will employ parallelized agent-based modeling to emulate mixed fleets in diverse urban and highway environments, coupled with reinforcement learning techniques to iteratively improve instructional modules. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for generating adaptive training simulations that respond to individual learner performance, predictive models for fuel efficiency optimization across heterogeneous vehicle types, and data-driven insights into risk mitigation strategies. By utilizing HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge critical gaps between theoretical instruction and real-world operational demands, ultimately contributing to reduced accident rates, lower emissions through optimized routing, and standardized metrics for assessing commercial driver proficiency. The proposed computational infrastructure will also enable future integration of emerging technologies such as vehicle-to-infrastructure communication systems into training curricula.
cip_title: Truck and Bus Driver/ Commercial Vehicle Operator and Instructor
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to drive trucks and buses, delivery vehicles, for-hire vehicles and other commercial vehicles, or to instruct commercial vehicle operators. Includes instruction in operating gas, diesel, or electrically-powered vehicles; loading and unloading cargo or passengers; reporting delays or accidents on the road; verifying load against shipping papers; arranging transportation for personnel; and keeping records of receipts and fares.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrated computational framework for optimizing sustainable urban real estate development under dynamic socio-environmental constraints. The core challenge lies in balancing rapid urbanization with climate resilience, affordability, and community well-being—a multidimensional problem requiring simultaneous analysis of interdependent variables such as shifting land-use regulations, evolving market demands, carbon emission targets, and infrastructure strain. Traditional modeling tools often silo these factors, leading to fragmented decision-making. To address this, the project proposes a novel agent-based simulation platform that combines generative urban design algorithms, real-time economic forecasting, and participatory stakeholder behavior modeling. The computational approach will integrate geospatial datasets (e.g., zoning maps, flood risk projections), machine learning models trained on historical development patterns, and Monte Carlo methods to simulate thousands of development scenarios across diverse policy and climate futures. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to metropolitan-level granularity while maintaining sub-neighborhood spatial resolution and hourly temporal resolution over decadal time horizons. Expected outcomes include a dynamic risk-assessment tool that quantifies trade-offs between profitability, equity, and ecological impact, as well as generative design prototypes for mixed-use developments adaptable to regional climate scenarios. By enabling rapid iteration through complex design-policy permutations, this work aims to advance evidence-based frameworks for public-private development partnerships, particularly in underserved communities facing disproportionate climate vulnerability. The resulting open-source models will provide municipal planners and developers with actionable insights to navigate conflicting priorities in urban growth, setting a precedent for computational resource integration in non-traditional, policy-adjacent applied research domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create and redevelop housing, offices, retail centers, and industrial sites. Includes instruction in architectural design and construction, historic preservation, landscape architecture, urban planning and design, business, real estate and land use law, public policy, and engineering.

abstract: Pediatric diseases often exhibit complex molecular and phenotypic heterogeneity, complicating the development of targeted therapies. This project aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in pediatric oncology by integrating multi-omics data, clinical variables, and pharmacological profiles. The research focuses on pediatric solid tumors, which account for significant morbidity and mortality yet remain understudied compared to adult cancers. A critical barrier is the computational complexity of analyzing large-scale genomic datasets while accounting for developmental context, tumor microenvironment dynamics, and drug response variability. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational framework. First, whole-genome sequencing and single-cell RNA-seq data from pediatric tumor cohorts will be processed using optimized pipelines for variant calling, clonal evolution inference, and spatial transcriptomic mapping. Second, machine learning models—including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers—will predict tumor progression and drug sensitivity by integrating genomic features with clinical outcomes and in vitro drug screening data. Third, molecular dynamics simulations will model protein-ligand interactions for prioritized therapeutic candidates, enabling virtual screening of compound libraries. These simulations require GPU-accelerated nodes due to the scale of conformational sampling. The HPC infrastructure will also support the development of a federated learning platform to collaborate with external institutions while preserving patient data privacy. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of subtype-specific biomarkers for early diagnosis, (2) optimized drug combination strategies to overcome resistance mechanisms, and (3) open-source computational tools for pediatric oncology research. By elucidating context-specific disease drivers and therapeutic vulnerabilities, this work will directly inform two ongoing clinical trials for high-risk neuroblastoma and rhabdomyosarcoma. The requested resources are essential for managing datasets exceeding 500 TB, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks, and reducing model training times from weeks to days. This project bridges critical gaps in pediatric cancer research and establishes a scalable framework for data-driven clinical decision-making.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Medicine

abstract: This project proposes a computational investigation of stylistic and thematic evolution in understudied 20th-century Anglophone speculative fiction, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze a corpus of 15,000 novels, short stories, and serialized works (1900–1999). While existing scholarship has focused on canonical authors, this study addresses the critical gap in understanding how marginalized voices—particularly women and writers of color—developed narrative strategies that reshaped genre conventions. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in linguistic innovation, metaphorical coherence, and cross-author influence at scales impractical for manual analysis. Using transformer-based language models fine-tuned on genre-specific texts, we will perform multi-task learning to classify rhetorical devices, track conceptual metaphor propagation through dynamic graph networks, and model semantic shifts in key speculative tropes (e.g., "utopia," "alienation"). HPC resources are required for three principal tasks: 1) distributed training of a BERT variant on 8TB of tokenized texts using GPU-accelerated nodes, 2) temporal network analysis of intertextual references via MPI-parallelized community detection algorithms, and 3) ensemble clustering of stylistic features across 50-dimensional semantic spaces. The pipeline integrates Python NLP stacks (spaCy, Hugging Face) with custom CUDA kernels for metaphor detection. Results will produce the first quantitative taxonomy of non-canonical speculative fiction’s narrative techniques, challenging existing periodization models in literary studies. A publicly accessible knowledge graph will map authorial networks and trope trajectories, enabling interactive exploration of how marginalized writers subverted dominant paradigms. This work establishes methodological foundations for computational literary analysis of large-scale, culturally significant corpora while recentering overlooked contributions to genre history. Resource requests prioritize GPU memory (4 nodes with 80GB VRAM) and high-throughput storage to manage iterative model training and graph database operations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in English language literature, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural and intellectual exchange across premodern and early modern societies using large-scale, cross-disciplinary datasets. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of knowledge transmission, adaptation, and synthesis in multilingual textual corpora, material culture records, and sociohistorical metadata—a task requiring the integration of methods from computational linguistics, network science, and spatial humanities. Current scholarship remains constrained by discipline-specific tools that struggle to reconcile qualitative nuance with quantitative scalability. To address this gap, we propose deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze heterogeneous datasets spanning 12th–17th century Eurasian literary works, trade ledgers, and archaeological inventories. Computational workflows will include transformer-based language models fine-tuned for historical multilingual text alignment, graph neural networks to map evolving intellectual networks, and agent-based simulations to model cultural diffusion processes. These methods demand parallelized processing of terabyte-scale textual data, dynamic network visualization at scale, and iterative parameter testing for simulation calibration—tasks exceeding the capacity of local workstations.
