abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of molecular mechanisms underlying chronic inflammatory diseases in companion animals, with a focus on feline chronic gingivostomatitis (FCGS). FCGS is a debilitating oral condition in cats, characterized by severe mucosal inflammation and pain, yet its pathogenesis remains poorly understood. Traditional experimental approaches have been limited in resolving the complex interactions between host immune dysregulation, microbiome dynamics, and viral cofactors. To address this gap, we propose an integrative computational approach combining bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from feline oral tissues with metagenomic profiling of microbial communities. HPC resources will enable large-scale alignment and annotation of host transcriptomes, de novo assembly of microbial genomes, and network-based analyses to identify critical pathways driving inflammation. Machine learning models will be trained to classify disease states and predict treatment responses using multi-omics features. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between host immune receptors and microbial antigens to pinpoint potential therapeutic targets. The scale of data (≥50 TB) and the computational intensity of these analyses—particularly the simulation of protein-ligand binding affinities across millions of conformations—necessitate parallelized processing and high-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers for early diagnosis, candidate molecules for immunomodulatory therapies, and a publicly accessible database of feline oral microbiome references. This work will directly inform clinical trials for FCGS while establishing computational frameworks applicable to other immune-mediated diseases in veterinary medicine, ultimately bridging translational gaps between animal and human biomedical research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern ground transportation systems necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing vehicle routing, traffic flow management, and energy consumption in mixed fleets of conventional and autonomous ground vehicles. A critical gap exists in scalable computational methods capable of modeling real-time interactions between diverse vehicle types, infrastructure constraints, and dynamic environmental conditions. To bridge this gap, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized agent-based simulations and machine learning algorithms. These tools will process large-scale datasets from urban traffic networks, vehicle telemetry, and environmental sensors to model scenarios such as congestion mitigation, emergency vehicle prioritization, and energy-efficient routing under variable demand. The computational workflow will integrate graph-based optimization, reinforcement learning for adaptive decision-making, and fluid dynamics models to simulate air resistance effects on fuel efficiency. By scaling these analyses across thousands of concurrent agents and multi-city datasets, the project aims to identify system-wide patterns that inform policy and operational strategies. Anticipated outcomes include novel algorithms for real-time traffic management, validated strategies for reducing fleet-wide emissions by 15-20% in simulated urban corridors, and open-source tools for adaptive infrastructure planning. The HPC resources are essential to handle the project’s computational demands, including petascale data ingestion, millions of parallel agent interactions per simulation cycle, and iterative training of deep neural networks for predictive traffic modeling. Results will directly benefit transportation agencies and logistics operators by providing actionable insights into system optimization, while advancing methodological innovations in computational transportation science. This work aligns with national priorities for intelligent infrastructure development and decarbonization of freight and passenger transport networks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle and equipment operation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating emerging digital tools and computational methodologies into art pedagogy, a critical gap in contemporary art teacher education. While traditional approaches to art instruction emphasize manual techniques and subjective assessment, the increasing prevalence of digital art platforms, generative algorithms, and immersive technologies necessitates new pedagogical frameworks. However, the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to analyze student interactions with these tools limits educators’ ability to adapt curricula effectively. This research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model student engagement, creativity, and skill development in digital art environments. Using anonymized datasets from classroom trials—including temporal interaction logs, multimodal artwork outputs (e.g., 3D models, digital paintings), and biometric feedback—we will train machine learning models to identify patterns in creative decision-making and technical proficiency. Computational image analysis pipelines will quantify stylistic evolution across student portfolios, while agent-based simulations will test hypothetical teaching strategies in virtual classroom environments. These methods require HPC capabilities to process terabyte-scale visual datasets, parallelize neural network training for generative adversarial networks (GANs) simulating art critiques, and run iterative simulations of pedagogical scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for assessing digital art competencies through computational metrics, (2) evidence-based recommendations for integrating generative AI tools into lesson plans, and (3) open-source visualization tools to help educators interpret complex learning analytics. By bridging computational analysis and art pedagogy, this work aims to equip future art teachers with empirically validated strategies to foster creativity in technology-rich classrooms, ensuring their readiness to educate students in rapidly evolving digital art landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach art and art appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical to global renewable energy portfolios, yet optimizing their efficiency, environmental sustainability, and integration with modern power grids remains a multifaceted challenge. This project seeks to address gaps in predictive modeling of hydroelectric infrastructure performance under dynamic environmental and operational conditions, particularly focusing on turbine efficiency degradation due to sediment erosion, reservoir sedimentation patterns, and transient grid stability during variable flow regimes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, discrete element modeling (DEM) for sediment transport analysis, and machine learning (ML)-enhanced predictive control algorithms. The CFD-DEM simulations will resolve turbulent flow-structure interactions and particle-laden flow dynamics at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, enabling precise characterization of turbine blade wear and reservoir bed morphology evolution. Concurrently, ML models trained on synthetic and historical operational datasets will optimize real-time turbine control strategies and grid load-balancing protocols. The integration of these computational approaches requires HPC capabilities to manage large-scale parallel simulations, iterative ML training processes, and probabilistic risk assessments under stochastic hydrological inputs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for mitigating sediment-induced efficiency losses, adaptive operational guidelines to extend infrastructure lifespans, and data-driven strategies for improving grid resilience. By advancing computational methodologies in hydroelectric system analysis, this research will directly support the development of more sustainable and economically viable hydroelectric technologies, aligning with global decarbonization targets. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration at scales impractical for local clusters, accelerating insights translatable to both existing infrastructure retrofits and next-generation hydropower designs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in hydroelectric energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Pediatric critical care patients with life-threatening organ failure face heterogeneous and dynamic physiological challenges, requiring precise, individualized interventions. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols that may not adapt to real-time changes in multi-organ interactions or patient-specific pathophysiology. This project aims to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating multi-scale clinical data to model organ system dynamics and predict patient trajectories. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of traditional analytical methods in capturing complex, nonlinear interactions between vital physiological systems (e.g., cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological) under critical illness. We propose to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid mechanistic-machine learning approach. Mechanistic models based on differential equations will simulate organ-level physiology, while deep neural networks trained on retrospective electronic health record data (including vital signs, laboratory results, and drug responses) will map population-derived patterns to patient-specific parameter tuning. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of high-frequency physiological time-series data (>10,000 data points/patient/day) and iterative optimization of coupled organ models across diverse clinical scenarios. HPC resources will enable 1) large-scale parameter space exploration for model calibration, 2) ensemble forecasting of intervention outcomes under physiological uncertainty, and 3) real-time simulation of crisis scenarios for clinical training modules. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for identifying early signs of decompensation, optimizing fluid/vasoactive drug regimens, and simulating extracorporeal life support strategies. This work will advance precision approaches in pediatric critical care by bridging population-level evidence with individualized physiological modeling, ultimately aiming to reduce mortality and morbidity in children with multi-organ failure. The computational infrastructure developed will be shared as an open-source toolkit for validating critical care interventions across diverse pediatric populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on advanced life support for children, from the term or near-term neonate to the adolescent. This includes critical care management of life-threatening organ system failure in both medical and surgical patients and support of vital physiological functions.

abstract: Hospice and palliative care patients present complex, multidimensional needs influenced by dynamic interactions between biological, psychosocial, and environmental factors. Current predictive models for symptom trajectories and care outcomes often rely on linear analyses of isolated variables, limiting their ability to capture the emergent, nonlinear behaviors that arise from these interactions. This project seeks to develop an integrative computational framework to model the interplay of physiological decline, psychosocial stressors, caregiver dynamics, and environmental constraints in end-of-life care. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis to simulate patient-caregiver ecosystems, incorporating real-world data from electronic health records (EHRs), wearable biosensors, and qualitative psychosocial assessments. Machine learning algorithms will identify latent patterns in time-series data to parameterize ABM agents, while network models will map cascading effects of interventions (e.g., pain management adjustments, caregiver support) across physical, emotional, and social domains. A key innovation is the integration of stochastic models to simulate rare but clinically critical events, such as rapid symptom exacerbation triggered by caregiver burnout or environmental instability. Computational workflows will be validated against longitudinal datasets from 3 hospice organizations, encompassing 1,200+ patients. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize personalized care plans, identify high-risk transition points, and quantify trade-offs between therapeutic intensity and quality of life. This work addresses a critical gap in palliative care research by providing a systems-level, computationally rigorous approach to understanding interdependencies often overlooked in traditional clinical studies. The resulting framework will serve as a scalable resource for simulating care scenarios, testing ethical decision-making algorithms, and advancing evidence-based strategies for holistic patient support. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges health sciences, complex systems theory, and computational ethics to address an urgent, underserved need in end-of-life care innovation.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to work with patients in hospice and palliative care and focuses on the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social needs of patients and families affected by advanced illness. Includes instruction in aging, thanatology, pharmacology, complementary and integrative therapies, pathophysiology, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize parametric design workflows in drafting and engineering technology applications, with a focus on reducing iterative design cycles and material inefficiencies in complex assemblies. Current drafting software tools struggle to efficiently process multi-variable design scenarios involving large-scale component interactions, particularly when integrating real-world constraints such as thermal expansion, load distribution, and manufacturability. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA) simulations and machine learning-driven topology optimization across thousands of design permutations. The computational approach combines CAD-based parametric modeling libraries with GPU-accelerated solvers to evaluate structural and functional performance under dynamically adjustable constraints. Key innovations include adaptive mesh refinement algorithms to balance simulation accuracy with computational cost and graph neural networks to predict failure modes in multi-material assemblies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educational use in drafting technology programs, enabling students to explore high-fidelity simulations of industrial-scale systems while adhering to ASME Y14.5-2018 standards. The project will also generate benchmark datasets correlating digital twin accuracy with physical prototyping results, addressing a critical need for validated predictive models in vocational engineering technology training. By reducing simulation time from days to hours, this resource will directly enhance curriculum delivery in computer-aided design (CAD) courses while providing industry partners with actionable insights into sustainable material usage. The requested computing allocation will support containerized workflows on Slurm-managed clusters, with an emphasis on scaling MPI-enabled optimization tasks across heterogeneous node architectures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally apply technical skills to create working drawings and computer simulations for a variety of applications. Includes instruction in specification interpretation, dimensioning techniques, drafting calculations, material estimation, technical communications, computer applications, and interpersonal communications.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in veterinary clinic operations through the development of a computational framework to model and optimize client-patient intake workflows, staff communication patterns, and administrative task prioritization. Veterinary receptionists operate in high-pressure environments where rapid decision-making—balancing urgent patient needs, client expectations, and regulatory compliance—directly impacts clinic efficiency and care outcomes. However, existing tools for workflow analysis in this niche lack the granularity to account for species-specific triage protocols, dynamic client emotional states, or the interplay between digital record-keeping and in-person interactions. The proposed study will leverage high-performance computing resources to simulate clinic operations using a hybrid agent-based model (ABM) integrated with natural language processing (NLP) trained on anonymized client communication logs. The ABM will parameterize variables including appointment type diversity, staff multitasking thresholds, and emergency interruption frequencies, while NLP analysis will identify correlations between client inquiry patterns and downstream workflow bottlenecks. By iteratively testing optimization strategies across synthetic clinic populations, the model will generate actionable protocols for task sequencing, client education resource allocation, and stress-tested contingency planning. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin framework adaptable to varied clinic sizes and specialties, with validation against real-world data from three partner veterinary hospitals. This work fills a critical gap in non-clinical veterinary operations research, offering computational tools to reduce staff burnout, improve patient throughput, and enhance client trust—a novel intersection of service sector analytics, behavioral modeling, and veterinary administrative science. The resource-intensive nature of simultaneous multi-clinic simulations and large-language model fine-tuning necessitates the requested computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers, veterinary technicians, or veterinarians, to provide customer service, visitor reception, and patient intake and discharge services. Includes instruction in veterinary office and animal care facility procedures, veterinary terminology, interpersonal skills, record-keeping, customer service, telephone skills, data entry, interpersonal communications skills, and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: The development of individualized education programs (IEPs) for students with disabilities requires educators to synthesize complex data from diverse sources, including academic performance records, behavioral assessments, and diagnostic evaluations. Current IEP design processes are labor-intensive and often lack systematic tools to model the longitudinal impacts of pedagogical strategies or predict student outcomes under varying interventions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and train machine learning models capable of optimizing IEP recommendations. The research will utilize anonymized student datasets spanning demographic information, standardized test scores, behavioral incident reports, and IEP goal-tracking data from K-12 special education programs. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to analyze qualitative IEP documents, coupled with multimodal neural networks to identify patterns linking intervention strategies to student progress. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling to simulate classroom dynamics and resource allocation scenarios, enabling educators to explore the potential outcomes of specific accommodations or teaching methods before implementation. The HPC environment is critical for processing large-scale educational datasets (n > 100,000 student-years) and iteratively refining models through hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive framework to assist educators in creating data-informed IEPs, reducing the time required for manual planning while improving the specificity of disability-specific interventions. By quantifying the efficacy of instructional approaches across diverse learner profiles, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in special education teacher preparation programs. The computational tools developed will undergo validation through partnerships with school districts, ensuring alignment with legal requirements (e.g., IDEA compliance) and practical classroom constraints.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children or adults with special learning needs or disabilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as special education teachers in a collaborative or team environment. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the socio-spatial dynamics of communal housing environments through computational modeling to address gaps in understanding how architectural layouts influence social cohesion and conflict. While housing design is recognized as a mediator of human interaction, existing studies lack granular, scalable tools to simulate emergent behaviors in diverse populations over time. The research proposes an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate how residents with varying cultural, economic, and behavioral profiles adapt to shared spaces under constraints such as limited privacy or resource access. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parameterize thousands of virtual agents with real-world demographic data, model multiyear interactions across high-resolution spatial grids, and analyze nonlinear outcomes through machine learning classifiers. The ABM will integrate datasets from urban ethnography, behavioral psychology, and architectural schematics to simulate scenarios ranging from high-density urban co-living complexes to transitional housing for displaced populations. Computational experiments will test how design interventions—such as modular partitions, decentralized amenities, or circulation patterns—affect metrics of well-being, conflict frequency, and collective problem-solving. Outcomes will yield a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for policymakers and designers to proactively evaluate housing prototypes for social resilience. By bridging computational social science with human-environment theories, this work advances an understudied interdisciplinary niche in housing studies, offering empirically grounded strategies to mitigate systemic inequities in communal living contexts. The project’s scale—requiring parallelized simulations across 10,000+ core-hours—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve the resolution and statistical power needed for generalizable insights.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in housing and human environments, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Early Childhood and Family Studies (ECFS) by developing a novel computational framework to model dynamic, multigenerational family interactions and their impact on early childhood developmental trajectories. Traditional ECFS research relies on observational, survey, or small-scale longitudinal data, limiting the ability to analyze complex, nonlinear relationships between family systems, socioenvironmental factors, and developmental outcomes. The proposed work addresses this gap by integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning techniques to simulate heterogeneous family units across diverse cultural and socioeconomic contexts. The computational model will incorporate parameters derived from developmental psychology, family sociology, and early childhood education datasets, including family communication patterns, caregiver stress dynamics, and resource allocation behaviors. HPC resources are critical to support large-scale parameter space exploration, real-time adaptation of agent behaviors via reinforcement learning, and sensitivity analyses across synthetic populations representing over 10,000 unique family configurations. Expected outcomes include the identification of critical leverage points for intervention in familial environments, predictive models of developmental risk factors under varying socioeconomic conditions, and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for policymakers and educators. By bridging computational social science with developmental theory, this work pioneers methodologies to study emergent family dynamics at unprecedented scale and granularity, offering transformative potential for evidence-based strategies in early childhood support systems.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the development and learning of children from birth to six years old within the context of the family. Includes instruction in child abuse and neglect, child and infant growth and development, early childhood education, early childhood language and literacy, early childhood math and science, early childhood special education, family literacy, family sociology, family and marriage relations, assessment and measurement, psychology, and psychopathology.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the structural and semantic evolution of U.S. case law, with the goal of identifying implicit patterns in judicial reasoning that are often opaque to foreign legal professionals. While traditional comparative legal pedagogy focuses on doctrinal differences, foreign lawyers trained in civil law systems frequently struggle with the dynamic, precedent-driven nature of common law jurisprudence. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model over 200 years of digitized federal court opinions, statutes, and law review articles, creating a multidimensional map of legal concept integration and divergence. Using transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned on legal corpora, we will perform semantic similarity analysis across temporal, jurisdictional, and doctrinal axes. Graph neural networks will then model citation networks and argumentative dependencies to quantify how specific legal principles (e.g., due process, contractual ambiguity) accumulate contextual weight through repeated judicial application. A novel attention mechanism will be implemented to detect latent references to foreign legal concepts in U.S. opinions—a phenomenon critical for comparative analysis but rarely systematically studied. The computational demands of training these models on terabyte-scale legal text corpora, particularly for long-context sequence processing and dynamic graph traversals, necessitate distributed GPU clusters and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include an open-access visualization platform that interactively traces concept evolution and a predictive model flagging potential jurisprudential divergence points for specific legal doctrines. This work aims to provide foreign lawyers with data-driven insights into the implicit logics of common law development while establishing computational methods tailored to legal epistemology—a niche intersecting jurisprudential theory, computational linguistics, and educational technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares lawyers educated outside the United States to understand U. S. or Canadian law and jurisprudence.

abstract: Dental caries and periodontal diseases remain significant public health challenges, driven by complex interactions between microbial communities, host factors, and behavioral determinants. Current clinical approaches in dental hygiene often rely on generalized preventive strategies, which may not account for the heterogeneity of oral microbiomes or individualized risk profiles. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale metagenomic, clinical, and demographic datasets, enabling the development of predictive models for personalized oral disease prevention. The research will focus on three objectives: (1) characterizing taxonomic and functional shifts in oral microbiomes associated with caries and periodontal disease progression using longitudinal metagenomic sequencing data; (2) integrating microbial data with patient-specific variables (e.g., diet, hygiene practices, medical history) through machine learning algorithms to identify high-risk profiles; and (3) simulating microbial community dynamics under varying preventive interventions to optimize treatment strategies. Computational workflows will employ parallelized bioinformatics pipelines for sequence analysis, graph-based neural networks for heterogeneous data integration, and agent-based modeling to simulate ecological interactions within oral biofilms. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing datasets spanning thousands of patients, performing real-time analytics during clinical consultations, and executing computationally intensive simulations. Expected outcomes include novel biomarkers for early disease detection, evidence-based guidelines for tailored preventive care, and open-source tools to support clinical decision-making in dental hygiene practice. By bridging computational science with dental hygiene, this work aims to advance precision oral healthcare while equipping future practitioners with data-driven approaches to improve patient outcomes and reduce disparities in oral disease burden.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean teeth and apply preventive materials, provide oral health education and treatment counseling to patients, identify oral pathologies and injuries, and manage dental hygiene practices. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, microbiology, and pathology; dental hygiene theory and techniques; cleaning equipment operation and maintenance; dental materials; radiology; patient education and counseling; office management; supervised clinical training; and professional standards.

abstract: Chronic wounds represent a significant clinical challenge, with persistent inflammation, impaired tissue repair, and microbial resistance contributing to prolonged patient suffering and healthcare costs. Current treatment strategies often lack personalization due to limited understanding of how patient-specific factors—including genetic variability, immune responses, and microbiome dynamics—interact with wound microenvironmental conditions. This project proposes to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating high-performance computing (HPC) to model wound healing processes across molecular, cellular, and tissue levels. Leveraging patient-derived genomic, proteomic, and clinical data, we will construct agent-based models simulating immune cell behavior, finite element analyses of biomechanical stress distributions, and machine learning algorithms to predict treatment outcomes. The computational pipeline will incorporate dynamic feedback between microbial colonization patterns, oxygen gradients, and cellular metabolic states, enabling real-time simulation of wound progression under various therapeutic interventions. HPC resources are essential to manage the high-dimensional parameter space, perform parallelized simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts, and optimize adaptive treatment protocols via reinforcement learning. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers predictive of healing trajectories, the design of personalized wound care regimens targeting patient-specific dysregulations, and the generation of mechanistic insights into stalled healing phases. Validated against retrospective clinical datasets from 2,000+ chronic wound cases, this framework aims to reduce trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice. Successful implementation could decrease time-to-healing by 20-30% in simulated cohorts, with potential translation to decision-support tools for clinicians. The resource allocation will directly support the scaling of models to incorporate real-world data streams from wearable wound sensors, advancing precision medicine in a field where computational approaches remain underexplored despite high clinical urgency.
cip_definition: Research focused on Wound Care

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the safety, innovation, and sustainability of nail care practices through computational modeling and data-driven analysis. While nail technology is often perceived as a purely aesthetic field, its technical demands—such as optimizing chemical formulations, mitigating occupational health risks, and improving sanitation protocols—present understudied computational challenges. Current gaps in understanding the molecular interactions of nail products, the efficacy of sterilization methods, and the long-term biomechanical effects of nail treatments limit evidence-based standards in the industry. To address this, the project will employ molecular dynamics simulations to analyze the structural stability and allergenicity of acrylate compounds in gel polishes, machine learning models to correlate autoclave performance metrics with microbial inactivation rates, and finite element analysis to evaluate stress distribution on natural nails under varying sculpting techniques. These computational approaches require large-scale parallel processing to manage complex datasets, including 3D molecular structures, thermal dynamics of sterilization equipment, and biomechanical models of nail-substrate interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for safer product formulations, optimized sterilization workflows to prevent infections, and biomechanical guidelines to reduce nail damage during cosmetic procedures. By integrating computational science into nail technology, this research aims to establish a precedent for data-driven decision-making in cosmetology, enhance occupational safety for nail technicians, and improve client outcomes. The results will be disseminated through open-access tools for small businesses and training modules for licensing programs, bridging the gap between empirical practice and computational innovation in a specialized, non-traditional field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shape fingernails and toenails, remove unwanted skin and blemishes, apply polish and cosmetics to nails, and function as licensed manicurists or nail technicians/specialists.  Includes instruction in manicuring theory; skin anatomy; nail growth, irregularities, and diseases; sterilization and sanitation; equipment and table maintenance; cuticle, blemish, and rough skin removal; nail filing, shaping, and polishing; cream application and extremity massage; nail sculpture and design art; product storage and use; customer service; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern hybrid cloud ecosystems has exposed critical gaps in adaptive resource management frameworks, particularly for organizations operating across distributed, multi-vendor IT infrastructures. This project addresses the challenge of real-time resource optimization in heterogeneous computing environments where traditional static allocation strategies fail to account for dynamic workload patterns, energy efficiency constraints, and evolving security requirements. We propose developing a novel decision architecture that integrates graph-based workload modeling with reinforcement learning to enable context-aware resource distribution. The computational approach will leverage temporal graph neural networks to model infrastructure interdependencies while training multi-objective reinforcement learning agents on HPC clusters to simultaneously optimize for latency, energy consumption, and fault tolerance. Key innovations include a differentiable simulation environment for hybrid cloud systems and a federated learning component that preserves organizational data sovereignty during model training. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to process real-world workload traces spanning 10,000+ node infrastructures, requiring parallelized training of multiple reinforcement learning agents across GPU nodes and large-scale graph processing capabilities for dependency analysis. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive resource orchestration that demonstrates 30-50% improvements in resource utilization efficiency compared to current industry standards, along with new metrics for quantifying resilience-energy tradeoffs in distributed systems. This work bridges computational systems engineering with operational IT management, advancing capabilities for next-generation sustainable computing infrastructure while establishing formal methods for intelligent service administration in complex, evolving technological ecosystems.
cip_title: Computer/ Information Technology Services Administration and Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer/information technology services administration and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Korean dialectology and historical linguistics, with a focus on analyzing phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variations across regional and temporal Korean language datasets. The primary research problem lies in the computational limitations of processing large-scale, multi-modal corpora—including textual archives, spoken dialect recordings, and historical manuscripts—that are critical for tracing language evolution and mapping dialect boundaries. Current methods for analyzing these datasets are constrained by the volume of unstructured data, the complexity of training cross-dialectal models, and the need for real-time processing of acoustic features in speech corpora. To address this, the project will employ neural network architectures, including transformer-based models for text analysis and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for speech signal processing, optimized for parallel computation on HPC clusters. Key tasks include automated phonetic alignment of non-standard dialect recordings, diachronic semantic vector modeling to track lexical shifts in pre-modern texts, and geospatial clustering of syntactic features. The computational pipeline will integrate existing NLP tools adapted for Korean’s agglutinative morphology and honorific systems, while novel codebases will be developed to handle historical orthographies and low-resource dialect variants. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Korean dialect variation, open-access models for dialect classification, and datasets annotating syntactic changes from Middle Korean to modern forms. These resources will directly support pedagogical tools for heritage language preservation and inform policy on standardized language education in multilingual communities. The project’s scale—processing over 10 TB of text and audio data, with iterative model training requiring thousands of GPU hours—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve feasible runtime and precision. By bridging computational linguistics with Korean philology, this work aims to set a methodological precedent for resource-intensive humanities research while addressing critical gaps in understanding Korea’s linguistic diversity.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization frameworks for next-generation heterogeneous computing architectures, which integrate CPUs, GPUs, and emerging accelerators to address growing computational demands in machine learning, real-time simulation, and edge computing. A critical challenge lies in dynamically balancing workloads, energy efficiency, and latency across these architectures, particularly as applications increasingly combine data-intensive and compute-intensive tasks. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, we will simulate heterogeneous systems using parameterized models of hardware behavior, interconnect topologies, and application profiles. These simulations will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods and evolutionary algorithms to explore design spaces at scale. Second, we will train machine learning models on simulation outputs to predict optimal task allocation and power management policies under varying constraints. Third, we will validate these models against physical testbeds deploying distributed computing workflows, including federated learning and real-time sensor fusion scenarios. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the exponential scaling of parameter combinations in system design, the terabyte-scale datasets generated by hardware telemetry, and the need for low-latency distributed training across thousands of concurrent nodes. Expected outcomes include: (1) open-source frameworks for adaptive resource management in heterogeneous systems, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing architectural tradeoffs for emerging workloads, and (3) energy-aware scheduling algorithms capable of reducing idle power consumption by 15-30% in simulated environments. This work will directly advance the design of efficient computing infrastructures for AI-driven applications while providing a methodological foundation for cross-layer optimization in hybrid architectures. Results will be disseminated through high-impact conferences in parallel computing and embedded systems, with derived tools made available to the broader research community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze longitudinal patterns in student behavioral interventions, with the goal of identifying optimal strategies for personalized support in K–12 educational settings. School psychologists face complex challenges in tailoring interventions due to heterogeneous student needs, dynamic classroom environments, and the interplay of academic, social-emotional, and developmental factors. While existing research emphasizes evidence-based practices, there is a critical gap in scalable models that integrate multi-source data (e.g., behavioral assessments, academic performance metrics, and teacher reports) to predict intervention efficacy. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble machine learning models on large-scale, de-identified datasets spanning 15,000+ students from diverse school districts. These datasets include structured behavioral logs, unstructured narrative notes from counseling sessions (processed via NLP techniques), and temporal academic records. Computational workflows will simulate intervention scenarios using agent-based modeling to account for social network influences and classroom-level dynamics. Key challenges involve managing high-dimensional data with varying temporal resolutions and addressing class imbalances in outcome variables. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across models, conducting Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, and storing intermediate outputs from iterative model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive tool to guide school psychologists in matching students to interventions based on multidimensional profiles, (2) quantitative benchmarks for intervention sequencing and dosage, and (3) open-source code for replicating analytic pipelines. By bridging computational scalability with school-based practicality, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in educational support systems while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for student privacy and algorithmic fairness.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized therapeutic interventions for patients undergoing physical rehabilitation. Current clinical practices in physical therapy often rely on generalized treatment protocols, which may not account for individual variations in biomechanics, neuromuscular response, or recovery trajectories. To address this gap, we propose a computational modeling framework to simulate patient-specific biomechanical and physiological responses to therapeutic exercises and interventions. Using anonymized patient data—including motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and clinical progress metrics—we will construct musculoskeletal models to analyze joint kinematics, muscle activation patterns, and load distribution during prescribed exercises. These models will integrate machine learning algorithms to predict optimal exercise parameters (e.g., intensity, range of motion, resistance) tailored to individual patient needs while minimizing injury risk. The computational workflow requires iterative simulations across diverse patient cohorts, necessitating HPC resources for parallel processing of large datasets and high-fidelity biomechanical computations. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomechanical biomarkers predictive of recovery efficiency, the generation of adaptive treatment recommendations, and the creation of open-access simulation tools for clinical educators. This work bridges computational science and physical therapy practice, offering a scalable method to enhance evidence-based care. By optimizing resource allocation in clinical settings and reducing trial-and-error approaches, the project aims to improve patient outcomes, accelerate recovery timelines, and inform pedagogical strategies in physical therapy assistant training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physical therapist, to implement physical therapy treatment care plans, train patients, conduct treatment interventions, use equipment, and observe and record patient progress. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, behavioral sciences, biomechanics, clinical documentation, clinical pathology, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing programming skill acquisition through adaptive, data-driven pedagogical frameworks, an emerging niche intersecting computational education and cognitive ergonomics. Traditional programming instruction often employs static curricula, which fail to account for heterogeneous learner backgrounds, cognitive styles, and knowledge retention patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computational infrastructure to model and simulate individualized learning trajectories. The core methodology involves deploying ensemble machine learning algorithms on multimodal educational datasets—including code submission histories, error-resolution patterns, and temporal engagement metrics—to identify latent correlations between instructional strategies and competency development. These models will drive dynamic content generation systems that adjust problem difficulty, conceptual focus, and feedback mechanisms in real time. The computational demands arise from processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning decades of anonymized student records, coupled with parallelized reinforcement learning architectures that require iterative optimization across thousands of simulated learner personas. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for personalized programming education, validated through longitudinal A/B testing against conventional teaching paradigms. Success metrics will quantify reductions in skill attainment disparities across demographic groups and improvements in complex problem-solving transfer rates. By establishing scalable, evidence-based approaches to programming pedagogy, this work aims to redefine how computational resources can democratize access to technical education while advancing interdisciplinary research at the nexus of educational psychology and adaptive systems design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer programming, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of German cultural identity through historical textual and visual media. The research problem centers on analyzing vast, multilingual corpora of 19th- and 20th-century German-language newspapers, pamphlets, and illustrated periodicals to trace shifts in representations of regional identity, particularly in border regions such as Alsace-Lorraine, Silesia, and South Tyrol. Current scholarship lacks systematic large-scale comparisons of how local narratives interacted with emerging national discourses during periods of geopolitical upheaval. The project will employ computational text analysis, image recognition algorithms, and geographic information system (GIS) mapping to process over 10 million pages of digitized materials from archives in Germany, France, Poland, and Italy. Key computational challenges include training custom transformer models for historical German script recognition (Fraktur), implementing multilingual topic modeling across dialect continua, and aligning visual motifs in illustrations with textual sentiment patterns. The HPC environment is critical for handling memory-intensive natural language processing pipelines and generating high-resolution spatial-temporal visualizations of discourse networks. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously overlooked transitional phases in identity construction preceding major political events, 2) an open-access annotated dataset linking visual and textual cultural markers, and 3) methodological innovations in computational analysis of historical hybrid media. This work will provide new insights into the complex interplay between local cultural practices and supranational identity formation, with implications for understanding contemporary debates about European cultural heritage. By integrating computational methods with close hermeneutic analysis, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for interdisciplinary area studies research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Germany, the neighboring countries of Austria and Switzerland, the German minorities in neighboring European countries, and the historical areas of German influence across Europe and overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the documentation, analysis, and revitalization of endangered Indigenous languages across the Americas. Many Native American languages exhibit complex morphological structures, intricate verb systems, and unique phonological patterns that challenge conventional linguistic analysis tools. The research problem centers on scaling computational methods to process large, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized oral histories, legacy texts, and modern speech recordings—across diverse language families such as Uto-Aztecan, Mayan, and Algonquian. Current software tools for morphological parsing, acoustic analysis, and corpus linguistics are not optimized for these languages’ typological features, nor do they efficiently handle the volume of multimodal data required for robust analysis. The project will employ parallelized workflows on HPC clusters to train neural models for automated morphological segmentation and syntactic annotation, conduct phylogenetic analyses of language diversification using Bayesian inference frameworks, and simulate sound change trajectories across dialect networks. These computational tasks demand significant memory allocation and multi-node processing due to the iterative nature of probabilistic modeling and the need to cross-reference thousands of lexical items across related languages. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access computational lexicons, enhanced speech recognition models for under-resourced languages, and phylogenetic trees that clarify historical relationships among language varieties. By integrating computational linguistics with community-driven documentation efforts, this work will provide scalable infrastructure for both academic research and Indigenous language revitalization programs, addressing critical gaps in linguistic theory while supporting cultural preservation imperatives. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the combinatorial complexity inherent in analyzing polysynthetic languages and to ensure equitable access to advanced computational methods for Indigenous language scholars.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: American Indian/ Native American Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the Western Hemisphere, with an emphasis on American Indian languages, but including other Native American languages. Includes instruction in philology; oral and written literatures; Inuit and Aleut languages; North American language families, including, but not limited to, Algonkian, Athabascan, Siouan, Muskogean, Iroquoian, Kumeyaay, Yuman, Mayan, Zapotecan, and Uto-Aztecan; South American language families, including, but not limited to, Andean-Equatorial, Ge-Pano-Carib, and Macro-Chibchan; and other minor languages.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a predictive framework for evaluating the cascading impacts of land-use transitions on coupled socio-ecological systems in rapidly urbanizing arid regions. Arid zones, which account for 40% of global land area, face intensifying pressures from climate change and human activity, yet existing sustainability models often inadequately capture feedback loops between ecological thresholds, infrastructure development, and informal economic adaptation strategies. Our interdisciplinary approach integrates high-resolution remote sensing data of vegetation-microclimate interactions, agent-based simulations of informal settlement patterns, and stochastic optimization models of decentralized water-energy-food networks. The computational challenge lies in resolving spatiotemporal mismatches between ecological processes (e.g., desertification fronts evolving over decades) and human system dynamics (e.g., seasonal migration affecting resource demand), requiring coupled simulations across 12 orders of magnitude in temporal scales. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to implement a nested modeling architecture, where continent-scale atmospheric-vegetation models (1 km resolution) are bidirectionally coupled with fine-grained agent-based models (1 m resolution) of human-environment interactions through adaptive mesh refinement techniques. This will enable the first unified simulation environment capable of testing how policy interventions in one subsystem (e.g., groundwater pricing reforms) propagate through cross-scale interactions to affect biodiversity corridors, informal labor markets, and renewable energy adoption rates. Expected outcomes include a decision-support toolkit for municipal planners that quantifies trade-offs between conventional urban expansion strategies and emergent adaptive approaches developed by local communities. By advancing computational methods for polycentric governance challenges, this work aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing complex adaptive systems in sustainability science, particularly in understudied arid regions where climate pressures intersect with rapid informal urbanization.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the concept of sustainability from an interdisciplinary perspective. Includes instruction in sustainable development, environmental policies, ethics, ecology, landscape architecture, city and regional planning, economics, natural resources, sociology, and anthropology.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation in tourism ecosystems under volatile environmental and demand conditions. The tourism and travel sector faces increasing complexity due to climate variability, geopolitical disruptions, and rapidly shifting consumer preferences, yet existing decision-support models lack the adaptive capacity to process multi-scale data streams in real time. We propose an agent-based simulation integrating heterogeneous datasets—including climate forecasts, social media sentiment, transportation network statuses, and hotel/attraction capacity metrics—to model tourist behavior, service provider responses, and environmental feedback loops. The computational approach combines deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with network optimization algorithms to generate adaptive pricing strategies and contingency plans for regional tourism operators. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to train DRL agents across millions of simulated scenarios accounting for stochastic weather events, supply chain disruptions, and evolving traveler priorities (e.g., sustainability preferences). The model will be validated against historical crisis events (e.g., pandemic travel restrictions, extreme weather incidents) and tested through partnerships with Mediterranean coastal tourism consortia facing climate-driven seasonality shifts. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision platform capable of recommending optimal pricing adjustments, staff allocation plans, and cross-business resource-sharing strategies under uncertainty. This work advances computational tourism studies by formalizing crisis-responsive resource management as a complex adaptive system, bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and climate resilience planning. Results will provide actionable insights for small-to-medium tourism enterprises lacking in-house predictive analytics capabilities, with particular emphasis on minimizing revenue loss during disruption events while maintaining service quality standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage travel-related enterprises and related convention and/or tour services. Includes instruction in travel agency management, tour arranging and planning, convention and event planning, travel industry operations and procedures, tourism marketing and promotion strategies, travel counseling, travel industry law, international and domestic operations, and travel and tourism policy.

abstract: The increasing complexity of firearm design and customization demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in precision, material performance, and safety. Traditional gunsmithing methods rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping and manual testing, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to model dynamic, multi-physics interactions such as thermal-stress coupling, ballistic gas dynamics, and long-term material wear. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing firearm components, including barrel harmonics, action reliability, and trigger mechanisms, under diverse operational conditions. By integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML), the research will simulate high-strain-rate deformation during firing cycles, heat dissipation in suppressors, and microstructural fatigue in alloys. These simulations will utilize open-source and commercial software (e.g., LS-DYNA, OpenFOAM) to generate multi-terabyte datasets, requiring parallel processing and GPU acceleration for efficient analysis. A key innovation involves training ML models on simulation outputs to predict failure thresholds and recommend design adjustments, reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation. The project will validate computational results through collaboration with industry partners, incorporating high-speed imaging and metallurgical testing. Outcomes will include open-access computational workflows tailored to gunsmithing applications, enabling educators and practitioners to integrate simulation-driven design into training programs. This work aims to advance the technical rigor of gunsmithing as a discipline, fostering safer, more durable firearms while reducing material waste and development costs. By bridging empirical craftsmanship with computational engineering, the project will establish a framework for next-generation firearms innovation, with broader implications for additive manufacturing and precision machining in related technical fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and modify firearms according to blueprints or customer specifications, using specialized hand tools and machines.

abstract: This research project addresses the challenge of optimizing predictive maintenance strategies for complex mechanical systems in industrial settings, where traditional diagnostic methods often fail to account for dynamic operational conditions and multi-physics interactions. Current approaches to fault detection and repair planning rely heavily on static thresholds or simplified models, leading to unnecessary downtime, inefficient resource allocation, and overlooked failure modes. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a computational framework integrating high-fidelity simulations of mechanical degradation processes with machine learning-driven anomaly detection. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) models simulating thermo-mechanical stress distributions across critical components under varying operational loads. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on synthetic and real-world sensor data to identify early-stage failure signatures in rotating machinery. The computational workflow requires large-scale parameter sweeps to account for material variability, environmental factors, and usage patterns, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for efficient model training and distributed memory architectures for physics-based simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive maintenance decision-support tool capable of recommending context-aware repair protocols and a comprehensive dataset mapping failure progression across common industrial equipment categories. By quantifying relationships between operational parameters and component lifespan, this research aims to advance repair technician training programs through data-driven insights into failure mechanisms while reducing maintenance costs by 15-30% in target applications. The HPC-enabled methodology will establish a scalable template for integrating multi-physics modeling with AI-driven diagnostics in underserved mechanical repair domains.
cip_title: Mechanic and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanic and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical computational bottlenecks in advancing nondestructive testing (NDT) and radioisotope-based material analysis within industrial radiologic technology. Current methods for simulating x-ray and gamma-ray interactions with complex materials rely on simplified models that compromise accuracy, particularly when analyzing heterogeneous structures or real-time thickness measurements in dynamic industrial environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop high-fidelity Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations coupled with machine learning-driven image reconstruction algorithms. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating multiscale computational models that account for material microstructure, radiation scattering, and detector response to improve defect detection sensitivity in welded metals and composite materials, and (2) optimizing neural networks for rapid tomographic reconstruction of thickness measurement data in rolling mill applications. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across varied material compositions, detector configurations, and beam energies while maintaining the temporal resolution required for inline quality control systems. Expected outcomes include validated simulation frameworks that reduce empirical calibration requirements by 40-60% and convolutional neural network architectures capable of processing high-dimensional radiometric data 15x faster than current industrial systems. This work will directly enhance the precision of radiation-based testing methodologies used in aerospace manufacturing, nuclear infrastructure maintenance, and sheet metal production. By sharing optimized computational workflows through an open-source platform, the project aims to establish new benchmarks for predictive modeling in industrial radiologic technology while providing training opportunities for students in GPU-accelerated scientific computing applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of industrial and research testing equipment using radioisotopes. Includes instruction in x-ray analysis of materials, nondestructive testing and inspection of materials, and continuous measurement of paper or metal thickness.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable packaging solutions requires advanced computational tools to optimize material performance, environmental impact, and supply chain efficiency. Current approaches to packaging design rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in addressing multi-objective constraints such as carbon footprint reduction, mechanical durability, and end-of-life recyclability. This project proposes the development of a multi-scale computational framework to simulate and predict the behavior of novel bio-based polymer composites under real-world distribution and usage conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model polymer-chain interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress distribution in package geometries, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to correlate material properties with lifecycle environmental impacts. The computational pipeline will also incorporate stochastic modeling of supply chain logistics, including temperature fluctuations, vibration during transportation, and compression forces in storage, to evaluate package failure risks. Key challenges include resolving time- and length-scale disparities between molecular-level material behavior and macro-scale mechanical performance, as well as optimizing ML training on heterogeneous datasets spanning material science, fluid dynamics, and logistics. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for bio-composite packaging performance, a decision-support tool for material selection based on sustainability metrics, and open-access datasets linking processing parameters to environmental outcomes. By reducing reliance on physical trials, this work aims to accelerate the development of circular packaging systems, directly supporting industry goals to minimize waste and energy use. The HPC resources are critical to handling the computational intensity of coupled simulations and enabling parameter sweeps across diverse scenarios, which are infeasible with local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific, technological, design, and business principles to the development of packages and packaging materials, including raw material production, conversion of raw materials into usable forms, design, distribution, and post-use recycling and reuse. Includes instruction in principles of packaging, materials sciences, distribution and transportation, engineering and technology, graphic design, packaging regulations, and business and marketing.

abstract: Understanding how environmental change drives shifts in species interactions and evolutionary trajectories remains a critical challenge in ecology and evolutionary biology. This project addresses the computational limitations hindering large-scale, integrative analyses of eco-evolutionary dynamics across spatial and temporal scales. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and implement spatially explicit, individual-based models that simulate multi-species interactions under historical and projected climate scenarios. These models will integrate genomic data to assess adaptive potential in focal species and quantify feedbacks between selection, dispersal, and community assembly. A key innovation involves scaling phylogenetic comparative methods to analyze diversification rates across entire clades while incorporating heterogeneous environmental data layers. The computational workflow will parallelize simulations across parameter spaces representing alternative evolutionary hypotheses, requiring substantial memory and processing capacity to handle complex matrix operations and genomic datasets. Expected outcomes include identifying thresholds of environmental change that disrupt coevolutionary relationships, predicting spatial patterns of genetic diversity loss under climate scenarios, and resolving how landscape connectivity mediates evolutionary rescue. By unifying ecological and evolutionary timescales in a single computational framework, this work will advance predictive capacity for biodiversity responses to anthropogenic change while providing open-source tools for simulating eco-evolutionary processes. The requested resources are essential for managing terabyte-scale environmental inputs, running millions of agent-based model iterations, and performing Bayesian phylogenetic analyses across high-dimensional parameter spaces—tasks infeasible with standard laboratory computing infrastructure. This project directly supports the program’s mission to elucidate connections across biological hierarchies and evolutionary timescales, with implications for conservation prioritization and theoretical synthesis in evolutionary ecology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions across levels of biological organization--genes and genomes, organisms, species, and ecosystems--and how these change over time, including the origins and history of species, the processes by which biodiversity has evolved, and the ecological context in which this evolution takes place. Includes instruction in animal, plant, population, functional, evolutionary, and ecosystem ecology; ecological and evolutionary genetics; molecular evolution; population and conservation biology; animal and plant diversity; biometry; and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying the therapeutic efficacy of trauma-informed yoga, an emerging movement and mind-body therapy, in mitigating symptoms of chronic post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). While preliminary clinical studies suggest benefits, the integrative neural, musculoskeletal, and autonomic processes driving these outcomes remain poorly characterized. We propose a computational modeling framework to simulate multi-scale interactions between motor control circuits, stress response pathways, and dynamic postural adaptations during yoga practice. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the integration of functional MRI datasets (n=150) capturing real-time brain activity during trauma-informed yoga sequences with biophysical models of spinal reflex arcs, muscle spindle feedback loops, and heart rate variability dynamics. Machine learning pipelines will identify latent movement signatures correlated with parasympathetic nervous system engagement and default mode network modulation. Concurrently, finite element simulations will map tissue-level stress distributions during therapeutic poses to optimize biomechanical dosing parameters. The anticipated outcomes include: 1) a validated multiscale model of mind-body integration during trauma-responsive movement practices, 2) predictive algorithms for personalizing yoga sequences based on neural-autonomic biomarkers, and 3) open-source tools for quantifying dose-response relationships in movement therapies. By bridging computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and trauma physiology, this work addresses critical gaps in evidence-based design of mind-body interventions while advancing methodological paradigms for studying embodied cognition in mental health applications. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated neural network training, large-scale parameter space exploration for coupled differential equation systems, and high-resolution finite element analysis of musculoskeletal dynamics.
cip_title: Movement and Mind-Body Therapies and Education, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in movement and mind-body therapies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of federal-provincial policy coordination in Canada through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale political datasets and simulate intergovernmental decision-making processes. The research problem centers on understanding how institutional design, partisan alignment, and public opinion interact to shape policy outcomes in Canada’s multilevel governance system. Existing scholarship has identified key variables in federal-provincial relations but lacks integrative, data-driven models capable of capturing the nonlinear feedback loops and adaptive behaviors inherent to these interactions. To address this gap, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate negotiations between federal and provincial actors under varying constitutional, electoral, and socioeconomic conditions. The computational approach will integrate historical datasets (e.g., intergovernmental agreements, legislative voting records, and public opinion polls) with machine learning techniques to calibrate agent decision rules and validate model outputs. HPC resources are essential to iteratively run thousands of policy negotiation scenarios, optimize model parameters, and analyze high-dimensional interaction networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational framework for mapping causal pathways in multilevel governance, (2) empirical insights into how asymmetrical federalism affects policy diffusion across provinces, and (3) predictive analyses of institutional reform scenarios, such as modifications to fiscal transfer mechanisms or emergency response protocols. By advancing methodological innovation in political science, this research will provide policymakers with evidence-based tools to anticipate bottlenecks in intergovernmental cooperation. The project aligns with national priorities for strengthening governance resilience while contributing open-access computational models to the Canadian political science community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of Canadian political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in British and North American political theory, political parties and interest groups, provincial and local governments, Constitutional law, federalism and national institutions, executive and legislative politics, judicial politics, popular attitudes and media influences, political research methods, and applications to the study of specific issues and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to assess the long-term structural integrity of aging munitions storage facilities under dynamic environmental and operational stressors. The degradation of such facilities—particularly those housing conventional and specialized ordnance—poses critical risks to safety, mission readiness, and lifecycle costs, yet current maintenance protocols rely on reactive, manual inspections ill-suited to detect latent corrosion or material fatigue. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose a multi-physics simulation approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), thermodynamic modeling, and machine learning to predict corrosion propagation, moisture ingress, and thermal cycling effects within complex storage environments. The model will incorporate heterogeneous datasets spanning decades of environmental monitoring records, material property tests, and nondestructive evaluation (NDE) reports, processed via parallelized algorithms to resolve multi-scale interactions between atmospheric conditions, structural materials, and stored munitions.
