Key innovations include adaptive meshing for localized corrosion hotspots and graph neural networks to infer degradation pathways from sparse inspection data. By simulating decade-scale aging processes at high spatial resolution, the framework aims to identify at-risk infrastructure components, optimize inspection schedules, and inform preemptive maintenance strategies. Outcomes will directly support DoD priorities in infrastructure modernization and risk reduction, while advancing computational methodologies for aging military systems. The resource request targets 250,000 node-hours on GPU-accelerated clusters to manage the computational intensity of coupled simulations and deep learning workflows, enabling parametric studies across diverse climatic zones and munitions types. This interdisciplinary effort bridges materials science, environmental engineering, and predictive analytics, offering a paradigm shift in infrastructure resilience for defense logistics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of ground or sea-based weapons systems, ordinance and munitions. Includes instruction in basic sciences, electronics, systems technology, fluid power, computer science, conventional weapons systems, nuclear weapons systems, munitions systems, storage and safety, equipment operation, guidance and control systems, hazardous materials, corrosion control, nondestructive testing and quality control, and maintenance management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling and optimization frameworks for sustainable construction materials and structural systems. The construction industry faces growing pressure to reduce environmental impacts while maintaining cost efficiency and structural integrity, yet current design practices rely heavily on empirical data and simplified analytical models. These approaches often fail to capture the complex, multiscale interactions between novel materials (e.g., carbon-reinforced composites, bio-based concrete alternatives) and dynamic environmental loads. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational platform integrating finite element analysis (FEA), discrete element modeling (DEM), and machine learning (ML) to simulate material behavior under real-world conditions. HPC resources are critical for resolving the high-dimensional parameter space of material compositions, microstructural heterogeneity, and time-dependent degradation mechanisms. The project will parameterize models using experimental datasets from partner laboratories, then scale simulations to evaluate building-scale performance under stochastic stressors, including seismic events and climate-induced thermal cycling. A key innovation involves coupling ML-driven surrogate models with optimization algorithms to rapidly identify material configurations that minimize embodied carbon while meeting safety standards. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation tools for predicting construction material lifespans, a database of optimized low-carbon material profiles, and guidelines for integrating computational insights into construction workflows. By enabling high-fidelity virtual prototyping, this work aims to accelerate the adoption of sustainable materials, reduce reliance on physical testing, and inform resilient infrastructure design in alignment with global decarbonization goals. The requested computing resources will support parallelized simulations, hyperparameter tuning for ML models, and large-scale sensitivity analyses across 50+ material variables.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers, engineering contractors and other professionals engaged in the construction of buildings and related structures. Includes instruction in basic structural engineering principles and construction techniques, building site inspection, site supervision, construction personnel supervision, plan and specification interpretation, supply logistics and procurement, applicable building codes, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate computational modeling and simulation into the creation and analysis of complex metal artworks, addressing the challenge of optimizing material behavior, structural integrity, and aesthetic outcomes in advanced metalworking processes. Traditional methods in metal arts—such as casting, welding, and electroforming—rely heavily on iterative physical experimentation, which is time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in its ability to predict nuanced material interactions. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to develop predictive models for thermomechanical stresses during casting, electrochemical dynamics in anodizing and electroforming, and microstructural evolution in alloys under varying fabrication conditions. These simulations will employ finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning algorithms trained on empirical data from studio experiments. The project also explores generative design algorithms to iteratively refine 3D-printed metal sculptures, balancing geometric complexity with manufacturability constraints. Outcomes will include a library of open-source computational tools tailored to metal arts practitioners, enabling data-driven decision-making in studio practice. Additionally, the research will produce a series of hybrid digital-physical artworks that demonstrate the integration of computational insights with traditional craftsmanship. By bridging gaps between material science, computational engineering, and artistic practice, this work aims to expand the technical and expressive possibilities of metal arts while reducing material waste and energy consumption. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling large-scale simulations of multi-physics processes and training neural networks on high-resolution imaging data of metal surfaces. This interdisciplinary approach positions computational methods as a transformative force in visual arts pedagogy and creative practice, fostering new dialogues between technology and handcrafted materiality.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of individual artistic expression and technical skills necessary for fabricating refined metal works. Includes instruction in aesthetics, anodizing, art history, casting, design, electroforming, enameling, metalsmithing, sculpture, two and three-dimensional design, wax carving, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of legal texts, policies, and historical records central to Tribal and Indigenous law. The research addresses a critical gap in legal scholarship: the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to analyze the complex interplay between federal Indian law, tribal legal systems, and Indigenous rights frameworks. Traditional legal research methods, which rely heavily on manual case review and qualitative interpretation, struggle to systematically map the evolution of legal doctrines, identify patterns in judicial decision-making, or trace the sociolegal impacts of colonial legal structures on Indigenous communities. To address this, the project proposes an interdisciplinary computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning (ML) to process large corpora of legal documents, treaties, court opinions, and tribal codes. Key objectives include developing custom NLP pipelines to extract relational data (e.g., citations, jurisdictional overlaps, treaty violations) and training ML models to detect latent biases or inconsistencies in judicial reasoning across federal-tribal legal interfaces. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale and complexity of datasets, which span centuries of legal texts and multilingual Indigenous language materials requiring advanced preprocessing. Anticipated outcomes include (1) an open-access computational toolkit for legal scholars and tribal policymakers to analyze precedent networks and policy impacts, (2) data visualizations illuminating systemic disparities in federal-tribal case law, and (3) a foundational dataset for comparative studies on Indigenous rights recognition. By integrating computational rigor with critical legal theory, this work aims to empower Tribal nations with evidence-based strategies for legal advocacy and policy reform while establishing a methodological precedent for computational legal studies in underrepresented juridical traditions.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting federal Indian law, tribal law and policy, and Indigenous peoples' human rights.

abstract: Dental prostheses fabrication faces critical challenges in balancing biomechanical functionality, material durability, and patient-specific anatomical compatibility. Current design protocols rely heavily on manual adjustments and generic material standards, leading to suboptimal long-term performance and patient discomfort. This project proposes a computational framework to optimize the design and material composition of dental prostheses using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate biomechanical interactions at unprecedented resolution. The research will integrate patient-specific intraoral scan data, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model stress distribution, fatigue resistance, and biocompatibility of prostheses under dynamic masticatory loads. Key objectives include developing multi-scale models linking microstructural ceramic/polymer composite properties to macro-scale functional outcomes, and training ML algorithms to predict ideal material formulations for individualized cases. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across material compositions, layer deposition patterns, and occlusal geometries, addressing the combinatorial complexity of variables influencing prosthesis longevity. Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for dental laboratories, validated predictive models for fracture risk reduction, and data-driven guidelines for 3D-printed material layering strategies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges dental materials science, biomechanics, and computational modeling, offering transformative potential for personalized prosthodontics. By reducing iterative physical prototyping, the project aligns with sustainable manufacturing practices while advancing clinical outcomes through precision-engineered solutions. Successful implementation will establish a paradigm shift in dental laboratory workflows, prioritizing computational pre-validation to enhance patient quality of life and reduce long-term healthcare costs associated with prosthesis failure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of dentists, to design and construct dental prostheses such as caps, crowns, bridges, dentures, splints, and orthodontic appliances. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, dental materials, ceramics technology, impressions, complete dentures, partial dentures, orthodontics, crowns and bridges, sculpture, bonding and assembly techniques, and equipment operation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of household resource allocation under economic stress, with a focus on decision-making patterns that influence family well-being and intergenerational equity. While prior research in Family and Consumer Sciences has explored qualitative or survey-based approaches to understanding resource management, this study addresses a critical gap by developing agent-based computational models to simulate complex, nonlinear interactions between economic constraints, cultural norms, and individual priorities within diverse family structures. The research problem centers on how households navigate trade-offs between immediate needs (e.g., food security, healthcare) and long-term investments (e.g., education, retirement savings) during periods of financial instability, particularly in underrepresented communities. Computational methods will integrate demographic data, behavioral economics principles, and psychometric profiles to create adaptive simulations of decision pathways across varying socioeconomic scenarios. HPC resources are essential for scaling these simulations to account for high-dimensional variables—including geographic disparities, lifecycle transitions, and policy interventions—while maintaining temporal granularity over multi-year horizons. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to identify resilience factors in household financial behavior and actionable insights for designing targeted financial literacy programs. By bridging computational social science with human developmental theory, this project aims to advance evidence-based strategies for improving socio-emotional outcomes in family systems, while establishing a methodological precedent for data-intensive research in applied human sciences. The scalability of the models will also support future investigations into crisis-response mechanisms and intergenerational wealth transfer patterns.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on family and consumer sciences, including how individuals develop and function in family, work, and community settings and how they relate to their physical, social, emotional, and intellectual environments.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between personality traits, neurophysiological markers, and contextual behavioral responses through computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome existing methodological limitations. Traditional personality psychology frameworks—such as Freudian, Skinnerian, and Rogerian models—often rely on static, reductionist assessments, limiting their ability to capture the temporal and multi-layered complexity of personality as a system. To address this, we propose developing an integrative agent-based model (ABM) that simulates how stable personality characteristics interact with situational variables and neurophysiological processes (e.g., stress-response pathways, dopaminergic activation) to shape behavior. The ABM will incorporate parameters derived from empirical datasets, including longitudinal behavioral studies, functional neuroimaging, and psychopharmacological interventions, to test competing hypotheses about trait-state interactions. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to optimize model fit and identify nonlinear patterns in high-dimensional data. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations across diverse theoretical scenarios (e.g., trait activation thresholds, reinforcement learning dynamics) and conducting Bayesian parameter estimation with large posterior distributions. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework that reconciles divergent theories of personality structure and generates testable predictions about individual differences in adaptive and maladaptive behaviors. This work will provide novel insights into the neurocomputational mechanisms underlying personality, bridging gaps between psychodynamic, behavioral, and physiological perspectives. The resulting open-source tools and simulated datasets will serve as a resource for the broader research community, enabling hypothesis-driven exploration of personality dynamics at unprecedented granularity. By integrating historically siloed theories within a unified computational architecture, this project aims to advance personality psychology into a new era of data-intensive, theory-generative science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the unique organization of fairly permanent characteristics that set the individual apart from other individuals and, at the same time, determine how others respond to that individual. Includes instruction in Freudian, Skinnerian, Rogerian, and Ellisonian psychology; neo-Freudian psychology; psychological systems, neurophysiology, and psychopharmacology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of digital communication ecosystems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze large-scale, multi-platform campaigns in public relations and advertising. Modern communication strategies increasingly rely on dynamic, data-driven interactions across social media, targeted advertising, and real-time audience engagement, yet existing tools for predicting campaign outcomes or optimizing message diffusion remain limited in scope and granularity. This research will develop computational models to simulate the spread of persuasive messages through heterogeneous networks, incorporating variables such as user behavior, platform algorithms, and cultural context. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques and network analysis, the project will process terabytes of multi-modal data—including text, image, and engagement metrics from platforms like Meta, TikTok, and X—to identify patterns in message resonance and virality. Agent-based modeling will be employed to test hypothetical campaign strategies under varying conditions, while machine learning frameworks will predict emergent effects of cross-platform coordination. The computational intensity of these tasks necessitates HPC resources to manage parallel processing of large datasets, real-time simulations, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for evaluating communication campaigns in silico, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches; (2) actionable insights into algorithmic biases in content amplification across demographics; and (3) predictive tools to optimize resource allocation for message targeting. By bridging computational methods with communication theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in digital persuasion while addressing ethical implications of AI-driven communication strategies. The requested resources will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling socio-technical systems, directly supporting the program’s mission to innovate at the intersection of strategic communication and emerging technologies.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on organizational communication, public relations, and advertising; and that prepares individuals to function in a wide range of public and private sector positions requiring the skills of persuasive communication. Includes instruction in communications, public relations, and advertising theory; principles and techniques of persuasion; message/image design; marketing strategy; professional writing; public speaking and multi-media presentation skills; digital communications; and applied research.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and simulating the evolution of interactive narrative structures in digital media, a niche area intersecting computational storytelling, dynamic user interaction modeling, and high-performance simulation. While narrative generation has been explored in limited contexts, existing tools struggle with scalability when handling multi-threaded, user-influenced stories that adapt in real time to complex inputs (e.g., collaborative audiences, sensor-driven environments). The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in representing and optimizing branching narrative graphs with probabilistic dependencies, where traditional tree-based models become intractable for stories exceeding 10^4 decision nodes. Using a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks and discrete-event simulation, the project will implement a distributed memory framework to parallelize narrative state updates and user intent predictions. High-performance computing resources are critical for training models on synthetically generated interaction datasets (simulating 10^5+ user pathways) and for benchmarking real-time inference capabilities under variable concurrency loads. Expected outcomes include a novel partitioning algorithm to decompose narrative graphs across GPU nodes while preserving temporal consistency, as well as a publicly available toolkit for prototyping large-scale adaptive stories. This work advances computational media applications by enabling previously infeasible narrative complexity in domains such as immersive theater, collaborative world-building platforms, and AI-augmented educational simulations. The results will be evaluated against industry-standard interactive storytelling engines, with performance metrics targeting a 40% reduction in latency for stories with dynamically inserted user content. By addressing both algorithmic and systems-level challenges, this project bridges gaps between computational creativity, human-computer interaction, and distributed systems, fostering new research avenues in emergent media design.
cip_title: Computer Software and Media Applications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer software and media applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Occupational exposure to hazardous substances and unsafe work practices remains a critical public health challenge, with existing risk assessment frameworks often limited by sparse data and simplistic modeling approaches. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational platform to model complex occupational exposure scenarios, integrate multi-source sensor data, and predict health risks in dynamic industrial environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques to simulate interactions between workers, equipment, and environmental hazards (e.g., airborne particulates, chemical leaks, ergonomic stressors) across diverse industries. The computational framework will ingest real-time sensor data from wearable devices, industrial IoT systems, and environmental monitors to parameterize exposure gradients and workplace behaviors. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in dose-response relationships, while graph neural networks will identify latent patterns in large-scale occupational injury datasets. Key challenges include scaling mechanistic toxicokinetic models across heterogeneous worker populations and optimizing computational fluid dynamics simulations for aerosol dispersion in complex workspaces. Expected outcomes include predictive risk maps for high-exposure scenarios, AI-driven recommendations for adaptive safety interventions, and open-source tools for probabilistic exposure assessment. This work will directly address gaps in current industrial hygiene practices by enabling data-driven, scenario-specific hazard mitigation strategies while advancing computational methodologies for occupational health research. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive simulations, training deep learning models on multi-terabyte datasets, and maintaining computational fidelity across spatial-temporal scales relevant to workplace exposure dynamics. Project results will inform regulatory decision-making, safety protocol optimization, and targeted worker health monitoring systems, ultimately contributing to reduced occupational morbidity in high-risk industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to monitor and evaluate health and related safety standards in industrial, commercial, and government workplaces and facilities. Includes instruction in occupational health and safety standards and regulations; health-related aspects of various occupations and work environments; health hazard testing and evaluation; test equipment operation and maintenance; industrial toxicology; worker health and safety education; and the analysis and testing of job-related equipment, behavior practices, and protective devices and procedures.

abstract: Aerospace medicine faces critical challenges in understanding and mitigating the physiological impacts of extreme flight environments on human health, particularly during prolonged space missions or high-performance aviation. Current models of cardiovascular, neurovestibular, and musculoskeletal adaptation to microgravity, hypergravity, and circadian disruption lack the resolution to predict individual risk profiles or optimize countermeasures. This project proposes to develop multiscale computational models integrating real-time biometric data, environmental parameters, and mechanistic simulations to advance personalized interventions. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement coupled fluid-structure interaction models of cerebral hemodynamics during rapid G-force transitions, agent-based simulations of bone remodeling under microgravity, and machine learning-driven analyses of autonomic nervous system responses to altered atmospheric conditions. These models will be validated against clinical datasets from astronaut cohorts, high-G training programs, and simulated spaceflight studies. The computational framework will also incorporate wearable sensor data streams to enable dynamic risk stratification. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for individualized compression garment optimization, fluid loading protocols, and exercise regimens to prevent orthostatic intolerance or bone loss. By resolving the nonlinear interactions between physiological systems and extreme environmental stressors, this work will directly inform next-generation clinical guidelines for crew health monitoring and emergency medical contingency planning in spaceflight. The scalable architecture of these models will also benefit commercial aviation medicine, particularly for passengers and crew with preexisting health conditions. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution in whole-body simulations and to process high-dimensional datasets from multimodal biosensors. This project bridges critical gaps in translational aerospace medicine by enabling precision health strategies for heterogeneous populations in abnormal environments.
cip_definition: Research focused on the health care of operating crews, support personnel, and passengers of air and space vehicles. Includes instruction in special conditions of physical and psychological stress, emergency medical procedures, adaptive systems and artificial environments. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This project addresses the pressing need for computational infrastructure to support large-scale linguistic analysis of under-documented Southeast Asian languages, with a focus on the Malayo-Polynesian and Tibeto-Burman families. Many languages in this region are critically endangered and exhibit complex phonological, morphological, and syntactic features that remain poorly understood due to limited resources for systematic study. The research aims to reconstruct historical sound changes, model dialectal variation, and analyze syntactic structures across these languages using computational methods that require significant processing power. Key tasks include training transformer-based neural models on sparse textual corpora, performing acoustic analysis of field recordings to map phonetic shifts, and running Bayesian phylogenetic algorithms to infer language relationships. These methods demand high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the volume of multimodal data (over 10,000 hours of speech and 2 million lexical items), the need for parallel processing in comparative analyses, and the computational intensity of deep learning approaches optimized for low-resource scenarios. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of annotated speech/text corpora for 15 endangered languages, probabilistic models of sound change trajectories, and a computational framework for syntactic typology in head-marking languages. The results will advance theoretical understanding of language diversification in Southeast Asia while providing practical tools for communities engaged in revitalization efforts. By enabling resource-intensive analyses previously inaccessible to field linguists, this project bridges a critical gap between traditional philological methods and modern computational linguistics, with implications for preserving linguistic diversity and decolonizing language technology infrastructures.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the modern languages spoken in mainland Southeast Asia and the Indonesian and Philippines Archipelagoes, including, but not limited to, members of the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian language families.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of identifying and mitigating reading difficulties in K–12 students through the development of a computational framework to analyze complex, high-dimensional datasets of literacy assessments, student interactions, and demographic variables. Current diagnostic methods for reading challenges often rely on manual, time-intensive evaluations, limiting scalability and real-time adaptability. This research proposes a machine learning approach to model the relationships between linguistic patterns, cognitive processing metrics, and instructional outcomes, enabling dynamic prediction of individual student needs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train and validate neural networks on multimodal data—including text, audio recordings of oral reading fluency, and eye-tracking metrics—while preserving the temporal and contextual nuances of literacy development. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to parse syntactic and semantic features in student-generated texts, coupled with clustering algorithms to identify subtypes of reading difficulties (e.g., dyslexia, comprehension deficits). Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate the efficacy of targeted interventions under diverse classroom conditions. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to manage iterative model training across terabytes of anonymized student records, ensuring computational scalability. Outcomes will include an open-access diagnostic tool that assists reading teachers in prioritizing interventions and personalizing lesson plans. By quantifying how specific instructional strategies correlate with literacy gains across learner profiles, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in reading education. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable rapid prototyping of models, sensitivity analyses of pedagogical variables, and secure large-scale data integration—capabilities otherwise unfeasible with standard institutional resources. Results will directly inform teacher training programs, emphasizing data-driven decision-making in literacy instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose reading difficulties and to teach reading programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing personalized support strategies for individuals with developmental disabilities. Current approaches to designing care plans in developmental services rely heavily on manual assessment and iterative adjustments, which can delay effective interventions and strain limited resources. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data—including behavioral logs, health records, caregiver observations, and environmental factors—to generate dynamic, adaptive models that predict individual responses to specific support interventions. By synthesizing data from psychology, sociology, and behavioral analysis, the project addresses a gap in computational tools tailored to non-clinical, community-based care settings. The computational approach employs agent-based modeling to simulate individual behaviors and interactions within diverse scenarios, coupled with machine learning techniques to identify patterns in longitudinal outcomes. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to account for high-dimensional variables (e.g., sensory sensitivities, communication styles, and social determinants of health) and for enabling real-time parameter adjustments during model training. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for simulating intervention efficacy, which could reduce trial-and-error periods in care planning and improve resource allocation for community organizations. Additionally, the project aims to uncover latent relationships between environmental factors and behavioral outcomes, offering novel insights for developmental services training programs. By bridging computational social science with applied disability support, this work advances an emerging interdisciplinary niche, demonstrating how HPC can address complex, human-centered challenges beyond traditional science and engineering domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply practical knowledge and skills to support individuals with a variety of physical, mental or developmental disabilities in a family or community setting. Includes instruction in health care, basic nutrition, pharmacology, nursing, autism, mental health, psychology, sociology, behavioral analysis, communication, intervention, counseling and community services, and developmental services, such as literacy and life skills training.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and optimize the effectiveness of adaptive learning systems for teaching French as a second language (FSL). A critical challenge in FSL education lies in personalizing instruction to address diverse learner needs, particularly in grammar acquisition and phonetic training, where individual error patterns and language transfer effects vary widely. Current adaptive systems often rely on static rule-based models, limiting their responsiveness to dynamic learner behaviors. To address this, we propose a machine learning approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal learner data—including written responses, speech recordings, and interaction logs—from a longitudinal corpus of 15,000+ FSL students across proficiency levels. The project will train transformer-based models to predict error types and recommend targeted interventions, using parallelized hyperparameter optimization to refine model architectures. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom-scale interactions to evaluate how adaptive tools impact group learning dynamics. The computational workload necessitates large-scale GPU clusters for neural network training (est. 8,000 GPU-hours) and high-memory nodes for processing audio datasets through speech recognition pipelines. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating personalized French grammar exercises and pronunciation feedback, validated through collaboration with FSL instructors. This work aims to establish computationally informed best practices for embedding adaptive technologies in teacher training programs, directly supporting educators in designing differentiated instruction strategies while maintaining pedagogical agency. By bridging computational linguistics with language teaching praxis, the project will provide novel insights into scalable methods for addressing heterogeneity in FSL classrooms.
cip_title: Teaching French as a Second or Foreign Language
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching French to students who are not proficient in French or who do not speak, read, or write French, and prepares individuals to serve as teachers and administrators.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance evidence-based policymaking in public administration by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model large-scale social service delivery systems under dynamic socioeconomic stressors. The research addresses a critical gap in public sector planning: the inability of conventional analytical tools to simulate complex interactions between policy interventions, demographic shifts, and resource constraints at metropolitan-scale resolutions. Using anonymized administrative records from municipal health and housing agencies, combined with census-derived demographic projections, we will develop a GPU-accelerated agent-based model to simulate household-level access to social services under multiple policy scenarios. The computational framework will integrate machine learning classifiers trained on historical service utilization patterns with discrete-event simulations of public health outreach workflows. Key challenges requiring HPC resources include managing heterogeneous data streams across 10+ million agent entities, optimizing parallelized policy outcome calculations, and conducting Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses across 50+ parameterized scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for evaluating trade-offs between centralized versus decentralized service delivery models, particularly in regions experiencing rapid population displacement due to climate migration. By enabling real-time simulation of multi-agency coordination during fiscal austerity periods, this work aims to provide municipal administrators with quantitative frameworks for maintaining service equity amid budgetary uncertainty. The resulting computational models and open-source simulation toolkit will be disseminated through public sector innovation networks, contributing methodological advances to the emerging field of computational public administration.
cip_definition: Any program in public administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between social network structures and demographic behaviors using large-scale computational simulations. The research problem centers on understanding how evolving social ties—such as kinship, friendship, and professional connections—influence population-level outcomes like migration patterns, fertility decisions, and household formation. Traditional survey-based methods struggle to capture the recursive feedback between individual agency and structural constraints at scale, particularly across heterogeneous populations. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) that simulates life-course decisions within dynamic, multi-layered social networks. The model will integrate demographic microdata, longitudinal social tie metrics, and empirically derived behavioral rules to explore emergent phenomena under varying policy and environmental scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational demands of simulating millions of interacting agents across decadal time horizons, while maintaining granular detail in network evolution and decision pathways. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallel processing for network topology updates, implementing adaptive sampling techniques for rare demographic events, and validating model outputs against census and panel study benchmarks. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how localized network disruptions (e.g., workforce automation, climate migration) propagate through social systems to alter demographic trajectories. The results will advance theoretical frameworks in computational sociology while providing actionable evidence for policymakers addressing population aging and spatial inequality. By open-sourcing the optimized ABM framework, this work will also create a reusable resource for studying complex social systems across disciplines.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sociology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance digital humanities research centered on the revitalization and preservation of Indigenous languages and cultural narratives within U.S. and Canadian Native communities. Despite growing efforts to document endangered languages, many existing archives remain fragmented, under-analyzed, or inaccessible to the communities they represent. This research addresses the critical gap in computational tools capable of processing complex, non-linear Indigenous oral histories and multilingual datasets while adhering to tribal data sovereignty protocols. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for low-resource languages and dialectal variations, alongside geospatial analysis of oral tradition narratives tied to ancestral landscapes. Computational workflows will integrate community-generated metadata and ethical access frameworks co-designed with tribal partners. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on distributed linguistic corpora, conducting large-scale pattern recognition in audio-visual archives, and simulating interactive 3D environments for cultural heritage education. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for Indigenous language reclamation initiatives, a federated database architecture respecting tribal data governance, and multimodal digital repositories that align with Native epistemologies. By centering computational methods on Indigenous knowledge systems, this work aims to redefine best practices in collaborative digital stewardship while providing scalable infrastructure for Native-led cultural preservation. The research directly supports academic-community partnerships in Native American Studies, offering methodological innovations at the intersection of computational linguistics, cultural geography, and decolonial digital humanities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the American Indian, Aleut, Inuit, Hawaiian and other native peoples of the Americas from earliest times until the present, with particular emphasis on U.S. and Canadian populations and their problems but including reference to Caribbean and Latin American native peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational linguistic research on under-resourced Uralic languages, with a focus on the documentation, structural analysis, and digital preservation of Karelian and Eastern Sami dialects. Despite their cultural significance, these languages lack robust computational tools for morphological parsing, syntactic modeling, and corpus analysis, hindering both scholarly research and community-led revitalization efforts. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational challenges posed by these languages’ complex agglutinative morphologies, dialectal variation, and limited digitized text resources. To address this, we propose developing neural sequence-to-sequence models for morphological segmentation and part-of-speech tagging, optimized for low-resource scenarios through transfer learning from related Uralic languages like Finnish and Estonian. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based architectures on distributed GPU clusters, process multimodal data (historical texts, transcribed oral narratives), and run large-scale comparative simulations across dialect continua. Computational workflows will integrate probabilistic finite-state transducers for rule-based morphological analysis with deep learning approaches to capture irregular patterns. Expected outcomes include open-source NLP pipelines tailored to Karelian and Sami, a harmonized diachronic corpus spanning 19th–21st century sources, and quantitative models of morphological convergence in contact zones. These resources will advance theoretical understanding of Uralic language evolution while supporting practical applications in language education technology and automated preservation workflows for endangered varieties. The requested HPC allocation is essential given the iterative nature of hyperparameter tuning for low-resource models, the computational intensity of processing under-annotated textual data, and the need for parallelized comparative analyses across multiple language subsystems.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Uralic languages, including, but not limited to, Finnish, Estonian, Karelian, and Sami. Includes instruction in philology; oral and written literatures; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex optimization challenges in golf course operations and sustainable grounds management. The core problem lies in balancing ecological sustainability, playability standards, and economic efficiency, which involves interdependent variables such as microclimate dynamics, soil-plant-water interactions, pest behavior models, and resource allocation logistics. Current industry practices rely on generalized heuristics or fragmented datasets, limiting precision in predicting outcomes of maintenance strategies or environmental stressors. To overcome these limitations, this project will develop a computational framework integrating geospatial analytics, agent-based modeling, and machine learning to simulate turfgrass ecosystems under diverse operational scenarios. Key objectives include parameterizing multi-scale models of grass health (incorporating hybrid grass cultivars, soil microbiology, and irrigation patterns) and optimizing mowing schedules, fertilizer application, and water usage through reinforcement learning algorithms. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-resolution sensor data from IoT-enabled grounds equipment, historical weather databases, and 3D topographic scans of golf course layouts. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for disease outbreak mitigation, dynamic irrigation protocols responsive to hyperlocal weather shifts, and decision-support systems for minimizing chemical inputs without compromising turf quality. By advancing computational methodologies tailored to golf course ecosystems, this work aims to establish scalable frameworks for environmentally conscious landscape management in recreational spaces, while contributing novel algorithms for spatiotemporal resource optimization in non-agricultural turf systems. The project’s computational demands necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and distributed memory architectures for large-scale Monte Carlo simulations evaluating long-term sustainability trade-offs.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Golf Course Operation and Grounds Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operation of golf courses. Includes instruction in turf grass science and management, golf course design and construction, grounds equipment and operation, pest control, and grounds management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for large-scale, interdisciplinary R&D programs, addressing a critical challenge in research management: balancing efficiency, innovation, and risk under dynamic constraints. While traditional project management tools excel in predictable environments, they often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between technical uncertainty, personnel expertise, and shifting organizational priorities inherent in complex R&D ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose an agent-based modeling approach combined with multi-objective optimization to simulate decision pathways across thousands of scenario permutations. The computational model will integrate historical R&D performance data, real-time project metrics, and probabilistic risk assessments to evaluate trade-offs between short-term deliverables and long-term innovation potential. Key variables include budget elasticity, team composition dynamics, and technology readiness levels across concurrent projects. By implementing parallelized genetic algorithms and Monte Carlo methods on HPC infrastructure, we aim to overcome computational bottlenecks in solving high-dimensional optimization problems that exceed the capabilities of conventional systems. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies the impact of resource allocation choices on program-wide KPIs, validated through case studies from pharmaceutical development and clean energy innovation partnerships. This work will contribute novel methodologies to the emerging field of computational research management, providing actionable insights for aligning R&D investments with strategic organizational goals while maintaining adaptive capacity. The requested computing resources are essential for achieving the necessary scale and temporal resolution to model enterprise-level R&D portfolios, with potential applications extending to government research agencies and cross-sector innovation consortia.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage projects, programs and organizations involving basic and applied research, or specialized technology applications, in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in all aspects of business management applied to the leadership and control of scientific, clinical, engineering and social scientific enterprises; the management of related operational, security and logistical issues; and technical competence in one or more research disciplines.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for enhancing the protection of cultural and archaeological sites from illicit activities such as looting, vandalism, and unauthorized excavation. Despite advances in remote sensing and site monitoring, law enforcement and heritage professionals lack robust computational tools to dynamically assess site vulnerability, simulate threat scenarios, and prioritize resource allocation across large, geographically dispersed regions. The project addresses this gap by integrating geospatial data, historical crime patterns, environmental variables, and real-time sensor inputs into a machine learning-driven platform capable of forecasting risks to cultural resources. Computational workflows will process multispectral satellite imagery, LiDAR datasets, and anonymized crime reports to train spatial-temporal models that identify high-risk zones and optimize patrol routes. Agent-based modeling will simulate looting networks and site intrusion dynamics under varying enforcement strategies, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will mine textual records from antiquities markets and dark web forums to detect emerging trafficking trends. The HPC environment is critical for handling the scale and complexity of these heterogeneous datasets, enabling parallelized simulations and rapid retraining of deep learning architectures as new data streams become available. Expected outcomes include an open-source risk assessment toolkit for cultural resource managers, validated predictive metrics for site vulnerability, and evidence-based protocols for deploying surveillance technologies in resource-constrained contexts. By bridging computational criminology and heritage conservation, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for proactive cultural resource protection, ultimately reducing response times to threats and preserving irreplaceable archaeological assets for future generations.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement principles and techniques to the protection of cultural resources and the investigation of related crimes. Includes instruction in cultural resources law, archaeological standards of value, site damage assessment, evidence collection, surveillance techniques, investigative techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in veterinary toxicology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the molecular interactions and systemic effects of synthetic and natural toxins across diverse animal species. Despite advancements in toxicological research, predicting species-specific responses to chemical exposures remains challenging due to the complexity of biological systems, interspecies metabolic variations, and the vast chemical space of emerging contaminants. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and often fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale mechanisms underlying adverse effects, particularly in reproductive, neurobehavioral, and genetic toxicology. To overcome these limitations, this project will employ computational toxicology methods, integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations. HPC resources will enable large-scale MD simulations to resolve atomic-level interactions between toxins and biological targets (e.g., ion channels, cytochrome P450 enzymes) across veterinary-relevant species. Concurrently, ML models trained on heterogeneous datasets—including toxin databases, genomic profiles, and clinical case reports—will predict species-specific toxicokinetic and toxicodynamic outcomes. PBPK models will simulate systemic toxin distribution and organ-specific effects under varied exposure scenarios. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro and historical clinical data from veterinary toxicology cases. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for identifying high-risk toxins, elucidating mechanisms of interspecies susceptibility, and informing evidence-based treatments for acute and chronic poisonings in domestic and wildlife species. This work will directly enhance clinical decision-making in veterinary medicine while contributing open-access models and datasets to advance translational toxicology research. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational demands of multi-omics integration, large parameter-space explorations, and real-time simulations of complex biological networks.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical application of research on the nature and extent of adverse effects of synthetic and naturally occurring chemical substances on animals. May included related research in chemical mechanisms and the specialties of reproductive, developmental, genetic, forensic, inhalation and neurobehavioral toxicology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content in the global arts and entertainment industries. As generative AI tools rapidly transform creative sectors, unresolved questions about copyright ownership, attribution, liability, and ethical compliance have created systemic uncertainty for stakeholders. Traditional legal research methods struggle to map the transnational, cross-industry impacts of these technologies due to the sheer volume of case law, licensing agreements, and policy drafts emerging from diverse jurisdictions. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis algorithms to process multilingual legal documents, contractual templates, and regulatory proposals from 50+ jurisdictions, identifying patterns in legislative approaches and liability allocation. Custom machine learning models will simulate hypothetical disputes across scenarios such as AI-remixed music catalogs, synthetic actor performances, and algorithmically generated visual art, assessing how existing intellectual property doctrines might adapt to novel creative workflows. By integrating legal text corpora with datasets tracking real-world AI adoption rates in entertainment sectors, the computational framework will quantify gaps between policy development and industry practices. Anticipated outcomes include a dynamic visualization platform for policymakers to test regulatory interventions and a risk-assessment toolkit for creative professionals navigating AI integration. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational legal analytics with arts industry needs, offering empirically grounded insights to stabilize an increasingly fragmented governance landscape while preserving creative autonomy in the algorithmic age. The scale of data processing and complexity of multi-agent simulations necessitate HPC capabilities to achieve legally rigorous, actionable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting the sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, and media industries.

abstract: Aging civil infrastructure systems face increasing stress from climate change, population growth, and evolving usage patterns, yet conventional modeling approaches struggle to capture multi-physics interactions at regional scales. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to assess infrastructure resilience by integrating structural mechanics, geospatial dynamics, and climate projection data. The research will focus on transportation networks and critical water management systems, simulating cascading failures under extreme weather events such as compound flooding and heatwaves. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multi-scale interactions, from localized material degradation in concrete bridges to system-wide traffic flow disruptions during floods. The computational approach combines finite element analysis for component-level stress modeling, agent-based simulations for population mobility patterns, and graph theory to evaluate network redundancy. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate probabilistic risk assessments under thousands of climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework capable of identifying vulnerable infrastructure corridors and quantifying the cost-benefit ratios of adaptive retrofits. This work will directly inform regional resilience plans by prioritizing interventions that maximize service continuity during disasters. The computational tools developed will be shared via open-source platforms to enable replication in other jurisdictions, advancing the civil engineering community’s capacity to address infrastructure challenges in an era of rapid environmental change. By leveraging parallelized simulations across millions of CPU core-hours, this project addresses critical gaps in scalable infrastructure analytics that cannot feasibly be resolved with institutional computing resources alone.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in civil engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze the systemic impacts of digital caregiving tools on intergenerational family dynamics and workforce participation patterns—a critical yet understudied intersection in Work and Family Studies. While emerging technologies increasingly mediate care coordination for aging populations, their effects on familial role negotiation, resource allocation, and vocational decision-making remain poorly quantified. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to process multimodal datasets encompassing time-use surveys, biometric monitoring streams, and employment records across three generational cohorts. A novel machine learning pipeline will be developed to detect latent patterns in caregiving burden redistribution following technology adoption, combining transformer-based natural language processing of qualitative family communication logs with graph neural networks modeling household resource flows. Concurrently, discrete-event simulations will model longitudinal outcomes of different digital tool deployment strategies under varying economic constraints. The computational intensity stems from processing petabyte-scale lifelogging data from participant cohorts while maintaining temporal synchronization across heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include predictive models quantifying technology-mediated caregiving impacts on career trajectory disruptions, a taxonomy of high-risk household configurations vulnerable to digital intervention failures, and evidence-based design principles for workforce development programs addressing tech-augmented care work. By establishing computational social science methodologies within family resource management research, this project aims to transform vocational training paradigms while providing policymakers with quantitative tools to evaluate equity implications of emerging care technologies.
cip_definition: An introductory program that focuses on family and consumer science concepts and principles at the basic and vocational levels, and the various potential career paths open to interested students. Includes instruction in career, community, and family connections; family and family/consumer resources; human development; interpersonal relationships; nutrition and wellness; parenting; and career possibilities in various related areas.

abstract: Critical care management in adult and gerontology populations faces significant challenges due to the heterogeneity of conditions such as sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and multi-organ failure, which require rapid, personalized interventions. Current predictive models for outcomes and treatment responses in critically ill patients often lack the granularity to account for complex interactions between aging-related physiological decline, comorbidities, and dynamic clinical variables. This project proposes to develop an advanced computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-omics data, real-time physiological monitoring, and electronic health records (EHRs) for precision risk stratification and therapeutic optimization. The research will employ machine learning algorithms, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, to analyze high-dimensional datasets from 5,000+ ICU patients across 15 institutions. Key computational tasks include federated learning to preserve data privacy, time-series analysis of vital sign trends, and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify aging-specific biomarkers of critical illness progression. HPC resources are essential for training models on large-scale datasets, simulating virtual patient cohorts to test intervention scenarios, and optimizing hyperparameters in computationally intensive workflows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for 72-hour mortality, renal injury, and ventilator liberation success, validated against prospective ICU data. The project will also generate open-source tools for real-time clinical decision support, enabling dynamic recalibration of treatment protocols based on evolving patient states. By elucidating mechanisms linking gerontological factors to critical care outcomes, this work aims to reduce ICU length of stay, minimize adverse events in vulnerable populations, and establish a scalable infrastructure for data-driven critical care research.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Critical Care

abstract: The increasing complexity of forensic evidence—particularly trace chemical mixtures in toxicology, controlled substance analysis, and explosive residue characterization—demands advanced computational tools to resolve ambiguities in analytical data. Current laboratory techniques, such as gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), often produce overlapping spectral signatures in multi-component samples, complicating accurate identification and quantification. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing machine learning (ML) models and quantum chemistry simulations to enhance the interpretation of forensic chemical data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train deep neural networks on large spectral libraries, optimize molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of analyte-matrix interactions, and compute density functional theory (DFT)-based reference spectra for novel or modified compounds. The computational workflow will integrate experimental data from collaborating forensic laboratories to validate models against real-world casework samples, including synthetic opioids, pyrolysis byproducts, and environmental interferents. By coupling ML-driven pattern recognition with atomistic simulations, this work aims to improve the resolution of co-eluting chromatographic peaks, predict degradation pathways of evidentiary materials, and reduce false positives/negatives in toxicological screening. Outcomes will include open-source software tools for forensic analysts, optimized protocols for spectral deconvolution, and a curated database of simulated spectra for emerging substances not yet represented in commercial libraries. This research directly supports the forensic chemistry community’s need for robust, interpretable computational methods to address evolving analytical demands, ultimately strengthening the reliability of evidence in criminal investigations and legal proceedings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical techniques and instrumentation to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence to aid in criminal investigations. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; biochemistry; forensic toxicology; instrumental analysis; crime scene processing; criminal investigation; forensic laboratory technology; and applicable law.

abstract: The increasing complexity of histopathological analyses, driven by high-resolution imaging and multi-omics integration, demands advanced computational tools to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. Current manual and semi-automated methods for tissue structure identification and disease correlation are time-intensive, prone to variability, and ill-equipped to handle the scale of modern datasets. This project proposes the development of a machine learning framework to automate the analysis of histopathological images and associated molecular data, enabling rapid, standardized detection of cellular abnormalities and their linkages to disease pathways. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on a curated dataset of 50,000 whole-slide images (WSIs) annotated with histological features and paired with transcriptomic profiles from public and institutional repositories. Computational workflows will include preprocessing pipelines for image normalization, artifact removal, and feature extraction, followed by multimodal integration of image data with RNA-seq datasets to identify spatially resolved biomarkers. The scale of WSIs (≥1 GB per image) and the complexity of 3D tissue reconstructions necessitate distributed computing for parallelized batch processing and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool for automated histologic classification, a validated set of computational biomarkers predictive of early-stage carcinomas, and a public repository of annotated training data. This work will directly address bottlenecks in diagnostic workflows while providing a scalable platform for correlating tissue morphology with molecular mechanisms. By integrating HPC-driven analytics into histotechnologist training pipelines, the project also aims to advance educational outcomes, equipping future professionals with skills to interpret AI-enhanced diagnostics. The resource request supports critical needs in storage (500 TB for raw/image data), GPU nodes for model training, and high-memory CPUs for multi-omics integration, enabling translational research at the intersection of computational pathology and precision medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, at the request of physicians, researchers, and laboratory scientists, to identify tissue structures and cell components and relate these findings to physiological functions and to the detection and diagnosis of diseases and other abnormalities. Includes instruction in medical chemistry, histochemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, medical informatics, applied mathematics, electron microscopy, instrumentation, quality control procedures, data recording and analysis, laboratory administration, medical terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The emergence and spread of infectious diseases in animal populations pose significant threats to global livestock industries, wildlife conservation, and public health. Current gaps in understanding transmission dynamics across heterogeneous environments and host species limit the efficacy of intervention strategies. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model multi-host pathogen spread, integrating ecological, epidemiological, and genomic data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based models simulating contact networks among domesticated animals, wildlife, and vectors across diverse landscapes. Machine learning algorithms will analyze terabyte-scale datasets from veterinary surveillance systems, climate sensors, and host-pathogen genomic sequences to identify critical drivers of spillover events. The computational pipeline will employ parallelized Bayesian inference methods to estimate transmission parameters and predict outbreak trajectories under various climate change scenarios. By coupling phylodynamic analyses with spatial modeling, this study will elucidate evolutionary adaptations in pathogens that enable cross-species jumps. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing complex simulations across millions of agent interactions, optimizing predictive models through iterative learning cycles, and handling the integration of multi-modal data streams at scale. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool for regional disease risk forecasting, genomic markers associated with increased zoonotic potential, and targeted vaccination strategies validated through in silico trials. This research will advance computational methodologies in veterinary epidemiology while providing actionable insights to mitigate economic losses in agriculture and reduce pandemic risks through proactive One Health interventions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Sciences/ Veterinary Clinical Sciences, General
cip_definition: An integrated program of study in one or more of the veterinary medical or clinical sciences or a program undifferentiated as to title.

abstract: Public works infrastructure systems face escalating challenges due to aging assets, climate disruptions, and dynamic population needs, requiring data-driven strategies to optimize maintenance and funding allocation. Current decision-making frameworks often rely on static models that inadequately capture the interdependencies between infrastructure performance, fiscal constraints, and socio-political priorities. This project seeks to develop an adaptive computational model to simulate long-term public works management scenarios under uncertainty, integrating demographic projections, budget volatility, and risk assessments of infrastructure failure. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the model will employ agent-based simulations to replicate stakeholder decision-making processes and Monte Carlo methods to evaluate probabilistic outcomes across multi-decadal timelines. Key parameters include labor resource availability, equity impacts of service delays, and trade-offs between preventive maintenance and emergency response budgets. The computational framework will process heterogeneous datasets spanning municipal financial records, geospatial infrastructure conditions, and climate vulnerability indices. By scaling analyses to regional levels, this approach aims to identify resilient allocation strategies that balance operational efficiency with ethical obligations to underserved communities. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool for municipal planners, validated through case studies in three U.S. cities experiencing distinct infrastructure pressures. The project will demonstrate how advanced computing can transform conventional public administration practices, enabling proactive governance that aligns technical, financial, and social dimensions of public works management. Results will inform curriculum updates in public administration programs, emphasizing computational literacy for future civic leaders.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design of next-generation composite materials with tailored mechanical and thermal properties for high-performance industrial applications, addressing critical gaps in predictive modeling of interfacial behavior between dissimilar material phases. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize composite architectures are time-intensive and costly, particularly when analyzing nanoscale interactions or multiphase systems under dynamic operational stresses. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), and finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate material behavior across atomic-to-macroscopic scales. The research will focus on metal-ceramic and polymer-graphene systems, examining interfacial bonding mechanisms, stress distribution under thermomechanical loads, and failure propagation patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational demands of large-scale MD simulations (>10^6 atoms), parameterized DFT calculations for interfacial energy landscapes, and iterative FEA optimizations of composite geometries. Expected outcomes include a validated open-access database of interfacial properties for common material pairs, predictive models for composite durability in extreme environments, and design guidelines for layered structures with enhanced fracture resistance. This work directly supports sustainable manufacturing goals by reducing trial-and-error prototyping cycles and enabling data-driven material selection for energy-efficient systems. The requested allocation will facilitate parallelized simulations across multiple length scales, significantly accelerating parameter space exploration compared to single-node computation. Results will be disseminated through collaborations with additive manufacturing laboratories to validate models against experimental benchmarks, fostering broader applications in automotive lightweighting and high-temperature industrial components. By bridging atomic-scale interactions to macroscopic performance metrics, this project aims to establish a computational toolkit for rapid development of advanced composites, addressing urgent industry needs for materials with higher strength-to-weight ratios and improved thermal stability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and materials science principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and related processes used in manufacturing in a wide variety of settings; the synthesis of new industrial materials, including marrying and bonding composites; analysis of materials requirements and specifications; and related problems of system design dependent on materials factors.

abstract: The design and optimization of orthotic and prosthetic devices require precise alignment with patient-specific biomechanical demands, yet current methods often rely on iterative physical prototyping and subjective clinical judgment, leading to prolonged development times and suboptimal functional outcomes. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for simulating, analyzing, and optimizing orthotic/prosthetic device performance across diverse patient populations. The research problem centers on the integration of multi-scale biomechanical modeling, patient-specific anatomical data, and advanced materials science to predict device efficacy under dynamic real-world conditions. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) to evaluate stress distribution and deformation in device materials, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on clinical gait analysis, diagnostic imaging (e.g., MRI, CT), and demographic data to predict patient-device interactions. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to account for anatomical variability, pathological gait patterns, and material properties, while reducing reliance on physical prototyping. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-source simulation platform capable of generating patient-specific device designs with quantifiable performance metrics, such as energy expenditure reduction, pressure distribution optimization, and durability predictions. This platform will also facilitate the exploration of novel materials and adaptive device architectures, including smart sensors or power-assisted components. By bridging computational engineering and clinical orthotics/prosthetics practice, this work aims to accelerate device personalization, improve functional outcomes for patients with limb loss or musculoskeletal impairments, and establish a foundation for data-driven clinical decision-making. The scalability of HPC-driven models will further support research into population-level trends, informing future standards for device design and postoperative care protocols.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity.
