By creating open-access computational tools and datasets, the project will provide a foundation for innovation in food engineering research and industry applications, bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical implementation in agricultural and food production systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the development and implementation of manufacturing, packaging, storage, and distribution technologies and processes for food products. Includes instruction in food engineering, food preservation and handling, food preparation, food packaging and display, food storage and shipment, and related equipment and facilities design, operation, and maintenance.

abstract: The development of effective and stable drug formulations requires a comprehensive understanding of molecular interactions, pharmacokinetics, and material properties under varying physiological conditions. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize drug delivery systems, particularly for complex formulations such as lipid nanoparticles or amorphous solid dispersions, are resource-intensive and limited in their ability to predict long-term stability or in vivo behavior. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of drug-polymer and drug-biomembrane interactions, enabling the rational design of next-generation formulations. The research will employ all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to study molecular self-assembly, phase separation, and diffusion kinetics in multicomponent drug delivery systems. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations will complement MD to quantify electronic interactions critical for predicting crystallization tendencies in amorphous formulations. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation-derived datasets to establish structure-property relationships and accelerate screening of excipient candidates. The computational workflow will integrate experimental validation using differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray scattering data from ongoing laboratory studies. By combining multiscale simulations with data-driven approaches, this work aims to identify formulation strategies that enhance drug solubility, stability, and targeted release profiles. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations across multiple thermodynamic conditions and polymer/excipient combinations, which are computationally prohibitive on local clusters. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for optimizing nanoparticle drug carriers and solid dispersions, directly addressing formulation challenges in poorly water-soluble therapeutics. This project will provide critical insights into the molecular drivers of drug formulation performance while establishing computational tools that reduce development timelines and costs for academic and industrial researchers in pharmaceutical sciences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the basic sciences that underlie drugs and drug therapy and that prepares individuals for further study and/or careers in pharmaceutical science and research, pharmaceutical administration and sales, biotechnology, drug manufacturing, regulatory affairs, and related fields. Includes instruction in mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, statistics, pharmaceutics, pharmacology and toxicology, dosage formulation, manufacturing, quality assurance, and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing adaptive urban infrastructure systems using high-fidelity digital twin simulations. The problem centers on the dynamic interplay between built environments, human activity patterns, and microclimate conditions—a complex multi-physics challenge requiring real-time optimization of energy distribution, thermal regulation, and crowd-flow management in dense urban centers. Current approaches lack the temporal resolution and cross-domain coupling necessary to address emergent phenomena such as heat island intensification during extreme weather events or congestion-driven energy demand spikes. The computational approach integrates graph-based representations of infrastructure networks with physics-informed neural operators to enable multi-scale simulations. A novel hybrid architecture will combine finite element models for building-scale thermal transport, agent-based crowd dynamics, and reinforcement learning controllers for distributed energy allocation. The framework will leverage heterogeneous computing architectures through domain decomposition strategies optimized for irregular urban geometries, with asynchronous coupling of fluid dynamics (ANSYS Fluent) and discrete event simulations (MATSim) via custom middleware. Key innovations include the development of neural surrogate models for rapid thermal prediction and a fault-tolerant task scheduler for distributed optimization under uncertainty. The project requests HPC resources to validate the framework through city-scale case studies comparing traditional static infrastructure management with adaptive control strategies. Expected outcomes include quantifiable reductions in peak energy demand (projected 15-20% through predictive load balancing) and improved thermal comfort metrics during heat waves. This work aims to establish a new paradigm for responsive urban infrastructure that bridges computational engineering, architectural science, and climate resilience planning, with open-source tools to support smart city development. Success metrics will evaluate both computational performance (scaling efficiency on >10^4 cores) and domain-specific impacts using IoT sensor validation datasets from partner municipalities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to engineering practice and research. Includes instruction in engineering and science fundamentals, advanced mathematics, algorithms, computer languages, and software engineering design.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic data in clinical diagnostics presents a critical challenge in accurately interpreting genetic variants linked to human diseases. Current approaches in Laboratory Genetics and Genomics often rely on fragmented analyses of cytogenetic (e.g., chromosomal aberrations) and molecular genetic (e.g., single nucleotide variants, copy number variations) data, limiting the ability to resolve ambiguous findings or uncover multilayered genomic contributions to phenotypes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing integrative computational frameworks to harmonize multi-omics datasets, enhance variant prioritization, and model structural genomic interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale whole-genome sequencing data, perform three-dimensional chromatin structure simulations, and train machine learning models capable of identifying pathogenic variants within heterogeneous clinical cohorts. Key computational tasks include parallelized alignment of sequencing reads, graph-based algorithms for structural variant detection, and dynamic modeling of chromatin conformation changes associated with chromosomal abnormalities. Machine learning workflows will integrate clinical metadata, functional genomic annotations, and population-scale datasets to improve the classification of variants of uncertain significance. The anticipated outcomes include novel bioinformatics pipelines for joint analysis of cytogenetic and molecular findings, validated predictive models for variant pathogenicity, and open-access tools to correlate chromatin architecture disruptions with developmental genetic disorders. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will enhance diagnostic accuracy for rare genetic diseases, reduce interpretation turnaround times, and provide a scalable framework for resolving complex cases where conventional analyses yield inconclusive results. The tools and datasets generated will be disseminated to the clinical genetics community, fostering precision medicine advancements and informing guidelines for integrative genomic reporting.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a dynamic, agent-based simulation framework for analyzing the systemic impacts of decentralized tax compliance strategies in multinational corporate networks. The research addresses a critical gap in computational tax policy analysis: current models often fail to capture the cascading effects of tax optimization behaviors across interconnected entities, especially in evolving regulatory environments such as the OECD’s global minimum tax framework. By integrating heterogeneous corporate decision-making algorithms with real-world tax treaty networks, supply chain interdependencies, and cross-border capital flow dynamics, the project aims to simulate how localized tax strategies propagate risk and inefficiency at scale. Computational methods will combine graph theory to map multi-jurisdictional relationships, Monte Carlo simulations to model uncertainty in audit outcomes, and reinforcement learning to emulate adaptive corporate behaviors. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling simulations to encompass over 10,000 entity networks—a requirement for statistically robust analysis of rare but high-impact compliance cascades. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible taxonomy of systemic vulnerabilities arising from common tax optimization patterns, (2) predictive metrics for policymakers to assess the stability of hybrid tax regimes, and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating regulatory interventions. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational economics, network science, and operational tax theory, offering novel methodologies to address emergent challenges in global tax coordination. The results will provide actionable insights for both corporate risk management and the design of next-generation international tax compliance architectures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide tax advice and management services to individuals and corporations. Includes instruction in tax law and regulations, tax record systems, individual and corporate income taxation, tax planning, partnerships and fiduciary relationships, estates and trusts, property depreciation, capital gains and losses, dispositions, transfers, liquidity, valuation, and applications to specific tax problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Bengali linguistics and literary analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable large-scale text processing, dialect classification, and syntactic pattern recognition. Despite Bengali’s status as the seventh most spoken language globally, computational tools for its analysis remain underdeveloped compared to Indo-European languages with more extensive digital infrastructure. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, annotated corpora and models capable of capturing regional dialect variations, historical linguistic shifts, and stylistic features in Bengali literature. To address this, we propose building a multi-dialectal corpus of Bengali texts spanning pre-modern to contemporary eras, integrating philological annotations, and training machine learning models to analyze linguistic evolution and literary trends. Computational methods will include neural network-based dialect classifiers, transformer models for syntactic parsing, and geospatial mapping of phonetic variations using distributed computing frameworks. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of textual data, optimize parallelized training of language models, and run iterative simulations for dialect boundary identification. Expected outcomes include (1) the first open-access, computationally annotated corpus of Bengali texts with metadata on regional and historical context, (2) quantitative frameworks for tracking syntactic simplification in modern literary Bengali, and (3) dialect classification models with applications in education, speech technology, and cultural preservation. By bridging computational linguistics with Bengali philology, this work will empower interdisciplinary scholarship while developing replicable methods for under-resourced languages. The requested resources will directly support data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale text rendering for visual analytics, enabling breakthroughs in both theoretical linguistics and applied language technologies for Bengali.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bengali language (Bangla) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The integration of synaptic plasticity mechanisms across molecular, cellular, and network levels remains a critical challenge in understanding neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. While experimental studies have identified key proteins and signaling pathways involved in synaptic modulation, dynamic interactions within intact neural circuits—particularly under pathological conditions—are difficult to capture experimentally due to temporal and spatial resolution limitations. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models that link molecular-scale dynamics of synaptic proteins (e.g., NMDA receptor trafficking, calcium-dependent kinase activation) with large-scale neural network activity associated with learning and memory. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate these multilevel interactions, which span time scales from microseconds (molecular conformational changes) to hours (network-level plasticity) and spatial scales from nanometers (synaptic clefts) to millimeters (cortical regions). We will employ molecular dynamics simulations to model protein interactions, coupled with mean-field and spiking neural network models to predict emergent circuit behaviors. These simulations will be validated against in vitro electrophysiological datasets and in vivo calcium imaging from rodent models of synaptic dysfunction. The computational framework will be parallelized using GPU-optimized libraries (OpenMM, NEURON) and scaled across nodes to manage memory-intensive tasks. Expected outcomes include identifying critical molecular "switches" that dysregulate network stability in disorders such as schizophrenia and Alzheimer’s disease, as well as predicting compensatory stimulation patterns to restore synaptic efficacy. By bridging molecular mechanisms with systems-level dysfunction, this work will provide a computational platform for testing novel therapeutic strategies targeting synaptic resilience, while reducing reliance on exploratory animal experiments. The requested HPC allocation will enable simulations encompassing >10^6 neurons with biologically realistic connectivity, exceeding the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interdisciplinary scientific study of the molecular, structural, physiologic, cognitive, and behavioral aspects of the brain and nervous system. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, molecular and biochemical bases of information processing, behavioral neuroscience, biology of neuropsychiatric disorders, and applications to the clinical sciences and biomedical engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing strategic decision-making frameworks for multi-domain military operations in dynamic, uncertain environments. Traditional models for resource allocation and contingency planning often struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between human, logistical, and environmental factors inherent in modern conflict scenarios. To bridge this gap, the proposed research will develop a high-fidelity computational platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate hybrid threat landscapes, integrating adversarial behavior patterns, supply chain vulnerabilities, and real-time intelligence constraints. The core computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with Monte Carlo methods to stochastically evaluate decision pathways under variable threat intensities and resource limitations. Machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning, will be applied to iteratively refine adaptive response protocols, enabling the system to propose context-sensitive resource reallocation strategies. The simulations will incorporate anonymized historical operational data alongside synthetic datasets representing emerging asymmetric threats, ensuring robustness against both known and novel scenarios. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve near-real-time analysis of large-scale scenarios, a critical requirement for operational relevance. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for evaluating mission-critical trade-offs in joint force deployments, validated against expert-derived performance metrics. This work will contribute to the advancement of decision-support systems in military applied sciences, offering a scalable framework to enhance preparedness for complex, evolving threats while minimizing risks associated with resource misallocation. The resulting methodologies will be disseminated through scenario-based training modules, providing actionable insights for strategic planners operating in multi-stakeholder environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The extraction and processing of mineral resources involve complex geological, operational, and environmental challenges that demand advanced computational modeling to optimize efficiency and safety. Current methods for predicting ore body characteristics, optimizing extraction workflows, and mitigating operational risks rely on simplified assumptions that fail to capture the dynamic interactions between geological heterogeneity, equipment performance, and real-time environmental conditions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate high-resolution, multi-physics simulations of mineral extraction processes. These simulations will integrate 3D geologic data from site surveys, sensor-derived operational parameters, and machine learning algorithms to model ore fragmentation, material transport, and waste management in a spatially explicit framework. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized finite element analysis and discrete element modeling to simulate stress distributions in rock masses, fluid dynamics in processing systems, and the impact of equipment configurations on productivity. Additionally, reinforcement learning techniques will be applied to iteratively optimize extraction sequences under varying geologic constraints. The outcomes will provide actionable insights into minimizing energy consumption, reducing environmental disruption, and enhancing worker safety through predictive hazard modeling. By enabling real-time scenario testing at scale, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in mining operations, directly addressing the program’s focus on integrating engineering principles with modern technical solutions. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational intensity of coupled simulations, which require terabytes of input data and thousands of parallelized iterations to achieve statistically robust results. Successful implementation will establish a scalable framework for sustainable mineral resource management, with potential applications in training the next generation of mining technologists.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Livestock diseases pose significant threats to agricultural productivity, food security, and public health, yet predicting outbreaks and optimizing interventions remains challenging due to the complex interplay of host genetics, pathogen evolution, and environmental drivers. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model disease transmission dynamics in heterogeneous animal populations and evaluate mitigation strategies under diverse agricultural scenarios. We will integrate genomic data from livestock and pathogens, geospatial environmental variables, and animal movement patterns to parameterize agent-based epidemiological models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate millions of agent interactions across multi-scale networks, perform sensitivity analyses on intervention parameters (e.g., vaccination schedules, biosecurity protocols), and apply machine learning to identify genomic markers associated with disease resilience in cattle. A parallelized workflow will be implemented to optimize model calibration against historical outbreak data from swine influenza and bovine respiratory disease complexes. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will probe interactions between novel antiviral compounds and evolving viral proteomes to inform targeted drug design. The computational scale required—including ensemble modeling across parameter spaces, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in 10,000+ animal cohorts, and nanosecond-resolution molecular simulations—exceeds the capacity of local institutional clusters. Outcomes will yield predictive tools for regional disease risk forecasting, genetic selection guidelines to enhance herd immunity, and prioritized therapeutic candidates for experimental validation. By bridging population-scale epidemiology and molecular-scale pathogen biology, this work aims to advance adaptive management strategies for livestock health, directly supporting agricultural sustainability and mitigating economic losses from emergent zoonotic threats.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the study, prevention, and control of diseases in agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in environmental science, pharmacology, animal population studies, genetics, animal physiology and diet, disease prevention, treatment methodologies, and laboratory and testing procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize mineral extraction processes while enhancing safety and environmental sustainability in mining operations. Traditional methods for mine planning and mineral processing often rely on simplified geological assumptions and static datasets, leading to inefficiencies in resource recovery and heightened risks of operational hazards. To address these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating dynamic 3D geological modeling, real-time sensor data assimilation, and machine learning (ML) to improve decision-making in subsurface resource allocation. The research will focus on simulating multiphase fluid flow through fractured rock formations, a critical challenge in leaching and in-situ recovery operations, using parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). These simulations will incorporate heterogeneous geological data from borehole logs, seismic surveys, and hyperspectral imaging, scaled across distributed-memory systems to resolve centimeter-scale features across kilometer-scale mining domains. Concurrently, an ML pipeline will analyze historical and real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled monitoring systems to predict equipment failures and hazardous gas accumulations. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter optimization for extraction protocols through ensemble simulations, reducing computational bottlenecks in scenario testing. Expected outcomes include predictive models for ore grade variability, validated strategies for minimizing groundwater contamination, and adaptive safety thresholds for automated monitoring systems. By coupling large-scale geomechanical simulations with operational analytics, this work aims to establish a computational toolkit for reducing energy consumption in mineral processing by 15–20% while maintaining compliance with evolving environmental regulations. The proposed resource allocation will directly support the training of mining technicians in HPC-aided mine design through case studies on GPU-accelerated visualization platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Rural populations face significant health disparities, including limited access to healthcare resources and higher burdens of chronic and infectious diseases. These disparities are compounded by geographic isolation, socioeconomic factors, and heterogeneous population distributions, which complicate the design of effective public health interventions. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing computational models to predict disease spread, optimize resource allocation, and evaluate intervention strategies tailored to rural settings. A critical barrier to progress is the lack of scalable, high-resolution models capable of integrating sparse, multi-source health data with geographic, demographic, and environmental variables. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based simulations, machine learning pipelines, and geospatial analyses. The agent-based framework will simulate disease transmission dynamics across synthetic rural populations, incorporating mobility patterns, healthcare access thresholds, and social determinants of health. Machine learning models will be trained on regional electronic health records, census data, and environmental sensor datasets to identify risk clusters and forecast outbreak trajectories. Geospatial tools will map healthcare deserts and model the impact of mobile clinics or telemedicine expansion. These computational workflows require parallel processing capabilities to manage large parameter spaces, stochastic simulations, and real-time data integration. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into cost-effective intervention strategies for rural regions, validated models for policymakers, and open-source tools to support adaptive public health planning. The project’s computational demands—including multi-terabyte datasets, millions of parallelized simulations, and iterative model calibration—necessitate HPC infrastructure for storage, processing speed, and scalability. By bridging clinical research with computational innovation, this work aims to reduce rural health inequities and establish a framework for data-driven decision-making in resource-limited settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rural Health

abstract: Neuroimaging plays a pivotal role in diagnosing and managing complex neurological disorders, yet current clinical workflows face challenges in analyzing multi-modal neuroimaging data at scale. This project seeks to develop an automated computational framework for integrating high-resolution structural MRI, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and functional MRI (fMRI) to identify subtle biomarkers of neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases. A critical bottleneck lies in processing terabyte-scale datasets with spatially and temporally resolved features while accounting for inter-patient variability and artifact correction. Traditional single-node computing resources are insufficient for these tasks, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) capabilities. The proposed work will deploy a hybrid deep learning architecture combining 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for volumetric feature extraction and graph neural networks (GNNs) to model connectivity patterns across imaging modalities. This approach will be optimized for distributed training across GPU clusters to handle memory-intensive operations on whole-brain imaging data. Key computational challenges include implementing scalable data augmentation pipelines for heterogeneous neuroimaging formats, developing domain-specific loss functions to prioritize clinically relevant pathological features, and enabling real-time inference for translational validation studies. The HPC environment will facilitate large-scale hyperparameter optimization and robustness testing across multi-institutional datasets from Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and traumatic brain injury cohorts. Successful implementation is expected to yield three outcomes: (1) a validated open-source toolkit for reproducible analysis of multi-modal neuroradiology data, (2) quantitative biomarkers predictive of disease progression in understudied patient subgroups, and (3) computational evidence guiding optimized MRI protocol selection for specific clinical scenarios. This work directly addresses neuroradiology’s growing need for precision imaging analytics while establishing infrastructure for future studies on AI-assisted diagnosis and treatment monitoring in neurologic care.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the brain, spine, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, and head and neck in adults and children.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time optimization of graphic and printing production workflows through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Traditional methods for calibrating equipment, managing color consistency, and minimizing material waste rely on manual adjustments and static protocols, leading to suboptimal resource utilization and quality variability in high-volume commercial printing. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning (ML)-driven framework to dynamically predict and adjust equipment parameters under variable production conditions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on multi-modal datasets, including spectral color measurements, substrate behavior under environmental stressors, and equipment sensor telemetry from industrial digital presses. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model ink dispersion and drying processes across diverse materials, while Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes of parameter combinations. The integration of these models aims to create a real-time decision support system that reduces trial runs, material waste, and energy consumption. Expected outcomes include a scalable optimization toolkit for graphic production workflows, validated through partnerships with regional printing facilities. This work will advance computational applications in non-traditional HPC domains by demonstrating how high-fidelity simulations and ML can address tactile challenges in graphic communications. Results will be disseminated through trade journals and academic conferences at the intersection of computational design and industrial printing, offering a template for data-driven innovation in vocational technical education programs. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the project’s large-scale simulations and iterative model training, which exceed the capacity of local institutional infrastructure.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: Dental implant success hinges on the complex interplay between biomechanical forces, osseointegration dynamics, and patient-specific anatomical constraints. Despite advances in implantology, unpredictable bone resorption and peri-implantitis remain significant causes of long-term failure, with conventional clinical methods offering limited predictive capacity for individual biomechanical responses. This project proposes a computational framework to model multiscale interactions between dental implants and host tissues under dynamic physiological loads, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with agent-based modeling (ABM) of cellular osseointegration processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve time-dependent micromechanical stresses across implant interfaces while simulating osteoblast-osteoclast activity at cellular resolution across clinically relevant timescales (6–24 months). Patient-specific mandibular anatomy derived from cone-beam CT scans will inform FEA meshes, with material properties calibrated via nanoindentation data from cadaveric bone samples. The ABM component will incorporate mechanobiological rules governing bone remodeling, informed by gene expression profiles from single-cell RNA sequencing of peri-implant tissues in a murine model. Parallelized simulations will assess how variables including implant thread geometry, alloy surface treatments, and occlusal loading patterns influence strain distributions and biological integration. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying failure-prone implant configurations, optimization guidelines for prosthodontic load distribution, and a novel metric quantifying "biomechanical compatibility" for patient-specific treatment planning. By bridging continuum mechanics with cellular-scale biology, this work aims to establish computational workflows for next-generation personalized implantology, reducing revision surgeries and improving functional outcomes. The scale of 3D transient simulations (>10^8 elements) and coupled ABM-FEA parameter optimization necessitates HPC capabilities exceeding local cluster capacities, particularly for GPU-accelerated solver routines and large parameter space exploration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.

abstract: Medical imaging generates complex, high-dimensional datasets that challenge conventional computing resources, particularly in large-scale radiology research. Current limitations in processing speed, algorithmic scalability, and data integration hinder the development of advanced tools for quantitative image analysis, which are critical for improving diagnostic accuracy, prognostic modeling, and personalized therapeutic strategies. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these barriers by enabling the deployment of deep learning architectures and multi-modal image fusion techniques tailored to radiological data. The research will focus on optimizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models for automated segmentation of pathological features in volumetric MRI and CT datasets, which require intensive GPU memory and parallelized processing. Additionally, we will develop computational pipelines to integrate imaging data with clinical metadata using distributed storage systems and containerized workflows, ensuring scalability and reproducibility. Key challenges include managing terabyte-scale datasets across heterogeneous modalities, reducing training times for 3D neural networks, and implementing federated learning frameworks to enable multi-institutional collaboration while preserving data privacy. The anticipated outcomes include validated models for early detection of neurodegenerative diseases and tumor progression, open-source tools for efficient radiomic feature extraction, and a scalable infrastructure for real-time image analysis in clinical research. By addressing computational bottlenecks, this work aims to accelerate the translation of imaging biomarkers into practice, ultimately enhancing precision diagnostics and expanding the role of artificial intelligence in radiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on Radiology

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize school-level administrative decision-making processes in K-7 educational settings, with a focus on resource allocation, emergency response planning, and student outcome forecasting. School administrators face complex challenges in balancing finite resources—such as staffing, budgets, and facility usage—with dynamic variables including fluctuating enrollment, safety protocols, and evolving pedagogical needs. Traditional decision-support tools often lack the capacity to simulate multi-variable scenarios or account for longitudinal data on student development. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate school operations under diverse constraints. These models will integrate anonymized demographic data, historical budget records, and facility blueprints from partner school districts, alongside synthetically generated datasets representing hypothetical scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify patterns in administrative efficiency and predict the downstream effects of policy decisions on student performance metrics. A key innovation involves coupling discrete-event simulations of daily school operations with geospatial analyses to optimize emergency evacuation routes and resource deployment during crisis events. The computational intensity of running thousands of parallel simulations across multi-year timescales necessitates access to HPC infrastructure with robust GPU acceleration and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support toolkit for school leaders, empirically validated strategies for equitable resource distribution, and evidence-based protocols for crisis management. By bridging computational modeling with practical administrative needs, this work aims to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and equity in elementary and middle school settings while maintaining strict adherence to ethical standards for data privacy and educational equity.
cip_title: Elementary and Middle School Administration/ Principalship
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the elementary and middle school (K-7) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of elementary and middle schools. Includes instruction in elementary and/or middle school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, childhood and pre-adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The development of advanced polymeric materials for extreme-environment applications—such as aerospace, deep-sea exploration, or next-gen energy systems—requires a fundamental understanding of how multiscale polymer dynamics respond to coupled stressors (e.g., high radiation, pressure, and thermal cycling). Current experimental methods struggle to isolate these interacting effects at relevant spatiotemporal scales, while existing computational models often oversimplify hierarchical material behavior, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to bridge this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate the nonlinear, nonequilibrium dynamics of engineered polymers under multifactorial stress conditions. Using a hybrid computational framework, we integrate coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) to capture mesoscale chain reorganization, finite element analysis (FEA) for continuum-level mechanical response, and machine learning (ML)-accelerated parameterization to link atomistic-scale chemical degradation pathways (via quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics simulations) to macroscopic failure modes. The HPC environment is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of concurrent stressors across disparate time scales (nanoseconds to hours) and spatial resolutions (Ångströms to micrometers). Key objectives include identifying design rules for radiation-resistant elastomers in orbital infrastructure and optimizing self-healing hydrogels for high-pressure submersible seals. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source simulation toolkit for multifactorial polymer degradation prediction, (2) mechanistic insights into stressor coupling effects on viscoelastic energy dissipation, and (3) accelerated discovery of three polymer formulations with tailored extreme-environment performance. By unifying materials chemistry, continuum mechanics, and data science approaches, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for computationally driven polymer design, reducing reliance on iterative physical prototyping. The requested resources will enable large-scale parametric studies (>10^6 core-hours) to resolve rare events and stochastic interactions central to polymer failure, directly supporting national priorities in advanced materials resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the structure and processing of polymeric materials and how these relate to properties and performance. Combines instruction in both Polymer science and engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, real-time flight simulation and training optimization platform to address the growing complexity of pilot training demands in evolving aviation environments. Current flight instruction programs often rely on static simulations and generalized training scenarios, which inadequately prepare pilots for dynamic, high-stakes situations such as extreme weather, system failures, or congested airspace. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create adaptive, data-driven training modules that integrate real-world flight data, probabilistic risk modeling, and aerodynamic simulations at scale. The computational approach will involve three phases: (1) generating synthetic flight scenarios using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of aircraft performance under diverse atmospheric and mechanical stress conditions, (2) implementing machine learning algorithms to analyze historical incident data and predict optimal training interventions, and (3) deploying agent-based modeling to simulate multi-aircraft interactions in complex airspace configurations. These components will be unified through a cloud-accessible interface capable of rendering real-time physics-based simulations to flight instructors and trainees. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated computing for CFD resolution and distributed computing frameworks for large-scale scenario generation. Expected outcomes include a validated training platform that reduces skill acquisition time by 15-20% in FAA assessment benchmarks, along with open-source datasets correlating simulation parameters with pilot competency metrics. By enabling instructors to dynamically adjust training rigor based on real-time performance analytics, this work aims to elevate safety standards in commercial aviation while providing a scalable model for integrating HPC resources into technical vocational education. The resulting infrastructure will also serve as a testbed for evaluating emerging aviation technologies, including electric propulsion systems and AI-assisted air traffic control protocols.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the training of pilots or navigators, to prepare them to fly and/or navigate commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue aircraft, and fixed or rotary wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications and navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to administer the FAA commercial air crew examinations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of transnational missionary networks between 1850 and 1950 through computational analysis of multilingual archival materials, including correspondence, field reports, and ethnographic records. Missionary activities during this period involved complex interactions between religious, medical, and colonial institutions, yet the scale and heterogeneity of these records have hindered systematic analysis of their global networks, knowledge exchanges, and unintended societal impacts. The research addresses this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to process and analyze over 500,000 digitized pages from missionary archives, spanning 15 languages and six continents. Computational methods will integrate transformer-based language models fine-tuned for historical texts, multilingual named entity recognition to map institutional and interpersonal connections, and network analysis to trace the evolution of resource flows and ideological diffusion. A key innovation involves simulating counterfactual scenarios of missionary mobility and resource allocation using agent-based modeling, informed by historical climate, disease, and geopolitical datasets. By leveraging GPU-accelerated NLP and distributed computing for large-scale network inference, this approach will reconstruct how missionary strategies adapted to local crises, colonial policies, and interdenominational competition. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking missionary activities to longitudinal demographic and cultural change indicators, as well as methodological frameworks for analyzing contested historical networks in low-resource languages. The project aims to provide new insights into the role of missionary institutions as early transnational actors while critically examining the computational challenges of studying marginalized voices and asymmetrical power dynamics in archival corpora. Results will inform interdisciplinary scholarship on religion, globalization, and cross-cultural encounter, with implications for heritage digitization and ethical archival practices.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of religious outreach, social service and proselytization, and that prepares individuals for mission vocations. Includes instruction in theology, evangelism, preaching, medical and social mission work, missionary education, missionary aviation, emergency services, legal and political aspects of working in other countries, and preparation for ordination as missionaries.

abstract: The accurate prediction of high-impact weather events, such as extreme precipitation and tropical cyclones, remains a critical challenge in meteorology due to the complex interactions between atmospheric dynamics and fine-scale processes. Current numerical weather prediction (NWP) models struggle to resolve convective systems and boundary layer interactions at resolutions coarser than 1 km, limiting their ability to capture localized extremes. This project proposes to advance the understanding and forecasting of mesoscale atmospheric phenomena by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct kilometer-scale simulations over multi-seasonal periods. Using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model coupled with a novel machine learning-based parameterization framework, we will dynamically downscale global climate model outputs to 500-meter resolution across tropical and midlatitude regions. The simulations will integrate ensemble-based data assimilation techniques to quantify uncertainties in initial conditions and model physics. Computational demands include parallelized model runs across thousands of CPU cores, real-time processing of multi-terabyte observational datasets (e.g., radar, satellite), and storage for petabyte-scale output. The proposed work will address two interconnected questions: (1) How do microphysical processes and land-atmosphere feedbacks modulate the intensity of extreme precipitation in warming climates? (2) Can machine learning-driven turbulence closure schemes improve the representation of convective initiation in NWP systems? Outcomes will include publicly accessible datasets of high-resolution climate projections, new metrics for evaluating model skill in capturing extreme event statistics, and optimized parameterizations for operational forecasting centers. This research directly supports climate resilience planning by reducing uncertainties in projections of storm frequency and intensity under anthropogenic forcing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the prediction of atmospheric motion and climate change. Includes instruction in general circulation patterns, weather phenomena, atmospheric predictability, parameterization, numerical and statistical analysis, large- and mesoscale phenomena, kinematic structures, precipitation processes, and forecasting techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of exotic nuclear structures and reaction dynamics in neutron-rich nuclei using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Despite their critical role in astrophysical processes like neutron star mergers and r-process nucleosynthesis, the properties of nuclei near the neutron drip line remain poorly characterized due to experimental inaccessibility and theoretical challenges in modeling many-body quantum systems with strong nucleon-nucleon correlations. The research will employ ab initio nuclear theory methods, combining chiral effective field theory (χEFT) nucleon-nucleon interactions with advanced many-body techniques such as the in-medium similarity renormalization group (IM-SRG) and coupled-cluster theory. These methods will be extended to systematically investigate nuclei with extreme neutron-to-proton ratios, including their ground-state energies, excited states, and decay modes. Large-scale configuration interaction (CI) calculations using the shell model will complement these approaches to study collective excitations and clustering phenomena. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated frameworks and hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization to manage the exponential scaling of model spaces in multi-nucleon systems. Key objectives include predicting β-decay half-lives for r-process nuclei, quantifying three-body force contributions to nuclear saturation, and benchmarking theoretical uncertainties against existing experimental data from rare isotope facilities. The requested HPC resources will enable the use of high-fidelity nuclear potentials and exact diagonalization techniques for systems with mass numbers A > 50, which are computationally prohibitive on smaller clusters. Outcomes will provide critical nuclear input parameters for astrophysical simulations, constrain models of neutron-rich matter, and guide future experiments at facilities such as FRIB. This work will also establish optimized computational protocols for next-generation nuclear structure studies, benefiting the broader low-energy nuclear physics community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of atomic nuclei. Includes instruction in nuclear reaction theory, quantum mechanics, energy conservation, nuclear fission and fusion, strong and weak forces, nuclear modeling, nuclear decay, nucleon scattering, pairing, photon and electron reactions, the physics of nuclear effects, statistical methods, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a large-scale computational framework to analyze stylistic evolution in English literary texts across distinct historical periods, with a focus on identifying patterns of linguistic innovation and intertextual influence. While traditional literary scholarship has relied on manual close reading, the sheer volume of extant texts—from Early Modern pamphlets to 20th-century novels—necessitates scalable computational methods to detect subtle, systemic shifts in language use and narrative structure. The research will employ natural language processing techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on period-specific corpora, to quantify syntactic complexity, semantic field distributions, and metaphor density across a curated dataset of 30,000 primary texts. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: parallel processing of heterogeneous archival formats (TEI XML, OCR-scanned texts), training domain-specific word embeddings using dynamic temporal contexts, and implementing graph neural networks to map citation networks and thematic diffusion. By correlating linguistic features with sociocultural metadata, the analysis will test hypotheses about how major events like the Industrial Revolution or suffrage movements influenced literary expression. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated texts, visualization tools for diachronic stylistic trends, and statistical models quantifying the relationship between lexical innovation and canon formation. This work will advance methodological debates in digital humanities by demonstrating how computational approaches can complement qualitative interpretation, while providing new empirical evidence for longstanding theoretical claims about literary periodization. The resource demands—particularly GPU-intensive model training and large-scale graph traversal—require dedicated HPC allocation to ensure feasible processing times for terabyte-scale textual data.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the English language, including its history, structure and related communications skills; and the literature and culture of English-speaking peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in managing large-scale clinical datasets, which are increasingly complex due to the volume, heterogeneity, and sensitivity of modern electronic health records (EHRs). Existing systems often struggle to efficiently validate, secure, and analyze these datasets while adhering to evolving regulatory standards. The research aims to develop a scalable computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enhance the accuracy, security, and utility of health information systems. Key objectives include automating error detection in unstructured clinical narratives, optimizing real-time encryption for distributed health databases, and enabling predictive modeling of patient outcomes from multi-source data. Computational methods will integrate machine learning (e.g., transformer-based natural language processing for clinical text validation) with blockchain-inspired decentralized architectures for auditability and access control. Parallelized algorithms will be designed to process terabyte-scale datasets across HPC nodes, while privacy-preserving techniques, such as federated learning and homomorphic encryption, will ensure compliance with HIPAA and GDPR. The project will validate the framework using synthetic EHRs mirroring diverse healthcare demographics and real-world data from partner institutions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for anomaly detection in medical records, a modular platform for secure health data aggregation, and benchmarks for computational efficiency in large-scale clinical analytics. By advancing the technical infrastructure for health information management, this work will directly support clinical decision-making, reduce administrative burdens, and strengthen compliance with data quality and security standards. The requested HPC resources are essential to train deep learning models on heterogeneous medical data, simulate network-wide security attacks for system hardening, and scale validation workflows to national-level datasets within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern vehicle systems necessitates advanced diagnostic and maintenance strategies to ensure operational reliability and cost efficiency. Traditional approaches often rely on reactive or schedule-based interventions, which can lead to unnecessary downtime, inflated costs, and suboptimal resource allocation. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to enable predictive maintenance modeling and real-time diagnostics for vehicular systems. By leveraging large-scale datasets—including sensor telemetry, historical repair records, and environmental operating conditions—the research will employ machine learning algorithms, such as recurrent neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees, to identify failure precursors and optimize maintenance intervals. Concurrently, finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics simulations will model mechanical wear, thermal stress, and fluid interactions in critical components like engines, transmissions, and braking systems. The integration of these computational methods requires HPC resources to manage parallelized simulation workflows, train complex models on heterogeneous data streams, and validate predictions against experimental benchmarks. Expected outcomes include a scalable predictive maintenance toolkit capable of reducing unplanned downtime by 20–30% in fleet operations, a repository of annotated failure mode datasets for educational use, and optimized resource allocation protocols for repair facilities. This work will directly enhance technician training programs by providing data-driven case studies and simulation environments, while advancing the integration of computational methodologies into vehicular maintenance research. The project bridges the gap between conventional repair practices and cutting-edge computational analytics, fostering innovation in a field critical to transportation sustainability and workforce development.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of vehicles and mobile equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the mechanisms underlying vascular remodeling in hypertension, a key driver of cardiovascular morbidity, using advanced computational modeling to bridge gaps in understanding how mechanical forces and cellular responses drive pathological changes in arterial structure. Hypertension-induced vascular remodeling involves complex interactions between hemodynamic stress, endothelial dysfunction, and smooth muscle cell proliferation, yet the precise spatiotemporal dynamics of these processes remain poorly characterized. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating fluid-structure interaction models of arterial hemodynamics with agent-based simulations of cellular behavior in the vascular wall. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the coupled biomechanical and biochemical processes across spatial scales (µm to cm) and time scales (milliseconds to weeks). The computational workflow will leverage finite element methods to simulate blood flow and wall stress in patient-derived arterial geometries, coupled with stochastic models of intracellular signaling pathways (e.g., mechanotransduction, oxidative stress) that regulate smooth muscle cell hyperplasia and extracellular matrix deposition. Machine learning techniques will be applied to parameterize models using experimental data from vascular histology and in vitro mechanical testing. By simulating disease progression under varied hemodynamic and pharmacological conditions, this work aims to identify critical thresholds in wall stress and signaling cascades that trigger maladaptive remodeling. Expected outcomes include predictive models of vascular adaptation specific to hypertensive pathophysiology, which will inform targeted therapies to mitigate arterial stiffening and prevent end-organ damage. The proposed HPC allocation will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and validation against clinical datasets, requiring parallelized computations across >10,000 CPU cores to achieve biologically relevant resolutions. This work aligns with cardiovascular science priorities by providing mechanistic insights into a prevalent disease process while advancing computational physiology methodologies.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and functioning of the heart, vascular system, and blood in animals and human beings and the disorders and diseases associated with the cardiovascular system. Includes instruction in cardiovascular physiology, blood physiology, vasculature, vascular metabolism, neural control of cardiovascular function, microvascular permeability and membrane transport, cardiac contraction mechanisms, homeostasis, and applications to topics such as arteriosclerosis, heart disease, diabetes, vascular remodeling, transplantation, transfusion, and pacemakers and artificial organs.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing forklift operational safety and efficiency in dynamic industrial environments through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Despite standardized training protocols, forklift-related workplace accidents remain a persistent issue, often linked to unpredictable variables such as load instability, operator decision-making under stress, and real-time environmental interactions. Traditional training methods and static risk assessments struggle to replicate the complexity of these scenarios. To bridge this gap, we propose the development of a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework powered by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The model will integrate physics-based dynamics of forklift movement, probabilistic risk matrices for load handling, and machine learning-driven operator behavior patterns trained on anonymized industrial incident datasets. Computational workflows will simulate thousands of concurrent operational scenarios, varying parameters such as warehouse layout complexity, operator fatigue levels, and emergency response protocols. Sensitivity analyses will identify high-risk factor combinations, while reinforcement learning subroutines will iteratively optimize safety-critical decision pathways. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing real-time sensor data streams from partner industrial sites and scaling multiphysics simulations that account for fluid-structure interactions in liquid-bearing loads and granular material shifts. Expected outcomes include a predictive risk assessment toolkit capable of generating site-specific safety recommendations and adaptive training modules that respond to operator performance metrics. By quantifying previously intractable risk variables through large-scale parallel computation, this research aims to reduce workplace accidents by 15-25% in participating facilities while improving throughput efficiency. The resulting open-source simulation platform will serve as a transformative resource for both forklift certification programs and industrial safety engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate forklifts in a variety of work environments. Includes instruction in accident prevention, forklift operation, materials handling, and worksite safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling second language acquisition (SLA) processes in adult learners of English as a Second Language (ESL) through advanced computational methods. Current SLA research lacks granular, data-driven models that account for the interplay of sociolinguistic, cognitive, and instructional variables across diverse learner populations. We propose developing a machine learning framework to analyze longitudinal datasets encompassing learner speech samples, writing outputs, demographic profiles, and instructional intervention records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multimodal data from 10,000+ learners across 15 institutional partners, including audio recordings (20,000+ hours), written compositions (150,000+ texts), and behavioral engagement metrics. The computational approach combines transformer-based architectures for natural language processing with graph neural networks to model dynamic learning trajectories, supplemented by agent-based simulations of classroom interactions. Key challenges include managing heterogeneous data formats at scale, implementing real-time feedback systems for error pattern detection, and optimizing ensemble models for cross-linguistic transfer predictions. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive models identifying critical thresholds in grammatical competency development, (2) evidence-based frameworks for personalizing instructional content sequencing, and (3) open-source tools for analyzing morphosyntactic complexity in learner language. This research will advance computational linguistics methodologies in SLA while directly informing the design of adaptive learning systems for credit-bearing ESL programs. The requested HPC allocation will enable GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and validation against longitudinal proficiency assessments, tasks infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the pharmacological understanding of Ayurvedic herbal formulations through multi-omics integration and systems biology approaches. Despite Ayurveda’s extensive use of complex polyherbal formulations for disease management, the molecular mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly characterized due to the combinatorial interactions of phytochemicals, multi-target physiology, and nonlinear dose-response relationships. To address this gap, we propose a computational workflow combining molecular docking, dynamic simulation, and machine learning to model interactions between Ayurvedic phytochemicals and human protein targets implicated in metabolic, inflammatory, and neurodegenerative disorders. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will be performed to assess binding stability and allosteric effects of prioritized phytochemicals (e.g., curcumin, withaferin A, bacosides) against targets such as NF-κB, COX-2, and acetylcholinesterase. Network pharmacology models will integrate transcriptomic and metabolomic datasets from clinical studies to map formulation-induced pathway modulations. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of structural biology data, running ensemble simulations across parameter spaces, and training graph neural networks to predict herb-herb synergies. Expected outcomes include mechanistic validation of classical Ayurvedic synergism (samyoga) principles, identification of bioactive lead compounds, and predictive models for optimizing formulation ratios. This work will establish a computational framework for bridging Ayurvedic empirical knowledge with modern systems biology, offering insights into personalized Ayurvedic therapeutics while informing ethical integration into global health paradigms. The requested resources will directly support 15,000+ GPU hours for deep learning tasks and 200,000+ CPU-core hours for molecular simulations, enabling unprecedented scale in Ayurvedic pharmacoinformatics research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop adaptive, real-time procedural content generation (PCG) systems for interactive game environments by integrating player behavior modeling with high-fidelity physics simulations. While procedural techniques are widely used to automate game asset creation, existing methods often lack dynamic responsiveness to individual player interactions, resulting in environments that feel static or disconnected from gameplay. This research addresses the challenge of balancing computational efficiency with real-time adaptability, particularly in complex 3D environments where player actions influence terrain deformation, object interactions, and non-player character (NPC) behaviors. The core computational methodology combines deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for player preference prediction with parallelized fluid dynamics and granular material simulations. High-performance computing resources will enable the simultaneous execution of multiple physics engines alongside DRL training cycles, allowing iterative optimization of environment generation algorithms under varying player interaction scenarios. Key technical hurdles include minimizing latency between player input and environmental response while maintaining visual fidelity, as well as ensuring scalable synchronization between discrete simulation modules. The project will validate outcomes through automated playtesting frameworks that measure emergent player engagement metrics across generated environments. Successful implementation could establish new paradigms for responsive PCG systems, reducing development costs for open-world games while enhancing player immersion through environments that evolve meaningfully in response to individual playstyles. This work bridges gaps between computational creativity, human-computer interaction, and real-time physics simulation—advancing game design capabilities through tightly integrated applications of machine learning and high-performance computational modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of design and computer programming to the development of computer games. Includes training in character and story development, computer programming, computer graphics, game design, game physics, human-computer interaction, human-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the escalating complexity of regulatory ecosystems in compliance law, where traditional legal analysis struggles to keep pace with dynamic, high-volume, and interdependent policy frameworks. The research focuses on developing computational models to automate the identification of latent compliance risks, predict regulatory conflicts, and simulate the operational impacts of emerging legislation. By integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques, we aim to process multilingual legal texts, supranational regulatory databases, and real-time legislative updates at scale. Key computational challenges include training domain-specific transformer models on heterogeneous legal corpora, constructing dynamic knowledge graphs to map cross-jurisdictional regulatory overlaps, and running agent-based simulations to stress-test organizational compliance protocols under hypothetical policy shifts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized processing of terabyte-scale legal datasets, iterative fine-tuning of deep learning architectures, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing risk propagation in multi-stakeholder compliance networks. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for compliance risk prediction, a framework for quantifying regulatory ambiguity in textual sources, and evidence-based recommendations for harmonizing conflicting compliance standards. This work bridges computational law and operational risk management, offering novel methodologies to enhance decision-making in corporate governance, regulatory technology (RegTech), and cross-border policy analysis. By formalizing the interaction between legal semantics and systemic risk, the project aims to advance computational literacy in compliance practice while establishing benchmarks for scalable, ethics-aware regulatory analytics.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in compliance, ethics, internal monitoring, regulatory affairs, and related areas.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex legal, economic, and spatial dynamics inherent in large-scale urban land development disputes. The study addresses a critical gap in real estate and land development law: the lack of predictive frameworks to assess how judicial rulings, regulatory interventions, and multi-stakeholder negotiations interact to shape urban growth patterns and property rights outcomes. By integrating computational legal analytics with geospatial and economic datasets, the project aims to simulate decision-making processes across heterogeneous jurisdictions, with a focus on scenarios involving conflicting claims to land use, environmental compliance, and infrastructure financing. The computational approach employs agent-based modeling to represent stakeholders (e.g., developers, municipalities, community groups) within dynamic legal environments, coupled with natural language processing to analyze precedent from appellate court decisions and administrative rulings. High-performance resources are required to manage the combinatorial complexity of legal constraints, simulate long-term development trajectories under alternative regulatory regimes, and process multi-terabyte geospatial datasets detailing parcel-level ownership histories and zoning modifications. Expected outcomes include a scalable simulation platform capable of identifying latent legal risks in proposed development projects, quantifying the economic impacts of statutory ambiguities, and forecasting litigation probabilities based on evolving case law trends. This work will provide policymakers and legal practitioners with evidence-based tools to balance private development interests with public welfare objectives, while advancing computational methods for legal-institutional analysis in non-science domains. The project’s interdisciplinary integration of legal theory, urban economics, and computational social science represents a novel application of HPC resources to challenges at the intersection of jurisprudence and sustainable land governance.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms that underpin complex cognitive processes, such as working memory and decision-making, requires analyzing large-scale brain networks with high spatiotemporal resolution. Current limitations in computational power restrict the ability to model dynamic interactions across distributed neural systems or integrate multimodal neuroimaging data (e.g., fMRI, EEG) at the scale necessary to capture population-level activity. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational neuroscience framework that bridges neural dynamics with cognitive function. The research will employ whole-brain biophysical models to simulate resting-state and task-evoked activity, informed by subject-specific structural connectivity derived from diffusion tensor imaging. These simulations will be optimized using Bayesian inference to fit empirical fMRI and electrophysiological datasets, enabling the exploration of parameter spaces governing excitatory-inhibitory balance and long-range coupling.
