Concurrently, machine learning pipelines will be developed to decode cognitive states from high-density EEG recordings, leveraging HPC capabilities for feature extraction and real-time pattern classification. The integration of modeling and empirical data aims to identify critical network hubs and oscillatory mechanisms that sustain cognitive operations. Expected outcomes include predictive models of cognitive load in healthy aging and mechanistic insights into network destabilization in conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease. By enabling the analysis of terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations, this project will establish an open-access resource for testing hypotheses about large-scale brain organization. The results will advance foundational knowledge in cognitive neuroscience and provide a computational toolkit for translating basic research into clinical biomarkers of neurocognitive health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the neural mechanisms underlying cognition.

abstract: The project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the role of submesoscale ocean dynamics—processes occurring at scales of 1-10 km—in mediating vertical nutrient fluxes and phytoplankton productivity in oligotrophic regions. While these processes are hypothesized to significantly influence marine ecosystem resilience and carbon export, their transient nature and fine spatial resolution have made them challenging to observe or simulate accurately. This research proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run a series of nested ocean circulation-biogeochemistry models at unprecedented resolution (horizontal grid ≤ 500 m) across the subtropical Pacific. The computational framework will integrate the MIT General Circulation Model (MITgcm) with a biogeochemical module tracking multiple nutrient species and phytoplankton functional types, explicitly resolving submesoscale instabilities, fronts, and eddy-wind interactions. Simulations will be forced with reanalysis atmospheric data and validated against autonomous underwater vehicle transects and satellite-derived productivity metrics. The HPC demand arises from the need to concurrently handle ~20 million grid cells, adaptive time-stepping for numerical stability, and ensemble runs spanning interannual climate variability (El Niño/La Niña cycles). Anticipated outcomes include quantifying the contribution of submesoscale features to annual primary production budgets and identifying thresholds in wind-forcing regimes that enhance vertical nutrient supply. Results will directly inform the scalability of Earth system model parameterizations and provide mechanistic insights into how climate-driven changes in ocean stratification may alter productivity in nutrient-limited ecosystems. The generated datasets, comprising 500+ TB of 4D hydrodynamic and biogeochemical fields, will be curated for community reuse in model intercomparison studies. This work underscores the necessity of HPC resources to bridge observational limitations and advance predictive capacity for marine biogeochemical cycles under global change.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the ocean/marine sciences, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare delivery systems necessitates advanced tools to optimize nursing workforce allocation, improve patient outcomes, and reduce operational costs. Traditional nurse staffing models often rely on static ratios or historical trends, which fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating patient acuity, real-time nurse competency data, and evolving care protocols. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven decision support system to model adaptive staffing strategies for hospital units. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train and validate ensemble models integrating electronic health record (EHR) data, nurse-reported workload metrics, and institutional cost structures. The computational workflow includes natural language processing of clinical notes to infer unmeasured care demands, graph-based simulations of interprofessional team dynamics, and multi-objective optimization to balance safety, efficiency, and staff well-being. Key challenges requiring HPC capabilities include processing terabyte-scale EHR datasets spanning 10 hospital networks, parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations for staffing scenario testing, and maintaining model interpretability through explainable AI techniques. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for unit-level staffing adjustments and system-level workforce planning, with preliminary results demonstrating a 15-20% improvement over existing scheduling systems in synthetic test environments. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated deep learning and large-memory nodes for optimization tasks—necessitates dedicated computing infrastructure. This work will provide nurse administrators with evidence-based tools to navigate staffing challenges in acute care settings while advancing computational methods for healthcare operations research. Successful implementation could inform policy discussions on nurse-patient ratios and contribute to the development of national benchmarks for intelligent staffing systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to manage nursing personnel and services in hospitals and other health care delivery agencies. Includes instruction in principles of health care administration, resource and financial management, health care law and policy, medical personnel management, and managed care operations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between lipid bilayers and integral membrane proteins, a critical yet poorly understood aspect of cellular biochemistry. Membrane proteins, such as transporters and receptors, operate within heterogeneous lipid environments that modulate their structure, stability, and function. Traditional experimental techniques face limitations in resolving atomic-level conformational changes and lipid-protein interactions over biologically relevant timescales. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and free energy calculations to elucidate how lipid composition and bilayer properties influence the conformational landscape of a model ABC transporter. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to conduct multi-microsecond all-atom MD simulations of the transporter embedded in lipid bilayers of varying composition, capturing rare transitions and lipid interaction hotspots. Coarse-grained simulations will extend the spatial and temporal scales to assess mesoscale bilayer remodeling effects. Potential of mean force (PMF) calculations will quantify the thermodynamic impact of specific lipid species on transporter gating mechanisms. This approach will generate unprecedented insights into lipid-driven allostery and stability determinants, validated through collaboration with experimental partners using cryo-EM and fluorescence spectroscopy. The outcomes will advance fundamental understanding of membrane protein regulation, with implications for engineering synthetic lipid systems to enhance protein stability in industrial applications and inform therapeutic strategies targeting lipid-dependent dysfunction in metabolic disorders. The project’s scale necessitates HPC resources to manage >500,000 core-hours for sampling complex systems, iterative trajectory analysis, and enhanced sampling workflows, which cannot be supported by local institutional infrastructure.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_title: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Molecular Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biochemistry, biophysics and molecular biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of decision-making workflows in executive support roles by developing a computational framework to optimize dynamic scheduling, communication prioritization, and resource coordination in high-stakes business environments. Executive assistants increasingly manage multilayered operational ecosystems involving real-time data streams, conflicting stakeholder priorities, and rapidly evolving crisis scenarios. Traditional productivity tools lack the predictive capacity and computational power to model these interdependent variables at scale. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling simulations that map decision cascades across three core domains: 1) time-sensitive task orchestration under resource constraints, 2) sentiment-aware communication routing using natural language processing, and 3) probabilistic risk assessment for schedule optimization. Custom algorithms will integrate historical behavioral patterns with real-world uncertainty parameters to generate adaptive workflow templates. By processing terabyte-scale datasets of anonymized executive communication logs and calendar interactions, the models will identify critical path dependencies and bottleneck thresholds unique to C-suite support operations. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit capable of simulating 10,000+ concurrent scenario permutations in under three minutes—a 150x improvement over current single-threaded solutions. This research fills a critical gap in computational resource allocation strategies for strategic support roles, offering novel insights into human-AI collaboration frameworks while advancing methodological approaches to operational complexity analysis in business ecosystems. The results will establish quantitative benchmarks for executive support efficiency metrics and inform the development of next-generation assistive technologies for high-pressure administrative environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and/or personal secretaries for business executives and top management. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, public relations, scheduling and travel management, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, conference and meeting recording, report preparation, office equipment and procedures, office supervisory skills, and professional standards and legal requirements.

abstract: Dental implant failure due to biomechanical complications, such as stress shielding, occlusal overload, or micromotion-induced bone resorption, remains a critical challenge in implantology. While clinical studies provide empirical insights, they often lack the resolution to quantify dynamic biomechanical interactions between implants, bone, and soft tissues over long-term functional loading. This project proposes a computational biomechanics approach to model the multiscale mechanical behavior of bone-implant systems under physiological and pathological conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are requested to perform large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) simulations integrating patient-specific bone microstructure derived from clinical CT scans, anisotropic bone remodeling algorithms, and stochastic loading profiles mimicking masticatory forces. A hybrid computational pipeline will be developed, combining deep learning-based segmentation of clinical imaging data, GPU-accelerated FEA solvers for simulating bone strain distributions, and agent-based modeling of osteocyte mechanotransduction. The project will parameterize models using retrospective data from 500+ implant cases, then prospectively validate predictions against longitudinal radiomic and biomechanical measurements. Outcomes will establish predictive relationships between implant design variables (e.g., thread geometry, surface roughness), surgical placement parameters, and bone adaptation patterns. This resource-intensive approach directly addresses the limitations of current trial-and-error clinical practices by enabling virtual prototyping of patient-specific implant configurations. Successful completion will yield (1) an open-source computational framework for implant biomechanics optimization, (2) clinical guidelines for minimizing stress-shielding risks in osteoporotic patients, and (3) AI-derived design principles for next-generation implants that actively promote biomechanical osseointegration. The requested HPC capabilities are essential to achieve the required spatial resolution (≤10 µm mesh elements) and temporal scope (≥5 years of simulated functional loading) while accommodating the biological variability inherent to clinical populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the surgical and restorative aspects of implant dentistry.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing epigenetic editing for tissue-specific gene therapy using high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic chromatin interactions. While CRISPR-based gene editing has advanced therapeutic targeting, epigenetic modifiers—such as CRISPR-dCas9 systems—require precise spatiotemporal control to avoid off-target effects and ensure stable transcriptional modulation. Current experimental approaches struggle to predict how epigenetic editors interact with the 3D genome architecture of specific cell types, particularly in dynamic disease contexts like fibrosis or neurodegenerative disorders. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omic data (ATAC-seq, Hi-C, and single-cell RNA-seq) with molecular dynamics simulations to predict optimal epigenetic editing windows and delivery strategies. The HPC component will involve two phases: (1) large-scale parallelized modeling of chromatin conformational changes under editing perturbations using coarse-grained molecular dynamics, and (2) machine learning-driven optimization of guide RNA designs for cell-type specificity by training on epigenomic landscapes from diverse human tissues. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to process terabyte-scale chromatin interaction datasets, while the ML models will employ federated learning techniques to maintain data privacy across collaborating clinical partners. Expected outcomes include a predictive atlas of editable epigenetic loci for 12 high-priority therapeutic targets, validated in vitro using patient-derived iPSC models. This work will establish a pipeline for rational design of epigenetic therapies, reducing experimental trial-and-error cycles and accelerating translational workflows. By prioritizing computational exploration of off-target risks and tissue-specific efficacy, the project addresses a critical bottleneck in scalable, ethical gene therapy development. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated via a cloud-based platform to support reproducibility and community-driven refinement of epigenetic editing strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics to the therapeutic treatment of diseases and inherited abnormalities through the targeted modification of gene expression, and prepares individuals to administer genetic therapies. Includes instruction in medical genetics, genome analysis, pharmacology of gene transfer, viral vectors, nonviral therapeutic techniques, genetic screening, targeted gene delivery, vector production, safety and quality assurance, clinical trials management, and bioethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of managing chronic diseases in primary care requires advanced analytical tools to optimize clinical decision-making. Family Medicine research faces unique challenges due to heterogeneous patient populations, multimorbidity, and the need for personalized, context-sensitive interventions. This project aims to develop predictive models for chronic disease trajectories and treatment outcomes using high-dimensional electronic health record (EHR) data from diverse primary care settings. A critical barrier is the computational demand of integrating structured EHR data, unstructured clinical notes, and social determinants of health while preserving temporal relationships across longitudinal patient records. We propose a multi-stage computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges. First, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will process unstructured clinical text at scale, extracting latent features related to symptom evolution and treatment adherence. Second, graph neural networks will model patient-provider interaction patterns and comorbidity networks across 300,000+ patient records. Finally, transformer-based architectures will predict 5-year risks of diabetes complications, cardiovascular events, and polypharmacy-related hospitalizations, adjusting for regional practice variation. HPC resources are essential for training these models on multi-terabyte datasets, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized Bayesian search, and conducting sensitivity analyses through large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated risk stratification tools deployable in real-world primary care workflows, (2) insights into modifiable social factors influencing chronic disease outcomes, and (3) open-source computational frameworks for temporal modeling of primary care data. This work will directly inform the development of adaptive clinical decision support systems, potentially reducing preventable hospitalizations by 15-20% in participating health networks while advancing methodological standards for computational research in Family Medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on Family Medicine

abstract: This research project aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of biomechanical and microbiological interactions in endodontically treated teeth, addressing critical gaps in predicting treatment outcomes. Despite clinical advancements, failures due to structural fractures and persistent infections remain prevalent, often linked to incomplete understanding of stress distributions in restored teeth and biofilm resilience in complex root canal anatomies. Current experimental methods cannot fully capture the dynamic 3D interplay between restorative materials, dental morphology, and microbial communities. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate (1) biomechanical stress patterns under functional loads and (2) biofilm dynamics under varying antimicrobial conditions. Patient-specific 3D models of root canal systems, reconstructed from clinical micro-CT datasets, will form the basis for FEA simulations evaluating stress concentrations in dentin and restorations. Concurrently, ABM will simulate spatially resolved biofilm growth and treatment response using empirical data on bacterial metabolic networks and fluid dynamics. The computational scale—involving >10^6 finite elements for mechanical simulations and stochastic modeling of microbial populations across micrometer-scale geometries—requires distributed-memory parallelization and GPU acceleration available only through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk anatomical configurations for mechanical failure and biofilm retention, as well as optimized irrigation protocols. These results will directly inform clinical guidelines for cavity preparation, material selection, and antimicrobial delivery, ultimately improving treatment longevity. By establishing a novel computational platform linking biomechanics and microbiology in endodontics, this work will provide a foundation for data-driven treatment personalization, reducing retreatments and enhancing tooth preservation strategies in complex cases.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the morphology, physiology, and pathology of human dental pulp and periradicular tissues, and prepares dentists to diagnose and treat internal diseases and injuries of teeth. Includes instruction in theory and practice of endodontics; pulpal disease; relationship of endodontic conditions to other dental/oral health issues; endodontic operative technique; and patient care and management.

abstract: Forensic nursing practice requires the integration of complex biological, legal, and contextual data to support victim care and criminal investigations. However, current methods for analyzing forensic evidence—such as injury documentation, toxicology reports, and crime scene data—often rely on manual processes or siloed computational tools, limiting scalability and accuracy. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to analyze multimodal forensic datasets, including wound patterns, genomic data from sexual assault cases, and longitudinal health records. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) creating machine learning models to classify injury mechanisms and predict associated health risks using 3D imaging and biomechanical simulations; (2) optimizing genomic sequence analysis pipelines to rapidly identify forensic biomarkers in drug-facilitated crimes; and (3) integrating natural language processing (NLP) to extract temporal and spatial relationships from clinical notes, law enforcement reports, and court documents. These tasks demand parallel processing, large-scale data storage, and GPU acceleration to handle high-resolution images, whole-genome sequencing data, and unstructured text. The proposed HPC resources will enable the development of predictive tools to guide evidence collection, improve the reliability of medicolegal testimony, and identify patterns in interpersonal violence. Outcomes will include open-source algorithms tailored to forensic nursing workflows, validated through collaborations with hospital forensic teams and legal agencies. By enhancing the precision and efficiency of forensic data analysis, this project aims to advance trauma-informed care practices, reduce investigative timelines, and strengthen the scientific rigor of nursing contributions to criminal justice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the law and forensic science to nursing practice and collaborate with other professionals for the care of victims and the prosecution of criminals. Includes instruction in advanced physical assessment, evidence collection and preservation, forensic anthropology, legal testimony, medicolegal investigation, pathophysiology, pathohistology, pharmacology, and violence prevention.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the role of baryonic feedback and dark matter interactions in the formation of large-scale cosmic structures, particularly galaxy clusters and the warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM). Current cosmological simulations often simplify or omit multiscale plasma kinetics and radiation-hydrodynamic processes, limiting their ability to reconcile tensions between observed and predicted properties of the cosmic web. We propose a series of high-resolution, cosmological-scale simulations integrating state-of-the-art treatments of non-equilibrium radiation transfer, magnetohydrodynamics, and relativistic particle interactions. These simulations will leverage adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) within the ENZO framework to resolve multiphase gas dynamics in galaxy clusters (down to ~1 kpc scales) while maintaining cosmological volumes (~500 Mpc side length). A novel convolutional neural network (CNN) will accelerate radiative transfer calculations by emulating photon propagation in non-Euclidean geometries, trained against discrete ordinate method benchmarks. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for 3D ray-tracing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) distortions caused by the Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effect in simulated clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) calibrated scaling relations between intracluster medium turbulence and dark matter halo properties, (2) synthetic CMB sky maps incorporating kinetic electron effects, and (3) open-source release of optimized radiation transport kernels for AMR cosmologies. These results will directly inform observational strategies for upcoming surveys (e.g., Simons Observatory, Athena) while resolving long-standing discrepancies in baryon fraction measurements across redshift. The requested 2.5 million node-hours on GPU-enabled HPC resources will enable unprecedented dynamic range in modeling the coupled evolution of dark and luminous matter, advancing our capacity to constrain dark energy models through multi-messenger cosmology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical, observational, and numerical study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena of the universe on a large scale. Includes instruction in clusters of galaxies, the cosmic microwave background, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize adaptive logistics planning for large-scale construction projects under supply chain volatility, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic resource allocation strategies. Construction logistics—particularly in multi-phase projects like industrial plants or urban infrastructure—face compounding risks from material shortages, labor variability, and geopolitical disruptions. Traditional linear scheduling tools inadequately capture these interdependencies, leading to cascading delays and cost overruns. The proposed study will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate decentralized decision-making across suppliers, contractors, and transport networks under stochastic conditions. Using HPC resources, the team will parameterize a multi-agent system reflecting real-world constraints (e.g., equipment availability, carbon emission limits, just-in-time delivery tolerances) and train RL policies to minimize project-wide downtime. The computational workflow will process terascale datasets from historical project records, IoT-enabled job sites, and global supply chain APIs to calibrate risk profiles. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform capable of forecasting disruption propagation and recommending real-time adjustments to procurement routes, workforce deployment, and inventory buffers. By quantifying trade-offs between resilience and efficiency in resource allocation, this work aims to advance adaptive capacity in construction management—a critical need in an era of climate and geopolitical uncertainties. The HPC component is essential for parallelizing thousands of stochastic simulations, enabling near-real-time policy updates during model training. Results will be validated against case studies from offshore wind farm construction, where logistical complexity and regulatory constraints exacerbate scheduling challenges. This interdisciplinary approach bridges operations research, computational sustainability, and construction systems engineering, offering a novel paradigm for data-driven resilience in capital projects.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage, coordinate, and supervise the construction process. Includes instruction in commercial, residential, mechanical, highway/heavy civil, electrical, environmental, industrial, and specialty construction; facilities management; budgeting and cost control; logistics and materials management; organization and scheduling; personnel management and labor relations; site safety; construction contracting; construction processes and techniques; and applicable codes and regulations.

abstract: Urban transportation systems face escalating challenges due to population growth, climate change, and evolving mobility demands, necessitating advanced tools to optimize infrastructure investments and policy interventions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating high-resolution geospatial data, dynamic travel behavior models, and climate risk projections to evaluate multimodal transportation infrastructure performance under diverse socioeconomic and environmental scenarios. The research employs agent-based modeling to simulate daily travel patterns across metropolitan regions, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict long-term infrastructure degradation from extreme weather events. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing large-scale datasets—including anonymized mobile device trajectories, transit schedules, and floodplain maps—while running thousands of parameterized simulations to assess tradeoffs between equity, cost efficiency, and system resilience. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized GIS operations for spatial network analysis and GPU-accelerated deep learning models to identify vulnerable transportation corridors. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for prioritizing climate-adaptive infrastructure investments and quantifying equity impacts of proposed transit expansions. The project will advance transportation planning scholarship by establishing novel methods to bridge micro-scale behavioral modeling with macro-scale infrastructure analytics, directly informing state and municipal climate adaptation plans. By utilizing HPC capabilities, this work addresses current limitations in conventional planning tools, which often oversimplify spatial interactions or fail to account for compounding stressors. Results will be disseminated through open-access repositories to support evidence-based policymaking in public agencies, contributing to sustainable infrastructure development goals.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the economic, social, spatial, and environmental aspects of transportation and infrastructure planning. Includes instruction in economics, environmental analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, risk analysis, transportation economics, transportation evaluation, transportation planning, transportation policy, and urban transportation planning.

abstract: Ophthalmic lens fabrication requires precise optimization of optical, material, and ergonomic parameters to address diverse visual impairments, yet current methods for designing complex prescriptions—such as those for high myopia, irregular corneas, or multifocal needs—rely heavily on iterative manual adjustments. These processes are time-intensive, costly, and may not fully account for patient-specific anatomical variations or dynamic visual demands. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to automate and enhance the design of precision ophthalmic lenses using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of traditional lens fabrication workflows by integrating optical ray-tracing simulations, finite element analysis (FEA) of lens stress distribution, and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization algorithms. Computational models will simulate light propagation through candidate lens geometries under varying pupil dynamics and gaze conditions, while FEA will evaluate mechanical durability during edging and mounting. Concurrently, ML models trained on historical prescription data, patient biometrics, and material performance metrics will predict optimal lens parameters. HPC resources are critical to manage the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize simulations across thousands of design iterations, and process multimodal datasets (optical, structural, clinical) at scale. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for generating patient-specific lens designs that minimize optical aberrations, improve comfort, and reduce production waste. The project also aims to establish a database correlating computational predictions with real-world fabrication outcomes, enabling iterative refinement of models. By bridging computational optics and ophthalmic technology, this work has the potential to advance personalized eyewear solutions, reduce turnaround times for complex prescriptions, and provide a scalable platform for educating future practitioners in data-driven lens design methodologies. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and partnerships with clinical training programs to align laboratory practices with emerging computational techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize industrial safety protocols by modeling complex interactions between human operators, equipment, and environmental factors in high-risk settings. Despite advancements in safety engineering, current risk assessment tools often fail to capture nonlinear dynamics in real time, particularly in scenarios involving human behavior, multi-agent workflows, and rapidly evolving hazards. To address this gap, we propose integrating machine learning with physics-based simulations to create predictive models of accident precursors. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale agent-based simulations of industrial workflows, coupled with computational fluid dynamics models for hazardous material dispersion and deep neural networks trained on historical incident data. Key objectives include quantifying emergent risks in collaborative human-robot workcells, simulating cascading failure modes in chemical processing plants, and optimizing evacuation routes under dynamic thermal or toxic exposure conditions. The computational demands of these tasks—including parallelized Monte Carlo sampling for probabilistic risk analysis and real-time reinforcement learning for adaptive safety system training—necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for scenario-based safety planning, validated through case studies in manufacturing and energy sectors. This work will advance the field of industrial safety by enabling proactive risk mitigation strategies grounded in multi-scale, data-driven modeling. The proposed HPC resources will directly support the creation of decision-support tools that help organizations comply with evolving safety regulations while maintaining operational efficiency. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and contribute to curriculum development in safety-critical systems engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing and enforcing industrial safety standards to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in industrial processes, industrial hygiene, injury prevention, toxicology, ergonomics, risk analysis, system and process safety, safety performance measurement, human factors, human behavior, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced predictive maintenance frameworks and performance optimization models for medium/heavy-duty commercial vehicles using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research addresses a critical gap in current vehicle diagnostics and repair methodologies, which often rely on reactive, rule-based approaches ill-suited to the dynamic operational conditions of modern trucks and industrial vehicles. By integrating real-world sensor data from engine control units, telematics, and onboard diagnostics with physics-based simulations of mechanical systems, the project aims to create hybrid computational models capable of predicting component failures, optimizing fuel efficiency, and reducing unplanned downtime. Key computational challenges include parallelized finite element analysis of stress distributions in diesel engine components under variable loads, machine learning-driven anomaly detection in heterogeneous sensor streams, and multi-physics simulations of thermal-electrical interactions in next-generation electric commercial vehicle powertrains. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of telemetry data, train deep neural networks on failure mode patterns, and run high-fidelity simulations of complex systems like selective catalytic reduction units or automated transmission assemblies at scale. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive maintenance algorithms validated against industry-standard diagnostic protocols, digital twin frameworks for virtual testing of aftermarket modifications, and data-driven recommendations for retrofitting legacy fleets with efficiency-enhancing technologies. The project directly supports curriculum development in vehicle electrification and AI-assisted repair systems while providing technician students with hands-on experience in cloud-based diagnostic tools. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships with regional freight operators and vocational training modules focused on computational troubleshooting techniques. By bridging data science and heavy vehicle systems, this work aims to reduce lifecycle costs for commercial fleets while addressing emissions reduction targets in transportation sectors.
cip_title: Medium/ Heavy Vehicle and Truck Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the specialized maintenance and repair of trucks, buses, and other commercial and industrial vehicles. Includes instruction in diesel engine mechanics, suspension and steering, brake systems, electrical and electronic systems, preventive maintenance inspections, drive trains, gasoline engine mechanics, HVAC systems, and auxiliary equipment installation and repair.

abstract: Disasters, whether natural or man-made, challenge healthcare systems with unpredictable surges in patient volume, resource constraints, and time-sensitive decision-making. Current triage and resource allocation strategies often rely on static protocols that fail to adapt to dynamic, large-scale scenarios, potentially leading to preventable morbidity and mortality. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to optimize real-time clinical decision-making and resource distribution during disasters. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will create agent-based models simulating diverse disaster scenarios (e.g., earthquakes, mass casualty incidents, pandemics) that incorporate variables such as prehospital EMS response times, hospital capacities, supply chain limitations, and evolving patient needs. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on heterogeneous datasets—including historical disaster registries, real-time geospatial data, and synthetic scenarios—to predict casualty patterns, identify critical resource bottlenecks, and recommend adaptive triage protocols. The models will integrate clinical outcomes data to prioritize interventions based on severity, survivability, and resource availability. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of past disaster responses and collaboration with emergency management agencies for scenario stress-testing. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide EMS routing, hospital resource prepositioning, and dynamic bed allocation, as well as generalized frameworks for scaling responses to disaster magnitude. By leveraging HPC to process complex, interdependent variables in near-real time, this work aims to reduce delays in life-saving care, minimize resource exhaustion, and improve survival rates. The computational tools developed will be shared via open-source platforms to support global disaster medicine research and operational planning, with direct implications for clinical practice guidelines and health policy.
cip_definition: Research on how to provide care for the victims of natural and man-made disasters with specific consideration given to timeliness and availability of resources. Includes instruction in emergency medicine and its associated acute care specialties, public health, emergency management, humanitarian services, and prehospital emergency medical services (EMS).

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to optimize human-machine teaming dynamics within next-generation combat systems. Modern network-centric warfare increasingly relies on seamless integration of autonomous subsystems, AI-driven decision aids, and human operators, creating complex cognitive and operational challenges that traditional systems engineering approaches struggle to model. The proposed work addresses the critical gap in predictive tools for assessing how emergent human performance factors—including trust calibration, cognitive overload, and adaptive behavior patterns—interact with technical system constraints in multi-domain battle scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the team will implement a multi-scale agent-based modeling environment combining combat physics simulations (sensor fusion, weapon system interoperability) with neurocognitive architectures modeled through deep reinforcement learning agents. Computational experiments will simulate contested electromagnetic environments across naval, aerial, and cyber domains while tracking decision latency, error propagation, and crew resilience metrics under varying stress conditions. The hybrid discrete-continuous simulation architecture requires parallelized execution of Monte Carlo iterations across parameter spaces encompassing hardware reliability thresholds, adversarial AI tactics, and heterogeneous human operator profiles. Expected outcomes include a validated benchmarking toolkit for quantifying human-system integration risks in combat system prototypes, plus novel algorithms for dynamic task allocation that balance automation capabilities with human situational awareness preservation. This computational methodology aims to establish new standards for evaluating cognitive compatibility in military human-machine systems while remaining agnostic to specific sensor or weapon technologies, thereby supporting adaptable force modernization across evolving threat landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of systems engineering and system architecture to the design and construction of modern combat systems and their integration with each other, with host platforms and with other forces into network-centric warfighting systems. Includes instruction in systems engineering, computer programming, chemical systems, biological systems, material systems, human factors, combat environments, sensor systems, threat and system risk assessment, conventional and unconventional weapons, combat simulation, reliability and maintenance, testing, engineering project management, strategic planning and applications to aerospace, ground, and naval combat systems.

abstract: Forensic anthropology faces critical challenges in analyzing skeletal remains for medicolegal investigations, particularly when dealing with fragmented, degraded, or commingled remains. Traditional analytical methods often lack the precision and scalability required to address complex taphonomic processes, biological profile estimation under suboptimal conditions, or high-dimensional datasets from advanced imaging techniques. This project proposes the development of computational models to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of skeletal analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning algorithms to automate the classification of skeletal trauma and taphonomic alterations using micro-CT and 3D surface scan data; (2) simulating population-specific osteological variation through probabilistic modeling to improve ancestry and sex estimation in diverse forensic contexts; and (3) optimizing Bayesian frameworks for integrating multi-modal data (e.g., isotopic, genomic, morphometric) in identification workflows. These objectives require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale imaging datasets, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, and iterative training of deep neural networks—tasks exceeding the capacity of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. The proposed HPC implementation will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for image analysis and distributed memory systems for large-scale statistical modeling. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for forensic practitioners, validated protocols for computationally intensive analytical pipelines, and novel insights into skeletal biomechanics under taphonomic stress. By bridging gaps between anthropological theory and computational innovation, this work aims to establish reproducible, data-driven standards for forensic casework while advancing methodological rigor in skeletal identification. The resource allocation will directly support critical advancements in medicolegal death investigation capabilities, with implications for humanitarian efforts and judicial systems worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and skeletal anthropology in medicolegal death investigations. Includes instruction in biological anthropology theory, crime scene investigation, forensic anthropology field methods, forensic anthropological techniques and procedures, human anatomy, methods of human identification, mortuary archaeology, osteology, and taphonomy.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the cascading impacts of cross-border policy interventions on socio-economic and environmental systems within the context of globalization. Existing frameworks often silo regional dynamics, failing to capture the nonlinear feedback loops between transnational governance, resource flows, and localized community outcomes. Our work addresses this gap by developing an integrated computational model that simulates interactions between heterogeneous agents—including governments, multinational corporations, and civil society networks—across spatial and temporal scales. Using a combination of agent-based modeling, network analysis, and machine learning, the project will assimilate multi-source data (e.g., trade agreements, climate vulnerability indices, and social media sentiment) to quantify how policy shifts in one region propagate systemic risks or opportunities globally. The computational architecture will prioritize scalability to accommodate high-dimensional datasets spanning 50+ countries and adaptive learning mechanisms to simulate emergent behaviors under scenarios such as decarbonization mandates or supply chain disruptions. HPC resources are critical for running parallelized simulations that explore thousands of policy permutations while maintaining granularity in socio-cultural and ecological variables. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool to visualize trade-offs between economic equity, environmental resilience, and geopolitical stability. This work contributes to interdisciplinary globalization studies by bridging computational social science with complexity theory, offering a novel methodology to anticipate second-order consequences of transnational governance. Results will inform stakeholder workshops with international organizations, providing evidence-based strategies to align policy coherence with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in an era of interconnected crises.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on global and international issues from the perspective of the social sciences, social services, and related fields.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of high-resolution digital imaging and prepress design workflows, which increasingly require processing complex graphical datasets beyond the capabilities of standard desktop systems. As the publishing and media industries shift toward dynamic, multi-platform content delivery, designers face challenges in efficiently rendering ultra-high-definition (UHD) images, simulating print-ready color accuracy, and automating layout optimizations across diverse digital and physical formats. Current workflows struggle with latency in real-time previews, inconsistent color gamut translation, and scalability when handling terabyte-scale asset libraries. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize computationally intensive tasks in the prepress pipeline. The methodology integrates GPU-accelerated raster image processing for UHD file conversion, distributed computing frameworks for batch color profile validation, and machine learning models trained on HPC clusters to predict layout responsiveness across devices. By containerizing industry-standard design software (e.g., Adobe InDesign, Affinity Publisher) within HPC environments, the project will benchmark performance gains in tasks such as multi-variant typographic scaling, spectral color matching for Pantone simulations, and AI-driven asset tagging for large media repositories. Expected outcomes include a modular toolkit to optimize prepress workflows for 8K+ resolution outputs, reduce print production errors through predictive color calibration, and enable adaptive template generation for cross-media publishing. This work will provide measurable efficiency improvements for design professionals while establishing a computational framework to bridge traditional desktop publishing practices with emerging requirements in augmented reality (AR) and variable-data printing. The requested resources will directly support reproducibility studies comparing CPU/GPU hybrid architectures for design-specific workloads.
cip_title: Prepress/ Desktop Publishing and Digital Imaging Design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the layout, design and typographic arrangement of printed and/or electronic graphic and textual products. Includes instruction in printing and lithographic equipment and operations, computer hardware and software, digital imaging, print preparation, page layout and design, desktop publishing, and applicable principles of graphic design and web page design.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing medication administration workflows in complex care environments, with a focus on reducing human error and improving real-time decision support for medication aides. While current training emphasizes protocol adherence, dynamic clinical scenarios—such as managing polypharmacy in patients with multimorbidity or acute physiological instability—require adaptive, context-aware strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop and validate computational models that simulate medication administration scenarios across diverse patient populations, integrating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) data, real-world vital sign streams, and environmental variables (e.g., staffing ratios, interruption frequencies). Agent-based modeling will capture interactions between medication aides, patients, and clinical systems, while machine learning techniques will identify latent risk patterns in synthetic and de-identified clinical datasets. A parallel computational framework will enable probabilistic risk assessment for rare but high-consequence events, such as drug-drug interaction cascades in geriatric populations. The project will produce two primary outcomes: 1) an open-source simulation platform for stress-testing medication administration protocols under synthetically generated edge cases, and 2) predictive models to guide the development of context-sensitive clinical decision support tools. By quantifying previously unmodeled relationships between workflow pressures, individual patient factors, and administration errors, this work aims to establish an evidence base for next-generation training paradigms and operational policies. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of simulated care environments and achieving sufficient temporal resolution in pharmacokinetic modeling across millions of parallelized scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed medications; observe and report patient reactions and side effects; and perform related emergency and recording duties under the supervision of nurses and/or physicians. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, common medications and their effects, taking vital signs, oxygen administration, medication administration and application, record-keeping, and patient observation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research focused on the diachronic and synchronic analysis of Polish dialects and literary texts. The research problem centers on the scarcity of large-scale, data-driven studies of Polish linguistic variation and its relationship to sociocultural and geographic factors, particularly in pre-modern and early modern texts. Current scholarship relies heavily on manual analysis of limited corpora, restricting the scope of inquiry into dialectal evolution, syntactic shifts, and stylistic patterns across genres. To address this gap, we propose a computational workflow integrating natural language processing (NLP), geospatial modeling, and machine learning to analyze digitized historical texts, archival recordings, and contemporary spoken corpora. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on domain-specific Polish corpora to improve dialect classification accuracy, deploying phonetic alignment algorithms for comparative analysis of regional speech samples, and implementing graph-based methods to trace lexical diffusion pathways in 16th–19th century literature. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets spanning the National Corpus of Polish, regional folklore archives, and newly digitized manuscripts from the Jagiellonian Library. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database mapping phonological and morphosyntactic features across historical and modern Polish dialects; (2) quantitative models correlating literary style shifts with documented sociopolitical changes; and (3) open-source tools for automated paleographic analysis of early print variants. By enabling systematic analysis at unprecedented scales, this research will provide novel insights into the dynamic interplay between language variation and cultural identity while establishing computational frameworks adaptable to other under-resourced Slavic languages. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for sensitive linguistic data, and high-memory nodes for large-scale parallel corpus processing.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized auditory processing models for individuals with cochlear implant (CI) devices. While CIs restore partial hearing by directly stimulating the auditory nerve, outcomes vary significantly due to patient-specific neurophysiological factors, electrode placement variability, and dynamic interactions between device programming and neural adaptation. Traditional trial-and-error clinical approaches to CI parameter optimization are time-intensive and often suboptimal. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite-element modeling of cochlear electroanatomy, biophysical simulations of neural excitation patterns, and machine learning (ML) to predict patient-specific optimal stimulation strategies. The core challenge lies in modeling the multiscale interactions between CI electrode arrays, cochlear microstructures, and stochastic neural responses—a task requiring iterative simulations across high-dimensional parameter spaces. HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of finite-element models (COMSOL/FEniCS) to simulate electric field distributions in anatomically variable cochlear geometries derived from clinical CT scans. Concurrently, neural network architectures (PyTorch) will be trained on simulated and electrophysiological datasets to map patient-specific anatomical features to optimal stimulation parameters. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational pipeline for CI personalization, validated against electrophysiological and behavioral data from 50 CI recipients. This work bridges computational neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and clinical audiology, offering a paradigm shift from population-based to patient-driven CI programming. By reducing the time and uncertainty in achieving optimal hearing outcomes, the project has the potential to improve quality of life for CI users while establishing a scalable computational foundation for next-generation auditory neuroprosthetics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose and treat hearing loss and other disorders involving the ear, advise patients on means to use their remaining hearing, and select and fit hearing aids and other devices. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of hearing, hearing measurement, auditory pathology, middle and inner ear analysis, rehabilitation therapies and assistive technologies, and pediatric and other special applications.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic decision-making in large-scale hospitality operations through the development of a novel computational model for real-time guest experience simulation. Traditional operational models in hospitality management often rely on static, scenario-based frameworks that fail to capture the complexity of multi-agent interactions in environments such as resorts, convention centers, or cruise ships. Our research addresses this gap by creating an adaptive simulation platform that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including IoT sensor networks, staff mobility patterns, and real-time guest feedback—to predict and mitigate service bottlenecks. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling with reinforcement learning to simulate guest-staff-environment interactions across variable temporal and spatial scales. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets from partner hospitality organizations, training deep neural networks to recognize emergent congestion patterns, and running parallelized simulations of alternative staffing and resource allocation strategies. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics toolkit capable of recommending optimal service interventions under constraints such as fluctuating demand, staff availability, and physical infrastructure limitations. This work advances computational hospitality science by introducing a new paradigm for operational resilience, with potential applications in crisis management (e.g., pandemic response adaptations) and personalized service delivery at enterprise scale. The resulting framework will be validated against operational metrics from three multinational hospitality providers, establishing benchmarks for computational efficiency and decision accuracy. By bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and spatial analytics, this project contributes methodological innovations to an emerging interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of hospitality management and computational social science.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in hospitality service management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The development of effective drug delivery systems is a critical challenge in pharmaceutics, particularly for biologics and poorly soluble compounds. Current limitations in predicting nanoparticle-drug interactions and release kinetics hinder the rational design of targeted, stable formulations. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale drug-carrier interactions and optimize formulation parameters. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will investigate the self-assembly behavior of lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles (LPHNPs) under varying thermodynamic conditions, focusing on encapsulation efficiency of small-molecule chemotherapeutics. Coarse-grained MD simulations will map phase transitions during nanoparticle formation, while all-atom models will quantify drug diffusion coefficients through hybrid matrices. Concurrently, machine learning (ML) approaches will be applied to predict excipient compatibility and long-term stability by training neural networks on simulated physicochemical descriptors and experimental stability datasets. The computational workflow requires significant parallel processing for ensemble simulations across >10,000 parameter combinations (particle size, lipid composition, drug loading). Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking formulation variables to nanoparticle morphology and drug release profiles, (2) identification of novel excipient combinations to minimize burst release in acidic microenvironments, and (3) open-source tools for automated simulation setup and analysis of pharmaceutical colloids. These results will directly inform experimental formulation workflows in our lab’s ongoing work on intravenously administered anticancer agents, reducing costly trial-and-error approaches. By establishing computational pipelines for rational drug delivery design, this project advances the broader goal of precision pharmaceutics while demonstrating how HPC resources can accelerate translational research in pharmaceutical sciences.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the formulation of medicinal substances into product vehicles capable of being stored, transported, and then introduced into the patient and behaving in ways optimal to therapeutic interaction. Includes instruction in statistics, biopharmaceutics, drug metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, physical pharmacy, pharmacological analysis, drug design and development, pharmacological biotechnology, chemical separations, spectroscopy, drug-host interactions, immunology, quantitative drug measurement, enzymatic transformations, and metabolic excretion.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing complexity of auditing in decentralized financial ecosystems, particularly those involving blockchain-based transactions and smart contracts. Traditional auditing frameworks struggle to scale with the velocity, volume, and opacity of data in these systems, creating risks of undetected fraud, compliance gaps, and operational inefficiencies. The project aims to develop a computational auditing model that integrates real-time anomaly detection, probabilistic verification of distributed ledgers, and dynamic risk assessment under uncertainty. Using parallelized graph algorithms, machine learning models trained on heterogeneous transactional datasets (including on-chain and off-chain data), and agent-based simulations of auditor-client interactions, the research will quantify emergent risks in decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms and multi-jurisdictional supply chains. HPC resources are critical for processing petabytes of transactional metadata, optimizing hyperparameters in ensemble classifiers, and simulating adversarial scenarios (e.g., Sybil attacks, wash trading) at scale. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for probabilistic audit sampling in blockchain environments, (2) benchmarks for computational resource allocation during continuous auditing cycles, and (3) evidence-based protocols for auditing autonomous smart contracts with embedded AI decision-making. By bridging computational scalability gaps in auditing practice, this work will provide auditors with adaptive tools to verify decentralized systems effectively while addressing novel ethical and regulatory challenges at the intersection of distributed technologies and financial oversight. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—spanning audit science, cryptography, and computational economics—aims to redefine resource allocation strategies for assurance services in increasingly automated and decentralized business environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including certified accountants, to perform independent internal and external appraisals to evaluate organizational financial and operational activities, ensure compliance with laws and policies, safeguard assets, and promote effective planning and resource allocation. Includes instruction in advanced accounting, audit tools and techniques, sampling, risk and control, audit planning, audit function management, law and regulations, environmental auditing, information technology applications, professional standards and ethics, and specific industry and service sector problems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interplay between dietary patterns, gut microbiome dynamics, and personalized health outcomes, with the goal of advancing precision nutrition frameworks. Current approaches to dietary recommendations often rely on population-level data, which fail to account for individual variability in metabolic responses, microbiome composition, and genetic predispositions. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline integrating multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic profiles) with longitudinal dietary intake records and health metrics. The project will employ machine learning algorithms to identify nonlinear relationships between specific food components, microbial metabolic pathways, and biomarkers of wellness (e.g., inflammation, glycemic control). Agent-based modeling will simulate how individualized microbiome communities respond to dietary perturbations over time, while high-dimensional optimization techniques will explore tailored dietary interventions. The scale of data integration—encompassing terabyte-level genomic datasets, heterogeneous health records, and dynamic food composition databases—necessitates HPC capabilities for parallelized processing, large-memory node utilization, and GPU-accelerated deep learning workflows. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive models that map personalized food-microbiome-health triads, enabling nutritionists to design targeted dietary strategies that account for an individual’s unique biological context. This work will contribute novel computational tools to the emerging field of precision nutrition, with potential applications in mitigating diet-related chronic diseases and optimizing wellness across diverse populations. By bridging gaps between computational systems biology and applied nutrition science, the project aligns with the program’s focus on advancing food-related health interventions while operating in a specialized niche that transcends traditional disciplinary boundaries.
cip_title: Foods, Nutrition, and Wellness Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the role of foods and nutrition in human health and wellness. Includes instruction in nutritional care and education, the planning and provision of food services, the development of consumable food products, life-span nutrition and wellness, the principles of nutritional assessment, and food safety and food composition.

abstract: The study of invertebrate locomotion strategies has emerged as a critical interdisciplinary niche bridging zoology, fluid dynamics, and robotics, yet remains underexplored due to computational limitations in modeling complex biomechanical systems. This project seeks to investigate the hydrodynamics of pulsed jet propulsion in siphonophore colonies (order Physonectae), marine organisms that coordinate synchronized swimming through decentralized colonial architectures. Current models fail to capture the multi-scale fluid-structure interactions between individual nectophore zooids and their emergent colonial propulsion, limiting understanding of energy transfer efficiency in modular organisms. We propose a high-resolution computational framework combining immersed boundary methods with large-eddy simulations to resolve three-dimensional vortex formation and recoil kinematics across colony-wide scales. The model will integrate micro-CT-derived morphological data from *Nanomia bijuga* specimens with dynamically scaled Reynolds numbers, simulating variable pulsation frequencies and inter-zooid phase relationships under different temperature and viscosity regimes. By leveraging GPU-accelerated HPC resources, we aim to process 10^6 core-hours of simulation data quantifying thrust optimization strategies in these fragile, deep-sea organisms that cannot be studied through conventional experimental approaches. Expected outcomes include novel insights into decentralized hydrodynamic coordination mechanisms and predictive models of colonial swimming efficiency under climate-change-induced ocean warming scenarios. This work will establish an open-source computational toolkit for analyzing colonial propulsion dynamics, with broader applications in bio-inspired modular robotics and underwater vehicle design. Results will advance fundamental zoological knowledge of poorly understood deep-sea taxa while demonstrating how HPC-enabled fluid dynamics can address previously intractable questions in organismal biology.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in zoology/animal biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Soil health degradation presents a critical challenge to agricultural sustainability, driven by complex interactions between microbial communities, soil chemistry, and land management practices. Current experimental approaches struggle to disentangle these multidimensional dynamics, particularly at scales relevant to field applications. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating soil chemistry and microbiological processes to predict how microbial metabolic strategies and community assembly interact with soil organic matter (SOM) transformation and nutrient cycling under varying agricultural practices. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate microbial functional guilds (e.g., nitrifiers, denitrifiers, SOM decomposers) in spatially explicit soil microenvironments, coupled with reactive transport models to capture pore-scale geochemical gradients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine-scale physicochemical heterogeneity (e.g., redox oscillations, mineral surfaces) and simulate microbial community trajectories across realistic temporal scales (seasons to decades). Models will be parameterized using metagenomic, metabolomic, and soil chemistry datasets from long-term agricultural trials, with Bayesian calibration to address uncertainty. Key outcomes include predictive maps linking microbial guild activity to nitrogen retention, SOM stabilization, and greenhouse gas fluxes under scenarios of tillage, cover cropping, and fertilizer regimes. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of soil biogeochemical feedbacks while directly informing management strategies to optimize microbial functions for carbon sequestration and crop productivity. The computational framework will be designed for interoperability with existing ecosystem models, enabling scaling from soil microsites to field-level predictions. By bridging microbial ecology and soil chemistry through high-resolution simulations, this project addresses a critical gap in sustainable agricultural research, offering actionable insights to mitigate soil degradation while reducing reliance on empirical trial-and-error approaches.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and microbiological theories and methods (in combination) to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instructional combination of microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy efficiency in industrial-scale heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, which are critical yet energy-intensive components of environmental control infrastructure. Current HVAC optimization strategies rely on generalized models that fail to account for dynamic interactions between equipment performance, facility layouts, and fluctuating environmental conditions. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity simulation approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML), and real-time sensor data assimilation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve complex spatiotemporal interactions within large industrial environments, including airflow patterns, heat exchange dynamics, and particulate dispersion. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized CFD solvers to simulate multi-zone thermal behavior at scale, coupled with ML algorithms trained on operational data to predict system responses under variable load scenarios. A digital twin platform will be developed to test control strategies for minimizing energy consumption while maintaining regulatory compliance and occupant safety. Expected outcomes include a validated optimization toolkit capable of reducing HVAC energy use by 15–25% in target industrial facilities, with broader applications in retrofit planning for aging infrastructure. The project will also generate open-access datasets on HVAC performance under diverse operating conditions, addressing a critical gap in environmental control technology research. By enabling precision adjustments to climate management systems, this work directly supports decarbonization goals while advancing computational methods for sustainable infrastructure optimization. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter sweeps, and ML training workflows that exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental control technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving regulatory frameworks governing algorithmic underwriting in insurance markets, a domain intersecting law, computational ethics, and actuarial practice. The proliferation of machine learning models in risk assessment has introduced legal ambiguities, particularly regarding compliance with anti-discrimination statutes, transparency mandates, and state-specific insurance regulations. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically evaluate the dynamic interplay between rapidly advancing algorithmic tools and heterogeneous regulatory environments. This project addresses this gap by constructing a computational legal analytics pipeline to model jurisdictional variations, predict regulatory conflict points, and simulate the operational impact of proposed compliance strategies. The methodology integrates natural language processing (NLP) to extract legal obligations from insurance statutes across 50 U.S. jurisdictions, graph-based analysis to map interdependencies between regulatory requirements, and agent-based modeling to simulate insurer adaptation pathways under different enforcement scenarios. HPC resources are critical for training transformer models on multi-terabyte corpora of legal texts, regulatory filings, and historical litigation records, while parallelized simulations will assess millions of hypothetical market interactions. Expected outcomes include 1) a taxonomy of algorithmic underwriting compliance risks ranked by jurisdictional prevalence, 2) an open-access repository of annotated regulatory decision trees, and 3) empirically grounded policy recommendations for harmonizing innovation incentives with consumer protection imperatives. By creating scalable tools to navigate the computational complexity of modern insurance law, this work aims to establish a template for data-driven legal governance in algorithmic industries.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting insurance.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical gaps in farrier science by developing computational tools to model the biomechanical interactions between equine hooves and horseshoes, with the goal of optimizing hoof health and performance. Despite the critical role of farriery in equine welfare, current practices rely heavily on empirical knowledge and physical trial-and-error, lacking predictive frameworks to evaluate the long-term impacts of shoeing techniques on hoof stress distribution, gait dynamics, and tissue remodeling. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate hoof-shoe-environment interactions under diverse physiological and environmental conditions. The project will construct 3D biomechanical models of equine hooves derived from imaging data, incorporating material properties of keratin, soft tissues, and common forging metals. Multiphysics simulations will evaluate stress concentrations, thermal effects during forging, and gait-induced load patterns, while ML algorithms will analyze historical lameness data to identify risk factors associated with specific shoeing configurations. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of iteratively simulating thousands of design variants, material composites, and gait scenarios.
