Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for farriers to preemptively assess the biomechanical consequences of corrective shoeing strategies, reducing trial periods and minimizing stress-related injuries. Additionally, the project will generate novel insights into the relationship between forging techniques (e.g., cooling rates, alloy composition) and shoe durability under dynamic loads. By integrating traditional farriery with computational modeling, this work aims to establish an evidence-based paradigm for hoof care, enhancing both equine welfare and the precision of an ancient craft.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to become specialists in equine hoof care (farriers). Includes instruction in equine science, equine health and first aid, general horseshoeing, corrective horseshoeing, gait analysis, and metal forging techniques using gas or coal.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the evidence-based practice of play therapy, an emerging interdisciplinary field integrating child development, psychotherapy, and computational analytics. Play therapy relies on nuanced, non-verbal interactions between therapists and children to address trauma, neurodevelopmental disorders, and social-emotional challenges. However, the dynamic, unstructured nature of play sessions poses significant challenges for systematically analyzing therapeutic mechanisms or predicting outcomes. Current manual coding methods are time-intensive, subjective, and fail to capture multidimensional behavioral patterns. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework to model therapist-child interactions using machine learning and multimodal data integration. The project will process video recordings, wearable sensor data (capturing physiological responses), and annotated clinical outcomes from 500+ archived play therapy sessions. Deep learning architectures, including 3D convolutional neural networks and transformer models, will be trained to classify micro-interactions (e.g., toy selection, symbolic play acts, therapist mirroring behaviors) and link these to therapeutic progress metrics. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution video frames, optimizing complex model architectures, and conducting large-scale hyperparameter searches. Additionally, graph-based simulations will explore how discrete play behaviors coalesce into therapeutic "tipping points" under varying developmental and diagnostic contexts. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated AI-assisted tool for quantifying play therapy fidelity and child engagement, (2) predictive models identifying high-impact therapist strategies, and (3) open-source code for temporal pattern analysis in unstructured therapeutic settings. By bridging developmental psychology with computational scalability, this work aims to establish play therapy as a data-informed discipline while preserving its creative, child-centered ethos.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: Dental pulp vitality is critical to tooth longevity, yet current diagnostic methods for early pulp inflammation lack sensitivity, often leading to delayed intervention and irreversible necrosis. This project addresses the challenge of identifying molecular biomarkers predictive of reversible versus irreversible pulpitis through computational modeling of pulp tissue microenvironment dynamics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to integrate single-cell RNA sequencing data from clinical pulp samples with spatially resolved biomechanical models of intrapulpal pressure changes during inflammatory progression. A multiscale computational framework will be developed to simulate cell-cell signaling networks (Notch, Wnt) under varying inflammatory cytokine gradients, coupled with finite element analysis of fluid dynamics within the confined pulp chamber geometry. Machine learning classifiers will then identify biomarker combinations that correlate with transition thresholds between recoverable and non-recoverable states. The HPC environment is essential for processing 10+ TB of spatial transcriptomic data, running agent-based inflammatory cascade simulations (>10⁶ cellular agents), and iteratively training predictive models across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital twin platform for in silico testing of diagnostic strategies and a ranked biomarker panel validated against longitudinal clinical data. This work bridges computational biology and dental pathophysiology to enable precision endodontics, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving early intervention accuracy. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulation workflows, large-scale parallelized parameter optimization, and secure HIPAA-compliant data integration from clinical partners.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the morphology, physiology, and pathology of human dental pulp and periradicular tissues, and prepares dentists to diagnose and treat internal diseases and injuries of teeth. Includes instruction in theory and practice of endodontics; pulpal disease; relationship of endodontic conditions to other dental/oral health issues; endodontic operative technique; and patient care and management.

abstract: The proliferation of digital media and the rapid dissemination of information have created unprecedented challenges for journalists, particularly in verifying the authenticity of user-generated content, analyzing large-scale social media data, and detecting misinformation. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational tools that enhance the efficiency and accuracy of investigative journalism. The research focuses on three core areas: automated fact-checking of multimedia content (text, images, video), real-time sentiment and network analysis of social media data during breaking news events, and the identification of coordinated disinformation campaigns using machine learning models. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) for cross-referencing claims against trusted databases, computer vision techniques to detect deepfakes or manipulated visuals, and graph-based algorithms to map the spread of narratives across platforms. These tasks require significant parallel processing capabilities due to the volume of data (terabytes of social media posts, images, and video) and the complexity of transformer-based models. By utilizing HPC resources, the project aims to reduce processing times for large datasets from days to hours, enabling journalists to respond to misinformation with evidence-based reporting in near real-time. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for newsrooms to automate preliminary verification workflows, a public dashboard tracking viral misinformation trends, and a framework for ethically integrating AI-assisted analysis into journalistic practice. This work will advance the field by demonstrating how computational scalability can uphold rigorous reporting standards in an era of information overload while adhering to journalism’s core principles of accuracy and accountability.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of gathering, processing, and delivering news and that prepares individuals to be professional print journalists, news editors, and news managers. Includes instruction in news writing and editing; reporting; photojournalism; layout and graphic design; journalism law and policy; professional standards and ethics; research methods; and journalism history and criticism.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of nuclear facilities requires advanced predictive capabilities to address complex multiphysics phenomena, including neutron transport, thermal-hydraulics, and structural responses under extreme conditions. Current computational tools for modeling nuclear systems often rely on simplified approximations or decoupled simulations, limiting their ability to resolve high-fidelity, time-dependent interactions in reactor components and accident scenarios. This project seeks to develop an integrated, high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate coupled neutronics-thermal-mechanical behaviors in advanced reactor designs, with a focus on identifying failure thresholds and optimizing safety protocols. The research will employ Monte Carlo methods for neutron transport, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for coolant flow and heat transfer, and finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain modeling in structural materials. These simulations will be coupled iteratively using in-house code and validated against experimental data from prototypic reactor experiments. The HPC resources will enable massively parallel simulations at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, reducing reliance on empirical safety margins. Key outcomes include a scalable open-source simulation toolkit for nuclear systems, predictive models for material degradation under irradiation and thermal cycling, and data-driven recommendations for regulatory updates on accident mitigation strategies. This work directly supports the development of next-generation nuclear technologies by providing insights into operational limits and failure modes, ultimately enhancing the safety and economic viability of nuclear energy. The computational framework will also serve as a training platform for students in nuclear engineering technology, bridging gaps between theoretical models and real-world applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering, knowledge and technical skills in support of engineer and other professionals operating nuclear facilities and engaged in nuclear applications and safety procedures. Includes instruction in physics, nuclear science, nuclear systems, nuclear plant and systems design, radiological safety, radiological applications, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the intergenerational transmission of cultural knowledge among Indigenous Pacific Islander communities, focusing on digitized oral histories, linguistic corpora, and community-generated multimedia archives. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural continuity and adaptation in the face of colonial disruption, environmental change, and globalization, with particular attention to non-textual forms of knowledge preservation (e.g., chants, weaving motifs, navigational practices). Current methodologies in Pacific Studies lack scalable tools to process multimodal datasets spanning decades of community recordings, Indigenous-language transcripts, and geospatial representations of cultural practices. This project will implement computational workflows integrating natural language processing for under-resourced Pacific languages, network analysis of kinship and knowledge-sharing patterns, and machine learning-assisted comparison of visual cultural symbols across temporal and spatial scales. The HPC environment is critical for training custom transformer models on fragmented historical texts, processing high-resolution imagery of material culture, and simulating cultural diffusion pathways through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of analyzed cultural data (developed in partnership with Indigenous stakeholders), new computational frameworks for ethically engaged area studies research, and quantitative insights into how specific governance structures within Pacific communities correlate with cultural resilience. By centering Indigenous epistemologies in its technical design, this work aims to advance decolonial methodologies in the digital humanities while providing Pacific Islander communities with tools to strengthen intergenerational knowledge systems. The requested resources will enable processing of ~50TB of heterogeneous cultural data, reducing runtime for comparative analyses from months to days, and facilitating real-time collaboration with international research partners and Indigenous knowledge holders.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Australasia and the Pacific Ocean, related island groups and bordering coastal regions, and including pre- and post-colonial migration patterns.

abstract: Nuclear medicine faces critical challenges in optimizing radiopharmaceutical design, tracer kinetic modeling, and personalized dosimetry due to the complex interplay of biological variability, imaging physics, and metabolic heterogeneity. Current computational approaches often rely on simplified compartmental models or population-averaged parameters, limiting their ability to predict tracer behavior at the individual patient level or account for dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions in theranostic applications. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale modeling framework to simulate radiopharmaceutical biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, and radiation dose deposition with unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. The computational approach integrates 1) physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling informed by patient-specific multi-omics data, 2) Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations for dosimetry, and 3) machine learning algorithms trained on dynamic PET/CT datasets to predict therapeutic response. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution voxelized phantoms, iterative optimization of tracer kinetic parameters across large patient cohorts, and uncertainty quantification through ensemble modeling. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for tumor targeting efficiency of novel theranostic agents, optimized dosing strategies for alpha-emitting radiotherapeutics, and an open-source computational platform for patient-specific treatment planning. By bridging molecular-scale tracer interactions with organ-level imaging phenotypes, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift in radiopharmaceutical development and clinical translation, potentially reducing off-target radiation exposure by 20-30% in therapy applications while improving diagnostic sensitivity for early-stage malignancies. The requested computing resources are essential for managing petabyte-scale medical imaging datasets and achieving the 10^6-core-hour simulations required for real-world clinical validation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the tracer principle, most often with radiopharmaceuticals, to evaluate molecular, metabolic, physiologic and pathologic conditions of the body for the purposes of diagnosis, therapy and research. Includes instruction in tracer kinetics, the biologic effects of radiation exposure, the fundamentals of the physical sciences, and the principles and operation of radiation detection and imaging systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in the Digital Humanities, focusing on the large-scale analysis of historical texts and cultural artifacts to uncover patterns of social and linguistic change across time and geography. The research problem centers on the limitations of traditional humanities methodologies in processing and interpreting vast, heterogeneous datasets—such as digitized manuscripts, newspapers, and ephemera from the 18th to 20th centuries—which require advanced computational techniques to analyze at scale. Current tools for text mining, network analysis, and geospatial mapping struggle with the volume, noise, and multilingual nature of these materials, particularly when integrating non-textual data like images or audiovisual records. To address this, the project will implement a computational workflow combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for semantic and sentiment analysis, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map intellectual and cultural networks, and computer vision algorithms to link visual motifs with textual themes. These methods will be optimized for parallel processing on HPC clusters to handle datasets exceeding 10 million documents and associated metadata. Key challenges include adapting machine learning frameworks for noisy, historical language data and developing scalable pipelines for multimodal integration. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized cultural transmission pathways, the creation of publicly accessible interactive visualizations of linguistic shifts, and open-source tools for cross-domain analysis in digital humanities research. By enabling the synthesis of fragmented archival materials into cohesive narratives, this work aims to demonstrate how HPC-driven methodologies can transform humanities scholarship, offering new insights into the dynamics of cultural exchange while fostering public engagement through dynamic digital archives. The project’s computational requirements—particularly GPU-intensive model training and large-memory data processing—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve its interdisciplinary goals.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of new technologies, advanced computing, and public engagement to investigate and analyze questions in the humanities. Includes instruction in anthropology, art, data mining and machine learning, design, digital archives, geospatial technologies, history, human-computer interface design, literature, markup languages, social media technologies, and software development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the evidence-based integration of somatic bodywork practices through computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. Despite the growing clinical use of touch-based therapies such as Rolfing/Structural Integration, lymphatic drainage, and hydrotherapy, the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly quantified. Current research is limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous outcome measures, and an inability to model complex tissue-level interactions in real time. To address these gaps, we propose a multi-modal computational framework combining finite element modeling (FEM) of soft tissue mechanics, machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of clinical outcomes data, and agent-based simulations of autonomic nervous system responses. HPC resources will enable the integration of high-resolution anatomical datasets (MRI/CT-derived 3D meshes) with dynamic physiological parameters to simulate pressure propagation during manual therapy techniques across diverse body types. Concurrently, federated learning architectures will be deployed to analyze anonymized treatment records from partner clinics, identifying predictors of efficacy while preserving patient confidentiality. A pilot study will focus on modeling fascial reorganization in Structural Integration therapy, correlating simulated strain patterns with longitudinal pain reduction metrics from a 500-patient cohort. Expected outcomes include the first open-source computational toolkit for optimizing touch intervention parameters based on individualized anatomical and biomarker profiles. This work will establish a scalable platform for validating somatic bodywork mechanisms, informing clinical training protocols, and personalizing therapeutic approaches. By bridging embodied practice with computational precision, the project aims to elevate somatic modalities’ scientific rigor while expanding access to data-driven, equitable care frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical and emotional balance and well-being through the application of skilled touch principles and techniques. Includes instruction in therapeutic massage and other hands-on touch methods, anatomy and physiology, structural/functional integration and various holistic health systems (Rolfing/Structural Integration, colon hydrotherapy, Breema, Hellerwork, lymphatic drainage, Rosen Method, hydrotherapy, and others), client counseling, practice management, and applicable regulations and professional standards.

abstract: The human gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as a critical mediator of dietary effects on health, yet the complex interplay between dietary components, microbial metabolism, and host physiology remains poorly understood. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational model to simulate how personalized variations in gut microbiota composition modulate nutrient bioavailability and metabolic outcomes in diverse populations. Current models lack the granularity to integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and host transcriptomic) with real-world dietary patterns, limiting their utility for precision nutrition. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The model will leverage large-scale datasets from longitudinal nutrition studies, including metagenomic sequences from stool samples, plasma metabolomics, and dietary logs, to simulate nutrient-microbiome-host interactions at the individual and population levels. Computational challenges include the integration of heterogeneous data streams, dynamic modeling of microbial community interactions under varying nutrient conditions, and probabilistic forecasting of metabolic outcomes. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of microbial taxa, iterative parameter optimization via neural networks, and sensitivity analyses to identify key dietary-microbial drivers of health outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible tool for predicting personalized responses to dietary interventions, (2) identification of microbial biomarkers for nutrient absorption efficiency, and (3) novel insights into how culturally diverse dietary patterns interact with microbiome ecology to influence chronic disease risk. This work bridges computational biology and nutritional epidemiology, offering a scalable approach to advance precision nutrition while addressing health disparities linked to dietary practices. The proposed models will serve as a foundation for future clinical trials and public health strategies aimed at microbiome-targeted dietary recommendations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationships between food consumption and human development and health. Includes instruction in the cellular and molecular processes of food processing in the human body, related metabolic processes, the relationship of food and nutrition to disease, and nutritional needs across the life span.

abstract: The accelerating impacts of climate change, habitat fragmentation, and invasive species necessitate advanced predictive tools to optimize conservation strategies for terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. This project seeks to develop a spatially explicit modeling framework to forecast wildlife population dynamics and habitat suitability under multiple environmental stressors, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current computational limitations. The research focuses on three interconnected challenges: (1) simulating fine-scale species-environment interactions across heterogeneous landscapes, (2) integrating genomic data to assess adaptive potential in climate-vulnerable species, and (3) evaluating the efficacy of proposed management interventions under diverse climate scenarios. Computational methods will combine agent-based models (ABMs) with machine learning approaches to analyze movement patterns, resource use, and genetic connectivity using multi-terabyte datasets from GPS collars, environmental sensors, and whole-genome sequencing. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of ensemble climate projections (CMIP6) at 1km resolution, nested within regional hydrological models to assess surface water availability for aquatic species. Expected outcomes include the identification of climate-resilient habitat corridors, genomic markers associated with thermal tolerance in keystone species, and decision-support tools for prioritizing restoration efforts. By quantifying trade-offs between conservation actions under uncertainty, this work will provide actionable strategies for maintaining biodiversity in managed wildlands and protected areas. The scale of spatiotemporal data integration and the need for real-time parameter optimization in adaptive management scenarios exceed the capabilities of local computing infrastructure, necessitating dedicated HPC allocation. This project directly supports the program’s mission to advance evidence-based wildlands management while training students in computational ecology techniques.
cip_title: Wildlife, Fish and Wildlands Science and Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conserve and manage wilderness areas and the flora, marine and aquatic life therein, and manage wildlife reservations and zoological/aquarium facilities for recreational, commercial, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in wildlife biology, marine/aquatic biology, environmental science, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, natural resources management and policy, outdoor recreation and parks management, the design and operation of natural and artificial wildlife habitats, applicable law and regulations, and related administrative and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, installation, and maintenance of hybrid renewable energy systems, with a focus on improving reliability and efficiency in dynamic operational environments. Current approaches to energy system installation and repair often rely on static guidelines or localized empirical data, which may not account for variable factors such as fluctuating energy demand, environmental stressors, or component degradation over time. To address this gap, the research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex energy systems—including solar arrays, wind turbines, and battery storage—under diverse real-world conditions. These simulations will integrate multi-physics modeling techniques, such as computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airflow around turbine blades and finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress in mounting hardware, alongside machine learning algorithms trained on historical failure and maintenance data. The computational workflow will prioritize scalability to accommodate systems of varying sizes, from residential setups to grid-scale installations. Key outcomes will include predictive maintenance frameworks to reduce downtime, data-driven protocols for optimizing component compatibility during installation, and risk assessment tools for identifying failure-prone configurations. By quantifying trade-offs between cost, durability, and energy output, the project aims to provide technicians and installers with actionable insights for system design and troubleshooting. The HPC resources are critical for handling the high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets and parallelized simulations required to model interactions between mechanical, electrical, and environmental variables. Results will be validated against field data from partner organizations, ensuring practical applicability. This work directly supports workforce training initiatives by generating case studies and simulation modules for instructional use, bridging computational research with hands-on technical education in energy systems management.
cip_title: Energy Systems Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize dispute resolution strategies across complex, multi-party scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome limitations of traditional analytical methods. Dispute resolution processes in settings such as labor negotiations, international diplomacy, or corporate mergers involve dynamic interactions among stakeholders with competing priorities, cultural differences, and asymmetric information. Existing theoretical models often fail to capture the nonlinear feedback loops, behavioral biases, and context-dependent decision-making inherent in these systems. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), game-theoretic simulations, and natural language processing (NLP). The ABM component will simulate thousands of negotiation trajectories using empirically derived behavioral profiles, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize mediation strategies under varying constraints. NLP tools will analyze historical arbitration transcripts and treaty documents to identify linguistic patterns correlated with successful outcomes, informing model parameters. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to realistic participant numbers (50+ agents per scenario), parallelizing scenario testing, and processing large textual datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated dispute resolution benchmarks, (2) quantitative metrics for predicting negotiation breakdown risks, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive mediation protocols. By bridging computational social science with conflict resolution theory, this work aims to provide practitioners with data-driven tools to de-escalate high-stakes disputes while advancing methodological innovation in multidisciplinary computational humanities research. The project’s scale—encompassing 10,000+ simulation hours and terabyte-scale text analysis—necessitates cluster computing infrastructure with GPU acceleration and distributed memory capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that provides individuals with skills in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration, that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: Climate change exacerbates the frequency and severity of extreme hydrological events, challenging existing flood risk management frameworks. Traditional hydrologic models often oversimplify interactions between surface water, groundwater, and engineered infrastructure, limiting their predictive accuracy under non-stationary climate conditions. This project seeks to develop an integrated high-resolution computational model to simulate coupled hydrologic processes and infrastructure responses across urban and rural watersheds. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the proposed framework will employ parallelized numerical solvers to resolve fine-scale spatial heterogeneities in soil properties, land cover, and drainage networks, while incorporating stochastic climate projections from CMIP6 datasets. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to calibrate model parameters using remote sensing data and real-time sensor networks, enhancing predictive reliability. The computational demands of multi-scale simulations, encompassing domains up to 10,000 km² with meter-level resolution, necessitate access to HPC clusters for efficient execution. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for flood inundation mapping under diverse climate scenarios, quantitative assessments of green infrastructure interventions, and scalable decision-support frameworks for adaptive water management. By advancing the integration of physical and anthropogenic factors in hydrologic modeling, this research will directly inform resilience planning for critical water systems and contribute to sustainable resource allocation strategies in rapidly changing environments.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for collecting, storing, moving, conserving and controlling surface- and groundwater, including water quality control, water cycle management, management of human and industrial water requirements, water delivery, and flood control.

abstract: This project seeks to advance diagnostic and therapeutic precision in radiology by developing computational models to optimize multi-modal imaging analysis and radiation dose delivery. Current limitations in real-time processing of high-resolution imaging data—including dynamic contrast-enhanced X-ray, diffusion-weighted MRI, and 4D ultrasound—hinder the ability to delineate subtle pathological features or adapt therapies during image-guided interventions. Additionally, the interplay between patient-specific anatomy and radiation dosimetry in emerging techniques, such as radiopharmaceutical therapies and hyperthermic ablation, remains inadequately modeled for clinical translation. To address these challenges, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating machine learning (ML) and physics-based simulations. First, a deep convolutional neural network will be trained on multi-institutional datasets to segment tumors and critical structures across heterogeneous imaging modalities, leveraging distributed GPU nodes for accelerated model optimization. Second, Monte Carlo simulations of ionizing radiation transport and ultrasound wave propagation will be implemented using parallelized computation to predict dose deposition and thermal effects in patient-specific 3D anatomies derived from CT/MRI. These models will be validated against phantom experiments and retrospective clinical cases. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabyte-scale imaging repositories, enabling submillimeter-resolution simulations, and reducing iterative computation times from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for real-time adaptive treatment planning, validated protocols to minimize off-target radiation exposure in novel radionuclide therapies, and quantitative biomarkers for early treatment response assessment. By unifying imaging analytics with biophysical modeling, this work aims to establish a scalable computational foundation for personalized radiologic care, directly addressing variability in interventional outcomes and enhancing the safety of advanced radiotherapeutic approaches.
cip_definition: Research on how to utilize x-ray, ionizing radiation, radionuclides, ultrasound, electromagnetic radiation, and image-guided intervention to diagnose and treat disease. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in hospital unit coordination workflows through the development of predictive computational models optimized for dynamic healthcare environments. Health Unit Coordinators (HUCs) manage critical administrative tasks—including patient scheduling, resource requisition, and interdepartmental communication—but current protocols rely heavily on static templates that fail to adapt to real-time variables such as fluctuating patient volumes, staff availability, and emergent care priorities. This project proposes a novel computational framework integrating discrete-event simulation and machine learning to model and optimize HUC workflows. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets from electronic health records, staff rostering systems, and real-time sensor logs capturing patient movement across units. Agent-based models will simulate interactions between HUCs, clinical staff, and patients under varying stress scenarios, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will predict bottlenecks in task completion times. The computational pipeline will be trained on historical data from three tertiary care hospitals and validated against prospective operational metrics. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating unit coordination workflows, (2) predictive algorithms to prioritize time-sensitive administrative tasks during high-census periods, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for dynamic resource reallocation protocols. By optimizing the responsiveness of administrative workflows, this work aims to reduce latent delays in care delivery, mitigate clinician burnout caused by communication gaps, and improve patient throughput in acute care settings. The scale and complexity of multimodal healthcare data necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve the temporal resolution required for actionable insights at the ward-clerk operational level.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: Endocrine signaling dysregulation is a critical driver in cancer progression, yet the systems-level integration of hormonal dynamics with tumor microenvironmental factors remains poorly understood. This project seeks to characterize how aberrant endocrine communication between stromal and epithelial compartments promotes oncogenic transformation in hormone-sensitive tissues, with a focus on pancreatic and adrenal malignancies. The research employs a multi-scale computational framework integrating spatially resolved hormone diffusion models, intracellular signaling cascades, and population-level cellular response dynamics. High-performance computing resources are essential to simulate three-dimensional tissue architectures containing >10⁶ interacting cellular agents, each governed by Boolean network models of endocrine-responsive pathways (including mTOR, MAPK, and cAMP-dependent systems). Molecular dynamics simulations will parameterize hormone-receptor binding affinities under hypoxic and normoxic conditions using adaptive sampling algorithms. Validation datasets from primary cell co-cultures and patient-derived xenograft transcriptomics will constrain model parameters through iterative Bayesian optimization. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of critical endocrine signaling nodes that amplify tumor-stromal crosstalk, 2) predictive maps of hormonal gradient thresholds that trigger epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and 3) mechanistic insights into circadian endocrine oscillations that modulate chemotherapy resistance. These results will advance targeted therapies for endocrine-related cancers while establishing novel computational paradigms for analyzing hormone-driven cellular decision-making. The proposed GPU-accelerated simulations require 12,000+ node-hours monthly to achieve necessary spatiotemporal resolution, necessitating dedicated allocation within a Tier 2 HPC environment. Successful implementation will provide the first integrative computational platform capable of resolving endocrine-disrupted signaling networks across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales in oncological contexts.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition, manufacture, and secretion of protein compounds by cells and glands and the role of endocrine substances in bodily processes. Includes instruction in protein chemistry, protein secretion, membrane biogenesis and transfer methods, cellular communication, gene and cell regulation, cytochemistry, fractionation, radioautography, and applications such as neuroendocrinology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance psychoanalytic research by enabling large-scale computational analysis of therapeutic interactions and psychodynamic processes. The research problem centers on the inherent complexity of psychoanalytic data—such as longitudinal clinical case studies, therapist-patient dialogue transcripts, and dream narratives—which are rich in qualitative and temporal patterns but challenging to analyze systematically using conventional methods. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the ability to model dynamic therapeutic processes, identify latent patterns in symptom evolution, or simulate theoretical constructs like transference networks at clinically meaningful scales. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of therapy session transcripts, machine learning (ML) models to detect predictive markers of therapeutic outcomes, and agent-based simulations of psychodynamic interactions grounded in Freudian and Jungian frameworks. These methods will be applied to a curated dataset of 10,000+ anonymized clinical hours from archival records and prospective studies, requiring HPC resources for parallel processing of high-dimensional text data, training of deep neural networks on temporal symptom trajectories, and Monte Carlo simulations of theoretical models. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for mapping transference-countertransference dynamics across therapy dyads, (2) predictive models linking specific intervention types to symptom remission in anxiety and personality disorders, and (3) validated simulations of Jungian archetype activation patterns in dream analysis. By bridging psychodynamic theory with computational rigor, this work aims to generate novel insights into therapeutic mechanisms while developing reproducible digital methodologies for psychoanalytic research. The requested resources are critical given the need for GPU-accelerated NLP pipelines, distributed memory architectures for large-scale simulations, and secure data handling compliant with clinical confidentiality standards. Results will directly inform evidence-based refinements to psychotherapeutic training protocols and outcome monitoring systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the provision of psychoanalytic counseling to individuals and groups based on the psychodynamic principles evolved from authorities such as Freud, Adler, and Jung. Includes instruction in self-analysis, personality theory, dream analysis, free association and transference theory and techniques, psychodynamic theory, developmental processes, applications to specific clinical conditions, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Anatomic pathology is increasingly reliant on the integration of multimodal data—including high-resolution histopathological images, genomic profiles, and clinical metadata—to improve diagnostic precision and uncover molecular mechanisms of disease. However, the computational demands of processing and analyzing these large, heterogeneous datasets present a critical bottleneck. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable scalable, AI-driven analysis of whole-slide imaging (WSI) datasets paired with multi-omics data, with the goal of identifying novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for solid tumors. The primary research challenge lies in the complexity of correlating spatially resolved tissue features (e.g., tumor morphology, immune cell infiltration) with molecular alterations (e.g., mutations, gene expression) across thousands of patient samples. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline leveraging deep learning architectures (e.g., vision transformers, graph neural networks) to process gigapixel WSIs, coupled with integrative clustering methods to map histopathologic patterns to genomic subtypes. HPC resources will be essential for training these models on distributed GPU nodes, performing hyperparameter optimization at scale, and conducting genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across multi-institutional cohorts. Additionally, we will develop a cloud-based platform to facilitate collaborative annotation and federated learning, ensuring data privacy compliance. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms for automated detection of rare anatomic abnormalities, (2) a publicly accessible repository of annotated WSI-omics datasets, and (3) predictive models linking spatial tumor heterogeneity to therapeutic resistance. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in surgical pathology, reduce inter-observer variability, and provide clinicians with actionable tools for personalized treatment stratification. By harnessing HPC capabilities, the project aims to bridge the gap between computational pathology research and clinical translation, ultimately advancing precision medicine in oncology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis of disease and anatomic abnormalities. Includes instruction in autopsy pathology, cytology, diagnostic surgical pathology, forensic medicine, laboratory management, and quality control.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in pharmacy operations and medication safety, with a focus on optimizing workflows and enhancing predictive models for adverse drug interactions. Pharmacy technicians and assistants play a vital role in medication dispensing, inventory management, and patient education, yet current computational tools for analyzing large-scale drug interaction datasets or simulating pharmacy workflows remain underdeveloped. The research problem centers on the need for robust, scalable methods to process real-world data from electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacy management systems, and drug databases to improve decision-making in dynamic clinical environments. Using HPC capabilities, we will develop machine learning models to predict high-risk drug combinations and patient-specific adherence patterns, integrating variables such as comorbidities, polypharmacy, and demographic factors. Parallelized simulations will model pharmacy workflow efficiency under varying demand scenarios, including peak hours and supply chain disruptions, to identify bottlenecks and inform staffing or inventory strategies. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will assess physicochemical stability of compounded medications under diverse storage conditions, supporting quality control. The computational approach will employ distributed computing frameworks (e.g., Apache Spark) for data preprocessing, graph neural networks to map drug interaction networks, and agent-based models for workflow simulations. Outcomes will include open-source tools for predicting medication-related risks, actionable insights for optimizing pharmacy operational protocols, and validated stability profiles for common compounded preparations. This work will directly enhance the safety and efficiency of pharmacy practices while providing training resources for pharmacy technicians in data-driven decision support systems. By bridging computational innovation with practical pharmacy operations, the project aims to reduce preventable medication errors and contribute to scalable solutions for evolving healthcare demands.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pharmacists, to prepare medications, provide medications and related assistance to patients, and manage pharmacy clinical and business operations. Includes instruction in medical and pharmaceutical terminology, principles of pharmacology and pharmaceutics, drug identification, pharmacy laboratory procedures, prescription interpretation, patient communication and education, safety procedures, record-keeping, measurement and testing techniques, pharmacy business operations, prescription preparation, logistics and dispensing operations, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: The development and dysfunction of neural circuits are central to understanding neurological disorders such as epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, and neurodevelopmental conditions. However, current experimental techniques face limitations in resolving the multiscale dynamics of neuronal networks, particularly in capturing how molecular and cellular interactions scale to circuit-level activity. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the functional connectivity and signaling dynamics of cortical and subcortical circuits under healthy and pathological states. We will focus on integrating empirical data from electrophysiological recordings, synaptic ultrastructure, and neurotransmitter receptor distributions to construct biophysically realistic simulations of neural networks. These models will simulate activity patterns across spatial scales—from individual synapses to macroscale network oscillations—using parallelized, compartmentalized neuron models and adaptive mesh refinement techniques. A key objective is to identify how perturbations in ion channel kinetics, synaptic plasticity rules, or glial interactions contribute to aberrant circuit behaviors observed in disease. Computational workflows will include parameter optimization via genetic algorithms, sensitivity analyses to pinpoint critical control points in network stability, and machine learning-driven classification of pathological activity signatures. The scale of these simulations (spanning millions of neurons with subcellular resolution) necessitates HPC resources for memory-intensive tasks and distributed processing of stochastic differential equations. Expected outcomes include predictive models of circuit dysfunction mechanisms in temporal lobe epilepsy and hypotheses for targeted neuromodulation strategies. By bridging molecular, cellular, and systems-level data, this work will advance the neuroanatomical basis of circuitopathies and provide a computational framework for testing therapeutic interventions in silico. The requested allocation will directly support the generation of open-access tools for simulating disease-relevant neural networks, fostering collaboration across experimental and computational neuroscience communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular studies of neuronal and glial cells and circuits, neural transmitters and receptors, neuronal signaling processes, membrane and synapse structure and communication, autonomic function, nervous system circuitry and mapping, and anatomical and functional basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project proposes the development of an interactive computational platform to explore emergent aesthetic forms through large-scale generative simulations, bridging digital methodologies with traditional studio art practices. Contemporary visual artists increasingly integrate algorithmic and data-driven processes into their work, yet existing tools often limit complexity due to computational constraints, hindering experimentation with dynamic, multi-layered systems. This research addresses this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate intricate interactions between procedural generation, real-time sensor input, and artist-guided parameters. The computational framework will employ agent-based models to simulate self-organizing patterns, neural style transfer algorithms to hybridize artistic techniques, and fluid dynamics simulations to iteratively refine digital-physical hybrids, such as 3D-printed sculptures informed by virtual erosion processes. By parallelizing these resource-intensive tasks across GPU clusters, the platform will enable artists to manipulate high-resolution datasets (e.g., 4D scanned material textures, environmental sensor feeds) while maintaining interactive creative workflows. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible suite of optimized tools for generative art creation, a corpus of computational artworks demonstrating HPC-enabled scale and complexity, and a methodological framework for evaluating computational aesthetics across cultural contexts. This work aims to redefine the technical and conceptual possibilities of studio art practice, fostering new dialogues between computational granularity and artistic intentionality. The resource allocation will directly support rendering neural radiance fields for immersive installations, training custom diffusion models on historical art corpora, and simulating multi-agent systems that respond to real-world gallery conditions, thereby advancing interdisciplinary research at the nexus of visual art, media theory, and high-performance computing.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally function as creative artists in the visual and plastic media. Includes instruction in the traditional fine arts media (drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, CAD/CAM) and/or modern media (ceramics, textiles, intermedia, photography, digital images), theory of art, color theory, composition and perspective, anatomy, the techniques and procedures for maintaining equipment and managing a studio, and art portfolio marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrative framework for modeling cross-domain interactions between ecological dynamics and public health outcomes, using machine learning (ML) and network science. The research addresses a critical gap in current predictive systems, which often treat environmental, biological, and epidemiological processes in isolation, despite their inherent interdependencies. We propose a novel computational approach that combines graph neural networks (GNNs) with multi-modal data assimilation to analyze heterogeneous datasets—including satellite-derived land-use patterns, species migration trajectories, and anonymized human health records—while preserving privacy constraints. The methodology integrates dynamic network representations to map habitat fragmentation, species interaction shifts, and pathogen spillover risks under climate change scenarios. A key innovation is the use of contrastive learning to align temporally mismatched ecological and health data streams, enabling the detection of latent correlations between environmental drivers and emergent disease hotspots. Computational challenges include scaling GNN training to handle billion-edge graphs representing species mobility and optimizing Bayesian uncertainty quantification for high-dimensional, sparse observational data. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated libraries for large-scale matrix operations and distributed training across nodes to manage memory-intensive tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible toolkit for simulating cross-domain ecological-health cascades, (2) predictive models identifying high-risk zones for zoonotic disease emergence, and (3) novel metrics quantifying network resilience to environmental perturbations. By unifying ecological and epidemiological modeling through advanced ML, this work aims to provide policymakers with actionable insights for preemptive health interventions and biodiversity conservation strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing petabyte-scale environmental datasets and achieving the temporal resolution required to capture rapid ecological transitions linked to public health crises.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of data mining and machine learning. Includes instruction in naive Bayes rule, artificial neural networks, genetic algorithms, decision tree learning, neural nets, network science, optimization, statistical computing, and graphical models and methods.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex dermatological conditions in companion animals, such as canine atopic dermatitis, feline autoimmune skin disorders, and multi-drug-resistant cutaneous infections, demands advanced approaches to understand disease mechanisms and optimize therapies. Current clinical research faces challenges in integrating multi-modal data—including genomic, histopathological, microbiome, and environmental variables—to predict treatment outcomes or identify molecular targets. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model host-microbe interactions, immune responses, and genetic predispositions in veterinary dermatology. We will develop machine learning pipelines to analyze heterogeneous datasets from 1,200 clinical cases (retrospective and prospective) encompassing skin transcriptomics, 16S/ITS microbiome sequencing, and longitudinal treatment records. Agent-based models will simulate epidermal barrier dysfunction and inflammatory cascades under varying therapeutic regimens, while molecular dynamics simulations will explore ligand-receptor interactions in allergic pathways. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle high-dimensional data and stochastic modeling scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive biomarkers for treatment resistance, in silico screening of novel topical therapeutics, and personalized intervention strategies for refractory cases. By establishing scalable models of cutaneous immunobiology, this work aims to reduce reliance on iterative in vivo trials and accelerate translational insights. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of multi-scale simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, particularly for parameter-space explorations of complex systems such as biofilm-mediated infections. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for veterinary researchers, fostering collaborative innovation in dermatologic care. This project bridges clinical veterinary medicine and computational systems biology, addressing critical gaps in precision dermatology while advancing methodological paradigms for analyzing animal health data.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize veterinary office operations through advanced computational modeling, addressing inefficiencies in resource allocation, client scheduling, and regulatory compliance—a critical challenge for clinics balancing high caseloads with complex administrative demands. Veterinary practices operate in dynamic environments where unpredictable variables (e.g., emergency cases, client no-shows, supply chain delays) disrupt workflows, yet existing management tools lack the predictive power to adapt proactively. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose developing an agent-based simulation framework to model clinic operations at scale, integrating real-world data on appointment patterns, staff workflows, inventory turnover, and regulatory constraints. The model will simulate scenarios such as surge capacity planning, staff-to-patient ratio optimization, and compliance risk assessment under varying conditions. Machine learning components will analyze historical clinic data to predict no-show probabilities, seasonal demand fluctuations, and supply usage trends, refining the simulation’s accuracy. By parallelizing these computations across HPC nodes, the project will achieve the processing speed necessary for real-time adaptive decision support—a capability unattainable with conventional software. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for veterinary administrators to test operational strategies virtually, reducing trial-and-error inefficiencies. This research fills a gap in non-scientific computational applications by translating HPC methodologies to veterinary administration, an underserved domain with direct impacts on animal healthcare accessibility. The project also establishes a framework for applying computational resource optimization techniques to other specialized service sectors, bridging a critical divide between technical infrastructure and niche administrative needs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a veterinary office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, veterinary care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and model the long-term preservation risks of digital cultural heritage materials, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability challenges inherent in large-scale archival ecosystems. As libraries and archives increasingly steward born-digital and digitized collections—spanning text, multimedia, and complex digital artifacts—existing preservation strategies struggle to dynamically assess risks across heterogeneous formats, dependencies, and evolving technological environments. The research problem centers on the absence of predictive, data-driven models capable of simulating degradation scenarios, format obsolescence, and metadata decay at the scale of modern digital repositories. Using a combination of graph neural networks (GNNs) and agent-based simulations, the project will map interdependencies within digital objects (e.g., software-hardware linkages, format compatibility networks) and model temporal decay patterns under varying preservation strategies. HPC resources will enable the processing of petabyte-scale metadata datasets from partner institutions, training machine learning models on historical preservation failure cases, and simulating multi-decadal preservation outcomes across diverse scenarios. Expected outcomes include a risk prioritization toolkit for archivists, optimized workflow recommendations for at-risk collections, and benchmarks for emulation-based preservation strategies. By integrating computational scalability with archival theory, this work aims to advance adaptive preservation frameworks that balance resource allocation, accessibility, and fidelity in digital stewardship. The project’s computational outputs will be released as open-source modules compatible with existing digital repository platforms, ensuring direct applicability to library and information science practice. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between data science, digital humanities, and archival studies, offering a novel methodology to safeguard cultural memory in an era of accelerating technological change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the knowledge and skills required to develop, organize, store, retrieve, administer, and facilitate the use of local, remote, and networked collections of information in print, audiovisual, and electronic formats and that prepares individuals for professional service as librarians and information consultants.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the sociocultural dynamics influencing the success of church planting initiatives in rapidly urbanizing contexts. While church planting programs traditionally rely on qualitative missiological frameworks, this study addresses a critical gap: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to predict how demographic shifts, urban infrastructure development, and localized social networks intersect with theological strategies to shape congregational viability. By integrating computational social science methods with mission-oriented theology, the project will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating population mobility, cultural assimilation patterns, and resource allocation scenarios across diverse urban environments. These models will be parameterized using mixed-method data, including geospatial records, census microdata, and ethnographic interviews from active church planting networks in three megacities. A key innovation involves applying natural language processing (NLP) to analyze historical denominational archives and contemporary mission reports, identifying latent correlations between theological discourse patterns and community resilience metrics. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities to manage large-scale Monte Carlo simulations testing over 10,000 scenario permutations, as well as training transformer-based NLP models on unstructured theological texts. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive toolkit for optimizing church planting site selection and strategy adaptation, validated through partnerships with denominational planting agencies. By bridging computational modeling and practical theology, this interdisciplinary work advances scholarly understanding of religious community formation in complex urban systems while providing actionable insights for faith-based social infrastructure development. The project’s computational architecture will also establish a replicable framework for analyzing emergent collective behaviors in other understudied religious movements.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to establish congregations of Christians in new locations. Includes instruction in models of church planting, church multiplication strategies, church leadership, evangelism, missiology, Christian ethics, and mission-oriented theology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of neuroimaging data and the demand for precision in diagnosing neurological disorders necessitate advanced computational tools to uncover subtle patterns in large-scale datasets. Current clinical neuroradiology workflows rely on qualitative assessments of structural and functional imaging, which may overlook critical biomarkers in conditions such as neurodegenerative diseases, small-vessel ischemia, and neuroinflammatory disorders. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a machine learning framework to analyze multi-modal neuroimaging data—including high-resolution MRI, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and perfusion-weighted sequences—to identify quantitative imaging signatures predictive of pathology. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on a multi-institutional dataset of 10,000 annotated clinical brain and spine studies, integrating heterogeneous data formats and correcting for scanner-specific biases. Computational workflows will be optimized for GPU-accelerated preprocessing, including skull stripping, motion correction, and spatial normalization, followed by ensemble modeling to classify lesions, quantify microstructural damage, and predict disease progression. A secondary aim involves simulating the hemodynamic impact of vascular anomalies using finite element modeling on patient-specific 3D angiographic reconstructions. The scale of data processing—terabytes of imaging data, millions of voxel-wise features, and iterative model training—requires the parallelized storage, memory, and processing capabilities unique to HPC environments. Successful implementation will yield validated algorithms for automated lesion detection, prognostication tools for multiple sclerosis and cerebral small-vessel disease, and open-source pipelines for reproducible analysis. These outcomes aim to enhance diagnostic accuracy, reduce interobserver variability, and enable earlier intervention in neurological care. By integrating computational neuroscience with clinical neuroradiology, this work will establish a scalable infrastructure for data-driven discovery, directly advancing the translation of quantitative imaging biomarkers into routine practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the brain, spine, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, and head and neck in adults and children.

abstract: The development of biopharmaceuticals involves complex challenges in optimizing production processes, ensuring quality control, and accelerating time-to-market while adhering to stringent regulatory standards. A critical bottleneck lies in predicting and validating the stability, bioavailability, and manufacturability of novel drug candidates, particularly biologics such as monoclonal antibodies and recombinant proteins. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and time-consuming, necessitating advanced computational methods to streamline development. This project proposes the integration of high-performance computing (HPC) to model molecular interactions, simulate large-scale bioprocess workflows, and analyze multi-omics datasets for industrial drug development. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will be employed to study protein-ligand binding affinities, aggregation tendencies, and formulation stability under varied physicochemical conditions. Parallelized genome-scale metabolic models will predict microbial host behavior in bioreactor environments, optimizing yield and purity for recombinant protein synthesis. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on heterogeneous datasets—including structural biology data, pharmacokinetic profiles, and historical manufacturing metrics—to identify predictive signatures of drug efficacy and scalability. The computational workflow will leverage containerized pipelines for reproducibility and integrate with existing laboratory information management systems (LIMS) to enable real-time data exchange. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the high dimensionality of these datasets, execute computationally intensive simulations, and validate models against experimental benchmarks. Expected outcomes include a reduction in late-stage clinical attrition rates, improved bioprocess efficiency through in silico design-of-experiments (DoE) optimization, and the establishment of open-source computational tools for quality-by-design (QbD) frameworks. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on bridging pharmaceutical science and industrial management by enabling data-driven decision-making across the drug development lifecycle, ultimately contributing to safer, more affordable therapies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific application of pharmacology, pharmaceutics, and industrial management to the development, production, marketing, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. Includes instruction in industrial microbiology, plasmids, expression vectors, protein chemistry, assay and evaluation, drug synthesis and purification, quality control, industrial management, production security, patent procedures, intellectual property regulations and issues, patent enforcement and defense, and research design and testing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of morphological and syntactic structures in Classical Sanskrit and Prakrit texts, with a focus on understudied post-Vedic works. A central challenge in analyzing these languages lies in their complex agglutinative morphology, irregular sandhi (phonetic merging) rules, and context-dependent syntactic variations, which complicate automated parsing and semantic modeling. Existing digital tools for Indo-Aryan languages remain limited in scope, often relying on manual intervention or rule-based systems that struggle with ambiguities in poetic and philosophical texts. To address this, we propose developing a hybrid machine learning framework integrating transformer-based language models with probabilistic morphological analyzers, trained on a curated corpus of digitized manuscripts from the Gupta and post-Gupta periods. The computational pipeline will include tokenization optimized for compound word decomposition, context-aware sandhi resolution using sequence-to-sequence models, and syntactic dependency parsing trained on manually annotated śāstric prose. HPC resources are critical for scaling model training across diverse textual genres (kāvya, śāstra, inscriptions) and iteratively refining hyperparameters to balance linguistic accuracy with computational efficiency. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated analysis of Classical Sanskrit-Prakrit hybrid texts, a diachronic dataset tracking syntactic shifts between 500 BCE–1000 CE, and quantitative insights into the influence of Dravidian substrate languages on Middle Indo-Aryan morphosyntax. This work will provide scholars with scalable methods to interrogate under-explored corpora, enabling large-scale comparative studies of literary, grammatical, and epigraphic traditions while reducing reliance on fragmentary manual analyses. The project bridges computational linguistics and classical philology, offering new methodologies for preserving and interpreting South Asia’s linguistic heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Sanskrit and Classical Indian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Sanskrit and related ancient and classical Indo-Aryan languages. Includes instruction in Vedic and Classical Sanskrit, Pali and other Prakrits, and the historical development of Indo-Aryan languages and their relation to Indo-European languages such as Greek, Latin and the Baltic languages.

abstract: Urban forests are critical for mitigating climate change, enhancing biodiversity, and improving public health, yet their management is challenged by dynamic interactions between biological systems, environmental stressors, and human activity. Current models struggle to predict species resilience, pest spread, or growth patterns under urban microclimates due to the computational complexity of simulating fine-scale ecological processes across heterogeneous landscapes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop spatially explicit, multi-agent models that integrate tree physiology, soil dynamics, pest behavior, and climate projections at city-wide scales. By coupling agent-based modeling with machine learning algorithms trained on remote sensing data (e.g., LiDAR, hyperspectral imagery), the research will simulate how diverse tree species and management strategies respond to stressors like heat islands, pollution gradients, and invasive pests. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of urban forest networks, parameterized with field data from municipal tree inventories and sensor networks, to quantify trade-offs between planting strategies, maintenance protocols, and ecosystem service outcomes. The computational framework will also incorporate stochastic climate scenarios to evaluate long-term resilience under varying policy interventions. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for optimizing species selection, canopy cover targets, and pest mitigation protocols tailored to specific urban zones. The models will directly inform municipal forestry plans, helping prioritize resource allocation for climate adaptation while quantifying carbon sequestration and air purification benefits. This work addresses a critical gap in urban forestry tools by bridging ecological theory with scalable computational methods, ultimately supporting cities in transforming green infrastructure planning from reactive to predictive.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of forestry and related sciences to the development, care, and maintenance of individual trees and forested areas within or close to areas of dense human habitation. Includes instruction in urban environments; effects of pollution on tree species; environmental design and landscaping; urban pest infestation; urban forest management; and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic evolution of visual symbolism within global digital media ecosystems, an understudied area at the intersection of cultural studies, digital anthropology, and computational analysis. While traditional humanities scholarship has examined symbolic communication within specific cultural contexts, the rapid proliferation of digital platforms has generated vast, interconnected visual datasets that transcend geographic and temporal boundaries. This research addresses the challenge of mapping and analyzing these complex, large-scale patterns to uncover how visual symbols emerge, mutate, and propagate across diverse online communities. The computational methodology employs deep learning architectures, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to detect and classify recurrent visual motifs across a curated corpus of 15 million images from social media platforms, digital art repositories, and collaborative wikis spanning 2010-2023. Temporal network analysis will track symbol diffusion pathways, while transformer-based models will analyze associated multilingual textual metadata to contextualize semantic shifts. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing high-resolution image data, training multimodal models, and simulating cultural transmission dynamics through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel taxonomy of digital visual symbology, 2) quantitative frameworks for measuring cross-cultural influence in digital aesthetics, and 3) open-source tools for temporal pattern detection in cultural datasets. This work will establish computational foundations for studying digital visual culture at scale while preserving humanistic interpretive rigor, offering new methodologies for understanding how globalization and technological mediation shape contemporary symbolic communication. The resource-intensive nature of processing heterogeneous multimedia data and maintaining temporal-spatial analyses across petabytes of information necessitates the requested computing infrastructure to achieve statistically robust, culturally nuanced insights.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any single instructional program in liberal arts and sciences, general studies and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Healthcare environments significantly influence patient recovery, staff efficiency, and operational outcomes, yet current design practices rely on static post-occupancy evaluations and simplified simulations that inadequately capture the dynamic interplay of spatial, sensory, and behavioral variables.
