This research will contribute to the field of applied and professional ethics by providing a novel, evidence-based methodology for evaluating ethical challenges, thereby supporting policymakers, ethics committees, and professionals in making informed, ethically robust decisions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of ethical issues in the workplace and public life, and the application of ethical decision-making to the practical problems of society and the professions. Includes instruction in ethical theory; history of ethics; contemporary social dilemmas; methods in applied ethics; and applications including medical ethics, legal ethics, business ethics, environmental ethics, and criminal justice ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of biomechanical efficiency in elite athletes through the integration of motion capture data, musculoskeletal modeling, and machine learning. While traditional sports science relies on generalized training frameworks, this research addresses the critical gap in personalized, real-time biomechanical optimization by developing computational models that adapt to individual physiological and kinematic variability. The core challenge lies in processing high-dimensional datasets—including 3D motion trajectories, electromyography signals, and force plate measurements—to simulate and predict performance outcomes under dynamic conditions. Current methods lack the scalability to handle the nonlinear interactions between biomechanical variables, limiting their utility in practical training environments. To overcome this, the project will employ a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate athlete-environment interactions and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to identify latent patterns in temporal data. These models will be trained on a curated dataset spanning 500+ athlete profiles across diverse sports, enabling the identification of individualized "performance signatures." The HPC infrastructure is essential for parallelizing ABM simulations across thousands of scenarios, optimizing hyperparameters for RNN architectures, and conducting sensitivity analyses on biomechanical risk factors. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive framework for injury prevention and a real-time feedback system prototype that adjusts training loads based on computational insights. By bridging sports science with advanced computing, this work will establish a foundation for data-driven precision coaching while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional STEM domains. The results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for sports analytics communities and partnerships with athletic training organizations.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Sports, Kinesiology, and Physical Education/ Fitness, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sports, kinesiology, and physical education/fitness, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Geothermal energy systems represent a critical component of renewable energy infrastructure, yet their efficient design and operation are hindered by complex subsurface interactions that challenge existing computational models. This project seeks to address the limitations of current geothermal reservoir simulations, which often oversimplify multiphase fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and rock-mechanical responses, leading to suboptimal system performance and increased operational risks. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to develop high-fidelity, three-dimensional models that integrate coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational approach will utilize finite element methods and parallelized solvers to simulate fluid flow through fractured geothermal reservoirs, accounting for heterogeneous rock properties, dynamic fracture networks, and reactive transport phenomena. Machine learning techniques will be employed to calibrate model parameters against field data from existing geothermal sites, enhancing predictive accuracy. The proposed simulations will enable the evaluation of enhanced geothermal system (EGS) configurations under varying operational scenarios, optimizing energy extraction rates while mitigating risks of reservoir depletion or induced seismicity. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for designing cost-effective geothermal installations, reducing exploration uncertainty, and extending reservoir lifespans. By advancing the precision of geothermal resource assessment and system management tools, this research directly supports the deployment of scalable, sustainable geothermal energy technologies. Access to HPC resources is essential to handle the computational intensity of multiphysics simulations, which require iterative solving of nonlinear equations across millions of grid cells. The results will inform industry best practices and contribute to academic curricula in geothermal engineering technologies, bridging the gap between theoretical models and real-world applications in renewable energy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and decentralized generation into electrical power systems has introduced unprecedented complexity in maintaining grid stability and operational efficiency. Traditional power plant control strategies, optimized for centralized fossil fuel or nuclear generation, struggle to adapt to the dynamic, nonlinear interactions introduced by variable renewable inputs, distributed energy resources, and bidirectional power flows. This project seeks to develop an adaptive, AI-driven control framework for hybrid power plant systems that harmonize conventional generation assets with renewable sources while ensuring compliance with evolving grid code requirements. The research will employ high-fidelity, multi-timescale simulations integrating electromagnetic transient (EMT) models of power electronics interfaces, transient stability analyses of synchronous generators, and reinforcement learning algorithms for real-time decision-making. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve the computational burden of parallelized Monte Carlo simulations assessing thousands of operational scenarios, including extreme weather events, fault conditions, and stochastic renewable generation profiles. Key innovations include a heterogeneous computing architecture coupling finite-element method solvers for equipment-level stress analysis with system-wide optimal power flow calculations, enabled by GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed memory parallelism. Expected outcomes include validated control protocols for inertia emulation in low-carbon hybrid plants, predictive maintenance models based on equipment degradation patterns under fluctuating loads, and open-source tools for resilience-aware power plant design. This work directly addresses the operational challenges of deep decarbonization in the energy sector, providing actionable insights for utilities navigating the transition to net-zero power systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan electrical systems and modify existing electrical systems that generate and use large amounts of electricity required for distribution networks that are economical, safe, and functional. Includes instruction in alternative/renewable energy systems; calculus; circuit analysis; electrical power systems and industry practices; electrical system design; microprocessor architecture; motor control systems; power electronics operation, planning and protection; programmable logic controllers; and project management.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the optimization of corporate communication strategies through advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques, with a focus on enhancing the alignment of organizational messaging with stakeholder expectations across cultural and linguistic boundaries. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies in current communication workflows, where manual processes for drafting, editing, and tailoring content for diverse audiences often lead to delays, inconsistent messaging, and misalignment with stakeholder sentiment. Existing tools lack the capacity to dynamically model the interplay between linguistic nuance, cultural context, and organizational objectives at scale. To address this gap, the project proposes developing a computational framework that integrates transformer-based language models, sentiment analysis, and cross-cultural semantic mapping. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train and fine-tune models on multilingual corpora of corporate communications (e.g., press releases, internal memos, social media content) and stakeholder feedback data, while simulating real-time adaptation scenarios. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of heterogeneous text datasets, hyperparameter optimization for domain-specific language models, and probabilistic modeling of communication impact across stakeholder networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source toolkit for automated analysis and generation of context-aware business communications, (2) quantitative metrics for evaluating cross-cultural message efficacy, and (3) evidence-based frameworks for adaptive communication strategy design. The research will contribute to emerging interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of computational linguistics, stakeholder theory, and organizational behavior, while providing practical tools to reduce operational friction in global corporate communications. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to overcome scalability limitations in current NLP applications, enabling organizations to proactively address communication challenges in fast-evolving business environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the cultural and social dynamics of Francophone minority communities in Canada outside Québec, with a focus on New Brunswick and Ontario. The study addresses the challenge of understanding how geographically dispersed linguistic minorities sustain cultural identity amid globalization, technological change, and shifting demographics. Traditional qualitative methods in regional studies struggle to synthesize large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—including multilingual archival records, contemporary social media, geospatial data, and oral history transcripts—into cohesive analyses of cultural resilience. The project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), geospatial network modeling, and machine learning to identify patterns in language use, cultural transmission, and community connectivity across temporal and spatial scales. NLP pipelines will process terabytes of digitized newspapers, government documents, and public social media posts in French and English, detecting shifts in linguistic practices and thematic priorities. Geospatial algorithms will map historical migration routes, institutional networks, and event participation to quantify community cohesion. Transformer-based models will analyze oral history interviews to correlate self-reported identity markers with external sociocultural drivers. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration to manage complex data integration and model training. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for analyzing cultural sustainability in regional minorities, open-access tools for interdisciplinary regional studies, and new insights into policy-independent strategies for identity preservation. The research will contribute to methodological innovation in digital humanities within area studies, offering a model for computationally aided investigations of regional identity that prioritize community-engaged scholarship without reliance on demographic or economic metrics. Results will be disseminated through public dashboards visualizing cultural dynamics and peer-reviewed publications on the computational methodology.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the defined geographic subregions and subcultures within modern and historical countries and societies. Includes such topics as Acadian Studies, French Canadian and Quebec Studies, Southern (U.S.) Studies, New England Studies, Southwestern Studies, Northern Studies, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize enzyme functionality in non-aqueous industrial solvents, a critical challenge in sustainable biomanufacturing. While enzymes are widely used as biocatalysts in green chemistry, their instability and reduced activity in organic solvents limit scalability and cost-effectiveness. Traditional experimental approaches to engineer solvent-resistant enzymes are resource-intensive and lack predictive power for diverse solvent environments. To address this, we propose an integrated computational strategy combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML), and evolutionary algorithms to model enzyme-solvent interactions and predict structural modifications that enhance stability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate enzyme conformations across a range of solvent conditions (e.g., ionic liquids, hydrocarbons) at microsecond timescales, generating datasets on free energy landscapes, solvent accessibility, and residue flexibility. These data will train ML models to identify solvent-tolerant structural motifs and guide in silico mutagenesis. Evolutionary algorithms will then iteratively optimize enzyme designs for target solvent systems. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform for rational enzyme engineering, validated through experimental partnerships, and a curated database of solvent-adaptive enzyme variants. This work bridges biophysics, synthetic biology, and industrial biotechnology, offering a transformative tool to advance solvent-based biocatalysis for applications such as biofuel production, polymer synthesis, and pharmaceutical intermediates. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, the project aims to accelerate the development of robust industrial enzymes, lowering energy costs and enabling novel bio-based manufacturing pathways.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences, biochemistry, and genetics to the preparation of new and enhanced agricultural, environmental, clinical, and industrial products, including the commercial exploitation of microbes, plants, and animals. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, gene identification, phylogenetics and comparative genomics, bioinorganic chemistry, immunoassaying, DNA sequencing, xenotransplantation, genetic engineering, industrial microbiology, drug and biologic development, enzyme-based production processes, patent law, biotechnology management and marketing, applicable regulations, and biotechnology ethics.

abstract: Hemodialysis efficacy relies on precise management of fluid dynamics and solute transport across semipermeable membranes, yet current empirical methods for optimizing treatment parameters remain suboptimal due to the complex interplay of patient-specific physiologic variables. This project proposes a computational framework to model multi-physics interactions during hemodialysis, integrating patient hemodynamic data, membrane material properties, and solute kinetics to predict treatment outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to simulate blood and dialysate flow patterns, shear stress effects on erythrocyte integrity, and dynamic solute clearance rates under variable treatment scenarios (e.g., dialyzer geometry, flow rates, anticoagulant dosing). Patient-specific models will be developed using anonymized clinical datasets from renal therapy centers, including hematocrit, albumin levels, and vascular access characteristics. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational cost by identifying dominant parameters influencing urea, phosphate, and β2-microglobulin clearance efficiency. The simulations will validate hypotheses regarding the impact of pulsatile flow modulation on intradialytic hypotension risk and filter clotting frequency—two major barriers to treatment adherence. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for dialysis technologists to virtually test operational protocols, optimize dialyzer reprocessing workflows, and personalize fluid removal rates. By bridging gaps between clinical practice and computational biophysics, this work advances precision nephrology technology while establishing a paradigm for HPC-driven optimization of extracorporeal therapies. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated finite element modeling, large-scale parameter sweeps, and AI training pipelines to address latency challenges in real-time predictive analytics for dialysis systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer hemodialysis treatments to patients with renal failure under the supervision of a nurse or physician. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, dialysis prescription interpretation, dialysate preparation, extracorporeal circuit and dialyzer set-up and maintenance, equipment monitoring, patient preparation, taking vital signs, documentation and communication, venipuncture and local anesthesia administration, emergency intervention, safety and sanitation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in forensic DNA mixture analysis, where current computational methods struggle to resolve complex biological samples containing genetic material from multiple contributors, particularly in cases involving degraded DNA or low-template quantities. Such limitations hinder the accuracy of forensic conclusions, impacting criminal investigations and judicial decisions. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy advanced probabilistic genotyping algorithms optimized for scalability and precision. The computational approach will integrate machine learning techniques with Bayesian statistical models to deconvolute DNA mixtures, accounting for stochastic artifacts, allele dropout, and environmental degradation factors. By parallelizing computationally intensive tasks—such as likelihood ratio calculations across millions of genotype combinations—HPC resources will enable rapid analysis of large-scale forensic datasets, including whole-genome sequencing data and population-specific allele frequency databases. The project will validate the framework using both simulated mixtures and real-world casework samples from active forensic investigations, ensuring robustness across diverse scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolset for forensic laboratories, significantly reducing turnaround times and improving the reliability of DNA evidence interpretation. This work directly supports homeland security priorities by enhancing the accuracy of suspect identification and reducing risks of wrongful convictions, thereby strengthening the integrity of forensic science in legal systems. The proposed HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the exponential growth in computational demand associated with high-resolution genomic data and complex modeling, ensuring this project’s alignment with next-generation forensic standards.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the physical, biomedical, and social sciences to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence, human testimony and criminal suspects. Includes instruction in forensic medicine, forensic dentistry, anthropology, psychology, entomology, pathology, forensic laboratory technology and autopsy procedures, DNA and blood pattern analysis, crime scene analysis, crime scene photography, fingerprint technology, document analysis, witness and suspect examination procedures, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of community resilience and spiritual engagement in underserved urban environments. While urban ministry has historically relied on qualitative and ethnographic methods, this study pioneers a computational approach to model how socio-spiritual interventions influence community networks over time. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to evaluate the longitudinal impact of ministry programs—such as neighborhood outreach, crisis counseling, and interfaith collaboration—on social cohesion and collective agency in rapidly gentrifying urban areas. Using anonymized demographic data, geospatial records, and anonymized textual archives from partner organizations, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between residents, religious institutions, and municipal systems. Machine learning techniques, including natural language processing (NLP), will be applied to historical sermon texts, community meeting transcripts, and social media artifacts to identify patterns in how theological narratives adapt to shifting urban stressors. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale ABM iterations and training transformer-based models on heterogeneous datasets, enabling the team to test hypotheses about intervention scalability and cultural contextualization. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital toolkit for ministry leaders to visualize potential ripple effects of programmatic decisions and a peer-reviewed framework for quantifying spiritual capital in urban policy contexts. By integrating computational social science with theological ethics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based urban ministry while contributing interdisciplinary methods to the digital humanities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to individuals and groups in urban communities. Includes instruction in bible study and theology, pastoral leadership and care, urban structure and context, inner city ministry, counseling ministries, family studies, homiletics, social ethics, and community organizing.

abstract: Secondary school administrators face complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation, policy implementation, and operational decision-making to meet diverse student needs while adhering to budgetary and ethical constraints. Traditional administrative strategies often rely on static models or qualitative assessments, which may fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating enrollment, evolving safety risks, and the heterogeneous academic and social-emotional needs of adolescents. This project proposes the development of an adaptive, data-driven decision-support framework for secondary school administration, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-factorial scenarios and simulate outcomes. The research will integrate anonymized longitudinal datasets from school districts (e.g., enrollment patterns, disciplinary records, academic performance metrics, and facility utilization logs) with computational models including agent-based simulations to evaluate the cascading effects of administrative decisions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive patterns in student outcomes under varying resource allocation strategies, while optimization algorithms will assess trade-offs between competing priorities such as budget constraints, staffing ratios, and equity goals. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of data (spanning 10+ years from 50+ schools), the complexity of simulating thousands of interdependent variables, and the need for real-time sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for administrators to (1) forecast the impacts of scheduling changes, facility investments, or safety protocols; (2) optimize staff deployment during crises; and (3) ethically balance resource distribution across student subgroups. By translating HPC-driven insights into actionable administrative strategies, this project aims to enhance operational efficiency, equity, and student support in secondary schools while establishing a novel computational paradigm for education leadership research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the junior high, secondary, or senior high school (7-12) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of secondary schools. Includes instruction in secondary school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of understanding drug resistance mechanisms in G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), a major obstacle in the development of targeted therapies for cardiovascular and neurological disorders. GPCRs exhibit complex, dynamic conformational changes upon ligand binding, and mutations or allosteric modulators can alter these dynamics, leading to reduced drug efficacy. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve the transient structural states and energetic landscapes underlying resistance. We propose to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and free energy calculations, capturing the full spectrum of GPCR conformational states and their interactions with ligands under resistance-inducing conditions. Simulations will integrate cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography data from collaborators to parameterize systems representing wild-type and mutant receptors bound to both therapeutic agonists and resistance-associated small molecules. Markov state models will be constructed to identify metastable states linked to impaired drug binding or signaling. Additionally, alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) methods will quantify how resistance mutations alter binding affinities across ligand classes. These computational insights will guide the design of novel ligands with enhanced resilience to mutation-driven resistance, which will be validated through collaborative functional assays. The HPC scale required—millions of core-hours for multi-microsecond simulations across mutant systems—exceeds local cluster capabilities. Success will provide a mechanistic framework to predict resistance trajectories in GPCR-targeted drugs and accelerate the development of adaptive therapeutic strategies, directly addressing unmet needs in precision pharmacology. This work aligns with the Molecular Pharmacology program’s focus on drug-receptor interactions and therapeutic innovation while avoiding methodological overlap with excluded computational biology domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biochemical and biophysical characteristics of drugs at the molecular level and their interaction with, and effects on, biological macromolecules and cellular structures and processes. Includes instruction in molecular biology and biophysics; pharmacology of signal transduction, transmitters, and protein synthesis and release; receptors, protein interaction and binding; drug discovery and recognition; molecular toxicology; drug design; pharmacodynamics; developmental genetics; and studies of therapeutic strategies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for enhancing strategic intelligence analysis through advanced pattern recognition and predictive modeling of multi-source, unstructured data. The research addresses the challenge of integrating heterogeneous intelligence streams—including signals intelligence (SIGINT), human intelligence (HUMINT), and open-source intelligence (OSINT)—into a unified analytical system capable of identifying latent threats and emergent adversarial strategies in near-real time. Current approaches struggle with scalability, temporal resolution, and the dynamic interplay of global socio-technical systems, particularly in environments characterized by misinformation campaigns and hybrid warfare tactics. The proposed solution leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-modal architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing, temporal graph neural networks, and agent-based simulation. Key computational challenges include processing petascale multilingual text corpora, modeling complex adaptive systems with millions of interacting entities, and maintaining decision-ready situational awareness through continuous model updates. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of intelligence feeds across modular pipelines: one subsystem focuses on entity recognition and relationship extraction from unstructured documents, while another performs dynamic network analysis to detect coordination patterns across communication channels. A third component simulates potential escalation pathways using game-theoretic principles adapted to asymmetric conflict scenarios. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of identifying second- and third-order effects of geopolitical events, quantifying systemic fragility in contested regions, and generating anticipatory assessments with reduced human analyst workload. This work aims to establish technical benchmarks for next-generation intelligence platforms while addressing ethical considerations in automated threat prioritization through embedded uncertainty quantification and explainability protocols. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a testbed for evaluating human-AI collaboration paradigms in time-sensitive decision environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the management, analysis and use of national-level, theatre-level, and international intelligence and related policy issues. Includes instruction in intelligence organization and management, strategic uses of intelligence, management of intelligence systems and assets, command and control, joint intelligence operations, electronic and signals intelligence, threat assessment and estimation, intelligence analysis and reporting, counterintelligence, and studies of specific regions and situations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to enhance the design and personalization of French language teaching materials through data-driven analysis of second language acquisition patterns. A critical challenge in French language teacher education lies in systematically addressing the diverse linguistic needs of learners, particularly in mastering complex grammatical structures (e.g., verb conjugation, gendered nouns) and phonological nuances. Current approaches often rely on generalized pedagogical strategies, which may not account for the variability in learner error patterns or the dynamic interplay between instructional methods and language retention. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets of learner interactions, including written compositions, oral recordings, and real-time feedback from simulated classroom environments. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on learner corpora, will be deployed to identify error typologies and predict developmental trajectories across proficiency levels. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate the impact of different pedagogical interventions on long-term language retention. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to handle multimodal data (text, audio) from over 10,000 anonymized learner profiles, alongside iterative training of machine learning models for adaptive content generation. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for generating differentiated French language exercises based on empirically derived error patterns, (2) open-source tools to help educators visualize learner progress and adjust instructional strategies, and (3) novel insights into the cognitive load dynamics of French grammar instruction. By enabling real-time analysis of complex language acquisition data, this project aims to equip French language educators with evidence-based resources to optimize classroom outcomes, while advancing computational applications in teacher preparation programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach French language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in veterinary administrative workflows through the development of a predictive resource allocation framework, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze heterogeneous datasets unique to veterinary practice management. Veterinary administrative services face growing complexity due to fluctuating patient volumes, diverse species-specific care protocols, and regulatory demands, yet lack tailored computational tools to optimize staffing, equipment use, or financial forecasting. Current methods rely on generalized business analytics, which fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between clinical workflows, seasonal zoonotic disease patterns, and client behavior. To bridge this gap, we propose a machine learning-driven approach integrating anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), facility operation logs, and regional epidemiological data. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-year, clinic-level datasets (spanning 500+ veterinary practices) and the training of ensemble models to predict resource demands at daily, weekly, and seasonal intervals. Agent-based simulations will further test dynamic staffing and inventory policies under scenarios informed by historical crisis events, such as pandemic-driven pet adoption surges. The computational pipeline will utilize Apache Spark for distributed data preprocessing and TensorFlow for recurrent neural networks capable of handling irregular time-series inputs common in veterinary EHRs. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolset for clinic administrators to simulate resource allocation strategies, reducing operational costs by an estimated 12–18% in pilot deployments. By focusing on the understudied intersection of veterinary operations research and computational logistics, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for administrative decision-making in a sector critical to public health preparedness and animal welfare, yet underserved by existing analytics paradigms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary administrative services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The brewing industry faces critical challenges in optimizing fermentation efficiency, predicting microbial stability, and maintaining product consistency amid variable raw material quality and environmental conditions. Traditional empirical approaches to process optimization and quality control are resource-intensive and lack the resolution to address complex microbial interactions and metabolic dynamics at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models of yeast metabolism, microbial community dynamics, and raw material interactions in beer production. Using genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and non-Saccharomyces strains, we will simulate fermentation kinetics under diverse substrate and stress conditions to identify genetic and environmental factors influencing ethanol yield, flavor compound production, and spoilage risks. Metagenomic datasets from industrial fermentation batches will be analyzed via machine learning pipelines to predict microbial contamination events and their impacts on product stability. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate enzyme-substrate interactions in malted barley to optimize mashing efficiency. These computational workflows require parallel processing capabilities and large-scale memory allocation due to the complexity of integrating multi-omics data, stochastic modeling of microbial populations, and high-resolution parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for strain selection, process parameter optimization, and contamination mitigation, directly addressing industry demands for energy-efficient brewing and reduced batch failure rates. The project aligns with agricultural science priorities by bridging brewing biotechnology with crop science (e.g., barley varietal impacts on malt enzymes) and microbial ecology, while providing open-source tools for the fermentation research community. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the necessary computational throughput and model fidelity to advance both academic brewing science and industrial applications.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the business, science, and technology of beer brewing operations. Includes instruction in biology, biochemistry, brewing, entrepreneurship, fermentation, malting, marketing, microbiology, quality control, and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of host-microbe interactions in mucosal immunity using high-performance computing (HPC) to model microbial community behavior and immune response networks. Current experimental approaches struggle to capture the spatial, temporal, and functional complexity of microbial populations in mucosal environments, particularly their bidirectional signaling with host immune cells. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and stochastic simulations to resolve how localized microbial metabolite gradients influence immune cell differentiation and barrier function. Metagenomic and proteomic datasets from murine gut and respiratory tract models will parameterize microbial community structures, while immune receptor-ligand binding kinetics and cytokine diffusion parameters will be derived from time-resolved microscopy and flow cytometry. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 3D mucosal environments at physiologically relevant scales (>10^6 interacting agents), incorporating dynamic host-microbe feedback loops. Key outcomes include predictive models of dysbiosis-induced immune dysregulation and identification of critical microbial taxa or metabolic pathways that stabilize mucosal homeostasis. This work addresses a fundamental gap in understanding how polymicrobial communities collectively modulate immune tolerance or inflammation—a question inaccessible to reductionist experimental systems. By bridging microbial ecology and immunology through scalable computational methods, the project will provide mechanistic insights into diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and asthma, while establishing an open-source simulation platform for hypothesis-driven microbial immunology research. The requested resources are essential to manage memory-intensive simulations and optimize machine learning pipelines for pattern recognition in high-dimensional host-microbe interaction datasets.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the microbiological sciences and immunology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Neuropathological research faces critical challenges in integrating and interpreting complex, multi-modal datasets derived from nerve biopsies, necropsies, and advanced molecular analyses. Current limitations in computational infrastructure hinder the ability to analyze high-resolution histopathological images, spatially resolved transcriptomic profiles, and clinical metadata at scale. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational modeling of neurodegenerative and neuromuscular disease mechanisms. The primary research problem centers on identifying spatially resolved molecular signatures that correlate with clinical disease progression, a task requiring the integration of terabyte-scale imaging data, single-cell RNA sequencing, and longitudinal patient records. Our computational approach combines deep learning-based image segmentation of nerve tissue microstructures with graph neural networks to model cell-cell interaction networks across disease states. Parallelized workflows will process whole-slide imaging datasets (≥20,000 images) to quantify axonal degeneration, inflammatory infiltrates, and protein aggregation patterns. Multi-omics integration pipelines will align these features with single-nucleus sequencing data from 500+ post-mortem neuromuscular specimens, leveraging dimension reduction and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to account for clinical heterogeneity. The HPC environment is essential for training three-dimensional convolutional neural networks on annotated tissue stacks, executing molecular dynamics simulations of pathogenic protein interactions, and performing genome-wide association studies (GWAS) on linked clinical-genomic datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive models of neuropathological progression validated against independent clinical cohorts, (2) novel digital biomarkers for early diagnosis of atypical neuromuscular disorders, and (3) open-source computational pathology tools optimized for GPU-accelerated HPC architectures. This resource allocation will directly advance diagnostic precision in neuropathology while establishing a scalable framework for integrating emerging spatial omics technologies into clinical research workflows.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory analysis of nerve tissues and the clinical diagnosis of neurological and neuromuscular diseases. May included related research in nerve biopsies and necropsies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to investigate the dynamic interplay between architectural design, environmental factors, and human physiological responses in healthcare settings. Despite growing recognition of the built environment’s impact on health outcomes, existing frameworks lack granular, real-time simulations that integrate spatial configurations, airflow dynamics, and stress biomarkers to optimize healing-centered design. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing a computational model that predicts how design variables—such as room geometry, material acoustics, and ventilation patterns—interact with occupant neurophysiological states (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels) to influence recovery rates. The computational approach combines three methodologies: (1) agent-based modeling to simulate occupant movement and social interactions within virtual architectural layouts, (2) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with machine learning to map airborne pathogen dispersion and thermal comfort under diverse design scenarios, and (3) Bayesian networks to analyze multimodal datasets linking environmental sensors, wearable biometrics, and clinical outcomes from partner hospitals. By iteratively refining these models using HPC-enabled parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses, the project aims to identify design interventions that minimize nosocomial infections, reduce patient stress, and enhance staff well-being. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for architects and public health practitioners, validated against empirical data from retrofitted clinical spaces. This work will advance evidence-based design paradigms, offering scalable solutions to mitigate health disparities in underserved communities where suboptimal infrastructure exacerbates disease burdens. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional optimization and real-time rendering required to resolve complex, nonlinear interactions between built environments and human health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the impact of design and architecture on the health of individuals and larger populations, and how to create settings that promote health, healing, and well-being. Includes instruction in architecture, interior design, human health services, communication studies, medical and clinical innovations, behavioral and engineering sciences, hospitals and health systems, and environmental conditions that influence health.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of next-generation spacecraft propulsion systems through high-fidelity computational modeling of plasma-based electric propulsion. Electric propulsion systems, such as Hall-effect and ion thrusters, offer high specific impulse for deep-space missions but face challenges in efficiency scaling, thruster erosion, and plasma-wall interactions under long-duration operation. Current models rely on simplified fluid approximations or low-resolution particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, limiting predictive accuracy for complex magnetic nozzle configurations and non-equilibrium plasma behavior. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining 3D implicit PIC methods, direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) for neutral gas dynamics, and machine learning-accelerated surrogate models. The framework will leverage GPU-optimized codebases to resolve electron timescales (∼1 ns) alongside ion and neutral transport (∼1 ms) across meshes exceeding 100 million cells. High-performance computing resources are critical to manage the memory demands of adaptive mesh refinement and the parallel communication overhead of coupled solvers. Expected outcomes include validated models of magnetic field-plasma coupling in cusped thrusters, predictive erosion maps for ceramic chamber materials, and optimized operating regimes for dual-mode propulsion systems. These results will directly inform the development of NASA-funded prototype thrusters for lunar Gateway station-keeping and Mars cargo missions. The open-source tools produced will enable the astronautical engineering community to simulate thruster lifetimes and performance with unprecedented fidelity, reducing reliance on costly empirical testing campaigns. This work aligns with national priorities in cislunar infrastructure sustainability and deep-space exploration while advancing computational capabilities at the intersection of plasma physics and spacecraft systems engineering.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and operational evaluation of aircraft and space vehicles. Includes instruction in control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in veterinary diagnostics and treatment planning through large-scale genomic and phenotypic data analysis. A critical challenge in veterinary medicine is the limited integration of multi-omics datasets (e.g., genomics, proteomics, metabolomics) with clinical records to predict disease susceptibility, treatment responses, and outcomes in diverse animal populations. Existing tools for analyzing these datasets are computationally constrained, limiting their resolution and scalability. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models optimized for HPC environments to identify biomarkers associated with chronic conditions in companion animals (e.g., feline diabetes, canine osteoarthritis) and production livestock (e.g., bovine respiratory disease). Computational workflows will integrate species-specific genomic databases, electronic health records, and environmental variables using parallelized algorithms for feature selection and ensemble learning. Additionally, agent-based models will simulate disease transmission dynamics in multi-species environments to evaluate biosecurity protocols. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce model training times, and improve predictive accuracy through hyperparameter optimization. Outcomes will include open-access predictive tools for veterinary practitioners, optimized treatment guidelines for high-risk populations, and educational modules for training veterinary technicians in computational data analysis. By bridging gaps between clinical practice and computational research, this work aims to enhance evidence-based decision-making in animal healthcare while fostering technical proficiency in emerging data-driven veterinary technologies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary/ Animal Health Technology and Veterinary Assistant
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of veterinarians, laboratory animal specialists, and zoological professionals, to provide patient management, care, and clinical procedures assistance as well as owner communication. Includes instruction in animal nursing care, animal health and nutrition, animal handling, clinical pathology, radiology, anesthesiology, dental prophylaxis, surgical assisting, clinical laboratory procedures, office administration skills, patient and owner management, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Greenhouse operations require precise environmental control to optimize plant growth, yet current management strategies often rely on static protocols that fail to dynamically adapt to real-time biological and environmental variability. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational model to simulate and predict plant-environment interactions in controlled agricultural settings. The research problem centers on the need for adaptive, energy-efficient greenhouse systems that balance productivity with resource constraints, particularly under fluctuating external conditions such as shifting weather patterns or pest pressures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-scale datasets—including sensor-derived climate data, hyperspectral plant imaging, and genomic information from key crop species—into a machine learning framework. This framework will employ neural networks and agent-based modeling to predict optimal adjustments to temperature, humidity, irrigation, and lighting systems in response to real-time plant physiological states. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will further refine spatial climate distribution models to minimize energy use while maintaining growth homogeneity across greenhouse zones. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high dimensionality of sensor data, parallelizing iterative optimization algorithms, and scaling simulations to represent diverse crop species and facility designs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for dynamic climate control, validated against experimental greenhouse trials, that reduces energy consumption by 15–20% while increasing yield consistency for high-value crops. By bridging computational modeling with operational greenhouse management, this work will provide a template for data-driven automation in controlled-environment agriculture, enhancing the resilience and scalability of food production systems. The proposed resource allocation will directly support the development of open-access computational tools tailored to the needs of commercial and research greenhouse operators.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce, store, and deliver plant species in controlled indoor environments for wholesale, commercial, research, or other purposes. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science; climate, irrigation, and nutrition control equipment operation and maintenance; facilities management; inventory control; safety procedures; and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision-focused research in developmental and behavioral pediatrics (DBP), specifically targeting the integration of multimodal datasets to model neurodevelopmental trajectories and predict behavioral outcomes. Current challenges in DBP include the heterogeneous presentation of conditions such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), as well as limited tools to disentangle the interplay of genetic, neuroimaging, and environmental factors in longitudinal outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining deep learning and dynamical systems modeling to analyze high-dimensional data from electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging (fMRI and DTI), and genomic sequencing. The project will utilize federated learning architectures to harmonize data across five pediatric clinical cohorts (total n ≈ 12,000), preserving privacy while enabling large-scale pattern recognition. Key computational tasks include 1) training graph neural networks to map developmental milestones against polygenic risk scores and neuroanatomical features, 2) simulating neural circuit maturation using biophysically grounded models, and 3) applying reinforcement learning to optimize personalized intervention strategies. HPC resources are critical for managing the iterative training of multimodal models (anticipating >50,000 GPU hours), processing terabyte-scale neuroimaging datasets, and running parallelized parameter sweeps in sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include the identification of computational biomarkers for early risk stratification, predictive models of treatment response variability, and open-source tools for developmental trajectory modeling. This work directly addresses the NIH’s emphasis on computational psychiatry in child health, with potential to transform clinical decision-making in DBP by bridging mechanistic insights and data-driven approaches. Resource allocation will support both proposed analyses and ongoing collaborations with the ABCD Study and Autism Speaks MSSNG consortium.
cip_definition: Research focused on Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting protein-ligand binding affinities with high accuracy and scalability, a critical bottleneck in structure-based drug discovery. Traditional methods, such as molecular docking and free-energy perturbation, face limitations in balancing computational cost, throughput, and predictive precision. To overcome these constraints, we propose an integrative computational framework combining enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with deep learning models trained on multi-modal biophysical data. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale, parallelized MD simulations across diverse protein targets and ligand libraries, generating conformational ensembles and interaction energetics datasets. These data will train graph neural networks (GNNs) that encode protein-ligand structures, dynamic interaction patterns, and thermodynamic descriptors to predict binding free energies. The computational workflow will be optimized for GPU-accelerated nodes to handle memory-intensive simulations and GNN training on terabytes of trajectory data. Validation will involve retrospective benchmarking against experimental binding affinities and prospective testing on understudied proteins with therapeutic relevance. Successful implementation will yield a scalable platform for rapid, accurate virtual screening, reducing reliance on costly experimental assays. This work will advance computational biology by bridging physics-based simulations with data-driven learning, providing insights into allosteric binding mechanisms and resistance mutations. Outcomes will be disseminated as open-source tools and pre-trained models, enabling broader applications in drug repurposing and target discovery. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the iterative simulation-training cycles, which require petabytes of storage, high-throughput job scheduling, and parallel processing capabilities exceeding local cluster capacities.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_title: Biomathematics, Bioinformatics, and Computational Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biomathematics, bioinformatics, and computational biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation propagation in digital communication networks, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets. While existing scholarship in communication studies has established foundational theories on media effects and information diffusion, the rapid evolution of digital platforms—and the unprecedented volume, velocity, and complexity of user-generated content—poses novel methodological challenges. Traditional analytical tools struggle to capture the nonlinear, context-dependent interactions that characterize misinformation spread across social networks, particularly when analyzing temporal patterns, cross-platform behavior, and the interplay of textual, visual, and algorithmic factors. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), social network analysis, and agent-based modeling. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets from platforms like Twitter, Reddit, and TikTok, including timestamped posts, user interaction graphs, and multimedia content. Machine learning models will classify content authenticity and emotional valence, while parallelized network simulations will map how community structures and platform affordances amplify or mitigate misinformation. This approach advances communication theory by quantitatively testing hypotheses derived from diffusion of innovations frameworks and cultural studies critiques of media power. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of key network signatures predictive of misinformation cascades, (2) empirical evaluation of platform-specific moderation policies, and (3) open-source tools for scalable communication research. By bridging qualitative communication theory with computational social science methods, this work will inform evidence-based strategies for media literacy interventions and platform governance, directly contributing to public discourse on the societal impacts of digital communication technologies.
cip_definition: An program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, research and research methods, and theories of communication, and that spans specialties within the field of communications. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: Hematologic malignancies and solid tumors exhibit complex molecular heterogeneity, driving variable treatment responses and resistance mechanisms. While advances in multi-omics profiling have generated vast genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets, integrating these data to identify predictive biomarkers and therapeutic vulnerabilities remains computationally prohibitive for standard clinical research infrastructure. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational analysis of multi-omics data from 5,000 patients across 15 cancer subtypes treated at our institution. We will develop a machine learning framework integrating genomic alterations, tumor microenvironment signatures, and longitudinal clinical outcomes to model treatment resistance. Key computational steps include dimensionality reduction of single-cell RNA-seq data, Bayesian network inference of signaling pathways, and ensemble learning to predict drug response. A second aim involves molecular dynamics simulations of recurrent mutation hotspots in hematologic drivers (e.g., FLT3, JAK2) to prioritize neomorphic binding sites for targeted therapy. These simulations require GPU-accelerated sampling of protein conformational states across microsecond timescales. The HPC environment is critical for managing petabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing workflows, and executing resource-intensive simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models of therapy resistance deployable via clinical decision support tools, (2) structural blueprints for designing inhibitors against previously undruggable oncoproteins, and (3) an open-source computational pipeline for adaptive oncology trial design. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work bridges the gap between high-throughput omics data and clinically actionable insights, directly addressing the National Cancer Institute’s priority of computationally-driven precision oncology. Resource allocation will support urgent analyses for three active clinical trials investigating resistance mechanisms in AML and NSCLC while establishing a scalable infrastructure for real-time genomic data interpretation in our molecular tumor board.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hematology-Oncology

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of how socio-cognitive and environmental factors interact to shape learning outcomes in technology-enhanced environments. A key challenge in the learning sciences is modeling the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between learners’ cognitive strategies, real-time physiological responses (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate variability), and contextual variables such as instructional scaffolding and peer collaboration patterns. Traditional analytical methods struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data streams at scale, limiting insights into adaptive learning processes. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework leveraging machine learning and multilevel network analysis to analyze multimodal datasets from 3,000+ learners using digital collaborative platforms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabytes of interaction logs, biometric sensor data, and natural language text, as well as training recurrent neural networks to detect temporal patterns in metacognitive behaviors. The project will implement GPU-accelerated pipelines for real-time feature extraction from eye-tracking videos and ensemble models to predict disengagement states. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model how variations in instructional feedback propagate through learner networks. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) a validated computational architecture for multimodal learning analytics, (2) evidence-based principles for adaptive scaffolding in collaborative learning systems, and (3) open-source tools for privacy-preserving analysis of sensitive educational data. By enabling large-scale integration of psychometric, behavioral, and contextual data, this work will provide novel insights into the mechanisms underlying successful learning interventions while addressing reproducibility challenges in educational research. The requested resources directly support the iterative training of deep learning models and complex network analyses that are computationally prohibitive on local infrastructure, ensuring rigorous exploration of how individual differences and social dynamics jointly influence learning pathways.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the multiple aspects of learning in different environments, including specific aspects of the content to be mastered, cognitive aspects of the student, the instructional environment and materials, the preparation and activities of the instructor, socio-cultural and linguistic components, and assessment outcomes. Includes instruction in the social, organizational, and cultural dynamics of learning; learning and cognition; learning strategies; educational psychology; educational testing and measurement; instructional design and technology; and statistical design of educational research.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in modeling the radiative and hydrodynamic processes governing the evolution of massive stellar systems and their surrounding environments. A key limitation in simulating these systems arises from the complex interplay of multi-scale physics, including non-equilibrium radiation transfer, magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities, and the coupled feedback between stellar populations and the interstellar medium. Current simulations often rely on simplified approximations for radiative transfer or neglect high-energy processes due to computational constraints, leading to uncertainties in predicting observational signatures of star-forming regions, supernova remnants, and accretion disks. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining 3D radiation-MHD simulations with Monte Carlo radiative transfer methods. The code will leverage adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) to resolve small-scale turbulent structures and incorporate wavelength-dependent opacity data for relativistic particles and dust grains. A novel aspect of this work involves coupling non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) ionization calculations with large-scale dynamics, enabling self-consistent modeling of photon-matter interactions in hypervelocity shocks and optically thick environments. The computational workflow will utilize MPI-OpenMP hybrid parallelism across GPU-accelerated nodes to manage memory-intensive radiation transport calculations. Expected outcomes include new insights into the role of radiation pressure in disrupting protostellar disks, improved constraints on dust formation mechanisms in supernova ejecta, and publicly accessible synthetic observables (spectra, light curves) for comparison with JWST and ALMA datasets. By resolving previously intractable scales of radiative feedback, this work will advance predictive models of galactic chemical evolution and inform next-generation telescope surveys. The requested allocation of 2.5 million node-hours on a Tier-2 HPC system will support parameter space exploration across stellar masses, metallicities, and turbulence regimes, generating 500+ TB of high-fidelity simulation data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and observational study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena. Includes instruction in cosmology, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of quantum many-body dynamics in ultracold molecular systems, a frontier area in atomic and molecular physics where experimental and theoretical efforts are constrained by the extreme computational demands of accurately modeling correlated quantum states. Current state-of-the-art methods struggle to simulate the non-equilibrium behavior of large molecular ensembles with sufficient precision, particularly in regimes dominated by long-range dipole-dipole interactions and external field effects. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining tensor network algorithms with large-scale exact diagonalization to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for systems of up to 50 interacting polar molecules. The simulations will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize the construction and evolution of many-body wavefunctions, employing adaptive basis sets and symmetry-aware partitioning to reduce memory overhead. Key objectives include characterizing entanglement growth during collisional processes and predicting the stability of proposed quantum phases in optical lattice traps. The computational methodology will be validated against existing experimental data on Stark deceleration and rotational quenching in trapped molecular gases. Successful implementation will yield predictive models for controlling quantum state transitions in next-generation ultracold chemistry experiments, while the developed codebase will be optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures and disseminated as an open-source tool. This work directly supports national priorities in quantum information science by providing essential theoretical benchmarks for molecular qubit design. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on HPC systems will enable simulations at unprecedented scales, resolving critical open questions about the role of many-body correlations in molecular quantum dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior of matter-energy phenomena at the level of atoms and molecules. Includes instruction in chemical physics, atomic forces and structure, molecular orbital theory, magnetic resonance, molecular bonding, phase equilibria, quantum theory of solids, and applications to the study of specific elements and higher compounds.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic, large-scale economic systems under conditions of resource scarcity and market uncertainty. The core problem addressed is the computational intractability of analyzing heterogeneous agent-based models (ABMs) that incorporate granular behavioral data, cross-border trade flows, and stochastic shocks. Traditional equilibrium-based approaches often oversimplify agent heterogeneity and fail to capture emergent phenomena in interconnected markets, limiting their utility for policy design. To address this gap, we propose developing a scalable ABM framework that simulates decision-making processes across millions of agents—including households, firms, and financial institutions—operating in a multi-country trade network. The model integrates real-world datasets on consumption patterns, production chains, and tariff policies, requiring parallelized computation for parameter calibration, Monte Carlo simulations, and sensitivity analyses. Key computational challenges include solving high-dimensional optimization problems for agent interactions, managing memory-intensive datasets spanning international input-output tables, and conducting counterfactual policy experiments under varying scarcity constraints. HPC resources will enable the use of distributed computing techniques to partition agent populations across nodes, accelerate Bayesian estimation of behavioral parameters, and reduce runtime for stochastic simulations from months to days. Expected outcomes include new insights into the resilience of global supply chains during resource shortages, quantitative evaluations of protectionist trade policies, and open-source tools for computationally intensive economic modeling. By bridging micro-level decision-making with macro-level systemic effects, this work aims to enhance predictive capacity in international economics while advancing methodological standards for computational economics research.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the systematic study of the production, conservation and allocation of resources in conditions of scarcity, together with the organizational frameworks related to these processes. Includes instruction in economic theory, micro- and macroeconomics, comparative economic systems, money and banking systems, international economics, quantitative analytical methods, and applications to specific industries and public policy issues.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling for adaptive workplace design, addressing the gap between static facility management practices and the dynamic needs of modern hybrid work environments. The core problem lies in optimizing spatial configurations, resource allocation, and environmental systems in response to real-time occupancy patterns, employee behavior data, and energy efficiency targets—a challenge requiring complex multivariate analysis beyond conventional planning tools. The computational approach integrates three methodological pillars: (1) agent-based modeling of workforce movement and space utilization patterns, calibrated using anonymized IoT sensor data from existing facilities; (2) machine learning algorithms to predict short- and long-term space demand under varying organizational scenarios; and (3) multi-objective optimization frameworks balancing ergonomic, sustainability, and operational cost considerations. By deploying these models at scale through HPC parallelization, the project aims to simulate 10,000+ workplace configurations across diverse industry use cases while processing high-frequency sensor data streams. Expected outcomes include the development of an open-source decision support toolkit for facility managers, capable of recommending dynamic space reconfigurations with 15-minute granularity. The research contributes novel methodologies at the intersection of environmental psychology, operations management, and computational design, with potential applications in crisis-responsive planning (e.g., pandemic protocols) and net-zero facility transitions. Results will be validated through partnerships with three corporate campus operators, comparing model predictions against empirical post-occupancy evaluations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on strategic workplace and facility planning and that prepares individuals to function as facility and event managers and workplace consultants. Includes instruction in the principles of aesthetic and functional design, environmental psychology and organizational behavior, real estate planning, principles of occupational health and safety, event planning and management, operations management, and applicable regulatory and policy issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of data-driven frameworks for optimizing culinary texture design in plant-based meat alternatives, a rapidly growing sector within the culinary and personal services industry. Current approaches to replicating the mouthfeel and structural integrity of animal-derived meats rely heavily on iterative experimental trials, which are resource-intensive and lack predictive precision. The research problem centers on the absence of scalable computational models capable of simulating the complex interactions between plant proteins, lipids, and processing parameters (e.g., temperature, shear stress) that govern texture formation. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model the hierarchical assembly of protein networks under varying mechanical and thermal conditions. MD simulations will capture nanoscale interactions of key proteins (e.g., pea, soy) and polysaccharides, while FEA will predict macroscale texture properties such as elasticity and fracture behavior. ML algorithms, trained on both simulated and experimental data, will identify optimal ingredient ratios and processing workflows. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of parameter space and the need for parallelized simulations across diverse biopolymer configurations. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive toolkit for culinary developers, reducing R&D cycles by 30-50%, and novel insights into the role of non-traditional binding agents (e.g., algal polysaccharides) in texture modulation. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational material science and culinary innovation, offering a template for data-driven design in food services while addressing sustainability challenges in protein production. The project will further establish computational gastronomy as a distinct niche within non-STEM research, with implications for vocational training programs in next-generation culinary technologies.
cip_title: Culinary, Entertainment, and Personal Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary, entertainment, and personal services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational linguistics and second language acquisition (SLA) within an English as a Second Language (ESL) academic program. The core research problem involves modeling the cognitive and linguistic processes of ESL learners as they acquire syntactic and semantic competencies in English, particularly in contexts where their first language (L1) exhibits significant structural divergence from English. Traditional methods for analyzing interlanguage development rely on manual corpus annotation or small-scale experimental data, limiting the capacity to identify nuanced patterns across diverse learner populations. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining large-scale learner corpus analysis with neural network-based simulations of syntactic transfer. HPC resources will enable the processing of multilingual text corpora (including longitudinal ESL writing samples and parallel L1-English datasets) and the training of transformer models to simulate L1-influenced grammatical errors. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for error annotation, graph-based representations of syntactic dependencies, and comparative analyses of model outputs against empirical learner data.
