Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for predicting and classifying L1-specific acquisition challenges, (2) evidence-based insights into the interaction between typological distance and error frequency, and (3) open-access tools for generating adaptive language learning materials tailored to learners’ L1 profiles. By integrating SLA theory with computational modeling at scale, this work aims to advance personalized ESL pedagogy and contribute methodological innovations to the interdisciplinary study of multilingualism. The scale of data processing and model training required—particularly for low-resource language pairs—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust results within feasible timeframes.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of decentralized labor negotiation systems in gig economy platforms, an understudied intersection of computational social science, labor economics, and industrial relations. Traditional collective bargaining frameworks struggle to adapt to platform-based work structures, where algorithmic management, fragmented worker populations, and real-time demand fluctuations complicate negotiation processes. The research problem centers on designing and simulating scalable, adaptive negotiation mechanisms that balance worker preferences, platform profitability, and regulatory constraints. Using agent-based modeling (ABM), we will construct a computational testbed representing heterogeneous stakeholders—workers with varying skill levels and availability patterns, customers with service quality expectations, and platform algorithms optimizing task allocation and pricing. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations across diverse economic scenarios (e.g., demand shocks, policy interventions) while incorporating machine learning to iteratively refine negotiation protocols. Key computational challenges include optimizing sparse communication networks between transient workers, resolving multi-objective conflicts in real-time bargaining, and quantifying systemic resilience to labor policy changes. Expected outcomes include (1) empirically grounded metrics for evaluating decentralized negotiation fairness and efficiency, (2) predictive insights into emergent labor market behaviors under proposed regulatory frameworks, and (3) open-source simulation tools for testing platform labor policies. By bridging gaps between computational economics and industrial relations, this work aims to inform both platform governance strategies and labor protection policies tailored to 21st-century work arrangements. The scale and complexity of modeling millions of agent interactions across parameterized policy landscapes necessitate HPC capabilities to achieve statistically robust, generalizable results within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on employee-management interactions and the management of issues and disputes regarding working conditions and worker benefit packages, and that may prepare individuals to function as labor or personnel relations specialists. Includes instruction in labor history, policies and strategies of the labor movement, union organization, labor-management negotiation, labor law and contract interpretation, labor economics, welfare and benefit packages, grievance procedures, and labor policy studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of under-resourced South Asian languages, with a focus on modeling historical linguistic evolution and cross-dialectal variation in literary texts. The primary research challenge lies in the scarcity of digitized corpora and computational tools tailored to languages such as Bengali, Tamil, and Sanskrit, which exhibit complex morphological structures, script diversity, and diachronic shifts across literary periods. To address this, we propose a multi-phase computational workflow. First, we will compile and preprocess a distributed corpus of classical and modern texts spanning eight languages, utilizing OCR correction pipelines optimized for historical manuscripts and palm-leaf inscriptions. Next, we will employ transformer-based models fine-tuned for low-resource languages to automate syntactic parsing, semantic role labeling, and metrical analysis across genres (poetry, prose, religious texts). Parallelized phylogenetic algorithms will then reconstruct language family relationships, while variational autoencoders will model dialectal divergence in phonology and lexicon. HPC resources are critical for scaling these processes across terabytes of text, training domain-specific language models, and running computationally intensive simulations of language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational models for tracking semantic change in premodern Bengali literature, a comparative dataset of syntactic structures across Dravidian and Indo-Aryan languages, and interactive visualizations of dialect boundaries in the Deccan region. These resources will directly support endangered language preservation initiatives and provide humanities scholars with quantitative frameworks for re-examining literary historiography. The project bridges computational linguistics with area studies, offering methodological innovations for analyzing non-Latin scripts and oral-literary interfaces in South Asia’s multilingual landscape.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: South Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the languages, literatures, and linguistics of the peoples of the Indian subcontinent and associated borderlands and island groups.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and visualize the spatial and cultural dynamics of Tibetan religious textual production across historical and contemporary contexts. The research problem centers on mapping the transmission and adaptation of Tibetan Buddhist texts, ritual manuals, and oral traditions across diverse regions, including Tibet and its global diaspora. Despite the rich corpus of digitized manuscripts, inscriptions, and ethnographic recordings, the integration of these heterogeneous datasets—spanning classical Tibetan, modern dialects, and multimedia sources—remains computationally prohibitive without advanced infrastructure. The study will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for classical Tibetan script and dialectal variations, alongside geospatial machine learning to model textual circulation patterns relative to pilgrimage routes, monastic networks, and exile settlements. Computational workflows will include transformer-based models for semantic analysis of doctrinal shifts in key texts, graph databases to reconstruct authorship and commentary networks, and 3D GIS tools to visualize sacred landscapes altered by environmental or political factors. By automating the alignment of multilingual fragments and oral histories, this approach aims to uncover previously obscured connections between pre-modern scholastic traditions and modern revitalization efforts in diaspora communities. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated texts, interactive maps of textual dissemination, and a framework for computational cultural analysis applicable to other marginalized linguistic and religious traditions. The project addresses a critical gap in Tibetan Studies by enabling large-scale, interdisciplinary inquiry into how cultural knowledge is preserved and transformed under conditions of displacement, offering methodological innovations for digital humanities in non-dominant languages.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Tibet and its borderlands, with emphasis on both pre-modern and modern Tibet and associated religious and exile movements.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance biomechanical modeling of foot and ankle pathologies, a critical yet computationally underexplored area in podiatric medicine. The research addresses a gap in personalized treatment planning for complex conditions such as Charcot neuroarthropathy, progressive flatfoot deformity, and post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Current clinical evaluations rely on static imaging and qualitative gait assessments, which fail to capture dynamic, tissue-level stresses contributing to disease progression. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing multiscale computational models integrating patient-specific anatomical data (from MRI/CT), real-time motion capture, and plantar pressure measurements. These models will simulate musculoskeletal dynamics, ligamentous strain, and bone-cartilage interactions during gait cycles under varying pathological and therapeutic conditions. HPC resources are essential to handle the high dimensionality of finite element analyses, machine learning-driven parameter optimization, and probabilistic modeling of intervention outcomes (e.g., orthotic designs, surgical corrections). Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to quantify how specific anatomical variations or treatment modifications influence mechanical load redistribution—a key factor in preventing ulceration, joint degeneration, and recurrent injury. The computational pipeline will be validated against clinical outcomes from a retrospective cohort of 150 patients with diabetic foot complications. By enabling unprecedented resolution in modeling foot biomechanics, this work aims to establish quantitative guidelines for intervention thresholds in podiatry, reduce trial-and-error in therapeutic approaches, and provide an open-access simulation toolkit for clinician-researchers. The project bridges computational mechanics, orthopedic pathophysiology, and clinical podiatry, positioning HPC as a transformative tool in a field where traditional research paradigms have been constrained by the anatomical complexity of the lower extremity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of podiatric medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and injuries to the foot and lower extremities. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, anatomy of the lower extremity, functional orthopedics, foot biomechanics, podiatric radiology, dermatology, podiatric surgery, podopediatrics, sports medicine, physical diagnosis, emergency medicine and traumatology, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between computational musicology, ritual studies, and the evolution of worship practices in underrepresented diasporic communities. Focusing on non-canonical religious music traditions—specifically, syncretic oral hymnodies from Afro-Caribbean and Indigenous Pacific spiritual communities—the research addresses a critical gap in understanding how decentralized musical practices shape collective memory and ritual efficacy outside institutional frameworks. The core challenge lies in analyzing complex, non-linear musical structures embedded in field recordings (1970s–present), which exhibit polymetric rhythms, microtonal variations, and improvisational layers that resist conventional transcription or Eurocentric analytical models. To address this, we propose developing a hybrid computational architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for modeling improvisational decision trees, high-resolution audio signal processing to isolate overlapping vocal/instrumental strata, and agent-based simulations of congregational participation dynamics. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of 12,000+ hours of audio-visual archives while training multimodal models that correlate musical features with ethnographic metadata on ritual contexts. Expected outcomes include: (1) a novel taxonomy of "ritual resilience" indicators quantifiably linking musical complexity to community identity preservation; (2) open-source tools for ethically repatriating analyzed materials to source communities through adaptive generative interfaces; and (3) computational evidence challenging dominant narratives about oral tradition fragility. By bridging ethnomusicology, complex systems theory, and decolonial digital humanities, this work pioneers methods for sustaining endangered spiritual repertoires while redefining HPC’s role in culturally grounded humanities scholarship.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious music and worship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dental pulp and periradicular infections represent a critical challenge in endodontics, with treatment outcomes heavily dependent on the complex interplay between microbial communities, biomechanical stresses, and biomaterial interactions. Current clinical approaches rely on empirical protocols for root canal disinfection and obturation, but persistent apical periodontitis occurs in 10-15% of cases, often requiring invasive retreatment. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that integrate microbiomic, biomechanical, and fluid dynamic factors influencing endodontic treatment failure. We will create patient-specific simulations of root canal systems using µCT-derived 3D geometries, incorporating viscoelastic dentin properties, non-Newtonian irrigant flow dynamics, and spatial biofilm organization patterns identified through multiplex fluorescence microscopy. Machine learning models trained on clinical outcome data from 2,300 retrospective cases will predict failure risks based on simulated mechanical stress distributions during obturation and residual microbial niches. A parallelized computational fluid dynamics framework will optimize irrigation protocols by modeling antimicrobial agent penetration into lateral canals and dentinal tubules under varying activation techniques. The HPC environment is essential for handling the 10^6-10^7 element meshes required for accurate dentin microstructure representation and for executing Monte Carlo analyses of biomechanical failure probabilities across anatomical variations. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for identifying high-risk cases requiring modified therapeutic strategies and data-driven guidelines for irrigation/obturation parameter selection based on patient-specific root canal morphology. This interdisciplinary synthesis of clinical endodontics, computational microbiology, and engineering mechanics aims to advance precision endodontic therapy while providing a novel framework for analyzing biomaterial-tissue-microbe interactions in confined anatomical spaces.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the morphology, physiology, and pathology of human dental pulp and periradicular tissues, and prepares dentists to diagnose and treat internal diseases and injuries of teeth. Includes instruction in theory and practice of endodontics; pulpal disease; relationship of endodontic conditions to other dental/oral health issues; endodontic operative technique; and patient care and management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform media influence on public opinion formation during complex sociopolitical events, with a focus on the interplay between legacy news outlets, social media networks, and emerging decentralized communication platforms. Traditional methods for analyzing media ecosystems struggle to process the scale and heterogeneity of modern communication data, particularly when examining temporal patterns, sentiment diffusion, and network-level information cascades across multiple modalities (text, video, audio). Our research will employ high-performance computing resources to implement a multimodal computational framework combining natural language processing, dynamic network analysis, and agent-based modeling. The proposed approach will process terabytes of timestamped media content from curated datasets spanning broadcast transcripts, social media posts, and podcast episodes, while simulating audience engagement patterns through parallelized discrete-event simulations. Computational tasks include transformer-based sentiment propagation models, community detection in temporal interaction networks, and large-scale topic alignment across heterogeneous media sources. Expected outcomes include new theoretical insights about attention economies in fragmented media environments, methodological advances in cross-platform communication analysis, and open-source tools for modeling information diffusion at societal scales. By leveraging GPU-accelerated machine learning and distributed memory architectures, this work will enable unprecedented granularity in examining how competing narratives emerge and stabilize across communication channels – a critical capability for addressing contemporary challenges in misinformation research, intercultural communication, and media effects scholarship. The requested resources directly support the development of computational social science capacity within communication studies while maintaining strict ethical protocols for large-scale media analysis.
cip_definition: An program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, research and research methods, and theories of communication, and that spans specialties within the field of communications. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of decentralized financial markets under heterogeneous agent behavior, with a focus on understanding how asymmetric information and varying risk preferences influence systemic stability. Traditional equilibrium models often fail to capture emergent phenomena, such as liquidity crises or contagion effects, due to their reliance on representative agents and linear assumptions. To address this gap, the research employs large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations to replicate complex interactions among diverse market participants, including institutional investors, algorithmic traders, and retail agents. The computational approach integrates adaptive learning algorithms, where agents dynamically update their strategies based on evolving market conditions and network-dependent information flows. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating millions of agents across thousands of parallelized market iterations, each with distinct behavioral parameters and network topologies. The project will utilize MPI-based parallelization for distributed memory architectures and GPU acceleration to optimize Monte Carlo sampling of parameter spaces. Key outcomes include quantifying the probability and severity of cascading failures under different regulatory scenarios, identifying early warning indicators of market fragility, and evaluating the efficacy of circuit-breaker mechanisms. Results will contribute to both academic and policy discussions by providing empirically grounded insights into non-linear market dynamics, enhancing predictive models for financial risk management. The computational framework developed will also serve as a scalable toolkit for future research in market microstructure and computational economics, enabling hypothesis testing at unprecedented granularity. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances the methodological frontier of economic simulation, bridging theoretical rigor with real-world applicability in decentralized financial systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in economics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the design and fitting of personalized ophthalmic lenses and eyewear, addressing variability in anatomical eye structures, facial geometries, and patient-specific visual needs. Current methods for lens adaptation and frame selection rely heavily on manual measurements and standardized templates, which may lead to suboptimal comfort, visual acuity, or long-term wearability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach integrating biomechanical simulations, optical ray-tracing, and machine learning. Finite element models will simulate the mechanical interaction between contact lenses, corneal topography, and tear film dynamics under dynamic conditions (e.g., blinking, eye movement). Concurrently, ray-tracing algorithms will evaluate optical performance across diverse pupil sizes and gaze angles, tailored to individual prescriptions. A parallelized machine learning framework will analyze datasets of 3D facial scans, historical fitting outcomes, and material properties to predict optimal frame geometries and lens parameters. These models require HPC resources due to the high resolution of anatomical meshes, iterative optimization loops, and the need for real-time parameter adjustments during simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for reducing trial-and-error in clinical fittings, enhancing precision in custom lens fabrication, and identifying design principles for underrepresented anatomical variations. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated lens-eye interactions, supporting future research in ophthalmic optics. By bridging computational engineering and opticianry practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based dispensing protocols, improve patient satisfaction, and reduce adaptation periods for complex prescriptions. The requested computing resources will enable scalable processing of multimodal patient data and foster training opportunities for students in computational opticianry applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern IT service ecosystems, driven by heterogeneous infrastructures and dynamic user demands, necessitates novel approaches to optimize administrative decision-making under uncertainty. This project addresses the challenge of real-time resource allocation in multi-tenant, edge-to-cloud service environments where traditional rule-based management systems fail to account for emergent operational patterns and cascading failures. We propose a hybrid computational framework combining graph-based anomaly detection, federated learning for privacy-aware workload forecasting, and multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to dynamically balance performance, energy efficiency, and service-level agreements. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to simulate large-scale service topologies using containerized microservice traces from public and private sector partners, encompassing over 100,000 concurrent service instances. Key computational challenges include parallelizing temporal graph neural networks for cross-layer dependency analysis and developing distributed MORL agents capable of negotiating conflicting optimization targets across administrative domains. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive service orchestration, validated against real-world incident response datasets from healthcare IoT and smart city deployments. The work advances computational methods in IT service management by introducing techniques for emergent behavior modeling in decentralized systems, with potential applications in critical infrastructure resilience and sustainable computing. Successful implementation requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep reinforcement learning workloads and high-memory instances to process service dependency graphs exceeding 1 billion edges.
cip_title: Computer/ Information Technology Services Administration and Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer/information technology services administration and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in business operations introduces novel liability risks, particularly concerning ethical failures such as algorithmic bias, privacy violations, and autonomous decision-making harms. Traditional actuarial models, which rely on historical data and static risk factors, are inadequate for quantifying these emerging, dynamically evolving risks. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for assessing AI ethics liability risks, enabling insurers to design tailored coverage products. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-modal datasets, including AI audit logs, legal dispute records, and real-time system outputs. Machine learning techniques, such as graph neural networks, will model interdependencies between AI system architectures and ethical risk propagation, while stochastic simulation will assess liability scenarios under varying regulatory environments. The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing to analyze evolving case law and regulatory guidelines, dynamically updating risk probabilities. Expected outcomes include a scalable risk quantification model that correlates technical system parameters with liability exposure, probabilistic forecasts of claim distributions, and a generative adversarial network (GAN)-based tool for simulating high-impact, low-probability ethical failure events. By bridging AI ethics and insurance underwriting, this research aims to establish foundational methodologies for a new class of liability insurance products, thereby supporting responsible AI adoption across industries. The project’s demands for parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and complex, multi-agent simulations necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve timely and actionable results.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage risk in organizational settings and provide insurance and risk-aversion services to businesses, individuals, and other organizations. Includes instruction in casualty insurance and general liability, property insurance, employee benefits, social and health insurance, loss adjustment, underwriting, risk theory, and pension planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that optimize medication safety and operational efficiency in pharmacy settings. A critical challenge in pharmacy practice is the risk of medication errors during dispensing, which can arise from factors such as workflow interruptions, high prescription volumes, or miscommunication. Current approaches to error prevention rely heavily on manual checks, which are time-intensive and inconsistent. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and discrete-event simulation (DES) to analyze historical prescription data, workflow patterns, and error reports. The ML component will identify risk factors and predict error-prone scenarios by training on anonymized datasets spanning prescription records, patient demographics, and staff scheduling logs. Concurrently, DES models will simulate pharmacy workflows under varying conditions (e.g., staffing levels, seasonal demand shifts) to quantify their impact on error rates and processing times. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these tasks, particularly for parallel processing of large datasets (>10^6 prescriptions) and iterative optimization of simulation parameters. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into workflow redesign, real-time error prediction tools, and evidence-based staffing recommendations. By reducing preventable errors and streamlining operations, this research directly supports pharmacy technicians’ roles in ensuring patient safety and maintaining regulatory compliance. The resulting models will be validated using retrospective data from partner community pharmacies, with potential for integration into pharmacy management software to enhance decision-making. This work bridges computational innovation and practical pharmacy operations, advancing the Health Professions field by demonstrating how HPC-driven analytics can transform traditional healthcare workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pharmacists, to prepare medications, provide medications and related assistance to patients, and manage pharmacy clinical and business operations. Includes instruction in medical and pharmaceutical terminology, principles of pharmacology and pharmaceutics, drug identification, pharmacy laboratory procedures, prescription interpretation, patient communication and education, safety procedures, record-keeping, measurement and testing techniques, pharmacy business operations, prescription preparation, logistics and dispensing operations, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Montessori pedagogy emphasizes individualized, self-directed learning within mixed-age classrooms, yet the dynamic interplay between student autonomy, teacher guidance, and environmental design remains understudied at scale. This project seeks to model the efficacy of Montessori instructional strategies using agent-based simulations to optimize teacher training frameworks. The research problem centers on identifying how computational modeling can predict the outcomes of Montessori practices—such as material selection, lesson sequencing, and classroom spatial organization—on student engagement and skill acquisition. Current studies rely on small observational datasets or qualitative assessments, limiting generalizability. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that replicates multi-agent classroom environments. The computational approach integrates behavioral data from Montessori classrooms (e.g., student-teacher interactions, material usage patterns, and movement logs) into adaptive algorithms that simulate learning trajectories under varying pedagogical conditions. Each agent will employ reinforcement learning to mimic child decision-making aligned with Montessori principles of intrinsic motivation. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess thousands of parameter combinations to identify optimal teacher interventions. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the stochasticity and combinatorial complexity inherent in modeling heterogeneous student cohorts over extended time horizons. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool to evaluate the impact of specific Montessori training modules on classroom outcomes, (2) data-driven recommendations for personalizing teacher guidance strategies, and (3) an open-source framework for simulating developmental pedagogies. This work will directly inform the design of competency-based assessments in Montessori teacher education programs, enhancing the scalability of training while preserving pedagogical fidelity. By bridging computational analytics with Montessori theory, the project advances a novel paradigm for evidence-driven teacher preparation in specialized educational methodologies.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Maria Montessori and her followers.

abstract: The proposed research focuses on developing a computational framework to optimize the design and control of decentralized quantum-thermal systems for next-generation energy-efficient computing architectures. As classical computing approaches physical limits in power density and heat dissipation, hybrid systems integrating quantum components with advanced thermal management strategies present a promising yet underexplored solution. The central challenge lies in modeling the nonlinear interplay between quantum information processing units, nanoscale heat transfer phenomena, and adaptive control systems—a multi-physics problem requiring simultaneous resolution of quantum master equations, phonon transport dynamics, and stochastic optimization at disparate timescales. This project will employ GPU-accelerated tensor network methods to simulate qubit arrays under thermal noise, coupled with finite-element analysis of nanostructured thermal interfaces. Machine learning surrogates will bridge quantum-thermal cross-domain interactions, enabling co-optimization through evolutionary algorithms deployed on high-performance computing clusters. Expected outcomes include predictive models for qubit coherence times under active cooling, optimized 3D integration geometries for hybrid quantum-classical chips, and open-source tools for quantum-thermal codesign. By addressing the critical gap between quantum computing potential and practical engineering constraints, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for implementing fault-tolerant quantum systems in real-world computing infrastructure. The requested computing resources will support large-scale parameter sweeps across material properties, device architectures, and control protocols, accelerating the transition from theoretical proposals to manufacturable quantum-thermal integrated systems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to solve a wide variety of practical problems in industry, social organization, public works, and commerce. Includes instruction in undifferentiated and individualized programs in engineering.

abstract: Plant diseases caused by airborne fungal pathogens pose significant threats to global food security. A critical challenge in managing these diseases is predicting long-distance spore dispersal, which drives rapid epidemic spread across regions. Current models lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale meteorological data, host landscape heterogeneity, and pathogen viability during transport, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computational framework to simulate atmospheric spore dispersal dynamics at unprecedented spatial and temporal granularity. Leveraging GPU-accelerated fluid dynamics solvers coupled with agent-based modeling, we will reconstruct turbulent transport processes across scales—from local canopy turbulence to synoptic weather patterns. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to assimilate real-time remote sensing data, refining predictions of deposition hotspots. The computational pipeline will parameterize biological viability thresholds using experimental data on UV tolerance and desiccation responses across key pathogenic fungi. By implementing ensemble simulations on heterogeneous computing architectures, we aim to quantify probabilistic dispersal frontiers under varying climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive platform for preemptive disease surveillance, enabling targeted fungicide deployment and resilience planning for staple crops. This interdisciplinary approach bridges micrometeorology, aerobiology, and phytopathology, advancing computational methodologies for sustainable agriculture. The requested resources will support iterative model calibration, large-scale climate scenario testing, and the generation of risk maps at farm-to-regional scales, directly addressing the urgent need for physics-informed decision tools in plant disease management.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: Current word processing tools often lack adaptive capabilities to optimize user efficiency and accuracy, particularly when handling large-scale documents or complex formatting tasks. This research project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and enhance text processing workflows. The core challenge lies in analyzing real-time user interactions, predicting formatting requirements, and minimizing errors without compromising processing speed—a task that demands significant computational power for parallelizable tasks such as keystroke pattern analysis, automated style optimization, and dynamic error correction. Using machine learning algorithms trained on large datasets of user-generated documents and interaction logs, the project will create predictive models to anticipate formatting adjustments and streamline document assembly processes. HPC clusters will enable rapid iteration of these models across diverse scenarios, including multi-user collaborative environments and high-volume batch processing. Additionally, the research will simulate stress-testing scenarios to evaluate system performance under extreme document sizes (e.g., >10^6 words) or concurrent user loads. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for intelligent document automation, benchmarks for computational efficiency in word processing tasks, and insights into human-computer interaction patterns that can inform future software design. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with user-centric design principles, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for computational tools in text processing, with potential applications in education, technical writing, and enterprise document management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize sustainable interior design solutions for complex residential and commercial environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in spatial efficiency, environmental systems integration, and user-centered functionality. Current design practices often rely on iterative manual adjustments or simplified software tools that inadequately model dynamic variables such as airflow, acoustics, and energy consumption. This limitation hinders the ability to holistically evaluate designs against evolving building codes, accessibility standards, and sustainability targets. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational approach combining parametric design algorithms, machine learning-driven optimization, and physics-based simulations. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large design spaces, including automated layout generation for furniture and fixtures, coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and acoustic performance. Machine learning models trained on historical design datasets will predict user comfort metrics, while real-time ray tracing will simulate natural and artificial lighting scenarios. The integration of these tools into a unified workflow will allow designers to rapidly prototype and validate configurations that balance aesthetic, functional, and regulatory requirements. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source platform for data-driven interior design, validated through case studies in mixed-use urban developments and adaptive reuse projects. By enabling precise simulation of material properties, energy flows, and ergonomic factors, this research aims to reduce resource waste in construction, enhance occupant well-being, and establish new benchmarks for computationally augmented design processes in the visual arts. The project will also advance pedagogical frameworks for integrating HPC workflows into interior design curricula, preparing students to address next-generation challenges in smart building technologies and circular design principles.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional planning, designing, equipping, and furnishing of residential and commercial interior spaces. Includes instruction in computer applications, drafting, and graphic techniques; principles of interior lighting, acoustics, systems integration, and color coordination; furniture and furnishings; textiles and their finishing; the history of interior design and period styles; basic structural design; building codes and inspection regulations; and applications to office, hotel, factory, restaurant and housing design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of physiological and environmental factors influencing labor progression in low-intervention birth settings, a critical yet understudied area within direct-entry midwifery care. While maternal health outcomes are well-researched in hospital contexts, the dynamic interplay of biomechanical, hormonal, and psychosocial variables in community-based births remains poorly quantified, limiting evidence-based tools for midwives managing physiological labor. We propose to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including longitudinal biometric data from wearable sensors (uterine activity, fetal heart rate), maternal microbiome profiles, and geospatial environmental stress indicators—to develop multiscale computational models predicting labor patterns and emergent complications. The computational workflow will employ federated learning architectures to preserve privacy across decentralized clinical partners, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate cervicodynamic responses to endogenous oxytocin fluctuations. HPC resources are essential for processing high-frequency biosensor streams (≥100 Hz sampling rates) across 10,000+ simulated labor hours, optimizing hyperparameters in recurrent neural networks, and conducting Monte Carlo analyses of intervention timing impacts on perinatal outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support framework identifying subtle risk signatures for postpartum hemorrhage or fetal distress, validated against a retrospective cohort of 1,200 community births. By bridging computational biology and midwifery practice, this work aims to establish quantitative biomarkers for physiological birth while maintaining the low-intervention philosophy central to direct-entry care paradigms. The resulting models will inform clinical guidelines for when and how to safely escalate care, directly addressing jurisdictional challenges in midwifery licensure related to emergency management competencies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide pre-natal, natural birth, and immediate postpartum care to pregnant women in jurisdictions licensing direct (non-nursing) training for midwives. Includes instruction in basic obstetrics, women's health, fetal development, childbirth education, maternal nutrition and health, labor support, natural childbirth, postpartum support, prebirth counseling and risk screening, management of obstetric emergencies, patient referral, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making in high-volume dining environments, integrating real-time operational data with predictive models to enhance service efficiency and customer experience. Traditional food service management relies on heuristic practices and static scheduling, which often fail to adapt to variable customer flow, staffing constraints, and resource availability. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining agent-based modeling, reinforcement learning, and discrete-event simulation to create adaptive systems for table allocation, server routing, and kitchen-staff coordination. The research will leverage anonymized customer traffic data, staff performance metrics, and sensor-derived dining duration patterns from partner restaurants to parameterize simulations. Computational experiments will test multi-objective optimization strategies that balance wait times, server workload equity, and revenue targets under stochastic demand. By scaling these simulations across thousands of parallelized scenarios using GPU-accelerated computing resources, the project aims to identify robust operational policies resilient to peak-hour variability and unforeseen disruptions. Anticipated outcomes include open-source decision-support tools for restaurant managers, predictive analytics modules for staff scheduling, and novel metrics for quantifying service quality through temporal-spatial analysis of customer-server interactions. This work bridges computational social science and operations research, offering methodological innovations for service industries while maintaining focus on human-centric outcomes in hospitality management. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of real-world dining ecosystems, enabling rapid iteration of optimization algorithms across diverse operational contexts.
cip_title: Food Service, Waiter/Waitress, and Dining Room Management/Manager.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve food to customers in formal or informal settings.  Includes instruction in the nutritional, sensory, and functional properties of food and its ingredients; food services principles; table and counter services; dining room operations and procedures; service personnel supervision and management; communication skills; business math; safety; and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay between legal frameworks, energy transition policies, and environmental justice outcomes in transboundary river basins. The research focuses on the legal and regulatory challenges of balancing hydropower development, ecological preservation, and Indigenous land rights across jurisdictions with conflicting governance models. Current policy evaluation methods lack the capacity to model multi-scalar legal interactions or simulate long-term socio-ecological impacts under evolving climate scenarios. The proposed computational approach combines legal text mining, agent-based modeling, and geospatial analysis to create a novel decision-support framework. Natural language processing will be applied to extract obligations and constraints from international water treaties, national energy policies, and judicial rulings, while hydrological-economic models will simulate basin-wide outcomes under different regulatory scenarios. By integrating legal corpus analysis with dynamic systems modeling, the project aims to quantify how variance in liability structures, permitting regimes, and compensation mechanisms affects both infrastructure investment patterns and ecosystem health metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for evaluating legal compatibility in transboundary energy projects and predictive models of policy intervention effectiveness under climate uncertainty. This work addresses critical gaps in energy governance research by enabling quantitative analysis of legal systems as dynamic components of coupled human-environment systems, rather than static textual frameworks. The requested HPC resources will support large-scale parallel processing of legal documents, Monte Carlo simulations of policy pathways, and high-resolution spatial-temporal analysis of ecological impacts across multi-decadal horizons. Results will provide evidence-based insights for reconciling clean energy targets with procedural justice requirements in contested resource landscapes.
cip_title: Energy, Environment, and Natural Resources Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing the energy industry, environmental protection, natural resources and land use, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale computational analysis of Polish linguistic and literary corpora, addressing critical gaps in diachronic and dialectal studies of the Polish language. While existing scholarship has produced foundational textual archives, the integration of advanced computational methods remains limited, particularly for analyzing morphosyntactic evolution, regional dialect variation, and stylistic patterns across centuries of Polish literature. The primary research problem centers on processing and modeling complex linguistic features in historical and contemporary Polish texts—tasks requiring significant computational capacity due to the language’s rich inflectional morphology, dialect diversity, and the scarcity of digitized resources optimized for machine learning. Proposed computational approaches include deploying NLP pipelines tailored for Polish to process multi-century textual data (14th–21st centuries), training transformer-based models for dialect classification, and implementing phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct historical language change. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale corpora, including digitized manuscripts, dialect recordings, and modern sociolectal data, while supporting GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models for semantic and stylistic analysis. Expected outcomes include (1) the first comprehensive digital atlas of Polish dialect evolution, mapping phonological and lexical shifts across time and space; (2) computational models quantifying the influence of Romantic-era literature on contemporary Polish syntax; and (3) open-access tools for morphological disambiguation and historical text normalization. These outputs will provide novel methodologies for Slavic linguistics, enhance preservation efforts for endangered regional dialects, and establish infrastructure for future computational research in Polish studies. The project’s scale—analyzing over 10 million text tokens across 40+ dialect variants—necessitates HPC capabilities unavailable through standard institutional resources, particularly for memory-intensive corpus alignment and real-time visualization of multidimensional linguistic data.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization frameworks for complex industrial systems under uncertainty, with applications in supply chain resilience and smart manufacturing. Industrial systems increasingly face disruptions from market volatility, resource constraints, and evolving sustainability requirements, necessitating advanced computational tools to balance competing objectives. Current methods struggle with real-time adaptability when handling high-dimensional decision spaces or nonlinear constraints inherent in integrated production-distribution networks. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational architecture combining stochastic programming, agent-based simulation, and data-driven surrogate modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized scenario generation for multi-objective optimization models, leveraging Monte Carlo sampling and distributed solvers to evaluate resilience strategies across diverse risk profiles. A key innovation involves embedding machine learning surrogates within decomposition algorithms to approximate complex system dynamics, reducing computational bottlenecks in iterative optimization loops. The project will validate these methods using case studies from semiconductor manufacturing and healthcare logistics, incorporating terabyte-scale operational datasets to train digital twin models. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source optimization toolkits for adaptive resource allocation under uncertainty, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational efficiency and solution quality across HPC configurations, and (3) generalized principles for balancing sustainability metrics with operational costs in multi-echelon systems. By overcoming scalability limits in traditional operations research methods, this work will provide practitioners with decision-support tools capable of handling modern industrial complexity while maintaining interpretability. The requested computing resources are critical for managing memory-intensive simulations, hyperparameter tuning across optimization modules, and validating results against industry-standard digital twin platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Includes instruction in applied mathematics, physical sciences, the social sciences, engineering analysis, systems design, computer applications, and forecasting and evaluation methodology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in precision nutrition, an emerging interdisciplinary domain integrating computational modeling, behavioral science, and metabolomics. Traditional nutritional frameworks often rely on population-level dietary guidelines, which fail to account for individual variability in metabolic responses, gut microbiome composition, and psychosocial factors influencing eating behaviors. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational architecture to model personalized nutrition pathways, enabling dynamic predictions of dietary outcomes based on multi-modal data inputs. The proposed approach combines machine learning (ML) with agent-based simulations to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including time-series metabolomic profiles, microbiome sequencing data, and longitudinal behavioral surveys. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle high-dimensional feature spaces and stochastic variability inherent in biological systems. Key innovations include the integration of gradient-boosted decision trees with mechanistic models of nutrient absorption and the development of hybrid algorithms to simulate diet-microbiome-host interactions across temporal scales. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source framework for precision nutrition analytics, validated against clinical trial data, capable of generating individualized dietary recommendations with quantified uncertainty metrics. This work addresses a critical gap in non-engineering computational nutrition science by creating tools to disentangle complex diet-disease relationships while accounting for socioeconomic and cultural influences on food choices. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, cross-validation of ensemble models, and real-time simulation of intervention scenarios—tasks infeasible on local infrastructure. By bridging computational scalability with nutritional epidemiology, this project aims to establish foundational methodologies for next-generation dietary guidance systems, with potential applications in chronic disease prevention and health equity initiatives.
cip_title: Foods, Nutrition, and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foods, nutrition, and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the regulatory dynamics of mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in bacterial populations under stress-induced mutagenesis. While MGEs such as transposons and integrative-conjugative elements drive horizontal gene transfer and genome plasticity, their activity under nutrient limitation, antibiotic exposure, or host immune pressure remains poorly characterized at the nucleotide-resolution level. We propose to integrate comparative genomics of longitudinal clinical *Escherichia coli* isolates with agent-based modeling to map the spatiotemporal activation patterns of MGEs during chronic infections. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process whole-genome sequencing data from 500+ isolates, detect structural variants and recombination events using graph-based genome alignment tools (e.g., PanGraph), and simulate population-level MGE dynamics under stochastic models of stress response. Custom scripts will parameterize mutation rates, horizontal transfer efficiency, and selection pressures derived from empirical data. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated phylogenetic inference (IQ-TREE) and parallelized simulations via SLURM job arrays to handle ~10^6 agent interactions per run. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved regulatory motifs associated with stress-induced MGE activation, (2) predictive models linking environmental cues to MGE-mediated antibiotic resistance dissemination, and (3) open-source tools for simulating context-dependent genome plasticity. This work will directly inform therapeutic strategies to counteract adaptive mutagenesis in pathogens, with broader implications for understanding evolutionary constraints on heritable information stability. The scale of genomic data (≥20 TB) and iterative simulation requirements (≥50,000 CPU-hr) necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve biologically meaningful resolution within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of genetic structures and mechanisms of organisms, including bacteria, phages, and viruses. Includes instruction in the replication, expression, transfer, structure, maintenance, and stability of heritable information in DNA, RNA, and proteins; the regulation of these processes; and neurogenetics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of geoenvironmental systems, such as waste containment facilities and soil stabilization projects, demands advanced predictive models to account for coupled thermal, hydraulic, mechanical, and chemical (THMC) processes over extended timescales. Traditional analytical and experimental methods often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between soil behavior, contaminant transport, and geosynthetic material performance under dynamic environmental loads, leading to conservative designs with high uncertainty. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate multiphysics processes in geotechnical and geoenvironmental systems, with a focus on optimizing the long-term performance of engineered barriers in landfills and contaminated site remediation. The research will employ parallelized finite element modeling using open-source platforms (e.g., FEniCS, OpenGeoSys) to resolve coupled THMC phenomena across spatial scales, validated against laboratory and field data. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate parameter calibration and sensitivity analysis, particularly for heterogeneous soil profiles and time-dependent material degradation. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the computational burden of 3D transient simulations involving 10^6–10^7 degrees of freedom, Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification, and multi-objective optimization of design parameters. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for assessing clay liner integrity under chemical attack, quantifying leachate migration risks in fractured geomembranes, and optimizing biocementation protocols for soil stabilization. The results will advance the scientific basis for sustainable geoenvironmental infrastructure design, directly supporting climate-resilient waste management strategies and reducing the environmental footprint of geotechnical construction. This work aligns with national priorities in infrastructure resilience and contaminated land rehabilitation, offering transferable computational methodologies for the broader civil engineering community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply geotechnical engineering methods, which deal with the analysis, design and construction of earth and earth supported structures, to the application of environmental problems, such as waste containment, waste disposal, construction of land fills, soil permeation, soil analysis, and soil improvement. Includes instruction in soil mechanics, soil dynamics, soil behavior, waste management and containment systems, geosynthetics, geochemistry, earth structures, geoenvironmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, earthquake engineering, and foundation engineering

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern agricultural systems, characterized by dynamic interactions between climate variability, market fluctuations, soil health, and livestock productivity, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize farm and ranch management decisions. Current approaches often rely on static models or fragmented datasets, limiting their ability to address multi-dimensional challenges such as real-time resource allocation, long-term financial planning, and risk mitigation under uncertainty. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision support framework to integrate heterogeneous data streams—including soil sensor networks, satellite imagery, livestock biometrics, and commodity pricing trends—into predictive models for farm operational planning. The computational approach will leverage agent-based modeling to simulate farm ecosystems at scale, coupling biophysical processes (e.g., crop growth, pasture rotation) with economic decision-making algorithms. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical and real-time data to forecast yield outcomes, input requirements, and market risks under diverse scenarios. Monte Carlo simulations will quantify financial uncertainties related to input costs, government policy changes, and climate extremes, enabling probabilistic budgeting and estate planning strategies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space, iterative optimization of management plans, and sensitivity analyses across temporal scales (daily operations to multi-year succession planning). Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for adaptive farm management, validated against empirical data from partner operations in diverse agroecological zones. This work will advance precision agriculture by bridging gaps between agronomic models and business optimization, ultimately enhancing the economic resilience and environmental sustainability of farm enterprises. The scalable architecture will support extension services in translating research outputs into user-friendly interfaces for producers with varying operational scales and technological capacities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage farms, ranches, and similar enterprises. Includes instruction in applicable agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, taxation, capitalization, purchasing, government programs and regulations, operational planning and budgeting, contracts and negotiation, and estate planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in professional and technical communication (PTC) through large-scale computational analysis of multimodal document design patterns. The research problem centers on the lack of systematic, data-driven frameworks for understanding how rhetorical strategies—such as visual hierarchy, semantic coherence, and interactive elements—shape user engagement and comprehension in complex technical documents. Current methods for analyzing such documents rely on manual coding or small-scale qualitative studies, limiting generalizability and scalability. This project will employ computational text analysis, computer vision algorithms, and machine learning models to analyze a corpus of over 100,000 technical documents (e.g., user manuals, white papers, grant proposals, and scientific reports) drawn from open-access repositories and industry partnerships. Using HPC resources, we will train models to identify correlations between document structures (e.g., layout, hyperlink density, image-text alignment) and measurable outcomes like readability scores, user task completion rates, and accessibility compliance metrics. The computational workflow will integrate NLP tools for semantic segmentation, OpenCV for visual feature extraction, and graph-based algorithms to map intra-document navigational patterns. Outcomes will include (1) a publicly available annotated dataset of technical documents tagged with rhetorical and design features, (2) predictive models to guide adaptive document authoring tools, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing multimodal communication in STEM and business contexts. This work directly supports the program’s focus on advancing digital literacy and document usability research while providing graduate students with training in computational humanities methodologies. By scaling analysis beyond manual capabilities, HPC resources will enable novel insights into how technical writers can harness emerging technologies to meet evolving demands for clarity, accessibility, and user-centered design.
cip_title: Professional, Technical, Business, and Scientific Writing
cip_definition: A program that focuses on professional, technical, business, and scientific writing; and that prepares individuals for academic positions or for professional careers as writers, editors, researchers, and related careers in business, government, non-profits, and the professions. Includes instruction in theories of rhetoric, writing, and digital literacy; document design, production, and management; visual rhetoric and multimedia composition; documentation development; usability testing; web writing; and publishing in print and electronic media.

abstract: Critically ill surgical patients, particularly those with multisystem trauma or sepsis-induced organ dysfunction, exhibit complex, dynamic physiological states that challenge conventional treatment paradigms. Existing risk stratification tools often lack the granularity to predict rapid clinical deterioration or personalize resuscitation strategies in real time. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating multimodal patient data—including high-frequency vital sign streams, electronic health records, and multi-omics biomarkers—to model the nonlinear interactions driving critical illness progression. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement ensemble machine learning architectures to process terabyte-scale datasets from 2,500 retrospective trauma cases, capturing temporal patterns in hemodynamic instability, coagulopathy, and immune dysregulation. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular responses to therapeutic interventions, while GPU-accelerated finite element analysis will map regional perfusion dynamics in organ-specific injury models. Validated against a prospective cohort of 300 surgical ICU patients, the platform aims to predict the probability of secondary organ failure 6-12 hours before clinical manifestation, with target AUC >0.92. Additional outcomes include identifying novel biomarker signatures of endothelial dysfunction and generating personalized fluid resuscitation protocols via reinforcement learning. By elucidating the coupling between macroscale physiology and molecular pathways, this work addresses a critical gap in dynamic decision-support systems for surgical intensivists. The requested HPC allocation will enable parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams, reduce model training times from weeks to days, and support the parameter optimization required for real-time clinical deployment. Successful implementation could transform the management of critically injured patients by enabling preemptive, precision interventions tailored to evolving pathophysiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares surgeons in the diagnosis, treatment, and support of critically ill and injured patients, particularly trauma victims and patients with multiple organ dysfunction.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and cognitive demands of clinical skill acquisition in pre-nursing students, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and optimize training protocols. Current approaches to teaching foundational clinical skills—such as patient transfer techniques or sterile field management—rely on static mannequins or observational learning, which lack dynamic feedback on ergonomic efficiency or error propagation. To address this gap, we propose a multimodal simulation environment integrating motion capture data, physiological stress markers, and machine learning to predict skill mastery and injury risk. The computational pipeline will process high-dimensional datasets from wearable sensors and video recordings of student performance during simulated tasks, using finite element modeling to assess joint loads and muscle activation patterns. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively adapt training scenarios to individual learning trajectories, optimizing task difficulty and feedback timing. By deploying these models on HPC clusters, we aim to achieve real-time analysis of complex biomechanical interactions and large-scale validation across diverse student cohorts. Expected outcomes include personalized training recommendations to reduce repetitive strain injuries and accelerate competency development. This work bridges gaps between health sciences education, computational biomechanics, and adaptive learning systems, offering a novel tool to enhance pre-nursing curricula while addressing musculoskeletal health—a critical yet understudied factor in clinical preparedness. The resulting open-source framework will provide a scalable platform for future research in skill-based training across health professions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in Nursing.

abstract: The proposed research addresses unresolved questions in the statistical mechanics of turbulent fluid systems, focusing on energy cascades and intermittency in non-equilibrium regimes. Traditional analytical models struggle to capture the multi-scale, nonlinear interactions governing these phenomena, particularly in three-dimensional flows with variable boundary conditions. This project will employ high-resolution direct numerical simulations (DNS) of the Navier-Stokes equations to resolve inertial-range dynamics across spatial and temporal scales inaccessible to laboratory experiments. A hybrid spectral-finite difference method will be implemented to balance accuracy and computational efficiency, with adaptive mesh refinement targeting regions of high vorticity. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed-memory parallelism to achieve the necessary scale, requiring access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources with dedicated nodes for sustained petascale workloads. Key objectives include quantifying anomalous scaling exponents in turbulent kinetic energy spectra, characterizing rare extreme events contributing to intermittency, and validating recently proposed universality classes for dissipation field structures. Data analysis pipelines will employ wavelet-based techniques and machine learning classifiers to identify coherent structures in simulation outputs. Expected outcomes include new empirical constraints for theoretical models of turbulent transport, with implications for improving subgrid-scale parameterizations in weather prediction and fusion plasma confinement systems. The generated datasets will be made publicly available through a curated repository, supporting reproducibility and cross-disciplinary comparisons. By resolving long-standing discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental observations, this work aims to advance fundamental understanding of turbulence while demonstrating the critical role of HPC resources in tackling computationally intractable problems in classical physics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric urology faces critical challenges in managing congenital and acquired genitourinary tract anomalies, where patient-specific anatomical variability and dynamic physiological processes complicate treatment optimization. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols, which may not account for the complex biomechanical interactions inherent to pediatric urinary and reproductive systems. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate genitourinary pathophysiology and predict surgical outcomes, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps. The research will focus on two key areas: (1) multi-scale modeling of bladder dynamics in neurogenic bladder dysfunction to assess tissue remodeling and compliance under varying therapeutic pressures, and (2) finite element analysis of urethral reconstruction techniques for hypospadias, incorporating patient-specific 3D reconstructions from MRI and ultrasound data. Computational pipelines will integrate machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective clinical datasets to identify biomarkers predictive of post-surgical complications. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution imaging datasets (>10 TB), running parallelized fluid-structure interaction simulations, and optimizing hyperparameters for deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to stratify surgical risks, virtual platforms for preoperative planning, and mechanistic insights into long-term tissue adaptation. By bridging computational biomechanics with clinical data, this work aims to establish a framework for personalized interventions in pediatric urology, reducing revision surgeries and improving quality of life for patients with complex genitourinary anomalies. The computational models and datasets generated will be disseminated as open-source resources to accelerate translational research in the field.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals in the study, prevention, and management of congenital, childhood-acquired, and overlapping adolescent anomalies of the genitourinary tract, including problems, diseases, tumors, and traumas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational visual arts and generative design, addressing the challenge of creating scalable, interactive tools for real-time artistic creation and analysis. Current methods for generating high-resolution digital art, simulating dynamic visual environments, or analyzing large-scale media datasets are constrained by conventional computing infrastructures, which lack the capacity to process complex generative algorithms or render immersive 3D models efficiently. This limitation hinders experimentation with emerging techniques such as neural style transfer, physically based rendering (PBR) at scale, and AI-driven design optimization. The proposed research will develop and deploy GPU-accelerated workflows to train generative adversarial networks (GANs) for procedural art generation, simulate light-field interactions in mixed-reality environments, and analyze patterns in historical visual media archives. Computational methods will integrate PyTorch and TensorFlow frameworks for machine learning tasks, OpenGL/Vulkan for real-time rendering, and custom CUDA kernels to optimize memory-intensive operations. By parallelizing tasks across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce rendering times for 4K/8K visual outputs by 70–80%, enable multi-user collaboration in shared virtual studios, and facilitate the analysis of terabyte-scale art datasets to identify cultural trends. Outcomes will include open-source tools for artists and designers, a publicly accessible repository of computationally generated artworks, and peer-reviewed studies on the intersection of HPC and creative practice. This work will expand the technical frontiers of digital art production, offering new methodologies for interdisciplinary research in visual culture, media studies, and computational design.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in visual and performing arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of large-scale musical datasets, with a focus on identifying cross-cultural patterns in rhythmic and melodic structures.
