The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, systematic methods for analyzing music as a dynamic, multimodal art form, particularly when integrating audio recordings, symbolic notation (e.g., MIDI, sheet music), and ethnographic performance data. Traditional approaches to musicology often rely on manual annotation or limited sample sizes, which restricts the ability to detect macro-level trends or quantify the influence of sociocultural factors on musical evolution. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining signal processing, graph theory, and machine learning to model musical works as temporal networks, where nodes represent discrete musical events (e.g., notes, rhythmic units) and edges encode relational features such as harmonic progression, timbral similarity, or choreographic coordination in performed works. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of over 100,000 audio and score-based datasets from open-access archives, as well as GPU-accelerated training of transformer-based models for style transfer analysis across genres and historical periods. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for computational musicology optimized for distributed computing environments, (2) quantitative models linking specific rhythmic motifs to regional dance traditions, and (3) a novel taxonomy of improvisational practices in global music cultures derived from latent feature analysis. By bridging computational methods with performing arts research, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying music as both an acoustic phenomenon and a culturally embedded practice, with applications in music education, digital humanities, and the preservation of intangible cultural heritage. The scale of data and complexity of multimodal alignment necessitate the requested HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust, generalizable results.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of music and the performing arts. Includes instruction in music, dance, and other performing arts media.

abstract: Chronic pain remains a complex clinical challenge with heterogeneous underlying mechanisms and variable treatment responses, necessitating advanced approaches to personalize care. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies often rely on subjective assessments or generalized protocols, which fail to account for multidimensional biological, psychological, and social factors. This project proposes to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets, including neuroimaging, genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and patient-reported outcome data. The primary objective is to develop predictive models that identify pain subtypes, forecast treatment efficacy, and uncover novel biomarkers. A machine learning framework will integrate these datasets to map interactions between genetic polymorphisms, neural circuit dysregulation, and pharmacological outcomes. Computational pipelines will process high-resolution functional MRI scans to quantify dynamic pain-related brain activity, while parallelized genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will identify loci associated with pain chronicity and opioid response variability. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) algorithms will extract clinically relevant features from unstructured EHR notes to enhance predictive accuracy. The scale and complexity of these analyses—spanning terabytes of imaging data, millions of genetic variants, and longitudinal clinical records—demand the parallel processing, large memory capacity, and high-speed storage unique to HPC systems. Expected outcomes include validated computational models for pain subtyping, decision-support tools for targeted therapy selection, and a publicly accessible database linking pain phenotypes to multi-omics profiles. This work will advance precision pain medicine by bridging mechanistic insights with clinical translation, ultimately reducing trial-and-error prescribing and improving functional outcomes for diverse patient populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of the entire range of painful disorders, either as a primary physician or consultant, for patients experiencing problems with acute, chronic, and/or cancer pain in both hospital and ambulatory settings.

abstract: Livestock diseases pose significant challenges to global food security, animal welfare, and agricultural economies. Traditional approaches to enhancing disease resistance through selective breeding are constrained by the polygenic nature of immune traits and the computational limitations of analyzing large-scale genomic datasets. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these barriers by integrating multi-omics data with machine learning models. We will develop a computational framework to identify genetic markers associated with disease resilience in cattle, simulate the impact of these markers on herd-level disease dynamics, and optimize breeding strategies using evolutionary algorithms. The research involves processing whole-genome sequences from 10,000 cattle, integrating transcriptomic and metabolomic data to contextualize genotype-phenotype relationships, and training deep neural networks to predict disease susceptibility. Agent-based models will then evaluate how selected genetic profiles influence pathogen transmission within heterogeneous herds. By enabling rapid analysis of complex datasets and high-resolution simulations, HPC resources will facilitate the design of precision breeding programs that enhance genetic resilience while maintaining productivity traits. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of candidate genetic markers, predictive models for livestock health management, and scalable protocols for genomic selection in diverse production environments. This work aligns with global priorities for sustainable livestock production by reducing reliance on antimicrobials and improving animal welfare through genetics-driven solutions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of livestock animals and the production and handling of meat and other products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, range science, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing wine program management in hospitality settings, with a focus on bridging data-driven insights and sommelier expertise. The core challenge lies in synthesizing heterogeneous datasets—including regional climate patterns, historical consumer preference data, chemical composition profiles of wines, and real-time sales metrics—into actionable models that can guide inventory selection, pricing strategies, and personalized pairing recommendations. Current industry practices rely heavily on heuristic knowledge, which may not scale effectively given increasing market complexity, climate-driven variability in wine production, and shifting consumer trends. The proposed computational approach integrates geospatial analysis of terroir characteristics, machine learning-based taste preference clustering, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to simulate dynamic wine program scenarios. By employing graph neural networks, the models will map relationships between physicochemical wine properties (e.g., tannin structure, acidity) and sensory descriptors, enabling prediction of optimal food pairings under varying menu constraints. A parallelized Monte Carlo framework will assess supply chain risks related to vintage variability and global distribution challenges. The computational workload necessitates HPC infrastructure due to the high dimensionality of datasets (10^6+ wine labels with 200+ attributes each), real-time sensor data from smart cellars, and the need for ensemble modeling across climate projection scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for sommeliers to simulate inventory resilience under environmental and economic stressors, alongside a novel flavor interaction graph database. This interdisciplinary work advances computational gastronomy methods while addressing critical gaps in sustainable hospitality management, offering a template for data-enhanced decision-making in niche culinary domains traditionally governed by artisanal practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage wine selection, purchasing, storage, sales, and service for a variety of establishments in the hospitality industry. Includes instruction in wine production, wine regions of the world, wine tasting, food and wine matching, service techniques, and wine program management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biomedical systems, such as adaptive prosthetics and biohybrid devices, demands high-resolution modeling to capture multiscale interactions between biological tissues, synthetic materials, and dynamic physiological environments. Current limitations in computational power restrict the ability to simulate these systems at clinically relevant spatiotemporal scales, hindering the optimization of device functionality and patient-specific design. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multi-physics framework for simulating biomechanical, electrochemical, and fluid-structure interactions in bioengineered systems. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) creating patient-specific models of neuromuscular-prosthetic interfaces to predict stress distributions, metabolic activity, and long-term tissue remodeling under cyclic loading, and (2) optimizing the design of soft robotic assistive devices through coupled fluid dynamics and machine learning algorithms that account for real-time physiological feedback. Computational methods will integrate finite element analysis, agent-based modeling, and convolutional neural networks trained on high-resolution imaging datasets (MRI, micro-CT) to capture anatomical variability. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations across multiple fidelity scales, reducing runtime for complex optimization tasks from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for reducing implant failure rates, a computational pipeline for personalized prosthetic design, and open-source tools for simulating biohybrid systems. These advances will directly support translational research in rehabilitation engineering and contribute to the development of adaptive biomedical devices that dynamically respond to physiological changes. The requested computing resources are critical for handling datasets exceeding 100TB, executing GPU-accelerated deep learning workflows, and maintaining the iterative optimization cycles required for clinically actionable results.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of biomedical and health systems and products such as integrated biomedical systems, instrumentation, medical information systems, artificial organs and prostheses, and health management and care delivery systems.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) necessitates scalable, evidence-based strategies for designing personalized educational interventions. Current approaches to developing individualized education plans (IEPs) for students with autism rely heavily on manual observation and trial-and-error adjustments, which are time-intensive and lack predictive precision. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model learning behaviors and predict optimal intervention strategies for students with ASD, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale data synthesis and real-time analytics. The research problem centers on bridging the gap between heterogeneous behavioral data—drawn from classroom interactions, sensory processing assessments, and communication logs—and actionable pedagogical recommendations. We will employ machine learning techniques, including multimodal deep learning and reinforcement learning, to analyze longitudinal datasets encompassing video recordings, biometric sensor outputs, and academic performance metrics from 500+ students across diverse educational settings. Computational models will be trained to identify patterns in skill acquisition trajectories, sensory overload triggers, and social communication barriers, with parallelized simulations testing hypothetical intervention scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-dimensional data (e.g., 30,000+ hours of annotated video), optimizing hyperparameters across neural architectures, and running ensemble models that integrate domain knowledge from special education frameworks. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool to recommend IEP components with quantified success probabilities, (2) generative models of student-teacher interaction dynamics to inform adaptive teaching strategies, and (3) open-source code for behavior pattern recognition tailored to low-resource school districts. By computationally encoding evidence-based practices in autism education, this work aims to empower educators with data-driven decision-support systems, ultimately improving the scalability and efficacy of specialized instruction for neurodiverse learners.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Autism
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with autism, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with autism, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising autistic students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Emerging challenges in multimedia production and distribution necessitate advanced computational resources to address scalability, real-time processing, and data-intensive analytics. This project seeks to utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop innovative frameworks for optimizing broadcast workflows, enhancing content personalization, and evaluating regulatory compliance in dynamic media environments. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) implementing machine learning models for automated analysis of audience engagement patterns across multi-platform content streams, (2) simulating large-scale broadcast network performance under varying urban infrastructure scenarios, and (3) creating GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines for real-time production of immersive media formats. By processing terabytes of historical viewership data and social media interactions, neural networks will identify latent trends in content consumption, enabling proactive programming strategies. Concurrently, finite-difference time-domain simulations will model electromagnetic wave propagation to optimize transmitter placement for next-generation broadcast standards. The computational demands of these tasks—including parallel processing of 4K/8K video assets and complex ray-tracing calculations—exceed the capabilities of local workstations, necessitating cluster-based computing with dedicated GPU nodes and high-throughput storage systems. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for predictive analytics in audience behavior, evidence-based guidelines for broadcast infrastructure modernization, and a scalable architecture for AI-assisted content creation. These contributions will advance scholarly understanding of computational media systems while providing industry stakeholders with practical solutions to emerging technological and operational challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, methods, and techniques used to plan, produce, and distribute audio and video programs and messages, and that prepares individuals to function as staff, producers, directors, and managers of radio and television shows and media organizations. Includes instruction in media aesthetics; planning, scheduling, and production; writing and editing; performing and directing; personnel and facilities management; marketing and distribution; media regulations, law, and policy; and principles of broadcast technology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the relationship between urban green space design and community physical activity patterns, a critical yet understudied intersection of recreational infrastructure, human movement dynamics, and public health outcomes. Current approaches to park planning rely on coarse demographic data and static observational metrics, failing to capture the complex interplay of spatial configurations, temporal usage fluctuations, and individualized movement signatures that shape activity engagement. The research employs agent-based modeling (ABM) paired with machine learning-driven analysis of anonymized wearable device data (heart rate, GPS traces, accelerometry) from diverse populations across 15 metropolitan regions. Computational workflows will integrate geospatial park topology datasets, climate conditions, and sociocultural preference indicators to simulate activity emergence under varying design scenarios. Key challenges include scaling ABM frameworks to process 10^6+ agent interactions across multi-year simulations, training graph neural networks on heterogeneous sensor data streams, and optimizing parameter space exploration for evidence-based design recommendations. Expected outcomes include predictive models quantifying how specific amenities (e.g., trail connectivity, obstacle density, shaded rest areas) differentially influence sustained moderate-to-vigorous physical activity across age groups and mobility capacities. This work will establish the first computational framework to systematically evaluate recreational infrastructure through the lens of kinesiological adaptation, informing equitable design standards that bridge urban planning, preventive health, and adaptive mobility needs. Successful implementation requires dedicated GPU nodes for parallelized simulation batches and high-memory nodes for large-scale spatial-temporal dataset integration, resources unavailable in conventional kinesiology research environments.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, Leisure, Fitness, and Kinesiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and kinesiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-omics datasets in comparative animal models necessitates advanced computational resources to address translational questions in human and veterinary medicine. Current limitations in processing high-dimensional genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data from murine, porcine, and non-human primate models restrict our ability to identify conserved disease pathways or optimize experimental designs. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale integration of multi-omics data across species, coupled with machine learning approaches to predict therapeutic responses in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) models. We will develop species-specific neural networks trained on existing single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from intestinal biopsies, then use cross-species transfer learning to identify conserved cellular states associated with treatment resistance. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate host-microbiome interactions in gnotobiotic mice under varying dietary conditions, requiring parallelized computation to track dynamic systems over biologically relevant timescales. The computational workflow will leverage containerized pipelines for reproducibility across experimental cohorts. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of evolutionarily conserved gene regulatory networks in mucosal immunity, 2) predictive biomarkers for personalized dosing in canine and primate IBD trials, and 3) optimized gnotobiotic husbandry protocols informed by in silico microbiome perturbations. By reducing reliance on exploratory animal cohorts through computational modeling, this work aligns with the 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) framework while advancing precision veterinary medicine. The proposed analyses exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters due to memory-intensive integration of spatial transcriptomics data (>10 TB per model system) and real-time simulation of microbial community dynamics. Successful implementation will establish a computational toolkit for cross-species translational research, directly supporting the program’s mission to enhance laboratory animal medicine through innovative biomedical modeling.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: Pediatric emergency medicine requires precise, evidence-based protocols to address the unique physiological and developmental characteristics of infants and children during critical care scenarios. Current clinical decision-making tools often rely on generalized guidelines that do not fully account for dynamic variables such as age-specific vital sign ranges, comorbidity interactions, or rare disease presentations. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing predictive computational models to optimize emergency interventions for pediatric patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-source clinical datasets, simulate emergent physiological responses, and generate risk-stratified treatment recommendations. Data from electronic health records, including vital signs, laboratory results, imaging, and outcomes from 15,000+ pediatric emergency visits, will be integrated into machine learning frameworks to identify critical predictors of deterioration and recovery. Agent-based modeling will simulate patient responses to interventions under varying physiological conditions, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in treatment outcomes. Computational demands are substantial due to the need for real-time processing of high-dimensional data, iterative model training, and large-scale simulations of rare events. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for sepsis, traumatic brain injury, and respiratory failure, which will prioritize time-sensitive interventions tailored to patient-specific factors. By enabling rapid analysis of complex, heterogeneous datasets, this work aims to reduce diagnostic delays, minimize treatment complications, and improve survival rates in pediatric emergencies. The resulting models and simulation tools will be disseminated as open-source resources to support clinical decision-making systems worldwide, bridging a critical gap in precision medicine for acute pediatric care.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage emergencies in infants and children.

abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are critical biodiversity hotspots facing unprecedented threats from climate change, eutrophication, and invasive species. However, predicting ecological responses to these stressors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of abiotic drivers, species interactions, and evolutionary adaptations across spatial and temporal scales. This project seeks to develop an integrated modeling framework to assess how multi-stressor regimes alter community dynamics and ecosystem function in temperate lakes. We will combine high-resolution environmental sensor data (temperature, dissolved oxygen, nutrient levels) with long-term ecological datasets spanning phytoplankton, zooplankton, and fish populations across 12 lake systems. Agent-based models will simulate population responses under climate scenarios (RCP 4.5, 8.5), while hydrodynamic models parameterized with bathymetric LiDAR will project habitat suitability shifts. A novel machine learning pipeline will identify tipping points in food web stability and cross-validate model outputs against empirical biodiversity surveys. The computational workflow demands high-performance computing resources to manage iterative simulations across >10^6 parameter combinations, parallel processing of 100+ TB sensor datasets, and Bayesian network analyses of community-scale adaptive capacity. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of keystone species vulnerable to synergistic stressors, (2) predictive maps of biogeochemical cycling alterations under warming regimes, and (3) a publicly accessible library of optimized reaction norms for 200+ aquatic taxa. This work will advance limnological theory on metacommunity resilience while providing actionable insights for watershed management strategies. By quantifying nonlinear ecological feedbacks at landscape scales, the project directly addresses urgent knowledge gaps in freshwater conservation under global change.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting inland fresh waters such as lakes, ponds, rivers, creeks, estuaries, and wetlands. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; aquatic ecosystems; microbiology; mycology; botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; population biology and biodiversity; studies of specific species, phyla, and habitats; and applications to fields such as natural resources conservation, fisheries science, and biotechnology.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face increasing pressure to optimize resource use, enhance productivity, and adapt to dynamic economic and environmental conditions. However, the complexity of interactions between biological processes, management practices, and market variables challenges traditional decision-making frameworks. This project proposes the development of a computational platform to model and simulate integrated agricultural production systems, with a focus on crop-livestock operations and agribusiness logistics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based models to simulate farm-scale decision-making under resource constraints, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets spanning soil health metrics, climate projections, equipment telemetry, and commodity pricing trends. Key computational challenges include parallelizing spatially explicit simulations of crop growth and livestock management, optimizing stochastic models of labor allocation, and resolving multi-objective trade-offs in real-time scenarios. The platform will integrate remote sensing data, IoT sensor inputs, and historical yield records to calibrate models for regional specificity. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to evaluate the economic and operational impacts of precision agriculture technologies, automated labor scheduling systems, and climate-resilient production strategies. By enabling rapid scenario testing at scale, this work aims to provide actionable insights for farmers and agribusinesses to reduce input waste, mitigate financial risks, and improve supply chain coordination. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handle the computational intensity of ensemble simulations across diverse agricultural contexts, which would otherwise be infeasible with local computing resources. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and collaborative workshops with extension services, fostering broader adoption of data-driven decision support systems in agricultural operations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general planning, economics, and use of facilities, natural resources, equipment, labor, and capital to produce plant and animal products, and that may prepare individuals for work in farming, ranching, and agribusiness.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of interpreting complex, multi-modal clinical laboratory data to improve diagnostic accuracy for heterogeneous autoimmune disorders, which often present with overlapping biomarkers and nonspecific symptomatology. Current diagnostic workflows rely on sequential, single-analyte testing, leading to delayed or ambiguous diagnoses. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing an integrated computational framework that combines high-throughput proteomic profiles, flow cytometry data, and autoantibody arrays from patient sera with clinical metadata. The research will employ machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, to identify latent patterns across disparate data types while accounting for technical variability inherent in clinical laboratory instrumentation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on multi-terabyte datasets, optimizing hyperparameters via large-scale grid searches, and performing permutation-based significance testing. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive algorithm for distinguishing clinically similar autoimmune conditions (e.g., Sjögren’s syndrome vs. lupus nephritis) and an open-source toolkit for adaptive data harmonization across different laboratory platforms. The computational pipeline will be designed for eventual deployment in clinical laboratory information systems, enabling real-time decision support. This work bridges gaps between experimental laboratory medicine, computational immunology, and diagnostic informatics, with potential to reduce diagnostic odysseys for patients while establishing new paradigms for data-driven test interpretation in routine clinical practice.
cip_title: Clinical/ Medical Laboratory Science and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in clinical/medical laboratory science and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dental assistants experience a high prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) due to prolonged static postures, repetitive motions, and suboptimal ergonomic practices inherent to clinical workflows. Current ergonomic guidelines for dental settings remain generalized, lacking task-specific, data-driven recommendations tailored to the unique biomechanical demands of chairside assisting, instrument handling, and radiographic procedures. This project proposes a computational biomechanics approach to model musculoskeletal stress patterns during common dental assisting tasks and identify interventions to mitigate injury risks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations integrating motion capture data from clinical scenarios, anatomically precise musculoskeletal models, and finite element analysis of joint and soft tissue loading. Machine learning algorithms will process kinematic datasets to classify high-risk movement patterns and predict the efficacy of ergonomic adjustments, such as equipment repositioning, postural modifications, or workflow redesign. By simulating thousands of task iterations under varying ergonomic conditions, the project aims to generate granular, evidence-based guidelines for workstation configuration, tool placement, and movement protocols specific to dental assisting. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models linking task duration, posture, and equipment design to cumulative injury risk, as well as a framework for real-time ergonomic feedback systems in training environments. This research addresses a critical gap in occupational health for dental professionals, combining computational biomechanics, machine learning, and clinical ergonomics to advance injury prevention strategies in a high-risk, understudied population. The findings will directly inform dental education curricula, workplace safety standards, and the design of ergonomic dental equipment, ultimately reducing MSD incidence and improving workforce sustainability in oral healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide patient care, take dental radiographs (x-ray photographs), prepare patients and equipment for dental procedures, and discharge office administrative functions under the supervision of dentists and dental hygienists. Includes instruction in medical record-keeping, general office duties, reception and patient intake, scheduling, equipment maintenance and sterilization, basic radiography, pre- and post-operative patient care and instruction, chairside assisting, taking tooth and mouth impressions, and supervised practice.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive computational framework to optimize personalized exercise prescriptions for diverse populations, addressing a critical gap in evidence-based methodologies for physical fitness programming. Despite advances in exercise science, current protocols often rely on generalized guidelines, which fail to account for individual variability in biomechanical, physiological, and behavioral responses to training. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex interactions between biometric data, exercise modalities, and longitudinal fitness outcomes. The research integrates anonymized datasets from wearable devices, 3D motion capture systems, and physiological biomarkers (e.g., heart rate variability, muscle oxygenation) to train machine learning models that predict individualized adaptations to resistance and aerobic training. Computational workflows will include finite element simulations of musculoskeletal stress under varying exercise loads, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine training recommendations. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (∼10 TB), running parallelized biomechanical simulations, and training deep neural networks with real-time feedback loops. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool to guide fitness technicians in designing dynamic, adaptive programs that maximize client adherence, performance gains, and injury risk mitigation. By establishing a data-driven framework for exercise prescription, this work bridges a methodological divide between empirical fitness practices and computational precision, offering scalable solutions for underserved populations, including older adults and individuals with mobility limitations. The resulting models and open-source codebase will serve as a foundation for future innovation at the intersection of fitness technology and computational analytics.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in health and fitness clubs, wellness centers, public and private recreation facilities, hospitals and corporate fitness programs where they will perform a variety of instructional and administrative duties. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, fitness techniques, exercise science, personal training, nutrition, and customer service.

abstract: Maternal health disparities, particularly among marginalized populations, remain a critical challenge in women’s healthcare, with multifactorial causes rooted in biological, social, and structural determinants. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a predictive computational framework to identify high-risk pregnancy trajectories and optimize personalized interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, longitudinal social determinants of health metrics, and population-level genomic data, which are computationally prohibitive to analyze using conventional methods. A hybrid machine learning approach will be employed, combining supervised learning models to predict adverse maternal outcomes (e.g., preeclampsia, postpartum hemorrhage) with unsupervised clustering to identify novel risk phenotypes. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between patient-specific factors (e.g., pharmacogenomic profiles, comorbid conditions) and systemic variables (e.g., healthcare access, socioeconomic stressors) to evaluate intervention efficacy under diverse scenarios. The computational workflow will require parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization, real-time sensitivity analyses, and validation across multi-institutional datasets. Anticipated outcomes include actionable risk stratification tools for clinical use by women’s health nurses, enabling earlier identification of high-risk patients and tailored care plans. Additionally, the project will generate open-access models to explore how structural inequities modulate biological risk, informing policy advocacy and nurse-led community interventions. By bridging computational innovation with nursing practice, this work aims to advance precision health in women’s nursing, reduce maternal morbidity, and demonstrate the transformative role of HPC in addressing complex, multidimensional health disparities. The requested resources are essential for managing data complexity, ensuring model reproducibility, and scaling analyses to underrepresented populations often excluded from smaller studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision-driven strategies for optimizing mechanical ventilation in critically ill patients, a core challenge in respiratory care therapy. Current clinical protocols for ventilator settings rely on population-based thresholds and iterative bedside adjustments, which may inadequately address heterogeneous lung mechanics and dynamic pathophysiological states. To address this gap, we propose developing patient-specific computational models that integrate real-time physiological data, imaging-derived lung biomechanics, and fluid-structure interaction simulations. The research will utilize anonymized clinical datasets (including ventilator waveforms, esophageal pressure measurements, and CT imaging) from patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) to parameterize multi-scale models of regional lung compliance and airflow distribution. Finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will be deployed to predict optimal positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) and tidal volume combinations under varying disease states. Machine learning methods will further refine these models by identifying patterns in temporal data streams from ventilators and physiological monitors. The computational intensity of concurrently running thousands of simulated ventilation scenarios with high spatial resolution necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to guide personalized ventilator adjustments, potentially reducing ventilator-induced lung injury risks and improving weaning success rates. This interdisciplinary approach bridges respiratory care practice with computational biomechanics and AI-driven analytics, offering a novel paradigm for precision critical care. Successful validation could inform the development of real-time decision support tools embedded in next-generation ventilator systems, directly enhancing respiratory therapists’ capacity to manage complex cases.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive decision-support framework for optimizing resource allocation in large-scale, dynamic engineering projects with high uncertainty. Traditional resource management models in engineering systems often rely on static assumptions or simplified probabilistic scenarios, which struggle to accommodate real-time data streams, interdependencies among subsystems, and evolving stakeholder constraints. The research addresses this gap by creating a hybrid computational architecture integrating multi-agent simulation, Bayesian inference, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to model complex engineering project ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training DRL agents on synthetic and historical project datasets, simulating thousands of concurrent decision pathways, and quantifying emergent risks under stochastic conditions. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate resource allocation strategies across heterogeneous parameters—including cost volatility, workforce scalability, and technology readiness levels—while enforcing domain-specific constraints through constrained optimization solvers. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for dynamically balancing capital expenditures, operational resilience, and sustainability metrics in cross-disciplinary engineering initiatives. The framework will be validated against case studies in distributed infrastructure deployment and phased technology adoption programs, with performance benchmarks comparing optimization efficiency against conventional project management heuristics. By advancing computational methods at the intersection of systems engineering and adaptive control theory, this work aims to establish new best practices for managing complexity in next-generation engineering enterprises, with potential applications in smart city development, disaster response logistics, and decentralized manufacturing networks. The HPC-enabled scalability of the proposed approach will enable previously intractable analyses of system-of-systems interactions, directly supporting data-driven governance in engineering management.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of management and administration principles to engineering systems and applications. Includes instruction in resource allocation theory, control theory, statistical analysis, business management and administration, and applications to specific engineering research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale digital humanities initiative focused on the computational analysis and preservation of culturally significant, multilingual textual corpora. The research addresses the challenge of efficiently processing and analyzing vast, heterogeneous collections of historical texts (15th–19th centuries) that exhibit complex linguistic variations, degraded typography, and non-standardized orthographies. Traditional methods in textual scholarship struggle to scale effectively with such datasets, limiting opportunities to trace transnational textual transmission, map semantic shifts, or identify patterns of editorial intervention across time. To overcome these barriers, the project proposes a hybrid computational approach combining machine learning-driven optical character recognition (OCR) correction, transformer-based natural language processing for semantic annotation, and graph-based network analysis. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific OCR correction models on GPU clusters using 50,000+ manually verified text-image pairs, as well as for deploying fine-tuned multilingual language models to perform entity recognition and sentiment analysis across six languages. A second phase will employ distributed computing to construct temporal knowledge graphs linking textual variants, authorship attributions, and bibliographic metadata, enabling the identification of previously undetected textual relationships at scale. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational textual criticism, a publicly accessible repository of annotated early modern texts, and methodological frameworks for applying HPC resources to pre-digital cultural heritage materials. This work will directly support interdisciplinary research in book history, comparative literature, and archival studies while establishing new benchmarks for computationally assisted textual scholarship. The requested allocation will ensure the feasibility of processing over 10 million pages of text within the project timeline, significantly expanding the scope of analyzable materials for humanistic inquiry.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on digital textual editing, archiving, and publishing, and on the study of new media and computing platforms from the perspectives of the humanities and computer science. Includes instruction in archiving, computer programming, cultural studies, and textual criticism.

abstract: Pediatric endocrine disorders, including diabetes, growth hormone deficiencies, and adrenal dysfunctions, exhibit complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies often rely on generalized protocols, which may inadequately address individual variability in disease progression and treatment response. This project seeks to address this gap by developing patient-specific predictive models of endocrine function and treatment outcomes using high-dimensional clinical, genomic, and metabolomic datasets. The primary challenge lies in integrating multi-scale biological data while accounting for dynamic hormonal feedback systems and developmental changes during childhood and adolescence—a task requiring computational resources beyond conventional clinical research infrastructure. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to implement multiscale computational models combining mechanistic simulations of hormone-receptor interactions with machine learning approaches. These models will analyze longitudinal patient data from electronic health records (n ≈ 10,000) and multi-omics profiles (whole-genome sequencing, proteomics, and steroid metabolomes) from a prospective cohort of 500 patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia and growth disorders. Computational workflows will include Bayesian hierarchical modeling to account for age-dependent endocrine parameters, deep learning architectures for pattern recognition in time-series hormone data, and agent-based simulations of pituitary-adrenal axis dynamics. The HPC environment is critical for training complex neural networks, running parallelized pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations across developmental stages, and performing genome-wide association studies with gene-environment interaction terms. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for optimizing glucocorticoid dosing schedules in adrenal insufficiency, (2) identification of novel biomarkers for early detection of treatment-related metabolic complications, and (3) open-source computational tools for simulating endocrine maturation trajectories. By enabling precision dosing and risk stratification, this work aims to reduce long-term sequelae of pediatric endocrine disorders while establishing a computational framework adaptable to other hormone-mediated developmental conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of endocrine diseases and the regulation of hormone balance in childhood and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of neurodevelopmental trajectories in children with psychiatric disorders, with a focus on autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and early-onset anxiety. Clinical child psychology faces a critical challenge in integrating multimodal data—such as longitudinal neuroimaging (fMRI, DTI), behavioral assessments, and genetic markers—to identify dynamic risk factors and intervention targets. Current statistical models lack the capacity to process these complex, high-dimensional datasets while accounting for temporal and individual variability. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework using graph neural networks (GNNs) and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to map interactions between neural circuitry maturation, environmental stressors, and symptom progression. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-site neuroimaging data (n ≈ 5,000 scans from 1,200 participants), real-time optimization of GNN architectures, and simulation of intervention effects across developmental windows. The project will validate models against clinical outcomes from a 3-year longitudinal cohort study of children aged 6–12, incorporating adaptive behavioral interventions. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of neural- behavioral biomarkers predictive of treatment response, (2) generation of patient-specific risk profiles to guide early intervention timing, and (3) open-source tools for developmental trajectory modeling in clinical populations. By elucidating mechanisms linking neurocognitive development to psychopathology, this work will directly inform personalized clinical decision-making and refine theoretical models of developmental neuropsychology. The scale of data integration and computational demands of simulating nonlinear developmental processes necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically actionable results within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the developmental processes of children and associated disorders and that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical child psychology. Includes instruction in developmental neuropsychology, child psychopathology, testing of children and adolescents, pediatric psychology, psychosocial variables in child development, clinical skills, family therapy, behavioral assessment and intervention, clinical skills, consultation, professional standards and ethics, and applications to topics such as infancy, childhood, and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling large-scale, interactive musical ecosystems, where real-time synthesis, machine learning, and complex acoustic simulations converge. Traditional methods for analyzing or generating music often struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions between performers, audiences, and environments, particularly in improvisational or culturally hybrid contexts. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate dynamic musical networks, integrating agent-based modeling, spectral analysis, and generative adversarial networks (GANs). The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) simulating improvisational decision-making processes across ensembles using reinforcement learning agents trained on multimodal performance data (audio, gesture, physiological signals), and (2) modeling acoustic environments at unprecedented spatial resolutions to study how architectural features influence collective musical experiences. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated signal processing and distributed memory parallelism to handle real-time constraints in scenario testing, requiring sustained access to nodes with high core counts and specialized audio processing libraries. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational musicology, validated through case studies spanning jazz, global traditional practices, and experimental electronic genres. By enabling the study of music as a complex adaptive system, this work aims to advance theoretical frameworks in participatory music-making while providing practical tools for composers and ethnomusicologists. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the project’s need for simultaneous execution of multiple neural networks, large-scale parameter space exploration, and terabyte-scale management of heterogeneous musical datasets spanning historical recordings, sensor-captured performances, and synthetically generated materials.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in music, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale, cross-cultural analysis of narrative structures and transnational literary influences across digitized archives spanning the 18th to 21st centuries. Current methodologies in cultural studies and comparative literature face limitations in systematically analyzing the vast, multilingual corpora necessary to trace evolving themes such as postcolonial identity, ecological consciousness, and diaspora experiences. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to identify patterns across temporal, linguistic, and geographic boundaries, while existing computational tools lack the capacity to process non-Latin scripts, low-resource languages, and culturally specific semantic contexts at scale. Our interdisciplinary team proposes a hybrid computational framework integrating transformer-based multilingual language models, graph neural networks, and culturally informed topic modeling to map intertextual networks and ideological shifts across 15 million pages of primary texts in 12 languages. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of OCR-corrected texts, training of domain-specific embeddings that account for historical semantic change, and dynamic visualization of transnational narrative flows through interactive knowledge graphs. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database linking literary works through shared thematic and stylistic features, 2) quantitative models tracing the diffusion of narrative conventions between Global South and Euro-American traditions, and 3) new methodologies for computational humanities research that balance scale with cultural nuance. By enabling the first systematic comparison of Indigenous storytelling frameworks, colonial-era texts, and contemporary world literature at this magnitude, the project aims to redefine theories of cultural hybridity while providing open-source tools for ethically grounded, cross-linguistic digital scholarship.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of cultural studies and comparative literature or a specialization which draws from cultural studies and comparative literature. Includes instruction in anthropology, comparative linguistics, cultural studies, history, literary criticism, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, sociology, and textual studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance nursing science by addressing critical gaps in analyzing complex, multi-modal healthcare datasets. Nursing research increasingly relies on integrating large-scale clinical, genomic, and sensor-derived data to optimize patient outcomes, yet traditional computational tools lack the capacity to process these datasets efficiently. The proposed study focuses on developing predictive models to identify risk factors for hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) in critical care units, a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. By synthesizing real-time electronic health records (EHRs), microbiome sequencing data, and continuous vital sign monitoring streams, the project aims to uncover dynamic interactions between patient physiology, microbial colonization, and clinical interventions that contribute to HAI development. Computational methods will include parallelized machine learning pipelines for feature selection and risk stratification, agent-based simulations of pathogen transmission, and time-series analysis of high-frequency sensor data. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce model training times for iterative algorithm development, and support the integration of heterogeneous data types through scalable containerized workflows. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of modifiable risk factors, personalized intervention thresholds, and a framework for real-time HAI prediction in clinical settings. This work will directly inform evidence-based nursing protocols to mitigate infection risks, reduce healthcare costs, and improve patient safety. By advancing computational methodologies tailored to nursing research, the project will also establish a replicable model for leveraging HPC in future studies on complex care delivery challenges, from chronic disease management to health equity analytics. The requested resources are essential to overcoming current computational bottlenecks and ensuring rigorous, translational outcomes that align with nursing science’s dual priorities of clinical innovation and methodological advancement.
cip_definition: A research program that focuses on the study of advanced clinical practices, research methodologies, the administration of complex nursing services, and that prepares nurses to further the progress of nursing research through experimentation and clinical applications.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of modern typographic design and dynamic text composition, particularly as digital communication platforms require increasingly complex, responsive layouts optimized for diverse devices and user contexts. Current software tools for typography and page composition struggle to efficiently process high-resolution graphical elements, variable fonts, and real-time layout adjustments at scale, leading to bottlenecks in creative workflows and limitations in design experimentation. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes the development of a parallelized computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate rendering, optimize spatial composition algorithms, and simulate user interaction patterns across heterogeneous display environments. The project will implement GPU-accelerated font rasterization techniques to handle multi-script typography at ultra-high resolutions, alongside distributed memory systems for batch processing large-scale layout variations (e.g., magazine spreads, interactive documents). Machine learning models trained on eye-tracking datasets will be integrated to automate readability optimization while preserving artistic intent. By deploying these methods on HPC infrastructure, the team aims to reduce rendering latency by orders of magnitude compared to conventional design workstations, enabling real-time manipulation of complex typographic systems with millions of glyph variants. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational typography that supports responsive design workflows in journalism and digital publishing, along with new benchmarks for performance-aware layout engines. This work will directly enhance the capabilities of communication professionals to create accessible, visually sophisticated content while maintaining compatibility with industry-standard design ecosystems. The requested computing resources are critical for training large-scale neural font models and conducting multivariate A/B testing of algorithmic layout strategies across thousands of simulated device profiles.
cip_title: Computer Typography and Composition Equipment Operator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to design and execute page formats, layouts and text composition, and to make typographical selections using computer graphics and other computer-assisted design programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize culinary workflows in commercial kitchens, addressing inefficiencies in food preparation, equipment utilization, and staff coordination that contribute to energy waste, operational delays, and inconsistent output. While culinary arts training emphasizes manual skill development and theoretical knowledge, the integration of computational modeling to analyze dynamic kitchen systems remains underexplored. The research problem centers on the lack of data-driven frameworks for simulating real-time kitchen operations under variable constraints, such as fluctuating order volumes, equipment failures, or staff availability. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES), this project will construct a virtual kitchen environment parameterized by empirical data—including task durations, equipment energy consumption, and spatial layouts—collected from partner restaurants. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations to test scenarios ranging from routine service to high-demand events, optimizing variables like workstation placement, staff-task assignments, and equipment scheduling. Machine learning techniques will further identify patterns in simulation outputs to recommend adaptive workflow adjustments. Expected outcomes include predictive models that reduce energy use by 15–20% in test kitchens, decrease food waste through improved task synchronization, and generate training modules for culinary students focused on systemic efficiency. By bridging culinary practice with computational systems analysis, this work aims to establish a novel interdisciplinary niche within gastronomic education and food service management, advancing sustainability and operational resilience in a critical, yet computationally underserved, sector.
cip_title: Cooking and Related Culinary Arts, General.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of the cooking and related culinary arts, and that may prepare individuals for a variety of jobs within the food service industry.  Includes instruction in food preparation, cooking techniques, equipment operation and maintenance, sanitation and safety, communication skills, applicable regulations, and principles of food service management.

abstract: The pharmaceutical industry faces increasing complexity in market dynamics, driven by evolving regulatory landscapes, heterogeneous patient populations, and competitive pressures. Traditional marketing and management strategies often struggle to integrate multi-dimensional data—including electronic health records, sales trajectories, social media sentiment, and supply chain variables—to inform real-time decision-making. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to optimize pharmaceutical marketing strategies and resource allocation using high-performance computing (HPC). The research problem centers on modeling the interplay between drug efficacy, pricing, promotional efforts, and patient access while accounting for regional healthcare policies and competitor behavior. Leveraging HPC resources, we will employ agent-based modeling to simulate market responses under diverse scenarios, machine learning algorithms to predict sales trends from multi-source datasets, and network analysis to identify critical stakeholders in drug adoption pathways. Large-scale parallel processing will enable the integration of terabyte-scale datasets, including anonymized patient records and global sales data, while reducing runtime for complex optimization tasks from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit to quantify the impact of marketing interventions, identify high-value patient segments, and optimize promotional budgets across therapeutic areas. This work will provide actionable insights for pharmaceutical managers to allocate resources efficiently, mitigate risks in product launches, and align marketing strategies with patient outcomes. By bridging computational scalability with domain-specific challenges in pharmaceutical management, this project aims to advance data-driven decision-making in healthcare industries, ultimately supporting equitable drug access and sustainable business practices.
cip_definition: A program that combines the study of basic and pharmaceutical sciences with marketing and management studies; and that prepares individuals for careers in pharmaceutical sales, marketing, management, and related fields within the health care industry. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, pharmaceutics, pharmacology, health care systems, issues and structure of pharmaceutical industry, management, pharmaceutical marketing, pharmaceutical and medical product management, and legal issues.

abstract: Aging populations present complex social challenges shaped by dynamic interactions between individual behaviors, community structures, and systemic policies. Traditional gerontological research often relies on static surveys or small-scale longitudinal studies, limiting the ability to model emergent, large-scale social phenomena or simulate interventions in heterogeneous populations. This project addresses this gap by developing an agent-based computational framework to investigate how multi-level social factors—such as community engagement patterns, technology adoption disparities, and localized policy impacts—interact to influence health outcomes and well-being in older adults. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate population-scale scenarios integrating individual-level cognitive, social, and mobility data with macro-level demographic and policy datasets. Computational models will be parameterized using harmonized longitudinal data from aging cohorts (e.g., social network structures, health records) and spatially explicit community resource maps. Machine learning techniques will identify critical leverage points for intervention by analyzing simulation outputs across diverse virtual populations. The scalable architecture will enable parallelized sensitivity analyses to account for geographic, cultural, and socioeconomic variability in aging experiences. Expected outcomes include predictive models of social isolation risk factors, optimized intervention strategies for community support programs, and open-source tools for policy-sensitive aging population simulations. By bridging computational social science and gerontology, this work advances methodological capacity to study aging as a complex adaptive system while providing actionable insights for equitable aging-in-place initiatives. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling petabyte-scale multimodal datasets, running computationally intensive simulations across parameter spaces, and deploying deep learning architectures to detect nonlinear interaction effects in aging trajectories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences and psychology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of economic network resilience under cascading shocks using advanced computational modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how interdependent economic systems—such as global supply chains, financial markets, and labor networks—respond to sequential disruptions, including geopolitical conflicts, climate events, or technological failures. Traditional equilibrium-based models struggle to capture nonlinear feedback loops and heterogeneous agent behaviors in such scenarios, limiting their predictive utility. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a large-scale agent-based model (ABM) simulating millions of heterogeneous firms, households, and institutions across multiple economic sectors. The ABM will integrate real-world data on trade flows, financial linkages, and adaptive decision-making rules calibrated from empirical studies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations across diverse shock sequences and policy responses, enabling Monte Carlo analyses of systemic risk propagation. Computational challenges include managing high-dimensional parameter spaces, optimizing memory usage for agent-state tracking, and processing real-time behavioral adjustments during shock cascades. Expected outcomes include quantifying resilience thresholds, identifying leverage points for policy intervention, and generating open-access datasets on simulated crisis trajectories. Results will advance methodological frameworks for complexity economics while providing actionable insights for designing adaptive regulatory strategies. The requested allocation of 200,000 CPU-hours and 50 TB of storage will support model calibration, sensitivity analyses, and scenario testing over a 12-month period, with scalability plans for future cross-disciplinary extensions. This work aligns with priorities in economic stability research and demonstrates how HPC-enabled granular modeling can inform crisis preparedness in increasingly interconnected systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in economics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in animal grooming practices through the development of a biophysical simulation framework for optimizing grooming protocols. Current approaches to grooming—particularly for specialized contexts such as show animals, working dogs, or pets with dermatological sensitivities—rely heavily on anecdotal expertise and trial-and-error experimentation. This limits scalability, reproducibility, and the ability to predict outcomes for novel coat types or health conditions. Our research addresses this gap by constructing computational models that simulate interactions between grooming tools, products, and animal integumentary systems. Using finite element analysis (FEA), we will model the mechanical stresses of brushing, shearing, and bathing on diverse coat morphologies (e.g., double-coated breeds, curly-haired varieties) under variable hydration and temperature conditions. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will evaluate the penetration and efficacy of grooming products (shampoos, conditioners, topical treatments) across species-specific skin barrier structures. These simulations will be validated against empirical data from 3D-scanned coat samples and biometric sensor arrays applied during live grooming trials. The computational pipeline will integrate machine learning to identify optimal tool-product combinations for minimizing skin irritation, maximizing coat health, and achieving aesthetic outcomes. By enabling predictive, data-driven grooming strategies, this work aims to reduce occupational hazards for groomers, improve animal welfare, and establish quantitative benchmarks for an industry currently lacking standardized protocols. The project’s HPC requirements stem from the need to process high-resolution volumetric datasets of coat structures, run parallelized multi-physics simulations, and train deep learning models on heterogeneous data streams. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools and a decision-support system for groomers, with potential applications in veterinary dermatology and regulatory policy development for grooming product safety.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize enterprise risk management strategies under high-dimensional uncertainty, with a focus on systemic risks arising from interconnected financial, operational, and cybersecurity factors. Traditional risk models often struggle to capture nonlinear dependencies across large-scale datasets or simulate cascading failures in real-world scenarios due to computational limitations. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized Monte Carlo simulations, stochastic optimization algorithms, and machine learning techniques to address these gaps. The research will specifically model portfolio risk exposures across insurance, investment, and supply chain domains using multi-agent systems that simulate interactions between market shocks, cyber-physical threats, and organizational response mechanisms. Key computational challenges include solving high-dimensional risk allocation problems with non-convex constraints, training graph neural networks on dynamic interdependency matrices, and performing sensitivity analyses across thousands of scenario parameters. The HPC environment will enable distributed computation of Value-at-Risk (VaR) metrics at unprecedented granularity while maintaining real-time responsiveness for stress testing applications. Expected outcomes include a novel risk prioritization framework that identifies latent vulnerabilities in business continuity plans, quantifies the cost-benefit tradeoffs of alternative mitigation strategies, and generates adaptive hedging policies through reinforcement learning. This work will advance computational methodologies in risk science by demonstrating how heterogeneous data streams—from IoT sensor networks to financial market feeds—can be synthesized into actionable risk intelligence. Results will be disseminated as open-source tools for scenario analysis, benefiting both academic researchers and practitioners in operational risk management. The requested computing resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and speed to model complex adaptive systems that conventional workstations cannot feasibly process.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles of business risk measurement, mitigation, and management. Includes instruction in business analytics, foundations of insurance and risk management, investments, life and health insurance, loss prevention, property and liability insurance risk assessment, risk control, risk financing, and security.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the emergent dynamics of cross-species disease systems under shifting environmental stressors—an integrative challenge requiring synthesis of ecological, physiological, and population-level data. Current models often silo host-pathogen interactions within single species or oversimplify environmental drivers, limiting predictive capacity for systems where climate change, habitat fragmentation, and biodiversity loss intersect. We propose developing a multi-scale computational framework to simulate how stressors alter disease transmission thresholds across interacting species with divergent life histories, immune strategies, and movement behaviors. Agent-based modeling will integrate empirical datasets on species traits (e.g., thermal tolerances, metabolic rates), landscape-level habitat connectivity, and pathogen viability under variable abiotic conditions. Machine learning pipelines will identify nonlinear feedbacks between stressor gradients and outbreak risks, validated against field observations from collaborative wildlife health monitoring networks. HPC resources are critical to parallelize stochastic simulations across parameter spaces encompassing >10^6 possible species-environment-pathogen combinations, enabling sensitivity analyses at ecological timescales. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible library of modular, scalable simulation workflows for stressor-disease systems, (2) predictive maps of outbreak hotspots under IPCC climate scenarios, and (3) mechanistic insights into how interspecific variability in stress resilience modulates community-level disease resilience. This work bridges gaps between organismal biology, landscape ecology, and conservation medicine, directly supporting proactive health interventions in rapidly changing ecosystems. By prioritizing computational flexibility, the framework will empower interdisciplinary researchers to adapt models to novel systems, from zoonotic spillover interfaces to managed pollinator networks.
cip_title: Integrative/ Interdisciplinary Biology, Biosciences, and Biomedical Sciences
cip_definition: A program that crosses multiple specializations within the biological and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in general biological research and variety of specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to optimize material efficiency, installation precision, and safety outcomes in carpet, floor, and tile installation workflows. Despite advances in manual techniques, industry practices remain prone to material waste, labor-intensive trial-and-error adjustments, and risks associated with structural instability or tool misuse. To address these challenges, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model installation processes, material behaviors, and environmental interactions. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize adhesive curing processes across temperature and humidity conditions, while finite element analysis will predict stress distribution in tile substrates under dynamic loads. Machine learning models trained on historical installation datasets will identify optimal cutting patterns for complex floor geometries, reducing material waste. Agent-based simulations will model worker ergonomics and tool trajectories to recommend safer workspace configurations. These computationally intensive models require parallelized workflows across GPU and CPU clusters to achieve practical resolution and scale. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for adhesive performance under job site conditions, AI-driven layout optimization software, and safety training modules informed by simulated risk scenarios.
