The project will validate results through collaboration with industry partners, comparing computational predictions against empirical measurements of material usage, installation time, and incident rates. By integrating computational science with trade-specific challenges, this work aims to establish data-driven practices that reduce costs, enhance durability, and improve workplace safety for flooring professionals. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the spatial and temporal resolutions required for actionable insights in these heterogeneous, multi-physics systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, prepare, install, and repair carpet; linoleum; vinyl; ceramic, marble, quarry, mosaic, and terrazzo tiles; and wood materials on floors, walls, and stairs. Includes instruction in measuring, cutting, and installing materials; use of hand and power-operated equipment; estimation of material and labor costs; and safety training.

abstract: The increasing complexity of high-dimensional biomedical data in laboratory medicine—spanning multi-omics, high-resolution imaging, and longitudinal clinical datasets—has created critical bottlenecks in computational workflows. Current infrastructure struggles to support integrative analyses required for precision diagnostics and predictive modeling, particularly for rare diseases where sparse datasets demand advanced imputation and machine learning techniques. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges by enabling scalable, reproducible pipelines for analyzing heterogeneous clinical data. The research will focus on optimizing computational workflows for three key areas: (1) real-time integration of genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data to identify novel biomarkers for sepsis progression, (2) GPU-accelerated processing of multiplex immunohistochemistry images for tumor microenvironment characterization, and (3) federated learning frameworks to train disease classification models across distributed hospital datasets while maintaining patient privacy. Custom algorithms will be developed using Python and R, leveraging parallel computing libraries (Dask, CUDA) and containerization (Singularity) for portability across HPC clusters. Benchmarking will compare runtime, memory efficiency, and predictive accuracy against existing clinical decision tools. Expected outcomes include validated computational workflows that reduce analysis time for complex diagnostic datasets by 40-60%, open-source tools for federated analysis of sensitive clinical data, and clinically actionable models predicting sepsis outcomes with >85% AUC. By overcoming current limitations in data integration and scalability, this work will enhance translational research capabilities in laboratory medicine, directly supporting the development of rapid, data-driven diagnostic protocols for critical care and oncology settings. Resource allocation will ensure rigorous validation of computational methods against gold-standard clinical endpoints.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied medical research and related techniques, equipment, data systems, and research design. Includes instruction in the management of medical laboratories in research and healthcare facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the efficacy of adaptive learning systems in K-12 science curricula, with the goal of optimizing personalized instructional material design. Despite advances in educational technology, a critical gap persists in understanding how dynamic, multimodal learner data—including interaction logs, formative assessments, and biometric feedback—can be systematically integrated to refine curriculum sequencing in real time. Current methods for evaluating adaptive systems rely on small-scale trials or simplified models, limiting their scalability and generalizability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and network analysis to model student learning pathways across heterogeneous datasets. The computational workflow will involve training multi-agent DRL models on anonymized student interaction data (spanning 50,000+ learners) to simulate decision-making processes in curriculum adaptation, coupled with temporal graph networks to identify latent patterns in concept mastery trajectories. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of multimodal educational data, parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across thousands of simulated classroom environments, and running evolutionary algorithms to stress-test curriculum designs under diverse pedagogical scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated predictive model for mapping learner behaviors to optimal instructional sequences, 2) an open-source toolkit for evaluating curriculum robustness against demographic and cognitive variability, and 3) evidence-based guidelines for embedding real-time analytics into adaptive learning platforms. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this work aims to advance computational curriculum theory while providing scalable methods for evaluating educational interventions—a critical need in post-pandemic learning environments where hybrid and personalized instruction have become ubiquitous. Results will be disseminated through an interactive web portal for educators and peer-reviewed publications on data-driven curriculum design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the curriculum and related instructional processes and tools, and that may prepare individuals to serve as professional curriculum specialists. Includes instruction in curriculum theory, curriculum design and planning, instructional material design and evaluation, curriculum evaluation, and applications to specific subject matter, programs or educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced mechanical drafting and CAD/CADD workflows, particularly in simulating complex mechanical systems with high geometric fidelity and multi-physics interactions. Traditional CAD tools often struggle with the computational intensity of iterative design optimization, real-time finite element analysis (FEA), and large-scale additive manufacturing simulations, leading to bottlenecks in design validation and prototyping. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize and accelerate critical drafting and simulation tasks. The research will focus on developing scalable algorithms for distributed mesh generation, GPU-accelerated stress-strain analysis, and topology optimization under thermal and mechanical constraints. Computational workflows will integrate open-source CAD frameworks with HPC-enabled solvers, enabling parameter sweeps across design variations and materials. A key innovation involves implementing machine learning models to predict optimal meshing strategies and reduce redundant computations in multi-iteration drafting processes. The project will validate these methods using case studies from industrial partnerships, including turbine blade drafting with fluid-structure interaction simulations and lightweight structural components for aerospace applications. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in simulation time for high-resolution models, demonstrated scalability to 10,000+ core-hour workloads, and improved convergence in generative design algorithms. By establishing best practices for HPC integration in mechanical drafting pipelines, this work aims to bridge the gap between academic CAD training and industry-scale computational demands, directly enhancing the precision and efficiency of next-generation mechanical design education. Resulting workflows and benchmarking data will be disseminated as open educational resources to strengthen CAD/CADD curricula in technology programs.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: Orthopedic interventions, such as casting, splinting, and bracing, require precise customization to optimize patient outcomes while minimizing complications like pressure injuries or delayed healing. Current clinical practices rely heavily on manual techniques and generalized protocols, which may not account for biomechanical variability across patients or dynamic changes in tissue response during recovery. This project proposes a computational framework to model patient-specific biomechanics and simulate the mechanical interactions between orthopedic devices and anatomical structures under varying physiological conditions. The research problem centers on developing predictive models that integrate heterogeneous data—including imaging, material properties, and load dynamics—to guide device design and application protocols. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large datasets from clinical imaging (e.g., CT, MRI) and wearable sensors, perform finite element analysis (FEA) of device-tissue interactions at scale, and train machine learning algorithms to identify optimal device configurations. Computational workflows will incorporate multiphysics simulations to evaluate stress distribution, tissue deformation, and microvascular perfusion in virtual patient cohorts representing diverse anatomies and injury patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models predicting device efficacy and risk profiles for specific clinical scenarios, (2) open-source tools for clinicians to simulate interventions preoperatively, and (3) data-driven guidelines for personalized device selection and adjustment timelines. By linking computational insights to clinical workflows, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error practices, improve recovery rates, and lower healthcare costs associated with prolonged immobilization or device-related complications. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable iterative model refinement, sensitivity analyses across thousands of virtual cases, and real-time visualization of biomechanical parameters—tasks infeasible with standard computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to cast, splint, and brace orthopedic injuries. Includes instruction in patient assessment; casting, splinting, and orthopedic appliances; radiographic interpretation; traction; and wound care.

abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation is a critical intervention for children with end-stage liver disease, yet significant challenges remain in predicting post-transplant outcomes, optimizing immunosuppression, and mitigating graft rejection. Current risk stratification models lack precision due to the complex interplay of genetic, immunological, metabolic, and clinical factors unique to pediatric populations. This project proposes to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating high-dimensional clinical data, genomic profiles, and longitudinal immune response metrics to identify predictive biomarkers and dynamic risk factors for graft survival and complications in pediatric transplant recipients. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will harmonize heterogeneous datasets from a multicenter cohort of 800+ pediatric liver transplant patients, including whole-exome sequencing, longitudinal cytokine profiles, electronic health records, and histopathology imaging. Machine learning algorithms (e.g., ensemble survival models and graph neural networks) will be employed to model non-linear interactions between variables and temporal patterns in rejection episodes. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further analyze vascular anastomosis geometries from 3D imaging to assess thrombosis risk. The scale of data integration—spanning terabytes of imaging, genomic, and time-series clinical data—necessitates distributed computing for parallel processing, large-scale matrix operations, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early detection of graft dysfunction, personalized immunosuppression dosing strategies based on immune repertoire dynamics, and mechanistic insights into alloimmune responses in developing immune systems. These computational tools aim to reduce late graft loss rates by enabling proactive clinical decision-making, directly addressing unmet needs in pediatric transplant hepatology. The requested HPC resources will accelerate model development cycles, enable validation across diverse patient subgroups, and support the translation of findings into clinical decision-support systems for precision management of pediatric liver transplant recipients.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge, skill, and expertise required of pediatric gastroenterologists to care for children and young adults prior to and following hepatic transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying manual therapy techniques in massage therapy, a specialized domain within rehabilitative health sciences. Despite widespread clinical use, the precise biophysical effects of techniques such as myofascial release, deep tissue manipulation, and cranio-sacral therapy remain poorly quantified, limiting evidence-based protocol development. Current practice relies heavily on subjective practitioner experience and qualitative patient feedback, creating gaps in understanding how tissue-specific force parameters (e.g., magnitude, direction, duration) modulate cellular responses, pain signaling pathways, or systemic autonomic outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of multi-layered soft tissue systems with machine learning-driven analysis of dynamic pressure distribution datasets. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of tissue deformation under varying manual intervention parameters, coupled with parallelized processing of high-resolution biomechanical data (collected via sensor-embedded massage platforms) and synchronized physiological recordings (heart rate variability, cortisol levels). Neural network architectures will identify patterns linking mechanical inputs to short- and long-term therapeutic outcomes across diverse demographic cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing force application strategies in treating chronic musculoskeletal pain and stress-related disorders, as well as novel biomarkers for real-time efficacy assessment during sessions. By quantifying previously intangible therapeutic processes, this work aims to establish a computational foundation for standardizing manual therapy practices while preserving their individualized application, ultimately advancing integration with conventional rehabilitative care pathways. The resource-intensive nature of multi-physics simulations and complex dataset integration necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve clinically relevant spatiotemporal resolution and statistical power.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being to clients through the application of manual techniques for manipulating skin, muscles, and connective tissues. Includes instruction in Western (Swedish) massage, sports massage, myotherapy/trigger point massage, myofascial release, deep tissue massage, cranio-sacral therapy, reflexology, massage safety and emergency management, client counseling, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and longevity of high-pressure steam boilers through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize fabrication and maintenance protocols. Steam boilers operate under extreme thermal and mechanical stresses, leading to material degradation, weld fatigue, and potential failure. Traditional experimental methods to predict failure modes or validate new materials are costly and time-intensive. This research proposes a computational framework to simulate multi-physics interactions within boiler systems, including heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and structural mechanics, under varying operational conditions. High-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will be developed to assess stress distribution, thermal expansion, and corrosion rates in boiler components such as welded joints, riveted seams, and pressure vessels. Machine learning techniques will further refine predictive models by correlating historical failure data with simulated stress profiles. The HPC environment is essential to handle the scale of these simulations, which involve millions of mesh elements, transient boundary conditions, and multi-scale material behavior. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for identifying high-risk failure zones, optimizing weld patterns and material selection, and informing maintenance schedules to extend boiler lifespans. By integrating computational insights with industry standards (e.g., ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code), this work aims to reduce operational downtime, enhance safety protocols, and lower fabrication costs for industrial and power generation boilers. The results will be disseminated through technical workshops for boilermaking professionals and open-access datasets to support further innovation in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and repair steam boiler components. Includes instruction in principles of steam power, material selection, welding, riveting, sealing materials, pressure testing, pipefitting, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to optimize predictive maintenance strategies for electric and hybrid vehicle systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. As modern vehicles increasingly integrate complex electrical, mechanical, and software components, traditional diagnostic methods struggle to efficiently analyze real-time sensor data, identify failure precursors, and predict maintenance needs. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating computational models that synthesize multi-modal data—including thermal, vibrational, and electrochemical signals—to forecast component degradation and system-level performance losses. Leveraging HPC capabilities, the project will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distributions in battery packs and drivetrain components under diverse operating conditions. Machine learning workflows will concurrently process historical repair records and telemetry data to identify failure patterns, trained using distributed computing frameworks to handle terabyte-scale datasets. Validation will involve comparing simulated degradation timelines against empirical wear data from accelerated lifecycle testing. The expected outcomes include (1) a scalable digital twin platform for simulating vehicle system health, (2) optimized neural network architectures for anomaly detection in high-dimensional sensor streams, and (3) actionable thresholds for preemptive part replacement calibrated to reduce unplanned downtime by ≥30%. By integrating HPC-driven simulations with field data analytics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive maintenance in vocational training contexts, directly enhancing the technical precision of repair protocols while reducing resource waste from unnecessary part replacements. The computational tools developed will be incorporated into instructional modules, equipping future technicians with data-driven decision-making skills aligned with Industry 4.0 standards.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of vehicles and mobile equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized care strategies for family practice nurses managing complex, multi-dimensional patient data. Family nursing requires synthesizing heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, genetic predispositions, socio-environmental factors, and longitudinal health trends—to tailor interventions for individuals and family units. However, existing analytical tools struggle to efficiently process these data at scale, limiting real-time clinical decision-making and holistic care planning. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models capable of predicting patient-specific health trajectories and simulating the outcomes of targeted interventions. The computational approach will integrate deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models for unstructured clinical notes) with agent-based simulations to model family health dynamics and disease propagation. Parallelized workflows will enable rapid analysis of large-scale datasets, while probabilistic modeling will quantify uncertainty in risk stratification for conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and geriatric syndromes. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for risk prediction, intervention optimization, and resource allocation tailored to family practice contexts. By elucidating patterns in family-level health determinants, this work aims to enhance evidence-based care delivery, reduce preventable hospitalizations, and support nurses in designing proactive, patient-centered care plans. The project will also advance methodological innovation in nursing science by establishing scalable computational workflows for integrating multi-omic and socio-behavioral data into clinical practice. Successful implementation will demonstrate the transformative potential of HPC in bridging gaps between precision health paradigms and frontline family nursing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the optimization of culinary techniques through computational modeling, with a focus on enhancing energy efficiency, ingredient utilization, and sensory outcomes in professional kitchens. The culinary arts have historically relied on empirical experimentation, but the growing complexity of modern gastronomy—driven by sustainability demands, personalized nutrition trends, and resource constraints—necessitates advanced predictive tools. The core research problem centers on developing a computational framework to simulate heat transfer dynamics, chemical interactions, and material stress in diverse cooking processes (e.g., sous-vide, fermentation, or multi-stage baking) under variable environmental conditions. A hybrid approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning will be employed to model thermodynamic behavior, ingredient degradation thresholds, and equipment performance. Large-scale parametric studies will simulate thousands of scenarios, varying parameters such as thermal conductivity, humidity, and time-temperature profiles, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine process recommendations. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive toolkit for minimizing energy waste, reducing food spoilage, and standardizing quality in heterogeneous kitchen environments. This work bridges computational science and culinary practice, offering a novel methodology to address sustainability challenges in food production. The HPC infrastructure is critical due to the need for parallelized simulations of multiphysics systems and real-time optimization of high-dimensional parameter spaces. By translating computational insights into actionable protocols for chefs and food manufacturers, this project aims to establish a foundation for data-driven culinary innovation while advancing the role of HPC in non-traditional, service-oriented domains.
cip_title: Culinary, Entertainment, and Personal Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary, entertainment, and personal services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address emerging challenges in broadcast journalism, particularly the analysis of large-scale multimedia datasets and the development of AI-driven tools for ethical news production. As digital media platforms expand, journalists face increasing demands to process, verify, and disseminate audiovisual content rapidly while adhering to professional standards. Traditional computational tools are insufficient for handling the volume and complexity of modern broadcast data, including real-time video analytics, cross-platform content tracking, and detection of AI-generated or manipulated media. The proposed research will employ parallelized machine learning models to automate metadata extraction, sentiment analysis of audiovisual narratives, and anomaly detection in video streams to identify potential deepfakes or context distortions. Additionally, network analysis algorithms will simulate information dissemination patterns across social and broadcast media ecosystems, assessing how editorial decisions impact public discourse. These computational workflows require significant GPU capacity for training vision-language models on terabyte-scale video corpora and CPU clusters for multi-agent simulations of news spread dynamics. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated fact-checking, real-time bias monitoring in live broadcasts, and predictive models to guide ethical content prioritization during crises. By integrating HPC-driven insights into journalism curricula, this project aims to equip future practitioners with advanced technical literacy, fostering responsible innovation in an era of rapidly evolving media technologies. The results will directly inform pedagogical frameworks and industry standards, addressing critical gaps in accountability and trust within digital journalism.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for reporting, producing, and delivering news and news programs via radio, television, and video/film media; and that prepares individuals to be professional broadcast journalists, editors, producers, directors, and managers. Includes instruction in the principles of broadcast technology; broadcast reporting; on- and off-camera and microphone procedures and techniques; program, sound, and video/film editing; program design and production; media law and policy; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of intercultural communication and conflict resolution in hyper-diverse urban environments, integrating sociolinguistic networks, behavioral psychology, and spatial anthropology. Current frameworks for understanding intercultural group interactions often rely on static demographic data or qualitative case studies, limiting their ability to predict emergent tensions or test intervention strategies in rapidly evolving communities. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating interaction patterns across ethnolinguistic, religious, and socioeconomic subgroups within simulated urban districts. The ABM will incorporate dynamic parameters such as shifting cultural value systems, asymmetric power relations, and multilingual communication barriers, calibrated using longitudinal survey data from three global cities. Computational challenges include real-time natural language processing (NLP) simulations of cross-cultural dialogues, network analysis of trust formation across 10^5+ agent interactions, and geospatial mapping of segregation thresholds. HPC resources are critical for scaling the model to reflect realistic population densities (>1 million agents) and enabling Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic outcomes of policy interventions, such as multicultural education programs or community mediation frameworks. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool to identify high-risk zones for intercultural conflict, optimize resource allocation for diversity initiatives, and quantify the cascading effects of micro-level biases on macro-level social cohesion. By fusing computational social science with intercultural theory, this work aims to provide actionable insights for policymakers managing diversity in education, workplace integration, and urban planning contexts, while advancing methodological synergies between HPC and cross-cultural research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in culinary arts innovation, specifically in optimizing complex recipe development and enhancing precision in large-scale food production. Traditional culinary experimentation relies on iterative, resource-intensive trial-and-error processes, which limit scalability and hinder the systematic exploration of novel ingredient combinations, cooking techniques, and sustainability outcomes. The research problem centers on developing computational models to simulate physicochemical interactions during cooking, predict sensory outcomes, and optimize resource allocation in commercial kitchens. A hybrid approach integrating molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML), and fluid dynamics modeling will be employed to analyze ingredient behavior under varying thermal and mechanical conditions. Datasets encompassing flavor compound interactions, texture profiles, and heat transfer dynamics will be processed using GPU-accelerated workflows to map multi-dimensional relationships between cooking parameters and culinary outcomes. Additionally, reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained to propose ingredient substitutions that maintain desired sensory attributes while reducing waste or cost. The computational framework will also model kitchen workflow efficiency, simulating equipment utilization and staff coordination to minimize energy use and operational bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for chefs to prototype recipes digitally, a decision-support system for sustainable menu planning, and foundational insights into the molecular basis of culinary creativity. By bridging gastronomy with computational science, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven culinary innovation, with potential applications in food security, cultural preservation, and adaptive cuisine design for dietary needs. The project’s scale—requiring parallelized simulations of thousands of ingredient matrices and real-time ML inference—necessitates HPC resources to achieve practical fidelity and speed, enabling transformative advancements in a field traditionally underserved by computational research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide professional chef and related cooking services in restaurants and other commercial food establishments.  Includes instruction in recipe and menu planning, preparing and cooking of foods, supervising and training kitchen assistants, the management of food supplies and kitchen resources, aesthetics of food presentation, and familiarity or mastery of a wide variety of cuisines and culinary techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing school counseling interventions through large-scale simulation and predictive modeling. School counselors face complex challenges in addressing students’ academic, social-emotional, and career development needs, yet evidence-based strategies for personalizing interventions remain limited due to the multivariate, dynamic nature of student-counselor interactions. This study will develop computational models to simulate student trajectories under varying counseling approaches while accounting for contextual factors such as socio-economic disparities, school climate metrics, and mental health trends. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be employed to represent heterogeneous student populations, with parameters informed by longitudinal datasets from partner school districts and national youth development surveys. Machine learning methods, including clustering algorithms and network analysis, will identify patterns in intervention efficacy across demographic subgroups. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of simulated student cohorts (N > 100,000 agent-student instances), multi-year temporal resolution, and iterative parameter testing for model validation. Expected outcomes include a framework to predict which counseling strategies—such as trauma-informed group sessions, individualized academic monitoring, or career readiness programs—are most likely to improve student outcomes in specific contexts. Results will inform the creation of decision-support tools for counselors, enabling data-driven resource allocation while preserving the irreplaceable human elements of therapeutic relationships. By bridging gaps between educational research and computational social science, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for evaluating equity-focused interventions in school counseling, with broader implications for scaling evidence-based practices in under-resourced educational settings. The project aligns with federal priorities for advancing educational equity through innovative uses of research computing infrastructure.
cip_title: Counselor Education/ School Counseling and Guidance Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the theory and principles of guidance and counseling to the provision of support for the personal, social, educational, and vocational development of students, and the organizing of guidance services within elementary, middle and secondary educational institutions. Includes instruction in legal and professional requirements, therapeutic counselor intervention, vocational counseling, and related sociological and psychological foundations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in clinical training efficacy and patient care outcomes for Licensed Practical/Vocational Nurses (LPN/LVNs) through advanced computational modeling of patient-nurse interactions. Current training paradigms often rely on static case studies and limited clinical simulations, which may not adequately prepare students for the dynamic, high-stakes decision-making required in real-world settings. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that models diverse patient scenarios, including acute physiological changes, medication administration errors, and interprofessional communication challenges. The platform will integrate anonymized electronic health record (EHR) data from partner healthcare institutions, employing machine learning algorithms to generate adaptive, context-sensitive training modules. Agent-based modeling will simulate multi-patient environments under varying nurse-to-patient ratios, enabling the study of workflow optimization and stress-induced decision-making patterns. Additionally, natural language processing techniques will be applied to simulate patient-provider communication, with reinforcement learning frameworks providing real-time feedback to trainees. The computational intensity of these parallelized simulations—particularly the need to process terabytes of EHR data and run millions of scenario iterations—necessitates HPC resources for feasible execution times. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal intervention strategies for common clinical errors, predictive models for skill competency progression, and data-driven recommendations for curriculum enhancements. By creating a scalable virtual clinical environment, this research aims to reduce preventable adverse events in nursing practice while advancing evidence-based pedagogical approaches in vocational nursing education. The resulting open-source tools will provide a foundation for longitudinal studies on clinical competency retention and adaptive learning systems in nursing education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in providing general nursing care under the direction of a registered nurse, physician or dentist. Includes instruction in taking patient vital signs, applying sterile dressings, patient health education, and assistance with examinations and treatment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision-driven care models for adults with complex chronic conditions, a critical challenge in adult health nursing. Current clinical decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to integrate multidimensional patient data—including electronic health records, biometric sensor outputs, and patient-reported outcomes—into dynamic, individualized care plans. The computational limitations of traditional analytics tools further restrict real-time risk prediction and intervention optimization. To address this, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) pipeline to analyze heterogeneous datasets from 15,000+ adult patients with comorbidities such as diabetes, hypertension, and heart failure. The pipeline will employ ensemble learning techniques to predict hospitalization risks, medication non-adherence patterns, and physiological decompensation events. Federated learning architectures will be implemented to preserve data privacy across collaborating healthcare institutions. A key innovation involves coupling these ML models with agent-based simulations of care delivery workflows, enabling the evaluation of nurse-led intervention strategies under varying resource constraints. HPC resources are essential for training deep neural networks on high-temporal-resolution sensor data (e.g., continuous glucose monitoring streams), conducting Monte Carlo simulations of clinical scenarios, and optimizing hyperparameters across distributed computing nodes. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early deterioration detection, a computational framework for simulating nurse care coordination strategies, and actionable insights into personalized health maintenance program design. This work directly supports the program’s focus on advancing clinical management and health promotion for adult populations, with potential translational impacts on reducing preventable hospitalizations and enhancing nurse-led care models. By integrating computational science with nursing practice, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for data-driven adult health nursing in complex care environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide general care for adult patients. Includes instruction in adult primary care, adult pathophysiology, clinical management of medication and treatments, patient assessment and education, patient referral, and planning adult health maintenance programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision agricultural decision-making tools for extension professionals and growers. A critical challenge in agricultural systems is optimizing site-specific management practices—such as irrigation scheduling, nutrient application, and integrated pest management—under dynamic environmental conditions. Current tools often rely on generalized models that lack the resolution to account for hyperlocal variability in soil properties, microclimates, and pest population dynamics, leading to suboptimal resource use and reduced crop resilience. To address this gap, we propose developing a scalable computational framework integrating multi-source geospatial data (soil sensors, drone imagery, regional weather stations) with mechanistic crop growth models and machine learning algorithms. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-resolution datasets (1–5m spatial granularity) across thousands of simulated agricultural fields, coupled with parameter optimization for pest lifecycle models (e.g., degree-day accumulations for invasive species). This approach will generate probabilistic risk maps and real-time management recommendations tailored to individual farms. The computational workflow will prioritize interoperability with existing extension service platforms to ensure practical deployment. Anticipated outcomes include a cloud-based decision support system that reduces input costs by 15–20% in pilot regions while maintaining yield targets, as well as modular training materials for extension agents on interpreting model outputs. By scaling fine-grained analyses across diverse agroecological zones, this work will enhance the precision and adaptability of outreach services, directly supporting the Agricultural and Extension Education Services mission to deliver science-based, context-specific solutions to agricultural stakeholders.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide referral, consulting, technical assistance, and educational services to gardeners, farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and other organizations. Includes instruction in basic agricultural sciences, agricultural business operations, pest control, adult education methods, public relations, applicable state laws and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predictive modeling for nanoscale thermal transport in hybrid quantum-material systems, an emerging area at the intersection of nanoscale engineering, quantum physics, and computational science. Current models for heat dissipation in nanodevices rely on simplified bulk approximations or single-material frameworks, failing to capture the complex, non-equilibrium dynamics of hybrid systems such as 2D material heterostructures coupled to quantum dots or superconducting resonators. These limitations hinder the design of energy-efficient nanoelectronics and quantum technologies, where thermal management at interfaces governs performance and stability. To overcome this gap, we propose a multiscale computational approach integrating first-principles density functional theory (DFT), non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) methods, and machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics (ML-MD) simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve atomic-scale phonon scattering, interfacial thermal resistance, and quantum confinement effects across heterogeneous material boundaries at experimentally relevant scales. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-optimized codes for DFT (VASP) and MD (LAMMPS), coupled with custom Python-based ML force fields trained on ab initio datasets to extend simulation timescales. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework for predicting thermal transport in hybrid nanosystems, new insights into interfacial phonon engineering for heat mitigation in quantum devices, and design guidelines for next-generation thermal interfaces in superconducting qubit arrays. This work bridges a critical gap between quantum device engineering and nanoscale thermal sciences, with potential applications in cryogenic computing, photonic-integrated circuits, and energy-efficient nanoelectronics. The requested resources will enable simulations spanning 10^4–10^6 atoms over nanosecond timescales, exceeding the capabilities of current local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, growth, properties, and fundamental interactions of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across scientific disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how postsecondary instructors adapt learner-centered teaching strategies when integrating emerging educational technologies, with a focus on identifying scalable practices that improve equity in diverse classrooms. Despite growing emphasis on active learning and inclusive pedagogy, many instructors struggle to implement these approaches effectively in technology-mediated environments, particularly when addressing variability in student backgrounds, digital literacy, and engagement. Current frameworks often lack empirical validation under real-world computational constraints, such as limited tools for real-time adaptive feedback or dynamic assessment. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based simulations of virtual classrooms to model instructor decision-making and student outcomes under varied pedagogical and technological conditions. Simulations will incorporate empirical data from learning management systems, student assessment records, and instructor surveys across multiple disciplines. Machine learning techniques, including clustering and reinforcement learning, will identify patterns in effective teaching adaptations, while natural language processing will analyze qualitative feedback from instructors and students. The computational workload requires high-performance resources due to the scale of simulations (parallelized across thousands of agent configurations) and the complexity of training models on multimodal datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of how specific technology integrations influence equity gaps in course outcomes, (2) a framework for designing adaptive professional development resources that help instructors align tool use with learner-centered principles, and (3) open-source code for simulating pedagogical scenarios that reflect diverse institutional contexts. This work directly supports teacher education programs in preparing faculty to critically evaluate and implement educational technologies, with implications for improving instructional design practices in STEM and humanities disciplines. Results will be disseminated through workshops for postsecondary teaching centers and a public repository of simulation tools.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of analyzing high-density electroencephalographic (EEG) data to improve the detection and characterization of neurological disorders such as epilepsy, sleep disorders, and encephalopathies. Current clinical workflows rely on manual review and basic signal processing tools, which are inefficient for handling the increasing volume and complexity of multichannel EEG data. These limitations hinder the identification of subtle or transient pathological patterns, delaying diagnosis and personalized treatment planning. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing an automated, machine learning-driven pipeline optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The pipeline will integrate advanced signal preprocessing techniques to mitigate artifacts, feature extraction algorithms to quantify spectral and temporal dynamics, and deep learning models (e.g., convolutional neural networks and transformers) trained to classify abnormal neurophysiological patterns. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing of long-term EEG recordings (24+ hours) from multiple patients, requiring scalable storage and GPU-accelerated training. By leveraging HPC resources, we aim to reduce processing times from hours to minutes while maintaining diagnostic accuracy validated against expert clinician annotations. Expected outcomes include a deployable tool for rapid, standardized EEG analysis and novel biomarkers for early seizure onset prediction. This work will directly enhance the capabilities of electroneurodiagnostic technologists by providing actionable insights to physicians, improving patient outcomes through timely intervention. Additionally, the open-source computational framework will serve as a foundation for future research in neurodiagnostic technology, fostering innovation in clinical neurophysiology training and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to study and record electrical activity in the brain and nervous system for purposes of patient monitoring and supporting diagnoses. Includes instruction in patient communication and care; taking and abstracting patient histories; application of recording electrodes; EEG, EP, and PSG equipment operation and procedural techniques; and data recording and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing multi-threat risk assessment and emergency response planning in complex urban environments, with a focus on mitigating cascading security and fire-related hazards. Current approaches to modeling interdependent threats—such as cyber-physical attacks, chemical spills, and fire propagation—often lack the resolution and scalability to address dynamic, large-scale scenarios. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate agent-based simulations, machine learning-driven threat prediction, and physics-based fire-spread modeling into a unified platform. Key computational challenges include resolving real-time interactions between human behavior, infrastructure vulnerabilities, and environmental factors at city-block scales. The framework will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate probabilistic threat scenarios and hybrid neural-physical models to predict hazard evolution under varying mitigation strategies. Validation will utilize geospatial datasets from municipal emergency management systems and historical incident reports. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable tool for identifying critical infrastructure interdependencies, quantifying resource allocation trade-offs during multi-threat incidents, and generating adaptive response protocols. This work directly addresses gaps in the Security Science and Technology field by advancing computational methods for holistic risk management. The HPC component is essential due to the need for rapid, high-fidelity simulations across thousands of scenario permutations, which would be intractable on conventional systems. Successful implementation will provide emergency planners with evidence-based strategies to prioritize interventions, reduce systemic vulnerabilities, and enhance cross-agency coordination. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation modules and partnerships with regional homeland security agencies, fostering transferability to diverse urban contexts.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: Optimizing plant growth and resource efficiency in nursery operations requires precise management of multivariate environmental and physiological factors, yet current practices often rely on generalized protocols leading to suboptimal yields and resource waste. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model plant-environment interactions in real time, enabling data-driven decision-making for nursery managers. The research problem centers on the dynamic interplay between abiotic factors (e.g., light spectra, irrigation schedules, nutrient concentrations) and plant responses across species, which are difficult to predict using conventional methods due to nonlinear relationships and temporal dependencies. We propose a hybrid approach combining mechanistic models of plant physiology with machine learning (ML) trained on multimodal datasets, including hyperspectral imagery, soil sensor telemetry, and phenotypic time-series from controlled nursery trials. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parallelize parameter optimization for species-specific growth models, simulate long-term outcomes of management scenarios, and train deep neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets. Key computational challenges include integrating heterogeneous data streams at scale, resolving time-lagged effects of environmental stressors, and quantifying uncertainty in predictions. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for simulating nursery environments and a decision-support tool that recommends optimal irrigation, fertilization, and climate control protocols. By linking plant science with computational analytics, this work aims to reduce water and nutrient use by 15–30% in pilot nurseries while improving seedling survival rates, directly addressing the program’s focus on operational efficiency. The resource allocation will enable iterative model refinement, sensitivity analyses, and validation against experimental data, advancing both agricultural computational methods and scalable solutions for sustainable nursery management.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage outdoor plant farms, tree and shrub nurseries, and related facilities that develop domesticated plant products for propagation, harvesting, and transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science, farm and business management, nursery operations, equipment operation and maintenance, safety procedures, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between protein conformational changes and lipid bilayer interactions in membrane-associated biological processes. A critical unresolved challenge in biophysics is understanding how mechanical and electrostatic forces at membrane interfaces govern the folding, stability, and functional dynamics of integral membrane proteins, particularly ion channels and transporters. Traditional experimental techniques struggle to resolve transient intermediate states or quantify energy landscapes at atomistic resolution, creating a need for advanced computational modeling. We propose to employ all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enhanced by free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations and Markov state models (MSMs) to study two prototypical systems: the voltage-dependent gating of potassium channels and the substrate-induced conformational shifts in ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. Simulations will integrate experimentally derived structural data (e.g., cryo-EM maps) to ensure biological relevance. The HPC resources will enable microsecond-to-millisecond timescale sampling across multiple thermodynamic ensembles, coupled with machine learning-driven analysis of trajectory data to identify metastable states and allosteric pathways. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how membrane composition modulates protein energetics and novel predictions about mutation-induced dysregulation relevant to channelopathies and drug resistance. This work will establish a scalable computational framework for probing membrane-protein systems, directly addressing the program’s emphasis on biophysical theory, molecular assemblies, and bioenergetics. The requested resources are essential for managing the ∼500 TB of trajectory data and performing parallelized free energy calculations across 50+ replicas per system. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools for lipid force field optimization, benefiting the broader biophysics community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic resource allocation in omnichannel sales ecosystems using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, real-time interactions between consumer behavior, inventory logistics, and workforce scheduling. Traditional sales operations frameworks struggle to balance competing demands across physical retail, e-commerce, and third-party distribution platforms, particularly under volatile demand patterns and supply chain disruptions. The computational challenge lies in simulating millions of interdependent variables—including shifting customer preferences, warehouse throughput, and sales personnel availability—while maintaining sub-hourly decision cycles for adaptive resource deployment. Leveraging agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations, the project will develop a parallelized framework to test allocation strategies under diverse market scenarios, incorporating real-world data from partner organizations in consumer goods and retail. Key innovations include the integration of time-dependent graph neural networks to predict cross-channel demand spillovers and a hybrid optimization engine combining reinforcement learning with mixed-integer programming. The HPC environment is critical for scaling simulations to enterprise-level complexity, enabling comparative analysis of strategies across 10^6+ parameter combinations. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support system capable of reducing stockouts by 12-18% and improving labor utilization rates by 20% in modeled scenarios, with open-source release of core algorithmic components. This work bridges computational scalability gaps in sales operations research, offering a replicable methodology for data-driven resource allocation in fragmented, high-velocity commercial environments.
cip_title: Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Operations, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general process and techniques of direct wholesale and retail buying and selling operations and introduces individuals to related careers. Includes instruction in the principles of entrepreneurial economics, basic sales skills, the distribution channels for goods and services, and supervised practical application experiences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and conceptual evolution of Hindu philosophical systems as articulated in classical Sanskrit texts, including the Vedas, Upanishads, and later commentarial traditions. The primary research problem centers on mapping the development of key doctrinal frameworks—such as the relationship between *dharma* (moral order), *moksha* (liberation), and sect-specific theological interpretations—across geographically and temporally dispersed sources. Current scholarship lacks systematic computational models to trace how these ideas were contested, synthesized, or reified through centuries of philosophical debate, particularly in non-linear textual traditions where intertextual influences are often implicit. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored for Sanskrit, trained on existing digitized corpora and newly encoded manuscripts, to identify semantic shifts, argumentative patterns, and citation networks. Computational workflows will integrate phylogenetic algorithms to model doctrinal divergence among *darshanas* (philosophical schools), alongside graph-based analytics to visualize the diffusion of concepts across regions and sects. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses to handle the syntactic complexity of Sanskrit compounds, the volume of textual variants (≈10^6 potential comparisons), and iterative simulations testing historical transmission hypotheses. Expected outcomes include an open-access knowledge graph linking philosophical claims to their textual origins and later adaptations, as well as quantitative frameworks for assessing the epistemic boundaries of Hindu theological debates. This work will provide a foundation for reinterpreting Hinduism’s intellectual history through data-driven models of philosophical change, offering scholars new tools to contextualize primary sources and trace the emergence of contested ideas in global religious thought.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the group of South Asian theologies and philosophies collectively known as Hinduism; together with the religious history and cultural and social manifestations of the faith. Includes instruction in Hindu theology and philosophy (dharma); literature (Vedas, Upanishads, Epics, and commentaries); the Hindu Pantheon, sects, and movements; schools and disciplines; and related arts and sciences.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize law enforcement record-keeping and evidence management systems, addressing critical inefficiencies in handling heterogeneous, high-volume data across physical and digital domains. Current practices often rely on fragmented software solutions and manual processes, leading to delays in case resolution, risks of evidence misclassification, and vulnerabilities in chain-of-custody documentation. The project will develop computational frameworks to automate metadata extraction, cross-reference case files, and simulate storage configurations under varying jurisdictional constraints. Using natural language processing (NLP) models, we will analyze unstructured police reports and evidence logs to standardize tagging protocols, while graph-based algorithms will map relationships between cases, personnel, and evidence items to identify systemic bottlenecks. Parallelized simulations will evaluate the resilience of proposed digital evidence storage architectures against cybersecurity threats and data corruption scenarios, incorporating real-world variables such as legacy system interoperability and compliance with evolving legal standards. By integrating anonymized datasets from multiple agencies, the computational workflows will prioritize scalability to accommodate diverse organizational sizes and resource limitations. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predictive evidence inventory management, risk-aware case prioritization models, and evidence-tracking simulations adaptable to regional policy changes. This work aims to establish a replicable computational foundation for improving transparency, reducing administrative burdens, and enhancing the integrity of law enforcement data ecosystems—a critical need as agencies increasingly navigate hybrid physical-digital workflows without standardized best practices. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets, training domain-specific NLP architectures, and running large-scale security simulations that mirror the complexity of modern evidence management challenges.
cip_title: Law Enforcement Record-Keeping and Evidence Management
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and procedures for managing records in police or other security offices, including storing and retrieving evidence and related data. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, office management, report preparation, organizational software, database software, physical and digital evidence properties, controlled storage and retrieval, investigative file inventories, case management, security systems, and communications skills.

abstract: The analysis of high-dimensional, multi-source datasets in domains such as precision medicine and climate science presents significant challenges for traditional statistical methodologies, particularly in scalability and computational efficiency. This project aims to address these limitations by developing advanced Bayesian non-parametric models and ensemble learning techniques that integrate heterogeneous data types while quantifying uncertainties. The research will employ Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods with adaptive proposal mechanisms and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) samplers to improve convergence in high-dimensional parameter spaces. Additionally, large-scale bootstrap aggregating and permutation tests will be utilized for robust inference in non-parametric settings. These approaches require extensive computational resources due to the iterative nature of MCMC algorithms (requiring >10^6 iterations per chain), the need for cross-validation across hyperparameter grids, and the storage of massive intermediate matrices. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel execution of thousands of chains, distributed memory management for terabyte-scale datasets, and GPU-accelerated linear algebra operations critical for matrix decompositions in variational inference. The expected outcomes include: (1) a framework for scalable Bayesian inference that reduces wall-clock time by two orders of magnitude through novel parallel tempering schemes; (2) open-source R/Python libraries implementing these methods for longitudinal and spatially correlated data; (3) applications to neurodegenerative disease progression modeling using multi-omics data, enhancing early diagnostic criteria. By overcoming current computational bottlenecks, this work will empower applied statisticians to tackle previously intractable problems in public health and environmental monitoring, while advancing methodology at the intersection of statistical computing and machine learning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research, focusing on the dynamic interplay between emerging technologies and the evolution of legal frameworks. The research problem centers on the inadequacy of traditional legal analysis methods to process and interpret the vast, unstructured datasets generated by decentralized technologies (e.g., blockchain-based smart contracts, AI-driven regulatory compliance tools) and their real-world legal implications. Current approaches struggle to model the nonlinear, adaptive interactions between technological systems and legal norms, particularly in cross-jurisdictional contexts. To address this gap, the project proposes a hybrid computational methodology combining natural language processing (NLP), graph-based network analysis, and agent-based modeling. Legal texts (statutes, case law, treaties) and technology governance artifacts (smart contract code, algorithmic audit trails) will be processed using transformer models fine-tuned on legal corpora to extract semantically rich representations of rule structures and obligations. These outputs will inform the construction of multilayer networks mapping relationships between technical systems, legal entities, and regulatory requirements across jurisdictions. Agent-based simulations will then model how perturbations in technological ecosystems—such as protocol upgrades or adversarial exploits—cascade through legal and institutional frameworks. The computational workflow demands HPC resources to handle terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize graph traversals for cross-jurisdictional analysis, and execute high-fidelity simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel framework for quantifying legal adaptability to technological change, 2) predictive models identifying systemic vulnerabilities in tech-law interfaces, and 3) an open-access repository of annotated legal-technical corpora. By enabling granular, data-driven analysis of legal systems as complex adaptive systems, this work aims to inform the design of more resilient governance mechanisms for emergent technologies while establishing computational methods as critical tools in advanced legal studies.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program in one or more of the legal research or advanced practice fields.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving ethical and cultural narratives surrounding end-of-life care through computational text analysis and network modeling of historical medical literature, patient narratives, and public discourse. The research addresses a critical gap in health humanities scholarship: while qualitative studies have explored attitudes toward death and dying, large-scale quantitative analyses of how these narratives shift across time, geography, and cultural contexts remain limited. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques and graph-based network analysis, we will analyze a curated corpus spanning 150 years of medical journals (PubMed archives), patient diaries (digitized special collections), and news media (Chronicling America, ProQuest Historical Newspapers). The computational pipeline will employ transformer-based models (BERT, GPT-3.5) for semantic topic modeling to track conceptual associations between medical ethics frameworks (e.g., autonomy vs. beneficence) and cultural representations of mortality. Network science methods will then map how key stakeholders (clinicians, patients, religious institutions) influence discourse trajectories. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing 12TB of unstructured text data, training domain-specific language models, and running iterative simulations of narrative propagation across temporal networks. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of pivotal historical moments when medical and cultural death narratives diverged or converged, 2) quantitative evidence for how marginalized voices became excluded from or incorporated into bioethical frameworks, and 3) open-access visualization tools enabling humanists to explore discourse networks through interactive temporal graphs. This computational humanities approach will provide novel methodological pathways for studying the co-evolution of medical ethics and cultural values at unprecedented scale, with implications for contemporary palliative care policy and clinician training programs.
cip_definition: A program that explores the ethical, historical, literary, philosophical, and religious dimensions of medicine or health. Includes instruction in art, cultural studies, economics, ethics, history, literature, medical anthropology, philosophy, religion and spiritual thought, science and technology, visual art, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing complex industrial systems under uncertainty, with applications in supply chain resilience, healthcare operations, and sustainable energy distribution. Industrial systems increasingly face disruptions from demand volatility, resource constraints, and dynamic interdependencies between human and automated processes. Existing optimization methods struggle to balance real-time decision-making with long-term strategic planning, particularly when modeling stochastic events or multi-objective trade-offs. We propose a hybrid approach combining high-fidelity discrete-event simulation, parallelized stochastic optimization, and machine learning-based scenario generation to address these challenges. The computational workload involves solving large-scale mixed-integer linear programs with embedded Markov decision processes, requiring distributed memory architectures for scenario tree evaluations and Monte Carlo sampling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable iterative refinement of risk-aware scheduling policies through GPU-accelerated deep reinforcement learning agents trained on synthetic and real-world operational datasets. Key innovations include adaptive decomposition algorithms to partition problem spaces across nodes and a novel convergence criterion for non-stationary environments. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for resilience planning in multi-echelon networks, validated through case studies on medical supply distribution during crisis events and cross-sector resource sharing in circular economies. The research will advance methodological integration of prescriptive analytics and simulation-based digital twins in industrial engineering, directly supporting NSF’s priorities for cybermanufacturing and intelligent systems. Resource allocation will prioritize GPU node hours for neural network training and MPI-enabled clusters for distributed optimization tasks, with an estimated need for 250,000 core-hours annually. Results will be disseminated through open-source code repositories and industry partnerships to bridge academic research and practical implementation gaps.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Includes instruction in applied mathematics, physical sciences, the social sciences, engineering analysis, systems design, computer applications, and forecasting and evaluation methodology.

abstract: Critically ill patients in intensive care units (ICUs) often present with complex, rapidly evolving multi-organ dysfunction, making timely prognosis and treatment selection challenging. Existing predictive models frequently lack accuracy due to their inability to integrate high-dimensional, time-sensitive physiological data and account for dynamic inter-organ interactions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create predictive models that synthesize multimodal clinical data, including real-time vital signs, laboratory results, imaging biomarkers, and treatment response histories. Machine learning techniques, particularly deep neural networks with attention mechanisms, will be employed to model temporal patterns and cross-modal dependencies across organ systems. Bayesian methods will quantify prediction uncertainty, while agent-based modeling will simulate critical care interventions under varying physiological constraints. The computational infrastructure will process terabytes of electronic health records from five tertiary care centers, requiring parallelized data pipelines and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include validated risk stratification tools for sepsis-associated organ failure, personalized ventilation strategies in acute respiratory distress syndrome, and optimized fluid resuscitation protocols. By enabling real-time analysis of complex clinical trajectories, this research aims to reduce mortality through earlier targeted interventions while providing a scalable computational platform for critical care innovation. The proposed HPC resources are essential given the need for rapid iteration across model architectures, sensitivity analyses of therapeutic simulations, and validation against emerging ICU datasets. This work bridges computational scalability with clinical translatability, offering a paradigm shift in data-driven critical care management.
cip_definition: Research focused on the management of care for patients with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. Includes instruction in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures and post-discharge care of former critical care patients.

abstract: Pediatric dentistry faces complex challenges in understanding the multifactorial determinants of oral health disparities and treatment outcomes across diverse populations, including children with disabilities. Current clinical studies often lack the computational power to integrate high-dimensional datasets—such as electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, longitudinal behavioral patterns, and 3D craniofacial imaging—into predictive models that account for dynamic interactions between biological, environmental, and care-access variables. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for analyzing these heterogeneous datasets, enabling precision oral health strategies tailored to pediatric populations. The research will employ machine learning (ML) models, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to identify risk trajectories for early childhood caries and orthodontic complications in patients with neurodevelopmental conditions. Large-scale simulations will model the impact of socioecological factors on care adherence, while finite element analysis of dental biomechanics will optimize restorative protocols for children with physical disabilities. Computational workflows will be parallelized to process multi-institutional EHRs and imaging repositories, requiring GPU-accelerated training of deep learning architectures and distributed memory systems for genome-wide association studies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for caries progression, data-driven clinical decision support systems, and mechanistic insights into oral-systemic health interactions in medically complex pediatric cohorts.
