By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to overcome current limitations in data integration and real-time analytics, directly informing personalized prevention programs and reducing oral health inequities. All models and pipelines will be disseminated as open-source resources to advance computational pediatric dentistry research, with translational potential to improve clinical guidelines and resource allocation for vulnerable populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on primary oral health care to infants, children, and adolescents, including patients with medical, physical or mental disabilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize traditional wooden boatbuilding techniques through advanced simulations of structural integrity, hydrodynamic performance, and material behavior. While empirical methods remain foundational in the craft, modern boatbuilders face challenges in balancing historical authenticity with performance efficiency, especially as demand grows for vessels that meet contemporary safety and sustainability standards. Current manual design iterations are time-intensive and limited in evaluating complex variables such as dynamic load distributions, moisture-induced wood degradation, or hydrodynamic drag patterns. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate multi-physics interactions in wooden boat systems. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution in hull joinery and planking under varying maritime conditions, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will assess hydrodynamic efficiency across hull geometries. Machine learning models, trained on historical and experimental datasets, will predict optimal wood species, joinery techniques, and spar configurations under environmental and operational constraints. These simulations will integrate parametric design principles to iteratively refine lofting and fairing processes, reducing material waste and labor costs. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale simulations of multi-variable scenarios, including probabilistic models of wood aging and composite material interactions. Outcomes will include a computational framework to guide boatbuilders in selecting empirically validated, high-performance designs and a publicly accessible database of material performance metrics. By bridging traditional craftsmanship with computational engineering, this work aims to enhance the durability and efficiency of wooden vessels while preserving artisanal techniques. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for FEA/CFD workloads and high-memory nodes for dataset training, enabling scalable, high-fidelity simulations that are otherwise computationally prohibitive.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to construct and repair traditional and modern wooden boats. Includes instruction in budgeting, drafting, fairing, lofting, joinery, planking, spars and rigging, and woodworking.

abstract: This research seeks to address the challenge of modeling and optimizing decentralized information ecosystems in underserved rural communities, where fragmented access to digital infrastructure exacerbates disparities in healthcare and agricultural knowledge dissemination. Traditional centralized informatics approaches often fail in these contexts due to intermittent connectivity, heterogeneous data formats, and diverse user capabilities. We propose a novel computational framework integrating adaptive information architecture design with human-centered trust metrics to analyze and improve community-specific knowledge networks. The project employs agent-based modeling to simulate multi-layer interactions between human users, legacy technologies, and intermittent cloud resources, incorporating real-world data from partner communities in three geographically distinct regions. High-performance computing resources are required to handle the stochastic optimization of network topologies across thousands of parallel scenarios, particularly for simulating latency-tolerant synchronization protocols in low-connectivity environments. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in community-generated content flows, while graph neural networks will model the emergence of trust relationships within constrained information environments. Expected outcomes include a generalizable toolkit for designing resilient socio-technical systems that balance local information preservation with global knowledge integration. The computational models will advance informatics theory by formalizing metrics for "information equity" that account for technological, linguistic, and cultural dimensions of access. Results will directly inform the deployment of adaptive mobile platforms being co-developed with regional NGOs, potentially impacting over 200 rural communities currently underserved by conventional digital infrastructure solutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in multi-level teacher education by modeling and analyzing the efficacy of adaptive teaching strategies across diverse classroom environments. A critical challenge in teacher preparation is designing training frameworks that equip educators to address the cognitive, social, and developmental variability inherent in teaching students at multiple grade levels (e.g., K-5, 6-8). Existing studies lack granular computational models to simulate how pedagogical approaches interact with factors such as student age, subject complexity, and classroom diversity. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based simulations that replicate multi-age classroom dynamics, integrating real-world data from partner school districts on student performance, teacher interventions, and longitudinal outcomes. These simulations will parameterize variables including instructional pacing, differentiated content delivery, and assessment feedback loops, enabling the testing of hypothetical teaching strategies under varied conditions. Machine learning methods will then identify optimal strategy combinations for target educational levels. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (10,000+ simulated classrooms with 20-30 agents each), the need for parallelized parameter sweeps, and the complexity of training neural networks on high-dimensional interaction data. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based insights into how specific instructional practices succeed or falter when applied across developmental stages, (2) a publicly accessible repository of simulated classroom scenarios for teacher training programs, and (3) predictive tools to help educators tailor strategies for mixed-level classrooms. By bridging computational modeling and teacher education, this work aims to transform how multi-level teaching competencies are developed, directly supporting the preparation of versatile educators capable of addressing 21st-century classroom diversity.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at more than one educational level, such as a combined program in elementary/secondary, early childhood/elementary, elementary/middle school, or junior high/high school teacher education.

abstract: The rapid expansion of online education necessitates evidence-based strategies to optimize instructional design and personalize learning experiences. However, existing approaches to analyzing learner engagement and pedagogical effectiveness in virtual environments are constrained by the scale and complexity of multimodal data—including interaction logs, video analytics, forum discussions, and real-time assessments. Traditional computational tools lack the capacity to process these datasets efficiently or model dynamic learner behaviors at a granular level. This project proposes the development of a scalable computational framework to identify patterns in online learning behaviors and evaluate the efficacy of adaptive teaching practices. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will apply machine learning techniques, including natural language processing (NLP) for discussion forum analysis, clustering algorithms to classify learner engagement types, and neural networks to predict outcomes based on interaction sequences. The computational workflow will integrate anonymized datasets from three fully online graduate-level courses (n ≈ 1,200 learners) to train models that map instructional design variables (e.g., multimedia integration, feedback timing) to learning gains. A parallelized architecture will enable real-time simulation of alternative pedagogical scenarios, allowing instructors to test interventions before implementation. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model of learner success in asynchronous environments, (2) a toolkit for generating automated recommendations to optimize course design elements, and (3) an open-source framework for processing multimodal educational data at scale. By enabling rapid analysis of complex teaching-learning interactions, this work addresses critical gaps in online teacher preparation, particularly in designing responsive, equitable virtual classrooms. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage memory-intensive NLP tasks and iterative model training across heterogeneous datasets, which would be computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure. Results will directly inform graduate-level courses in instructional design and contribute to scholarly understanding of scalable analytics in teacher education.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various academic levels through online instructional technologies. Includes instruction in andragogy, pedagogy, assessment, instructional design and technology, and learning science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize real-time, data-driven decision-making in tourism promotion operations, an interdisciplinary niche intersecting computational social science, behavioral economics, and digital marketing analytics. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of current promotional strategies in adapting to rapidly shifting tourist behaviors, dynamic regional event landscapes, and volatile economic conditions. Existing models often rely on static datasets or simplified assumptions, failing to integrate multimodal data streams—including social media sentiment, transportation network fluctuations, and climate-related disruptions—into actionable insights. To address this gap, we propose developing an adaptive simulation framework using agent-based modeling (ABM) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to predict and optimize tourism campaign outcomes. The computational approach will involve three phases: 1) Training graph neural networks (GNNs) on heterogeneous data (e.g., geolocated visitor patterns, event registries, and accommodation pricing trends) to model destination attractiveness; 2) Implementing multi-agent systems simulating tourist decision processes under variable constraints (budgets, seasonal preferences, infrastructure limitations); and 3) Applying ensemble DRL algorithms to iteratively refine promotional strategies across simulated scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations, particularly when processing high-resolution spatial-temporal data across 50+ tourism regions simultaneously. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset capable of recommending optimized promotional allocations (e.g., targeted advertising budgets, event scheduling priorities) with 72-hour forecast windows, validated against historical crisis recovery datasets from three UNESCO World Heritage Sites. This work aims to establish a new paradigm for agile tourism resource allocation while contributing methodological advances in complex system simulation for public-private partnership environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of tourism in public and private sector settings. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between socio-cultural behaviors and the functional design of multi-use residential spaces in urban environments, leveraging computational modeling to optimize housing adaptability amid shifting demographic and lifestyle trends. As urban populations grow increasingly diverse, traditional housing models—designed around static assumptions about household composition and daily routines—often fail to meet the needs of non-nuclear families, remote workers, and aging populations. This research addresses this gap by developing an agent-based simulation framework to model how occupants interact with built environments under varying constraints, such as limited square footage, shared amenities, and evolving technological integration. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parameterize thousands of virtual households, incorporating heterogeneous behavioral data (e.g., activity patterns, spatial preferences, and social dynamics) sourced from ethnographic studies and IoT-derived occupancy datasets. Machine learning techniques will iteratively refine spatial configurations and policy recommendations, testing hypotheses about modular design efficacy, resource-sharing efficiency, and quality-of-life outcomes. The computational workflow integrates graph neural networks to map relational dependencies between occupants and built features, while Monte Carlo methods will assess robustness against stochastic variables like fluctuating occupancy rates or emergency scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital toolkit for architects and urban planners to simulate user-centric housing prototypes, alongside evidence-based guidelines for policymakers to incentivize adaptable housing codes. By bridging computational social science with human-centered design, this project aims to advance equitable, sustainable living solutions that respond dynamically to societal change, offering a novel methodological framework for interdisciplinary housing research.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the behavioral, social, economic, functional, and aesthetic aspects of housing, interiors, and other built environments. Includes instruction in analyzing, planning, designing, furnishing, and equipping residential, work, and leisure spaces to meet user needs and the study of related public policies.

abstract: The integration of cytogenetic and molecular genetic data remains a critical challenge in the diagnosis of human genetic disorders. Current analytical approaches struggle to synthesize high-throughput genomic datasets, including chromosomal microarray analyses, next-generation sequencing, and epigenetic profiling, leading to incomplete characterization of pathogenic variants. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable bioinformatics pipelines for multi-modal data integration. We will employ distributed computing frameworks to process and harmonize large-scale genomic datasets, enabling simultaneous analysis of structural variants, single-nucleotide mutations, and regulatory element alterations. Machine learning models, trained on integrated clinical and genomic data, will be implemented to prioritize variants based on their predicted functional impact and association with disease phenotypes. These models will utilize graph-based algorithms to map variant interactions across heterogeneous datasets and deep learning architectures to predict pathogenicity from sequence context and three-dimensional chromatin architecture. The computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing on HPC clusters, substantially reducing analysis times compared to conventional infrastructure. Success in this endeavor will enhance the resolution of variant detection, improve the accuracy of clinical interpretations, and uncover novel biomarkers for genetic syndromes. The resulting open-source tools will provide the community with robust methods for data synthesis, fostering collaborative research and standardized reporting in clinical genomics. By elucidating complex genotype-phenotype relationships, this work will advance our understanding of genetic disease mechanisms and inform targeted therapeutic strategies, directly aligning with the mission of the Laboratory Genetics and Genomics program to translate genomic insights into improved patient care.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the historical evolution of diagnostic uncertainty in 19th-century clinical medicine through large-scale computational analysis of archival medical casebooks, practitioner correspondence, and institutional records. Despite advances in digital humanities, the dynamic interplay between diagnostic ambiguity and therapeutic decision-making in pre-modern medicine remains understudied, particularly at the intersection of epistemic shifts in pathology and sociocultural perceptions of medical fallibility. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical medical lexicons to analyze patterns of diagnostic hedging, error documentation, and therapeutic adaptation across digitized collections spanning British, French, and German hospital archives (1800–1899). High-performance computing resources are required to process over 250,000 pages of handwritten and printed materials using transformer-based models fine-tuned for multilingual historical texts, with iterative semantic clustering to map temporal and regional variations in uncertainty expression. Concurrent agent-based modeling will simulate how diagnostic ambiguity propagated through professional networks, informed by extracted data on physician collaborations and citation practices. Expected outcomes include a quantitative framework for analyzing historical medical epistemology, identification of critical transitions in tolerance for diagnostic uncertainty during the bacteriological revolution, and open-access tools for temporal concept mapping in medical humanities. This computationally intensive approach addresses a significant gap in the historiography of clinical reasoning while demonstrating novel methodologies for analyzing historical medical uncertainty as both cognitive phenomenon and cultural practice. Results will inform contemporary debates about error disclosure in medicine by providing longitudinal perspective on the relationship between diagnostic technologies, professional identity, and the management of uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution and socio-economic context of medical theories, education, practices, and technologies; and on the history of diseases, therapeutics, patients, and healers. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of the historiography of medicine; the history of science, medicine, and technology; and of research methods in the history of medicine.

abstract: The integration of advanced imaging modalities, such as cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), has transformed diagnostic workflows in oral and maxillofacial radiology. However, the increasing resolution and complexity of 3D/4D imaging datasets pose significant computational challenges for real-time analysis, particularly in detecting early-stage pathologies (e.g., osteonecrosis, tumors) and modeling dynamic biomechanical processes in the temporomandibular joint. Current clinical tools lack the capacity to process multi-terabyte datasets efficiently or integrate machine learning (ML)-based predictive analytics at scale. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for automated, high-throughput image analysis and biomechanical simulation. The proposed work will utilize GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures, including 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers, to segment craniofacial structures, detect microarchitectural bone changes, and classify lesion progression across longitudinal scans. Concurrently, finite element modeling (FEM) simulations will be deployed on HPC clusters to analyze stress distributions in jawbone implants under physiological loading conditions, incorporating patient-specific CBCT-derived geometries. These computational workflows will be validated against histopathological and clinical outcome data from a retrospective cohort of 850 patients. The HPC environment is critical for managing data parallelism during model training, reducing FEM solve times from days to hours, and enabling ensemble approaches to uncertainty quantification in ML predictions. Anticipated outcomes include novel biomarkers for early disease detection, optimized implant design parameters, and open-source tools for scalable image analysis. This work will directly enhance diagnostic precision in complex cases while establishing a computational infrastructure to support future research in AI-driven personalized treatment planning for maxillofacial disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on producing and interpreting images of the jaws, teeth, bone, and other structures of the head and neck region; and to diagnose and manage diseases, disorders, and conditions that affect this area of the body.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Latin textual evolution across historical periods, with a focus on interdisciplinary methodologies bridging philology, linguistics, and digital humanities. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks for analyzing morphological, syntactic, and stylistic shifts in Latin literature from the Classical era through Late Antiquity and into medieval ecclesiastical usage. Existing manual approaches struggle to process the vast corpus of digitized Latin texts (e.g., the Patrologia Latina, classical works, and medieval charters) required to systematically trace linguistic continuity and innovation. This project proposes a computational pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) tools optimized for historical Latin variants, machine learning models for detecting diachronic and genre-based patterns, and high-throughput comparative analysis of semantic networks. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of over 50,000 texts (∼10 billion tokens) across multiple linguistic registers, as well as the training of transformer-based models to identify understudied philological phenomena, such as the diffusion of Christian Latin lexical features into secular contexts. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database cataloging linguistic transitions correlated with historical events and textual genres; (2) quantitative models mapping the influence of Italic dialects and non-literary Latin on formal literature; and (3) open-source tools for automated dating and attribution of fragmentary or anonymized ecclesiastical texts. By integrating computational rigor with domain-specific expertise, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of Latin’s evolution as a living language, while establishing scalable methods for interdisciplinary textual analysis in premodern studies. The requested allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale text clustering, and storage for intermediate linguistic datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Latin language and literature from its origins through its decline and its current ecclesiastical usage, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, related Italic dialects, Late Roman and Medieval Latin, and modern Church Latin.

abstract: Child care systems face complex challenges in balancing dynamic factors such as fluctuating demand, regulatory constraints, workforce availability, and equitable access to services. Traditional management approaches often rely on static models, which inadequately capture the nonlinear interactions between these variables, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation and policy implementation. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize child care service delivery at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct an agent-based model (ABM) that integrates demographic data, parental behavior patterns, staff scheduling dynamics, and policy-driven constraints. The ABM will simulate scenarios ranging from routine operations to crisis responses (e.g., pandemic-related closures), enabling the evaluation of interventions such as subsidy adjustments, facility expansion thresholds, and workforce training cascades. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical childcare utilization datasets to identify latent demand patterns and predict service gaps across socioeconomic strata. The computational intensity arises from the need to process fine-grained spatial-temporal data across multiple metropolitan regions while maintaining real-time interactivity for parameter sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of quantifying trade-offs between cost, quality, and accessibility in childcare systems; evidence-based recommendations for optimizing public-private funding structures; and scalable templates for adaptive staffing models. By bridging computational social science with operational management theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven child care system design that prioritizes developmental outcomes alongside economic sustainability. The proposed HPC resources are critical to achieving the required scale and resolution, as conventional computing infrastructure cannot support the simultaneous optimization of millions of interacting variables across heterogeneous datasets.
cip_title: Child Care and Support Services Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the provision and management of child care services and that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage child care facilities and programs that meet children's developmental needs and interests and that provide safe and healthy environments. Includes instruction in child development and psychology; home- and institution-based child care; identification of diseases, injuries, and psychological trauma and applicable referrals; parent relations; personnel and business management principles; and related laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize the analysis of multidimensional datasets generated by heterogeneous scientific experiments, addressing the growing challenge of efficiently processing and interpreting complex, high-volume data in resource-constrained research environments. The research problem centers on the limitations of existing laboratory informatics tools, which struggle to integrate disparate data types—such as spectral, imaging, and time-series measurements—while maintaining computational efficiency and analytical rigor. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized data processing pipelines combining machine learning-driven feature extraction, physics-informed neural networks, and graph-based data fusion algorithms. The computational approach will focus on three pillars: (1) distributed computing architectures for real-time preprocessing of terabyte-scale experimental datasets, (2) hybrid quantum-classical optimization techniques for enhancing pattern recognition in noisy datasets, and (3) containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility across experimental modalities. The project will validate these methods through case studies spanning materials characterization, chemical reaction dynamics, and biological system modeling, using benchmark datasets from collaborating experimental laboratories. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive data integration, demonstrated reductions in computational overhead for common analytical tasks (projected 40-60% improvement versus existing tools), and new protocols for maintaining data provenance in multiuser HPC environments. By creating a unified platform that bridges experimental data streams with advanced computational analytics, this work aims to significantly enhance research throughput in laboratory settings while establishing best practices for FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data management in science-related technologies. The requested computing resources—including GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory processors—are critical for testing the framework at biologically and physically relevant scales, enabling translation from computational prototypes to practical laboratory implementations.
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of scientific research and development. Includes instruction in standard laboratory practices and procedures; techniques for analysis, testing and inspection; laboratory instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance; laboratory and materials handling safety; and computer applications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate emergent behavioral dynamics in heterogeneous populations during homeland security crises, with a focus on scenarios involving disinformation propagation and decentralized threat coordination. Current models often oversimplify socio-cultural variables or lack granularity to address the interplay between digital communication networks and real-world collective behavior, limiting their utility for proactive threat mitigation. The research will integrate agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and multilayer network analysis to capture how ideologically fragmented groups adapt to security interventions in digitally mediated environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing large-scale simulations that incorporate 1) real-time social media data streams, 2) cognitive bias parameters derived from experimental psychology studies, and 3) geospatial constraints on physical mobilization patterns. The computational architecture will leverage GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to analyze cross-platform information cascades alongside reinforcement learning agents that simulate adversarial adaptation strategies. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit to identify tipping points in crisis escalation trajectories and evaluate the resilience of communication protocols used by emergency responders. By bridging computational social science with security informatics, this work aims to advance decision-support systems for managing hybrid threats that exploit the sociotechnical vulnerabilities of modern interconnected societies. The resulting models will be validated against historical case studies of coordinated disruption campaigns and stress-tested through scenario-based war-gaming exercises with homeland security stakeholders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to model the long-term impacts of environmental and socioeconomic factors on cultural heritage sites, enabling data-driven policy recommendations for sustainable preservation. Cultural resource management faces challenges in balancing preservation needs with urban development, climate change, and tourism pressures, yet existing tools often lack the capacity to simulate complex, dynamic interactions across spatial, temporal, and cultural variables. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-source datasets—including geospatial records, climate projections, archaeological surveys, and visitor traffic patterns—through agent-based modeling and machine learning. The computational workflow will simulate site degradation scenarios under varying policy interventions, such as zoning restrictions, conservation funding allocations, or disaster preparedness protocols. A key innovation involves training graph neural networks to identify nonlinear relationships between preservation outcomes and contextual factors like land-use changes or regional economic trends. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across HPC nodes, we will quantify uncertainties in policy efficacy while scaling analysis to over 500 heritage sites documented in transnational databases. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support toolkit for heritage managers, optimized preservation prioritization algorithms, and policy briefs evaluating trade-offs between conservation rigor and community development goals. This work advances interdisciplinary methodologies in cultural resource management by bridging computational scalability with humanities-driven preservation ethics, offering replicable models for mitigating risks to vulnerable heritage assets worldwide. The requested resources will enable processing petabyte-scale environmental datasets and iterative policy testing at resolutions previously unfeasible for non-engineering disciplines.
cip_title: Cultural Resource Management and Policy Analysis
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of cultural studies, public policy analysis, and management skills to planning, promoting, and implementing programs to preserve and protect cultural heritage sites and artifacts. Includes instruction in historical preservation and conservation, business management, policy analysis, applied economics, public relations, applied history, historical archaeology, and environmental impact studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the efficacy of embodied learning pedagogies in drama and dance teacher education. A critical challenge in preparing educators for these disciplines lies in quantifying how multimodal teaching strategies—integrating movement, spatial awareness, and emotional expression—affect skill acquisition and instructional outcomes. Traditional qualitative assessments, while valuable, struggle to capture real-time physiological and behavioral data at scales necessary to generalize findings. Our research addresses this gap by developing computational models to simulate classroom interactions and evaluate teacher-student dynamics in virtual environments. Motion capture datasets from dance rehearsals and drama exercises will be processed using machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in pedagogical effectiveness, correlating instructors’ kinematic choices with student engagement metrics. Agent-based modeling will simulate diverse classroom scenarios, enabling stress-testing of instructional approaches under variable group sizes, skill levels, and spatial configurations. The computational workflow requires parallel processing for three-dimensional motion analytics and Monte Carlo simulations of pedagogical interventions. Expected outcomes include a framework to optimize evidence-based curriculum design for drama and dance educators, with quantified thresholds for movement complexity, feedback timing, and scaffolded skill progression. By bridging performing arts pedagogy with computational analytics, this work aims to establish scalable benchmarks for teacher training programs, directly impacting how institutions prepare educators to adapt kinesthetic teaching methods across learning environments. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional data and iterative modeling required to advance this emerging intersection of performing arts education and computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach drama and/or dance programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize wholesale purchasing decisions in fashion merchandising by integrating real-time consumer sentiment analysis, supply chain dynamics, and macroeconomic trend modeling. The challenge lies in aligning volatile consumer preferences—driven by rapidly evolving social media trends and cultural shifts—with production lead times and supplier constraints. Traditional linear regression models fail to capture the nonlinear interdependencies between hyper-localized trend signals, global logistics disruptions, and wholesale buyer behavior. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for social media text/image analysis, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model supplier-retailer networks, and agent-based simulations of bulk purchasing decisions. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to train multi-modal models on petabytes of structured (historical purchase orders, inventory turnover rates) and unstructured data (Instagram posts, TikTok videos, influencer content) while simulating supply chain scenarios across 18 global fashion hubs. Computational experiments will benchmark proposed models against industry-standard forecasting tools using custom loss functions that prioritize minimizing both overstock waste and opportunity costs from understocking trending items. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system capable of recommending optimized wholesale purchase quantities with 72-hour trend anticipation windows, demonstrated to reduce deadstock by an estimated 34-41% in pilot simulations using historical data from mid-sized apparel brands. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, operations research, and fashion studies, offering a novel methodology for responsive resource allocation in trend-driven industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote product lines/brands, and organize promotional campaigns, at the wholesale level to attract retailer interest, wholesale purchasing, and supply contracts. Includes instruction in wholesaling, wholesale advertising, selling, and customer relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of household resource allocation under socioeconomic stressors, a critical yet understudied area within Work and Family Studies. Traditional approaches to understanding family decision-making often rely on qualitative or small-scale quantitative data, limiting their capacity to model nonlinear interactions between factors such as income volatility, caregiving demands, and access to community resources. This research addresses this gap by developing computational models that simulate household behavior across diverse demographic and economic scenarios, integrating heterogeneous datasets including census data, time-use surveys, and public health records. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be employed to represent individual household members’ decision-making processes, while machine learning techniques will identify patterns in resource prioritization (e.g., budgeting, childcare, nutrition) under varying constraints. The computational pipeline will require iterative calibration against empirical data, necessitating parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses. Key challenges include managing high-dimensional data inputs, ensuring model scalability across regional contexts, and addressing ethical considerations in simulating vulnerable populations. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for predicting how policy interventions (e.g., subsidized childcare, emergency financial assistance) might stabilize household resource networks, particularly in underserved communities. The project will also yield educational modules for Work and Family Studies programs, demonstrating computational literacy applications in family resource management. By bridging data science and human ecology, this work advances methodological innovation in a field traditionally reliant on non-computational approaches, offering actionable insights for policymakers and educators while expanding the role of HPC in non-STEM disciplines.
cip_definition: An introductory program that focuses on family and consumer science concepts and principles at the basic and vocational levels, and the various potential career paths open to interested students. Includes instruction in career, community, and family connections; family and family/consumer resources; human development; interpersonal relationships; nutrition and wellness; parenting; and career possibilities in various related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of computational modeling and machine learning in the study of alternative and complementary medicine (ACM) modalities. Despite growing interest in ACM therapies such as acupuncture, herbal medicine, and mind-body interventions, their biochemical mechanisms, efficacy, and interactions with conventional treatments remain understudied at a systems level. A key barrier is the complexity of analyzing multi-scale data—from molecular interactions to clinical outcomes—using traditional methods. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, network pharmacology, and predictive analytics to model ACM therapies. MD simulations will characterize the binding dynamics of herbal compounds (e.g., curcumin, ginsenosides) with biological targets, while machine learning algorithms will analyze clinical datasets to identify patterns in treatment responses. Network models will map interactions between ACM interventions and cellular pathways, integrating multi-omics data to predict synergistic or adverse effects. The project will focus on two case studies: (1) optimizing herbal formulations for inflammatory conditions by simulating compound-target networks, and (2) modeling neurophysiological responses to acupuncture using patient-specific electrophysiological data. HPC resources are essential for handling large-scale simulations (e.g., 10⁶-atom systems in MD), training deep learning models on heterogeneous datasets (clinical, genomic, and imaging data), and conducting ensemble analyses to account for biological variability. Outcomes will include validated predictive models of ACM therapy mechanisms, open-source tools for ACM research, and evidence-based frameworks for personalizing integrative treatments. This work will bridge gaps in ACM evidence by providing mechanistic insights, supporting safer integration with conventional care, and advancing computational methods tailored to holistic health systems. The requested resources will enable unprecedented scalability in modeling the complexity of ACM, directly aligning with national priorities for interdisciplinary health research.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of industrial piping and fire protection systems through advanced computational modeling. Current methodologies for system design rely heavily on empirical guidelines and static calculations, which often fail to account for dynamic operational conditions, such as fluctuating fluid pressures, thermal expansion, or multi-phase flow interactions. These limitations can lead to suboptimal system performance, increased maintenance costs, or safety risks. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop high-fidelity simulations of complex piping networks and sprinkler systems under diverse operational scenarios. The computational approach will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model fluid behavior, finite element analysis (FEA) to assess structural stresses in piping materials, and machine learning algorithms to optimize system layouts and component configurations. Simulations will incorporate real-world variables, including transient thermal loads, corrosion rates, and seismic activity, to evaluate system resilience and compliance with evolving industry standards. The project will also explore the integration of digital twin frameworks to enable predictive maintenance strategies. By utilizing HPC resources, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks associated with large-scale 3D simulations and parametric studies, enabling rapid iteration of design alternatives. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for pipe system performance, a modular optimization toolkit for sprinkler network design, and data-driven recommendations for material selection under extreme conditions. These results will advance the technical rigor of pipefitting education by providing instructors with interactive simulation tools for classroom use, while offering industry partners actionable insights to improve system efficiency and safety. The project will also train students in computational methods, bridging gaps between traditional trade skills and modern digital workflows in the piping trades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, install, and test industrial and commercial piping systems and automatic fire and exposure protection systems. Includes instruction in water systems, steam systems, heating and cooling systems, lubricating systems, piping materials, installation tools operation and maintenance, valve installation and repair, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a dynamic simulation framework for optimizing equitable access and environmental resilience in urban parks and recreational facilities. As urbanization intensifies, park systems face competing pressures: growing demand for recreational spaces, climate-driven stressors on green infrastructure, and disparities in service distribution. Traditional planning tools lack the capacity to model these interconnected factors at scale, particularly when integrating real-time data on usage patterns, ecological thresholds, and socioeconomic equity metrics. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate visitor behavior, facility wear-and-tear dynamics, and ecosystem impacts under varying management scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to anonymized mobile device data and environmental sensor inputs to calibrate visitation patterns and predict stress points in infrastructure. A key innovation involves coupling hydrological models with crowd dynamics simulations to assess how stormwater management features (e.g., bioswales, permeable surfaces) interact with high-traffic recreational zones during extreme weather events. Computational outputs will inform adaptive design principles for park systems that balance human-centered needs with ecological carrying capacities. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support toolkit for municipal planners, enabling scenario testing of maintenance schedules, capacity limits, and climate adaptation strategies. By quantifying trade-offs between accessibility, operational costs, and environmental health at unprecedented spatial-temporal resolutions, this work advances computational methodologies for leisure space management while addressing pressing societal challenges in urban livability and climate justice. The scale of data integration and need for iterative, high-resolution simulations necessitate HPC capabilities to process multi-terabyte geospatial datasets and run parallelized scenario analyses across heterogeneous urban landscapes.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Facilities Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage park facilities and other indoor and outdoor recreation and leisure facilities. Includes instruction in supervising support personnel, health and safety standards, public relations, and basic business and marketing principles.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of aerosol-cloud-climate interactions in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere (UTLS), a critical region where heterogeneous chemistry and microphysical processes influence radiative forcing and climate feedbacks. Current global climate models (GCMs) inadequately resolve the fine-scale dynamics and multiphase chemistry governing aerosols and ice cloud formation in this region, leading to persistent uncertainties in projections of cirrus cloud radiative effects and stratospheric aerosol impacts on ozone recovery. We propose to address these gaps by developing a high-resolution modeling framework that couples the Community Earth System Model (CESM) with a newly parameterized cloud microphysics module, incorporating stochastic ice nucleation processes and size-resolved aerosol chemistry. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct ensemble simulations at 25 km horizontal resolution, nested within global 100 km simulations, to capture cross-scale interactions between deep convection, aerosol transport, and cirrus formation. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs in simulating sulfate-organic aerosol partitioning and ice crystal growth kinetics. The project will utilize observational datasets from recent airborne campaigns (e.g., ATom, POSIDON) for model validation, focusing on tropical UTLS regions where model-data discrepancies in aerosol extinction and ice water content exceed 40%. Expected outcomes include improved quantification of aerosol indirect effects on cirrus cloud lifetime and a refined understanding of how volcanic injections and anthropogenic emissions interact to modify UTLS composition. This work directly supports international climate assessment reports (IPCC, WMO) by reducing key uncertainties in climate sensitivity estimates. The requested HPC allocation (2.5 million core-hours annually) will enable the computationally intensive nested simulations and ensemble-based uncertainty analysis, which are infeasible with current institutional resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of atmospheric constituents, reactions, measurement techniques, and processes in predictive, current, and historical contexts. Includes instruction in climate modeling, gases and aerosols, trace gases, aqueous phase chemistry, sinks, transport mechanisms, computer measurement, climate variability, paleoclimatology, climate diagnosis, numerical modeling and data analysis, ionization, recombination, photoemission, and plasma chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives in Soviet and post-Soviet media, focusing on representations of national identity across Russian-language newspapers, journals, and digital archives from 1980 to 2000. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how rapid sociopolitical transformations during this period—including perestroika, the Soviet Union’s dissolution, and the early years of the Russian Federation—were reflected in and shaped by media discourse. Existing studies have relied on manual close readings of limited texts, but the scale and linguistic complexity of the corpus (over 10 million pages of digitized materials) necessitate advanced computational methods. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for Russian-language text, to conduct large-scale semantic analysis, sentiment tracking, and topic modeling. Custom algorithms will identify shifts in keyword usage, framing of historical events, and rhetorical strategies tied to identity construction. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific language models, parallel processing of high-resolution scanned documents (including OCR correction for Cyrillic texts), and running iterative simulations to map discourse networks across time and publication types. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of annotated texts, visualizations of narrative trajectories, and quantitative evidence linking media discourse to broader cultural and institutional changes. This work will provide a novel framework for interdisciplinary scholarship in Russian Studies, enabling researchers to trace cultural dynamics at unprecedented scale while preserving the contextual nuance critical to area studies. Findings will also inform methodological advancements in computational humanities, particularly for non-English and Cyrillic-language materials.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Russian Federation and its Soviet, Czarist, and medieval predecessors and related borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable, high-throughput data processing frameworks to address inefficiencies in managing heterogeneous, large-scale datasets across scientific and industrial domains. Modern data workflows increasingly involve unstructured or semi-structured data (e.g., sensor streams, multimedia, genomic sequences) that challenge conventional relational database systems and batch processing tools. Existing methods struggle with real-time transformation, cross-format interoperability, and maintaining data integrity at petabyte scales. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational architecture leveraging distributed computing paradigms, GPU-accelerated preprocessing, and adaptive metadata management. The project will implement and benchmark a modular pipeline using Apache Spark for partitioned data ingestion, coupled with optimized CUDA kernels for parallelized transformation tasks such as tokenization, dimensionality reduction, and anomaly detection. A novel graph-based metadata tracker will be developed to enable lineage tracing and reproducibility across iterative processing stages. The computational workflow will be stress-tested against diverse datasets, including high-frequency IoT telemetry, multi-spectral satellite imagery, and longitudinal biomedical records, each requiring distinct normalization strategies. By utilizing high-performance computing resources—particularly GPU clusters and parallel file systems—we aim to achieve sub-second latency for terabyte-scale transformations while maintaining 99.9% pipeline reliability under variable load conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithmic libraries for fault-tolerant data reshaping, performance benchmarks comparing distributed vs. GPU-accelerated approaches, and a reproducibility framework compliant with FAIR data principles. This work will directly enhance capabilities in fields requiring rapid, auditable processing of complex data, such as precision agriculture, smart city infrastructure, and personalized healthcare. The resource allocation will additionally support training initiatives to prepare students in distributed systems programming and performance optimization for non-uniform data architectures.
cip_title: Data Processing and Data Processing Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master and use computer software programs and applications for inputting, verifying, organizing, storing, retrieving, transforming (changing, updating, and deleting), and extracting information. Includes instruction in using various operating system configurations and in types of data entry such as word processing, spreadsheets, calculators, management programs, design programs, database programs, and research programs.

abstract: Community-based interventions aimed at addressing systemic inequities require nuanced understanding of how social networks, environmental stressors, and programmatic supports interact across time. Current evaluation methods often struggle to model dynamic, multilevel systems or predict long-term outcomes of prevention strategies under varying community conditions. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate agent-based models (ABMs) simulating community response to culturally tailored mental health interventions in marginalized populations. The ABMs will integrate longitudinal survey data from 12 urban neighborhoods (N≈15,000 individuals) with geospatial data on resource accessibility, social service utilization patterns, and neighborhood-level stressors. Computational challenges include scaling networks to reflect realistic community structures, modeling bidirectional person-environment interactions, and simulating intervention effects across decadal timescales. Parallelized model iterations will assess how variations in intervention timing, dosage, and cultural adaptation influence the emergence of community resilience or entrenched disparities. Sensitivity analyses will identify critical leverage points where small resource allocations yield disproportionate improvements in collective mental health outcomes. Outcomes will advance prevention science by enabling virtual testing of intervention strategies that account for complex social ecologies—a capability beyond traditional regression or cohort models. The computational framework will be shared as open-source software to support community psychology researchers in designing data-driven, context-sensitive programs. This work directly aligns with national priorities to reduce mental health disparities through scalable community capacity building, while pushing methodological boundaries in applying computational social science to applied psychology. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter space explorations, and storage of multidimensional output data for public dissemination.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply psychological principles to the analysis of social problems, and the implementation of intervention strategies for addressing these problems. Includes instruction in social ecology, primary and secondary prevention of social pathologies, social intervention strategies and tactics, large group counseling, social services systems behavior, creating settings, cultural stress, and the dynamics of social change.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between digital communication patterns and family relational health across generational cohorts, leveraging computational modeling to uncover latent behavioral signatures in longitudinal interaction data. The proliferation of asynchronous communication platforms has fundamentally altered family ecosystems, yet there remains a critical gap in understanding how temporally fragmented interactions influence developmental outcomes across family subsystems. We propose to analyze multi-year datasets comprising timestamped digital communications (texts, social media interactions, video call logs) from 1,200 family triads (adolescent, parent, grandparent), paired with quarterly psychosocial assessments. The computational challenge involves developing temporal network models that simultaneously track 1) emotional valence trajectories derived through NLP sentiment analysis, 2) interaction rhythm variability across multiple time scales, and 3) cross-generational contagion effects in communication patterns. High-performance computing resources are essential for implementing parallelized hierarchical hidden Markov models that can process over 18 million timestamped events while maintaining family-level and individual-level state transitions. The analysis pipeline will integrate graph neural networks to detect emergent interaction motifs predictive of family cohesion metrics, with particular attention to life-stage-specific vulnerabilities in developmental trajectories. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for identifying critical transition points in family communication systems and evidence-based guidelines for digital interaction thresholds that optimize developmental outcomes across generations. This work bridges developmental psychology, computational social science, and family systems theory, providing urgently needed insights into how evolving communication technologies reshape the temporal architecture of family development.
cip_title: Human Development and Family Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on basic human developmental and behavioral characteristics of the individual within the context of the family. Includes instruction in the conditions that influence human growth and development; strategies that promote growth and development across the life span; and the study of family systems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance psychometric methodology by addressing computational challenges in estimating high-dimensional item response theory (IRT) models and conducting large-scale simulation studies to evaluate their statistical properties. Traditional estimation methods, such as marginal maximum likelihood and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), face prohibitive runtime and memory constraints when applied to complex models with thousands of interactive item parameters or latent traits. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing and validating scalable Bayesian and variational inference algorithms optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The research will implement distributed computing frameworks to parallelize parameter sampling, leverage GPU acceleration for matrix-intensive operations, and automate dynamic resource allocation for heterogeneous tasks. A key focus is simulating polytomous, multidimensional IRT models under realistic conditions (e.g., missing data, cross-classified response dependencies) to assess parameter recovery, model fit, and computational efficiency across hardware configurations. Empirical validation will utilize the Program for International Student Assessment (PISA) dataset, requiring processing of over 600,000 respondents’ polytomous responses with nested latent skill dimensions. The project’s computational demands necessitate HPC resources for 1) running 10,000+ parallel simulation conditions to establish numerical stability benchmarks, 2) storing intermediate outputs from 50TB of generated response data, and 3) training neural network-based IRT approximations via distributed tensor operations. Anticipated outcomes include open-source software for large-scale psychometric modeling, validated guidelines for HPC resource allocation in IRT studies, and methodological advances in quantifying uncertainty for adaptive test assembly algorithms. These contributions will directly enhance the precision and feasibility of modern educational and psychological assessments while providing a computational framework for next-generation measurement models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical procedures used in psychological test construction and validation; the general problems of the measurement of behavior; and the application of quantitative methods to research design and other methodological topics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of silicate melt behavior in magmatic systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of multicomponent phase equilibria and reactive transport. A critical gap persists in modeling the coupled effects of volatile species (e.g., H2O, CO2) and trace elements on melt crystallization kinetics at pressures and temperatures relevant to planetary crust formation. Traditional thermodynamic models often oversimplify non-ideal mixing in silicate melts, leading to inaccuracies in predicting mineral stability fields and melt-vapor partitioning. To address this, we propose an integrated computational approach combining atomistic-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using density functional theory (DFT) with mesoscale phase-field modeling. The MD simulations will parameterize melt structure and diffusion properties under varying fugacities of volatiles, while phase-field models will simulate crystal growth/dissolution dynamics in multicomponent systems. These datasets will inform machine learning-driven optimization of existing geochemical software (e.g., MELTS) to improve predictive capacity for disequilibrium processes. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of quantum mechanical calculations (VASP) across thousands of cores, coupled with GPU-accelerated phase-field simulations of polycrystalline textures. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of silicate melt properties validated against experimental studies, (2) open-source modules for modeling volatile-bearing magmatic systems, and (3) new constraints on timescales of magma reservoir evolution prior to volcanic eruptions. By resolving microscale controls on macroscale geochemical signals preserved in igneous rocks, this work will enhance interpretations of planetary differentiation processes and volcanic hazard forecasting. The computational demands—particularly the need for teraflop-scale processing of 3D reactive transport models with >10^7 grid points—necessitate dedicated allocation of HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemical properties and behavior of the silicates and other substances forming, and formed by geomorphological processes of the earth and other planets. Includes instruction in chemical thermodynamics, equilibrium in silicate systems, atomic bonding, isotopic fractionation, geochemical modeling, specimen analysis, and studies of specific organic and inorganic substances.

abstract: This project seeks to address fundamental challenges in the classification and structural analysis of high-dimensional non-commutative algebraic systems, with a focus on Lie algebras, associative algebras, and their representations. A central problem in modern algebra involves resolving the complexity of isomorphism testing and decomposition for these structures, particularly as their dimensions grow. Traditional computational methods, limited by serial processing and memory constraints, fail to handle the exponential growth in algebraic relations and invariant calculations required for such tasks. To overcome these barriers, we propose a hybrid computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. This framework integrates parallelized Gröbner basis algorithms, distributed linear algebra routines for structure constant matrices, and optimized homological computations to analyze extensions and cohomology groups. Key innovations include the development of MPI-based distributed memory implementations for invariant subspace searches and CUDA-accelerated tensor decomposition methods to identify direct summands in large algebras. The computational workflows will be validated against conjectures in the classification of low-dimensional Jordan and nilpotent Lie algebras, with extensions to modular representation theory. Successful execution will yield scalable, open-source software tools for the algebraic community, enabling the study of previously intractable systems. Anticipated outcomes include progress on long-standing classification problems, new invariants for distinguishing non-isomorphic algebras, and insights into the geometric structure of moduli spaces. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance the theoretical foundations of algebra while establishing computational paradigms that bridge abstract mathematical research with large-scale numerical experimentation. The requested resources are critical to achieving the necessary scale and precision, as initial pilot studies on smaller clusters have already identified promising pathways for generalization.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on algebraic structures and linear algebra.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and installation of high-load structural ironwork systems under dynamic environmental and operational conditions. Traditional empirical methods for evaluating joint integrity, load distribution, and fatigue resistance in complex welded or riveted assemblies often lack the precision required for modern infrastructure demands, particularly in extreme climates or seismic zones. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multi-physics finite element analysis (FEA) simulations coupled with machine learning (ML) models. These simulations will integrate real-world data from material stress tests, thermal expansion coefficients, and weld penetration profiles to predict failure modes in structural connections under combined mechanical, thermal, and vibrational loads. A key innovation involves training graph neural networks (GNNs) on simulated and historical failure datasets to identify high-risk design patterns in ornamental and load-bearing components. The computational workflow will also analyze crane operation dynamics during beam placement through discrete element method (DEM) simulations, optimizing lift paths and stability thresholds. By scaling these resource-intensive models across HPC clusters, we aim to generate adaptive design guidelines that improve compliance with evolving safety codes while reducing material waste. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of validated structural reinforcement templates and a decision-support tool for ironworkers to preview installation challenges in virtual environments. This work bridges critical gaps between theoretical metallurgical principles and field practices, offering transformative potential for disaster-resilient infrastructure and energy-efficient fabrication workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to make and install structural, ornamental, and reinforcing metal structures and supports. Includes instruction in drafting, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, welding, riveting, beam placement, ornamental design, structural reinforcement, crane operation, safety, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of variability and inefficiency in histologic tissue processing through the development of a computational framework for protocol optimization. Current methods for tissue fixation, dehydration, embedding, and sectioning rely on empirical adjustments, leading to inconsistent sample quality, prolonged processing times, and suboptimal diagnostic outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating multi-scale computational modeling, machine learning (ML), and high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and predict the effects of processing variables on tissue integrity. The research will focus on two primary computational objectives: (1) simulating chemical diffusion dynamics during fixation and dehydration using fluid dynamics models, and (2) analyzing mechanical stress distributions during paraffin embedding and microtome sectioning via finite element analysis. These simulations will generate datasets correlating processing parameters (e.g., reagent concentrations, temperature, time, blade geometry) with tissue quality metrics (e.g., structural preservation, section uniformity). HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of thousands of parameter combinations, while ML algorithms will identify optimal protocols under constraints such as time, cost, and tissue type. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from murine and human tissue samples processed under controlled conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for protocol optimization, open-source simulation tools tailored for histotechnicians, and a framework for real-time adaptive adjustments in clinical workflows. By bridging computational science and histologic technique, this project aims to standardize tissue processing, reduce manual trial-and-error, and enhance diagnostic reliability in anatomic pathology. The scalability of the approach also opens avenues for addressing rare tissue types or novel processing methods, advancing precision in both research and clinical histology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of next-generation electric and hybrid vehicle systems through high-fidelity computational modeling of thermal management and energy efficiency in high-density battery arrays. A critical challenge in automotive electrification lies in balancing energy storage capacity with thermal safety, particularly under dynamic operating conditions. Current empirical methods for optimizing thermal interfaces and cooling systems are time-intensive and limited in capturing multiphysics interactions at scale. To address this, we propose a multi-phase computational workflow leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate coupled electrochemical-thermal-fluid dynamics across diverse battery geometries and operational scenarios. The project will implement finite element analysis (FEA) using ANSYS Mechanical and Fluent to model heat generation, dissipation, and stress distribution at cell and pack levels, complemented by machine learning techniques to accelerate parameter optimization. A key innovation involves integrating real-world drive cycle data from vehicle telemetry systems to create transient boundary conditions, enabling predictive modeling of thermal runaway risks in urban versus highway use cases. The computational framework will be validated against experimental data from our partner automotive testing facility, ensuring alignment with physical prototypes. Expected outcomes include optimized cooling system designs capable of reducing peak operating temperatures by 15-20% compared to current industry benchmarks, along with predictive maintenance algorithms to extend battery lifespan. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping of thermal management solutions, this work will directly support the automotive industry’s transition to sustainable electrification while reducing reliance on physical testing resources. The resulting datasets and models will be made available to the broader research community through an open-access computational repository, fostering collaboration in energy storage innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, safety, and maintenance protocols of recreational vehicle (RV) systems, with a focus on integrating multi-physics simulations to address complex engineering challenges. RVs are subject to dynamic mechanical, thermal, and environmental stresses during operation, yet traditional testing methods for critical systems—such as hydraulic braking, electrical networks, propane distribution, and structural frames—are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict failure modes under real-world conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate interactions between mechanical, electrical, and fluid systems under diverse operating scenarios. Key objectives include modeling stress distribution in welded joints during towing, predicting thermal profiles of propane appliances under extreme temperatures, and analyzing corrosion propagation in aluminum frames exposed to road salts. These simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and parallelized workflows to handle large-scale datasets spanning material properties, environmental conditions, and usage patterns. The outcomes will inform the development of predictive maintenance algorithms and design guidelines to enhance component longevity and safety. Additionally, the project will generate open-access training modules to introduce RV technicians to computational diagnostics, bridging gaps between traditional hands-on repair practices and data-driven decision-making. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing, this work aims to reduce reliance on physical prototypes, lower R&D costs for manufacturers, and advance technical education in the RV service sector. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the required resolution for multi-system simulations and ensuring scalable, reproducible results across heterogeneous RV configurations.
