Current methodologies often rely on static case analyses or qualitative assessments, limiting their ability to predict outcomes in complex, evolving scenarios such as triage during public health emergencies, equitable organ allocation, or AI-driven clinical tools. To address this, the project will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating interactions among patients, providers, and policymakers under varying ethical priorities and resource conditions. These models will integrate datasets from clinical trials, public health records, and sociological surveys to parameterize agents’ decision-making behaviors. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to analyze historical ethical guidelines, case law, and institutional policies, identifying patterns and biases in ethical reasoning. Machine learning algorithms will further assess how demographic, socioeconomic, and cultural factors influence perceptions of ethical care. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the parallel processing required for Monte Carlo simulations exploring thousands of scenario permutations—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify trade-offs in policy decisions, a repository of scenario-based ethical “stress tests” for healthcare systems, and evidence-based frameworks to guide resource allocation in crises. By bridging computational scalability with normative analysis, this work aims to enhance the rigor, equity, and adaptability of bioethics in practice, offering stakeholders actionable insights for policy design and clinical training.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of consumer preferences in global apparel markets, integrating multi-modal data streams to address inefficiencies in textile product lifecycle management. Current approaches to forecasting demand and optimizing design choices rely on fragmented datasets (e.g., historical sales, limited social media trends) and lack the computational capacity to analyze dynamic interactions between cultural trends, sustainability metrics, and real-time consumer behavior. The research problem centers on the inability of existing marketing models to holistically simulate the impact of emerging textile technologies, such as smart fabrics or biodegradable materials, on purchasing decisions across diverse demographic segments. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining deep learning, agent-based modeling, and large-scale sentiment analysis. Neural networks will be trained on unstructured data from visual social media platforms (e.g., Instagram, TikTok) to decode aesthetic preferences, while parallelized agent models simulate how sustainability claims interact with regional economic factors. A novel aspect involves embedding physics-based simulations of textile wear patterns and environmental impact projections into consumer choice algorithms, requiring GPU-accelerated rendering and lifecycle assessment tools. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of petabyte-scale datasets spanning 10 years of global sales records, 4K textile imagery, and multi-language consumer feedback. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of predicting region-specific adoption rates for innovative apparel products with 85% accuracy, reducing overproduction waste by an estimated 30% in test markets. This work establishes a methodological bridge between computational social science and textile engineering, creating a replicable framework for data-driven marketing in resource-constrained industries. The resource request prioritizes memory-intensive nodes for graph-based trend analysis and high-throughput storage for iterative model validation across 22 international market profiles.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on marketing research and management as applied to the products and services of the apparel and textile industries. Includes instruction in applicable principles of textile and apparel design and manufacturing, sales and distribution systems, domestic and international market research, profitability, consumer research, and the design and implementation of marketing campaigns.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to assess multi-hazard threats to critical infrastructure, focusing on scenarios involving coordinated cyber-physical attacks and cascading failures exacerbated by natural disasters such as wildfires. The increasing interdependence of infrastructure systems (e.g., power grids, communication networks, and transportation) and the evolving tactics of adversarial groups necessitate advanced computational tools to simulate complex, high-stakes scenarios. Current models often lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between human-driven threats, environmental conditions, and infrastructure vulnerabilities. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The framework will integrate agent-based modeling to simulate adversarial decision-making, finite element analysis for structural response under fire and blast loads, and network theory to evaluate cascading failures. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical incident data and real-time sensor inputs to refine threat prediction and adaptive response strategies. Key computational challenges include managing large-scale graph computations for infrastructure interdependencies, parallelizing fluid dynamics simulations for wildfire propagation, and optimizing reinforcement learning models for adversarial behavior. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and distributed memory systems for Monte Carlo simulations assessing probabilistic risk across thousands of scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support toolkit for emergency planners, validated against case studies from recent wildfires and security breaches. This work will advance the field of protective services by enabling proactive, data-driven resource allocation for heterogeneous threats while contributing novel methodologies for coupled human-natural-technological system modeling. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary spatial-temporal resolution and computational throughput required for operational relevance in homeland security applications.
cip_title: Homeland Security, Law Enforcement, Firefighting and Related Protective Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, law enforcement, firefighting, and related protective services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize the design and simulation of complex mechanical systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Mechanical drafting and CAD/CADD workflows increasingly require high-fidelity simulations to validate designs for manufacturability, structural integrity, and operational efficiency. However, traditional CAD tools struggle with the computational demands of multi-physics simulations (e.g., thermal-stress coupling, fluid-structure interactions) and large-scale parametric studies, particularly when applied to intricate assemblies or high-resolution geometries. This bottleneck limits the ability to explore design spaces efficiently and delays iterative improvements. To address this, the proposed research will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers tailored for mechanical drafting applications. These solvers will leverage GPU acceleration and distributed-memory architectures to handle meshes with >10^6 elements, enabling rapid evaluation of geometric variations under realistic operating conditions. Additionally, machine learning models will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to predict stress concentrations, deformation thresholds, and manufacturing tolerances, integrating these predictions directly into CAD/CADD software via API-based frameworks. The outcomes will include optimized algorithms for automated geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) compliance, reduced computational overhead for multi-objective design optimization, and open-source templates for scalable simulation workflows. By bridging the gap between high-resolution simulation and practical drafting workflows, this work aims to enhance the precision of mechanical design processes, reduce prototyping costs, and support the adoption of additive manufacturing and other advanced production techniques. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary scale and speed for these computationally intensive tasks, which cannot be feasibly executed on local workstations.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEMs) represent a complex group of genetic disorders with heterogeneous clinical presentations and biochemical profiles, posing significant challenges in diagnosis and lifelong management. Current approaches to correlate genomic variants with dynamic metabolic dysfunction and clinical outcomes remain limited by the scale and integration of multi-modal data, including genomics, metabolomics, electronic health records (EHRs), and longitudinal phenotypic data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that unify these diverse datasets, enabling precision diagnostics and personalized treatment strategies for IEMs. The research will focus on three computational aims: (1) large-scale genomic variant analysis coupled with dynamic modeling of metabolic networks to identify pathogenic mechanisms, (2) machine learning-driven integration of metabolomic profiles and EHR data to predict disease progression and therapeutic responses, and (3) the creation of a federated knowledge base for rare IEMs to support real-time clinical decision-making. Computational workflows will employ parallelized Bayesian inference frameworks, constraint-based metabolic modeling, and deep learning architectures optimized for sparse, high-dimensional clinical data. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these analyses across thousands of patient cases and simulating metabolic perturbations under diverse physiological conditions. Expected outcomes include validated biomarkers for early diagnosis, risk stratification tools for acute metabolic decompensation, and optimized treatment recommendations tailored to individual genetic and metabolic profiles. By bridging computational innovation with clinical care, this work aims to reduce diagnostic delays, improve outcomes for patients with rare IEMs, and establish a scalable platform for translating complex biochemical data into actionable insights. All models and pipelines will be shared openly to accelerate collaborative research in medical biochemical genetics.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and medical management of individuals with inborn errors of metabolism, including the provision of direct care and consultative care for individuals of all ages.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision dentistry through the development of a computational framework for modeling oral microbiome dynamics and their interactions with host immune responses. The oral microbiome plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of dental caries, periodontal disease, and systemic conditions, but its complex, time-dependent behavior under varying clinical interventions remains poorly understood. Current limitations stem from the inability to integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) with patient-specific factors (genetics, diet, treatment history) at scale. To address this, we propose a hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling approach to simulate microbial community shifts and host-pathogen interactions under clinically relevant scenarios. The computational pipeline will process terabytes of longitudinal microbiome datasets from ongoing clinical cohorts of high-caries-risk patients, employing neural ordinary differential equations to model metabolic networks and immune signaling pathways. Parallelized molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate how dental materials and antimicrobial agents influence biofilm mechanics and virulence factor expression. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to identify predictive biomarkers of dysbiosis, optimize personalized treatment schedules via reinforcement learning, and simulate the efficacy of novel bioactive dental composites. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time risk stratification in dental EHR systems and a validated in silico platform for testing preventive strategies without lengthy clinical trials. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models and large-scale parameter sweeps in sensitivity analyses—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation. This research directly aligns with national priorities to reduce oral health disparities through computationally driven innovation, offering transformative potential for both clinical decision-making and mechanistic studies in dental medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of dentistry/dental medicine, encompassing the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, and adjacent structures and their impact on the human body and health. Includes instruction in the basic biomedical sciences, occlusion, dental health and prevention, oral pathology, cariology, operative dentistry, oral radiology, principles of the various dental specialties, pain management, oral medicine, clinic and health care management, patient counseling, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The integration of alternative and complementary medical practices (ACMP) into mainstream healthcare requires robust evidence to validate efficacy, safety, and mechanistic underpinnings. However, research in this domain faces challenges due to the complexity of multi-modal datasets—including genomic, metabolomic, phytochemical, and patient-reported outcomes—that are often high-dimensional, heterogeneous, and temporally dynamic. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework to model interactions between ACMP interventions (e.g., herbal formulations, mind-body therapies) and biological systems. The primary research problem lies in resolving how multi-component interventions exert systemic effects, which necessitates advanced computational methods to integrate disparate data types and simulate biological networks. We propose a hybrid approach combining machine learning (ML) and network pharmacology to identify critical pathways and biomarkers associated with ACMP outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale data integration, leveraging ensemble ML models to predict intervention-response relationships across diverse patient subgroups. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model phytochemical-protein interactions to elucidate mechanisms of action for plant-derived therapies. Network analysis will map cross-talk between immune, metabolic, and neurological systems under ACMP modulation. The computational pipeline will be validated using existing datasets from clinical trials on mindfulness-based stress reduction and traditional herbal protocols, with iterative refinement based on newly generated multi-omics data. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for personalizing ACMP interventions, (2) mechanistic hypotheses for experimental validation, and (3) open-source tools for reproducibility in ACMP research. By addressing computational bottlenecks in data synthesis and hypothesis generation, this work aims to strengthen the evidence base for integrative healthcare strategies, ultimately supporting the development of precision frameworks for ACMP implementation. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project’s scale, particularly in managing parallelized simulations, optimizing hyperparameters for heterogeneous data integration, and enabling real-time analytics for collaborative research workflows.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medical Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medical support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze the integration of decentralized blockchain protocols with ecological economics in accounting systems—a novel interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of accounting, sustainability, and distributed ledger technologies. Traditional accounting frameworks struggle to dynamically quantify and verify ecological externalities (e.g., carbon footprints, biodiversity impacts) in real time, particularly for complex supply chains. This project addresses this gap by designing a high-fidelity simulation environment to test hybrid blockchain architectures that automate the tracking of ecological-economic data flows while ensuring auditability, scalability, and compliance with evolving sustainability reporting standards. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate stakeholder interactions across supply networks, cryptographic validation mechanisms for multi-party data reconciliation, and machine learning to predict regulatory compliance risks under varying ecological scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the parallel processing demands of large-scale blockchain network simulations, optimize consensus algorithms for energy efficiency, and train predictive models on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., IoT sensor data, financial ledgers, ecological inventories). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating sustainable accounting systems, benchmarks for blockchain-driven ecological auditing, and scalability analyses to inform policy and corporate governance. By bridging distributed systems engineering with sustainability accounting, this work aims to advance computational methods for transparent, real-time ecological accountability in business operations—a pressing need as global regulations shift toward mandatory environmental disclosure frameworks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in accounting, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Veterinary radiology faces challenges in analyzing complex, heterogeneous imaging data across diverse animal species, where variations in anatomy, pathology, and imaging protocols complicate diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic planning. This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to automate the analysis of veterinary radiologic images, including X-ray, CT, and MRI datasets, with the goal of improving detection, classification, and treatment monitoring of diseases such as osteosarcoma, degenerative joint disorders, and thoracic neoplasms in companion and livestock animals. The primary research problem lies in overcoming the limitations of manual or semi-automated image analysis, which is time-intensive, operator-dependent, and poorly scalable for multi-modal or longitudinal studies. To address this, we propose a machine learning framework leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer architectures optimized for veterinary-specific anatomies and pathologies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train models on multi-institutional datasets comprising over 50,000 annotated veterinary images spanning 15 species, process high-resolution 3D volumetric scans, and simulate radiation dose distributions for therapeutic applications. Key computational tasks include species-adaptive image segmentation, lesion quantification in dynamic contrast-enhanced studies, and radiomic feature extraction for predictive modeling of treatment responses. The project will also develop open-source tools for veterinary image registration and real-time processing of fluoroscopic data during interventional procedures. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for automated detection of subtle pathologic changes in cross-species imaging, quantitative biomarkers for disease progression, and optimized workflows for radiation therapy planning in veterinary oncology. Successful implementation will provide the first scalable computational platform tailored to veterinary radiology research, enabling precision medicine approaches in animal healthcare while generating translatable insights for human comparative oncology. The requested HPC infrastructure will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data parallelism, and validation against clinical outcomes from collaborating veterinary hospitals.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of radiologic imaging and therapies to diagnose and treat animal diseases and health problems. May included related research in the use and handling of equipment for radionuclides detection and application.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize dynamic, data-driven decision-making in tourism promotion operations—an interdisciplinary domain intersecting marketing analytics, behavioral economics, and computational social science. Current tourism marketing strategies often rely on static segmentation models and lagging indicators, limiting responsiveness to real-time shifts in traveler behavior, competitive pressures, and exogenous shocks (e.g., climate events or geopolitical disruptions). The project addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate tourism demand patterns and promotional campaign impacts at unprecedented spatial-temporal resolutions. Using agent-based modeling and graph neural networks, the system will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including social media sentiment, transportation network dynamics, localized event calendars, and macroeconomic variables—to predict destination attractiveness under multiple scenarios. HPC resources are critical for training models on multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10+ years of global tourism metrics and for running parallelized simulations of promotional interventions across diverse demographic cohorts. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for tourism boards and destination marketing organizations to (1) quantify the cascading effects of promotional budget allocations on regional economic ecosystems and (2) identify high-leverage intervention points in traveler decision journeys. Validation will focus on case studies of "underbooked" cultural heritage sites where traditional marketing fails to translate awareness into visits. By enabling real-time adaptation of promotional operations at scale, this work advances computational methods for experience-centric marketing while addressing pressing challenges in sustainable tourism resource distribution. The resulting models could reduce campaign testing costs by 30-40% compared to A/B field trials while improving predictive accuracy of visitor yield estimates.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of tourism in public and private sector settings. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling and decision-support frameworks for homeland security threat scenarios, with a focus on optimizing emergency response strategies and infrastructure resilience. The research addresses the challenge of simulating large-scale, dynamic threats—such as cyber-physical attacks, cascading infrastructure failures, and natural disasters—in a manner that integrates real-time data streams, multi-agent systems, and stochastic risk assessments. Current models often lack the resolution and scalability to capture interdependencies between critical infrastructure systems (e.g., power grids, transportation networks) and human behavior during crises, limiting their utility for proactive planning. To bridge this gap, the proposed computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate crowd dynamics and responder actions, graph-theoretic network analysis to assess infrastructure vulnerabilities, and machine learning (ML) techniques to process heterogeneous datasets, including satellite imagery, social media feeds, and sensor networks. These components will be integrated into a unified simulation environment, requiring parallelized computation to manage the high dimensionality of geospatial-temporal data and the concurrent interactions of millions of agents. HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across threat scenarios, sensitivity analyses to identify critical failure thresholds, and the training of ML models on synthetic and historical incident datasets. Expected outcomes include scalable tools for evaluating evacuation protocols, resource allocation strategies, and communication systems under stress, validated against historical case studies such as hurricane responses and cyberattack mitigation efforts. The results will provide actionable insights for policymakers and operational agencies, advancing the development of adaptive, data-driven homeland security frameworks. By open-sourcing modular components of the computational pipeline, this work will also foster collaborative innovation in public-sector resilience planning.
cip_definition: A program focusing on security policy, planning and operations dedicated to the protection of U.S. territory, assets, infrastructure, institutions and citizens from external threats. Includes instruction in national security policy, government relations, intelligence, law enforcement, security technology, communications and information technology, homeland security planning and operations, disaster planning and applications to specific threat scenarios.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the preservation of culturally significant historic structures through computational modeling of environmental and structural stressors. The research addresses a critical gap in current conservation practices, which often rely on static, localized assessments that fail to account for dynamic interactions between aging materials, climate variability, and human interventions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate multiscale degradation processes across entire building systems over extended temporal horizons. Using 3D laser scan datasets of three at-risk 19th-century timber-framed buildings in coastal environments, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) to model moisture infiltration patterns under projected climate scenarios while coupling these outputs with machine learning algorithms trained on historical decay records. The computational workflow will integrate material science data (e.g., wood density variations, corrosion rates of period fasteners) with hyperlocal climate projections to predict failure thresholds in structural joints and cladding systems. By parallelizing these simulations across multiple nodes, we aim to achieve sufficient resolution to capture micro-crack propagation in wooden members while maintaining building-scale analysis—a computational challenge exceeding conventional workstation capacities. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for prioritizing preservation interventions based on probabilistic failure timelines and climate resilience metrics. This work will establish new interdisciplinary methodologies bridging architectural history, environmental engineering, and computational science, with immediate applications for heritage site managers adapting to intensifying preservation challenges under climate change. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across 50+ climate-emission scenarios while maintaining the submillimeter spatial resolution required for actionable conservation insights.
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on architectural design and building techniques for historic and restored structures, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Radiation exposure induces complex molecular perturbations in biological systems, particularly through direct and indirect ionization events that damage critical biomolecules such as DNA and associated repair proteins. While the broad biological effects of radiation are well-documented, the atomistic mechanisms underlying radiation-induced DNA-protein crosslinking (DPC) and the dynamic interplay between ionization cascades and cellular repair pathways remain poorly resolved. This project seeks to address this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the biophysical interactions of ionizing radiation with biomolecular systems at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations coupled with quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) hybrid methods, we will investigate radiation-induced radical propagation, DNA strand break dynamics, and the structural consequences of DPC formation in chromatin environments. These simulations will integrate experimental data from time-resolved spectroscopy and crystallography to validate force field parameters and refine reaction pathways. A secondary aim involves developing machine learning-driven predictive models to map ionization patterns to repair outcomes, leveraging multi-scale simulation datasets to identify key determinants of radiation sensitivity. The computational workflows will require large-scale parallelization for ensemble sampling of stochastic ionization events and long-timescale MD trajectories (microsecond range) across heterogeneous systems. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic insights into radiation-induced damage propagation and repair protein recruitment, (2) predictive frameworks linking radiation quality (e.g., LET, particle type) to DPC persistence, and (3) open-source simulation tools optimized for radiobiological applications. This work will directly inform targeted radiotherapy strategies and radiation protection standards by elucidating molecular vulnerabilities in DNA damage response pathways. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in system size and sampling efficiency, enabling biologically relevant simulations of chromatin-scale radiation damage.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the effects of radiation on organisms and biological systems. Includes instruction in particle physics, ionization, and biophysics of radiation perturbations, cellular and organismic repair systems, genetic and pathological effects of radiation, and the measurement of radiation dosages.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing horticultural production systems for specialty crops through advanced computational modeling, with a focus on improving yield predictability, resource efficiency, and economic viability for small-to-medium horticultural enterprises. Current decision-making tools in horticultural business services often lack the resolution to account for dynamic interactions between plant physiology, environmental variables, and market constraints. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating hyperspectral imaging data, real-time climate sensor inputs, and machine learning models. The computational workflow will simulate crop growth under varying resource allocation scenarios (e.g., irrigation schedules, nutrient regimens, lighting configurations) while incorporating stochastic market demand forecasts. Parallelized agent-based modeling will be employed to evaluate how localized microclimate variations and supply chain disruptions propagate through multi-site production networks. By leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations, we aim to process terabyte-scale datasets from distributed greenhouse monitoring systems, enabling near-real-time optimization of horticultural operations. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of recommending resource allocation strategies that balance profitability with sustainability metrics such as water-use efficiency and carbon footprint. This work will advance precision horticulture by providing business operators with scalable computational tools to navigate complex trade-offs between production targets, operational costs, and environmental impacts. The proposed models will be validated against empirical data from partner nurseries, with results disseminated through an open-access API tailored for agricultural extension services. By demonstrating the value of HPC in horticultural business analytics, this project aims to establish a template for data-driven resource management in understudied specialty crop sectors.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Applied Horticulture/ Horticultural Business Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in horticultural service operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing modular construction supply chains, which are critical for meeting rising demands for affordable housing and sustainable infrastructure. Current methodologies struggle to dynamically adapt to volatile material costs, labor shortages, and logistical disruptions, leading to project delays and cost overruns. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision support system to model and simulate multi-echelon modular supply chains under uncertainty. The research will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with discrete-event simulation (DES) to capture complex interactions among suppliers, manufacturers, transporters, and construction sites across geographies. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks (GNNs) and reinforcement learning (RL), will be deployed to predict bottlenecks and optimize real-time resource allocation. The computational framework will require parallel processing of large-scale spatiotemporal datasets—including IoT sensor feeds, supplier transaction records, and weather patterns—to generate probabilistic scenarios for risk mitigation. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing, the team aims to reduce simulation runtime for 12-month project horizons from weeks to hours, enabling rapid iteration of "what-if" analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of recommending resilient procurement strategies, inventory buffers, and transportation routing adjustments. This work bridges gaps in construction informatics and operations research, offering a scalable solution to enhance the economic and environmental efficiency of modular building techniques. The computational infrastructure will also support future extensions into circular economy models for material reuse, advancing the industry’s transition toward net-zero construction practices.
cip_definition: Any program in construction management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time, context-aware multimedia resource allocation in adaptive web environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address latency and scalability challenges in dynamic content delivery. Current web-based multimedia systems struggle to balance user experience quality—such as personalized visual, auditory, and interactive elements—with the computational demands of real-time adaptation across heterogeneous devices and network conditions. Traditional optimization methods, which rely on static heuristics or simplified user models, fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between user behavior, device capabilities, and fluctuating bandwidth. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for predicting user interaction patterns with distributed reinforcement learning (RL) agents to optimize resource allocation dynamically. The GNN component will model complex user navigation pathways and multimedia engagement trends using large-scale clickstream and sensor datasets, while RL agents, trained in parallel on HPC clusters, will iteratively refine content delivery policies across simulated network environments. Computational workflows will integrate GPU-accelerated tensor operations for GNN training and MPI-based distributed simulations to emulate global user traffic patterns. Key outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive multimedia scheduling and empirical benchmarks quantifying trade-offs between computational overhead, latency, and quality-of-experience metrics. This work bridges gaps in web design research by introducing scalable, AI-driven methods for resource-intensive multimedia applications, with implications for next-generation educational platforms, immersive e-commerce, and low-infrastructure regions requiring bandwidth-sensitive content adaptation. Successful implementation will require access to HPC resources capable of supporting concurrent training of multiple RL agents, large-scale graph processing, and real-time simulation of >10,000 concurrent user sessions with variable device and network profiles.
cip_title: Web Page, Digital/ Multimedia and Information Resources Design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply HTML, CSS, XML, JavaScript, graphics applications, and other authoring tools to the design, editing, and publishing (launching) of documents, images, graphics, sound, and multimedia products on the World Wide Web. Includes instruction in Internet theory, web page standards and policies, elements of web page design, user interfaces, vector tools, special effects, interactive and multimedia components, search engines, navigation, morphing, e-commerce tools, and emerging web technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between intergenerational communication patterns and cognitive development in early childhood using agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis. While family systems are recognized as critical to developmental outcomes, the nonlinear, bidirectional influences between caregivers’ communicative behaviors and children’s emerging cognitive skills remain poorly quantified. Traditional longitudinal methods struggle to disentangle these recursive interactions, particularly across varying cultural and socioeconomic contexts. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating empirically grounded behavioral data with high-fidelity simulations of family communication networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the creation of large-scale ABMs parameterized by real-world observational datasets (e.g., parent-child dialogue recordings, developmental assessments) to simulate how micro-level communicative exchanges aggregate into macro-level cognitive trajectories. Machine learning techniques will identify critical thresholds in communication quality that predict developmental milestones, while sensitivity analyses will quantify how socioeconomic variables moderate these relationships. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to run thousands of parallel simulations across diverse demographic profiles, enabling robust statistical inference about universal versus context-specific mechanisms. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel open-source toolkit for simulating developmental processes in family systems, (2) evidence-based criteria for identifying at-risk communication patterns before observable delays emerge, and (3) computational proofs-of-concept for personalized family-centered interventions. By bridging developmental psychology, computational social science, and data-intensive modeling, this work aims to advance precision approaches in human development research while providing a scalable methodology for studying complex familial interactions.
cip_title: Human Development and Family Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on basic human developmental and behavioral characteristics of the individual within the context of the family. Includes instruction in the conditions that influence human growth and development; strategies that promote growth and development across the life span; and the study of family systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the historical evolution and dialectal variation of under-resourced Slavic languages using advanced computational methods, with a focus on identifying phonological and morphosyntactic shifts in lesser-studied Eastern and South Slavic vernaculars. The primary challenge lies in processing and analyzing large, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized historical texts, modern spoken corpora, and fragmentary archival records—which require significant computational power to align, annotate, and model effectively. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to implement neural sequence-to-sequence models for automated grapheme-phoneme conversion across orthographic systems, coupled with transformer-based architectures to detect syntactic and semantic changes in diachronic corpora. A key innovation involves adapting existing NLP pipelines to accommodate non-standardized orthographies and code-switching patterns prevalent in Balkan Slavic-Albanian contact zones. The computational workflow will integrate phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct proto-features and quantify linguistic divergence, while geospatial analysis will map dialect continua against historical migration patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable digital repository of annotated Slavic linguistic data, (2) evidence-based models of language contact dynamics in multiethnic regions of Eastern Europe, and (3) methodological frameworks for analyzing low-resource languages with irregular written traditions. This work will advance computational Slavic linguistics by addressing critical gaps in comparative dialectology while developing open-source tools adaptable to other non-dominant language families. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing of terabyte-scale textual data, parallelized training of deep learning models across multiple GPU nodes, and high-throughput simulations of language change scenarios—tasks infeasible on standard academic computing infrastructure. By bridging computational linguistics with area-specific philological expertise, the project aims to generate new insights into the cultural-historical factors shaping linguistic diversity in Eastern Europe while contributing methodological innovations to the digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic, Baltic, and Albanian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Slavic languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Public works agencies face mounting challenges in optimizing resource allocation amid aging infrastructure, climate-related disruptions, and constrained budgets. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model complex, dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, interdependent infrastructure systems, and equity considerations in service delivery. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to simulate public works operations under diverse scenarios, enabling data-driven prioritization of maintenance, emergency response, and long-term investments. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate large-scale spatial datasets—including infrastructure condition reports, climate projections, and socioeconomic indicators—with agent-based models that simulate stakeholder interactions and system-wide outcomes. Computational methods will include network analysis to map infrastructure interdependencies, Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risk under uncertainty, and machine learning algorithms to predict service gaps in vulnerable communities. By parallelizing these processes, HPC will enable rapid iteration of "what-if" scenarios, such as budget reallocations or extreme weather events, while preserving granularity in geographic and demographic variables. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that visualizes trade-offs between cost, resilience, and equity in public works management. This tool will assist agencies in aligning operational strategies with ethical priorities, such as reducing disparities in infrastructure access and minimizing disruptions for marginalized populations. The project will also generate methodological insights into scaling computational models for non-technical stakeholders, fostering transparency in resource allocation processes. By bridging computational scalability with public administration priorities, this work aims to advance evidence-based governance in a sector critical to community well-being.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for optimized hardware-software integration in embedded systems and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, where real-time processing constraints and energy efficiency are critical challenges. Existing simulation tools often lack the scalability to model complex interactions between heterogeneous computing components, leading to suboptimal system designs and prolonged development cycles. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a parallelized simulation framework capable of evaluating multi-core embedded architectures, peripheral device interoperability, and energy consumption patterns under varying workloads. The computational approach will combine discrete-event simulation with machine learning-driven optimization to iteratively refine hardware configurations and task-scheduling algorithms. Large-scale parameter sweeps will be conducted across HPC nodes to assess trade-offs between processing latency, power efficiency, and thermal performance in simulated edge computing environments. Validation will involve cross-referencing simulation results with physical prototype measurements from FPGA-based testbeds. Expected outcomes include a validated library of energy-aware design templates for embedded systems, an open-source toolchain for rapid co-design of hardware and real-time software, and quantitative guidelines for balancing computational throughput with thermal constraints in compact devices. This work will directly support curriculum development in embedded systems design and IoT applications within the Computer Engineering Technology program, while providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-accelerated engineering workflows. The resource-intensive nature of concurrently simulating hundreds of hardware configurations and their software interactions necessitates access to cluster computing infrastructure with parallel processing capabilities, which this allocation request aims to secure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: The human gut microbiota plays a critical role in modulating host metabolism, yet the mechanisms linking dietary patterns to microbial dynamics and metabolic health remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model diet-microbiota-host interactions in the context of obesity and type 2 diabetes. Current limitations stem from the complexity of integrating multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and host transcriptomic) with dynamic models of nutrient flux, microbial ecology, and metabolic regulation. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions, and machine learning to simulate how specific dietary components—such as fiber diversity or saturated fat intake—reshape microbial community structure and function, subsequently influencing host inflammation and insulin sensitivity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and validate these models using longitudinal human cohort data, enabling the parallel processing of terabyte-scale omics datasets and stochastic simulations of microbial ecosystems under varying dietary conditions. The computational pipeline will also leverage probabilistic graphical models to identify key microbial taxa and metabolic pathways that mediate dietary effects on glycemic control. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of personalizing dietary recommendations based on an individual’s microbial profile and mechanistic insights into how diet-induced microbiota shifts contribute to metabolic dysfunction. This work bridges nutritional biochemistry, systems biology, and computational ecology, offering a novel platform to explore diet as a modifiable factor in metabolic disease. By elucidating microbiota-dependent mechanisms of nutrient utilization, the project will advance translational applications in precision nutrition while providing scalable computational tools for future studies at the intersection of diet, microbiology, and chronic disease.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the utilization of food for human growth and metabolism, in both normal and dysfunctional states, from the interdisciplinary perspective of the agricultural, human, biological, and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in food science, biochemistry, physiology, dietetics, food and nutrition studies, biotechnology, biophysics, and the clinical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time, hyper-personalized promotional campaigns in niche consumer markets, specifically targeting special products such as artisanal foods, bespoke floristry, and curated home-office bundles. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of traditional marketing models in addressing the rapid demand fluctuations, fragmented consumer preferences, and supply-chain volatilities inherent to these markets. Current approaches often rely on static demographic segmentation or historical sales data, failing to account for real-time behavioral signals, cross-product affinity patterns, and micro-influencer impact dynamics unique to specialty goods. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled system integrating live social sentiment analysis, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and probabilistic supply-demand matching. The computational architecture will process heterogeneous data streams—including social media interactions, IoT-enabled product usage telemetry, and supplier capacity updates—through GPU-accelerated transformer models for preference inference. A distributed agent-based simulation environment will then test millions of promotional scenario permutations, optimizing for simultaneous objectives: maximized short-term conversions, sustained brand equity metrics, and ethical sourcing constraints. The project requires HPC resources to manage 1) large-scale graph neural networks analyzing emergent product association networks, and 2) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations evaluating campaign resilience under supply-chain disruptions. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of generating adaptive promotion portfolios at 15-minute intervals, dynamically balancing inventory-aware incentives with long-term customer experience goals. This work advances computational marketing science by formalizing interaction effects between perishable product psychographics and operational logistics—a critical but understudied intersection in special products marketing. Successful implementation could reduce campaign design costs by 30-40% for small-batch producers while decreasing perishable goods waste through improved demand synchronization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of special products, including floristry, food, and home and office products. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of linguistic variation and evolution in Italian dialects and historical texts. While Italian philology has traditionally relied on manual textual analysis, the increasing digitization of historical manuscripts, dialectal corpora, and spoken language archives presents an opportunity—and challenge—to systematically investigate patterns of phonetic, syntactic, and lexical change across time, geography, and social contexts. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the scope of such studies, particularly when analyzing high-resolution audio data, multi-regional text corpora, or complex diachronic models. This project proposes the development of machine learning pipelines to automate the identification of dialectal features in textual and acoustic data, paired with phylogenetic modeling to reconstruct historical language relationships. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) tools adapted for regional Italian variants, neural networks trained on diachronic corpora, and geospatial visualization of linguistic shifts. By parallelizing these processes across HPC nodes, the project aims to process terabytes of digitized texts (e.g., medieval manuscripts, modern regional literature) and speech samples from understudied dialects, many at risk of extinction. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database mapping dialectal evolution in post-unification Italy, (2) quantitative models correlating linguistic changes with sociohistorical factors, and (3) open-source tools for low-resource Italian language variant analysis. These results will directly inform debates in Italian historical linguistics regarding the impact of standardization policies on regional languages while providing methodologies applicable to minority language preservation efforts globally. The scale of data and complexity of spatiotemporal modeling necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust, fine-grained insights into the dynamics of Italian linguistic diversity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Italian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing hybrid solar energy systems integrated with advanced thermal storage solutions, a key frontier in improving the reliability and scalability of solar power. Despite the growing adoption of solar technologies, inefficiencies persist in balancing intermittent energy generation with dynamic demand, particularly under variable environmental conditions. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model, simulate, and optimize coupled photovoltaic-thermal (PV-T) systems with phase-change material (PCM) storage. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute multi-scale, multi-physics simulations that concurrently resolve photon absorption, heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and energy storage processes. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to identify optimal system configurations, operational parameters, and control strategies under diverse climatic and load profiles. The computational models will be validated against experimental data from lab-scale prototypes, ensuring physical accuracy. By employing parallelized finite element analysis and Monte Carlo methods on HPC clusters, the team will overcome the prohibitive computational cost of simulating years of operational data across thousands of design permutations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for designing regionally tailored PV-T systems with 20-30% improved energy yield and 40% reduction in grid intermittency compared to conventional designs. These advancements will directly support the development of cost-effective, grid-resilient solar solutions, accelerating the transition to sustainable energy infrastructure. The resulting open-source simulation platform will serve as a critical resource for engineers and policymakers working to meet decarbonization targets, while the methodology will establish a template for computational innovation in renewable energy system design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing solar-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in solar energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing clinical decision-making models for family practice nurses (FPNs) managing multi-morbidity in diverse family systems. FPNs routinely encounter complex, interconnected health challenges across age groups and family dynamics, requiring integration of heterogeneous data—including electronic health records, socio-environmental factors, and longitudinal health trends—to deliver holistic care. However, existing predictive tools lack the computational scalability to model multi-scale interactions between biological, behavioral, and family-unit variables. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework using graph neural networks (GNNs) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate family health trajectories under varying intervention scenarios. The GNN component will map relational dependencies among family members’ health states, comorbidities, and care behaviors, while ABM will simulate how nurse-led interventions propagate through family networks. HPC resources are critical for training models on synthetic datasets reflecting demographic diversity (age, ethnicity, rural/urban settings) and for sensitivity analyses testing clinical hypotheses. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational tool identifying high-risk family clusters and intervention priorities, (2) probabilistic forecasts of intervention efficacy across family structures, and (3) open-source algorithms to help FPNs tailor care plans using dynamically updated data. By enabling real-time analysis of complex family health ecosystems, this work aims to reduce preventable hospitalizations in pediatric and geriatric populations while advancing nursing informatics methodologies. The computational infrastructure will support future expansions, including integration with federated electronic health record systems and genomics data, ensuring scalability for nationwide FPN training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in Arabic linguistic analysis and dialectology. The research focuses on the computational modeling of linguistic variation across Classical Arabic, Modern Standard Arabic, and regional dialects, which exhibit significant phonological, morphological, and syntactic diversity. Traditional methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these variations, particularly when analyzing historical texts, sociolinguistic corpora, and real-world dialectal speech data. The primary research problem lies in developing scalable, data-driven models to map linguistic evolution, identify cross-dialectal patterns, and quantify the impact of sociocultural factors on language change. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, machine learning algorithms, and large-scale corpus analysis. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on digitized classical texts and dialectal datasets, implementing parallelized phonetic alignment algorithms for speech corpora, and applying graph-based methods to trace lexical diffusion across regions and time periods. The project will utilize distributed computing frameworks to manage multi-terabyte datasets spanning 7th-century manuscripts to contemporary social media content. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for diachronic and synchronic Arabic language analysis, (2) open-access tools for automated dialect classification and morphological segmentation, and (3) novel quantitative insights into language standardization processes. These results will advance Arabic philological studies, support NLP applications for under-resourced dialects, and inform language policy in education and technology. The requested HPC resources are essential for training large language models, processing high-resolution audio recordings of endangered dialects, and running iterative simulations of linguistic change—tasks that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. By bridging computational methods with Arabic linguistic scholarship, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying Semitic languages in the digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Arabic language. Includes instruction in philology; Classical Arabic; Modern Standard Arabic; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time decision-making frameworks for multi-domain aerospace operations in contested environments, where dynamic constraints such as adversarial threats, rapidly evolving weather patterns, and equipment degradation intersect. Traditional mission-planning tools struggle to reconcile these variables at scale, particularly when balancing operational objectives against probabilistic risks to personnel and hardware. The proposed work leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an adaptive simulation environment capable of modeling complex, nonlinear interactions between human operators, autonomous systems, and environmental factors. Computational methods will integrate agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, and reinforcement learning architectures to identify robust decision pathways under emergent conditions. Key innovations include the synthesis of real-time telemetry data with predictive maintenance algorithms to simulate fleet readiness impacts and the development of a physics-informed neural network to forecast localized atmospheric disturbances at hyper-resolution scales (sub-100m granularity). Expected outcomes include a validated framework for evaluating trade-offs between mission latency, resource expenditure, and survivability metrics across simulated scenarios. This work directly supports next-generation command-and-control systems by providing quantifiable insights into resilience thresholds for mixed human-AI operational teams. The computational demands—particularly parallelized ensemble simulations spanning millions of agent interactions and high-dimensional parameter spaces—necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve operational fidelity within militarily relevant timescales. Results will inform doctrinal updates for adaptive contingency planning and contribute open-source tools for probabilistic risk assessment in aerospace operations, bridging gaps between theoretical optimization research and applied military logistics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of systems and equipment used in aerospace operations. Includes instruction in astronomy and astronautics, solid state theory, air and space operations, electronics, computer science, aviation and space flight safety, life support systems, flight operations management systems, programming, propulsion systems, weaponry, maintenance management and applications to specific systems and operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of covert terrorist network dynamics and optimize counterterrorism operational planning. The research addresses a critical gap in current analytical frameworks, which often struggle to integrate heterogeneous data streams—such as fragmented financial transaction records, encrypted communication patterns, and dark web activity—into unified models capable of forecasting emergent threats. By developing computational tools that synthesize these multimodal datasets, the project aims to identify latent network structures, simulate resource allocation scenarios for terrorist cells, and evaluate the cascading impacts of counterterrorism interventions. The methodology employs a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate adaptive terrorist group behaviors, graph neural networks (GNNs) to analyze relational data across temporal and spatial dimensions, and natural language processing (NLP) to extract actionable intelligence from unstructured multilingual sources (e.g., propaganda materials, intercepted communications). Computational challenges include managing high-dimensional data with varying granularity, scaling simulations to account for global interdependencies among regional threats, and maintaining probabilistic uncertainty quantification across models. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time threat prioritization, validated against historical case studies of terrorist escalation patterns, and decision-support tools for evaluating the second-order effects of operational strategies. The resource-intensive nature of these tasks—particularly the parallel processing required for Monte Carlo simulations of intervention scenarios and the training of deep learning models on sensitive, sparse datasets—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. By bridging computational social science with operational analytics, this research will provide novel insights into the resilience mechanisms of asymmetric threat networks while addressing ethical considerations in predictive security applications.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the study of terrorism as a global and national threat and the methods for analyzing and countering it. Includes instruction in psychology, cultural studies, terrorist history and organization, terrorist capabilities, terrorist finance and international money-laundering, threat assessment, intelligence operations, incident command systems, border security, emergency response, joint operations, surveillance and communications systems, cyberterrorism, weapons of mass destruction, counterterrorist operations, and applications to specific terrorist organizations and threats.

abstract: Ophthalmic diagnostics increasingly rely on complex multimodal imaging and dynamic biomechanical modeling, yet current clinical tools lack the resolution and computational power to integrate these datasets for early detection of corneal ectatic disorders. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational platform to analyze corneal biomechanical behavior using multi-scale finite element modeling (FEM) coupled with machine learning-driven pattern recognition. The research problem centers on improving the diagnostic sensitivity for early-stage keratoconus, a progressive thinning disorder of the cornea, by integrating real-world clinical data from Scheimpflug tomography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), and dynamic bidirectional applanation tonometry. Current clinical parameters exhibit limited predictive value in subclinical cases, leading to delayed interventions. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process 4D corneal deformation datasets (>10 TB/week from participating clinics), train convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to identify microstructural strain patterns, and simulate corneal stress distributions under physiological loading conditions. A custom FEM pipeline will incorporate anisotropic hyperelastic material properties derived from ex vivo corneal layer spectroscopy, with GPU-accelerated solvers optimizing runtime for patient-specific models. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel diagnostic index combining biomechanical and tomographic features, validated against longitudinal clinical outcomes, and (2) open-source visualization tools for 3D strain mapping compatible with standard ophthalmic imaging formats. This resource-intensive computational framework addresses a critical gap in ocular diagnostics by bridging clinical imaging data with biomechanical theory, ultimately enhancing ophthalmic technicians' ability to stratify at-risk patients through quantitative, personalized analyses. The project’s computational demands necessitate dedicated HPC allocation for large-scale parallel processing of heterogeneous medical imaging data and iterative model training, exceeding the capabilities of local clinical workstations. Successful implementation could establish new standards for pre-emptive management of corneal ectasias while demonstrating the value of computational biomechanics in frontline ophthalmic care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist ophthalmologists and optometrists in examining and treating patients with vision problems, vision disorders, and eye diseases. Includes instruction in taking patient histories, administering directed treatments and topical medications, diagnostic test procedures and equipment operation, anatomical and functional ocular measurements, patient care and instruction, ophthalmic and surgical equipment maintenance, safety and sterilization procedures, and office administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Norwegian dialectal variation and its historical evolution, a critical gap in current Scandinavian linguistics research. Norwegian dialects exhibit exceptional diversity due to geographical, social, and historical factors, yet large-scale, data-driven studies remain limited by the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous linguistic data. The proposed research will develop and apply machine learning models to analyze multi-modal datasets, including digitized historical texts (e.g., Old Norse manuscripts, 19th-century records), contemporary spoken corpora, and dialect atlas annotations. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) techniques for morphological tagging, syntactic parsing, and phonetic feature extraction, with geospatial modeling to map dialect boundaries and their shifts over time. A key innovation involves training transformer-based models on non-standardized orthographies and oral transcripts to identify patterns in grammaticalization and lexical borrowing across regions. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale of data (≥50 TB of audio and text), parallelizing feature extraction across thousands of dialect samples, and optimizing neural architectures for low-resource language scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible Norwegian Dialect Evolution Repository, computational tools for automatic dialect classification, and quantitative insights into the impact of language policy (e.g., Nynorsk vs. Bokmål) on regional speech practices. This work will directly support endangered dialect preservation efforts and inform technology applications such as Norwegian-language speech recognition systems adaptable to diverse dialects. By bridging traditional philological methods with computational linguistics, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for data-intensive research in minority language studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Norwegian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize urban soundscape design for cognitive performance enhancement, an emerging interdisciplinary challenge at the intersection of acoustics, neuroscience, and human-centered engineering. Urban noise pollution is a well-documented public health concern, but existing engineering approaches lack predictive models to relate dynamic acoustic environments to real-time cognitive outcomes such as attention, stress, and creativity. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating high-resolution aeroacoustic simulations with neurophysiological response models. The computational approach combines three pillars: (1) large-eddy simulations of sound propagation in complex urban geometries using GPU-accelerated computational fluid dynamics (CFD), (2) machine learning surrogate models trained on psychoacoustic datasets to predict human perceptual responses, and (3) multi-objective optimization algorithms to balance acoustic performance metrics against cognitive outcome targets. The proposed work requires high-performance computing resources to handle the multiscale nature of the problem—from micrometer-scale vortex interactions in airflow around architectural features to city-block-scale sound field predictions, coupled with real-time neural network inference. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for urban soundscape design, validated against both controlled laboratory experiments and field measurements in partner cities. This work will establish quantitative relationships between engineered acoustic environments and measurable cognitive impacts, providing urban planners and architects with evidence-based design principles. The computational framework will also advance methodologies for human factors integration in infrastructure modeling, creating a template for addressing similar challenges in sensory environment engineering. By focusing on the underexplored interface of physical acoustics and cognitive neuroscience, this project occupies a specialized niche in engineering science with direct applications to public health and urban sustainability.
cip_definition: A program with a general focus on the general application of various combinations of mathematical and scientific principles to the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems, including applied research in human behavior, statistics, biology, chemistry, the earth and planetary sciences, atmospherics and meteorology, and computer applications.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the detection and interpretation of complex financial anomalies in large-scale transactional datasets, with applications to real-time auditing processes. Traditional auditing methods often struggle to identify subtle, systemic irregularities in high-volume, heterogeneous data environments, particularly in cross-border transactions or decentralized financial ecosystems. The proposed work leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized machine learning models capable of processing terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining the chain of evidence required for regulatory compliance. Key computational challenges include optimizing graph-based anomaly detection algorithms to map multi-hop transaction networks, integrating temporal-spatial analysis of financial flows, and simulating adversarial evasion tactics to stress-test audit models. The project will employ hybrid architectures combining GPU-accelerated deep learning for pattern recognition and CPU-driven agent-based simulations to model evolving fraud strategies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive audit sampling, a benchmark dataset of synthetically generated transaction networks with embedded anomalies, and performance metrics comparing computational efficiency against conventional auditing software. By enabling near-real-time analysis of dynamic financial systems, this research aims to reduce false-positive rates in anomaly detection by at least 40% while maintaining audit trail integrity, ultimately supporting more proactive risk mitigation in global supply chains and cryptocurrency transaction monitoring.
