The scalability of the proposed methods will be validated through partnerships with fintech auditing firms, focusing on use cases involving blockchain-based assets and multi-jurisdictional tax compliance datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including certified accountants, to perform independent internal and external appraisals to evaluate organizational financial and operational activities, ensure compliance with laws and policies, safeguard assets, and promote effective planning and resource allocation. Includes instruction in advanced accounting, audit tools and techniques, sampling, risk and control, audit planning, audit function management, law and regulations, environmental auditing, information technology applications, professional standards and ethics, and specific industry and service sector problems.

abstract: Aquaculture systems face critical challenges in optimizing production efficiency while ensuring environmental sustainability, particularly concerning disease management, feed optimization, and environmental stressor mitigation. Current empirical approaches often lack the predictive capacity to address the dynamic interplay of biological, chemical, and physical factors in aquatic environments. This project proposes the development of a multiscale computational framework to model key processes in aquaculture systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations, agent-based biological models, and machine learning-driven predictive analytics. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) simulating water quality dynamics and waste dispersion in recirculating aquaculture systems under varying operational parameters; (2) predicting disease transmission pathways through coupled host-pathogen-environment interaction models; and (3) optimizing feeding regimes using reinforcement learning trained on metabolic and growth data. The computational workflow will incorporate real-time sensor data from experimental aquaculture facilities, genomic information on species-specific stress responses, and environmental monitoring datasets. By employing parallelized finite volume methods for fluid dynamics and graph neural networks to capture complex biological interactions, the models will operate at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying optimal stocking densities, early-warning systems for disease outbreaks, and adaptive feeding strategies that minimize resource waste. These computational advances will directly inform the design of next-generation aquaculture systems, enhancing productivity while reducing ecological impacts. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational complexity of three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations across extended temporal scales and enabling the training of deep learning models on multimodal datasets. This work will establish a paradigm for data-driven aquaculture management, bridging critical gaps between biological understanding and operational decision-making in sustainable aquatic food production.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to select, culture, propagate, harvest, and market domesticated fish, shellfish, and marine plants, both freshwater and saltwater. Includes instruction in the basic principles of aquatic and marine biology; health and nutrition of aquatic and marine life; design and operation of fish farms, breeding facilities, culture beds, and related enterprises; and related issues of safety, applicable regulations, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and social dynamics of colonial administrative networks in Spanish America (16th–18th centuries). Traditional historiography has relied on qualitative analysis of fragmented archival records, limiting systematic investigation of how bureaucratic practices shaped regional integration and resistance. Our research addresses this gap by constructing a relational database from digitized colonial correspondence, census records, and tribute logs to model interactions between administrative nodes (e.g., audiencias, viceroyalties, municipal councils) and subaltern communities. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for early modern Spanish and Indigenous-language loanwords, we will extract named entities, sentiment patterns, and network ties from over 50,000 pages of digitized texts. Graph analysis algorithms will then map hierarchical and lateral communication flows, while geospatial modeling (GIS) will visualize how resource extraction routes correlated with demographic shifts derived from tribute data. Computational demands include training custom NLP models for historical orthography, running parallelized network centrality calculations across temporal slices, and processing high-resolution georeferenced datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying critical junctures when administrative centralization intensified regional inequalities, (2) quantifying the relationship between bureaucratic expansion and Indigenous population displacement, and (3) generating open-access datasets for interdisciplinary study of imperial governance. By integrating computational methods with archival research, this project advances methodological innovation in Latin American history, offering scalable frameworks to analyze how colonial institutions mediated power across diverse geographies and populations. The scale of textual and spatial data analysis required necessitates HPC support to execute computationally intensive tasks within feasible timeframes, enabling historiographical insights unattainable through manual methods alone.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking areas of the world, including the Iberian, Latin American, and Lusophone worlds.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing complexity of simulating and optimizing dynamic theatrical environments. Modern productions increasingly integrate multidimensional design elements—such as adaptive lighting systems, spatially responsive soundscapes, and kinetic set components—that require real-time computational modeling to predict interactions between technical systems, human performers, and audience experience. Current workflows rely on fragmented, low-fidelity simulations that struggle to account for nonlinear variables like acoustic diffraction in non-static sets or energy-efficient lighting transitions across moving geometries. The proposed research will develop a unified computational framework to model these interactions at scale, employing parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) for acoustic propagation studies, GPU-accelerated ray tracing for spectral light behavior in deformable environments, and agent-based simulations to evaluate human movement constraints within evolving stage configurations. By running iterative optimization algorithms on HPC clusters, the project aims to generate predictive models that reduce physical prototyping costs while enabling unprecedented precision in design feasibility testing. Outcomes will include open-source tools for parametric theater space analysis, validated datasets linking computational predictions to empirical performance metrics, and case studies demonstrating resource-efficient solutions for productions integrating automation and immersive technologies. This work directly advances the technical theater field’s capacity to balance artistic innovation with operational sustainability, while providing students with hands-on training in computational design methodologies critical to next-generation live performance ecosystems.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Technical Theatre/ Theatre Design and Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic, technical and dramatic principles and techniques to the communication of dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through technical theatre methods. Includes instruction in set design, lighting design, sound effects, theatre acoustics, scene painting, property management, costume design, and technical direction and production and use of computer applications to support these functions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing adaptive learning systems (ALS) to deliver personalized, real-time instructional interventions in large-scale educational environments. While ALS have shown promise in improving learning outcomes, their effectiveness is constrained by the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous data streams—including learner interactions, multimodal content engagement, and biometric indicators—in dynamic, real-world educational contexts. Current approaches struggle to balance model granularity with latency requirements, particularly when scaling to thousands of concurrent users. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for training and deploying machine learning models that analyze temporal patterns in learner behavior while maintaining responsiveness. The research will utilize distributed deep learning architectures to process multimodal educational datasets, including clickstream logs, video annotation patterns, and writing process analytics captured from 15,000+ learners across six institutional partners. Computational experiments will compare transformer-based models, temporal graph networks, and hybrid neuro-symbolic approaches for predicting learner confusion states and knowledge retention. GPU-accelerated simulations will model intervention timing effects across diverse pedagogical scenarios, while containerized microservices will enable A/B testing of adaptive strategies in live environments. Expected outcomes include optimized algorithms for low-latency personalization in web-based instruction, validated metrics for computational efficiency in educational AI systems, and open-source tools for scalable learning analytics. By establishing HPC-powered methods to reconcile model complexity with real-time constraints, this work aims to advance the design of next-generation educational software capable of supporting equitable, data-driven instruction at institutional scales. The results will provide empirically grounded frameworks for integrating high-dimensional learning data into adaptive curricula, contributing to evidence-based practices in educational technology research.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, computer applications, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: Antibiotic resistance in veterinary pathogens poses a significant threat to livestock health, food security, and zoonotic disease management. Current methods for predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens affecting animals often lack the resolution to identify emerging genetic mechanisms or model complex host-pathogen-drug interactions. This project proposes a computational genomics approach to characterize AMR evolution in priority veterinary pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius and multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli. We will integrate whole-genome sequencing data from clinical veterinary isolates with pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models to identify resistance-associated genomic variants and epistatic interactions. Machine learning algorithms, trained on multi-omics datasets (including metagenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic profiles), will predict resistance phenotypes from genotypic data while accounting for host immune factors and treatment regimens. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate how structural modifications in target proteins (e.g., penicillin-binding proteins, efflux pumps) confer resistance to beta-lactams and other critical antimicrobials. These computationally intensive tasks require high-performance computing resources for large-scale genomic alignment (≥10,000 isolates), parallelized molecular simulations (µs-scale trajectories), and iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization. The project will generate three key outcomes: 1) a predictive AMR database for veterinary clinical decision support, 2) mechanistic models of resistance evolution under different treatment protocols, and 3) computational frameworks for optimizing drug dosing regimens in species-specific physiological contexts. By enabling precision antimicrobial use in veterinary practice, this work addresses critical gaps in One Health initiatives while advancing computational methods for translational veterinary biomedical research. The requested resources will directly support the development of open-access tools for veterinary diagnostic laboratories and contribute to sustainable antimicrobial stewardship in agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern office machinery, such as multifunctional printers, advanced point-of-sale systems, and AI-integrated data processing units, presents significant challenges for maintenance and repair protocols. Traditional diagnostic methods, which rely heavily on manual inspection and static troubleshooting guides, are insufficient to address intermittent failures, component degradation patterns, or compatibility issues arising from firmware updates. This project proposes the development of a machine learning (ML)-driven predictive maintenance framework tailored to business machine repair, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze operational telemetry, historical failure data, and environmental sensor inputs. The research will focus on constructing computational models that simulate mechanical wear, electrical signal anomalies, and software-hardware interactions across diverse machine architectures. By employing parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) for stress modeling on critical components and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to process time-series performance data, the project aims to predict failure probabilities with greater accuracy than current industry standards. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to account for variations in machine usage patterns, manufacturing tolerances, and regional power stability factors. Expected outcomes include a cloud-deployable diagnostic tool capable of recommending preemptive repairs, optimizing spare parts inventory management, and extending equipment lifespans through adaptive maintenance schedules. This work will directly benefit vocational training programs by integrating simulation-based failure scenarios into curricula, while its computational methodologies may inform sustainability initiatives aimed at reducing electronic waste. The resource request emphasizes GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory instances for multiphysics simulations, ensuring scalability across the heterogeneous device categories prevalent in business environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain and repair a variety of office machines, such as typewriters, word processing and dictation machines, calculators, data processing equipment, duplicating machines, and mailing machines. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment, and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of business machines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation platform to optimize training protocols and operational safety for commercial vehicle operators through advanced computational modeling. Despite the critical role of trucks, buses, and delivery vehicles in global supply chains, training programs often rely on static scenarios that inadequately prepare drivers for dynamic real-world conditions, such as unpredictable traffic patterns, adverse weather, or mechanical failures. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create large-scale, adaptive simulations that integrate real-time vehicle dynamics, environmental variables, and human decision-making factors. The computational framework will employ agent-based modeling to simulate multi-vehicle interactions across diverse road networks, coupled with machine learning algorithms to analyze historical accident data and predict high-risk scenarios. Additionally, finite element analysis will be applied to model vehicle responses under varying load distributions and emergency maneuvers. The simulations will generate granular datasets on driver performance metrics, fuel efficiency outcomes, and collision avoidance behaviors, enabling the development of personalized training modules and evidence-based safety guidelines. By scaling these simulations to thousands of concurrent virtual drivers, HPC resources will allow systematic testing of instructional strategies while accounting for regional infrastructure differences and regulatory constraints. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of scenario-based training tools, optimized route planning algorithms that balance safety and efficiency, and predictive models for vehicle maintenance scheduling. This work directly supports the program’s mission to modernize commercial vehicle instruction through data-driven methodologies, ultimately aiming to reduce accident rates, lower operational costs, and improve compliance with evolving transportation standards.
cip_title: Truck and Bus Driver/ Commercial Vehicle Operator and Instructor
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to drive trucks and buses, delivery vehicles, for-hire vehicles and other commercial vehicles, or to instruct commercial vehicle operators. Includes instruction in operating gas, diesel, or electrically-powered vehicles; loading and unloading cargo or passengers; reporting delays or accidents on the road; verifying load against shipping papers; arranging transportation for personnel; and keeping records of receipts and fares.

abstract: Immunologic diseases present complex diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to the dynamic interplay of genetic, molecular, and environmental factors driving dysregulated immune responses. This project seeks to advance precision immunotherapy strategies for autoimmune disorders and transplant rejection by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model immune cell interactions and predict patient-specific treatment outcomes. A critical barrier in current clinical practice is the inability to integrate multi-omics data (e.g., single-cell RNA sequencing, T-cell receptor repertoires, and proteomic profiles) with real-time patient metrics to guide therapy selection. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework combining mechanistic models of immune signaling pathways with machine learning (ML) to predict disease progression and therapeutic responses. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of immune cell population dynamics under diverse therapeutic perturbations, coupled with the training of ensemble ML classifiers on multi-institutional datasets encompassing rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and post-transplant immunophenotyping data. Key computational tasks include parallelized parameter optimization for ordinary differential equation models of cytokine networks, graph neural network analysis of cell-cell interaction networks, and Bayesian inference for biomarker discovery. The resulting models will identify candidate biomarkers for early diagnosis, stratify patients by predicted drug response, and optimize dosing schedules for biologic therapies. This work will directly inform two ongoing clinical trials at our institution investigating personalized IL-6 inhibitor regimens and tolerance induction protocols in kidney transplant recipients. By bridging mechanistic immunology with clinical datasets through HPC-driven analytics, the project aims to establish a scalable computational platform for immunotherapy personalization, reducing trial-and-error treatment approaches. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for immune cell trajectory prediction and clinically validated algorithms to guide therapeutic decision-making in immunopathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment and laboratory management of immunologic diseases. Includes instruction in diagnostic surgical pathology, management of organ transplantation and immunotherapy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on the historical evolution and regional variation of Korean dialects, with a focus on sociolinguistic dynamics. Despite extensive documentation of modern Korean dialects, computational analyses of their diachronic development remain limited due to the complexity of processing heterogeneous datasets spanning pre-modern texts, 20th-century archival records, and contemporary spoken corpora. The research problem centers on modeling phonetic, morphological, and lexical shifts across time and space while accounting for sociocultural factors such as migration patterns and language policy changes. Proposed computational methods include the development of NLP pipelines optimized for historical Hangul orthography, dialectometric algorithms for quantifying linguistic distances, and transformer-based models trained on regional speech corpora to detect gradient dialect boundaries. A key innovation involves adapting neural architectures to handle non-standardized spellings in pre-1945 texts and align them with modern dialect features. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of multi-terabyte text and audio datasets, hyperparameter optimization for deep learning models, and probabilistic simulations of language change. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database of annotated dialect features spanning five centuries, 2) quantitative models correlating linguistic variation with extralinguistic variables, and 3) open-source tools for automated dialect classification applicable to language preservation efforts and educational resource development. This work will provide novel insights into the mechanisms of dialectal divergence in Korean, addressing gaps in both philological scholarship and computational linguistics. By integrating traditional humanities methodologies with advanced machine learning, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven analysis of lesser-studied language varieties, with implications for digital humanities infrastructure in non-English contexts.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the integrative physiological responses of humans to sustained exposure to microgravity and space radiation, with a focus on systemic adaptations and cancer risk mitigation. Prolonged spaceflight induces multi-organ stressors, including musculoskeletal atrophy, cardiovascular deconditioning, and fluid redistribution, compounded by cosmic radiation exposure linked to genomic instability and oncogenesis. Current physiological models lack the resolution to capture dynamic, cross-system interactions under these conditions, limiting predictive capabilities for countermeasure development. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating physiological datasets from astronaut cohorts, radiation oncology studies, and experimental models of microgravity. Agent-based modeling will simulate tissue-specific responses to mechanical unloading and radiation-induced DNA damage, emphasizing crosstalk between musculoskeletal degeneration, immune dysfunction, and cancer predisposition pathways. Fluid dynamics simulations will characterize cerebral and cardiovascular hemodynamic alterations during gravitational transitions, while machine learning approaches will identify biomarkers predictive of individual resilience to spaceflight-associated carcinogenesis. The HPC environment is critical for managing high-dimensional data from wearable biosensors, histopathological imaging, and genomic/proteomic profiling, enabling real-time parameter optimization in multi-compartment models. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for personalized countermeasure regimens targeting concurrent physiological deconditioning and cancer risk, as well as mechanistic insights into gravity-dependent regulation of tumor suppressor pathways. This work directly addresses NASA’s goals for sustainable lunar and Martian missions by advancing computational tools to safeguard astronaut health, with translational potential for Earth-based oncology through novel models of mechano-radiation interactions in cancer progression.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physiological processes involved in low and high-altitude flight and living in space and related low-pressure and low-gravity environments, including sensorimotor interactions, response mechanisms, and the effects of injury, disease, and disability. Includes instruction in anatomy, molecular and cellular basis of muscle contraction, fuel utilization, neurophysiology of motor mechanics, systemic physiological responses (respiration, blood flow, endocrine secretions, and others), fatigue and exhaustion, systemic environmental pathologies, muscle and body training, physiology of specific exercises and activities, physiology of injury, and the effects of disabilities and disease.

abstract: Dairy production systems face critical challenges in optimizing milk yield, quality, and safety while minimizing economic and environmental costs. A key bottleneck lies in understanding the dynamic interactions between microbial communities in raw milk, processing environments, and final dairy products, which govern spoilage, pathogen persistence, and fermentation efficiency. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the complexity of these spatially and temporally variable systems. This project proposes an integrative computational framework to model microbial ecology and metabolic networks across dairy production stages. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable agent-based simulations of microbial population dynamics under varying processing conditions (e.g., pasteurization temperatures, storage durations) and genomic-scale flux balance analyses to predict metabolite exchange influencing product characteristics. Machine learning models trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metabolomic profiles from longitudinal sampling) will identify critical control points for quality assurance. The computational workflow will leverage containerized pipelines for reproducible analysis of sequencing data, coupled with GPU-accelerated neural networks to resolve patterns in high-dimensional sensor data from dairy processing equipment. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking operational parameters to microbial risks and product traits, validated through targeted lab experiments. This research will provide actionable insights for designing precision intervention strategies, reducing food waste from spoilage, and enhancing the safety of dairy products. By bridging gaps between microbial ecology, process engineering, and data science, the project advances computational capabilities in dairy science while addressing industry needs for sustainable innovation. Successful implementation requires HPC infrastructure capable of parallel processing for large-scale simulations (>10^6 agent interactions), high-memory nodes for genome-scale metabolic reconstructions, and scalable storage for petabyte-level multi-omics datasets.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of dairy animals and the production and handling of dairy products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic spatial organization of cellular components during tissue morphogenesis, a fundamental yet poorly understood process in developmental anatomy. A critical gap persists in modeling how mechanical forces and intracellular signaling pathways collectively drive the emergence of three-dimensional tissue architecture. To address this, we propose an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with continuum mechanics to simulate multicellular systems at subcellular resolution. The ABM component will represent individual cells as discrete entities with rule-based behaviors, while finite element methods will model stress propagation across extracellular matrices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the scale of these simulations, which require tracking >10^5 interacting cellular agents with micrometer-level spatial precision over developmental timescales (48-72 simulated hours). Parallelized code will leverage GPU acceleration to optimize force calculations and matrix solvers. Experimental validation will utilize time-lapse microscopy datasets of avian limb bud development, with machine learning pipelines (deployed on HPC clusters) quantifying cytoskeletal dynamics and strain patterns from 4D imaging data. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of critical force thresholds regulating epithelial folding patterns, 2) predictive models of tissue buckling under genetic perturbation scenarios, and 3) open-source simulation tools for visualizing mechanochemical coupling in developing tissues. This work will advance our mechanistic understanding of how cellular-scale processes generate anatomical form, with implications for congenital defect research and bioengineered tissue design. The requested computing allocation (500,000 CPU-core hours, 2 TB RAM allocation, and GPU node access) will enable parameter space exploration across physiologically relevant mechanical regimes currently inaccessible through conventional computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_title: Cell/ Cellular Biology and Anatomical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cell/cellular biology and anatomical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Hematologic and coagulation disorders present complex diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their multifactorial etiology, involving genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. Current laboratory approaches often struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data—limiting the ability to identify predictive biomarkers or optimize treatment strategies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable computational framework for multi-omics data integration and predictive modeling in hematologic pathologies. The primary research objectives include (1) identifying molecular signatures associated with thrombotic and hemorrhagic disorders through whole-genome sequencing and mass spectrometry data analysis, (2) constructing machine learning models to predict disease progression and treatment responses in myeloid malignancies, and (3) simulating coagulation cascade dynamics under varied physiological conditions to refine diagnostic algorithms. The computational workflow will utilize containerized pipelines for reproducibility, parallelized processing of large-scale genomic datasets, and GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational burden of processing terabytes of sequencing data, running millions of molecular dynamics simulations, and training complex neural networks on high-dimensional clinical datasets. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel genetic variants linked to clotting dysregulation, validated predictive models for personalized anticoagulant therapy, and optimized laboratory protocols for coagulation testing. By enhancing the resolution and scalability of hematologic data analysis, this project aims to advance precision diagnostics and inform evidence-based guidelines for laboratory management, ultimately improving patient outcomes in diverse hematologic disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory and analytical procedures for studying all facets of hematologic and coagulation disorders. May included related research in the management of hematology laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing neuroprosthetic device control through advanced computational modeling of neuromuscular-skeletal systems. While neuroprosthetics hold transformative potential for individuals with motor impairments, current systems often suffer from limited adaptability, high cognitive load for users, and suboptimal integration with biological feedback loops. Our research focuses on developing a multiscale simulation framework that bridges biomechanical modeling of limb dynamics, spiking neural network simulations of motor neuron pools, and reinforcement learning algorithms to refine real-time control strategies. The core computational challenge lies in integrating high-fidelity, real-time simulations of neuromuscular activation (using Hodgkin-Huxley-type models) with physics-based musculoskeletal rigid-body dynamics—a task requiring parallelized solvers and large-scale parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 1) whole-limb simulations at millisecond temporal resolution across 10⁵+ motor units, 2) evolutionary optimization of neural network architectures for adaptive control, and 3) closed-loop virtual trials incorporating stochastic biological variability in muscle fatigue and neural signal noise. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation platform for neuroprosthetic design, quantitative benchmarks for control latency versus stability tradeoffs, and novel co-adaptation algorithms that reduce user learning time by >40% in preliminary in silico testing. This work directly addresses NIH priorities in rehabilitative engineering while advancing computational methods for bidirectional neural interface systems. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated finite element modeling, distributed parameter sweeps across 50,000+ core-hours, and petascale data workflows integrating experimental electromyography datasets from clinical collaborators. By establishing a computational testbed for neuroprosthetic innovation, this project aims to accelerate the translation of adaptive neural interfaces into clinical practice.
cip_title: Medical Clinical Sciences/ Graduate Medical Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in medical clinical sciences or graduate medical studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of optimizing heterogeneous computing architectures for next-generation embedded systems and edge computing applications. As Internet of Things (IoT) devices and cyber-physical systems increasingly require real-time processing of multimodal sensor data, traditional simulation tools fail to adequately model the interplay between hardware components, software pipelines, and energy constraints at scale. The research aims to develop a novel framework for co-designing task-scheduling algorithms and reconfigurable hardware architectures using large-scale parametric simulations. The computational approach leverages parallelized discrete-event simulations to evaluate millions of design permutations across variables including memory hierarchy configurations, power-delivery networks, and thermal profiles. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to predict optimal resource allocation strategies under dynamic workloads. Implementation will utilize GPU-accelerated computing for neural network training and distributed memory systems for batched simulation trials. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly available benchmark dataset of optimized architectures for real-time edge computing workloads, (2) adaptive algorithms that reduce energy consumption by 15-20% in simulated IoT nodes compared to state-of-the-art schedulers, and (3) open-source tools for hardware-software co-simulation in resource-constrained environments. This work will provide critical insights into scalability challenges for distributed edge computing networks while advancing methodological approaches for high-fidelity computer engineering simulations. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of design space exploration and enabling timely convergence of machine learning models through distributed training across thousands of concurrent trials.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The interpretation of genetic variants in clinical diagnostics remains a critical challenge due to the growing volume and complexity of genomic data. While advances in sequencing technologies have enabled comprehensive profiling of structural variants, noncoding regions, and epigenetic modifications, distinguishing pathogenic mutations from benign variants requires scalable computational frameworks capable of integrating heterogeneous datasets. This project seeks to address this bottleneck by developing and deploying high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipelines to analyze multi-omics data from patients with suspected genetic disorders. Specifically, we aim to (1) optimize parallelized workflows for detecting rare structural variants and copy-number variations in whole-genome sequencing data, (2) train deep learning models to predict variant pathogenicity using integrated genomic, epigenomic, and clinical data, and (3) establish a cloud-compatible platform for real-time prioritization of candidate variants in clinical case reviews. The computational approach will leverage GPU-accelerated tools such as DeepVariant and CNN-based architectures for sequence analysis, alongside graph-based algorithms to model gene regulatory networks perturbed by pathogenic variants. By processing over 50 TB of existing cohort data—including long-read sequencing, Hi-C chromatin interaction maps, and RNA-seq from 1,200 undiagnosed cases—this work will identify novel disease-associated loci and improve diagnostic yield. The HPC resources requested are essential for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as population-scale allele frequency filtering, and reducing runtime for iterative model training. Outcomes will include validated pipelines for clinical laboratories, a curated variant classification framework, and open-source software to enhance interoperability between research and diagnostic platforms. This project directly aligns with the Laboratory Genetics and Genomics mission by bridging computational innovation with clinical interpretation, ultimately enabling faster, more accurate diagnosis of genetic diseases and informing targeted therapeutic strategies.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: Clinical Nurse Specialists (CNSs) are critical in optimizing patient outcomes through advanced clinical decision-making, yet resource constraints and complex care environments limit their capacity to predict and mitigate adverse events in real time. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model patient deterioration risks and intervention efficacy in acute care settings, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal health data. The research problem centers on integrating real-time electronic health record (EHR) data, wearable sensor outputs, and longitudinal patient histories to identify early warning signals of clinical decline—a task requiring large-scale data processing and predictive analytics beyond the capabilities of standard clinical systems. The computational approach will employ machine learning (ML) techniques, including ensemble models and neural networks, to synthesize heterogeneous datasets and simulate patient trajectories under varying intervention scenarios. Key tasks include parallelized training of ML models on retrospective EHR data, validation against prospective clinical outcomes, and agent-based modeling to evaluate the impact of CNS-led interventions on care workflows. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated computing for model optimization and deploy scalable storage solutions for terabyte-level datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for sepsis, acute respiratory failure, and delirium risks, tailored to prioritize CNS clinical actions. By enabling dynamic risk stratification and intervention planning, this work aims to reduce preventable complications, shorten hospital stays, and inform scalable decision-support tools for nurses. The HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of real-time data assimilation, multi-parameter simulations, and validation across diverse patient cohorts. This research aligns with national priorities to enhance clinical reasoning in nursing and advance data-driven care delivery models, with implications for healthcare cost reduction and patient safety improvement.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver direct patient and client care in clinical settings. Includes instruction in clinical pharmacotherapeutics, advanced clinical practice, holistic nursing, nursing practice and health care policy, administration and consultation services, health assessment, patient stabilization and care, and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize urban policing strategies through the development of a dynamic, agent-based simulation framework to model patrol allocation and response efficacy in real-world environments. Current approaches to police resource deployment often rely on historical crime data and static zoning, which fail to account for the complex, evolving interactions between criminal activity, community dynamics, and officer mobility. To address this gap, we propose a computational model integrating geospatial crime patterns, time-dependent socioeconomic variables, and real-time incident feeds to simulate urban crime ecosystems at high spatiotemporal resolution. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize and execute large-scale simulations capturing heterogeneous factors such as traffic flow, population density shifts, and ad hoc criminal behavior adaptations. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks and reinforcement learning, will be applied to iteratively refine patrol route recommendations under stochastic conditions. Key computational challenges include parallelizing spatially nested simulations, managing latency-critical data streams from live city sensors, and ensuring ethical guardrails in predictive outputs. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for precinct-level resource allocation, empirically grounded insights into emergent crime displacement effects, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated urban policing scenarios. By combining computational social science with operational police logistics, this work aims to advance evidence-based policing practices while fostering transparency in algorithmic resource allocation. The HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the required scale—simulating 10,000+ agent interactions across city-scale geometries—which cannot feasibly be replicated on local computing clusters. Successful implementation will provide law enforcement agencies with a proactive, data-driven framework to balance public safety objectives with community trust imperatives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of police and public security officers, including patrol and investigative activities, traffic control, crowd control and public relations, witness interviewing, evidence collection and management, basic crime prevention methods, weapon and equipment operation and maintenance, report preparation and other routine law enforcement responsibilities.

abstract: The increasing complexity of financial systems and the growing volume of transactional data necessitate advanced computational methods to address challenges in accounting accuracy, fraud detection, and regulatory compliance. This project seeks to develop a scalable, machine learning-driven framework for real-time anomaly detection in large-scale financial datasets, integrating techniques from accounting principles, distributed computing, and deep learning. A critical barrier to existing methods is the computational inefficiency of processing heterogeneous financial data—spanning structured ledgers, unstructured audit documents, and transactional metadata—at the speeds required for proactive decision-making. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model transactional relationships, transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for auditing text analysis, and high-performance distributed computing to enable parallelized training and inference. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to optimize model training on multi-terabyte datasets, simulating real-world financial networks using synthetically generated transactions compliant with accounting standards (e.g., GAAP/IFRS). Key innovations include a novel attention mechanism for cross-modal data fusion (tabular, text, and temporal) and differential privacy protocols to maintain data confidentiality during distributed processing. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive anomaly detection, validated against partnered institutional datasets, capable of identifying emerging fraud patterns with 30-50% higher precision than existing rule-based systems. This work will advance interdisciplinary research by establishing computationally rigorous methods for accounting analytics, while providing benchmarks for resource allocation in financial machine learning tasks. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling experiments across nodes, managing memory-intensive graph computations, and reducing iterative development cycles from weeks to days, ensuring timely validation of hypotheses in dynamic financial environments.
cip_definition: A program that combines accounting with computer science and/or computer studies.

abstract: Hematologic malignancies and disorders, such as leukemia, lymphoma, and myelodysplastic syndromes, are driven by complex genetic and molecular mechanisms that remain incompletely characterized. Current approaches to analyzing high-dimensional multi-omic datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic) in hematologic diseases face computational limitations in scalability, integration, and predictive modeling. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these challenges by developing advanced computational frameworks for identifying disease subtypes, predictive biomarkers, and therapeutic vulnerabilities. We will integrate whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, and clinical data from a cohort of 1,200 patients with myeloid neoplasms to map clonal evolution patterns and resistance mechanisms. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble algorithms, will be trained on these datasets to predict treatment response and relapse risk. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate the structural consequences of recurrent mutations in splicing factors (e.g., SF3B1, U2AF1) to identify targetable sites. The scale of these analyses—requiring parallel processing of >100 TB of genomic data, real-time optimization of hyperparameters, and iterative simulation workflows—necessitates HPC infrastructure with GPU acceleration and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) novel classifiers for risk stratification of myelodysplastic syndromes, (2) mechanistic insights into mutation-driven dysregulation of hematopoiesis, and (3) a validated pipeline for multi-omic data integration in hematology. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs and personalized therapeutic strategies, addressing critical gaps in the management of high-risk hematologic conditions. The requested computing resources are essential to achieve the throughput and precision required for translating complex datasets into biologically and clinically actionable knowledge.
cip_definition: Research focused on the mechanisms and therapy of diseases of the blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lymph, including patient management, diagnostic tests, biopsies, and other procedures.

abstract: Occupational therapy interventions rely on evidence-based approaches to optimize functional outcomes for individuals with physical, cognitive, or psychosocial impairments. However, a critical gap exists in understanding how task-specific motor learning activities—central to occupational therapy practice—induce neuroplastic changes at scale. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating individualized biomechanical modeling with neural network simulations to predict and analyze the effects of therapeutic tasks on cortical reorganization and functional recovery. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal data streams, including motion capture kinematics, electromyography (EMG), and synthetic neuroimaging data generated via biologically plausible neural models. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to identify patterns linking task parameters (e.g., repetition schedules, resistance levels) to predicted neural adaptation profiles across diverse patient populations. A key innovation involves creating patient-specific digital twins capable of simulating rehabilitation trajectories under varying intervention protocols. Computational demands stem from real-time optimization of multi-scale models (molecular to organismal levels) and stochastic simulations accounting for intersubject variability in neuroanatomy and pathology. Outcomes will include an open-source toolset for designing personalized therapeutic activities informed by simulated neuroplastic responses, bridging gaps between systems neuroscience and clinical occupational therapy practice. This work advances precision rehabilitation by establishing computational biomarkers for intervention efficacy, ultimately enabling data-driven clinical decision-making to improve functional independence in patients with neurological conditions such as stroke or traumatic brain injury. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the iterative model training, large-scale parameter space exploration, and validation against longitudinal clinical outcome data required by this translational approach.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: Gastrointestinal disorders, such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colorectal cancer, involve complex interactions between genetic, immunological, and microbial factors. Current clinical approaches often lack predictive precision due to the multifactorial nature of these conditions, necessitating advanced computational models to unravel underlying mechanisms. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metagenomic) from patient cohorts, integrating these with clinical data to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets. A key challenge lies in processing and interpreting the high-dimensional, heterogeneous data generated by next-generation sequencing and mass spectrometry, which demands scalable computational infrastructure. We propose a hybrid machine learning and network biology approach to model disease pathways, host-microbiome interactions, and treatment response variability. Deep learning architectures, including graph neural networks, will be trained on multi-omics data to predict disease progression and drug efficacy, while mechanistic agent-based models will simulate mucosal immune dynamics in silico. The computational workflow will require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, optimization of hyperparameters across thousands of concurrent jobs, and real-time visualization of spatial-temporal simulations. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel microbial signatures associated with IBD subtypes, predictive models for personalized biologic therapy selection, and a publicly accessible computational platform for simulating gut inflammation scenarios. By elucidating the systems-level drivers of gastrointestinal pathology, this work aims to advance precision medicine in gastroenterology, reducing diagnostic delays and optimizing therapeutic strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the project’s goals, as standard clinical workstations lack the capacity to handle the computational intensity of these analyses. Successful implementation will provide a template for data-driven gastroenterology research, bridging clinical observations with molecular mechanisms at scale.
cip_definition: Research focused on Gastroenterology

abstract: The increasing complexity of pharmaceutical policy decision-making, driven by evolving therapeutic landscapes, cost constraints, and regulatory requirements, necessitates advanced computational tools to evaluate population-level outcomes and system-wide impacts. This project seeks to develop a scalable modeling framework to optimize drug formulary design and reimbursement policies while balancing clinical effectiveness, economic sustainability, and regulatory compliance. Current limitations in formulary decision support systems stem from insufficient integration of real-world evidence, dynamic pharmacoeconomic variables, and multi-stakeholder risk preferences at scale. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized discrete event simulations and machine learning algorithms trained on linked claims data, electronic health records (EHRs), and drug utilization databases (∼10 TB). Agent-based models will simulate patient cohorts under varying formulary restrictions, reimbursement tiers, and adherence scenarios, incorporating stochastic processes for disease progression, treatment switching, and adverse events. Bayesian hierarchical models will quantify uncertainty in cost-effectiveness estimates across heterogeneous subpopulations. Computational challenges include managing sparse high-dimensional data through distributed memory architectures, optimizing Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for probabilistic sensitivity analyses, and enabling real-time policy scenario testing via GPU-accelerated neural networks. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support platform capable of evaluating 10^6+ policy permutations, validated against retrospective Medicaid and commercial insurance data. This work will advance methodological rigor in formulary science by enabling granular trade-off analyses between patient access, payer budgets, and manufacturer incentives under evolving regulatory constraints. The requested resources will directly support parameter estimation workflows requiring 50,000+ core-hours and memory-intensive genome-wide association study (GWAS) integrations to assess equity impacts of coverage policies. By bridging computational pharmacoeconomics with regulatory policy design, this project aims to establish best practices for evidence-based formulary management while demonstrating HPC’s transformative potential in pharmacy administration research.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Pharmacy Administration and Pharmacy Policy and Regulatory Affairs
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial, social, and economic sciences to the study and management of the distribution and use of pharmaceutical products and the provision of pharmacy services. Includes instruction in research design and methods, statistics, social and organizational behavior, pharmacoeconomics, management of pharmacy services, outcomes research, product planning and reimbursement, cost-benefit analysis, drug marketing, pharmacy and pharmaceutics law and regulation, risk assessment, and organization of the health care system.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of algorithmic curation in shaping cultural diversity through the analysis of large-scale streaming data from digital music platforms. As algorithmic recommendation systems increasingly mediate access to cultural content, concerns have emerged about their potential to homogenize consumption patterns or amplify niche genres. This research addresses a critical gap in understanding how these systems influence the evolution of musical taste and the circulation of cultural meaning within digital ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process and analyze anonymized user interaction datasets encompassing billions of streams, playlist creations, and cross-platform sharing events. Computational methods will include network analysis to map genre diffusion patterns, transformer-based NLP models to interpret user-generated metadata, and agent-based simulations to model long-term cultural dynamics under different recommendation paradigms. The project will also employ counterfactual modeling to assess how alternative algorithmic designs might foster diversity. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying cultural homogenization in streaming environments, identification of platform-specific bias patterns in content promotion, and evidence-based recommendations for ethical algorithmic design. By bridging computational social science with digital musicology, this work advances humanistic inquiry into the technological mediation of cultural practices while providing actionable insights for platform developers and policymakers. The scale of data processing—requiring parallelized workflows for graph computations and real-time simulation of user behavior networks—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve research objectives within viable timeframes. Results will contribute to emerging debates about cultural preservation in algorithmic societies and establish methodologies for interdisciplinary humanities computing in understudied domains of digital culture.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on combined studies and research in the humanities subjects as distinguished from the social and physical sciences, emphasizing languages, literatures, art, music, philosophy and religion.

abstract: The integration of sustainable tourism practices within natural resource settings requires advanced tools to model complex socio-ecological systems, yet current approaches often lack the computational capacity to capture dynamic interactions between visitor behavior, ecosystem resilience, and policy scenarios. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution simulation framework to optimize tourism planning while minimizing environmental degradation in protected areas. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning, we will simulate visitor movement patterns, resource utilization, and ecological impacts across diverse landscapes under varying climate and management conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process multi-scale datasets, including geospatial layers of habitat sensitivity, real-time visitor tracking data, and climate projections, while running computationally intensive parameter sweeps to identify sustainable carrying capacities. The models will integrate stakeholder-defined thresholds for ecological disturbance and visitor satisfaction, enabling iterative testing of adaptive management strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to forecast site-specific tourism pressures under climate change, identify conflict zones between recreation and conservation goals, and evaluate trade-offs in proposed infrastructure development. Results will directly inform land management agencies and tourism operators in designing spatially explicit, data-driven policies that align with regional biodiversity targets and cultural heritage preservation efforts. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project advances the methodological rigor of sustainable tourism research, offering scalable solutions for balancing economic viability with long-term ecosystem health in natural resource-dependent communities.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resource Recreation and Tourism
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, develop, and manage tourism in a natural resource setting, with an emphasis on applying environmentally sound, culturally sensitive, and economically sustainable principles. Includes instruction in environmental studies; natural resource management and interpretation; tourism planning, management, and policies; public land use management and policies; communications; marketing; and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of thematic and stylistic evolution in American literature from the Colonial Era to the 21st century. While traditional literary scholarship has relied on close reading and manual comparative analysis, the sheer volume of texts and the complexity of intertextual connections across centuries present challenges for identifying macro-level patterns. This research addresses this gap by applying natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to a curated corpus of over 50,000 primary texts, including novels, essays, poetry, and transcribed oral traditions. The computational workflow will involve topic modeling to trace shifts in dominant themes (e.g., individualism, regional identity, modernity) and transformer-based models to analyze stylistic innovations, such as syntax variation and narrative voice. A key innovation will be the development of a graph-based network to map influences among authors and regional traditions, using semantic similarity metrics and citation analysis. HPC resources are critical for training custom ML models on heterogeneous text data, processing high-dimensional linguistic features, and running iterative simulations to validate historical-critical hypotheses. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital archive of annotated texts, visualization tools for exploring literary networks, and quantitative frameworks to supplement qualitative scholarship. By bridging computational methods with literary theory, this project aims to uncover previously underexamined connections between folkloric traditions and canonical works, as well as provide new methodologies for periodizing American literary movements. The results will directly support pedagogical applications and inform ongoing debates about the role of regionalism and orality in shaping national literary identity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the United States from the Colonial Era to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and regional and oral traditions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive machine learning framework to predict acute health deteriorations in homebound individuals receiving care from home health aides (HHAs). Despite advances in remote monitoring, real-time prediction of emergent events (e.g., falls, sepsis, cardiac episodes) in home settings remains limited by heterogeneous data streams, environmental variability, and sparse annotation. The research problem centers on integrating multimodal data—including wearable sensor outputs, HHA-reported activity logs, and ambient smart home device signals—to identify early risk signatures while accounting for the unique constraints of home-based care (e.g., intermittent connectivity, non-clinical observers). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-frequency sensor data (accelerometry, pulse oximetry), train temporal-convolutional neural networks on irregularly sampled time series, and simulate stochastic home-environment scenarios through agent-based modeling. The computational approach includes three phases: (1) federated learning across synthetic patient cohorts to preserve privacy while capturing demographic and comorbidity diversity; (2) reinforcement learning to optimize HHA alert thresholds based on evolving patient states and caregiver capacity; (3) uncertainty quantification to flag low-confidence predictions for human review. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for adaptive risk stratification in resource-constrained home environments, validated against retrospective HHA intervention records. The project addresses a critical gap in decentralized care by enabling proactive, data-driven decision-making for HHAs—a workforce traditionally underserved by predictive technologies. Success could reduce avoidable hospitalizations among homebound populations while establishing a computational toolkit for ethically aligned AI in paraprofessional healthcare settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and support services for homebound disabled, recovering, or elderly people. Includes instruction in basic nutrition, home sanitation, infection control, first aid, taking vital signs, personal hygiene, interpersonal communication skills, supervised home management, emergency recognition and referral, geriatric care, and legal and ethical responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of infectious disease transmission dynamics and evaluate the impact of public health interventions in diverse urban populations. Current models often lack the granularity to integrate real-time demographic, socio-economic, and mobility data at scale, limiting their utility for localized policy decisions. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling framework that simulates disease spread across synthetic populations constructed from multi-source data, including anonymized electronic health records, census data, and transportation networks. The computational demands of simulating millions of agents with heterogeneous behavioral patterns, coupled with parameter sweeps to test intervention scenarios (e.g., vaccination strategies, school closures), require parallelized processing and significant memory allocation. Additionally, machine learning pipelines will be implemented to calibrate models using historical outbreak data and generate probabilistic forecasts under varying public health policies. Outcomes will quantify trade-offs between intervention efficacy, economic costs, and health equity metrics, with a focus on reducing disparities in vulnerable communities. This work will directly inform state and local health departments on optimizing resource allocation during emerging outbreaks. The requested HPC resources are critical for overcoming current bottlenecks in model runtime and complexity, enabling simulations at unprecedented spatial resolution (census tract level) and temporal scales (12-month projections). By integrating high-dimensional datasets and advancing computational methods in epidemiology, this project aims to establish a scalable toolkit for evidence-based public health decision-making in complex urban environments.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, manage, and evaluate public health care services; to function as public health professionals in public agencies, the private sector, and other settings; and to provide leadership in the field of public health. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, public health principles, preventive medicine, health policy and regulations, health care services and related administrative functions, public health law enforcement, health economics and budgeting, public communications, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive maintenance models and energy-efficient design frameworks for heating, air conditioning, ventilation, and refrigeration (HVACR) systems. Current industry practices rely heavily on reactive maintenance and generalized design standards, leading to energy inefficiencies, frequent system failures, and excessive operational costs. To address this, the research aims to integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML), and thermodynamic simulations to model HVACR system performance under diverse operational and environmental conditions. High-fidelity CFD simulations will analyze airflow, heat transfer, and refrigerant behavior in complex geometries, while ML algorithms trained on historical maintenance data will predict component degradation and optimize service schedules. Additionally, thermodynamic models will evaluate alternative refrigerants and system configurations to minimize environmental impact. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the need to process large datasets from IoT-enabled HVACR systems and run parallelized simulations across thousands of scenarios—necessitates HPC resources. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-source predictive maintenance tools, validated frameworks for retrofitting legacy systems with eco-friendly refrigerants, and data-driven guidelines for optimizing energy consumption in residential and commercial HVACR installations. These results will directly benefit technicians and engineers by reducing diagnostic uncertainties, extending equipment lifespans, and supporting compliance with evolving environmental regulations. By bridging computational modeling with practical HVACR maintenance strategies, this project aims to drive sustainable innovation in a sector critical to global energy management and climate resilience.
cip_title: Heating, Air Conditioning, Ventilation and Refrigeration Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, install, service and maintain the operating condition of heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration systems. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of heating, air conditioning and refrigeration systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for analyzing cross-jurisdictional legal reasoning patterns, specifically tailored to support foreign lawyers navigating U.S. case law. The challenge lies in the vast, unstructured nature of U.S. judicial opinions, which contain implicit reasoning frameworks, cultural assumptions, and citation networks that are often opaque to those trained in non-Common Law systems. Traditional legal education tools struggle to systematically decode these patterns at scale, creating barriers for foreign legal professionals. This project proposes an interdisciplinary approach combining computational linguistics, graph theory, and comparative legal analysis to map doctrinal evolution and argumentation structures within U.S. appellate decisions. Using transformer-based language models fine-tuned on legal corpora, we will process ~500,000 federal and state court opinions to identify latent reasoning templates, citation dynamics, and rhetorical strategies characteristic of U.S. jurisprudence. Graph neural networks will then model precedent hierarchies and temporal influence patterns across jurisdictions. The computational workflow requires distributed training of large language models across GPU nodes, parallel processing of heterogeneous legal texts, and iterative visualization of multidimensional legal concept spaces. Expected outcomes include an open-access analytical platform that visually surfaces implicit reasoning norms, predicts jurisprudential trends, and generates comparative syntheses between U.S. and non-U.S. legal approaches. This resource will directly enhance pedagogical tools for foreign lawyers by providing data-driven insights into the contextual logic of U.S. legal arguments, while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of computational social science and legal education. The project’s scale demands HPC capabilities to manage memory-intensive model training, real-time querying of massive legal graphs, and dynamic simulation of hypothetical legal scenarios based on historical reasoning patterns.
cip_definition: A program that prepares lawyers educated outside the United States to understand U. S. or Canadian law and jurisprudence.

abstract: The increasing complexity of air traffic management systems, driven by rising global air travel demand and evolving operational constraints, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize safety, efficiency, and scalability. Current air traffic control (ATC) methodologies rely on heuristic models and static protocols that struggle to adapt to dynamic variables such as weather disruptions, heterogeneous aircraft performance, and real-time rerouting requirements. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate and optimize next-generation ATC decision-making processes. The research will focus on integrating real-time flight data, weather patterns, and airspace constraints into a scalable, agent-based simulation environment to model traffic flow management, conflict detection, and resolution strategies. Computational methods will include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic risks, machine learning models for predictive traffic pattern analysis, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to balance competing priorities such as fuel efficiency, delay minimization, and safety margins. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale scenario testing across diverse airspace configurations, including extreme-density scenarios and edge cases involving simultaneous system failures. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for operational improvements under variable conditions, validated machine learning architectures for adaptive traffic prediction, and open-source simulation tools to support FAA modernization initiatives. By leveraging distributed computing resources, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical ATC research and deployable solutions, providing a foundation for data-driven policy updates and automated decision-support systems. The results will directly inform ongoing efforts to enhance the National Airspace System’s capacity and resilience while maintaining stringent safety standards in an era of unprecedented aviation growth.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to air-traffic management and control, usually with additional training at the FAA Flight Control Center in a cooperative education program. Includes instruction in flight control, the use of radar and electronic scanning devices, plotting of flights, radio communication, interpretation of weather conditions affecting flights, flight instrumentation used by pilots, and maintenance of flight-control center or control-tower log books.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance applied psychological research on optimizing community-based mental health interventions. A critical challenge in counseling and applied psychology is understanding how dynamic, multilevel factors—such as individual cognitive-behavioral patterns, social network influences, and organizational resource allocation—interact to shape intervention outcomes in real-world settings. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to model these nonlinear, time-dependent relationships, particularly when analyzing large-scale longitudinal datasets from community programs. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) integrated with machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate intervention scenarios across diverse populations and environments. The ABMs will incorporate empirical data from existing studies, including demographic variables, behavioral metrics, and social network structures, to represent individuals and their interactions within community systems. ML algorithms will then identify predictors of intervention success and iteratively refine model parameters. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of running thousands of parallel simulations, processing high-dimensional data (e.g., electronic health records, ecological momentary assessments), and training deep reinforcement learning models to propose adaptive intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into how counseling programs can be tailored to individual and community needs, predictive tools for evaluating intervention scalability, and a publicly accessible computational framework for applied psychology researchers.
