By bridging psychological theory with advanced computational modeling, this work aims to enhance the precision and effectiveness of mental health support in community settings while advancing methodological innovation in applied psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychological theories and methods to real-world settings and problems, such as business and industry, government, education, military, and community settings. Includes instruction in applications of psychology, industrial/organizational psychology, developmental psychology, social psychology, cognitive psychology, counseling, human factors, research methods and statistics, and program evaluation.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of musculoskeletal disorders necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize rehabilitation strategies and understand movement biomechanics. Current limitations in modeling the multiscale interactions between neuromuscular activation, tissue mechanics, and joint dynamics hinder the development of personalized therapeutic interventions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps by constructing high-fidelity simulations of human movement and rehabilitation processes. The research focuses on two primary aims: (1) developing patient-specific musculoskeletal models to predict strain distributions in soft tissues during rehabilitative exercises, and (2) analyzing motor control patterns in neurological populations using machine learning-driven kinematic datasets. Computational methods will integrate finite element modeling (FEM) of muscle-tendon units with opensim-based multibody dynamics, requiring parallel processing to manage the high-dimensional parameter space and nonlinear material properties. Large-scale motion capture datasets from clinical populations will be processed using GPU-accelerated neural networks to identify movement biomarkers predictive of rehabilitation outcomes. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across anatomical variability, exercise intensities, and pathological conditions, which are computationally prohibitive on local workstations. Expected outcomes include novel computational frameworks for optimizing exercise prescriptions, risk stratification tools for overuse injuries, and open-source biomechanical datasets to support therapeutic device design. By elucidating the relationships between movement patterns, tissue adaptation, and functional recovery, this work will advance evidence-based practices in kinesiology and provide a scalable platform for future research in precision rehabilitation. The requested resources are critical for achieving the necessary computational throughput to resolve submillisecond neuromuscular responses and millimeter-scale tissue deformations across prolonged exercise durations.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of neural circuits underlying sensory integration and decision-making in mammalian models, with a focus on how nonlinear network interactions generate behaviorally relevant spatiotemporal activity patterns. A key challenge in studying these systems is the integration of multiscale data—from synaptic-level electrophysiology to population-wide calcium imaging—into predictive models that capture how microscale connectivity shapes macroscale function. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale spiking neural network simulations that incorporate empirically derived connectivity rules and biologically realistic synaptic plasticity mechanisms. Our computational approach will utilize modular workflows: (1) Parameter optimization via evolutionary algorithms to identify network configurations capable of reproducing in vivo recordings, (2) GPU-accelerated simulation of candidate networks under diverse stimulus conditions using the NEST simulator, and (3) Topological analysis of network dynamics through persistent homology and dimensionality reduction techniques. These simulations will generate petabyte-scale spiking activity datasets requiring distributed storage and parallelized post-processing. The requested HPC resources will enable systematic exploration of how structural variability (e.g., inhibitory/excitatory balance, neuromodulatory gradients) influences functional stability and information encoding capacity. Expected outcomes include predictive models of circuit dysfunction relevant to neurodevelopmental disorders and a publicly accessible database of simulated network architectures. This work will establish a computational framework for bridging cellular-resolution neurobiology with systems-level phenomena, directly supporting hypothesis generation for ongoing experimental studies in collaborative labs. By characterizing fundamental principles of neural circuit organization, the project aims to advance both theoretical neuroscience and the development of biologically inspired machine learning architectures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in neurobiology and neurosciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of generative design frameworks for adaptive urban microclimates, a niche interdisciplinary domain within architectural sciences. Traditional architectural simulations prioritize static environmental performance metrics (e.g., energy efficiency, thermal comfort) but lack dynamic, context-aware models that integrate real-time socio-environmental data streams, cultural behavioral patterns, and material aging processes. This gap limits the ability to design urban architectures that adaptively respond to evolving climate stressors and heterogeneous human needs. The proposed work will address this by constructing a multi-agent computational model that simulates interactions between built environments, transient microclimate conditions, and pedestrian behavior. The framework will employ a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model spatial connectivity, convolutional recurrent networks (CRNNs) to process time-series environmental data from IoT sensors, and reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize adaptive façade and circulation systems. HPC resources are critical for training these models at urban scales, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of agent-environment interaction scenarios and high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source toolkit for simulating feedback loops between architectural interventions and localized climate impacts; (2) predictive metrics for evaluating design resilience against stochastic weather events; and (3) evidence-based protocols for deployable kinetic architectural components. By bridging architectural design, urban climatology, and computational social science methods, this work aims to establish new methodologies for context-responsive architecture while demonstrating how HPC can enable novel research trajectories in underdeveloped areas of architectural technology.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in floriculture operations, specifically optimizing post-harvest longevity, supply chain efficiency, and floral design innovation. Commercial floristry faces persistent losses due to premature flower senescence, logistical inefficiencies in perishable product distribution, and labor-intensive design processes. Current experimental approaches to these issues are constrained by the dynamic interactions of genetic, environmental, and logistical variables that defy simple linear modeling. We propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data analysis, agent-based supply chain simulations, and generative machine learning models. Genomic and transcriptomic datasets from key ornamental species (e.g., roses, chrysanthemums) will be analyzed to identify molecular markers linked to vase life under varying storage conditions. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will model optimal delivery routes and inventory strategies across heterogeneous climate zones, incorporating real-time weather and market demand data. For design automation, graph neural networks will be trained on 3D-scanned floral arrangements to generate space-efficient, aesthetically validated compositions. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing capabilities for large-scale parameter optimization, climate model downscaling, and high-resolution image synthesis. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for cultivar selection based on supply chain destinations, dynamic inventory management protocols, and AI-assisted design platforms that reduce material waste by 15-20%. The integration of plant biology insights with operational analytics will provide a novel decision-support framework for floristry enterprises, enhancing both biological resource utilization and business profitability. By bridging molecular-scale phenomena with enterprise-level logistics, this research aims to establish computational floriculture as a data-driven discipline within agricultural sciences.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage commercial and contract florist enterprises, supply and delivery services, and flower catering services. Includes instruction in the applicable principles of plant science; purchasing, storage, and delivery systems; floral design and arranging; and principles of business management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the computational modeling of large-scale, interdisciplinary music performance dynamics, with a focus on real-time synchronization and improvisation patterns in ensemble settings. While music performance analysis has traditionally relied on qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods, the integration of high-dimensional sensor data (e.g., motion capture, audio waveform analysis, and biometric feedback from performers) presents a significant computational challenge. The research problem centers on resolving latency and scalability bottlenecks when analyzing temporal interactions between musicians, dancers, and audience response metrics in complex, improvisatory contexts. Proposed methods include the development of parallelized signal-processing pipelines to synchronize multimodal datasets at sub-millisecond resolution, coupled with machine learning models trained to identify emergent patterns in collaborative creativity. The computational workflow will employ GPU-accelerated frameworks for feature extraction from audio-visual recordings and graph-based network analysis to map decision-making hierarchies during unrehearsed performances. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for quantifying tacit knowledge in collective artistic practices, with applications in pedagogy, augmented performance systems, and the preservation of intangible cultural heritage. By enabling the processing of terabyte-scale datasets from experimental performances, this work aims to advance computational musicology’s capacity to address questions of embodied cognition and cross-cultural improvisation strategies at previously intractable resolutions. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive workloads during model training and for simulating agent-based models of performer interaction, which require distributed computing architectures to achieve real-world relevance.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of music and the performing arts. Includes instruction in music, dance, and other performing arts media.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in pediatric populations by integrating multi-omics data with clinical outcomes. Pediatric diseases often involve complex, multifactorial mechanisms influenced by genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors, yet current diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks rely on generalized protocols that lack personalization. A critical barrier is the computational challenge of analyzing large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets while accounting for developmental variability across pediatric age groups. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining machine learning (ML) and network-based modeling to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets specific to developmental stages and disease subtypes. The pipeline will integrate raw sequencing data from a cohort of 2,000 pediatric patients with congenital heart defects (CHD) and neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), alongside longitudinal clinical records. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of whole-genome sequences, RNA-seq datasets, and proteomic profiles using tools such as GATK, DESeq2, and PyTorch for deep learning-based feature extraction. Network models will map gene-protein interaction dynamics across developmental timelines, while federated learning frameworks will preserve patient privacy during cross-institutional data harmonization. Key outcomes include (1) stage-specific molecular signatures predictive of CHD-NDD comorbidity, (2) a validated ML classifier for early intervention targeting, and (3) open-source computational workflows tailored for pediatric multi-omics integration. This work will directly address the scarcity of pediatric-specific computational models in clinical decision support systems, with implications for reducing diagnostic delays and optimizing therapeutic efficacy. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the project’s data volume (~1.2 PB), enable real-time simulations of developmental pathways, and support iterative model training across heterogeneous datasets. Findings will be disseminated through clinical partnerships to inform trial designs for precision therapies in pediatric populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the analysis of speech and language disorders using machine learning models, with the goal of improving the precision and scalability of clinical assessments conducted by speech-language pathology assistants (SLPAs). Current methods for diagnosing and monitoring communication disorders often rely on manual, time-intensive analyses of speech samples, which can introduce subjectivity and limit the capacity to detect subtle patterns in large datasets. To address this, we propose training deep learning models to automate the identification of phonological, fluency, and voice quality anomalies in multilingual speech datasets. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process over 10,000 hours of annotated audio recordings from diverse clinical populations (e.g., aphasia, stuttering, dysarthria) and control groups. Computational workflows will include spectrogram feature extraction, transformer-based sequence modeling for temporal pattern recognition, and multimodal integration of speech signals with demographic and treatment history data. A key innovation is the development of adaptive models that account for dialectal variations and comorbid conditions, which are often underrepresented in existing tools. The outcomes will include open-source algorithms for real-time speech error detection and a web-based interface optimized for SLPA workflows, enabling faster, evidence-based clinical decisions. By automating routine analyses, this project aims to free SLPAs to focus on patient-centered care while providing quantitative metrics to guide treatment personalization. The scalability of these tools—dependent on HPC-enabled training of large neural networks—will directly support translational research in underserved populations, where access to specialized speech-language pathologists is limited. Successful implementation will advance equitable outcomes in communication disorder management and establish a computational foundation for future SLPA-led research initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a precision nutrition framework that models the interplay between individual metabolic variability, dietary patterns, and microbiome dynamics to optimize clinical dietetic interventions. Traditional dietary recommendations often adopt a one-size-fits-all approach, which fails to account for heterogeneity in nutrient metabolism driven by genetic, epigenetic, and microbial factors. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline integrating multi-omics data (genomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic) with real-time physiological biomarkers to predict personalized dietary responses. The research will utilize dynamic computational models, including genome-scale metabolic reconstructions and agent-based simulations of gut microbiome ecosystems, to map how specific nutrients and food matrices modulate metabolic pathways across diverse populations. HPC resources are critical for executing high-throughput simulations of thousands of virtual patient profiles, training deep learning algorithms on complex phenotypic datasets, and resolving temporal interactions between host metabolism and microbial communities. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers predictive of dietary responsiveness, the generation of patient-specific nutritional optimization strategies, and the creation of an open-access tool for dietitians to simulate dietary interventions in silico. This work bridges computational systems biology and clinical dietetics, advancing the capacity to tailor nutrition therapies for conditions such as metabolic syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, and diabetes. By elucidating mechanisms underlying interindividual variability, the project aims to establish a foundation for data-driven precision nutrition, directly enhancing the efficacy of dietetic practice while reducing trial-and-error in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to integrate and apply the principles of the food and nutrition sciences, human behavior, and the biomedical sciences to design and manage effective nutrition programs in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in human nutrition; nutrient metabolism; the role of foods and nutrition in health promotion and disease prevention; planning and directing food service activities; diet and nutrition analysis and planning; supervision of food storage and preparation; client education; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This research seeks to optimize energy consumption patterns in full-service hotel operations through high-fidelity simulations of integrated building management systems (BMS) and guest behavior dynamics. The hospitality industry faces mounting pressure to reduce operational costs and carbon footprints, yet existing energy models inadequately capture the complex interplay between HVAC systems, real-time occupancy fluctuations, and guest comfort preferences in multi-use hospitality spaces. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose developing an agent-based modeling framework that synthesizes three data streams: 1) IoT sensor data from 12 participating hotels (covering thermal zones, equipment loads, and occupancy patterns), 2) behavioral data from 50,000+ anonymized guest profiles, and 3) weather and event scheduling data for six distinct geographic markets. The computational model will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate energy demand scenarios across 15-minute intervals over a five-year horizon, incorporating machine learning subroutines to predict adaptive guest responses to dynamic temperature adjustments. By creating a digital twin environment capable of processing 2.3 billion data points, this project aims to identify energy-saving protocols that maintain guest satisfaction thresholds while reducing HVAC-related energy consumption by a projected 18-22% in simulated environments. The resulting framework will provide hotel operators with actionable insights for balancing sustainability initiatives with service quality imperatives, addressing a critical gap in data-driven decision-making for hospitality infrastructure management. Successful validation could establish new benchmarks for smart energy allocation in adaptive reuse buildings and inform AI-driven BMS standards for the lodging industry.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide food and/or lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage, and control; hotel and restaurant facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; facilities management; marketing and sale promotion strategies; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotel, motel, and/or restaurant operations. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 52.0902.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions require personalized approaches to address the diverse motor, cognitive, and psychosocial needs of patients. However, optimizing these interventions remains challenging due to the complex interplay of individual biomechanical, neurological, and environmental factors. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that simulate patient-specific responses to OT interventions, enabling data-driven customization of therapeutic strategies. The research focuses on two interrelated aims: (1) creating biomechanical and neural simulations to predict functional outcomes of motor rehabilitation tasks, and (2) employing machine learning algorithms to analyze multimodal datasets (e.g., motion capture, electromyography, patient-reported outcomes) for identifying optimal intervention parameters. Computational workflows will integrate finite element modeling of joint mechanics, reinforcement learning for adaptive task progression, and Bayesian optimization to balance therapeutic efficacy with patient comfort. By parallelizing these processes across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce simulation times for complex motor tasks from days to hours, facilitating rapid iteration of intervention designs. The project will validate models against clinical data from collaborating OT practitioners, ensuring translational relevance. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for predicting patient-specific recovery trajectories and generating evidence-based intervention recommendations. This work will advance OT practice by bridging gaps between clinical expertise and computational precision, ultimately supporting the development of standardized yet adaptable protocols for pre-OT education and practice. The requested computing resources are critical for handling large-scale parameter optimization, real-time sensitivity analyses, and the integration of heterogeneous datasets that exceed the capacity of local workstations. Findings will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for OT educators and peer-reviewed publications, fostering collaboration between computational science and rehabilitation disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in occupational therapy.

abstract: The emergence of complex xenobiotic exposures in veterinary populations—driven by environmental contaminants, novel pharmaceuticals, and multi-chemical interactions—poses significant challenges for predicting toxicological outcomes and optimizing therapeutic interventions. Current experimental models struggle to resolve the combinatorial effects of mixed exposures or species-specific variations in drug metabolism, particularly in non-model animals. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive multiscale models of toxicokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions in veterinary-relevant species. We will integrate molecular dynamics simulations of xenobiotic-receptor binding, machine learning-driven quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) frameworks to characterize interspecies differences in drug metabolism and toxicity thresholds. Large-scale genomic and metabolomic datasets from bovine, canine, and avian models will be processed to identify conserved biomarkers of hepatotoxicity and neurotoxicity. The computational workflow will prioritize HPC-dependent tasks, including parallelized docking studies of pesticide metabolites with cytochrome P450 isoforms, ensemble modeling of probabilistic exposure scenarios, and Bayesian optimization of antidote dosing regimens. Expected outcomes include a cloud-accessible database of cross-species toxicity predictions, open-source tools for veterinary risk assessment, and validated protocols for rapid antidote development in cases of mass toxicosis events. By enabling granular simulations of drug-pathogen-environment interactions, this work will directly inform clinical guidelines for managing poisoning outbreaks in livestock and companion animals while reducing reliance on invasive in vivo testing. The resource allocation will support critical advancements in veterinary precision medicine, with translational implications for understanding chemical threats at the human-animal-environment interface.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of specific environmental and food hazards affecting domestic and wild animals and the development and action of chemical antidotes and treatments. Includes instruction in small and large animal toxicology and pharmacology, neurotoxicology, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, neuropharmacology, xenobiotics, drug resistance, pesticides, toxicological pathology, genetic and molecular toxicology, environmental toxicology, drug and toxicant analysis and evaluation, and environmental radiology.

abstract: Occupational safety in high-risk industrial environments requires advanced predictive models to anticipate and mitigate hazards arising from complex interactions between human workers, machinery, and environmental factors. Current risk assessment tools often rely on static datasets or simplified simulations, limiting their ability to model dynamic scenarios with multiple concurrent variables. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework for simulating workplace safety risks using agent-based modeling (ABM) and multi-physics simulations. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create scalable models that integrate real-time sensor data, ergonomic stressors, equipment failure probabilities, and chemical exposure dynamics. Computational workflows will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess probabilistic risk outcomes across diverse industrial configurations, while finite element analysis will model localized hazards such as structural collapses or ventilation failures in confined spaces. Validation will utilize historical incident datasets from manufacturing and construction sectors. The proposed HPC infrastructure is critical to handle the computational demands of simulating thousands of interacting agents and physics-based systems at sub-second temporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for scenario-based hazard prediction, quantitative risk prioritization metrics, and optimized safety protocol recommendations tailored to variable workplace conditions. This work directly addresses gaps in proactive occupational safety planning, with potential applications in regulatory compliance, workforce training, and emergency preparedness. By enabling computationally intensive simulations previously infeasible on local clusters, the project aims to advance data-driven decision-making in occupational health, reducing preventable workplace injuries through predictive analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining job-related health and safety standards. Includes instruction in safety engineering principles, inspection and monitoring procedures, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, applications to specific work environments, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing family-centered care models for managing chronic diseases in diverse populations. Chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and mental health disorders disproportionately affect underserved communities, with outcomes influenced by complex interactions between biological, behavioral, and socioenvironmental factors. Current clinical decision-support tools often lack the computational power to integrate multi-dimensional data—including electronic health records, genomic markers, social determinants of health, and longitudinal family health patterns—into actionable insights for nurses. This research will develop machine learning models to predict disease trajectories and evaluate the efficacy of tailored family nursing interventions. Computational workflows will process terabyte-scale datasets using federated learning frameworks to preserve patient privacy while aggregating heterogeneous data from regional health networks. Agent-based simulations will model family dynamics and caregiving behaviors under varying clinical and socioeconomic scenarios, enabling hypothesis testing for intervention strategies. HPC resources are essential for training deep neural networks on high-resolution temporal health data, running parallelized simulations, and conducting sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include scalable predictive tools to guide family nurse practitioners in personalizing prevention plans, reducing hospital readmissions, and addressing health disparities. The project will also generate open-source computational frameworks to support reproducible research in family nursing, bridging gaps between data-driven methodologies and holistic care practices. By integrating computational innovation with clinical expertise, this work aims to redefine how family nurses leverage large-scale health data to improve outcomes for patients and their families.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: The commercial poultry industry faces persistent challenges in managing infectious diseases that threaten animal welfare, food security, and economic stability. Rapidly evolving pathogens such as avian influenza viruses and multidrug-resistant bacterial strains demand advanced computational tools to predict transmission dynamics, optimize intervention strategies, and mitigate risks. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale epidemiological models integrating genomic, environmental, and husbandry data from commercial poultry operations. The research will employ agent-based modeling frameworks to simulate disease spread within and between flocks under varying biosecurity protocols, vaccination schedules, and environmental conditions. Genomic sequencing data from field isolates will be analyzed using phylogenetic tools to track pathogen evolution and identify emerging virulence or resistance traits. Machine learning pipelines will further assess risk factors associated with disease hotspots by processing heterogeneous datasets, including climate variables, farm geolocations, and livestock movement records. The computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to manage large-scale simulations and genomic alignments, requiring significant memory and GPU resources. Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide real-time surveillance, scenario-based evaluation of containment strategies, and actionable insights into genetic markers linked to disease resilience in poultry. By identifying optimal vaccination timelines and high-risk transmission corridors, this work aims to reduce antibiotic reliance and production losses while informing industry-wide biosecurity standards. The project aligns with clinical veterinary priorities by bridging data-driven decision support with practical interventions, ultimately enhancing the sustainability of poultry health systems. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the resolution and scalability required for these analyses, which traditional computing environments cannot feasibly support.
cip_definition: Research focused on the commercial poultry industry, providing services and technical support pertaining to prevention, diagnosis, and management of disease; epidemiology; genetics; and nutrition.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing public resource allocation in rapidly growing urban environments, where competing demands for infrastructure, social services, and fiscal sustainability strain traditional decision-making frameworks. Municipal governments often rely on static, siloed data and heuristic approaches to allocate budgets and prioritize projects, leading to inefficiencies and inequities in service delivery. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a dynamic computational model integrating high-dimensional datasets—including demographic shifts, real-time service utilization metrics, economic indicators, and geospatial constraints—to simulate the long-term impacts of allocation strategies under uncertainty. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized Monte Carlo simulations that explore thousands of policy scenarios, machine learning algorithms to predict emergent demand patterns, and network analysis tools to evaluate accessibility gaps in public services. By modeling interdependencies between sectors such as transportation, housing, and healthcare, the framework will identify trade-offs and synergies across policy domains. The computational scale required for these analyses exceeds conventional infrastructure due to the need for fine-grained spatial-temporal modeling across multi-terabyte municipal datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for public administrators, empirically grounded benchmarks for equitable resource distribution, and a methodological framework for stress-testing fiscal policies against demographic and economic shocks. This work aims to advance evidence-based governance by enabling data-driven prioritization of public investments while maintaining transparency and accountability—a critical step in addressing trust deficits between communities and institutions. The project’s computational demands necessitate sustained access to HPC resources to achieve the latency tolerance and processing power required for iterative, large-scale policy simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as managers in the executive arm of local, state, and federal government and that focuses on the systematic study of executive organization and management. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a spatially explicit modeling framework to quantify cascading climate risks in urban coastal zones, integrating dynamic interactions between environmental stressors, infrastructure systems, and socioeconomic vulnerability. Rapid urbanization and intensifying climate hazards—particularly compound flooding and extreme heat—are creating novel challenges for coastal communities, yet existing models often treat physical processes and human systems in isolation. Our research addresses this gap through a coupled computational approach combining high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations, satellite-derived land surface temperature analyses, and agent-based representations of adaptive capacity across diverse neighborhoods. The proposed work will leverage GPU-accelerated shallow water equations solvers to model pluvial and tidal flooding at 2m resolution across three major estuarine cities, synchronized with thermal infrared data processing from Sentinel-3 satellites to characterize heat island microclimates. These biophysical outputs will be linked to socioeconomic vulnerability indices through graph neural networks that map accessibility to critical services under disruption scenarios. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing resources for three core tasks: 1) parallelized execution of ensemble flood simulations under multiple precipitation and sea-level rise projections; 2) automated fusion of multi-temporal remote sensing datasets (10TB+) spanning urban morphology and thermal regimes; and 3) graph-based optimization of resilience strategies through Monte Carlo analysis of 10^6 possible intervention combinations. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that identifies neighborhoods at highest risk of climate-driven systemic failures, validated through partnerships with municipal planning agencies. This work advances interdisciplinary geographic research by creating novel methodologies to bridge physical exposure modeling with human vulnerability dynamics at scales directly applicable to urban climate adaptation planning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on interactions between people and the natural and built environments. Includes instruction in climate science, sustainability, environmental science and policy, research methods, geographic information systems (GIS), human geography, physical geography, remote sensing, and public policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing maternal-fetal health outcomes in community-based midwifery care. Despite growing evidence supporting the safety of midwife-led care for low-risk pregnancies, systemic gaps persist in predicting and mitigating risks during natural births, particularly in underserved populations. Current clinical decision-making relies on static risk stratification models that inadequately account for dynamic, patient-specific factors such as maternal biomechanics, real-time fetal positioning, and environmental stressors. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating biomechanical modeling, machine learning, and multi-omics data analysis to predict labor progression and obstetric complications. The research will utilize 3D pelvic floor simulations derived from anonymized MRI datasets and stochastic models of uterine contractility patterns, requiring parallelized processing of terabyte-scale imaging data. Recurrent neural networks will be trained on longitudinal electronic health records from midwifery practices (n≈50,000 births) to identify subtle predictors of dystocia or hemorrhage. Additionally, metagenomic analysis of maternal microbiome samples (n=2,000) will investigate associations between microbial communities and preterm labor risk. The computational intensity of simultaneously running finite element analyses, deep learning workflows, and genome assembly pipelines necessitates HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for personalized birth planning, validated through retrospective clinical data and prospective pilot studies with partnering midwifery clinics. By creating open-source tools for dynamic risk assessment, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based practice in direct-entry midwifery while maintaining its philosophy of low-intervention care. The resource demands reflect the need to process heterogeneous biological, imaging, and clinical data at scales previously unexamined in midwifery research, ultimately bridging computational innovation with equitable perinatal care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide pre-natal, natural birth, and immediate postpartum care to pregnant women in jurisdictions licensing direct (non-nursing) training for midwives. Includes instruction in basic obstetrics, women's health, fetal development, childbirth education, maternal nutrition and health, labor support, natural childbirth, postpartum support, prebirth counseling and risk screening, management of obstetric emergencies, patient referral, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision health initiatives in nursing science by integrating large-scale clinical, genomic, and behavioral datasets. The research problem centers on the limitations of current predictive models for patient outcomes, which often fail to account for the complex, nonlinear interactions between biological, environmental, and social determinants of health. Traditional statistical methods lack the computational power to process high-dimensional data from electronic health records (EHRs), wearable devices, and multi-omics platforms, hindering the development of personalized care strategies. To address this, we propose a machine learning framework optimized for HPC environments to identify dynamic risk profiles and intervention targets for patients with chronic conditions, such as heart failure and diabetes. The computational approach will involve training ensemble models (e.g., gradient-boosted trees, neural networks) on federated EHR data from 10+ healthcare systems, comprising over 2 million patient records, alongside genomic data from linked biobanks. Parallelized workflows will enable real-time feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning, and validation across nested cohorts. Agent-based simulations will further model the impact of nurse-led interventions on long-term health outcomes under varying clinical and socioeconomic scenarios. The anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for early deterioration detection, (2) genomic biomarkers associated with intervention responsiveness, and (3) scalable decision-support tools to guide nurse practitioners in tailoring care plans. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this project aims to overcome computational bottlenecks in multi-modal data integration, directly addressing nursing science’s priority to translate heterogeneous evidence into actionable clinical protocols. The results will provide a foundation for deploying AI-driven precision health frameworks in real-world nursing practice, with potential implications for reducing hospital readmissions, improving patient quality of life, and optimizing resource allocation in complex care systems.
cip_definition: A research program that focuses on the study of advanced clinical practices, research methodologies, the administration of complex nursing services, and that prepares nurses to further the progress of nursing research through experimentation and clinical applications.

abstract: The development of adaptive nanomaterials capable of self-reconfiguration in response to external stimuli requires precise modeling of dynamic nanoscale interfaces, a challenge compounded by the interplay of quantum effects, surface thermodynamics, and mechanical strain. Current computational approaches struggle to resolve these multi-physics phenomena across relevant spatiotemporal scales, particularly for hybrid organic-inorganic nanostructures exhibiting non-equilibrium behavior. This project proposes an integrated computational framework combining reactive molecular dynamics (RMD), time-dependent density functional tight-binding (TD-DFTB), and graph neural networks (GNNs) to simulate stimulus-responsive nanoparticle assemblies. The research focuses on silver-polymer core-shell systems undergoing photoinduced morphological changes, where ligand conformation dynamics and plasmon-exciton coupling must be co-optimized. HPC resources will enable 1) million-atom RMD simulations capturing polymer chain reorganization under thermal/optical stimuli, 2) TD-DFTB calculations of electron transfer processes at metal-polymer interfaces across picosecond timescales, and 3) GNN-based surrogate modeling to accelerate exploration of design parameters. Unique algorithmic developments include a dynamic charge partitioning scheme for interfacial systems and a hybrid continuum-discrete solver for solvent interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking nanoparticle architecture to reconfiguration kinetics, validated against in situ TEM data from collaborators. This work will establish computational protocols for designing next-generation responsive nanomaterials with applications in programmable drug delivery and tunable optical sensors. The resource-intensive nature of simulating coupled electronic-structural dynamics at experimental scales (10-100 nm, 1-100 μs) necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory systems, as traditional cluster architectures cannot efficiently handle the mixed precision requirements and irregular data structures inherent to multi-scale nanomaterial simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, growth, properties, and fundamental interactions of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across scientific disciplines.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address unresolved questions in the interdisciplinary study of classical languages and literatures. The core problem centers on the computational analysis of understudied multilingual textual corpora from the ancient Mediterranean, which include fragmentary inscriptions, papyri, and literary works in Greek, Latin, and select Near Eastern languages. Traditional philological methods struggle to systematically identify patterns in linguistic evolution, cross-cultural semantic shifts, or stylistic features across such fragmented and heterogeneous datasets. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a hybrid computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques, phylogenetic algorithms for language evolution modeling, and network analysis to trace literary influences. Custom pipelines will be developed to preprocess noisy textual data (e.g., OCR outputs from digitized manuscripts), while transformer-based models will be fine-tuned for ancient language tasks, including automated gap-filling in damaged texts and authorship attribution for pseudepigrapha. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of data (estimated 50TB of textual and contextual metadata), the complexity of training multilingual models, and the need for parallelized simulations of language change over millennia. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated texts with cross-referenced linguistic features, 2) quantitative frameworks for evaluating hypotheses about dialectal convergence in Hellenistic-era documents, and 3) novel computational methods tailored to low-resource ancient languages. By bridging computational linguistics and classical philology, this work aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing cultural transmission in antiquity while providing infrastructure for future interdisciplinary research in digital humanities. The requested resources will directly support the first large-scale computational study of its kind in classical multilingualism, with implications for historiography, epigraphy, and the preservation of fragmentary literary heritage.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in classics and classical languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing challenge of analyzing large-scale, multimodal news data in the digital age. Contemporary journalism faces a dual crisis: the rapid proliferation of misinformation and the need to process unprecedented volumes of text, image, and video content across global platforms. Traditional computational tools are insufficient for analyzing terabytes of heterogeneous data, identifying real-time misinformation patterns, or modeling complex information diffusion networks. Our research aims to develop scalable computational frameworks to support investigative journalism, enhance news verification processes, and map the lifecycle of news stories across digital ecosystems. Using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision models, we will automate the detection of semantic inconsistencies in cross-platform news coverage and flag potentially manipulated visual media. Graph-based algorithms will trace information cascades through social networks and news aggregators, while transformer-based models will assess bias and factual accuracy in multilingual contexts. These methods require parallelized processing of petabyte-scale datasets, necessitating HPC infrastructure for distributed training of machine learning models and simulation of network dynamics. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for newsrooms to prioritize fact-checking efforts, empirical insights into misinformation propagation in understudied linguistic regions, and a public dashboard visualizing media credibility metrics. By integrating computational journalism methodologies with HPC capabilities, this work will advance the field’s capacity to uphold ethical reporting standards, mitigate AI-generated disinformation risks, and foster transparency in news ecosystems. The requested resources will directly support graduate student researchers in communication studies and collaborative partnerships with investigative journalism organizations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of gathering, processing, and delivering news and that prepares individuals to be professional print journalists, news editors, and news managers. Includes instruction in news writing and editing; reporting; photojournalism; layout and graphic design; journalism law and policy; professional standards and ethics; research methods; and journalism history and criticism.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and linguistic patterns underlying successful grant proposals, with the aim of developing predictive models to optimize grantsmanship strategies. Despite the critical role of grant funding in sustaining organizations, current approaches to proposal development remain largely anecdotal, relying on subjective expertise rather than data-driven insights. This study addresses this gap by investigating how computational text analysis and machine learning can identify quantifiable features—such as semantic coherence, keyword density, and narrative structure—that correlate with funding success across diverse disciplines. Using a corpus of over 500,000 publicly available grant proposals (funded and unfunded) from federal, corporate, and philanthropic sources, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models (e.g., BERT, GPT variants), to extract syntactic and thematic features. These will be combined with metadata such as funding agency priorities, reviewer demographics, and temporal trends. HPC resources are essential for training multi-modal neural networks capable of processing terabytes of unstructured text while integrating heterogeneous data streams. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate reviewer decision-making dynamics under varying proposal constraints. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating proposal viability, a generative AI tool to assist writers in aligning content with funder expectations, and actionable insights into evolving interdisciplinary funding trends. By bridging computational linguistics and organizational strategy, this work aims to democratize access to funding opportunities, particularly for underrepresented groups and resource-constrained institutions, while advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of data science and philanthropic innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and write grant proposals to support an organization or cause. Includes instruction in identifying grant opportunities, developing an effective proposal, budget justifications, and developing a working relationship with the funder.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of material behaviors, structural optimization, and generative design in traditional and contemporary craft practices. While crafts such as ceramics, textile weaving, and metalworking rely on deeply rooted manual techniques, the integration of computational modeling can address critical challenges in material efficiency, structural integrity, and iterative design exploration. Current limitations in simulating complex material interactions—such as clay shrinkage during firing, stress distribution in woven fabrics, or thermal gradients in glassblowing—hinder the ability to predict outcomes without resource-intensive physical prototyping. This research proposes a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and parametric design tools to model these processes at scale. High-fidelity simulations will analyze material properties under varying conditions, while ML algorithms trained on historical craft datasets will identify patterns in traditional motifs to inform generative design systems. The HPC environment is essential for handling large-scale 3D voxel datasets, real-time multi-physics simulations, and parallel processing of iterative design variants. Outcomes will include predictive models for material deformation, open-access digital tools for artisans to virtually test designs, and a repository of algorithmically generated patterns rooted in cultural heritage. By bridging computational precision with artisanal knowledge, this work aims to reduce material waste, preserve endangered craft techniques through digital archiving, and expand creative possibilities for hybrid analog-digital craftsmanship. The project underscores the transformative role of HPC in sustaining craft traditions while fostering innovation at the intersection of art, technology, and cultural preservation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Crafts/ Craft Design, Folk Art and Artisanry
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the aesthetics, techniques, and creative processes for designing and fashioning objects in one or more of the handcraft or folk art traditions, and that prepares individuals to create in any of these media.

abstract: Infectious diseases caused by microbial pathogens remain a critical global health challenge, exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance and the emergence of novel pathogens. Current methods for isolating and identifying causative agents often rely on culture-based techniques or targeted molecular assays, which can be slow, biased toward known taxa, or insufficiently resolved for strain-level characterization. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance metagenomic pathogen detection and genomic epidemiology workflows, enabling rapid, unbiased identification of microbial agents directly from clinical samples. The proposed research integrates large-scale sequencing datasets from patient specimens (e.g., blood, sputum, tissue biopsies) with advanced computational methods, including de novo assembly of fragmented microbial genomes, machine learning-based taxonomic classification, and phylogenetic reconstruction of virulence or resistance determinants. A key focus is optimizing algorithms to disentangle host-pathogen genomic signals in complex samples, particularly for low-abundance pathogens or co-infections. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce processing times from days to hours while improving sensitivity for detecting emerging fungal species, fastidious bacteria, and highly divergent viral strains. Additionally, we will model pathogen evolutionary dynamics using agent-based simulations to predict resistance gene dissemination patterns in hospital environments. The computational infrastructure will support the analysis of over 50,000 microbial genomes and 10,000 clinical metagenomes, with validation against gold-standard clinical microbiology results. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source pipelines for real-time pathogen characterization in clinical settings, (2) high-resolution maps of antimicrobial resistance gene distribution across microbial taxa and geographic regions, and (3) predictive frameworks for outbreak strain behavior. This work will directly enhance diagnostic precision, inform empirical treatment guidelines, and provide a scalable computational foundation for responding to future infectious disease threats.
cip_definition: Research focused on the isolation and identification of microbial agents that cause infectious disease, including viruses, bacteria, fungi, and parasites.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the bidirectional interactions between chronic stress-induced neuroinflammation and maladaptive decision-making behaviors, integrating computational neuroscience, immunology, and behavioral psychology. While the role of inflammatory markers in mood disorders is well-documented, the mechanistic links between real-time glial cell signaling, neural circuit dynamics, and persistent risky behavioral patterns remain poorly understood—a gap requiring multiscale modeling approaches. We propose to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining 1) agent-based simulations of microglial activation and cytokine diffusion across blood-brain barrier interfaces, 2) dynamic network models of prefrontal-limbic system interactions during decision-making tasks, and 3) machine learning analysis of longitudinal behavioral datasets from stress-primed rodent models. The computational pipeline will utilize GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods to model neuroinflammatory cascades at micrometer resolution while concurrently simulating population-level neural activity through adaptive Hodgkin-Huxley neural networks. By parameterizing models with in vivo cytokine measurements and single-unit electrophysiology data, we aim to identify critical thresholds where localized inflammation disrupts cost-benefit valuation circuits. Expected outcomes include a predictive model of stress-induced behavioral dysfunction that maps temporal patterns of astrocyte signaling to specific decision-making pathologies, potentially revealing novel targets for circuit-based neuromodulation therapies. This interdisciplinary approach requires HPC resources to manage the integration of stochastic molecular-scale simulations (10^6 agents) with whole-brain network models (10^4 neurons) across biologically relevant timescales—a computational challenge unfeasible without parallelized architecture. Results will advance biopsychological understanding of how neuroimmune interactions translate molecular events into sustained cognitive-behavioral phenotypes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological and psychological linkages, especially the linkages between biochemical and biophysical activity and the functioning of the central nervous system.

abstract: Hemodialysis treatment efficacy is critically dependent on the precise calibration of operational parameters, including dialysate composition, blood flow rates, and session duration, which must account for dynamic patient-specific physiological factors. However, current clinical practices often rely on generalized protocols, leading to suboptimal outcomes such as intradialytic complications, electrolyte imbalances, and variable toxin clearance efficiency. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing predictive computational models to optimize hemodialysis parameter personalization using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate multi-scale physiological simulations, incorporating cardiovascular dynamics, solute transport kinetics, and fluid-electrolyte homeostasis to replicate patient responses during dialysis. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on retrospective clinical data—including patient vital signs, biochemical profiles, and dialysis machine telemetry—to identify patterns linking parameter adjustments to outcomes. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of model iterations, sensitivity analyses to quantify uncertainty in physiological inputs, and real-time optimization of treatment variables under simulated scenarios. Validation will involve comparing model predictions to prospective clinical data from partnering dialysis centers. The anticipated outcomes include a framework for generating patient-specific treatment profiles that minimize adverse events while maximizing metabolic waste clearance. This work aims to provide dialysis technologists with an evidence-based decision-support tool to refine treatment delivery, reducing trial-and-error adjustments in clinical practice. Additionally, the computational models will be adapted into interactive training modules for dialysis technologist students, enhancing their understanding of parameter interdependencies. By bridging computational innovation with clinical training, this project aligns with the program’s focus on advancing technical proficiency and ethical care standards in renal replacement therapy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer hemodialysis treatments to patients with renal failure under the supervision of a nurse or physician. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, dialysis prescription interpretation, dialysate preparation, extracorporeal circuit and dialyzer set-up and maintenance, equipment monitoring, patient preparation, taking vital signs, documentation and communication, venipuncture and local anesthesia administration, emergency intervention, safety and sanitation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Norwegian language and dialectology, addressing critical gaps in the analysis of regional linguistic variation and historical language change. Despite Norway’s rich dialectal diversity, large-scale quantitative studies remain limited due to the computational demands of processing heterogeneous speech corpora, textual archives, and sociolinguistic metadata. This research will develop and apply machine learning models to classify dialect features across spoken and written datasets, including digitized historical texts, modern speech recordings, and crowdsourced dialect samples. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for dialect identification, implementing phonetic alignment algorithms to map sound shifts, and conducting network analysis to trace the diffusion of grammatical innovations. The scale of data—spanning over 10 TB of audio, text, and annotated linguistic features—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which are infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for Norwegian dialect analysis, novel insights into the dynamics of language contact and standardization, and high-resolution visualizations of dialect boundaries. These results will directly inform scholarly debates on language preservation and identity while supporting practical applications in speech technology, such as improving automatic speech recognition for underrepresented dialects. By integrating computational methods with traditional philological expertise, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven research in Norwegian linguistics, with methodological frameworks adaptable to other minority languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Norwegian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic evolution of family systems under external socioeconomic stressors using computational agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis. While family dynamics have traditionally been studied through qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods, the complexity of multi-generational interactions, coupled with variable environmental pressures, demands a scalable computational framework to simulate emergent behaviors and systemic resilience. The research problem centers on identifying critical thresholds in family cohesion and resource-sharing patterns when subjected to simulated stressors such as unemployment shocks, migration events, or intergenerational caregiving demands. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose to develop a modular ABM platform that integrates demographic data, psychological trait distributions, and culturally specific kinship norms to model family units as adaptive networks. The computational approach will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore parameter spaces encompassing diverse family structures (nuclear, extended, chosen families) and stressor combinations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to classify emergent stability profiles and predict cascading effects of interventions. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating family system dynamics at population scales, 2) quantitative evidence linking specific communication patterns and resource allocation strategies to long-term family resilience, and 3) policy-relevant insights into how institutional support systems might proactively address vulnerability thresholds identified through simulation. By bridging computational social science with family systems theory, this work aims to establish a methodological foundation for studying relational ecosystems through data-driven simulation while adhering to ethical AI guidelines for sensitive human behavior modeling. The requested computing resources will enable the handling of complex adaptive systems with over 10^6 agent interactions per simulation cycle, a scale necessary to capture rare but consequential systemic transitions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the family as a social unit in its developmental, dynamic, comparative, and structural aspects, and the significance of the family as a system that impacts individuals and society. Includes instruction in related principles of sociology, psychology, behavioral sciences, and the humanities.

abstract: Turfgrass systems are critical components of agricultural and recreational landscapes, yet their sustainability is increasingly threatened by climate variability, urbanization pressures, and evolving biotic stressors. Traditional approaches to turfgrass breeding and management often lack the resolution to predict genotype-environment interactions under dynamic stress conditions, limiting the development of resilient cultivars and adaptive management strategies. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance genomic and ecological modeling efforts aimed at optimizing turfgrass selection, growth, and stress mitigation. Using whole-genome sequencing data from diverse turfgrass populations, we will perform genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify genetic markers linked to drought tolerance, disease resistance, and nutrient-use efficiency. Concurrently, we will develop agent-based models to simulate turfgrass establishment and persistence across heterogeneous soil and microclimate conditions, integrating real-world environmental data from agricultural extension networks. Machine learning pipelines will analyze multi-omics datasets (transcriptomics, metabolomics) to predict trait expression under projected climate scenarios. The computational scale of these tasks—including the alignment of terabase-scale sequencing reads, Bayesian inference of genotype-phenotype-environment relationships, and high-resolution spatial modeling—necessitates access to parallelized computing architectures and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of candidate genes for breeding programs targeting climate-resilient turfgrasses, (2) data-driven recommendations for site-specific turfgrass selection and management, and (3) open-source computational workflows to accelerate turfgrass research. By bridging genomic insights with landscape-scale ecological modeling, this work will provide actionable strategies to reduce water, pesticide, and fertilizer inputs in turf systems while maintaining functional and aesthetic value—a critical need for agricultural stakeholders and urban planners managing green spaces under resource constraints.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on turfgrasses and related groundcover plants and prepares individuals to develop ornamental or recreational grasses and related products; plant, transplant, and manage grassed areas; and to produce and store turf used for transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable plant sciences, genetics of grasses, turf science, use analysis, turf management, and related economics.

abstract: The built environment faces growing challenges in energy efficiency, operational cost reduction, and system reliability, driven by aging infrastructure and increasing demands for sustainability. Current approaches to building maintenance often rely on reactive or rule-based strategies, which inadequately address the dynamic interactions between mechanical systems (e.g., HVAC, plumbing), environmental conditions, and occupancy patterns. This project proposes a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance and energy management in mixed-use buildings through high-fidelity simulations and machine learning. The research will develop multi-physics models of integrated building systems, coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for HVAC performance analysis, finite element methods for structural wear prediction, and graph neural networks to map interdependencies among electrical, plumbing, and appliance systems. A key innovation involves training physics-informed machine learning models on synthetic data generated from parametric simulations of fault scenarios, including pipe corrosion, refrigerant leaks, and electrical load imbalances. These models will be validated against real-world sensor data from partner facilities. The computational intensity of simultaneously simulating building-scale systems at fine spatiotemporal resolutions—particularly when accounting for stochastic occupancy behaviors and climate variability—necessitates high-performance computing resources. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for CFD workloads and distributed memory clusters for ensemble simulations exploring maintenance intervention strategies across 10,000+ parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include (1) a digital twin platform for scenario-based maintenance planning, (2) adaptive control algorithms that reduce energy waste from suboptimal system interactions by 15–25%, and (3) failure prediction models with 72-hour advance warning capabilities for critical components. By transforming maintenance from schedule-driven to system-aware decision-making, this work aims to establish new computational paradigms for intelligent building operations that balance cost, comfort, and carbon footprint. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits tailored for facility management education programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to keep a building functioning, and to service a variety of structures including commercial and industrial buildings and mobile homes. Includes instruction in the basic maintenance and repair skills required to service building systems, such as air conditioning, heating, plumbing, electrical, major appliances, and other mechanical systems.

abstract: Montessori pedagogy emphasizes individualized, self-directed learning within prepared environments, yet the dynamic interplay between student behaviors, environmental design, and learning outcomes remains underexplored at scale. This project seeks to computationally model Montessori classroom interactions to identify patterns that optimize student engagement and skill development. The research problem centers on analyzing how variations in material sequencing, instructor interventions, and peer dynamics influence learning trajectories across diverse student profiles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate complex, multi-agent classroom environments and process longitudinal datasets of observed student activities. Agent-based modeling will be used to represent students as autonomous agents with parameterized learning styles, while reinforcement learning frameworks will simulate instructor decisions in response to agent behaviors. The models will integrate empirical data from anonymized classroom observations (e.g., material selection frequencies, task completion times) collected from Montessori training centers. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about critical thresholds in environmental design, such as the balance between structured guidance and independent exploration. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for tailoring material rotations and instructor scaffolding strategies, as well as visualizations of emergent learning patterns under different pedagogical conditions. These results will directly inform the development of adaptive training modules for Montessori educators, providing quantitative insights to complement qualitative pedagogical training. By bridging computational analysis with Montessori principles, this work aims to establish a novel framework for evidence-based teacher education that preserves the method’s humanistic ethos while enhancing its reproducibility across educational contexts. The requested HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of large-scale simulations and machine learning workflows that cannot feasibly run on local infrastructure, ensuring statistically robust conclusions from high-dimensional educational data.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Maria Montessori and her followers.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a machine learning (ML) framework to optimize personalized learning strategies for elementary-aged students in special education programs. Students in these programs exhibit diverse cognitive, behavioral, and sensory needs, yet teachers often lack tools to rapidly analyze multimodal data (e.g., academic performance logs, behavioral observations, sensor-based engagement metrics) and adapt instruction in real time. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating computational models that identify patterns in student responses to instructional methods, predict individualized learning trajectories, and recommend targeted interventions. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate deep neural networks on large-scale, de-identified datasets spanning 5,000+ students from collaborating K-6 special education programs. These datasets include structured records (e.g., IEP goals, assessment scores) and unstructured inputs (e.g., teacher notes, speech samples, wearable device outputs). Computational methods will integrate natural language processing to analyze qualitative feedback, computer vision techniques to assess engagement from video recordings, and reinforcement learning to simulate intervention outcomes. HPC capabilities are critical for processing heterogeneous data at scale, running parallelized hyperparameter tuning for multi-modal model architectures, and conducting sensitivity analyses across diverse student subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source ML toolkit that helps teachers prioritize IEP objectives, predict skill acquisition rates, and allocate instructional time more effectively. By quantifying relationships between pedagogical strategies and student progress, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in special education while maintaining strict ethical standards for data privacy and algorithmic transparency.
