The resulting models could reduce the trial-and-error period for identifying effective interventions, directly supporting the dual mandate of special education: equitable access and individualized growth.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Elementary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the elementary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for elementary special education; and teaching elementary education subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize safety and efficacy in patient handling practices by health aides and attendants through advanced biomechanical modeling and machine learning. Despite being critical to patient care, routine tasks such as transfers, repositioning, and mobility assistance lack evidence-based, personalized protocols, contributing to high rates of musculoskeletal injuries among caregivers and suboptimal patient outcomes. Current guidelines rely on static risk assessments that fail to account for dynamic variables such as patient-specific biomechanics, real-time fatigue metrics, or environmental constraints. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating wearable sensor data, 3D motion capture, and patient-specific digital twin simulations to model biomechanical stress during caregiving tasks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of diverse handling scenarios, incorporating variables such as patient body composition, caregiver ergonomic patterns, and adaptive assistive devices. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulated and empirical datasets to identify risk-minimizing techniques and generate predictive models for injury prevention. The project will also develop a real-time feedback system prototype to guide caregivers via augmented reality interfaces during complex maneuvers. Outcomes include open-access datasets of biomechanical interactions, validated computational models for training program design, and a proof-of-concept adaptive guidance tool. This work bridges gaps between rehabilitation science, occupational biomechanics, and human-computer interaction, offering translational insights to improve safety standards in an understudied yet essential healthcare workforce. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process multimodal sensor data and simulate high-resolution dynamic interactions, the project advances precision approaches to caregiver training and patient handling protocols.
cip_definition: Any other instructional program that prepares individuals to provide routine patient care and assistance.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-national policy diffusion and institutional adaptation using advanced computational modeling. The research problem centers on understanding how heterogeneous political systems adopt or resist policy innovations in interconnected governance environments. Traditional comparative methods struggle to account for the multi-scalar interactions between domestic institutions, transnational networks, and global shocks. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating policy transfer processes across 200+ national and subnational entities over a 50-year timeline. The computational framework will integrate historical institutional data (from sources like the Varieties of Democracy Project and Comparative Constitutions Project) with dynamic network analyses of international organizations and epistemic communities. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) running ensemble simulations to test competing theories of policy contagion under alternative global scenarios, (2) processing natural language corpora of legislative texts to parameterize institutional learning mechanisms, and (3) conducting sensitivity analyses across 10^6+ parameter combinations using Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in policy adoption cascades, quantifying the relative impact of democratic vs. authoritarian governance structures on innovation resistance, and generating predictive metrics for institutional vulnerability to ideological shocks. The resulting models will provide novel insights into the computational political economy of globalization while advancing methodological integration between complexity science and comparative politics. By enabling simultaneous analysis of micro-level decision-making and macro-level systemic effects at unprecedented scale, this work addresses fundamental questions about political system resilience in an era of increasing transnational interdependence.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in political science and government, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the therapeutic impacts of structured arts interventions on chronic pain management through computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. Chronic pain, a complex biopsychosocial condition, often resists conventional treatment, yet emerging evidence suggests arts-based therapies may modulate pain perception through neurocognitive and community-based pathways. However, the mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly characterized due to the multidimensional nature of arts-health interactions. We propose to develop machine learning models integrating heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, biometric sensor data from wearable devices during arts sessions, and qualitative narratives from participatory theater workshops—to identify patterns linking specific artistic modalities to measurable health outcomes. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing multimodal data streams (e.g., motion-capture video analysis of dance therapy sessions, natural language processing of patient journals) and training neural networks to detect subtle correlations across biological, behavioral, and social domains. The computational pipeline will employ federated learning techniques to preserve participant confidentiality while analyzing sensitive health data from five clinical partner sites. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for personalizing arts interventions based on individual neurophysiological profiles and social determinants of health, as well as agent-based models simulating community-level impacts of arts programming on healthcare utilization. This work will advance evidence-based design of arts-in-medicine initiatives while establishing scalable computational methods for studying complex arts-health ecosystems. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data storage for longitudinal analyses, and virtual reality simulations of therapeutic arts environments. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for arts-health researchers and clinical guidelines for implementing data-driven arts interventions in diverse care settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of programs that use the visual and performing arts in support of health and wellness among diverse individuals and communities. Includes instruction in dance, literary arts, music, theatre, healthcare systems, program administration, and public health.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance French language teacher training through computational modeling of second language acquisition (SLA) processes, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, interactional classroom datasets. A critical challenge in French language teacher education is the limited empirical basis for understanding how novice instructors adapt pedagogical strategies to diverse learner profiles in real time. Traditional observational methods lack the granularity to model dynamic factors such as error correction efficiency, metalinguistic feedback timing, or the interplay of phonological, syntactic, and sociolinguistic competencies in classroom interactions. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate teacher-student discourse patterns, informed by multimodal data from francophone immersion classrooms (audio, video, and written productions). These ABMs will integrate psycholinguistic theories of SLA with empirical datasets from intermediate-level French learners, processed through natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for HPC parallelization. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models on error-annotated learner corpora to predict intervention points, and simulating the longitudinal impacts of pedagogical decisions on language development trajectories. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of virtual classroom configurations, testing hypotheses about optimal feedback mechanisms and curriculum sequencing. Expected outcomes include a framework for data-driven teacher training modules that visualize the cascading effects of instructional choices, as well as open-source tools for analyzing French learner interlanguage development. By bridging computational linguistics with teacher education, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for cultivating adaptive teaching competencies in French language educators, ultimately improving the quality of francophone language instruction across secondary and postsecondary contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach French language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modeling large-scale socioecological systems under climate change necessitates advanced computational resources to address critical gaps in conservation planning. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, spatially explicit framework to simulate dynamic interactions between biodiversity, ecosystem services, and anthropogenic pressures across heterogeneous landscapes. Current models often lack the granularity to capture non-linear feedbacks between species migration patterns, habitat fragmentation, and shifting climate regimes at ecologically relevant scales. To overcome these limitations, we propose implementing an agent-based modeling (ABM) system integrated with machine learning-driven climate projections and real-time remote sensing data. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning 40 years of biodiversity records, LiDAR-derived topography, and IPCC AR6 climate scenarios at 1km² resolution. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess probabilistic outcomes of conservation interventions under 8 warming trajectories, while graph-theoretic analyses will quantify connectivity resilience in protected area networks. Memory-intensive tasks, including 4D visualization of trophic cascades and hydrological shifts, require node configurations with ≥512GB RAM and GPU acceleration for deep learning submodules. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of climate refugia for endangered species in understudied biomes, (2) optimization algorithms for corridor design in fragmented landscapes, and (3) uncertainty-quantified projections of ecosystem service provision through 2100. Results will directly inform adaptive management strategies for three UN-recognized biodiversity hotspots facing imminent hydrological stress. By overcoming current hardware constraints on model complexity and spatial-temporal scope, this work advances predictive capacity in conservation decision-making while establishing a replicable computational architecture for coupled human-natural systems analysis. All models and workflows will be containerized for public access through an NSF-funded repository.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing volume and heterogeneity of clinical data present significant challenges in extracting actionable insights to improve patient care. Current analytical approaches often struggle with the scale and complexity of integrating multimodal data sources, including electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and genomic data. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable computational frameworks for clinical informatics research. Our primary objectives are to create integrated data pipelines that harmonize diverse data types and to build predictive models capable of supporting real-time clinical decision-making. The computational approach involves the deployment of distributed machine learning algorithms optimized for HPC environments, enabling efficient processing of large-scale datasets. Techniques such as natural language processing (NLP) will be applied to unstructured clinical notes, while deep learning models will analyze medical images and genomic sequences. Additionally, we will implement federated learning architectures to facilitate multi-institutional collaborations without compromising data privacy. The expected outcomes include the development of robust predictive tools for early disease detection, personalized treatment recommendations, and enhanced interoperability across healthcare systems. By utilizing HPC resources, this research aims to overcome existing computational barriers, thereby accelerating the translation of complex clinical data into meaningful improvements in patient outcomes and healthcare delivery. The proposed work underscores the critical role of advanced computing infrastructure in advancing clinical informatics and addressing pressing challenges in modern healthcare.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Informatics

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for simulating multi-physics systems governed by coupled nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), with applications to geophysical flows and additive manufacturing processes. These systems involve complex interactions between fluid dynamics, thermal transport, and material phase transitions, posing significant challenges due to their high dimensionality, stiff nonlinearities, and disparate temporal/spatial scales. Traditional solvers struggle with computational efficiency and stability when applied to such problems, particularly at industrially relevant scales. To address this, we propose a hybrid finite element/discrete element framework that combines adaptive mesh refinement, implicit-explicit time-stepping schemes, and reduced-order modeling techniques. The core computational challenges include resolving localized phenomena (e.g., melt pool dynamics in metal 3D printing) while maintaining global solution accuracy, as well as managing data dependencies in distributed-memory architectures. Our approach leverages recent advances in matrix-free iterative solvers and GPU-accelerated linear algebra libraries to optimize memory usage and parallel scalability. We will validate the methods against experimental datasets from collaborating partners in geothermal energy and advanced manufacturing, focusing on error quantification and convergence under mesh adaptation. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable large-scale weak and strong scaling studies of our algorithms on heterogeneous architectures, with target problem sizes exceeding 10^8 degrees of freedom. Successful implementation will provide open-source tools for the applied mathematics community, significantly reducing computational expense for multiphase simulations while improving predictive accuracy. Outcomes will directly inform the design of next-generation additive manufacturing protocols and subsurface energy extraction systems, bridging critical gaps between theoretical models and engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of a broad range of mathematical and computational methods to modeling, analysis, algorithm development, and simulation for the solution of complex scientific and engineering problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, discrete mathematics, operations research, optimization, differential equations, statistics, scientific computation, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: Maternal and child health outcomes are shaped by complex interactions between biological, social, and environmental determinants, yet existing models often fail to capture these multidimensional relationships at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large, integrated datasets spanning clinical records, socioeconomic indicators, environmental exposures, and public health program participation across diverse populations. The research will develop computational models to identify critical risk factors for adverse pregnancy outcomes, childhood chronic conditions, and disparities in healthcare access. Using machine learning algorithms optimized for HPC environments, including ensemble methods and neural networks, we will analyze longitudinal data from 2.5 million maternal-child dyads across five U.S. regions. These analyses will be coupled with agent-based simulations to model the population-level impacts of proposed interventions, such as nutritional support programs or prenatal care policy changes. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to manage high-dimensional data integration, real-time geospatial mapping of health resource availability, and sensitivity analyses across simulated scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize high-risk populations, evidence-based frameworks for tailoring community health initiatives, and policy simulations quantifying the potential health equity impacts of legislative proposals. By elucidating how structural determinants interact with biological factors, this work will provide novel insights for reducing perinatal mortality, addressing childhood obesity disparities, and optimizing resource allocation in public health systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale health data while maintaining privacy-preserving federated learning architectures across institutional partners. This project directly aligns with national maternal health equity goals and advances computational methodologies for translational public health research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between geopolitical risk factors and global supply chain resilience, with a focus on emerging trade corridors in underrepresented regions. Traditional international business models often fail to account for the nonlinear, cascading disruptions caused by geopolitical shocks (e.g., sanctions, trade wars, or regulatory fragmentation) interacting with climate-driven logistical bottlenecks. The computational challenge lies in simulating multi-agent systems that integrate real-time trade data, corporate decision-making algorithms, and stochastic environmental variables across heterogeneous regulatory environments. Using an adaptive agent-based modeling framework, the project will simulate 10,000+ node supply networks across Southeast Asia and East Africa, incorporating granular data on port capacities, trade agreement compliance costs, and political risk indicators. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical disruption datasets to parameterize firm-level adaptation strategies, while Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes under varying crisis scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of cross-border interactions, enabling parallel processing of terabyte-scale trade flow datasets and near-real-time scenario testing. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for businesses operating in volatile markets, predictive metrics for systemic supply chain fragility, and policy recommendations for multilateral trade institutions addressing resilience gaps. This work bridges computational social science, environmental economics, and trade analytics, advancing methodological innovation in international business research while addressing urgent practical challenges in sustainable commerce.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international businesses and/or business operations. Includes instruction in the principles and processes of export sales, trade controls, foreign operations and related problems, monetary issues, international business policy, and applications to doing business in specific countries and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic decision-making processes in multi-agent environments, a core challenge in experimental psychology. Traditional behavioral experiments often simplify real-world complexity to maintain analytical tractability, limiting ecological validity. To address this gap, we propose large-scale computational simulations of interactive learning scenarios involving hundreds of autonomous agents operating under evolving reward structures. The research problem centers on identifying how decentralized cognitive systems self-organize behavioral strategies when individual learning algorithms (e.g., temporal difference learning) interact with social information networks. Computational demands arise from the need to model high-dimensional parameter spaces across nested timescales, including real-time reinforcement learning at the agent level and emergent group dynamics at the system level. Our approach combines parallelized agent-based modeling with Bayesian optimization techniques to efficiently explore parameter interactions, supplemented by neural network approximations for predicting phase transitions in collective behavior. The HPC infrastructure will enable simultaneous execution of 10,000+ experimental conditions, each simulating 300 agents across 50,000 decision trials, generating petabyte-scale behavioral trajectory data. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for mapping individual cognitive constraints to population-level behavioral patterns, (2) empirically testable hypotheses about resource allocation in human group decision-making, and (3) open-source tools for scalable behavioral simulation. Results will directly inform experimental designs for laboratory studies of cooperative problem-solving while advancing methodological integration between cognitive modeling and complex systems theory. By characterizing how decentralized cognitive systems balance exploration-exploitation tradeoffs under variable environmental pressures, this work aims to establish foundational principles for adaptive behavior in uncertain social ecologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of behavior under experimental conditions and the analysis of controlled behavioral responses. Includes instruction in learning theory, research design and experimental methods, psychological measurement, statistical design and methods, analysis of cognitive and behavioral variables, and the conduct of specialized and large-scale studies.

abstract: The rapid expansion of online education necessitates evidence-based frameworks to optimize pedagogical strategies and adaptive learning environments. However, current approaches to personalizing instruction in digital settings often rely on static, coarse-grained data, limiting their capacity to address the dynamic, multifaceted needs of diverse learners in real time. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models that leverage high-frequency, multimodal data from online learning platforms—including interaction logs, video analytics, and formative assessment performance—to dynamically predict learner engagement and tailor instructional interventions. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale datasets from three semesters of asynchronous and synchronous online courses (n ≈ 4,500 students) while preserving participant anonymity through federated learning architectures. Computational methods will integrate deep reinforcement learning to simulate student decision-making pathways, natural language processing to analyze discussion forum interactions, and graph neural networks to model social learning dynamics. These techniques will enable real-time identification of pedagogical “tipping points,” such as moments when learners require scaffolded support or collaborative opportunities. The resulting models will be validated through A/B testing of adaptive course modules in a controlled virtual learning environment. By quantifying relationships between instructional design choices, technological affordances, and learning outcomes at scale, this work aims to produce actionable insights for educators seeking to implement responsive, equitable online teaching practices. The project’s computational outputs—including open-source tools for real-time classroom analytics—will directly address critical challenges in online teacher education, particularly the need for empirically grounded training in data-driven instructional adaptation. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible benchmark dataset for the educational computing community and evidence-based guidelines for integrating predictive analytics into graduate-level online teaching curricula.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various academic levels through online instructional technologies. Includes instruction in andragogy, pedagogy, assessment, instructional design and technology, and learning science.

abstract: The increasing complexity of toxicological exposures—spanning novel synthetic drugs, environmental contaminants, and mass casualty threats—demands advanced computational tools to predict toxicity mechanisms, optimize treatments, and mitigate public health risks. Current clinical approaches rely heavily on observational data and animal models, which lack the resolution to address heterogeneous patient responses or rapidly evolving exposure scenarios. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model toxin-receptor interactions, predict patient-specific outcomes, and guide antidote development. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train deep neural networks on multi-modal datasets (electronic health records, toxicogenomics databases, and structural biology repositories) to identify biomarkers of severe poisoning and simulate time-dependent toxin pharmacokinetics. Large-scale MD simulations will characterize binding affinities of emerging synthetic opioids, nanoparticles, and biotoxins to critical physiological targets (e.g., mu-opioid receptors, ion channels), enabling in silico screening of antidote candidates. A parallelized systems biology model will map population-level exposure risks by analyzing geospatial, socio-economic, and clinical data to forecast toxicity hotspots. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling petabyte-scale data, running iterative simulations across parameter spaces, and optimizing ML architectures via hyperparameter tuning. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking toxin structures to clinical severity, (2) actionable protocols for personalized antidote dosing, and (3) a risk stratification toolkit for preemptive resource allocation during toxicological emergencies. This work will directly enhance the precision and scalability of medical toxicology practice, offering clinically validated tools to address acute poisoning crises, chemical terrorism events, and environmental exposure disparities.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians who specialize in the prevention, evaluation, treatment, and monitoring of injury and illness from exposures to drugs and chemicals, as well as exposures to biological and radiological agents. Important areas include acute drug poisoning; adverse drug events; drug abuse, addiction, and withdrawal; chemicals and hazardous materials; terrorism preparedness; venomous bites and stings; and environmental and workplace exposures.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the modeling and optimization of urban infrastructure resilience under climate-driven stressors using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Aging transportation networks, water distribution systems, and flood mitigation structures face increasing risks from extreme weather events, yet existing simulation tools struggle to integrate multi-physics interactions at city scales. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework coupling finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity, hydrodynamic models for flood propagation, and machine learning (ML)-based surrogate models to accelerate scenario testing. The research will develop parallelized workflows using open-source codes (e.g., OpenFOAM, SWMM) enhanced with graph neural networks to capture interdependencies between infrastructure components. Key challenges include resolving spatiotemporal conflicts between millimeter-scale material degradation processes and kilometer-scale urban hydrological systems while maintaining computational feasibility. HPC resources will enable parametric studies of 10,000+ stormwater management scenarios, optimizing green-gray infrastructure retrofits under probabilistic precipitation forecasts. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin prototype for mid-sized cities, reduced-order models for rapid risk assessment, and open-access datasets quantifying failure cascades across transportation and water networks. This work directly supports climate adaptation planning by providing engineers and policymakers with scalable tools to prioritize investments in critical infrastructure hardening. The requested computing allocations will allow unprecedented resolution in simulating coupled hydraulic-structural systems, overcoming memory and runtime barriers that currently limit conventional single-node simulations.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of vocal physiology and performance optimization through computational modeling and machine learning. While traditional voice pedagogy relies on subjective feedback and empirical methods, the complex biomechanical interactions underlying vocal production—such as airflow dynamics, tissue vibration, and acoustic resonance—remain inadequately quantified. This gap limits the ability to predict vocal strain, optimize technique, or personalize training for diverse repertoires. Our research aims to develop a multi-scale computational framework that simulates the human vocal system under varying performance conditions, integrating physiological data from laryngeal imaging, motion capture, and acoustic recordings. High-fidelity fluid-structure interaction models will replicate airflow through the glottis and supraglottal tract during phonation, while neural networks trained on performance datasets (e.g., operatic vibrato, dynamic articulation) will map physiological parameters to perceptual qualities like timbre and projection. The computational intensity of coupling finite element analysis with real-time acoustic propagation models necessitates HPC resources for parallelized simulations and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to assess vocal load thresholds, identify injury risks in demanding roles, and generate feedback protocols for technical refinement. By bridging computational biomechanics and artistic practice, this work will provide evidence-based strategies for vocal health, expand pedagogical frameworks, and enhance interpretive flexibility in performance. The proposed models will also establish a foundation for future interdisciplinary studies in computational arts, enabling data-driven innovations in repertoire selection and expressive movement analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the human voice and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers in concert, choir, opera, or other forms of singing. Includes instruction in voice pedagogy, diction, vocal physiology and exercise, expressive movement, repertoire, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing resource allocation strategies in non-profit and public organizations facing dynamic operational constraints. Non-profit entities must balance competing priorities—such as program impact, financial sustainability, and regulatory compliance—under conditions of uncertainty, including fluctuating donor funding, shifting policy environments, and heterogeneous stakeholder demands. Traditional decision-making models often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these variables, leading to suboptimal resource distribution. To address this gap, we propose a multi-method computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM), Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning-driven scenario analysis. The ABM component will simulate interactions between stakeholders (e.g., donors, beneficiaries, regulatory bodies) to identify emergent patterns in resource utilization, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify risks associated with budget volatility and external shocks. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical organizational data to predict outcomes of alternative allocation strategies. The computational intensity of simultaneously modeling thousands of interacting agents, probabilistic scenarios, and high-dimensional datasets necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve tractable runtime. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolkit for non-profits to evaluate allocation trade-offs in real time, improve long-term resilience, and align resource decisions with mission-critical goals. This project will also generate novel insights into the interplay between organizational governance structures and computational decision-support systems, with implications for public policy and cross-sector collaboration. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with management theory, the research aims to advance evidence-based practices in non-profit leadership while contributing methodological innovations to computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the business affairs of non-profit corporations, including foundations, educational institutions, associations, and other such organizations, and public agencies and governmental operations. Includes instruction in business management, principles of public administration, principles of accounting and financial management, human resources management, taxation of non-profit organizations, and business law as applied to non-profit organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in early childhood pedagogical optimization through large-scale analysis of multimodal learning interactions in preschool classrooms. The core research problem centers on identifying effective, individualized teaching strategies for diverse learners aged 3-6 years by analyzing complex patterns in teacher-student engagement, behavioral responses, and learning outcome correlations. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the scope of analysis to small datasets using conventional methods, leaving critical gaps in understanding how dynamic classroom interactions influence foundational skill development. To address this, we propose implementing machine learning models on HPC clusters to process and correlate longitudinal datasets encompassing video recordings of classroom activities (annotated for verbal/nonverbal communication), standardized developmental assessments, and biometric sensor data tracking attention patterns. Computational workflows will integrate computer vision for automated behavior coding, natural language processing of teacher-student dialogues, and multilevel regression analyses to model how micro-level interaction sequences predict macro-level skill acquisition in literacy, numeracy, and socioemotional domains. The HPC environment is essential for training transformer-based architectures on over 10,000 hours of classroom video while maintaining temporal resolution critical for analyzing moment-to-moment learning processes. Expected outcomes include 1) evidence-based frameworks for optimizing instructional timing and modality selection based on child-specific developmental trajectories, 2) predictive tools to guide adaptive lesson planning, and 3) open-source computational models for analyzing classroom interaction dynamics. By enabling large-scale pattern recognition across heterogeneous datastreams, this work aims to transform empirical foundations for personalized early childhood pedagogy while establishing computational methods tailored to education research in teacher preparation programs.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in formal settings prior to beginning regular elementary school, usually ranging in age from three to six years (or grade one), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for detecting subtle cardiac arrhythmias in high-resolution electrocardiograph (ECG) datasets. Traditional arrhythmia classification systems, while effective for common rhythm disorders, struggle to identify rare or morphologically ambiguous patterns, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities or implanted devices that distort electrical signals. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in analyzing multi-lead ECG waveforms at sub-millisecond resolution, which is critical for capturing transient anomalies indicative of emerging pathological states. The proposed computational approach integrates three components: (1) parallelized preprocessing of raw ECG signals using adaptive filtering and time-frequency decomposition to isolate arrhythmic signatures from noise and artifacts; (2) training of transformer-based deep learning architectures on heterogeneous ECG datasets spanning diverse patient demographics, sensor types, and clinical scenarios; and (3) mechanistic modeling of cardiac electrical propagation using finite element simulations to generate synthetic training data for low-prevalence arrhythmia subtypes. By employing HPC-enabled distributed training across GPU nodes, we aim to develop ensemble models capable of real-time analysis of prolonged (>72-hour) ambulatory ECG recordings while maintaining interpretability through attention mapping. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for granular ECG phenotyping, validated against invasive electrophysiology studies in a partner clinical cohort. The project addresses a critical gap in personalized cardiac monitoring by enabling early detection of arrhythmias that evade conventional diagnostic thresholds, with potential applications in wearable ECG technology and automated treatment guidance systems. Computational outputs will be disseminated as containerized tools optimized for clinical research infrastructure, lowering barriers for translating advanced analytics into point-of-care electrocardiography practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to administer EKG and ECG diagnostic examinations and report results to the treatment team. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, the cardiovascular system, medical terminology, cardiovascular medications and effects, patient care, EKG and ECG administration, equipment operation and maintenance, interpretation of cardiac rhythm, patient record management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to enhance the detection and forensic analysis of covert communication channels used in terrorist activities, with a focus on ephemeral encryption protocols and decentralized platforms. Current forensic tools struggle to efficiently process the growing volume of encrypted data intercepted in counterterrorism operations, particularly when faced with dynamically evolving obfuscation techniques. The research addresses this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable real-time decryption, pattern recognition, and network traffic analysis at unprecedented scales. Using a combination of GPU-accelerated brute-force decryption, machine learning models trained on known terrorist communication signatures, and graph-based anomaly detection algorithms, the project aims to identify latent connections within intercepted data while preserving forensic integrity. Computational workflows will integrate adaptive sampling methods to prioritize high-risk data streams, reducing processing overhead. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit optimized for distributed memory systems, validated against real-world case studies provided by law enforcement partners. The project also explores the ethical and legal implications of automated decryption in cross-jurisdictional investigations, aiming to establish reproducible workflows that adhere to evidentiary standards. By enabling rapid analysis of terabyte-scale forensic datasets, this work directly supports proactive counterterrorism operations while advancing computational methods for cyber forensics in resource-constrained scenarios. The resulting frameworks will be disseminated through interdisciplinary partnerships bridging cybersecurity, legal studies, and national security stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques used to identify, search, seize and analyze digital media and to conduct cyber investigations against criminal and terrorist activity. Includes instruction in computer boot processes and drives, jumper setting, file access and reconstruction, hacking, network systems, cryptography, programming, investigative techniques, forensic imagery, web-based investigation methods, cyberterrorism, and applicable laws and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Southeast Asian languages, which remain underrepresented in natural language processing (NLP) research despite their structural complexity and sociolinguistic diversity. The research focuses on developing scalable models for syntactic parsing and dialect classification across under-resourced languages in the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian families, such as Burmese, Javanese, and Tagalog. A central challenge lies in these languages’ typological variation—including agglutinative morphology, verb serialization, and topic-prominent syntax—which existing NLP tools, primarily designed for Indo-European languages, fail to capture accurately. To overcome this, the project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on a newly compiled multilingual corpus of annotated texts, oral narratives, and historical records. Computational workflows will include distributed training of large language models, parallelized alignment of cross-dialectal lexicons, and probabilistic simulations of syntactic change. The scale of data—spanning over 20 languages and 10TB of audio-textual materials—necessitates HPC infrastructure for efficient batch processing, hyperparameter optimization, and memory-intensive tasks like graph-based parsing of long-distance dependencies. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access models for morphosyntactic annotation and dialect identification, (2) quantitative insights into contact-induced grammatical shifts in mainland vs. insular Southeast Asia, and (3) a public repository of interoperable language resources. By enabling fine-grained analysis of under-documented linguistic systems, this work will advance theoretical understanding of areal typology while supporting applied goals like speech technology development for minority language communities. The computational frameworks developed will also provide a template for analyzing other non-configurational languages, bridging gaps between linguistic theory and data-driven methodologies. Access to HPC resources is critical given the iterative nature of model training and the need for reproducibility across heterogeneous datasets.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the modern languages spoken in mainland Southeast Asia and the Indonesian and Philippines Archipelagoes, including, but not limited to, members of the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian language families.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and temporal dynamics of trade networks and cultural exchange in the medieval Near East (c. 600–1500 CE). The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how shifting political boundaries, environmental pressures, and economic systems influenced the connectivity of urban centers and hinterlands across regions such as Mesopotamia, the Levant, and the Arabian Peninsula. Traditional historiographic methods struggle to synthesize fragmented archaeological, textual, and climatic data at scale, limiting holistic interpretations of cross-regional interactions. To overcome this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis to simulate trade routes, resource distribution, and information diffusion under variable historical conditions. Computational workflows will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including digitized merchant correspondence, geospatial records of caravan paths, paleoclimatic reconstructions, and archaeological site inventories. HPC resources are essential for running large-scale ABM simulations with probabilistic parameters (e.g., drought frequency, political instability) and iteratively testing hypotheses about network resilience and cultural hybridization. Expected outcomes include (1) dynamically mapped trade corridors that correlate with archaeological evidence of material culture distribution, (2) quantitative assessments of how specific events (e.g., Mongol invasions, plague outbreaks) disrupted or redirected exchange patterns, and (3) open-access tools for historians to model multi-causal interactions in premodern societies. By computationally reconstructing these networks, the project aims to redefine narratives of economic and cultural interdependence in a region often studied through fragmented, nation-state frameworks. The findings will contribute to broader debates about the role of connectivity in state formation and identity construction, while demonstrating the value of HPC-driven methodologies in historical research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: Pediatric emergency care requires rapid, evidence-based decision-making under significant time constraints, yet current clinical tools to predict deterioration or guide interventions in critically ill children remain limited. This project aims to develop a computational framework leveraging machine learning (ML) and physiological simulation to improve risk stratification and treatment personalization for pediatric emergencies. The primary challenge lies in integrating multi-source clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), vital sign waveforms, and imaging studies—into predictive models that account for the dynamic, age-specific physiology of children. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, train deep neural networks on temporal patterns of deterioration, and simulate physiological responses to interventions across developmental stages. Proposed computational methods include federated learning to aggregate de-identified EHR data from multiple pediatric trauma centers, transformer-based architectures for free-text clinical note analysis, and finite element modeling of cardiopulmonary dynamics in shock states. Validation will involve agent-based simulations of virtual patient cohorts under varying emergency scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source ML pipeline for early prediction of sepsis and traumatic brain injury progression in children, (2) physics-informed digital twin models to simulate fluid and drug responses, and (3) optimization algorithms for resource allocation during mass casualty incidents. By enabling real-time analysis of complex clinical data streams, this work has the potential to reduce diagnostic delays, minimize treatment complications, and establish computational standards for pediatric crisis care. The requested HPC infrastructure will directly support large-scale model training, multi-center data harmonization, and validation studies required for eventual clinical implementation.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage emergencies in infants and children.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize nondestructive testing (NDT) and material analysis techniques using industrial radiologic technologies, with a focus on x-ray imaging and radioisotope-based thickness measurement systems. Current methods for detecting subsurface defects or measuring material properties in high-throughput industrial environments face challenges in balancing resolution, speed, and radiation safety. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and may lack the precision required for complex composite materials or dynamic manufacturing conditions. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate photon-matter interactions, detector responses, and noise characteristics at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Monte Carlo methods will model x-ray and gamma-ray transport through heterogeneous materials, while finite element analysis will predict mechanical stress distributions that correlate with radiologic signatures. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to automate defect classification and enhance measurement accuracy in real-time monitoring scenarios. The computational workload requires parallelized GPU-accelerated simulations to handle stochastic modeling of particle interactions and iterative optimization of imaging parameters across millions of voxel-based material representations. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for defect detection in additive manufacturing components, adaptive algorithms for continuous thickness monitoring in rolling mill processes, and radiation dose reduction strategies compliant with ALARA principles. By leveraging HPC resources, this research will advance the precision and scalability of industrial radiologic systems, directly supporting quality assurance in aerospace, automotive, and energy sectors. All models and datasets will be made available to the scientific community, fostering innovation in radiation-based materials characterization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of industrial and research testing equipment using radioisotopes. Includes instruction in x-ray analysis of materials, nondestructive testing and inspection of materials, and continuous measurement of paper or metal thickness.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the quantitative analysis of ballet movement and choreographic innovation, addressing a critical gap in the computational modeling of dance artistry. While ballet training traditionally relies on qualitative feedback and subjective interpretation, emerging motion-capture datasets and biomechanical models now enable data-driven insights into technique, stylistic fidelity, and injury prevention. However, processing high-dimensional movement data—captured across diverse repertoires, dancer physiologies, and historical schools of technique—exceeds the capacity of standard computing systems. This research proposes developing a scalable computational framework to analyze and simulate ballet movement at unprecedented resolution. Key objectives include: (1) optimizing physics-based simulations of complex choreographic sequences (e.g., grand allegro, partnered adagio) using GPU-accelerated rigid-body dynamics; (2) training machine learning classifiers to map motion-capture data to stylistic signatures (e.g., Vaganova vs. Bournonville leg articulation) via distributed deep learning workflows; and (3) rendering interactive 3D visualizations of archival choreographies reconstructed from Labanotation scores. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets from international ballet archives, as well as real-time feedback systems for dancers during rehearsals. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for quantifying technical precision in training, predictive models of injury risk based on biomechanical stressors, and a digital repository of choreographies annotated with stylistic metadata. By bridging computational rigor and artistic practice, this work aims to preserve dance heritage while empowering choreographers and educators with evidence-based methods. The requested resources are essential to handle the non-linear optimization, neural network training, and large-scale data integration inherent to modeling ballet’s physical and aesthetic complexities.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to express ideals and feelings through interpretation of classical dance choreography. Includes instruction in ballet exercise, solo and ensemble dance, history of ballet, ballet choreography, Laban notation, ballet technique, and interpretations of specific styles and schools.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing clinical decision support through the integration of multi-omic data with heterogeneous electronic health records (EHRs), leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome scalability and interoperability barriers in health information systems. Current EHR architectures struggle to efficiently process high-dimensional genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets alongside structured clinical data, creating silos that limit precision medicine applications. Our research will develop a computational framework using graph-based neural networks and federated learning models to harmonize disparate data types while maintaining compliance with privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR). The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets across distributed nodes, facilitating real-time pattern recognition in multi-omic-clinical data correlations. Key technical innovations include adaptive metadata ontologies for cross-domain data mapping and quantum-resistant encryption protocols for secure federated analysis. Computational validation will utilize synthetic datasets mirroring the complexity of 10+ million patient records from partner institutions, followed by pilot testing on de-identified oncology and rare disease cohorts. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source middleware solution for omic-enabled EHR systems, benchmarked against existing clinical decision support tools in accuracy (AUROC >0.92), latency (<50ms per query), and genomic variant interpretation concordance. This work bridges critical gaps in health informatics by enabling scalable, privacy-preserving analysis of emergent biological data types within operational medical record systems, with potential applications in therapeutic target discovery, dynamic risk stratification, and automated clinical guideline updates. The requested HPC resources are essential for training deep learning architectures on whole-genome-scale features and simulating hospital-scale federated networks under realistic computational constraints.
cip_title: Health Information/ Medical Records Administration/ Administrator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage systems, processes, and facilities used to collect, store, secure, retrieve, analyze, and transmit medical records and other health information used by clinical professionals and health care organizations. Includes instruction in the principles and basic content of the biomedical and clinical sciences, information technology and applications, data and database management, clinical research methodologies, health information resources and systems, office management, legal requirements, and professional standards.

abstract: Brewing science faces significant challenges in optimizing fermentation processes, which are central to product consistency, flavor profile development, and operational efficiency. Traditional experimental approaches to strain selection, metabolic pathway analysis, and process parameter tuning are time-intensive and limited in their ability to resolve the complex interplay of microbial dynamics, biochemical reactions, and environmental variables. This project proposes a computational framework to model and simulate yeast metabolism and microbial interactions during fermentation at an unprecedented resolution. Leveraging genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and non-Saccharomyces species, we will integrate multi-omics data (transcriptomics, metabolomics) with dynamic fluid dynamics simulations to predict metabolic fluxes, substrate utilization, and byproduct formation under varying brewing conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational load of these multi-scale simulations, which involve solving systems of differential equations across spatial and temporal scales, from intracellular enzyme kinetics to vessel-scale nutrient gradients. Machine learning techniques will further refine parameter optimization, enabling rapid iteration of strain engineering targets and process variables. Expected outcomes include identifying yeast strain combinations and fermentation protocols that minimize off-flavor compounds, enhance ethanol yield, and improve temperature resilience. This work will advance precision brewing methodologies, reduce production waste, and provide a transferable computational toolkit for microbial community management in fermentation-dependent industries. By bridging systems biology with brewing technology, the project aligns with the agricultural sciences' mandate to innovate food production systems while addressing industry demands for scalability and sustainability.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the business, science, and technology of beer brewing operations. Includes instruction in biology, biochemistry, brewing, entrepreneurship, fermentation, malting, marketing, microbiology, quality control, and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of phonological and morphological evolution in underdocumented Celtic languages, with a focus on the historical development of Cornish and Manx. Despite their cultural significance, these languages suffer from fragmented textual records and a lack of comprehensive computational models to analyze sound changes, dialectal variation, and morphological shifts across time. Traditional comparative methods, limited by manual analysis and small datasets, struggle to reconstruct intermediate linguistic stages or quantify the probabilistic drivers of language change. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational workflow combining digitized corpora of surviving texts, phonetic transcriptions, and dialectal records with machine learning techniques. Neural networks will be trained to model phonetic and morphological transformations across temporal and geographic axes, while phylogenetic algorithms will infer evolutionary relationships between Celtic languages and their regional variants. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution acoustic data from modern revitalized speakers, aligning fragmented manuscript tokens, and running large-scale simulations of language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include a probabilistic atlas of sound changes in Cornish and Manx, enhanced tools for semi-automated parsing of Middle Breton and Early Irish texts, and open-access databases linking linguistic features to sociocultural metadata. By quantifying patterns of divergence and convergence in Celtic languages, this work will provide novel insights into the dynamics of language death and revitalization, while supporting interdisciplinary research in philology, historical linguistics, and digital humanities. The computational frameworks developed will be adaptable to other minority and revived languages, advancing methodological innovation in the field.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by the Celtic peoples of the British Isles, Continental Europe, and Asia Minor, including, but not limited to, modern languages such as Irish, Scots Gaelic, Welsh, and Breton; and extinct or revived languages such as Cornish, Manx, Galatian, and others. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational literary analysis and generative modeling within creative writing research. While traditional literary studies focus on manual close reading, the scale of contemporary digital archives—encompassing millions of novels, short stories, and poems—demands new methods to analyze narrative patterns, stylistic evolution, and genre boundaries at scale. The research problem centers on identifying latent structural and linguistic features that distinguish successful manuscripts in specific genres, as well as modeling how these features interact with reader engagement metrics. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach: (1) deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze a curated corpus of 50,000 contemporary English-language fiction works (novels, short stories) and associated reader response data (reviews, sales metrics), and (2) training transformer-based generative models to simulate genre-specific narrative strategies. The HPC environment is critical for processing terabyte-scale text datasets, running parallelized sentiment/theme extraction algorithms, and iterating deep learning architectures capable of capturing multi-scale narrative dynamics. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for writers to analyze their drafts against genre benchmarks, novel quantitative insights into the relationship between stylistic devices and audience reception, and a framework for ethically informed AI-assisted creative ideation. By bridging computational analysis with craft-focused pedagogy, this work aims to establish new methodologies for data-driven literary research while maintaining rigorous engagement with the humanistic values of creative expression. The requested resources will enable processing times 40-60x faster than local computing infrastructure, making large-model training and corpus-level comparisons feasible within the project timeline.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process and techniques of original composition in various literary forms such as the short story, poetry, the novel, and others. Includes instruction in technical and editorial skills, criticism, and the marketing of finished manuscripts.

abstract: Aromatherapy leverages the complex chemical composition of essential oils to elicit therapeutic effects, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their efficacy remain poorly characterized. This gap hinders the development of evidence-based protocols for optimizing blends, ensuring safety, and personalizing treatments. Traditional experimental methods struggle to address the combinatorial complexity of essential oil mixtures, which often contain hundreds of bioactive compounds interacting synergistically or antagonistically with physiological targets. This project proposes a computational framework to model these interactions at scale, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in processing power and data handling. The research will integrate molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning, and cheminformatics to investigate three key areas: (1) the binding affinities of essential oil constituents (e.g., terpenes, phenolics) to human receptors involved in pain, inflammation, and neurotransmission; (2) the physicochemical dynamics of dermal and olfactory absorption pathways; and (3) the stability and interaction profiles of blended oils under varying carrier formulations. Large datasets from public repositories (e.g., PubChem, ChEMBL) and phytochemical databases will be cross-referenced with ethnobotanical records to prioritize understudied botanicals. Simulations will employ GPU-accelerated docking (AutoDock-GPU) and all-atom molecular dynamics (GROMACS) to model multi-component systems, while neural networks will predict synergistic relationships and toxicity risks. Outcomes will include predictive models for optimizing therapeutic blends, a curated database of aroma-chemical interactions, and quantitative safety thresholds for common application methods. By elucidating structure-activity relationships in aromachemistry, this work aims to advance clinical aromatherapy from anecdotal practice to a precision modality grounded in molecular evidence, directly informing curriculum updates in safety protocols and blend design for academic training programs. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the terabytes of simulation data and enabling real-time analysis of multi-scale biochemical networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide therapeutic care through the preparation and application of extracted essential oils from plants, including flowers (botanicals), roots, berries, and bark. Includes instruction in aromatherapy history and theory, basic physiology of absorption, aromachemistry, organic chemistry, botanical taxonomy, carrier oils, essential oils, extraction methods, blending techniques, application methods, safety, client consultation and treatment planning, business management, professional standards and ethics, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in social service delivery systems by developing computational models to optimize resource allocation for vulnerable populations. Social service agencies often operate with constrained budgets and complex caseloads, yet current decision-making frameworks rely on outdated heuristics or qualitative assessments, risking inequitable outcomes. We propose a data-driven approach using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate service networks, predict emergent gaps in care, and identify allocation strategies that maximize equitable access. The research will integrate anonymized administrative data from partner agencies (e.g., child welfare referrals, housing waitlists, disability service utilization) with demographic and socioeconomic datasets to parameterize models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these simulations, which involve thousands of interdependent agents (clients, caseworkers, institutions) operating under dynamic policy constraints. Computational experiments will test allocation policies under varying demand scenarios, including crisis-driven spikes in service needs. Sensitivity analyses will assess how factors like staff turnover, funding volatility, and cross-agency coordination impact outcomes. Expected results include a scalable framework for real-time resource prioritization and policy prototyping, validated through partnerships with three state-level social service agencies. This work directly aligns with social work’s ethical imperative to advance social justice by embedding equity metrics into allocation algorithms. By translating computational insights into actionable tools for practitioners, the project aims to reduce service disparities for marginalized groups while improving systemic resilience. The HPC infrastructure will also enable training opportunities for graduate students in computational social work, bridging technical and applied competencies in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional practice of social welfare administration and counseling, and that focus on the study of organized means of providing basic support services for vulnerable individuals and groups. Includes instruction in social welfare policy; case work planning; social counseling and intervention strategies; administrative procedures and regulations; and specific applications in areas such as child welfare and family services, probation, employment services, and disability counseling.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for the verification and validation (V&V) of safety-critical, distributed software systems, addressing the growing computational challenges posed by their increasing complexity and scale. Modern software systems in domains such as autonomous systems and smart infrastructure integrate heterogeneous components with real-time data processing, requiring rigorous V&V to ensure reliability. Traditional sequential testing and simulation methods struggle with the combinatorial explosion of states and interactions in these systems, leading to prohibitive computational costs and incomplete coverage. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining parallelized model checking, distributed symbolic execution, and machine learning-guided test generation. The project will implement GPU-accelerated bounded model checking to verify temporal properties across large state spaces and deploy distributed memory architectures to partition and analyze component interactions in real-time control systems. Additionally, reinforcement learning agents will be trained on HPC clusters to prioritize high-risk test scenarios, optimizing resource allocation during validation. The computational workflows will leverage containerized environments for reproducibility and integrate with existing software engineering toolchains. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for parallel V&V, benchmarks quantifying scalability improvements in verification tasks, and novel heuristics for fault localization in distributed systems. This work will advance methodologies for certifying complex software systems while demonstrating how HPC resources can address computational bottlenecks in software engineering research. The results will directly support ongoing collaborations with industry partners in autonomous vehicle software development, where scalable V&V is critical for regulatory compliance and safety assurance. By bridging gaps between software engineering practices and HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish new paradigms for efficient, rigorous analysis of next-generation software systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, analysis, verification, validation, implementation, and maintenance of computer software systems using a variety of computer languages. Includes instruction in discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, computer science, managerial science, and applications to complex computer systems.

abstract: The efficient extraction of hydrocarbons from complex subsurface reservoirs remains a critical challenge in petroleum engineering, particularly as industry shifts toward unconventional resources with heterogeneous geomechanical properties and multiphase flow dynamics. Traditional reservoir simulation tools often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes governing fluid behavior in fractured shale and tight sandstone formations. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity, three-dimensional computational models to simulate multiphysics interactions at reservoir scales. The research will employ parallelized finite element methods coupled with machine learning techniques to optimize adaptive grid refinement, enabling efficient resolution of microscale fractures and macroscale reservoir heterogeneity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of solving nonlinear partial differential equations across billions of grid cells, as well as training neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets of historical well production and seismic imaging. Key objectives include quantifying fracture propagation under varying stress regimes, predicting fluid phase behavior in nanoporous media, and optimizing hydraulic fracturing designs to maximize recovery while minimizing environmental risks. The anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation frameworks for real-time decision support in well placement and completion strategies, validated against field data from Permian Basin assets. By advancing the resolution and predictive accuracy of reservoir models, this work aims to reduce operational uncertainties, enhance hydrocarbon recovery rates by an estimated 10–15% in target formations, and provide scalable computational tools for sustainable resource management. The requested HPC allocation will directly support large-scale ensemble simulations, sensitivity analyses, and the development of reduced-order models deployable in industry-standard workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for locating, extracting, processing and refining crude petroleum and natural gas, including prospecting instruments and equipment, mining and drilling systems, processing and refining systems and facilities, storage facilities, transportation systems, and related environmental and safety systems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of information operations (IO) and psychological warfare (PSYWAR) in contemporary conflict environments, with a focus on modeling the interplay between military media strategies, adversarial disinformation campaigns, and public perception. As digital platforms accelerate the spread of narratives and erode traditional boundaries between civilian and combatant information spaces, military planners require predictive tools to assess how IO tactics influence strategic outcomes. Current models often lack the computational granularity to simulate multi-domain information ecosystems—spanning social media, state-aligned media, and covert influence networks—while accounting for cultural, linguistic, and behavioral variables. The research proposes a hybrid computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling (ABM), and network science to analyze real-time information flows and forecast the efficacy of counter-messaging strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing petabytes of multilingual social media data, training transformer-based models to detect emerging narrative patterns, and running large-scale simulations of population-level cognitive responses to IO campaigns. The project will leverage existing military doctrine documents, historical PSYWAR case studies, and live data streams from conflict zones to validate models. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for optimizing media engagement timelines, identifying vulnerabilities in adversarial information networks, and quantifying the second-order effects of narrative interventions. By bridging computational social science with defense-specific operational requirements, this work aims to advance the empirical foundations of information warfare while addressing ethical considerations in AI-driven influence analytics. Results will inform policy frameworks for responsible military-civilian media coordination in contested information environments.
cip_title: Information/ Psychological Warfare and Military Media Relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the support of military and strategic operations and policy via the use of information as a tool of statecraft and warfighting. Includes instruction in information technology and systems, information security, command and control, satellite communications, global information dissemination, communications and media management, intelligence, psychological warfare, strategic planning, security policy and doctrine, and applications to specific operations, services, and scenarios.
