Expected outcomes include novel design methodologies that reduce power consumption by 15–20% in target applications such as edge-computing devices and 5G transceivers, as well as open-source tools to bridge the gap between academic research and industrial design flows. By enabling high-fidelity simulations of emerging materials (e.g., gallium nitride) and non-von Neumann architectures, this work will advance the scalability of IC design tools while providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-accelerated electronic design automation, fostering workforce readiness in semiconductor innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to design circuits in microelectronics. Includes instruction in circuit design, circuit layout, circuit analysis, computer-aided drafting, and semi-conductor technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of personality dynamics by integrating multi-theoretical frameworks to simulate how trait-state interactions influence interpersonal behavior. Traditional personality models often rely on static, theory-specific assumptions, limiting their ability to capture the dynamic feedback loops between intrinsic traits, situational contexts, and social responses. To address this, we propose developing a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM) that synthesizes principles from Freudian conflict theory, Skinnerian reinforcement paradigms, and neurophysiological trait activation mechanisms. The ABM will simulate virtual agents with heterogeneous personality profiles interacting in dynamically evolving social environments, with parameters informed by empirical datasets of trait-behavior associations and neurocognitive task performance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of agents across extended temporal sequences, while Bayesian hierarchical modeling will quantify uncertainty in trait-environment coupling effects. A second computational phase will employ transformer-based neural architectures to analyze naturalistic text corpora (e.g., interview transcripts, ecological momentary assessments) for latent personality signatures, linking these to simulated interaction patterns. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework for testing competing hypotheses about personality stability and change, novel metrics for quantifying person-environment transaction dynamics, and predictive models of how neurophysiological moderators shape trait expression in social feedback loops. By bridging psychodynamic, behavioral, and neurocomputational perspectives at scale, this work aims to resolve longstanding debates about the mechanistic boundaries of personality systems while providing methodological infrastructure for future computationally intensive research in personality psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the unique organization of fairly permanent characteristics that set the individual apart from other individuals and, at the same time, determine how others respond to that individual. Includes instruction in Freudian, Skinnerian, Rogerian, and Ellisonian psychology; neo-Freudian psychology; psychological systems, neurophysiology, and psychopharmacology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational cultural exchanges and identity formation processes within South Asian diaspora communities through large-scale computational text and multimedia analysis. The study addresses a critical gap in Asian Studies by examining how digital platforms and vernacular media (e.g., community archives, social media, and independent film) shape collective memory and cultural preservation among displaced populations. Current scholarship remains constrained by small-scale qualitative methods, limiting systematic analysis of multilingual, multimodal data spanning decades and geographic regions. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned for South Asian languages (including Urdu, Bengali, and Tamil) to process textual corpora from digital forums, oral history transcripts, and subtitled media. Concurrently, computer vision techniques will be applied to analyze visual motifs in independently produced films and social media imagery. These computational workflows will be integrated with geographic information systems (GIS) to map temporal-spatial patterns of cultural transmission. The HPC infrastructure is essential for training domain-specific language models, processing terabyte-scale multimedia datasets, and running iterative simulations of network-based diffusion models. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of understudied nodes in diaspora cultural networks, 2) quantitative frameworks for assessing hybrid identity expression in multilingual contexts, and 3) open-access tools for processing low-resource South Asian languages. By bridging computational methods with critical cultural theory, this research aims to redefine analytical paradigms for studying diasporic communities while preserving nuanced contextual knowledge often lost in large-scale digital humanities projects. The resource allocation will directly support processing previously inaccessible archives, enabling unprecedented scope in tracing the evolution of vernacular cultural practices across generations of displacement.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Asian Continent, including the study of the Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of next-generation thermal protection systems (TPS) for hypersonic and re-entry vehicles by leveraging high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and conjugate heat transfer simulations. Current TPS design methods rely on simplified models with limited resolution of turbulent boundary layers, chemical nonequilibrium effects, and material ablation processes, leading to conservative margins that increase vehicle mass and reduce payload capacity. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating state-of-the-art solvers for reacting hypersonic flows, porous media ablation, and anisotropic composite material response. The simulations will resolve microscale pyrolysis gas transport within charring ablators while coupling to macroscale aerothermal loads using adaptive mesh refinement. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical due to the extreme computational demands of 3D transient simulations with detailed chemical kinetics (20+ species) and spatially varying material properties across billion-cell domains. The workflow will employ GPU-accelerated finite volume methods for compressible Navier-Stokes equations and implicit finite element solvers for structural thermal response, coordinated through in-memory coupling libraries to minimize I/O bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for carbon-carbon composite ablation rates under Mars-return atmospheric conditions and optimized TPS thickness distributions for a prototype crewed lunar re-entry vehicle. Results will directly inform NASA-funded design studies while advancing open-source toolchains for aerothermoelastic analysis. The requested allocation of 750,000 node-hours on a tier-2 HPC system will enable parameter sweeps across Mach 8–25 regimes and uncertainty quantification through ensemble runs—capabilities unattainable with current campus cluster resources. This work bridges critical gaps between experimental test data and flight certification requirements for high-speed aerospace systems.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing aircraft, spacecraft and their systems. Includes instruction in aircraft/spacecraft systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Rheumatological disorders, including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and scleroderma, are characterized by complex, heterogeneous molecular mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Current treatment strategies often rely on trial-and-error approaches due to variability in patient responses and a lack of robust predictive biomarkers. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets from large-scale clinical cohorts, integrating genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and epigenomic data to identify novel disease subtypes, therapeutic targets, and mechanisms of treatment resistance. A key computational challenge is the scalable integration of high-dimensional datasets spanning bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and longitudinal proteomic profiles, which require advanced machine learning frameworks and network biology algorithms. The project will employ unsupervised clustering methods to stratify patients based on molecular signatures, develop graph neural networks to model cell-cell communication in synovial tissue microenvironments, and apply Bayesian inference models to predict drug response trajectories. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will be performed to characterize interactions between autoimmune-associated genetic variants and candidate therapeutic compounds. By combining these approaches, the research aims to uncover shared and distinct pathobiological pathways across rheumatological conditions, identify biomarkers for personalized treatment selection, and accelerate the discovery of repurposed or novel therapies. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing petabytes of multi-institutional clinical data, training deep learning models on GPU-optimized clusters, and running large-scale simulations of protein-ligand interactions. Expected outcomes include open-source computational workflows for rheumatology research, validated predictive models for clinical decision support, and prioritized therapeutic candidates for preclinical validation. This work has the potential to transform the management of rheumatic diseases by bridging gaps between molecular mechanisms, patient heterogeneity, and therapeutic outcomes.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rheumatology

abstract: Environmental health research faces critical challenges in understanding complex, multi-scale interactions between environmental exposures and population-level health outcomes. This project seeks to address gaps in predicting how spatially and temporally dynamic environmental hazards—such as airborne particulate matter, industrial chemical releases, and emerging contaminants in water systems—contribute to chronic disease burdens in urban populations. Current models lack the resolution to integrate high-dimensional exposure data, socio-demographic vulnerability factors, and mechanistic toxicological pathways at scale. We propose developing a computational framework leveraging agent-based modeling, machine learning, and geospatial analytics to simulate exposure-disease relationships across 10+ years of environmental monitoring data and electronic health records from 2 million residents in the Northeastern U.S. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize stochastic models capturing individual mobility patterns, multi-pollutant synergies, and gene-environment interactions while maintaining census-tract-level spatial fidelity. Parallelized processing will enable sensitivity analyses across 50+ toxicological and epidemiological parameters, Bayesian calibration of exposure thresholds, and uncertainty quantification in risk projections. The computational pipeline will utilize GPU-accelerated neural networks to identify nonlinear associations between pollutant mixtures and respiratory/cardiovascular hospitalization rates, validated against longitudinal cohort studies. Outcomes will yield a publicly accessible modeling toolkit to prioritize high-risk zones, evaluate intervention scenarios, and inform equitable regulatory strategies. By enabling previously infeasible integrations of environmental, clinical, and omics datasets at scale, this work will advance causal inference in environmental epidemiology and provide actionable insights for reducing disease burdens in vulnerable communities. The requested allocation of 500,000 CPU-core hours and 200 TB of scalable storage will directly support these computationally intensive simulations and data harmonization processes over 18 months.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of environmental sciences, public health, the biomedical sciences, and environmental toxicology to the study of environmental factors affecting human health, safety, and related ecological issues, and prepares individuals to function as professional environmental health specialists. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, toxicology, public policy analysis, public management, risk assessment, communications, environmental law, occupational health and safety emergency response, and applications such as air quality, food protection, radiation protection, solid and hazardous waste management, water quality, soil quality, noise abatement, housing quality, and environmental control of recreational areas.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and ecological drivers of collective escape dynamics in mixed-species fish shoals under predation risk, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve multi-scale interactions inaccessible to conventional experimental approaches. While collective behavior is well-studied in single-species contexts, the functional consequences of interspecific heterogeneity in escape responses—including variations in sensory acuity, propulsion kinematics, and neural processing delays—remain poorly understood. We propose a novel computational framework integrating species-specific biomechanical data from 3D motion capture of live specimens (e.g., damselfish, wrasses, and goatfish) into GPU-accelerated, agent-based simulations. These models will incorporate hydrodynamic interactions, visual occlusion fields, and neurophysiological latency parameters derived from electrophysiological recordings to simulate predator-prey encounters in coral reef environments. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across ecological gradients (group composition, predator attack angles, habitat complexity) while resolving millisecond-scale decision cascades within shoals containing >10,000 individuals. Key deliverables include (1) quantification of survival trade-offs between interspecific trait diversity and coordination efficiency, (2) identification of non-linear thresholds in predator confusion effects across group size-biodiversity continua, and (3) open-source tools for simulating multi-taxa fluid-structure interaction in biologically realistic turbulence regimes. Outcomes will advance fundamental knowledge of how biodiversity mediates emergent anti-predator adaptations in marine vertebrates, with applications to artificial swarm robotics and evidence-based management of coastal ecosystems facing altered predator guilds due to climate change. The computational demands of concurrently modeling physiological, hydrodynamic, and behavioral processes at ecological scales necessitate dedicated access to HPC resources supporting massively parallel simulations and large-scale fluid dynamics computations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in zoology/animal biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and semantic evolution of medieval religious legal corpora, with a focus on understudied canonical commentaries from the 12th to 16th centuries. While traditional canon law research has prioritized doctrinal analysis, this study addresses a critical gap: the lack of systematic, data-driven investigations into how interpretive frameworks in canonical jurisprudence evolved in response to shifting theological, political, and social contexts. The research problem centers on disentangling complex patterns of influence among glossators, commentators, and institutional authorities across a multilingual corpus comprising over 15,000 pages of digitized manuscripts and early printed editions. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored for Latin, Old Occitan, and Medieval Iberian vernaculars, supplemented by network analysis to map citation practices and conceptual dependencies. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on low-resource historical languages, conducting large-scale parallel text comparisons, and visualizing 3D network representations of juristic dialogue across temporal and geographic axes. Expected outcomes include (1) the identification of previously unrecognized doctrinal transmission pathways between monastic schools and secular courts, (2) quantitative models correlating rhetorical shifts in legal argumentation with major ecclesiastical reforms, and (3) an open-access digital repository of annotated texts and interactive analytical tools. By integrating computational humanities approaches with canonical jurisprudence, this project aims to establish new methodologies for studying how religious legal systems dynamically negotiate authority and adaptation—a question with enduring implications for understanding law’s role in shaping cultural worldviews.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, theology, and philosophy of religious, church, and ecclesiastical law and that prepares individuals to serve as professional canonists.

abstract: This project seeks to advance biology teacher preparation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex biological systems and simulate classroom implementation of computational tools. A critical challenge in biology teacher education lies in bridging the gap between rapidly evolving computational methods in life sciences and their practical integration into K–12 curricula. Many pre-service teachers lack exposure to scalable, interactive tools for exploring dynamic biological processes (e.g., population genetics, protein folding, or ecosystem modeling), limiting their ability to design authentic, inquiry-driven lessons. To address this, we propose developing and testing a suite of agent-based models and simulations that mirror real-world biological phenomena, optimized for HPC environments. These simulations will enable pre-service teachers to manipulate variables at scales impractical for physical classrooms—such as modeling evolutionary trajectories across millions of generations or visualizing molecular interactions in real time—while simultaneously training them to deploy such resources in diverse educational settings. Computational workflows will be designed using parallelized Python frameworks (e.g., Mesa) and containerized for portability across HPC clusters and classroom hardware. Machine learning methods will analyze user interaction patterns to refine simulation usability and pedagogical effectiveness. The project’s outcomes include: (1) a repository of open-access, curriculum-aligned computational modules for biology education, (2) quantitative data on how HPC-driven modeling impacts teachers’ conceptual mastery of systems-level biology, and (3) frameworks for integrating computational thinking into teacher training programs. By equipping educators with the skills to utilize advanced computing resources, this work aims to transform how biology is taught, fostering student engagement with data-rich, interdisciplinary problems that reflect modern scientific practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach biology programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for dynamic risk assessment in industrial processes, addressing the critical challenge of predicting and mitigating low-probability, high-consequence safety events. Traditional static risk models often fail to account for real-time operational variability, interdependencies between process parameters, and cascading failure modes. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrated approach combining agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, and probabilistic risk assessment techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate complex chemical process scenarios at scale, including multiphase flow dynamics, heat transfer anomalies, and equipment degradation patterns under transient conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be deployed on HPC clusters to analyze terabytes of simulated operational data, identifying latent risk signatures and optimizing safety system responses. The computational workflow will incorporate time-dependent failure rate databases and human factors analysis through discrete event simulation. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for process deviation escalation pathways, (2) quantitative benchmarks for safety-critical control system response times, and (3) an open-source toolkit for probabilistic consequence analysis of containment failures. By enabling near-real-time risk visualization and scenario testing at unprecedented resolution, this research directly supports the development of adaptive safety systems for chemical manufacturing, pharmaceutical production, and energy storage facilities. The HPC implementation will prioritize scalability through hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization, with anticipated utilization of 200,000+ core-hours to achieve statistically significant results across diverse process configurations. This work aims to establish new computational standards for proactive safety engineering while reducing reliance on empirical safety factors that constrain operational efficiency.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing methods to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in design for injury prevention, engineering for process safety, environmental psychology, function-based risk analysis, fundamentals of industrial engineering, operations research, probability and statistics, risk assessment and reduction, and safety engineering.

abstract: Dental implantology faces significant challenges in optimizing biomechanical performance and long-term stability of implants, particularly in patients with compromised bone quality or complex anatomical constraints. Current empirical approaches to implant design and surgical planning lack the resolution to account for patient-specific variability in bone microstructure, dynamic loading patterns, and mechanobiological responses during osseointegration. This project proposes a computational framework to model multiscale interactions between titanium implants, bone tissue, and biomechanical forces using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models integrating micro-CT-derived bone architecture data, viscoelastic material properties, and mechanoregulation algorithms simulating osteogenesis under functional loads. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize implant surface topographies and thread geometries by training on simulated outcomes across diverse bone density scenarios. A parallelized computational pipeline will evaluate millions of design permutations while predicting stress shielding effects, micromotion thresholds, and biological fixation timelines. Validation will leverage retrospective clinical data from 3D-printed implants with embedded strain sensors. The HPC environment is critical for resolving sub-100μm-scale bone-implant interface phenomena while maintaining whole-system biomechanical context—a computational challenge requiring petascale memory bandwidth and GPU-accelerated solvers. Expected outcomes include predictive models for patient-specific implant customization, evidence-based guidelines for load-aware prosthetic design, and an open-source simulation toolkit for implant stability analysis. This work bridges clinical dentistry, materials science, and computational biomechanics, advancing precision in implantology through digital twin methodologies that could reduce revision surgeries by 20-30% in at-risk populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design of adaptive engineering systems that integrate heterogeneous subsystems with conflicting operational requirements. Such systems—common in smart infrastructure, reconfigurable robotics, and modular industrial platforms—require balancing dynamic adaptability with structural or functional efficiency, a challenge compounded by the absence of unified design methodologies. Current approaches rely on sequential optimization of individual subsystems, leading to suboptimal global performance when interdependent variables are not co-evolved. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach coupled with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to simulate and iteratively refine system-wide design parameters under uncertainty. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parallelize thousands of design simulations, each modeling interactions between mechanical, control, and human-in-the-loop decision-making subsystems. Computational workflows will integrate physics-based simulations (e.g., finite element analysis for structural integrity) with stochastic agent-based models to evaluate emergent system behaviors. Key innovations include a conflict-resolution metric space to quantify trade-offs between subsystem requirements and a co-evolutionary algorithm to identify Pareto-optimal configurations. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated framework for cross-domain system design that reduces iterative prototyping costs by 30-50% in early-stage engineering, (2) benchmark datasets for adaptive system performance under multi-physics constraints, and (3) open-source tools enabling modular integration of domain-specific simulators. This work advances computational engineering design by formalizing methods to manage complexity in next-generation systems where flexibility, resilience, and interdisciplinary coordination are critical to success. Case studies will focus on validating the approach for modular energy harvesting platforms and reconfigurable aerospace testbeds, though the methodology is generalizable to broader applications.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to engineering problems involving marrying or coordinating multiple dissimilar systems to carry out single functions or achieve common purposes, organizing system components for maximum flexibility and utility, planning engineering projects involving multiple tasks and design solutions, planning design testing and evaluation procedures, resolving specification and requirement conflicts, and choosing among competing theoretical solutions. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 14.2901.

abstract: The proposed research aims to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the design of adaptive underwater energy harvesting systems for low-power marine sensing networks in dynamic coastal environments. The core challenge lies in modeling the bidirectional interactions between turbulent, sediment-laden flows and deformable piezoelectric structures that convert hydrodynamic energy into electricity. Current approaches rely on oversimplified quasi-steady flow assumptions and linear structural dynamics, failing to capture critical phenomena such as vortex-induced vibrations in stratified flows, sediment deposition impacts on energy conversion efficiency, and material fatigue under stochastic wave loading. To address these limitations, this project will implement a fully coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) approach using partitioned multi-physics solvers. High-performance computing resources will enable large-eddy simulations of three-dimensional wave-current interactions at Reynolds numbers exceeding 10^6, coupled with nonlinear viscoelastic material models and discrete element methods for suspended sediment transport. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate the exploration of Pareto-optimal designs balancing energy density, durability, and environmental disturbance minimization. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated libraries for matrix-free solver operations and adaptive mesh refinement to resolve boundary layer dynamics near flexible energy harvesters. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for coastal energy harvesting system performance, open-source simulation tools for marine renewable energy applications, and design guidelines for environmentally sustainable underwater power systems. This research directly supports the development of persistent, self-powered ocean observation networks critical for climate monitoring and coastal resilience planning, while advancing computational methods for fluid-structure interaction problems in multi-phase marine environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to monitor, control, manipulate and operate within coastal or ocean environments, such as underwater platforms, flood control systems, dikes, hydroelectric power systems, tide and current control and warning systems, and communications equipment; the planning and design of total systems for working and functioning in water or underwater environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as the action of water properties and behavior on physical systems and people, tidal forces, current movements, and wave motion.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing educational and vocational outcomes for students with intellectual disabilities enrolled in Comprehensive Transition and Postsecondary (CTP) programs. While CTP programs integrate academic, social, and career development components, there is a critical need to systematically analyze how these elements interact to influence long-term employment success. Current evaluation methods rely on limited datasets and linear models, which fail to capture the complexity of multidimensional student experiences. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining large-scale longitudinal data integration, agent-based modeling, and machine learning to simulate and predict outcomes under varying program configurations. Data sources include anonymized student records (academic progress, skill assessments), employment metrics, and qualitative feedback from stakeholders. Agent-based models will simulate individual student trajectories, incorporating dynamic variables such as skill acquisition rates, social network influences, and workplace integration barriers. Machine learning pipelines will identify patterns in success factors and test interventions via predictive analytics. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of parallelized simulations, optimize hyperparameters for heterogeneous datasets, and scale analyses across diverse demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into which program components—such as tailored academic supports, peer mentorship structures, or workplace accommodation strategies—most effectively correlate with employment retention and advancement. This research will provide CTP administrators with evidence-based tools to allocate resources strategically, while contributing novel methodologies for studying complex educational ecosystems. The project also establishes a replicable computational infrastructure to support future interdisciplinary work at the intersection of disability studies, education policy, and data science.
cip_definition: A comprehensive transition and postsecondary (CTP) program that provides students with intellectual disabilities with academic enrichment, socialization, independent living skills, self-advocacy skills, and integrated work experiences and career skills that lead to gainful employment.

abstract: Clinical psychology requires advanced tools to address the complexity of psychological disorders, particularly in predicting treatment outcomes and understanding heterogeneous patient responses. Current approaches often struggle to integrate high-dimensional data—such as neuroimaging, genomic variants, and real-time behavioral metrics—due to computational limitations. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive models that optimize treatment personalization for major depressive disorder (MDD) and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). The research will employ multi-modal data from 1,500 patients, including functional MRI scans, polygenic risk scores, electronic health records, and ecological momentary assessments (EMA). Computational workflows will combine deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models for temporal symptom tracking and 3D convolutional networks for neuroimaging analysis, with Bayesian hierarchical frameworks to account for individual- and population-level variability. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification in treatment effect estimates, and hyperparameter optimization across 50,000+ model configurations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms predicting CBT and SSRI response probabilities with >80% cross-validated accuracy, (2) dynamic biomarkers linking default mode network connectivity to relapse risk, and (3) open-source software for clinical decision support integrating these models. By enabling rapid analysis of interactions between neurocognitive profiles, genetic predispositions, and therapeutic interventions, this work will directly inform stepped-care protocols while reducing the societal burden of treatment-resistant cases. The computational infrastructure requested is essential to overcome memory and processing constraints inherent in federated learning across multi-site datasets, ensuring clinically actionable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical psychology, involving the analysis, diagnosis, and clinical treatment of psychological disorders and behavioral pathologies. Includes instruction in clinical assessment and diagnosis, personality appraisal, psychopathology, clinical psychopharmacology, behavior modification, therapeutic intervention skills, patient interviewing, personalized and group therapy, child and adolescent therapy, cognitive and behavioral therapy, supervised clinical practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale communication data and model the dynamics of strategic messaging in crisis scenarios. As organizations increasingly operate in volatile digital environments, the rapid spread of misinformation and shifting public sentiment pose critical challenges to effective crisis communication. Traditional analytical methods struggle to process the volume, velocity, and complexity of multimodal data—including social media, news cycles, and organizational messaging—necessary to evaluate real-time communication strategies. This research addresses this gap by developing computational models to simulate crisis scenarios, predict stakeholder responses, and optimize adaptive communication strategies. The project employs natural language processing (NLP) to analyze sentiment and thematic patterns across public datasets, machine learning (ML) algorithms to forecast information diffusion trajectories, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate stakeholder interactions under varying crisis conditions. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of unstructured text and multimedia data, train deep learning models on heterogeneous datasets, and run parallelized simulations of complex communication ecosystems. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for assessing crisis communication efficacy, evidence-based recommendations for message timing and platform prioritization, and open-source tools for real-time sentiment monitoring. By integrating computational social science methods with communication theory, this research aims to advance strategic decision-making in high-stakes environments while contributing to interdisciplinary methodologies for analyzing digital communication dynamics. The findings will directly inform curriculum development in crisis communication and provide practitioners with actionable insights for mitigating reputational risks in an era of rapid information exchange.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the critical thinking, analysis, and practical skills essential to developing and implementing communication strategies that advance organizations goals and missions. Includes instruction in communication management, crisis communication, communications law, digital and traditional marketing strategies, media relations, social media strategies, strategic communication, traditional and emerging media, and writing for the media.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay of legal, demographic, and socioeconomic variables influencing outcomes in family, child, and elder law systems. The research focuses on identifying systemic disparities in judicial decision-making and policy implementation across jurisdictions, particularly in cases involving marginalized populations. By integrating large-scale datasets—including anonymized court records, census data, and longitudinal social services metrics—we aim to model how legal frameworks interact with cultural, economic, and regional factors to shape access to justice and resource distribution. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) of judicial opinions and custody evaluations to detect latent biases, agent-based modeling to simulate the cascading effects of policy changes on family structures, and machine learning classifiers to predict gaps in legal aid utilization among aging populations. A key innovation lies in applying graph neural networks to map relational dynamics in multi-generational guardianship cases, where traditional statistical approaches fail to capture nonlinear dependencies. The project will also develop open-source tools for legal professionals to visualize risk factors in real time, such as predictive alerts for elder financial exploitation patterns. By quantifying how procedural variations (e.g., evidentiary standards in child welfare hearings) correlate with long-term outcomes, this work will provide actionable insights for policymakers to design equitable interventions. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for processing petabytes of sensitive data under secure, partitioned environments while maintaining compliance with ethical legal research standards. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational legal analytics platform and evidence-based guidelines for reforming guardianship protocols and cross-jurisdictional custody enforcement mechanisms.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting domestic relations across the lifespan.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize hemodialysis treatment protocols by simulating solute transport dynamics and fluid mechanics in extracorporeal circuits. Despite advances in dialysis technology, variability in patient-specific factors—such as blood flow rates, vascular access limitations, and comorbid conditions—leads to suboptimal solute clearance and treatment efficacy in many cases. Current clinical guidelines rely on generalized models that inadequately account for these heterogeneities. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model hemodialysis processes at molecular, cellular, and systemic levels. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize urea, creatinine, and phosphate transport across dialyzer membranes with varying pore geometries and surface chemistries. Concurrently, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate blood and dialysate flow patterns under clinically relevant operating conditions, including transient pressure changes and shear stress effects on blood cells. These models will be integrated with machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized electronic health record data to predict patient-specific clearance rates and optimize treatment parameters. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the computational intensity of 3D CFD meshes, iterative parameter optimization, and large-scale data assimilation from heterogeneous sources. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for solute kinetics under diverse physiological scenarios, (2) evidence-based recommendations for personalized dialysate composition and flow rate adjustments, and (3) a risk stratification tool for complications such as intradialytic hypotension. By bridging computational engineering with renal therapy optimization, this work aims to reduce treatment-related morbidity and improve quality of life for patients with end-stage renal disease. The resulting open-source simulation tools will also serve as educational resources for dialysis technologists, enhancing their understanding of biophysical principles underlying clinical protocols.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer hemodialysis treatments to patients with renal failure under the supervision of a nurse or physician. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, dialysis prescription interpretation, dialysate preparation, extracorporeal circuit and dialyzer set-up and maintenance, equipment monitoring, patient preparation, taking vital signs, documentation and communication, venipuncture and local anesthesia administration, emergency intervention, safety and sanitation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Early childhood special education requires personalized interventions tailored to the diverse cognitive, sensory, and communication needs of children with disabilities. However, designing effective, individualized teaching strategies remains challenging due to the dynamic interplay of developmental variables and limited frameworks for predicting intervention outcomes. This project seeks to develop a computational model that simulates learning trajectories for children aged 3–5 with developmental delays or autism spectrum disorder (ASD), leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal educational data and optimize teaching approaches. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational limitations of existing small-scale studies, which struggle to model complex, longitudinal interactions between instructional methods, learner responsiveness, and neurodevelopmental factors. We propose a two-phase approach: (1) Training machine learning algorithms on aggregated datasets (including IEP records, classroom interaction videos, and sensor-based engagement metrics) to identify patterns in skill acquisition rates, and (2) Implementing agent-based modeling to simulate how different teaching strategies propagate through developmental domains under varying conditions. HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, parallelized training of deep neural networks for behavior recognition, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing 10^4+ intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework that maps developmental baselines to optimized teaching sequences, validated against longitudinal classroom data from 15 early childhood special education programs. This work will provide evidence-based computational tools to help educators dynamically adapt instruction, reduce trial-and-error in IEP development, and improve school readiness outcomes. The project’s scale necessitates HPC capabilities for real-time analysis of heterogeneous data streams and large-scale parameter space exploration—tasks infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through open-source models and professional development modules for special education teachers, advancing data-informed practice in this critical field.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Early Childhood Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to infant and pre-school age children with special learning needs or disabilities, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: The classification of high-dimensional manifolds remains a central challenge in algebraic topology, constrained by the intractable computation of homological invariants beyond low dimensions. Traditional serial algorithms fail to address the exponential growth in complexity associated with computing cohomology rings and Betti numbers for manifolds of dimension ≥5. This project requests high-performance computing resources to implement a parallelized computational framework for large-scale homology computations. By leveraging distributed-memory architectures via MPI and optimized linear algebra libraries such as PETSc, the proposed methods will decompose chain complex computations across multiple nodes, employing spectral sequence techniques to iteratively approximate homology groups. Scalability studies will assess the efficiency of parallelizing matrix reduction algorithms critical to resolving boundary operators in high-dimensional simplicial complexes. The research will focus on manifolds arising from symplectic geometry, where precise homological data are critical to understanding geometric structures. Successful execution will generate novel datasets on high-dimensional cohomology, enabling the formulation of conjectures regarding topological equivalences and informing ongoing work in related areas such as quantum topology. The outcomes will provide foundational insights into the algebraic properties of manifolds, with potential applications to unresolved questions in geometric group theory and knot invariants. By establishing scalable computational methodologies, this project aims to bridge a critical gap between theoretical advances and computational feasibility in pure mathematics. This work underscores the necessity of HPC in overcoming barriers that currently impede progress in topology and related disciplines.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the analysis of quantities, magnitudes, forms, and their relationships, using symbolic logic and language. Includes instruction in algebra, calculus, functional analysis, geometry, number theory, logic, topology and other mathematical specializations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling in neuromarketing, an emerging interdisciplinary field integrating neuroscience, behavioral psychology, and marketing analytics. The core challenge lies in processing and interpreting large-scale, multimodal neurophysiological datasets—including electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, and facial electromyography (fEMG)—to predict consumer preferences and decision-making processes in real time. Traditional statistical tools and single-node computing systems are inadequate for handling the volume (10+ TB/week), velocity (millisecond-resolution temporal data), and heterogeneity of these inputs, particularly when modeling dynamic interactions between subconscious neural responses and explicit behavioral outcomes. The proposed computational approach combines deep learning architectures (3D convolutional neural networks and transformer-based models) with graph analytics to map neural activation patterns to latent consumer preference variables. Parallelized preprocessing pipelines will clean and synchronize raw biometric data, while distributed training frameworks (Horovod, PyTorch Lightning) will optimize model performance across GPU clusters. A key innovation involves real-time simulation of market scenarios using agent-based modeling to test how neurocognitive predictors scale to population-level market behaviors. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source framework for multimodal neuromarketing analytics, (2) novel insights into neural correlates of cross-cultural product affinity, and (3) performance benchmarks for HPC-accelerated consumer choice prediction versus traditional survey-based methods. By enabling granular analysis of implicit decision drivers at unprecedented scale, this work aims to establish computational neuromarketing as a rigorous subfield while providing actionable strategies for personalized marketing interventions. The requested resources—500 GPU node-hours/month with high-throughput storage—are critical for overcoming current bottlenecks in model training and complex systems simulation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide analytical descriptions of consumer behavior patterns and market environments to marketing managers and other business decision-makers. Includes instruction in survey research methods, research design, new product test marketing, exploratory marketing, consumer needs and preferences analysis, geographic analysis, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing community resource allocation in underserved regions through advanced computational modeling. Community organizations often operate with limited data and tools to predict evolving needs, leading to inefficiencies in service delivery. To bridge this gap, our research will develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework that integrates demographic, socioeconomic, and spatial data to model community needs and service gaps dynamically. The computational approach leverages agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between residents, service providers, and advocacy networks under varying policy scenarios. We will employ machine learning techniques to analyze historical service utilization patterns and predict demand surges caused by economic shifts, public health crises, or policy changes. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing large-scale datasets from municipal records, nonprofit partners, and public surveys, as well as for running thousands of parallel simulations to test intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that enables community organizations to visualize resource disparities, forecast service bottlenecks, and prioritize advocacy efforts through evidence-based scenario planning. This work will advance methodological innovation in public administration by demonstrating how computational social science methods can enhance equity-focused community practice. The project’s open-source models and training materials will be disseminated through partnerships with regional advocacy networks, strengthening capacity for data-driven decision-making in the nonprofit sector. By aligning computational scalability with participatory design principles, this research contributes to more responsive and resilient community support systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, principles, and practice of organizing and providing services to communities. May prepare individuals to apply such knowledge and skills in community service positions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of individualized education programs (IEPs) and instructional strategies for secondary students with disabilities, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the complex, multidimensional challenges inherent in special education. Secondary special education teachers face significant barriers in efficiently synthesizing diverse data—including academic performance metrics, behavioral observations, and vocational readiness indicators—to create adaptive, evidence-based learning plans that meet students’ unique needs while aligning with curricular standards. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable tools to model dynamic interactions between pedagogical approaches, student-specific variables, and postsecondary transition outcomes. To address this, the project will deploy machine learning (ML) algorithms on HPC clusters to analyze anonymized longitudinal datasets from school districts, encompassing academic records, IEP documents, and post-graduation tracking. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to extract actionable insights from unstructured IEP text, while agent-based modeling will simulate classroom scenarios to test the efficacy of differentiated instructional strategies under varying constraints. The computational workflow will prioritize identifying patterns in effective interventions for specific disability profiles and generating predictive models to guide real-time curricular adjustments. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for teachers to simulate IEP modifications, predict student responses to interventions, and evaluate vocational training pathways. By integrating large-scale data analytics with HPC-driven simulations, this work aims to reduce the planning burden on educators, enhance the personalization of secondary special education, and improve postsecondary transition success rates for students with disabilities. The results will advance computational applications in teacher education, offering scalable methods to bridge gaps between special education research, classroom practice, and policy implementation.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Secondary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the secondary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for secondary grades special education; content, methods, and modifications in specific subject areas; issues in vocational education; and promoting successful transitions to postsecondary settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing need for advanced computational tools in cosmetology education and practice, particularly in understanding the interplay between cultural trends, individualized grooming techniques, and material interactions. Current training methodologies rely heavily on manual experimentation, which limits scalability, personalization, and the ability to predict outcomes for diverse hair textures, skin types, or aesthetic preferences. To bridge this gap, we propose the development of a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic grooming processes, including heat styling, chemical treatments, and makeup application. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling to simulate hair strand behavior under varying conditions, computer vision algorithms to analyze facial symmetry and skin tone variations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to predict culturally resonant aesthetic outcomes based on regional trend data. By creating a virtual environment that accounts for biomechanical properties, environmental factors, and sociocultural preferences, this platform will enable trainees to explore "what-if" scenarios across diverse demographics without physical resource constraints. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of simulated grooming workflows, predictive models for style longevity under environmental stressors, and adaptive training modules that respond to real-time user input. This work aims to establish computational cosmetology as a novel interdisciplinary domain, fostering innovation in vocational education while reducing waste associated with traditional trial-and-error practices. The requested HPC resources will support large-scale parallelization of physics-based simulations and training of deep learning models on multimodal data, including 3D-scanned hair samples and global trend analytics.
cip_title: Cosmetology and Related Personal Grooming Arts, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cosmetology and related personal grooming services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in mathematics teacher education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze the dynamics of teacher-student interactions in virtual learning environments. A central challenge in preparing effective mathematics educators lies in understanding how pedagogical strategies influence student engagement and conceptual mastery, particularly in complex domains such as algebraic reasoning or calculus. While qualitative studies offer valuable insights, they often lack the scalability to generalize findings across diverse classroom contexts. To bridge this gap, we propose developing agent-based simulations (ABS) that replicate decision-making processes of teachers and learners during mathematics instruction. These simulations will integrate empirical data from classroom observations, student assessments, and teacher surveys to parameterize agent behaviors, enabling the exploration of "what-if" scenarios under varying instructional conditions. The computational intensity of modeling thousands of interacting agents across heterogeneous learning trajectories necessitates HPC resources for parallelized simulations and large-scale parameter sweeps. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in simulation outputs, correlating specific teaching strategies with measurable improvements in student outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting the efficacy of pedagogical interventions and actionable recommendations for optimizing teacher training curricula. By quantifying relationships between instructional practices and learning outcomes, this research aims to advance evidence-based approaches in mathematics education. The resulting computational tools will be disseminated as open-access resources, enabling teacher educators to simulate and refine instructional strategies in silico before classroom implementation. This project aligns with national priorities to strengthen STEM education through data-driven innovations in teacher preparation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach mathematics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize plant health and landscape design resilience under dynamic environmental stressors, with applications in commercial and recreational landscaping. A central challenge in groundskeeping is predicting how diverse plant species—varying in water needs, nutrient uptake, and pest resistance—will interact within designed ecosystems under fluctuating climate conditions. Current industry practices rely on generalized guidelines, which often lead to resource inefficiencies (e.g., over-irrigation, excessive pesticide use) or landscape failures during extreme weather. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling approach integrating high-resolution environmental data, plant physiological models, and machine learning. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallel simulation of thousands of plant-environment scenarios, capturing interactions between soil hydrology, microclimate variability, and species-specific growth patterns. We will train neural networks on synthetic and empirical datasets (e.g., soil moisture sensors, historical pest outbreaks) to predict optimal irrigation schedules, turfgrass combinations, and nutrient supplementation strategies under region-specific constraints. Agent-based models will further evaluate how landscaping designs propagate or mitigate heat island effects in urban settings. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental plots with controlled drought and pest exposure. Outcomes will include open-access tools for landscape managers to simulate site-specific maintenance plans, reducing water and chemical use by an estimated 15–30% while improving plant survival rates. This work bridges gaps between precision agriculture methods and ornamental horticulture, advancing sustainable practices in an industry critical to urban ecosystem services. The scale of parameter space exploration and real-time sensor data integration necessitates HPC capabilities, as individual simulations require 10–20 core-hours for coupled hydrological-biological dynamics.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, multi-stakeholder projects under uncertainty, a critical challenge in project management. Traditional project management tools often rely on static models that inadequately capture real-world complexities such as fluctuating resource costs, interdependent task risks, and evolving stakeholder priorities. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning to analyze resource allocation strategies in stochastic project environments. The platform will simulate thousands of project scenarios, incorporating variables such as workforce availability, budget constraints, supply chain disruptions, and risk propagation across project phases. Machine learning algorithms will identify patterns in optimal resource distribution, while real-time sensitivity analyses will quantify the impact of variable interactions on project outcomes. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, the framework will process complex optimization problems at scales unachievable with conventional software, enabling granular analysis of projects with 10,000+ tasks and 500+ resource types. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that reduces cost overruns and delays by predicting resource bottlenecks and recommending adaptive allocation strategies. The research will also advance methodological integration of computational modeling with project management theory, providing insights into risk mitigation and cost-time-quality tradeoffs in agile environments. Results will be tested against historical data from construction and technology sector case studies, with benchmarks for computational efficiency and predictive accuracy. This work will empower project managers to navigate volatility in globalized industries while establishing a foundation for HPC applications in project management education and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply quantitative and qualitative knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage projects in a wide range of fields and occupations. Includes instruction in project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on early identification and intervention strategies for students with reading difficulties, a critical challenge in language and literacy education. Current approaches to diagnosing and addressing atypical reading development rely on static assessments and small-sample studies, limiting their ability to model the dynamic, multifactorial nature of reading acquisition. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale behavioral, neurocognitive, and linguistic datasets to simulate reading development trajectories under varied instructional conditions. The project will aggregate longitudinal data from 15,000+ K-3 students, including eye-tracking metrics, phonological awareness assessments, and structured literacy intervention outcomes, to train machine learning models predicting individual responses to targeted literacy instruction. Key computational tasks include natural language processing (NLP) of curriculum materials, parallelized analysis of multimodal learner data, and agent-based modeling of classroom-scale intervention scenarios. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of audiovisual recordings of reading instruction, running ensemble models to account for sociolinguistic variability, and optimizing neural networks that map developmental precursors (e.g., oral language skills) to later reading outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating the impact of evidence-based literacy practices across diverse learner profiles and generating individualized intervention recommendations. This work will directly inform teacher preparation by quantifying how specific instructional strategies interact with cognitive-linguistic profiles, enabling educators to proactively address reading challenges. The scale and complexity of modeling whole-class literacy development in real-world contexts necessitate the parallel processing and storage capabilities unique to HPC environments, which cannot be replicated through standard educational research infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach language and literacy subject matter areas, at various educational levels. Includes instruction in language development, typical and atypical reading development, and diagnosing reading difficulties.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to enhance the security and reliability of mechanical and electronic locking systems, addressing critical vulnerabilities in modern safe and lock designs. Traditional locksmithing methods rely heavily on physical testing and iterative manual adjustments, which are time-consuming, costly, and insufficient for addressing increasingly sophisticated security threats. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex lock mechanisms, analyze material stress under forced entry attempts, and optimize combination algorithms for electronic safes. The research will focus on three primary areas: (1) finite element analysis (FEA) of lock components under mechanical stress to identify failure points and improve durability, (2) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of thermal attacks on safes to evaluate insulation performance, and (3) machine learning-driven simulations to predict vulnerabilities in digital lock systems against brute-force and side-channel attacks. These computational approaches will integrate multi-physics simulations and probabilistic risk assessment frameworks, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle large datasets and iterative optimization tasks. The outcomes will include predictive models for lock and safe failure modes, validated against empirical data from industry partners, and open-source tools for designing next-generation security systems. By bridging computational engineering with traditional locksmithing practices, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive security system development, reducing reliance on reactive repairs. The requested HPC resources will enable scalability in simulating diverse attack scenarios and material behaviors, which are infeasible with local computing infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops for locksmithing professionals and peer-reviewed publications, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational scientists and security technology experts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, modify, and open locks; to make keys; to enter and change lock and safe combinations; and install and repair safes.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in computational Korean linguistics, particularly in modeling dialectal variation and historical language shifts. The Korean language exhibits complex morphological, syntactic, and sociolinguistic features that challenge conventional analytical methods, especially when applied to large, multidialectal corpora spanning pre-modern to contemporary texts. Current tools for Korean natural language processing (NLP) are often optimized for standardized Seoul speech, neglecting regional dialects and historical texts, which limits their utility in academic and applied settings. This project aims to develop scalable, dialect-aware NLP models to analyze linguistic evolution, sociolinguistic patterns, and pragmatic features across diverse Korean corpora. Computational tasks will include training transformer-based architectures (e.g., tailored Korean BERT variants) on multidialectal datasets, implementing distributed algorithms for diachronic phonology analysis, and simulating dialect convergence using agent-based models. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale text corpora, including annotated historical documents, spoken dialect recordings, and web-crawled modern sources. HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of deep learning workflows, hyperparameter optimization for low-resource dialect models, and large-scale sentiment analysis across regional and temporal contexts. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated dialect classification, a diachronic Korean corpus with sociolinguistic metadata, and frameworks for preserving endangered dialect features. The project will directly support applications in language education, localization technologies, and cross-cultural NLP systems, while advancing methodological innovation in non-English-centric computational linguistics. By integrating philological expertise with HPC-driven analytics, this work aims to redefine the scope of Korean language research in both academic and industry-oriented contexts.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational frameworks for enhancing explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) protocols through predictive modeling and real-time simulation of complex blast dynamics. Traditional EOD methodologies rely heavily on static risk assessments and empirical data, which lack granularity in accounting for variable environmental conditions, heterogeneous material interactions, and emergent explosive device designs. The research problem centers on developing adaptive, physics-informed models capable of simulating multi-domain blast effects (thermal, mechanical, electromagnetic) and fragmentation patterns under diverse operational scenarios. By integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) algorithms, this project aims to create a unified simulation platform that predicts device behavior during neutralization, evaluates countermeasure efficacy, and optimizes personnel safety protocols. Key computational challenges include resolving microsecond-scale detonation physics, modeling composite material failure in improvised explosive devices (IEDs), and incorporating sensor-derived environmental variables (e.g., urban vs. rural terrain) into probabilistic risk matrices. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to train ML models on blast signature recognition and automate anomaly detection in multi-modal sensor data streams. Anticipated outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for virtual EOD training, predictive analytics modules for device categorization, and data-driven recommendations for equipment hardening against emerging asymmetric threats. The project bridges gaps in defense-oriented computational engineering by addressing the unique intersection of battlefield dynamics, advanced materials science, and safety-critical decision-making—a niche not systematically explored within conventional scientific or engineering domains. Success will directly inform next-generation EOD standards, reduce operational risks, and provide a template for computational resource allocation in specialized military research applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the identification, containment, analysis and neutralization of explosive devices. Includes instruction in nuclear science, computer science, ordinance and bomb systems, electronics, computer science, industrial radiography, non-destructive testing, equipment operation, inventory management, investigative techniques, forensics, schematic interpretation, safety procedures, site containment and emergency medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable, real-time rendering pipeline for immersive 3D environments using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current bottlenecks in processing photorealistic visual effects (VFX) and dynamic interactive media. As demand grows for hyper-realistic animation in film, gaming, and virtual production, existing workflows struggle to render complex scenes—such as those involving fluid simulations, volumetric lighting, or AI-driven character interactions—with sufficient speed for iterative creative exploration. Traditional single-node systems cannot process the terabyte-scale asset libraries or physics-based computations required for frame-accurate previews, leading to delays in collaborative workflows. This research will deploy distributed rendering across GPU clusters to parallelize ray tracing and neural radiance field (NeRF) computations, optimizing memory allocation for multi-user access via a cloud-based platform. Machine learning models will be trained on HPC nodes to automate texture synthesis and denoising, reducing manual post-processing. A key innovation involves integrating Unreal Engine’s virtual production tools with Slurm-based job scheduling to enable real-time adjustments to lighting and geometry during live capture sessions. Outcomes will include an open-source framework for scalable VFX rendering, validated through case studies simulating crowd animations and environmental destruction sequences. By enabling artists and engineers to interact with high-fidelity scenes in real time, this work aims to democratize access to advanced visualization tools, accelerating production timelines and fostering novel storytelling techniques. The resource request supports benchmarking across 50+ node configurations, with results disseminated through industry partnerships and workshops targeting animation studios and journalism-based VR content creators.
cip_title: Animation, Interactive Technology, Video Graphics, and Special Effects
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use computer applications and related visual and sound imaging techniques to manipulate images and information originating as film, video, still photographs, digital copy, soundtracks, and physical objects in order to communicate messages simulating real-world content. Includes instruction in specialized camerawork and equipment operation and maintenance, image capture, computer programming, dubbing, CAD applications, and applications to specific commercial, industrial, and entertainment needs.

abstract: The increasing demand for precision nutrition in veterinary medicine necessitates a deeper understanding of species-specific nutrient metabolism and its interaction with health outcomes. Current models for dietary recommendations in companion animals and livestock often rely on generalized physiological assumptions, which fail to account for individual variability in digestion, microbiome composition, and metabolic disease states. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate nutrient absorption, transport, and utilization across diverse animal species and clinical conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and proteomic profiles) with mechanistic models of gastrointestinal dynamics and hepatic metabolism. These models will parameterize species-specific factors such as gut transit times, enzyme kinetics, and microbiota-host interactions, calibrated using existing in vivo data from canine, feline, and equine studies. Machine learning algorithms will then identify critical nodes in nutrient metabolism that predict clinical outcomes in obesity, renal dysfunction, and inflammatory bowel disease. The computational pipeline will require iterative simulations across millions of parameter combinations to optimize model fidelity, necessitating parallelized processing and large-scale memory allocation.
