Expected outcomes include predictive tools for personalized dietary interventions, quantitative biomarkers of nutrient bioavailability, and mechanistic insights into diet-disease interactions. By enabling in silico testing of novel therapeutic diets, this work aims to reduce reliance on prolonged feeding trials while accelerating the translation of nutritional research into clinical practice. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of dynamic, multi-scale models and to advance evidence-based veterinary nutrition strategies tailored to individual animals’ physiological and pathological states.
cip_definition: Research focused on the chemical nature of food substances; the processes by which animals ingest, digest, absorb, transport, utilize and excrete food and nutrients; and their relation to animal behavior and health.

abstract: Modern software systems, particularly in domains requiring high reliability such as autonomous systems and distributed computing, face escalating complexity that challenges traditional verification and validation methodologies. This project seeks to address the critical need for scalable computational approaches to ensure the correctness, performance, and security of large-scale software systems. The research will focus on developing parallel algorithms for automated formal verification, integrating statistical model checking with machine learning techniques to enhance fault detection efficiency. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations, enabling the analysis of system behavior under diverse operational scenarios and edge cases. Additionally, the project will investigate optimization strategies for resource allocation in cloud-native environments, utilizing distributed computing frameworks to minimize latency and maximize throughput. The computational intensity of these tasks—requiring real-time processing of terabytes of log data and simultaneous evaluation of millions of potential execution paths—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure with multi-node GPU clusters and high-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include novel software tools for accelerated verification processes, empirically validated optimization models, and a publicly accessible dataset of annotated system traces to benchmark future research. By advancing the scalability of software engineering practices, this work aims to reduce development cycles for safety-critical applications while maintaining rigorous compliance with functional and non-functional requirements. The requested resources will directly support the generation of generalizable methodologies applicable to industries reliant on robust, high-assurance software systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, analysis, verification, validation, implementation, and maintenance of computer software systems using a variety of computer languages. Includes instruction in discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, computer science, managerial science, and applications to complex computer systems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the morphosyntactic and phonetic evolution of understudied Slavic dialects in the Carpathian region using computational methods that require high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research addresses a critical gap in Slavic linguistics: while major Slavic languages are well-documented, peripheral dialects—particularly those influenced by prolonged contact with non-Slavic languages—remain underanalyzed, leaving their historical development and synchronic variation poorly understood. The project will process a corpus of primary data, including digitized archival recordings, transcribed oral histories, and contemporary field recordings from 15 endangered dialects, to model phonetic shifts and grammatical restructuring over time. Computational tasks will include parallelized acoustic analysis of vowel and consonant systems using Praat scripting, machine learning classification of morphosyntactic patterns (e.g., case system erosion and aspectual innovation), and agent-based simulations of language contact scenarios. These methods demand significant memory and processing capacity due to the scale of audio data (≈12 TB) and the complexity of training transformer-based models on low-resource languages with non-standard orthographies. Expected outcomes include (1) a diachronic typology of Carpathian dialect features, challenging existing assumptions about the conservatism of mountain dialects; (2) open-source tools for automated analysis of under-resourced Slavic varieties; and (3) a public-facing interactive database linking linguistic features to sociohistorical metadata. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will enable systematic comparisons across time and space that are computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure, advancing both Slavic historical linguistics and computational methods for minority language documentation. Results will inform revitalization efforts and contribute theoretical insights into contact-induced change in morphologically complex languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Slavic languages of Central and Eastern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Medication-related adverse events remain a significant public health challenge, contributing to increased morbidity, healthcare costs, and patient harm. Current approaches to predicting and mitigating these events often lack the granularity to account for complex interactions between patient-specific factors, polypharmacy, and dynamic treatment pathways. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model medication-use safety risks at scale, integrating multidimensional clinical, genetic, and pharmacologic data. The research will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from 2.3 million patients, including medication histories, laboratory results, and longitudinal outcomes, alongside pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) simulations and drug interaction databases. Machine learning models—including graph neural networks to represent drug-drug interaction networks and transformer-based architectures for temporal EHR analysis—will be trained to identify high-risk medication regimens and predict adverse event trajectories. Computational workflows will parallelize parameter optimization across thousands of simultaneous simulations to model rare adverse events and quantify uncertainty in heterogeneous patient populations. The project will also implement real-time risk stratification algorithms for clinical decision support, requiring GPU-accelerated inference to maintain sub-second latency during model deployment. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized risk factors for medication-related harm, validated predictive models for adverse drug reactions in vulnerable populations, and open-source tools for scalable medication safety analytics. By enabling analysis of complex, high-dimensional datasets beyond the capacity of traditional computing infrastructure, this work aims to advance precision medication management and inform targeted safety interventions, ultimately reducing preventable patient harm. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training, and large-scale in silico experiments required to achieve these objectives.
cip_definition: Research focused on Medication-Use Safety

abstract: Wilderness medicine requires clinicians to adapt therapeutic interventions to austere environments where resource limitations and extreme conditions—such as altitude, thermal stress, or geographic isolation—exacerbate patient morbidity. Current clinical guidelines for these settings lack robust empirical support, particularly for dynamic, multi-stressor scenarios where environmental physiology interacts with acute injury or illness. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to simulate patient outcomes under diverse environmental and resource-constrained conditions. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create multi-scale, physiologically informed models that integrate real-world environmental data, patient vital dynamics, and treatment protocol variables. Agent-based modeling will simulate patient trajectories across scenarios including hypothermia in remote settings, traumatic injury at high altitude, and heat-related illness in desert environments. Machine learning techniques will optimize adaptive treatment pathways under constraints such as limited medical supplies, delayed evacuation timelines, and fluctuating environmental parameters. By parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, HPC resources will enable rapid exploration of intervention efficacy while accounting for stochastic physiological responses. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to guide triage and treatment prioritization in austere settings, (2) quantitative evidence for revising wilderness medicine protocols, and (3) open-source computational frameworks for simulating environmental-clinical interactions. This work will directly inform clinical training programs and emergency response planning, with potential applications in disaster medicine, military healthcare, and global health equity. The scale of required parameter space exploration, coupled with the need for high-resolution physiological modeling in transient environmental conditions, necessitates the processing power and memory allocation uniquely available through HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine with limited resources in austere environments or to provide healthcare anywhere in which environmental conditions have physiologic insult to a patient.

abstract: The increasing clinical demand for precise quantitative nuclear imaging necessitates advanced computational methods to address limitations in spatial resolution, noise reduction, and biodistribution modeling. Current approaches for single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET) image reconstruction and analysis often rely on simplified physical models or iterative algorithms with high computational costs, limiting their utility in time-sensitive clinical workflows. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-optimized framework for multi-scale radiation transport modeling and image reconstruction to improve diagnostic accuracy in oncologic and neurodegenerative applications. The research will leverage Monte Carlo simulations (Geant4/GATE) to model radionuclide interactions in patient-specific anatomies derived from hybrid CT/MRI datasets, coupled with iterative maximum-likelihood reconstruction algorithms accelerated via GPU parallelization. A novel component involves training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on simulated and clinical datasets to predict optimal reconstruction parameters and compensate for partial volume effects in sub-centimeter lesions. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter optimization for radionuclide kinetic modeling, addressing heterogeneity in tumor perfusion and blood-brain barrier permeability. Expected outcomes include validated pipelines for improved lesion detectability (<4mm diameter) and quantitative accuracy (targeting <10% error in activity concentration) compared to conventional clinical protocols. The developed tools will be disseminated as open-source modules compatible with common nuclear medicine platforms, potentially enabling personalized dosimetry for emerging alpha-emitter therapies. This work directly addresses critical bottlenecks in translating advanced reconstruction methodologies to clinical practice, with particular relevance to optimizing theranostic applications in neuroendocrine and prostate cancers. Resource allocation will support GPU-node intensive tasks including 3D Monte Carlo simulations (10^8-10^9 particles/scan), simultaneous multi-tracer biodistribution modeling, and hyperparameter optimization for deep learning architectures.
cip_definition: Research focused on the imaging by external detection of radionuclides and/or biodistribution by external detection of radionuclides for diagnosis of disease. Requires prior partial completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: The growing complexity of global retail ecosystems, characterized by volatile consumer preferences, fragmented supply chains, and dynamic competitive landscapes, demands advanced computational tools to optimize merchandising decisions. Traditional product assortment and buying strategies rely on historical sales data and heuristic frameworks, which struggle to integrate real-time multi-modal data streams or simulate emergent market behaviors at scale. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven decision support system to model and predict optimal product assortment strategies under uncertainty, with a focus on bridging gaps between localized consumer behavior, supplier reliability, and sustainability constraints. Leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate heterogeneous buyer-supplier interactions and Monte Carlo methods to quantify risks in procurement scenarios, the research will integrate machine learning algorithms trained on terabyte-scale datasets—including social media sentiment, geospatial foot traffic patterns, and real-time inventory telemetry—to forecast demand elasticity for product variants. The computational workflow will require parallelized optimization of non-linear objective functions across thousands of simulated market conditions, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for ABM ensembles and distributed memory architectures for scenario analysis. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for quantifying the trade-offs between product diversification, inventory turnover, and ethical sourcing priorities, validated against proprietary retail transaction datasets from three multinational apparel chains. By enabling near-real-time "what-if" analyses of buying decisions across seasonal cycles, this work aims to reduce overstock waste by an estimated 12-18% in test cases while maintaining profit margins. The project will advance computational merchandising as an interdisciplinary niche, integrating operations research, behavioral economics, and environmental sustainability metrics into next-generation retail analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional buyers of resale products and product lines for stores, chains, and other retail enterprises. Includes instruction in product evaluation, merchandising, applicable aspects of brand and consumer research, principles of purchasing, and negotiation skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance epidemiological modeling of infectious disease transmission dynamics in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where complex socio-environmental factors and fragmented health systems complicate disease control. Current models often oversimplify interactions between demographic, environmental, and behavioral variables, limiting their utility for real-world policy decisions. We propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate disease spread across heterogeneous populations, integrating geospatial data, climate variables, healthcare access metrics, and mobile-derived mobility patterns. The computational demands of modeling millions of agents with fine-grained behavioral rules—particularly for diseases like malaria, cholera, and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis—exceed the capacity of standard computing infrastructure. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across diverse LMIC contexts, sensitivity analyses to identify critical intervention leverage points, and machine learning-driven optimization of resource allocation strategies under budget constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of cost-effective, context-specific intervention portfolios combining vaccination, vector control, and community health worker deployment; (2) predictive insights into climate change impacts on disease burden; and (3) open-source tools for local health authorities to adapt models using region-specific data. By capturing nonlinear interactions between pathogens, human behavior, and health systems, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical epidemiology and implementation science, directly supporting SDG targets for reducing preventable deaths in resource-limited settings. The requested allocation will sustain iterative model refinement, validation against longitudinal health datasets from partner clinics in sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia, and training for LMIC researchers in computational public health methods.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, the social and behavioral sciences, and policy and communications methods to the study of health problems in low- and middle-income countries and regions, and prepares individuals to function as professional international health specialists. Includes instruction in health education and promotion, research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, public nutrition and food security, information systems, program evaluation, medical anthropology, international communication, behavioral sciences, maternal and child health, demography and population policy, and health care finance and economics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in medical insurance coding workflows, with a focus on optimizing the accuracy and interoperability of coded clinical data. Despite advancements in electronic health records (EHRs), persistent challenges in coding consistency—such as variability in ICD/CPT code assignment, contextual misinterpretation of clinical documentation, and time lags in claims processing—undermine billing integrity, healthcare analytics, and reimbursement fairness. Using anonymized insurance claims datasets paired with linked clinical narratives, we propose a computational framework to model coding decision pathways, quantify error propagation, and simulate the downstream impacts of coding discrepancies on payer-provider workflows. Machine learning models (e.g., transformer-based NLP for clinical text analysis and graph neural networks to map coding dependencies) will be trained on multi-institutional datasets to identify high-risk patterns in code assignment. Agent-based simulations will replicate coder-payer interactions under varying regulatory constraints and EHR interface designs. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale claims data, iterative model training across heterogeneous data types, and real-time simulation of complex adaptive systems—tasks requiring HPC infrastructure for GPU-accelerated NLP, distributed memory scaling, and high-throughput job scheduling. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to flag error-prone coding scenarios, evidence-based recommendations for EHR template redesign, and generative AI prototypes to assist coders in resolving ambiguous documentation. By bridging computational modeling and health information management, this work aims to reduce administrative waste, enhance data quality for translational research, and establish scalable methods for auditing emerging AI-driven coding tools. The resource allocation will directly support the development of open-source benchmarking tools tailored to coding specialists, fostering transparency in a field critical to healthcare sustainability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized data entry, classification, and record-keeping procedures related to medical diagnostic, treatment, billing, and insurance documentation. Includes instruction in medical records and insurance software applications, basic anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, fundamentals of medical science and treatment procedures, data classification and coding, data entry skills, and regulations relating to Medicare and insurance documentation.

abstract: Fire dynamics and arson investigation present unique challenges due to the complex interplay of chemical, thermal, and human behavioral factors influencing fire spread and evidence preservation. Current investigative methods often rely on static, empirical models that inadequately capture real-world variability in fire behavior, particularly in cases involving accelerated combustion or concealed ignition sources. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a multi-physics computational framework to simulate fire propagation under diverse environmental and anthropogenic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to integrate finite element analysis of heat transfer, computational fluid dynamics modeling of smoke dispersion, and probabilistic machine learning algorithms trained on historical arson case data. The framework will account for variables such as material heterogeneity, ventilation effects, and human intervention patterns (e.g., accelerant placement or structural modifications), which are critical for reconstructing fire origins but poorly represented in existing tools. Validation will occur through comparative analysis against controlled burn experiments and resolved case files from municipal fire archives. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive model capable of identifying statistically significant ignition signatures and a digital toolkit for visualizing fire progression scenarios with forensic relevance. By enabling granular analysis of spatiotemporal fire dynamics at scale, this work aims to enhance evidentiary robustness in arson investigations while advancing computational methodologies for fire science applications. The resource-intensive nature of coupled multi-domain simulations and large-scale pattern recognition in heterogeneous datasets necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve sufficient resolution and statistical power. Successful implementation could establish new standards for data-driven fire investigation protocols and inform preventive strategies targeting high-risk scenarios identified through computational scenario testing.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and principles of fire combustion and behavior applied to the analysis of fires and their causes. Includes instruction in fire behavior and combustion, fire dynamics, hazardous materials chemistry, incendiary fire analysis, fire-related human behavior, forensic procedures, investigative techniques, case management and case preparation.

abstract: Blood transfusion safety and efficacy depend on precise compatibility testing, yet current methods for detecting clinically significant antibodies and predicting rare antigen interactions remain limited by traditional serological approaches. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model complex antigen-antibody interactions at scale, enabling proactive identification of high-risk transfusion scenarios and optimizing donor-recipient matching in understudied populations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will analyze multi-modal datasets, including historical hemolytic reaction records, genomic profiles of rare blood group variants, and dynamic 3D structural simulations of erythrocyte membrane glycoproteins. Machine learning models will be trained to predict alloimmunization risks and antigen expression patterns using neural networks and molecular dynamics simulations, incorporating population-specific HLA and blood group allele frequencies. The computational pipeline will integrate antibody affinity predictions with blood bank inventory data to generate real-time compatibility rankings for patients with complex antibody profiles. This approach addresses critical gaps in managing transfusion-dependent disorders such as sickle cell disease, where alloimmunization rates exceed 20% despite extended phenotype matching. By simulating over 10^6 potential antigen-antibody pairings across diverse demographic cohorts, the project aims to establish predictive thresholds for clinically relevant interactions currently classified as "of uncertain significance." Anticipated outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for blood bank specialists, improved guidelines for rare donor recruitment, and a curated database of computational epitope mappings for variant RH and Kell system antigens. The HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale immunohematology datasets while maintaining the low-latency requirements essential for clinical applicability, directly advancing precision transfusion medicine capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Occupational health hazards in industrial settings arise from complex interactions between chemical, physical, and ergonomic factors, posing significant challenges for real-time risk assessment and mitigation. Current methods for evaluating multifactorial exposures often rely on simplified models or isolated hazard analyses, which may underestimate cumulative risks or fail to capture dynamic workplace conditions. This project addresses these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop integrated computational models that simulate exposure scenarios, predict health outcomes, and optimize safety interventions. The research employs agent-based modeling and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to recreate spatially resolved industrial environments, incorporating real-time sensor data on airborne contaminants, noise levels, and biomechanical stressors. Machine learning algorithms will analyze large-scale occupational health datasets to identify patterns in exposure-response relationships and worker behavior. By coupling these approaches, the project aims to generate predictive tools capable of assessing synergistic effects of concurrent hazards and testing the efficacy of protective measures under varying operational conditions. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for dynamic risk assessment, data-driven recommendations for workplace safety protocols, and open-source computational tools to support industrial hygiene decision-making. This work will advance the capacity of occupational health professionals to proactively address emerging hazards, reduce work-related illnesses, and align safety practices with evolving industrial technologies. The computational demands of multi-physics simulations, large dataset analytics, and real-time scenario testing necessitate HPC resources to ensure feasibility and scalability across diverse workplace contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to monitor and evaluate health and related safety standards in industrial, commercial, and government workplaces and facilities. Includes instruction in occupational health and safety standards and regulations; health-related aspects of various occupations and work environments; health hazard testing and evaluation; test equipment operation and maintenance; industrial toxicology; worker health and safety education; and the analysis and testing of job-related equipment, behavior practices, and protective devices and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of crustal stress accumulation and release in tectonically active regions using high-resolution numerical modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how heterogeneous lithospheric properties and evolving fault geometries influence seismic hazard potential. Current models often oversimplify subsurface rheology or rely on static fault representations, limiting their predictive capability for complex fault systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a coupled computational framework integrating 3D finite element simulations of viscoelastic stress transfer with machine learning-assisted parameter optimization. The models will assimilate geodetic (GNSS, InSAR) and seismological datasets spanning the San Andreas Fault System and Himalayan frontal thrusts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve meter- to kilometer-scale variations in rock strength, pore pressure, and fault geometry across domains exceeding 100 km³ while capturing multi-decadal tectonic loading cycles. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for elastodynamic equations and parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling to constrain mechanical parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative maps of strain localization probabilities in poorly instrumented regions, (2) validation of stress transfer hypotheses between major fault segments, and (3) open-source tools for community use in probabilistic seismic hazard assessment. By elucidating how crustal heterogeneity modulates earthquake interactions, this work will advance fundamental knowledge of lithospheric mechanics while providing actionable constraints on maximum credible earthquakes for critical infrastructure planning. The scale of required simulations—involving >10⁹ grid elements and petabyte-scale output—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation beyond institutional cluster capacities to maintain temporal resolution below 0.1 years across 50+ model realizations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and relationships between the solids, liquids and gases comprising it.

abstract: Theatre arts management faces growing complexity in optimizing production logistics, financial planning, and audience engagement within dynamic, resource-constrained environments. Current decision-making frameworks often rely on static models that inadequately capture the interdependencies between artistic vision, operational costs, spatial constraints, and evolving audience behaviors. This project seeks to develop a computational platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model theatre production ecosystems at unprecedented scale and resolution. The research will integrate multi-source datasets—including historical box office records, spatial layouts of performance venues, real-time social media sentiment analysis, and demographic trends—into agent-based simulations and machine learning architectures. Key computational challenges include parallelizing simulations of audience flow patterns under varying seating configurations, training ensemble models to predict regional ticket sales under economic uncertainty, and optimizing production schedules via mixed-integer programming with non-linear constraints. HPC resources will enable parameter space exploration for rare-event scenarios (e.g., pandemic-level disruptions) through Monte Carlo methods while maintaining real-time responsiveness for iterative design testing. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support system that quantifies trade-offs between artistic choices, operational budgets, and community impact metrics. This tool aims to help theatre organizations mitigate financial risks through predictive scenario analysis while enhancing accessibility through data-driven seating price stratification. By bridging computational modeling with arts management theory, the project establishes a framework for evidence-based stewardship of cultural resources in an era of technological and social change.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business management principles to the management of theatres and production corporations. Includes instruction in theatrical production, theatre design and planning, fund-raising and promotion, investment strategies, human resources management, theatre operations management, marketing, public relations, financial management and insurance, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, multi-stakeholder decision-making in decentralized business ecosystems enabled by blockchain-based smart contracts. As organizations increasingly adopt distributed ledger technologies for supply chain coordination, dynamic pricing, and cross-institutional governance, existing computational models struggle to scale to the complexity of continuously evolving, trustless networks with conflicting stakeholder incentives. The project will develop agent-based simulation frameworks to model emergent behaviors in these systems, incorporating game-theoretic reward mechanisms, stochastic market dynamics, and privacy-preserving data-sharing protocols. Computational demands arise from the need to simulate thousands of autonomous agents operating under Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus rules while maintaining cryptographic audit trails. Proposed methods include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for scenario testing, evolutionary algorithms to optimize incentive structures, and graph neural networks to predict network congestion patterns. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for designing resilient decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) and quantified metrics for trade-offs between transaction finality speeds, incentive alignment costs, and system vulnerability surfaces. By advancing computational modeling capabilities at the intersection of distributed systems theory and operational business processes, this work aims to establish performance benchmarks for next-generation enterprise blockchain implementations while informing protocol standardization efforts. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations of large-scale networks (>10^4 nodes) and enabling rapid iteration cycles for machine learning components trained on synthetic transaction graphs.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This research proposes the development of a computational framework to investigate the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying yoga therapy’s therapeutic efficacy, with a focus on chronic stress and musculoskeletal rehabilitation. Despite empirical evidence supporting yoga’s clinical benefits, the integration of multi-scale physiological data to model its systemic effects remains underexplored due to computational limitations. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze high-dimensional datasets from wearable biosensors (capturing heart rate variability, electromyography, and respiratory dynamics), 3D motion capture systems, and functional MRI scans collected during structured yoga interventions. Machine learning models will identify patterns linking specific yoga postures (asanas), breathwork (pranayama), and meditation practices to dynamic changes in autonomic nervous system activity, joint kinematics, and cortical activation. Concurrently, finite element modeling will simulate biomechanical stress distribution during complex asanas to optimize therapeutic posture adjustments for injury recovery. A parallel computational pipeline will employ network analysis to characterize stress-related biomarker interactions (e.g., cortisol, IL-6) modulated by yoga therapy protocols. By integrating these multimodal datasets, the project aims to establish predictive algorithms for personalizing yoga interventions based on individual neurophysiological profiles and musculoskeletal constraints. The outcomes will advance evidence-based frameworks for yoga therapy standardization, address mechanistic gaps in mind-body intervention research, and provide open-source tools for modeling biobehavioral responses to therapeutic yoga. This computational approach bridges Eastern contemplative traditions with systems biology paradigms, offering novel insights into yoga’s role in integrative rehabilitation medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional instructors in the spiritual and physical therapy of Yoga in private, institutional, and clinical settings. Includes instruction in the principles of Ayurveda, philosophy of Yoga, warm-up and progressive exercises, breathing exercises, meditation, Yamas and Niyamas, instructional techniques, posture adjustment, student/client counseling and assessment, advanced Yoga disciplines and styles, business practices, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Agricultural business operations face increasing complexity due to volatile market dynamics, climate variability, and the need for sustainable resource allocation. This project seeks to develop a computational decision-support framework to optimize agricultural supply chains, predict commodity price fluctuations, and evaluate operational sustainability. Current approaches often rely on static models with limited capacity to integrate high-dimensional datasets (e.g., real-time market trends, climate projections, and soil health metrics) or account for stochastic disruptions. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational workflow will train recurrent neural networks on historical commodity pricing and climate data to forecast short- to medium-term market trends, while agent-based simulations will model interactions among producers, distributors, and retailers under diverse risk scenarios. A parallelized optimization engine will then identify resilient resource allocation strategies that balance profitability, carbon footprint, and water-use efficiency. Key computational challenges include processing multi-terabyte datasets from USDA databases, IoT-enabled farm sensors, and global trade records, as well as managing the combinatorial complexity of multi-objective optimization across spatially distributed agricultural systems. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in price forecasts and supply chain vulnerabilities. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for agribusiness planners, validated against case studies in Midwestern U.S. corn-soybean systems and California specialty crop networks. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing operational risks, improving market responsiveness, and advancing sustainability goals in commercial agriculture. By integrating computational scalability with domain-specific constraints, the project aims to bridge critical gaps between agricultural business theory and data-driven decision-making in rapidly evolving food systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage agricultural businesses and agriculturally related operations within diversified corporations. Includes instruction in agriculture, agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, finance, marketing, planning, human resources management, and other managerial responsibilities.

abstract: Zoological medicine faces unique challenges in addressing health issues across diverse species, each with distinct anatomical, physiological, and ecological characteristics. Current diagnostic and treatment frameworks for non-domesticated animals often rely on extrapolations from domestic species or limited case studies, leading to gaps in precision and efficacy. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing species-specific computational models to predict disease progression, optimize therapeutic interventions, and evaluate conservation-related health risks. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets spanning clinical records, genomic sequences, environmental variables, and biomechanical metrics from zoo animals, wildlife populations, and performing animals. A key focus is the integration of machine learning algorithms to identify cross-species patterns in pathogen evolution, drug metabolism, and stress response dynamics. Computational workflows will include agent-based simulations of disease transmission in mixed-species environments, phylogenetic comparative methods to trace adaptive immune traits, and finite element modeling to assess injury risks in anatomically diverse taxa. These analyses require parallel processing capabilities to manage high-dimensional data and complex iterative computations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for tailoring anesthesia protocols, antimicrobial regimens, and surgical plans to species-specific constraints, as well as frameworks for prioritizing conservation health interventions in rapidly changing ecosystems. By bridging clinical zoological medicine and computational biology, this work aims to establish scalable, data-driven methodologies for advancing care standards in non-domesticated animal populations. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current bottlenecks in processing latency and model granularity, enabling real-time analytics and high-resolution simulations that are infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the specialized treatment and care of zoo animals, performing animals, and animals living in the wild. May included related research in the principles and procedures used in the observation, diagnosis, care and treatment of illness, disease, injury, deformity, or other anomalies in non-domesticated animals.

abstract: Health services research faces growing challenges in analyzing complex, large-scale datasets to inform evidence-based policy and practice. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the multi-level determinants of healthcare utilization patterns among patients with chronic conditions, using integrated claims data, electronic health records, and socioeconomic contextual data. The research problem centers on disentangling individual clinical factors, provider characteristics, and community-level barriers that drive disparities in care access and outcomes. To achieve this, we propose developing a machine learning framework incorporating ensemble methods and graph neural networks to model patient-provider-community interactions across heterogeneous data sources spanning 15 million patients. The computational approach requires processing petabyte-scale datasets with temporal, spatial, and relational components through distributed computing workflows. High-performance computing resources are essential for training deep learning architectures on GPU clusters, running parallelized propensity score matching across 200+ covariates, and conducting monte carlo simulations to evaluate policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include identification of modifiable factors associated with 30-day readmission reductions and optimized care coordination pathways. The analysis will produce scalable models to predict resource allocation needs at the health system level while preserving privacy through federated learning techniques. This work significantly advances health services research methodology by enabling integration of previously siloed data types at unprecedented scale, with direct applications to value-based care initiatives and health equity interventions. The requested computing resources will support both the development of novel analytical pipelines and the generation of actionable insights for healthcare delivery organizations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on basic and applied inquiry, that examines access to, and the use, costs, quality, delivery, organization, financing, and outcomes of health care services to produce new knowledge about the structure, processes, and effects of health services for individuals and populations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in textile recycling systems through advanced computational modeling and simulation. The global apparel industry faces mounting challenges in managing post-consumer textile waste, exacerbated by the complexity of blended synthetic and natural fibers, which resist mechanical and chemical separation. Current recycling methods remain energy-intensive, cost-prohibitive, and limited in scalability, necessitating novel approaches to optimize material recovery. Our research integrates discrete element modeling (DEM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate the behavior of heterogeneous textile fragments during sorting and decomposition processes. By parameterizing fiber composition, weave structures, and degradation states, we aim to develop predictive models that identify optimal conditions for separating blended textiles into reusable feedstock. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of particle interactions under varying mechanical, thermal, and solvent-based treatments, generating datasets to train ML classifiers for real-time waste stream analysis. A secondary focus involves agent-based modeling of decentralized textile collection networks to evaluate the environmental and economic trade-offs of localized versus centralized recycling infrastructures. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for designing adaptive textile recycling protocols, (2) open-source tools for simulating fiber separation dynamics, and (3) evidence-based policy recommendations for circular supply chain integration. This work bridges gaps between computational materials science and sustainable apparel systems, offering scalable solutions to reduce landfill dependency while advancing the computational toolkit available to textile researchers. By situating HPC-driven innovation within an understudied domain of applied textiles, the project underscores the transformative potential of non-traditional computing applications in addressing pressing industrial and ecological challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in apparel and textiles, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of intercultural conflict resolution and cooperation in digitally mediated environments using large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis. As globalized societies increasingly rely on virtual platforms for cross-cultural collaboration, tensions arising from divergent communication norms, values, and power asymmetries pose challenges to equitable participation. Traditional social science methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, adaptive interactions that characterize these complex systems. The research will develop computational models to simulate how culturally situated agents negotiate shared goals under conditions of linguistic bias, information inequality, and competing identity narratives. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to parameterize agents using empirical data from ethnographic studies (e.g., conflict resolution styles, trust-building rituals) and scale simulations to reflect realistic population diversity. Neural networks will be trained on multilingual dialog corpora to emulate culturally coded communication patterns, while graph-theoretic methods will analyze emergent alliance structures and polarization thresholds. The computational framework integrates anthropological theories of ritual interaction, sociological models of social capital, and psychological principles of intergroup attribution bias. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for identifying critical intervention points in cross-cultural collaborations and generative algorithms for designing inclusive digital deliberation spaces. By quantifying how micro-level cultural exchanges propagate to macro-level group outcomes, this work aims to inform policies addressing systemic inequities in education, remote work, and transnational governance. The resource-intensive nature of simulating millions of culturally contextualized interactions across parameter spaces necessitates parallelized computing architectures to achieve statistical robustness. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation toolkits tailored for intercultural studies researchers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: Orthopedic interventions, such as casting and bracing, rely heavily on static, generalized designs that may not account for patient-specific biomechanical variability or dynamic healing processes. This project seeks to address the critical gap in personalized, adaptive orthopedic solutions by leveraging computational modeling to optimize device design and predict biomechanical outcomes. The research focuses on developing a high-fidelity simulation framework that integrates patient-specific anatomical data, material science, and real-time biomechanical feedback to improve load distribution, reduce complications (e.g., pressure ulcers, joint stiffness), and accelerate recovery. Key challenges include modeling the nonlinear behavior of casting materials under physiological conditions, simulating soft tissue responses to prolonged mechanical stress, and predicting bone remodeling dynamics during healing. To overcome these, we propose a multi-scale computational approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain mapping, machine learning (ML) to correlate clinical outcomes with device parameters, and fluid-structure interaction models to simulate microenvironmental changes in tissues. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of iterating through thousands of design permutations, processing high-resolution 3D imaging datasets, and running parallelized simulations of time-dependent biological processes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for optimizing orthopedic device configurations based on individual patient anatomy and injury patterns, (2) quantitative guidelines for material selection and device adjustment timelines, and (3) open-source simulation tools to support clinical decision-making. This work bridges engineering innovation and clinical orthopedics, offering a transformative shift from reactive to proactive, data-driven care in a field traditionally reliant on empirical practices. The computational pipeline developed here will serve as a foundation for future research into smart orthopedic technologies, including sensor-integrated adaptive braces and AI-driven treatment monitoring systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to cast, splint, and brace orthopedic injuries. Includes instruction in patient assessment; casting, splinting, and orthopedic appliances; radiographic interpretation; traction; and wound care.

abstract: Chronic wound healing remains a critical challenge in clinical medicine, with persistent inflammation, infection, and impaired tissue regeneration contributing to prolonged recovery, high healthcare costs, and patient morbidity. Current therapeutic strategies lack precision due to incomplete understanding of the dynamic molecular, cellular, and biomechanical interactions within wound microenvironments. This project proposes a computational approach to model the multiscale processes underlying chronic wound pathophysiology and predict patient-specific healing trajectories. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate high-dimensional clinical data—including longitudinal multi-omics (transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic), microbiomic, and host immune profiles—with spatially resolved tissue biomechanics simulations. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular interactions (e.g., fibroblast-macrophage crosstalk, microbial dynamics), while finite element analysis will map mechanical stress distributions in wound beds. Deep learning architectures will be trained on these synthetic datasets alongside real-world electronic health records to identify predictive biomarkers and optimize treatment parameters. The computational pipeline will be validated against prospective clinical cohorts of diabetic foot ulcers and pressure injuries. By leveraging HPC capabilities for parallelized simulation, large-scale parameter optimization, and federated learning across heterogeneous datasets, this work aims to uncover mechanistic drivers of healing stagnation and generate actionable insights for personalized wound care. Expected outcomes include a predictive decision-support tool for clinicians, novel biomarkers for targeted therapies, and mechanistic hypotheses to guide wet-lab experimentation. This resource-intensive computational framework addresses a critical gap in wound care research, where traditional reductionist approaches fail to capture systemic complexity. Successful implementation could transform therapeutic paradigms, reducing healing times and healthcare burdens for millions of patients globally.
cip_definition: Research focused on Wound Care

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of language contact and hybridity in shaping cultural resilience among multilingual Indigenous communities, with a focus on underdocumented sign languages and their interaction with spoken languages. While prior research has centered on lexical borrowing or syntactic convergence, this study addresses a critical gap: how multimodal communication (gesture, sign, speech) in culturally significant practices—such as storytelling, ritual, and ecological knowledge transmission—facilitates the preservation of intangible heritage amid rapid sociocultural change. The research employs a computational linguistic framework to analyze terabyte-scale video corpora from community-partnered fieldwork, capturing dynamic interactions across sensory modalities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for deploying transformer-based models fine-tuned on minority languages to automate annotation of phonological, syntactic, and prosodic features, while agent-based simulations will model the diffusion of hybrid linguistic practices across social networks. Challenges include processing heterogeneous data (3D motion capture, audiovisual recordings) and scaling neural architectures to handle rare language morphosyntax. Expected outcomes include: (1) novel metrics quantifying the relationship between linguistic hybridity and cultural adaptability, (2) open-source tools for multimodal corpus analysis optimized for low-resource languages, and (3) evidence-based frameworks for Indigenous language revitalization that prioritize community-defined ontologies of resilience. By bridging computational linguistics, ethnography, and complexity science, this work advances understanding of how emergent communication patterns sustain cultural systems under pressure, offering methodological innovations for studying language as a dynamic, embodied social practice. The requested resources will enable processing of time-aligned multimodal features at scale, reduce bias in underrepresented language AI pipelines, and support ethical data sovereignty protocols through federated learning architectures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the anthropological, historical, and sociological context of language with a particular emphasis on language use and its role in shaping cultural and social diversity. Includes instruction in applied linguistics, data management, field methods, language heritage, socialization, structure, linguistic analysis, linguistic theory, and multilingualism.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic pricing and resource allocation in multi-unit hospitality ecosystems through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate complex, real-time interactions between market demand, operational constraints, and sustainability goals. Traditional pricing and resource management strategies in hospitality often rely on static models or isolated datasets, failing to account for the interdependencies between lodging, transportation, recreational facilities, and evolving traveler preferences influenced by climate variability and digital platforms. Our research proposes a novel agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with machine learning (ML) to capture granular behavioral data from travelers, supply-chain dynamics, and environmental factors (e.g., seasonal weather patterns, local event schedules) across geographically distributed hospitality networks. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations of millions of agent interactions, incorporating real-time data streams from reservation systems, social media sentiment analysis, and IoT sensors in facilities. Key computational challenges include optimizing GPU-accelerated clustering algorithms for demand segmentation and solving mixed-integer linear programming models for resource allocation under carbon emission constraints. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of recommending adaptive pricing and staffing policies at sub-daily intervals, reducing operational costs by an estimated 12–18% in simulated scenarios while maintaining compliance with regional sustainability regulations. This work bridges gaps between hospitality management, computational economics, and environmental informatics, offering a scalable framework for an industry increasingly reliant on data-driven resilience in the face of climate and market disruptions. The requested resources will specifically support the training of deep reinforcement learning models on historical occupancy datasets and the validation of simulations against real-world case studies from partner hotel and tourism networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as general managers and directors of hospitality operations on a system-wide basis, including both travel arrangements and promotion and the provision of traveler facilities. Includes instruction in principles of operations in the travel and tourism, hotel and lodging facilities, food services, and recreation facilities industries; hospitality marketing strategies; hospitality planning; management and coordination of franchise and unit operations; business management; accounting and financial management; hospitality transportation and logistics; and hospitality industry policies and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the integrative physiological mechanisms underlying extreme thermoregulatory adaptations in heterothermic mammals, with a focus on hibernating species and their capacity to survive prolonged hypometabolic states. While mammalian thermoregulation is well-studied under normative conditions, the dynamic interplay between neural regulation, metabolic scaling, and organ-specific thermal responses during torpor-arousal cycles remains poorly resolved. This gap limits translational applications for improving organ preservation in transplant medicine or mitigating hypothermic injuries in humans. To address this, we propose a computational physiology framework combining species-specific biophysical models with whole-organism metabolic network analyses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the integration of multiscale datasets, including infrared thermographic maps of heat distribution, in vivo electrophysiological recordings of hypothalamic regulation, and mitochondrial efficiency metrics across tissues. Machine learning algorithms will parameterize a novel reaction-diffusion model capturing spatiotemporal thermal gradients in vital organs during rapid rewarming phases. Comparative analyses will contrast obligate hibernators (e.g., ground squirrels) with facultative species (e.g., bears) to identify conserved versus specialized adaptations. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine models using empirical data from collaborator labs, incorporating phylogenetic constraints and allometric relationships. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform for simulating interspecific resilience to metabolic instability, identification of critical thresholds for organ viability during hypothermia, and biomarkers of thermoregulatory plasticity. This work bridges comparative animal physiology with computational thermodynamics—an underexplored niche—to advance both fundamental understanding of heterothermy evolution and biomedical strategies for targeted temperature management in critical care. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the complex numerical simulations and high-dimensional data integration required to resolve these nonlinear physiological dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of function, morphology, regulation, and intercellular communications and dynamics within vertebrate and invertebrate in animal species, with comparative applications to homo sapiens and its relatives and antecedents. Includes instruction in reproduction, growth, lactation, digestion, performance, behavioral adaptation, sensory perception, motor action, phylogenetics, biotic and abiotic function, membrane biology, and related aspects of biochemistry and biophysics.

abstract: The optimization of pharmacotherapeutic regimens in complex clinical populations remains a critical challenge due to the interplay of genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors influencing drug response. Traditional statistical methods often fail to capture the high-dimensional interactions inherent in pharmacogenomic datasets or simulate drug behavior at scales necessary for precision dosing. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of drug efficacy and toxicity by integrating multi-omics data, electronic health records, and real-world pharmacovigilance datasets. The research will employ machine learning frameworks, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to identify patient-specific predictors of treatment outcomes while accounting for population-level heterogeneity. Molecular dynamics simulations will be conducted to model drug-target interactions under varying physiological conditions, enabling the exploration of off-target effects and polypharmacy risks. Additionally, large-scale pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations will quantify interindividual variability in drug exposure-response relationships across virtual patient cohorts. These computational workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization, and stochastic simulations spanning millions of agent-based interactions—tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for dose individualization, mechanistic insights into adverse drug reaction pathways, and a computational platform for in silico testing of therapeutic strategies in underrepresented patient subgroups. The project aims to advance precision pharmacotherapy by enabling data-driven treatment personalization, ultimately reducing trial-and-error prescribing and improving medication safety in complex clinical scenarios. Successful implementation will provide a template for integrating computational biology into therapeutic decision support systems, bridging translational gaps between bench research and bedside care.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pharmacotherapy

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the digitization, preservation, and spatial analysis of historical and contemporary Indigenous cultural knowledge systems. The research problem centers on the fragmented accessibility of culturally significant materials—including oral histories, land-use practices, and intertribal exchange networks—which are often siloed in non-interoperable archives or constrained by the limitations of conventional computational tools. By applying advanced natural language processing (NLP) and geospatial machine learning models to digitized records, this study aims to identify patterns of cultural transmission, linguistic evolution, and land stewardship practices across diverse Native American communities in North America. The computational approach involves training transformer-based models on multilingual corpora (spanning Indigenous languages, historical documents, and ethnographic records) to trace semantic shifts in cultural terminology over time, paired with georeferenced data analysis to map sacred sites and migration routes. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets (text, audio, maps) and running iterative simulations to model the impact of environmental and socio-political changes on Indigenous knowledge systems. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository co-designed with tribal partners, tools for dynamic visualization of cultural data, and frameworks for ethically centering Indigenous data sovereignty in computational research. This work addresses a gap in area studies by integrating decolonial methodologies with advanced computing, offering scalable models for interdisciplinary scholarship that prioritizes Native community needs and intellectual traditions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the American Indian, Aleut, Inuit, Hawaiian and other native peoples of the Americas from earliest times until the present, with particular emphasis on U.S. and Canadian populations and their problems but including reference to Caribbean and Latin American native peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and simulating large-scale orchestral compositions through advanced machine learning and acoustic modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. A central challenge in contemporary music theory and composition lies in understanding how complex harmonic, timbral, and structural decisions interact in orchestral works, particularly when accounting for dynamic performance contexts or experimental instrumentation. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to model these multidimensional relationships at scale, while real-time synthesis of high-fidelity orchestral textures remains computationally prohibitive for standard workstations. To address this, the proposed research will implement a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on symbolic score data with physics-based acoustic simulations of instrument interactions. The GNN component will map hierarchical patterns in historical and contemporary orchestral repertoire, identifying latent relationships between harmonic progressions, voice leading, and timbral density. Concurrently, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) models will simulate air resonance and spectral blending in virtual ensemble configurations, informed by empirical measurements from instrument libraries. By integrating these methods through distributed computing pipelines, the system will enable both retrospective analysis of compositional strategies and predictive generation of orchestration proposals for new works. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing memory-intensive score corpora (10,000+ annotated compositions), parallelizing wave equation solvers across 3D spatial domains, and optimizing generative adversarial networks (GANs) for timbral interpolation tasks. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolbox for computational orchestration analysis, novel metrics for quantifying textural complexity in large ensembles, and a real-time prototyping environment for composers exploring extended instrumental techniques. This work bridges music theory’s analytical traditions with computational creativity, offering new methodologies to study orchestration as a time-dependent system while expanding access to AI-assisted compositional processes. The resource demands of multi-scale audio rendering and cross-modal machine learning necessitate dedicated GPU clusters and high-throughput storage, positioning HPC access as foundational to the project’s goals.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the principles of sound manipulation as applied to the creation of music, and the techniques of creating and arranging music. Includes instruction in aural theory, melody, counterpoint, complex harmony, modulation, chromatics, improvisation, progressions, musical writing, instrumentation, orchestration, electronic and computer applications, studies of specific musical styles, and development of original creative ability.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address emerging challenges in broadcast journalism, specifically the ethical and technical complexities of analyzing large-scale multimedia news content in real-time environments. As broadcast media increasingly relies on digital workflows, vast quantities of video, audio, and metadata are generated daily, creating a critical need for scalable computational tools to assess content accuracy, bias, and editorial decision-making patterns. Traditional methods for analyzing such datasets are constrained by processing limitations, particularly when handling high-resolution video streams, multi-track audio, and synchronized metadata across diverse geographic and temporal contexts. This research proposes a computational framework combining machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to automate the detection of editorial inconsistencies, potential misinformation, and ethical deviations in broadcast content. The project will train ML models on annotated datasets of archival and live news footage to identify visual, auditory, and textual markers associated with biased framing or factual inaccuracies. NLP pipelines will analyze speech transcripts and closed captioning data to map semantic shifts in recurring news narratives. Additionally, the workflow will integrate video fingerprinting techniques to track content reuse and modification across affiliate networks. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of multimedia data, optimizing parallelized workflows for frame-level video analysis, and maintaining low-latency performance during model inference. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for newsroom analytics, empirical insights into evolving editorial practices under digital pressures, and benchmarks for ethical AI-assisted journalism. By enabling large-scale, longitudinal studies of broadcast content, this work aims to strengthen accountability in public communication while providing journalism educators with data-driven case studies on modern media ethics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for reporting, producing, and delivering news and news programs via radio, television, and video/film media; and that prepares individuals to be professional broadcast journalists, editors, producers, directors, and managers. Includes instruction in the principles of broadcast technology; broadcast reporting; on- and off-camera and microphone procedures and techniques; program, sound, and video/film editing; program design and production; media law and policy; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize mineral extraction and processing systems under complex geological and operational constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical gaps in predictive modeling. Traditional methods for mine planning and mineral recovery often rely on simplified assumptions about ore body heterogeneity, dynamic fracture propagation during blasting, and fluid-particle interactions in slurry transport, leading to inefficiencies in resource utilization and energy consumption. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating discrete element modeling (DEM), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to resolve the coupled mechanical, hydraulic, and chemical processes governing mineral systems. The HPC resources will enable 3D simulations of fracture networks in heterogeneous rock masses at meter-to-micron scales, coupled with CFD-DEM models of flotation cells and heap leaching processes. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on simulation datasets to accelerate parameter optimization for site-specific conditions. Key challenges include managing the computational cost of resolving grain-scale mineral liberation in bulk ore samples and ensuring scalability across spatially variable geological domains. The outcomes will provide validated models for predicting optimal blast fragmentation patterns, mineral recovery rates, and processing plant configurations under uncertainty. By enabling high-fidelity virtual prototyping of integrated extraction-to-refinement workflows, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error field testing, lower energy intensity per ton of processed ore, and extend the economic viability of marginal deposits. The computational tools developed will be shared via open-source platforms to advance collaborative research in sustainable mining practices. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for ML training and large-memory systems for domain-decomposed geomechanical simulations, with an estimated need for 200,000 core-hours annually to support the proposed mesoscale resolution targets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of mineral extraction, processing and refining systems, including open pit and shaft mines, prospecting and site analysis equipment and instruments, environmental and safety systems, mine equipment and facilities, mineral processing and refining methods and systems, and logistics and communications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing spinal adjustment protocols in chiropractic care by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of manual therapies. Current clinical decision-making relies heavily on static imaging and qualitative assessments, which lack the resolution to capture dynamic, patient-specific responses to spinal manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of spinal kinematics with machine learning (ML) analysis of multimodal patient data, including dynamic motion capture, radiographic imaging, and real-time electromyography (EMG) recordings. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of spinal segment interactions under varying adjustment forces, coupled with ML-driven pattern recognition to identify correlations between treatment parameters, biomechanical stressors, and patient outcomes (e.g., pain reduction, mobility improvement). A key innovation is the incorporation of probabilistic modeling to account for anatomical variability across diverse patient populations, enhancing the generalizability of findings. The computational pipeline will process terabytes of 3D imaging data and sensor-derived biomechanical metrics, requiring parallelized workflows for FEM solvers and GPU-accelerated neural network training. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool to recommend patient-specific adjustment techniques, reducing trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice. This work will also establish quantitative benchmarks for spinal load distribution during manipulations, informing safer, more effective protocols. By advancing computational methodologies tailored to chiropractic technical practice, this project aims to enhance the precision of assistant-delivered therapies while contributing novel data science frameworks to the broader field of manual medicine research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a chiropractor, to provide patient management, examination, and treatment services. Includes instruction in the principles and procedures of chiropractic, radiographic X-Ray procedures and techniques, X-Ray film analysis and media studies, orthopedic and neurological testing, clinical laboratory procedures, patient management and education, office administrative skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study of cultural narratives in Polish diaspora communities through large-scale textual and visual analysis. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of collective memory, identity formation, and cultural adaptation within Polish émigré publications (1945–1990), including periodicals, memoirs, and community archives, which remain understudied due to their fragmented, multilingual nature and the technical challenges of processing non-Latin scripts at scale.
