The computational approach integrates optical character recognition (OCR) fine-tuned for mid-20th-century Polish typography, transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for semantic analysis of Polish, English, and German texts, and graph-based network analysis to map transnational connections between diaspora nodes. Key technical challenges include managing OCR errors across degraded print sources, cross-lingual sentiment analysis to trace evolving attitudes toward post-war Poland, and processing high-resolution scanned materials (estimated 15 TB uncompressed). The project will employ distributed computing to parallelize text extraction pipelines, GPU-accelerated fine-tuning of multilingual BERT variants, and spatial-temporal visualization of diaspora networks using community detection algorithms. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible corpus of processed texts, an interactive map visualizing cultural exchange hubs, and quantitative insights into how gender roles and regional identities were renegotiated in diaspora contexts. This work will provide the first computationally derived framework for understanding Polish émigré cultural production as a dynamic system, offering methodological innovations for Slavic digital humanities while preserving vulnerable archival materials. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the scale of data, need for rapid iteration on custom OCR/NLP workflows, and memory-intensive network analysis across temporal slices.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Poland and the current and historical inhabitants of the Polish lands, including borderlands, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in commercial aviation operations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to advance flight efficiency, safety, and crew training protocols. The increasing complexity of air traffic management, coupled with stringent environmental and operational regulations, demands innovative approaches to optimize flight paths, mitigate risks, and enhance pilot decision-making in dynamic scenarios. Current simulation tools often lack the computational power to integrate real-time variables such as weather systems, aerodynamic stress, and human factors at scale, limiting their utility for predictive analysis. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-disciplinary computational framework combining high-fidelity fluid dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven route optimization, and agent-based modeling of crew interactions. Large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model aircraft performance under diverse atmospheric conditions, while ML algorithms trained on historical flight data will identify fuel-efficient routes and emergency response strategies. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate crew decision-making processes during high-stress scenarios, such as system failures or airspace conflicts, to refine training protocols. The integration of these methods requires HPC resources to process terabytes of sensor data, weather forecasts, and air traffic logs in near-real time. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for reducing fuel consumption by 10–15% on high-density routes, virtual training modules for FAA-certified emergency preparedness, and data-driven insights for updating air traffic control algorithms. This research aligns with FAA mandates to curb aviation emissions and improve crew readiness, offering scalable solutions for airlines and regulatory bodies. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the necessary computational throughput, enabling simulations that capture the interplay of technical, environmental, and human factors shaping modern aviation.
cip_title: Airline/ Commercial/ Professional Pilot and Flight Crew
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the flying and/or navigation of commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue fixed wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications, navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to sit for the FAA commercial and airline aircrew examinations.

abstract: The proliferation of high-definition video streaming and immersive media technologies has intensified demands on telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in balancing low-latency delivery with consistent quality across diverse network conditions. Current adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithms and content delivery networks (CDNs) often struggle to optimize resource allocation dynamically, leading to suboptimal user experiences during peak demand or in bandwidth-constrained environments. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing machine learning-driven models for real-time optimization of streaming protocols and network resource distribution. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will simulate large-scale, heterogeneous network environments to train and validate deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents capable of predicting bandwidth fluctuations and preemptively adjusting video encoding parameters and routing strategies. Computational experiments will involve parallelized processing of real-world network trace datasets, emulating global user bases with varying device capabilities and connectivity profiles. The project further aims to model economic trade-offs between infrastructure costs and quality-of-service metrics, integrating principles of communications technology management into algorithmic decision-making. Successful outcomes will include open-source frameworks for adaptive streaming optimization, empirically validated strategies for reducing buffering and resolution drops by an estimated 30–50%, and scalable benchmarks for next-generation CDN architectures. By enhancing the efficiency of computational resources in media delivery systems, this research will directly benefit telecommunications providers, streaming platforms, and end-users, while advancing scholarly understanding of HPC applications in non-traditional, latency-sensitive domains.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to function as workers and managers within communications industries. Includes instruction in business economics; basic management; principles of interpersonal and mediated communications; radio, television, and digital media production; and related aspects of technology and communications systems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid network infrastructures, which integrate legacy systems with edge computing and IoT deployments, has exposed critical gaps in real-time resource allocation strategies for dynamic, multi-stakeholder LAN/WAN environments. Traditional threshold-based management systems struggle to adapt to the nonlinear demand patterns and heterogeneous security requirements characteristic of modern cyber-physical ecosystems. This project proposes the development of an adaptive resource orchestration framework leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to optimize computational resource distribution across federated network segments. The research will employ high-performance computing resources to simulate large-scale network topologies (10,000+ nodes) with varying traffic profiles, hardware constraints, and failure scenarios. Computational experiments will focus on training GNN architectures to model network state transitions and MARL policies to coordinate distributed allocation decisions while maintaining compatibility with existing Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) standards. Key challenges include developing lightweight model architectures for edge deployment, ensuring backward compatibility with legacy monitoring tools, and establishing failure recovery mechanisms that meet service-level agreements under partial network outage conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predictive network resource management, quantitative benchmarks comparing neural and traditional allocation strategies across simulated disaster scenarios, and novel metrics for evaluating infrastructure resilience in mixed-criticality environments. Successful implementation could enable autonomous reconfiguration of enterprise networks during sudden demand surges or cybersecurity incidents, particularly benefiting organizations managing distributed healthcare systems or smart manufacturing campuses where uptime requirements conflict with evolving attack surface profiles.
cip_title: System, Networking, and LAN/ WAN Management/ Manager
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to oversee and regulate the computer system and performance requirements of an entire organization or network of satellite users. Includes instruction in performance balancing; redundancy; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) network management; system migration and upgrading; outage control; problem diagnosis and troubleshooting; and system maintenance, budgeting, and management.

abstract: Agroecological systems are inherently complex, integrating biological, environmental, and socioeconomic processes across multiple spatial and temporal scales. A critical challenge in advancing sustainable agriculture lies in predicting the long-term outcomes of management practices—such as diversified crop rotations, integrated pest management, or precision nutrient application—under dynamic climate conditions. Current modeling frameworks often lack the resolution to capture fine-scale interactions (e.g., soil microbiome dynamics, pollinator behavior, or farmer decision-making) while simultaneously addressing landscape-level impacts on yield stability, carbon sequestration, and resource use efficiency. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational platform to simulate agroecosystem performance under varying management and climate scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate agent-based modeling, machine learning, and process-based biogeochemical simulations to resolve interactions between crop genotypes, soil health metrics, pest populations, and farm-level economic constraints. Key computational tasks include parameterizing spatially explicit models with field sensor data and remote sensing inputs, calibrating hybrid ML-process models for regional weather patterns, and optimizing trade-offs between productivity and environmental outcomes via parallelized Monte Carlo methods. The HPC infrastructure will enable ensemble simulations across decades of projected climate data at sub-field resolution, a computational demand exceeding the capacity of local resources. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to identify management strategies that maximize nitrogen-use efficiency in staple crops, minimize yield gaps in agroforestry systems, and enhance resilience to extreme weather events. By quantifying linkages between farm practices and ecosystem services, this work will directly inform stakeholder-driven frameworks for climate-smart agriculture. All models and datasets will be made publicly available through an interactive portal, supporting broader research and extension efforts in sustainable agrifood systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on agricultural principles and practices that, over the long term, enhance environmental quality, make efficient use of nonrenewable resources, integrate natural biological cycles and controls, and are economically viable and socially responsible; and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of agricultural and environmental problems. Includes instruction in principles of agroecology, crop and soil sciences, entomology, horticulture, animal science, weed science and management, soil fertility and nutrient cycling, applied ecology, agricultural economics, and rangeland ecology and watershed management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrative machine learning framework for modeling complex, nonlinear interactions in urban ecosystem resilience, a domain intersecting environmental science, urban planning, and computational social dynamics. Urban ecosystems are governed by multifaceted feedback loops between anthropogenic activity, biodiversity, microclimate patterns, and infrastructure, yet existing models often oversimplify these interdependencies due to computational constraints. We propose a novel approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs), spatially explicit reinforcement learning, and multi-agent simulations to capture dynamic, scale-dependent interactions across ecological and social datasets. The computational workflow will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including high-resolution satellite imagery, distributed IoT sensor networks, citizen science biodiversity reports, and socioeconomic indices—to train models that predict resilience thresholds under varying policy and climate scenarios. Key challenges include scaling GNNs to city-wide spatial graphs with millions of nodes, optimizing reinforcement learning policies for conflicting stakeholder objectives, and quantifying uncertainty in cross-domain causal inferences. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized training of ensemble models, hyperparameter optimization via Bayesian methods, and real-time simulation of urban adaptation strategies over decadal timescales. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for adaptive urban planning, validated against case studies in three climatically diverse metropolitan regions. This work will advance methodological integration of network science and decision-focused machine learning while addressing urgent societal needs in sustainable development. By bridging computational scalability with interdisciplinary theory, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven resilience analytics in complex human-environment systems.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of data mining and machine learning. Includes instruction in naive Bayes rule, artificial neural networks, genetic algorithms, decision tree learning, neural nets, network science, optimization, statistical computing, and graphical models and methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in furniture design and manufacturing, particularly in optimizing material efficiency, structural integrity, and sustainable production processes. Traditional design methods often rely on iterative physical prototyping and simplified computational models, which are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in capturing the complex interactions between materials, environmental factors, and user-specific ergonomic requirements. The research problem centers on developing predictive models that integrate multi-scale simulations—from molecular-level material behavior to macroscopic structural performance—to enable data-driven design decisions while minimizing waste and energy consumption. The computational approach combines finite element analysis (FEA) for stress and load distribution modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and humidity effects on material processing, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to optimize generative design parameters. These methods will be applied to simulate scenarios such as the durability of joint systems under dynamic loads, the environmental impact of bio-based composite materials, and the customization of ergonomic features for diverse user populations. By parallelizing simulations across HPC clusters, the project aims to rapidly explore design spaces that are infeasible with conventional tools, reducing prototyping cycles by an estimated 60–70%. Expected outcomes include novel frameworks for sustainable furniture design, validated digital twins for manufacturing processes, and open-access datasets correlating material properties with lifecycle performance. The results will advance the field’s capacity to produce high-quality, environmentally responsible furniture while supporting workforce training in computational design tools. This work bridges a critical gap between traditional craftsmanship and cutting-edge computational methodologies, positioning furniture manufacturing as a leader in adopting Industry 4.0 practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare and execute furniture design projects, assemble and finish furniture articles or subassemblies, repair furniture, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: Laser systems operating in nonlinear media exhibit complex spatiotemporal dynamics that challenge conventional modeling approaches, particularly under high-intensity conditions where beam distortion, filamentation, and instability degrade performance. This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of laser-matter interactions in nonlinear optical systems by developing high-fidelity computational frameworks to optimize beam control and energy delivery. The research focuses on simulating ultrashort pulse propagation in engineered photonic devices and laser-driven plasma environments, where coupled nonlinear effects—including Kerr self-focusing, stimulated Raman scattering, and thermal nonlinearities—require simultaneous resolution across multiple physical scales. The computational approach integrates parallelized finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for electromagnetic wave propagation with adaptive split-step Fourier techniques to model nonlinear optical responses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing 3D simulations with sub-wavelength spatial resolution and femtosecond-scale temporal resolution, which exceed the capabilities of local computing clusters. By leveraging GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed-memory architectures, the team will parameterize nonlinear material properties, validate against experimental spectroscopic data, and quantify uncertainty in multi-physics models. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for mitigating optical breakdown in laser amplifiers, optimizing frequency conversion in quasi-phase-matched crystals, and designing compact directed-energy systems with enhanced beam quality. These advances will directly support next-generation photonic device development while providing open-source computational modules to the laser engineering community. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter space exploration at unprecedented scale, reducing reliance on costly empirical prototyping for nonlinear optical systems in defense, manufacturing, and telecommunications applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of optical systems, lasers and related electronic devices. Includes instruction in wave theory and mechanics, electromagnetic applications, linear and non-linear optics, photon detecting, laser beam properties, directed energy, harmonic generation, optical systems, shielding and the design and implementation of related systems and equipment.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens poses a critical threat to global health, driven by genetic variation and horizontal gene transfer (HGT) mechanisms. This project seeks to elucidate the genomic and structural dynamics underlying AMR evolution in clinically relevant bacterial populations and associated mobile genetic elements (e.g., plasmids, phages). A key challenge lies in resolving large-scale genomic patterns and predicting emergent resistance phenotypes, which requires analyzing terabyte-scale datasets spanning thousands of bacterial genomes, metagenomic samples, and longitudinal clinical isolates. Current methods lack the resolution to integrate pan-genome variability, phage-mediated HGT, and regulatory element interactions at scale. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform comparative genomics, phylogenetic reconstruction, and machine learning-driven simulations. Computational workflows will include (1) alignment-free k-mer indexing of 50,000+ bacterial genomes to identify resistance-associated genomic regions, (2) network modeling of phage-bacteria gene exchange using probabilistic graph frameworks, and (3) deep learning architectures trained on epigenetic and recombination hotspot data to predict resistance gene dissemination. These analyses demand parallelized processing of multi-dimensional genomic data, with iterative model training requiring GPU-accelerated nodes. Expected outcomes include identifying high-risk genetic elements that accelerate AMR spread, characterizing understudied phage contributions to resistance transmission, and generating predictive maps of resistance gene stability under selective pressure. The resource-intensive nature of these tasks—particularly genome-scale motif discovery and population genetic simulations—necessitates HPC support for storage, in-memory data handling, and distributed computing. Results will advance fundamental understanding of molecular genetic drivers in AMR evolution and inform targeted therapeutic strategies to disrupt resistance transmission pathways.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of genetic structures and mechanisms of organisms, including bacteria, phages, and viruses. Includes instruction in the replication, expression, transfer, structure, maintenance, and stability of heritable information in DNA, RNA, and proteins; the regulation of these processes; and neurogenetics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation for sustainable tourism ecosystems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between traveler behavior, environmental constraints, and regional economic systems. The tourism industry faces critical challenges in balancing profitability with ecological and social sustainability, particularly as climate change and overcrowding strain destination resilience. Existing models often oversimplify these interdependencies, failing to integrate real-time data streams—such as shifting traveler preferences, weather disruptions, or localized carbon footprints—into adaptive decision-making systems. This project addresses this gap by constructing a multi-agent simulation environment that models tourists, service providers, and environmental systems as interacting agents with evolving objectives. The framework will incorporate machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets, including geo-tagged social media activity, transportation network performance metrics, and biodiversity impact indicators, to predict demand surges and resource bottlenecks. HPC resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations at scale, enabling sensitivity analyses across diverse climate scenarios and policy interventions. Key outcomes include a decision-support tool for tourism operators to dynamically adjust pricing, capacity, and conservation investments while maintaining compliance with region-specific sustainability thresholds. The computational approach also advances methodological innovation by combining graph neural networks to represent destination ecosystems as interconnected nodes, optimizing for both economic efficiency and environmental equity. By integrating real-world data from partner organizations in coastal and mountain tourism regions, this project aims to establish a replicable model for mitigating overtourism and fostering regenerative travel practices. The resulting open-source framework will provide actionable insights for policymakers and businesses navigating the trade-offs between short-term revenue and long-term destination viability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage travel-related enterprises and related convention and/or tour services. Includes instruction in travel agency management, tour arranging and planning, convention and event planning, travel industry operations and procedures, tourism marketing and promotion strategies, travel counseling, travel industry law, international and domestic operations, and travel and tourism policy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of communication networks in large, distributed organizations and their impact on decision-making latency during crisis scenarios. As organizations increasingly rely on digitally mediated communication (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams, email), understanding how message propagation, information silos, and hierarchical structures influence collective responsiveness remains understudied. Existing research lacks granular computational models to simulate real-time communication flows under stress, particularly in organizations with 500+ members. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis tools to simulate multi-channel communication patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing large-scale organizational datasets (including anonymized message logs from partner organizations) and running parallelized simulations across diverse scenarios. The model will incorporate variables such as team cohesion metrics, power asymmetry in communication networks, and the role of automated bots in information routing. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of bottleneck thresholds in crisis-related decision-making, (2) predictive metrics for optimizing communication protocols during high-stakes events, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing latent power structures in organizational networks. Results will advance theoretical frameworks in organizational communication by quantifying how symbolic interactions (e.g., urgency signaling, status markers in messages) mediate operational outcomes. The computational approach also contributes methodologically to non-STEM HPC applications, demonstrating scalable text analysis techniques for communication studies. Partner organizations in healthcare and disaster response will receive tailored benchmarks to improve their crisis communication infrastructures, directly linking academic research to practical interventions in human-technology systems.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on general communication processes and dynamics within organizations. Includes instruction in the development and maintenance of interpersonal group relations within organizations; decision-making and conflict management; the use of symbols to create and maintain organizational images, missions, and values; power and politics within organizations; human interaction with computer technology; and how communications socializes and supports employees and team members.

abstract: The study of collective animal behavior in response to dynamic environmental stressors remains a critical yet under-researched area at the intersection of zoology, environmental science, and computational modeling. This project seeks to investigate how rapid environmental fluctuations—such as microclimate variability and resource patchiness—drive decision-making in eusocial insect colonies (focusing on termites of the genus *Macrotermes*) using high-resolution, agent-based simulations. Current models of collective behavior often oversimplify environmental inputs or fail to capture the multi-sensory integration processes that govern individual and group responses, limiting their predictive power in ecologically complex scenarios. To address this, we propose developing a novel computational framework that integrates real-world microhabitat data (temperature, humidity, chemical gradients) with empirically derived behavioral algorithms to simulate colony-scale decision pathways. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the iterative parameterization of millions of interacting agents across spatially heterogeneous landscapes, as well as to run parallelized simulations testing hypotheses about emergent resilience strategies under climate perturbation scenarios. Machine learning pipelines will analyze simulation outputs to identify critical thresholds in environmental stability that trigger colony-level adaptive responses, such as nest architecture modifications or foraging reorientation. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable, open-source model for simulating eusocial insect behavior in dynamic environments, (2) quantitative insights into how microscale environmental variance propagates through collective systems to impact ecosystem-scale processes like nutrient cycling, and (3) predictive metrics for assessing colony vulnerability to anthropogenic habitat fragmentation. This work will establish new methodologies for bridging individual sensory biology with macroecological patterns, offering tools applicable to conservation planning and bio-inspired robotics. The requested computational resources will enable unprecedented resolution in simulating organism-environment interactions, advancing zoological research into complex adaptive systems.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the biology of animal species and phyla, with reference to their molecular and cellular systems, anatomy, physiology, and behavior. Includes instruction in molecular and cell biology, microbiology, anatomy and physiology, ecology and behavior, evolutionary biology, and applications to specific species and phyla.

abstract: Phlebotomy procedures, including venipuncture and capillary puncture, are foundational to diagnostic medicine but carry risks of complications such as hemolysis, hematoma, and patient discomfort. Variability in practitioner technique, patient physiology, and equipment interaction complicates the standardization of best practices. This project proposes a computational biomechanics study to model blood draw dynamics, aiming to identify optimal needle insertion parameters, tube handling protocols, and patient-specific considerations. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will simulate multi-phase fluid-structure interactions during venipuncture, incorporating patient-specific vascular geometries derived from anonymized ultrasound datasets. Finite element analysis will model tissue deformation, blood flow dynamics, and shear stress distributions under varying needle gauge sizes, insertion angles, and vacuum tube pressure conditions. Machine learning algorithms will then analyze simulation outputs alongside a clinical dataset of 15,000 documented phlebotomy procedures to correlate computational predictions with real-world outcomes such as hemolysis rates and specimen viability. The HPC environment is critical for resolving the high spatial-temporal resolution required to capture turbulent flow transitions near needle tips and the viscoelastic response of vein walls. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for complication risks based on procedural variables, (2) evidence-based guidelines for needle selection and handling protocols across demographic subgroups, and (3) an open-access simulation toolkit for phlebotomy training programs. By integrating computational biomechanics with clinical data analytics, this work seeks to advance evidence-based practice in phlebotomy education while directly addressing operational challenges in high-throughput clinical settings. The proposed resource allocation will enable large-scale parameter sweeps and validation against emerging clinical datasets, which are computationally infeasible on local laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and other health care professionals, to draw blood samples from patients using a variety of intrusive procedures. Includes instruction in basic vascular anatomy and physiology, blood physiology, skin puncture techniques, venipuncture, venous specimen collection and handling, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex social dynamics of prison populations, with a focus on predicting and mitigating systemic violence through simulated interventions. While criminological theories provide frameworks for understanding prison behavior, the nonlinear interactions between individual psychological profiles, gang affiliations, and institutional policies remain poorly quantified. Traditional analytical methods struggle to account for the emergent, adaptive behaviors that characterize these environments. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach that integrates anonymized demographic data, historical incident reports, and behavioral psychology principles to simulate population-scale interactions within a virtual correctional facility. The model will parameterize factors such as inmate movement patterns, communication networks, and staff scheduling, enabling the exploration of "what-if" scenarios under varying policy conditions (e.g., modified visitation protocols or adjusted guard-to-inmate ratios). Computational demands are significant due to the need for high-fidelity simulations across thousands of agents with real-time adaptive decision-making algorithms. HPC resources will facilitate parallelized runs to statistically validate model outputs against empirical data from three state correctional systems. Expected outcomes include identifying latent risk factors for violence escalation and evaluating the theoretical efficacy of targeted de-escalation strategies. This work bridges computational social science with correctional practice, offering a novel toolkit for evidence-based prison management that prioritizes both security and rehabilitative outcomes. Results will be disseminated to policymakers through interactive visualizations of simulation data, providing actionable insights into resource allocation and procedural reforms.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general study of criminal justice and corrections. Includes instruction in criminology, criminal justice, correctional science, forensic science, law enforcement, psychology, and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational analysis of Urdu literary texts and dialects, addressing critical gaps in digital Urdu linguistics. Despite Urdu’s rich literary history and over 100 million global speakers, computational tools for Urdu remain underdeveloped compared to those for Indo-European languages. The project focuses on two interconnected challenges: (1) analyzing stylistic and thematic evolution in Urdu prose and poetry across historical periods and (2) modeling dialectal variations in spoken Urdu using machine learning. A corpus of digitized texts spanning 700+ works from the 18th century to modern era will be processed using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for Urdu’s Perso-Arabic script and complex morphology. Computational stylometry methods will be adapted to track linguistic features (lexical choice, metaphor patterns, syntactic structures) correlated with literary movements. Concurrently, neural network models will be trained on audio recordings and transcripts from regional Urdu dialects to map phonetic, lexical, and grammatical variations. HPC resources are essential due to the scale of text processing (estimated 15 million tokens), the computational intensity of training dialect models on speech data (5,000+ hours), and the need for parallelized analysis across temporal, geographic, and genre-based dimensions. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive computational framework for Urdu literary analysis, an open-source dialect classification tool, and datasets that bridge humanities scholarship with language technology applications. These resources will enable quantitative validation of philological theories about Urdu’s development while supporting practical applications in education, speech recognition, and cross-dialect communication. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to transform research paradigms in Urdu studies while contributing to equitable language technology development for South Asian languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Urdu language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Urdu; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Early childhood education involves complex, dynamic interactions between educators, young learners, and their environments, yet existing research methods often struggle to capture and analyze these processes at scale. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding how teacher-student interactions, curricular strategies, and environmental factors collectively influence developmental outcomes in children aged 0–8 years. To achieve this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multimodal datasets—including video recordings of classroom interactions, longitudinal assessments of child development, and environmental sensor data—using machine learning and agent-based modeling. Current computational tools are insufficient for handling the volume and complexity of these datasets, which require parallel processing and advanced algorithms to detect patterns in real-time interactions, simulate the long-term impacts of pedagogical approaches, and model heterogeneous learning trajectories. The project will develop a computational framework to (1) train deep learning models for automated analysis of nonverbal communication and engagement cues in classroom videos, (2) run large-scale simulations to evaluate how variations in instructional strategies affect emergent literacy and numeracy skills, and (3) optimize resource allocation in virtual classroom environments via reinforcement learning. By integrating these approaches, the research aims to identify evidence-based practices that maximize equitable learning outcomes while accounting for developmental variability. Outcomes will directly inform the design of teacher training modules and adaptive curricular tools, bridging the gap between data-driven insights and classroom practice. This work underscores the transformative potential of computational methods in early childhood education, enabling granular, scalable analyses that traditional observational or survey-based studies cannot achieve. The requested HPC resources are essential for executing these computationally intensive tasks within feasible timeframes, ensuring robust results with practical significance for educators and policymakers.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students ranging in age from infancy through eight years (grade three), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber warfare tactics demands advanced computational tools to model, simulate, and analyze adversarial behaviors in contested digital environments. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for evaluating adaptive cyber defense strategies against multi-vector, AI-driven attacks in large-scale, heterogeneous networks. The research addresses a critical gap in current cyber operations planning: the inability to dynamically model evolving threat landscapes that integrate machine learning-based offensive tools, decentralized command structures, and hybrid human-AI decision-making processes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will implement a distributed agent-based modeling system to simulate adversarial campaigns across emulated infrastructure spanning military tactical networks, civilian IoT systems, and satellite communication nodes. Computational methods will combine graph-theoretic analysis of attack surfaces, reinforcement learning for adaptive threat behavior, and probabilistic risk assessment calibrated to operational scenarios. The framework will incorporate real-world data on historical cyber conflicts, vulnerability databases, and network traffic patterns to enhance model validity. Key outcomes include predictive metrics for infrastructure resilience under persistent attack, optimized dynamic defense postures for degraded network conditions, and decision-support tools for prioritizing system hardening measures. By enabling large-scale, parallelized simulation of multi-domain cyber conflicts, this research aims to advance operational readiness against emergent threats while informing policy frameworks for ethical constraints in autonomous cyber warfare systems. The computational demands of concurrently modeling thousands of interacting nodes, training adaptive AI agents, and processing real-time threat intelligence datasets necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve militarily relevant latency and scenario complexity thresholds.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the technological and operation aspects of information warfare, including cyber attack and cyber defense. Includes instruction in computer and network security, cryptography, computer forensics, systems security engineering, software applications, threat and vulnerability assessment, wireless networks and satellite communications, tactical and strategic planning, legal and ethical issues, and cyber warfare systems development and acquisition.

abstract: The dynamic organization of cellular architecture is fundamental to understanding how structural adaptations drive specialized functions in eukaryotic cells. Despite advances in imaging, the mechanisms underlying spatial reorganization of organelles during differentiation, stress response, and disease remain poorly resolved at a systems level. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict large-scale intracellular reorganization by integrating high-resolution microscopy data with biophysical constraints. We propose to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate 3D spatial distributions of organelles under varying metabolic and mechanical conditions, using iterative agent-based modeling calibrated with experimental datasets from polarized epithelial cells and mesenchymal stem cells. Key challenges include scaling simulations to represent heterogeneous organelle interactions across micrometer-scale cellular volumes and optimizing parameter space exploration to identify critical thresholds for structural transitions. The computational pipeline will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods and machine learning-based pattern recognition to analyze simulation outputs against experimental benchmarks, including cryo-electron tomography and live-cell imaging trajectories. Successful implementation will provide predictive insights into how organelle positioning and cytoskeletal remodeling coordinate during processes such as epithelial polarization or stress-induced autophagy. This work will establish a publicly accessible toolkit for simulating cell-scale structural dynamics, filling a critical gap between molecular-scale modeling and tissue-level analyses. By linking subcellular anatomy to functional adaptability, the project aims to advance mechanistic understanding of cellular resilience in pathological contexts, including ischemic injury and age-related tissue degeneration. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of multi-parameter, multi-scale simulations, enabling transformative progress in quantitative cell biology.
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cells, cellular systems, and the molecular basis of cell structure and function. Includes instruction in cell biology, cell chemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, and structural biology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of neural circuit dynamics underlying adaptive and maladaptive behaviors, with a focus on anxiety-related disorders and addiction. A central challenge in behavioral neuroscience is characterizing how distributed neural populations encode, integrate, and transform information across timescales, particularly in scenarios requiring real-time behavioral adaptation. Current limitations in processing large-scale electrophysiological datasets (e.g., multi-region spike trains, local field potentials) and simulating biologically plausible neural network models hinder progress in mapping these processes. Our research integrates two computational approaches: (1) data-driven analysis of in vivo recordings from rodents performing decision-making tasks under threat-reward conflict, and (2) theory-driven simulations of cortico-limbic-striatal circuits using biologically constrained spiking neural network models. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale neural datasets through optimized machine learning pipelines for detecting cross-frequency coupling patterns and population coding dynamics. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated simulations will model circuit-level interactions between prefrontal cortical modules and subcortical structures under varying neuromodulatory states (e.g., dopamine, norepinephrine). This dual approach addresses critical gaps in relating cellular-resolution mechanisms to system-level behavioral outputs. Expected outcomes include novel computational frameworks for predicting stress-induced decision-making biases and identifying network resilience factors against addiction-related plasticity. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the need for parameter space exploration in neural models and high-dimensional data reduction—necessitates dedicated HPC support. By bridging mesoscale neural activity patterns with behavioral phenotypes, this work will provide foundational insights into the organizational principles of affective circuits while developing open-source tools for the neuroscience community. Results may inform future targets for neuromodulatory interventions in neuropsychiatric disorders, advancing experimental capabilities in computational psychiatry research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biological bases of behavior and psychological functioning, and their application to experimental and therapeutic research problems. Includes instruction in functional neuroanatomy, neural system development, biochemical neural regulatory mechanisms, neurological biophysics, memory storage and retrieval, physiology of cognition and perception, physiological bases of psychopathology and behavioral disorders, psychopharmacology, comparative psychobiology, molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, and specialized experimental design and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and evaluate dynamic, large-scale simulations of classroom environments for training pre-service teachers in adaptive instructional strategies. A critical challenge in teacher education is preparing educators to respond effectively to diverse, evolving classroom dynamics, including integrating technology equitably, addressing heterogeneous student needs, and managing real-time decision-making. Traditional training methods, such as role-playing or video case studies, lack the scalability and complexity to model the multivariate interactions between pedagogy, student behavior, and environmental factors. To address this gap, we propose building agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate classroom ecosystems under varied conditions (e.g., socioeconomic contexts, technology access, learning disabilities). These simulations will incorporate real-world datasets on student development, curriculum standards, and classroom interaction patterns to generate synthetic yet realistic scenarios. Using HPC resources, we will run parallelized simulations to test how different instructional approaches—such as project-based learning, differentiated instruction, or technology-mediated interventions—affect emergent outcomes like engagement, skill acquisition, and equity gaps. Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to identify high-leverage teaching practices and predict longitudinal impacts of pedagogical choices. The computational workload requires significant memory and processing power due to the high dimensionality of variables (e.g., 30+ student agents per classroom, each with unique behavioral parameters) and the need for Monte Carlo methods to assess probabilistic outcomes. Outcomes will inform the design of a scalable, AI-driven training platform for teacher candidates, enabling them to experiment with evidence-based strategies in risk-free virtual environments. This work advances the use of computational modeling in teacher education, offering a novel framework to bridge theoretical knowledge and practical skill development while addressing systemic educational inequities.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education that prepares individuals to be effective educators or trainers. Includes instruction in school reform and design; arts and technology in the classroom; theories of teaching and learning; adult and adolescent development; race, class, and gender dynamics; and the history and future of education in America.

abstract: This research seeks to investigate how spatial configurations in housing design influence the well-being and functional independence of aging populations, a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of architectural design, gerontology, and computational social science. Current housing standards often lack empirical rigor in addressing the dynamic interactions between elderly residents and their living environments, particularly as mobility and sensory capabilities decline. To address this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate human-environment interactions across diverse housing layouts. Agent-based modeling will simulate daily activities (e.g., navigation, object interaction) of virtual elderly agents with varying physical and cognitive profiles, while machine learning techniques will analyze emergent patterns of risk (e.g., fall likelihood, accessibility barriers). The simulations will integrate real-world data on movement patterns, ergonomic thresholds, and environmental stressors to parameterize agents and spaces. By iteratively testing design modifications—such as doorway widths, lighting gradients, and fixture placement—the project aims to identify optimal spatial features that mitigate hazards and promote autonomy. The computational intensity of modeling thousands of agent-environment interactions across multidimensional design variables necessitates HPC resources to achieve statistical robustness and granularity. Outcomes will yield a framework for evidence-based housing adaptations tailored to aging populations, with implications for architects, policymakers, and healthcare providers. This work bridges a critical methodological gap in housing studies by translating qualitative design principles into quantifiable, dynamic models, advancing both gerontechnology and computational design methodologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in housing and human environments, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation diffusion in digital political communication ecosystems, with a focus on how algorithmic curation and user engagement patterns on social media platforms amplify partisan content. As political discourse increasingly shifts online, understanding the interplay between platform architectures, user behavior, and message virality has become critical to addressing challenges to democratic deliberation. The research will employ large-scale computational social science methods, utilizing high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets comprising timestamped social media posts, network graphs of user interactions, and platform-specific metadata from three election cycles. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to classify political messaging strategies and detect misinformation markers across text, image, and video content, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will model information cascades in polarized networks. Agent-based simulations will further test hypotheses about attention economies and filter bubble formation. The scale of data ingestion (spanning 50M+ posts across six platforms) and the complexity of multimodal analysis necessitate HPC capabilities for distributed storage, parallelized model training, and real-time network visualization. Expected outcomes include 1) a computational framework for mapping cross-platform misinformation flows, 2) empirical evidence quantifying the relationship between platform affordances and divisive content amplification, and 3) policy-ready metrics for auditing algorithmic transparency in political contexts. By advancing methodological capacity to study sociotechnical systems at unprecedented granularity, this work will provide communication scholars and policymakers with tools to mitigate systemic risks to electoral integrity while preserving open digital public spheres. The requested computing resources directly enable the temporal, spatial, and multimodal analyses required to capture emergent phenomena in modern political communication.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human and media communication in the political process and that prepares individuals to function as members of political and public affairs organizations, political campaign staffs, and related government and media entities. Includes instruction in media effects, political speaking and debating, political advertising and marketing, image management, political journalism, opinion polling, and aspects of print and broadcast media related to the production and distribution of media messages in political settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern motorcycle systems, including advanced fuel injection, hybrid-electric powertrains, and integrated sensor networks, demands innovative approaches to diagnostics and performance optimization. Traditional maintenance techniques, which rely heavily on manual inspection and static diagnostic codes, struggle to address dynamic, interdependent failures in these systems. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model motorcycle systems under varied operating conditions, enabling predictive maintenance strategies and performance tuning. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to simulate multi-physics interactions within engine components, exhaust aftertreatment systems, and electrical networks at unprecedented resolution. Key computational methods include finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and thermal stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion and lubrication system optimization, and machine learning (ML) techniques to correlate sensor data streams with component degradation patterns. The research will utilize open-source simulation tools (e.g., OpenFOAM, FEniCS) alongside custom Python-based ML pipelines trained on experimental data from dynamometer tests and field-deployed motorcycles. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive failure models for high-stress components such as camshafts and catalytic converters, (2) optimized maintenance schedules reducing downtime by 15-30% in fleet operations, and (3) open-access datasets characterizing wear patterns in alternative fuel systems. By integrating HPC-driven insights with hands-on technician training protocols, this work bridges gaps between theoretical system dynamics and practical repair workflows. The computational models will additionally serve as educational tools in advanced diagnostics courses, preparing students to work with data-rich maintenance environments. Successful implementation will position motorcycle repair technology as a testbed for scalable computational methods applicable to broader small-engine and electric vehicle domains.
cip_title: Motorcycle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain motorcycles and other similar powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication and cooling systems, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuel systems and adjustments of moving parts.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate the dynamic interactions between environmental regulatory shifts and corporate financial decision-making, with a focus on emergent carbon accounting practices. Traditional accounting systems struggle to integrate real-time environmental data, probabilistic regulatory scenarios, and nonlinear market responses, creating valuation inaccuracies and strategic blind spots for firms navigating decarbonization mandates. We propose a hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning approach to analyze how heterogeneous firms adapt their capital allocation, risk disclosure, and operational strategies under evolving climate policy regimes. The ABM component will simulate firm interactions within competitive markets, incorporating multi-tiered supply chain dependencies and stakeholder pressure dynamics, while deep reinforcement learning modules will train adaptive agents on historical regulatory patterns and forward-looking climate scenario projections. High-performance computing resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of 10,000+ agent-firm simulations across geographies and industries, parallelize Monte Carlo experiments for policy uncertainty quantification, and process terabyte-scale datasets integrating financial disclosures, satellite emissions monitoring, and regulatory text corpora. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for stress-testing corporate carbon transition pathways under disputed valuation assumptions, (2) quantitative evidence on policy design features that accelerate accounting convergence for Scope 3 emissions, and (3) probabilistic industry benchmarks for climate-aligned capital budgeting. This work aims to advance computational accounting methodologies while providing actionable insights for standard-setting bodies and firms balancing financial resilience with planetary boundaries.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and business administration/management that prepares individuals to function as accountants and business managers.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in algebraic number theory and arithmetic geometry by addressing computational challenges inherent to studying class groups, Selmer groups, and rational points on higher-genus curves. The central problem involves developing scalable algorithms to analyze invariants of algebraic structures associated with number fields and elliptic curves, with applications to longstanding conjectures such as the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and the Cohen-Lenstra heuristics. Current methods for computing étale cohomology groups, regulator constants, or Tate-Shafarevich groups face exponential complexity when scaling to degrees or conductors relevant to theoretical predictions, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The proposed computational approach combines optimized implementations of p-adic cohomology algorithms, distributed parallelization of lattice-based attacks on Diophantine equations, and hybrid CPU-GPU architectures for sieving in quadratic form spaces. Key tasks include enumerating isomorphism classes of abelian extensions with prescribed ramification, computing Hecke eigenvalues for automorphic forms over totally real fields, and verifying divisibility properties in Iwasawa modules. These methods will leverage existing libraries (PARI/GP, SageMath) alongside custom C++/MPI codes for distributed memory models. Expected outcomes include the first large-scale verification of stability patterns in Tamagawa numbers under base change, empirical bounds for ranks of Jacobians of genus-2 curves, and open datasets of class group structures for fields of degree ≥6. The results will directly inform conjectures in Galois deformation theory and refine asymptotic models in analytic number theory. By overcoming memory and runtime barriers in exact arithmetic, this work will enable algebraic techniques to address problems previously accessible only through analytic or probabilistic approximations, strengthening synergies between computational experimentation and theoretical innovation in pure mathematics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the expression of quantities and their relationships by means of symbols, vectors, matrices, and equations, and the properties of integers. Includes instruction in algebraic structures, quadratic and automorphic forms, combinatorics, linear algebra, and algebraic geometry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making in juvenile corrections systems by modeling the dynamic interplay of behavioral, environmental, and institutional factors influencing rehabilitation outcomes. Despite advances in correctional practices, juvenile facilities often rely on static risk-assessment tools that fail to account for real-time behavioral data, situational stressors, or the heterogeneous needs of youth populations. This gap limits the ability to allocate resources effectively or predict the long-term impacts of intervention strategies. To address this, we propose an agent-based simulation platform that integrates individual-level psychological profiles, facility-specific operational constraints, and longitudinal recidivism data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the stochasticity and scalability required for these simulations, which will model thousands of synthetic agents across diverse demographic and behavioral categories. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibration and validation datasets derived from anonymized records of 15,000 juvenile cases, including behavioral logs, educational progress metrics, and post-release outcomes. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about the efficacy of targeted staffing allocations, therapeutic programming schedules, and crisis response protocols under varying resource constraints. The resulting models aim to identify cost-effective policy adjustments that reduce recidivism while maintaining facility safety. By bridging computational social science with correctional practice, this work will provide juvenile justice administrators with evidence-based tools to prioritize interventions for high-need individuals and simulate the systemic effects of resource reallocation before implementation. Anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation software adaptable to regional correctional contexts and a policy whiteboard outlining computational best practices for non-specialist stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to specialize in the provision of correction services to underage minor populations. Includes instruction in corrections, juvenile delinquency, juvenile development and psychology, juvenile law and justice administration, social services, record-keeping procedures, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize clinical decision-making and care coordination for complex patient populations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in real-time, evidence-based practice. Clinical Nurse Leaders (CNLs) face challenges in synthesizing heterogeneous data—including electronic health records, real-time physiological monitoring, and longitudinal patient histories—to guide interventions for high-acuity patients. Current methods often rely on static protocols or fragmented analyses, which may fail to capture dynamic interactions between comorbidities, treatment responses, and care team workflows. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation and predictive modeling approach. Agent-based models will simulate patient trajectories and care team interactions under varying clinical scenarios, parameterized by data from a retrospective cohort of 15,000+ patients with chronic cardiopulmonary conditions. Machine learning models, trained on this dataset, will predict risks of decompensation and resource bottlenecks. These components will be integrated into an HPC-optimized decision support tool, enabling CNLs to test intervention strategies in silico before implementation. The computational workflow requires parallel processing for large-scale parameter sweeps and real-time Bayesian updating of patient-specific predictions. Anticipated outcomes include validated models of care coordination efficiency, personalized risk stratification algorithms, and a prototype interface for scenario planning. This work will advance nursing science by establishing a methodological bridge between granular clinical data and systems-level care optimization, directly supporting the CNL role in improving patient outcomes while reducing preventable complications. By quantifying the impact of nurse-led interventions on care quality metrics, the project aims to generate scalable insights for evidence-based practice in acute and transitional care settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses for careers as clinical nurse leaders in which they work as part of an interdisciplinary team that provides direct medical care for patients based on evidence-based practice and research. Includes instruction in pharmacology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, research in nursing methods, advanced health assessment, statistics, and clinical practice management.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for real-time, large-scale sustainability accounting integration, addressing the growing disconnect between dynamic environmental impact data and traditional financial reporting systems. As corporations face increasing regulatory and stakeholder pressure to disclose sustainability metrics, existing accounting practices struggle to integrate complex, high-frequency environmental data streams—including satellite-derived deforestation rates, real-time carbon emissions tracking, and supply chain water usage patterns—with conventional financial statements. The proposed computational approach combines agent-based modeling of multi-tier supply networks with machine learning techniques for anomaly detection in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets from heterogeneous sources, including IoT sensor networks, global climate models, and blockchain-based transaction ledgers. The research will implement novel graph neural networks to map temporal relationships between environmental externalities and financial risk exposure while maintaining audit trails compliant with emerging sustainability reporting standards (e.g., EU CSRD, IFRS S2). Key computational challenges include developing hybrid architectures that reconcile the discrete event simulation requirements of supply chain modeling with the continuous data assimilation needs of carbon accounting systems. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated triple bottom line reporting, validated against Fortune 500 corporate datasets, that reduces manual reconciliation efforts by 70% while improving ESG metric accuracy across scope 3 emissions categories. This work bridges critical gaps between environmental science data infrastructures and accounting information systems, providing practitioners with scalable methods to operationalize planetary boundary constraints within conventional financial decision-making frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the profession of accounting and to perform related business functions. Includes instruction in accounting principles and theory, financial accounting, managerial accounting, cost accounting, budget control, tax accounting, legal aspects of accounting, auditing, reporting procedures, statement analysis, planning and consulting, business information systems, accounting research methods, professional standards and ethics, and applications to specific for-profit, public, and non-profit organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical need for culturally responsive computational tools to support K-12 STEM education in Tribal and First Nation schools. Despite growing efforts to integrate Indigenous knowledge systems into science curricula, educators face challenges in designing adaptive, place-based learning materials that align with both local cultural frameworks and state/national standards. Existing educational technologies often lack the flexibility to model the dynamic relationships between traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) and Western scientific concepts, limiting their utility in Indigenous classrooms. To bridge this gap, we propose developing an open-source, high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform for simulating and visualizing place-based STEM learning scenarios. The platform will leverage agent-based modeling to represent interactions between ecological systems, cultural practices, and pedagogical strategies specific to Southwestern Tribal communities. Computational workflows will integrate geospatial data, oral history databases, and Indigenous language corpora to generate customizable lesson prototypes. Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze historical educational outcomes and optimize culturally grounded problem-solving activities. By utilizing HPC resources, we aim to process multimodal datasets (including natural language, student interaction logs, and environmental sensor data) at scales necessary to account for regional diversity in Indigenous pedagogies. The project will partner with three Tribal school districts to co-design validation frameworks, ensuring computational outputs respect local epistemologies. Anticipated outcomes include a repository of validated simulation modules for teacher training programs and evidence-based guidelines for scaling place-based computational pedagogy. This work directly supports the preparation of educators to implement culturally sustaining STEM instruction while advancing methodological innovations in Indigenous education research through ethical HPC applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of instructional and advising services for American Indian, Alaska Native, and Hawaiian Native students at various learning levels and that prepares individuals to perform teaching and administrative functions in Tribal/First Nation schools. Includes instruction in the cultural traditions and social patterns, history and politics, learning styles and issues, curriculum design, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling techniques and social issues, rural education services, distance education, adult education techniques, school administration, applicable laws and regulations, and research issues.

abstract: The increasing complexity of patient care in clinical settings necessitates innovative approaches to optimize workflows and improve outcomes for nursing assistants and patient care aides. This project addresses the challenge of modeling patient-caregiver interactions and care delivery patterns in high-acuity environments, where dynamic staffing needs and heterogeneous patient populations create inefficiencies. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop agent-based simulations of nursing aide workflows, integrating real-world data from electronic health records (EHRs), time-motion studies, and wearable sensors. These simulations will model multi-agent systems representing patients with varying acuity levels, nursing aides, and environmental factors across hospital and long-term care facility contexts. Machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks and clustering algorithms, will be applied to identify patterns in care delays, predict task completion times, and evaluate the impact of staffing ratios on patient outcomes such as fall risk and pressure injury incidence. The computational demands of processing high-resolution temporal data (e.g., minute-by-minute caregiver movement patterns) and running Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of scenario permutations require parallelized computing architectures. Expected outcomes include evidence-based recommendations for task prioritization protocols and a predictive tool for identifying high-risk care transitions. By quantifying relationships between aide workload distribution and quality metrics, this research aims to inform both operational decisions in healthcare facilities and competency-based training programs for nursing assistants. The resulting computational framework will provide a novel platform for testing interventions to reduce cognitive overload and improve care team coordination, directly addressing critical challenges in nursing science education and clinical practice.
cip_title: Nursing Assistant/ Aide and Patient Care Assistant/ Aide
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine nursing-related services to patients in hospitals or long-term care facilities, under the training and supervision of a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse.

abstract: Atmospheric chemistry and climate systems are intricately linked through complex feedback mechanisms involving aerosols, trace gases, and radiative processes. Current models often inadequately resolve these interactions at regional scales, particularly in understudied regions such as the rapidly warming Arctic and tropical marine boundary layers, leading to uncertainties in climate projections. This project seeks to advance understanding of aerosol-cloud-climate interactions and the role of short-lived climate forcers (SLCFs) using high-resolution simulations that integrate atmospheric chemistry with dynamic climatological processes. The primary computational challenge lies in resolving fine-scale processes (e.g., aerosol nucleation, heterogeneous chemistry, and cloud microphysics) while maintaining global scalability over multi-decadal timescales. We propose to employ the Community Earth System Model (CESM) with customized chemistry-climate coupling, enhanced with a GPU-accelerated version of the Modal Aerosol Module (MAM4) and nested regional grids (3–5 km resolution) over target domains. This setup will leverage petascale computing resources to perform ensemble simulations under varying emission scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0) and conduct sensitivity analyses on ozone-depleting halogen chemistry and secondary organic aerosol formation. Data assimilation techniques will integrate satellite-derived aerosol optical depth (AOD) and in situ trace gas measurements to constrain model uncertainties. The expected outcomes include improved quantification of aerosol indirect effects on Arctic amplification, refined estimates of methane’s regional radiative forcing, and identification of SLCF mitigation co-benefits for climate and air quality. These results will directly inform the next IPCC assessment cycle and provide actionable insights for policymakers addressing both climate change and tropospheric ozone pollution. The computational demands—requiring ~2 million core-hours, 200 TB of storage, and GPU-accelerated workloads for machine learning-based parameterization—necessitate dedicated high-performance computing allocation to achieve the proposed resolution and ensemble size within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of atmospheric constituents, reactions, measurement techniques, and processes in predictive, current, and historical contexts. Includes instruction in climate modeling, gases and aerosols, trace gases, aqueous phase chemistry, sinks, transport mechanisms, computer measurement, climate variability, paleoclimatology, climate diagnosis, numerical modeling and data analysis, ionization, recombination, photoemission, and plasma chemistry.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of cross-lingual neural language models capable of capturing syntactic and semantic regularities across typologically diverse languages. Current language models often underperform on low-resource languages due to data sparsity and structural dissimilarities from high-resource languages like English. The project addresses this limitation through a computational linguistics framework that integrates transformer-based architectures with structured linguistic annotations, including universal dependency parses and morphological typology features. The core research problem involves designing dynamic alignment mechanisms that enable knowledge transfer between languages with divergent grammatical systems while minimizing catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning. Methodologically, the work combines large-scale multilingual corpus preprocessing (covering 50+ languages from 15 language families), neural architecture search for optimal cross-lingual attention configurations, and systematic evaluation using both intrinsic linguistic probes (e.g., grammatical agreement tests) and downstream tasks (machine translation, semantic parsing). HPC resources are essential for training billion-parameter models on heterogeneous linguistic data, conducting ablation studies across architectural variants, and processing parallel text-annotation streams at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) open-source models demonstrating improved zero-shot performance on understudied languages, 2) quantitative insights into the relationship between linguistic typology and transfer learning efficiency, and 3) novel methods for integrating discrete linguistic constraints into neural representations.
