The computational infrastructure will enable experiments requiring 15,000+ GPU hours, including multilingual pretraining runs with 2TB of text data and real-time syntactic feature injection pipelines. By bridging formal linguistic theory with deep learning scalability challenges, this work aims to establish more equitable NLP tools while advancing fundamental understanding of how machines acquire cross-linguistic generalizations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationship between computer and human language and computational techniques applied to natural language. Includes instruction in computer programming, human languages, linguistic analysis, logic, natural language processing, semantics, machine learning, psycholinguistics, software engineering, and syntax.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving cultural narratives surrounding chronic illness through computational analysis of historical and contemporary medical literature, patient-authored texts, and public health communications. The research problem centers on understanding how sociocultural values, ethical frameworks, and power dynamics have shaped representations of chronic disease across different eras and communities—a gap in current health humanities scholarship that traditional qualitative methods alone cannot address at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze multimodal datasets spanning 4.5 million pages of digitized texts from 1850 to present, including medical journals, personal diaries, policy documents, and visual media captions. Custom transformer models will be trained to detect patterns in disease conceptualization, tracing shifts in metaphorical language, moral attributions, and patient agency narratives across temporal, geographic, and demographic axes. Network analysis will map the co-evolution of medical authority structures and lay health epistemologies, while GPU-accelerated topic modeling will identify latent themes in understudied patient communities. The computational demands of processing heterogeneous historical documents—including OCR correction of archival materials and multimodal alignment of text-image relationships—require parallelized workflows and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible annotated corpus documenting two centuries of chronic illness discourse, 2) computational models for ethical analysis of health narratives, and 3) new frameworks for understanding how cultural representations influence healthcare disparities. By bridging humanistic inquiry with scalable computational methods, this project aims to establish novel methodologies for critical health humanities research while generating insights with practical applications in medical education and equitable care design.
cip_definition: A program that explores the ethical, historical, literary, philosophical, and religious dimensions of medicine or health. Includes instruction in art, cultural studies, economics, ethics, history, literature, medical anthropology, philosophy, religion and spiritual thought, science and technology, visual art, and writing.

abstract: The rapid evolution of broadcast media demands innovative technical solutions to address challenges in real-time content production, high-resolution streaming, and adaptive audience engagement. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize computational workflows for next-generation radio and television broadcasting. Specifically, we aim to tackle the inefficiencies in processing 4K/8K video feeds, synchronizing multi-channel audio in live environments, and automating quality control through machine learning (ML) models. Current consumer-grade hardware struggles with the latency and computational load required for real-time rendering, dynamic bitrate adaptation, and AI-driven content analysis, particularly in live sports, news, and interactive talk shows. Our research will employ parallelized GPU-accelerated encoding/decoding algorithms, distributed audio-video synchronization frameworks, and neural networks trained on broadcast-quality datasets to minimize processing delays and enhance production scalability. By simulating large-scale virtual production environments and stress-testing network configurations, we will identify bottlenecks in existing broadcast pipelines and propose optimized resource allocation strategies. The outcomes will include open-source software tools for automated error detection in live feeds, predictive bandwidth allocation models, and adaptive lighting/camera control systems powered by real-time analytics. These advancements will directly benefit educational training in broadcasting technology by providing students with access to industry-standard computational workflows while reducing the cost barriers associated with high-end production hardware. The project’s significance lies in bridging the gap between academic training and emerging industry practices, ensuring graduates are prepared to implement scalable, efficient solutions in a media landscape increasingly reliant on computationally intensive technologies. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the fidelity and speed required for prototyping these systems at production scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the production of radio and television programs, and related operations, under the supervision of broadcast and studio managers, directors, editors, and producers. Includes instruction in sound, lighting, and camera operation and maintenance; power and feed control; studio operations; production preparation; broadcast engineering; related computer applications; and specialized applications such as news, entertainment, live talk, sports, commercials, and taping.

abstract: Aerospace systems demand increasingly sophisticated computational tools to address complex challenges in design, testing, and operational performance. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on high-fidelity simulations of next-generation aircraft propulsion systems, with a focus on optimizing hybrid-electric architectures. Current models struggle to capture the coupled aerothermal, structural, and electromagnetic interactions inherent in these systems, limiting predictive accuracy during early design phases. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and transient electrical network simulations. The HPC environment will enable parallelized execution of coupled solvers using partitioned coupling algorithms, with adaptive mesh refinement for boundary layer resolution in turbulent flow regions. Large-scale parametric studies will assess performance across flight envelopes, while machine learning surrogates trained on simulation data will accelerate design space exploration. Expected outcomes include validated models for hybrid-electric propulsion thermal management, identification of optimal component integration strategies, and reduced prototyping costs through virtual testing. By leveraging HPC resources, this work will directly support the development of energy-efficient propulsion technologies aligned with net-zero aviation goals. The computational workflows developed will also provide a template for analyzing other multi-physics aerospace systems, such as hypersonic vehicle thermal protection or reusable spacecraft re-entry dynamics. Resource requests emphasize GPU-accelerated nodes for tensor operations in surrogate model training and high-memory nodes for resolving fine-scale combustion dynamics in afterburner simulations. This project bridges critical gaps in aerospace engineering technology by enabling high-accuracy virtual prototyping capabilities that are inaccessible with current institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing aircraft, spacecraft and their systems. Includes instruction in aircraft/spacecraft systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of ancient urban networks through large-scale spatiotemporal simulation and machine learning-driven artifact analysis. While traditional archaeological methods have reconstructed past societies through localized excavations and qualitative interpretations, the integration of computational modeling and big data analytics remains underdeveloped in the field, limiting insights into systemic interactions across regions and eras. Our research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate trade, migration, and resource distribution patterns in the Bronze Age Aegean (3000–1100 BCE), a critical period of early urbanization. The ABMs will incorporate heterogeneous datasets, including settlement surveys, climatic proxies, ceramic provenance records, and textual archives, to test hypotheses about how socioenvironmental pressures influenced connectivity among emerging palatial centers. Concurrently, deep learning algorithms will be trained on a corpus of 50,000+ digitized pottery fragments to automate the classification of stylistic motifs, enabling quantitative analysis of cultural transmission dynamics. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the ABM parameter space exploration and 3D convolutional neural networks for artifact imagery—necessitates parallelized processing, high-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration unavailable on local infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models identifying key drivers of ancient economic resilience, (2) an open-access toolset for stylistic seriation of archaeological materials, and (3) novel frameworks for interdisciplinary data integration in regional studies. By bridging computational science and archaeological theory, this work will establish scalable methodologies for investigating long-term human responses to complexity and crisis, with implications for both heritage science and contemporary urban sustainability debates.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of extinct societies, and the past of living societies, via the excavation, analysis and interpretation of their artifactual, human, and associated remains. Includes instruction in archeological theory, field methods, dating methods, conservation and museum studies, cultural and physical evolution, and the study of specific selected past cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interactions between legal frameworks, market forces, and environmental constraints in urban land development. As real estate and land development law increasingly intersects with complex systems—such as climate adaptation policies, algorithmic valuation tools, and multi-jurisdictional regulatory conflicts—traditional legal analysis struggles to account for nonlinear feedback loops and emergent outcomes. The research problem centers on quantifying how iterative changes to zoning laws, tax incentives, or sustainability mandates propagate through development ecosystems, influencing long-term urban form and equity. Using high-performance computing resources, the project will deploy agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate stakeholder decision-making—including developers, municipalities, and community groups—under varying legal scenarios. Computational legal analytics methods will process structured and unstructured data from case law, municipal codes, and environmental impact reports to parameterize models. A parallel focus involves training graph neural networks (GNNs) to map precedent citation networks in land use litigation, identifying patterns that predict judicial outcomes. The integration of ABM and GNNs aims to reveal latent dependencies between localized legal decisions and systemic risks, such as displacement cascades or infrastructure fragility. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating policy impacts at metropolitan scales and a novel dataset linking legal reasoning architectures to development trajectories. By bridging computational social science with legal informatics, this work advances evidence-based approaches to statutory design while addressing critical gaps in how legal education engages with complex systems analytics. The requested resources will enable large-scale sensitivity analyses across 10^4 parameter combinations and real-time visualization of multi-agent interactions, tasks infeasible without parallelized computing architectures.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize patient care unit workflows in hospital settings through advanced simulation and predictive modeling. Health unit coordinators (HUCs) face dynamic challenges in managing administrative tasks, such as scheduling procedures, coordinating staff, and prioritizing patient needs, all while balancing time-sensitive communication across interdisciplinary teams. Current manual or rule-based systems often struggle to adapt to real-time variables, including fluctuating patient volumes, emergent care demands, and resource constraints. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that models patient flow, staff availability, and task interdependencies within a virtual ward environment. The platform will integrate anonymized electronic health record (EHR) datasets, historical staff activity logs, and real-time sensor data (where available) to train agent-based models and reinforcement learning algorithms. These models will simulate scenarios such as surge capacity planning, task prioritization under resource limitations, and interruption management—common pain points for HUCs. By leveraging parallel computing, we will iteratively test thousands of workflow configurations to identify optimal strategies for minimizing delays, reducing clerical errors, and improving care team coordination. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of historical workflow inefficiencies and prospective pilot studies in partner hospitals. The outcomes will include open-source predictive tools for HUC training programs and adaptive scheduling templates that respond to real-time ward conditions. This work directly supports the Health Unit Coordinator field by translating computational insights into practical strategies for enhancing administrative efficiency, ultimately contributing to safer patient care and reduced operational costs in healthcare facilities. Access to HPC resources is critical due to the scale of multivariate simulations and the need for rapid model iteration to reflect diverse clinical environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced stochastic optimization models to address dynamic resource allocation challenges in large-scale, human-in-the-loop operational systems, such as supply chain logistics and healthcare delivery networks. A critical gap exists in existing methods to handle real-time decision-making under uncertainty with high-dimensional state spaces and nonlinear constraints, particularly when human operators influence system behavior through intermittent interventions. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework integrating two-stage stochastic programming with scenario reduction techniques and decomposition algorithms tailored for parallel computing architectures. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to solve multi-objective mixed-integer programming models with embedded machine learning surrogates, which capture human decision patterns from historical intervention data. Key computational challenges include managing memory-intensive scenario trees, solving nested Lagrangian dual problems via distributed optimization, and conducting sensitivity analyses on intervention impact parameters. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive resource allocation in partially automated systems, validated through case studies on hospital staff scheduling under demand surges and resilient inventory routing for perishable goods. The HPC environment is essential to achieve tractable solve times for instances involving >10^6 decision variables and to enable rapid re-optimization cycles required for real-world implementation. By advancing both methodological rigor and computational scalability, this work will provide operations researchers with new capabilities to design human-centered systems that balance automation with expert oversight, ultimately improving resource utilization efficiency by 15-30% in pilot applications compared to conventional static allocation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary dialectal variation in the German language. The research addresses a critical gap in German philology: the systematic mapping of phonetic, morphological, and syntactic shifts across regional dialects, particularly in underdocumented rural areas and transitional zones between major dialect groups. While traditional dialectology relies on manual corpus analysis, the scale and complexity of modern linguistic datasets—including audio recordings, digitized historical texts, and sociolinguistic surveys—demand advanced computational methods. The project will develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze multi-modal data spanning the 19th century to the present, with a focus on identifying patterns of language change influenced by migration, urbanization, and digital communication. Computational workflows will include neural network-based phonetic alignment for comparing archival speech samples, transformer models for syntactic divergence detection, and phylogenetic algorithms to model dialect evolution. A key innovation involves adapting speech recognition architectures to low-resource German dialects, which lack standardized orthographies. By parallelizing these processes across HPC nodes, the team aims to process over 50,000 hours of audio and 10 million text tokens within the grant period. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of dynamically mapped German dialect features, predictive models of language shift in border regions (e.g., Frisian-Low German contact zones), and methodological frameworks for computational dialectology applicable to minority languages globally. This work will directly support preservation initiatives and inform policy on language education in multilingual communities, while advancing interdisciplinary connections between linguistics and computational science. The requested resources are essential for handling memory-intensive phonetic analyses and training domain-specific language models, tasks infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the German language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The development of advanced polymers with tailored functional properties requires precise understanding of structure-dynamics relationships at molecular scales. Experimental characterization of these relationships in complex polymer systems remains limited by resolution and throughput, particularly when targeting unstable or dynamically evolving assemblies. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to establish predictive multiscale models that bridge quantum mechanical interactions, mesoscale polymer dynamics, and bulk material behavior. Computational workflows will integrate reactive force field molecular dynamics (ReaxFF MD) to simulate polymerization mechanisms under varied thermodynamic conditions, coarse-grained MD for long-timescale phase segregation studies, and machine learning algorithms trained on simulation datasets to identify key descriptors linking synthesis parameters to emergent properties. The primary focus will be on two industrially relevant challenges: (1) designing photo-responsive polymers for optoelectronic applications, requiring explicit modeling of exciton transfer through conjugated backbones, and (2) optimizing catalytic degradation pathways for environmentally persistent perfluorinated polymers. Anticipated outcomes include validated protocols for simulating metastable polymer phases, open-source tools for automated parameterization of reactive polymer systems, and structure-property guidelines to inform the synthesis of next-generation adaptive materials. By enabling atomistic insight into processes inaccessible to laboratory observation—such as real-time bond rearrangement during stress-induced polymer failure—this work aims to significantly reduce iterative experimentation in polymer development while advancing fundamental theories of macromolecular assembly. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieve the necessary sampling of conformational landscapes and chemical space, with individual simulations spanning >10^6 processor-hours for systems exceeding 1 million atoms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of synthesized macromolecules and their interactions with other substances. Includes instruction in molecular bonding theory, polymerization, properties and behavior of unstable compounds, the development of tailored polymers, transition phenomena, and applications to specific industrial problems and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of moral reasoning and collective decision-making in politically polarized environments through an interdisciplinary lens integrating computational social science, behavioral economics, and formal epistemology. The research problem centers on understanding how heterogeneous belief systems—shaped by philosophical frameworks, economic incentives, and institutional structures—interact to produce stable or unstable societal equilibria. While existing studies often analyze polarization through single-discipline models, this work proposes a novel agent-based simulation platform that operationalizes concepts from social epistemology (e.g., testimony, epistemic trust) and political economy (e.g., public goods dilemmas, preference aggregation) within a unified computational framework. The computational approach combines game-theoretic models of strategic interaction with network-based opinion diffusion algorithms, scaled to simulate populations of up to 10^6 agents with dynamically evolving belief matrices. High-performance computing resources are essential for parameter space exploration across diverse scenarios, including the effects of misinformation campaigns, redistributive policies, and deliberative democratic interventions on collective rationality. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of conditions under which polarized groups converge toward cooperative equilibria versus descending into epistemic fragmentation, and (2) empirically testable hypotheses about institutional designs that mitigate polarization while preserving pluralism. By bridging normative philosophy with computational social dynamics, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for studying complex societal challenges and provide policymakers with evidence-based frameworks for fostering resilient democratic discourse.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on philosophical foundations, political institutions, collective behavior, economic theory, and economic influences. Includes instruction in econometrics, logic, metaphysics, moral responsibility, philosophy of language, philosophy of perception, philosophy through history, reasoning and persuasion, and social epistemology.

abstract: The optimization of animal feed formulations to enhance productivity and health requires a comprehensive understanding of nutrient interactions at metabolic, genomic, and microbiological levels. Current experimental approaches face limitations in resolving the non-linear dynamics of nutrient utilization, host-microbiome interactions, and their combined effects on animal physiology. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing multi-scale computational models to simulate nutrient metabolism in livestock species, with a focus on cattle and poultry. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate transcriptomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic datasets to construct dynamic models of metabolic flux across tissues and microbial communities. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to predict optimal feed compositions under varying physiological conditions, while molecular dynamics simulations will elucidate structure-function relationships of key enzymes involved in nutrient absorption and conversion. The computational framework will be validated against empirical data from in vivo trials measuring growth performance, metabolic markers, and microbiome profiles. This project aims to identify novel feed additive synergies, reduce reliance on unsustainable dietary components, and improve predictions of nutrient requirements during stress or disease. Outcomes will provide a scalable platform for precision nutrition strategies, directly contributing to advancements in sustainable animal agriculture and food security. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the computational complexity of multi-omics integration, large-scale parameter optimization, and stochastic modeling of biological variability across populations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biology and chemistry of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, water, vitamins, and feed additives as related to animal health and the production of improved animal products. Includes instruction in nutrition science, animal health and physiology, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, animal husbandry, and food science.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling complex ethical and doctrinal systems across diverse religious traditions using computational methods, with a focus on identifying cross-cultural patterns in moral reasoning and metaphysical frameworks. While qualitative analysis has dominated philosophical and religious studies, the scale and structural complexity of sacred texts, commentaries, and ritual practices necessitate quantitative approaches. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-lingual corpora spanning Buddhist sutras, Abrahamic scriptures, Hindu philosophical treatises, and Indigenous oral tradition transcripts. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to map argument structures, ethical imperatives, and ontological claims, while graph-based neural networks will model relationships between concepts such as suffering, justice, and transcendence. A parallelized framework will enable comparative analysis of over 10,000 texts across 15 linguistic traditions, accounting for historical semantic shifts through transformer models trained on diachronic data. The computational workload—involving terabyte-scale text processing, high-dimensional embedding spaces, and Monte Carlo simulations of ethical decision-making scenarios—requires GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include: (1) a taxonomy of moral reasoning patterns correlated with cosmological frameworks, (2) probabilistic models predicting how specific theological axioms influence ethical systems, and (3) open-source tools for computational philosophy of religion. This work pioneers methods to systematically test long-standing philosophical hypotheses about religious worldviews while preserving hermeneutic nuance, bridging analytic philosophy’s formal rigor with religious studies’ interpretive traditions. Results will advance interdisciplinary dialogue about universalism versus cultural particularism in ethics and metaphysics.
cip_definition: A general program that combines the study of philosophy and religious studies. Includes instruction in logic; ethics; epistemology; symbolism; phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature, and art of religion; and world religions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the gap in evidence-based, personalized protocols for facial treatments by leveraging computational modeling to simulate skin biomechanical responses under varying therapeutic interventions. Despite advances in cosmetic science, facialists rely heavily on generalized product formulations and manual techniques, which may not account for individual variations in skin elasticity, hydration, or sensitivity. Current training models lack predictive tools to optimize treatment outcomes or mitigate adverse reactions. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with machine learning (ML) to model the dynamic interactions between facial tissues and treatment modalities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate multi-layered skin deformation, chemical diffusion, and thermal effects during procedures such as exfoliation, massage, or mask application. A dataset of 3D facial scans, histology-derived material properties, and clinical treatment records will inform model parameters. ML algorithms will iteratively refine predictions of short- and long-term skin responses based on demographic, genetic, and environmental variables. The computational pipeline will output personalized treatment recommendations, including pressure thresholds during massage, optimal product viscosity, and exposure times for chemical agents. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for training facialists in virtual scenarios, reducing trial-and-error practices in live settings. This project will establish a novel interdisciplinary nexus between cosmetology, biomechanics, and data science, advancing the field toward precision skincare while maintaining compliance with dermatological safety standards. The scalability of HPC-enabled models will further enable future research into rare skin conditions or underrepresented demographic groups, fostering equity in aesthetic healthcare accessibility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and scalp with chemical and cosmetic preparations, and to function as licensed facial specialists in specialized and full service salons.  Includes instruction in facial surface anatomy; skin properties; skin decontamination and infection control; facial massage; facial makeup; facial wrapping; selection and application of creams, lotions, oils, and other chemicals and cosmetics; European and other facial techniques; client evaluation and care; applicable laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Thai language and literature, addressing critical gaps in digital philology, dialectology, and textual analysis. Thai, a tonal language with a complex orthographic system and significant regional dialect variation, presents unique challenges for computational modeling. Existing tools for text processing, corpus linguistics, and dialect mapping remain underdeveloped compared to those for Indo-European languages, limiting scholarly analysis and practical applications in areas such as natural language processing (NLP), cultural preservation, and educational technology. Our research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) developing machine learning models to analyze syntactic and semantic patterns in classical and modern Thai literature, (2) creating a computationally derived dialect atlas of Thai regional varieties using acoustic and lexical data, and (3) building a searchable digital corpus of historical Thai texts with automated annotation for philological study. The computational workflow will integrate neural language models, phonetic alignment algorithms, and graph-based methods for dialect similarity mapping, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale text (10+ GB) and audio datasets. HPC resources will enable rapid training of transformer-based architectures for low-resource language tasks, dynamic visualization of dialect boundaries, and efficient storage/retrieval of annotated textual data. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for Thai NLP, a public repository of linguistically tagged texts and audio recordings, and novel interdisciplinary frameworks for studying language change and literary style. This work will directly support Thailand’s efforts to preserve linguistic diversity amid rapid sociocultural shifts while providing foundational infrastructure for global researchers in Southeast Asian studies. By bridging computational methods with humanistic inquiry, the project aims to redefine analytical paradigms in Thai philology and empower cross-disciplinary applications in education, technology, and heritage management.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Thai languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interdependencies within family systems through computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate complex interactions that influence resilience and adaptation during sociocultural stressors. Family systems theory posits that familial relationships operate as interconnected networks, yet quantitative analysis of these nonlinear, multigenerational dynamics remains underdeveloped due to computational limitations. The research problem centers on identifying critical thresholds and feedback mechanisms that govern family stability or fragmentation under external pressures such as economic instability, migration, or health crises. By constructing agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate behavioral, sociodemographic, and temporal data, this study will simulate family decision-making processes across diverse cultural contexts. The computational approach employs parallelized Monte Carlo methods to explore parameter spaces, Bayesian networks to infer latent relational patterns, and machine learning techniques to classify emergent family archetypes. Datasets include longitudinal surveys, ethnographic interviews, and public records, harmonized into a graph-based structure representing kinship ties, communication flows, and resource allocation strategies. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale of stochastic simulations (10^5+ iterations) and the high dimensionality of variables encoding emotional, economic, and cultural factors. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for mapping family adaptive capacities, identifying intervention points to mitigate systemic collapse, and generating evidence-based guidelines for culturally responsive support programs. This work bridges computational social science and family systems theory, offering novel methodologies to analyze human relational systems at unprecedented granularity. Results will advance both academic discourse and practical tools for policymakers, therapists, and community organizations working to strengthen familial infrastructures in rapidly changing societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the family as a social unit in its developmental, dynamic, comparative, and structural aspects, and the significance of the family as a system that impacts individuals and society. Includes instruction in related principles of sociology, psychology, behavioral sciences, and the humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the interdisciplinary study of historical textual transmission and cultural exchange through large-scale computational analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in digital humanities: the inability to efficiently process and analyze vast, multilingual corpora spanning multiple centuries, which are essential for tracing the evolution of ideas, textual reuse, and cross-cultural influence. Traditional methods, limited by scale and computational power, struggle to identify subtle patterns in syntax, semantic shifts, or intertextual connections across such datasets. The proposed work will develop and apply machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures and graph neural networks, to map textual relationships within a curated corpus of over 50,000 digitized manuscripts, pamphlets, and printed works from 1500–1900. These models will be trained to detect stylistic features, semantic anomalies, and citation networks, while accounting for OCR errors, orthographic variations, and multilingual contexts. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) pipelines with geospatial and temporal metadata to visualize knowledge dissemination pathways. HPC resources are essential for training large language models on heterogeneous historical data, parallelizing feature extraction across distributed systems, and optimizing memory-intensive tasks such as network graph generation. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for diachronic text analysis, novel metrics for quantifying textual influence, and case studies demonstrating how computational methods can revise existing narratives about the circulation of Enlightenment-era political texts. By enabling scalable analysis of understudied primary sources, this project aims to bridge methodological divides between computational linguistics and traditional hermeneutics, offering humanities scholars new frameworks for interrogating cultural change at unprecedented granularity.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in digital humanities and textual studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for high-integrity welded joints in advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, and robotic automation requires precise control of welding processes under complex multi-physics conditions. However, traditional experimental methods and low-fidelity simulations struggle to resolve dynamic interactions between thermal gradients, phase transformations, residual stresses, and molten pool behavior at the spatiotemporal scales relevant to industrial applications. This project seeks to address these challenges through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled modeling of arc welding processes, with a focus on optimizing parameter selection and predicting defect formation in multi-pass steel welds. A coupled computational framework will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for heat transfer and stress evolution, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for melt pool dynamics, and machine learning (ML) for rapid parameter optimization. High-resolution simulations will capture microstructural changes during rapid solidification using CALPHAD-based phase prediction tools, while parallelized thermal-mechanical models will quantify distortion and residual stress accumulation across sequential weld passes. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of 3D transient simulations with adaptive meshing, particularly when analyzing the effects of process variables (e.g., travel speed, current waveform) on defect susceptibility metrics like hot cracking indices. Validation will leverage experimental data from in-situ monitoring systems, including high-speed imaging and acoustic emission sensors. Expected outcomes include a predictive digital twin framework capable of reducing trial-and-error prototyping by 40-60% for complex joint configurations, as well as new insights into process-structure-property relationships for emerging wire-arc additive manufacturing applications. By enabling atomistic-to-macroscale simulations on timescales aligned with industrial R&D cycles, this work will directly support workforce training in computational welding engineering and advance the adoption of AI-driven process control systems in welding technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the design and engineering of welding and joining systems and the implementation of welding processes. Includes instruction in materials science; computer-aided design; welding design; welding processes; welding metallurgy; automation and robotics; and codes, inspections, testing, and quality assurance.

abstract: The study of African-American/Black diasporic history and literature requires synthesizing vast, heterogeneous datasets spanning centuries and geographies, from colonial-era manuscripts to contemporary digital archives. Traditional humanities methods face challenges in systematically analyzing these materials at scale, particularly in identifying transnational patterns of cultural exchange, resistance, and identity formation across North America and the Caribbean. This project requests high-performance computing resources to apply advanced computational methods to three interrelated tasks: (1) topic modeling and semantic analysis of 18th–20th century Black newspapers, pamphlets, and literary works to trace the evolution of political rhetoric; (2) network analysis of correspondence and organizational records to reconstruct intellectual collaborations among Black writers and activists; and (3) geospatial mapping of migration narratives in oral histories and fiction using NLP-derived metadata. The computational pipeline will integrate custom Python scripts for text preprocessing, TensorFlow models for style transfer analysis in multilingual texts (including French- and Spanish-language Caribbean sources), and graph databases to visualize knowledge networks. By processing over 15TB of digitized primary sources—many previously unstudied as cohesive corpora—this work aims to reveal how Black communities sustained ideological coherence amid displacement and adaptation. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of diasporic cultural production and peer-reviewed publications redefining periodization models in Black literary studies. The project demonstrates how HPC-enabled humanities research can recover marginalized epistemic traditions while providing scalable methodologies for interdisciplinary diaspora studies. Resource requirements emphasize GPU-accelerated NLP training and distributed storage for collaborative annotation of sensitive historical materials.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: The proposed interdisciplinary research examines the complex evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in digitally connected societies, integrating methodologies from computational linguistics, historical sociology, and behavioral analytics. Current scholarship lacks robust frameworks to analyze how traditional cultural systems interact with global digital information flows, particularly across underrepresented linguistic communities. This project addresses this gap by developing scalable computational models that synthesize ethnographic records, multilingual social media data, and digitized historical documents. The research requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage three core challenges: (1) processing petabyte-scale unstructured text across 40+ languages using transformer-based NLP models, (2) simulating multi-agent cultural transmission networks with >10^6 node populations, and (3) conducting temporal graph analyses spanning two centuries of cultural exchange data. Methodological innovations include hybrid neural architectures for cross-lingual semantic alignment, adaptive sampling techniques for sparse historical data, and uncertainty-aware agent-based modeling. Anticipated outcomes comprise a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping cultural convergence/divergence patterns, predictive metrics for cultural resilience under information overload scenarios, and open-source tools for interdisciplinary digital humanities research. By enabling simultaneous analysis of micro-level individual behaviors and macro-level societal trends, this work provides new insights into preserving cultural diversity in the digital age while demonstrating how computationally intensive humanities research can leverage HPC ecosystems. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous datasets, and large-memory simulations impractical on standard academic computing clusters, ultimately advancing multidisciplinary methodologies for studying cultural complexity in the 21st century.
cip_definition: A program that derives from two or more distinct programs and that is integrated around a unifying theme or topic that cannot be subsumed under a single discipline or occupational field.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face mounting pressure to enhance efficiency and resilience amid climate variability, population growth, and resource constraints. Current approaches to optimizing crop management often rely on fragmented models that lack the computational capacity to integrate high-resolution environmental, genetic, and operational data. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a scalable, high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate and predict crop responses under dynamic agricultural scenarios. The research will focus on coupling process-based crop growth models with machine learning algorithms to analyze interactions between genotype, environment, and management practices. Key objectives include parameterizing multi-scale simulations using heterogeneous datasets—such as genomic sequences of stress-tolerant crop varieties, UAV-derived hyperspectral imagery, and IoT sensor networks monitoring microclimatic conditions—and conducting ensemble runs to identify robust strategies for irrigation, nutrient application, and planting density. HPC resources will enable parallel execution of thousands of simulations across diverse agroecological contexts, facilitating real-time optimization of management decisions through adaptive algorithms. Expected outcomes include predictive tools that quantify trade-offs between yield stability, input use efficiency, and economic returns under climate uncertainty. These tools will support precision agriculture applications, enabling producers to tailor practices to localized conditions while reducing environmental footprints. The project will also deliver open-source computational workflows to accelerate agricultural systems modeling, fostering collaboration across research institutions. By leveraging HPC capabilities to overcome scalability barriers in traditional agronomic models, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in crop production, directly contributing to global food security and sustainable intensification efforts.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural production operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of disaster response logistics demands real-time integration of heterogeneous data streams—including social media, satellite imagery, and IoT sensor networks—to optimize resource deployment and situational awareness. Existing decision-support systems lack the computational scalability to process multi-modal data under latency constraints, leading to suboptimal coordination during critical events. This project proposes the development of a dynamic, graph-based resource allocation framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to model evolving disaster scenarios, prioritize interventions, and simulate cascading impacts across infrastructure networks. The computational approach combines time-series graph neural networks (GNNs) for spatiotemporal pattern recognition with multi-agent reinforcement learning to adaptively allocate personnel, equipment, and communication bandwidth. Key challenges include handling petascale geospatial-temporal datasets, maintaining sub-minute inference times for real-time decision loops, and ensuring robustness against data source failures. The research will utilize parallelized graph processing on GPU clusters to accelerate GNN training and inference, while distributed agent-based simulations will model resource interactions across urban-rural divides. Expected outcomes include an open-source middleware layer for interoperable disaster data fusion and a set of validated performance benchmarks for emergency response HPC workflows. This work bridges gaps between operational research, distributed systems, and crisis informatics, offering a template for computational resilience in public-sector resource management. Successful implementation could reduce emergency response latency by 40-60% in simulated scenarios, directly supporting climate adaptation planning and regional infrastructure hardening initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of technological information systems, including computing systems, as solutions to business and research data and communications support needs. Includes instruction in the principles of computer hardware and software components, algorithms, databases, telecommunications, user tactics, application testing, and human interface design.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize decision-making processes in high-stakes critical incident response scenarios, such as hostage negotiations, active shooter incidents, and coordinated terrorist threats. Current training and planning tools rely heavily on static simulations or after-action reviews, which lack the dynamic, data-driven adaptability required for real-time operational environments. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including situational telemetry, behavioral psychology models, and resource deployment logistics—into a unified predictive system to enhance tactical outcomes while minimizing collateral risk. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate multi-actor interactions under crisis conditions, machine learning algorithms to predict escalation pathways, and Monte Carlo methods to stress-test response protocols against probabilistic threat landscapes. Key computational challenges include real-time processing of unstructured incident data, parallelized scenario branching for contingency planning, and ethical AI governance to avoid bias in risk assessment tools. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support platform capable of generating adaptive response templates for law enforcement agencies, validated through historical case studies and partnership feedback from tactical operations units. The project’s interdisciplinary significance lies in bridging computational social systems analysis with applied police science, advancing both methodological rigor in public safety analytics and operational frameworks for crisis de-escalation. By quantifying historically qualitative aspects of special operations—such as trust dynamics in negotiation or spatial cognition under stress—this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based critical incident preparedness.
cip_title: Critical Incident Response/ Special Police Operations
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for dealing with police emergencies such as hostage situations, bomb threats, barricades and terrorist incidents. Includes instruction in crisis management, command procedures, incident containment, information collection and debriefing, first responder negotiation, victim and criminal psychology, site survey and surveillance, special weapons and tactics, interagency communications and joint operations, pre-confrontation and contingency planning, assault and rescue operations, security and crowd control, media relations, and post-operation procedures.

abstract: Periodontitis, a prevalent inflammatory disease affecting the periodontal tissues, is a leading cause of tooth loss and is increasingly linked to systemic conditions such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Current clinical interventions often fail to fully address the complex, multifactorial interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and biomechanical forces that drive disease progression. This project proposes to develop a multi-scale computational model to simulate the dynamic interplay of these factors within the periodontal microenvironment. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate high-dimensional datasets—including 16S rRNA sequencing of subgingival plaque, single-cell transcriptomics of host tissues, and biomechanical strain data from occlusal forces—to construct a spatially resolved, agent-based model. This framework will simulate microbial biofilm dynamics, immune cell trafficking, and tissue remodeling under varying biomechanical and inflammatory conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify critical biomarkers and predictive signatures of disease progression or treatment response. The computational workflow will require teraflop-scale processing to handle stochastic simulations across millions of agents, parallelized finite element analysis of mechanical stress distributions, and real-time optimization of model parameters. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, such as keystone bacterial species or host signaling pathways that amplify inflammatory damage, and the development of patient-specific treatment strategies informed by simulated responses to mechanical or pharmacological interventions. By elucidating how biomechanical forces modulate microbial virulence and immune dysregulation, this work will advance precision periodontology, offering a paradigm shift from empirical therapies to mechanistically grounded, personalized care. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary spatial-temporal resolution in simulations and to scale the model for clinical translation, ultimately improving prognostication and long-term outcomes for patients with refractory periodontitis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: Periodontal disease involves complex interactions between microbial biofilms, host immune responses, and biomechanical factors that drive tissue degradation. While microbial dysbiosis is well-studied, the role of spatially heterogeneous mechanical forces on gingival and bone remodeling remains poorly characterized. This project aims to develop a multiscale computational model integrating microbial dynamics, inflammatory signaling, and biomechanical stress distributions to predict site-specific progression of periodontitis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to simulate three-dimensional periodontal pocket geometries derived from clinical intraoral scans and micro-CT data, incorporating time-dependent biofilm growth, cytokine diffusion, and mechanobiological bone resorption processes. Agent-based modeling will capture stochastic microbial community interactions, while finite element analysis will quantify stress distributions in periodontal ligaments and alveolar bone under occlusal loading. Machine learning approaches will analyze longitudinal clinical datasets to parameterize model inputs and validate predictions against patient outcomes. The computational framework will identify critical thresholds in biofilm composition, immune mediator concentrations, and occlusal forces that synergistically accelerate tissue destruction. Expected outcomes include predictive biomarkers for localized disease progression and mechanotherapeutic targets to disrupt pathological feedback loops. By bridging microbial ecology, biomechanics, and immunology, this work will establish a novel paradigm for personalized periodontics, enabling clinicians to stratify risk and optimize interventions based on patient-specific microbial and biomechanical profiles. The HPC environment is essential for managing large-scale simulations, high-resolution spatial datasets, and iterative model calibration, which exceed the capacity of local workstations. This interdisciplinary approach advances periodontal research into computational systems biology, offering translational insights for precision oral healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance understanding of how dynamic, multigenerational family systems influence early childhood developmental trajectories. Traditional research in Early Childhood and Family Studies relies heavily on longitudinal surveys or small-scale observational datasets, limiting the ability to model complex, nonlinear interactions between caregivers, siblings, and extended family members across diverse sociocultural contexts. The proposed research addresses this gap by developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) that simulate family decision-making processes, stressor cascades, and adaptive behaviors affecting child outcomes. These models integrate empirical data from existing developmental psychology studies, demographic datasets, and novel synthetic populations generated via generative adversarial networks (GANs) to account for underrepresented family structures. HPC resources will enable parallelized parameter sweeps across thousands of simulated family units, capturing emergent patterns in caregiving quality, resource allocation, and developmental risk factors under varying socioeconomic conditions. A key innovation involves coupling these ABMs with reinforcement learning frameworks to model how families dynamically optimize childcare strategies amid competing priorities. Expected outcomes include identification of critical leverage points for early interventions, predictive tools for assessing cumulative risk in nontraditional family systems, and open-source computational workflows tailored to social science researchers. By bridging developmental theory with scalable computational experimentation, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying family dynamics at unprecedented granularity while maintaining ecological validity—a critical step toward equitable, data-driven policies in early childhood support systems.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the development and learning of children from birth to six years old within the context of the family. Includes instruction in child abuse and neglect, child and infant growth and development, early childhood education, early childhood language and literacy, early childhood math and science, early childhood special education, family literacy, family sociology, family and marriage relations, assessment and measurement, psychology, and psychopathology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between digital cultural shifts and liturgical practice in contemporary Christian communities through large-scale computational analysis of multimedia worship archives. As congregations increasingly integrate digital tools—from streaming platforms to AI-generated visual art—into worship spaces, theological and pastoral frameworks for evaluating their impact remain underdeveloped. This research addresses the urgent need to map how digital media reshape liturgical aesthetics, congregational engagement, and theological meaning-making, focusing on non-denominational megachurches and online faith communities where innovation is most pronounced. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the team will analyze a curated corpus of 50,000+ hours of worship recordings (2015-2023), including video liturgies, sermon transcripts, and social media interactions, using multimodal machine learning architectures. Custom transformer models will detect patterns in gesture, vocal modulation, visual symbolism, and textual rhetoric across traditions, while graph neural networks will model how digital elements influence perceived spiritual presence in hybrid worship contexts. The computational workflow integrates computer vision for analyzing liturgical choreography, NLP for theological theme extraction, and network analysis to track innovation diffusion across communities. Expected outcomes include 1) a taxonomy of emerging digital-liturgical genres, 2) predictive models identifying media integration strategies that correlate with long-term congregational vitality, and 3) an open-source toolkit for denominational bodies to ethically evaluate worship technologies. By bridging computational humanities and practical theology, this work aims to establish evidence-based frameworks for ministerial training programs navigating rapid technological change while preserving liturgical integrity. The scale of multimedia analysis and need for real-time processing of complex interaction data necessitate GPU-accelerated clusters capable of simultaneous video, audio, and text analysis at petabyte scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as ministers or priests in any of the Christian religious traditions. Includes instruction in the theology and polity of a particular church, church law, liturgy and ritual, principles of pastoral ministry, homiletics, evangelism, church/parish organization and management, Christian ethics, church history, and related studies.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced simulation and optimization framework for improving the efficiency and equity of child care service allocation in urban environments. The growing demand for affordable, high-quality child care, coupled with uneven spatial distribution of resources and complex regulatory constraints, has created systemic challenges in matching supply to family needs. Traditional analytical tools struggle to model dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand patterns, workforce availability, transportation logistics, and policy impacts at scale. Our computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, geospatial analytics, and multi-objective optimization to simulate child care ecosystems across diverse socioeconomic contexts. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-resolution demographic datasets, real-time scenario testing, and sensitivity analyses across thousands of parametric combinations. Key innovations include machine learning-enhanced demand forecasting, fairness-aware resource allocation algorithms, and policy intervention simulations that account for cascading effects on workforce participation and community well-being. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying optimal facility placement strategies, dynamic pricing frameworks to improve accessibility for low-income families, and evidence-based policy recommendations for mitigating service deserts. By bridging computational social science with operations research methodologies, this project aims to create transferable tools for public and private child care administrators while advancing methodological paradigms for social infrastructure optimization. The computational intensity of simultaneously resolving spatial, economic, and behavioral variables necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve actionable insights within operationally relevant timeframes.
cip_title: Child Care and Support Services Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the provision and management of child care services and that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage child care facilities and programs that meet children's developmental needs and interests and that provide safe and healthy environments. Includes instruction in child development and psychology; home- and institution-based child care; identification of diseases, injuries, and psychological trauma and applicable referrals; parent relations; personnel and business management principles; and related laws and policies.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens affecting livestock poses a critical threat to animal health, food security, and zoonotic disease management. Current gaps in understanding the genomic and immunologic drivers of AMR evolution limit targeted intervention strategies. This project seeks to integrate multi-omics data—including bacterial pan-genomes, host transcriptomic profiles, and metagenomic surveillance data—to model pathogen-host-environment interactions driving AMR in *Staphylococcus aureus* and *Escherichia coli* isolates from dairy cattle. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale sequencing datasets (>10 TB) and perform computationally intensive analyses, including phylogenetic reconstruction, machine learning-based prediction of resistance phenotypes, and agent-based simulations of bacterial transmission dynamics under varying immune pressures. Custom pipelines will align sequencing reads, annotate resistance genes, and quantify expression of host immune markers (e.g., TLRs, cytokines) from RNA-seq data. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize mutations in key virulence proteins linked to immune evasion. The computational framework will be validated against in vitro antimicrobial susceptibility testing and in vivo challenge studies in bovine models. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of genomic signatures predictive of AMR emergence in cattle-associated pathogens, (2) spatial-temporal models of AMR spread within herds, and (3) mechanistic insights into how host immunobiology modulates pathogen evolution. These results will directly inform vaccine development and precision antibiotic stewardship programs, addressing urgent needs in veterinary infectious disease management. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work bridges computational microbiology and immunobiology to advance translational strategies for mitigating AMR in agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microbial causation and immunologic processes related to animal disease, prevention, and treatment. Includes instruction in bacteriology, mycology, virology, immune response mechanisms, humoral and cell function, cancer defenses, immune system dysfunction, immunologic diseases, parasitology, pathogenesis, and disease vectors.

abstract: Pediatric pathologies, particularly those manifesting during fetal development and early childhood, present unique diagnostic challenges due to the dynamic interplay of genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors. Current limitations in understanding the molecular trajectories of these diseases stem from the complexity of multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and histopathological imaging) and the computational demands of integrating such data at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of pediatric disease mechanisms, focusing on rare developmental disorders and therapy-resistant pediatric cancers. The research will employ a multi-modal computational approach, integrating bulk and single-cell sequencing data with spatially resolved histopathology images to map disease-specific molecular networks. Machine learning frameworks, including graph neural networks and transformer-based architectures, will be trained to identify cross-modal biomarkers and predict cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of high-resolution whole-slide imaging data, performing large-scale genomic variant prioritization, and simulating developmental pathways using systems biology models. HPC resources will enable parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, distributed model training, and in silico hypothesis testing, which are infeasible on local infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel diagnostic signatures for congenital anomalies, stratification markers for pediatric tumor subtypes, and mechanistic insights into dysregulated developmental pathways. These findings will be validated against clinical cohorts and experimental models, with the goal of translating computational predictions into targeted molecular assays. By establishing scalable analytical pipelines for pediatric pathology, this work aims to advance precision diagnostics and therapeutic strategies for understudied childhood diseases, while generating publicly accessible tools for the research community. The requested computing resources are critical to overcoming current bottlenecks in data integration and model optimization, ensuring robust, reproducible analyses that bridge computational discovery and clinical application.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory diagnosis of diseases that occur during fetal growth, infancy, and child development, based on knowledge of general pathology, normal growth and development, and pediatric medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of simulating large-scale civil engineering structures and infrastructure systems using advanced computer-aided drafting and design (CAD/CADD) workflows. While traditional CAD tools are sufficient for small-scale projects, modern civil engineering challenges—such as modeling seismic resilience in multi-story buildings, optimizing stormwater drainage systems under climate change scenarios, or simulating traffic flow in smart city designs—require high-fidelity simulations that exceed the capabilities of standard workstations. The research problem centers on overcoming hardware limitations that restrict the resolution, complexity, and iterative optimization of civil engineering models, particularly when integrating geospatial data, real-time sensor inputs, or multi-physics interactions. To resolve this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessments, accelerate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations for hydraulic systems, and enable machine learning-driven design optimization. The computational approach will involve adapting open-source CAD frameworks like FreeCAD and Code_Aster for distributed computing architectures, while validating results against physical scale models and field data. Key workflows will include automated meshing of LiDAR-derived terrain models, GPU-accelerated rendering for 3D visualizations of subsurface utility networks, and Monte Carlo simulations to assess failure probabilities in earthquake-prone regions. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in simulation runtime for complex models, the ability to process city-scale infrastructure datasets at sub-meter resolution, and improved predictive accuracy for material stress thresholds in novel composite materials. By integrating HPC capabilities into civil drafting education, this project will also provide students with hands-on experience in cloud-based CAD workflows, preparing them for industry demands. The results will directly support municipal partners in optimizing infrastructure planning and contribute open-access simulation templates to the civil engineering CAD community.
cip_title: Civil Drafting and Civil Engineering CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawing and electronic simulations in support of civil engineers, geological engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic civil engineering principles, geological and seismographic mapping, machine drafting, computer-aided drafting (CAD), pipe drafting, survey interpretation, and blueprint reading.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized neuromuscular rehabilitation protocols through multiscale biomechanical and neurophysiological modeling. Despite progress in exercise science, optimizing post-injury recovery—particularly for complex musculoskeletal injuries like anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears—remains limited by insufficient integration of individual variability in neuromuscular control, tissue healing dynamics, and sensorimotor adaptation. Current clinical models rely on population-level data, neglecting patient-specific biomechanical loading patterns and neural drive interactions that influence recovery outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining finite element modeling of joint and soft tissue mechanics with dynamic simulations of motor neuron activation patterns derived from electromyography (EMG) and functional neuroimaging data. The HPC environment will enable the parallelization of multibody dynamics simulations to predict joint stresses under varying rehabilitation exercises, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on high-resolution diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) datasets to map corticospinal tract plasticity during recovery. This integration requires processing terabytes of motion capture, EMG, and neuroimaging data alongside stochastic modeling of motor unit recruitment thresholds. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers predictive of rehabilitation efficacy, optimization of patient-specific exercise regimens to minimize re-injury risk, and the creation of open-source simulation tools for clinical movement analysis. The computational demands of this project—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated neural network training and real-time finite element analysis—exceed the capacity of local resources. By bridging biomechanics, neurophysiology, and data science, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for precision rehabilitation, directly addressing the National Academy of Medicine’s priority of translating mechanistic movement science into actionable clinical tools.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of cross-domain cognitive processes through the development of a multi-scale computational model integrating neural, behavioral, and environmental data. While existing approaches often isolate cognitive functions like memory, perception, or decision-making, real-world cognition involves continuous interaction between these domains, shaped by contextual and physiological constraints. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how such interactions scale across biological and situational variables, particularly in neurodiverse populations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to simulate a hybrid architecture combining spiking neural networks with reinforcement learning frameworks, calibrated against empirical neuroimaging and eye-tracking datasets. The model will dynamically map how sensory inputs are gated through attentional mechanisms, integrated with prior knowledge, and transformed into adaptive behaviors under varying cognitive loads. Key computational challenges include real-time synchronization of modular network components, parameter optimization across 10^6+ possible configurations, and probabilistic inference under noisy input conditions—all requiring parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows. Outcomes will generate predictive insights into individual differences in cognitive flexibility, with applications to personalized neuroeducational interventions and assistive technologies. By bridging computational neuroscience, developmental psychology, and machine learning, this work advances methodological frameworks for studying cognition as a complex adaptive system rather than a collection of isolated modules. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving biologically plausible temporal resolutions in whole-brain simulations while maintaining ecological validity through embedded virtual environments. Successful implementation will produce open-source tools for scalable cognitive modeling, addressing reproducibility challenges in interdisciplinary research.
