The research addresses a critical gap in historical scholarship: the lack of large-scale, comparative studies that systematically map how Black communities navigated systemic oppression, forged transnational networks, and sustained cultural practices under shifting legal and social regimes. Traditional archival methods struggle to synthesize fragmented records, such as census data, fugitive slave advertisements, church registries, and oral histories, into a cohesive analytical framework. To overcome this, we propose a computational approach combining geospatial analysis, network modeling, and machine learning techniques to process digitized archival materials from over 50 repositories. HPC resources will enable the processing of multi-terabyte datasets, including georeferenced maps, handwritten text corpora, and 3D-scanned artifacts, while machine learning models (e.g., NLP for handwritten document analysis) will identify patterns in migration routes, kinship ties, and communication networks. Agent-based simulations will test hypotheses about the diffusion of resistance tactics and cultural knowledge across regions. Expected outcomes include an open-access interactive atlas visualizing community resilience strategies, a publicly shared corpus of annotated historical data, and new methodological frameworks for computational historical analysis. This work will advance understanding of how African-American communities adapted to and resisted structural violence while contributing to interdisciplinary dialogues on diaspora studies. The scale of data integration and computational complexity necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve timely processing and high-resolution modeling, which are infeasible with standard institutional computing capacities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: The development of immersive, adaptive virtual environments faces significant computational barriers, particularly in scaling real-time interactions, dynamic physics simulations, and multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) systems within interactive media. Current consumer-grade hardware and standard cloud infrastructure lack the capacity to simulate complex, persistent worlds with high-fidelity visuals, responsive environments, and emergent user-driven narratives—key requirements for advancing next-generation game design and interactive storytelling. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these limitations through three interconnected computational approaches: (1) real-time, GPU-accelerated rendering of procedurally generated 3D environments using neural radiance fields (NeRF) and physics-informed generative adversarial networks (GANs); (2) parallelized agent-based modeling for AI-driven non-player character (NPC) populations capable of dynamic social and environmental interactions; and (3) distributed simulation of large-scale virtual ecosystems with evolving terrain, weather, and resource systems. By deploying containerized workloads across HPC nodes, the team will optimize resource allocation for concurrent rendering, AI inference, and environmental simulation tasks, while maintaining sub-100ms latency for user inputs. The research builds on Unreal Engine 5’s Nanite and Lumen systems but extends their capabilities through custom CUDA kernels and OpenMPI-based distributed physics calculations. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for designing persistent virtual worlds with unprecedented interactivity, benchmark data on HPC-driven design workflows, and open-source tools for real-time environment generation. These advancements will directly benefit academic research in adaptive narrative systems and AI-mediated player experiences while offering industry applications in training simulations, collaborative virtual workspaces, and large-scale multiplayer environments. The project’s computational demands—including petascale storage for asset generation datasets and sustained GPU utilization for ray-traced visualizations—necessitate dedicated HPC support to achieve its objectives.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and programming of interactive media entertainment, including computer and video games, virtual environments, Internet applications, and other interactive media. Includes instruction in theory of games, turn-based games, real-time games, visual and interactive design, story development, animation, simulation, and programming.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of reaction mechanisms and molecular design in organic chemistry, with a focus on developing sustainable catalytic systems for hydrocarbon functionalization. A central challenge in this field lies in accurately modeling complex, multi-step reactions involving transition metal catalysts and electronically diverse substrates. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve short-lived intermediates or subtle stereoelectronic effects that dictate reaction selectivity, while conventional computational methods lack the precision or scalability to handle large, dynamic systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) framework combined with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations to map free energy landscapes and electron transfer processes in asymmetric catalysis. These simulations will integrate density functional theory (DFT) for active site modeling with machine learning force fields to extend sampling timescales. Key targets include elucidating the role of non-covalent interactions in enantioselective C–H activation and optimizing ligand architectures for CO2 fixation via hydrocarbon carboxylation. The computational workflow will employ GPU-accelerated quantum chemistry codes (e.g., CP2K, ORCA) and enhanced sampling algorithms to handle systems exceeding 500 atoms, requiring thousands of concurrent CPU/GPU hours. Expected outcomes include predictive models for catalyst design, atomistic insights into solvent effects on stereocontrol, and identification of novel activation pathways for inert substrates. Success will directly inform experimental collaborations targeting pharmaceutical intermediates and renewable polymer feedstocks. By bridging gaps between theoretical reactivity models and synthetic applicability, this work aims to establish computational organic chemistry as a predictive tool for green chemistry innovation, with broader implications for energy-efficient synthesis and molecular medicine. The scale of electronic structure calculations and conformational sampling necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve statistically meaningful results within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of hydrocarbon compounds and their derivatives. Includes instruction in molecular conversion and synthesis, molecular synthesis and design, the molecular structure of living cells and systems, the mutual reactivity of organic and inorganic compounds in combination, the spectroscopic analysis of hydrocarbon compounds, and applications to specific problems in research, industry, and health.

abstract: The reactivity of silicate minerals governs critical geochemical and physical processes shaping Earth’s surface and subsurface environments. However, modeling the coupled effects of silicate weathering, fluid transport, and mechanical deformation at scales spanning atomic interactions to landscape evolution remains a fundamental challenge due to computational limitations. This project seeks to advance predictive understanding of silicate-dominated systems by developing high-resolution, multiscale models of mineral-fluid interactions under varying thermodynamic and stress conditions. The research will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to quantify atomic-scale dissolution-precipitation kinetics and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to refine interatomic potentials for silicate-water interfaces. These data will parameterize continuum-scale reactive transport models, implemented using the open-source software CrunchTope, to simulate weathering fronts and fracture propagation in heterogeneous rock matrices. A key innovation involves coupling geochemical reaction networks with discrete element method (DEM) simulations to resolve feedbacks between chemical weathering and mechanical breakdown. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from laboratory mesocosms and field observations of weathering profiles in granitic terrains. This project requires high-performance computing resources to manage the iterative multiscale simulations, particularly the massively parallel MD runs (using LAMMPS) and high-resolution DEM domains with >10^6 particles. Anticipated outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into rate-limiting steps during silicate weathering, (2) predictive frameworks for fracture network development in engineered geothermal systems, and (3) improved scaling relationships for global biogeochemical models. By integrating atomistic and continuum approaches, this work will provide novel constraints on how silicates regulate terrestrial carbon cycling, soil formation, and subsurface hydrology over geologic timescales. The requested allocation of 500,000 CPU-hours and 50 TB of storage will enable these computationally intensive simulations, fostering advances in geomorphology, environmental geology, and sustainable resource management.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the silicates and other substances formed by chemical and physical geomorphological processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance consumer advocacy through the development of a predictive modeling framework that evaluates product safety risks and ecological impacts across dynamic consumption patterns. Despite regulatory frameworks, consumers remain vulnerable to poorly understood risks from emerging products, particularly those intersecting with sustainability challenges. Current analytical methods struggle to integrate real-time consumer feedback, longitudinal product safety data, and environmental impact metrics at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational system combining natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling (ABM), and lifecycle assessment (LCA) simulations. The NLP component will analyze unstructured consumer complaint data from public databases and social media to identify latent risk signals. ABM will simulate decision-making patterns among diverse consumer demographics, while LCA modules will quantify ecological footprints of products under varying usage scenarios. HPC resources are critical to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, train deep learning models for anomaly detection, and run Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic risks. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for advocacy groups to prioritize high-risk products, forecast regulatory gaps, and quantify trade-offs between product safety and environmental sustainability. By enabling rapid, data-driven assessment of complex consumption ecosystems, this research aims to empower consumer protection initiatives with scalable analytical tools, reduce response times to emerging hazards, and inform policy debates at the intersection of consumer rights and ecological stewardship. The project aligns with the program’s mission to enhance consumer advocacy through innovative research techniques, bridging computational scalability challenges with applied social and environmental priorities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on providing end-use advice and representational services to individuals and groups within a variety of settings, and the analytical and research techniques needed to protect consumers from unsafe, unreliable, and/or unhealthy products and services. Includes instruction in consumer advocacy, family management systems, ecological impacts of consumption practices, and analyzing and testing product quality and safety.

abstract: The study of kinetic-scale turbulence in high-temperature plasmas is critical for advancing magnetic confinement fusion, yet existing fluid-based models struggle to capture the multi-scale interactions between electrons, ions, and electromagnetic fields. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-fidelity, particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation framework to resolve non-equilibrium plasma dynamics in regimes relevant to tokamak edge plasmas. The primary research challenge lies in bridging the temporal and spatial scales between electron-scale kinetic effects and macro-scale magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities, which drive anomalous transport and energy losses. To achieve this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining GPU-accelerated PIC algorithms for kinetic electron dynamics with reduced-order fluid models for ion species. The simulations will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to concentrate resolution on regions of strong gradients, such as plasma-material interfaces and magnetic island boundaries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the projected 10^9-particle ensemble and resolve sub-micron Debye lengths in a 3D toroidal geometry. Expected outcomes include quantifying the role of kinetic electron effects in destabilizing edge-localized modes (ELMs) and validating reduced turbulence models against experimental measurements from the DIII-D tokamak. The results will directly inform the design of ELM suppression techniques for ITER and future reactors. Additionally, the project will produce an open-source software toolset optimized for exascale architectures, enabling the plasma physics community to simulate multi-scale phenomena with unprecedented accuracy. By elucidating the interplay between kinetic and fluid processes, this work aims to advance predictive capabilities for plasma confinement, ultimately supporting the development of stable, high-performance fusion plasmas.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of properties and behavior of matter at high temperatures, such that molecular and atomic structures are in a disassociated ionic or electronic state. Includes instruction in magnetohydrodynamics, free electron phenomena, fusion theory, electromagnetic fields and dynamics, plasma and non-linear wave theory, instability theory, plasma shock phenomena, quantitative modeling, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: Occupational health research faces significant challenges in understanding the complex interactions between workplace exposures, worker physiology, and long-term health outcomes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of occupational disease risk by integrating heterogeneous datasets, including longitudinal electronic health records, environmental sensor data from workplaces, and biomonitoring results. Current analytical approaches struggle to account for temporal patterns in exposure, individual susceptibility factors, and the combinatorial effects of multiple stressors—a gap this work aims to address through advanced computational methods. We propose a two-stage approach: first, employing machine learning techniques to identify latent patterns in multi-modal occupational health data, and second, using agent-based modeling to simulate workforce health outcomes under varying exposure scenarios. The computational workflow will utilize distributed computing frameworks to process terabyte-scale datasets, while GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures will enable real-time analysis of high-dimensional sensor data. Key innovations include the development of dynamic exposure indices that adapt to individual worker characteristics and the creation of probabilistic risk maps for sector-specific occupational hazards. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into dose-response relationships for understudied occupational exposures, validated predictive tools for early intervention in at-risk worker populations, and scalable frameworks for regulatory decision-making. This work directly supports the program’s mission by advancing data-driven strategies to preserve workforce health while addressing critical computational bottlenecks in occupational epidemiology. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project’s large-scale simulations, optimizing complex models, and ensuring reproducibility through version-controlled, high-throughput analyses.
cip_definition: Research focused on the maintenance of the health of workers, the ability to perform work, the arrangements of work, and the physical and chemical environments of the workplace. Includes instruction in data collection and management and the administration and regulation of occupational medical services. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the coupled thermal-hydrological-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes governing the formation of magmatic-hydrothermal ore deposits, with a focus on porphyry copper systems. A critical gap exists in understanding how dynamic feedbacks between fluid flow, fracture propagation, and mineral precipitation control the localization of economic metal concentrations. Current laboratory experiments and field observations cannot resolve the spatial-temporal scales of these interactions, while existing numerical models often oversimplify multi-physics couplings. We propose to develop 3D high-resolution simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics, geomechanics, and reactive transport modeling using open-source codes (e.g., OpenFOAM, PFLOTRAN) modified with custom constitutive relationships for rock deformation and sulfide precipitation kinetics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to handle the nonlinear system of partial differential equations across heterogeneous domains exceeding 10^8 grid cells, with adaptive meshing for evolving fracture networks. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs in sensitivity analyses of key parameters (e.g., magma chamber depth, host rock permeability). The simulations will be validated against petrological data from well-characterized porphyry deposits and experimental fracture-sealing datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative models linking geophysical signals (seismic velocity, resistivity) to subsurface mineralization patterns, (2) predictive frameworks for ore deposit geometry based on pre-mineralization lithospheric conditions, and (3) open-access code modules for THMC modeling in igneous systems. This work will provide novel constraints on the timescales of ore-forming processes while advancing computational methods for analyzing multi-physics interactions in geochemistry. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter space exploration at unprecedented resolution, addressing fundamental questions about energy and mass transfer during upper crustal magma degassing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the igneous, metamorphic, and hydrothermal processes within the earth and the mineral, fluid, rock, and ore deposits resulting from them. Includes instruction in mineralogy, crystallography, petrology, volcanology, economic geology, meteoritics, geochemical reactions, deposition, compound transformation, core studies, theoretical geochemistry, computer applications, and laboratory studies.

abstract: Clinical informatics research faces growing challenges in leveraging large-scale, heterogeneous clinical datasets to improve patient outcomes and healthcare delivery. While electronic health records (EHRs), wearable device streams, and multimodal imaging data hold transformative potential, their effective integration and analysis require computational resources beyond the capacity of standard institutional infrastructure. This project proposes to develop a scalable computational framework for real-time predictive modeling of sepsis progression in critical care settings, integrating high-frequency physiological data, longitudinal medication records, and clinical notes. The research will employ graph neural networks to model temporal relationships in vital sign trends, transformer-based architectures for processing clinician narratives, and multimodal fusion techniques to synthesize these data streams. Key computational challenges include processing sub-second resolution physiological data from thousands of simultaneous ICU patients, optimizing memory-intensive model training across multimodal embeddings, and validating predictions against evolving diagnostic criteria. High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized preprocessing of 12+ TB of raw clinical data, distributed training of ensemble models across hundreds of GPU nodes, and probabilistic simulations of treatment effect heterogeneity. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive analytics pipeline validated across three health systems, novel interpretability metrics for clinical machine learning models, and quantitative evidence on optimal sensor sampling rates for early detection protocols. By addressing critical bottlenecks in processing real-world clinical data streams, this work aims to establish computational standards for next-generation clinical decision support systems while advancing methodological rigor in translational informatics. The requested resources will directly support time-sensitive analyses of emerging sepsis biomarkers and validation studies required for regulatory compliance, which are infeasible with current computing allocations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Informatics

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing next-generation military radar systems for dynamic, contested electromagnetic environments through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Modern radar operations face increasing complexity due to spectrum congestion, adversarial signal interference, and the need for real-time adaptability across multi-domain operations (air, land, sea, cyber). Traditional hardware-in-the-loop testing is resource-intensive and insufficient for exploring adaptive algorithms at scale. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a modular simulation framework capable of modeling radar-physics interactions, signal processing workflows, and cognitive decision-making processes under variable threat scenarios. Key computational components include finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for wave propagation analysis, Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic interference modeling, and machine learning pipelines to train resource allocation algorithms. The framework will integrate domain-specific parameters such as platform mobility constraints, weather effects on signal attenuation, and adversarial electronic warfare tactics. By parallelizing these workloads across GPU-accelerated nodes, the project aims to achieve 100x speedup over conventional cluster-based approaches, enabling rapid iteration of cognitive radar coordination strategies. Anticipated outcomes include validated protocols for dynamic spectrum sharing, interference mitigation templates for multi-static radar networks, and performance benchmarks for AI-driven adaptive beamforming. This work directly supports the development of resilient, software-defined radar architectures critical for modern defense systems, with potential dual-use applications in autonomous vehicle coordination and spectrum management policy. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale parameter space exploration that is currently infeasible with institutional infrastructure, accelerating the transition from theoretical models to field-testable solutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of air, sea and ground-based radar systems. Includes instruction in electronic principles and digital techniques, transistors and solid-state component theory, radar systems; maintenance technology, data processing systems, wiring and circuit schematics, maintenance management, safety procedures, and applications to specific systems and services.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the reliability and efficiency of next-generation electrical power transmission systems, with a focus on installation methodologies for emerging grid architectures. As renewable energy integration, decentralized generation, and smart grid technologies reshape power networks, traditional installation practices for conductors, insulators, and substation components struggle to adapt to dynamic load patterns, fault propagation risks, and environmental variability. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in power transmission infrastructure under diverse operational scenarios. The project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to model mechanical stresses in tower-conductor systems during extreme weather events, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on synthetic datasets to predict insulation degradation in high-voltage components. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulations will assess failure probabilities across installation configurations while accounting for spatial variations in soil conductivity and electromagnetic interference patterns. By integrating these computational approaches, the research aims to establish data-driven guidelines for adaptive installation protocols that minimize energy losses, extend component lifetimes, and enhance grid resiliency. The requested HPC resources will enable parametric studies at unprecedented scale, processing tera-scale datasets encompassing material properties, geographic information systems (GIS) data, and real-time sensor inputs. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for optimal conductor sag-tension relationships in hybrid AC/DC systems, validated mitigation strategies for corona discharge in compact transmission corridors, and probabilistic risk maps informing climate-resilient installation standards. This work directly supports workforce training initiatives in advanced power transmission installation by generating open-access simulation tools and case studies, bridging theoretical electrical engineering principles with practical field implementation challenges.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installers, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and power transmission installation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for modeling consumer decision-making processes in multi-sensory digital marketing environments. Traditional marketing models often oversimplify consumer behavior by isolating visual, auditory, or textual stimuli, neglecting the dynamic integration of these factors in immersive digital platforms such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and interactive social media. The research problem centers on understanding how heterogeneous sensory inputs interact nonlinearly to influence purchasing decisions, particularly in contexts where real-time personalization and adaptive interfaces are critical. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) combined with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to simulate large-scale consumer populations interacting with multi-modal marketing content. The ABM component will capture individual variability in sensory preferences and cognitive processing, while DRL will optimize stimulus combinations in real time based on evolving behavioral feedback. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional data streams (e.g., eye-tracking, biometric responses, and clickstream patterns) and scaling simulations to reflect diverse demographic cohorts. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing these simulations, reducing latency in reinforcement learning feedback loops, and enabling sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for sensory-driven consumer behavior, actionable insights into optimal stimulus integration strategies, and an open-source toolkit for adaptive digital marketing design. This work bridges gaps between cognitive science, human-computer interaction, and marketing analytics, offering a novel methodological foundation for personalized, sensory-aware marketing strategies in rapidly evolving digital ecosystems. The results will directly inform the design of next-generation marketing platforms, enhancing both consumer engagement and ethical targeting practices by reducing reliance on invasive data collection.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general marketing and marketing research, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community-level predictive modeling of health disparities and intervention outcomes in underserved populations. Public health interventions often rely on heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, socioeconomic surveys, environmental exposure metrics, and geospatial data—that are computationally intensive to integrate and analyze at scale. Current limitations in processing capacity hinder the ability to model complex, multifactorial drivers of health outcomes or simulate long-term impacts of preventive strategies across diverse demographic subgroups. To address this gap, we propose a computational epidemiology framework combining machine learning, agent-based modeling, and geospatial analytics. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets from regional health systems and national surveys (e.g., CDC PLACES, BRFSS) while supporting fine-grained simulations of disease transmission and intervention scenarios across synthetic populations. Key computational challenges include optimizing graph-based algorithms for social network analysis, training ensemble models to account for spatial autocorrelation in health behaviors, and conducting Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses for policy decision support. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of neighborhood-level predictors of preventable hospitalizations through high-resolution risk mapping, (2) development of open-source simulation tools for evaluating resource allocation trade-offs in community health campaigns, and (3) predictive models quantifying the intersectional effects of housing policies, clinic accessibility, and public health messaging on chronic disease outcomes. By enabling analysis at unprecedented spatial and temporal granularity, this work will provide actionable insights for reducing service gaps in low-resource settings while advancing methodological innovation in computational public health. The requested resources directly support the program’s mission to equip practitioners with evidence-based strategies for equitable health services delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to plan and manage health services in local community settings, including the coordination of related support services, government agencies, and private resources. Includes instruction in public health, community health services and delivery, health behavior and cultural factors, local government operations, human services, health communication and promotion, health services administration in local settings, environmental health, preventive and comparative medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics, family and community health, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Pediatric pathologies, particularly those manifesting during fetal development and early childhood, present unique diagnostic challenges due to the dynamic interplay of genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors influencing disease mechanisms. Current diagnostic paradigms in pediatric pathology often rely on static histopathological or molecular analyses, which may fail to capture the complex spatiotemporal dynamics of disease progression in developing tissues. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multi-omic datasets—including single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and longitudinal clinical-pathological data—to model disease trajectories in developmental disorders and pediatric cancers. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic and imaging datasets, which are computationally prohibitive for standard clinical workstations. Computational workflows will employ machine learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) to identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression and unsupervised clustering algorithms to delineate novel molecular subtypes. Network analysis tools will map interactions between dysregulated developmental pathways and tumor microenvironments, while GPU-accelerated image processing pipelines will quantify histomorphometric features in whole-slide imaging data. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source computational models to correlate multi-omic signatures with clinical outcomes, enabling earlier and more precise diagnoses. These models will be validated against a retrospective cohort of 500 pediatric cases spanning neurodevelopmental anomalies, congenital heart defects, and embryonal tumors. By elucidating the computational pathology of developmental diseases, this work aims to advance personalized diagnostic frameworks tailored to pediatric patients, ultimately reducing diagnostic turnaround times and improving prognostic accuracy. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the petabyte-scale data generated by multi-institutional collaborations and for ensuring reproducibility through containerized workflows (Singularity/Docker). This project bridges computational innovation with clinical translation, addressing an unmet need in pediatric medicine by transforming complex biological data into actionable diagnostic insights.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory diagnosis of diseases that occur during fetal growth, infancy, and child development, based on knowledge of general pathology, normal growth and development, and pediatric medicine.

abstract: The increasing complexity of chemical systems in environmental, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications demands advanced analytical methods capable of resolving intricate molecular interactions and trace-level components. Current experimental techniques in analytical chemistry, such as chromatography and spectroscopy, face limitations in predicting optimal separation conditions or interpreting overlapping spectral signatures in multi-component systems. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate and optimize analytical workflows, enabling data-driven enhancements to experimental design. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of solute-stationary phase interactions in chromatographic systems and quantum chemical calculations to predict spectroscopic signatures of complex mixtures. These simulations will integrate machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in retention behavior, spectral interference, and matrix effects across diverse chemical environments. A key focus will be modeling the behavior of emerging contaminants and pharmaceutical metabolites in non-ideal matrices, where experimental characterization remains resource-intensive. The computational framework will be validated against experimental datasets from collaboration partners, including hyphenated mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance results. Successful implementation will yield predictive tools for optimizing analytical method parameters, reducing trial-and-error experimentation, and enhancing detection limits in complex samples. The anticipated outcomes include open-source software modules for simulating chromatography-mass spectrometry workflows and a database of computationally predicted spectroscopic reference standards. This work will advance the molecular-level understanding of separation science and spectral interpretation while providing training resources for computational analytical chemistry. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the ∼10^6 CPU-hour requirement of multi-scale simulations and enabling rapid iteration of machine learning models on terabyte-scale spectral datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of techniques for analyzing and describing matter, including its precise composition and the interrelationships of constituent elements and compounds. Includes instruction in spectroscopy, chromatography, atomic absorption, photometry, chemical modeling, mathematical analysis, laboratory analysis procedures and equipment maintenance, and applications to specific research, industrial and health problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in sports communication by analyzing large-scale multimedia datasets generated across sports media platforms. The proliferation of digital content—including live broadcasts, social media interactions, athlete interviews, and audience engagement metrics—presents a critical challenge: traditional analytical tools lack the capacity to process and synthesize these heterogeneous, high-volume data streams efficiently. This limits the ability to study real-time communication dynamics, audience sentiment, and the impact of emerging media formats on sports narratives. Our research addresses this gap by developing computational models to examine how sports stories are constructed, disseminated, and received in a fragmented media landscape. Using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML), we will analyze textual data from social media, press releases, and commentary transcripts to identify patterns in framing, bias, and rhetorical strategies. Concurrently, computer vision techniques will assess visual and audiovisual content from broadcasts and promotional materials to quantify representation trends (e.g., gender, ethnicity) and production techniques. Network analysis will map information flow among journalists, athletes, and fans to uncover influence hierarchies and misinformation pathways. These tasks require HPC resources due to the scale of data (terabytes of video, millions of social media posts) and the complexity of multimodal fusion algorithms. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for optimizing audience engagement, improving equity in sports media representation, and mitigating the spread of false information during major sporting events. The project will also produce open-source tools tailored for sports communication research, enabling reproducibility and collaboration across academia and industry. By integrating computational methods with media theory, this work aims to redefine best practices for sports journalism, public relations, and digital content creation in an era of rapid technological change.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for communicating about sports in a variety of formats, media, and contexts; and that prepares individuals to be sports reporters and writers, photojournalists, radio and television announcers, producers and directors, recreational sports promoters, and public relations specialists. Includes instruction in sports writing, photography, broadcast journalism, sports production, game rules, media and public relations, and sports promotion.

abstract: Disasters and complex emergencies present dynamic, multi-scale challenges that strain traditional incident command systems (ICS) due to uncertainties in hazard behavior, resource availability, and human response. This project addresses the critical gap in predictive, real-time decision support tools capable of optimizing resource allocation and ICS coordination under rapidly evolving crisis conditions. We propose developing an adaptive, high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model cascading disaster impacts, interdependencies between critical infrastructure systems, and population mobility patterns. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) for civilian and responder behavior, graph-based network analysis for infrastructure resilience, and machine learning (ML) to predict emergent risks from heterogeneous data streams, including satellite imagery, social media, and IoT sensor feeds. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic scenarios for natural hazards (e.g., hurricanes, wildfires) and human-driven incidents (e.g., mass casualty events), while reinforcement learning algorithms will train adaptive resource allocation policies. The HPC environment is essential for resolving spatiotemporal conflicts in large-scale simulations involving millions of agents, cross-jurisdictional resource networks, and stochastic event progressions at meter-level resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support platform that quantifies trade-offs in ICS strategies, identifies failure cascades in supply chains, and recommends prioritized response actions validated against historical incident data. This work will advance computational emergency management by enabling scenario stress-testing for regional preparedness plans, reducing latency in life-saving interventions, and providing empirical insights into scalability limits of current ICS frameworks. Results will directly inform training protocols and contingency planning for agencies participating in joint operations, with particular relevance to climate-accelerated disaster risks.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of the incident command system model to formulating and implementing effective response to natural and man-made disasters. Includes instruction in contingency planning, hazard and risk assessment, joint operations, law and ethics, emergency response and recovery, event mitigation, emergency rescue and medical operations, incident command, terrorism and national security issues, law enforcement, relief administration, volunteer and citizen coordination, public relations and applications to specific types of incidents.

abstract: Fungal pathogens pose a significant threat to global health and food security, with rising antifungal resistance complicating treatment strategies. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding fungal pathogenesis and environmental drivers of resistance by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex host-fungus-environment interactions. Current experimental methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multiscale nature of these systems, particularly the interplay between fungal phenotypic plasticity, host immune evasion mechanisms, and variable environmental stressors. We propose a dual computational approach: (1) agent-based modeling of fungal growth and dissemination within host tissues, integrating empirical data on fungal morphogenesis, host histopathology, and antifungal pharmacokinetics; and (2) dynamic systems models simulating environmental selection pressures on antifungal resistance across ecological niches. These models will incorporate heterogeneous datasets spanning clinical isolates, soil microbiome compositions, and climatic variables to identify key predictors of treatment failure and resistance emergence. The scale of parameter space exploration—encompassing thousands of fungal strains, host conditions, and environmental scenarios—necessitates parallelized computing for sensitivity analyses and optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for resistance risk assessment, identification of high-risk environmental reservoirs for zoonotic pathogens, and mechanistic insights into fungal stress adaptation strategies. By elucidating context-dependent virulence factors, this work will directly inform surveillance priorities and antifungal stewardship programs. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations at biologically relevant spatiotemporal resolutions, which are computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure, advancing both fundamental mycology and translational applications in clinical and agricultural settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of fungi, lichenous plants, eukaryotic microorganisms, myxomycetes, and plasmodiophorales and their relationship to diseases in higher plants, animals, and human beings as well as to pharmacologically useful products. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology; histopathology; fungal growth and behavior; environmental mycology; antifungal sensitivity; mycoses; pathogens and pathogenesis; pharmacological properties; and computer and laboratory research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced predictive models and simulations for optimizing operational efficiency and customer experience in casino environments. While casino operations intersect with hospitality, entertainment, and risk management, the computational challenges inherent in modeling complex, real-time decision-making processes—spanning game dynamics, staffing logistics, and customer behavior—remain underexplored. Traditional analytical tools are insufficient for handling the scale, variability, and interdependencies of data streams generated by modern casino ecosystems, including player tracking systems, slot machine telemetry, and surveillance networks. This research addresses this gap by constructing a multi-layered computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to analyze spatial, temporal, and behavioral patterns. Key objectives include simulating crowd flow to minimize congestion, optimizing game floor layouts for revenue maximization, and predicting equipment maintenance needs to reduce downtime. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution datasets (e.g., terabyte-scale transaction logs and video analytics outputs) and iterative testing of hypothetical scenarios under varying constraints, such as regulatory changes or seasonal demand fluctuations. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for resource allocation, such as dynamic staff scheduling algorithms and real-time anomaly detection systems to mitigate fraud. By advancing computational methods tailored to casino operations, this project aims to establish a benchmark for data-driven decision-making in the gaming industry while contributing novel methodologies to computational social science and operational research domains. The scalability of the proposed models may also inform resource optimization strategies in analogous service-oriented environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in casino operations and services not listed above.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face increasing pressure to optimize resource use while maintaining profitability and sustainability. However, the complexity of interactions between environmental variables, management practices, and economic factors challenges traditional decision-making approaches. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model and optimize agricultural production operations at scale. By integrating real-time sensor data, historical climate records, and crop growth simulations, the research aims to generate actionable insights for precision agriculture applications. The computational approach leverages machine learning algorithms to predict crop yields under varying irrigation, fertilization, and pest management strategies, while parallelized simulations assess the economic and environmental trade-offs of different operational plans. High-performance computing resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets, train complex neural networks, and execute millions of scenario iterations within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include scalable models for site-specific management recommendations, reducing input waste and enhancing yield stability. Furthermore, the framework will enable scenario testing for emerging challenges such as climate variability and market fluctuations, providing agribusiness stakeholders with robust tools for strategic planning. By advancing data-driven decision-making in agricultural operations, this research contributes to the sustainable intensification of food production systems, aligning with global efforts to address food security and resource efficiency.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general planning, economics, and use of facilities, natural resources, equipment, labor, and capital to produce plant and animal products, and that may prepare individuals for work in farming, ranching, and agribusiness.

abstract: Higher education institutions face growing demands to evaluate program efficacy and equity using increasingly complex, multi-source datasets. Traditional analytical methods often fail to integrate unstructured data (e.g., student feedback, course evaluations) with structured metrics (e.g., retention rates, learning assessments) at scale, limiting actionable insights. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for evaluating higher education programs by leveraging advanced machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze heterogeneous datasets. The research will address two core questions: (1) How can large-scale, mixed-method data be systematically processed to identify predictors of program effectiveness? (2) What computational strategies enable real-time equity assessments across diverse student populations? High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train transformer-based NLP models on qualitative text data from millions of course evaluations and institutional surveys, while simultaneously running ensemble ML models on structured longitudinal data (e.g., enrollment, graduation, and employment records). GPU-accelerated clusters will be used to optimize hyperparameter tuning for deep learning architectures and enable parallel processing of sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for program evaluators, validated computational workflows for bias detection in evaluation metrics, and predictive models linking curricular interventions to equity outcomes. By scaling analysis beyond conventional statistical approaches, this work aims to advance evidence-based policy design and provide institutions with adaptive frameworks to address systemic inequities in higher education.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for generating information about educational programs in higher education, staff and methods, and the analysis of such information for planning purposes outside of institutional research. Includes instruction in evaluation theory, evaluation research design and planning, administering evaluations and related data collection activities, data reporting requirements, data analysis and interpretation, and related economic and policy issues in higher education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in English as a Second Language (ESL) education through advanced computational linguistics and data-driven methodologies. The research problem centers on analyzing the complex interplay between language acquisition patterns, instructional interventions, and sociolinguistic variables in adult ESL learners. Traditional analytical methods struggle to process the scale and multidimensionality of learner corpora—including written texts, speech recordings, and interaction logs—which are essential for identifying nuanced proficiency trajectories and instructional efficacy. Our approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, machine learning models, and large-scale statistical analyses to examine syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic features in learner output. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for error pattern detection, clustering learners by developmental stages using unsupervised learning, and simulating language environment impacts via agent-based modeling. HPC resources are indispensable for handling terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing deep learning architectures (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned for learner language), and running parallelized simulations of classroom dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for predicting individual proficiency bottlenecks, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive curricular design, and (3) open-access tools for automated discourse analysis tailored to ESL contexts. By revealing how specific instructional strategies correlate with measurable linguistic gains, this research will directly inform the development of personalized learning systems and enhance the scalability of ESL programs in postsecondary institutions. The project bridges computational innovation and applied linguistics, offering transformative potential for both pedagogical practices and theoretical models of second language acquisition.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize training protocols for court interpreters by addressing the challenges posed by linguistic diversity and regional dialect variations in legal settings. While court interpreters are trained to manage standard language pairs, existing pedagogical tools inadequately address non-standard sociolects, code-switching patterns, and low-resource dialects prevalent in multicultural jurisdictions. These gaps risk misinterpretations during legal proceedings, potentially compromising equitable access to justice. To bridge this divide, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and simulate complex interpreting scenarios through two parallel computational approaches. First, neural machine translation architectures will be trained on curated multilingual legal corpora, emphasizing rare dialects and vernacular speech, to generate adaptive interpretation benchmarks. Second, real-time speech processing simulations will model courtroom dynamics—including overlapping dialogue, ambient noise, and rapid speaker turns—to evaluate interpreter performance under stress. These simulations will utilize generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize hybrid acoustic environments and speaker profiles, enabling scalable stress-testing of trainee responses. The computational pipeline will further integrate psycholinguistic metrics to quantify cognitive load and decision latency during interpretation tasks. Outcomes will include an open-source platform for dialect-aware interpreter training, a repository of synthetically generated legal discourse datasets, and evidence-based guidelines for optimizing certification exams. By aligning computational linguistics with jurisprudential requirements, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for equity-focused interpreter education while demonstrating how HPC resources can address critical gaps in non-STEM professional training ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to provide accurate translation and interpretation between two or more languages for parties involved in a legal proceeding. Includes instruction in courtroom standards and procedures, court interpreting, legal terminology, consecutive interpretation, simultaneous interpretation, and sight translation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to optimize digital platemaking and imaging workflows, addressing critical inefficiencies in color accuracy, material waste, and processing time for high-resolution graphic reproduction. Current workflows in platemaking often rely on iterative manual adjustments to balance ink viscosity, plate surface properties, and press dynamics, leading to resource-intensive trial-and-error processes. This research proposes a data-driven approach using machine learning (ML) models and fluid dynamics simulations to predict optimal plate configurations under variable conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train ML algorithms on large datasets of historical print jobs, material properties, and environmental variables, as well as to simulate ink dispersion patterns across diverse plate geometries at micrometer resolution. The computational pipeline will integrate finite element analysis for modeling substrate interactions, convolutional neural networks for defect detection in pre-press imaging, and generative adversarial networks to propose corrective adjustments. By automating parameter optimization, this framework aims to reduce material waste by 20–30% in test cases and improve color consistency metrics by 15% compared to industry standards. Outcomes will include an open-source toolset for print professionals and validation datasets linking simulation results to physical press outcomes. The project directly supports sustainability goals in graphic communication industries while advancing pedagogical resources for imaging workflows in journalism and media production programs. Successful implementation will demonstrate how computational methods can bridge traditional print practices and emerging digital fabrication technologies, offering scalable solutions for small-scale publishers and large-scale commercial operations alike.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare film, digital data, and surfaces to reproduce printed or graphic images. Includes instruction in platemaking, stripping, camerawork, imposition, digital imaging, computer direct-to-plate and direct-to-press, and related processes.

abstract: The increasing complexity of abdominal and pelvic imaging modalities, such as multiparametric MRI and spectral CT, has created a critical need for advanced computational tools to improve diagnostic precision and streamline clinical workflows. Current manual and semi-automated approaches for analyzing large volumetric datasets are time-intensive, prone to variability, and ill-equipped to handle the integration of multi-modal imaging with clinical data. This project proposes the development of a deep learning framework to automate the detection, segmentation, and quantitative analysis of abdominal pathologies, including hepatic tumors, inflammatory bowel disease, and pelvic organ prolapse. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte imaging repositories from three institutional cohorts (n=2,100 patients) and public datasets, train 3D convolutional neural networks with attention mechanisms, and validate models against histopathological and longitudinal clinical outcomes. Key computational challenges include managing heterogeneous data formats, optimizing memory-intensive processing of high-resolution dynamic imaging sequences, and implementing federated learning protocols to enable multi-institutional collaboration while preserving data privacy. The proposed framework will leverage GPU-accelerated pipelines for distributed training and inference, with containerized deployment to ensure reproducibility. Successful implementation is expected to yield validated algorithms for lesion characterization, treatment response prediction, and automated report generation, significantly reducing diagnostic turnaround times while improving inter-reader consistency. By enabling granular analysis of radiomic features across diverse patient populations, this work aims to establish new quantitative biomarkers for abdominal disorders and support precision medicine initiatives. The requested HPC infrastructure will directly address scalability barriers in translating computational radiology innovations to clinical practice, ultimately enhancing diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes in abdominal imaging.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the abdomen and pelvis in adults and children.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated electron systems, with a focus on non-equilibrium dynamics in low-dimensional quantum materials. The central challenge lies in simulating the time-dependent behavior of these systems under external perturbations, such as ultrafast laser pulses or high electric fields, where conventional mean-field approximations fail to capture critical many-body effects. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining tensor network methods with exact diagonalization techniques to model the real-time evolution of interacting electrons in reduced dimensions. The simulations will integrate advanced numerical algorithms optimized for parallel architectures, including matrix product state (MPS) representations for 1D chains and variational quantum circuit methods for 2D lattices, to balance accuracy with computational feasibility. Key objectives include mapping phase diagrams for non-equilibrium quantum states, quantifying entanglement entropy growth during dynamical processes, and identifying signatures of transient topological order. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations at previously inaccessible system sizes (up to 100+ lattice sites) and timescales (beyond picosecond resolution), with data analysis pipelines employing distributed-memory frameworks for efficient post-processing. Success in this endeavor will advance fundamental understanding of quantum thermalization breakdowns and metastable states, with potential implications for designing novel quantum sensors and energy-efficient nanoelectronic devices. By pushing the boundaries of numerically exact quantum dynamics simulations, this work will also contribute methodological innovations to the broader computational physics community, particularly in optimizing memory-intensive tensor operations for next-generation computing architectures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the theories that explain the fundamental structure of our world and the universe and which draws from physics and astronomy. Includes instruction in astronomy, calculus, cosmology, differential equations, electricity, magnetism, data analysis, physics, quantum mechanics, space science, spectroscopy, and thermal physics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social network formation and their impact on population-level inequality patterns using large-scale computational simulations. The research problem centers on understanding how micro-level interactions—such as homophily, resource sharing, and spatial mobility—generate macro-scale disparities in access to social capital across diverse demographic groups. While existing survey-based studies capture static network snapshots, they lack the temporal resolution and scalability needed to model evolving network structures across heterogeneous populations. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) framework coupled with demographic microsimulation techniques, which will integrate census data, longitudinal social survey inputs, and synthetic population generation algorithms. The computational approach requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate networks at metropolitan-regional scales (≈10^6 agents) over multi-decadal time horizons, with parameter spaces exploring variations in migration policies, economic shocks, and aging population effects. Each simulation iteration involves dynamic graph computations, spatial clustering analyses via GPU-accelerated kernels, and Bayesian calibration against historical inequality metrics. The project’s computational demands stem from (1) parallel execution of 50,000+ parameter combinations to quantify uncertainty in emergent inequality pathways and (2) memory-intensive handling of multilayer network data (node attributes, temporal edges, and geospatial coordinates). Expected outcomes include novel metrics for predicting inequality tipping points in urban systems and open-source tools for scalable social network analysis. Results will inform targeted policy interventions to mitigate access disparities in healthcare and employment networks. This work advances computational sociology methodologies by establishing a framework to reconcile individual agency with structural constraints in population studies, objectives unattainable without HPC-enabled large-population simulations.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sociology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for collision damage assessment and repair optimization in automotive bodies. Current methodologies in collision repair rely heavily on empirical techniques and manual inspection, which can lead to inefficiencies in diagnosing structural weaknesses, estimating repair costs, and selecting materials. To address these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and multi-physics simulations to model collision dynamics, material deformation, and adhesive bonding behavior under diverse impact scenarios. High-fidelity simulations will replicate real-world collisions, analyzing stress distribution in vehicle frames, composite material failure thresholds, and the performance of adhesives and coatings under thermal and mechanical loads. ML algorithms will be trained on simulated and empirical datasets to predict optimal repair strategies, including material selection, heat treatment parameters, and refinishing techniques. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across thousands of collision scenarios while accounting for variables such as impact angle, velocity, and material heterogeneity. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of collision simulation results, predictive tools for rapid damage assessment, and data-driven guidelines for improving repair durability and safety. By integrating computational modeling into collision repair education, this project also aims to enhance technician training programs with virtual labs and scenario-based learning modules. The results will directly contribute to reducing material waste, lowering repair costs, and advancing the adoption of lightweight materials in automotive design, aligning with industry demands for sustainability and precision in collision repair technologies.
cip_title: Autobody/ Collision and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, reconstruct and finish automobile bodies, fenders, and external features. Includes instruction in structure analysis, damage repair, non-structural analysis, mechanical and electrical components, plastics and adhesives, painting and refinishing techniques, and damage analysis and estimating.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the biomechanical and physiological factors contributing to sports-related injuries through advanced computational modeling. Athletic trainers currently rely on generalized protocols for injury prevention and rehabilitation, which often lack personalization due to the complexity of human movement dynamics and tissue response. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate injury mechanisms, optimize therapeutic interventions, and predict recovery outcomes. The research will integrate multi-modal data, including motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and medical imaging, to construct patient-specific models of musculoskeletal stress during athletic activities. Finite element analysis and machine learning algorithms will be employed to model tissue-level damage (e.g., ligament tears, muscle strains) and evaluate the efficacy of rehabilitation exercises under varying biomechanical conditions. The computational pipeline will leverage parallel processing to handle large datasets and perform iterative simulations across diverse scenarios, such as sport-specific movements, equipment adjustments, and physiological stressors. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk movement patterns, data-driven guidelines for personalized rehabilitation, and open-source tools to assist athletic trainers in designing targeted interventions. By elucidating the relationships between biomechanical load, tissue adaptation, and recovery, this work aims to reduce injury recurrence rates and improve return-to-play decision-making. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling these analyses across heterogeneous datasets and ensuring robust validation through parameter sweeps and sensitivity testing. This project will advance evidence-based practices in athletic training, offering a transformative approach to injury management grounded in computational precision.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work in consultation with, and under the supervision of physicians to prevent and treat sports injuries and associated conditions. Includes instruction in the identification, evaluation, and treatment of athletic injuries and illnesses; first aid and emergency care; therapeutic exercise; anatomy and physiology; exercise physiology; kinesiology and biomechanics; nutrition; sports psychology; personal and community health; knowledge of various sports and their biomechanical and physiological demands; and applicable professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the empirical understanding of art therapy interventions through large-scale computational analysis of multimodal clinical and artistic data. While art therapy is recognized for its capacity to address mental, emotional, and developmental disorders, the field lacks robust quantitative frameworks to systematically evaluate how specific artistic media, creative processes, or therapeutic interactions correlate with clinical outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating anonymized patient-generated art, session transcripts, and longitudinal behavioral health data from art therapy clinics. Machine learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines, will be trained to identify visual and linguistic patterns in artwork and dialogue that predict therapeutic progress across diverse demographics. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution art images, feature extraction from temporal sequences of artistic expression, and ensemble modeling to account for individualized patient trajectories. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothesized neurocognitive mechanisms underlying art therapy’s impact, such as emotion regulation or neural plasticity, using biologically informed parameters. The computational demands of processing terabytes of image data, training complex models with cross-validation, and running iterative simulations necessitate scalable storage, GPU acceleration, and distributed computing. Outcomes will include open-source tools for art therapists to quantitatively assess interventions, predictive frameworks linking artistic engagement to symptom reduction, and mechanistic insights into art therapy’s therapeutic pathways. By bridging data-driven computational methods with clinical art therapy practice, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based protocols, inform personalized treatment planning, and establish scalable infrastructure for future translational research in creative arts therapies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use drawing and other art media forms to assess, treat, and rehabilitate individuals with mental, emotional, developmental, or physical disorders. Includes instruction in art, history and theory of art therapy, art therapeutic techniques, psychopathology, patient assessment and diagnosis, cultural diversity issues, legal and ethical practice issues, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation medicine faces the challenge of addressing complex, multifactorial conditions in children and young adults with congenital or childhood-onset physical impairments. These patients often present with overlapping medical, functional, and psychosocial needs that require individualized, interdisciplinary care. Current limitations in predicting treatment outcomes and optimizing intervention strategies stem from an inability to integrate heterogeneous clinical, imaging, and multi-omics datasets at scale. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the interactions between biological, biomechanical, and environmental factors influencing rehabilitation outcomes. We will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze longitudinal electronic health records, motion capture data, neuroimaging, and patient-reported outcomes from a multi-institutional cohort of 2,500+ participants with cerebral palsy, spinal cord injuries, and neuromuscular disorders. Agent-based modeling will simulate musculoskeletal growth patterns under different therapeutic interventions, while finite element analysis will quantify tissue stress responses during rehabilitative exercises. Federated learning architectures will enable privacy-preserving data integration across institutions. The computational pipeline will be validated against prospective clinical outcomes, including measures of mobility, pain reduction, and quality of life. Expected outcomes include predictive models for personalized intervention timing, dosage, and modality selection; biomechanical risk stratification tools for contracture prevention; and a shared computational resource for hypothesis testing in pediatric rehabilitation. By enabling large-scale integration of multimodal data, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies that bridge gaps between neurodevelopmental biology, rehabilitation engineering, and clinical practice. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling computationally intensive simulations, training deep learning models on 3D motion datasets, and maintaining secure data harmonization across partner institutions.
cip_definition: Research on how to use an interdisciplinary approach to prevent, diagnose, treat, and manage congenital and childhood-onset physical impairments in children and young adults, including related medical, physical, functional, psychosocial, and vocational limitations or conditions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the technical and artistic methodologies of taxidermy through computational modeling and simulation. Traditional taxidermy practices rely heavily on manual techniques for specimen preservation, form construction, and aesthetic finishing, which are time-intensive and susceptible to inconsistencies. The research problem centers on optimizing these processes by developing predictive models for material behavior, environmental interactions, and biomechanical degradation in preserved specimens. By integrating computational tools, this work aims to address gaps in precision, scalability, and sustainability within the field. Key computational approaches include finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution in taxidermy forms under varying environmental conditions, machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on historical specimen degradation data to predict preservation outcomes, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze the efficacy of novel synthetic materials in replicating organic textures. Additionally, 3D reconstruction algorithms will be employed to digitize anatomical reference data, enabling automated form customization for rare or delicate species. The computational workflows will require parallel processing for large-scale simulations of material interactions and iterative optimization of preservation parameters. Expected outcomes include open-source frameworks for taxidermists to simulate preservation scenarios, a digital repository of biomechanical models for endangered species, and data-driven guidelines for sustainable material use. This research holds significance for preserving ecological heritage, reducing waste in traditional taxidermy workflows, and establishing computational taxidermy as a bridge between artisanal craftsmanship and emerging technologies. By formalizing taxidermy’s intersection with computational design and materials science, the project aims to catalyze innovation in a historically analog field while fostering ethical standards through predictive analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to reproduce life-like three-dimensional representations of living animals for permanent display using elements of the deceased specimen(s) as well as artificial materials, and to manage taxidermy services and businesses.
