Includes instruction in specimen grading and selection, caping and fleshing, preservation procedures, tanning, drying, measurements, form and armature construction, carpentry and woodworking, molding and casting, drawing, sculptural techniques, painting and finishing techniques, basic business operations, customer communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Metal fabrication processes are critical to manufacturing and construction industries, yet optimizing parameters such as thermal cutting, welding dynamics, and structural integrity remains challenging due to the complex interplay of heat transfer, material deformation, and metallurgical phase changes. Traditional trial-and-error methods are time-consuming, resource-intensive, and often fail to predict defects like warping, residual stress, or microstructural inconsistencies. This project proposes a computational approach to model and simulate metal fabrication processes at high resolution, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome the limitations of conventional experimental and low-fidelity numerical methods. The research will develop multi-physics models integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for thermo-mechanical behavior, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for gas-metal interactions in cutting and welding, and machine learning (ML) to correlate process parameters with material outcomes. These simulations will account for variable inputs such as alloy composition, toolpath geometries, and energy input rates, validated against experimental datasets from partnered fabrication workshops. By scaling simulations across HPC clusters, the project aims to map optimal fabrication parameters for diverse materials and geometries, reducing defects and energy consumption while improving yield strength and dimensional accuracy. Anticipated outcomes include open-access predictive models for industry use, a digital twin framework for real-time process adjustment, and data-driven guidelines for interpreting technical drawings under dynamic fabrication conditions. This work will advance precision manufacturing in sectors reliant on custom metal components, such as aerospace and renewable energy infrastructure, while establishing a computational toolkit to modernize vocational training in metal fabrication.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to further process ferrous and/or non-ferrous metal plates or shapes, and to manufacture and/or install products as interpreted through technical drawings. Includes instruction in trade tools, shop equipment, reading and interpreting blueprints, material handling, welding, thermal cutting, metallurgy, template pattern development, plate and structural fabrication, destructive and non-destructive testing, inspection, shipment preparation and fabrication installation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven system to automate and enhance the accuracy of medical transcription processes, addressing critical inefficiencies in manual workflows that lead to delays, errors, and increased healthcare costs. Current transcription methods rely heavily on human expertise to interpret complex medical terminology, contextualize ambiguous dictations, and adhere to evolving regulatory standards. However, variability in speech patterns, acoustic environments, and terminology usage across specialties introduces risks of inaccuracies. To overcome these challenges, we propose training a suite of deep learning models on a curated corpus of medical dictations, paired with corresponding validated transcripts and metadata. The computational workflow will integrate speech recognition, natural language processing (NLP), and domain-specific knowledge graphs to resolve ambiguities, enforce compliance with documentation standards, and dynamically adapt to speaker-specific patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of audio data, train transformer-based architectures (e.g., fine-tuned Wav2Vec 2.0 and BERT models), and simulate real-time transcription scenarios with low-latency inference requirements. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated pipelines for parallelized feature extraction, hyperparameter optimization, and ensemble model training. Expected outcomes include a deployable AI-assisted transcription tool with measurable improvements in error rates and processing speed compared to existing commercial systems, as well as open-source benchmarks for medical speech-to-text adaptation. By reducing reliance on manual labor, this work aims to improve the scalability of medical documentation, enhance patient record accuracy, and provide a framework for continuous learning as clinical terminology evolves. Results will be validated against gold-standard transcripts from collaborating healthcare institutions, with performance metrics and model architectures disseminated to advance research at the intersection of computational linguistics and clinical informatics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to execute verbatim medical conference minutes, medical reports, and medical orders. Includes instruction in dictation and simultaneous recording, analysis of notes and visual evidence, medical terminology, data processing applications and skills, formal medical report and correspondence formats, professional standards, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time decision-making in decentralized business ecosystems through the development of a quantum-inspired computational framework for resource orchestration. As organizations increasingly rely on distributed, cross-industry partnerships to deliver complex services, traditional centralized optimization methods fail to scale with the latency, privacy, and coordination demands of dynamic multi-stakeholder environments. The research will implement a hybrid approach combining tensor network simulations of quantum optimization algorithms with classical graph neural networks, creating a novel computational architecture capable of resolving conflicting resource constraints across decentralized supply chains. High-performance computing resources are required to simulate quantum-inspired optimization processes at scale, including the training of neural networks on synthetic datasets representing multi-agent bargaining scenarios, supply chain disruptions, and evolving regulatory constraints. The computational methodology involves three phases: 1) Quantum circuit simulations using QuEST and Qiskit to model entangled decision states across partner organizations, 2) Distributed training of graph neural networks on GPU clusters to predict coalition formation patterns, and 3) Multi-objective optimization benchmarking against classical game-theoretic models. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for privacy-preserving resource allocation in business ecosystems, quantitative benchmarks comparing quantum-inspired approaches to conventional optimization techniques, and open-source tools for simulating decentralized decision protocols. This work bridges gaps between quantum information science, operations research, and collaborative business models, offering new computational paradigms for managing resources in emerging organizational structures such as decentralized autonomous enterprises and cross-sector innovation networks. The results will inform both technical strategies for distributed systems management and policy frameworks for governing computational resource sharing in business ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of information technology, computer systems management, and business operations to the planning, management, and evaluation of information services in organizations. Includes instruction in telecommunications, systems planning and integration, information policy, information security, contracting and purchasing, budgeting, information technology, operations management, human resources, communications skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address operational inefficiencies and risk management challenges in casino environments, an understudied domain within non-science and engineering research. Casinos operate as complex socio-technical systems where dynamic variables—such as patron behavior, game mechanics, regulatory compliance, and real-time resource allocation—intersect. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between these factors, limiting the ability to optimize operations, mitigate financial risks, or enhance customer experience. This project aims to develop a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and discrete-event simulation (DES) to model casino ecosystems at scale. The ABM component will simulate patron decision-making patterns and crowd dynamics, informed by anonymized behavioral datasets from partner casinos. ML algorithms will analyze transactional and surveillance data to predict anomalies, such as fraud or problem gambling behaviors, while DES will optimize staffing, game floor layouts, and service workflows under stochastic demand conditions. The computational intensity of concurrently running these models—requiring real-time data assimilation, high-dimensional parameter spaces, and Monte Carlo simulations for risk forecasting—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a decision-support toolkit for casino managers, enabling proactive resource allocation, compliance automation, and personalized customer engagement strategies. By bridging computational social science, operations research, and hospitality management, this work will establish a methodological foundation for data-driven governance in gaming industries while advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of emergent service-sector challenges and HPC applications. The project’s computational outputs will be shared via open-source repositories to foster collaboration in niche domains of operational analytics beyond conventional disciplinary boundaries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in casino operations and services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between neurobiological processes, individual decision-making, and collective social behaviors using a novel computational framework integrating multimodal data. Traditional behavioral science studies often isolate biological, psychological, or social factors, limiting understanding of how these systems co-evolve in real-world contexts. Our research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) coupled with neurophysiological simulations to explore how neural mechanisms scale to influence group-level phenomena such as cooperation, conflict resolution, and information spread. The core computational challenge lies in simulating heterogeneous neural networks (derived from fMRI and EEG datasets) within socially embedded agents while capturing emergent population dynamics—a task requiring high-performance computing (HPC) due to the combinatorial complexity of multi-scale interactions. We will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to sample parameter spaces governing neuro-social linkages and use deep reinforcement learning to model adaptive behavior patterns. The project leverages existing datasets encompassing neuroimaging, behavioral experiments, and social network analyses from collaborative studies in psychology and public health. By implementing distributed memory architectures, we aim to overcome current limitations in simulating populations exceeding 10^5 agents with biologically grounded decision algorithms. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models of neuro-social system resilience under stress, validated against empirical observations of community responses to crises. This work will provide a methodological bridge between individual-level neurocognitive processes and population-level behavioral trends, offering new tools for policymakers to design interventions that account for both biological and social dimensions of human behavior. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving sufficient temporal and spatial resolution in these simulations, enabling unprecedented integration of molecular, individual, and societal data scales within a unified framework.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on the social sciences, psychology, and biomedical sciences to study complex problems of human individual and social growth and behavior.

abstract: This project investigates the cognitive and social dynamics underlying the spread of misinformation in digital communities, focusing on how individual cognitive biases interact with network structures to amplify or mitigate misinformation propagation. While traditional psychological studies have examined biases in isolation, this research employs an interdisciplinary framework integrating computational social science, cognitive psychology, and network theory to model these phenomena at scale. The central research problem lies in quantifying how specific biases (e.g., confirmation bias, illusory truth effect) influence information-sharing behaviors in heterogeneous social networks, particularly in contexts of high uncertainty. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled agent-based modeling (ABM) approach, simulating large-scale networks (N > 100,000 agents) with parameterized cognitive profiles derived from empirical behavioral datasets. Agents will interact within dynamic network topologies, exposing them to procedurally generated misinformation and factual content. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations across diverse bias-network configurations, real-time natural language processing (NLP) of simulated communication, and machine learning analysis of emergent diffusion patterns. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about critical thresholds in bias prevalence and network connectivity that trigger misinformation cascades. The project further incorporates validation against real-world datasets from social media platforms, using graph neural networks to compare simulated and observed diffusion trajectories. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking cognitive bias distributions to network-level misinformation risks, with applications in designing targeted interventions (e.g., algorithmic nudges, educational tools). By bridging computational granularity with psychological theory, this work advances fundamental knowledge about human decision-making in digital ecosystems while providing scalable tools for policymakers and platform designers addressing misinformation challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the use of industrial radiologic technologies for non-destructive testing (NDT) and material characterization. Current methods for analyzing complex material defects or thickness variations—such as x-ray diffraction, gamma radiography, and real-time thickness monitoring—often rely on empirical calibration or simplified analytical approximations. These approaches struggle to account for heterogeneous material compositions, irregular geometries, or dynamic industrial environments, leading to measurement inaccuracies and operational inefficiencies. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations, finite element modeling, and machine learning (ML) to enhance the precision and adaptability of industrial radiologic systems. The computational workflow will simulate interactions between radioisotope-generated radiation (e.g., x-rays, gamma rays) and multi-layered or composite materials under varying industrial conditions. Large-scale parametric studies will train ML models to correlate simulated radiation scattering patterns with real-world material properties, enabling automated defect detection and thickness prediction. The HPC environment is critical due to the high dimensionality of the problem: simulations must resolve micrometer-scale material features across meter-scale industrial components while incorporating stochastic radiation interactions. This requires parallelized execution of computationally intensive tasks, including 3D voxel-based radiation transport and iterative ML optimization. Expected outcomes include validated models for real-time, high-resolution material inspection, reducing reliance on physical test coupons and minimizing downtime in industries such as additive manufacturing, aerospace, and pipeline construction. The project will also produce open-source tools to bridge gaps between radiologic theory and industrial practice, fostering innovation in NDT methodologies. By leveraging HPC resources, this work aims to advance the reliability of radiation-based industrial testing while training the next generation of technologists in computational radiologic science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of industrial and research testing equipment using radioisotopes. Includes instruction in x-ray analysis of materials, nondestructive testing and inspection of materials, and continuous measurement of paper or metal thickness.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the systemic impacts of policy interventions on organizational behavior within educational institutions. Current policy development in education leadership often relies on qualitative case studies or linear statistical analyses, which struggle to account for dynamic feedback loops, heterogeneous stakeholder interactions, and emergent outcomes in complex organizational systems. The research problem centers on identifying how institutional policies—such as equity initiatives, professional development mandates, or resource reallocation strategies—propagate through multilayered networks of administrators, staff, and community actors, potentially generating unintended consequences. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis, this project will simulate decision-making processes across educational organizations under varying policy conditions. Computational agents will be parameterized using empirical data from school district records, leadership surveys, and institutional climate assessments to represent diverse actor behaviors, communication patterns, and power structures. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to realistic organizational sizes (10,000+ agents), incorporating adaptive learning algorithms for agent decision-making, and iterating through thousands of policy scenarios with probabilistic risk analysis. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting policy implementation bottlenecks, quantifying trade-offs between centralized mandates and distributed leadership models, and identifying leverage points for sustainable organizational change. This work will advance education leadership practice by providing actionable tools to test policies computationally before real-world deployment, reducing costly trial-and-error approaches. By integrating computational social science methods with education administration theory, the project aims to bridge gaps between policy design, organizational complexity, and equity-oriented leadership in K-12 and higher education systems.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Organizational Leadership and Policy Development with an emphasis on education. Includes instruction on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, education administration and supervision, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment planning for complex dental malocclusions and craniofacial anomalies requires precise understanding of biomechanical forces, bone remodeling dynamics, and individualized patient anatomy. Current clinical approaches rely on generalized protocols that do not fully account for patient-specific variations in bone density, periodontal ligament properties, or genetic predispositions, leading to suboptimal outcomes, prolonged treatment times, or relapse. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to simulate orthodontic tooth movement and predict treatment responses using high-performance computing (HPC). We will integrate patient-specific 3D craniofacial imaging (CBCT), intraoral scans, and genomic data to construct multi-scale finite element models (FEMs) that capture interactions between orthodontic appliances, biological tissues, and mechanotransduction pathways. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on retrospective clinical datasets to identify biomarkers associated with treatment efficacy and bone remodeling rates. HPC resources are critical for running iterative, high-resolution FEM simulations across diverse anatomical scenarios, optimizing force vectors in real time, and processing large-scale genomic datasets to uncover polymorphisms linked to differential treatment responses. The anticipated outcomes include a predictive modeling platform that enables clinicians to tailor force systems and treatment timelines to individual biomechanical and genetic profiles. This work has the potential to reduce treatment durations, minimize adverse outcomes, and improve the predictability of orthodontic interventions, advancing the field toward data-driven precision care. By leveraging computational scalability, the project will also generate open-access tools for simulating craniofacial growth adaptations, fostering collaborative research in biomechanically complex orthodontic cases.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and techniques involved in the prevention and correction of dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies.

abstract: Modern automotive systems face escalating complexity in balancing performance, safety, and sustainability, particularly with the rise of electrified and autonomous technologies. Current design and validation workflows rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-intensive, costly, and limited in capturing real-world operational variability. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for simulating and optimizing next-generation vehicular systems. The research will focus on two interconnected challenges: (1) multi-physics modeling of electric vehicle (EV) battery thermal management systems under extreme operating conditions, and (2) reinforcement learning-driven optimization of hybrid powertrain control strategies across diverse driving cycles. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for battery cell degradation modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for pack-level thermal dispersion analysis, and data-driven surrogate models trained on experimental datasets. Parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms will explore optimal torque distribution policies for hybrid configurations, accounting for transient thermal-electrical-mechanical couplings. The HPC environment will enable parametric sweeps across 10,000+ simulated driving scenarios, leveraging GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed computing frameworks to reduce per-case simulation times by 85% compared to existing cluster infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for battery lifespan extension under thermal stress, adaptive energy management strategies that reduce EV energy consumption by 12-18% in urban settings, and open-source simulation tools for vehicle systems co-design. These results will directly support industry partners in reducing physical testing costs by an estimated 30% while accelerating development cycles for low-emission vehicles. The project will further establish a template for HPC-enabled digital twin methodologies within automotive engineering technology curricula, enhancing workforce training in computational automotive systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design, optimization, and reliability of modern security systems through advanced computational modeling and simulation. As security technologies grow in complexity—integrating IoT-enabled sensors, multi-camera surveillance networks, and AI-driven threat detection—existing installation and inspection practices often lack robust frameworks to evaluate system performance under dynamic real-world conditions. The research problem centers on the computational limitations of current tools, which struggle to simulate large-scale, heterogeneous security ecosystems or process high-resolution sensor data in real time. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics simulation platform that models interactions between physical security components (e.g., motion sensors, access control systems, perimeter barriers) and environmental variables (e.g., weather, structural vibrations, electromagnetic interference). Computational methods will include finite element analysis for structural integrity testing, Monte Carlo simulations to assess failure probabilities across device networks, and machine learning models trained on synthetic and field-collected datasets to optimize alarm threshold calibration. Additionally, parallelized algorithms will enable real-time anomaly detection in distributed sensor arrays, reducing false positives. The expected outcomes include predictive models for identifying vulnerabilities in existing installations, AI-assisted tools for rapid system diagnostics, and data-driven guidelines for adaptive security configurations in diverse environments (residential, industrial, urban). By providing technicians with scalable computational resources to virtually prototype and stress-test systems, this research aims to elevate industry standards for security system resilience, reduce operational downtime, and enhance threat response accuracy. The resulting open-source framework will be validated against real-world case studies, ensuring direct applicability to the Security System Installation, Repair, and Inspection Technology field.
cip_title: Security System Installation, Repair, and Inspection Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair household, business, and industrial security alarms, sensors, video and sound recording devices, identification systems, protective barriers, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how dynamic neural circuit interactions underlie decision-making deficits in stress-related neuropsychiatric disorders. While rodent studies have identified prefrontal-amygdala-hippocampal circuits as critical for adaptive behavior under threat, the mechanisms by which chronic stress disrupts their coordination during decision processes remain poorly understood. Existing models lack the spatiotemporal resolution to capture millisecond-scale network dynamics across distributed regions during complex behavioral tasks. To address this, we propose a computational neuroscience approach combining biophysically detailed spiking neural network models with behavioral reinforcement learning frameworks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of >100,000 neurons with region-specific connectivity derived from tract tracing data, incorporating synaptic plasticity rules modulated by stress hormones. The models will be constrained by in vivo electrophysiology recordings from mice performing threat-conditioned probabilistic foraging tasks. Parallelized parameter optimization will identify circuit configurations that reproduce stress-induced behavioral rigidity observed experimentally. Memory-intensive GPU-accelerated simulations will resolve subcellular signaling cascades influencing synaptic efficacy during task epochs. Expected outcomes include: 1) A mechanistic explanation for how stress disrupts phase-locked oscillations between prefrontal and amygdala populations during conflict resolution 2) Predictive models of optogenetic intervention strategies to restore adaptive network dynamics 3) Open-source simulation tools for multiscale neural circuit analysis. This work directly addresses NIH priorities in computational neurobiology by bridging molecular neurophysiology with behavioral phenotypes of mental health disorders. The requested 200,000 CPU-hr allocation and 64TB scratch storage will support 18 months of large-scale simulations, enabling unprecedented resolution of stress pathophysiology mechanisms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates as it relates to control of behavior. Includes instruction in neuronal systems and circuits, higher level studies of behavior and cognition, computational neurobiology, and behavioral manifestations of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: Public works management faces growing complexity due to intersecting challenges in infrastructure demand, environmental sustainability, fiscal constraints, and equity considerations. Traditional decision-making frameworks often fail to account for dynamic interactions between these variables, resulting in suboptimal resource allocation and operational inefficiencies. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing an integrated computational model to simulate and optimize public works operations under uncertainty. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-method approach combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and discrete-event simulation to analyze large-scale datasets on infrastructure performance, demographic trends, and budgetary constraints. The agent-based component will simulate stakeholder interactions (e.g., municipal agencies, contractors, residents) to predict conflicts and collaboration patterns, while machine learning algorithms will identify predictive relationships between maintenance schedules, labor allocation, and service outcomes. Discrete-event simulations will model operational workflows for resource-intensive tasks like road maintenance and utility upgrades, incorporating probabilistic climate and demand scenarios. By parallelizing these computationally intensive processes through HPC, the project will enable real-time sensitivity analyses across multi-year planning horizons. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source decision support tool for optimizing budget allocation across competing public works priorities, (2) evidence-based strategies to balance short-term operational needs with long-term infrastructure resilience, and (3) scalable frameworks for ethical labor distribution and equity-aware service delivery. This work will advance computational social science methodologies in public administration while providing actionable insights for municipalities seeking to improve service efficiency, reduce lifecycle costs, and align operations with sustainability goals. The requested computing resources are critical to handling the project's spatial-temporal data granularity and enabling rapid scenario testing for diverse urban contexts.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the dynamic behavior and reaction mechanisms of enzyme-catalyzed processes under non-equilibrium conditions, with a focus on systems relevant to pharmaceutical and environmental chemistry. A critical challenge in modeling such systems lies in accurately simulating large, flexible biomolecular structures over biologically relevant timescales while capturing quantum mechanical effects in active-site chemistry. Current computational approaches struggle to balance the competing demands of spatial resolution and temporal sampling, particularly when studying pH-dependent conformational changes or proton-transfer events that govern catalytic activity. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational strategy combining hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling techniques, including metadynamics and Markov state models. These simulations will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform parallelized free energy calculations across distributed reaction coordinates while maintaining explicit solvent representations. The project will employ modified versions of the AMBER and CP2K software packages, optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures, to study three target systems: (1) pH-dependent substrate specificity in beta-lactamase enzymes, (2) proton-coupled electron transfer in laccase-mediated pollutant degradation, and (3) allosteric regulation of kinase domains under oxidative stress. Each system requires extensive conformational sampling (>10 μs aggregate simulation time) and quantum-level treatment of critical active-site residues. The requested computing resources will enable systematic benchmarking of density functional theory (DFT) methods for metalloenzyme clusters, comparative analysis of protonation state ensembles, and development of machine learning potentials to accelerate conformational search algorithms. Expected outcomes include atomistic insights into non-equilibrium catalytic mechanisms, predictive models for enzyme engineering applications, and methodological advances in multi-scale simulation workflows. By bridging quantum mechanical accuracy with biologically relevant timescales, this work aims to establish computational protocols that enhance the integration of theoretical modeling with experimental enzymology studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of principals of mathematical algorithms, statistics, and large databases to integrate chemical theory and modeling with experimental observations. Includes instruction in chemistry or a related scientific field, computer training, a familiarity with chemical principles, including conformational analysis, acid–base equilibria, physical organic chemistry, molecular structure, thermodynamics, and stereochemistry.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of adverse maternal and neonatal health outcomes using multi-source clinical and biomarker data. Despite advances in prenatal care, preterm birth, preeclampsia, and neonatal sepsis remain leading causes of morbidity and mortality, with complex interactions between genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors complicating risk stratification. Current statistical models lack the computational power to integrate high-dimensional datasets—including electronic health records, placental histopathology imaging, longitudinal cytokine profiles, and microbiome sequencing data—at the scale required for personalized risk prediction. This project will develop machine learning pipelines to analyze linked datasets from 25,000 maternal-neonatal dyads in the National Perinatal Registry, incorporating time-series analyses of vital sign trends, natural language processing of clinical notes, and convolutional neural networks for placental image classification. Computational challenges include harmonizing heterogeneous data formats, addressing class imbalances in rare outcomes, and optimizing parallel processing for real-time model retraining as new patient data streams in. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks such as genome-wide association studies (GWAS) coupled with electronic phenotyping, as well as for validating models through large-scale Monte Carlo simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive analytics framework for early identification of high-risk pregnancies, (2) biomarkers associated with dynamic risk trajectories, and (3) simulation tools to evaluate resource allocation strategies for neonatal intensive care units. By enabling integration of previously siloed data types at unprecedented scale, this work will provide clinically actionable insights to reduce health disparities in perinatal outcomes while serving as a training platform for nurse scientists in computational precision health methodologies.
cip_title: Maternal/ Child Health and Neonatal Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide prenatal care to pregnant women and to mothers and their newborn infants. Includes instruction in perinatal and newborn health assessment, stabilization, and care; pathophysiology of pregnancy, fetuses, and the newborn; clinical management of high-risk pregnancies and newborns; perinatal and neonatal technology and clinical procedures; and patient education.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational approaches in Slovak language studies, with a focus on analyzing linguistic variation and historical text corpora. Slovak’s rich morphological structure, dialectal diversity, and under-resourced status in digital humanities present unique challenges for automated analysis. Current tools optimized for major languages often fail to capture Slovak’s grammatical complexity, particularly in historical or non-standard texts. This project addresses these gaps by developing scalable pipelines for morphological tagging, dialect classification, and diachronic linguistic change detection. A corpus of digitized texts spanning 19th-century manuscripts to contemporary web-based sources will be processed using transformer-based models adapted for Slovak, supplemented by rule-based systems to handle irregular orthography in older documents. Computational workflows will map phonetic and lexical shifts across dialects using clustering algorithms and phylogenetic modeling, while GPU-accelerated training will optimize neural architectures for low-resource scenarios. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of annotated historical Slovak texts, a dialect classification toolkit, and quantitative models tracing language standardization processes. These resources will enable novel research in philology, support pedagogical tools for dialect preservation, and inform NLP applications in Slovak business and governmental contexts. The project’s computational demands—including large-scale parallel processing of terabyte-scale text data and iterative model training—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve timely results. By integrating computational linguistics with Slovak studies, this work aims to establish a methodological framework for under-resourced languages while deepening scholarly understanding of Slovak linguistic heritage. Results will be disseminated through open-source platforms, peer-reviewed publications, and collaborations with cultural institutions in Slovakia.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Slovak language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Sustainable forest management requires balancing timber production with ecological conservation, a challenge exacerbated by climate variability, shifting species distributions, and complex socio-economic demands. Current models for optimizing harvest schedules, predicting growth yields, and assessing ecological impacts lack the resolution and integration needed to address these multidimensional factors at landscape scales. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate forest growth, harvesting operations, and long-term sustainability outcomes under dynamic environmental and management scenarios. The research will integrate remote sensing data, machine learning-driven species distribution models, and agent-based simulations of harvesting workflows to quantify trade-offs between production efficiency, carbon sequestration, and biodiversity preservation. Computational workflows will process multi-terabyte LiDAR and hyperspectral datasets to parameterize forest structure and health metrics, while parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will evaluate millions of potential harvest strategies across synthetic and real-world forest landscapes in the Pacific Northwest. Key innovations include coupling discrete-event logging system models with ecophysiological growth projections, enabling fine-grained analysis of how equipment selection, road networks, and processing technologies influence both economic returns and ecosystem resilience. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive spatial analyses, reducing runtime for iterative optimization algorithms, and scaling validation across heterogeneous forest types. Expected outcomes include open-source decision support tools that enable stakeholders to visualize trade-offs in near-real time, prioritize climate-adaptive silviculture practices, and mitigate habitat fragmentation risks. By bridging industrial forestry operations with ecological forecasting, this work aims to establish computationally rigorous protocols for sustainable resource allocation in working forests under 21st-century environmental uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of forestry principles to the production, harvesting, and processing of forest resources and that prepares individuals to perform associated technical and managerial functions. Includes instruction in forest production and utilization, industrial forestry, agroforestry, transplantation, timber harvesting, selection and identification of trees, processing technologies and systems, equipment operations and maintenance, and related management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in the culinary science of baking and pastry arts, focusing on the optimization of complex ingredient interactions and environmental variables in artisanal and commercial baking processes. While traditional baking relies heavily on empirical trial-and-error methods, this research addresses the gap in predictive modeling for multi-scale phenomena such as gluten network formation, starch gelatinization dynamics, and moisture migration during baking. By integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for oven environment simulations, molecular dynamics (MD) for ingredient behavior at the nanoscale, and machine learning (ML) to correlate sensor data from baking trials with texture/quality outcomes, the project aims to develop a unified computational framework. This framework will model how variables like humidity, thermal gradients, and ingredient composition influence product consistency, shelf life, and sensory attributes. Key challenges include resolving time-dependent phase changes in heterogeneous mixtures (e.g., laminated doughs) and validating models against real-world baking scenarios captured via thermal imaging and 3D structure analysis. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations of multi-physics systems, large-scale parameter space exploration, and training of neural networks on high-dimensional datasets spanning diverse flour types, fermentation conditions, and baking techniques. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for reducing material waste in recipe development, adaptive baking protocols for non-standard environments (e.g., high-altitude adjustments), and data-driven insights into optimizing energy efficiency in commercial ovens. By bridging gastronomy, materials science, and computational modeling, this work will establish a novel methodological paradigm for culinary innovation while addressing pressing industry needs for sustainability and quality control in artisanal food production.
cip_definition: A program that prepares  individuals to serve as professional bakers and pastry specialists in restaurants or other commercial baking establishments.  Includes instruction in bread and pastry making, bread and pastry handling and storage, cake and pastry decorating, baking industry operations, product packaging and marketing operations, and counter display and service.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of dialectal variation in modern Catalan, with a focus on understudied regional and sociolinguistic dynamics. Despite Catalan’s status as a medium-sized European language with rich dialect diversity, comprehensive computational models of its phonetic, lexical, and morphosyntactic variability remain underdeveloped, particularly for non-standard registers and informal communication contexts. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models and phonetic alignment algorithms, to analyze a 20-million-word multimodal corpus comprising oral histories, social media data, and regional literature. Key computational challenges include training domain-specific language models for low-resource Catalan dialects, automating the detection of contact-induced innovations from neighboring languages, and simulating diachronic shifts in lexical usage across geographic micro-regions. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution audio data (via spectral clustering and formant analysis), optimizing dialect classification models through distributed hyperparameter tuning, and handling memory-intensive alignment tasks across heterogeneous text sources. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for Catalan dialectometry, a geolocative prediction model for text attribution, and a phonetically annotated corpus to support cross-disciplinary research in Catalan philology. By integrating computational rigor with traditional linguistic scholarship, this project aims to redefine methodological standards for regional language studies while providing actionable insights for language preservation initiatives and educational resource development in Catalan-speaking territories. The scalability of the framework will also establish a template for computational approaches to other minority languages with complex dialect landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Catalan language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing demand for effective postsecondary teaching practices in online and hybrid learning environments necessitates a deeper understanding of how instructional design choices impact learner engagement and outcomes. While existing research identifies broad principles for adult education (andragogy), there is a critical gap in modeling how specific pedagogical interventions—such as adaptive feedback mechanisms, multimodal content delivery, or discussion forum structures—affect heterogeneous student populations at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models that simulate learning processes across diverse virtual classroom environments, enabling data-driven optimization of teaching strategies. The research will leverage anonymized student interaction datasets from learning management systems (LMS), including timestamped resource accesses, assessment results, and discussion thread participation, paired with instructor-designed course structures. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks to model social learning dynamics and transformer-based architectures to analyze text interactions, will be implemented to identify patterns linking instructional variables to learning outcomes. Large-scale parameter sweeps will simulate variations in course design, while reinforcement learning frameworks will explore adaptive teaching policies. The computational demands of processing multimodal educational data (10M+ student interaction events across 500+ simulated course iterations) and training complex models require high-performance computing resources for parallelized simulations and efficient hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models quantifying relationships between instructional design features and discipline-specific critical thinking development, (2) evidence-based frameworks for personalizing scaffolding strategies in large-enrollment courses, and (3) open-source tools to help educators prototype and evaluate course designs computationally. By bridging learning science research with practical teaching applications, this work aims to advance computational pedagogy as a discipline while directly supporting faculty development programs in implementing effective, equitable teaching practices.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced computational framework for optimizing real-time decision-making in police patrol allocation and emergency response coordination. Current strategies for distributing law enforcement resources rely on static crime prediction models and historical data, which fail to adapt dynamically to emerging incidents, fluctuating urban mobility patterns, or complex socioenvironmental variables such as large-scale events or weather disruptions. The proposed study will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including real-time crime reports, traffic sensor feeds, social media activity, and public infrastructure status—into a machine learning-driven simulation environment to model dynamic risk landscapes. Agent-based modeling will simulate patrol units, civilian populations, and incident scenarios under varying constraints, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize allocation strategies. The computational intensity of training these models across thousands of simulated urban scenarios necessitates HPC capabilities to manage parallel processing of high-dimensional data streams and near-real-time parameter adjustments. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of proposing resource distribution adjustments at 15-minute intervals, validated against historical response efficiency metrics from three metropolitan police departments. This project addresses a critical gap in computational criminology by moving beyond retrospective crime mapping into proactive, adaptive resource management. Successful implementation could reduce emergency response latency by an estimated 18-22% in test jurisdictions while providing a framework to evaluate equity implications of allocation algorithms. The resulting models and simulation infrastructure will be made available to law enforcement agencies under collaborative agreements, prioritizing interpretability and ethical oversight in algorithmic decision-making processes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of police and public security officers, including patrol and investigative activities, traffic control, crowd control and public relations, witness interviewing, evidence collection and management, basic crime prevention methods, weapon and equipment operation and maintenance, report preparation and other routine law enforcement responsibilities.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an AI-driven framework for optimizing dynamic risk mitigation strategies in large-scale construction projects using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Construction projects face complex, interdependent risks—such as supply chain volatility, weather disruptions, labor shortages, and regulatory changes—that evolve unpredictably over time. Traditional risk management approaches, which rely on static models and linear assumptions, struggle to address the nonlinear interactions and real-time decision-making required for modern megaprojects. The computational challenge lies in modeling thousands of risk variables across technical, environmental, and socioeconomic domains while simulating adaptive mitigation pathways under uncertainty. Leveraging HPC capabilities, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating graph neural networks (GNNs) to map risk interdependencies, multi-agent reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate stakeholder decision dynamics, and discrete-event simulations to model cascading schedule impacts. The framework will ingest real-time data streams from IoT sensors, procurement databases, and geopolitical event feeds, processed through a scalable pipeline to update risk probabilities and mitigation ROI estimates. Key innovations include a stochastic scenario generator for stress-testing contingency plans and a combinatorial optimization layer to balance cost, safety, and sustainability constraints. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool that identifies high-probability risk cascades and recommends prioritized interventions, validated against historical data from three transnational infrastructure projects. This work aims to advance computational decision support systems in construction management by addressing latency and scalability barriers in existing software, ultimately reducing average project overruns by an estimated 12–18%. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 10^6+ scenario permutations per hour, surpassing current desktop-based solutions by three orders of magnitude. Findings will contribute methodological insights to the emerging field of adaptive resilience engineering in built environment management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply project management knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques in the construction and facility management industries. Includes instruction in facilities operations and maintenance, construction estimating, OSHA standards, sustainability, drafting, construction plans, project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: Cancer therapies often exhibit significant variability in patient response due to tumor heterogeneity, genetic polymorphisms, and dynamic resistance mechanisms. Optimizing drug selection, dosing, and combination strategies in oncology pharmacy remains a critical challenge, particularly for targeted therapies and immunomodulatory agents. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models integrating multi-omics data, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations, and clinical outcomes to guide precision dosing in solid tumors. The computational workflow will process large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets from public repositories (e.g., TCGA, GDSC) and institutional electronic health records, harmonizing these with drug exposure data from therapeutic drug monitoring programs. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to identify biomarkers associated with drug resistance and toxicity. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model drug-target interactions under varying mutational landscapes to prioritize combination therapies. HPC infrastructure is essential for managing petabyte-scale data, parallelizing molecular simulations across thousands of protein conformations, and optimizing hyperparameters in deep learning architectures through distributed computing. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for irinotecan and checkpoint inhibitor response in colorectal cancer, (2) a computational framework for simulating dose optimization scenarios under pharmacogenomic constraints, and (3) open-source tools for real-time toxicity risk stratification. This research will directly inform clinical trial designs for adaptive dosing regimens and provide oncology pharmacists with decision-support algorithms to personalize therapies. By bridging computational biology and clinical pharmacy, the project aims to reduce adverse drug events and improve progression-free survival rates in molecularly stratified patient cohorts.
cip_definition: Research focused on oncology pharmacy.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop and validate computational models for adaptive educational systems that dynamically personalize learning experiences using real-time multimodal data. A critical challenge in educational technology is the lack of scalable methods to process diverse learner interactions (e.g., clickstreams, assessment responses, and forum posts) while integrating contextual factors like prior knowledge and engagement patterns. Current systems often rely on static rules or simplified machine learning approaches, limiting responsiveness to individual needs. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining deep learning, reinforcement learning, and graph-based analytics. The project will utilize anonymized datasets from three online learning platforms containing 2.7 million learner interactions, including text, temporal sequences, and performance metrics. Computational workflows will involve training transformer-based architectures to model knowledge progression, graph neural networks to map concept dependencies, and multi-agent reinforcement learning simulations to optimize intervention strategies. The intensive nature of hyperparameter tuning for these models—particularly the memory-intensive processing of long interaction sequences and parallelized simulation of learner cohorts—necessitates GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory resources. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for adaptive learning system design, 2) empirical validation of model-driven personalization strategies across diverse demographic subgroups, and 3) scalable architectures for real-time inference in resource-constrained educational environments. By enabling more sophisticated analysis of learning trajectories at scale, this work aims to advance evidence-based approaches for equitable educational technology design while establishing computational benchmarks for the field. The requested resources will support both model training and the creation of synthetic datasets to address data scarcity issues in low-resource educational contexts.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, computer applications, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of enhancing pedagogical effectiveness in Latin language instruction by developing a data-driven, adaptive learning platform tailored for pre-service Latin teachers. Despite Latin’s structural complexity and its role in fostering critical linguistic and cultural competencies, current teacher training often relies on static curricula and limited personalized feedback mechanisms. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to design and train machine learning models that dynamically analyze learner interactions, predict areas of student difficulty, and generate real-time instructional recommendations for teacher candidates. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) to parse and evaluate Latin syntax, morphology, and translation exercises submitted by simulated K–12 students, alongside reinforcement learning algorithms to model adaptive teaching strategies. By processing large-scale datasets of historical student performance metrics and annotated classical texts, the platform will simulate diverse classroom scenarios, enabling teacher candidates to refine their instructional techniques in a risk-free virtual environment. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling these simulations, optimizing model accuracy through iterative training, and supporting concurrent user interactions during pilot testing. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for personalized Latin teacher training, open-access datasets of annotated pedagogical interactions, and evidence-based insights into optimizing metacognitive feedback in second-language acquisition. This work directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance innovative, scalable tools for Latin education, ultimately contributing to improved student outcomes in classical language programs and fostering equitable access to high-quality Latin instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach Latin at various grade levels.

abstract: Clinical Nurse Specialists (CNSs) operate in complex care environments where optimizing patient outcomes requires synthesizing multidimensional data, including clinical histories, pharmacotherapeutic interactions, and dynamic health indicators. However, the scale and heterogeneity of these datasets challenge traditional analytical approaches, limiting the ability to predict risks, personalize interventions, and inform evidence-based policies. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulation tools that enhance clinical decision-making for CNSs. The research will integrate anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), real-time biosensor data, and pharmacogenomic profiles to analyze patterns in adverse drug events, treatment responses, and recovery trajectories across diverse patient populations. Machine learning algorithms, including neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on HPC clusters to identify risk factors for hospital-acquired infections, predict opioid tolerance development, and model the efficacy of holistic interventions. Computational simulations will further test hypothetical care scenarios, such as dose adjustments in renal impairment or comorbidity-driven care pathway modifications. By parallelizing data processing and enabling high-dimensional parameter exploration, HPC resources will overcome bottlenecks in model training and validation. Expected outcomes include open-access decision support tools for bedside CNSs, risk stratification frameworks for health systems, and policy recommendations grounded in large-scale computational evidence. This work directly aligns with the CNS role in bridging direct care, consultation, and administrative leadership, offering scalable solutions to reduce preventable harm, address health disparities, and advance precision nursing. The requested computing infrastructure is critical to handling sensitive health data securely while delivering timely, actionable insights for clinical practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver direct patient and client care in clinical settings. Includes instruction in clinical pharmacotherapeutics, advanced clinical practice, holistic nursing, nursing practice and health care policy, administration and consultation services, health assessment, patient stabilization and care, and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze emergent vulnerabilities in hybrid physical-digital critical infrastructure systems, with a focus on interdependencies that could be exploited during multi-vector homeland security threats. While traditional risk assessments often isolate technological, human, and environmental factors, modern infrastructure networks—such as smart grids coupled with decentralized communication protocols or transportation systems reliant on crowdsourced data—exhibit complex, nonlinear behaviors that defy sector-specific analysis. The research problem centers on identifying cascading failure pathways that arise from adversarial manipulation of understudied interfaces between legacy infrastructure and adaptive, AI-driven systems. To address this, we propose a multi-method approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate hyper-realistic threat scenarios through agent-based modeling, dynamic network analysis, and stochastic optimization. Computational models will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including anonymized operational technology logs, geospatial threat intelligence, and behavioral patterns from synthetic population analogs, to stress-test resilience protocols under evolving attack modalities. Key innovations include the development of a modular simulation environment capable of scaling to city-level infrastructure networks while preserving granular details of subsystem interactions. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of latent vulnerabilities unique to hybrid infrastructure ecosystems, (2) predictive metrics for quantifying cascading impacts across cyber-physical-human domains, and (3) adaptive mitigation templates for infrastructure operators. By bridging infrastructure engineering principles with computational social science and adversarial machine learning techniques, this work aims to establish new paradigms for preemptive security planning in complex adaptive systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for maintaining fidelity across parallelized simulations, enabling real-time analysis of petascale datasets that mirror the complexity of modern national infrastructure networks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize the integration of geological and seismic data into civil engineering computer-aided drafting (CAD) and design (CADD) processes. Current civil drafting workflows struggle to efficiently process high-resolution geological datasets, particularly when simulating subsurface conditions or dynamic seismic loads in large-scale infrastructure projects. These limitations hinder the accuracy of risk assessments and the scalability of designs for complex sites. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML)-driven terrain modeling within CADD frameworks. The research will focus on three objectives: (1) implementing distributed computing algorithms to accelerate finite element simulations of soil-structure interactions under seismic loads, (2) training graph neural networks to predict optimal pipe network layouts in geologically heterogeneous environments, and (3) developing GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines for real-time visualization of 3D geological models in CAD software. The HPC infrastructure will allow iterative testing of parametric designs against probabilistic seismic hazard scenarios, reducing computational bottlenecks in multi-physics simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source CADD plugin for geotechnical data integration, validated against case studies of bridge and pipeline projects in seismically active regions. This work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven civil drafting that improves design resilience while maintaining compatibility with industry-standard workflows. By coupling HPC resources with CADD tools, the project will directly enhance educational training in computational civil engineering, providing students with hands-on experience in high-fidelity infrastructure modeling. The resulting methodologies will address critical gaps in drafting efficiency and precision for projects requiring complex geological considerations.
cip_title: Civil Drafting and Civil Engineering CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawing and electronic simulations in support of civil engineers, geological engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic civil engineering principles, geological and seismographic mapping, machine drafting, computer-aided drafting (CAD), pipe drafting, survey interpretation, and blueprint reading.

abstract: The increasing complexity of vendor-specific software ecosystems demands robust, scalable methods to automate certification processes for installation and maintenance engineers. Current approaches rely on static checklists and manual validation, which struggle to adapt to dynamic dependencies, heterogeneous environments, and evolving vendor requirements. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate, validate, and optimize certification workflows for vendor-supported software products using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on developing adaptive certification pipelines that account for real-world system variability, including hardware configurations, network topologies, and cross-product interactions. The computational approach integrates discrete-event simulation, dependency graph analysis, and machine learning to model installation scenarios across thousands of virtualized environments in parallel. Containerized testing environments will be orchestrated at scale to evaluate certification criteria under diverse conditions, while reinforcement learning agents will iteratively optimize maintenance protocols. Key challenges include minimizing false positives in automated compliance checks and ensuring deterministic reproducibility across hybrid cloud architectures. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration over combinatorial parameter spaces, including multi-vendor interoperability edge cases that exceed the capabilities of conventional testing platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating vendor-agnostic certification profiles, predictive models for installation failure risk assessment, and quantitative benchmarks for certification process efficiency. This work bridges gaps between software engineering practice and computational validation methodologies, offering a paradigm shift in how vendor qualifications are designed and assessed. The results will directly benefit professional certification bodies, software vendors seeking to streamline partner onboarding, and organizations requiring auditable compliance with technical support standards. By addressing certification as a computational reproducibility challenge, this project establishes foundational methods for trustable automation in product-specific engineering credentials.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to fulfill the requirements set by vendors for professional qualification as certified installation, customization, and maintenance engineers for specific software products and/or processes. Includes training in specific vendor-supported software products and their installation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to evaluate the effectiveness of multi-jurisdictional public policy interventions, with a focus on resource allocation efficiency and equity in complex governance systems. Public policy analysis increasingly relies on simulating dynamic interactions between policy design, stakeholder behavior, and systemic constraints, but existing approaches often oversimplify spatial, temporal, and institutional heterogeneity. Our research addresses this gap by creating an agent-based model that integrates geospatial data, institutional decision-making rules, and demographic microdata to simulate policy outcomes across diverse governance structures. The computational demands stem from modeling thousands of interdependent policy actors (e.g., municipal agencies, community organizations) operating under varying regulatory and resource conditions, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized scenario testing. We will utilize Python-based frameworks (Mesa, NumPy) enhanced with GPU-accelerated libraries (CuPy, RAPIDS) to optimize large-scale parameter sweeps analyzing trade-offs between centralized vs. decentralized policy implementation strategies. The model will be validated against historical records of housing affordability policies across three U.S. metropolitan regions, incorporating 10+ years of budgetary, demographic, and service utilization data. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for simulating resource allocation paths in policy domains such as emergency response coordination and infrastructure investment. This work will advance computational social science methodologies by formalizing decision-making heuristics used in public administration, while providing evidence-based insights about scaling localized policy solutions. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations of 100,000+ agent interactions across variable network topologies, enabling real-world applications to multi-agency collaboration challenges. Results will directly inform a longitudinal study on policy diffusion mechanisms funded by the National Center for Public Policy Research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues and decision processes. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, microeconomic analysis of policy issues, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze the nuanced linguistic structures of American Sign Language (ASL) in real-time interpretation scenarios, addressing critical gaps in automated support tools for sign language interpreters. Current technologies struggle to process the multimodal nature of ASL—which integrates handshapes, facial expressions, spatial grammar, and dynamic motion—at the speed and accuracy required for effective human-AI collaboration. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose training deep neural networks on a large-scale, annotated corpus of ASL video data to capture these complex features. The computational pipeline will include 3D convolutional networks for spatiotemporal feature extraction, transformer-based architectures for contextual disambiguation, and reinforcement learning to simulate real-world interpretation constraints. A key innovation involves parallelizing model training across GPU nodes to handle the high dimensionality of video data while maintaining sub-second latency for practical deployment. Outcomes will include open-source models for ASL phoneme recognition, a benchmarking toolkit for evaluating computational interpretation systems, and novel insights into the relationship between non-manual markers and semantic intent. This work directly supports the development of assistive technologies to reduce cognitive load for interpreters during extended sessions, with broader implications for accessibility in education, healthcare, and public services. The requested HPC resources are essential given the project’s scale: initial experiments suggest that processing 10,000+ hours of annotated ASL video requires petascale storage and weeks of compute time on specialized accelerators to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy. By advancing computational methods for under-resourced visual languages, this research bridges critical gaps between linguistic theory, translation practice, and equitable access to communication technologies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as simultaneous interpreters of American Sign Language

abstract: The proliferation of digital media has amplified challenges in understanding and mitigating misinformation across global communication ecosystems. Traditional analytical frameworks in communication and journalism studies struggle to process the scale, velocity, and multimodal nature of contemporary data, which spans terabytes of social media content, news archives, and multimedia sources. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable models for real-time misinformation detection and network dynamics analysis. Using a combination of natural language processing (NLP) techniques, deep learning architectures, and temporal network simulations, the research will analyze patterns of misinformation diffusion across platforms, identifying key actors, content characteristics, and contextual factors that drive virality. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to train transformer-based models on multilingual datasets, while agent-based simulations will map intervention strategies under varying sociotechnical conditions. The expected outcomes include (1) open-source tools for journalists and fact-checkers to prioritize high-impact misinformation cases, (2) evidence-based frameworks for platform governance informed by large-scale behavioral modeling, and (3) novel theoretical insights into the role of algorithmic amplification in cross-cultural communication contexts. By integrating computational rigor with media scholarship, this project aims to advance methodological innovation in communication research while addressing urgent societal needs for resilient information ecosystems.
cip_title: Communication, Journalism, and Related Programs, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication, journalism, and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Sustainable management of fish populations requires advanced predictive tools to address compounding pressures from climate change, habitat degradation, and overfishing. Current stock assessment models often lack the resolution to integrate dynamic environmental variables, species interactions, and human activity at ecologically relevant scales.
