Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking artifacts to reconstructed production contexts, quantitative models of regional stylistic convergence/divergence, and visualizations of previously unstudied coastal and overland exchange networks. This work will provide new methodologies for analyzing non-textual historical evidence while challenging nation-centric narratives of East Asian cultural heritage. The computational framework developed could be adapted to other regions and periods, advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of area studies, digital humanities, and heritage science.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of East Asia, defined as including China, Korea, Japan, Mongolia, Taiwan, Tibet, related borderlands and island groups, and including the study of the East Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in pediatric dentistry by modeling the complex interactions between oral microbiome dynamics, biomechanical stress patterns in developing dentition, and risk factors for early childhood caries (ECC) and enamel defects. Despite advances in preventive care, ECC remains a pervasive global health issue, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations, while developmental dental anomalies in children with disabilities present unique clinical challenges. Current predictive models lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale data—from genomic and metagenomic datasets to 3D biomechanical simulations—limiting personalized prevention strategies. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling of microbial communities, finite element analysis (FEA) of primary tooth structures under physiological stress, and machine learning (ML) to identify risk patterns from longitudinal clinical and imaging data. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of microbiome-host interactions under varying dietary and behavioral conditions, parallelized FEA of tooth morphology derived from cone-beam CT scans, and training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., genomic, sociodemographic, and geospatial data). Expected outcomes include predictive models of caries progression tailored to individual risk profiles, biomechanical insights into enamel fracture susceptibility, and optimized treatment planning protocols for children with developmental disabilities. By integrating multi-omics and biomechanical data at unprecedented scale, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of pediatric oral diseases and inform precision prevention strategies. The computational pipelines developed will be shared openly to support translational research in pediatric dentistry, with direct implications for reducing oral health disparities and improving clinical outcomes for vulnerable populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of children from birth through adolescence, and the care of adults with physical, mental, and emotional disabilities. Includes instruction in developmental oral biology, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, patient management, pediatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and the treatment of handicapped patients.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision firearm design and safety analysis through high-fidelity computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in gunsmithing research. Traditional gunsmithing relies heavily on empirical testing and manual iteration, which limits the ability to predict complex mechanical behaviors under dynamic stresses, such as barrel deformation, heat transfer during rapid firing, or gas flow dynamics in suppressor systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate and optimize firearm components under operational conditions. Key objectives include modeling stress distribution in custom barrel rifling designs, simulating thermal degradation in high-cycle firing scenarios, and analyzing gas dispersion patterns in modular suppressor configurations. These simulations will require parallelized solvers and large-scale parameter sweeps to account for material variability, geometric tolerances, and transient physical interactions. The HPC environment will enable multi-physics coupling at millisecond resolution while maintaining the granularity needed for micro-scale feature analysis (e.g., bore surface interactions, primer ignition dynamics). Expected outcomes include predictive models for component failure thresholds, data-driven design guidelines to reduce prototyping iterations, and open-access simulation toolkits tailored for gunsmithing education. By bridging computational engineering with applied gunsmithing, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based firearm customization while enhancing safety standards across the trade. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations, ML training on terabyte-scale datasets generated from parametric studies, and collaborative visualization of 3D simulation results for technical validation with practicing gunsmiths.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and modify firearms according to blueprints or customer specifications, using specialized hand tools and machines.

abstract: This project seeks to advance teacher professional development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze the efficacy of adaptive instructional strategies in diverse classroom environments. A critical challenge in teacher education is the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to evaluate how nuanced teaching behaviors—such as real-time feedback, differentiated instruction, and culturally responsive practices—impact student engagement and learning outcomes. Traditional observational studies are constrained by small sample sizes, manual coding, and limited generalizability. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom dynamics under varied pedagogical strategies. Large-scale datasets of teacher-student interactions (video, audio, and text transcripts from K-12 classrooms) will be processed using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to identify behavioral patterns. These patterns will inform the parameterization of ABMs, which will simulate how modifications to teacher strategies propagate through student networks, affecting collective learning. HPC resources are essential to train deep learning models on multimodal data (requiring GPU-accelerated processing) and to run thousands of parallelized ABM iterations, enabling robust sensitivity analyses across demographic and contextual variables. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework linking specific teaching practices to equity-focused student outcomes, (2) open-access tools for teacher educators to visualize and test strategy adaptations in virtual environments, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for personalized professional development programs. By quantifying the systemic impacts of teaching methods at scale, this work aims to transform how teacher preparation programs design clinical training and support data-informed instructional decision-making.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Levels and Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education and professional development, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize real-time decision-making in fashion show logistics and display design through advanced computational modeling, addressing the gap in data-driven frameworks for dynamic event coordination within the fashion modeling industry. Current practices rely heavily on experiential knowledge, leading to inefficiencies in managing variables such as model scheduling, spatial layouts, audience movement, and environmental factors (e.g., lighting, acoustics). The project proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation platform leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and reinforcement learning (RL) to predict and optimize resource allocation across these interdependent parameters. Using anonymized historical data from partner agencies—including model gait speeds, set change timelines, and audience engagement metrics—the ABM will simulate interactions between human agents (models, crew, attendees) and physical elements (runways, lighting rigs). RL algorithms will then iteratively refine scheduling and spatial configurations to minimize delays and maximize aesthetic impact. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to reflect the complexity of large-scale fashion events, enabling parallelized testing of thousands of scenario variations under stochastic conditions (e.g., equipment failures, last-minute lineup changes). Expected outcomes include a proprietary optimization toolkit capable of reducing event setup times by 15–20% while improving audience sightline coverage by 30%, metrics that directly translate to cost savings and enhanced brand value for stakeholders. Additionally, the project will produce a novel dataset correlating computational design choices with perceptual outcomes (e.g., audience attention patterns quantified via virtual eye-tracking), advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of operational logistics and sensory marketing. By formalizing tacit industry knowledge into transferable AI-driven models, this work establishes a foundation for computational resource management in niche creative industries that remain underserved by conventional business analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to present and display fashion, apparel, and accessories products in wholesale and retail settings, either on the person or via props and natural or artificial settings. Includes instruction in modeling skills, health and cosmetic principles, fashion show management, display design and production, and applicable aspects of advertising and fashion photography.

abstract: Dental materials must exhibit exceptional mechanical durability, biocompatibility, and bioactivity to withstand the dynamic oral environment while promoting tissue integration and minimizing adverse systemic effects. However, current material systems—such as resin composites, ceramics, and bioactive coatings—face challenges in balancing these properties, leading to premature failure, secondary caries, or inflammatory responses. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize next-generation dental biomaterials at multiple scales. We propose a computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to investigate material-tissue interactions, stress distribution in restorative interfaces, and degradation kinetics of bioactive compounds. MD will simulate atomic-scale interactions between novel zwitterionic polymers and oral microbiota to predict biofilm-resistant surfaces. FEA will model the viscoelastic behavior of resin-infiltrated dentin under cyclic masticatory loads, incorporating anisotropic tissue properties derived from micro-CT datasets. ML algorithms will identify correlations between material composition, processing parameters, and clinical performance metrics across heterogeneous datasets, enabling inverse design of composites with tailored stiffness and polymerization shrinkage profiles. HPC resources are critical to resolve the temporal and spatial complexity of these multiscale simulations, which involve millions of atoms in MD systems, micron-scale FEA meshes, and terabyte-scale experimental datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking molecular structure to biofilm adhesion and mechanical fatigue resistance, (2) optimized processing protocols for 3D-printed zirconia scaffolds with graded porosity, and (3) a computational database informing the design of antimicrobial calcium silicate cements. These results will advance the development of durable, bioactive dental materials while reducing reliance on iterative experimental testing. The resource allocation will directly support open-source tool development for the dental materials community, fostering collaboration between computational scientists and clinical researchers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing real-time, multi-platform advertising campaigns in fragmented media environments, where dynamic consumer behaviors and competitive bidding systems challenge traditional campaign management approaches. While advertising theory emphasizes personalized messaging and agile media buying, existing tools struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between audience segmentation, creative variations, and platform-specific algorithms at scale. The research will develop computational models to simulate cross-channel consumer response patterns under competing campaign parameters, using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in processing speed and dataset size. Methods integrate three components: 1) natural language processing of historical campaign creatives to identify sentiment and semantic features correlated with engagement metrics; 2) agent-based modeling of user attention dynamics across social, search, and streaming platforms; and 3) reinforcement learning architectures to simulate bid optimization strategies under budget constraints. The simulations will utilize anonymized industry datasets encompassing 2.3 billion ad impressions, requiring parallelized processing of temporal interaction chains and high-dimensional feature spaces. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting audience saturation points in multi-touchpoint campaigns and quantifying the marginal returns of creative refreshes under different budget allocation scenarios. By enabling granular analysis of platform interdependencies that influence campaign wear-out rates, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for maintaining message effectiveness in oversaturated media ecosystems. The computational models will be validated against experimental campaign data from three partner agencies, with open-source release of non-proprietary algorithm components to support pedagogical applications in advertising program curricula. This project demonstrates how HPC capabilities can expand the methodological toolkit for communication research, particularly in addressing scalability challenges inherent to modern digital advertising systems.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creation, execution, transmission, and evaluation of commercial messages in various media intended to promote and sell products, services, and brands; and that prepares individuals to function as advertising assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in advertising theory, marketing strategy, advertising design and production methods, campaign methods and techniques, media management, related principles of business management, and applicable technical and equipment skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making in correctional facility management through predictive modeling and simulation of inmate population dynamics, resource allocation, and operational risk factors. Corrections administration faces complex challenges, including fluctuating incarceration rates, overcrowding, staff shortages, and budgetary constraints, yet traditional analytical tools often lack the capacity to model nonlinear interactions between institutional policies, demographic trends, and behavioral outcomes. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate facility operations under varying policy scenarios, integrating heterogeneous data sources such as historical incarceration patterns, program participation records, and environmental sensor data from correctional infrastructure. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of autonomous agents (inmates, staff, and administrators) with dynamic rule sets governing movement, rehabilitation programming, and crisis response protocols. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibration datasets from three state correctional systems to improve model fidelity, while Monte Carlo methods will assess uncertainty in policy outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of identifying high-risk operational bottlenecks, forecasting the impact of diversion programs on recidivism, and evaluating cost-benefit tradeoffs in facility modernization initiatives. By translating qualitative administrative principles into quantitative decision-support tools, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in a domain where computational approaches remain underutilized despite growing demands for systemic efficiency and accountability. The project will further establish methodological precedents for applying HPC to operational challenges in non-traditional, public-sector contexts, with potential extensions to emergency management and institutional logistics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage institutional facilities and programs for housing and rehabilitating prisoners in the public and/or private sectors. Includes instruction in the principles and practice of correction, facilities planning and management, safety and security, social and health services, staff and inmate management, budgeting, communication skills, correctional psychology, and applications to specific types of correctional facilities approaches.

abstract: Climate variability and emerging plant pathogens increasingly threaten global crop productivity, necessitating advanced tools to predict and mitigate agricultural risks. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale modeling framework that integrates genomic, phenotypic, and environmental data for optimizing crop resilience strategies. The research focuses on staple crops critical to regional food security, employing machine learning algorithms to analyze terabyte-scale datasets spanning decades of agronomic trials, satellite-derived climate records, and high-throughput sequencing data. Key computational challenges include parallelizing genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify stress-responsive genetic markers and training neural networks to simulate crop responses under diverse biotic and abiotic stressors. By coupling these models with real-time sensor data from precision agriculture systems, the project aims to generate dynamic recommendations for cultivar selection, planting schedules, and disease management. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable parameter optimization across millions of simulated scenarios while maintaining computational tractability. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for extension services, molecular breeding targets with validated drought tolerance traits, and risk maps identifying vulnerable agricultural zones under projected climate scenarios. This work directly supports evidence-based policymaking and on-farm decision-making, bridging the gap between genomic discovery and field-scale implementation. Successful implementation will demonstrate how computational advances can accelerate the development of climate-smart agricultural systems while preserving genetic diversity in key crops.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general agricultural sciences and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the efficacy of adaptive health education curricula in diverse classroom environments, with the goal of optimizing training strategies for pre-service health teachers. Despite evidence that personalized pedagogical approaches improve student health literacy, existing teacher education programs often rely on static, generalized content, limiting preparedness to address varied student needs. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate classroom scenarios and evaluate how dynamically adjusted curricula impact both teacher competency and hypothetical student outcomes. Agent-based modeling will be used to represent interactions between teachers-in-training and simulated student populations with heterogeneous socioeconomic, cultural, and cognitive characteristics. Machine learning algorithms will iteratively refine curriculum recommendations based on emergent patterns in pedagogical effectiveness across 10,000+ simulated classroom trials. The computational workload requires parallelized processing of multidimensional datasets tracking knowledge retention, engagement metrics, and behavioral outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of core adaptability competencies for health educators, (2) data-driven frameworks for tailoring teacher training modules, and (3) open-source simulation tools to help education programs test curriculum designs in silico before implementation. By quantifying how specific instructional strategies propagate through educational systems, this work aims to establish scalable methods for enhancing health teacher readiness. The project directly aligns with national priorities to improve preventive health education through evidence-based teacher preparation while avoiding administrative or policy-focused analyses excluded by the program scope. Successful implementation depends on HPC capabilities to manage complex parameter spaces and real-time model optimization beyond the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach health education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern automotive systems, particularly in hybrid and electric vehicle architectures, demands advanced computational tools to optimize component integration, system efficiency, and durability under dynamic operating conditions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support the development of multi-physics simulation frameworks for next-generation vehicular systems. Current design and testing methodologies rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-intensive and costly, especially when evaluating interactions between electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical subsystems. The proposed research will address this gap by creating scalable computational models to simulate coupled phenomena in battery thermal management, power electronics cooling, and lightweight composite material behavior under mechanical stress. High-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will be implemented using open-source and commercial solvers (e.g., OpenFOAM, ANSYS) to predict system-level performance across diverse operating scenarios. Machine learning techniques will augment these models to identify optimal design parameters and accelerate convergence. The HPC environment is critical for handling large-scale datasets from sensor-integrated prototype testing and enabling parallelized simulations of transient, multi-domain interactions. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for component degradation, energy-efficient thermal regulation strategies, and data-driven design guidelines to extend the operational lifespan of electric drivetrain systems. This work will provide a foundation for virtual prototyping workflows that reduce reliance on physical testing, lower development costs, and enhance the reliability of emerging automotive technologies. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and integrated into applied engineering curricula, bridging gaps between computational research and hands-on automotive technology training.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate high-performance computing (HPC) into the creation and analysis of advanced metal artworks, addressing the growing complexity of computational design and material simulations in contemporary metal arts practice. Traditional fabrication methods, such as casting, welding, and electroforming, often rely on iterative physical prototyping, which limits the exploration of intricate geometries and material behaviors. To overcome these constraints, this research proposes the development of computational models to simulate metallurgical processes, thermal dynamics in welding, and stress distribution in sculptural forms. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be applied to predict outcomes of anodizing, enameling, and wax-carving workflows, enabling data-driven refinements before physical execution. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on historical and contemporary metalwork datasets to propose novel design configurations that balance aesthetic intent with structural feasibility. The HPC resources will facilitate large-scale parameter testing for alloy interactions during electroforming, high-resolution 3D modeling of texture variations in repoussé, and real-time rendering of kinetic metal installations. Expected outcomes include optimized fabrication protocols for reducing material waste, a publicly accessible database of simulation results for educational use, and a framework for integrating computational tools into studio practice. By bridging computational modeling with hands-on craftsmanship, this project aims to expand the technical and expressive possibilities of metal arts while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between digital methodologies and traditional studio disciplines. The results will contribute to pedagogical resources for training artists in hybrid digital-physical workflows, ensuring the field’s adaptation to emerging technologies in the visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of individual artistic expression and technical skills necessary for fabricating refined metal works. Includes instruction in aesthetics, anodizing, art history, casting, design, electroforming, enameling, metalsmithing, sculpture, two and three-dimensional design, wax carving, and welding.

abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified challenges in managing real-time decision-making, scalability, and security across dynamic digital markets. Existing computational methods struggle to optimize complex, large-scale systems—such as personalized recommendation engines, supply chain networks, and fraud detection algorithms—while maintaining responsiveness and data integrity. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test computational models that address these limitations. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) simulating multi-agent e-commerce ecosystems to evaluate adaptive pricing strategies under fluctuating demand, (2) training deep reinforcement learning models for real-time inventory optimization across distributed warehouses, and (3) deploying privacy-preserving federated learning frameworks to detect cross-platform transactional fraud without compromising sensitive user data. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized architectures to process terabyte-scale datasets, including customer interaction logs, supply chain telemetry, and synthetic transaction records generated via generative adversarial networks (GANs). The project integrates graph neural networks to model interdependencies in global supplier networks and employs GPU-accelerated hyperparameter tuning to enhance model accuracy. Outcomes will include open-source tools for scalable demand forecasting, resource allocation algorithms to reduce logistics-related emissions, and a benchmark dataset for evaluating e-commerce fraud detection systems. By enabling granular analysis of system-wide trade-offs between efficiency, cost, and security, this work will advance scalable solutions for sustainable digital commerce. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming memory and latency constraints inherent in traditional cloud environments, ensuring the practical applicability of findings for businesses operating in data-intensive, latency-sensitive markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, supervise, and market electronic business operations, products, and services provided online via the Internet. Includes instruction in business administration, information technology, information resources management, web design, computer and Internet law and policy, computer privacy and security, e-trading, insurance, electronic marketing, investment capital planning, enterprise operations, personnel supervision, contracting, and product and service networking.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural evolution of European political networks from the late medieval period to the early modern era (c. 1400–1700) through computational analysis of digitized archival materials. Traditional historiography has often relied on selective case studies due to the sheer volume and linguistic diversity of primary sources, leaving broader patterns of institutional collaboration and conflict under-explored. The research will employ high-performance computing resources to process and analyze multilingual corpora comprising over 100,000 digitized documents—including treaties, diplomatic correspondence, and administrative records—from repositories across Europe. Natural language processing techniques, customized for historical linguistic variants through transformer-based models, will enable entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and semantic mapping of political discourse. Concurrently, network analysis algorithms will reconstruct shifting alliances and power dynamics across temporal and spatial dimensions. A second component utilizes computer vision to examine the material evolution of legal and governmental documents, identifying visual markers of bureaucratic formalization through layout analysis and symbol recognition. These computational approaches require significant parallel processing capabilities for training domain-specific language models, processing high-resolution manuscript images, and running iterative simulations of network interactions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking analyzed documents to network visualizations, quantitative frameworks for assessing institutional continuity amid political fragmentation, and new methodological protocols for computationally assisted historiography. By systematically addressing scale and complexity barriers in primary source analysis, this project aims to redefine scholarly understanding of state formation processes and cross-cultural governance models in premodern Europe.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of European society, culture, and institutions from the origins to the present. Includes instruction in European historiography, European history sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize drywall installation workflows, enhance material efficiency, and improve structural performance in residential and commercial construction. While modern drywall practices rely on empirical guidelines and manual techniques, there is a critical need for data-driven approaches to address challenges such as material waste (up to 15% in typical projects), inconsistent joint finishing quality, and suboptimal load distribution in complex architectural designs. We propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element modeling (DEM) to simulate drywall panel behavior under mechanical stresses, environmental changes, and human installation factors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parametric studies of 1) panel cutting patterns minimizing waste while maintaining structural integrity, 2) spackle compound curing dynamics under varying humidity/temperature conditions, and 3) ergonomic analysis of installer movements to reduce workplace injuries. Machine learning models trained on simulated and experimental data (from partner contractors) will predict optimal installation sequences and material combinations. The computational pipeline will integrate building information modeling (BIM) data, material property databases, and ASTM standards to ensure practical applicability. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for drywall contractors that recommends installation strategies balancing cost, durability, and code compliance, validated through physical prototypes. By establishing quantitative relationships between installation parameters and long-term wall performance, this research aims to advance technical education in drywall programs while reducing construction waste by an estimated 8-12% in modeled scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling 3D transient simulations of composite drywall systems at relevant spatial scales (0.1–10 m) and temporal resolutions (minutes to decades of service life).
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, tape, and plaster drywall installations in interior and exterior construction jobs. Includes instruction in drywall handling and transport, cutting and mounting, taping and spackling, finishing, job analysis and estimation, site safety, tool operation and maintenance, blueprint and specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding population dynamics under rapidly evolving environmental, social, and public health stressors. Traditional demographic models often struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions between migration, fertility, mortality, and spatial redistribution, particularly when incorporating high-dimensional data from satellite imagery, mobile device tracking, and longitudinal surveys. The research will develop and validate a scalable computational framework to simulate population responses to multi-scale shocks, such as climate-induced displacement, pandemic recovery disparities, and urbanization pressures. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with Bayesian hierarchical models, the project will simulate individual and household decision-making processes across diverse geographic and socioeconomic contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of iteratively parameterizing millions of agents, processing petabyte-scale geospatial inputs, and running ensemble projections under uncertainty. Parallelized algorithms will optimize spatial microsimulations across GPU clusters, while machine learning pipelines will identify latent patterns in heterogeneous demographic datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible library of modular code for demographic ABMs, (2) high-resolution projections of migration corridors under climate scenarios for vulnerable regions, and (3) probabilistic estimates of policy impacts on fertility transitions. By enabling real-time assimilation of emerging data streams—such as crisis-driven migration flows—the framework will advance capacity for adaptive policy planning. The requested resources will support comparative analyses across 15+ countries, leveraging census microdata and Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) harmonized over three decades. Validation against historical counterfactuals will quantify model robustness. This work directly addresses methodological limitations in current population projections by formalizing complex feedback between individual behaviors and structural constraints, with particular attention to gender disparities in migration accessibility. The computational tools developed will provide foundational infrastructure for the demography community to explore "what-if" scenarios through accessible, replicable workflows.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of population models and population phenomena, and related problems of social structure and behavior. Includes instruction in population growth, spatial distribution, mortality and fertility factors, migration, dynamic population modeling, population estimation and projection, mathematical and statistical analysis of population data, population policy studies, and applications to problems in economics and government planning.

abstract: Understanding the systemic interplay between metabolic regulation and immune activation during chronic inflammatory diseases remains a critical challenge in biomedical research. Traditional experimental approaches often fail to capture the dynamic, multi-organ interactions that drive disease progression and treatment resistance. This project seeks to develop a large-scale computational model integrating metabolic pathways, immune signaling networks, and tissue-specific responses to investigate system-level dysregulations in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease. The proposed framework will employ differential equation-based modeling to simulate real-time crosstalk between hepatic metabolic processes, circulatory cytokine dynamics, and immune cell recruitment across affected tissues. High-performance computing resources are essential to solve millions of coupled equations simultaneously, parameterize models using heterogeneous clinical datasets, and perform sensitivity analyses across physiological timescales. Expected outcomes include identification of critical regulatory nodes governing inflammatory persistence, prediction of combinatorial therapeutic targets addressing both metabolic and immunological components, and generation of patient-specific in silico platforms for treatment optimization. By elucidating emergent properties of systemic inflammation, this work aims to advance precision medicine strategies for complex chronic diseases while providing a scalable computational framework applicable to diverse biomedical research contexts.
cip_definition: A general, program that focuses on the integrative scientific study of biological issues related to health and medicine, or a program in one or more of the biomedical sciences that is undifferentiated as to title. Includes instruction in any of the basic medical sciences at the research level; biological science research in biomedical faculties; and general studies encompassing a variety of the biomedical disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven educational tools for students with multiple disabilities. Current pedagogical approaches for this population often rely on generalized strategies that fail to account for the complex interplay of sensory, cognitive, and motor impairments unique to each learner. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multimodal data—including eye-tracking, physiological sensors, and behavioral assessments—to model individualized learning pathways. The research problem centers on optimizing real-time analysis of heterogeneous datasets to dynamically adjust instructional content, environmental stimuli, and assistive technologies during teaching sessions. Computational methods will involve training machine learning classifiers to recognize patterns in student engagement and distress signals, coupled with agent-based simulations to predict the efficacy of intervention strategies across diverse disability profiles. HPC resources are critical for processing high-frequency sensor data, running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and iteratively refining neural network architectures for personalized recommendation systems. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educators to design responsive lesson plans informed by predictive analytics, as well as empirically validated thresholds for sensory input modulation to reduce cognitive overload. By bridging educational theory with computational modeling, this work aims to establish scalable methods for tailoring instruction to the needs of students with co-occurring disabilities, ultimately improving academic participation and reducing barriers to learning. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated through partnerships with special education training programs, ensuring direct translation of technical advances into teacher preparation frameworks.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Multiple Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with multiple disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with multiple disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with multiple handicaps, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for integrating heterogeneous medical data sources—including electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and genomic datasets—to enable precision medicine applications in clinical decision-making. A critical challenge in medical informatics lies in synthesizing high-dimensional, multi-modal data to generate actionable insights while preserving patient privacy and data integrity. Current methods struggle with computational inefficiency when processing terabytes of imaging data, harmonizing unstructured clinical notes, and identifying biomarkers from genome-wide associations. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline leveraging distributed deep learning, federated learning architectures, and natural language processing (NLP) to analyze de-identified EHRs, radiology images, and sequencing data from [Institution]’s clinical research repositories. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated clusters for training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on 3D medical imaging data, parallelized NLP models for extracting phenotypic features from clinical narratives, and privacy-preserving federated learning to integrate insights across institutions without raw data sharing. The HPC environment is essential to manage memory-intensive tasks, such as whole-slide image analysis, and to reduce model training times from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for early detection of [specific disease/complication, e.g., sepsis, cancer progression] using multi-modal data fusion, (2) an open-source toolkit for federated analysis of sensitive medical datasets, and (3) benchmarks demonstrating scalability to petabyte-scale data. This work will advance medical informatics infrastructure by enabling efficient, secure analysis of large-scale clinical data, directly supporting translational research in personalized treatment planning and real-time decision support systems. The requested computing resources will ensure rigorous validation of these methods, fostering reproducibility and deployment in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to medical research and clinical information technology support, and the development of advanced imaging, database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in computer science, health information systems architecture, medical knowledge structures, medical language and image processing, quantitative medical decision modeling, imaging techniques, electronic medical records, medical research systems, clinical decision support, and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic relationship between digital communication platforms and emergent linguistic phenomena, focusing on how decentralized, large-scale online interactions drive rapid syntactic and semantic shifts in understudied multilingual contexts. While traditional sociolinguistic frameworks have examined language change in physical communities, the computational demands of analyzing real-time, cross-platform digital discourse—particularly in low-resource languages and non-standard dialects—remain a critical barrier. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process terabytes of timestamped textual data from social media, messaging apps, and collaborative platforms across five linguistically diverse regions, targeting communities with limited prior documentation of their digital linguistic practices. A hybrid methodology combining transformer-based neural architectures for morphosyntactic annotation, agent-based modeling of lexical diffusion networks, and graph-theoretic analysis of semantic field evolution will be implemented. Custom pipelines will be developed to handle code-switching patterns, non-Latin scripts, and platform-specific orthographic variations, with iterative model training conducted on GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for detecting latent grammatical innovations in noisy, multilingual digital corpora; (2) quantitative models correlating platform affordances (e.g., character limits, reaction features) with rates of semantic change; and (3) an open-access repository of annotated datasets representing under-resourced digital language varieties. By elucidating the computational signatures of online language adaptation, this work aims to advance theoretical understanding of how technosocial systems shape linguistic diversity while providing practical tools for educators and developers working with marginalized language communities in digital spaces. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive graph computations, parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams, and large-scale comparative simulations across linguistic subsystems.
cip_title: Linguistic, Comparative, and Related Language Studies and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in linguistic, comparative, and related language studies and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The management of pediatric liver transplantation faces significant challenges in predicting graft survival, optimizing immunosuppressive regimens, and mitigating post-transplant complications. Current clinical decision-making relies on static biomarkers and population-level data, which inadequately address the dynamic interplay of immunological, metabolic, and developmental factors unique to children. This project proposes to bridge this gap by developing patient-specific computational models to predict individualized outcomes and therapeutic responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate longitudinal clinical data (e.g., liver function tests, immunosuppressant levels), multi-omics profiles (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic), and serial imaging from a retrospective cohort of 500 pediatric liver transplant recipients. Machine learning pipelines will be designed to identify dynamic signatures of graft rejection, metabolic dysregulation, and drug toxicity, while agent-based models will simulate immune-cell interactions and hepatic regeneration patterns under varying therapeutic conditions. Computational workflows will require parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization, Bayesian inference for uncertainty quantification in sparse pediatric datasets, and real-time visualization of multi-dimensional data. Anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms for early rejection risk stratification, personalized dosing guidelines for immunosuppression, and mechanistic insights into age-specific immune tolerance pathways. These tools aim to reduce graft loss rates, minimize treatment-related morbidity, and establish a scalable framework for precision hepatology in pediatric transplantation. The project’s computational demands—including terabyte-scale data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and ensemble simulation runs—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve clinically actionable results within the study timeline.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge, skill, and expertise required of pediatric gastroenterologists to care for children and young adults prior to and following hepatic transplantation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cyber-physical systems and the dynamic nature of modern cyber threats have exposed critical gaps in traditional security auditing frameworks, which often rely on static rule sets and manual validation processes. These methods struggle to adapt to evolving attack vectors, heterogeneous network architectures, and the scale of data generated by distributed systems, leaving organizations vulnerable to sophisticated breaches. This project proposes the development of an adaptive, bio-inspired auditing framework that integrates spiking neural networks (SNNs) with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to autonomously detect, classify, and respond to anomalies in real time. By simulating the decentralized decision-making observed in natural systems—such as immune response and swarm intelligence—the framework will dynamically prioritize threats, optimize audit policies, and identify latent vulnerabilities across large-scale infrastructures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train SNN models on petabyte-scale network telemetry datasets, simulate diverse attack scenarios (including adversarial machine learning tactics), and optimize MARL agents through parallelized evolutionary algorithms. The computational workload involves iterative cycles of anomaly injection, policy adaptation, and resilience testing across hybrid cloud-edge environments. Expected outcomes include a novel auditing toolkit capable of operating in resource-constrained settings, a benchmark dataset of adaptive threat signatures, and quantifiable metrics for auditing process efficacy under zero-day attack conditions. This work bridges gaps between cybersecurity, computational biology, and autonomous systems engineering, offering a paradigm shift from compliance-centric audits to proactive, self-healing security architectures. The resulting framework will be validated against NIST SP 800-53 controls and tested in partnership with a regional healthcare consortium managing IoT-enabled critical infrastructure.
cip_title: Computer and Information Systems Security/ Auditing/ Information Assurance
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assess the security needs of computer and network systems, recommend safeguard solutions, and manage the implementation, auditing, and maintenance of security devices, systems, and procedures. Includes instruction in computer architecture, programming, and systems analysis; networking; telecommunications; cryptography; security system auditing and design; applicable law and regulations; risk assessment and policy analysis; contingency planning; user access issues; investigation techniques; and troubleshooting.

abstract: Military information systems face escalating demands for real-time data processing, secure communication, and adaptive decision-making in dynamic operational environments. Existing architectures often struggle to balance computational efficiency with robust cybersecurity, particularly when scaling to support distributed, resource-constrained edge devices in contested networks. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing and validating a novel framework for intelligent resource orchestration in tactical networks using high-performance computing (HPC) simulations. The research will model multi-domain military operations with variable latency thresholds, intermittent connectivity, and adversarial cyber-physical threats to identify performance bottlenecks in current resource allocation strategies. Computational methods will combine discrete-event simulation, graph-based network analysis, and reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to optimize task offloading, energy-aware routing, and dynamic encryption schema selection under realistic constraints. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter space exploration across heterogeneous node configurations, threat profiles, and mission-critical workload types. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for trust-aware resource partitioning, predictive models for bandwidth allocation during network degradation, and adaptive policies for balancing cryptographic overhead with quality-of-service requirements. The resulting framework aims to provide a testbed for evaluating emergent technologies like quantum-resistant protocols and neuromorphic computing architectures in militarily relevant scenarios. By bridging computational theory with applied systems design, this work will inform next-generation standards for secure, autonomous decision-support systems in defense networks while maintaining alignment with operational security constraints. Success metrics emphasize reproducible performance gains in simulated contested environments and the development of open-source simulation tools adaptable to diverse military use cases.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, design and application of computer and networking technology to the military environment. Includes instruction in planning; program development; graphical user interfaces; rapid prototyping; program construction; data types, operations; control flow; arrays; records; file I/O; database access; event-driven OOP structures; and enabling global-networked communications, including databases, systems analysis and design, decision support systems, and network security.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in nursing education and clinical decision-making through advanced simulation and predictive modeling. Despite the growing complexity of healthcare environments, practical and vocational nursing programs often rely on static training scenarios, limiting students’ exposure to high-risk, low-frequency clinical events. Additionally, optimizing nurse-patient assignment strategies in dynamic care settings remains an understudied area with significant implications for patient outcomes and workforce efficiency. To bridge these gaps, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and discrete-event simulation (DES). The ABM component will simulate diverse clinical environments with variable patient acuity, staffing ratios, and workflow interruptions, generating synthetic training datasets for adaptive virtual simulations. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze historical electronic health record (EHR) data to identify patterns in patient deterioration, enabling real-time risk prediction. The DES module will model facility-wide patient flow to evaluate nurse-patient assignment policies under resource constraints. HPC resources are essential for parallel execution of thousands of simulation iterations across parameter spaces encompassing patient demographics, care protocols, and staffing variables. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access virtual clinical training platform with dynamically responsive patient avatars, (2) predictive tools for early detection of clinical deterioration in acute care settings, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for nurse-patient assignment optimization. By combining large-scale synthetic data generation with empirical EHR analysis, this computational approach will enhance both nursing education and clinical practice while maintaining alignment with real-world care environments. The project’s outputs will directly benefit practical nursing programs seeking to improve simulation fidelity and healthcare institutions aiming to reduce adverse events through data-driven staffing strategies.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in voice-driven data entry systems, which remain prone to errors and latency in dynamic real-world environments, limiting their adoption in settings requiring hands-free operation, such as healthcare or industrial workflows. While existing speech-to-text tools excel in controlled conditions, their performance degrades under acoustic variability, overlapping speech, or domain-specific terminology. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing an adaptive, high-throughput framework for voice data entry by integrating noise-robust acoustic modeling, real-time natural language processing (NLP), and context-aware error correction. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize three core tasks: (1) training hybrid deep learning models on multi-domain speech corpora augmented with environmental noise profiles, (2) simulating real-time transcription workflows under scaled user concurrency to optimize resource allocation, and (3) deploying ensemble NLP techniques to infer contextual intent from fragmented or ambiguous audio inputs. By distributing model training across GPU nodes and emulating heterogeneous microphone arrays through virtualized audio streams, the system will dynamically adapt to speaker accents, background noise levels, and task-specific vocabularies. Expected outcomes include an open-source middleware library for low-latency voice data entry, validated against clinical dictation and logistics reporting use cases. Success metrics prioritize a 40% reduction in post-editing effort compared to commercial tools under noisy conditions. This work bridges gaps between speech processing, human-computer interaction, and microcomputer application design, offering a scalable solution to enhance accessibility and efficiency in data capture workflows. The requested computing resources will enable the large-scale simulations and model optimizations necessary to achieve robust, generalizable performance across underserved domains.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform basic data and text entry using standard and customized software products. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, personal computer and work station operation, reading draft texts and raw data forms, audio and tape dictation, and various interactive software programs used for tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, databases, and others.

abstract: Dental implantology faces a critical challenge in predicting long-term biomechanical stability due to the complex interplay between implant design, bone remodeling, and patient-specific anatomical factors. Current clinical methods rely on static imaging and empirical protocols, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between mechanical stress distributions, cellular bone adaptation, and soft tissue integration. This project proposes a computational framework to model the multiscale biomechanical and biological processes governing osseointegration and peri-implant tissue remodeling. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop patient-specific finite element models derived from cone-beam CT data, integrated with agent-based simulations of osteoblast-osteoclast activity and mechanobiological feedback loops. The models will incorporate time-dependent variables such as occlusal loading patterns, micromotion at the bone-implant interface, and systemic factors (e.g., bone density, metabolic rates) to predict long-term outcomes under diverse physiological conditions. A machine learning pipeline will optimize parameter space exploration, enabling probabilistic risk assessment for implant failure modes including marginal bone loss and prosthetic complications. The computational workflow will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from 300+ implant cases with 5-year follow-up. By establishing predictive relationships between biomechanical stimuli and biological responses, this research aims to generate actionable guidelines for implant selection, surgical planning, and load management protocols. The resulting framework will advance precision in implant dentistry while providing a template for computational biomechanics applications in other medical device integration challenges. HPC resources are essential to manage the high-resolution multiphysics simulations, large-scale parameter optimization, and complex data assimilation required for this real-time adaptive modeling approach.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in chemistry teacher education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate complex chemical systems for use in instructional design. A persistent challenge in chemistry education is the limited accessibility of advanced computational tools for pre-service and in-service teachers, which restricts their ability to integrate modern research-grade simulations into classroom pedagogy. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a suite of interactive, curriculum-aligned computational chemistry modules that model dynamic molecular processes, reaction mechanisms, and spectroscopic data analysis. These modules will employ density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using software packages such as Gaussian and GROMACS, which require HPC resources to handle the computational intensity of multi-electron systems and nanosecond-scale trajectories. The project will also incorporate machine learning approaches to analyze simulation outputs and generate simplified visualizations tailored to diverse learner backgrounds. By coupling these computational workflows with guided pedagogical frameworks, the research aims to empower educators to demystify abstract chemical concepts through real-time visualization and hypothesis testing. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of scalable lesson plans, validation data on student learning gains when taught using these tools, and evidence-based guidelines for integrating HPC-driven simulations into teacher training programs. This work will advance science education by establishing a model for merging computational chemistry research with classroom-ready applications, ultimately fostering teacher confidence in using cutting-edge scientific tools to inspire deeper student engagement with chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach chemistry programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Clinical informatics research faces a critical challenge in integrating heterogeneous healthcare data—including electronic health records (EHRs), imaging, genomic data, and real-time sensor outputs—into actionable insights for precision medicine. Existing methods often struggle with scalability, interoperability, and computational efficiency, particularly when analyzing multi-modal datasets across large patient populations. This project proposes the development of a federated machine learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to address these limitations. The research will focus on creating computational workflows that harmonize structured and unstructured clinical data while preserving patient privacy through distributed learning architectures. Key technical objectives include training deep learning models for cross-institutional predictive analytics, deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract latent features from clinical notes, and simulating patient-specific treatment outcomes using graph neural networks. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization at scale, and real-time validation of models against synthetic clinical trial data. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for temporal data fusion, a validated pipeline for federated model training across geographically dispersed EHR systems, and probabilistic decision-support tools for personalized intervention planning. This work will directly advance clinical informatics by addressing computational bottlenecks in multi-omics integration, enhancing the reproducibility of predictive models, and enabling resource-efficient analysis of longitudinal health data. The requested computing resources are essential for managing memory-intensive operations, reducing wall-clock time for model convergence, and supporting secure, large-scale federated analyses across collaborating medical centers. Successful implementation will provide a template for computationally rigorous clinical informatics research while contributing open-source tools to the broader biomedical community.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Informatics

abstract: The increasing complexity of global financial systems and evolving regulatory frameworks has created a critical need for advanced computational tools to analyze the interplay between legal structures, corporate behavior, and systemic risk. This project proposes the development of a novel computational legal analytics platform to model the cascading effects of securities law modifications across multinational financial networks. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to simulate how changes in key regulatory parameters—such as disclosure requirements, derivatives trading restrictions, and cross-border merger protocols—propagate through interconnected corporate entities and financial markets. The research employs a hybrid methodology combining natural language processing (NLP) of international legal texts, agent-based modeling of institutional actors, and network analysis of financial interdependencies. A custom-built legal ontology will map jurisdictional variations in corporate law while machine learning algorithms identify historical patterns in regulatory enforcement actions. The computational framework will integrate these components to perform multi-scale simulations, assessing scenarios ranging from single-entity compliance failures to systemic shocks precipitated by conflicting international regulations. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for regulatory arbitrage hotspots, visualization tools for legal exposure mapping, and quantitative assessments of proposed financial policy interventions. This work addresses a significant gap in legal informatics by creating the first computational model capable of analyzing second- and third-order effects within tightly coupled legal-financial systems. Successful implementation will provide policymakers and financial institutions with evidence-based tools to anticipate unintended consequences of regulatory changes, strengthen corporate governance frameworks, and mitigate transnational compliance risks. The scale of textual analysis (covering 50+ jurisdictions’ legal corpora) and complexity of network simulations (modeling >10^6 dynamic entities) necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory nodes, and high-throughput data workflows.
cip_title: Banking, Corporate, Finance, and Securities Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law and process related to the regulation of businesses and the financial services industry. Includes instruction in corporate law, antitrust law, securities law and regulation, negotiation, incorporation, partnerships, trusts, and related topics

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision-support tool to optimize clinical workflows for medical assistants (MAs) during patient intake and preliminary diagnostics. Current protocols for symptom triage and prioritization rely on static guidelines, which lack adaptability to dynamic clinic conditions or individualized patient factors, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation and delays in acute care identification. To address this, we propose a machine learning framework that integrates real-time patient data—including vital signs, historical medical records, and free-text symptom descriptions—with contextual clinic metrics (e.g., staffing levels, equipment availability) to generate adaptive triage recommendations. The computational approach involves training transformer-based models on multimodal datasets spanning de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from diverse outpatient settings and simulating clinic flow scenarios via agent-based modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing terabytes of structured and unstructured EHR data, fine-tuning large language models for symptom parsing, and running parallelized simulations to evaluate system performance under variable clinic conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool that reduces triage decision time by ≥30% in pilot testing while maintaining diagnostic accuracy comparable to physician benchmarks. By enhancing MA decision-making capacity, this tool aims to mitigate bottlenecks in high-volume clinical environments, improve patient outcomes through timely intervention, and establish a framework for human-AI collaboration in frontline healthcare roles. The project bridges clinical operations research, natural language processing, and predictive analytics, advancing an understudied area in health sciences where computational innovation can directly empower non-physician clinical staff.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical office administrative services and perform clinical duties including patient intake and care, routine diagnostic and recording procedures, pre-examination and examination assistance, and the administration of medications and first aid. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology; medical terminology; medical law and ethics; patient psychology and communications; medical office procedures; and clinical diagnostic, examination, testing, and treatment procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing multimodal transportation networks under dynamic demand and climate resilience constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome computational bottlenecks in large-scale infrastructure modeling. Urbanization and climate change necessitate transportation systems that balance efficiency, safety, and sustainability, yet existing simulation tools struggle to integrate real-time traffic data, freight logistics, and extreme weather impacts at metropolitan scales. The research will develop a parallelized computational framework combining dynamic traffic assignment models, agent-based freight movement simulations, and probabilistic flood-risk analysis. By coupling GPU-accelerated traffic microsimulations with graph neural networks trained on multi-source datasets (e.g., connected vehicle telemetry, IoT sensor feeds, and climate projections), the framework will enable scenario testing of adaptive traffic management policies, infrastructure hardening strategies, and emergency evacuation routing. The HPC environment is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of modeling 10^6+ agent interactions across 24-hour periods while maintaining sub-minute temporal resolution. Anticipated outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for evaluating tradeoffs between congestion pricing schemes, electric vehicle charging infrastructure placement, and flood-resistant highway designs. This work will provide state DOTs and metropolitan planning organizations with quantitative metrics to prioritize investments that reduce travel delay by 15-25%, lower transportation-related emissions, and enhance network robustness against 100-year flood events. The computational workflows will be open-sourced to enable replication in diverse geographic contexts, advancing scalable methods for next-generation transportation systems analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems for the physical movement of people, materials and information, including general network design and planning, facilities planning, site evaluation, transportation management systems, needs projections and analysis, and analysis of costs.

abstract: Orthotic and prosthetic devices are critical for restoring mobility and function in patients with musculoskeletal impairments, yet persistent challenges in personalized device design contribute to secondary complications such as tissue injury and device abandonment. Current biomechanical models used to optimize these devices often rely on simplified assumptions about tissue behavior and interface dynamics, limiting their ability to predict real-world performance. This project proposes a computational framework to advance the design of patient-specific orthoses by integrating high-resolution biomechanical simulations with clinical data. The primary research problem centers on modeling the complex interactions between orthotic materials, soft tissue deformation, and physiological loading during dynamic activities. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop finite element models that incorporate heterogeneous tissue properties derived from medical imaging, real-time gait analysis data, and viscoelastic material responses under cyclical loading. Machine learning techniques will be applied to parameterize device configurations that minimize peak interfacial shear stress while maintaining therapeutic biomechanical alignment. The computational workflow will iteratively validate predictions against experimental pressure-mapping and motion capture datasets from a cohort of patients with lower-limb pathologies. By enabling submillimeter-scale resolution of tissue-device interactions and stochastic optimization of design variables, this approach aims to reduce iterative clinical adjustments and mitigate skin breakdown risks. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for orthotists to prototype device designs virtually, coupled with mechanistic insights into tissue tolerance thresholds during prolonged device use. This interdisciplinary work bridges clinical orthotics, computational biomechanics, and materials engineering, offering a paradigm shift toward data-driven personalization in assistive technology. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational intensity of multiscale modeling and large-parameter-space optimizations, which exceed the capacity of local clinical workstations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of 19th-century transnational missionary networks through computational analysis of multilingual archival materials, including correspondence, ethnographic reports, and institutional records. Despite the centrality of missionary activities to global cultural exchange, existing scholarship often relies on fragmented, region-specific studies due to the sheer volume and linguistic diversity of primary sources. Our research addresses this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze over 500,000 digitized pages from missionary societies in North America, Europe, and Asia. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical texts in English, French, German, and Mandarin, we will identify patterns in rhetorical strategies, cross-cultural negotiation tactics, and the dissemination of ideological frameworks. Spatial network models will map the flow of personnel, resources, and information across continents, while transformer-based models will assess how local vernaculars influenced doctrinal adaptations. The computational workflow integrates optical character recognition (OCR) correction for low-quality scans, multilingual entity recognition, and sentiment analysis tailored to religious discourse.
