Expected outcomes include 1) a geotemporal database of missionary interactions with Indigenous communities, 2) quantitative evidence for evaluating claims about "civilizing mission" narratives in postcolonial theory, and 3) open-source tools for analyzing marginalized voices in missionary-produced indigenous language texts. This work requires HPC resources to manage memory-intensive NLP tasks across languages and GPU-accelerated training of custom classification models. By bridging digital humanities, historical sociology, and colonial studies, the project aims to establish computational methods as critical tools in missiology while recovering previously inaccessible dimensions of intercultural encounter.
cip_title: Missions/ Missionary Studies and Missiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in missions, missionary studies, and missiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Aircraft structural integrity and maintenance efficiency are critical to aviation safety and operational cost reduction. Current methods for assessing airframe fatigue, stress distribution, and material degradation rely heavily on physical inspections and standardized replacement intervals, which may not account for localized operational conditions or advanced composite material behaviors. This project proposes a computational approach to model multi-physics interactions in airframe structures under operational loads, enabling predictive maintenance strategies tailored to real-world wear patterns. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models to simulate stress-strain dynamics in wing assemblies, fuselage joints, and landing gear components across diverse environmental conditions. These models will integrate empirical data from material fatigue tests, aerodynamic load profiles, and corrosion rate datasets to predict failure probabilities at microstructural levels. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to optimize inspection schedules by correlating simulation outputs with historical maintenance records. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale meshing for complex geometries, iterative solvers for non-linear material responses, and high-throughput parameter sweeps to account for operational variability. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for identifying high-risk fatigue zones in aging aircraft, (2) validated digital twins for evaluating retrofit modifications, and (3) machine learning-driven maintenance protocols that reduce unplanned downtime by 15-20%. By transitioning from reactive to simulation-informed maintenance practices, this research aims to extend component lifespans while maintaining FAA compliance. The HPC resources will additionally support educational modules for training technicians in computational diagnostics, bridging traditional hands-on practices with Industry 4.0 methodologies in airframe maintenance programs.
cip_title: Airframe Mechanics and Aircraft Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all aircraft components other than engines, propellers, avionics, and instruments. Includes instruction in layout and fabrication of sheet metal, fabric, wood, and other materials into structural members, parts, and fittings, and replacement of damaged or worn parts such as control cables and hydraulic units.

abstract: Pediatric critical care faces significant challenges in managing life-threatening organ failure due to the dynamic, heterogeneous nature of physiological responses in critically ill children. Current clinical decision-making often relies on static thresholds and population-level data, which may not account for the complex, time-dependent interactions between organ systems or individual patient trajectories. This project aims to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to model multi-organ dysfunction and predict patient-specific outcomes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose to integrate multimodal clinical data—including high-resolution physiological waveforms, electronic health records, and biomarker profiles—from a retrospective cohort of 2,500 pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) patients with sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and traumatic brain injury. Mechanistic models of cardiopulmonary, neurological, and immune system interactions will be coupled with machine learning algorithms to simulate disease progression under varying therapeutic strategies. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabytes of waveform data, training ensemble prediction models, and running parallelized in silico trials to optimize ventilation protocols, fluid resuscitation, and immunomodulatory interventions. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel digital biomarkers for early deterioration, personalized risk stratification tools, and adaptive treatment guidelines informed by real-time physiological simulations. This work will provide foundational insights into the systems-level pathophysiology of pediatric critical illness while advancing computational methods for precision care in resource-limited PICU environments. Successful implementation could reduce mortality from organ failure by enabling data-driven escalation decisions and computationally optimized life support strategies tailored to individual patients’ evolving physiological states.
cip_definition: Research focused on advanced life support for children, from the term or near-term neonate to the adolescent. This includes critical care management of life-threatening organ system failure in both medical and surgical patients and support of vital physiological functions.

abstract: The integration of multimodal patient data to optimize psychotropic medication selection and dosing remains a critical challenge in psychiatric care, particularly for frontline mental health technicians managing complex cases. Current approaches rely heavily on trial-and-error protocols, contributing to prolonged treatment timelines, adverse side effects, and suboptimal outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to analyze high-dimensional clinical datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacogenomic profiles, and real-time behavioral monitoring data—to predict individualized treatment responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop machine learning models capable of identifying patterns across heterogeneous data types while accounting for ethical and regulatory constraints inherent to mental health data. The computational pipeline will incorporate federated learning techniques to preserve patient confidentiality across institutions and dynamic simulation modules to model neuropharmacological interactions. Key deliverables include an open-source predictive tool for medication efficacy estimation and a risk stratification system for adverse event prediction, both designed for integration into technician workflow platforms. Anticipated outcomes include reduced medication trial periods by 30-50% in simulated cohorts and improved detection of high-risk pharmacological interactions. This work bridges computational psychiatry and clinical operations, offering a novel decision-support mechanism for non-prescribing mental health professionals. By aligning predictive analytics with the procedural scope of psychiatric technicians, the project aims to enhance precision in treatment plan execution while maintaining human-centric care standards. Successful implementation could establish a template for embedding computational guidance into frontline mental health roles, potentially reducing systemic burdens in overextended care environments.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of psychiatrists, psychologists, nurses, and other mental health care professionals, to provide direct patient care services, assist in developing and implementing treatment plans, administer medications, and perform related administrative functions. Includes instruction in mental health theory, applied psychopathology, patient communication and management, crisis intervention, psychotropic medication, mental health treatment procedures, substance abuse, record-keeping, clinical administrative skills, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of social networks and spatial interactions within urban communities served by faith-based organizations. Urban ministry practitioners face challenges in addressing systemic inequities, fragmented community relationships, and rapidly shifting demographic patterns, yet lack robust computational tools to model the interplay of cultural, economic, and spiritual factors in these environments. Our research will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating decision-making processes among urban residents, clergy, and community partners under varying conditions of resource scarcity, social trust, and crisis events. These models will integrate qualitative data from ethnographic interviews, historical congregational records, and geospatial datasets on urban infrastructure to create multi-scale representations of community resilience. Using HPC clusters, we will run iterative simulations to test how different ministry strategies—such as collaborative resource distribution networks or trauma-informed outreach protocols—affect neighborhood-level outcomes like social cohesion and economic mobility. Parallelized NLP pipelines will further process unstructured textual data from sermon archives and community meetings to identify patterns in moral reasoning and ethical prioritization across diverse urban contexts. The computational outputs aim to provide actionable frameworks for optimizing pastoral leadership training programs, particularly in balancing individualized care with systemic advocacy. By bridging computational social science and theological ethics, this project will establish a novel methodology for evidence-based urban ministry, offering scalable models to support adaptive community engagement in an era of rapid urbanization and socio-technical change.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to individuals and groups in urban communities. Includes instruction in bible study and theology, pastoral leadership and care, urban structure and context, inner city ministry, counseling ministries, family studies, homiletics, social ethics, and community organizing.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing ergonomic workflows for health aides providing routine patient mobility assistance—a task associated with high rates of musculoskeletal injuries. Current guidelines for manual patient handling lack personalization to individual aide-patient dyads, leading to suboptimal safety outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to develop a biomechanical simulation framework that models complex physical interactions during transfers (e.g., bed-to-chair) across diverse body types, mobility limitations, and environmental constraints. Wearable sensor data from health aides (inertial measurement units, surface electromyography) will be integrated with patient-specific anatomical models derived from de-identified clinical imaging datasets. Finite element analysis and reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively simulate force distributions and movement trajectories to identify configurations that minimize spinal load and muscle fatigue while maintaining patient comfort. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing of multi-modal datasets (motion capture, 3D musculoskeletal models, and real-time biomechanical feedback) to generate adaptive, personalized handling strategies. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool that recommends context-specific techniques to reduce injury risk and a generative AI module to train health aides via virtual reality simulations. By bridging biomechanics, occupational health, and machine learning, this work aims to establish a scalable computational foundation for redefining safety standards in direct patient care—a niche yet urgent priority as aging populations increase demands on frontline health workers. The resource-intensive nature of modeling high-dimensional human movement data necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve clinically actionable resolution and speed.
cip_definition: Any other instructional program that prepares individuals to provide routine patient care and assistance.

abstract: Educational leaders face growing complexity in optimizing institutional performance amid constraints such as fluctuating budgets, evolving policy landscapes, and diverse student needs. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model dynamic interactions between administrative variables or simulate long-term impacts of resource allocation strategies. This project proposes the development of computational models to analyze large-scale educational datasets and simulate administrative scenarios, enabling data-driven leadership practices. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-year institutional records, including enrollment patterns, staffing configurations, budget allocations, and student outcome metrics from K-12 and higher education systems. Agent-based modeling techniques will be employed to simulate decision cascades across organizational hierarchies, while machine learning algorithms will identify predictive relationships between resource distribution strategies and equity outcomes. Key computational challenges include managing heterogeneous data structures across districts, scaling simulations to represent systems with >10,000 organizational agents, and optimizing parameter spaces for policy interventions. Expected outcomes include: (1) validated models quantifying how specific allocation strategies affect equity in student access to advanced coursework, (2) sensitivity analyses of budget reallocation impacts on staff retention in under-resourced schools, and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating the second-order consequences of administrative decisions. By enabling leaders to stress-test policies in computational environments before implementation, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error approaches in real-world systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations across multiple governance models and accelerating iterative model training processes. Results will contribute methodological advances in computational decision support systems for educational administration while providing practical frameworks for improving the cost-effectiveness and equity of resource distribution strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and techniques of administering a wide variety of schools and other educational organizations and facilities, supervising educational personnel at the school or staff level, and that may prepare individuals as general administrators and supervisors.

abstract: The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources into modern power grids has introduced unprecedented challenges in maintaining dynamic stability, particularly during transient events such as fault-induced delayed voltage recovery (FIDVR) or rapid frequency deviations. Traditional grid models, which rely on static assumptions and decoupled analyses of electromechanical and electromagnetic phenomena, are insufficient to capture the complex, multi-timescale interactions between inverter-based resources, legacy synchronous generators, and emerging grid-forming technologies. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL)-validated computational framework to simulate power system dynamics at unprecedented resolution, integrating device-level semiconductor switching behaviors with grid-scale transient stability models. The research will employ parallelized differential-algebraic equation solvers optimized for heterogeneous computing architectures to concurrently resolve nanosecond-scale power electronics transitions and second-scale machine dynamics. Machine learning techniques will be applied to surrogate modeling of component-level behaviors, enabling real-time predictive stability assessment without sacrificing physical interpretability. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing resources for three primary tasks: (1) massively parallel time-domain simulations of 10,000+ bus systems with mixed AC/DC topologies, (2) training physics-informed neural networks on petascale datasets generated by parametric sweeps of renewable penetration scenarios, and (3) deployment of digital twins for contingency analysis through cloud-HPC hybrid architectures. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible library of validated component models, adaptive protection coordination algorithms for hybrid grids, and stability margin quantification metrics that account for multi-energy coupling effects. This work aims to provide grid operators with computationally tractable tools for maintaining reliability in systems with >80% renewable generation, directly supporting decarbonization targets while addressing a critical gap in current power plant engineering capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan electrical systems and modify existing electrical systems that generate and use large amounts of electricity required for distribution networks that are economical, safe, and functional. Includes instruction in alternative/renewable energy systems; calculus; circuit analysis; electrical power systems and industry practices; electrical system design; microprocessor architecture; motor control systems; power electronics operation, planning and protection; programmable logic controllers; and project management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of preparing geography educators to teach complex geospatial concepts through data-driven, computationally intensive approaches. While geography education increasingly relies on tools like geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and spatial analytics, many teacher training programs lack scalable methods to model how novice learners engage with multidimensional spatial data. This gap limits the ability to design evidence-based pedagogical strategies that bridge theoretical knowledge and practical skill development. To resolve this, we propose a research initiative leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and analyze student interactions with geospatial learning environments at unprecedented scales. Using anonymized datasets from geography classrooms—including eye-tracking patterns, task completion times, and error rates in spatial reasoning exercises—we will train machine learning models to identify cognitive bottlenecks in understanding topics like map projections, spatial autocorrelation, and landscape evolution. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution geospatial datasets (e.g., LiDAR, satellite imagery) used in training exercises, as well as agent-based modeling of virtual classroom scenarios to test instructional interventions. The computational workflow integrates geostatistical analysis, neural network-based pattern recognition, and Monte Carlo simulations to account for variability in learner backgrounds. Outcomes will include a framework for optimizing geography lesson plans based on predictive analytics, interactive visualizations of common conceptual hurdles, and open-access computational modules for teacher training programs. By revealing relationships between instructional design choices and spatial skill acquisition, this work aims to transform how geography educators are trained to scaffold complex concepts, ultimately improving secondary students’ readiness to address real-world challenges in climate science, urban planning, and sustainable development. The requested computing resources are essential given the terabyte-scale geospatial data inputs, need for real-time rendering of 3D landscape models in simulations, and iterative model training requirements across diverse pedagogical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach geography at various grade levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing additive manufacturing (AM) processes through high-fidelity simulations of multi-physics interactions during material deposition. Current AM techniques, particularly in polymer and composite systems, suffer from defects such as warping, delamination, and inconsistent layer adhesion due to poorly understood thermal gradients and stress dynamics. Existing experimental approaches are costly and time-intensive, while simplified computational models lack the resolution to capture critical localized phenomena. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a parallelized finite element model that couples transient thermal analysis, viscoelastic stress evolution, and material phase transitions at micrometer-scale resolutions. The model will integrate experimental calibration data from in-situ thermal imaging and mechanical testing to refine boundary conditions. Key computational challenges include managing the high spatial-temporal resolution required for defect prediction (exceeding 10^8 degrees of freedom) and implementing adaptive meshing strategies to track moving heat sources. The simulations will be validated against synchrotron X-ray tomography data of defect formation in printed specimens. Successful implementation will enable predictive optimization of process parameters (e.g., laser power, scan speed, cooling rates) for novel material formulations, reducing trial-and-error prototyping by an estimated 60%. Outcomes will be disseminated as open-source workflow templates to support broader adoption of simulation-driven AM process design. This work directly aligns with national priorities in advanced manufacturing while avoiding overlap with excluded engineering disciplines through its exclusive focus on process simulation rather than material development or end-use structural analysis. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated computations and large-scale parameter sweeps essential for establishing statistically robust process-property relationships.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to optimize the design of next-generation neural interface devices, which face critical challenges in achieving stable long-term performance due to dynamic biological responses and mechanical mismatch with neural tissue. Current neural interfaces, such as brain-machine interfaces or peripheral nerve stimulators, are limited by signal degradation from glial scarring, inflammatory protein adsorption, and mechanical stress at the tissue-device boundary. To address this, we propose a hybrid modeling approach integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of protein-device surface interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) of strain distribution in peri-electrode neural tissue, and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization of device geometry and material properties. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve time- and length-scale disparities: atomistic MD simulations (nanoscale, femtosecond resolution) will parameterize mesoscale FEA models (micrometer to millimeter scales), while ML algorithms will iteratively refine device designs using terabytes of combined simulation data. The HPC environment will enable parallel execution of 500+ MD simulations across varying surface coatings (conductive polymers, bioactive hydrogels) and FEA models under cyclical mechanical loading mimicking in vivo conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps linking device material properties to inflammatory biomarker expression and signal fidelity over simulated 6-month periods, and (2) optimized neural electrode architectures demonstrating <15% chronic signal attenuation in validation models, compared to >50% in current designs. This computational pipeline will provide the first integrated platform for evaluating both biological integration and electromechanical performance in neural interfaces, accelerating the development of devices that maintain functionality over clinically relevant timescales. The framework will be extensible to other bioelectronic implants, including cardiac and retinal prostheses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of biomedical and health systems and products such as integrated biomedical systems, instrumentation, medical information systems, artificial organs and prostheses, and health management and care delivery systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of immersive theatrical environments through large-scale simulation and real-time rendering. The research problem centers on the challenge of modeling dynamic, multi-sensory performance spaces that integrate complex variables such as acoustics, lighting, audience movement, and interactive set elements. Traditional stagecraft tools lack the computational capacity to simulate these interdependent systems at scale, limiting the design and testing of innovative productions. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate audience-performer interactions, finite element analysis for acoustic propagation in non-static set designs, and GPU-accelerated ray tracing to optimize dynamic lighting configurations. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to historical performance datasets to identify patterns in audience engagement, informing adaptive staging strategies. The computational workflows will be validated against empirical data from live theatrical experiments, with iterative refinements to improve accuracy. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for prototyping immersive environments, reducing reliance on physical mock-ups, and enabling the exploration of previously impractical staging concepts. This work holds significance for the performing arts by expanding the creative possibilities of theatrical design while addressing logistical and safety constraints inherent to live productions. The resulting tools will be disseminated as open-source resources to support collaborative innovation across academic and professional theatre communities. By integrating computational rigor with artistic practice, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven stagecraft, fostering interdisciplinary advancements at the intersection of performing arts and HPC.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Dramatic/ Theatre Arts and Stagecraft, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dramatic/theatre arts and stagecraft, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the multiscale fluid-structure interactions governing pollen dispersal in heterogeneous environments, integrating principles from botany, aerodynamics, and environmental physics. Pollen grains, with their diverse morphologies and adaptive biomechanical properties, exhibit complex dispersal behaviors that influence ecosystem resilience, agricultural productivity, and airborne allergen distribution. However, predictive models remain limited by oversimplified representations of turbulence-pollen interactions across scales and an incomplete understanding of how microenvironmental variability (e.g., localized wind shear, humidity gradients) modulates dispersal efficiency. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC) framework coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with discrete element modeling (DEM) to resolve pollen trajectories at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. The simulations will parameterize pollen geometries derived from micro-CT scans of 50 species, incorporating hygroscopic deformation dynamics and stochastic wind fields calibrated to LiDAR-measured canopy architectures. Multi-GPU parallelization will enable ensemble runs across parameter spaces encompassing realistic atmospheric boundary layers and climate perturbation scenarios. Validation will leverage field data from particle image velocimetry and pollen-trap networks across forest-grassland ecotones. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into morphology-mediated dispersal optimization, probabilistic maps of cross-pollination ranges under shifting precipitation regimes, and open-source tools for eco-evolutionary forecasting. By bridging microscale biophysics to landscape-scale ecological processes, this work will advance fundamental knowledge of plant adaptation while providing actionable data for biodiversity conservation and precision agriculture. The computational demands—iterative 3D Navier-Stokes solutions across billion-cell domains coupled to 10^6-particle DEM systems—necessitate allocation of 250,000 node-hours on a tier-1 HPC system, enabling transformative leaps in scale integration for environmental fluid dynamics.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on one or more of the physical and biological sciences.

abstract: Oral health disparities persist across populations due to uneven access to preventive and curative dental services, compounded by complex socioeconomic, geographic, and behavioral factors. Current public health strategies often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between these variables, limiting the precision of interventions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate population-level oral health outcomes under varying service delivery scenarios, enabling data-driven policy recommendations. The research will integrate anonymized electronic health records, demographic surveys, and environmental data from public health databases to model disease progression, resource allocation efficiency, and intervention impacts at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations that represent millions of individuals with heterogeneous risk profiles, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict emergent patterns of dental caries, periodontal disease, and service utilization. Computational workflows will optimize parallel processing for parameter sensitivity analyses and scenario testing, such as evaluating the cost-effectiveness of community fluoride programs or mobile clinic deployments in underserved regions. Geospatial analytics will further map service gaps and forecast demand under demographic shifts. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into optimal intervention timing, resource distribution, and policy adjustments to reduce inequities. By quantifying trade-offs between preventive and reactive care strategies, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in dental public health. The scalability of the models will also provide a adaptable toolkit for addressing oral health challenges in diverse global contexts, with implications for reducing systemic healthcare costs and improving population-level oral health outcomes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the formulation and delivery of public preventive and curative dental health services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive maintenance framework for building systems using high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize the reliability and energy efficiency of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and structural components in commercial, industrial, and mobile home structures. Current maintenance practices often rely on reactive or scheduled interventions, which can lead to unexpected failures, energy waste, and high operational costs. To address this, the research will integrate sensor-derived operational data with physics-based simulations of building systems, creating dynamic models to predict degradation patterns and system-wide interdependencies. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model HVAC airflow and thermal distribution, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess stress and wear in plumbing and structural components. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical maintenance records and real-time sensor data to identify failure precursors and recommend preemptive actions. The scale and complexity of these multi-physics simulations, coupled with the need for real-time analytics across distributed sensor networks, necessitate HPC resources to manage large datasets and parallelize computations. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive maintenance toolkit that quantifies risk thresholds, prioritizes interventions, and simulates energy-saving scenarios. This framework aims to reduce unplanned downtime by 30–50% in pilot buildings and lower annual energy consumption by 15–20%, directly supporting sustainability goals in facility management. By leveraging HPC to bridge empirical data and systems modeling, this work will advance data-driven decision-making in building maintenance curricula and provide scalable computational strategies for retrofitting aging infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to keep a building functioning, and to service a variety of structures including commercial and industrial buildings and mobile homes. Includes instruction in the basic maintenance and repair skills required to service building systems, such as air conditioning, heating, plumbing, electrical, major appliances, and other mechanical systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in real-time computational modeling of American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current machine translation systems for signed languages struggle to process the multimodal, continuous, and context-dependent nature of ASL, particularly its non-manual markers (e.g., facial expressions, body movements) and spatial grammar. These limitations hinder the development of assistive technologies for the Deaf community and tools to support human interpreters. The research problem centers on optimizing neural architectures to model ASL’s visual-kinetic structure at scale while maintaining real-time inference speeds. The computational approach integrates 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatiotemporal feature extraction from video data with transformer-based models to capture syntactic and discourse-level dependencies. Training will utilize a novel multimodal dataset of annotated ASL dialogues, including motion-capture data and gloss transcriptions, to align linguistic features with visual signals. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution video inputs, parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across model variants, and deploying large-scale transformer fine-tuning. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for ASL machine interpretation with sub-second latency and improved accuracy relative to existing methods, measured by human interpreter validation. The project also aims to release open-source tools for preprocessing ASL video data and a curated dataset to advance research in low-resource signed languages. By addressing computational bottlenecks in processing ASL’s unique morphology and syntax, this work will directly support the development of next-generation interpretation technologies, reducing communication barriers and enhancing educational and professional accessibility for Deaf individuals. The interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational linguistics and sign language studies, offering new pathways for research in under-resourced language technologies within the Humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as simultaneous interpreters of American Sign Language

abstract: Orthopedic disorders, including degenerative joint diseases and complex fractures, present significant challenges due to the interplay of biomechanical, biological, and patient-specific factors. Traditional experimental approaches often fail to capture the multiscale complexity of bone remodeling, implant-tissue interactions, and individualized treatment outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multiscale computational models that integrate mechanical loading, cellular activity, and molecular signaling in orthopedic healing and implant performance. The primary research problem revolves around predicting patient-specific responses to surgical interventions, such as joint replacements or fracture fixation, while optimizing implant designs for diverse biomechanical environments. Using finite element analysis (FEA), agent-based modeling, and machine learning, we will simulate bone adaptation under dynamic loads, evaluate stress shielding in prosthetic devices, and model the spatiotemporal regulation of osteogenesis in fracture repair. These simulations will incorporate heterogeneous clinical datasets, including medical imaging, genomic profiles, and biomechanical measurements, to generate patient-specific predictions. The computational workflows demand HPC resources due to the high-resolution meshing required for bone-implant interfaces, the stochastic nature of cell-level interactions, and the iterative optimization of machine learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for implant longevity, identification of biomechanical risk factors for post-surgical complications, and data-driven guidelines for personalized rehabilitation protocols. By elucidating the mechanobiological mechanisms underlying bone healing and device failure, this research aims to advance evidence-based orthopedic care, reduce revision surgery rates, and improve functional recovery timelines. The proposed HPC-enabled approach will provide a transformative platform for integrating multiscale clinical data into precision orthopedics, addressing a critical gap in current translational research methodologies.
cip_definition: Research focused on Orthopedic

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the development and interaction of theological concepts across major Christian traditions, including Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism, and Protestantism. While historical and doctrinal scholarship has long studied these traditions, the scale and complexity of textual sources—spanning scripture, patristic writings, medieval scholasticism, and modern theological works—pose challenges for manual analysis. This research aims to computationally map shifts in theological reasoning, trace doctrinal influences, and identify patterns in the adaptation of Christian thought to diverse cultural contexts. The primary research problem centers on how computational methods can enhance understanding of continuity and divergence in core theological themes, such as salvation, ecclesiology, and Christology, across time and denominational boundaries. The proposed approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic similarity analysis and topic modeling, with network analysis to visualize conceptual relationships within and between traditions. A curated corpus of digitized primary texts, commentaries, and synodal documents will be processed to extract theological arguments, metaphor usage, and doctrinal formulations. HPC resources are critical for training custom language models on ancient Greek, Latin, and early modern vernacular texts, as well as for running large-scale comparative analyses across multilingual sources. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated theological texts, visualizations of doctrinal development trajectories, and quantitative frameworks for assessing interdenominational theological dialogue. This work will provide scholars with new tools to analyze Christianity’s intellectual history systematically, offering insights into how theological ideas have been shaped by—and have shaped—cultural and philosophical movements. The project aligns with the Christian Studies program’s emphasis on rigorous engagement with primary sources while demonstrating the transformative potential of computational humanities in religious studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy and teachings of Jesus Christ and his apostles, and the subsequent intellectual and cultural movements and institutions based on Christianity. Includes instruction in Christian sacred scripture, Christian literature and philosophy, and studies of one or more of the main branches of the faith and their cultural context including Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism, Protestantism, Evangelicalism, and others.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient, safe, and environmentally sustainable maritime operations necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize vessel performance and navigation strategies. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to analyze hydrodynamic interactions, fuel efficiency, and route optimization for commercial vessels operating in dynamic ocean environments. A critical challenge lies in integrating real-time environmental data—such as wave spectra, currents, and weather patterns—with vessel-specific parameters, including hull design, propulsion systems, and cargo loads, to model complex maritime scenarios. Traditional methods often rely on static models or simplified assumptions, limiting their predictive accuracy under variable conditions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale, multi-physics simulations using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning (ML) algorithms. The CFD component will resolve turbulent flow around vessel hulls and propellers at high spatial resolution, while ML models trained on historical voyage data will predict optimal speed profiles and routing adjustments to minimize fuel consumption and emissions. The simulations will incorporate stochastic environmental inputs to assess operational risks and resilience in diverse scenarios. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC clusters, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks associated with iterative parameter testing and ensemble forecasting. Expected outcomes include validated models for decision support systems that enable real-time operational adjustments, reducing fuel costs by an estimated 10–15% and greenhouse gas emissions by 8–12% per voyage. This work will directly inform maritime training curricula and industry best practices, bridging gaps between theoretical naval architecture and practical fleet management. The computational infrastructure will also support future research in autonomous vessel navigation and adaptive marine energy systems, aligning with global efforts to decarbonize maritime transport.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as captains, executive officers, engineers and ranking mates on commercially licensed inland, coastal and ocean-going vessels. Includes instruction in maritime traditions and law, maritime policy, economics and management of commercial marine operations, basic naval architecture and engineering, shipboard power systems engineering, crew supervision, and administrative procedures.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with complex mechanisms underlying conditions such as heart failure, arrhythmias, and ischemic heart disease. A critical barrier to advancing personalized cardiology is the integration of multi-modal clinical data—including imaging, electrophysiology, and genomics—into predictive models that account for patient-specific variability. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational frameworks capable of simulating cardiac pathophysiology at unprecedented resolution. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) creating multi-scale models of cardiac electromechanics that incorporate patient-derived data from MRI, CT, and intracardiac mapping to simulate arrhythmia propagation and hemodynamic outcomes, and (2) employing machine learning to identify genomic and proteomic biomarkers associated with adverse cardiac remodeling, using whole-genome sequencing and proteomic datasets from longitudinal cohort studies. The computational workflows will utilize finite element modeling, computational fluid dynamics, and deep learning algorithms, necessitating parallelized processing and large-scale memory allocation. By simulating interventions such as catheter ablation or pharmacological therapies in silico, the models aim to predict optimal treatment strategies for individual patients. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for sudden cardiac death risk stratification, the development of open-source simulation tools for clinical researchers, and validation of patient-specific treatment planning protocols through retrospective clinical data analysis. This work addresses a pressing need for computationally intensive approaches in cardiology, where traditional methods fail to capture the interplay between molecular, cellular, and organ-level dynamics. Successful implementation will advance precision cardiology by bridging gaps between computational research and clinical translation, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcomes for patients with complex cardiovascular conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on Cardiology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in personalized intervention strategies for students with disabilities, addressing the critical challenge of optimizing educational outcomes in heterogeneous learning environments. Special education requires tailored approaches due to the wide variability in students’ needs, but current methods for designing individualized education programs (IEPs) often rely on static, manually analyzed datasets, limiting scalability and real-time adaptability. To bridge this gap, we propose developing computational models that integrate multimodal educational data—including longitudinal academic performance, behavioral logs, speech-language pathology records, and demographic factors—to predict intervention efficacy and recommend dynamic adjustments. The research will employ machine learning techniques, such as ensemble models and transformer-based architectures, to analyze high-dimensional datasets spanning multiple school districts. These models will account for nested data structures (e.g., students within classrooms, classrooms within schools) using multilevel statistical frameworks, requiring distributed computing for parameter estimation. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom interactions under varying resource constraints and disability profiles to identify optimal support configurations. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of data (anticipated 10TB+ from partner districts), the complexity of training multimodal neural networks, and the parallel processing demands of Monte Carlo simulations for sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to guide IEP development using real-time data, (2) evidence-based frameworks for allocating assistive technologies and personnel, and (3) open-source software enabling educators to simulate intervention impacts. By quantifying how specific computational strategies correlate with student progress, this work aims to transform special education practices from reactive to proactive while maintaining compliance with legal and ethical standards for student data. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable the iterative refinement of models that would otherwise be computationally intractable, directly supporting the program’s mission to innovate inclusive teaching methodologies through data-driven decision-making.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children or adults with special learning needs or disabilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as special education teachers in a collaborative or team environment. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Buddhist philosophical texts and their historical-comparative interpretations. The research problem centers on the vast and linguistically diverse corpus of Buddhist scriptures, commentaries, and ritual manuals, which present significant challenges for systematic doctrinal analysis. Traditional hermeneutic methods struggle to map cross-traditional doctrinal developments, semantic shifts in key concepts (e.g., *anātman*, *śūnyatā*), and the diffusion of ritual practices across regions and time periods. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), multilingual semantic modeling, and network analysis to trace philosophical continuities and divergences among Theravāda, Mahāyāna, and Vajrayāna textual traditions. Using OCR-processed digitized manuscripts from Pali, Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and Tibetan sources, we will train transformer-based models to identify doctrinal patterns, contextualize metaphorical language, and reconstruct conceptual genealogies. A key innovation involves adapting phylogenetic algorithms—typically used in evolutionary biology—to model the "migration" of doctrinal elements across traditions, accounting for translation artifacts and commentarial reinterpretations. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of approximately 15TB of multilingual textual data, including rare manuscripts from the Tibetan Buddhist canon. Expected outcomes include (1) a graph database mapping relationships between core philosophical concepts and their sectarian adaptations, (2) quantitative models of doctrinal synthesis in East Asian Buddhist schools, and (3) open-access tools for automated analysis of Buddhist hybrid Sanskrit compounds. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational humanities with Buddhist philology, offering new frameworks to study how philosophical ideas transformed as Buddhism spread across Asia. The computational infrastructure developed will support future collaborative projects in cross-cultural religious studies while preserving rigorous textual scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy preached by Siddartha Gautama, the Buddha, in ancient India and subsequently interpreted by his disciples and apostles; together with the intellectual, cultural, social, and ritual developments of the faith and its branches. Includes instruction in Buddhist sacred literature (Tripitaka, etc.) and study of one or more of the main branches including Early Buddhism, Hinayana, Theravada, Madhyamaka, Yogacara, Pure Land, Shingon, Tendai, Nichiren Shu, Zen, Tibetan, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational text analysis in Talmudic Studies, a field requiring nuanced engagement with complex legal, philosophical, and ethical texts. The Talmud and its vast commentarial tradition present a unique research challenge: their intertextual, non-linear structure—spanning centuries of debate and interpretation—resists traditional linear analysis. Current manual methods for tracing conceptual evolution, identifying patterns in legal reasoning, or mapping cross-references across thousands of folios are labor-intensive and prone to oversight. This project proposes a computational approach to analyze large-scale digitized corpora of Talmudic and post-Talmudic literature (e.g., responsa, codes, and hermeneutic works) to uncover latent connections, model argumentative structures, and quantify shifts in ethical or jurisprudential discourse. Using natural language processing (NLP) tailored to Rabbinic Hebrew and Aramaic, combined with graph-based algorithms to visualize conceptual networks, we aim to systematize how Talmudic reasoning adapts to new contexts over time. HPC resources are critical for training transformer models on low-resource Semitic languages, running semantic similarity analyses across multi-terabyte text repositories, and simulating network growth in legal-ethical systems. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database linking Talmudic concepts to their later interpretations, annotated with computational metadata; (2) quantitative frameworks for evaluating the influence of specific commentators or historical events on Jewish legal philosophy; and (3) open-source tools for interdisciplinary researchers analyzing multilayered textual traditions. By bridging computational humanities and Talmudic scholarship, this work will enhance pedagogical resources, inform contemporary ethical debates grounded in classical texts, and demonstrate how HPC can expand the scale and precision of humanistic inquiry in religious studies.
cip_definition: A program focused on intense study of the Talmud that fosters values, critical thinking, and scholarship skills; prepares students for entry into a broad spectrum of graduate and professional schools; and prepares students for entry into a variety of careers including the Rabbinate. Includes instruction in Jewish law, Jewish jurisprudence, ethics, philosophy, and related disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize well drilling operations in heterogeneous geological formations, with the goal of minimizing equipment wear, reducing environmental risks, and improving drilling efficiency. The research addresses critical challenges in predicting subsurface conditions—such as rock fracturing dynamics, fluid flow interactions, and thermal stresses—that lead to costly drilling inefficiencies or failures. Current analytical models struggle to account for the multi-scale, time-dependent interactions between drilling equipment and complex geological media, particularly in deep or unconventional reservoirs. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining finite element modeling (FEM), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate drill-bit interactions with stratified formations under varying operational parameters. High-resolution 3D models will integrate real-world geophysical data to capture lithological variability, while ML algorithms will train on simulation outputs to predict optimal drilling paths and torque-rpm configurations. The HPC infrastructure is essential for resolving micron-scale tool wear effects alongside kilometer-scale formation heterogeneity within coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to avoid stuck-pipe incidents and blowouts by identifying high-risk zones in advance, (2) quantitative guidelines for adaptive drilling parameter adjustments in real time, and (3) open-source simulation modules for training drillers in scenario-based decision-making. By enabling unprecedented resolution in modeling tool-rock-fluid systems, this work aims to reduce non-productive drilling time by an estimated 15–20% in test cases while mitigating groundwater contamination risks. The computational toolkit will be validated against field data from partner drilling companies, with results disseminated through industry workshops and a publicly accessible benchmark dataset for future research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, maintain, repair, and operate well drilling equipment; locate, drill, construct, and develop water, gas, and oil wells; and test and monitor wells to ensure adequate flow. Includes applications to home, business, and industrial uses.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize land use planning under competing demands of urbanization, conservation, and climate resilience. Rapid population growth and shifting environmental conditions are intensifying pressures on finite land resources, yet existing models often lack the resolution and integration of socio-economic, ecological, and geospatial data required for dynamic decision-making. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-agent simulation system coupled with machine learning-driven scenario analysis. The model will integrate high-resolution satellite imagery, regional climate projections, demographic datasets, and economic indicators to simulate land use outcomes across spatial scales (local to regional) and temporal horizons (5–50 years). Computational workflows will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess uncertainty in policy interventions, while graph-based algorithms will identify connectivity corridors for biodiversity preservation amidst urban expansion. A key innovation is the incorporation of real-time stakeholder preference data through participatory modeling interfaces, enabling adaptive feedback loops between community input and predictive analytics. The HPC environment is critical for managing petabytes of heterogeneous geospatial data, running ensemble simulations to evaluate trade-offs between development goals and ecosystem services, and training deep learning models to predict habitat fragmentation risks. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for policymakers to visualize the long-term impacts of zoning decisions, infrastructure projects, and conservation policies. By quantifying trade-offs between economic growth, carbon sequestration, water resource availability, and social equity, this work aims to advance evidence-based land management strategies that align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The project will directly support regional planning agencies in three pilot areas facing distinct land use challenges, providing a transferable framework for balancing human and ecological needs in resource-constrained environments.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Land Use Planning and Management/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how public and/or private land and associated resources can be preserved, developed, and used for maximum social, economic, and environmental benefit. Includes instruction in natural resources management, natural resource economics, public policy, regional and land use planning, environmental impact assessment, applicable law and regulations, government and politics, principles of business and real estate land use, statistical and analytical tools, computer applications, mapping and report preparation, site analysis, cost analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize the resilience of urban transportation networks under climate-driven hydrological stressors. Increasingly frequent extreme precipitation events exacerbate flooding risks, disrupting critical infrastructure and amplifying economic losses. Current models often lack the spatial granularity and dynamic coupling of hydrological, structural, and traffic flow processes needed to assess cascading failures in complex urban systems. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating 2D hydrodynamic flood modeling, finite element analysis of bridge and pavement integrity, and agent-based transportation network simulations. The framework will leverage GPU-accelerated shallow water equations solvers (using Clawpack and ANSYS Fluent) to model surface water dynamics at 1-meter resolution across a 200 km² testbed region, coupled with machine learning surrogates to predict infrastructure degradation thresholds under hydraulic loading. Concurrently, a parallelized MATSim implementation will simulate traffic rerouting behaviors during flood propagation. The integration of these modules requires high-performance computing resources to manage the computational intensity of transient, multi-physics simulations and large-scale optimization tasks. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to identify high-risk infrastructure chokepoints, evaluate adaptive mitigation strategies (e.g., green stormwater infrastructure placement), and inform climate-resilient urban planning policies. The research directly aligns with national priorities for sustainable infrastructure adaptation, with particular relevance to coastal cities experiencing compound flooding threats. Successful implementation will provide open-source computational workflows to advance coupled human-infrastructure-environment modeling capabilities within civil and environmental engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures. Combines instruction in civil and environmental engineering.

abstract: The increasing complexity of managing acute, life-threatening conditions in veterinary patients—such as sepsis, trauma, or multi-organ failure—demands advanced tools to optimize time-sensitive clinical decisions. Current protocols for emergency and critical care rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for the dynamic interplay of physiological variables, comorbidities, and treatment responses in individual animals. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive modeling framework to analyze real-time and retrospective clinical data from veterinary intensive care units (ICUs). Leveraging electronic health records, continuous vital sign monitoring, and biomarker data from dogs and cats admitted to tertiary care facilities, we will train machine learning models to predict patient-specific risks of decompensation, treatment efficacy, and long-term outcomes. Computational workflows will integrate multi-modal datasets, including time-series hemodynamic parameters, laboratory results, and imaging findings, to simulate disease trajectories under varying intervention scenarios. The models will employ ensemble learning and mechanistic modeling to address data sparsity and physiological heterogeneity inherent in veterinary critical care. By deploying these tools on HPC infrastructure, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional data and enable real-time decision support during emergencies. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for early detection of sepsis-induced organ dysfunction, optimized fluid resuscitation strategies, and personalized prognostic scoring systems. This work will provide a foundation for data-driven critical care protocols, directly improving survival rates and resource allocation in veterinary ICUs while advancing translational insights into human-animal comparative medicine. The requested computing resources are essential for scaling complex simulations, hyperparameter optimization, and validation across diverse patient cohorts.
cip_title: Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Medicine
cip_definition: Research focused on the emergency treatment and management of care for animals with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. May included related research in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures, and long-term care of critically diseased animals.

abstract: The proposed research addresses a critical gap in radiation protection protocols by investigating the complex interplay of low-dose, mixed-radiation fields in occupational and environmental settings. Current risk models, which primarily rely on linear extrapolations from high-dose exposures, inadequately capture the biological effects of prolonged, low-dose exposure to heterogeneous radiation types (e.g., alpha, beta, gamma, neutron). This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multiscale simulation framework integrating radiation transport, cellular response dynamics, and probabilistic risk assessment. Monte Carlo N-Particle (MCNP) simulations will model radiation interactions at the subcellular level across diverse exposure scenarios, while agent-based modeling will simulate DNA damage repair mechanisms and tissue-level responses. Machine learning algorithms will analyze terabyte-scale datasets generated by these simulations to identify nonlinear dose-response patterns and predict long-term health risks. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental radiobiology data from in vitro cell cultures exposed to controlled radiation mixtures. By quantifying the synergistic effects of mixed radiation fields on genomic instability and carcinogenic potential, this research aims to establish evidence-based thresholds for radiation safety in emerging contexts such as nuclear decommissioning sites, space travel, and advanced radiotherapy facilities. The outcomes will directly inform the development of adaptive radiation monitoring systems and personalized dosimetry strategies, bridging the gap between theoretical health physics and practical safety implementations. Access to HPC resources is essential due to the iterative nature of radiation transport simulations, the combinatorial complexity of mixed-field analyses, and the need for real-time uncertainty quantification across billions of particle histories. This interdisciplinary approach advances radiation protection science by providing a computational toolkit to address 21st-century challenges in occupational and environmental health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health physicists, occupational safety and health specialists, and public health officials, to monitor and control radiation exposure and implement preventive measures in health care, work, and natural environments. Includes instruction in radiation physics, environmental radioactivity, radiological instrumentation, electronics of radiation detection equipment, radioactive waste management and control, safety and handling procedures, decontamination procedures, radioactivity testing and analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and validation of computational models for play therapy interventions, a specialized niche within child mental health that integrates developmental psychology, psychotherapy, and data-driven behavioral analysis. Play therapy relies on nuanced, real-time interpretation of children’s play behaviors to assess emotional states and therapeutic progress, but current methods depend heavily on subjective clinician judgments, limiting scalability and consistency. To address this, we propose a multimodal machine learning framework to analyze structured and unstructured play therapy session data—including video, audio, and sensor-based movement metrics—to identify patterns predictive of therapeutic outcomes. The computational pipeline will process high-resolution video recordings (annotated for play themes, emotional expression, and therapist-child interactions) alongside wearable device data capturing physiological markers (e.g., heart rate variability, motion dynamics). Deep learning architectures, including 3D convolutional neural networks and transformer-based temporal models, will be trained to map behavioral sequences to clinically validated assessments of anxiety, trauma, and social engagement. HPC resources are critical for handling the volume and complexity of these data (terabytes of video, ~10,000 annotated sessions) and for optimizing model hyperparameters across diverse demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for objective, quantitative play therapy progress monitoring, (2) predictive models linking specific play behaviors to diagnostic profiles, and (3) foundational insights into how computational methods can enhance fidelity in therapist training. By bridging developmental psychopathology and AI, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-informed play therapy while adhering to ethical standards for child-centered mental health research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across Latin American and Caribbean communities through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The study addresses a critical gap in interdisciplinary area studies: the lack of computationally driven frameworks to systematically trace how cultural symbols, linguistic patterns, and mediated representations (e.g., literature, digital media, archival imagery) intersect with gender, ethnicity, and regional identities in historically marginalized groups. Current scholarship often relies on manual qualitative methods, limiting the scope of comparative analysis across time periods, geographies, and media types. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and computer vision techniques. The project will process multilingual corpora spanning 19th-century newspapers, contemporary social media, indigenous language documents, and visual archives from institutional repositories across six countries. Key computational challenges include training custom transformer models for low-resource languages (e.g., Guarani, Creole variants), detecting semantic shifts in identity-related terminology, and mapping visual motifs in historical photographs through convolutional neural networks. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale of unstructured data (estimated at 120 TB), parallelizing model training across GPU nodes, and running iterative simulations to validate cultural diffusion patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital atlas visualizing identity discourse dynamics, a benchmark dataset for interdisciplinary cultural analytics, and methodological advancements in applying computational tools to non-Western epistemologies. By bridging area-specific expertise with scalable technical infrastructure, this work aims to redefine how cultural hybridity and postcolonial memory are studied in Latin American and Caribbean contexts, offering transferable frameworks for global ethnic and gender studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of dialectal variation in modern Spanish, with a focus on understudied regional and social dialects across Latin America and Spain. While traditional dialectology relies on manual data collection and qualitative analysis, the scale and complexity of contemporary spoken and written corpora—including audiovisual archives, social media texts, and transcribed interviews—require automated methods to identify patterns across phonological, lexical, and syntactic features. The research problem centers on overcoming computational limitations in processing terabyte-scale multilingual datasets, which currently restrict the granularity of dialectal mapping and the integration of real-time sociolinguistic variables. The proposed approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned for code-switching and dialect identification, with geospatial clustering algorithms to model dialect boundaries and contact zones. Computational workflows will parallelize corpus preprocessing, feature extraction, and statistical analysis across HPC nodes, enabling the comparison of over 50 regional variants simultaneously. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of Spanish dialectal features, scalable tools for educators and policymakers working with multilingual populations, and novel metrics for quantifying the impact of globalization on dialect convergence. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this project aims to redefine the scope of Spanish dialectology, offering methodological frameworks applicable to minority language preservation and technology development—such as dialect-aware speech recognition systems—in line with the program’s emphasis on applied linguistic contexts. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, reducing processing timelines from months to days, and ensuring reproducibility for future studies in Hispanic linguistics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Spanish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Castilan; Latin American and regional Spanish dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing adaptive instructional strategies for teaching English or French as a second language (L2) by leveraging computational modeling to analyze patterns in learner variability and pedagogical effectiveness. Current methods for tailoring L2 instruction to diverse learner profiles—including variations in linguistic background, cognitive load, and interaction dynamics—are limited by the manual analysis of small datasets, hindering scalability and generalizability. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach to process large-scale learner corpora, including longitudinal interaction logs, writing samples, and multimodal proficiency assessments. Computational linguistics methods, including transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models, will be trained to classify learner errors, predict developmental trajectories, and simulate the impact of targeted feedback strategies. The HPC infrastructure will support parallelized training of multiple neural architectures (e.g., BERT, GPT variants) on multilingual datasets, enabling cross-linguistic comparisons between English and French learner cohorts. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments to test hypotheses about scaffolded instruction under resource constraints. Outcomes will include open-source tools for generating adaptive lesson plans, real-time diagnostic dashboards for teacher trainees, and a repository of annotated learner data for the L2 education community. By quantifying relationships between instructional variables and learning outcomes, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in language teacher education, equipping educators with scalable strategies to address heterogeneous learner needs. The project’s computational outputs will directly inform professional development frameworks for pre-service teachers, emphasizing data-driven decision-making in diverse classroom contexts.
cip_title: Teaching English or French as a Second or Foreign Language, Other
cip_definition: Any program in teaching English or French as a second or foreign language, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Palliative care research faces a critical challenge in integrating complex, multi-dimensional datasets—including patient-reported outcomes, clinical biomarkers, and psychosocial variables—to predict treatment responses and optimize personalized care plans. Existing analytical methods often fail to account for the dynamic interactions between biological, psychological, and social factors that influence patient trajectories in serious illness. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model these interactions and generate actionable insights for clinical decision-making. The research will utilize longitudinal datasets from palliative care cohorts, including electronic health records, genomic profiles, and real-time symptom tracking from wearable devices. Machine learning algorithms, such as ensemble models and recurrent neural networks, will be employed to identify patterns in disease progression, symptom clusters, and treatment outcomes. A key innovation involves simulating patient-specific trajectories under varying intervention scenarios using agent-based modeling, which requires substantial computational resources to iteratively refine parameters across thousands of virtual patients. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) will analyze unstructured clinical notes to quantify clinician-patient communication patterns and their association with care quality metrics. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the scale of data integration, parallelizing computationally intensive simulations, and optimizing hyperparameters for predictive models. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for dynamic risk stratification in palliative care, validated predictive algorithms for 30-day symptom exacerbation, and a computational platform to simulate the impact of resource allocation strategies on patient outcomes. This work will advance the precision of palliative care interventions, reduce trial-and-error approaches in symptom management, and provide a template for data-driven resource prioritization in clinical settings with limited capacity. By bridging computational innovation and patient-centered care, the project aims to establish a scalable methodology for improving quality of life in seriously ill populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care
