High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to run ensemble simulations testing adaptive management scenarios under varying climate projections (RCP 4.5 and 8.5), while accounting for uncertainties in larval dispersal mechanisms and interspecies trophic relationships. Parallel processing will enable sensitivity analyses across 10^4 parameter combinations to identify critical thresholds in spawning habitat viability and fleet dynamics. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs in pattern recognition from output datasets exceeding 100TB in scale. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize seasonal quota allocations, evaluate marine protected area network efficacy under thermal stress, and quantify trade-offs between ecosystem-based management approaches. This computational framework will directly support state and federal agencies in meeting mandated stock rebuilding timelines while maintaining coastal livelihoods. By advancing coupled biophysical modeling capabilities, the project addresses a critical gap in fisheries science: scaling individual-level processes to inform regional management policies in rapidly changing oceans.
cip_title: Fishing and Fisheries Sciences and Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the husbandry and production of non-domesticated fish and shellfish populations for recreational and commercial purposes and the management of fishing and marine/aquatic product processing to ensure adequate conservation and efficient utilization. Includes instruction in the principles of marine/aquatic biology, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, water resources, fishing production operations and management, fishing policy and regulation, and the management of recreational and commercial fishing activities.

abstract: Students with diverse learning needs require highly personalized educational interventions, yet designing effective strategies remains challenging due to the complex interplay of cognitive, behavioral, and environmental factors. Traditional analytical approaches often struggle to model these multidimensional interactions at scale. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets from special education settings, including student performance metrics, behavioral observations, and physiological sensor data. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns predictive of intervention success, while agent-based simulations will model classroom dynamics under varying instructional scenarios. The computational demands of processing heterogeneous data streams and running iterative simulations necessitate parallelized workflows and substantial memory allocation. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to guide educators in tailoring interventions to individual learner profiles and (2) optimized simulation environments for testing the scalability of adaptive teaching strategies. By integrating computational modeling with special education pedagogy, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in teacher preparation programs, ultimately supporting more equitable learning outcomes for students with disabilities. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable rapid prototyping of models, real-time analysis of complex datasets, and validation of intervention efficacy across simulated and real-world classroom contexts. This project bridges gaps between computational innovation and special education practice, offering transformative potential for teacher training and individualized instruction.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in special education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize human-centric spatial configurations within dynamic urban environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in traditional environmental design methodologies. While conventional approaches prioritize static metrics such as traffic flow or energy efficiency, this research focuses on the interplay between socio-cultural behaviors, ephemeral environmental conditions (e.g., microclimates, seasonal light shifts), and adaptive design interventions. The core problem lies in simulating real-time, multi-agent interactions within hyper-localized contexts—such as transient pop-up community spaces or disaster-resilient urban layouts—where existing tools lack the resolution to capture nonlinear human-environment feedback loops. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) paired with generative adversarial networks (GANs), the project will simulate scenarios integrating pedestrian movement patterns, sensory perception data (crowd-sourced via anonymized geotagged audio/visual inputs), and dynamic material responses (e.g., phase-changing materials in temporary shelters). HPC resources are critical to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations testing thousands of design permutations under stochastic environmental stressors (e.g., heatwaves, flash floods) while maintaining sub-meter spatial granularity. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive environmental design, validated against case studies in three climate-vulnerable regions, and a novel metric system quantifying "socio-spatial resilience." By bridging computational social science, sensory ethnography, and parametric design, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for environments that are both ecologically responsive and culturally inclusive, addressing a critical gap in non-engineering design research. The scalability of the framework will enable policymakers and designers to prototype context-sensitive solutions without relying on resource-intensive physical mock-ups, thereby democratizing access to high-fidelity environmental modeling tools.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental design, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing human-centric spatial experiences in rapidly densifying urban environments through the development of a computational framework for adaptive environmental design. As cities face pressures from climate change, population growth, and evolving socio-cultural needs, traditional architectural approaches struggle to model the complex interactions between built forms, environmental flows, and human behavioral patterns at metropolitan scales. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create multi-agent simulation systems that integrate real-time climate data, pedestrian movement analytics, and material performance metrics across temporal scales ranging from diurnal cycles to decadal projections. The computational methodology combines three novel components: 1) A neural network trained on global urban morphology datasets to predict microclimate impacts of design interventions, 2) A generative adversarial network (GAN) architecture for synthesizing spatial configurations that balance competing performance criteria, and 3) Dynamic graph-based simulations of crowd movement patterns under varying environmental conditions. By employing parallelized finite element analysis for thermal modeling and GPU-accelerated agent-based simulations, the framework will enable iterative testing of design hypotheses at unprecedented resolution across 50+ city block prototypes. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for evaluating human-environment interaction metrics in architectural proposals, along with a curated dataset linking spatial design parameters to quantifiable well-being indicators. This work bridges critical gaps between architectural theory, urban climate science, and computational social dynamics, providing evidence-based strategies for creating adaptive public spaces in megacity contexts. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte lidar scans, running coupled fluid dynamics simulations, and training deep learning models on heterogeneous urban datasets – tasks that exceed the capacity of conventional design software and local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design public and private spaces, indoor and outdoor, for leisure, recreational, commercial, and living purposes, and for professional practice as environmental designers and architects. Includes instruction in the design and planning of public and private open spaces and their relationship to buildings and other aspects of the built environment; facilities management; related aspects of interior design and architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework for optimizing large-scale industrial operations under dynamic constraints, with a focus on enhancing decision-making in manufacturing systems, supply chain logistics, and environmental management. A critical challenge in industrial management is balancing competing objectives—such as cost efficiency, resource utilization, sustainability, and workforce safety—amidst stochastic demand, equipment variability, and regulatory requirements. Existing optimization tools often struggle with the combinatorial complexity of these multi-objective problems, particularly when scaling to real-world systems with thousands of interdependent variables. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized metaheuristic algorithms, hybrid simulation-optimization models, and machine learning-driven predictive analytics. The computational workflow will integrate discrete-event simulations of production lines with multi-agent reinforcement learning to model adaptive supply chain behaviors, while mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) methods will optimize energy and material flows under carbon emission constraints. Large-scale sensitivity analyses will evaluate resilience to disruptions, including raw material shortages and demand volatility. The HPC environment is essential for handling the memory-intensive nature of industrial digital twins, which require real-time processing of IoT sensor data streams and high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support toolkit capable of identifying Pareto-optimal solutions for operational planning, validated through case studies with manufacturing partners in the automotive and renewable energy sectors. This work will advance methodological integration across operations research and industrial engineering while providing actionable strategies for sustainable productivity gains. By quantifying trade-offs between economic and environmental performance metrics at unprecedented resolution, the project aims to establish best practices for data-driven resource allocation in Industry 4.0 environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of engineering principles to the planning and operational management of industrial and manufacturing operations, and prepares individuals to plan and manage such operations. Includes instruction in accounting, engineering economy, financial management, industrial and human resources management, industrial psychology, management information systems, mathematical modeling and optimization, quality control, operations research, safety and health issues, and environmental program management.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in metadata generation and resource discovery for large-scale digital collections within academic libraries, a challenge exacerbated by the exponential growth of digitized and born-digital materials. Traditional metadata creation workflows, which rely on manual or semi-automated processes, struggle to scale with the volume and heterogeneity of contemporary collections, leading to inconsistent tagging, incomplete descriptions, and reduced discoverability. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and train machine learning models capable of automating metadata extraction, enrichment, and cross-collection semantic linking. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for text analysis, computer vision techniques for non-textual media, and graph neural networks to model relationships between disparate collections. These models will be trained on a corpus of 15 million digitized items—spanning texts, images, and multimedia—drawn from six institutional repositories. The scale of data and complexity of multi-modal integration necessitate distributed computing architectures for parallel processing, hyperparameter optimization, and validation against existing library metadata schemas. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive metadata generation, capable of handling diverse formats and evolving collection priorities, as well as a semantic search interface prototype that leverages inferred connections between materials. This work aims to significantly reduce metadata creation costs, improve cross-collection discoverability, and enable dynamic resource allocation strategies for digital repositories. By bridging computational methods with library science practices, the project advances infrastructural capacity for cultural heritage preservation while maintaining rigorous alignment with ethical standards in collection management and accessibility.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Adult literacy programs face persistent challenges in personalizing instruction to address the diverse cognitive, linguistic, and sociocultural backgrounds of learners. Traditional methods often rely on static curricula or generalized assessments, which fail to adapt dynamically to individual learner needs or optimize engagement. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven adaptive learning system, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and predict learner progress across multimodal data streams. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in adult learners’ behavioral, linguistic, and physiological interactions with digital literacy tools—such as text input dynamics, eye-tracking metrics, and error-correction pathways—to generate real-time instructional adjustments. A computational pipeline will be designed to process terabyte-scale datasets from anonymized learner interactions, integrating natural language processing (NLP) for semantic error analysis, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for temporal progression modeling, and reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks to simulate tutor intervention strategies. The HPC environment is critical for training multi-modal models concurrently, enabling rapid iteration of hyperparameters and large-scale validation against heterogeneous learner cohorts. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive toolkit for literacy instructors, capable of recommending targeted skill-building activities and visualizing learner metacognitive patterns. By bridging computational linguistics, cognitive modeling, and educational practice, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for adaptive adult literacy instruction, with potential applications in low-resource or multilingual contexts. The project’s computational demands—particularly in distributed training of deep learning architectures and real-time data integration—necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and parallelized storage systems to ensure feasibility within iterative research cycles.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as instructors and mentors for adults in basic or functional literacy programs in school, institutional, community, and private settings.

abstract: The proliferation of next-generation wireless systems, such as 6G networks and massive IoT deployments, has introduced critical challenges in scalability, latency, and energy efficiency for communication networks. Existing optimization frameworks struggle to model ultra-dense, heterogeneous environments with dynamic user mobility and interference patterns, limiting their ability to support emerging applications like real-time holographic communications and autonomous vehicle coordination. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven computational platform to optimize resource allocation, beamforming, and network slicing in large-scale communication systems. The research will leverage parallelized graph neural networks (GNNs) and stochastic optimization algorithms, implemented on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, to simulate multi-tier networks with thousands of nodes and dynamic channel conditions. Key methodologies include distributed training of GNNs for adaptive beamforming, Monte Carlo simulations for interference analysis, and GPU-accelerated numerical solvers for non-convex power allocation problems. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, real-time protocol validation, and the generation of high-resolution performance metrics under varying traffic loads. Anticipated outcomes include novel algorithms for spectral efficiency improvement in dense urban networks, energy-aware network slicing protocols, and open-source simulation tools for 6G research. These contributions will address fundamental bottlenecks in communication system design, directly impacting the deployment of low-latency industrial IoT networks and high-reliability public safety infrastructures. By bridging the gap between theoretical models and practical network constraints, this work will provide actionable insights for standardization bodies and telecom operators, advancing the state of the art in scalable and sustainable communication engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and maintenance of communications technology, networks, and systems. Includes instruction in communications networks and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the impact of trade policy uncertainty on global supply chain dynamics and multinational firm investment behavior using a large-scale computational structural model. Recent geopolitical shifts and the proliferation of nontariff barriers have introduced unprecedented complexity in forecasting international trade flows, particularly in intermediate goods. Traditional partial equilibrium trade models fail to capture the interdependencies between policy announcements, currency fluctuations, and firms’ adaptive strategies across multiple jurisdictions. The research will develop a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) model with heterogeneous firms, incorporating real-world data on 1.2 million bilateral trade relationships, firm-level capital adjustment costs, and stochastic policy shock processes derived from textual analysis of trade agreement negotiations. The computational approach requires high-performance computing resources to solve the model’s high-dimensional fixed points through parallelized Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) methods, while maintaining micro-level heterogeneity across 45 countries and 30 industrial sectors. Key challenges include handling sparse matrix operations for input-output tables at unprecedented granularity and simulating counterfactuals under alternative trade regime scenarios. Expected outcomes include quantified estimates of policy uncertainty spillovers through global value chains, identification of sector-specific vulnerability thresholds, and predictive metrics for trade diversion effects under coordinated vs. unilateral policy interventions. The resulting computational framework will provide policymakers with a decision-support tool for evaluating the stability implications of proposed trade agreements, while advancing methodological integration of machine learning techniques with structural economic modeling. This work directly addresses critical gaps in international economics literature regarding the nonlinear propagation of policy risks in interconnected markets, requiring teraflop-scale computation capacity unavailable through conventional research computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study and analysis of international commercial behavior and trade policy. Includes instruction in international trade theory, tariffs and quotas, commercial policy, trade factor flows, international finance and investment, currency regulation and trade exchange rates and markets, international trade negotiation, and international payments and accounting policy.

abstract: Palliative care research faces critical challenges in integrating complex, multimodal datasets to improve patient-centered outcomes. Current approaches often lack the computational capacity to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and patient-reported outcomes in tandem, limiting the ability to predict disease trajectories or personalize interventions. This project proposes the development of a machine learning (ML) framework to model multidimensional palliative care data, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in data integration, model training, and validation. The research will utilize de-identified EHRs from three tertiary healthcare systems (n ≈ 150,000 patients), paired with genomic biomarkers of symptom burden and longitudinal quality-of-life surveys. A hybrid neural architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing for clinical notes, convolutional networks for imaging-derived pain assessments, and survival analysis modules will be implemented to predict 6-month mortality risks, hospitalization events, and optimal care pathways. Computational workflows will leverage distributed training across GPU nodes to manage memory-intensive tasks, including federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across institutions. Validation will involve prospective clinical trials comparing model-guided palliative care referrals against standard protocols. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for temporal phenotyping of palliative care needs, risk stratification algorithms deployable in clinical settings, and evidence-based frameworks for resource allocation in hospice programs. By enabling real-time analysis of petabyte-scale datasets, this HPC-driven approach aims to reduce latency in palliative care delivery, decrease unnecessary invasive interventions, and improve alignment between patient preferences and treatment plans. The computational infrastructure will support reproducibility through containerized pipelines and benchmark datasets for future research in value-based care optimization.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in American Sign Language (ASL) linguistics, focusing on the analysis of spatial-grammatical structures and non-manual markers in ASL discourse. While ASL’s morphology and syntax are well-documented qualitatively, quantitative modeling of its dynamic, multi-channel visual features—such as simultaneous handshape transitions, facial expressions, and 3D signing space utilization—remains underdeveloped due to the computational complexity of processing high-dimensional visual-kinetic data. The proposed research will compile and analyze a corpus of annotated ASL video data (500+ hours) to train machine learning models capable of parsing and classifying grammatical constructions, including classifier predicates and role-shift markers. Computational workflows will integrate 3D pose estimation, optical flow analysis, and temporal convolutional networks to model the interplay of manual and non-manual signals. A key innovation involves adapting transformer architectures to process spatial-temporal dependencies in sign sequences, enabling granular syntactic and discourse-level analysis. By automating the extraction of linguistic features from video, this project aims to generate scalable datasets for cross-dialectal comparisons and create computational tools to assist in ASL transcription, pedagogy, and preservation. The requested HPC resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parallel processing of video frames, and storage of intermediate kinematic datasets. Outcomes will advance theoretical understanding of ASL grammar while providing open-source computational frameworks for sign language research, with implications for improving accessibility technologies and resources for Deaf communities. This work bridges computational linguistics and ASL studies, addressing a critical gap in infrastructure for analyzing sign languages as full natural languages within high-performance computing environments.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on American Sign Language as a visual and motor medium of communication and discourse for deaf individuals and deaf culture. Includes instruction in the development of ASL, ASL morphology and syntax, signing technique, English translation of ASL, formal and colloquial ASL, and ASL transcription.

abstract: Neuropharmacological research faces a critical challenge in elucidating the dynamic interactions between psychoactive drugs and their neuronal targets at molecular resolution. Traditional experimental methods struggle to capture the transient binding mechanisms and allosteric effects of drugs on ion channels, neurotransmitter transporters, and G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), particularly within the context of neurological disorders such as addiction, chronic pain, and neurodegenerative diseases. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and virtual screening of novel compounds targeting the dopaminergic and glutamatergic systems. Using GPU-accelerated simulations, we will model the conformational changes induced by FDA-approved drugs and experimental compounds in neuronal voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav1.7) and metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluR5), which are implicated in neuropathic pain and schizophrenia, respectively. The computational pipeline will integrate homology modeling, free-energy perturbation calculations, and machine learning-driven quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) analysis to predict binding affinities and selectivity profiles. A key innovation involves simulating lipid bilayer-embedded receptor systems over microsecond timescales to resolve drug-induced modulation of membrane protein dynamics—a process infeasible without HPC-scale resources. Expected outcomes include the identification of lead compounds with optimized blood-brain barrier permeability and reduced off-target effects, directly informing wet-lab validation. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of neuropharmacological agents while accelerating the development of precision therapies for CNS disorders. By prioritizing computational prediction over trial-and-error screening, the project aligns with NIH priorities to reduce costs and timelines in CNS drug discovery. The requested resources will support 20 concurrent simulation trajectories, high-throughput docking of 50,000-compound libraries, and data analysis workflows, enabling transformative insights into neurotherapeutic design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drugs that modify the function of the brain and central nervous system, the effects of such drugs on health, disease, perception, motor action, and behavior; and the development of countermeasures and treatment therapies. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, behavioral neuroscience, neurobiochemistry, neuropathology, the mechanisms of brain function, medicinal chemistry, pharmaceutics, and studies of specific drugs and drug therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of contaminant transport and transformation in heterogeneous environmental systems. A critical challenge in environmental chemistry lies in understanding the coupled physical, chemical, and biological processes governing pollutant fate across scales—from molecular interactions at mineral-water interfaces to plume-scale reactive transport in soils and groundwater. Current models often oversimplify these dynamics due to computational constraints, limiting their utility for remediation planning or risk assessment. To address this gap, we propose multiscale simulations integrating quantum mechanical calculations, molecular dynamics (MD), and reactive transport modeling (RTM) to investigate the behavior of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and heavy metal complexes in iron oxide-rich soils. Quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT) will parameterize adsorption energetics and degradation pathways at mineral surfaces, while MD simulations resolve interfacial solvation dynamics. These outputs will inform continuum-scale RTM frameworks implemented in open-source codes (e.g., PFLOTRAN), simulating field-relevant scenarios with spatially variable hydrology and redox conditions. The HPC environment is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of reactive species, stochastic parameterization of heterogeneous media, and ensemble runs quantifying uncertainty. Anticipated outcomes include (1) mechanistically grounded rate laws for PFAS transformation under iron-reducing conditions, (2) scalable reactive transport workflows linking nanoscale interactions to macroscopic predictions, and (3) open-access datasets informing regulatory thresholds for co-contaminated sites. By resolving cross-scale feedbacks between pollutant chemistry and environmental matrices, this work aims to advance predictive tools for contaminant mitigation while establishing computational protocols adaptable to emerging contaminants of concern.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of natural systems (air, water, and soil) through the use of chemical techniques and instrumentation, with an emphasis on the movement and fate of pollutants and chemical aspects of contaminant remediation. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; aquatic, soil, and atmospheric chemistry; environmental engineering; environmental toxicology; and analytical methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing adaptive supply chain networks under dynamic disruptions by integrating behavioral economics with machine learning (ML) models, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve computational bottlenecks in real-time decision-making. Traditional supply chain optimization frameworks often assume static stakeholder behavior or deterministic risk profiles, limiting their applicability in contexts with volatile human decision patterns (e.g., panic buying, supplier trust erosion) and multi-scale disruptions (e.g., geopolitical shifts, climate events). We propose a novel computational framework that combines agent-based modeling of behavioral economic dynamics with non-convex ML-driven optimization, explicitly accounting for time-varying human and environmental uncertainties. The research will develop a hybrid architecture using reinforcement learning to adaptively update supply chain topologies and game-theoretic models to simulate stakeholder interactions, trained on heterogeneous datasets spanning historical transaction records, social media sentiment, and climate projection data. HPC resources are critical to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, optimize hyperparameters in high-dimensional ML models, and solve large-scale mixed-integer nonlinear programming problems under time constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for resilience-aware supply chain design, validated against case studies in pharmaceutical and agricultural industries, and policy recommendations for incentivizing robustness in public-private supply networks. By bridging behavioral theory with computational scalability, this work aims to advance business analytics methodologies for complex adaptive systems while providing actionable insights for stakeholders operating in interconnected, disruption-prone environments. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—synthesizing operations research, cognitive science, and climate informatics—exemplifies a niche within multidisciplinary science not fully addressed by existing domain-specific paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to solve business challenges. Includes instruction in machine learning, optimization methods, computer algorithms, probability and stochastic models, information economics, logistics, strategy, consumer behavior, marketing, and visual analytics.

abstract: Pediatric radiology faces unique challenges in diagnostic imaging due to the dynamic anatomical and physiological changes across developmental stages, coupled with the need to minimize radiation exposure and invasive procedures in young patients. Current imaging protocols and diagnostic tools are often adapted from adult studies, which may not account for pediatric-specific pathologies, size variations, or motion artifacts. This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize pediatric imaging workflows, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and enable personalized risk-stratified protocols. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning algorithms on multimodal pediatric imaging datasets (MRI, CT, and ultrasound) from diverse age groups and pathologies, including congenital anomalies, oncology, and trauma. Computational pipelines will integrate image segmentation, artifact correction, and feature extraction tailored to pediatric anatomy, with a focus on minimizing radiation dose in CT through synthetic image generation and dose simulation. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be employed to augment limited pediatric datasets, addressing data scarcity while preserving demographic and pathological diversity. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-resolution 3D/4D imaging data, running iterative simulations, and validating models across multi-institutional cohorts. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated pediatric image analysis, validated age-specific imaging protocols, and predictive models linking imaging biomarkers to clinical outcomes. This work aims to establish a computational framework that improves diagnostic precision, reduces procedural risks, and supports evidence-based imaging guidelines for pediatric populations. By prioritizing scalability and interoperability, the resulting resources will foster collaboration across pediatric radiology networks, ultimately advancing equitable access to high-quality diagnostic care for children worldwide.
cip_definition: Research focused on all forms of diagnostic imaging as it pertains to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases in the newborn, infant, child, and adolescent.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in clinical esthetics through computational modeling of skin biomechanics and treatment outcomes. The esthetics field faces a critical gap in evidence-based protocols for personalized skin interventions, particularly in post-operative care and advanced dermatological esthetics. Current methods rely heavily on generalized guidelines, with limited capacity to predict individual responses to treatments such as chemical peels, microdermabrasion, or lymphatic drainage techniques. To address this, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of skin tissue dynamics, agent-based simulations of cellular responses to esthetic treatments, and machine learning (ML) models trained on clinical and biometric datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution 3D skin scans, real-time fluid dynamics simulations for product absorption studies, and probabilistic analysis of treatment efficacy across diverse skin types and conditions. Key challenges include optimizing biomechanical parameters for heterogeneous skin layers and validating models against longitudinal clinical data from partner dermatology clinics. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing treatment sequences, reducing adverse reactions, and tailoring interventions to individual healing trajectories. This work will establish a novel computational paradigm for esthetic medicine, bridging gaps between empirical practice and quantitative analysis. By enabling data-driven personalization of care, the project aims to elevate clinical standards, improve patient outcomes in post-operative settings, and inform the development of next-generation esthetic technologies. The computational frameworks generated will also serve as foundational resources for educational programs, fostering integration of computational literacy into esthetician training curricula.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and body with advanced chemical and cosmetic preparations and esthetic medical treatments, and to function as licensed master or medical estheticians in dermatologists' and plastic surgeons' offices as well as in salons and spas. Includes instruction in advanced anatomy and physiology, skin properties and disorders, sanitation and infection control, advanced facial treatments, spa body treatments, advanced extractions, corrective makeup, chemical peels, microdermabrasion, lymphatic drainage and advanced massage techniques, pre- and post-operative esthetic skin care, client/patient evaluation and care, applicable laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling and simulating multiscale, nonlinear dynamical systems with applications to fluid-structure interaction in biomedical and environmental contexts. The research problem centers on resolving the coupled dynamics of deformable structures immersed in turbulent flows—a scenario common in cardiovascular biomechanics, airborne particulate transport, and marine energy systems. Existing methods struggle to balance accuracy with computational feasibility due to the wide separation of spatiotemporal scales, stochastic boundary conditions, and the need for high-resolution discretization of both fluid and solid domains. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining adaptive immersed boundary methods, parallelized lattice Boltzmann solvers, and reduced-order stochastic modeling of uncertain material parameters. The approach leverages hierarchical grid refinement to resolve critical flow features near moving boundaries while employing probabilistic surrogate models to propagate parameter uncertainties across scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three primary tasks: (1) large-scale direct numerical simulations to generate training data for surrogate models, (2) ensemble-based uncertainty quantification across geometrically complex domains, and (3) validation against experimental particle image velocimetry datasets. The requested allocation will enable simulations at physiologically and environmentally relevant Reynolds numbers (Re > 10^3) with sub-millimeter spatial resolution across cubic-meter-scale domains—a 100x improvement over current capabilities. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for coupled fluid-structure simulation, quantitative error bounds for clinical vascular flow predictions, and optimized designs for wave energy converter arrays. By advancing scalable algorithms for stochastic multiscale systems, this work will provide foundational tools applicable to diverse fields requiring high-fidelity fluid-structure interaction modeling, from targeted drug delivery systems to coastal infrastructure resilience.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in applied mathematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and spatial dynamics of cellular interactions during tissue morphogenesis, with a focus on musculoskeletal development. A central challenge in anatomical research is understanding how individual cell behaviors—such as adhesion, contractility, and matrix remodeling—scale to produce organized tissue architectures in three dimensions. Current experimental models lack the resolution to track emergent structural patterns across multiple scales in dynamic environments. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate multicellular self-organization under physiological mechanical constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the nonlinear interactions of 10⁶-10⁷ simulated cells while incorporating heterogeneous material properties derived from empirical micromechanical testing of developing embryonic tissues. The ABM component will model cell decision-making based on local chemical gradients and neighbor interactions, while FEA will predict stress-strain distributions influencing tissue-scale alignment and compaction. Simulations will be validated against time-lapse microscopy data of murine limb bud development, focusing on tendon-muscle interface formation. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical mechanical thresholds that stabilize functional tissue boundaries, (2) predictive maps of cellular force transmission pathways during organogenesis, and (3) open-source simulation tools for visualizing multiscale anatomical relationships. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of structural birth defects involving connective tissues and provide a computational testbed for optimizing regenerative medicine scaffold designs. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration at biologically relevant scales, which is computationally prohibitive on local clusters due to memory-intensive 3D spatial calculations and iterative solver requirements.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of organ systems, tissue structures, and whole bodies together with their cellular and structural components and dynamics. Includes instruction in cell biology and histology, structural biology, molecular mechanics, regional and gross anatomy, embryology, neuroanatomy, endocrinology and secretory dynamics, and applications to such topics as aging and disease conditions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between digital media practices and cultural identity formation within transnational diaspora communities. The research addresses a critical gap in area studies by examining how geographically dispersed populations negotiate cultural belonging through hybridized digital spaces, which traditional qualitative methods struggle to analyze at scale. Focusing on underrepresented Southeast Asian and Afro-Caribbean diasporas, the study will employ computational text analysis, multimodal network mapping, and machine learning to process large-scale datasets comprising multilingual social media content, collaborative digital archives, and user-generated multimedia. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned for code-switching patterns, graph-based algorithms to trace cross-platform cultural exchange networks, and computer vision techniques to analyze visual symbolism in user-shared imagery. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale data, parallelize resource-intensive tasks such as transformer model training, and execute real-time simulations of cultural diffusion dynamics. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of emergent digital ethnolinguistic practices, the mapping of decentralized cultural preservation efforts, and the development of open-source tools for ethically grounded computational area studies. The project aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for studying globalization’s impact on cultural production while providing scalable frameworks to amplify marginalized community narratives. Results will inform both scholarly debates about technology-mediated identity and practical initiatives supporting digital cultural heritage, with findings disseminated through public dashboards and partnerships with diaspora-led archival projects.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: Any instructional program in specifically defined area studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural and functional dynamics of neural circuits underlying sensory processing in the mammalian somatosensory cortex. A critical gap persists in understanding how synaptic plasticity and glial interactions collectively shape network-level activity patterns during tactile discrimination tasks. Traditional experimental approaches alone cannot capture the multiscale complexity of these interactions, which span molecular signaling at synapses, activity-dependent plasticity in neuronal ensembles, and emergent network oscillations. To address this, we propose developing a biophysically detailed computational model integrating empirical data from in vivo electrophysiology, two-photon calcium imaging, and ultrastructural connectomics of layer 4 cortical circuits in mice. The model will simulate activity across 50,000+ neurons and associated glial networks, incorporating experimentally derived parameters for synaptic strength, short-term plasticity, and astrocyte-mediated modulation. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of circuit dynamics under varying sensory input patterns and plasticity rules, with iterative model refinement via machine learning-based parameter optimization. Key outcomes include identifying glia-neuron signaling motifs that stabilize network activity during learning, predicting how specific synaptic alteration patterns (observed in neurodevelopmental disorders) disrupt sensory encoding fidelity, and generating testable hypotheses for optogenetic validation. This work will provide foundational insights into the interplay between cellular plasticity mechanisms and large-scale network function, with direct relevance to understanding circuitopathies in autism spectrum disorders and epilepsy. The computational framework will be shared as an open-access tool for the neuroanatomy community, facilitating collaborative exploration of structure-function relationships in neural systems. Successful execution requires sustained HPC access to manage the computational load of multi-day simulations, real-time data processing from parallel model instances, and large-scale parameter space exploration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular studies of neuronal and glial cells and circuits, neural transmitters and receptors, neuronal signaling processes, membrane and synapse structure and communication, autonomic function, nervous system circuitry and mapping, and anatomical and functional basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze fragmented and heterogeneous datasets from Holocaust archives, survivor testimonies, and wartime administrative records, with the goal of uncovering systemic patterns of persecution, survival, and memory. Despite extensive scholarship, critical gaps persist in understanding how localized policies, transnational networks, and individual agency intersected during the Holocaust, particularly across understudied regions and marginalized victim groups. The research integrates multilingual textual analysis, geospatial modeling, and network science to process digitized records—including deportation lists, ghetto administration documents, oral histories, and postwar compensation claims—that are currently siloed by format, language, or institutional collection. Computational challenges include OCR correction for degraded documents, transformer-based NLP for semantic extraction across German, Yiddish, Polish, and Hebrew sources, and dynamic network reconstruction to map evolving perpetrator hierarchies. HPC resources are essential for training custom multilingual models, conducting Monte Carlo simulations to address archival lacunae, and visualizing large-scale displacement trajectories through time-series geodatabases. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible data repository with cross-referenced metadata, algorithmic tools tailored to historical genocide research, and quantitative insights into factors influencing survival rates among vulnerable subgroups such as women, children, and forced laborers. By bridging archival historiography with computational scalability, this project aims to establish a methodological framework for analyzing mass violence that prioritizes interdisciplinary rigor while addressing ethical imperatives in data representation. The results will directly inform educational initiatives, memorialization practices, and policy discussions on atrocity prevention, emphasizing the role of digital humanities in preserving complex narratives of resilience and loss.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on genocide in human history with particular reference to Twentieth Century genocides such as that of the Ottoman Armenians during World War I and the Nazi Holocaust during World War II. Programs also focus on topics such as survivor studies and counseling, war crimes research and prevention, reconciliation and compensation, ethical and spiritual issues, holocaust art and literature, and legacy and effect in relation to subsequent generations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance pedagogical innovation in drama and dance teacher education through the development of a computational framework for analyzing and simulating embodied teaching practices. While movement-based pedagogies are central to effective drama and dance instruction, current teacher training relies heavily on qualitative observation and subjective reflection, limiting scalability and systematic feedback. Our research addresses this gap by creating quantitative models of kinesthetic teaching strategies, classroom spatial dynamics, and student responsiveness. Using motion capture data from instructor demonstrations and classroom simulations, we will train machine learning models to identify patterns in effective movement pedagogies across diverse learning contexts. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom interactions to evaluate how variations in teacher positioning, gestural cues, and choreographic scaffolding influence student engagement. The computational workflow requires processing high-resolution motion datasets, real-time rendering of 3D classroom environments, and parallelized optimization of instructional scenario parameters. Outcomes will include an open-access toolkit for visualizing teaching strategies, predictive analytics to guide reflective practice, and evidence-based frameworks for integrating embodied learning theories into teacher preparation curricula. By bridging performing arts pedagogy with computational analytics, this work aims to transform how dance and drama educators are trained to design inclusive, culturally responsive learning experiences grounded in the science of embodied cognition. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the complex spatial-temporal datasets and iterative modeling necessary to advance this emerging interdisciplinary field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach drama and/or dance programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable Bayesian hierarchical models to analyze high-dimensional, spatially correlated environmental health data, addressing critical computational bottlenecks in uncertainty quantification for large-scale epidemiological studies. Traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods struggle with convergence and efficiency when applied to datasets exceeding 10^6 observations with complex spatial dependencies, common in modern public health and environmental monitoring applications. The research proposes a hybrid computational approach combining stochastic variational inference (SVI), parallelized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), and distributed Gaussian process approximations to enable tractable inference. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-chain MCMC sampling across GPU nodes, optimize memory usage for sparse precision matrices via distributed linear algebra libraries, and validate model performance through simulation studies mirroring real-world environmental sensor network data structures. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for efficient spatial Bayesian modeling, methodological advances in handling non-stationary covariance structures at scale, and applied insights into air pollution exposure risks across urban-rural gradients using a case study of 2.3 million particulate matter measurements. The requested computing resources—particularly GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory capacity—are essential for benchmarking algorithmic scalability, testing multi-resolution spatial process representations, and maintaining chain persistence during weeks-long sampling tasks. Results will directly inform public health policy by improving exposure assessment accuracy while advancing statistical computing methodology for massive geospatial datasets. This work bridges theoretical innovations in spatial statistics with practical computational infrastructure demands, demonstrating how HPC-enabled Bayesian methods can overcome dimensionality barriers in applied environmental statistics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance high-resolution earthquake cycle simulations to better constrain seismic hazard in complex tectonic regions. Current models of fault rupture dynamics and wave propagation often rely on simplified 2D geometries or homogeneous material properties, limiting their ability to capture the multiscale interactions between fault geometry, stress heterogeneity, and seismic wave amplification in realistic 3D settings. This project will develop and deploy scalable computational frameworks to simulate earthquake sequences and ground motions in geometrically intricate fault systems, with a focus on the transpressional plate boundary zone of the San Andreas Fault System. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve meter-scale fault roughness, kilometer-scale crustal heterogeneities, and multi-physics coupling between poroelastic deformation, thermal pressurization, and dynamic rupture processes. The computational workflow integrates spectral boundary integral methods for long-term tectonic loading with finite-element models for dynamic rupture and wave propagation, leveraging adaptive mesh refinement and GPU-accelerated solvers. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce the dimensionality of parameter space and identify critical thresholds in fault stress states that govern rupture arrest or propagation. Anticipated outcomes include improved constraints on maximum magnitude estimates for segmented faults, probabilistic assessments of off-fault damage patterns, and validated ground motion predictions for high-risk urban areas. The resulting open-source software tools will enable community reproducibility and extension to other fault systems. By addressing computational bottlenecks in earthquake physics, this work directly supports seismic hazard mitigation efforts and advances the integration of physics-based models into probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) frameworks. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on an HPC system with GPU capabilities is required to achieve the necessary spatiotemporal resolution across ensemble simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physics of solids and its application to the study of the earth and other planets. Includes instruction in gravimetric, seismology, earthquake forecasting, magnetrometry, electrical properties of solid bodies, plate tectonics, active deformation, thermodynamics, remote sensing, geodesy, and laboratory simulations of geological processes.

abstract: The increasing complexity of architectural design demands advanced computational tools to optimize energy efficiency, structural integrity, and material performance while adhering to cost and regulatory constraints. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating and iterating architectural designs at unprecedented scales, integrating parametric modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization. Current architectural drafting workflows rely on static CAD models and manual adjustments, limiting the exploration of design alternatives under dynamic environmental and operational conditions. By leveraging HPC resources, this research aims to automate multi-objective optimization of building designs, enabling real-time feedback on energy consumption, thermal comfort, and structural resilience across thousands of design permutations. Computational methods will include parallelized parametric simulations using architectural CADD software APIs, coupled with GPU-accelerated physics engines for fluid dynamics and stress analysis. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to predict optimal design parameters for site-specific constraints, reducing computational overhead for future projects. The proposed work will validate this approach through case studies on mixed-use urban structures, evaluating trade-offs between embodied carbon, operational energy, and construction costs. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable workflow for generative architectural design, open-source tools for integrating HPC into CADD education, and datasets linking design features to sustainability metrics. This research will advance computational drafting methodologies, providing educators and practitioners with evidence-based strategies to address climate-responsive design challenges. Successful implementation will require access to HPC clusters for large-scale simulations, distributed storage for managing terabyte-scale 3D model datasets, and GPU nodes to accelerate deep learning training phases. Results will be disseminated through academic publications and modular curriculum components for architectural technology programs.
cip_title: Architectural Drafting and Architectural CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations for architectural and related construction projects. Includes instruction in basic construction and structural design, architectural rendering, architectural-aided drafting (CAD), layout and designs, architectural blueprint interpretation, building materials, and basic structural wiring diagramming.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving cultural narratives within Irish diaspora communities through the computational analysis of multilingual textual and visual archives spanning the 18th to 21st centuries. While traditional scholarship has relied on selective case studies to trace cultural retention and adaptation, this research addresses the challenge of synthesizing fragmented, large-scale historical records to identify underrepresented patterns in identity formation, gender roles, and transnational cultural exchange. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to analyze digitized collections of emigrant letters, community publications, and visual media from Irish diaspora hubs in North America, Australia, and Argentina. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on low-resource languages (e.g., Irish-language materials), processing heterogeneous data formats at scale, and conducting cross-temporal sentiment analysis. Multilayer network models will map the diffusion of cultural motifs, while geospatial analysis will visualize shifting centers of cultural production. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking previously siloed archival materials, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural hybridity in diaspora studies, and the identification of under-researched gender-specific migration narratives. By integrating computational methods with critical cultural theory, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in Irish Studies while providing new insights into how marginalized voices within diaspora communities negotiated identity under evolving sociopolitical conditions. The resource-intensive nature of processing terabytes of image-based archives and computationally modeling nonlinear narrative structures necessitates the parallelized workflows and GPU acceleration uniquely available through HPC infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Ireland and the Irish Diaspora, from the early Christian period to the present.

abstract: Emerging infectious disease threats require rapid, data-driven modeling to inform public health interventions, yet existing computational tools often lack the scalability to integrate heterogeneous datasets or simulate complex transmission dynamics across diverse populations. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework to assess the spread of vector-borne diseases in urban environments under varying climate and mobility scenarios. The proposed computational approach will integrate demographic data, real-time mobility patterns, climate projections, and vector habitat suitability maps to simulate disease transmission at a household-level granularity across metropolitan regions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and execute millions of parallelized simulations that capture stochastic variability in human-vector interactions, seasonality effects, and intervention impacts. Machine learning techniques will be applied to simulation outputs to identify nonlinear relationships between environmental covariates, socioeconomic factors, and outbreak trajectories. The resulting models will enable policymakers to evaluate targeted vaccination strategies, vector control measures, and healthcare resource allocation plans under projected climate change scenarios. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing for spatial-temporal pattern recognition and optimization algorithms, this work will advance methodological capabilities for real-time epidemic forecasting while addressing critical gaps in health equity through explicit modeling of neighborhood-specific vulnerability factors. Successful implementation will provide open-source tools for scalable disease modeling and establish a template for integrating high-resolution environmental and behavioral data into public health decision-making frameworks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public health, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to optimize evidence-based instructional design for postsecondary educators, addressing the challenge of tailoring teaching strategies to diverse adult learner populations. While current pedagogical research emphasizes learner-centered approaches, postsecondary instructors often lack scalable, data-driven methods to evaluate how specific interventions—such as adaptive assessment techniques, technology-enhanced active learning modules, or syllabus structures aligned with learning science principles—impact student outcomes across varied institutional and demographic contexts. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-phase computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, we will process anonymized, multi-institutional datasets (including learning management system interactions, assessment results, and course evaluations) using natural language processing and graph neural networks to identify latent patterns linking instructional design choices to longitudinal student performance. Second, we will build agent-based models simulating virtual classrooms, parameterized by andragogical principles and real-world demographic distributions, to test how hypothetical teaching strategies affect emergent outcomes like critical thinking development and learner motivation. These simulations will incorporate stochastic variability in learner backgrounds, engagement trajectories, and institutional resource constraints. The computational demands of training machine learning models on terabyte-scale educational datasets, coupled with the need for parallelized, large-scale parameter sweeps in classroom simulations, necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive framework to help instructors optimize syllabi, assessments, and technology integration based on course-specific constraints, as well as generalized insights into how adaptive teaching practices can equitably support nontraditional and underrepresented student populations. By grounding teacher preparation in computationally derived models of instructional effectiveness, this work aims to advance discipline-specific andragogy while maintaining scalability across resource-constrained higher education environments.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for estimating high-dimensional item response theory (IRT) models, which are critical for advancing precision in psychological measurement but remain intractable under conventional computing resources. Contemporary psychometric challenges—such as modeling multifaceted latent traits in large-scale educational assessments or dynamic behavioral data from intensive longitudinal studies—require complex IRT specifications with thousands of parameters, hierarchical structures, and adaptive sampling designs. Traditional estimation techniques, including maximum likelihood and variational inference, struggle with convergence and accuracy in these high-dimensional settings due to computational bottlenecks in evaluating multidimensional integrals and inverting large covariance matrices. To address this, we propose a hybrid parallel computing framework integrating Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) and stochastic variational inference (SVI) optimized for distributed-memory architectures. The HMC component will leverage GPU-accelerated gradient calculations for efficient exploration of posterior distributions, while the SVI component will employ asynchronous parameter updates across nodes to reduce communication overhead. Computational workflows will be validated through systematic simulations comparing parameter recovery, runtime efficiency, and scalability against existing IRT software (e.g., Stan, mirt). A case study will apply these methods to a national dataset of 500,000 respondents’ cognitive assessments with 20 correlated latent traits, enabling the detection of nuanced skill profiles previously obscured by estimation error. The project’s outcomes will include open-source software for high-performance psychometric modeling, benchmarks for distributed computing in IRT applications, and methodological guidelines for deploying hybrid algorithms in resource-constrained research environments. By overcoming current computational barriers, this work will enhance the fidelity of psychological measurement in population-level studies, support the development of adaptive testing systems, and provide a template for resource-efficient estimation of complex statistical models in quantitative psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical procedures used in psychological test construction and validation; the general problems of the measurement of behavior; and the application of quantitative methods to research design and other methodological topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational methods to address high-dimensional, nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in multiscale modeling of complex physical systems, such as turbulent fluid flows and heterogeneous material deformation. These problems are characterized by coupled spatial and temporal scales, rendering traditional discretization techniques computationally intractable. The research aims to design scalable, adaptive algorithms that combine reduced-order modeling, parallelized iterative solvers, and machine learning-driven surrogate models to enable efficient simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Key computational challenges include managing memory constraints for high-dimensional parameter spaces, optimizing load balancing in dynamically adaptive mesh refinement, and minimizing communication overhead in distributed solvers. The proposed approach integrates numerical analysis techniques—such as sparse grid collocation and operator splitting—with graph-based neural networks to approximate unresolved scales, thereby accelerating convergence while preserving accuracy. HPC resources will be critical for benchmarking hybrid CPU-GPU implementations of these algorithms against established industrial simulation tools, with test cases targeting aerodynamics and composite material failure. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for adaptive PDE solvers, validated against experimental datasets from collaborating engineering laboratories. The project will advance computational mathematics by bridging gaps between theoretical convergence guarantees and practical scalability, ultimately providing robust tools for industries reliant on predictive multiscale modeling. Successful implementation will demonstrate how applied mathematical innovations, coupled with HPC infrastructure, can overcome dimensionality barriers in scientific computing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of a broad range of mathematical and computational methods to modeling, analysis, algorithm development, and simulation for the solution of complex scientific and engineering problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, discrete mathematics, operations research, optimization, differential equations, statistics, scientific computation, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: Cancer progression and therapeutic resistance are driven by complex interactions between heterogeneous tumor cell populations and dynamic microenvironmental conditions. Traditional experimental models often lack the resolution to capture the spatiotemporal evolution of these interactions, limiting our understanding of mechanisms underlying treatment failure. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale modeling framework to simulate tumor-ecosystem dynamics in physiologically relevant microenvironments, with a focus on hypoxia-mediated resistance in epithelial carcinomas. The computational approach integrates agent-based models of tumor cell decision-making with continuum-based nutrient transport equations and discrete extracellular matrix remodeling events. Each cell agent will employ Boolean networks to emulate phenotype-specific responses to microenvironmental stressors, including oxygen gradients, metabolic competition, and chemotherapy exposure. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations across parameter spaces representing diverse tissue architectures (e.g., ductal vs. solid tumor geometries) and treatment regimens. Validation will leverage longitudinal histopathology data from neoadjuvant therapy cohorts and in vitro live-cell imaging of 3D tumor organoids under controlled hypoxic conditions. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of critical microenvironmental thresholds that trigger resistant phenotype selection, 2) predictive maps of spatial resistance patterns in anatomically structured tissues, and 3) optimization test beds for stroma-modulating adjuvant therapies. This resource-intensive modeling framework will provide unprecedented resolution of cancer cell adaptation dynamics, directly informing clinical strategies to disrupt resistance pathways in physiologically distinct tumor niches. The requested computing allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulation kernels, large-scale parameter sensitivity analyses, and machine learning-enhanced model calibration against multi-modal experimental datasets.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_title: Physiology, Pathology, and Related Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physiology, pathology, and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for analyzing the structural and semantic evolution of legal systems across jurisdictions, with a focus on understudied intersections between civil law and religious or customary legal traditions. Traditional comparative law research relies heavily on manual textual analysis, limiting scalability and the ability to detect latent patterns in large, multilingual corpora of legal texts. This project addresses this gap by developing machine learning models to map doctrinal divergences, trace the diffusion of legal concepts, and quantify the influence of non-state normative systems on statutory frameworks. The research will process a curated dataset spanning 20 jurisdictions, including historical legal codes, judicial decisions, and ethnographic records, using multilingual natural language processing (NLP) techniques tailored to legal language. Computational legal network analysis will be employed to model interactions between formal statutes and informal normative practices, while transformer-based models will identify semantic shifts in core concepts (e.g., “property rights” or “obligation”) across cultural contexts. The HPC environment is critical for training domain-specific language models on terabyte-scale legal text collections and running iterative simulations of legal harmonization scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing cross-jurisdictional legal relationships, 2) predictive metrics for identifying areas of potential normative conflict in transnational legal integration efforts, and 3) new computational methodologies for legal pluralism studies. By enabling systematic analysis of complex legal ecosystems at unprecedented scale, this work aims to provide policymakers and legal practitioners with evidence-based tools for addressing challenges in multicultural jurisprudence while establishing computational comparative law as a distinct interdisciplinary research domain.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of legal systems and philosophies in comparative perspective.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic pathogens pose significant risks to animal and human health, yet predicting transmission dynamics across species and environments remains a critical challenge in veterinary medicine. This project seeks to develop high-resolution computational models to simulate pathogen evolution, interspecies transmission, and outbreak patterns in livestock and companion animal populations. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-scale datasets, including genomic sequences of circulating pathogens, host mobility data, and environmental variables such as land use and climate. Agent-based modeling frameworks will be employed to simulate transmission scenarios under varying conditions, while machine learning algorithms will identify risk factors for spillover events and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) gene transfer. A key focus is optimizing resource allocation for disease surveillance and intervention strategies in veterinary practice. Computational demands are substantial due to the need for parallel processing of large genomic datasets (e.g., metagenomic sequencing of animal microbiomes) and stochastic simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for regional pathogen spread, identification of high-risk interfaces for zoonotic transmission, and data-driven protocols for antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary care. These results will directly support clinical decision-making, inform One Health policies, and advance methodological frameworks for analyzing complex veterinary datasets. By addressing computational bottlenecks in modeling biological systems at scale, this work will enhance capacity to mitigate emerging infectious disease threats in animal populations while safeguarding public health.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of veterinary medicine, involving the diagnosis, treatment, and health care management of animals and animal populations and the prevention and management of zoonosis. Includes instruction in the veterinary basic sciences, infectious and noninfectious disease, diagnostic procedures, veterinary clinical medicine, obstetrics, radiology, anesthesiology, surgery, toxicology, animal health and preventive medicine, clinical nutrition, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Secondary educators face significant challenges in designing instructional strategies that address heterogeneous student learning needs while maintaining alignment with curriculum standards.
