This project proposes to develop and validate computational models that simulate the impact of differentiated teaching approaches on secondary classroom outcomes, with particular focus on STEM subjects where achievement gaps persist. The research problem centers on identifying optimal pedagogical strategies that adapt to varying student prior knowledge levels, cognitive load capacities, and engagement patterns within realistic classroom constraints. We will employ agent-based modeling techniques to create synthetic student cohorts reflecting demographic and cognitive diversity observed in national education datasets. High-performance computing resources are required to run parallelized simulations testing thousands of instructional scenarios, including variations in lesson sequencing, multimodal content delivery, and formative assessment timing. Machine learning architectures will analyze resulting interaction patterns to identify teaching strategies that maximize learning gains across student subgroups. The computational framework will incorporate principles from educational psychology, curriculum theory, and cognitive science to ensure pedagogical validity. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that helps pre-service and practicing teachers visualize potential impacts of instructional choices, along with evidence-based guidelines for implementing adaptive teaching practices in secondary classrooms. This work advances the strategic integration of computational modeling in teacher education while maintaining strict adherence to ethical standards regarding educational data privacy. By bridging computational science with classroom practice, the project aims to enhance the scalability of personalized learning strategies without increasing teacher workload – a critical innovation for improving educational equity in diverse secondary school environments.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the secondary grades, which may include grades seven through twelve, depending on the school system or state regulations. May include preparation to teach a comprehensive curriculum or specific subject matter.

abstract: Infant and toddler mental health is a critical yet understudied domain, with early developmental disruptions having lifelong consequences for emotional regulation and social functioning. Current diagnostic frameworks lack predictive precision due to the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between biological, behavioral, and environmental factors during this developmental window. This project proposes to address this gap by developing a computational model that integrates multimodal data—including high-density EEG, motion-capture behavioral recordings, and caregiver-child interaction videos—to identify biomarkers of emergent mental health risk in children aged 6-36 months. The research leverages recent advances in graph neural networks (GNNs) and transformer architectures to model temporal dependencies and cross-modal interactions at multiple timescales, from millisecond-level neural oscillations to month-long developmental trajectories. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing petabyte-scale datasets, training ensemble models with over 10^8 parameters, and simulating developmental cascades under varying environmental conditions. Computational workflows will include federated learning across five clinical cohorts to preserve privacy while maximizing statistical power. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for predicting anxiety and dysregulation phenotypes 12-18 months before symptomatic onset, (2) open-source tools for real-time analysis of infant-caregiver dyadic synchrony, and (3) generative models to test hypotheses about critical period interventions. By bridging developmental neuroscience, computational psychiatry, and AI ethics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for preventative mental health care while addressing unique computational challenges in modeling rapidly evolving biological systems. The requested resources will enable latency-sensitive analyses crucial for translating findings into clinical tools used during well-child visits.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide mental health services to infants, toddlers, and preschoolers and their families. Includes instruction in developmental psychology, cognitive and biological development, social and emotional development, research methods, and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time encrypted data query processing for decentralized business intelligence systems, a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of cybersecurity, quantum-inspired algorithms, and distributed database architectures. As organizations increasingly adopt hybrid cloud-edge infrastructures, conventional encryption methods create latency bottlenecks when analyzing sensitive operational data across fragmented networks, limiting the agility of decision-support systems. The study proposes a novel computational framework leveraging lattice-based homomorphic encryption combined with quantum annealing-inspired optimization to enable secure, parallelized query execution on distributed business datasets. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-node environments with varying data locality constraints, testing neural network-based workload predictors against combinatorial optimization models for query routing. Key objectives include developing a GPU-accelerated library for privacy-preserving aggregate operations and benchmarking against traditional federated learning approaches using synthetic datasets modeling supply chain logistics and cross-institutional financial transactions. Expected outcomes include quantifiable performance metrics for encrypted join operations at petabyte scale and adaptive resource allocation strategies for heterogeneous computing clusters. This work aims to advance the state of practice in secure distributed analytics, directly supporting compliance-driven industries requiring both rigorous data protection and subsecond response times for complex business queries. The computational intensity of simulating quantum annealing effects on classical hardware and the need for massively parallel encryption/decryption cycles necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with specialized cryptographic acceleration capabilities. Successful validation of the framework could inform new standards for responsive security architectures in management information systems, particularly for organizations operating in regulated verticals with strict data sovereignty requirements.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of horizontal gene transfer (HGT) and its impact on adaptive evolution in microbial and eukaryotic systems. While HGT is a well-documented driver of genetic diversity in prokaryotes, its role in eukaryotic organisms, particularly in symbiotic and parasitic contexts, remains poorly understood. The research will integrate large-scale genomic datasets from diverse microbial communities and eukaryotic host-parasite systems to identify transfer events, assess their functional consequences, and model their evolutionary trajectories. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte sequencing datasets, performing de novo genome assemblies, and conducting comparative genomic analyses across hundreds of species. Additionally, population genomic simulations will be employed to quantify the selective pressures influencing HGT frequency and stability in varying environmental conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to predict donor-recipient compatibility and integration sites based on sequence features and epigenetic markers. Expected outcomes include a comprehensive atlas of cross-species gene transfer events, mechanistic insights into barriers preventing HGT in eukaryotic systems, and predictive models linking transfer dynamics to ecological resilience. This work will advance fundamental understanding of genetic exchange mechanisms at microbial-eukaryotic interfaces and inform strategies to mitigate the spread of antimicrobial resistance genes or engineer beneficial microbial consortia. The requested computational resources will enable analyses at unprecedented scale, bridging gaps between genome-level processes and macroevolutionary patterns in diverse biological systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of viruses, infectious agents, organelles, nuclear genomes, eubacteria, archaebacteria, and eukaryotic organisms. Includes instruction in molecular genetics and evolution, parasitic and symbiotic interaction at the genetic level, epigenetic phenomena, microbial interactions, and genomics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of climate change impacts on watershed ecosystems through high-resolution modeling of coupled hydrological and ecological processes. As anthropogenic stressors intensify, predicting shifts in water availability, biodiversity, and ecosystem services requires integrating complex, nonlinear interactions between precipitation patterns, land cover dynamics, and species responses. Existing regional models often oversimplify these relationships due to computational constraints, limiting their utility for adaptive management. We propose a novel computational framework combining a hydrodynamic model (2D Saint-Venant equations) with an agent-based ecological model simulating keystone species’ behavioral and physiological adaptations. The integration will operate at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolutions (10m grid cells, hourly timesteps) across a 50-year projection horizon, capturing fine-scale feedbacks between hydrologic variability and biotic responses. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the ∼10^14 computational operations required for ensemble simulations under multiple IPCC climate scenarios (SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5). Parallelization strategies will optimize the Message Passing Interface (MPI) for heterogeneous workloads across GPU and CPU nodes, while in-memory data handling will address I/O bottlenecks during real-time coupling of hydrological and ecological modules. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold precipitation regimes triggering irreversible shifts in riparian community composition, and (2) spatially explicit vulnerability maps linking hydrological extremes to species-specific extinction risks. These results will directly inform the National Water Model’s conservation prioritization tools and provide testable hypotheses for field monitoring campaigns in three critical watersheds. By advancing coupled modeling capabilities, this work bridges a critical gap between theoretical ecology and actionable resource management strategies in rapidly changing environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on environment-related issues using scientific, social scientific, or humanistic approaches or a combination. Includes instruction in the basic principles of ecology and environmental science and related subjects such as policy, politics, law, economics, social aspects, planning, pollution control, natural resources, and the interactions of human beings and nature.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methodologies in the analysis and generation of dramatic narratives for playwriting and screenwriting. While traditional script development relies on iterative human collaboration and qualitative feedback, this research addresses the lack of scalable, data-driven tools for analyzing narrative structures, emotional arcs, and audience engagement patterns across large corpora of scripts. By applying natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques, the project aims to model the relationship between textual features—such as dialogue rhythm, scene transitions, and character dynamics—and the perceptual outcomes reported by audiences or critics. Key computational challenges include training transformer-based models on dramatic texts, which require parsing non-standard formatting (e.g., stage directions, parentheticals) and contextualizing sparse, emotionally charged dialogue. HPC resources will enable the processing of multimodal datasets—including annotated scripts, performance recordings, and audience biometric data—to identify latent patterns in successful narratives. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for script analysis, capable of simulating audience responses to draft scenes and proposing structural edits informed by historical precedents. Additionally, the project will explore generative AI applications to assist writers in overcoming creative blocks, though ethical frameworks to preserve authorial intent will be prioritized. By bridging computational rigor with artistic practice, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying narrative craft at scale while maintaining the integrity of creative processes central to the performing arts.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for communicating dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the composition of creative written works for the theatre, film, and/or television. Includes instruction in creative writing craft, scene writing, script development, stage and/or camera instructions, line and moment analysis, script reading, script editing, and the creation of full productions.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in predicting aerothermal-structural interactions during hypersonic flight, where extreme aerodynamic heating and dynamic loads threaten vehicle integrity. Current models often decouple fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and structural deformation, leading to inaccuracies in design margins for thermal protection systems (TPS) and airframe components. To overcome these limitations, we propose a tightly coupled computational framework integrating high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD), transient heat transfer analysis, and nonlinear structural mechanics. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve multiscale phenomena, including turbulent boundary layer dynamics, nonequilibrium gas chemistry in plasma formations, and anisotropic material degradation in ceramic matrix composites. Direct numerical simulations of hypersonic flowfields will be paired with finite element models of TPS assemblies under spatially varying thermal gradients, enabling probabilistic assessments of failure modes. A key innovation involves machine learning-augmented surrogate models to accelerate iterative fluid-structure interaction analyses while preserving physics-based fidelity. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental shock tunnel data and in-flight measurements from collaborative hypersonics programs. Successful implementation will advance predictive capabilities for reusable spacecraft re-entry systems and next-generation high-Mach vehicles, directly supporting national priorities in aerospace resilience. The requested HPC allocation will enable parametric studies across flight regimes (Mach 5–15) and material configurations, requiring millions of core-hours for large-eddy simulations, conjugate heat transfer solvers, and uncertainty quantification via Monte Carlo sampling. Outcomes will include open-source modules for coupled multiphysics analysis and design guidelines for adaptive TPS architectures, significantly reducing reliance on over-conservative empirical margins in hypersonic engineering.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of physical systems used in manufacturing and aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their system. Combines instruction in mechanical and aerospace engineering.

abstract: Oral diseases in animals present complex challenges due to species-specific anatomical variations, dynamic biomechanical forces during mastication, and interactions between microbial communities and host tissues. Current clinical approaches in veterinary dentistry often rely on extrapolations from human dental research, which may inadequately address the unique physiological and pathological features of diverse animal species. This project seeks to advance the understanding of oral disease mechanisms and optimize treatment strategies in veterinary dentistry through computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support simulations of biomechanical stress distributions in heterodont dentition, agent-based modeling of oral biofilm dynamics, and machine learning-driven analysis of clinical imaging datasets. The research will integrate species-specific anatomical data derived from computed tomography (CT) and micro-CT scans of canine, feline, and equine specimens with material properties of dental tissues to construct finite element models. These models will simulate occlusal forces under various pathological conditions, such as periodontal bone loss or malocclusions, to predict fracture risks and guide restorative interventions. Concurrently, agent-based models will investigate how microbial community interactions within biofilms influence disease progression, incorporating genomic data from oral microbiomes of animals with and without diagnosed dental disease. A parallel component will employ deep learning architectures to automate detection of subtle radiographic lesions in dental imaging datasets, improving diagnostic accuracy for early-stage pathologies. The computational intensity of these multi-scale simulations, coupled with the need to process high-resolution 3D imaging data across hundreds of clinical cases, necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for parallel processing and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for treatment planning, identification of biomechanical risk factors for dental fractures, and characterization of pathogenetic microbial interaction networks. This work will provide evidence-based computational tools to enhance clinical decision-making in veterinary dentistry, ultimately improving outcomes in pain management, oral function preservation, and preventive care for companion and working animals. All developed models and analytical pipelines will be made available as open-source resources to support broader research efforts in veterinary oral health.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of dental care procedures to the teeth, eating surfaces, and oral cavities of animals. May included related research in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases and abnormalities of animal teeth and gums and related parts of the oral cavity; and related anatomical and physiological principles.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of a large-scale simulation framework for evaluating the equity and efficiency of public policy interventions targeting complex social systems. Traditional policy analysis often relies on simplified models or aggregated datasets, which struggle to capture nonlinear feedback loops, heterogeneous agent behaviors, and dynamic interactions inherent in real-world systems such as healthcare access, urban service delivery, or disaster response coordination. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations to enable granular, adaptive policy testing under diverse socioeconomic scenarios. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning techniques to simulate multi-stakeholder decision-making processes across spatially explicit environments. The ABM framework will parameterize individual and institutional agents using empirical data from public records, surveys, and geospatial repositories, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize policy parameters in response to emergent system behaviors. Key computational challenges include managing millions of interacting agents, processing high-resolution geotemporal datasets, and conducting parallelized scenario analyses. Requested HPC resources will support workload distribution across CPU-GPU architectures, enabling rapid iteration of policy simulations at unprecedented scale. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated open-source toolkit for computationally intensive policy impact assessments, (2) evidence-based recommendations for improving equity in targeted policy domains, and (3) methodological advances in coupling simulation paradigms with real-time data assimilation. This work directly addresses critical gaps in computational social science methodologies while providing actionable insights for policymakers navigating tradeoffs between system-wide efficiency and distributional justice. The scalability of the framework will permit future adaptation to other complex policy challenges beyond the initial use cases.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public policy analysis, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of coupled hydrological and biogeochemical processes in critical terrestrial systems under climate change. Rapid shifts in precipitation regimes and land use are altering water availability, contaminant transport, and biogeochemical cycling in watersheds, yet existing models often lack the spatial resolution and process complexity needed to quantify nonlinear interactions between these systems. Our research aims to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework that couples surface-subsurface hydrology with reactive transport of nutrients and pollutants. The computational approach combines finite-element groundwater flow simulations, particle-tracking methods for contaminant dispersion, and machine learning algorithms to parameterize biogeochemical reaction networks across heterogeneous landscapes. The HPC environment is essential for scaling simulations to watershed-level domains while preserving meter-scale resolution, enabling the incorporation of high-dimensional remote sensing datasets (e.g., LiDAR, hyperspectral imagery) to constrain soil properties and land cover dynamics. Key outcomes will include (1) improved quantification of feedbacks between hydrological extremes (e.g., droughts, floods) and pollutant mobilization in agricultural and urbanized basins, and (2) probabilistic projections of contaminant risks to groundwater resources under future climate scenarios. By integrating multi-scale data with process-based modeling, this work will provide actionable insights for stakeholders managing water quality and land-use planning. The requested resources will support iterative model calibration/validation, ensemble simulations to capture uncertainty, and the development of open-source tools to disseminate workflows to the geoscience community. This project aligns with Earth & Environmental Sciences’ mission to address human-environment challenges through advanced computational geoscience, with direct applications to sustainable resource management and pollution mitigation.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on earth, its environments, human activities, and the linkages between them. Includes instruction biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, pollution control and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: Musculoskeletal neoplasms present significant clinical challenges due to their biological heterogeneity, complex anatomic involvement, and variable response to multimodal therapies. Current approaches to risk stratification, treatment optimization, and outcome prediction remain suboptimal, in part due to the limitations of conventional statistical methods in modeling high-dimensional multi-omics, imaging, and clinical datasets. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative computational models that bridge these data modalities, enabling precision oncology applications. The primary research objectives are threefold: (1) to establish predictive models of tumor behavior and treatment response by harmonizing genomic, transcriptomic, and radiomic data from institutional and public repositories; (2) to simulate biomechanical consequences of limb-sparing surgeries through finite element analysis informed by patient-specific MRI/CT imaging; and (3) to optimize radiation therapy dosing schedules using agent-based modeling of tumor-microenvironment interactions. Computational workflows will employ scalable machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) for feature extraction and predictive analytics, coupled with parallelized numerical solvers for biomechanical and pharmacokinetic simulations. The anticipated resource requirements include multi-node GPU clusters for deep learning tasks, high-memory nodes for genome-scale analyses, and distributed storage solutions for managing >500 TB of multimodal clinical data. Expected outcomes include validated prognostic algorithms for metastatic progression risk, biomechanical risk maps to guide surgical planning, and adaptive radiotherapy protocols informed by simulated tumor evolution trajectories. By addressing critical gaps in data integration and computational scalability, this work aims to advance personalized therapeutic strategies, reduce morbidity from current treatment paradigms, and establish a reusable HPC pipeline for translational musculoskeletal oncology research. All tools and models will be disseminated as open-source resources to accelerate collaborative innovation in the field.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal neoplasm, and the application of cancer therapy regimes.

abstract: Nuclear radiology relies on precise imaging and quantification of radionuclide biodistribution to diagnose diseases such as cancer, neurological disorders, and cardiovascular conditions. However, current methods for reconstructing tomographic images and modeling radiotracer kinetics face limitations in accuracy and resolution, particularly in heterogeneous tissues or dynamic physiological conditions. These challenges stem from computational constraints in handling complex photon transport physics, noise reduction, and the integration of multi-modal patient data. This project proposes to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational frameworks for optimizing nuclear imaging protocols and predictive biodistribution models. The research will focus on two aims: (1) creating patient-specific Monte Carlo simulations of photon interactions in hybrid SPECT/CT and PET/MRI systems to improve image reconstruction accuracy, and (2) training deep learning models to predict radiotracer kinetics using spatially resolved, time-dependent datasets from clinical studies. The simulations will account for tissue heterogeneity, scatter effects, and motion artifacts, while the machine learning component will integrate imaging data with genomic and metabolic profiles to identify biomarkers of abnormal tracer uptake. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization, parallel processing of high-resolution voxelized phantoms, and iterative training of neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for reducing radiation dose without compromising diagnostic quality, predictive models linking biodistribution patterns to molecular subtypes of disease, and open-source tools for reproducible analysis of nuclear radiology data. This work has direct translational implications for personalizing diagnostic workflows, enhancing early detection of treatment-resistant malignancies, and improving the safety of longitudinal imaging in vulnerable populations. By bridging computational innovation with clinical nuclear radiology, the project aims to establish a scalable framework for advancing precision medicine in radionuclide-based diagnostics.
cip_definition: Research focused on the imaging by external detection of radionuclides and/or biodistribution by external detection of radionuclides for diagnosis of disease. Requires prior partial completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: Fungal pathogens pose significant threats to human health, agricultural productivity, and ecosystem stability, yet their adaptive mechanisms—particularly under environmental stress and antifungal exposure—remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting antifungal resistance and virulence evolution in clinically and agriculturally relevant fungi, including *Aspergillus fumigatus* and *Fusarium graminearum*. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the complex interplay of genomic, transcriptomic, and environmental factors driving these traits. We propose an integrative computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model fungal adaptive pathways and identify high-risk resistance or virulence markers. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize structural and functional changes in membrane-bound proteins (e.g., ergosterol biosynthesis enzymes) under mutational and drug-binding pressures, while agent-based models will simulate population-level dynamics of resistance acquisition in heterogeneous environments. Comparative genomic analyses across resistant and susceptible strains will prioritize candidate loci linked to stress adaptation. These computational workflows require large-scale parallelism for iterative simulations of protein conformations, genomic dataset alignment (500+ isolates), and stochastic modeling of fungal communities. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of multi-terabyte datasets, reduce runtime for molecular simulations from months to days, and support machine learning-driven prediction of emergent resistance phenotypes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of genetic and structural biomarkers predictive of antifungal resistance, (2) mechanistic insights into fungal environmental sensing and host interaction pathways, and (3) open-access tools for dynamic risk assessment of fungal pathogen evolution. This work will directly inform surveillance strategies and antifungal development, bridging critical gaps between mycological research and translational applications. By integrating computational modeling with experimental validation, the project advances methodological innovation in medical mycology while addressing urgent needs in public health and food security.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of fungi, lichenous plants, eukaryotic microorganisms, myxomycetes, and plasmodiophorales and their relationship to diseases in higher plants, animals, and human beings as well as to pharmacologically useful products. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology; histopathology; fungal growth and behavior; environmental mycology; antifungal sensitivity; mycoses; pathogens and pathogenesis; pharmacological properties; and computer and laboratory research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the safety and efficiency of next-generation nuclear reactor systems through high-fidelity, multi-physics simulations enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current reactor designs face challenges in balancing performance with safety, particularly under transient conditions such as coolant loss or power surges. Traditional modeling approaches often simplify coupled physical phenomena—such as neutron transport, thermal-hydraulics, and structural mechanics—leading to conservative design margins that limit operational flexibility and economic viability. To address this, we propose developing an integrated computational framework to simulate reactor behavior at unprecedented resolution, capturing feedback mechanisms between neutronics, fluid flow, heat transfer, and material deformation in real time. The project will employ Monte Carlo methods for precise neutron transport modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for turbulent coolant flow, and finite element analysis (FEA) for stress prediction in reactor components. These tools will be coupled iteratively using in-house code to enable dynamic, multi-scale simulations. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational load, as simulations will involve billion-element meshes, probabilistic neutron tracking across 10^6 energy groups, and adaptive time-stepping over millisecond-scale transients. Expected outcomes include identifying optimal fuel configurations for reduced waste production, validating passive safety mechanisms for accident scenarios, and predicting material degradation in reactor vessels under prolonged irradiation. Results will inform regulatory guidelines and prototype testing for molten salt and small modular reactor designs, directly supporting the transition to low-carbon energy systems. Additionally, this work will establish an open-access database of benchmarked simulation cases, enhancing collaborative research in nuclear engineering. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to bridge gaps between experimental data and computational predictions, accelerating the deployment of safer, more efficient nuclear technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of research scientists and operating engineers engaged in the running of nuclear reactors, and in nuclear materials processing and disposal. Includes instruction in basic nuclear physics and nuclear engineering, monitoring and safety procedures, radioactive materials handling and disposal, equipment maintenance and operation, and record keeping.

abstract: Animal training methodologies have historically relied on heuristic approaches, with limited integration of quantitative frameworks to optimize individual learning trajectories across species and contexts. This project seeks to establish a computational foundation for personalized animal training protocols by analyzing multimodal behavioral datasets through machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling. The primary research challenge lies in decoding the high-dimensional interactions between trainer actions, environmental variables, and animal-specific learning patterns—a task requiring analysis of heterogeneous data streams (biometric sensors, movement tracking, vocalization spectra) that exceed the processing capabilities of conventional computing infrastructure. We propose developing species-specific neural networks to classify stress markers, engagement levels, and skill acquisition rates from real-time training sessions, supplemented by synthetic data generation through physiological simulations of sensory-motor learning. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallel processing of 10+ TB multimodal datasets from canine service-animal programs and marine mammal rehabilitation centers, while GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning frameworks will model optimal reward schedules under dynamic constraints. Anticipated outcomes include: 1) predictive algorithms for tailoring training intensity to individual stress thresholds, 2) generative models of interspecies communication patterns to reduce anthropomorphic bias in instruction, and 3) open-source tools for quantifying behavioral plasticity across phylogenetic lineages. By establishing quantitative benchmarks for training efficacy, this work aims to bridge ethological research with applied animal education practices while advancing computational methods for cross-species interaction analysis—an emerging niche in non-STEM disciplines requiring specialized infrastructure typically reserved for physical sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach and exercise animals for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes. Includes instruction in animal psychology, health, and safety; human-animal interaction; learning and behavior styles associated with different breeds and species; and the technical and pedagogical aspects of training animals for such specific functions as obedient household pets, performing show animals, animal athletes, caregiving (e.g., seeing-eye dogs), search and rescue, and police/security work.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of securing distributed software systems against evolving cyber threats by developing an adaptive, machine learning-driven framework for vulnerability detection and mitigation. Modern software architectures, particularly those leveraging cloud-native and microservices paradigms, face challenges in maintaining security across dynamic, interconnected components. Traditional static analysis tools struggle to scale with system size and complexity, while real-time monitoring solutions often lack predictive capabilities. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational approach combining graph-based anomaly detection, ensemble machine learning models, and automated penetration testing simulations. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to 1) process large-scale dependency graphs of software components and network traffic patterns, 2) train deep neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets of historical vulnerability reports and attack vectors, and 3) simulate distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) scenarios across virtualized network topologies. By parallelizing static code analysis, runtime behavior monitoring, and attack surface modeling across HPC nodes, the framework aims to achieve sublinear time complexity improvements compared to existing sequential methods. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated security auditing that demonstrates improved detection accuracy (targeting ≥95% recall on zero-day vulnerability prediction) and reduced false positive rates compared to current industry standards. The computational results will provide new insights into emergent attack patterns within containerized environments and contribute benchmark datasets for evaluating security solutions in large-scale distributed systems. This work directly supports the program's focus on developing practical software engineering solutions through advanced computational methods, with potential applications in healthcare data systems and financial transaction platforms requiring high-assurance security.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in developing, implementing, and evaluating computer software and program applications. Includes instruction in computer programming, programming languages, databases, user interfaces, networking and warehousing, encryption and security, software testing and evaluation, and customization.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamic interplay between family systems and societal resilience during prolonged crises, such as climate disruptions or economic instability. While family systems theory provides a framework for understanding relational and structural dynamics within families, existing models often lack the computational granularity to simulate how micro-level interactions scale to influence macro-level societal outcomes over extended periods. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework that integrates longitudinal demographic data, behavioral psychology principles, and sociohistorical case studies to simulate family decision-making processes under stress. The computational approach will involve constructing multi-layered networks representing family units, their interpersonal ties, and resource-sharing patterns, with parameters informed by anonymized census data, ethnographic records, and crisis-response literature. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model agents’ adaptive behaviors based on historical analogs, while Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes across diverse scenarios. By simulating thousands of parallel timelines under varying policy interventions and environmental pressures, this project aims to identify critical leverage points where family-level support systems could mitigate cascading societal risks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for policymakers and family therapists, predictive frameworks for resilience planning, and novel metrics quantifying the societal “carrying capacity” of family networks. The use of HPC is essential due to the combinatorial complexity of modeling nonlinear interactions across temporal scales (months to decades) and spatial scales (household to regional). This work occupies an interdisciplinary niche, merging systems theory, computational social science, and family dynamics without aligning with traditional STEM or the excluded non-STEM categories, thereby advancing methodological innovation in understudied aspects of human systems research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the family as a social unit in its developmental, dynamic, comparative, and structural aspects, and the significance of the family as a system that impacts individuals and society. Includes instruction in related principles of sociology, psychology, behavioral sciences, and the humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Ukrainian linguistics, focusing on the analysis of dialectal variation and historical text corpora. While Ukrainian dialects and literary evolution have been studied through traditional philological methods, large-scale quantitative analyses remain limited due to the computational demands of processing unstructured textual data spanning diverse regions and time periods. The research problem centers on mapping phonetic, morphological, and lexical features across digitized dialect recordings (20th–21st centuries) and early modern literary texts (16th–18th centuries) to identify patterns of language change and regional influences. Computational methods will include training transformer-based models for automated morphological tagging of non-standardized orthographies, implementing phonetic alignment algorithms for speech corpora, and conducting cluster analyses of lexical distributions across geographic and temporal dimensions. The HPC environment is critical for managing the project's scale: initial datasets comprise approximately 15 TB of text and audio recordings, requiring parallel processing for feature extraction and comparative modeling. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of annotated Ukrainian dialect features, machine learning tools optimized for historical Ukrainian texts, and quantitative models tracing the relationship between literary standardization and spoken language variants. These resources will enable novel research in Ukrainian sociolinguistics, support educational applications in language preservation, and provide methodological frameworks for under-resourced Slavic languages. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological expertise, this project aims to address gaps in digital Ukrainian studies while demonstrating how HPC capabilities can transform research paradigms in lesser-studied languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Ukrainian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Therapeutic radiologic physics faces a critical challenge in optimizing radiation dose delivery while minimizing toxicity to adjacent healthy tissues, particularly for complex tumor geometries and heterogeneous patient anatomies. Current treatment planning systems rely on simplified dose calculation algorithms that may underestimate dose deposition uncertainties in scenarios involving high-density implants, tissue interfaces, or charged particle beams. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity, GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulation framework for radiation transport modeling to improve the accuracy of dose prediction in clinically challenging cases. The computational approach will implement Geant4-based simulations with patient-specific CT-derived phantoms, incorporating dynamic motion modeling for thoracic and abdominal tumors. Machine learning methods will be integrated to generate surrogate models for rapid sensitivity analyses of beam parameters, enabling efficient exploration of multi-criteria optimization spaces. High-performance computing resources are essential to process the required 10⁹–10¹⁰ particle histories per simulation, manage terabyte-scale datasets from 4DCT imaging, and train deep neural networks on heterogeneous radiation response patterns. Expected outcomes include validated models for proton beam range uncertainty reduction in titanium implant scenarios, optimized fluence maps for spatially fractionated grid therapy, and open-source tools for GPU-accelerated secondary electron tracking. The resource-intensive simulations will directly inform clinical protocol development at our institution’s proton therapy center, with particular significance for pediatric and re-irradiation cases where millimeter-scale dose precision impacts outcomes. By establishing a computational pipeline linking first-principles physics modeling to treatment planning system inputs, this work aims to bridge the gap between research-grade dose calculation accuracy and clinically feasible implementation timelines. Results will be disseminated through the OpenDose collaboration to support benchmarking efforts across therapeutic radiologic physics programs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physical aspects of the therapeutic applications of x-rays, gamma rays, electron, and other charged particle beams, neutrons, and radiations from sealed radionuclide sources; and with the equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: Health education plays a critical role in promoting lifelong wellness, yet the development of evidence-based pedagogical strategies for training health educators remains understudied. Current approaches to evaluating teaching effectiveness in health education often rely on small-scale qualitative assessments or self-reported data, limiting the ability to generalize findings or model complex interactions between instructional methods, learner engagement, and knowledge retention. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large multimodal datasets from simulated and real-world health education classrooms. The research will employ machine learning techniques to process video recordings, biometric feedback (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate), and pre/post-assessment data from 500+ teacher candidates across diverse virtual teaching scenarios. Computational models will be developed to quantify relationships between specific teaching behaviors (e.g., questioning techniques, multimedia use), student attention patterns, and learning outcomes. A parallel agent-based modeling framework will simulate how variations in health education curricula propagate through student populations with differing socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds. By utilizing GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures and distributed memory processing, these analyses will identify optimal instructional strategies while accounting for multidimensional confounding variables. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking pedagogical approaches to competency development in health-specific domains (e.g., sexual health, substance abuse prevention), and (2) open-source tools for generating personalized training modules that adapt to teacher candidates’ evolving skills. The computational workflow will directly inform the redesign of clinical practice components in health teacher education programs, with potential to improve the scalability and efficacy of training pipelines addressing national shortages of qualified health educators.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach health education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating computational modeling and data-driven insights into STEM pedagogy for K-12 teacher preparation. Current approaches to designing STEM lesson plans often rely on static curricula or anecdotal evidence, limiting educators’ ability to dynamically adapt instruction to diverse student needs or rapidly evolving technological contexts. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate classroom learning environments, analyze multimodal educational datasets, and develop predictive models for optimizing STEM instructional strategies. Key computational tasks include large-scale agent-based modeling of student-teacher interactions, natural language processing of classroom discourse transcripts, and machine learning-driven analysis of longitudinal student performance data from 15 regional school districts. These datasets encompass structured assessments, project-based learning artifacts, and sensor-based engagement metrics from STEM labs. By parallelizing resource-intensive tasks such as hyperparameter tuning for personalized learning algorithms and 3D simulations of engineering design tasks, the HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of pedagogical models that balance conceptual rigor, inclusivity, and real-world relevance. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access repository of computationally informed STEM lesson frameworks, validated through virtual classroom simulations and comparative effectiveness studies. The project aims to advance teacher education by establishing scalable methods for embedding computational thinking into STEM instructional design while maintaining alignment with Next Generation Science Standards. Results will directly inform a graduate-level course on data-enhanced STEM pedagogy, benefiting 200+ annual enrollees in our teacher preparation program. This work bridges educational theory with computational practice, providing novel tools for educators to cultivate adaptive, evidence-based teaching practices in STEM disciplines.
cip_title: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Educational Methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to connect education practices with scientific, engineering, and mathematical principles for PreK-12 students. Includes instruction in critical thinking, curriculum and instruction, history of STEM education, integrating STEM across curricula, learning sciences and technology, STEM education methods, and teacher leadership in STEM education.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of biomechanical forces in tumor progression and therapeutic resistance within physiologically relevant microenvironments. Despite advances in cancer biology, the interplay between mechanical stress, hypoxia, and interstitial fluid pressure in driving metastatic behavior remains poorly understood. Traditional in vitro models fail to capture the dynamic complexity of these interactions, while clinical data alone cannot isolate causative biomechanical factors. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of tumor cell populations with finite element analysis (FEA) of tissue-scale mechanical properties. The ABM component will simulate cellular responses to variable stiffness, fluid shear stress, and oxygen gradients, informed by experimental data from 3D-bioprinted tumor models. Concurrently, FEA will map stress distribution patterns in patient-derived tumor geometries obtained via medical imaging. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatiotemporal interactions across scales, particularly for parameter optimization, sensitivity analyses, and validation against longitudinal clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of mechanical biomarkers predictive of invasion risk, (2) quantification of stress-mediated changes in chemoresistance pathways, and (3) a predictive platform for testing mechanotherapeutic interventions. This work will advance integrative pathobiology by bridging tissue-level biomechanics with organ-scale disease manifestations, offering novel strategies to disrupt force-dependent metastatic niches. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations of up to 10^6 interacting cells in heterogeneous environments, large-scale fluid-structure interaction computations, and machine learning-driven analysis of multiparametric output data. By elucidating how mechanical cues shape tumor evolution, this research aligns with the program’s mission to decode disease mechanisms across biological scales while directly informing translational approaches in solid tumor management.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanisms underlying human disease. Includes instruction in the causes and nature of disease processes in animals and humans at the molecular, cellular, tissue, organ and organ systems level, tissue structure and function, cellular mechanisms of disease and organ systems response to disease.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and promotional strategies for perishable and seasonal special products (e.g., artisanal foods, floral arrangements) using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex market interactions. The challenge lies in balancing real-time demand fluctuations, supply chain constraints, and profit margins for niche products with short shelf lives and highly variable consumer appeal. Traditional marketing models struggle to account for the nonlinear relationships between social media-driven demand spikes, localized inventory thresholds, and time-sensitive pricing adjustments. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based computational framework integrating real-time social sentiment analysis, supply chain telemetry, and consumer behavior simulations. The model will leverage GPU-accelerated machine learning to predict regional demand patterns from heterogeneous data streams (e.g., Instagram engagement metrics, weather data, local event calendars) while simultaneously optimizing pricing tiers and promotion schedules through Monte Carlo methods. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations across thousands of hypothetical market scenarios, enabling rapid sensitivity analysis for parameters like flash sale timing or influencer partnership ROI. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that reduces perishable product waste by 18-25% while maintaining premium pricing integrity, alongside novel metrics for quantifying the viral potential of visual-centric special products. This work bridges computational social science and operations research, advancing marketing analytics for small-batch producers in underserved sectors. By mapping how micro-influencer networks spatially propagate demand signals, the project will also yield methodological innovations in simulating decentralized marketing ecosystems—a critical capability as special product markets increasingly rely on hyper-localized, community-driven promotion strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of special products, including floristry, food, and home and office products. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: Students with specific learning disabilities (SLDs) require highly individualized instructional strategies, but designing effective interventions remains challenging due to the variability in cognitive and behavioral profiles. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale multimodal datasets—including eye-tracking, response latency, and physiological signals—collected during technology-assisted learning tasks. By applying deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models and temporal convolutional networks, we aim to identify patterns in attentional engagement, cognitive load, and error-correction behaviors that predict intervention efficacy. The computational demands of processing high-frequency temporal data (sampled at 1kHz across 500+ participants) and training ensemble models necessitate parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows. Expected outcomes include: (1) a predictive framework for matching learners with optimal instructional modalities (e.g., multisensory vs. sequential scaffolding) based on real-time biomarkers; (2) open-source tools for educators to simulate intervention impacts through synthetic learner models. This work directly addresses the critical need for data-driven personalization in special education, with potential to transform how individualized education programs (IEPs) are dynamically optimized. The proposed computational pipelines will also advance methodological integration of neuroeducational data streams at previously unfeasible temporal resolutions, enabling educators to refine scaffolding techniques while accounting for the dynamic interplay of cognitive, affective, and environmental factors in SLD populations.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Specific Learning Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with specific learning disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with specific learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with specific learning disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Cybersecurity threats continue to grow in scale and sophistication, necessitating advanced computational approaches to evaluate and optimize defense strategies in dynamic, large-scale environments. This project addresses the critical challenge of modeling multi-stage cyberattacks and defense policies in complex, interconnected systems, where traditional analytical methods fail to account for real-time adversarial behavior, network interdependencies, and cascading failures. We propose developing a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze attack-defense interactions across infrastructure sectors, including energy grids, financial systems, and government networks. Agent-based modeling will simulate threat actors’ tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), while game-theoretic models will evaluate strategic policy interventions, such as proactive threat hunting, deception technologies, and adaptive resource allocation. The computational workflow will integrate real-world datasets, including network topology maps, vulnerability databases, and incident reports, to parameterize scenarios ranging from ransomware campaigns to state-sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs). HPC resources are essential to execute parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic risk assessment, sensitivity analysis of defense policies, and optimization of response protocols under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for policy effectiveness (e.g., mean time to containment, cost-benefit ratios of cyber investments) and actionable frameworks for resilient system design. The project will also produce open-source tools for scenario generation and policy testing, enabling reproducibility and collaboration across the cybersecurity research community. By bridging computational modeling with strategic cybersecurity policy, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making for national security stakeholders, ultimately enhancing the scalability and adaptability of cyber defense mechanisms in an era of escalating digital conflict.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational comparative law framework analyzing the evolution and interaction of legal principles across civil and common law systems. The core research problem lies in the inability of traditional legal scholarship to systematically evaluate how doctrinal concepts—such as proportionality, fiduciary duty, or good faith—emerge, diverge, or converge within large-scale, multilingual corpora of judicial decisions, statutes, and scholarly commentaries. While qualitative comparative analysis dominates the field, the scale and linguistic complexity of global legal texts (spanning 50+ jurisdictions and six languages) necessitate computational methods to detect latent patterns, semantic shifts, and cross-jurisdictional influences. The project will develop a pipeline combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for semantic similarity analysis, dynamic network models to trace doctrinal migration, and phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct legal concept evolution. HPC resources are critical for training multilingual legal language models, processing terabyte-scale text datasets, and running parallelized simulations of normative diffusion across jurisdictions. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of understudied convergence points between civil and common law systems in emerging areas like digital rights and climate liability, 2) a quantitative framework for predicting legal harmonization pressures, and 3) open-access tools for mapping citation networks and conceptual analogies across legal traditions. By integrating computational social science methodologies with doctrinal legal analysis, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-driven comparative law research while addressing infrastructure gaps in non-STEM disciplines. The results will provide actionable insights for international judicial training programs and transnational policy design, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in advancing rigorous, empirically grounded legal scholarship.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of legal systems and philosophies in comparative perspective.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze the emergent dynamics of decentralized information ecosystems, with a focus on resilience against systemic manipulation. Traditional studies of information flow often prioritize network structure or content propagation in isolation, neglecting the interplay between adaptive user behavior, multi-modal data fusion, and self-organizing governance protocols. Our research addresses this gap by creating agent-based simulations that integrate machine learning-driven persona models with graph-based trust metrics and decentralized consensus mechanisms. The computational challenges include simulating millions of heterogeneous agents operating across temporal scales from real-time interactions to longitudinal behavioral shifts, requiring distributed memory architectures for state management and GPU acceleration for parallel evaluation of decision policies. We propose implementing a hybrid simulation architecture using asynchronous many-task runtime systems (AMTs) coupled with dynamic graph partitioning strategies to handle scale-free interaction patterns. Expected outcomes include: 1) quantitative metrics for ecosystem vulnerability to coordinated disinformation campaigns, 2) protocol designs for distributed fact-checking systems that preserve privacy through homomorphic encryption schemes, and 3) open-source tools enabling policy analysts to stress-test governance models under synthetic crisis scenarios. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable parameter space exploration across sociotechnical variables currently intractable on commodity cloud infrastructure, particularly in modeling the phase transitions between stable and chaotic information regimes. This work bridges computational social science with decentralized system design, offering novel methodologies for assessing digital public goods in an era of increasingly fragmented information environments.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on computing, computer science, and information science and systems. Such programs are undifferentiated as to title and content and are not to be confused with specific programs in computer science, information science, or related support services.

abstract: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) systems face complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation, response strategies, and clinical outcomes during high-acuity, time-sensitive scenarios such as mass casualty incidents (MCIs) and disasters. Current approaches to EMS system design and medical oversight often rely on retrospective data or simplified models, which inadequately capture the dynamic, multi-variable interactions inherent to prehospital care. This project proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate EMS operations under diverse crisis conditions, evaluate resource deployment strategies, and predict patient outcomes. The research will integrate real-world EMS datasets—including dispatch logs, patient care records, and geospatial traffic patterns—with agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate MCI scenarios, disaster responses, and routine EMS operations. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify patterns in clinical outcomes linked to specific resource allocation decisions, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in operational variables such as ambulance routing and hospital capacity. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, run thousands of parallelized simulations, and train predictive models with high-dimensional inputs. Expected outcomes include evidence-based protocols for optimizing EMS triage hierarchies, dynamic resource redistribution during crises, and data-driven tools for medical directors to evaluate system performance. This work will advance the integration of computational analytics into EMS leadership, enabling proactive system design, enhanced clinical oversight, and improved resilience in emergency care delivery. By bridging gaps between operational data and decision-making, the project aims to reduce preventable morbidity in prehospital settings and strengthen disaster preparedness frameworks.
cip_definition: Research focused on the leadership and medical oversight of pre- and out-of-hospital emergency care systems with advanced competencies in Emergency Medical System (EMS) system design, administration, and clinical care. Includes instruction in clinical aspects of EMS, medical oversight of EMS, mass casualty management, disaster planning and operations, wilderness EMS systems, and quality management and research.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance protocols for aging aircraft airframes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Aircraft structural components, including sheet metal assemblies, control surfaces, and hydraulic systems, are subject to complex, multi-physics degradation processes influenced by operational loads, environmental exposure, and material fatigue. Current maintenance schedules often rely on conservative, time-based inspections that may miss emerging defects or inefficiently allocate resources. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven approach trained on high-fidelity simulations of airframe degradation mechanisms. Finite element analysis (FEA) models will simulate stress distribution, crack propagation, and corrosion effects across heterogeneous materials (aluminum alloys, composites, etc.), while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model aerodynamic loading and moisture ingress scenarios. These multi-scale simulations will generate synthetic training data for neural networks designed to predict failure risks based on operational history and sensor inputs. The HPC environment is critical due to the computational intensity of simulating large airframe sections at micron-scale resolution for material fatigue analysis, coupled with the need for ensemble modeling across diverse environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include a digital twin framework capable of recommending component-specific inspection intervals and repair priorities, reducing unplanned downtime by an estimated 15-20% in legacy aircraft fleets. This work aligns with FAA initiatives to integrate data-driven maintenance strategies while preserving safety margins. By leveraging parallel computing architectures, the project aims to overcome current limitations in modeling localized damage progression across full-scale airframe geometries, ultimately contributing to extended service lifetimes and cost-effective maintenance practices in aviation.
cip_title: Airframe Mechanics and Aircraft Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all aircraft components other than engines, propellers, avionics, and instruments. Includes instruction in layout and fabrication of sheet metal, fabric, wood, and other materials into structural members, parts, and fittings, and replacement of damaged or worn parts such as control cables and hydraulic units.

abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation remains a critical intervention for children with end-stage liver disease, yet significant challenges persist in predicting post-transplant outcomes and optimizing immunosuppressive regimens. Current clinical decision-making relies on static biomarkers and limited phenotypic data, which inadequately capture the complex interplay of immunological, metabolic, and genomic factors influencing graft survival. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing predictive computational models that integrate multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with longitudinal clinical records from pediatric transplant recipients. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ machine learning frameworks to analyze high-dimensional datasets from a multicenter cohort of 1,200 patients, including rare post-transplant complications such as biliary strictures and antibody-mediated rejection. Computational workflows will include ensemble learning for risk stratification, neural networks to identify nonlinear interactions between immunosuppression levels and immune cell profiles, and agent-based simulations of immune response dynamics. The scale of data—spanning >50,000 genomic variants, longitudinal cytokine measurements, and electronic health record parameters—necessitates distributed computing for feature selection, model training, and validation. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated algorithm to predict graft rejection risk within the first post-transplant year, (2) optimization protocols for personalized immunosuppression dosing based on real-time immune monitoring, and (3) identification of novel biomarkers for early detection of fibrotic graft injury. By enabling rapid analysis of heterogeneous data streams, HPC resources will accelerate translational insights into pediatric-specific immunological tolerance mechanisms, directly addressing the urgent need for evidence-based strategies to improve long-term outcomes in this vulnerable population. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for pediatric transplant centers and integrated into clinical trial designs for targeted immunosuppressive therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge, skill, and expertise required of pediatric gastroenterologists to care for children and young adults prior to and following hepatic transplantation.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex, large-scale datasets on household financial decision-making in the context of emerging decentralized digital economies. The study focuses on behavioral patterns and economic trade-offs in consumer adoption of blockchain-based financial tools, such as non-custodial wallets and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), which operate outside traditional banking systems. Current models in family and consumer economics lack the computational granularity to simulate dynamic interactions between heterogeneous household actors, rapidly evolving decentralized technologies, and volatile cryptocurrency markets. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling framework that integrates behavioral economic principles, transaction ledger analysis, and machine learning-driven sentiment parsing from niche online communities. The computational workflow will involve parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to stress-test household financial resilience under varying adoption scenarios, coupled with graph neural networks to map information diffusion pathways influencing consumer trust. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds in decentralized tool adoption that destabilize household liquidity, (2) predictive metrics for technology acceptance factors in demographically diverse families, and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating consumer behavior in Web3 ecosystems. By combining unconventional data sources—including on-chain transaction records and pseudonymous forum interactions—with novel computational methods, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying consumer economics in technologically disruptive environments. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets, running computationally intensive sensitivity analyses across 10^5 agent variations, and training deep learning models on non-Euclidean financial interaction graphs. Results will provide actionable insights for policymakers navigating regulatory challenges in decentralized finance while advancing computational social science methodologies in understudied domains of consumer economics.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Economics and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer economics and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives and linguistic patterns across Slavic communities through computational analysis of large-scale textual and archival datasets. Slavic Studies faces a critical challenge in synthesizing fragmented historical records, multilingual primary sources, and diasporic cultural production into cohesive analyses of identity formation and cross-regional exchange. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the volume and linguistic diversity of materials, particularly when tracing transnational influences or long-term shifts in discursive frameworks. Our research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze a curated corpus of 19th–21st century Slavic literary texts, periodicals, folkloric collections, and émigré publications, encompassing over 15 languages and non-standard orthographies. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical Slavic languages, we will quantify lexical borrowings, semantic shifts, and narrative structures across temporal and geographic axes. Network analysis will model the diffusion of motifs through migration pathways and political borders, while transformer-based models will identify latent patterns in representations of collective memory. The computational workload requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including OCR correction for Cyrillic and Glagolitic scripts, cross-lingual embedding alignment, and dynamic topic modeling across century-long timespans. Expected outcomes include 1) a geotemporal map of narrative transmission linking Baltic, Balkan, and Eurasian Slavic groups, 2) quantitative evidence for understudied intercultural contact zones, and 3) open-access tools for diachronic Slavic text analysis. This work will provide the first computational framework to systematically trace how vernacular traditions adapted to state-building projects, displacement events, and technological modernization, offering new empirical foundations for debates about cultural cohesion in Slavic Studies. The requested resources will enable processing efficiencies impossible on local clusters, particularly for memory-intensive alignment of multilingual embeddings and GPU-accelerated training of custom language models.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Slavic peoples inhabiting Europe, Asia, and in immigrant groups elsewhere, including the study of the emergence and migration patterns of Slavic culture, languages, and populations.

abstract: This project proposes a computational investigation into the linguistic and structural evolution of Jewish liturgical poetry (piyyutim) across medieval Mediterranean communities, integrating textual analysis with cultural history. While piyyutim served as central vehicles for theological and communal expression, their adaptation patterns remain understudied due to the scale of manuscripts, dialectal diversity in Hebrew/Aramaic hybrid texts, and nonlinear transmission paths.
