The research will develop machine learning models to analyze 8,000+ digitized piyyut texts from Cairo Genizah fragments and European manuscripts (8th–15th centuries), employing HPC resources for three parallel workflows: 1) neural OCR refinement of challenging Judeo-Arabic scribal hands using vision transformers, 2) multilingual semantic segmentation to disentangle Hebrew liturgical formulae from vernacular glosses and meta-commentary, and 3) phylogenetic network modeling of poetic meter variations correlated with diaspora migration routes. Custom transformer architectures will be trained to detect intertextual references to Talmudic vs. contemporary philosophical sources, testing hypotheses about liturgical acculturation. The computational pipeline requires large-scale GPU clusters for training domain-specific language models on non-standard Hebrew morphosyntax and CPU-intensive Monte Carlo simulations for textual phylogenetics. Outcomes will include the first comprehensive digital typology of piyyutim genres linked to historical contexts, a publicly accessible analysis toolkit for liturgical studies, and quantitative evidence reevaluating the role of women’s oral traditions in preserving poetic variants. This interdisciplinary methodology advances both Jewish cultural heritage preservation and computational humanities approaches to ritual texts, offering new paradigms for studying how liturgical forms negotiate religious authority and communal identity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as Rabbis. Includes instruction in Talmud, Halacha, Liturgy and Rituals, Rabbinical Thought, Jewish Ethics, Jewish Education, Pastoral Counseling and Homiletics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive radar signal processing frameworks for contested electromagnetic environments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Modern military radar systems face escalating challenges from dynamic interference, spectrum congestion, and adversarial countermeasures, necessitating real-time, intelligent signal adaptation. However, existing optimization methods struggle to balance computational efficiency with the fidelity required for multi-domain operational scenarios. The research addresses this gap by developing a hybrid computational architecture integrating machine learning-driven predictive models with physics-based radar simulations. Key objectives include (1) simulating high-resolution, multi-sensor radar environments under diverse interference profiles, (2) training neural networks to predict optimal waveform and filtering parameters, and (3) validating adaptive control algorithms through hardware-in-the-loop virtual testing. The computational approach combines Monte Carlo simulations of radar cross-section variability, finite-difference time-domain modeling of propagation effects, and parallelized reinforcement learning for policy optimization. HPC resources are critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of threat scenarios, particularly when modeling coordinated electronic warfare attacks across terrestrial and airborne platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for rapid radar configuration prototyping and quantitative benchmarks comparing algorithmic adaptability against conventional rule-based systems. This work directly supports next-generation cognitive radar development by establishing computationally tractable methods for maintaining detection performance in spectrally contested battlespaces. Successful implementation will provide validated models for transitioning machine learning capabilities to fielded systems while maintaining compliance with military spectrum regulations and operational security constraints.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of air, sea and ground-based radar systems. Includes instruction in electronic principles and digital techniques, transistors and solid-state component theory, radar systems; maintenance technology, data processing systems, wiring and circuit schematics, maintenance management, safety procedures, and applications to specific systems and services.

abstract: Radiological imaging data are growing in complexity and volume, driven by advancements in multi-parametric and multi-modal acquisition techniques. However, conventional computational methods struggle to efficiently process and analyze these large-scale datasets, limiting the development of robust tools for disease diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to accelerate the analysis of heterogeneous radiological data, including dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging, and radiomic features extracted from CT and PET scans. The core challenge lies in integrating multi-dimensional imaging data with clinical variables while addressing computational bottlenecks in feature extraction, model training, and validation. We will employ distributed computing strategies to parallelize image preprocessing pipelines, optimize memory-intensive radiomic feature calculations, and train deep learning architectures for tumor phenotyping and outcome prediction. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of ensemble models combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image analysis and graph-based methods for capturing spatial relationships within lesions. Validation will involve multi-institutional datasets from oncology cohorts, requiring scalable workflows to handle >50,000 imaging studies and associated metadata. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source computational platform for large-scale radiological data integration, (2) validated predictive models for glioblastoma progression and lung cancer treatment response, and (3) benchmarks comparing HPC-optimized algorithms against conventional methods in processing speed and predictive accuracy. This work will directly address current limitations in translating quantitative imaging biomarkers into clinical practice by providing the computational infrastructure needed to analyze complex radiological data at scale. Successful implementation could reduce time-to-insight for imaging research by orders of magnitude while enabling discovery of novel biomarkers through analysis of previously intractable datasets. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated computations, distributed storage for intermediate outputs, and high-throughput job scheduling essential for reproducible radiomics research.
cip_definition: Research focused on Radiology

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in large-scale, cross-cultural analyses of folklore as dynamic expressions of collective identity and creativity. While folklore studies have traditionally relied on qualitative methods, the increasing availability of digitized oral histories, folk narratives, and performance records from diverse communities presents an opportunity to systematically investigate patterns of aesthetic adaptation and cultural transmission. However, analyzing these heterogeneous datasets—spanning multilingual texts, audiovisual materials, and ethnographic metadata—requires computational resources beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource languages and dialectal variations to trace motif distributions across regional folklore corpora. Concurrently, graph-based algorithms will model the nonlinear dissemination of narrative elements through social and kinship networks inferred from ethnographic records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on fragmented or non-standardized textual data, running multilevel simulations of cultural exchange dynamics, and processing high-resolution audiovisual materials documenting performative traditions. Expected outcomes include: (1) a scalable framework for identifying understudied intersections between gender roles and genre evolution in folk narratives; (2) computational evidence for how marginalized communities reconfigure shared folklore motifs during cultural disruptions; and (3) open-access tools tailored for ethically sourcing and analyzing Indigenous knowledge systems. By enabling the integration of previously siloed regional collections, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for preserving intangible cultural heritage while centering the agency of tradition-bearers in large-scale analyses. The requested resources directly support the program’s mandate to investigate creativity as a socially embedded practice, offering new paradigms for studying cultural resilience without relying on anthropological or sociological paradigms.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of creativity and aesthetic expression in everyday life, as expressed in narrative, literature, performing arts, culture, work, family and community.

abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are critical reservoirs of biodiversity and provide essential ecosystem services, yet they face escalating threats from climate change, eutrophication, and habitat fragmentation. A persistent challenge in aquatic ecology lies in disentangling the complex, nonlinear interactions between environmental stressors and the population dynamics of freshwater organisms across spatial and temporal scales. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model multi-trophic interactions in lake ecosystems, with a focus on how temperature gradients, nutrient loading, and invasive species alter community structure and ecosystem resilience. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate agent-based models (ABMs) with spatially explicit hydrological data and long-term ecological datasets to simulate scenarios of environmental change. The ABMs will parameterize species-specific responses for key taxa—including phytoplankton, zooplankton, and fish—using empirical data on metabolic rates, dispersal behavior, and trophic interactions. Parallelized simulations will enable probabilistic assessments of tipping points in water quality and biodiversity loss under varying management strategies. Additionally, machine learning pipelines will identify emergent patterns in community assembly and functional trait shifts across heterogeneous habitats. By quantifying feedbacks between physicochemical drivers and evolutionary adaptations, this work will advance predictive capacity for conserving freshwater biodiversity in a changing climate. The computational outputs will directly inform regional fisheries management plans and prioritize habitats for restoration. Access to HPC resources is essential given the high dimensionality of ecological networks, the need for stochastic parameterization across thousands of iterations, and the integration of multi-terabyte remote sensing datasets. This project bridges theoretical ecology and applied resource management, providing a scalable toolkit to address urgent challenges in aquatic ecosystem sustainability.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting inland fresh waters such as lakes, ponds, rivers, creeks, estuaries, and wetlands. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; aquatic ecosystems; microbiology; mycology; botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; population biology and biodiversity; studies of specific species, phyla, and habitats; and applications to fields such as natural resources conservation, fisheries science, and biotechnology.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an integrative computational framework to optimize decision-making for agribusinesses facing dynamic risks from climate variability, market fluctuations, and supply chain disruptions. Current agricultural business models often rely on static or compartmentalized data, limiting their ability to adapt to real-time challenges such as extreme weather events, commodity price volatility, or livestock disease outbreaks. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build a scalable, multi-agent simulation platform that synthesizes heterogeneous datasets—including historical climate records, real-time satellite imagery, IoT sensor outputs from farm equipment, and global market trends—into predictive analytics. The computational approach will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between stakeholders (e.g., producers, distributors, retailers) and hybrid machine learning techniques to forecast short- and long-term agricultural outcomes. Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in yield predictions, while graph-based algorithms will optimize logistics for resilient supply chains. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to reduce model runtime by 70–80% compared to existing tools, enabling near-real-time scenario testing for farm managers and corporate planners. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool for evaluating trade-offs in resource allocation, risk mitigation strategies, and sustainability metrics. The framework will be validated through case studies focused on midwestern U.S. grain cooperatives and poultry supply networks in Southeast Asia, with results directly applicable to improving operational efficiency, reducing financial losses from disruptions, and balancing profitability with environmental stewardship. This work bridges computational innovation and agribusiness management, offering scalable solutions to enhance food system resilience in a rapidly changing global economy.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage agricultural businesses and agriculturally related operations within diversified corporations. Includes instruction in agriculture, agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, finance, marketing, planning, human resources management, and other managerial responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociocultural dynamics of fan engagement in global esports communities, a rapidly growing domain within Sports Studies that intersects with digital humanities, behavioral psychology, and data science. While traditional sports research has focused on physical activity and institutional structures, the rise of esports—a hybrid of competitive gaming, entertainment, and online social ecosystems—presents novel challenges in understanding decentralized, transnational fan networks. The research problem centers on mapping and modeling the emotional, ideological, and identity-based drivers of participation in these communities, which generate petabytes of unstructured data across streaming platforms, forums, and in-game interactions. Current methodologies lack the computational capacity to process this scale of multimodal data while preserving the temporal and contextual nuances critical to sociological interpretation. The proposed computational approach combines transformer-based natural language processing for sentiment and discourse analysis, graph neural networks to model community hierarchies and influence patterns, and agent-based simulations to test theories of collective behavior under varying cultural and regulatory scenarios. By deploying these methods on HPC infrastructure, the project will process over 10 terabytes of multilingual text, audio-visual streams, and gameplay telemetry from five major esports titles, enabling comparative cross-cultural analysis at unprecedented resolution. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting community responses to ethical controversies (e.g., athlete misconduct, governance disputes) and a public dashboard visualizing real-time sentiment shifts during international tournaments. This work will advance Sports Studies by establishing computational social science techniques tailored to digital-native athletic phenomena, while providing stakeholders with evidence-based strategies to address toxicity, inclusivity gaps, and geopolitical tensions in global esports ecosystems.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological, sociological, and historical aspects of sport and physical activity. Includes instruction in theory of sport, sport psychology, sport in American society, gender and race/ethnicity and sport, and sports history.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the construction and evolution of cultural narratives within Latinx digital media, with a focus on Mexican-American/Chicano and Puerto Rican communities. The research problem centers on understanding how intersecting identities—such as ethnicity, gender, and migration experiences—are dynamically represented in online platforms, including social media, digital archives, and community-driven literary publications. Traditional qualitative methods have provided foundational insights but are limited in scalability, particularly when examining vast, multilingual corpora that reflect the diversity of Latinx voices. This project will apply natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to systematically identify patterns in linguistic expression, thematic emphasis, and discursive shifts across time and subgroups. Key computational tasks include sentiment analysis to trace emotional valence in narratives related to cultural resistance and belonging, topic modeling to map recurring themes (e.g., hybrid identity, intergenerational memory), and semantic network analysis to uncover connections between cultural symbols and sociopolitical contexts. The dataset comprises over 5 million text entries from publicly accessible forums, curated digital archives (e.g., Chicano poetry collections, Puerto Rican activist blogs), and ethically sourced social media posts. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models capable of handling code-switching (Spanish/English) and dialectal variations, as well as for parallel processing of high-dimensional text data. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational framework for analyzing cultural narratives in underrepresented communities, a longitudinal dataset tracking thematic evolution from 1990 to present, and visualizations highlighting regional and generational differences in identity expression. By bridging computational methods with cultural theory, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary scholarship on Latinx cultural production while providing actionable insights for community organizations and educational initiatives focused on preserving diasporic heritage.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Hispanic-American, Puerto Rican, Latinx, and Mexican-American/ Chicano Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic American immigrant populations within the U.S. and Canada, including Mexican-American Studies, Cuban American Studies, Puerto Rican Studies, and others.

abstract: Endocrine signaling plays a central role in physiological regulation and cancer progression, yet the dynamic interplay between hormone-secreting cells, receptor activation, and downstream signaling networks remains poorly quantified in complex tissues. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding how spatially heterogeneous endocrine microenvironments influence tumor evolution and therapy resistance, with a focus on hormone-responsive cancers such as breast and prostate malignancies. Current experimental models struggle to capture the multiscale dynamics of endocrine signaling—from intracellular protein secretion kinetics to intercellular communication across tumor-stroma interfaces—limiting predictive insights into microenvironment-driven treatment outcomes. We propose an integrative computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model endocrine signaling networks across cellular, tissue, and organismal scales. Agent-based models will simulate hormone gradient formation and receptor activation patterns in 3D tumor architectures derived from clinical imaging data, while coupled ordinary differential equation systems will predict time-resolved protein secretion dynamics under genetic and metabolic perturbations. Machine learning pipelines will analyze single-cell transcriptomic datasets from patient-derived xenografts to identify endocrine signaling states correlated with metastatic progression. The HPC environment is essential for parameterizing these models using high-resolution microscopy, bulk RNA sequencing, and proteomic datasets (>20 TB across cohorts), as well as for executing ensemble simulations to quantify microenvironmental variability. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of endocrine signaling crosstalk in therapy-resistant tumor niches and mechanistic insights into how stromal-endocrine interactions drive cancer cell plasticity. This work will establish scalable computational tools to optimize hormone-targeted therapies while advancing systems-level paradigms for endocrine physiology research. By bridging spatial biology with dynamic network modeling, the project addresses NIH priorities in cancer systems medicine and provides an open-source framework for simulating endocrine microenvironments in diverse pathological contexts.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition, manufacture, and secretion of protein compounds by cells and glands and the role of endocrine substances in bodily processes. Includes instruction in protein chemistry, protein secretion, membrane biogenesis and transfer methods, cellular communication, gene and cell regulation, cytochemistry, fractionation, radioautography, and applications such as neuroendocrinology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the development of advanced biomedical technologies through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of complex biological systems and medical device interactions. Current limitations in computational power restrict the resolution and scale of models used to optimize implantable devices, biosensors, and therapeutic delivery systems, often leading to oversimplified assumptions about dynamic biological environments. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging HPC resources to execute multi-scale simulations integrating molecular dynamics, finite element analysis, and fluid-structure interaction modeling. These methods will enable real-time analysis of biomechanical stress distributions in cardiovascular stents, protein-ligand binding kinetics for targeted drug delivery nanoparticles, and hemodynamic patterns in artificial organ prototypes. A key innovation involves coupling machine learning algorithms with physics-based models to predict long-term biocompatibility and failure modes of biomedical devices under physiological conditions. The computational workflows will utilize parallelized codebases optimized for GPU-accelerated nodes, enabling parameter sweeps across design variations and biological variability. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal material configurations for neural interface electrodes, validated predictive models of inflammatory responses to synthetic implants, and data-driven protocols for calibrating biosensor arrays. By bridging high-fidelity simulations with experimental validation, this work will accelerate the translation of robust biomedical technologies into clinical applications while reducing reliance on iterative physical prototyping. The resulting open-source computational tools and datasets will provide the broader research community with frameworks to advance personalized medical device development and precision therapeutic systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing biological or medical systems and products. Includes instruction in instrument calibration, design and installation testing, system safety and maintenance procedures, procurement and installation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in American Indian and Native American Studies, focusing on the digital revitalization and analysis of endangered Indigenous cultural heritage. The research problem centers on the urgent need to process, preserve, and interpret vast, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized oral histories, ethnographic recordings, and multilingual textual archives—many of which remain underutilized due to computational limitations. Current methodologies lack the capacity to efficiently analyze non-linear narratives, contextualize intergenerational knowledge transfers, or map spatial-temporal relationships within these materials, particularly for smaller or marginalized Native communities whose records are often fragmented. The proposed computational approach integrates machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and geospatial modeling to develop scalable tools for pattern recognition in oral traditions, automated transcription of Indigenous languages, and 3D reconstructions of culturally significant sites from archival imagery. Custom algorithms will be designed to prioritize community-defined ethical frameworks, ensuring data sovereignty and minimizing extractive practices. By parallelizing workflows across HPC clusters, the project aims to process terabytes of audio-visual data and centuries of intertribal exchange records, enabling comparative studies of cultural resilience and adaptation. Expected outcomes include open-source computational models tailored to Indigenous epistemologies, a collaborative digital repository co-designed with Native stakeholders, and new interdisciplinary frameworks for analyzing cultural continuity in the face of colonialism. This work directly supports Tribal nations in reclaiming endangered knowledge systems while advancing scholarship that centers Native perspectives. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s data-intensive demands, which exceed the capabilities of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the American Indian, Aleut, Inuit, Hawaiian and other native peoples of the Americas from earliest times until the present, with particular emphasis on U.S. and Canadian populations and their problems but including reference to Caribbean and Latin American native peoples.

abstract: The proposed research project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms of neuropharmacological agents targeting neurotransmitter receptors implicated in neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders. Despite advances in identifying candidate drugs, predicting their dynamic interactions with neural receptors and downstream signaling pathways remains challenging due to the complexity of brain-specific pharmacokinetics and the limited resolution of traditional experimental models. This project aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate drug-receptor binding dynamics, allosteric modulation, and functional outcomes in heterogeneous neural environments. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will be conducted using optimized force fields to capture atomic-level interactions of small molecules with G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and ion channels over biologically relevant timescales. Machine learning frameworks will integrate MD trajectories with experimental pharmacokinetic data to predict blood-brain barrier penetration, off-target effects, and dose-response relationships. The computational pipeline will further employ ensemble docking strategies to screen compound libraries against receptor conformations associated with disease states, such as hyperactive NMDA receptors in Alzheimer’s disease or dysregulated dopamine receptors in schizophrenia. By utilizing GPU-accelerated HPC clusters, these resource-intensive simulations will achieve the sampling depth required to resolve rare conformational states and stochastic binding events. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel lead compounds with improved selectivity, the characterization of drug-induced neural signaling cascades, and predictive models of neurotoxicity risk. This work will directly inform preclinical drug development, reduce reliance on low-throughput in vivo screening, and advance personalized therapeutic strategies for neurological conditions with high unmet clinical need. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome current limitations in processing power and data storage, enabling iterative modeling of complex neuropharmacological systems at unprecedented resolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drugs that modify the function of the brain and central nervous system, the effects of such drugs on health, disease, perception, motor action, and behavior; and the development of countermeasures and treatment therapies. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, behavioral neuroscience, neurobiochemistry, neuropathology, the mechanisms of brain function, medicinal chemistry, pharmaceutics, and studies of specific drugs and drug therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resilient supply chain networks under dynamic disruptions, such as geopolitical shifts, environmental crises, or pandemics. Current models often lack the scalability to handle real-time data integration, multi-echelon inventory dependencies, and nonlinear risk propagation across global networks. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining agent-based simulation, stochastic optimization, and machine learning. The research will model supply chains as complex adaptive systems, with agents representing suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, and retailers interacting under uncertainty. Computational experiments will evaluate scenarios including demand surges, transportation bottlenecks, and supplier failures, using historical disruption data and synthetic datasets reflecting emerging risks. Key algorithms will include parallelized Monte Carlo methods for risk quantification, graph neural networks to predict cascading delays, and multi-objective optimization to balance cost, service levels, and carbon footprint. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale logistics datasets, including IoT sensor feeds, vendor lead times, and customs clearance records. Expected outcomes include: (1) a decision support tool for dynamic resource reallocation during disruptions, (2) quantitative metrics for supply chain resilience tailored to industry-specific constraints, and (3) open-source benchmarks for large-scale logistics simulation. This work will advance academic understanding of disruption propagation in multi-tier networks while providing actionable insights for enterprises managing globalized supply chains. The computational demands—particularly the need for distributed memory parallelism in optimization routines and GPU acceleration for deep reinforcement learning components—necessitate dedicated HPC resources beyond standard institutional computing capacities. Successful implementation will directly inform curriculum development in supply chain analytics and sustainable operations management within the program.
cip_title: Logistics, Materials, and Supply Chain Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and coordinate all logistical functions in an enterprise, ranging from acquisitions to receiving and handling, through internal allocation of resources to operations units, to the handling and delivery of output. Includes instruction in acquisitions and purchasing, inventory control, storage and handling, just-in-time manufacturing, logistics planning, shipping and delivery management, transportation, quality control, resource estimation and allocation, and budgeting.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to predict the coupled hydro-mechanical behavior of unsaturated soils in geoenvironmental systems, with a focus on optimizing the design of waste containment structures under dynamic environmental loads. The research addresses critical gaps in modeling fluid flow and deformation interactions in heterogeneous, partially saturated soils, which are central to the long-term stability of landfills, embankments, and other earth-supported systems. Current analytical methods often oversimplify soil anisotropy, time-dependent cracking, and preferential flow pathways, leading to unreliable predictions of contaminant transport or structural failure. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) with discrete fracture network simulations and machine learning-based parameter optimization. The models will incorporate real-world data from geophysical surveys and laboratory triaxial tests to capture multi-phase flow, soil-structure interaction, and cyclic wetting-drying effects. HPC resources are essential to resolve the computational intensity of 3D transient analyses across varying spatial scales (microstructural pore networks to macro-scale landfill systems) and temporal scales (minutes to decades). Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for predicting crack propagation in clay liners, quantifying leachate migration risks, and evaluating the performance of geosynthetic clay liners under seismic loading. The research will directly inform the design of next-generation waste containment systems, reducing environmental contamination risks while enhancing resilience to climate-induced hydrological extremes. By enabling large-scale parallelized simulations of coupled processes, this work advances foundational knowledge in geoenvironmental engineering and supports regulatory decision-making for sustainable infrastructure. The requested computing resources will facilitate parameter sensitivity studies, stochastic uncertainty quantification, and high-resolution visualization of failure mechanisms—tasks infeasible with standard institutional computing capacities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply geotechnical engineering methods, which deal with the analysis, design and construction of earth and earth supported structures, to the application of environmental problems, such as waste containment, waste disposal, construction of land fills, soil permeation, soil analysis, and soil improvement. Includes instruction in soil mechanics, soil dynamics, soil behavior, waste management and containment systems, geosynthetics, geochemistry, earth structures, geoenvironmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, earthquake engineering, and foundation engineering

abstract: The controlled use of explosives in construction and demolition projects requires precise optimization of blast parameters to ensure safety, efficiency, and environmental compliance. Current empirical methods for blast design often rely on trial-and-error approaches, which can lead to suboptimal outcomes, including excessive vibration, unintended rock fragmentation, and collateral structural damage. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate explosive-material interactions and predict blast outcomes under diverse geological and operational conditions. The research problem centers on the lack of robust, physics-informed tools capable of dynamically integrating variables such as charge distribution, detonation timing, material heterogeneity, and environmental constraints. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute multi-physics simulations combining finite element analysis (FEA), smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), and machine learning (ML). The computational framework will model shockwave propagation, fracture dynamics, and debris dispersion at scale, incorporating real-world data from sensor arrays and historical blast records. Parametric studies will systematically evaluate the sensitivity of outcomes to input variables, enabling the derivation of optimized blast patterns. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for minimizing overbreak and vibration, a digital twin platform for virtual blast testing, and data-driven guidelines for charge placement in complex terrains. The project’s significance lies in its potential to reduce material waste, enhance worker safety, and mitigate environmental risks in blasting operations. By transitioning from empirical to computational-first methodologies, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for precision blasting, with applications in infrastructure development, mining, and hazardous site remediation. The scalability of the proposed models, enabled by HPC, will support real-time decision-making and foster innovation in a field historically constrained by physical experimentation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in using a variety of explosive materials to aid in the construction process. Includes instruction in safety procedures for storing, handling, placement, charge power determination, drilling, pounding, building demolition, preparing rocky surfaces for building foundations and demolition of explosives.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of quantifying and optimizing movement therapy interventions through advanced computational modeling of neuromuscular and biomechanical processes. Movement therapy relies on nuanced, individualized interactions between practitioners and clients to enhance somatic awareness and functional movement patterns. However, current methods for assessing therapeutic efficacy remain largely qualitative, limiting scalability and evidence-based refinement of techniques. We propose developing a high-resolution simulation framework to model neuromuscular responses to therapeutic touch and guided movement, integrating motion capture data, electromyography (EMG), and pressure sensor inputs from clinical sessions. High-performance computing resources will enable the creation of multi-scale models that correlate external biomechanical forces with internal tissue strain, proprioceptive feedback, and cortical activation patterns derived from existing neuroimaging datasets. Machine learning approaches will identify critical kinematic and temporal features predictive of therapeutic outcomes across diverse populations, including individuals with chronic pain or movement disorders. The computational pipeline will also simulate hypothetical intervention scenarios to test mechanistic hypotheses about sensorimotor integration during therapy. By bridging embodied therapeutic practices with systems biology and computational neuroscience, this work aims to establish predictive biomarkers for treatment efficacy, inform personalized intervention protocols, and generate open-access tools for movement educators. Expected outcomes include a novel ontology for classifying movement therapy modalities based on computational signatures and a proof-of-concept platform for virtual therapy prototyping. This interdisciplinary approach advances the scientific rigor of somatic practices while preserving their human-centered ethos, offering new pathways to validate and innovate within movement-based therapeutic traditions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use functional and expressive integration strategies to help promote somatic awareness and optimal psychophysical functioning. Includes instruction in skilled touch techniques, kinesthetic awareness processes, movement observation, patterning, client assessment and guidance, verbal and nonverbal communication, practice management, professional standards and ethics, and specific therapeutic and educational modalities

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interplay between public fiscal policies and decentralized financial networks, with a focus on optimizing resource allocation in municipal debt markets. Public finance institutions increasingly face challenges in managing multi-layered fiscal ecosystems where traditional budget projection tools fail to account for real-time market volatility, interjurisdictional dependencies, and emergent decentralized finance (DeFi) instruments. The core research problem lies in creating predictive models that integrate stochastic public revenue forecasting with network effects arising from cross-municipal bond market interactions—a gap not addressed by conventional linear budgeting approaches. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the project will implement a hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) system combined with Monte Carlo simulations to capture nonlinear fiscal cascades and systemic risk propagation. The ABM component will simulate interactions between municipal entities, institutional investors, and retail participants across 10,000+ node networks, while deep reinforcement learning modules will test adaptive policy interventions under varying macroeconomic shock scenarios. Computational demands stem from the need to process high-frequency financial data streams, optimize multi-objective fiscal constraints (liquidity vs. sustainability), and quantify second-order effects of regulatory arbitrage in DeFi-collateralized public instruments. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for stress-testing municipal debt portfolios against climate transition risks and interest rate shockwaves, as well as novel metrics for assessing the systemic stability of hybrid public-private fiscal architectures. By enabling granular, real-time analysis of complex fiscal networks, this research aims to redefine how public agencies evaluate long-term liability management in an era of financial digitization and interconnected crises.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the financial assets and budgets of public sector organizations. Includes instruction in public trusts and investments; the laws and procedures used to plan, prepare and administer public agency budgets; and the preparation and analysis of public budget projections and policies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of educational assessments, driven by digital learning environments and adaptive testing platforms, demands advanced computational methods to analyze high-dimensional response data, optimize test designs, and ensure valid interpretations. Traditional psychometric approaches often struggle to scale with modern datasets containing millions of interactions, fine-grained process data (e.g., clickstreams, response latencies), and complex item types. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning-enhanced psychometric models for large-scale educational assessments. The research will focus on two interrelated challenges: (1) improving the detection of aberrant response patterns in computer-based diagnostic assessments using deep learning architectures, and (2) optimizing automated essay scoring systems through ensemble models that integrate natural language processing with cognitive writing features. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized parameter estimation for mixed-effects item response theory (IRT) models, Monte Carlo simulations for testing differential item functioning across diverse populations, and hyperparameter tuning for neural networks trained on multimodal assessment data. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive operations involving tens of millions of student-item interactions from state longitudinal databases and international assessments (e.g., PISA, NAEP). Expected outcomes include open-source software packages for scalable psychometric analysis, evidence-based guidelines for deploying computationally intensive measurement models in operational testing contexts, and novel validity indices for AI-driven assessment systems. This work directly addresses the need for robust computational infrastructure in educational measurement research, enabling innovations that balance statistical rigor with practical constraints in real-world testing environments. Findings will inform the development of fairer, more adaptive assessments while establishing methodological frameworks for handling emergent data types in digital learning ecosystems.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for designing, developing, implementing and evaluating tests and other mechanisms used to measure learning, evaluate student progress, and assess the performance of specific teaching tools, strategies and curricula. Includes instruction in psychometric measurement, instrument design, test implementation techniques, research evaluation, data reporting requirements, and data analysis and interpretation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting the impacts of climate change and anthropogenic pressures on habitat connectivity and biodiversity across heterogeneous landscapes. Current models often lack the spatial resolution and computational scalability to integrate dynamic socioecological variables—such as shifting land-use patterns, species dispersal behaviors, and policy-driven resource allocation—across regional to continental scales. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that couples mechanistic species distribution models with agent-based simulations of human decision-making. The research will utilize remotely sensed environmental data, climate projections under multiple emissions scenarios, and stakeholder-derived policy constraints to simulate future habitat fragmentation risks for keystone species in North American boreal and temperate forests. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized processing for spatially explicit, fine-grained simulations (1 km² resolution) across decadal timescales, while machine learning techniques will optimize parameterization and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of habitat vulnerability under alternative management policies, quantitative assessments of conservation corridor efficacy, and open-source tools for evaluating trade-offs between ecological resilience and resource extraction priorities. By integrating ecological complexity with real-world policy variables, this work will provide actionable insights for adaptive management strategies, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance evidence-based natural resources governance. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the petabyte-scale geospatial datasets and computationally intensive ensemble modeling required to reduce uncertainties in multispecies conservation planning.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Management and Policy, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, develop, manage, and evaluate programs to protect and regulate natural habitats and renewable natural resources. Includes instruction in the principles of wildlife and conservation biology, environmental science, animal population surveying, natural resource economics, management techniques for various habitats, applicable law and policy, administrative and communications skills, and public relations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a novel framework for real-time, large-scale anomaly detection in decentralized financial transaction networks—an emerging challenge at the intersection of business statistics, computational finance, and distributed systems. Traditional statistical methods for fraud detection struggle to adapt to the dynamic, high-dimensional data generated by blockchain-based payment systems and IoT-enabled supply chain transactions, where latency, scalability, and interpretability constraints limit existing analytical pipelines. The proposed computational approach integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) with Bayesian nonparametric models to simultaneously capture spatial-temporal dependencies and evolving fraud patterns across heterogeneous transaction graphs. By implementing distributed training protocols optimized for GPU clusters, the project aims to process terabyte-scale datasets encompassing timestamped transaction records, entity relationship graphs, and external market signals. Key innovations include a hybrid sampling technique to address class imbalance in fraud labels and a quantum-inspired optimization layer for feature selection under uncertainty. The HPC environment will enable iterative testing of model architectures against synthetic and real-world datasets, including a proprietary multinational payment processor’s ledger spanning 180 million nodes. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source anomaly detection toolkit optimized for business applications, quantitative benchmarks against industry-standard methods, and new statistical metrics for evaluating model robustness in nonstationary environments. This work addresses a critical gap in business statistics by providing computationally feasible methods to analyze emergent financial network behaviors, with direct implications for risk management in decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms and cross-border transaction ecosystems. The resource-intensive nature of graph-based deep learning and the need for rapid hyperparameter tuning across massive datasets necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve statistically significant results within operational time constraints.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data. Includes instruction in statistical theory and methods, computer applications, data analysis and display, long- and short-term forecasting methods, and market performance analysis.

abstract: Forensic nursing practice requires the integration of complex, multidimensional datasets—including medical records, forensic evidence, and legal case data—to support victim care and criminal investigations. However, existing analytical methods often struggle to process these heterogeneous datasets at scale, limiting the ability to identify patterns in violence trends, predict case outcomes, or optimize evidence collection protocols. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that address these challenges. The research focuses on two primary objectives: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to analyze anonymized clinical-forensic datasets for risk stratification of interpersonal violence recurrence, and (2) simulating biological evidence degradation patterns under diverse environmental conditions using physics-informed neural networks. The computational workflow will integrate natural language processing for clinical note analysis, graph-based algorithms to map perpetrator-victim interaction networks, and multi-scale simulations of biological evidence preservation dynamics. By parallelizing these processes across HPC architectures, the project aims to overcome current limitations in processing speed and model complexity. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to guide clinical interventions for at-risk populations, optimized forensic evidence handling protocols validated through simulation, and a computational framework for correlating longitudinal health data with legal case resolutions. These outputs will directly enhance forensic nurses' capacity to deliver data-driven care while strengthening evidentiary rigor in legal proceedings. The project will also generate open-access computational workflows tailored for forensic nursing applications, bridging a critical gap between healthcare informatics and legal medicine. Access to HPC resources is essential given the project's requirement for large-scale data integration, real-time model training across thousands of medicolegal cases, and high-fidelity simulations of biological systems. This work represents a novel convergence of computational science and forensic nursing practice with implications for improving both patient outcomes and criminal justice efficiency.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the law and forensic science to nursing practice and collaborate with other professionals for the care of victims and the prosecution of criminals. Includes instruction in advanced physical assessment, evidence collection and preservation, forensic anthropology, legal testimony, medicolegal investigation, pathophysiology, pathohistology, pharmacology, and violence prevention.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced computer-aided design (CAD) and drafting workflows in engineering technology applications, particularly for complex 3D solids modeling and simulation tasks. Current CAD software tools face scalability limitations when handling high-fidelity geometric models, multi-physics simulations, or real-time collaborative design iterations, leading to productivity bottlenecks in engineering design processes. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing and optimizing parallelized computational workflows leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) implementing distributed computing frameworks to accelerate finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations integrated with CAD geometry processing, and (2) creating machine learning-enhanced algorithms for automated design optimization and error detection in large-scale assembly models. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for rendering-intensive tasks and MPI-based parallelization for parametric design studies. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in simulation runtime for typical mechanical systems, improved accuracy in stress analysis for composite materials, and scalable solutions for collaborative CAD environments. These advancements will directly benefit engineering technology education by enabling students to work with industry-scale models and simulations, while providing a foundation for resource-efficient design methodologies applicable to renewable energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing systems. The computational workflows and benchmarking data generated will be made available as open educational resources to support CAD/CADD programs nationwide.
cip_title: CAD/ CADD Drafting and/ or Design Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and advanced computer software and hardware to the creation of graphic representations and simulations in support of engineering projects. Includes instruction in engineering graphics, two-dimensional and three-dimensional engineering design, solids modeling, engineering animation, computer-aided drafting (CAD), computer-aided design (CADD), and auto-CAD techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to advance radiation transport modeling and material response analysis in complex nuclear and industrial environments using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. A critical challenge in radiologic safety and system design is accurately predicting radiation field behavior and its interaction with heterogeneous materials under dynamic operational conditions. Current analytical models struggle to resolve fine-scale spatial-temporal variations in radiation flux, particularly in irregular geometries or during transient scenarios, leading to overconservative shielding designs or unanticipated material degradation. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations with machine learning-driven material response models. The Monte Carlo component will leverage GPU-accelerated particle tracking to simulate neutron and gamma-ray interactions in 3D geometries representative of industrial radiologic systems, including robotic inspection platforms and waste immobilization facilities. Parallelized sensitivity analyses will quantify uncertainties in source terms, material compositions, and detection thresholds. Concurrently, neural networks trained on ab initio molecular dynamics datasets will predict radiation-induced defect evolution in structural alloys and shielding composites. By coupling these approaches through iterative feedback, the project aims to establish a predictive digital twin platform for optimizing radiation-hardened component lifespans and real-time dose management. HPC resources are essential to achieve the required spatial resolution (<1 mm) and statistical confidence (>10^9 particle histories per simulation), which are computationally intractable on local clusters. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for adaptive shielding configurations in high-radiation industrial environments, reduced conservatism in safety factor calculations, and predictive models for material failure thresholds under mixed-field irradiation. These results will directly inform next-generation radiologic system designs, decommissioning workflows, and regulatory guidelines, enhancing operational safety and cost efficiency across the nuclear energy and radiologic manufacturing sectors.
cip_title: Nuclear and Industrial Radiologic Technologies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in nuclear and industrial radiologic technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Play therapy is a critical intervention for addressing developmental, emotional, and behavioral challenges in children, yet the field lacks robust computational tools to analyze the complex dynamics of therapeutic play sessions and their outcomes. Current methods for evaluating play therapy efficacy rely heavily on qualitative observations and manual coding, which are time-intensive, subjective, and limited in scalability. This project seeks to address this gap by developing machine learning (ML) models and computational frameworks to quantitatively assess play therapy interactions, predict therapeutic outcomes, and optimize intervention strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets, including video recordings of therapy sessions, physiological data (e.g., heart rate variability), and longitudinal behavioral assessments. Computational workflows will integrate computer vision techniques for automated gesture and play behavior recognition, natural language processing (NLP) to analyze therapist-child verbal exchanges, and graph-based models to map relational patterns in play narratives. A key innovation will involve training ensemble ML algorithms on labeled datasets to identify biomarkers of therapeutic progress, such as shifts in emotional regulation or social engagement. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothetical play scenarios to test the impact of different therapeutic approaches under varying developmental conditions. The project’s outcomes will include open-source tools for play therapy analytics, validated predictive models for treatment response, and a computational framework to guide personalized intervention plans. By enabling large-scale, data-driven insights into play therapy mechanisms, this work aims to enhance training protocols for play therapists, improve clinical decision-making, and advance equity in mental health care for diverse pediatric populations. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of training deep neural networks on high-dimensional data and running parallelized simulations, which cannot feasibly be executed on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the complex dynamics of personalized learning environments in K-12 classrooms, focusing on the interplay between adaptive educational technologies and student cognitive development. While personalized learning tools are increasingly integrated into classrooms, their long-term impacts on neurocognitive processes—such as memory consolidation, attentional regulation, and metacognitive skill formation—remain poorly understood at scale. The research problem centers on quantifying how algorithmically driven educational interventions interact with neurodevelopmental trajectories, particularly in diverse student populations with varying socioeconomic, cultural, and neurodivergent profiles. Using agent-based modeling (ABM), we will simulate classroom ecosystems where virtual student agents, parameterized with neuropsychological and behavioral data from empirical studies, engage with adaptive learning platforms. The computational framework will integrate reinforcement learning algorithms to model platform decision-making and neurocognitive growth curves derived from developmental psychology literature. Monte Carlo methods will assess variability in outcomes across simulated demographic conditions, while graph neural networks will map emergent patterns in skill acquisition and cognitive load distribution. This approach requires HPC capabilities to handle high-dimensional parameter spaces (10^6+ agent configurations) and real-time feedback loops between simulated learners and adaptive systems. Expected outcomes include predictive models of neurocognitive response thresholds to personalized learning stimuli, identification of algorithmic bias risks in educational technology systems, and evidence-based design principles for cognitively sustainable adaptive interfaces. By bridging computational neuroscience, machine learning, and educational psychology, this work aims to establish a foundational framework for ethically optimizing emerging educational technologies while safeguarding student cognitive health—a critical gap in contemporary educational practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory and practice of learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: Occupational exposures to complex mixtures of hazardous agents—including chemical, physical, and biological stressors—pose significant challenges for risk assessment and mitigation in industrial environments. Traditional exposure assessment methods often struggle to account for dynamic interactions between multiple hazards, variable workplace conditions, and individual worker susceptibility, limiting the ability to predict health outcomes or optimize safety protocols. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multi-scale computational models that simulate exposure dynamics, dose-response relationships, and intervention efficacy in diverse occupational settings. The research will integrate large-scale datasets from wearable sensors, environmental monitoring systems, toxicological databases, and epidemiological studies to parameterize agent-based models, machine learning algorithms, and fluid dynamics simulations. Key computational tasks include probabilistic risk assessment of co-exposures, real-time prediction of airborne contaminant dispersion in complex workspaces, and toxicokinetic modeling of metabolic interactions for mixed chemical exposures. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC clusters, the project aims to resolve spatial-temporal exposure patterns at unprecedented resolution while incorporating stochastic variability in worker behaviors and environmental factors. Expected outcomes include actionable frameworks for exposure prioritization, optimized design of ventilation systems and personal protective equipment, and predictive tools to evaluate emerging risks from novel industrial materials or processes. The computational infrastructure will enable scalable, data-driven decision-making to advance occupational health standards, reduce work-related illnesses, and support regulatory compliance. This work aligns with public health priorities to mitigate inequities in workplace safety and foster resilient industrial ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to monitor and evaluate health and related safety standards in industrial, commercial, and government workplaces and facilities. Includes instruction in occupational health and safety standards and regulations; health-related aspects of various occupations and work environments; health hazard testing and evaluation; test equipment operation and maintenance; industrial toxicology; worker health and safety education; and the analysis and testing of job-related equipment, behavior practices, and protective devices and procedures.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of nuclear facilities relies on high-fidelity modeling of complex phenomena, such as neutron transport, thermal-hydraulic behavior, and material degradation under extreme conditions. Current computational tools often rely on simplified approximations to manage the multi-physics, multi-scale nature of these systems, limiting their predictive accuracy for next-generation reactor designs and safety evaluations. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a scalable, high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate coupled neutronics, thermal-fluid dynamics, and structural responses in advanced nuclear systems. The research will focus on optimizing parallel algorithms for deterministic and stochastic neutron transport solvers, integrating them with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) codes for coolant flow analysis, and coupling these outputs to finite element models (FEM) for stress prediction in reactor components. Key innovations include adaptive mesh refinement to resolve localized phenomena (e.g., turbulent mixing in molten salt reactors) and machine learning-driven surrogate models to accelerate convergence in iterative multi-physics simulations. The HPC resources requested will enable large-scale 3D simulations of reactor core configurations, transient accident scenarios, and fuel cycle analyses at resolutions impractical for conventional computing systems. Expected outcomes include validated models for small modular reactor (SMR) designs, improved uncertainty quantification for safety margins, and a publicly accessible dataset to support regulatory reviews. By advancing computational capabilities for nuclear systems, this work aims to reduce reliance on empirical correlations in reactor licensing, accelerate the deployment of advanced nuclear technologies, and enhance operational safety protocols for existing facilities. The results will directly inform graduate-level curriculum development in nuclear computational methods and provide training opportunities for students in HPC-driven engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering, knowledge and technical skills in support of engineer and other professionals operating nuclear facilities and engaged in nuclear applications and safety procedures. Includes instruction in physics, nuclear science, nuclear systems, nuclear plant and systems design, radiological safety, radiological applications, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic neural and linguistic patterns underlying therapeutic outcomes in psychodynamic psychotherapy. While psychoanalytic frameworks have long emphasized unconscious processes and relational dynamics, the computational modeling of these phenomena—particularly how they manifest in real-time therapist-patient interactions—remains underexplored. Current limitations include the inability to process large-scale multimodal datasets (e.g., therapy session transcripts, fMRI/EEG neuroimaging, and longitudinal clinical assessments) in an integrated manner, which hinders the identification of biomarkers for treatment efficacy. The proposed research will develop machine learning models to analyze linguistic markers of transference, resistance, and emotional regulation in therapy transcripts, paired with neural activity patterns from neuroimaging data. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be optimized to detect latent psychodynamic constructs (e.g., defense mechanisms, affective shifts) at scale, while graph-based neural networks will model the temporal interplay between neural connectivity shifts and therapeutic milestones. HPC resources are critical for training these models on heterogeneous data from 500+ therapy sessions (totaling ~10 TB) and simulating dynamic systems representing intrapsychic processes. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks linking specific interaction patterns to symptom remission, (2) validated computational signatures of therapeutic alliance formation, and (3) open-source tools for real-time session analysis to guide clinician decision-making. By bridging psychodynamic theory with computational psychiatry, this work aims to establish an empirical foundation for personalized psychoanalytic interventions while addressing longstanding critiques regarding the field’s methodological opacity. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory nodes for graph computations, and secure storage for sensitive clinical data, ensuring compliance with ethical standards for confidentiality.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the provision of psychoanalytic counseling to individuals and groups based on the psychodynamic principles evolved from authorities such as Freud, Adler, and Jung. Includes instruction in self-analysis, personality theory, dream analysis, free association and transference theory and techniques, psychodynamic theory, developmental processes, applications to specific clinical conditions, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Albanian linguistic evolution and dialectal variation. Despite Albania’s rich linguistic heritage, the dynamic interplay between Gheg and Tosk dialects—and their divergence from earlier Illyrian and medieval Albanian forms—remains underexplored at scale. Traditional philological methods struggle to process the vast, fragmented corpus of historical texts, oral recordings, and modern digital sources required to model these relationships comprehensively. The research problem centers on reconstructing phonological, morphological, and lexical shifts across dialects and historical periods while identifying patterns that illuminate the sociolinguistic forces driving linguistic change. Proposed computational methods include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to automate the parsing and annotation of digitized texts (e.g., archival manuscripts, contemporary literature) and speech datasets, coupled with machine learning models to detect latent dialectal features. Phylogenetic algorithms will be adapted to model branching relationships between dialects, while transformer-based architectures will analyze semantic and syntactic evolution in context-aware frameworks. The scale of data—spanning centuries of texts, regional speech corpora, and cross-referenced etymological databases—necessitates parallelized computing for training and inference. Expected outcomes include a unified diachronic map of Albanian linguistic development, open-access tools for dialect classification, and a public corpus annotated for pedagogical and technological applications. These resources will directly support endangered dialect preservation efforts, inform computational linguistics models for under-resourced languages, and enhance Albanian language education through data-driven insights into dialectal diversity. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this project aims to redefine the methodological possibilities for Albanian language studies while fostering interdisciplinary innovation in digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Albanian language. Includes instruction in Albanian/Illyrian philology; Ghegg and Tosk dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving cultural narratives and identity formation within the United States through large-scale textual and multimedia archival data. The research focuses on understudied intersections of regional, ethnic, and gender-based discourses in 20th-century American media, including digitized newspapers, community publications, and oral history recordings. A critical challenge lies in processing and cross-referencing heterogeneous, unstructured datasets—spanning millions of pages and audio-visual files—to identify patterns in the representation of marginalized groups and the diffusion of cultural symbols across geographic and demographic boundaries. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical vernacular and speech-to-text algorithms adapted for regional dialects, we will map semantic shifts in identity-related terminology and trace the influence of immigrant communities on mainstream cultural production. Graph-based network analysis will model the spread of narratives through media ecosystems, while transformer-based models will assess multimodal correlations between textual themes and visual iconography in propaganda materials. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed storage solutions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas of cultural discourse dynamics, methodological frameworks for computationally analyzing degraded or incomplete archival materials, and new insights into how localized identity negotiations shaped national narratives. This work advances interdisciplinary scholarship in American Studies by bridging qualitative theories of cultural hybridity with data-driven approaches, while also addressing technical gaps in processing historically marginalized linguistic and audiovisual forms. Results will inform curricula and public history initiatives focused on inclusive representations of U.S. civilization.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the United States and its Pre-Columbian and colonial predecessors, and including the flow of immigrants from other societies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural resilience and identity negotiation among diasporic communities through large-scale analysis of multilingual digital archives and social media data. As global migration patterns intensify, digital platforms have become critical spaces where marginalized groups articulate hybrid identities, preserve cultural practices, and contest dominant narratives. However, existing scholarship lacks robust computational tools to systematically analyze the interplay of language, visual culture, and networked discourse in these contexts. Our research employs natural language processing (NLP) optimized for low-resource languages and multimodal machine learning to process heterogeneous datasets spanning text, images, and video from platform APIs and community-generated repositories. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on terabyte-scale corpora while maintaining sensitivity to contextual cultural codes. The computational pipeline integrates geospatial metadata analysis with sentiment detection frameworks adapted for non-Western epistemologies, enabling longitudinal tracking of identity markers across transnational digital networks. Expected outcomes include 1) new metrics for quantifying cultural hybridity in digitally mediated spaces, 2) identification of platform-specific barriers to cultural preservation, and 3) open-source tools for ethical community-centered archiving. By bridging computational social science methodologies with critical cultural studies frameworks, this work will advance understanding of how marginalized groups navigate digital publics while confronting algorithmic bias and linguistic hegemony. The requested resources directly support processing capacity for cross-lingual embeddings and GPU-intensive simulations of cultural transmission dynamics across synthetic social networks, enabling unprecedented scale in comparative diaspora studies. Results will inform policy discussions on digital cultural rights and provide methodological foundations for equitable computational approaches in transnational identity research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Area, Ethnic, Cultural, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in area, ethnic, cultural, gender, or group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dental caries and periodontal diseases remain highly prevalent globally, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations despite established preventive measures. Emerging evidence suggests oral microbial dysbiosis interacts with systemic conditions (e.g., diabetes, cardiovascular disease) through complex host-microbiome-metabolite networks, but current analytical frameworks lack resolution to model these interactions at population scales.
