This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets from a longitudinal cohort study (n=2,400) exploring bidirectional relationships between oral microbiome dynamics, epigenetic modifications, and metabolic syndrome markers in underserved urban populations. Computational challenges include processing 45TB of metagenomic sequencing data, integrating heterogeneous datasets (16S rRNA, shotgun metagenomics, plasma metabolomics, epigenetic clocks), and implementing dynamical systems models to identify critical transition states in disease progression. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to predict community-specific caries risk thresholds based on microbial interaction networks and social determinants of health covariates. A novel agent-based model will simulate the population-level impact of targeted microbiome-modifying interventions (e.g., pH-stabilizing nanotherapies) on oral health disparities. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of keystone microbial taxa driving oral-systemic disease synergies, (2) computational tools for personalized caries prevention strategies in public health dentistry, and (3) policy-relevant simulations of intervention scalability across diverse community dental infrastructures. This work requires HPC capabilities for parallelized metagenomic assembly (using MetaSPAdes and HUMAnN3), GPU-accelerated deep learning (PyTorch geometric for graph-based microbiome networks), and large-scale parameter sweeps in epidemiological modeling (Repast4Py). By bridging computational biology and dental public health paradigms, the project aims to establish a framework for precision prevention strategies that address oral health inequalities through microbiome-informed community programming.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of dental disease prevention and control, community dental health promotion, and prepares dentists and public health professionals to function as dental health specialists. Includes instruction in preventive dentistry, the relationship of oral disease to health and quality of life, patient and practitioner behavior, dental epidemiology, nutrition and dental health, dental care policy and delivery, oral health program planning and administration, biostatistics, and research methods.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable food production and safety necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize food processing and preservation techniques. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational framework to model microbial dynamics in complex food matrices, with a focus on spoilage organisms and pathogens under varying environmental conditions. Current predictive models lack the resolution to capture heterogeneous microenvironments within food systems, limiting their utility in designing targeted interventions. We propose integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to bridge this gap. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating microbial population interactions at multiple scales, from molecular-level protein-lipid interactions in cell membranes to colony-scale spatial competition. The ABM component will leverage parallel computing to simulate 10^6–10^7 individual microbial agents across dynamic physicochemical gradients, while MD simulations will characterize membrane permeability changes in response to antimicrobial compounds. A convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on hyperspectral imaging data of food samples to correlate simulated microbial behavior with empirical spoilage patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps of microbial growth hotspots in heterogeneous food matrices, (2) optimized combinations of hurdle technologies (e.g., pH, temperature, preservatives) to extend shelf life, and (3) mechanistic insights into membrane-level responses to stress factors. This work will directly inform the design of energy-efficient processing protocols and reduce food waste by enabling precision preservation strategies. The computational framework will be shared as an open-source tool for the food science community, facilitating broader applications in product development and safety assurance. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU nodes for MD/ML workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale ABM simulations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in food sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of cancer treatment, yet optimizing therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicity requires precise modeling of radiation interactions with biological tissues and dynamic patient anatomy. Current clinical tools often rely on simplified approximations of radiation transport, tumor response, and normal tissue tolerance, which may limit personalization and accuracy in complex cases. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework for radiation treatment planning and outcome prediction by integrating patient-specific radiobiological models, real-time anatomical dynamics, and advanced Monte Carlo dose calculations. The primary research challenges include (1) modeling stochastic variations in radiation-induced DNA damage across heterogeneous tumor and normal tissue microenvironments, (2) simulating the interplay between fractionated radiation delivery and temporal changes in tumor oxygenation/geometry, and (3) establishing predictive relationships between multi-scale biological parameters and clinical outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to implement GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo radiation transport algorithms (based on TOPAS-nBio and Geant4-DNA) coupled with finite-element biomechanical models of organ motion and deep learning-based auto-segmentation. The computational workflow will process high-resolution 4D CT/MRI datasets (>2 TB/patient cohort) while performing parallelized parameter sweeps across radiobiological variables. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform capable of resolving sub-millimeter dose deposition patterns under respiratory motion constraints (<1% statistical uncertainty) and probabilistic forecasts of tumor control probability/normal tissue complication probability incorporating spatial and temporal heterogeneity. This resource will enable unprecedented investigation of dose escalation strategies in moving targets, rare toxicity prediction in serial organs-at-risk, and biologically optimized fractionation schemes. By bridging computational physics with clinical radiobiology, the project aims to establish a paradigm shift toward simulation-driven personalized radiation oncology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of ionizing radiation to treat patients with cancer and other diseases. Includes instruction in treatment planning, instrument design and operation, radiation physics and radiobiology. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time decision-making architectures for businesses operating in hyper-volatile markets, where traditional management information systems (MIS) struggle to balance computational efficiency, predictive accuracy, and interpretability. The core problem lies in the inability of conventional rule-based or single-model machine learning (ML) systems to adaptively process streaming multi-modal data—including text, sensor inputs, and transactional records—while maintaining audit trails required for regulatory compliance. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a heterogeneous ensemble learning framework that dynamically allocates computational resources to specialized submodels based on real-time feature importance and uncertainty quantification. The computational approach combines graph neural networks for cross-modal relationship extraction, lightweight online learning algorithms for rapid adaptation, and Monte Carlo dropout techniques for confidence estimation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for both training base models on historical datasets (spanning terabyte-scale financial, logistics, and social media data) and simulating market shock scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include: 1) A resource-aware scheduling algorithm that optimizes model ensemble composition under strict latency constraints, 2) Quantitative benchmarks comparing energy efficiency and prediction quality across CPU/GPU hybrid architectures, and 3) Open-source tools for deploying adaptive ML pipelines within existing MIS infrastructures. This work advances the integration of edge computing paradigms with enterprise information systems, particularly for applications in algorithmic trading, emergency supply chain management, and dynamic pricing—domains where subsecond decision cycles intersect with complex business logic. The computational artifacts will enable organizations to validate the cost-benefit tradeoffs of AI-enhanced MIS architectures before large-scale implementation.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrative computational framework to analyze the spatiotemporal dynamics of urban climate adaptation strategies and their equity implications, leveraging heterogeneous datasets spanning environmental sensor networks, socioeconomic surveys, and infrastructure geodatabases. Current approaches to climate resilience planning often operate in disciplinary silos, neglecting feedback loops between microclimatic conditions, human behavior, and infrastructure performance. Our methodology combines graph neural networks with agent-based modeling to capture multiscale interactions between built environments, vegetation systems, and population mobility patterns at unprecedented spatial granularity. High-performance computing resources are required to process terabyte-scale LiDAR datasets, simulate heat island mitigation scenarios across diverse urban morphologies, and optimize green infrastructure placement through multi-objective evolutionary algorithms. The computational pipeline integrates 3D urban canopy models with street-level thermal comfort indices while accounting for demographic vulnerability factors through spatially explicit fairness constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for equity-aware climate adaptation planning, validated against hyperlocal temperature measurements and emergency response records from six major metropolitan regions. This work advances data science methodologies for high-dimensional urban systems analysis while providing actionable insights for reducing climate risk disparities. The resource-intensive nature of coupling fine-scale environmental simulations with human mobility patterns necessitates parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows and distributed memory architectures to achieve practical runtime for city-scale optimization tasks. Successful implementation will establish new paradigms for interdisciplinary urban analytics that bridge environmental engineering, social science, and computational modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis of large scale data sources from the interdisciplinary perspectives of applied statistics, computer science, data storage, data representation, data modeling, mathematics, and statistics. Includes instruction in computer algorithms, computer programming, data management, data mining, information policy, information retrieval, mathematical modeling, quantitative analysis, statistics, trend spotting, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in optimizing large-scale sports event logistics and facility management, a critical yet understudied area within Sport and Fitness Administration. The research problem centers on the inability of traditional linear models to dynamically simulate the interplay of variables such as crowd behavior, real-time resource allocation (e.g., staffing, emergency response, concessions), and environmental factors (e.g., weather, facility wear-and-tear) during high-attendance events. Current industry tools rely on static heuristics or compartmentalized datasets, limiting predictive accuracy and adaptability to emergent scenarios. To overcome these barriers, the project proposes developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with machine learning (ML) to simulate complex, multi-scale interactions within sport event ecosystems. The computational approach will involve constructing synthetic environments mirroring real-world stadiums and event schedules, populated by agents representing spectators, staff, and infrastructure systems. These agents will be programmed with behavior profiles derived from anonymized historical data (ticket sales, sensor logs, incident reports) and augmented by reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive decision-making under uncertainty. High-fidelity simulations will require parallelized computation to manage millions of agent interactions across variable time scales, necessitating HPC resources for memory-intensive Monte Carlo iterations and hyperparameter tuning of ML components. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of forecasting operational bottlenecks, optimizing staff deployment, and mitigating safety risks in real time. The project’s significance lies in bridging computational science with sports management praxis, offering a novel methodology for resource optimization in an industry increasingly reliant on data-driven governance. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation templates and partnerships with collegiate athletic departments, advancing both academic research and applied best practices in sport administration.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business, coaching and physical education principles to the organization, administration and management of athletic programs and teams, fitness/rehabilitation facilities and health clubs, sport recreation services, and related services. Includes instruction in program planning and development; business and financial management principles; sales, marketing and recruitment; event promotion, scheduling and management; facilities management; public relations; legal aspects of sports; and applicable health and safety standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in modeling cascading failures within interdependent infrastructure systems (e.g., power grids, telecommunications, transportation networks) exposed to deliberate threats, such as terrorist attacks. Current analytical frameworks struggle to capture the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between these systems at scale, limiting the ability to predict vulnerabilities and optimize resilience strategies. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-resolution computational model leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-infrastructure interdependencies under threat scenarios. The approach integrates network theory, agent-based modeling, and stochastic optimization to quantify how localized disruptions propagate across systems. HPC capabilities will enable parallelized simulations of large-scale infrastructure networks, incorporating real-world spatial data, probabilistic failure thresholds, and adaptive threat actor behaviors. Key computational challenges include managing terabytes of infrastructure topology datasets, resolving time-dependent coupling effects between systems, and iterating thousands of scenario permutations to identify high-risk failure pathways. Outcomes will include a validated framework for assessing infrastructure resilience, prioritized mitigation strategies for policymakers, and open-source tools for simulating threat-induced cascades. This work directly supports homeland security priorities by advancing predictive capabilities for critical infrastructure protection, enabling proactive resource allocation to safeguard national security and economic stability. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the project’s computational demands, as traditional computing environments lack the memory, processing speed, and scalability required for such high-dimensional, stochastic analyses.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Plants exhibit complex, dynamic responses to mechanical vibrations—such as those caused by wind, herbivory, or acoustic stimuli—through poorly understood signaling mechanisms that integrate biophysical and biochemical processes. This project seeks to model the propagation and transduction of mechanical vibrations in plant tissues at cellular and subcellular scales, with a focus on how such signals influence gene expression related to stress adaptation. Current experimental methods struggle to capture the spatiotemporal resolution required to map vibration-induced mechanotransduction pathways, particularly in species with intricate vascular architectures. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating tissue-level vibration dynamics with agent-based modeling (ABM) to predict calcium ion signaling and downstream transcriptional regulation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multiscale nature of these interactions, which involve heterogeneous material properties, nonlinear fluid-structure interactions in cell walls, and stochastic intracellular signaling events. Simulations will be parameterized using empirical data from Arabidopsis thaliana and Zea mays, with validation via live imaging of calcium fluxes and RNA sequencing of vibration-exposed tissues. Expected outcomes include the identification of vibration frequency thresholds that activate stress-responsive genes and a predictive model linking tissue mechanics to transcriptional reprogramming. This work will advance fundamental understanding of plant mechanobiology while offering insights into optimizing acoustic treatments for agriculture—a novel, non-invasive approach to enhance crop resilience. By bridging biomechanics, systems biology, and computational physics, the project occupies an emerging niche at the intersection of plant physiology and biophysical modeling, distinct from traditional domains within biological sciences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant internal dynamics and systems, plant-environment interaction, and plant life cycles and processes. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology; plant nutrition; plant respiration; plant growth, behavior, and reproduction; photosynthesis; plant systemics; and ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the morphosyntactic complexity of understudied Slavic languages, with a focus on dialectal variations in Eastern European minority language communities. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational models for analyzing non-standardized Slavic dialects, which exhibit high morphological richness and syntactic ambiguity. Traditional methods struggle to process these features efficiently, particularly when handling large corpora of spoken and historical texts. The project will employ transformer-based neural architectures and probabilistic graphical models to automate the parsing and annotation of dialectal data, integrating diachronic (historical) and synchronic (contemporary) linguistic patterns. Key tasks include training language-specific models on curated datasets of Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Serbian dialects, optimizing for low-resource scenarios, and simulating language contact effects through agent-based modeling. HPC resources are critical for managing the iterative training of deep learning models on terabyte-scale text corpora, parallelizing hyperparameter searches, and running large-scale simulations of language evolution. Expected outcomes include open-source NLP tools tailored to Slavic dialectology, a comparative analysis of morphological convergence in border regions, and a framework for predicting language shift dynamics in minority communities. These results will directly contribute to preservation efforts for endangered Slavic varieties while offering methodological innovations for computational linguistics. The project bridges gaps between traditional philological research and data-driven approaches, demonstrating how HPC can address longstanding challenges in Slavic linguistic typology and support interdisciplinary humanities scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Slavic languages of Central and Eastern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of manufacturing systems demands advanced computational tools to optimize process efficiency, material utilization, and energy consumption in production environments. This project seeks to address critical bottlenecks in computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) workflows by developing high-fidelity simulations of multi-axis machining processes and additive manufacturing systems. Traditional experimental approaches to parameter optimization are time-intensive and cost-prohibitive, particularly when scaling to industrial production volumes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this research will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) models to predict tool wear, thermal distortion, and residual stresses in subtractive manufacturing operations. Concurrently, lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations will be deployed to analyze powder bed dynamics and melt pool behavior in metal additive manufacturing. These computational models will integrate machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets—including sensor data from CNC machines and in-process monitoring systems—to enable real-time adaptive control predictions. The proposed workflows require distributed memory architectures to manage large-scale meshing operations and transient multiphysics simulations with microsecond temporal resolution. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive frameworks for minimizing material waste in machining operations, optimizing energy-efficient laser sintering parameters, and reducing post-processing requirements for hybrid manufacturing systems. By bridging gaps between simulation fidelity and practical deployability, this work aims to advance digital twin capabilities for small-to-medium manufacturing enterprises, directly supporting the program’s focus on accessible engineering solutions. The requested computing resources will enable parametric studies at unprecedented scales, reducing reliance on physical prototyping while providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-driven manufacturing research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the identification and resolution of production problems in the manufacture of products. Includes instruction in machine operations, production line operations, engineering analysis, systems analysis, instrumentation, physical controls, automation, computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), manufacturing planning, quality control, and informational infrastructure.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across Russia, Central Asia, and Eastern Europe through large-scale multilingual text analysis. Existing scholarship on cultural dynamics in this region has been constrained by fragmented datasets and manual methodologies, limiting the scope of temporal, geographic, and linguistic comparisons. Our research addresses this gap by computationally examining digitized archives of literary works, periodicals, and oral histories (19th–21st centuries) to trace how ethnic, gender, and regional identities are constructed and contested in diverse cultural texts. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques optimized for non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, Georgian) and low-resource languages (e.g., Kazakh, Uzbek, Belarusian). Custom transformer models will be trained to identify semantic shifts in identity-related lexicon across time and political regimes, while graph-based algorithms will map the diffusion of narrative motifs through transnational networks. HPC resources are critical for processing over 15 terabytes of unstructured text, enabling parallelized tokenization of heterogeneous sources (novels, newspapers, folk tales) and GPU-accelerated training of multilingual embeddings. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible corpus of annotated texts, visualization tools for cross-regional narrative analysis, and quantitative frameworks to challenge Eurocentric periodizations of cultural change in Eurasian studies. By revealing understudied connections between localized identity discourses and broader ideological transformations, this work aims to reshape methodological paradigms in area studies, emphasizing computational scalability without sacrificing the contextual nuance central to humanities research. The project will also contribute open-source tools for non-Latin script NLP, addressing a persistent gap in digital scholarship on post-Soviet and Central Asian societies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Russian, Central European, East European and Eurasian Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the region encompassing Russia, Central Europe, Eastern Europe, and Eurasia, including the Balkan, Baltic, Caucasus, and Central Asian states that were republics of the former Soviet Union.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in documentary production workflows, particularly in processing and analyzing large-scale audiovisual datasets. As documentary filmmakers increasingly adopt high-resolution formats (4K/8K), 360-degree video, and AI-driven tools for archival research, traditional computing infrastructure struggles to handle the volume and complexity of data involved. This research focuses on optimizing two critical stages: (1) automated analysis of archival footage using machine learning models to identify narrative-relevant patterns across thousands of hours of historical media, and (2) real-time rendering of interactive documentary prototypes that incorporate spatial audio-visual elements and viewer-driven branching narratives. The computational approach will utilize GPU-accelerated neural networks for feature detection in archival materials and parallel processing frameworks for testing immersive documentary environments. By deploying containerized workflows on HPC clusters, we aim to reduce processing times for scene classification tasks by 85% compared to local workstations while enabling simultaneous multi-user testing of interactive documentary interfaces. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for documentary researchers working with large media corpora, validated benchmarks for AI-assisted archival analysis in nonfiction contexts, and novel methods for scaling participatory storytelling systems. This work bridges computational media studies and documentary practice, offering new pathways for preserving cultural memory through technically innovative nonfiction forms while establishing performance standards for HPC applications in media production curricula. The requested resources will directly support 12 graduate student projects exploring ethical AI integration in documentary workflows and three faculty-led experiments in volumetric video storytelling.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce nonfiction film and video. Includes instruction in film and video writing, directing, and production; film studies; history of the documentary; research techniques; videography; editing; and business aspects of film production.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of political disinformation spread across social media platforms and its interaction with traditional media ecosystems during election cycles. The rise of computationally sophisticated disinformation campaigns—which leverage AI-generated content, microtargeting, and cross-platform coordination—presents novel challenges for understanding how false narratives emerge, evolve, and influence public opinion. Existing studies often lack the scale and temporal resolution to model these phenomena holistically, particularly in multilingual and cross-media contexts. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods computational framework combining large-scale social media data ingestion (X/Twitter, Facebook, Telegram), broadcast media transcripts, and longitudinal polling data. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will classify disinformation narratives and track their mutation across platforms using transformer-based models fine-tuned for political discourse. Temporal network analysis will map coordination patterns among accounts and media outlets, while agent-based modeling will simulate information diffusion under varying platform moderation scenarios. The scale of analysis—spanning 10TB of multimodal data across six election contexts—necessitates high-performance computing resources for distributed data processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and parallelized simulations. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available benchmark dataset of annotated disinformation clusters, 2) computational models quantifying the cross-platform amplification of false narratives, and 3) evidence-based recommendations for real-time monitoring systems to be used by journalists and fact-checking organizations. By elucidating the interplay between algorithmic content distribution and human information processing, this work aims to advance theoretical frameworks in political communication while providing actionable tools to mitigate electoral interference. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impractical on standard infrastructure, particularly for transformer inference on multilingual text and dynamic network analysis at sub-hourly resolutions.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human and media communication in the political process and that prepares individuals to function as members of political and public affairs organizations, political campaign staffs, and related government and media entities. Includes instruction in media effects, political speaking and debating, political advertising and marketing, image management, political journalism, opinion polling, and aspects of print and broadcast media related to the production and distribution of media messages in political settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the scientific understanding of complex, multi-component interventions in alternative and complementary medicine (ACM), such as herbal formulations, acupuncture, and mind-body therapies. A central challenge in ACM research lies in deciphering the synergistic mechanisms of therapies that involve numerous bioactive compounds, non-linear physiological responses, or dynamic interactions between biological systems. Traditional experimental methods often struggle to capture these multidimensional relationships, limiting mechanistic insights and evidence-based optimization. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular docking, machine learning, and dynamical systems modeling to analyze how ACM modalities interact with human physiology at scale. HPC resources will enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to predict interactions between herbal compounds and protein targets, Bayesian network inference to map acupuncture’s systemic effects on neuro-immunological pathways, and ensemble machine learning models to identify patterns in clinical outcome data from heterogeneous ACM trials. Additionally, agent-based models will simulate the long-term impacts of mind-body therapies on stress-response networks. These methods require parallelized processing of multi-omics datasets, high-throughput virtual screening of phytochemical libraries, and iterative parameter optimization for non-linear systems—tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models of ACM treatment efficacy, safety profiles of herbal synergies, and mechanistic hypotheses for experimental validation. By bridging computational science and ACM, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for evaluating holistic therapies, informing personalized treatment strategies, and fostering integration of evidence-based ACM into broader healthcare paradigms. The requested resources will directly support 3–5 pilot studies, with results disseminated through open-access tools and interdisciplinary collaborations.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: This project seeks to analyze the heterogeneous impacts of trade policy uncertainty on global supply chain reconfiguration and bilateral investment flows using a large-scale computational econometric model. Recent geopolitical shifts and the proliferation of nontariff barriers have created complex, dynamic interdependencies in international trade networks that challenge conventional equilibrium analyses. The research problem centers on quantifying how firms’ cross-border capital allocation decisions adapt to multi-country regulatory risks, currency volatility, and asymmetric trade cost shocks—a task requiring simultaneous estimation of high-dimensional parameters across spatial and temporal scales. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling with Bayesian structural vector autoregression techniques, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process real-time global trade alert datasets, firm-level foreign direct investment records, and multi-regional input-output tables. Key methodological innovations include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for policy counterfactuals and GPU-accelerated estimation of stochastic volatility components in exchange rate dynamics. The project will develop open-source tools for trade elasticity estimation under uncertainty, addressing critical gaps in existing trade policy simulation frameworks. Expected outcomes include granular insights into sector-specific vulnerability thresholds and a decision-support matrix for multilateral agreement design. By enabling rapid scenario analysis of cascading protectionist measures, this research will provide empirical foundations to mitigate trade diversion risks and inform optimal currency hedging strategies for emerging markets. Successful execution requires HPC capabilities to manage petabyte-scale data integration, with particular demands on memory bandwidth and distributed storage for iterative model calibration across 150+ national economies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study and analysis of international commercial behavior and trade policy. Includes instruction in international trade theory, tariffs and quotas, commercial policy, trade factor flows, international finance and investment, currency regulation and trade exchange rates and markets, international trade negotiation, and international payments and accounting policy.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing theatrical production workflows through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and analyze complex variables in live performance dynamics. Theatrical productions require the precise coordination of human performers, technical elements (lighting, sound, set changes), and audience engagement—a multidimensional system often constrained by time, budget, and spatial limitations. Traditional rehearsal and production planning methods struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between these factors, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation and creative outcomes. This research proposes the development of an agent-based simulation framework to model rehearsal processes, technical cue execution, and audience-performer interactions in virtual performance environments. By parameterizing variables such as actor movement patterns, technician response times, and audience sightline distributions, the model will identify bottlenecks, predict the impact of design choices, and recommend optimized scheduling and spatial configurations. HPC resources are critical to running large-scale simulations that reflect the real-world complexity of diverse venues, cast sizes, and technical requirements. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze historical production data, identifying patterns in successful artistic outcomes relative to logistical constraints. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for directors and production managers to dynamically test staging concepts, allocate personnel, and preemptively address technical risks. The project aims to advance the integration of computational decision-support systems in performing arts pedagogy and practice, reducing the gap between artistic vision and practical execution while preserving creative flexibility. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of theatrical collaboration, this work will contribute new methodologies to the field, fostering resource-efficient productions without compromising artistic integrity.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the planning, design, preparation, and production of plays and other theatrical entertainment programs. Includes instruction in theatrical design, program management, dramatic production, rehearsal management, personnel management and casting, actor coaching, directing concepts and techniques, theater history, scene work, script interpretation, business management, marketing, public relations, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the performance and sustainability of coating materials used in professional painting and wall covering applications. Despite advances in material science, the selection and application of paints, lacquers, and wallpapers remain largely reliant on empirical methods, with limited predictive tools to account for dynamic environmental conditions, substrate interactions, or long-term durability. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model adhesion dynamics, moisture resistance, and degradation patterns of coating systems. Molecular dynamics simulations will evaluate interfacial bonding between common substrates (e.g., drywall, wood, masonry) and coating formulations under varying humidity and temperature conditions. Concurrently, finite element analysis will predict stress distribution and crack propagation in layered coatings subjected to mechanical wear. A machine learning pipeline will integrate experimental data from industry partners with simulation outputs to train predictive models for coating lifespan and failure modes. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of parameter spaces (e.g., material compositions, application thicknesses, climate variables) and the need for ensemble simulations across realistic time scales. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for professionals to select optimal coatings based on project-specific environmental and structural factors, as well as guidelines for formulating low-VOC materials with enhanced durability. By bridging computational materials science and trade practice, this work aims to reduce material waste, improve safety standards, and extend maintenance cycles in residential and commercial settings. Results will be validated against accelerated aging tests and field data from collaborating painting contractors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to finish exterior and interior structural surfaces by applying protective or decorative coating materials, such as paint, lacquer, and wallpaper. Includes instruction in surface preparation; selecting, preparing, and applying paints and other coatings; hanging wallpaper; equipment operation and maintenance; finish selection; safety and clean-up; environmental effects on finishes; adhesion properties; and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The development of advanced metallic alloys capable of withstanding extreme thermomechanical and corrosive environments remains a critical challenge in metallurgical engineering. Current experimental approaches to optimize alloy compositions and processing parameters are resource-intensive and often fail to capture multiscale interactions between microstructure evolution, defect propagation, and environmental degradation. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to establish a predictive framework for designing next-generation nickel-based superalloys and high-entropy alloys tailored for high-temperature energy systems. The research will employ multi-physics computational models integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of dislocation dynamics at atomic scales, phase-field modeling of grain boundary interactions, and finite element analysis (FEA) of component-scale stress distributions under cyclic thermal loading. A key innovation involves coupling these methods through machine learning surrogates to bridge temporal and spatial gaps between microstructural phenomena and bulk material performance. The computational workflow will process terabytes of parametric simulation data to identify alloy systems that maximize creep resistance while maintaining fracture toughness across operational temperature ranges (600–1200°C). Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for microstructural stability under combined oxidative and mechanical stress, optimized heat treatment protocols to minimize residual stresses, and a ranked list of candidate alloy compositions for experimental validation. This work will advance fundamental understanding of defect-mediated failure mechanisms in polycrystalline metallic systems while directly supporting industry partnerships focused on durable materials for turbine components and high-efficiency thermal energy storage. The requested HPC resources are essential due to the parallel nature of ensemble MD simulations, memory-intensive phase-field computations tracking 3D grain networks, and iterative optimization algorithms requiring >10^4 core-hours per parametric sweep. Successful implementation will establish a scalable computational metallurgy platform applicable to diverse alloy design challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and metallurgical principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of metal components of structural, load-bearing, power, transmission, and moving systems; and the analysis of engineering problems such as stress, creep, failure, alloy behavior, environmental fluctuations, stability, electromagnetic and thermodynamic characteristics, optimal manufacturing processes, and related design considerations.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable animal production systems necessitates precise optimization of feed efficiency and nutrient utilization. Current nutritional models often lack the resolution to account for dynamic interactions between dietary components, host physiology, and gut microbiota, leading to suboptimal predictions. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating multi-omics data, metabolic network analysis, and machine learning to model nutrient metabolism in ruminants. The primary research problem involves elucidating how variations in dietary lipid and carbohydrate composition influence microbial fermentation pathways, host energy partitioning, and methane emissions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing large-scale simulations of microbial community dynamics using agent-based modeling, as well as parameterizing genome-scale metabolic models for key microbial taxa. Additionally, neural networks will be trained on heterogeneous datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiles) to identify nonlinear relationships between diet formulations and production outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive platform for optimizing feed compositions to maximize protein synthesis in muscle tissues while minimizing metabolic waste and greenhouse gas emissions, and (2) mechanistic insights into host-microbiome co-regulation of nutrient absorption. The computational tools developed will enable rapid in silico testing of novel feed additives and precision nutrition strategies, reducing reliance on costly in vivo trials. By advancing the granularity of nutritional models, this work will directly support the agricultural sector in balancing productivity with environmental sustainability. The requested HPC allocation will facilitate the analysis of petabyte-scale multi-omics datasets and iterative simulation workflows, which are computationally prohibitive on local clusters. This project aligns with broader goals of improving food security and reducing the ecological footprint of livestock systems through data-driven innovation in animal nutrition science.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biology and chemistry of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, water, vitamins, and feed additives as related to animal health and the production of improved animal products. Includes instruction in nutrition science, animal health and physiology, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, animal husbandry, and food science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to predict adverse neonatal outcomes in high-risk pregnancies by integrating multi-modal clinical, imaging, and genomic data. Despite advances in neonatal-perinatal medicine, early identification of infants at risk for complications such as hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, sepsis, or metabolic disorders remains limited by the heterogeneity of physiological responses and fragmented data streams. Current risk stratification tools lack the granularity to model dynamic interactions between maternal-fetal physiology, genetic susceptibility, and postnatal adaptation. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), placental histopathology images, and umbilical cord blood metabolomic profiles from a retrospective cohort of 12,000 neonates. Computational workflows will include 3D convolutional neural networks for placental image segmentation, Bayesian hierarchical models to infer temporal risk trajectories from EHR time-series data, and graph-based algorithms to map metabolite-pathway interactions. The integration of these disparate data types requires distributed memory parallelism for large-scale matrix operations and GPU-accelerated training of ensemble models. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive algorithm for neonatal morbidity in preterm and growth-restricted infants, (2) mechanistic insights into metabolomic signatures of perinatal stress, and (3) open-source tools for real-time risk visualization in clinical settings. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling transitional physiology during the critical perinatal period. The resulting computational infrastructure will directly inform targeted intervention trials and provide a template for data-driven consultation in maternal-fetal medicine. Resource allocation is essential to manage the project's ∼450 TB multimodal dataset and computationally intensive integration steps, which exceed the capacity of local clinical servers.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physiology of the normal neonate, the pathophysiology of the sick infant, and the diagnosis and management of problems of the newborn infant, including consulting with obstetricians to plan for the care of women with high-risk pregnancies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural knowledge exchange in historical trade networks, integrating methods from computational social science, digital humanities, and environmental studies. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how non-economic factors—such as linguistic evolution, ecological adaptation, and informal social institutions—shaped the resilience of pre-modern trade systems. Current models prioritize economic metrics or geopolitical frameworks, neglecting the interdisciplinary interactions that sustained these networks. By analyzing heterogeneous data spanning archaeological records, multilingual manuscripts, and paleoenvironmental proxies, this work aims to reconstruct a multidimensional view of trade as a socio-ecological system. Computational challenges include processing irregularly sampled, multilingual textual corpora (10^4–10^5 documents) alongside geospatial and climatic datasets. The proposed workflow employs transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for historical languages, coupled with agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about adaptive behaviors under resource constraints. HPC resources are essential for scaling three core tasks: (1) parallelized training of custom NLP architectures to handle low-resource historical dialects and script variations; (2) spatiotemporal alignment of fragmented records using Bayesian hierarchical modeling across 10^6 parameter combinations; and (3) multi-agent simulation runs (10^3–10^4 iterations) to quantify system robustness under stochastic environmental shocks. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework for interdisciplinary historical analysis, validated against documented cases of network collapse/persistence. Results will contribute methodological innovations in handling temporally misaligned multidisciplinary data while offering empirical insights into how diverse knowledge systems co-evolved with environmental pressures. The resource allocation will directly support scalability testing, sensitivity analyses, and the development of modular pipelines adaptable to other interdisciplinary studies of complex human-environment systems.
cip_definition: A program that derives from two or more distinct programs and that is integrated around a unifying theme or topic that cannot be subsumed under a single discipline or occupational field.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced signal processing algorithms to enhance the detection and classification of stealth submarines in complex underwater environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges unique to military acoustics. Modern undersea warfare requires overcoming significant limitations in existing sonar systems, particularly in cluttered coastal regions where multipath interference, biologics, and anthropogenic noise degrade detection accuracy. Traditional methods, optimized for open-ocean scenarios, struggle to adapt to these dynamic conditions, necessitating novel computational approaches. The research will focus on simulating high-fidelity acoustic propagation models under diverse environmental parameters (e.g., bathymetry, salinity gradients, sediment layers) and integrating machine learning (ML) techniques to isolate target signatures from confounding noise. HPC resources will enable large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to train deep neural networks on synthetic and experimentally validated datasets, optimizing robustness against adversarial conditions such as echo-reduction coatings or decoy deployment. Key computational tasks include finite element modeling of transient acoustic wave interactions, parallelized processing of multi-static sonar array data, and real-time classification algorithm development. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for adaptive sonar signal processing, validated against classified field data, capable of improving detection probabilities in contested littoral zones. This work bridges gaps between theoretical acoustics, computational engineering, and tactical military requirements, offering a pathway to next-generation antisubmarine warfare systems. The HPC component is critical due to the exponential computational demands of 3D wave propagation modeling and ML training, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters. By advancing both algorithmic efficiency and physical modeling accuracy, this project aims to deliver actionable tools for undersea domain awareness while contributing open-source computational methodologies to the broader acoustics community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of acoustics and signals processing to undersea and antisubmarine warfare. Includes instruction in acoustics; electrical engineering; the generation, propagation and reception of underwater sound waves; military applications of underwater sound; and acoustic signal processing.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between neurochemical signaling, neural circuit activity, and stress-induced behavioral adaptation using advanced computational modeling. While biopsychological studies have established broad correlations between neuromodulator systems (e.g., cortisol, dopamine) and behavioral outcomes, the multiscale mechanisms linking molecular-level neurochemical fluctuations to macroscopic brain network reorganization and adaptive decision-making remain poorly understood. This project addresses this gap by developing an integrative computational framework that bridges molecular neurobiology, systems neuroscience, and cognitive psychology through three synergistic components: (1) agent-based modeling of stress propagation in biologically plausible neural networks, (2) biophysically detailed simulations of cortico-limbic-striatal circuits under time-varying neurochemical conditions, and (3) machine learning analysis of behavioral phenotyping data from concurrent rodent electrophysiology and biomarker studies. The computational approach requires high-performance computing resources to manage multi-parameter optimization across spatial scales (molecular to network-level) and temporal resolutions (millisecond neurodynamics to hour-long behavioral epochs). Expected outcomes include predictive models of stress response trajectories based on individual neurochemical profiles, identification of critical transition points in network stability, and data-driven hypotheses about pharmacological targets for enhancing cognitive flexibility. By unifying experimental data from molecular assays, neural recordings, and behavioral tasks within a single computational architecture, this work aims to establish new quantitative bridges between biological psychiatry and psychological theory. The requested computing resources will enable parallelized simulation of 10⁵-10⁶ unique parameter combinations, real-time integration of heterogeneous datasets through custom GPU-accelerated pipelines, and dimensional reduction of high-parameter space to identify clinically actionable biomarkers. This interdisciplinary methodology advances biopsychology research capabilities by providing a systems-level computational toolkit to investigate emergent neurobehavioral phenomena that cannot be captured through reductionist experimental approaches alone.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological and psychological linkages, especially the linkages between biochemical and biophysical activity and the functioning of the central nervous system.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of European social and institutional networks during the Thirty Years’ War (1618–1648), a critical period of state formation and societal fragmentation. The research problem centers on understanding how localized conflicts escalated into a continent-wide crisis, with a focus on the interplay between economic resource distribution, military logistics, and environmental stressors. Traditional historiography relies on qualitative analysis of fragmented archival sources, but this project proposes a computational approach to synthesize disparate datasets—including tax records, grain price fluctuations, troop movement logs, and climate data—into a unified analytical framework. The scale and complexity of these datasets, spanning over 30,000 digitized records across seven modern-day countries, necessitate HPC capabilities to manage data integration, perform spatiotemporal mapping, and run probabilistic simulations. Machine learning models will identify patterns in resource allocation and conflict propagation, while agent-based modeling will simulate decision-making processes of key institutional actors (e.g., mercenary armies, urban councils, and monarchies) under varying constraints. Expected outcomes include a dynamic, open-access geospatial database of war-related socioeconomic metrics and a series of network analyses quantifying the role of logistical bottlenecks in prolonging hostilities. By integrating computational methods with archival scholarship, this project aims to resolve longstanding debates about the war’s geographic unevenness and its legacy for early modern statecraft. The resource allocation request prioritizes GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale network simulations, ensuring scalability as additional datasets are incorporated. Results will provide a template for computational humanities research on premodern European institutions, with implications for interdisciplinary studies of conflict resilience and resource governance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of European society, culture, and institutions from the origins to the present. Includes instruction in European historiography, European history sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of sociopolitical discourse in 19th-century European literature through a computational analysis of multilingual textual corpora, archival documents, and historical records. While traditional scholarship has examined these connections qualitatively, the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources—spanning French, German, and Italian texts—pose challenges for manual analysis. This research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to trace semantic shifts, intertextual references, and rhetorical patterns across genres (e.g., novels, political pamphlets, correspondence) and historical contexts, including the Revolutions of 1848 and the unification of Italy and Germany. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabytes of digitized texts, training multilingual transformer models for semantic analysis, and running iterative topic modeling algorithms (e.g., BERT-based embeddings, dynamic topic modeling) to map diachronic changes in ideological expression. The computational workflow will integrate historical metadata—such as publication dates, author affiliations, and censorship records—to contextualize linguistic trends within specific political events. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated texts, visualizations of discourse networks across regions, and statistical models correlating literary rhetoric with archival evidence of social mobilization. This interdisciplinary approach aims to advance digital humanities methodologies by bridging historiographical frameworks with computational linguistics, offering new insights into how literature both reflected and shaped nationalist movements. The project’s scale—encompassing over 50,000 texts in three languages—requires parallelized computing for efficient data processing, cloud-based storage for collaborative annotation, and GPU acceleration for deep learning tasks. Results will contribute to scholarly debates about the agency of literary texts in historical change while providing a replicable model for multilingual, corpus-driven research in cultural studies.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in historiography; historical research methods; linguistics; literature, philology; and studies of specific periods, issues and cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution of U.S. legal doctrine through large-scale textual and network analysis of federal court decisions. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in judicial reasoning that reflect shifts in constitutional interpretation, particularly in areas of civil rights and administrative law, where precedent-driven systems create complex, non-linear doctrinal trajectories. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on manual case review, limiting scalability and obscuring macro-level trends. By applying computational methods to a corpus of 1.2 million federal court opinions (1790–2023), this study aims to map how legal concepts propagate, mutate, and interact within judicial networks. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques—including transformer-based embeddings for semantic similarity and topic modeling—with graph-theoretic analyses to model citation networks and concept diffusion. HPC resources are critical for training custom language models on legal texts, executing distributed graph algorithms to detect community structures in judicial citation patterns, and running temporal simulations of doctrinal convergence/divergence. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database linking legal concepts to their network positions and evolutionary pathways, 2) quantitative frameworks for assessing the stability of constitutional interpretations under ideological or societal pressures, and 3) predictive models identifying areas of law prone to abrupt doctrinal change. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges legal theory, computational linguistics, and complex systems science, offering novel tools for understanding the dynamics of jurisprudential systems while maintaining fidelity to legal scholarship's interpretive traditions. The results will inform judicial education programs, policy design for legal infrastructure resilience, and empirical studies of constitutional governance.
cip_title: American/ US Law/ Legal Studies/ Jurisprudence
cip_definition: An advanced, professional program of the U.S. legal system, Constitution law, and jurisprudence. Includes instruction in legal history, legal sociology, philosophy of law, Constitutional law, legal procedure, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing next-generation superconducting energy storage systems through high-fidelity simulations and machine learning-driven design. Modern superconducting networks face critical challenges in balancing energy density, thermal stability, and electromagnetic interference mitigation, particularly when scaling to grid-level applications. Existing simulation tools struggle to model the multi-physics interactions between quantum material behaviors, transient electromagnetic fields, and cryogenic thermal dynamics at relevant spatial and temporal scales. Our interdisciplinary approach combines finite-element analysis of electromagnetic wave propagation in type-II superconductors with graph neural networks trained on mesoscale material defect distributions. The proposed computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods for modeling flux pinning dynamics and hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for optimizing coil geometries in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems. By employing distributed-memory parallelization across multi-node clusters, we aim to simulate full-scale superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) units with sub-micron spatial resolution—a 100x improvement over current state-of-the-art models. Expected outcomes include predictive digital twins for superconducting component degradation and open-source machine learning models for topology optimization under electromagnetic constraints. This work will directly address the computational bottlenecks preventing widespread adoption of superconducting energy storage, while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies at the intersection of computational electromagnetics, materials informatics, and high-performance computing. The developed framework will enable the design of more efficient fault-tolerant power networks and provide foundational tools for simulating emerging quantum-electronic hybrid systems. Resource allocation will support critical benchmarks in parallel scaling efficiency and memory optimization required for transitioning from laboratory-scale prototypes to utility-scale deployment models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of electrical and electronic systems and their components computer theory, computing problems and solutions, including electrical power generation systems; the design of computer systems and user interfaces; and the analysis of problems such as superconductor, wave propagation, energy storage and retrieval, and reception and amplification. c and the design of computer systems and user interfaces

abstract: The rapid evolution of computing demands necessitates innovative approaches to optimize next-generation computer hardware architectures, particularly in balancing performance, energy efficiency, and thermal management. Current hardware design workflows face limitations in simulating complex, large-scale systems with realistic workloads, often relying on simplified models that inadequately capture interdependencies between processor components, peripheral systems, and emerging technologies like 3D-integrated circuits. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable high-fidelity simulations of advanced computer hardware designs. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) developing multi-physics simulation frameworks to model thermal, electrical, and mechanical behaviors in heterogeneous computing architectures, and (2) implementing machine learning-guided optimization algorithms to iteratively refine designs for energy efficiency under dynamic workloads. Computational methods will integrate finite element analysis for thermal-stress modeling, register-transfer level (RTL) simulations for digital logic validation, and graph-based neural networks to predict performance bottlenecks. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the project aims to overcome memory and scalability constraints inherent to conventional simulation tools. Expected outcomes include validated designs for a novel processor-memory hierarchy with reduced power leakage, open-source simulation modules for hardware-software co-design, and a benchmark dataset linking architectural features to thermal resilience. These results will advance the development of sustainable, high-performance computing systems while providing a methodological framework for resource-aware hardware innovation. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the required simulation resolution and iteration speeds, enabling exploration of design spaces orders of magnitude larger than current industry-standard approaches. This work directly aligns with national priorities in semiconductor manufacturing and energy-efficient computing, offering pathways to mitigate hardware-related bottlenecks in artificial intelligence, edge computing, and other data-intensive applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize extracorporeal circulation protocols during cardiac surgeries, addressing critical gaps in personalized perfusion strategies. Despite advances in perfusion technology, current approaches often rely on generalized parameters for blood flow, oxygenation, and temperature management, which may not account for patient-specific physiological variability. This can lead to suboptimal outcomes, including postoperative neurological deficits or end-organ injury. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating hemodynamic simulations, machine learning, and patient-specific data to model real-time interactions between extracorporeal systems and individual cardiovascular physiology. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-resolution imaging data, simulate fluid dynamics within custom-designed oxygenators and circuits, and train predictive algorithms on heterogeneous clinical datasets. The computational pipeline will leverage finite element analysis for device-level flow optimization and reinforcement learning to adapt perfusion parameters dynamically based on simulated physiological feedback. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting patient-specific responses to extracorporeal circulation, which will inform the design of adaptive perfusion protocols. By correlating simulation results with retrospective clinical outcomes, this work aims to establish computational thresholds for safe perfusion under diverse physiological conditions, such as pediatric cases or patients with comorbid vascular pathologies. The resulting framework will provide perfusionists with a decision-support tool to preoperatively simulate and refine intervention strategies, reducing reliance on intraoperative trial-and-error adjustments. Successful implementation of this project has the potential to improve patient safety, minimize perioperative complications, and advance the integration of computational modeling into perfusion education and clinical practice. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieve the necessary computational scale, particularly for parallelized simulations of multi-physics systems and large-scale validation against multicenter clinical data.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to operate extracorporeal circulation and autotransfusion equipment during medical procedures and surgeries where the support or temporary replacement of a patient's own respiratory or circulatory system is required. Includes instruction in equipment selection and operation, physician and medical team consultation, patient condition monitoring, procedural techniques, and principles of respiratory and circulatory physiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model the resilience of urban transportation networks under multi-hazard environmental scenarios, including extreme flooding, seismic events, and long-term climate stressors. Current infrastructure assessment tools often lack the integration of dynamic environmental variables with structural and hydrological models, limiting their ability to predict cascading failures in complex, interconnected systems. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach combining finite element analysis for structural integrity, hydrodynamic modeling for flood propagation, and network theory to assess system-wide vulnerabilities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these interactions, particularly for simulating real-time flood-structure interactions across city-scale domains and iterating probabilistic hazard scenarios. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers for coupled fluid-structure equations, machine learning surrogates to accelerate Monte Carlo-based risk assessments, and graph algorithms to prioritize critical nodes in transportation networks. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying infrastructure segments at highest risk of failure under compound hazards, as well as adaptive mitigation strategies such as optimized flood barrier placement or traffic rerouting protocols. These results will directly inform climate resilience planning for municipal agencies and provide open-source tools for the civil engineering community to evaluate infrastructure interdependencies. The project’s scale—encompassing terabytes of geospatial data, stochastic climate projections, and parametric structural simulations—necessitates access to HPC clusters with GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity. By integrating environmental and civil engineering paradigms, this work advances the development of infrastructure systems that are both adaptive to emerging climate risks and aligned with sustainable urban development goals.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures. Combines instruction in civil and environmental engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of cross-species signaling networks in rapidly changing coastal ecosystems, integrating ecological, geochemical, and acoustic data streams to model anthropogenic impacts on interspecies communication. Coastal zones face unprecedented pressures from urbanization, climate change, and industrial activity, yet the computational synthesis of multi-modal biological and environmental data remains underdeveloped. Our research addresses this gap by developing a novel framework to analyze how noise pollution, chemical contaminants, and habitat fragmentation disrupt vibrational and chemical signaling among invertebrates, fish, and marine mammals—processes critical to mating, predation avoidance, and collective behavior. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will process petabyte-scale datasets from hydrophone arrays, mass spectrometry, and satellite imagery using hybrid convolutional neural networks and graph-based dynamical systems models. The computational workflow will synchronize heterogeneous temporal resolutions (millisecond acoustic events to decadal chemical concentration trends) and spatially explicit interactions across three study regions with varying anthropogenic footprints. Key innovations include adaptive attention mechanisms for cross-domain feature fusion and agent-based simulations of signaling cascades under future climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include the first unified atlas of coastal biosignaling networks, predictive models of threshold effects on communication resilience, and open-source tools for real-time monitoring of ecosystem-scale stress indicators. By bridging marine biology, complexity science, and environmental informatics, this work will establish computational standards for assessing multispecies vulnerability while informing policy frameworks for acoustic and chemical pollution mitigation. The scale of data integration and need for ensemble simulation across parameter spaces necessitates HPC resources to achieve sufficient temporal granularity and spatial coverage for robust ecological inference.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to optimize resource allocation strategies for adult and continuing education (ACE) programs through computational modeling of learner engagement patterns, program cost structures, and institutional capacity constraints. Despite growing demand for ACE services, administrators face persistent challenges in equitably distributing limited resources—such as instructional staff, facility availability, and technology access—across diverse learner populations with varying needs. Current allocation practices often rely on static, experience-based heuristics that fail to account for dynamic enrollment fluctuations, regional socioeconomic disparities, or emerging workforce development priorities. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based simulation models that integrate historical program data, demographic trends, and policy scenarios to predict resource demand under multiple conditions.
