High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10+ years of regional ACE participation records, workforce development metrics, and community need indices. Computational tasks will include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate allocation risks, machine learning-driven forecasting of enrollment shifts, and geospatial analysis of access inequities. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that enables administrators to (1) simulate the multi-year impacts of funding or policy changes, (2) identify threshold points for facility or staffing investments, and (3) quantify trade-offs between program scalability and learner support quality. By translating complex administrative challenges into computationally tractable models, this work aims to advance data-driven leadership practices in ACE institutions while maintaining focus on equitable access for underserved adult learners. The project directly aligns with priorities in education leadership by strengthening institutional capacity to adapt resources to evolving community needs—a critical competency as ACE programs increasingly serve as hubs for workforce retraining and digital literacy development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of administering programs and facilities designed to serve the basic education needs of undereducated adults, or the continuing education needs of adults seeking further or specialized instruction, and that prepares individuals to serve as administrators of such programs. Includes instruction in adult education principles, program and facilities planning, personnel management, community and client relations, budgeting and administration, professional standards, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Long-term care (LTC) facilities face persistent challenges in optimizing staffing models to balance resident care quality, regulatory compliance, and operational costs. Traditional staffing approaches rely on static ratios and retrospective adjustments, which fail to account for real-time fluctuations in resident acuity, seasonal demand variability, and staff availability. This project proposes the development of a dynamic, machine learning-driven staffing optimization framework tailored to LTC administration. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), staff scheduling logs, resident mobility sensor data, and facility-level admission/discharge trends—to predict hourly care demand and recommend adaptive staffing configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-modal data streams at scale, train ensemble models combining time-series forecasting and reinforcement learning, and simulate staffing scenarios under diverse constraints (e.g., budget limits, infection control protocols). Computational workflows will employ federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across partner facilities while aggregating insights. Anticipated outcomes include a validated predictive model that reduces staffing-related inefficiencies by ≥15% in simulation trials, a decision support tool for administrators, and generalized insights into resource allocation trade-offs in aging populations. The project bridges computational science and LTC management by addressing a critical operational gap through data-driven innovation, with potential to inform policy on adaptive staffing standards in rapidly aging societies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances methodological rigor in a domain traditionally underserved by predictive analytics, while directly addressing systemic sustainability challenges in LTC systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of nursing homes, assisted living facilities, adult day care, home health services, and other long term care settings and agencies serving the elderly and disabled. Includes instruction in social and clinical aspects of aging, health care delivery systems, nursing home administration, assisted living administration, aging policy and government programs, ethics, business management, financial management, human resource management, marketing, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Critically ill surgical patients, particularly trauma victims and those with multi-organ dysfunction, present complex, dynamic clinical trajectories that challenge conventional diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Current approaches to predicting outcomes or optimizing interventions in this population are limited by the inability to integrate high-dimensional, multi-modal data—including real-time physiological signals, biomarkers, imaging, and electronic health records (EHRs)—into actionable clinical models. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive artificial intelligence (AI) models and multi-scale simulations of critical illness. The primary research objective is to create computational tools that improve risk stratification, personalize resuscitation strategies, and identify novel therapeutic targets in surgical critical care. Using retrospective EHR data from 15,000 trauma and sepsis patients, we will train ensemble deep learning models to predict sepsis progression, organ failure, and mortality. Concurrently, mechanistic computational models will simulate hemodynamic, inflammatory, and metabolic responses to fluid resuscitation, vasopressors, and extracorporeal support. These models will integrate molecular data from biorepositories (e.g., cytokine profiles, metabolomics) with clinical variables to identify context-specific treatment thresholds. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of time-series data, optimizing hyperparameters across distributed neural networks, and running parallelized simulations of organ system interactions. Validation will occur through prospective observational studies and in silico clinical trials comparing model-guided protocols to standard care. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early intervention in sepsis-related organ dysfunction, computational criteria for personalized fluid dosing in trauma, and open-source simulation frameworks for testing resuscitation strategies. This work aims to reduce mortality in surgical ICU patients by translating complex physiological data into real-time decision support, while establishing scalable computational methods for critical care research.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares surgeons in the diagnosis, treatment, and support of critically ill and injured patients, particularly trauma victims and patients with multiple organ dysfunction.

abstract: Understanding the drivers of taxonomic diversity and biogeographic patterns requires resolving large-scale phylogenetic histories and modeling complex evolutionary processes, tasks hindered by computational limitations. This project seeks to reconstruct the phylogeny of a globally distributed plant clade with persistent taxonomic conflicts, integrating genomic, morphological, and ecological data to test hypotheses about diversification rates, biogeographic dispersal, and trait evolution. Current maximum likelihood and Bayesian approaches struggle to handle datasets of this size (>5,000 species, 2.5 million sites concatenated alignment) while accommodating site-heterogeneous substitution models and fossil-informed divergence time calibrations. We propose a parallelized computational workflow using HPC resources to (1) perform partitioned phylogenetic inference under heterogeneous models via IQ-TREE and RevBayes, (2) conduct Bayesian tip-association biogeographic reconstructions with stochastic mapping, and (3) fit state-dependent diversification models in a hierarchical Bayesian framework. High-memory nodes will enable joint analysis of genome-scale data with phenotypic trait matrices, while GPU acceleration will optimize likelihood calculations during branch-length estimation. The project also includes simulations to quantify the impact of gene tree discordance and missing data on biogeographic inference. Expected outcomes include a robust, time-calibrated phylogeny clarifying taxonomic boundaries in the clade, spatial and temporal patterns of diversification linked to Cenozoic climate shifts, and open-source scripts for scalable comparative analyses. This work will advance systematic methods for synthesizing heterogeneous data across deep evolutionary scales, directly informing conservation prioritization in biodiversity hotspots. By quantifying how computational constraints bias empirical inferences, the results will also guide best practices in phylogenomics. The requested resources are critical given the infeasibility of these analyses on standard lab servers, as preliminary runs on 200 taxa required >72 hours using 40 CPUs.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) interventions, including stent placement and atherectomy, are limited by an incomplete understanding of patient-specific hemodynamic and biomechanical factors that influence procedural success. Traditional risk stratification tools often overlook dynamic interactions between blood flow patterns, vascular anatomy, and device-tissue interactions, resulting in suboptimal patient outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations through advanced computational modeling requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose to develop a multi-scale simulation platform integrating time-resolved computational fluid dynamics (CFD), structural mechanics analysis, and machine learning to predict intervention outcomes. Patient-specific coronary anatomies will be reconstructed from high-resolution CT angiography and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) datasets (n=750), with hemodynamic simulations performed under rest and hyperemic conditions. Finite element modeling will assess stent-vessel interactions and plaque mechanical stress, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize device selection based on simulated outcomes. The computational intensity of processing ~5 TB/patient of 4D imaging data, coupled with the need for real-time parameter optimization across thousands of simulation iterations, necessitates HPC capabilities including GPU-accelerated parallel processing and distributed memory architectures. Validation will occur through prospective comparison with post-interventional fractional flow reserve measurements and optical coherence tomography findings. The anticipated outcomes include a clinically deployable decision-support system that reduces target vessel failure rates by ≥25% and a publicly accessible database of simulated intervention scenarios. This resource will enable unprecedented personalization of interventional strategies while providing a testbed for developing next-generation bioresorbable stents and hemodynamic-guided therapy protocols.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of specialized imaging and other diagnostic techniques to evaluate blood flow and pressure in the coronary arteries and chambers of the heart, and in the use of technical procedures and medications to treat abnormalities that impair the function of the cardiovascular system.

abstract: This project seeks to advance rehabilitation outcomes for individuals with mobility impairments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize personalized assistive technologies. Current exoskeleton designs often employ generalized parameters that fail to account for the biomechanical heterogeneity of patients, resulting in suboptimal gait training efficacy and prolonged device adaptation periods. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale musculoskeletal modeling, dynamic simulations, and machine learning to identify patient-specific exoskeleton configurations that maximize functional recovery. A diverse dataset of kinematic, kinetic, and electromyographic data from 200 individuals with spinal cord injuries will inform the development of physiologically accurate models. These models will simulate gait under thousands of exoskeleton control parameters (e.g., torque profiles, joint alignment) to map interactions between device configurations and biomechanical outcomes. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations, reduce computational time from months to days, and manage the 50+ TB of generated data. Machine learning algorithms will then analyze simulation outputs to predict optimal device settings for individual users, validated through motion capture and clinical gait assessments in a pilot cohort. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for rapid exoskeleton personalization, reducing device calibration time by 70% compared to manual methods. This work will directly inform clinical practices in assistive technology deployment, enhance mobility outcomes for patients, and provide an open-source computational toolkit for rehabilitation researchers. By bridging biomechanics, data science, and clinical rehabilitation, this project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in enabling precision rehabilitation technologies tailored to individual functional needs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human function, disability, and rehabilitation from the perspectives of the health sciences, social sciences, psychology, engineering, and related fields. Includes instruction in psychological, social, and cultural aspects of disability and rehabilitation; sensory and motor function and dysfunction; biomechanics and kinesiology; assistive technology; rehabilitation instrumentation and methodology; statistics; and health and rehabilitation policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of sustainable, high-performance wood-based materials and optimize pulping processes through multiscale computational modeling. A critical challenge in wood science lies in understanding the molecular-scale interactions governing lignin removal during chemical pulping, which remains energy-intensive and environmentally impactful. Additionally, predicting the mechanical behavior of engineered wood products under dynamic environmental conditions requires resolving complex, hierarchical structures across scales—a task infeasible with traditional experimental methods alone. To address these gaps, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will model lignin-polysaccharide networks in softwood and hardwood species under varying thermochemical pulping conditions, identifying reaction pathways to improve delignification efficiency. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning will predict moisture-induced stress distributions in cross-laminated timber (CLT), integrating anisotropic material properties and hygrothermal effects. These computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from lab-scale pulping trials and mechanical testing. The HPC environment is essential for handling the >10^6-atom systems in MD, iterative parameter optimization in FEA, and large datasets linking microstructural features to macroscale performance. Anticipated outcomes include actionable strategies for reducing energy consumption in pulp production by 15–20% and frameworks for designing moisture-resistant CLT panels with extended service life. By bridging molecular insights to industrial-scale processes, this work aligns with natural resource conservation goals, offering pathways to decarbonize wood product manufacturing while enhancing material circularity. The generated models and datasets will be shared openly to accelerate innovation in sustainable forest product technologies.
cip_title: Wood Science and Wood Products/ Pulp and Paper Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the analysis of the properties and behavior of wood and wood products and the development of processes for converting wood into paper and other products. Includes instruction in wood classification and testing, product development, manufacturing and processing technologies, and the design and development of related equipment and systems.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between collective visual attention dynamics and environmental design in public spaces, leveraging computational modeling to understand how psychological principles of perception and social behavior shape crowd movement patterns. While urban design often prioritizes physical efficiency, the cognitive and emotional factors influencing how individuals navigate shared environments remain understudied, particularly at scale. We propose developing a high-fidelity agent-based model (ABM) that integrates eye-tracking data, spatial cognition metrics, and real-world pedestrian flow datasets to simulate decision-making processes in diverse architectural contexts. The model will employ deep reinforcement learning frameworks to capture how individuals dynamically allocate attention to environmental cues (e.g., signage, crowd density gradients, aesthetic landmarks) while balancing goal-directed navigation with spontaneous exploration. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training neural networks on multimodal behavioral datasets (10,000+ simulated agents per iteration) and running parallelized simulations across parameterized urban layouts. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework quantifying how specific design elements modulate collective visual engagement and wayfinding efficiency, validated against 3D-reconstructed movement data from partnered civic centers. This work bridges environmental psychology, computational neuroscience, and architectural theory, offering evidence-based strategies for creating public spaces that harmonize functional demands with psychologically informed experiential quality. The resulting open-source toolkit will enable urban planners to prototype designs through a human cognition lens while advancing methodological convergence between behavioral modeling and spatial analytics.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in autonomous agricultural machinery operations through the development of high-fidelity computational models that optimize equipment performance under dynamic field conditions. Modern agricultural systems face challenges in balancing operational precision, energy efficiency, and environmental impact, particularly as autonomous technologies become more prevalent. Current approaches to machinery optimization often rely on static models that inadequately account for real-time interactions between equipment, soil variability, and crop responses. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-physics simulation framework integrating soil dynamics, plant biomechanics, and machine learning-based control systems. The computational approach will employ finite element analysis to model soil-tool interactions across diverse soil moisture and compaction scenarios, coupled with discrete element methods to simulate granular crop material flows during harvesting operations. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on these simulations to develop adaptive control policies for autonomous machinery, optimizing parameters such as tillage depth, harvesting speed, and implement geometry. The scale of these simulations necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources, as each parametric combination requires solving coupled partial differential equations across 3D domains with submillimeter spatial resolutions over operational timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive models quantifying the trade-offs between fuel consumption, soil disturbance, and crop yield preservation under varying agronomic conditions. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation smart implements and provide open-source simulation templates for agricultural engineers. By enabling precise, data-driven optimization of field operations, this work aims to reduce energy inputs by an estimated 15-20% while maintaining yield targets, contributing to both economic sustainability for farmers and reduced environmental footprint. The requested computing allocation will support parallelized simulation batches, neural network training on terabyte-scale datasets, and sensitivity analyses across 10+ crop-soil-climate combinations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural mechanization, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and demographic evolution of African-descended communities in North America and the Caribbean from the 17th to early 20th centuries. The research addresses critical gaps in understanding how forced and voluntary migration, economic shifts, and social resistance shaped community formation and longevity. Existing historical datasets—including census records, plantation inventories, maritime logs, and fugitive slave advertisements—are fragmented and geographically dispersed, complicating large-scale pattern analysis. The project will integrate these datasets into a unified geospatial-temporal framework, enabling dynamic modeling of population movements, settlement clustering, and resource access disparities. Computational methods will include network analysis to trace kinship and resistance networks, agent-based modeling to simulate migration decision-making under constraints, and machine learning to identify understudied patterns in textual archives (e.g., regional variations in labor resistance tactics). HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data, running parallelized simulations across multiple historical scenarios, and optimizing natural language processing models for handwritten documents. Expected outcomes include (1) interactive maps visualizing demographic changes and community resilience hubs, (2) a publicly accessible database linking dispersed archival materials, and (3) quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric narratives of passive adaptation within diaspora histories. By centering computational historiography on African-descended experiences, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of agency, survival, and cultural continuity in contexts of systemic oppression. The resource request aligns with institutional priorities to advance interdisciplinary, data-driven humanities research while addressing historical inequities in archival representation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and sustainability practices in independent hotel operations through high-fidelity simulation of guest behavior, energy consumption, and market volatility. The hospitality industry faces critical challenges in balancing profitability with environmental stewardship, particularly for small-to-medium hotels lacking access to enterprise-level analytics. Current pricing models often fail to account for real-time energy market fluctuations, localized weather patterns, and evolving guest preferences for sustainable accommodations. We propose an agent-based modeling system that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including smart meter outputs, regional energy pricing APIs, and anonymized booking patterns—to simulate operational scenarios at 15-minute intervals across a 36-month horizon. The computational approach combines deep reinforcement learning for price optimization with fluid dynamics-inspired models of energy flow through building systems, requiring parallel processing of 10^6+ parameter combinations. High-performance computing resources will enable simultaneous evaluation of 1) demand response strategies during peak energy pricing events, 2) carbon footprint trade-offs between pricing incentives and operational adjustments, and 3) workforce scheduling impacts from automated system interventions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that predicts optimal pricing-floor thresholds while maintaining net-positive guest satisfaction scores (NPS ≥ 40) and reducing energy expenditures by 12-18% compared to static pricing models. The hybrid methodology advances computational hospitality research by introducing lattice Boltzmann methods to guest flow prediction and establishes a novel evaluation metric (Sustainability-Adjusted Revenue per Available Room) that bridges hospitality management with energy informatics. Results will provide empirical guidance for regulatory frameworks governing small-business sustainability incentives in the tourism sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage and control; hotel facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; marketing and sales promotion; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotels and motel operations.

abstract: Child abuse pediatrics requires integrating complex, multimodal data—including medical imaging, electronic health records, legal documents, and social determinants of health—to improve diagnostic accuracy, guide interventions, and inform prevention strategies. Current approaches to synthesizing these datasets remain fragmented, often relying on manual review or siloed analyses, which limits scalability, introduces subjectivity, and delays time-sensitive decisions. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing computational models to automate and enhance evidence-based decision-making in child abuse evaluation and prevention. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to (1) train machine learning algorithms on heterogeneous datasets to identify patterns predictive of abusive injury versus accidental trauma, (2) analyze longitudinal social and clinical risk factors using large-scale probabilistic graphical models, and (3) simulate population-level outcomes of targeted prevention programs via agent-based modeling. Key computational hurdles include processing high-dimensional imaging data (e.g., skeletal surveys, retinal scans), parsing unstructured text from clinical and legal documents via natural language processing, and handling missing data inherent in multi-agency records. HPC infrastructure is critical for deploying deep neural networks on medical images, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in risk stratification, and optimizing resource allocation for prevention strategies through combinatorial optimization. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools to reduce diagnostic errors, risk assessment frameworks to prioritize high-risk cases for multidisciplinary review, and data-driven protocols to tailor prevention initiatives. By enabling rapid, reproducible analysis of complex datasets, this work aims to strengthen clinical-legal collaboration, reduce disparities in abuse identification, and improve outcomes for children affected by maltreatment. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to support translational research in child welfare.
cip_definition: Research on how to accurately diagnose abuse, consult with community agencies on child safety, provide expertise in courts of law, treat consequences of abuse and neglect, direct child abuse and neglect prevention programs and participate on multidisciplinary investigative teams, and manage child abuse cases.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing musical ensemble performance through computational analysis of complex conducting patterns and real-time ensemble interactions. While traditional conducting pedagogy emphasizes experiential training and subjective feedback, the integration of large-scale performance data and computational modeling remains underexplored. The research problem centers on developing predictive frameworks to analyze how conductors’ gestures, score interpretations, and rehearsal strategies correlate with measurable ensemble outcomes such as synchronization accuracy, dynamic balance, and expressive coherence. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multimodal approach combining motion capture data from conductors, synchronized audio recordings of ensemble performances, and computational score analysis. Machine learning models will be trained on this dataset to identify patterns in conducting techniques across diverse repertoire and ensemble configurations. Concurrently, physics-based simulations will model wave propagation and acoustic interactions in virtual ensemble environments, enabling parametric studies of rehearsal configurations and venue acoustics. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for training deep neural networks on high-dimensional motion and audio data, as well as large-scale finite element simulations of performance spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive toolkit to quantify relationships between gestural precision, communicative clarity, and ensemble responsiveness; (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing score preparation and rehearsal workflows; and (3) open-source software for simulating acoustic impacts of conducting decisions in variable performance contexts. By bridging computational musicology and conducting pedagogy, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-informed artistic leadership while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies in performing arts research. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the processing of terabyte-scale performance datasets and the development of scalable models for real-time conducting analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the art of leading bands, choirs, orchestras and other ensembles in performance, and related music leadership. Includes instruction in score analysis and arranging, rehearsal and performance leadership, music coaching, arrangement and performance planning, ensemble operations management, and applications to specific school or professional ensembles.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of Slavic cultural narratives and their transnational transmission through computational analysis of digitized historical texts, folklore archives, and linguistic corpora. While traditional Slavic Studies scholarship has relied on close reading and manual comparative methods, the scale and complexity of available digitized materials—spanning centuries, multiple languages, and diverse regions—require advanced computational resources to systematically identify patterns in cultural expression. The research problem centers on mapping how narrative motifs, symbolic systems, and linguistic innovations migrated among Slavic communities during key periods of demographic shift, particularly in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Using high-performance computing resources, we will apply multilingual natural language processing pipelines optimized for historical Slavic languages (including Church Slavonic variants and minority languages with limited digital infrastructure) to analyze a corpus of 50,000+ digitized texts from archival partners in six countries. Computational methods will include transformer-based semantic similarity modeling across languages, network analysis of motif distribution patterns, and temporal geospatial mapping of linguistic features. The workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to handle non-Latin orthographic conversions, morphological complexity in highly inflected languages, and dialectal variations within the corpus. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously undocumented narrative transmission routes linking diasporic communities, 2) quantitative models of language contact phenomena in border regions, and 3) an open-access annotated dataset of culturally significant motifs with cross-referenced metadata. This project will advance Slavic Studies by enabling systematic large-scale analysis of cultural production while developing computational workflows adaptable to other under-resourced languages. The requested resources directly address the technical challenges of working with heterogeneous historical materials at scale, which exceed the capacity of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Slavic peoples inhabiting Europe, Asia, and in immigrant groups elsewhere, including the study of the emergence and migration patterns of Slavic culture, languages, and populations.

abstract: Cellular adhesion and extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions are critical for tissue organization, mechanotransduction, and dynamic cell behaviors, yet the spatiotemporal coordination of these processes remains poorly resolved at subcellular scales. This project seeks to model the dynamic interplay between transmembrane adhesion receptors (e.g., integrins) and ECM components in 3D microenvironments using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate molecular-scale interactions across physiologically relevant timeframes. Current experimental approaches, while valuable, lack the resolution to capture rapid, stochastic binding events or the emergent effects of localized force distribution during adhesion complex formation. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with continuum models of cytoskeletal remodeling. The model will parameterize known biophysical properties of integrin-ECM binding, actin polymerization forces, and membrane elasticity derived from live-cell imaging and traction force microscopy data. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale of these simulations, which require parallel processing to track >10^6 interacting agents across milliseconds of simulated time while resolving nanometer-scale spatial changes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds in receptor clustering that trigger adhesion maturation, (2) predictive maps of force propagation during early adhesion site formation, and (3) testable hypotheses about how ECM composition regulates collective cell migration patterns. These results will advance fundamental understanding of cell-ECM crosstalk and provide a computational toolset for interrogating adhesion-related pathologies. The requested resources will enable simulations across diverse ECM conditions, significantly accelerating discovery compared to experimental trial-and-error approaches. This work directly aligns with cellular biology priorities by bridging structural analysis of adhesion components with system-level functional studies, while avoiding overlap with excluded molecular or genomic methodologies.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure, function, and regulation of cells as individual units and as components of larger systems. Includes instruction in cell chemistry, cellular dynamics, cellular replication and reproduction, cell anatomy, membrane function, organelles, cell adhesion and extracellular matrices, cell dynamics and motility, meiosis and mytosis, signal transduction, regulation, recognition and defense mechanisms, the cell cycle, cell metabolism and respiration, gene expression, and studies of cell types and characteristics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of distributed computing environments, particularly in edge and fog architectures, demands novel approaches to dynamic resource allocation that transcend conventional reactive strategies. Current methods struggle to balance latency-sensitive workloads with energy efficiency and infrastructure heterogeneity, often leading to suboptimal utilization and service degradation during demand spikes. This project proposes the development of an adaptive resource orchestration framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) simulations to model multi-tiered edge networks at unprecedented scale. By creating a parameterized digital twin of geographically dispersed nodes, we will train machine learning models to predict workload patterns while incorporating real-world constraints such as intermittent connectivity, hardware variability, and security postures. The computational methodology combines discrete-event simulation with multi-objective optimization algorithms, evaluating millions of potential resource distribution scenarios under diverse failure modes and attack vectors. HPC resources will enable parallel execution of evolutionary computation techniques to identify Pareto-optimal allocation policies that simultaneously minimize latency, energy consumption, and security risk exposure. Expected outcomes include a decision support system that proactively reallocates computational, storage, and networking resources based on predictive analytics, validated through simulation against industrial IoT and smart city use cases. This research addresses critical gaps in autonomic system administration by introducing prescriptive analytics to resource management, potentially reducing operational costs by 18-25% in preliminary models while maintaining strict service-level agreements. The resulting framework will provide network administrators with empirically validated strategies for maintaining performance parity across hybrid infrastructures, particularly valuable for organizations managing distributed systems with constrained local resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the computer operations and control the system configurations emanating from a specific site or network hub. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software and applications; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) networking; principles of information systems security; disk space and traffic load monitoring; data backup; resource allocation; and setup and takedown procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in the computational analysis of Hungarian linguistic and literary corpora. While Hungarian (Magyar) is a Uralic language with unique structural and historical features, existing digital resources and methodologies for its computational study remain underdeveloped compared to Indo-European languages. The project focuses on two interrelated objectives: (1) the development of a large-scale, diachronic corpus of Hungarian texts spanning the 16th to 21st centuries, including literary works, periodicals, and technical documents, and (2) the application of natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to analyze morphological, syntactic, and semantic shifts in the language over time. Computational challenges include managing non-standard orthographies in historical texts, optimizing tokenization for agglutinative morphology, and training transformer-based models on limited annotated data. HPC resources are critical for parallel processing of terabyte-scale text datasets, GPU-accelerated model training, and running comparative simulations of linguistic change. Expected outcomes include the first open-access corpus of Hungarian with diachronic annotations, a suite of NLP tools tailored to Hungarian’s linguistic features, and quantitative insights into language contact effects from neighboring Slavic and Germanic languages. These resources will directly support philological research, pedagogy, and applications in language technology—such as improved machine translation systems for Hungarian—while preserving cultural heritage through enhanced digital access. By integrating computational methods with traditional Magyar linguistics, this project aims to establish a scalable framework for under-resourced language analysis, with methodological implications for other Uralic and non-Indo-European languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hungarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in processing and analyzing large-scale historical datasets critical to public history initiatives. Public historians increasingly work with digitized archival records, oral histories, and community-sourced materials, yet existing computational tools are often inadequate for handling the volume, diversity, and unstructured nature of these datasets. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to identify, contextualize, and preserve historically significant patterns within such data, particularly for under-documented communities and events. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques to automate the transcription and semantic analysis of oral histories, enabling efficient tagging of themes, actors, and temporal-spatial relationships. Concurrently, graph-based network analysis will model interactions between individuals, organizations, and events in municipal archives to reconstruct historical networks of influence and resource flows. A geospatial component will integrate historical maps, census data, and urban development records using spatial-temporal modeling to visualize demographic shifts and land-use changes. These computational workflows require HPC resources due to the scale of data (including terabytes of text, images, and multimedia), the complexity of machine learning models for handwritten document analysis, and the need for parallel processing in generating multidimensional visualizations. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of processed datasets, interactive public-facing tools for exploring local history, and a methodological framework for applying computational analysis to community heritage projects. By enhancing the capacity to synthesize fragmented historical sources, this work aims to support more equitable preservation practices, inform public policy related to cultural resource management, and expand access to historical narratives for non-academic audiences. The project aligns with applied history’s mandate to bridge academic research with public needs while addressing technical gaps in current digital history methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of history and administrative skills to the recording of public events and the management of related historical resources. Includes instruction in historical research methods, the planning and administration of public history projects, and applications to specific problems in public organizations, government agencies, foundations, and other facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the economic dynamics of renewable energy adoption in manufacturing sectors, with a focus on how policy incentives and market competition jointly influence firms’ investment decisions. A key challenge in modeling these interactions lies in capturing heterogeneous firm behaviors, nonlinear feedback between regulatory environments and technological adoption, and the spatial distribution of resource costs—all of which require computationally intensive simulations to avoid oversimplification. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled agent-based model (ABM) that integrates firm-level microeconomic decision-making with macro-scale market equilibria. The ABM will simulate firms as autonomous agents optimizing production costs under dynamic constraints, including carbon pricing mechanisms, subsidies, and regional energy infrastructure limitations. Bayesian estimation techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters using historical data from 15 U.S. manufacturing industries, requiring parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling across thousands of iterations. Additionally, large-scale Monte Carlo simulations will assess policy scenarios under uncertainty, quantifying the economic trade-offs of delayed investment in renewables. The computational workload necessitates access to HPC resources for three core tasks: (1) running ensemble simulations to explore parameter spaces efficiently, (2) processing multi-terabyte datasets linking firm financial records to energy usage patterns, and (3) solving high-dimensional optimization problems for equilibrium analysis. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into the design of phased subsidy programs, estimates of sector-specific price thresholds for rapid renewable adoption, and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for policymakers. By advancing computational methods for industry-specific economic modeling, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical resource allocation frameworks and empirically grounded decision-making tools, directly supporting the transition to low-carbon manufacturing systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic principles and analytical techniques to the study of particular industries, activities, or the exploitation of particular resources. Includes instruction in economic theory; microeconomic analysis and modeling of specific industries, commodities; the economic consequences of resource allocation decisions; regulatory and consumer factors; and the technical aspects of specific subjects as they relate to economic analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize microbial conversion processes for lignocellulosic biofuel production while minimizing environmental resource use, a critical challenge in scaling sustainable bioenergy systems. Current bottlenecks in bioprocessing efficiency arise from poorly understood interactions between engineered microbial consortia, heterogeneous feedstocks, and reactor conditions. To address this, we propose an integrated computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale bioenergy systems. Genome-scale metabolic models of key cellulolytic and solventogenic microbes will be coupled with agent-based simulations of microbial community dynamics under variable feedstock compositions. Machine learning algorithms will iteratively refine parameters using experimental data from microbial metagenomics, metabolomics, and reactor performance metrics. Concurrently, life cycle assessment (LCA) models will evaluate water and land use impacts across hypothetical scaling scenarios, incorporating hydrology data and feedstock supply chain logistics. The HPC environment is essential for resolving the combinatorial complexity of microbial interactions, feedstock variability, and nonlinear reactor kinetics, which exceed the capacity of local computing resources. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for tailoring microbial consortia to regional feedstock profiles, optimized pretreatment and fermentation protocols, and identification of trade-offs between biofuel yield and environmental resource demands. This work will advance the design of scalable, regionally adaptable bioenergy systems that align production efficiency with natural resource conservation goals. By bridging bioprocess engineering and ecosystem sustainability analytics, the project aims to deliver actionable frameworks for reducing the water footprint and land-use conflicts associated with biofuel expansion, directly supporting the program’s focus on economically viable and ecologically responsible bioenergy solutions.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the environmental and economic impact of using plants and microbes for the production of bio-based fuels such as ethanol and biodiesel. Includes instruction in biochemical engineering, bioprocessing, bioseparations, conversion, feedstock, economics, environmental sustainability, hydrology, and natural resource management.

abstract: Clinical education in health professions faces significant challenges in evaluating and optimizing training strategies that effectively translate to improved clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. Traditional educational research methods often lack the granularity and scalability to model complex interactions between pedagogical approaches, learner competencies, and evolving clinical environments. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate and analyze educational interventions across diverse clinical training scenarios. Leveraging multimodal data from structured assessments, simulation-based training logs, and longitudinal performance metrics, we will implement agent-based modeling to replicate learner-clinical environment interactions. Machine learning pipelines will be deployed to identify latent patterns in skill acquisition trajectories and predict the impact of curriculum modifications. Computational demands arise from the need to process terabytes of time-series simulation data, train deep reinforcement learning models for adaptive educational pathway optimization, and run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess intervention robustness across synthetic patient populations. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale natural language processing of qualitative feedback from clinical educators and learners, paired with network analysis of interprofessional collaboration dynamics in virtual case studies. Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide competency-based curriculum design, personalized remediation strategies for at-risk trainees, and evidence-based thresholds for clinical readiness. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of health professions education—such as context-specific clinical reasoning patterns and adaptive teaching efficacy—this work will advance data-driven approaches to reduce variability in training outcomes. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source resources to support reproducibility and collaboration across academic health centers, directly addressing national priorities for equitable, scalable health professions education.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on education and administration leadership skills for clinical educators across health professions and specialties. Includes instruction in academic leadership, assessment, clinical decision making, curriculum development, ethics, primary care education, program evaluation, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing equitable access and long-term sustainability in urban park systems through advanced computational modeling of dynamic visitor behavior and environmental stressors. As cities face increasing pressure to balance recreational demand with ecological preservation, traditional facility management strategies struggle to account for complex interactions between seasonal visitor patterns, climate variability, and infrastructure degradation. The research will employ agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques to simulate park utilization under various climate scenarios while integrating real-world sensor data on foot traffic, vegetation health, and facility wear from municipal partners. High-performance computing resources are required to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10 years of park operations records, LiDAR-derived topography, and IoT sensor networks across 500+ urban green spaces. Computational workflows will parameterize visitor decision-making algorithms through reinforcement learning trained on anonymized mobile location data, enabling predictive analysis of crowding patterns and maintenance needs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support framework for adaptive resource allocation that reduces facility downtime by 15-20% while maintaining accessibility thresholds for diverse user groups. The models will specifically investigate trade-offs between centralized mega-parks and distributed micro-green spaces under projected urban population growth. By bridging computational social science with landscape architecture principles, this work establishes novel methodologies for data-driven leisure facility management while advancing foundational knowledge about human-environment interactions in non-STEM recreational contexts. Results will be deployed through an open-source toolkit to help municipal planners evaluate capital investment strategies against equity and sustainability metrics.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Facilities Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage park facilities and other indoor and outdoor recreation and leisure facilities. Includes instruction in supervising support personnel, health and safety standards, public relations, and basic business and marketing principles.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework to investigate multiscale interactions between stochastic atmospheric forcing and oceanic submesoscale dynamics, a critical but under-resolved component of Earth’s climate system. Current climate models struggle to capture submesoscale processes (1–10 km), which mediate energy transfer between turbulent oceanic flows and larger-scale circulation. This gap limits predictive accuracy in scenarios such as extreme weather preconditioning and carbon sequestration rates. Leveraging advances in mathematical stochastic modeling and high-resolution ocean simulations, we propose a hybrid approach combining GPU-accelerated, non-hydrostatic oceanic models with data-informed stochastic parameterizations of atmospheric boundary layer variability. The computational workflow will integrate direct numerical simulation of submesoscale turbulence using the MITgcm framework, coupled to a Markov chain-based stochastic forcing model calibrated via ERA5 reanalysis data. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve sub-kilometer oceanic features while iteratively training the stochastic model across ensemble simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of noise-induced transitions in submesoscale frontal stability, (2) improved parameterizations for climate-scale models, and (3) open-source tools for stochastic ocean-atmosphere coupling. The work bridges mathematical rigor in uncertainty quantification with geophysical fluid dynamics, addressing a pressing need to incorporate nonlinear, stochastic multiscale interactions into climate projections. Successful implementation will require sustained access to GPU clusters capable of handling 10^4 core-hour workloads per ensemble member, with petascale storage for 4D turbulence datasets. This interdisciplinary effort aligns with priorities in climate resilience science while advancing methodological synergies between applied mathematics and geophysical modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to atmospheric and oceanic problems. Includes instruction in chemistry, physics, atmospheric/ocean dynamics, climatology, weather simulation, climate modeling, mathematics, oceanography, and atmospheric science.

abstract: Radiation safety protocols in complex environments require precise understanding of radionuclide interactions with heterogeneous materials, yet current predictive models lack resolution to account for microscale variability in surface chemistry and environmental conditions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate radionuclide adsorption and penetration dynamics across diverse materials (e.g., polymers, alloys, biological matrices) under variable humidity, temperature, and contamination scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations coupled with Monte Carlo radiation transport modeling to resolve atomic-scale interactions of common contaminants (e.g., cesium-137, uranium-238) with decontamination substrates and protective equipment materials. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify nonlinear relationships between material properties, environmental parameters, and decontamination efficacy, training on simulation outputs and experimental validation datasets. The computational workflow will optimize parallelization across GPU nodes to manage the high dimensionality of parameter space (>10^6 configurations) and nanosecond-scale temporal resolution required for accurate free energy calculations. Expected outcomes include predictive models for site-specific decontamination strategies, a validated database of material-radionuclide interaction coefficients, and probabilistic risk assessment tools for low-dose exposure scenarios in mixed-radiation fields. This work directly addresses critical gaps in radiation protection practice by enabling evidence-based selection of containment materials and decontamination protocols, with applications spanning nuclear medicine facilities, legacy waste sites, and emergency response planning. The proposed HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in classical modeling approaches, which oversimplify interfacial interactions and fail to capture emergent behaviors in real-world contamination events.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health physicists, occupational safety and health specialists, and public health officials, to monitor and control radiation exposure and implement preventive measures in health care, work, and natural environments. Includes instruction in radiation physics, environmental radioactivity, radiological instrumentation, electronics of radiation detection equipment, radioactive waste management and control, safety and handling procedures, decontamination procedures, radioactivity testing and analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: Plants employ intricate signaling mechanisms to coordinate physiological responses, yet the role of bioacoustic vibrations in interplant communication remains poorly understood. This project investigates the hypothesis that plants transmit and interpret species-specific vibrational signals to mediate adaptive behaviors, such as resource competition or symbiosis initiation, in dense ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will model wave propagation dynamics through plant tissues and root-soil matrices to decode vibrational signatures associated with stress responses or mutualistic signaling. Finite element analysis and machine learning frameworks will simulate mechanical wave interactions across 3D plant architectures derived from micro-CT scans of root networks and shoot systems. The computational pipeline will integrate biophysical parameters (tissue density, Young’s modulus) with environmental variables (soil composition, hydraulic gradients) to predict signal attenuation, resonance frequencies, and receptor activation thresholds. By reconstructing vibration-based signaling landscapes, this work aims to identify universal acoustic motifs that correlate with observed phenotypic changes in controlled growth experiments. Successful validation of these models will establish a foundational framework for "phytoacoustics," an emerging interdisciplinary niche bridging plant biomechanics, environmental physics, and information theory. The requested HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to ecosystem-level interactions, enabling parameter sweeps across thousands of plant-microbe-soil configurations. Outcomes will advance our understanding of non-chemical plant communication, with potential applications in sustainable agriculture, such as optimizing crop spacing or developing vibration-based pest deterrence strategies. This work transcends traditional botany by redefining sensory perception in plants through a computational biophysics lens, offering novel tools to study organismal coordination in biological systems without neural networks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in botany/plant biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Punjabi language dynamics and literary heritage. Despite Punjabi’s status as a major global language with rich dialectal diversity and a vast literary corpus, systematic large-scale studies of its linguistic evolution, regional variations, and sociocultural influences remain limited due to computational constraints. The research problem centers on the need to model phonetic, syntactic, and lexical patterns across Punjabi dialects and historical texts, which require processing terabytes of unstructured data, including digitized manuscripts, oral recordings, and modern digital content. The project proposes a multi-phase computational approach. First, parallelized text processing and phonetic alignment algorithms will be deployed to analyze dialectal variations in spoken and written corpora, spanning major Punjabi dialects (e.g., Majhi, Doabi, Malwai). Second, transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to automate the semantic and stylistic analysis of pre-modern and modern Punjabi literature, identifying temporal shifts in thematic focus and linguistic innovation. Third, graph-based network analyses will map the diffusion of loanwords and syntactic structures across contact languages (e.g., Urdu, Hindi) in urban and rural contexts. These methods demand significant GPU-accelerated computing power for training deep learning architectures and processing high-resolution scans of aging manuscripts via optical character recognition (OCR) optimized for Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi scripts. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-access computational repository for Punjabi linguistics, comprising dialect atlases, annotated literary corpora, and tools for low-resource language NLP applications. The project will directly contribute to preserving endangered dialectal forms, enhancing pedagogical resources for Punjabi instruction, and informing policy frameworks for language technology development in South Asia. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to establish a paradigm for interdisciplinary research in less-resourced languages within digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Punjabi language (Punjabi) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of efficiently managing and preserving heterogeneous digital collections within libraries and archives, a task complicated by the exponential growth of digitized materials, born-digital assets, and legacy analog formats. Current workflows for metadata generation, format migration, and long-term preservation often rely on manual processes or siloed tools ill-equipped to handle the scale and complexity of modern collections. The research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable, automated frameworks for intelligent metadata extraction, format risk assessment, and adaptive preservation planning. Computational methods will integrate machine learning models—trained on curated cultural heritage datasets—to analyze text, images, and audiovisual materials for context-aware metadata enrichment. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be optimized to parse historical documents and handwritten materials, while computer vision algorithms will identify degradation patterns in digitized and born-digital media. A parallelized simulation environment will model the long-term impacts of format obsolescence and storage media decay under varying preservation strategies. By deploying containerized workflows across HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce processing times for large-scale collections by orders of magnitude compared to existing library-specific software. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for automated preservation prioritization, dynamic metadata augmentation, and predictive risk visualization, all designed to integrate with existing library management systems. This work bridges computational efficiency with archival theory, offering a replicable model for institutions struggling to balance resource constraints against the demands of digital stewardship. The developed frameworks will directly enhance accessibility of cultural heritage materials while establishing new benchmarks for computationally assisted curation practices in non-STEM research domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist professional librarians and archivists. Includes instruction in principles, systems, processes, and procedures of library and archive operation; library resources and services; processes of acquisition, cataloging, storage, and display systems; discovery and retrieval of requested materials; and management of books, periodicals, and other documents and records.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of persuasive communication in digital media environments through large-scale computational analysis of multimodal discourse. As digital platforms increasingly shape public opinion, understanding how rhetorical strategies—such as argumentation frameworks, emotional appeals, and nonverbal cues—interact across text, audio, and visual modalities remains a critical challenge. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the scale and complexity of modern communication ecosystems, necessitating advanced computational tools. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to analyze a corpus of 10 million social media posts, political speeches, and multimedia content from diverse cultural contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models to detect rhetorical patterns, sentiment trajectories, and cross-modal coherence at scale, while maintaining sensitivity to contextual factors like audience demographics and platform-specific norms. Parallel processing will enable real-time simulation of information diffusion networks to model how persuasive messages evolve through user interactions. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of effective multimodal rhetorical strategies in digital persuasion, (2) predictive models linking specific communication patterns to audience engagement metrics, and (3) open-source tools for ethical discourse analysis. These contributions will advance rhetorical theory by quantitatively testing classical frameworks against contemporary digital practices while providing evidence-based guidance for communication professionals addressing societal challenges like misinformation and polarization. The project’s scale—requiring simultaneous analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, complex neural network architectures, and dynamic network simulations—fundamentally depends on HPC capabilities for distributed processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and high-memory data handling beyond conventional computing infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific, humanistic, and critical study of human communication in a variety of formats, media, and contexts. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of interpersonal, group, organizational, professional, and intercultural communication; speaking and listening; verbal and nonverbal interaction; rhetorical theory and criticism; performance studies; argumentation and persuasion; technologically mediated communication; popular culture; and various contextual applications.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical grids, driven by the integration of renewable energy sources, distributed generation, and smart grid technologies, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize power transmission infrastructure. This project seeks to address critical challenges in dynamic load balancing, fault prediction, and grid resilience by developing a high-fidelity simulation framework for power transmission networks. Current analytical models often lack the resolution to account for real-time variability in energy demand, intermittent renewable generation, and cascading failure risks in interconnected systems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a hybrid computational approach combining machine learning (ML)-based predictive analytics with physics-informed numerical simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallelization of power flow analyses, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic fault scenarios, and training of deep neural networks on historical grid performance data. The computational workflow will integrate grid topology datasets, real-time sensor inputs, and weather-dependent generation profiles to model transmission line stresses, voltage stability, and failure propagation under diverse operating conditions. Key outcomes include a scalable software toolkit for utilities to simulate grid behavior at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, identify high-risk infrastructure segments, and test mitigation strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in traditional power system analysis, enabling rapid scenario evaluation for grids with 10,000+ nodes. The results will provide actionable insights for upgrading aging transmission infrastructure, improving renewable integration capacity, and minimizing outage risks. This work aligns with national priorities for modernizing energy systems while advancing computational methodologies applicable to emerging smart grid technologies. All developed models and simulation datasets will be made publicly available to support industry and academic collaboration.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installers, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and power transmission installation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing prevalence of diet-related chronic diseases in companion animals, such as obesity, diabetes, and gastrointestinal disorders, highlights critical gaps in understanding how nutrient metabolism interacts with individual variability in health outcomes. Current nutritional models for veterinary patients often rely on generalized population-level data, which fail to account for complex host-microbiome interactions, genetic polymorphisms affecting nutrient utilization, and dynamic metabolic responses to dietary interventions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a multi-scale computational framework to model nutrient metabolism in dogs and cats, with an emphasis on predicting individualized dietary responses in clinically compromised patients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including species-specific genome-scale metabolic reconstructions, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models of nutrient absorption, and longitudinal clinical trial data—into a unified simulation environment. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify metabolic signatures from multi-omics data (metabolomics, gut microbiome sequencing) collected from veterinary patients undergoing therapeutic diet trials, enabling the parameterization of patient-specific models. These models will simulate nutrient flux across tissues, predict biomarkers of dietary efficacy, and quantify the impact of dietary modifications on disease progression. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized optimization routines to handle high-dimensional parameter spaces and stochastic variability inherent in biological systems. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide precision diet formulation for animals with metabolic disorders, validated against clinical outcomes from partner veterinary hospitals. By establishing a scalable platform for in silico nutrition research, this work will advance translational applications of computational biology in veterinary medicine, offering a template for personalized dietary interventions that improve animal health outcomes while reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of models across diverse physiological scenarios, directly addressing the resource-intensive nature of in vivo nutritional studies in veterinary populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the chemical nature of food substances; the processes by which animals ingest, digest, absorb, transport, utilize and excrete food and nutrients; and their relation to animal behavior and health.

abstract: Critically ill surgical patients, especially trauma victims and those with multi-organ dysfunction, present complex, dynamic clinical trajectories that challenge existing outcome prediction models. Current approaches often fail to integrate high-dimensional, real-time data streams or account for multi-system interactions, limiting their accuracy and clinical utility. This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to predict patient outcomes and optimize treatment strategies in surgical critical care. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze heterogeneous datasets including electronic health records, continuous physiological monitoring, genomic profiles, and medical imaging. Machine learning techniques such as deep neural networks and ensemble methods will be employed to identify patterns predictive of deterioration, survival, and organ failure. Concurrently, mechanistic computational physiology models will simulate multi-organ system interactions under critical illness conditions. The integration of data-driven and theory-based approaches aims to overcome limitations of static scoring systems by capturing temporal dynamics and biological complexity. HPC capabilities are essential for training models on terabyte-scale datasets, performing parameter optimization in computational simulations, and conducting sensitivity analyses across millions of virtual patient scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for mortality, sepsis, and organ dysfunction, as well as computational tools for simulating treatment effects at both individual and population levels. This research will provide critical insights into the pathophysiology of multi-system failure while delivering clinically actionable decision-support frameworks. The requested resources will enable processing timelines unachievable with conventional infrastructure, directly supporting the translation of complex computational models into bedside applications that improve outcomes for critically ill surgical patients.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares surgeons in the diagnosis, treatment, and support of critically ill and injured patients, particularly trauma victims and patients with multiple organ dysfunction.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized surgical instrument design using biomechanical simulations and machine learning, addressing variability in patient-specific tissue responses that limit the efficacy of standard surgical tools. Current approaches to instrument selection rely on surgeon experience and population-level data, leading to suboptimal outcomes in complex cases involving atypical anatomy or pathological tissue properties. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate real-time intraoperative data with patient-specific biomechanics to recommend instrument parameters, such as grip geometry or force distribution, tailored to individual procedural contexts. The computational approach combines finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating tissue-instrument interactions with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to iteratively optimize designs under physiological constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling multidomain simulations across heterogeneous tissue types (e.g., fibrotic vs. healthy liver parenchyma) and processing high-resolution intraoperative imaging datasets. Parallelized FEA workflows will model nonlinear tissue deformation, while graph neural networks will map spatial stress distributions to instrument performance metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for adaptive surgical tool optimization and validated prototypes tested against ex vivo porcine models. This work bridges gaps in precision surgery and medical device innovation by enabling data-driven instrument customization, with potential to reduce operative times, tissue trauma, and revision rates in hepatobiliary and oncologic surgeries. The computational infrastructure developed will also provide a template for integrating real-time sensor data into procedural planning systems, advancing broader efforts in adaptive surgical robotics and AI-enhanced operative decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to innovate solutions and lead change within a healthcare organization. Includes instruction in innovation management, medical device development, evidence-based practice, systems thinking, information technology, healthcare policy and finance, organizational change, and leadership.

abstract: Statistical analysis of high-dimensional and complex datasets presents significant computational challenges, particularly in settings requiring uncertainty quantification or model-based inference.
