This project seeks to develop and implement scalable Bayesian methods for high-dimensional statistical learning, with applications to large-scale biomedical and environmental datasets. The research addresses two critical bottlenecks: (1) efficient sampling from posterior distributions in models with millions of parameters, and (2) robust model comparison techniques for hierarchical models with complex dependency structures. The computational approach combines adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms with variational inference techniques, leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed computing paradigms. Key innovations include the development of parallel tempered MCMC chains with automated tuning mechanisms, gradient-based variational approximations for structured latent variable models, and distributed implementations of Bayesian stacking for model averaging. Proposed implementations will utilize Python-based frameworks augmented with CUDA-optimized kernels for critical computational routines, with validation performed through synthetic datasets and case studies in genomic epidemiology and spatial extreme value analysis. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable systematic benchmarking against existing methods, large-scale simulation studies to assess frequentist properties of Bayesian procedures, and analysis of whole-genome sequencing data with complex phenotypic interactions. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for large-scale Bayesian computation, theoretical insights into the scalability of approximate inference methods, and applied contributions to statistical methodology for high-dimensional biomarker studies. This work directly addresses the growing need for statistically rigorous yet computationally feasible approaches to modern data challenges, with particular emphasis on maintaining uncertainty quantification at scale. Successful implementation will provide both methodological advances in computational statistics and practical tools for researchers working with massive, complex datasets across scientific domains.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and statistics or a specialization which draws from mathematics and statistics. Includes instruction in calculus, linear algebra, numerical analysis and partial differential equations, discrete mathematics, probability theory, statistics, computing, and other related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize resource allocation strategies in large, multi-school educational systems, addressing the complex challenges faced by district-level administrators. School districts must balance competing priorities—such as equitable funding distribution, staffing needs, facility maintenance, and compliance with policy mandates—while contending with dynamic variables like fluctuating enrollment, budget constraints, and shifting demographic patterns. Traditional decision-making approaches often rely on static spreadsheets or historical precedents, which fail to account for systemic interdependencies or simulate long-term outcomes of policy choices. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach coupled with machine learning (ML) techniques to create dynamic simulations of district-wide resource allocation scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to support the iterative training of ML models on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., student performance metrics, staffing ratios, facility utilization rates, and regional socioeconomic indicators) and to run large-scale simulations that capture the behavior of thousands of interacting agents (schools, administrators, students, and community stakeholders) across multi-year time horizons. The computational workflow will integrate geospatial analysis to evaluate equity impacts of funding decisions and discrete-event simulations to stress-test contingency plans for enrollment shifts or budget cuts. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between competing allocation strategies, predicts downstream effects of policy interventions, and identifies cost-efficient pathways to achieve district performance goals. This work will provide superintendents and system administrators with evidence-based frameworks to navigate complex resource allocation challenges while advancing computational social science methodologies in educational leadership. The project’s scale—modeling entire districts with 50+ schools and 30,000+ students—requires HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory data handling, and rapid scenario testing to deliver actionable insights within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leading and managing multi-school educational systems and school districts and prepares individuals to serve as systems administrators and district superintendents. Includes instruction in educational administration; education of students at various levels; system planning and budgeting; educational policy; educational law and regulations; public relations; professional standards and ethics; and applications to specific issues, cultural context, and geographic locales.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of individualized learning dynamics in Montessori classrooms through large-scale simulation and analysis. Montessori pedagogy emphasizes child-centered, self-directed learning, but quantitatively modeling the long-term impacts of specific material sequences, environmental factors, and teacher interventions remains challenging due to the multidimensional nature of developmental trajectories. We propose developing an agent-based modeling framework to simulate student interactions with Montessori materials, peer groups, and educators across varied virtual classroom environments. The computational model will integrate developmental psychology datasets, observational studies of Montessori classrooms, and probabilistic representations of material mastery timelines. HPC resources are essential to parameterize thousands of simulated learners, parallelize scenario testing across diverse pedagogical conditions, and process longitudinal interaction data. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds for material sequencing efficiency, quantifying the impact of environmental variables on self-regulated learning patterns, and generating predictive metrics to optimize Montessori teacher guidance strategies. Results will inform the design of adaptive training modules for Montessori educators, particularly in digital learning contexts where traditional observational training methods are limited. By bridging computational modeling with Montessori theory, this work aims to establish scalable methods for evaluating pedagogical effectiveness while preserving the humanistic principles central to teacher education programs. The proposed simulations will require sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep reinforcement learning components and high-memory nodes for processing multimodal interaction logs. This project represents a novel application of HPC capabilities in teacher education research, with potential extensions to personalized educator training systems and evidence-based refinements of Montessori credentialing standards.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Maria Montessori and her followers.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in algebraic and geometric topology by developing computational tools to classify high-dimensional topological structures under continuous transformations. The central challenge lies in analyzing invariants such as homotopy groups, homology, and transformation actions in complex configurations where manual or symbolic computation becomes intractable. Specifically, we aim to resolve open questions regarding the stability of links in higher-dimensional continua and the classification of non-free group actions on exotic manifolds. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining persistent homology techniques with large-scale simplicial complex generation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the systematic enumeration of equivalence classes under multi-directional transformations through distributed-memory Monte Carlo sampling and parallelized spectral sequence calculations. A key innovation involves implementing optimized algorithms for Čech complex construction at scales exceeding current literature, targeting simplicial complexes with cardinality >10^7. The computational pipeline will integrate rigorous proof-assistant modules (Lean 4/Mathlib) to maintain mathematical correctness during automated conjecture testing. Expected outcomes include (1) a classification scheme for (n, k)-links in 4-manifolds under homotopy equivalence, (2) quantitative bounds on transformation group actions in Zariski-type topologies, and (3) open-source software for homology computation in non-compact continua. These results will directly contribute to the Fields Institute's priority areas in foundational topology by resolving connectivity conjectures in geometric group theory and providing computable invariants for exotic smooth structures. The requested resources—particularly GPU-accelerated nodes for persistent homology calculations and high-memory nodes for sheaf cohomology simulations—are essential given the O(n^3) complexity of matrix reductions in homology computations at target scales. Successful implementation will establish new computational paradigms for pure mathematical research while advancing core theoretical knowledge in transformation topology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of unaltered geometric configurations under conditions of continuous, multi-directional transformations. Includes instruction in mathematical logic, proof theory, model theory, set theory, combinatorics, continua, homotopy, homology, links, and transformation actions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational frameworks for optimizing acoustic environments in adaptive architectural spaces. Traditional architectural acoustics design relies on static models and empirical adjustments, which fail to account for dynamic occupant interactions, real-time material responses, or variable spatial configurations in modern adaptive structures. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating a scalable simulation platform capable of modeling complex, time-dependent acoustic phenomena in architecturally fluid environments, such as transformable concert halls, hybrid indoor-outdoor venues, or reconfigurable urban soundscapes. The computational approach integrates finite element method (FEM) simulations with agent-based modeling to capture both physical wave propagation dynamics and human behavioral patterns. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs in iterative design optimization, while GPU-accelerated ray tracing will enable real-time auralization for stakeholder feedback integration. The project will validate models against experimental data from sensor-equipped prototype spaces. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation tools for parametric acoustic design, a database of optimized adaptive acoustic configurations, and evidence-based guidelines for integrating computational fluid-acoustic-structural modeling into architectural practice. By enabling precise prediction of how transient spatial modifications impact auditory experiences, this work aims to establish new methodologies for human-centric acoustic design in responsive built environments. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces inherent to multi-physics architectural simulations, particularly when scaling from room-specific analyses to urban-scale soundscape studies. This research occupies an emerging niche at the intersection of architectural technology, computational physics, and psychoacoustics, distinct from traditional engineering or social science domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the long-term evolution of trade networks and cultural exchange in the medieval Near East (c. 600–1500 CE). A central challenge in studying this region lies in synthesizing fragmented textual, archaeological, and geographic data—including merchant correspondence, tax records, and caravan route maps—into cohesive models of socioeconomic interaction. Traditional historiographic methods struggle to integrate these heterogeneous datasets at scale, limiting insights into how political upheavals, environmental shifts, and technological innovations reshaped regional connectivity. To address this, we propose a computational workflow combining natural language processing (NLP), geospatial analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM). Multilingual OCR and transformer-based NLP will process Arabic, Persian, and Syriac texts to extract structured data on trade goods, prices, and mobility patterns. These outputs will inform a geodatabase integrating archaeological site distributions, climate proxy records, and transportation networks. Finally, ABM simulations will test hypotheses about the resilience of trade systems to disruptions such as Mongol invasions or climatic fluctuations. HPC resources are critical for training custom NLP models on low-resource historical languages, processing high-resolution geospatial layers, and running large-scale parameterized simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) dynamic visualizations of trade network transformations across key historical transitions, (2) quantitative assessments of factors driving regional integration or fragmentation, and (3) open-access tools for computational historiography. By bridging qualitative sources and computational analytics, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of how cross-cultural systems in the Near East adapted to crises, with implications for broader debates about globalization and societal resilience in premodern contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: The graphic and printing industry faces increasing demands for high-quality, customizable products while balancing efficiency and sustainability. Current production workflows often rely on trial-and-error adjustments to manage variables such as substrate compatibility, ink behavior, and equipment performance, leading to material waste and operational delays. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and optimize digital printing processes at scale. The research will develop computational frameworks to simulate dynamic interactions between inks, substrates, and printer hardware under diverse environmental conditions. Machine learning models will be trained on multi-modal datasets—including sensor data from printing equipment, high-resolution image outputs, and material property databases—to predict optimal print parameters, detect defects in real time, and recommend maintenance interventions. Additionally, HPC-enabled rendering pipelines will be designed to accelerate the processing of complex variable-data print jobs, enabling rapid iteration for personalized designs. By integrating these computational tools, the project aims to reduce waste by 20–30% in test scenarios, improve color accuracy across substrates, and shorten production cycles. Outcomes will advance the integration of data-driven decision-making into graphic communications training programs, equipping operators with predictive tools to enhance precision and adaptability in industrial workflows. The resource request prioritizes GPU nodes for neural network training and parallelized simulation tasks, as well as high-memory nodes for large-scale image analysis. This work bridges gaps between traditional print production practices and emerging computational methodologies, fostering innovation in a sector critical to global communication and media ecosystems.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: Maternal and child health disparities persist globally, driven by complex interactions between biological, social, and environmental factors. This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of adverse maternal and child health outcomes by integrating heterogeneous data sources—including electronic health records, demographic surveys, and environmental exposure datasets—to identify high-risk populations and optimize intervention strategies. A key challenge lies in scaling computationally intensive analyses across large, multi-modal datasets while accounting for spatial, temporal, and socio-behavioral variables. To address this, we propose developing an adaptive machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble models that combine deep neural networks with interpretable causal inference methods. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing terabyte-scale health datasets, implementing distributed training of graph-based models to capture community-level health dynamics, and running agent-based simulations to evaluate intervention scenarios. HPC capabilities are critical for managing memory-intensive operations during feature extraction from longitudinal records, parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations for policy impact assessments, and reducing runtime for hyperparameter optimization across nested cross-validation folds. Expected outcomes include: (1) a scalable pipeline for identifying prenatal risk factors associated with preterm birth and neonatal mortality in underserved populations; (2) geospatial-temporal models quantifying the interaction between environmental stressors (e.g., air quality, heat islands) and maternal comorbidities; and (3) open-source tools enabling reproducible analysis of equity-focused intervention trade-offs. By enabling rapid iteration on complex models that synthesize clinical and public health data, this work will directly inform state-level maternal health initiatives and federal perinatal quality collaboratives, bridging computational innovation with translational health policy. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data storage, and high-throughput batch processing essential for achieving statistically robust, generalizable results.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: The management of chronic, multifactorial diseases in adult populations presents a significant challenge in internal medicine due to the heterogeneity of patient responses to standardized treatment protocols. Current approaches often rely on population-level evidence, which may fail to account for individual variability in genetics, comorbidities, environmental exposures, and health behaviors. This project proposes to develop predictive computational models that integrate multi-omics data, electronic health records (EHRs), and patient-reported outcomes to optimize personalized treatment strategies for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and comorbid cardiovascular disease. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze longitudinal datasets from 15,000+ patients across three health systems, incorporating genomic variants, proteomic profiles, medication histories, lifestyle factors, and socioeconomic determinants. Machine learning approaches, including ensemble neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees, will be employed to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response and adverse event risks. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate the impact of behavioral interventions on long-term disease trajectories, accounting for patient adherence patterns and care coordination workflows. The computational workload requires parallel processing of high-dimensional data (≥500 features per patient) and iterative model training across multiple hypothesis scenarios. Expected outcomes include: (1) a framework for dynamically updating treatment recommendations based on evolving patient data, (2) risk stratification tools for cardiovascular complications in T2DM, and (3) quantitative evidence to guide resource allocation for chronic disease management programs. This work directly addresses the program's focus on non-surgical clinical problem-solving while advancing methodological integration of computational biology and clinical decision science. The requested HPC resources are essential for maintaining data security standards, performing genome-wide association studies at scale, and achieving clinically actionable model convergence within project timelines.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of general medical services to adult patients with a wide range of non-surgical clinical problems. May included related research in behavioral aspects of diseases, patient and family counseling and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the efficacy of outdoor education programs in fostering adaptive leadership and environmental stewardship, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multi-dimensional datasets derived from field-based interventions. Outdoor education relies on dynamic interactions between participants, instructors, and natural environments, yet existing evaluation methods often lack granularity in quantifying how situational variables—such as weather patterns, terrain complexity, and group behavior—impact learning outcomes. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating predictive models that integrate real-time biometric data (e.g., heart rate variability, stress biomarkers), environmental sensor data (e.g., microclimate conditions, geospatial features), and qualitative assessments of teamwork and decision-making. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning algorithms, the project will simulate scenarios across diverse wilderness contexts—from kayaking expeditions to rock-climbing courses—to identify critical thresholds where environmental stressors either enhance resilience or impede skill acquisition. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of unstructured data from wearable devices and drones, training neural networks to recognize patterns in participant performance, and running Monte Carlo simulations to test risk-mitigation strategies. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for optimizing program design, evidence-based protocols for balancing challenge and safety in remote settings, and novel metrics for assessing long-term retention of leadership competencies. By situating computational rigor within a traditionally experiential domain, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven outdoor education research, with implications for curriculum development, environmental policy, and disaster preparedness training.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work as an educator, instructor or facilitator in parks, recreational facilities, camps and other outdoor settings. Includes instruction in leadership skills, wilderness survival skills, first aid, group processes, counseling techniques, environmental studies and instruction in recreational activities such as rock climbing, ropes courses, backpacking, kayaking and canoeing.

abstract: This project seeks to address persistent challenges in cross-cultural survey research by developing computational methods to quantify and mitigate the impact of metaphorical framing in questionnaire design on response patterns. While prior work has examined linguistic biases in surveys, the role of conceptual metaphors—cognitive structures that map abstract concepts to concrete domains (e.g., “time is money”)—remains underexplored, particularly in multilingual contexts. These implicit frameworks may systematically skew responses when metaphors embedded in questions resonate differently across cultural or linguistic groups. Our research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze parallel survey datasets from 12 languages, applying natural language processing (NLP) techniques to detect metaphor usage and structural equation modeling (SEM) to map its cognitive effects on response validity. The computational workflow involves three phases: (1) training multilingual transformer models to identify metaphor-rich survey items using semantic role labeling and conceptual metaphor detection algorithms; (2) implementing multi-group SEM across 50,000+ respondent datasets to quantify metaphor-induced measurement non-invariance; and (3) simulating alternative question phrasings through agent-based modeling to predict cross-population equivalence. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of textual and response data, running parallelized SEM configurations, and executing large-scale cultural simulations with adaptive sampling techniques. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for metaphor-aware survey design, empirically grounded guidelines for minimizing conceptual bias in transnational studies, and novel metrics for assessing linguistic equivalence beyond direct translation accuracy. By bridging cognitive linguistics with computational survey methodology, this work aims to advance rigorous comparative research in understudied linguistic populations while demonstrating how HPC-enabled text analytics can address emerging challenges in measurement theory.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on survey research design to gather data about behaviors, demographics, opinions, and data analysis to answer complex questions. Includes instruction in the analysis of survey data, cross-cultural and multi-population survey methodology, data collection methods, modes of survey analysis, quantitative analysis, questionnaire design, research design, sampling, survey error, and structural equation modeling.

abstract: Plants dynamically modulate root exudate composition to mediate rhizosphere interactions, yet the spatiotemporal coordination of these processes under drought stress remains poorly understood. This project integrates high-resolution metabolomic data, soil hydrology models, and microbial community dynamics to simulate plant-root exudate-microbe feedback loops in drought-affected systems. Current models lack the computational power to resolve root exudation at cellular resolution while scaling to ecosystem-level hydrology, creating a critical gap in predicting crop resilience strategies. We propose a hybrid high-performance computing (HPC) framework combining lattice Boltzmann methods for soil water transport, agent-based microbial community simulations, and machine learning-driven exudate pattern prediction. The model will parameterize experimentally validated root anatomical features from Zea mays (maize) and Sorghum bicolor, incorporating single-cell transcriptomic data to predict exudate composition shifts during drought. By parallelizing finite element soil simulations with GPU-accelerated microbial network analysis, we aim to achieve 10^6-fold scalability over existing rhizosphere models. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of drought-induced exudate metabolites that stabilize beneficial microbial functions, (2) quantification of root anatomical traits optimizing water-for-microbes trade-offs, and (3) open-source simulation tools for plant-soil feedback prediction. This work bridges plant cellular biology with ecosystem hydrology through computational scaling previously unattainable in botanical research, directly informing the development of drought-resilient crops through mechanistic understanding of root-mediated resilience strategies. Successful implementation requires access to GPU clusters with ≥500 nodes and 2 PB scalable storage to handle heterogeneous data integration across molecular, organismal, and environmental scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plants, related microbial organisms, and plant habitats and ecosystem relations. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and structure, phytochemistry, cytology, plant genetics, plant morphology and physiology, plant ecology, plant taxonomy and systematics, paleobotany, and applications of biophysics and molecular biology.

abstract: This project investigates the psychological dynamics of trust formation in human-AI collaborative decision-making, a nascent area at the intersection of cognitive science, computational modeling, and ethics. As AI systems increasingly mediate high-stakes domains like healthcare and finance, understanding how users calibrate trust—particularly in contexts where AI recommendations conflict with human intuition—is critical. Current frameworks lack granularity in modeling the cognitive and emotional factors driving trust adaptation over time. To address this gap, we propose a dual-method approach combining behavioral experiments with large-scale computational simulations. Participants will engage in a series of iterative decision-making tasks with AI partners of varying reliability, with multimodal data collection (eye tracking, galvanic skin response, and behavioral logs) capturing real-time trust modulation. These empirical data will inform the development of neural network models simulating trust adaptation mechanisms under different uncertainty conditions. The computational component requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train recurrent neural networks on longitudinal interaction patterns and to run parallelized agent-based simulations exploring emergent trust dynamics in population-scale human-AI systems. Key challenges include modeling the nonlinear integration of affective states and rational risk assessment in trust decisions, as well as simulating rare but consequential trust breakdown scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework predicting trust trajectories across human-AI interaction types, identification of critical intervention points for maintaining appropriate trust calibration, and evidence-based design principles for AI transparency features. This work will establish foundational insights into the psychology of human-machine trust while advancing methodology for studying complex cognitive processes through tightly coupled empirical-computational research. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the 15TB of experimental data, executing computationally intensive trust model simulations (>10,000 agent permutations), and achieving the temporal resolution required to capture micro-level trust adjustments in simulated decision cycles.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the integration of participatory mapping and high-resolution geospatial modeling to analyze emergent patterns of informal urban infrastructure development in underserved communities. While traditional geographic information science (GIS) research often prioritizes top-down data collection, this study addresses a critical gap in understanding how community-sourced spatial narratives—captured through mobile platforms and mixed-methods fieldwork—can be computationally harmonized with satellite imagery and sensor-derived datasets to reveal adaptive urban systems. The research problem centers on the disconnect between dynamic, community-driven spatial practices (e.g., self-organized transit networks, ephemeral markets) and static institutional geospatial databases, which limits equitable urban planning. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will develop scalable pipelines to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, including crowdsourced geotagged multimedia, LiDAR scans, and real-time environmental sensor feeds from three case study regions in rapidly urbanizing areas. Computational methods will combine deep learning architectures for spatial feature extraction (e.g., transformer-based models for irregular temporal geodata) with agent-based simulations to model how informal systems evolve under resource constraints. A novel aspect involves adapting graph neural networks to analyze multi-modal spatial relationships between physical infrastructure and social network structures derived from participatory mapping sessions. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for fusing community-centric qualitative data with large-scale geospatial analytics, advancing methodological innovation in critical cartography. The work will generate new insights into resilience strategies employed by marginalized populations, with implications for more inclusive urban policy tools. By pushing the boundaries of real-time spatial data integration and computationally intensive participatory models, this research expands the role of GIS in addressing socio-spatial equity challenges beyond conventional administrative mapping paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of map-making and the application of mathematical, computer, and other techniques to the analysis of large amounts of geographic data and the science of mapping geographic information. Includes instruction in cartographic theory and map projections, computer-assisted cartography, geographic information systems, map design and layout, photogrammetry, air photo interpretation, remote sensing, spatial analysis, geodesy, cartographic editing, and applications to specific industrial, commercial, research, and governmental mapping problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for adaptive, real-time typographic systems in dynamic digital media environments, where traditional composition tools struggle to balance aesthetic precision with computational efficiency. As content delivery platforms diversify—spanning variable-screen devices, responsive web interfaces, and generative publishing workflows—existing type rendering and layout engines often produce suboptimal visual hierarchies, inconsistent kerning at scale, or latency in reflow operations. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning-augmented typographic optimization framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will train neural networks on a corpus of professionally designed documents (10,000+ annotated pages) to model implicit design principles, then integrate these models with GPU-accelerated constraint solvers for real-time layout generation. Key computational challenges include parallelizing font rasterization across heterogeneous display densities, optimizing attention-based models for spatial composition decisions, and simulating reader eye-tracking patterns to validate aesthetic outcomes. The HPC cluster will enable large-batch training of transformer architectures on high-resolution page images and facilitate multi-objective optimization testing across 50+ layout parameters. Expected outcomes include an open-source composition engine capable of sub-100ms adaptive layout generation, quantitative metrics for typographic quality assessment, and empirically validated guidelines for AI-assisted design systems in journalism and digital publishing. This work directly supports communication professionals by reducing iterative design labor while maintaining editorial control, ultimately enhancing the accessibility and visual coherence of data-driven stories. Resource allocation is critical to process terabyte-scale typography datasets and achieve the necessary iteration speed for model refinement within the project timeline.
cip_title: Computer Typography and Composition Equipment Operator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to design and execute page formats, layouts and text composition, and to make typographical selections using computer graphics and other computer-assisted design programs.

abstract: The development of stable and efficacious pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations is a resource-intensive process, often hindered by the empirical nature of traditional trial-and-error experimentation. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling approaches for predicting the physicochemical behavior of complex drug delivery systems and cosmetic emulsions. The research will focus on overcoming challenges in preformulation evaluation, stability testing, and product reformulation by integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) models, and finite element analysis (FEA) of multi-phase systems. Key objectives include simulating API-excipient interactions under varied thermodynamic conditions, optimizing emulsion droplet size distributions through computational fluid dynamics, and predicting degradation pathways for small molecules in topical formulations. The computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated MD packages (e.g., GROMACS) for nanoscale system characterization and distributed ML frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow) to analyze structure-stability correlations across large formulation datasets. By enabling rapid in silico screening of prototype formulations, this approach aims to reduce experimental iterations in physical stability testing by an estimated 40-60%, while providing mechanistic insights into failure modes observed during accelerated aging studies. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-throughput simulations required to model complex semi-solid matrices and for training neural networks on historical formulation data spanning multiple product categories. Outcomes will directly inform industrial formulation strategies, enhance predictive capabilities in pharmaceutical development, and establish computational workflows that align with quality-by-design (QbD) principles for regulatory submissions. This work bridges critical gaps between computational pharmaceutics and real-world formulation challenges, offering transformative potential for both industrial pharmacy operations and cosmetic science innovation.
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize precision manufacturing processes, addressing critical challenges in material efficiency, toolpath accuracy, and production scalability within the precision production trades. While modern computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) tools have improved workflows, complex interactions between materials, tools, and environmental factors—such as thermal deformation or vibration-induced errors—remain difficult to predict, leading to suboptimal outcomes in high-stakes applications like aerospace components or medical device fabrication. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning, and real-time sensor data analytics. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model material behavior under diverse machining conditions, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize toolpaths and process parameters. These models require parallelized computations to handle high-resolution meshes, transient thermal-mechanical couplings, and stochastic process variations at production-relevant scales. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, reduce simulation wall-clock time from weeks to hours, and support training of deep neural networks on terabytes of sensor-derived machining data. Expected outcomes include predictive models for minimizing tool wear and material waste, a digital twin framework for adaptive process control, and open-source software tools tailored for precision production educators and small manufacturers. By bridging computational innovation with applied trades, this work aims to democratize access to high-accuracy manufacturing insights, reduce reliance on trial-and-error methods, and enhance the sustainability of precision production workflows. Results will be validated against experimental datasets from collaborating vocational training centers and industrial partners, ensuring translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in creating products using precision crafting and technical illustration.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing leadership decision-making and policy implementation in educational organizations through advanced computational modeling. Educational institutions increasingly face complex, dynamic environments where leadership strategies and policy choices must adapt to shifting demographics, resource constraints, and stakeholder expectations. Traditional qualitative or small-scale quantitative approaches often fail to capture the systemic interdependencies and longitudinal impacts of these decisions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) and network simulations that replicate organizational behavior in multi-tier educational systems, including district-office-school interactions, staff collaboration patterns, and policy diffusion processes. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will parameterize models with real-world administrative datasets (e.g., leadership turnover records, policy compliance timelines, and professional development participation logs) and conduct large-scale sensitivity analyses to identify leverage points for improving organizational resilience. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical workforce data to predict leadership pipeline vulnerabilities, while natural language processing (NLP) will analyze policy documents and meeting transcripts to quantify alignment between strategic priorities and operational practices. The computational demands of simultaneously modeling thousands of agent interactions across multi-year horizons necessitate parallelized simulations and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include a framework for stress-testing leadership succession plans, evidence-based recommendations for reducing policy implementation lag times, and visualizations of communication network efficiencies in diverse educational settings. This work will provide education administrators with empirically grounded tools to anticipate unintended consequences of organizational change initiatives and allocate resources more effectively. By integrating computational social science methods with leadership theory, the project advances interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of education policy and complex systems analysis.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Organizational Leadership and Policy Development with an emphasis on education. Includes instruction on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, education administration and supervision, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the complex dynamics of intergenerational resource allocation within families, a critical yet underexplored area in Work and Family Studies. While traditional research in this field relies on qualitative surveys or small-scale quantitative studies, the proposed work addresses a gap in scalable, data-driven simulations of how families navigate competing demands—such as childcare, eldercare, financial planning, and time management—under varying socioeconomic conditions. The research problem centers on understanding how systemic stressors (e.g., inflation, healthcare access disparities) disrupt decision-making patterns in households, particularly in marginalized communities where resource constraints amplify trade-offs. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate household behavior across diverse demographic profiles, integrating real-world datasets on income, health outcomes, and policy landscapes. Computational workflows will parallelize thousands of scenario iterations to capture nonlinear interactions between individual choices, institutional policies, and macroeconomic trends. Machine learning techniques will then identify emergent patterns in caregiving strategies and resilience mechanisms. By quantifying the cascading effects of policy interventions (e.g., subsidized childcare, flexible work mandates) on family well-being, this research aims to generate actionable frameworks for policymakers and educators. The use of HPC is critical to managing the high dimensionality of variables (e.g., cultural norms, geographic disparities) and enabling probabilistic forecasts at population scales. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools tailored for family resource educators and validated metrics for assessing the equity of caregiving support systems. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, economics, and human development, advancing Work and Family Studies into data-intensive domains while preserving its focus on applied, human-centered outcomes.
cip_definition: An introductory program that focuses on family and consumer science concepts and principles at the basic and vocational levels, and the various potential career paths open to interested students. Includes instruction in career, community, and family connections; family and family/consumer resources; human development; interpersonal relationships; nutrition and wellness; parenting; and career possibilities in various related areas.

abstract: Public health education campaigns face significant challenges in tailoring interventions to diverse populations and dynamically evolving health threats, particularly when addressing disparities in health literacy and access to information. This project seeks to optimize the design and evaluation of adaptive, data-driven health promotion strategies using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral datasets. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate the spread of health behaviors through agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate demographic, sociocultural, and spatial data from national health surveys, social media, and electronic health records. These models will account for multi-level influences on health decision-making, including social networks, educational messaging efficacy, and environmental barriers. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to identify population-specific predictors of intervention success and generate personalized communication strategies. Computational experiments will test hypothetical scenarios for disease prevention campaigns (e.g., vaccination uptake, chronic disease management) across varied virtual populations, quantifying the projected impact of different educational approaches under resource constraints. The scalability of ABMs requires parallelized computing to manage complex interactions between millions of agents representing geographic and cultural subgroups. Expected outcomes include a framework for rapidly prototyping equity-focused health education strategies, predictive metrics for campaign performance, and evidence-based guidelines for allocating outreach resources. By enabling real-time simulation of intervention effects across heterogeneous communities, this work aims to advance the precision and cost-effectiveness of public health promotion while reducing evaluation timelines. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the memory-intensive nature of network-based behavioral models and the computational demands of iterative parameter optimization in high-dimensional public health datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of educational and communications principles and methods to the promotion of preventive health measures and the education of targeted populations on health issues, and prepares individuals to function as public health educators and health promotion specialists. Includes instruction in human development, health issues across the life span, population-specific health issues, principles and methods of public health education, administration of health education campaigns and programs, evaluation methods, public communications, and applications to specific public health subjects and issues.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biological systems demands advanced computational tools to model dynamic, multi-scale interactions that traditional experimental methods cannot fully capture. This project seeks to develop and apply scalable, high-resolution computational frameworks to study emergent behaviors in cellular signaling networks, with a focus on poorly understood non-equilibrium processes. A key challenge lies in integrating stochastic, spatially resolved models of intracellular signaling with tissue-scale microenvironmental cues, which requires managing high-dimensional parameter spaces and computationally intensive simulations. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) for molecular-scale interactions, partial differential equations (PDEs) for microenvironmental gradients, and machine learning (ML) surrogate models to accelerate parameter exploration. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources for three critical tasks: (1) parallelized execution of >10⁵ stochastic ABM-PDE coupled simulations across parameter sweeps, (2) training deep neural networks on simulated datasets to predict system-level behaviors from reduced input dimensions, and (3) large-scale validation against newly generated and publicly available single-cell proteomic datasets. The computational infrastructure will enable time-resolved modeling of signaling cascades across minutes to days while maintaining subcellular spatial resolution—a feat currently unattainable with existing resources. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for adaptive time-stepping in hybrid models, an open-source software package optimized for GPU-accelerated HPC environments, and fundamental insights into how noise propagation in signaling networks influences cell population decision-making. This work will establish a template for resource-efficient multiscale modeling in computational biology while addressing critical gaps in predictive systems biology. Successful implementation will directly benefit the broader community through publicly shared computational tools and benchmark datasets, advancing capabilities to simulate complex biological systems with clinical relevance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computational theoretical approaches to understanding biological systems, including computational models of biological processes, computational management of large-scale projects, database development and data-algorithm development, and high-performance computing, as well as statistical and mathematical analyses.

abstract: The development of advanced drug delivery systems requires precise understanding of molecular interactions between active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and polymeric carriers to optimize stability, release kinetics, and bioavailability. Current experimental approaches face limitations in resolving dynamic, atomic-level behavior of these systems under physiological conditions, particularly for complex multi-drug formulations or stimuli-responsive carriers. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive modeling of API-polymer interactions. The research will focus on poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA)-based nanoparticles co-loaded with hydrophilic and hydrophobic anticancer agents—a system prone to unpredictable crystallization and phase separation that compromises dosing accuracy. All-atom and coarse-grained MD simulations will characterize drug-polymer interfacial dynamics, solvation effects, and aggregation tendencies across varying pH, temperature, and hydration conditions. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on simulation outputs and experimental literature data to predict compatibility scores for novel API combinations. The computational workflow requires massive parallelization to handle 10-100 million atom systems over microsecond timescales, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory capacity. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into microenvironment-driven drug-polymer interactions, (2) a validated ML framework for rapid screening of co-formulation candidates, and (3) design guidelines for next-generation nanocarriers with improved drug loading and release profiles. By reducing trial-and-error experimentation, this computational approach directly addresses critical bottlenecks in controlled release formulation development, with potential applications in combination chemotherapy and targeted drug delivery. Access to HPC resources will enable the generation of predictive models that could accelerate translational research in precision pharmaceutics by 12-18 months compared to conventional methods.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the formulation of medicinal substances into product vehicles capable of being stored, transported, and then introduced into the patient and behaving in ways optimal to therapeutic interaction. Includes instruction in statistics, biopharmaceutics, drug metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, physical pharmacy, pharmacological analysis, drug design and development, pharmacological biotechnology, chemical separations, spectroscopy, drug-host interactions, immunology, quantitative drug measurement, enzymatic transformations, and metabolic excretion.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of African-American/Black literary texts across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. The research addresses the challenge of systematically tracing thematic, stylistic, and intertextual connections within a vast and heterogeneous corpus spanning three centuries, including novels, poetry, oral histories, and folkloric narratives. Traditional close-reading methods, while foundational, struggle to map the scale and complexity of diasporic literary evolution, particularly in identifying patterns of cultural retention, adaptation, and resistance across geographic and temporal boundaries. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic similarity analysis, topic modeling to detect recurring motifs, and network analysis to visualize influence and citation patterns among authors and regions. Customized computational workflows will be developed to handle non-standardized orthographies in archival texts and oral transcriptions, while ethical AI frameworks will guide the responsible use of culturally sensitive material. The computational pipeline will process approximately 50,000 texts drawn from digitized archives, supplemented by metadata on publication contexts and author backgrounds. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized literary movements, quantitative evidence of transnational thematic continuities, and an open-access interactive database linking textual patterns to sociopolitical contexts. This work will provide a foundational resource for scholars re-evaluating canon formation, pedagogical approaches, and the role of computational methods in humanities research. By integrating HPC capabilities with literary scholarship, the project aims to deepen understanding of how African-descended communities in North America have shaped—and been shaped by—shared and divergent expressive traditions, offering new methodological pathways for intersectional and comparative studies in Black literary arts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive energy management systems for hybrid energy networks by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize dynamic interactions between distributed energy resources, storage systems, and demand-side loads. Current energy systems face inefficiencies in balancing variable renewable generation with fluctuating demand, particularly in decentralized architectures where legacy infrastructure and siloed control strategies limit responsiveness. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in simulating real-time, multi-scale energy flows and control responses across heterogeneous systems—a challenge exacerbated by the need to integrate high-resolution sensor data, predictive weather models, and equipment performance degradation algorithms. The proposed computational approach combines agent-based modeling with parallelized transient stability analysis to simulate grid-interactive buildings, renewable microgrids, and thermal-electrical storage systems at 1-second resolution over annual cycles. Machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning for optimal dispatch policies and graph neural networks for fault propagation analysis, will be implemented using GPU-accelerated frameworks. The project will validate models against experimental data from a campus-scale testbed instrumented with IoT-enabled energy meters and power quality sensors. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source simulation platform for hybrid energy system resilience testing, (2) predictive control algorithms that reduce energy waste during renewable intermittency by 15-25% in simulated scenarios, and (3) quantitative frameworks for lifecycle-aware component sizing in mixed-technology energy networks. By enabling granular analysis of efficiency tradeoffs across electrical, thermal, and fuel-based subsystems, this work will provide critical tools for training energy technologists in next-generation system design while supporting industry transitions toward decarbonized, adaptive energy infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing energy-efficient systems or monitoring energy use. Includes instruction in principles of energy conservation, instrumentation calibration, monitoring systems and test procedures, energy loss inspection procedures, energy conservation techniques, and report preparation.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between multigenerational family communication patterns and adolescent identity development in emergent digital socialization spaces. While prior work in Human Development and Family Studies has examined offline family interactions, the proliferation of hybrid communication ecosystems—integrating messaging platforms, social media, and AI-mediated tools—creates novel developmental contexts that remain poorly understood. The research addresses this gap by analyzing longitudinal, multimodal interaction data (text, audio, video) from 150 families to model how digitally mediated communication influences identity negotiation processes during adolescence. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets through three integrated computational approaches: 1) transformer-based NLP pipelines to detect semantic and pragmatic features in cross-generational dialogues, 2) temporal network analysis of interaction patterns across platforms, and 3) agent-based modeling simulating identity development trajectories under varying communication constraints. The computational framework will incorporate psychological theories of self-concept formation while advancing methodological integration of developmental science with computational social science. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of digital communication ecotypes in family systems, predictive models of technology-mediated identity development pathways, and open-source tools for analyzing multimodal family interactions at scale. This work provides critical insights into how evolving digital environments reshape fundamental developmental processes, with implications for designing family-centered interventions that support healthy identity formation in technologically saturated societies. The requested resources will enable processing of temporally dense, high-dimensional data that exceeds conventional computing capabilities, particularly for training domain-specific language models and running large-scale simulations of longitudinal developmental processes.
cip_title: Human Development and Family Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on basic human developmental and behavioral characteristics of the individual within the context of the family. Includes instruction in the conditions that influence human growth and development; strategies that promote growth and development across the life span; and the study of family systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of adversarial information campaigns and their impact on public perception during military conflicts. The proliferation of digital platforms has transformed psychological warfare, enabling state and non-state actors to deploy targeted disinformation at unprecedented scale and speed. Traditional analytical frameworks struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between narrative propagation, socio-cultural variables, and real-world conflict outcomes. This project addresses this gap by developing computational models to simulate multi-platform information ecosystems, quantify the efficacy of counter-narrative strategies, and predict cascading effects on strategic communication efforts. Using natural language processing (NLP) and transformer-based models, we will process multilingual social media datasets, state-aligned media outputs, and leaked adversarial playbooks to identify narrative templates and coordination patterns. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate population-scale responses to competing information streams under varying sociopolitical conditions, incorporating network analysis to map cross-platform amplification dynamics. HPC resources are critical for training large-scale language models on heterogeneous text corpora, running parallelized ABM iterations across diverse scenarios, and performing real-time sentiment tracking across geolocated datasets. Expected outcomes include a framework for assessing information campaign resilience, metrics for evaluating cognitive vulnerabilities in target populations, and decision-support tools for optimizing proactive communication strategies. By integrating computational social science with defense-focused media analysis, this work aims to advance evidence-based approaches to countering next-generation information warfare while maintaining ethical boundaries in strategic communication practices.
cip_title: Information/ Psychological Warfare and Military Media Relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the support of military and strategic operations and policy via the use of information as a tool of statecraft and warfighting. Includes instruction in information technology and systems, information security, command and control, satellite communications, global information dissemination, communications and media management, intelligence, psychological warfare, strategic planning, security policy and doctrine, and applications to specific operations, services, and scenarios.

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing resource allocation across multiple concurrent projects, particularly under conditions of uncertainty such as fluctuating material costs, labor shortages, and environmental disruptions. Traditional resource management strategies often rely on static schedules and deterministic models, which fail to account for dynamic, real-world variability, leading to inefficiencies, cost overruns, and project delays. This research proposes the development of a stochastic optimization framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and simulate multi-project resource allocation under uncertainty. The project integrates operations research, machine learning, and discrete-event simulation to create adaptive decision-support tools capable of dynamically reallocating labor, equipment, and materials in response to stochastic events. Computational methods will include Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risks, parallelized genetic algorithms to explore solution spaces efficiently, and reinforcement learning to refine allocation policies iteratively. By harnessing HPC resources, the framework will process large-scale datasets—including historical project performance, real-time supply chain data, and environmental sensors—to generate probabilistic forecasts and optimize decisions at enterprise scales. Expected outcomes include a scalable software prototype that reduces idle resource time by 15–20%, minimizes emergency procurement costs by modeling contingent scenarios, and improves adherence to project timelines through proactive risk mitigation. The research will advance computational methods in construction management by bridging gaps between prescriptive analytics and operational agility, offering a novel paradigm for resource optimization in complex, multi-stakeholder environments. Results will be validated against case studies from collaborative industry partners, ensuring practical relevance and scalability. This work positions HPC as a critical enabler of next-generation construction management tools, with implications for cost efficiency, sustainability, and resilience in global infrastructure development.
cip_definition: Any program in construction management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of identifying and diagnosing atypical reading development in early childhood education through advanced computational modeling of linguistic and cognitive processes. Current diagnostic tools for reading difficulties often rely on static assessments, which lack the granularity to capture dynamic interactions between phonological awareness, vocabulary acquisition, and decoding skills. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing machine learning models trained on multimodal datasets—including longitudinal reading assessments, eye-tracking data, and spoken language samples—to map trajectories of typical and atypical literacy development. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing these heterogeneous datasets, which encompass terabytes of audio, video, and text from 5,000+ K–3 learners in diverse linguistic environments. Neural networks will be deployed to detect subtle patterns in phonemic errors, gaze fixation durations, and syntactic complexity that correlate with emerging reading difficulties. Parallelized feature extraction pipelines will analyze speech recordings for prosodic and morphosyntactic markers, while transformer-based models will evaluate written responses for semantic coherence and orthographic processing. The computational outputs will inform the creation of dynamic risk profiles to guide early intervention strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities for large-scale data integration and real-time model retraining, this work aims to produce scalable diagnostic tools that help educators personalize literacy instruction. Anticipated outcomes include open-source algorithms for processing educational language data and evidence-based frameworks for integrating computational analytics into teacher training programs. This research directly aligns with the Language and Literacy Education program’s focus on bridging theoretical knowledge of reading development with practical pedagogical innovations, offering transformative potential for both teacher preparation and student outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach language and literacy subject matter areas, at various educational levels. Includes instruction in language development, typical and atypical reading development, and diagnosing reading difficulties.

abstract: Urban planning frameworks often prioritize quantitative metrics such as transportation efficiency, zoning compliance, and economic growth, yet struggle to systematically integrate socio-cultural dynamics—such as community identity, informal cultural practices, and heritage narratives—into decision-making processes. This gap limits the ability of planners to foster equitable, culturally resonant spaces in rapidly evolving urban environments. To address this, our research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled spatial simulation platform that models the interplay between cultural dynamics and physical urban form. The platform will synthesize heterogeneous datasets, including ethnographic records, participatory mapping outputs, historical land-use patterns, and real-time socio-demographic data, to simulate how cultural practices influence—and are influenced by—urban design interventions over time. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be employed to represent community stakeholders, cultural institutions, and informal networks as dynamic actors within a geospatial environment. Computational demands arise from the need to process high-resolution spatial-temporal data, manage complex ABM interactions across multi-scalar urban systems, and run iterative scenario analyses under varying policy constraints. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid calibration of models against real-world case studies in three diverse urban contexts, each characterized by distinct cultural heritage challenges. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolset for planners to visualize the long-term cultural impacts of zoning policies, infrastructure projects, and redevelopment initiatives. By quantifying traditionally qualitative socio-cultural variables, this research aims to advance evidence-based planning practices that balance technical efficiency with cultural sustainability, ultimately supporting more inclusive urban governance. The project bridges computational social science, digital humanities, and planning theory, establishing a novel methodological niche at the intersection of cultural analytics and urban systems modeling.
detailed_field: City/ urban, community, and regional planning
cip_title: City/ Urban, Community, and Regional Planning
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of planning, analysis, and architecture to the development and improvement of urban areas and surrounding regions, and to function as professional planners. Includes instruction in principles of architecture; master plan development; service, communications, and transportation systems design; community and commercial development; zoning; land use planning; applied economics; policy analysis; applicable laws and regulations; and professional responsibilities and managerial duties.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized interventions for individuals with complex communication disorders involving concurrent auditory and speech-language pathologies. Traditional approaches in audiology and speech-language pathology often address auditory processing deficits and speech-motor impairments in isolation, despite evidence that these systems interact dynamically. This gap is particularly critical for populations with conditions such as neurogenic stuttering with comorbid central auditory processing disorder, where heterogeneous symptom profiles defy one-size-fits-all therapies. The research aims to construct multiscale computational models integrating neurophysiological, acoustic, and behavioral data to simulate these interactions and predict individualized therapeutic outcomes. The computational workflow involves three phases: (1) large-scale analysis of high-density EEG and real-time speech acoustics data from 200 participants to identify neural signatures of auditory-speech network coupling; (2) development of biophysically informed neural network models simulating cortico-subcortical pathways involved in auditory feedback integration during speech production; and (3) machine learning-driven optimization of simulated intervention parameters (e.g., auditory masking profiles, speech rate modulation thresholds) using evolutionary algorithms. HPC resources are essential for managing the 50+ TB multimodal dataset, parallel processing of real-time speech signal analyses, and executing computationally intensive multiscale simulations. Anticipated outcomes include a novel computational framework for identifying patient-specific therapeutic targets and a proof-of-concept digital twin system capable of predicting intervention efficacy across varying noise environments and linguistic contexts. This work bridges clinical audiology, motor speech neuroscience, and computational modeling to address a critical need for precision rehabilitation tools in complex communication disorders, while establishing methodological foundations for HPC applications in integrated audiologic-speech pathology research.
cip_title: Audiology/ Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathology/ Pathologist
cip_definition: An integrated program that prepares individuals to work as both audiologists and speech-language pathologists. Includes instruction in a variety of communication disorder studies, audiology, speech pathology, language acquisition, and the design and implementation of comprehensive therapeutic and rehabilitative solutions to communications problems.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in healthcare administrative workflows through the development of predictive computational models to optimize resource scheduling and communication in clinical environments. Medical administrative personnel, including executive assistants and medical secretaries, face dynamic challenges in coordinating interdisciplinary care teams, managing high-volume patient interactions, and navigating complex facility operations. Traditional rule-based scheduling systems often fail to account for real-time variables such as provider availability fluctuations, urgent care prioritization, or cascading delays in shared clinical spaces. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing resources to analyze multi-source operational data—including electronic health record metadata, communication logs, and facility utilization patterns—to build adaptive machine learning frameworks. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing for triaging clinical correspondence, agent-based modeling to simulate staffing scenarios, and graph neural networks to map interdependencies in resource allocation. By processing historical and streaming data at scale, the models aim to predict bottlenecks in administrative workflows, recommend optimal task prioritization strategies, and automate context-aware scheduling adjustments. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for healthcare operations optimization, validated through retrospective analysis of institutional datasets and prospective pilot testing in partner clinics. This work bridges health systems management and computational science, offering novel approaches to reduce administrative burden, improve care coordination efficiency, and enhance the capacity of medical support staff to adapt to evolving healthcare demands. The requested computing resources are critical for training complex models on sensitive, large-scale healthcare data while maintaining necessary privacy safeguards through encrypted in-memory processing.
cip_title: Medical Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Medical Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing physicians and nurses, health care facilities and services administrators, and other health care professionals.
