Includes instruction in business and medical communications, medical terminology, principles of health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced commercial photography workflows, particularly in processing high-resolution image and video datasets for applications in advertising, archival documentation, and immersive media. Current workflows in dynamic lighting simulation, AI-assisted post-processing, and multi-sensor panoramic stitching are constrained by consumer-grade hardware, limiting output resolution, processing speed, and the ability to implement emerging computational photography techniques at scale. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop optimized pipelines for three core tasks: 1) physics-based rendering of complex product photography scenes using spectral ray tracing, 2) training domain-adaptive generative models for artifact removal in high-ISO capture environments, and 3) real-time alignment and blending of gigapixel-scale multi-camera arrays. Computational methods will combine parallelized OpenCL implementations for GPU-accelerated image processing with distributed deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) for model training on terabyte-scale visual datasets. The research will employ containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility across mixed-node architectures. Expected outcomes include novel benchmarking data for HPC-accelerated photography pipelines, open-source tools for automated quality assessment in computational imaging, and optimized neural architectures for commercial-grade image enhancement. By enabling complex simulations and large-batch processing of ultra-high-definition media, this work aims to establish new technical standards for resolution scalability and processing efficiency in applied visual arts. The resource allocation will directly support graduate student research in AI-driven photographic workflows while providing undergraduate commercial photography students with cloud-based access to professional-grade rendering capabilities through JupyterHub interfaces. Resulting methodologies will be disseminated through industry partnerships with regional media studios, bridging academic research in computational imaging with practical applications in advertising and digital content production.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences, and recording events and people, via digital, film, still and video photography. Includes instruction in specialized camera and equipment operation and maintenance, applications to commercial and industrial needs, and photography business operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing crop yield resilience under climate variability for smallholder farming systems in sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia. The research problem centers on the inability of current crop-climate models to integrate high-resolution genomic, soil, and meteorological data at scale, limiting actionable insights for region-specific cultivar recommendations. Existing models often oversimplify genotype-environment interactions, particularly for staple crops like cassava and drought-tolerant maize, which are vital to food security in these regions. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining mechanistic crop growth models with machine learning to analyze terabyte-scale datasets spanning 20 years of phenotyping trials, satellite-derived climate data, and genomic sequences from 10,000+ crop accessions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations of crop performance under 50+ climate scenarios (RCP 4.5/8.5 projections) while integrating heterogeneous data layers through Bayesian hierarchical modeling. Key computational challenges include optimizing memory-intensive genome-environment association studies and scaling dynamic vegetation models across distributed nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of genomic markers linked to climate resilience traits, (2) predictive maps of optimal cultivar deployment zones under 2030–2050 climate projections, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive breeding prioritization. By enabling rapid analysis of complex agricultural systems, this work will directly inform international breeding consortia and extension services, providing a template for computational agronomy in resource-limited contexts. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, 500TB of genomic-climate data fusion workflows, and real-time sensitivity analyses—tasks infeasible on existing campus infrastructure. This project aligns with global food security imperatives by translating computational advances into targeted strategies for climate adaptation in tropical agriculture.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of agricultural management and scientific principles to the problems of global food production and distribution, and to the study of the agricultural systems of other countries. Includes instruction in agricultural economics; comparative agricultural systems; international agribusiness and law; third-world development studies and economic development; and global applications of climate, soil, water resources, ecological and environmental studies, and animal and plant sciences.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the fiscal resilience of municipal governments facing climate-driven infrastructure shocks—an understudied intersection of public finance, climate economics, and computational social science. Municipalities increasingly confront budget destabilization from recurrent extreme weather events, yet existing public financial management frameworks lack dynamic tools to simulate compounding stressors such as deferred maintenance costs, fluctuating bond ratings, and intergovernmental grant dependencies under probabilistic climate scenarios. The computational problem centers on resolving stochastic interactions between infrastructure decay models, climate hazard projections, and fiscal policy constraints at scale. We propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating 10,000+ municipality archetypes across diverse socioeconomic and climatological contexts, integrating datasets from the National Flood Insurance Program, Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, and downscaled CMIP6 climate projections. The ABM will parameterize decision rules for bond issuance, emergency reserves, and service cutbacks under iterative budget stress tests. Machine learning components will train on historical fiscal crisis patterns to improve predictive accuracy of tipping points in public creditworthiness. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to quantify thresholds where climate physical risks propagate into systemic municipal liquidity crises—a novel contribution to fiscal vulnerability assessment. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for local governments to stress-test capital improvement plans against climate scenarios and a policy framework for optimizing adaptive fiscal buffers. This work advances public finance theory by formalizing non-linear relationships between environmental shocks and budgetary resilience while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in addressing emergent, cross-disciplinary challenges in public sector financial planning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the financial assets and budgets of public sector organizations. Includes instruction in public trusts and investments; the laws and procedures used to plan, prepare and administer public agency budgets; and the preparation and analysis of public budget projections and policies.

abstract: The effective management of research and development (R&D) initiatives requires balancing complex variables—including technical feasibility, budget constraints, and dynamic market demands—while ensuring optimal resource allocation. Traditional project management frameworks often struggle to account for the inherent uncertainties and interdependencies in multidisciplinary R&D environments, leading to inefficiencies in decision-making. This project proposes the development of a computational decision-support system to model and optimize R&D resource allocation under uncertainty. The research problem centers on integrating stochastic optimization techniques with real-time data analytics to simulate scenarios, prioritize projects, and dynamically allocate personnel, funding, and infrastructure. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will deploy Monte Carlo simulations and reinforcement learning algorithms to evaluate millions of potential allocation strategies across simulated R&D portfolios. These models will incorporate heterogeneous datasets, including historical project performance metrics, market trends, and technical risk assessments, to generate probabilistic forecasts. The computational workflow will be parallelized to accelerate scenario testing, enabling near-real-time sensitivity analyses to identify critical risk factors and trade-offs. Outcomes will include a scalable framework for R&D managers to visualize trade-offs, predict bottlenecks, and adjust allocations in response to evolving project conditions. By quantifying the impact of resource decisions on innovation timelines and organizational ROI, this work aims to advance evidence-based R&D management practices. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of multi-project portfolios and the high-dimensional parameter space of machine learning models. Successful implementation will provide a foundation for translating computational insights into operational strategies, enhancing the agility and competitiveness of R&D-driven organizations in sectors such as biotechnology, advanced manufacturing, and clean energy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage projects, programs and organizations involving basic and applied research, or specialized technology applications, in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in all aspects of business management applied to the leadership and control of scientific, clinical, engineering and social scientific enterprises; the management of related operational, security and logistical issues; and technical competence in one or more research disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of stylistic and rhetorical patterns in digital writing across genres and media using advanced computational text analysis. While contemporary writing studies emphasize the dynamic, multimodal nature of communication in professional, academic, and public contexts, existing research lacks scalable methods to systematically analyze how stylistic choices intersect with technological platforms, audience expectations, and cultural shifts over time. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods study combining corpus linguistics, rhetorical theory, and machine learning to examine a terabyte-scale dataset of digital texts (e.g., blogs, social media, technical documentation, hybrid genres) produced between 2000–2023. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing this heterogeneous corpus, which includes structured and unstructured data across multiple file formats, languages (limited to English per program scope), and metadata contexts. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract syntactic, lexical, and discourse features; train transformer-based models for genre classification and rhetorical move detection; and visualize diachronic patterns in writing conventions. Parallelized processing will enable comparative analysis of stylistic adaptation across three dimensions: platform affordances (e.g., character limits, multimedia integration), disciplinary norms (e.g., technical vs. creative writing), and intercultural communication practices. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible annotated corpus for writing research, 2) quantitative frameworks linking stylistic variation to contextual factors in digital composition, and 3) open-source tools for real-time rhetorical analysis integrated with common writing platforms. By bridging humanistic inquiry with computational methods, this project aims to advance evidence-based pedagogies for multimodal writing while demonstrating how HPC resources can support large-scale humanities research traditionally constrained by manual analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on writing for applied and liberal arts purposes. Includes instruction in writing and document design in multiple genres, modes, and media; writing technologies; research, evaluation, and use of information; editing and publishing; theories and processes of composing; rhetorical theories, traditions, and analysis; communication across audiences, contexts, and cultures; and practical applications for professional, technical, organizational, academic, and public settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the optimization of real-time, multi-stakeholder communication networks in global corporate environments using advanced computational modeling. As businesses increasingly rely on decentralized, cross-cultural teams and dynamic external partnerships, traditional communication frameworks struggle to address latency, information asymmetry, and cultural translation inefficiencies at scale. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to simulate how emergent communication patterns—spanning human and AI-mediated interactions—impact decision-making velocity and stakeholder trust in multinational organizations. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of cross-platform corporate communications (emails, Slack, press releases) with multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate stakeholder behavior under varying information flow regimes. The models will incorporate parameters for cultural dimensions, time-zone constraints, and crisis scenarios derived from real-world corporate datasets. Expected outcomes include a computational framework to quantify trade-offs between communication transparency and operational security, identify network fragility points in cross-border collaborations, and optimize message propagation strategies during reputation-critical events. This work bridges computational social science with organizational theory, offering novel metrics for evaluating communication resilience in business ecosystems increasingly shaped by AI intermediation and geopolitical complexity. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale parallelism for training culturally contextualized language models and running Monte Carlo simulations across diverse corporate hierarchy structures, directly addressing the combinatorial explosion inherent in modeling global, multi-channel communication systems.
cip_definition: Any program in business or corporate communications, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on leadership dynamics in complex organizational systems. While traditional leadership studies often rely on qualitative analyses or small-scale quantitative models, the complexity of modern sociotechnical systems—such as global virtual teams, crisis response networks, and decentralized organizations—requires computational approaches to model emergent leadership behaviors at scale. The research problem centers on understanding how leadership patterns arise, stabilize, or collapse in heterogeneous groups under dynamic stressors, including resource scarcity, cultural friction, and rapid information exchange. Current analytical methods struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between individual agency, situational variables, and systemic outcomes in these contexts. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate multilevel leadership processes across diverse scenarios. These models will integrate behavioral theories from psychology, decision-making frameworks from management science, and network dynamics from sociology. Computational experiments will systematically vary parameters such as power distribution thresholds, communication latency, and trust decay rates to identify critical tipping points in collective leadership efficacy. HPC resources are essential for running thousands of parallel simulations with high-fidelity agents (n > 10,000 per trial) and analyzing resulting petabyte-scale datasets through machine learning clustering techniques. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated computational framework for predicting leadership emergence in adaptive systems, 2) quantitative evidence linking specific intervention strategies to organizational resilience metrics, and 3) open-access datasets documenting leadership pattern formation under crisis conditions. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying decentralized leadership phenomena while providing practical insights for designing agile, ethics-aware leadership structures in multinational and digitally mediated environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the universal phenomenon of leadership in human groups. Includes instruction in general or multidisciplinary leadership theory, practice and philosophy.

abstract:
Orthodontic treatment planning for complex malocclusions requires precise understanding of biomechanical interactions between teeth, periodontal tissues, and orthodontic appliances. Current clinical methods rely on generalized force systems and population-level data, which often fail to account for patient-specific variations in bone density, root morphology, and soft tissue response. This limitation leads to suboptimal force application, prolonged treatment times, and risks of iatrogenic damage. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific biomechanical modeling with machine learning to predict and optimize tooth movement trajectories. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-resolution cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) datasets, simulate multifactorial tissue responses, and train predictive models across heterogeneous anatomical presentations.  

The project will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models incorporating individualized bone mechanical properties derived from grayscale-based bone density mapping, coupled with viscoelastic representations of periodontal ligaments. Fluid-structure interaction simulations will model blood flow and interstitial fluid dynamics during orthodontic loading. Concurrently, a neural network will be trained on retrospective clinical data (n ≈ 2,500 cases) to correlate pretreatment anatomical features with observed tooth movement patterns. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulation of 100+ patient-specific scenarios, iterative optimization of force vectors via genetic algorithms, and large-scale hyperparameter tuning for the predictive model.  

Expected outcomes include a clinically deployable tool for simulating treatment outcomes under varying biomechanical conditions, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches. This work will advance personalized orthodontics by quantifying tissue-specific force thresholds and identifying anatomical predictors of treatment response. The computational pipeline may later extend to craniofacial growth modeling and clear aligner design optimization. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning and high-memory CPUs for multiscale biomechanical simulations, necessitating the requested allocation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and techniques involved in the prevention and correction of dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES) to enhance grid reliability and scalability amid increasing energy demand and decarbonization goals. Current HRES designs struggle to balance intermittent renewable generation, storage dynamics, and demand variability, particularly at multi-megawatt scales. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity modeling, multi-objective optimization, and machine learning to design adaptive HRES configurations. The research will develop parallelized simulations of photovoltaic-wind-storage systems under diverse climatic and load profiles, leveraging historical weather data and projected demand scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute these computationally intensive tasks, including Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, mixed-integer linear programming for component sizing, and recurrent neural networks for short-term generation forecasting. By coupling these methods, the framework will identify Pareto-optimal system designs that minimize levelized costs while maximizing renewable penetration and fault tolerance. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for HRES planning, validated against operational data from three regional grids, and policy-ready metrics quantifying storage requirements under 2030 decarbonization targets. The scalability of solutions will be tested through distributed computing experiments simulating 10,000+ node networks, enabling insights into infrastructure redundancy needs. This work directly supports the transition to resilient, low-carbon energy systems by providing computationally accessible strategies to integrate variable renewables at scale. Successful implementation will reduce reliance on heuristic design practices and enable data-driven decision-making for utilities and policymakers.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex, interconnected questions at the intersection of environmental change, socio-cultural dynamics, and economic resilience in underserved global communities. Traditional disciplinary approaches often fail to capture the nonlinear feedback loops and emergent behaviors inherent in systems where ecological stressors, such as drought or deforestation, intersect with human decision-making, resource allocation, and cultural practices. By integrating heterogeneous datasets—including geospatial climate records, ethnographic fieldwork transcripts, and longitudinal economic surveys—this research aims to develop agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate adaptive responses to environmental shocks. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing multi-modal data (e.g., converting qualitative narratives into quantifiable decision trees), calibrating models using Bayesian inference, and running ensemble simulations to explore scenario-dependent outcomes under varying policy interventions. A key innovation lies in coupling machine learning classifiers with dynamical systems theory to identify tipping points in socio-ecological systems. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the scale of these simulations, which require parallel processing of thousands of stochastic realizations and real-time sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible computational framework for interdisciplinary resilience studies, (2) empirically grounded insights into how localized cultural practices mediate the efficacy of top-down climate adaptation policies, and (3) methodological advances in reconciling qualitative and quantitative data within unified modeling environments. This work will directly inform collaborative efforts with community organizations while contributing to broader theoretical debates about equity in resource distribution during systemic crises. By situating itself at the nexus of environmental humanities, computational social science, and complexity theory, the project exemplifies the transformative potential of undifferentiated general studies in addressing 21st-century grand challenges.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated program that includes instruction in the general arts, general science, or unstructured studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural and linguistic identities across Russia, Central Europe, Eastern Europe, and Eurasia through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The research problem centers on gaps in understanding how transnational cultural narratives—expressed in literature, media, and public discourse—have shaped collective identities in these regions, particularly following geopolitical shifts such as the dissolution of the Soviet Union and EU expansion. Existing studies often rely on localized, manual analysis, limiting the scope to detect macro-level patterns across languages, time periods, and media formats. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, image recognition, and multilingual natural language processing (NLP) models to examine digitized archives, periodicals, and contemporary digital media in over 15 languages, including Russian, Ukrainian, Baltic, and Central Asian languages. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for low-resource languages, cross-lingual sentiment analysis to trace narrative diffusion, and network analysis of thematic clusters in visual propaganda. HPC resources are critical due to the scale of data (estimated 50 TB of unstructured text and images), the complexity of parallelizing multilingual model training, and the need for GPU-accelerated processing of image metadata. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible dataset of annotated cultural narratives spanning 1990–2020, (2) computational workflows tailored to understudied Eurasian languages, and (3) visualizations mapping the interplay between regional identity discourses and transnational cultural flows. By integrating area studies expertise with machine learning, this work aims to advance methodologies in digital humanities while providing policymakers and cultural institutions with evidence-based insights into identity dynamics in a geopolitically pivotal region.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Russian, Central European, East European and Eurasian Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the region encompassing Russia, Central Europe, Eastern Europe, and Eurasia, including the Balkan, Baltic, Caucasus, and Central Asian states that were republics of the former Soviet Union.

abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders represent a leading cause of global disability, yet current diagnostic imaging modalities face limitations in early detection and prognostic accuracy. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing advanced computational tools to analyze multi-modal imaging data, integrating quantitative biomarkers with clinical parameters for improved patient stratification and outcome prediction. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a two-pronged approach: (1) the implementation of deep learning architectures, including 3D convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks, to automate segmentation of osseous and soft tissue structures across MRI, CT, and dynamic radiograph series while extracting novel imaging biomarkers; (2) the creation of multi-scale biomechanical models utilizing finite element analysis to simulate load distribution patterns in pathological joints. The computational pipeline will process terabytes of imaging data from longitudinal cohorts of osteoarthritis, spinal degeneration, and traumatic injury patients. HPC capabilities will enable parallel processing of high-resolution volumetric datasets, accelerate iterative model training through GPU-optimized frameworks, and facilitate complex biomechanical simulations across anatomical variations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for disease progression in early osteoarthritis, optimized surgical planning parameters for spinal stabilization procedures, and machine learning algorithms capable of identifying subvisual degenerative patterns in articular cartilage. This resource-intensive computational methodology aims to establish new standards for image-based assessment in musculoskeletal radiology, directly informing personalized treatment strategies and improving functional outcomes for patients across the care continuum.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders or injuries of the joints, bones, muscles, and spine in adults and children.

abstract: Parasitic infections remain a critical global health challenge, with complex host-parasite interactions driving pathogenicity, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. This project seeks to advance understanding of molecular mechanisms underlying parasitic adaptation by integrating large-scale genomic, proteomic, and host immune response datasets from clinically relevant parasites, including *Plasmodium* spp., *Leishmania* spp., and helminths. A key challenge lies in analyzing the dynamic interplay between parasite virulence factors, host cell receptors, and immune modulation strategies across spatial and temporal scales—a task requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the volume and complexity of multi-omics data. We propose a computational framework combining molecular dynamics simulations of parasite-host protein interactions, phylogenetic comparative analyses of virulence gene evolution, and machine learning models to predict antigenic variation patterns. Simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to model conformational changes in critical parasite proteins (e.g., MSP-1 in *Plasmodium*, gp63 in *Leishmania*) during host cell invasion, while population genomic datasets (>1,000 parasite isolates) will be analyzed to identify selective pressures driving drug resistance. Machine learning pipelines will integrate proteomic and immunological data to map conserved epitopes as potential vaccine targets. This work directly addresses gaps in predicting cross-species infectivity and designing targeted interventions. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of structurally stable parasite proteins for chemotherapeutic development, (2) evolutionary insights into antigenic diversity across parasite lineages, and (3) predictive models of immune evasion strategies in zoonotic parasites. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations that are infeasible on local clusters. By elucidating mechanisms of parasitic adaptation, this research aims to inform novel strategies for disease control, aligning with global priorities in parasitology and translational immunology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biological organisms living in ecologically exploitative and competitive relationships with host organisms, and the role of parasites in causing injury, disease, and environmental damage. Includes instruction in vector biology, immunoparasitology, medical parasitology, molecular biology of parasitical associations, veterinary and comparative parasitology, chemotherapeutics, and ecological and systematic parasitology.

abstract: Land use planning faces critical challenges in balancing urban and rural development with ecological preservation, particularly under climate change and population growth. Current models often lack the resolution and integration needed to simulate complex interactions between socioeconomic drivers, environmental constraints, and policy interventions at regional scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based land use change model that integrates multi-source geospatial data, climate projections, and stakeholder-defined policy scenarios to evaluate trade-offs between development goals and ecosystem services. The computational approach will leverage machine learning algorithms to parameterize land use decision-making processes based on historical patterns, while physics-based hydrological and ecological modules will assess impacts on water resources, carbon sequestration, and biodiversity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for running ensemble simulations across decadal timeframes at 100m spatial resolution, processing terabytes of satellite imagery and LiDAR data, and conducting sensitivity analyses of policy variables through Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include a scalable modeling framework to (1) quantify how zoning policies, conservation incentives, and infrastructure investments affect landscape-level sustainability metrics, (2) identify conflict zones where development pressures threaten critical habitats or watershed functions, and (3) optimize land allocation strategies under climate uncertainty. The project will provide planners and policymakers with an open-source decision-support tool validated for three rapidly urbanizing watersheds in the Pacific Northwest, directly addressing the program’s focus on evidence-based resource management. By enabling simultaneous analysis of economic viability, environmental regulations, and community needs at unprecedented granularity, this work advances computational capabilities in spatial planning while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between geosciences, data science, and public policy domains.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Land Use Planning and Management/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how public and/or private land and associated resources can be preserved, developed, and used for maximum social, economic, and environmental benefit. Includes instruction in natural resources management, natural resource economics, public policy, regional and land use planning, environmental impact assessment, applicable law and regulations, government and politics, principles of business and real estate land use, statistical and analytical tools, computer applications, mapping and report preparation, site analysis, cost analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern security infrastructures—spanning cyber-physical systems, decentralized IoT networks, and human-centric threat landscapes—demands advanced computational tools to model emergent risks and optimize mitigation strategies. This project seeks to address the critical gap in scalable, adaptive frameworks for securing hybrid environments where human behavior, digital interfaces, and physical infrastructure intersect. Traditional security paradigms often treat these domains in isolation, leading to vulnerabilities at their convergence points. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-agent systems that integrate real-time behavioral data, network traffic patterns, and stochastic threat propagation models. The research will develop a dynamic, graph-based simulation platform capable of modeling large-scale scenarios, such as crowd behavior during evacuation protocols under cyber-physical attacks or cascading failures in smart city grids. Machine learning algorithms will be deployed to identify latent threat signatures within heterogeneous datasets, while Monte Carlo methods will assess risk probabilities under varying constraints. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU clusters, the project aims to achieve sub-second latency in threat response simulations, enabling preemptive security policy testing. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for simulating hybrid threat scenarios, predictive models for infrastructure resilience benchmarking, and empirically validated strategies to mitigate cross-domain vulnerabilities. This work will advance security science by establishing a methodological bridge between computational social dynamics, cybersecurity, and critical infrastructure management, offering actionable insights for policymakers and operational stakeholders in an era of increasingly interconnected risks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in security science and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Medication-related errors and inefficiencies in healthcare systems contribute significantly to adverse patient outcomes and increased costs. Current approaches to optimizing medication systems often lack the computational power to model complex, real-world scenarios at scale, limiting their predictive accuracy and practical utility. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that simulate medication delivery processes, predict system failures, and identify optimal intervention strategies. The research will integrate heterogeneous data sources, including electronic health records, pharmacy dispensing logs, and real-time sensor data from smart medication dispensers, to construct a multi-scale simulation framework. Agent-based modeling will be employed to capture interactions between patients, healthcare providers, and infrastructure, while machine learning algorithms will analyze temporal patterns associated with medication errors. Monte Carlo methods will assess the probabilistic impact of operational changes under diverse scenarios. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need for parallel processing of large datasets, real-time optimization of stochastic models, and high-dimensional parameter space exploration—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-risk workflow components, predictive tools for error prevention, and evidence-based recommendations for system redesign. By enabling granular analysis of medication operations at unprecedented scales, this research aims to establish a foundation for data-driven decision-making in clinical settings, ultimately enhancing patient safety and operational efficiency in healthcare delivery.
cip_definition: Research focused on Medication Systems and Operations

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamical evolution of galactic substructures in high-redshift galaxy clusters, with a focus on resolving the interplay between dark matter halos and baryonic processes during cluster assembly. Current simulations struggle to capture the multiscale physics of these environments, particularly the feedback mechanisms between star formation, interstellar medium (ISM) thermodynamics, and gravitational interactions at sub-kiloparsec resolutions across cosmologically representative volumes. We propose a suite of adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) hydrodynamical simulations using the Enzo code, coupled with a novel subgrid model for turbulent ISM phases, to track the formation of stellar populations and their chemical enrichment histories in protocluster regions at z ≈ 2–4. The simulations will integrate dark matter dynamics, radiative cooling, and spatially varying ultraviolet background radiation, with initial conditions derived from Planck Collaboration cosmological parameters. Each realization will span 100 Mpc³ volumes, requiring 50 million core-hours to achieve the necessary spatial and mass resolution. Key deliverables include a publicly accessible catalog of simulated protoclusters, quantifying the statistical prevalence of tidal stellar streams and globular cluster precursors as tracers of hierarchical merging. The outcomes will directly inform observational strategies for JWST and the Vera Rubin Observatory by identifying optimal spectral diagnostics and spatial tracers of early cluster assembly. This work addresses a critical gap in theoretical models of galaxy evolution, where existing predictions diverge significantly from recent kinematic observations of high-z quasar host environments. By resolving the coupling between dark matter substructure survival timescales and baryonic feedback, the project will constrain the role of mergers in establishing the mass-metallicity relation of present-day galaxy clusters. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter space exploration currently infeasible with local computing resources, particularly in managing the memory overhead of high-resolution AMR datasets across distributed nodes.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the planetary, galactic, and stellar phenomena occurring in outer space. Includes instruction in celestial mechanics, cosmology, stellar physics, galactic evolution, quasars, stellar distribution and motion, interstellar medium, atomic and molecular constituents of astronomical phenomena, planetary science, solar system evolution, and specific methodologies such as optical astronomy, radioastronomy, and theoretical astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the neurophysiological and biomechanical effects of yoga-based interventions, with the goal of optimizing therapeutic protocols for chronic pain and stress-related disorders. Despite growing evidence of yoga’s clinical benefits, the lack of mechanistic, individualized models limits its integration into precision health paradigms. Current approaches rely on generalized cohort studies, overlooking inter-subject variability in anatomy, neural plasticity, and stress response dynamics. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-scale interactions between yoga practices (e.g., asana sequences, pranayama techniques) and physiological systems. The research integrates three computational strands: (1) biophysical modeling of musculoskeletal stress distribution during posture transitions using finite element analysis; (2) dynamic network modeling of autonomic nervous system modulation via heart rate variability and EEG data from wearable sensors; and (3) machine learning-driven optimization of personalized yoga therapy sequences based on individual biomarkers and comorbidities. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across anatomically diverse digital twins and real-time analysis of high-density physiological datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for mapping yoga interventions to patient-specific neurobiomechanical profiles, with applications in chronic low back pain, anxiety disorders, and post-stroke rehabilitation. The project bridges gaps between traditional yogic knowledge systems and computational health sciences, offering a novel paradigm for non-pharmacological therapy design. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for clinicians and yoga therapists, alongside computational datasets correlating yogic parameters (e.g., breath-to-movement ratios, postural alignment thresholds) with quantifiable health outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional instructors in the spiritual and physical therapy of Yoga in private, institutional, and clinical settings. Includes instruction in the principles of Ayurveda, philosophy of Yoga, warm-up and progressive exercises, breathing exercises, meditation, Yamas and Niyamas, instructional techniques, posture adjustment, student/client counseling and assessment, advanced Yoga disciplines and styles, business practices, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of neuromuscular disorders and mobility impairments necessitates advanced tools to model the complex interplay between biomechanical forces, neural control, and tissue adaptation during therapeutic exercise. Current computational models in rehabilitation science lack the resolution to simulate real-time, patient-specific neuromuscular responses to dynamic loading, limiting the precision of personalized intervention strategies. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity multiscale simulation framework integrating musculoskeletal dynamics, neural drive patterns, and mechanobiological tissue remodeling to optimize rehabilitation protocols for individuals with acquired motor deficits. The core computational challenge involves coupling finite element models of muscle-tendon deformation with reinforcement learning algorithms that emulate adaptive motor control under variable resistance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations of 10,000+ motor unit recruitment strategies across heterogeneous tissue architectures, validated against motion capture and electromyography data from clinical cohorts. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated solvers for viscoelastic tissue mechanics and graph neural networks to predict load redistribution patterns in pathological gait. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of recommending patient-specific exercise parameters (load, frequency, range of motion) that maximize functional recovery while minimizing reinjury risk. This resource will fill a critical gap in precision rehabilitation by bridging movement biomechanics with neuroadaptive plasticity principles, directly informing the design of next-generation assistive devices and closed-loop biofeedback systems. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source tools to catalyze interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computational physiology and therapeutic robotics.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: Forest operations face critical challenges in balancing ecological preservation with the demand for efficient timber production, particularly as climate variability intensifies and regulatory frameworks evolve. Traditional forest harvesting optimization models often rely on static environmental parameters or simplified spatial assumptions, limiting their ability to adapt to dynamic conditions such as soil moisture fluctuations, habitat fragmentation risks, and real-time equipment performance data. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize forest harvesting systems under spatially and temporally variable constraints. The research will integrate multi-source geospatial data (LiDAR, satellite imagery, IoT-enabled soil sensors) with agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between harvesting machinery, forest ecosystems, and environmental conditions at unprecedented scales. Machine learning techniques will be applied to predict equipment wear patterns and energy consumption across diverse terrain types, while constraint programming will address multi-objective optimization of extraction routes that minimize soil compaction, carbon emissions, and canopy disturbance. The computational framework will leverage GPU-accelerated parallel processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets encompassing multi-year environmental observations and detailed forest structural inventories. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool capable of generating adaptive harvesting plans that respond to real-time environmental feedback, reducing operational costs by an estimated 15-20% while maintaining compliance with biodiversity protection thresholds. The HPC resources will enable sensitivity analyses across 10^6+ parameter combinations to identify critical thresholds in system resilience, providing novel insights into the coupled dynamics of mechanized forestry operations and ecosystem health. This work bridges gaps between precision forestry, ecological engineering, and industrial systems optimization, offering a replicable methodology for sustainable resource extraction in climate-vulnerable regions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and forestry principles to the design of mechanical devices and processes for efficient forest management, timber production and related forest logistics systems. Includes instruction in forest products processing, forest management, forest harvesting, timber structure design, production analysis, road and bridge construction, vehicle adaptation and design, and harvesting equipment design.

abstract: The growing global demand for sustainable energy solutions requires innovative approaches to optimize solar energy systems, particularly in enhancing photovoltaic (PV) efficiency and thermal energy storage. Current challenges include material-level inefficiencies in light absorption, thermal losses in storage systems, and dynamic performance variability under real-world environmental conditions. This project proposes a computational research initiative to model, simulate, and optimize next-generation solar energy technologies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) atomistic-scale simulations to design novel PV materials with tailored bandgap structures and defect tolerance, and (2) system-scale modeling of hybrid solar-thermal storage configurations to minimize energy dissipation and maximize grid compatibility. Advanced machine learning algorithms will be integrated with multiphysics simulations to predict material stability and system performance across spatial and temporal scales. HPC resources are critical to handle the computational intensity of density functional theory (DFT) calculations for material screening, finite element analysis (FEA) of thermal-fluid dynamics, and ensemble-based optimization of system parameters. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-efficiency perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell architectures, optimized phase-change material composites for thermal storage, and data-driven guidelines for scalable solar farm deployment. By reducing reliance on iterative physical prototyping, this work will accelerate the development of commercially viable solar technologies, directly supporting decarbonization goals. The resulting open-source computational frameworks will also provide a foundation for future research in renewable energy systems integration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing solar-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in solar energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Grapevine physiology and wine quality are profoundly influenced by dynamic environmental factors, yet predictive models to optimize vineyard management under climate variability remain underdeveloped. This project seeks to establish a computational framework integrating hyperspectral imaging data, multi-omics analyses (genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics), and terroir-specific climate models to predict grape biochemical trajectories and wine composition under shifting environmental conditions. We will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of sensor data from IoT-enabled vineyard monitoring systems, coupled with multi-scale modeling of vine-soil-microbe interactions. Machine learning architectures (convolutional neural networks and transformer-based models) will be trained on historical yield records, pest incidence patterns, and wine chemistry databases to identify resilience-associated genetic markers and stress-response pathways. Parallelized finite element simulations will model water transport dynamics in grape berries under drought scenarios, while molecular dynamics simulations will characterize the stability of key aroma compounds during fermentation. The computational pipeline will also incorporate regional climate projections to assess genotype-environment interactions across 15 major winegrowing regions. Expected outcomes include (1) a decision-support system for precision irrigation and harvest scheduling, (2) predictive maps of disease risk and nutrient deficiency hotspots, and (3) a digital twin framework for testing vineyard adaptation strategies. This resource-intensive approach addresses critical gaps in viticultural sustainability by enabling real-time optimization of cultural practices while preserving wine typicity. The computational models and datasets produced will be made available through an open-access portal, providing foundational tools for climate-resilient grape production and enological innovation. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities for large-scale parameter optimization, genomic sequence alignment, and 3D fluid dynamics simulations that exceed current campus computing infrastructure.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific and agribusiness principles to the production of grapes, the making of wine, and the wine business. Includes instruction in grapes and wines of the world; grape production; winemaking technology; plant biology; chemistry; food science, safety, and packaging; soil science; pest management; and marketing and business management.

abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias present a significant clinical challenge due to their complex mechanisms and variable patient-specific manifestations. Current approaches to predicting arrhythmia susceptibility and optimizing therapies, such as catheter ablation, often rely on generalized anatomical or electrical models that inadequately capture individual variability in cardiac structure, tissue heterogeneity, and dynamic electrophysiological behavior. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing patient-specific computational models of cardiac electrophysiology to predict arrhythmia dynamics and guide precision therapies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support large-scale simulations of heart rhythm disorders, integrating high-resolution imaging data (e.g., cardiac MRI or CT), intracardiac electroanatomic mapping, and biophysically detailed cellular models. The computational workflow will involve finite element modeling of myocardial geometry, parameterization of ion channel kinetics and fibrosis distribution from clinical data, and simulation of arrhythmia initiation/perpetuation using monodomain reaction-diffusion equations. Machine learning methods will be applied to analyze simulation outputs and identify predictive biomarkers of arrhythmia recurrence or treatment success. The project will leverage parallel computing to perform sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces and conduct population-scale simulations to evaluate phenotypic variability. Expected outcomes include the creation of validated, open-source tools for patient-specific arrhythmia modeling, optimized criteria for selecting ablation targets in atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, and novel mechanistic insights into how fibrosis patterns or genetic channelopathies modulate arrhythmia risk. This work has direct translational significance, with potential to improve procedural outcomes, reduce healthcare costs from repeat interventions, and advance personalized management strategies in clinical electrophysiology. The scale of data processing, iterative model optimization, and multi-dimensional simulations necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for feasible computation times, enabling clinically relevant discovery within a research timeline.
cip_definition: Research focused on, within the subspecialty of cardiovascular disease, which prepares physicians in intricate technical procedures to evaluate heart rhythms and determine appropriate treatment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance protocols for hybrid and electric vehicle (HEV/EV) systems, addressing gaps in real-time diagnostics and lifecycle management. Current maintenance strategies rely heavily on static schedules or reactive repairs, leading to unnecessary downtime, resource waste, and premature component failures. The research problem centers on the lack of adaptive models capable of integrating heterogeneous data streams—including telemetry, material wear patterns, and environmental stressors—to forecast system degradation in HEV/EV powertrains. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets from vehicle sensors, historical maintenance records, and synthetic failure simulations. Computational methods will include the development of hybrid neural networks combining time-series analysis (via LSTM architectures) and graph-based models to map interdependencies among battery, motor, and power electronics subsystems. Physics-informed reinforcement learning will be employed to iteratively refine maintenance recommendations based on simulated operational scenarios. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated training pipelines and distributed computing frameworks to manage parameter optimization across large-scale models. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive maintenance toolkit capable of reducing unplanned downtime by ≥30% and extending critical component lifespans by 15–20%, as quantified through comparative testing against industry-standard diagnostic systems. By enabling dynamic, data-driven decision-making, this work aims to establish a new paradigm in vehicle maintenance technologies, directly supporting the transition to sustainable transportation infrastructure. The resulting models and datasets will be made available to the academic community, fostering collaboration in transportation electrification research.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in identifying and interpreting pathogenic genetic variants underlying rare Mendelian disorders. Despite advances in sequencing, a significant proportion of patients with suspected genetic diseases remain undiagnosed due to difficulties in distinguishing causal variants from benign polymorphisms, particularly in non-coding regulatory regions and structural variants. Our research will integrate whole-genome sequencing data from 5,000 undiagnosed patients with functional genomic datasets (e.g., chromatin accessibility, histone modification, and spatial chromatin conformation profiles) to prioritize variants disrupting transcriptional regulation or 3D genome architecture. Computational workflows will employ deep learning models trained on epigenetic signatures and allele-specific expression patterns to predict variant pathogenicity, coupled with population-scale allele frequency filtering using diverse genomic databases. The scale of multi-omics data integration necessitates HPC capabilities for parallelized processing of terabyte-level datasets, accelerated training of neural networks, and large-memory nodes for genome-wide association testing. Expected outcomes include novel variant classifications enabling diagnoses for 15-20% of currently unresolved cases, identification of previously unannotated regulatory elements linked to developmental disorders, and insights into tissue-specific gene regulatory mechanisms. This work will directly inform clinical reporting guidelines for non-coding variants and accelerate the discovery of therapeutic targets for gene-based therapies. By bridging gaps between genomic variation and mechanistic pathophysiology, the project advances precision medicine in human genetics while addressing computational bottlenecks in analyzing complex, multi-dimensional genomic data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of human genetics from the standpoint of medical applications such as clinical diagnosis, genetic engineering and therapy, transplantation, and the study of genetic diseases and disabilities and their defense. Includes instruction in human molecular genetics; genetic factors causing disease; changes in gene expression during development, differentiation, and pathogenesis; recombinant DNA; gene therapy; clinical genetics; genetic epidemiology; immunogenetics; cytogenetics; and genetics of specific disorders and diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive maintenance framework for commercial and industrial vehicles using high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in traditional diagnostic and repair methodologies. Current practices in vehicle maintenance often rely on reactive strategies, leading to unplanned downtime, costly repairs, and suboptimal resource allocation. To overcome these challenges, this research will leverage computational modeling and machine learning (ML) to predict mechanical failures, optimize maintenance schedules, and extend vehicle lifespans. The core research problem involves integrating heterogeneous data streams—including sensor telemetry, historical repair records, and environmental conditions—into a unified predictive system capable of identifying failure patterns in complex vehicle subsystems such as engines, transmissions, and braking systems. Computational methods will include the development of ensemble ML models trained on terabyte-scale datasets to classify fault precursors, coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to model stress distributions and wear dynamics in critical components under varying operational loads. HPC resources are essential to process real-time data from vehicle fleets, execute parallelized simulations of mechanical degradation, and iteratively refine ML architectures through hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin framework for simulating vehicle health, anomaly detection algorithms with >90% precision in fault prediction, and data-driven maintenance protocols to reduce repair costs by an estimated 15–25%. By transitioning from time-based to condition-based maintenance, this work aims to enhance operational safety, reduce environmental waste from premature part replacements, and establish new benchmarks for computational applications in vehicle repair technologies. The project will also generate open-source tools to bridge gaps between automotive technicians and data science practices, fostering innovation in vocational technical education.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of vehicles and mobile equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive biomechanical and physiological models for optimizing injury prevention and rehabilitation strategies in athletic training. Despite advances in sports medicine, the complexity of human movement, tissue response, and individualized recovery trajectories remains inadequately captured by conventional analytical tools. The research problem centers on the need for granular, multi-scale simulations to evaluate how biomechanical stressors—such as repetitive joint loading or sudden impact—interact with physiological factors (e.g., muscle fatigue, ligament elasticity) to influence injury risk and recovery outcomes. By integrating motion capture data, clinical injury records, and physiological biomarkers, we will construct computational models to simulate injury mechanisms and test the efficacy of therapeutic interventions under diverse scenarios. Key computational methods include finite element analysis for tissue stress modeling, machine learning algorithms to identify risk patterns from heterogeneous datasets, and agent-based simulations to evaluate rehabilitation protocols. These approaches require HPC resources to manage large-scale data processing, parallelize computationally intensive simulations, and iteratively refine models using high-dimensional inputs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide personalized injury prevention plans, data-driven criteria for modifying rehabilitation exercises in real time, and a framework for assessing sport-specific biomechanical demands. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform athletic training practices by bridging gaps between clinical observation and computational precision, ultimately reducing recovery times and improving long-term athlete health. By enabling dynamic, patient-specific analyses, this work will contribute foundational insights into the interplay of biomechanics, physiology, and therapeutic exercise, with applications in sports medicine education, clinical practice, and athlete performance optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work in consultation with, and under the supervision of physicians to prevent and treat sports injuries and associated conditions. Includes instruction in the identification, evaluation, and treatment of athletic injuries and illnesses; first aid and emergency care; therapeutic exercise; anatomy and physiology; exercise physiology; kinesiology and biomechanics; nutrition; sports psychology; personal and community health; knowledge of various sports and their biomechanical and physiological demands; and applicable professional standards and regulations.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic and transboundary animal diseases pose significant threats to global food security, livestock economies, and public health. Current epidemiological models often struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, environmental, and livestock movement data—to predict disease dynamics at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale, data-driven models that capture the complex interactions driving disease transmission in heterogeneous animal populations. The research will focus on optimizing agent-based simulation frameworks to analyze spatiotemporal spread patterns of high-consequence pathogens, such as avian influenza and foot-and-mouth disease, across livestock production systems. Computational workflows will integrate high-throughput sequencing data, satellite-derived environmental variables, and real-time livestock trade networks to parameterize transmission risks. Machine learning methods, including graph neural networks, will be applied to identify critical control points in disease dissemination and evaluate intervention strategies under diverse scenarios. By parallelizing stochastic simulations across HPC nodes, the project aims to quantify uncertainty in outbreak trajectories and refine resource allocation for vaccination, surveillance, and biosecurity measures. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for scalable epidemic forecasting, risk maps to guide regional preparedness, and evidence-based recommendations for mitigating antimicrobial resistance emergence in livestock-associated pathogens. This work directly supports veterinary public health priorities by enhancing predictive capacity for proactive disease management, ultimately reducing economic losses and zoonotic spillover risks. The requested computing resources are essential to process terabytes of genomic-epi data and execute millions of simulation replicates, enabling granular insights impractical on standard infrastructure.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology, and Public Health
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the prevention and control of communicable animal diseases, diseases affecting humans, and prepares veterinarians to function as public health specialists. Includes instruction in animal epidemiology, biostatistics, food safety and quality assurance, food toxicology, zoonotic and infectious diseases, disease vectors and transference, production medicine, animal health, veterinary public health practice, and inspection and evaluation methods.

abstract: Accurate and efficient land surveying is critical for infrastructure development, environmental management, and geospatial data integrity. However, modern surveying technologies such as terrestrial laser scanning (TLS), unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry, and satellite-based positioning systems generate vast datasets that challenge conventional computational methods. This project seeks to address the computational bottlenecks in processing high-resolution 3D point clouds, geodetic corrections, and error modeling by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Specifically, the research aims to develop scalable algorithms for automated feature extraction, real-time deformation analysis, and multi-sensor data fusion in complex terrain. Current workflows for point cloud registration and noise reduction rely on iterative, single-threaded processes that are prohibitively slow for large-scale surveys. By parallelizing these workflows using distributed computing frameworks, we will reduce processing times from days to hours while improving the precision of outputs. The project will also integrate machine learning models to classify geological features and predict subsidence risks, tasks that require extensive training on high-dimensional datasets. HPC resources will enable the simulation of error propagation across multi-temporal surveys, a computationally demanding process essential for quantifying uncertainties in long-term monitoring applications. Anticipated outcomes include open-source software tools optimized for HPC environments, which will enhance the capacity of surveying professionals to manage geospatial big data. The results will advance methodological standards in geodetic surveying, support resilient infrastructure planning, and contribute to the broader geosciences community by providing scalable solutions for terrain modeling. This work aligns with national priorities for sustainable land use and disaster preparedness, addressing gaps in computational infrastructure that currently limit the resolution and reliability of large-area surveys.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the delineation, determination, planning and positioning of land tracts, land and water boundaries, land contours and features; and the preparation of related maps, charts and reports. Includes instruction in applied geodesy, computer graphics, photointerpretation, plane and geodetic surveying, mensuration, traversing, survey equipment operation and maintenance, instrument calibration, and basic cartography.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in forklift operation safety and efficiency through advanced computational modeling of human-machine interactions in dynamic industrial environments. Despite standardized training protocols, forklift-related accidents remain a leading cause of workplace injuries, often attributed to unpredictable human decision-making, environmental complexity, and real-time operational stressors. Current training simulations lack the fidelity to replicate high-risk scenarios, while operational analytics in warehouse settings rarely account for the interplay of ergonomic, behavioral, and spatial variables. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates multi-agent reinforcement learning, real-time sensor data emulation, and physics-based modeling. The computational model will simulate warehouse environments with variable layouts, traffic patterns, and load configurations, while agent-based operators (both human and automated) will be trained under diverse hazard conditions. High-resolution LiDAR and inertial measurement unit (IMU) datasets from operational forklifts will inform the physics engine, with parallelized Monte Carlo methods employed to stress-test safety protocols across millions of simulated scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling three core components: 1) neural network training for adaptive operator behavior prediction, 2) finite element analysis of load stability under combined mechanical stresses, and 3) probabilistic risk assessment matrices accounting for fatigue metrics and environmental interference. Expected outcomes include predictive models for accident hot-spot identification, optimized warehouse layout recommendations validated through synthetic data, and AI-driven training modules that adapt to individual operator performance metrics. By leveraging large-scale parameter sweeps and ensemble modeling techniques, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive forklift safety management while advancing computational methods for industrial human factors analysis. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated through an open-access platform to support workforce training programs and OSHA compliance strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate forklifts in a variety of work environments. Includes instruction in accident prevention, forklift operation, materials handling, and worksite safety.

abstract: The safe and efficient management of hazardous materials requires advanced predictive tools to address the complex interplay of chemical, physical, and environmental factors influencing waste behavior. Current methods for optimizing hazardous waste disposal and containment systems often rely on simplified models, which inadequately capture nonlinear interactions, degradation kinetics, or multi-phase transport phenomena under variable field conditions. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate hazardous material interactions with engineered containment systems and natural environments, enabling data-driven strategies for waste stabilization, transport risk mitigation, and long-term storage. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement multiphysics models integrating reactive transport equations, machine learning-enhanced material degradation predictors, and stochastic uncertainty quantification. Key simulations will focus on (1) thermochemical stability of composite waste matrices under thermal and mechanical stress, (2) probabilistic mapping of contaminant plume dispersion in heterogeneous subsurface environments, and (3) accelerated aging studies for novel bioremediation substrates. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-optimized solvers for large-scale parameter sweeps and ensemble simulations, validated against experimental datasets from partner laboratories. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing waste treatment protocols, risk assessment matrices for regulatory compliance, and open-source modules for simulating biohazard transport in infrastructure-adjacent environments. By addressing critical gaps in system-level modeling of hazardous material dynamics, this research will directly support technological advancements in waste processing facilities, emergency response planning, and remediation site design, while reducing reliance on costly empirical trial-and-error approaches.
cip_title: Hazardous Materials Management and Waste Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in identifying and disposing of hazardous materials. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, biohazard identification, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, hazardous waste disposal procedures and systems, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design of next-generation high-performance ceramic composites through large-scale atomistic and mesoscale simulations, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research addresses a critical challenge in ceramic sciences: the formation of microcracks and interfacial defects during sintering and thermal cycling, which degrade mechanical stability and limit applications in extreme environments. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve dynamic defect evolution at atomic and grain-boundary scales, while existing computational models lack the resolution to predict microstructural responses under multi-physics loads. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of atomic-scale diffusion and phase-field modeling of grain growth and stress distribution. The HPC allocation will support parallelized simulations of polycrystalline alumina and silicon carbide systems, incorporating up to 10^8 atoms in MD ensembles and mesoscale domains exceeding 100 μm³. Key parameters include temperature-dependent diffusion coefficients, anisotropic thermal expansion, and interfacial energy landscapes derived from density functional theory (DFT) benchmarks. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking processing conditions (sintering temperature, pressure) to defect nucleation thresholds and fracture toughness. These results will directly inform the synthesis of ceramics with enhanced thermal-mechanical stability for energy storage systems and industrial cutting tools. The computational workflows developed will also establish open-access protocols for simulating rare-earth-free ceramic matrices, addressing supply chain vulnerabilities in advanced manufacturing. By correlating simulated microstructures with experimental XRD and nanoindentation data from collaborating labs, this work aims to accelerate the discovery of ceramics optimized for high-temperature corrosion resistance and load-bearing capacity.
