The requested resources are essential to manage the memory-intensive phase-field iterations and time-resolved MD trajectories required for statistically robust predictions of microcrack propagation dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of inorganic non-metallic materials, such as porcelains, cements, industrial ceramics, ceramic superconductors, abrasive, and related materials and systems.

abstract: Nuclear energy remains a vital component of global efforts to transition to low-carbon power, but challenges in reactor safety, materials degradation, and waste management persist. This project addresses the critical need for advanced computational tools to model complex multiphysics phenomena in nuclear systems, particularly under extreme operational and accident scenarios. Current simulation approaches for reactor core dynamics, neutron transport, and radioactive material behavior often rely on simplified models that lack the resolution to capture heterogeneous fuel geometries, transient thermal-hydraulic feedback, or long-term material corrosion in storage environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning-driven materials degradation models. The project will focus on two primary objectives: (1) simulating high-resolution, 3D neutron flux distributions in advanced reactor fuel assemblies to identify localized power peaking risks, and (2) modeling the coupled thermo-mechanical behavior of spent nuclear fuel canisters during extended storage, incorporating radiation-induced embrittlement and cyclic thermal stresses. These simulations will utilize open-source nuclear codes, including OpenMC and MOOSE, adapted for GPU-accelerated parallel processing to handle billion-cell meshes and multi-year decay timelines. The HPC resources will enable parametric studies across diverse reactor configurations and waste storage conditions, generating datasets to train reduced-order models for industry use. Expected outcomes include validated safety margins for accident-tolerant fuel designs, predictive tools for canister integrity assessment, and publicly accessible benchmarks for multiphysics validation. By bridging high-fidelity modeling with practical nuclear technology challenges, this work aims to directly inform operational protocols, regulatory standards, and next-generation reactor development, enhancing the safety and sustainability of nuclear energy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of research scientists and operating engineers engaged in the running of nuclear reactors, and in nuclear materials processing and disposal. Includes instruction in basic nuclear physics and nuclear engineering, monitoring and safety procedures, radioactive materials handling and disposal, equipment maintenance and operation, and record keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between biological maturation, cognitive development, and social-environmental influences on decision-making processes during adolescence. Traditional analytical approaches struggle to model the high-dimensional, longitudinal datasets required to capture these non-linear interactions, particularly when integrating neuroimaging, behavioral, and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data from a diverse cohort of 800 participants aged 12–25. We propose developing a computational framework using hierarchical Bayesian neural networks and agent-based modeling to simulate developmental trajectories across multiple timescales. The models will incorporate individual differences in pubertal timing, neural connectivity patterns, and real-world social learning experiences to predict risk perception and adaptive choice behavior. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: 1) parallel processing of multi-modal neurodevelopmental data (fMRI, DTI, hormonal assays), 2) training complex reinforcement learning architectures that map evolving cognitive strategies onto neural maturation gradients, and 3) running population-scale simulations to test competing theories of adolescent neurocognitive development under varying environmental conditions. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks and distributed memory systems to handle the 12TB dataset, which includes 15,000+ hours of time-series behavioral data and 2.5 million neuroimaging voxels. Expected outcomes include a novel computational model of adolescent decision-making architecture that quantifies developmental phase transitions, identifies critical windows for cognitive plasticity, and predicts individual trajectories of self-regulation capacity. Results will advance fundamental understanding of how maturational asynchronies between limbic and prefrontal systems interact with social learning mechanisms, while providing open-source tools for developmental psychologists studying complex system-level interactions. This work directly addresses methodological gaps in developmental science by enabling integrative analysis of processes that operate across biological, psychological, and temporal scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from adolescence to adulthood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of digital communication patterns within online communities that influence real-world criminal behavior, with a focus on identifying predictive signals of organized retail crime networks. While traditional criminal justice research has examined socioeconomic or geographic risk factors, the proliferation of encrypted messaging platforms and decentralized forums has created new challenges for understanding how digital interactions facilitate coordinated illicit activities. The research employs a computational social science framework, combining natural language processing (NLP) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to analyze multi-modal data from anonymized platform archives, law enforcement incident reports, and geospatial transaction records. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of unstructured text with transformer-based models to detect coded language, reconstructing temporal interaction networks to map influence hierarchies, and simulating information diffusion patterns under varying moderation policies. High-performance computing resources are critical for training domain-specific large language models on sensitive, restricted-access corpora while maintaining privacy-preserving federated learning protocols. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of digital behavioral markers associated with escalation to criminal coordination, validated against ground-truth interdiction cases. The project aims to produce scalable tools for public safety agencies to prioritize investigative resources and assess intervention strategies in digitally mediated environments. By bridging computational techniques with criminological theory, this work addresses a critical gap in contemporary safety studies, where existing analytical frameworks lack the capacity to operationalize insights from ephemeral, large-scale digital trace data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the criminal justice system, its organizational components and processes, and its legal and public policy contexts. Includes instruction in criminal law and policy, police and correctional systems organization, the administration of justice and the judiciary, and public attitudes regarding criminal justice issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the transmission of cultural and intellectual ideas across late medieval and early Renaissance Europe (c. 1300–1600 CE). While textual, artistic, and material evidence from this period is abundant, synthesizing fragmented datasets—including digitized manuscripts, archival records, artifact provenance data, and iconographic corpora—remains a critical challenge. Current methodologies struggle to map the spatial-temporal diffusion of motifs, texts, and practices at scale, particularly across multilingual and multi-regional contexts. This project proposes a computational framework integrating network analysis, machine learning, and geospatial modeling to reconstruct cultural exchange pathways. Key objectives include training transformer-based models to identify semantic and stylistic parallels in multilingual texts (Latin, vernaculars) and applying graph neural networks to analyze relationships between patronage networks, trade routes, and artistic production centers. A pilot study on 15th-century Florentine merchant correspondence and contemporaneous fresco cycles has demonstrated preliminary success in cross-referencing economic data with visual motifs, but scaling this to pan-European scope requires HPC capabilities. The computational workflow will utilize containerized pipelines for reproducibility, with iterative model training on GPU clusters and large-scale simulations of hypothetical diffusion scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of cultural transmission nodes, quantitative models of influence dynamics, and a dataset linking art-historical features with socioeconomic metadata. By enabling systematic analysis of interdisciplinary evidence, this project aims to reshape scholarly understanding of how premodern globalization operated, while providing a replicable computational toolkit for humanistic inquiry. The requested resources will directly support data storage, parallel processing of terabyte-scale image/text corpora, and complex network simulations that are infeasible on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the Medieval and/or Renaissance periods in European and circum-Mediterranean history from the perspective of various disciplines in the humanities and social sciences, including history and archeology, as well as studies of period art and music.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between international education policies, cross-national student mobility trends, and educational equity outcomes using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to analyze how heterogeneous policy environments and socio-economic factors shape disparities in access to higher education for migrant students globally. While existing studies rely on small-n comparative case analyses, this project will process multi-modal data—including UNESCO demographic statistics, OECD policy documents, and longitudinal student migration records from 150+ countries—to identify systemic drivers of inequity. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) to classify policy rhetoric in 20 languages, network analysis to model migration pathways, and hierarchical Bayesian models to assess multi-level interactions between institutional, national, and regional variables. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based NLP models on multilingual text corpora, running parallelized simulations of policy impact scenarios, and processing spatial-temporal datasets exceeding 15TB. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated predictive model of student migration flows sensitive to policy changes, (2) a typology of education systems based on equity outcomes for displaced learners, and (3) open-access tools for visualizing cross-national policy alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education). By enabling large-scale pattern detection across diverse geopolitical contexts, this work will provide actionable insights for international organizations designing inclusive education frameworks while advancing computational social science methodologies in comparative education research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the educational phenomena, practices, and institutions within different societies and states in a comparative perspective, and the study of international educational issues. Includes instruction in comparative research methods, country- or area-specific studies, cross-national studies of learning and teaching styles, international educational policy and development, and analyses of educational migration patterns and experiences.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the optimization of multisensory worship environments through computational modeling, focusing on the integration of live musical performance, digital media, and spatial acoustics in Christian worship contexts. While contemporary Worship Ministries increasingly rely on technology to create immersive experiences, there is a lack of empirical frameworks guiding the harmonization of artistic, theological, and technical elements. The project addresses this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and analyze how dynamic interactions between sound, visual media, and architectural variables affect congregational engagement and spiritual resonance. Using parametric models of worship spaces, real-time acoustic simulations will be paired with agent-based modeling to predict how adjustments in audio hardware placement, digital projection mapping, or musical key signatures influence participant responses. Machine learning algorithms will process datasets derived from historical worship service recordings, sensor-generated biometric data (e.g., congregational vocal participation), and liturgical texts to identify patterns in spiritually impactful moments. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated rendering for 3D visualizations of proposed worship designs and parallel processing to evaluate thousands of scenario permutations. Expected outcomes include a scalable software toolkit for Worship Ministry practitioners to prototype environment designs virtually, reducing trial-and-error in physical spaces, and a taxonomy of multisensory worship “signatures” correlated with theological intentions (e.g., penitence vs. celebration). By bridging computational acoustics, aesthetic theory, and worship theology, this work aims to establish an evidence-based paradigm for designing worship experiences that are both technologically robust and theologically coherent, offering a model for interdisciplinary humanities research at the intersection of art, technology, and spirituality.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the use of musical and theatrical arts in Christian worship. Includes instruction in digital media, electronic hardware design and installation, music, theater, and worship theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution of U.S. constitutional jurisprudence through large-scale legal text analysis and network modeling. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in judicial reasoning across pivotal Supreme Court cases, particularly those involving shifts in constitutional interpretation that defy traditional doctrinal categorization. Existing scholarship often relies on manual case analysis or small-sample qualitative methods, limiting the ability to systematically trace how legal concepts interact, mutate, or stabilize over multi-decadal timescales. We propose a computational legal analytics framework combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques with dynamic network modeling to process a curated corpus of 50,000+ federal court opinions (1790–2024), with particular focus on First Amendment and Due Process Clause jurisprudence. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect semantic relationships between legal concepts, while temporal graph networks will map how citation patterns and conceptual dependencies evolve alongside sociopolitical changes. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of heterogeneous legal texts (PDFs, OCR outputs, metadata), GPU-accelerated model training for domain-specific legal language understanding, and iterative simulation of competing doctrinal development hypotheses. Expected outcomes include: 1) a novel taxonomy of constitutional argumentation pathways, 2) quantitative metrics for measuring doctrinal stability during constitutional "tipping points," and 3) open-source tools for legal temporal network analysis. By bridging computational social science methodologies with constitutional theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying legal change as a complex adaptive system, with implications for legal education, judicial analytics, and predictive modeling of jurisprudential trends. The scale of textual data and need for real-time simulation of multi-century legal interactions necessitates dedicated HPC resources beyond typical humanities computing infrastructure.
cip_title: American/ US Law/ Legal Studies/ Jurisprudence
cip_definition: An advanced, professional program of the U.S. legal system, Constitution law, and jurisprudence. Includes instruction in legal history, legal sociology, philosophy of law, Constitutional law, legal procedure, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize precision in perioperative anesthetic management by developing computational models to predict patient-specific responses to anesthesia, with a focus on reducing adverse outcomes in complex surgical and obstetric populations. Current approaches to dosing and monitoring often rely on population averages, which inadequately account for genetic, physiological, and pharmacological variability, leading to suboptimal hemodynamic stability, prolonged recovery, or postoperative complications. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework integrating electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-time physiological signals to simulate drug pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) under diverse clinical scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train machine learning models on multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10,000+ surgical cases, including obstetric and high-risk patients, and to run parallelized, agent-based simulations of drug interactions at cellular and systemic levels. Molecular dynamics simulations will further model anesthetic binding affinities to receptor variants linked to interindividual variability. Key computational challenges include managing high-dimensional data streams from intraoperative monitoring devices, resolving stochastic variability in virtual patient cohorts, and enabling real-time predictive analytics for critical decision support. Expected outcomes include validated models for personalized anesthetic dosing, early warning systems for hemodynamic instability, and risk stratification tools for postoperative pain trajectories. This work will directly inform clinical protocols to enhance safety in operating rooms and critical care settings, particularly for vulnerable populations such as obstetric and geriatric patients. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to bridge translational gaps in precision anesthesiology, reducing trial-and-error practices and improving recovery outcomes across surgical specialties.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical patient care, and the care of pain problems. Includes instruction in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize the material behavior of ceramic clays and glazes under varying firing conditions, addressing a critical gap in the empirical understanding of ceramic arts processes. Traditional approaches to ceramic arts rely heavily on trial-and-error experimentation to achieve desired aesthetic and structural outcomes, which is resource-intensive and limits the exploration of novel material combinations. The research problem centers on predicting the relationships between clay composition, glaze chemistry, kiln conditions, and final ceramic properties (e.g., color variation, surface texture, structural integrity) to empower artists with data-driven insights. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will implement multiphysics simulations integrating thermal dynamics, fluid mechanics, and chemical reaction modeling to replicate kiln environments and material interactions at microscales. Machine learning models will be trained on both simulated data and experimental datasets from historical and contemporary ceramic works to identify predictive patterns. The computational workflow will include parameter sweeps across clay-glaze combinations (e.g., silica-alumina ratios, oxide additives) and firing protocols (temperature ramps, oxidation/reduction cycles). Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for artists to virtually test formulations, a database correlating material inputs with artistic outputs, and the discovery of previously undocumented glaze effects achievable through controlled atmospheric conditions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges material science and artistic practice, offering ceramicists a systematic method to innovate while preserving traditional techniques. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space and parallelize thermally coupled simulations, which exceed the capacity of local workstations. By reducing the stochasticity inherent in ceramic arts, this project aims to expand creative possibilities and contribute to the sustainability of the field through optimized resource use.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by producing art works out of clay and similar materials. Includes instruction in handbuilt and wheel thrown techniques; molding; slips and glazes; trimming and decorating; firing and kiln operation; oxidation; mixed media; ceramic murals; and personal style development.

abstract: The increasing demand for German language education across diverse learner populations necessitates innovative pedagogical tools that address individualized learning needs. Current approaches to assessing language proficiency and designing adaptive instructional materials often rely on static frameworks, which may not account for the dynamic interplay of linguistic, cognitive, and cultural factors influencing second language acquisition. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational model to analyze learner interactions and predict proficiency trajectories, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale multilingual datasets. The research problem centers on optimizing real-time adaptive assessment tools for German language learners, particularly in classroom settings where teachers must balance heterogeneous skill levels. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based architectures, the project will process spoken and written learner corpora to identify patterns in syntactic complexity, lexical diversity, and pragmatic accuracy. These datasets, drawn from anonymized student interactions across proficiency levels (A1–C1), will be enriched with contextual metadata such as task type, error frequency, and corrective feedback responses. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of machine learning models to classify learner errors, simulate language development pathways, and generate personalized feedback recommendations. The computational workflow will integrate fine-tuned BERT models for German-specific error detection and graph-based algorithms to map interlanguage development. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for German language instructors, offering dynamic proficiency analytics and evidence-based strategies for differentiated instruction. By modeling the variability in learner outcomes at scale, this project aims to advance the integration of computational linguistics into teacher education, equipping future German language educators with data-driven methodologies to enhance curricular design and classroom practice. The scalability of this approach, enabled by HPC infrastructure, will support replication across less commonly taught languages, fostering equity in language education resource development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach German language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to optimize individualized learning strategies for middle school students in special education programs, addressing the challenge of designing adaptive curricula that account for diverse cognitive, behavioral, and sensory needs. Special education teachers often face limited time and resources to analyze complex student data manually, which can delay the implementation of targeted interventions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including academic performance metrics, behavioral observations, speech-language assessments, and individualized education program (IEP) records—and train machine learning models capable of predicting student-specific instructional approaches. The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to evaluate written and verbal student responses, computer vision techniques to analyze engagement patterns from classroom video data, and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate the longitudinal impacts of pedagogical strategies. By scaling these analyses across synthetic cohorts generated via agent-based modeling, we aim to identify robust, generalizable principles for middle school special education curriculum design. The outcomes will include open-source tools for teachers to generate data-driven IEP recommendations and real-time classroom adjustment prompts. This work will advance the integration of computational methods into special education teacher training programs, providing educators with actionable frameworks to address learning disabilities, sensory processing challenges, and social-emotional needs. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional data and iterative simulations required to ensure model accuracy and equity across student subgroups, ultimately supporting more inclusive and effective middle school special education practices.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Junior High/ Middle School Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in junior high/middle school. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for middle school special education; and principles of middle school instruction in specific subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to advance personalized rehabilitation strategies for neuromusculoskeletal disorders by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific biomechanical and physiological responses to therapeutic interventions. Current rehabilitation protocols often rely on generalized population data, limiting their efficacy for individuals with complex, multifactorial impairments. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multiscale biomechanical modeling, machine learning, and clinical data from motion capture, electromyography, and medical imaging. The primary research problem centers on predicting optimal rehabilitation pathways for heterogeneous patient populations, accounting for variables such as tissue healing dynamics, neuromuscular adaptation, and functional recovery trajectories. HPC resources are critical to process high-dimensional datasets (e.g., 3D musculoskeletal simulations, real-time sensor data from wearable devices) and perform iterative optimization of treatment parameters. Computational methods include finite element modeling of load distribution in healing tissues, reinforcement learning to adapt therapeutic exercise regimens, and network analysis to evaluate rehabilitation team coordination strategies. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for tailoring rehabilitation plans, reducing recovery times, and minimizing complications such as compensatory movement patterns. By simulating thousands of patient-specific scenarios, this work will establish quantitative benchmarks for intervention timing, intensity, and modality across conditions like stroke, spinal cord injury, and osteoarthritis. The scalability of this approach will enable future integration with telehealth systems, fostering equitable access to precision rehabilitation. Successful implementation will directly inform clinical guidelines and provide an open-source toolkit for adaptive rehabilitation planning, addressing a critical gap in evidence-based physical medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, etiology, treatment, prevention and rehabilitation of neuromusculo-skeletal, cardiovascular, pulmonary and other system disorders common to patients of both sexes and all ages. May included related research in physical examinations, design and prescription of rehabilitation strategies and the supervision of rehabilitation teams.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing water supply systems for resilience against contamination and variable demand using advanced computational modeling. Despite advancements in plumbing infrastructure, aging systems and emerging contaminants (e.g., Legionella, microplastics) pose persistent public health risks, particularly in complex urban networks. Traditional hydraulic models lack the resolution to predict localized stagnation, biofilm formation, or chemical disinfection efficacy at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating fluid dynamics, water quality simulations, and machine learning to analyze pipe networks at unprecedented spatiotemporal detail. The research will develop parallelized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models using OpenFOAM to simulate flow regimes, solute transport, and microbial growth dynamics in multi-branch systems under varying pressure conditions. Machine learning surrogates will reduce the computational cost of scenario testing for infrastructure retrofits, such as looped vs. branched layouts or smart valve placements. Additionally, graph neural networks will predict contamination spread patterns using synthetic training data generated from HPC simulations. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to handle millions of cell meshes for 3D pipe geometries and years of operational data. Outcomes include open-source tools for designing contamination-resistant plumbing systems, risk maps identifying high-stagnation zones in municipal networks, and evidence-based guidelines for pipe material selection. By enabling fine-grained analysis of water age, disinfectant decay, and biofilm hotspots, this work aims to reduce waterborne disease risks while improving energy efficiency in recirculation systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling simulations to real-world network sizes and informing next-generation plumbing codes and smart sensor deployment strategies.
cip_title: Plumbing and Related Water Supply Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plumbing and related water supply services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in casino operations and services, focusing on the optimization of dynamic decision-making frameworks for real-time gaming floor management. Traditional approaches to casino operations—such as staffing allocation, game layout optimization, and patron flow analysis—rely on static models or heuristic strategies that fail to account for the complex, stochastic interactions between human behavior, operational variables, and regulatory constraints. The research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework that integrates agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and reinforcement learning to simulate high-fidelity scenarios of casino floor dynamics. Key challenges include processing large-scale datasets from surveillance systems, transactional records, and IoT-enabled gaming equipment, as well as modeling adaptive strategies for resource allocation under uncertainty. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, enabling real-time sensitivity analyses, and training machine learning models on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of recommending optimal staffing schedules, game configurations, and risk-mitigation protocols in response to fluctuating demand patterns and regulatory requirements. This work will contribute to the emerging field of computational casino operations by establishing methodologies for data-driven, adaptive management in a high-stakes, rapidly evolving industry. The project also aims to publish open-source algorithms tailored to gaming industry challenges, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between operations research, behavioral economics, and hospitality management. By addressing computational bottlenecks inherent to real-time casino operations, this research will provide foundational insights for enhancing operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and customer satisfaction in a specialized sector underserved by conventional scientific and engineering disciplines.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in casino operations and services not listed above.

abstract: The proliferation of decentralized communication networks in distributed organizations has introduced significant challenges in modeling information flow and decision-making latency. Traditional centralized frameworks fail to capture the dynamic, asynchronous interactions characteristic of ad-hoc human-AI collaborative systems, particularly in crisis response scenarios. This project proposes the development of a novel agent-based simulation platform to analyze emergent communication patterns and optimize resource allocation under constraints of incomplete information and temporal uncertainty. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale parallel simulations incorporating heterogeneous agent models with varying cognitive architectures, communication protocols, and decision heuristics. Computational methods integrate discrete-event simulation with graph neural networks to model multi-scale information diffusion across temporal hypergraphs, where nodes represent hybrid human-AI teams and edges encode context-dependent communication modalities. The framework incorporates real-world data from emergency coordination protocols while maintaining synthetic population generation capabilities for stress-testing organizational structures. Key innovations include adaptive message prioritization algorithms that learn latent information criticality patterns and a temporal attention mechanism for bottleneck prediction in decision cascades. Expected outcomes include quantitative metrics for organizational resilience, predictive models of coordination failure points, and open-source tools for designing robust human-AI communication infrastructures. This work advances informatics methodologies for complex socio-technical systems by bridging cognitive science principles with computational scalability, ultimately contributing to more effective information architectures in time-sensitive collaborative environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing bioprocess workflows for recombinant protein production, a cornerstone of modern biotechnology. Despite advances in fermentation and downstream purification techniques, inefficiencies persist in scaling laboratory-scale protocols to industrial bioreactor systems due to the complex interplay of biological, chemical, and physical variables. Traditional experimental optimization is time-intensive, costly, and limited in resolving multi-parameter interactions. To overcome these barriers, we propose a computational framework integrating dynamic metabolic modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate and predict optimal bioprocessing conditions. Metabolic models of Escherichia coli and Pichia pastoris will be parameterized using existing experimental data to simulate growth kinetics, substrate utilization, and recombinant protein expression under varying fermentation conditions. CFD simulations will model oxygen transfer, shear stress, and nutrient gradients in industrial-scale bioreactors, enabling the identification of suboptimal mixing zones. These datasets will train ML algorithms to predict yield outcomes and recommend parameter adjustments for fed-batch fermentation cycles. Downstream purification steps will be similarly optimized via molecular dynamics simulations of protein-surface interactions in chromatography columns, focusing on ligand binding efficiency under varying pH and ionic strength conditions. The integration of these computational approaches requires HPC resources to manage large-scale parallelization, iterative model refinement, and high-throughput data analysis. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for fermentation yield enhancement, reduced purification costs through optimized resin utilization, and a publicly accessible database of simulated bioprocess parameters. This work will directly support the development of scalable, cost-effective biologics production pipelines while providing training opportunities for students in computational biology tools, bridging gaps between experimental biotechnology and data-driven process engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of biologists and biotechnologists in research, industrial, and government settings. Includes instruction in fermentation technology, cell culturing, protein purification, biologic synthesis, assaying and testing, quality control, industrial microbiology, bioprocessing, chromatography and bioseparation, genetic technology, laboratory and hazardous materials safety, and computer applications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and control of adaptive soft matter systems, a novel class of engineered materials capable of programmable shape-morphing and dynamic mechanical responses. These systems, which integrate stimuli-responsive polymers, embedded microfluidic networks, and distributed actuation elements, hold transformative potential for applications in wearable assistive technologies, reconfigurable robotics, and adaptive infrastructure. However, their nonlinear material behaviors, multi-physics coupling (fluid-solid-electrical-thermal), and spatiotemporal control challenges demand high-fidelity simulations surpassing current capabilities. We propose to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-scale modeling approach combining lattice Boltzmann methods for microscale fluid-structure interactions, phase-field formulations for polymer network dynamics, and reinforcement learning for closed-loop control optimization. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated solvers to handle the inherent stiffness of governing equations across disparate timescales, while graph neural networks will predict emergent mesoscale material properties from molecular dynamics datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for soft matter system design, validated against experimental prototypes, and novel control paradigms enabling autonomous adaptation to external stimuli. This work bridges gaps between continuum mechanics, active matter physics, and cyber-physical control theory, establishing computational tools for next-generation engineering of dynamically tunable material systems. Successful implementation will accelerate the translation of soft matter innovations into functional technologies, with particular relevance to healthcare and energy-efficient robotics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized virtual reality (VR)-based interventions for trauma-related anxiety disorders, an emerging area at the intersection of clinical psychology, neurobiology, and immersive technology. Current VR therapies often use static scenarios, limiting their adaptability to individual patient responses. The research problem centers on creating dynamic, real-time VR environments that adjust stimuli based on multimodal biometric feedback (e.g., heart rate variability, electrodermal activity, gaze patterns) to maximize therapeutic efficacy while minimizing retraumatization risks. The computational approach integrates federated learning models trained on decentralized neurophysiological datasets to predict patient-specific stress thresholds, coupled with agent-based simulations of therapeutic scenario evolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) processing high-frequency biometric streams (500 Hz/s per patient) during live sessions with <50 ms latency, (2) training generative adversarial networks to synthesize culturally responsive virtual environments, and (3) running Monte Carlo simulations to model intervention pathways across diverse demographic cohorts. Expected outcomes include an open-source adaptive VR platform and evidence-based protocols for biometric-guided exposure therapy. This work addresses a critical gap in scalable, precision mental health tools by combining computational psychiatry principles with immersive computing—an underexplored niche in health services research. The requested resources will enable analysis of multi-terabyte datasets from ongoing clinical trials while preserving privacy through distributed learning architectures. Successful implementation could establish new paradigms for real-time neuroadaptive interventions, particularly for rural or underserved populations lacking access to specialized care.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Hospice and palliative care patients often present with complex, multidimensional symptom burdens and heterogeneous trajectories that challenge personalized prognostication and intervention. Current risk-stratification tools lack the granularity to integrate dynamic clinical, biomarker, and patient-reported data, limiting their utility in real-world decision-making. This project proposes to develop a high-dimensional predictive modeling framework to identify patient subgroups with distinct symptom progression patterns, treatment responses, and end-of-life trajectories. Leveraging longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) from 15,000+ patients across six hospice networks, we will integrate structured clinical data, unstructured clinician notes, biomarker panels, and family caregiver reports using natural language processing and multimodal machine learning. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage iterative training of ensemble models on clustered time-to-event data, including recurrent neural networks for temporal symptom patterns and transformer-based architectures for free-text analysis. Key challenges include imputation of sparse observational data, harmonization of heterogeneous data streams sampled at different frequencies, and ethical AI implementation to mitigate biases in palliative care delivery. Anticipated outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for 60-day symptom exacerbation risks, (2) dynamic visualizations of individualized prognosis estimates for shared decision-making, and (3) open-source tools for reproducible palliative care analytics. The scale of multimodal data integration—processing >8TB of EHRs, 500,000 clinician notes, and longitudinal genomics—necessitates parallelized computing with GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and sensitivity analyses. Results will advance computational palliative care by enabling early identification of patients needing tailored interventions, optimizing hospice referral timing, and establishing benchmarks for AI-assisted prognosis communication. This work directly addresses NIH priorities for scalable predictive analytics in serious illness care while adhering to FAIR data principles and HIPAA-compliant computational workflows.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hospice and Palliative Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling in hospice and palliative care, addressing critical gaps in personalized end-of-life symptom management and prognosis estimation. Current clinical tools often fail to account for the multidimensional heterogeneity of patient trajectories, including dynamic interactions between biological, psychosocial, and treatment-related variables. We propose to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models capable of integrating large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-time sensor-derived symptom reports to predict individualized risks of uncontrolled pain, delirium, and 30-day mortality. The computational approach will involve federated learning frameworks to ensure privacy-preserving analysis of distributed EHR data across six hospice networks, coupled with natural language processing (NLP) of clinician notes and caregiver narratives. Deep neural networks will be trained on multimodal inputs, including polygenic risk scores, longitudinal opioid dosing patterns, and free-text symptom descriptions, to identify high-risk patient subgroups and latent predictors of therapeutic response. HPC resources are essential for processing >10 TB of multimodal data, optimizing hyperparameters across thousands of concurrent model iterations, and simulating stochastic outcomes under varying palliative intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) validated prediction algorithms for terminal symptom crises, deployable via clinician-facing dashboards; (2) mechanistic insights into genetic and environmental modifiers of opioid efficacy in advanced illness; and (3) open-source computational workflows for ethical AI applications in palliative care. By enabling rapid analysis of complex datasets that traditional statistical methods cannot process, this work will provide a foundation for data-driven clinical decision support systems tailored to hospice populations, ultimately reducing preventable suffering during life’s final stages.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hospice and Palliative Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of high-energy laser (HEL) systems for military applications by addressing critical computational challenges in beam propagation through dynamic atmospheric conditions. The primary research problem centers on mitigating the disruptive effects of atmospheric turbulence—such as thermal blooming, scattering, and phase distortion—which degrade beam coherence and targeting precision over operational distances. Current analytical models lack the resolution and adaptability to simulate complex, real-world scenarios involving multi-physics interactions between laser beams, adaptive optics, and rapidly changing environmental variables. To overcome these limitations, this research will employ high-fidelity numerical simulations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model beam propagation at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales. The computational framework integrates wave-optics algorithms with machine learning techniques to optimize adaptive optics control systems in real time, leveraging GPU-accelerated solvers for nonlinear Schrödinger equations and turbulence phase screens derived from meteorological data. Additionally, the project will develop hybrid models coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with laser-matter interaction simulations to predict thermal blooming effects under varying aerosol densities and wind profiles. Expected outcomes include novel mitigation strategies for beam degradation, validated predictive frameworks for adaptive optics tuning, and scalable computational tools to inform the design of next-generation HEL systems. By enabling precise, large-scale simulations of directed energy systems in realistic environments, this work aims to enhance the operational viability of energy beam weapons while contributing foundational methodologies for HPC-driven research in photonics and military technology. The results will directly support mission-critical advancements in defense capabilities, addressing a specialized interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of applied physics, computational engineering, and military systems innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of lasers and other directed energy phenomena and their application to the creation of energy beam weapons systems. Includes instruction in photonics, electro-optics, microwave phenomena, laser chemistry, spectroscopy, chemical lasers, fibre lasers, imaging and optics, laser propagation and control, laser communication, infrared remote sensing, modeling and simulation, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community psychology research on optimizing social intervention strategies for marginalized populations experiencing systemic inequities. The research problem centers on modeling the dynamic interplay between community-level risk factors (e.g., resource scarcity, cultural stressors) and intervention outcomes across diverse social ecologies. Traditional methods struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions among multi-level variables, including individual behaviors, social networks, and institutional policies. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate population-scale interactions under varying intervention scenarios. These computational models will integrate empirical data from community surveys, social services records, and geographic information systems (GIS) to parameterize agents representing individuals, community organizations, and local policymakers. HPC resources are essential to run large-scale simulations that capture heterogeneity in agent attributes, test stochastic variations in intervention timing and delivery, and assess emergent outcomes across thousands of parallel iterations. Key analyses will evaluate how intervention "dosage," cultural adaptation fidelity, and social network structures mediate the prevention of community-level pathologies such as substance abuse cycles or intergenerational trauma. Expected outcomes include identifying critical leverage points for scalable interventions, generating actionable metrics for equity-centered program design, and publishing open-source simulation tools for community stakeholders. By combining computational social science with community psychology frameworks, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for primary prevention while reducing reliance on reactive, individual-level treatments. The requested computing infrastructure will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling socioecological complexity, directly supporting the program’s mission to foster systemic, sustainable social change.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply psychological principles to the analysis of social problems, and the implementation of intervention strategies for addressing these problems. Includes instruction in social ecology, primary and secondary prevention of social pathologies, social intervention strategies and tactics, large group counseling, social services systems behavior, creating settings, cultural stress, and the dynamics of social change.

abstract: The integration of traditional herbal medicine with modern computational approaches presents a critical challenge due to the complexity of multi-compound botanical formulations and their dynamic interactions with human physiological systems. While such formulations are central to many alternative medical systems, their mechanisms of action remain poorly characterized, limiting scientific validation and optimization. This project seeks to address this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model the polypharmacological effects of a curated library of 500 plant-derived compounds, focusing on their synergistic interactions within inflammation-related pathways. Leveraging molecular docking, machine learning-based binding affinity prediction, and dynamic network pharmacology, the research will simulate compound-target interactions across proteome-scale datasets to identify key bioactive agents and their cooperative effects. The computational pipeline integrates AlphaFold-predicted protein structures, molecular dynamics simulations for conformational sampling, and Bayesian network analysis to map multi-target modulation patterns. HPC resources are essential to manage the iterative, high-throughput processing of over 10^6 potential compound-target pairs, requiring parallelized GPU-accelerated simulations and distributed memory architectures for large-scale graph-based network analyses. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel synergistic herbal combinations with predicted anti-inflammatory properties, validated through subsequent in vitro testing. The project will generate an open-access database of compound interaction profiles, bridging traditional knowledge systems with computational systems biology. By establishing a framework for analyzing complex botanical formulations at molecular resolution, this work aims to advance evidence-based integration of alternative medicine into contemporary healthcare paradigms while contributing computational methodologies applicable to other understudied therapeutic modalities.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized learning pathways in adaptive educational technologies, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the scalability and real-time responsiveness challenges inherent in dynamic, multimodal learning environments. While adaptive learning systems increasingly integrate artificial intelligence (AI) to tailor content delivery, existing approaches often rely on simplified models of learner behavior, neglecting the interplay between cognitive load, affective states, and environmental factors. This research addresses the critical gap in modeling these complex, interdependent variables at scale, particularly for learners with neurodiverse profiles or in resource-constrained settings. The project will utilize heterogeneous datasets, including eye-tracking metrics, physiological signals (e.g., heart rate variability), and interaction logs from digital learning platforms, to train multimodal deep learning architectures. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of temporal data streams, hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models, and simulations of population-level learning outcomes under varying intervention strategies. Key computational challenges include real-time fusion of sparse, noisy multimodal data and the development of reinforcement learning agents capable of operating within ethical constraints for educational decision-making. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive system design, validated against randomized controlled trials in K-12 mathematics classrooms, and a novel benchmarking dataset for evaluating computational models of situated learning. By advancing the computational fidelity of learner-state representations, this work aims to establish new standards for ethically grounded, evidence-driven adaptive technologies while providing scalable methods for resource-efficient personalization—a critical need as education systems worldwide confront growing demands for inclusivity and accessibility.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into neuroradiology is critical to address the growing complexity of diagnosing and managing disorders of the nervous system. Current clinical workflows struggle to process the increasing volume of high-resolution imaging data—such as multi-parametric MRI, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and functional MRI (fMRI)—alongside clinical and molecular datasets. Traditional analysis tools lack the scalability to identify subtle biomarkers of diseases like glioblastoma, multiple sclerosis, and neurovascular malformations, leading to delays in diagnosis and suboptimal treatment personalization. This project seeks to bridge this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate novel machine learning (ML) algorithms for multi-modal data integration and predictive modeling. The research will focus on three aims: (1) creating automated pipelines for segmenting and quantifying pathological features in heterogenous imaging datasets, (2) training deep learning models to correlate imaging phenotypes with genomic and clinical outcomes, and (3) simulating disease progression patterns using patient-specific biomechanical models. These tasks require intensive parallel processing, large-scale GPU-accelerated model training, and high-memory nodes to handle datasets exceeding 500 TB from retrospective cohorts and prospective trials. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures, as well as finite element modeling of tissue deformation in neurodegenerative conditions. Successfully implementing this computational framework is expected to yield clinically validated tools for early detection of tumor recurrence, precise stratification of stroke risk, and optimized surgical planning for epilepsy. By unifying imaging, molecular, and clinical data into actionable insights, this project aims to establish a scalable platform for advancing precision neuroimaging, ultimately reducing diagnostic variability and improving patient outcomes in neuroradiology practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the brain, spine, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, and head and neck in adults and children.

abstract: Child care environments significantly influence developmental outcomes, yet optimizing these spaces for safety, engagement, and equitable access remains a complex, understudied challenge. Traditional approaches rely on observational studies or small-scale trials, which are resource-intensive and lack scalability. This project proposes a novel computational framework to model and simulate child care environments, integrating behavioral dynamics, spatial design, and caregiver workflows. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to develop agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate interactions between children, caregivers, and physical environments under diverse conditions. The ABMs will incorporate real-world data on child behavior patterns, regulatory requirements, and environmental variables (e.g., noise levels, furniture layout) to generate probabilistic risk assessments and optimize space utilization. Machine learning techniques will be applied to iteratively refine models using anonymized sensor data from partner child care centers, capturing movement, activity transitions, and safety incidents. The computational pipeline will require large-scale parameter sweeps to account for variability in group sizes, developmental stages, and staffing ratios, necessitating parallelized workflows and significant memory allocation. Outcomes will include predictive tools to identify high-risk configurations, recommend adaptive layout modifications, and simulate the impact of policy changes (e.g., adjusted caregiver-to-child ratios) on operational efficiency. By bridging computational modeling and early childhood education practice, this work will provide evidence-based strategies to enhance care quality while reducing operational costs. The project represents a unique interdisciplinary niche, advancing methodologies in non-STEM fields by applying HPC to systemic challenges in community-focused professions. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools tailored for child care providers, enabling data-driven decision-making without requiring computational expertise.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be primary providers of home, family, residential, or institutional-based child care services. Includes instruction in child growth and development, nutrition, recreation, planning and supervision of play and learning activities, child abuse and neglect prevention, parent-child relationships, and applicable legal and administrative requirements.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in supervisory decision-making processes within K-12 educational settings by developing computational models to optimize resource allocation and instructional leadership strategies. School administrators face complex challenges in balancing personnel assignments, professional development investments, and curricular alignment amid dynamic institutional constraints. Traditional qualitative approaches to these problems often lack scalability and predictive precision, particularly in diverse or under-resourced districts. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a two-phase computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, an agent-based modeling framework will simulate interactions between administrators, teachers, and students across varied demographic and resource scenarios, incorporating longitudinal data on staffing patterns, student outcomes, and budget parameters from state education databases. Second, machine learning techniques will analyze the simulation outputs to identify patterns in effective supervisory strategies, with particular attention to equity in resource distribution and curriculum implementation fidelity. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of modeling thousands of interdependent variables across multi-year timescales in simulated school systems. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs in supervisory approaches and predicts the downstream impacts of leadership decisions on instructional quality metrics. This work will provide education administrators with evidence-based frameworks for strategically allocating human and material resources while maintaining compliance with instructional standards. By bridging computational social science with educational leadership theory, the project aims to advance data-driven supervision practices that enhance curricular coherence and operational efficiency in diverse educational contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise instructional and support personnel at the school building, facility or staff level. Includes instruction in the principles of staffing and organization, the supervision of learning activities, personnel relations, administrative duties related to departmental or unit management, and specific applications to various educational settings and curricula.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of culinary precision and innovation through computational modeling of complex gastronomic processes. The research focuses on optimizing cooking techniques and ingredient interactions in large-scale food production, addressing challenges such as inconsistent texture, flavor degradation, and energy inefficiency in commercial kitchens. Current empirical approaches to recipe scaling and equipment calibration lack predictive accuracy, particularly for novel cooking methods (e.g., sous-vide, flash-freezing) or alternative protein matrices. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning to model heat and mass transfer phenomena during cooking. High-fidelity simulations will analyze time-temperature profiles in heterogeneous food systems, predict protein denaturation pathways, and quantify nutrient retention under varying processing conditions. A parallelized workflow will process tera-scale datasets capturing ingredient physicochemical properties, equipment performance metrics, and sensory outcome correlations from partnered culinary institutes. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from controlled cooking trials, with iterative model refinement using neural networks trained on heterogeneous data streams (thermal imaging, spectroscopy, sensory panels). Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing cooking parameters in industrial kitchens, reducing energy consumption by 15–20% through dynamic equipment scheduling algorithms, and enabling data-driven design of plant-based meat analogs with improved palatability. This work establishes a novel computational paradigm for culinary science, merging food chemistry, thermodynamics, and data analytics to address pressing challenges in sustainable food systems and global foodservice operations. By transcending traditional trial-and-error methodologies, the project aims to catalyze innovation in culinary arts education and industrial practice through quantitatively grounded, computation-first approaches.
cip_title: Cooking and Related Culinary Arts, General.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of the cooking and related culinary arts, and that may prepare individuals for a variety of jobs within the food service industry.  Includes instruction in food preparation, cooking techniques, equipment operation and maintenance, sanitation and safety, communication skills, applicable regulations, and principles of food service management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of zoonotic disease transmission dynamics in livestock populations, with a focus on optimizing intervention strategies. Emerging animal pathogens pose significant risks to global food security and public health, yet existing epidemiological models often fail to account for the complex interplay of host genetic diversity, pathogen evolution, and environmental factors that drive transmission. Current limitations in processing large-scale genomic, metagenomic, and environmental datasets restrict the resolution and predictive accuracy of these models. To address this gap, we propose developing an integrative simulation framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and phylogenetic inference to analyze multi-omics data from cattle and poultry systems. The computational workflow will incorporate whole-genome sequences of priority pathogens (e.g., avian influenza viruses, Mycobacterium bovis), host immune gene profiles, and high-resolution environmental covariates to simulate transmission pathways under varying management practices. HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of >10,000 stochastic simulations to quantify intervention efficacy across diverse production systems and climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of genetic markers associated with superspreader hosts, 2) predictive models of outbreak hotspots based on evolving pathogen strains, and 3) optimized vaccine deployment protocols balancing epidemiological impact and agricultural economics. The resulting open-source tools will empower veterinary researchers to perform resource-efficient genomic surveillance and scenario testing at scale. By bridging gaps between theoretical epidemiology and applied animal health decision-making, this work directly supports the development of precision veterinary interventions while mitigating risks of zoonotic spillover. The scale of genomic datasets (>50 TB) and need for real-time parameter optimization in spatial-temporal models necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve biologically relevant resolutions within operational timeframes.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary or animal health technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Radiation therapy efficacy hinges on optimizing tumor targeting while minimizing damage to healthy tissues, yet current treatment planning systems struggle to predict dynamic biological responses to radiation at the cellular and molecular levels. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution computational model integrating radiomic features from clinical imaging, biophysical simulations of radiation-induced DNA damage repair mechanisms, and machine learning (ML) to predict patient-specific radiosensitivity. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of static dose-painting approaches by creating an adaptive framework that accounts for temporal changes in tumor microenvironment heterogeneity and normal tissue tolerance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport at submillimeter scales across serial CT/MRI datasets, coupled with stochastic modeling of repair protein kinetics derived from published -omics databases. A neural network architecture will be trained on retrospective clinical outcomes data (local control and toxicity rates) to identify predictive signatures linking simulated biological responses to observed therapeutic ratios. The computational workflow will parallelize image segmentation, dose deposition calculations, and ML training across GPU nodes, requiring petascale storage for multi-terabyte imaging cohorts and iterative model validation. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for personalized radiation dose optimization, validated against a 500-patient institutional dataset, that quantifies uncertainty in biological response predictions. This work addresses a critical gap in radiobiological treatment personalization, with potential to reduce late complications in radiosensitive organs-at-risk while enabling dose escalation for resistant tumor subvolumes. Successful implementation could redefine adaptive radiotherapy workflows by integrating real-time biological feedback into treatment planning systems.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of neuromuscular disorders necessitates advanced methodologies to optimize rehabilitation strategies for patients undergoing physical therapy. Current clinical protocols rely on generalized biomechanical models that inadequately capture individual variability in musculoskeletal dynamics, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to design personalized therapeutic interventions by modeling patient-specific neuromuscular responses to rehabilitation exercises. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to integrate high-resolution motion capture data, electromyography (EMG), and medical imaging into multiscale biomechanical simulations that predict tissue stress distributions, motor unit recruitment patterns, and energy expenditure during task-specific movements. The computational pipeline will employ finite element analysis to simulate soft tissue deformation, coupled with agent-based modeling of motor neuron activation, to create dynamic, patient-adaptive digital twins. Machine learning techniques will be applied to iteratively refine these models using real-world clinical outcome data, enabling the identification of movement patterns that maximize functional recovery while minimizing injury risk. Challenges include managing the computational complexity of real-time feedback loops between sensor data and model parameters, which requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a deployable tool for clinicians to virtually test and compare rehabilitation protocols tailored to individual biomechanical constraints. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and rehabilitation science, offering a novel paradigm for precision physical therapy. Successful implementation could reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, accelerate recovery timelines, and inform the development of next-generation assistive devices. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the intensive memory and processing demands of multiscale simulations, enabling parameter optimization at unprecedented resolution across anatomical hierarchies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physical therapist, to implement physical therapy treatment care plans, train patients, conduct treatment interventions, use equipment, and observe and record patient progress. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, behavioral sciences, biomechanics, clinical documentation, clinical pathology, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Cellular architecture and dynamic structural organization are fundamental to tissue development, homeostasis, and disease, yet the mechanisms coordinating these processes remain poorly resolved at multi-scale levels. This project seeks to address this gap by investigating how subcellular features—such as organelle positioning, cytoskeletal rearrangements, and membrane topology—integrate with tissue-level organization in vertebrate epithelial systems. We propose a computational framework combining large-scale 3D electron microscopy datasets of developing avian epithelia with agent-based modeling to simulate cellular behavior under varying biophysical constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of imaging data via automated segmentation pipelines leveraging deep learning architectures (3D U-Net variants) and to iteratively parameterize multi-agent models that simulate cell-cell mechanical interactions across thousands of cells. The computational workflow will first reconstruct spatial relationships between organelles and cell boundaries from segmented EM stacks, then use these geometric descriptors to inform rule sets for agent behaviors in tissue context. Validation will involve comparative analysis against live-imaging datasets of epithelial morphogenesis. This integrative approach aims to identify conserved principles of structural coordination across scales, with expected outcomes including predictive models of how perturbations in organelle dynamics propagate to tissue-scale deformations. The work will advance understanding of developmental malformations linked to cytoskeletal dysregulation and provide open-source tools for correlative structural-computational analysis in cell biology. By elucidating feedback between subcellular organization and tissue mechanics, this research will establish a foundation for probing analogous processes in human epithelial pathologies, offering insights into potential therapeutic strategies targeting structural plasticity.
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cells, cellular systems, and the molecular basis of cell structure and function. Includes instruction in cell biology, cell chemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, and structural biology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for efficient, scalable solutions to optimize real-time media content delivery in high-bandwidth communication networks. As streaming platforms, immersive media applications (e.g., augmented/virtual reality), and personalized content distribution systems expand, existing infrastructure struggles to balance latency, quality, and resource utilization. Traditional approaches to network optimization often rely on static models that fail to account for dynamic user behavior, heterogeneous device capabilities, and fluctuating bandwidth availability.
