The computational workflow will utilize GPU-optimized packages (e.g., GROMACS, AMBER) for large-scale parallel simulations, requiring terabytes of memory and thousands of core-hours to achieve microsecond-scale sampling for complex lipid bilayer systems. Expected outcomes include the identification of three lead compounds with improved metabolic stability for experimental validation, alongside predictive models correlating simulation-derived descriptors with in vitro absorption parameters. This work directly supports precision pharmacy initiatives by enabling rational drug design strategies that reduce reliance on iterative trial-and-error approaches. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of ligand-receptor systems, solvent interactions, and free energy calculations inherent to pharmaceutical sciences, providing foundational insights for optimizing therapeutic regimens and patient-specific dosing protocols.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent or employed practice of preparing and dispensing drugs and medications in consultation with prescribing physicians and other health care professionals, and for managing pharmacy practices and counseling patients. Includes instruction in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmacy practice, pharmacy administration, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance multidisciplinary research on cultural exchange and urbanization patterns in the ancient Mediterranean and Near East (circa 2000 BCE–500 CE). The research problem centers on synthesizing fragmented archaeological, textual, and environmental datasets—spanning regions such as Mesopotamia, Anatolia, and the Levant—to model how trade networks, migration, and resource distribution influenced the rise of urban centers. Traditional methods struggle to integrate disparate data types at scale, limiting holistic analysis of socio-political and economic dynamics. To address this, the project will employ computational approaches including agent-based modeling (ABM), geospatial network analysis, and machine learning (ML) techniques for artifact classification and textual analysis. ABM simulations will reconstruct hypothetical trade routes and demographic shifts, calibrated against archaeological records and climate proxy data. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze multilingual corpora (Akkadian, Hittite, Greek) to identify references to resource management, treaties, or labor practices, cross-referenced with material evidence. HPC resources are critical for handling the scale of 3D site reconstructions, iterative ML training on ceramic typologies, and parallel processing of simulation scenarios. Expected outcomes include dynamically mapped interaction networks, predictive models of urban growth under environmental stressors, and open-access tools for artifact-image recognition. By computationally bridging gaps between archaeology, epigraphy, and environmental studies, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of connectivity in antiquity, offering methodologies applicable to understudied regions and periods. The project aligns with broader efforts to digitize and democratize cultural heritage data while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in ancient studies.
cip_title: Classical, Ancient Mediterranean, and Near Eastern Studies and Archaeology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the classical ancient civilizations of the ancient Near East, Europe, and the Mediterranean Sea, such as Athens, Anatolia, Egypt, Greece, Israel, Mesopotamia, North Africa, and Rome. Includes instruction in ancient languages, ancient history, archaeology, anthropology, Greek and Roman mythology, philosophy, and religion.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to address the challenges of creating scalable, high-fidelity digital illustrations that integrate dynamic data sources and real-time interactivity. Traditional illustration workflows often struggle to adapt to scenarios requiring rapid iteration, such as interactive children’s books, augmented reality (AR) visualizations, or data-driven editorial graphics. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational bottlenecks in rendering complex, multi-layered visual narratives that respond to user input or live data streams. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate and optimize these processes, particularly for projects involving large-scale datasets, physics-based simulations of artistic media (e.g., watercolor diffusion, ink dispersion), or AI-driven style transfer across thousands of frames. The computational approach combines procedural generation algorithms, neural networks trained on artistic style corpora, and GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines. For example, one proposed method involves using generative adversarial networks (GANs) to automate texture synthesis for background elements in storyboard illustrations, reducing manual labor while preserving artistic intent. Another focus area is real-time collaboration tools for distributed illustration teams, requiring low-latency synchronization of high-resolution assets. The project will leverage HPC clusters to parallelize tasks such as batch processing of 3D model textures, training domain-specific AI models on historical illustration datasets, and stress-testing interactive platforms under simulated user loads. Expected outcomes include open-source software plugins for popular illustration tools, optimized workflows for data-intensive projects, and case studies demonstrating reduced production timelines for complex commissions. By bridging computational efficiency with artistic nuance, this work aims to expand the scope of illustration as a medium for responsive, adaptive storytelling in education, journalism, and entertainment, while establishing best practices for integrating HPC resources into creative disciplines.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to identify structural inequities in postsecondary student outcomes using institution-scale datasets, a task requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the volume and complexity of the data. Institutional researchers often face challenges in analyzing longitudinal datasets that integrate academic records, demographic variables, and student engagement metrics—processes hindered by conventional computing infrastructure. The research problem centers on improving the scalability and precision of equity-focused analytics to support data-driven interventions. We propose a computational approach combining machine learning (e.g., ensemble classifiers, clustering algorithms) with causal inference techniques to analyze multi-year datasets from a diverse public university system (N ≈ 250,000 students). Key tasks include preprocessing unstructured data (e.g., academic advising notes via NLP), training predictive models on GPU nodes to accelerate hyperparameter tuning, and simulating policy impacts via agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will leverage Python libraries (Dask, PyTorch) optimized for distributed computing, with validation against traditional statistical methods. The project’s significance lies in its capacity to address latency and resource constraints inherent in single-node systems, enabling near-real-time analysis of equity gaps across intersecting demographic categories. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source pipeline for scalable equity analytics in higher education, (2) evidence-based recommendations for targeted retention strategies, and (3) benchmarks for HPC-enabled institutional research workflows. By demonstrating how parallelized computing can advance equity-focused decision-making, this work aims to establish new methodological standards for institutional researchers while directly addressing computational bottlenecks in handling sensitive, high-dimensional educational data.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares an individual to be an institutional researcher at a postsecondary educational institution. Includes instruction in data analysis, data-driven decision-making, data mining, higher education administration and organization, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: Construction engineering projects face growing demands for efficiency, sustainability, and resilience, yet current methods for structural optimization, supply chain logistics, and risk assessment often rely on oversimplified models that fail to capture real-world complexities. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate and optimize construction processes at scale, integrating multi-physics structural analysis, machine learning-driven resource allocation, and stochastic modeling of project uncertainties. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to parallelize finite element simulations of novel construction materials under dynamic environmental loads, such as seismic activity and extreme weather, while coupling these with agent-based models of on-site workflows. A key innovation involves training graph neural networks on historical project data to predict delays and optimize procurement schedules, accounting for interdependencies between suppliers, labor availability, and regulatory constraints. The computational workflow will also incorporate real-time data streams from IoT sensors at construction sites to enable adaptive decision-making. By leveraging HPC resources, this work will overcome limitations in conventional single-node simulations, enabling whole-system analysis of billion-element structural models and Monte Carlo simulations of project timelines across thousands of scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying cost-risk tradeoffs in design choices, validated strategies for resilient material procurement, and open-source modules for automated code compliance checking. These advances will directly support construction professionals in mitigating delays and cost overruns while improving adherence to safety standards. The project will further bridge gaps between computational engineering and construction management, establishing new benchmarks for data-driven infrastructure planning in the Technology and Technical fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers, engineering contractors and other professionals engaged in the construction of buildings and related structures. Includes instruction in basic structural engineering principles and construction techniques, building site inspection, site supervision, construction personnel supervision, plan and specification interpretation, supply logistics and procurement, applicable building codes, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in nursing education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize clinical training scenarios. A persistent gap exists in scalable, evidence-based methods for preparing nursing educators to design and evaluate clinical instruction, particularly in resource-constrained or high-demand settings. Traditional approaches to clinical education rely heavily on in-person placements, which are limited by capacity, variability in patient encounters, and inconsistent access to rare or high-risk scenarios. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates diverse clinical learning environments, predicts student competency outcomes, and identifies optimal instructional strategies. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning, we will create dynamic, data-driven simulations of clinical decision-making scenarios. These simulations will integrate anonymized electronic health record data, student performance metrics, and educator feedback to generate synthetic patient cases and learner interactions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of thousands of simulated training sessions, allowing us to test variables such as instructor-student ratios, case complexity, and intervention timing. Additionally, natural language processing will be applied to analyze qualitative feedback from nursing educators, identifying patterns in instructional effectiveness. The outcomes will include (1) a validated predictive model linking instructional design choices to competency development, (2) an open-access toolkit for generating adaptive clinical training modules, and (3) recommendations for balancing simulation-based and traditional clinical hours in nursing curricula. By quantifying relationships between educational inputs and learner outcomes, this work will directly inform accreditation standards and faculty development programs, ultimately enhancing the capacity of nursing educators to train clinicians capable of addressing complex healthcare needs. The scale and interdependencies of the datasets necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust, generalizable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to teach in academic and clinical settings, including staff development. Includes instruction in advanced nursing practice, nursing role development, curriculum and instruction, program and course design, clinical instruction, and evaluation of learning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the design and safety of outdoor education programs through the development of predictive environmental-behavioral models. Outdoor education relies on dynamic interactions between participants, instructors, and natural environments, yet current risk assessment and curriculum design practices lack robust computational tools to anticipate emergent challenges such as weather variability, terrain complexity, and group decision-making under stress. Traditional approaches prioritize retrospective analysis or static scenario planning, leaving gaps in proactive adaptability. This research addresses these limitations by constructing agent-based simulations that integrate real-time environmental data, physiological stress indicators, and historical incident datasets to model participant behavior and instructor responses in wilderness contexts. Computational workflows will process geospatial data (e.g., elevation, vegetation density) and biometric inputs (e.g., heart rate variability, movement patterns) to simulate scenarios ranging from routine skill-building exercises to crisis events like sudden storms or injuries. Machine learning algorithms will identify patterns in decision trees and resource allocation, enabling the optimization of evacuation routes, equipment distribution, and group pacing strategies. By coupling HPC-enabled simulations with field data from partner outdoor education organizations, the project aims to generate adaptive frameworks for risk mitigation and curriculum personalization. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for instructors to forecast site-specific hazards, dynamically adjust activity plans, and evaluate training efficacy through virtual scenario testing. This work bridges computational modeling and experiential pedagogy, offering a novel methodology to enhance safety protocols and educational outcomes in non-institutionalized learning environments. The requested computing resources will support large-scale parallelized simulations, data assimilation from heterogeneous sources, and the development of interactive visualization platforms for stakeholder engagement.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work as an educator, instructor or facilitator in parks, recreational facilities, camps and other outdoor settings. Includes instruction in leadership skills, wilderness survival skills, first aid, group processes, counseling techniques, environmental studies and instruction in recreational activities such as rock climbing, ropes courses, backpacking, kayaking and canoeing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the technical and creative possibilities of printmaking through computational modeling and simulation. Traditional printmaking processes—such as lithography, intaglio, and relief printing—rely on manual experimentation to predict ink behavior, substrate interactions, and layered image alignment. However, this trial-and-error approach limits the scale, precision, and complexity of achievable outcomes, particularly when working with novel materials or multi-layered compositions. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to simulate ink dispersion, viscosity dynamics, and registration accuracy across diverse printmaking techniques, enabling artists to previsualize results and optimize workflows computationally. Using fluid dynamics simulations, finite element analysis, and agent-based modeling, the project will quantify how variables such as ink chemistry, pressure gradients, and surface texture influence print fidelity. Machine learning models will be trained on empirical data from physical prints to correlate simulated parameters with artistic outcomes, iteratively refining predictive accuracy. Additionally, HPC resources will support the development of algorithmic tools for generative design, enabling the creation of intricate, large-scale patterns that transcend manual drafting limitations. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation frameworks tailored to printmaking workflows, validated through collaborative experiments with practicing artists. These tools aim to reduce material waste, expand creative possibilities in multi-process printmaking, and establish a bridge between computational research and studio practice. By integrating HPC-driven insights into traditional techniques, this project will contribute to the evolution of printmaking as a hybrid discipline, fostering innovation at the intersection of visual art, materials science, and computational design. The broader significance lies in demonstrating how advanced computing can enhance tactile art forms while preserving their material integrity, offering a model for interdisciplinary resource sharing in the visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by rendering art concepts onto surfaces and transferring images, via ink or dyes, onto paper or fabric. Includes instruction in monochrome and color printing; tonality; chemistry; equipment set-up and maintenance; techniques such as serigraphy, lithography, intaglio, woodcut, block, stencil, relief, etching, and composite; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize individualized learning pathways for middle school students in special education programs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational data. Students with disabilities often exhibit heterogeneous learning profiles, yet educators face challenges in efficiently integrating diverse data sources—such as academic performance, behavioral logs, individualized education program (IEP) goals, and real-time classroom interactions—to inform instructional decisions. Current tools lack the scalability to process these complex datasets or simulate longitudinal outcomes of pedagogical strategies. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline that processes structured and unstructured data (e.g., written teacher feedback, sensor-based engagement metrics) using natural language processing and time-series analysis. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of ensemble models to predict student progress across learning domains (e.g., literacy, numeracy) under varying intervention scenarios. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom-scale interactions, testing how resource allocation (e.g., assistive technology deployment, paraeducator support timing) affects both individualized and group outcomes. The computational workflow will integrate anonymized datasets from 15 middle school special education programs, comprising over 5,000 student-hours of observational and assessment data. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable tool for generating dynamic IEP recommendations based on predictive analytics, (2) quantified thresholds for intervention efficacy across disability categories, and (3) optimized scheduling strategies for special education classrooms derived from simulation results. This work will provide evidence-based frameworks to help teachers prioritize instructional targets, reduce trial-and-error in intervention design, and allocate limited classroom resources more effectively. By coupling educational theory with computational modeling, the project aims to advance data-driven practices in special education teacher preparation and middle school classroom implementation.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Junior High/ Middle School Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in junior high/middle school. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for middle school special education; and principles of middle school instruction in specific subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in healthcare administrative workflows, particularly in scheduling, communication, and resource coordination, which contribute to operational delays, increased costs, and reduced patient satisfaction. Medical administrative professionals are critical to managing these workflows, yet existing tools often lack the computational power to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets (e.g., electronic health records, appointment logs, staff communications) required for optimizing decision-making. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that identify bottlenecks in healthcare operations. Using anonymized datasets from partner clinics, we will train machine learning algorithms to forecast patient no-show rates, predict resource utilization conflicts, and model the impact of alternative scheduling protocols. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to analyze communication patterns between administrative staff and clinical teams, identifying inefficiencies in task delegation and urgency prioritization. Agent-based simulations will further test the scalability of proposed workflow adjustments under varying patient volumes and staffing conditions. The computational intensity of processing multi-modal data (structured records, unstructured text, temporal sequences) necessitates HPC infrastructure to enable parallelized model training and real-time simulations. Outcomes will include actionable insights for redesigning administrative protocols, reducing patient wait times, and improving alignment between staffing resources and demand. This work directly supports the training goals of medical administrative professionals by advancing data-driven tools for operational decision-making, while adhering to healthcare privacy regulations and ethical standards. Results will be disseminated through open-source workflow optimization frameworks tailored for non-technical users, ensuring accessibility for healthcare administrators and educators.
cip_title: Medical Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Medical Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing physicians and nurses, health care facilities and services administrators, and other health care professionals. Includes instruction in business and medical communications, medical terminology, principles of health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The development of advanced solid-state electrolytes with high ionic conductivity and mechanical stability is critical for next-generation energy storage technologies. However, a fundamental challenge lies in understanding the atomic-scale mechanisms governing ion transport in amorphous and composite materials, which exhibit complex interfacial dynamics and heterogeneous structural evolution. This project seeks to address this gap by employing large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and machine learning-accelerated density functional theory (DFT) simulations to model ion diffusion pathways, interfacial strain effects, and defect interactions in novel sulfide- and oxide-based electrolytes. The proposed computational workflows will integrate multiscale modeling frameworks to resolve time-dependent material responses under operational conditions, including thermal cycling and mechanical stress. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the ∼10-million-atom systems required for statistically meaningful sampling of amorphous phase boundaries and the iterative training of neural network potentials for reactive ion dynamics. Expected outcomes include identifying descriptor-based design rules for optimizing ionic conductivity through targeted doping and nanostructuring, as well as predictive models linking interfacial morphology to degradation mechanisms. The results will directly inform experimental synthesis efforts aimed at achieving stable, high-capacity solid-state batteries, with potential applications in electric vehicles and grid-scale storage. By elucidating structure-property relationships in these disordered materials, this work will advance the broader field of computational materials design for energy technologies, while establishing scalable protocols for simulating multiphase interfaces under non-equilibrium conditions. The requested allocation supports 1.2 million core-hours on GPU-accelerated nodes for MD trajectories and 400,000 CPU-hours for ensemble DFT calculations, enabling parametric studies across compositionally graded material libraries.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in materials sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The rapid integration of urban ecosystems and human-modified landscapes has created complex challenges for biodiversity conservation, requiring novel approaches that bridge ecological modeling, spatial data science, and urban planning. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to predict how heterogeneous urban environments influence species persistence and ecosystem resilience at regional scales. Current models often oversimplify the interplay between fine-grained habitat fragmentation, microclimate variability, and species behavior, limiting their utility for adaptive urban design. To address this gap, we propose coupling high-resolution geospatial datasets—including LiDAR-derived 3D urban structures, IoT sensor networks, and citizen science biodiversity observations—with agent-based simulations and machine learning to model multi-species responses to dynamic urban conditions. The computational workflow will integrate graph neural networks to analyze habitat connectivity, physics-informed neural operators to simulate microclimate cascades, and reinforcement learning to optimize conservation interventions. This requires high-performance computing resources to manage petabyte-scale environmental datasets, parallelize spatially explicit simulations across thousands of urban grid cells, and train generative models for scenario exploration. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform enabling municipalities to evaluate the ecological impact of infrastructure projects in near-real time, with pilot applications focused on pollinator corridor design and heat island mitigation. By fusing ecological theory with scalable data science methods, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for urban biodiversity analytics, directly informing policy frameworks that balance development needs with ecosystem health. The computational infrastructure developed will be adaptable to other interdisciplinary challenges requiring the synthesis of hyper-local environmental data with complex system dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis of large scale data sources from the interdisciplinary perspectives of applied statistics, computer science, data storage, data representation, data modeling, mathematics, and statistics. Includes instruction in computer algorithms, computer programming, data management, data mining, information policy, information retrieval, mathematical modeling, quantitative analysis, statistics, trend spotting, and visual analytics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of translational research in laboratory animal medicine demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in modeling human diseases, optimizing experimental design, and managing high-dimensional datasets. Current limitations in analyzing multimodal data—including biomedical imaging, genomic profiles, and longitudinal physiological metrics—hinder the development of robust, predictive animal models. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these barriers by integrating heterogeneous datasets from murine and non-human primate studies of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The research will focus on three aims: (1) developing machine learning pipelines to identify cross-species biomarkers of disease progression using RNA sequencing, histopathology, and microbiome data; (2) implementing agent-based simulations to model host-microbe interactions and predict treatment responses; and (3) optimizing experimental power calculations through synthetic data generation to reduce animal use while maintaining statistical rigor. Computational workflows will utilize containerized environments for reproducibility, with GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models) applied to temporal data analysis. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of high-resolution imaging, scaling ensemble ML methods across thousands of simulated experimental conditions, and performing real-time analytics in ongoing studies. Expected outcomes include novel predictive frameworks for IBD pathogenesis, validated computational models for prioritizing therapeutic candidates, and open-source tools for ethical experimental design in translational animal research. By bridging gaps between veterinary medicine and computational biology, this work aims to enhance the translational relevance of animal studies while advancing resource-efficient practices in laboratory animal facilities.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied veterinary research and related techniques, equipment, data systems and research design. May included related research in the management of veterinary and other animal research laboratories and health care facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for law enforcement agencies operating in dynamic, high-stakes environments. The research problem centers on the challenge of balancing finite personnel, equipment, and budgetary resources against unpredictable demands, including fluctuating crime patterns, emergency response priorities, and community engagement requirements. Traditional decision-making models often rely on historical data or static protocols, which fail to account for real-time variables such as traffic disruptions, simultaneous critical incidents, or shifting public safety needs. To address this gap, we propose the creation of an adaptive simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model urban ecosystems, criminal behavior networks, and emergency response workflows at scale. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling to simulate civilian and law enforcement interactions, graph theory to analyze crime correlation patterns across jurisdictions, and Monte Carlo methods to stress-test allocation strategies under stochastic scenarios. By incorporating real-time data streams—such as 911 call logs, traffic sensors, and social media sentiment analysis—the system will dynamically adjust resource distribution algorithms to minimize response times while maintaining preventive policing presence. Expected outcomes include a suite of predictive tools to visualize trade-offs in deployment decisions, quantify the cascading impacts of resource reallocation, and identify latent vulnerabilities in existing operational frameworks. The project’s significance lies in its potential to provide law enforcement administrators with evidence-based strategies that enhance public safety outcomes without proportional increases in budgetary expenditure. Additionally, the modular architecture of the simulation platform will enable adaptation to diverse urban and rural contexts, offering a scalable solution for agencies with varying resource constraints. This work bridges computational social systems analysis with practical criminal justice administration, advancing a data-driven paradigm for public safety resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply theories and practices of organization management and criminal justice to the administration of public law enforcement agencies and operations. Includes instruction in law enforcement history and theory, operational command leadership, administration of public police organizations, labor relations, incident response strategies, legal and regulatory responsibilities, budgeting, public relations, and organizational leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance early childhood education (ECE) by modeling and optimizing individualized teaching strategies for diverse learners aged 0–8 years. A critical challenge in ECE is designing scalable, adaptive pedagogical approaches that account for variability in developmental trajectories, learning styles, and socioemotional needs. Traditional observational and survey-based methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multivariate interactions between instructional practices, child behavior, and learning outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom environments and predict the efficacy of teaching interventions. Large-scale datasets—including longitudinal assessments, video-recorded classroom interactions, and physiological response metrics (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate)—will be analyzed using deep neural networks to identify patterns in engagement and skill acquisition. Concurrently, ABM will simulate hypothetical teaching scenarios, varying parameters such as lesson pacing, group composition, and multimodal instruction (e.g., tactile vs. visual tools). These simulations will generate probabilistic outcomes for skill mastery and socioemotional growth, enabling data-driven recommendations for personalized teaching practices. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, training complex ML models, and running thousands of parallelized ABM iterations to ensure statistical robustness. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of computational models linking teaching strategies to learner profiles, (2) evidence-based guidelines for adapting curricula in real-time classroom settings, and (3) a pipeline for translating simulated insights into teacher training modules. By bridging computational analytics and ECE pedagogy, this work aims to equip educators with scalable tools to enhance equity and efficacy in early learning environments.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students ranging in age from infancy through eight years (grade three), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: Wildfire behavior prediction and forensic investigation require advanced computational tools to address the complex, multi-scale interactions between fire dynamics, environmental variables, and human interventions. Current operational models often lack the resolution and integration needed to simulate coupled fire-atmosphere interactions, heterogeneous fuel distributions, and fire suppression impacts in diverse terrains, limiting their utility for real-time decision-making and post-fire cause analysis. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to advance wildfire simulation accuracy and forensic reconstruction capabilities. The research will employ coupled fire-atmosphere modeling using WRF-Fire and FIRETEC, enhanced by machine learning algorithms trained on historical fire data, satellite imagery, and sensor networks to improve predictions of fire spread under varying meteorological and fuel conditions. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate firefighter operations and suppression tactics to evaluate their effectiveness in dynamic scenarios. For forensic applications, inverse modeling techniques and Bayesian networks will be implemented to probabilistically reconstruct ignition sources and fire pathways using post-fire scene data, weather records, and terrain information. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, ensemble simulations for uncertainty quantification, and 3D visualization of fire progression. Expected outcomes include a validated, open-access modeling platform for predicting fire behavior at sub-100m resolution, evidence-based guidelines for airborne firefighting resource deployment, and a forensic toolkit to support arson investigations. By integrating fire science, computational fluid dynamics, and data-driven methods, this work aims to reduce wildfire risks, enhance responder safety, and improve the precision of fire cause determinations, directly supporting the resilience goals of homeland security and fire protection agencies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science, firefighting and investigation to the prevention, control and mitigation of wildland fires and the analysis of causes. Includes instruction in fire science and behavior, wildland environments, meteorology, wildland fire hydraulics and dynamics, water and chemical supply systems, wildland firefighting operations, airborne firefighting, firebreak engineering, communications systems, wildland arson, forensic procedures, wildland fire prevention, investigation techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in clinical decision-making for physician assistants (PAs), with a focus on optimizing diagnostic accuracy and treatment outcomes in underserved populations. A critical challenge in PA practice is the integration of heterogeneous clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), imaging, and genomic biomarkers—to inform timely, evidence-based decisions under resource-constrained settings. Traditional analytical tools struggle to process these multimodal datasets efficiently, particularly in rural or homebound patient populations where access to specialized diagnostics is limited. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models trained on federated healthcare datasets to predict disease progression and therapeutic responses across diverse demographics. Computational workflows will prioritize scalability and interpretability, utilizing natural language processing (NLP) to extract features from unstructured clinical notes and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze medical imaging. These models will be validated against retrospective outcomes from partner community health networks. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of training ensemble models on distributed datasets while ensuring compliance with patient privacy regulations through secure, encrypted data pipelines. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools tailored to PA workflows, such as risk stratification algorithms for sepsis in homecare settings and decision-support systems for managing comorbidities in geriatric populations. By reducing diagnostic latency and personalizing treatment plans, this research aims to mitigate disparities in care access and improve health equity. The project will also provide PA students with training in computational health applications, bridging gaps between clinical education and emerging data-driven methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice medicine, including diagnoses and treatment therapies, under the supervision of a physician. Includes instruction in the basic medical and clinical sciences and specialized preparation in fields such as family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, gynecology, general surgery, psychiatry, and behavioral medicine; the delivery of health care services to homebound patients, rural populations, and underserved populations; and community health services.

abstract: The increasing complexity of urban environments demands innovative approaches to environmental design that integrate dynamic socio-spatial patterns, ecological resilience, and human behavioral data. Traditional design methodologies often rely on static models or simplified simulations, limiting their capacity to address interconnected challenges such as climate adaptability, resource efficiency, and community well-being in real-world contexts. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate multi-scalar interactions between built environments, human activity, and environmental systems using high-performance computing (HPC). Leveraging agent-based modeling, real-time sensor data assimilation, and generative adversarial networks (GANs), the research will analyze how micro-scale design interventions—such as green infrastructure placement or material selection—propagate effects across urban networks over time. The computational workflow will integrate geospatial datasets, climate projections, and anonymized mobility patterns to generate adaptive design scenarios that optimize for carbon neutrality, thermal comfort, and spatial equity. By parallelizing parametric design exploration across HPC clusters, the project aims to overcome computational bottlenecks in processing high-resolution urban models with 10^6+ interacting agents and fine-grained environmental variables. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dynamic spatial analysis, validated against case studies in three climate-vulnerable cities, and a novel metrics framework quantifying design impacts on systemic resilience. This work bridges gaps between architectural practice, computational social science, and urban ecology, offering scalable methods to inform policy and participatory design processes in an era of rapid environmental change. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations and enabling iterative machine learning training cycles that traditional workstations cannot support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design public and private spaces, indoor and outdoor, for leisure, recreational, commercial, and living purposes, and for professional practice as environmental designers and architects. Includes instruction in the design and planning of public and private open spaces and their relationship to buildings and other aspects of the built environment; facilities management; related aspects of interior design and architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern statistical datasets, characterized by high dimensionality, heterogeneous structures, and intricate dependencies, demands advanced computational methods to enable robust inference. This project seeks to develop and implement scalable Bayesian hierarchical models for spatial-temporal data with non-Gaussian response variables, a class of problems where traditional estimation techniques become computationally prohibitive due to high parameter dimensionality and non-conjugate likelihoods. The core challenge lies in efficiently sampling from high-dimensional posterior distributions while maintaining theoretical guarantees on mixing rates and convergence. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) with structured variational approximations, leveraging parallel tempering strategies to escape local posterior modes. The implementation will utilize GPU-accelerated gradient computations for HMC and distributed memory parallelism via MPI to scale Markov chain transitions across nodes. A key innovation involves dynamically partitioning spatial-temporal random effects using graph-based clustering algorithms to optimize load balancing during distributed inference. The computational workflow will be validated on synthetic datasets with known ground truth and applied to a multi-terabyte epidemiological dataset tracking disease incidence across 10,000+ geographic units over a 20-year period, incorporating covariates from disparate sources (satellite imagery, electronic health records). Successful implementation will yield (1) open-source software for large-scale hierarchical modeling, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational-accuracy tradeoffs across architectures, and (3) novel epidemiological insights into spatiotemporal risk factors for disease transmission. The requested high-performance computing resources are critical for testing algorithmic scalability beyond 1,000 nodes and processing raw input data through GPU-optimized preprocessing pipelines. This work directly advances statistical methodology for complex modern datasets while providing a computational blueprint for integrating Bayesian nonparametrics with exascale computing architectures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to optimize multi-modal transportation networks under dynamic operational constraints, addressing critical inefficiencies in resource allocation and routing for mixed freight systems. Current logistical models struggle to adapt to real-time disruptions, such as weather events, traffic variability, and shifting demand, particularly when integrating diverse transportation modes (e.g., autonomous trucks, drones, maritime shipping) and material handling technologies. The computational complexity of modeling these interdependent systems at scale necessitates advanced parallel computing capabilities. We propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and reinforcement learning (RL) to dynamically optimize routing, scheduling, and energy consumption across heterogeneous networks. The agent-based component will simulate individual vehicle and infrastructure behaviors, while RL algorithms will train decision-making policies on historical and synthetic data representing regional freight patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) running large-scale simulations with >10^5 concurrent agents, (2) training deep RL models on high-dimensional spatiotemporal datasets, and (3) conducting Monte Carlo analyses to quantify system resilience under stochastic disruptions. Expected outcomes include a validated optimization toolkit that reduces average freight delay by ≥15% and energy use by ≥10% compared to state-of-the-art solutions, with open-source code and benchmark datasets for the research community. The work directly advances the National Academy of Engineering’s Grand Challenge in urban infrastructure modernization, while providing transferable computational methods for complex logistics systems. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for RL training and high-memory CPU clusters for distributed simulations, resources not available in our current institutional environment.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in transportation and materials moving, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of simulating and optimizing civil infrastructure designs in complex geological environments, a critical challenge in civil drafting and engineering CAD/CADD workflows. Current software tools struggle to efficiently model large-scale infrastructure systems—such as water distribution networks or transportation corridors—while integrating high-resolution geological, hydrological, and seismic data. These limitations hinder the ability to predict system resilience under dynamic stressors like earthquakes or climate-induced soil instability. To overcome this, we propose developing a scalable computational framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multi-physics simulations that couple finite element analysis, geospatial data processing, and automated drafting parameter optimization. The project will leverage parallelized algorithms to distribute tasks across HPC nodes, accelerating iterative design testing and sensitivity analyses. Key computational components include GPU-accelerated rendering for 3D geological mapping, machine learning models to predict material stress thresholds from historical survey data, and parametric scripting to automate CADD blueprint revisions. By integrating these methods, the framework will reduce simulation runtime for large infrastructure projects from weeks to days while improving precision in risk assessment. Outcomes will include open-source CADD workflow modules tailored for academic training and a case study validating the approach on a regional stormwater management system with variable soil composition. This work will advance computational drafting methodologies, support climate-resilient infrastructure design, and provide students with hands-on experience in HPC-aided civil engineering workflows, bridging gaps between traditional drafting techniques and modern computational geotechnics.
cip_title: Civil Drafting and Civil Engineering CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawing and electronic simulations in support of civil engineers, geological engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic civil engineering principles, geological and seismographic mapping, machine drafting, computer-aided drafting (CAD), pipe drafting, survey interpretation, and blueprint reading.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize railroad network operations and safety through advanced simulation and predictive modeling. The increasing complexity of modern railway systems, compounded by demands for higher freight volumes and passenger service efficiency, creates challenges in managing traffic flow, minimizing delays, and mitigating risks associated with hazardous material transport. Current operational models rely on static scheduling and simplified heuristics, which inadequately account for dynamic variables such as weather disruptions, equipment failures, or real-time telecommunication system performance. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate railway networks at unprecedented resolution. Agent-based models will represent individual trains, crew shifts, and signal systems, while graph neural networks will predict congestion propagation and optimize routing decisions under uncertainty. Monte Carlo methods will quantify risks in hazardous material transport scenarios, incorporating stochastic weather and track condition data. The computational workflow will parallelize discrete-event simulations across thousands of rail segments and integrate real-time telemetry from onboard sensors and trackside IoT devices. By harnessing HPC capabilities, we aim to reduce simulation wall-clock time for continent-scale networks from weeks to hours, enabling iterative scenario testing for infrastructure planning and emergency response protocols. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for adaptive scheduling, risk-aware routing algorithms compliant with General Code of Operation rules, and a digital twin prototype for railway system resilience testing. This work will provide transportation agencies and operators with data-driven strategies to improve network throughput by 15–20% while maintaining safety margins, directly supporting the railway industry’s transition toward intelligent transportation systems. The computational framework will be made available as an open-source toolkit to advance research in railway operations optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation of railroads and other aspects of the railway industry, including railroad and railyard service. Includes instruction in railway culture, operating skills, General Code of Operation rules, conductor service, signal systems, switching, transportation of hazardous materials, safety, and railway telecommunications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a computational framework for simulating health education classroom dynamics to optimize pedagogical strategies for diverse student populations. Health teacher education programs often face challenges in preparing educators to address varied learning needs, cultural contexts, and behavioral outcomes in real-world classrooms. Existing training methods rely on observational practicums and hypothetical scenarios, which lack scalability and fail to capture the complex interplay of variables influencing health education efficacy. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model classroom interactions, student engagement patterns, and long-term knowledge retention using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML). The computational approach will integrate anonymized demographic data, learning analytics from virtual health modules, and physiological feedback datasets (e.g., attention metrics from wearable sensors) to create multi-scale simulations of classroom environments. These simulations will test the impact of different teaching methodologies, curriculum structures, and intervention timing on student outcomes. HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space, including individual learner traits, social dynamics, and stochastic behavioral inputs across thousands of parallelized simulations. Expected outcomes include identifying pedagogical strategies that maximize engagement in underrepresented student groups, predicting the efficacy of adaptive lesson plans, and generating synthetic datasets to train health educators in evidence-based decision-making. The resulting framework will provide a novel tool for teacher education programs to complement traditional training, enabling data-driven refinements to health pedagogy. By aligning computational modeling with educational theory, this work aims to enhance the preparedness of health educators to address public health challenges in K-12 and community settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach health education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to optimize dynamic pricing strategies in multi-sided digital platforms under stochastic demand and regulatory constraints. Traditional pricing models struggle to account for real-time interdependencies between heterogeneous user groups (e.g., buyers, sellers, service providers), nonlinear network effects, and evolving compliance requirements in sectors like fintech or decentralized marketplaces. The project will implement a multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture with graph-based reward propagation, simulating platform ecosystems through agent-based models that capture strategic adaptation across 10^5+ nodes. Computational challenges include solving high-dimensional partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) while integrating legal constraint modules derived from automated regulatory text analysis. The proposed HPC implementation will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo tree search with asynchronous gradient updates across GPU clusters, enabling scenario testing at scales exceeding current commercial implementations by three orders of magnitude. Expected outcomes include 1) a benchmark dataset of optimized pricing trajectories under varying regulatory regimes, 2) quantifiable metrics for platform stability-risk tradeoffs in emergent digital economies, and 3) open-source tools for ethical pricing architecture design. This work bridges computational game theory, regulatory technology, and operations research, addressing critical gaps in managing next-generation business platforms where economic incentives, user behavior, and compliance landscapes co-evolve nonlinearly. Resource allocation will support large-scale simulations across diverse market topologies, substantially advancing predictive capabilities for platform governance beyond conventional equilibrium-based approaches.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the application of statistical modeling, data warehousing, data mining, programming, forecasting and operations research techniques to the analysis of problems of business organization and performance. Includes instruction in optimization theory and mathematical techniques, data mining, data warehousing, stochastic and dynamic modeling, operations analysis, and the design and testing of prototype systems and evaluation models.

abstract: The application of advanced computational methods in forensic pathology has the potential to transform the precision and scope of postmortem investigations, yet remains underexplored. This project seeks to address critical gaps in the integration and analysis of complex, multi-modal datasets generated during medical autopsies, including high-resolution imaging, toxicology, genetic data, and crime scene reconstructions. Traditional approaches often struggle with the volume and heterogeneity of these data, limiting the ability to identify subtle pathological patterns or contextualize findings within legal frameworks. To overcome these challenges, we propose a computational pathology platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for cause-of-death determination, injury mechanism analysis, and population-level mortality trends. Key computational methods include deep learning architectures (e.g., 3D convolutional neural networks) for processing whole-body CT scans and histopathology slides, finite element simulations to model traumatic injury dynamics, and natural language processing algorithms to extract actionable insights from autopsy reports and legal documents. These workflows will be integrated into a unified framework, enabling probabilistic linkages between biological findings, circumstantial evidence, and forensic standards. The HPC environment is essential for training large-scale models on anonymized datasets spanning 20,000+ historical cases, running iterative biomechanical simulations, and performing genome-wide association studies to identify mortality-linked biomarkers. Expected outcomes include validated tools for (1) automated detection of occult pathologies in decomposed remains, (2) quantitative assessment of injury causation probabilities for courtroom testimony, and (3) geospatial mortality dashboards to guide public health interventions. By bridging computational innovation with forensic practice, this research aims to enhance the objectivity of postmortem diagnoses, reduce diagnostic discrepancies in contentious cases, and strengthen the scientific foundation of death investigation systems. The proposed platform will be disseminated as an open-source toolkit for medical examiners, fostering equitable access to advanced computational resources in forensic pathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the performance of medical autopsies, the analysis of human remains and crime scenes, and the legal follow-up and responsibilities of public pathologists.

abstract: The emergence and persistence of infectious diseases in livestock populations present complex challenges to veterinary medicine, food security, and agricultural economies. This project addresses the critical need to model host-pathogen-environment interactions in bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC), a multifactorial syndrome responsible for substantial morbidity and economic losses in cattle. Current experimental models struggle to capture the dynamic interplay between viral and bacterial co-infections, host immune heterogeneity, and environmental stressors such as transportation-induced stress. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of pulmonary immune dynamics with population-scale epidemiological simulations. The ABM component will simulate pathogen spread within alveolar microenvironments under varying immune cell recruitment scenarios, informed by single-cell RNA sequencing data from infected bovine lung tissues. Concurrently, network-based epidemiological models will incorporate real-world herd mobility data and climate variables to predict BRDC outbreaks. These components will be coupled via machine learning surrogates to enable iterative hypothesis testing across scales. The project requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the parameter space of 10^6+ agent interactions per simulation, optimize deep learning architectures for data integration, and perform ensemble runs accounting for genomic variability across cattle breeds. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of biomarkers predictive of BRDC progression, validated against longitudinal field data from feedlot cohorts, and (2) a decision-support tool quantifying intervention efficacy under different management practices. By establishing causal links between molecular-scale interactions and herd-level disease patterns, this work will advance precision veterinary approaches for respiratory syndromes while demonstrating how computational immunology can bridge gaps in large-animal clinical research. The developed models will be adaptable to other polymicrobial infections of agricultural significance.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between geopolitical risk, climate-driven supply chain disruptions, and adaptive trade strategies in global manufacturing networks. As international commerce faces unprecedented volatility from compounding crises—including resource scarcity, regulatory fragmentation, and extreme weather events—existing analytical frameworks struggle to capture the multi-scale, nonlinear relationships shaping cross-border operational resilience. The study addresses this gap by developing an agent-based digital twin of multinational production ecosystems, integrating real-time trade policy data, climate projection ensembles, and firm-level behavioral parameters. Computational experiments will simulate decision cascades across 10,000+ synthetic firms operating in contested critical mineral markets, with parallelized Monte Carlo methods quantifying the propagation of regional shocks through multi-tier supplier networks. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks, will identify emergent patterns in reshoring behaviors and export diversification strategies under competing decarbonization and national security constraints. By coupling discrete-event logistics simulations with multi-layered network analysis, the project aims to generate predictive insights into systemic interdependencies between trade policy mechanisms and supply chain reconfiguration pathways. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support toolkit for policymakers and corporate strategists, enabling scenario testing of tariff structures, export controls, and climate adaptation investments. The computational intensity of modeling hyper-connected global production networks—spanning petabyte-scale supplier databases and high-resolution climate impact timelines—necessitates HPC capabilities for distributed memory management and GPU-accelerated optimization algorithms. Results will advance methodological integration of complexity science and international business theory while informing evidence-based responses to polycrisis challenges in 21st-century commerce.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international businesses and/or business operations. Includes instruction in the principles and processes of export sales, trade controls, foreign operations and related problems, monetary issues, international business policy, and applications to doing business in specific countries and markets.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical and electronic systems necessitates advanced diagnostic and predictive maintenance strategies to minimize equipment downtime and repair costs. Current methodologies in electrical/electronics equipment repair often rely on reactive troubleshooting or static maintenance schedules, which are inefficient for dynamic, interconnected systems. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate failure modes, optimize diagnostic protocols, and predict maintenance needs for industrial and consumer electrical equipment. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will model multi-physics interactions within electrical circuits, electromechanical components, and environmental stressors (e.g., thermal cycling, vibration) using finite element analysis (FEA) and time-domain circuit simulations. Machine learning models will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to correlate sensor data with degradation patterns. The computational workflow will integrate parametric sweeps across component tolerances, load conditions, and failure thresholds to establish robust fault-detection algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for equipment health monitoring and a decision-support tool for technicians prioritizing repair tasks. By enabling granular simulation of transient electrical behaviors and wear mechanisms at scale, this work addresses critical gaps in predictive maintenance capabilities for aging infrastructure. The HPC environment is essential to manage the computational burden of parallelized simulations spanning thousands of operational scenarios, which would otherwise be intractable on local hardware. Successful implementation will provide actionable insights for optimizing repair workflows, reducing energy waste from inefficient equipment, and informing curriculum updates in technician training programs. Resource allocation will directly support the generation of open-access simulation templates and benchmarking datasets tailored to common repair challenges in power distribution, motor control, and embedded systems.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, simple gearing, linkages and lubrication of machines and appliances, and the use of testing equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance consumer advocacy through the development of a predictive modeling framework for identifying systemic risks in consumer product ecosystems. The research addresses the challenge of fragmented, heterogeneous data—including consumer complaints, product recalls, social media sentiment, and supply chain metadata—that inhibits timely detection of emerging threats to consumer safety and equity. Current methods for analyzing such risks rely on manual aggregation or siloed statistical tools, which lack the scalability to process dynamic, multimodal datasets in real time. To bridge this gap, we propose an interdisciplinary computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), graph neural networks (GNNs), and agent-based simulations. NLP will extract latent risk signals from unstructured consumer narratives and regulatory documents, while GNNs will map relationships between products, manufacturers, and regional regulatory environments to identify vulnerability cascades. Agent-based models will simulate consumer behavior and market responses under varying policy interventions, enabling proactive advocacy strategies. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training across thousands of graph configurations, and large-scale parameter sweeps for scenario testing—tasks requiring HPC-grade GPU clusters and distributed memory architectures. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source risk-assessment toolkit for consumer protection organizations, real-time dashboards for prioritizing high-impact advocacy campaigns, and evidence-based policy recommendations to mitigate disparities in product safety access across socioeconomic groups. By synthesizing computational social science, data ethics, and consumer law, this work pioneers a novel methodology for equitable resource allocation in advocacy contexts, with potential applications in decentralized consumer watchdog networks and AI-driven regulatory compliance systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on providing end-use advice and representational services to individuals and groups within a variety of settings, and the analytical and research techniques needed to protect consumers from unsafe, unreliable, and/or unhealthy products and services. Includes instruction in consumer advocacy, family management systems, ecological impacts of consumption practices, and analyzing and testing product quality and safety.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) pathogens in veterinary clinical settings pose a critical threat to animal health, food security, and zoonotic disease management. Current limitations in predicting AMR evolution and transmission dynamics stem from the complexity of microbial genomics, host-pathogen interactions, and environmental variables in livestock populations. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model AMR dynamics across scales, from molecular mechanisms to herd-level epidemiological patterns. We propose a multi-modal computational approach integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of resistance-conferring mutations in bacterial proteins with agent-based models (ABMs) simulating pathogen transmission in heterogeneous livestock populations. MD simulations will employ all-atom and coarse-grained methods to predict structural impacts of mutations in key AMR-associated proteins (e.g., beta-lactamases, efflux pumps), while ABMs will incorporate geospatial data, veterinary treatment protocols, and animal movement patterns to map resistance spread. Machine learning models trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic) from clinical veterinary samples will identify biomarkers associated with resistance emergence. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing petabytes of genomic data, running parallelized simulations across parameter spaces, and optimizing predictive algorithms through iterative learning. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for AMR hotspot identification in veterinary populations, mechanistic insights into resistance evolution under treatment pressures, and decision-support tools for targeted antimicrobial stewardship in livestock management. By bridging molecular and population-level analyses, this work aims to directly inform clinical veterinary practices while contributing foundational knowledge to the One Health initiative's efforts against AMR.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Sciences/ Veterinary Clinical Sciences, General
cip_definition: An integrated program of study in one or more of the veterinary medical or clinical sciences or a program undifferentiated as to title.

abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing involves complex physical and chemical processes that require precise control to optimize yield, performance, and cost. A critical challenge lies in modeling multiphysics phenomena—such as thermal stress during rapid thermal processing (RTP), plasma dynamics in etching, and defect propagation in crystalline structures—which are computationally intensive and influence device reliability at scale. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale simulations that bridge atomic-level interactions with continuum-scale manufacturing processes. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) simulating defect formation in silicon wafers under varying process conditions using molecular dynamics (MD) and finite element analysis (FEA), and (2) training machine learning (ML) models to predict optimal process parameters for minimizing defects while maximizing throughput. The computational workflow will integrate open-source tools (LAMMPS, OpenFOAM) with custom Python-based ML pipelines to analyze terabyte-scale datasets of process variables, material properties, and real-time sensor data. HPC resources are essential to handle the parallelized MD simulations of nanoscale interactions (10^6–10^9 atoms) and the iterative optimization of ML hyperparameters across thousands of experimental permutations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting thermal gradient-induced wafer warpage, a framework for coupling ML with multiphysics simulations, and a publicly accessible dataset of process-structure-property relationships. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation semiconductor fabrication protocols, reducing trial-and-error experimentation in industrial settings. By elucidating the interplay between process variables and defect mechanics, this work aims to advance foundational knowledge in semiconductor manufacturing technology while providing students with hands-on training in computational modeling and data-driven materials engineering. The project aligns with national priorities to strengthen domestic semiconductor production capabilities through innovation in advanced manufacturing technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to operate and monitor equipment for the fabrication of semiconductors or microchips from silicon wafers, and to troubleshoot, maintain, and repair the specialized equipment used in this process. Includes instruction in AC and DC circuits, digital fundamentals, solid state devices, manufacturing processes, vacuum principles and technology, industrial electronics, quality assurance, and semiconductor manufacturing technology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Francophone cultural narratives across postcolonial literary and visual media. The research problem centers on understanding how cultural hybridity and identity formation are represented in works produced by Francophone communities in former French colonies (e.g., Algeria, Senegal, Vietnam) and diasporic populations. Existing scholarship often relies on qualitative close readings, which limit the scale at which patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance can be systematically traced. To address this gap, the project employs computational methods to process and analyze a multilingual corpus of novels, poetry, films, and digital media (1900–present), totaling approximately 250,000 texts and 10,000 hours of audiovisual material. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to identify recurring themes, semantic shifts in key terms (e.g., “métissage,” “diaspora”), and intertextual references across genres and regions. Computer vision techniques will supplement this by decoding visual motifs in films and artworks. Graph-based network analysis will map transnational influences among creators and communities. These tasks require HPC resources due to the volume of unstructured data, the complexity of training multilingual transformer models (e.g., CamemBERT, PhoBERT), and the iterative nature of hyperparameter tuning for cross-modal analysis. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated cultural artifacts, quantitative frameworks for tracking narrative evolution, and visualizations of transnational Francophone cultural networks. The project aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in Francophone studies while illuminating understudied dynamics of cultural preservation and innovation in postcolonial contexts. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, it will provide new tools for analyzing how global Francophone communities negotiate identity in response to historical and contemporary pressures.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
