cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of France, other Francophone countries inside and outside Europe, and the French colonial experience and the associated French minorities around the world.

abstract: Cognitive neuroscience faces a critical challenge in understanding how distributed neural networks give rise to complex cognitive processes such as memory consolidation, attentional control, and decision-making. Traditional approaches often struggle to integrate multimodal neuroimaging data (e.g., high-density EEG, fMRI) with behavioral and electrophysiological recordings at scale, limiting insights into dynamic brain-wide interactions. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate large-scale neural network models that bridge spatiotemporal scales. The research will focus on three aims: (1) simulating whole-brain dynamics using biologically constrained models informed by participant-specific structural and functional connectivity data, (2) implementing machine learning pipelines to identify multivariate patterns linking transient neural states to behaviorally measured cognitive performance, and (3) optimizing computational frameworks for real-time analysis of high-density electrophysiology during complex cognitive tasks. The proposed methods integrate dynamic causal modeling, graph theoretical analyses, and hybrid machine learning architectures to process petascale datasets derived from 7T fMRI, intracranial EEG, and eye-tracking experiments. By parallelizing computationally intensive processes—including Monte Carlo simulations of neural population activity and Bayesian inference of network states—HPC resources will enable parameter space explorations intractable on local clusters. Expected outcomes include novel biomarkers of network flexibility during cognitive control tasks, validated models predicting individual differences in executive function, and open-source tools for simulating multiregional neural interactions. This work will advance fundamental understanding of how distributed neural circuits support cognition while providing methodological innovations for analyzing high-dimensional neuroimaging data. The requested computing allocation will directly support these computationally demanding workflows, facilitating transformative insights into the organizational principles of cognitive neural systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the neural mechanisms underlying cognition.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of non-clinical pastoral counseling interactions in diverse crisis contexts, with a focus on optimizing ethical and culturally responsive care frameworks. While pastoral counseling integrates theological principles with psychological support, there is a critical gap in understanding how real-time communication patterns, emotional resonance, and cultural variables interact during counseling sessions—particularly in high-stakes scenarios such as community trauma or existential distress. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the complexity of these multilayered exchanges, necessitating computational tools to model interactional nuances at scale. The research will utilize a corpus of anonymized pastoral counseling transcripts (n≈10,000 sessions) and audio-visual recordings (≈2,000 hours) from interfaith contexts, applying natural language processing (NLP) techniques to identify latent emotional signatures, rhetorical strategies, and narrative coherence markers. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will model temporal dynamics in counselor-consultee dialogues, while transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT variants) will classify theological-ethical decision points in emergent scenarios. Agent-based modeling will simulate counseling interactions under variable cultural and stress parameters to test resilience of proposed care frameworks. Computational demands include training domain-specific language models on theological-counseling lexica and parallel processing of multimodal data streams. Expected outcomes include 1) a taxonomy of high-efficacy communication patterns in crisis pastoral care, 2) an open-source toolkit for ethically auditing cultural bias in counseling language, and 3) evidence-based protocols for integrating adaptive spiritual narratives into counselor training simulations. By bridging computational humanities with pastoral praxis, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for enhancing the quality and cultural agility of non-clinical spiritual care in pluralistic communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and principles of pastoral care and prepares ordained clergy to provide non-clinical pastoral counseling to individuals and groups. Includes instruction in pastoral leadership, counseling psychology; crisis intervention; individual and group procedures; theological and spiritual counseling; pastoral care; and applications to specific types of ministry.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing usability and accessibility in scientific and technical communication (STC) through advanced computational analysis of user engagement patterns. Despite the critical role of effective communication in translating complex technical information, existing tools for evaluating document usability—such as heatmaps, A/B testing, and readability metrics—often fail to account for the dynamic, context-dependent ways diverse audiences interact with multimodal content. To bridge this gap, this research proposes a machine learning-driven framework to model user behavior across web-based technical documentation, integrating real-time interaction data (e.g., scroll patterns, click-through rates, and time-on-page) with semantic analysis of textual and visual content. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets from user testing sessions (n ≈ 10,000 interactions) and train neural networks capable of identifying latent usability barriers in complex documents. The computational workflow includes natural language processing (NLP) for semantic segmentation of technical texts, computer vision algorithms to assess graphical information hierarchies, and reinforcement learning models to simulate adaptive user pathways. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive toolset for preemptive usability optimization, reducing iterative design cycles by 30–40% in pilot testing scenarios. This work will directly benefit technical communicators in high-stakes fields such as healthcare documentation and engineering manuals, where clarity and precision impact safety outcomes. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to establish scalable methodologies for data-driven STC design, advancing the program’s mission to integrate computational rigor with human-centered communication practices. Resource requests emphasize GPU nodes for deep learning workloads and parallel processing to handle heterogeneous data streams from video recordings, eye-tracking logs, and responsive web interfaces.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the communication of technical and scientific knowledge to a variety of audiences through print, video, and digital media; and that prepares individuals to function as technical writers and editors, documentation developers, web designers, and usability specialists. Includes instruction in scientific and technical writing and editing, graphic and information design, web design, audience analysis, document usability and field testing, publications management, and applications to specific technical fields.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research by analyzing patterns in judicial decision-making and statutory interpretation across large-scale, unstructured legal text corpora. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on manual case review or small-sample statistical analysis, limiting the scope of inquiries into systemic biases, doctrinal evolution, or the predictability of legal outcomes. Our research addresses this gap by developing machine learning models capable of processing millions of court opinions, administrative rulings, and legislative documents to identify latent trends in judicial reasoning, particularly in understudied areas of procedural law and regulatory enforcement. The computational approach combines transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of legal arguments, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model citation networks and precedent hierarchies, and agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about institutional interactions within legal systems. Key technical challenges include adapting domain-specific language models to handle the syntactic complexity of legal texts and designing interpretable frameworks for legal scholars without computational backgrounds. Expected outcomes include: (1) open-source tools for automated legal document classification and argumentation mapping, (2) quantitative evidence of temporal shifts in judicial deference to regulatory agencies, and (3) a novel dataset linking case outcomes to contextual socioeconomic variables. By enabling analysis at unprecedented scale, this work aims to establish new methodologies for empirical legal studies while providing actionable insights into the relationship between legal structures and equitable access to justice. The requested HPC resources are critical for training large-language models on specialized legal corpora and running parallelized simulations of legal decision-making processes across diverse jurisdictional scenarios.
cip_definition: Any program in law, legal services, and legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable algorithms for dynamic graph analysis, addressing the computational challenges of modeling large-scale, evolving networks in real time. Modern applications—such as social network dynamics, distributed systems optimization, and biological interaction networks—require efficient methods to process graphs with millions of nodes and edges that change continuously. Traditional sequential algorithms and static graph frameworks struggle with these demands due to memory constraints and computational latency. The proposed research will integrate combinatorial optimization, parallel computing, and distributed systems design to create novel algorithms that decompose dynamic graphs into temporally coherent substructures, enabling incremental updates and asynchronous processing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to evaluate these methods at scale, particularly for simulating dynamic networks with synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., internet topology traces, genomic interaction networks). Key computational tasks include large-scale parallelism using MPI for distributed memory architectures, GPU-accelerated subgraph processing, and adaptive load-balancing strategies to manage irregular workloads. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for dynamic graph analysis optimized for HPC environments, (2) theoretical advances in complexity bounds for dynamic graph decomposition, and (3) empirical validation of scalability on graphs exceeding 10^8 edges. This work bridges mathematical rigor—drawing from spectral graph theory and temporal logic—with computational innovation, offering tools that can transform network analysis in interdisciplinary domains. The requested resources will support iterative testing, hyperparameter tuning, and comparative benchmarking against state-of-the-art frameworks, ensuring robustness and practical utility. By addressing the gap between mathematical models and computational feasibility, this project aims to establish a foundation for real-time, large-scale network analytics in both academic and industrial contexts.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and computer science or a specialization which draws from mathematics and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Burmese language and literature, addressing critical gaps in digital scholarship and linguistic analysis. While Burmese has a rich literary tradition and complex morphological structures, computational tools for its study remain underdeveloped compared to those for Indo-European languages. Current challenges include the lack of large-scale digitized corpora, limited automated parsing for classical and modern texts, and insufficient infrastructure to analyze linguistic evolution across historical periods. This project proposes a multi-phase computational approach to address these gaps. First, we will develop and optimize optical character recognition (OCR) models for digitizing Burmese palm-leaf manuscripts and print materials, utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on diverse orthographic styles. Second, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models, to automate morphological segmentation, syntactic annotation, and semantic analysis of both literary and non-literary Burmese texts. Third, we will conduct diachronic analyses of lexical and grammatical shifts using distributed word embeddings and probabilistic topic modeling, correlating linguistic changes with sociocultural developments. The computational demands of training custom models on heterogeneous datasets—spanning 12th-century Pagan-era inscriptions to modern social media texts—require scalable storage, parallel processing, and GPU acceleration. Outcomes will include an open-access digital corpus of Burmese texts, computational workflows tailored to Tibeto-Burman languages, and interdisciplinary insights into language preservation, literary genre evolution, and dialect variation. By integrating HPC capabilities with humanities-driven research questions, this project aims to establish a foundation for data-intensive Burmese studies while contributing methodological innovations to computational linguistics. The resources requested will directly support text preprocessing, model training, and large-scale simulations that are infeasible on local infrastructure, ensuring reproducibility and enabling future collaborations with regional scholars.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Burmese language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Occupational safety and health (OSH) professionals face growing challenges in predicting and mitigating workplace hazards as industrial environments grow more complex. Current risk assessment methods often rely on static datasets or simplified models, limiting their ability to address dynamic interactions between equipment, environmental factors, and human behavior. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate workplace hazard scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable real-time analysis of multifactorial risks. The research focuses on modeling exposure to airborne contaminants, machinery-related injuries, and ergonomic stressors in manufacturing and construction settings. Computational methods will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for contaminant dispersion, finite element analysis (FEA) for equipment failure prediction, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate worker movement and decision-making under safety-critical conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to optimize sensor placement for hazard detection systems using synthetic training data generated from these simulations. The scale of these interdependent models necessitates HPC infrastructure to manage parallelized simulations across diverse spatial and temporal resolutions, with anticipated workloads requiring 50,000+ core-hours monthly. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for proactive hazard identification, optimized emergency response protocols, and data-driven recommendations for safety engineering controls. By bridging gaps between theoretical safety standards and real-world operational variability, this work aims to reduce workplace accidents through adaptive, scenario-based risk mitigation strategies. The computational framework will also serve as an educational resource for OSH technology students, providing case studies and interactive modules to enhance training in advanced risk assessment techniques. Successful implementation will support industry compliance with evolving regulatory requirements while advancing the integration of computational modeling into occupational safety practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining job-related health and safety standards. Includes instruction in safety engineering principles, inspection and monitoring procedures, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, applications to specific work environments, and report preparation.

abstract: Understanding population dynamics in the context of rapid environmental and societal change requires advanced computational tools to model complex interactions between individual behaviors and macro-level demographic trends. This project seeks to investigate how environmental stressors, such as extreme weather events and resource scarcity, interact with social networks and policy interventions to shape migration patterns and population redistribution. Traditional demographic models often struggle to capture the nonlinear feedback loops and heterogeneous decision-making processes that drive these phenomena. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM) that simulates individual and household-level migration decisions under varying environmental and policy scenarios. The ABM will integrate spatially explicit environmental data, longitudinal demographic surveys, and policy records to parameterize agents’ adaptive behaviors. Given the scale of simulation—encompassing millions of agents over multi-decadal timeframes—high-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for parallelizing computational workloads, optimizing parameter space exploration, and enabling real-time visualization of emergent population patterns. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into how targeted policy measures could mitigate displacement risks in climate-vulnerable regions, as well as methodological advances in coupling demographic theory with computational social science frameworks. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance the granularity and predictive accuracy of demographic models, providing a replicable toolkit for studying complex socio-environmental systems. The results will contribute to interdisciplinary dialogues on sustainable development while addressing a critical gap in demography’s capacity to inform adaptive governance in an era of global change.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in demography, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Palliative care nursing requires the integration of complex, multidimensional data—including patient-reported outcomes, clinical metrics, psychosocial factors, and treatment responses—to optimize comfort and quality of life for patients with life-limiting illnesses. Current approaches to care planning often rely on generalized guidelines that may not account for dynamic interactions between pain management, symptom trajectories, and individual patient contexts. This project seeks to address this gap by developing predictive computational models to personalize palliative care strategies, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in patient responses to palliative interventions, particularly in pain management and psychosocial support, to enable real-time, data-driven clinical decision-making. The computational approach integrates electronic health records, longitudinal symptom assessments, pharmacogenomic data, and qualitative patient narratives using machine learning (ML) techniques, including ensemble models and natural language processing (NLP). HPC resources will enable the training of deep learning architectures to model temporal changes in symptom severity and treatment efficacy, while agent-based simulations will explore the systemic impacts of tailored care protocols under diverse demographic and clinical scenarios. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers predictive of opioid responsiveness, dynamic risk stratification tools for proactive grief and symptom management, and a framework for simulating patient-specific care pathways. By elucidating the interplay between biological, psychological, and social determinants of palliative outcomes, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in palliative nursing, reduce trial-and-error in pain management, and improve resource allocation in end-of-life care. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source resources for the nursing research community, fostering collaboration between clinical expertise and data science in addressing complex care challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide a combination of active and compassionate therapies intended to comfort and support patients and their families who are living with life-threatening illness. Includes instruction in pathophysiology, palliative care processes, pain management, pharmacology, loss, grief, death, and bereavement.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize medication synchronization programs in community pharmacy settings through advanced computational modeling, addressing gaps in operational efficiency and patient adherence. Medication synchronization—aligning multiple prescription refills to a single pickup date—reduces administrative burden and improves adherence but faces challenges in scalability due to dynamic variables such as patient-specific dosing schedules, insurance constraints, and pharmacy workflow bottlenecks. Current manual or rule-based scheduling systems are error-prone and fail to adapt to real-time disruptions, leading to suboptimal outcomes. We propose a machine learning (ML) framework integrated with discrete-event simulation (DES) to model and predict optimal synchronization schedules while minimizing operational costs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train ML models on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., electronic health records, prescription claim logs, and time-motion studies) and simulate thousands of scheduling scenarios under variable constraints. The DES component will incorporate stochastic elements such as staffing fluctuations, patient no-show rates, and supply chain delays, requiring parallelized computation to evaluate scenario trade-offs. Anticipated outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that recommends personalized synchronization timelines and resource allocation strategies for pharmacy technicians, who manage prescription logistics. This tool will be tested against retrospective data from 15 community pharmacies, with success metrics including a 20% reduction in workflow inefficiencies and a 15% improvement in patient adherence rates over six months. By bridging computational optimization and pharmacy operations, this research advances a niche area within health sciences that intersects healthcare informatics, logistics, and patient-centered care. The resulting framework will provide a scalable model for integrating AI-driven tools into technician workflows, enhancing their role in chronic disease management without expanding traditional pharmaceutical science domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pharmacists, to prepare medications, provide medications and related assistance to patients, and manage pharmacy clinical and business operations. Includes instruction in medical and pharmaceutical terminology, principles of pharmacology and pharmaceutics, drug identification, pharmacy laboratory procedures, prescription interpretation, patient communication and education, safety procedures, record-keeping, measurement and testing techniques, pharmacy business operations, prescription preparation, logistics and dispensing operations, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of regional Italian dialect variation and its historical-literary intersections. While Italian dialects and regional linguistic practices have been studied extensively through traditional philological methods, large-scale quantitative analyses remain underdeveloped due to the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous textual and spoken corpora spanning diverse time periods and geographic regions. The research problem centers on mapping dialectal evolution in relation to sociohistorical shifts (e.g., post-unification standardization efforts) and identifying latent stylistic patterns in regional literature that resist mainstream Tuscan-based Italian norms. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and non-standard texts, including tokenization models adapted for orthographic variation, graph-based algorithms for semantic network analysis, and transformer-based architectures fine-tuned on dialect-specific corpora. These methods will be applied to a curated multilingual dataset comprising 19th–21st-century literature, transcribed oral histories, and digitized archival materials from Lombardy, Sicily, and Veneto. Parallelized workflows will enable comparative sentiment analysis, lexical diffusion modeling, and the identification of morphosyntactic features that correlate with extralinguistic factors such as urbanization rates and educational policy changes. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-access computational toolkit for Italian dialect studies, high-resolution visualizations of dialect convergence/divergence patterns, and statistically grounded insights into how regional identity is encoded in linguistic variation. By enabling the processing of previously intractable datasets, this project aims to bridge gaps between computational linguistics and traditional philological scholarship while informing contemporary efforts to preserve endangered dialects. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, including training domain-specific language models and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to validate diachronic linguistic hypotheses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Italian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in resource allocation for small businesses operating in highly dynamic, hyperlocal markets. While small businesses are critical to economic resilience, many lack the computational capacity to model complex, real-time interactions between shifting consumer preferences, supply chain volatility, and localized regulatory constraints. Traditional optimization tools often fail to account for these multidimensional, nonlinear relationships, particularly in niche sectors such as microbatch manufacturing or adaptive reuse retail. This project proposes the development of a granular simulation framework using agent-based modeling (ABM) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to map decision cascades across three interdependent layers: microeconomic actor behavior, geospatial resource flows, and regulatory boundary conditions. The HPC environment will enable simultaneous execution of thousands of scenario variants, incorporating stochastic demand shocks, supplier reliability thresholds, and jurisdictional policy gradients derived from unstructured municipal data. Validation will focus on case studies from underrepresented small business ecosystems, including peri-urban agricultural cooperatives and artisan-led circular economy networks. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system capable of identifying latent operational vulnerabilities and generating adaptive resource distribution strategies at subquarterly time horizons. By integrating computational social science methods with business operational analytics, this work aims to advance predictive capabilities for small-scale enterprises while contributing methodological innovations in modeling path-dependent market behaviors. The resulting toolkit could reduce trial-and-error resource expenditure by 18-22% in pilot sectors, as estimated through posterior predictive checks against historical business failure modes. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between complexity science and applied business strategy, offering scalable computational solutions for enterprises typically excluded from advanced analytics ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage independent small businesses. Includes instruction in business administration; enterprise planning and entrepreneurship; start-up; small business operations and problems; personnel supervision; capitalization and investment; taxation; business law and regulations; e-commerce; home business operations; and applications to specific sectors, products, and services.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between economic policy shifts and the evolution of linguistic narratives in multilingual trade regions, with a focus on 20th-century Southeast Asia. By integrating computational text analysis of regional literary corpora with econometric modeling, the research aims to quantify how macroeconomic events—such as trade liberalization, currency crises, and labor migration policies—are reflected in the thematic and semantic patterns of vernacular literature across Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore. The central hypothesis posits that localized literary production acts as both a cultural response to and a driver of economic behavioral changes in communities undergoing rapid globalization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multilingual textual datasets spanning 15,000+ literary works (novels, short stories, and poetry) in Bahasa Indonesia, Malay, and Chinese dialects, alongside parallel economic indicators from colonial and post-independence eras. Natural language processing pipelines will be developed to track lexical shifts related to economic concepts (e.g., "debt," "labor," "value") across temporal and geopolitical boundaries, while Bayesian hierarchical models will correlate these linguistic trajectories with macroeconomic variables. Custom transformer-based architectures will be trained to detect subtle narrative strategies that mediate between global economic forces and local cultural identities. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel computational framework for cross-disciplinary analysis of economic-literary systems, 2) empirically grounded insights into how vernacular literature shapes economic decision-making in multilingual contexts, and 3) open-access multilingual embeddings optimized for low-resource languages in socioeconomic contexts. The work bridges computational linguistics, economic anthropology, and postcolonial studies, offering policymakers and cultural institutions tools to analyze narrative impacts on economic resilience and identity formation in globalizing societies.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in comparative economic systems, econometrics, economic theory, money and banking systems, international economics, international trade, linguistics, philology, and translation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize texture-modified meal planning for patients with dysphagia, a swallowing disorder affecting over 500 million individuals globally. Current dietitian-led approaches rely on manual adjustments to food consistency using standardized scales (e.g., IDDSI), but these methods often fail to account for dynamic interactions between nutritional content, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability during preparation. We propose an HPC-driven approach to model multi-parameter relationships between ingredient composition, processing techniques (e.g., mechanical softening, thickening agents), and post-preparation food behavior. A hybrid pipeline will integrate molecular dynamics simulations of hydrocolloid interactions, finite element analysis of mechanical stress distribution in heterogeneous food matrices, and machine learning models trained on clinical outcomes data from 15,000+ patient records. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated parallel processing to iteratively optimize meal plans against conflicting constraints: maximizing nutrient retention, ensuring safe swallowing rheology, maintaining palatability, and minimizing preparation time. Validation will involve 3D-printed food analogs with embedded sensors to quantify real-world deformation forces against simulated predictions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that reduces dietitians’ trial-and-error workload by 40–60% while improving patient adherence through personalized texture-nutrient profiles. This work bridges gaps between food rheology, clinical nutrition, and computational modeling, addressing a critical need in under-resourced healthcare settings where dysphagia management is frequently deprioritized. The resulting framework will establish scalable methodologies for adaptive meal optimization applicable to other chronic conditions requiring specialized diets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing multiphase reactive transport processes within advanced chemical reactors, a problem central to improving efficiency in chemical manufacturing and energy conversion systems. Current models struggle to resolve the coupled interactions between turbulent fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and heterogeneous chemical kinetics at industrially relevant scales, limiting predictive accuracy for reactor design. This project will develop a high-fidelity computational framework combining large-eddy simulation (LES) for turbulence modeling, discrete element methods (DEM) for granular catalyst dynamics, and adaptive chemical kinetic mechanisms. The integration of these components requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to handle the extreme resolution demands of three-dimensional reactor geometries, sub-millisecond temporal scales of reaction fronts, and parameter sensitivity analyses across thousands of parallel simulations. Our approach leverages GPU-accelerated solvers and machine learning-based surrogate models to reduce computational costs while maintaining physical fidelity. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for optimizing gas-solid fluidized bed reactors and catalytic membrane systems, with direct applications in sustainable chemical synthesis and carbon capture technologies. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented spatial resolution (>10^8 grid cells) and parallel scaling for transient simulations spanning seconds of real reactor operation—an order-of-magnitude improvement over current capabilities. By bridging molecular-scale kinetic data with macro-scale transport phenomena, this work will provide fundamental insights into rate-limiting processes under non-ideal flow conditions, directly supporting the development of intensified reactor designs with reduced energy footprints. The requested HPC allocation is essential for handling the petabyte-scale datasets generated during multi-parametric optimization studies and for training neural networks on high-dimensional reaction space representations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the spatial and temporal dynamics of infectious disease transmission in urban environments using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Urban centers, characterized by high population density and mobility, present complex transmission networks that challenge traditional epidemiological models. Current models often oversimplify human behavior, environmental interactions, and healthcare access disparities, limiting their utility for targeted public health interventions. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with machine learning to simulate disease spread across heterogeneous urban populations. The model will incorporate multi-source data, including anonymized electronic health records, geolocated mobility patterns, and socio-demographic datasets, to parameterize individual and community-level interactions. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of simulating millions of agents across dynamic networks, parallelize scenario testing for varying public health strategies (e.g., vaccination campaigns, quarantine protocols), and train deep learning models to identify latent risk factors from high-dimensional data. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable, open-source ABM platform optimized for urban public health applications, (2) evidence-based projections of intervention efficacy under diverse socio-economic conditions, and (3) identification of neighborhood-specific vulnerability indicators linked to healthcare inequities. This work will directly inform municipal health agencies in optimizing resource allocation during outbreaks and provide a methodological foundation for future studies on health disparities in complex urban systems. The requested computing resources will enable iterative model calibration using historical outbreak data and real-time scenario analyses, which are computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure. By bridging computational innovation and public health practice, this project aims to advance equitable outbreak response strategies in high-risk urban settings.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public health, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance strategies for aging energy infrastructure, including power grids, renewable energy systems, and distributed generation networks. Current maintenance protocols in energy systems rely heavily on reactive or schedule-based approaches, leading to unplanned downtime, inefficient resource allocation, and accelerated equipment degradation. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven methodology leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex failure mechanisms, simulate multi-physics interactions, and predict maintenance needs in dynamic operational environments. The computational workflow will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and corrosion effects, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to analyze interdependencies in networked energy systems. Training datasets will combine historical maintenance records, real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled infrastructure, and synthetically generated failure scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations across heterogeneous system components while maintaining temporal resolution necessary for transient analysis. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated digital twin platform capable of identifying high-risk components in energy networks, (2) adaptive maintenance scheduling algorithms that reduce downtime by 15–30% compared to conventional methods, and (3) open-source tools for probabilistic remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. By enabling data-driven decision-making at scale, this research aims to extend the operational lifespan of critical energy assets while reducing costs associated with emergency repairs. The computational framework will be tested against operational data from three regional power utilities and two offshore wind farms, with results directly informing revised maintenance standards in the IEEE 1547 series for distributed energy resource interoperability.
cip_title: Energy Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize interoperability and security of proprietary medical software systems used in ambulatory care settings, addressing critical gaps in real-time data integration between heterogeneous devices and electronic health records (EHRs). Despite advances in medical software, fragmented communication protocols and legacy system dependencies persist, leading to workflow inefficiencies, data integrity risks, and delayed clinical decision-making. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to model network architectures and data flow patterns across simulated multi-vendor clinical environments, including IoT-enabled diagnostic devices, cloud-based EHR platforms, and edge computing nodes. Parallelized agent-based simulations will evaluate latency, error propagation, and vulnerability surfaces under varying workloads, while machine learning pipelines will identify optimal protocol translation strategies for non-standardized medical data streams. A key innovation involves adapting blockchain-inspired cryptographic methods to audit cross-platform data transactions without compromising legacy system functionality. The computational workflow will integrate containerized microservices to mirror real-world clinic IT ecosystems, enabling stress-testing of proposed interoperability solutions at scale. Outcomes will yield validated algorithms for adaptive middleware deployment, prioritized cybersecurity patches for high-risk medical office software, and a benchmark dataset of simulated clinical data exchange scenarios. This work directly supports safer implementation of emerging technologies in outpatient care while maintaining compliance with evolving healthcare data standards. By addressing computational bottlenecks in cross-system validation, the project aims to reduce preventable errors linked to software interoperability failures, ultimately enhancing the reliability of clinical workflows dependent on specialized health information technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply computer programming, troubleshooting, and information technology skills to the installation, maintenance, and upgrade of standard, customized, or proprietary medical software and associated hardware. Includes instruction in computer programming, systems analysis, networking, telecommunications, medical records and informatics software applications, information technology, systems administration, computer security, and applicable regulations and certifications or licenses.

abstract: The increasing demand for advanced materials with tailored mechanical and thermal properties necessitates a deeper understanding of microstructural evolution under extreme conditions. Current experimental methods face challenges in resolving atomic-scale dynamics during rapid phase transformations or high-strain deformation, limiting predictive capabilities for material design. This project seeks to address this gap by employing large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and phase-field simulations to model defect propagation, grain boundary interactions, and thermal transport in polycrystalline alloys under thermomechanical stress. The study focuses on titanium-aluminum-vanadium (Ti-6Al-4V) systems, widely used in aerospace applications, where localized stress concentrations and thermal gradients often lead to premature failure. Simulations will integrate quantum-mechanically informed interatomic potentials to enhance accuracy in capturing dislocation dynamics and void nucleation. A parallel computational framework will be implemented to handle systems exceeding 10 million atoms, with adaptive meshing techniques applied to phase-field models for tracking interface evolution across multiple timescales. Machine learning tools will be applied to analyze simulation datasets, identifying key descriptors for fracture toughness and thermal stability. The requested high-performance computing resources are critical for achieving the necessary spatial and temporal resolution, as parameter sweeps across temperature, strain rate, and compositional variables require petabytes of distributed storage and sustained petaflop-scale computation. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking processing conditions to microstructural resilience, validated against synchrotron X-ray diffraction data from collaborating institutions. This work will provide fundamental insights into deformation mechanisms of multiphase alloys, directly informing the design of next-generation lightweight materials for high-temperature applications. The computational workflows developed will be shared as open-source tools to accelerate community-wide efforts in materials informatics, bridging the gap between atomistic simulations and industrial-scale component optimization.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of mathematical and scientific principles to the analysis and evaluation of the characteristics and behavior of solids, including internal structure, chemical properties, transport and energy flow properties, thermodynamics of solids, stress and failure factors, chemical transformation states and processes, compound materials, and research on industrial applications of specific materials.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern construction practices by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize material performance, structural resilience, and energy efficiency in building systems. Current methods for evaluating construction materials and designs often rely on physical prototyping or simplified computational models, which can overlook complex interactions between variables such as thermal stress, load distribution, and environmental exposure. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a multi-physics simulation framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model building systems under diverse real-world conditions. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of composite materials (e.g., insulated concrete forms, cross-laminated timber) and modular construction assemblies, simulating scenarios like seismic activity, extreme weather, and long-term wear. Additionally, generative design algorithms will iteratively explore geometries and material configurations to minimize waste while meeting safety codes. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce simulation times from weeks to days, allowing rapid iteration of sustainable designs. Anticipated outcomes include validated models for predicting material lifespan under climate stressors, data-driven guidelines for retrofitting aging structures, and open-source tools to help small-scale contractors adopt simulation-driven design. This work aligns with industry demands for decarbonization and disaster-resilient infrastructure, offering computational strategies to reduce construction costs and environmental impacts. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations, ML training on terabyte-scale sensor datasets from smart buildings, and high-fidelity visualization of structural failures. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with vocational training programs to bridge gaps between computational research and hands-on construction education.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the building, inspecting, and maintaining of structures and related properties. May include instruction in masonry, carpentry, electrical and power transmission installation, building/construction finishing, management, inspection and other construction-related applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary investigation into the dynamics of cultural and intellectual exchange across premodern Afro-Eurasian societies. The research problem centers on analyzing fragmented, multilingual textual and material records (e.g., trade logs, religious manuscripts, artistic motifs) to trace the diffusion of ideas, technologies, and social practices between 500–1500 CE. Existing scholarship lacks systematic computational frameworks to integrate these heterogeneous datasets, which span archaeology, linguistics, and historiography. The project will develop scalable natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to parse and align digitized texts in Arabic, Sanskrit, and classical Chinese, combined with network analysis models to map connectivity patterns across trade routes and urban hubs. Computational challenges include handling non-Latin scripts, fragmentary or damaged source materials, and spatial-temporal data normalization across disparate scholarly corpora. The HPC environment is critical for training transformer-based models on low-resource historical languages, running agent-based simulations of cultural transmission, and visualizing multilayer networks at continental scales. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access digital repository of annotated, cross-referenced primary sources; (2) quantitative metrics for assessing the role of environmental factors versus institutional actors in shaping intercultural exchange; and (3) methodological frameworks for reconciling humanistic interpretations with computational pattern detection. By bridging computational social science and digital humanities approaches, this work aims to redefine narratives about globalization’s antecedents while demonstrating how HPC can catalyze resource-intensive, multidisciplinary inquiry in liberal arts contexts. The results will inform curriculum development in global history and computational humanities programs, emphasizing data-driven perspectives on cultural complexity.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences/ Liberal Studies
cip_definition: A program that is a structured combination of the arts, biological and physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities, emphasizing breadth of study. Includes instruction in independently designed, individualized, or regular programs.

abstract: Dental material degradation and its long-term biocompatibility remain poorly understood despite widespread clinical use. Current materials, including ceramics, polymers, and resin-based composites, exhibit variable mechanical fatigue and chemical leaching behaviors under dynamic oral conditions, potentially contributing to restoration failure, localized inflammation, or systemic biomaterial-related sequelae. This project proposes a multi-scale computational framework to model the physicochemical interactions between dental materials and the oral microenvironment, emphasizing the synergistic effects of mechanical stress, enzymatic activity, and microbial biofilm dynamics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable molecular dynamics simulations to characterize interfacial bonding stability at the nanoscale, finite element analysis to predict stress distribution in complex prosthetic geometries, and agent-based modeling of biofilm-induced corrosion. Machine learning algorithms will integrate empirical material property datasets with simulated degradation pathways to identify high-risk failure modalities. The computational workflow will be validated against in vitro tribocorrosion experiments and clinical micro-CT scans of retrieved restorations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking material microstructure to clinical failure mechanisms, (2) a quantitative biocompatibility risk index for novel material formulations, and (3) optimized design parameters for additive-manufactured prostheses with enhanced fatigue resistance. By bridging molecular-scale interactions to macroscopic clinical outcomes, this work aims to establish a computational paradigm for accelerating the development of next-generation dental materials while reducing reliance on iterative physical prototyping. The requested HPC allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated molecular simulations (>200,000 core-hours) and large-scale finite element meshes (>50 million elements) required to resolve time-dependent material behavior across biologically relevant timescales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the historical evolution of medical ontologies—structured frameworks of medical knowledge—across Euro-American contexts from the 18th to the mid-20th century. While existing scholarship has mapped broad shifts in medical paradigms (e.g., humoral to germ theory), granular computational analysis of how localized clinical practices, terminologies, and diagnostic logic coalesced into standardized systems remains underexplored. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of knowledge fragmentation, synthesis, and epistemic conflict within digitized corpora of medical textbooks, practitioner journals, and institutional case records. Key computational challenges include processing multilingual, non-standardized historical texts with high lexical variability, temporal drift in terminology, and regionally divergent classifications of disease and treatment. The project will employ transformer-based language models fine-tuned on historical medical corpora to trace semantic networks, augmented by graph analytics to model ontology convergence/divergence across time and geography. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific embeddings on ~50TB of heterogeneous textual data (1700-1950), running parallelized topic modeling at scale, and simulating knowledge diffusion pathways via agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include 1) a geotemporal atlas of medical ontology development, 2) quantitative metrics for historical epistemic stability/rupture in clinical decision-making frameworks, and 3) open-access tools for diachronic analysis of medical corpora. By computationally reconstructing how communities negotiated medical "facts," this work aims to provide novel insights into present-day challenges in knowledge translation and standardization, bridging historical scholarship with contemporary debates about evidence hierarchies in rapidly evolving biomedical landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution and socio-economic context of medical theories, education, practices, and technologies; and on the history of diseases, therapeutics, patients, and healers. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of the historiography of medicine; the history of science, medicine, and technology; and of research methods in the history of medicine.

abstract: Early childhood education (ECE) faces critical challenges in understanding how dynamic, multimodal classroom interactions influence developmental and learning outcomes for young children. Current observational and assessment methods struggle to capture the complexity of these interactions at scale, particularly across diverse linguistic, cultural, and socioeconomic contexts. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets of early childhood classrooms (video, audio, and sensor data) to model teacher-student interactions and their relationship to learning trajectories. The research will employ machine learning techniques, including computer vision for gesture and activity recognition, natural language processing for dialogue analysis, and network modeling to map social-emotional dynamics within classrooms. These computational methods will be applied to an existing corpus of 5,000+ hours of classroom recordings from a multi-state ECE study, supplemented by real-time data from wearable sensors pilot-tested in three partner preschools. The scale and resolution of this data—requiring parallel processing of high-dimensional video streams, synchronization of heterogeneous data sources, and iterative model training—necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory systems. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of interaction patterns predictive of language acquisition and executive function development, (2) a framework for assessing equitable teaching practices across demographic subgroups, and (3) open-source tools to help educators reflect on interactional biases. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of ECE pedagogy, this work will directly inform teacher training programs and the design of adaptive curricula responsive to neurodiverse and multilingual learners. The requested computing resources are essential for processing datasets of this magnitude while maintaining the temporal and spatial fidelity required for meaningful educational insights.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students ranging in age from infancy through eight years (grade three), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize traffic flow and infrastructure resilience in urban transportation networks under dynamic demand and climate stressors. Current transportation models often lack the granularity to capture real-time interactions between multimodal networks, population growth patterns, and extreme weather events, leading to suboptimal infrastructure investments and operational strategies. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating agent-based traffic modeling, pavement degradation algorithms, and machine learning-driven demand forecasting. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process city-scale networks with 1+ million vehicle agents, simulate decade-long pavement deterioration under probabilistic climate scenarios, and solve mixed-integer optimization problems for adaptive traffic signal control. Key innovations include parallelized vehicle routing algorithms using GPU acceleration, coupled hydrodynamic models to assess flood-induced network disruptions, and reinforcement learning agents trained on synthetic data representing diverse urban morphologies. The project will validate results against real-world sensor data from three metropolitan regions while generating synthetic scenarios for understudied cities. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source computational toolkit for transportation system vulnerability assessment, (2) quantitative guidelines for climate-adaptive infrastructure design, and (3) predictive models to prioritize congestion mitigation investments. By enabling simultaneous analysis of social-behavioral patterns, material performance, and environmental pressures at unprecedented scales, this work will advance decision-support capabilities for transportation agencies. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive network graphs, executing ensemble simulations across parameter spaces, and reducing wall-clock time for optimization cycles from weeks to days.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems for the physical movement of people, materials and information, including general network design and planning, facilities planning, site evaluation, transportation management systems, needs projections and analysis, and analysis of costs.

abstract: Respiratory care therapies are critical for managing chronic and acute pulmonary diseases, yet optimizing treatment protocols remains a challenge due to the complex interplay of biomechanical, physiological, and patient-specific factors. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for individual variations in lung mechanics, disease progression, or response to interventions such as mechanical ventilation or aerosolized drug delivery. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing patient-specific computational models of respiratory system dynamics to predict optimal therapeutic strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate multi-scale physiological processes, including airflow dynamics, gas exchange, and parenchymal stress-strain relationships under varying therapeutic conditions. Using finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will model the respiratory tract at high resolution, integrating clinical data from pulmonary function tests, imaging, and real-time monitoring to personalize parameters. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to analyze heterogeneous datasets and identify patterns linking therapeutic variables to clinical outcomes. The computational workflows will be validated against retrospective patient data and tested prospectively in collaboration with clinical partners. This research aims to generate predictive tools that enable clinicians to tailor ventilation settings, drug delivery modes, and rehabilitation protocols to individual patients, reducing trial-and-error approaches and minimizing risks of ventilator-induced lung injury or suboptimal therapy. Outcomes will include open-source computational frameworks for respiratory care optimization, data-driven guidelines for personalized treatment, and a deeper understanding of mechano-biological interactions in diseased lungs. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges computational biomedicine and clinical practice, offering transformative potential for advancing precision respiratory care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize data-driven decision-making models for educational administrators managing complex, multi-institutional systems. A critical challenge in educational leadership is the equitable and efficient allocation of finite resources—such as staffing, funding, and facility access—across diverse school districts with competing priorities. Traditional analytical tools often fail to account for dynamic variables, including fluctuating enrollment, community needs, and policy shifts, leading to suboptimal or inequitable outcomes. To address this gap, the research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning techniques to simulate district-wide administrative scenarios, incorporating real-world data on student demographics, staff retention, budget cycles, and infrastructure capacity. These computational models will enable granular analysis of how different allocation strategies propagate through interconnected systems, predicting outcomes such as academic performance disparities, resource saturation, and operational inefficiencies. By parallelizing simulations across HPC clusters, the project will iteratively test thousands of allocation permutations, identifying high-impact intervention points while accounting for stochastic variables like economic volatility or demographic changes. The resulting framework will provide administrators with evidence-based strategies to balance equity, sustainability, and academic outcomes in resource distribution. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for scenario planning, a repository of optimized allocation templates adaptable to varying district contexts, and policy recommendations to mitigate systemic biases in resource access. This work directly advances the capacity of educational leaders to enact data-informed governance, promoting more equitable and resilient educational systems at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and techniques of administering a wide variety of schools and other educational organizations and facilities, supervising educational personnel at the school or staff level, and that may prepare individuals as general administrators and supervisors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing complexity of regulatory compliance frameworks across multinational jurisdictions, a challenge exacerbated by the rapid evolution of laws, conflicting international standards, and the need for real-time risk assessment in organizational decision-making. Traditional legal research methods struggle to dynamically model the cascading effects of regulatory changes or predict compliance risks in interconnected global systems. The research will develop a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling to analyze multilingual legal texts, map regulatory interdependencies, and simulate compliance scenarios under variable geopolitical and operational conditions. By training machine learning models on curated datasets of legislation, case law, and enforcement actions from 50+ jurisdictions, the project aims to identify latent patterns in regulatory divergence and convergence, particularly in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence governance, cross-border data privacy, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelism for three core tasks: (1) semantic clustering of regulatory requirements across jurisdictions using transformer-based architectures, (2) dynamic network visualization of compliance obligation conflicts, and (3) stochastic simulations of regulatory enforcement outcomes based on multi-agent interactions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predictive compliance analytics, validated through case studies with partner organizations in the financial and healthcare sectors. The computational approach advances methodological innovation at the intersection of legal informatics and complex systems theory, offering a paradigm shift from reactive to proactive compliance strategies. By quantifying previously qualitative aspects of regulatory interpretation, this work will provide organizations with evidence-based frameworks to prioritize compliance investments and navigate multijurisdictional legal uncertainties.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in compliance, ethics, internal monitoring, regulatory affairs, and related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in analyzing and modeling complex dance movement patterns, with a focus on advancing interdisciplinary methodologies in dance research. While dance is inherently embodied and ephemeral, emerging technologies now enable the capture and quantification of movement at unprecedented resolution. However, processing large-scale motion capture datasets—often comprising terabytes of multimodal data from wearable sensors, inertial measurement units, and optical systems—requires scalable computational infrastructure. The research problem centers on decoding the relationship between biomechanical efficiency and aesthetic intent in improvised contemporary dance, a domain lacking systematic computational frameworks. Current methods for segmenting and classifying movement sequences rely on simplified kinematic models, failing to capture the high-dimensional interplay of physiological, cultural, and creative factors that define dance practice. To address this, we propose a parallelized computational pipeline integrating musculoskeletal simulations, deep learning-based gesture recognition, and network analysis of improvisational logic. HPC resources will enable 1) biomechanical optimization of movement sequences using OpenSim-based simulations at scale, 2) training of transformer models on annotated video datasets to identify choreographic motifs across diverse cultural dance forms, and 3) real-time rendering of ensemble interactions in virtual environments for compositional experimentation. Expected outcomes include a publicly available movement analysis toolkit for dance scholars, quantitative frameworks for assessing injury risk in choreography, and novel metrics linking kinematic complexity to perceived artistic expression. By bridging computational science and dance theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for preserving intangible cultural heritage, enhancing dance pedagogy, and fostering collaborative creativity at the intersection of art and technology.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dance, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in sustainable construction material development and structural optimization through advanced computational modeling. Current approaches to evaluating novel materials (e.g., bio-based composites, recycled aggregate concretes) and complex structural systems rely heavily on physical prototyping and simplified analytical models, which are time-intensive, costly, and lack the resolution needed to predict long-term performance under dynamic environmental conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this research will implement multi-scale finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning (ML) to simulate material behavior, structural integrity, and lifecycle environmental impacts. Computational models will integrate molecular dynamics simulations at the microstructural level with macro-scale building component analyses, incorporating variable loads, moisture diffusion, and thermal cycling. A parallelized ML framework will iteratively refine these models using experimental data from partner laboratories, enabling predictive optimization of material formulations and structural configurations. The HPC environment is critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space, including stochastic environmental variables and nonlinear material responses, which require distributed-memory computations across thousands of cores. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for 15+ emerging sustainable materials, an open-access digital toolkit for construction trade professionals, and performance benchmarks for hybrid material systems in energy-efficient building envelopes. By reducing reliance on physical trials, this work aims to accelerate the adoption of low-carbon construction materials while maintaining safety standards, potentially decreasing material development timelines by 40-60% and informing updates to industry building codes. The resource request supports 18 months of simulations, including GPU-accelerated ML training and petascale data storage for multi-terabyte output from coupled thermo-mechanical analyses.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in construction trades, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary leadership studies by modeling complex, large-scale social dynamics in human groups. Leadership, as a universal yet context-dependent phenomenon, remains understudied through computational frameworks capable of capturing nonlinear interactions, adaptive decision-making, and emergent behaviors in diverse organizational settings. Traditional qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods struggle to simulate the interdependencies between leadership styles, group cohesion, and situational variables in dynamic environments. This project addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) and network simulations to explore how leadership strategies propagate through heterogeneous groups, adapt to crises, and influence collective outcomes. The computational approach integrates behavioral theory, organizational psychology, and complexity science to parameterize agents with traits such as risk tolerance, communication patterns, and decision heuristics. Simulations will test hypotheses about the resilience of distributed vs. hierarchical leadership structures under stressors like resource scarcity or conflicting priorities. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to thousands of agents, iterating across probabilistic scenarios, and applying machine learning techniques to identify patterns in leadership efficacy. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for leadership studies, (2) data-driven insights into how contextual factors moderate leadership success, and (3) open-access tools for simulating leadership interventions in virtual environments. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this work aims to generate actionable knowledge for training adaptable leaders in sectors ranging from corporate governance to community organizing. The project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional disciplines, advancing methodological innovation while addressing real-world challenges in human systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the universal phenomenon of leadership in human groups. Includes instruction in general or multidisciplinary leadership theory, practice and philosophy.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural literary influence and ideological transmission through large-scale computational analysis of multilingual textual corpora spanning the 19th to 21st centuries. The central research problem addresses how geopolitical shifts, colonial histories, and transnational exchanges have shaped narrative structures and thematic preoccupations across literatures of the Global South and North, a question previously constrained by the manual analysis of fragmented datasets. By integrating methods from comparative literature, digital humanities, and cultural sociology, the project will employ high-performance computing resources to process and analyze over 20 terabytes of primary texts, critical works, and archival materials in 12 languages. Computational approaches will include multilingual transformer models fine-tuned for literary analysis, network graphs tracing citation patterns and adaptation histories, and spatial-temporal modeling of thematic diffusion. These methods require parallelized computing architectures to handle complex natural language processing tasks across diverse linguistic systems and script traditions while maintaining attention to historical context. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for computational comparative literary studies that accounts for non-Western epistemologies, 2) quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric models of literary periodization, and 3) open-access visualizations mapping 200 years of transcultural narrative exchanges. The project aims to establish new methodologies for studying cultural production at scale while providing humanists with tools to interrogate systems of canon formation and cultural hegemony. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process marginalized texts often excluded from dominant literary histories, this work directly supports the program’s mission to advance interdisciplinary research at the intersection of political economy, textual studies, and critical theory.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of cultural studies and comparative literature or a specialization which draws from cultural studies and comparative literature. Includes instruction in anthropology, comparative linguistics, cultural studies, history, literary criticism, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, sociology, and textual studies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing radar network configurations in dynamic, contested electromagnetic environments, with a focus on enhancing resilience against adversarial electronic warfare (EW) tactics. Modern military radar systems face escalating challenges from adaptive jamming, spectrum congestion, and emerging low-observable threats, necessitating advanced computational tools to model complex interactions between radar emissions, target signatures, and countermeasure strategies. Current simulation approaches often lack the resolution to capture multi-domain effects at scale, particularly when evaluating distributed radar architectures or networked coordination protocols. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-physics simulation environment integrating electromagnetic wave propagation models, real-time adversarial action-reaction dynamics, and machine learning-driven optimization.
