cip_definition: Any instructional program in the soil sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time auditing of multinational financial transactions across heterogeneous regulatory environments, a growing challenge in global accounting practices. Traditional auditing systems struggle to dynamically adapt to the volume, velocity, and complexity of cross-border transactions, particularly as regulatory frameworks evolve and diverge. The project will employ graph neural networks (GNNs) and agent-based modeling to simulate and analyze transactional networks under varying jurisdictional rules, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to process terabytes of structured and unstructured financial data. By training GNNs on multi-language regulatory texts and historical transaction patterns, the models will identify anomalies and compliance risks in real time, while agent-based simulations will test the cascading effects of regulatory changes on audit workflows. The computational demands include parallel processing of distributed ledger data, large-scale graph traversal for transaction linkage analysis, and real-time natural language processing of legal updates. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for adaptive audit trail analysis, reducing manual review times by an estimated 40–60% in test cases. This work bridges gaps in computational accounting, regulatory technology, and graph-based AI, offering a scalable solution for auditors operating in fragmented legal landscapes. The research will also generate benchmark datasets linking transaction semantics to jurisdictional constraints, advancing interdisciplinary work at the intersection of accounting, computational linguistics, and complex systems analysis. Successfully demonstrating this approach could redefine standards for agile audit systems in an era of accelerating global financial digitization.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in accounting, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution of medieval ecclesiastical legal systems through computational textual and network analysis. While canon law has been studied extensively through traditional philological and theological methods, the dynamic interplay between localized legal practices and centralized doctrinal codification remains underexplored at scale. The research addresses this gap by processing a corpus of digitized manuscripts, conciliar decrees, and commentaries (ca. 800–1500 CE) to model how regional norms were assimilated, contested, or suppressed within broader ecclesiastical frameworks. Key computational challenges include parsing non-standardized Latin juridical terminology, tracing citation networks across multilingual sources, and identifying temporal patterns in legal adaptation. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical Latin and vernacular variants, complemented by graph-based algorithms to reconstruct relationships between legal provisions, institutions, and geographic regions. By simulating hypothetical diffusion pathways of doctrinal influence using agent-based models, the study aims to quantify the relative impact of factors such as episcopal authority, monastic networks, and secular political interventions on legal standardization. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated canon law texts with linked metadata, interactive visualizations of normative development, and statistical frameworks for assessing the durability of specific legal innovations. This computational approach offers novel insights into how decentralized religious legal systems balance uniformity and contextual flexibility—a challenge with analogues in contemporary pluralistic societies. The resource-intensive nature of processing over 50,000 pages of manuscript-derived text, coupled with the need for iterative model training across multilingual datasets, necessitates HPC support for parallelized text analysis, large-scale graph computations, and storage of intermediate semantic representations. Results will advance methodological synergies between digital humanities and legal history while providing scalable tools for interdisciplinary studies of normative systems.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, theology, and philosophy of religious, church, and ecclesiastical law and that prepares individuals to serve as professional canonists.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and safety of industrial and commercial piping and sprinkler systems through high-fidelity computational modeling and optimization. Current industry practices for designing complex piping networks—particularly those integrating fire suppression, thermal regulation, and fluid transport—rely heavily on standardized codes and iterative physical testing. However, these methods struggle to account for dynamic multi-physics interactions, such as transient fluid-structure interactions during pressure surges or thermal gradients in high-temperature environments, which can lead to suboptimal designs, material fatigue, or catastrophic failures. To address these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multi-scale simulation framework that integrates computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization. The framework will model fluid flow, thermal stresses, and mechanical vibrations in piping systems under diverse operational scenarios, including emergency sprinkler activation and exposure to extreme temperatures. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to explore design permutations at unprecedented resolution, reducing reliance on costly physical prototypes. Additionally, ML algorithms will identify optimal pipe routing, material selection, and joint configurations to minimize pressure losses and failure risks while adhering to ASME and NFPA standards. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for system performance, open-source simulation tools tailored to pipefitting applications, and data-driven guidelines for resilient system design. This work will directly enhance training curricula by integrating computational best practices into pipefitter education, while providing industry stakeholders with actionable insights to improve safety and efficiency in critical infrastructure. The scalability of the proposed methods also lays groundwork for future research into smart piping systems with embedded IoT sensors and real-time adaptive controls.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, install, and test industrial and commercial piping systems and automatic fire and exposure protection systems. Includes instruction in water systems, steam systems, heating and cooling systems, lubricating systems, piping materials, installation tools operation and maintenance, valve installation and repair, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural and linguistic identities in Ukraine’s border regions, with a focus on the interplay between historical narratives, media representation, and community-driven discourses. The research addresses a critical gap in Ukraine Studies: the lack of large-scale, longitudinal analyses of cultural self-determination in multiethnic border zones, particularly in contexts of geopolitical conflict and shifting territorial affiliations. By integrating digitized archival materials, regional press corpora (1945–present), and contemporary social media data, the project aims to map patterns of cultural hybridity, language use, and collective memory across time and space. Computational methods will include multilingual natural language processing (NLP) tailored to Ukrainian, Crimean Tatar, and minority languages; network analysis to trace thematic linkages in media narratives; and geospatial modeling to visualize cultural diffusion. These methods require HPC capabilities due to the scale of unstructured text data (estimated at 15 TB), the complexity of training transformer models on low-resource languages, and the iterative processing needed for temporal network reconstructions. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible digital atlas of cultural identity markers in Ukraine’s borderlands, (2) algorithms for detecting linguistic interference and code-switching in multiethnic media, and (3) quantitative frameworks to assess the impact of state-level cultural policies on regional identity formation. The project will advance methodological innovation in area studies by demonstrating how computational approaches can disentangle overlapping cultural narratives while respecting contextual specificities. Results will inform cultural preservation initiatives and provide empirical grounding for debates on minority rights in post-conflict societies. By prioritizing computational reproducibility, the workflows developed will serve as a template for interdisciplinary studies of identity in other contested regions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Ukraine and its inhabitants, and related border regions, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between urban environmental design, digital surveillance infrastructure, and spatial patterns of cyber-physical hybrid crimes (e.g., coordinated cyber fraud with physical asset retrieval). While traditional criminological frameworks often treat digital and physical crime domains separately, emerging criminal strategies exploit gaps at their intersection, challenging existing predictive models and policy responses. The research employs agent-based modeling (ABM) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to simulate multi-layered offender networks operating across both digital platforms and built environments, using anonymized datasets spanning dark web transaction records, IoT device logs, and geotagged police reports from three metropolitan regions. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: 1) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations testing how varying urban surveillance densities influence criminal network adaptation strategies, 2) temporal graph embeddings of cross-platform communication patterns at sub-minute resolution, and 3) hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models predicting spatial-temporal crime hot spots under different infrastructure investment scenarios. The computational architecture integrates geographic information systems (GIS) data with dark web crawl outputs through a custom spatial-temporal graph transformer framework. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for hybrid crime simulation, empirical evidence quantifying the diminishing returns of surveillance saturation in interconnected crime systems, and policy matrices identifying infrastructure configurations that maximize cyber-physical deterrence synergies. By advancing computational methods to model multi-domain criminal ecosystems, this work aims to establish new normative frameworks for evaluating 21st-century crime prevention strategies that account for the sociotechnical entanglement of digital and physical environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of crime as a sociopathological phenomenon, the behavior of criminals, and the social institutions evolved to respond to crime. Includes instruction in the theory of crime, psychological and social bases of criminal behavior, social value systems and the theory of punishment, criminal law and criminal justice systems, penology, rehabilitation and recidivism, studies of specific types of crime, social attitudes and policy, and applications to specific issues in law enforcement administration and policy.

abstract: Mental health disorders represent a significant global burden, yet their underlying biological and computational mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the complexity of integrating multi-modal data across genetic, neuroimaging, and behavioral domains. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model the interactions between genetic risk factors, brain network dynamics, and symptom trajectories in psychiatric conditions such as schizophrenia and major depressive disorder. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale datasets, including whole-genome sequencing, functional MRI (fMRI) time series, and longitudinal clinical assessments from multinational cohorts. Key computational methods include the implementation of deep learning architectures to identify transdiagnostic biomarkers, Bayesian network models to infer causal pathways linking genetic variants to neural circuit dysfunction, and graph theoretical analyses to characterize dynamic brain connectivity patterns. These approaches require intensive parallel processing due to the high dimensionality of genomic data (~10^6–10^7 variants), the temporal resolution of fMRI datasets (~10^5 voxel-timepoints per subject), and the need for iterative simulations across diverse patient subgroups. Anticipated outcomes include the discovery of stratified risk profiles for treatment-resistant depression and psychosis, as well as predictive models of disease progression informed by genotype-neurophenotype interactions. The project will also generate open-source tools for scalable multi-omics integration in psychiatric research. By elucidating mechanisms that transcend traditional diagnostic boundaries, this work aims to advance precision psychiatry and inform the development of targeted neurotherapeutic interventions. The scale of data harmonization, model training, and validation necessitates access to HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes, large-memory capacity, and distributed storage to accommodate petabyte-scale datasets.
cip_definition: Research focused on Psychiatric/Mental Health

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing decentralized, self-organizing networks for dynamic environmental monitoring in underserved rural regions. Traditional network protocols struggle to maintain reliability and low latency in such environments due to rapidly changing physical conditions, intermittent power availability, and heterogeneous device capabilities. The research proposes a novel computational framework inspired by adaptive biological systems, integrating swarm intelligence algorithms with lightweight machine learning models to enable networks to autonomously reconfigure topology, routing paths, and resource allocation in response to environmental perturbations. The core innovation lies in developing multi-agent simulations that model network nodes as autonomous entities capable of collective decision-making through localized data exchange, prioritizing energy efficiency and fault tolerance without centralized coordination. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for simulating large-scale networks (10,000+ nodes) under diverse environmental stress scenarios, including stochastic weather patterns, electromagnetic interference, and partial node failures. Computational methods will combine discrete-event network simulations with evolutionary optimization techniques, requiring parallel processing to evaluate millions of configuration permutations. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available benchmark dataset quantifying network resilience metrics under real-world constraints, 2) adaptive protocol designs that reduce energy consumption by 30-50% compared to existing mesh networking standards, and 3) predictive models for optimal node placement in terrain-aware deployments. This work bridges gaps between distributed computing, environmental sensing, and complex systems theory, with potential applications in disaster response networks, precision agriculture telemetry, and IoT infrastructure for climate-vulnerable regions. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits to support replicable research in emerging fields of ecological networking.
cip_title: Computer Systems Networking and Telecommunications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer systems networking and telecommunications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the urgent need for large-scale computational analysis of under-documented and endangered languages across the Australian, Oceanic, and Pacific regions. Many languages in these areas, particularly Papuan, Indigenous Australian, and Polynesian languages, face critical threats of extinction, while their complex morphological and syntactic structures remain understudied due to limited resources and methodological constraints. Traditional linguistic workflows struggle to manage the volume and diversity of multimodal data—including audio recordings, oral histories, and community texts—required to model these languages effectively. To bridge this gap, we propose deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced machine learning pipelines for automated phonetic alignment, morphological segmentation, and cross-dialectal comparison. Our computational approach integrates transformer-based models adapted for low-resource languages, Bayesian phylogenetic algorithms to trace language contact dynamics, and distributed processing of terabyte-scale corpora spanning 30+ languages from Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, and Micronesia. These methods will enable systematic analysis of tonal variation in Austronesian languages, allomorphy in Papuan verb systems, and semantic shift in Polynesian navigational lexicons—phenomena that demand iterative, resource-intensive simulations. Anticipated outcomes include the first open-source digital toolkit for Pacific language documentation, probabilistic maps of language family diversification, and community-accessible databases for revitalization programs. The project will advance linguistic theory by revealing patterns in grammaticalization pathways and contact-induced change while addressing equity gaps in NLP resource distribution. HPC infrastructure is indispensable for training cross-lingual embeddings on non-Latin scripts, parallelizing comparative analyses across language subgroups, and optimizing hyperparameters for speech recognition models in noise-prone field recordings. This work directly supports Indigenous data sovereignty goals while pioneering computational methods tailored to the typological diversity of Oceania’s linguistic heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Australian/ Oceanic/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages native to Papua/New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and the island groups of the Pacific Ocean, including, but not limited to, the Papuan languages, the Australian languages, the Micronesian languages, and the Polynesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the performance and sustainability of advanced fenestration systems through computational modeling and simulation. As architectural designs increasingly prioritize energy efficiency, safety, and material durability, glaziers face complex demands in selecting, installing, and maintaining transparent materials under diverse environmental and structural conditions. Current empirical methods for evaluating stress distribution, thermal behavior, and long-term wear in glass and polymer-based systems lack the precision needed to predict failures or optimize installations for novel geometries and climates. This project will develop high-fidelity computational models to simulate the mechanical and thermal performance of glazing systems across scales—from molecular interactions in adhesive interfaces to macro-scale stress analysis in multi-pane assemblies. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will quantify the effects of environmental factors (e.g., wind load, thermal cycling, UV exposure) on material integrity and sealing efficacy. Machine learning techniques will be applied to correlate simulation data with real-world failure patterns from historical installation datasets, enabling predictive maintenance frameworks. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing resources to manage iterative parametric studies, multiscale model coupling, and large-scale optimization of installation parameters (e.g., fastening patterns, edge clearance tolerances). Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for glaziers to evaluate site-specific material selections and installation techniques, reducing waste and improving lifecycle performance. By bridging computational materials science with applied glazing practices, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for energy-efficient building envelopes and contribute to updated industry standards for resilient fenestration systems. The resource allocation will directly support parallelized simulations across 10,000+ core-hours, leveraging GPU-accelerated workloads for ML training and 3D stress visualization, which are infeasible with existing campus computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair fixtures, sheets, windows, and skylights made of glass, plexiglass, and other transparent materials. Includes instruction in site measurement, job analysis and estimation, material cutting and trimming, window and door installation, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced simulation frameworks for optimizing the design and operational efficiency of industrial-scale electromechanical systems, with a focus on integrated servo-actuated mechanisms and automated control architectures. Modern electromechanical systems increasingly demand precision in dynamic load management, energy efficiency, and real-time adaptability, yet physical prototyping and testing remain resource-intensive and time-consuming. To address this, we propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-domain interactions—including mechanical stress, thermal dynamics, and electromagnetic feedback—within complex electromechanical assemblies. High-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) and transient system simulations will be deployed to evaluate component-level performance under variable operational scenarios, such as fluctuating torque demands in servo-driven systems or transient thermal loads in automated production lines. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to iteratively refine control algorithms and predictive maintenance schedules based on simulated degradation patterns. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations to industrial-relevant configurations, enabling parallelized parameter sweeps and probabilistic failure analysis that exceed the capabilities of conventional workstations. Anticipated outcomes include validated digital twins for electromechanical systems, optimized control strategies to reduce energy consumption by 15–20% in target applications, and generalized frameworks for rapid fault diagnosis in industrial automation contexts. This work will directly support curriculum development in electromechanical system design and provide students with hands-on experience in computational engineering tools, while advancing industry-relevant methodologies for sustainable manufacturing and smart automation. The requested resources will ensure scalability to real-world systems, bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical implementation in engineering technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing and testing automated, servomechanical, and other electromechanical systems. Includes instruction in prototype testing, manufacturing and operational testing, systems analysis and maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance earth science education by developing and deploying high-resolution computational models to simulate complex Earth systems for use in teacher training and K-12 classrooms. A critical challenge in earth science pedagogy is the lack of accessible, interactive tools that accurately represent dynamic processes such as climate feedbacks, hydrological cycles, and tectonic activity. Existing educational models often oversimplify these systems, limiting students’ ability to engage with authentic scientific practices like hypothesis testing and data-driven decision-making. To address this gap, we propose creating a suite of scalable, GPU-accelerated Earth system simulations optimized for educational contexts. These simulations will integrate real-world datasets from satellite observations, ground-based sensors, and paleoclimate archives, downscaled to regional resolutions relevant to classroom case studies. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will run ensemble climate models under varying parameters to generate probabilistic outputs, which will be packaged into modular, age-appropriate virtual labs. Concurrently, machine learning methods will analyze patterns in how pre-service teachers adapt these tools for lesson design, identifying computational bottlenecks and pedagogical misconceptions. The project will also leverage distributed computing to host collaborative modeling exercises, enabling cross-institutional cohorts of educators to compare localized climate projections or geologic hazard scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access computational curricula aligned with Next Generation Science Standards, (2) a framework for integrating HPC-derived datasets into teacher training programs, and (3) benchmarks for scaling geoscientific modeling tasks across heterogeneous classroom technologies. By grounding earth science instruction in cutting-edge computational research, this work aims to enhance spatial reasoning skills and systems thinking among both educators and students, while fostering familiarity with computational tools critical to modern geoscience careers. The requested resources are essential for managing the high-throughput simulations, real-time data assimilation, and large-scale user testing required to validate the educational efficacy of these models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach earth science programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive bio-hybrid materials for environmental remediation, integrating principles from plant biomechanics, synthetic biology, and fluid dynamics. Current remediation technologies struggle to address low-concentration, multi-component pollutants in dynamic aquatic environments. Inspired by the hierarchical pore structures and responsive behaviors of plant root systems, we propose a computational framework to design and optimize synthetic bio-hybrid membranes capable of selective pollutant capture and self-regulating permeability. The central challenge lies in modeling the coupled physicochemical processes across disparate spatiotemporal scales: molecular interactions at ligand-pollutant interfaces (nanoseconds, Ångströms), mesoscale polymer network rearrangements (milliseconds, micrometers), and macroscale fluid transport (seconds, meters). A multi-method approach will combine molecular dynamics with machine learning-accelerated free energy calculations, lattice Boltzmann methods for porous media flow, and hybrid continuum-discrete models for shape-memory material responses. These simulations will be validated against microfluidics experiments and synchrotron-based X-ray tomography of prototype materials. The HPC environment is critical for resolving the nonlinear feedback between chemical selectivity and hydraulic efficiency across 8-10 orders of magnitude in space and time, requiring tightly coupled simulations across GPU- and CPU-optimized architectures. Expected outcomes include a predictive computational platform for bio-hybrid material design, identification of optimal pore topology-property relationships under flow constraints, and dynamic control strategies for adaptive pollutant capture. This work will establish quantitative links between biological design principles and engineered remediation systems while advancing computational methods for multiscale reactive transport in deformable media. Results will directly inform the fabrication of next-generation smart membranes, with potential applications in decentralized water treatment and environmental monitoring.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of scientific computing and its application. Includes instruction in scientific visualization, multi-scale analysis, grid generation, data analysis, applied mathematics, numerical algorithms, high performance parallel computing, and numerical modeling and simulation with applications in science, engineering and other disciplines in which computation plays an integral role.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic and transboundary animal diseases pose critical threats to global food security, livestock economies, and public health. Current challenges in predicting disease dynamics stem from the complex interplay of host-pathogen interactions, environmental drivers, and anthropogenic factors, which are poorly captured by traditional epidemiological models. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to simulate disease transmission dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes and livestock populations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate agent-based modeling, machine learning, and spatially explicit risk mapping to analyze large-scale datasets, including national livestock movement records, climate projections, and genomic surveillance data. The computational pipeline will parameterize disease spread mechanisms for priority pathogens such as avian influenza and foot-and-mouth disease, incorporating stochastic variability in host behavior, pathogen evolution, and intervention efficacy. Key innovations include the fusion of real-time environmental sensor data with livestock demographic networks to model climate-driven vector activity and the use of deep learning architectures to identify high-risk transmission corridors. This resource-intensive approach requires parallelized simulations across thousands of scenarios to quantify uncertainty in outbreak trajectories and control measures. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize vaccine allocation, early warning systems for cross-species spillover events, and decision-support frameworks for mitigating antimicrobial resistance emergence in animal reservoirs. By advancing computational capabilities in veterinary epidemiology, this work will directly inform One Health policies, enhance biosecurity planning for agricultural systems, and reduce economic losses from production-limiting diseases. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing of petabyte-scale genomic and geospatial datasets, which is currently infeasible with institutional computing infrastructure.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology, and Public Health
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the prevention and control of communicable animal diseases, diseases affecting humans, and prepares veterinarians to function as public health specialists. Includes instruction in animal epidemiology, biostatistics, food safety and quality assurance, food toxicology, zoonotic and infectious diseases, disease vectors and transference, production medicine, animal health, veterinary public health practice, and inspection and evaluation methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling and rendering large-scale, interactive sound environments for experimental artistic practice. Sound arts research increasingly relies on simulating complex acoustic phenomena, real-time processing of spatial audio, and generative sound design—tasks that demand significant processing power, memory, and parallelization. Current consumer-grade systems lack the capacity to handle high-channel-count spatial audio diffusion, dynamic wave-field synthesis, or machine learning-driven sound synthesis at the granularity required for immersive installations. The proposed research will develop computational frameworks for two interconnected strands: (1) simulating acoustic environments with wave-based algorithms to model sound propagation in non-linear, site-specific spaces, and (2) training neural networks to generate adaptive soundscapes responsive to real-time sensor inputs during live performances. Methods will include finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) acoustic simulations, GPU-accelerated spectral processing, and distributed computing approaches to synchronize audio rendering across multi-channel arrays. By utilizing HPC infrastructure, these workflows will scale to handle 3D spatial audio resolutions exceeding 256 discrete channels and latency-sensitive generative systems incorporating motion capture and environmental data streams. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for computational sound design, validated through public installations and performances, that demonstrate how HPC can expand the creative possibilities of sound as a performative medium. This work will contribute new methodologies at the intersection of auditory culture and computational arts while establishing benchmarks for resource-intensive sonic practices within performing arts research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on sound as a form of cultural expression, and its relationship to other disciplines such as computer programming, performance, and video. Includes instruction in acoustics; arranging, composing, and editing music; music theory; musicology; orchestration and scoring; and sound design.

abstract: The construction industry faces significant challenges in optimizing resource allocation, energy efficiency, and structural performance while adhering to evolving safety and sustainability standards. Traditional approaches to construction planning and material selection often rely on generalized guidelines or localized testing, which may fail to account for complex interactions between building materials, environmental conditions, and long-term wear patterns. This project proposes a computational framework to model multi-physics interactions in construction systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. By integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) techniques, we aim to simulate the behavior of composite building materials under dynamic stressors such as thermal fluctuations, moisture ingress, and mechanical loads. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parametric studies of masonry, timber, and steel assemblies across diverse climatic scenarios, generating datasets to predict failure modes and lifecycle costs. A key innovation involves coupling these simulations with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to automate the design of energy-efficient building envelopes tailored to regional environmental conditions. The computational workflow will leverage parallel processing to reduce simulation times for complex 3D models from weeks to hours, facilitating rapid iteration of design alternatives. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access database of validated material performance metrics under multi-stressor conditions, (2) machine learning models for predictive maintenance scheduling in built environments, and (3) optimization algorithms to minimize embodied carbon in construction projects without compromising structural integrity. This work addresses critical gaps in data-driven construction practices and provides actionable tools for reducing waste and improving resilience in residential and commercial infrastructure. The requested computing resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations and distributed training of deep neural networks, which are computationally prohibitive on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the building, inspecting, and maintaining of structures and related properties. May include instruction in masonry, carpentry, electrical and power transmission installation, building/construction finishing, management, inspection and other construction-related applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying synergistic interactions in multi-herbal formulations used in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) for chronic inflammatory conditions. While TCM formulations are clinically observed to exhibit enhanced efficacy when herbs are combined, the systems-level biochemical and pharmacokinetic principles governing these synergies remain poorly understood. Conventional experimental approaches struggle to model the combinatorial complexity of multi-component herbal extracts interacting with human physiological systems. To address this gap, we propose an integrative computational pipeline combining molecular docking, machine learning-driven network pharmacology, and multi-scale pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) modeling. HPC resources will enable large-scale virtual screening of phytochemical libraries against inflammatory targets (e.g., COX-2, TNF-α), construction of herb-herb interaction networks using graph neural networks, and dynamic simulations of formulation bioavailability across tissue compartments. The workflow will be validated against existing in vitro and clinical data for a prototypical TCM anti-arthritic formulation, followed by predictive modeling of optimized herb combinations. This computational framework aims to establish a predictive platform for deconstructing traditional polyherbal synergies, potentially identifying novel anti-inflammatory mechanisms while respecting TCM's holistic paradigm. Successful implementation could advance the evidence base for integrative medicine approaches, inform standardization of complex botanical products, and provide a template for computational ethnopharmacology studies. The requested resources are critical for handling the project's scale, including processing >1 billion molecular docking conformations, training multi-modal neural networks on heterogeneous biological datasets, and running parallelized PK-PD simulations across parameter spaces.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing predictive maintenance protocols in precision electromechanical systems, addressing the critical challenge of minimizing downtime in high-stakes industries such as aerospace, semiconductor manufacturing, and medical device production. Current maintenance strategies often rely on static schedules or reactive measures, leading to unnecessary resource expenditure or catastrophic failures. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multi-scale machine learning (ML) models that integrate real-time sensor data, historical failure patterns, and physics-based simulations of component degradation. The computational workflow will involve parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distributions in micro-tolerance components under operational loads, coupled with time-series forecasting models to predict wear trajectories. Reinforcement learning algorithms will then optimize maintenance schedules by balancing cost, risk, and operational constraints across interconnected subsystems. A key innovation lies in developing hybrid digital twins capable of dynamically updating maintenance recommendations based on evolving system states and environmental conditions. The required HPC resources will enable processing terabyte-scale datasets from industrial partners, including vibration spectra, thermal imaging, and lubrication performance metrics. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source predictive maintenance algorithms validated against industrial case studies, (2) a benchmark dataset for precision system failure modes, and (3) quantitative guidelines for sensor network density required to achieve target reliability thresholds. This work will advance the integration of computational decision-support tools into technician training programs while providing a scalable template for resource-efficient maintenance in next-generation nanoscale and quantum-enabled systems.
cip_title: Precision Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision systems maintenance and repair, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, sparse, and heterogeneous datasets commonly encountered in applied settings such as healthcare analytics, environmental monitoring, and industrial quality control. Traditional statistical tools often struggle with computational inefficiency or instability when applied to modern, large-scale datasets characterized by complex dependencies, missing data, or non-linear relationships. To address these challenges, we propose a computationally intensive framework combining Bayesian hierarchical modeling, non-parametric regression techniques, and Monte Carlo-based inference. The core innovation lies in adapting these methods for distributed computing architectures to enable robust uncertainty quantification in high-dimensional problems. Key computational tasks include Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for hierarchical models with millions of parameters, parallelized cross-validation for tuning non-parametric estimators, and simulation-based power analyses for experimental design optimization. These workflows require high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to their iterative nature, memory-intensive data structures, and need for massive parallelization across thousands of cores. The proposed research will leverage GPU-accelerated libraries for linear algebra operations and distributed computing frameworks such as Apache Spark to manage I/O bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for sparse signal detection in noisy observational data, open-source software packages implementing distributed statistical learning routines, and methodological advances in causal inference for temporally correlated measurements. Successfully implementing this work will directly benefit applied researchers through improved analytical tools for complex datasets while advancing statistical computing methodology. The requested allocation of 200,000 CPU-hours and 50 TB of temporary storage will support algorithm development, large-scale simulation studies to validate method performance, and analysis of real-world datasets from collaborative projects in precision medicine and climate impact modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of climate-driven ecosystem transitions in understudied boreal and montane regions. Rapid environmental changes are altering species distributions, disturbance regimes, and carbon sequestration dynamics in these critical biomes, but existing models lack the spatial resolution and mechanistic detail needed to inform adaptive conservation strategies. To address this gap, we propose a coupled modeling framework integrating dynamic vegetation models, hydrologic simulations, and species dispersal algorithms at 1 km² resolution across 10⁶ km² of North American and Eurasian study areas. The computational workflow will utilize a hybrid machine learning and process-based approach, assimilating remotely sensed land cover data, downscaled CMIP6 climate projections, and empirical biodiversity datasets. Key challenges include scaling individual species niche models to community-level interactions and resolving feedbacks between vegetation shifts, wildfire patterns, and permafrost degradation. The requested HPC resources will enable parallel execution of ensemble simulations across 500+ parameter combinations, requiring ~2.8 million core-hours for model calibration, sensitivity analysis, and scenario testing. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of ecosystem tipping points under varying emission trajectories, (2) high-resolution vulnerability maps prioritizing areas for habitat corridors, and (3) open-source tools for simulating coupled biogeochemical and biodiversity responses to climate forcing. These outputs will directly support international conservation initiatives focused on climate resilience while advancing computational methods for cross-scale ecological forecasting. The project’s scale and complexity necessitate dedicated HPC infrastructure to manage memory-intensive spatial analyses and iterative model optimization, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local computing clusters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Medical transcription accuracy is critical for patient safety, legal compliance, and operational efficiency in healthcare, yet persistent challenges remain in automating the processing of complex, context-dependent medical dictations. This project proposes the development of an adaptive, multimodal transcription system leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address three core limitations of current tools: (1) poor generalization across diverse speaker accents, speech patterns, and acoustic environments; (2) inadequate handling of specialized medical terminology with overlapping semantic meanings across specialties; and (3) latency constraints in processing long-form, continuous dictations with real-time error correction. The computational approach integrates transformer-based architectures with domain-adapted speech recognition models, trained on a curated corpus of 50,000+ hours of de-identified clinical dictations spanning 12 medical specialties. Parallelized training pipelines will optimize Whisper-X and Wav2Vec frameworks using dynamic time warping for speaker normalization, while graph neural networks will map contextual relationships between medical entities in paired audio-text datasets. A novel confidence scoring module will probabilistically flag uncertain transcriptions using ensemble methods, enabling targeted human review. HPC resources are essential for processing the 200TB audio corpus, running distributed hyperparameter optimization across speech and language model components, and simulating real-time inference workloads under variable clinical noise conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source transcription toolkit achieving <5% word error rate on rare medical terms (compared to 15-20% in commercial systems), validated through blinded comparisons with certified medical transcriptionists. The project will additionally produce benchmark datasets and evaluation protocols for context-aware clinical speech processing, addressing a critical gap in health informatics infrastructure. By reducing reliance on error-prone manual workflows, this work directly supports improved diagnostic accuracy, streamlined clinical documentation, and enhanced interoperability between voice-based data entry systems and electronic health records.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to execute verbatim medical conference minutes, medical reports, and medical orders. Includes instruction in dictation and simultaneous recording, analysis of notes and visual evidence, medical terminology, data processing applications and skills, formal medical report and correspondence formats, professional standards, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of leadership decision-making and its impact on organizational resilience in complex, large-scale teams. Traditional studies of leadership efficacy often rely on qualitative case analyses or simplified simulations, limiting their ability to model nonlinear interactions, emergent behaviors, and multi-level feedback loops inherent in real-world organizations. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework that simulates decision cascades, communication patterns, and stress-testing scenarios under varying leadership styles (e.g., transformational, transactional, distributed). The computational model will integrate empirical data from organizational surveys and historical crisis management cases to parameterize agents representing team members, mid-level managers, and executive leaders. HPC resources are essential to execute millions of parallel simulations across diverse parameters, including team size, resource constraints, and external disruptions, while employing machine learning techniques to identify critical thresholds where leadership interventions maximize adaptive capacity. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model linking leadership strategies to measurable organizational outcomes such as decision latency, trust erosion, and recovery rates during crises; (2) actionable insights into optimizing communication networks and resource allocation protocols for leaders in cross-functional teams; and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating leadership scenarios tailored to nonprofit, corporate, and hybrid organizational structures. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based training programs and adaptive policy frameworks for leaders navigating volatile, uncertain environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leadership skills that can be applied to a business, government, non-profit, or educational setting. Includes instruction in organizational planning, dynamics of leadership, finance, team building, conflict resolution and mediation, communication and other management skills.

abstract: Wind energy systems face critical challenges in optimizing turbine performance, minimizing mechanical failures, and adapting to dynamic environmental conditions. Current predictive maintenance protocols and turbine placement strategies often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture complex fluid-structure interactions, terrain effects, and long-term material degradation patterns. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate wind farm operation under realistic multi-physical constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a two-phase computational approach: 1) Large-eddy simulations using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis to map turbulent airflow patterns around turbine arrays across diverse terrain profiles, and 2) Machine learning-driven predictive maintenance frameworks trained on synthetic data from physics-based degradation models of key components like gearboxes and blade pitch systems. The CFD simulations will resolve turbulence at meter-scale resolutions across multi-kilometer domains, requiring parallelized GPU-accelerated computations to achieve practical timescales. Material degradation models will incorporate multi-year weather datasets and operational telemetry to predict component fatigue under cyclical loading. Expected outcomes include optimized turbine placement templates that increase energy capture by 8-12% in complex terrain, failure prediction algorithms with 72-hour warning thresholds for critical components, and validated digital twins for technician training simulations. These computational tools will directly inform curriculum development for wind turbine maintenance certification programs while providing actionable insights for wind farm operators. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the petabyte-scale datasets and non-linear optimization challenges inherent in this multi-disciplinary analysis, ultimately advancing both wind energy technology and workforce training methodologies through data-driven innovation.
cip_title: Wind Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair wind energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an AI-driven simulation environment to optimize training protocols for teacher assistants (TAs) working with neurodiverse and multilingual student populations in inclusive classrooms. While TAs play a critical role in bridging gaps between instructional goals and student needs, existing training frameworks lack personalized, scenario-based tools to prepare TAs for the dynamic challenges of heterogeneous classrooms. The research problem centers on the computational modeling of high-variability classroom interactions—including non-verbal cues, language transitions, and sensory processing differences—that require real-time adaptive strategies from TAs. We propose a two-phase computational approach: (1) creating synthetic classroom cohorts using generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on multimodal educational datasets (speech, gesture, eye-tracking), and (2) implementing reinforcement learning agents that model TA decision-making processes during simulated interventions. The high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of over 10,000 unique student-TA interaction scenarios, each requiring real-time analysis of linguistic, behavioral, and environmental parameters through coupled natural language processing and computer vision pipelines. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform capable of generating TA training modules that adapt to individual learning trajectories, along with quantitative frameworks for assessing TA competency in managing complex classroom dynamics. This work intersects educational psychology, computational linguistics, and machine learning, offering novel methodologies for scaling specialized educator training while maintaining fidelity to the nuanced realities of diverse learning environments. The resulting tools could significantly reduce preparation time for TAs entering specialized classrooms while providing empirical insights into effective support strategies for students at the intersection of multiple learning modalities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist a teacher in regular classroom settings or in providing instruction and supervision to special student populations, such as bilingual/bicultural students, special education students, adult learners, and students learning English. Includes instruction in techniques of general classroom supervision, maintaining order, assisting with lessons and carrying out related assignments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation within Canadian multicultural communities, with a focus on Indigenous, Francophone, and immigrant groups from the late 19th century to the present. The research problem centers on understanding how large-scale textual and visual archives—including newspapers, oral history transcripts, public artworks, and community publications—reflect shifting intersections of language, heritage, and belonging. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the volume and heterogeneity of these materials, which span terabytes of digitized records in English, French, and Indigenous languages. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to identify patterns in thematic emphasis, symbolic representation, and cross-cultural dialogue across time and regions. Computational workflows will include transformer-based models for multilingual text classification, network analysis of co-occurring cultural references, and spatial-temporal mapping of discourse trends using GPU-accelerated clustering algorithms. A key innovation involves training domain-specific embeddings on Canadian French and Indigenous language corpora to improve semantic accuracy. By integrating HPC-enabled scalability with critical cultural theory, this work aims to reveal how decentralized cultural production has shaped Canada’s pluralist identity, particularly during periods of policy shifts such as multiculturalism legislation and Truth and Reconciliation Commission initiatives. Outcomes will include open-access datasets, visualization tools for public humanities engagement, and a framework for computationally analyzing cultural resilience in settler-colonial contexts. The resource request supports parallelized processing of over 10 million text pages and 500,000 images, enabling unprecedented granularity in tracing the dynamics of cultural exchange while centering marginalized voices. This interdisciplinary approach advances methodological synergies between Canadian Studies and digital humanities, offering scalable models for comparative ethnic and cultural research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Canada and its Pre-Columbian, colonial, and pre-federation predecessors, including immigrant flows and related borderlands and island groups.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design, safety, and operational efficiency of recreational vehicle (RV) systems through advanced simulations and predictive modeling. RVs integrate complex mechanical, electrical, and structural subsystems that interact dynamically under real-world conditions, yet current industry practices rely heavily on physical prototyping and reactive maintenance. This approach limits the ability to predict systemic failures, assess long-term material performance, or optimize energy use in hybrid propane-electric systems. To address these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-physics interactions across RV subsystems at scale. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate airflow and thermal loads on exterior components, while finite element analysis (FEA) will evaluate stress distributions in structural frames under variable towing and road conditions. Machine learning models, trained on operational data from RV sensors, will predict wear patterns in braking and hydraulic systems. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulations will assess failure probabilities in propane delivery systems under extreme temperatures. The integration of these computational methods will enable virtual testing of design modifications, reducing reliance on costly physical prototypes. Expected outcomes include predictive maintenance algorithms for RV service technicians, optimized component lifespans, and safety guidelines informed by probabilistic risk analysis. By centralizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to accelerate simulation runtime for parameter sweeps and multi-scale analyses, which are infeasible on local machines. Results will be disseminated through an open-access database of material performance metrics and simulation templates, bridging gaps between computational engineering and hands-on RV technical training. This work will provide a foundation for data-driven decision-making in RV design and servicing, enhancing both educational resources for technicians and sustainability outcomes for the industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to build, test, inspect, repair, service and maintain recreational vehicles, systems, and interior and exterior components. Includes instruction in brake, hydraulic, and towing systems; electrical systems; propane systems and propane and electric appliances; carpentry; plumbing; welding; and structural frames.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven decision-making in wine stewardship, a specialized domain within hospitality management that intersects sensory science, cultural geography, and supply chain analytics. The core challenge lies in modeling the complex, nonlinear relationships between wine chemical composition, sensory perception, and consumer preferences at scale—a problem requiring computational capabilities beyond conventional statistical approaches. Current methods for optimizing wine programs rely heavily on subjective expertise, limiting reproducibility and scalability in dynamic markets. This project will develop machine learning frameworks to analyze multidimensional datasets encompassing mass spectrometry profiles, sommelier tasting notes, regional climate data, and historical sales patterns. Computational workflows will integrate transformer-based natural language processing to decode qualitative tasting descriptors, graph neural networks to map regional typicity patterns, and Bayesian optimization for predictive inventory modeling. By parallelizing these tasks across GPU-accelerated nodes, the project aims to establish predictive models that quantify how specific chemical markers correlate with perceived quality across demographic cohorts and culinary contexts. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for wine program optimization, validated through partnerships with hospitality institutions, that reduces waste and improves pairing success rates. This work bridges gaps between enology, data science, and hospitality logistics while demonstrating how HPC can transform traditionally expertise-driven fields through scalable analytics. The resource request focuses on GPU cluster allocations for model training and memory-intensive simulations of vintage variation impacts on cellar management strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage wine selection, purchasing, storage, sales, and service for a variety of establishments in the hospitality industry. Includes instruction in wine production, wine regions of the world, wine tasting, food and wine matching, service techniques, and wine program management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze evolving narrative structures, thematic patterns, and representations of identity in anglophone children’s and adolescent literature across the 20th and 21st centuries. While qualitative studies of individual texts or authors dominate the field, large-scale computational analysis remains underutilized, limiting scholars’ ability to trace macro-level trends in genre development, cultural values, and audience engagement. This project will apply natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to a curated corpus of over 50,000 primary texts, including novels, picture books, and award-winning titles, alongside paratextual data (reviews, publisher catalogs). Computational methods will identify shifts in linguistic complexity, recurring motif clusters, and demographic representation patterns across age categories, historical periods, and geographic regions. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models to classify genre hybrids (e.g., eco-fiction, verse novels) and to map semantic networks connecting character archetypes, plot devices, and moral frameworks. Additionally, GPU-accelerated text mining will enable sentiment analysis of protagonist agency and emotional tonality at scale, addressing gaps in scholarship regarding evolving depictions of childhood adversity. Outcomes will include an open-access annotated dataset, visualizations of thematic evolution, and statistical models linking literary trends to educational policies and publishing industry data. By bridging computational literary studies with youth literature research, this project aims to inform inclusive curriculum design, library collection practices, and evidence-based discussions about canon formation. The requested resources will support processing multi-terabyte text corpora, running parallelized semantic analyses, and iteratively refining classification algorithms to account for the unique linguistic and narrative conventions of literature for young audiences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scholarly study of children's and adolescent literature and that may enhance the professional work of teachers, librarians, publishers, booksellers, and creative writers. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, studies of various types of literary text, book artists, and children's films.

abstract: The rising complexity of pharmaceutical markets and healthcare policy demands advanced analytical tools to evaluate cost-effectiveness, pricing strategies, and population health outcomes. Current pharmacoeconomic models often rely on simplified assumptions or aggregated data, limiting their capacity to capture real-world heterogeneity in patient responses, treatment pathways, and market dynamics. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework integrating real-world data (RWD) from electronic health records, insurance claims, and pharmaceutical supply chains to model the economic and clinical impacts of novel therapies under diverse policy scenarios. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between patients, providers, payers, and manufacturers, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict individual-level treatment outcomes and costs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across large synthetic populations (10⁶–10⁷ agents) and iterating policy parameters (e.g., reimbursement thresholds, value-based pricing contracts) with Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized optimization routines to identify formulary designs and pricing policies that balance affordability, manufacturer incentives, and population health gains. Outcomes will include open-source tools for dynamic cost-effectiveness analysis and policy briefs quantifying trade-offs between therapeutic innovation, healthcare expenditure, and equity. By enabling granular, systems-level pharmacoeconomic modeling, this project aims to inform evidence-based decision-making for payers, regulators, and manufacturers while advancing methodological integration of RWD and computational economics in pharmaceutical sciences.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics and policy analysis to the study of the relationship of pharmacy services and pharmaceutical processes and products to the health care system and their impact on health care organizations. Includes instruction in health economics, pharmacoeconomics, health care systems, health care organization and management, statistics and biostatistics, outcomes research, health care policy, pharmacy services, and pharmaceutical industry operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in optimizing food processing techniques for improved nutritional retention and safety. A critical challenge in food science lies in modeling the complex interactions between processing parameters (e.g., temperature, pressure, enzymatic activity) and the physicochemical properties of agricultural products. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and limited in their ability to predict outcomes across diverse food matrices. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML) to model the degradation pathways of micronutrients during thermal processing and storage. The study will focus on key vitamin complexes (e.g., B-group vitamins in fortified cereals) and plant-based proteins, examining how processing variables influence stability, bioavailability, and potential toxin formation. Large-scale MD simulations will parameterize time-dependent molecular interactions under varying thermal and mechanical stresses, while ML models trained on these datasets will predict optimal processing conditions. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the high-dimensional data generated by these simulations, enabling parallel computation of multi-scale models, and iteratively refining predictive algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated computational toolkit to guide the design of energy-efficient processing methods that minimize nutrient loss and mitigate safety risks. This work will directly inform industry practices, reduce reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, and support the development of scalable strategies for sustainable food production. By linking molecular-scale phenomena to macroscopic food quality metrics, the project bridges gaps in predictive modeling for agricultural product engineering, with broader implications for addressing global nutrition security.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of converting raw agricultural products into processed forms suitable for direct human consumption, and the storage of such products. Includes instruction in applicable aspects of the agricultural sciences, human physiology and nutrition, food chemistry, agricultural products processing, food additives, food preparation and packaging, food storage and shipment, and related aspects of human health and safety including toxicology and pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between urban recreational spaces and socio-environmental equity, a niche interdisciplinary domain within Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Studies. Despite the critical role parks play in community health and ecological resilience, current planning frameworks lack granular computational tools to simulate long-term outcomes of design decisions under shifting demographic and climatic conditions. The research problem centers on developing predictive models that integrate heterogeneous datasets—including geospatial park usage patterns, vegetation health metrics, and socioeconomic vulnerability indices—to evaluate how park allocation strategies affect equitable access and environmental justice in urban landscapes. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and geospatial temporal analysis, the project will simulate scenarios of park development, maintenance, and programming under varying budget constraints and climate projections. Computational workflows will process high-resolution satellite imagery, anonymized mobility data, and municipal infrastructure records to parameterize models, requiring parallelized processing for large-scale spatial datasets. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support framework that quantifies trade-offs between recreational resource allocation, canopy cover expansion, and neighborhood-level equity metrics. By coupling machine learning optimization techniques with participatory planning principles, the project aims to advance computational methods for leisure studies while generating actionable insights for municipalities addressing climate adaptation and social inclusion mandates. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the iterative, multi-agent simulations and scaling analyses across diverse urban typologies, enabling real-time visualization of complex system interactions that traditional planning tools cannot capture. This work bridges computational social science, urban ecology, and public policy, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional research domains focused on community well-being.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles underlying recreational and leisure activities, and the practices involved in providing indoor and outdoor recreational facilities and services for the general public.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling for social entrepreneurship ecosystems, with a focus on optimizing resource allocation and intervention strategies in underserved communities. Social enterprises face unique challenges in balancing financial sustainability with measurable social impact, particularly in dynamic environments where socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental variables interact nonlinearly. Traditional business analytics tools are ill-equipped to model these complexities, which involve high-dimensional datasets (e.g., community needs assessments, real-time philanthropic funding flows, environmental impact metrics) and stochastic decision-making under uncertainty. The proposed work will develop a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, network analysis, and reinforcement learning to simulate ecosystem-level interactions between social enterprises, beneficiaries, investors, and policymakers. By parameterizing models with geospatial data, historical intervention outcomes, and behavioral economic datasets, the project aims to identify leverage points for scaling impact while minimizing systemic risks such as resource depletion or community dependency. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale parallel simulations to explore "what-if" scenarios across diverse socioeconomic contexts, as well as training deep learning models to predict emergent outcomes of hybrid financing mechanisms (e.g., impact bonds blended with grassroots crowdfunding). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive resource allocation in social entrepreneurship, validated against case studies from renewable energy cooperatives and equitable healthcare initiatives in three regions. This work bridges computational social science, operations research, and ethical AI, offering novel insights into how data-driven approaches can enhance the resilience of mission-driven business models without compromising their social mandates. The results will inform policy frameworks and investment strategies aimed at democratizing access to entrepreneurial resources in marginalized communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on blending entrepreneurial ideas and management skills for issue advocacy and social change. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, design, entrepreneurship, finance, investing, resource management, project management, prototype development, and marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical inefficiencies in personalized medical device design and adaptive treatment planning through the development of a computational framework enabled by high-performance computing (HPC). Current medical devices and therapeutic protocols often lack dynamic responsiveness to individual patient physiology, leading to suboptimal outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose integrating multiscale biomechanical modeling with machine learning to optimize device functionality and treatment personalization. The research will leverage heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic profiles, real-time biosensor data, and medical imaging, to train predictive models that account for patient-specific variability. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional data, running parallelized finite element simulations to test device designs under diverse physiological conditions, and deploying deep reinforcement learning to iteratively refine treatment strategies. These tasks demand HPC resources for distributed storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate robustness across virtual patient cohorts. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source framework for in silico medical device testing, reducing reliance on physical prototyping, and predictive algorithms capable of recommending device adjustments or therapy modifications in near real-time. This work aligns with healthcare innovation priorities by accelerating the translation of adaptive technologies into clinical practice, potentially lowering costs and improving patient outcomes. The computational tools developed will also provide a foundation for data-driven decision-making in healthcare leadership, offering insights into scalability, risk stratification, and cost-benefit analyses for novel interventions. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance precision medicine and establish a replicable pipeline for innovation in medical device development and personalized care delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to innovate solutions and lead change within a healthcare organization. Includes instruction in innovation management, medical device development, evidence-based practice, systems thinking, information technology, healthcare policy and finance, organizational change, and leadership.
