abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural dynamics of large-scale human behavioral networks in prehistoric settlement systems using advanced computational modeling. Anthropological research on ancient societies often faces challenges in reconstructing complex social interactions from fragmented archaeological data, particularly when analyzing regional settlement patterns over multi-century timescales. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to systematically evaluate how ecological constraints, resource distribution, and social exchange networks shaped community resilience and cultural transmission. Our research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate decision-making processes among Neolithic agricultural populations in understudied regions of Southwest Asia. The computational framework integrates paleoenvironmental datasets, archaeological site distributions, and ethnographic analogs to parameterize agent behaviors related to land use, mobility, and intergroup cooperation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for running ensemble simulations at population scales exceeding 10^4 autonomous agents across 500-year temporal sequences, with sensitivity analyses testing 27 ecological and social variables. Parallelized model iterations will quantify emergent properties of settlement clustering, trade network formation, and systemic responses to climate stressors. Expected outcomes include the identification of non-linear thresholds in carrying capacity dynamics and evidence for adaptive strategies that promoted long-term socio-ecological stability. Results will advance anthropological theories about collective action in pre-state societies while establishing a reusable computational workflow for analyzing sparse archaeological records through simulation-based hypothesis testing. The requested allocation of 200,000 CPU-hours and GPU-accelerated nodes will enable statistically robust exploration of parameter spaces that are computationally intractable on local workstations, directly supporting peer-reviewed publications and open-source model releases to the anthropological research community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Anthropology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of automating the extraction and coding of complex clinical information from unstructured electronic health record (EHR) narratives, a process currently limited by manual inefficiencies and inconsistencies. Traditional natural language processing (NLP) methods struggle with the syntactic variability, contextual ambiguity, and domain-specific jargon inherent in clinical notes, leading to suboptimal accuracy in tasks such as phenotype identification, treatment outcome documentation, and compliance with evolving billing code standards (e.g., ICD-11). We propose developing a transformer-based multimodal deep learning framework that integrates textual narratives with structured EHR data (laboratory results, medication orders) and temporal patient trajectories to improve contextual interpretation. The computational approach will involve pre-training language models on a curated corpus of 10 million deidentified clinical notes across 15 medical specialties, followed by federated fine-tuning to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these large models, processing heterogeneous data streams at scale, and conducting parallelized hyperparameter optimization to balance accuracy with computational efficiency. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive clinical information extraction, validated against manually curated gold-standard datasets, capable of reducing coding errors by ≥40% in pilot deployments. The project will further generate novel benchmarks for evaluating context-aware NLP in specialized clinical domains such as rare disease documentation and post-market medical device surveillance. By advancing scalable methods to transform unstructured narratives into computable data, this work aims to enhance the fidelity of medical records for precision medicine initiatives and real-world evidence generation while maintaining alignment with evolving healthcare data governance standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: The development of treatment resistance in solid tumors remains a critical challenge in oncology, driven by heterogeneous cellular responses to therapy within dynamic tumor microenvironments. This project seeks to elucidate how spatially organized metabolic interactions and mechanical stresses in tumor tissue contribute to the emergence of resistant cancer cell subpopulations. We propose a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling with continuum biomechanical simulations to map the evolution of treatment resistance in physiologically representative tumor systems. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve interactions between 10^5–10^6 individual cell agents while concurrently modeling oxygen/nutrient diffusion, extracellular matrix remodeling, and interstitial fluid pressure across millimeter-scale domains. The hybrid approach will parameterize cancer cell phenotypes using experimental data from 3D-bioprinted tumor models subjected to variable hypoxia and chemotherapy exposure. Simulations will predict how regional variations in metabolic activity and cytoskeletal adaptation influence the selection of pro-survival mutations during treatment cycles. Expected outcomes include identifying microenvironmental triggers that accelerate resistant clone expansion and quantifying the impact of tumor spatial architecture on drug penetration efficiency. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of therapy failure in heterogeneous cancers while providing a predictive platform to optimize combination treatment schedules targeting both biochemical and biomechanical drivers of resistance. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source tools for testing adaptive therapeutic strategies in physiologically relevant contexts.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanisms underlying human disease. Includes instruction in the causes and nature of disease processes in animals and humans at the molecular, cellular, tissue, organ and organ systems level, tissue structure and function, cellular mechanisms of disease and organ systems response to disease.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of information diffusion and polarization in digital media ecosystems using advanced computational modeling, with a focus on understanding how algorithmic mediation shapes collective discourse. As digital platforms increasingly influence public opinion and social behavior, traditional communication theories struggle to account for the scale, speed, and nonlinearity of modern information flows. The research problem centers on identifying key mechanisms—such as echo chamber formation, viral misinformation spread, and platform-specific affordances—that drive divergences between online communication patterns and established theoretical frameworks. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate large-scale networked interactions, integrating natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze real-world social media datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for running parallelized simulations with millions of agent interactions, processing multi-terabyte text corpora, and training machine learning classifiers to detect rhetorical strategies in platform content. Expected outcomes include a computational framework mapping relationships between platform architectures, user behavior, and systemic outcomes like polarization amplification. This work will advance communication theory by providing empirically grounded models of digitally mediated discourse, offering insights into the sociotechnical factors that undermine consensus-building in public spheres. Results will also inform evidence-based policy recommendations for platform governance and algorithmic transparency. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration across diverse communication scenarios while maintaining computational feasibility, significantly extending the scope beyond what traditional workstation-based approaches can achieve in this interdisciplinary domain.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on theories of communication. Includes instruction in theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: Dental caries and periodontal diseases remain prevalent global health challenges, driven by pathogenic biofilms resistant to conventional antimicrobial therapies. Current experimental approaches struggle to capture the dynamic, multi-species interactions and spatial heterogeneity inherent in oral biofilms, limiting the development of effective treatments. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models elucidating biofilm resilience mechanisms and identifying targeted therapeutic strategies. We will employ molecular dynamics simulations to investigate antimicrobial agent interactions with bacterial membranes, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate community-level biofilm responses to environmental stressors. Machine learning algorithms will integrate multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic) and clinical parameters to predict biofilm virulence patterns and treatment outcomes. The computational framework will be validated against in vitro biofilm assays and patient-derived microbiological samples. By mapping genetic and metabolic pathways underpinning antimicrobial resistance, this research aims to accelerate the design of precision topical agents and optimize treatment regimens. Successful outcomes will provide a foundational platform for personalized biofilm management, reducing invasive dental procedures and systemic antibiotic use. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to manage the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations required for these multi-dimensional analyses, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local computing resources. This work aligns with translational dentistry priorities by bridging computational discovery with clinical innovation to improve oral health equity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of dentistry/dental medicine, encompassing the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, and adjacent structures and their impact on the human body and health. Includes instruction in the basic biomedical sciences, occlusion, dental health and prevention, oral pathology, cariology, operative dentistry, oral radiology, principles of the various dental specialties, pain management, oral medicine, clinic and health care management, patient counseling, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the resilience of military space systems by developing a computational framework to optimize satellite constellation configurations under adversarial conditions. Modern military operations rely on satellite networks for communications, navigation, and surveillance, yet existing tools inadequately address dynamic threats such as anti-satellite (ASAT) weapons, cyber intrusions, and signal jamming. The research problem centers on balancing operational continuity, resource efficiency, and rapid reconfigurability in contested orbital environments. To address this, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach integrated with high-fidelity orbital mechanics simulations. The computational workflow will model adversarial interactions in a simulated battlespace, incorporating realistic constraints such as fuel limitations, collision avoidance, and electromagnetic spectrum vulnerabilities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parallelize thousands of scenario iterations, train deep neural networks on heterogeneous threat data, and validate emergent constellation behaviors under varying orbital regimes and attack profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable optimization toolkit to recommend resilient satellite topologies and contingency protocols, (2) probabilistic risk assessments for different threat vectors, and (3) novel metrics for quantifying constellation survivability and mission assurance. The project bridges military strategy, astrodynamics, and machine learning, offering a paradigm shift in space systems operations planning. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the resulting models will inform next-generation satellite architectures and enhance the U.S. Department of Defense’s capacity to maintain space superiority in evolving conflict scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and operation of missiles, satellites and other space-based systems for military purposes. Includes instruction in the military applications of space, space technology, aerospace engineering, systems architecture, orbital mechanics, launch and retrieval systems, ground support systems, satellite communications, and space-based sensor systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the morphosyntactic and lexical divergence of Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian (BCS) languages in contemporary digital texts, a critical yet understudied area in South Slavic linguistics. While these languages share a high degree of mutual intelligibility, socio-political shifts since the 1990s have amplified regional standardization efforts, fostering subtle but consequential linguistic differentiation. Current scholarship lacks large-scale computational studies tracking these changes, particularly in informal digital communication (e.g., social media, forums), where language evolution is most dynamic. The research problem centers on identifying and modeling emergent patterns of divergence across dialects and registers, which traditional manual methods cannot feasibly address due to data volume and complexity. The project will employ computational linguistics techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on BCS corpora, dialectometric analysis, and diachronic word embedding alignment, to process multilingual and multidialectal text datasets spanning 2010–2024. HPC resources are essential for training custom neural models on terabytes of unstructured text, running parallelized comparative analyses across regional variants, and simulating lexical diffusion patterns using agent-based models. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible corpus of annotated digital BCS texts, 2) quantitative metrics of divergence rates across grammatical features, and 3) visualizations of dialect continua influenced by digital communication networks. This work will advance understanding of how digital spaces accelerate language standardization and differentiation, with applications in language preservation policy, machine translation for under-resourced South Slavic varieties, and educational tools for dialect navigation. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, the project bridges methodological gaps between humanities research and data science, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in tracking linguistic change within closely related language systems.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian Languages and Literatures
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bosnian, Serbian and/or Croatian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for the analysis of Slovak dialectal variation, a phenomenon increasingly threatened by linguistic homogenization. Traditional methods, limited in scale and granularity, have struggled to systematically document and model the phonetic, lexical, and syntactic diversity across Slovakia’s regional dialects. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), this study will process and analyze a corpus comprising over 10,000 hours of spoken dialect recordings and corresponding textual transcripts, spanning six major dialect groups. Computational workflows will integrate speech-to-text conversion, machine learning-based phonetic feature extraction, and geospatial clustering algorithms to map linguistic features across geographic and sociocultural contexts. The HPC environment is essential for handling the dataset’s size (≈50 TB), parallelizing feature extraction across thousands of audio files, and training neural networks for dialect classification. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of annotated Slovak dialect data, interactive visualization tools for dialect boundaries, and quantitative models correlating linguistic variation with historical migration patterns. By enabling large-scale, data-driven approaches to Slovak philology, this project aims to preserve endangered linguistic heritage while advancing methodologies for digital dialectology in under-resourced languages. Resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multilingual corpora, and high-throughput processing of audio-text alignments.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Slovak language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic resource allocation in casino operations through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the complex interplay of real-time demand forecasting, spatial logistics, and behavioral economics. Casinos face unique operational challenges due to fluctuating patron densities, heterogeneous gaming preferences, and the need to balance revenue generation with regulatory compliance and customer satisfaction. Traditional heuristic approaches fail to adapt to the nonlinear interactions between variables such as table game utilization, staffing shifts, slot machine performance analytics, and emergency egress constraints. This study proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework coupled with Monte Carlo simulations to model patron movement, spending behavior, and facility-scale resource deployment. The computational model will integrate anonymized historical gaming data, IoT-derived foot traffic patterns, and environmental sensor inputs to simulate millions of scenario permutations across a 24-hour operational cycle. Key innovations include the development of a graph neural network architecture to map interdependencies between gaming floor zones and a parallelized optimization engine for dynamically pricing table game minimums based on real-time capacity thresholds. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabyte-scale datasets from surveillance systems, player loyalty programs, and mobile app interactions while maintaining sub-minute latency for decision support outputs. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for reducing operational overhead costs by 12–18%, improving per-customer revenue through personalized incentive targeting, and enhancing compliance with gaming jurisdiction occupancy regulations. Results will advance niche applications of computational social science in hospitality management while establishing novel benchmarks for AI-driven resource allocation in constrained physical environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage casinos and gaming establishments. Includes instruction in business and financial management; casino operations; casino security and surveillance; hospitality, facilities, and personnel management; and principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Baltic languages, particularly understudied and extinct varieties such as Old Prussian and Curonian. While Baltic linguistics has made strides in philological and comparative studies, the application of advanced computational methods remains limited, hindering progress in modeling language evolution, reconstructing fragmentary textual corpora, and analyzing complex morphological systems. The primary research challenge lies in processing sparse, irregular, or non-standardized historical data at scales impractical for manual analysis, compounded by the need to train language-specific models where pre-existing tools for low-resource languages are inadequate. The proposed computational approach integrates corpus linguistics, machine learning, and phylogenetic modeling to analyze digitized texts, inscriptions, and comparative lexical datasets. Key tasks include the development of transformer-based models for automated morphological parsing of Old Prussian relics, Bayesian phylogenetic inference to refine Proto-Baltic divergence timelines, and GPU-accelerated alignment algorithms for cross-dialectal Latvian-Lithuanian semantic mapping. These methods require parallelized workflows, large-memory nodes for handling heterogeneous textual data, and sustained GPU capacity for training deep learning architectures on underrepresented languages. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated Baltic language corpora, probabilistic models for reconstructing fragmentary Curonian texts, and novel insights into language contact dynamics between Baltic and Finnic groups. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of historical linguistics data, this project aims to advance scholarly understanding of the Baltic language family’s structural diversity and historical development while establishing scalable methodologies for endangered language research. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current bottlenecks in processing speed, model training efficiency, and data integration across disparate sources, ensuring rigorous replication of results in this under-resourced domain.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of the Baltic peoples, including, but not limited to, the modern languages of Latvian and Lithuanian, and extinct languages such as Old Prussian and Curionian. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making in casino operations, focusing on real-time resource allocation, patron behavior modeling, and risk mitigation strategies. While casino operations integrate elements of hospitality, security, and logistics, existing approaches often rely on static protocols or fragmented data analysis, limiting adaptability to fluctuating demand patterns, regulatory constraints, and emerging threats such as fraud or cybersecurity risks. The project addresses this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-agent systems that model interactions between patrons, staff, gaming equipment, and surveillance infrastructure at scale. Agent-based models will integrate anonymized transaction data, video surveillance patterns, and historical incident reports to replicate casino floor dynamics under diverse operational scenarios. Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes of staffing strategies, game configuration adjustments, and emergency response protocols. Machine learning components will train on simulated and real-world datasets to predict high-risk events, such as collusion attempts or equipment malfunctions, while preserving patron privacy through synthetic data generation techniques. The computational demands of this work—including parallelized simulation of thousands of concurrent agents, real-time sensitivity analyses, and federated learning architectures—necessitate access to HPC resources with GPU-accelerated nodes and large memory capacity. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario testing in gaming environments, predictive models to balance service efficiency with regulatory compliance, and novel metrics for quantifying operational resilience. By advancing computational methods tailored to the unique constraints of casino operations, this research aims to establish a foundation for data-driven decision-making in gaming industries while addressing ethical and legal challenges specific to the domain.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on casino operations and services. Includes instruction in casino operations, casino security and surveillance, casino dealing, principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for personalized health behavior interventions by integrating heterogeneous, multi-modal datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in health sciences: the lack of scalable computational frameworks that dynamically synthesize physiological, behavioral, and environmental data to optimize individual wellness strategies. Current approaches often rely on static, population-level recommendations, which fail to account for real-time biometric variability (e.g., from wearables), contextual factors (e.g., geolocated environmental stressors), and behavioral patterns (e.g., sleep or dietary habits). To overcome this limitation, we propose an adaptive machine learning pipeline that processes streaming data from wearable devices, mobile apps, and environmental sensors to generate context-aware intervention recommendations. The computational workflow includes federated learning techniques to preserve privacy while aggregating data across participants, graph neural networks to model temporal and spatial dependencies in behavior patterns, and agent-based simulations to forecast intervention outcomes under diverse scenarios. HPC resources are essential for training large-scale models on longitudinal datasets (>100 TB) encompassing biometric, geospatial, and psychosocial variables from 10,000+ participants, as well as for running parallelized simulations of intervention efficacy. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time, personalized health optimization and novel insights into the nonlinear interactions between micro-level behaviors (e.g., activity bursts) and macro-level health outcomes (e.g., metabolic resilience). This work bridges health science, data science, and behavioral economics, offering a scalable computational foundation for precision wellness applications in community and occupational settings.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to assume roles as health/wellness professionals in private business and industry, community organizations, and health care settings. Includes instruction in personal health, community health and welfare, nutrition, epidemiology, disease prevention, fitness and exercise, and health behaviors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in organizational decision-making under complex, dynamic environments. A critical challenge in business administration lies in optimizing strategic and operational decisions when faced with incomplete information, rapidly shifting market conditions, and interdependencies among stakeholders. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the scale, nonlinearity, and stochasticity inherent in such scenarios, limiting their predictive accuracy and practical utility. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-agent simulation framework integrated with machine learning (ML) techniques to model decision-making processes across hierarchical organizational structures. The computational approach will involve large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate risk propagation, resource allocation efficiency, and emergent network behaviors under varying constraints. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be deployed to train adaptive decision policies, while graph neural networks will analyze interdependencies among departments, suppliers, and customers. The HPC environment is essential to manage the parallel processing demands of simulating thousands of agents with heterogeneous behavioral rules, as well as to support the iterative training of ML models on synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., supply chain logs, financial transaction records). Expected outcomes include actionable insights into resilience-building strategies for organizations, data-driven frameworks for real-time decision support, and scalable benchmarks for evaluating management policies. By quantifying trade-offs between centralized and decentralized decision architectures, this research aims to contribute novel methodologies to management theory while providing practitioners with tools to enhance operational agility. The project aligns with broader priorities in business administration, including sustainable resource use, crisis response optimization, and adaptive leadership strategies in volatile markets.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, organize, direct, and control the functions and processes of a firm or organization. Includes instruction in management theory, human resources management and behavior, accounting and other quantitative methods, purchasing and logistics, organization and production, marketing, and business decision-making.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in veterinary administrative workflows through the development of predictive analytics and optimization models tailored to veterinary practice operations. Veterinary administrative services face unique challenges, including dynamic client scheduling, high-volume record-keeping, and compliance with evolving regulatory and ethical standards. Traditional software solutions often lack the capacity to model complex, clinic-specific variables such as client no-show patterns, emergency case prioritization, or staff-task allocation under fluctuating caseloads. This research proposes a computational approach using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate clinic operations, analyze historical administrative data, and generate adaptive strategies for resource allocation. Large-scale datasets from anonymized veterinary practice records—spanning appointment logs, billing cycles, and staff performance metrics—will be processed using parallelized workflows to train ML classifiers predicting operational bottlenecks. ABM simulations will test hypothetical scenarios, such as the impact of telehealth integration or staff cross-training protocols, on clinic efficiency. The computational demands of processing multi-terabyte datasets and running thousands of parallel simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for veterinary administrators to optimize scheduling, reduce overhead costs, and improve compliance tracking. By translating HPC-driven insights into practical administrative decision-making frameworks, this project aims to establish a novel interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of veterinary management and computational social systems, demonstrating the untapped potential of advanced computing in non-traditional, service-oriented domains.
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to provide administrative support services in a veterinary office or animal care facility. Includes instruction in business office operations, customer service, principles of veterinary health care operations, record-keeping, veterinary terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing psychosocial interventions in athletic performance contexts. While evidence-based psychological strategies—such as mindfulness training, motivational interviewing, and team cohesion protocols—are increasingly integrated into sport settings, individual variability in intervention efficacy remains poorly understood. Current approaches often rely on static, population-level analyses that inadequately account for dynamic interactions between athletes’ neurocognitive profiles, physiological stress responses, and situational performance demands. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multimodal data streams—including biometric wearables (e.g., heart rate variability, EEG), psychometric assessments, and longitudinal performance metrics—to model athlete-specific intervention pathways. Machine learning architectures, including recurrent neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees, will be trained on a curated dataset of 5,000 athlete-seasons spanning collegiate and elite developmental leagues. Computational workflows will prioritize real-time feature extraction from heterogeneous data sources, coupled with multilevel Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty in personalized intervention recommendations. The HPC environment is critical for managing the scale of parallelized model training, particularly in simulating counterfactual outcomes under varying intervention scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for predicting individual response trajectories to performance psychology interventions, (2) mechanistic insights into neurophysiological moderators of behavior change in competitive environments, and (3) open-source tools enabling practitioners to adapt models to diverse sport contexts. By bridging counseling psychology principles with computational modeling, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for ethically enhancing athletic achievement while supporting mental well-being, directly aligning with the program’s focus on integrative, evidence-based approaches to sport behavior.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the motor, physiological, and psychosocial aspects of sport behavior. Includes instruction in applied sport psychology, clinical mental health counseling, coaching, exercise physiology, ethical performance enhancement; human development, leadership and team building, mind-body practices, neuroscience, and personality and health.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets and reconstruct demographic, social, and spatial dynamics of African-descended populations in North America and the Caribbean from the 17th to early 20th centuries. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how forced and voluntary migrations, coupled with localized community formation, shaped Black lived experiences across diasporic regions. Traditional archival methods struggle to synthesize fragmented records—such as plantation inventories, Freedmen’s Bureau documents, and census data—across geographies and time periods. This project employs computational text analysis, geospatial modeling, and network analysis to identify patterns of resilience, kinship, and mobility within these datasets. Key objectives include mapping interregional migration routes using probabilistic record linkage algorithms, simulating population distribution shifts via agent-based models, and analyzing community networks through graph-based approaches. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of digitized primary sources, many of which are unstructured or multilingual (e.g., colonial-era Spanish Caribbean records), and to run computationally intensive simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas of Black migration and settlement, quantitative frameworks for assessing the long-term impacts of displacement policies, and novel datasets linking individual and community trajectories across borders. By integrating computational methods with historiographical inquiry, this work aims to advance scholarly understanding of diasporic connectivity and provide scalable tools for analyzing marginalized voices in archival materials. The results will directly support curriculum development in African-American history and inform public history initiatives focused on reparative documentation practices.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the existence, regularity, and stability properties of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in mathematical physics, particularly those governing high-dimensional wave propagation and quantum dynamical systems. Traditional analytical techniques for such problems often encounter significant obstacles due to the complexity of solution spaces and the presence of non-local interactions. To address these challenges, we propose a computational framework leveraging spectral Galerkin methods combined with adaptive wavelet discretizations, which are uniquely suited to capture multiscale phenomena and singular structures inherent in these equations. The implementation of this approach necessitates high-performance computing resources due to the exponential scaling of basis functions in high dimensions and the iterative nature of solvers required for the resulting nonlinear systems. Key objectives include the development of parallel algorithms for efficient matrix assembly and solution propagation, validation of numerical results against known analytical benchmarks in lower dimensions, and exploration of conjectured solution behaviors in physically relevant regimes. The anticipated outcomes encompass rigorous numerical verification of stability criteria for critical dynamical systems, characterization of energy transfer mechanisms in nonlinear wave equations, and the establishment of scalable computational tools for functional analysis in high-dimensional settings. This work aims to bridge theoretical advancements in analysis with practical computational methodologies, offering new perspectives on longstanding problems in PDE theory while advancing the infrastructure for mathematical research in resource-intensive environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and behavior of equations, multivariate solutions, functions, and dynamic systems. Includes instruction in differential equations, variation, approximations, complex variables, integrals, harmonic analysis and wavelet theory, dynamic systems, and applications to mathematical physics.

abstract: Immunopathologic disorders, including autoimmune diseases and transplant rejection, involve complex, dynamic interactions between immune cells, signaling pathways, and host tissues that remain incompletely understood. Current clinical strategies for diagnosis and immunotherapy often lack precision due to the heterogeneous nature of these conditions and the limitations of reductionist experimental models. This project proposes to address these challenges by developing multi-scale computational models of immune dysregulation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate molecular, cellular, and systemic interactions in immunologic diseases. We will integrate single-cell RNA sequencing data from patient-derived samples, proteomic profiles of inflammatory mediators, and clinical metadata to construct agent-based models (ABMs) of autoimmune effector responses and allograft rejection dynamics. These simulations will map spatial and temporal patterns of immune cell infiltration, cytokine crosstalk, and tissue damage under varying therapeutic interventions. A parallelized computational pipeline will employ machine learning to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response from high-dimensional datasets, enabling patient stratification. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of these models, which involve >10^6 interacting cellular agents and stochastic simulations across parameter spaces encompassing genetic, epigenetic, and environmental variables. Expected outcomes include: (1) mechanistic insights into failure modes of current immunotherapies, (2) in silico optimization of combination therapies targeting checkpoint inhibitors and cytokine networks, and (3) predictive algorithms for graft survival timelines in transplant recipients. The models will be validated against longitudinal clinical datasets from collaborating transplant centers and autoimmune disease registries. By bridging molecular mechanisms with clinical phenotypes through large-scale simulation, this work aims to establish computational frameworks for personalized immunotherapy design and real-time treatment adaptation, directly addressing the program’s focus on advancing diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in immunopathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment and laboratory management of immunologic diseases. Includes instruction in diagnostic surgical pathology, management of organ transplantation and immunotherapy.

abstract: This research addresses the growing challenge of preserving urban architectural heritage in the face of rapid urbanization and climate change. Traditional conservation methods often lack the predictive capacity to anticipate structural vulnerabilities or the socio-cultural impact of environmental stressors. To bridge this gap, this project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational model integrating multi-physics simulations with socio-spatial analytics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the team will create dynamic 3D reconstructions of heritage sites, incorporating material decay algorithms, microclimate data, and human interaction patterns derived from IoT sensors and historical archives. Machine learning techniques will identify risk thresholds for degradation processes, while agent-based modeling will simulate long-term usage scenarios under varying urban development policies. The computational framework will enable real-time visualization of preservation trade-offs, balancing structural integrity with cultural functionality. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive toolkit for architects and urban planners, offering evidence-based strategies for adaptive reuse and risk mitigation. By fusing computational engineering with architectural theory and ethnographic data, this project advances a novel methodology for heritage stewardship, positioning HPC as a critical tool in culturally sustainable design. The resource allocation will support large-scale parallel processing of LiDAR datasets, finite element analysis across heterogeneous materials, and training deep neural networks on architectural pattern recognition—tasks infeasible without dedicated HPC infrastructure. This work pioneers a non-engineering application of computational resources in architecture, establishing a precedent for data-driven cultural preservation in the Anthropocene era.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Woodworking practices have historically relied on empirical methods to predict material behavior, optimize toolpaths, and ensure structural integrity in finished products. However, the anisotropic nature of wood, coupled with variable environmental factors like humidity and temperature, introduces complex nonlinear dynamics that challenge traditional trial-and-error approaches. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model wood deformation, stress distribution, and tool interaction at unprecedented resolution, enabling data-driven design and manufacturing processes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to capture multi-scale mechanical responses in wood under varying grain orientations, moisture levels, and machining forces. These simulations will integrate machine learning models trained on experimental datasets—including digital image correlation measurements and CNC machining telemetry—to predict optimal cutting parameters, minimize material waste, and prevent tool wear. The computational workflow will also couple hygrothermal models with structural analyses to assess long-term durability of joinery systems under cyclic environmental loads. By parallelizing these resource-intensive simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to generate a parametric library of material performance profiles applicable to furniture design, architectural components, and heritage restoration. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation tools tailored to woodworking education, a decision-support system for sustainable material selection, and predictive metrics to reduce energy consumption in kiln-drying processes. This research bridges gaps between traditional craftsmanship and computational engineering, offering scalable methodologies to preserve material resources while advancing precision in wood-based manufacturing.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to lay out and shape stock; assemble wooden articles or subassemblies; mark, bind, saw, carve, and sand wooden products; repair wooden articles, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: The increasing reliance on space-based systems for military operations necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize the resilience and adaptability of satellite constellations in contested environments. This project addresses the challenge of dynamically allocating limited on-orbit resources—such as fuel, sensor time, and communication bandwidth—across distributed satellite networks during multi-domain conflicts. Traditional static scheduling methods fail to account for real-time threats, evolving mission priorities, and unpredictable system degradation, creating vulnerabilities in critical space infrastructure. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning-driven decision framework powered by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational approach integrates reinforcement learning (RL) agents trained on high-fidelity simulations of orbital mechanics, electronic warfare scenarios, and adversarial action patterns. These agents will operate within a federated learning architecture to preserve security while enabling collective adaptation across classified and unclassified systems. Key technical hurdles include modeling microsecond-scale signal propagation delays in distributed satellite networks and simulating emergent behaviors in large-scale constellation interactions—tasks requiring parallelized GPU-accelerated computations and petascale memory bandwidth. Expected outcomes include a validated resource allocation engine capable of generating contingency plans 40-60% faster than existing optimization solvers under tested threat profiles, as well as novel metrics for quantifying constellation-wide resilience. The resulting framework will provide military operators with AI-assisted tools to maintain space domain awareness and prioritize assets during degraded operations. By bridging gaps between astrodynamics, autonomous systems, and tactical decision-making, this research advances computational methodologies for next-generation space command-and-control systems while adhering to strict operational security constraints. Successfully demonstrating this approach could inform future standards for responsive space operations across allied militaries.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and operation of missiles, satellites and other space-based systems for military purposes. Includes instruction in the military applications of space, space technology, aerospace engineering, systems architecture, orbital mechanics, launch and retrieval systems, ground support systems, satellite communications, and space-based sensor systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Mongolian language studies, addressing critical gaps in scalable analysis of the language’s philological complexity, dialectal diversity, and literary heritage. Despite its rich linguistic and cultural significance, Mongolian remains understudied in computational contexts due to its agglutinative morphology, dialect variations, and limited digital corpora. The research aims to develop and apply computational models to analyze historical and contemporary Mongolian texts, oral narratives, and regional dialects, enabling large-scale pattern recognition and linguistic feature extraction that traditional manual methods cannot achieve. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for morphological segmentation, dialect classification using deep neural networks, and semantic analysis of classical and modern literary works. Additionally, the project will employ parallelized algorithms to reconstruct phonetic shifts in regional dialects and simulate language evolution across historical periods. By processing terabytes of digitized manuscripts, audio recordings, and modern publications, the HPC infrastructure will accelerate corpus construction, annotation, and cross-referencing, while ensuring reproducibility through containerized workflows. Anticipated outcomes include open-access datasets, computational tools tailored for Mongolian NLP, and novel insights into the structural evolution of Mongolian literature. This work will directly support interdisciplinary scholarship in linguistics, cultural preservation, and digital humanities, while fostering collaborations with Mongolian-speaking communities to enhance language technologies for education and heritage conservation. The requested resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive workloads and reduce runtime bottlenecks, enabling scalable analysis that aligns with the program’s mission to bridge traditional scholarship with computational innovation.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Mongolian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; oral and written literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the evolutionary and neurophysiological underpinnings of cross-species behavioral variation, with a focus on decision-making strategies in social contexts. A critical gap in comparative psychology lies in quantifying how adaptive behaviors emerge from interactions between neural circuit dynamics, environmental pressures, and phylogenetic history. Traditional approaches often rely on simplified models or small datasets, limiting their capacity to disentangle these multidimensional factors. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, phylogenetically informed machine learning, and large-scale neuroethological simulations to analyze behavioral datasets spanning 50+ species, including primates, corvids, and cetaceans. HPC resources will enable (1) parallelized simulations of neural reinforcement learning mechanisms under varying ecological scenarios, (2) Bayesian comparative analyses of behavioral trait evolution across 10 million years of phylogenetic divergence, and (3) dimensionality reduction of high-resolution behavioral tracking data (≈500 TB) from collaborative field studies. The computational pipeline will employ GPU-accelerated neural networks to identify conserved patterns in reward processing across species, while Markov chain Monte Carlo methods will model evolutionary transitions in social cognition. Expected outcomes include a quantitative mapping of neurobehavioral adaptations to ecological niches, predictive models of decision-making convergence in distantly related species, and open-source tools for cross-species behavioral alignment analysis. This work will advance comparative frameworks in evolutionary psychology by bridging micro-scale neurophysiological mechanisms with macro-scale adaptive patterns, providing foundational insights into the computational principles governing behavioral diversity. Results will be disseminated through the Open Behavior Project repository, fostering collaboration across neuroethology and computational psychology communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the behavior of members of particular species or groups and the relationship of the behaviors of the species or group to their evolutionary origins. Includes instruction in differential psychology, experimental and physiological psychology, psychopharmacology, psychology of individual differences, reinforcement theory, and neurophysiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize medication administration protocols and predict adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in elderly patients, a population particularly vulnerable to polypharmacy and complex therapeutic regimens. Medication aides, tasked with administering medications and monitoring patient responses, require evidence-based tools to mitigate risks and enhance decision-making in real-time clinical settings. However, existing protocols often lack personalization and rely on static guidelines, which fail to account for dynamic patient-specific factors such as fluctuating vital signs, comorbidities, and drug-drug interactions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets and simulate pharmacodynamic responses across diverse patient profiles. Machine learning models, including ensemble classifiers and recurrent neural networks, will be trained on multi-modal data (e.g., vital signs, medication histories, laboratory results) to identify high-risk ADR patterns and predict individual patient tolerances. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model drug-receptor interactions for commonly administered medications, enabling mechanistic insights into toxicity thresholds. The computational pipeline will integrate these approaches to generate adaptive dosing recommendations and risk-alert systems tailored to real-world scenarios encountered by medication aides. By utilizing HPC capabilities for parallelized model training and large-scale parameter optimization, this project aims to deliver a scalable, open-source toolkit that enhances medication safety protocols, informs educational curricula for medication aide training programs, and reduces preventable healthcare complications. Outcomes will be validated through collaboration with clinical partners, with potential applicability to nursing homes, assisted living facilities, and home healthcare settings where medication aides operate.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed medications; observe and report patient reactions and side effects; and perform related emergency and recording duties under the supervision of nurses and/or physicians. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, common medications and their effects, taking vital signs, oxygen administration, medication administration and application, record-keeping, and patient observation.

abstract: Coastal marine ecosystems are increasingly threatened by eutrophication-driven hypoxia and harmful algal blooms (HABs), yet predictive understanding of these phenomena remains limited by the complex interplay of physical, chemical, and biological processes across multiple scales. This project seeks to advance high-resolution, coupled modeling of coastal biogeochemical dynamics in the context of climate-driven changes in nutrient loading, stratification, and microbial community interactions. We propose to develop and validate a novel three-dimensional model integrating hydrodynamic circulation (via the Regional Ocean Modeling System), nutrient transport, and trait-based microbial community dynamics, with a focus on nitrogen cycling pathways and phytoplankton functional groups implicated in HAB formation. The computational demands of resolving sub-kilometer spatial gradients, diel-scale biogeochemical cycling, and ensemble simulations under multiple climate scenarios necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Key objectives include (1) quantifying feedbacks between microbial metabolism and water column redox conditions in seasonally hypoxic systems, (2) assessing how altered precipitation regimes modulate land-to-ocean dissolved organic matter fluxes and heterotrophic community responses, and (3) evaluating cross-scale interactions between turbulent mixing processes and dinoflagellate vertical migration strategies. Simulations will leverage existing observational datasets from long-term monitoring arrays and autonomous underwater vehicles in the Mid-Atlantic Bight, with model-data fusion techniques applied to constrain uncertain parameters. The requested allocation of 500,000 CPU-hours on a parallelized computing cluster will enable multi-year hindcast experiments and scenario analyses at unprecedented spatial resolution (<500 m grid). Anticipated outcomes include improved probabilistic forecasts of hypoxic zone extent and HAB initiation thresholds, with direct applications to coastal management strategies addressing nutrient pollution and climate adaptation. By explicitly resolving microbial functional diversity within a dynamic physical framework, this work aims to advance fundamental understanding of coastal ecosystem resilience while providing decision-support tools for water quality agencies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of biology, chemistry, geology and physics applied to marine, estuarine and coastal environments. Includes instruction in marine biogeochemistry, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, coastal ecology, coastal ocean processes, microbial ecology, marine ecosystem modeling, and polar microbiology.

abstract: Dental pathologies, such as periodontitis and peri-implantitis, are driven by complex microbial communities that interact dynamically with host immune responses. Traditional culture-based and low-resolution sequencing methods fail to capture the spatial organization, metabolic cross-talk, and strain-level diversity of these biofilms, limiting mechanistic insights into disease progression and treatment resistance. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omic datasets from clinical oral biofilm samples, integrating metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and host immunoproteomics data. We aim to resolve strain-specific virulence pathways, predict microbial community resilience under antimicrobial stress, and identify host-microbe interaction networks that exacerbate tissue destruction. Computational workflows will include customized pipelines for hybrid assembly of nanopore and Illumina sequencing data, GPU-accelerated phylogenetic inference, and agent-based modeling of biofilm dynamics under simulated treatment conditions. Machine learning models trained on longitudinal patient data will stratify disease subtypes based on microbial signatures and predict therapeutic outcomes. The scale of data—terabytes of sequencing reads, hyperspectral imaging of biofilm matrices, and single-cell proteomic profiles—necessitates cluster-based parallel processing and large-memory nodes for in silico reconstruction of community metabolic networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of oral biofilm genomic and functional annotations, (2) predictive algorithms to guide personalized debridement and antimicrobial therapies, and (3) mechanistic insights into treatment-refractory biofilm phenotypes. By bridging clinical dentistry with scalable computational biology, this work will establish a framework for precision oral microbiome engineering, directly informing next-generation diagnostic tools and targeted interventions for complex dental infections.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program that generally prepares dentists in one or more of the oral sciences and advanced/graduate dentistry specialties.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern software systems, particularly in safety-critical domains such as autonomous systems and cybersecurity, demands rigorous methods for ensuring reliability and performance under dynamic conditions. Current software verification and validation (V&V) approaches struggle to scale with the combinatorial explosion of states in heterogeneous, distributed systems, leading to incomplete testing and latent vulnerabilities. This project proposes the development of a hybrid computational framework integrating symbolic model checking, probabilistic simulations, and machine learning-driven test generation to address these challenges. The framework will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize state-space exploration, optimize fault injection campaigns, and train neural networks for predictive analysis of system behavior under edge-case scenarios. Key computational components include distributed memory parallelism for scaling bounded model checking across thousands of cores, GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations for reliability estimation, and federated learning techniques to handle proprietary subsystem models. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for adaptive test suite generation, quantitative benchmarks comparing computational efficiency against traditional V&V methods, and open-source tooling extensions for widely used verification frameworks. The research will directly contribute to improving the safety assurance of software-dependent infrastructure while advancing methodologies for computational resource allocation in large-scale software engineering tasks. By enabling exhaustive analysis of systems with >10^8 possible states, this work addresses critical gaps in scalable software certification processes, with applications to autonomous vehicle control stacks and secure distributed ledger architectures. Resource requests emphasize GPU nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory CPU nodes for symbolic reasoning tasks, with proposed scalability studies targeting 90% parallel efficiency on 512-node clusters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, analysis, verification, validation, implementation, and maintenance of computer software systems using a variety of computer languages. Includes instruction in discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, computer science, managerial science, and applications to complex computer systems.

abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of legal documentation present significant challenges for legal support services, particularly in public interest law and resource-constrained environments. Traditional methods of manual review and categorization struggle to manage the scale of case law, statutory texts, and litigation records, leading to delays in legal research and reduced accessibility for practitioners. This project proposes the development of an automated framework leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to analyze legal texts at scale, aiming to identify precedential patterns, predict case outcomes, and streamline document triage. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on a corpus of over 10 million legal documents, including court opinions, motions, and administrative rulings. Computational workflows will focus on distributed training of domain-specific language models, graph-based analysis of citation networks, and ensemble methods for outcome prediction. Key challenges include addressing the low-resource nature of legal subdomains (e.g., immigration appeals, tenant rights) and ensuring interpretability of model outputs for legal practitioners. The expected outcomes include open-source tools for semantic search and case similarity assessment, as well as a public dataset of annotated legal decisions. This work will directly enhance the capacity of legal aid organizations to prioritize cases, allocate resources efficiently, and identify systemic trends in jurisprudence. By bridging computational linguistics and legal informatics, the project establishes a framework for scalable analysis of legal systems while maintaining ethical standards for data privacy and algorithmic transparency. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the necessary model performance within practical timeframes, enabling real-world deployment to support access to justice initiatives.
cip_definition: Any program in legal support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of Latin language evolution and literary traditions across key historical periods, including Classical, Late Antique, Medieval, and Ecclesiastical Latin. The central challenge lies in analyzing vast, heterogeneous textual corpora—spanning secular, theological, and administrative genres—to trace linguistic shifts, stylistic developments, and intercultural influences over two millennia. Traditional philological methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these materials, particularly when addressing understudied areas such as regional dialect variation, non-standard orthography in manuscript traditions, and the interplay between Latin and vernacular languages. The project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and corpus linguistics techniques. Customized pipelines will be developed to handle morphological analysis of irregular verb forms, syntactic parsing of late antique legal texts, and semantic modeling of theological treatises. Multilayer neural networks will train on annotated datasets to identify stylistic markers differentiating Classical and Medieval Latin authorship, while graph-based algorithms will map lexical borrowing between Latin and co-existing Italic dialects. HPC resources are critical for processing digitized incunabula and manuscripts with variable OCR accuracy, running parallelized comparisons across 10,000+ texts in the Patrologia Latina and other key corpora, and simulating language change through agent-based models. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible diachronic Latin lexicon with frequency metrics, new quantitative frameworks for dating anonymous ecclesiastical documents, and visualizations of literary influence networks in medieval Europe. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to redefine methodological paradigms in philology while preserving endangered digital heritage. The requested allocation will directly support 30+ researchers across six institutions collaborating on multilingual text analysis workflows, with findings disseminated through open-access tools and interdisciplinary publications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Latin language and literature from its origins through its decline and its current ecclesiastical usage, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, related Italic dialects, Late Roman and Medieval Latin, and modern Church Latin.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for educators working with young children (ages 0–5) with disabilities in early childhood special education (ECSE) settings. A critical challenge in ECSE is designing individualized instructional strategies that account for the heterogeneous developmental trajectories, sensory processing profiles, and communication needs of children with disabilities. Traditional approaches rely on manual observation and static assessment tools, which struggle to capture dynamic learning patterns or provide real-time feedback for educators. To address this gap, we propose creating computational models that simulate child-teacher interactions under varied instructional scenarios, integrating multimodal data from wearable sensors, video recordings, and structured assessments. These simulations will train machine learning algorithms to predict optimal intervention timing, modality (e.g., visual vs. tactile cues), and complexity based on individual learner profiles. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (e.g., motion-tracking data from classroom activities) and running iterative, agent-based models of learning behaviors. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating personalized ECSE lesson plans, validated against empirical data from partner preschool programs. This work will provide educators with evidence-based, scalable tools to improve responsiveness to neurodiverse learners while reducing planning burdens. By aligning computational modeling with early childhood pedagogy, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for special education research that bridges developmental theory, classroom practice, and emergent technologies.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Early Childhood Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to infant and pre-school age children with special learning needs or disabilities, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale comparative analyses of syntactic, semantic, and stylistic patterns across understudied modern languages and their literary traditions. While computational methods have transformed linguistic and literary research, their application remains disproportionately focused on widely spoken languages, leaving regional and minority languages underrepresented in digital scholarship. This gap limits our understanding of global linguistic diversity and its cultural intersections. To address this, our research will employ parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze multilingual corpora spanning 15+ languages, including Indigenous and diasporic varieties, with a focus on morphosyntactic variation, dialectal evolution, and cross-cultural narrative structures. The computational workflow integrates transformer-based models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, geospatial-temporal mapping of dialect features, and graph-based network analysis to trace literary influence across linguistic boundaries. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models, processing terabytes of digitized texts and speech data, and simulating language-contact scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include: (1) novel frameworks for quantifying stylistic and structural convergence in multilingual literature, (2) open-access tools for automated analysis of under-resourced languages, and (3) high-resolution visualizations of dialect boundaries correlated with sociocultural factors. By enabling computationally intensive, cross-linguistic comparisons at unprecedented scale, this project will provide foundational insights into language preservation, the diffusion of literary forms, and the role of technology in sustaining linguistic diversity. Results will be disseminated through an interactive platform for collaborative humanities research, fostering interdisciplinary partnerships between computational linguists, literary scholars, and language communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more modern foreign languages that is not specific as to the name of the language(s) studied; that is otherwise undifferentiated; or that introduces students to language studies at the basic/elementary level.

abstract: Aquaculture systems face critical challenges in optimizing production efficiency while ensuring environmental sustainability, particularly in managing disease outbreaks, nutrient dynamics, and water quality under varying environmental conditions. Current empirical approaches to these challenges are resource-intensive and often fail to capture the complex, nonlinear interactions between biological, chemical, and physical factors in aquaculture environments. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution computational modeling framework to simulate multi-scale processes in aquaculture systems, integrating hydrodynamics, nutrient transport, fish behavior, and pathogen dynamics. The research will employ coupled agent-based models (ABMs) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to represent individual fish interactions, population-level responses, and water flow patterns in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) and open-water net pen environments. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate models using historical production data and sensor-derived water quality metrics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatiotemporal variability across systems, particularly for parallelized simulations of large-scale aquaculture operations over multi-year production cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize stocking densities, feeding regimes, and water treatment protocols under climate variability; identify early warning signals for disease transmission; and evaluate infrastructure designs for energy-efficient operations. The models will be validated against experimental datasets from partner aquaculture facilities. By enabling data-driven decision-making, this work aims to advance precision aquaculture practices, reduce economic losses from disease, and minimize environmental impacts. The resulting open-source computational tools will provide a scalable platform for researchers and industry stakeholders to test management strategies in silico, accelerating the development of resilient aquaculture systems to meet global food security demands.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to select, culture, propagate, harvest, and market domesticated fish, shellfish, and marine plants, both freshwater and saltwater. Includes instruction in the basic principles of aquatic and marine biology; health and nutrition of aquatic and marine life; design and operation of fish farms, breeding facilities, culture beds, and related enterprises; and related issues of safety, applicable regulations, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate machine learning-driven adaptive learning environments tailored for computer science education, addressing the critical challenge of student engagement and knowledge retention in heterogeneous classrooms. Despite advancements in pedagogical strategies, many computer science curricula struggle to accommodate varying student backgrounds, learning paces, and problem-solving aptitudes. To address this, we propose creating a dynamic framework that leverages real-time analytics and personalized content delivery, powered by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will utilize large-scale educational datasets—including student interaction logs, code submission patterns, and assessment results—to train deep reinforcement learning models that optimize instructional pathways. Computational workflows will involve parallelized hyperparameter tuning for neural networks, clustering algorithms to identify learning style archetypes, and agent-based simulations to model classroom-scale interventions. The project’s HPC requirements stem from the need to process multi-terabyte datasets, execute thousands of concurrent simulation instances, and iteratively refine generative AI models for automated feedback generation. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for adaptive computer science instruction, validated through A/B testing across virtual and in-person classrooms, and a corpus of computational teaching strategies deployable via open-source tools. This work will advance computational pedagogy by establishing data-driven methods to reduce achievement gaps in programming literacy while providing teacher training institutions with evidence-based frameworks for curriculum design. The requested resources will enable rapid prototyping of ensemble models and sensitivity analyses, which are computationally prohibitive on local infrastructure, ensuring statistically robust conclusions about the efficacy of adaptive systems in diverse educational settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach computer education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the coevolution of biomechanical and biochemical signaling in hybrid biological-physical systems, focusing on the self-organization of synthetic cell-matrix composites under dynamic environmental stimuli. This project bridges evolutionary developmental biology, soft matter physics, and nonlinear dynamical systems to address a critical gap in understanding how spatially heterogeneous mechanical forces and chemical gradients jointly govern emergent multicellular patterning in artificial tissues.
