The central challenge lies in modeling multiscale feedback loops—where subcellular signaling cascades influence macroscopic matrix remodeling, which in turn alters local stress fields and nutrient diffusion—a process requiring high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations of coupled reaction-diffusion-advection systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement hybrid computational frameworks combining lattice Boltzmann methods for fluid-structure interactions, agent-based models for cellular decision-making, and finite element analysis for continuum-scale mechanics. Unique algorithmic developments will focus on adaptive mesh refinement to capture boundary instabilities at cell-matrix interfaces and machine learning-accelerated parameter optimization for rare-event sampling. Expected outcomes include predictive models of synthetic morphogenesis in mechanically active biomaterials, with applications to programmable tissue engineering and adaptive soft robotics. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scaling to simulate >10^6 interacting cellular agents within viscoelastic matrices across physiologically relevant timescales (hours-days). By establishing open-source simulation tools for this emerging interdisciplinary niche, the project aims to catalyze convergence between developmental biology, active matter physics, and synthetic biology communities, while providing benchmark datasets for data-driven discovery of universal principles in hybrid living-nonliving systems.
cip_definition: A program that is either a general synthesis of one or more of the biological and physical sciences, or a specialization which draws from the biological and physical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize training protocols and care delivery workflows for nursing assistants and patient care aides, addressing critical gaps in personalized skill development and patient safety. Nursing assistants face dynamic challenges in clinical settings, including variable patient acuity, time-sensitive tasks, and the need to adapt to evolving care guidelines. Existing training models often rely on static simulations or aggregated population data, which may not capture the complex, real-time decision-making required in practice. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that integrates multimodal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), motion-tracking sensors, and environmental inputs—to model patient-caregiver interactions at scale. Agent-based modeling will simulate diverse clinical scenarios (e.g., mobility assistance, infection control, emergency response) while machine learning algorithms trained on historical EHRs and adverse event reports will predict risk factors for patient injury or procedural errors. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of sensor data, running parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, and optimizing neural networks for real-time feedback in virtual training environments. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying high-risk care contexts, (2) dynamically adaptable training modules tailored to individual learner performance, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for staffing ratios and task prioritization. By linking computational outputs to measurable reductions in patient falls, pressure injuries, and caregiver burnout, this work will directly support the program’s mission to advance nursing aide education while improving healthcare equity. The requested resources will enable scaling to multi-institution datasets, ensuring generalizability across diverse care settings.
cip_title: Nursing Assistant/ Aide and Patient Care Assistant/ Aide
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine nursing-related services to patients in hospitals or long-term care facilities, under the training and supervision of a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized athletic training regimens through the integration of biomechanical modeling, physiological data analytics, and machine learning. Current training programs often rely on generalized protocols that fail to account for individual variability in biomechanics, metabolic responses, and recovery dynamics, leading to suboptimal performance gains and heightened injury risks. To address this gap, the research proposes a computational framework that synthesizes motion capture data, wearable sensor outputs, and physiological biomarkers to model athlete-specific adaptations in real time. The core computational challenge involves simulating high-dimensional interactions between musculoskeletal dynamics, tissue stress responses, and metabolic load distributions across diverse athlete profiles. Agent-based modeling will be employed to replicate population-level training outcomes, while deep reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize individualized exercise prescriptions by iteratively balancing performance targets with injury risk thresholds. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations, enabling parallel processing of heterogeneous datasets and reducing latency in model training and validation. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive toolset for coaches and sports scientists to design dynamically adaptive training programs, alongside open-source computational workflows that bridge gaps between sports science and data-driven decision-making. By quantifying previously intractable relationships between training variables and athlete outcomes, this work aims to establish a foundational platform for precision sports science, with potential applications in rehabilitation, talent development, and injury prevention across amateur and elite athletic populations.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Sports, Kinesiology, and Physical Education/ Fitness, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on activities and principles that promote physical fitness, achieve and maintain athletic prowess, and accomplish related research and service goals. Includes instruction in human movement studies, motivation studies, rules and practice of specific sports, exercise and fitness principles and techniques, basic athletic injury prevention and treatment, and organizing and leading fitness and sports programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for analyzing cross-jurisdictional legal decision-making patterns, with a focus on resolving conflicts between civil law and common law traditions in transnational commercial arbitration. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven methodologies to systematically compare judicial reasoning across legal systems, particularly in cases involving harmonized international statutes but divergent interpretive practices. Traditional comparative law approaches rely on manual case analysis, limiting the scope and generalizability of insights, especially as global legal datasets grow in volume and complexity. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for legal corpora, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on multilingual case law from 25 jurisdictions. Computational workflows will map argumentation structures, citation networks, and semantic patterns in judicial opinions, while clustering algorithms identify latent doctrinal divergences not apparent through qualitative review alone. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models on terabyte-scale legal texts and running iterative simulations of hypothetical arbitration scenarios based on extracted reasoning templates. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access repository of annotated transnational arbitration decisions, (2) a predictive model quantifying the influence of home jurisdiction legal traditions on arbitral outcomes, and (3) visualization tools for interactively exploring systemic biases in procedural fairness norms. By enabling large-scale empirical analysis of legal epistemology, this work aims to provide policymakers and arbitral institutions with evidence-based strategies for reducing forum shopping incentives and improving the coherence of cross-border dispute resolution mechanisms. The computational infrastructure developed will establish a foundation for subsequent AI-assisted comparative law research in understudied areas of private international law.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of legal systems and philosophies in comparative perspective.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance technology teacher education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and evaluate immersive, simulation-based pedagogical tools for industrial arts training. A critical challenge in preparing educators for technology and industrial arts instruction is the limited access to scalable, safe, and cost-effective environments where trainees can engage with complex tools, machinery, and manufacturing processes. Traditional methods often rely on physical workshops, which are constrained by space, safety risks, and resource availability. To address this, we propose the creation of a computational platform that integrates physics-based simulations, 3D modeling, and machine learning to replicate industrial tools and workflows in a virtual environment. The platform will enable teacher candidates to design, test, and troubleshoot technical projects—such as automated systems or material fabrication processes—while receiving real-time feedback on pedagogical strategies and technical decisions. HPC resources will be essential for running large-scale parallel simulations of mechanical systems, optimizing finite element analyses for material behavior, and training adaptive AI models to assess trainee performance. The computational workflow will utilize open-source frameworks like Gazebo for robotic simulations and PyTorch for skill-assessment algorithms, with validation against empirical data from partner K-12 schools. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible repository of modular simulation scenarios tailored to industrial arts curricula and a comparative analysis of simulation-based versus traditional training methods. By bridging the gap between theoretical instruction and hands-on practice, this project aims to improve the readiness of technology educators to teach advanced manufacturing, engineering design, and applied STEM concepts in diverse classroom settings. The scalability of the platform will also support future research on adaptive learning technologies in vocational and technical education.
cip_title: Technology Teacher Education/ Industrial Arts Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach technology education/industrial arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of biomechanical efficiency and injury prevention in student-athletes, a critical area within physical education teaching and coaching. Current pedagogical approaches often rely on generalized movement templates, which may not account for individual variability in physiology, motor skill development, or real-time performance dynamics. The research problem centers on developing personalized coaching frameworks through computational modeling of athletic movements, integrating multi-modal data from wearable sensors, motion capture systems, and video analysis. A key challenge lies in processing large, heterogeneous datasets to identify patterns in technique, load distribution, and injury risk factors across diverse populations. The proposed computational approach combines machine learning models—including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for video-based pose estimation and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for temporal movement analysis—with biomechanical simulations to model joint stresses and muscle activation under varying training conditions. These models will be trained on datasets encompassing youth, collegiate, and amateur athletes across multiple sports, requiring parallelized processing capabilities to handle high-dimensional data streams. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize skill acquisition protocols, reduce overuse injuries, and dynamically adapt training loads based on real-time feedback. The project will also generate open-access datasets and visual analytics modules to support evidence-based coaching practices in physical education curricula. By bridging computational analytics with practical teaching methodologies, this work aims to transform how educators individualize instruction, enhance student-athlete performance, and address equity gaps in access to advanced training resources. The scale of data processing and complexity of multi-physics simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically relevant latency and accuracy thresholds.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physical education programs and/or to coach sports at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of family health outcomes, addressing gaps in personalized care strategies for family practice nursing. Family health dynamics are shaped by complex, interdependent variables—including genetic predispositions, socio-environmental factors, and longitudinal health behaviors—that challenge traditional analytical methods. Current approaches often fail to integrate these multi-dimensional datasets at scale, limiting the ability to forecast risks or optimize interventions for diverse family structures. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework that combines machine learning (ML) and network analysis to model family health trajectories. The project will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from primary care systems, merged with publicly available socio-economic and environmental data, to train predictive algorithms. Key computational tasks include feature engineering for temporal health events, graph-based modeling of family relationship impacts, and simulation of intervention scenarios across synthetic family cohorts. HPC resources are critical to manage the high dimensionality of datasets, accelerate hyperparameter tuning for ML models, and enable large-scale Monte Carlo simulations assessing care pathway efficacy. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for identifying at-risk families, predicting deteriorations in chronic conditions, and recommending tailored prevention strategies. This work will directly inform clinical decision-making for nurse practitioners, bridging gaps between population-level data and individualized family care. By demonstrating the role of computational analytics in family nursing, the project aims to establish a precedent for data-driven primary care innovation while advancing methodological synergies between nursing practice and computational science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the challenge of optimizing sustainable textile design through advanced computational modeling of complex, irregular woven structures. Traditional textile design tools often rely on simplified geometric assumptions, limiting their ability to predict the performance of innovative, non-repeating patterns that incorporate recycled or biodegradable fibers with heterogeneous material properties. This project will develop and validate a high-fidelity simulation framework using finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning to model nonlinear interactions between yarn composition, weave topology, and mechanical behavior under dynamic stress conditions. The computational workflow will integrate multi-scale material datasets spanning molecular polymer dynamics, fiber-level friction coefficients, and macro-scale drape characteristics. A key innovation involves adapting graph neural networks to predict failure points in asymmetrical weave configurations informed by historical textile archives from cultural heritage collections, creating a novel bridge between traditional craft knowledge and computational design. The research requires high-performance computing resources to manage iterative simulations across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 variables, including GPU-accelerated tensor operations for real-time design feedback loops. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive model for sustainable textile engineering that reduces physical prototyping waste by 40-60%, as well as new metrics for assessing the cultural relevance of computational design outputs through embedded ethnomathematical frameworks. This work fills a critical gap in apparel research infrastructure by enabling data-driven exploration of design solutions that simultaneously address technical performance, environmental impact, and cultural preservation imperatives.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in apparel and textiles, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing the design and maintenance of civil infrastructure systems, with a focus on bridges and highway networks. A critical challenge in civil engineering technology lies in balancing structural integrity, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability under dynamic loads, material degradation, and climate variability. Current analytical tools often rely on simplified assumptions or limited datasets, which reduce their accuracy for complex, real-world scenarios. To address this gap, the research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate multiphysics interactions—including stress distribution, thermal expansion, and corrosion effects—across large-scale structural systems. High-resolution sensor data from existing infrastructure will inform model calibration, while parametric studies will evaluate the resilience of novel materials such as ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) and fiber-reinforced polymers. The computational workflow will parallelize simulations across thousands of cores to assess probabilistic failure risks under extreme weather events and traffic patterns, enabling scenario-based optimization of maintenance schedules. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for infrastructure lifecycle management, validated against laboratory-scale physical prototypes and field data. By integrating HPC capabilities, this work will provide civil engineering practitioners with data-driven tools to prioritize resource allocation, extend asset longevity, and mitigate safety risks in public works projects. The project will also train undergraduate and graduate students in computational modeling techniques, fostering workforce readiness in advanced civil engineering technologies. Results will be disseminated through open-access repositories to support replication and collaboration across institutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of civil engineers engaged in designing and executing public works projects such as highways, dams, bridges, tunnels and other facilities. Includes instruction in site analysis, structural testing procedures, field and laboratory testing procedures, plan and specification preparation, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly threatened by climate change, invasive species, and anthropogenic disturbances, necessitating advanced predictive models to inform sustainable management strategies. Current approaches often fail to capture the multi-scale interactions between forest dynamics, soil biogeochemistry, and microclimate variability due to computational limitations in resolving fine-grained ecological processes across large spatial and temporal domains. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, process-based computational model integrating forest growth, hydrology, and soil nutrient cycling using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The model will simulate forest responses to climate scenarios (RCP 4.5 and 8.5) at a 1 km² resolution across heterogeneous landscapes in the Pacific Northwest, incorporating species-specific traits, disturbance regimes, and edaphic factors. Key computational challenges include parallelizing agent-based tree population dynamics, coupling hydrological and biogeochemical submodels via scalable numerical solvers, and assimilating multi-source remote sensing data (LiDAR, hyperspectral) for parameterization. The HPC infrastructure will enable ensemble simulations spanning decadal timescales, sensitivity analyses, and Bayesian calibration against long-term forest inventory datasets. Anticipated outcomes include identifying resilient forest compositions under climate stress, quantifying carbon sequestration trade-offs in managed versus unmanaged stands, and mapping drought-induced mortality risks. This work will directly support regional conservation planning and climate adaptation policies by providing actionable projections of forest health and ecosystem services. By open-sourcing the model framework and workflows, the project will also establish a replicable computational platform for interdisciplinary forest research, bridging gaps between empirical ecology and predictive modeling. The requested resources are critical to overcoming memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in scaling ecological simulations, ensuring robust uncertainty quantification essential for stakeholder decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of one or more forest-related sciences to the study of environmental factors affecting forests and the growth and management of forest resources. Includes instruction in forest biology, forest hydrology, forest mensuration, silviculture, forest soils, water resources, environmental science, forest resources management, and wood science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of a computational framework for optimizing law enforcement investigative interview techniques through large-scale behavioral data analysis and simulation. Current interview protocols often rely on anecdotal or manually derived insights, limiting their adaptability to dynamic scenarios and diverse populations. The research problem centers on the absence of empirically validated, real-time decision-support tools that integrate psychological, linguistic, and contextual variables to guide interview strategies while adhering to legal and ethical standards. To address this gap, the project will utilize machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to analyze structured and unstructured datasets, including de-identified interview transcripts, audio-visual recordings, and case outcomes. These data will inform agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations to test hypothetical scenarios, evaluate the efficacy of interview tactics, and predict outcomes under varying conditions (e.g., suspect demographics, emotional states, or legal constraints). HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of multimodal data, training deep neural networks to detect micro-expressions and vocal stress patterns, and running parallelized ABM iterations to ensure statistical robustness. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics toolkit that identifies high-yield questioning strategies, flags cognitive biases in interviewer behavior, and generates adaptive recommendations for rapport-building or evidence disclosure. The framework will be validated against historical case data and peer-reviewed investigative protocols. By combining computational social science with law enforcement practices, this research aims to reduce investigative errors, enhance procedural fairness, and provide scalable training modules for agencies. The project bridges a specialized niche in applied computational criminology, offering a model for data-driven policy refinement without overlapping with existing disciplines such as public administration or multidisciplinary studies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, procedures, techniques, legal concerns, and problems associated with a criminal investigation. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, courtroom evidence management and preparation, case presentation and court testimony, description and identification, state and federal criminal law and procedures, informant and suspect rights, officer liability, informant and witness management, victim awareness, tactical interviewing, psychology, criminal investigation methods and procedures, report writing and documentation, investigative techniques, and case management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision manufacturing in sheet metal fabrication by developing computational models to optimize forming processes, reduce material waste, and predict structural integrity under complex loads. Traditional sheetworking methods rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is resource-intensive and limits innovation in applications such as aerospace components, architectural cladding, and energy-efficient HVAC systems. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate multi-stage forming operations, including bending, stamping, and deep drawing, using finite element analysis (FEA) with explicit material nonlinearity and contact dynamics. The computational workflow will integrate machine learning to correlate simulated stress distributions with real-world deformation data from digital image correlation (DIC) systems, enabling adaptive process parameter tuning. A key challenge lies in modeling anisotropic behavior of advanced alloys and composite laminates under high-strain-rate conditions, which demands parallelized solvers and large-scale matrix operations. The HPC resources will support parametric studies across geometric variables (e.g., flange angles, bend radii) and environmental factors (e.g., thermal gradients, tool wear), reducing physical trials by an estimated 60-75%. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for minimizing springback defects in high-strength steels, topology optimization guidelines for lightweighting aluminum components, and failure prediction models for hydroforming operations. These tools will be validated against experimental datasets from collaborating industry partners. The project’s computational outputs—including open-source simulation templates and a material property database—will directly benefit workforce training programs by integrating virtual prototyping into sheet metal technology curricula. By bridging computational mechanics with manufacturing practice, this work aims to establish a digital twin paradigm for sheetworking processes, with potential annualized cost savings of $2.1M per mid-sized fabrication facility through reduced scrap rates and energy consumption.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to form, shape, bend and fold extruded metals, including the creation of new products, using hand tools and machines such as cornice brakes, forming rolls, and squaring shears.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing STEM learning experiences for PreK-12 students by developing data-driven models to evaluate the efficacy of integrated, technology-enhanced curricula. Despite growing emphasis on interdisciplinary STEM education, educators lack robust tools to dynamically assess how combinations of pedagogical strategies, digital tools, and content sequencing influence student outcomes. Current methods rely on limited observational data and static assessments, which fail to capture the complex interactions between instructional variables and learner development. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build large-scale simulations of STEM learning environments. These simulations will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including student performance metrics, engagement analytics from educational technology platforms, and teacher-reported instructional logs—to train machine learning models capable of predicting how specific interventions affect conceptual understanding and critical thinking skills. Agent-based modeling frameworks will simulate diverse classroom scenarios, incorporating cognitive science principles to represent individual learner behaviors and social learning dynamics. The computational pipeline will employ parallelized parameter sweeps to evaluate thousands of curricular configurations, while natural language processing techniques will analyze unstructured data from student artifacts and discourse. By identifying high-impact instructional patterns across demographic contexts, this research aims to generate actionable frameworks for personalized STEM curriculum design. The outcomes will directly support teacher leadership initiatives by providing evidence-based strategies for adapting STEM integration approaches to local needs. The scalability of these models, made feasible through HPC infrastructure, offers transformative potential for addressing equity gaps in STEM education at a systems level. This work will advance both educational practice and computational methodology, establishing new paradigms for data-intensive research in science and mathematics education.
cip_title: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Educational Methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to connect education practices with scientific, engineering, and mathematical principles for PreK-12 students. Includes instruction in critical thinking, curriculum and instruction, history of STEM education, integrating STEM across curricula, learning sciences and technology, STEM education methods, and teacher leadership in STEM education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving cultural and social dynamics of Canadian identity formation through large-scale, multimodal datasets. The research focuses on understudied intersections of Indigenous and immigrant narratives in 20th-century Canadian literature, visual art, and community archives, which remain fragmented across disparate repositories. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to synthesize patterns across these heterogeneous sources, particularly when addressing spatial, temporal, and linguistic variations in cultural production. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis (English, French, and Indigenous languages in transliterated form), computer vision techniques for visual culture artifacts, and network modeling to trace cross-community influences. Key challenges include processing low-quality historical scans, aligning temporally shifting semantic contexts, and managing ethical considerations in representing Indigenous knowledge systems. HPC resources are essential for training custom transformer models on culturally specific corpora, running parallelized sentiment and thematic analyses across decades, and visualizing geotemporal diffusion patterns through interactive 3D mapping. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas of Canadian cultural intersections, quantitative frameworks for measuring narrative convergence/divergence in multicultural contexts, and methodological innovations in computationally assisted critical heritage studies. The project aims to advance interdisciplinary scholarship by bridging computational social science with humanities-driven Canadian Studies, while providing actionable insights for cultural institutions seeking to decolonize archival practices. By scaling analysis beyond isolated case studies, this work will offer new perspectives on how marginalized voices have shaped—and been shaped by—Canada’s complex identity landscapes, with implications for both academic research and public memory initiatives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Canada and its Pre-Columbian, colonial, and pre-federation predecessors, including immigrant flows and related borderlands and island groups.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the resilience and sustainability of urban infrastructure systems under multi-hazard conditions, with a focus on high-rise buildings and long-span bridges. Current design frameworks often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the nonlinear, time-dependent interactions between structural components, material degradation, and extreme loads such as earthquakes, wind, and progressive collapse scenarios. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale, multi-physics computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM), nonlinear dynamic analysis, and machine learning-driven surrogate models. The computational approach will enable high-fidelity simulations of composite steel-concrete structures subjected to stochastic load combinations, explicitly accounting for material plasticity, connection behavior, and soil-structure interaction. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated solvers for real-time parametric studies of retrofitting strategies and probabilistic risk assessments of existing infrastructure. The HPC environment is essential to process terabytes of simulation data, train neural networks for rapid damage prediction, and optimize reinforcement designs using genetic algorithms. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting failure mechanisms in aging structures, performance-based guidelines for adaptive retrofitting, and open-source tools to prioritize infrastructure investments in seismic zones. By advancing the integration of computational mechanics and data-driven methods, this work will directly inform next-generation building codes and enhance the climate adaptability of urban systems, reducing societal and economic risks associated with structural failures. The requested resources will support large-scale parallel simulations across 10,000+ CPU cores and GPU nodes, reducing computation time from weeks to days for critical disaster preparedness studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and systems used in building load-bearing structures for various purposes and in different environments, including buildings, roads, rail lines, bridges, dams, conduits, offshore platforms and work stations, and other structural shells; and the analysis of structural problems such as, failure, fabrication, safety, and natural hazards.

abstract: Musculoskeletal neoplasms present significant clinical challenges due to their heterogeneity, complex molecular landscapes, and variable responses to therapies. Current approaches to diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment optimization rely on histopathological and imaging data, which often fail to capture the dynamic interplay of genomic, proteomic, and microenvironmental factors driving tumor behavior. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating multi-omics data, longitudinal imaging, and clinical outcomes. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating predictive models of tumor progression and treatment response using machine learning algorithms trained on genomic sequencing, radiomics, and patient-specific biomechanical data, and (2) simulating the effects of combination therapies—including targeted agents, immunotherapies, and radiation—to identify optimal treatment regimens. Computational workflows will involve large-scale data harmonization, deep learning for feature extraction from histopathology slides and MRI/CT scans, and agent-based modeling of tumor-immune interactions. HPC resources are critical for managing petabytes of multimodal data, running parallelized simulations, and training complex neural networks. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early metastasis detection, patient-specific therapy recommendations, and a publicly accessible computational platform for simulating treatment scenarios. This work will advance precision oncology by enabling dynamic, data-driven decision-making, reducing trial-and-error in therapy selection, and providing a framework to accelerate translational discoveries in musculoskeletal oncology. The proposed models and tools will be validated against retrospective clinical datasets, with findings directly informing prospective trials at our institution.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal neoplasm, and the application of cancer therapy regimes.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical to sustainable power generation, yet optimizing their performance and longevity remains a challenge due to complex fluid-structure interactions, sediment erosion, and variable operational conditions. Current predictive models for turbine efficiency and structural wear often lack the resolution to account for dynamic environmental factors, leading to suboptimal maintenance schedules and unplanned downtime. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate hydroelectric turbine performance under realistic, multi-scale operating conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with discrete element modeling (DEM) to analyze turbulent flow patterns, sediment transport, and their impact on turbine blade erosion. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs and historical maintenance data to identify predictive signatures of component degradation. The computational workflow will integrate time-varying parameters such as water inflow rates, sediment concentrations, and grid demand fluctuations to generate adaptive maintenance recommendations. By validating these models against sensor data from operational hydroelectric facilities, the project aims to establish a framework for real-time predictive analytics tailored to field technicians. Expected outcomes include optimized repair timelines, extended turbine lifespan, and a 10–15% reduction in energy loss due to blade erosion. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated as open educational resources for hydroelectric technology training programs, bridging the gap between computational research and hands-on technician education. This work underscores the transformative potential of HPC in advancing both the reliability of renewable energy infrastructure and the technical proficiency of its workforce.
cip_title: Hydroelectric Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address unresolved questions in computational complexity theory, particularly the classification of problems within emerging complexity hierarchies and the limits of efficient approximation under non-standard computational models. A central focus is the theoretical and empirical analysis of quantum-inspired classical algorithms, which simulate quantum parallelism using classical resources, to evaluate their potential for bridging complexity classes such as BPP and BQP. The research problem centers on whether such simulations can achieve meaningful speedups for combinatorial optimization problems while maintaining polynomial resource bounds, a question with implications for both complexity theory and practical algorithm design. The computational approach combines formal proof techniques with large-scale simulations of algorithm families across varied input regimes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to systematically test conjectures about asymptotic behavior in high-dimensional solution spaces, where brute-force analysis becomes intractable. Custom C++/MPI code will implement parallelized simulations of adiabatic algorithmic frameworks, while SAT solvers and proof assistants (e.g., Lean 4) will automate portions of formal verification. Expected outcomes include: (1) rigorous bounds on the approximation ratios achievable by hybrid quantum-classical methods in polynomial time, (2) evidence-based refinements to the polynomial hierarchy through counterexample generation, and (3) optimized simulation pipelines for evaluating complexity-theoretic hypotheses. Results will advance foundational understanding of computation under physical constraints while providing practical benchmarks for near-term quantum algorithm research. The HPC environment is critical for managing exponential state spaces in simulation trials and enabling comparative analysis across thousands of parameterized problem instances, a scale unattainable with departmental computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computability theory, complexity theory, and the nature of computation.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance vocational home economics education by developing data-driven models to optimize curriculum design and student engagement. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, evidence-based frameworks for personalizing instruction in interdisciplinary home economics domains (e.g., nutrition science, financial literacy, sustainable resource management), which are critical for preparing students to address real-world challenges. Current pedagogical strategies often rely on static curricula that do not adapt to regional socio-economic variability, learner diversity, or emerging trends in household technologies. To address this, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal educational datasets, including anonymized student performance metrics, demographic records, and longitudinal engagement surveys from 15 U.S. states. Machine learning models (e.g., transformer-based architectures for text analysis, graph neural networks for mapping skill acquisition pathways) will be trained to identify patterns in learning barriers and resource utilization efficiency. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model classroom dynamics under varying instructional scenarios, incorporating stochastic variables such as regional policy changes and household technology adoption rates. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative model tuning, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to recommend adaptive teaching strategies for diverse learner cohorts, (2) a simulation platform for stress-testing curriculum interventions, and (3) open-access benchmarks for competency progression in family resource management. By quantifying relationships between instructional methods, contextual factors, and skill retention, this work will provide teacher educators with actionable insights to modernize pedagogical training, ultimately strengthening the pipeline of home economics instructors equipped to address 21st-century societal needs.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Home Economics Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational home economics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The emergence and spread of infectious diseases in animal populations present complex challenges to veterinary and public health systems, particularly in multi-host environments where pathogen transmission dynamics are influenced by diverse ecological and anthropogenic factors. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling disease transmission networks across heterogeneous animal and human communities, with a focus on identifying high-risk interfaces and optimizing targeted intervention strategies. Current limitations in existing epidemiological models—such as oversimplified host interactions, static environmental parameters, and an inability to integrate real-time genomic and surveillance data—hinder predictive accuracy and translational utility. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and spatially explicit simulations. The agent-based model will incorporate individual host behavior, mobility patterns, and environmental variables (e.g., land use, climate data) at scale, while deep learning architectures will analyze genomic sequencing data to detect emerging pathogen variants and transmission hotspots. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations across thousands of cores to process petabyte-scale datasets from national animal health databases, remote sensing platforms, and participatory surveillance systems. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool capable of simulating outbreak scenarios for zoonotic pathogens (e.g., avian influenza, leptospirosis) at regional resolutions, quantifying the impact of proposed vaccination or culling protocols, and informing adaptive resource allocation for veterinary public health programs. By leveraging HPC resources, this project will advance the integration of multi-modal data streams into dynamic, decision-ready models, directly supporting the One Health initiative's goal of mitigating cross-species disease risks. The resulting computational pipelines and datasets will be shared openly to strengthen collaborative research in veterinary preventive medicine and comparative epidemiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the investigation of and intervention in health and disease problems of animal and related human communities, comparative medicine, and animal public health. May included related research in biostatistics, epidemiology, environmental control, toxicology and the planning and administration of animal health programs and services.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the cascading impacts of evolving international tax regulations on global supply chain networks and corporate compliance strategies. As multinational enterprises (MNEs) navigate complex frameworks such as the OECD’s Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) 2.0 and the EU’s digital levy proposals, the interplay between heterogeneous national tax policies, cross-border transaction structures, and corporate risk mitigation tactics remains understudied. Traditional legal analysis struggles to quantify how iterative policy changes propagate through interconnected financial and operational systems, particularly under scenarios involving simultaneous regulatory shifts in multiple jurisdictions. To address this gap, the project employs agent-based modeling (ABM) and dynamic network analysis to simulate MNE decision-making processes under varying tax regimes. Computational agents will represent MNEs, tax authorities, and intermediary entities, with behavioral rules derived from empirical legal datasets, treaty texts, and case law. The simulations will integrate machine learning techniques to predict adaptive strategies, such as transfer pricing adjustments or entity reclassification, in response to hypothetical policy interventions. High-performance computing is critical to manage the scale of these simulations, which involve thousands of agents operating across multilayered networks with real-time feedback loops. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to assess the resilience of existing tax planning architectures, identify systemic vulnerabilities in global compliance ecosystems, and evaluate the second-order effects of proposed legislation. The resulting models will provide policymakers and legal practitioners with actionable insights into unintended consequences of regulatory fragmentation, while advancing computational methods for legal-economic systems analysis. This work bridges a critical methodological divide between qualitative legal scholarship and quantitative economic modeling, offering a novel toolkit for anticipatory governance in international tax law.
cip_title: International Business, Trade, and Tax Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing transnational business and commercial practices, including the specialized tax law related to international financial transactions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in optimizing the usability and accessibility of technical documentation for diverse global audiences. A critical challenge in technical and scientific communication lies in efficiently tailoring complex information to meet the needs of users with varying cultural, linguistic, and educational backgrounds. Current manual approaches to audience analysis and document testing are time-intensive and lack scalability, particularly when applied to large technical datasets or multilingual contexts. To address this gap, the proposed research will employ computational text analysis, machine learning (ML), and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to automate the identification of usability barriers in technical documents and predict audience-specific comprehension patterns. HPC resources will enable the processing of vast corpora of technical writing (e.g., engineering manuals, scientific reports, software documentation) and user feedback datasets, as well as the training of ML models to detect patterns in readability, terminology consistency, and visual-information alignment. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model user interactions with digital documentation across hypothetical scenarios, assessing how design choices affect information retention and task success rates. Outcomes will include an open-source framework for automated usability testing, predictive models for audience-centric content adaptation, and evidence-based guidelines for integrating computational tools into technical communication workflows. This research will directly contribute to the emerging field of data-driven communication design, offering scalable solutions to enhance the efficacy of scientific and technical knowledge dissemination in an increasingly globalized digital landscape. By bridging computational methods with human-centered communication practices, the project aligns with the program’s focus on advancing technical communication through interdisciplinary innovation.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the communication of technical and scientific knowledge to a variety of audiences through print, video, and digital media; and that prepares individuals to function as technical writers and editors, documentation developers, web designers, and usability specialists. Includes instruction in scientific and technical writing and editing, graphic and information design, web design, audience analysis, document usability and field testing, publications management, and applications to specific technical fields.

abstract: Climate-driven changes in ocean stratification and circulation are altering the vertical transport of dissolved carbon and oxygen, with cascading impacts on marine ecosystems and biogeochemical cycles. However, existing models struggle to resolve the multiscale interactions between turbulent mixing processes, mesoscale eddies, and basin-wide circulation patterns that govern these transports. This project seeks to advance understanding of how submesoscale to basin-scale physical dynamics modulate the ocean’s carbon sink and oxygen minimum zones through high-resolution coupled modeling. We propose to develop and validate a 3D ocean biogeochemical model with nonhydrostatic physics and adaptive mesh refinement, capable of simultaneously representing kilometer-scale turbulent mixing and basin-wide tracer advection. The model will integrate satellite-derived boundary conditions and in situ biogeochemical data from autonomous platforms to simulate carbon export, oxygen consumption, and nutrient cycling processes across critical ocean regions including the North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre and Eastern Tropical Pacific. High-performance computing resources are essential to execute ensemble simulations at 1-5 km resolution, capture intermittent mixing events, and quantify uncertainties in particle flux parameterizations. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into how altered vertical shear influences carbon sequestration efficiency, (2) improved projections of oxygen decline in boundary current systems under IPCC scenarios, and (3) open-source code enhancements for community ocean models. By bridging scale-dependent physical-chemical interactions, this work will provide actionable constraints for climate mitigation strategies and inform international ocean carbon budgeting initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemical components, mechanisms, structure, and movement of ocean waters and their interaction with terrestrial and atmospheric phenomena. Includes instruction in material inputs and outputs, chemical and biochemical transformations in marine systems, equilibria studies, inorganic and organic ocean chemistry, oceanographic processes, sediment transport, zone processes, circulation, mixing, tidal movements, wave properties, and seawater properties.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision engineering and material innovation in watchmaking and jewelry design—fields that demand micron-level accuracy and robust performance under mechanical stress. The research addresses two critical challenges: (1) simulating the long-term behavior of micro-mechanical components in timekeeping devices under dynamic operating conditions, and (2) optimizing the structural integrity and aesthetic properties of jewelry alloys and gemstone settings. Traditional experimental methods for testing these systems are constrained by material costs, fabrication time, and the inability to non-destructively analyze microscale interactions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML)-driven design optimization. FEA will model stress distribution in watch escapements, balance springs, and prong-based gemstone settings under thermal and mechanical loads, while MD simulations will investigate atomic-scale wear mechanisms in lubricant-free silicon-based gear systems. ML algorithms will iteratively refine parametric designs for jewelry clasps and ornamental patterns to maximize durability and minimize material use. These simulations require HPC resources due to the high resolution needed for submillimeter component geometries, the long timescales required to predict fatigue effects, and the combinatorial complexity of alloy compositions and gemstone arrangements. Expected outcomes include predictive models for component failure thresholds, data-driven guidelines for alloy selection in 3D-printed jewelry, and open-access simulation templates for industry use. By integrating computational materials science with traditional craftsmanship, this work aims to reduce prototyping waste, extend the lifecycle of mechanical timepieces, and enable novel design possibilities in jewelry. The project will also train students in computational tools, bridging gaps between artisanal techniques and modern engineering practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make repairs, and maintain timepieces, time-measuring devices, and jewelry items. Includes instruction in mechanical timekeeping systems, digital timekeeping systems, timesetting, casting, engraving, polishing, stonesetting, soldering, fine microscopic work, equipment and tool maintenance, redesign and restyling techniques, and customer relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the emergent dynamics of cross-kingdom signaling in synthetic microbial consortia, integrating principles from synthetic biology, ecological network theory, and non-equilibrium thermodynamics. Microbial communities drive critical biogeochemical cycles and biotechnological processes, yet their stability and functional outputs in engineered systems remain unpredictable due to complex metabolite exchange, resource competition, and stress-induced signaling between prokaryotic and eukaryotic members. Current models oversimplify cross-kingdom interactions by neglecting the role of redox-driven metabolic trade-offs and extracellular electron transfer mechanisms that couple microbial energetics to community spatial organization. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining lattice-based reaction-diffusion models, genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions, and stochastic game theory to simulate consortium assembly under dynamic nutrient gradients. The HPC environment will enable parallelized parameter sweeps across 10^4+ simulated communities, varying strain composition, metabolite diffusivity, and environmental stressor profiles. Machine learning methods will then identify phase transitions in community stability and map metabolic “cooperation bottlenecks” linked to redox imbalance. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for optimizing synthetic consortia in bioremediation and bioproduction applications, (2) a publicly accessible database of simulated cross-kingdom interaction networks, and (3) new metrics for quantifying thermodynamic efficiency in multi-domain symbioses. This work bridges molecular-scale electron flux models with ecosystem-level resilience theory, offering foundational insights for designing robust microbial technologies while advancing computational tools for interdisciplinary systems biology.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Healthcare systems face escalating demands for operational efficiency amid resource constraints, yet traditional management approaches often fail to leverage the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between patient flow, staffing patterns, and infrastructure utilization. This project proposes the development of an adaptive simulation-optimization framework to model hospital operations in real time, integrating heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records, sensor-derived equipment usage, and staff scheduling systems—to inform resource allocation decisions. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to execute agent-based simulations of patient pathways and parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms that optimize bed assignments, personnel deployment, and equipment routing under uncertainty. Key computational challenges include managing high-dimensional temporal data at enterprise scale, resolving stochastic optimization problems with competing objectives (e.g., cost minimization vs. care quality), and maintaining model interpretability for administrative stakeholders. The project will validate outputs against historical operational data from three tertiary care hospitals, assessing scenarios ranging from routine capacity planning to surge response protocols. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for healthcare administrators to evaluate resource allocation strategies under diverse constraints, with preliminary simulations suggesting potential reductions in patient wait times (15-22%) and equipment idle periods (25-30%) compared to current heuristic-driven approaches. By bridging operations research, data science, and health systems management, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based healthcare administration, where HPC-enabled predictive analytics directly inform managerial decision-making. The scalability of the framework will be tested across simulated health networks of varying sizes, providing insights into interoperability requirements for multi-institutional resource coordination.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, plan, and manage health care operations and services within health care facilities and across health care systems. Includes instruction in planning, business management, financial management, public relations, human resources management, health care systems operation and management, health care resource allocation and policy making, health law and regulations, and applications to specific types of health care services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of generative, human-centric building systems that dynamically adapt to occupant behavior and environmental conditions. Traditional building performance simulations rely on static models and predefined occupancy schedules, which inadequately capture the complexity of real-world human-building interactions. By integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with real-time sensor data streams and machine learning, this research aims to create a computational framework capable of simulating adaptive architectural environments that optimize both energy efficiency and occupant well-being. The core challenge lies in modeling stochastic occupant behavior, multi-physics building responses (e.g., thermal, acoustic, and visual fluxes), and machine learning-driven control systems within a unified simulation environment. HPC resources are critical to parallelize the computationally intensive tasks of training neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (including IoT-derived occupant movement patterns and environmental sensor data) while simultaneously resolving high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models for microclimate analysis. The proposed framework will be validated against empirical data from a retrofitted mixed-use building instrumented with biometric and environmental sensors. Anticipated outcomes include novel algorithms for predictive building system control, a publicly available simulation toolkit for adaptive architecture, and evidence-based design guidelines that balance technical performance with human physiological and psychological needs. This work bridges architectural design, behavioral science, and computational engineering, offering a paradigm shift in how buildings respond to occupants while maintaining stringent energy targets. The scalability of the developed models will directly inform next-generation smart building standards and retrofit strategies, addressing gaps in current tools that treat human and environmental factors as separate domains rather than interdependent systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of advanced technology to building design and construction, retrofitting existing buildings, and efficient operation of buildings, including lighting and daylight design, acoustics, solar design, building conservation, and energy-conscious design. Includes instruction in architecture, building technology, civil and structural engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental control systems, sustainability, and computer tools and applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities investigation of cultural narratives and linguistic patterns within Appalachian communities. Appalachia’s rich oral traditions, dialects, and folkways remain underdocumented in machine-actionable formats, limiting systematic analysis of their evolution amid socioeconomic and environmental shifts. The research problem centers on disentangling the interplay between cultural preservation and modernization in Appalachia by analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized oral histories, vernacular music recordings, and regional literature—that are currently siloed across archives. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to map linguistic features across temporal and geographic axes, machine learning classifiers to identify themes in community storytelling, and network analysis to trace cultural diffusion pathways. A custom pipeline will process audio recordings of Appalachian English dialects and folk music, applying speech-to-text conversion and acoustic feature extraction to correlate linguistic shifts with demographic data. Concurrently, geospatial visualization tools will contextualize findings within Appalachia’s topography and settlement history. This computationally intensive workflow demands HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize feature extraction tasks, and train deep learning models on multi-modal data. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated cultural artifacts, interactive maps detailing subregional narrative networks, and statistical models quantifying the resilience of Appalachian identity markers. By bridging gaps in digital scholarship on Appalachia, this work aims to empower community-led heritage initiatives and inform equitable policy frameworks that respect the region’s cultural sovereignty. The project’s computational infrastructure will also establish a replicable framework for interdisciplinary humanities research in underserved regions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, sociology, culture, and economics of the Appalachian region of the United States. Includes instruction in contemporary issues in Appalachia, political economy of Appalachia, community-based research, ethnomusicology, and oral and written languages of Appalachia.

abstract: The increasing complexity and volume of healthcare data present significant challenges in efficiently managing, analyzing, and securing medical records while adhering to evolving regulatory standards. This project seeks to address the computational limitations hindering the development of advanced predictive models and real-time analytics for large-scale, heterogeneous health datasets. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to design and validate scalable algorithms for integrating structured and unstructured clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), imaging data, and genomic information—into unified, privacy-preserving frameworks. The computational approach will involve distributed machine learning techniques optimized for parallel processing, enabling the training of multimodal models to identify patterns in disease progression, treatment efficacy, and population health trends. A key focus will be on implementing federated learning architectures to maintain data security and compliance with HIPAA and GDPR requirements while facilitating cross-institutional collaboration. Additionally, we will develop automated tools for anomaly detection in medical records to improve data quality and reduce errors in clinical decision support systems. The use of GPU-accelerated computing will allow rapid processing of high-dimensional datasets, such as radiomics features and longitudinal patient data, which are infeasible to analyze using conventional infrastructure. Expected outcomes include novel methodologies for real-time data harmonization, enhanced predictive analytics for chronic disease management, and open-source frameworks for secure, interoperable health information systems. This work will directly contribute to improving the scalability and accuracy of medical record technologies, supporting healthcare providers in delivering personalized care and public health agencies in resource allocation. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming memory and processing bottlenecks, enabling iterative model refinement, and validating results across diverse simulated and real-world datasets. Success in this project will advance both academic understanding of health data science and practical applications in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: Healthcare environments significantly influence patient outcomes, yet current design practices often rely on static, anecdotal frameworks that inadequately address the dynamic interplay of spatial, environmental, and behavioral factors. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize healthcare spaces for healing efficacy, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate heterogeneous datasets spanning architectural layouts, patient biometrics, environmental sensors, and staff workflows. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive, evidence-based tools to evaluate how design variables—such as lighting gradients, acoustics, wayfinding complexity, and communal area configurations—interact with patient physiology and care delivery workflows. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate occupant movement and interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) for environmental factor propagation, and machine learning (ML) to correlate spatial features with clinical outcomes (e.g., stress biomarkers, recovery rates). HPC resources are critical for processing real-world architectural models, high-resolution sensor data, and longitudinal patient records while enabling parameter sweeps across design permutations. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform to quantify the impact of design choices on operational efficiency and healing metrics, as well as generative AI tools to propose optimized layouts under constraints. This work bridges architecture, healthcare, and computational science, offering a novel methodology to transform subjective design conventions into data-driven standards. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping of healthcare spaces, the project aims to reduce iterative physical construction costs and advance the understanding of how built environments mediate biological and behavioral responses in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and performance of healthcare environments to optimize healing. Includes instruction in interior design, architecture, healing sciences, healthcare environments, human-centered design, and healthcare delivery.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in developing scalable, real-time anomaly detection systems for automated accounting platforms. Modern bookkeeping increasingly relies on AI-driven tools to process high-volume transactional data, yet existing systems struggle to balance real-time validation accuracy with the computational demands of multi-currency, multi-jurisdictional compliance checks. The project focuses on optimizing hybrid machine learning architectures that combine graph neural networks (GNNs) for transactional relationship mapping with transformer-based temporal models to detect irregularities in distributed ledger environments. Key challenges include parallelizing feature extraction across heterogeneous financial data streams (invoices, bank feeds, tax codes) and maintaining sub-second latency thresholds during peak processing loads. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale simulations of synthetic transaction networks (10^8+ events) to stress-test model robustness under adversarial conditions, including coordinated fraud patterns and regulatory edge cases. Computational methods will integrate quantum-inspired optimization algorithms to refine risk-scoring heuristics while preserving audit trails. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive resource allocation in accounting AI systems, benchmark datasets for anomaly detection performance metrics, and novel convergence strategies for federated learning in privacy-preserving financial data environments. This work aims to establish computational best practices for next-generation accounting technologies, particularly in blockchain-integrated bookkeeping systems where traditional validation paradigms fail to scale. By addressing the intersection of computational efficiency, regulatory complexity, and machine learning reliability, the project contributes to emergent research at the nexus of accounting technology, decentralized finance, and high-performance analytics infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical administrative support to professional accountants and other financial management personnel. Includes instruction in posting transactions to accounts, record-keeping systems, accounting software operation, and general accounting principles and practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and cellular dynamics underlying tumor microenvironment (TME)-driven therapy resistance in advanced carcinomas, with a focus on integrating spatial transcriptomic and proteomic data to model disease progression. Despite advances in oncology, the mechanisms by which stromal-immune interactions within the TME promote resistance to targeted therapies remain poorly resolved, particularly in organ-specific contexts such as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Current experimental models inadequately capture the dynamic reciprocity between neoplastic cells, fibroblasts, and immune infiltrates during treatment, limiting the identification of actionable therapeutic targets. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining spatial transcriptomic datasets from clinical biopsies with agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate cell-cell signaling networks and stress-response pathways under therapeutic pressure. The ABM will integrate cell-specific proteomic profiles, hypoxia gradients, and extracellular matrix remodeling data to predict clonal selection patterns and immune evasion mechanisms. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to classify TME subtypes associated with rapid progression, using feature selection algorithms to prioritize molecular markers of stromal reprogramming. By correlating in silico predictions with longitudinal patient outcomes, this work aims to uncover conserved regulators of therapy-resistant niches and identify combinatorial targeting strategies. The scale of spatial omics datasets (≥50,000 cells/sample) and the stochastic nature of ABM simulations necessitate HPC resources for parallel processing, Monte Carlo iterations, and high-dimensional data integration. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational platform for simulating TME adaptation and a prioritized list of microenvironmental drivers of resistance validated in ex vivo organoid co-cultures. This work will advance experimental pathology by bridging tissue-scale pathophysiology with subcellular signaling dynamics, offering translational insights into personalized therapeutic design.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the expression, initiation, maintenance and progression of tissue injury and disease, including death, and the relationship of pathogenesis to fundamental molecular and cellular mechanisms. Includes instruction in immunology, microbiology, gene expression, inflammation, cell injury, apoptosis, immunopathology, molecular markers of disease and toxins, neoplasia, growth regulation, and organ- and system-specific investigations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methodologies for analyzing and simulating the physical and perceptual dynamics of traditional drawing media. While manual techniques in drawing—such as charcoal, ink, and pastel—are deeply rooted in tactile material interactions, their digital counterparts often lack nuanced simulations of texture, layering, and medium-substrate behavior. Current computational tools for artists prioritize efficiency over fidelity, limiting their ability to replicate the subtleties of physical media or support innovative hybrid practices. This research addresses this gap by developing physics-based models and machine learning frameworks to simulate and predict the behavior of traditional drawing materials at scale. High-resolution scans of physical artworks will inform finite element simulations of medium-substrate interactions (e.g., charcoal on textured paper), while generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained to predict stylistic outcomes from variable input parameters, such as pressure, stroke direction, and layering sequences. These models require HPC resources due to the computational intensity of simulating micro-scale material dynamics and processing terabyte-scale datasets of high-fidelity artistic workflows. The project will also explore real-time rendering techniques to integrate these models into digital drawing interfaces, enabling artists to experiment with hybrid physical-digital workflows. Anticipated outcomes include open-source software prototypes for enhanced digital drawing tools, a publicly accessible dataset of material interaction simulations, and peer-reviewed insights into the relationship between computational modeling and artistic practice.
