By bridging computational precision with artistic intuition, this work aims to expand creative possibilities in visual arts education and professional practice while preserving the material knowledge embedded in traditional techniques.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions through representation by lines made on a surface. Includes instruction in eye-hand coordination; line, value, shape, and perspective; figure and still life drawing; the use of media such as pen and ink, pencil, charcoal, pastel, and brush; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of ancient urban systems through large-scale spatiotemporal modeling of archaeological settlement patterns. While traditional archaeological methods focus on site-specific analyses, this research addresses the challenge of synthesizing disparate datasets—spanning environmental, architectural, and material culture evidence—to model the dynamic interactions between human communities and their landscapes across multi-century timescales. The computational problem lies in integrating heterogeneous, fragmentary datasets (e.g., LiDAR surveys, excavation records, radiocarbon dates, and paleoenvironmental proxies) into a unified simulation framework that can test hypotheses about resource allocation, resilience strategies, and sociopolitical complexity in pre-industrial cities. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with geographic information systems (GIS), the project will reconstruct plausible decision-making processes of ancient populations under constraints such as climate variability, resource scarcity, and infrastructural demands. HPC resources are critical for running thousands of parallelized simulations to account for data gaps and uncertainties inherent in archaeological records, enabling probabilistic assessments of urban growth patterns and collapse triggers. The workflow includes machine learning-assisted pattern recognition in ceramic assemblages to refine chronological frameworks and network analysis of trade routes to quantify economic interdependence. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for scalable archaeological simulation, new insights into how past societies balanced short-term needs with long-term sustainability, and empirically grounded comparative models of urban adaptation applicable to modern resilience planning. By bridging computational social science methodologies with humanistic inquiries into historical trajectories, this project aims to establish a replicable framework for analyzing past human-environment systems at unprecedented temporal and spatial resolutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of extinct societies, and the past of living societies, via the excavation, analysis and interpretation of their artifactual, human, and associated remains. Includes instruction in archeological theory, field methods, dating methods, conservation and museum studies, cultural and physical evolution, and the study of specific selected past cultures with a focus on the humanistic aspects of archaeology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern railway systems demands advanced computational tools to optimize operational efficiency, safety, and infrastructure resilience. This project seeks to address critical challenges in railroad transportation—such as real-time traffic management, predictive maintenance of track networks, and risk mitigation for hazardous material transport—through the development of high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation and machine learning frameworks. Current approaches often rely on static models or simplified heuristics, which fail to capture the dynamic interactions between trains, infrastructure, environmental conditions, and human operators at scale. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-faceted computational strategy. First, large-scale agent-based simulations will model rail traffic under variable scenarios (e.g., weather disruptions, track failures) using parallelized computing to resolve micro-level interactions across continental-scale networks. Second, graph neural networks will be trained on historical maintenance records and sensor data to predict localized track degradation, requiring GPU-accelerated processing of terabyte-scale datasets. Third, probabilistic risk analysis frameworks will evaluate hazardous material routing strategies under uncertainty, leveraging Monte Carlo methods to quantify low-probability, high-consequence events. These efforts depend on HPC resources to achieve the necessary computational throughput, particularly for time-sensitive operational decision support. Expected outcomes include validated models for reducing network-wide delays by 15–20%, identifying at-risk infrastructure components weeks in advance of failures, and optimizing safety protocols for hazardous shipments. The project will also generate open-source tools to help railway operators transition from legacy systems to data-driven management practices. By integrating domain-specific railway operational constraints with cutting-edge computational methods, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for scalable, adaptive railway system optimization, directly supporting the transportation industry’s goals of reliability, safety, and sustainability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation of railroads and other aspects of the railway industry, including railroad and railyard service. Includes instruction in railway culture, operating skills, General Code of Operation rules, conductor service, signal systems, switching, transportation of hazardous materials, safety, and railway telecommunications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the persistent challenge of preparing physics educators to effectively teach complex, computation-intensive concepts in K-12 and undergraduate classrooms. Despite advances in physics education research, many teachers lack access to training tools that model realistic, large-scale physical systems or leverage modern computational workflows. To bridge this gap, we propose developing and deploying interactive, high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled pedagogical simulations tailored for physics teacher education. The research problem centers on two key barriers: (1) the scarcity of accessible computational resources for modeling multi-scale physics phenomena (e.g., quantum interactions, astrophysical systems) in classroom-relevant contexts, and (2) the need to train educators in utilizing parallelized computational methods as both teaching tools and learning objectives. Our approach combines physics education frameworks with HPC-driven numerical modeling using finite element analysis and Monte Carlo methods adapted for pedagogical use cases. Simulations will be optimized for scalability on distributed-memory architectures while maintaining user-friendly interfaces for non-specialist educators. We will employ comparative analysis of learning outcomes across three cohorts: pre-service teachers using HPC-accelerated modules, those using traditional single-node simulations, and a control group. The computational workload involves parameter sweeps across educational scenarios, requiring ~50,000 core-hours to model diverse classroom contexts and physical systems. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for integrating HPC resources into physics teacher training, quantitative evidence of improved pedagogical content knowledge among participants, and open-source simulation templates adaptable to regional curricula. By demonstrating how advanced computing can enhance physics education preparation, this work aims to establish scalable models for equipping teachers with skills to navigate increasingly computational STEM landscapes while deepening their own conceptual mastery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing project timelines, cost efficiency, and safety due to the dynamic interplay of workforce allocation, material logistics, and environmental variables. Traditional methods for construction planning and risk assessment rely heavily on static models and historical data, which inadequately capture real-world complexity and variability. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate large-scale construction processes under diverse constraints, enabling data-driven decision-making. The research will focus on integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES) to replicate interactions between workers, equipment, and site conditions, while incorporating stochastic factors such as weather disruptions, supply chain delays, and safety incidents. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize these models using real-world datasets—including geospatial surveys, equipment telemetry, and labor productivity records—and to perform Monte Carlo analyses quantifying probabilistic outcomes. Key objectives include identifying bottlenecks in resource allocation, evaluating the resilience of schedules under stress scenarios, and optimizing contingency protocols. The computational workflow will leverage parallel processing to scale simulations across thousands of scenarios, reducing runtime from weeks to hours compared to conventional tools. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for construction managers to preemptively mitigate risks, a repository of scenario-driven best practices, and sensitivity analyses quantifying the impact of variables like crew size or material delivery intervals. By advancing computational capabilities in construction engineering, this work aims to reduce project overruns by an estimated 15–20% in modeled cases while improving adherence to safety standards, directly supporting the program’s mission to bridge technical innovation with practical construction applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers, engineering contractors and other professionals engaged in the construction of buildings and related structures. Includes instruction in basic structural engineering principles and construction techniques, building site inspection, site supervision, construction personnel supervision, plan and specification interpretation, supply logistics and procurement, applicable building codes, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making processes during critical incident response operations, such as hostage rescues, active shooter scenarios, and coordinated terrorist threats. While traditional approaches rely on static protocols and human intuition, the dynamic, high-stakes nature of these events demands adaptive tools capable of integrating real-time data streams, environmental variables, and behavioral predictions. The core challenge lies in modeling complex, multi-agent interactions under uncertainty while accounting for psychological, logistical, and tactical constraints unique to law enforcement emergencies. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the project will implement a hybrid simulation architecture combining agent-based modeling, game-theoretic decision trees, and machine learning-driven risk assessment. The computational models will incorporate anonymized historical incident data, 3D geospatial reconstructions of real-world venues, and behavioral datasets derived from de-escalation training simulations. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will stress-test response strategies across thousands of scenario permutations, evaluating outcomes through metrics including civilian survivability rates, operational timeline efficiency, and resource deployment precision. A novel component involves integrating natural language processing to analyze negotiation transcripts and predict perpetrator escalation patterns. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system prototype that generates probabilistic action pathways during live incidents and an after-action analysis toolkit for identifying procedural bottlenecks. The computational intensity of simultaneously processing IoT sensor data, biometric inputs, and environmental variables necessitates cluster-scale resources for both training deep reinforcement learning models and running multi-parameter sensitivity analyses. By bridging computational social science with operational tactics, this work aims to establish an evidence-based paradigm for critical incident management while advancing methodological frameworks for HPC applications in public safety domains.
cip_title: Critical Incident Response/ Special Police Operations
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for dealing with police emergencies such as hostage situations, bomb threats, barricades and terrorist incidents. Includes instruction in crisis management, command procedures, incident containment, information collection and debriefing, first responder negotiation, victim and criminal psychology, site survey and surveillance, special weapons and tactics, interagency communications and joint operations, pre-confrontation and contingency planning, assault and rescue operations, security and crowd control, media relations, and post-operation procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to identify early risk factors and optimize personalized intervention strategies for children with developmental-behavioral challenges, integrating multimodal data spanning genetic, neuroimaging, environmental, and longitudinal clinical records. Current approaches to understanding developmental trajectories often rely on static, population-level analyses, which inadequately capture the dynamic interplay of biological, psychosocial, and environmental factors contributing to outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale datasets from multicenter electronic health records (EHRs), genomic databases, and behavioral assessments, alongside ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data capturing real-time family interactions. Machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures for temporal EHR analysis and graph neural networks to model family-environment interactions, will be trained to predict developmental risks and intervention responses. Agent-based simulations will further test how hypothetical community-level policies (e.g., access to early intervention programs) might reduce disparities in care. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization across thousands of model configurations, and stochastic simulations of population-scale scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to stratify children by risk of developmental delays or maladaptive behaviors, validated against prospective clinical cohorts; (2) actionable insights into modifiable family-environmental factors; and (3) open-source frameworks for simulating intervention impacts across diverse socioeconomic contexts. By elucidating mechanisms linking multilevel factors to developmental outcomes, this work aims to advance precision medicine in developmental-behavioral pediatrics, directly supporting the program’s mission to bridge research, clinical care, and advocacy. The scale and complexity of these analyses require HPC resources to achieve clinically meaningful resolution while ensuring reproducibility and generalizability across populations.
cip_definition: Research on how to assist in the prevention, diagnosis, and management of developmental difficulties and problematic behaviors in children, and in the family dysfunctions that compromise children's development; and to foster understanding and promotion of optimal development of children and families through research, education, clinical care, and advocacy efforts.

abstract: The study of driven quantum systems far from equilibrium presents a fundamental challenge in modern physics, with implications for quantum control, information processing, and emergent macroscopic phenomena. While equilibrium phase transitions are well-characterized, the interplay of strong interactions, time-periodic driving, and dissipation in such systems leads to novel non-equilibrium phases whose stability and universal properties remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by employing large-scale numerical simulations to map phase diagrams, characterize critical dynamics, and identify robust protocols for maintaining coherence in driven quantum many-body systems. The computational approach combines tensor network methods for one-dimensional systems with quantum trajectory techniques to model open systems under periodic driving. These methods require high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the exponential scaling of Hilbert space, the need for long-time evolution to assess stability, and the statistical sampling required for dissipative systems. Key simulations will focus on parametrically driven spin chains and bosonic arrays, where competing instabilities and interaction effects are predicted to generate exotic phases such as time-crystalline order and prethermalization plateaus. The requested resources will enable systematic parameter sweeps across driving frequencies, interaction strengths, and dissipation rates, which are computationally prohibitive on local clusters. Expected outcomes include predictive criteria for phase boundaries in experimental platforms like superconducting circuits and cold-atom arrays, as well as general insights into thermalization breakdown in driven quantum matter. This work will provide foundational results for harnessing non-equilibrium quantum phenomena in next-generation technologies while advancing computational methodologies for time-dependent open quantum systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interactions between horticultural environments and human health outcomes in the context of horticulture therapy (HT). Despite growing evidence of HT’s benefits for individuals with physical, cognitive, or emotional challenges, the field lacks predictive frameworks to quantify how specific plant species, spatial arrangements, or sensory stimuli (e.g., scent, color) contribute to therapeutic efficacy. Current studies rely heavily on qualitative or small-scale observational data, limiting the ability to optimize interventions for diverse populations. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating ecological, psychophysiological, and design data to identify actionable patterns in HT delivery. Multivariate datasets—including plant metabolomic profiles, biometric data from wearable sensors (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels), and behavioral assessments—will be analyzed using machine learning algorithms to isolate key variables driving positive health outcomes. Agent-based models will simulate patient interactions within virtual therapeutic gardens, testing hypotheses about layout efficacy and plant selection under varying clinical scenarios. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses, particularly for processing high-resolution ecological data (e.g., 3D plant growth models, volatile organic compound emission rates) and running parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include the development of a predictive framework to guide evidence-based HT garden design, personalized to patient needs (e.g., neurocognitive disorders, chronic pain). This work will establish a foundation for computational horticulture therapy as a data-driven subfield, bridging gaps between landscape architecture, plant science, and clinical practice. By quantifying the biopsychosocial mechanisms underlying HT, the project aims to advance standardized protocols and expand access to nature-based interventions in healthcare settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on plant science and horticulture techniques to achieve measurable physical and mental health outcomes for individuals with physical or mental challenges. Includes instruction in abnormal psychology, adult development and aging, botany, facilities design, horticultural therapy, plant pathology, people-plant relationships, and psychology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive computational framework to analyze fire dynamics and arson risk patterns, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical gaps in fire investigation and prevention. Fire behavior in complex environments—such as urban interfaces or structures with mixed combustible materials—remains poorly understood, limiting the accuracy of forensic reconstructions and proactive mitigation strategies. Current methods often rely on simplified models or empirical data, which fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between fire chemistry, airflow, material properties, and human factors. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML), and probabilistic risk assessment. The CFD component will model fire spread and heat transfer at high spatial-temporal resolution using FireFOAM and FDS, validated against experimental datasets. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze historical arson case data, environmental variables, and socio-economic indicators to identify high-risk zones and modus operandi patterns. These models will be coupled through a Bayesian inference framework to quantify uncertainties and refine predictions. The HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of 3D fire simulations across diverse scenarios, parallelize ML training on large heterogeneous datasets, and enable real-time sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible arson risk mapping tool for law enforcement and fire agencies, (2) improved forensic guidelines for fire scene reconstruction, and (3) validated mitigation strategies for high-risk infrastructure. By bridging fire science, data analytics, and HPC-driven modeling, this work aims to enhance the precision of fire cause determination and support evidence-based policies to reduce arson-related losses in urban and wildland-urban interface communities.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and principles of fire combustion and behavior applied to the analysis of fires and their causes. Includes instruction in fire behavior and combustion, fire dynamics, hazardous materials chemistry, incendiary fire analysis, fire-related human behavior, forensic procedures, investigative techniques, case management and case preparation.

abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources into power grids necessitates advanced energy storage solutions to address intermittency and stability challenges. Superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) systems offer high efficiency and rapid response but require optimization of electromagnetic and thermal properties under dynamic operating conditions. Current design approaches rely on simplified models that inadequately capture multiphysics interactions, limiting performance predictions. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to optimize SMES configurations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Multiphysics simulations combining finite element analysis (FEA) for electromagnetic fields and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management will be implemented, leveraging parallel computing architectures to resolve micron-scale geometric features and transient behaviors across timescales. Machine learning techniques will accelerate parameter space exploration to identify designs maximizing energy density while minimizing AC losses and cryogenic loads. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies involving 10^4-10^5 concurrent simulations, which are infeasible on local clusters. Expected outcomes include validated optimization frameworks for SMES systems, quantitative guidelines for superconducting coil geometries under grid-relevant cycling conditions, and open-source tools for coupled electromagnetic-thermal analysis. This work will advance scalable energy storage technologies critical for decarbonizing power systems while demonstrating HPC-driven innovation in electrical infrastructure design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of electrical and electronic systems and their components, including electrical power generation systems; and the analysis of problems such as superconductor, wave propagation, energy storage and retrieval, and reception and amplification.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how mechanical forces and cellular dynamics drive tissue-level morphogenesis during embryonic development, with a focus on integrating multiscale anatomical and cell biological data. A critical gap exists in understanding how subcellular processes—such as cytoskeletal reorganization, cell-cell adhesion remodeling, and force transduction—scale up to produce organized 3D tissue architectures. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture these hierarchical interactions in real time, particularly in complex vertebrate systems. To address this, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale model that simulates cellular behaviors within anatomically accurate embryonic tissue templates. The model will integrate live-imaging data from avian embryo limb bud development, histochemical staining patterns of extracellular matrix composition, and biomechanical parameters from atomic force microscopy. Agent-based modeling frameworks will represent individual cells as discrete entities with dynamic mechanical properties, while finite element methods will simulate tissue-scale stress distributions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized computation of cell population behaviors over developmental timescales, with iterative validation against experimental morphometric and kinematic datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of critical force-sensitive checkpoints in limb patterning, (2) predictive maps of cellular response thresholds to mechanical perturbations, and (3) an open-access computational toolset for simulating cell-anatomy interplay in other developing systems. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of how cellular dynamics are coordinated across anatomical scales, with implications for congenital defect research and regenerative bioengineering strategies. The requested computing resources are essential for managing the high-dimensional parameter space, real-time visualization of emergent tissue behaviors, and large-scale simulation iterations required to establish statistically robust correlations between subcellular events and macroscopic anatomical outcomes.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cell structure, function, and dynamics within the context of organismic, regional, and gross anatomical systems. Includes instruction in molecular biology, cell biology and histology, structural biology, anatomy, embryology, endocrinology, and applications to specific systems, diseases, defects, and processes.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay between legal frameworks, urban development patterns, and socioeconomic outcomes in real estate and land development law. Traditional legal analyses of zoning regulations, environmental compliance, and property rights often lack the capacity to model dynamic interactions across large-scale geospatial and temporal datasets. This limitation hinders the ability to predict how localized policy changes might propagate systemic risks, such as housing inequities, land-use conflicts, or regulatory compliance bottlenecks. To address this gap, the project proposes a computational legal analytics framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), geospatial simulation, and agent-based modeling. NLP algorithms will parse and classify legal texts—including municipal codes, court rulings, and environmental impact assessments—to identify latent patterns in regulatory language and enforcement trends. Geospatial simulations will map the cascading effects of hypothetical land-use policies across urban and rural jurisdictions, incorporating variables such as population density, infrastructure capacity, and climate vulnerability. Agent-based models will simulate stakeholder decision-making (e.g., developers, municipalities, community groups) under evolving legal constraints, enabling probabilistic forecasts of litigation risks or development delays. By deploying these computationally intensive methods on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to generate predictive insights into how legal frameworks can adapt to emerging challenges like climate migration, smart city technologies, and affordable housing crises. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access toolkit for policymakers to evaluate the systemic impacts of land-use regulations and a novel methodology for computational legal studies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between legal theory, urban planning, and data science, offering a scalable model for analyzing complex sociolegal systems in real time.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing crop yield and resilience under increasing environmental stressors, including climate variability, emerging pest resistance, and soil degradation. Traditional approaches to modeling crop responses to these variables often lack the resolution to account for complex interactions between genomic traits, microclimate conditions, and agronomic practices. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating high-throughput genomic data, real-time environmental sensor inputs, and multi-scale crop growth models. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to identify genotype-environment-management (G×E×M) interactions predictive of stress tolerance and yield outcomes, while agent-based models will simulate pest and pathogen spread under projected climate scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of hyperspectral imaging data from field trials, execute parallelized genomic prediction models across diverse crop varieties, and run ensemble climate simulations at regional scales. Expected outcomes include the development of a decision-support tool for dynamically optimizing irrigation, fertilization, and pest management strategies, validated against experimental data from partner farms. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets linking crop genomic markers to stress resilience traits, enabling faster breeding cycles. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance precision agriculture frameworks that enhance resource efficiency, reduce chemical inputs, and stabilize production in variable climates, directly supporting food security priorities. The computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other staple crops, amplifying their long-term impact across agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cultivate grain, fiber, forage, oilseed, fruits and nuts, vegetables, and other domesticated plant products. Includes instruction in basic principles of plant science, health, and nutrition as applied to particular species and breeds; soil preparation and irrigation; pest management; planting and harvesting operations; product marketing; and applicable issues of safety, regulation, logistics, and supply.

abstract: Immunopathologic diseases, including autoimmune disorders and transplant rejection, involve complex interactions between immune cells, molecular pathways, and clinical variables that remain inadequately characterized. Current challenges in predicting patient-specific immunotherapy responses or post-transplant outcomes stem from limitations in modeling dynamic immune processes across genomic, proteomic, and clinical datasets. This project proposes to develop an integrated computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal immunopathology data, with the goal of identifying predictive biomarkers and optimizing therapeutic strategies. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) constructing patient-specific immune network models using single-cell RNA sequencing, serum proteomics, and clinical histopathology data from cohorts with autoimmune vasculitis and renal transplant recipients, and (2) simulating immune response trajectories under varying therapeutic regimens through mechanistic modeling. Computational methods will combine deep learning architectures for feature extraction from high-dimensional pathology images, Bayesian network inference for identifying critical immune pathway interactions, and parallelized agent-based simulations of immune cell dynamics. The HPC environment is essential for managing datasets exceeding 500 TB, running iterative model optimizations, and executing large-scale in silico clinical trials comparing immunosuppression protocols. Expected outcomes include validated computational models capable of predicting graft rejection risk with >85% accuracy in retrospective validation cohorts and identifying optimal combination therapies for refractory autoimmune cases. By enabling the integration of real-time diagnostic data with dynamic systems immunology models, this work aims to advance precision management of immunologic diseases while reducing reliance on trial-and-error treatment approaches. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, high-memory nodes for whole-genome association analyses, and scalable storage for multi-institutional collaborative datasets.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment and laboratory management of immunologic diseases. Includes instruction in diagnostic surgical pathology, management of organ transplantation and immunotherapy.

abstract: This project addresses the challenge of optimizing art pedagogy through the computational analysis of student engagement and creative processes in digital art environments. As K–12 and postsecondary art education increasingly incorporates digital tools—such as graphic design software, 3D modeling platforms, and virtual reality (VR) art spaces—educators require deeper insights into how students interact with these technologies. However, the volume and complexity of interaction data (e.g., gesture tracking, workflow patterns, temporal usage metrics) generated by these tools exceed the analytical capacity of conventional computing resources. This limits educators’ ability to adapt instruction to diverse learning styles or diagnose barriers to creative expression. To bridge this gap, we propose a mixed-methods study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model student behaviors and evaluate pedagogical strategies. Multimodal datasets—including screen recordings, VR motion logs, and biometric feedback—will be processed using GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines to classify creative workflows, identify engagement correlates, and simulate the impact of instructional interventions. Natural language processing (NLP) will further analyze written or verbal peer critiques to map conceptual development. By integrating these computational outputs with qualitative classroom observations, the project aims to establish evidence-based frameworks for personalized art instruction. The requested HPC resources are critical for training deep learning models on large-scale datasets (≥10 TB) and running iterative simulations of teaching scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive tools to help educators tailor feedback to individual creative processes, (2) a public repository of annotated interaction datasets for art education research, and (3) scalable methods to assess the efficacy of digital art platforms in fostering technical and conceptual skills. This work will advance art teacher education by grounding pedagogical practices in data-driven insights while preserving the subjective, exploratory nature of artistic learning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach art and art appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design of next-generation integrated circuits (ICs) for advanced semiconductor nodes (3nm and below), where traditional simulation tools struggle to balance accuracy, scalability, and runtime. As transistor densities increase and novel materials are adopted, existing computer-aided design (CAD) workflows face limitations in modeling parasitic effects, thermal gradients, and electromigration risks across multi-layer architectures. The research proposes a hybrid computational framework combining physics-based simulations with machine learning (ML) surrogate models to accelerate design validation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train ML models on large datasets generated via finite-element analysis (FEA) of thermal-mechanical stress and Monte Carlo-based statistical circuit simulations. Parallelized SPICE simulations will evaluate performance-variability tradeoffs across 10,000+ device instances under process-induced variations, while GPU-accelerated tensor networks will optimize power grid decoupling capacitor placement. The computational workflow will integrate open-source EDA tools with custom Python libraries for automated parameter sweeping and uncertainty quantification. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated ML-enhanced design framework reducing sign-off verification time by 40-60% compared to commercial tools, (2) thermal reliability models for heterogeneous 3D-IC architectures, and (3) open-access datasets correlating layout features with electromigration failure thresholds. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge the gap between academic research and industrial IC design requirements, enabling cost-effective exploration of emerging technologies like gallium nitride (GaN) power devices and resistive RAM (ReRAM) integration. Results will directly support curriculum development in nanometer-scale IC layout courses while providing foundational data for semiconductor manufacturing partnerships.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to design circuits in microelectronics. Includes instruction in circuit design, circuit layout, circuit analysis, computer-aided drafting, and semi-conductor technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing persuasive communication strategies in digital public relations and advertising campaigns. The rapid evolution of digital platforms has created vast, dynamic datasets that traditional analytical tools struggle to process efficiently. Current methods for analyzing audience engagement, sentiment, and message diffusion across social media, search engines, and multimedia channels are limited in scalability, hindering the ability to model real-time campaign performance or predict emergent trends. This research addresses this gap by employing computational methods to analyze multi-modal communication data—including text, image, and video content—at unprecedented speed and scale. The project will develop machine learning models to identify patterns in audience behavior, simulate message dissemination networks, and test the efficacy of personalized advertising content. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment analysis, graph-based algorithms to map influencer networks, and reinforcement learning to iteratively refine campaign strategies. HPC resources are critical for training large-scale neural networks, processing terabytes of unstructured data, and running parallelized simulations of communication scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for real-time adaptive messaging, predictive tools for audience segmentation, and evidence-based insights into how cultural, linguistic, and contextual factors shape persuasive communication in digital environments. Results will directly inform best practices for PR and advertising professionals while advancing theoretical understanding of computational persuasion. By enabling the analysis of cross-platform communication ecosystems at scale, this work bridges the gap between applied communication research and data-driven strategy development, offering transformative potential for both academic inquiry and industry practice.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on organizational communication, public relations, and advertising; and that prepares individuals to function in a wide range of public and private sector positions requiring the skills of persuasive communication. Includes instruction in communications, public relations, and advertising theory; principles and techniques of persuasion; message/image design; marketing strategy; professional writing; public speaking and multi-media presentation skills; digital communications; and applied research.

abstract: This project seeks to advance geropsychological research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interplay of psychosocial, cognitive, and behavioral factors influencing mental health outcomes in aging populations. Older adults face unique challenges, including social isolation, cognitive decline, and barriers to accessing tailored mental health interventions. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture dynamic, multidimensional relationships in large-scale longitudinal datasets, limiting the personalization of counseling strategies. To address this gap, we propose developing computational models integrating machine learning (ML) and network analysis to identify predictors of intervention efficacy and resilience patterns in adults over 65. The project will analyze multimodal data from geropsychology studies, including electronic health records, ecological momentary assessments of mood and social engagement, and structured interviews on coping strategies. HPC resources will enable the training of ensemble ML algorithms to predict treatment outcomes while accounting for high-dimensional interactions between variables such as cognitive reserve, social support, and personality traits. Concurrently, Gaussian graphical network models will map temporal dependencies among depressive symptoms, anxiety, and adaptive behaviors, simulating intervention effects under varying psychosocial conditions. The computational workflow will prioritize interpretability to inform actionable counseling frameworks. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable ML pipeline for stratifying older adults by intervention needs, (2) dynamic network models of symptom-behavior interactions across the aging trajectory, and (3) open-source tools for simulating personalized therapy scenarios. By elucidating mechanisms of resilience and vulnerability in later life, this work will directly enhance evidence-based practices in geropsychological counseling while addressing computational bottlenecks in aging research. The requested HPC allocation is critical for handling memory-intensive network simulations and enabling rapid cross-validation of predictive models across diverse aging cohorts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychology of aging and of elderly individuals and populations, with reference to growth and decline across the life span. Includes instruction in gerontology, developmental and adult psychology, age-related development and decline of cognitive processes, age-related psychological and neurological disorders, social and personality development in aging populations and individuals, and applications to the clinical treatment and care of older adults.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing multiphysics systems in advanced manufacturing processes, where concurrent thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamics phenomena create complex, nonlinear interactions. Traditional simulation tools struggle to resolve these coupled processes at industrially relevant scales due to prohibitive computational costs, limiting the design and operational efficiency of systems such as additive manufacturing platforms, composite material curing systems, and energy-intensive thermal processing units. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a parallelized finite element method (FEM) solver enhanced with adaptive mesh refinement and machine learning-driven surrogate models. The solver will integrate open-source libraries, including PETSc and Deal.II, to exploit distributed-memory architectures for large-scale simulations. Machine learning components will accelerate parameter space exploration by predicting optimal mesh configurations and reducing the need for full-order model evaluations. Key computational challenges include managing memory bottlenecks during multiphysics data transfers, optimizing load balancing across >10,000 CPU cores, and validating results against experimental datasets from collaborative industry partners. The outcomes will enable high-fidelity simulations of manufacturing systems with sub-millimeter spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution, a 50–100x improvement over current capabilities. This will directly support the design of energy-efficient industrial processes, reducing material waste and carbon footprints in sectors such as aerospace and renewable energy component fabrication. The resulting open-source tools will be disseminated to academic and industrial users, fostering broader adoption of HPC-driven optimization in engineering. Resource requests include 200,000 node-hours on a GPU-accelerated cluster for solver development and 50 TB of storage for managing multiphysics datasets and surrogate model training.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing global supply chain resilience in the face of multi-factor disruptions, including geopolitical volatility, climate events, and trade policy shifts. Traditional supply chain models fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between international trade networks, regional regulatory frameworks, and real-time market signals. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose developing a multi-agent simulation platform that integrates heterogeneous data streams—from customs databases and satellite imagery to foreign exchange markets—to model cross-border commerce as a complex adaptive system. The computational framework will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate millions of disruption scenarios across temporal and spatial scales, while machine learning techniques will identify latent risk patterns in multimodal trade data. Key innovations include the incorporation of non-linear tariff escalation effects, currency arbitrage behaviors, and sustainability constraints aligned with evolving international trade agreements. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of quantifying trade-off matrices between cost efficiency and supply chain robustness, with particular relevance to small and medium enterprises operating in emerging markets. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing petabyte-scale logistics datasets and resolving optimization problems with high-dimensional constraints across 190+ jurisdictional domains. Results will advance both academic understanding of cascade failures in global value chains and practical strategies for maintaining compliance with disparate international trade regulations under uncertainty. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational economics, operations research, and data science to address pressing challenges in modern cross-border commerce.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international businesses and/or business operations. Includes instruction in the principles and processes of export sales, trade controls, foreign operations and related problems, monetary issues, international business policy, and applications to doing business in specific countries and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine approaches in pediatric critical care, specifically targeting sepsis—a leading cause of mortality and long-term morbidity in children. Current predictive models for sepsis outcomes lack the granularity to integrate high-dimensional multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with real-time clinical and electronic health record (EHR) data, limiting their utility in dynamic, individualized treatment planning. The computational complexity of analyzing these heterogeneous datasets, which include longitudinal measurements from over 5,000 patients, exceeds the capacity of standard clinical computing infrastructure. To address this, we propose developing a scalable machine learning framework to model sepsis progression and therapeutic response. The framework will employ federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions while training neural networks on multimodal inputs. Bayesian hierarchical models will quantify uncertainty in treatment effect predictions, and agent-based simulations will explore emergent interactions between immune response pathways and pharmacodynamics. HPC resources are critical for optimizing hyperparameters across thousands of parallelized simulations, processing terabytes of time-series EHR data, and accelerating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) via GPU-optimized pipelines. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for sepsis trajectory and organ failure risk, deployable via cloud-based clinical decision support tools, and (2) mechanistic insights into age-specific host-pathogen interactions to guide immunomodulatory therapy design. By enabling rapid integration of complex biological and clinical data, this project aims to reduce algorithm development timelines by 60% compared to conventional methods, directly addressing the urgent need for computationally driven innovations in pediatric acute care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the comprehensive care and treatment of all aspects of human growth and development from conception through fetal life, infancy, childhood and adolescence, including preventive and therapeutic regimes. May included related research in behavioral aspects of illness, related family and community medicine issues, and emergency and critical care procedures.

abstract: The development of efficient catalytic processes for hydrocarbon upgrading is hindered by the multiscale nature of reaction networks, which span molecular interactions to reactor-scale hydrodynamics. Current computational models struggle to integrate these scales due to prohibitive resource demands, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable coupled molecular dynamics (MD) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of catalytic systems under industrially relevant conditions. By employing hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization, we will resolve atomic-scale surface reactions while capturing macroscale transport phenomena in multiphase reactor environments. Machine learning surrogates will accelerate parameter estimation for rate constants and adsorption equilibria, informed by quantum mechanics calculations on key intermediates. The resulting multiscale framework will predict catalyst performance metrics (e.g., selectivity, deactivation) and optimize reactor configurations for methane pyrolysis—a promising pathway to low-carbon hydrogen production. Successful implementation will provide a validated computational toolkit for accelerating the design of intensified chemical processes, directly supporting energy transition goals through reduced computational trial-and-error. Access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory architectures is critical for managing the 10^6-core-hour requirements of cross-scale simulations spanning nanoseconds to process timescales. This work bridges a critical gap in process systems engineering by enabling first-principles prediction of catalytic reactor behavior, with potential applications in petrochemicals, carbon capture, and renewable fuel synthesis.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to optimize traffic control strategies in construction and maintenance zones, with the goal of enhancing safety for workers, drivers, and pedestrians while minimizing traffic disruption. Current flagging protocols rely on static guidelines that often fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating traffic volumes, weather conditions, or unexpected incidents, leading to increased risks of accidents and congestion. To address this, we will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate traffic flow patterns, worker positioning, and pedestrian interactions in diverse scenarios. The project integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) to represent vehicles, pedestrians, and construction zones as autonomous agents with rule-based behaviors, coupled with Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in driver responses to flagging signals. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be employed to iteratively refine traffic control policies, optimizing the placement of flaggers, signage, and temporary lane configurations. Large-scale parameter sweeps will evaluate the impact of variables such as traffic speed, visibility, and work zone geometry on safety outcomes. The computational demands of simulating millions of agent interactions across thousands of scenarios necessitate distributed-memory parallelization and GPU-accelerated training for machine learning components. Expected outcomes include data-driven recommendations for adaptive flagging protocols, predictive tools for incident risk assessment, and a publicly available simulation engine to train personnel in scenario-based decision-making. By bridging computational engineering with traffic safety practices, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for dynamic traffic control that responds in real time to evolving conditions, ultimately reducing collision rates and improving compliance with work zone regulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to control the movement of traffic through construction and maintenance zones and to protect the safety of work crews, drivers, and pedestrians. Includes instruction in flagging duties and responsibilities, the traffic control zone, flagging signals, pavement markers, freeway flagging, utility flagging, emergency response flagging, and night traffic control.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in large-scale, data-driven analysis of sociocultural and historical dynamics in translation practices. While translation studies has traditionally relied on qualitative, case-based methods, the increasing availability of digitized multilingual corpora—spanning literary, technical, and commercial texts—presents an opportunity to systematically analyze patterns of linguistic transfer, ideological shifts, and institutional influences across time and geographies. However, processing these heterogeneous datasets (e.g., parallel texts, translation metadata, paratextual commentaries) at scale requires advanced computational capabilities beyond local infrastructure. The research will develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and contemporary translation data, including transformer-based models fine-tuned to detect stylistic anomalies, semantic distortions, and sociolinguistic biases in translated works. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model how translation norms emerge through interactions between translators, institutions, and audiences, incorporating real-world data on publishing trends and geopolitical contexts. By integrating machine learning, network analysis, and computational linguistics, this project aims to uncover systemic factors shaping translation outcomes—such as the impact of colonial histories on technical translation practices or the role of digital platforms in homogenizing literary translation. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for corpus-based translation analysis, a public repository of annotated multilingual datasets, and empirically grounded frameworks for evaluating equity in global translation workflows. The computational demands—training multilingual models on terabytes of text, running thousands of simulation iterations with parameter variations, and cross-referencing results against sociohistorical databases—necessitate HPC support for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated workflows. Findings will advance interdisciplinary scholarship in translation theory while informing practical strategies for ethical translation policy and technology design.
cip_definition: A multidisciplinary program that prepares individuals to explore the historical, social, institutional and cultural facets of translation. Includes instruction in general and literary translation, business translation, technical translation, and other specific applications of linguistic skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research in Thai language and literature, addressing critical gaps in scalable analysis of Thai textual corpora. While Thai is a linguistically complex language with rich dialectal diversity and a unique orthographic system, computational tools for its large-scale analysis remain underdeveloped compared to those for Indo-European languages. This limits scholarly capacity to systematically study historical language evolution, dialect variation, and stylistic patterns in Thai literature across genres and periods. The proposed research will develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for Thai, utilizing transformer-based models and unsupervised learning techniques to analyze multi-genre corpora spanning classical literature, modern prose, and regional oral narratives. Key computational challenges include processing Thai’s non-segmented script, dialectal code-mixing, and sparse annotated training data. HPC resources will enable distributed training of custom tokenization models, parallelized comparative analysis of syntactic structures across historical texts, and semantic clustering of thematic motifs in literary works. Expected outcomes include: (1) open-source NLP tools for Thai dialect identification and temporal linguistic feature extraction; (2) a diachronic corpus mapping lexical and grammatical shifts in Thai literary language from the 15th century to present; and (3) quantitative frameworks for detecting authorial style and intertextual relationships in classical poetry. By integrating computational methods with philological expertise, this work will establish new methodologies for digital humanities scholarship in Southeast Asian languages while preserving linguistic heritage. The requested resources directly support computationally intensive tasks—including GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale text embedding generation—that are infeasible with standard academic computing infrastructure. Outcomes will benefit interdisciplinary researchers, educators developing Thai language technologies, and cultural institutions curating digital archives.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Thai languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize high-performance engine tuning and aftermarket modification processes, with the goal of reducing trial-and-error testing while improving power output, efficiency, and emissions compliance. Current methods for enhancing diesel and automotive engines rely heavily on empirical dynamometer testing and technician expertise, which are time-intensive, resource-limited, and often fail to account for multivariate interactions between fuel systems, exhaust flow dynamics, and engine control unit parameters. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining 3D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of combustion chambers and exhaust systems with machine learning algorithms trained on dynamometer datasets. High-performance computing resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of piston geometry, turbocharger configurations, and fuel injection timing across diverse operating conditions. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) will model thermal and mechanical stresses in modified powertrain components to predict failure modes. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from partner automotive workshops, creating a feedback loop to refine predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include a decision-support framework for identifying optimal modification combinations, predictive maps for engine tuning under real-world load scenarios, and open-access simulation templates tailored to common aftermarket parts. This work will directly benefit technical education by providing students with virtual experimentation tools to study engine performance trade-offs, while offering industry partners reduced development cycles for performance upgrades. The requested computing resources are essential given the need for massively parallel simulations of transient combustion events and the iterative nature of machine learning model training on heterogeneous engine telemetry data.
cip_title: High Performance and Custom Engine Technician/ Mechanic
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to increase the power of diesel and automotive engines; enhance the performance of automobiles; and repair, service, and maintain high performance vehicles. Includes instruction in adding performance accessories; modifying powertrains; tuning custom engines, suspension, and exhaust systems; and using dynamometers and other diagnostic equipment.

abstract: Maternal morbidity and mortality remain critical public health challenges, with persistent disparities in outcomes influenced by biological, social, and structural factors. Current clinical decision-making tools in women’s health nursing often lack the granularity to account for complex interactions between genetic predispositions, pharmacogenomic variability, and environmental determinants, particularly in marginalized populations. This project proposes to develop predictive models for adverse maternal outcomes and individualized treatment optimization using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate multi-modal datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data from underrepresented cohorts, and community-level social determinants of health, to identify risk trajectories and therapeutic targets. Computational workflows will employ machine learning frameworks (e.g., neural networks, ensemble methods) to analyze high-dimensional data, coupled with simulation-based approaches to model pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic responses in diverse obstetric and gynecologic scenarios. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of EHR data, perform genome-wide association studies (GWAS) at scale, and train computationally intensive models that account for temporal and spatial heterogeneity in health outcomes. Expected outcomes include validated risk stratification tools for preeclampsia, postpartum hemorrhage, and medication adverse events, as well as open-source algorithms to guide dose personalization for commonly prescribed therapeutics in women’s health. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance precision health frameworks in nursing practice, reduce inequities in care delivery, and provide scalable computational resources for future studies in women’s health. The results will directly inform clinical guidelines and educational curricula for advanced practice nurses, bridging gaps between data-driven discovery and patient-centered care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: Avionics systems in modern aircraft are increasingly complex, integrating advanced sensors, real-time communication networks, and adaptive control algorithms. While these systems improve safety and efficiency, their maintenance presents significant challenges due to interdependencies between components, dynamic operational conditions, and the need for rapid fault diagnosis. Current maintenance protocols often rely on static diagnostic frameworks or historical failure data, which struggle to account for emergent behaviors in interconnected systems or evolving environmental stressors. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational model to simulate avionics system performance under diverse operational and failure scenarios, enabling predictive maintenance strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct a multi-physics digital twin of a representative aircraft avionics suite, incorporating fluid dynamics (for thermal management), electromagnetic interference patterns, and real-time signal processing for sensor networks. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated fault data to identify early warning signatures of component degradation, with parallelized Monte Carlo methods used to quantify uncertainty across variable flight profiles and maintenance histories. The computational workflow will require large-scale matrix operations for finite element analysis, distributed memory architectures for ensemble simulations, and GPU acceleration for neural network training. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for optimizing maintenance intervals, reducing unplanned downtime, and improving fault localization accuracy by 30–40% compared to legacy methods. This work will directly support curriculum modernization in avionics maintenance training programs, providing students and industry partners with data-driven tools to address next-generation aircraft systems. By integrating HPC-enabled predictive analytics into maintenance workflows, the project aims to enhance operational safety while lowering lifecycle costs for aviation fleets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft operating, control, and electronic systems. Includes instruction in flight instrumentation, aircraft communications and homing systems, radar and other sensory systems, navigation aids, and specialized systems for various types of civilian and military aircraft.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision and efficacy in electrology, the specialized practice of permanent hair removal using targeted electrical currents. Despite its established clinical use, electrology lacks robust computational frameworks to model the biophysical interactions between electrical probes, skin tissue, and hair follicles. Current practice relies heavily on empirical protocols, leading to variability in treatment outcomes, client discomfort, and inefficiencies in probe design. This project aims to address these gaps by developing multiscale computational models to simulate the thermal, electrical, and mechanical dynamics of electrolysis, thermolysis, and blend modality treatments. A finite element analysis (FEA) approach will be employed to model tissue-probe interactions across spatial scales, integrating parameters such as current frequency, voltage, probe geometry, and tissue heterogeneity. These simulations will be validated against clinical data, including thermal imaging and histological outcomes, to ensure biological fidelity. Machine learning techniques will then optimize treatment parameters for diverse skin types and hair morphologies, reducing trial-and-error in practice. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations and large parameter spaces inherent to this nonlinear, multiphysics problem. Expected outcomes include predictive models for follicle destruction thresholds, optimized probe configurations, and evidence-based protocols to minimize collateral tissue damage. By bridging electrology’s practical expertise with computational biophysics, this work will establish a foundational framework for personalized, data-driven treatments, enhancing both safety and efficacy. The results will directly inform electrology training programs, equipment design, and regulatory standards, positioning computational modeling as a transformative tool in this specialized field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to permanently remove hair from the human scalp, face, and body using specialized charged solid needle probes, and to function as licensed electrologists and electrolysis technicians.  Includes instruction in direct current electrolysis, alternating current/high frequency thermolysis, blend/dual modality treatments, equipment theory and operation, safety and sanitation, client evaluation and care, laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing decentralized edge computing architectures for real-time, privacy-sensitive applications in healthcare IoT ecosystems. While edge computing offers latency and bandwidth benefits, existing resource allocation frameworks struggle to balance dynamic workloads, heterogeneous device capabilities, and stringent regulatory constraints—particularly in environments like hospital networks where data sovereignty and failover resilience are critical. Current approaches in IT service management often prioritize generic cloud-edge paradigms, neglecting the unique interdependencies between device-level autonomy, context-aware workload partitioning, and compliance-aware data routing in regulated sectors. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel computational framework integrating adaptive graph neural networks with constraint-driven optimization to model multi-tier edge networks under dynamically evolving operational and regulatory conditions. The research will employ high-fidelity simulations of hospital IoT deployments, leveraging synthetic and anonymized real-world datasets to train models that predict optimal resource allocation while enforcing HIPAA-compliant data flow constraints. High-performance computing resources are essential for scaling these simulations to realistic network sizes (10,000+ nodes) and for parallelizing the evaluation of distributed optimization strategies across diverse failure scenarios. Expected outcomes include a dynamically reconfigurable allocation engine capable of reducing edge-to-cloud latency by 30–50% in constrained environments while maintaining audit-ready compliance logs. This work will contribute new methodologies for administrating IT services in regulated edge ecosystems, with implications for emergency response systems, smart manufacturing, and other domains requiring tight integration of computational efficiency and governance-aware resource management. The computational artifacts and datasets will be made available to support further research in specialized IT administration frameworks.
cip_title: Computer/ Information Technology Services Administration and Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer/information technology services administration and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between household decision-making dynamics and resource management strategies under conditions of socioeconomic disruption, with a focus on optimizing resilience in diverse family structures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the study will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate decision pathways related to financial allocation, time use, and consumption patterns across heterogeneous households. Current methodologies in family science often rely on survey-based or qualitative approaches, which struggle to capture nonlinear interactions and feedback loops inherent in multi-agent systems. The computational approach integrates granular demographic data, longitudinal economic indicators, and behavioral parameters derived from machine learning analysis of existing household datasets. By simulating millions of scenario permutations—including job loss, healthcare emergencies, and supply chain interruptions—the models will identify critical leverage points for enhancing adaptive capacity. The HPC environment is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of variables, including real-time optimization of intervention strategies through evolutionary algorithms. Expected outcomes include a scalable modeling framework capable of predicting household-level resilience thresholds and generating personalized resource allocation recommendations. This work bridges computational social science with human development theory, offering novel insights into how digital twins of family systems can inform both policy-level interventions and individualized support tools. The resulting computational platform will be adaptable to emerging challenges in household sustainability, with potential applications ranging from personalized financial planning aids to crisis response simulations for community organizations. By advancing data-driven approaches in family and consumer sciences, this project aims to establish new paradigms for studying human-environment interactions at microsystem scales.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on family and consumer sciences, including how individuals develop and function in family, work, and community settings and how they relate to their physical, social, emotional, and intellectual environments.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize precision cutting workflows in commercial meat processing, addressing inefficiencies in yield prediction, tool wear management, and food safety compliance. Traditional meat cutting operations rely heavily on manual expertise to balance product quality with regulatory requirements, often resulting in suboptimal material utilization (15-20% loss industry-wide) and variable compliance outcomes. We propose a hybrid simulation approach combining biomechanical modeling of carcass structures, machine learning-based cut path optimization, and microbial growth prediction under dynamic storage conditions. High-performance computing resources are required to process 3D scans of livestock anatomy (captured via CT and spectral imaging), simulate tissue separation dynamics using finite element analysis at millimeter resolution, and train neural networks on multi-objective optimization parameters including yield maximization, energy expenditure reduction, and sanitation protocol adherence. The computational pipeline will integrate real-time data streams from IoT-enabled cutting implements monitoring blade integrity and bacterial load, enabling adaptive recalibration of cutting strategies. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of recommending cut sequences that improve yield by 8-12% while maintaining USDA safety standards, predictive models for tool maintenance scheduling that reduce equipment downtime by 30%, and digital twins of storage environments that minimize spoilage risks through probabilistic shelf-life forecasting. By bridging gaps between empirical butchering practices, materials science, and computational microbiology, this research establishes a novel paradigm for sustainable meat processing—a $250B global industry currently lacking AI-driven optimization tools tailored to its unique biological and regulatory constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, cut, and package animal meat products in commercial establishments and to function as licensed meat cutters/butchers.  Includes instruction in product recognition for beef, veal, lamb, pork, poultry, and fancy and smoked meats; retail and wholesale cutting and specialty cuts; packaging and counter display; shop safety; meat sanitation, storage and rotation; quality control; meat handling laws and regulations; and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to enhance pedagogical training for pre-service computer science educators through adaptive simulation and data-driven feedback systems. A critical challenge in computer teacher education is the lack of accessible, high-fidelity environments for educators to practice responsive teaching strategies tailored to diverse student needs in computational thinking and programming concepts. Existing training models often rely on limited classroom role-playing scenarios or static case studies, which inadequately prepare teachers for the dynamic, problem-solving nature of computer science instruction.
