To address this gap, we propose building a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform that simulates heterogeneous virtual classrooms through agent-based modeling and real-time interaction analysis. The system will leverage parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms to generate student personas with distinct learning trajectories, error patterns, and engagement behaviors, replicating the variability encountered in authentic educational settings. Machine learning models trained on multimodal datasets (including code submission histories, discourse patterns, and gesture recognition from existing teaching footage) will provide instructors with granular feedback on their pedagogical choices. The computational intensity of simultaneously modeling hundreds of interactive agents, processing natural language queries, and maintaining low-latency response times for immersive training scenarios necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for simulating computational pedagogy scenarios, 2) empirical evidence on effective intervention strategies for common conceptual hurdles in programming education, and 3) performance benchmarks for teacher responsiveness in adaptive learning environments. By enabling large-scale experimentation with synthetic classroom dynamics, this work aims to establish new standards for evidence-based teacher preparation in computer science education while advancing methodological approaches to educational simulation through heterogeneous computing paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach computer education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias remain a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity, with treatment efficacy limited by incomplete understanding of patient-specific electrophysiological mechanisms. Existing approaches, such as catheter ablation, often rely on generalized anatomical templates, resulting in variable success rates and prolonged procedures. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing personalized computational models of cardiac electrical activity to optimize therapeutic strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct patient-specific atrial and ventricular models derived from clinical imaging (MRI/CT) and electroanatomic mapping data. These models will integrate biophysical properties, including tissue conductivity, ion channel dynamics, and fibrosis distribution, simulated using finite element methods. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to analyze multi-scale electrophysiological datasets, identifying critical arrhythmogenic substrates and predicting optimal ablation targets. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to assess arrhythmia susceptibility under varying physiological conditions and virtual ablation scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for ablation targeting, reducing procedural time and recurrence rates by 30-50% compared to conventional methods. Additionally, this work will elucidate mechanisms of arrhythmia initiation in structural heart disease, informing novel therapeutic approaches. The computational framework developed here will serve as a translatable platform for clinical decision support, bridging the gap between quantitative modeling and bedside care. By addressing the computational demands of multi-modal data integration and real-time simulation, this research aims to establish a paradigm shift toward precision electrophysiology, ultimately improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare costs associated with recurrent arrhythmias.
cip_definition: Research focused on, within the subspecialty of cardiovascular disease, which prepares physicians in intricate technical procedures to evaluate heart rhythms and determine appropriate treatment.

abstract: Improving animal feed efficiency through precision nutrition requires understanding complex interactions between dietary components, host metabolism, and microbial communities in the gastrointestinal tract. Current models often oversimplify these dynamic systems, limiting their predictive capacity for optimizing feed formulations. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating mechanistic models of nutrient metabolism with machine learning approaches to predict outcomes of novel feed strategies in ruminants. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and validate genome-scale metabolic network models of rumen microbiota using metagenomic and metabolomic datasets from in vivo trials. We will employ flux balance analysis and agent-based modeling to simulate microbial community dynamics under varying dietary conditions, coupled with deep neural networks trained on historical productivity data to identify nonlinear relationships between nutrient inputs and animal outputs (e.g., milk yield, methane emissions). The computational pipeline will process >10 TB of multi-omics data while running ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainty in model predictions. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for virtual testing of feed additives and ration formulations, reducing costly empirical trials. By elucidating how specific dietary interventions modulate microbial contributions to protein synthesis and energy harvest, this work will advance strategies for sustainable livestock production. The requested HPC allocation will enable the intensive parameter optimization and parallelized simulations required to bridge molecular-scale microbial interactions with herd-level productivity metrics, directly supporting the program’s mission to enhance animal health and agricultural resource efficiency through nutritional innovation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biology and chemistry of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, water, vitamins, and feed additives as related to animal health and the production of improved animal products. Includes instruction in nutrition science, animal health and physiology, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, animal husbandry, and food science.

abstract: Adolescents face complex health challenges shaped by dynamic interactions between biological development, psychosocial stressors, and environmental factors. Current clinical models often struggle to predict individualized risks for adverse outcomes—such as mental health crises, substance use escalation, or chronic disease progression—due to limitations in analyzing multidimensional, longitudinal datasets. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging data, genomic biomarkers, and social determinants of health to model trajectories of adolescent health outcomes. The primary research problem involves resolving the computational demands of harmonizing high-dimensional datasets across timescales and modalities while preserving patient privacy. We propose using federated learning architectures to train predictive models on distributed EHR data from 15 pediatric hospitals, combined with GPU-accelerated analyses of neurodevelopmental imaging patterns (3T MRI) and polygenic risk scores. Deep learning models, including transformer-based temporal networks and 3D convolutional neural networks, will be optimized to identify cross-domain risk signatures predictive of depression relapse, metabolic syndrome, and treatment adherence. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) large-scale hyperparameter optimization of ensemble models, (2) simulation of synthetic cohorts to address data sparsity in underrepresented populations, and (3) real-time sensitivity analyses for clinical translation. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adolescent health risk stratification, validated against prospective clinical data from 2,000 patients. This work will advance precision medicine in adolescent care by enabling computationally intensive integrations of biological and social data, directly addressing healthcare disparities through improved early intervention targeting. The requested resources will support 18 months of model development, requiring 256-core parallel processing, 8 TB of temporary storage for intermediate imaging outputs, and GPU nodes for neural network training.
cip_definition: Research focused on the unique physical, psychological, and social characteristics of adolescents and their healthcare problems and needs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation for private security operations, addressing the challenge of real-time adaptation in unpredictable environments. Traditional security deployment strategies often rely on static protocols, which struggle to account for fluctuating threat levels, heterogeneous client environments, and evolving criminal tactics. The research problem centers on creating adaptive models that integrate real-time data streams—such as surveillance feeds, IoT sensor networks, and historical incident reports—to predict and preempt security breaches. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate patrol routes, threat response protocols, and resource prioritization under variable conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to reflect the complexity of urban and industrial environments, enabling parallel processing of multi-agent interactions and large-scale scenario testing. Additionally, the project will employ graph neural networks (GNNs) to analyze spatial-temporal relationships in security incident data, identifying latent patterns in criminal behavior across disparate client sites. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of recommending optimal resource distributions—such as personnel shifts, surveillance focus areas, and emergency response staging—while balancing cost-efficiency and risk mitigation. This work bridges computational social science and operational research, offering a novel methodology for loss prevention that adapts to emergent threats. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to establish a benchmark for data-driven security strategies, directly enhancing the efficacy of private security services in safeguarding assets and reducing preventable losses. The resulting framework will be validated against real-world case studies from corporate and residential security providers, with potential applications in critical infrastructure protection and event security planning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine inspection, patrol and crime prevention services for private clients. Includes instruction in the provision of personal protection as well as property security.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens affecting animals presents a critical challenge to veterinary medicine, with direct implications for animal welfare, food security, and zoonotic disease risks. Current gaps in understanding the genomic plasticity of veterinary pathogens and their interactions with host immune systems hinder the development of targeted therapies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic datasets and model host-pathogen dynamics at unprecedented resolution. The research will focus on clinically relevant bacterial species, including *Staphylococcus pseudintermedius* and multidrug-resistant *Escherichia coli*, which cause severe infections in companion and livestock animals. Whole-genome sequencing data from clinical isolates will be integrated with transcriptomic and proteomic profiles to identify AMR-associated genetic markers and regulatory pathways. Computational methods will include machine learning models to predict resistance phenotypes from genomic features, molecular dynamics simulations to characterize mutations altering drug-target binding affinities, and agent-based models to simulate immune response dynamics during infection. These analyses require HPC resources due to the scale of genomic datasets (>10,000 isolates), the complexity of simulating protein-ligand interactions across conformational landscapes, and the need for high-throughput parallelization. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel AMR biomarkers, predictive models linking pathogen evolution to clinical outcomes, and mechanistic insights into immune evasion strategies. The findings will directly inform the design of rapid diagnostics and narrow-spectrum antimicrobials tailored to veterinary pathogens, reducing reliance on broad-spectrum drugs. By elucidating transmission dynamics between animal populations, this work will also contribute to One Health frameworks aimed at mitigating zoonotic AMR spread. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome the limitations of in silico analyses on local infrastructure, enabling iterative, large-scale simulations that bridge genomic data and clinical applications in veterinary microbiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-border information operations in geopolitical crises using computational social science methods, with a focus on real-time data integration and network analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how state and non-state actors exploit decentralized communication platforms to manipulate public perception during emerging conflicts, particularly in understudied regions where digital infrastructure intersects with fragile governance. Current models of information warfare analysis remain siloed, lacking capacity to process multilingual unstructured data at scale or model adaptive adversarial strategies in dynamic environments. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment and narrative detection in 15 languages, temporal network analysis of coordinated account behavior, and agent-based modeling to simulate crisis escalation pathways. The computational framework will ingest heterogeneous data streams—including social media posts, encrypted messaging app metadata, and satellite-derived mobility patterns—to identify latent signatures of hybrid threat campaigns. Leveraging GPU-accelerated transformer models and distributed graph databases, the system will enable near-real-time detection of influence operation patterns across terabyte-scale datasets. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of three case studies: maritime territorial disputes in Southeast Asia, election interference patterns in post-Soviet states, and humanitarian crisis narratives in the Sahel region. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational disinformation research, novel metrics for assessing information resilience in national security frameworks, and predictive models of cross-platform narrative diffusion. By advancing methodological integration between social network analysis, security studies, and AI-driven linguistics, this work aims to establish new standards for evidence-based policy responses to next-generation information threats.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_title: International Relations and National Security Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in international relations and national security studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Understanding the dynamics of intercultural relations in increasingly diverse societies requires novel approaches to model complex, non-linear interactions between cultural values, socio-political factors, and institutional policies. Existing frameworks often oversimplify these interactions, limiting their utility in predicting conflict triggers or identifying pathways to sustainable cooperation. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational model integrating agent-based simulations, machine learning, and network analysis to study emergent group behaviors in multicultural environments. Leveraging demographic datasets, historical conflict records, and real-time social media streams, the model will simulate scenarios spanning educational, urban, and workplace settings under varying policy conditions. High-performance computing resources are critical to parallelize thousands of parameterized simulations, process multi-terabyte datasets, and train deep learning architectures to detect subtle patterns in intercultural communication and conflict escalation. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework to quantify how localized interventions—such as community dialogue programs or inclusive policy design—ripple through interconnected social systems, and (2) predictive tools to assess resilience against polarization in hypothetical demographic or economic shifts. By bridging computational scalability with sociological nuance, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for managing diversity in rapidly changing societies while establishing methodological benchmarks for interdisciplinary complexity studies. The computational artifacts and anonymized datasets will be made available to support replication and policy prototyping.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and personalized pharmacotherapy demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in optimizing drug efficacy, minimizing adverse effects, and understanding molecular interactions at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-scale computational models for predicting drug-target interactions, pharmacokinetic profiles, and polypharmacy risks. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) employing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the binding mechanisms of novel therapeutics to disease-specific protein targets, including those with high conformational flexibility or mutation-driven resistance, and (2) applying machine learning (ML) frameworks to analyze large-scale pharmacogenomic datasets, enabling the identification of patient-specific factors influencing drug response variability. Computational workflows will integrate quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods for modeling enzymatic reactions, hybrid ML-MD pipelines for virtual screening of compound libraries, and graph neural networks to predict drug-drug interaction risks in multi-medication regimens. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized MD simulations and distributed computing architectures for training deep learning models on heterogeneous biomedical data, including electronic health records, structural proteomics, and metabolomics datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of lead compounds with improved selectivity for neurodegenerative disease targets, predictive models for dose optimization in renal-impaired populations, and open-source tools for real-time polypharmacy risk assessment in clinical pharmacy practice. By addressing computational bottlenecks in simulating complex biological systems and analyzing high-dimensional healthcare data, this work aims to advance precision pharmacy paradigms while providing a scalable framework for accelerating therapeutic development and improving medication safety outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent or employed practice of preparing and dispensing drugs and medications in consultation with prescribing physicians and other health care professionals, and for managing pharmacy practices and counseling patients. Includes instruction in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmacy practice, pharmacy administration, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the cultural and linguistic evolution of Slavic diasporic communities through large-scale textual and visual data. Traditional methods in Slavic Studies, often limited to manual archival work or small-scale surveys, struggle to address the dynamic, transnational interactions that shape diasporic identities over time. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural transmission, adaptation, and hybridity across dispersed Slavic populations by examining digitized folklore collections, multilingual periodicals, and community-generated media from the 19th century to the present. A computational approach will be employed, combining natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis (including Cyrillic and Latin script variations), network analysis to map transnational cultural exchanges, and machine learning models to detect visual motifs in folk art and digital media. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data, training transformer-based models on low-resource Slavic languages, and running iterative simulations of cultural diffusion pathways. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital archive of annotated materials, quantitative frameworks for measuring cultural hybridity, and visualizations of diasporic networks across temporal and geographic scales. This work will advance Slavic Studies by enabling systematic comparisons of cultural retention strategies among immigrant groups, challenging monolithic narratives of Slavic identity, and illuminating understudied interactions between diasporic communities and their host societies. The computational tools developed will also contribute to interdisciplinary methodologies for ethnic and cultural studies, particularly in analyzing non-Western, multilingual datasets. By integrating HPC-driven scale with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to redefine scholarly understanding of Slavic diasporas as dynamic, interconnected systems rather than isolated cultural enclaves.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Slavic peoples inhabiting Europe, Asia, and in immigrant groups elsewhere, including the study of the emergence and migration patterns of Slavic culture, languages, and populations.

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems require precise maintenance and optimization to ensure reliability, efficiency, and safety under diverse operational conditions. Traditional experimental and analytical methods are often insufficient to capture the complex multiphysics interactions within modern turbine engines, leading to suboptimal performance and unanticipated failures. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that simulate critical aspects of aircraft powerplant systems, including thermal management, structural integrity, and fuel combustion dynamics. Using multiphysics simulation frameworks integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning algorithms, the research will analyze high-fidelity datasets generated from engine sensor networks and operational profiles. HPC capabilities will enable the resolution of microsecond-scale transient events in combustion chambers, stress distribution in turbine blades under extreme temperatures, and real-time predictive maintenance algorithms. The computational models will also assess wear patterns in propeller assemblies and optimize lubrication flow in gearbox systems under variable load scenarios. The expected outcomes include optimized cooling channel geometries to mitigate thermal degradation, predictive models for component fatigue, and data-driven strategies for fuel injection timing. These results will directly inform maintenance protocols, reduce operational costs, and extend engine service life. By integrating HPC-driven insights into aircraft powerplant technology, this research aims to advance the precision of technician training programs and contribute to next-generation engine design standards. The project aligns with industry demands for sustainable aviation solutions, emphasizing reduced emissions and enhanced operational safety through computational innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: Healthcare environments are complex systems where spatial design intersects with clinical outcomes, patient experience, and operational efficiency. Despite growing recognition of architecture’s role in healing, existing tools for modeling healthcare spaces remain siloed, relying on static simulations that inadequately capture dynamic human-environment interactions. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate and optimize healthcare facility designs through high-resolution, real-time modeling of multi-agent interactions (patients, staff, equipment) and environmental variables (light, acoustics, airflow). The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate parametric architectural models with discrete-event simulations, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and sensor-derived behavioral datasets. Key computational challenges include scaling agent-based models to simulate thousands of concurrent actors, resolving micro-scale spatial conflicts in macro-scale floorplans, and training neural networks to predict stress-reducing design features. By iteratively testing virtual environments against clinical outcome proxies—such as simulated staff workflow efficiency, patient mobility patterns, and pathogen dispersion risks—the framework will identify design configurations that balance operational demands with evidence-based healing principles. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive healthcare space planning and novel metrics quantifying design impact on care delivery. This work bridges architectural theory, human-computer interaction, and healthcare operations research, offering a computational foundation for data-driven design standards in rapidly evolving clinical contexts. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale data integration, and validation studies comparing virtual predictions with real-world observational data from partner hospitals.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and performance of healthcare environments to optimize healing. Includes instruction in interior design, architecture, healing sciences, healthcare environments, human-centered design, and healthcare delivery.

abstract: The integration of high-resolution histopathological imaging, multi-omics data, and clinical patient information presents a critical computational challenge in advancing precision diagnostics for complex skin diseases. Current approaches in dermatopathology often rely on manual, time-consuming analysis of tissue samples and disjointed molecular datasets, limiting the ability to identify subtle diagnostic patterns or molecular drivers of disorders such as cutaneous lymphomas, autoimmune blistering diseases, and rare genodermatoses. This project proposes the development of a scalable computational framework to unify heterogeneous data types through deep learning and network-based analytics, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. High-throughput whole-slide image processing will employ GPU-accelerated convolutional neural networks to quantify spatial features of inflammation, neoplasia, and tissue remodeling across terabyte-scale imaging datasets. Parallelized bioinformatics pipelines will analyze paired single-cell RNA sequencing and proteomic profiles to resolve disease-specific cellular states, while graph neural networks will model cross-modal interactions between histologic, molecular, and clinical variables. The HPC environment is essential for managing memory-intensive image analysis, iterative model training across thousands of experimental conditions, and large-scale integration of multi-dimensional data. Expected outcomes include automated diagnostic classifiers with explainable AI components for clinical translation, novel biomarkers for therapeutic targeting, and publicly available computational workflows optimized for dermatopathology research. By establishing an HPC-supported infrastructure for multimodal data synthesis, this work aims to address critical bottlenecks in diagnostic accuracy and mechanistic understanding of understudied dermatologic conditions, directly supporting the training of pathology residents and computational biologists through hands-on engagement with cutting-edge analytical pipelines.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical and microscopic diagnosis and analysis of skin diseases and disorders. May included related research in laboratory administration and the supervision and training of support personnel.

abstract: The proposed research aims to investigate the mechanistic pathways and kinetic behavior of complex, multi-step chemical reactions in solution-phase environments, with a focus on systems relevant to sustainable catalysis and green chemistry. A central challenge in modeling such reactions lies in accurately simulating solvent effects, transient intermediates, and non-adiabatic electron transfer processes, which require quantum mechanical precision over experimentally relevant timescales. To address this, we will employ hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations coupled with enhanced sampling techniques, including metadynamics and path-integral molecular dynamics. These methods will be implemented using the CP2K and ORCA software packages on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to model systems containing 500–1,000 atoms over nanosecond-scale trajectories. Key targets include elucidating solvation-driven selectivity in transition metal-catalyzed C–H activation reactions and characterizing proton-coupled electron transfer mechanisms in bio-inspired redox mediators. The computational workflow will integrate machine learning potentials trained on ab initio data to accelerate free energy calculations while maintaining chemical accuracy. Expected outcomes include atomistic insights into solvent-catalyst interactions, predictive kinetic models for reaction optimization, and benchmark datasets for validating density functional theory (DFT) functionals in multi-component systems. This work directly supports experimental collaborations developing Earth-abundant catalysts for CO₂ reduction and hydrogen production. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of configurational sampling, electronic structure calculations, and statistical averaging across reaction coordinates. By bridging quantum dynamics with macroscopic observables, this project advances fundamental understanding of reaction engineering principles while providing computational tools to accelerate the design of energy-efficient chemical processes.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition and behavior of matter, including its micro- and macro-structure, the processes of chemical change, and the theoretical description and laboratory simulation of these phenomena.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay between legal frameworks governing energy transitions and emerging environmental justice disputes. As nations accelerate decarbonization efforts, regulatory systems face unprecedented strain from conflicting mandates: balancing rapid infrastructure deployment (e.g., renewable energy siting, grid modernization) with equitable resource distribution and procedural fairness for marginalized communities. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically evaluate the growing volume of litigation data, regulatory comments, and land-use decisions shaping these tensions. Our computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis to map patterns in three key areas: 1) judicial interpretations of "public interest" in energy project approvals across 50,000+ U.S. state and federal cases, 2) semantic shifts in environmental impact assessments under evolving climate policy regimes, and 3) spatial correlations between energy development patterns and historical environmental justice violations. By training transformer-based models on a curated corpus of legal documents, administrative records, and geospatial metadata, we aim to identify latent biases in decision-making frameworks and simulate policy intervention scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of heterogeneous datasets at unprecedented scale, including OCR restoration of legacy documents and real-time sentiment analysis of public participation records. Expected outcomes include a predictive model for assessing regulatory conflict risks in energy transition projects and a novel taxonomy of legal arguments bridging property rights with climate equity principles. This work will provide policymakers with computational tools to anticipate bottlenecks in clean energy deployment while advancing methodological innovations for quantitative legal analysis in resource governance contexts.
cip_title: Energy, Environment, and Natural Resources Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing the energy industry, environmental protection, natural resources and land use, and related topics.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in precision medicine by developing computational models to predict patient-specific responses to combination therapies for complex chronic diseases. Current approaches often fail to account for the dynamic interplay between genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors that influence treatment efficacy, particularly in conditions such as autoimmune disorders or multi-factorial metabolic syndromes. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omics data (genome-wide sequencing, proteomics, and metabolomics) with longitudinal clinical records from diverse patient cohorts. A hybrid machine learning framework will be implemented, combining graph neural networks to model biological pathway interactions and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate treatment optimization over time. Computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale datasets, training high-dimensional models with interpretability constraints, and conducting sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous virtual patient populations. The HPC environment will enable parallelized model training, large-scale parameter sweeps, and validation against experimental datasets from collaborating clinical institutions. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated predictive platform for identifying optimal therapeutic combinations tailored to individual patient profiles, (2) novel biomarkers of treatment resistance, and (3) open-source tools for simulating intervention scenarios in underrepresented demographic groups. This work directly supports the translation of complex biological data into clinically actionable insights, with potential to reduce adverse drug events and improve therapeutic targeting in populations with comorbid conditions. The requested computing resources are essential for achieving statistically robust results within biologically relevant timeframes, as conventional infrastructure cannot support the memory-intensive analyses or iterative model refinement required for this precision medicine pipeline.
cip_definition: Any program in medicine, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the precision and efficiency of ophthalmic lens fabrication by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize lens design and manufacturing processes. Current methods for producing corrective lenses rely on empirical adjustments and simplified optical models, which can lead to suboptimal visual outcomes, material waste, and prolonged production timelines. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating optical theory, patient-specific anatomical data, and advanced manufacturing parameters. High-fidelity ray-tracing simulations will model light propagation through lenses to evaluate optical performance under diverse conditions, while finite element analysis will assess structural integrity during lens surfacing, grinding, and impact resistance testing. Machine learning algorithms will further optimize lens geometry and material selection by analyzing large datasets of patient prescriptions, corneal topography, and historical fabrication outcomes. These computationally intensive tasks necessitate HPC resources to manage parallelized simulations, iterative design optimizations, and multi-parameter sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive models for personalized lens designs that minimize aberrations, enhance durability, and reduce production errors. The project will also generate open-access computational tools to streamline prescription interpretation and improve alignment between laboratory processes and clinical requirements. By advancing the integration of computational precision into ophthalmic laboratory workflows, this research aims to elevate the standard of care for corrective eyewear, reduce costs associated with trial-and-error fabrication, and support the development of next-generation lens coatings and frame materials. The results will directly benefit training programs in ophthalmic technology by providing data-driven insights into optical manufacturing principles and safety-critical testing protocols.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: The study of neural circuit dynamics underlying complex behaviors and cognitive functions requires sophisticated computational approaches to model and analyze large-scale, high-dimensional datasets. Current limitations in processing power and memory allocation hinder the ability to simulate biologically realistic neural networks or integrate multimodal data (e.g., electrophysiological recordings, calcium imaging, and behavioral metrics) at the spatiotemporal resolution necessary to capture emergent network properties. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models of cortico-hippocampal interactions during memory consolidation. We will employ biophysically detailed neural network simulations incorporating synaptic plasticity rules, coupled with machine learning pipelines to identify latent activity patterns across terabytes of experimental data. The computational framework will integrate GPU-accelerated simulations using NEURON and NEST simulators with distributed deep learning workflows (TensorFlow, PyTorch) to map network dynamics onto behavioral outcomes. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to >100,000 neurons with realistic connectivity, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized parameter sweeps, and processing high-resolution neural datasets at scale. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how oscillatory synchrony and synaptic homeostasis jointly stabilize memory representations during sleep, as well as an open-source toolset for simulating and analyzing multiregional brain circuits. This work will directly test hypotheses about circuit-level dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases, providing a computational platform to evaluate potential neuromodulatory interventions. By bridging systems neuroscience with advanced computational modeling, the project aims to advance mechanistic understanding of memory-related disorders while establishing scalable workflows for data-driven neurobiological discovery.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in neurobiology and neurosciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex, longitudinal datasets examining the interplay between early childhood developmental trajectories and dynamic family systems. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how nonlinear, multilevel interactions—such as caregiver mental health fluctuations, socioeconomic stressors, and early intervention efficacy—coalesce to influence developmental outcomes in children aged 0–6. Traditional statistical methods often oversimplify these interdependencies due to computational constraints, limiting actionable insights for tailored family support strategies. By employing agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques, we aim to simulate heterogeneous family environments and identify patterns predictive of resilience or risk. The computational approach integrates three components: (1) ABM frameworks to model bidirectional caregiver-child interactions across temporal and contextual scales, (2) ensemble ML algorithms to analyze multimodal data (e.g., ecological momentary assessments, administrative records, and neurobehavioral metrics), and (3) network analysis to map cascading effects of interventions within family subsystems. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the high-dimensional parameter space, running parallelized simulations under diverse hypothetical scenarios, and optimizing predictive models via hyperparameter tuning. Expected outcomes include the identification of critical leverage points for early childhood interventions, a scalable computational toolkit for assessing family-system dynamics, and evidence-based guidelines for personalizing support services. This work bridges developmental science with computational social science, advancing methodological innovation in a field traditionally reliant on small-sample studies. By elucidating how micro-level interactions propagate to macro-level outcomes, the project holds transformative potential for policies addressing childhood inequities and fostering intergenerational well-being.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the development and learning of children from birth to six years old within the context of the family. Includes instruction in child abuse and neglect, child and infant growth and development, early childhood education, early childhood language and literacy, early childhood math and science, early childhood special education, family literacy, family sociology, family and marriage relations, assessment and measurement, psychology, and psychopathology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of evaluating the efficacy of large-scale educational interventions using advanced computational methods. Educational evaluation increasingly relies on complex, multi-source datasets—including longitudinal student performance metrics, demographic records, and qualitative feedback—to assess program outcomes. Traditional statistical tools often struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data types at scale or model non-linear relationships between intervention components and student outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The framework will employ ensemble models to combine structured quantitative data (e.g., standardized test scores, attendance) with unstructured qualitative data (e.g., open-ended teacher surveys) processed via natural language processing (NLP) techniques. A key innovation involves simulating counterfactual scenarios through agent-based modeling to estimate intervention impacts under varying socioeconomic conditions. The computational demands of training these models on statewide K-12 datasets (N ≈ 2.5 million students) and conducting Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and parallelized workflows. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated open-source toolkit for causal inference in educational program evaluation, 2) scalable pipelines for merging administrative and text-based data, and 3) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing intervention designs across diverse school districts. By enabling faster, more granular analysis of equity-related outcomes (e.g., achievement gaps by socioeconomic status), this work aims to advance methodological standards in evaluation research while directly informing state-level policy decisions on resource allocation for Title I programs. The requested computing resources will support both the initial model development phase and ongoing validation studies using real-time data from 12 partner school districts.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for generating information about educational programs, personnel and methods, and the analysis of such information for planning purposes. Includes instruction in evaluation theory, evaluation research design and planning, administering evaluations and related data collection activities, data reporting requirements, data analysis and interpretation, and related economic and policy issues.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop neuroadaptive interface systems that dynamically respond to users’ cognitive and affective states in real time, integrating multimodal biometric data (e.g., EEG, eye tracking, galvanic skin response) with behavioral interaction patterns. While traditional human-computer interaction (HCI) frameworks prioritize usability and task efficiency, they often lack the computational capacity to process high-dimensional physiological datasets at low latency, limiting their ability to support truly responsive, personalized interfaces. The core challenge lies in creating a scalable architecture capable of fusing heterogeneous data streams—sampled at varying frequencies and resolutions—into a unified model that predicts user states while operating within strict real-time constraints. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining lightweight edge computing for initial signal preprocessing with high-performance computing (HPC) resources for training and deploying deep learning models that generalize across diverse user populations. The HPC environment will enable parallelized hyperparameter optimization for spatiotemporal neural networks designed to handle irregularly sampled time-series data, alongside large-scale simulations of interface adaptation strategies under varying cognitive load scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for neuroadaptive system design, validated through controlled experiments measuring performance and cognitive load in augmented reality (AR) navigation tasks. By leveraging HPC resources to overcome latency and scalability barriers, this work aims to establish a foundation for next-generation interfaces that proactively mitigate user frustration, attentional drift, and decision fatigue. The results will directly inform design principles for high-stakes applications such as medical assistive technologies, adaptive learning platforms, and immersive training systems, where aligning interface behavior with users’ cognitive states is critical to safety and efficacy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on incorporating a human perspective into designing, researching, and creating technological interfaces. Includes instruction in design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between collective narrative dynamics and psychological well-being in digital communities, a niche emerging at the intersection of cultural psychology, computational social science, and data ethics. While narratives shape identity and group cohesion, their rapid evolution in online ecosystems—driven by algorithmic curation and decentralized interactions—remains poorly understood. Traditional survey-based methods lack the temporal resolution to capture real-time narrative shifts or their psychological correlates at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze how narrative structures in social media platforms influence users’ emotional regulation and perceived social support. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets of timestamped posts (from Reddit and Twitter/X archives) and simulating large-scale interaction networks. NLP pipelines will identify narrative elements (e.g., metaphor use, valence shifts) and link them to psycholinguistic markers of well-being. Dynamic network models will map how users cluster around narratives over time, while ABMs test hypotheses about feedback loops between algorithmic content prioritization and collective emotional states. The project’s computational demands include training transformer-based models for context-aware narrative segmentation, parallelized graph computations for evolving networks, and parameter sweeps across ABM scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated taxonomy of narrative patterns predictive of psychological outcomes, 2) open-source tools for real-time narrative monitoring in moderation systems, and 3) evidence-based insights into how platform design choices amplify or mitigate psychosocial risks. By bridging qualitative psychological constructs with large-scale computational analysis, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for studying digital culture’s impact on mental health.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: Public works systems are critical to urban resilience and community well-being, yet their management faces escalating complexity due to dynamic variables such as fluctuating budgets, climate disruptions, and evolving infrastructure demands. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the computational capacity to model these systems holistically, limiting the ability to optimize resource allocation, workforce deployment, and emergency response strategies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced simulation and optimization models tailored to public works management. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) simulating infrastructure interdependencies (e.g., transportation networks, water systems) under stress scenarios, (2) optimizing budget and labor allocation across competing priorities using reinforcement learning, and (3) evaluating ethical and equity impacts of resource distribution policies through agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will integrate real-world datasets—including municipal budgets, workforce demographics, and climate projections—with machine learning algorithms to predict system vulnerabilities and test mitigation strategies. HPC resources are essential to process large-scale spatiotemporal data, run parallelized simulations of urban systems, and train predictive models that account for nonlinear interactions between financial, operational, and social variables. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational toolkit for public agencies to simulate “what-if” scenarios, such as balancing maintenance schedules against extreme weather risks or resolving labor disputes through dynamic resource reallocation. By bridging computational science and public administration, this project aims to advance evidence-based strategies for equitable service delivery, cost-effective operations, and adaptive governance in public works. The resulting models will be validated through partnerships with municipal agencies, with findings disseminated to policymakers via interactive dashboards and scenario-planning workshops.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: The development of next-generation aerospace systems demands advanced computational tools to address complex, multi-physical challenges inherent in hypersonic flight and spacecraft operations. A critical barrier lies in accurately modeling transient aerothermal-structural interactions during high-speed atmospheric entry, where extreme heat fluxes, fluid dynamics, and material responses couple nonlinearly over rapidly evolving time scales. Existing simulation frameworks often decouple these phenomena or rely on oversimplified material models, limiting their predictive capability for novel thermal protection systems (TPS) and morphing structure designs. This project proposes a high-fidelity computational approach to resolve these interactions by integrating compressible reactive flow solvers, anisotropic ablation models, and thermomechanical finite element analysis within a tightly coupled HPC framework. Leveraging adaptive mesh refinement and implicit time-stepping algorithms, the simulations will capture microscale material degradation effects alongside macroscale aerodynamic loads, enabling the evaluation of emerging ceramic matrix composites and metamaterials under realistic mission profiles. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental arc-jet data and flight measurements from prior re-entry vehicles. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for aerothermal-structural analysis, performance benchmarks for candidate TPS materials under combined thermal-mechanical loading, and design guidelines for adaptive cooling architectures in hypersonic platforms. By enabling high-resolution studies of off-nominal scenarios (e.g., partial shield failure, turbulent transition effects), this work aims to reduce conservatism in current design margins while improving failure prediction accuracy. The requested computing resources will support large-scale parameter sweeps across Mach numbers, angles of attack, and material configurations, which are computationally prohibitive with existing campus cluster capabilities. Results will directly inform ongoing NASA partnerships on crewed lunar return vehicle development and contribute foundational data for certification of reusable hypersonic systems.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematic principles to the design, technology, and development of systems and equipment used in aerospace and astronautical operations. Includes instruction in basic and applied sciences related to astronomy and astronautics, control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: Clinical cytogenetics research faces escalating computational demands due to the growing complexity and scale of multi-omics data required to diagnose genetic disorders, optimize transplant compatibility, and characterize cancer-associated chromosomal aberrations. Current analytical pipelines struggle to integrate high-resolution genomic, cytogenetic, and imaging datasets—including whole-genome sequencing, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) imaging, and photomicrography—while maintaining clinical-grade accuracy and speed. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable computational framework for multi-modal data integration, enabling real-time analysis of structural variants, epigenetic patterns, and spatial genomic features critical to clinical decision-making. The proposed framework will leverage GPU-accelerated machine learning models to automate the detection of subtle chromosomal abnormalities from terabyte-scale imaging datasets, coupled with graph-based algorithms to resolve complex structural rearrangements in leukemia and solid tumor genomes. Parallelized workflows will align and annotate sequencing data from transplant recipients and donors, incorporating population-scale haplotype references to predict immunological compatibility. Additionally, the system will support 3D genomic simulations to model chromatin interactions influencing cancer progression. By unifying these computational approaches on an HPC platform, this project aims to reduce diagnostic turnaround times by 40%, improve resolution of mosaic variants in prenatal and oncology samples, and identify novel biomarkers for post-transplant outcome prediction. The resource will directly enhance ongoing studies on therapy-related myeloid neoplasms and congenital disorder cohorts, while providing a shared analytical infrastructure for collaborative clinical research. Outcomes will advance precision medicine in cytogenetics by bridging the gap between large-scale genomic data generation and actionable clinical interpretation, with open-source tools disseminated to the biomedical community.
cip_definition: The clinical research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This project addresses the critical challenge of optimizing horticultural crop resilience and productivity under rapidly changing climatic conditions. Traditional plant breeding and phenotyping approaches are often slow, labor-intensive, and insufficient to decode complex genotype-environment interactions in species such as citrus, nursery crops, and ornamental plants. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and environmental data. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to identify genetic markers associated with stress tolerance traits, while mechanistic models will simulate plant physiological responses to abiotic stressors like drought and extreme temperatures. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will be conducted on curated datasets encompassing 15+ horticultural species, requiring parallelized processing of terabyte-scale genomic data. Additionally, 3D plant architecture models will be parameterized using LiDAR and hyperspectral imaging data to predict light interception and photosynthetic efficiency under different cultivation scenarios. These computational workflows demand significant memory allocation and GPU acceleration due to the complexity of deep neural networks training and agent-based simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for accelerating marker-assisted breeding, optimized growth protocols for high-value crops, and climate-resilient cultivar recommendations tailored to regional environmental profiles. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source packages to support the horticultural research community. By enabling rapid analysis of multidimensional biological data, this project aims to transform precision horticulture, enhancing sustainable production of nutrient-dense crops and ornamental species critical to global food systems and ecosystem services.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific principles related to the cultivation of garden and ornamental plants, including fruits, vegetables, flowers, and landscape and nursery crops. Includes instruction in specific types of plants, such as citrus; breeding horticultural varieties; physiology of horticultural species; and the scientific management of horticultural plant development and production through the life cycle.

abstract: The emergence and persistence of antimicrobial-resistant bacterial pathogens and rapidly evolving viral strains in animal populations present critical challenges to veterinary medicine and public health. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale genomic datasets and simulating molecular interactions hinder the development of targeted therapies and preventive strategies. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps through integrative computational approaches. We will perform whole-genome sequencing and comparative phylogenomics on clinical isolates of multidrug-resistant bacteria (e.g., Staphylococcus pseudintermedius) and avian influenza viruses obtained from veterinary diagnostic cases. These data will be analyzed using machine learning models to identify genetic determinants of virulence and resistance, as well as patterns of cross-species transmission risk. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize the structural stability of viral envelope proteins under selective pressure from host immune responses, informing epitope prediction for vaccine design. Additionally, agent-based epidemiological modeling will simulate outbreak scenarios under varying intervention strategies. The HPC environment is essential for managing petabytes of sequencing data, executing computationally intensive simulations, and training predictive algorithms with high-dimensional inputs. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers for rapid diagnostics, the prioritization of therapeutic targets resistant to evolutionary drift, and evidence-based recommendations for outbreak containment protocols. By elucidating mechanisms of pathogen adaptation at scale, this research aims to directly enhance clinical decision-making in veterinary settings, reduce antimicrobial misuse, and mitigate zoonotic spillover events. The proposed computational workflows will also establish a framework for real-time pathogen surveillance in animal populations, addressing a critical need in One Health initiatives.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the precision and scalability of competency assessment in medical education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal educational data. Medical training programs face challenges in evaluating clinical reasoning, procedural skills, and adaptive learning trajectories due to the complexity of integrating diverse data sources—such as simulation logs, electronic health record interactions, wearable sensor outputs, and longitudinal assessment results. Traditional statistical methods struggle to model the dynamic, high-dimensional relationships within these datasets, limiting the ability to personalize training or predict performance gaps. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models trained on linked educational and clinical datasets from 12,000+ medical students and residents across six institutions. The computational workflow will employ natural language processing to analyze free-text clinical notes from virtual patient encounters, computer vision techniques to assess surgical simulation videos, and recurrent neural networks to model temporal skill progression. HPC resources are critical for processing 300+ terabytes of raw data, enabling parallelized hyperparameter optimization of ensemble models, and conducting counterfactual simulations of curricular interventions. By creating GPU-accelerated inference pipelines, we aim to generate real-time feedback for trainees and educators while maintaining data privacy through federated learning architectures. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for entrustment decisions, a framework for simulating the downstream clinical impacts of curricular changes, and open-source tools to quantify latent competencies from unstructured data. This work will provide medical educators with evidence-based strategies to individualize training pathways, optimize resource allocation for high-stakes assessments, and align educational outcomes with patient care quality metrics. The scalability of these methods, powered by HPC, addresses a critical need for data-driven reforms in competency-based medical education.
cip_definition: Research on how to teach deliver, design, and evaluate courses and curricula for medical students, residents, and faculty.

abstract: Understanding the interplay between ecological dynamics and evolutionary processes across spatial and temporal scales is critical for predicting biodiversity responses to rapid environmental change. This project seeks to address how species interactions and dispersal limitations mediate adaptive evolution in fragmented landscapes under climate warming scenarios, using a combination of individual-based simulations and empirical data integration. Current models often oversimplify either ecological complexity or evolutionary mechanisms, limiting their predictive power. We propose developing a high-resolution, spatially explicit framework that couples eco-evolutionary dynamics with landscape genetics, parameterized using field data from montane plant communities in biodiversity hotspots. The computational approach will integrate agent-based population models with genomic-informed trait evolution algorithms, simulating >10^6 individuals across heterogeneous environments over 500-year horizons. Each simulation iteration requires tracking multi-trait selection gradients, gene flow between metapopulations, and stochastic disturbance events while maintaining genomic-resolution inheritance patterns. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core components: 1) Parallel execution of parameter sweeps across climate projection ensembles (CMIP6), 2) Bayesian calibration of hybrid models using fossil pollen records and contemporary range shift observations, and 3) Variance partitioning analysis of evolutionary versus ecological contributions to range dynamics. Expected outcomes include quantifying thresholds of climate velocity beyond which evolutionary rescue becomes unlikely, identifying landscape configurations that enhance adaptive capacity, and generating testable predictions about phylogenetic turnover patterns in warming mountain ecosystems. By bridging microevolutionary processes with macroecological patterns, this work will advance fundamental theory while providing actionable insights for conservation prioritization. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scaling of eco-evolutionary models to realistic landscape extents, establishing an open-source framework for predicting biodiversity responses to anthropogenic change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions across levels of biological organization--genes and genomes, organisms, species, and ecosystems--and how these change over time, including the origins and history of species, the processes by which biodiversity has evolved, and the ecological context in which this evolution takes place. Includes instruction in animal, plant, population, functional, evolutionary, and ecosystem ecology; ecological and evolutionary genetics; molecular evolution; population and conservation biology; animal and plant diversity; biometry; and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This project aims to investigate the neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-dependent decision-making deficits in Parkinson’s disease (PD), focusing on how basal ganglia-thalamocortical networks dynamically integrate sensory and contextual information to guide action selection. While PD is characterized by motor symptoms, growing evidence suggests that dopamine depletion disrupts broader cognitive processes, including adaptive decision-making under uncertainty. However, the specific circuit-level computations driving these deficits remain unclear due to the complexity of large-scale network interactions. We propose to address this gap by developing biologically constrained spiking neural network models of cortico-basal ganglia pathways, incorporating multi-scale experimental data from PD rodent models and human behavioral studies. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate network dynamics across 500,000+ neurons with realistic synaptic properties, implement reinforcement learning algorithms for behavioral task modeling, and perform Bayesian inference on parameter spaces linking cellular dysfunction to system-level outcomes. Key innovations include the integration of in vivo electrophysiology datasets with machine learning techniques to constrain model architectures and the development of novel metrics quantifying information routing efficiency in simulated circuits. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of circuit motifs most vulnerable to dopamine depletion, 2) predictive models of how targeted deep brain stimulation parameters could restore functional network states, and 3) a publicly available computational framework for testing hypotheses about neuromodulation strategies. This work will advance our understanding of distributed neural computations in health and disease while establishing scalable methods for simulating complex brain-behavior relationships, directly addressing NIMH priorities for computational psychiatry research. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter sweeps across clinically relevant conditions that are infeasible with local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates as it relates to control of behavior. Includes instruction in neuronal systems and circuits, higher level studies of behavior and cognition, computational neurobiology, and behavioral manifestations of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: Veterinary dermatology faces significant challenges in addressing the complex etiologies of skin diseases in animals, which often involve interactions between genetic, immunological, microbial, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches are constrained by the limited integration of multi-omics data, high-resolution imaging, and real-world clinical datasets, hindering personalized care for diverse species. This project proposes a computational research initiative to advance understanding of cutaneous pathologies through large-scale data integration and predictive modeling. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including genomic and transcriptomic profiles of dermatologic conditions (e.g., atopic dermatitis, autoimmune disorders), 3D histopathology imaging, and longitudinal electronic health records from veterinary clinics. Machine learning models, particularly graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be developed to identify biomarkers, predict treatment responses, and map host-microbiome interactions. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will also model topical drug permeation across species-specific skin morphologies to optimize therapeutic formulations. By unifying these approaches, the project aims to generate actionable insights into disease mechanisms, improve diagnostic accuracy, and enable data-driven treatment protocols. The scale of data processing—terabytes of imaging, thousands of genomes, and millions of clinical observations—necessitates parallelized workflows, GPU-accelerated model training, and distributed storage systems, all requiring dedicated HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include open-access computational pipelines for veterinary dermatology, a resource allocation framework for prioritizing rare or severe cases, and clinically validated predictive tools for allergy management and antimicrobial stewardship. This work will directly address critical gaps in veterinary dermatologic care while establishing a template for computational translational research in animal health sciences.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: The pharmaceutical industry faces increasing complexity in optimizing drug commercialization strategies due to dynamic market conditions, heterogeneous patient populations, and evolving regulatory landscapes. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the multidimensional interactions between drug efficacy, payer policies, prescriber behavior, and competitive market forces. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model pharmaceutical market dynamics and simulate intervention scenarios for novel therapeutics. Leveraging large-scale datasets including electronic health records, claims data, drug characteristics, and historical sales figures, we will implement agent-based models to simulate stakeholder decision-making processes across healthcare systems. Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models will be integrated with econometric analyses to quantify relationships between drug properties, pricing structures, and market adoption rates. Machine learning approaches will identify predictive biomarkers for treatment response that influence market segmentation strategies. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to manage stochastic simulations across diverse demographic and regulatory scenarios, with iterative optimization of launch parameters through genetic algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for evaluating market access strategies under uncertainty, with specific applications to specialty drug launches and biosimilar competition analysis. This work will advance methodological integration of computational pharmacology and marketing science while providing actionable insights for pharmaceutical management. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling terabyte-scale datasets, running complex PK/PD-market hybrid models, and performing sensitivity analyses across 10,000+ simulated launch scenarios. Results will directly inform curriculum development in pharmaceutical marketing analytics and create an open-source framework for simulating healthcare market behavior.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that combines the study of basic and pharmaceutical sciences with marketing and management studies; and that prepares individuals for careers in pharmaceutical sales, marketing, management, and related fields within the health care industry. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, pharmaceutics, pharmacology, health care systems, issues and structure of pharmaceutical industry, management, pharmaceutical marketing, pharmaceutical and medical product management, and legal issues.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of legal reasoning in transnational human rights adjudication, focusing on patterns of judicial decision-making across intersecting legal systems (e.g., national courts, regional human rights tribunals, and international bodies). The study addresses a critical gap in computational legal studies: the lack of scalable frameworks to model how legal concepts migrate, hybridize, or conflict in cross-jurisdictional contexts, particularly in cases involving emergent technologies or non-Western legal traditions. Using a corpus of 1.2 million multilingual legal documents (judicial opinions, treaties, and secondary commentaries) spanning 1945–2023, the project will apply transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned for legal semantics to trace conceptual networks and argumentative structures. Computational methods will include dynamic topic modeling to identify doctrinal shifts, graph neural networks to map precedent citation anomalies, and counterfactual analysis to simulate how alternative reasoning frameworks might affect case outcomes. The scale and linguistic diversity of the corpus—combined with the need for real-time alignment of heterogeneous legal ontologies—necessitate HPC capabilities for distributed training of custom NLP architectures and large-scale knowledge graph construction. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access repository of annotated transnational human rights jurisprudence, 2) a computational model quantifying the impact of cultural-legal bias in cross-systemic precedent adoption, and 3) methodological innovations in applying HPC to comparative legal hermeneutics. By revealing systemic patterns in how courts negotiate pluralistic legal values, this work aims to inform both doctrinal scholarship and procedural reforms for transnational judicial cooperation, while establishing a template for computationally intensive humanities research at the intersection of law, philosophy, and artificial intelligence.
