cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on law and legal issues from the perspective of the social sciences and humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale, interdisciplinary study of cultural and regional identity formation in the Acadian diaspora across northeastern North America. The research problem centers on understanding how historical migration patterns, linguistic evolution, and material culture practices have shaped distinct Acadian subregional identities in Quebec, New Brunswick, and Louisiana from the 18th century to the present. Traditional archival methods struggle to synthesize the scale and diversity of relevant data, including digitized colonial records, multilingual oral history transcripts, geospatial land-use maps, and artifact metadata from over 50 regional repositories. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for analyzing French and English textual sources, geospatial clustering algorithms to map settlement patterns, and graph-based network models to trace kinship and trade connections across diasporic communities. HPC resources are critical for training custom transformer models on low-resource historical French dialects, processing high-resolution georeferenced datasets (10+ TB), and simulating cultural diffusion processes through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include the first longitudinal digital atlas of Acadian cultural geography, quantitative frameworks for assessing linguistic hybridity in minority Francophone communities, and open-source tools tailored for subregional studies in resource-constrained language contexts. By computationally bridging dispersed archival collections, this project aims to redefine scholarly understanding of how microregional identities persist amid transnational cultural flows while establishing scalable methods for comparative studies of other diasporic groups. Results will directly support heritage preservation initiatives led by Acadian cultural organizations and inform curricular development in North American regional studies programs.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the defined geographic subregions and subcultures within modern and historical countries and societies. Includes such topics as Acadian Studies, French Canadian and Quebec Studies, Southern (U.S.) Studies, New England Studies, Southwestern Studies, Northern Studies, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of dialectal variation in contemporary Portuguese through large-scale computational analysis, addressing critical gaps in understanding how regional and sociolinguistic factors shape language evolution. Despite the global presence of Portuguese, comprehensive models of its dialectal diversity—particularly across underserved regions like Africa and Asia—remain underdeveloped due to the scarcity of integrated, high-resolution linguistic data and the computational demands of processing multimodal corpora. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze a curated dataset of 10,000+ hours of spoken and written Portuguese from eight countries, integrating sociodemographic metadata to map correlations between linguistic features and variables such as urbanization, education, and migration. Computational methods will include phonetic alignment using hidden Markov models (HMMs) to trace vowel shifts, transformer-based NLP for syntactic variation detection, and graph-theoretical network analysis to model lexical borrowing patterns. These tasks require parallelized processing of audio transcripts, text corpora, and historical records, which exceed the capacity of standard workstations due to memory-intensive algorithms and terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-access geotemporal dialect atlas, predictive models of language change, and a benchmark dataset for Lusophone computational linguistics. The project will directly support pedagogical tools for heritage language preservation and inform natural language processing systems serving multilingual Portuguese-speaking populations. By elucidating how non-European varieties influence global Portuguese, this work aims to reshape philological frameworks and foster equitable representation of underrepresented dialects in academic and technological contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Portuguese language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Metropolitan Portuguese; Luso-Brazilian Portuguese; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic decision-making processes in complex organizational systems under uncertainty. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the interdependencies, stochastic variables, and adaptive behaviors inherent in multi-agent business environments, such as global supply chains or decentralized corporate structures. To overcome these limitations, the proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop large-scale simulations integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and reinforcement learning algorithms. These simulations will model scenarios involving resource allocation, risk propagation, and strategic coordination across hierarchical and networked organizational designs. The computational approach will parallelize scenario testing over thousands of parameter combinations to identify robust decision policies resilient to market volatility and operational disruptions. Key deliverables include a framework for real-time adaptive strategy optimization and predictive analytics tools to quantify trade-offs between efficiency, risk exposure, and scalability in management operations. By enabling the analysis of previously intractable problem spaces—such as emergent behaviors in cross-functional teams or cascading failures in interconnected business units—this work aims to advance computational organizational theory while providing actionable insights for leaders navigating rapidly evolving markets. The outcomes will directly contribute to methodological innovations in business analytics, with applications in crisis management, capacity planning, and decentralized governance systems. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to process terabytes of synthetic and real-world operational data while maintaining the low-latency requirements of interactive decision-support systems.
cip_title: Business Administration, Management and Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating emergent narrative structures in procedurally generated game environments, integrating principles from cognitive science, procedural content generation, and interactive storytelling. Current game engines struggle to dynamically adapt narrative elements to player decisions while maintaining coherent story arcs and character consistency, particularly in open-world scenarios with complex player-environment interactions. The research will employ high-performance computing resources to train and deploy machine learning models that analyze player behavior patterns in real time, combined with multi-agent systems simulating non-player character (NPC) decision-making processes. A novel hybrid architecture will be developed, combining transformer-based language models for dialogue generation with graph neural networks to maintain narrative consistency across branching story paths. Computational experiments will focus on optimizing parallel processing pipelines for real-time narrative adaptation, requiring distributed memory systems to handle the combinatorial complexity of player-NPC interactions at scale. Expected outcomes include a new metric system for evaluating narrative coherence in dynamic environments, open-source tools for adaptive storytelling in game engines, and fundamental insights into the computational requirements of human-like narrative reasoning in interactive media. The work bridges gaps between artificial intelligence, digital humanities, and game design, offering potential applications in educational gaming and immersive storytelling platforms while advancing computational methods for modeling complex creative processes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of design and computer programming to the development of computer games. Includes training in character and story development, computer programming, computer graphics, game design, game physics, human-computer interaction, human-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of executive coaching interventions in driving organizational change, with a focus on modeling nonlinear relationships between coaching strategies, leader behavior, and team outcomes. While executive coaching is widely utilized to enhance leadership effectiveness, the mechanisms through which specific coaching approaches translate to measurable organizational impact remain poorly quantified. Traditional qualitative methods dominate the field, limiting scalability and predictive precision. This study proposes a computational social science framework combining agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis to simulate how coaching-driven behavioral changes propagate through organizational hierarchies. High-fidelity simulations will integrate real-world data from anonymized coaching sessions (text and audio), psychometric assessments, and organizational performance metrics to train multi-agent models reflecting diverse leadership archetypes and team structures. The HPC environment will enable parallelized testing of coaching strategy variants across thousands of simulated organizational scenarios, capturing emergent phenomena in decision-making cascades and group dynamics. Key computational challenges include optimizing NLP pipelines for extracting coaching intent signals from unstructured dialogue and calibrating network diffusion parameters using federated learning approaches to maintain data confidentiality. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for predicting the ROI of coaching interventions under different organizational conditions, with specific deliverables quantifying how micro-level coaching interactions amplify into macro-level cultural shifts. This work aims to establish a new evidence-based paradigm for designing coaching programs in complex enterprises while advancing computational methods for behavioral modeling in business contexts.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on assisting individuals achieve career goals or assisting business leaders achieve organizational change. Includes instruction in executive coaching, group dynamics, leadership, management, organizational behavior, organizational communication, and team building.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the optimization of real-time auction dynamics, focusing on hybrid auction formats that integrate live, in-person bidding with digital platforms. The proliferation of multi-channel auctions—common in specialized markets such as rare collectibles, agricultural equipment, and real estate—introduces complex challenges in bidder behavior modeling, price discovery, and allocation efficiency. Traditional auction theory, which often assumes homogeneous participant behavior or static environments, fails to account for the high-dimensional data generated by hybrid auctions, including temporal bid patterns, cross-platform interactions, and contextual factors like item provenance or buyer sentiment. The project aims to develop a computational framework to simulate and analyze these dynamics at scale, enabling data-driven strategies for auctioneers to maximize seller returns while maintaining bidder engagement. Using agent-based modeling (ABM), deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and real-time clustering algorithms, the research will simulate heterogeneous bidder populations under varying auction rules (e.g., reserve pricing, bid increments, timing protocols). HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale simulations across diverse auction scenarios (e.g., livestock vs. luxury estate auctions) and training predictive models on historical bidstream data. Expected outcomes include (1) adaptive pricing algorithms that dynamically adjust auction parameters based on real-time participant behavior, (2) a taxonomy of hybrid auction inefficiencies linked to specific bidder demographics or item categories, and (3) open-source tools for auctioneers to evaluate rule changes or platform integrations. By bridging computational economics, behavioral analytics, and auctioneering practice, this work will address a critical gap in specialized auction management, offering empirically validated strategies to enhance transparency and competitiveness in emerging hybrid markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional careers as auctioneers and auction managers, and for meeting applicable state licensing requirements. Includes instruction in bid calling, public speaking, ringworking, auction techniques, salesmanship skills, auction clerking and cashiering, auction advertising, working independently or with auction houses, contracts and agency, applicable sales law, and managing both general auctions and auctions specializing in commodities such as antiques, consignments, farm equipment, industrial equipment, real estate, livestock, and automobiles.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize clinical decision-making and resource allocation in acute care nursing settings, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets. Nurses in hospital environments face critical challenges in anticipating patient deterioration, managing workloads, and prioritizing interventions, particularly during staffing shortages or high-patient-acuity periods. Current risk-stratification tools often lack the granularity to account for dynamic, multifactorial patient trajectories, leading to delayed care and suboptimal outcomes. To address this, we propose training machine learning models on retrospective EHR data—including vital signs, medication administration records, lab results, and nurse documentation—to predict near-term clinical events such as sepsis, falls, or unplanned ICU transfers. The computational workload involves preprocessing heterogeneous clinical data streams, training deep neural networks with attention mechanisms to identify temporal patterns, and simulating real-time inference scenarios. HPC resources are essential given the scale of data (projected 2.5 million patient-days from 10 partner hospitals), the complexity of transformer-based architectures, and the need for hyperparameter optimization across thousands of concurrent model iterations. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive pipeline capable of generating hourly risk scores for individual patients, (2) quantitative insights into modifiable risk factors within nursing workflows, and (3) an open-source tool for simulating nurse-to-patient assignment strategies under varying acuity conditions. By enabling proactive rather than reactive care, this work aims to reduce adverse events by an estimated 15-20% in pilot units while providing evidence-based guidance for staffing decisions. The models and simulation frameworks will be disseminated through nursing education modules, ensuring translational impact on both clinical practice and training curricula.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals in the knowledge, techniques and procedures for promoting health, providing care for sick, disabled, infirmed, or other individuals or groups. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting a physician during treatments and examinations, Referring patients to physicians and other health care specialists, and planning education for health maintenance.

abstract: Emerging zoonotic pathogens and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in animal populations present critical challenges to veterinary and public health. Current approaches to modeling disease transmission dynamics and AMR gene spread often lack the resolution to account for heterogeneous host-pathogen interactions, genomic variability, and environmental drivers at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating veterinary clinical data, genomic surveillance, and ecological variables. We will employ agent-based modeling to simulate pathogen spread within and between animal populations, incorporating real-world data on livestock mobility, wildlife interfaces, and veterinary care access. Phylogenetic reconstruction of bacterial whole-genome sequencing data from clinical veterinary samples will trace AMR transmission pathways, requiring Bayesian evolutionary analysis and machine learning to identify hotspots of resistance emergence. Additionally, deep learning architectures will be trained on veterinary imaging databases to automate the detection of early disease signatures in radiographs and histopathology slides. These computational workflows demand parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration due to the volume of genomic data (>10 TB), stochastic simulation complexity, and image analysis tasks. Outcomes will include predictive frameworks to optimize outbreak response in animal populations, actionable insights into AMR mitigation strategies, and open-source tools for rapid veterinary diagnostics. By addressing computational bottlenecks, this work will advance translational veterinary medicine, directly supporting the One Health initiative’s goal of cross-species disease prevention. The requested resources will enable scaling to national-level datasets, fostering collaboration between veterinary researchers, epidemiologists, and public health agencies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of veterinary medicine, involving the diagnosis, treatment, and health care management of animals and animal populations and the prevention and management of zoonosis. Includes instruction in the veterinary basic sciences, infectious and noninfectious disease, diagnostic procedures, veterinary clinical medicine, obstetrics, radiology, anesthesiology, surgery, toxicology, animal health and preventive medicine, clinical nutrition, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the evolution of legal frameworks governing digital cultural heritage in non-professional contexts, a niche interdisciplinary domain intersecting law, digital humanities, and public memory studies. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how decentralized, non-institutional actors—such as community archives, independent researchers, and grassroots initiatives—navigate complex legal landscapes to preserve and share digital cultural materials. Traditional legal scholarship often overlooks the computational demands of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets spanning legal texts, case law, digitized cultural artifacts, and metadata from informal repositories. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to mine legal documents and policy discourse, combined with network analysis to map relationships between legal constraints, stakeholder behaviors, and digital preservation outcomes. Custom algorithms will be developed to simulate scenarios of legal compliance and risk assessment under varying jurisdictional conditions, while machine learning models will identify patterns in the adaptive strategies employed by non-professional practitioners. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to handle terabyte-scale datasets, including text corpora, image repositories, and temporal geospatial metadata. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for modeling legal-informational ecosystems in non-professional contexts, open-source tools for scalable analysis of legal-textual data, and empirically grounded insights into how emergent digital practices challenge conventional legal categories. This work will advance scholarly discourse at the intersection of law and digital culture while providing practical resources for communities engaged in ethically complex preservation work. By situating computational legal analysis within a humanistic inquiry, the project demonstrates the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional, interdisciplinary research domains.
cip_definition: Any program in non-professional legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational study of Hindu philosophical and theological systems, particularly through the analysis of textual and doctrinal networks across historical periods. The research problem centers on the fragmented and often siloed nature of Hindu studies scholarship, which has limited systematic exploration of cross-textual influences, conceptual evolution, and the structural relationships between core philosophical schools (e.g., Vedanta, Nyaya) and devotional traditions. Traditional hermeneutic methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of primary sources, including multilingual commentaries, ritual manuals, and metaphysical treatises spanning millennia. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, graph-based network modeling, and semantic similarity algorithms to map conceptual linkages across digitized corpora of Sanskrit and vernacular texts (e.g., Upanishads, Puranas, Bhakti poetry). HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of linguistic data, training transformer models for context-aware translation of understudied works, and simulating the diffusion of ideas through sectarian networks. Expected outcomes include an open-access knowledge graph visualizing interactions between dharmic principles, ritual practices, and regional traditions, as well as quantitative frameworks to trace the adaptation of Vedic concepts in later philosophical systems. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to reveal previously unrecognized patterns in Hindu thought, offering new insights into the dynamic interplay of theology, culture, and philosophy. The resulting tools and datasets will serve as a foundation for interdisciplinary collaborations, bridging humanities scholarship and data science methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the group of South Asian theologies and philosophies collectively known as Hinduism; together with the religious history and cultural and social manifestations of the faith. Includes instruction in Hindu theology and philosophy (dharma); literature (Vedas, Upanishads, Epics, and commentaries); the Hindu Pantheon, sects, and movements; schools and disciplines; and related arts and sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing generative artificial intelligence (AI) in creative industries, with a focus on copyright, attribution, and liability challenges in digital art, music, and synthetic media. As generative AI tools rapidly proliferate, existing legal paradigms struggle to address ambiguities in authorship, fair use boundaries, and cross-jurisdictional compliance—issues critical to artists, entertainment firms, and policymakers. The research will employ computational legal analytics, combining natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis to process large-scale datasets of international case law, licensing agreements, and regulatory proposals (2010–2024). Custom machine learning models will identify latent patterns in judicial reasoning, contractual risk allocation trends, and policy fragmentation across 50+ jurisdictions. Simulations will model the cascading effects of hypothetical litigation outcomes and regulatory interventions on creative workflows and market dynamics. By integrating legal texts with economic and behavioral data from arts industry repositories, this approach aims to quantify systemic risks in AI-driven content production and propose adaptive governance frameworks. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool for rights holders, a taxonomy of emergent legal conflicts, and predictive benchmarks for liability exposure in AI-assisted creative works. The computational scale required—processing terabytes of multimodal legal, artistic, and transactional data—necessitates GPU-accelerated parallel processing and distributed memory architectures to train transformer-based models and run multi-agent simulations. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges gaps between computational law, cultural economics, and AI ethics, offering a novel evidence base for stakeholders navigating uncharted legal terrain in the algorithmic creative economy.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting the sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, and media industries.

abstract:
This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze large-scale behavioral and interactional datasets generated during play therapy sessions, with the goal of identifying patterns predictive of therapeutic outcomes in children. Play therapy relies on nuanced, non-verbal communication and symbolic play, which are challenging to quantify systematically. Current manual coding methods are time-intensive, prone to subjective bias, and lack scalability. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal data—including video, audio, and biometric sensor streams—captured during therapist-child interactions. The research problem centers on extracting actionable insights from these complex datasets to refine evidence-based play therapy protocols and training tools for aspiring Registered Play Therapists (RPTs).  

The computational approach integrates computer vision (OpenCV, MediaPipe) for tracking play behaviors and facial expressions, natural language processing (NLP) for therapist verbal interventions, and machine learning (TensorFlow, PyTorch) to model temporal dynamics in child responses. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of ~10,000 hours of anonymized session recordings from partnered clinics, as well as real-time simulations of hypothetical therapist decision pathways using reinforcement learning. Ethical considerations include secure data handling compliant with HIPAA/FERPA and bias mitigation via adversarial validation in model training.  

Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model linking specific play therapy techniques (e.g., sandtray, role-play) to reductions in anxiety or aggression metrics, (2) an open-source tool for automated session annotation to support RPT supervision, and (3) generative AI prototypes to simulate developmentally tailored play scenarios for therapist training. By bridging computational analytics with developmental psychology, this work aims to advance scalable, data-informed practices in play therapy while preserving the relational and creative core of the discipline. The requested HPC allocation is critical for managing GPU-intensive deep learning workflows and storing multi-terabyte datasets securely.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing predictive maintenance protocols in industrial electronic systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in current reactive maintenance practices. Industrial electronics, such as motor drives, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), and power distribution systems, are critical to manufacturing operations but often fail unexpectedly due to complex interdependencies between thermal, electrical, and mechanical stressors. Traditional diagnostic methods rely on heuristic evaluations or simplified models, which struggle to account for real-world operational variability. The proposed research will employ multiphysics simulations to model equipment degradation under dynamic industrial conditions, integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on synthetic and historical sensor data to predict failure probabilities. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of high-fidelity simulations spanning electromechanical component interactions, as well as to process terabytes of sensor data for ML training. Key objectives include creating a digital twin platform to simulate fault propagation in PLC-controlled systems and developing an adaptive neural network capable of real-time anomaly detection. Outcomes will provide a scalable, data-driven framework for predicting remaining useful life of industrial electronics, reducing unplanned downtime by an estimated 20–30% in test-case manufacturing environments. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular code repositories to support workforce training in advanced diagnostic techniques, aligning with the Industrial Electronics Technology program’s emphasis on practical technical skills. By bridging simulation-driven insights with operational data, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive maintenance in smart manufacturing, directly enhancing the reliability and efficiency of industrial electronic infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair electrical/electronic equipment used in industry and manufacturing. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cyber-physical systems and regulatory environments has outpaced traditional security auditing methodologies, which struggle to efficiently analyze large-scale, dynamic networks in real time. This project addresses the critical need for scalable, high-performance computational tools to automate and enhance security auditing processes in complex infrastructures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose the development of a parallelized auditing framework that integrates real-time log analysis, probabilistic risk modeling, and compliance verification across distributed systems. The computational approach involves the deployment of GPU-accelerated anomaly detection algorithms and agent-based simulations to model adversarial behaviors under diverse regulatory scenarios. By processing multi-terabyte datasets of network traffic and configuration snapshots, the framework will identify policy deviations, quantify risk exposure, and generate adaptive compliance reports. The expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for automated security auditing, validated against industrial control systems and cloud environments, which reduces audit cycle times by orders of magnitude while improving detection accuracy. This research bridges a critical gap in information assurance by enabling proactive, evidence-based security governance in environments where manual oversight is impractical, thereby strengthening organizational resilience against emerging cyber threats.
cip_title: Computer and Information Systems Security/ Auditing/ Information Assurance
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assess the security needs of computer and network systems, recommend safeguard solutions, and manage the implementation, auditing, and maintenance of security devices, systems, and procedures. Includes instruction in computer architecture, programming, and systems analysis; networking; telecommunications; cryptography; security system auditing and design; applicable law and regulations; risk assessment and policy analysis; contingency planning; user access issues; investigation techniques; and troubleshooting.

abstract: The increasing complexity of digital arts projects, particularly those involving real-time rendering, large-scale simulations, and generative algorithms, demands computational resources beyond the capacity of standard workstations. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support the creation and analysis of computationally intensive digital artworks that integrate machine learning, 3D physics simulations, and interactive media. A central challenge in contemporary digital arts is balancing aesthetic innovation with technical feasibility, especially when working with high-resolution assets, dynamic procedural systems, or AI-driven generative models. Current workflows often face bottlenecks in rendering times, memory limitations, and the inability to process real-time interactivity at scale, constraining both creative exploration and scholarly research. To address this, the proposed research will leverage GPU-accelerated clusters for parallel rendering of 4K/8K animations, distributed computing frameworks to train custom diffusion models for generative art, and real-time simulation environments for interactive installations. Key computational methods include optimizing neural radiance fields (NeRF) for 3D scene reconstruction from multimedia inputs, deploying fluid dynamics solvers for virtual material interactions, and developing hybrid CPU/GPU pipelines for multi-user VR collaborations. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for scalable digital content creation, a publicly accessible dataset of procedurally generated 3D assets, and a series of exhibitions demonstrating HPC-enabled artworks. The project will advance methodologies for integrating computational research into artistic practice, provide benchmarks for resource allocation in digital arts programs, and foster interdisciplinary collaborations between artists, computer scientists, and design researchers. By bridging gaps between creative intent and technical execution, this work aims to expand the expressive potential of digital media while establishing reproducible workflows for resource-intensive artistic inquiry.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the use of computerized digital images as the primary medium of expression in the visual and performing arts, and that may prepare individuals for a wide variety of careers using new media, including graphic design, digital animation, motion graphics, 3D visualization, game and interactive media design, music and sound design, video production, web design, photography, and other fields.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the fitting of specialty contact lenses for patients with irregular corneal topography, a challenge frequently encountered in optometric practice. Current protocols rely heavily on iterative trial-and-error adjustments, leading to prolonged patient discomfort, increased risk of corneal complications, and inefficiencies in clinical workflows. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling approach integrating corneal biomechanics, tear film dynamics, and optical ray tracing to predict optimal lens parameters for individual patients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate the complex interactions between lens materials, ocular surface morphology, and fluid dynamics under varying physiological conditions. Finite element models of patient-specific corneal geometries—derived from clinical topographical data—will be coupled with computational fluid dynamics simulations of the post-lens tear layer and machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective fitting outcomes. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to reduce simulation timescales from days to hours, enabling near-real-time parameter optimization. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive tool that reduces fitting iterations by ≥50%, improves visual acuity metrics in patients with keratoconus and post-surgical corneas, and establishes quantitative guidelines for lens-edge lift and fluid reservoir design. By bridging optometric practice, materials science, and computational engineering, this work advances precision eyecare tools while addressing a critical gap in ophthalmic technology. The resulting open-source simulation platform will empower optometric technicians to make data-informed decisions during lens fitting, enhancing both clinical efficiency and patient outcomes. Successful implementation could redefine standards of care for complex contact lens cases, with translational potential for adaptive optics and dry eye management applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist optometrists in providing patient care, administering examinations and treatments, and performing office administrative functions. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology of the eye, visual testing, patient communication, patient preparation, medications and administration, dispensing and fitting of eyeglasses and contact lenses, record-keeping, and office management skills.

abstract: This project proposes the development of an adaptive, AI-driven simulation environment to optimize training protocols for teaching assistants (TAs) in large-scale, heterogeneous classroom settings. While TAs play a critical role in bridging instructional gaps, existing training frameworks lack personalized, data-driven approaches to address the dynamic challenges of diverse student populations and hybrid learning modalities. The research problem centers on creating computational models that predict TA-student interaction outcomes, identify skill gaps in real-time pedagogical support, and generate scenario-based training modules tailored to individual TA strengths and classroom needs. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement a multimodal machine learning pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) of student-TA dialogue, computer vision analysis of classroom engagement metrics, and reinforcement learning to simulate decision-making pathways. Datasets will include de-identified video recordings from STEM discussion sections, anonymized student performance metrics, and TA feedback logs across 50+ courses. The computational workflow involves training transformer-based models on interaction patterns, clustering TA intervention strategies, and validating simulations against ground-truthed observational studies. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating TA competency profiles, predictive analytics tools for instructors to allocate TA resources efficiently, and evidence-based guidelines for adaptive training in emerging educational technologies. This work occupies a novel niche at the intersection of educational psychology, human-computer interaction, and computational pedagogy, offering scalable solutions to enhance equity in academic support systems without overlapping with traditional teacher education domains. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing multimodal data streams, running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and iterating deep learning architectures to accommodate ethical AI constraints in educational contexts.
cip_definition: Any teaching assistant/aide program, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEMs) represent a complex group of genetic disorders characterized by disruptions in biochemical pathways, leading to diverse clinical manifestations and long-term health complications. Current diagnostic and management strategies often face challenges due to heterogeneity in phenotypic presentation, incomplete understanding of genotype-phenotype correlations, and limitations in integrating multi-omics data for personalized care. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for variant pathogenicity, metabolic network analysis, and multi-omics integration. The research will utilize whole exome sequencing, metabolomic profiling, and longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 500 patients with suspected IEMs. Computational workflows will include machine learning frameworks to prioritize variants of uncertain significance, molecular dynamics simulations to assess protein stability and ligand binding perturbations, and constraint-based flux balance analysis to model metabolic pathway disruptions. A custom pipeline will integrate genomic, metabolomic, and electronic health record data to identify predictive biomarkers for disease progression and treatment response. The anticipated outcomes include: (1) improved classification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting metabolic pathways, (2) dynamic models linking specific biochemical perturbations to clinical outcomes, and (3) decision-support algorithms for personalized dietary and pharmacological interventions. By enabling large-scale integration of heterogeneous datasets and computationally intensive simulations, HPC resources are critical for overcoming current limitations in processing speed and data complexity. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy, enable proactive management of metabolic decompensation events, and provide a scalable computational framework for investigating rare IEM subtypes. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for metabolic network analysis and a clinical-genomic database accessible to the medical biochemical genetics community.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and medical management of individuals with inborn errors of metabolism, including the provision of direct care and consultative care for individuals of all ages.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of quantum turbulence in superfluid systems through large-scale numerical simulations. Quantum turbulence, characterized by chaotic tangles of quantized vortices in ultra-cold superfluids, presents unresolved questions about energy transfer mechanisms, decay pathways, and connections to classical turbulence. Current experimental and analytical approaches face limitations in resolving the full spatiotemporal complexity of these systems, necessitating advanced computational methods. We propose to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to solve the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, a nonlinear Schrödinger equation governing superfluid dynamics, across three-dimensional domains. Our simulations will model vortex interactions, reconnections, and collective behavior under varying initial conditions and external perturbations. A hybrid pseudo-spectral and finite-difference approach will be implemented to balance accuracy and computational efficiency, with adaptive mesh refinement applied to resolve fine vortex structures. The simulations will track energy spectra, vortex line density, and topological invariants to characterize turbulence evolution. By scaling to system sizes exceeding current state-of-the-art simulations, we aim to identify universal statistical properties and test theoretical predictions about energy cascade processes. Outcomes will directly inform ongoing experimental efforts in superfluid helium systems and contribute to foundational models of quantum turbulence. This work will establish a computational framework for probing non-equilibrium quantum hydrodynamics, with potential implications for understanding analogous phenomena in neutron star interiors and quantum-enhanced fluid systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary resolution and statistical sampling to advance this emerging frontier in quantum fluid dynamics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Hearing aid personalization remains a critical challenge in audiological rehabilitation, as conventional fitting protocols often rely on population-averaged prescriptive formulas that inadequately address individual variations in cochlear damage patterns, neural processing deficits, and listening environment demands. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating biophysical cochlear models with machine learning to optimize hearing aid parameter selection at the individual level. The research will address two core limitations: (1) current clinical tools lack the resolution to map specific cochlear pathologies to frequency-specific amplification needs, and (2) real-world listening environments introduce complex nonlinear interactions between amplified signals and residual auditory function that cannot be captured by threshold-based fitting approaches. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of cochlear mechanics using finite element models incorporating patient-specific otoacoustic emission data and histological patterns of hair cell loss. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on synthetic auditory nerve spiking patterns derived from these simulations to predict optimal gain-frequency responses across diverse noise environments. A multi-objective optimization layer will balance speech intelligibility metrics with perceptual comfort constraints derived from psychoacoustic models. The computational pipeline will be validated against electrophysiological data from human temporal bone specimens and behavioral outcomes from 120 clinical hearing aid users. By establishing quantitative relationships between cochlear microstructure, neural coding fidelity, and amplification benefits, this work aims to create the first patient-specific hearing aid optimization platform that adapts to both biological constraints and environmental acoustics. Successful implementation could reduce the trial-and-error period in hearing aid fittings by 40-60% while improving speech recognition scores in noisy environments by 15-20%, significantly advancing rehabilitation outcomes for individuals with sensorineural hearing loss.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to test the hearing of, and to select, fit and dispense appropriate hearing aids for, patients. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of the ear, hearing testing, hearing aid fitting and technology, health promotion and rehabilitation, counseling and communication, business management, and professional ethics.

abstract: The proliferation of data-intensive workflows in sectors such as healthcare, logistics, and finance has exposed critical bottlenecks in conventional data entry and microcomputer applications, particularly in scalability and real-time processing. This project seeks to address the inefficiencies of legacy systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test a novel framework for intelligent, automated data entry and processing. The research problem centers on overcoming latency and accuracy limitations in handling heterogeneous, high-volume datasets—common in modern applications—where traditional single-threaded architectures fail to meet performance demands. The proposed computational approach integrates machine learning (ML) models for optical character recognition (OCR) and semantic validation with parallelized data ingestion pipelines. By utilizing distributed computing frameworks such as Apache Spark and GPU-accelerated ML training, the project aims to optimize resource allocation across multi-node clusters, enabling real-time preprocessing of terabyte-scale datasets. Key methods include benchmarking hybrid CPU-GPU workflows, simulating load-balanced task distribution, and validating results against industry-standard accuracy metrics. The expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolkit for adaptive data entry systems capable of reducing manual intervention by 40–60% while maintaining >99% accuracy under variable workloads. This work will also produce a comparative analysis of HPC-driven versus conventional microcomputer architectures, providing actionable insights for organizations transitioning to data-centric operations. The significance lies in democratizing access to high-efficiency data processing for small-to-medium enterprises, which currently lack the infrastructure to implement costly proprietary solutions. By demonstrating the feasibility of HPC-resourced frameworks in everyday microcomputer applications, this research will bridge a critical gap between theoretical scalability and practical, equitable implementation in technology-driven fields.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data entry/microcomputer applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance fundamental research in algebraic topology and geometric analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve conjectures related to the classification and stability of high-dimensional manifolds. A central challenge in pure mathematics involves analyzing topological invariants—such as homology groups and characteristic classes—for complex manifolds in dimensions ≥5, where traditional analytical methods become computationally intractable. Current limitations in processing large-scale simplicial complexes and sheaf cohomology calculations restrict progress on longstanding problems, including the existence of exotic smooth structures on spheres and the classification of simply connected manifolds under cobordism. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining symbolic algebra libraries (e.g., Singular, GAP) with distributed-memory parallelization to compute higher-order cohomology rings and Betti numbers for manifolds defined by non-linear systems. The project will implement novel algorithms for persistent homology and spectral sequence convergence, optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures, to manage the exponential growth of chain complex data in higher dimensions. Additionally, we will develop machine learning models trained on topological feature spaces to predict stable homotopy types, enabling targeted computations. Successful execution will yield verified classifications for families of 7-manifolds relevant to the Andrews-Curtis conjecture, resolve ambiguities in surgery theory for dimension 6, and produce open-source software tools for large-scale algebraic topology. These outcomes will directly contribute to the foundational understanding of geometric structures while establishing computational methodologies adaptable to unsolved problems in knot theory, dynamical systems, and geometric group theory. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming memory and runtime barriers inherent to these computations, which involve matrices exceeding 10^8 elements and require months of sustained parallel processing.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the analysis of quantities, magnitudes, forms, and their relationships, using symbolic logic and language. Includes instruction in algebra, calculus, functional analysis, geometry, number theory, logic, topology and other mathematical specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular dynamics of highly diluted homeopathic formulations using high-performance computing (HPC) to model solute-solvent interactions at ultrahigh dilutions (beyond Avogadro’s limit). Despite clinical usage, homeopathic remedies lack a robust physicochemical explanation for purported bioactivity, particularly in regimes where active solute molecules are absent. The research problem centers on characterizing nanoscale solvent structures or long-range ordering in aqueous solutions that may arise during succussion (serial dilution with agitation)—a process hypothesized to impart therapeutic information via persistent hydrogen-bond networks or epitaxial water clusters. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will model succussed solutions of exemplar substances (e.g., Arnica montana, silica) across dilution levels (6X to 30X), analyzing solvent conformational stability, interfacial phenomena, and emergent supramolecular patterns under varying agitation parameters. Quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods will assess electronic polarization effects. Parallelized simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to achieve millisecond-scale sampling for statistically robust trajectory analysis. Machine learning pipelines will classify agitation-induced structural signatures correlated with in vitro bioassay data from collaborating labs. Outcomes aim to identify reproducible solvent-level phenomena that differentiate homeopathic preparations from controls, providing a testable framework for the "memory of water" hypothesis. By bridging nanoscale modeling with empirical validation, this work could redefine the biophysical plausibility of homeopathic mechanisms while advancing computational methodologies for ultra-dilute systems. Results will inform optimized remedy production protocols and contribute foundational data to interdisciplinary debates on water structure-function relationships in therapeutic contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of homeopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic system using naturally occurring substances in highly diluted forms to mimic symptoms of illness and trigger autoimmune responses, based on the law of similars and other principles derived from the work of Samuel Hahnemann and others. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, toxicology, philosophy and theory of homeopathy, casetaking and case analysis, repertory, material medica, constitutional typing, proving, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of nonlinear optical phenomena in laser systems, with a focus on optimizing high-power laser designs and photon-matter interactions. Current experimental approaches to characterize beam propagation in nonlinear media, thermal effects in high-energy laser cavities, and ultrafast pulse shaping face limitations in resolving multi-scale spatiotemporal dynamics. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for electromagnetic field evolution, rate equations for carrier dynamics in gain media, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management. The project will implement parallelized algorithms using MPI and GPU-accelerated computing to model 3D laser resonator configurations, including non-uniform optical coatings and structured beam profiles at petawatt-scale intensities. Key challenges involve resolving picosecond-scale nonlinear interactions (e.g., Kerr lensing, Raman scattering) while maintaining micron-level spatial fidelity across centimeter-scale optical components—a multi-physics problem requiring teraflop-scale computations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for harmonic generation efficiency in periodically poled crystals, thermally induced wavefront distortion thresholds in Yb-doped amplifiers, and optimal plasma grating configurations for pulse compression. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation industrial laser systems with improved beam quality and energy conversion rates. The requested HPC resources will enable parameter space explorations impractical on local clusters, particularly for full-wave simulations of ultra-short pulse propagation in photonic crystal waveguides—a critical step toward developing compact directed-energy prototypes. By bridging computational optics with HPC-driven engineering optimization, this work aims to establish new methodologies for photonic device simulation while addressing fundamental challenges in nonlinear laser physics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of optical systems, lasers and related electronic devices. Includes instruction in wave theory and mechanics, electromagnetic applications, linear and non-linear optics, photon detecting, laser beam properties, directed energy, harmonic generation, optical systems, shielding and the design and implementation of related systems and equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of generative, computationally intensive frameworks for adaptive architectural systems that integrate real-time environmental feedback with culturally responsive design. Current approaches to dynamic architecture often prioritize technical performance metrics (e.g., energy efficiency, structural optimization) or static cultural narratives, failing to reconcile the complex interplay between evolving environmental conditions and sociocultural meaning-making in urban contexts. Our research addresses this gap by creating a hybrid methodology combining agent-based spatial modeling, multi-temporal climate data analysis, and semantic networks trained on localized architectural heritage datasets. The computational workflow involves three interdependent phases: 1) simulating pedestrian movement patterns and microclimate interactions using particle systems and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models at neighborhood scale; 2) training graph neural networks to identify latent relationships between historical design motifs and contemporary spatial behaviors; and 3) employing multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to generate design prototypes that balance thermodynamic performance with culturally legible formal languages. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space of these concurrent processes, particularly in resolving time-dependent simulations of shade, wind, and crowd dynamics at sub-meter resolutions across diurnal and seasonal cycles. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational pipeline for context-sensitive adaptive architecture, validated through physical prototype installations in two climatically distinct heritage districts. This work aims to establish new metrics for evaluating architectural adaptability that integrate quantitative environmental performance with qualitative cultural resonance, providing a template for computationally augmented design processes that address both ecological urgency and cultural continuity in urban transformation.
cip_definition: An advanced program of study for architects and related professionals that focuses on theoretical and practical issues in architecture and integrates digital technologies into architectural design, fabrication, and construction. Includes instruction in architectural history and urban theory, 3-D digital technologies, construction, design and fabrication methods, and sustainable practices in architecture.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and reliability of electrical power transmission systems under dynamic load conditions, with a focus on integrating renewable energy sources into existing grid infrastructures. The increasing complexity of modern electrical grids, compounded by variable renewable inputs and fluctuating demand, poses significant challenges for safe and efficient installation practices. Traditional analytical methods often fail to account for real-time variability, leading to suboptimal designs, increased risk of equipment failure, and non-compliance with evolving safety standards. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale, multi-physics models of power transmission networks. These simulations will incorporate real-world data on load patterns, environmental factors, and material properties to evaluate stress distribution, thermal behavior, and electromagnetic interference across transmission lines and connected components. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to predict failure modes and identify optimal wiring configurations, grounding strategies, and insulation materials under diverse operational scenarios. The computational pipeline will also integrate code-compliant safety thresholds to automate compliance checks during the design phase. By enabling rapid iteration of system designs and proactive risk assessment, this work aims to reduce installation costs, minimize downtime, and enhance grid resilience. Outcomes will include open-source tools for simulating region-specific transmission networks and evidence-based guidelines for installers to adapt to emerging technologies such as distributed solar arrays and battery storage systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the high-dimensional parameter space and real-time data processing demands, which exceed the capabilities of local computational clusters. This research directly supports the program’s mission to advance technical training in electrical installation by bridging theoretical knowledge with data-driven, scalable solutions for next-generation power infrastructure.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installation/ Installer, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install indoor and outdoor residential, commercial, and industrial electrical systems, and associated power transmission lines. Includes instruction in electricity, safety procedures, wiring, insulation and grounding, schematic blueprint interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Pediatric respiratory diseases present unique challenges due to the dynamic nature of lung development and the heterogeneity of disease manifestations across developmental stages. Current gaps in understanding disease mechanisms—particularly in rare conditions such as childhood interstitial lung disease (chILD) and severe asthma phenotypes—stem from the complexity of integrating multimodal data (e.g., longitudinal pulmonary function tests, high-resolution chest CT imaging, and single-cell genomic profiles) with dynamic models of airway physiology. This project proposes to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate pediatric lung growth, disease progression, and treatment responses. Using anonymized clinical datasets from a multicenter cohort of 1,200 patients (ages 0–18 years), we will employ finite element modeling to predict airway remodeling in asthma and machine learning algorithms to identify genomic and imaging biomarkers associated with rapid disease progression in chILD. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will quantify the impact of developmental airway geometry on aerosolized drug delivery, optimizing dosing strategies for noninvasive ventilation. These models require parallelized processing of high-dimensional data, necessitating HPC capabilities for large-scale parameter optimization, 3D image segmentation, and real-time simulation of heterogeneous patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms to stratify patients by treatment responsiveness, validated models of lung growth under disease stress, and open-source computational tools for pediatric respiratory research. By elucidating developmental drivers of respiratory pathology, this work aims to advance personalized therapeutic strategies, reduce invasive diagnostic procedures, and improve long-term pulmonary outcomes in children. The requested computing resources will enable the handling of datasets and simulations that are infeasible on local infrastructure, directly supporting translational innovations in pediatric pulmonology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention and treatment of all respiratory diseases affecting infants, children, and young adults, based on knowledge of the growth and development of the lung, assessment of respiratory function in infants and children, and experience in a variety of invasive and noninvasive diagnostic techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern printing press operations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize complex variables in real-time press workflows. Despite advancements in digital printing technologies, operators face persistent challenges in balancing speed, material conservation, and color accuracy, particularly for high-volume or specialized print runs. Current trial-and-error calibration methods result in significant material waste, energy overuse, and production delays. This research proposes a computational approach to simulate press dynamics under diverse conditions, integrating sensor data from industrial presses with machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict optimal parameter configurations. Key computational tasks include finite element analysis of mechanical stress on press components, fluid dynamics modeling of ink distribution, and neural network training using historical performance data from partner printing facilities. The HPC environment is critical for handling large-scale simulations of multi-physics interactions and iterative ML training across heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include a predictive optimization toolkit that recommends pressure, temperature, and alignment settings for specific substrate-ink combinations, reducing setup time by an estimated 30-50% and waste by 15-25% in initial pilot tests. By establishing a computational framework tailored to non-scientific domains, this work aims to bridge gaps between industrial practices and data-driven decision-making in vocational printing education. The resource request supports the creation of adaptable digital twins for training purposes while advancing sustainable practices in communication industries reliant on physical media production.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate, and maintain printing presses.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic data in clinical cytogenetics demands advanced computational tools to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of diagnosing structural chromosomal abnormalities, such as translocations, deletions, and copy number variations (CNVs). Current manual and semi-automated methods for analyzing fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) images, karyotypes, and next-generation sequencing (NGS) datasets are time-intensive and prone to variability, particularly in rare or complex cases. This project proposes the development of a machine learning (ML)-driven pipeline to automate the detection and interpretation of chromosomal aberrations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) training deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to identify subtle chromosomal anomalies in high-resolution FISH and photomicroscopy images, and (2) integrating multi-omics data (e.g., whole-genome sequencing, RNA-seq) to predict the functional impact of detected variants on disease phenotypes. Computational workflows will leverage containerized environments (e.g., Singularity) for reproducibility, with parallelized processing of terabyte-scale imaging and sequencing datasets. Key challenges include optimizing image segmentation algorithms for heterogeneous cell samples and developing interpretable models to prioritize clinically actionable variants. Successfully implementing this pipeline will reduce diagnostic turnaround times, improve detection rates of low-frequency mosaic events, and enable scalable reanalysis of historical datasets as new disease-gene associations emerge. The outcomes will directly benefit precision oncology and prenatal diagnostics by providing clinicians with robust, data-driven insights for treatment planning and genetic counseling. Access to HPC resources is critical for training large-scale models, performing hyperparameter optimization, and conducting genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across diverse patient cohorts. This project bridges a vital gap between computational genomics and clinical practice, advancing the capacity of cytogenetic technologies to address complex genetic disorders.
cip_title: Cytogenetics/ Genetics/ Clinical Genetics Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform analyses of the human genome and chromosomes for the research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes instruction in chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: Law enforcement agencies face escalating challenges in managing heterogeneous records and evidence types, spanning physical artifacts, digital media, and case documentation, often across fragmented legacy systems. This project addresses critical gaps in scalable, secure, and auditable evidence lifecycle management by developing computational frameworks to optimize storage, retrieval, and chain-of-custody verification processes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to model and simulate large-scale evidence ecosystems integrating IoT sensor data from storage environments, metadata from case management databases, and unstructured digital evidence (e.g., bodycam footage, encrypted communications). The research will employ graph-based neural networks to identify latent patterns in evidence access logs, flagging anomalous retrieval attempts or procedural deviations. Parallelized natural language processing pipelines will automate cross-referencing of case reports with evidentiary inventories to detect documentation mismatches. A novel blockchain-inspired architecture will be stress-tested under simulated multi-agency workflows to evaluate decentralized audit trails while preserving data sovereignty. Computational experiments will quantify tradeoffs between cryptographic security overhead, retrieval latency, and system-wide integrity across varying evidence volumes and types. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predictive evidence lifecycle modeling, validated against historical case data from three partner agencies. This work aims to establish computational benchmarks for next-generation record-keeping systems that balance operational efficiency with legal accountability, directly informing national standards for digital evidence governance. By addressing scalability constraints inherent to conventional systems, the project seeks to enable law enforcement organizations to adapt to evolving evidence complexities while maintaining public trust through transparent, tamper-resistant documentation practices.
cip_title: Law Enforcement Record-Keeping and Evidence Management
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and procedures for managing records in police or other security offices, including storing and retrieving evidence and related data. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, office management, report preparation, organizational software, database software, physical and digital evidence properties, controlled storage and retrieval, investigative file inventories, case management, security systems, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the role of structural genomic variation (SGV) in shaping complex traits and adaptation in domesticated and wild animal populations. While single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are well-studied in animal genetics, the contribution of large-scale structural variants—including deletions, duplications, inversions, and translocations—to phenotypic diversity, fitness, and evolutionary trajectories remains poorly characterized. Current limitations stem from the computational complexity of detecting SGV across diverse genomes and modeling its interactions with regulatory elements. We propose a multi-stage computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze whole-genome sequencing data from 15 agriculturally and ecologically significant animal species, including bovids, equids, and avian taxa. Long-read sequencing datasets will be processed using scalable alignment and variant-calling pipelines optimized for distributed memory architectures. Graph-based pan-genome representations will be constructed to capture population-level SGV, followed by integrative analyses linking variants to gene expression datasets (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq) and trait databases. To model evolutionary dynamics, spatially explicit forward-time simulations will quantify how recombination rates, selection pressures, and demography interact to shape SGV distributions. Machine learning models trained on these outputs will predict the functional impact of structural variants on development, metabolism, and disease resilience. This work will establish novel computational workflows for SGV analysis in non-model organisms, identify candidate structural variants underlying key domestication and adaptation phenotypes, and provide comparative insights into the evolutionary constraints shaping animal genomes. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing data storage (~500 TB), parallelizing genome-wide analyses, and running computationally intensive simulations. Outcomes will directly inform selective breeding programs, conservation strategies, and biomedical models of human genetic disorders with structural variant etiologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of multicellular animal life forms from the experimental, comparative, and clinical (veterinary and medical) viewpoints. Includes instruction in molecular genetics, gene expression, gene regulation, genomics, epigenetic phenomena, DNA recombination and repair, genetic interactions at the microbial and higher levels, and molecular evolution.

abstract: The safe and efficient management of hazardous materials requires advanced computational tools capable of modeling complex environmental interactions, predicting risks, and optimizing mitigation strategies. Current information systems often lack the capacity to integrate real-time environmental data, material toxicity profiles, and human behavioral dynamics at scale, limiting their utility during rapidly evolving incidents. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for dynamic hazardous materials risk assessment and decision support. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating multi-scale models to simulate the dispersion of hazardous substances in diverse environmental conditions, incorporating variables such as terrain, weather, and material degradation; (2) training machine learning algorithms to predict human exposure risks and infrastructure vulnerabilities using historical incident data and synthetic scenarios; and (3) optimizing emergency response protocols through parallelized agent-based simulations of evacuation patterns and resource deployment. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated simulations for fluid dynamics modeling and distributed computing frameworks for large-scale parameter space exploration. The project will utilize existing environmental monitoring datasets while generating new synthetic training data through physics-informed neural networks. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational platform that enables real-time risk visualization, adaptive response planning, and regulatory compliance analysis. By integrating HPC capabilities with hazardous materials informatics, this work aims to significantly reduce decision latency during critical incidents while improving the precision of containment strategies. The resulting tools will provide emergency managers, environmental agencies, and industrial operators with evidence-based solutions to mitigate public health risks and environmental damage, advancing the technological infrastructure for hazardous materials management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing, monitoring, and enforcing hazardous materials management and removal. Includes instruction in environmental science, environmental health, human behavior, economics, management science, information systems and applications, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of contraband distribution networks within correctional facilities, a critical yet understudied challenge in criminal justice systems. Contraband, including illicit drugs and weapons, undermines institutional safety and rehabilitation efforts, but traditional interventions often fail due to the complexity of social and logistical networks that facilitate its spread. Current research lacks scalable computational tools to simulate these networks, which involve thousands of interacting agents (e.g., incarcerated individuals, staff, visitors) and dynamic environmental factors. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with network analysis to simulate contraband flow under varying conditions. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations across multiple scenarios, incorporating real-world data on facility layouts, movement patterns, and historical incident reports. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify latent network structures and predict high-risk interactions. The computational workflow will also test the hypothetical impacts of policy changes, such as altered visitation protocols or staff allocation strategies, on contraband reduction. Outcomes will include a validated simulation toolkit for prison administrators to proactively design interventions, as well as novel insights into the resilience of covert networks within constrained environments. By bridging criminological theory with computational social science, this project advances interdisciplinary methodologies for correctional system optimization while adhering to ethical guidelines for data anonymization and institutional confidentiality. The scalability of the approach offers potential applications to broader criminal justice contexts, including community corrections and reentry programs.
