abstract: Modern bioinformatics research requires advanced computational infrastructure to address the challenges of modeling complex biological systems through integration of multi-modal, large-scale datasets. This project seeks to develop and apply novel machine learning frameworks to analyze dynamic protein interaction networks and predict context-specific cellular responses, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in scalability and resolution. The central research problem involves deciphering how transient protein-protein interactions drive cell-state transitions in heterogeneous biological samples, a question hindered by the computational intensity of integrating time-resolved proteomics, structural biology data, and single-cell transcriptomics. We propose a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with physics-based molecular simulations to model interaction kinetics across spatial and temporal scales. The computational pipeline will implement distributed memory parallelism for training GNNs on population-scale proteomic datasets (>10^6 cells), while GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics simulations will characterize atomic-level binding affinities for prioritized targets. Containerized workflows will enable reproducible analysis across HPC architectures, with adaptive sampling strategies reducing conformational search space by 40-60%. This resource request specifically supports the deployment of these workflows on clusters with >500 nodes, requiring 150,000 core-hours/month, 20 TB of high-speed temporary storage, and multi-GPU allocations for deep learning tasks. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available software suite for scalable protein network analysis, 2) predictive models of signaling pathway rewiring in cancer progression validated against experimental datasets, and 3) novel algorithms for optimizing simulation-experiment iteration cycles. By enabling unprecedented resolution of cellular decision-making processes, this work will advance computational methodologies in systems biology while generating translational insights into therapeutic target discovery. The requested resources are critical for maintaining feasibility given the project’s O(n³) computational complexity in network inference and need for rapid iteration across biological scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer-based technologies and services to biological, biomedical, and biotechnology research. Includes instruction in algorithms, network architecture, principles of software design, human interface design, usability studies, search strategies, database management and data mining, digital image processing, computer graphics and animation, CAD, computer programming, and applications to experimental design and analysis and to specific quantitative, modeling, and analytical studies in the various biological specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community health interventions by modeling complex social determinants of health (SDOH) and optimizing resource allocation strategies for underserved populations. Despite widespread recognition of SDOH—such as housing instability, food insecurity, and transportation barriers—as critical drivers of health disparities, current approaches to integrating these factors into community health planning remain fragmented. Traditional analytical tools struggle to account for the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between socioeconomic variables, service accessibility, and health outcomes at scale. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework coupled with machine learning (ML) to simulate community-level health behaviors, service utilization patterns, and intervention impacts under varying resource allocation scenarios. The ABM will incorporate multimodal datasets, including electronic health records, census data, and community service utilization logs, to represent heterogeneous populations and their interactions with health and social systems. ML components will identify high-risk subgroups, forecast service demand, and optimize referral networks between healthcare providers and social services. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of simulating large-scale populations (N > 100,000 agents), parallelizing parameter sweeps across diverse intervention strategies, and training deep reinforcement learning models for real-time decision support. Expected outcomes include a validated computational toolkit for predicting the downstream health effects of resource allocation policies, identifying priority areas for community health worker deployment, and quantifying the cost-effectiveness of cross-sector partnerships. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on bridging health services and social care by providing data-driven methods to enhance advocacy, improve multilingual service coordination, and reduce disparities in marginalized communities. Results will be disseminated through open-source computational models and partnerships with local health departments to ensure translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as facilitators, advocates, and referral professionals linking health care and related social services with affected recipient communities. Includes instruction in public and community health, human and social services, health services administration, group counseling, health education, group advocacy, cross-cultural and multilingual communication, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Neurological disorders affecting the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves present profound diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their complex, multiscale pathophysiology. Current clinical tools often lack the resolution to capture dynamic disease mechanisms or predict individual treatment responses. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to model disease progression and optimize therapeutic strategies for neurodegenerative and neuromuscular disorders, including Alzheimer’s disease, ALS, and diabetic neuropathy. The research will integrate multimodal clinical data—such as high-resolution MRI, electrophysiological recordings, genomic profiles, and longitudinal patient outcomes—into biophysically grounded neural network models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale neural circuits, parameterize patient-specific models via Bayesian inference, and perform virtual trials of pharmacological and neuromodulatory interventions. Machine learning pipelines will be deployed to identify biomarkers predictive of treatment efficacy, while parallelized simulations will map how genetic variants and cellular stressors propagate dysfunction across brain-body networks. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated optimization and distributed memory architectures to manage terabyte-scale datasets and stochastic modeling demands. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking molecular and systems-level pathology, a scalable platform for in silico therapeutic testing, and clinically actionable stratification tools to personalize neuromodulation protocols. By elucidating mechanisms of network resilience and failure, this work aims to accelerate the translation of basic neuroscience insights into targeted therapies. The requested HPC allocation will enable the analysis of heterogeneous datasets and complex simulations that are computationally intractable with existing resources, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance precision neurology through integrative, data-driven approaches.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of all types of disease or impaired function of the brain, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, muscles and autonomic nervous system, as well as the blood vessels that relate to these structures.

abstract: Chronic diseases account for a substantial global health burden, yet many are preventable through early intervention. Current risk prediction models in preventive medicine often lack precision due to limited integration of multi-dimensional data, including genomic, environmental, and behavioral factors. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution predictive framework to identify at-risk populations and optimize personalized prevention strategies. Leveraging linked electronic health records (EHRs), genomic datasets, and geospatial environmental exposures from a cohort of 500,000 participants, we aim to model complex interactions influencing chronic disease onset, focusing on cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes. The computational approach involves training ensemble machine learning models (XGBoost, deep neural networks) on multimodal data to predict 10-year disease risk, while employing explainable AI techniques to prioritize modifiable risk factors. Agent-based simulations will then evaluate population-level impacts of hypothetical prevention strategies under varying resource allocation scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the scale and complexity of these tasks: distributed computing will enable parallel processing of EHRs and genomic data (~2 PB total), GPU acceleration will reduce deep learning training times from months to days, and large-memory nodes will support genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with fine-grained environmental interaction terms. Expected outcomes include (1) validated risk prediction models with improved accuracy (target AUC >0.90) compared to current clinical standards, (2) mechanistic insights into gene-environment-lifestyle interactions, and (3) simulation-optimized prevention protocols for resource-constrained health systems. This work will advance computational methodologies for preventive medicine while delivering scalable tools to guide clinical decision-making and public health policy. By enabling analysis at unprecedented resolution, the requested resources directly address critical bottlenecks in translating heterogeneous data into actionable prevention strategies.
cip_definition: Research focused on Preventive Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize clinical decision-making and resource allocation in acute care nursing settings using high-performance computing (HPC). A critical challenge in registered nursing is balancing patient acuity, staffing constraints, and dynamic care demands, which directly impacts patient outcomes and nurse workload. Current heuristic-based approaches for task prioritization and shift planning often fail to account for the complexity of real-time variables, including patient vitals, medication schedules, and interdisciplinary team workflows. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning (ML) model trained on multimodal electronic health record (EHR) data, including temporal trends in patient conditions, nurse-patient interactions, and institutional protocols. The model will integrate reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive care pathways under varying constraints. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of structured and unstructured EHR data, train deep neural networks with attention mechanisms for temporal pattern recognition, and run Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of staffing and intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for early identification of patient deterioration, an optimized shift scheduling algorithm to reduce nurse burnout, and a generative AI module to propose context-aware clinical interventions. These tools will be validated against retrospective data from three hospital systems, with performance metrics compared to existing nurse-led protocols. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance data-driven nursing practices, enhance patient safety, and provide scalable solutions for healthcare institutions facing staffing shortages and rising care complexity. Results will be disseminated through open-source computational workflows and continuing education modules for nursing professionals.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals in the knowledge, techniques and procedures for promoting health, providing care for sick, disabled, infirmed, or other individuals or groups. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting a physician during treatments and examinations, Referring patients to physicians and other health care specialists, and planning education for health maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in clinical workflow optimization and resource allocation within multi-specialty healthcare facilities through advanced computational modeling. The research focuses on developing a dynamic, real-time decision support system that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records (EHRs), equipment utilization logs, and staff availability metrics—to optimize clinical operations while adhering to medical regulatory standards. A critical challenge lies in balancing patient care priorities, staffing constraints, and equipment accessibility in environments with unpredictable demand, such as emergency departments or surgical units. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid machine learning and discrete-event simulation framework hosted on high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The model will employ reinforcement learning agents trained on historical operational data to predict short-term patient influx and resource demand, coupled with parallelized simulations to evaluate potential allocation strategies under diverse scenarios. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing, the system will rapidly iterate through millions of potential workflow configurations, identifying configurations that minimize patient wait times while maintaining compliance with healthcare management protocols. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive clinical operations management, validated against retrospective data from three partner hospitals. This work bridges gaps between health systems management and clinical operations by introducing computational methods traditionally used in logistics optimization to medical administration, with potential applications in disaster response planning and value-based care initiatives. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project's scale, which involves processing >10 TB of anonymized patient flow data and running complex, multi-agent simulations in near-real time.
cip_title: Medical/ Health Management and Clinical Assistant/ Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, nurses, or other health care professionals, to perform medical office or facilities management services and perform one or more clinical allied health specialties. Includes instruction in health care management; medical office administration; medical law and regulations; training in one or more diagnostic, treatment, therapy, or laboratory specialties at the assistant level or above; and applicable professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Consultation-Liaison (CL) Psychiatry by modeling the bidirectional interactions between psychiatric symptoms and complex medical illnesses. A critical challenge in this field is the lack of predictive frameworks that integrate dynamic, multimodal clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, and biomarkers—to identify patients at highest risk of psychiatric complications during medical treatment or to optimize psychopharmacological interventions in medically vulnerable populations. To address this, we propose developing computational models using machine learning (ML) and network analysis to analyze longitudinal datasets from 5,000+ patients with comorbid psychiatric and medical conditions (e.g., cancer, autoimmune disorders, post-transplant care). Key computational tasks include natural language processing (NLP) of unstructured clinical notes to extract psychiatric symptom trajectories, federated learning across multi-institutional EHRs to preserve privacy, and Bayesian network modeling to infer causal pathways linking inflammatory markers, medication regimens, and neuropsychiatric outcomes. HPC resources are essential for training deep learning architectures on high-dimensional neuroimaging data (e.g., fMRI to assess delirium risk post-surgery) and for running large-scale simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for depression exacerbation in oncology patients and delirium prevention protocols in critical care, both prioritized for real-world clinical integration. By quantifying how psychiatric and medical factors interact over time, this work aims to generate scalable tools for personalized intervention, reducing hospital readmissions and improving quality of life in medically complex populations. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as a template for future studies at the intersection of psychiatry and systemic medical illness, a domain underrepresented in precision medicine research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of psychiatric disorders and symptoms in complex medically ill patients. This includes treatment of patients with acute or chronic medical, neurological, obstetrical, or surgical illness in which psychiatric illness is affecting their medical care and/or quality of life, and patients who have a psychiatric disorder that is the direct consequence of a primary medical condition, a somatoform disorder, or psychological factors affecting a general medical condition.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address analytical and creative challenges in Jazz Studies that exceed the capabilities of traditional methodologies. Jazz, characterized by improvisation, complex harmonic structures, and dynamic ensemble interactions, generates intricate artistic data that remains underexplored at scale. Current manual and low-throughput computational approaches struggle to systematically analyze decades of audio recordings, disentangle improvisational patterns, or model real-time collaborative processes in ensemble performances. This research proposes a computational framework combining machine learning (ML), signal processing, and agent-based modeling to study jazz as both a historical corpus and a living creative practice. ML models, including convolutional and recurrent neural networks, will be trained on annotated jazz recordings to identify stylistic signatures of improvisation across eras and artists, while audio feature extraction pipelines will quantify timbral, rhythmic, and harmonic evolution in large-scale discographies. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model improvisational decision-making in virtual ensembles, incorporating jazz theory rules and stochastic creativity parameters. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources to process terabytes of audio data, parallelize model training across epochs, and run real-time multi-agent interactions. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking improvisational motifs to historical contexts, generative tools for composers exploring hybrid human-AI collaboration, and new analytical metrics for jazz scholarship. By bridging computational methods with artistic inquiry, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of jazz’s evolution, expand pedagogical resources, and preserve improvisational traditions through data-driven insights. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical to handling the project’s scale, enabling analyses of thousands of recordings and high-fidelity simulations of ensemble dynamics that individual workstations cannot support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study and master the performance and composition of Jazz. Includes instruction in the history of Jazz and related musical styles such as the Blues, Jazz composition and theory, improvisation, Jazz instrument and ensemble performance, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing autonomous vehicle (AV) deployment across heterogeneous jurisdictional boundaries. As transportation systems increasingly integrate AI-driven technologies, existing legal doctrines—spanning liability, privacy, cybersecurity, and interoperability standards—face unprecedented strain. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically map conflicts or synergies between municipal, state, federal, and international AV regulations, particularly as these policies adapt dynamically to technological advancements. The research employs computational legal analytics, combining natural language processing (NLP) and network modeling to parse over 250,000 regulatory documents, court rulings, and policy drafts from 15 countries. Custom transformer-based models will identify latent patterns in liability attribution clauses, while multi-agent simulations will test how conflicting regional laws impact cross-border AV operations. A graph database will model dependencies between technical standards (e.g., sensor data retention mandates) and ethical-legal principles (e.g., algorithmic transparency requirements). By quantifying the "regulatory friction" impeding scalable AV ecosystems, this study aims to produce a decision-support toolkit for policymakers, identifying high-impact areas for legal harmonization. The computational workload necessitates GPU-accelerated NLP pipelines for real-time clause extraction and terabyte-scale graph traversals to simulate policy cascades. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of annotated regulatory networks and a framework for stress-testing proposed legislation against emergent risks in AI-driven transportation. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between legal hermeneutics, computational social science, and systems engineering, offering a novel methodology for 21st-century transportation law scholarship.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting land, sea, air, and space transportation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges in modeling and optimizing next-generation power electronic systems for grid-scale renewable energy integration. The increasing complexity of modern power converters—driven by high switching frequencies, wide-bandgap semiconductor devices, and dynamic grid stability requirements—demands high-fidelity simulations that exceed the capabilities of conventional computing resources. Current models struggle to resolve nanosecond-scale switching transients while simultaneously simulating system-level interactions over millisecond timescales, creating a critical gap in predicting electromagnetic interference, thermal stresses, and control stability. To overcome this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining finite-element analysis (FEA) for device physics, circuit-level transient simulations, and data-driven surrogate modeling accelerated through machine learning. The requested high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallel execution of massively parameterized FEA simulations using COMSOL Multiphysics, coupled with real-time co-simulation of network dynamics via MATLAB/Simulink. GPU-accelerated tensor operations will train neural networks to approximate device behavior, reducing simulation times by orders of magnitude while maintaining physical accuracy. Expected outcomes include validated models for 10kV SiC MOSFET-based converters, predictive algorithms for harmonic mitigation in hybrid AC/DC microgrids, and open-source tools for power electronics co-design. This work directly supports national priorities for decarbonization by enabling the development of efficient, resilient power conversion systems critical for integrating offshore wind and solar farms into aging grid infrastructure. The computational methodologies developed will also find broader applications in electric vehicle drivetrains and industrial motor drives, advancing the state of the art in power electronics research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of electrical and electronic systems and their components, including electrical power generation systems; and the analysis of problems such as superconductor, wave propagation, energy storage and retrieval, and reception and amplification.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational frameworks to optimize the design of next-generation catalytic materials for sustainable chemical processes, a critical challenge in chemical and petroleum engineering. Traditional experimental approaches to catalyst discovery are time- and resource-intensive, particularly for complex systems such as multicomponent alloys or nanostructured surfaces. To address this, we propose a multiscale modeling strategy combining density functional theory (DFT), kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to predict catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability under industrially relevant conditions. The research will focus on transition metal catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation and biomass-derived feedstock conversion, targeting enhanced efficiency and reduced energy costs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale DFT calculations for surface adsorption energetics, simulate microkinetic pathways at reaction interfaces, and train ML models on datasets spanning composition-structure-property relationships. The computational workflow will integrate open-source quantum chemistry packages (e.g., Quantum ESPRESSO) with custom kinetic codes, leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes for ML-driven optimization. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel catalyst formulations with improved performance metrics, atomistic insights into deactivation mechanisms, and a publicly accessible database of computed catalytic properties. This work directly supports the Engineering Chemistry program’s goals by advancing materials innovation for green chemical processes and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational chemistry and reaction engineering. The requested HPC allocation will enable the parameterization of models with experimental validation data from project collaborators, ensuring relevance to real-world engineering systems. By bridging molecular-scale simulations with process-scale optimization, this research aims to accelerate the development of sustainable technologies central to the decarbonization of the chemical industry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of chemical principles to the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems, such as development of electronic materials, solid-state science and technology, polymers, ceramics, and biomaterials. Includes instruction in physical chemistry, organic chemistry, materials science, chemical processes and systems, chemical reaction engineering, biochemical engineering, engineering mathematics, classical and modern physics, and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing real-time, adaptive communication networks for emerging media environments. As digital platforms evolve, there is a critical need to model and simulate complex, large-scale communication systems that can dynamically adjust to fluctuating user demands, bandwidth constraints, and heterogeneous data types (e.g., augmented reality, 4K/8K streaming). Traditional computational tools lack the capacity to handle the latency-sensitive, multi-modal datasets inherent to these scenarios, limiting progress in designing resilient infrastructures. The proposed research will develop parallelized machine learning models to simulate network behavior under stress conditions, integrating real-world data from social media, IoT devices, and telecommunication logs. Key computational tasks include training neural networks for predictive traffic routing, deploying agent-based models to emulate user interaction patterns, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to assess failure thresholds. These workflows require distributed computing architectures to manage terabytes of data and reduce processing times from weeks to hours. Successfully implementing this project will yield two primary outcomes: (1) a publicly accessible framework for simulating next-generation communication networks, validated against industry benchmarks, and (2) actionable insights into protocol design to minimize latency in high-density user environments. By addressing scalability challenges through HPC-driven methods, this work directly supports the development of robust communication technologies capable of meeting future societal demands. The resource allocation will enable iterative testing of hypotheses at unprecedented scales, bridging gaps between theoretical network models and practical deployment requirements in non-scientific sectors such as media distribution and emergency response systems.
cip_title: Communications Technologies and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications technologies and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern computing systems, driven by applications in artificial intelligence, edge computing, and cyber-physical systems, demands advanced methods to optimize hardware-software co-design under stringent energy and latency constraints. Existing simulation frameworks struggle to model emerging heterogeneous architectures—such as chiplets, near-memory computing units, and reconfigurable accelerators—at scale, limiting the ability to explore design trade-offs efficiently. This project proposes a computational framework to address these challenges by integrating system-level simulation, machine learning-driven optimization, and hardware-aware algorithm co-development. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale simulations of multi-physics system behavior, including thermal dynamics, power delivery, and interconnect performance, across diverse workloads. Parallelized optimization algorithms will iteratively refine hardware configurations and scheduling policies while accounting for real-time operational variability. A key innovation involves developing surrogate models trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate design space exploration for domain-specific architectures. The computational workload necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training, distributed memory clusters for batched simulations, and high-memory nodes for analyzing multi-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source tools for simulating next-generation heterogeneous systems, (2) validated co-design methodologies to reduce energy-delay product by 30–50% compared to baseline architectures, and (3) a publicly available benchmark suite capturing cross-layer interactions in edge-to-cloud computing pipelines. This work will directly advance capabilities in energy-efficient computing and provide a foundation for academic and industry researchers to optimize emerging technologies such as neuromorphic accelerators and quantum-classical hybrid systems. The requested resources will enable critical scaling studies and sensitivity analyses that are infeasible on local research computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing energy-efficient communication protocols for next-generation wireless networks, which require real-time adaptability to dynamic channel conditions and heterogeneous user demands. Current methods for protocol design struggle to balance computational complexity, latency, and energy consumption in scenarios involving massive device connectivity, such as IoT-enabled smart infrastructure or ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining graph neural networks (GNNs) and multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to autonomously generate context-aware resource allocation strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale network environments with 10,000+ nodes, train deep reinforcement learning models with parallelized experience replay buffers, and perform Monte Carlo analyses of protocol robustness under stochastic interference patterns. Key computational tasks include distributed training of GNNs across GPU clusters, real-time optimization of MORL policies via evolutionary algorithms, and validation through hardware-in-the-loop emulation of 5G/6G baseband processing. The project will utilize CUDA-accelerated tensor operations and MPI-based synchronization for cross-node parameter updates. Expected outcomes include a novel protocol suite that reduces energy consumption by 20-35% compared to existing standards while maintaining sub-millisecond latency thresholds. These advancements will directly support the development of sustainable, high-density communication systems critical for smart cities and industrial IoT applications. The resulting datasets and open-source simulation toolkit will provide the research community with scalable benchmarks for evaluating network optimization algorithms under realistic constraints. By integrating machine learning with HPC-driven network modeling, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical protocol design and deployable solutions for emerging wireless technologies.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronics, and Communications Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical, electronics, and communications engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation models for boutique hotel networks using high-performance computing (HPC) to address the challenge of real-time demand forecasting in hyper-seasonal tourism markets. Traditional revenue management systems struggle to integrate real-time data streams—such as social media sentiment, localized event triggers, and climate anomalies—with operational constraints like staff scheduling and energy consumption patterns. The computational complexity of modeling these multidimensional variables at scale requires advanced parallel processing capabilities. We propose developing an adaptive machine learning framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of tourist decision-making behaviors with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to simulate pricing strategies across heterogeneous market conditions. The HPC infrastructure will enable simultaneous processing of terabyte-scale datasets from property management systems, IoT sensors, and third-party booking platforms, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in demand projections. Key innovations include spatial-temporal graph neural networks to capture cross-property demand spillover effects and a federated learning architecture to preserve data privacy across independent hotel operators. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of reducing revenue leakage by 12-18% in pilot implementations, with particular significance for small-to-midsize hospitality businesses competing in algorithmically dominated markets. The computational workflows will be containerized for cloud deployment, creating a scalable template for ethical AI adoption in tourism micro-enterprises. This interdisciplinary approach bridges operations research, behavioral economics, and computational social science, advancing resource optimization paradigms beyond conventional yield management frameworks.
cip_title: Tourism and Travel Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide direct retail services to hotel and motel clients and customers in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in the principles of hotel/motel operations, customer sales and assistance operations and techniques, telephone operations, and basic office management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of algorithmic labor coordination in platform-based gig economies, focusing on how computational systems shape worker autonomy, wage volatility, and collective action potential. While existing labor studies research has qualitatively examined gig work conditions, this study employs large-scale computational modeling to quantify the emergent effects of platform algorithms on labor markets. The research problem centers on the lack of transparency in how real-time task allocation, surge pricing mechanisms, and performance metrics create systemic inequities across demographic groups and geographic regions. Using anonymized ride-hailing and delivery platform datasets (simulated where proprietary data is unavailable), we will develop agent-based models that simulate worker decision-making under competing algorithmic constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for running thousands of parallelized simulations that account for heterogeneous worker populations, dynamic pricing environments, and evolving labor regulations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns of algorithmic bias in historical wage data, while natural language processing will analyze worker forum discussions to map grievance escalation pathways. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting tipping points in labor mobilization efforts and a policy toolkit for regulating adaptive pricing systems. This computationally intensive approach advances labor studies by bridging discrete case analyses with systemic modeling of platform economies, offering new methodologies to assess how business-driven AI systems reconfigure power relationships in 21st-century work structures. The project will generate open-source simulation tools to help worker advocacy groups test intervention strategies in silico before real-world implementation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of various aspects of work, labor organization and policy, and labor movements from the perspective of the social sciences and history. Includes instruction in labor history; political and ideological issues; worker movements and social organizations; civil rights; labor law and policy studies; labor economics; international and comparative labor studies; and applications to specific industries, groups, locations, and time periods.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize predictive maintenance frameworks for next-generation military aerospace ground equipment (AGE) using high-fidelity simulations of equipment degradation under operational stress. Current maintenance protocols rely on static schedules or reactive diagnostics, leading to unplanned downtime, resource inefficiencies, and risks to mission-critical operations. To address this, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) model trained on multiphysics simulations of thermal, vibrational, and corrosion-induced failures in AGE components such as hydraulic test stands, nitrogen servicing carts, and cryogenic cooling units. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize these simulations across diverse environmental conditions (e.g., desert, maritime, arctic) and operational loads, generating the terabyte-scale datasets required to capture rare failure modes. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and corrosion dynamics, and time-series analytics to map sensor data to simulated degradation pathways. The resulting ML model will predict remaining useful life (RUL) of components with quantified uncertainty, enabling condition-based maintenance aligned with mission readiness requirements. Outcomes include a digital twin framework adaptable to emerging AGE systems, validated against field data from three active U.S. Air Force bases. This work bridges gaps between legacy maintenance practices and data-driven decision-making, directly supporting the U.S. Department of Defense’s priorities for sustainment modernization. By reducing unnecessary maintenance cycles and mitigating catastrophic failures, the project aims to decrease lifecycle costs by an estimated 12–18% per platform while enhancing operational safety in contested logistics environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology, and maintenance of ground-based systems and equipments used to support aviation flight operations and space operations. Includes instruction in computer science, electronics, basic sciences and quantitative methods, air conditioning and refrigeration, corrosion control, fluid power, hazardous materials, industrial safety, maintenance management, vehicle and equipment operation, and applications to specific ground support systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic decision-making in multi-location restaurant supply chains through the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework. The food services industry faces escalating complexity in balancing perishable inventory logistics, sustainability goals, and hyper-localized demand patterns across franchise networks—a challenge compounded by climate variability and shifting consumer preferences. Current analytical tools often fail to integrate real-time environmental data, supplier reliability metrics, and waste-tracking systems at scales necessary for enterprise-level optimization. We propose a computational approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to create a multi-objective decision support system. The framework will simulate interactions between 1) climate-impacted agricultural supply timelines, 2) regionalized menu engineering constraints, and 3) waste-reduction targets across distribution networks. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets spanning historical spoilage rates, weather patterns, and cross-location sales correlations. Expected outcomes include a predictive model capable of generating adaptive procurement strategies that reduce supply chain carbon emissions by 12-18% while maintaining <2% stockout rates across simulated franchise clusters. The research will produce open-source optimization algorithms tailored for small-to-midsize restaurant groups lacking dedicated analytics infrastructure. By quantifying trade-offs between localized menu flexibility and centralized purchasing efficiencies, this work addresses a critical gap in food service operations research while advancing computational methods for ethical supply chain design in perishable goods industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market restaurants, food services in hospitality establishments, food service chains and franchise networks, and restaurant supply operations. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, food services management, wholesale logistics and distribution, franchise operations, business networking, personnel management, culinary arts, business planning and capitalization, food industry operations, marketing and retailing, business law and regulations, finance, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance image-guided interventional radiology (IR) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize the integration of multi-modal imaging data and real-time device tracking during minimally invasive procedures. Current limitations in computational speed and data synthesis hinder the precision of fluoroscopy, CT, and MRI-guided interventions, particularly in complex anatomical environments where rapid decision-making is critical. We aim to develop a computational framework that dynamically fuses pre-procedural 3D anatomical models with intraprocedural imaging streams, enabling adaptive navigation of catheters, stents, and embolization devices. The research problem centers on overcoming latency and resolution mismatches between imaging modalities, which contribute to suboptimal device placement, prolonged radiation exposure, and procedural complications. To address this, we will implement GPU-accelerated deformable registration algorithms to align real-time 2D fluoroscopic sequences with high-resolution 3D vascular maps, coupled with machine learning models trained on retrospective IR case data to predict tissue-device interactions. HPC resources will be essential for processing terabytes of imaging data, running finite element simulations of device navigation, and training deep learning networks for artifact reduction in low-dose fluoroscopy. Expected outcomes include a validated software pipeline that reduces procedure time by 15–20% in simulated angioplasty and embolization workflows, improves target vessel accuracy to sub-millimeter levels, and decreases radiation dose through predictive collimation. This work will establish a foundation for real-time, AI-enhanced IR systems capable of handling heterogeneous imaging inputs, directly benefiting patients requiring urgent interventions (e.g., stroke thrombolysis) or anatomically challenging drainages. The computational tools developed will be shared via an open-source platform to accelerate innovation in image-guided therapy research.
cip_definition: Research focused on image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages. Does NOT require prior completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: Radiation therapy efficacy is critically dependent on the precise delivery of tumoricidal doses while sparing adjacent healthy tissues, a challenge exacerbated by dynamic anatomical changes (e.g., organ motion, tumor shrinkage) during treatment. Current adaptive radiotherapy workflows, which adjust plans using periodic imaging, are limited by computational bottlenecks in processing high-resolution, real-time imaging data and rapidly recalculating optimized dose distributions. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework for real-time adaptive radiation therapy (RT-ART) in Medical Radiologic Technology. The research problem centers on integrating continuous MRI-guided imaging with instantaneous dose recalculation, enabling submillimeter accuracy in targeting moving tumors. The computational approach combines GPU-accelerated deformable image registration algorithms, Monte Carlo dose simulation, and machine learning models trained to predict short-term anatomical shifts from time-resolved 4D-MRI data. These models will be iteratively refined using retrospective clinical datasets from thoracic and abdominal radiotherapy patients, with HPC resources enabling parallel processing of multi-terabyte imaging repositories. Key technical challenges include reducing latency in dose optimization loops to under 10 seconds and validating computational predictions against physical phantom measurements. Expected outcomes include a scalable RT-ART pipeline capable of dynamically adjusting beam parameters during treatment delivery, potentially reducing planning target volume margins by 30–50% and lowering radiation-induced toxicity risks. The project’s significance lies in bridging a critical gap between emerging imaging technologies and their clinical translation, offering a foundation for personalized, motion-robust radiotherapy. Successful implementation will require access to HPC clusters with high-memory nodes, multi-GPU configurations, and fast interconnects to handle concurrent image analysis, dose computation, and uncertainty modeling tasks.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making in complex, multi-stakeholder business ecosystems under uncertainty, with a focus on ethical and regulatory constraints. Traditional business analytics models often simplify interactions between firms, consumers, and regulators as linear or static systems, inadequately addressing real-world complexities such as conflicting incentives, evolving policies, and emergent collective behaviors. We propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate adaptive strategies across interconnected supply chains, consumer networks, and regulatory bodies. The research will leverage high-performance computing to scale simulations involving >10^5 heterogeneous agents with time-dependent interactions, incorporating real-world datasets on market transactions, environmental impact metrics, and policy timelines. Key computational challenges include parallelizing RL training across distributed agents, managing sparse reward structures in ethical constraint optimization, and quantifying cascading effects of localized decisions. Methodologies will combine graph neural networks for relationship encoding, Monte Carlo tree search for multi-agent coordination, and interpretability frameworks to audit emergent system behaviors. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available toolkit for simulating policy-business-consumer feedback loops, 2) quantitative metrics for resilience and fairness in cross-organizational decision systems, and 3) case studies demonstrating conflict resolution in pharmaceutical supply chains during humanitarian crises. By bridging computational social science, operations research, and AI ethics, this work aims to advance decision-support systems that balance profitability with societal impact—a critical gap in current business analytics paradigms. The scale of interaction modeling and need for rapid scenario testing necessitate GPU-accelerated clusters with large-memory nodes to handle the combinatorial state space and enable real-time sensitivity analyses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to solve business challenges. Includes instruction in machine learning, optimization methods, computer algorithms, probability and stochastic models, information economics, logistics, strategy, consumer behavior, marketing, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in predictive modeling for mental health treatment outcomes by integrating multimodal data sources—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, social determinants of health, and real-time behavioral data—through advanced computational methods. Current approaches often analyze these datasets in isolation, limiting their ability to capture the complex interactions between biological, psychological, and social factors that influence mental health trajectories. The research problem centers on developing scalable, interpretable models to predict individualized treatment responses and long-term outcomes for patients with mood and anxiety disorders, which account for a significant proportion of global disability. To achieve this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble machine learning models on heterogeneous datasets, leveraging parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, feature selection, and hyperparameter optimization. Graph neural networks will model social network influences, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will extract semantic features from clinical notes. Federated learning architectures will enable privacy-preserving analysis across institutional EHR systems. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the integration of high-dimensional genomic data with temporal behavioral patterns—necessitate GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for treatment-resistant depression identification, (2) a framework for dynamic risk stratification using streaming mobile health data, and (3) open-source tools for reproducible computational psychiatry research. By elucidating interactions between treatment modalities and psychosocial contexts, this work aims to inform personalized intervention strategies and optimize resource allocation in overburdened mental health systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the scale and complexity of these analyses, which would be computationally infeasible with standard institutional infrastructure.
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric emergency care requires rapid, evidence-based decisions under high-stakes conditions, yet clinical guidance often relies on data from adult populations or small pediatric cohorts. Children exhibit unique physiological responses to critical illness, and the ethical complexity of conducting interventional studies in this vulnerable population limits the availability of high-quality real-world data. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to model pediatric emergency scenarios, predict outcomes, and optimize treatment strategies using high-performance computing (HPC). The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs) from 15 tertiary pediatric emergency departments, high-frequency vital sign streams, and genomic biomarkers of shock and sepsis. A machine learning pipeline will be implemented to identify dynamic risk patterns for decompensation in critically ill children, leveraging recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer architectures to process temporal data. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate physiological responses to interventions (e.g., fluid resuscitation, vasopressor titration) across developmental stages, incorporating pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic variability from neonatal to adolescent populations. Finite element analysis will model trauma-related injuries in pediatric anatomies derived from de-identified CT/MRI repositories. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, necessitating HPC resources for GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter space exploration, and real-time ensemble forecasting. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for early recognition of clinical deterioration, validated against multicenter prospective data; (2) age-stratified intervention thresholds for hemorrhagic shock and respiratory failure; and (3) open-source computational models of pediatric physiological systems. By creating the first HPC-enabled platform specifically designed for pediatric emergency simulations, this work aims to transform time-sensitive clinical decision-making while establishing scalable infrastructure for pediatric translational research.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage emergencies in infants and children.

abstract: Dental implant failure, often attributed to biomechanical factors such as inadequate osseointegration, stress shielding, or occlusal overload, remains a critical challenge in implantology. Current clinical guidelines lack robust predictive models to optimize implant placement, design, and postoperative loading protocols for heterogeneous patient populations. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate bone-implant biomechanics under multifactorial physiological conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome the limitations of traditional in vitro and low-resolution modeling approaches. The research will integrate patient-specific computed tomography (CT) data, material property variations, and dynamic occlusal forces into finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify patterns in multi-terabyte datasets encompassing implant survival rates, bone remodeling responses, and microbial biofilm interactions at the implant surface. Key objectives include (1) quantifying stress distribution patterns in peri-implant bone under simulated masticatory cycles, (2) predicting long-term bone adaptation using mechanoregulation theory-based algorithms, and (3) establishing computational thresholds for safe immediate loading protocols in osteoporotic bone. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of 3D microstructure-informed models across 10,000+ core hours, incorporating stochastic variations in bone quality and occlusal forces. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for implant success probability, optimized taper angle and thread design recommendations for at-risk populations, and data-driven guidelines for prosthodontic load distribution. This computational approach addresses a critical gap in personalized implant treatment planning while reducing reliance on trial-and-error clinical methodologies. The resulting models and datasets will be made available to the implantology research community through a curated repository, potentially transforming evidence-based practice in surgical and restorative decision-making.
cip_definition: Research focused on the surgical and restorative aspects of implant dentistry.

abstract: This project seeks to advance diesel engine diagnostics and performance optimization through high-fidelity computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in diesel mechanics. Modern diesel engines face increasing demands for efficiency, reduced emissions, and reliability under diverse operating conditions. However, experimental testing alone is insufficient to explore the complex interplay of combustion dynamics, mechanical stress, and thermal behavior in real-world scenarios. Current diagnostic tools also lack predictive capabilities for emerging hybrid and alternative-fuel systems. To bridge this gap, this research will develop multi-physics simulation frameworks integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion analysis, finite element analysis (FEA) for component stress prediction, and machine learning models trained on engine sensor data. HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of fuel injection timing, turbocharger efficiency, and aftertreatment system performance across millions of operational cycles. A key innovation involves coupling real-world telemetry from fleet vehicles with digital twin simulations to predict maintenance needs and failure modes. The computational workload requires parallel processing of 3D transient combustion simulations, automated meshing of complex engine geometries, and ensemble training of neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include optimized combustion chamber designs for biodiesel blends, predictive algorithms for injector fouling, and a publicly accessible database of simulated engine degradation scenarios. This work will provide diesel technicians with enhanced diagnostic protocols and training modules for next-generation engines while contributing open-source tools for the heavy equipment industry. By applying HPC to diesel mechanics, the project aims to reduce lifecycle costs of industrial engines by 15-20% and accelerate the adoption of sustainable fuel technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain diesel engines in vehicles such as automobiles, buses, ships, trucks, railroad locomotives, and construction equipment; as well as stationary diesel engines in electrical generators and related equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing prehospital emergency interventions performed by EMT paramedics. Prehospital care involves rapid, high-stakes decision-making under resource constraints, yet existing protocols rely on generalized guidelines that may not account for dynamic patient variables, environmental factors, or real-time biosignal trends. The research problem centers on improving the precision of field interventions—such as fluid resuscitation, airway management, or drug administration—by integrating multimodal data streams (e.g., vital signs, injury kinematics, geospatial data, and wearable sensor outputs) into adaptive, patient-specific predictive models. The computational approach combines mechanistic modeling of physiological systems with machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate intervention outcomes across diverse trauma and medical emergency scenarios. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to refine hybrid models that link hemodynamic simulations with probabilistic outcome predictions, accounting for noise and uncertainty inherent in field-acquired data. Additionally, reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and de-identified clinical datasets to identify context-aware intervention strategies that balance risks of over- and under-treatment. The project will validate models against retrospective EMS data and in silico trials simulating rare but critical edge cases (e.g., pediatric trauma, polytrauma with comorbid conditions). Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for simulating prehospital care decisions and a proof-of-concept decision support system that prioritizes interpretability for EMT workflows. By bridging computational physiology, operational analytics, and emergency medicine, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven protocols that enhance patient outcomes while respecting the unique constraints of prehospital care environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the remote supervision of physicians, to recognize, assess, and manage medical emergencies in prehospital settings and to supervise Ambulance personnel. Includes instruction in basic, intermediate, and advanced EMT procedures; emergency surgical procedures; medical triage; rescue operations; crisis scene management and personnel supervision; equipment operation and maintenance; patient stabilization, monitoring, and care; drug administration; identification and preliminary diagnosis of diseases and injuries; communication and computer operations; basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: The safe and efficient management of hazardous materials requires advanced predictive tools to address complex interactions between contaminants, environmental systems, and engineered remediation strategies. Current risk assessment models often lack the resolution to account for dynamic multi-phase transport, heterogeneous subsurface conditions, and site-specific biogeochemical processes, leading to uncertainties in waste disposal protocols. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate contaminant fate and transport in hazardous waste scenarios, with a focus on optimizing containment and treatment systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to integrate multi-scale numerical models coupling fluid dynamics, reactive transport, and microbial degradation processes. The computational approach will employ finite element and lattice Boltzmann methods to resolve pore-scale interactions in engineered barriers, while machine learning techniques will parameterize regional-scale models using historical contamination datasets. Key objectives include validating simulations against experimental column studies of heavy metal leaching and organic compound biodegradation, then scaling these results to predict long-term performance of landfill liners and in situ bioremediation systems. The HPC environment is critical for managing large parameter spaces, iterative optimization of remediation designs, and probabilistic risk analyses under varying climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible modeling toolkit for predicting contaminant breakthrough times, quantifying uncertainty in waste containment systems, and identifying cost-effective strategies for legacy site cleanup. By enabling higher-resolution simulations of coupled physical, chemical, and biological processes, this work aims to reduce environmental liabilities and advance evidence-based policies for hazardous waste management. The requested computing resources will directly support 3D transient simulations requiring parallelized solvers, GPU-accelerated machine learning workflows, and petascale data storage for sensitivity analyses across thousands of scenario permutations.
cip_title: Hazardous Materials Management and Waste Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in identifying and disposing of hazardous materials. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, biohazard identification, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, hazardous waste disposal procedures and systems, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance real-time decision-making in multi-domain command and control (MDC2) environments by addressing the challenge of integrating heterogeneous, dynamic data streams under adversarial conditions. Military operations increasingly rely on fused intelligence from distributed sensors, human reports, and networked platforms, yet delays in synthesizing these inputs into actionable insights persist due to fragmented data architectures and escalating cyber-physical threats. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate contested information environments, focusing on adaptive algorithms for data prioritization, trust scoring, and resilient resource allocation. Agent-based modeling will emulate adversarial behaviors and network disruptions, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will analyze dependencies between entities in command hierarchies and sensor grids. A hybrid approach combining federated learning and edge computing paradigms will be tested to balance latency constraints with computational demands in tactical edge scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for evaluating resource allocation policies under varying threat profiles, validated against synthetic scenarios mirroring peer-conflict escalation dynamics. The work will advance methodologies for autonomous system coordination in denied environments, directly contributing to the development of next-generation command systems capable of maintaining decision superiority amid information warfare tactics. By bridging gaps between distributed computing, adversarial machine learning, and doctrinal command principles, this project occupies a specialized niche at the intersection of computational resilience and military operations theory.
cip_title: Intelligence, Command Control and Information Operations, Other (MILITARY)
cip_definition: Any instructional program in intelligence, command control and information operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern construction projects demands precise and safe operation of mobile cranes, yet dynamic load management, environmental interactions, and human-machine coordination remain critical challenges. Current operational models and training protocols often rely on static load charts and simplified simulations, which inadequately capture real-world variables such as wind forces, ground instability, and operator decision-making under stress. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate mobile crane operations under diverse, high-risk scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps. The research will integrate multi-physics simulations—combining structural mechanics, fluid dynamics, and control systems—to model crane behavior during lifting, swinging, and emergency braking. Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze operator performance data, identifying patterns in decision-making errors and optimizing response protocols. Validated against real-world sensor data from crane-mounted IoT devices, these models will enable scalable, real-time simulations of complex job sites, including variable terrain and multi-crane coordination. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need for parallel processing of high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets and iterative optimization of control algorithms—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for dynamic load capacity adjustments, risk assessment tools for site-specific hazards, and adaptive training modules that respond to operator behavior in simulated environments. By bridging the gap between theoretical models and operational realities, this work aims to reduce accident rates, enhance safety standards, and inform updates to certification protocols. The project will also provide a template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into vocational training programs, fostering technological literacy in crane operations and advancing the technical rigor of heavy machinery education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to hoist and swing loads via complex rotating machinery that is driver operated. Includes instruction in crane operational characteristics, load and capacity chart usage, emergency control skills, safety, specific types of mobile cranes and loading devices, applicable codes and standards, and applications to particular types of jobs and loads.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of legal norms in transnational digital governance frameworks, an emerging interdisciplinary niche intersecting computational social science, legal theory, and data ethics. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable methodologies to systematically trace how decentralized, cross-jurisdictional legal systems—such as those governing data privacy, algorithmic accountability, and AI ethics—adapt to conflicting cultural, political, and technical pressures. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on manual case law analysis or qualitative policy comparisons, which struggle to capture the dynamic, large-scale interactions between formal statutes, corporate self-regulation, and grassroots advocacy in digital spaces. To address this gap, the project will employ transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models and temporal network analysis to map semantic shifts and influence pathways across a corpus of over 10 million legal documents, including international treaties, corporate transparency reports, and digital platform governance policies. Computational workflows will involve fine-tuning domain-specific language models to detect latent patterns in legal argumentation, paired with graph-based algorithms to model the diffusion of regulatory concepts across jurisdictions and stakeholders. The scale of data ingestion (spanning 15+ languages and 120+ jurisdictions) and the need for real-time simulation of norm formation scenarios necessitate HPC capabilities for distributed data processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-memory network analysis. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a novel framework for quantifying legal interoperability in transnational digital governance, 2) open-access tools for visualizing regulatory divergence in multi-stakeholder systems, and 3) empirically grounded policy recommendations to address asymmetries in global tech lawmaking. By integrating computational methods with critical legal studies, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying law as a complex adaptive system in digitally mediated societies.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on law and legal issues from the perspective of the social sciences and humanities.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in unstructured administrative workflow optimization, a critical yet understudied challenge within business operations support. Traditional process management tools struggle to adapt to dynamic, non-routine tasks characteristic of cross-functional secretarial services, particularly in environments requiring rapid coordination between human agents, digital systems, and evolving compliance requirements. The study proposes developing a hybrid computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), reinforcement learning, and multi-agent system modeling to simulate and optimize decision pathways in complex administrative ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on historical communication logs (emails, meeting transcripts, project trackers) and operational metadata, while simultaneously running parallelized simulations of workflow alternatives. The computational approach will employ graph neural networks to map latent dependencies between tasks and participants, coupled with Monte Carlo tree search algorithms to identify resource allocation strategies that minimize process latency without increasing error rates. Expected outcomes include a novel metric system for quantifying "administrative friction" in real-world scenarios and an open-source toolkit for predicting workflow bottlenecks under variable staffing conditions or regulatory constraints. This research bridges computational social science with operational analytics, offering significant potential to advance evidence-based practices in administrative services—a sector historically reliant on heuristic methods. By demonstrating how HPC-enabled models can transform unstructured business operations, the project aims to establish new standards for adaptive resource allocation in hybrid human-digital work environments.
cip_title: Business Operations Support and Secretarial Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in administrative and secretarial services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model stochastic gene regulatory networks governing cellular differentiation, with applications to developmental biology and cancer. A central challenge in understanding cell fate transitions lies in quantifying how stochastic fluctuations in gene expression interact with nonlinear network dynamics to drive phenotypic outcomes. While deterministic models capture average behaviors, they fail to predict rare but biologically critical events, such as aberrant differentiation or therapy-resistant cancer cell emergence. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid approach combining continuous-time Markov chain models for small networks with scalable agent-based simulations for larger systems. The chemical master equation framework will be adapted to incorporate epigenetic state transitions and spatially heterogeneous signaling cues, while parallelized agent-based models will track single-cell trajectories across experimentally parameterized gene networks. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the combinatorial complexity of state spaces, perform parameter sweeps across uncertain kinetic rates, and statistically characterize rare transition paths. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into how noise amplification in specific network motifs biases differentiation decisions, (2) predictive metrics for identifying critical control nodes in pathological cell state transitions, and (3) open-source simulation tools optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures. By bridging spatial stochastic modeling with single-cell omics data from collaborating experimental labs, this work will establish quantitative principles for manipulating cell fate landscapes. The computational infrastructure developed will directly support three ongoing studies on neural crest cell differentiation, hematopoietic stem cell aging, and tumor microenvironment-driven drug resistance, with models deployable to broader cellular decision-making contexts. Resource allocation will enable parameter estimation at biologically realistic scales, where brute-force simulation of 10^5–10^6 interacting cells remains infeasible on institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to genomics, molecular modeling, structural biology, ecology, evolutionary biology and systems of analysis of neurobiology, physiology, and metabolism. Includes instruction in computational mathematics, chaos and nonlinear systems, perturbation methods, evolutionary biology, molecular biology, bioinformatics, and neurobiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize individualized educational interventions for students with intellectual disabilities (ID), leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of personalizing learning strategies at scale. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual, qualitative assessments, which are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict the long-term efficacy of pedagogical strategies across diverse cognitive and behavioral profiles. To overcome these barriers, we propose a data-driven approach integrating multimodal student data—including academic performance, behavioral observations, and sensor-based engagement metrics—with computational models of learning progression. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical and simulated datasets to identify patterns in skill acquisition, predict barriers to learning, and recommend adaptive instructional strategies tailored to individual needs.
