HPC resources are critical for processing large datasets, running complex simulations of intervention outcomes, and optimizing parameters for heterogeneous learner populations. The project will also employ agent-based modeling to simulate classroom dynamics, enabling the testing of intervention scalability under varying resource constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educators to generate evidence-based IEP recommendations, validated through partnerships with K-12 special education programs. By bridging computational analytics and special education praxis, this work aims to empower teachers with actionable insights, reduce disparities in educational access, and improve functional and academic outcomes for students with ID. The scalability of the proposed models will also inform policy discussions on equitable resource allocation in special education.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with intellectual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with intellectual disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising mentally handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Plant diseases caused by fungal pathogens pose significant threats to global food security, yet predicting their emergence and spread under shifting climatic conditions remains a critical challenge. Current models often fail to integrate the complex interplay of pathogen genomic plasticity, host phenotypic variability, and dynamic environmental stressors at regional scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, spatiotemporal simulation framework to predict the adaptive evolution of *Fusarium graminearum*, a devastating cereal pathogen, in response to climate-driven temperature and precipitation gradients. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will parameterize agent-based models with empirical genomic data from pathogen populations, multi-decadal climate projections, and heterogeneous crop landscape data across the U.S. Midwest. The computational pipeline will simulate fungal mutation rates, hybridization events, and selection pressures under projected warming scenarios, while coupling these outputs with epidemiological models of spore dispersal and host infection. Machine learning methods will identify genomic loci and environmental covariates most predictive of virulence escalation. By parallelizing stochastic simulations across thousands of HPC nodes, we will quantify probabilistic outcomes for pathogen adaptability and disease risk under mitigation strategies such as crop rotation adjustments or resistant cultivar deployment. The resulting framework will enable the prioritization of region-specific interventions to preempt pathogen evolution, reducing reliance on broad-spectrum fungicides. This work bridges gaps between evolutionary biology, agronomy, and climate science, offering a scalable computational tool to safeguard staple crops against emerging phytopathological threats in a warming world.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms from an agricultural perspective. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, correlated datasets with complex dependency structures, a common challenge in modern applications such as genomic studies, environmental monitoring, and network analysis. Traditional statistical tools often fail to account for spatial, temporal, or graph-based dependencies in large-scale data, leading to biased estimates or computationally intractable models. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid Bayesian and non-parametric framework that integrates Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling with stochastic variational inference. The approach will leverage hierarchical modeling to capture multi-level dependencies while maintaining interpretability. A critical bottleneck is the computational cost of evaluating high-dimensional posterior distributions and optimizing variational parameters across millions of data points. We request access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallelized MCMC chains, distributed memory architectures for variational optimization, and GPU-accelerated linear algebra operations for covariance matrix computations. The computational workflow will be implemented using R/Python interfaces to MPI and CUDA libraries, with benchmarking on synthetic and real-world datasets, including fMRI brain imaging data and spatially resolved climate records. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for dependency-aware Bayesian modeling, (2) theoretical guarantees on the convergence of hybrid inference algorithms under dependency constraints, and (3) applied insights into uncertainty quantification for climate extremes and neural connectivity patterns. This work will advance statistical methodology for dependent data while providing a computational blueprint for resource-efficient inference. The requested HPC allocation is essential to overcome memory and runtime barriers inherent to existing methods, ensuring scalability to petabyte-scale datasets in future applications.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze the heterogeneous impacts of infrastructure investment policies on long-term economic growth in low-income countries. A central challenge in development economics is disentangling the causal effects of multi-sector interventions—such as transportation networks, energy grids, and digital infrastructure—given complex spatial spillovers, nonlinear threshold effects, and interacting institutional factors. To address this, we implement a high-dimensional econometric model integrating 15 years of georeferenced World Bank infrastructure data, satellite-derived nighttime luminosity, and demographic surveys across 38 countries. The computational approach combines machine learning techniques for causal inference with spatial dynamic general equilibrium modeling, requiring iterative estimation of over 12,000 parameters across nested geographic scales. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: (1) parallel processing of 50km-resolution counterfactual scenarios through GPU-accelerated matrix operations, (2) Bayesian hierarchical modeling of institutional covariates using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods with adaptive sampling, and (3) validation against historical growth patterns via petabyte-scale geospatial raster algebra. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative taxonomy of infrastructure synergies that identifies context-specific sequencing rules to maximize GDP multipliers while minimizing regional inequality. The computational architecture will be designed for reproducibility across Global South contexts, with open-source code and training materials for development economists. By enabling granular analysis of trillion-parameter policy spaces within feasible runtime, this research directly supports SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) while advancing methodological integration of econometrics and high-performance computing in development studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the economic development process and its application to the problems of specific countries and regions. Includes instruction in economic development theory, industrialization, land reform, infrastructural development, investment policy, the role of governments and business in development, international development organizations, and the study of social, health, and environmental influences on economic development.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation for public sector entities facing climate-related fiscal risks. As governments increasingly confront budgetary pressures from extreme weather events, shifting regulatory landscapes, and transitional climate policies, traditional static budget models fail to capture the complex interdependencies between environmental volatility, infrastructure investments, and long-term fiscal health. The project will create a high-resolution simulation platform integrating stochastic climate projections, heterogeneous agent-based modeling of municipal stakeholders, and machine learning-driven vulnerability assessments. Using historical fiscal data from coastal municipalities and climate scenario outputs from IPCC reports, we will parameterize a multi-objective optimization model that balances short-term service delivery obligations against long-term resilience investments. The computational approach leverages parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate thousands of budget pathway permutations under variable carbon pricing regimes, disaster frequency distributions, and intergovernmental funding constraints. By implementing this framework on high-performance computing infrastructure, we aim to overcome current limitations in temporal granularity and system complexity that restrict conventional econometric tools. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of real-time sensitivity analysis for public finance officers, novel metrics for climate-adjusted municipal bond risk assessment, and policy recommendations for adaptive capital budgeting processes. This work bridges computational sustainability science with public financial management, addressing a critical gap in fiscal policy tools for climate-vulnerable jurisdictions while advancing methodological innovations in resource allocation modeling under deep uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the financial assets and budgets of public sector organizations. Includes instruction in public trusts and investments; the laws and procedures used to plan, prepare and administer public agency budgets; and the preparation and analysis of public budget projections and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance precision and efficiency in Computer Numerically Controlled (CNC) machining processes through advanced computational modeling and optimization. While CNC machining is a cornerstone of modern manufacturing, challenges persist in minimizing material waste, reducing cycle times, and optimizing toolpath trajectories—particularly for complex geometries and high-tolerance components. Traditional trial-and-error methods for parameter selection and toolpath design are resource-intensive and limit scalability. To address these limitations, this research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning, and generative design algorithms. Finite element analysis (FEA) models will simulate thermal-mechanical stresses during cutting operations, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will evaluate coolant flow and heat dissipation. These simulations will be coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively optimize machining parameters (e.g., spindle speed, feed rate, depth of cut) and toolpaths under dynamic operating conditions. A generative adversarial network (GAN) will further explore design-for-manufacturability solutions by proposing component geometries that balance functional requirements with machining feasibility. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high resolution of voxel-based material models, parallelized Monte Carlo sampling for uncertainty quantification, and real-time sensor data integration from CNC systems. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for predictive machining optimization, reduced computational overhead for CAM software, and data-driven guidelines for minimizing tool wear. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolpath optimization modules compatible with industry-standard CAD/CAM platforms, as well as workshops for CNC educators to integrate simulation-based training into curricula. By bridging computational engineering with applied machining workflows, this work aims to advance smart manufacturing capabilities while fostering workforce readiness in CNC technologies.
cip_title: Computer Numerically Controlled (CNC) Machinist Technology/ CNC Machinist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) machine tools, such as lathes, mills, precision measuring tools, and related attachments and accessories, to perform machining functions, such as cutting, drilling, shaping, and finishing products and component parts. Includes instruction in CNC terminology, setup, programming, operations, and troubleshooting; blueprint reading; machining; lathe and mill operations; technical mathematics; computer literacy; CAD/CAM systems; shop and safety practices; equipment capabilities; and regulations and laws.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance geography teacher education by integrating geospatial simulation and computational modeling into pedagogical training, addressing a critical gap in current methods that often lack tools to demonstrate dynamic, large-scale geographic processes. Traditional teacher preparation programs rely heavily on static maps, case studies, and qualitative analyses, limiting preservice teachers’ ability to engage students with real-time data, complex systems thinking, or interactive scenario-based learning. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a suite of high-resolution computational models simulating phenomena such as urbanization patterns, climate change impacts, and human-environment interactions. These models will be designed for use in teacher training modules, enabling educators to visualize multidimensional geographic processes, manipulate variables, and generate localized case studies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run agent-based models, spatial statistics analyses, and machine learning algorithms on large geospatial datasets (e.g., satellite imagery, census data, climate projections). Key computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale datasets for real-time visualization, parallelizing spatially explicit models across regions, and optimizing algorithms for interactive scenario testing. Outcomes will include open-access curricular materials with embedded computational tools, a repository of adaptable model templates, and evidence-based frameworks for integrating computational thinking into geography pedagogy. By equipping educators with skills to teach data-driven, systems-oriented geography, this work aims to improve K-12 students’ spatial reasoning and preparedness to address societal challenges. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the scale, speed, and complexity required for these simulations, which cannot feasibly run on standard institutional infrastructure. This project aligns with national priorities in STEM education reform while advancing the use of computational methods in teacher preparation programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach geography at various grade levels.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical and electronic systems necessitates advanced predictive maintenance strategies to optimize equipment reliability and reduce operational downtime. Current diagnostic approaches in electrical/electronics installation and repair often rely on reactive or rule-based maintenance, which struggles to address intermittent faults, cascading failures in interconnected systems, or degradation patterns influenced by dynamic environmental conditions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for predictive fault detection and lifespan estimation in industrial electrical systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on modeling multi-physics interactions within critical components such as power converters, motor windings, and circuit boards, integrating thermal, electrical, and mechanical degradation processes. Machine learning models will be trained on synthetic datasets generated through finite element analysis (FEA) simulations of stress scenarios, supplemented by field data from vibration, thermal imaging, and impedance spectroscopy measurements. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to account for component tolerances, variable load profiles, and environmental factors while maintaining computational feasibility. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for failure mode classification, a digital twin framework for real-time condition monitoring, and optimized maintenance scheduling algorithms validated against industrial case studies. The computational models will provide technicians with enhanced diagnostic decision-support tools while advancing curriculum development in predictive maintenance strategies for electrical systems. By bridging data-driven approaches with fundamental repair principles, this work aims to establish new best practices for resource-efficient equipment management in energy infrastructure, manufacturing, and telecommunications sectors.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, simple gearing, linkages and lubrication of machines and appliances, and the use of testing equipment.

abstract: The management of infectious diseases in non-domesticated animal populations presents significant challenges due to ecological complexity, host biodiversity, and limited access to longitudinal health data. Emerging pathogens in wildlife, such as avian influenza in migratory birds or mycobacterial infections in captive zoo species, threaten conservation efforts, animal welfare, and public health. Current predictive models often lack the resolution to account for species-specific physiological traits, behavioral interactions, and environmental stressors. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing high-resolution, multi-scale computational models to predict disease transmission dynamics and optimize therapeutic interventions for zoological species. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate genomic, ecological, and clinical datasets to simulate pathogen spread within heterogeneous animal populations. Agent-based modeling frameworks will be employed to represent individual host movement, contact networks, and immune responses across diverse habitats, from captive enclosures to migratory corridors. Machine learning algorithms will analyze historical outbreak data and electronic health records from zoological institutions to identify risk factors for disease susceptibility and treatment failure. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further model aerosolized pathogen transmission in mixed-species enclosures. The scale of these analyses—encompassing genomic sequences from 50+ species, GPS tracking data from 10,000+ individuals, and 3D enclosure geometries—necessitates parallelized processing and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide prophylactic measures, habitat design modifications, and species-specific dosing regimens for antimicrobials. This work will advance the evidence base for precision medicine in zoological health while providing a framework for One Health initiatives addressing zoonotic threats. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across ecological scenarios, sensitivity analyses of intervention strategies, and real-time model calibration using wildlife health monitoring data.
cip_definition: Research focused on the specialized treatment and care of zoo animals, performing animals, and animals living in the wild. May included related research in the principles and procedures used in the observation, diagnosis, care and treatment of illness, disease, injury, deformity, or other anomalies in non-domesticated animals.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a comparative analysis of stylistic and thematic patterns across non-Anglophone literary traditions, focusing on 19th- and 20th-century French, Japanese, and Arabic prose. The research addresses a critical gap in computational literary studies: existing methods for large-scale cross-linguistic comparison remain underdeveloped, particularly for non-European languages with distinct morphological and syntactic structures. By integrating multilingual natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques, the project aims to systematically map how narrative strategies (e.g., free indirect discourse, focalization) and themes of urbanization diverge or converge across these traditions. The computational workflow involves preprocessing digitized texts in their original scripts using transformer-based models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, followed by dimensionality reduction and clustering algorithms to identify latent stylistic and semantic patterns. Key challenges include aligning syntactic features across typologically diverse languages and mitigating translation bias in multilingual embeddings. HPC resources are essential to train and validate custom models on the project’s corpus of 2,000+ novels and short stories, enabling parallelized feature extraction and large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) a reproducible pipeline for cross-linguistic literary analysis, (2) quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric periodizations of literary modernity, and (3) open-access datasets annotated for narrative devices in Arabic and Japanese. This work will provide new methodological frameworks for computational comparative literature while deepening interdisciplinary dialogue between area studies and NLP. By prioritizing underrepresented literatures, the project contributes to diversifying the scope of digital humanities research and supports curricular development in global literary history.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on two or more literary traditions in the original languages or in translation. Includes instruction in comparative linguistics; applicable foreign languages; English/French language and literature; literary criticism; and applications to genre, period, national, and textual studies as well as literary forms such as poetry, prose, and drama.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between urban soundscapes and public health outcomes, integrating acoustic ecology, epidemiological modeling, and machine learning. Urban noise pollution is a growing yet understudied determinant of health disparities, with complex interactions between environmental, social, and physiological factors. Current studies are limited by sparse, low-resolution noise data and simplistic analytical frameworks that fail to capture nonlinear relationships or spatial-temporal heterogeneity. To address this, we propose a novel computational pipeline combining large-scale acoustic sensor datasets (10+ TB), anonymized electronic health records, and geospatial demographic data. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and transformer-based architectures, will be trained to identify latent patterns linking noise exposure profiles (e.g., spectral characteristics, temporal variability) to cardiovascular and mental health outcomes. A parallelized agent-based modeling framework will simulate population-level health impacts under diverse urban planning scenarios. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the high dimensionality of audio spectrograms, the iterative nature of sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces, and the real-time processing requirements for streaming sensor data. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible noise-health risk atlas with hyperlocal risk stratification, (2) predictive tools for evaluating noise mitigation policies, and (3) novel methodology for fusing time-series environmental data with heterogeneous health datasets. This work bridges gaps between environmental science, public health, and urban analytics, offering a scalable framework for studying multisensory environmental stressors. Results will directly inform noise regulation guidelines and equitable infrastructure design, while the computational architecture will be adaptable to other interdisciplinary studies of environmental exposure dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to generate insights from data and identify and predict trends. Includes instruction in computer databases, computer programming, inference, machine learning, optimization, probability and stochastic models, statistics, strategy, uncertainty quantification, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the socio-political networks of early modern Europe (1500–1800) through large-scale textual and relational data. The research problem centers on understanding how intellectual and institutional networks—such as those between universities, religious organizations, and emerging scientific societies—shaped cultural and political transformations across the continent. Existing historiography relies heavily on localized case studies, limiting systematic comparisons of transnational connectivity and its impact on phenomena like the Enlightenment or state centralization. To address this gap, the project will computationally integrate fragmented archival sources—including correspondence records, institutional membership lists, and published polemics—into a unified relational database. Natural language processing (NLP) methods will be applied to extract entities, affiliations, and semantic themes from multilingual texts (Latin, French, German, Italian), while graph-based algorithms will model network dynamics over time. HPC resources are critical for processing ~50,000 digitized documents (estimated 10 TB of text and metadata) and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about information flow and institutional influence. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database of early modern European networks; (2) visualizations of regional and temporal variations in connectivity; and (3) statistical models identifying key hubs and brokers in knowledge dissemination. This computational approach will enable a quantitatively grounded re-evaluation of how decentralized networks facilitated or resisted centralized authority, offering new insights into Europe’s transition to modernity. The project aligns with digital humanities priorities by bridging traditional historiographic methods with scalable computational tools, while its findings will inform broader debates about the interplay between intellectual exchange and political change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of European society, culture, and institutions from the origins to the present. Includes instruction in European historiography, European history sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of African diasporic cultural narratives across North America and the Caribbean from the 19th century to the present. The research problem centers on identifying and analyzing understudied patterns in Black cultural production—including literature, periodicals, oral histories, and visual art—to trace how transnational Black communities have articulated resistance, identity, and solidarity. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these multimodal datasets, which include digitized archives, OCR-processed texts, and audiovisual materials totaling over 20 terabytes. To address this, the project employs computational text analysis, machine learning (ML), and network modeling. Custom NLP pipelines will be developed to detect thematic shifts in Black-authored newspapers (e.g., *The North Star*, *The Negro World*) and Caribbean literary journals, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will classify visual motifs in protest art and photography. Graph-based models will map intellectual and artistic collaborations across geographic boundaries. These workflows require parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated training to handle sparse, multilingual data and mitigate biases inherent in historical OCR outputs. Expected outcomes include a public-facing digital archive of annotated materials, interactive visualizations of cultural networks, and ML models fine-tuned for African diasporic studies. By computationally uncovering latent connections—such as the circulation of Pan-Africanist thought between Harlem and Port-au-Prince—this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of how Black cultural praxis has shaped collective memory and political action. The project aligns with institutional goals to expand interdisciplinary research in Black Studies while providing scalable methodologies for analyzing marginalized narratives in the digital humanities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: Cerebrovascular diseases, including ischemic stroke and intracranial hemorrhage, are leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in clinical management, significant challenges remain in predicting individual patient outcomes, optimizing acute interventions, and tailoring secondary prevention strategies. These limitations stem from the multifactorial nature of vascular neurology pathologies, which involve dynamic interactions between genetic predispositions, hemodynamic parameters, neuroimaging biomarkers, and clinical variables. Traditional analytical approaches often fail to capture these high-dimensional, non-linear relationships. This project proposes to address these gaps through the development of advanced computational models enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate multi-modal data from institutional stroke registries, neuroimaging repositories (MRI/CT perfusion, vessel wall imaging), and genomic databases to construct predictive frameworks for stroke recurrence, hemorrhagic transformation risk, and long-term functional recovery. Machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be implemented to analyze complex datasets encompassing over 10,000 patient records and 50,000 imaging studies. Concurrently, finite element modeling powered by HPC clusters will simulate cerebral blood flow dynamics in patient-specific vascular geometries to investigate hemodynamic contributors to aneurysm formation and clot lysis patterns. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing capabilities for both large-scale data analytics (via Spark-based pipelines) and intensive fluid dynamics simulations (using FEniCS-based solvers). Expected outcomes include: (1) validated predictive algorithms for clinical deployment in stroke units, (2) mechanistic insights into flow-disease relationships through in silico experimentation, and (3) open-source computational tools for vascular neurology research. By leveraging HPC resources, this project aims to transform big data into actionable clinical knowledge, ultimately improving personalized care for patients with cerebrovascular diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation, prevention, treatment, and recovery from vascular diseases of the nervous system resulting from a large number of causes, such as ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, spinal cord ischemia, and spinal cord hemorrhage.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and safety of industrial and commercial piping systems through high-fidelity computational modeling of fluid dynamics, thermal stress, and material performance under extreme conditions. Current pipefitting and sprinkler system design practices rely on standardized codes and empirical data, which may not fully account for complex, dynamic interactions in modern high-pressure, high-temperature, or mixed-use environments. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multiphase flow behavior, transient thermal gradients, and structural fatigue in piping networks, with a focus on optimizing system reliability and compliance with evolving safety standards. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will be developed to analyze turbulent flow in sprinkler systems during emergency activation, including droplet dispersion patterns and coverage efficiency under varying building geometries. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) will assess stress distribution in pipe joints and supports during thermal expansion-contraction cycles, incorporating material datasets for common alloys and composite materials. Machine learning techniques will be applied to iteratively refine simulation parameters using historical failure data from industrial case studies. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of 3D meshing requirements (10⁶–10⁸ elements), coupled multiphysics simulations, and Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification across diverse operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive models for identifying high-risk configurations in existing systems, data-driven design guidelines for corrosion-resistant layouts, and a publicly accessible database of simulated failure thresholds to support training programs. By integrating computational engineering with pipefitting practice, this research aims to reduce installation retrofit costs by 15–20% in typical industrial settings while enhancing fire suppression system efficacy—a critical advancement for infrastructure resilience in energy, manufacturing, and urban development sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, install, and test industrial and commercial piping systems and automatic fire and exposure protection systems. Includes instruction in water systems, steam systems, heating and cooling systems, lubricating systems, piping materials, installation tools operation and maintenance, valve installation and repair, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Pediatric patients exhibit significant variability in treatment responses and health trajectories due to developmental, genetic, and environmental factors. Existing clinical decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to integrate dynamic, multidimensional data—such as longitudinal growth metrics, pharmacogenomic profiles, and socioenvironmental determinants—to optimize personalized care. This project proposes the development of a computational modeling platform to predict patient-specific responses to common pediatric interventions, enabling nurses to tailor care plans and health education strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets from diverse pediatric populations, encompassing over 500,000 patient encounters, paired with genomic and demographic metadata. Agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques will be employed to simulate physiological responses to medications, nutritional interventions, and chronic disease management protocols across developmental stages. Computational workflows will prioritize identifying critical thresholds in drug efficacy, adverse event risks, and health behavior adoption rates. By parallelizing these simulations across HPC nodes, the project aims to overcome limitations in traditional statistical approaches, which struggle to model nonlinear interactions between time-varying biological and social variables. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide nurse-led dose adjustments, family education priorities, and early intervention strategies for at-risk populations. The platform will be validated against prospective clinical data from three pediatric primary care networks. This work aligns with nursing priorities to reduce trial-and-error care, mitigate health disparities, and improve longitudinal outcomes for children with complex chronic conditions. The computational infrastructure developed will also serve as a scalable resource for future studies on precision health interventions in pediatric nursing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care for children from infancy through adolescence. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting physicians, patient examination and referral, and planning and delivering health maintenance and health education programs.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of ethical reasoning in health professions education through large-scale computational analysis of qualitative textual data. Current research in health ethics education is constrained by the labor-intensive nature of manual content analysis, limiting the scope and scalability of studies. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze diverse datasets—including historical ethics case studies, digital forum discussions among medical trainees, and longitudinal curriculum materials—using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML). The computational approach will involve training transformer-based models to identify and classify ethical themes, sentiment trajectories, and pedagogical patterns across multilingual and temporally stratified texts. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of unstructured data, optimizing deep learning architectures, and conducting hyperparameter tuning at scale. Additionally, network analysis will map the interconnectedness of ethical concepts within educational materials to evaluate curricular coherence. Expected outcomes include identifying gaps in contemporary ethics training, revealing shifts in prioritization of ethical principles over time, and generating evidence-based recommendations for integrating humanities-driven content into competency frameworks. By enabling rapid, reproducible analysis of complex narratives, this project aims to advance methodological innovation in health professions education research while fostering ethically nuanced pedagogical strategies. The findings will be disseminated through open-access platforms to support global health education initiatives, emphasizing equity in resource-limited settings. This work underscores the transformative potential of computational methods in bridging humanities scholarship and health professions training.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of data-driven frameworks for optimizing animal training protocols across diverse species and functional contexts. Traditional animal training methodologies often rely on trial-and-error approaches informed by generalized behavioral principles, which may inadequately account for individual variability in learning styles, species-specific cognition, or dynamic environmental factors. To address this gap, the research will employ computational modeling and machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze multimodal datasets—including behavioral logs, biometric signals (e.g., heart rate, motion tracking), and environmental sensors—collected from training sessions for service dogs, marine mammals in rehabilitation, and avian species used in search-and-rescue operations. Agent-based models will simulate trainer-animal interactions under varying constraints, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively identify optimal reward schedules and task segmentation strategies. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to accommodate high-dimensional data, parallelize scenario testing, and train deep neural networks capable of predicting training outcomes based on historical datasets. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access predictive tools to guide trainers in tailoring protocols to individual animals, reducing training time and stress, and improving task retention rates. The project also aims to establish a computational foundation for ethical frameworks in animal training by quantifying stress indicators and optimizing for welfare-centric metrics. By integrating behavioral science with computational analytics, this work bridges a critical gap in non-engineering domains, offering scalable solutions for emerging applications in assistive animal training, wildlife conservation, and interspecies collaboration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach and exercise animals for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes. Includes instruction in animal psychology, health, and safety; human-animal interaction; learning and behavior styles associated with different breeds and species; and the technical and pedagogical aspects of training animals for such specific functions as obedient household pets, performing show animals, animal athletes, caregiving (e.g., seeing-eye dogs), search and rescue, and police/security work.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time document processing and collaborative editing workflows by developing adaptive algorithms optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. While modern word processors handle basic tasks effectively, challenges persist in scaling operations for large documents (e.g., technical manuals, legal contracts) and supporting latency-sensitive collaborative environments with hundreds of concurrent users. Current implementations often struggle with version conflict resolution, dynamic formatting consistency checks, and predictive text rendering—particularly when processing multilingual content or complex layouts. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) transformers with graph-based document representation models. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated parallelism to train domain-specific language models on a corpus of 50,000+ technical documents, while implementing distributed memory protocols to simulate multi-user editing scenarios at scale. Key innovations include a dynamic dependency graph architecture to track document element relationships and a reinforcement learning system to optimize keyboard-to-render latency in variable network conditions. The HPC resources will enable large-scale ablation studies comparing neural and rule-based formatting engines, as well as Monte Carlo simulations of user interaction patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source algorithms for real-time collaborative editing with sub-100ms synchronization latency at 1,000-user concurrency levels, (2) quantitative benchmarks for formatting accuracy across 15+ document types, and (3) a novel evaluation framework measuring human-proxy efficiency gains in transcription tasks. By establishing computational baselines for next-generation word processing systems, this work will directly inform the development of accessible, high-performance authoring tools for technical fields while advancing HPC applications in human-computer text interaction research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in the planning, execution, and quality assurance of modern construction finishing processes. While advancements in materials and prefabrication have accelerated building timelines, critical gaps persist in optimizing finishing workflows, predicting defect risks, and validating compliance with evolving safety and sustainability standards. Current computational tools for these tasks are limited by their reliance on simplified models or small datasets, which fail to capture the dynamic interactions between material properties, environmental conditions, and labor productivity. To overcome these limitations, this project will develop and deploy a multi-scale simulation framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for material behavior, agent-based modeling for workforce dynamics, and machine learning for real-time defect detection in inspection imagery. The FEA modules will simulate stress distribution and curing dynamics in finishing materials (e.g., coatings, sealants) under variable humidity and temperature conditions, while agent-based models will optimize task sequencing and resource allocation across diverse construction teams. Concurrently, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on high-resolution LiDAR and thermal imaging data will automate the identification of subsurface defects and non-compliant installations. These computationally intensive workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, necessitating HPC infrastructure for iterative model calibration and large-batch simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce rework rates by 15–25%, data-driven protocols for adaptive workforce scheduling, and open-source benchmarks for automated inspection accuracy. By enabling granular, physics-informed decision-making, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for precision in construction management, directly contributing to waste reduction and lifecycle resilience in built environments. The proposed computational framework will also serve as a scalable template for integrating HPC into broader construction informatics curricula.
cip_title: Building/ Construction Finishing, Management, and Inspection, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in building/construction finishing, management, and inspection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a critical role in modulating host immunity and susceptibility to pathogenic infections, yet the mechanisms underlying microbial community resilience during pathogen invasion remain poorly understood. This project seeks to investigate how native gut microbiota resist colonization by opportunistic pathogens such as *Clostridioides difficile* through interspecies competition and metabolic cross-talk. We propose to develop a high-resolution computational model integrating microbial growth dynamics, resource utilization patterns, and host epithelial cell signaling to simulate gut microenvironment conditions during infection. The model will leverage existing metagenomic and metabolomic datasets from clinical studies to parameterize species-specific metabolic networks and simulate community-level responses to perturbations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of microbial interactions, which involves thousands of differential equations representing metabolite fluxes, quorum sensing, and host immune factor secretion. Simulations will map how resource competition for amino acids, short-chain fatty acids, and bile acids shapes pathogen exclusion or proliferation. Sensitivity analyses will identify keystone species and metabolic pathways critical for community stability. This work will generate testable hypotheses about intervention strategies to enhance microbiota-mediated colonization resistance, with potential applications in probiotic design and personalized antimicrobial therapies. The computational framework will also advance methodologies for studying host-microbe ecosystems by bridging gap between reductionist in vitro models and population-scale omics data. By elucidating principles of microbiome resilience, this research directly aligns with microbiology’s foundational goals of understanding microbial behavior in complex environments and its implications for human health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of unicellular organisms and colonies, and subcellular genetic matter and their ecological interactions with human beings and other life. Includes instruction in microbial genetics, cell biology, cell physiology, virology, pathogenic microbiology, environmental microbiology, immunology, biostatistics, bioinformatics, and laboratory methods including microscopy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dynamic resource allocation in decentralized economic systems, integrating advances in algorithmic game theory, econometrics, and high-performance computing. The research addresses the challenge of modeling large-scale, adaptive markets where heterogeneous agents with bounded rationality interact under evolving constraints, such as energy markets with real-time renewable generation shifts or decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms. Existing equilibrium-based models often fail to capture the temporal and spatial complexity of such systems, particularly when accounting for strategic behavior, network effects, and incomplete information. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid agent-based modeling approach combining evolutionary optimization, reinforcement learning for adaptive agent strategies, and econometric validation against historical market data. The computational architecture will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across multiple market scenarios, implemented using MPI for distributed memory systems, with graph neural networks to model inter-agent influence patterns. Key innovations include a novel mechanism for endogenous preference formation using attention-based architectures and a scalable auction protocol optimizer tested through evolutionary algorithms. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of interacting agents across extended time horizons, with anticipated workloads exceeding 50,000 core-hours for parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available toolkit for simulating decentralized resource allocation systems, 2) empirical insights into the computational tractability of incentive-compatible mechanisms in large networks, and 3) policy-relevant findings on market design under high volatility. Results will advance both economic theory by quantifying previously intractable forms of strategic interdependence and computer science through developments in scalable mechanism design, with applications to sustainable infrastructure planning and digital market regulation.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the theoretical and practical connections between computer science and economics. Includes instruction in data analysis, database design, data mining, computer algorithms, economics, econometrics, computer programing, mathematics, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to optimize material selection, installation workflows, and long-term performance forecasting for carpet, floor, and tile systems. Despite advances in materials science, the industry lacks predictive models to evaluate how composite flooring systems—particularly those combining textiles, adhesives, and rigid substrates—respond to dynamic mechanical stresses, environmental humidity, or temperature fluctuations. Current empirical approaches for testing installation techniques and material compatibility are time-intensive, costly, and limited in generalizability. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning. FEA will model macroscale stresses on flooring assemblies under simulated loads (e.g., foot traffic, furniture), while molecular dynamics will characterize microscale interactions between adhesives, moisture barriers, and substrate materials. A neural network trained on experimental data from industry partners will predict optimal cutting patterns to minimize material waste during installation. The HPC environment is critical for managing multi-scale simulations across parameter spaces (e.g., material thickness, weave density, adhesive curing times) and iterating machine learning models. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational pipeline to quantify trade-offs between material durability, installation efficiency, and cost; (2) open-access datasets correlating simulation results with real-world wear testing; and (3) a decision-support tool for contractors to visualize how design choices impact project timelines and lifecycle performance. By reducing trial-and-error in physical prototyping, this work aims to lower material waste by an estimated 15–20% in complex installations while improving safety outcomes through data-driven recommendations for load-bearing limits and substrate preparation protocols.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, prepare, install, and repair carpet; linoleum; vinyl; ceramic, marble, quarry, mosaic, and terrazzo tiles; and wood materials on floors, walls, and stairs. Includes instruction in measuring, cutting, and installing materials; use of hand and power-operated equipment; estimation of material and labor costs; and safety training.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive biomechanical models for optimizing rehabilitation protocols in post-surgical orthopedic recovery, a niche intersecting clinical rehabilitation, computational biomechanics, and machine learning. Physical therapy technicians play a critical role in implementing personalized therapeutic interventions, yet current protocols often rely on generalized guidelines that inadequately account for individual variations in tissue healing rates, biomechanical stressors, or patient adherence. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific data—including gait analysis, electromyography (EMG), and medical imaging—into dynamic simulations of musculoskeletal adaptation during recovery. The research problem centers on modeling the nonlinear interactions between therapeutic exercise dosages, tissue remodeling, and functional outcomes to identify protocols that minimize re-injury risk while accelerating recovery timelines. Computational methods will involve finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating stress distribution in healing bone and soft tissue, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively optimize exercise parameters in silico. Deep neural networks will be trained on retrospective clinical datasets to predict patient-specific adherence patterns and biomechanical responses. The scale of data processing (high-resolution 3D movement capture, real-time sensor inputs from wearable devices) and the complexity of multi-physics simulations necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized model training and large-scale parameter sweeps. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolbox for generating patient-adaptive rehabilitation plans, validated against prospective clinical data from collaborating physical therapy clinics. This work aims to empower physical therapy technicians with evidence-based, computationally derived insights to enhance decision-making in routine care, bridging a critical gap between theoretical biomechanics and practical rehabilitation workflows. By focusing on computational personalization within a technician-aided care model, the project occupies an emerging niche in health sciences, distinct from traditional clinical or public health paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of physical therapists, and to perform routine functions in support of physical therapy and rehabilitation. Includes instruction in applied kinesiology, basic function of the human body, communication skills, principles and procedures of physical therapy, physical therapy modalities, and professional ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the psychological dynamics underlying human interactions with autonomous algorithmic systems in decentralized digital environments, focusing on decision-making patterns and trust formation in the absence of centralized authority. While traditional psychological frameworks have examined human-technology interactions in structured settings, the emergence of decentralized platforms (e.g., blockchain-based systems, distributed AI networks) introduces novel cognitive and behavioral challenges. The research problem centers on identifying how individuals develop heuristic strategies when navigating systems where agency is distributed across opaque, non-human actors, and how these strategies relate to pre-existing cognitive biases. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with psychometric network analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating large-scale, stochastic ABMs that capture heterogeneous agent behaviors across parameterized trust thresholds and system transparency levels. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines will analyze multimodal behavioral data (eye tracking, response latencies, and interaction logs) from controlled human experiments, mapping decision pathways onto network models of cognitive bias activation. The integration of simulated and empirical datasets will enable validation of emergent patterns through iterative model tuning. Expected outcomes include 1) a computational taxonomy of trust heuristics specific to decentralized systems, 2) identification of bias mitigation points in algorithmic interface design, and 3) open-source tools for dynamic psychometric network visualization. This work bridges gaps between computational psychology, behavioral economics, and distributed systems engineering, offering foundational insights for ethical AI deployment in increasingly decentralized digital ecosystems. The requested resources will support parallelized simulations across 10^6 parameter combinations and real-time analysis of 15TB of experimental data, scales unattainable with standard computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural properties and classification of high-dimensional algebraic systems, particularly focusing on non-associative algebras and their cohomological invariants. The central challenge lies in the exponential growth of computational complexity associated with analyzing these systems as their dimensions increase, rendering traditional computational methods infeasible. To address this, the research will implement parallelized algorithms optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments, leveraging distributed-memory architectures to decompose large algebraic structures into tractable subproblems. Key methodologies include the development of scalable algorithms for computing cohomology groups, automorphism groups, and derivation spaces, utilizing symbolic computation frameworks such as Singular and GAP. The project will also employ hybrid MPI-OpenMP paradigms to efficiently manage memory and computational workloads across nodes. Expected outcomes include the classification of previously unresolved algebraic structures in dimensions ≥8, the generation of comprehensive databases for use by the mathematical community, and new theoretical insights into the interplay between algebraic properties and topological invariants. The requested computing resources are critical for executing memory-intensive calculations and enabling large-scale distributed computations that are foundational to advancing pure algebraic research. By bridging theoretical conjectures with computational verification, this work aims to resolve long-standing questions in ring theory and Lie algebra representation while establishing scalable computational frameworks for future algebraic inquiries.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on algebraic structures and linear algebra.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the arithmetic properties and solution structures of a family of Diophantine equations arising from algebraic number theory. The research focuses on determining the existence and density of integer solutions under varying parameterizations, a problem that remains unresolved despite its fundamental implications for understanding rational points on higher-dimensional algebraic varieties. Traditional analytical methods have proven insufficient due to the exponential growth in computational complexity as parameters scale, necessitating advanced high-performance computing techniques. The core computational approach involves the development and implementation of parallelized algorithms designed to systematically explore the solution space across distributed computing architectures. These algorithms will integrate optimized lattice basis reduction routines and real-time validation checks to efficiently prune infeasible regions and isolate potential solution candidates. By leveraging large-scale parallelism, the project aims to process parametric regimes previously inaccessible to classical methods, enabling the statistical analysis of solution distributions over orders of magnitude in parameter values. Anticipated outcomes include the classification of solvability criteria for targeted equation classes, the identification of asymptotic patterns governing solution densities, and the formulation of conjectures linking these patterns to deeper invariants in arithmetic geometry. The results are expected to provide foundational insights into the interplay between algorithmic computation and theoretical discovery in pure mathematics, while the developed computational frameworks will offer reusable tools for future investigations in Diophantine analysis and related areas.
cip_definition: Any program in mathematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the impact of leadership decision-making frameworks on organizational adaptability in dynamic environments. While leadership strategies are well-studied in static contexts, there is a critical gap in understanding how computational models can simulate and predict the efficacy of different leadership approaches during periods of rapid change, such as market disruptions or internal crises. The study will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate organizational behavior under varying leadership styles, including hierarchical, distributed, and hybrid decision-making structures. These models will incorporate variables such as communication latency, resource allocation efficiency, and team cohesion dynamics, calibrated using empirical data from case studies of technology firms and non-profit organizations. HPC resources are essential to run large-scale, parallel simulations that capture the nonlinear interactions between leadership decisions, environmental stressors, and workforce responses. Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to identify patterns in successful adaptive strategies. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to guide leaders in selecting optimal decision-making structures under uncertainty, as well as actionable insights into mitigating bottlenecks in organizational resilience. This work bridges computational social science and leadership theory, offering a novel methodology for evaluating leadership efficacy in complex systems. By quantifying the relationship between leadership practices and adaptive outcomes, the project aims to advance evidence-based strategies for organizational sustainability, directly contributing to the Business Administration and Management field’s understanding of computational leadership analytics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leadership skills that can be applied to a business, government, non-profit, or educational setting. Includes instruction in organizational planning, dynamics of leadership, finance, team building, conflict resolution and mediation, communication and other management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational models that analyze the dynamic interplay between psychosocial, physiological, and motor factors influencing athletic performance. Current approaches to optimizing sport behavior often rely on isolated assessments of variables such as stress, motivation, or biomechanical efficiency, limiting the ability to predict holistic performance outcomes under real-world conditions. The proposed research addresses this gap by integrating multi-modal datasets—including biometric sensor data (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels), motion-capture kinematics, and self-reported psychological assessments—into a unified computational framework. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques, we will simulate how individual differences in personality traits, team cohesion dynamics, and neurocognitive responses to pressure collectively shape performance outcomes in competitive environments. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to account for high-dimensional interactions across thousands of athlete profiles and situational contexts, enabling the identification of non-linear relationships and thresholds that dictate performance success or decline. Expected outcomes include predictive models to personalize mental skills training (e.g., attention regulation, resilience strategies) and evidence-based frameworks for coaches to optimize team communication and leadership structures. By bridging motor behavior analysis with psychosocial dynamics, this work will contribute novel tools for ethical performance enhancement in applied sport psychology, with potential applications in youth athlete development, injury recovery protocols, and elite performance optimization. The computational pipelines developed will also be shared as open-source resources to support interdisciplinary research at the intersection of counseling psychology, neuroscience, and sport science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the motor, physiological, and psychosocial aspects of sport behavior. Includes instruction in applied sport psychology, clinical mental health counseling, coaching, exercise physiology, ethical performance enhancement; human development, leadership and team building, mind-body practices, neuroscience, and personality and health.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the sociocultural dynamics influencing the success of church planting initiatives in urbanizing regions, using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between demographic shifts, community networks, and theological outreach strategies. While church planting is traditionally guided by qualitative missiological principles, this study addresses a critical gap in applying data-driven approaches to optimize location selection, resource allocation, and contextual adaptation strategies for new congregations. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of current heuristic methods in rapidly changing urban environments, where overlapping cultural, economic, and spatial variables challenge traditional planning models. Leveraging HPC resources, the project will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with geospatial analytics and natural language processing (NLP) to simulate population-level responses to different church planting methodologies. Data sources include anonymized census records, social media sentiment analysis, historical church growth datasets, and ethnographic interviews processed through transformer-based language models. Computational workflows will test hypotheses about network effects in community formation, threshold dynamics in congregational scalability, and the role of digital platforms in hybrid (physical/digital) church planting efforts. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for evaluating site-specific viability, a taxonomy of contextual challenges correlated with demographic variables, and generative models for culturally adaptive evangelism frameworks. By bridging computational social science with missiological studies, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based religious community development while contributing methodological innovations in simulating belief-driven collective behavior—an understudied area in digital humanities. The project’s scalability (enabled by HPC) will permit comparative analysis across 15 global cities, offering transferable insights for interfaith organizational strategies in pluralistic societies.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to establish congregations of Christians in new locations. Includes instruction in models of church planting, church multiplication strategies, church leadership, evangelism, missiology, Christian ethics, and mission-oriented theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in the allocation of specialized educational resources for students with disabilities. Despite federal mandates for equitable access, school districts face persistent challenges in optimizing resource distribution, staff training, and compliance monitoring across diverse student needs. Current administrative decision-making often relies on fragmented datasets, static policy models, and manual processes, limiting the ability to predict resource gaps or adapt to dynamic student populations. To overcome these barriers, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate resource allocation scenarios under varying constraints. Large-scale longitudinal datasets—including Individualized Education Program (IEP) records, staffing patterns, and budget trajectories from 50 school districts—will be analyzed using ensemble ML algorithms to identify predictors of service delays or compliance risks. Concurrently, ABM will simulate interactions between administrators, educators, and families to evaluate how policy adjustments (e.g., staffing ratios, funding reallocations) impact service equity. HPC resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets, training high-parameter models, and running thousands of stochastic simulations to quantify uncertainty. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that enables administrators to forecast resource needs, prioritize interventions, and model the downstream effects of budgetary or regulatory changes. This work will advance the field of special education administration by providing empirically grounded, scalable methods to align resource deployment with the heterogeneous needs of students with disabilities while adhering to legal and ethical standards. By integrating computational social science with educational leadership, the project aims to transform static compliance frameworks into adaptive systems that proactively address inequities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage programs for exceptional students and their parents. Includes instruction in special education theory and practice, special education program development, evaluation and assessment in special education, state and federal law and regulations, managing individual education plans, problems of low- and high- disability students, mainstreaming, special education curricula, staff management, parent education, communications and community relations, budgeting, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance science teacher education by developing scalable computational models to simulate classroom interactions and student learning processes in general science contexts. A critical challenge in preparing science educators is the limited access to dynamic, data-driven tools that reflect the complexity of real-world classrooms, particularly when addressing interdisciplinary science concepts. Traditional training methods often rely on static scenarios or anecdotal experiences, which may not adequately prepare teachers for the diverse, evolving challenges of STEM education. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate student cohorts with varied cognitive profiles, prior knowledge, and engagement levels. These models will integrate empirical data from classroom observations, student assessments, and science education research to parameterize interactions between teacher strategies, curricular content, and learner behaviors. The computational framework will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to explore thousands of pedagogical scenarios, assessing how different instructional approaches affect conceptual understanding across physical and biological science domains. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in simulated learning outcomes, enabling the generation of adaptive teaching recommendations. The resulting platform will serve as both a research tool for studying science education dynamics and a training resource for pre-service teachers. Expected outcomes include novel insights into the relationship between instructional design, student diversity, and science learning efficacy, as well as the creation of open-access simulation modules for teacher education programs. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge the gap between educational theory and classroom practice, ultimately strengthening the preparation of science educators to address complex, real-world teaching challenges.
cip_title: Science Teacher Education/ General Science Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general science programs, or a combination of the biological and physical science subject matter areas, at various educational levels.

abstract: The development of safe and effective investigational drugs requires robust computational frameworks to model complex biological interactions, predict clinical outcomes, and optimize therapeutic strategies. Current limitations in clinical trial design and drug evaluation—such as high costs, ethical constraints, and heterogeneous patient responses—underscore the need for advanced computational approaches to accelerate translational research. This project proposes a multi-scale computational platform to simulate drug-target interactions, predict patient-specific therapeutic responses, and identify biomarkers for personalized treatment regimens in oncology and autoimmune diseases. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, and population-scale genomic analyses. MD simulations will characterize binding affinities and resistance mechanisms of investigational small-molecule inhibitors, while ensemble ML models will predict adverse drug reactions and efficacy using multi-omics datasets from public repositories and institutional clinical trials. Agent-based models will simulate immune-drug interactions in virtual patient cohorts, incorporating real-world variability in immune cell populations and genetic backgrounds. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handle large-scale parallelization of MD trajectories (>10,000 GPU hours), training of deep neural networks on terabyte-scale genomic data, and iterative optimization of virtual trial parameters. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate drugs with reduced off-target effects, predictive biomarkers for patient stratification, and adaptive clinical trial designs tailored to genetic subpopulations. This resource will enable rapid in silico prioritization of drug candidates, reducing reliance on costly preclinical experimentation and enhancing the success rate of early-phase trials. By bridging computational innovation with clinical validation, the project aims to establish a scalable framework for precision drug development, directly addressing unmet needs in therapeutic areas with high morbidity and complex pathophysiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on Investigational Drugs and Research

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems, a rapidly growing but understudied domain within Banking, Corporate, Finance, and Securities Law. The proliferation of blockchain-based financial instruments, smart contracts, and autonomous governance protocols has created novel challenges for traditional regulatory paradigms, particularly in areas such as liability attribution, jurisdictional conflicts, and compliance automation.
