The requested resources will facilitate benchmarking against industry-standard software while addressing critical gaps in computational capacity for next-generation surveying applications, including autonomous surveying systems and smart city digital twin development.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the determination of the location, elevations, and alignment of natural and manmade topographic features. Includes instruction in property line location, surveying, surface measurement, aerial and terrestrial photogrammetry, remote sensing, satellite imagery, global positioning systems, computer applications, and photographic data processing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic office management processes, with a focus on resource allocation, workforce scheduling, and operational efficiency in complex organizational environments. Current methodologies for office supervision often rely on static models that fail to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating task priorities, employee skill heterogeneity, and unexpected disruptions. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent simulation model integrated with machine learning algorithms to analyze office workflows, predict bottlenecks, and recommend adaptive management strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale office environments with granular agent interactions, incorporating datasets spanning employee performance metrics, task completion times, and space utilization patterns. Monte Carlo methods will be employed to assess uncertainty in operational outcomes, while reinforcement learning will train decision-making models under diverse scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable tool for evaluating "what-if" management strategies, evidence-based recommendations for balancing productivity and employee well-being, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated office management scenarios. The computational intensity of modeling hundreds of concurrent agents across extended time horizons necessitates parallelized simulations and GPU-accelerated machine learning workflows, which exceed the capabilities of standard institutional computing infrastructure. By bridging operations research and computational social science, this work aims to advance data-driven approaches in office management education and practice. Results will directly inform curriculum development in workforce optimization and provide a foundation for future research on AI-assisted supervisory systems in business administration contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and manage the operations and personnel of business offices and management-level divisions. Includes instruction in employee supervision, management, and labor relations; budgeting; scheduling and coordination; office systems operation and maintenance; office records management, organization, and security; office facilities design and space management; preparation and evaluation of business management data; and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic research on the historical evolution and dialectal variation of Arabic. A core challenge in Arabic language studies lies in systematically analyzing vast, heterogeneous text corpora spanning Classical Arabic (CA), Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), and regional dialects, which exhibit significant phonological, morphological, and syntactic differences. Traditional manual methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these datasets, limiting insights into language change, dialect classification, and sociolinguistic patterns. This research proposes a computational pipeline combining natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to model linguistic features across time, register, and geography. Key objectives include (1) training transformer-based models on curated corpora of CA and MSA texts to detect diachronic shifts in grammatical structures; (2) developing dialect identification algorithms using parallel speech and text data from under-resourced regional varieties; and (3) creating visualization tools to map linguistic variation across the Arab world. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets, fine-tuning large language models, and running computationally intensive tasks like phylogenetic analysis of dialect relationships. Expected outcomes include open-access computational models for Arabic dialectology, an annotated multilingual corpus linking historical and contemporary texts, and novel methodologies for digital philology. This work will enable quantitative validation of hypotheses about language contact and change while providing resources to support applied domains like machine translation, language education, and computational social science research in Arabic contexts. By bridging traditional humanistic inquiry with advanced computing, the project aims to transform the scale and precision of research in Arabic linguistics.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Arabic language. Includes instruction in philology; Classical Arabic; Modern Standard Arabic; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance applied psychology research on optimizing workplace mental health interventions in high-stress industries. Despite evidence supporting organizational well-being programs, scalable implementation remains challenging due to variability in employee needs, intervention timing, and contextual factors. Current statistical models lack the capacity to handle dynamic, multilevel datasets (e.g., longitudinal employee surveys, productivity metrics, and real-time biometric data) that capture the interplay between individual psychological states and organizational outcomes. To address this, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) simulating employee behavior and intervention effects under diverse workplace conditions. These models will integrate empirical data from a 12-month organizational study (N = 2,500 employees) with existing psychological frameworks on stress, resilience, and team dynamics. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses to identify intervention configurations that maximize effectiveness across heterogeneous subgroups. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess robustness under stochastic variations, while machine learning pipelines will analyze emergent patterns in intervention outcomes. Expected outcomes include actionable guidelines for adaptive, personalized mental health support systems in workplace settings, as well as open-source computational tools for applied psychologists to model complex human behavior in organizational contexts. This work bridges gaps between psychological theory and practical implementation, offering a scalable framework to evaluate interventions before real-world deployment. By utilizing HPC capabilities, the project aims to advance methodological innovation in applied psychology, ensuring solutions are both empirically grounded and computationally tractable for stakeholders in industry and public health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychological theories and methods to real-world settings and problems, such as business and industry, government, education, military, and community settings. Includes instruction in applications of psychology, industrial/organizational psychology, developmental psychology, social psychology, cognitive psychology, counseling, human factors, research methods and statistics, and program evaluation.

abstract: This project seeks to address computational bottlenecks in the design and optimization of heterogeneous computing systems for real-time machine learning applications. As neural network architectures grow in complexity, traditional hardware-software co-design strategies struggle to balance latency, power efficiency, and adaptability across dynamic workloads. The research aims to develop a scalable framework for simulating and optimizing custom accelerators (e.g., FPGA-based architectures) integrated with adaptive machine learning models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to enable large-scale parameter sweeps, high-fidelity simulations of hardware-software interactions, and reinforcement learning-based optimization across multi-objective design spaces. Computational methods will leverage distributed computing paradigms via MPI and GPU-accelerated libraries (e.g., CUDA, TensorFlow) to parallelize cycle-accurate simulations of hardware architectures and concurrent training of neural networks under varying constraints. Key innovations include a hybrid differentiable programming approach to co-optimize hardware configurations and model weights, as well as a graph-based representation for encoding system-level dependencies. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for joint hardware-software optimization, validated benchmarks for edge-AI systems, and open-source tools to bridge architecture simulation with machine learning workflows. The project will directly advance the scalability of design automation tools in computer engineering, enabling rapid prototyping of efficient, domain-specific computing systems. Results will be disseminated through conferences in computer architecture and machine learning, with broader impacts in autonomous systems and embedded AI. The requested HPC resources will support iterative experimentation with 10,000+ core-hour simulations, terabyte-scale dataset processing, and real-time performance modeling across diverse hardware targets.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving dynamics of compliance mechanisms in international environmental law, with a focus on multilateral treaty regimes. The research problem centers on the computational challenges of modeling state behavior, treaty adherence patterns, and the cascading effects of non-compliance across interconnected legal frameworks. Traditional legal methodologies struggle to process the scale and complexity of modern treaty networks, which encompass thousands of ratified agreements, dynamic reservation clauses, and heterogeneous compliance reports spanning decades. The project will employ a hybrid computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) for automated analysis of treaty texts and state submissions, network science to map interdependencies between legal obligations, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate strategic state decision-making under conflicting international commitments. Custom algorithms will be developed to quantify legal obligation "spillover" effects and predict systemic vulnerabilities in treaty architectures. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based NLP models on multilingual legal corpora, running large-scale ABM simulations with parameterized state actors, and processing temporal network datasets spanning 50+ years of treaty ratification histories. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for identifying latent conflicts in multilateral treaty design, predictive metrics for compliance risk assessment, and visual analytics tools to support treaty negotiation processes. By integrating computational social science methods with doctrinal legal analysis, this work aims to advance evidence-based approaches to international legal design while establishing scalable methodologies for computational legal studies. The resulting models and datasets will be made available to intergovernmental organizations and legal researchers through a curated open-access platform.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law affecting relations between nations, the behavior of international organizations, and the international activities of private citizens and organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate advanced statistical models to analyze complex, high-dimensional social science datasets, with a focus on understanding dynamic socioeconomic disparities and their drivers in urban populations. The research addresses key computational challenges in modeling non-linear relationships, temporal dependencies, and spatial heterogeneity within social systems using observational data prone to selection bias and missingness. We propose a hybrid computational framework combining Bayesian hierarchical modeling, stochastic agent-based simulations, and non-parametric regression techniques to account for multi-level social interactions and confounding factors. The methodology will implement Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms with adaptive sampling to estimate posterior distributions for key parameters governing inequality dynamics, while employing distributed computing strategies to handle longitudinal datasets spanning millions of records from census microdata, social surveys, and digital trace sources. High-performance computing resources are essential for three critical components: 1) Parallelized model fitting across hundreds of demographic strata using variational inference methods 2) Large-scale simulation studies to evaluate model robustness under different missing data mechanisms 3) Bootstrapped uncertainty quantification for policy impact projections through resampling techniques requiring 10^5+ iterations. Expected outcomes include new statistical approaches for causal inference in observational social data, validated computational tools for counterfactual analysis of intervention scenarios, and evidence-based insights into the temporal evolution of opportunity gaps across population subgroups. The developed methods will advance statistical computing practices in social sciences by creating scalable implementations of complex models that respect the hierarchical structure and measurement limitations inherent in real-world social data. Results will be disseminated through open-source software packages optimized for HPC architectures and policy briefs quantifying the potential impacts of different equity-oriented interventions.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the social scientific applications of relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in quantitative social science methodologies, the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational methods for analyzing high-dimensional, sparse biological datasets commonly encountered in agricultural and natural resource studies, where traditional statistical approaches face limitations due to complex error structures, unbalanced designs, and temporal-spatial dependencies. The research focuses on creating scalable Bayesian hierarchical models integrated with machine learning frameworks to address challenges in phenotypic prediction, genotype-environment interaction analysis, and dynamic resource optimization. A core innovation involves adapting stochastic variational inference algorithms for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to enable efficient parameter estimation in complex mixed-effects models, particularly when applied to longitudinal agricultural data with missing observations. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling and GPU-accelerated tensor operations to handle matrices exceeding 10^6 dimensions, typical in modern crop phenomics studies. Method validation will employ synthetic datasets generated through HPC-powered simulations mimicking real-world agricultural trials with controlled sparsity patterns and noise distributions. Successful implementation will provide open-source tools for 1) imputing unbalanced experimental measurements in plant breeding datasets, 2) quantifying uncertainty in resource allocation strategies under climatic variability, and 3) optimizing sensor network designs for precision agriculture applications. The requested computing resources will directly support large-scale benchmarking against existing biometrical methods, with performance metrics assessing both statistical accuracy and computational scalability. Outcomes will advance quantitative methodology for sparse data analysis in biological systems while delivering practical software solutions tailored to agricultural researchers working with increasingly complex, high-throughput phenotyping datasets. This work bridges critical gaps between modern statistical theory and computational practice in biometric applications, enabling more robust analysis of biological systems under real-world data constraints.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics and other computational methods to the study of problems in the biological sciences and related fields in agriculture and natural resources. Includes instruction in computational biology, mathematical statistics, matrix algebra, applied calculus, experimental design, linear modeling, sampling theory, stochastic processes, spatial and temporal analysis, longitudinal analysis, sparse/unbalanced data and complex error, and applications to such topics as population genetics, animal breeding, forest genetics, population dynamics, wildlife biometry, ecology, and agricultural and natural resource management.

abstract: Plant breeding programs face increasing pressure to develop climate-resilient, high-yield crop varieties amid shifting environmental conditions and population growth. This project addresses the computational bottleneck in analyzing large-scale genomic and phenotypic datasets to identify adaptive traits and optimize selection strategies. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable genome-wide association studies (GWAS), genomic prediction models, and multi-environment trial simulations for hybrid crop systems. The research focuses on integrating terabyte-scale genomic data from next-generation sequencing of staple crops (e.g., wheat, tomato) with hyperspectral imaging and environmental sensor datasets from field trials. Computational workflows will employ machine learning architectures, including convolutional neural networks for image-based phenotyping and transformer models for genotype-environment interaction analysis. Key challenges involve parallelizing population-scale variant calling pipelines using GPU-accelerated tools (GATK, PLINK) and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to predict trait heritability under drought and pathogen stress scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of candidate genes associated with nutrient-use efficiency and disease resistance, (2) optimized genomic selection indices for accelerated breeding cycles, and (3) open-access models predicting phenotypic responses to regional climate projections. This computational framework will directly support six ongoing field trials across three breeding stations, reducing experimental redundancy by simulating 10^6 potential crosses prior to physical hybridization. The allocated resources will enable processing >5,000 whole-genome sequences and 50TB of time-series phenotypic data through custom Python/R workflows containerized for Slurm-based clusters. By establishing scalable pipelines for multi-omics data integration, this work aims to bridge the gap between molecular discovery and agronomic application, providing plant breeders with decision-support tools to address 21st-century food security challenges. Results will be disseminated through the National Agricultural Genomics Database and integrated into graduate curriculum for computational plant breeding.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural plant health, the development of new plant varieties, and the selective improvement of agricultural plant populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, agronomy, plant protection, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the spatial dynamics of informal knowledge networks in urban food systems and their resilience to climate-induced disruptions, leveraging computational geography to address gaps in socio-environmental systems research. While urbanization intensifies, informal food networks—such as community gardens, street vendors, and localized barter systems—remain critical yet understudied components of urban resilience. The research problem centers on how these networks adapt to climate stressors (e.g., extreme heat, flooding) and how their spatial configurations influence equity in resource access. Current models often neglect the fine-grained, dynamic interactions between human agency, infrastructure, and environmental variability. To address this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multi-agent simulation framework integrating high-resolution geospatial data (satellite imagery, Lidar), climate projections, and agent-based behavioral models derived from participatory mapping surveys. Computational workflows will parallelize spatial network analysis to model cascading disruptions across temporal scales (daily interactions to decadal climate trends) and spatial scales (neighborhood to metropolitan regions). Machine learning methods will identify emergent patterns in network adaptability, while geostatistical models will quantify disparities in access under varying climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational toolkit for simulating socio-spatial resilience, predictive maps of vulnerability hotspots, and policy-relevant insights into infrastructure investments that bolster equitable food security. By bridging computational geography with social practice theory, this work advances methodological innovation in modeling human-environment interactions while contributing empirical knowledge to nascent interdisciplinary research on informal urban systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling large raster datasets, optimizing complex network algorithms, and running ensemble simulations to capture uncertainty in socio-environmental feedbacks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the spatial distribution and interrelationships of people, natural resources, plant and animal life. Includes instruction in historical and political geography, cultural geography, economic and physical geography, regional science, cartographic methods, remote sensing, spatial analysis, and applications to areas such as land-use planning, development studies, and analyses of specific countries, regions, and resources.

abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation outcomes remain highly variable due to complex interactions between immunological, metabolic, and clinical factors. Current risk stratification tools lack precision in predicting graft rejection, long-term complications, and patient-specific responses to immunosuppression, particularly in pediatric populations. This project proposes the development of a multi-omics computational framework to model post-transplant outcomes by integrating longitudinal genomic, metabolomic, and clinical data from pediatric recipients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process and analyze large-scale datasets, including whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing of graft biopsies, and dynamic metabolite profiles, alongside real-world clinical variables such as immunosuppression levels, infection episodes, and growth metrics. Machine learning approaches, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, will be employed to identify predictive signatures of graft dysfunction and optimize personalized immunosuppression protocols. Agent-based modeling will simulate immune cell interactions within the hepatic microenvironment to explore mechanistic drivers of rejection. The computational pipeline will leverage parallelized workflows for data harmonization, feature selection, and model validation across heterogeneous datasets from three international pediatric transplant centers. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for 5-year graft survival, actionable biomarkers for early rejection detection, and in silico platforms to simulate therapeutic interventions. This research will directly address critical gaps in pediatric transplant hepatology by enabling data-driven clinical decision-making, reducing trial-and-error dosing strategies, and improving long-term outcomes for children requiring hepatic transplantation. The requested HPC infrastructure will provide the necessary capacity for large-scale data integration, complex model training, and real-time analytics to support translational applications in this underserved population.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge, skill, and expertise required of pediatric gastroenterologists to care for children and young adults prior to and following hepatic transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational analysis of Sanskrit and Classical Indo-Aryan language corpora, addressing challenges in processing complex morphological structures and tracing diachronic linguistic developments. Traditional methods for analyzing these texts are hindered by the vast volume of sources and the intricate grammatical rules governing Sanskrit and its related languages, such as Pali and Prakrits. The research will employ parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to ancient Indo-Aryan languages, including tokenization of sandhi compounds, morphological parsing using finite-state transducers, and probabilistic modeling of syntactic constructions. By deploying these tools on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to process multi-gigabyte text corpora spanning Vedic to post-classical Sanskrit, enabling comparative analysis of lexical, phonological, and grammatical features across historical periods and related dialects. Key outputs will include an open-access annotated corpus with machine-readable linguistic annotations, quantitative models of language change in the Indo-Aryan family, and optimized NLP tools for classical South Asian languages. The computational resources will facilitate previously intractable analyses, such as network modeling of intertextual relationships in commentarial traditions and phylogenetic analysis of Prakrit dialect variation. These outcomes will provide novel methodologies for digital philology in Indology while offering substantive contributions to historical linguistics through data-driven perspectives on Sanskrit's linguistic ecology and its development within the broader Indo-European context.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Sanskrit and Classical Indian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Sanskrit and related ancient and classical Indo-Aryan languages. Includes instruction in Vedic and Classical Sanskrit, Pali and other Prakrits, and the historical development of Indo-Aryan languages and their relation to Indo-European languages such as Greek, Latin and the Baltic languages.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the scientific understanding of material interactions and biomechanical stress dynamics in nail care practices, an understudied domain within cosmetology. While nail technicians specialize in aesthetic and functional care of nails, there is limited empirical research on the long-term effects of common procedures—such as gel polish curing, acrylic application, or cuticle treatments—on nail plate integrity and underlying tissue health. Current training relies on observational best practices, but emerging concerns about repetitive strain injuries among technicians and clients, coupled with rising demand for durable, biocompatible products, necessitate a computational approach to model these interactions at scale. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution during manual filing and polishing techniques, molecular dynamics (MD) to study adhesive interactions between synthetic coatings and keratin structures, and machine learning (ML) to correlate historical client outcome data with procedural variables. By integrating 3D-scanned nail morphology datasets and material property libraries, the simulations will predict fracture risks, degradation rates of coatings, and optimal tool geometries. Outcomes will inform evidence-based guidelines for safer, more sustainable techniques and product formulations, while establishing a computational framework for ongoing innovation in this specialized field. This work bridges cosmetology, materials science, and biomechanics, addressing a critical gap in practitioner training and consumer safety without overlapping with traditional STEM or social science domains. The requested HPC resources are essential due to the high resolution required for sub-millimeter anatomical modeling and the iterative optimization of multivariate procedural parameters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shape fingernails and toenails, remove unwanted skin and blemishes, apply polish and cosmetics to nails, and function as licensed manicurists or nail technicians/specialists.  Includes instruction in manicuring theory; skin anatomy; nail growth, irregularities, and diseases; sterilization and sanitation; equipment and table maintenance; cuticle, blemish, and rough skin removal; nail filing, shaping, and polishing; cream application and extremity massage; nail sculpture and design art; product storage and use; customer service; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of electrical and electronic system design by developing advanced computational workflows optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. Modern electrical drafting and CAD/CADD applications face challenges in simulating large-scale circuits, optimizing component layouts for energy efficiency, and validating designs against multi-domain constraints (e.g., thermal, electromagnetic). Current software tools often lack the scalability to handle intricate industrial systems, leading to time-consuming iterative processes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating parallelized electromagnetic field solvers, machine learning-assisted routing algorithms, and distributed multi-physics simulation frameworks. The HPC resources will enable rapid evaluation of thousands of design permutations for power distribution networks and embedded systems, with automated constraint checking against industry standards (e.g., IPC, IEEE). Key innovations include GPU-accelerated parasitic extraction for high-frequency circuits and topology optimization algorithms adapted for manufacturability in printed circuit board (PCB) design. Expected outcomes include a prototype computational pipeline capable of reducing design iteration cycles by 40-60% for complex systems, validated through case studies involving smart grid components and industrial automation controllers. The project will additionally produce benchmark datasets for AI-driven layout optimization, bridging gaps between traditional drafting practices and emerging computational design paradigms. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish new best practices for resource-efficient electrical CAD workflows while enhancing educational materials for next-generation drafting technicians. Success metrics will focus on computational efficiency gains, design error reduction rates, and scalability demonstrations for systems exceeding 10,000 components.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Drafting and Electrical/ Electronics CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working schematics and representations in support of electrical/electronic engineers, computer engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic electronics, electrical systems and computer layouts; electrode-mechanical drafting; manufacturing circuitry; computer-aided drafting (CAD); and electrical systems specification interpretation.

abstract: The development of advanced materials with tailored optoelectronic and mechanical properties is critical for next-generation photonic devices and molecular electronics. However, the rational design of such materials—particularly hybrid organic-inorganic systems and semiconductor nanowires—is hindered by the complexity of predicting how nanoscale structural features, such as interfacial bonding, defects, or lattice strain, influence macroscopic behavior. Experimental trial-and-error approaches remain costly and time-intensive, while existing computational models often lack the resolution or scalability to address multiscale phenomena. This project seeks to overcome these limitations through high-performance computing (HPC)-driven simulations to map structure-property relationships in two target systems: (1) self-assembled molecular arrays for chemical sensing and (2) gallium nitride (GaN) nanowires with engineered dopant profiles for enhanced optoelectronic efficiency. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations will parameterize electronic interactions and defect energetics, while machine-learned interatomic potentials will enable large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess thermal stability and strain propagation. These methods will be integrated with evolutionary algorithms to screen >10,000 candidate configurations for optimal charge transport, optical absorption, and mechanical resilience. The scale of these simulations—requiring thousands of concurrent cores for MD trajectories exceeding 100 ns and DFT models with >1,000 atoms—necessitates HPC resources. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for doping strategies in GaN nanowires to minimize non-radiative recombination and design rules for π-conjugated molecular assemblies to amplify sensor response times. Results will directly guide experimental synthesis efforts at our collaborator’s lab, accelerating the development of materials for energy-efficient photodetectors and high-sensitivity chemical sensor arrays. By bridging atomic-scale insights with device-level performance, this work aims to establish a computational pipeline for materials discovery that reduces reliance on empirical approaches.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis and study of organic or inorganic materials and their electronic, magnetic, optical or mechanical properties. Includes instruction in advanced materials for photonics, lasers, chemical sensors and arrays or nanochemistry; semiconductor nanowires; and molecular electronics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Black cultural production across the 20th-century United States and Caribbean, with a focus on interdisciplinary connections between literature, visual art, and music. While existing scholarship has documented key movements like the Harlem Renaissance or Negritude, significant gaps remain in mapping large-scale patterns of creative exchange, thematic recurrence, and diasporic influence due to the scale and complexity of archival materials. Our research will employ computational text analysis, image recognition, and network modeling to process digitized collections of novels, paintings, oral histories, and musical recordings from 1900–1999. Using natural language processing (NLP) tools fine-tuned for African-American Vernacular English and Creole languages, we will identify linguistic motifs in literary works alongside parallel visual patterns in contemporaneous artworks. Audio analysis algorithms will cross-reference musical structures with textual/visual datasets to trace transmedia cultural signatures. Graph neural networks will then model spatial and temporal diffusion of creative themes across geographic nodes (e.g., New York, New Orleans, Port-au-Prince). This approach requires HPC capabilities to manage heterogeneous data (10TB+ of text, images, audio) and run multi-modal machine learning pipelines. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously understudied connections between regional artistic movements, 2) visualization of how specific aesthetic strategies persisted or transformed through migration and political change, and 3) an open-access computational framework for analyzing diasporic cultural production. By enabling systematic study of cross-disciplinary creative practices at scale, this project aims to reshape understandings of Black cultural innovation while developing methodologies that center African-American Studies’ unique archival challenges and opportunities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) and related dysfunctions present complex, multifaceted challenges due to the interplay of biological, mechanical, and systemic factors that influence outcomes. Despite advances in clinical care, treatment efficacy remains limited, in part due to insufficient understanding of injury heterogeneity, recovery mechanisms, and patient-specific predictors of complications. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive multiscale models of SCI pathophysiology and recovery trajectories. The research will integrate heterogeneous clinical, imaging, and biomolecular datasets to simulate injury mechanisms, optimize therapeutic interventions, and identify personalized rehabilitation strategies. A key focus is modeling the dynamic interactions between secondary injury processes (e.g., inflammation, ischemia) and patient-specific factors such as lesion severity, comorbidities, and neuroanatomical variability. Computational methods will include finite element modeling of spinal biomechanics, agent-based simulations of cellular responses, and machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal patient data from multicenter registries. These approaches require HPC resources to manage large-scale parameter optimization, real-time visualization of 3D neural networks, and ensemble modeling of probabilistic outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational platform for simulating SCI progression and intervention effects across spatiotemporal scales, (2) predictive biomarkers for complications such as neuropathic pain and autonomic dysreflexia, and (3) AI-driven decision-support tools for clinical trial stratification and rehabilitation planning. By enabling the synthesis of high-dimensional data into actionable insights, this work aims to advance precision medicine in SCI care, reduce long-term disability burdens, and provide a scalable framework for future translational studies. The requested computing resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in processing speed, model complexity, and data integration that hinder clinically relevant discoveries in this field.
cip_definition: Research on how to address the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and management of traumatic spinal cord injury and non-traumatic etiologies of spinal cord dysfunction, including related medical, physical, psychological, and vocational disabilities and complications.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing additive manufacturing (AM) processes for complex, high-performance components through advanced computational modeling. Despite the growing adoption of AM in industry, defects such as porosity, residual stress, and anisotropic material behavior persist due to insufficient understanding of multi-physics interactions during fabrication. Current models often oversimplify thermo-mechanical dynamics or lack the resolution to predict localized phenomena, limiting their utility for process parameter optimization. To overcome these barriers, we propose the development of a high-fidelity, multi-scale simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) for heat transfer and stress evolution with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model melt pool behavior and powder-bed interactions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify correlations between process parameters (e.g., laser power, scan speed) and defect formation, enabling adaptive parameter optimization. The simulations will operate at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, requiring parallelized computations across thousands of cores to manage the ~10^8-element meshes and nanosecond-scale timesteps. Experimental validation will utilize in-situ monitoring data from collaborative partners to refine model accuracy. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to minimize post-processing, improve part reliability, and expand the viable design space for AM components in sectors requiring high geometric complexity, such as customized medical implants and lightweight industrial tooling. By elucidating the interdependencies between process parameters and material responses, this work will advance the scalability of AM for critical applications while reducing material waste and energy consumption. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current computational bottlenecks, enabling the iterative simulations and large datasets required for robust model training and validation.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize care strategies for pediatric patients with chronic respiratory conditions, such as asthma and cystic fibrosis, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Despite advances in pediatric nursing, individualized care planning remains challenging due to the dynamic interplay of genetic, environmental, and socio-economic factors influencing disease progression. Current clinical tools often lack the computational power to integrate multi-modal data (e.g., electronic health records, genomic profiles, environmental sensors) at scale, limiting their utility in real-world decision-making. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning framework to analyze longitudinal patient data and simulate intervention outcomes. The computational workflow will employ ensemble learning algorithms to identify risk factors for acute exacerbations and reinforcement learning to model optimal intervention timing. Agent-based simulations will further evaluate how care protocols perform under varying demographic and resource constraints. By utilizing HPC resources, we aim to process terabyte-scale datasets from three pediatric health networks while maintaining compliance with privacy standards (e.g., HIPAA). Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for exacerbation risk, open-source decision-support tools for nursing teams, and scalable templates for personalizing care pathways. This work will directly inform nursing education by identifying critical data literacy competencies and provide evidence for resource allocation in underserved populations. The requested computing infrastructure is essential to handle memory-intensive genomic analyses and parallelized simulations, which are infeasible on local clinical servers. Successful implementation could reduce hospital readmissions by enabling proactive, data-driven care—a priority in pediatric nursing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care for children from infancy through adolescence. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting physicians, patient examination and referral, and planning and delivering health maintenance and health education programs.

abstract: Gene therapies hold transformative potential for treating genetic disorders, yet their development is hindered by challenges in optimizing delivery systems, predicting off-target effects, and personalizing treatments. This project seeks to address these barriers by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the interactions of viral and nonviral gene delivery vectors with host genomes, tissues, and immune systems. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of current vector design pipelines, which rely heavily on trial-and-error experimental approaches that are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to simulate complex biological systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven genome editing prediction, and multi-omics data analysis. MD simulations will model structural dynamics of adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids and lipid nanoparticles to identify modifications that enhance tissue-specific targeting and evade immune detection. Concurrently, neural networks trained on CRISPR-Cas9 editing outcomes and single-cell RNA-seq datasets will predict gene expression profiles following therapeutic interventions, enabling in silico screening of candidate therapies. These workflows will be scaled using GPU-accelerated nodes to handle systems with >10^6 atoms (for MD) and terabyte-scale genomic datasets (for ML/omics integration). The expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for vector-host interactions, (2) optimized vector designs with improved efficacy and safety profiles, and (3) a computational platform for patient-specific therapy simulation. By reducing reliance on low-throughput experimental methods, this work aims to accelerate the translation of gene therapies into clinical practice while addressing critical bioethical concerns around off-target risks. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary computational granularity and throughput, which cannot be supported by local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics to the therapeutic treatment of diseases and inherited abnormalities through the targeted modification of gene expression, and prepares individuals to administer genetic therapies. Includes instruction in medical genetics, genome analysis, pharmacology of gene transfer, viral vectors, nonviral therapeutic techniques, genetic screening, targeted gene delivery, vector production, safety and quality assurance, clinical trials management, and bioethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and behavioral impacts of dynamic tax code complexity in U.S. jurisdictions, with a focus on identifying patterns in compliance decision-making under evolving regulatory conditions. While traditional tax law research relies on case studies or econometric models, this study employs computational legal analytics to simulate how multi-layered federal and state tax provisions interact with taxpayer behavior at scale. The research problem centers on the opacity of cascading tax rule changes—such as those introduced by recent legislation addressing digital asset reporting and international corporate minimum taxes—and their downstream effects on compliance workflows, dispute resolution timelines, and strategic planning by filers. Using anonymized tax tribunal case records, legislative text corpora (2010–2023), and synthetically generated taxpayer profiles, the project will implement graph-based neural networks to model provision dependencies and agent-based simulations to test behavioral responses to hypothetical policy shifts. HPC resources are critical for training transformer models on terabyte-scale legal text datasets and running Monte Carlo experiments quantifying uncertainty in audit risk assessment under varying regulatory scenarios. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of computational friction points in tax code implementation, predictive metrics for compliance bottleneck formation, and an open-source toolkit for simulating the second-order effects of proposed tax legislation. By bridging computational modeling and legal informatics, this work aims to establish a framework for proactive complexity management in tax system design while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of statutory analysis and high-dimensional systems simulation.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of tax law and taxation procedures in U.S. or Canadian jurisdictions affecting individuals and corporations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools for enhancing the precision and efficiency of three-dimensional (3D) radiographic analysis in oral and maxillofacial radiology (OMFR). The increasing clinical reliance on high-resolution imaging modalities—such as cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and intraoral scanners—has generated vast, high-dimensional datasets. However, conventional methods for segmenting anatomical structures, detecting pathologies, and simulating biomechanical outcomes remain labor-intensive, error-prone, and computationally limited. To address these challenges, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating deep learning, finite element analysis (FEA), and multi-scale modeling to automate and optimize image-based diagnostics and treatment planning. The research will focus on two core objectives: (1) developing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on annotated CBCT/MRI datasets to autonomously segment critical structures (e.g., mandibular canals, temporomandibular joints) and detect pathologies (e.g., osteonecrosis, tumors), and (2) constructing patient-specific FEA models to simulate biomechanical responses of craniofacial bone under surgical or prosthetic loading. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated processing for rapid inference and large-scale parameter optimization. Anticipated outcomes include novel algorithms for artifact reduction in low-quality scans, predictive models for bone remodeling post-intervention, and open-source tools for automated lesion quantification. By overcoming current computational bottlenecks, this work aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy for conditions such as osteoradionecrosis and obstructive sleep apnea while enabling personalized surgical planning. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling datasets exceeding 50TB, training complex neural architectures, and running iterative FEA simulations at clinically relevant scales. This project bridges a critical gap in OMFR by translating computational innovation into scalable clinical tools, ultimately improving patient outcomes in the diagnosis and management of complex craniofacial disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on producing and interpreting images of the jaws, teeth, bone, and other structures of the head and neck region; and to diagnose and manage diseases, disorders, and conditions that affect this area of the body.

abstract: Dairy production systems face critical challenges in optimizing feed efficiency, animal health, and environmental sustainability, particularly under the constraints of climate variability and evolving microbial threats. A key gap lies in understanding the complex interactions between dairy cattle microbiomes, metabolic pathways, and dietary interventions at a systems level. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating metagenomic, metabolomic, and physiological data from lactating Holstein cows. We will employ machine learning algorithms to identify microbial consortia and host-microbe interactions associated with enhanced nutrient utilization and methane mitigation, followed by genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions of prioritized microbial communities. Agent-based modeling will simulate herd-level outcomes of targeted dietary modifications informed by these microbial signatures. The computational workflow will process >10 TB of sequencing data and require iterative simulations across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 combinations, necessitating parallelized processing and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to guide precision feeding strategies that improve milk yield efficiency while reducing enteric methane emissions by ≥15%. The models will also elucidate microbial biomarkers for early detection of metabolic disorders, supporting proactive herd health management. By bridging gaps between microbial ecology, nutrition, and dairy systems engineering, this work will provide novel decision-support tools for producers and advance fundamental knowledge of ruminant-microbe symbiosis. The requested HPC allocation will enable computationally intensive analyses that are infeasible with local institutional clusters, directly supporting the agricultural sciences’ mandate to develop climate-smart livestock production systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of dairy animals and the production and handling of dairy products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting and managing hypoxia in coastal marine ecosystems, a growing threat to biodiversity and water quality under climate change and nutrient pollution. Hypoxic zones, characterized by dangerously low oxygen levels, are expanding in estuaries and coastal waters globally, yet current models lack the resolution to integrate fine-scale hydrodynamic processes with biogeochemical feedbacks across land-marine interfaces. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework coupling a three-dimensional hydrodynamic model (FVCOM) with a reactive-transport biogeochemical model (Delft3D-WAQ) to simulate oxygen dynamics in the Chesapeake Bay, a system experiencing severe seasonal hypoxia. The HPC resources will facilitate nested modeling at unprecedented 50-meter resolution, capturing tidal influences, riverine nutrient inputs, and sediment oxygen demand simultaneously across the bay’s 11,000 km² domain. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize parameterization of organic matter decay rates and phytoplankton productivity using historical monitoring data and remote sensing inputs. By simulating scenarios of reduced nutrient loading and altered hydrology under climate projections, this work will quantify thresholds for hypoxia mitigation and identify priority regions for conservation or regulatory intervention. The computational scale required—millions of grid cells, hourly time steps over decadal spans, and ensemble runs for uncertainty analysis—exceeds the capacity of local cluster resources. Outcomes will provide actionable strategies for state agencies managing the Chesapeake Bay Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) program and advance open-source modeling tools applicable to other coastal systems. This project directly supports the program’s mission to integrate marine science, resource economics, and computational innovation for sustainable water resource management.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Water, Wetlands, and Marine Resources Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of marine/aquatic biology, oceanography, natural resource economics, and natural resources management to the development, conservation, and management of freshwater and saltwater environments. Includes instruction in subjects such as wetlands, riverine, lacustrine, coastal, and oceanic water resources; water conservation and use; flood control; pollution control; water supply logistics; wastewater management; aquatic and marine ecology; aquatic and marine life conservation; and the economic and recreational uses of water resources.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of terrorist network dynamics and cyber-physical threat convergence. The research addresses critical gaps in counterterrorism operations, particularly the challenge of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—including dark web communications, financial transaction records, and geospatial incident reports—to identify emerging threats and optimize resource allocation. Current methods struggle to integrate real-time data streams with historical patterns, limiting proactive responses to adaptive terrorist organizations. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), natural language processing (NLP), and graph neural networks (GNNs). The ABM component will simulate terrorist network behaviors under varying counterterrorism strategies, incorporating psychological and cultural factors derived from multilingual propaganda and intercepted communications processed via NLP. GNNs will map evolving relationships between entities, while Monte Carlo simulations assess probabilistic risks of cyber-physical attacks, including weaponized AI systems and critical infrastructure targeting. HPC resources are essential for scaling these computationally intensive models across multi-terabyte datasets and enabling parallelized scenario testing. Expected outcomes include a threat prioritization tool for intelligence analysts, identifying high-risk nodes in terrorist finance networks, and a vulnerability assessment protocol for hybrid threats blending cyberterrorism and physical operations. The resulting open-source framework will enhance situational awareness for homeland security agencies, enabling rapid, data-driven decisions in counterterrorism operations. By quantifying cascading impacts of potential attacks, this work directly supports national security objectives to mitigate risks from adaptive adversaries and emerging technologies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the study of terrorism as a global and national threat and the methods for analyzing and countering it. Includes instruction in psychology, cultural studies, terrorist history and organization, terrorist capabilities, terrorist finance and international money-laundering, threat assessment, intelligence operations, incident command systems, border security, emergency response, joint operations, surveillance and communications systems, cyberterrorism, weapons of mass destruction, counterterrorist operations, and applications to specific terrorist organizations and threats.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in Scandinavian Studies by analyzing the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across Nordic regions through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The primary research problem centers on understanding how historical and contemporary cultural artifacts—such as folklore collections, regional literature, and digital media—reflect and shape collective identities in Scandinavia, particularly among marginalized groups like the Sámi and Greenlandic Inuit. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the vast, multilingual corpora and visual archives available, necessitating computational approaches to identify patterns, semantic shifts, and cross-cultural influences. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for low-resource languages (e.g., Old Norse, modern Sámi dialects) and computer vision algorithms to analyze digitized manuscripts, oral histories, and iconographic traditions. Custom transformer models will be trained to detect thematic clusters, gendered representations, and mythological motifs across temporal and geographic axes, while graph-based analytics will map transnational cultural exchanges. Computational workflows will integrate metadata from Nordic digital libraries, requiring parallelized processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for computational cultural analysis in Scandinavian contexts, new insights into the interplay of indigeneity and modernity in Nordic identity discourses, and high-resolution visualizations of narrative diffusion. This work will establish methodological benchmarks for applying HPC resources to area studies, offering scalable tools for interdisciplinary researchers while addressing gaps in the digital humanities’ engagement with Nordic and Arctic cultural heritage. The requested allocation will support GPU-intensive model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous data, and runtime for cross-validation experiments across linguistic and visual domains.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Scandinavia, defined as Northern Europe including Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and related island groups (e.g., Greenland) and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the design and delivery of workforce education programs through the development of adaptive simulation tools to model skill acquisition in technical training environments. Workforce educators face persistent challenges in personalizing instruction for learners with diverse educational backgrounds and industry-specific skill gaps, particularly in rapidly evolving technical fields such as advanced manufacturing and renewable energy. Existing pedagogical frameworks often lack empirically validated strategies to optimize training pathways, leading to inefficiencies in learner outcomes and resource allocation. To address this, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate skill development trajectories across varied instructional scenarios. Agent-based modeling will be used to represent heterogeneous learner cohorts, incorporating variables such as prior knowledge, cognitive load thresholds, and hands-on practice intervals. Machine learning algorithms will then analyze simulated outcomes to identify instructional designs that maximize skill retention and time-to-proficiency. The computational workflow will integrate real-world training data from partner vocational institutions, including performance metrics from augmented reality (AR) welding trainers and industrial automation labs. By scaling these simulations to model thousands of concurrent learners—a task requiring parallelized computing capabilities—the project will generate actionable insights into how workforce educators can adapt curricula for emerging technologies. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for predicting optimal training interventions based on learner profiles and industry requirements, as well as evidence-based guidelines for integrating adaptive learning technologies in technical classrooms. This work directly supports the Workforce Education and Development program’s mission by advancing data-driven approaches to workforce training, ultimately strengthening the alignment between educational practices and employer needs in technical sectors.
detailed_field: Adult, continuing, and workforce education and development
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach programs designed to develop or upgrade specific employment-related knowledge and skills in various settings, and to various age groups.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time language interpretation and specialized translation systems, particularly for low-resource and morphologically complex languages, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced neural machine translation (NMT) models. Current translation tools often struggle with context-aware accuracy in dynamic settings (e.g., legal, medical, or technical interpretation) and underperform for Indigenous and minority languages in Canada, such as Inuktitut or Cree, due to limited parallel corpora and computational constraints. Our research will employ transformer-based architectures trained on augmented datasets combining domain-specific terminology, synthetically generated parallel texts, and multimodal inputs (audio-visual data for interpretation contexts). HPC resources will enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization, cross-lingual transfer learning across 15+ language pairs, and real-time latency simulations for simultaneous interpretation scenarios. We will integrate linguistic typology features to improve morphological parsing and evaluate models using novel metrics that balance semantic fidelity, cultural nuance, and temporal constraints. Outcomes will include open-source multilingual NMT frameworks optimized for sector-specific translation tasks, a curated repository of Indigenous language resources, and protocols for deploying low-latency interpretation systems in professional settings. This work directly supports Canada’s linguistic diversity by enhancing computational tools for under-resourced languages while advancing translation studies through scalable, empirically tested methods for context-sensitive language processing. The requested computing allocation will facilitate training billion-parameter models across GPU clusters, enabling comparative studies of model efficiency and robustness that are infeasible with standard academic infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be professional interpreters and/or translators of documents and data files, either from English or (Canadian) French into another language or languages or vice versa. Includes intensive instruction in one or more foreign languages plus instruction in subjects such as single- and multiple-language interpretation, one- or two-way interpretation, simultaneous interpretation, general and literary translation, business translation, technical translation, and other specific applications of linguistic skills.

abstract: Developmental-behavioral pediatrics faces a critical challenge in predicting and addressing heterogeneous developmental trajectories in children, particularly those at risk for neurodevelopmental disorders or behavioral difficulties due to complex interactions between genetic, environmental, and psychosocial factors. Current statistical models lack the capacity to integrate multi-modal data—including longitudinal electronic health records, neuroimaging, genomic variants, and family-environmental metrics—at scales necessary to capture non-linear relationships or identify early biomarkers. This project proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to construct predictive models for individualized risk stratification and intervention planning. Using machine learning architectures (e.g., graph neural networks, transformer-based temporal models), we will analyze de-identified datasets from 15,000+ children enrolled in a national developmental-behavioral cohort, incorporating dynamic variables such as caregiver-reported behavioral logs, speech-language samples, and neighborhood-level social determinants of health. Computational workflows will prioritize interpretability through attention mechanisms and feature importance mapping to ensure clinical relevance. HPC resources are essential for training multi-task models on GPU clusters, performing hyperparameter optimization across combinatorial variable spaces, and simulating developmental trajectories under hypothetical intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms for early identification of children at risk for autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or disruptive behavioral phenotypes, with improved sensitivity over existing screening tools; (2) a publicly accessible toolkit for simulating the developmental impact of targeted family support strategies; and (3) foundational insights into critical periods for intervention efficacy. This work directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance evidence-based, equitable care by enabling data-driven personalization of developmental-behavioral healthcare. The requested resources will support computationally intensive tasks that cannot feasibly be performed on local clinical servers, ensuring scalability and reproducibility for future translational studies.
cip_definition: Research on how to assist in the prevention, diagnosis, and management of developmental difficulties and problematic behaviors in children, and in the family dysfunctions that compromise children's development; and to foster understanding and promotion of optimal development of children and families through research, education, clinical care, and advocacy efforts.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic coordination of circadian-regulated metabolic processes in plant root systems under fluctuating nutrient availability, a specialized niche integrating plant molecular biology, chronobiology, and systems-level computational modeling. While plant circadian systems are well studied in aerial tissues, the spatiotemporal regulation of root metabolic networks—particularly their synchronization with diurnal environmental changes and shoot-derived signaling—remains poorly understood. We propose to develop a multiscale computational framework combining agent-based modeling of root tip cell clusters with whole-organ metabolic flux analyses to decipher how circadian oscillators optimize nutrient uptake efficiency while balancing trade-offs between growth and stress adaptation. High-performance computing resources will enable the integration of single-cell RNA-seq datasets from Brassica rapa roots (generated through companion wet-lab experiments) with mechanistic models of transporter protein dynamics, phytohormone signaling gradients, and carbon allocation patterns. Key challenges include parameterizing stochastic variations in oscillator gene expression across root cell types and scaling these to predict emergent tissue-level behaviors under nutrient stress scenarios. The computational pipeline will leverage parallelized simulations to test hypotheses about phase entrainment mechanisms between shoot and root circadian systems, as well as machine learning approaches to identify critical nodes for metabolic resilience. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible model database for root chronometabolism, novel predictions about circadian control of root exudate composition, and foundational insights into engineering crop species with improved nutrient use efficiency through temporal optimization strategies. This work bridges molecular-scale regulatory mechanisms with organism-level adaptive responses, requiring computational resources capable of handling complex hybrid models that exceed current laboratory infrastructure capacities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of molecular biology, biochemistry, and biophysics to the study of biomolecular structures, functions, and processes specific to plants and plant substances. Includes instruction in the biochemistry of plant cells, nuclear-cytoplasmic interactions, molecular cytostructures, photosynthesis, plant molecular genetics, and the molecular biology of plant diseases.

abstract: The increasing demand for real-time, photorealistic rendering of dynamic volumetric datasets in augmented reality (AR) applications presents a critical computational challenge. Current rasterization and ray-tracing techniques struggle to efficiently handle the complex light-matter interactions inherent in heterogeneous materials, such as biological tissues or engineered metamaterials, particularly when these materials exhibit time-dependent optical properties. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a hybrid rendering pipeline that integrates finite-element electromagnetic simulations with adaptive neural radiance fields (NeRF), optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. The research will focus on two computational bottlenecks: (1) the prohibitive cost of repeatedly solving Maxwell’s equations for dynamically deforming volumetric objects, and (2) the memory limitations of training NeRF-like models on terabyte-scale simulation outputs. Our approach employs a distributed GPU-accelerated framework using domain decomposition for parallel finite-element computations, coupled with a novel wavelet-based compression scheme to enable hierarchical training of neural radiance representations. The HPC resources will facilitate large-scale parameter sweeps across material permittivity tensors and deformation gradients, generating a foundational dataset for training generalized neural rendering surrogates. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for coupling electromagnetic solvers with differentiable rendering engines and demonstrated scalability to billion-element meshes. This work will directly benefit AR surgical navigation systems and virtual material design platforms, where accurate real-time visualization of light propagation through complex media is essential. The project’s computational strategies will also advance interdisciplinary efforts in computational optics and inverse material design by establishing a template for HPC-accelerated, physics-informed neural rendering.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the software, hardware, and mathematical tools used to represent, display, and manipulate topological, two-, and three-dimensional objects on a computer screen and that prepares individuals to function as computer graphics specialists. Includes instruction in graphics software and systems; digital multimedia; graphic design; graphics devices, processors, and standards; attributes and transformations; projections; surface identification and rendering; color theory and application; and applicable geometry and algorithms.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of climate change impacts on critical watershed ecosystems through the development of high-resolution, integrated hydrological-ecological models. The research addresses a pressing gap in predicting how altered precipitation regimes and extreme weather events will affect water availability, sediment transport, and habitat resilience in mountainous regions that serve as freshwater sources for downstream communities. Current models either operate at coarse spatial resolutions that fail to capture topographic complexity or treat hydrological and ecological processes in isolation, limiting their utility for conservation planning. To overcome these limitations, we propose a coupled modeling framework that integrates a physically based hydrological model with agent-based ecological simulations, explicitly resolving interactions between water flows, sediment dynamics, and keystone species responses at 30-meter resolution across multi-decadal timescales. This approach requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage three core challenges: (1) processing terabytes of LiDAR-derived terrain data and climate projection ensembles, (2) executing parallelized model runs across diverse climate scenarios (RCP 4.5, 8.5), and (3) optimizing parameter space exploration through machine learning-assisted calibration against historical sensor networks and satellite observations. The anticipated outcomes include predictive maps of watershed vulnerability indices, identification of climate-resilient conservation corridors, and open-source tools for adaptive water resource management. By quantifying threshold behaviors in coupled human-natural systems, this work will directly inform state and federal agencies in prioritizing infrastructure investments and habitat protection measures. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and large-memory processors to handle high-resolution spatial simulations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and model improvisational structures in jazz performance, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome existing limitations in processing large-scale audio datasets. Improvisation, a cornerstone of jazz, remains poorly quantified due to its spontaneous and complex nature, which combines harmonic, rhythmic, and melodic innovation. Current analytical methods struggle to systematically decode the relationships between improvisational choices, historical styles, and performer intent, particularly at the scale required for comprehensive genre-wide insights. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach integrating signal processing, machine learning, and graph-based network analysis. Audio recordings from archival jazz collections (1920s–present) will be preprocessed into symbolic representations (MIDI, transcriptions) and audio features (spectrograms, pitch contours) using parallelized workflows optimized for HPC clusters. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer models will be trained to identify patterns in improvisational phrasing, while graph networks will map the evolution of stylistic influences across performers and eras. Computational demands are significant: training models on terabytes of audio requires distributed memory systems and GPU acceleration to handle hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation across diverse jazz subgenres. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database linking improvisational features to historical contexts, (2) generative models capable of producing stylistically informed improvisation templates for educational use, and (3) quantitative metrics assessing originality and stylistic convergence in solo performances. This work bridges computational musicology and jazz studies, offering new tools for preserving artistic legacy and enriching pedagogical strategies.
