By clarifying the computational signatures of jazz improvisation, the project aims to deepen scholarly understanding of creativity in performative arts while demonstrating how HPC resources can catalyze research in disciplines traditionally underserved by advanced cyberinfrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study and master the performance and composition of Jazz. Includes instruction in the history of Jazz and related musical styles such as the Blues, Jazz composition and theory, improvisation, Jazz instrument and ensemble performance, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing sustainable product design processes through high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial and product design faces growing challenges in balancing aesthetic innovation, material efficiency, and environmental impact, particularly when prototyping complex forms or novel materials. Traditional iterative design methods, which rely on physical prototypes and manual adjustments, are resource-intensive and limit exploration of high-dimensional design variables. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) for form exploration, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and thermal performance prediction, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to reconcile competing design criteria (e.g., ergonomics, manufacturability, carbon footprint). The computational workload requires parallel processing of large-scale parametric studies, including real-time rendering of 3D models in virtual environments and physics-based simulations of biodegradable material behaviors under stress. HPC resources will enable simultaneous evaluation of thousands of design variants across distributed GPU nodes, reducing iteration cycles from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include a validated workflow for generating structurally sound, visually compelling product designs with minimized material waste, alongside an open-access dataset correlating computational predictions with physical prototype testing. This research directly supports the program’s focus on cost-effective, sustainable design by establishing quantitative links between digital modeling choices and real-world performance. The project will also advance computational methods for aesthetic evaluation through machine learning, bridging gaps between subjective visual criteria and engineering constraints in applied visual arts. Results will be disseminated through design software plugins and workshops to empower practitioners in adopting HPC-driven methodologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via the creation of effective forms, shapes, and packaging for manufactured products. Includes instruction in designing in a wide variety of plastic and digital media, prototype construction, design development and refinement, principles of cost saving, and product structure and performance criteria relevant to aesthetic design parameters.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) by integrating multi-modal clinical, genomic, and proteomic data to model disease heterogeneity and treatment response. RA is characterized by complex, dynamic interactions between genetic susceptibility, immune dysregulation, and environmental factors, leading to variable patient outcomes and suboptimal therapeutic targeting. Current clinical biomarkers lack the sensitivity to predict disease progression or stratify patients for biologic therapies, resulting in prolonged trial-and-error treatment approaches. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS), single-cell RNA sequencing, and longitudinal proteomic profiling from a cohort of 1,200 RA patients. Machine learning models will identify combinatorial biomarkers associated with divergent disease trajectories, while mechanistic simulations of synovial tissue inflammation will map cytokine networks driving treatment resistance. HPC resources are essential to process >50 TB of raw sequencing data, perform distributed hyperparameter optimization for deep learning architectures, and execute multiscale agent-based models simulating immune cell interactions at tissue resolution. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive algorithm for anti-TNF therapy response validated against real-world clinical outcomes, (2) dynamically annotated maps of synovial microenvironment states linked to radiographic progression, and (3) open-source tools for scalable integration of -omics data in rheumatology. This work will establish computational infrastructure to decode RA heterogeneity, directly informing the design of biomarker-guided clinical trials and personalized therapeutic strategies. Successful implementation requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training, high-memory nodes for genome-scale analyses, and parallel computing capabilities to run 10⁴ stochastic simulations of immune-pathogenetic scenarios.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rheumatology

abstract: Individual variability in drug response remains a critical challenge in clinical pharmacogenomics, driven by complex interactions between genetic, clinical, and environmental factors. Traditional analytical approaches often fail to account for the high-dimensional nature of multi-omics data or the nonlinear dynamics underlying drug-gene interactions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic datasets with real-world clinical outcomes. The computational framework will employ machine learning techniques, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, to identify polygenic risk signatures and simulate pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic profiles across diverse patient populations. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will be conducted to prioritize clinically actionable variants, while parallelized simulations will model drug-gene-environment interactions at scale. The HPC environment is essential for managing petabytes of genomic data, enabling rapid iteration of complex models, and performing real-time analytics on electronic health record (EHR)-linked datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for warfarin dosing, statin-induced myopathy risk, and chemotherapy toxicity stratification, which will be disseminated through open-source tools and integrated into clinical decision support systems. By elucidating the mechanistic basis of drug response variability, this research aims to advance precision prescribing paradigms, reduce adverse drug events, and optimize therapeutic outcomes across diverse patient cohorts. The proposed computational infrastructure will also establish a scalable platform for future pharmacogenomics discovery, bridging the gap between genomic insights and actionable clinical guidelines.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Pharmacogenomics

abstract: The efficient allocation of social services remains a critical challenge in public administration, particularly in addressing disparities among vulnerable populations. Traditional policy evaluation methods often rely on simplified models that fail to capture the dynamic interactions between socioeconomic factors, institutional constraints, and individual behaviors. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate the impact of social service interventions on heterogeneous populations, enabling data-driven decision-making. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct an agent-based model integrating multi-source data—including census records, service utilization histories, and real-time socioeconomic indicators—to emulate decision-making processes at individual, community, and institutional levels. The computational approach will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess policy scenarios under varying demographic and economic conditions, coupled with machine learning techniques to identify latent patterns in service access barriers. By scaling these analyses across millions of synthetic agents, the project aims to quantify trade-offs between resource allocation strategies, predict unintended consequences of policy changes, and optimize service delivery networks. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the memory-intensive datasets and computationally demanding iterative simulations, which exceed the capacity of local computing resources. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible policy simulation toolkit for municipal planners, evidence-based recommendations for reducing service disparities, and methodological advances in computational social science applications within public administration. This work directly supports the program’s mission to enhance societal well-being through innovative administrative strategies grounded in rigorous, scalable analytical frameworks.
cip_title: Public Administration and Social Service Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public administration and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Long-term care (LTC) facilities face complex operational challenges in balancing individualized resident care, regulatory compliance, and financial sustainability. Traditional management approaches often rely on static models that fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating staff-to-resident ratios, real-time health deterioration patterns, and evolving regulatory constraints. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to optimize staff allocation, care delivery workflows, and emergency response protocols in LTC settings. By integrating multi-modal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), staff scheduling logs, sensor-derived mobility data, and historical incident reports—the framework will employ agent-based modeling and reinforcement learning to simulate facility operations under diverse scenarios. Computational experiments will test interventions such as dynamic staffing adjustments, predictive task prioritization algorithms, and hybrid human-AI decision support systems. The scalability of these simulations requires HPC resources to manage the parallel processing of high-dimensional temporal data across thousands of simulated facility-days while preserving the granularity of individual resident needs. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for operational efficiency gains, risk reduction in adverse events (e.g., falls, medication errors), and evidence-based thresholds for cost-quality tradeoffs. The resulting models will provide administrators with actionable insights into resource allocation strategies that align clinical priorities with organizational constraints. By addressing the computational complexity of real-world LTC management, this research bridges gaps between healthcare operations research, predictive analytics, and gerontological care standards, offering a novel methodology for sustainable long-term care administration in aging populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of nursing homes, assisted living facilities, adult day care, home health services, and other long term care settings and agencies serving the elderly and disabled. Includes instruction in social and clinical aspects of aging, health care delivery systems, nursing home administration, assisted living administration, aging policy and government programs, ethics, business management, financial management, human resource management, marketing, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational journalism, specifically addressing the challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous media datasets to study the dynamics of misinformation and audience engagement in digital news ecosystems. Contemporary journalism faces unprecedented demands to process and interpret vast volumes of unstructured data—including text, video, social media interactions, and multimedia content—which traditional analytical tools struggle to manage efficiently. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to identify patterns in misinformation propagation, quantify biases in news framing, and model the interplay between media content and public perception. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines, graph-based network analysis, and machine learning models trained on multimodal datasets (e.g., news articles, Twitter/X threads, YouTube metadata). These computational tasks require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization, and real-time simulation of information diffusion networks—workflows that demand HPC capabilities for memory-intensive operations and GPU-accelerated computing. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated fact-checking, bias detection algorithms tailored to journalistic workflows, and visual analytics platforms to map narrative shifts over time. By enabling rapid analysis of cross-platform media content, this research aims to empower journalists and media organizations with evidence-based strategies to counter misinformation, enhance transparency in reporting, and foster audience trust. The project bridges computational innovation with journalistic practice, offering novel methodologies to address pressing challenges in digital public discourse while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources in non-traditional, humanities-centric domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in journalism, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the diffusion dynamics of misinformation across digital media platforms, a critical challenge in contemporary communication studies. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in how false narratives propagate through social networks, particularly during politically sensitive periods, and how user engagement behaviors—such as sharing, commenting, and algorithmic amplification—contribute to their virality. Traditional analytical tools are insufficient for processing the scale and complexity of these datasets, which include terabytes of timestamped social media posts, user metadata, and multimedia content. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, network analysis, and agent-based modeling to map misinformation cascades across platforms like X (formerly Twitter), Reddit, and TikTok. Custom machine learning models will classify content sentiment, detect coordinated inauthentic behavior, and simulate diffusion scenarios under varying platform policies. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants) on multimodal data, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to test intervention strategies, and storing intermediate outputs from large-scale graph analyses. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying the role of echo chambers in misinformation persistence, identifying key network actors that amplify harmful content, and modeling the efficacy of counter-messaging campaigns. This work will contribute novel methodologies to communication research by bridging computational social science with media effects theory, offering empirically grounded insights for policymakers and platform designers. Results will be disseminated through open-access datasets and a visualization toolkit to support public literacy initiatives, aligning with the program’s emphasis on the societal consequences of media technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on research and research methods in communication, and that spans the study of mass communication/media studies, old and new media technologies, social and political applications, and speech communication and rhetoric. Includes instruction in quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing personalized care plans for elderly patients with multiple chronic conditions, a population often underrepresented in clinical trials despite their complex healthcare needs. Current approaches to predicting adverse events—such as polypharmacy complications, falls, or hospital readmissions—rely on generalized models that fail to account for the heterogeneity of aging-related physiological changes, social determinants of health, and comorbidities. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models capable of integrating multi-modal geriatric health data, including longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), medication histories, wearable device outputs, and patient-reported outcomes. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing large-scale EHR datasets (spanning 10+ years) to extract geriatric-specific features, followed by training ensemble ML algorithms to identify risk patterns and simulate interventions. Deep learning architectures will be tested for their ability to model temporal relationships in medication adherence and disease progression, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will parse unstructured clinical notes for social and cognitive risk factors. The HPC environment is essential for managing data volumes (>100 TB), parallelizing hyperparameter tuning across thousands of model iterations, and conducting real-time simulations of care pathway outcomes. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for adverse event risk stratification, optimized medication reconciliation protocols accounting for age-related pharmacokinetic changes, and dynamic care plan recommendations adaptable to individual patient trajectories. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of geriatric-specific datasets, this work will advance evidence-based precision nursing practices, inform policy for aging populations, and reduce preventable complications in vulnerable elderly patients.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and tuning of high-performance automotive engines and vehicle systems, addressing the growing complexity of modifying modern powertrains for competitive and custom applications. Current approaches to engine enhancement rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping and dynamometer testing, which are costly, time-intensive, and limited in their ability to explore multidimensional design spaces. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate combustion dynamics, exhaust gas flow, thermal stress distributions, and suspension kinematics under high-load conditions. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model air-fuel mixing and exhaust scavenging efficiency across custom intake and exhaust geometries, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict component fatigue in turbocharged engines operating at extreme boost pressures. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on dynamometer datasets to correlate simulated parameters with empirical power output and emissions data, enabling predictive optimization of camshaft timing, fuel injection maps, and forced induction configurations. These multi-physics simulations will account for transient interactions between modified engine subsystems, a critical gap in current single-domain modeling tools. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these resource-intensive computations across parametric variations in displacement, compression ratio, and aftermarket component combinations. Expected outcomes include a framework for virtual prototyping of performance engines, reducing physical testing cycles by an estimated 40-60%, and generating actionable insights into trade-offs between horsepower gains, drivetrain reliability, and regulatory compliance. This work will directly support curriculum development in computational engine tuning, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-driven automotive research. The resulting open-source models aim to democratize access to high-fidelity simulation tools for small-scale mechanics and custom fabricators, fostering innovation in the high-performance automotive sector.
cip_title: High Performance and Custom Engine Technician/ Mechanic
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to increase the power of diesel and automotive engines; enhance the performance of automobiles; and repair, service, and maintain high performance vehicles. Includes instruction in adding performance accessories; modifying powertrains; tuning custom engines, suspension, and exhaust systems; and using dynamometers and other diagnostic equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research by analyzing the structural and semantic evolution of judicial decision-making patterns across transnational jurisdictions. While legal scholarship traditionally relies on qualitative methods, the increasing volume and complexity of case law—coupled with the need to identify latent biases and systemic inconsistencies in judicial reasoning—demand scalable computational approaches. The research focuses on developing a machine learning framework to process multilingual legal texts from supranational courts (e.g., European Court of Human Rights, Inter-American Court of Human Rights) and national high courts, spanning 150 years of jurisprudence. By integrating natural language processing (NLP) techniques with graph-theoretic network analysis, the project aims to model how legal concepts propagate, mutate, and interact within and across jurisdictions. Key computational challenges include handling noisy historical texts, resolving cross-lingual legal terminology discrepancies, and constructing dynamic knowledge graphs to trace precedent influence. The HPC environment is critical for training transformer-based models on terabyte-scale legal corpora and simulating hypothetical legal reasoning scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database mapping temporal and jurisdictional shifts in legal argumentation, (2) quantitative metrics for assessing judicial consistency, and (3) prototype tools to visualize precedent cascades in complex litigation contexts. This work bridges computational social science and legal informatics, offering novel methodologies for evaluating legal systems’ responsiveness to societal change while circumventing the constraints of manual doctrinal analysis. Results could inform judicial training programs, treaty design, and reforms addressing algorithmic transparency in automated legal decision-making systems.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program in one or more of the legal research or advanced practice fields.

abstract: Dairy production systems face challenges in optimizing feed efficiency and milk composition, which are critical for both animal health and product quality. Current models of ruminant metabolism and nutrient utilization lack resolution to account for the complex interactions between host physiology, microbial communities in the rumen, and dietary components. This project aims to develop a high-resolution, multi-scale computational model integrating genomic, metabolomic, and environmental data to predict how variations in feed formulations impact dairy cattle metabolism and milk output. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ flux balance analysis and agent-based modeling to simulate rumen microbial dynamics alongside host metabolic networks. Machine learning techniques will be applied to parameterize these models using existing datasets on cattle genomics, microbiome sequencing, and longitudinal milk composition records. The computational framework will enable stochastic simulations to assess variability in nutrient absorption and methane byproduct formation under different dietary regimes. This approach addresses a critical gap in precision dairy nutrition by providing a systems-level understanding of feed-host-microbiome interactions. Expected outcomes include identifying optimal feed formulations that enhance milk yield, fatty acid profiles, and animal health while minimizing metabolic disorders. The models will be validated against experimental trials conducted in collaboration with dairy research farms. By elucidating the biochemical pathways governing nutrient utilization, this work will advance strategies for sustainable dairy production and inform innovations in feed science. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the computational complexity of multi-omic integration and large-scale simulations, which exceed the capacity of local institutional resources.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of dairy animals and the production and handling of dairy products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: Healthcare environments significantly influence patient outcomes, yet existing design frameworks often lack integration of dynamic, data-driven approaches to optimize healing. Current methodologies rely on static architectural principles or retrospective evaluations, limiting real-time adaptability to evolving clinical needs, patient demographics, and environmental variables. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate and iteratively refine healthcare spaces using high-performance computing (HPC). The research leverages agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between patients, staff, and built environments, coupled with machine learning (ML) to analyze multi-modal datasets (e.g., biometric feedback, spatial utilization patterns, and environmental sensor data). Parametric modeling tools will generate design alternatives that balance operational efficiency, patient well-being, and clinical workflows. HPC resources are critical for scaling ABM simulations to hospital-level complexity, training ML models on heterogeneous datasets, and running iterative optimizations across thousands of design permutations. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific design features—such as spatial layout, lighting, and material acoustics—to measurable health outcomes (e.g., stress reduction, mobility improvement). Additionally, the project aims to produce an open-access generative design toolkit enabling architects and healthcare providers to prototype evidence-based environments. By integrating computational science with architectural practice, this work advances a novel paradigm for healthcare design that is responsive to both human needs and systemic constraints. The resulting frameworks will support the creation of adaptive, healing-oriented spaces, ultimately reducing recovery times and operational costs while addressing gaps in interdisciplinary research at the intersection of design, healthcare, and data science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and performance of healthcare environments to optimize healing. Includes instruction in interior design, architecture, healing sciences, healthcare environments, human-centered design, and healthcare delivery.

abstract: Adolescence is marked by dynamic interactions between neurocognitive development and environmental influences, which shape long-term psychological outcomes. However, the mechanisms linking these processes—particularly how time-varying patterns of brain maturation interact with social or environmental stressors to influence decision-making and emotional regulation—remain poorly understood. This project aims to develop a computational framework integrating longitudinal neuroimaging, behavioral, and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data to model these interactions across adolescence. The primary challenge lies in analyzing high-dimensional, multimodal datasets with temporally nested variables (e.g., neural connectivity changes, daily social interactions) while accounting for individual differences in developmental trajectories. To address this, we propose using hierarchical Bayesian models and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture nonlinear developmental dynamics and time-lagged effects between neural, behavioral, and environmental variables. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) parallelized parameter estimation of Bayesian growth mixture models across 800+ participants from the ABCD Study; (2) training RNNs on dense temporal data (10,000+ EMA entries) to predict emotional regulation outcomes from concurrent neural and social variables; and (3) large-scale simulations testing how stochastic environmental inputs interact with maturational timing in a validated neurodevelopmental model. Expected outcomes include identifying critical periods when specific neural systems are most sensitive to environmental inputs, characterizing subtypes of developmental trajectories associated with risk/resilience, and generating testable hypotheses about windows for targeted interventions. By bridging computational neuroscience and developmental psychology methods, this work will advance precision models of adolescent development while providing open-source tools for analyzing high-frequency multimodal developmental data. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impossible with standard workstations, given the need for GPU-accelerated model training and daily Monte Carlo simulations over 12-month developmental windows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from adolescence to adulthood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural identity and intersectional gender narratives across Latin American and Caribbean digital archives through advanced computational text analysis. The research addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing vast, multilingual corpora—including historical newspapers, literary works, and grassroots publications—to trace evolving representations of marginalized communities and hybrid cultural expressions. Current methodologies in regional studies lack scalable tools to process heterogeneous, non-standardized texts spanning Spanish, Portuguese, Creole languages, and indigenous linguistic variants. Our approach integrates transformer-based natural language processing models optimized for low-resource languages with graph-based network analysis to map semantic shifts and discourse networks across temporal and geographic axes. High-performance computing resources are critical for training custom multilingual language models on distributed text datasets (>10 TB), conducting parallelized sentiment and topic coherence analyses, and simulating cultural transmission dynamics via agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of 20th-century Caribbean feminist writings, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural hybridity in postcolonial contexts, and visual analytics tools to contextualize identity formation processes. By enabling large-scale interrogation of underrepresented narratives, this work aims to redefine methodological paradigms in area studies while informing contemporary debates on cultural preservation and inclusive historiography in digitization initiatives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in commercial meat-cutting workflows through advanced simulation and predictive modeling. While manual meat cutting remains a skill-intensive practice, current training and operational frameworks lack data-driven tools to optimize yield, reduce waste, and standardize precision across diverse meat products. The research problem centers on developing computational models that simulate the physical and structural properties of animal tissues under varying cutting parameters, such as blade angle, force, and temperature, to identify optimal techniques for different meat types (e.g., beef, poultry, smoked products). A secondary focus involves analyzing historical sales and waste data to predict demand-driven cutting strategies, minimizing surplus while maintaining quality. The computational approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) to model tissue mechanics, machine learning algorithms to correlate cutting patterns with yield outcomes, and agent-based modeling to simulate real-world shop-floor dynamics. High-resolution 3D scans of meat morphology will inform tissue models, while GPU-accelerated training will refine predictive algorithms using datasets spanning regional market trends, seasonal demand fluctuations, and regulatory constraints. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these resource-intensive simulations across thousands of permutations, enabling real-time parameter adjustments. Expected outcomes include a decision-support framework for butchers to maximize yield efficiency, reduce training time for novice cutters via virtual reality (VR)-compatible simulations, and dynamic inventory management tools aligned with sanitation and storage regulations. By bridging computational analytics with artisanal practice, this project aims to modernize meat-cutting operations, enhance sustainability through waste reduction, and establish a template for integrating HPC-driven optimization into vocational trades. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools for small-scale butchers and collaborations with industry partners to validate models in commercial settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, cut, and package animal meat products in commercial establishments and to function as licensed meat cutters/butchers.  Includes instruction in product recognition for beef, veal, lamb, pork, poultry, and fancy and smoked meats; retail and wholesale cutting and specialty cuts; packaging and counter display; shop safety; meat sanitation, storage and rotation; quality control; meat handling laws and regulations; and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision health strategies in family practice nursing by analyzing complex, multi-dimensional datasets related to familial health outcomes. Family nurses require robust tools to assess interrelated biological, behavioral, and environmental factors influencing health across generations, yet existing analytical methods often fail to account for the dynamic, non-linear interactions within family systems. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and socioenvironmental metrics to model family health trajectories. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be applied to identify predictive patterns of chronic disease risk, care utilization disparities, and intervention responsiveness within family clusters. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parallel processing of high-dimensional datasets spanning thousands of families, while agent-based modeling will simulate longitudinal health outcomes under varying care scenarios. Key deliverables include open-source tools for family-centric risk stratification and a repository of optimized predictive models tailored to diverse demographic contexts. Anticipated outcomes include novel insights into transgenerational determinants of conditions like diabetes and hypertension, as well as evidence-based protocols for personalized preventive care. By enhancing computational capacity to analyze family-level health data, this work will directly support nurses in designing targeted interventions that address systemic health inequities while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of nursing science and computational epidemiology. The requested resources will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, secure storage for sensitive health data, and scalable infrastructure for collaborative tool development with clinical partners.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying skill acquisition in structured learning environments, leveraging computational modeling to bridge gaps between educational theory and cognitive neuroscience. Traditional pedagogical frameworks often lack empirical validation at the neurocomputational level, limiting their ability to adapt to individual learners’ dynamic cognitive states. To address this, the research will develop large-scale neural network models simulating how cortical and subcortical systems interact during skill mastery, with a focus on domains such as procedural learning (e.g., mathematics, music) and metacognitive regulation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate biologically plausible neural architectures, parameterize models using empirical neuroimaging datasets (e.g., fMRI, EEG), and run iterative optimization algorithms to test hypotheses about synaptic plasticity and attentional resource allocation during learning. The computational framework will integrate reinforcement learning paradigms with dynamic systems theory to map how instructional pacing, feedback timing, and task complexity influence neural efficiency and behavioral outcomes. Expected outcomes include predictive models that quantify trade-offs between cognitive load and skill retention, offering actionable insights for designing adaptive learning technologies. By elucidating how specific instructional strategies alter neural circuit dynamics, this work aims to establish a neurocomputational foundation for personalized education tools, transcending one-size-fits-all pedagogies. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—synthesizing education, computational neuroscience, and machine learning—addresses a critical gap in understanding the biological basis of learning optimization, with implications for curriculum design, educational software development, and policy frameworks aimed at reducing disparities in skill acquisition rates. HPC resources will enable the scaling of simulations to population-level variability, ensuring models capture neurodiverse learning trajectories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory and practice of learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: The management of chronic diseases in adult populations presents significant challenges due to the complex interplay of physiological, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors influencing patient outcomes. Current approaches to risk stratification and personalized care planning in adult health nursing often lack the precision required to address this complexity, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and preventable hospital readmissions. This project proposes the development of a predictive computational framework to optimize care strategies for adults with chronic conditions, such as heart failure or diabetes, by integrating multi-modal patient data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), including clinical measurements, medication adherence patterns, and social determinants of health, alongside longitudinal outcomes data. Machine learning models, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, will be trained to identify high-risk patients, predict decompensation events, and simulate the impact of tailored nursing interventions. Computational demands arise from the need to process heterogeneous datasets encompassing millions of data points across diverse patient cohorts while maintaining temporal resolution for trend analysis. The HPC environment will enable parallelized model training, hyperparameter optimization, and sensitivity analyses to ensure robustness across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that quantifies individualized risk profiles and recommends evidence-based care pathways. This work will advance nursing practice by providing data-driven methods to prioritize interventions, reduce avoidable hospitalizations, and allocate clinical resources more effectively. By bridging computational science and nursing research, the project aims to establish scalable frameworks for personalized adult healthcare while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in health informatics. Successful implementation will require dedicated GPU nodes and high-memory computing infrastructure to handle the computational intensity of multi-task learning architectures and large-scale simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide general care for adult patients. Includes instruction in adult primary care, adult pathophysiology, clinical management of medication and treatments, patient assessment and education, patient referral, and planning adult health maintenance programs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools for modeling and synthesizing immersive 3D sound environments, addressing the challenge of creating spatially dynamic audio experiences for interactive media and live performance. While spatial audio technologies have grown in prominence, existing methods for real-time sound propagation modeling and adaptive synthesis remain computationally prohibitive, limiting their accessibility and scalability in artistic applications. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) acoustic simulations, enabling efficient modeling of complex virtual environments with frequency-dependent material absorption and diffraction effects. Concurrently, machine learning frameworks will be implemented to train neural networks on spectral and spatial audio features, optimizing adaptive synthesis algorithms for dynamic listener interactions. The computational workflow will integrate these components into a GPU-accelerated pipeline, validated through case studies in augmented-reality music performance and interactive sound installations. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to overcome latency and fidelity barriers in real-time spatial audio processing, facilitating novel creative workflows for composers and sound designers. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for parametric spatial audio rendering, a dataset of annotated 3D acoustic environments, and performance benchmarks for music-oriented HPC applications. This work bridges computational acoustics and artistic practice, offering scalable solutions for emerging domains such as VR/AR-enhanced performances and AI-driven interactive composition. The resource allocation will directly support graduate student researchers in music technology while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations between performing arts and computational science communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creative aspects of the blending of music and technology; and that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the composition, recording, synthesis, and performance of music; audio-visual production; scoring for film and multimedia; and software and multimedia development. Includes instruction in music theory, music history, composition, acoustics, recording technology, computer composition, electronic music synthesis, technology-based performance, 3D sound and spatial audio, and music business and law.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between attentional allocation and decision-making under uncertainty using large-scale computational modeling. While traditional behavioral experiments have provided foundational insights, they struggle to disentangle the nonlinear interactions of cognitive processes in real-world scenarios. To address this, we propose developing a parallelizable neural network framework that simulates hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) mechanisms during multi-task decision-making. The model will integrate drift-diffusion processes with adaptive reward prediction error algorithms to capture individual differences in uncertainty tolerance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three core components: (1) Bayesian parameter estimation across high-dimensional spaces using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods applied to behavioral datasets from 10,000+ trial sessions, (2) real-time synchronization of simulated neural ensembles across distributed compute nodes to model population-level decision dynamics, and (3) evolutionary optimization of network architectures through genetic algorithms requiring population sizes >1,000 per generation. Initial pilot data demonstrate that conventional computing infrastructure becomes prohibitive beyond 200 parallel model instantiations due to memory constraints in maintaining trial-by-trace synaptic weight matrices. The requested resources will enable scaling to 50,000 unique agent-based simulations across diverse environmental uncertainty profiles, generating approximately 8TB of synthetic neural activity patterns for comparative validation against fMRI and eye-tracking data from ongoing experiments. Expected outcomes include a novel computational account of how prefrontal-basal ganglia interactions trade off exploration-exploitation strategies under varying noise conditions, with implications for developing quantitative biomarkers of cognitive flexibility. All models and simulation pipelines will be made open-source through the Psychology Computational Models Repository, establishing a community resource for testing alternative theories of adaptive decision-making.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in research and experimental psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Respiratory care therapy faces a critical challenge in personalizing mechanical ventilation strategies for patients with heterogeneous lung pathologies, such as acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Current clinical protocols rely on generalized algorithms, which often fail to account for dynamic, patient-specific biomechanical factors, leading to suboptimal outcomes and ventilator-induced lung injury. This project proposes a computational framework to model individualized respiratory mechanics and predict optimal ventilator settings by integrating high-fidelity simulations of lung airflow, tissue deformation, and gas exchange. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) simulations, informed by patient-specific thoracic CT scans, pulmonary function tests, and real-time ventilator data. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational cost by training surrogate models on simulation outputs, enabling rapid parameter optimization for clinical decision support. Key deliverables include an open-source software pipeline for simulating multiscale lung mechanics and a validated predictive model for recommending personalized positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) and tidal volume settings. The computational demands are significant, requiring parallelized processing of 3D meshes with >10 million elements, iterative solvers for nonlinear fluid-structure interactions, and large-scale hyperparameter tuning for neural networks. Successfully linking patient-specific lung dynamics to ventilator responses could revolutionize precision respiratory care, reducing morbidity associated with mechanical ventilation. This work bridges clinical respiratory therapy, biomechanical engineering, and computational science, offering a novel paradigm for resource allocation in critical care environments while advancing foundational knowledge in cardiopulmonary pathophysiology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical drivers of cellular dysfunction in traumatic brain injury (TBI) through multiscale computational modeling, integrating neurophysiology, biophysics, and machine learning. Despite advances in TBI clinical management, the mechanistic links between mechanical impact forces, microscale tissue deformation, and downstream biochemical cascades remain poorly characterized, limiting predictive diagnostics and targeted therapies. The research will develop a novel computational framework coupling finite element models of whole-brain dynamics with agent-based simulations of neuronal membrane integrity and calcium signaling under strain. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatiotemporal interactions across scales—from millisecond mechanical transients during impact to hour-long pathophysiological responses in neural networks. Custom GPU-optimized algorithms will simulate tissue deformation at 0.1 mm resolution across anatomically accurate brain geometries derived from clinical MRI datasets, while parallelized Monte Carlo methods model stochastic ion channel behaviors in >10^6 simulated neurons. Machine learning classifiers will identify deformation patterns predictive of axonal injury biomarkers in paired neuroimaging and proteomic data from a TBI patient cohort (n=120). Expected outcomes include: 1) the first open-source platform linking macroscale impact mechanics to subcellular neuropathology, 2) validated predictive models of strain thresholds for blood-brain barrier compromise, and 3) candidate mechanical biomarkers for rapid triage in TBI cases. By elucidating how mechanical energy translates to cellular damage, this work could inform next-generation neuroprotective devices and personalized impact-risk assessments in contact sports and military settings. The computational pipeline will be adaptable to other mechanopathological processes in neurodegeneration or cardiovascular health.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical professional preparation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the ethical verification and contextual analysis of visual media in photojournalism, addressing the growing challenges posed by misinformation and AI-generated content. As digital photography and generative models advance, verifying the authenticity of images and videos while maintaining narrative integrity has become critically complex. Current manual methods are insufficient for analyzing high-resolution media at scale, particularly in time-sensitive news environments. This research proposes the integration of machine learning (ML) and high-performance computing (HPC) to automate and augment workflows for detecting manipulated content, cross-referencing metadata, and reconstructing the provenance of visual assets. The project will employ convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models trained on diverse datasets of authentic and altered imagery to identify anomalies in pixel patterns, lighting inconsistencies, and metadata tampering. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 4K/8K video frames, rapid model iteration, and large-scale simulations of manipulation techniques to improve detection accuracy. Additionally, graph-based algorithms will map the lifecycle of visual content—from capture to publication—using timestamped geolocation data, device signatures, and editorial logs. By automating labor-intensive verification tasks, this system aims to reduce human error and accelerate the validation process for news organizations. Outcomes include open-source tools for real-time forensic analysis, a benchmark dataset for training ethical AI models in journalism, and scalable workflows to support photojournalists in maintaining public trust. The project bridges computational innovation and journalistic ethics, advancing the responsible use of emerging technologies while preserving the integrity of visual storytelling in the digital age.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of still and motion photography in journalism and prepares individuals to function as news photographers and photographic editors. Includes instruction in photography, journalism, studio procedures and techniques, camera and equipment operation and technique, news editing, print and film editing, news scene composition, subject surveillance, media law and policy, news team field operations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to optimize hazardous materials (hazmat) transportation risk assessment and emergency response planning using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current hazmat routing models often rely on static risk metrics or simplified environmental datasets, which fail to account for dynamic variables such as real-time traffic, weather patterns, or evolving population densities. This limitation hinders proactive risk mitigation and complicates emergency response coordination. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning-enhanced simulation platform that dynamically models multi-hazard interactions (e.g., chemical spills intersecting with flood zones) and evaluates mitigation strategies under uncertainty. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate hazmat transport scenarios with Monte Carlo methods to quantify probabilistic risks across diverse environmental and infrastructural conditions. High-resolution geospatial data, including real-time IoT sensor inputs and climate projections, will be integrated through parallelized data pipelines. The HPC environment is critical for processing large-scale spatiotemporal datasets, running ensemble simulations of rare but high-consequence events, and training deep learning models to predict cascading failure pathways in urban-rural interface zones. Expected outcomes include a risk prioritization tool that identifies vulnerable corridors, quantifies economic and public health impacts, and recommends adaptive routing protocols. The computational framework will be validated against historical incident data from national hazmat registries and tested through collaborative scenarios with regional emergency management agencies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance decision-support systems for hazmat logistics while aligning with the program’s interdisciplinary focus on information systems, environmental health, and management science. Results will inform policy updates and provide scalable computational methods for emerging challenges in hazardous materials management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing, monitoring, and enforcing hazardous materials management and removal. Includes instruction in environmental science, environmental health, human behavior, economics, management science, information systems and applications, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the thermal and power efficiency of next-generation computer processors through advanced computational modeling and simulation. As processor architectures scale toward smaller transistor sizes and higher component densities, managing heat dissipation and power distribution becomes increasingly complex, directly impacting device reliability and performance. Traditional empirical testing methods are insufficient for exploring the vast design space of modern multi-core processors and heterogenous computing units, necessitating high-fidelity simulations to guide hardware design. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model thermal gradients, material stress, and power delivery networks at the microarchitecture level. These simulations will integrate machine learning-driven optimization to iteratively refine cooling solutions, substrate materials, and power gating configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multi-physics interactions across nanometer-scale geometries and millisecond-scale operational cycles, which require parallelized solvers and large memory allocations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting thermal runaway thresholds, identifying optimal layouts for on-chip cooling structures, and proposing material interfaces to mitigate electromigration in high-current conditions. This work will directly support the development of energy-efficient processors for high-performance computing clusters and edge devices, while advancing methodologies for virtual prototyping in computer hardware design. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ design permutations, reducing reliance on physical prototyping and accelerating iteration cycles for industry partners in semiconductor manufacturing. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and collaboration with hardware testing laboratories to bridge computational predictions with empirical validation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociolinguistic and cultural impacts of 19th-century missionary print media on Indigenous Pacific Islander communities, a niche interdisciplinary area within missiology and digital humanities. Missionary-produced texts—including vernacular translations, educational materials, and religious tracts—played a pivotal role in mediating colonial encounters, yet their large-scale linguistic patterns and semantic networks remain underexplored due to the volume and fragmentation of archival sources. The research problem centers on disentangling how these texts both preserved and transformed Indigenous knowledge systems, while negotiating power asymmetries. Computational methods will be applied to a corpus of digitized missionary publications (15,000+ pages in English and Polynesian languages), combining NLP techniques—such as topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and word embedding—with network analysis to map lexical borrowing, conceptual hybridization, and paratextual framing strategies. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual OCR outputs, training custom transformer models for low-resource languages, and simulating semantic shifts across temporal and geographic axes. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for analyzing historical intercultural texts, (2) visualizations of how mission presses reconfigured Indigenous epistemologies through lexical innovation, and (3) quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric narratives of cultural erasure by highlighting bidirectional adaptation in missionary-Indigenous discourse. The project will produce an open-access database and computational toolkit tailored for missiological research, enabling scholars to interrogate the complex interplay of religion, language, and colonialism at unprecedented scale. By integrating HPC-driven humanities methodologies with mission studies, this work advances interdisciplinary frameworks for decolonial historiography while expanding the technical frontiers of digital missiology.
cip_title: Missions/ Missionary Studies and Missiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in missions, missionary studies, and missiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize sustainable apparel supply chain operations through the development of a machine learning-driven framework for dynamic demand forecasting and resource allocation. The apparel industry faces mounting pressure to reduce overproduction and waste, yet existing models struggle to reconcile real-time consumer behavior data with complex variables such as seasonal trends, sustainability metrics, and multi-channel inventory flows. Our work addresses this gap by integrating heterogeneous datasets—including social media sentiment analysis, RFID-tracked in-store traffic patterns, and environmental impact scores—to predict demand volatility at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational challenge lies in processing petabyte-scale datasets from global retail partners while maintaining sub-hourly model updates across 50+ product categories. We propose a hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks to map supplier-retailer dependencies, transformer-based models for cross-channel trend synthesis, and agent-based simulations to stress-test allocation strategies under climate disruption scenarios. High-performance computing resources are critical for training ensemble models on historical sales data (2018-2023) spanning 15 markets, as well as running Monte Carlo simulations to quantify carbon footprint trade-offs under various production scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that reduces excess inventory by 18-22% in pilot implementations while maintaining 98% service-level agreements, directly addressing the $210B annual loss from apparel overstock. The project will further establish computational benchmarks for ethical AI in fashion operations, creating transferable methodologies for balancing profitability with circular economy objectives in fast-moving consumer goods sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of apparel and accessories. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, apparel technologies, distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation and operational efficiency within fine and studio arts organizations through advanced computational modeling. Art institutions, such as galleries, museums, and community arts programs, face complex decisions in balancing financial constraints, spatial logistics, and audience engagement strategies. Traditional methods often rely on qualitative assessments or limited datasets, leading to suboptimal outcomes in sustainability and community impact. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to analyze multi-source data—including visitor demographics, exhibition attendance patterns, environmental sensor metrics, and financial records—to model and simulate operational scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical and real-time datasets to predict visitor flow, assess climate control efficiency in preservation-sensitive spaces, and optimize spatial layouts for exhibitions. Agent-based models will further simulate staffing and funding allocation under variable conditions, such as fluctuating attendance or grant availability. By leveraging HPC resources, these computationally intensive simulations will enable dynamic, large-scale analyses that account for interdependencies between variables, a task infeasible with standard computing infrastructure. The expected outcomes include actionable insights for reducing operational costs, enhancing visitor experiences, and improving environmental sustainability in art facilities. Additionally, the project aims to produce open-source tools tailored to arts management, enabling smaller organizations to adopt data-driven strategies. This work bridges gaps between computational analytics and arts administration, offering a novel approach to sustaining cultural institutions in an era of increasing fiscal and ecological pressures.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage fine and studio art organizations, operations, and facilities. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; public relations and arts advocacy; arts law; and applications to specific arts activities such as galleries, museums, studios, foundations, and community organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of complex anatomical and microstructural relationships in veterinary species through high-performance computing (HPC)-driven modeling and analysis. A critical challenge in veterinary anatomy is resolving how cellular and tissue-scale structural adaptations—such as neuronal network organization, musculoskeletal biomechanics, or pathological tissue remodeling—relate to organism-level physiological functions or disease states. Traditional histological and imaging methods lack the capacity to integrate multiscale structural data or simulate dynamic interactions across biological hierarchies. To address this, we propose leveraging HPC resources to develop 3D computational models of anatomical systems in species of veterinary relevance, including equine, canine, and bovine subjects. These models will integrate ultrastructural data from electron microscopy, diffusion tensor imaging, and molecular histology to simulate biomechanical stresses, electrophysiological signaling, or immune-cell trafficking in healthy and diseased tissues. Machine learning pipelines will be deployed to automate the analysis of terabyte-scale imaging datasets, identifying patterns in tissue microarchitecture linked to clinical outcomes. Molecular dynamics simulations will further probe how subcellular structures, such as ion channels or extracellular matrix components, influence tissue resilience or degeneration. The computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to reduce runtime for large parameter-space explorations. Expected outcomes include predictive models of disease progression in conditions like osteoarthritis or neuropathies, as well as open-source tools for veterinary researchers to correlate anatomical variants with therapeutic responses. By bridging microanatomical features to macro-scale functions, this work will directly inform surgical planning, regenerative therapies, and species-specific biomedical device design, enhancing translational outcomes in veterinary care and comparative medicine.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of small and large animal cellular, organ, tissue, and body systems and their relation to physiologic function, disease, and therapeutic treatment. Includes instruction in histology, ultrastructure, molecular biology, biochemistry, developmental biology, neuroscience, electrophysiology, electron microscopy, computer imaging, and applications to specific species.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven pedagogical tools for multilingual classrooms. A critical challenge in bilingual education lies in designing instruction that dynamically responds to learners’ evolving linguistic proficiencies, cultural backgrounds, and cognitive loads. Current approaches often rely on static curricular frameworks or generalized assessments, which fail to account for the complex interplay of sociolinguistic, cognitive, and instructional variables in real-world classrooms. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating longitudinal classroom interaction datasets—including speech, writing samples, and engagement metrics—with cognitive models of bilingual language acquisition. Large-scale natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze multilingual discourse patterns across 10,000+ hours of annotated classroom recordings in Spanish-English and Mandarin-English contexts. Concurrently, neural network architectures will simulate the impact of code-switching frequency, vocabulary complexity, and instructional scaffolding on learning outcomes. These models require HPC resources to process terabytes of multimodal data, train deep learning architectures with cross-lingual embeddings, and run parallelized simulations of instructional scenarios under diverse sociolinguistic parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for optimizing language allocation (L1/L2) in content-based instruction, (2) evidence-based thresholds for cognitive load in simultaneous literacy development, and (3) open-source tools for generating differentiated bilingual lesson plans. By quantifying how specific instructional strategies interact with individual learner trajectories, this work will directly inform teacher preparation programs on data-supported practices for heterogeneous multilingual classrooms. The computational infrastructure will enable scaling to underrepresented language pairs and low-resource educational contexts in subsequent phases.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to bilingual/bicultural children or adults, and/or the design and implementation of educational programs having the goal of producing bilingual/bicultural individuals. Includes preparation to serve as teachers and administrators in bilingual/bicultural education programs.

abstract: Musculoskeletal neoplasms present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their molecular heterogeneity, dynamic interactions with surrounding tissues, and variable responses to existing therapies. Current approaches to treatment planning and outcome prediction often rely on static clinical or imaging data, which inadequately capture the complex biomechanical and biological interplay driving tumor progression and therapy resistance. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing integrative computational models that simulate tumor behavior across molecular, cellular, and tissue-level scales. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to create multi-omics network models to identify genomic and proteomic drivers of tumor aggressiveness and metastasis, coupled with biomechanical finite element models to predict tumor-induced bone remodeling and biomechanical failure risks under therapeutic loads. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to multimodal datasets—including radiomics, histopathology, genomics, and patient-specific biomechanics—to stratify patients by predicted treatment response and optimize personalized therapy regimens. Key computational challenges include managing terabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing multi-physics simulations, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data. The HPC infrastructure will enable iterative model calibration using evolutionary algorithms and large-scale parameter sweeps to account for biological variability. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for sarcoma progression, tools to simulate radiotherapy and surgical outcomes in silico, and actionable biomarkers for therapy personalization. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs and advance precision oncology by bridging computational discovery with translational applications. By quantifying previously intractable interactions between tumor biology and biomechanics, the project aims to reduce complications such as pathologic fractures and improve survival rates for patients with advanced musculoskeletal cancers.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal neoplasm, and the application of cancer therapy regimes.

abstract: Health care systems face escalating demands for efficient resource allocation amidst dynamic challenges such as fluctuating patient volumes, workforce shortages, and evolving public health crises. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the granularity and scalability to model complex, system-wide interactions or rapidly test policy interventions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform to optimize resource allocation strategies across health care networks. The research will employ agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation techniques to replicate multi-scale operational dynamics, including patient flow, staff scheduling, equipment utilization, and facility capacity constraints. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict demand surges, identify bottlenecks, and evaluate adaptive policies under scenarios such as pandemic waves, natural disasters, or budget reductions. The computational framework will leverage large-scale datasets from electronic health records, staffing logs, and supply chain inventories, requiring parallel processing for real-time scenario testing and sensitivity analyses. By simulating thousands of allocation strategies across diverse care settings, the project aims to quantify trade-offs between cost, equity, and clinical outcomes while accounting for regulatory and ethical constraints. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for balancing resource investments, mitigating operational risks, and enhancing health system resilience. The platform will provide administrators with open-source tools to visualize cascading impacts of allocation decisions and prioritize evidence-based interventions. This work aligns with national priorities to strengthen health care infrastructure through data-driven management, with potential applications in emergency preparedness, telehealth expansion, and value-based care delivery. Results will be disseminated through policy white papers and decision support modules adaptable to rural, urban, and safety-net health systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, plan, and manage health care operations and services within health care facilities and across health care systems. Includes instruction in planning, business management, financial management, public relations, human resources management, health care systems operation and management, health care resource allocation and policy making, health law and regulations, and applications to specific types of health care services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize private security operations through advanced computational modeling, addressing gaps in proactive threat mitigation for Security and Loss Prevention Services. Current security strategies often rely on reactive measures, historical incident data, and static patrol patterns, which struggle to adapt to dynamic, real-world environments. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including geospatial crime trends, IoT sensor inputs from secured sites, and behavioral anomaly detection from surveillance systems—into a unified model capable of forecasting high-risk scenarios and recommending adaptive resource allocation. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model spatial-temporal relationships between threat factors, reinforcement learning to simulate patrol route optimization under uncertainty, and agent-based modeling to stress-test security protocols against synthetic threat scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets spanning urban crime records, client-site sensor logs, and simulated adversarial behavior, while enabling real-time parameter tuning for evolving threat landscapes.
