Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating risk heatmaps, dynamic scheduling algorithms for security personnel, and probabilistic forecasts of asset vulnerability under varying conditions. The project bridges computational criminology, operations research, and IoT analytics, offering private security providers a scalable method to transition from generalized patrols to intelligence-driven deployment. By leveraging HPC to handle the combinatorial complexity of threat variables, this work aims to establish a new paradigm in loss prevention, reducing response latency by 30-50% in simulated environments while maintaining compliance with privacy-preserving data governance standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine inspection, patrol and crime prevention services for private clients. Includes instruction in the provision of personal protection as well as property security.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for community-based organizations (CBOs) addressing systemic inequities in urban service delivery. Many CBOs operate with limited resources and fragmented data, hindering their ability to equitably prioritize neighborhoods with overlapping vulnerabilities (e.g., housing instability, food insecurity, and healthcare access gaps). While existing studies emphasize qualitative approaches, there is a critical need for computational tools that synthesize large-scale socioeconomic datasets to model service gaps and simulate intervention impacts. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-source data—including public census records, municipal service usage logs, and community health surveys—across a 10-year period for seven major U.S. cities. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate how different resource distribution policies affect neighborhood-level outcomes under varying demographic and economic scenarios. Network analysis will map inter-organizational collaboration patterns to identify bottlenecks in service coordination. Machine learning classifiers (e.g., random forests, gradient-boosted trees) will predict emerging vulnerability hotspots using real-time data streams. Computational demands arise from the scale of geospatial-temporal data (~50 TB), the complexity of ABM iterations (10,000+ parallel simulations), and the need for rapid retraining of predictive models. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for CBOs to dynamically assess resource trade-offs and a policy report quantifying the equity impacts of algorithmically guided allocation strategies. By integrating computational social science methods with community advocacy practices, this work aims to bridge technical and grassroots approaches to systemic change, ensuring that marginalized populations are prioritized in data-driven decision-making. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive simulations and enabling reproducible, large-scale analysis beyond the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, principles, and practice of organizing and providing services to communities. May prepare individuals to apply such knowledge and skills in community service positions.

abstract: This research project addresses the challenge of designing sustainable, structurally complex textile artworks through computational modeling and simulation, bridging gaps between traditional craft and advanced computational methods. Current approaches in fiber arts rely heavily on manual experimentation, limiting scalability and precision when predicting material behavior, structural integrity, or dye interaction in multidimensional textile systems. To overcome these constraints, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multi-scale simulation framework for analyzing fibrous materials under dynamic environmental and mechanical conditions. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model dye diffusion and pigment interaction across diverse textile substrates, while finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate stress distribution in woven and non-woven architectures to optimize tensile strength and flexibility. Machine learning models, trained on datasets of historical and synthetic textile patterns, will generate novel weaving algorithms that balance aesthetic intent with material efficiency. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution 3D simulations of multi-layered textiles and iterating generative designs across parameter spaces impractical for local computing. Expected outcomes include an open-access computational toolkit for artists and researchers, enabling predictive design of textiles with reduced material waste and enhanced functional properties. This work aims to advance the field of fiber arts by establishing data-driven methodologies for innovation, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational scientists and textile artists, and expanding the creative potential of sustainable textile practices. The project’s computational workflows will also contribute to broader discourse on digital craft, offering replicable models for integrating HPC into material-based visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by constructing art works from woven or non-woven fabrics and fibrous materials. Includes instruction in weaving techniques and loom operation; non-woven techniques such as knitting, coiling, netting, and crocheting; quilting; dyeing and pigmentation; printing and other finishing techniques; pattern design; tapestry; and personal style development.

abstract: Military operations in multi-domain environments (land, sea, air, cyber, space) demand rapid, coordinated decision-making amid escalating complexity and information overload. Traditional command structures, however, often struggle to synthesize dynamic, cross-domain data streams into actionable strategies, risking delays or suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate and optimize decision-making processes in large-scale, contested environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will model multi-domain operations through agent-based simulations that integrate real-time intelligence, adversarial actions, and resource constraints. Computational agents will represent command nodes, each with varying levels of autonomy, communication bandwidth, and domain-specific expertise. Machine learning techniques will be employed to dynamically adapt decision pathways in response to simulated disruptions, such as cyberattacks or contested communications. The simulations will stress-test decision hierarchies under scenarios involving conflicting priorities, incomplete information, and rapidly evolving threats. Key metrics include decision latency, coordination accuracy, and operational effectiveness. By scaling these simulations to thousands of concurrent agents and domains, the project will quantify trade-offs between centralized control and decentralized execution. Expected outcomes include empirically derived frameworks for restructuring command architectures to enhance agility and interoperability across military branches. This work directly supports the development of adaptive doctrines for joint all-domain operations, with potential applications in training, mission planning, and resource allocation. The computational demands of modeling hypercomplex, real-time interactions necessitate HPC infrastructure to manage parallelized simulations, high-throughput data analysis, and machine learning workflows. Findings will contribute to a nascent interdisciplinary niche within military applied sciences, bridging operational theory, computational social systems, and decision engineering.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in computational research on Korean linguistic variation and historical text analysis. While Korean language studies have increasingly incorporated digital methods, large-scale analyses of dialectal diversity and premodern textual corpora remain underdeveloped due to the computational complexity of processing non-Latin scripts, morphological richness, and sparse annotated datasets. The proposed research will employ deep learning models to analyze two interconnected domains: (1) geospatial variation in post-1945 Korean dialects using a corpus of 10,000+ hours of transcribed speech from underrepresented regions, and (2) syntactic evolution in literary Korean through semantic role labeling of 15th–19th century texts. Computational challenges include training transformer-based architectures on vertically written historical documents, managing GPU-intensive alignment of phonetic representations across dialects, and running parallelized simulations of language change. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets through distributed memory systems, while fine-tuning multilingual language models (e.g., KoBERT, XLM-R) on historical and regional Korean variants. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of annotated historical Korean syntax, a dynamic map of dialect boundaries correlated with sociolinguistic variables, and publicly released neural architectures optimized for agglutinative language processing. These resources will advance quantitative methods in Korean philology, provide infrastructure for cross-disciplinary language technology applications, and offer new empirical insights into language standardization processes. By bridging computational linguistics with area-specific humanities scholarship, this project aims to establish replicable frameworks for under-resourced languages while addressing core questions in Korean language evolution and regional identity.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling and simulating multiscale, multiphysics systems with inherent nonlinearities and stochastic components, which are central to applications in materials science and fluid dynamics. Traditional numerical methods often fail to efficiently resolve the interplay between disparate spatial and temporal scales, leading to prohibitive computational costs or oversimplified approximations. The research will develop and implement a hybrid computational framework combining adaptive finite element methods, stochastic spectral techniques, and physics-informed neural networks to enable robust, high-fidelity simulations. Key innovations include the integration of uncertainty quantification directly into adaptive mesh refinement strategies and the use of operator learning to accelerate the resolution of microscale interactions within macroscale models. The computational approach will leverage distributed-memory parallelism and GPU-accelerated linear algebra libraries to optimize scalability for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Expected outcomes include a publicly available software toolkit for multiscale simulation, validated against experimental data from collaborative studies on turbulent flow in porous media and phase transitions in shape-memory alloys. The project will advance methodological paradigms in applied mathematics by bridging deterministic and stochastic modeling approaches while providing actionable insights for engineering design. Successful implementation requires access to HPC resources capable of supporting large-scale parametric studies, with an estimated need for 500,000 core-hours to handle memory-intensive matrix computations and ensemble-based uncertainty propagation. The results will directly inform ongoing industry partnerships focused on energy-efficient material synthesis and subsurface flow prediction, demonstrating the transformative potential of applied mathematical research in computational science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of a broad range of mathematical and computational methods to modeling, analysis, algorithm development, and simulation for the solution of complex scientific and engineering problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, discrete mathematics, operations research, optimization, differential equations, statistics, scientific computation, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of computational linguistics, cultural heritage preservation, and machine learning. The core problem addressed is the automated reconstruction and semantic analysis of fragmentary or degraded historical texts, which are critical to understanding marginalized linguistic traditions but remain understudied due to their incomplete nature and lack of aligned multilingual corpora. Current approaches in text restoration rely heavily on manual expertise, limiting scalability, while existing machine learning models lack the contextual awareness needed for low-resource languages. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining transformer-based neural architectures with graph-based knowledge representation. The model will integrate unsupervised learning on non-parallel historical texts, domain-specific embeddings trained on archaeological metadata, and probabilistic reasoning to infer missing content through cross-linguistic patterns and cultural context. HPC resources are essential for training multi-modal networks on terabyte-scale datasets spanning digitized manuscripts, epigraphic databases, and ethnographic records, as well as for optimizing hyperparameters across heterogeneous data types. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for philological analysis, a benchmark dataset for evaluating computational reconstruction methods, and novel insights into linguistic evolution across three underdocumented language families. By bridging gaps between NLP, historical research, and heritage informatics, this work aims to establish scalable computational methods for preserving endangered cultural knowledge while advancing foundational techniques for handling incomplete, multilingual textual data.
cip_title: Computer and Information Sciences and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer and information sciences and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of hypersonic flow-structure-thermal interactions in next-generation aerospace vehicles, a critical challenge in high-speed flight systems. Current predictive tools struggle to resolve the coupled physics of turbulent boundary layers, aerodynamic heating, and thermoelastic material responses at Mach 10+ conditions, limiting the design of reliable thermal protection systems and reusable spacecraft. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity simulation framework combining adaptive mesh refinement, implicit large-eddy turbulence modeling, and partitioned fluid-structure-thermal coupling algorithms. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for compressible Navier-Stokes equations integrated with nonlinear finite-element analysis of anisotropic composite materials. Our approach requires petascale high-performance computing resources to resolve multiscale phenomena across spatial scales (boundary layer vortices to global vehicle deformation) and temporal scales (microsecond shock oscillations to minute-long aerodynamic heating). Initial validation will focus on experimental data from arc-jet wind tunnels and published flight test measurements. Expected outcomes include new insight into transition regimes between laminar and turbulent hypersonic flows, quantified uncertainty bounds for coupled ablation-erosion processes, and optimized material architectures for sharp leading-edge components. These results will directly inform ongoing NASA and Department of Defense initiatives on crewed Mars reentry systems and responsive hypersonic platforms. The resource request supports 18 months of simulations across 20M core-hours on parallel architectures, enabling parametric studies at unprecedented resolution. Deliverables will include open-source solver modules for the computational aerospace community and datasets to accelerate machine learning surrogate models for real-time hypersonic design applications.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of physical systems used in manufacturing and aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their system. Combines instruction in mechanical and aerospace engineering.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the evolutionary and functional dynamics of recombination rate variation across eukaryotic genomes, with a focus on identifying genetic and epigenetic factors that influence localized crossover frequency. Despite the central role of recombination in generating genetic diversity and ensuring proper chromosome segregation, the mechanisms underlying its striking variation within and between species remain poorly resolved. This project will employ population genetic simulations and comparative genomic analyses to model how sequence features, chromatin accessibility, and epigenetic modifications interact to shape recombination landscapes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for executing large-scale, stochastic simulations of evolving populations under varying selective pressures and recombination parameters. These simulations will integrate empirical data from model organisms to parameterize context-dependent recombination rates, enabling the exploration of evolutionary scenarios that cannot be tested experimentally. Key outcomes will include (1) a computational framework linking epigenetic states to recombination hotspot formation, (2) quantitative estimates of selection’s role in maintaining recombination rate variation, and (3) predictions about how chromatin architecture constrains crossover positioning over evolutionary timescales. The work will leverage parallelized algorithms to analyze genome-wide association datasets and simulate population-scale inheritance patterns across millions of generations. By clarifying how genetic and epigenetic systems jointly modulate recombination, this research will advance fundamental knowledge of genome evolution while providing insights into fertility-related disorders linked to aberrant crossover distributions. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration at biologically relevant scales, overcoming current limitations in simulating complex interactions between nucleotide sequences, chromatin features, and population dynamics.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the organization, recombination, function, regulation, and transmission of heritable information in biological organisms at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in Mendelian genetics, mechanisms of gene regulation, chromosome structure and replication, epigenetic phenomena, DNA repair and recombination, sex determination, genetic interactions between genomes, and molecular evolution.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize the resilience of next-generation hybrid energy grids under high-dimensional uncertainty, integrating quantum-inspired optimization methods with classical high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Modern energy systems increasingly rely on distributed renewable generation, multi-vector storage, and demand-responsive loads, creating complex interdependencies that challenge traditional optimization tools. Existing approaches struggle to balance real-time stability, cost efficiency, and fault tolerance in systems with thousands of nonlinear, stochastic variables. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm leveraging tensor network simulations and graph-based decomposition techniques to partition grid optimization problems into tractable subdomains. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of synthetic energy networks with embedded cyber-physical dynamics, including stochastic weather patterns, device-level degradation models, and adversarial threat scenarios. Key innovations include (1) a meta-reinforcement learning module to adapt optimization heuristics across grid topologies and (2) a quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) emulator targeting mixed-integer nonlinear programs. Computational experiments will benchmark solution quality and convergence rates against conventional solvers under varying resource constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for resilience-aware grid optimization and quantitative guidelines for quantum advantage thresholds in energy systems applications. By fusing techniques from quantum computing, control theory, and network science, this work aims to establish foundational methods for managing the complexity of future decarbonized energy infrastructures. The requested computing resources will support parallelized parameter sweeps across 10,000+ scenario combinations, requiring petascale storage for high-resolution temporal-spatial simulations and GPU-accelerated tensor operations. Success in this effort could reduce computational overhead for grid operators by up to 70% compared to state-of-the-art commercial tools, as quantified through normalized optimality gap metrics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of tear film instability in dry eye syndrome (DES), a multifactorial disorder affecting millions globally, by leveraging advanced computational modeling to uncover biomechanical and biophysical mechanisms underlying tear film dynamics. Current clinical approaches to DES diagnosis and management remain largely empirical, with limited tools to predict individual responses to therapies or environmental stressors. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity, multiscale computational model of the ocular surface environment, integrating fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, and molecular interactions within the tear film layers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of tear film behavior under varied physiological conditions, including blink dynamics, evaporation rates, and lipid layer morphology, using lattice Boltzmann methods and finite element analysis. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze simulation outputs to identify predictive biomarkers of tear film instability and optimize therapeutic interventions. The computational framework will be validated against experimental data from in vitro models and clinical imaging (e.g., interferometry, OCT). By elucidating the interplay between tear film components and environmental factors, this work aims to advance personalized DES management strategies, inform the design of next-generation ocular lubricants, and establish a platform for simulating other anterior segment disorders. The project’s interdisciplinary approach, combining optometric science, computational biophysics, and data science, addresses an unmet need in ocular surface health while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in niche clinical applications. Outcomes will include open-source simulation tools for researchers and clinically actionable insights to improve diagnostic precision in optometric practice.
cip_title: Ophthalmic and Optometric Support Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ophthalmic and optometric support services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Agricultural mechanization faces critical challenges in optimizing equipment performance and operational efficiency across diverse and dynamic farming environments. Current approaches to machinery selection, deployment, and maintenance often rely on generalized heuristics or small-scale empirical data, limiting their adaptability to variable field conditions, crop types, and sustainability goals. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating and optimizing agricultural machinery systems at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The research will integrate multi-source data—including soil sensors, equipment telemetry, weather forecasts, and crop growth models—into a coupled computational architecture using agent-based modeling and machine learning. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of machinery interactions across thousands of virtual farm scenarios, capturing nonlinear relationships between equipment configurations, energy consumption patterns, and agronomic outcomes. Key computational challenges include real-time parameterization of heterogeneous equipment datasets, adaptive clustering of operational patterns, and predictive maintenance modeling using time-series analysis of sensor streams. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that recommends context-specific machinery configurations to minimize fuel use while maintaining yield targets, alongside predictive failure algorithms to reduce downtime. The project will directly advance precision agriculture capabilities by demonstrating how computational scaling can transform equipment management paradigms, with potential applications in automated implement control systems and farm-level digital twins. By focusing on computational methods rather than empirical hardware modifications, this work aims to create transferable optimization strategies applicable to both smallholder and industrial farming operations, strengthening the technological foundation for sustainable agricultural intensification.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to sell, select, and service agricultural or agribusiness technical equipment and facilities, including computers, specialized software, power units, machinery, equipment structures, and utilities. Includes instruction in agricultural power systems, planning and selecting materials for the construction of support facilities, mechanical practices associated with irrigation and water conservation, erosion control, and agricultural data processing systems.

abstract: The safe and efficient management of blood products relies on precise compatibility testing, donor-recipient matching, and understanding complex immunological interactions. However, current methods for predicting transfusion outcomes, particularly in patients with rare blood types or antibody profiles, remain limited by incomplete datasets and the computational complexity of modeling dynamic antigen-antibody interactions at scale. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate immunohematological processes and optimize transfusion protocols. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will model the structural and thermodynamic properties of red blood cell antigens and their interactions with antibodies implicated in hemolytic transfusion reactions. Parallelized MD workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to resolve time- and resource-intensive calculations, enabling the analysis of rare antigen variants and low-probability binding events. Complementing this, machine learning (ML) models trained on regional blood bank datasets—including donor histories, antigen frequencies, and adverse reaction reports—will predict compatibility risks and identify optimal donor pools for sensitized recipients. The integration of these computational approaches requires HPC resources to manage large-scale genomic data, run iterative simulations across parameter spaces, and validate ML predictions against clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive atlas of high-risk antigen-antibody interactions, (2) an open-source tool for rapid compatibility scoring in complex transfusion scenarios, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for inventory management to reduce wastage and improve access to rare blood products. By advancing computational methods in immunohematology, this work aims to mitigate transfusion-related complications, enhance donor recruitment strategies, and support clinical decision-making in blood banks operating under resource constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Educational system administrators face complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation, policy implementation, and equity across multi-school districts, particularly in dynamic environments with diverse student populations and fluctuating funding. This project seeks to develop a computational decision-support framework to model district-wide outcomes of administrative strategies under varying demographic, financial, and policy conditions. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, evidence-based tools to simulate long-term impacts of leadership decisions—such as budget reallocations, school consolidation, or intervention programs—on student achievement gaps, staff retention, and systemic equity. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run large-scale agent-based simulations that integrate real-world data from school districts, including student performance metrics, socioeconomic variables, staffing patterns, and facilities costs. Computational models will emulate interactions between schools, administrators, communities, and policymakers, incorporating machine learning techniques to predict cascading effects of decisions across time and geographies. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-dimensional datasets, parallelizing thousands of scenario iterations, and validating models against historical outcomes. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source toolset for district leaders to quantify trade-offs in strategic planning, anticipate unintended consequences of policies, and identify intervention thresholds for equitable resource distribution. This work bridges computational social science and educational leadership by advancing data-driven methods for systemic administration, with particular relevance for under-resourced districts navigating demographic shifts or post-pandemic recovery. Results will inform best practices in superintendency training programs and provide a replicable framework for optimizing educational systems in diverse cultural and socioeconomic contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leading and managing multi-school educational systems and school districts and prepares individuals to serve as systems administrators and district superintendents. Includes instruction in educational administration; education of students at various levels; system planning and budgeting; educational policy; educational law and regulations; public relations; professional standards and ethics; and applications to specific issues, cultural context, and geographic locales.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research by developing scalable models for analyzing large-scale legal text corpora. The research addresses a critical gap in legal studies: the inability to systematically evaluate the evolution of judicial reasoning, statutory interpretation patterns, and latent biases across decades of case law using traditional manual methods. By focusing on U.S. appellate court decisions and state statutes, the project aims to identify longitudinal trends in legal argumentation, particularly in understudied areas such as procedural fairness in administrative law and the impact of non-precedential opinions. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on legal terminology, with graph-based analytics to map citation networks and concept diffusion. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific embeddings on multi-terabyte text datasets, running parallelized semantic similarity analyses across millions of documents, and simulating argumentation patterns through agent-based models. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for temporal legal document analysis, 2) quantitative frameworks to assess the propagation of judicial reasoning heuristics, and 3) empirical insights into how computational bottlenecks in current legal research practices affect access to justice. The project’s interdisciplinary methodology bridges gaps between computational linguistics, complex systems theory, and doctrinal legal analysis, offering a novel paradigm for understanding legal systems as dynamic information networks. Results will provide practitioners with actionable metrics for precedent analysis while informing policy debates about AI-assisted legal research tools. This work establishes a foundation for data-intensive legal epistemology research, requiring HPC capabilities to manage the combinatorial complexity inherent in large-scale jurisprudential systems.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program in one or more of the legal research or advanced practice fields.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of integrated building systems modeling tools for sustainable architectural design. Current approaches to optimizing energy efficiency, structural resilience, and environmental performance in buildings often rely on fragmented simulations that inadequately capture the interdependencies between mechanical, thermal, and structural systems. This limitation hinders the ability to holistically evaluate design trade-offs in complex urban environments. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework coupling finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate multi-physics interactions within building systems at unprecedented resolution. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of building prototypes under dynamic environmental loads, integrating real-world climate data and material behavior models. Key tasks include validating a coupled FEA-CFD model for predicting heat transfer and airflow in mixed-use structures, training ML surrogates to accelerate parametric design optimization, and conducting probabilistic risk assessments of structural failures under extreme weather scenarios. The computational workflow will utilize open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM, FEniCS) alongside custom Python-based optimization routines, requiring distributed memory architectures for large-scale matrix computations and GPU acceleration for neural network training. Expected outcomes include a novel digital twin methodology for building performance analysis, actionable insights into climate-adaptive design strategies, and open-access datasets quantifying energy-structure-environment synergies. By enabling high-fidelity, system-level simulations, this research will directly support architects and engineers in creating next-generation buildings that balance operational efficiency, safety, and environmental stewardship. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational intensity of 3D transient simulations and ML model development, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing burden of vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases in resource-limited regions underscores the urgent need for advanced computational tools to model complex disease dynamics and optimize intervention strategies. Current approaches often fail to capture the multiscale interactions between pathogens, vectors, human populations, and environmental drivers, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative, spatially explicit models of disease transmission for pathogens such as malaria, dengue, and chikungunya. The research will combine agent-based modeling, machine learning, and genomic epidemiology to simulate transmission dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes, incorporating real-world data on vector ecology, climate variability, host immunity, and human mobility. Key computational challenges include parameterizing large-scale models with genomic datasets from pathogen surveillance, optimizing spatiotemporal resolution for regional forecasts, and quantifying uncertainty in intervention outcomes. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to explore scenarios such as vaccine deployment strategies, insecticide resistance evolution, and climate-driven shifts in vector habitats. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to identify high-risk transmission hotspots, evaluate the durability of vaccine-induced immunity, and prioritize targeted vector control measures. By integrating high-resolution genomic and environmental data, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of pathogen adaptation and spillover risks. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to support public health decision-making in endemic regions. This project directly addresses critical gaps in tropical disease management, with potential to reduce morbidity and mortality through data-driven, precision public health interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to prevent and control vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases. Includes instruction in microbiology, parasitology, mycology, virology, vector biology, vaccinology, laboratory diagnosis, travelers' health, epidemiology, and disease management.

abstract: Franchising, a critical growth strategy in global business ecosystems, faces systemic challenges in optimizing network expansion due to the dynamic interplay of market heterogeneity, regulatory constraints, and operational interdependencies. Traditional analytical models fail to capture the spatiotemporal complexity of multi-unit franchising decisions, particularly when balancing local adaptability with brand consistency. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate and optimize franchise network growth under real-world constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability limitations in existing decision-support tools. The research will develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) system integrating geospatial analytics, reinforcement learning, and multi-objective optimization to evaluate franchise performance drivers across diverse demographic and economic contexts. By parameterizing legal requirements, setup costs, and market saturation thresholds, the model will simulate thousands of franchise configurations while dynamically adjusting for competitive landscapes and consumer behavior patterns. Computational experiments will utilize historical franchise performance data and synthetic datasets to stress-test expansion strategies under varying capital allocation scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics platform capable of identifying optimal franchise density thresholds, quantifying cannibalization risks in overlapping territories, and forecasting ROI timelines under different financing structures. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional optimization problems involving 10^6+ parameter combinations, a computational scale intractable with conventional methods. By bridging operations research, computational economics, and spatial analytics, this work aims to advance evidence-based franchising strategies while establishing methodological foundations for complex franchise system analysis. Resulting open-source tools and simulation libraries will empower franchisors to mitigate expansion risks and enhance network resilience, with direct applications to emerging markets where data scarcity exacerbates traditional planning challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and operate franchises. Includes instruction in legal requirements, set-up costs and capitalization requirements, financing, and applications to specific franchise opportunities.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic challenges in educational administration by developing data-driven decision-making models to optimize resource allocation and policy implementation in K-12 school districts. School superintendents and system leaders face complex trade-offs when balancing budgetary constraints, equity mandates, staffing needs, and fluctuating enrollment, yet existing tools for scenario analysis often lack the computational power to account for dynamic variables at scale. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build predictive simulations that integrate multi-agent modeling, machine learning, and geospatial analysis. These simulations will process district-level datasets—including student performance metrics, financial records, demographic trends, and facility capacities—to model the long-term impacts of administrative decisions under diverse conditions. Agent-based frameworks will simulate interactions between schools, communities, and policy changes, while Monte Carlo methods will assess risk and uncertainty in budget reallocations or school consolidation scenarios. The computational intensity of iterating thousands of policy permutations across multi-year timelines necessitates parallelized computing architectures to achieve feasible runtime. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for district leaders to evaluate the equity and efficiency implications of proposed interventions, particularly in under-resourced regions. This work will advance scholarship in educational leadership by demonstrating how computational social science methods can address real-world administrative problems, with direct applications to crisis response planning, Title I fund distribution, and infrastructure modernization. By quantifying the second-order effects of leadership decisions, the project aims to reduce trial-and-error approaches in system administration and provide evidence-based strategies to improve outcomes for historically marginalized student populations. The requested HPC resources will enable the processing of high-dimensional datasets across 10+ simulated years of district operations, a task exceeding the capacity of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leading and managing multi-school educational systems and school districts and prepares individuals to serve as systems administrators and district superintendents. Includes instruction in educational administration; education of students at various levels; system planning and budgeting; educational policy; educational law and regulations; public relations; professional standards and ethics; and applications to specific issues, cultural context, and geographic locales.

abstract: The increasing complexity of global financial networks, driven by interconnected markets, decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems, and heterogeneous data streams, poses significant challenges for systemic risk assessment. Traditional models often fail to capture nonlinear dependencies, temporal volatility, and cross-domain interactions at scale. This project proposes an interdisciplinary framework integrating multilayer network theory, dynamic Bayesian inference, and adaptive machine learning to model systemic risk propagation across asset classes, geopolitical events, and emerging digital financial infrastructures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process petabytes of structured and unstructured financial data—including transaction records, sentiment signals from alternative text sources, and real-time blockchain metrics—to construct a time-evolving risk topology. Computational challenges include solving stochastic partial differential equations for contagion dynamics, training graph neural networks (GNNs) on temporal heterogeneous graphs, and optimizing ensemble models for scenario forecasting under uncertainty. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across 10,000+ synthetic market shock scenarios, enabling GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition of high-dimensional financial time series, and maintaining low-latency pipelines for real-time data assimilation. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for multilayer financial network analysis, (2) predictive early-warning indicators for cascading failures in hybrid (traditional/DeFi) systems, and (3) empirically validated stress-testing protocols that incorporate climate-related financial disclosures and geopolitical risk factors. This work bridges gaps between financial mathematics, computational social science, and climate economics, offering regulators and institutions a computationally robust platform to navigate systemic vulnerabilities in an era of escalating interdisciplinary financial risks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on financial big data modeling from algorithms to cloud-based data-driven financial technologies. Includes instruction in financial analytics, financial data processing, knowledge management, data visualization, effective decision communication, machine learning for finance, statistical inference and dynamic modeling on financial data, and project management.

abstract: This research project addresses the challenge of optimizing quantitative accuracy in radionuclide-based diagnostic imaging, specifically in single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET), where photon attenuation, scatter, and dynamic tracer kinetics limit diagnostic precision. Current clinical protocols rely on generalized correction algorithms that inadequately account for patient-specific anatomical variability and tracer biodistribution dynamics, particularly in heterogeneous tumor environments or patients with complex comorbidities. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes the development of patient-adaptive, time-resolved computational models that integrate multi-modal imaging data (CT/MRI) with Monte Carlo-based radiation transport simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute these resource-intensive simulations at scale, enabling voxel-level modeling of radionuclide decay physics, tissue-specific attenuation, and kinetic parameter estimation across 4D (3D spatial + temporal) datasets. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated iterative reconstruction algorithms and machine learning frameworks to reduce noise amplification while preserving spatial resolution. Expected outcomes include validated correction maps for improved lesion quantification (±10% error reduction target) and a predictive model linking tracer kinetics to tumor receptor density in neuroendocrine neoplasms. Successful implementation will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in staging and therapy response assessment, with downstream applications in personalized radionuclide therapy dosing. The scale of required computations—including parallel processing of 10⁶ photon histories per patient timepoint and population-level Bayesian optimization of kinetic parameters—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve clinically feasible turnaround times. This work bridges a critical gap between nuclear imaging physics and clinical decision-making, with methodological advancements applicable to emerging theranostic radiotracers.
cip_definition: Research focused on the imaging by external detection of radionuclides and/or biodistribution by external detection of radionuclides for diagnosis of disease. Requires prior partial completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: Plants rely on intricate mechanical and hydrodynamic processes within their cells to adapt to environmental stressors, yet the multiscale dynamics of these systems remain poorly understood. This project seeks to model the biomechanical behavior of plant cell wall-fluid interactions during rapid osmotic stress responses, a critical process for survival in fluctuating environments. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will simulate the coupled mechanical deformation of cellulose microfibrils and cytoplasmic fluid flow in 3D cellular geometries derived from experimental cryo-electron tomography data of *Arabidopsis thaliana* root hairs. The computational framework integrates finite element methods for solid mechanics, lattice Boltzmann simulations for viscous fluid dynamics, and stochastic models for ion transport across dynamically changing membranes. By resolving nanosecond-scale molecular interactions alongside minute-long tissue-level stress redistribution, these multiscale simulations will uncover how localized wall loosening propagates hydraulic signals through adjacent cells—a phenomenon hypothesized to coordinate systemic drought avoidance behaviors. Key challenges include optimizing parallelized solvers for irregular cellular geometries and validating models against microfluidic pressure perturbation experiments. Successful implementation will provide the first quantitative map of energy dissipation thresholds in plant cell networks under hydraulic shock, offering insights into evolutionary constraints on cell wall architecture. Outcomes will directly inform bioinspired material designs for soft robotics and advance predictive models of crop resilience to climate-driven water volatility. This work bridges plant biophysics, computational mechanics, and soft matter engineering, establishing a new paradigm for studying plant environmental sensing through HPC-enabled mechanohydraulic analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plants, related microbial organisms, and plant habitats and ecosystem relations. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and structure, phytochemistry, cytology, plant genetics, plant morphology and physiology, plant ecology, plant taxonomy and systematics, paleobotany, and applications of biophysics and molecular biology.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in industrial process optimization by developing a computational framework that integrates human factors, resource constraints, and dynamic workflow interdependencies. Traditional optimization models in industrial settings often oversimplify human-machine interactions or fail to account for real-time variability in operator performance, equipment reliability, and workflow disruptions. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-agent simulation environment coupled with parallelized metaheuristic algorithms to model complex industrial systems at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute these computationally intensive simulations, which will incorporate discrete-event simulation for process flows, agent-based modeling for worker behavior, and GPU-accelerated genetic algorithms for multi-objective optimization. The framework will be validated using anonymized production data from a mid-scale manufacturing partner, with scenarios testing adaptive scheduling, ergonomic risk mitigation, and energy-consumption trade-offs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for industrial technologists to simulate process improvements under realistic constraints, as well as predictive metrics for balancing throughput, workforce safety, and operational costs. The project directly supports workforce training objectives by generating case studies for instructional use in industrial technology curricula. By enabling more holistic modeling of human-in-the-loop systems, this work aims to advance decision-support tools for industries adopting Industry 4.0 technologies while maintaining alignment with human-centric operational values. The requested computing resources will specifically support the parallel execution of optimization trials, large-scale parameter space exploration, and validation against stochastic disturbance models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of industrial engineers and managers. Includes instruction in optimization theory, human factors, organizational behavior, industrial processes, industrial planning procedures, computer applications, and report and presentation preparation.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in zoonotic pathogens present critical challenges to veterinary medicine and public health. Current gaps in understanding the genomic and ecological drivers of AMR transmission between livestock, wildlife, and humans limit the development of targeted interventions. This project proposes an integrative computational approach to model AMR dynamics in multi-host systems, with a focus on Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica in livestock populations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale genomic datasets (whole-genome sequencing of 5,000+ bacterial isolates) and simulate pathogen spread under varying husbandry practices, antimicrobial use policies, and environmental conditions. Agent-based models will be developed to represent host-pathogen interactions across heterogeneous landscapes, incorporating real-world data on animal movement, farm density, and veterinary antimicrobial prescriptions. Machine learning pipelines will identify genomic signatures associated with resistance persistence and horizontal gene transfer events. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized genomic analysis tools (e.g., AMBER for resistance gene prediction) and spatially explicit modeling frameworks (e.g., SpaDES in R). The requested HPC allocation will enable 1) comparative phylogenomic reconstruction of AMR gene dissemination pathways, 2) parameterization of stochastic transmission models through approximate Bayesian computation, and 3) high-resolution simulations of intervention scenarios across 10^6 agent-days. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of AMR emergence risk in livestock-dense regions and evidence-based recommendations for stewardship protocols. This work will directly inform veterinary clinical decision-making while advancing methodological frameworks for One Health research, with particular significance for food animal production systems contributing to global protein supplies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance perioperative patient outcomes and surgical team efficiency through advanced computational modeling of intraoperative risk factors and workflow optimization. Despite standardized protocols, variability in surgical complications—such as surgical site infections (SSIs), hypothermia, and hemodynamic instability—persists, driven by complex interactions between patient-specific factors, real-time physiological data, and operating room (OR) logistics. Traditional statistical methods lack the capacity to model these multidimensional, dynamic relationships at scale. We propose developing a machine learning (ML) framework to analyze high-resolution electronic health records (EHRs), intraoperative sensor data, and OR workflow logs from 15 collaborating institutions (>200,000 procedures). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train ensemble models integrating convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for temporal vital sign analysis, natural language processing (NLP) for surgical narrative annotation, and agent-based simulations to evaluate staffing patterns. The computational pipeline will prioritize scalability, with distributed training across GPU nodes to manage terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for SSI risk and hemodynamic deterioration, validated against prospective cohorts, and (2) simulated workflow interventions to reduce instrument preparation delays by ≥15%. Results will be disseminated as open-source tools for real-time decision support, enabling surgical nurses to personalize preoperative preparations and anticipate critical intraoperative transitions. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work addresses a critical gap in perioperative informatics, translating large-scale data into actionable clinical strategies that align with nursing priorities of patient safety, efficiency, and evidence-based practice.
cip_title: Perioperative/ Operating Room and Surgical Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care to patients before and during surgery, and provide tableside assistance to surgeons. Includes instruction in operating room safety and preparation, aseptic technique, anesthesia, patient preparation, surgical instruments and procedures, sterilization and disinfecting, surgical drugs and solutions, hemostasis, emergency procedures, and patient/family education.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanistic and neurophysiological effects of Asian Bodywork Therapy (ABT) modalities using computational modeling to quantify their therapeutic impacts on chronic musculoskeletal pain. While ABT practices such as Shiatsu, Thai massage, and Tui na are empirically recognized for pain management, their mechanisms remain poorly characterized due to the multifactorial nature of manual interventions and dynamic tissue responses. The research aims to address this gap by developing multiscale models integrating real-time pressure dynamics, fascial network interactions, and systemic biomarker data to map how specific ABT techniques modulate pain pathways. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable finite element analysis of force propagation in soft tissues under varying therapeutic pressures, coupled with agent-based simulations of inflammatory mediator dispersion. Machine learning pipelines will analyze multimodal datasets from 120 clinical ABT sessions (including pressure sensor arrays, cortisol assays, and patient-reported pain scores) to identify predictive signatures of treatment efficacy. A secondary objective involves optimizing ABT protocols via in silico testing of pressure-duration matrices across virtual patient cohorts with heterogeneous biomechanical profiles. Outcomes will establish quantitative frameworks for ABT dose-response relationships, advancing evidence-based standardization while preserving individualized practice principles. By bridging traditional somatic therapies with computational systems biology, this work aims to catalyze interdisciplinary innovation in non-pharmacological pain management and foster translational collaborations between manual medicine practitioners and biomedical engineers. The requested HPC allocation is critical for managing the iterative simulation workloads, large-scale data integration, and complex parameter space exploration required to model these dynamic, person-centered interventions at clinically relevant resolutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being based on Chinese medical principles through one or more of the traditional bodywork therapies of Asia. Includes instruction in acupressure, AMMA(r) Therapy, Chi Nei Tsang, Five Element Shiatsu, Integrative Eclectic Shiatsu, Japanese Shiatsu, Jin Shin Do(r) Bodymind Acupressure(tm), Macrobiotic Shiatsu, Anma Therapy, Thai massage, Tui na, Zen Shiatsu, Qigong, Okazaki(r) Restorative Massage, principles of Western and Chinese medicine, patient counseling and observation, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in fashion show production, addressing the challenge of real-time decision-making under constraints such as budget, spatial logistics, and environmental variability. Fashion modeling events require precise coordination of human models, lighting, stage elements, and digital media, yet current planning tools rely on static schedules and heuristic adjustments, leading to inefficiencies in time, cost, and creative execution. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-agent systems simulating interactions between models, stage crews, and environmental factors (e.g., lighting transitions, audience movement) across diverse venue configurations. Agent-based modeling will be combined with reinforcement learning to iteratively optimize workflows, while Monte Carlo simulations will assess risk under stochastic variables like equipment delays or model availability. A novel computational layer will integrate real-time data streams from wearable IoT sensors on models and stage equipment to enable adaptive rescheduling during live events. The research will utilize parallelized workflows on GPU clusters to handle high-dimensional parameter spaces, including 3D venue renderings and temporal dependencies across 10,000+ concurrent agents. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that reduces production costs by 15–20% in simulated scenarios, minimizes idle time for personnel, and improves synchronization of multimedia elements. The computational framework will also enable rapid prototyping of sustainable event designs by quantifying energy use and material waste under alternative configurations. By bridging operations research, computer graphics, and behavioral modeling, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven creative production in the fashion industry, with implications for live event management in adjacent sectors such as theater and experiential retail.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to present and display fashion, apparel, and accessories products in wholesale and retail settings, either on the person or via props and natural or artificial settings. Includes instruction in modeling skills, health and cosmetic principles, fashion show management, display design and production, and applicable aspects of advertising and fashion photography.

abstract: Maintaining the operational efficiency and longevity of complex building systems (e.g., HVAC, electrical, plumbing) requires predictive and adaptive strategies, yet existing approaches often rely on reactive or static maintenance protocols. This project addresses the challenge of developing dynamic, data-driven models to optimize building system performance and preemptively identify maintenance needs across heterogeneous structures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a computational framework integrating sensor-derived operational data, weather patterns, and material degradation models to simulate and predict system failures. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between mechanical components under varying environmental and usage conditions, while machine learning algorithms trained on historical maintenance records will identify failure precursors. Finite element analysis will further assess stress distributions in critical infrastructure, such as piping networks and HVAC ductwork, under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale spatial-temporal datasets and iterative simulations across diverse building types (commercial, industrial, mobile homes). Expected outcomes include predictive maintenance schedules tailored to specific building configurations, energy-optimized operational protocols for aging systems, and failure risk matrices for prioritization of infrastructure upgrades. The project will produce open-source tools enabling facility managers to simulate maintenance scenarios and allocate resources effectively. By transitioning from time-based to condition-based maintenance paradigms, this work aims to reduce operational costs by an estimated 15–25% in testbed structures while extending equipment lifespans. The HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary resolution in multi-physics simulations and ensuring scalability across the spectrum of building technologies addressed in vocational training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to keep a building functioning, and to service a variety of structures including commercial and industrial buildings and mobile homes. Includes instruction in the basic maintenance and repair skills required to service building systems, such as air conditioning, heating, plumbing, electrical, major appliances, and other mechanical systems.

abstract: Fungal pathogens pose significant threats to human health, agriculture, and ecosystem stability, with rising antifungal resistance complicating treatment strategies. This project seeks to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying fungal pathogenesis and environmental adaptation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex datasets derived from experimental mycology. A key focus is elucidating how stress-response pathways in pathogenic fungi, such as *Candida auris* and *Aspergillus fumigatus*, modulate virulence and drug resistance under host-mimicking conditions. Traditional laboratory methods face limitations in scaling to analyze multi-omics data (transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) generated from fungal cultures exposed to antifungal agents and immune system stressors. The project will employ computational workflows integrating molecular dynamics simulations to model fungal protein-ligand interactions, particularly those involving antifungal targets like lanosterol demethylase and β-glucan synthase. Parallelized pipelines will process high-throughput imaging data of fungal morphogenetic shifts (e.g., hyphal growth in host tissue), correlating structural changes with gene expression profiles. Machine learning models trained on phenotypic and environmental data will predict adaptive mutations linked to resistance. By deploying these HPC-driven approaches, the project aims to identify novel therapeutic targets, forecast resistance evolution, and characterize ecological drivers of fungal pathogenicity. Outcomes will advance understanding of host-fungal interactions, inform antifungal development, and support predictive frameworks for managing mycoses in clinical and environmental contexts. The requested computing resources are critical for handling terabyte-scale datasets, running iterative simulations, and optimizing predictive algorithms, enabling insights unattainable with standard laboratory infrastructure. This work bridges mycological research with computational innovation, addressing urgent challenges in microbial pathogenesis and antimicrobial resistance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of fungi, lichenous plants, eukaryotic microorganisms, myxomycetes, and plasmodiophorales and their relationship to diseases in higher plants, animals, and human beings as well as to pharmacologically useful products. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology; histopathology; fungal growth and behavior; environmental mycology; antifungal sensitivity; mycoses; pathogens and pathogenesis; pharmacological properties; and computer and laboratory research methods.

abstract: The increasing complexity of engineering systems demands advanced computational tools to address multi-physics, multi-scale challenges that are intractable with traditional methods. This project seeks to develop and validate a high-fidelity computational framework for optimizing next-generation energy conversion systems, focusing on hybrid thermofluid-electrochemical processes. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable models capable of resolving coupled thermal, fluid, and electrochemical phenomena across disparate temporal and spatial scales—from molecular-level charge transfer at electrode interfaces to system-level heat and mass transport. Current experimental approaches are cost-prohibitive for iterative design, while existing simulations often rely on oversimplified assumptions that limit predictive accuracy. To overcome these barriers, we propose a hierarchical computational strategy combining first-principles molecular dynamics (MD), mesoscale lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM), and macroscopic finite element analysis (FEA). The workflow will leverage machine learning surrogates to bridge scale-dependent simulations, enabling concurrent optimization of material properties and system architecture. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for executing large-scale parametric studies involving 10^6+ core-hours to resolve nanosecond-scale interfacial dynamics (via MD), millimeter-scale transport (via LBM), and hour-scale operational cycles (via FEA). Expected outcomes include validated multi-scale models for proton-exchange membrane assemblies, optimized reactor geometries achieving 15-20% efficiency gains over conventional designs, and open-source computational tools for hybrid energy system analysis. The work will advance fundamental understanding of cross-scale interactions in electrochemical systems while providing actionable insights for sustainable energy infrastructure. By integrating HPC-driven simulation with data-driven methods, this project establishes a template for accelerating the design of complex engineering systems across technology domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling electromagnetic interference (EMI) within high-frequency integrated circuits (ICs), a critical bottleneck in advancing next-generation electronic systems. As ICs scale to nanometer dimensions and operate at gigahertz frequencies, traditional simulation tools fail to capture the complex electromagnetic coupling effects that degrade signal integrity and power efficiency. The research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework combining full-wave electromagnetic solvers with machine learning (ML) to predict and mitigate EMI in multi-layer circuit architectures. The computational approach will leverage finite-element method (FEM) simulations to model near-field coupling across 3D IC stacks, generating terabyte-scale datasets of spatial field distributions under varying frequency and material conditions. These datasets will train graph neural networks (GNNs) to identify EMI hotspots and recommend layout optimizations, enabling real-time design feedback. The HPC resources will facilitate parallel execution of thousands of parameterized FEM simulations on GPU clusters, reducing computation time from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include validated ML models for EMI prediction with >90% accuracy compared to experimental measurements, open-source simulation workflows, and design guidelines for reducing cross-talk in 5G/6G communication chips. This work will directly benefit semiconductor manufacturers and IoT device developers by accelerating the design of interference-resistant electronics while maintaining compliance with international EMI standards. The proposed computational pipeline also establishes a template for integrating physics-based modeling with AI/ML in electromagnetic compatibility research, addressing a critical gap in electrical engineering education and industry practice.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronic engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to enhance the creation of adaptive, high-resolution digital illustrations through machine learning and real-time rendering, addressing the growing demand for dynamic visual content in client-driven contexts. Current illustration workflows often struggle to efficiently integrate complex client specifications—such as multi-style hybridization, contextual object placement, or material texture simulation—while maintaining artistic intent. We propose a two-phase approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources: first, training generative adversarial networks (GANs) on a curated dataset of 50,000+ annotated illustrations spanning historical and contemporary styles, material textures, and spatial compositions; second, implementing real-time neural rendering pipelines to enable iterative client-artist collaboration. The GAN architecture will utilize transformer-based attention mechanisms to parse textual and visual input constraints, requiring distributed training across multiple GPUs to handle the model’s 12-billion-parameter scale. Concurrently, physics-based simulations of traditional media (e.g., watercolor pigment dispersion, charcoal grain dynamics) will be optimized through parallel computing to generate texture libraries with microsecond temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for style-adaptive illustration generation, reducing revision cycles by enabling rapid prototyping of client-directed edits. This work bridges computational aesthetics and practical design workflows, offering empirical insights into human-AI collaborative creativity. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing memory-intensive rendering tasks, distributed model training, and large-scale user testing simulations—processes infeasible on local hardware. Results will be validated through partnerships with digital media studios and peer-reviewed benchmarks against industry-standard illustration tools, with potential applications in interactive book illustration, augmented reality design, and customizable asset generation for cross-platform publishing.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in biology teacher education programs regarding the integration of computational modeling and data-driven pedagogical strategies for teaching complex biological systems. While modern biology increasingly relies on computational tools to analyze ecosystems, genetic networks, and population dynamics, pre-service biology teachers often lack exposure to high-performance computing (HPC) resources and their applications in classroom-relevant contexts. The research will develop and evaluate scalable computational workflows to simulate biological systems commonly taught in secondary and postsecondary curricula, such as predator-prey dynamics, disease transmission, and phylogenetic trait evolution. Using agent-based modeling frameworks and network analysis tools, we will generate adaptable simulation modules that mirror real-world biological variability while remaining accessible for educators with limited coding experience. The project leverages HPC resources to run large-scale parameter sweeps across ecological and evolutionary scenarios, enabling the creation of probabilistic outcome libraries for student-led inquiry activities. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to anonymized simulation data to identify common misconceptions in trainee teachers’ reasoning about stochastic biological processes. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of optimized computational models aligned with Next-Generation Science Standards, (2) evidence-based guidelines for incorporating HPC-derived datasets into teacher training programs, and (3) quantitative metrics comparing the efficacy of computational modeling exercises versus traditional pedagogical approaches in improving conceptual understanding of emergent biological phenomena. The computational demands of simultaneously running thousands of stochastic simulations with variable initial conditions, coupled with the need for real-time visualization of multidimensional data during teacher workshops, necessitate dedicated HPC allocation. This work bridges computational biology and science education research, equipping future biology educators with tools to foster data literacy and systems thinking in diverse classroom settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach biology programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between cognitive security threats and transnational information ecosystems, focusing on how AI-generated media (e.g., deepfakes, synthetic narratives) erode public trust and influence geopolitical stability. While traditional security studies prioritize physical or cyber infrastructure, this research addresses an understudied dimension: the computational modeling of human cognitive vulnerabilities in digital environments. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and neural network architectures, we simulate the diffusion of AI-manipulated content across multilingual social networks, incorporating behavioral data from diverse sociopolitical contexts.
