The research employs natural language processing (NLP) to analyze cross-cultural semantic shifts in manipulated narratives and federated learning to model decentralized disinformation campaigns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling simulations to reflect global social networks (~10^8 nodes), processing real-time multilingual datasets, and training adversarial models to predict emergent threat patterns. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying cognitive risk thresholds in targeted populations and a dynamic threat-assessment tool capable of identifying latent vulnerabilities in national security communication systems. This work bridges gaps between computational social science, cognitive psychology, and security informatics, offering policymakers actionable insights into mitigating non-kinetic threats. By mapping how synthetic media exploits cultural and cognitive biases, the project advances interdisciplinary methodologies for security studies while addressing ethical challenges in AI-mediated human behavior analysis. The computational models and datasets will be modular, enabling adaptation to evolving threat landscapes and fostering international collaboration in cognitive security research.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_title: International Relations and National Security Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in international relations and national security studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in dynamic print production workflows, a critical challenge in the graphic and printing equipment operations field. Traditional methods for optimizing job scheduling, color calibration, and material usage in commercial printing rely on static heuristics or manual adjustments, leading to suboptimal resource allocation, increased waste, and delays under variable demand. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a computational framework that integrates real-time data from digital printing systems, environmental sensors, and customer specifications to model and simulate production scenarios. The core computational challenge lies in processing heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution image files, substrate behavior models, and machine performance metrics—to generate adaptive scheduling algorithms and predictive maintenance protocols. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of finite element analysis (FEA) simulations for substrate deformation under different printing conditions, as well as training machine learning models to correlate historical job data with optimal ink-volume profiles. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that reduces material waste by 15-20% in testbed environments and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated print production scenarios for educational use. The project aligns with the Communication and Journalism field’s growing emphasis on sustainable media production by bridging technical operations research with practical workforce training. Results will directly inform curriculum updates in graphic equipment operation courses, ensuring students engage with data-driven methodologies that reflect industry advancements. This work fills a critical gap in non-STEM computational applications by demonstrating how HPC can transform traditionally manual trade processes into precision-oriented, digitally integrated systems.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in obstetrics and gynecology by addressing critical gaps in predicting and managing adverse maternal-fetal outcomes. The clinical complexity of conditions such as preeclampsia, preterm birth, and gestational diabetes arises from multifactorial interactions between genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, and environmental factors. Current predictive models lack the resolution to integrate these heterogeneous data types at scale, limiting their utility in risk stratification and personalized intervention. To overcome this, we propose developing a unified computational framework that synthesizes multi-omics data (genome-wide association studies, methylation arrays, single-cell RNA sequencing) with real-world clinical data from electronic health records. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to identify predictive biomarkers and model dynamic risk trajectories across pregnancy. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of genomic data, optimizing hyperparameters in high-dimensional spaces, and running simulations to validate model robustness against demographic and clinical variability. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel biomarker panels for early detection of preeclampsia, a risk prediction tool deployable in clinical settings, and foundational insights into shared molecular pathways underlying disparate obstetric complications. By enabling large-scale integration of biological and clinical data, this work will accelerate translational discoveries, reduce health disparities through equitable risk modeling, and inform targeted therapeutic strategies. The requested computing infrastructure will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multi-institutional datasets, and parallelized pipeline execution to meet the computational demands of this initiative.
cip_definition: Research focused on Obstetrics and Gynecology

abstract: This project seeks to develop and deploy advanced computational methods to address high-dimensional optimization problems arising in the analysis of complex dynamical systems, with applications in materials science and biophysical modeling. The core challenge lies in efficiently solving non-convex, multiscale optimization frameworks that govern system behaviors, which are critical for predicting phase transitions in smart materials or protein folding dynamics. Traditional gradient-based solvers and Monte Carlo methods struggle with the curse of dimensionality and the non-smooth nature of these problems, limiting their utility for realistic, large-scale simulations. To overcome these barriers, we propose a hybrid approach combining neural operator networks with topology-driven optimization algorithms. The neural operators will be trained to approximate high-dimensional solution manifolds using precomputed simulation data, while a novel topology-aware optimization protocol, leveraging persistent homology, will guide the search for global minima in the landscape. Implementing this framework requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage two primary computational tasks: (1) parallelized generation of training data via distributed finite element simulations, and (2) iterative optimization cycles involving large-scale linear algebra operations on sparse matrices representing topological descriptors. The requested resources will enable scaling to systems with over 10^6 degrees of freedom, exceeding the capacity of local computing infrastructure. Success in this effort will yield a generalizable computational toolkit for high-dimensional optimization in applied mathematics, with immediate applications in designing metamaterials and understanding biomolecular dynamics. Outcomes will be disseminated as open-source software, along with benchmarking studies quantifying performance gains over existing methods. This work bridges theoretical advances in numerical analysis with practical HPC implementation, addressing a critical gap in computational applied mathematics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in applied mathematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the digital preservation and analysis of Latinx cultural narratives across media, with a focus on Mexican-American/Chicano and Puerto Rican diasporic communities. The research addresses a critical gap in accessible computational methodologies for analyzing large-scale, multilingual, and multimodal cultural archives—such as community oral histories, independent film, and social media—that reflect the dynamic interplay of identity, migration, and resistance within these groups. Current tools for text, audio, and visual analysis often fail to account for code-switching, regional vernaculars, or culturally specific symbolism, limiting their utility for Latinx studies. To address this, the project will deploy machine learning models optimized for Spanish-English code-switched speech-to-text transcription, alongside computer vision pipelines trained to recognize iconography in Chicano art and community murals. These workflows will be integrated into a scalable digital repository hosted on HPC infrastructure, enabling semantic search, network analysis of thematic trends, and geospatial mapping of cultural production across decades. Computational demands include GPU-accelerated training of multilingual transformer models, large-scale metadata processing, and high-throughput rendering of 3D-scanned cultural artifacts. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible platform for scholars and community stakeholders to engage with digitized collections, as well as new computational frameworks tailored to the linguistic and cultural nuances of Latinx materials. By centering technical innovation in service of community-driven narratives, this project aims to reshape digital humanities methodologies while safeguarding marginalized cultural knowledge against erasure. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data and ensure equitable access to tools that amplify Latinx voices in academic and public discourse.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Hispanic-American, Puerto Rican, Latinx, and Mexican-American/ Chicano Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic American immigrant populations within the U.S. and Canada, including Mexican-American Studies, Cuban American Studies, Puerto Rican Studies, and others.

abstract: This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying spatial memory consolidation, with a focus on hippocampal-prefrontal cortical interactions during sleep-associated replay. Current limitations in analyzing high-density electrophysiological data from simultaneous multi-region recordings and simulating large-scale neural networks hinder progress in understanding how synaptic plasticity rules integrate across brain systems to stabilize memory traces. We will develop a computational pipeline combining data-driven modeling and theory-driven simulations to address this gap. Electrophysiological datasets from rodents performing navigation tasks, including spike trains and local field potentials, will be processed using GPU-accelerated sorting algorithms and spectral analysis tools. These empirical data will parameterize a biologically detailed spiking neural network model of the hippocampus-prefrontal circuit, simulated using the NEST framework. The model will incorporate activity-dependent synaptic plasticity mechanisms and simulate replay events across sleep-wake cycles. Machine learning approaches, including graph-based analyses of functional connectivity dynamics, will identify critical network states predictive of memory retention metrics. By scaling simulations to replicate population-level interactions across 10^5 neurons, this work will resolve how system-specific oscillatory coupling (theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling) coordinates cross-regional memory consolidation. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for predicting memory stabilization thresholds and novel biomarkers of replay efficacy derived from network topology analyses. This resource-intensive approach is unfeasible without HPC capabilities due to the terabyte-scale electrophysiological data, real-time processing requirements for multi-channel recordings, and the need for parameter space exploration in neural simulations. The results will advance translational research on memory disorders by establishing quantitative links between cellular plasticity rules, large-scale network dynamics, and behavioral outcomes, while providing methodological innovations for integrating multimodal neuroscience data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biological bases of behavior and psychological functioning, and their application to experimental and therapeutic research problems. Includes instruction in functional neuroanatomy, neural system development, biochemical neural regulatory mechanisms, neurological biophysics, memory storage and retrieval, physiology of cognition and perception, physiological bases of psychopathology and behavioral disorders, psychopharmacology, comparative psychobiology, molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, and specialized experimental design and research methods.

abstract: Chronic pain is a multifaceted condition affecting millions globally, with substantial variability in individual treatment responses due to heterogeneous biological, psychological, and social factors. Current approaches to pain management often rely on trial-and-error strategies, leading to prolonged patient suffering, opioid dependence, and increased healthcare costs. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets and develop predictive models for personalized pain therapy. The research focuses on integrating genomic, neuroimaging, proteomic, and clinical data from patients with chronic pain to identify biomarkers of treatment response and uncover mechanisms underlying pain persistence. A key computational challenge lies in harmonizing high-dimensional, sparse datasets while accounting for patient-specific covariates. To achieve this, we will employ machine learning frameworks, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, optimized for parallel processing on HPC clusters. These models will be trained to predict analgesic efficacy and adverse event risk across diverse patient subgroups, with validation against longitudinal outcomes from electronic health records. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between pain-related protein targets and candidate therapeutics, enabling structure-based drug design. The HPC environment is critical for managing the scale of omics data (e.g., whole-genome sequencing, RNA expression matrices), accelerating iterative model training, and running large-scale simulations of neural network dynamics derived from functional MRI. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel combinatorial biomarkers for pain phenotyping, predictive algorithms for treatment matching, and atomistic insights into drug-target binding affinities. This work will establish a computational pipeline for precision pain medicine, directly informing clinical trial design and therapeutic decision-making. By elucidating the systems-level biology of pain, the project aims to reduce reliance on empirical treatment strategies and improve functional outcomes for patients with refractory pain conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of the entire range of painful disorders, either as a primary physician or consultant, for patients experiencing problems with acute, chronic, and/or cancer pain in both hospital and ambulatory settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Arabic linguistic and literary corpora. Arabic’s rich morphological complexity, dialectal diversity, and the historical breadth of its textual traditions present unique obstacles to large-scale analysis. Existing computational tools often inadequately handle Classical Arabic’s inflectional systems or fail to account for regional dialect variations, limiting the scalability of research on language evolution, stylistic patterns, and sociolinguistic dynamics. This project proposes the development and deployment of advanced natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to Arabic’s linguistic features, enabling the systematic study of multi-genre corpora spanning pre-Islamic poetry, medieval philosophical texts, Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) media, and contemporary dialectal speech. Computational methods will include the training of transformer-based models for dialect identification, graph-based algorithms for morphological parsing, and neural architectures for cross-period semantic shift detection. These workflows require HPC capabilities to process terabytes of text data, optimize deep learning models, and run parallelized analyses across heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible annotated corpus of Classical and MSA texts with dialectal annotations, (2) quantitative insights into syntactic and lexical changes between historical and modern Arabic registers, and (3) open-source tools for dialect-aware machine translation. By enabling unprecedented scale and precision in Arabic linguistic research, this project aims to advance scholarly understanding of the language’s development while supporting practical applications in language education, digital humanities, and region-specific NLP technologies. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive processing demands and reduce training times for complex models, which are infeasible with standard academic infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Arabic language. Includes instruction in philology; Classical Arabic; Modern Standard Arabic; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern railway systems, compounded by dynamic operational variables such as fluctuating demand, real-time disruptions, and stringent safety regulations, necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize network efficiency and reliability. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate large-scale railway operations, integrating real-time data streams, signal system dynamics, and hazardous material transport protocols. Current methodologies often rely on static models that fail to capture the interdependencies between scheduling, infrastructure constraints, and emergent risks, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and increased vulnerability to delays. The proposed research will employ parallelized agent-based simulations to model train movements, crew assignments, and switching operations across interconnected railyards, while machine learning algorithms will predict congestion patterns and optimize schedules under stochastic disturbances. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing clusters, the framework will perform Monte Carlo analyses to assess the probabilistic impact of extreme weather events, equipment failures, and cargo-specific hazards on network resilience. The anticipated outcomes include actionable insights into capacity expansion strategies, adaptive scheduling protocols, and risk mitigation measures tailored to heterogeneous railway environments. This work aims to establish a scalable computational platform that enhances decision-making for railway operators, reduces operational costs through predictive maintenance models, and improves compliance with safety standards outlined in the General Code of Operation rules. The integration of HPC resources is critical to achieving the requisite computational granularity and temporal resolution, enabling stakeholders to transition from reactive to proactive management paradigms in an increasingly interconnected transportation landscape.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation of railroads and other aspects of the railway industry, including railroad and railyard service. Includes instruction in railway culture, operating skills, General Code of Operation rules, conductor service, signal systems, switching, transportation of hazardous materials, safety, and railway telecommunications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to understand how rapid environmental change influences the stability of ecological networks and species coexistence mechanisms in biodiverse ecosystems. As anthropogenic disturbances and climate variability alter resource availability and species interactions, predicting community-level responses remains a critical challenge in environmental biology. We propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based models (ABMs) of multi-trophic interactions with spatially explicit dynamic vegetation models (DVMs) to simulate ecosystem responses under projected climate scenarios. The ABMs will parameterize species-specific traits, including dispersal capacity, phenological shifts, and niche breadth, derived from empirical datasets spanning tropical and temperate forest inventories. DVMs will integrate regional climate projections (CMIP6) and soil hydrology data to simulate abiotic drivers at mesoscale resolutions (1–10 km²). High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve the stochastic, high-dimensional interactions inherent to these simulations, particularly for scaling individual-level processes to landscape-level patterns over decadal timeframes. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess variance in community resilience metrics across >10,000 parameter combinations, while machine learning algorithms (random forests, gradient-boosted regression trees) will identify key predictors of ecosystem collapse thresholds. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of biodiversity hotspots at elevated risk under IPCC warming scenarios, validated against long-term ecological monitoring data from established forest dynamics plots. By quantifying nonlinear feedbacks between species traits and environmental filters, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of extinction cascades while informing habitat corridor designs for climate-vulnerable taxa. The generated models and code will be optimized for open-source distribution, providing a transferable toolkit for conservation planning in understudied biodiverse regions.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the origins, functions, relationships, interactions, and natural history of living populations, communities, species, and ecosystems in relation to dynamic environmental processes. Includes instruction in biodiversity, molecular genetic and genomic evolution, mesoscale ecology, computational biology and modeling, conservation biology, local and global environmental change, and restoration ecology.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of real-time financial data processing in modern accounting ecosystems, where traditional bookkeeping frameworks struggle to scale efficiently amid increasing transaction volumes, multi-source data integration demands, and evolving regulatory requirements. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop and test a novel computational architecture for automated ledger reconciliation and anomaly detection in distributed accounting environments. The core challenge lies in processing heterogeneous financial datasets—including blockchain-based smart contracts, IoT-enabled supply chain transactions, and multi-currency operational records—while maintaining audit trails and compliance safeguards. Our methodology combines graph-based transaction mapping algorithms with federated learning models to enable secure, decentralized validation of accounting events across organizational boundaries. The computational workflow will simulate enterprise-scale accounting networks using parallelized Monte Carlo methods to stress-test system resilience under varying transaction loads (50,000–5 million daily events) and adversarial scenarios. Key innovations include the integration of dynamic accrual accounting heuristics into streaming data pipelines and the development of probabilistic consensus mechanisms for inter-organizational ledger synchronization. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for real-time accounting system scalability, quantitative metrics for computational resource allocation in automated bookkeeping deployments, and open-source modules for anomaly detection latency optimization. By establishing performance baselines for next-generation accounting infrastructures, this work aims to inform both technological standards and regulatory guidance for emergent paradigms in decentralized finance (DeFi) integration and AI-driven auditing practices. The requested HPC resources are critical for maintaining experimental fidelity given the combinatorial complexity of multi-agent financial simulations and the need for cryptographic operations at scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical administrative support to professional accountants and other financial management personnel. Includes instruction in posting transactions to accounts, record-keeping systems, accounting software operation, and general accounting principles and practices.

abstract: This project addresses the computational challenges of analyzing semantic evolution in Czech technical vocabulary from the late 19th century to the present, a process shaped by rapid technological advancements but underexplored due to the scale and complexity of historical textual data. Traditional methods struggle to systematically track contextual shifts across decades, particularly in specialized domains such as engineering, medicine, and information technology, where lexical innovation and repurposing are prevalent. We propose a computational linguistics approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze a diachronic corpus of Czech technical texts, including manuals, academic journals, and industry periodicals, alongside literary works incorporating technical discourse. The corpus will be digitized, normalized, and annotated using NLP tools adapted for historical Czech orthography and morphosyntax. Transformer-based models (e.g., BERT) will be fine-tuned to generate temporally sensitive word embeddings, enabling quantitative analysis of semantic drift through methods such as dynamic visualization of vector space trajectories and cosine similarity metrics across time slices. HPC resources are critical for training these models on terabytes of text and running parallelized simulations to test hypotheses about the interplay between technological change and lexical adaptation. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of semantic shift metrics for key terms, computational workflows adaptable to other under-resourced languages, and new insights into how Czech technical registers have negotiated cross-linguistic influences (e.g., German, English) while maintaining distinctiveness. This research will directly support pedagogical tools for technical Czech instruction and inform lexicographical updates to reflect historical usage patterns, bridging gaps between linguistic scholarship and applied language industries.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Czech language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that optimize decision-making processes in educational supervision and curriculum administration. A critical challenge in educational leadership is the dynamic allocation of instructional resources—such as staff, training, and curricular materials—across diverse learning environments. Traditional methods for modeling these complex systems are limited in scalability and fail to account for real-time variables, including fluctuating student needs, staff capacity, and interdisciplinary program requirements. To address this gap, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate interactions between administrators, educators, and students under varying resource constraints, using anonymized district-level datasets on staffing patterns, student performance, and budget allocations. Second, machine learning algorithms will identify optimal supervisory strategies by analyzing historical outcomes and iteratively refining predictive models. The HPC environment is essential for processing large-scale datasets (spanning 10+ years from 200+ institutions) and running parallel simulations to evaluate thousands of resource allocation scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for real-time decision support in curriculum supervision, validated through retrospective comparison with existing administrative data. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing inefficiencies in staff deployment and curricular resource distribution, directly addressing priorities in education leadership training programs. By open-sourcing the computational tools developed, the project aims to establish a replicable methodology for data-driven supervision in K-12 and higher education settings, advancing the integration of computational analytics into administrative practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise instructional and support personnel at the school building, facility or staff level. Includes instruction in the principles of staffing and organization, the supervision of learning activities, personnel relations, administrative duties related to departmental or unit management, and specific applications to various educational settings and curricula.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a novel computational framework to model and optimize dynamic financial ecosystems under high-dimensional uncertainty, with a focus on integrating real-time accounting data streams into adaptive risk-assessment systems. The core problem lies in the inability of traditional financial models to process granular, time-sensitive transactional data (e.g., blockchain-enabled ledgers, IoT-enabled supply chain finance signals) at scale while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory accounting standards. We propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations enhanced by quantum-inspired optimization algorithms, and natural language processing (NLP) to parse regulatory documents. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simultaneously simulate millions of interacting financial agents, model cascading risk scenarios across heterogeneous accounting frameworks (IFRS vs. GAAP), and train neural networks to detect emerging compliance patterns in real-time audit trails. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable architecture for stress-testing financial resilience under concurrent operational, geopolitical, and sustainability reporting constraints, 2) probabilistic estimates of systemic accounting disclosure risks in decentralized finance networks, and 3) open-source tools for automating materiality threshold adjustments in continuously closing ledgers. This work bridges computational finance, regulatory technology, and accounting information systems, offering practitioners a decision-support platform to navigate volatile multi-stakeholder environments while maintaining auditability. The requested HPC resources will enable unprecedented temporal resolution (<10ms event granularity) and spatial complexity (>10^6 agent interactions) in simulating next-generation financial ecosystems where accounting integrity directly determines systemic stability.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and finance that prepares individuals to function as accountants and financial managers or analysts.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in complex, multi-stakeholder projects, addressing a critical gap in project management methodologies. Traditional resource allocation models often fail to account for real-time uncertainties, interdependent task networks, and competing stakeholder priorities, leading to cost overruns and delays. We propose an integrative approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to analyze how resource allocation strategies impact project outcomes under varying constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale simulations of project scenarios, including parametric variations in team composition, budget reallocations, and risk event cascades. Using historical project data from construction and IT sectors, neural networks will be trained to predict resource bottlenecks, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize allocation policies. The computational workflow will incorporate domain-specific parameters such as earned value management metrics, stakeholder influence networks, and risk exposure thresholds. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between resource allocation strategies and project success criteria (e.g., time, cost, quality). This work will advance project management practice by enabling data-driven, adaptive resource planning in environments with high uncertainty. The resulting models and open-source simulation toolkit will provide empirical insights into how granular resource decisions propagate through project lifecycles, benefiting both industry practitioners and academic research in adaptive project governance. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this study aims to overcome computational limitations that have previously restricted the scale and granularity of resource allocation analyses in business contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply quantitative and qualitative knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage projects in a wide range of fields and occupations. Includes instruction in project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy consumption and guest experience trade-offs in smart hotel environments, leveraging real-time IoT sensor data and predictive behavioral analytics. Modern hotels face escalating operational costs due to energy-intensive systems (HVAC, lighting, water heating) while simultaneously needing to meet rising guest expectations for personalized comfort. Traditional management approaches rely on static schedules or heuristic rules, failing to account for dynamic factors such as fluctuating occupancy patterns, microclimate variations, or individual guest preferences inferred from digital interactions. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) model trained on multi-modal data streams—including room occupancy sensors, energy meters, weather APIs, and anonymized guest app usage patterns—to autonomously coordinate building management systems. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to simulate hotel environments through digital twins, enabling parallel training of RL agents across diverse operational scenarios (seasonal demand shifts, event-driven occupancy spikes, equipment failure states). Computational challenges include processing high-frequency sensor data (sampled every 5 seconds across 500+ simulated rooms), maintaining low-latency inference for real-time control, and ensuring interpretability of AI-driven decisions for managerial oversight. Expected outcomes include a scalable optimization engine capable of reducing energy waste by 18-25% while maintaining guest satisfaction metrics, quantified through simulated A/B testing against conventional strategies. This work bridges hospitality operations research with computational sustainability science, offering a novel decision-support tool for an industry increasingly pressured to balance economic constraints with environmental stewardship and service quality imperatives. The resulting models and simulation datasets will be made available to advance research in smart hospitality infrastructure, particularly for independent hotels lacking corporate R&D resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage and control; hotel facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; marketing and sales promotion; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotels and motel operations.

abstract: The proposed research aims to advance precision rehabilitation in physical therapy by developing a computational framework to model neuromuscular adaptation during recovery from traumatic brain injury (TBI). Current clinical protocols for restoring motor function rely on generalized exercise regimens, which inadequately address the heterogenous neurophysiological and biomechanical profiles of patients. This project seeks to overcome this limitation by integrating patient-specific neuroimaging data, electromyography (EMG) signals, and motion capture kinematics into a multiscale simulation environment. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the coupled dynamics of neural circuit reorganization, muscle activation patterns, and joint-level mechanics at temporal resolutions necessary to capture adaptive processes. A hybrid computational approach will be employed, combining finite element modeling of corticospinal tract lesion effects, dynamic musculoskeletal simulations via OpenSim, and reinforcement learning algorithms to predict optimal therapeutic exercise parameters. The framework will be trained and validated against longitudinal data from a cohort of 50 TBI patients undergoing rehabilitation. Key outcomes include a validated predictive model of neuromuscular adaptation trajectories and an open-source tool for generating patient-specific exercise progressions. By linking neuroplasticity mechanisms to functional movement outcomes, this work addresses a critical gap in personalized rehabilitation strategies. The computational pipeline will enable clinicians to tailor interventions based on individual neural recovery rates and biomechanical constraints, potentially reducing long-term disability burdens. This interdisciplinary project bridges neurorehabilitation, computational biomechanics, and machine learning, advancing a niche at the intersection of health sciences and high-performance computing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate, examine, diagnose, and alleviate physical functional impairments and limitations caused by injury or disease through the design and implementation of therapeutic interventions to promote fitness and health. Includes instruction in anatomy, behavioral sciences, biology, biomechanics, biophysical agents, care plan development and documentation, cellular histology, clinical evaluation and measurement, clinical reasoning, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, pharmacology, pathology, physiology, professional standards and ethics, rehabilitation psychology, and therapeutic exercise.

abstract: This project investigates the biomechanical and biochemical dynamics of plant root exudate-mediated mineral weathering in oligotrophic environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model microscale interactions between root systems and heterogeneous soil matrices. While plant-microbe interactions are well studied, the direct role of root exudates in dissolving mineral substrates to access trace nutrients—a critical process for survival in nutrient-poor ecosystems—remains poorly quantified at the systems level. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of exudate diffusion, mineral dissolution kinetics, and root membrane transport processes occurring simultaneously across root architectures. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating finite element modeling of exudate dispersion, reactive transport simulations of mineral weathering, and dynamic nutrient uptake algorithms calibrated via experimental data from specialized lithophytic plants. HPC resources will enable 3D simulations of entire root networks interacting with realistic soil mineralogies, incorporating stochastic variability in pore-scale hydrology and exudation patterns. Parallelized parameter sweeps will assess how exudate composition (organic acids, reductants) and root hair morphology synergistically enhance phosphorus and iron acquisition from apatite and iron oxide substrates. Expected outcomes include predictive models of plant-driven mineral weathering efficiency under drought and acidic conditions, with applications in developing bioinspired strategies for sustainable crop cultivation in marginal soils. The computational toolkit developed will also advance broader efforts to quantify plants as geochemical agents, bridging gaps between botany, geobiology, and subsurface reactive transport modeling. By elucidating mechanisms underlying plant-rock interactions at unprecedented resolution, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for studying nutrient acquisition strategies in extreme environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in botany/plant biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Prosthodontic rehabilitation relies on the precise integration of biomechanical principles with patient-specific anatomical and functional demands. However, current computational models for simulating the biomechanical behavior of dental implants, prostheses, and associated tissues lack the resolution to predict long-term performance under dynamic physiological conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing multiscale, patient-specific computational models to optimize prosthodontic device design and treatment planning. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform finite element analysis (FEA) of stress distribution in bone-implant systems, molecular dynamics simulations of interfacial interactions between implant surfaces and biological tissues, and machine learning-driven predictive modeling of clinical outcomes. Key challenges include modeling the heterogeneous viscoelastic properties of bone and soft tissues, simulating micro-scale osseointegration processes, and integrating real-world data from intraoral scans, CBCT imaging, and occlusal force sensors. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across multiple spatial and temporal scales, significantly reducing computational bottlenecks inherent in conventional single-node systems. Expected outcomes include (1) validated computational frameworks for predicting biomechanical failure risks in implant-supported prostheses, (2) optimized surface topography designs for enhanced osseointegration in compromised bone conditions, and (3) AI-driven treatment planning algorithms that account for patient-specific factors such as bone density, occlusal patterns, and systemic health parameters. This work will provide novel insights into the mechanobiological principles governing prosthodontic success while establishing scalable computational workflows for personalized restorative dentistry. The resulting tools aim to reduce prosthetic complications, improve functional and aesthetic outcomes, and inform evidence-based clinical guidelines—advancing the field toward data-driven, precision prosthodontics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the restoration and maintenance of teeth, oral function, and aesthetic form through the use of single or compound materials, structures, and artificial devices. Includes instruction in implant dentistry, surgical procedures, denture design and fabrication, fixed and removable prosthodontics, restorative techniques, occlusion therapy and devices, geriatric dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in metal fabrication processes, specifically the prediction and mitigation of thermal distortion and residual stress in welded structures—a persistent issue affecting dimensional accuracy, material integrity, and production costs. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to optimizing fabrication parameters are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in generalizability. To overcome these constraints, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-physics interactions during welding and thermal cutting processes. The research will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models incorporating transient heat transfer, phase transformations, and thermo-mechanical coupling, validated against experimental data from controlled welding trials. HPC resources will enable parametric studies at unprecedented scales, simulating diverse material grades (ferrous and non-ferrous), joint geometries, and process conditions (e.g., heat input, cooling rates). Machine learning techniques will further analyze simulation outputs to identify optimal parameter sets minimizing distortion while maintaining structural performance. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for fabricators to preemptively adjust manufacturing variables, reducing scrap rates and post-weld corrections by an estimated 20–30%. The project will also generate open-access datasets on thermo-mechanical behavior of hybrid materials, addressing a gap in publicly available fabrication data. By integrating computational modeling with empirical validation, this work aims to advance precision in metal fabrication, lower production costs, and contribute to sustainable manufacturing practices. The scalability of the developed models will support future research into additive manufacturing and advanced alloy systems, reinforcing the role of computational resources in modernizing technical education and industry workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to further process ferrous and/or non-ferrous metal plates or shapes, and to manufacture and/or install products as interpreted through technical drawings. Includes instruction in trade tools, shop equipment, reading and interpreting blueprints, material handling, welding, thermal cutting, metallurgy, template pattern development, plate and structural fabrication, destructive and non-destructive testing, inspection, shipment preparation and fabrication installation.

abstract: The emergence and persistence of zoonotic infectious diseases present complex challenges to veterinary and public health, demanding advanced tools to unravel pathogen evolution, host-pathogen interactions, and transmission dynamics. Traditional experimental approaches often struggle to address the multi-scale complexity of these systems, particularly when analyzing high-dimensional genomic data, simulating population-level disease spread, or predicting antigenic evolution in rapidly mutating pathogens. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative computational models that bridge molecular, ecological, and epidemiological scales. We will focus on three priority areas: (1) phylogenetic reconstruction and machine learning to identify evolutionary drivers of virulence in avian influenza viruses across poultry and wild bird reservoirs, (2) molecular dynamics simulations of host receptor binding in coronaviruses affecting livestock to predict cross-species transmission risks, and (3) agent-based modeling of vector-borne disease outbreaks (e.g., Rift Valley fever) under varying climate and land-use scenarios. The computational workflows will incorporate next-generation sequencing data from field surveillance, structural proteomics, and geospatial environmental variables, requiring parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets. HPC resources will enable the use of ensemble modeling techniques to quantify uncertainty in outbreak predictions and parameterize intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for identifying high-risk pathogen variants, mapping transmission hotspots, and optimizing vaccine target selection. By elucidating mechanisms of antibody resistance in retroviruses and vector competence dynamics, this work will directly inform One Health strategies for disease prevention in agricultural systems while advancing computational methodologies for pathogen surveillance. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale genomic alignment, and real-time analytics pipelines critical for translating computational insights into actionable veterinary interventions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of zoonotic infectious diseases, disease mechanisms, and prevention and treatment strategies. Includes instruction in disease pathogenesis, vector biology, mycobacterial infection, blood parasites, retroviruses, food-borne diseases, new infectious agents, ecotoxicology, mechanisms of disease transfer, antibody resistance, comparative pathology, communicable diseases, and disease prevention and eradication.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate dysregulated intracellular signaling networks that drive cancer cell proliferation and metastasis, with a focus on ion channel-mediated calcium signaling in tumor microenvironments. Despite established links between calcium dynamics and oncogenic pathways, the spatiotemporal regulation of these signals across cell populations remains poorly understood due to experimental limitations in capturing multiscale physiological interactions. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop agent-based models integrating molecular-scale ion channel kinetics, subcellular calcium wave propagation, and tissue-scale mechanical signaling. Computational frameworks will incorporate experimental data from live-cell imaging and patch-clamp electrophysiology of breast cancer models to parameterize stochastic channel behaviors and receptor crosstalk. Key objectives include simulating how hypoxia-induced channelopathies alter calcium-dependent transcription factors (e.g., NFAT) and quantifying emergent patterns of collective cell migration. The HPC environment is critical for executing ensemble simulations across parameter spaces characterizing heterogeneous cell states, requiring parallelized computation of 10⁵–10⁶ interacting cellular agents over physiologically relevant timescales (hours to days). Expected outcomes include identification of network motifs that amplify pro-metastatic signaling and predictive maps of microenvironmental factors promoting therapy-resistant phenotypes. These results will directly inform ongoing wet-lab investigations targeting intercellular calcium synchronization as a vulnerability in invasive cancers. By bridging molecular biophysics with tissue-level pathophysiology, this work aims to establish computational pipelines for probing multiscale dysregulation in solid tumors, ultimately advancing strategies to disrupt metastatic signaling while preserving normal physiological functions. The requested resources will enable parameter sensitivity analyses, validation against single-cell omics datasets, and 3D simulation of organotypic tumor models at unprecedented resolution.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of physiological processes operating within and among cells, and intracellular communication and behavior, in the context of larger systems and whole organisms. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology, molecular physiology, cell cycle control, signal transduction, protein structure, membrane biochemistry and structure, ion channel physics, cell respiration and digestion, secretory functions, cell adhesion and communication, information encoding and decoding, and the relation of cell physiology to tissue, organ, and organismic functioning.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Baltic languages, with a focus on understudied and extinct varieties such as Old Prussian and Curionian. Despite their historical and cultural significance, these languages remain underrepresented in digital philology and natural language processing (NLP) research due to fragmented textual records, non-standard orthographies, and limited computational tools tailored to their linguistic features. The research problem centers on reconstructing phonological, morphological, and syntactic patterns in these languages to advance scholarly understanding of their evolution and interrelationships. To achieve this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process digitized corpora of historical texts, inscriptions, and comparative data from extant Baltic languages. Computational methods will include the development of transformer-based models for automated morphological parsing, phylogenetic algorithms to model language divergence, and semantic network analysis to trace lexical shifts across time and dialects. The scale of data—spanning centuries of textual fragments and multilingual parallel texts—requires distributed computing for efficient storage, preprocessing, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Old Prussian and Curionian texts, probabilistic reconstructions of unattested phonological systems, and open-source NLP pipelines optimized for Baltic language structures. These resources will directly support philological research, language revitalization initiatives, and applications in cross-lingual information retrieval for regional archives. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological expertise, the project aims to establish a methodological framework for analyzing low-resource historical languages, with implications for both Baltic studies and digital humanities methodologies. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage memory-intensive tasks, such as training deep learning models on heterogeneous textual data and running large-scale comparative simulations, which cannot feasibly be executed on local infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of the Baltic peoples, including, but not limited to, the modern languages of Latvian and Lithuanian, and extinct languages such as Old Prussian and Curionian. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the acoustic and biomechanical interactions between brass instrumentalists and their instruments through high-fidelity computational modeling, addressing gaps in understanding how physiological variables influence sound production and artistic expression. While traditional pedagogical methods in brass performance emphasize empirical techniques, the complex interplay of airflow dynamics, embouchure mechanics, and instrument resonance remains underexplored at a quantitative level. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multiphysics models integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airflow, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural vibrations, and machine learning to correlate physiological inputs with acoustic outputs. These models will simulate real-world performance scenarios, including dynamic pitch modulation, articulation variations, and extended techniques (e.g., flutter tonguing), while accounting for anatomical differences among players. Validation will involve synchronizing simulation data with motion-capture and pressure-sensor measurements from live performances. The computational intensity of resolving microsecond-scale fluid-structure interactions across anatomically accurate geometries necessitates scalable parallel computing and GPU-accelerated solvers. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to map embouchure configurations and respiratory strategies to timbral qualities, enabling objective feedback tools for pedagogy. Additionally, the project aims to generate open-access datasets linking biomechanical parameters to acoustic signatures, fostering innovation in instrument design and performance practice. By bridging computational engineering and musical artistry, this work will establish a foundation for data-driven approaches to brass performance research while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in advancing performing arts scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a brass instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to improve the predictive accuracy of high-impact weather systems in a changing climate by advancing the resolution and physical representation of atmospheric processes in regional climate models. Current models struggle to resolve critical mesoscale phenomena, such as convective initiation, cloud-aerosol interactions, and extreme precipitation dynamics, which are exacerbated by climate change. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model coupled with a cloud-resolving configuration, targeting horizontal resolutions of 1-3 km over North American hotspot regions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to conduct decade-long climate simulations that explicitly resolve storm-scale dynamics and microphysical processes, which are typically parameterized in coarser models. The computational workflow will leverage ensemble-based sensitivity analysis to quantify uncertainties in boundary conditions and cloud microphysics schemes, requiring ~10,000 core-hours per ensemble member. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to downscale global climate model outputs, refining boundary conditions for the regional simulations. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how localized extreme precipitation and severe storm regimes respond to warming scenarios, reduced biases in modeled cloud feedbacks, and improved quantification of prediction uncertainties. The resulting datasets will support the development of next-generation parameterizations for climate models and provide actionable data for regional resilience planning. This work demands access to HPC infrastructure capable of managing petabytes of output data, parallelized model execution across thousands of cores, and GPU-accelerated post-processing. The resource allocation will directly enable transformative progress in bridging the gap between climate projections and actionable regional-scale weather extremes forecasting.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition and behavior of the atmospheric envelopes surrounding the earth, the effect of earth's atmosphere on terrestrial weather, and related problems of environment and climate. Includes instruction in atmospheric chemistry and physics, atmospheric dynamics, climatology and climate change, weather simulation, weather forecasting, climate modeling and mathematical theory; and studies of specific phenomena such as clouds, weather systems, storms, and precipitation patterns.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the longitudinal efficacy of digital engagement strategies in contemporary youth ministry, focusing on the interplay between spiritual development, psychosocial dynamics, and technology-mediated communication. While youth ministry traditionally operates through in-person community building, the proliferation of digital platforms—especially among Generation Z and Alpha cohorts—has created complex, data-rich environments that challenge conventional pastoral approaches. The research problem centers on mapping how asynchronous and synchronous digital interactions (e.g., virtual small groups, gamified spiritual practices, AI-driven counseling chatbots) influence measurable outcomes in youth resilience, ethical decision-making, and communal belonging. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP) of anonymized pastoral counseling transcripts, agent-based modeling (ABM) of social network dynamics within virtual youth groups, and machine learning (ML) analysis of multimodal engagement metrics (app usage patterns, biometric wearables data from retreat participants). The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of unstructured text, audio, and video data from partnered ministry organizations, simulating large-scale network interactions, and training deep learning models to identify latent patterns in spiritual maturation trajectories. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for optimizing digital ministry interventions, a taxonomy of risk/resilience factors in online spiritual communities, and novel ethical frameworks for AI integration in faith-based youth contexts. By bridging computational social science, developmental psychology, and practical theology, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for data-driven pastoral care while advancing interdisciplinary dialogue on technology’s role in humanistic formation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to children, adolescents, and young adults. Includes instruction in child and adolescent psychology, human growth and development, family studies, communication skills, religious education, youth counseling, small group leadership, planning and organizing youth activities, volunteer supervision, and youth evangelism and worship.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive analytics framework for optimizing resource allocation in small businesses operating within hyperlocal, niche markets. While small businesses are critical to economic ecosystems, those in specialized sectors—such as artisanal manufacturing, microgreen agriculture, or bespoke digital services—face unique challenges in balancing operational scalability with niche market demands. Traditional business analytics tools often fail to account for the high-dimensional, nonlinear interactions between localized consumer behavior, microsupply chain volatility, and resource constraints. This research addresses this gap by constructing agent-based models (ABMs) and stochastic optimization algorithms to simulate decision-making scenarios under uncertainty. The computational approach integrates real-time data streams (e.g., social media sentiment, hyperlocal weather patterns, microinventory databases) with machine learning techniques to forecast demand-supply mismatches and recommend adaptive strategies. HPC resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of interdependent variables across diverse small business archetypes while maintaining sub-second latency for scenario testing. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit that enables small businesses to dynamically allocate human capital, inventory, and financial resources in response to micro-market shifts. The project also aims to quantify the economic resilience gained through computationally guided decision-making, with potential applications in policy design for small business support programs. By bridging computational economics and small business strategy, this work advances a novel paradigm for data-driven entrepreneurship in underserved market niches.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage independent small businesses. Includes instruction in business administration; enterprise planning and entrepreneurship; start-up; small business operations and problems; personnel supervision; capitalization and investment; taxation; business law and regulations; e-commerce; home business operations; and applications to specific sectors, products, and services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced diagnostic and optimization frameworks for computer hardware systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and analyze complex hardware interactions. Current methodologies in computer installation and repair often rely on manual testing and static troubleshooting protocols, which can be time-intensive and fail to account for dynamic, system-wide interactions between components such as power supplies, memory architectures, and peripheral devices. To address this, we propose a computational approach utilizing parallelized simulations to model stress scenarios, thermal dynamics, and failure propagation across heterogeneous hardware configurations. By deploying finite element analysis (FEA) for thermal and mechanical stress modeling, alongside Monte Carlo methods to predict component failure probabilities under varying workloads, this research aims to identify optimal hardware configurations and preemptive maintenance strategies. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and empirical datasets to classify failure patterns and recommend repair protocols. The HPC environment is critical to this work, as it enables large-scale parameter sweeps across processor architectures, power delivery systems, and network interfaces, which would otherwise be computationally prohibitive. Expected outcomes include open-source diagnostic tools that integrate predictive analytics for technicians, reducing equipment downtime and repair costs. Furthermore, the project will generate a publicly accessible database of simulated hardware failure scenarios, enhancing educational resources for workforce training programs. By bridging computational modeling with practical repair techniques, this research advances the technical precision of computer maintenance workflows and supports the development of adaptive, data-driven repair standards in the industry.
cip_title: Computer Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair computers and related instruments. Includes instruction in power supplies, number systems, memory structure, buffers and registers, microprocessor design, peripheral equipment, programming, and networking.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing decentralized data ecosystems in multi-stakeholder business environments, where fragmented information systems hinder real-time decision-making and resource efficiency. As organizations increasingly rely on distributed data sources—such as IoT devices, third-party vendors, and cross-platform transactions—managing these heterogeneous systems while maintaining compliance, security, and operational agility remains computationally intractable with conventional infrastructure. The study proposes a novel framework integrating federated machine learning, adaptive graph-based resource allocation algorithms, and privacy-preserving analytics to enable dynamic coordination of computational workflows across organizational boundaries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for simulating large-scale, multi-agent business environments (modeling 10,000+ concurrent entities) and training deep reinforcement learning models that optimize data routing, storage prioritization, and latency-sensitive processing under varying regulatory constraints. The computational methodology combines agent-based modeling of supply chain networks with graph neural networks to predict system-wide bottlenecks, coupled with quantum-inspired optimization techniques for resource distribution. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for sustainable data governance in federated business ecosystems, validated through case studies in healthcare logistics and circular economy platforms. Results will provide quantitative benchmarks for interoperability standards while advancing computational techniques to balance information utility with ethical AI requirements. This work directly supports the IRM discipline by developing scalable methods for systems integration in privacy-critical environments, with particular emphasis on adaptive contracting mechanisms and energy-efficient data lifecycle management. The requested HPC allocation enables experimentation at realistic scales, which is unfeasible with traditional cloud infrastructure due to memory-intensive graph computations and the need for secure, isolated processing environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of information technology, computer systems management, and business operations to the planning, management, and evaluation of information services in organizations. Includes instruction in telecommunications, systems planning and integration, information policy, information security, contracting and purchasing, budgeting, information technology, operations management, human resources, communications skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Polish dialectology and literary analysis, addressing gaps in large-scale, data-driven studies of the Polish language. While Polish regional dialects and historical literary corpora are rich subjects for linguistic inquiry, their complexity and volume have limited systematic analysis through traditional methods. This research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to analyze two key datasets: a multi-regional corpus of spoken and written contemporary Polish dialects, and a digitized collection of 19th- and 20th-century Polish literary texts. The first component focuses on dialect classification, using neural models to map phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variations across regions, while the second investigates stylistic evolution and intertextual patterns in literature. Computational challenges include training transformer-based models on non-standard orthography, handling dialectal code-switching in transcribed speech, and detecting subtle stylistic features across decades of literary production. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of text and audio data, optimizing hyperparameters for domain-specific models, and running parallelized analyses of linguistic features. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access dialect atlas visualizing regional language variation, (2) quantitative frameworks for tracking literary style shifts in response to sociohistorical contexts, and (3) annotated datasets to support future Slavic NLP applications. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to reveal previously inaccessible patterns in language change and cultural expression, while strengthening infrastructure for digital scholarship in Polish studies. Results will inform both academic research and applied domains, such as improving automated tools for Polish dialect recognition and preservation.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between biomineralization processes and microbial community resilience in extreme saline environments, integrating geochemical, microbiological, and materials science approaches. The central challenge lies in understanding how microbial metabolic networks adapt to hypersaline conditions while simultaneously mediating the nucleation and growth of complex mineral phases—a process with implications for biogeochemical cycling, subsurface energy storage, and the design of stress-resistant biohybrid materials. Current models lack the resolution to capture feedback loops between genetic regulation, ion transport kinetics, and emergent mineral-microbe architectures at relevant spatiotemporal scales. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining molecular dynamics simulations of ion-protein interactions under high ionic strength, genome-scale metabolic modeling of halophilic consortia, and reactive transport models informed by microfluidics-derived mineral growth parameters. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: (1) simulating interfacial water dynamics during mineral nucleation at saline interfaces (requiring >1 million core-hours for all-atom simulations across gradient conditions), (2) optimizing community-scale metabolic networks through parallelized flux balance analysis across 10^4+ parameter combinations, and (3) resolving micrometer-to-meter scale mineral deposition patterns via GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods. Expected outcomes include predictive models of microbially enhanced mineral carbonation under high-salinity stress, identification of genetic markers for coupled stress tolerance and mineralization capacity, and open-source tools for simulating biofilm-mineral composite formation. This work will provide foundational insights into extreme environment biogeochemistry while advancing computational methods for interfacial processes in multi-kingdom systems. The resulting frameworks could inform strategies for carbon sequestration in saline aquifers and the engineering of adaptive biomaterials for harsh operational environments.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on one or more of the physical and biological sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance our understanding of dynamic neural network dysfunction in neuropsychiatric disorders, with a focus on schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders. Current limitations in modeling large-scale brain circuits at cellular resolution hinder progress in identifying mechanisms underlying aberrant synaptic plasticity and oscillatory activity. To address this, we propose multiscale computational simulations integrating biophysically detailed neuron models with macro-scale network dynamics. The research will utilize NEURON and NEST simulators to reconstruct cortical-subcortical circuits, incorporating empirical data from electrophysiology, fMRI, and postmortem transcriptomics to parameterize disease-specific perturbations. A key innovation involves simulating the interplay between neuromodulatory systems (e.g., dopaminergic and glutamatergic signaling) and emergent network states across spatiotemporal scales. HPC resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of parameter space exploration, requiring parallelized execution of millions of in silico experiments. Expected outcomes include identification of critical circuit nodes driving pathological beta/gamma oscillations and predictive models linking molecular alterations to network-level dysfunction. The computational framework will be validated against clinical EEG datasets using machine learning techniques to detect signature patterns of network dysregulation. This work will provide foundational insights into transdiagnostic mechanisms of neuropsychiatric disease while establishing an open-access modeling platform for the neuroscience community. Successful implementation demands sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time simulation scaling and high-memory nodes for processing whole-brain functional connectivity matrices. The proposed resource allocation will directly support the development of novel computational biomarkers and accelerate therapeutic target discovery through in silico screening of network-stabilizing interventions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interdisciplinary scientific study of the molecular, structural, physiologic, cognitive, and behavioral aspects of the brain and nervous system. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, molecular and biochemical bases of information processing, behavioral neuroscience, biology of neuropsychiatric disorders, and applications to the clinical sciences and biomedical engineering.

abstract: Livestock breeding programs face increasing complexity in integrating multi-omics data to optimize genetic selection while balancing productivity, health, and sustainability goals. Current genomic prediction models struggle to efficiently process large-scale datasets encompassing genotypes, phenotypes, metabolomics, and environmental variables, particularly for traits with non-additive genetic architectures. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy advanced machine learning frameworks for predictive modeling of complex traits in cattle. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture gene interaction networks and transformer-based architectures to model temporal patterns in longitudinal production data. The workflow will integrate existing genomic databases from 50,000 Holstein cattle with new hyperspectral imaging data quantifying meat and milk quality traits. Computational experiments will benchmark model performance against traditional genomic selection methods, with validation through CRISPR-edited cell lines. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized training across thousands of genomic loci, reducing runtime for genome-wide association analyses from weeks to days.
