Expected outcomes include optimized neural architecture configurations for polygenic trait prediction and open-source tools for efficient parameter tuning in agricultural genomics. Successful implementation will advance precision breeding strategies to enhance disease resistance and nutrient utilization efficiency in livestock, directly supporting sustainable animal protein production. By establishing scalable pipelines for multi-omics data integration, this work will provide a template for computational genomics applications across agricultural sciences, bridging the gap between high-throughput biological data and practical breeding decisions. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory nodes for genome assembly tasks, and secure storage for sensitive agricultural data.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding and husbandry of agricultural animals, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural animal products. Includes instruction in the animal sciences, animal husbandry and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize precision anesthetic dosing through the development of a machine learning (ML) framework integrating genetic, physiological, and clinical data to predict individual responses to anesthetic agents. Current dosing protocols rely on population-level pharmacokinetic models that inadequately account for genetic polymorphisms affecting drug metabolism (e.g., CYP450 variants) or dynamic intraoperative variables such as hemodynamic fluctuations and tissue oxygenation. The resulting dosing inaccuracies contribute to adverse outcomes, including postoperative delirium and prolonged recovery. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning models on retrospective electronic health records (n ≈ 50,000 surgical cases), genomic datasets from pre-anesthesia testing, and high-frequency intraoperative biosensor data. Recurrent neural networks will process temporal physiological signals, while transformer-based architectures will analyze heterogeneous inputs (genetic variants, comorbidities, drug histories) to predict real-time drug effect-site concentrations. Parallelized pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations will generate synthetic training data to address clinical dataset sparsity. The computational workflow requires GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and large-memory nodes for genome-wide association analysis. Successful validation could yield a clinical decision support system that dynamically adjusts dosing recommendations based on evolving patient states, reducing complications by an estimated 15–20%. This work bridges artificial intelligence and translational anesthesiology, advancing personalized perioperative care while establishing scalable methods for integrating multi-omics data into real-time clinical workflows. The requested HPC resources are essential given the computational intensity of processing terabyte-scale biosensor streams and performing genome-phenome association studies across diverse anesthetic scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in developing and implementing patient anesthesia care plans, including preoperative, surgical theater, recovery room, and postoperative/intensive care procedures. Includes instruction in patient data collection, catheter insertion, airway management and drug administration, assisting the administration and monitoring of regional and peripheral nerve blockades, support therapy, adjusting anesthetic levels during surgery, interoperative monitoring, postoperative procedures, pain clinics and patient education, and administrative tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address unresolved questions about the transmission and evolution of cultural practices in the ancient Mediterranean world. Traditional scholarship in Classical and Ancient Studies has struggled to synthesize fragmentary textual, epigraphic, and archaeological datasets spanning diverse regions and time periods, limiting holistic analysis of socio-cultural networks. Our research focuses on modeling the diffusion of religious rituals and iconographic motifs across Greco-Roman Egypt, a critical hub of cross-cultural exchange. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for analyzing multilingual papyri, machine learning for classifying visual motifs in 3D artifact scans, and agent-based modeling to simulate how social hierarchies influenced cultural adoption. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets—including digitized scrolls, pottery corpora, and settlement maps—which exceed the capacity of standard workstations. HPC resources will enable large-scale feature extraction from texts (e.g., Coptic, Greek, and Demotic) and artifacts, while dynamic network simulations will reconstruct possible pathways of cultural transmission between urban centers and peripheral communities. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated datasets, visualization tools for interdisciplinary collaboration, and new frameworks for quantifying the impact of hybrid identities in antiquity. By bridging gaps between philology, archaeology, and computational social science, this project aims to redefine how scholars trace cultural connectivity in premodern societies, offering methodological innovations applicable to other underdocumented historical contexts. The results will directly support three peer-reviewed publications and a grant proposal for extending the model to Silk Road studies.
cip_definition: Any program in classical and ancient studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of human-system interactions in safety-critical environments by developing computational models of human decision-making under cognitive workload constraints. Traditional experimental methods in human factors psychology face limitations in capturing dynamic, multi-variable scenarios, particularly when analyzing how individuals adapt to real-time system feedback or competing task demands. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid approach integrating cognitive architectures with reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks to simulate human behavior in high-stakes operational contexts, such as air traffic control or medical emergency response systems. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate these models using large-scale datasets of human performance metrics, including eye-tracking, physiological sensor data, and task error rates from prior empirical studies. Key computational challenges include parallelizing RL training across heterogeneous workloads, optimizing neural network architectures for real-time behavioral prediction, and conducting sensitivity analyses on parameters influencing workload-performance tradeoffs. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying threshold conditions for performance degradation under multitasking scenarios, (2) empirically validated design principles for adaptive human-machine interfaces that mitigate cognitive overload, and (3) open-source simulation tools to benchmark human reliability in complex systems. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will enable previously intractable analyses of time-dependent interaction patterns at scale, directly contributing to the optimization of system safety protocols and operator training frameworks. Results will be disseminated through human factors conferences and collaborations with industry partners in transportation and healthcare technology sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to understand of interactions among humans and other elements of a system. Includes instruction in applying theory, principles, data and methods to design in order to optimize human well-being and overall system performance.

abstract: Operational oceanography in military contexts requires high-resolution, real-time environmental predictions to support tactical decision-making in dynamic coastal and nearshore environments. Existing models often lack the spatial granularity and adaptive capabilities needed to resolve small-scale hydrodynamic processes—such as rapidly evolving currents, sediment transport, and acoustic propagation anomalies—that critically influence mission success in contested littoral zones. This project seeks to develop a coupled wave-circulation modeling framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) systems to address these gaps. The research will integrate multi-source observational data (satellite, buoy, and unmanned underwater vehicle sensors) with advanced numerical methods, including non-hydrostatic fluid dynamics solvers and machine learning-based data assimilation, to improve nearshore predictions at sub-100-meter resolutions. Computational workflows will prioritize parallelized simulations of tidal harmonics, wind-driven surges, and sediment resuspension events under varying bathymetric conditions, with validation against classified field datasets from recent naval exercises. The HPC allocation will enable ensemble forecasting to quantify uncertainty in tactical-scale oceanographic variables, such as optical clarity and acoustic attenuation, which directly impact mine countermeasures and amphibious operations. Expected outcomes include a deployable model interface for real-time operational support, reducing environmental risk in mission planning, and a publicly accessible dataset (scrubbed of sensitive details) to advance foundational understanding of coastal boundary layer processes. By bridging gaps between ocean physics, computational scalability, and defense requirements, this work will establish a template for resource-efficient, high-fidelity environmental forecasting in militarily strategic regions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of physical oceanography as applied to the naval tactical and strategic environment and the support of military operations. Includes instruction in atmospheric thermodynamics and radiation propagation, air-ocean fluid dynamics, ocean waves, nearshore environments and processes, ocean acoustics, ocean analysis, tactical oceanography, prediction, and related quantitative and experimental methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing preservation strategies for historic structures under dynamic environmental and socioeconomic pressures by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Historic buildings and landscapes face degradation from climate change, urban development, and material aging, yet existing methods for prioritizing interventions often rely on static assessments or simplified models that fail to integrate multidisciplinary data. This research will develop a computational framework to simulate long-term preservation outcomes by coupling architectural degradation models, economic viability analyses, and climate projections. The core computational challenge lies in processing heterogeneous datasets—including 3D LiDAR scans of structures, regional climate models, and real estate valuation trends—while resolving fine-grained spatial and temporal interactions. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate the resilience of different conservation materials and policies under thousands of scenarios, integrating agent-based modeling to simulate stakeholder decision-making. Machine learning techniques will be applied to automate damage detection in historical imagery and predict site-specific risks using geospatial and archival records. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between preservation integrity, adaptive reuse potential, and development costs across multi-decadal horizons. This work will provide preservationists and urban planners with evidence-based strategies to allocate limited resources effectively, particularly in climate-vulnerable regions. By bridging computational engineering, material science, and heritage policy, the project advances interdisciplinary methodologies for sustainable cultural heritage management while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in non-traditional computational fields.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of plans to restore and maintain historic buildings, districts, and landscapes in a way that balances conservation and preservation with commercial and development interests. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation, cultural resource management, economics, historical documentation and preservation, land-use and zoning codes, public policy, public relations, real estate law, and taxation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of African-American/Black literary texts across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. While the corpus of Black diasporic literature has expanded significantly, traditional close-reading methods struggle to systematically trace thematic continuities, stylistic innovations, and intertextual dialogues across its vast, multilingual, and historically layered body of work. This research addresses this gap by applying natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to analyze a curated digital archive of 10,000+ texts, including novels, poetry, essays, and transcribed oral narratives from the 18th century to the present. Key computational tasks include semantic topic modeling to identify evolving motifs (e.g., resistance, migration, cultural hybridity), sentiment analysis to map emotional registers in works addressing racial trauma and joy, and network analysis to visualize influences among authors and regions. The scale of data—encompassing diverse dialects, code-switching, and non-standardized orthographies in historical texts—demands HPC capabilities for preprocessing, training transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned on African-American English), and running parallelized simulations. Expected outcomes include: (1) a public interactive dashboard visualizing thematic and stylistic trends across periods and geographies; (2) quantitative evidence challenging canonical boundaries between “oral” and “literary” traditions; and (3) new frameworks for computationally engaging with marginalized vernacular aesthetics. By centering computational humanities on Black diasporic voices, this project aims to reshape methodological paradigms in literary studies while making critical interventions in debates about archival equity and the digital preservation of cultural memory.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance forensic psychology research by developing predictive models for violence risk assessment and intervention outcomes in justice-involved populations. Current risk assessment tools in forensic settings often rely on static historical factors, which lack dynamic sensitivity to psychosocial or contextual changes, limiting their utility in guiding real-world treatment or legal decisions. To address this, the proposed research will integrate large-scale datasets—including clinical evaluations, criminal histories, and behavioral monitoring data from correctional and community settings—to train machine learning models capable of identifying dynamic risk and protective factors. Computational workflows will involve preprocessing multimodal data (e.g., text-based clinical notes, structured demographic records, and time-series behavioral metrics) using NLP techniques and feature engineering. Deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models and graph neural networks, will be tested to capture complex interactions between individual traits, social networks, and environmental stressors. The project will also simulate intervention scenarios via agent-based modeling to evaluate how tailored counseling strategies might mitigate recidivism risk. HPC resources are critical for managing the computational burden of training models on heterogeneous data, optimizing hyperparameters at scale, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations for outcome uncertainty analysis. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic risk prediction, empirically validated guidelines for personalizing forensic interventions, and novel insights into the temporal stability of risk factors. By bridging computational advances with applied psychological practice, this work aims to enhance the fairness and efficacy of forensic decision-making while addressing ethical concerns related to algorithmic bias in legal systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical, counseling, school, and neuropsychology skills to the provision of psychological services within the criminal justice and civil legal systems, including consultation, assessment, and interventions. Includes instruction in the epidemiology of mental/behavioral disorders, risk factors for violence and criminality, profiling and patterning, psychological testing, prediction and intervention measurement, forensic assessment, criminal and civil law and procedures, secure environments, forensic treatment and intervention skills, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the biophysical mechanisms underlying voltage-dependent conformational changes in ion channels, a critical process for cellular signaling and homeostasis. Despite structural insights from cryo-EM and crystallography, the dynamic coupling between transmembrane voltage sensing and pore gating remains poorly resolved at atomic-scale temporal resolution. We propose to employ all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enhanced with adaptive sampling algorithms to model the free energy landscape of a prototypical voltage-gated potassium channel (Kv1.2) embedded in a phospholipid bilayer. Simulations will integrate explicit solvent, membrane deformation, and applied electric fields to mimic physiological voltage gradients. The computational demands are substantial, requiring microsecond-scale trajectories across multiple replicas to capture rare gating transitions, with systems exceeding 500,000 atoms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parallelize these simulations using GPU-optimized MD software (NAMD, OpenMM) and perform Markov state model analysis to identify metastable states and transition pathways. This approach will resolve how voltage-sensor helix motions allosterically drive pore opening, quantify the role of lipid-protein interactions in modulating gating kinetics, and validate predictions against patch-clamp electrophysiology data from collaborators. The outcomes will advance mechanistic models of electromechanical coupling in ion channels, with broader implications for understanding channelopathies and designing targeted therapeutics. Successful allocation of HPC resources will directly enable the statistical rigor and temporal resolution required to dissect these nanosecond-to-microsecond dynamics, which are inaccessible to current experimental methods alone.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: The administration of anesthetic agents requires precise pharmacological management to balance efficacy and safety, yet interpatient variability in drug response remains a significant challenge in clinical practice. Current dosing protocols often rely on population averages, which may inadequately address individual differences in genetics, comorbidities, or physiological states, leading to suboptimal outcomes such as intraoperative awareness, prolonged recovery, or hemodynamic instability. This project proposes to develop patient-specific predictive models of anesthetic pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. By integrating multiscale physiological simulations with machine learning, we aim to characterize how genetic polymorphisms, organ function, and drug-drug interactions influence anesthetic variability. The computational framework will leverage existing clinical datasets, including electronic health records and genomic profiles, to train neural networks predicting individualized drug metabolism and sensitivity. Concurrently, finite element modeling of drug diffusion across tissue compartments and agent-specific molecular dynamics simulations will refine parameters for rare patient subgroups underrepresented in clinical data. HPC resources are essential to process these multimodal datasets at scale, optimize hyperparameters across thousands of parallel simulations, and validate models against real-world perioperative outcomes. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for simulating anesthetic scenarios in virtual patient cohorts, enabling clinicians to preemptively assess dosing risks and optimize regimens. This work aligns with the Nurse Anesthetist program’s emphasis on advanced pharmacology and evidence-based practice, offering a pathway to personalize perioperative care while reducing adverse events. The resulting models could also inform the design of safer anesthetic protocols for high-risk populations, directly addressing gaps in pain management and postoperative recovery highlighted in current clinical training frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: Neurodevelopmental disabilities (NDDs) in children, including autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, and sensory impairment-related delays, present complex challenges due to heterogeneous etiology, multifactorial interactions, and variability in treatment response. Current clinical approaches often lack precision, partly due to insufficient understanding of the interplay between genetic, neural, and environmental factors shaping neurodevelopmental trajectories. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of neurodevelopmental outcomes and optimize personalized intervention strategies. The research integrates multimodal datasets—including longitudinal neuroimaging (fMRI, DTI), electrophysiology (EEG), genomic data, and clinical phenotyping from a cohort of 1,200 children with NDDs—to identify biomarkers of treatment response and developmental progression. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms (e.g., graph neural networks, ensemble methods) to model dynamic brain network reorganization during skill acquisition, simulating how targeted therapies alter neural plasticity. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of sensorimotor and cognitive skill development, calibrated to patient-specific parameters derived from real-world wearable sensor data. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional neuroimaging datasets (>10 TB), parallelizing computationally intensive simulations of neural circuit maturation, and enabling real-time optimization of adaptive therapeutic protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for stratifying children into subgroups based on computationally derived neurobehavioral profiles, (2) predictive models linking early biomarkers to long-term functional outcomes, and (3) open-source tools for simulating intervention effects across developmental timelines. This work addresses a critical gap in translating neurocomputational insights into clinical practice, with potential to reduce diagnostic delays and improve targeted resource allocation in early intervention programs. By elucidating mechanisms of neuroplasticity in diverse NDD populations, the project aims to advance evidence-based, individualized therapeutic approaches for children with complex developmental needs.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat children having developmental delays or learning disorders, including those associated with visual and hearing impairment, developmental delays, cerebral palsy, spina bifida, autism, and other chronic neurologic conditions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) methodologies for modeling and predicting dynamic human-environment interactions in contested or crisis-driven landscapes. Traditional GEOINT frameworks often struggle to integrate real-time, heterogeneous data streams—such as satellite imagery, social media geotags, and crowd-sourced environmental sensors—into cohesive predictive models, particularly in regions where rapid socio-political or ecological shifts outpace conventional analytical workflows. The research addresses this gap by developing a scalable computational architecture optimized for spatiotemporal pattern detection, anomaly identification, and scenario forecasting. Using GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks and distributed spatial databases, the project will process multi-modal datasets at continental scales, with a focus on quantifying uncertainties in human mobility patterns, resource conflicts, and infrastructure vulnerability under climate stressors. Key computational challenges include parallelizing raster/vector data fusion for high-resolution satellite time series, optimizing graph neural networks for irregular geospatial networks, and implementing real-time simulation engines to test mitigation strategies. Outcomes will include open-source tools for adaptive resampling of imbalanced geospatial training data and a probabilistic modeling library tailored for intelligence analysts operating in low-latency decision environments. By integrating domain-specific knowledge from human geography and conflict studies with computational innovations in spatial AI, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for anticipatory intelligence—bridging the gap between theoretical spatial models and operational requirements in security and disaster response contexts. The requested HPC resources are critical for benchmarking model performance across diverse geopolitical scenarios, validating predictions against historical crisis datasets, and ensuring scalability to global monitoring applications. Anticipated impacts include enhanced situational awareness for humanitarian operations and a methodological foundation for ethical AI applications in non-traditional intelligence domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to analyze security and intelligence problems using a geographic perspective by relating human actions to cultural, political, economic, social, and physical landscapes. Includes instruction in aerial photography analysis, cartography, geographic information systems (GIS), physical geography, remote sensing, spatial programming, and quantitative methods in geographic research.

abstract: Oral and maxillofacial diseases present complex diagnostic challenges due to overlapping clinical, radiographic, and histopathologic features, often leading to delayed or ambiguous diagnoses. Current methods for integrating multimodal patient data—including 3D radiographic imaging, whole-slide histopathology scans, and molecular biomarkers—lack scalable computational frameworks to analyze these high-dimensional datasets cohesively. This project proposes the development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic platform to unify heterogeneous data types and identify predictive signatures of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), osteonecrosis, and benign odontogenic tumors. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models on multi-terabyte datasets comprising clinical records, cone-beam CT scans, digitized microscopy slides, and RNA sequencing data from a retrospective cohort of 1,200 patients. Computational workflows will include 3D convolutional neural networks for radiographic pattern detection, vision transformers for whole-slide image analysis, and graph neural networks to model spatial relationships between histologic and molecular features. Validation will involve prospective testing against gold-standard pathologic diagnoses and survival outcomes. The HPC environment is critical for managing GPU-accelerated model training, parallel processing of large-scale image datasets, and hyperparameter optimization across multimodal architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated AI framework for early and differential diagnosis of oral maxillofacial diseases, (2) quantitative biomarkers predictive of malignant transformation in oral dysplasia, and (3) open-source tools for computational pathology integration into clinical workflows. This work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven decision support in oral pathology, directly addressing variability in diagnostic interpretation while providing scalable infrastructure for precision medicine applications in head and neck oncology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases affecting the oral and maxillofacial regions, using clinical, radiographic, microscopic, biochemical, or other examinations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study focused on mapping the evolution of cultural and philosophical concepts across premodern Chinese textual traditions. The central research problem addresses the lack of systematic, large-scale analyses of how key ideas—such as *ren* (仁, humaneness) and *li* (礼, ritual)—were interpreted, contested, and redefined in literary, historical, and religious texts from the Han to Qing dynasties (206 BCE–1911 CE). Existing scholarship relies on manual close reading of curated excerpts, limiting the scope to assess longitudinal patterns or regional variations. To address this, the project will computationally analyze a curated corpus of over 25,000 digitized texts, including classical works, regional gazetteers, and Buddhist/Daoist canons, to trace semantic shifts and contextual associations of these concepts across time, genre, and geography. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques—such as dynamic word embeddings, topic modeling, and collocation network analysis—with geospatial visualization tools. HPC resources are critical for training custom Chinese-language transformer models on historical texts, which require significant memory and parallel processing to handle character-level tokenization, variant character reconciliation, and context-aware disambiguation of classical Chinese syntax. Expected outcomes include (1) interactive visualizations of concept diffusion and reinterpretation, (2) a publicly accessible database of annotated text passages with metadata, and (3) new methodological frameworks for computational analysis of premodern Sinographic texts. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to reveal previously undetectable patterns in China’s intellectual history, offering scholars a scalable toolset to interrogate cultural narratives and challenging assumptions about ideological continuity in Chinese studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of present-day China and its historical predecessors, related borderlands and island groups, and the overseas Chinese diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize animal grooming practices through biomechanical and behavioral modeling, addressing gaps in standardized, evidence-based methodologies for diverse species and coat types. Despite the growing demand for specialized pet grooming services, current techniques often rely on anecdotal expertise, leading to variability in outcomes, potential animal stress, and suboptimal coat health. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to simulate interactions between grooming tools (e.g., clippers, brushes) and biological systems (skin, fur, muscle) across species, integrating data from 3D coat texture scans, physiological stress markers, and behavioral response datasets. Computational models will employ finite element analysis to map tool pressure distribution, machine learning to predict coat matting dynamics, and agent-based modeling to assess animal discomfort thresholds during grooming procedures. The workflow will parallelize simulations across grooming variables (tool type, speed, angle) and biological parameters (coat density, skin sensitivity, species-specific anatomy). Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that recommends grooming protocols tailored to individual animals, minimizing stress while maximizing coat health. This research bridges computational biomechanics and animal care, establishing quantitative metrics for grooming efficacy and safety. By formalizing data-driven guidelines, the project aims to advance professional training standards, reduce industry reliance on trial-and-error practices, and improve welfare outcomes for companion animals. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handling high-resolution biological datasets and scaling simulations across the combinatorial space of grooming scenarios, which cannot feasibly be tested in vivo due to ethical and logistical constraints. Results will be disseminated through open-access models and collaborations with grooming certification bodies, fostering innovation in this understudied yet socially impactful domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in modeling the phonological, syntactic, and sociolinguistic structures of American Sign Language (ASL) and other global sign languages. While sign languages exhibit complex linguistic properties comparable to spoken languages, their visual-spatial modality—dependent on simultaneous articulators (hands, face, body)—poses unique computational hurdles. Existing tools for spoken language analysis are ill-suited to handle the high-dimensional kinematic data (e.g., motion-capture recordings, 3D handshape trajectories) or the sociolinguistic variability inherent in deaf communities. This research aims to develop scalable computational models to analyze large, multimodal sign language datasets, enabling cross-linguistic comparisons of ASL, LSF (French Sign Language), Auslan (Australian Sign Language), and others. Key objectives include (1) creating machine learning pipelines to automate phonological segmentation using HamNoSys and SignWriting annotation systems, (2) simulating syntactic dependencies in spatial grammar through graph-based neural networks, and (3) mapping sociolinguistic variation across regional ASL dialects via probabilistic clustering algorithms. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on video corpora, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks like optical flow analysis across GPU nodes, and running large-scale agent-based simulations of language emergence in deaf communities. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for sign language processing, novel insights into the universality of linguistic structures across modalities, and foundational data for improving assistive technologies like real-time sign language translation systems. By bridging computational linguistics and sign language research, this work will advance theoretical frameworks for visual-spatial grammar while supporting equitable access to language technologies for deaf individuals.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Linguistics of ASL and Other Sign Languages
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and scholarly study of the development, structure, and use of American Sign Language (ASL) and other visual signed languages, both as vehicles for communication within the deaf community and in relation to spoken and written languages. Includes instruction in cognitive linguistics; ASL and sign language phonology, syntax, and morphology; sociolinguistics of the deaf community; comparative linguistics; and studies of specific sign languages, including, but not limited to, ASL, Auslan (Australian Sign Language), LSF (French Sign Language), Shuwa jiten (Japanese Sign Language), HamNoSys (German Sign Language), and Gestuno.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize task prioritization for health aides in ambulatory care settings, leveraging high-frequency sensor data from wearable devices and environmental monitors. Health aides face increasing demands in managing patients with complex, chronic conditions, yet existing decision-support tools lack real-time adaptability to dynamic physiological and contextual data streams. The research problem centers on computational bottlenecks in processing multimodal time-series data (e.g., vital signs, motion patterns, ambient conditions) to detect early signs of patient deterioration or environmental risks while maintaining workflow efficiency. We propose a hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks to model patient-environment interactions and lightweight reinforcement learning agents for adaptive task recommendations. The computational workflow will integrate raw data from IoT devices (sampled at 10-100Hz) with electronic health record snapshots, requiring high-performance computing resources for parallelized feature extraction, temporal pattern mining across overlapping event windows, and multi-agent simulation of care scenarios. Key technical challenges include maintaining low-latency inference on streaming data while training models on historical datasets spanning 50,000+ patient-hours from partnered home care agencies. Expected outcomes include an open-source temporal fusion framework optimized for edge-cloud healthcare systems and empirical validation of predictive accuracy against current protocol-based prioritization methods. This work will advance human-AI collaboration in paraprofessional care by addressing computational scalability barriers in real-time assistive technologies, with potential applications to workforce training and resource allocation in decentralized care networks. Successful implementation could reduce emergency interventions by 15-20% in pilot populations through earlier detection of physiological instability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and assistance to patients under the direct supervision of other health care professionals, and/or to perform routine maintenance and general assistance in health care facilities and laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) protocols and improve clinical outcomes for decompression illness, non-healing wounds, and radiation-induced tissue damage through advanced computational modeling of physiological responses under hyperbaric conditions. Current HBOT treatment schedules rely on empirical data and generalized frameworks, which may inadequately address patient-specific factors such as tissue perfusion heterogeneity, gas solubility dynamics, and oxidative stress thresholds. To address this gap, we propose developing multi-scale computational models integrating fluid dynamics, gas transport, and cellular metabolic pathways under varying hyperbaric exposures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of gas bubble formation and resolution in decompression sickness using three-dimensional fluid-structure interaction models, coupled with pharmacokinetic modeling of oxygen radical scavenging in ischemic tissues. Machine learning algorithms will analyze multi-parametric clinical datasets from 450 historical diving injury cases and 300 HBOT-treated chronic wound patients to identify predictive biomarkers for treatment response. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess probabilistic risks of oxygen toxicity across diverse patient phenotypes, informing adaptive treatment algorithms. The computational framework will be validated against real-time tissue oxygenation data from hyperbaric chamber trials and retrospective clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include personalized HBOT dosing schedules, risk stratification tools for iatrogenic complications, and predictive models for wound healing trajectories. This work will directly enhance evidence-based protocol design for diving injury management while advancing mechanistic understanding of hyperbaric interventions in complex tissue repair processes. By leveraging HPC capabilities to manage large-scale biomechanical simulations and high-dimensional clinical data integration, the project aims to establish a translational pipeline from computational discovery to optimized therapeutic strategies in undersea and hyperbaric medicine.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat decompression illness and diving accident cases; to use hyperbaric oxygen therapy treatment for conditions such as carbon monoxide poisoning, gas gangrene, non-healing wounds, tissue damage from radiation and burns, and bone infections; to serve as consultant in all aspects of hyperbaric chamber operations; and to assess risks and apply appropriate standards to prevent disease and disability in divers and other persons working in altered atmospheric conditions.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the complex relationship between musical performance practices and the acoustic properties of architectural spaces through high-fidelity computational simulations. While historical and contemporary performance practices are often studied in isolation, the dynamic interaction between sound production, spatial acoustics, and performer adaptation remains underexplored due to the computational complexity of modeling real-world environments. The project will employ wave-based acoustic simulation methods, including finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) and boundary element modeling (BEM), to recreate the acoustic signatures of diverse performance venues—from Baroque churches to modern concert halls. These simulations will be coupled with machine learning techniques to analyze how performers intuitively adapt their technique to spatial acoustics, using motion-capture data of instrumentalists and vocalists. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve 3D wave propagation at audio frequencies across large volumetric meshes, requiring parallelized computations across thousands of cores to achieve real-world accuracy within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include a novel database of performer-acoustic interaction patterns and an open-source framework for virtual acoustic rehearsal environments. This work will provide new insights into the embodied cognition of musical performance while developing tools that enable artists to experience historically informed acoustic environments digitally. The computational methodologies developed may also inform future architectural designs for performance spaces, bridging artistic practice with acoustic engineering. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project addresses critical gaps in musicology and performance studies through an interdisciplinary approach that transcends traditional analytical limitations.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of music and the performing arts. Includes instruction in music, dance, and other performing arts media.

abstract: This project seeks to advance speech-language pedagogy by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale datasets of classroom interactions and student speech patterns. A critical challenge in speech teacher education is the lack of efficient, evidence-based tools to model and assess the progression of communication skills in diverse learners. Traditional methods rely on manual evaluation of student recordings, which limits scalability and fails to capture nuanced patterns in speech development across varied linguistic and sociocultural contexts. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework that integrates machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to automate the analysis of spoken language samples from K–12 classrooms. The project will process audio recordings of student presentations, debates, and collaborative discussions using GPU-accelerated speech-to-text conversion and acoustic feature extraction. Deep learning models, trained on annotated datasets of speech fluency, articulation, and rhetorical effectiveness, will classify developmental milestones and identify pedagogical intervention points. The computational workflow will also simulate language acquisition scenarios through agent-based modeling, enabling prospective speech educators to explore how instructional strategies impact hypothetical student cohorts with varying communication needs. By utilizing HPC resources, we aim to process over 10,000 hours of multilingual speech data, train high-parameter models for real-time feedback systems, and generate synthetic datasets to address privacy concerns in educational research. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access platform for speech educators to visualize student progress, customize lesson plans using predictive analytics, and practice diagnostic decision-making in virtual environments. This work will directly enhance teacher training programs by bridging computational linguistics with evidence-based pedagogy, equipping educators to better support students with speech-language disorders, multilingual learners, and those developing public speaking skills.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach speech and language arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of coupled hydro-mechanical processes in contaminated soil systems, with a focus on improving the stability and environmental performance of waste containment structures. The research addresses critical gaps in understanding how dynamic loading events, such as earthquakes or cyclic waste settlement, interact with geochemical degradation processes to compromise landfill liners and subsurface barriers. Current analytical models oversimplify the interplay between soil deformation, fluid flow, and contaminant transport, particularly under time-varying boundary conditions. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a parallelized finite element framework integrating three-dimensional elastoplastic soil behavior, transient multiphase flow, and reactive solute transport. High-resolution simulations will capture microstructural changes in engineered clay-geosynthetic composites during cyclic wet-dry and load-unload scenarios, informed by experimental datasets on material properties under extreme environmental conditions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter calibration and uncertainty quantification across heterogeneous soil profiles. The computational workflow will be validated against field monitoring data from instrumented landfill sites and scaled to assess regional-scale impacts of proposed waste containment designs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing barrier system resilience against climate-induced hydraulic gradients and seismic hazards, directly supporting sustainable infrastructure design. By enabling previously intractable simulations of long-term geoenvironmental system performance, this work will provide novel insights into failure mechanisms at the soil-contaminant interface, informing regulatory guidelines and risk mitigation strategies for contaminated land management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply geotechnical engineering methods, which deal with the analysis, design and construction of earth and earth supported structures, to the application of environmental problems, such as waste containment, waste disposal, construction of land fills, soil permeation, soil analysis, and soil improvement. Includes instruction in soil mechanics, soil dynamics, soil behavior, waste management and containment systems, geosynthetics, geochemistry, earth structures, geoenvironmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, earthquake engineering, and foundation engineering

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in credit risk assessment frameworks by integrating high-dimensional, non-traditional data sources with dynamic macroeconomic indicators, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome computational bottlenecks in real-time decision systems. Traditional credit scoring models rely on static financial histories and fail to adapt to rapidly evolving market conditions or incorporate unstructured data such as transactional behavior patterns, supply chain interdependencies, and sentiment signals from financial communications. The proposed computational approach employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex relationships between borrowers, lenders, and interconnected financial entities, while deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract risk-relevant insights from regulatory filings, customer service interactions, and collateral documentation. Agent-based simulations will further test systemic stability under stress scenarios involving cascading defaults. HPC resources are critical for training multi-modal machine learning architectures on terabyte-scale datasets spanning 10 years of global credit transactions, insurance claims, and real estate collateral records, as well as for optimizing hyperparameters across distributed GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include a prototype AI-driven credit allocation platform capable of reducing Type I/II errors in default prediction by 15–20% compared to industry-standard models, alongside computational frameworks to quantify ethical trade-offs in algorithmic lending. The project aims to provide financial institutions with tools to enhance credit accessibility for underserved sectors while maintaining portfolio resilience, directly supporting the integration of ESG (environmental, social, governance) metrics into automated credit management systems. By advancing scalable methods to process heterogeneous financial data, this work bridges gaps between computational finance, regulatory technology, and ethical AI—a niche with growing relevance as credit systems confront climate-related disruptions and geopolitical volatility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and/or manage operations concerning personal and corporate credit, collateral, loan processing, and related financial agency communications. Includes instruction in general finance and banking principles, insurance, real estate, taxation, business law and regulations, quantitative methods, financial computer systems applications, database management, communications skills, business and office management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Emerging infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance in livestock present critical challenges to global veterinary medicine, food security, and public health. Current limitations in predicting pathogen evolution, transmission dynamics, and host-pathogen interactions at scale hinder proactive interventions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) patterns and disease spread in bovine respiratory pathogens, with a focus on *Mannheimia haemolytica* and *Pasteurella multocida*. We aim to integrate multi-omics datasets (whole-genome sequencing, metagenomics, and host transcriptomics) from clinical veterinary samples with epidemiological metadata to identify drivers of resistance and virulence. Machine learning models will be trained on these data to predict AMR gene transfer probabilities and spatiotemporal outbreak risks, while agent-based simulations will model transmission dynamics across heterogeneous cattle populations. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize structural changes in bacterial proteins linked to beta-lactamase activity under selective antibiotic pressure. These computationally intensive workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale genomic datasets and iterative optimization of predictive algorithms, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) high-resolution maps of resistance gene dissemination in US livestock systems, (2) predictive tools for veterinary clinicians to prioritize antimicrobial therapies based on local pathogen profiles, and (3) mechanistic insights into resistance evolution at the protein-ligand level. By bridging gaps between veterinary genomics, computational epidemiology, and structural biology, this work will directly inform antimicrobial stewardship programs, vaccine development targets, and biosecurity protocols for livestock operations. The requested resources will enable transformative advances in translating complex biological data into actionable strategies for mitigating zoonotic risks and improving herd health outcomes.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Sciences/ Veterinary Clinical Sciences, General
cip_definition: An integrated program of study in one or more of the veterinary medical or clinical sciences or a program undifferentiated as to title.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance the understanding of complex reaction mechanisms in heterogeneous catalysis, a critical area for sustainable energy and chemical synthesis. While experimental studies provide valuable insights, they often struggle to resolve transient intermediates and solvent effects at atomic resolution, particularly in multi-component systems. This project addresses these limitations by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model catalytic cycles at the quantum-mechanical level, focusing on transition metal clusters in liquid-phase environments. The primary challenge lies in accurately simulating dynamic solvent interactions and entropy contributions, which require extensive sampling of free energy landscapes. To overcome this, we will implement hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations coupled with enhanced sampling techniques, such as metadynamics and replica-exchange molecular dynamics. These methods demand substantial computational resources due to the need for large periodic boundary condition systems (500–1,000 atoms), long simulation timescales (nanosecond range), and iterative optimization of reaction coordinates. The HPC allocation will enable parallelized calculations across multiple nodes, leveraging GPU acceleration for density functional theory (DFT) computations and force field parametrization. Expected outcomes include identifying solvent-mediated pathways for CO₂ hydrogenation and ammonia synthesis, quantifying the role of entropy in rate-determining steps, and validating theoretical predictions against in situ spectroscopic data. This work will provide a predictive framework for tailoring catalyst selectivity under realistic conditions, directly informing experimental efforts to develop energy-efficient processes. Additionally, the generated datasets will be curated into an open-access repository, supporting reproducibility and community-driven method development in computational chemistry. By bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical catalysis, this project aims to accelerate the discovery of environmentally benign chemical technologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemistry, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of relational dynamics in therapeutic contexts, specifically within Marriage and Family Therapy (MFT). Traditional MFT research relies heavily on qualitative analysis or small-scale quantitative studies, limiting the ability to model complex, nonlinear interactions within family systems or predict long-term outcomes of therapeutic interventions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), multilevel agent-based modeling (ABM), and network analysis to analyze longitudinal therapy session transcripts and simulate family interaction patterns. The research problem centers on identifying critical thresholds in communication dynamics that correlate with therapeutic success or relapse, particularly in cases involving intergenerational trauma or chronic mental health conditions. Using anonymized session datasets (audio transcripts and clinician notes) from a multi-site cohort study, NLP pipelines will extract semantic, emotional, and relational features, while ABM simulations will map how micro-level interactions propagate through family networks over time. Computational demands include training transformer-based models for context-aware dialogue analysis, running ensemble simulations to account for psychosocial variability, and optimizing graph neural networks to detect latent relational patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model of intervention efficacy based on early-session communication features, (2) a generative toolkit for clinicians to explore "what-if" scenarios in treatment planning, and (3) novel metrics for quantifying resilience in family systems. By bridging computational social science with clinical practice, this work aims to establish an evidence base for personalized, data-informed MFT strategies while addressing scalability challenges in relational health research. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high dimensionality of interaction data, enabling real-time simulation of complex adaptive systems, and ensuring reproducibility across diverse demographic subgroups.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of marriage and family therapy, involving the diagnosis of cognitive, affective, and behavioral domain disorders, both mental and emotional, within the context of marriage and family systems and the application of short- and long-term therapeutic strategies in family group contexts. Includes instruction in psychotherapy, family systems and studies, small group intervention and therapy, marital problems, depression, identification of psychopathologies and behavioral disorders, holistic health care, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve large-scale phylogenetic and biogeographic patterns in understudied clades of tropical flora, with a focus on disentangling the drivers of diversification and extinction in biodiversity hotspots. A critical barrier in systematic biology is the computational limitation of analyzing complex evolutionary models across vast genomic, morphological, and environmental datasets. Existing approaches often simplify biogeographic histories or ignore trait-environment interactions due to processing constraints, leading to incomplete reconstructions of lineage diversification. We propose a computational pipeline integrating Bayesian phylogenetic inference with spatially explicit birth-death models to simultaneously evaluate speciation, extinction, and dispersal dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes. This approach will process whole-genome sequence data from 500+ species, fossil calibration points, and global paleoclimate layers to infer time-calibrated phylogenies, ancestral biogeographic ranges, and diversification rate shifts. Key computational challenges include Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for high-dimensional phylogenetic networks and agent-based simulations of lineage dispersal under historical climate scenarios. These tasks require parallelized processing on HPC clusters to handle memory-intensive genomic alignments (≥10 TB) and iterative likelihood calculations across millions of tree topologies. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of biomes and biotic interactions that disproportionately influenced tropical plant diversification, (2) quantification of extinction risk in lineages with low adaptive plasticity to past climatic shifts, and (3) open-source tools for integrating fossil data and trait-dependent models in phylogenetics. Results will advance systematic methods for predicting species responses to anthropogenic climate change while providing a scalable framework for synthesizing ecological, genomic, and paleontological data. The requested resources will enable parameter estimation at biologically realistic complexities, overcoming a major bottleneck in reconstructing evolutionary processes from large, multidimensional datasets.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: The fabrication and repair of musical instruments rely heavily on empirical knowledge and iterative physical prototyping, which limits the ability to systematically optimize materials, structural designs, and acoustic performance. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing computational models to simulate the vibrational, acoustic, and material behaviors of stringed, wind, and electronic instruments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to achieve the necessary resolution for modeling complex geometries, nonlinear material interactions, and multiphysics phenomena such as air resonance in wind instruments or electromagnetic feedback in amplified systems. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will simulate stress distributions in instrument components under dynamic loads, transient acoustic wave propagation, and energy dissipation patterns in materials like wood composites, metals, and synthetic polymers. Machine learning techniques will be applied to correlate simulation outputs with empirical acoustic data (e.g., frequency spectra, sustain times) to refine predictive models. A key focus is optimizing repair strategies for aging instruments by simulating long-term material degradation and testing virtual restoration interventions. The project will also explore generative design algorithms to propose novel instrument geometries that balance acoustic quality, ergonomics, and manufacturing feasibility. Expected outcomes include open-source computational toolkits for luthiers and repair technicians, reducing reliance on trial-and-error methods. By quantifying relationships between material properties, construction techniques, and sonic outcomes, this work aims to advance sustainable instrument design through data-driven material selection and preservation protocols. The scale of these simulations—requiring parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and GPU-accelerated solvers—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure to achieve practical runtime for parameter studies and sensitivity analyses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and tune acoustic and electric musical instruments. Includes instruction in methods and equipment for making musical instruments, electronic instrument amplification systems, techniques of cleaning, and methods of tuning musical instruments.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the operational efficiency and safety of commercial marine vessels through advanced computational modeling of hydrodynamic performance and structural integrity. Merchant marine operations face increasing pressure to reduce fuel consumption, minimize environmental impact, and enhance navigational safety in dynamic maritime environments. Current design and operational frameworks often rely on generalized empirical models, which inadequately capture the complex fluid-structure interactions experienced by vessels under real-world conditions, including turbulent flows, wave impacts, and variable cargo loads. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-fidelity computational approach combining large-eddy simulation (LES) for turbulent wake analysis, finite element modeling (FEM) for hull stress prediction, and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization of voyage parameters. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve multi-scale phenomena across 3D vessel geometries, incorporating real-time environmental data streams and operational constraints. Key deliverables include a validated framework for predicting hull resistance under diverse loading scenarios, a digital twin prototype for adaptive route optimization, and machine learning models to identify fuel-efficient engine configurations. These tools will directly inform curriculum updates in naval architecture and marine systems engineering courses, while providing merchant marine trainees with hands-on experience in computational decision support systems. The anticipated outcomes—reducing vessel energy use by 10-15% in simulated use cases and improving fatigue life predictions for critical structural components—will advance both economic and environmental sustainability in commercial shipping. By integrating HPC-driven insights into maritime training and vessel operations, this work bridges the gap between traditional naval engineering practices and emerging computational technologies, fostering safer and more efficient global marine transportation networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as captains, executive officers, engineers and ranking mates on commercially licensed inland, coastal and ocean-going vessels. Includes instruction in maritime traditions and law, maritime policy, economics and management of commercial marine operations, basic naval architecture and engineering, shipboard power systems engineering, crew supervision, and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the diachronic evolution of Swedish dialects and their sociolinguistic interfaces using advanced computational methods, with a focus on modeling phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variation across historical and contemporary corpora. Despite Sweden’s rich dialectal diversity, systematic large-scale analyses of regional language change—particularly under the influence of urbanization, digital communication, and language policy—remain underexplored due to the technical challenges of processing heterogeneous, unstructured text and speech data. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on a curated multilingual corpus spanning 19th-century manuscripts, modern regional speech recordings, and social media texts. Computational workflows will integrate dialectometric clustering, neural machine translation for historical orthographies, and prosodic feature extraction from audio data, enabling comparative analyses across temporal, geographic, and sociodemographic axes. Key challenges include managing non-standard orthographies in pre-20th-century texts, aligning audio recordings with dialect-specific phonetic inventories, and scaling semantic role labeling for low-resource Swedish variants. The HPC environment is critical for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, fine-tuning large language models, and running iterative simulations of language contact scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated Swedish dialect features, (2) quantitative models correlating linguistic shifts with extralinguistic factors (e.g., migration patterns, education policies), and (3) novel methods for diachronic dialectology applicable to minority languages globally. By bridging computational linguistics with Swedish philology, this work aims to redefine scholarly approaches to language preservation and policy while providing infrastructure for cross-disciplinary humanities research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Swedish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare delivery systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize clinical workflows, resource allocation, and patient outcomes. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to address inefficiencies in ambulatory care coordination, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal healthcare data. The research problem centers on the challenge of integrating heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), facility utilization metrics, and patient-reported outcomes—to identify systemic bottlenecks in care delivery and predict clinical resource needs under dynamic operational conditions. A hybrid machine learning approach will be employed, combining time-series analysis of historical patient flow patterns with natural language processing (NLP) of unstructured clinical notes to model care coordination risks. Computational experiments will simulate staffing and equipment allocation scenarios across virtual clinic environments, incorporating real-world constraints such as personnel availability, infection control protocols, and diagnostic testing capacity. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of large-scale synthetic datasets representing diverse healthcare settings, allowing for robust validation of adaptive resource allocation algorithms. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that quantifies the impact of resource distribution strategies on clinical throughput, patient wait times, and staff workload equity. This work directly aligns with the program's emphasis on medical management and clinical operations, providing evidence-based methods to enhance healthcare system resilience while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards. By bridging computational analytics with practical clinical workflows, the project aims to establish scalable solutions for healthcare facilities managing competing priorities in patient care delivery.
cip_title: Medical/ Health Management and Clinical Assistant/ Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, nurses, or other health care professionals, to perform medical office or facilities management services and perform one or more clinical allied health specialties. Includes instruction in health care management; medical office administration; medical law and regulations; training in one or more diagnostic, treatment, therapy, or laboratory specialties at the assistant level or above; and applicable professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of theological and philosophical arguments across religious traditions using computational textual analysis, with a focus on identifying patterns in doctrinal development and cross-cultural influence. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically analyzing vast corpora of primary religious texts (e.g., scriptures, commentaries, polemical works) and secondary literature to trace how specific concepts—such as divine justice, ritual purity, or soteriology—are articulated, contested, and transformed. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to address the scale and linguistic complexity of these materials, particularly when spanning multiple languages (e.g., Sanskrit, Arabic, Classical Chinese) and historical periods. To overcome these limitations, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned for ancient religious texts, semantic network analysis, and multilingual topic modeling. High-performance computing resources are critical for training custom word embeddings across diverse linguistic corpora, running large-scale comparative analyses of conceptual frameworks, and simulating diffusion patterns of theological ideas through historical networks. Expected outcomes include 1) a computational framework for mapping doctrinal relationships across traditions, 2) quantitative evidence supporting or challenging existing theories about interreligious philosophical exchange (e.g., between Abrahamic and Dharmic traditions), and 3) open-access tools for the digital humanities community to analyze understudied religious texts. The project will advance Religious Studies methodology by demonstrating how HPC-enabled approaches can complement hermeneutic traditions while addressing questions of scale previously inaccessible to scholars. Results will contribute to ongoing debates about religious pluralism, comparative theology, and the cognitive foundations of belief systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature of religious belief and specific religious and quasi-religious systems. Includes instruction in phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature and art of religion; mythology; scriptural and textual studies; religious history and politics; and specific studies of particular faith communities and their behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate complex driver-vehicle-environment interactions for enhancing safety pedagogy in driver education programs. Current driver training curricula often rely on static scenarios or limited real-world data, which inadequately prepare instructors to teach dynamic risk assessment and decision-making in diverse driving conditions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to generate high-fidelity, data-driven simulations that replicate heterogeneous traffic environments, variable weather patterns, and emergent hazards. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, adaptive tools for training driver educators to address evolving challenges such as autonomous vehicle coexistence, distracted driving behaviors, and infrastructure variability. Our computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, real-world traffic datasets, and machine learning algorithms to simulate thousands of interactive driving scenarios with parametric adjustments for road types, vehicle technologies, and driver demographics. These simulations will enable probabilistic analysis of accident precursors and the evaluation of pedagogical interventions through virtual instructor-student interactions. By utilizing parallel computing architectures, we aim to optimize scenario generation speeds while maintaining physiologically realistic driver response models derived from eye-tracking and biometric datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation platform for driver education programs, evidence-based curriculum recommendations for hazard perception training, and predictive models of skill retention across learner populations. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform safety teacher education through computationally intensive, scenario-based training tools that bridge the gap between theoretical instruction and real-world competency. Resource allocation will support the storage and processing of multi-terabyte simulation outputs, enabling iterative refinement of pedagogical models through large-scale parameter space exploration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach driver and safety education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, heterogeneous biomedical data, with a focus on addressing challenges in clinical trial design and public health surveillance. Modern biomedical datasets, such as longitudinal electronic health records and spatially referenced disease incidence data, often exhibit complex structures—including missingness, temporal dependencies, and multi-level clustering—that violate assumptions of traditional statistical models. To address these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating Bayesian hierarchical modeling, nonparametric machine learning, and distributed optimization algorithms. The core methodological innovation involves adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers with gradient-based proposals for high-dimensional parameter spaces, coupled with spatial-temporal Gaussian process priors to model geographic and temporal variation in disease outcomes. A key computational challenge lies in efficiently scaling these methods to national-scale datasets with millions of patients while maintaining uncertainty quantification.
