The requested high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelization of MCMC chains across GPU nodes, distributed memory management for massive sparse covariance matrices, and benchmarking of variational inference approximations against gold-standard sampling methods. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for robust analysis of incomplete, correlated biomedical data and novel insights into intervention effect heterogeneity across demographic subgroups in ongoing cardiovascular clinical trials. This work will advance biostatistical methodology for causal inference with complex observational data while directly supporting public health decision-making through improved risk stratification models. The computational infrastructure will be critical for achieving clinically relevant runtimes when analyzing datasets exceeding 100 million observations, with particular emphasis on ensuring reproducibility through containerized workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of descriptive and inferential statistics to biomedical research and clinical, public health, and industrial issues related to human populations. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, modeling, clinical trials methodology, disease and survival analysis, longitudinal analysis, missing data analysis, spatial analysis, computer tomography, biostatistics consulting, and applications to such topics as genetics, oncology, pharmacokinetics, physiology, neurobiology, and biophysics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, three-dimensional modeling framework to assess the long-term impacts of anthropogenic groundwater extraction on regional aquifer stability and land subsidence in sedimentary basin environments. The research problem centers on the urgent need to predict how prolonged groundwater depletion—driven by agricultural, industrial, and urban demands—interacts with heterogeneous subsurface geology to exacerbate soil compaction, infrastructure damage, and irreversible aquifer capacity loss. Current models lack the spatial granularity and computational scalability to resolve fine-scale lithological variations or simulate multi-decadal feedbacks between fluid dynamics and sediment mechanics. To address this gap, we propose a coupled hydrogeomechanical approach using finite element modeling (FEM) integrated with stochastic lithology distributions derived from borehole and geophysical datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations at basin scales (1–10 km resolution) while preserving meter-scale geological heterogeneity across 10^6–10^7 grid elements. Machine learning workflows will be implemented to optimize parameterization of sediment compressibility and hydraulic conductivity fields, reducing computational overhead. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of high-risk zones where subsurface heterogeneity amplifies subsidence rates, (2) probabilistic forecasts of aquifer degradation under climate and demand scenarios, and (3) open-source tools for regulatory agencies to evaluate sustainable extraction limits. By quantifying the coupled impacts of geological complexity and human activity on groundwater systems, this work will directly inform hazard mitigation strategies, water resource policies, and infrastructure resilience planning in vulnerable regions. The computational framework will also advance broader capabilities in environmental geosciences by enabling scalable, physics-based assessments of human-geosphere interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the environmental implications of geological processes and human activities on Earth. Includes instruction in environmental/natural resource management, geographic information systems (GIS), geology, hydrology, regulatory agency compliance, hazard identification and mitigation, environmental law, environmental policy, and sustainability studies.

abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), including Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, present significant clinical challenges due to their heterogeneous progression and variable treatment responses. A critical barrier to personalized management lies in understanding the complex interplay between gut microbiome dynamics, host genetics, and environmental factors, which collectively drive disease phenotypes. While advances in multi-omics technologies have generated vast datasets—spanning metagenomics, metabolomics, serologic profiles, and longitudinal clinical records—traditional analytical tools lack the capacity to integrate these high-dimensional data types or model their dynamic interactions at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive frameworks that elucidate mechanisms of treatment resistance and identify patient-specific therapeutic targets. Using a cohort of 1,200 deeply phenotyped IBD patients, we will apply parallelized machine learning algorithms (e.g., graph neural networks, ensemble classifiers) to integrate terabyte-scale metagenomic sequences, host immunoproteomic data, and electronic health record-derived treatment histories. Computational workflows will include genome-wide microbial gene variant calling, time-series analysis of microbiome-immune mediator networks, and in silico perturbation modeling to simulate microbial community responses to dietary or pharmacologic interventions. These analyses will be iteratively validated against prospective clinical outcomes, including endoscopic healing and biologic therapy failure. The HPC environment is essential for managing data-intensive tasks, such as metagenomic assembly across thousands of samples, and for training complex models requiring GPU-accelerated computation. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of microbiome-derived biomarkers predictive of early treatment response, mechanistic insights into microbial pathways influencing anti-TNFα efficacy, and a scalable computational platform for stratifying IBD subphenotypes. By bridging multi-omic data with clinical trajectories, this work aims to advance precision gastroenterology, reduce trial-and-error prescribing, and inform the development of microbiota-targeted therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on Gastroenterology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of geomorphological modeling, machine learning, and archaeological datasets for reconstructing ancient human-environment interactions in dynamic coastal landscapes. The research addresses a critical gap in geoarchaeology: the inability to systematically model how episodic geophysical events (e.g., storm surges, sediment accretion) and gradual climatic shifts collectively influenced site preservation, settlement patterns, and material culture distributions in Holocene-era coastal zones. Current approaches often treat environmental and anthropogenic factors in isolation, limiting holistic interpretations of archaeological contexts. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining 3D sediment transport simulations, Bayesian chronostratigraphic modeling, and agent-based settlement simulations calibrated against paleoenvironmental proxies (e.g., microfossil assemblages, isotopic records) and archaeological survey data. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-resolution LiDAR-derived topographic data, probabilistic dating of stratified cultural layers, and iterative scenario testing across multi-century timescales. Key computational challenges include coupling discrete element models of sediment dynamics with neural networks trained to detect anthropogenic landscape modifications in geophysical datasets, requiring terabyte-scale memory allocation and GPU-accelerated workflows. Anticipated outcomes include: 1) a scalable open-source toolkit for simulating site formation processes in transitional environments, 2) quantitative reconstructions of taphonomic bias in three study regions spanning the North Sea Basin to the Southeast Asian Maritime Realm, and 3) probabilistic maps of archaeological potential integrating paleo-tidal models and ethnographic settlement patterns. By bridging earth science process modeling and archaeological predictive analytics, this work will establish new protocols for assessing climate-driven threats to coastal cultural heritage while resolving longstanding debates about the role of episodic environmental stressors in early maritime adaptations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of analytical techniques, concepts, and field methods from the earth sciences to solve archaeological questions related to human settlement, artifacts, site taphonomy, and paleoenvironments. Includes instruction in anthropology, ancient civilizations, archeology, geology, paleoclimatic reconstruction, sedimentology, and site taphonomic research.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize irrigation scheduling and system design in water-scarce agricultural regions. Current irrigation management practices often rely on static thresholds or coarse environmental data, leading to inefficiencies in water use, energy consumption, and crop yield variability. Our research addresses these limitations by integrating dynamic soil-plant-atmosphere continuum models with real-time sensor data and predictive weather analytics. The proposed framework will employ machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets—including soil moisture profiles, evapotranspiration rates, crop-specific water requirements, and hydraulic system parameters—to generate adaptive irrigation strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process multi-terabyte datasets from distributed field sensors, satellite imagery, and hydraulic simulations at scale. Parallelized simulations will model water distribution across diverse irrigation topographies (e.g., drip, pivot, and subsurface systems) under stochastic climate scenarios, while reinforcement learning agents will iteratively optimize valve control policies and pumping schedules. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that reduces water use by 15-30% compared to conventional methods while maintaining crop yields, alongside predictive metrics for infrastructure wear-and-tear to guide system maintenance. The computational workflows will be containerized for broad adoption by agricultural extension services and irrigation technology developers. By leveraging HPC capabilities to resolve spatial-temporal complexities in irrigation dynamics, this work aims to advance precision water management practices, directly supporting the program’s mission to train professionals in next-generation agricultural technology implementation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in the field of agricultural technology and irrigation. Includes instruction in irrigation and drainage methodologies, pumping and delivery systems, system design and evaluation, and principles of installation and repair of irrigation systems.

abstract: The increasing availability of large-scale, high-dimensional datasets in fields such as public health and environmental science has exposed critical limitations in traditional statistical methodologies, particularly in Bayesian hierarchical modeling and non-parametric regression. These approaches, while theoretically robust, often face prohibitive computational demands when applied to modern datasets due to their reliance on iterative sampling techniques and complex dependency structures. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing scalable computational frameworks optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. Specifically, we propose the implementation of parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms designed to leverage distributed memory architectures, enabling efficient sampling from high-dimensional posterior distributions. Additionally, we will investigate adaptive Monte Carlo methods combined with stochastic gradient-based variational inference to reduce convergence times in hierarchical models. The computational workflows will be integrated with non-parametric bootstrap resampling techniques, parallelized across multiple nodes to handle massive datasets. By utilizing HPC resources, this research aims to overcome existing bottlenecks in statistical computation, facilitating the analysis of datasets that are currently intractable due to size or complexity. The expected outcomes include novel algorithmic implementations that bridge statistical theory with computational efficiency, validated through case studies in climate modeling and epidemiological surveillance. These advancements will not only expand the applicability of Bayesian and non-parametric methods but also provide open-source tools to the statistical community, fostering reproducible research in data-intensive domains. The project underscores the critical role of HPC in advancing modern statistical methodology, ensuring that theoretical rigor keeps pace with the growing scale of real-world data challenges.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for creating dynamic, multi-sensory installations that integrate generative visuals, spatial audio, and interactive elements in real time. A central challenge in intermedia art lies in synchronizing heterogeneous data streams—such as motion capture, environmental sensors, and audience inputs—while maintaining low-latency responses critical for immersive experiences. Current tools often fragment workflows, limiting scalability and forcing artists to compromise between complexity and real-time performance. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline leveraging parallelized rendering, machine learning models for adaptive content generation, and distributed networking protocols. The project will utilize GPU clusters to train generative adversarial networks (GANs) capable of synthesizing visual and auditory content conditioned on real-time sensor data, while MPI-based simulations will model spatial interactions in large-scale installations. A key innovation involves developing hybrid neural-radiance field (NeRF) techniques optimized for rapid viewpoint synthesis, enabling viewers to influence volumetric projections through movement. Resource-intensive tasks like latent space exploration for multi-modal outputs and physics-based sound propagation modeling will require dedicated HPC allocations to achieve sub-20ms latency thresholds. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for intermedia artists, quantitative benchmarks for temporal synchronization in mixed-reality environments, and two public installations demonstrating scalable interaction paradigms. By establishing computationally rigorous methods for unifying disparate media layers, this work aims to expand the boundaries of participatory art while providing a replicable framework for resource-intensive creative computation. The requested resources directly support both the training of large-scale generative models and the deployment of interactive systems that would be infeasible on consumer-grade hardware, addressing critical gaps in current digital art infrastructure.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions in either two or three dimensions, through simultaneous use of a variety of materials and media.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of the dynamic interplay between psychosocial factors and athletic performance through the development of multilevel computational models. Despite growing recognition of the complexity inherent in sport behavior—where motor, physiological, and psychological variables interact in real time—existing methodologies often rely on static, reductionist analyses that fail to capture nonlinear or emergent effects. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and analyze large-scale datasets integrating psychometric assessments (e.g., resilience, attentional focus), biometric data (e.g., heart rate variability, motion capture), and performance outcomes across diverse athletic populations. Agent-based modeling will be employed to investigate how individual differences in personality traits and stress responses propagate within team dynamics, while machine learning techniques will identify predictive biomarkers of optimal performance states under competitive pressure. A key innovation involves coupling these models with real-time neurofeedback data to simulate the efficacy of mind-body interventions (e.g., mindfulness, imagery) on performance consistency. The computational demands of processing high-dimensional, multimodal datasets—often spanning millions of data points from wearable sensors and video analytics—necessitate parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated training of deep neural networks. Expected outcomes include actionable frameworks for coaches and sport psychologists to personalize mental skills training, optimize team cohesion strategies, and mitigate performance anxiety. By elucidating the mechanistic links between psychosocial factors and motor outcomes, this work will establish a scalable computational toolkit for ethical performance enhancement, directly aligning with the program’s mission to bridge counseling practices with sport science. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter-intensive simulations that are infeasible on local hardware, ensuring robust validation of models across demographic and sport-specific contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the motor, physiological, and psychosocial aspects of sport behavior. Includes instruction in applied sport psychology, clinical mental health counseling, coaching, exercise physiology, ethical performance enhancement; human development, leadership and team building, mind-body practices, neuroscience, and personality and health.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of real-time, data-driven visual communication design by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable advanced computational workflows in interactive media and immersive environments. Contemporary design challenges—such as rendering photorealistic 3D visualizations, simulating dynamic user interactions at scale, and optimizing generative AI models for adaptive branding systems—require processing capabilities beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The research focuses on developing and testing algorithmic frameworks for two core applications: (1) real-time parametric design systems that iteratively optimize visual outputs based on user behavior analytics, and (2) large-scale neural network training for AI-assisted design tools capable of predicting aesthetic preferences across diverse demographic datasets. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines, distributed processing of multi-modal interaction data, and evolutionary algorithms for automated layout optimization. By utilizing HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce iterative design cycles from hours to minutes while maintaining 4K/8K resolution fidelity, enabling unprecedented experimentation with hyper-personalized visual narratives. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic typography generation, a benchmark dataset linking biometric feedback to design effectiveness metrics, and scalable models for sustainable digital packaging simulations. This work will directly enhance pedagogical approaches in visual communication by integrating computational design literacy into curricula while providing industry-relevant frameworks for energy-efficient rendering pipelines. The requested resources are critical to overcoming memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in simulating complex viewer-environment-design interactions, ultimately advancing the field’s capacity to create ethically informed, computationally sophisticated visual solutions.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that focuses on the general principles and techniques for effectively communicating ideas and information, and packaging products, in digital and other formats to business and consumer audiences, and that may prepare individuals in any of the applied art media.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions aim to address complex, individualized patient needs influenced by dynamic interactions between physical, cognitive, psychosocial, and environmental factors. Current methodologies for designing and optimizing these interventions face limitations in scalability, personalization, and real-time adaptability due to the high dimensionality of patient data and the computational demands of modeling multifaceted health outcomes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a computational framework for simulating patient-specific OT intervention strategies. The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, wearable sensor data, environmental scans, and patient-reported outcomes—to construct predictive models of functional improvement and quality-of-life metrics. Machine learning algorithms, such as reinforcement learning and graph neural networks, will be employed to model the nonlinear relationships between intervention variables (e.g., assistive technologies, task modifications, therapeutic schedules) and patient progress. Agent-based simulations will further explore how environmental adaptations and social determinants of health interact with clinical interventions in diverse virtual scenarios. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing capabilities to manage large-scale parameter sweeps, optimize hyperparameters, and conduct sensitivity analyses across thousands of simulated patient profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolset for dynamically personalizing OT interventions, (2) quantitative evidence linking specific intervention components to functional gains in populations with neurological and musculoskeletal conditions, and (3) a framework for real-time intervention adjustment using streaming data from IoT-enabled assistive devices. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of multi-modal data, this project aims to advance evidence-based practice in OT, reduce trial-and-error approaches in care delivery, and establish scalable methods for translating complex biopsychosocial models into clinical decision support systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the spatial, temporal, and parametric resolution required for these simulations within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist patients limited by physical, cognitive, psychosocial, mental, developmental, and learning disabilities, as well as adverse environmental conditions, to maximize their independence and maintain optimum health through a planned mix of acquired skills, performance motivation, environmental adaptations, assistive technologies, and physical agents. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, psychology, sociology, patient assessment and evaluation, standardized and non-standardized tests and measurements, assistive and rehabilitative technologies, ergonomics, environmental health, special education, vocational counseling, health education and promotion, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of small business resilience within hyperlocal digital marketplaces, a nascent domain intersecting computational economics, behavioral analytics, and decentralized platform design. Small businesses increasingly rely on geographically constrained digital platforms (e.g., neighborhood delivery apps, community-based e-commerce) to compete with larger enterprises, yet the systemic interdependencies between platform algorithms, consumer behavior, and micro-enterprise decision-making remain poorly understood. The core research problem centers on identifying computational strategies to simulate and optimize small business survival rates in these environments, where traditional econometric models fail to capture real-time feedback loops and nonlinear scaling effects. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) frameworks, we will simulate multi-stakeholder interactions across 10,000+ agent businesses and consumers, incorporating geospatial data, dynamic pricing algorithms, and stochastic demand shocks. HPC resources will enable parallelized scenario testing of platform governance policies (e.g., fee structures, visibility algorithms) and their impact on small business viability under varying macroeconomic conditions. The computational architecture integrates reinforcement learning to model adaptive business strategies, validated against empirical datasets from regional small business alliances. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable simulation toolkit to predict platform-induced market distortions and evidence-based design principles for equitable digital ecosystems. This work addresses a critical gap in small business policy by quantifying how algorithmic platform features disproportionately affect micro-enterprises, providing actionable insights for policymakers and platform developers. The project’s computational demands—including terabyte-scale scenario libraries and real-time optimization of high-dimensional parameter spaces—necessitate cluster computing infrastructure to achieve practical runtime for iterative, data-driven experimentation. Results will directly inform regulatory frameworks and small business training programs focused on digital transition challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage independent small businesses. Includes instruction in business administration; enterprise planning and entrepreneurship; start-up; small business operations and problems; personnel supervision; capitalization and investment; taxation; business law and regulations; e-commerce; home business operations; and applications to specific sectors, products, and services.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize casino floor operations, with a focus on dynamic resource allocation and risk mitigation in live gaming environments. The problem addressed is the lack of scalable, real-time decision-making tools for casino managers to balance operational efficiency, customer experience, and regulatory compliance amid fluctuating demand patterns and security challenges. Current industry practices rely heavily on static scheduling and human intuition, which struggle to adapt to complex variables such as patron flow, game popularity shifts, and evolving fraud tactics. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patron behaviors, staff movements, and security incidents across a parameterized virtual casino environment. High-performance computing resources are required to run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations that account for probabilistic gaming outcomes, surveillance system latency, and multi-objective optimization constraints (e.g., labor costs vs. table game coverage). Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify patterns in historical security breach data and generate predictive alerts for anomalous activities. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit capable of testing operational scenarios at casino-scale resolution, quantitative metrics for evaluating surveillance system responsiveness, and adaptive staffing algorithms that reduce service bottlenecks by 15-20% in benchmark tests. By bridging computational systems theory with gaming operations management, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for next-generation casino resource planning while maintaining compliance with jurisdictional gaming regulations. The computational infrastructure will enable replication studies across diverse virtual floor layouts and regulatory regimes, providing a foundation for data-driven policymaking in the global gaming industry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on casino operations and services. Includes instruction in casino operations, casino security and surveillance, casino dealing, principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: Mental health disorders represent a significant global burden, yet their underlying biological and psychosocial mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the complexity of interacting genetic, neuroimaging, behavioral, and environmental factors. This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting treatment outcomes for major depressive disorder (MDD) and schizophrenia by integrating multi-modal datasets at unprecedented scale. Current analytical approaches are limited by fragmented data sources, statistical power constraints, and an inability to model dynamic interactions across spatiotemporal biological systems. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to unify neuroimaging (fMRI, DTI), genomic (GWAS, RNA-seq), electronic health record (EHR), and real-time digital phenotyping data from 15,000 patients across 6 international cohorts. Custom machine learning pipelines will be implemented to handle feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, and cross-modal alignment of heterogeneous data types. Deep graph neural networks will model brain connectome dynamics alongside polygenic risk scores, while transformer-based architectures will process longitudinal EHR text for symptom trajectory analysis. Computational demands necessitate large-memory nodes and GPU clusters for training multi-task models with >100 million parameters. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of reproducible biotypes predicting antidepressant response with ≥80% accuracy, 2) dynamic risk stratification models for psychosis conversion, and 3) open-source tools for federated analysis of sensitive mental health data. The resource allocation will directly support clinical translation by enabling validation of computational biomarkers in active randomized trials (NCT04508712, NCT05331767). This work addresses NIH priorities for precision psychiatry by creating infrastructure to overcome current computational bottlenecks in multi-scale data integration, with potential to redefine diagnostic paradigms and accelerate therapeutic discovery.
cip_definition: Research focused on Psychiatric/Mental Health

abstract: The increasing complexity of music industry ecosystems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize decision-making in artist management, event logistics, and revenue generation. This project seeks to address the challenge of dynamically modeling music market trends, audience engagement patterns, and resource allocation strategies for mid-sized music organizations, which currently lack access to scalable analytical frameworks. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose developing a hybrid simulation platform integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and network analysis to evaluate multi-variable scenarios in real time. The computational framework will process heterogeneous datasets—including streaming platform metrics, social media sentiment, historical ticket sales, and artist contractual constraints—to simulate outcomes of marketing campaigns, tour routing configurations, and digital distribution strategies. Key objectives include quantifying the cascading effects of regional audience preferences on venue selection, optimizing merchandise pricing elasticity under fluctuating demand, and predicting the financial viability of hybrid live-virtual events. By parallelizing resource-intensive tasks such as cross-platform data fusion and probabilistic risk assessment, HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of scenarios accounting for stochastic variables like shifting consumer behavior and supply chain disruptions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support toolkit for music managers, validated through case studies with three independent record labels and festival organizers. This work will contribute novel methodologies for computational arts management, particularly in balancing creative objectives with operational constraints. The project’s scalable approach to simulating music industry micro-economies has broader implications for equitable resource distribution in cultural sectors, with potential applications in policy development for regional arts funding models.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage music organizations, operations, facilities, and personnel. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; music products merchandising; artist agency and promotion; music law; and applications to specific activities such as managing theaters, recording studios and companies, bands and other ensembles, individual artists, and music organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing personalized care coordination for patients with complex, overlapping chronic conditions in community-based health settings. Health aides, who serve as frontline support in these environments, often lack access to real-time computational tools to integrate and interpret heterogeneous patient data streams—including wearable sensor outputs, electronic health record snippets, and patient-reported symptom logs—into actionable insights. The research aims to develop a machine learning (ML) framework that dynamically synthesizes these multimodal datasets to predict acute health event risks (e.g., falls, medication non-adherence crises) and recommend preemptive interventions. A core innovation lies in adapting transformer-based architectures, typically used in natural language processing, to model temporal patterns in sparse, irregularly sampled physiological and behavioral data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train these models on synthetic datasets mirroring real-world noise and missingness, followed by validation on de-identified data from community health partnerships. Computational workflows will prioritize low-latency inference to enable integration with mobile health aide platforms. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source pipeline for lightweight model deployment and evidence-based guidelines for health aide workflows that balance predictive accuracy with interpretability. By focusing on the understudied intersection of edge computing, temporal ML, and community health operations, this work aims to bridge a critical gap in decision support tools for non-specialist caregivers, ultimately reducing preventable hospitalizations in underserved populations. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for parallelized hyperparameter optimization and large-scale synthetic data generation—necessitate GPU-accelerated clusters and scalable storage solutions, aligning with HPC infrastructure capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and assistance to patients under the direct supervision of other health care professionals, and/or to perform routine maintenance and general assistance in health care facilities and laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address unresolved questions regarding the evolutionary drivers of morphological and genetic variation in hominins. A central challenge in physical anthropology lies in disentangling the complex interplay of genetic, environmental, and functional factors that shaped skeletal and physiological adaptations in human ancestors. Current limitations stem from the computational intensity required to integrate large-scale genomic datasets, biomechanical simulations, and comparative morphological analyses across fragmented fossil records. We propose a multi-pronged computational approach combining paleogenomic association studies, finite element analysis (FEA) of cranial biomechanics, and agent-based modeling of population dynamics. HPC resources will enable genome-wide scans for selection in archaic hominin DNA, coupled with 3D FEA simulations to test functional hypotheses about mastication and cranial capacity across Pleistocene taxa. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate ecological pressures and social behaviors influencing adaptive trajectories. This integrative framework requires parallel processing capabilities to manage terabyte-scale genomic datasets, iterative biomechanical simulations across parameter spaces, and probabilistic modeling of evolutionary scenarios. Expected outcomes include identifying candidate genomic regions associated with key adaptations (e.g., encephalization, dietary shifts), quantifying biomechanical trade-offs in fossil morphology, and reconstructing selective pressures during hominin dispersals. The computational pipeline developed through this work will be disseminated as an open-source toolkit, enhancing reproducibility in evolutionary anthropology. By bridging molecular, morphological, and ecological datasets through scalable computing, this research aims to advance mechanistic understanding of human evolution while establishing infrastructure for data-intensive anthropological inquiry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and anthropology to the study of the adaptations, variability, and the evolution of human beings and their living and fossil relatives. Includes instructions in anthropology, human and mammalian anatomy, cell biology, paleontology, human culture and behavior, neuroscience, forensic anthropology, anatomical reconstruction, comparative anatomy, and laboratory science and methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in precision machining processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize advanced manufacturing workflows. Modern machine tool operations face increasing demands to fabricate high-tolerance components from complex materials, such as high-strength alloys and composites, while minimizing waste, energy consumption, and tool wear. Current experimental trial-and-error methods are time-intensive and costly, particularly for novel materials or intricate geometries. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and multi-physics simulations to predict machining outcomes under diverse conditions. HPC resources will enable high-resolution modeling of dynamic interactions between cutting tools, workpieces, and coolant systems, incorporating variables such as thermal deformation, vibration, and material microstructure. A key focus is developing predictive models for tool wear and surface finish quality across varying feed rates, spindle speeds, and toolpath strategies. Experimental data from CNC machining centers will validate simulations, creating feedback loops to refine ML algorithms. The computational workflow will also assess sustainability metrics, including energy efficiency and material utilization, to guide eco-conscious process design. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping, this project aims to reduce physical testing cycles by 40-60% while improving machining accuracy for aerospace and medical device applications. Outcomes will include open-access simulation templates and a decision-support tool for machinists to optimize parameters in real time. This work bridges computational engineering with hands-on manufacturing expertise, offering a scalable solution to enhance both precision and productivity in machine tool operations. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the tera-scale datasets and parallelized simulations required for these multi-layered analyses, which cannot feasibly run on local computing resources. The results will directly benefit industrial partners and advance curriculum development in smart manufacturing technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, manufacture, assemble, test, and repair parts, mechanisms, machines, and structures in which materials are cast, formed, shaped, molded, heat treated, cut, twisted, pressed, fused, stamped or worked.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of modeling phonetic and syntactic evolution in regional Chinese dialects, many of which are under-documented and at risk of obsolescence due to linguistic homogenization. While existing studies have cataloged select dialects, systematic computational analyses of their dynamic interactions with Standard Mandarin remain limited. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this research will process and analyze multi-modal linguistic data—including spoken corpora, historical texts, and contemporary social media—to map dialectal variations and their sociolinguistic trajectories. Computational methods will integrate neural language models fine-tuned for low-resource dialects, phonetic alignment algorithms to trace sound shifts, and graph-based networks to model syntactic convergence. The scale of data (projected at 50+ TB of audio recordings and 10 million+ text samples from 15 dialect groups) necessitates distributed storage and GPU-accelerated processing for training transformer-based architectures. Expected outcomes include a dynamically annotated dialect atlas, predictive models of language change, and open-source tools for automated dialect identification. These resources will advance philological research on Chinese language diversity while supporting practical applications in education, speech technology, and heritage preservation. By quantifying how regional dialects adapt within multilingual ecosystems, this work will provide novel insights into language contact phenomena and inform policy efforts to sustain linguistic diversity in China’s rapidly urbanizing society. The project’s computational demands—particularly in parallelized feature extraction and large-scale semantic clustering—are only feasible with HPC infrastructure, which will enable iterative analysis across spatial, temporal, and sociocultural dimensions of dialect data.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of China and associated dialects and literature. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling complex, nonlinear interactions between human cultural dynamics and ecological systems to improve predictive accuracy in environmental management. Traditional ecological models often overlook localized socio-cultural factors—such as community resource-use practices, informal governance structures, or culturally mediated responses to policy—that significantly influence ecosystem outcomes. We propose an interdisciplinary framework integrating ecological sensor data, ethnographic surveys, and social media analytics to quantify these interactions at scale. The research will develop a hybrid computational architecture combining agent-based modeling (ABM), graph neural networks (GNNs), and Bayesian hierarchical models to capture feedback loops between cultural behaviors (e.g., seasonal harvesting traditions) and biophysical processes (e.g., species population dynamics). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) parallelized ABM simulations of human-environment interactions across diverse cultural and ecological scenarios; (2) training GNNs on heterogeneous data streams (10+ TB of spatiotemporal ecological data paired with socio-cultural indicators); and (3) global sensitivity analyses to identify leverage points for culturally informed conservation strategies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible library of adaptable cultural-ecological modules for environmental modeling and novel metrics quantifying "cultural resonance" in policy effectiveness. This work bridges anthropology, conservation biology, and computational social science, offering a template for embedding human complexity into sustainability science while advancing scalable methods for multimodal data integration. The requested allocation of 500,000 CPU-hours and GPU-accelerated nodes will enable parameter exploration at resolutions necessary to inform UNESCO Biosphere Reserve management protocols, with direct applications to 15 partnered Indigenous-led conservation initiatives.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data analytics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on Appalachian cultural heritage through large-scale analysis of ethnographic, linguistic, and musical datasets. Appalachia’s rich cultural traditions, including its dialects, oral histories, and folk music, face challenges in preservation and contextualization due to the region’s geographic dispersion and the volume of unstructured historical data. Current methodologies, reliant on manual curation and localized studies, struggle to synthesize patterns across diverse communities or trace cultural transmission over time. This project addresses these limitations by applying computational techniques to digitized archives, including audio recordings of Appalachian English variants, transcribed oral narratives, and ethnomusicological collections. Machine learning models will be trained to identify linguistic features and dialect boundaries, while natural language processing tools will map thematic evolution in oral histories. Concurrently, audio signal processing algorithms will analyze melodic and rhythmic structures in traditional music to explore cross-community influences. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize computationally intensive tasks such as neural network training and spectral analysis, and support geospatial visualization of cultural networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of analyzed materials, tools for automated dialect classification, and interactive maps illustrating cultural exchange pathways. By integrating computational rigor with community-engaged scholarship, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of Appalachian identity while providing actionable resources for heritage preservation initiatives. The project’s findings will contribute to broader discourses on regional cultural sustainability and demonstrate the transformative potential of HPC in humanities-driven area studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, sociology, culture, and economics of the Appalachian region of the United States. Includes instruction in contemporary issues in Appalachia, political economy of Appalachia, community-based research, ethnomusicology, and oral and written languages of Appalachia.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance structural optimization and safety analysis in ironworking through computational modeling and simulation. Ironworkers face persistent challenges in designing and installing metal structures that balance cost, material efficiency, and compliance with evolving safety standards. Traditional trial-and-error methods for testing load capacities, weld integrity, and dynamic responses to environmental stressors are time-intensive and limited in scope. To address these constraints, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and generative design algorithms. The framework will simulate structural behaviors under diverse loads, temperatures, and corrosion scenarios, with a focus on optimizing beam placement, joint reinforcement, and ornamental design stability. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of large-scale structural assemblies, such as multi-story steel frames and complex architectural features, while ML models trained on historical failure data will predict high-risk configurations. A key innovation involves coupling generative adversarial networks (GANs) with physics-based solvers to automate the creation of code-compliant, material-efficient designs. The computational pipeline will be validated against physical testing data from partner workshops and real-world case studies of structural failures. Outcomes include open-source tools for rapid structural analysis, a database of optimized design templates for educational use, and evidence-based recommendations for updating training protocols and safety codes. By integrating computational rigor into ironworking workflows, this research aims to reduce material waste, enhance disaster resilience, and bridge gaps between traditional craftsmanship and modern computational engineering. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces and iterative optimization processes inherent to this work, which cannot feasibly be executed on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to make and install structural, ornamental, and reinforcing metal structures and supports. Includes instruction in drafting, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, welding, riveting, beam placement, ornamental design, structural reinforcement, crane operation, safety, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational frameworks for optimizing law enforcement interview and interrogation strategies, with a focus on minimizing cognitive bias and improving the reliability of investigative outcomes. Current practices in tactical interviewing rely heavily on manual analysis of verbal and non-verbal cues, which are susceptible to human error, subjective interpretation, and contextual variability. To address these limitations, the research will employ machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze large-scale datasets of recorded interviews, interrogations, and case outcomes. These datasets will include multimodal inputs such as speech transcripts, vocal tone patterns, facial microexpressions, and physiological data (e.g., heart rate variability) from body-worn sensor recordings. Computational models will be trained to identify patterns associated with truthful versus deceptive responses, stress indicators, and interviewer techniques that correlate with successful case resolutions. A key innovation involves simulating diverse interview scenarios through agent-based modeling to test the efficacy of adaptive questioning strategies under varying psychological and legal constraints. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of audiovisual data, running parallelized ML training workflows, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in model predictions. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-source tools for real-time decision support during interviews, validated protocols to reduce investigator bias, and a framework for ethically integrating AI-assisted analytics into legal and procedural guidelines. By bridging computational science with forensic psychology and investigative praxis, this work aims to enhance the fairness, efficiency, and transparency of law enforcement processes while maintaining strict adherence to legal and human rights standards.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, procedures, techniques, legal concerns, and problems associated with a criminal investigation. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, courtroom evidence management and preparation, case presentation and court testimony, description and identification, state and federal criminal law and procedures, informant and suspect rights, officer liability, informant and witness management, victim awareness, tactical interviewing, psychology, criminal investigation methods and procedures, report writing and documentation, investigative techniques, and case management.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in resource allocation for youth social service programs by developing a computational framework to model service demand, optimize intervention strategies, and predict long-term outcomes. Current approaches to planning youth services often rely on static demographic data and qualitative assessments, which struggle to account for dynamic factors such as shifting community needs, interrelated risk factors (e.g., housing instability, educational access), and the cascading effects of policy changes. We propose a multi-agent simulation system that integrates real-world datasets—including anonymized case management records, regional economic indicators, and public health statistics—to create adaptive models of service ecosystems. The computational approach will employ Bayesian network analysis to identify critical leverage points in service delivery chains, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate and compare intervention scenarios. High-performance computing resources are essential to process these complex, high-dimensional datasets and run thousands of parallel simulations testing variations in funding distributions, staffing patterns, and collaborative partnerships across agencies. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between short-term budgetary constraints and long-term youth outcomes, such as reduced juvenile justice involvement or improved school retention rates. The models will also evaluate how ethical considerations embedded in program designs (e.g., equity in service access, cultural responsiveness) correlate with system-wide performance metrics. By bridging computational social science with public administration praxis, this work aims to provide actionable insights for scaling evidence-based youth programs while maintaining fidelity to professional standards in social services. The resulting framework will be shared as open-source software to enable replication in diverse municipal contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and implement social services for children, youth, and families. Includes instruction in child development and psychology, adolescence, family studies, social work, social services administration, juvenile and family law, program and facilities planning, youth leadership, counseling, probation, casework, applicable procedures and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Cybersecurity threats to critical infrastructure and national systems are evolving in complexity and scale, necessitating advanced computational tools to model, analyze, and preempt adversarial strategies. Current approaches to cybersecurity policy and defense strategy development often rely on static risk assessments or isolated simulations, which inadequately capture the dynamic, large-scale interactions between attackers, defenders, and infrastructure. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-layered simulation framework for evaluating cybersecurity policies under realistic, evolving threat conditions. The research will model adversarial behavior, network vulnerabilities, and defensive countermeasures across interconnected systems—such as power grids, emergency response networks, and federal databases—using agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning-driven threat prediction. Computational experiments will simulate millions of attack-defend scenarios to stress-test policy interventions, including incident response protocols, zero-trust architecture adoption, and cross-sector recovery coordination. The HPC environment will enable parallelized analysis of scenario outcomes, real-time adaptation of threat actors, and probabilistic assessments of policy effectiveness. Outcomes will include a validated policy optimization toolkit for cybersecurity decision-makers, actionable metrics for infrastructure resiliency, and a public dataset of simulated attack patterns to inform national defense standards. By quantifying trade-offs between proactive deterrence, rapid recovery, and systemic vulnerability reduction, this work aims to advance evidence-based cybersecurity strategy in homeland security domains, ensuring computational scalability to match the pace of modern cyber threats.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of personalized dietary intervention optimization by investigating the complex interplay between host metabolism, gut microbiota dynamics, and nutritional inputs. Current clinical nutrition frameworks often rely on population-level recommendations, which fail to account for individual variations in microbial community structure, metabolic pathways, and nutrient processing efficiency. We propose to develop a computational platform integrating multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and proteomic profiles) with physiological parameters to model personalized nutrient-microbiome-host interactions. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to identify predictive biomarkers of dietary response variability and agent-based modeling to simulate microbial community shifts under different nutritional regimes. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (>10 TB of multi-omics data from clinical cohorts), training deep neural networks to recognize nonlinear relationships between dietary components and metabolic outcomes, and running parallelized simulations of gut ecosystem dynamics across diverse virtual patient profiles. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-source predictive tool for optimizing clinical nutrition strategies in metabolic disorders, identification of microbial taxa associated with differential nutrient absorption efficiency, and novel insights into temporal patterns of microbiome-mediated food compound transformation. This work bridges computational biology, systems nutrition, and clinical dietetics, offering a transformative approach to precision nutrition that could inform therapeutic dietary interventions for conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and micronutrient deficiency syndromes. The computational framework developed will enable real-time adjustment of dietary recommendations based on individual microbial and metabolic signatures, advancing the field beyond current one-size-fits-all paradigms in clinical nutrition practice.
cip_title: Dietetics and Clinical Nutrition Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dietetics and clinical nutrition services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the socio-economic and political transformations of urban centers in the medieval Near East (8th–14th centuries CE) through the integration of heterogeneous historical datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how cities such as Baghdad, Cairo, and Damascus adapted to shifting trade networks, environmental pressures, and governance structures. Existing scholarship relies heavily on qualitative analysis of textual sources, which limits the ability to systematically model complex, interdependent variables across time and space. To overcome this, the project will employ computational methods to synthesize Arabic chronicles, archaeological records, climate proxy data, and economic documents (e.g., waqf deeds, tax registers) into a unified geotemporal framework. Key computational tasks include natural language processing (NLP) of classical Arabic texts to extract entity relationships and event chronologies, agent-based modeling to simulate trade dynamics and resource allocation under varying climatic conditions, and network analysis to map shifts in political and commercial connectivity. These workflows require HPC capabilities due to the scale of textual corpora (over 10,000 digitized pages), the iterative nature of agent-based simulations (1,000+ parameter combinations), and the need for high-resolution spatial analysis. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized patterns in urban resilience, such as the role of decentralized water management systems in mitigating drought impacts, and the reconstruction of trade corridor efficiencies under different political regimes. The project will produce open-access datasets and computational models, enabling comparative studies of premodern urbanization. By bridging computational methods with region-specific historiography, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in Near Eastern studies while generating insights into the long-term dynamics of human-environment interaction in arid-zone societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing digital printing workflows by modeling the interactions between variable substrate materials, dynamic ink deposition, and equipment performance. The graphic and printing industry faces growing demands for high-throughput, customizable production, yet traditional trial-and-error approaches to process calibration remain resource-intensive and environmentally costly. Current research lacks robust predictive tools to account for the nonlinear behavior of hybrid printing systems, particularly when integrating sustainable substrates or adaptive color management protocols. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Finite element analysis will model mechanical stress distributions in novel biodegradable substrates during high-speed printing, while computational fluid dynamics simulations will characterize ink transfer dynamics across diverse nozzle geometries and rheological profiles. Machine learning models trained on experimental datasets will predict color consistency under variable humidity and temperature conditions, with reinforcement learning algorithms iteratively optimizing press configurations. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of high-resolution 3D substrate meshes (10⁶–10⁷ elements) and real-time analysis of multi-spectral imaging data streams. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support system for predictive maintenance scheduling and substrate-ink pairing recommendations, validated through physical trials on industrial-grade equipment. By reducing material waste through virtual prototyping and enabling energy-efficient process parameter optimization, this research directly supports the graphic communications industry’s transition toward sustainable manufacturing practices. The project will also generate open-access educational modules demonstrating computational modeling applications in press operations, enhancing workforce training in emerging digital workflow strategies. Resource requests emphasize GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and high-memory nodes for handling large-scale spectral datasets, with an estimated 200,000 core-hours required for initial model development and validation phases.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the socio-cultural and structural determinants of health disparities in underserved populations by leveraging advanced computational modeling to analyze complex interactions between community practices, healthcare access, and disease outcomes. The research problem centers on understanding how non-biological factors—such as cultural beliefs, stigma, and informal care networks—shape health-seeking behaviors and contribute to inequities in treatment efficacy for chronic conditions. Existing ethnographic and public health datasets, while rich, are often siloed or insufficiently integrated to model multi-scale dynamics. To address this, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate decision-making processes at individual, household, and community levels, informed by qualitative fieldwork data (e.g., interviews, participant observation) and quantitative health records from partner clinics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of these models, which will incorporate probabilistic reasoning, network analysis of social support systems, and geospatial mapping of care accessibility. Parallelized simulations will explore scenarios varying cultural norms, economic constraints, and policy interventions, requiring iterative parameter adjustments and large-scale sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include identifying leverage points for reducing disparities—such as optimizing community health worker outreach or adapting clinic hours to local schedules—and generating predictive frameworks to assess how stigma reduction programs might alter care utilization patterns. By bridging ethnographic insights with computational social science methods, this work will advance methodological innovation in medical anthropology, offering scalable tools to analyze cultural systems in health contexts. Results will be shared with regional healthcare providers and policymakers to inform culturally grounded interventions, while model architectures will be made open-source to support interdisciplinary research on health inequities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological, socio-cultural, psychological, and behavioral factors as they relate to health, illness, medical practices, and access to health care services. Includes instruction in ethno-medicine, urban health, international health, psychiatric and psychological anthropology, aging, and health and identity.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the therapeutic efficacy of multimodal arts-based interventions in chronic pain management through advanced computational modeling of biometric and behavioral data. While arts-in-medicine programs increasingly integrate creative practices into clinical care, quantitative evidence linking specific artistic modalities—such as improvisational dance, interactive soundscapes, or generative visual art—to neurophysiological responses remains limited. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze synchronized datasets from wearable biosensors (EEG, HRV, galvanic skin response), motion capture systems, and patient-reported outcomes across 300 participants engaged in structured arts-health protocols. A custom machine learning pipeline will process temporal patterns in stress biomarkers, movement kinematics, and emotional valence metrics to identify intervention-specific signatures correlated with pain modulation. Parallel agent-based simulations will model neuroaesthetic engagement dynamics during art co-creation activities, incorporating real-world data to optimize therapeutic parameters. The computational workflow requires large-scale matrix operations for multivariate time-series alignment, GPU-accelerated neural networks for latent feature extraction, and distributed memory architectures for simulating complex patient-artist-environment interactions. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for personalizing arts prescriptions based on individual stress-pain pathways, novel digital twins of creative therapeutic processes, and publicly shareable tools for quantifying arts’ biological impact. By establishing computational links between artistic engagement and measurable health outcomes, this work aims to advance evidence-based integration of arts modalities into clinical pain management while demonstrating the critical role of HPC in emerging health humanities research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of programs that use the visual and performing arts in support of health and wellness among diverse individuals and communities. Includes instruction in dance, literary arts, music, theatre, healthcare systems, program administration, and public health.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving rhetorical strategies employed in multimodal digital compositions across diverse online platforms, with a focus on understanding how visual, textual, and interactive elements are integrated to persuade, inform, and engage audiences. While existing scholarship in rhetoric and composition has explored the theoretical dimensions of multimodality, there remains a critical gap in large-scale empirical analyses of how these strategies function in practice, particularly in dynamic, real-world digital contexts. To address this, the research will employ computational text analysis, image recognition algorithms, and network analysis to examine a corpus of over 500,000 multimodal texts (e.g., social media posts, digital essays, interactive infographics) sourced from public platforms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process this heterogeneous dataset, which includes high-resolution images, video metadata, and hyperlinked content, as well as to train machine learning models capable of identifying recurring rhetorical patterns across modalities. The computational workflow will involve parallel processing of multimedia files, GPU-accelerated deep learning for visual rhetoric classification, and natural language processing to map textual-visual cohesion. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for analyzing multimodal rhetoric at scale, (2) data-driven insights into how digital composers adapt classical rhetorical concepts (e.g., ethos, pathos) to hybrid media environments, and (3) pedagogical recommendations for teaching multimodal literacy in composition curricula. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance both methodological innovation in humanities research and practical understanding of 21st-century writing practices, ultimately supporting writing program administrators in designing curricula responsive to rapidly changing communicative norms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the humanistic and scientific study of rhetoric, composition, literacy, and language/linguistic theories and their practical and pedagogical applications. Includes instruction in historical and contemporary rhetoric/composition theories; composition and criticism of written, visual, and mixed-media texts; analysis of literacy practices in cultural and cross-cultural contexts; and writing program administration.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework to model emergent dynamics in coupled socio-technical-ecological systems (STES), with a focus on resilience thresholds in urban food-energy-water (FEW) networks under climate volatility. While existing approaches often isolate technical or ecological subsystems, our work integrates granular behavioral data, infrastructure interdependencies, and stochastic environmental stressors into a unified agent-based and system dynamics model. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting cascading failures when human adaptive behaviors, such as shifting resource consumption patterns, interact with engineered systems and biophysical constraints during prolonged droughts or heatwaves. The computational methodology combines three elements: (1) high-resolution network analysis of FEW flows across urban and peri-urban regions, (2) bounded-rationality decision algorithms for households and institutional actors calibrated to survey data, and (3) climate ensembles projecting compound extreme events at city-region scales. By implementing hybrid parallelization strategies across GPU and CPU architectures, the framework will simulate decade-scale trajectories at 12-hour temporal resolution for systems comprising >10^6 interdependent agents and infrastructure nodes. Key innovations include adaptive meshing techniques to handle multi-physics interactions between discrete behavioral choices and continuous material flows, along with uncertainty quantification through iterative Latin hypercube sampling. Expected outcomes include identification of leverage points for preventing systemic collapse, validated against historical crisis events in three climate-vulnerable megacities. The resulting open-source toolkit will enable policymakers to stress-test intervention portfolios across social, technical, and ecological domains simultaneously—a capability critical for achieving climate adaptation goals under deep uncertainty. This work advances systems science by creating the first scalable platform to observe phase transitions in STES through the lens of distributed human-environment coupling rather than traditional sectoral boundaries.
cip_definition: A program with a multidisciplinary approach to the analysis and solution of complex problems, requiring a combined approach using data and models from the natural, social, technological, behavioral and life sciences, and other specialized fields.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the computational challenges in modeling active matter systems—engineered or natural materials that exhibit autonomous motion or dynamic reorganization through energy dissipation. These systems, such as synthetic particle swarms or stimuli-responsive metamaterials, present complex multiscale interactions involving hydrodynamic, mechanical, and activity-induced forces. Existing simulation frameworks struggle to resolve the emergent collective behaviors of these systems at experimentally relevant scales due to prohibitive computational costs and limitations in coupling discrete activity models with continuum mechanics. This project will develop a scalable, hybrid computational framework combining smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), discrete element methods (DEM), and graph neural networks (GNNs) to model active matter across spatiotemporal scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallelization of particle-based solvers for systems exceeding 10^8 degrees of freedom, while machine learning surrogates will accelerate closure terms for activity-induced stress fields. Validation will leverage experimental datasets from collaborative studies on magnetically actuated colloidal assemblies. The outcomes will provide an open-source software toolkit for simulating active matter, advancing the design of adaptive materials for applications in reconfigurable robotics, energy-efficient smart composites, and programmable matter. By integrating particle methods with data-driven modeling on HPC architectures, this work will establish new benchmarks for computational mechanics in understudied, non-equilibrium systems, bridging gaps between classical continuum theories and discrete, activity-driven phenomena. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for ML integration and high-memory nodes to handle large-scale particle datasets, critical for achieving the proposed methodological innovations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to the application of mechanics. Incudes instruction in method development in solid, fluid mechanics and materials simulations with application to biomechanics and mechanics in medicine, multiphysics, fracture mechanics, multiscale mechanics, particle and meshfree methods.

abstract: Directed energy systems (DES) represent a critical frontier in modern defense technology, yet their operational effectiveness is constrained by the complex interplay of atmospheric turbulence, thermal blooming, and dynamic target engagement scenarios. This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling high-energy laser (HEL) propagation under real-world conditions, with a focus on optimizing beam control and mitigating performance-degrading effects in tactical environments. Current simulations often rely on oversimplified atmospheric models or static scenarios, limiting their utility for real-time decision-making and system design. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating wave optics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven adaptive optics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the execution of high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations to model laser propagation through stochastic atmospheric layers, coupled with GPU-accelerated CFD analyses of thermal blooming effects during prolonged beam engagement. A novel machine learning component will train surrogate models on this dataset to predict optimal mirror actuator configurations for beam correction under rapidly changing conditions.
