The computational workflow will leverage containerized workflows for scalability across heterogeneous architectures, ensuring efficient resource utilization. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for beam degradation thresholds, open-source simulation tools tailored for DES applications, and actionable insights into adaptive optics configurations for field-deployable systems. This research directly supports the advancement of resilient directed energy platforms by providing a computationally tractable pathway to simulate scenarios currently beyond the reach of single-node systems, thereby informing both next-generation hardware designs and real-time operational protocols.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of lasers and other directed energy phenomena and their application to the creation of energy beam weapons systems. Includes instruction in photonics, electro-optics, microwave phenomena, laser chemistry, spectroscopy, chemical lasers, fibre lasers, imaging and optics, laser propagation and control, laser communication, infrared remote sensing, modeling and simulation, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize customer service operations in large-scale, dynamic environments. Customer service management faces growing complexity due to the integration of multichannel support systems (e.g., call centers, chatbots, email) and the need for real-time decision-making under fluctuating demand. Traditional analytical methods struggle to simulate these systems at scale, particularly when accounting for stochastic customer behavior, agent skill variability, and operational constraints. To address this gap, the research will develop agent-based simulation models and machine learning frameworks to analyze customer interaction patterns, predict service bottlenecks, and test adaptive resource allocation strategies. Computational workflows will integrate anonymized customer service datasets—including call logs, chat transcripts, and resolution metrics—to train models on historical patterns. Parallelized simulations will evaluate scenarios such as demand surges, staff scheduling adjustments, and technology integration (e.g., AI-assisted routing). The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations to enterprise-level volumes, enabling the processing of millions of simulated interactions across parameterized scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to minimize wait times, balance agent workloads, and improve service quality metrics. Additionally, the project will produce a modular framework for operationalizing real-time analytics in customer service dashboards, empowering managers to make data-driven adjustments. By quantifying trade-offs between resource costs and service outcomes, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in customer service management while demonstrating the value of computational methods in business decision-making. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and open-source toolkits to bridge academic research and applied management challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and monitor customer service performance and manage frontline customer support services, call centers/help desks, and customer relations. Includes instruction in customer behavior, specialized information technology and systems management, developing and using customer service databases, user surveys and other feedback mechanisms, strategic and performance planning and analysis, operations management, personnel supervision, and communications and marketing skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing electrical system design and fault detection for modern residential, commercial, and industrial applications. As electrical infrastructure grows in complexity—driven by renewable energy integration, smart grid technologies, and evolving safety standards—traditional empirical methods for system analysis and troubleshooting are increasingly insufficient. To bridge this gap, we propose the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate electrical network behavior under diverse load conditions, fault scenarios, and code compliance requirements. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) to model thermal and electromagnetic interactions in wiring systems, motor controls, and distribution panels at unprecedented resolution. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and real-world electrical fault data to predict failure risks and recommend preemptive maintenance strategies. The computational workflow will integrate industry-standard electrical codes (e.g., NEC, IEC) as boundary conditions, enabling automated compliance verification during design simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for electricians to optimize system layouts, reduce energy waste, and improve safety margins in complex installations. Additionally, the project will generate benchmark datasets correlating computational predictions with physical testing results from partner training facilities. By combining HPC-driven modeling with practical electrical work paradigms, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for data-informed electrical system design and diagnostics, directly enhancing workforce training outcomes and infrastructure resilience. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the multi-physics simulations and large-scale optimization tasks inherent to modeling heterogeneous electrical networks with sub-millisecond transient event resolution.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain, and repair electric apparatus and systems such as residential, commercial, and industrial electric-power wiring; and DC and AC motors, controls, and electrical distribution panels. Includes instruction in the principles of electronics and electrical systems, wiring, power transmission, safety, industrial and household appliances, job estimation, electrical testing and inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and simulate the dynamic interplay of line, texture, and perspective in large-scale digital drawing processes, with the goal of expanding the technical and expressive boundaries of hand-drawn art in virtual environments. While traditional drawing relies on physical media, the increasing complexity of digital workflows—particularly for high-resolution, layered compositions—demands advanced computational resources to model real-time interactions between simulated tools (e.g., charcoal, ink brushes) and virtual surfaces. Current consumer-grade systems struggle with latency and fidelity when rendering nuanced mark-making at scale, limiting artists’ ability to experiment with intricate, data-heavy compositions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize two core processes: (1) physics-based simulations of tool-surface interactions using finite element analysis, optimized for GPU-accelerated rendering, and (2) machine learning models trained on high-resolution scans of traditional artworks to predict stylistic outcomes of digital strokes. The computational workflow will integrate these components within an open-source drawing platform, enabling artists to manipulate multi-gigapixel canvases with sub-millisecond latency while preserving the tactile variability of analog media. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for computational drawing research, quantitative metrics for evaluating digital tool realism, and a dataset correlating algorithmic parameters with perceptual qualities of linework. By bridging computational scalability with artistic practice, this work aims to establish new methodologies for preserving the material intelligence of hand-drawn art in digital ecosystems, with implications for archival practices, art education, and cross-disciplinary media design. The requested HPC resources are critical for training vision-transformers on terabyte-scale art datasets and maintaining iterative rendering pipelines across 10,000+ core-hour simulations.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions through representation by lines made on a surface. Includes instruction in eye-hand coordination; line, value, shape, and perspective; figure and still life drawing; the use of media such as pen and ink, pencil, charcoal, pastel, and brush; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the morphological and syntactic variations across German dialects through the development and application of computational models, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While regional dialects are critical to understanding the sociolinguistic fabric of German-speaking communities, their systematic analysis remains challenging due to the scarcity of digitized resources and the computational intensity required to process heterogeneous linguistic data. Current studies often rely on manual annotation or small-scale corpora, limiting the scope and generalizability of findings. To address this, our research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models, to analyze a newly compiled corpus comprising over 10 million words of dialectal texts spanning the 19th century to the present. This corpus integrates historical manuscripts, transcribed oral narratives, and contemporary social media data, reflecting both temporal and geographic diversity. HPC resources will enable the training of dialect-specific language models, automated morphological tagging at scale, and the identification of syntactic patterns through parallelized dependency parsing. Additionally, we will apply phylogenetic algorithms to model the divergence of dialects over time, correlating linguistic shifts with sociocultural factors. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated model training and large-memory processing of high-dimensional linguistic data—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialectal features, predictive models for dialect classification, and visualizations of dialect evolution trajectories. This research will advance the field of German philology by providing scalable methods for dialect studies, while also informing resource development for NLP applications tailored to non-standard language varieties, such as regional speech recognition systems. By bridging computational linguistics with traditional dialectology, the project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in preserving and analyzing linguistic diversity.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the German language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the urgent challenge of optimizing sustainable forest resource management under rapidly changing climatic conditions by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex ecological and operational interactions. Traditional forest management models often lack the resolution to integrate dynamic variables such as species-specific growth responses, climate-driven disturbance regimes, and spatially explicit harvesting impacts. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining remote sensing data, climate projections, and ecological process models to simulate forest growth, carbon dynamics, and harvesting outcomes across multiple spatial and temporal scales. The project will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze LiDAR and multispectral satellite data for real-time forest health monitoring, coupled with agent-based modeling to evaluate harvesting strategies under diverse climate scenarios. These computationally intensive workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale geospatial datasets and iterative simulations of 50-year forest trajectories across heterogeneous landscapes. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sensitivity analyses, uncertainty quantification through ensemble modeling, and high-resolution visualization of management trade-offs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to balance timber production with biodiversity conservation, identify climate-resilient species mixtures, and optimize harvest schedules to minimize soil erosion risks. By quantifying carbon sequestration potentials under alternative management regimes, this research will directly inform policy frameworks for sustainable forestry certification and climate adaptation planning. The computational pipelines developed will be modularly designed for transferability to other forest ecosystems, providing a scalable resource for academia and industry to align forest production goals with ecological preservation in a warming world.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of forestry principles to the production, harvesting, and processing of forest resources and that prepares individuals to perform associated technical and managerial functions. Includes instruction in forest production and utilization, industrial forestry, agroforestry, transplantation, timber harvesting, selection and identification of trees, processing technologies and systems, equipment operations and maintenance, and related management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in landscape management systems by developing predictive models to optimize plant health and resource use in dynamic environmental conditions. Traditional approaches to irrigation scheduling, turf maintenance, and pest management often rely on static guidelines, leading to water waste, nutrient imbalances, and increased operational costs. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating real-time sensor data, weather forecasts, and species-specific physiological thresholds to generate adaptive management strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-modal datasets—including soil moisture telemetry, hyperspectral plant stress imagery, and microclimate variables—at the scale required for actionable insights. Machine learning models will be trained to predict irrigation needs, disease risks, and growth patterns across heterogeneous landscapes, with validation against experimental plots at the university’s horticultural research station. Parallelized simulations will evaluate thousands of scenario combinations to identify resilient planting configurations under climate variability. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning for image-based plant phenotyping and CPU clusters for Monte Carlo analyses of resource allocation trade-offs. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that reduces water consumption by 15-25% in managed green spaces while maintaining aesthetic and functional standards. By quantifying interactions between plant genotypes, soil microbiomes, and maintenance practices, this work will advance precision horticulture methods applicable to urban parks, commercial landscapes, and recreational facilities. The requested HPC resources will enable the parameterization of species-specific response curves for 50+ ornamental plants, establishing a scalable framework to enhance sustainability in landscape management without compromising design integrity.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: The increasing complexity of building retrofitting demands computational tools capable of modeling dynamic interactions between structural integrity, energy efficiency, and occupant well-being in aging structures. Current approaches often treat these factors in isolation, neglecting synergistic effects that arise during adaptive reuse. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework integrating architectural geometry, material decay patterns, and real-time environmental data to optimize retrofit strategies for mid-20th century urban buildings. Leveraging GPU-accelerated finite element analysis and machine learning clustering algorithms, the proposed computational model will analyze terabyte-scale datasets encompassing 3D laser scans of building facades, decade-long urban microclimate records, and occupant behavior patterns. Key challenges include resolving time-dependent thermal bridging effects in non-uniform masonry assemblies and predicting acoustic transmission changes during spatial reconfiguration. The workflow employs hybrid computing techniques, coupling parametric building information modeling (BIM) with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to assess ventilation efficacy across multiple retrofit scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source digital twin platform that quantifies trade-offs between preservation priorities, energy savings, and indoor environmental quality metrics at unprecedented spatial-temporal resolutions. This resource will enable architects and preservationists to test intervention strategies against probabilistic climate models while maintaining historical fabric integrity. By addressing the computational bottleneck in whole-building performance analysis, the project aims to establish new benchmarks for data-driven decision-making in heritage-sensitive retrofits, directly supporting municipal carbon neutrality goals through culturally informed building reuse.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of advanced technology to building design and construction, retrofitting existing buildings, and efficient operation of buildings, including lighting and daylight design, acoustics, solar design, building conservation, and energy-conscious design. Includes instruction in architecture, building technology, civil and structural engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental control systems, sustainability, and computer tools and applications.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-border digital misinformation campaigns and their impact on diplomatic trust-building processes, leveraging computational social science methods within the interdisciplinary domain of International Relations and Affairs. While traditional studies focus on state-level policy or institutional responses, this research addresses a gap in understanding how algorithmically amplified misinformation disrupts non-state actors’ roles in Track II diplomacy—a critical yet understudied facet of modern conflict resolution. The core research problem examines how machine learning-driven content recommendation systems interact with grassroots diplomatic networks, potentially eroding the credibility of informal dialogue channels in post-conflict regions. To model these complex interactions, the project will employ large-scale agent-based simulations incorporating neural network architectures to represent adaptive misinformation actors, paired with graph-theoretic analyses of real-world diplomatic communication networks. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing multilingual social media corpora (spanning 10TB of historical data from conflict zones), running Monte Carlo simulations of trust dynamics under varying misinformation regimes, and training transformer-based models to detect emerging narrative manipulation patterns. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying diplomatic resilience to digital misinformation, predictive metrics for early warning systems in multilateral organizations, and open-source tools for simulating hybrid threats in informal diplomacy contexts. By bridging computational linguistics, network science, and diplomatic theory, this work aims to establish empirical foundations for safeguarding non-traditional peacebuilding mechanisms in an era of weaponized information ecosystems.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of international politics and institutions, and the conduct of diplomacy and foreign policy. Includes instruction in international relations theory, foreign policy analysis, international law and organization, the comparative study of specific countries and regions, and the theory and practice of diplomacy.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic workflow prioritization for frontline receptionist roles using high-performance computing (HPC) to model real-time decision-making under constraints. Receptionists in high-traffic environments (e.g., corporate offices, medical facilities, or emergency response centers) face complex, overlapping demands: managing call volumes, visitor interactions, scheduling conflicts, and ad-hoc information requests. Traditional queuing models fail to account for the multivariate, context-sensitive nature of these tasks, particularly when integrating emotional labor metrics (e.g., stress detection in vocal tone) or prioritizing stakeholders with competing urgencies. We propose developing a hybrid computational framework combining reinforcement learning (RL) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate receptionist workflows at scale. The RL component will train on synthetic datasets encompassing call logs, visitor patterns, and sentiment analysis from real-world receptionist interactions, while ABM agents will represent heterogeneous visitor/caller personas with stochastic behavioral profiles. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations across thousands of scenarios, enabling rapid iteration of prioritization policies under variable load conditions. Key outcomes include (1) a validated decision-support algorithm to minimize task dropout rates and visitor/caller dissatisfaction, (2) quantitative thresholds for workload redistribution to adjacent staff, and (3) sensitivity analyses identifying resilience thresholds in high-stakes environments. Results will advance resource allocation strategies for human-centric service roles, with potential applications in automated triage systems and ethical AI-assisted workflow tools. By focusing on an understudied yet operationally critical role, this work bridges computational social science and service operations management, offering novel insights into human-in-the-loop optimization for frontline business functions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform frontline public relations duties for a business, organization, or answering service. Includes instruction in telephone answering techniques, responding to information requests, keeping caller and/or visitor records, placing business calls, operating telephone switchboards and/or other communications equipment, relaying incoming and interoffice calls, schedule maintenance, and public relations skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in veterinary anesthesiology and pain management protocols, a critical yet understudied area in animal health technology. Current anesthetic dosing guidelines for companion and livestock species rely on generalized metrics, often leading to suboptimal outcomes due to interspecies variability, breed-specific metabolic differences, and individual patient factors. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating species-specific pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models with machine learning to predict optimal drug regimens. The research will utilize retrospective clinical datasets from veterinary hospitals (including vital signs, drug responses, and recovery metrics) alongside genomic and metabolomic profiles from public repositories. High-dimensional simulations will model drug distribution across tissue compartments under varying physiological conditions, while neural networks will identify predictors of adverse events. The computational workflow requires parallel processing to manage iterative parameter optimizations across millions of simulated patient scenarios. Expected outcomes include breed-specific anesthetic risk profiles, validated dosing algorithms for high-risk populations, and an open-access decision support tool for veterinary technicians. By reducing trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice, this work directly aligns with the program’s focus on improving patient management and clinical standards. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the project’s scale, as single-node processing would extend runtime to impractical durations (estimated 18+ months versus 3 weeks with parallelization). Results will be integrated into veterinary assistant training modules, enhancing educational outcomes in anesthesia delivery and perioperative care.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary/ Animal Health Technology and Veterinary Assistant
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of veterinarians, laboratory animal specialists, and zoological professionals, to provide patient management, care, and clinical procedures assistance as well as owner communication. Includes instruction in animal nursing care, animal health and nutrition, animal handling, clinical pathology, radiology, anesthesiology, dental prophylaxis, surgical assisting, clinical laboratory procedures, office administration skills, patient and owner management, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for real-time, AI-driven cinematographic rendering and adaptive scene synthesis to address the growing demand for high-fidelity, dynamic visual storytelling in film and interactive media. Current workflows in virtual production and computer-generated imagery (CGI) face limitations in processing photorealistic environments at scale, particularly when integrating machine learning models for automated lighting, camera path optimization, and physics-based simulations of natural phenomena. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize neural rendering pipelines, train generative adversarial networks (GANs) on multi-modal cinematographic datasets (including 4K/8K footage and LiDAR-captured environments), and simulate complex particle systems for atmospheric effects like fog, smoke, and dynamic water surfaces. By leveraging GPU-accelerated clusters, the team will prototype an adaptive rendering system that adjusts visual parameters in response to narrative cues and director inputs, reducing manual post-production labor. A secondary focus involves developing a distributed computing architecture for collaborative, cloud-based editing of high-bitrate video streams, enabling frame-accurate synchronization across geographically dispersed teams. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for AI-assisted cinematographic decision-making, benchmark datasets for virtual production research, and novel techniques for preserving artistic intent in computationally intensive workflows. This work directly advances the integration of emerging media technologies with traditional filmmaking practices, offering scalable solutions for independent creators and commercial studios alike while contributing new methodologies to computational visual arts research. The requested resources are critical for handling terabyte-scale visual assets and achieving sub-second latency in rendering iterations during experimental phases.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to communicate dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the making and producing of films and videos. Includes instruction in theory of film, film technology and equipment operation, film production, film directing, film editing, cinematographic art, film audio, techniques for making specific types of films and/or videos, media technologies, computer image making, multi-media production, and the planning and management of film/video operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the computational challenges of optimizing real-time, multi-channel digital marketing campaigns through large-scale consumer behavior simulation and adaptive machine learning (ML) models. Current approaches to cross-channel campaign optimization struggle to integrate real-time data streams from social media, e-commerce platforms, and web analytics into unified decision-making frameworks, particularly at the scale required for global enterprises. The research problem centers on the latency and scalability limitations of existing marketing decision systems when processing heterogeneous data streams (e.g., clickstreams, sentiment analysis, purchase histories) to dynamically adjust advertising bids, content personalization, and channel allocation. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation environment that models consumer decision pathways across 10+ digital channels while training deep reinforcement learning agents to optimize budget allocation and content strategies. The computational approach involves three phases: 1) Parallelized agent-based modeling of 100 million synthetic consumer profiles with psychographic and behavioral diversity, 2) Distributed training of transformer-based recommendation systems using GPU clusters to process real-time campaign performance data, and 3) Evolutionary optimization of channel mix parameters through massively parallel A/B testing simulations. The project requires HPC resources for both the synthetic data generation (leveraging probabilistic graphical models at scale) and the continuous retraining cycles of the ML architecture. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for latency-sensitive marketing resource allocation, quantitative benchmarks for computational efficiency in real-time campaign adjustments, and open-source tools for simulating cross-channel consumer journeys. This work aims to establish computational best practices for next-generation marketing systems that require sub-second decision cycles across petabyte-scale datasets, directly addressing the gap between traditional marketing analytics and emerging HPC capabilities in distributed systems optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop a digital marketing plan and integrate marketing, advertising, sales, and logistics across physical and digital channels. Includes instruction in digital marketing, e-commerce, online consumer psychology, search engine optimization, social media marketing, and web analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing water distribution and waste removal systems in residential and commercial plumbing networks. Current methodologies for designing and maintaining piping systems rely heavily on static codes and generalized empirical data, which often fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, pipe corrosion rates, or transient pressure waves in complex networks. The research problem centers on integrating real-time sensor data, fluid dynamics simulations, and machine learning to create adaptive models that improve system resilience, reduce water waste, and preemptively identify failure points. Computational workflows will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating stress distributions in pipe materials under varying thermal and mechanical loads, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model water flow efficiency and sediment accumulation, and graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on historical failure datasets to predict vulnerabilities in networked systems. These multi-scale simulations require HPC resources to process large spatial-temporal datasets, resolve fine-grained interactions in 3D pipe geometries, and iteratively optimize system designs under thousands of operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for plumbers and engineers to simulate system upgrades, validate code compliance computationally, and prioritize maintenance interventions. By bridging computational engineering with applied plumbing practices, this work aims to reduce infrastructure costs, extend system lifespans, and mitigate public health risks from leaks or contamination. The project will also generate training modules to integrate computational literacy into plumbing technology curricula, fostering a workforce capable of deploying data-driven solutions in the trades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice as licensed plumbers by applying technical knowledge and skills to lay out, assemble, install, and maintain piping fixtures and systems for steam, natural gas, oil, hot water, heating, cooling, drainage, lubricating, sprinkling, and industrial processing systems in home and business environments. Includes instruction in source determination, water distribution, waster removal, pressure adjustment, basic physics, technical mathematics, blueprint reading, pipe installation, pumps, welding and soldering, plumbing inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to advance technology teacher education by developing scalable computational models to simulate and optimize classroom-based technical systems, enhancing pedagogical strategies for industrial arts instruction. A critical challenge in technology education is the lack of accessible tools to model complex, real-world systems—such as automated manufacturing processes, robotics workflows, or sustainable design systems—in classroom settings. Existing simulation tools often lack the fidelity or interactivity needed to support hands-on learning, limiting educators’ ability to demonstrate dynamic system behaviors or assess student-designed solutions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build modular, physics-based simulations of industrial systems that mirror real-time operational constraints. These simulations will integrate parametric design inputs, material behavior models, and stochastic process variables (e.g., machine failure rates, energy consumption fluctuations) using finite element analysis and discrete-event simulation frameworks. By parallelizing computationally intensive tasks such as multi-objective optimization of student-proposed designs or Monte Carlo analyses of system reliability, HPC resources will enable rapid iteration and visualization of outcomes. The project will also develop machine learning models to classify common student misconceptions from simulation interaction data, informing adaptive feedback mechanisms for instructors. Outcomes will include an open-access repository of simulated industrial systems aligned with K-12 and postsecondary curricula, validated through partnerships with teacher training programs. This work will directly enhance the preparedness of technology educators to teach emerging industrial concepts, bridging the gap between theoretical instruction and practical, systems-level thinking. The computational infrastructure will also serve as a foundation for future research into AI-driven pedagogical tools for technical education, fostering innovation in a field critical to workforce development.
cip_title: Technology Teacher Education/ Industrial Arts Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach technology education/industrial arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational evolution of Italian cultural identity through a large-scale, interdisciplinary study of digitized archival materials. The central research problem addresses how regional and diasporic cultural production—spanning literature, periodicals, visual art, and correspondence from the 19th century to the present—has shaped competing narratives of "Italianness" beyond national borders. Traditional humanities methodologies struggle to systematically process the vast, multilingual corpora (over 500,000 digitized pages from libraries in Argentina, Australia, and Italy) required to map these dynamics. The project will implement computational text analysis, network modeling, and computer vision techniques to identify patterns in thematic content, stylistic evolution, and cross-regional cultural exchange. Custom NLP pipelines will be developed to handle historical Italian dialects and mixed-language texts, while graph-based models will reconstruct networks of influence among authors, artists, and publishers. Image recognition algorithms will classify visual motifs in digitized artworks and illustrations. These computationally intensive tasks demand parallel processing capabilities for training transformer models on heterogeneous data and conducting hyperparameter optimization at scale. Expected outcomes include: (1) a geotemporal visualization platform tracking the diffusion of cultural narratives across migration pathways; (2) quantitative evidence challenging centralized models of national identity formation; and (3) open-access tools for multilingual heritage analysis. The research will provide novel insights into how marginalized voices—particularly from southern Italy and emigrant communities—contributed to redefining cultural boundaries. By bridging digital humanities and Italian Studies, this work aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing cultural identity in transnational contexts while preserving endangered diasporic archives through computational curation.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of modern Italy and its predecessors on the Italian Peninsula, including the overseas migrations of Italian peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Polish linguistic and literary corpora, addressing critical gaps in the digital study of regional dialects and historical language evolution. While Polish philology has a rich tradition of qualitative research, large-scale quantitative analyses of dialectal variation and diachronic shifts remain underdeveloped due to the computational demands of processing heterogeneous, unstructured textual data spanning centuries. The research problem centers on mapping phonetic, morphological, and syntactic features across digitized manuscripts, regional speech archives, and contemporary sociolinguistic datasets to model language change and dialect boundaries with unprecedented granularity. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and dialectal Polish, including transformer-based models for morphosyntactic tagging, dialect classification algorithms, and geospatial visualization tools. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte text collections, training of domain-specific language models on non-standard varieties, and probabilistic simulations of linguistic divergence patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of Polish dialects, annotated corpora for understudied regional varieties, and machine learning frameworks adaptable to other Slavic languages. By bridging computational linguistics with traditional philological inquiry, this project will provide novel methodologies for preserving linguistic diversity, tracing cultural influences in literature, and informing language policy. The infrastructure developed will serve as a foundational resource for interdisciplinary studies in Polish linguistics, digital humanities, and heritage conservation, positioning HPC as a transformative tool for Slavic language research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate an adaptive simulation platform for training teacher assistants (TAs) in managing dynamic, inclusive classroom environments. TAs play a critical role in supporting diverse learners, including multilingual students and those with individualized education plans, yet existing training tools lack the capacity to simulate real-time, complex decision-making scenarios influenced by variables such as language barriers, behavioral cues, and differentiated instruction needs. The research problem centers on the gap between static, scripted training methods and the unpredictable, high-stakes demands of modern classrooms. To address this, the project will construct a computational model that integrates multimodal data—including speech, gaze, and gesture patterns from real classroom recordings—to generate responsive, AI-driven simulations. These simulations will emulate student-teacher-TA interactions under varying conditions, enabling TAs to practice pedagogical strategies in a risk-free virtual environment. Computational methods will involve large-scale natural language processing to model dialogue dynamics, reinforcement learning to adapt scenarios based on trainee decisions, and agent-based modeling to simulate student behaviors. The HPC infrastructure will be critical for processing terabytes of audiovisual training data, parallelizing thousands of simulation iterations, and optimizing deep learning architectures for real-time feedback. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source platform that quantifies TA competency development through metrics like intervention timeliness and cultural responsiveness. The project’s significance lies in its interdisciplinary fusion of educational psychology, computational linguistics, and machine learning to address an underserved area of para-educator preparation. By transforming TA training into a data-driven, immersive experience, this work aims to enhance equity in instructional support for historically marginalized student populations while establishing a framework for computational resource applications in non-traditional educational research domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist a teacher in regular classroom settings or in providing instruction and supervision to special student populations, such as bilingual/bicultural students, special education students, adult learners, and students learning English. Includes instruction in techniques of general classroom supervision, maintaining order, assisting with lessons and carrying out related assignments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of computational biology and systems pharmacology into Ayurvedic medicine research. A critical challenge in modernizing Ayurveda lies in systematically validating the therapeutic mechanisms of its complex herbal formulations, which often involve synergistic interactions among hundreds of bioactive compounds. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to address the combinatorial complexity of these polyherbal formulations, their multi-target effects on human physiology, and their alignment with Ayurvedic principles such as *dosha* balance and *agni* (metabolic) regulation. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning to model interactions between Ayurvedic phytochemicals and human protein targets implicated in conditions like metabolic syndrome, chronic inflammation, and neurodegenerative disorders. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale virtual screening of classical formulations documented in Sanskrit texts such as the *Charaka Samhita*, coupled with network pharmacology analyses to map formulation-specific effects onto Ayurvedic pathophysiology models. Concurrently, we will develop AI-driven pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models to predict herb-herb and herb-drug interactions, informed by traditional detoxification (*shodhana*) and preparation methods. This dual approach—grounded in both biomedical data and Ayurvedic theory—aims to establish predictive models for personalized *rasayana* (rejuvenation) therapies while preserving the holistic framework of the tradition. Expected outcomes include a curated database of Ayurvedic formulation-target interactions, computational validation of *prakriti* (constitution)-specific treatment responses, and optimized protocols for translating classical interventions into evidence-based practice. By applying advanced computational resources to decode Ayurveda’s empirical wisdom, this work will strengthen its scientific foundation, facilitate interdisciplinary dialogue, and support the development of integrative healthcare solutions validated through both traditional and modern paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Chemical reactions in complex environments, such as enzymatic systems or solvent networks, often involve dynamic interactions that challenge conventional experimental and theoretical approaches. This project seeks to elucidate the mechanisms of such reactions by integrating quantum mechanical (QM) and molecular mechanical (MM) simulations with enhanced sampling techniques. A key focus is on understanding how solvation effects and protein environments modulate reaction pathways, transition states, and catalytic efficiency in systems relevant to sustainable chemistry and drug discovery. Current limitations in modeling these systems arise from the need for high-accuracy electronic structure calculations across large spatial and temporal scales, which demand substantial computational resources. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining hybrid QM/MM methods, machine learning-accelerated free energy sampling, and large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable ab initio MD simulations of reactive trajectories, coupled with adaptive sampling to explore rare events, while machine learning potentials will reduce the cost of free energy calculations. The project will apply this approach to two systems: (1) the solvent-dependent kinetics of organocatalytic C–H activation reactions and (2) the role of non-covalent interactions in enzyme-catalyzed halogenation. Outcomes will include validated mechanistic models, open-source tools for reaction path optimization, and quantitative insights into environmental effects on reactivity. This work will advance predictive capabilities in computational chemistry, with direct implications for catalyst design, synthetic biology, and green chemistry initiatives. The requested HPC allocation is critical to managing the >1 million CPU-hour demand for ensemble simulations and data-intensive analysis workflows.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemistry, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic resource allocation for distributed computing systems, a critical challenge in modern computing environments where heterogeneous workloads and fluctuating demands strain traditional static allocation models. Current approaches often lack the responsiveness needed to optimize hardware utilization, leading to energy waste, latency spikes, and underprovisioning risks in applications ranging from cloud services to edge computing networks. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an adaptive resource management framework that integrates real-time telemetry data with predictive machine learning models. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale distributed systems under diverse workload scenarios, training neural networks to forecast resource needs while accounting for hardware constraints and energy efficiency targets. Computational experiments will evaluate allocation strategies across simulated data center architectures and IoT-edge configurations, measuring metrics including task completion times, energy consumption, and fault tolerance. By iteratively refining models through GPU-accelerated training and validation cycles, the project aims to produce allocation algorithms capable of reducing resource overprovisioning by ≥30% in benchmark tests while maintaining service-level agreements. Outcomes will include open-source optimization tools compatible with container orchestration platforms and a reference architecture for intelligent resource scheduling. This work directly supports the Engineering Technologies field by advancing practical methodologies for maintaining complex computer systems, with applications in industrial automation, smart infrastructure, and scalable computing education platforms. Successful implementation could lower operational costs for computing infrastructure providers while improving the sustainability of large-scale deployments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of professionals who use computer systems. Includes instruction in basic computer design and architecture, programming, problems of specific computer applications, component and system maintenance and inspection procedures, hardware and software problem diagnosis and repair, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the resilience of small business ecosystems under dynamic economic shocks, such as supply chain disruptions, regional crises, or rapid market shifts. While small businesses are critical to economic stability, their capacity to adapt to volatile conditions remains poorly understood due to the complex interdependencies between localized markets, resource availability, and digital infrastructure. Traditional analytical methods lack the granularity and scalability to simulate real-time decision-making across heterogeneous small business networks. This project addresses this gap by developing an agent-based computational framework to simulate thousands of small business entities interacting within a multi-layered economic environment. Each agent will incorporate decision-making algorithms informed by real-world data on cash flow constraints, supplier relationships, customer behavior, and e-commerce adoption. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations to test how varying levels of access to capital, digital tools, or policy interventions (e.g., emergency grants, tax relief) impact system-wide recovery rates. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to identify critical leverage points for enhancing adaptive capacity. Outcomes will include predictive models to forecast small business vulnerability under different crisis scenarios, as well as optimization strategies for resource allocation at regional and sectoral levels. By integrating computational social science with business operations research, this work aims to provide actionable insights for policymakers, nonprofit organizations, and small business owners to prioritize investments in technologies, training, and safety nets. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to process high-resolution datasets (e.g., transaction records, geospatial logistics) and execute millions of stochastic simulations to capture nonlinear system behaviors. Results will advance interdisciplinary methodologies for small business resilience planning while directly supporting evidence-based strategies to mitigate economic fragility in underserved communities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage independent small businesses. Includes instruction in business administration; enterprise planning and entrepreneurship; start-up; small business operations and problems; personnel supervision; capitalization and investment; taxation; business law and regulations; e-commerce; home business operations; and applications to specific sectors, products, and services.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the electronic structure and reactivity of high-valent transition metal complexes, which are central to catalysis and energy conversion processes but remain poorly characterized due to their dynamic bonding and open-shell configurations. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve transient intermediates and subtle electronic interactions in these systems, necessitating advanced computational modeling. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multiscale quantum mechanical simulations, including density functional theory (DFT), multireference complete active space (CASSCF), and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), to map the reaction pathways and electronic landscapes of iron(IV)-oxo and manganese(V)-nitrido complexes. These systems are pivotal in C–H activation and nitrogen transfer reactions but exhibit unpredictable selectivity due to spin-state crossovers and ligand-field effects. The computational workflow will integrate explicit solvation models and periodic boundary conditions to mimic experimental environments, while machine learning force fields will extend sampling timescales for rare event dynamics. Key objectives include identifying ligand architectures that stabilize high-spin states, quantifying orbital hybridization effects on bond activation barriers, and validating predictions through collaboration with experimental groups using X-ray absorption spectroscopy and magnetometry. The outcomes will establish design principles for tunable, earth-abundant catalysts with applications in sustainable synthesis and energy storage. By leveraging HPC capabilities to overcome the prohibitive cost of correlated-electron methods for large inorganic clusters, this work will advance predictive modeling in inorganic chemistry, enabling rational targeting of functional materials beyond trial-and-error approaches. The requested computing resources are essential to manage the >10,000 core-hour/month demand for stochastic sampling and wavefunction-based accuracy in systems exceeding 200 atoms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the elements and their compounds, other than the hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Includes instruction in the characterization and synthesis of non-carbon molecules, including their structure and their bonding, conductivity, and reactive properties; research techniques such as spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and photoelectron analysis; and the study of specific compounds, such as transition metals, and compounds composed of inorganic and organic molecules.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of symbolic communication systems in understudied pre-modern visual cultures, focusing on non-textual iconographic traditions from Indigenous communities in the Pacific Northwest and Mesoamerica. While these systems represent sophisticated modes of cultural knowledge transmission, their structural complexity and spatial-temporal variation remain poorly understood due to the absence of deciphered textual records and the scale of multimodal data involved. The research employs a computational humanities framework to analyze over 15,000 digitized artifacts (petroglyphs, textiles, and ceremonial objects) using deep learning architectures optimized for pattern recognition in irregular, fragmented visual datasets. Key challenges include developing transfer learning models that account for material degradation patterns and cultural hybridity in iconographic repertoires, requiring iterative training on GPU clusters. A three-phase approach combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for motif identification, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map symbolic relationships, and agent-based modeling to simulate cultural transmission dynamics across ecological boundaries. The computational pipeline will integrate archaeological metadata, ethnographic records, and environmental data to contextualize symbolic evolution within socioecological systems. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for analyzing non-linear symbolic systems outside alphabetic traditions, 2) evidence-based reconstructions of cultural exchange networks challenging colonial-era ethnographic assumptions, and 3) open-source tools for Indigenous communities to computationally document endangered heritage. By bridging cognitive anthropology, visual semiotics, and machine learning, this work advances methodological innovation in studying non-Western knowledge systems while addressing ethical computational practices in collaborative heritage research. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution 3D artifact models and training multi-modal networks with parameters exceeding 500 million dimensions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on combined studies and research in the humanities subjects as distinguished from the social and physical sciences, emphasizing languages, literatures, art, music, philosophy and religion.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized motor learning interventions for individuals with neurological impairments, such as stroke or traumatic brain injury. Occupational therapist assistants (OTAs) play a critical role in implementing rehabilitation strategies, yet current protocols often rely on generalized approaches that do not account for the dynamic, individual-specific nature of sensorimotor recovery. The research problem centers on optimizing task-specific training regimens by modeling the interaction between neural plasticity, biomechanical constraints, and environmental feedback in real time. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating wearable sensor data, biophysical simulations, and reinforcement learning algorithms. Wearable devices will capture high-resolution kinematic and physiological data during therapeutic activities, which will be processed using GPU-accelerated pipelines to extract movement variability, muscle activation patterns, and fatigue metrics. These datasets will train a multiscale neural network model that simulates corticospinal adaptation processes, enabling the prediction of optimal task difficulty, feedback timing, and assistive device configurations for individual patients. The HPC environment is essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of the model, which includes over 10^6 variables representing neural, musculoskeletal, and environmental factors. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool that OTAs can use to dynamically adjust interventions during sessions, reducing trial-and-error decision-making. By bridging computational neuroscience with rehabilitation practice, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for precision neuromotor rehabilitation, potentially decreasing recovery times by 15-20% in pilot cohorts. The resulting open-source framework will also provide a foundation for future research at the intersection of AI-driven biomechanics and occupational therapy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: Postoperative complications remain a critical challenge in surgical care, contributing to increased morbidity, extended hospital stays, and elevated healthcare costs. While existing risk assessment tools aid perioperative nurses in identifying high-risk patients, these tools often lack the granularity to account for dynamic, multifactorial interactions between patient-specific variables, surgical procedures, and real-time physiological data. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution predictive model leveraging machine learning (ML) and high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze heterogeneous perioperative datasets. The research will integrate structured electronic health records (EHRs), intraoperative vital sign streams, and nursing documentation from surgical cases to train ensemble ML algorithms capable of predicting complications such as surgical site infections, sepsis, and hemodynamic instability. Computational workflows will utilize distributed computing frameworks to manage data at scale, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and attention mechanisms will model temporal patterns in physiological trends. Bayesian optimization will refine hyperparameters across HPC nodes to maximize predictive accuracy. The anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated risk stratification tool operable in real-time clinical workflows, enabling perioperative nurses to prioritize interventions for at-risk patients, and (2) novel insights into modifiable risk factors within nursing control, such as preoperative preparation protocols or intraoperative monitoring strategies. By harnessing HPC resources, this project aims to advance precision in perioperative nursing practice, directly aligning with national priorities to improve surgical outcomes through data-driven innovation. Resource requests include GPU nodes for model training, high-memory nodes for large dataset manipulation, and scalable storage for multi-institutional data harmonization.
cip_title: Perioperative/ Operating Room and Surgical Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care to patients before and during surgery, and provide tableside assistance to surgeons. Includes instruction in operating room safety and preparation, aseptic technique, anesthesia, patient preparation, surgical instruments and procedures, sterilization and disinfecting, surgical drugs and solutions, hemostasis, emergency procedures, and patient/family education.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the dynamic stability of hybrid power plants integrating intermittent renewable energy sources with traditional thermal generation systems. As power grids increasingly incorporate distributed solar, wind, and battery storage, the transient interactions between fast-responding inverters and slow-responding thermal components create complex stability challenges. Conventional simulation tools struggle to model these multi-timescale phenomena accurately, particularly during fault conditions or rapid load changes. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled electro-thermal-mechanical model that simultaneously resolves sub-millisecond power electronics switching, minute-scale thermal inertia in steam turbines, and hour-scale fuel supply dynamics. Parallelized finite element solvers will be integrated with network-level transient stability analysis using adaptive time-stepping algorithms to capture cross-domain interactions. Machine learning techniques will train surrogate models on HPC-generated datasets to predict instability thresholds under varying renewable penetration levels. The computational workflow will leverage GPU acceleration for real-time contingency analysis and optimal protection coordination across heterogeneous generation assets. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation platform capable of identifying stability bottlenecks in existing hybrid plants and providing design guidelines for future systems with 50-100% renewable capacity. This work addresses a critical gap in power plant engineering by enabling predictive control of electromechanical transients in decarbonized grids, directly supporting utility-scale transitions to low-carbon energy. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling the framework to realistically sized networks with 10,000+ bus systems and stochastic renewable profiles, which exceed the capabilities of commercial software tools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan electrical systems and modify existing electrical systems that generate and use large amounts of electricity required for distribution networks that are economical, safe, and functional. Includes instruction in alternative/renewable energy systems; calculus; circuit analysis; electrical power systems and industry practices; electrical system design; microprocessor architecture; motor control systems; power electronics operation, planning and protection; programmable logic controllers; and project management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern spatial and temporal datasets presents significant computational challenges for Bayesian hierarchical modeling, a cornerstone of uncertainty quantification in statistics. While these models provide flexible frameworks for capturing dependencies in data—such as environmental monitoring networks or epidemiological case counts—their estimation via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods becomes intractable at scale. This project seeks to develop and validate scalable algorithms for high-dimensional Bayesian spatiotemporal models, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome existing bottlenecks. The research problem centers on two key limitations: (1) the prohibitive runtime of traditional MCMC samplers when applied to datasets with millions of spatially referenced observations, and (2) the inability of existing approximation methods to maintain calibration across multi-scale hierarchical structures. Our computational approach combines parallelized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) implementations with structured variational inference techniques, exploiting GPU acceleration for gradient calculations and distributed memory architectures for parameter subspace decomposition. We will extend these methods to handle non-Gaussian response variables and anisotropic covariance structures, testing robustness through synthetic experiments mirroring real-world environmental and public health monitoring scenarios. The proposed HPC workflows will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art alternatives using metrics of predictive accuracy, parameter recovery, and wall-clock time. Successful implementation is expected to yield a 10-50x speedup for models with >10⁶ observations while maintaining posterior fidelity, as measured by Wasserstein distances between full and approximate posterior samples. Outcomes will directly enable novel analyses of continental-scale air quality datasets and infectious disease transmission networks, while the open-source software tools developed will provide the statistical community with scalable infrastructure for next-generation spatiotemporal modeling. This work bridges critical gaps between statistical methodology and computational feasibility, advancing reproducible research in domains where both uncertainty quantification and large-scale data integration are imperative.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of generative design and adaptive urban microclimate modeling within architectural practice. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of current computational tools in addressing dynamic interactions between architectural form, localized environmental conditions, and human behavioral patterns at neighborhood scales. While existing software platforms excel in static building performance analysis, they lack the capacity to simulate real-time feedback loops between evolving microclimates—such as heat island effects or wind patterns—and occupant-driven spatial adaptations. This gap limits architects' ability to design resilient, context-responsive urban interventions amid climate volatility. The proposed computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) for occupant behavior simulation, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for microclimate analysis, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to optimize generative design iterations. By parallelizing these typically sequential workflows through distributed computing architectures, the project aims to develop a framework capable of processing high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets (LiDAR, IoT sensor arrays, and pedestrian movement tracking) while maintaining sub-hourly simulation cycles for multi-year climate projections. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational pipeline that enables architects to test design hypotheses against coupled environmental-behavioral scenarios, significantly reducing the latency between design iteration and performance validation. The research will validate the framework through three case studies of transit-oriented urban developments in climatically distinct regions, generating comparative datasets on energy use intensity, thermal comfort variance, and spatial adaptation rates. This work bridges architectural design, urban climatology, and machine learning, offering a novel computational methodology for addressing climate resilience challenges through spatially embedded, data-driven design strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of architecture and to conduct research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in architectural design, history, and theory; building structures and environmental systems; project and site planning; construction; professional responsibilities and standards; and related cultural, social, economic, and environmental issues.

abstract: Histologic analysis is foundational to diagnosing diseases, yet manual evaluation of complex tissue architectures remains time-intensive and subject to interpretive variability. Emerging computational approaches offer transformative potential but require scalable infrastructure to process high-resolution histologic datasets. This project proposes the development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven platform to automate the detection and quantification of subtle pathologic features in multi-layered, whole-slide histology images. The research focuses on integrating weakly supervised deep learning models with advanced image segmentation techniques to identify spatial patterns indicative of early-stage fibrotic remodeling in renal biopsies—a process critical to understanding progressive kidney disease but notoriously challenging to standardize. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational load of training models on terabyte-scale datasets comprising thousands of annotated and unannotated digitized slides, each exceeding 100,000 × 100,000 pixels. Parallelized processing will enable rapid feature extraction, while graph-based neural networks will map cellular interactions within tissue microenvironments. The project further aims to establish a scalable pipeline for correlating histomorphometric data with multiplexed immunohistochemistry results, requiring iterative alignment of multimodal datasets. Successful implementation will yield an open-source framework for quantifying fibrosis progression with subcellular resolution, reducing diagnostic subjectivity, and accelerating translational research in nephropathology. By enabling large-scale analysis of spatial biomarkers, this work addresses a critical gap in precision histopathology, with direct implications for clinical trial design and personalized therapeutic strategies. The computational tools developed will be adaptable to other tissue types and disease contexts, positioning HPC as a cornerstone of next-generation histotechnologic innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, at the request of physicians, researchers, and laboratory scientists, to identify tissue structures and cell components and relate these findings to physiological functions and to the detection and diagnosis of diseases and other abnormalities. Includes instruction in medical chemistry, histochemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, medical informatics, applied mathematics, electron microscopy, instrumentation, quality control procedures, data recording and analysis, laboratory administration, medical terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The development of advanced chemical processes for sustainable energy and materials production requires high-fidelity computational models to address multi-scale, dynamic interactions inherent in catalytic systems, multiphase reactors, and membrane-based separations. Current challenges include accurately resolving atomic-level reaction mechanisms, predicting fluid dynamics in turbulent reactor environments, and optimizing process parameters under transient conditions—tasks that demand significant computational resources. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) allocations to enable large-scale simulations integrating molecular dynamics (MD), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) frameworks. The research focuses on two interconnected thrusts: (1) modeling catalytic surface reactions in novel metal-organic framework (MOF) materials for carbon capture and conversion, and (2) optimizing multiphase flow and heat transfer in intensified reactor designs for electrochemical ammonia synthesis. MD simulations will elucidate reaction pathways and adsorption energetics at the quantum-mechanical level, while GPU-accelerated CFD simulations will resolve micron-scale bubble dynamics and species transport in three-dimensional reactor geometries. A surrogate ML model, trained on simulation data, will accelerate parameter optimization and uncertainty quantification. The computational workflow leverages hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization in LAMMPS and OpenFOAM, coupled with PyTorch-based neural networks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for MOF-catalyzed CO₂ hydrogenation kinetics, design guidelines for scalable electrochemical reactors, and open-source tools for reactive flow simulation. These advances will directly inform experimental efforts to develop energy-efficient chemical processes, with potential applications in decarbonized fuel production and distributed chemical manufacturing. The requested resources are critical for handling simulations exceeding 10⁶ CPU-core hours, including 500,000-atom MD systems and reactor meshes with >100 million cells, which are computationally intractable on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems employing chemical processes, such as chemical reactors, kinetic systems, electrochemical systems, energy conservation processes, heat and mass transfer systems, and separation processes; and the applied analysis of chemical problems such as corrosion, particle abrasion, energy loss, pollution, and fluid mechanics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational legal analysis of intertribal dispute resolution mechanisms, focusing on the intersection of traditional Indigenous governance systems and contemporary tribal court jurisprudence. While federal Indian law frameworks are well-documented, the procedural and substantive nuances of intertribal conflicts—particularly those involving overlapping territorial claims, cultural resource management, and cross-jurisdictional enforcement—remain understudied due to the complexity of parsing decentralized, non-uniform legal narratives. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based network analysis to map historical and modern dispute resolution patterns across 1,200+ tribal legal documents, oral history transcripts, and intergovernmental agreements. Computational challenges include processing unstructured, multilingual texts (including Indigenous languages in transliterated formats), identifying latent legal principles in non-Western jurisprudential traditions, and modeling the evolution of intertribal norms under shifting federal policies. By training transformer models on a curated corpus of tribal court opinions and ethnographic records, the project aims to identify scalable frameworks for predicting conflict resolution outcomes while preserving context-specific cultural logics. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated intertribal legal data, a computational toolkit for analyzing Indigenous law’s adaptive responses to colonialism, and policy recommendations for enhancing tribal judicial capacity. This work fills a critical gap in legal informatics by centering Indigenous epistemologies in computational analysis, offering methodological innovations for studying non-state legal systems while supporting tribal sovereignty through evidence-based resource allocation. The HPC environment is essential for handling large-scale parallel processing of heterogeneous data and optimizing machine learning architectures for low-resource language contexts.
