Includes instruction in health systems planning, public health organization and management, pubic health policy formulation and analysis, finance, business and operations management, economics of health care, organizational and health communications, marketing, human resources management, and public health law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges of modeling dynamic, multi-omics interactions within host-microbiome ecosystems to predict personalized therapeutic responses in chronic inflammatory diseases. While advances in multi-omics technologies have generated vast datasets linking microbial communities to conditions like inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), existing analytical frameworks struggle to integrate temporal, spatially resolved genomic, metabolomic, and proteomic data with host immune profiles. This limitation hinders the development of precision interventions targeting microbiome-host crosstalk. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled pipeline combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with agent-based modeling to simulate microbiome-immune system interactions across scales. Longitudinal multi-omics data from IBD patient cohorts will be structured as heterogeneous knowledge graphs, capturing microbial taxa, metabolite fluxes, and cytokine signaling networks. GNNs will train on these graphs to identify predictive interaction patterns, while parallelized agent-based simulations model real-time microbial community dynamics under simulated therapeutic perturbations. The computational workflow requires large-scale memory optimization for graph processing (≥1TB RAM/node) and GPU-accelerated training of attention-based GNN architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel framework for identifying microbiome-derived biomarkers of treatment response, (2) predictive models of host-microbial feedback loops in inflammation, and (3) open-source tools enabling time-resolved analysis of multi-omics ecosystems. By leveraging HPC resources to overcome current bottlenecks in data integration and mechanistic simulation, this work aims to advance computational methodologies in microbiome therapeutics while providing clinically actionable insights for managing complex chronic diseases. The project bridges biomedical informatics, systems biology, and computational immunology, demonstrating how advanced computing can unlock mechanistic insights from high-dimensional biological data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to health and/or biomedical research,  and the development of advanced database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in biomedical and/or health sciences; information science and technology; social and behavioral sciences; biomedical/health information science and technology; human factors and socio-technical systems;  applied social, behavioral, and information science and technology; and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of quantum many-body dynamics in ultracold molecular systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research addresses a critical challenge in atomic and molecular physics: accurately modeling the non-equilibrium behavior of interacting polar molecules in optical lattices under time-varying electromagnetic fields. Such systems exhibit complex entanglement, long-range dipole-dipole interactions, and competing quantum phases, but existing theoretical frameworks struggle to capture these phenomena at experimentally relevant scales due to prohibitive computational costs. We propose to implement a hybrid computational approach combining tensor network methods with adaptive basis set techniques to simulate the real-time evolution of molecular ensembles. The methodology will leverage massively parallel algorithms to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for systems of 50-100 molecules, explicitly accounting for rotational-vibrational coupling and anisotropic interactions. Key innovations include the development of dynamically compressed matrix product operators to mitigate memory bottlenecks and GPU-accelerated diagonalization routines for handling non-adiabatic transitions. These simulations will provide first-principles predictions of correlation propagation timescales, metastable phase boundaries, and collective excitation spectra—quantities directly testable in current ultracold molecule experiments. Successful completion will establish new benchmarks for quantum dynamics in strongly correlated molecular arrays, with potential impacts on the design of molecular quantum simulators and precision measurement devices. The requested HPC resources are essential due to the exponential scaling of Hilbert space dimensions with molecular count, requiring petascale capabilities for storage (>1 PB projected) and computation (>2 million core-hours). Results will be disseminated through open-source code releases and collaborations with experimental groups working on quantum-controlled molecular platforms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior of matter-energy phenomena at the level of atoms and molecules. Includes instruction in chemical physics, atomic forces and structure, molecular orbital theory, magnetic resonance, molecular bonding, phase equilibria, quantum theory of solids, and applications to the study of specific elements and higher compounds.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance and novel zoonotic pathogens in veterinary populations presents critical challenges to animal health and food security. Traditional experimental approaches to characterize pathogen-host interactions and evaluate therapeutic strategies are often limited in scalability and temporal resolution, particularly for complex microbial communities or rapidly evolving viruses. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps through multiscale computational modeling of microbial pathogenesis and host immune responses in agriculturally significant species. Specifically, we aim to (1) simulate molecular dynamics of viral envelope proteins from highly pathogenic avian influenza strains to predict antigenic evolution and vaccine escape variants, (2) model population-level genomic interactions between bovine mastitis-associated bacterial biofilms and host epithelial cells under varying antibiotic exposure regimes, and (3) employ machine learning to analyze metagenomic datasets from clinical veterinary samples for early detection of emerging antimicrobial resistance patterns. These objectives require intensive parallelized computing for molecular dynamics simulations (using AMBER and GROMACS), agent-based modeling of microbial communities, and training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous genomic data. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale genomic datasets, microsecond-scale trajectory sampling for protein conformational analyses, and high-throughput virtual screening of antimicrobial compounds. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for pathogen evolution under selective pressures, identification of conserved therapeutic targets across bacterial strains, and optimized treatment protocols informed by mechanistic models of host-microbe dynamics. By integrating computational immunology with clinical veterinary data, this work will directly inform vaccine development strategies, antimicrobial stewardship programs, and rapid diagnostic tools for livestock diseases with zoonotic potential. The resulting models and datasets will be made available through open-access portals to support broader One Health initiatives addressing microbial threats at the animal-human-environment interface.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of intercultural communication and conflict resolution in digitally mediated environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, large-scale social interactions. As globalization and digital platforms intensify cross-cultural exchanges, existing frameworks for understanding diversity-related tensions remain limited by static, small-scale analyses. The proposed work addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate emergent behaviors in heterogeneous populations, incorporating variables such as linguistic nuance, cultural norms, and power asymmetries. These models will integrate qualitative data from ethnographic studies and historical conflict databases with real-time social media interactions, processed via natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource languages and dialectal variations. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about how adaptive algorithms—simulating interventions like moderated dialogue or equity-focused policy adjustments—affect the evolution of group cohesion or polarization. By parallelizing thousands of parameter combinations across HPC clusters, the project will identify scalable strategies for mitigating intercultural friction in contexts ranging from online education platforms to multinational workforce management. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for simulating diversity-aware policy impacts and a publicly accessible dataset linking computational social dynamics to empirically observed intercultural outcomes. This work bridges computational scalability with sociocultural specificity, offering novel methodologies to advance both diversity studies and resource-efficient HPC applications in understudied linguistic and cultural contexts. The results aim to inform policymakers and organizational leaders operating in multicultural environments while establishing a framework for ethical, computationally rigorous approaches to studying diversity in evolving digital ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical need for culturally responsive educational resources in Native American communities by developing adaptive teaching tools that integrate Indigenous knowledge systems and learning styles. Current digital educational platforms often fail to incorporate the cultural contexts and linguistic diversity of Tribal/First Nation students, contributing to disparities in academic engagement and outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this research will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze multimodal datasets—including oral histories, language corpora, and student interaction patterns—to identify pedagogical strategies aligned with community-specific values. Computational models will simulate the effectiveness of culturally grounded lesson plans across diverse learning environments, optimizing content delivery while preserving regional traditions. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to support the integration of endangered Indigenous languages into bilingual curricula, addressing the scarcity of resources for low-resource languages. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter tuning for these models and facilitate the creation of an open-access repository of customizable educational modules. Anticipated outcomes include a framework for dynamically adapting instructional materials to local cultural contexts, tools for teachers to incorporate Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) into STEM subjects, and enhanced support for language revitalization efforts. By centering Indigenous epistemologies in computational pedagogy, this project aims to empower Tribal educators with scalable, community-informed resources that bridge technological innovation with cultural sustainability, ultimately fostering equitable academic success for Native learners.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of instructional and advising services for American Indian, Alaska Native, and Hawaiian Native students at various learning levels and that prepares individuals to perform teaching and administrative functions in Tribal/First Nation schools. Includes instruction in the cultural traditions and social patterns, history and politics, learning styles and issues, curriculum design, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling techniques and social issues, rural education services, distance education, adult education techniques, school administration, applicable laws and regulations, and research issues.

abstract: Sleep disorders present complex challenges in diagnosis and management, often requiring the integration of multimodal physiological data. Traditional polysomnographic analysis relies on manual scoring of sleep stages and events, a process limited by subjectivity, time-intensive protocols, and an inability to capture dynamic interactions between neurophysiological signals, cardiorespiratory patterns, and environmental factors. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model sleep architecture and disorder phenotypes using large-scale polysomnography datasets. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process and analyze terabytes of multichannel recordings (EEG, EMG, EOG, respiratory effort, SpO2) from 5,000+ clinical sleep studies, integrating concurrent actigraphy, environmental sensor data, and electronic health records. Machine learning pipelines will be optimized to identify latent patterns in sleep-wake transitions, autonomic instability during REM sleep, and microstructural biomarkers of neurodegenerative comorbidity. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model upper airway collapse mechanisms in obstructive sleep apnea, correlating real-time pressure gradients with anatomical imaging data. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of signal decomposition tasks, GPU-accelerated training of transformer-based models for event detection, and large-scale validation of predictive algorithms across heterogeneous patient subgroups. Expected outcomes include (1) automated tools for quantifying sleep continuity disturbances with sub-second precision, (2) novel metrics linking sleep microstructure to cognitive decline trajectories, and (3) personalized airflow collapse risk profiles derived from biomechanical simulations. By advancing computational methods in polysomnography, this work aims to establish scalable infrastructure for precision sleep medicine, reducing diagnostic latency for rare parasomnias and improving prognostic accuracy in complex cases where sleep pathology intersects with neurological, metabolic, and cardiovascular disease states.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of spiritual communication and community formation in digital ministry contexts, with a focus on how lay ministers adapt traditional pastoral practices to virtual environments. The proliferation of online worship spaces, hybrid congregations, and algorithmically mediated spiritual content demands new frameworks for understanding efficacy in lay-led ministry. While existing studies in practical theology address in-person pastoral care, there is a critical gap in analyzing large-scale behavioral and linguistic data from digital platforms to assess engagement, emotional resonance, and ethical challenges unique to decentralized spiritual leadership. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to analyze multimodal datasets comprising sermon transcripts, video content from virtual worship services, and asynchronous spiritual counseling interactions across three major platforms. High-performance computing resources are required to process over 250TB of audiovisual data, train transformer-based models for sentiment analysis specific to theological discourse, and simulate network models of community vulnerability/resilience across digitally fragmented congregations. Computational outcomes will be triangulated with qualitative interviews from 120 lay ministers to develop evidence-based best practices for algorithmic transparency, crisis response protocols in digital spaces, and culturally adaptive communication strategies. Expected contributions include the first open-source toolkit for ethical analytics in digital ministry and a typology of emergent leadership patterns in algorithmically shaped spiritual communities. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational social science, media studies, and practical theology while maintaining its core humanistic focus on preserving intentionality and relational depth in technologically mediated spiritual care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained individuals to serve as lay pastors, religious educators, youth leaders, and other professional positions open to the laity in local churches and other settings. Includes instruction in bible studies, theology, spirituality, pastoral counseling, foundations of ministry, effective communication, and church leadership.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of keyboard performance practice through computational analysis of historical and contemporary演奏 techniques. The primary challenge lies in systematically modeling the relationship between biomechanical input (e.g., touch, pedal use, articulation) and acoustic output across diverse keyboard instruments, accounting for variables such as instrument physics, performer physiology, and stylistic traditions. Current pedagogical frameworks often rely on subjective assessments of technique, limiting the scalability of personalized instruction and the preservation of ephemeral performance practices. To address this gap, we propose developing a multimodal computational pipeline integrating motion capture data from演奏ers, high-resolution audio analysis, and finite element modeling of instrument responses. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabytes of performance recordings from archival collections, real-time fluid dynamics simulations of pipe organ wind systems, and machine learning models that correlate tactile gestures with timbral outcomes across historical fortepianos, modern grands, and digital keyboards. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database quantifying technical approaches to canonical repertoire, 2) AI-driven feedback tools for remote pedagogy that adapt to individual students' biomechanical profiles, and 3) physics-based synthesis engines capable of recreating historical performance conditions for scholarly study. By bridging computational musicology with performance practice, this work aims to establish quantitative frameworks for preserving interpretative traditions while expanding access to advanced keyboard training. The requested resources are essential for handling the project's spatial audio processing demands, training neural networks on heterogeneous performance data, and running iterative simulations of complex mechanical systems inherent to keyboard instruments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the piano, organ, or related keyboard instruments and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in piano and keyboard pedagogy, ensemble playing, accompanying, service playing, repertoire, keyboard and pedal skills, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and optimize the integration of live musical theatre performance elements—vocal delivery, choreography, and technical staging—using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While musical theatre relies on the real-time synchronization of diverse artistic and technical components, existing methods for evaluating performance cohesion remain largely subjective or constrained by small-scale empirical studies. This research addresses the challenge of modeling complex interactions between performers, audience perception, and technical systems (e.g., acoustics, lighting) in dynamic, large-venue environments. The computational approach combines biomechanical motion capture data, real-time vocal acoustics analysis, and audience sightline simulations to quantify performance coherence. Machine learning models will be trained on multimodal datasets—including historical performance recordings, sensor data from wearable devices on actors, and environmental variables from stage machinery—to identify patterns in successful artistic integration. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of audiovisual data, running parallelized simulations of audience experience across seating configurations, and optimizing reinforcement learning algorithms for adaptive technical cueing systems. Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide rehearsal prioritization, a digital twin framework for pre-visualizing staging choices, and evidence-based recommendations for balancing artistic expression with technical feasibility. By establishing quantitative metrics for traditionally qualitative aspects of musical theatre, this work aims to advance pedagogical tools for training performers and technicians while enhancing the scalability of productions across diverse venues. The computational pipeline developed here will be shared as an open-source toolkit, fostering collaboration between performing arts practitioners and computational researchers.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for integrating theatre, music, and dance into a unified production. Includes instruction in acting, dance, voice, technical theater, musical genres, piano, and history of musical theater.

abstract: Critical infrastructure systems—spanning energy grids, transportation networks, and communication systems—are increasingly interdependent, creating vulnerabilities to cascading failures from cyber-physical threats. Current risk assessment models often lack the computational granularity to capture dynamic interdependencies between infrastructure sectors or simulate multi-vector attacks, limiting proactive mitigation strategies. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-fidelity, multi-layered simulation framework to model cascading failures across critical infrastructure networks under diverse threat scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate agent-based modeling, network theory, and machine learning to simulate infrastructure interdependencies, adversarial attack patterns, and system-wide resilience. The computational approach will involve large-scale graph analytics to map sector-specific dependencies, stochastic simulations to evaluate failure propagation under cyber intrusions or physical disruptions, and reinforcement learning to optimize adaptive response protocols. The framework will be validated using case studies from energy and transportation systems, incorporating real-world data on infrastructure topologies, threat intelligence, and historical incident reports. By enabling parallelized scenario testing across millions of nodes and edges, HPC resources are essential to achieving the required scale, speed, and complexity for these simulations. Anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive metrics for identifying high-risk failure pathways, (2) data-driven mitigation strategies to reduce systemic vulnerabilities, and (3) policy recommendations for enhancing redundancy and response coordination across infrastructure operators. This work directly supports national security priorities by providing actionable tools to prioritize resource allocation, strengthen contingency planning, and improve the adaptive capacity of critical infrastructure systems against evolving threats.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the design, planning and management of systems and procedures for protecting critical national physical and cyber infrastructure from external threats, including terrorism. Includes instruction in homeland security policy, critical infrastructure policy, information security, matrix vulnerability assessment, threat assessment, physical security, personnel security, operational security, contingency planning, case analyses of specific industries and systems, redundancy planning, emergency and disaster planning, security systems, and intelligence operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven agricultural communication strategies by analyzing the dynamics of information dissemination across diverse stakeholder networks. Agricultural communication faces unique challenges in translating complex scientific and technical content—such as precision farming techniques, livestock health protocols, or climate-resilient crop practices—into accessible, actionable information for farmers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders. Current approaches often lack granular insights into how audience segmentation, platform-specific content optimization, or misinformation propagation influence outreach efficacy. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale social media analytics, natural language processing (NLP), and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate and predict information flow patterns. HPC resources will enable the processing of multi-terabyte datasets from platforms like Twitter, agricultural extension databases, and farmer survey responses, which will train machine learning models to classify audience preferences and misinformation risks. Concurrently, ABM simulations will map how localized communication interventions affect knowledge adoption rates in spatially diverse agricultural regions. By parallelizing these workflows, we aim to identify optimal messaging strategies tailored to regional agronomic practices, literacy levels, and socio-technical barriers. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for agricultural journalists and extension services to design targeted campaigns, reduce misinformation persistence, and improve stakeholder engagement metrics. This work bridges computational scalability with agricultural communication theory, offering novel methodologies to enhance the reach and impact of science-based farming practices in an era of rapidly evolving digital landscapes.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply journalistic, communication, and broadcasting principles to the development, production, and transmittal of agricultural information. Includes instruction in basic journalism, broadcasting, film/video, and communication techniques; the production of technically specialized information products for agricultural audiences; and the principles of agricultural sciences and business operations needed to develop and communicate agricultural subject matter in effective ways.

abstract: The administration of anesthetic agents requires precise titration to balance efficacy with patient safety, yet current protocols rely on generalized dosing models that inadequately account for dynamic intraoperative variables, including real-time biometric fluctuations and pharmacogenomic heterogeneity. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a machine learning framework to predict individualized anesthetic requirements using high-dimensional physiological, genomic, and pharmacokinetic data. The research will integrate multimodal inputs—including continuous electroencephalogram (EEG) waveforms, hemodynamic trends, and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiles—to model interpatient variability in drug metabolism and sedation depth. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets (>10 TB) from retrospective electronic health records and prospective intraoperative monitoring systems, enabling parallelized training of deep neural networks and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations. Key computational challenges include optimizing time-series analysis of EEG data to detect subclinical arousal states and resolving stochastic differential equations for real-time drug distribution modeling. The resulting predictive algorithms will be validated against clinical outcomes in a simulated surgical environment, with performance metrics compared to standard dosing protocols. Successfully linking patient-specific biological signatures to anesthetic responsiveness will advance precision sedation practices, reducing postoperative complications such as delirium and hemodynamic instability. This work bridges computational neuroscience, systems pharmacology, and clinical anesthesiology, establishing a novel paradigm for data-driven perioperative care. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to deliver an open-source software toolkit for anesthesiologist assistants to dynamically adjust anesthetic regimens, enhancing both patient safety and procedural efficiency in diverse surgical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in developing and implementing patient anesthesia care plans, including preoperative, surgical theater, recovery room, and postoperative/intensive care procedures. Includes instruction in patient data collection, catheter insertion, airway management and drug administration, assisting the administration and monitoring of regional and peripheral nerve blockades, support therapy, adjusting anesthetic levels during surgery, interoperative monitoring, postoperative procedures, pain clinics and patient education, and administrative tasks.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-omics data in comparative disease models presents a critical challenge in identifying molecular mechanisms shared between laboratory animals and humans. Current analytical workflows often lack the computational power to integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics—across species, limiting insights into conserved disease pathways. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable computational framework for cross-species analysis of experimental animal models, with a focus on immune-mediated disorders. Using machine learning algorithms, we will train species-agnostic models on existing multi-omics repositories to predict conserved biomarkers of chronic inflammation. Molecular dynamics simulations will further elucidate protein interaction networks perturbed in these conditions, leveraging comparative gene mapping data from murine, porcine, and non-human primate models. The HPC environment is essential for managing large-scale genomic alignments, parallelized simulations, and iterative model training, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models of disease susceptibility, prioritized therapeutic targets, and optimized protocols for translational studies. By enhancing the resolution of cross-species analyses, this work will advance the ethical refinement of animal models through reduced experimental variability and improved preclinical trial design. The resulting tools will be disseminated as open-source packages to support reproducible research in laboratory animal medicine, aligning with institutional goals to integrate computational biology into veterinary training programs. This project directly addresses the program’s emphasis on bioethics, computational modeling, and interdisciplinary approaches to experimental animal science, with implications for both human medicine and laboratory animal welfare.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: The growing need for scalable, personalized mental health interventions in community and educational settings requires advanced computational tools to decode complex patterns in counseling efficacy. This project aims to develop predictive models to identify optimal counseling strategies for mitigating anxiety and stress in non-clinical populations, using large-scale, multimodal datasets from school-based and community mental health programs. The research integrates anonymized session transcripts, client self-reports, and longitudinal outcome data (e.g., academic performance, social engagement) to analyze how counselor-client interaction dynamics and intervention timing influence therapeutic success. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to extract linguistic features (e.g., emotional valence, topic coherence) and interaction patterns from text, while time-series modeling will assess trajectories of client progress. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based NLP models on over 100,000 session transcripts, conducting Bayesian network analyses to map psychosocial risk and resilience factors, and running agent-based simulations to test intervention scalability. These computational methods will address the challenge of modeling nested data structures (clients within counselors within institutions) and temporal dependencies in longitudinal outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for matching counseling techniques to client profiles, evidence-based guidelines for session frequency and content sequencing, and open-source tools for real-time monitoring of intervention fidelity. By bridging applied psychology with computational innovation, this work will empower counselors to deliver data-informed, equitable care while advancing theoretical understanding of mechanisms underlying brief interventions. The project directly aligns with institutional priorities to reduce mental health disparities in underserved communities through translational research.
cip_title: Clinical, Counseling and Applied Psychology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in clinical, counseling and applied psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing cross-border energy infrastructure projects, with a focus on reconciling environmental protection mandates with energy security imperatives. The study addresses a critical gap in computational legal research by developing scalable models to simulate the impacts of heterogeneous national regulations, multilateral climate agreements, and stakeholder litigation patterns on transnational energy corridors. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) of legal texts (treaties, case law, environmental impact assessments) with geospatial analytics of energy transmission routes and ecological sensitivities. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify latent conflicts between project proponents' risk assessments and emerging judicial interpretations of "net-zero compliance" across jurisdictions. Agent-based modeling will simulate negotiation dynamics between state actors, private developers, and indigenous communities under varying policy scenarios. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets of legal documents, satellite imagery, and energy market variables while maintaining the temporal resolution required to model decade-long project lifecycles. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support framework for policymakers addressing the legal bottlenecks in sustainable energy transmission, predictive metrics for regulatory convergence across jurisdictions, and an open-access repository of annotated legal corpora optimized for computational analysis. By quantifying previously qualitative aspects of energy law through advanced simulations, this work aims to establish new methodologies for anticipatory governance in complex resource management systems.
cip_title: Energy, Environment, and Natural Resources Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing the energy industry, environmental protection, natural resources and land use, and related topics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of computational methods in visual culture analysis, focusing on large-scale pattern recognition and generative modeling within historical and contemporary art datasets. The central research problem lies in the limitations of traditional analytical frameworks for processing vast, heterogeneous visual datasets—such as digitized artworks, digital media archives, and experimental design outputs—which hinder the identification of cross-cultural stylistic trends, the quantification of aesthetic evolution, and the simulation of generative artistic processes. To address this, the project proposes a hybrid computational approach integrating computer vision algorithms, graph-based network analysis, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on curated datasets spanning diverse visual media, including paintings, digital art, and design prototypes. These methods will enable the automated classification of stylistic features, the mapping of influence networks across artistic movements, and the synthesis of novel hybrid visual forms informed by historical data. The intensive computational demands of processing high-resolution image corpora (over 500,000 images at 4K resolution) and training multi-modal generative models necessitate parallelized GPU workflows and distributed storage systems, which are only feasible through HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for computational art historical analysis, new insights into the dynamics of visual innovation, and ethically informed generative tools for artistic experimentation. This work bridges computational scalability with humanistic inquiry, offering transformative potential for interdisciplinary research in digital art history, media theory, and computational creativity while maintaining critical engagement with the cultural contexts of visual production.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of the visual arts. Includes instruction in art, photography, and other visual communications media.

abstract: Greenhouse operations require precise control of environmental variables to optimize plant growth, resource efficiency, and operational costs. However, current climate management strategies often rely on generalized models that inadequately capture the dynamic, species-specific interactions between plants and their microenvironment. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and predict plant-environment feedback loops in heterogeneous greenhouse systems. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate agent-based modeling of plant growth with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of airflow, temperature, and humidity distribution. These coupled models will incorporate real-world data from sensor arrays monitoring light intensity, irrigation, and nutrient delivery in a commercial-scale greenhouse. Machine learning algorithms will then iteratively optimize climate control parameters to balance yield outcomes against energy and water use. The computational demands are substantial, as the spatial and temporal resolution required to resolve microclimate variability at the plant-canopy level necessitates parallelized simulations across thousands of cores. Outcomes will include validated predictive models for species-specific climate management, a decision-support tool for adaptive greenhouse control systems, and open-source code for scalable plant-environment simulations. This work will advance precision agriculture by enabling data-driven optimization of greenhouse operations, with potential reductions in energy consumption (15–20%) and water use (10–15%) while maintaining crop yields. By elucidating the mechanistic links between microenvironmental conditions and plant physiology, the project also contributes foundational knowledge for designing next-generation controlled environment agriculture systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in modeling complexity and scaling simulations to operational greenhouse dimensions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce, store, and deliver plant species in controlled indoor environments for wholesale, commercial, research, or other purposes. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science; climate, irrigation, and nutrition control equipment operation and maintenance; facilities management; inventory control; safety procedures; and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to advance equitable educational assessment practices by analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets to identify systemic biases in learning outcome evaluations. Traditional statistical methods struggle to model complex, nonlinear interactions in multimillion-row datasets spanning standardized test results, demographic surveys, and digital learning platform logs. We propose developing machine learning architectures to 1) detect latent bias patterns in assessment instruments across diverse student subgroups and 2) simulate how modified evaluation frameworks could reduce observed disparities. The computational workflow integrates natural language processing (NLP) to analyze open-response items, graph neural networks to map relationships between institutional policies and localized achievement gaps, and Bayesian hierarchical models to account for nested data structures (e.g., district-school-classroom hierarchies). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on text responses from 12 million K-12 assessments, conducting Monte Carlo simulations of alternative grading rubrics, and running sensitivity analyses across 150+ demographic cross-sections. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source bias detection toolkit for assessment designers, 2) empirically validated thresholds for differential item functioning in AI-assisted grading systems, and 3) policy recommendations for weighting socioeconomic covariates in accountability frameworks. By leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed memory parallelism, this work will overcome current limitations in handling sparse, high-dimensional education data while maintaining interpretability constraints required for ethical AI in assessment contexts. The results will directly inform state-level reforms in competency modeling and help institutions audit assessment equity under proposed Title IX regulatory changes.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_title: Educational Assessment, Evaluation, and Research, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in educational evaluation, research and statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project addresses critical challenges in advancing laser system performance through computational modeling of complex optical phenomena that currently limit high-power and ultra-fast applications. The research focuses on developing predictive simulations for thermal-optical coupling, beam propagation instability, and nonlinear frequency conversion processes in advanced laser architectures. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture multi-physics interactions across spatial and temporal scales, particularly in emerging high-energy-density systems and photonic integration platforms. We propose a hybrid computational strategy combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for nanoscale light-matter interactions with ray-transfer matrix analysis for macroscopic beam control systems. High-performance computing resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization of phase-stabilized laser arrays and multi-layer optical coatings through massively parallelized finite element analysis. The computational framework will incorporate machine learning techniques to accelerate inverse design of gradient-index optics and predict thermal lensing effects in solid-state gain media. Expected outcomes include validated models for mitigating transverse mode instability in fiber laser systems and optimizing second-harmonic generation in quasi-phase-matched nonlinear crystals. These results will directly inform the development of next-generation laser systems with enhanced power scalability and spectral purity for applications in precision metrology and materials processing. The project will produce open-source simulation tools that bridge current gaps between nanophotonic design principles and macroscopic laser engineering, providing new capabilities for the optical technology community to prototype complex systems computationally before physical fabrication. By establishing correlations between computational predictions and experimental validation datasets from partner institutions, this work aims to reduce development cycles for novel laser architectures while improving safety through virtual testing of failure scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using lasers and other optical for commercial or research purposes. Includes instruction in laser and optical principles, testing and maintenance procedures, safety precautions, specific applications to various tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel framework for optimizing hybrid quantum-classical programming workflows, addressing the computational challenges of integrating noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices with classical high-performance computing (HPC) systems. While quantum computing has seen rapid theoretical advances, practical implementations face bottlenecks in efficiently orchestrating resource allocation between quantum processors and classical co-processors, particularly for iterative algorithms in machine learning and optimization. The research problem centers on mitigating latency and error propagation in hybrid systems, which are not adequately addressed by existing quantum programming toolchains or classical parallelization paradigms. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation of hybrid task scheduling with variational quantum algorithm (VQA) benchmarking, leveraging GPU-accelerated quantum circuit simulations and reinforcement learning-based resource negotiators. A custom middleware layer will be prototyped to dynamically partition computational graphs across quantum and classical resources based on real-time fidelity metrics and cost models. The project requires HPC resources to 1) simulate NISQ device behaviors at scale using noise models derived from experimental calibration data, 2) train neural schedulers on heterogeneous architectures, and 3) validate the framework against combinatorial optimization problems in network routing. Expected outcomes include quantifiable performance benchmarks for hybrid quantum-classical workflows, open-source scheduling algorithms optimized for current-generation quantum co-processors, and novel metrics for evaluating quantum resource efficiency in heterogeneous compute environments. This work will provide foundational insights into practical co-design strategies for emerging hybrid computing architectures, with potential applications in logistics, quantum-enhanced machine learning, and error-corrected quantum memory systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer programming, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of maintaining precision in manufacturing and construction quality control (QC) processes, where traditional statistical methods struggle to handle the scale and complexity of modern sensor-driven data streams. Current QC systems often rely on offline sampling and manual inspections, leading to delayed defect detection, increased waste, and inefficiencies in high-throughput environments. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a real-time, computational quality control framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating multi-physics simulations of manufacturing processes to predict defect formation under variable conditions, and (2) training machine learning models for adaptive anomaly detection in heterogeneous production data. Computational methods will include parallelized finite element analysis for simulating material stresses in additive manufacturing, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic failure modeling, and deep neural networks trained on terabyte-scale sensor datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of complex simulations across diverse manufacturing scenarios while supporting distributed training of ensemble models for real-time quality prediction. Expected outcomes include an open-source QC analytics toolkit optimized for HPC architectures, validated against industrial case studies in precision machining and composite material fabrication. By enabling near-instantaneous analysis of high-dimensional process data, this work aims to reduce defect rates by an estimated 15–30% in partner manufacturing systems while decreasing computational latency for quality assessments by 80% compared to current cloud-based solutions. The project will directly enhance the scalability of automated QC systems, providing technical education programs with advanced computational case studies for curriculum development in quality assurance technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining consistent manufacturing and construction standards. Includes instruction in quality control systems management principles, technical standards applicable to specific engineering and manufacturing projects, testing procedures, inspection procedures, related instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize individualized educational strategies for students with intellectual disabilities (ID). Despite advances in special education pedagogy, educators face persistent challenges in efficiently designing personalized interventions that account for the heterogeneous cognitive, behavioral, and sensory profiles of students with ID. Current methods for creating individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual, time-consuming assessments and trial-and-error adjustments. This research proposes a computational approach to model learning trajectories and predict intervention outcomes by analyzing multimodal educational data, including student response patterns, behavioral logs, and longitudinal academic performance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large-scale datasets from diverse student populations, train machine learning models to identify predictors of skill acquisition, and simulate the efficacy of tailored instructional sequences under varying constraints. The project will integrate reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically adapt proposed interventions based on simulated student interactions, coupled with agent-based modeling to explore how different classroom resource allocations (e.g., assistive technology configurations, educator-to-student ratios) influence outcomes. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, these simulations will iteratively test thousands of scenario permutations, enabling the identification of robust, generalizable strategies for IEP design. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework to assist educators in generating data-driven IEP recommendations, reducing the time and subjectivity inherent in manual processes. The models will also quantify the impact of specific resource limitations (e.g., limited access to speech-generating devices) on achievable learning goals, informing policy discussions about equitable resource distribution. This work bridges educational theory and computational analytics, offering a scalable methodology to enhance evidence-based practices in special education while respecting the complexity of individual learner needs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with intellectual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with intellectual disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising mentally handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in Tibetan Studies through the analysis of large-scale cultural and historical datasets. The primary challenge lies in synthesizing fragmented textual, visual, and oral sources—spanning classical Tibetan manuscripts, modern exile community archives, and multimedia records of religious practices—to trace the evolution of Tibetan cultural identity across temporal and spatial boundaries. Traditional humanities methodologies are insufficient for processing this volume of unstructured, multilingual data or detecting subtle patterns in ritual practices, artistic motifs, and narrative traditions. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for classical and modern Tibetan corpora, computer vision techniques to analyze thangka paintings and ritual objects, and network modeling to map transnational connections between monastic institutions and diaspora communities. Key tasks include training domain-specific language models for classical Tibetan to automate the translation and semantic analysis of pre-modern religious texts, as well as developing spatial-temporal visualizations of pilgrimage routes and cultural transmission nodes. These methods will enable systematic comparisons between historical records and contemporary ethnographic materials while preserving the contextual integrity of sources. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of processed datasets, new frameworks for studying cultural continuity amid displacement, and quantitative evidence challenging reductionist narratives about Tibetan identity formation. By bridging computational methods with area studies expertise, this project aims to establish scalable protocols for analyzing marginalized cultural heritage in ethically engaged ways, with implications for both academic research and community-led preservation initiatives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Tibet and its borderlands, with emphasis on both pre-modern and modern Tibet and associated religious and exile movements.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of health misinformation propagation and the efficacy of corrective communication strategies across digital media platforms. Public health institutions increasingly struggle to counter health-related misinformation, which undermines trust in evidence-based guidance and influences health behaviors. Current gaps persist in understanding how misinformation networks form, evolve, and respond to corrective messaging, particularly across linguistically and culturally diverse populations. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate misinformation diffusion and test communication interventions. Large-scale social media datasets—spanning platforms like X (Twitter), Facebook, and Reddit—will be processed to identify patterns in misinformation narratives, sentiment shifts, and community polarization. NLP pipelines will classify content themes and linguistic markers of persuasion, while temporal network models will map how clusters of misinformation propagate. ABM simulations will then model hypothetical public health campaigns, varying message framing, source credibility, and dissemination timing to predict optimal strategies for countering false narratives. This computationally intensive workflow requires HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train deep learning models for real-time text classification, and execute parallelized simulations across diverse demographic parameters. Expected outcomes include a framework for designing resilient health communication campaigns, predictive metrics for identifying high-risk misinformation “superspreaders,” and actionable insights into platform-specific intervention timing. Results will be disseminated to public health agencies and communication researchers, offering scalable tools to mitigate the societal harms of health misinformation while advancing computational methods for media analysis in non-STEM disciplines.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how people, individually and collectively, understand and accommodate to health and illness and the role of communication and media in shaping professional health care messages and public acceptance of these messages. Includes instruction in the development and use of health-related and care-related messages and media; the goals and strategies of health care promotion; relationships, roles, situations, and social structures in the context of health maintenance and promotion; and applications to disease prevention, health advocacy, and communications concerning treatments.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the legal and regulatory frameworks governing generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the arts and entertainment industries. As generative AI tools rapidly evolve, they challenge existing intellectual property regimes, contractual norms, and ethical standards, particularly in areas such as copyright attribution, derivative work classification, and rights management for AI-generated content. Traditional legal research methods struggle to map the scale and complexity of emerging case law, licensing agreements, and policy proposals across global jurisdictions. To address this gap, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) models to systematically parse legal documents, court rulings, and regulatory guidance, combined with network analysis to visualize relationships between stakeholders, rights holders, and AI developers. Computational simulations will model potential legal outcomes under varying regulatory scenarios, including proposed EU AI Act provisions and U.S. Copyright Office guidance on AI-authored works. The research will utilize GPU-accelerated computing to train custom transformer models on a corpus of interdisciplinary texts spanning entertainment law, digital humanities, and AI ethics frameworks. Expected outcomes include a dynamic decision-support tool for legal practitioners navigating AI-related disputes and a predictive framework for assessing compliance risks in AI-driven content creation. By bridging computational methods with arts law scholarship, this project aims to establish scalable analytical frameworks for addressing 21st-century intellectual property challenges while maintaining alignment with creative industries’ economic and cultural priorities.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting the sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, and media industries.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of real-time analysis and optimization of corporate communication networks in large organizations, a critical yet underexplored challenge at the intersection of computational linguistics, behavioral analytics, and organizational strategy. Corporate communications generate vast unstructured datasets—including internal memos, stakeholder emails, press releases, and social media interactions—that require advanced computational methods to evaluate for consistency, sentiment alignment, and crisis response efficacy. Traditional tools lack the capacity to process multimodal data (text, audio, visual) at scale while preserving contextual nuance, leading to inefficiencies in strategic decision-making. The proposed work will develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model communication flows, simulate stakeholder response dynamics, and identify latent risks in real time. Using transformer-based neural architectures fine-tuned on industry-specific corpora, the system will perform semantic coherence checks, sentiment trajectory mapping, and anomaly detection across hierarchical communication layers. Graph convolutional networks will map interdependencies between internal teams and external partners, while reinforcement learning agents will stress-test proposed messaging strategies against simulated crisis scenarios. The computational pipeline will leverage distributed GPU clusters for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, enabling subsecond latency in critical-path analyses. Expected outcomes include a novel metric system for quantifying communication network resilience, automated tools for preemptive reputation risk mitigation, and generative models to optimize cross-departmental content alignment. This work bridges a gap in applied business communication research by providing empirically grounded, computation-driven methods to enhance organizational agility in high-stakes environments. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive workloads in training domain-specific large language models and running millions of stochastic simulations for scenario validation. Results will be validated against historical corporate crisis datasets and peer-reviewed via partnerships with communications analytics firms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize dairy cattle health, feed efficiency, and methane emission dynamics in large-scale dairy production systems. Dairy farming faces mounting challenges in balancing productivity, animal welfare, and environmental sustainability, particularly as herd sizes grow and climate regulations tighten. Current empirical methods struggle to disentangle the multivariate interactions between genetics, microbiota, feed composition, and facility design that govern these outcomes. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, metagenomic analysis, and machine learning to simulate dairy herd metabolism at scale. The model will parameterize individual cows using genomic data, rumen microbiome profiles, and real-time sensor inputs (e.g., activity, milk yield), while simulating facility-level factors like feed delivery systems and barn ventilation. High-throughput simulations will test how variations in feed additives, breeding strategies, and facility layouts affect herd-wide methane output and milk production efficiency. Metagenomic datasets from rumen fluid samples (sequenced via shotgun metagenomics) will be processed using bioinformatics pipelines to characterize microbial functional networks linked to methane synthesis and nutrient absorption. Machine learning models trained on these multi-omics datasets will predict optimal feed formulations under seasonal forage variability. The HPC environment is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of 10,000+ agent-based simulations, parallel processing of terabyte-scale metagenomic data, and iterative optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include actionable strategies to reduce enteric methane emissions by ≥15% while maintaining production targets, decision-support tools for precision feeding, and genomic markers for breeding low-emission dairy lines. This work directly addresses gaps in scalable, systems-level dairy management tools while advancing computational methods for agricultural applications. Results will be disseminated through open-source models and partnerships with regional dairy cooperatives.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the selection and care of dairy animals and associated dairy farm and processing facilities and operations. Includes instruction in basic animal and dairy science; dairy animal nutrition and health; design and operation of dairy housing, feeding, and processing facilities and equipment; and related issues of safety, sanitation, shipping and handling, and applicable regulations.

abstract: Directed energy systems represent a critical frontier in modern defense technology, requiring advanced computational tools to address complex challenges in beam propagation, system resilience, and operational optimization. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity models for laser weapon systems operating in dynamic atmospheric conditions, with a focus on mitigating nonlinear optical effects and thermal blooming that degrade beam efficacy. Current analytical frameworks inadequately capture the interplay between turbulence, particulate matter, and high-energy laser interactions at scale, particularly in urban or maritime environments where humidity and aerosol densities vary unpredictably. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-scale simulation architecture integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), Maxwell’s equations solvers, and machine learning-driven adaptive optics control algorithms. The computational workflow will employ GPU-accelerated ray tracing to model photon-matter interactions across kilometer-scale propagation paths while resolving micron-level thermal gradients in beam-forming optics. A novel feature involves coupling discrete element methods with quantum cascade laser simulations to assess degradation pathways in high-power fiber laser arrays under sustained operation. Validation will utilize classified field test datasets from military partners, enabling iterative refinement of predictive models. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source framework for directed energy system simulation, real-time beam correction protocols resilient to adversarial countermeasures, and thermal management strategies extending operational lifetimes by 40-60%. This work bridges gaps between photonic theory and deployable military systems, directly informing next-generation energy weapon design while establishing computational best practices for a domain where experimental testing remains logistically prohibitive and cost-intensive.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of lasers and other directed energy phenomena and their application to the creation of energy beam weapons systems. Includes instruction in photonics, electro-optics, microwave phenomena, laser chemistry, spectroscopy, chemical lasers, fibre lasers, imaging and optics, laser propagation and control, laser communication, infrared remote sensing, modeling and simulation, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to address gaps in understanding the evolution of Western polyphonic compositional practices between the 14th and 16th centuries by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale musical datasets. While historical musicology has traditionally relied on manual score analysis, the sheer volume of surviving manuscripts—coupled with complex intertextual relationships between works—has hindered systematic study of stylistic transitions, regional influences, and theoretical innovations. Our research will computationally process digitized musical corpora, including the Digital Image Archive of Medieval Music and the Josquin Research Project, using optical music recognition (OMR) adapted for early notation systems. Converted symbolic data will undergo feature extraction for harmonic progressions, contrapuntal patterns, and cadential structures through custom Python pipelines integrating music21 and librosa. Machine learning models (LSTMs, transformer networks) will then identify temporal and geographic patterns in compositional techniques, trained on metadata-rich subsets before scaling to full corpora. HPC resources are critical for managing storage demands (50+ TB of high-resolution manuscript images), parallel processing of OMR workflows, and training complex models across thousands of scores. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of analyzed works, quantitative maps of stylistic diffusion across Europe, and detection of previously unrecognized theoretical treatise influences on compositional practice. By bridging computational methods with musicological expertise, this work will enable novel insights into Renaissance musical networks while establishing reproducible frameworks for computational music analysis. Results will directly inform ongoing debates about the transmission of musical knowledge and the technological constraints shaping early modern composition.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical evolution of music as a social and intellectual phenomenon, the development of musical instruments and techniques, and the analysis and criticism of musical literature. Includes instruction in music history research methods, aesthetic analysis of musical compositions, history of musical writing and notation, the development of musical instruments, the development of music theory, and the study of specific periods, cultural traditions, styles, and themes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize automated analysis of complex tissue microarchitecture in histologic samples, addressing critical inefficiencies in current manual and semi-automated methods. Histologic technicians routinely process tissue sections for diagnostic and research purposes, yet quantitative assessment of structural features—such as extracellular matrix organization, cellular spatial distributions, and microvascular patterns—remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability. Our research focuses on creating deep learning models capable of parsing high-resolution whole-slide images (WSIs) to map 3D tissue architecture from serial sections, a task requiring immense computational resources due to gigapixel-scale datasets and the need for volumetric reconstructions. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will train 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on annotated WSIs spanning diverse tissue types and staining protocols (e.g., H&E, Masson’s trichrome), integrating spatial transcriptomics data where available to ground structural patterns in molecular context. A parallel computational pipeline will simulate tissue deformation during processing—factoring in fixation, embedding, and sectioning variables—to improve alignment algorithms for 3D reconstructions. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and CPU clusters for large-scale batch processing of archival slides. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for volumetric histologic analysis, validated against gold-standard manual annotations, and a novel simulation engine to guide optimal tissue preparation protocols. This work directly enhances the precision and scope of histotechnicians' diagnostic capabilities while enabling researchers to interrogate tissue structure-function relationships at unprecedented scales. By bridging computational science and histotechnology, the project establishes a foundation for AI-driven innovation in tissue-based diagnostics, with applications in fibrosis research, tumor microenvironment studies, and regenerative medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling the emergent dynamics of decentralized information ecosystems, with a focus on resilience against systemic cognitive biases. The research addresses the challenge of simulating large-scale, heterogeneous agent interactions in environments where information is dynamically generated, filtered, and propagated through both algorithmic and human-mediated processes. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement a hybrid architecture combining discrete-event simulation, graph neural networks, and evolutionary optimization to capture multi-scale feedback loops between individual cognitive processing and collective information landscapes. The computational model will integrate empirically derived parameters from behavioral studies with synthetic data generation techniques to explore scenarios spanning 10^4 to 10^6 interacting agents. Key methodological innovations include adaptive topology management for evolving communication networks and a novel bias-injection mechanism that quantifies the systemic impact of cognitive heuristics under varying information loads. Expected outcomes include a publicly available simulation platform for testing intervention strategies in misinformation resilience, quantitative metrics for ecosystem vulnerability assessment, and fundamental insights into phase transitions within attention-driven information economies. This work bridges computational social science, complexity theory, and human-computer interaction, offering new tools to address critical challenges in digital community governance while advancing methodological paradigms for studying emergent phenomena in socio-technical systems. The scale of required parameter space exploration and real-time network analysis necessitates access to parallel computing infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Parasitic diseases remain a critical global health burden, with emerging resistance to existing therapeutics underscoring the urgent need for novel intervention strategies. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underpinning host-parasite interactions and chemotherapeutic resistance in two understudied helminth species: *Schistosoma mansoni* and *Ancylostoma duodenale*. A key challenge lies in resolving the structural dynamics of parasite-specific proteins implicated in immune evasion and drug metabolism, particularly those with high conformational flexibility or transient binding sites that evade traditional crystallographic methods. We propose an integrative computational approach combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free-energy perturbation (FEP) calculations, and machine learning-enhanced virtual screening to model parasite protein targets at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolutions. MD simulations will be performed on GPCR-like neuropeptide receptors unique to schistosomes, using all-atom explicit solvent models to capture ligand-binding pathways over microsecond timescales. Concurrently, FEP will quantify the binding affinity landscapes of anthelmintic candidates against hookworm glutathione S-transferase isoforms associated with benzimidazole resistance. These analyses will integrate multi-omics datasets—including cryo-EM density maps of parasite membranes and host immunoglobulin repertoires—to contextualize molecular interactions within physiological host environments. The computational workflow demands large-scale parallelization, requiring >50,000 CPU-core hours per target system and GPU-accelerated sampling for enhanced phase-space exploration. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved allosteric sites in parasite signaling proteins and prioritized small molecules with predicted sub-nanomolar binding to resistance-conferring enzymes. This work will directly inform downstream in vitro validation of lead compounds and guide the rational design of next-generation antiparasitics. By elucidating resistance mechanisms and host-specific adaptation strategies, the project advances foundational knowledge in ecological parasitology while addressing translational gaps in chemotherapeutic development.
