Access to HPC resources is essential to overcome current limitations in simulating membrane-bound parasite systems and achieving the statistical rigor required for robust free-energy calculations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biological organisms living in ecologically exploitative and competitive relationships with host organisms, and the role of parasites in causing injury, disease, and environmental damage. Includes instruction in vector biology, immunoparasitology, medical parasitology, molecular biology of parasitical associations, veterinary and comparative parasitology, chemotherapeutics, and ecological and systematic parasitology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in real-time decision-making within customer service support systems, specifically focusing on call center and teleservice operations. Traditional approaches to optimizing customer-agent interactions, sentiment analysis, and resource allocation rely on static models or simplified simulations, which fail to capture the dynamic, high-dimensional nature of modern multichannel customer service ecosystems. The core research problem centers on developing adaptive computational frameworks that integrate real-time telemetry data (e.g., voice tone, query complexity, agent expertise, and customer history) with predictive analytics to enhance service personalization and operational efficiency. The project will employ large-scale agent-based modeling to simulate millions of concurrent customer journeys across voice, chat, and hybrid interfaces, coupled with machine learning techniques—including transformer-based natural language processing and reinforcement learning—to optimize routing policies and agent training protocols. Computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale interaction logs, training low-latency recommendation systems for live service escalations, and quantifying the impact of emotional valence in customer dialogues on long-term retention metrics. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU clusters and utilizing distributed memory architectures, the research aims to identify non-linear relationships between service variables (e.g., wait time thresholds, script adherence, and empathy indicators) and business outcomes (e.g., resolution rates, churn reduction). Expected outcomes include open-source tools for simulating service operation scenarios under resource constraints, validated benchmarks for AI-assisted customer interaction design, and actionable insights into balancing automation with human-centric service delivery. This work will provide a foundation for data-driven policymaking in customer experience management, bridging gaps between behavioral economics, computational linguistics, and operations research within an understudied business niche.
cip_title: Customer Service Support/ Call Center/ Teleservice Operation
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist customers with inquiries and problems in frontline call centers, help desks, teleservice centers, and online. Includes instruction in user interfaces and user behavior, principles of hardware and software systems operation, customer interaction skills, telephone and e-mailing skills, data entry, and database and Internet searching and retrieval.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the long-term impacts of anthropogenic groundwater extraction and contamination on regional aquifer systems in semi-arid regions. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting how coupled hydrological, geochemical, and mechanical processes—exacerbated by agricultural and industrial activities—affect groundwater sustainability and subsurface integrity. Current models often oversimplify fracture-mediated contaminant transport or fail to integrate dynamic stress-strain relationships in heterogeneous geological media, limiting their predictive power. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-physics computational framework combining 3D finite element hydrogeological simulations with machine learning-enhanced reactive transport models. The workflow will integrate high-resolution LiDAR-derived fracture networks, borehole geochemistry datasets, and InSAR-derived land subsidence measurements to parameterize a coupled fluid flow-geomechanics model. Parallelized simulations will resolve pore-scale to basin-scale interactions using adaptive mesh refinement, while graph neural networks will optimize predictions of contaminant dispersion pathways under varying extraction scenarios. The HPC environment is essential for managing the computational burden of ensemble simulations spanning decadal timescales and for quantifying uncertainties through Monte Carlo analysis of stochastic fracture properties. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of aquifer vulnerability, quantitative risk assessments for contaminant breakthrough in water supply wells, and optimized mitigation strategies for regulatory stakeholders. By advancing the integration of heterogeneous datasets across spatial and temporal scales, this work will provide a transferable computational toolkit for sustainable groundwater management in stressed basins, directly supporting environmental policy development and hazard mitigation efforts mandated in resource-limited regions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the environmental implications of geological processes and human activities on Earth. Includes instruction in environmental/natural resource management, geographic information systems (GIS), geology, hydrology, regulatory agency compliance, hazard identification and mitigation, environmental law, environmental policy, and sustainability studies.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of urban transportation networks under climate-induced stressors using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Rapid urbanization and intensifying weather extremes strain aging infrastructure, necessitating dynamic modeling approaches to balance safety, efficiency, and sustainability. Current methodologies often rely on static traffic flow models or oversimplified climate projections, limiting their ability to capture cascading failures in interconnected systems. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based traffic simulations, hydrodynamic flood modeling, and probabilistic failure analysis. The HPC environment will enable parallel execution of coupled models at city-scale resolution, incorporating real-time sensor data and ensemble climate scenarios to assess infrastructure vulnerabilities. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize adaptive traffic signal control and evacuation routing under flood conditions, while finite element analysis will evaluate the structural integrity of bridges and culverts under hydrodynamic loading. Outcomes will include a predictive toolset for identifying high-risk corridors, prioritizing retrofit investments, and testing resilience strategies such as green infrastructure integration. By quantifying trade-offs between mitigation costs and long-term service reliability, this work aims to inform data-driven policy decisions for municipalities facing climate adaptation challenges. The requested computing resources are critical to handling the computational intensity of 3D hydraulic simulations, large-scale network optimization, and uncertainty quantification across thousands of scenario iterations. Results will be disseminated through open-source models and partnerships with regional transportation agencies to support equitable infrastructure planning.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern construction materials and techniques demands advanced tools to ensure compliance with evolving safety standards and building codes. Current inspection practices often rely on manual assessments, which can be time-consuming, subjective, and limited in detecting latent structural vulnerabilities. This project proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and predict material degradation, structural failures, and environmental impacts on buildings. By integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and large-scale sensor data analytics, the research aims to create predictive models that assess structural integrity under diverse stressors, including seismic activity, thermal fluctuations, and prolonged load-bearing scenarios. Key computational tasks include simulating multi-physics interactions in composite materials, training ML algorithms on historical inspection datasets to identify defect patterns, and optimizing real-time analysis of IoT sensor networks deployed on construction sites. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution 3D building models, accelerate Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic risk assessment, and support the development of AI-driven anomaly detection systems. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for automated defect classification, risk prioritization maps for inspectors, and dynamic compliance checklists tailored to regional building codes. This work will advance evidence-based inspection protocols, reduce human error in safety evaluations, and provide a scalable platform for preemptive maintenance planning. By bridging computational engineering with practical inspection workflows, the project seeks to transform regulatory oversight in the construction industry, ultimately enhancing public safety and resource efficiency in urban infrastructure management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply industrial, labor, and governmental standards and laws to the oversight of construction projects and the maintenance of completed buildings and other structures. Includes instruction in construction processes and techniques, materials analysis, occupational safety and health, industry standards, building codes and specifications, blueprint interpretation, testing equipment and procedures, communication skills, accident investigation, and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize extracorporeal circulation protocols during cardiac surgeries, addressing critical gaps in personalized perfusion management. Despite advances in perfusion technology, current methods for determining optimal pump flow rates, anticoagulation strategies, and temperature management during cardiopulmonary bypass remain generalized, potentially leading to suboptimal outcomes such as end-organ injury or thromboembolic complications. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create patient-specific hemodynamic simulations that integrate real-time physiological data with multi-scale models of circulatory dynamics. A hybrid computational approach will be employed, combining finite element analysis for device-circuit interactions, computational fluid dynamics for blood flow modeling, and machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective surgical data to predict patient-specific responses. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution 3D vascular geometries derived from perioperative imaging, coupled with stochastic modeling of hematological parameters under varying anticoagulation regimes. Expected outcomes include predictive models that recommend individualized perfusion parameters based on preoperative patient characteristics and intraoperative variables, validated against clinical outcomes from a 500-case institutional database. The computational framework will also simulate rare but catastrophic scenarios (e.g., massive air embolism) to refine emergency response protocols. By bridging computational modeling with clinical perfusion practice, this work aims to reduce postoperative complications by an estimated 15-20% in modeled cohorts while establishing a scalable platform for simulating next-generation perfusion technologies. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated computations for neural network training, large-scale fluid-structure interaction simulations, and secure HIPAA-compliant data integration from electronic health records. This project represents a novel convergence of computational biomechanics and perfusion science, with potential to transform evidence-based guidelines in extracorporeal circulation management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to operate extracorporeal circulation and autotransfusion equipment during medical procedures and surgeries where the support or temporary replacement of a patient's own respiratory or circulatory system is required. Includes instruction in equipment selection and operation, physician and medical team consultation, patient condition monitoring, procedural techniques, and principles of respiratory and circulatory physiology.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between climate-driven environmental shifts, human migration patterns, and the emergence of infectious diseases through an interdisciplinary lens integrating climatology, epidemiology, and sociocultural dynamics. Rapid environmental changes, including rising temperatures and altered precipitation regimes, are reshaping ecosystems and human habitats, potentially amplifying disease transmission risks while displacing vulnerable populations. Existing models often treat ecological, epidemiological, and social factors in isolation, limiting predictive accuracy for health outcomes in migrating populations. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution computational framework that couples climate projection data with agent-based models of human mobility and dynamic disease transmission networks. The framework will incorporate region-specific socioeconomic variables, cultural practices affecting health behaviors, and pathogen ecophysiology under varying climatic conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process petabyte-scale climate datasets from CMIP6 models, simulate migration decision-making processes across millions of agents, and model pathogen spread through spatially explicit contact networks. Machine learning techniques will be employed to identify nonlinear interactions between environmental stressors and disease emergence thresholds, validated against historical outbreak records and contemporary field surveillance data. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of climate-migration-disease hotspots, quantitative assessments of intervention strategies, and open-source tools for adaptive public health planning. By bridging scales from molecular pathogen dynamics to continental-scale human movements, this work aims to advance preparedness for climate-associated health crises while providing a novel paradigm for studying biological-social system interdependencies. The computational infrastructure developed will enable future investigations of cascading risks at the human-environment interface, with implications for global health equity and climate resilience policy.
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on understanding the human being from the biological, social science, and humanities perspectives and that addresses contemporary issues related to biology and society, such as global health and disease, environmental policy, bioethics, and biotechnology.

abstract: Occupational therapy interventions rely on personalized strategies to enhance patient engagement in daily activities, yet current methods for predicting intervention efficacy lack granularity in modeling dynamic interactions between patient-specific biomechanical, cognitive, and environmental factors. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating wearable sensor data, biomechanical simulations, and reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize task-specific interventions for individuals with upper limb motor impairments. The research problem centers on the inability of traditional clinical assessments to account for real-time physiological variability and environmental context when designing therapeutic activities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal data streams—including inertial measurement units, electromyography, and 3D motion capture—from a cohort of 120 patients undergoing occupational therapy. Computational workflows will employ OpenSim for musculoskeletal modeling to simulate limb dynamics under varying task demands, coupled with RL algorithms trained on individualized reward functions that prioritize motor learning efficiency and pain reduction. Sensitivity analyses will quantify how subtle changes in task parameters (e.g., object weight, workspace layout) impact therapeutic outcomes. Expected outcomes include a predictive model capable of generating adaptive intervention blueprints that respond to patient progress and contextual factors, validated against longitudinal functional independence measures. This work bridges health sciences and computational engineering, advancing evidence-based practices for occupational therapist assistants by providing data-driven tools to personalize therapeutic task progression. The computational infrastructure will enable scaling to diverse impairment populations while maintaining the low-latency processing required for eventual translation to real-time clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational linguistics and second language acquisition (SLA) within English as a Second Language (ESL) pedagogy. A critical challenge in ESL instruction is the variability in learners’ linguistic proficiency, influenced by factors such as native language transfer, phonological processing, and syntactic complexity. Current methods for analyzing these dynamics are limited by the scale of data required to model diverse learner populations and the computational demands of simulating real-world language use. This research addresses these gaps by developing machine learning models to analyze large-scale, multimodal learner corpora—including written texts, speech recordings, and interaction logs—to identify patterns in error types, fluency development, and pragmatic competence. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, such as transformer-based architectures for syntactic parsing and phonetic alignment algorithms, with longitudinal statistical models to track proficiency trajectories. HPC resources are essential for training these models on heterogeneous datasets spanning multiple proficiency levels and language backgrounds, enabling parallel processing of high-dimensional linguistic features. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for identifying persistent learner challenges specific to L1-English contrasts, (2) optimized intervention strategies for error correction, and (3) open-access tools for generating adaptive ESL instructional materials. By mapping computational insights to pedagogical frameworks, this work aims to enhance the personalization of ESL curricula in postsecondary settings, directly supporting the program’s mission to meet academic and occupational language demands. The project’s computational outputs will be validated against established SLA assessments, ensuring alignment with educational standards while advancing methodological innovation in applied linguistics research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of leadership decision-making under complex organizational constraints using computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. A critical challenge in organizational leadership is understanding how leaders balance competing priorities—such as financial efficiency, team cohesion, and stakeholder demands—in rapidly evolving environments. Existing studies often rely on qualitative case analyses or simplified simulations, limiting generalizability and scalability. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate multi-level organizational interactions under varying leadership strategies, resource allocations, and crisis scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize these models with real-world organizational datasets (e.g., communication logs, performance metrics, and employee surveys) and to execute thousands of parallel simulations. The computational framework will integrate machine learning techniques to identify patterns in leadership effectiveness across diverse virtual scenarios, including supply chain disruptions, workforce restructuring, and cross-cultural team conflicts. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of adaptive leadership behaviors correlated with organizational resilience, quantified metrics for resource allocation trade-offs, and predictive tools to assess intervention impacts before implementation. This work will advance scholarly understanding of leadership as a dynamic, data-driven process while providing actionable insights for training programs and policy design. The requested computing resources will enable handling of sensitive, large-scale organizational datasets securely, support real-time visualization of network-level decision cascades, and reduce simulation runtime from weeks to days. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this project aims to establish a replicable methodology for evidence-based leadership development in business and non-profit sectors.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leadership skills that can be applied to a business, government, non-profit, or educational setting. Includes instruction in organizational planning, dynamics of leadership, finance, team building, conflict resolution and mediation, communication and other management skills.

abstract: The rising global burden of liver diseases, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), demands advanced computational approaches to unravel complex molecular mechanisms and optimize therapeutic strategies. Current limitations in integrating multi-modal clinical, genomic, and imaging data hinder the development of predictive models for disease progression and treatment response. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-omics datasets from longitudinal patient cohorts, including whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to identify genomic signatures of disease heterogeneity, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate liver microenvironment interactions driving fibrogenesis and tumor evolution. A key innovation involves integrating spatially resolved transcriptomic data with computational fluid dynamics models to map hemodynamic changes in portal hypertension. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of 50+ TB of raw data, Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters for deep neural networks, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing therapeutic target robustness across 10,000+ virtual patient avatars. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early HCC detection, predictive models for MASH progression risk stratification, and in silico screening of combination therapies targeting immune-metabolic crosstalk. This resource-intensive approach addresses critical gaps in translating molecular insights into clinical decision support tools, with potential to reduce liver-related mortality through precision diagnostics and adaptive treatment paradigms. The computational pipelines developed will be shared openly to accelerate hepatology research, fostering collaboration across institutions addressing similar data integration challenges.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hepatology

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing thermal processing of liquid and semi-solid food products, a key bottleneck in achieving energy-efficient, nutrient-preserving manufacturing while ensuring microbial safety. Current empirical models for heat transfer and microbial inactivation in heterogeneous food matrices lack the resolution to predict localized temperature gradients or microbial survival probabilities at scale, leading to overprocessing, nutrient degradation, and excessive energy use. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), discrete element modeling (DEM), and machine learning to simulate coupled heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and microbial inactivation kinetics in complex food systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations of 3D multiphase flows within industrial-scale retorts and pasteurizers, coupled with stochastic modeling of microbial subpopulations under dynamic thermal stress. The workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for Navier-Stokes equations modified for non-Newtonian fluids, while neural networks trained on in silico data will predict optimal process parameters for novel food formulations. Validation will utilize experimental data from pilot-scale processing of model systems (e.g., particulate-laden sauces, protein gels) instrumented with embedded temperature loggers and microbial challenge studies. Successful implementation will generate predictive tools to reduce thermal processing times by 15-30% while maintaining safety margins, potentially decreasing energy consumption in commercial operations by an estimated 20%. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source modules adaptable to diverse food processing geometries, with particular relevance for nutrient-dense functional foods requiring precise thermal treatment. This work directly advances the USDA’s priority areas in sustainable food manufacturing by providing a physics-informed digital twin platform for process optimization, bridging critical gaps between food engineering principles and scalable industrial implementation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the development and implementation of manufacturing, packaging, storage, and distribution technologies and processes for food products. Includes instruction in food engineering, food preservation and handling, food preparation, food packaging and display, food storage and shipment, and related equipment and facilities design, operation, and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the neurobiological and psychosocial factors influencing treatment response heterogeneity in late-life depression (LLD), a leading cause of disability in older adults. Despite advances in geriatric psychiatry, up to 50% of patients exhibit poor response to first-line therapies, yet predictive biomarkers and personalized treatment algorithms remain elusive. To overcome limitations of small-sample studies, we propose a computational psychiatry approach integrating multi-modal data—including structural/functional neuroimaging, polygenic risk scores, electronic health records (EHRs), and real-time digital phenotyping—from a prospective cohort of 800 LLD patients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process and analyze this complex dataset, which encompasses >10 TB of neuroimaging data, genome-wide association study (GWAS) outputs, and longitudinal behavioral metrics. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to identify subtypes of treatment-resistant depression using transformer-based models for EHR text analysis, graph neural networks to map brain connectome dynamics, and ensemble methods to fuse biological and psychosocial predictors. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for voxel-based morphometry, GPU-accelerated training of 3D convolutional neural networks on amyloid-PET data, and distributed computing for Bayesian causal inference modeling of intervention outcomes. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated predictive model of antidepressant response with clinical deployment potential, (2) novel neuroinflammatory biomarkers detectable via diffusion tensor imaging, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for geriatric mental health prognostics. By elucidating mechanisms of treatment resistance, this work will directly inform precision psychiatry interventions while establishing scalable analytical frameworks for aging-related mental health research. The requested HPC allocation will enable transformative insights into LLD heterogeneity that cannot be achieved through conventional statistical approaches.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of mental and emotional disorders in the elderly, and to improve the psychiatric care of the elderly both in health and in disease.

abstract: Maternal and neonatal health outcomes are influenced by complex interactions between clinical, genetic, and socio-environmental factors, yet current predictive models often fail to account for this multifactorial complexity. This project seeks to address critical gaps in perinatal care by developing computational models that integrate heterogeneous datasets to predict adverse outcomes such as preterm birth, preeclampsia, and neonatal sepsis. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and socio-environmental variables from diverse patient populations. Machine learning algorithms, including ensemble and deep learning methods, will be employed to identify risk factors, stratify patient cohorts, and forecast complications with higher precision than traditional statistical approaches. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate the impact of targeted interventions—such as personalized prenatal care plans or community health programs—on reducing disparities in maternal and neonatal morbidity. The computational workflow will require parallel processing for training predictive models on terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters, and conducting sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for dynamic risk prediction, validated against retrospective clinical data, and actionable frameworks for real-time decision support in clinical settings. By elucidating how intersecting risk factors contribute to adverse outcomes, this work aims to advance equitable, evidence-based care strategies, reduce preventable complications, and improve long-term health trajectories for birthing individuals and newborns. The scale of data integration and the computational intensity of modeling multifactorial interactions necessitate robust HPC infrastructure to ensure feasibility, reproducibility, and translational impact.
cip_title: Maternal/ Child Health and Neonatal Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide prenatal care to pregnant women and to mothers and their newborn infants. Includes instruction in perinatal and newborn health assessment, stabilization, and care; pathophysiology of pregnancy, fetuses, and the newborn; clinical management of high-risk pregnancies and newborns; perinatal and neonatal technology and clinical procedures; and patient education.

abstract: Animal-assisted therapy (AAT) faces a critical research challenge in understanding the dynamic, multivariate interactions between patients, therapy animals, and clinical environments that drive therapeutic outcomes. Current studies often rely on small-sample observational data or qualitative assessments, limiting the ability to model complex behavioral, physiological, and environmental factors at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to predict optimal AAT configurations for specific patient populations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets and simulate intervention scenarios. The research will integrate anonymized patient records (including biometric data, session outcomes, and longitudinal progress metrics) with animal behavior logs (movement patterns, stress biomarkers, and trainer evaluations) using machine learning techniques. Neural networks and ensemble methods will be trained to identify non-linear relationships between therapy-animal traits, session structures, and patient responses across neurodevelopmental disorders and physical rehabilitation cases. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate human-animal interaction dynamics under varying clinical constraints. Computational demands include processing high-frequency biosensor data (≥100Hz sampling rates) from wearable devices, parallelized parameter optimization for intervention designs, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing protocol robustness. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to guide animal selection, session pacing, and environment customization based on patient profiles, significantly advancing evidence-based AAT practices. By establishing scalable computational methods for this interdisciplinary domain, the project will enable data-driven refinements to therapeutic protocols while preserving the individualized care ethos central to AAT. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the project’s terabyte-scale datasets, computationally intensive model architectures, and real-time simulation requirements that exceed the capacity of local institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares health and human service professionals to integrate the use of animals into their treatment practices in order to facilitate change in people with mental and physical disabilities. Includes instruction in psychology, psychology of disabilities, animal behavior, animal training, the human-animal bond, integration of animals into therapeutic settings, and ethical and cultural issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrative computational framework to analyze the ethical and pedagogical dimensions of clinical decision-making in health professions education. A critical challenge in training healthcare professionals lies in understanding how implicit biases, ethical reasoning, and humanities-based training influence clinical judgment, particularly in high-stakes, ambiguous scenarios. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to model the dynamic interplay of these factors at scale. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct large-scale simulations of clinical decision-making processes using agent-based modeling (ABM) and natural language processing (NLP). The ABM component will simulate diverse learner profiles, integrating variables such as prior ethics training, cultural competency, and exposure to humanities curricula, while NLP will analyze longitudinal datasets of clinical case discussions, reflective writing, and standardized patient interactions to identify patterns in ethical reasoning. The computational workflow will require parallel processing to manage thousands of simulated scenarios and iterative model refinement. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model of how specific educational interventions correlate with ethical decision-making competence, (2) identification of curricular elements that most effectively mitigate bias in clinical judgments, and (3) open-source tools for dynamically visualizing ethics training outcomes. By quantifying relationships between humanities-oriented education and clinical ethics performance, this work aims to provide evidence-based strategies for optimizing health professions curricula. The scale of data synthesis—encompassing over 10,000 historical case records and 500+ simulated training pathways—necessitates HPC capabilities for memory-intensive NLP tasks and concurrent simulation runs. This research directly aligns with institutional priorities to advance empirical methodologies in health humanities education while addressing accreditation requirements for competency-based assessment in clinical ethics.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in creating large-scale, immersive digital artworks that integrate real-time interactivity and dynamic generative systems. The core research problem lies in overcoming the limitations of conventional computing infrastructure, which struggles to process high-resolution visual data, multi-sensor inputs, and machine learning models simultaneously at the scale required for public installations. Current tools for interactive media art often sacrifice complexity or latency, restricting artists’ capacity to explore nuanced audience engagement or intricate algorithmic aesthetics. To bridge this gap, the project proposes a computational workflow combining real-time neural style transfer, physics-based simulations of virtual materials, and distributed rendering across multiple output channels. Custom code will integrate GPU-accelerated inference for vision-based audience tracking (using pose estimation and gesture recognition models) with procedural generation algorithms that adapt visual outputs to participant behavior. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data streams, reducing latency during multi-user interactions while maintaining 4K-resolution outputs across projection-mapped surfaces. Expected outcomes include a publicly exhibited installation exploring emergent narratives in human-AI collaboration, alongside an open-source framework for scalable interactive art production. This work advances methodological intersections between computational design and media theory, offering new models for resource-intensive creative practices. By demonstrating how HPC can expand the technical and conceptual boundaries of digital art, the project aims to influence both artistic methodologies and interdisciplinary discourse on computational aesthetics, fostering innovation in visual storytelling and participatory media environments.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Fine Arts and Art Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fine arts and art studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Veterinary dermatology faces significant challenges in diagnosing and managing complex, multifactorial skin diseases in diverse animal species, which often involve intricate interactions between genetic predispositions, environmental factors, and microbial communities. Current clinical approaches are limited in their ability to integrate and analyze high-dimensional datasets—such as host genomics, metagenomic profiles, and longitudinal clinical records—to derive actionable insights. This project proposes to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive computational models for personalized diagnosis and treatment optimization. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) constructing machine learning frameworks to identify biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response in atopic dermatitis and autoimmune skin disorders across companion animals and exotic species, and (2) simulating host-microbiome interactions through agent-based modeling to predict how therapeutic interventions alter microbial ecology and skin barrier function. HPC capabilities will enable the processing of multi-terabyte datasets from transcriptomic sequencing, mass spectrometry-based proteomics, and electronic health records, while facilitating large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of drug penetration through species-specific skin morphologies. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for clinical risk stratification, optimized therapeutic protocols tailored to individual patients, and novel insights into conserved pathological mechanisms across taxa. By enabling the integration of heterogeneous data types at unprecedented scale, this work will advance precision medicine in veterinary dermatology, reduce trial-and-error treatment approaches, and provide a computational framework applicable to rare or poorly characterized dermatologic conditions. The requested resources will directly support iterative model training, validation against clinical outcomes from partner veterinary hospitals, and the creation of publicly accessible databases to accelerate translational research in this field.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing energy-efficient hardware-software co-design for next-generation embedded systems, which require real-time processing of complex computational workloads under stringent power constraints. Current simulation frameworks lack the scalability to evaluate emerging architectures that integrate heterogeneous computing elements (e.g., custom accelerators, reconfigurable logic, and low-power CPUs) with adaptive machine learning algorithms. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity modeling platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-objective design spaces spanning hardware configurations, task scheduling policies, and dynamic voltage-frequency scaling strategies. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation for system-level behavior with machine learning-driven surrogate models to approximate physical-layer circuit characteristics, enabling rapid exploration of Pareto-optimal solutions. Parallelized parameter sweeps will be implemented using MPI to assess design tradeoffs across 10^4–10^5 configurations, while deep reinforcement learning agents trained on HPC clusters will identify adaptive control policies for runtime resource management. Expected outcomes include a publicly available benchmark suite quantifying energy-performance tradeoffs for edge computing architectures, novel algorithms for hardware-aware neural network partitioning, and predictive models linking microarchitectural features to application-specific efficiency metrics. This work will provide critical insights for designing sustainable embedded AI systems, with applications in autonomous robotics, smart infrastructure, and biomedical devices. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome memory and throughput limitations in existing single-node simulations, reducing time-to-solution by two orders of magnitude.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance clinical decision-making models for physician assistants (PAs) in underserved and rural care settings. The research addresses the challenge of diagnostic and treatment variability in resource-limited environments, where PAs often operate with constrained access to specialist support or real-time data. By integrating large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets, demographic data, and clinical outcome metrics, we aim to develop predictive algorithms that identify high-risk patients, optimize treatment pathways, and reduce disparities in care delivery. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) for extracting clinical insights from unstructured provider notes, federated learning to preserve patient privacy across multi-institutional datasets, and agent-based modeling to simulate care delivery scenarios under varying resource constraints. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale data volumes, parallelize computationally intensive tasks, and iteratively refine models through ensemble machine learning techniques. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for conditions disproportionately affecting underserved populations (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, maternal health complications) and open-source clinical decision support modules tailored to PA workflows. The project also proposes benchmarking these tools against existing clinical guidelines to quantify potential reductions in diagnostic latency and unnecessary referrals. By aligning computational outputs with PA training in family medicine, behavioral health, and community care, this work has the potential to directly enhance point-of-care decision-making while informing scalable strategies for equitable healthcare delivery. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, secure data storage compliant with HIPAA standards, and collaborative platforms for interdisciplinary validation involving PA clinicians, epidemiologists, and computational researchers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice medicine, including diagnoses and treatment therapies, under the supervision of a physician. Includes instruction in the basic medical and clinical sciences and specialized preparation in fields such as family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, gynecology, general surgery, psychiatry, and behavioral medicine; the delivery of health care services to homebound patients, rural populations, and underserved populations; and community health services.

abstract: Industrial safety in complex manufacturing environments requires the integration of dynamic human, mechanical, and environmental factors to prevent accidents. Traditional risk assessment models often fail to capture real-time interactions and emergent behaviors, leading to gaps in hazard mitigation. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-agent interactions, ergonomic stressors, and system-wide failure cascades in industrial settings. By employing agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics for contaminant dispersion analysis, and machine learning techniques trained on large-scale sensor datasets, the research aims to identify latent risks and optimize safety protocols. The simulations will integrate heterogeneous data streams, including worker mobility patterns, equipment telemetry, and environmental sensors, to model scenarios such as equipment malfunctions, human error, and toxic exposure events. Expected outcomes include predictive risk analytics tools capable of real-time hazard detection, data-driven recommendations for process redesign, and validated thresholds for safety-critical parameters. The computational intensity of modeling thousands of concurrent variables across spatial and temporal scales necessitates access to parallelized computing architectures and GPU-accelerated nodes. Successful implementation will advance the field of industrial safety technology by enabling proactive risk management strategies, reducing workplace injuries, and informing regulatory standards through evidence-based simulations. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on system safety engineering while avoiding overlap with excluded engineering disciplines through its emphasis on human factors and operational process safety.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing and enforcing industrial safety standards to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in industrial processes, industrial hygiene, injury prevention, toxicology, ergonomics, risk analysis, system and process safety, safety performance measurement, human factors, human behavior, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Aging populations present unique challenges in geriatric dentistry, particularly regarding the interplay between polypharmacy, systemic diseases, and oral health deterioration. Geriatric patients frequently experience medication-induced xerostomia, altered salivary composition, and accelerated dental caries or periodontal disease, yet predictive frameworks to identify high-risk individuals and optimize care remain underdeveloped. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multimodal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), medication logs, intraoral 3D scans, and salivary biomarker profiles—to model the synergistic effects of polypharmacy and aging on oral health outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process heterogeneous data at scale, including natural language processing (NLP) of unstructured clinical notes to extract medication side effects and dental outcomes, coupled with machine learning (ML) algorithms to identify risk patterns. Computational models will be trained to predict caries progression and soft-tissue pathology using dynamic Bayesian networks and ensemble classifiers, accounting for time-dependent variables such as medication adherence and comorbid disease trajectories. The expected outcomes include a risk stratification tool to guide personalized treatment plans and interdisciplinary care coordination between dentists and physicians. By elucidating medication-related oral health risks, this work aims to reduce preventable dental morbidity in geriatric populations, lower healthcare costs, and establish a computational framework adaptable to other age-related oral-systemic health interactions. The scale of data integration and iterative model training necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve clinically actionable precision within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of geriatric patients. Includes instruction in aging, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, geriatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and patient management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing industrial safety protocols in high-risk manufacturing environments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial processes involving complex machinery, hazardous materials, and human-machine interactions present dynamic risks that are challenging to model using traditional risk assessment tools. Current methods often fail to account for real-time operational variability, ergonomic stressors, and cascading failure scenarios, leading to gaps in proactive hazard mitigation. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning to predict safety-critical events under diverse operational conditions. The agent-based component will simulate worker behavior and equipment interactions, while CFD models will analyze chemical dispersion and thermal risks in confined spaces. Machine learning algorithms, trained on historical incident data and sensor-generated operational logs, will identify latent risk patterns and predict failure probabilities. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of parallelized simulations across thousands of scenario permutations, including rare but high-consequence events. Expected outcomes include a predictive safety analytics toolkit capable of recommending context-aware safety interventions, optimizing evacuation routes, and dynamically adjusting risk thresholds based on real-time sensor inputs. This work will advance the field of industrial safety technology by enabling data-driven, scenario-adaptive safety protocols, reducing workplace injuries, and minimizing downtime in sectors such as chemical manufacturing and heavy machinery operations. The resulting models and datasets will be disseminated to industry partners and regulatory bodies to inform safety standards and training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing and enforcing industrial safety standards to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in industrial processes, industrial hygiene, injury prevention, toxicology, ergonomics, risk analysis, system and process safety, safety performance measurement, human factors, human behavior, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of legal reasoning in judicial decisions across multiple jurisdictions, focusing on how cultural, historical, and linguistic factors shape the interpretation of constitutional rights. While legal scholarship traditionally relies on qualitative methods, the increasing availability of digitized court opinions and metadata presents an opportunity to quantitatively model complex patterns in judicial decision-making at scale. The research problem centers on identifying latent biases and inconsistencies in the application of legal principles, particularly in cases involving emerging technologies or sociopolitical conflicts. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, transformer-based language models will be fine-tuned to classify legal arguments, map citation networks, and detect semantic shifts in key constitutional concepts over time. Computational legal realism frameworks will be employed to correlate judicial outcomes with sociodemographic variables and institutional contexts. The project requires HPC capabilities to process terabyte-scale legal text corpora spanning federal and state courts in the United States and select international jurisdictions, as well as to train deep learning architectures for multi-task legal analysis. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational legal studies, longitudinal visualizations of doctrinal change, and statistical models quantifying the relationship between judicial language and external societal factors. By bridging legal theory with data-driven computational methods, this work aims to advance empirical understandings of law as a dynamic social system while providing actionable insights for legal practitioners, policymakers, and scholars navigating interdisciplinary challenges at the intersection of law, technology, and culture.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on law and legal issues from the perspective of the social sciences and humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and systemic mechanisms underlying metabolic disorders in ruminants, with a focus on dairy cattle experiencing ketosis—a prevalent and economically significant condition in livestock agriculture. Current experimental approaches to study these disorders face limitations in resolving dynamic, multi-scale interactions between hormonal regulation, tissue-specific metabolism, and systemic pathophysiology. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) with physiologically based pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PBPK-PD) models. These models will simulate hormone-receptor binding kinetics, hepatic lipid metabolism, and inter-organ crosstalk under varying metabolic stressors. Machine learning algorithms will identify critical regulatory nodes and predict biomarkers for early disease detection. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of stochastic molecular dynamics simulations (using tools like GROMACS) and large-scale parameter optimization for organ-level models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets to modulate hepatic ketogenesis, predictive models of metabolic resilience, and a publicly accessible database of ruminant-specific physiological parameters. This work will advance precision veterinary medicine by enabling targeted interventions, reducing livestock morbidity, and improving agricultural sustainability. The developed computational pipelines will also provide a template for studying analogous metabolic syndromes in non-mammalian species, broadening translational applications in veterinary physiology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the functional dynamics of animal biological systems and their relationship to the diagnosis and treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in mammalian and non-mammalian physiology, laboratory physiology, physiological responses to the environment, endocrinology, animal biotechnology, mechanisms of hormone action, organ systems, metabolism, and pathophysiology.

abstract: Turfgrass systems play a critical role in agricultural sustainability, urban landscapes, and recreational industries, yet optimizing their resilience to biotic and abiotic stressors remains a persistent challenge. Current approaches to cultivar development and management practices often rely on resource-intensive field trials, which are limited in scalability and fail to capture complex genotype-environment interactions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model turfgrass responses to environmental variables, disease pressures, and management regimes at unprecedented resolution. We propose a two-phase computational approach. First, genomic and phenotypic data from diverse turfgrass varieties will be integrated into machine learning frameworks to identify genetic markers associated with drought tolerance, disease resistance, and nutrient use efficiency. Second, agent-based models will simulate turfgrass growth dynamics under varying climate scenarios, incorporating soil microbiomes, irrigation patterns, and maintenance practices. These models will be parameterized using multi-omics datasets and validated against experimental field data from controlled trials. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale genomic datasets, training deep neural networks, and running iterative simulations necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with parallel processing capabilities and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for accelerating the development of climate-resilient turfgrass cultivars and data-driven recommendations for precision turf management. By reducing reliance on empirical trial-and-error approaches, this research aims to decrease water and pesticide use in turf systems while maintaining functional performance—a critical advancement for agricultural sustainability. The resulting computational pipelines will be shared as open-source resources to support broader innovation in plant sciences.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on turfgrasses and related groundcover plants and prepares individuals to develop ornamental or recreational grasses and related products; plant, transplant, and manage grassed areas; and to produce and store turf used for transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable plant sciences, genetics of grasses, turf science, use analysis, turf management, and related economics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic reorganization of cellular architectures during tissue morphogenesis, with a focus on identifying biomechanical principles governing cell shape transitions in epithelial monolayers. A central challenge in cell biology lies in understanding how spatially heterogeneous mechanical forces, mediated by cytoskeletal networks and cell-cell adhesion complexes, coordinate large-scale tissue remodeling. Traditional experimental approaches lack the resolution to model emergent behaviors arising from subcellular interactions across multicellular systems. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale 3D modeling framework integrating finite element analysis of actomyosin contractility with vertex-based simulations of epithelial sheet dynamics. The computational workflow will parameterize cell-scale biophysical properties—derived from live-imaging datasets of Drosophila dorsal closure—to simulate force propagation across thousands of interacting cells. HPC resources are essential for executing parallelized simulations that capture stochastic variations in cytoskeletal organization and adhesion dynamics over developmental timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of stress distribution patterns preceding topological defects in epithelia and quantitative assessment of how extracellular matrix compliance modulates collective cell migration. This work will establish an open-source platform for simulating mechanobiological feedback in developing tissues, with direct applications to understanding congenital malformations linked to cytoskeletal dysregulation. By bridging molecular-scale mechanics with tissue-level phenotypes, the project advances foundational knowledge in cellular morphogenesis while providing computational tools applicable to diverse anatomical systems.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_title: Cell/ Cellular Biology and Anatomical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cell/cellular biology and anatomical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of image-guided interventions in interventional radiology demands advanced computational tools to optimize procedural accuracy, patient safety, and therapeutic outcomes. Current limitations in real-time processing of high-resolution multimodal imaging data (e.g., fluoroscopy, CT, MRI) and the integration of heterogeneous datasets—including patient-specific anatomy, device tracking, and hemodynamic parameters—restrict the ability to predict procedural challenges or personalize treatment strategies. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to model, simulate, and analyze image-guided therapies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) creating patient-specific, biomechanically accurate simulations of vascular and non-vascular interventions (e.g., angioplasty, embolization, abscess drainage) by integrating 3D reconstructions from clinical imaging with finite-element modeling of device-tissue interactions, and (2) training machine learning algorithms to predict procedural outcomes, such as stent malposition or post-embolization ischemia, using multi-institutional datasets. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated processing for real-time image segmentation, hybrid finite-element/discrete-element simulations for device navigation, and federated learning to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale simulations (>10^6 mesh elements per case), iterative optimization of neural networks, and parallel processing of retrospective clinical data (>10,000 anonymized cases). Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for complication risk stratification, open-source simulation tools for procedural training, and optimized imaging protocols to reduce radiation exposure. By enhancing the precision of image-guided therapies, this work aims to establish a computational foundation for next-generation interventional radiology practices, directly improving clinical decision-making and patient outcomes in minimally invasive treatments.
cip_definition: Research focused on image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages. Does NOT require prior completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between cognitive development and environmental influences in early childhood using advanced computational modeling techniques. Current theoretical frameworks in developmental psychology lack granular mechanistic explanations for how individual differences in neural maturation interact with environmental stimuli (e.g., caregiver interactions, educational exposures) to shape emerging executive functioning skills. To address this gap, we propose developing a series of neural network models that simulate developmental trajectories of working memory and cognitive flexibility in children aged 3–8 years. The computational approach integrates longitudinal behavioral datasets (N=1,200+ participants across 4 existing cohorts) with biologically inspired reinforcement learning architectures to model how synaptic pruning rates and reward prediction errors co-evolve with environmental feedback. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) Bayesian parameter estimation of neurodevelopmental timetables using hierarchical models with 10⁶+ interacting variables, (2) parallelized sensitivity analyses across 500+ simulated developmental pathways under varying environmental conditions, and (3) real-time integration of multimodal data streams (eye-tracking, fNIRS, and structured behavioral assessments) through adaptive hybrid machine learning systems. The project will produce the first computational architecture capable of simulating individual differences in cognitive development at sub-second temporal resolution while maintaining ecological validity across diverse socioeconomic contexts. Expected outcomes include identifying critical neurocomputational thresholds for environmental intervention efficacy and generating testable hypotheses about sensitive periods for specific executive function components. By bridging developmental theory with computational psychiatry methods, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for predicting atypical developmental trajectories and optimizing early learning environments through mechanism-based modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from infancy through childhood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of LGBTQ+ cultural narratives and community formation through computational analysis of large-scale multimedia archives. Current research in Gay/Lesbian Studies often relies on qualitative methods, limiting the scope to isolated case studies. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze digitized collections spanning literature, visual art, film, and activist publications from the 20th and 21st centuries. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) for thematic modeling of texts, computer vision techniques to identify visual motifs in art and film, and network analysis to trace collaborative relationships among creators and organizations. These approaches require HPC capabilities due to the volume of data (over 10 million text pages and 500,000 visual artifacts) and the computational intensity of transformer-based models for cross-modal pattern detection. Expected outcomes include mapping shifts in LGBTQ+ representation across media, identifying understudied contributors to cultural movements, and uncovering intersections between artistic production and legal/policy milestones. The findings will advance scholarly understanding of how marginalized communities negotiate visibility in hostile environments while informing contemporary efforts to preserve LGBTQ+ heritage. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to establish new methodologies for studying identity-based cultural phenomena at scale.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on homosexuality in history, society, politics, and cultural life; usually with an emphasis on the modern emergence of gays and lesbians as a sociocultural minority movement, the identification of social, literary, and artistic themes and the definition of, and public policy and legal issues surrounding, the gay and lesbian community.

abstract: The increasing complexity of autoimmune disease diagnostics in primary care settings presents a critical challenge for physician assistants (PAs), particularly when serving rural and underserved populations where specialist access is limited. This project proposes to develop a machine learning (ML)-driven clinical decision support system (CDSS) optimized for PAs, leveraging multi-omic data integration to improve early detection of atypical autoimmune presentations. Current diagnostic tools often lack specificity in general practice environments, leading to delayed referrals and increased morbidity. We will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), serum proteomics, and patient-reported outcome measures from 15 regional clinics serving health professional shortage areas. A novel ensemble learning architecture will be trained on GPU-accelerated nodes to identify subtle patterns across immunological, demographic, and clinical variables that may escape conventional diagnostic heuristics. Computational experiments will compare neural ordinary differential equation models against transformer-based approaches for temporal symptom progression analysis. The resulting framework will be validated against gold-standard rheumatology assessments while maintaining interpretability constraints essential for PA workflow integration. Successful implementation could reduce diagnostic latency by 40-60% in preliminary simulations, significantly impacting outcomes for conditions like seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and lupus variants. This work bridges clinical immunology, computational biomedicine, and primary care practice, directly supporting PAs’ expanding role in managing complex chronic conditions within resource-constrained settings. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale federated learning across distributed clinical sites while preserving patient privacy through secure, containerized data pipelines. Outcomes will include open-source diagnostic algorithms optimized for edge computing devices commonly used in mobile clinics and community health centers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice medicine, including diagnoses and treatment therapies, under the supervision of a physician. Includes instruction in the basic medical and clinical sciences and specialized preparation in fields such as family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, gynecology, general surgery, psychiatry, and behavioral medicine; the delivery of health care services to homebound patients, rural populations, and underserved populations; and community health services.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of spatially dynamic extracellular pH gradients in modulating cellular communication within tumor microenvironments, a critical yet underexplored factor in cancer progression and therapeutic resistance. Traditional studies in molecular medicine have focused on biochemical signaling, but emerging evidence suggests that physical microgradients—specifically proton concentration fluctuations driven by metabolic activity—act as non-canonical regulators of intercellular behavior. We hypothesize that these pH gradients create adaptive signaling "landscapes" that influence drug permeability, immune cell infiltration, and metastatic potential. To test this, we will develop a multiscale computational model integrating real-time proton diffusion dynamics, cellular metabolic states, and microenvironmental topology. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate three-dimensional tumor spheroids at subcellular resolution, capturing stochastic interactions between pH-sensitive ion channels, extracellular matrix composition, and hypoxia-driven metabolic shifts. The model will leverage GPU-accelerated finite element analysis for diffusion-reaction equations and agent-based frameworks to represent heterogeneous cell populations. Experimental validation datasets from microfluidic tumor models and pH-sensitive fluorescent reporters will iteratively refine simulation parameters. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of pH-mediated therapeutic vulnerability zones within tumors and identification of microenvironmental conditions that amplify the efficacy of pH-modulating adjuvants. This work bridges biophysical principles with molecular medicine, offering a novel paradigm for targeting physical microgradients in precision oncology. By characterizing how spatial pH dynamics encode cellular decision-making, the results could inform the design of adaptive drug delivery systems and improve prognostic models for treatment resistance. The computational framework will be openly shared as a modular platform for studying other physicochemical gradients in pathological contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the molecular and cellular basis of disease, and the application of this knowledge to the development of new clinical and diagnostic tools, medications, and therapies. Includes instruction in cell biology, molecular biology, physiology, pharmacology, biochemistry, genetics, pathology, molecular immunology, research and quantitative methods, and biomedical research computing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized learning interventions for students with developmental delays, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze heterogeneous educational data. Students with developmental delays exhibit highly variable learning trajectories influenced by interacting cognitive, social, and physiological factors. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) rely on manual, time-intensive assessments that struggle to integrate multidimensional data or adapt dynamically to student progress. The proposed research will address this gap by constructing machine learning models trained on longitudinal datasets spanning behavioral observations, academic performance metrics, physiological sensor data, and teacher-reported outcomes. These models will simulate learning pathways under varied intervention strategies, identifying optimal sequences of instructional supports tailored to individual profiles. HPC resources are essential for processing high-frequency sensor data, running parallelized parameter sweeps to test intervention combinations, and performing real-time updates to models as new student data is acquired. Key computational challenges include managing sparse, noisy input streams and ensuring interpretable model outputs for educator use. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating data-driven IEP recommendations, validated through collaboration with special education teachers in classroom trials. By enabling rapid analysis of complex developmental patterns, this work aims to reduce the latency between student assessment and intervention deployment while preserving the critical role of educator expertise. The project will contribute computational methodologies to bridge learning sciences and classroom practice in special education, with broader implications for scalable, equitable resource allocation in inclusive educational settings.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals Who are Developmentally Delayed
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults who exhibit slow social, physical, cognitive, or emotional growth patterns related to age, or a combination of such factors that affect learning, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identification of developmental delay patterns, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising developmentally delayed students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in biology teacher education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze complex student learning processes in biological systems.
