While biology education research has advanced in identifying pedagogical strategies, current methods often lack the computational power to simulate dynamic, large-scale interactions between instructional approaches, student cognition, and conceptual understanding of multidimensional topics like ecosystems, genetics, or cellular processes. This limitation hinders the development of targeted, evidence-based training tools for pre-service and in-service biology teachers. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate classroom learning environments. The ABM framework will represent students as agents with variable prior knowledge, engagement levels, and problem-solving strategies, interacting with teacher-led interventions modeled after empirically validated biology education techniques. Large-scale parameter sweeps will be conducted to evaluate how different instructional sequences affect conceptual mastery across diverse student populations. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze historical datasets of student performance and teacher feedback to identify predictive patterns in instructional efficacy. By deploying these models on HPC clusters, we aim to process terabytes of interaction data and run thousands of parallel simulations, enabling real-time optimization of teaching strategies. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational platform for prototyping biology lesson plans, predictive analytics tools to personalize teacher training, and evidence-based guidelines for addressing misconceptions in core biological concepts. This work will directly inform the design of adaptive professional development modules for biology educators, ultimately enhancing their capacity to foster deeper student learning in K-12 and undergraduate settings. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome current limitations in simulation fidelity and data processing speed, ensuring robust results that can transform biology education practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach biology programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to model and simulate the structural, material, and spatial dynamics of large-scale sculptural installations, addressing a critical gap in the integration of advanced computational methods within sculpture practice. Traditional approaches to designing monumental or geometrically complex sculptures rely on iterative physical prototyping and manual material testing, which are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in their capacity to predict long-term structural behavior under dynamic environmental conditions. We propose a hybrid methodology combining finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML)-driven material behavior prediction, and generative 3D modeling to optimize the design and fabrication of sculptures using materials such as metal alloys, biodegradable composites, and tension-based assemblies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-physics simulations that analyze stress distribution, thermal expansion, and material degradation over time, particularly for sculptures intended for public outdoor installations. Additionally, neural networks will be trained on datasets of material properties and historical structural failures to recommend adaptive design modifications. The computational pipeline will interface with digital fabrication tools, enabling real-time feedback between virtual models and physical output. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for reducing material waste in sculpture production, predictive models for longevity of experimental media, and a publicly accessible database of simulation templates tailored to artistic workflows. This work bridges computational engineering and sculptural practice, offering new methods to explore form, scale, and material innovation while addressing sustainability challenges in the visual arts. By democratizing access to HPC-driven design validation, the project aims to expand the technical and creative possibilities for sculptors working with complex geometries or unconventional materials.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by creating three-dimensional art works. Includes instruction in the analysis of form in space; round and relief concepts; sculptural composition; modern and experimental methods; different media such as clay, plaster, wood, stone, and metal; techniques such as carving, molding, welding, casting, and modeling; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational text analysis of Czech literary and historical documents, with a focus on tracing the evolution of syntactic and semantic patterns in 19th- and early 20th-century Czech prose. While Czech philology has a rich tradition of manual textual analysis, large-scale quantitative studies of language change remain underdeveloped due to the computational challenges of processing morphologically complex Czech texts at scale. The research will utilize a curated corpus of digitized novels, essays, and periodicals (approximately 10 million tokens) to investigate how grammatical structures and lexical choices shifted in response to sociopolitical transformations, such as the Czech National Revival and the rise of modernist movements. Key computational methods include the application of transformer-based language models (fine-tuned for historical Czech) to automate morphological tagging, dependency parsing, and semantic role labeling across temporal strata. Parallelized workflows will enable systematic comparisons of syntactic complexity, metaphor density, and register variation using statistical models and graph-based representations of co-occurrence networks. The project also aims to develop an open-access toolkit for diachronic Czech corpus linguistics, integrating existing annotation standards with computational workflows optimized for HPC environments. Expected outcomes include novel insights into the relationship between linguistic innovation and cultural identity in Czech literary history, as well as methodological advancements in processing under-resourced Slavic languages. By enabling large-scale, reproducible analysis of Czech textual heritage, this work will support broader interdisciplinary research in digital humanities, Slavic linguistics, and transnational literary studies, while preserving computational resources for future scholarship through publicly shared datasets and pipelines.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Czech language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The development of efficient quantum-enhanced nanoscale energy systems presents a critical challenge at the intersection of applied physics and engineering, where traditional thermodynamic frameworks fail to capture the interplay of quantum coherence, nonequilibrium dynamics, and nanoscale heat transport. This project addresses the computational bottleneck in modeling energy transduction processes within hybrid quantum-classical systems, particularly focusing on optically active nanostructures coupled to superconducting resonators. Current analytical methods cannot resolve the timescales required to optimize energy transfer efficiency while accounting for quantum fluctuations and decoherence effects across multiple physical domains. The proposed research employs large-scale numerical simulations combining time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for electron-photon interactions, stochastic Lindblad master equations for open quantum system dynamics, and finite-element modeling of thermal gradients in superconducting substrates. These coupled simulations will be implemented on high-performance computing clusters using a hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization scheme to handle the exponential scaling of quantum state spaces with system size. Key objectives include identifying geometric and material parameters that maximize coherent energy transfer under cryogenic conditions and developing machine learning surrogates to accelerate device optimization. The computational demands arise from the need to simulate 10^4–10^5 interacting quantum states across picosecond-to-nanosecond trajectories while maintaining nanoscale spatial resolution. Successful implementation will yield validated design principles for quantum-enhanced energy harvesting systems, with potential applications in photonic computing and ultra-low-power sensor networks. This work establishes a computational framework to bridge quantum thermodynamics with practical nanodevice engineering, addressing a critical gap in the scalable implementation of quantum-coherent energy technologies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the use of physics principles in the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems and other scientific applications. Includes instruction in high- and low-temperature phenomena, computational physics, superconductivity, applied thermodynamics, molecular and particle physics applications, and space science research.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate the spread of chronic diseases in urban communities and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of preventive health interventions. Chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension disproportionately affect underserved populations, yet resource allocation for community-level prevention remains suboptimal due to gaps in predicting dynamic interactions between social determinants, health behaviors, and local policy constraints. The research will integrate multi-source data—including electronic health records, geospatial environmental exposures, and community survey responses—to parameterize a high-resolution simulation of disease transmission and intervention outcomes. Computational demands are substantial, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run thousands of parallelized simulations that account for heterogeneous population attributes, stochastic behavioral patterns, and time-dependent policy scenarios. Models will leverage machine learning techniques to calibrate parameters from real-world datasets and quantify uncertainties in intervention efficacy. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool to identify priority neighborhoods and intervention types (e.g., mobile screening clinics, subsidized nutrition programs) that maximize reductions in disease incidence per allocated dollar. This work directly addresses the program’s focus on community health planning by bridging epidemiological theory with practical resource allocation challenges. The computational framework will be designed for adaptability to other urban settings, with open-source code and documentation to empower local health departments. By simulating the long-term impacts of preventive strategies under budget constraints, this project aims to advance evidence-based approaches for reducing health disparities while optimizing finite public health resources. Successful implementation will depend on HPC capabilities to manage complex, memory-intensive simulations and enable rapid scenario testing for stakeholder engagement.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to plan and manage health services in local community settings, including the coordination of related support services, government agencies, and private resources. Includes instruction in public health, community health services and delivery, health behavior and cultural factors, local government operations, human services, health communication and promotion, health services administration in local settings, environmental health, preventive and comparative medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics, family and community health, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of innovative ceramic materials and firing techniques through computational modeling and simulation. While traditional ceramic arts rely on iterative physical experimentation to optimize clay bodies, glazes, and kiln conditions, the inherent variability of materials and thermal processes often leads to inefficiencies in time, energy, and resource use. This research addresses these challenges by constructing physics-based models to simulate the molecular behavior of ceramic materials during drying, oxidation, and vitrification, as well as the thermodynamic dynamics of kiln environments. Multiscale modeling approaches will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for macro-scale thermal stress distribution and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to predict phase transitions in glaze compositions under varying atmospheric conditions. These models will be validated against empirical data collected from controlled kiln firings and material characterization techniques such as X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy. By coupling HPC-enabled simulations with machine learning algorithms, the project aims to identify optimal material combinations and firing protocols that minimize defects, reduce energy consumption, and expand aesthetic possibilities for ceramic artists. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access computational toolkit for predicting glaze interactions and thermal outcomes, as well as novel frameworks for designing hybrid ceramic-media artworks incorporating digitally modeled structural elements. This interdisciplinary approach bridges material science, computational thermodynamics, and studio practice, offering transformative potential for both artistic innovation and sustainable resource management in ceramic arts education and professional practice.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by producing art works out of clay and similar materials. Includes instruction in handbuilt and wheel thrown techniques; molding; slips and glazes; trimming and decorating; firing and kiln operation; oxidation; mixed media; ceramic murals; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the microbial dynamics underlying periodontal disease, a pervasive public health concern with significant implications for systemic health. Despite advances in preventive dental hygiene practices, the complexity of oral microbial communities and their interactions with host immune responses remains poorly characterized, limiting the development of targeted interventions. Current clinical and laboratory methods struggle to model the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of biofilm formation or predict how specific hygiene protocols alter microbial resilience. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate oral microbiome dynamics under varying hygiene regimens. The ABM framework will incorporate empirical data from clinical plaque samples, metagenomic sequencing, and biochemical assays to represent microbial species interactions, nutrient availability, and the effects of antimicrobial agents. ML algorithms will then identify patterns in biofilm resilience and predict optimal intervention strategies. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to model millions of microbial agents across diverse environmental conditions while accounting for patient-specific variables such as saliva composition and immune status. Expected outcomes include the identification of microbial biomarkers predictive of disease progression, the optimization of personalized hygiene protocols, and the development of decision-support tools for clinicians. By elucidating mechanistic links between hygiene practices and microbial behavior, this work aims to bridge gaps in preventive care, reduce health disparities in oral disease outcomes, and inform the next generation of dental hygiene education. The computational pipelines developed will be shared openly to support translational research in preventive oral health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean teeth and apply preventive materials, provide oral health education and treatment counseling to patients, identify oral pathologies and injuries, and manage dental hygiene practices. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, microbiology, and pathology; dental hygiene theory and techniques; cleaning equipment operation and maintenance; dental materials; radiology; patient education and counseling; office management; supervised clinical training; and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal studies, an emerging interdisciplinary field that applies quantitative and computational methods to analyze complex legal systems. The research problem centers on the challenge of modeling large-scale, dynamic interactions within legal frameworks, particularly in contexts where traditional doctrinal analysis fails to capture systemic behaviors. Specifically, the project will investigate how algorithmic decision-making tools, when integrated into legal processes, influence the predictability and equity of outcomes in administrative law systems. The computational approach involves constructing agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate interactions between legal actors (e.g., regulators, litigants, AI-driven adjudication systems) under varying policy conditions. These models will integrate natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze historical case law and regulatory texts, training on terabyte-scale datasets of judicial opinions and administrative rulings. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, manage memory-intensive NLP tasks, and optimize machine learning classifiers that detect latent biases in synthetic decision trajectories. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating the second-order effects of AI integration in legal systems, with applications to regulatory design and procedural fairness audits. The project will also produce open-source tools for legal system simulation, enabling reproducibility in computational legal research. By bridging gaps between legal theory, complex systems science, and computational modeling, this work aims to establish methodological foundations for evidence-based legal process design while addressing ethical and operational risks associated with algorithmic governance.
cip_definition: Any program in law, legal services, and legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance forensic nursing research by analyzing complex, multimodal datasets related to violence-related injuries and associated medicolegal evidence. Forensic nurses face critical challenges in identifying subtle injury patterns, predicting patient outcomes, and correlating clinical findings with legal requirements for evidence integrity. Current manual methods for synthesizing clinical, demographic, and forensic data are time-intensive and lack the capacity to detect nuanced relationships across large-scale datasets. The proposed research will develop machine learning models to 1) identify predictive biomarkers of injury recidivism using electronic health records and forensic documentation, 2) optimize evidence collection protocols through computational simulations of biological sample degradation under varying environmental conditions, and 3) create natural language processing tools to automate forensic report analysis for legal testimony consistency. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams—including 3D wound imaging, toxicology reports, and longitudinal patient histories—while maintaining chain-of-custody data security requirements. Computational experiments will utilize federated learning frameworks to preserve patient privacy across multi-institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for clinical decision support, evidence-based guidelines for biological sample preservation timelines, and open-source tools for forensic documentation quality assessment. This work directly addresses gaps in violence prevention strategies and forensic practice standardization, with potential to enhance both patient care and legal outcomes. By integrating computational science with forensic nursing expertise, the project aims to establish scalable methodologies for translating complex clinical-forensic correlations into actionable insights for healthcare and legal systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the law and forensic science to nursing practice and collaborate with other professionals for the care of victims and the prosecution of criminals. Includes instruction in advanced physical assessment, evidence collection and preservation, forensic anthropology, legal testimony, medicolegal investigation, pathophysiology, pathohistology, pharmacology, and violence prevention.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance trauma counseling research by analyzing complex interactions between neurobiological, psychological, and contextual factors influencing trauma recovery. Current trauma interventions exhibit variable efficacy, partly due to heterogeneous manifestations of trauma-related disorders such as PTSD and gaps in understanding how individual differences in neurobiology, trauma history, and social environments shape treatment outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating multimodal datasets—including neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), genetic markers, clinical assessments, and longitudinal patient-reported outcomes—to model predictors of therapeutic success. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale neuroimaging data, training machine learning (ML) models to identify subtypes of trauma response, and simulating neurodynamic changes associated with evidence-based interventions. Computational workflows will include (1) preprocessing and feature extraction from imaging data using tools such as FSL and FreeSurfer; (2) ML-driven clustering to delineate trauma phenotypes based on neural, genetic, and behavioral profiles; and (3) biophysically informed neural circuit simulations to quantify how trauma disrupts functional connectivity and how interventions may restore adaptive patterns. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to overcome limitations of traditional statistical methods in handling high-dimensional, multilevel data. Anticipated outcomes include predictive biomarkers for personalized treatment matching, mechanistic insights into trauma-related neural plasticity, and open-source computational tools for the trauma research community. This work will directly inform the development of trauma-sensitive, precision counseling frameworks while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in bridging clinical practice and computational neuroscience within health professions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on understanding elements of traumatic exposure, trauma-sensitive care, and crisis intervention. Includes instruction in disaster response, grief and loss counseling, crisis intervention and management, trauma counseling, neurobiology of trauma, PTSD and combat-related trauma, relational trauma and treatment of trauma-related disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling complex, multi-system biological interactions across scales to understand emergent properties in organismal resilience. Traditional reductionist approaches often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between physiological, developmental, and environmental factors that collectively shape biological outcomes. We propose an integrative computational framework to simulate cross-scale interactions—from molecular signaling cascades to organism-level stress responses—within a unified high-performance computing (HPC) environment. The research will focus on a model system integrating data from stress-induced hormonal regulation, tissue repair mechanisms, and metabolic adaptation in vertebrates exposed to environmental perturbations. Agent-based models will simulate cellular and tissue interactions, while system dynamics modules will couple these with organism-wide physiological processes. A key innovation involves adaptive network modeling to identify critical nodes where localized disruptions propagate into systemic failure, enabling predictions of resilience thresholds. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of interacting variables, real-time parameter optimization, and large ensemble simulations to quantify probabilistic outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational platform for interdisciplinary hypothesis testing in integrative biology, (2) predictive maps of stress response trajectories under varying environmental scenarios, and (3) identification of conserved intervention points to enhance organismal resilience. This work will provide a foundation for translational applications in conservation biology and preventive health strategies, bridging gaps between experimental data and theoretical models. By leveraging parallelized computing resources, the project will advance methodologies for studying biological complexity while addressing pressing questions about systemic adaptability in changing environments.
cip_title: Integrative/ Interdisciplinary Biology, Biosciences, and Biomedical Sciences
cip_definition: A program that crosses multiple specializations within the biological and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in general biological research and variety of specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation and risk mitigation in large-scale clinical trials, a critical challenge in research administration. Clinical trials are resource-intensive endeavors requiring strategic coordination of personnel, funding, compliance, and timelines. Current approaches to planning and monitoring often rely on static models, which inadequately account for dynamic variables such as participant recruitment delays, protocol deviations, and budget constraints. This research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform to model clinical trial workflows under diverse scenarios. Using agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo methods, the platform will simulate trial phases, incorporating probabilistic inputs for enrollment rates, regulatory audits, and financial variables. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to predict bottlenecks and recommend adaptive resource reallocation strategies. The HPC environment is essential to process large datasets from historical trials (e.g., NIH RePORTER, ClinicalTrials.gov) and perform real-time, parallel simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between trial speed, cost, and compliance, enabling administrators to prioritize funding, adjust staffing, and preemptively address ethical or regulatory risks. This work aligns with the program’s focus on advancing leadership in research administration by bridging gaps in data-driven project management. The tool’s predictive analytics could enhance grant proposal competitiveness by improving budget justifications and risk management plans. By leveraging HPC, this project addresses a systemic need for adaptive, evidence-based frameworks in clinical research administration, with potential applications in academic, governmental, and industry settings.
cip_definition: A program designed to prepare formally trained, advanced-level personnel for research administration leadership positions at colleges and universities, government agencies, hospitals, nonprofit agencies, and in industry. Includes instruction in bioethics, biostatistics, ethical, legal and regulatory consideration in clinical investigation, financial analysis, grant writing, managing and monitoring clinical trials, project management, strategic planning, and team building.

abstract: The increasing complexity of household financial ecosystems, characterized by dynamic income streams, volatile asset valuations, and evolving debt structures, presents significant challenges for families navigating long-term financial stability. Existing models in family resource management often rely on static or simplified assumptions, limiting their capacity to simulate real-world interdependencies between socioeconomic factors, behavioral decision-making, and policy impacts. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate household financial trajectories under diverse economic scenarios, integrating granular data on regional cost-of-living variances, employment trends, and access to public assistance programs. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the study will employ agent-based modeling to represent heterogeneous household decision-making strategies, coupled with machine learning techniques to identify patterns in financial resilience. The computational architecture will simulate interactions between 100,000+ agent-households across multi-year timescales, incorporating stochastic shocks such as medical emergencies, job displacement, and interest rate fluctuations. Sensitivity analyses will evaluate the efficacy of proposed interventions, including personalized debt management algorithms and policy-driven safety nets. By utilizing parallelized optimization routines and large-scale parameter sweeps, the project aims to quantify thresholds at which households transition between financial stability and distress. Expected outcomes include a scalable predictive tool for assessing vulnerability to economic disruptions and evidence-based recommendations for tailoring public resources to demographic subgroups. This work bridges computational social science and family economics, offering a novel methodology to advance resource management strategies in non-engineering domains. The requested HPC allocation is critical to handling the computational load of high-dimensional simulations, enabling real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets derived from public financial surveys and anonymized credit records. Results will inform both academic research and community-level financial literacy programs, addressing gaps in proactive household risk mitigation.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and implementation of policies and processes contributing to successful individual and family resource management. Includes instruction in financial goal-setting and strategies; household income, assets, and debt management; preventing and resolving financial difficulties; and the use of relevant public resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in personalized financial planning tools for households by integrating high-dimensional behavioral data with dynamic economic modeling. Current tools often rely on static demographic profiles or oversimplified assumptions about decision-making, limiting their applicability to diverse family structures and evolving economic conditions. The project will develop a computational framework to simulate household financial behaviors under variable stressors, such as income volatility, healthcare costs, and intergenerational resource transfers. Using anonymized transaction records from partnered financial institutions (N ≈ 2.5 million households), combined with longitudinal survey data on consumption patterns and family lifecycle transitions, we will train agent-based models to capture nonlinear relationships between socioeconomic factors and financial resilience. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing petabyte-scale financial datasets, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of long-term financial outcomes, and optimizing machine learning architectures that account for temporal dependencies in household decision sequences. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source predictive engine capable of generating adaptive financial planning recommendations for heterogeneous family configurations, (2) quantitative thresholds for intervention efficacy in debt mitigation strategies across cultural and socioeconomic subgroups, and (3) novel metrics for assessing intertemporal trade-offs in multi-generational household resource allocation. By bridging computational social science with consumer economics, this work aims to advance evidence-based tools for financial educators and family service providers while establishing methodological foundations for complex systems analysis in human sciences research. The requested resources will enable comparative analysis of model performance across hardware configurations, ensuring scalability for future integration with real-time financial counseling platforms.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Business Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer sciences/human sciences business services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Wildfire behavior prediction and mitigation strategies remain critical challenges in fire science, requiring advanced computational models to address complex interactions between combustion dynamics, environmental variables, and suppression tactics. Current models often lack the resolution to simulate multi-scale phenomena, such as fire-atmosphere coupling or the impact of heterogeneous fuel distributions on flame spread, limiting their utility in real-time decision support. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity wildfire simulation framework using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning (ML) techniques to improve predictive accuracy and operational planning. The research will employ physics-based fire propagation models grounded in combustion chemistry and heat transfer principles, integrated with real-time weather data and satellite-derived fuel moisture inputs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve centimeter-scale turbulence effects in fire fronts, simulate large-domain wildfire scenarios (>10 km²), and train ML surrogates for rapid risk assessment. Key objectives include validating simulations against experimental prescribed burn datasets, quantifying uncertainty in ember transport predictions, and optimizing resource deployment strategies under dynamic fire conditions. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for reactive flow equations and graph neural networks to model fire spread across discontinuous fuel beds. Outcomes will advance fundamental understanding of fire whirl formation, structure ignition mechanisms in wildland-urban interfaces, and the efficacy of next-generation fire-retardant delivery systems. By providing open-access simulation tools and datasets, this work aims to enhance situational awareness for fire agencies, inform policy updates to fire codes, and reduce computational barriers for future research in fire suppression technology development. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter sweeps across 100+ scenario variations, reducing time-to-solution for critical case studies from weeks to days.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and practice of fires and fire-fighting. Includes instruction in fire chemistry and physics, combustible materials, computer science, building construction, fire codes and related laws, fire hydraulics, fire command, fire prevention/inspection, fire protection systems, fire suppression systems, fire/arson investigation, occupational safety, equipment operation, emergency medicine and communications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in classical philology and linguistic evolution through the computational analysis of understudied multilingual corpora from late antiquity. The primary research problem centers on tracing syntactic and semantic shifts in post-classical Latin, Greek, and Coptic textual traditions (circa 3rd–7th centuries CE), where manual analysis of complex multilingual interactions remains impractical due to fragmentary sources, non-standardized orthography, and the scale of cross-linguistic comparison required. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for morphological tagging, dependency parsing, and semantic role labeling with graph-based network analysis to model linguistic contact phenomena. Custom transformer-based models will be fine-tuned on curated datasets of digitized papyri, inscriptions, and literary texts to handle orthographic variation and code-switching patterns. HPC resources are critical for training these models at scale, parallelizing comparative analyses across linguistic domains, and visualizing high-dimensional network representations of syntactic convergence. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel computational framework for diachronic multilingual analysis, 2) quantitative evidence challenging traditional periodization boundaries in Latin linguistic history, and 3) open-access tools for automated annotation of non-canonical classical languages. This work bridges computational linguistics and classical studies, offering methodological innovations for analyzing linguistic diversity in fragmentary historical corpora while addressing substantive questions about language contact in the Mediterranean world. The requested computing allocation will enable processing of terabyte-scale textual repositories through GPU-accelerated model training and distributed memory workflows, tasks infeasible on standard departmental infrastructure. Results will contribute to both humanistic scholarship and NLP methodologies for low-resource historical languages.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in classics and classical languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale textual and visual datasets in children’s and adolescent literature, addressing gaps in quantitative and computational approaches to genre evolution, representation, and narrative structure. While traditional literary scholarship has relied on close reading and manual content analysis, the sheer volume of published works across historical periods—coupled with the growing diversity of multimedia formats like illustrated books and film adaptations—demands scalable computational methods. This research will focus on two interconnected problems: (1) identifying patterns in thematic shifts and representational equity (e.g., gender, race, disability) across 20th- and 21st-century children’s literature, and (2) modeling the relationship between textual and visual narrative strategies in multimodal works. Using natural language processing (NLP) tools and computer vision techniques, the project will process digitized texts, illustrations, and film stills from curated corpora, including award-winning books, bestsellers, and understudied independent publications. Computational methods will include transformer-based models for semantic analysis, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for visual feature extraction, and graph-based algorithms to map character interactions and narrative arcs. These approaches require HPC resources to handle high-dimensional data, train custom models on genre-specific materials, and run iterative simulations testing hypotheses about cultural transmission and reader reception. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated literary works, visualizations of genre dynamics, and statistical frameworks for assessing representational trends. By integrating computational rigor with literary theory, this project aims to produce actionable insights for educators, librarians, and publishers while advancing methodological innovation in humanities scholarship. The scalability of this work will also establish a foundation for future interdisciplinary collaborations exploring the intersection of children’s literature, media studies, and computational humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scholarly study of children's and adolescent literature and that may enhance the professional work of teachers, librarians, publishers, booksellers, and creative writers. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, studies of various types of literary text, book artists, and children's films.

abstract: Respiratory care therapy faces challenges in integrating multi-modal clinical data—such as real-time ventilator metrics, pulmonary function tests, imaging, and genomic profiles—to optimize patient-specific treatment strategies. Current approaches often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for individual variability in disease progression or treatment response. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that inform personalized respiratory care. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets from critical care units, and (2) simulating respiratory mechanics under diverse pathological conditions using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models. The machine learning component will employ deep neural networks to identify patterns in ventilator weaning success, infection risk, and drug response, while the CFD models will simulate airflow dynamics in obstructive and restrictive lung diseases, incorporating patient-specific anatomical data from CT scans. Both approaches require significant computational resources due to the scale of data (terabytes of longitudinal patient records and high-resolution imaging) and the complexity of simulations involving multiphysics interactions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing for model training, hyperparameter optimization, and large ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainty. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide ventilator management, reduce weaning failure rates, and optimize aerosol drug delivery in mechanically ventilated patients. By integrating these computational tools into clinical workflows, this research aims to advance precision respiratory care, reduce ICU stays, and improve patient outcomes. The resulting datasets and models will be shared with the respiratory therapy community to foster collaborative innovation in treatment personalization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address unresolved questions in paleontological research concerning the drivers of morphological evolution and ecosystem dynamics during the Mesozoic Era. A critical challenge in analyzing fossil datasets—spanning vertebrate, invertebrate, and plant assemblages—is disentangling the interplay of biotic and abiotic factors, such as climate shifts, tectonic activity, and species interactions, that shaped ancient biodiversity. Traditional statistical methods often struggle with the complexity, scale, and temporal resolution of these datasets, which include 3D fossil morphometrics, geochemical proxies, and stratigraphic records. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating Bayesian phylogenetic comparative methods, agent-based ecosystem modeling, and machine learning-driven image analysis of fossil specimens. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of high-resolution CT scans for automated trait quantification across thousands of specimens, as well as the simulation of multi-scale ecological networks under varying paleoclimatic scenarios derived from global circulation models. Key objectives include reconstructing adaptive landscapes for Mesozoic reptiles and early angiosperms, identifying tipping points in marine invertebrate community resilience prior to mass extinction events, and quantifying rates of phenotypic evolution in response to environmental stressors. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to handle terabyte-scale imaging data, perform Monte Carlo Markov chain analyses across complex phylogenies, and run ensemble ecosystem simulations at geologic timescales. Expected outcomes include publicly accessible tools for fossil data integration, novel insights into evolutionary tempo and mode under climate volatility, and a scalable workflow for testing macroevolutionary hypotheses. By bridging paleontological data with advanced computational techniques, this work will advance predictive frameworks for understanding biodiversity dynamics in deep time, with implications for modern conservation paleobiology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of extinct life forms and associated fossil remains, and the reconstruction and analysis of ancient life forms, ecosystems, and geologic processes. Includes instruction in sedimentation and fossilization processes, fossil chemistry, evolutionary biology, paleoecology, paleoclimatology, trace fossils, micropaleontology, invertebrate paleontology, vertebrate paleontology, paleobotany, field research methods, and laboratory research and conservation methods.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of structural degradation in historic masonry buildings, a critical challenge in heritage conservation. Traditional methods for assessing material decay and structural instability in aging masonry rely on localized physical sampling or simplified simulations, which often fail to capture complex interactions between environmental stressors, material heterogeneity, and long-term load dynamics. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate deterioration processes across spatial and temporal scales. The FEA component will model stress distributions and crack propagation in 3D-scanned masonry assemblies under varying moisture, thermal, and seismic conditions. Concurrently, ML algorithms trained on historical degradation data from archival records and LiDAR surveys will predict site-specific vulnerability patterns. ABM will simulate cumulative micro-scale material interactions (e.g., salt crystallization, freeze-thaw cycles) to forecast macro-scale structural outcomes. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution 3D models (10^6–10^7 elements), iterate ML training on terabyte-scale datasets, and run parallelized ABM scenarios spanning decades of simulated time. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for conservators to prioritize intervention sites, optimize reinforcement materials, and test “virtual restoration” strategies before physical implementation. This work bridges computational engineering and preservation practice, offering a scalable method to safeguard irreplaceable heritage structures against climate change and anthropogenic risks. By quantifying previously intractable degradation mechanisms, the project will inform policy frameworks for adaptive reuse and risk mitigation, contributing to interdisciplinary scholarship at the nexus of cultural heritage and computational science.
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on architectural design and building techniques for historic and restored structures, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing venipuncture success rates while minimizing procedural complications by leveraging computational modeling of vascular dynamics and patient-specific biomechanical interactions. Despite its foundational role in diagnostics, phlebotomy remains reliant on empirical techniques, with limited quantitative frameworks to predict outcomes in patients exhibiting anatomical variations, dehydration, or fragile vasculature. We propose developing a high-fidelity computational pipeline integrating hemodynamic simulations, tissue deformation models, and machine learning to analyze how biomechanical factors—including needle insertion angle, velocity, and tissue layer interactions—affect venipuncture outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis of 3D vascular models derived from anonymized ultrasound datasets, capturing diverse anatomical scenarios (e.g., rolling veins, sclerosed vessels). Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will process retrospective phlebotomy outcome data (10,000+ procedural records) to identify predictive signatures linking patient physiology, technician technique, and success rates. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental phantom models instrumented with pressure sensors. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework to guide needle insertion strategies for atypical vascular presentations, (2) a risk stratification tool flagging high-probability complication scenarios, and (3) generative models of synthetic vascular anatomies for augmented reality training simulations. By bridging biomechanics, clinical data science, and medical device interaction modeling, this work aims to advance evidence-based procedural optimization in phlebotomy—a critical yet understudied interface between human physiology and clinical technique. The resulting tools could reduce hematoma incidence by an estimated 15-30% in vulnerable populations while providing a computational foundation for adaptive training platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and other health care professionals, to draw blood samples from patients using a variety of intrusive procedures. Includes instruction in basic vascular anatomy and physiology, blood physiology, skin puncture techniques, venipuncture, venous specimen collection and handling, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that enhance the personalization of educational interventions for students with speech or language impairments (SLI). Despite advances in special education pedagogy, creating individualized education plans (IEPs) remains labor-intensive, relying heavily on manual assessment and trial-and-error adjustments. This research addresses the critical gap in scalable, data-driven tools to optimize intervention strategies by analyzing complex, multimodal datasets (e.g., speech recordings, language samples, and behavioral logs) from diverse student populations. Using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML), we will train models to identify patterns in communication development, predict responsiveness to specific interventions, and recommend tailored instructional adjustments. The computational workflow involves preprocessing terabyte-scale audio and text data to extract linguistic features (e.g., phonemic accuracy, syntactic complexity), followed by federated learning techniques to preserve participant confidentiality while aggregating insights across institutions. Deep reinforcement learning will then simulate iterative educator-student interactions, testing hypothetical intervention sequences in silico to prioritize strategies with the highest predicted efficacy. HPC resources are essential to manage the distributed training of large neural networks, hyperparameter optimization, and real-time inference required for dynamic model refinement. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educators to generate data-informed IEP recommendations, reducing planning time while improving intervention precision. By bridging computational innovation with special education practice, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for addressing the heterogeneous needs of students with SLI, ultimately advancing equity in speech-language pathology and teacher preparation programs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Speech or Language Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study and design of educational services for children or adults with speech and language impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with speech and language impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with speech disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in naturopathic medicine by modeling the synergistic effects of multi-modal therapies on chronic disease outcomes. Despite growing clinical interest in holistic interventions, the complexity of interactions between natural therapies—such as botanical compounds, dietary modifications, and mind-body practices—poses a challenge for traditional experimental designs. Current approaches often isolate individual treatments, limiting understanding of how combined protocols influence biological networks. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning and systems biology to simulate patient-specific responses to naturopathic treatment regimens. Using de-identified clinical datasets from integrative health centers, including longitudinal biomarker profiles, lifestyle logs, and treatment histories, we will train ensemble models to predict metabolic, immune, and neurological outcomes under varying therapeutic combinations. Molecular dynamics simulations will further explore mechanisms of action for prioritized botanical-drug interactions identified in silico. HPC resources are critical for managing the high dimensionality of multi-omics data (genomic, metabolomic, and proteomic), enabling parallelized parameter optimization in neural network architectures, and running large-scale virtual cohorts to assess protocol efficacy across diverse patient phenotypes. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms to guide personalized naturopathic care, mechanistic insights into polypharmacological synergies, and a publicly accessible computational toolkit for simulating non-pharmacological interventions. This work will bridge gaps in evidence-based frameworks for complex naturopathic protocols while demonstrating scalable methods to study holistic health paradigms. By elucidating systems-level therapeutic impacts, the project aims to strengthen clinical decision-making, inform policy on integrative care models, and establish computational naturopathy as a viable domain for precision medicine innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of naturopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic approach combining medical knowledge with noninvasive natural, homeopathic, and non-Western therapies and emphasizing disease prevention, wellness, and self-healing. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, epidemiology, neuroscience, biostatistics, public and community health, laboratory and clinical diagnosis, pharmacognosy, botanical medicine, homeopathy, principles of Oriental medicine and Ayurveda, manipulative therapy, naturopathic therapeutics, therapeutic nutrition, case analysis and management, philosophy of naturopathy, patient counseling, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the role of microbial biogeochemical cycling in shaping ancient sedimentary iron formations, a critical yet poorly understood component of Earth’s early redox evolution. While iron-rich sedimentary deposits from the Precambrian eon provide a key archive of biotic-abiotic interactions in anaerobic marine environments, the metabolic networks and environmental feedbacks that governed their formation remain unresolved. We propose an interdisciplinary computational framework integrating genome-resolved metabolic modeling with reactive transport simulations to quantify how microbial iron oxidation, sulfur cycling, and organic matter remineralization interacted with fluctuating chemical gradients in Precambrian oceans. Customized genome-scale metabolic reconstructions of ancestral microbial communities, informed by phylogenetic analyses of extant extremophiles and geochemical proxies from paleodepositional settings, will be coupled to reactive transport models simulating fluid flow, mineral precipitation, and redox dynamics at basin scales. This approach requires HPC capabilities to resolve multi-dimensional, nonlinear interactions between biological activity and geological processes across spatial scales (μm to km) and temporal resolutions (seconds to millennia). Parallelized simulations will employ adaptive meshing and hybrid solver algorithms to optimize performance while handling heterogeneous geochemical datasets. Anticipated outcomes include mechanistic insights into how microbial communities influenced global iron cycling during Earth’s oxygenation, quantitative constraints on the preservation of biosignatures in iron formations, and a scalable modeling framework for linking microbial ecophysiology to planetary-scale biogeochemical patterns. The results will advance predictive models of co-evolving life and environments in extreme conditions, with applications to astrobiology and the interpretation of ancient Martian lithologies. By bridging computational microbiology and paleoenvironmental geochemistry, this work addresses a critical gap in understanding Earth’s early biosphere while demonstrating the value of HPC-driven approaches in geobiological research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of how living things interact with geological systems. Includes instruction in evolution of Earth systems, geochemistry, geology, geomicrobiology, marine chemistry, paleobiology, paleoecology, paleontology, and petrology.

abstract: Wildfire behavior prediction and forensic investigation require high-fidelity modeling of complex, dynamic interactions between fire, terrain, meteorology, and human interventions. Current operational models struggle to resolve fine-scale fire-atmosphere coupling, ember transport dynamics, or post-fire evidence degradation processes, limiting predictive accuracy and investigative reliability. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance multi-physics wildfire simulations integrating combustion dynamics, computational fluid dynamics, and stochastic weather interactions at unprecedented spatial resolutions (≤1 m grid scale) and temporal scales (sub-minute increments). Coupled atmosphere-fire models (WRF-SFIRE, FIRETEC) will be extended with custom modules for ember lofting, suppression system impacts (retardant dispersal, water droplet evaporation), and forensic degradation processes under varying environmental conditions. Machine learning methods will be applied to HPC-generated datasets to develop surrogate models for real-time forecasting and probabilistic cause attribution. Simulations will be validated against experimental prescribed burn data, historical wildfire case studies, and forensic evidence patterns from agency partnerships. Anticipated outcomes include (1) improved operational tools for predicting fire spread in complex urban-interface zones, (2) quantitative frameworks for evaluating airborne suppression tactics, and (3) physics-based criteria for preserving and interpreting post-fire ignition evidence. The computational scale required—ensemble runs exceeding 10^4 core-hours per scenario—necessitates dedicated HPC allocations to manage memory-intensive 3D transport equations and Monte Carlo uncertainty analyses. This work directly supports national priorities for wildfire resilience by bridging critical gaps between firefighting operations, arson investigation, and next-generation fire science. Resource allocations will enable parameter sweeps across climatological regimes and fuel types while maintaining readiness for urgent simulations during active fire incidents.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science, firefighting and investigation to the prevention, control and mitigation of wildland fires and the analysis of causes. Includes instruction in fire science and behavior, wildland environments, meteorology, wildland fire hydraulics and dynamics, water and chemical supply systems, wildland firefighting operations, airborne firefighting, firebreak engineering, communications systems, wildland arson, forensic procedures, wildland fire prevention, investigation techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of high-resolution, high-dynamic-range (HDR) media processing in photographic and film/video workflows. Current workflows struggle to efficiently process 8K+ video streams and gigapixel-scale image datasets, particularly when applying real-time AI-driven enhancements, multi-sensor fusion for immersive media, or dynamic lighting simulations. These bottlenecks limit creative experimentation, delay production timelines, and hinder the development of next-generation visual storytelling tools. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize computationally intensive tasks across three domains: 1) GPU-accelerated rendering of physics-based lighting models for virtual production environments, 2) distributed processing of RAW sensor data through machine learning pipelines for noise reduction and dynamic range expansion, and 3) real-time compositing of multi-camera arrays in volumetric video capture systems. The computational workflow will utilize containerized environments with optimized builds of OpenImageIO, FFmpeg, and PyTorch, orchestrated through Slurm job arrays to manage heterogeneous workloads spanning CPU-based color grading simulations and GPU-accelerated neural rendering tasks. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for scaling cinematic post-production workflows, open-source toolkits for HPC-optimized media processing, and quantitative analyses of computational tradeoffs in resolution versus latency for emerging formats like light field video. By enabling rapid iteration on computationally prohibitive techniques—such as AI-assisted depth map generation at full sensor resolutions or Monte Carlo simulations for adaptive lighting control—this research will directly enhance pedagogical resources for film technology education while providing industry-relevant insights into scalable production architectures. The requested resources will support both experimental algorithm development and large-scale testing using professionally captured 16-bit RAW datasets from ARRI and RED cinema cameras.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation and maintenance of camera and lighting equipment and the production of finished still, video, and film products under the supervision of photographers, directors, and editors. Includes instruction in equipment setup and maintenance; lighting; power supplies; studio and film set tasks such as camera operator, grip, and best boy; plate and negative handling and development; laboratory procedures; and digital software applications.

abstract: Dental implantology faces challenges in predicting long-term biomechanical stability and osseointegration success due to variability in patient anatomy, bone density, and occlusal loading patterns. Traditional clinical methods often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for patient-specific biomechanical interactions between implants, prosthetics, and bone. This project proposes a computational framework to model the biomechanical and biological responses of dental implants at scale, enabling personalized treatment planning and optimized implant design. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate three-dimensional stress distributions in bone and implant interfaces under dynamic masticatory loads using finite element analysis (FEA), coupled with agent-based modeling of bone remodeling and soft tissue adaptation. Patient-specific anatomies derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans will be integrated into these simulations to evaluate the impact of variables such as implant angulation, thread design, and grafting material properties. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to identify predictive biomarkers for implant failure and optimize surgical parameters. The computational workload involves iterative, high-resolution FEA across thousands of virtual patient scenarios, requiring parallel processing capabilities for rapid convergence. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for biomechanical risk assessment, data-driven guidelines for graft material selection in low-density bone, and open-source tools for simulating bone-implant interactions. By quantifying the effects of clinical variables in silico, this work aims to reduce post-operative complications, improve prosthetic longevity, and advance computational dentistry methodologies. The scale of data generation and model complexity necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically relevant resolutions and throughput, which is unfeasible with standard computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Danish linguistic evolution and literary patterns across historical and contemporary corpora. While Danish language studies have traditionally relied on manual textual analysis, the increasing availability of digitized texts—from medieval runic inscriptions to modern social media—presents an opportunity to systematically investigate linguistic shifts, dialectal variations, and literary trends at scale. However, the computational demands of processing large, heterogeneous datasets (including unstructured text, audio recordings, and metadata) exceed the capacity of standard workstations. The research problem centers on identifying and modeling patterns in Danish phonology, morphology, and syntax across temporal, geographic, and sociocultural contexts, as well as quantifying stylistic features in literature that reflect genre or authorial evolution. Proposed methods include training transformer-based language models on curated historical and regional Danish texts, employing clustering algorithms to map dialectal boundaries, and applying neural networks for automated philological annotation. Additionally, graph-based analyses will explore intertextual networks in Danish literature, linking thematic motifs to sociopolitical developments. These workflows require parallelized processing, significant memory allocation, and GPU acceleration to handle tokenization of archaic orthographies, alignment of multilingual parallels, and probabilistic modeling of rare constructions. Expected outcomes include open-access datasets of annotated Danish texts, computational tools tailored for low-resource North Germanic languages, and interdisciplinary insights into language contact dynamics between Danish and minority languages in the region. The project aims to bridge gaps in digital humanities infrastructure for Scandinavian studies while providing a replicable framework for computational literary analysis in linguistically under-resourced contexts. By integrating HPC-driven methods with traditional philological expertise, this work will enhance scholarly capacity to trace the adaptive trajectories of Danish in technological, educational, and globalized settings.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Danish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and optimization of next-generation aerospace propulsion systems, with a focus on hybrid-electric architectures. The integration of electric propulsion components into traditional gas turbine engines introduces complex multi-physics challenges, including unsteady fluid-structure interactions, thermal management constraints, and coupled electromagnetic-aerodynamic effects. Current experimental approaches are limited in resolving these phenomena at relevant scales, while existing computational models lack the fidelity to capture transient behaviors across disparate time and spatial domains. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and dynamic system modeling. High-fidelity LES (Large Eddy Simulation) will model turbulent combustion and flow separation in hybrid combustors, coupled with conjugate heat transfer analysis for thermal stress prediction in critical components. GPU-accelerated solvers will enable parametric studies of electric motor-generator configurations under varying flight conditions, while reduced-order models will bridge component-level simulations with full-system performance optimization. The computational workload demands distributed-memory parallelism and large-scale data handling capabilities due to the billion-cell meshes required for resolving boundary layer physics and the need for ensemble runs across design permutations. Expected outcomes include validated performance maps for hybrid propulsion subsystems, identification of optimal power management strategies for reduced emissions, and predictive models for component degradation under cyclic thermal loading. These results will directly inform prototype testing protocols and certification pathways for sustainable aviation technologies, accelerating the translation of theoretical concepts into field-deployable solutions. By advancing simulation-driven design in aerospace engineering technology, this work aims to reduce reliance on costly physical iterations while improving the reliability of emerging propulsion systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing aircraft, spacecraft and their systems. Includes instruction in aircraft/spacecraft systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Understanding the molecular mechanisms of enzymatic allostery remains a critical challenge in biochemistry, with implications for designing therapeutics and engineered biocatalysts. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve the dynamic, multi-scale conformational changes that underlie allosteric regulation. This project seeks to integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and free energy calculations to map the thermodynamic landscapes of allosteric transitions in a model enzyme system: aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase). ATCase’s complex hexameric architecture and cooperative substrate binding make it an ideal system for probing how localized perturbations propagate across protein domains to modulate activity. We propose to perform multi-microsecond, all-atom MD simulations of ATCase under varying ligand-binding states and mutant backgrounds, combined with Markov state models to identify metastable conformations and transition pathways. Enhanced sampling techniques, including replica exchange and metadynamics, will be employed to overcome timescale limitations and quantify free energy barriers. These simulations will be validated against existing crystallographic and mutagenesis data, with newly generated experimental kinetic measurements from collaborators. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing resources due to the system size (~300,000 atoms), need for extensive sampling across multiple replicates, and iterative analysis of terabyte-scale trajectory data. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific residue interactions to allosteric efficiency, which could inform the rational design of allosteric inhibitors or engineered enzymes with tailored regulatory properties. By elucidating fundamental principles of protein dynamics, this work will advance methodologies for studying complex biomolecular systems and bridge gaps between structural data and functional mechanisms in molecular biology.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_title: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Molecular Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biochemistry, biophysics and molecular biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) is critical for preventing neurological injury during high-risk surgeries, yet existing systems face challenges in real-time processing of complex neurophysiological data and predictive accuracy under dynamic surgical conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a machine learning framework to enhance the interpretation of multimodal IONM signals, including electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs). Current methods rely on threshold-based alerts and static models, which lack sensitivity to patient-specific variability and evolving intraoperative risks. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to train deep neural networks on large-scale, heterogeneous datasets of intraoperative neurophysiological recordings, surgical parameters, and postoperative outcomes. The computational workflow will integrate time-series analysis of raw signals, feature extraction using wavelet transforms, and attention-based architectures to prioritize clinically relevant patterns. Parallelized training across GPU nodes will enable rapid iteration on model architectures, while in-memory data processing will reduce latency for real-time inference simulations. A key innovation involves finite element modeling to simulate signal propagation in patient-specific anatomical geometries derived from intraoperative imaging, enhancing the biological plausibility of feature mappings. The project will leverage existing institutional datasets (retrospective, n≈12,000 cases) and prospectively collected data from 350 surgeries. Expected outcomes include a deployable model demonstrating ≥92% accuracy in predicting intraoperative neurological compromise (validated against ground-truth surgical outcomes) and a 30% reduction in false-positive alerts compared to current standards. By optimizing computational efficiency, the framework aims to achieve sub-second latency for intraoperative decision support. This work will advance precision neuromonitoring protocols, reduce postoperative morbidity, and provide an open-source toolkit for adaptive IONM signal processing. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the ∼450 TB of signal data, iterative model training, and large-scale biomechanical simulations, which are infeasible on local clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to become neuromonitoring technicians who analyze, monitor, and record nervous system function to promote the effective treatment of pathological conditions. Includes instruction in EEG technology, EMG technology, anatomy, and neuroanatomy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the stability and transfer of heritable information in bacteriophage populations under environmental stress. While phage genomes are highly compact, their ability to rapidly acquire mutations or horizontally transferred genetic elements contributes to adaptability, yet the regulatory processes that balance genome stability with plasticity remain poorly understood. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale genomic datasets from phage populations subjected to mutagenic conditions (e.g., UV exposure, chemical mutagens) to identify conserved regulatory motifs and mutation hotspots. Computational models will simulate the dynamics of DNA replication and repair processes under varying stress intensities, integrating empirical data on mutation rates, recombination frequency, and gene expression. These simulations will employ parallelized algorithms to track probabilistic outcomes of replication errors and repair pathway efficacy across millions of simulated generations. Additionally, network analysis tools will map interactions between phage-encoded stability factors (e.g., terminases, integrases) and host machinery to pinpoint evolutionary constraints on genome architecture. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific genetic elements to mutation tolerance, insights into selective pressures driving horizontal gene transfer in viral populations, and mechanistic explanations for stress-induced genomic instability.
