This work will advance foundational knowledge in molecular genetics by elucidating how phage genomes maintain functional integrity despite rapid evolution, with broader implications for understanding genetic adaptation in pathogenic viruses. The scale of genomic data and complexity of stochastic modeling necessitate HPC resources to achieve statistically robust, high-resolution analyses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of genetic structures and mechanisms of organisms, including bacteria, phages, and viruses. Includes instruction in the replication, expression, transfer, structure, maintenance, and stability of heritable information in DNA, RNA, and proteins; the regulation of these processes; and neurogenetics.

abstract: Wilderness medicine requires clinicians to address complex physiologic challenges in environments where resource limitations and environmental stressors intersect. This research project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize medical interventions under austere conditions, where factors such as hypothermia, altitude illness, traumatic injury, and limited diagnostic tools interact nonlinearly. The core computational challenge lies in simulating dynamic, multi-scale physiologic responses to environmental insults while incorporating stochastic resource constraints—a task demanding high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose an agent-based modeling framework to simulate patient outcomes across diverse environmental scenarios (e.g., high-altitude rescue, tropical expedition medicine) using physiologic data from wilderness medicine case reports, environmental sensor datasets, and pharmacokinetic models adapted to extreme conditions. Monte Carlo methods will assess intervention efficacy across thousands of simulated scenarios with variable resource availability, while machine learning approaches will identify critical decision thresholds for field use. The HPC environment is essential for managing three-dimensional parameter spaces encompassing environmental variables (temperature, oxygen tension), patient states (core temperature, injury severity), and resource inventories (medical supplies, evacuation timelines). Expected outcomes include validated decision trees for fluid resuscitation in hypovolemic shock at altitude, thermoregulation strategies for combined hypothermia-trauma cases, and adaptive dosing guidelines for antimicrobials in tropical environments. These models will inform evidence-based protocols for wilderness medicine practitioners and contribute to a computational library of resource-constrained clinical decision support tools. By leveraging large-scale parallel processing to address the combinatorial complexity of environmental medicine, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in actionable clinical knowledge for austere care settings.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine with limited resources in austere environments or to provide healthcare anywhere in which environmental conditions have physiologic insult to a patient.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of somatic bodywork therapies, specifically Rolfing/Structural Integration and Hellerwork, through advanced computational modeling and multi-modal data integration. Despite anecdotal evidence of efficacy in improving chronic pain and postural dysfunction, the mechanisms by which these manual therapies influence fascial plasticity, proprioceptive recalibration, and autonomic nervous system regulation remain poorly characterized. Current limitations stem from an inability to non-invasively quantify three-dimensional force propagation patterns during dynamic therapist-client interactions or model their cascading biological effects across temporal scales. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution finite element model of human fascial networks integrated with neural circuit simulations, parameterized by motion capture data from certified practitioners and synchronized biometric feedback (heart rate variability, galvanic skin response) from recipients. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated iterative solvers to simulate tissue deformation dynamics under varying manual input parameters (force vectors, velocity, duration) and predict downstream cellular responses via coupled mechanotransduction models. Machine learning approaches will identify optimal treatment patterns through inverse analysis of clinical outcomes data from a 120-participant study on chronic low back pain. By establishing the first multiscale simulation framework for somatic bodywork, this research will provide quantitative insights into dose-response relationships, tissue-specific adaptive thresholds, and neuroimmune interaction pathways. The resulting models and datasets will be made available through an open-access portal to support evidence-based refinement of manual therapy protocols, practitioner training tools, and personalized treatment planning algorithms. This work bridges the gap between empirical bodywork traditions and systems biology, advancing computational methods for studying complex manual interventions in health sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical and emotional balance and well-being through the application of skilled touch principles and techniques. Includes instruction in therapeutic massage and other hands-on touch methods, anatomy and physiology, structural/functional integration and various holistic health systems (Rolfing/Structural Integration, colon hydrotherapy, Breema, Hellerwork, lymphatic drainage, Rosen Method, hydrotherapy, and others), client counseling, practice management, and applicable regulations and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized fitness programming by integrating heterogeneous biometric, behavioral, and environmental data. Despite advances in exercise science, current methodologies for designing individualized fitness regimens rely heavily on generalized population standards and manual trial-and-error adjustments, resulting in suboptimal adherence rates and physiological outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address this gap through large-scale simulation of multifactorial interactions between exercise variables, real-time physiological feedback, and longitudinal client outcomes. The research will aggregate anonymized datasets from wearable devices, electronic health records, and environmental sensors (e.g., sleep quality, local air quality indices) to train ensemble machine learning models predicting client-specific responses to exercise interventions. Agent-based modeling will simulate long-term adherence patterns under varying program designs, while finite element analysis will map biomechanical stress distributions across diverse body types during complex movements. A custom optimization pipeline will reconcile competing objectives such as metabolic efficiency, injury risk minimization, and psychological engagement thresholds. The computational intensity of concurrently processing high-frequency biometric streams (≥10 Hz sampling rates) across simulated cohorts (n > 10,000 virtual agents) necessitates distributed-memory parallelization and GPU-accelerated tensor operations. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system that dynamically prioritizes exercise variables based on evolving client data, reducing the iterative burden on fitness technicians. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of historical program success rates against model predictions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between exercise physiology, behavioral economics, and computational modeling, offering a novel paradigm for data-driven fitness program personalization while operating outside traditional STEM-domain resource allocations.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in health and fitness clubs, wellness centers, public and private recreation facilities, hospitals and corporate fitness programs where they will perform a variety of instructional and administrative duties. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, fitness techniques, exercise science, personal training, nutrition, and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize the design and real-time performance of industrial automation systems, with a focus on multi-axis robotic control and sensor-integrated process monitoring. Current challenges in automation engineering include the need to simulate complex interactions between programmable logic controllers (PLCs), heterogeneous actuator networks, and vision-based feedback systems under dynamic production conditions. Existing simulation tools struggle to model latency effects, synchronization errors, and failure propagation in large-scale automated workflows, particularly when integrating legacy pneumatic components with modern IoT-enabled devices. To address this, we propose a hybrid modeling approach combining discrete-event simulations of control logic with finite element analysis of mechanical stress distributions in high-cycle robotic assemblies. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations assessing fault tolerance across 10,000+ operational scenarios while maintaining millisecond-scale temporal resolution. Custom CUDA kernels will accelerate machine learning models trained to predict wear patterns in servo-driven components using vibrational spectroscopy data. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of optimizing PLC code deployment across distributed manufacturing cells and reducing system validation timelines by 40% compared to conventional ladder logic testing methods. The resource-intensive nature of simultaneously modeling electrical, mechanical, and control subsystems at production-scale fidelity necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory partitions. Successful implementation will provide new methodologies for lifecycle prediction in hybrid electro-pneumatic systems while advancing workforce training tools through synthetic datasets of rare failure modes. This work directly supports the Automation Engineer Technology program’s mission to bridge theoretical control principles with industrial implementation challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, installing, calibrating, modifying and maintaining automated systems. Includes instruction in computer systems; electronics and instrumentation; programmable logic controllers (PLCs); electric, hydraulic and pneumatic control systems; actuator and sensor systems; process control; robotics; applications to specific industrial tasks; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of emergent communication patterns in shaping organizational decision-making and conflict resolution processes, with a focus on how digitally mediated interactions influence power dynamics and team cohesion. While prior research has established the importance of communication networks in organizational outcomes, existing methodologies lack the capacity to model large-scale, real-time interaction data or simulate complex feedback loops between human and technological actors. To address this gap, we propose a computational study combining natural language processing (NLP) of longitudinal organizational communication datasets (e.g., email archives, meeting transcripts, and collaboration platform exchanges) with agent-based modeling of multi-team systems. High-performance computing resources are essential to process terabytes of unstructured text data, train transformer-based models for semantic analysis of power-laden discourse, and run parallelized simulations exploring how communication bottlenecks affect decision latency across hierarchical structures. The computational workflow will integrate network analysis to map evolving influence relationships and machine learning classifiers to detect patterns predictive of conflict escalation or resolution. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting communication-driven organizational risks, validated against case studies from healthcare and tech sectors, and actionable insights for designing communication protocols that balance efficiency with equity. By bridging communication theory with computational social science methods, this research aims to advance scholarly understanding of how organizations can adapt their communication infrastructures to complex socio-technical environments while maintaining employee engagement. The requested resources will enable scaling analyses to unprecedented data volumes, directly supporting the development of evidence-based strategies for organizational communication in digitally transformed workplaces.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on general communication processes and dynamics within organizations. Includes instruction in the development and maintenance of interpersonal group relations within organizations; decision-making and conflict management; the use of symbols to create and maintain organizational images, missions, and values; power and politics within organizations; human interaction with computer technology; and how communications socializes and supports employees and team members.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven decision-making in funeral service management, focusing on optimizing operational workflows and improving grief support interventions. The funeral service industry faces unique challenges in balancing logistical demands—such as resource allocation during peak service periods, inventory management for burial merchandise, and compliance with evolving regulatory frameworks—with the need to provide personalized, culturally sensitive care to grieving families. Traditional approaches to these challenges often rely on anecdotal experience or static models, which fail to account for dynamic variables like regional mortality trends, seasonal demand fluctuations, or psychosocial factors influencing client needs. This research proposes a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate funeral home operations under variable conditions, analyze historical service data, and predict emergent patterns in client preferences. Large-scale datasets will be synthesized from anonymized funeral home records, demographic databases, and natural language processing (NLP) of grief counseling transcripts to train models that optimize staffing, inventory, and service scheduling. Concurrently, sentiment analysis of counseling interactions will identify correlations between linguistic markers and long-term client outcomes, informing evidence-based training protocols for funeral directors. The computational intensity of simulating multi-agent systems across thousands of scenarios, coupled with the need for real-time analysis of unstructured textual data, necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve actionable resolution. Outcomes will include predictive tools for operational efficiency, a taxonomy of grief communication patterns, and scalable frameworks for ethical AI integration in thanatology practice. By bridging computational social science with funeral service management, this work aims to establish a precedent for data-informed stewardship in a profession traditionally guided by qualitative expertise, ultimately enhancing service resilience and client-centered care in end-of-life industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional licensure as funeral directors and as managers of funeral homes, cemeteries, and related services.  Includes instruction in the sociology of death and dying, psychology of grief and grief counseling, history of funeral service, funeral direction, business law, funeral service law, funeral home management, accounting and related computer operations, and funeral services marketing and merchandising.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern footwear and leather goods, combined with sustainability demands for product longevity, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize repair techniques and material interactions. Traditional methods in shoe, boot, and leather repair often rely on trial-and-error approaches to address material degradation, structural failures, and compatibility issues between legacy and modern components. This project proposes a computational framework to model leather biomechanics, adhesive-substrate interactions, and stress distribution in repaired footwear systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models to simulate mechanical wear on footwear under dynamic loading conditions, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to study the molecular-scale behavior of dyes, finishes, and adhesives, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict optimal repair protocols based on material composition and damage patterns. The FEA workflows will incorporate anisotropic material properties of leather and composite soles, while MD simulations will focus on interfacial bonding mechanisms between aged leather and modern repair materials. A curated dataset of material properties, historical repair outcomes, and environmental degradation factors will train ML models to recommend context-specific solutions. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for leather fatigue and adhesive failure thresholds, (2) optimized repair strategies for hybrid materials (e.g., vintage leather paired with 3D-printed components), and (3) an open-access simulation toolkit for the trade community. By reducing material waste through precision repair forecasting, this research aligns with circular economy goals while preserving artisanal craftsmanship. The scale of multi-physics simulations—requiring parallel processing of 10⁶–10⁷ element meshes and nanosecond-scale MD trajectories—necessitates HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity. This interdisciplinary approach bridges empirical craftsmanship with computational materials science, offering transformative potential for technical education programs and small-business repair operations worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair all types of footwear, including replacement and mending of worn parts, repairing orthopedic footwear, refinishing and dyeing leather, and repairing other leather goods such as handbags, belts, and luggage.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the structural and cultural dynamics of congregational hymnody across underrepresented religious traditions using computational methods, with a focus on patterns of melodic adaptation and lyrical transmission in diasporic communities. While existing scholarship has cataloged liturgical music within major traditions, the evolution of hymns in marginalized or syncretic practices—such as Indigenous Christian blends, Afro-Caribbean spirituals, or post-Soviet Baptist communities—remains understudied due to the scale and complexity of cross-cultural analysis required. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze a multilingual corpus of over 20,000 hymn texts and 15,000 audio recordings spanning 150 years, integrating optical music recognition (OMR), semantic network analysis, and phylogenetic modeling. Custom machine learning pipelines will identify melodic motifs and lyrical adaptations, tracing regional variations against historical migration data and ethnographic records. By parallelizing feature extraction across audio and textual datasets, the computational workflow will map how theological narratives and musical practices mutate in response to sociopolitical pressures, linguistic shifts, and interfaith contact. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated hymns, statistical models of cultural retention thresholds in displaced communities, and a framework for quantifying the interplay between musical complexity and congregational participation. This work bridges ethnomusicology, diaspora studies, and digital humanities, offering methodological innovations for analyzing cultural resilience through performative worship traditions. The scale of data processing—requiring GPU-accelerated OMR, distributed NLP for low-resource languages, and Monte Carlo simulations of transmission pathways—necessitates HPC resources to achieve feasible runtime for iterative model training and large-scale comparative analysis.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious music and worship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing the performance and sustainability of advanced textile materials through computational modeling of multi-scale structural and chemical interactions. Fiber-based materials, particularly synthetic-natural hybrid composites and functionalized textiles, exhibit complex behaviors arising from molecular-scale polymer dynamics, mesoscale fiber interactions, and macroscale mechanical responses. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to efficiently explore these interdependent phenomena, limiting the development of materials with tailored properties for applications in smart textiles, high-strength composites, and environmentally responsive fabrics. We propose an integrated computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model hierarchical material behavior across spatial and temporal scales. The MD component will simulate molecular interactions in novel polymer blends and dye-fiber systems, while FEA will predict mechanical performance under complex stress-strain conditions. ML models trained on simulation outputs and experimental datasets will identify optimal processing parameters for target material properties. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of multi-million-atom MD systems, coupled multi-physics FEA models, and neural network training on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models for (1) energy absorption in bio-inspired fiber composites, (2) chemical stability of sustainable dye alternatives under thermal stress, and (3) moisture-wicking behavior in hierarchically structured textiles. This work will establish computational design guidelines that reduce empirical trial cycles by 40-60% in prototyping phases, accelerating the development of high-performance materials with reduced environmental impact. The resource allocation will directly support the program's mission to advance textile engineering through computational innovation, with potential applications in protective gear, biomedical textiles, and recyclable composite systems. All developed models and datasets will be made available to the textile research community through an open-access repository.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to test and manufacture fibers and fiber products, both synthetic and natural; to develop new and improved fibers, textiles and their uses; and to the analysis of related engineering problems such as structural factors, molecular synthesis, chemical manufacturing, weaves, strength and stress, useful life, dyes, and applications to composite systems.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC) resources into the study of ceramic materials and processes to advance artistic innovation and technical precision in ceramic arts. Traditional approaches to developing ceramic bodies, glazes, and firing protocols rely heavily on iterative physical experimentation, which is time-intensive, resource-heavy, and constrained by material variability. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations by simulating the physicochemical behaviors of clay bodies and glazes under diverse compositional and thermal conditions, enabling data-driven predictions of aesthetic and structural outcomes. Proposed computational methods include molecular dynamics simulations to model clay-water interactions during forming stages, finite element analysis (FEA) to predict stress distributions in complex ceramic geometries during drying and firing, and machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on empirical datasets to correlate glaze chemistry with visual effects like color variation, texture, and surface reflectance. High-resolution thermal modeling of kiln environments will also be conducted to optimize energy efficiency and reduce firing anomalies. By leveraging HPC resources, these simulations will operate at scales necessary to capture microstructural evolution in clay matrices and glaze layers, which directly influence macroscale artistic properties. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for designing ceramic materials with tailored aesthetic features, reduced material waste, and reproducible firing protocols. This interdisciplinary approach bridges ceramic arts with materials science and computational engineering, offering novel tools for artists to expand creative possibilities while addressing sustainability challenges inherent in traditional practices. The project will also generate open-access datasets and models to support pedagogical innovation in ceramic arts education, fostering a new paradigm of computationally informed studio practice.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by producing art works out of clay and similar materials. Includes instruction in handbuilt and wheel thrown techniques; molding; slips and glazes; trimming and decorating; firing and kiln operation; oxidation; mixed media; ceramic murals; and personal style development.

abstract: Osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) leverages the interdependence of the musculoskeletal system and systemic health, yet the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain incompletely characterized. This project seeks to develop multiscale computational models to quantify how OMT-induced mechanical forces propagate through tissues, modulate cellular signaling, and influence systemic physiological outcomes. A critical barrier to progress is the integration of high-resolution biomechanical simulations with dynamic models of neuroimmune interactions, which requires computationally intensive iterative analyses across spatial and temporal scales. We propose using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled finite element and agent-based modeling framework. This framework will simulate OMT interventions on anatomically accurate, patient-derived musculoskeletal geometries (obtained via clinical imaging) to predict strain distribution in connective tissues, mechanotransduction in fibroblasts and immune cells, and downstream cytokine signaling. Machine learning pipelines will optimize model parameters using multi-omics datasets (transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiles from pre/post-OMT clinical samples) to identify mechanosensitive pathways implicated in OMT efficacy. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from in vitro cell-strain assays and in vivo motion capture/EMG studies. By elucidating how localized manual interventions translate to systemic health outcomes, this work aims to establish predictive models for personalizing OMT protocols in conditions such as chronic low back pain and inflammatory disorders. The project will generate open-source tools for simulating osteopathic techniques, advancing both clinical training and evidence-based practice. Successful execution requires HPC capabilities to manage large-scale parameter optimization, real-time visualization of 3D biomechanical cascades, and ensemble simulations accounting for interpatient variability. Outcomes will provide a foundational computational platform for bridging osteopathic principles with precision medicine paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of osteopathic medicine, involving a combination of medical principles and procedures and osteopathic principles of holistic medicine and the relationship of the musculoskeletal system to general health. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, preventive medicine, family and community medicine, medical informatics, disease systems, organ and physiologic systems, osteopathic principles and practice, osteopathic manipulative treatment, musculoskeletal and skin systems, clinical specialty rotations, medical ethics, and professional standards and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between microbial biofilm dynamics and microplastic transport in coastal hydrodynamic environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve multiscale interactions across biology, fluid dynamics, and polymer chemistry. Microplastics in marine systems act as vectors for microbial colonization and nutrient transport, yet the feedback mechanisms between biofilm growth, particle buoyancy, and turbulent flow remain poorly quantified. Current models treat these processes in isolation, neglecting emergent behaviors that influence microplastic aggregation, sedimentation, and degradation. We propose a novel computational framework integrating three-dimensional large-eddy simulation (LES) of wave-driven boundary layers with discrete element modeling (DEM) of biofilm-coated microplastics, coupled to agent-based simulations of microbial metabolism and extracellular polymer secretion. This approach requires HPC resources to resolve millimeter-scale biofilm-particle interactions within meter-scale hydrodynamic domains over ecologically relevant timescales (weeks to months). GPU-accelerated simulations will parameterize turbulent kinetic energy spectra, biofilm-induced drag modifications, and polymer weathering rates, validated against experimental flume data and field observations from instrumented buoy arrays. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of microplastic-biofilm hotspot formation under varying hydrodynamic regimes, quantified thresholds for biofilm-mediated sedimentation, and open-source modules for environmental fate models. By bridging microbial ecology, materials science, and environmental fluid mechanics, this work addresses a critical gap in forecasting anthropogenic impacts on coastal ecosystems while advancing computational methods for coupled biophysical systems. The requested allocation will enable unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution to capture nonlinear feedbacks at the biofilm-particle-flow interface, directly supporting natural resource management strategies and pollution mitigation frameworks.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on one or more of the physical and biological sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the evolution of cultural and gender identities across Pacific Islander communities through the computational analysis of multilingual textual archives and oral histories. The research addresses a critical gap in Pacific Studies: the systematic integration of large-scale, regionally dispersed cultural records—including digitized colonial-era manuscripts, post-independence literature, and transcribed oral narratives—to trace how Indigenous knowledge systems and gender roles have adapted to colonial and post-colonial disruptions. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the volume and linguistic diversity of these materials, which span English, French, and Indigenous languages such as Hawaiian, Māori, and Samoan. The proposed computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) tailored for low-resource languages, network analysis of narrative themes, and machine learning-driven semantic mapping to identify patterns in cultural retention, hybridity, and gendered agency across time and space. By parallelizing workflows across HPC nodes, the team will process over 50,000 multilingual documents and audio transcripts, enabling cross-regional comparisons of how Pacific Island communities navigated cultural erasure and reasserted Indigenous frameworks. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of analyzed texts, visualizations of cultural exchange networks, and new methodologies for ethically centering Indigenous perspectives in computational humanities. This work will provide scholars, educators, and Pacific communities with tools to interrogate colonial legacies while foregrounding Indigenous resilience, offering a model for decolonial computational research in Area Studies. The scale of data and need for iterative model training—particularly for under-resourced language models—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve rigorous, culturally nuanced results within project timelines.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Australasia and the Pacific Ocean, related island groups and bordering coastal regions, and including pre- and post-colonial migration patterns.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation research faces critical challenges in understanding the heterogeneous mechanisms underlying motor recovery and treatment response in children with neurological or musculoskeletal impairments. Traditional clinical assessments and small-scale datasets often lack the resolution to capture dynamic, patient-specific factors influencing rehabilitation outcomes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models integrating biomechanical, neurophysiological, and clinical data to predict individualized rehabilitation trajectories. The research will focus on children with cerebral palsy, spinal cord injuries, or acquired brain injuries, analyzing high-dimensional datasets from motion capture systems, wearable sensors, neuroimaging, and electronic health records. Computational methods will include finite element modeling of musculoskeletal dynamics, machine learning algorithms for pattern recognition in longitudinal outcomes, and network-based analyses of neuromotor control adaptations. By simulating intervention effects across virtual patient cohorts, the project aims to identify critical biomarkers of recovery and optimize therapy parameters. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, running parallelized simulations of biomechanical systems, and training deep neural networks on sparse clinical datasets through federated learning approaches. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific rehabilitation strategies to functional gains, validated against prospective clinical studies. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source tools to enable reproducible, data-driven decision-making in pediatric rehabilitation. This work addresses a pressing need for precision rehabilitation paradigms in pediatric populations, with potential to reduce trial-and-error treatment selection and improve long-term functional outcomes. The scale of data integration and computational complexity necessitates dedicated HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically meaningful results within practical timeframes, accelerating translation to real-world practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Rehabilitation

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the integration of Physician Assistants (PAs) into telemedicine-driven post-surgical care, addressing variability in recovery outcomes and resource utilization. As PAs increasingly manage post-operative monitoring in decentralized healthcare settings, systemic inefficiencies persist due to a lack of data-driven protocols tailored to their scope of practice. The study will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time biosensor data from wearable devices, and PA decision logs, to model patient recovery trajectories under varying care pathways. Machine learning algorithms will identify critical intervention windows where PA-led telehealth interactions most effectively mitigate complications, while agent-based simulations will test strategies for balancing caseloads and triaging high-risk patients. Computational models will be validated against retrospective surgical outcomes data from hybrid care models deployed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to personalize PA involvement in post-acute care coordination and simulation-generated workflow templates that reduce 30-day readmission rates by ≥15% in benchmark scenarios. By quantifying how PA expertise complements surgeon-led teams in virtual care environments, this work aims to establish scalable frameworks for maximizing PA impact in specialized surgical subspecialties, particularly in resource-constrained regions lacking onsite specialist coverage. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale clinical datasets and concurrent execution of complex simulation ensembles, which are computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice medicine, including diagnoses and treatment therapies, under the supervision of a physician. Includes instruction in the basic medical and clinical sciences and specialized preparation in fields such as family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, gynecology, general surgery, psychiatry, and behavioral medicine; the delivery of health care services to homebound patients, rural populations, and underserved populations; and community health services.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing irrigation efficiency in diverse agricultural systems through advanced computational modeling. Traditional irrigation management strategies often rely on static schedules or generalized climate data, leading to over- or under-watering due to dynamic environmental variables, heterogeneous soil properties, and crop-specific water requirements. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a high-resolution, machine learning-integrated simulation framework that dynamically models water transport in soil-plant-atmosphere systems. The framework will incorporate real-time sensor data (e.g., soil moisture, evapotranspiration rates, and localized weather forecasts) with crop growth models to predict site-specific irrigation needs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale spatial datasets, execute parallelized hydrological simulations across variable terrains, and train deep learning models that adapt to shifting climatic conditions and crop responses. Key computational tasks include finite element analysis of subsurface water flow, Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification for sensor data integration, and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize irrigation scheduling under resource constraints. The expected outcomes include predictive models that reduce water waste by 15–30% compared to conventional methods while maintaining crop yield targets, as well as open-source tools for adaptive irrigation decision-making. By enabling precision at scale, this work will directly support agricultural producers in mitigating water scarcity risks and operationalizing climate-resilient practices. The HPC-driven approach bridges gaps between theoretical models and field-level implementation, advancing both irrigation technology and computational applications in agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in the field of agricultural technology and irrigation. Includes instruction in irrigation and drainage methodologies, pumping and delivery systems, system design and evaluation, and principles of installation and repair of irrigation systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural and material networks of the ancient Mediterranean world. Traditional methodologies in classical and ancient studies often struggle to synthesize fragmentary archaeological, textual, and epigraphic data at scale, limiting insights into long-term patterns of exchange, migration, and cultural adaptation. Our research addresses this gap by developing computational models to analyze spatially and temporally distributed datasets spanning the 1st millennium BCE, including trade artifacts, linguistic variations in inscriptions, and settlement patterns. Using graph-based network analysis, agent-based modeling, and machine learning classifiers, we will reconstruct dynamic interactions between urban centers, peripheral communities, and environmental factors. The scale of data integration—encompassing over 50,000 cataloged artifacts, 15,000+ inscriptions, and paleoenvironmental records—requires HPC resources to manage memory-intensive graph computations and iterative simulations. Key objectives include identifying latent connectivity patterns in trade routes, modeling the diffusion of cultural practices under climatic stressors, and quantifying the role of maritime vs. overland pathways in knowledge transmission. Expected outcomes include open-access digital tools for ancient network analysis, a publicly accessible geotemporal database of curated datasets, and peer-reviewed publications re-evaluating assumptions about "core-periphery" dynamics in antiquity. By integrating computational methods with domain-specific expertise in philology, archaeology, and ancient history, this project aims to establish a new framework for data-driven inquiry in classical studies while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources for humanities scholarship. The results will provide actionable insights for heritage preservation policies and stimulate cross-disciplinary dialogue on complexity in premodern societies.
cip_definition: Any program in classical and ancient studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized biomechanical models for optimizing non-invasive neuromodulation therapies in patients with vocal fold paralysis (VFP). VFP, a debilitating condition affecting speech and swallowing, is traditionally managed through surgical interventions or voice therapy, yet outcomes remain inconsistent due to interpatient variability in laryngeal anatomy and neural recovery patterns. Current approaches lack the capacity to dynamically simulate patient-specific neuromuscular responses to emerging non-invasive techniques, such as transcutaneous electrical stimulation (TES). To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating high-resolution laryngeal imaging data, finite element modeling of electrical field distributions, and biophysically grounded neural activation algorithms. The research will utilize HPC clusters to process multimodal datasets (CT/MRI, electromyography) from a retrospective cohort of 50 VFP patients, constructing 3D finite element models of individualized laryngeal geometries. Machine learning pipelines will then iteratively optimize stimulation parameters (electrode placement, current amplitude, frequency) to predict neuromuscular recruitment patterns while minimizing off-target effects. Validation will involve cross-referencing computational predictions with clinical outcomes from a prospective pilot study (n=15). By enabling real-time, patient-specific simulations of TES interventions, this work aims to establish a paradigm for precision neuromodulation in otolaryngology, reducing reliance on trial-and-error therapeutic strategies. The anticipated outcomes include open-source computational tools for laryngeal biomechanics modeling and a foundation for integrating HPC-driven predictive analytics into clinical decision-making workflows. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between computational biomechanics, neural engineering, and rehabilitative medicine, offering a template for advancing personalized therapies in understudied neuromuscular disorders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical professional preparation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision-support tool to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of initial diagnostic image observations performed by radiologist assistants (RAs). While RAs play a critical role in triaging imaging studies, variability in human interpretation and increasing imaging workloads pose challenges to timely, consistent evaluations. We propose to train deep learning models to automatically identify anomalies in common radiographic studies—including X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs—and provide probabilistic assessments to guide RA decision-making. The research problem centers on optimizing model generalizability across diverse patient populations and imaging protocols while maintaining clinical interpretability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets of de-identified imaging studies from partnering healthcare institutions, which include annotated findings spanning musculoskeletal, thoracic, and abdominal pathologies. Computational workflows will involve distributed training of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers using TensorFlow and PyTorch, with hyperparameter optimization via Bayesian methods. Memory-intensive preprocessing steps, such as 3D volumetric analysis of CT/MRI series and domain adaptation to address scanner-specific heterogeneity, will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes. Validation will compare model performance against RA preliminary assessments in a retrospective cohort, measuring sensitivity, specificity, and time-to-detection metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive AI-assisted image triage, validated against clinical standards, which could reduce diagnostic oversights and streamline workflows. The project aligns with the Radiologist Assistant program’s emphasis on enhancing procedural and analytical competencies in emerging technologies. By integrating computational rigor with clinical workflows, this work aims to empower RAs with scalable tools that complement—rather than replace—their critical judgment, ultimately supporting safer and more efficient patient care pathways.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to perform patient assessment, patient management, selected imaging procedures and to make initial observations of diagnostic images. Includes instruction in radiologic procedures and techniques, cross sectional anatomy, pharmacology, pathophysiology, patient assessment, patient care and management, and radiation biology.

abstract: Soil degradation driven by chemical and physical processes poses a critical challenge to agricultural productivity and environmental sustainability. A key knowledge gap lies in understanding how microscale interactions between soil organic matter, mineral surfaces, and fluid phases govern macroscale phenomena such as nutrient leaching, carbon sequestration, and structural stability. This project seeks to develop multiscale computational models that bridge molecular-level soil chemistry with continuum-scale physical behavior to predict soil responses under varying agricultural management practices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to parameterize reactive transport models using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of organic-mineral interfacial reactions, coupled with finite element analyses of pore-scale fluid dynamics in heterogeneous soil architectures. The MD simulations will quantify binding energies, ion exchange kinetics, and colloidal stability for organo-clay complexes across thermodynamic gradients, while continuum models will resolve advection-diffusion processes in 3D soil structures derived from X-ray microtomography data. Machine learning techniques will be employed to upscale molecular interactions into predictive frameworks for soil hydraulic conductivity and nutrient retention capacity. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source modeling platform for simulating soil biogeochemical processes across spatial scales, (2) mechanistic insights into how organic amendments alter soil-water retention curves and cation exchange capacities, and (3) optimization strategies for tillage practices and fertilizer applications that minimize nutrient loss. By integrating quantum-chemical calculations with macroscopic transport physics, this work will advance precision soil management approaches that enhance agricultural resilience while maintaining computational feasibility through GPU-accelerated HPC implementations. The requested resources will enable simulations at previously unattainable resolutions, directly supporting the program's mission to apply fundamental chemical and physical principles to sustainable soil stewardship.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and physical principles to research and analysis concerning the nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instruction in soil and fluid mechanics, mineralogy, sedimentology, thermodynamics, geomorphology, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive computational framework to model and optimize decentralized information ecosystems, with a focus on ecological monitoring networks that integrate heterogeneous sensor data, citizen science inputs, and legacy biodiversity records. The research addresses the challenge of real-time knowledge synthesis in environmental informatics, where current systems struggle with scaling multi-modal data streams while maintaining semantic consistency, provenance tracking, and low-latency decision support. Our methodology combines graph neural networks with probabilistic knowledge fusion techniques to create dynamic representations of ecological states across spatial-temporal scales. The computational approach requires distributed training of attention-based architectures on streaming data from 40+ biodiversity observation platforms while maintaining synchronization with centralized taxonomic authority files. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: 1) Continuous integration of unstructured citizen reports through transformer-based semantic alignment, 2) Multi-objective optimization of sensor network configurations under resource constraints, and 3) Ensemble forecasting of ecosystem tipping points using coupled physical-digital twin simulations. The proposed framework will leverage GPU-accelerated graph databases and parallelized Bayesian inference pipelines to enable hourly updates of regional biodiversity dashboards. Expected outcomes include a novel architecture for hybrid human-AI ecological intelligence systems, benchmarked against traditional centralized monitoring approaches in three bioregions. This work advances informatics foundations for collective environmental knowledge systems while developing transferrable methods for quality-aware information integration across decentralized networks. Successful implementation will provide open-source tools for adaptive resource allocation in participatory sensing infrastructures and establish performance baselines for edge-cloud orchestration in community-driven conservation informatics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the emergence and propagation of nonlinear economic cascades in heterogeneous agent-based markets using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Traditional macroeconomic models often rely on representative agent frameworks, which inadequately capture systemic risks arising from heterogeneous decision-making, cognitive biases, and network-dependent interactions observed in real-world financial systems. We propose developing a multilayer network model integrating behavioral microfoundations from cognitive science with dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) components, enabling analysis of how localized shocks propagate through interconnected credit, production, and information networks. The computational approach combines massively parallelized agent-based simulations with numerical solutions to high-dimensional partial differential equations describing market-clearing conditions under bounded rationality constraints. Key innovations include adaptive graph neural networks to model evolving interbank exposures and a novel entropy-regularized optimization framework for approximating strategic complementarities in decentralized markets. HPC resources will be critical for processing agent-level decision trees across 10^6+ heterogeneous entities, solving inverse problems in network reconstruction via Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, and conducting sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces exceeding 10^8 configurations. Expected outcomes include quantitative metrics for early warning signals of cascade failures, policy-relevant insights into the resilience of modular versus centralized financial architectures, and open-source algorithmic tools for stress-testing economic networks under non-Gaussian shock distributions. This work bridges theoretical gaps between behavioral economics, complex systems science, and computational statistics while providing empirically grounded methods for monitoring systemic risk in increasingly digitalized markets. The requested computing resources will enable unprecedented scale in simulating hybrid mechanistic-phenomenological market dynamics, advancing predictive capabilities at the intersection of economic theory and data-driven complexity science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical methods to the development of economic theory, models, and quantitative analysis. Includes instruction in data analysis, applied business economics, calculus, econometrics, linear algebra, microeconomic theory, probability, and statistical methods.

abstract: The relentless scaling of semiconductor technologies toward sub-10nm nodes and the proliferation of heterogeneous 3D-integrated circuits (3D-ICs) have introduced unprecedented challenges in circuit design, including parasitic effects, thermal management, and electromagnetic interference. Traditional simulation tools and local computing resources are insufficient to address the multi-physics complexity and vast design spaces of modern integrated circuits, leading to suboptimal performance, extended development cycles, and costly post-fabrication revisions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, parallelized simulations for optimizing next-generation IC designs. The research will focus on two interconnected thrusts: (1) developing machine learning (ML)-accelerated models for predicting parasitic capacitance and inductance in advanced node interconnects, and (2) implementing coupled electro-thermal simulations for 3D-IC architectures using finite-element analysis and computational fluid dynamics. The computational workflow will leverage distributed memory parallelism for Monte Carlo-based variation analysis and GPU-accelerated tensor operations for training neural networks on TCAD-generated datasets. By scaling simulations across hundreds of nodes, the project aims to reduce parameter sweep times from weeks to days while maintaining nanometer-scale accuracy. Expected outcomes include validated design guidelines for mitigating crosstalk in high-density routing, optimized thermal through-silicon-via (TSV) configurations, and open-source scripts for automated HPC job orchestration in commercial EDA tools. These results will directly benefit industry partners transitioning to 3D-IC platforms and academic researchers investigating materials-aware circuit design. The requested resources will also support the integration of HPC methodologies into graduate curricula, training students in scalable simulation techniques critical for advancing semiconductor innovation in areas such as edge AI hardware and ultra-low-power IoT devices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to design circuits in microelectronics. Includes instruction in circuit design, circuit layout, circuit analysis, computer-aided drafting, and semi-conductor technologies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of radiation therapy planning, diagnostic imaging optimization, and radiopharmaceutical dosimetry demands advanced computational tools to address unresolved challenges in clinical radiologic physics. Current limitations in modeling radiation-tissue interactions, particularly for heterogeneous anatomies and emerging modalities like MRI-guided radiotherapy and alpha-emitting radionuclides, restrict the precision of treatment delivery and diagnostic accuracy. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity, multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate radiation transport, energy deposition, and biological effect prediction across therapeutic, diagnostic, and nuclear medicine applications. The research will implement GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations (using Geant4/GATE toolkits) coupled with finite element biomechanical models to account for patient-specific tissue heterogeneity and dynamic motion (e.g., respiratory shifts, cardiac cycles). Machine learning architectures will be trained on simulated and clinical datasets to optimize real-time adaptive radiotherapy dose calculations and reduce uncertainties in SPECT/CT quantitative imaging. A dedicated focus will address the computational bottlenecks in modeling short-range alpha-particle interactions for targeted radionuclide therapy, requiring massively parallelized track structure simulations. The HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10^6+ beam configurations, 4D anatomical phantoms, and radiobiological models incorporating DNA damage repair kinetics. Expected outcomes include validated open-source modules for clinical translation, reducing systematic errors in tumor control probability calculations by ≥15% compared to current commercial algorithms. The work will directly inform safety protocols for FLASH proton therapy and improve dosimetric accuracy for pediatric nuclear medicine patients, addressing critical gaps in personalized radiologic care. By integrating HPC-driven insights into clinical workflows, this project aims to establish scalable computational standards for next-generation radiologic physics applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on that branch of physics which includes the physical aspects of radiation therapy, radiologic diagnosis, and/or nuclear medicine. Radiologic physicists must specialize in at least one of the three subspecialty areas: therapeutic radiological physics, diagnostic radiological physics, and/or medical nuclear physics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the transmission of cultural and intellectual traditions across medieval and Renaissance Europe. A central challenge in studying premodern textual, artistic, and musical exchange lies in analyzing vast, fragmented datasets—including digitized manuscripts, archival records, and iconographic corpora—that require computational methods to identify patterns of influence, adaptation, and regional variation. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to systematically trace thematic or stylistic connections across multilingual sources spanning centuries. Our team proposes to address this by developing a computational pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning models optimized for historical languages (e.g., Latin, Old French, Middle English) and visual motif recognition. Key objectives include training domain-specific language models on curated corpora of digitized texts (500,000+ pages from partner libraries) and implementing graph-based algorithms to map the diffusion of literary motifs and artistic conventions. A parallel workflow will apply computer vision techniques to analyze 3D-scanned artifacts and paintings, correlating stylistic features with sociopolitical metadata. By deploying these workflows on HPC infrastructure, we aim to process terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining the granularity necessary for humanistic inquiry. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of cultural exchange networks (1100–1600 CE), computational tools tailored for premodern source analysis, and interdisciplinary publications re-evaluating cross-regional dynamics in medieval-Renaissance transitions. This work will provide novel methodologies for synthesizing dispersed cultural heritage materials while offering scalable models for computationally assisted humanities research. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks such as training multimodal neural networks and conducting large-scale simulations of transmission pathways across reconstructed historical geographies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the Medieval and/or Renaissance periods in European and circum-Mediterranean history from the perspective of various disciplines in the humanities and social sciences, including history and archeology, as well as studies of period art and music.

abstract: Surgical wound healing and tissue reconstruction outcomes remain highly variable due to complex interactions between patient-specific biological factors, surgical techniques, and postoperative care. Current clinical models lack the resolution to predict individualized healing trajectories or optimize reconstructive strategies, leading to preventable complications such as dehiscence, infection, and poor aesthetic outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to model multiscale wound healing dynamics and simulate reconstructive outcomes under diverse biological and biomechanical conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate patient-derived genomic, proteomic, and imaging data with mechanistic models of cellular behavior, extracellular matrix remodeling, and mechanical stress distributions. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular interactions during inflammation and proliferation phases, while finite element analyses will predict tissue deformation and perfusion in complex anatomical geometries. Machine learning pipelines will identify predictive biomarkers from multi-omics datasets and clinical records, enabling risk stratification. The computational platform will be validated against a retrospective cohort of 850 surgical cases with longitudinal wound imaging and histopathological data. By enabling real-time simulation of hypothetical surgical interventions—including flap design modifications or adjunct therapies—this resource will advance personalized decision-making in reconstructive surgery. Anticipated outcomes include a validated predictive tool for wound complication risks, biomechanical guidelines for flap design optimization, and novel biomarkers for targeted therapies. The HPC environment is critical for scaling spatially explicit simulations across anatomical variability, managing high-dimensional data integration, and enabling rapid parameter sweeps to test clinical hypotheses. This work bridges computational systems biology and surgical innovation, with potential to reduce revision surgeries, improve functional recovery, and lower healthcare costs in complex wound management.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: Understanding the molecular mechanisms of enzyme catalysis and regulation remains a central challenge in chemical biology, particularly for systems where experimental characterization of transient intermediates or allosteric networks is limited. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic behavior and chemical interactions underlying enzymatic function, focusing on ATP-dependent enzymes implicated in cellular signaling and metabolic dysregulation. Traditional experimental techniques often lack the spatiotemporal resolution to capture rapid conformational changes or solvent-mediated proton transfers critical to catalytic cycles. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational approach combining quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations, enhanced sampling methods, and machine learning-guided free energy calculations. These methods will model enzyme-substrate complexes at atomic resolution, map reaction pathways, and quantify the energetic contributions of key residues and cofactors. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will further probe allosteric communication networks by analyzing correlated motions across microsecond timescales. The computational workflows demand significant parallel processing capabilities, particularly for ab initio QM/MM simulations and Markov state model construction, necessitating access to GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory resources. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into enzymatic fidelity and allostery, with direct implications for designing small-molecule modulators or engineering enzymes for biocatalytic applications. By integrating computational predictions with ongoing experimental validations (e.g., kinetic assays, X-ray crystallography), this work will establish a framework for interrogating complex biochemical systems at unprecedented detail. The requested resources will enable the execution of computationally intensive tasks that are otherwise infeasible on local clusters, accelerating discovery in chemical biology and fostering collaboration with experimental groups.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the chemical principles of biological functions, based on the methods and theories in chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize institutional foodservice operations through advanced computational modeling of dynamic supply chain and labor allocation challenges, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in real-time decision-making. Traditional foodservice management relies on static models ill-equipped to handle fluctuating demand, perishable inventory constraints, and staff scheduling variables in institutional settings such as hospitals, universities, and correctional facilities. The research problem centers on developing a scalable simulation framework to model complex interactions between procurement workflows, nutritional compliance, waste reduction targets, and workforce productivity—a gap exacerbated by the absence of integrated computational tools tailored to non-commercial food systems. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation, agent-based modeling, and machine learning algorithms to process multi-source operational data, including historical meal demand patterns, real-time IoT sensor inputs from storage facilities, and staff performance metrics. HPC resources will enable parallelized scenario testing across diverse institutional profiles (e.g., varying bed counts in hospitals or academic calendars in universities) while maintaining sub-hourly temporal resolution for 12-month operational cycles. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of predicting optimal vendor order thresholds, dynamically adjusting prep schedules to minimize waste, and balancing temporary staffing needs against overtime costs. Validation will utilize anonymized data from a multi-state hospital network, with model accuracy benchmarks targeting ≥15% reduction in perishable stockouts and 20% improvement in labor-hour utilization compared to current industry standards. By formalizing computational strategies for these understudied operational intersections, this work aims to establish scalable best practices for resource-constrained institutional foodservices while advancing methodological innovation in non-STEM applied systems analytics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practices relating to the administration of food service systems in institutional settings, and that prepares individuals to manage such operations in public and private facilities. Includes instruction in human nutrition, food safety, the design and organization of food service systems, purchasing, personnel management, and related business practices.

abstract: This project investigates the optimization of information resilience in decentralized knowledge networks through computational modeling of dynamic trust propagation and data prioritization strategies. As distributed information ecosystems grow in scale and complexity—from community-driven environmental monitoring networks to federated research repositories—existing approaches struggle to balance integrity, accessibility, and adaptability across heterogeneous nodes with varying capabilities and reliability. The research addresses this gap by developing a novel framework that integrates temporal graph neural networks with multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate emergent information flow patterns under resource constraints. High-performance computing resources are essential for training and validating models across large-scale synthetic networks (10^5-10^6 nodes) that capture realistic topological diversity, dynamic membership changes, and evolving trust relationships. Computational experiments will systematically evaluate how adaptive resource allocation strategies affect system-wide metrics of information persistence, latency, and consensus formation under simulated adversarial conditions (e.g., misinformation injection, node failures). The project advances information science methodologies by bridging discrete network analysis with continuous trust dynamics modeling, while providing practical insights for designing robust decentralized knowledge infrastructures. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation tools for stress-testing distributed information systems and evidence-based guidelines for protocol parameterization in resource-constrained environments. This work directly contributes to the interdisciplinary study of socio-technical information systems, offering new approaches to preserve information utility in emerging applications such as participatory sensing networks and crisis response coordination platforms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, organization, and process of information collection, transmission, and utilization in traditional and electronic forms. Includes instruction in information classification and organization; information storage and processing; transmission, transfer, and signaling; communications and networking; systems planning and design; human interfacing and use analysis; database development; information policy analysis; and related aspects of hardware, software, economics, social factors, and capacity.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a quantum machine learning (QML) framework for optimizing algorithmic trading strategies in high-frequency financial markets. While traditional machine learning models have been applied to predictive trading, their efficacy is constrained by the nonlinear complexity of market microstructure data and latency limitations. The research problem centers on overcoming these barriers by integrating quantum computing principles—such as quantum parallelism and entanglement—into adaptive trading algorithms, enabling real-time analysis of multi-modal data streams (order book dynamics, macroeconomic indicators, and sentiment-driven news feeds). The computational approach involves simulating hybrid quantum-classical neural networks on GPU clusters to model market anomalies, followed by quantum annealing processes to optimize trade execution paths under stochastic volatility regimes. A proprietary dataset comprising 10 years of global equities trading data (structured and unstructured) will be used to train and validate the models. Key challenges include mitigating quantum noise in simulated environments and achieving sub-millisecond inference speeds compatible with live trading systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable QML architecture demonstrating superior risk-adjusted returns compared to classical reinforcement learning benchmarks, as well as novel metrics for quantifying quantum advantage in financial decision-making. The project’s significance lies in its potential to redefine computational efficiency boundaries in fintech, offering insights into how emergent quantum technologies can address combinatorial optimization problems inherent to liquidity management and arbitrage detection. By open-sourcing select modules, this work will also contribute foundational tools for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of quantum computing, computational finance, and decentralized financial infrastructure. Successful implementation requires sustained access to HPC resources for large-scale quantum circuit simulations, concurrent Monte Carlo experiments, and real-time backtesting across distributed memory systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform a wide variety of customer services in banks, insurance agencies, savings and loan companies, and related enterprises. Includes instruction in communications and public relations skills, business equipment operation, and technical skills applicable to the methods and operations of specific financial or insurance services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets and model complex socio-cultural dynamics across pre-modern and early modern societies. The research problem centers on identifying and interpreting patterns of social change, economic exchange, and political conflict in understudied regions, using fragmented or heterogeneous archival sources that resist conventional qualitative analysis. By applying computational methods to digitized records—including merchant ledgers, census fragments, and correspondence networks—the project aims to reconstruct probabilistic models of historical processes that are otherwise obscured by gaps in traditional archives. Key computational approaches include natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis, agent-based modeling to simulate decision-making in trade networks, and graph-based algorithms to map shifting alliances in political systems. These methods require HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (terabytes of text and tabular records), the need for parallel processing to iteratively refine models, and the resource-intensive nature of uncertainty quantification in historical reconstructions. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for historical data integration, novel visualizations of temporal-spatial relationships in archival materials, and peer-reviewed publications re-evaluating theories of state formation and cross-cultural exchange. The project will also produce annotated datasets for public reuse, fostering collaboration between computational researchers and historians. By demonstrating how HPC can address historiographical challenges—such as reconciling conflicting primary sources or modeling counterfactual scenarios—this work aims to expand methodological frontiers in digital humanities while generating empirically grounded insights into the longue durée of human societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study and interpretation of the past, including the gathering, recording, synthesizing and criticizing of evidence and theories about past events. Includes instruction in historiography; historical research methods; studies of specific periods, issues and cultures; and applications to areas such as historic preservation, public policy, and records administration.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the modeling of aerothermodynamic phenomena in hypersonic re-entry vehicles through high-fidelity simulations of transitional flow regimes and material response under extreme thermal loads. Current predictive tools for coupled fluid-structure interactions in rarefied and continuum flow regimes lack the resolution to capture multiscale turbulence, gas-surface chemistry, and ablation effects simultaneously, leading to uncertainties in thermal protection system (TPS) design for crewed and uncrewed spacecraft. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating direct numerical simulation (DNS) of compressible Navier-Stokes equations with a kinetic Monte Carlo approach for surface degradation modeling. The simulations will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve boundary layer transitions, shock-shock interactions, and carbon-composite material pyrolysis across Mach 10–25 conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical due to the need for billion-cell meshes, transient simulations spanning milliseconds to seconds of physical time, and ensemble runs to quantify uncertainty in material property inputs. Expected outcomes include validated models for oxide layer formation and recession rates in phenolic-impregnated carbon ablators, with direct applications to next-generation lunar return capsules and Mars ascent vehicles.
