The computational datasets will inform reduced-order models for real-time trajectory planning tools and establish best practices for coupling hypersonic flow solvers with material response codes at scale. Successful implementation requires access to parallel architectures optimized for memory-intensive workloads, with allocations supporting 10,000+ core-hour jobs and petabyte-scale output for post-processing vortex dynamics and heat flux distributions. This work aligns with national priorities in safe human space exploration and addresses foundational gaps in aerothermoelasticity identified in the Decadal Survey on Aeronautics.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any program in aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, or space engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance applied demographic research on the spatial and temporal dynamics of aging populations in urban and rural regions. The research problem centers on modeling complex interactions between demographic shifts, healthcare accessibility, and infrastructure demands under varying policy and environmental scenarios. Current models lack the granularity to integrate high-resolution census data, real-time health system metrics, and geospatial variables at scale, limiting their utility for localized decision-making. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling, Bayesian hierarchical regression, and geospatial simulation techniques. The agent-based component will simulate individual-level migration, health, and economic behaviors across multi-generational cohorts, while Bayesian methods will quantify uncertainty in projections of population aging and service needs. Geospatial simulations will incorporate satellite-derived land-use data and transportation networks to assess accessibility disparities. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of integrated demographic records (IPUMS, CDC WONDER) and geospatial layers (OpenStreetMap, Landsat), running parallelized simulations across 50+ policy scenarios, and performing sensitivity analyses via Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. Expected outcomes include: 1) open-source models predicting sub-county population health needs under climate migration and healthcare policy changes, 2) visualization tools mapping 10-year accessibility gaps in elder care infrastructure, and 3) uncertainty-adjusted projections to guide municipal budget allocations. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of multidimensional demographic data, this work will provide actionable insights for health departments and urban planners while advancing methodological integration in applied demography. The requested resources directly support scalability beyond pilot regions, reducing runtime for spatial microsimulations from weeks to days.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the practical application of demographic methods and materials for decision-making in business, education, health, and government. Includes instruction in statistics, research methods, geographic information systems, and demographic methods and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the relationship between artistic expression and psychological states, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to advance preparatory research for evidence-based art therapy practices. While art therapy relies on qualitative interpretation of creative works to assess mental health, there is a critical gap in scalable, quantitative tools to systematically evaluate artistic outputs and correlate them with standardized psychometric data. This limits the reproducibility of assessments and hinders the development of predictive models for therapeutic outcomes. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining computer vision, machine learning, and psychometric analysis. The project will utilize neural networks trained on annotated datasets of digital art created by participants in pre-art therapy programs, paired with longitudinal mental health assessments (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7 scores). HPC resources will enable large-scale processing of high-resolution artwork, extraction of multimodal features (color distributions, brushstroke patterns, compositional complexity), and integration with behavioral data through federated learning architectures. Key computational challenges include managing heterogeneous data types, mitigating bias in artistic style interpretation, and ensuring privacy-preserving analysis of sensitive health information. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for quantifying expressive elements in therapeutic art, (2) predictive models linking specific artistic features to mental health trajectories, and (3) a benchmark dataset for computational art therapy research. By establishing quantitative bridges between creative practice and clinical metrics, this work will provide pre-art therapy students with novel computational literacy tools while informing the design of future clinical art therapy programs. The requested HPC allocation will directly support GPU-intensive model training, parallel processing of 10,000+ artwork images, and simulations testing therapeutic intervention scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional art therapy program.

abstract: The proliferation of high-resolution, multidimensional media in contemporary visual arts has introduced significant computational challenges, particularly in projects requiring real-time interactivity, machine learning-driven synthesis, or large-scale archival analysis. Existing consumer-grade hardware struggles to process ultra-high-resolution (8K+) video streams, complex generative neural networks, or photogrammetric 3D reconstructions of cultural heritage artifacts within artistically viable timeframes. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a hybrid pipeline integrating GPU-accelerated rendering, distributed deep learning, and parallelized simulation of light-field datasets. Central to this effort is the training of a diffusion model on a terabyte-scale corpus of historical photographic negatives—digitized at 16-bit depth—to automate the restoration of degraded visual materials while preserving artistic intent. Concurrently, the research will prototype a real-time, interactive environment for 4D (3D+time) video synthesis, employing ray-tracing clusters to simulate dynamic volumetric scenes derived from multi-camera arrays. These workflows demand petabytes of storage, hundreds of simultaneous GPU threads, and low-latency inter-node communication to maintain frame coherence in output streams. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source framework for computational media artists, quantitative benchmarks for HPC adoption in visual arts practice, and a publicly accessible dataset linking computational aesthetics with archival preservation metrics. By establishing scalable workflows for next-generation media creation, this work aims to redefine the technical and conceptual boundaries of computationally intensive visual arts practice while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between media studies and high-performance computing domains.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_title: Film/ Video and Photographic Arts, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in film/video and photographic arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of patient outcomes in clinical support workflows, a critical challenge in allied health and medical assisting services. The research addresses the growing complexity of patient triage and resource allocation in outpatient and emergency care settings, where variability in patient acuity, staffing constraints, and evolving clinical protocols create inefficiencies that impact care quality. Current approaches to workflow optimization rely on retrospective data analyses or simplified heuristic models, which lack the capacity to integrate real-time multi-modal data (e.g., electronic health records, sensor-derived vitals, imaging metadata) or adapt to dynamic operational conditions. To address this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework capable of simulating patient flow scenarios and predicting bottlenecks using high-dimensional datasets. The computational approach will involve training ensemble models on historical patient interaction data (demographics, diagnostic codes, time-to-service metrics) and validating them against synthetic datasets generated via agent-based modeling. HPC resources will enable parallelized hyperparameter optimization, large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to account for operational uncertainty, and real-time inference testing under varying resource constraints. Key outcomes include a deployable decision-support tool for medical assistants and clinic managers, designed to recommend optimal patient prioritization and staff assignment strategies. The project’s significance lies in its potential to reduce wait times, improve resource utilization, and mitigate clinician burnout in high-volume care environments. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with clinical workflows, this work aligns with broader efforts to enhance precision in medical operational decision-making while maintaining compliance with evolving healthcare standards. All models and simulation pipelines will be made accessible to the allied health research community to support reproducibility and scalability across care settings.
cip_title: Allied Health and Medical Assisting Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health and medical assisting services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The intensifying challenges of climate variability and soil degradation necessitate advanced strategies to optimize crop resilience and nutrient efficiency. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational model to simulate genotype-environment-management (GxExM) interactions in staple crops under dynamic soil conditions, with a focus on nitrogen and phosphorus cycling. Current models lack the granularity to resolve root-soil-microbe feedbacks at scale, limiting their utility for precision agriculture. We propose a hybrid approach integrating mechanistic soil biogeochemistry models with machine learning (ML) to predict crop performance across heterogeneous field environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable (1) large-scale parameterization of partial differential equation systems describing nutrient transport and root exudation dynamics, (2) ensemble simulations of crop growth responses under 10^4 distinct soil-climate scenarios derived from historical and projected weather data, and (3) training of deep neural networks on the resultant datasets to identify optimal fertilization strategies. The computational framework will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for soil hydrology and parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification. Validation will utilize multi-year field trial data from collaborating institutions, incorporating hyperspectral imagery and rhizosphere microbiome sequencing. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive nutrient management and novel biomarkers for root efficiency traits. By elucidating nonlinear relationships between soil heterogeneity, microbial communities, and crop productivity, this work will directly inform breeding programs and reduce fertilizer waste in row-crop systems. The requested HPC allocation is critical for achieving biologically realistic spatiotemporal resolutions in simulations, which cannot be processed on local clusters due to memory constraints and the combinatorial complexity of GxExM interactions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the chemical, physical, and biological relationships of crops and the soils nurturing them. Includes instruction in the growth and behavior of agricultural crops, the development of new plant varieties, and the scientific management of soils and nutrients for maximum plant nutrition, health, and productivity.

abstract: Costume design for theater and performing arts requires balancing historical accuracy, aesthetic innovation, and practical functionality under constrained timelines. Current workflows rely heavily on manual iteration for fabric selection, movement simulation, and environmental interaction (e.g., lighting effects), leading to inefficiencies in prototyping and material waste. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and optimize costume design parameters at scale. The research problem centers on modeling complex, dynamic interactions between textiles, performer movement, and stage environments—tasks that exceed the capabilities of standard design software. Using physics-based simulation engines and machine learning (ML), we will quantify how diverse fabrics respond to biomechanical stresses, airflow, and light absorption across performance durations. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 100+ material variants under variable stage conditions (e.g., temperature, humidity) and motion-captured choreography datasets. A convolutional neural network will be trained to predict visual outcomes (e.g., drape, reflectivity) from simulated data, accelerating iterative design adjustments. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will propose historically plausible yet novel costume designs by analyzing archival records of period garments. Outcomes will include an open-access toolkit for simulating material-stage interactions and a database linking fabric properties to performance requirements. This work aims to reduce physical prototyping by 40–60% in preliminary testing phases, lowering costs and environmental impacts while preserving creative flexibility. By integrating computational methods into costume design workflows, the project bridges performing arts practice with data-driven innovation, offering new methodologies for interdisciplinary collaboration in theater production. The requested GPU nodes and high-memory nodes are critical for handling large-scale 3D rendering, ML model training, and real-time multi-physics simulations.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and select costumes for characters in theatre and the performing arts and to serve as part of a production team. Includes instruction in costume design, script analysis, theory and criticism, period styles, history of costume, stage makeup, rendering, and costume construction.

abstract: Medical office management faces growing complexity due to evolving regulatory requirements, dynamic patient scheduling demands, and the integration of heterogeneous data streams from electronic health records (EHRs), billing systems, and operational workflows. Current decision-support tools often rely on simplified heuristics that fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between administrative variables, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and operational inefficiencies. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to model medical office operations as adaptive systems, with the goal of identifying context-sensitive strategies for staff scheduling, patient flow optimization, and compliance risk mitigation. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between patients, providers, and administrative staff under diverse operational scenarios. The framework will integrate real-world datasets spanning appointment histories, EHR metadata, and staffing patterns, processed through graph neural networks to identify latent dependencies between operational parameters. Temporal convolution networks will be trained to predict bottlenecks in patient throughput, while reinforcement learning architectures will explore optimal policy adaptations under constraints such as budget limitations or emergent regulatory changes. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of historical clinic performance data and prospective pilot testing in three outpatient facilities. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of recommending dynamic staffing adjustments, automated identification of compliance vulnerabilities in billing practices, and scenario-testing interfaces for administrators. By bridging computational systems science with healthcare operations management, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven decision-making in medical administration, reducing operational costs by an estimated 12-18% in modeled environments while maintaining patient care quality standards. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a template for scalable, adaptive management systems in medium-sized healthcare practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a medical or clinical office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, medical and health care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the systemic risks and regulatory compliance challenges arising from the rapid adoption of decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols within global financial markets. As blockchain-based financial instruments and smart contracts increasingly intersect with traditional securities law frameworks, gaps in regulatory oversight and enforcement mechanisms have created vulnerabilities with potential cascading effects on market stability. The research problem centers on modeling complex interactions between decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), cross-jurisdictional regulatory regimes, and investor behavior to identify critical failure points in existing legal and computational architectures. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate market dynamics under stress scenarios, combining synthetic transaction datasets with natural language processing (NLP) of international securities regulations and court rulings. Graph neural networks (GNNs) will map liability structures across pseudonymous entities, while cryptographic audit trails will be analyzed through distributed ledger forensics. The computational workload requires parallel processing of terabyte-scale legal texts and blockchain data, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning tasks and high-memory instances for large-scale network analysis. Expected outcomes include a risk assessment framework for regulators addressing algorithmic compliance in DeFi ecosystems, along with protocol-level recommendations for embedding legal safeguards into smart contract designs. By bridging computational jurisprudence with financial network theory, this work aims to establish methodological foundations for anticipatory governance of emergent financial technologies while demonstrating the critical role of HPC in modern legal informatics research.
cip_title: Banking, Corporate, Finance, and Securities Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law and process related to the regulation of businesses and the financial services industry. Includes instruction in corporate law, antitrust law, securities law and regulation, negotiation, incorporation, partnerships, trusts, and related topics

abstract: The integration of biomechanical modeling and neurophysiological simulations holds significant potential to advance the understanding of spinal health and chiropractic interventions. However, the complexity of modeling dynamic interactions between spinal structures, neural pathways, and manual adjustment techniques necessitates high-resolution computational approaches that are currently underdeveloped in pre-chiropractic research. This project proposes the development of a multi-scale computational framework to simulate spinal biomechanics and their effects on nervous system function, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in mechanistic knowledge. The research problem centers on characterizing how vertebral misalignments (subluxations) alter stress distribution across spinal tissues and modulate afferent signaling to the central nervous system, a process hypothesized to underlie chiropractic therapeutic outcomes. The computational approach combines finite element modeling of spinal segment mechanics with machine learning-driven analysis of neural network responses to simulated adjustments. High-fidelity models of lumbar and cervical spine segments will be constructed using clinical imaging data, incorporating material properties of intervertebral discs, ligaments, and musculature. Concurrently, neural network models will simulate somatosensory processing under varying biomechanical conditions. HPC resources will enable parameter optimization across millions of potential adjustment scenarios, coupled with real-time visualization of tissue strain patterns and neural activation profiles. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific adjustment parameters to neurobiomechanical responses, quantitative safety thresholds for spinal loading, and evidence-based frameworks for optimizing manual therapy protocols. The computational tools developed will also serve as educational resources for pre-chiropractic students, enhancing their understanding of spinal pathophysiology through interactive simulations. By bridging biomechanical and neurological perspectives, this work aims to strengthen the scientific foundation of chiropractic medicine while demonstrating the transformative potential of computational methods in manual therapy research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in chiropractic medicine.

abstract: Public works agencies face mounting challenges in managing aging infrastructure, balancing fiscal constraints, and addressing climate-related disruptions. Existing decision-making tools often lack the capacity to model complex, dynamic interactions between infrastructure systems, budgetary limitations, and socio-environmental factors at municipal scales. This project proposes the development of an integrated computational framework to optimize public works resource allocation through high-performance computing (HPC). The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate infrastructure interdependencies (e.g., water distribution, transportation networks, and energy grids) under multiple stressor scenarios, including extreme weather events and population growth. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical maintenance records and real-time sensor data to predict failure risks, while multi-objective optimization algorithms will balance cost, equity, and service reliability considerations. The computational architecture requires parallel processing capabilities to handle 10,000+ concurrent agent interactions across multi-year simulations, with validation against case studies from three mid-sized U.S. cities. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between preventive maintenance schedules, capital investments, and emergency response preparedness. This work will advance public administration scholarship by establishing scalable methods for infrastructure resilience planning while addressing critical gaps in workforce training through open-source model development. Successful implementation could help municipalities reduce lifecycle costs by 15-25% in pilot regions while maintaining service levels during disruptive events. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in modeling resolution and computational speed that hinder practical application of complex systems approaches in non-technical public works departments.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation and logistics for large-scale construction projects, addressing critical inefficiencies in material delivery, workforce scheduling, and equipment deployment. Current practices in construction engineering often rely on static planning models that fail to adapt to dynamic variables such as weather disruptions, supply chain variability, and real-time site conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) system coupled with discrete-event simulation to model complex interactions between stakeholders, materials, and environmental constraints. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on synthetic datasets representing diverse construction scenarios, including high-rise buildings, bridge construction, and urban infrastructure projects. Computational workflows will integrate geotechnical data from site surveys, real-time sensor inputs from IoT devices, and historical project timelines to generate adaptive scheduling recommendations. Validation will occur through parallel simulations comparing traditional critical path methods against the AI-driven approach under stochastic disturbance models. Expected outcomes include a 15-30% reduction in project delays and a 10-20% decrease in material waste across simulated use cases. The computational tools developed will enable construction managers to perform risk-aware resource optimization at unprecedented scales, directly supporting sustainability goals through reduced carbon footprints from idle equipment and excess material transport. By advancing data-driven decision-making in construction engineering, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for resilient infrastructure development in rapidly urbanizing environments. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the necessary computational throughput for simulating millions of agent interactions and training high-dimensional optimization models within practical timeframes.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and management principles to the planning, design, and building of facilities and structures. Includes instruction in civil engineering, structural principles, site analysis, computer-assisted design, geology, evaluation and testing, materials, contracting, project management, graphic communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Healthcare unit operations require dynamic coordination of personnel, equipment, and workflows to maintain quality care, yet existing management strategies often rely on static protocols ill-suited to real-world variability. This project proposes the development of an adaptive decision-support framework for health unit managers using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning to simulate and optimize patient flow in acute care wards. The research problem centers on mitigating operational bottlenecks—such as bed allocation delays, staff assignment inefficiencies, and equipment utilization imbalances—that compromise care delivery during peak demand periods. Current approaches lack the computational granularity to model complex interactions between patient acuity profiles, staff skill matrices, and resource availability in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will construct a multi-scale simulation environment integrating electronic health record data, sensor-derived equipment usage patterns, and personnel shift logs from three tertiary care facilities. Machine learning models will predict demand fluctuations, while parallelized ABM simulations test intervention scenarios under stochastic conditions (e.g., emergent admissions, staff absences). The computational architecture will employ GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to model care team interactions and reinforcement learning to iteratively refine scheduling policies. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for identifying latent operational risks and protocol templates for adaptive resource reallocation. This work bridges clinical operations management with computational systems engineering, offering a novel methodology to enhance health unit resilience. Successful implementation could reduce patient transfer delays by an estimated 15-20% in simulated environments, providing unit managers with evidence-based tools to balance efficiency and staff workload—a critical need in post-pandemic healthcare systems facing chronic capacity constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nursing or medical service administrators, to supervise and coordinate the operations of one or more patient care units in hospitals or other health care facilities. Includes instruction in planning and initiating administrative procedures, personnel supervision, interpersonal skills, general and/or specialized health care operations and procedures, and consultation with other medical, nursing, and administrative team members.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision care strategies for pediatric patients through the development of predictive models for treatment response and adverse event risk. Pediatric nursing faces unique challenges due to the dynamic physiological and developmental changes in children, which complicate medication dosing, therapeutic monitoring, and long-term care planning. Current clinical decision-making tools often rely on generalized population data, inadequately accounting for individual variability in growth trajectories, genetic factors, and comorbidities. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-time biometric monitoring data from pediatric patients (ages 0–18) to build patient-specific predictive models. Machine learning algorithms, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, will be trained to identify patterns linking patient characteristics to clinical outcomes such as medication efficacy, hospitalization risk, and developmental delays. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale multimodal datasets, optimizing hyperparameters in complex models, and running simulations to evaluate hypothetical care pathways. The project will also employ agent-based modeling to simulate the impact of nurse-led interventions, such as tailored health education programs or adjusted medication schedules, on patient outcomes across diverse demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include actionable frameworks for personalized care plans, risk stratification tools to guide nursing assessments, and open-source computational models that can be integrated into clinical workflows. By elucidating the interactions between biological, developmental, and environmental factors in pediatric health, this work aims to empower nurses with data-driven strategies to improve patient safety, reduce treatment delays, and optimize health education initiatives—ultimately advancing equitable, evidence-based pediatric nursing practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care for children from infancy through adolescence. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting physicians, patient examination and referral, and planning and delivering health maintenance and health education programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize workflow dynamics in commercial kitchens, addressing inefficiencies in food preparation processes that contribute to operational delays, energy waste, and inconsistent output quality. While culinary workflows are traditionally refined through experiential trial and error, the complexity of variables—including staff coordination, equipment utilization, temperature control, and real-time demand fluctuations—presents a computational challenge requiring large-scale simulation. The research will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate kitchen operations under diverse scenarios, integrating stochastic elements such as variable order volumes, equipment failure probabilities, and staff skill heterogeneity. These models will be calibrated using empirical data from partner restaurants and validated against real-world performance metrics. Parallel computing will enable rapid iteration of scenarios to identify optimal task sequencing, equipment placement, and staffing configurations. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be applied to predict bottlenecks and recommend adaptive workflow adjustments in near-real time. The anticipated outcomes include a scalable computational framework for kitchen optimization, reducing energy consumption by 15–20% and food waste by 10–15% in simulated environments, while improving throughput consistency. By translating culinary workflows into computationally addressable problems, this work bridges gastronomic practice with data-driven decision-making, offering a novel methodology for sustainable, high-efficiency food service operations. The project further establishes a foundation for future research in computational gastronomy, particularly in modeling emergent behaviors in collaborative food preparation environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve under the supervision of chefs and other food service professionals as kitchen support staff and commercial food preparation workers.  Includes instruction in kitchen organization and operations, sanitation and quality control, basic food preparation and cooking skills, kitchen and kitchen equipment maintenance, and quantity food measurement and monitoring.

abstract: This project seeks to address the escalating complexity of next-generation wireless communication systems, which require ultra-reliable low-latency connectivity, high energy efficiency, and scalable resource allocation for heterogeneous networks. Current analytical models struggle to capture the dynamic interplay of massive MIMO arrays, millimeter-wave/terahertz channels, and dense user environments, limiting the design of adaptive protocols. To overcome these challenges, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating multi-physics channel modeling, machine learning (ML)-based optimization, and large-scale network simulations. The research will develop GPU-accelerated stochastic models to simulate spatially correlated fading in 3D urban environments, leveraging ray-tracing principles and measured propagation data. Parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms will then optimize beamforming, user scheduling, and interference management under time-varying constraints. A hierarchical simulation architecture will evaluate network slicing performance across distributed edge computing nodes, emulating traffic patterns from IoT, augmented reality, and critical infrastructure use cases. The computational demands necessitate access to HPC resources for: 1) Training graph neural networks on terabyte-scale channel state information datasets, 2) Running Monte Carlo trials for statistical validation of reliability in 10^6-device scenarios, and 3) Real-time co-simulation of physical-layer dynamics and network-layer control loops. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for latency-aware resource slicing in Open RAN architectures, validated interference mitigation strategies for shared spectrum access, and open-source simulation tools for 6G system prototyping. This work will directly inform standardization efforts while providing a computational foundation for energy-efficient, scalable communication infrastructure, critical for emerging smart city and industrial IoT deployments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and maintenance of communications technology, networks, and systems. Includes instruction in communications networks and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of sign languages’ structural diversity and evolution by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While sign languages such as ASL, LSF, and Auslan exhibit complex morphological and syntactic features, large-scale comparative studies are hindered by the multidimensional nature of visual-spatial data and the lack of tools capable of processing heterogeneous datasets. The research problem centers on identifying linguistic universals and variations across sign languages, particularly in syntax and morphology, while accounting for sociolinguistic factors such as regional dialects and community-driven language change. To achieve this, the project will integrate computational linguistics, computer vision, and machine learning to analyze annotated video corpora, motion-capture datasets, and historical records of sign language use. Key methods include developing neural networks tailored for sequential sign language data, implementing 3D spatial modeling to track articulatory trajectories, and applying phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct historical relationships between sign languages. HPC resources are essential for training deep learning models on high-resolution video data, conducting parallelized simulations of language evolution, and storing/processing terabytes of multimodal linguistic data. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework for cross-linguistic sign language analysis, novel insights into the typological classification of sign languages, and open-access tools for automated annotation and syntactic parsing. The project’s significance lies in advancing empirical methodologies for sign language linguistics, enabling rigorous comparisons with spoken language theories, and supporting technologies such as sign language recognition systems. By bridging computational and linguistic research, this work will contribute to preserving endangered sign languages and fostering equitable access to linguistic resources for deaf communities globally.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Linguistics of ASL and Other Sign Languages
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and scholarly study of the development, structure, and use of American Sign Language (ASL) and other visual signed languages, both as vehicles for communication within the deaf community and in relation to spoken and written languages. Includes instruction in cognitive linguistics; ASL and sign language phonology, syntax, and morphology; sociolinguistics of the deaf community; comparative linguistics; and studies of specific sign languages, including, but not limited to, ASL, Auslan (Australian Sign Language), LSF (French Sign Language), Shuwa jiten (Japanese Sign Language), HamNoSys (German Sign Language), and Gestuno.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design, installation, and maintenance of solar energy systems through high-fidelity simulations and predictive modeling. Current challenges in solar energy system deployment include variable environmental conditions, material degradation, and complex system interdependencies that affect efficiency and longevity. While existing empirical approaches provide foundational guidance, they often lack the precision needed to account for site-specific variables or dynamic operational stressors. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model photovoltaic (PV) array performance under diverse climatic and structural conditions, simulate long-term degradation of components, and optimize system configurations for reliability and cost-effectiveness. A multi-scale computational approach will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress testing of PV panels, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to evaluate thermal management in inverters and battery storage systems, and machine learning (ML) models trained on historical performance data to predict fault patterns. The simulations will incorporate geospatial weather data, material property datasets, and real-world installation parameters to ensure practical applicability. By parallelizing these computationally intensive workflows across HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce simulation timescales from weeks to days, enabling rapid iteration of design prototypes and maintenance strategies. Expected outcomes include optimized system layouts for varying environments, predictive maintenance algorithms to minimize downtime, and data-driven guidelines for technician training programs. These results will directly support the Solar Energy System Installation and Repair Technology field by advancing evidence-based practices for system durability, reducing operational costs, and accelerating the adoption of solar energy infrastructure. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the resolution and scale required for these simulations, which cannot feasibly be performed on local hardware.
cip_title: Solar Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair solar energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: The increasing demand for optimized equine breeding, health management, and facility operations necessitates advanced computational approaches to address complex biological and logistical challenges. Current methods for predicting genetic traits, optimizing training regimens, and managing large-scale equine facilities often rely on fragmented datasets or simplified models, limiting their predictive accuracy and practical applicability. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative, data-driven models that bridge genomic, physiological, and environmental factors in equine science. Specifically, we aim to (1) analyze high-dimensional genomic datasets to identify markers associated with athletic performance, disease resistance, and reproductive efficiency in thoroughbreds; (2) simulate biomechanical stress patterns during training using finite element modeling to inform injury prevention strategies; and (3) optimize facility layouts and operational workflows via agent-based modeling to enhance efficiency and welfare in large stables. Computational workflows will integrate machine learning (e.g., convolutional neural networks for gait analysis, gradient-boosted trees for genotype-phenotype associations) with physical simulations, requiring parallel processing capabilities for large-scale parameter sweeps and real-time data assimilation from IoT sensors in equine facilities. The anticipated outcomes include open-source predictive tools for breeders and trainers, evidence-based guidelines for facility design, and a publicly accessible database linking genetic profiles to performance metrics. By enabling the synthesis of disparate data types—from wearable device outputs to whole-genome sequences—this work will advance precision management practices in the equine industry while establishing a computational framework adaptable to other livestock sectors. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Horse Husbandry/ Equine Science and Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the selection, breeding, care, and maintenance of work, athletic, and show horses; and to manage horse farms, stables, tracks and related equipment and operations. Includes instruction in applicable principles of animal science, care, and health; stable and track management; design and operation of facilities and equipment; and related issues such as regulations, business management; and logistics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized fabric and apparel recommendations through advanced simulations of textile behavior and consumer preference dynamics. While fashion consulting traditionally relies on heuristic expertise, emerging challenges—such as demand for hyper-personalized styling, sustainability-driven material substitutions, and real-time adaptation to shifting aesthetic trends—require data-intensive modeling beyond manual analysis. The research addresses this gap by creating a machine learning (ML)-enhanced system that predicts optimal fabric-apparel pairings for individual clients based on biomechanical, environmental, and stylistic parameters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of fabric drape, stress, and thermal properties across diverse body morphologies and climate conditions using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Concurrently, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will synthesize visual style compatibility metrics from heterogeneous datasets spanning historical fashion archives, social media trend analyses, and client-supplied imagery. A novel agent-based model will integrate these outputs to simulate longitudinal client preference evolution, optimizing consultant decision pathways. The computational pipeline will be validated against ground-truth data from partner consultancies serving niche markets such as adaptive clothing for mobility impairments and eco-conscious event styling. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for dynamic fabric-apparel matching, a repository of simulated textile performance profiles, and quantifiable metrics for sustainability trade-offs in material recommendations. By bridging computational materials science with aesthetic intelligence systems, this work aims to establish scalable infrastructure for next-generation fashion consulting while addressing understudied intersections of embodied aesthetics, inclusive design, and resource-efficient textile utilization. The project’s HPC requirements stem from parallelized multiscale simulations, terabyte-scale image synthesis workloads, and iterative reinforcement learning for preference modeling—tasks infeasible without GPU-accelerated clusters and distributed memory architectures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in apparel and fashion selection, style coordination, customer sales and consulting, fabric selection, clothing specifications, and contract buying activities. Includes instruction in supplying regular clothing needs or acting as a consultant for special events such as weddings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable numerical methods for solving high-dimensional, nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in multiscale fluid-structure interaction problems, with applications to biomedical engineering and renewable energy systems. The core challenge lies in efficiently resolving coupled dynamics across disparate spatial and temporal scales while maintaining numerical stability, particularly for problems involving complex geometries or stochastic boundary conditions. Traditional discretization techniques struggle with the computational cost of resolving fine-scale features in three-dimensional domains, necessitating advanced algorithmic strategies. The proposed approach combines adaptive finite element methods with parallelized model reduction frameworks, leveraging tensor-train decompositions to compress high-dimensional solution manifolds. Key innovations include hybrid CPU-GPU implementations of iterative solvers for ill-conditioned linear systems and dynamic load-balancing algorithms to optimize resource utilization during mesh adaptation cycles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for benchmarking these methods against established solvers on large-scale test cases, including pulsatile blood flow in deformable arterial networks and turbulent wake interactions in offshore wind turbine arrays. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for parameter-sensitive preconditioning and data-driven reduced-order modeling, validated on O(10^4) core-hour simulations using petascale-ready codebases. The project will quantify trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost for problems with >10^8 degrees of freedom, providing guidelines for HPC-driven PDE solver design. Successful implementation will advance predictive modeling capabilities for multiphysics systems while contributing new methodological insights at the intersection of numerical analysis and computational science. Resource requests focus on allocations for memory-intensive computations (>1 TB per node) and sustained access to multi-node GPU clusters to profile weak scaling performance up to 16,384 cores.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of a broad range of mathematical and computational methods to modeling, analysis, algorithm development, and simulation for the solution of complex scientific and engineering problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, discrete mathematics, operations research, optimization, differential equations, statistics, scientific computation, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: Microbial communities exhibit complex interactions with host immune systems, yet the mechanisms driving pathogen resilience and immune evasion in polymicrobial infections remain poorly understood. This project seeks to investigate how interspecies microbial dynamics influence immune response modulation and contribute to chronic infections, with a focus on Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa co-infections in mucosal environments. To address this, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of microbial population dynamics with stochastic simulations of host-pathogen molecular interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model spatial heterogeneity in infection sites, track ligand-receptor binding events across immune cell surfaces, and simulate emergent community behaviors over biologically relevant timescales (days to weeks). The ABM will incorporate experimental data on microbial growth rates, metabolite exchange, and cytokine secretion profiles obtained from in vitro co-culture systems. Parallelized parameter sweeps will evaluate how variations in host neutrophil recruitment efficiency and microbial quorum-sensing cross-talk affect infection outcomes. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in immune cell density required for pathogen clearance, characterizing metabolic cooperation strategies that enhance microbial survival under immune pressure, and predicting temporal windows for effective therapeutic intervention. These computational insights will guide subsequent validation experiments using synthetic microbial consortia and air-liquid interface epithelial cell models. The resource request supports 18 months of large-scale simulations requiring 200,000+ CPU hours for multi-scale parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses. Results will advance fundamental understanding of immune evasion in polymicrobial contexts while providing a predictive framework to optimize antimicrobial stewardship strategies in clinical settings facing rising antibiotic resistance challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the microbiological sciences and immunology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of terrestrial system responses to climate-driven disturbances by developing a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to simulate coupled hydrological, geochemical, and ecological processes in critical zone environments. A key challenge in Earth system science lies in resolving multiscale interactions between subsurface hydrology, weathering dynamics, and vegetation feedbacks, particularly under shifting precipitation regimes and extreme drought-flood cycles. Current models often treat these systems in isolation or employ coarse spatial resolutions that fail to capture critical heterogeneities in soil properties, bedrock permeability, and root-water uptake patterns. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a parallelized version of a coupled reactive transport model (CLM-PFLOTRAN) integrated with satellite-derived vegetation productivity data and geophysical constraints from distributed sensor networks. The computational workflow will employ adaptive mesh refinement to resolve meter-scale hydrologic gradients across watersheds while maintaining continental-scale forcing from CMIP6 climate projections. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize parameterization of soil-rock moisture exchange processes using terabyte-scale LiDAR and hyperspectral remote sensing datasets. Anticipated outcomes include (1) quantification of nonlinear feedbacks between bedrock weathering rates and forest water stress under projected climate scenarios, (2) identification of hydrologic tipping points in groundwater-dependent ecosystems, and (3) open-source tools for coupling reactive transport models with ecological dynamics. The HPC resources are essential for managing ensemble simulations across >10^4 processor cores, enabling probabilistic uncertainty analysis through 10^3+ model realizations. Results will directly inform land management strategies for climate resilience in bedrock-dominated catchments while advancing computational capabilities for multiscale Earth system modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction of the Earth's oceanographic, atmospheric, and terrestrial systems. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in real-time spatial audio processing and machine learning-driven audio synthesis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Spatial audio rendering, which simulates three-dimensional soundscapes for applications in immersive media and virtual acoustic environments, requires intensive signal processing to model wave propagation, diffraction, and listener-specific head-related transfer functions (HRTFs). Similarly, machine learning models for tasks such as automated audio mixing, noise suppression, and timbre transfer demand large-scale training on high-resolution audio datasets. Current local computing infrastructure lacks the parallelism, memory bandwidth, and GPU acceleration required to optimize these workflows at scale, resulting in prohibitive processing times and limited model complexity. The proposed research will implement a hybrid CPU-GPU computational framework to parallelize finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) acoustic simulations and neural network training pipelines. Custom CUDA kernels will accelerate HRTF-based binaural rendering, while distributed TensorFlow workflows will enable batch processing of multitrack audio datasets for deep learning applications. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for real-time spatial audio processing with latency reductions of 40-60% compared to existing solutions, (2) generative adversarial networks (GANs) capable of synthesizing high-fidelity instrumental timbres under variable acoustic conditions, and (3) open-source tools for GPU-accelerated audio analysis integrated into Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) environments. These advancements will directly support pedagogical initiatives in immersive audio production and provide industry partners with optimized algorithms for next-generation audio technologies. By overcoming current computational bottlenecks, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical acoustics and practical, studio-grade engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the mixing, recording, and production of music. Includes instruction in acoustics, audio mixing, audio production, audio recording, computer composition of music, music theory, digital devices, and sound technology.

abstract: This research project seeks to enhance operational decision-making in protective services through advanced computational modeling of high-risk security scenarios. Protective services operations require rapid, evidence-based responses to dynamic threats, yet existing tools for simulating complex security environments—such as crowd disturbances, coordinated attacks, or hybrid threats involving physical and digital vectors—remain underdeveloped. Current approaches often rely on static risk assessments or oversimplified scenario planning, limiting their utility in real-world applications where variables like human behavior, environmental constraints, and adversarial adaptability interact unpredictably. To address this gap, we propose the development of a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The model will integrate real-world geospatial data, behavioral dynamics derived from historical security incident datasets, and probabilistic threat propagation algorithms to simulate multi-agent interactions across diverse operational contexts, including urban environments, critical infrastructure sites, and large-scale public events. Computational workflows will prioritize parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate thousands of scenario permutations, optimizing contingency plans for variables such as evacuation efficiency, resource allocation under resource constraints, and adversarial tactic prediction. Machine learning components will refine threat recognition patterns by analyzing simulated and operational data streams. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool capable of generating adaptive response protocols, quantifying emergent risks in novel threat landscapes, and reducing latency in critical decision loops. By bridging computational science and protective operations methodologies, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive security management, with applications in law enforcement training, infrastructure resilience planning, and public safety policy development. The project’s computational demands—particularly its need for large-scale parallelism, real-time data integration, and high-throughput scenario testing—necessitate dedicated HPC resources to achieve operational fidelity and practical scalability.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques of providing physical security protection to clients in various environments and situations. Includes instruction in security intelligence and information resources, operations planning and surveying, operations security, weapons and explosives, defense and offense techniques, security and surveillance systems, communications systems, perimeter and access control, weapons of mass destruction, contingency planning, crowd control, cover and evacuation, combat and vehicle techniques, and applicable legal and administrative responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance biology teacher education by integrating computational modeling tools to simulate complex biological systems, thereby addressing a critical gap in preparing educators to teach dynamic, systems-level concepts. Traditional pedagogical approaches often struggle to convey the scalability, interdependencies, and emergent behaviors inherent in biological networks (e.g., ecosystems, cellular processes), limiting student engagement and conceptual understanding. To bridge this gap, we propose developing interactive, high-fidelity simulations of biological phenomena using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. These simulations will model multi-scale processes, such as population genetics in evolving ecosystems or protein interaction networks in cellular environments, through agent-based modeling and differential equation systems. The computational workload requires parallelized processing to handle real-time parameter adjustments, large datasets (e.g., genomic or ecological monitoring data), and stochastic variability across thousands of iterations. HPC resources will enable the creation of modular, adaptable simulation frameworks that pre-service and in-service biology teachers can customize for grade-specific learning objectives. Expected outcomes include (1) a suite of open-access simulation tools optimized for classroom use, (2) evidence-based guidelines for integrating computational thinking into biology pedagogy, and (3) quantitative assessments of how simulation-aided instruction impacts teacher confidence and student learning gains in systems biology. By leveraging HPC to balance model complexity with pedagogical accessibility, this work aims to equip educators with scalable tools to demystify abstract biological concepts, fostering deeper student inquiry and alignment with Next Generation Science Standards. The project will also provide training workshops to help biology educators utilize these computational resources effectively, promoting broader adoption of data-driven, interactive teaching strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach biology programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Geothermal energy systems offer a sustainable pathway to meet growing energy demands, but their efficiency and scalability are limited by complex subsurface interactions between fluid flow, heat transfer, and rock mechanics. Current models often oversimplify heterogeneous geological formations, leading to suboptimal reservoir design and operational inefficiencies. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate multiphase fluid dynamics and thermal behavior in geothermal reservoirs under varying operational and geological conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will conduct 3D simulations of geothermal systems using finite element analysis coupled with machine learning-driven parameter optimization. The computational framework will integrate open-source subsurface flow codes (e.g., TOUGHREACT) with custom Python-based solvers to model fracture propagation, mineral precipitation, and heat extraction rates at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Key objectives include quantifying the impact of reservoir heterogeneity on long-term energy output, optimizing well placement strategies, and evaluating reinjection protocols to mitigate thermal depletion. By scaling simulations to regional geological datasets, the project will generate predictive tools for site selection and system design tailored to diverse geothermal settings, including enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) and low-temperature direct-use applications. The requested HPC allocation will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of cores, reducing runtime for ensemble models from months to days. Expected outcomes include publicly accessible datasets of simulated reservoir performance metrics and open-sourced workflow templates for adaptive mesh refinement in fractured media. This work will directly support the development of cost-effective, resilient geothermal technologies, aligning with national priorities to decarbonize energy infrastructure. The computational advancements will also provide a transferable framework for addressing subsurface uncertainties in renewable energy systems, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between engineering technologists and geoscientists.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Rehabilitation interventions for individuals with neuromotor impairments require precise, personalized approaches to optimize functional recovery. Current methods for configuring assistive devices and therapeutic protocols rely heavily on clinician expertise and iterative adjustments, which can be time-intensive and suboptimal. This project seeks to develop a computational framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific biomechanics and predict optimal rehabilitation parameters. The research problem centers on bridging gaps in real-time, data-driven decision-making for rehabilitation aides, who currently lack tools to rapidly evaluate the biomechanical impact of device adjustments or therapeutic exercises. Using motion capture data, electromyography signals, and patient health records, we will train physics-informed neural networks to simulate musculoskeletal dynamics under varying device configurations and intervention scenarios. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify configurations that maximize functional outcomes while minimizing joint stress or compensatory movements. A key innovation involves integrating reinforcement learning to adapt simulations to individual patient progress over time. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating patient-specific rehabilitation recommendations, validated against clinical data from 200 participants with stroke-related mobility impairments. This work will advance the precision of rehabilitation support by introducing computational methods to a field traditionally reliant on qualitative assessment. By reducing the trial-and-error period in device fitting and exercise prescription, the project has the potential to lower healthcare costs, accelerate recovery timelines, and improve quality of life for patients with complex mobility challenges. The computational models developed may also inform the design of next-generation adaptive assistive technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and other therapeutic professionals, and to perform routine functions in support of rehabilitation. Includes instruction in roles and responsibilities of rehabilitation providers, basic function of the human body, disabling conditions, therapeutic skills, client management, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the evidence-based understanding of Polarity Therapy’s mechanisms by developing computational models of the Human Energy Field (HEF) and its interactions with physiological systems. Despite clinical reports of efficacy, the biophysical and energetic principles underlying Polarity Therapy—including its effects on stress reduction, pain modulation, and homeostasis—remain poorly characterized. Current limitations stem from an inability to dynamically model multiscale energy-body interactions or analyze complex datasets spanning bioelectromagnetic measurements, clinical outcomes, and patient-reported metrics. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate HEF dynamics, integrate multimodal health data, and identify predictive biomarkers of therapeutic response. Computational workflows will combine finite element modeling of electromagnetic field distributions (derived from polarity bodywork and yoga protocols) with agent-based simulations of cellular responses to energy-based interventions. Machine learning pipelines will analyze high-resolution physiological time-series data (e.g., heart rate variability, EEG, and bioimpedance) alongside qualitative assessments from polarity processing sessions. By correlating simulated energy patterns with empirical outcomes, the project aims to establish quantifiable links between HEF modulation and systemic health effects. Expected outcomes include validated models of polarity principles, such as the proposed relationships between energetic blockages, oscillatory field coherence, and autonomic nervous system regulation. These results will provide a foundational computational framework for Polarity Therapy, enabling personalized treatment optimization and fostering interdisciplinary dialogue with conventional medicine. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling petascale datasets, running parallelized simulations of multi-layered energy-body networks, and training deep learning architectures to decode nonlinear therapeutic signatures. This work aligns with national priorities in integrative health research, offering novel computational tools to bridge energy medicine paradigms with biomedical science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote health and well-being through application of the integrative therapeutic system based on the Human Energy Field theory developed by Randolph Stone. Includes instruction in polarity theory and principles, energy-based and orthodox anatomy and physiology, polarity processing, polarity bodywork, polarity yoga, energetic nutrition, energetic evaluation and assessment, client communication, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing railway network efficiency and safety through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Railway systems face increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and sustainability, yet current operational strategies often rely on static scheduling and legacy infrastructure management practices. These approaches struggle to adapt to dynamic variables such as fluctuating freight volumes, passenger demand, weather disruptions, and evolving safety regulations. To overcome these limitations, this research will develop a multi-scale simulation framework integrating real-time data assimilation, machine learning, and discrete-event modeling to replicate complex railway operations. The computational approach will focus on three core components: (1) a high-fidelity agent-based model simulating train movements, signaling interactions, and railyard logistics under variable constraints; (2) predictive analytics for infrastructure wear-and-tear assessment using convolutional neural networks trained on track sensor data; and (3) risk-optimized routing algorithms for hazardous material transport that dynamically account for environmental factors and regulatory compliance. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of large-scale scenarios, including system-wide stress tests and probabilistic safety analyses that incorporate historical incident data. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for network throughput improvement, predictive maintenance frameworks to reduce service interruptions, and decision-support tools for emergency response planning. By creating an open-source computational platform adaptable to diverse railway configurations, this work aims to provide transportation agencies and operators with scalable strategies to enhance operational resilience while maintaining compliance with evolving industry standards. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models and distributed memory processing for system-wide simulations—directly necessitate access to HPC resources to achieve practical runtime efficiencies and model fidelity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation of railroads and other aspects of the railway industry, including railroad and railyard service. Includes instruction in railway culture, operating skills, General Code of Operation rules, conductor service, signal systems, switching, transportation of hazardous materials, safety, and railway telecommunications systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in developing large-scale, interactive multimedia installations that synthesize real-time data streams, generative artificial intelligence (AI), and immersive visual environments. A critical barrier in intermedia art practice lies in the integration of dynamic, high-dimensional inputs—such as motion capture, environmental sensors, or live audience biometrics—with computationally intensive rendering processes, which often exceed the capabilities of consumer-grade hardware. The proposed work will focus on optimizing parallelized workflows for real-time generative systems, enabling seamless interaction between human participants and algorithmic processes within spatially complex, multi-sensory artworks. Central to this effort is the development of custom machine learning models trained on heterogeneous datasets (visual, auditory, and temporal) to drive adaptive content generation, coupled with GPU-accelerated physics simulations for environmental feedback loops. Methodologically, the project will employ containerized deployment of AI pipelines using PyTorch and TensorFlow frameworks, alongside distributed rendering techniques via Unity and Unreal engines, to evaluate scalability across HPC architectures. Anticipated outcomes include novel frameworks for resource-efficient latency reduction in interactive systems, a publicly available toolkit for artists working with AI-mediated environments, and a series of exhibited works demonstrating computational frontiers in participatory art. By bridging the gap between artistic intent and technical feasibility, this research aims to advance both the creative potential of intermedia practices and the methodological understanding of HPC applications in experimental design contexts, while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between computational sciences and visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions in either two or three dimensions, through simultaneous use of a variety of materials and media.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in administrative workflow optimization, focusing on the intersection of computational methods and secretarial science. Administrative professionals manage complex, dynamic workflows involving communication prioritization, document routing, and resource coordination, yet existing tools often rely on static rules or manual input, leading to latency and suboptimal task allocation. This study proposes a data-driven approach to model and simulate administrative workflows using machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to analyze large-scale datasets of real-world office communications, task logs, and scheduling patterns. By training ML models on anonymized email threads, calendar entries, and document metadata, the project aims to identify latent patterns in task urgency, stakeholder interaction networks, and resource bottlenecks. HPC resources will enable the processing of multi-terabyte datasets, parallelized simulations of workflow interventions, and real-time optimization of task prioritization algorithms. Key computational challenges include scaling NLP pipelines for semantic analysis of unstructured communications and deploying graph neural networks to model interdependencies between tasks, personnel, and deadlines. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive workflow optimization, validated against benchmarks from partner organizations, and actionable insights into reducing administrative latency in high-volume environments. This work bridges a critical gap in secretarial science by introducing computational rigor to office procedure design, with potential applications in automated task routing, predictive resource allocation, and AI-assisted scheduling systems. The results will advance both academic understanding of administrative efficiency and practical tools for modern office environments, emphasizing scalability, interoperability, and human-AI collaboration in administrative support roles.
cip_title: Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform the duties of administrative assistants and/or secretaries and stenographers. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, word processing and data entry, office machines operation and maintenance, office procedures, public relations, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, and report preparation.

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems face increasing demands for efficiency, reliability, and environmental compliance, necessitating advanced computational analysis to address complex operational challenges. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate thermal degradation and dynamic stress patterns in turbine blades, combustion chamber performance under extreme conditions, and predictive maintenance strategies for hybrid-electric propulsion systems. Current experimental methods are limited in capturing multi-physics interactions at operational extremes, while computational models require fine-grained resolution of fluid-structure interactions, transient thermal gradients, and material fatigue mechanisms. The research will employ coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to model high-Reynolds-number flows, combustion instabilities, and anisotropic thermal expansion in next-generation turbine alloys. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to analyze sensor-derived operational data and optimize maintenance intervals based on simulated wear patterns.
