Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting blade lifespan under varying throttle cycles, combustion efficiency improvements through injector geometry optimization, and a framework for real-time anomaly detection in hybrid-electric systems. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in turbine diagnostics and propulsion system design while providing industry partners with tools to reduce unscheduled maintenance events by an estimated 15-20%. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the required spatial-temporal resolution in multi-scale simulations, particularly for capturing boundary layer effects in turbulent combustion and micro-crack propagation in composite materials. By bridging computational engineering with applied powerplant maintenance practices, this work aims to advance both academic training standards and sustainable aviation technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the socio-political networks and demographic transformations in colonial Latin America (16th–18th centuries) through large-scale textual and spatial data. The research problem centers on understanding how imperial administrative practices, indigenous resistance, and transatlantic exchange shaped regional power dynamics—a topic traditionally limited by fragmented archival sources and the manual analysis of multilingual documents. By integrating computational methods with historical inquiry, this project aims to reconstruct relational patterns across understudied regions, such as the Viceroyalty of Peru and Portuguese Amazonia, at an unprecedented scale. Key computational approaches include natural language processing (NLP) to parse Spanish, Portuguese, and digitized indigenous-language records (e.g., wills, legal disputes, and trade logs), network analysis to map elite kinship and economic ties, and geospatial modeling to track migration and resource extraction. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on historical Iberian languages, conducting Monte Carlo simulations to address source gaps, and processing high-resolution georeferenced datasets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated colonial documents, interactive visualizations of socio-economic networks, and statistical models quantifying the impact of forced labor systems on demographic collapse. This work will advance debates about colonialism’s longue durée effects while demonstrating how computational scalability can address methodological constraints in pre-modern history. By synthesizing dispersed archives into a unified analytical framework, the project aims to provide new insights into how local agency and imperial structures co-evolved, offering a model for interdisciplinary humanities scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking areas of the world, including the Iberian, Latin American, and Lusophone worlds.

abstract: This project seeks to address challenges in optimizing additive manufacturing processes for high-performance metallic alloys, where traditional trial-and-error methods lead to excessive material waste and suboptimal mechanical properties. The research aims to develop a computational framework that integrates multiphysics simulations with machine learning (ML) to predict and control process parameters such as laser power, scan speed, and thermal gradients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the coupled thermal-structural-fluid dynamics inherent in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) processes, which involve micron-scale melt pool dynamics and rapid solidification phenomena. Large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model heat transfer, residual stress formation, and defect generation across varying temporal and spatial scales. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze simulation outputs to identify parameter combinations that minimize porosity and distortion while maximizing tensile strength. The computational workload necessitates parallelized solvers, distributed memory architectures, and GPU acceleration to handle datasets exceeding 10^6 degrees of freedom per simulation. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for LPBF parameter optimization, reducing experimental iterations by 40-60% while achieving target material properties. This work will directly benefit aerospace and biomedical industries by enabling faster development of complex, defect-free components. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will also serve as a resource for advancing digital twin technologies in additive manufacturing, contributing to sustainable practices through reduced material waste and energy consumption.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of under-resourced African languages by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model linguistic structures and oral literatures at scale. Despite the rich diversity of African languages—encompassing over 2,000 distinct languages across major phyla such as Niger-Congo, Nilo-Saharan, and Khoisan—many remain under-documented and under-analyzed due to limited computational resources and tools tailored to their unique morphosyntactic, tonal, and discourse features. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational bottlenecks in processing large corpora of oral narratives, dialectal variations, and non-linear morphological systems, which are often incompatible with existing natural language processing (NLP) frameworks optimized for Indo-European languages. To address this, the project will deploy parallelized algorithms on HPC clusters to train machine learning models for automated morphological segmentation, tonal pattern recognition, and cross-dialectal similarity mapping. These models will be trained on curated datasets of annotated texts and audio recordings from languages such as isiZulu (Bantu), Oromo (Cushitic), and !Xun (Khoisan), incorporating both written and oral sources. Additionally, graph-based computational methods will be used to model the structural relationships in oral narratives, enabling the identification of culturally significant motifs and their diffusion across linguistic boundaries. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale simulations of language contact scenarios, shedding light on historical linguistic processes in the Sahel and Great Lakes regions. Expected outcomes include open-access computational tools for African language analysis, a scalable digital repository of annotated oral literatures, and novel insights into the typological diversity of African languages. By advancing computational methods for these understudied languages, the project aims to support revitalization efforts, inform pedagogical frameworks, and contribute to global linguistic theory. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks, such as training transformer-based models on low-resource languages, and for reducing processing times in comparative phylogenetic analyses from months to days.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the African continent, including, but not limited to, Bantu languages, Nilo-Saharan languages, Niger-Congo languages, Khoisan languages, and the Chadic and Ethiopic languages of the Hamito-Semitic language family. Includes instruction in philology, dialects, and oral and written literatures.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing cross-border digital trade compliance under fragmented and evolving regulatory frameworks. As global e-commerce expands, businesses face mounting challenges in navigating real-time compliance checks, tariff classifications, and export control screenings across jurisdictions, particularly when handling dynamic product data (e.g., software updates, AI-driven services). Traditional rule-based systems struggle to process multimodal trade documents, multilingual regulatory texts, and adaptive supply chain configurations efficiently. We propose developing a machine learning framework leveraging transformer architectures and graph neural networks to model multi-jurisdictional trade rules as interconnected decision graphs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training models on heterogeneous datasets spanning 150+ national regulatory corpuses, 10 million+ global trade records, and synthetic scenarios simulating emergent trade barriers. The computational workflow will integrate natural language processing for real-time regulation parsing, reinforcement learning for compliance pathway optimization, and uncertainty quantification to flag high-risk transactions. Expected outcomes include an open-source API for automated compliance scoring and a novel metric quantifying regulatory divergence costs in digital trade corridors. This work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in cross-border decision-making while providing policymakers with simulation tools to assess the systemic impacts of new digital trade agreements. By focusing on the computational scalability of compliance systems, the project bridges gaps between international business operations, computational linguistics, and regulatory informatics—an emerging nexus requiring HPC capabilities to manage the combinatorial complexity of global digital commerce.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international businesses and/or business operations. Includes instruction in the principles and processes of export sales, trade controls, foreign operations and related problems, monetary issues, international business policy, and applications to doing business in specific countries and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the diachronic syntactic evolution of Romance languages through large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary textual corpora. Despite rich literary traditions, comparative studies of syntactic structures across major Romance languages (e.g., French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese) remain limited by the manual analysis of fragmentary datasets. The proposed research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multi-gigabyte corpora spanning the 12th to 21st centuries, enabling systematic tracking of syntactic phenomena such as clitic placement, verb movement, and subordination patterns. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored for historical texts, machine learning classifiers to detect syntactic shifts, and phylogenetic algorithms to model divergence pathways. HPC capabilities are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks, including parallel processing of heterogeneous text formats and training neural models on centuries-spanning linguistic data. Expected outcomes include (1) a granular reconstruction of syntactic change timelines across four languages, (2) open-source tools for diachronic Romance linguistics analysis, and (3) empirically grounded insights into the interplay between language contact and syntactic innovation. By leveraging computational scalability, this project aims to overcome traditional limitations in corpus size and temporal resolution, offering new methodologies for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of linguistics and digital humanities. The resulting datasets and analytical frameworks will be disseminated through a public repository, fostering collaborative advancements in Romance language studies.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Romance languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research proposes the development of a novel computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in multi-project IT environments, where competing priorities, uncertainty in task completion times, and interdependencies between workflows create complex decision-making challenges. Traditional project management tools lack the capacity to model real-time resource constraints at scale or account for stochastic variables such as shifting requirements, team availability, and emergent risks. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale IT project portfolios under thousands of probabilistic scenarios, integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and reinforcement learning (RL) to identify adaptive allocation strategies. Computational workflows will be designed to parallelize scenario testing, enabling rapid evaluation of how human resource distributions, budget reallocations, and risk mitigation investments impact cross-project outcomes like delivery timelines, quality metrics, and stakeholder satisfaction. Key innovations include the synthesis of discrete event simulation for workflow modeling with graph neural networks to map task dependencies and RL-driven policy optimization for dynamic intervention. The resulting framework will provide IT project managers with evidence-based strategies to balance competing objectives while maintaining system-wide visibility. Expected outcomes include quantifiable benchmarks for resource allocation efficiency under uncertainty, open-source tools for scenario-driven project planning, and novel metrics to evaluate the cascading impacts of localized resource decisions in multi-team environments. By bridging computational optimization with organizational behavior theory, this work advances the emerging interdisciplinary niche of data-driven project management science, offering scalable solutions for enterprises managing complex IT portfolios in rapidly evolving technological landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, develop, and manage information technology projects in a variety of companies and organizations. Includes instruction in principles of project management, risk management, procurement and contract management, information security management, software management, organizational principles and behavior, communications, quality assurance, financial analysis, leadership, and team effectiveness.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in grapevine cultivation and wine production under shifting climatic conditions. Rising temperatures and altered precipitation patterns increasingly threaten grape yield, quality, and regional wine characteristics, necessitating advanced predictive models to guide adaptive strategies. We propose an integrated computational approach combining genomic, metabolomic, and environmental datasets to identify genetic markers linked to heat and drought resilience in *Vitis vinifera* cultivars. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on multi-omics data to predict genotype-phenotype-environment interactions, enabling the prioritization of breeding targets for climate-adaptive rootstocks and scions. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate microbial dynamics during fermentation under varying temperature regimes to optimize yeast strain selection and fermentation protocols for consistent wine quality. These computational workflows require large-scale parallel processing to handle terabyte-scale genomic datasets, complex metabolic network reconstructions, and stochastic simulations of microbial communities. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for genome-wide association studies. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for grapevine resilience, data-driven fermentation management tools, and open-access models to support vineyard decision-making. By elucidating the molecular and ecological drivers of crop performance and product stability, this work aims to enhance the sustainability of viticulture systems and economic viability of wine businesses amid climate uncertainty. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in processing speed and data integration, providing actionable insights for an industry facing escalating environmental pressures.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific and agribusiness principles to the production of grapes, the making of wine, and the wine business. Includes instruction in grapes and wines of the world; grape production; winemaking technology; plant biology; chemistry; food science, safety, and packaging; soil science; pest management; and marketing and business management.

abstract: The rapid growth of global air traffic, coupled with increasing demands for operational efficiency and environmental sustainability, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize air transportation systems. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for analyzing and improving air traffic flow management (ATFM) under dynamic weather disruptions and airspace capacity constraints. Current ATFM models struggle to integrate real-time weather data, stochastic demand patterns, and multi-objective optimization at scale, leading to suboptimal decisions that propagate delays and increase fuel consumption. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms. The framework will simulate network-wide aircraft movements at 1-second resolution across 24-hour operational windows, incorporating live weather radar inputs and probabilistic passenger demand forecasts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training DRL agents on historical flight data spanning 10 million+ records, running parallelized scenario analyses for continental-scale airspaces, and solving mixed-integer linear programming problems for slot allocation. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support system capable of reducing average delay propagation by 15-20% and curbing CO2 emissions through improved trajectory optimization. The research will also generate open-source datasets of simulated air traffic scenarios under varying disruption levels, supporting broader academic investigations into resilient aviation infrastructure. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this project aims to advance the computational frontiers of air transportation research while addressing critical industry challenges in capacity management and environmental performance.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in aviation and air transportation services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing digitization of cultural heritage materials has generated vast collections of digital artifacts, yet libraries and archives face significant challenges in preserving and providing access to these resources as formats degrade and obsolescence accelerates. This project seeks to address the critical gap in scalable computational methods for analyzing and preserving heterogeneous digital collections, particularly those with complex dependencies between file formats, metadata schemas, and software ecosystems. Current approaches often rely on manual curation or limited automation, which cannot scale to the petabytes of data held in modern repositories. We propose developing a machine learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to automate the detection of at-risk digital objects, predict degradation pathways, and recommend preservation interventions. The computational workflow will integrate graph neural networks to model format dependencies, transformer-based architectures for metadata enrichment, and agent-based simulations to evaluate preservation strategy outcomes under varying resource constraints. By leveraging GPU-accelerated training and distributed storage systems, the framework will process multi-modal data (text, images, binary files) across millions of objects while maintaining chain-of-custody documentation required for archival integrity. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for large-scale digital preservation analytics, empirical models of format obsolescence patterns, and benchmark datasets for evaluating computational preservation methods. This work will provide libraries with evidence-based strategies to prioritize at-risk materials, reduce curation costs, and extend the lifespan of digital collections. The HPC infrastructure is essential given the need for parallel processing of terabyte-scale corpora, real-time simulation of decade-spanning preservation scenarios, and comparative analysis across diverse institutional collections. Results will advance both library science practice and computational preservation as an emerging interdisciplinary field.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research aims to investigate the molecular and systemic mechanisms underlying the efficacy of multimodal complementary therapies, with a focus on integrating ethnomedical practices with modern computational systems biology. Despite growing clinical interest in therapies such as acupuncture, herbal synergies, and biofield modulation, their mechanistic foundations remain poorly characterized due to the complexity of multi-target interactions and nonlinear physiological responses. This project addresses the critical gap in predictive models capable of simulating polypharmacological effects across multiple biological scales, from protein-ligand dynamics to neural-immune network modulation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop a multiscale computational framework combining molecular dynamics simulations, Bayesian network inference, and agent-based modeling to map how combinations of stimuli (e.g., phytochemical mixtures, mechanical/energetic inputs) induce emergent therapeutic outcomes. The computational workflow will integrate structural proteomics data, ethnomedical compound libraries, and clinical metabolomics datasets to model context-dependent therapeutic synergies. Key objectives include: 1) simulating ligand-receptor binding affinities for 50,000+ herbal constituents across human proteome targets using enhanced sampling MD techniques; 2) constructing probabilistic causal networks linking intervention-specific molecular patterns to immune-endocrine signaling outcomes; and 3) validating models against longitudinal multi-omics data from practitioner-guided case series. Expected outcomes include the first open-source computational platform for predicting complementary therapy synergies, identification of novel bioactivity hubs in ethnopharmacopeias, and quantitative frameworks for personalizing multimodal treatment sequences. By elucidating system-level therapeutic mechanisms, this work will advance the evidence-based integration of complementary modalities into mainstream care pathways while preserving their holistic practice paradigms. The scale of combinatorial analysis and whole-body modeling necessitates HPC capabilities for parallelized simulation ensembles and large-scale graph inference, far exceeding conventional clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medical Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medical support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a computational framework for optimizing dynamic pricing and inventory management strategies in omnichannel retail environments. Modern retail systems face complex challenges due to fluctuating consumer demand, supply chain disruptions, and competitive market dynamics, particularly in hybrid models integrating physical stores and e-commerce platforms. Existing analytical models often fail to account for real-time data granularity, stochastic variables, and multi-agent interactions at scale, limiting their practical utility. To address this, we propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and reinforcement learning algorithms. The agent-based component will simulate customer behavior, competitor actions, and supply chain networks, while Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in demand forecasting and lead times. Reinforcement learning agents will then iteratively optimize pricing and inventory decisions across sales channels. The computational intensity of training these models on large-scale historical transaction data, coupled with the need for parallelized scenario testing under diverse market conditions, necessitates HPC resources for feasible runtime and resolution. Expected outcomes include validated decision-support tools that adapt pricing and stock allocation strategies in near-real time, reducing waste and maximizing profitability. The project will also generate novel insights into behavioral economics patterns in digital-physical retail interfaces. By overcoming current computational bottlenecks, this work aims to advance both academic research in retail operations management and practical applications for businesses navigating increasingly complex consumer markets. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits tailored for retail management education and industry partnerships.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operations of a wide variety of retail businesses, including department stores; independent and chain stores; fashion, food and beverage, and pharmaceutical establishments; and online retail businesses. Includes instruction in retail management, merchandise management, customer service management, marketing, organizational behavior, accounting, finance, business law, and personnel management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic stagecraft design through computational modeling and simulation. Contemporary theater increasingly integrates complex, adaptive staging elements—such as responsive lighting, movable set pieces, and real-time audiovisual effects—that require precise coordination to maintain artistic coherence. However, existing tools for pre-production planning lack the capacity to simulate the interplay of these elements at scale, leading to inefficiencies in design iteration and risk mitigation during live performances. To address this gap, we propose developing a physics-informed, agent-based modeling framework to simulate multi-dimensional stage environments under variable performance conditions. The computational approach will combine real-time rendering engines with discrete event simulation to model interactions between mechanical systems, environmental factors (e.g., acoustics, airflow), and human performers. HPC resources will enable parallelized testing of thousands of design permutations, optimizing for safety, timing accuracy, and aesthetic impact. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to predict failure points in staging workflows and recommend adaptive adjustments. Expected outcomes include a novel software toolkit for theater practitioners, validated through collaboration with regional theater companies, that reduces technical rehearsal time by 30-50% while enhancing creative flexibility. This work will establish a foundation for computational methods in performance design, bridging gaps between artistic practice and engineering precision. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the high-resolution spatial data and concurrent processes inherent to simulating large-scale theatrical environments, which exceed the capabilities of standard workstations.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Dramatic/ Theatre Arts and Stagecraft, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dramatic/theatre arts and stagecraft, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of conflict dynamics in fragile states, integrating sociopolitical, economic, and environmental data to predict escalation pathways and evaluate de-escalation strategies. Contemporary peace studies lack scalable frameworks to analyze the nonlinear interactions between diverse conflict drivers—such as resource scarcity, ethnic polarization, and external intervention—in real-world scenarios. Current models often oversimplify feedback loops or fail to account for spatial-temporal heterogeneity, limiting their utility for policymakers. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) coupled with machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate multi-actor decision-making under conditions of uncertainty, incorporating geospatial data, historical conflict datasets, and ethnographic case studies. The ABM will parameterize state and non-state actors (e.g., governments, insurgent groups, NGOs) with adaptive behavioral rules derived from game-theoretic principles and empirical observations, while ML components will identify latent patterns in historical escalation events to refine model accuracy. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale parallel simulations across diverse parameter spaces, enabling sensitivity analyses of intervention strategies (e.g., aid distribution protocols, ceasefire negotiation timing) under stochastic conditions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for conflict forecasting, validated against historical cases (e.g., post-2011 Syria, Lake Chad Basin crises), and policy-reducible insights into resilience-building mechanisms. By bridging computational social science and peace studies, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven conflict resolution, offering granular risk assessments and scenario-testing capabilities to practitioners working in complex, evolving crises.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of international and inter-group conflicts. Includes instruction in peace research methods and related social scientific and psychological knowledge bases.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the acoustic and biomechanical interactions inherent in advanced stringed instrument performance. While traditional pedagogical methods for stringed instruments rely on qualitative assessments of tone production, articulation, and expressive phrasing, the complex physical dynamics underlying these elements—including string vibration, bow contact mechanics, and performer motor control—remain insufficiently quantified. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing computational models that simulate real-world performance scenarios at high temporal and spatial resolutions. These models will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for instrument-body resonance, fluid-structure interaction simulations for bow-string friction dynamics, and machine learning (ML) techniques to correlate biomechanical sensor data (e.g., motion capture, electromyography) with perceptual outcomes in recorded performances. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve sub-millisecond temporal resolution in simulations, enabling the identification of micro-variations in technique that distinguish expert-level artistry. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database of performance-optimized physical models for violins, cellos, and related instruments; (2) ML-driven diagnostic tools for personalized feedback in pedagogical contexts; and (3) novel insights into the biomechanical efficiency of historically significant performance practices. The resource request targets GPU-accelerated nodes for ML training and high-memory nodes for FEA, with an estimated 200,000 core-hours required annually. This work advances the performing arts by establishing quantitative frameworks for artistic mastery while fostering interdisciplinary innovation between computational physics and music pedagogy. Results will directly inform curriculum development in the Stringed Instruments program and provide a foundation for future studies on injury prevention and ergonomic design for musicians.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individual to master a stringed instrument and performing arts as solo, ensemble and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and performance of energy-efficient building systems through high-performance computing (HPC). Urbanization and climate change demand structures that minimize environmental impact while maintaining resilience, but current design workflows struggle to balance complex, interdependent variables such as thermal efficiency, structural integrity, and airflow dynamics. Traditional simulations often oversimplify multi-physics interactions or are computationally prohibitive, limiting innovation in sustainable architectural solutions. To address this, we propose an HPC-driven approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model building systems at unprecedented resolution and scale. High-fidelity simulations will capture coupled heat transfer, mechanical stress, and ventilation dynamics across diverse urban microclimates, while ML algorithms iteratively optimize material selection, geometric configurations, and passive energy strategies. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of large parametric datasets and real-time visualization of 3D structural-thermal models, facilitating rapid design iteration. Key outcomes include validated predictive models for energy consumption and load-bearing capacity, a generative design toolkit for architects and engineers, and actionable guidelines for retrofitting existing buildings. By resolving computational bottlenecks, this work will advance the integration of performance-driven design into architectural practice, directly supporting decarbonization goals and adaptive reuse of urban infrastructure. The requested resources will also train students in HPC applications for architectural engineering, bridging technical skills gaps in the emerging sustainable construction sector. This project aligns with national priorities for smart cities and positions architectural engineering as a critical field for scalable climate resilience solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing demand for specialized pet grooming services necessitates advanced methodologies to optimize animal well-being and procedural efficiency. Current practices rely heavily on empirical knowledge, with limited integration of computational tools to address complex biomechanical, physiological, and behavioral factors inherent in grooming processes. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model interspecies variability in skin, coat, and musculoskeletal responses to grooming techniques, enabling data-driven protocol optimization. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement multiscale simulations integrating finite element analysis for mechanical stress distribution during brushing, clipping, and bathing; computational fluid dynamics for product absorption kinetics; and agent-based modeling to predict animal stress responses under varying handling conditions. Machine learning pipelines will be trained on aggregated datasets comprising 3D coat morphology scans, biometric sensor outputs from wearable grooming aids, and ethological video annotations. The computational workflow will address critical gaps in (1) quantifying microdamage thresholds for diverse coat types under mechanical grooming loads, (2) optimizing product application parameters for minimal dermal irritation, and (3) identifying handling patterns that minimize physiological stress markers across temperamental spectra. Validation will occur through parallel in-situ measurements using force transducers, thermal imaging, and cortisol assays in controlled grooming environments. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for injury risk stratification, a cloud-based decision support system for personalized grooming plans, and an open-access database of species-specific material property benchmarks. By establishing computational grooming science as a novel interdisciplinary domain, this research aims to transform anecdotal practices into evidence-based protocols while reducing occupational hazards for grooming professionals. The requested HPC allocation will enable the intensive parameter space exploration required to account for biological variability at scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic organization of cellular compartments and their role in maintaining structural integrity during stress responses, a fundamental question in cell biology with implications for understanding disease mechanisms. A major gap exists in mapping how organelles such as lysosomes, endosomes, and the cytoskeleton coordinate spatial reorganization under metabolic or mechanical stress, particularly in human epithelial cells. Traditional imaging and biochemical approaches lack the resolution to model these interactions at subcellular scales across time. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations to reconstruct 3D organelle dynamics within realistic cell geometries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and run spatially resolved models that integrate live-cell imaging data, simulating millions of interacting agents (e.g., vesicles, cytoskeletal filaments) over biologically relevant timescales (hours to days). The ABM will encode rules for organelle motility, tethering, and membrane remodeling, while LBM will simulate cytoplasmic fluid dynamics and diffusion gradients. Validation will leverage experimental datasets from collaborating labs, including light-sheet microscopy and traction force microscopy of stressed epithelial monolayers. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of stress-induced organelle redistribution, (2) identification of critical thresholds in cytoskeletal strain that trigger loss of compartmentalization, and (3) open-source simulation tools for visualizing multiscale cell architecture changes. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of how spatial organization failures contribute to pathologies such as epithelial barrier dysfunction, directly supporting the program’s focus on cell structure-function relationships. The requested resources—200,000 CPU-hours and GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized LBM—will enable parameter sweeps across physiologically relevant conditions currently inaccessible to local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cells, cellular systems, and the molecular basis of cell structure and function. Includes instruction in cell biology, cell chemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, and structural biology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the long-term evolution of political institutions and their responsiveness to societal crises through an integrative computational analysis of historical records, legislative texts, and demographic data spanning the 19th to 21st centuries. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how institutional adaptability—measured through legislative language, policy shifts, and administrative continuity—correlates with systemic resilience during periods of upheaval, such as pandemics, economic collapses, or revolutions. By combining methods from computational historiography and political network analysis, we propose to develop a novel framework for quantifying institutional change across temporal and geopolitical contexts. The computational approach leverages natural language processing (NLP) to track semantic shifts in parliamentary proceedings and constitutional documents, paired with dynamic network analysis to map changes in power structures and policy diffusion patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multilingual historical corpora (exceeding 50 million pages) and simulating agent-based models of institutional decision-making under crisis scenarios. These models will integrate socioeconomic variables from archival census records and conflict databases to test hypotheses about path dependence in political systems. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking institutional adaptability metrics to historical outcomes, as well as machine learning classifiers capable of identifying latent crisis-response patterns across diverse governance models. The project’s interdisciplinary methodology bridges archival research traditions with computational social science, offering new tools for analyzing path-dependent political behavior while providing empirical insights into contemporary debates about institutional reform and crisis preparedness. Results will advance both historical scholarship and policy-relevant political science through data-driven comparisons of long-term institutional trajectories.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and political science or a specialization which draws from history and political science. Includes instruction in comparative government and politics, historiography, historical research methods, political science, political theory, records administration, and systematic study of political institutions and behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the design and reconstruction of internal combustion engines, addressing critical challenges in durability, performance, and emissions for automotive and commercial vehicle applications. A core research problem lies in the lack of predictive models that integrate the multiphysics interactions within engine components—such as thermal stresses in cylinder heads, dynamic loading on crankshafts, and wear patterns in piston assemblies—under real-world operating conditions. Current empirical methods for engine machining and repair often rely on iterative physical testing, which is resource-intensive and limits innovation in balancing performance with sustainability goals. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate component behavior at unprecedented resolution. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution and fatigue in engine blocks, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate combustion dynamics and heat transfer. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to predict optimal machining tolerances, material removal strategies, and assembly configurations. The HPC environment is essential to manage the scale of these simulations, which involve billions of mesh elements for component-level analysis and require parallel processing for parametric studies across diverse engine architectures (e.g., diesel vs. gasoline, legacy vs. modern designs). Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework to guide precision machining processes, reduce trial-and-error prototyping by 40–60%, and identify design modifications that lower emissions without compromising power output. This work will directly support curriculum advancements in engine diagnostics and remanufacturing, while providing industry partners with open-source tools to extend engine lifespans in alignment with circular economy principles. The requested computing resources will enable the integration of multi-scale physics into actionable insights for machinists, bridging the gap between theoretical mechanics and hands-on technical training.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the building and reconstruction of automotive and commercial vehicle engines. Includes instruction in cylinder head and block, crack repair, crankshaft inspection and repair, connecting rods and pistons, balancing, block preparation, disassembly and repair, engine assembly, gas and diesel technology, and inspection and machining.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interplay between environmental dynamics and cultural-geographic patterns in historical Inner/Central Asia, with a focus on Ural-Altaic communities. The study addresses a critical gap in understanding how climatic shifts and landscape features influenced migration routes, settlement systems, and cultural exchange networks among Turkic and Mongolian populations from the 6th to 16th centuries. The project integrates multi-modal datasets, including high-resolution topographic data, paleoclimate reconstructions, archaeological site records, and multilingual historical texts from Silk Road archives. Computational methods will involve geospatial machine learning to model ancient travel corridors, agent-based simulations of pastoralist migration patterns, and network analysis of cultural artifact distribution across the Tian Shan and Altai regions. Key challenges include processing petabyte-scale satellite imagery, resolving temporal mismatches in heterogeneous datasets, and simulating complex human-environment interactions over millennial timescales. The requested HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of geospatial layers, ensemble climate model runs, and large-scale network optimization algorithms. Anticipated outcomes include the first high-resolution digital atlas of historical mobility patterns in Central Asia, identification of previously undocumented cultural contact zones, and open-source tools for temporal-spatial analysis of archaeological records. Results will contribute to preserving endangered cultural heritage by digitally reconstructing at-risk sites and informing conservation priorities. This computational approach advances interdisciplinary methodologies in area studies while providing new insights into long-term human adaptation strategies in arid and mountainous ecosystems. The project aligns with the program's mission to deepen scholarly understanding of Central Asia's historical development through innovative integration of traditional humanistic inquiry and cutting-edge computational techniques.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries of Inner/Central Asia, including the Turkic and Mongolian inhabitants of the Caspian, Amur, Tien Shan, Baikal, Gobi, Siberian, and Manchurian areas and the historical Silk Road, in terms of their past and present development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in organizational decision-making under dynamic market conditions, a critical challenge in business administration. The research problem centers on optimizing resource allocation strategies for large firms operating in volatile environments, where traditional static models fail to account for real-time data fluctuations, interdependencies between operational units, and nonlinear feedback effects. Current approaches to simulating such complex systems are computationally constrained, limiting their ability to model enterprise-scale scenarios with granularity. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based computational framework that integrates multi-objective optimization algorithms with machine learning techniques to simulate decision hierarchies, resource flows, and market interactions. The HPC environment will enable parallelized execution of Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of stochastic market scenarios while maintaining millisecond-scale resolution for intra-organizational processes. Key computational components include graph neural networks to model interdepartmental dependencies and evolutionary algorithms to identify Pareto-optimal allocation policies under competing performance metrics. The project will validate models against historical case studies spanning manufacturing, retail, and service industries, using anonymized operational datasets. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support toolkit for adaptive resource allocation, quantitative benchmarks for organizational resilience metrics, and theoretical insights into scalability limits of hierarchical management structures. By enabling unprecedented simulation fidelity across temporal and organizational scales, this research aims to advance evidence-based management practices while contributing methodological innovations to computational organizational theory. The requested computing resources are essential for handling memory-intensive network optimizations and supporting real-time parameter sensitivity analyses across high-dimensional solution spaces.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on developing and expanding the theory and research in regards to the planning, organizing, directing , and controlling the functions and processes of a firm or organization.

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of contaminant transport in heterogeneous groundwater systems, a critical challenge for sustainable water resource management in regions impacted by industrial and agricultural pollution. Current models struggle to resolve fine-scale variations in aquifer properties and dynamic biogeochemical interactions that govern contaminant mobility, leading to uncertainties in remediation strategies. To address this, we propose a high-resolution, coupled hydrogeochemical simulation framework integrating stochastic hydrogeological parameterization, reactive transport modeling, and machine learning-driven sensitivity analysis. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized finite element methods (FEniCS) and deep neural networks (PyTorch) to model multi-species reactive transport across scales, explicitly capturing heterogeneity in hydraulic conductivity and redox zonation. High-performance computing resources are essential to execute ensemble simulations across 10^4 parameter realizations at meter-scale resolution over watershed domains (>100 km²), requiring ~250,000 CPU-hours and 50 TB of distributed memory for transient 3D simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable open-source framework for probabilistic contaminant fate prediction, (2) quantification of how sub-grid chemical heterogeneity influences plume evolution timelines, and (3) machine learning-derived thresholds for monitoring network density in contaminated aquifers. Results will directly inform groundwater management policies by identifying dominant controls on emerging contaminant persistence (e.g., PFAS, chromium-VI) and optimizing sensor placement strategies. This work bridges gaps between process-rich geochemical modeling and decision-focused risk assessment tools, with methodological advances transferable to other Earth science domains requiring multiscale reactive transport solutions.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on earth, its environments, human activities, and the linkages between them. Includes instruction biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, pollution control and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: The increasing complexity of decentralized IT service ecosystems, particularly in edge computing environments with heterogeneous IoT devices, presents critical challenges in dynamic resource coordination. Traditional centralized management frameworks struggle to adapt to the scale, latency sensitivity, and energy constraints of modern applications such as distributed smart grids or real-time industrial automation. This project proposes the development of a novel, decentralized resource allocation framework leveraging multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and adaptive consensus protocols to optimize computational workflows across edge nodes while minimizing operational overhead. The research addresses the gap in scalable, self-organizing algorithms for IT service administration in environments with intermittent connectivity and competing stakeholder priorities. Computational experiments will simulate large-scale edge networks (10,000+ nodes) under variable load conditions to train and validate MARL policies that balance task throughput, energy efficiency, and fault tolerance. High-performance computing resources are essential for parallelized training of diverse network topologies and stress-testing consensus mechanisms under failure scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for adaptive resource negotiation in edge environments, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing decentralized strategies against conventional orchestration approaches, and (3) novel metrics for evaluating administration overhead in permissionless device coalitions. The work advances IT service management paradigms by introducing biologically inspired coordination mechanisms that could reduce infrastructure provisioning costs by 15-30% in target use cases while maintaining QoS guarantees. Results will directly inform standardization efforts for autonomic computing in 5G/6G-enabled industrial IoT deployments, bridging theoretical distributed systems research with practical IT administration challenges in emergent edge architectures.
cip_title: Computer/ Information Technology Services Administration and Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer/information technology services administration and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational music conducting, focusing on the optimization of ensemble performance through data-driven analysis of gesture-sound relationships and score interpretation. While traditional conducting pedagogy emphasizes experiential learning and subjective evaluation, this study addresses the lack of scalable, quantitative frameworks for analyzing how conductor gestures influence ensemble synchronization, dynamic balance, and expressive outcomes. The research problem centers on modeling the complex, nonlinear interactions between conductor movements, ensemble responsiveness, and acoustic results across diverse musical works and ensemble configurations. Computational methods will include machine learning algorithms trained on motion-capture data (recorded from professional conductors) synchronized with ensemble audio recordings, enabling the identification of gesture patterns correlated with specific performance outcomes. Large-scale simulations of virtual ensembles will be developed using agent-based modeling to test hypotheses about gesture efficacy under varying conditions. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data (including 3D motion trajectories, audio spectra, and score metadata) and running real-time simulations of up to 100 virtual musicians. Expected outcomes include a novel computational system for evaluating conducting strategies, predictive models of gesture effectiveness by musical genre, and open-source tools for automated feedback in conducting education. By bridging empirical analysis with artistic practice, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying music leadership while providing conservatories and professional ensembles with evidence-based frameworks to enhance rehearsal efficiency and interpretive decision-making. The project’s computational infrastructure will also enable future studies on historical conducting practices through analysis of archival performance recordings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the art of leading bands, choirs, orchestras and other ensembles in performance, and related music leadership. Includes instruction in score analysis and arranging, rehearsal and performance leadership, music coaching, arrangement and performance planning, ensemble operations management, and applications to specific school or professional ensembles.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in forensic anthropology related to the accurate identification of skeletal remains and interpretation of perimortem trauma in complex taphonomic contexts. Traditional analytical methods often struggle with fragmented, burned, or environmentally degraded remains, leading to uncertainties in estimating biological profiles and distinguishing antemortem pathology from postmortem damage. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational workflow integrating high-resolution 3D imaging, machine learning, and biomechanical simulations requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Micro-CT scans of skeletal specimens from documented forensic cases will be processed through automated segmentation algorithms to reconstruct trauma patterns and surface modifications. Deep learning models trained on diverse skeletal datasets will classify fracture mechanics (blunt force vs. ballistic trauma) and predict postmortem interval through multivariate analysis of taphonomic markers. Concurrently, finite element analysis simulations will model bone response to dynamic loading under varying environmental conditions. The scale of data—terabyte-level imaging datasets, iterative model training, and multiphysics simulations—necessitates parallelized computing with GPU acceleration and large-memory nodes. Anticipated outcomes include validated computational tools for trauma analysis, improved statistical frameworks for biological profile estimation in compromised remains, and open-source algorithms to quantify taphonomic change. This work will advance methodological rigor in medicolegal investigations while establishing scalable computational protocols for anthropological research. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project bridges gaps between traditional osteological analysis and data-driven forensic science, with direct applications to cold case resolutions and mass disaster response.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and skeletal anthropology in medicolegal death investigations. Includes instruction in biological anthropology theory, crime scene investigation, forensic anthropology field methods, forensic anthropological techniques and procedures, human anatomy, methods of human identification, mortuary archaeology, osteology, and taphonomy.

abstract: The increasing adoption of solar energy systems demands advancements in installation efficiency, reliability, and long-term performance. Current practices face challenges in optimizing system layouts for variable environmental conditions, predicting component degradation, and mitigating performance losses due to factors like shading, thermal stress, and material wear. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model and simulate solar energy systems under diverse real-world conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating multi-physics models to evaluate the impact of environmental variables (e.g., irradiance, temperature gradients, particulate accumulation) on photovoltaic panel efficiency and structural integrity; (2) training machine learning algorithms on simulated and empirical datasets to predict maintenance needs and failure modes for inverters, wiring, and mounting hardware; and (3) optimizing installation configurations using evolutionary algorithms that account for site-specific constraints, such as roof geometry and local weather patterns. Computational methods will integrate finite element analysis for stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics for thermal management simulations, and Monte Carlo techniques to assess probabilistic performance outcomes across decades-long system lifetimes. The scale of these simulations—requiring parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets spanning millions of parameter combinations—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide technicians in designing failure-resistant installations, data-driven maintenance schedules to extend system longevity, and open-source simulation modules for training purposes. By bridging computational modeling with practical technician workflows, this project aims to reduce solar system downtime by an estimated 15–20%, lower operational costs, and contribute to standardized best practices in the renewable energy technical workforce.
cip_title: Solar Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair solar energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making for wildfire incident response and resource allocation, integrating real-time environmental data, historical fire behavior patterns, and operational constraints specific to municipal fire services. Wildfire management faces escalating complexity due to climate variability, urban-wildland interface expansion, and competing demands for personnel and equipment. Existing models often lack granularity in simulating dynamic risk factors—such as shifting wind patterns, community evacuation logistics, and apparatus deployment trade-offs—under resource-constrained scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose an adaptive simulation platform that couples agent-based modeling (ABM) with multi-objective optimization to evaluate tactical trade-offs in real time. The ABM layer will simulate fire spread at a hyperlocal scale (10m resolution) using weather feeds, fuel load datasets, and infrastructure topology, while parallelized optimization algorithms will iteratively assess resource allocation strategies against objectives like property protection, firefighter safety, and operational cost efficiency. Validation will employ historical incident data from partner fire agencies, with scenario testing focused on low-probability, high-consequence events where traditional heuristics fail. Computational demands arise from the need to process high-resolution geospatial inputs, run ensemble simulations for probabilistic forecasting, and solve combinatorial optimization problems under rapidly changing constraints. Outcomes will include an open-source decision support toolkit for fire service administrators, enabling scenario planning and real-time strategy adaptation. By quantifying previously intangible factors—such as the cascading impacts of apparatus redeployment or the value of preemptive community notifications—this work aims to bridge gaps between operational firefighting practices and computational risk management, fostering resilience in fire-prone regions.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, theory, and practices associated with the management of fire operations, firefighting services, and community fire issues. Includes instruction in fire protection history and theory, incident command leadership, administration of public fire organizations, labor relations, emergency medical services management, fire emergency response strategies and mitigation, legal and regulatory responsibilities, budgeting, public relations, and organizational leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of geometric structures on manifolds with non-trivial holonomy, particularly those arising in the study of special metrics (e.g., Einstein, Hermitian-Yang-Mills) and their stability under geometric flows. A central challenge lies in analyzing the nonlinear partial differential equations governing these structures, which exhibit high-dimensional symmetry and require resolving fine-scale geometric singularities. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture dynamic bifurcations or quantify metastable configurations in such systems, necessitating a computational approach. We propose large-scale numerical simulations of geometric flows, including Ricci and mean curvature flow, on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to probe stability thresholds and singularity formation in dimensionally reduced settings. The computational framework will combine adaptive finite element discretization for evolving geometries with parallelized spectral methods to handle curvature-driven nonlinearities. Key tasks include implementing distributed-memory algorithms for tensor bundle operations over stratified manifolds and optimizing GPU-accelerated solvers for time-stepping in low-regularity regimes. These simulations aim to generate conjectures about topological obstructions to metric convergence and identify universal scaling behaviors near singularities. Outcomes will directly inform ongoing work on classifying holonomy groups in dimension ≥8 and contribute to open problems in geometric analysis, such as the existence of asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau metrics. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the O(10^6) core-hour scaling required for resolving multiscale interactions in high co-dimension embeddings and the need for petascale data handling during persistent homology analyses of flow trajectories. Successful execution will provide quantitative benchmarks for theoretical studies while advancing computational methodologies at the interface of differential geometry and numerical PDEs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties, measurements, and relationships pertaining to points, lines, angles, surfaces, and solids. Includes instruction in global analysis, differential geometry, Euclidian and Non-Euclidian geometry, set theory, manifolds, integral geometry, and applications to algebra and other topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dance as a dynamic cultural and biomechanical phenomenon through computational analysis of movement patterns and choreographic structures. While dance has historically been examined through qualitative frameworks, the growing availability of motion-capture data and digitized Labanotation archives presents an opportunity to quantitatively analyze large-scale movement datasets. However, processing these datasets—spanning diverse dance traditions, temporal scales, and cultural contexts—requires significant computational power beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The research problem centers on identifying cross-cultural movement signatures and choreographic evolution patterns, which are obscured in smaller datasets or manual analysis. Using motion-capture data from global dance archives and Labanotation transcriptions, the project will apply machine learning algorithms to classify movement sequences, simulate kinematic variations, and model choreographic decision-making processes. Computational methods will include time-series analysis of joint kinematics, graph-based representations of choreographic networks, and probabilistic modeling of improvisational structures in jazz and contemporary dance. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the team aims to process over 10,000 hours of annotated dance data, enabling comparative studies of biomechanical efficiency in classical ballet versus folk traditions, as well as the cultural transmission of gestural motifs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of computationally tagged movement elements, tools for automated Labanotation generation, and new theoretical frameworks linking choreographic complexity to cultural narratives. This work will provide dance scholars with unprecedented scalability in analyzing movement as data, while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations between performing arts and computational sciences. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations and training deep learning models on heterogeneous movement corpora, tasks that are infeasible without distributed computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to express ideas, feelings, and/or inner visions through the performance of one or more of the dance disciplines, including but not limited to ballet, modern, jazz, ethnic, and folk dance, and that focuses on the study and analysis of dance as a cultural phenomenon. Includes instruction in technique, choreography, Laban notation, dance history and criticism, and dance production.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance trauma counseling interventions by integrating neurobiological, behavioral, and therapeutic data into predictive models of treatment response. Current approaches to trauma-related disorders, such as PTSD, often rely on generalized protocols that do not account for individual variability in neurocognitive adaptations post-trauma. A critical gap exists in understanding how dynamic interactions between neural circuit reorganization, epigenetic markers, and therapeutic engagement influence recovery trajectories. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining multimodal datasets—including functional neuroimaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), epigenomic profiles, and longitudinal clinical outcomes—from a cohort of 800 individuals with trauma-related disorders. Machine learning models will be trained to identify neurobehavioral subtypes predictive of responsiveness to specific trauma-focused therapies, such as cognitive processing therapy or eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR). HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution neuroimaging data, running parallelized simulations of neural network plasticity under varying intervention scenarios, and optimizing deep learning architectures to handle temporal patterns in treatment adherence and symptom remission. The project also includes the development of an open-source toolkit for real-time analysis of client-reported outcomes during therapy sessions, using natural language processing to detect latent indicators of progress or relapse. Expected outcomes include validated predictive biomarkers for personalized trauma therapy selection, computational models of neuroplasticity linked to therapeutic dosing, and scalable tools for dynamic treatment adaptation. By bridging neurobiology, artificial intelligence, and clinical counseling practice, this work aims to establish a data-driven paradigm for precision trauma care, reducing trial-and-error in treatment planning and improving long-term recovery rates.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on understanding elements of traumatic exposure, trauma-sensitive care, and crisis intervention. Includes instruction in disaster response, grief and loss counseling, crisis intervention and management, trauma counseling, neurobiology of trauma, PTSD and combat-related trauma, relational trauma and treatment of trauma-related disorders.

abstract: Urban horticulture faces unique challenges due to dynamic environmental conditions, fragmented land use, and the need for resource-efficient food production in densely populated areas. This project seeks to optimize crop selection and management strategies for urban horticulture systems by modeling complex interactions between plant physiology, microclimate variability, and soil-plant-water dynamics at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The research problem centers on developing predictive frameworks that account for heterogeneous urban conditions—including heat island effects, pollution gradients, and variable substrate quality—to recommend context-specific cultivars and cultivation practices. Current approaches rely on generalized agronomic data or simplified models that fail to capture site-specific urban biophysical interactions, leading to suboptimal yields and unsustainable resource use. To address this gap, we propose a computational workflow integrating high-resolution environmental sensor data from distributed urban farms with process-based crop models and machine learning. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized execution of modified Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Continuum (SPAC) models across thousands of simulated urban growing scenarios, incorporating 3D radiative transfer modeling for vertical farming systems and hydrodynamic simulations of engineered substrates. Bayesian optimization will identify robust cultivar-management combinations under uncertainty, while graph neural networks will analyze spatial dependencies across urban zones. Expected outcomes include (1) a decision-support tool for adaptive crop planning in heterogeneous urban environments, (2) quantitative benchmarks for water-use efficiency and yield stability across representative city morphologies, and (3) open-source computational models linking urban microclimate data to plant performance predictions. This work will directly inform municipal horticulture policies and provide scalable computational methods for sustainable urban food production, advancing both applied agricultural science and data-driven resource management in cities. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the combinatorial complexity of modeling fine-grained environmental variables across diverse urban topographies and the need for real-time parameter optimization in iterative simulations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on principles and techniques for the production of horticultural crops in an urban environment. Includes instruction in ecology, environmental sustainability, food production systems, and plant and soil sciences.

abstract: Orthotic and prosthetic (O&P) device design faces persistent challenges in balancing biomechanical efficacy, patient-specific customization, and material durability under dynamic physiological loads. Current empirical methods for optimizing device parameters (e.g., socket geometry, material layering, or joint alignment) are time-intensive and often lack the resolution to predict long-term biomechanical interactions in diverse patient populations. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to simulate and optimize O&P devices using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Leveraging patient-specific data—including gait analysis, musculoskeletal imaging, and material stress-strain profiles—we will construct finite element models (FEMs) to evaluate device performance under simulated physiological conditions (e.g., walking, running, load-bearing). Multiscale modeling techniques will integrate tissue-level biomechanics with whole-body dynamics to predict pressure distribution, energy expenditure, and tissue adaptation over time. Machine learning algorithms will then iteratively refine device designs to minimize interface stresses, improve gait symmetry, and enhance comfort. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational complexity of these simulations, which involve millions of mesh elements, nonlinear material properties, and stochastic optimization processes. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for personalized O&P design, a scalable optimization pipeline for clinical workflows, and novel insights into the interplay between device mechanics and patient physiology. This work will directly inform evidence-based practices in orthotics/prosthetics, reducing iterative fitting times and improving functional outcomes for patients with limb loss or musculoskeletal impairments. By enabling high-resolution, patient-specific simulations, this project bridges gaps between computational engineering and clinical O&P practice, fostering innovation in assistive technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: The efficient control of turbulent transport in magnetically confined plasmas remains a critical challenge for advancing fusion energy technologies. Current experimental and theoretical frameworks struggle to resolve the multi-scale, nonlinear interactions between electromagnetic fields, plasma instabilities, and particle dynamics under extreme temperatures.
