This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform kinetic simulations of turbulent transport in tokamak-relevant plasmas, focusing on the interplay between microturbulence, macro-scale magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) modes, and non-local transport phenomena. Using a hybrid computational approach, we will combine gyrokinetic Particle-in-Cell (PIC) methods for small-scale turbulence with global MHD solvers to capture system-scale dynamics. These simulations will resolve ion and electron kinetics at temporal and spatial scales inaccessible to existing experimental diagnostics, enabling the study of cross-scale coupling mechanisms that drive anomalous heat and particle losses. The computational workload necessitates large-scale parallelization, with simulations spanning millions of core-hours to achieve the required resolution across three-dimensional domains. Key objectives include identifying instability thresholds under varying magnetic configurations, quantifying the impact of sheared flows on turbulence suppression, and validating models against experimental data from fusion devices. The outcomes will directly inform the optimization of magnetic confinement strategies for next-generation fusion reactors and advance fundamental understanding of non-equilibrium plasma behavior. By elucidating the role of multi-scale interactions in transport processes, this work will also contribute to the broader development of predictive models for high-temperature plasmas, with applications spanning laboratory plasmas and advanced propulsion systems. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current memory and processing limitations, enabling parameter scans at experimentally relevant plasma beta values and collisionality regimes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of properties and behavior of matter at high temperatures, such that molecular and atomic structures are in a disassociated ionic or electronic state. Includes instruction in magnetohydrodynamics, free electron phenomena, fusion theory, electromagnetic fields and dynamics, plasma and non-linear wave theory, instability theory, plasma shock phenomena, quantitative modeling, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: The management of diseases affecting the inner ear and temporal bone remains challenging due to the complex microanatomy and biomechanical interactions underlying auditory and vestibular function. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized anatomical models, which may not adequately capture patient-specific pathophysiology or predict individualized treatment outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multiscale computational models of the human temporal bone and its neurotological systems. High-resolution imaging data from clinical CT and MRI scans will be integrated into finite element models simulating mechanical, acoustic, and fluid-structure interactions within the cochlea, semicircular canals, and associated neural structures. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to optimize model parameters using retrospective clinical datasets, enabling predictive analyses of surgical interventions, implant design optimization, and drug delivery systems. The computational workflows will be validated against intraoperative findings and post-treatment outcome data from collaborating neurotology clinics. By enabling submillimeter-scale simulations of pathological processes—such as otosclerosis, Meniere’s disease, and superior canal dehiscence—this research aims to uncover mechanistic insights into disease progression and treatment resistance. The anticipated outcomes include the development of patient-specific surgical planning tools, virtual testing platforms for implantable devices, and predictive models for non-invasive therapies. This work will provide a computational foundation for advancing precision medicine in neurotology, with direct implications for improving functional outcomes in hearing restoration and vestibular rehabilitation. The scale of these simulations necessitates HPC resources, as individual models may require >10^6 core-hours to resolve multiphysics interactions across anatomical scales while maintaining clinical relevance.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat diseases of the ear and temporal bone, including disorders of hearing and balance.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and sustainable well-drilling practices necessitates advanced computational tools to address complex subsurface challenges. Current models for predicting borehole stability, multiphase fluid dynamics, and equipment performance under extreme conditions lack the resolution and integration required to optimize drilling operations in heterogeneous geological environments. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation framework to model coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical processes during drilling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) simulating real-time fluid-structure interactions during drill bit penetration using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA), (2) predicting formation fracture gradients through machine learning (ML)-enhanced geomechanical modeling, and (3) optimizing wellbore trajectory planning via multi-objective evolutionary algorithms. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 3D subsurface domains with millimeter-scale resolution, integrating terabytes of lithological data from regional drilling logs and downhole sensors. The computational workflow will employ hybrid MPI-OpenMP architectures to resolve transient phenomena such as cuttings transport efficiency and pressure surge effects during tripping operations. Validation will utilize field data from active oil and water wells in sedimentary basins, comparing model outputs with downhole pressure measurements and rate-of-penetration records. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for minimizing non-productive time (NPT) due to stuck pipe incidents, a risk quantification framework for lost circulation scenarios, and optimized drilling parameters for reduced energy consumption. This work will advance the integration of physics-based modeling and data-driven decision-making in drilling operations, with direct applications to geothermal well design and environmentally sensitive hydrocarbon extraction. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the required scale and fidelity for these simulations, which cannot feasibly run on local clusters due to memory and runtime constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, maintain, repair, and operate well drilling equipment; locate, drill, construct, and develop water, gas, and oil wells; and test and monitor wells to ensure adequate flow. Includes applications to home, business, and industrial uses.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in real-time legal transcription and captioning, an interdisciplinary niche within court reporting that intersects computational linguistics, accessibility technology, and judicial workflow optimization. Current court reporting systems face limitations in processing speed, accuracy, and adaptability when handling complex legal terminology, overlapping speech, or low-quality audio inputs, particularly in high-stakes environments such as multi-accents, multilingual proceedings, or remote testimony scenarios. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to enhance real-time transcription fidelity while maintaining compliance with legal standards for verbatim accuracy. The proposed approach combines machine learning models for domain-specific speech recognition (trained on legal corpora) with natural language processing (NLP) techniques to contextualize utterances within procedural norms, statutory language, and case-specific glossaries. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of neural networks on heterogeneous datasets—including historical court transcripts, simulated audio distortions, and synthetic edge cases—to improve robustness against acoustic variability and dialect diversity. Additionally, real-time inference pipelines will be optimized using GPU-accelerated architectures to reduce latency below human perception thresholds (≤100ms). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive legal transcription, validated against certified court reporter benchmarks, and a public dataset of annotated legal proceedings to support future research. The project’s significance lies in its potential to democratize access to accurate captioning in underserved jurisdictions, reduce cognitive load for human reporters, and establish computational best practices for ethical AI integration in legally sensitive contexts. By bridging gaps between linguistic precision, computational efficiency, and judicial integrity, this work aims to set a precedent for emerging technologies in non-STEM disciplines that prioritize equitable access to justice.
cip_title: Court Reporting and Captioning/ Court Reporter
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to record and transcribe examinations, testimony, judicial orders and instructions, legal opinions, and other formal proceedings via print or electronic methods. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcription, shorthand, verbatim recording, equipment operation and procedures, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Healthcare administrative systems face increasing complexity due to evolving regulatory demands, patient volume variability, and the integration of multi-modal health data. Current manual or semi-automated approaches to scheduling, resource allocation, and compliance tracking often lead to inefficiencies, contributing to delayed care and operational costs. This project proposes to develop and validate computational models to optimize medical administrative workflows using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on three interconnected areas: (1) simulating clinic scheduling dynamics under stochastic patient demand, (2) automating compliance checks for electronic health record (EHR) documentation using natural language processing (NLP), and (3) optimizing resource allocation for multi-site healthcare networks through constraint-based modeling. Agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation frameworks will be implemented to capture interactions between patients, providers, and administrative staff, while transformer-based NLP models will be trained to identify documentation gaps in clinical narratives. Monte Carlo methods will assess operational risk under diverse scenarios. The computational intensity of training NLP models on large-scale de-identified EHR datasets and running parallel simulations across thousands of parameter combinations necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing patient wait times, algorithms for real-time compliance auditing, and decision-support systems for equitable resource distribution. Results will be validated against operational data from three partner healthcare networks. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on advancing healthcare operations through technology, offering scalable solutions to reduce administrative burdens while maintaining ethical data stewardship. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to establish computationally informed best practices for medical administration, directly benefiting training curricula in healthcare management and executive assistance.
cip_title: Medical Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Medical Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing physicians and nurses, health care facilities and services administrators, and other health care professionals. Includes instruction in business and medical communications, medical terminology, principles of health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between household financial decision-making, economic uncertainty, and adaptive resource management strategies. The research problem centers on understanding how families navigate complex financial trade-offs—such as debt prioritization, emergency savings allocation, and long-term investment decisions—under conditions of macroeconomic volatility. Traditional linear models often fail to capture the nonlinear, interdependent factors influencing these choices, particularly when accounting for heterogeneous household demographics, regional economic disparities, and evolving policy landscapes. To address this gap, the project will develop an agent-based computational framework simulating decision-making processes across diverse household archetypes, integrating real-world data on income variability, expenditure patterns, and behavioral biases. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallelization of scenarios, testing the resilience of financial strategies under stochastic shocks such as job loss, inflation spikes, or healthcare emergencies. Machine learning techniques will be applied to anonymized public datasets (e.g., consumer expenditure surveys, credit market trends) to parameterize agent behaviors and validate model outputs. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for identifying households most vulnerable to fiscal instability, a comparative analysis of intervention efficacy (e.g., debt relief programs, financial literacy initiatives), and a novel methodological bridge between computational social science and family resource management. By quantifying the cascading effects of micro-level financial choices on macroeconomic stability, this work aims to inform policy design while advancing computational approaches in a domain traditionally reliant on qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods. The scalability of the proposed models, made feasible through HPC resources, will support reproducible, granular insights into how families adapt resource allocation strategies in an era of accelerating economic complexity.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and implementation of policies and processes contributing to successful individual and family resource management. Includes instruction in financial goal-setting and strategies; household income, assets, and debt management; preventing and resolving financial difficulties; and the use of relevant public resources.

abstract: The immune system’s ability to distinguish self from non-self is central to effective pathogen clearance and prevention of autoimmunity. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying host-pathogen recognition and immune evasion by highly adaptable pathogens, such as influenza A virus (IAV) and Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), remain incompletely resolved. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model dynamic interactions between pathogen-derived antigens, host immune receptors, and regulatory signaling networks. A key focus is elucidating how structural variability in viral/bacterial epitopes and host major histocompatibility complex (MHC) polymorphisms influence T-cell receptor (TCR) binding affinity and subsequent immune activation or tolerance. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will be performed on experimentally validated epitope-MHC-TCR complexes to map energy landscapes and conformational changes across microsecond timescales. Parallelized docking algorithms will screen large libraries of pathogen-derived peptides against MHC alleles prevalent in human populations, prioritizing candidates for experimental validation. Additionally, agent-based models will simulate spatial-temporal immune cell interactions in infected tissues, integrating single-cell RNA-seq data to predict how cytokine gradients and cellular migration patterns shape effector vs. regulatory responses. These computational workflows require HPC resources due to the scale of conformational sampling (≥10^6 MD frames per system), combinatorial complexity of peptide-MHC binding predictions (>10^8 combinations), and stochasticity in multicellular simulations. Expected outcomes include identifying conserved epitopes for cross-protective vaccine design, characterizing immune evasion mutations in persistent infections, and uncovering TCR signaling thresholds that predispose to autoimmune dysregulation. This work will advance translational immunology by bridging structural insights with systems-level models of immune decision-making, directly informing targeted immunotherapy strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on scientific study of the biological mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of disease, host-pathogen interactions, and host response to disease. Includes instruction in antigen and antibody structure and function, effector mechanisms, receptors, histocompatibility, host-pathogen recognition, disease modeling, autoimmune systems, antibody formation, cytotoxic responses, regulation of immune response, virulence determinants, intercellular signaling, immunosuppression, immunotherapy, immunogenetics, disease markers, transplantation, antibody humanization, and microbial pathogenesis.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the chemical dynamics of silicate mineral interactions under extreme pressure and temperature conditions prevalent in Earth’s mantle and crustal systems. A critical gap persists in understanding how silicate reactivity governs elemental redistribution and isotopic fractionation during metamorphic and magmatic processes, particularly at scales relevant to planetary differentiation. Current models rely on simplified thermodynamic approximations or experimental extrapolations, which fail to capture the coupled kinetic and equilibrium behavior of multicomponent silicate systems over geological timescales. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating quantum mechanical simulations, reactive transport modeling, and machine learning–accelerated free energy calculations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform large-scale density functional theory (DFT) simulations of silicate melt structures, molecular dynamics (MD) modeling of diffusion-limited reactions, and Monte Carlo sampling of isotopic exchange equilibria. These datasets will parameterize a reactive transport code designed to simulate geochemical evolution in spatially heterogeneous systems, accounting for variable redox states, fluid-rock ratios, and crystallographic controls. The project will prioritize benchmarking against experimental studies of olivine-pyroxene equilibria and subduction zone fluid metasomatism. Successful implementation will yield (1) atomistic insights into silicate melt speciation under lithospheric conditions, (2) predictive models of rare earth element partitioning during metamorphic reactions, and (3) open-source tools for interpreting non-traditional stable isotope data in igneous systems. By resolving discrepancies between existing geochemical proxies and observed natural samples, this work will advance quantitative constraints on planetary-scale element cycling and inform exploration strategies for critical mineral resources. The requested computing allocation will enable simulations at previously inaccessible spatiotemporal resolutions, directly supporting the development of a unified, physics-based framework for high-temperature geochemical processes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemical properties and behavior of the silicates and other substances forming, and formed by geomorphological processes of the earth and other planets. Includes instruction in chemical thermodynamics, equilibrium in silicate systems, atomic bonding, isotopic fractionation, geochemical modeling, specimen analysis, and studies of specific organic and inorganic substances.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance the design and operational efficiency of next-generation submerged marine energy harvesting systems by addressing unresolved fluid-structure-sediment interactions in dynamic tidal environments. Current designs for underwater tidal turbines and oscillating hydrofoils face performance degradation due to complex, small-scale turbulent flow phenomena, biofouling, and sediment transport effects—interactions poorly captured by existing low-fidelity models. This project will develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating large-eddy simulation (LES), discrete element modeling (DEM), and phase-field methods to resolve multiphysics interactions across spatiotemporal scales. The computational approach leverages adaptive mesh refinement to dynamically resolve boundary layers, vortex shedding, and particle-laden flows around deformable structures, while machine learning surrogate models will accelerate parameter optimization. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the anticipated 10^8–10^9 degree-of-freedom simulations across parametric variations of turbine geometry, sediment grain size distributions, and unsteady inflow conditions derived from field data. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for power output and fatigue life under realistic sediment-laden flows, (2) optimized blade morphologies balancing energy capture efficiency with erosion resistance, and (3) open-source tools for assessing site-specific environmental impacts of marine energy installations. By bridging gaps between coastal hydrodynamics, materials science, and renewable energy systems, this work will directly inform the engineering of robust marine energy converters while establishing computational benchmarks for fluid-sediment-structure interaction problems in ocean engineering applications. The resulting framework will be extensible to other submerged infrastructure challenges, including underwater sensor networks and habitat restoration structures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to monitor, control, manipulate and operate within coastal or ocean environments, such as underwater platforms, flood control systems, dikes, hydroelectric power systems, tide and current control and warning systems, and communications equipment; the planning and design of total systems for working and functioning in water or underwater environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as the action of water properties and behavior on physical systems and people, tidal forces, current movements, and wave motion.

abstract: Histologic analysis remains foundational in diagnosing diseases, yet current methodologies for interpreting complex tissue architectures often rely on subjective, qualitative assessments. This project seeks to address the critical gap in quantitative, high-resolution analysis of three-dimensional (3D) histologic datasets, particularly in the context of early-stage neoplasia detection and microenvironmental characterization. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop and validate a computational pipeline integrating artificial intelligence (AI)-driven image segmentation, spatial transcriptomic alignment, and biomechanical modeling of tissue integrity. The research will utilize whole-slide imaging (WSI) datasets from clinical biopsy specimens, focusing on epithelial-mesenchymal transition patterns in gastrointestinal tissues. Computational workflows will be designed to process terabytes of multiplexed immunofluorescence and second-harmonic generation microscopy data, employing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) optimized for volumetric feature extraction. Parallelized finite element analysis will model tissue stress distributions correlated with cellular atypia. The integration of these multimodal datasets demands significant memory bandwidth and GPU acceleration to achieve clinically relevant turnaround times. Anticipated outcomes include novel quantitative biomarkers for dysplasia grading and an open-source framework for 3D histologic reconstruction. This work bridges the technical divide between traditional histotechnologist expertise and computational pathology, offering a paradigm shift in diagnostic objectivity. Successful implementation will directly enhance diagnostic concordance in borderline histologic cases while providing a scalable platform for investigating tissue-level biomarkers in precision medicine initiatives. The requested HPC allocation is essential for managing the nonlinear computational complexity of correlating nanoscale cellular features with macroscale tissue biomechanics across diverse patient cohorts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, at the request of physicians, researchers, and laboratory scientists, to identify tissue structures and cell components and relate these findings to physiological functions and to the detection and diagnosis of diseases and other abnormalities. Includes instruction in medical chemistry, histochemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, medical informatics, applied mathematics, electron microscopy, instrumentation, quality control procedures, data recording and analysis, laboratory administration, medical terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing generative artificial intelligence (AI) in creative industries, a critical emerging issue in Arts and Entertainment Law. The rapid proliferation of AI-generated content in music, visual arts, and digital media has created unprecedented legal ambiguities regarding copyright attribution, fair use boundaries, and contractual obligations—challenges compounded by the lack of cohesive transnational standards. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically process the scale and complexity of intersecting data, including international case law, licensing agreements, platform policies, and AI training data sources. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to mine and classify legal documents, contractual templates, and regulatory proposals from 50 jurisdictions, while graph neural networks will map citation patterns and normative conflicts across jurisdictions. Computational models will simulate hypothetical litigation scenarios based on varying AI training data disclosure requirements and authorship frameworks, evaluating their potential impacts on creative markets. By integrating legal text analysis with predictive modeling, this interdisciplinary approach aims to identify high-risk gaps in current intellectual property regimes and generate evidence-based proposals for adaptive governance structures. The computational outcomes will provide stakeholders—including policymakers, content platforms, and legal practitioners—with scalable tools to navigate AI-related disputes and negotiate equitable standards for human-AI creative collaboration. This work bridges computational legal studies and digital humanities, advancing methodological innovation in non-STEM domains while addressing urgent questions about artistic authorship in the algorithmic age.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting the sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, and media industries.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an adaptive modeling framework for optimizing personalized physical fitness regimens, with a focus on bridging gaps between exercise science, biomechanical data analytics, and client-specific behavioral patterns. Current fitness programming often relies on generalized protocols that inadequately account for individual variability in biomechanics, metabolic response, and adherence dynamics. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate heterogeneous datasets—including wearable device metrics, 3D motion capture kinematics, nutritional logs, and psychological readiness assessments—to generate dynamic, client-specific training prescriptions. Computational challenges arise from the need to process high-frequency biometric streams (e.g., EMG, heart rate variability) alongside qualitative client feedback in real time, requiring parallelized algorithms for pattern recognition and decision-tree optimization. The proposed method employs a hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks to map physiological interdependencies and agent-based models to simulate long-term adherence scenarios under varying program parameters. Expected outcomes include a scalable system capable of recommending exercise modifications during active training sessions while projecting longitudinal progress trajectories. This work addresses a critical gap in fitness technology, which currently lacks robust computational tools to harmonize acute biomechanical efficiency with chronic behavioral sustainability. Successful implementation could redefine standards for physical fitness technicians by providing evidence-based, computationally derived insights that enhance client outcomes while reducing injury risks. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the project’s multi-terabyte datasets and executing complex simulations of multivariate adaptation processes within physiologically relevant timeframes. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools tailored for fitness professionals, alongside novel metrics for quantifying program personalization efficacy.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in health and fitness clubs, wellness centers, public and private recreation facilities, hospitals and corporate fitness programs where they will perform a variety of instructional and administrative duties. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, fitness techniques, exercise science, personal training, nutrition, and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neurocognitive and phenomenological dynamics of contemplative practices across diverse cultural and philosophical traditions. While meditation, mindfulness, and related techniques are increasingly studied for their psychological and neurological effects, the integrative mechanisms linking subjective experience, neural plasticity, and behavioral outcomes remain poorly quantified. A core challenge lies in synthesizing heterogeneous datasets—including high-density neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), physiological biomarkers, first-person phenomenological reports, and historical-textual analyses—to model how contemplative training modulates attention, emotion regulation, and metacognition. Computational workflows will integrate multilevel Bayesian network analysis to identify cross-scale interactions between neural activity patterns, autonomic nervous system responses, and qualitative self-report data. Machine learning classifiers will be trained on curated datasets of contemplative narratives spanning Buddhist, Stoic, and mystical traditions to detect latent semantic structures associated with specific cognitive outcomes. Concurrently, biophysical neural simulations will explore how rhythmic electrical stimulation (e.g., transcranial alternating current stimulation) might entrain brain oscillations linked to states of focused attention or open monitoring. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale parameter optimization in neural models, real-time analysis of streaming biosensor data, and probabilistic fusion of sparse, high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for mapping subjective contemplative states to neurodynamic signatures, validated against both experimental data and philosophical accounts of consciousness. This work aims to advance evidence-based models of contemplative cognition while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between neuroscience, digital humanities, and ethics. By bridging quantitative and qualitative paradigms, the project will inform the design of personalized contemplative interventions and contribute foundational tools for studying consciousness across scientific and humanistic domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophical, psychological, and scientific bases of human contemplative experience. Includes instruction in cognitive science, meditation, mindfulness, neuroscience, philosophy, psychology, and religion.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the impact of enrollment trends, demographic shifts, and financial aid policies on institutional sustainability in higher education. As universities face mounting pressures from fluctuating enrollment patterns, changing student demographics, and evolving funding landscapes, administrators require predictive tools to optimize resource allocation and strategic planning. Traditional linear models often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between these variables, limiting their utility for decision-making. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled agent-based modeling (ABM) approach that simulates multi-year enrollment scenarios under varying policy and economic conditions. The model will integrate institutional datasets (e.g., applicant demographics, financial aid awards, retention rates) with external data sources (e.g., labor market trends, census projections) to simulate student decision-making processes, institutional revenue streams, and operational costs. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to refine parameter estimation and validate model outputs against historical patterns. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, we aim to run thousands of parameterized scenarios to identify optimal financial aid distribution strategies, predict enrollment cliffs, and quantify the fiscal impacts of alternative tuition models. Expected outcomes include a scalable tool for higher education administrators to proactively address enrollment challenges, mitigate financial risks, and evaluate equity implications of policy changes. The computational intensity of simulating diverse student populations and longitudinal interactions necessitates access to HPC resources for memory-intensive simulations and rapid iteration. This work aligns with national priorities in higher education administration by advancing data-driven approaches to institutional resilience while addressing critical gaps in predictive analytics for enrollment management and strategic finance.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in four-year colleges, universities and higher education systems, the study of higher education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in higher education economics and finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; college student services; research on higher education; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural and regional identities within Italian diaspora communities through the computational analysis of historical texts, oral histories, and multimedia archives. The research problem centers on understanding how localized traditions, dialects, and collective memories were preserved, adapted, or transformed across generations of migration, particularly in North and South American contexts from the late 19th to mid-20th centuries. Current methodologies in cultural studies lack scalable tools to systematically analyze the vast, multilingual corpus of personal correspondence, community newspapers, and audio recordings that document these transnational experiences. To address this gap, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical Italian dialects and English-Italian code-switching patterns, alongside network analysis to map the circulation of cultural narratives across migrant networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on fragmented, noisy textual data, as well as for running large-scale simulations of cultural transmission dynamics using agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include the development of a novel computational framework for diasporic cultural analysis, identification of key factors influencing identity retention in migrant enclaves, and geotemporal visualizations of cultural exchange hotspots. The findings will contribute to interdisciplinary scholarship on cultural memory and ethnic identity formation while providing open-access tools for analyzing underrepresented narratives in Italian diasporic heritage. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to overcome current limitations in processing heterogeneous historical sources at scale, offering new insights into how migration shaped modern conceptions of Italianness beyond national borders.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of modern Italy and its predecessors on the Italian Peninsula, including the overseas migrations of Italian peoples.

abstract: The increasing complexity of forensic evidence, particularly in cases involving trace chemical mixtures, presents significant challenges for traditional analytical methods. Current techniques for deconvoluting overlapping spectral data from gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) or liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) often lack the resolution and sensitivity required to identify low-abundance compounds in degraded or contaminated samples. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing machine learning (ML) models optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of forensic chemical analysis. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating scalable algorithms to resolve complex spectral signatures from multi-component forensic samples (e.g., synthetic drug mixtures, environmental toxins in biological matrices) and (2) simulating degradation pathways of forensically relevant compounds under varying environmental conditions using molecular dynamics (MD). HPC resources will enable the training of deep neural networks on curated spectral libraries encompassing >100,000 authenticated forensic samples, as well as the execution of large-scale MD simulations to model compound stability in real-world scenarios (e.g., accelerated UV exposure, microbial interactions). The computational workflows will integrate open-source cheminformatics tools with custom Python scripts for parallelized data processing. Expected outcomes include a validated ML framework for automated compound identification with quantified uncertainty metrics and predictive models for evidence degradation timelines. These tools will directly support forensic casework by reducing turnaround times for toxicology reports, improving error rates in trace evidence analysis, and providing scientifically robust data for legal proceedings. The developed software will be disseminated as modular packages compatible with existing forensic laboratory information management systems (LIMS), ensuring broad applicability across the criminal justice sector.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical techniques and instrumentation to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence to aid in criminal investigations. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; biochemistry; forensic toxicology; instrumental analysis; crime scene processing; criminal investigation; forensic laboratory technology; and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to develop adaptive neurocognitive interfaces that dynamically respond to users’ real-time physiological and behavioral signals to optimize human-technology collaboration. The core challenge lies in integrating high-dimensional data streams—such as electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, and interaction logs—into predictive models that can infer cognitive states (e.g., attention, cognitive load, decision uncertainty) and adjust interface parameters within milliseconds. Existing approaches often rely on preconfigured heuristics or offline analyses, limiting their capacity to support fluid, context-aware interactions in dynamic environments like emergency response simulations or augmented reality training systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational architecture combining deep reinforcement learning (RL) for adaptive decision-making with lightweight neuromorphic models for low-latency signal processing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for two phases: (1) training large-scale RL agents on heterogeneous datasets spanning neurophysiological, behavioral, and environmental variables, and (2) deploying optimized models in virtualized testbeds that simulate real-world latency and concurrency constraints. Using GPU-accelerated clusters, we will parallelize hyperparameter optimization across RL policy networks and validate models through multi-agent simulations of human-machine teams. Expected outcomes include open-source frameworks for embedding real-time neuroadaptive logic into user interfaces, along with benchmarks quantifying performance gains in task completion time, error reduction, and user satisfaction. This work bridges gaps between affective computing, neuroergonomics, and distributed systems, offering a foundation for next-generation adaptive technologies in high-stakes domains where human-machine synergy is mission-critical.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on incorporating a human perspective into designing, researching, and creating technological interfaces. Includes instruction in design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in livestock populations poses a critical threat to animal health, food security, and zoonotic disease management. This project seeks to model the genomic and epidemiological drivers of AMR transmission in bovine populations, with a focus on identifying high-risk pathways for resistance gene dissemination. Current gaps in understanding the interplay between bacterial genomics, host immunity, and management practices hinder the development of targeted interventions in veterinary medicine. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating whole-genome sequencing data from pathogenic Escherichia coli isolates with agent-based epidemiological simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabyte-scale genomic datasets, perform phylogenetic reconstruction, and simulate transmission dynamics across heterogeneous herd environments. Machine learning models will identify genomic signatures associated with resistance persistence, while stochastic simulations will evaluate the efficacy of hypothetical intervention strategies, such as optimized antibiotic rotation protocols or vaccination schedules. The study will leverage existing data from regional veterinary diagnostic laboratories (n=15,000 isolates) and generate new sequencing data from longitudinal herd monitoring. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible genomic database annotated with resistance profiles, (2) predictive models linking management practices to AMR emergence rates, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for mitigating resistance spread in pre-clinical settings. This work directly supports pre-veterinary training by providing students with access to cutting-edge computational tools and datasets that reflect real-world challenges in livestock health management. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ simulation iterations and comparative genome analyses at unprecedented resolution, significantly advancing capacity to address AMR through computational veterinary science.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in veterinary medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the dynamics of decision-making processes in educational leadership under complex policy environments. Educational institutions increasingly face challenges such as resource constraints, equity-driven reforms, and crisis response demands, requiring leaders to balance competing priorities while navigating multilayered policy frameworks. Traditional qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods often fail to capture the emergent, system-level behaviors arising from interactions between stakeholders, policies, and institutional structures. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach simulating how school administrators, district leaders, and policymakers adapt strategies in response to shifting regulations, community needs, and organizational constraints. The model will integrate real-world datasets on school funding, student demographics, and policy compliance records, parameterized through interviews with education leaders. HPC resources are critical to scaling simulations across thousands of hypothetical policy scenarios, enabling sensitivity analyses of variables such as funding allocation models, staff retention strategies, and communication networks. Machine learning techniques will further identify patterns in decision pathways that correlate with equitable outcomes or institutional resilience. Expected outcomes include a computational framework to predict unintended consequences of policy designs, optimize leadership training protocols, and inform adaptive strategies for systemic change. By bridging computational social science with education leadership praxis, this work aims to advance data-driven tools for fostering agile, equity-centered organizations in K-12 and higher education systems.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Organizational Leadership and Policy Development with an emphasis on education. Includes instruction on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, education administration and supervision, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: The dynamical evolution of small bodies in the early solar system remains poorly understood, particularly how gravitational interactions with forming planets shaped their orbital distribution and influenced planetary migration. This project seeks to model the complex interplay between protoplanets, planetesimals, and giant planets during the first 100 million years of solar system formation, with a focus on resolving how these interactions produced observed features in the asteroid belt, Kuiper Belt, and comet reservoirs. Current simulations struggle to capture the multi-scale nature of these dynamics, which require simultaneously resolving short-term close encounters and long-term orbital resonances over gigayear timescales. To address this, we propose high-resolution N-body simulations using the REBOUND code, enhanced with custom GPU-accelerated modules for collision detection and tidal forces. These simulations will track the trajectories of up to 10^5 particles under gravitational and radiative influences, incorporating time-variable protoplanetary disk conditions and stochastic perturbations from early giant planet migration. The parameter space will explore variations in initial disk mass profiles, planetary embryo configurations, and Jupiter’s hypothesized orbital excursions. By leveraging high-performance computing resources, we aim to achieve the necessary temporal and spatial resolution to identify mechanisms driving small-body scattering, resonant capture, and ejection. Expected outcomes include statistically robust constraints on the solar system’s primordial architecture, new insights into the role of chaotic resonances in depleting the asteroid belt, and improved models linking present-day small-body populations to early migration events. Results will directly inform interpretations of upcoming observational campaigns, such as LSST detections of distant solar system objects and JWST spectroscopy of exoplanetary debris disks. This work requires large-scale parallelization, with an estimated need for 500,000 core-hours to complete parameter sweeps and validate against planetary chronometer datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of planets, small objects, and related gravitational systems. Includes instruction in the structure and composition of planetary surfaces and interiors, planetary atmospheres, satellites, orbital mechanics, asteroids and comets, solar system evolution and dynamics, planetary evolution, gravitational physics, and radiation physics.

abstract: Healthcare facility operations rely heavily on efficient administrative workflows to ensure timely patient care, but manual processes for scheduling, order transcription, and resource coordination remain prone to inefficiencies and errors. This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize ward clerk workflows by analyzing patterns in patient intake, staff availability, and procedural scheduling across diverse hospital units. The research problem centers on the lack of data-driven tools to predict and mitigate workflow bottlenecks in dynamic healthcare environments. Using anonymized electronic health record (EHR) data and historical unit operation logs from partner institutions, we will employ machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate patient flow scenarios and evaluate the impact of alternative scheduling strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning years of operational records, including free-text nursing orders requiring natural language processing (NLP) for automated classification. Computational experiments will test reinforcement learning models for adaptive staff assignment and GPU-accelerated simulations of emergency department intake patterns under varying patient volumes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce procedural delays, algorithms to prioritize time-sensitive orders, and visual dashboards for real-time workload monitoring. By quantifying relationships between administrative decisions and patient throughput, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for health unit coordination training programs. The scalability of these models will be validated across simulated urban, rural, and specialty care settings, with potential to reduce preventable care delays by 15-20% in pilot units. Results will inform curriculum updates for health unit coordinator certification programs while maintaining compliance with healthcare privacy regulations through synthetic data generation techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: Palliative care nursing requires the integration of complex clinical, psychosocial, and patient-reported data to optimize care for individuals with life-threatening illnesses. However, current approaches to analyzing these multidimensional datasets are limited by conventional statistical methods, which struggle to model nonlinear interactions, longitudinal trends, and heterogeneous patient trajectories. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced machine learning models capable of identifying patterns in palliative care outcomes, such as pain management efficacy, quality-of-life metrics, and caregiver burden. The research will utilize de-identified electronic health records, longitudinal symptom assessments, and qualitative data from patient-family interactions (e.g., transcribed nurse interviews, free-text clinical notes) to train predictive and clustering algorithms. Key computational tasks include natural language processing (NLP) of unstructured narratives to quantify psychosocial distress, ensemble modeling to predict hospitalization risk, and time-series analysis of symptom progression. These methods demand significant memory and parallel processing capabilities due to the scale of multimodal data (>50,000 patient records with high-dimensional features) and the iterative nature of model optimization. The outcomes will enable the identification of patient subgroups most likely to benefit from specific palliative interventions, real-time risk stratification tools for clinicians, and dynamic care planning frameworks that adapt to evolving patient needs. By integrating computational rigor with nursing expertise, this work aims to advance evidence-based palliative care strategies, reduce trial-and-error in treatment decisions, and improve resource allocation in hospice and homecare settings. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical to handling data complexity, ensuring reproducibility, and scaling models for real-world clinical deployment. This project underscores the transformative potential of computational methods in palliative nursing, offering a template for data-driven innovation in health professions research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide a combination of active and compassionate therapies intended to comfort and support patients and their families who are living with life-threatening illness. Includes instruction in pathophysiology, palliative care processes, pain management, pharmacology, loss, grief, death, and bereavement.

abstract: The development of next-generation hypersonic vehicles requires resolving complex, multi-physics interactions between turbulent flows, aerodynamic heating, and structural response under extreme conditions. Current computational models struggle to predict transitional flow regimes and coupled aerothermal-structural behavior with sufficient accuracy, limiting design optimization and risk assessment. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale simulations of hypersonic boundary layer transition, turbulence, and material response using a coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) framework. High-fidelity direct numerical simulations (DNS) and wall-modeled large-eddy simulations (LES) will be performed for Mach 5–8 flows over representative vehicle geometries, resolving multiscale fluid-thermal-structural interactions across temporal and spatial scales. The computational approach integrates open-source solvers (SU2, FEniCS) with custom coupling algorithms, leveraging adaptive mesh refinement and hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization to optimize scalability on heterogeneous architectures. Simulations will utilize 5,000–10,000 cores per run, with petascale data outputs analyzed via in-situ machine learning techniques to extract coherent flow structures and quantify uncertainty. Expected outcomes include validated models for hypersonic transition prediction, aerothermal load characterization, and lightweight thermal protection system (TPS) design guidelines. These results will address critical gaps in physics-based predictive capabilities for high-speed flight regimes, directly supporting safer and more efficient aerospace vehicle development. The resource allocation will also advance computational methods for coupled multi-physics problems, fostering collaboration with national hypersonics research initiatives. By enabling unprecedented resolution of fluid-thermal-structural coupling, this work aims to accelerate the translation of fundamental aerodynamic insights into engineering solutions for next-generation aerospace systems.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aeronautics/ Aviation/ Aerospace Science and Technology, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of aviation and the aviation industry, including in-flight and ground support operations. Includes instruction in the technical, business, and general aspects of air transportation systems.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying plant responses to combined abiotic stresses, with a focus on drought and soil salinity—two interconnected challenges threatening global crop productivity. While prior studies have characterized plant stress responses under isolated conditions, real-world agricultural systems often expose plants to concurrent stressors, triggering nonlinear physiological and genomic interactions that remain poorly resolved. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets (genome, transcriptome, and metabolome) from maize (Zea mays) and soybean (Glycine max) subjected to combinatorial stress treatments. A hybrid computational pipeline will integrate machine learning-based feature selection, dynamic network modeling, and comparative genomics to identify conserved regulatory modules and stress-specific adaptive pathways. Bulk RNA-seq data from controlled-environment experiments will be supplemented with publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize structural changes in key stress-responsive proteins under varying ionic and osmotic conditions. The computational workload necessitates large-scale parallel processing for Bayesian network inference, GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures for pattern recognition in hyperspectral imaging data, and high-memory nodes for genome assembly tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model of core signaling hubs governing cross-stress adaptation, (2) candidate gene targets for breeding programs aimed at stress-resilient crops, and (3) open-source tools for multi-scale integration of plant phenomic and genomic data. By elucidating emergent properties of stress combination responses, this work will advance fundamental knowledge in plant systems biology while directly informing translational efforts to mitigate climate-related agricultural losses. The requested allocation of 250,000 CPU-core hours and 50 TB of temporary storage will support data-intensive workflows spanning 18 months, enabling analyses impractical on local institutional clusters.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plant sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance research in the Digital Humanities by addressing the computational challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous cultural datasets. Traditional methods in humanities scholarship often struggle to manage the volume and complexity of digitized archives, multimodal artifacts (e.g., texts, images, geospatial data), and dynamically generated social or historical datasets. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable pipelines for processing and analyzing these materials, integrating natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, geospatial mapping, and machine learning. The research focuses on two interdisciplinary case studies: (1) tracing the evolution of linguistic patterns and visual motifs in early modern manuscripts using transformer-based models and convolutional neural networks, and (2) reconstructing historical urban networks through geospatial analysis of archaeological records and trade documents. Both workflows require parallelized computation to process terabytes of high-resolution manuscript scans, multilingual texts, and spatially tagged metadata. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for training domain-specific ML models and CPU clusters for batch processing of markup languages (TEI-XML) and 3D artifact reconstructions. Outcomes will include open-source tools for corpus alignment and semantic annotation, interactive visualizations of cultural data, and a public digital repository of processed datasets. By enabling new forms of inquiry across anthropology, art history, and literature, this work aims to demonstrate how HPC can transform humanities scholarship—bridging qualitative analysis with computational rigor while fostering public engagement through accessible digital platforms. The results will provide methodological frameworks for resource-intensive humanities research, emphasizing reproducibility and interdisciplinary collaboration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of new technologies, advanced computing, and public engagement to investigate and analyze questions in the humanities. Includes instruction in anthropology, art, data mining and machine learning, design, digital archives, geospatial technologies, history, human-computer interface design, literature, markup languages, social media technologies, and software development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven decision-making models for optimizing district-level educational administration. A critical challenge in educational leadership is the dynamic allocation of limited resources—such as staffing, funding, and infrastructure—across schools with heterogeneous needs, particularly in rapidly changing demographic and policy environments. Traditional analytical tools struggle to integrate real-time data streams, simulate multi-year outcomes of resource distribution strategies, or account for complex interdependencies between variables like student mobility, budget fluctuations, and regulatory compliance. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate resource allocation scenarios under uncertainty. The ABM component will represent schools, administrators, and external stakeholders as interactive agents with rule-based and adaptive behaviors, while ML algorithms will train on historical administrative datasets (e.g., budget records, student performance metrics, staffing patterns) to predict emergent systemic outcomes. The project requires HPC resources to manage large-scale parallel simulations, process high-dimensional datasets from 10+ school districts, and optimize hyperparameters for scenario-based ML models. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable tool for district leaders to test hypothetical policies, identify equity gaps in resource distribution, and mitigate risks associated with centralized decision-making. This work will contribute novel methodologies to educational administration by bridging computational social science techniques with leadership practice, offering a replicable framework for data-intensive governance in K-12 systems. The computational demands of this project—particularly in handling terabyte-scale datasets and concurrent simulation runs—exceed the capacity of local institutional servers, necessitating access to HPC infrastructure for model training, validation, and real-time analytics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in education administration and supervision, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality, with complex conditions such as acute myocardial infarction and malignant arrhythmias posing persistent therapeutic challenges. Current clinical decision-making often relies on generalized guidelines, which inadequately address patient-specific anatomical, electrophysiological, and hemodynamic variability. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework for multiscale cardiac modeling to enable precision management of these conditions. The research will integrate clinical imaging data (CT, MRI), electroanatomical maps, and biomarker profiles to construct patient-specific simulations of cardiac electrophysiology, biomechanics, and blood flow dynamics. Key computational challenges include resolving spatiotemporal disparities between cellular-scale ion channel behavior (milliseconds, micrometers) and organ-level pathophysiology (minutes, centimeters), necessitating adaptive mesh refinement and parallelized solvers. The HPC infrastructure will support finite element modeling of ventricular arrhythmia substrates, coupled with computational fluid dynamics simulations of coronary perfusion in infarct border zones. Machine learning methods will be implemented to optimize parameter calibration from heterogeneous clinical datasets and predict arrhythmia susceptibility under stress conditions. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for sudden cardiac death risk stratification, virtual ablation target identification for ventricular tachycardia, and hemodynamic optimization strategies for post-infarct remodeling. By enabling real-time simulation of disease mechanisms across scales, this resource-intensive approach will advance the translation of mechanistic insights into individualized therapeutic protocols. The proposed computational platform will be disseminated as an open-access tool for clinical researchers, addressing a critical gap in cardiac care innovation. Successful implementation will directly inform therapeutic trials and refine guidelines for managing ischemic and arrhythmic complications, ultimately reducing the societal burden of advanced cardiovascular disease.
cip_definition: Research on how to specialize in diseases of the heart and blood vessels and to manage complex cardiac conditions such as heart attacks and life-threatening, abnormal heartbeat rhythms.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of extracorporeal circulation (ECC) dynamics during cardiopulmonary bypass and other perfusion-dependent surgical procedures. The clinical challenge lies in optimizing perfusion parameters—such as flow rates, oxygenation levels, and anticoagulation management—to mitigate risks of organ ischemia, hemolysis, or thromboembolic events, which remain significant sources of perioperative morbidity. Current practice relies on generalized protocols and real-time physiological monitoring, but interpatient variability in hemodynamic responses, comorbidities, and surgical demands complicates personalized optimization. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating patient-specific hemodynamic modeling, machine learning (ML)-based predictive analytics, and real-time simulation of ECC circuit interactions. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate blood flow and shear stress in ECC components, informed by 3D reconstructions of individual patient vasculature from pre-operative imaging. Concurrently, ML algorithms trained on retrospective perfusion data—including vital signs, blood gas analyses, and circuit performance metrics—will predict patient-specific responses to perfusion parameter adjustments. These models will be coupled via a real-time digital twin platform, enabling virtual testing of intervention strategies before clinical implementation. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational load of parallelized CFD simulations, large-scale ML training datasets (>10,000 case records), and iterative optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool capable of recommending personalized perfusion parameters, reducing trial-and-error adjustments during surgery. This work will establish a foundation for data-driven perfusion protocols, directly enhancing patient safety and operational efficiency in cardiac surgery. By integrating HPC-driven modeling into perfusion education, the project also aims to train future perfusionists in computational literacy, bridging gaps between clinical practice and quantitative biomedical engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to operate extracorporeal circulation and autotransfusion equipment during medical procedures and surgeries where the support or temporary replacement of a patient's own respiratory or circulatory system is required. Includes instruction in equipment selection and operation, physician and medical team consultation, patient condition monitoring, procedural techniques, and principles of respiratory and circulatory physiology.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the challenge of optimizing quantum-enhanced sensor networks for real-time monitoring of dynamic urban infrastructure systems. Current sensing technologies, while effective in controlled environments, struggle with resolution limits, signal-to-noise ratios, and data fusion inefficiencies when deployed across large-scale, heterogeneous systems such as smart bridges or underground utility networks. This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-layered computational framework integrating quantum sensor simulations, adaptive signal processing algorithms, and distributed network optimization. Using finite-element modeling and quantum master equation solvers, we will simulate nitrogen-vacancy center-based sensors operating under non-ideal field conditions, accounting for thermal fluctuations and electromagnetic interference. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on HPC clusters to enable predictive resource allocation across sensor arrays, optimizing measurement intervals and energy use while maintaining sub-millimeter spatial resolution. The computational workflow will employ hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization to handle the multi-scale nature of the problem, from nanoscale quantum interactions to city-scale infrastructure networks. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of guiding hardware-software co-design for next-generation urban monitoring systems, with potential applications in preemptive structural health assessment and emergency response coordination. This work bridges gaps between quantum device engineering, distributed systems theory, and infrastructure informatics, establishing computational methodologies for emerging "quantum smart city" technologies. The requested resources will enable parametric studies across 10^4+ sensor-node configurations and experimental noise profiles, significantly accelerating development cycles for field-deployable quantum sensing networks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of personalizing rehabilitation protocols for individuals with musculoskeletal impairments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate biomechanical modeling and machine learning. Current approaches often apply generalized treatment plans, which fail to account for individual variability in anatomy, movement patterns, and tissue healing, leading to suboptimal recovery outcomes. To overcome this limitation, we propose a computational framework that combines patient-specific biomechanical simulations with predictive analytics to optimize rehabilitation strategies. Motion capture data, electromyography (EMG) recordings, and clinical imaging will inform finite element models of musculoskeletal dynamics, simulating the biomechanical effects of therapeutic exercises across diverse patient cohorts. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze longitudinal clinical data to identify predictors of recovery success. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations and the processing of high-dimensional datasets. The integration of these computational outputs will generate adaptive rehabilitation protocols tailored to individual biomechanical profiles and recovery trajectories. Expected outcomes include validated models that predict patient-specific responses to therapy, a decision-support tool for rehabilitation aides, and a deeper understanding of mechanobiological factors influencing recovery. This research bridges computational biomechanics and clinical rehabilitation, offering a novel paradigm to enhance precision in rehabilitative care. By reducing trial-and-error in therapy design, the project has the potential to accelerate functional recovery, minimize complications, and improve resource allocation in rehabilitation settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and other therapeutic professionals, and to perform routine functions in support of rehabilitation. Includes instruction in roles and responsibilities of rehabilitation providers, basic function of the human body, disabling conditions, therapeutic skills, client management, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate computational modeling and machine learning into the design and fabrication of jewelry art, addressing the challenge of optimizing material behavior and structural integrity in complex, non-traditional forms. Traditional jewelry design relies heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which limits exploration of geometries that push the boundaries of metalsmithing, enameling, and composite material integration. This research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations to predict stress distribution, thermal dynamics, and fluid flow in advanced electroforming and casting processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolving multi-physics interactions at micron-scale resolutions across diverse materials such as precious metal alloys, reactive enamels, and polymer composites. Concurrently, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on historical and contemporary jewelry datasets to propose novel design frameworks that balance aesthetic innovation with manufacturability. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine generative outputs using physical simulation feedback, enabling data-driven adjustments to material ratios, layer thicknesses, and structural supports prior to fabrication. Expected outcomes include a validated workflow for computationally assisted jewelry creation, reducing material waste and production time while expanding viable design parameters. The project will further contribute open-source tools for simulating metal-art material interactions, bridging gaps between traditional craft knowledge and computational design methodologies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for jewelry arts that harmonizes artistic vision with predictive engineering principles, fostering innovation in both academic training and professional practice.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by fashioning jewelry from gems, other stones, and precious metals. Includes instruction in design concepts, electroforming, enameling, gemology, lapidary technique and art, metal and non-metal casting and molding, metal coloring, metalsmithing and finishing, personal style development, photo etching, and stone cutting and polishing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing strategies in hybrid auction environments, where real-time, multi-platform bidding intersects with specialized commodity markets (e.g., industrial equipment, rare collectibles). The core research problem lies in addressing the inefficiencies of current auctioneering models, which struggle to adapt pricing mechanisms to volatile bidder behavior, cross-platform competition, and heterogeneous asset valuations at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach to simulate hyperrealistic auction ecosystems, incorporating stochastic bidder networks, temporal valuation shifts, and regulatory constraints derived from sales law parameters. The computational model will process terascale datasets of historical auction transcripts, bid timing patterns, and post-auction market outcomes to train adaptive agents capable of predicting optimal bid-calling sequences, reserve price adjustments, and anti-collusion safeguards. By parallelizing agent interactions across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to evaluate millions of auction scenario permutations, identifying robust strategies that maximize auction house revenue while preserving bidder participation incentives. Expected outcomes include an open-source auction simulation toolkit validated against real-world data from automotive and agricultural equipment auctions, as well as predictive metrics for platform-specific revenue leakage risks. This work bridges computational economics and auctioneering practice, offering empirically grounded solutions for emerging challenges in decentralized digital auctions and high-stakes specialty markets. The HPC infrastructure is critical for maintaining temporal fidelity in agent training cycles and scaling scenario testing across diverse regulatory jurisdictions, directly addressing the computational intensity of modeling asynchronous, multi-lot auction events.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional careers as auctioneers and auction managers, and for meeting applicable state licensing requirements.
