Includes instruction in reproduction, growth, lactation, digestion, performance, behavioral adaptation, sensory perception, motor action, phylogenetics, biotic and abiotic function, membrane biology, and related aspects of biochemistry and biophysics.

abstract: The development of advanced materials with tailored mechanical and thermal properties is critical for applications in extreme environments, such as high-temperature industrial manufacturing or energy storage systems. However, experimental approaches to optimize these materials are often hindered by the complexity of multiscale phenomena, including atomic-scale defect dynamics and mesoscale microstructural evolution. This project seeks to address these challenges through a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and predict the behavior of novel refractory alloys and ceramic composites. We will employ ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and phase-field crystal (PFC) simulations to investigate atomic-scale interactions, defect nucleation, and grain boundary stability under thermomechanical stress. Concurrently, mesoscale phase-field models will elucidate microstructural evolution and crack propagation mechanisms. The integration of these methods across scales will be facilitated by hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization, enabling efficient utilization of HPC architectures. Machine learning algorithms will further accelerate parameter space exploration by correlating simulation data with experimental benchmarks. The anticipated outcomes include the identification of alloy compositions with enhanced high-temperature strength and thermal shock resistance, as well as predictive models linking processing conditions to microstructural outcomes. By providing fundamental insights into deformation and failure mechanisms, this work will guide the synthesis of next-generation materials for energy-efficient industrial processes. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the ∼10^6-atom systems in AIMD, the large-domain phase-field simulations, and the data-intensive machine learning workflows, which exceed the capacity of local cluster infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of mathematical, engineering and scientific principles such as internal structure, chemical properties, transport and energy flow properties, thermodynamics of solids, stress and failure factors, chemical transformation states and processes, and compound materials, to the analysis, design, evaluation, industrial applications, and production of materials a in a wide variety of settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance our understanding of hierarchical galaxy assembly through high-resolution cosmological simulations of merging galactic systems. A critical gap persists in modeling the multiscale physics governing gas dynamics, star formation, and feedback mechanisms during mergers, particularly in low-mass galaxies at intermediate redshifts (z ≈ 1–3). Existing simulations often oversimplify the interplay between turbulence, magnetic fields, and radiative cooling, limiting predictive power for observables such as metallicity gradients and stellar population distributions. To address this, we propose a suite of adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) simulations using the Enzo code, coupled with subgrid models for stellar feedback, chemical enrichment, and primordial magnetic field amplification. The simulations will resolve spatial scales down to 10 parsecs, capturing the formation of star-forming regions and the impact of supernova-driven winds on gas stripping in tidally disturbed systems. Initial conditions will be derived from cosmological volumes in the IllustrisTNG archives, with a focus on 50 merger events spanning gas-rich major mergers to minor accretion scenarios. Each simulation will integrate radiative transfer for UV background modulation and employ hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelism to optimize memory usage across GPU-CPU architectures. Expected outcomes include calibrated scaling relations between merger parameters, star formation bursts, and kinematic disk stabilization timescales, providing testable predictions for JWST and ALMA observations of resolved high-z mergers. The resulting datasets will be made publicly available through a dedicated portal, enabling follow-on studies of black hole seeding and dark matter halo response in merging systems. By quantifying the role of mergers in driving galactic diversity, this work will directly inform interpretations of upcoming large-scale surveys (e.g., LSST, Euclid) while refining the astrophysical priors used in semi-analytic galaxy formation models.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in astronomy and astrophysics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the role of biomechanical and molecular interactions in the progression of temporomandibular joint disorders (TMJD), a poorly understood class of conditions affecting jaw function and chronic pain. Despite their prevalence and impact on quality of life, TMJD mechanisms remain elusive due to the complex interplay between joint tissue mechanics, inflammatory pathways, and neural feedback. Current clinical models lack the resolution to capture these multiscale dynamics, hindering the development of targeted therapies. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of joint biomechanics with agent-based simulations of cellular inflammatory responses. The FEM component will simulate strain distributions and stress patterns in patient-specific jaw geometries derived from clinical CT/MRI data, while the agent-based module will model cytokine diffusion, immune cell migration, and nociceptor activation in response to mechanical stressors. This coupled approach requires iterative, high-resolution simulations across multiple temporal and spatial scales, necessitating HPC capabilities for parallel processing of large parameter spaces and optimization of machine learning-derived tissue constitutive models. Expected outcomes include identification of mechanobiological thresholds linked to TMJD progression and predictive biomarkers for patient stratification. The resource allocation will also support the development of an open-source simulation toolkit for musculoskeletal disorders, enabling reproducibility and extension to other joint systems. By elucidating TMJD pathophysiology through computational integration of biomechanical and molecular data, this work aims to advance precision medicine approaches for chronic musculoskeletal pain, a critical need underserved by conventional clinical paradigms.
cip_definition: Any program in medicine, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dental assisting practice faces critical challenges in optimizing clinical workflows, improving diagnostic support tools, and advancing educational simulations. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale clinical datasets and simulating complex biomechanical processes hinder progress in these areas. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address three interconnected aims: (1) developing machine learning models to automate anomaly detection in dental radiographs, (2) simulating sterilization efficacy under varying instrument configurations and microbial loads, and (3) creating virtual reality training environments with real-time biomechanical feedback. The computational workflow will integrate convolutional neural networks for radiographic image analysis, computational fluid dynamics simulations for sterilization chamber optimization, and finite element modeling for tooth-material interaction studies. A novel multimodal dataset will be curated from partner clinics, encompassing 50,000 anonymized radiographs, instrument sterilization logs, and 3D intraoral scans. Resource-intensive tasks include training vision transformers on radiographic datasets requiring GPU-accelerated nodes and running parallelized fluid dynamics simulations across multiple CPU cores. Expected outcomes include an open-source diagnostic support tool for early caries detection (achieving >90% sensitivity in preliminary benchmarks), validated sterilization protocols reducing process time by 15-20%, and adaptive training modules demonstrating improved student competency scores. By establishing computational frameworks tailored to dental assisting challenges, this research aims to elevate clinical standards, enhance educational outcomes, and provide evidence-based protocols for infection control—directly addressing critical needs in dental workforce development. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing of clinically significant dataset sizes while maintaining temporal resolution required for practical implementation timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide patient care, take dental radiographs (x-ray photographs), prepare patients and equipment for dental procedures, and discharge office administrative functions under the supervision of dentists and dental hygienists. Includes instruction in medical record-keeping, general office duties, reception and patient intake, scheduling, equipment maintenance and sterilization, basic radiography, pre- and post-operative patient care and instruction, chairside assisting, taking tooth and mouth impressions, and supervised practice.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of climate-resilient crop systems in diverse agroecological zones, addressing critical gaps in global food security. Current agricultural systems face escalating pressure from climate variability, population growth, and shifting pest dynamics, yet existing models often lack the spatial resolution and integration of multidisciplinary datasets required to inform actionable strategies. Our research focuses on developing a scalable computational framework that synthesizes high-resolution climate projections, soil-plant-atmosphere continuum data, and genomic information for staple crops such as maize, rice, and wheat. Using ensemble machine learning and agent-based modeling, we will simulate crop performance under multiple climate scenarios (RCP 4.5, 6.0, 8.5) while incorporating regional socioeconomic constraints, such as smallholder farming practices and market access limitations. The HPC infrastructure is essential to process petabytes of satellite imagery, hyperspectral data, and global soil databases, as well as to parallelize computationally intensive genotype-by-environment interaction analyses. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal crop varieties and management practices for understudied regions in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, alongside an open-access decision support tool for policymakers. By bridging gaps between agronomic research, computational scalability, and real-world agricultural constraints, this work aims to enhance the resilience of food systems across geopolitical and ecological boundaries, directly supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2 (Zero Hunger) and 13 (Climate Action). The proposed computational workflows will also establish a replicable template for integrating heterogeneous agricultural datasets, fostering international collaboration in sustainable agri-food system design.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of agricultural management and scientific principles to the problems of global food production and distribution, and to the study of the agricultural systems of other countries. Includes instruction in agricultural economics; comparative agricultural systems; international agribusiness and law; third-world development studies and economic development; and global applications of climate, soil, water resources, ecological and environmental studies, and animal and plant sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a real-time adaptive control system for next-generation neuroprosthetic devices that integrate bidirectional neural interfaces with wearable robotic exoskeletons. Current systems face critical limitations in dynamically interpreting user intent while delivering proprioceptive feedback, particularly during complex locomotor tasks. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in decoding high-dimensional neural data (ECoG, EMG) and synthesizing responsive mechanical assistance within physiologically relevant latencies (<50ms). We propose a hybrid computational architecture leveraging federated learning for personalized intent recognition models and physics-informed neural networks for predictive gait optimization. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel training of patient-specific neural decoders across multiple GPU nodes while simultaneously simulating musculoskeletal dynamics and exoskeleton interaction forces through multibody finite element analysis. The computational workflow will integrate heterogeneous data streams from our partner rehabilitation center, including motion capture, embedded force sensors, and chronic neural recordings from ongoing clinical trials. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for co-adaptive neuro-mechanical control that maintains synchronization across timescales spanning milliseconds (neural processing) to seconds (gait adaptation). Successful implementation could demonstrate clinically significant improvements in stair negotiation and obstacle avoidance tasks for lower-limb prosthesis users, measured through validated mobility metrics. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience and rehabilitation robotics by addressing the temporal hierarchy of sensorimotor integration—a prerequisite for restoring naturalistic movement patterns in patients with spinal cord injuries or stroke-related mobility impairments. The requested resources directly support large-scale parameter optimization and validation of our novel control paradigm against existing clinical datasets.
cip_title: Assistive/ Augmentative Technology and Rehabilitation Engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of psychology, engineering, and occupational therapy to the design and implementation of technological interventions and systems to promote patient rehabilitation and function. Includes instruction in ergonomics, seating and mobility design, universal and near environment systems design, rehabilitation research, rehabilitation biomechanics, access and communications design, microprocessor-based technologies, neurological trauma, standards and testing, and service delivery management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize decision-making in sport facility management through large-scale simulation and predictive analytics. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies in dynamic resource allocation within multi-use athletic facilities, where conflicting demands—such as concurrent events, maintenance schedules, and spectator traffic—create operational bottlenecks. Traditional heuristic approaches often fail to account for real-time variables, including weather disruptions, crowd behavior analytics, and emergency response logistics, leading to suboptimal utilization of space, personnel, and equipment. To address this, the project will develop a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate facility operations under diverse scenarios. The ABM module will map interactions between stakeholders (athletes, staff, spectators) and infrastructure, while ML algorithms trained on historical facility usage data will predict demand patterns and prioritize resource allocation. HPC resources are critical for running thousands of parallel simulations to identify robust management strategies under uncertainty, as well as for processing high-resolution sensor data from IoT-enabled equipment and wearables. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of real-time adaptive scheduling, risk mitigation protocols for crowd management, and energy-efficient facility maintenance plans. This work bridges computational modeling and sport management theory, offering novel methodologies for an industry increasingly reliant on data-driven operations. The results will provide actionable insights for reducing operational costs, enhancing safety compliance, and improving user experience in athletic facilities—a growing concern as urban venues face pressure to serve broader community needs while maintaining profitability. By advancing computational applications in this specialized niche, the project aims to establish a benchmark for interdisciplinary research in sport administration.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business, coaching and physical education principles to the organization, administration and management of athletic programs and teams, fitness/rehabilitation facilities and health clubs, sport recreation services, and related services. Includes instruction in program planning and development; business and financial management principles; sales, marketing and recruitment; event promotion, scheduling and management; facilities management; public relations; legal aspects of sports; and applicable health and safety standards.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between social connectivity patterns and cognitive resilience in aging populations through an interdisciplinary lens integrating gerontology, computational social science, and network neuroscience. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how dynamic social behaviors—shaped by life course transitions, technological adoption, and sensory decline—modulate neurodegenerative risk profiles in older adults. While prior work has focused on static social metrics (e.g., marital status), we propose a novel computational framework to model time-varying, multilevel social interactions (in-person, digital, and community-based) and their bidirectional relationships with domain-specific cognitive trajectories. High-performance computing resources are essential to process multimodal longitudinal datasets—including geolocated activity traces, dyadic communication logs, and neuropsychological assessments from 5,000 participants in the AgingConnect Cohort—while accounting for individual differences in mobility, socioeconomic context, and sensory health. Agent-based models will simulate how age-related changes in social prioritization and communication capacity propagate through personal networks, with neural network architectures identifying nonlinear associations between interaction patterns and MRI-derived brain integrity markers. The computational pipeline requires parallelized processing of petabyte-scale temporal graph data and Monte Carlo simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated predictive model of social-cognitive interdependencies across the aging spectrum, (2) generative algorithms to optimize community-level support systems for neuroprotective social engagement, and (3) open-source tools for analyzing lifespan social dynamics at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. By bridging micro-scale behavioral data with macro-scale population aging trends, this work will establish computational gerontology as a distinct interdisciplinary domain, advancing both methodological innovation and translational strategies for dementia risk mitigation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in the preservation, analysis, and accessibility of large-scale digital cultural heritage collections within library science. As libraries increasingly digitize rare and fragile materials, managing heterogeneous datasets—spanning text, images, audiovisual media, and metadata—has become computationally intensive. Existing tools for cataloging and retrieval often struggle with scalability, especially when handling non-standard formats or integrating machine learning (ML) models for automated metadata generation. The research focuses on optimizing workflows for ingesting and processing digitized collections using parallelized pipelines to accelerate tasks such as optical character recognition (OCR) correction, semantic clustering of unstructured text, and feature extraction from visual materials. A key innovation involves training domain-specific ML models on curated library corpora to improve accuracy in identifying historical linguistic patterns, visual motifs, and contextual relationships within archival materials. Computational experiments will benchmark performance across distributed CPU-GPU architectures to determine optimal resource allocation for latency-sensitive tasks like real-time search augmentation. Outcomes will include open-source software modules tailored for library infrastructure, alongside a framework for ethical AI integration in cultural heritage contexts. By advancing computational methods for non-standardized, multilingual, and multimedia collections, this work aims to enhance the capacity of libraries to steward digital assets while improving discoverability for researchers and the public. The project bridges gaps between traditional library practices and emerging computational techniques, offering scalable solutions with implications for digital humanities, archival science, and open-access initiatives.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Urban landscapes present dynamic, heterogeneous ecosystems where wildlife must navigate complex sensory environments shaped by anthropogenic activity. However, the physiological and behavioral mechanisms enabling vertebrate species to adapt to urban acoustic and thermal stressors remain poorly understood, particularly for understudied taxa such as urban-adapted reptiles and amphibians. This project seeks to model the real-time interplay between environmental stressors, species-specific sensory biology, and adaptive decision-making in human-dominated habitats using high-performance computing (HPC). We will integrate biophysical data from field sensors (acoustic arrays, thermal imagers) with species-specific physiological thresholds and movement data from GPS/accelerometer-tagged animals to construct agent-based models (ABMs) simulating individual and population-level responses to urban microenvironments. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized processing for 1) high-resolution spatiotemporal analysis of urban heat island dynamics and noise pollution gradients, 2) Bayesian inference of stressor impact thresholds across species, and 3) ensemble forecasting of habitat selection under future urban development scenarios. Machine learning architectures will be employed to classify behavioral modes from high-frequency movement data and predict evasion strategies across sensory modalities. The HPC environment is critical for handling the project's multi-terabyte datasets, running computationally intensive parameter sweeps for ABM validation, and executing 3D acoustic propagation models in complex urban topography. Outcomes will establish a novel framework for quantifying sensory-driven habitat suitability in anthropogenic landscapes while providing municipal planners with predictive tools to mitigate human-wildlife conflict through noise/thermal buffer design. This work bridges comparative sensory physiology, urban climatology, and computational ethology—advancing wildlife management in emerging Anthropocene ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological principles to the study of vertebrate wildlife, wildlife habitats, and related ecosystems in remote and urban areas. Includes instruction in animal ecology; adaptational biology; urban ecosystems; natural and artificial habitat management; limnology; wildlife pathology; and vertebrate zoological specializations such as mammalogy, herpetology, ichthyology, ornithology, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy-efficient building designs and construction workflows through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations. The construction industry faces increasing pressure to reduce energy consumption and carbon footprints while maintaining cost-effectiveness and structural integrity. However, traditional methods for evaluating building performance—such as manual load calculations, static energy models, and physical prototyping—are time-intensive, lack granularity, and struggle to account for dynamic interactions between structural systems, HVAC efficiency, and regional climate variability. To address these limitations, this research will employ HPC resources to run multi-physics simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress testing, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airflow and thermal modeling, and machine learning algorithms to predict material performance under varying environmental conditions. Large datasets from existing building projects, including sensor-derived thermal profiles, material properties, and regional weather patterns, will inform these models. The simulations will assess novel construction materials, hybrid HVAC configurations, and modular building designs to identify optimal solutions that balance energy efficiency, durability, and cost. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin framework for real-time performance prediction of residential and commercial structures, validated against physical prototypes. This work will directly advance the Building Construction Technology field by enabling data-driven decision-making in design phases, reducing iterative testing costs, and providing actionable insights for sustainable code-compliant construction. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational load of parallelized simulations, which require terabytes of memory and thousands of core-hours to process high-resolution 3D models and stochastic climate datasets. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools tailored for construction technicians, fostering industry adoption of simulation-driven practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to residential and commercial building construction and remodeling. Includes instruction in construction equipment and safety; site preparation and layout; construction estimating; blueprint reading; building codes; framing; masonry; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning; electrical and mechanical systems; interior and exterior finishing; and plumbing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in digital rhetoric and multimodal composition by analyzing large-scale datasets of student-generated digital texts. While contemporary composition studies increasingly emphasizes the role of visual, auditory, and interactive media in communication, existing scholarship lacks robust computational methods to systematically examine how rhetorical strategies operate across these multimodal formats. This gap limits the field’s capacity to theorize emergent literacies and design equitable pedagogical interventions. To address this, our interdisciplinary team will apply natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, and network analysis algorithms to a corpus of 50,000+ student-produced digital artifacts (e.g., blogs, infographics, video essays) drawn from 15 institutional writing programs. HPC resources will enable the processing of heterogeneous file types (text, images, video metadata) and the training of machine learning models to identify patterns in rhetorical appeals, genre adaptation, and cross-modal coherence. Key computational tasks include sentiment analysis of textual-visual juxtapositions, object recognition for visual argumentation frameworks, and graph-based modeling of hyperlinked discourse communities. By scaling qualitative close-reading practices to big-data contexts, this project aims to produce: (1) a publicly accessible annotated dataset for cross-institutional research on digital writing; (2) a suite of open-source tools for analyzing multimodal rhetorical choices; and (3) evidence-based frameworks to support writing instructors in addressing algorithmic bias and accessibility barriers in digitally mediated composition. The computational demands of parallelized media processing and deep learning model training necessitate HPC infrastructure, as local workstations lack the storage capacity and GPU parallelism required for timely analysis. Outcomes will directly inform revisions to national standards for writing program administration and advance humanistic inquiry into how computational methods can ethically enhance the study of rhetoric in the digital age.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the humanistic and scientific study of rhetoric, composition, literacy, and language/linguistic theories and their practical and pedagogical applications. Includes instruction in historical and contemporary rhetoric/composition theories; composition and criticism of written, visual, and mixed-media texts; analysis of literacy practices in cultural and cross-cultural contexts; and writing program administration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and application of multiscale quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods for modeling complex chemical reactions in biological and condensed-phase systems. A critical challenge in theoretical chemistry lies in accurately simulating reactive pathways in large, heterogeneous environments—such as enzyme active sites or solvated interfaces—where traditional quantum chemical methods are computationally prohibitive, and classical force fields lack the precision to capture bond-breaking/forming processes. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating highly parallelized ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with machine learning-accelerated free-energy sampling. The QM region will employ density functional theory (DFT) with advanced exchange-correlation functionals to model electronic rearrangements during catalysis, while the MM environment will utilize polarizable force fields parameterized via neural network potentials trained on high-level coupled-cluster data. Key targets include elucidating proton-coupled electron transfer mechanisms in metalloenzymes and predicting solvent reorganization effects on reaction barriers in aqueous organic systems. These simulations demand significant HPC resources due to the need for extensive configurational sampling, large-scale parallelization of electronic structure calculations, and iterative training of machine learning models on terabytes of trajectory data. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for balancing accuracy and efficiency in multiscale simulations, atomistic insights into experimentally observed kinetic isotope effects in biocatalysis, and open-source software tools for automating QM/MM workflow management on distributed-memory architectures. The results will directly inform experimental efforts in enzyme engineering and sustainable catalyst design, bridging gaps between theoretical predictions and empirical observations in reactive chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of mathematical and computational methods and fundamental laws of physics to describe chemical phenomena and to develop empirical models of molecules and their interactions. Includes instruction in properties of small, isolated molecules; dynamics of elementary chemical processes; reaction pathways of organic molecules; hydrogen bonding patterns in liquids; reaction rates of biological pathways; and advanced computational techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a multidisciplinary study of cultural and historical dynamics through the analysis of large-scale textual and visual datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in digital humanities scholarship: the limited capacity to process and interpret complex, unstructured historical materials—such as manuscripts, ephemera, and artistic works—at a scale that reveals long-term sociocultural patterns. Current methodologies struggle to efficiently integrate multimodal data (text, images, geospatial metadata) while maintaining sensitivity to contextual nuance, a challenge exacerbated by the computational demands of machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) models. This project proposes a computational pipeline combining transformer-based NLP, computer vision techniques, and geospatial mapping to analyze digitized collections spanning five centuries of global cultural exchange. HPC resources will enable the training of custom deep learning models for semantic analysis, image classification, and entity recognition across multilingual corpora and heterogeneous visual archives. Concurrently, graph-based network analysis will model the dissemination of cultural motifs and ideological shifts, while containerized workflows will ensure reproducibility and interoperability with existing digital humanities platforms. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of previously obscured transnational influences in artistic and literary movements, as well as publicly accessible interactive visualizations that contextualize findings for scholarly and public audiences. The project will also release open-source tools for preprocessing historical data, addressing domain-specific challenges such as OCR error correction and markup language integration. By scaling analytical possibilities for humanities research, this work aims to demonstrate how advanced computing can deepen our understanding of cultural evolution while fostering collaborative frameworks for interdisciplinary, data-driven inquiry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of new technologies, advanced computing, and public engagement to investigate and analyze questions in the humanities. Includes instruction in anthropology, art, data mining and machine learning, design, digital archives, geospatial technologies, history, human-computer interface design, literature, markup languages, social media technologies, and software development.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in algebraic topology and geometric combinatorics by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address computational challenges in homotopy theory and transformation group actions. The central research problem involves characterizing higher-dimensional homotopy invariants of non-simply connected spaces and analyzing the dynamics of group actions on continua—problems that are theoretically intricate and computationally intractable with conventional methods. Key obstacles include the exponential growth of combinatorial configurations in cell complex decompositions, the memory-intensive nature of persistent homology calculations over large simplicial complexes, and the need for parallelized algorithms to explore transformation orbits in high-dimensional representation spaces. The proposed computational approach combines novel algorithmic frameworks for distributed computation of spectral sequences, optimized parallel processing of chain complex data structures, and GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods to sample group action dynamics. These methods will be implemented via a hybrid MPI-CUDA architecture to efficiently distribute computational tasks across nodes, minimize inter-process communication overhead, and optimize memory utilization during large-scale homology computations. Expected outcomes include the first systematic classification of homotopy types for certain families of 6-dimensional CW-complexes, quantitative bounds on stabilizer dimensions in profinite group actions, and open-source software tools for computational topology. The results will directly contribute to open conjectures in shape theory and transformation group topology while establishing new benchmarks for applying HPC to pure mathematical research. By addressing these computationally prohibitive problems, the project aims to bridge theoretical advances in foundational topology with cutting-edge computational techniques, creating infrastructure that will benefit multiple subfields within pure mathematics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of unaltered geometric configurations under conditions of continuous, multi-directional transformations. Includes instruction in mathematical logic, proof theory, model theory, set theory, combinatorics, continua, homotopy, homology, links, and transformation actions.

abstract: The dynamic behavior of macromolecular complexes underpins critical biological processes such as energy transduction and signal propagation, yet the structural mechanisms governing these phenomena remain poorly resolved. This project seeks to elucidate the conformational pathways and energy landscapes of membrane-embedded ATP synthase complexes during proton-driven rotational catalysis, a process central to cellular energy homeostasis. Current limitations in experimental resolution and computational sampling hinder atomic-level understanding of how proton motive force is transduced into mechanical rotation and ATP synthesis. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational strategy integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations, and Markov state modeling. All-atom MD simulations will model the 20-subunit ATP synthase complex in explicit lipid bilayers and solvent, capturing microsecond-scale dynamics of rotary substeps and intermediate states. Enhanced sampling techniques, including adaptive biasing force calculations, will map free energy barriers associated with proton translocation and γ-subunit rotation. These simulations will be coupled with experimental cryo-EM density maps through iterative flexible fitting to resolve transient conformations. The computational workload demands high-performance computing resources due to system size (>1.5 million atoms), simulation duration required to observe full rotational cycles, and ensemble-based analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of metastable states governing torque generation, (2) quantification of protonation-coupled strain propagation through the c-ring rotor, and (3) predictive models of how pathogenic mutations disrupt energy transduction. This work will establish a framework for analyzing mechanochemical coupling in rotary molecular machines, with implications for designing bioinspired energy conversion systems and therapies targeting mitochondrial dysfunction. Successful execution requires dedicated GPU-node allocations for trajectory generation and CPU resources for ensemble analysis, as conventional cluster access cannot support the sustained throughput needed for statistically robust sampling.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the dynamics and interactions of macromolecules and other three-dimensional ultrastructures, the architecture of supramolecular structures, and energy transfer in biomolecular systems. Includes instruction in energy transduction, structural dynamics, mechanisms of electron and proton transfer in biological systems, bioinformatics, automated analysis, and specialized research techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives in Russian-language media and literary texts from the late Soviet period (1970s–1991) through the first post-Soviet decade (1992–2000). The research problem centers on identifying patterns of continuity and rupture in cultural discourse during this transformative era, with a focus on themes such as national identity, collective memory, and ideological adaptation. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to systematically track subtle linguistic shifts across vast textual corpora, necessitating computational approaches to uncover latent structures in language use. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic analysis and dynamic topic modeling, to a curated multilingual corpus of over 500,000 pages from state-aligned newspapers, samizdat publications, and post-Soviet digital archives. Computational workflows will be designed to detect semantic clustering, lexical innovation, and intertextual references while accounting for orthographic variations and Soviet-era linguistic conventions. By integrating HPC-enabled neural embeddings with historical contextualization, the analysis aims to reveal how cultural producers negotiated state ideology, global influences, and emergent post-Soviet identities. Expected outcomes include a reusable computational framework for diachronic cultural analysis in Slavic studies, quantitative maps of discursive transformations across institutional and grassroots texts, and evidence-based insights into the relationship between linguistic change and sociopolitical upheaval. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parallel text processing, and storage for intermediate linguistic datasets. This work will advance digital humanities methodologies in area studies while contributing new perspectives on cultural resilience during Russia’s late-20th-century transitions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Russian Federation and its Soviet, Czarist, and medieval predecessors and related borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and semantic evolution of ethical frameworks within understudied religious and philosophical textual traditions. The research addresses a critical gap in comparative philosophy: the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to systematically trace how ethical concepts (e.g., justice, virtue, moral agency) are articulated, contested, and transformed across diverse cultural contexts. By integrating computational linguistics with hermeneutic analysis, the project will process multilingual corpora spanning classical South Asian śāstric literature, premodern Islamic philosophical treatises, and Indigenous oral narratives (transcribed into text). Key computational methods include transformer-based language models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, graph-based semantic network analysis to map conceptual relationships, and unsupervised clustering algorithms to identify latent thematic shifts across historical periods. These techniques require HPC capabilities due to the scale of textual data (estimated 50,000+ pages), the complexity of training domain-specific models, and the need for parallel processing to iteratively refine hermeneutic interpretations against computational outputs. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated ethical concept trajectories, (2) methodological frameworks for bridging computational analysis with qualitative philosophical inquiry, and (3) new insights into cross-cultural convergences in ethical reasoning. The project advances the digital humanities by demonstrating how HPC can expand the scope of philosophical research, enabling systematic engagement with marginalized traditions while preserving context-sensitive interpretation. Results will inform interdisciplinary scholarship on ethical pluralism and support pedagogical tools for global philosophy curricula.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in philosophy and religion, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Bulgarian linguistics and literary analysis. The research problem centers on two interconnected challenges: (1) the computational modeling of morphosyntactic variation in historical and modern Bulgarian texts, and (2) the quantitative analysis of stylistic patterns across Bulgarian literary movements from the National Revival to contemporary works. Current methods for analyzing these phenomena rely on manual annotation or limited-scale computational tools, which cannot adequately process the growing corpus of digitized Bulgarian texts, including rare manuscripts, periodicals, and modern publications. To address this, we propose developing a hybrid natural language processing (NLP) pipeline combining transformer-based models for morphological disambiguation, graph-based algorithms for syntactic pattern extraction, and unsupervised machine learning methods for stylistic clustering. The computational workflow will process a curated corpus exceeding 10 million tokens, spanning 19th-century archival materials to 21st-century novels. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific language models on Bulgarian’s rich inflectional morphology, parallelizing large-scale syntactic dependency parsing, and enabling iterative hyperparameter optimization for clustering algorithms. Expected outcomes include the first open-source toolkit for diachronic Bulgarian text analysis, a annotated multilingual corpus (Bulgarian-English-Russian) of comparative literary excerpts, and quantitative evidence mapping linguistic changes to sociocultural shifts. This work will provide novel methodologies for Slavic computational philology, enable previously impractical comparative studies of Balkan literary traditions, and create infrastructure for digital humanities research in under-resourced languages. Results will directly support graduate research in Bulgarian linguistics and inform curriculum development for computational literary studies within the program.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bulgarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Jewish philosophical thought and hermeneutic traditions across multilingual textual corpora. The central research problem concerns the dynamic interplay between scriptural exegesis, ethical frameworks, and metaphysical concepts in classical Jewish texts, particularly how these elements were reinterpreted during critical historical transitions. Current scholarship faces challenges in systematically tracing conceptual shifts across vast, linguistically diverse primary sources—including Talmudic literature, medieval philosophical treatises (e.g., Maimonides' works), and early modern Kabbalistic writings—due to the scale of data and complexity of cross-referential networks. The proposed computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) optimized for Hebrew, Aramaic, and Judeo-Arabic texts with network analysis algorithms to map conceptual relationships and transmission pathways. Key technical challenges include developing custom OCR models for digitized manuscripts with unique scribal features, implementing semantic similarity metrics for cross-linguistic philosophical terminology, and training transformer-based models on curated corpora to detect implicit argumentation structures. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of over 50,000 digitized pages from the National Library of Israel’s archives, computational text alignment across multiple manuscript versions, and 3D visualization of conceptual networks spanning ten centuries. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously unrecognized doctrinal influences between rationalist and mystical traditions, 2) quantitative models of interpretive innovation in response to historical crises, and 3) an open-access database linking philosophical concepts to their textual instantiations. This research will provide novel methodological frameworks for studying religious epistemology while advancing computational tools for low-resource historical languages. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive NLP pipelines and sustaining complex graph analyses across multi-terabyte datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, culture, and religion of the Jewish people. Includes instruction in Jewish religious heritage, sacred texts, and law; Jewish philosophy and intellectual history; Jewish life and culture, both in Israel and the Jewish Diaspora; historical Jewish minority cultures such as the Yiddish, Sephardic, and other; anti-Semitism, gentile relations and Shoa; Zionism; and modern developments within Judaism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize school-based behavioral interventions by analyzing multi-faceted student data, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address scalability challenges inherent in traditional approaches. School psychologists must evaluate complex interactions between developmental, cognitive, and environmental factors when designing interventions, yet existing tools often struggle to integrate longitudinal behavioral data, real-time classroom observations, and socioecological variables (e.g., family dynamics, school climate). Our research will employ machine learning techniques, including ensemble methods and neural networks, to model how these variables collectively influence intervention efficacy across diverse student populations. HPC resources will enable iterative training of models on large-scale datasets from partner school districts, incorporating time-series analyses of behavioral trajectories and natural language processing of qualitative case notes. A key innovation involves agent-based simulations to test hypothetical intervention scenarios, simulating how individualized strategies might propagate effects within classroom social networks. Outcomes will include (1) a framework for identifying students at risk of poor response to standard interventions, (2) decision-support tools for tailoring strategies based on developmental and contextual profiles, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for allocating school psychological resources. By addressing computational bottlenecks in analyzing high-dimensional educational data, this work aims to advance precision support strategies in school psychology while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for data privacy and algorithmic fairness. The requested computing infrastructure is critical for handling the project’s data volume (~50 TB of structured/unstructured records) and enabling real-time model validation—a necessity for translating research into practical tools usable by practitioners without computational expertise.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: The development of sustainable chemical manufacturing processes requires precise control over reaction kinetics and transport phenomena in complex multiphase systems. However, current computational models often fail to capture the coupled effects of microscale interfacial dynamics and macroscale reactor hydrodynamics, particularly for reactions involving non-Newtonian fluids or catalytic surfaces with heterogeneous active sites. This project seeks to address this gap by implementing a multiscale simulation framework to optimize catalytic membrane reactor designs for selective hydrogenation processes. The computational approach integrates quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT) calculations of surface reaction pathways with continuum-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, bridged by mesoscopic lattice Boltzmann methods to resolve interfacial phenomena. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to manage the iterative coupling between time- and length-scales, particularly for parallelized simulations of turbulent flow through porous catalytic substrates with spatially varying activity. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for local mass transfer coefficients under non-ideal flow conditions and identification of optimal catalyst distributions that maximize selectivity while minimizing hot-spot formation. The proposed simulations will directly inform experimental reactor prototyping efforts for bio-derived feedstock conversion, with potential energy savings of 15-20% compared to conventional fixed-bed systems. By establishing an open-source computational workflow for multiscale reactor analysis, this work will provide a template for accelerating the design of intensified chemical processes across academia and industry. The requested HPC allocation will enable 3D transient simulations across >10^6 computational cells with chemical species tracking, requiring sustained petascale capabilities for ensemble calculations of catalytic surface heterogeneity effects.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing catalytic reaction systems for sustainable chemical manufacturing by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial catalytic processes, particularly those involving complex multi-phase reactors or non-ideal fluid dynamics, often suffer from inefficiencies due to incomplete understanding of coupled transport phenomena, reaction kinetics, and surface interactions at scale. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in resolving spatiotemporal heterogeneities, while existing computational models struggle to integrate atomistic catalyst behavior with reactor-scale fluid dynamics. This project aims to develop a multi-scale computational framework combining quantum mechanical calculations of active sites, molecular dynamics simulations of interfacial processes, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of reactor hydrodynamics. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of density functional theory (DFT) calculations to screen catalyst candidates, coupled with GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods for turbulent reactive flow simulations. Key objectives include identifying optimal operating conditions for CO₂ hydrogenation reactors, elucidating pore-scale mass transfer limitations in hierarchical zeolite catalysts, and predicting long-term catalyst deactivation patterns. Expected outcomes include validated open-source simulation tools for hybrid continuum-microkinetic modeling and actionable insights into designing energy-efficient catalytic systems. The computational demands—including O(10⁵) core-hours for ensemble uncertainty quantification and petascale data management for 4D reactor simulations—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation. Successful implementation will advance fundamental knowledge of reactive transport in complex media while directly supporting decarbonization efforts in chemical production. This work aligns with national priorities in sustainable manufacturing and provides a template for integrating machine learning with multi-physics simulations in chemical engineering research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of cultural journalism and computational text/media analysis. Cultural journalism faces a critical challenge in systematically analyzing the vast, heterogeneous datasets generated by contemporary arts and entertainment ecosystems—including digital archives of criticism, social media discourse, streaming platform metrics, and multimedia artistic works. Traditional qualitative methods, while foundational to the discipline, struggle to scale with the volume and complexity of this data, limiting opportunities to identify cultural patterns, trace thematic evolution across media, or contextualize emerging art forms. This project proposes developing computational workflows to analyze multimodal cultural data through natural language processing (NLP), image recognition, and network analysis techniques. Key objectives include training custom transformer models to detect stylistic trends in arts criticism across decades of journalism archives, applying computer vision to map visual themes in photojournalism and digital art exhibits, and constructing temporal knowledge graphs to visualize relationships between cultural producers, critics, and audiences. The computational demands are significant: processing high-resolution image/video datasets, fine-tuning large language models on domain-specific corpora (e.g., theater reviews, music journalism), and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about cultural influence networks. By integrating these computational methods with humanistic critique, the research aims to 1) reveal understudied patterns in how artistic movements gain journalistic attention, 2) develop open-source tools for augmented cultural analysis, and 3) establish best practices for ethically applying machine learning to arts criticism. Outcomes will directly enhance pedagogical resources for training journalists in data-driven cultural storytelling while providing new frameworks to interrogate power dynamics in arts coverage. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to process terabytes of multimedia data within viable timeframes, enabling novel scholarship that bridges computational rigor with the interpretive traditions of cultural journalism.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to be journalists who critically examine current culture as expressed through the visual and performing arts, design, film, music, radio, television, dance, theater, and written text. Includes instruction in arts criticism, art and entertainment reporting, cultural critique, investigative reporting, newspaper reporting, photojournalism, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the transmission of Tibetan religious and cultural narratives across digital archives, with a focus on understudied texts produced in diaspora communities. While Tibetan Studies has increasingly engaged digital humanities methods, the scale and complexity of multilingual textual corpora—spanning classical Tibetan, modern vernaculars, and exile community publications—present computational challenges that exceed the capacity of standard workstations. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in doctrinal adaptation, lexical shifts, and cross-regional knowledge exchange within these texts, which are critical to understanding how Tibetan cultural identity is reconstituted in transnational contexts. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will apply transformer-based language models fine-tuned for classical Tibetan and Himalayan languages to perform semantic similarity analyses, temporal topic modeling, and network mapping of textual references across 15,000 digitized manuscripts, pamphlets, and periodicals. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing on GPU clusters to handle non-Latin script tokenization, low-resource language alignment, and sparse-data training scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for cross-temporal and cross-community textual analysis in Tibetan Studies, (2) quantitative evidence of narrative preservation versus innovation in post-1959 exile literature, and (3) open-access visualization tools mapping doctrinal linkages between pre-modern and contemporary sources. By enabling large-scale interrogation of cultural production mechanisms, this work will provide new empirical foundations for theorizing resilience in diasporic knowledge systems while directly supporting the preservation priorities of Tibetan archival institutions. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets and train domain-specific models that account for Tibetan Buddhism’s unique lexico-conceptual structures, which mainstream NLP tools frequently misrepresent.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Tibet and its borderlands, with emphasis on both pre-modern and modern Tibet and associated religious and exile movements.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize prosthetic and cosmetic material integration for clinical and security applications, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in realism, durability, and environmental adaptability. Traditional prosthetic design relies heavily on manual trial-and-error processes, which limit scalability and precision in addressing diverse anatomical and environmental variables. This research focuses on creating predictive models to simulate the interaction between synthetic materials (e.g., silicone, adhesives, pigments) and biological tissues under dynamic conditions, such as temperature fluctuations, moisture exposure, and prolonged wear. By employing finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML), the project will model biomechanical stress distribution, adhesive failure thresholds, and pigment degradation rates across heterogeneous skin types and environmental scenarios. High-resolution 3D scans of anatomical structures will inform simulations, while ML algorithms trained on material science datasets will predict optimal material combinations and application protocols. The computational workflow will integrate multi-physics simulations (thermal, mechanical, chemical) to evaluate real-world performance, reducing reliance on physical prototyping. Expected outcomes include a validated library of material-behavior profiles, adaptive application guidelines for practitioners, and open-source tools for simulating prosthetic-cosmetic outcomes in virtual environments. This work bridges gaps between cosmetic artistry, materials engineering, and computational modeling, offering novel solutions for medical prosthetics (e.g., post-surgical reconstruction) and security-focused disguise systems. The HPC resources are critical to handling the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelized simulations, and large-scale data processing required for robust, generalizable models. Results will advance evidence-based practices in prosthetic cosmetology, enhancing accessibility and efficacy for diverse populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to professionally apply cosmetic makeup preparations and perform complete and specialized appearance makeovers including hairdressing, wig work, masking, temporary prosthesis applications, cosmetic applications, and related costuming for leisure or for professional stage, camera, clinical, or security purposes.  Includes instruction in period and contemporary hairstyling and costuming; wig work and hairpiece application; synthetic hair and masks; cosmetic preparations and treatments; makeup artistry; attachment, removal, and camouflaging of prostheses; health and safety; client consultation and care; pre- and post-production operations; set and crew conduct and relations; script, instruction, and prescription interpretation; labor relations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows for optimizing high-resolution digital imaging and prepress design processes, addressing the growing demand for scalable, cross-platform publishing solutions in communication and journalism. Current workflows struggle with processing ultra-high-definition (UHD) graphics, dynamic typographic layouts, and color management across print/digital media, leading to inefficiencies in rendering times, accuracy, and adaptability. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize computationally intensive tasks, including raster image processing (RIP), color space transformations, and AI-driven layout optimization. Using GPU-accelerated rendering frameworks and distributed computing architectures, the project will simulate large-scale design environments to test automated prepress workflows, multi-device compatibility checks, and real-time collaborative editing scenarios. A key focus is training machine learning models on diverse datasets of print and digital publications to predict design errors, optimize asset compression, and adapt layouts for variable output formats (e.g., responsive web, augmented reality). Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for reducing prepress production time by 30–50% while maintaining fidelity across media, along with benchmarks for UHD image processing scalability. Results will directly benefit journalism and design education by providing open-access computational models that demonstrate HPC’s role in modern publishing pipelines. The resource request prioritizes GPU nodes for neural network training and high-memory nodes for batch processing complex vector/raster composites, enabling replication of industry-scale design environments. This work bridges a critical gap in non-STEM computational research by demonstrating how HPC can advance creative disciplines reliant on precision, iteration speed, and multi-channel publishing demands.
cip_title: Prepress/ Desktop Publishing and Digital Imaging Design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the layout, design and typographic arrangement of printed and/or electronic graphic and textual products. Includes instruction in printing and lithographic equipment and operations, computer hardware and software, digital imaging, print preparation, page layout and design, desktop publishing, and applicable principles of graphic design and web page design.

abstract: The development of advanced semiconductor nanowires for optoelectronic applications is hindered by incomplete understanding of how atomic-scale defects influence electronic and optical properties. Experimental characterization struggles to resolve dynamic defect interactions under operational conditions, necessitating high-fidelity computational models. This project seeks to employ multiscale simulations integrating density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), and machine learning (ML) to systematically investigate defect formation, migration, and collective effects in III-V semiconductor nanowires. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale DFT calculations to map defect-induced electronic structure modifications, accelerated MD simulations to track defect evolution at picosecond resolutions across nanometer-length scales, and ML-driven surrogate models to predict optimal defect configurations for enhanced charge carrier mobility. The computational workflow will be validated against synchrotron X-ray diffraction and photoluminescence data from collaborative experimental efforts. Expected outcomes include atomistic insights into defect engineering strategies, predictive guidelines for synthesizing nanowires with tailored bandgap properties, and open-source simulation tools for the materials chemistry community. By bridging nanoscale defect dynamics to macroscopic device performance, this research aims to accelerate the design of next-generation photonic sensors and energy-efficient optoelectronic components. The requested HPC allocation is critical to overcome current limitations in system size and simulation timescales, ensuring statistically robust sampling of defect ensembles and temperature-dependent phenomena.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis and study of organic or inorganic materials and their electronic, magnetic, optical or mechanical properties. Includes instruction in advanced materials for photonics, lasers, chemical sensors and arrays or nanochemistry; semiconductor nanowires; and molecular electronics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale digitized archives of 20th-century Latin American cultural production, focusing on understudied regional artistic movements and their transnational networks. While historical and cultural studies of Latin America have traditionally relied on qualitative methods, the scale and fragmentation of primary sources—including periodicals, visual art catalogs, and ephemera from Mexico, the Andes, and the Southern Cone—pose challenges for identifying patterns of cultural exchange, ideological diffusion, and identity formation beyond localized case studies. The research will apply natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to a corpus of over 500,000 multilingual texts and 100,000 images, spanning 1900–1990, to trace the evolution of decolonial aesthetics and intellectual collaborations across borders. Computational methods will include transformer-based language models fine-tuned for historical Spanish and Portuguese variants, network analysis of artist collectives using graph-based algorithms, and spatial-temporal mapping of thematic shifts in visual media. By integrating HPC-enabled optical character recognition (OCR) correction for degraded print materials and clustering techniques for visual motif detection, the project aims to reconstruct obscured connections between Indigenous cultural revitalization initiatives, avant-garde movements, and state-sponsored art programs. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access annotated dataset of cross-regional cultural interactions, interactive visualizations of ideological networks, and quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric narratives of Latin American modernism. This computationally intensive approach will enable novel synthesis of dispersed materials at a scale impractical for manual analysis, offering methodological innovations for digital humanities in underrepresented linguistic and cultural contexts while advancing interdisciplinary debates about technology’s role in decolonial scholarship.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic peoples of the North and South American Continents outside Canada and the United States, including the study of the Pre-Columbian period and the flow of immigrants from other societies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of disease registry data—spanning multimodal sources such as genomic profiles, longitudinal clinical records, and high-resolution imaging—presents critical challenges in data integration, analysis, and scalability. Current registry frameworks often struggle to harmonize unstructured or semi-structured datasets, limiting their utility for precision medicine and real-time epidemiological insights. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven computational pipeline to automate the curation, linkage, and predictive modeling of heterogeneous disease registry data at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement distributed data processing architectures to manage terabyte-scale datasets from national registries, including rare disease cohorts with sparse multimodal entries. The pipeline will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for clinical text abstraction, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map patient trajectory relationships, and federated learning frameworks to enable privacy-preserving cross-registry analyses. Key computational challenges include optimizing memory-intensive operations for whole-slide imaging metadata, parallelizing feature extraction across GPU nodes, and validating model generalizability in low-data regimes through synthetic data augmentation. Anticipated outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for registry data harmonization, validated predictive models for disease progression subtypes, and benchmarks for computational efficiency in federated registry environments. This work will directly enhance the capacity of disease registries to support advanced analytics for personalized treatment pathways while addressing ethical and technical barriers to large-scale data sharing. By bridging gaps between clinical data management and computational scalability, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for next-generation registry infrastructures in underserved health domains such as autoimmune disorders and post-infectious syndromes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to find, interpret, and record demographic and medical information on individuals for healthcare agencies and disease registries. Includes instruction in anatomy, data management, disease registry organization and operations, epidemiology, ethics, fundamentals of disease coding and staging, medical terminology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, physiology, quality management, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the ethical implications of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven clinical decision-making systems through advanced computational modeling of bias propagation in heterogeneous patient populations. As AI adoption accelerates in diagnostic and treatment planning contexts, concerns persist about algorithmic fairness, transparency, and the amplification of health disparities—particularly for marginalized groups underrepresented in training datasets. Current ethical frameworks lack empirical grounding in how bias manifests across real-world clinical scenarios, limiting the development of actionable mitigation strategies. To address this gap, we propose a computational bioethics approach combining ethical theory with large-scale simulation of AI-mediated decisions. High-performance computing resources will enable the creation of synthetic patient cohorts reflecting demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical diversity, coupled with reinforcement learning models trained on multimodal health data (e.g., EHRs, imaging, genomic data). The simulations will quantify how different bias mitigation interventions—including algorithmic re-weighting, fairness constraints, and human-in-the-loop verification—affect equity metrics across subgroups while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Multi-objective optimization techniques will identify trade-offs between competing ethical priorities (e.g., autonomy vs. beneficence) in constrained resource environments. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for evaluating "ethical robustness" in clinical AI systems and evidence-based recommendations for bias auditing protocols. By bridging computational modeling with normative analysis, this work aims to establish quantitative benchmarks for equitable AI deployment while advancing methodological integration between health informatics and medical ethics. The requested resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of simulated care pathways and enabling real-time ethical impact assessments across millions of virtual patient encounters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of energy systems infrastructure, including aging power grids, renewable energy arrays, and distributed generation networks, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize maintenance and repair strategies. This project seeks to develop a predictive maintenance framework for hybrid energy systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-physics interactions, simulate failure scenarios, and identify optimal intervention protocols. Current approaches often rely on generalized maintenance schedules or reactive repairs, leading to unnecessary downtime, resource waste, and cascading failures in interconnected systems. To address this gap, we propose a computational workflow integrating three-dimensional finite element analysis (FEA) of mechanical degradation, machine learning-driven anomaly detection in sensor networks, and discrete-event simulations of repair operations. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale operational datasets from wind turbines, photovoltaic systems, and grid substations while simultaneously executing high-fidelity simulations of material stress, thermal cycling, and electrical load imbalances. Key innovations include the development of coupled digital twins for critical infrastructure components and a reinforcement learning algorithm to prioritize maintenance tasks under resource constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model identifying failure precursors with ≥90% accuracy 72 hours before critical thresholds, (2) optimized repair sequencing protocols reducing system downtime by an estimated 15-20%, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive maintenance planning in heterogeneous energy networks. By enabling data-driven decision-making at scale, this research will advance workforce training paradigms for energy technicians while supporting the transition to resilient, low-carbon energy systems. The computational demands of processing multi-modal sensor data, training deep neural networks on historical failure patterns, and running ensemble simulations across parametric variations necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve statistically significant results within operational timeframes.
cip_title: Energy Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
