cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predicting and controlling thermal transport in hybrid nanoscale systems, where quantum confinement effects and heterogeneous material interfaces lead to non-classical behaviors that defy conventional engineering models. While advances in nanotechnology have enabled the fabrication of devices with features below 10 nm, existing continuum-based thermal management frameworks fail to capture the interplay of phonon-boundary scattering, interfacial energy localization, and emergent quantum thermal states in these systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop a multiscale simulation platform integrating first-principles lattice dynamics, semiclassical Boltzmann transport equations, and machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics to model heat dissipation in 2D/3D heterostructures and metamaterials. The computational workflow will resolve atomic-scale vibrational spectra using density functional theory (DFT), propagate phonon distributions across mesoscale geometries via GPU-optimized transport solvers, and predict macroscopic thermal conductivity under operational stresses. Key objectives include identifying design rules for anisotropic nanostructures that suppress hot-spot formation in next-generation nanoelectronics and quantifying the role of defects in modulating interfacial thermal resistance. By validating simulations against in situ TEM thermal mapping data from collaborators, this work will establish an open-source codebase for nanoscale thermal engineering. The outcomes are anticipated to enable energy-efficient nanoelectronic architectures, inform scalable manufacturing protocols for thermally stable nanomaterials, and advance fundamental understanding of non-equilibrium energy transport at quantum-classical boundaries. Access to HPC resources is essential to handle the ∼10^6-atom systems and petascale datasets inherent to cross-domain simulations spanning femtosecond-scale atomic vibrations to millisecond device-level thermal transients.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical, scientific, and engineering principles and technical skills to manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) and to design, fabricate, and integrate nanoscale structures, devices, and systems. Includes instruction in materials science, thermodynamics, nanomaterials, nanoelectronics, and nano/micro device fabrication and testing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize adaptive modular production systems (AMPS) for agile manufacturing in volatile markets. Traditional manufacturing systems struggle with rapid reconfiguration due to fixed layouts, slow response times to demand shifts, and inefficiencies in scaling hybrid production (e.g., mixed material use or multi-product lines). The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in modeling dynamic, large-scale AMPS that integrate real-time sensor data, supply chain variables, and sustainability constraints. Current simulation tools lack the scalability to handle the combinatorial complexity of reconfigurable hardware, variable workflows, and transient resource allocation, limiting industry adoption. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining multi-agent system simulations, evolutionary optimization, and physics-informed graph neural networks (GNNs). High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized evaluation of millions of system configurations under stochastic demand scenarios, coupled with multi-fidelity modeling that links granular equipment-level dynamics (e.g., energy consumption, wear prediction) to plant-wide logistics. The GNN architecture will assimilate IoT data streams from pilot-scale AMPS testbeds to refine digital twin accuracy. Expected outcomes include an open-source optimization engine capable of recommending reconfiguration strategies with <10-minute latency for systems comprising 500+ modular units, validated against real-world metrics such as energy use per product variant and retooling downtime. This work bridges gaps between discrete event simulation, control theory, and lifecycle assessment—advancing applied engineering in adaptive manufacturing. By leveraging HPC to manage hyper-parametric optimization and high-dimensional data integration, the project aims to establish scalable computational workflows for next-generation production systems, directly supporting industrial decarbonization and circular economy goals.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles inherent to engineering to the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and hydrodynamic interactions of aquatic plant-microbe symbioses in turbulent freshwater ecosystems, a specialized niche integrating plant biology, fluid dynamics, and microbial ecology. Aquatic plants, such as submerged macrophytes, dynamically interact with epiphytic microbial communities and fluid forces, yet the computational tools to model these tripartite interactions at biologically relevant scales remain underdeveloped. The research problem centers on resolving how plant morphology, microbial biofilm elasticity, and hydrodynamic stressors collectively influence nutrient exchange and ecosystem resilience. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) for fluid-structure interaction simulations with agent-based modeling (ABM) of microbial metabolic networks. The LBM-ABM hybrid approach will simulate 3D fluid flow around morphologically diverse plant structures (e.g., dissected vs. broad leaves) while tracking microbial community dynamics under varying turbulence regimes. This requires parallelized GPU-accelerated simulations to handle the trillion-cell lattice scales necessary to capture micrometer-scale biofilm deformation and meter-scale hydrodynamic patterns concurrently. Anticipated outcomes include: 1) novel predictive models linking plant architectural traits to microbially mediated nutrient cycling efficiency, 2) identification of turbulence thresholds that destabilize plant-microbe mutualisms, and 3) open-source computational tools for simulating benthic ecosystem processes. Results will advance foundational knowledge of hydrodynamic niche partitioning in aquatic flora while providing actionable insights for wetland restoration strategies facing increased climatic turbulence. The requested HPC resources are critical for overcoming current limitations in spatial scaling and temporal resolution that hinder conventional fluid dynamics or ecological modeling approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plants, related microbial organisms, and plant habitats and ecosystem relations. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and structure, phytochemistry, cytology, plant genetics, plant morphology and physiology, plant ecology, plant taxonomy and systematics, paleobotany, and applications of biophysics and molecular biology.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions aim to optimize patient independence through personalized strategies, yet predicting individual outcomes remains challenging due to the complex interplay of biomechanical, cognitive, and environmental factors. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the efficacy of OT interventions for individuals with upper limb motor impairments, such as those caused by stroke or traumatic brain injury. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including motion capture kinematics, electromyography (EMG) signals, patient-reported outcomes, and environmental context data—to simulate and predict patient-specific responses to therapeutic activities. A multi-scale modeling approach will be employed, combining machine learning (ML) algorithms to identify movement pattern biomarkers, finite element analysis to simulate musculoskeletal stress during task performance, and agent-based modeling to evaluate how environmental modifications influence motor learning. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing of high-dimensional datasets (e.g., terabytes of sensor data from wearable devices) and iterative optimization of intervention parameters. Expected outcomes include predictive models that quantify the relationship between therapeutic task complexity, biomechanical adaptability, and functional recovery trajectories. These models will inform the design of adaptive OT protocols, enabling clinicians to dynamically adjust interventions based on real-time computational feedback. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work addresses a critical gap in OT research: the need for scalable, data-driven tools to personalize rehabilitation in heterogeneous patient populations. The resulting framework will be disseminated as an open-source toolkit, fostering collaboration across rehabilitation science and computational research communities while adhering to ethical standards for patient data security and algorithmic transparency.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist patients limited by physical, cognitive, psychosocial, mental, developmental, and learning disabilities, as well as adverse environmental conditions, to maximize their independence and maintain optimum health through a planned mix of acquired skills, performance motivation, environmental adaptations, assistive technologies, and physical agents. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, psychology, sociology, patient assessment and evaluation, standardized and non-standardized tests and measurements, assistive and rehabilitative technologies, ergonomics, environmental health, special education, vocational counseling, health education and promotion, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing controlled-environment horticulture systems through advanced computational modeling of plant-soil-water dynamics. Current irrigation and nutrient delivery methods in greenhouse and vertical farming operations often rely on generalized protocols, leading to inefficiencies in water use, fertilizer runoff, and suboptimal plant growth. The research problem centers on the lack of high-resolution, crop-specific models that account for real-time root architecture development, soil heterogeneity, and microclimate variability. To overcome this, we propose developing a GPU-accelerated 3D multiphase transport model using finite element methods to simulate water and nutrient movement through growth media at unprecedented spatial (sub-millimeter) and temporal (minute-level) resolutions. The computational approach integrates hyperspectral imaging data from plant phenotyping systems with IoT sensor networks monitoring soil moisture, pH, and electrical conductivity across experimental greenhouse arrays. Machine learning techniques will be employed to parameterize species-specific root uptake patterns for ten high-value crops, requiring iterative training on terabyte-scale datasets. High-performance computing resources are essential for running ensemble simulations that test 50,000+ parameter combinations across different growth media compositions, irrigation schedules, and climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for precision irrigation control systems that reduce water use by 25-40% while maintaining yield targets, and a decision-support tool for substrate optimization in commercial horticulture. The models will also enable rapid prototyping of novel hydroponic configurations through in silico testing prior to physical implementation. By bridging the gap between plant physiology and computational fluid dynamics, this work aims to establish new standards for resource efficiency in controlled-environment agriculture while providing open-access datasets to advance digital twin applications in horticultural science.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general production and processing of domesticated plants, shrubs, flowers, foliage, trees, groundcovers, and related plant materials; the management of technical and business operations connected with horticultural services; and the basic scientific principles needed to understand plants and their management and care.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in resource allocation and risk mitigation strategies for large-scale, multi-disciplinary R&D programs by developing a computational framework to model and optimize decision-making processes. Traditional project management approaches often struggle to account for the dynamic interdependencies between technical milestones, budgetary constraints, and personnel logistics in complex research initiatives. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations that capture the nonlinear relationships between R&D variables at unprecedented scale. The computational model will integrate historical project performance data, real-time resource utilization metrics, and probabilistic risk assessments to generate adaptive allocation strategies. Key innovations include machine learning modules to predict bottlenecks in collaborative workflows and scenario analysis tools to evaluate trade-offs between parallel development pathways. By simulating 10,000+ concurrent decision trees across distributed computing nodes, the system will identify robust management policies resilient to common failure modes such as personnel attrition or funding volatility. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for optimizing capital expenditure distribution in technology development programs, predictive models for stakeholder risk tolerance thresholds, and generalized guidelines for scaling computational decision-support tools across public and private R&D sectors. This work bridges gaps between computational social science and operational management theory, with potential applications ranging from pharmaceutical development pipelines to national laboratory research consortia. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of multi-agent simulations and enabling near-real-time parameter optimization in our models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage projects, programs and organizations involving basic and applied research, or specialized technology applications, in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in all aspects of business management applied to the leadership and control of scientific, clinical, engineering and social scientific enterprises; the management of related operational, security and logistical issues; and technical competence in one or more research disciplines.

abstract: The increasing complexity of student needs in postsecondary education demands innovative approaches to optimize counseling interventions and resource allocation. Current practices in student counseling often rely on static assessments or generalized protocols, which may fail to address the dynamic, interconnected factors influencing student well-being and academic success. This project proposes to develop a predictive modeling framework using machine learning and network analysis to identify patterns in multi-source student data (e.g., academic performance, service utilization, and anonymized counseling session transcripts) that correlate with critical outcomes such as retention, mental health crises, and career readiness. The computational approach will integrate natural language processing techniques to analyze unstructured text data from counseling interactions with structured institutional records, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale datasets (>1 million anonymized student records across 15 partner institutions) and train complex neural architectures. A key innovation involves simulating intervention pathways through agent-based modeling to predict how tailored counseling strategies might propagate through student support networks. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing for real-time analysis of longitudinal data streams and ethical AI validation processes to mitigate algorithmic bias. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for higher education institutions to prioritize at-risk populations, dynamically adjust counseling resource distribution, and evaluate intervention effectiveness through counterfactual simulations. This work advances education research by establishing computationally rigorous methods to personalize student support while maintaining strict privacy standards. Results will directly inform national best practices for data-informed counseling in the College Student Counseling and Personnel Services field, with particular relevance to underserved populations in community colleges and minority-serving institutions.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing instrumental performance pedagogy through computational analysis of biomechanical and acoustic data. While traditional music training emphasizes subjective feedback, emerging computational methods offer opportunities to quantitatively assess performance techniques, yet such approaches remain underexplored in wind and string instrument pedagogy. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and high-fidelity audio recordings—captured during live performances by advanced student musicians. Computational workflows will integrate kinematic modeling of embouchure (for wind instruments) and bow-arm dynamics (for strings) with spectral analysis of timbral output, correlating physiological patterns with acoustic outcomes. Machine learning models trained on these datasets will identify biomechanical inefficiencies linked to suboptimal sound production or injury risks, enabling the development of adaptive feedback tools for performers. A parallel strand will simulate large-scale ensemble coordination dynamics by modeling real-time acoustic interactions between instrumentalists in virtual performance spaces, requiring distributed-memory parallelization to resolve latency-sensitive auditory feedback loops. Expected outcomes include open-source frameworks for performance analysis, evidence-based pedagogical guidelines to reduce repetitive strain injuries, and novel metrics for ensemble synchronization. By bridging computational rigor with artistic practice, this work aims to advance data-driven methodologies in music performance research while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in domains beyond traditional STEM fields. Resource requests focus on GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory systems for handling terabyte-scale multimodal datasets.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to master musical instruments and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers. Includes instruction on one or more specific instruments from various instrumental groupings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of digital communication dynamics within Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS), focusing on the dissemination and reception of nutrition, financial literacy, and household safety information across socioeconomically diverse populations. The core challenge lies in modeling how complex, context-dependent consumer information spreads through fragmented digital ecosystems (e.g., social media, community forums, and targeted advisories) and how such communication influences decision-making in resource-constrained households. Current tools for analyzing these interactions lack the capacity to process multimodal data (text, video, temporal behavioral logs) at the scale required to capture nonlinear feedback loops between information exposure, cultural norms, and practical adoption of recommendations. The project will develop agent-based models simulating information diffusion pathways, integrating demographic data, psychometric profiles, and platform-specific engagement patterns. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing to analyze semantic shifts in user-generated content, graph neural networks to map community-level information cascades, and reinforcement learning frameworks to predict intervention efficacy under varying resource access scenarios. By parallelizing these tasks across GPU clusters, the models will achieve the resolution needed to identify critical leverage points for improving communication equity. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for optimizing FCS messaging strategies, evidence-based criteria for prioritizing high-impact content delivery channels, and open-source tools tailored to non-technical FCS practitioners. This work addresses a critical gap in human sciences communication by bridging computational social science methodologies with applied consumer education goals, ultimately aiming to reduce disparities in access to actionable, life-enhancing information.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Communication
cip_definition: A program that focuses on communication of human sciences subject matter and related consumer information to a variety of audiences through print and non-print media.

abstract: The global fashion industry faces increasing pressure to optimize live and virtual presentation strategies that balance consumer engagement, operational efficiency, and environmental impact. This project addresses the computational challenge of simulating and predicting outcomes for hybrid (physical-digital) fashion modeling events, where dynamic variables such as audience attention patterns, model choreography, real-time garment physics, and sustainability metrics intersect. Current industry practices rely on heuristic decision-making, leading to resource-intensive trial-and-error processes in event design. We propose developing an agent-based modeling framework enhanced by computer vision and reinforcement learning to simulate audience reactions, model movement efficiency, and material waste patterns under diverse staging scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal datasets—including 3D garment simulations, eye-tracking data from past shows, and environmental impact metrics—while training neural networks to identify pareto-optimal configurations that maximize aesthetic impact and minimize carbon footprint. The computational pipeline will integrate real-time rendering engines with discrete-event simulation tools, requiring parallel processing of terabyte-scale spatial-temporal data streams. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that quantifies trade-offs between creative choices and sustainability benchmarks, potentially reducing material waste in set construction by 15-30% and improving audience retention metrics for virtual shows. This research establishes a novel computational foundation for data-driven fashion presentation design, bridging operational research, behavioral analytics, and environmental science within the business context of modeling program optimization. Results will be validated through partnerships with three Milan-based fashion houses implementing 2025 hybrid show formats.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to present and display fashion, apparel, and accessories products in wholesale and retail settings, either on the person or via props and natural or artificial settings. Includes instruction in modeling skills, health and cosmetic principles, fashion show management, display design and production, and applicable aspects of advertising and fashion photography.

abstract: The project seeks to develop advanced computational methods to address optimization challenges in high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems arising in real-world applications such as autonomous vehicle coordination and energy grid management. These systems are characterized by complex interactions between agents, non-convex objective functions, and stochastic environmental factors, rendering traditional optimization frameworks intractable. The research will focus on designing hybrid algorithms that integrate stochastic optimal control theory with scalable numerical linear algebra techniques, specifically targeting systems governed by partial differential equations with uncertain parameters. A central innovation involves leveraging parallelized tensor decomposition methods to reduce the dimensionality of the state space while preserving critical system dynamics. The computational approach will employ iterative Krylov subspace solvers accelerated by GPU-based preconditioning, coupled with adaptive importance sampling for uncertainty propagation. Key challenges include maintaining numerical stability in ill-conditioned regimes and achieving load balancing across distributed memory architectures during large-scale eigenvalue computations. The project will validate methods using benchmark problems from swarm robotics and phase-field material modeling, with scalability tests targeting system sizes exceeding 10^6 degrees of freedom. Successful implementation will provide open-source software tools for solving a class of non-smooth optimization problems common in applied mathematics, along with theoretical guarantees on convergence rates under relaxed convexity assumptions. Outcomes are expected to impact the design of resilient infrastructure systems and multi-agent control protocols, particularly in scenarios requiring real-time decision-making with incomplete information. High-performance computing resources are critical to evaluate algorithm performance at relevant scales, as preliminary estimates indicate a requirement of 250,000 core-hours for parameter space exploration and 40 TB of distributed memory for handling dense Jacobian matrices in sensitivity analyses. This work bridges gaps between numerical analysis and computational engineering, offering novel pathways to manage complexity in applied dynamical systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in applied mathematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the morphological and syntactic convergence of under-documented Romance language varieties in the Western Mediterranean, with a focus on Gascon Occitan, Sardinian, and Algherese Catalan. The central research problem revolves around identifying and modeling contact-induced grammatical changes in these minority languages, which have historically coexisted with dominant linguistic systems but lack comprehensive computational analysis. Current methodologies for comparative Romance linguistics remain limited by manual annotation processes and insufficient processing power to analyze complex syntactic dependencies across large, heterogeneous corpora. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a transformer-based architecture fine-tuned for low-resource language processing. The computational approach will involve training multilingual models on digitized historical texts, transcribed oral narratives, and modern community-generated content (totaling ~15 billion tokens) to perform cross-linguistic dependency parsing and morphological feature extraction. Parallel GPU-accelerated workflows will enable comparative analysis of grammatical structures across temporal (13th–21st centuries) and geographic dimensions, while variational autoencoders will model potential convergence pathways. The project will generate three key outcomes: (1) an open-access repository of annotated parallel corpora for endangered Romance varieties, (2) a computational framework for tracking morphosyntactic change in language contact situations, and (3) quantitative evidence testing theoretical models of areal linguistics in the Mediterranean context. By combining computational linguistics with philological expertise, this work aims to advance methodological paradigms in Romance studies while providing critical resources for preserving linguistic diversity. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive processing of historical orthographies, simultaneous training of comparative models, and large-scale simulation of language change scenarios that cannot be replicated on standard departmental infrastructure.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Romance languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of Italian cultural identity through large-scale textual and visual analysis. The research focuses on tracing how regional dialects, literary movements, and visual media (e.g., film, posters, and archival photography) have shaped collective narratives of belonging and dissent across Italy from the post-Unification period (post-1861) to the late 20th century. A central challenge lies in processing and analyzing unstructured, multilingual datasets—including digitized newspapers, manuscripts, and audiovisual materials—that exceed the capacity of standard computational tools due to their volume (estimated at 15+ TB) and linguistic complexity. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical Italian and regional languages (e.g., Neapolitan, Sicilian), combined with computer vision models to detect stylistic patterns in visual media. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for semantic analysis of ideological shifts in literature, clustering dialectal variations across time and geography, and mapping visual motifs tied to socio-political movements. These workflows require parallelized GPU computing for model training, distributed storage for cross-referencing heterogeneous datasets, and high-memory nodes for network analysis of cultural influence patterns. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital archive of annotated materials, visualizations of cultural transmission pathways, and methodological frameworks for computationally analyzing underrepresented Italian dialects. The findings aim to deepen scholarly understanding of how localized cultural production influenced national identity formation, while demonstrating scalable approaches for interdisciplinary humanities research. By integrating HPC capabilities with archival research, this project addresses critical gaps in Italian Studies’ engagement with computational methods and fosters new avenues for studying cultural change at scale.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of modern Italy and its predecessors on the Italian Peninsula, including the overseas migrations of Italian peoples.

abstract: Licensed Practical/Vocational Nurses (LPNs/LVNs) play a critical role in patient care, yet clinical workflows often lack data-driven tools to optimize their decision-making in dynamic care environments. This project addresses the challenge of predicting patient deterioration in acute care settings, where delays in recognizing early warning signs can lead to adverse outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop machine learning (ML) models that analyze multimodal clinical data—including vital signs, medication administration records, and nurse-reported observations—to identify high-risk patients in real time. Current approaches rely on static protocols, which do not adapt to individual patient trajectories or contextual factors such as staffing constraints. The computational workload involves processing heterogeneous datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), requiring parallelized pipelines for data cleaning, feature engineering, and temporal analysis. Deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models and recurrent neural networks, will be trained on historical patient data to detect subtle patterns preceding clinical deterioration. HPC resources are essential to manage the scale of EHR data (spanning millions of patient-hours), optimize hyperparameters via distributed computing, and validate models across diverse patient subgroups. The outcomes will include an open-source predictive framework tailored for integration into LPN workflows, providing actionable alerts to prioritize interventions. This research directly aligns with nursing science by enhancing LPNs’ capacity to deliver proactive care, potentially reducing hospital-acquired complications and readmissions. By simulating care scenarios under varying resource conditions, the models will also inform training programs on adaptive clinical judgment. The project underscores the transformative role of computational methods in nursing practice, bridging data science and hands-on patient care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in providing general nursing care under the direction of a registered nurse, physician or dentist. Includes instruction in taking patient vital signs, applying sterile dressings, patient health education, and assistance with examinations and treatment.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of industrial-scale multiphase chemical reactors through high-fidelity computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical inefficiencies in reaction yield and energy consumption. Industrial reactors, particularly those involving gas-liquid-solid interactions, face challenges in achieving uniform mixing, heat transfer, and mass transfer, which directly impact process efficiency, safety, and environmental footprint. Traditional scale-up methods rely on empirical correlations and physical prototyping, which are costly, time-intensive, and often fail to capture complex multiphase dynamics. To overcome these limitations, this research employs computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with reactive transport modeling to simulate turbulent multiphase flows, species transport, and reaction kinetics at industrially relevant scales. High-resolution simulations will utilize open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM) to model reactor geometries under varying operational parameters, including flow rates, temperature gradients, and catalyst distributions. HPC resources are essential to resolve the wide range of spatial and temporal scales inherent to these systems, enabling parallelized simulations with meshes exceeding 10 million cells and transient analyses spanning seconds of real-time operation. Validation against experimental data from lab-scale reactors will ensure model accuracy. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to optimize reactor configuration, reduce energy use by 15–20%, and minimize hazardous byproduct formation. The computational tools developed will also provide training opportunities for students in advanced process simulation, bridging gaps between theoretical principles and industrial applications. By integrating HPC-driven insights with practical engineering constraints, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-informed reactor design, directly supporting the Chemical Engineering Technology program’s mission to enhance sustainable and safe chemical production.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: Aging populations present complex healthcare challenges due to the interplay of chronic illnesses, polypharmacy, cognitive decline, and physiological vulnerability. Geriatric nurses require evidence-based tools to predict adverse outcomes and optimize care plans, but existing predictive models often fail to account for the multidimensional, dynamic interactions between biological, pharmacological, and psychosocial factors in elderly patients. This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to identify high-risk geriatric patients and recommend personalized interventions by integrating electronic health records, medication adherence data, wearable sensor outputs, and patient-reported outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-dimensional datasets spanning years of longitudinal care, train ensemble models capturing nonlinear relationships between variables (e.g., drug-drug interactions, frailty trajectories), and simulate intervention impacts across diverse patient subgroups. Computational workflows will leverage natural language processing to extract unstructured clinical notes, graph neural networks to model comorbidity networks, and reinforcement learning to adapt treatment recommendations based on evolving patient states. Validation will involve retrospective analysis of 15,000+ patient records from geriatric clinics and prospective pilot testing with 200 patients monitored via remote sensors. Expected outcomes include a validated risk stratification tool for falls, delirium, and medication-related hospitalizations, as well as decision-support algorithms to guide nurse-led care transitions. By enabling real-time analysis of multifactorial risks, this project aims to advance precision geriatric nursing practices, reduce preventable complications, and establish scalable computational methods for aging-related nursing research. The requested HPC resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data integration, and virtual patient simulations to rigorously test hypotheses before clinical implementation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate dysregulated intracellular signaling mechanisms in cancer cells, with a focus on how tumor microenvironments alter ion channel dynamics and calcium-dependent signaling pathways to promote metastatic behavior. A critical gap exists in understanding how spatial and temporal variations in ion gradients, particularly calcium and potassium, integrate with oncogenic signaling cascades to drive phenotypic plasticity in solid tumors. This project will develop multiscale computational models to simulate ion flux dynamics, membrane potential changes, and downstream effector activation (e.g., calmodulin kinases, transcription factors) within 3D tumor architectures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these stochastic, nonlinear processes at subcellular resolution across physiologically relevant timescales (milliseconds to days). Agent-based modeling frameworks will be coupled with partial differential equation solvers to capture feedback between single-cell electrophysiology, paracrine signaling, and collective migration patterns. Model parameters will be informed by live-cell imaging data of calcium transients and membrane voltage fluctuations in breast cancer organoids. The computational pipeline will identify critical thresholds in ion channel cooperativity and network motifs that stabilize pro-metastatic states. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of microenvironmental triggers for invasion and actionable targets for disrupting pathological intercellular synchronization. By elucidating how cancer cells exploit physiological signaling architectures to bypass homeostatic controls, this work will advance therapeutic strategies that selectively impair malignant communication networks without compromising normal tissue function. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter sweeps across >10^6 simulated cell-hours and Bayesian inference of high-dimensional datasets, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of physiological processes operating within and among cells, and intracellular communication and behavior, in the context of larger systems and whole organisms. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology, molecular physiology, cell cycle control, signal transduction, protein structure, membrane biochemistry and structure, ion channel physics, cell respiration and digestion, secretory functions, cell adhesion and communication, information encoding and decoding, and the relation of cell physiology to tissue, organ, and organismic functioning.

abstract: This project addresses the growing demand for advanced computational tools in generative design and immersive media art, where current workflows are constrained by the scale and complexity of data-driven creative processes. The research focuses on developing a framework for real-time, interactive 3D environments that integrate generative adversarial networks (GANs) and fluid dynamics simulations to model dynamic visual narratives. These environments, intended for large-scale public installations, require rendering high-resolution, physics-accurate interactions between light, materials, and virtual agents—a task exceeding the capacity of standard computing infrastructure. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize two core processes: (1) training GANs on terabyte-scale datasets of cultural artifacts and environmental sensor data to generate context-aware visual patterns, and (2) running GPU-optimized simulations of particle systems that respond to real-time audience inputs via motion capture feeds. By deploying containerized workflows across HPC nodes, the team aims to achieve sub-100ms latency in rendering feedback loops, enabling unprecedented interactivity in digital art. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible toolkit for artists working with computationally intensive media, validated through case studies in augmented reality (AR) exhibitions and parametric architectural prototypes. This work bridges gaps between algorithmic creativity and human-centered design, offering new methodologies for sustainable, data-informed public art while advancing interdisciplinary discourse on computational aesthetics. The requested resources directly support scalability testing, ensuring reproducibility for complex installations requiring exascale rendering capabilities.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in design and applied arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular and cellular dynamics underlying therapy-resistant neoplasms in epithelial tissues, with a focus on resolving how spatial heterogeneity in tumor microenvironments drives pathological progression. A critical barrier in experimental pathology is the inability to model multiscale interactions between aberrant cell signaling, immune evasion, and matrix remodeling processes that sustain aggressive tumor phenotypes. We propose an integrative computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze high-dimensional datasets from multiplexed tissue imaging, single-cell transcriptomics, and longitudinal patient-derived xenograft models. Agent-based modeling will simulate spatial competition between neoplastic clones under varying stromal conditions, while machine learning pipelines will identify conserved molecular signatures predictive of metastatic transformation. The computational architecture will integrate Python-based analytical workflows with optimized C++ kernels for large-scale parameter space exploration, requiring dedicated GPU nodes and parallel processing capabilities to handle 10^6-cell simulations and terabyte-scale histopathology datasets. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of microenvironmental checkpoints regulating therapy-resistant niche formation, 2) predictive models linking extracellular matrix topology to clonal selection dynamics, and 3) candidate biomarkers for early detection of occult metastatic populations in archival tissue specimens. This resource-intensive approach addresses a fundamental gap in experimental pathology by bridging organ-scale pathophysiology with subcellular resolution of molecular effectors, directly informing the development of precision diagnostics for advanced carcinomas. The requested allocation will enable unprecedented resolution of spatial oncogenic processes while maintaining compatibility with clinical data standards used in translational cancer biology.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the expression, initiation, maintenance and progression of tissue injury and disease, including death, and the relationship of pathogenesis to fundamental molecular and cellular mechanisms. Includes instruction in immunology, microbiology, gene expression, inflammation, cell injury, apoptosis, immunopathology, molecular markers of disease and toxins, neoplasia, growth regulation, and organ- and system-specific investigations.

abstract: The study of non-adiabatic dynamics in photochemical reactions is critical for understanding energy transfer and reaction pathways in complex molecular systems. However, simulating these processes remains computationally prohibitive due to the need for quantum mechanical accuracy across multiple electronic states and the exponential scaling of traditional methods with system size. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced multiscale simulations that combine trajectory surface hopping (TSH) with machine learning (ML)-accelerated potential energy surfaces (PES). The research will focus on prototypical systems, such as organic chromophores and transition metal complexes, where intersystem crossing and conical intersections govern photochemical outcomes. Ab initio calculations (TDDFT and CASSCF) will generate training data for neural network PES models, while TSH simulations will propagate ensembles of trajectories to quantify quantum coherence and state-resolved reaction probabilities. The computational workflow will utilize hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization to distribute electronic structure computations across nodes and accelerate ML inference. Key outcomes include predictive dynamical models for ultrafast excited-state processes, benchmarks of ML-PES accuracy against full quantum dynamics, and mechanistic insights into spin-orbit coupling effects in metal-containing systems. This work will advance the theoretical framework for simulating photochemical reactions with explicit treatment of electron-nuclear correlations, enabling the design of light-driven molecular devices and photocatalysts. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the ∼10^4 core-hour scale of ab initio data generation and the statistical demands of ensemble-based dynamics, which exceed the capacity of local computing clusters. By integrating computational chemistry, quantum dynamics, and machine learning, this project bridges methodological innovation with applications in energy conversion and synthetic chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of structural phenomena combining the disciplines of physical chemistry and atomic/molecular physics. Includes instruction in heterogeneous structures, alignment and surface phenomena, quantum theory, mathematical physics, statistical and classical mechanics, chemical kinetics, and laser physics.

abstract: Dental implant failure remains a significant challenge due to biomechanical incompatibilities and suboptimal osseointegration. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in capturing the complex interplay between implant design, bone microstructure, and functional loading patterns. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate the biomechanical behavior of dental implants under physiologically realistic conditions. By integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with patient-specific computed tomography (CT) data and machine learning algorithms, we aim to predict stress distribution, micro-motion, and long-term bone remodeling outcomes across diverse anatomical variations. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate the atomic-scale interactions between titanium implant surfaces and biological fluids to optimize surface treatments for enhanced osseointegration. The computational framework will be validated against in vitro mechanical testing and longitudinal clinical data. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical due to the high-resolution 3D modeling requirements, which involve millions of mesh elements, and the iterative nature of parameter optimization in machine learning pipelines. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for personalized implant design, evidence-based guidelines for occlusal load management, and novel surface modification protocols. This research will advance the understanding of implant biomechanics, reduce postoperative complications, and establish a computational workflow adaptable to other craniofacial reconstructive applications. The generated datasets and models will be made available to the dental research community, fostering collaboration and innovation in computational dentistry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of dentistry/dental medicine, encompassing the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, and adjacent structures and their impact on the human body and health. Includes instruction in the basic biomedical sciences, occlusion, dental health and prevention, oral pathology, cariology, operative dentistry, oral radiology, principles of the various dental specialties, pain management, oral medicine, clinic and health care management, patient counseling, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and semantic patterns underlying ethical symbolism across religious and philosophical traditions using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically analyzing large, multilingual corpora of primary texts (e.g., scriptural exegeses, philosophical treatises) to identify how ethical concepts are symbolically encoded and evolve within and between traditions. Current manual approaches struggle to scale across diverse texts, limiting comparative studies of shared ethical frameworks. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), semantic network analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM). NLP pipelines will process digitized texts in Sanskrit, Arabic, Classical Chinese, and Greek, leveraging transformer-based models for cross-lingual concept extraction. Dynamic semantic networks will map relationships between ethical symbols (e.g., "justice," "compassion") and their contextual associations, while ABM simulations will test hypotheses about how these symbolic systems influence decision-making paradigms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training multilingual NLP models, analyzing terabyte-scale text datasets, and running complex simulations of symbolic interaction across thousands of cultural-historical scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel computational framework for comparative ethics research, 2) a publicly accessible database of annotated ethical symbols spanning six religious-philosophical traditions, and 3) peer-reviewed insights into cross-cultural convergences in symbolic moral reasoning. This work will provide humanities researchers with scalable tools to study ethical systems as dynamic, interconnected phenomena, bridging gaps between philosophical analysis, religious studies, and computational social science.
cip_definition: A general program that combines the study of philosophy and religious studies. Includes instruction in logic; ethics; epistemology; symbolism; phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature, and art of religion; and world religions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in analyzing the syntactic and semantic evolution of Modern Greek across its post-medieval development, with a focus on understudied regional dialects and literary texts from the 18th century to the present. While prior scholarship has cataloged grammatical shifts in standardized Greek, computational limitations have hindered large-scale comparative analyses of non-canonical texts, vernacular sources, and dialectal variations—critical gaps this study aims to fill. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models and dynamic word embedding frameworks, to process a curated corpus of digitized manuscripts, newspapers, and transcribed oral histories (totaling ~15 TB). Computational workflows will be designed to identify diachronic patterns in morphological structures, lexical borrowing, and pragmatic features, particularly in texts from Crete, the Aegean islands, and Asia Minor communities. Parallelized sentiment analysis and topic modeling will further illuminate stylistic divergences between literary movements and regional vernacular traditions. By integrating computational philology with dialectometry, this approach will generate interactive maps and network graphs visualizing linguistic change across temporal and geographic axes. The outcomes will include the first open-access database of annotated Modern Greek dialectal corpora, machine learning models fine-tuned for low-resource Greek variants, and quantitative frameworks for assessing language contact phenomena. These resources will advance scholarly understanding of Greek’s sociolinguistic stratification while providing tools for educators and policymakers addressing language preservation. The scale of data processing—requiring GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multilingual alignment, and high-memory nodes for graph-based analytics—necessitates HPC infrastructure beyond typical departmental capacities. This work bridges computational humanities and linguistic research, offering methodological innovations applicable to other under-resourced languages in historical contexts.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and use of the Greek language in the period dating from the late 15th century to the present. Includes instruction in modern Greek literature, current Greek dialects, and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Statistical inference in high-dimensional and complex data settings often encounters computational bottlenecks, particularly when Bayesian methodologies or non-parametric techniques are applied to large-scale datasets. This project seeks to address the challenge of scaling statistical analyses for modern, massive datasets by developing and optimizing computationally intensive methods for uncertainty quantification, model selection, and posterior sampling. The research focuses on three interrelated objectives: (1) implementing parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms with adaptive tuning for high-dimensional hierarchical models, (2) evaluating the performance of variational inference methods under non-conjugate likelihood-prior pairs in multi-modal scenarios, and (3) optimizing stochastic gradient-based samplers for non-parametric Bayesian models with millions of observations. These tasks require high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the iterative nature of Monte Carlo methods, the need for repeated cross-validation across parameter subspaces, and the memory demands of processing large covariance matrices in Gaussian process regression. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated libraries for linear algebra operations and distributed computing frameworks to parallelize chain initialization and likelihood evaluations across nodes. Expected outcomes include new algorithmic implementations that reduce wall-clock time for complex statistical models by 40-60% compared to existing open-source tools, as well as benchmarks quantifying trade-offs between approximation accuracy and computational cost in modern Bayesian workflows. The developed methods will be applied to two case studies: genomic association mapping with spatially correlated noise structures and real-time uncertainty quantification in streaming environmental sensor data. By enabling faster, more reliable statistical inference at scale, this work aims to advance methodological capabilities in fields where computational constraints currently limit the adoption of rigorous probabilistic approaches.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural evolution of medieval ecclesiastical legal systems through computational analysis of canon law texts spanning the 12th to 15th centuries. While traditional scholarship has focused on doctrinal or theological interpretations, this research employs computational methods to map the development of legal frameworks across time and geography, with a focus on their adaptation to shifting socio-political contexts. The central problem lies in identifying patterns of influence, textual reuse, and procedural innovation within a corpus of over 10,000 digitized Latin and vernacular legal documents—a scale requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical Latin and Middle English, the project will analyze semantic shifts in key juridical concepts (e.g., “dispensatio,” “excommunicatio”) and their relationship to parallel developments in secular legal systems. Graph network models will trace citation patterns between canonical collections, papal decretals, and regional synodal statutes to quantify how localized practices became systematized into universal church law. A second phase will employ agent-based modeling to simulate how hypothetical changes in canonical procedures might have influenced historical outcomes in documented case disputes. The computational workflow demands parallel processing of heterogeneous text formats (manuscript transcriptions, printed editions, secondary literature) alongside geospatial data on diocesan boundaries. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated canon law texts with cross-referenced computational metadata; (2) quantitative models demonstrating the diffusion of legal innovations across medieval Europe; and (3) methodological frameworks for applying NLP to understudied premodern legal corpora. By bridging computational approaches with canonistic scholarship, this project aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing the dynamic interplay between religious law and historical change.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, theology, and philosophy of religious, church, and ecclesiastical law and that prepares individuals to serve as professional canonists.

abstract: The study of textual transmission and variation across historical manuscripts presents significant challenges due to the scale and complexity of extant materials. Traditional methods in textual criticism and stemmatology struggle to efficiently analyze large corpora, limiting the scope of cultural and literary inquiry. This project proposes the application of high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable computational models for mapping textual relationships, identifying scribal practices, and reconstructing manuscript genealogies. By employing machine learning algorithms to detect patterns in orthography, syntax, and semantic content across digitized manuscripts, alongside phylogenetic approaches adapted from bioinformatics, this research aims to automate and enhance the accuracy of stemma construction. Concurrently, large-scale text analysis pipelines will be deployed to examine cultural and historical influences embedded within textual variants, utilizing natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical languages. The computational infrastructure will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including high-resolution manuscript images and multilingual texts, through distributed storage and parallelized workflows. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-source tools for textual scholars, new insights into the transmission of specific literary works, and methodological frameworks for interdisciplinary collaboration between humanities research and computational sciences. This project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in advancing textual studies, offering unprecedented capacity to address questions of authorship, dissemination, and cultural exchange that have remained intractable with conventional approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interconnected histories of digital or print texts and manuscripts for cultural and literary study. Includes instruction in archiving texts, bibliography, book and literary history, cultural studies, codicology, paleography, stemmatology, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize supply chain efficiency in agricultural retail and wholesale systems through data-driven modeling of dynamic market and environmental factors. Agricultural input suppliers face significant challenges in balancing inventory, pricing, and distribution across seasonal demand fluctuations, perishable goods, and unpredictable climate impacts. Current analytical tools often fail to integrate real-time weather patterns, soil health data, and regional commodity price trends at scale. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate multi-agent agricultural supply networks under diverse climatic and economic scenarios. The computational model will leverage machine learning algorithms trained on 10 years of historical sales data from Midwest U.S. cooperatives, paired with NOAA weather records and USDA crop reports. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess risk propagation across distribution nodes, while graph neural networks will map optimal restocking routes under resource constraints. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale geospatial datasets and running millions of parameter combinations to identify resilient inventory strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing fertilizer waste in transit, dynamic pricing models responsive to regional yield forecasts, and adaptive logistics templates to reduce energy costs in perishable goods transport. This work will directly support agricultural retailers in mitigating climate-related revenue losses while maintaining affordable access to farm inputs. Results will be disseminated through an open-access decision support platform tailored for small-to-midsize agricultural suppliers, with validation trials planned across three state-level farm bureaus. The computational pipelines developed will establish reproducible methods for integrating heterogeneous agricultural data streams into operational retail management systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Farm Supplies Retailing and Wholesaling
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to sell agricultural products and supplies, provide support services to agricultural enterprises, and purchase and market agricultural products. Includes instruction in basic business management, marketing, retailing and wholesaling operations, and applicable principles of agriculture and agricultural operations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social network evolution and its impact on demographic disparities in urban environments using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on understanding how large-scale social interactions, structural inequalities, and institutional policies collectively shape population outcomes—such as access to resources, migration patterns, and community resilience—across heterogeneous urban populations. Traditional sociological methods struggle to model these multilevel, nonlinear interactions due to the scale and complexity of longitudinal social data, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with machine learning techniques to simulate interactions among millions of agents representing individuals, households, and institutions. These agents will operate under rule sets derived from sociological theory, incorporating variables such as economic mobility, social capital, and policy interventions. The models will be calibrated using anonymized census data, public health records, and geospatial information, with validation against historical demographic trends. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing simulations across diverse parameter spaces, enabling sensitivity analyses and Bayesian optimization to identify key drivers of inequality. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for predicting how localized social policies might amplify or mitigate demographic disparities, particularly in education and healthcare access. The results will contribute to computational sociology by advancing methodologies for analyzing large-scale social systems, while also providing empirical evidence to inform equitable policy design. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges theoretical sociology and data-driven policymaking, addressing gaps in understanding how micro-level social behaviors aggregate into macro-level population trends.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human social institutions and social relationships. Includes instruction in social theory, sociological research methods, social organization and structure, social stratification and hierarchies, dynamics of social change, family structures, social deviance and control, and applications to the study of specific social groups, social institutions, and social problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized therapeutic exercise protocols for patients with mobility impairments due to neurological or musculoskeletal conditions. Current rehabilitation strategies often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for individual variability in biomechanics, physiology, and pathology. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create patient-specific simulations that model the biomechanical and physiological effects of therapeutic exercises. The research problem centers on identifying how individualized parameters—such as joint kinematics, muscle activation patterns, and tissue load distribution—interact during rehabilitation, and how these factors influence functional recovery outcomes. The computational approach integrates musculoskeletal modeling, machine learning, and dynamic simulations to predict optimal exercise intensity, duration, and modality for diverse patient profiles. Multiscale models will simulate neuromuscular responses to therapeutic movements using open-source biomechanics software (e.g., OpenSim), while machine learning algorithms will analyze clinical datasets (e.g., gait analysis, electromyography, and patient-reported outcomes) to identify predictive biomarkers of rehabilitation success. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across large patient cohorts and high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool to guide kinesiotherapists in designing adaptive, evidence-based interventions for conditions such as stroke, spinal cord injury, and osteoarthritis. This work will advance precision rehabilitation by bridging gaps between clinical practice and computational biomechanics, potentially reducing trial-and-error in therapy design and improving patient adherence. The resulting open-access models and datasets will serve as a resource for interdisciplinary research in rehabilitation science, motor control, and assistive technology development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the direction of physicians, to treat the effects of disease, injury, and congenital disorders through therapeutic exercise and education. Includes instruction in human anatomy, human physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, therapeutic exercise and adapted physical education, human growth and development, motor learning and performance, testing and measurement, first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, psychology, rehabilitation procedures, patient assessment and management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the complex interactions between environmental variables, group dynamics, and educational outcomes in outdoor education programs. While outdoor education emphasizes experiential learning in natural settings, there is a critical gap in understanding how dynamic environmental factors (e.g., weather patterns, terrain complexity) and interpersonal behaviors (e.g., communication networks, leadership emergence) collectively influence participant engagement, skill acquisition, and risk mitigation. Traditional qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods lack the capacity to process multimodal datasets or simulate scenarios at the scale required to inform evidence-based program design. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate participant interactions within virtual environments mirroring real-world outdoor education contexts, integrating geospatial data, biometric inputs (e.g., heart rate variability from wearable sensors), and behavioral logs. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive patterns linking environmental stressors, group cohesion metrics, and learning outcomes across diverse demographic cohorts. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulations will assess risk probabilities for varying activity configurations, enabling the development of adaptive safety protocols. By synthesizing ecological, psychological, and pedagogical data streams, this computational approach aims to generate actionable frameworks for optimizing program efficacy, accessibility, and safety. Outcomes will include open-source tools for scenario modeling, risk prediction dashboards for instructors, and evidence-based guidelines for tailoring activities to participant needs. The project represents a novel interdisciplinary fusion of computational social science, environmental analytics, and education research, advancing methodological innovation in non-STEM fields while addressing pressing challenges in outdoor education practice.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work as an educator, instructor or facilitator in parks, recreational facilities, camps and other outdoor settings. Includes instruction in leadership skills, wilderness survival skills, first aid, group processes, counseling techniques, environmental studies and instruction in recreational activities such as rock climbing, ropes courses, backpacking, kayaking and canoeing.

abstract: The development of efficient catalytic processes for sustainable chemical manufacturing is limited by the complex interplay of reaction kinetics, transport phenomena, and catalyst surface dynamics. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-scale phenomena in heterogeneous catalysis. Current models often decouple atomistic catalyst behavior from reactor-scale fluid dynamics, leading to inaccuracies in predicting selectivity and activity under industrial conditions. We propose a hybrid computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to resolve these interactions. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of catalytic surface reactions at the quantum mechanical level while coupling these results with continuum-scale reactor models. Key objectives include elucidating the role of surface defects in reaction pathways for CO₂ hydrogenation systems and optimizing mass transfer in structured catalytic reactors. The computational workflow will employ machine learning surrogates trained on DFT datasets to accelerate parameterization of CFD models, requiring significant GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive models for catalyst design under non-ideal flow conditions and actionable insights into scaling modular reactor systems for decentralized chemical production. This work directly supports the development of energy-efficient processes aligned with net-zero emissions targets, bridging molecular-scale insights with engineering-scale implementation. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the memory-intensive MD simulations (>10,000 atoms) and the concurrent execution of multi-physics reactor models, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters. Results will be disseminated through open-access quantum chemistry databases and validated against experimental collaborator data from flow reactor trials.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model patient-specific responses to anesthetic agents, addressing critical gaps in predicting adverse perioperative outcomes. Despite advances in anesthesia protocols, significant variability in patient reactions—driven by factors such as comorbidities, genetic polymorphisms, and drug interactions—remains poorly characterized. Current clinical decision-making relies on population averages, which often fail to account for individual pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic heterogeneity. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct multi-scale machine learning models integrating electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-time physiological metrics. The computational pipeline will include three phases: (1) preprocessing and harmonization of high-dimensional clinical datasets using parallelized data reduction techniques; (2) training of ensemble neural networks to predict hemodynamic instability and drug sensitivity patterns across diverse patient subgroups; and (3) agent-based simulations of anesthetic interactions at the cellular level, informed by molecular dynamics datasets of common anesthetic agents (e.g., propofol, opioids). The HPC environment is essential for handling the scale of EHR data (≥50,000 patient cases), optimizing hyperparameters for deep learning architectures, and running stochastic simulations of drug-receptor binding kinetics. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for individualized anesthetic dosing, identification of genetic biomarkers associated with anesthesia-related complications, and mechanistic insights into rare adverse events such as malignant hyperthermia. By enabling real-time, data-driven adjustments to anesthesia delivery, this work has the potential to reduce postoperative morbidity, shorten recovery times, and improve patient safety in diverse clinical settings. The models and code will be disseminated through open-access platforms to support evidence-based practice for nurse anesthetists and advance precision nursing science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models for optimizing office management processes in dynamic organizational environments.
