The research addresses a critical gap in evidence-based decision-making tools for office supervisors, particularly in balancing personnel workflows, physical space allocation, and operational costs under fluctuating workplace demands. Current approaches to office management optimization rely heavily on static guidelines or oversimplified simulations that fail to capture the complex interdependencies between human factors, resource constraints, and evolving business priorities. We propose a multi-method computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to analyze large-scale datasets capturing employee productivity patterns, facility usage metrics, and workflow coordination challenges. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional optimization scenarios, including real-time simulations of office reconfigurations during mergers, remote work transitions, and peak operational periods. Sensitivity analyses will evaluate how variations in supervisory strategies—such as shift scheduling algorithms or workspace redesign protocols—impact team performance metrics and operational efficiency. By incorporating anonymized organizational data from industry partners, the models will account for sector-specific constraints while maintaining generalizability across office environments. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for evaluating management interventions, prescriptive analytics for space utilization optimization, and adaptable templates for crisis response planning. This research will advance computational social science methodologies in business administration while delivering practical decision-support systems that bridge theoretical management principles with operational realities. The scalability of the developed framework through HPC resources ensures applicability to both small business offices and large corporate divisions, with potential extensions to hybrid work ecosystems. Results will inform curriculum development in office management education and provide empirical foundations for next-generation supervisory training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and manage the operations and personnel of business offices and management-level divisions. Includes instruction in employee supervision, management, and labor relations; budgeting; scheduling and coordination; office systems operation and maintenance; office records management, organization, and security; office facilities design and space management; preparation and evaluation of business management data; and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for scalable, secure, and efficient software solutions in data-intensive environments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current software development practices struggle to optimize performance for large-scale datasets while maintaining robust security protocols, particularly in distributed systems. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study focused on developing and benchmarking parallelized algorithms for real-time data encryption, dynamic resource allocation in cloud-based environments, and machine learning-driven software testing frameworks. The research will employ distributed computing models to simulate multi-node systems, using MPI and CUDA frameworks to parallelize encryption processes and automate security vulnerability detection. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on HPC clusters to identify edge cases in software testing scenarios by synthesizing complex input patterns. The computational workload necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning tasks and high-memory nodes for processing terabyte-scale datasets representative of modern IoT networks and cloud infrastructures. Expected outcomes include optimized algorithms for AES-256 and post-quantum encryption schemes with demonstrated scalability, an open-source framework for adaptive resource allocation in containerized environments, and AI-generated test suites that improve code coverage by 30-40% compared to conventional methods. These results will directly benefit industries relying on secure, high-throughput software systems, such as healthcare informatics and financial technologies, while advancing pedagogical resources for parallel programming and secure software design in academic curricula. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving statistically significant benchmarks across diverse hardware configurations and for validating the proposed methods against industry-standard performance metrics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in developing, implementing, and evaluating computer software and program applications. Includes instruction in computer programming, programming languages, databases, user interfaces, networking and warehousing, encryption and security, software testing and evaluation, and customization.

abstract: Critical care nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to manage patients with life-threatening conditions, yet current methods for analyzing complex, high-dimensional clinical data remain limited. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that optimize real-time clinical decision support in critical care settings. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records (EHRs), continuous vital sign monitoring, and laboratory results—to identify early warning signals of clinical deterioration, predict patient-specific responses to interventions, and model the efficacy of treatment protocols under varying physiological conditions. Current computational tools struggle to process these datasets at scale, particularly when analyzing time-sensitive, multimodal data in dynamic ICU environments. To address this, the project will employ machine learning (ML) algorithms, such as ensemble models and deep neural networks, to identify patterns in retrospective EHR data from adult, neonatal, and pediatric ICUs. Parallel computing will enable large-scale parameter optimization for these models, while agent-based simulations will test hypothetical clinical scenarios, such as sepsis progression or ventilator weaning protocols. The HPC infrastructure will also support real-time data processing pipelines to validate models against prospective ICU data. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for early detection of complications (e.g., acute respiratory failure, septic shock) and evidence-based recommendations for personalized intervention thresholds. By enhancing the precision and speed of clinical assessments, this work aims to reduce preventable mortality, shorten ICU stays, and improve resource allocation in critical care units. The computational frameworks developed will be scalable to diverse healthcare systems, offering a template for data-driven innovation in nursing practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide specialized care to patients with life-threatening problems, including those in intensive care facilities and on life support. Includes instruction in adult, neonatal, and pediatric critical care; technical skills; patient monitoring and assessment; normal and abnormal readings; and troubleshooting.

abstract: Periodontal diseases, characterized by dysbiotic microbial communities and host inflammatory responses, present complex etiologies influenced by genetic, environmental, and biomechanical factors. Traditional analytical approaches often fail to integrate multi-omics datasets (e.g., metagenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) with biomechanical simulations of occlusal forces and implant loading, limiting predictive models for disease progression or implant failure. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multiscale computational framework for simulating periodontal and peri-implant tissue responses under diverse clinical scenarios. The research will combine three computational approaches: (1) finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distribution in periodontal tissues and implant-bone interfaces under dynamic loading conditions, (2) agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate host-microbiome interactions and immune cell dynamics in gingival tissues, and (3) machine learning (ML) pipelines to analyze longitudinal clinical data paired with multi-omics profiles from a 500-patient cohort. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large-scale FEA simulations (10,000+ parameter combinations), real-time ABM of 3D tissue microenvironments at cellular resolution, and training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (>50 TB). Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk biomechanical-immune signatures for periodontitis recurrence, optimized implant design parameters based on patient-specific bone density and occlusion patterns, and biomarkers for early detection of peri-implantitis. These computational tools will address critical gaps in personalized treatment planning and preventive strategies, directly supporting translational goals in periodontal care. The proposed work requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for ML tasks, high-memory nodes for ABM/FEA integration, and scalable storage for multi-institutional data harmonization. By bridging computational biomechanics with systems biology, this project aims to establish a novel paradigm for data-driven decision-making in periodontology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth, and in the placement and maintenance of dental implants.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize vehicle emission inspection protocols and improve diagnostic accuracy for aging emission control systems. Current inspection methods rely heavily on standardized test cycles and static thresholds, which inadequately capture real-world emission variability, especially in older vehicles with deteriorating components. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale interactions between engine performance, exhaust aftertreatment systems, and sensor outputs under diverse operating conditions. A hybrid approach will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of catalytic converter efficiency, machine learning algorithms trained on historical inspection data, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in fault detection. The CFD models will resolve spatially resolved chemical reactions within catalytic substrates, while recurrent neural networks will correlate transient sensor patterns (e.g., O2 sensor waveforms) with specific emission system failures. By parallelizing these computations across thousands of scenarios, we aim to establish dynamic, vehicle-specific emission thresholds that account for component wear and environmental factors. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool for inspection stations to prioritize high-risk vehicles, reducing false pass/fail rates by an estimated 40%. Additionally, the simulations will inform technician training modules by visualizing failure progression in virtual emission systems. This work directly supports regulatory compliance with evolving emission standards and reduces the environmental health burden of undetected high emitters. The computational demands—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated CFD solvers and distributed training of deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve practical runtime for operational deployment.
cip_title: Vehicle Emissions Inspection and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to test, repair, service, and maintain vehicle emission systems in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interconnected cultural narratives of African diasporas through large-scale, multilingual textual and audiovisual datasets. Current research on diasporic cultural memory often relies on fragmented or regionally siloed sources, limiting comprehensive insights into transnational influences and identity preservation. Our interdisciplinary approach integrates computational text analysis, network modeling, and geospatial visualization to map the evolution of shared narratives across digitized archives, oral histories, and contemporary media from diasporic communities in the Americas, Europe, and the Indian Ocean region. The primary challenge lies in processing heterogeneous, unstructured data—including Creole, Swahili, Portuguese, and French texts, as well as transcribed oral traditions—while identifying semantic and thematic linkages at scale. Using NLP tools optimized for low-resource languages and transformer-based models fine-tuned on African linguistic contexts, we will extract entities, sentiments, and narrative motifs. Graph-based algorithms will then model the diffusion of cultural themes over time and space, requiring iterative computation of dynamic networks with millions of nodes. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing these workflows, reducing processing times for terabyte-scale datasets from months to days, and enabling hyperparameter tuning for language-specific models. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas of diasporic narrative networks, methodological frameworks for under-resourced language analysis in cultural studies, and new insights into how digital preservation can combat the erasure of hybrid identities. This work directly supports the African Studies mission of centering diaspora perspectives in cultural scholarship while providing scalable computational tools for future research on transnational heritage. By clarifying how shared stories sustain community cohesion across geographic and generational divides, the project aims to inform cultural revitalization initiatives and policy discussions on inclusive archival practices.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara, and including the African diasporas overseas.

abstract: Critically ill adult and gerontology patients in intensive care units (ICUs) face high risks of mortality and long-term morbidity due to the complex interplay of age-related physiological decline, multi-organ dysfunction, and heterogeneous treatment responses. Existing risk stratification tools often lack the granularity to model dynamic, high-dimensional clinical data streams—such as real-time vital signs, electronic health records (EHRs), and multimodal biomarker trends—limiting their predictive accuracy for individualized outcomes. This project proposes to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models capable of integrating these diverse data sources to predict critical events, including sepsis progression, delirium onset, and 30-day mortality, with higher precision than current clinical standards. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the computational demands of processing terabytes of EHR data, training deep neural networks on temporal sequences, and conducting large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Key computational steps include federated learning across multi-institutional datasets to enhance generalizability, Bayesian hierarchical modeling to account for patient-specific covariates, and simulation of physiological trajectories using differential equations. The anticipated outcomes include open-source predictive algorithms validated against retrospective ICU datasets, with prospective pilot testing planned in Year 2. Successful implementation will provide clinicians with real-time decision-support tools to prioritize high-risk patients, tailor interventions to geriatric vulnerabilities, and reduce avoidable complications. By addressing the computational bottlenecks inherent in multimodal critical care analytics, this work aims to advance precision medicine in a resource-constrained clinical environment, directly aligning with national priorities to improve outcomes for aging critically ill populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Critical Care

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate advanced computational models to optimize energy system performance and integration of renewable energy sources in complex industrial and urban environments. The research addresses a critical gap in energy systems technology: the lack of high-fidelity, scalable tools to simulate dynamic interactions between legacy infrastructure, renewable generation, and energy storage systems under real-world constraints. Current analytical methods often oversimplify multi-physical couplings (e.g., thermal-electrical-mechanical behaviors) and fail to account for transient operational patterns, leading to suboptimal efficiency gains. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining physics-based simulations with machine learning (ML) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallelization of 3D computational fluid dynamics models for thermal system analysis, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic energy demand forecasting, and neural network training using multi-year smart grid datasets. Key objectives include quantifying energy loss mechanisms in heterogeneous systems, optimizing dispatch strategies for hybrid renewable microgrids, and developing adaptive control algorithms for demand response scenarios. The computational workflow will integrate open-source tools (OpenFOAM, TensorFlow) with custom Python-based optimization routines leveraging MPI and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include validated digital twins of campus-scale energy systems, generalized performance benchmarks for retrofit technologies, and predictive maintenance protocols to reduce downtime in critical infrastructure. By providing open-access models and datasets, this work will directly support regional efforts to decarbonize industrial energy use while advancing curriculum development in energy systems analytics. The requested HPC allocation is essential for handling petabyte-scale sensor data streams and achieving the necessary temporal-spatial resolution in multi-domain simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing energy-efficient systems or monitoring energy use. Includes instruction in principles of energy conservation, instrumentation calibration, monitoring systems and test procedures, energy loss inspection procedures, energy conservation techniques, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance next-generation signature management capabilities for military platforms through high-fidelity computational modeling of multi-spectral low-observable (LO) phenomena. Current stealth technologies face escalating challenges from distributed sensor networks, multi-static detection systems, and adaptive threat algorithms operating across electromagnetic (EM), acoustic, and infrared spectra. Existing design frameworks struggle to model complex interactions between radar-absorbing materials, structural acoustics, and thermal management systems under dynamic operational conditions. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-physics simulation environment leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve coupled EM-acoustic-thermal signatures at unprecedented resolution. The computational approach integrates finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for radar cross-section analysis, discontinuous Galerkin formulations for broadband acoustic scattering, and finite element models for anisotropic heat dissipation in composite materials. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize material layering configurations and surface topology patterns across conflicting performance requirements. The HPC implementation will enable parametric studies at scale, including Monte Carlo analyses of manufacturing tolerances and environmental degradation effects on signature persistence. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for hybrid LO material behavior, a digital twin framework for virtual prototyping of adaptive stealth systems, and quantitative trade-space analyses for multi-domain signature suppression. This work directly supports the development of survivable platforms in contested environments while advancing computational methods for multi-physics defense applications. Resource allocations will prioritize GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized wave propagation solvers and high-memory instances for large-scale optimization workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of electromagnetic field theory, electro-optics and materials science to the reduction of radar, optical and acoustic signatures of weapons systems. Includes instruction in computational electromagnetics, electro-optics, acoustics, guided wave theory, radiation capture, antenna applications in layered environments, material characterization, radar cross-section analysis, sonar signature analysis, non-destructive testing, remote sensing, and applications to specific weapons systems and operational environments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of sensory perception modeling in immersive culinary environments, a niche interdisciplinary domain intersecting gastronomy, cognitive science, and computational design. Traditional culinary research has focused on ingredient chemistry or nutritional outcomes, leaving a critical gap in understanding how multisensory stimuli—such as visual presentation, ambient sound, and contextual storytelling—collectively shape diners’ experiential and emotional responses. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to simulate and optimize hyper-realistic dining scenarios, enabling chefs and experiential designers to prototype sensory-driven menus or entertainment-based culinary services without costly physical trials. The computational approach integrates three core components: (1) agent-based modeling to simulate diner behavior and decision-making under variable sensory inputs, (2) machine learning algorithms trained on biometric datasets (e.g., eye-tracking, galvanic skin response) to correlate environmental factors with emotional engagement, and (3) fluid dynamics simulations to model the interaction of aroma dispersion with spatial design elements. These methods will be unified within a scalable, GPU-accelerated framework to handle the high-dimensional parameter space of real-world culinary environments. The project’s significance lies in its potential to establish a new paradigm for data-driven culinary innovation, reducing resource-intensive experimentation while enhancing personalized dining experiences. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for sensory scenario prototyping, validated through partnerships with experimental restaurants and immersive theater groups. By bridging computational rigor with creative culinary practices, this work aims to catalyze advancements in entertainment-driven gastronomy and expand the methodological toolkit for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of art, technology, and hospitality.
cip_title: Culinary, Entertainment, and Personal Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary, entertainment, and personal services not listed above.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive security protocols in dynamic, large-scale urban environments, where traditional static security measures often fail to address evolving threats. The core challenge lies in integrating real-time behavioral data, environmental variables, and threat prediction models to enable responsive security systems capable of adjusting to unpredictable scenarios. Current approaches lack the granularity to model complex human-environment interactions at city-wide scales, particularly under conditions of partial observability or rapidly shifting risks. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and reinforcement learning (RL) approach, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate millions of agent decisions across multi-layered urban networks. The computational model will incorporate anonymized mobility patterns, infrastructure interdependencies, and stochastic threat generators to test resilience against cascading security failures. Key technical innovations include the development of a graph neural network architecture to predict emergent crowd behaviors and a parallelized optimization engine for evaluating countermeasure efficacy across simulated scenarios. By coupling these components through distributed computing workflows, the framework aims to identify latent vulnerabilities in existing security configurations while proposing dynamic resource allocation strategies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible benchmark dataset of simulated threat-response scenarios and open-source tools for adaptive security planning. This work bridges computational social dynamics with security operations, offering a novel paradigm for proactive risk mitigation in complex human-centric systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and temporal resolution in simulations, enabling validation against real-world incident datasets from partner security agencies.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: Clinical cytogenetics research is critical for diagnosing genetic disorders, guiding cancer treatment, and improving transplant compatibility, yet current analytical workflows face limitations in processing increasingly complex, high-dimensional datasets. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address bottlenecks in integrating multi-omics cytogenetic data—including karyotyping, FISH, whole-genome sequencing, and high-resolution photomicrography—with clinical outcomes. The primary research problem lies in resolving ambiguities in structural chromosomal variations and low-frequency somatic mosaicism, which contribute to diagnostic uncertainty in leukemias, solid tumors, and congenital disorders. Traditional cytogenetic analysis struggles to reconcile conflicting findings across assays or detect subtle abnormalities at scale, particularly when handling terabyte-scale imaging data and population-level genomic repositories. Our computational approach combines GPU-accelerated deep learning for automated anomaly detection in photomicrographs with distributed-memory frameworks for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of structural variants. Custom pipelines will align multi-modal data using graph-based genomes, while Monte Carlo simulations model the statistical significance of rare cytogenetic events in transplant rejection scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated workflow for identifying cryptic chromosomal rearrangements with <1% mosaicism in hematologic malignancies, 2) predictive models linking specific aneuploidy patterns to post-transplant immunosuppression requirements, and 3) open-source tools for real-time FISH signal quantification during time-lapse cytogenetic monitoring. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing of 50,000+ whole-genome equivalents from collaborating clinical centers, reduce turnaround times for complex cases by 40-60%, and support training of neural networks on >100,000 annotated metaphase spreads. This work directly addresses NIH priorities for computational pathology innovation, with potential to redefine diagnostic standards in 15+ cancer types and improve genetic risk stratification for organ transplant recipients.
cip_definition: The clinical research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex legal and regulatory frameworks governing urban real estate development, with a focus on simulating the cascading impacts of zoning law variations, environmental compliance mandates, and municipal code enforcement patterns. The study addresses a critical gap in computational legal analysis by modeling how localized legal constraints interact with large-scale land development strategies, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and natural language processing (NLP), the project will process structured legal datasets (e.g., zoning ordinances, case law, permitting records) and unstructured text from municipal codes across 15 U.S. jurisdictions to identify latent conflicts between land use policies and development feasibility. Computational workflows will simulate development scenarios under evolving regulatory conditions, quantifying delays, costs, and litigation risks arising from jurisdictional inconsistencies. A custom-built legal decision tree algorithm will map precedent-driven outcomes in eminent domain disputes and environmental review challenges, integrating historical court rulings with geospatial land parcel data. The HPC environment is essential for parallel processing multi-terabyte legal corpora and running Monte Carlo simulations to assess policy impacts across heterogeneous urban landscapes. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to evaluate regulatory trade-offs in development planning, tools for automating compliance risk assessments, and visualizations of policy-driven market distortions. By bridging computational modeling and legal analysis, this work aims to advance evidence-based policymaking in land use law while establishing scalable methods for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of legal theory, urban economics, and data science.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive mechanisms underlying dynamic decision-making in uncertain environments using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral datasets. A core challenge in experimental psychology lies in disentangling how individuals integrate probabilistic feedback, adjust strategies over time, and exhibit inter-individual variability in adaptive learning. Traditional behavioral methods lack the granularity to model nonlinear interactions between cognitive parameters (e.g., learning rates, exploration-exploitation trade-offs) and task dynamics. To address this, we propose a hierarchical Bayesian framework coupled with reinforcement learning (RL) models to simulate and analyze decision trajectories across parametrically varied uncertainty conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) Parallelized parameter estimation across 10,000+ synthetic and empirical trial sequences, (2) Comparative model evidence calculations using nested Monte Carlo sampling for 15 competing cognitive architectures, and (3) Population-level hierarchical inference to quantify individual differences in cognitive flexibility. The empirical dataset comprises behavioral responses from N = 300 participants completing a novel multi-stage decision task with shifting reward contingencies, generating ~4.5 million data points. Without HPC, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for model comparison would exceed 6 months of computation time due to high-dimensional parameter spaces and cross-validated likelihood evaluations. Expected outcomes include identifying latent cognitive profiles predictive of adaptation speed, validating a computational account of uncertainty-driven strategy switching, and releasing open-source tools for efficient RL model fitting in psychology. This work advances methodological capabilities for studying complex decision processes while providing theoretical insights into how humans navigate volatile environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in research and experimental psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical pathology laboratories generate vast, heterogeneous datasets from diverse diagnostic modalities, including genomic sequencing, mass spectrometry, and digital pathology. Integrating these data to improve diagnostic accuracy and uncover novel disease biomarkers remains a critical challenge due to the computational complexity of multi-omics integration, high dimensionality, and the need for real-time analysis in clinical workflows. This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable predictive modeling of disease states using multi-modal clinical laboratory data. The research will focus on integrating genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets from patients with sepsis—a condition requiring rapid diagnosis—to identify predictive signatures of pathogen type, host response, and treatment resistance. Computational methods will include parallelized Bayesian network inference to model molecular interactions, GPU-accelerated deep learning for time-series analysis of longitudinal lab data, and ensemble clustering algorithms to stratify patient subgroups. HPC resources will be essential for processing terabytes of raw mass spectrometry data, training neural networks on whole-slide pathology images, and running millions of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) iterations for probabilistic modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for real-time integration of clinical laboratory data streams, (2) novel prognostic biomarkers for sepsis progression, and (3) open-source tools optimized for distributed memory architectures to facilitate reproducible analyses. This work will directly address bottlenecks in translating complex laboratory data into actionable clinical insights, with potential applications in personalized antimicrobial stewardship and automated diagnostic decision support. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to advance computational methods in clinical pathology while maintaining rigorous standards for interpretability and regulatory compliance required in medical diagnostics.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease. Includes instruction in performing clinical chemistry, cytogenetics, immunology, laboratory management, microbiology, molecular biology, quality control, serology, toxicology, and virology.

abstract: Pediatric hematologic malignancies, such as leukemia and lymphoma, exhibit marked molecular heterogeneity that drives variable treatment responses and long-term outcomes. While genomic and transcriptomic profiling has advanced risk stratification, integrating multi-omics data with clinical variables to predict relapse or optimize therapy remains computationally prohibitive for most research groups. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of treatment resistance and clonal evolution in pediatric blood cancers. We will analyze whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, and epigenetic datasets from two multi-institutional cohorts: a retrospective group of 800 patients with relapsed/refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and a prospective cohort of 120 newly diagnosed lymphoma patients. Computational workflows will include dimensionality reduction techniques for multi-omics integration, Bayesian network models to map clonal dynamics during treatment, and deep learning architectures to identify high-risk molecular signatures masked by tumor microenvironment interactions. The scale of data—particularly single-cell resolution datasets exceeding 500 TB—necessitates parallelized processing across GPU-accelerated nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for tracking minimal residual disease evolution, (2) predictive biomarkers for early relapse in ALL subgroups with currently ambiguous risk classifications, and (3) in silico simulations of combination therapies targeting adaptive resistance mechanisms. These results will directly inform two ongoing clinical trials (NCT04543422, NCT05218903) testing risk-adapted treatment de-escalation. By enabling real-time analysis of complex molecular trajectories, this HPC-supported approach aims to reduce computational bottlenecks that currently delay translational insights. The proposed models and pipelines will be shared via public repositories to advance precision medicine capabilities across pediatric oncology.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Hematology-Oncology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize computational models for improving decision-making in office management systems. Modern office environments face complex challenges in resource allocation, workforce scheduling, and operational efficiency, particularly as hybrid work models and dynamic labor demands introduce nonlinear variables. Traditional analytical tools often fail to account for the interdependencies between human behavior, spatial logistics, and real-time workflow adjustments. To address this gap, we propose a simulation-driven approach using agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES) to analyze office operations under diverse scenarios. These models will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including employee performance metrics, office layout schematics, and equipment utilization logs, to quantify trade-offs in supervisory strategies. The computational intensity of running thousands of parallel simulations—varying parameters such as staffing levels, task prioritization protocols, and emergency disruption responses—necessitates HPC capabilities. Machine learning algorithms will further refine these models by identifying patterns in simulation outputs, enabling predictive recommendations for office managers. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating office management policies, validated against real-world case studies from corporate partners. This research will contribute novel methodologies to the field of business administration by bridging computational analytics with office supervision practices, offering actionable insights for reducing operational latency, minimizing resource waste, and enhancing employee productivity. The project’s computational demands—particularly its need for multi-node processing, large memory allocation, and rapid data I/O—highlight the necessity of HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust results within feasible timeframes. Findings will be disseminated through open-source toolkits tailored for office management training programs, ensuring broader academic and industry impact.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and manage the operations and personnel of business offices and management-level divisions. Includes instruction in employee supervision, management, and labor relations; budgeting; scheduling and coordination; office systems operation and maintenance; office records management, organization, and security; office facilities design and space management; preparation and evaluation of business management data; and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for enhancing precision in anatomical modeling and diagnostic visualization by integrating multi-modal medical imaging data with patient-specific genomic and proteomic profiles. Current approaches to medical illustration often rely on static, population-averaged anatomical templates, limiting their utility in personalized treatment planning for complex conditions such as congenital anomalies or post-oncological reconstruction. The research problem centers on the computational challenges of dynamically reconciling high-resolution imaging data (e.g., 4D MRI, micro-CT) with heterogeneous molecular datasets to generate patient-adaptive 3D anatomical models. The proposed solution leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid pipeline combining geometric deep learning for feature extraction from imaging data, Bayesian networks for probabilistic integration of multi-omics data, and real-time physically based rendering techniques. Key computational challenges include processing petascale voxel datasets, optimizing memory-intensive tensor operations for neural network training on irregular anatomical meshes, and parallelizing radiative transfer simulations for photorealistic tissue visualization. The workflow will be validated using a cohort of 200 patients with craniofacial abnormalities, correlating model predictions with surgical outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source platform for multi-scale anatomical modeling, novel metrics for quantifying spatial concordance between molecular markers and phenotypic manifestations, and GPU-accelerated visualization modules for clinical decision support. This work bridges gaps between computational anatomy, biomedical informatics, and visual computing, with potential applications in surgical simulation, medical education, and biomarker discovery. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-distributed processing of whole-body scans, maintaining submillimeter spatial fidelity across imaging modalities, and achieving interactive frame rates during volumetric rendering of complex tissue interfaces.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in medical illustration and informatics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Veterinary internal medicine faces significant challenges in diagnosing and managing complex, multifactorial diseases in animals, where heterogeneous clinical presentations, diverse species-specific physiologies, and limited validated biomarkers hinder timely interventions. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework to analyze multi-modal clinical, genomic, and environmental datasets, enabling precision diagnostics and predictive modeling of disease outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale electronic health records (EHRs) from companion and livestock animals, integrating genomic data (whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomics) with real-time sensor data (wearables, IoT-enabled vitals monitoring) and owner-reported behavioral metrics. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to identify subphenotypes of chronic conditions such as feline chronic kidney disease, canine diabetes mellitus, and equine metabolic syndrome. These models will account for interspecies variability, age-related pathophysiological changes, and comorbidity patterns. A parallel computational pipeline will simulate host-pathogen-environment interactions in infectious diseases with zoonotic potential, using agent-based modeling to optimize outbreak response protocols. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabyte-scale datasets, enabling rapid hyperparameter optimization, and supporting computationally intensive tasks such as 3D molecular dynamics simulations of drug-protein interactions across species. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early disease detection, decision-support tools for treatment personalization, and open-access repositories of species-specific biomarker libraries. By advancing computational methods tailored to veterinary medicine, this work aims to bridge translational gaps between human and animal health research, improve clinical outcomes in diverse species, and strengthen capacity for One Health initiatives.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of general medical services to animals with a wide range of non-surgical clinical problems. May included related research in behavioral aspects of diseases, animal diagnosis, animal aging, and referral procedures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of acute care management in adult and geriatric populations demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in rapid clinical decision-making and personalized treatment optimization. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for clinical deterioration and therapeutic outcomes in critically ill adults and older adults with multimorbidity. The research problem centers on the limitations of existing risk stratification tools, which often fail to integrate real-time multimodal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), continuous physiological monitoring, and genomic biomarkers—into dynamic, patient-specific predictions. Current methods also struggle to account for age-related physiological variability and drug-drug interactions in geriatric populations. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models for temporal EHR analysis) and agent-based simulations of pharmacodynamic responses. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data streams from 10,000+ retrospective cases across three tertiary care centers, as well as real-time validation in a prospective cohort of 500 patients. Key computational challenges include optimizing federated learning approaches to maintain data privacy across institutions and scaling Monte Carlo simulations to model stochastic outcomes in polypharmacy scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive algorithm for sepsis progression and organ failure in older adults, (2) a decision-support tool for dose optimization in acute kidney injury populations, and (3) open-source code for reproducible clinical simulation workflows. This work will directly inform time-sensitive interventions in critical care settings while advancing methods for computational gerontology. The requested resources—particularly GPU nodes for model training and high-memory nodes for large-scale genomic-EHR integration—are essential given the project’s 18-month timeline and the need for hourly model retraining using live ICU data streams. By bridging acute care medicine with computational innovation, this research aims to reduce preventable complications in vulnerable populations and establish a template for HPC-driven clinical discovery.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Acute Care

abstract: The customization of ophthalmic lenses remains constrained by traditional methods that inadequately account for the complex anatomical and optical variations among patients. Current approaches to lens design and fitting rely on generalized models, which often lead to suboptimal visual outcomes, prolonged adaptation periods, and patient discomfort. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that simulate the interaction between personalized lens designs and individual ocular anatomy. The research will focus on integrating high-resolution 3D imaging data, dynamic tear film behavior, and biomechanical properties of ocular tissues to optimize lens parameters such as curvature, thickness, and material composition. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to analyze large datasets of patient-specific measurements, including corneal topography, pupillary distance, and blink patterns, to predict optimal lens configurations. Computational fluid dynamics and finite element analysis will model the mechanical and optical performance of lenses under real-world conditions, such as eye movement and environmental stressors. By utilizing HPC capabilities, these resource-intensive simulations will be scaled to evaluate thousands of design iterations rapidly, enabling precise customization. The expected outcomes include a novel framework for designing patient-specific lenses that minimize adaptation time, enhance visual acuity, and reduce complications such as dry eye syndrome. This work will also generate open-access datasets and computational tools to support further innovation in ophthalmic dispensing. Successful implementation of this project has the potential to advance evidence-based practices in opticianry, improve clinical outcomes, and reduce costs associated with trial-and-error fitting processes. Additionally, the integration of computational methods into opticianry education will prepare future practitioners to adopt data-driven approaches in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize dynamic decision-making processes in casino operations, focusing on the integration of real-time data analytics and probabilistic modeling to enhance gaming floor efficiency and security. The research addresses a critical gap in operational strategies for casinos, where traditional heuristic methods often fail to adapt to complex, variable environments such as fluctuating patron behavior, game demand patterns, and security threat detection. By developing computational models that simulate high-dimensional scenarios—including player traffic, dealer performance, and surveillance system responsiveness—the project aims to create adaptive frameworks for resource allocation, staff scheduling, and anomaly detection. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and deep learning architectures to process large-scale datasets from casino management systems, surveillance feeds, and historical gaming records. Key challenges include scaling neural networks for real-time video analysis of surveillance streams to identify irregular behaviors and optimizing parallelized simulations to predict optimal table game configurations under varying demand. The expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for probabilistic risk assessment in gaming operations, a predictive model for minimizing service bottlenecks, and a novel anomaly detection algorithm tailored to casino environments. These outputs will provide actionable insights for reducing operational costs, improving regulatory compliance, and mitigating fraud risks. The project’s interdisciplinary nature bridges computational social science, operations research, and ethical AI applications, offering a template for data-driven decision-making in hospitality industries while adhering to jurisdictional gaming laws. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC-enabled analytics can address niche, high-stakes challenges in non-traditional STEM domains, fostering innovation in service industries with complex human-technological interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on casino operations and services. Includes instruction in casino operations, casino security and surveillance, casino dealing, principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in optimizing blood component storage and transfusion outcomes through advanced computational modeling of cellular degradation and immunomodulatory dynamics. Despite standardized protocols, variability in storage-related damage to red blood cells (RBCs), platelets, and stem cells remains poorly understood, contributing to adverse reactions and suboptimal therapeutic efficacy in transfusion and transplantation. Current experimental models struggle to capture the multi-scale complexity of biochemical and biophysical interactions during storage, limiting predictive capabilities. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach integrating molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning, and multi-omics data fusion to model temporal changes in blood components under diverse storage conditions. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize membrane protein behavior and oxidative stress responses in RBCs at near-atomic resolution, while neural networks trained on longitudinal metabolomic, proteomic, and transcriptomic datasets from banked blood samples will identify degradation biomarkers. Agent-based models will simulate platelet activation cascades influenced by storage solution additives and temperature fluctuations. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro hemolysis assays, flow cytometry, and clinical outcomes data from transfused patients. By leveraging GPU-accelerated clusters for large-scale parameter space exploration, this work aims to establish predictive frameworks for component shelf-life optimization and personalized transfusion matching. Anticipated outcomes include evidence-based guidelines for storage protocol refinements, reduced wastage through expiration prediction tools, and risk stratification models for transfusion-related complications. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing petabyte-scale simulations and enabling real-time analysis of heterogeneous clinical datasets, ultimately advancing the safety and precision of blood banking practices.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for the maintenance of an adequate blood supply, blood donor and patient-recipient safety, and appropriate blood utilization. Includes directing the preparation and safe use of specially prepared blood components, including red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and plasma constituents, and marrow or stem cells for transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and demographic dynamics of African-American communities in the United States and the Caribbean during the Reconstruction era (1865–1877). Traditional historical methods face challenges in systematically reconstructing migration patterns, land ownership shifts, and community networks across fragmented archival sources, including census records, Freedmen’s Bureau documents, and regional land deeds. This research aims to integrate these dispersed datasets into a unified geospatial-temporal framework, employing computational methods to model population movements, economic transitions, and social resilience strategies among newly emancipated Black communities. Key objectives include mapping migration corridors using agent-based modeling, quantifying changes in land tenure through statistical clustering algorithms, and analyzing kinship networks via graph theory. The scale and complexity of these tasks—particularly the processing of unstructured textual data, geocoding historical locations, and simulating population interactions—require HPC capabilities for parallelized data processing, large-scale simulations, and machine learning-driven pattern recognition. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously understudied migration pathways, the visualization of community formation processes in contested post-emancipation landscapes, and the development of an open-access digital repository for interdisciplinary scholarship. By computationally bridging gaps in the archival record, this project will advance understanding of how African-American communities navigated structural inequities to establish autonomous institutions, shaping long-term cultural and political legacies. The findings will contribute to public history initiatives and K-12 curricula, emphasizing data-driven narratives of Black agency during Reconstruction. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s terabyte-scale datasets and ensuring reproducibility of complex spatial-historical analyses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized meal planning for individuals with complex dietary needs, a critical challenge in dietetics practice. Current manual methods for creating nutritionally balanced, culturally appropriate, and preference-aligned meal plans are time-intensive and often fail to account for multidimensional constraints such as medical requirements, ingredient availability, cost fluctuations, and sustainability metrics. We propose to address these limitations through large-scale data integration and algorithmic optimization using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will aggregate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, nutrient databases, regional food cost data, and patient-reported preferences, into a unified graph-based model. Machine learning techniques will identify patterns in dietary adherence and health outcomes, while mixed-integer linear programming will generate optimized meal plans under dynamic constraints. A key innovation involves simulating population-scale dietary scenarios to model the impact of socioeconomic variables on nutrition accessibility. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the combinatorial complexity of optimizing thousands of ingredient combinations across multiple objective functions and the need for real-time adaptation in clinical workflows. Expected outcomes include an open-source meal planning toolkit that enables dietitians to rapidly prototype and evaluate meal plans while maintaining compliance with evolving dietary guidelines. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of clinical outcomes data and prospective simulations comparing algorithm-generated plans with expert-designed regimens. This work bridges computational nutrition and clinical practice, offering scalable solutions to improve dietary interventions for populations with chronic diseases, food allergies, and socioeconomic barriers to nutrition security. The requested computing resources will directly support advancements in precision nutrition and expand the evidence base for data-driven dietetic decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to simulate and analyze the effectiveness of pedagogical strategies for secondary education classrooms, with a focus on personalized instruction and classroom management. A critical challenge in teacher preparation is the limited opportunity for pre-service teachers to practice nuanced decision-making in dynamic, diverse classroom environments. Existing training tools often lack the capacity to model complex student interactions or adapt to varied learning contexts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build large-scale, agent-based simulations that replicate heterogeneous secondary classrooms. These simulations will integrate real-world data from classroom observations, student performance metrics, and demographic records to generate adaptive scenarios reflecting diverse learner needs. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to evaluate how different instructional approaches—such as differentiated scaffolding or behavior intervention sequences—affect simulated student engagement and academic outcomes. The computational intensity of training these models, particularly when processing high-dimensional data from thousands of simulated classroom interactions, necessitates parallelized computing architectures. Expected outcomes include 1) a framework for predicting the efficacy of pedagogical strategies under varying classroom conditions, 2) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing teacher training simulations, and 3) open-source tools to help educator preparation programs implement these models. By quantifying relationships between teaching practices and student outcomes in simulated environments, this work aims to provide empirically grounded insights that complement traditional teacher training methods. The requested HPC resources will enable the iterative refinement of models at a scale unachievable with standard computing infrastructure, directly supporting the development of more effective, data-informed approaches to secondary teacher education.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the secondary grades, which may include grades seven through twelve, depending on the school system or state regulations. May include preparation to teach a comprehensive curriculum or specific subject matter.

abstract: Pediatric urology faces significant challenges in managing congenital and acquired genitourinary tract anomalies, where anatomical variability and dynamic growth complicate treatment optimization. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols, often lacking patient-specific predictive tools to anticipate surgical outcomes or long-term functional risks. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework integrating patient-specific anatomical modeling, biomechanical simulations, and machine learning to predict postoperative outcomes in complex pediatric urologic conditions, such as bladder exstrophy and obstructive uropathies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the multi-scale, multi-modal datasets involved, including high-resolution imaging, urodynamic studies, and longitudinal clinical records. Anatomical models derived from MRI/CT scans will undergo finite element analysis to simulate tissue mechanics and urinary flow dynamics under surgical correction scenarios. Concurrently, machine learning models will analyze clinical datasets to identify biomarkers predictive of complications, such as renal dysfunction or incontinence. The integration of these approaches requires large-scale parallel processing for iterative simulation refinements and training of predictive algorithms on heterogeneous data. By leveraging HPC, this project aims to establish a platform for virtual surgical planning and risk stratification, enabling personalized intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for postoperative bladder compliance, urinary flow rates, and renal functional preservation, which will be tested against retrospective clinical data and prospectively validated in a pilot cohort. This work has the potential to transform clinical practice by reducing revision surgeries, optimizing resource allocation, and improving quality of life for pediatric patients. The computational pipelines developed will also be shared as open-source tools to advance collaborative research in pediatric urology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals in the study, prevention, and management of congenital, childhood-acquired, and overlapping adolescent anomalies of the genitourinary tract, including problems, diseases, tumors, and traumas.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to optimize hazardous materials (hazmat) risk assessment and emergency response planning through advanced data analytics and simulation. Current hazmat management systems face challenges in synthesizing real-time environmental data, regulatory constraints, and human behavioral factors, leading to suboptimal risk mitigation strategies. To address this gap, the research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-modal datasets—including geospatial hazard maps, sensor networks, incident reports, and economic activity logs—and simulate dynamic hazmat dispersal scenarios. A hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling approach will be implemented to predict material behavior under varying environmental conditions (e.g., temperature, airflow) and model stakeholder decision-making during emergencies. The computational workflow will prioritize parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in contamination spread and evaluate the efficacy of containment protocols. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of recommending context-specific evacuation routes, resource allocation strategies, and regulatory compliance pathways. By integrating human behavior patterns and economic impact projections into risk models, this work aims to reduce response latency during hazmat incidents while balancing mitigation costs. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of regional-scale simulations and achieving near-real-time analysis for emergency applications. Results will be validated against historical incident data and disseminated through an open-access platform designed for local emergency management agencies. This research directly aligns with the program’s focus on information systems applications in hazmat management, advancing computational methodologies at the intersection of environmental health, systems engineering, and public safety.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing, monitoring, and enforcing hazardous materials management and removal. Includes instruction in environmental science, environmental health, human behavior, economics, management science, information systems and applications, and communication skills.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into veterinary dentistry remains limited, despite the growing complexity of diagnostic and treatment challenges posed by diverse animal species. Current approaches to analyzing oral biomechanics, disease progression, and treatment efficacy often rely on generalized models or low-resolution imaging, which fail to account for species-specific anatomical variations and dynamic physiological processes. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing high-fidelity computational models of animal oral structures using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) constructing 3D finite element models from micro-CT and MRI datasets to simulate biomechanical stress distributions during mastication in companion animals and exotic species; (2) applying computational fluid dynamics to map oral cavity environments and microbial biofilm formation under varying dietary and pathological conditions; and (3) training machine learning algorithms on multi-species dental radiographs to automate the detection of periodontal disease and enamel defects. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale imaging data, iterative simulation of biomechanical interactions, and optimization of deep neural networks—workflows that demand the memory, storage, and GPU capabilities of HPC infrastructure. The outcomes will yield species-specific insights into oral biomechanics, predictive tools for early disease identification, and evidence-based frameworks for evaluating dental materials and surgical interventions. By enabling the first large-scale, cross-species computational analysis in veterinary dentistry, this project will advance precision care strategies, reduce invasive diagnostic procedures, and establish open-access simulation tools for the broader research community. The requested resources will directly support the generation of publishable datasets, with translational potential to improve clinical outcomes in both domestic and wildlife veterinary practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of dental care procedures to the teeth, eating surfaces, and oral cavities of animals. May included related research in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases and abnormalities of animal teeth and gums and related parts of the oral cavity; and related anatomical and physiological principles.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the long-time asymptotic behavior of solutions to high-dimensional nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in the study of infinite-dimensional dynamical systems. The research focuses on equations with non-local interactions and singular potentials, which pose significant analytical challenges due to the interplay between nonlinearities, unbounded domains, and weak regularity. A central objective is to characterize the stability and convergence properties of solutions under perturbations, a problem of fundamental importance in mathematical analysis with implications for models in quantum field theory and turbulence. To address these questions, we propose a computational framework combining adaptive wavelet discretization techniques with spectral methods to resolve multiscale features and singular structures efficiently. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for implementing parallelized algorithms that handle the exponential growth of degrees of freedom in high dimensions, particularly for matrix-free iterative solvers and large-scale eigenvalue computations. The wavelet-based approach will leverage harmonic analysis tools to decompose solution spaces, enabling localized error control and adaptive mesh refinement. Simulations will target systems with up to six spatial dimensions, requiring distributed-memory architectures for scalability. Expected outcomes include rigorous numerical evidence supporting conjectures about solution decay rates in Sobolev spaces, new insights into the role of symmetries in stabilizing dynamics, and the development of optimized wavelet bases for singular integral operators. Results will advance analytical methods for PDEs by bridging gaps between existence theory and quantitative behavior, while computational tools developed here will be disseminated as open-source software for the analysis community. This work aligns with the mathematical physics focus of the program, emphasizing foundational analysis rather than applied modeling. The requested resources will directly support parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and validation against emerging analytical techniques in variational calculus.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and behavior of equations, multivariate solutions, functions, and dynamic systems. Includes instruction in differential equations, variation, approximations, complex variables, integrals, harmonic analysis and wavelet theory, dynamic systems, and applications to mathematical physics.

abstract: Acute care medicine faces critical challenges in predicting patient deterioration and optimizing time-sensitive interventions, particularly in high-stakes environments such as intensive care units (ICUs) and emergency departments. Current predictive models for sepsis, acute respiratory failure, and multi-organ dysfunction lack the precision and generalizability required for real-world clinical deployment, often due to insufficient integration of high-dimensional clinical data and inadequate computational scalability. This project proposes the development of a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal ICU data—including high-frequency vital sign streams, laboratory results, imaging metadata, and unstructured clinical notes—to predict acute decompensation events and guide personalized treatment protocols. The computational approach will involve training ensemble models and transformer-based architectures on retrospective datasets spanning 50,000+ ICU admissions from five academic medical centers. Parallelized preprocessing pipelines will harmonize heterogeneous data formats, while distributed computing will enable hyperparameter optimization and cross-validation at scale. A federated learning component will address data privacy constraints by training localized models across institutions without raw data transfer. The project will further simulate real-time prediction workflows using GPU-accelerated inference to quantify latency requirements for clinical integration. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for sepsis onset (target AUC ≥0.92) and respiratory failure (target AUC ≥0.89) with interpretable feature attribution maps, alongside benchmarks for computational efficiency in acute care settings. By overcoming existing limitations in processing speed and model complexity, this work aims to establish an HPC-supported infrastructure for rapid, granular clinical decision support, directly addressing the National Institutes of Health’s priorities for scalable AI in critical care. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU node utilization for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale cohort analyses.
cip_definition: Research focused on Acute Care Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for modeling the dynamic interactions between urban green spaces, human behavior, and environmental sustainability. As urbanization intensifies, parks and recreational areas face competing demands: balancing ecological preservation, equitable access, and evolving public leisure preferences. Traditional planning tools struggle to integrate real-time behavioral data, ecological metrics, and predictive scenario analysis at scale. The research problem centers on creating a spatially explicit simulation platform to optimize park design, management policies, and visitor experience while addressing climate resilience. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) paired with machine learning, the project will simulate visitor movement patterns, vegetation growth under varying climate scenarios, and infrastructure wear-and-tear dynamics across heterogeneous urban landscapes. Computational workflows will integrate geospatial datasets (LiDAR, satellite imagery), anonymized mobile device mobility traces, and ecological sensor data to parameterize models. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to city-level resolution, enabling Monte Carlo analyses of intervention strategies (e.g., trail rerouting, canopy expansion) under stochastic weather events. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for park administrators to test "digital twin" scenarios, quantifying trade-offs between biodiversity conservation, visitor capacity, and operational costs. The work bridges computational social science, landscape ecology, and urban planning within the understudied domain of recreational infrastructure resilience. By advancing data-driven decision-making in parks management, this project aims to establish a methodological precedent for integrating HPC into leisure studies, with implications for public health outcomes and climate-adaptive urban design.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles underlying recreational and leisure activities, and the practices involved in providing indoor and outdoor recreational facilities and services for the general public.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized learning pathways for secondary students with disabilities in special education programs. A critical challenge in secondary special education is designing individualized education plans (IEPs) that effectively address diverse learning needs while aligning with academic, vocational, and transitional goals. Existing methods for predicting intervention outcomes or tailoring curriculum modifications remain largely qualitative and labor-intensive, limiting scalability. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal educational datasets—including academic performance records, behavioral assessments, and postsecondary transition outcomes—and simulate the efficacy of targeted instructional strategies. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns in student responses to interventions, while agent-based simulations will test hypothetical scenarios for optimizing classroom-level resource allocation. Computational experiments will focus on two domains: (1) predicting the impact of subject-specific accommodations (e.g., mathematics instruction modifications for students with dyscalculia) and (2) modeling the longitudinal effects of vocational training integration on post-school employment outcomes. The scale of data—spanning thousands of anonymized student records with high-dimensional temporal features—necessitates parallelized processing and large-scale parameter space exploration enabled by HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will include open-source tools for generating data-driven IEP recommendations and a simulation platform for educators to virtually assess intervention trade-offs. By bridging computational analytics and special education pedagogy, this work aims to provide teachers with scalable, evidence-based strategies to improve secondary learning experiences and postsecondary readiness for students with disabilities.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Secondary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the secondary grades.
