Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for secondary grades special education; content, methods, and modifications in specific subject areas; issues in vocational education; and promoting successful transitions to postsecondary settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing surgical outcomes and therapeutic precision for companion animals through advanced computational modeling. Despite advances in veterinary medicine, significant variability in patient responses to treatments—particularly in oncology, orthopedics, and complex soft tissue surgeries—remains poorly understood. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in their ability to model the interplay of genetic, physiological, and biomechanical factors that influence outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating genomic, proteomic, and biomechanical data from canine and feline patients. These models will simulate tumor progression under chemotherapeutic regimens, biomechanical stress distributions in orthopedic implants, and soft tissue healing dynamics post-surgery. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response and surgical risk factors from heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, medical imaging, and real-time intraoperative monitoring. The computational workflows will require parallel processing for finite element analysis of implant designs, GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models, and large-scale genomic association studies. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for personalized treatment plans, optimized surgical protocols, and novel insights into species-specific pathophysiological mechanisms. By enabling rapid, high-fidelity simulations of complex biological systems, this research will directly enhance clinical decision-making in small animal medicine, reduce postoperative complications, and inform the development of targeted therapies. The generated datasets and models will be shared via open-access veterinary research repositories, fostering collaboration across institutions. This work aligns with national priorities in agricultural and veterinary sciences to improve animal health outcomes through innovation in computational methodologies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Small/ Companion Animal Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of companion and household animals. Includes instruction in avian medicine, pet care, companion animal medicine, pathophysiology, small animal diseases, small animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: The development of high-performance polymeric fibers with tailored mechanical, thermal, and interfacial properties requires a precise understanding of how molecular-scale interactions govern macroscopic behavior. However, existing models struggle to predict the nonlinear dynamics of polymer chains under high-strain conditions or in complex environments, such as during dyeing or surface functionalization. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multiscale processes in fiber formation, dye-polymer interactions, and stress-response mechanisms. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) and dissipative particle dynamics (DPD), we will model the alignment and entanglement of polymer chains during electrospinning and melt-spinning processes. These simulations will integrate machine learning (ML) to parameterize force fields for novel copolymer systems, including bio-based polyamides and elastomeric composites. A second focus will involve quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations to study the adsorption mechanisms of organic dyes on functionalized fiber surfaces, aiming to optimize binding affinity while minimizing energy-intensive post-processing. The computational workflow will require large-scale parallelization to handle systems exceeding 1 million particles and nanosecond-scale trajectories, necessitating access to GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory resources. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for designing fibers with enhanced toughness, recyclability, and dyeability, directly informing experimental synthesis protocols. By elucidating the role of side-chain topology and interfacial polarity in stress distribution, this work will advance sustainable textile engineering and high-strength material applications. The resulting open-source simulation tools will bridge critical gaps between polymer physics and industrial fiber production, offering a template for data-driven material innovation in the field.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis, structure and properties of polymers with an emphasis on fibers. Includes instruction in polymer chemistry and synthesis, fiber and polymer physics and physical chemistry, the production, processing and properties of fibrous materials, and chemistry of dyes, finishes, and their processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Polish philology and dialectology, addressing gaps in large-scale analysis of linguistic variation and historical language change. The core research problem centers on the limited application of computational methods to study regional Polish dialects and their evolution, particularly in relation to sociocultural influences and literary production. While existing scholarship has cataloged dialectal features manually, the scale and complexity of audio recordings, historical texts, and modern speech corpora require advanced processing to uncover patterns across time and geography. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze digitized texts spanning the 16th to 21st centuries, including regional literature, archival manuscripts, and transcribed oral histories. Parallelized acoustic analysis workflows will process dialect recordings to map phonetic shifts, while transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned for Polish) will quantify stylistic and lexical changes in literary works against sociopolitical contexts. Computational demands include training multilingual models for cross-dialect comparison, running phylogenetic algorithms to model language divergence, and storing/querying multi-terabyte linguistic datasets. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Polish dialect boundaries, an annotated corpus of diachronic linguistic features linked to literary movements, and open-access tools for automated dialect classification. These resources will directly support endangered language preservation efforts and inform curriculum development for advanced Polish studies. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological frameworks, this work aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing Slavic languages at scale while providing infrastructure for future interdisciplinary collaborations in digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the integration of adaptive, sustainable materials into residential interior design workflows, with a focus on enhancing efficiency and reducing waste in home furnishings installation. Current practices in home furnishings and equipment installation rely heavily on manual assessments for material selection, spatial planning, and environmental impact estimation, leading to inconsistencies and resource inefficiencies. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the interplay between dynamic environmental conditions, material durability, and user-centric design parameters. The computational pipeline will integrate three core components: (1) physics-based simulations of textile behavior under variable humidity, temperature, and mechanical stress; (2) machine learning models trained on consumer preference datasets to predict aesthetic compatibility across material combinations; and (3) generative algorithms for space optimization that balance ergonomic requirements with installation logistics. By coupling finite element analysis of novel bio-composite materials with real-time rendering of virtual interiors, the system will enable installers to test thousands of design permutations while quantifying sustainability metrics such as carbon footprint and recyclability. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of material properties, climate scenarios, and spatial constraints. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that reduces material overages by ≥30% in installation projects and a public database cataloging performance characteristics of emerging sustainable furnishings materials. This work bridges gaps between environmental science, computational design, and tradecraft knowledge, offering a paradigm shift toward data-driven practices in an industry traditionally reliant on empirical methods.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in home furnishings and decorations. Includes instruction in selecting, purchasing, and designing home furnishings, decorations, and equipment; floral design; accessory construction; textiles; and upholstery.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the heterogeneous mechanisms underlying chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations, which remain a leading cause of hospitalization and mortality worldwide. Current predictive models for exacerbation risk and treatment response lack granularity, failing to integrate multi-omic data with dynamic physiological parameters. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating single-cell RNA sequencing data from bronchial epithelial cells, sputum proteomics, real-time continuous physiological monitoring (via wearable sensors), and spatially resolved computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of patient-specific airway geometries. The computational pipeline will employ machine learning models to identify exacerbation-associated molecular signatures and link these to functional airway obstruction patterns predicted by CFD. By simulating thousands of patient-specific airway geometries under varying inflammatory and mucociliary clearance conditions, the study aims to quantify how localized epithelial remodeling drives airflow limitation. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of longitudinal multi-omic data, training deep neural networks on high-dimensional feature sets, and executing parallelized CFD simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for exacerbation subtyping, predictive models of treatment response to inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators, and optimized in silico templates for personalized bronchodilator delivery strategies. This work will advance precision medicine in COPD by establishing a computational platform to decode patient-specific pathophysiological cascades, directly informing clinical trial design and therapeutic targeting. The requested resources will enable scaling to cohort sizes required for robust validation, with immediate implications for reducing the global burden of COPD-related morbidity.
cip_definition: Research focused on pulmonary physiology and the treatment of lung diseases, pulmonary malignancies, related vascular diseases, respiratory disorders, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, and pulmonary pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing metadata generation and semantic enrichment for large-scale, heterogeneous digital collections in libraries and archives. As institutions increasingly digitize cultural heritage materials, existing metadata creation workflows—often reliant on manual or semi-automated processes—struggle to scale while maintaining accuracy and contextual depth. The research proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging transformer-based language models and graph neural networks to automate the extraction of hierarchical relationships, temporal linkages, and domain-specific ontologies from unstructured text and multimedia assets. The methodology involves training multi-modal machine learning models on curated corpora spanning digitized manuscripts, oral history transcripts, and image collections, with iterative validation by domain experts in archival science. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing terabytes of unstructured data, fine-tuning large language models on specialized vocabularies, and simulating knowledge graph embeddings that preserve contextual nuances across diverse cultural contexts. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive metadata augmentation, capable of dynamically updating semantic networks as collections expand. The project aims to significantly reduce latency in resource description workflows while enhancing discoverability through AI-generated contextual annotations. By bridging computational linguistics, digital preservation, and knowledge organization systems, this work advances the capacity of memory institutions to manage exponentially growing digital assets and supports interdisciplinary research requiring complex, cross-collection queries. The computational infrastructure will enable reproducibility studies across multiple institutions, fostering collaborative benchmarking of AI-assisted curation methodologies in library science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the knowledge and skills required to develop, organize, store, retrieve, administer, and facilitate the use of local, remote, and networked collections of information in print, audiovisual, and electronic formats and that prepares individuals for professional service as librarians and information consultants.

abstract: Respiratory diseases in pediatric populations present unique challenges due to the dynamic nature of lung development and the limited applicability of adult-derived diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular and biomechanical mechanisms underlying childhood respiratory diseases, including bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), cystic fibrosis, and viral-induced airway remodeling. Current barriers include the computational complexity of modeling growth-dependent lung mechanics, integrating multi-omics data across developmental stages, and simulating patient-specific responses to therapies. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that bridge molecular, cellular, and organ-level dynamics in pediatric respiratory systems. The computational framework will incorporate longitudinal clinical data from pulmonary function tests, chest imaging, and biomarker profiles with mechanistic models of airway inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and mechanotransduction pathways. Machine learning approaches will be applied to identify predictive signatures of disease progression from high-dimensional datasets spanning genomics, proteomics, and clinical metadata. A key innovation involves GPU-accelerated simulations of ciliary function and mucus transport in developing airways, which require fine-grained spatial-temporal resolution exceeding standard computing capabilities. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to optimize ventilator support strategies in in silico models of neonatal lungs and facilitate virtual clinical trials for rare pediatric conditions. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets for BPD, personalized risk stratification algorithms for post-viral airway complications, and optimized intervention protocols for mechanical ventilation in preterm infants. By creating open-source computational tools validated against clinical datasets, this work will establish a paradigm for data-driven pediatric pulmonology research while addressing the critical need for developmentally appropriate respiratory care strategies. The requested resources will directly support computationally intensive tasks that cannot be feasibly executed on local clusters, including the analysis of whole-genome sequencing data from 5,000+ patient samples and real-time simulation of airway biomechanics across pediatric age groups.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention and treatment of all respiratory diseases affecting infants, children, and young adults, based on knowledge of the growth and development of the lung, assessment of respiratory function in infants and children, and experience in a variety of invasive and noninvasive diagnostic techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary study examining the intersection of cultural, economic, and environmental factors influencing community resilience in rapidly urbanizing regions. Traditional approaches to urban resilience often silo disciplinary insights, limiting holistic solutions. Our research addresses this gap by integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with geospatial analytics and machine learning to simulate dynamic interactions between human behavior, infrastructure development, and ecological stressors. The computational complexity of modeling heterogeneous agents—including residents, policymakers, and environmental systems—across high-resolution spatial and temporal scales necessitates HPC capabilities. We propose parallelizing ABM simulations to evaluate scenarios such as flood adaptation strategies, resource allocation under economic constraints, and cultural preservation amid land-use changes. These simulations will synthesize datasets spanning decades of demographic records, satellite imagery, and qualitative community surveys. A key innovation involves training graph neural networks on simulated interaction networks to identify emergent patterns in decision-making and resource flows. Outcomes will include an open-source computational framework for interdisciplinary resilience planning, validated against case studies in Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. This work aims to provide policymakers with evidence-based tools to balance socioeconomic equity, cultural integrity, and environmental sustainability in urban systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive geospatial computations, reducing runtime for Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses, and scaling generative models to diverse regional contexts. By bridging computational social science, environmental humanities, and urban informatics, this project exemplifies the transformative potential of interdisciplinary methodologies supported by advanced computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Adolescent healthcare presents unique challenges due to the interplay of developmental, psychosocial, and biological factors during this critical life stage. This project seeks to address gaps in understanding how multi-modal data—including genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and social determinants of health (SDOH) metrics—interact to influence health outcomes in adolescents with chronic conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes, and depression. Traditional statistical methods often fail to capture the non-linear relationships and high-dimensional interactions inherent in these datasets, limiting the development of personalized interventions. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning (ML) and systems biology approaches. The computational workflow will integrate genomic variant data from whole-exome sequencing, longitudinal EHR data (e.g., medication histories, lab results), and SDOH data (geospatial, socioeconomic) from a cohort of 5,000 adolescents enrolled in a multi-site clinical study. Deep learning models will be trained to identify predictive biomarkers and environmental risk profiles associated with disease progression, while graph neural networks will map gene-environment interaction networks. Agent-based simulations will model the impact of hypothetical interventions on population-level outcomes. The scale of data (≥200 TB) and complexity of models require distributed computing frameworks, GPU-accelerated training, and large-memory nodes for in-memory processing of genomic matrices. Expected outcomes include (1) validated ML models for risk stratification of adolescent metabolic and mental health disorders, (2) mechanistic insights into puberty-related shifts in disease trajectories, and (3) open-source computational tools optimized for adolescent health research. By elucidating the synergistic effects of biological and environmental factors, this work aims to advance precision medicine strategies tailored to adolescents’ evolving physiology and social contexts, ultimately reducing long-term morbidity in this vulnerable population.
cip_definition: Research focused on the unique physical, psychological, and social characteristics of adolescents and their healthcare problems and needs.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving role of digital pedagogy in non-institutional religious education, a niche interdisciplinary domain intersecting educational theory, digital humanities, and theology. While traditional religious education research has focused on classroom or congregational settings, the proliferation of decentralized, online learning platforms—such as faith-based mobile apps, virtual scripture study groups, and AI-driven mentorship tools—has created complex, unstructured datasets that resist conventional qualitative analysis. The central research problem involves mapping how these digital environments influence the transmission of religious knowledge, particularly across intergenerational and intercultural contexts, while maintaining theological coherence. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) of user-generated content (e.g., forum discussions, video transcripts) to identify patterns in conceptual retention and ethical reasoning, network analysis of collaborative learning behaviors, and agent-based modeling to simulate the long-term impacts of algorithmically curated content on community belief systems. A key innovation involves adapting transformer models to recognize context-specific theological nuance in training data drawn from diverse religious traditions, requiring fine-tuning on curated corpora of sacred texts and annotated dialogue. By analyzing terabytes of interaction logs from three partner platforms serving global Muslim, Jewish, and Buddhist communities, this project aims to establish quantitative metrics for evaluating digital religious pedagogy effectiveness. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for ethically aligned curriculum optimization in faith-based learning technologies and predictive models to mitigate ideological fragmentation in digitally mediated religious communities. The scale of multimodal data analysis and the need for real-time simulation of complex social learning dynamics necessitate HPC resources to advance this understudied frontier in humanities computing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of providing educational services to members of faith communities, within the context of a particular religion, and that prepares individuals to serve as religious educators. Includes instruction in planning and teaching lessons, organizing and supervising instructional activities, designing and developing instructional materials, and administering religious education programs and facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of user engagement with algorithmically curated multimedia content across decentralized digital platforms, a critical challenge in contemporary digital communication. As decentralized platforms (e.g., blockchain-based social networks, peer-to-peer media-sharing systems) gain prominence, their reliance on distributed algorithms to personalize content raises questions about transparency, ethical design, and unintended behavioral outcomes. Existing studies lack scalable methods to analyze real-time, cross-platform interactions at the intersection of algorithmic design, user behavior, and content diffusion. To address this gap, the research employs high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale, dynamic networks of user-content interactions and simulate algorithmic curation processes. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate user decision-making under varying algorithmic conditions, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map content propagation pathways, and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze multimedia metadata and user-generated text. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets spanning synthetic and real-world platform data (e.g., activity logs, multimedia metadata). HPC resources are essential for training GNNs on evolving network topologies, running thousands of ABM iterations to test ethical design parameters, and performing real-time sentiment analysis on user feedback. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework to evaluate transparency in decentralized algorithmic systems, (2) evidence-based guidelines for mitigating echo chamber effects in peer-to-peer content distribution, and (3) open-source tools for simulating user-algorithm interactions at scale. The project will directly inform policy discussions on decentralized media governance and provide practitioners with actionable insights for designing ethically aligned multimedia platforms. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances computational communication research methods while addressing urgent sociotechnical challenges in digital media ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, critical evaluation, and regulation of new electronic communication technologies using computer applications; and that prepares individuals to function as developers and managers of digital communications media. Includes instruction in computer and telecommunications technologies and processes; design and development of digital communications; marketing and distribution; digital communications regulation, law, and policy; the study of human interaction with, and use of, digital media; and emerging trends and issues.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in nanoscale thermal transport within hybrid nanostructured materials, a domain pivotal to advancing next-generation nanoelectronics and energy-efficient nanodevices. As device architectures shrink below 10 nm, classical continuum models fail to capture quantum confinement effects, interfacial phonon scattering, and nonlinear thermal behaviors, leading to unreliable predictions of heat dissipation and operational stability. Current experimental techniques also struggle to resolve spatially and temporally heterogeneous thermal dynamics at these scales. To bridge this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM), and machine learning (ML)-accelerated surrogate modeling. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate heat transfer across graphene-metal nanocomposites and transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) heterostructures, systems central to nanoelectronic thermal management. AIMD simulations will parametrize interfacial phonon spectra and electron-phonon coupling coefficients, while GPU-optimized LBM solvers will model mesoscale thermal transport across defect-engineered interfaces. A graph neural network (GNN) surrogate model, trained on these datasets, will enable rapid exploration of design spaces for optimal thermal conductivity anisotropy. The computational workflow demands large-scale parallelization due to the ∼10^6-atom system sizes, picosecond-scale timestep requirements, and combinatorial material configurations. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source codebase for nanothermal simulations, quantitative design rules for heat-optimized nanocomposites, and ML-derived maps correlating interfacial defects with thermal boundary conductance. This work will directly inform experimental synthesis efforts in our collaborator’s lab, targeting nanoelectronics with 40% reduced thermal throttling. The requested HPC allocation is essential for handling the project’s ∼2 PB of combined quantum-mechanical and mesoscale simulation data, enabling transformative insights into nanoscale energy transport physics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical, scientific, and engineering principles and technical skills to manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) and to design, fabricate, and integrate nanoscale structures, devices, and systems. Includes instruction in materials science, thermodynamics, nanomaterials, nanoelectronics, and nano/micro device fabrication and testing.

abstract: The structural integrity and longevity of masonry systems are critically dependent on material interactions, load distribution, and environmental factors, yet predictive modeling of these complex behaviors remains computationally underdeveloped. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate and optimize masonry structures under dynamic stressors such as seismic activity, moisture infiltration, and thermal cycling. Current empirical methods for assessing masonry performance are limited in scalability and fail to account for the heterogeneous nature of composite materials like mortar, brick, and reinforcement systems. To address this gap, we will implement multiscale finite element models (FEM) that integrate micro-scale material properties—derived from laboratory-tested compressive and tensile datasets—with macro-scale structural dynamics. These models will simulate stress propagation, crack formation, and failure thresholds across diverse masonry configurations, including decorative and load-bearing designs. Machine learning algorithms will further refine predictive accuracy by correlating simulation outputs with real-world failure case studies. The HPC environment is essential for processing large-scale 3D simulations and iterative parameter analyses, which are computationally prohibitive on standard systems. Anticipated outcomes include a validated digital toolkit for optimizing masonry designs to meet evolving building codes, reduce material waste through precision engineering, and enhance vocational training via interactive simulation modules. This work will directly inform curriculum advancements in structural masonry education, providing students with data-driven insights into modern construction challenges. By bridging computational innovation with traditional masonry practices, the project aims to establish new standards for resilient, sustainable building techniques while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational scientists and masonry professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the laying and/or setting of exterior brick, concrete block, hard tile, marble and related materials, using trowels, levels, hammers, chisels, and other hand tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, blueprint reading, structural masonry, decorative masonry, foundations, reinforcement, mortar preparation, cutting and finishing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The integration of ethical reasoning and humanities into health professions education remains a critical yet underexplored area, particularly in understanding how complex sociocultural dynamics influence decision-making among trainees. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to analyze large-scale qualitative and quantitative datasets from interdisciplinary health education contexts, including simulation-based training, reflective narratives, and longitudinal assessments of ethical competency. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to systematically evaluate unstructured textual data—such as student journals, patient interaction transcripts, and ethics case discussions—for patterns in moral reasoning, bias, and contextual sensitivity. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate educational environments to assess how variable curricula, institutional policies, and cultural factors interact to shape trainee outcomes. These computational approaches require the parallel processing capabilities of HPC to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train deep learning architectures, and run iterative simulations with dynamic parameter adjustments. Expected outcomes include the identification of pedagogical strategies that robustly enhance ethical decision-making, predictive models linking specific educational interventions to competency development, and a publicly accessible framework for analyzing humanities-based health education data. By elucidating the multidimensional drivers of ethical formation in health professions training, this work will inform curriculum design, accreditation standards, and policies aimed at fostering equitable, culturally responsive care. The requested HPC allocation will enable the scalability, speed, and reproducibility necessary to advance this emerging intersection of computational social science and health professions education.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the spatial and temporal dynamics of cultural practices within sub-Saharan African communities and their diasporas, with a focus on gender roles and indigenous knowledge systems. The research addresses a critical gap in African cultural studies: the lack of large-scale, interdisciplinary analyses that integrate fragmented historical, ethnographic, and contemporary data to trace how cultural norms evolve and adapt across geographic and generational boundaries. Current scholarship often relies on localized case studies, limiting systematic comparisons of cultural transmission pathways, particularly in contexts of migration, urbanization, and technological change. To overcome these constraints, the project will employ computational text analysis, geospatial modeling, and network analysis on a curated corpus of multilingual oral histories, community archives, and ethnographic records spanning the 20th and 21st centuries. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of digitized texts in under-resourced African languages, training transformer-based NLP models to detect semantic patterns related to gender and cultural knowledge, and simulating diffusion processes across dynamically mapped migration corridors. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for analyzing cultural continuity and transformation in African diasporic contexts, 2) novel visualizations of gendered knowledge networks in agrarian and urban communities, and 3) open-access tools for ethical computational analysis of culturally sensitive materials. By enabling the synthesis of dispersed cultural data at unprecedented scale, this work will advance methodological innovation in area studies while providing actionable insights for heritage preservation initiatives and gender-inclusive policy frameworks in transnational African communities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara, and including the African diasporas overseas.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic resource allocation in enterprise-grade 5G network slicing environments, where heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) devices compete for low-latency, high-reliability connectivity under fluctuating demand. As organizations increasingly adopt private 5G networks to support mission-critical IoT operations—from smart manufacturing to autonomous logistics—existing telecommunication management frameworks struggle to balance technical constraints (e.g., bandwidth, interference) with business priorities (e.g., service-level agreements, cost efficiency) in real time. We propose developing a novel computational framework that integrates multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with hybrid digital twin simulations to model complex interactions between network infrastructure, IoT device behavior, and business operational requirements. The project requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train MARL agents on large-scale network topologies (simulating 10,000+ concurrent devices) while incorporating real-world data streams from partner organizations in manufacturing and healthcare. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to predict traffic patterns and containerized microservices to emulate edge computing environments. Expected outcomes include: (1) an optimization framework that reduces service degradation incidents by ≥30% compared to static allocation baselines, (2) quantitative insights into trade-offs between network performance metrics and business Key Performance Indicators, and (3) open-source tools for simulating business-driven network slicing scenarios. By bridging telecommunications engineering with operational decision-making, this work aims to establish new methodologies for managing next-generation enterprise networks as strategic business assets rather than purely technical systems. Results will be disseminated through telecommunications policy white papers and machine learning conferences to engage both technical and executive audiences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business skills to design, implement, and manage the voice, video, and data networking systems of organizations. Includes instruction in telecommunications concepts and technologies, network operations and management, wireless communications and mobile computing, cybersecurity, regulation and public policy, business practices and management, and written and oral communications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in normative ethics, specifically addressing the challenge of modeling complex, multi-agent moral decision-making scenarios under competing ethical frameworks. Traditional analytical methods in ethics often struggle to systematically evaluate the dynamic interactions between agents with divergent moral priorities or to predict emergent outcomes in large-scale, heterogeneous populations. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with formal ethical reasoning systems. Agents will be programmed with distinct ethical decision algorithms (e.g., utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics) derived from canonical philosophical texts and contemporary theoretical developments. These agents will interact in simulated environments designed to replicate ethically charged dilemmas in domains such as resource allocation, AI ethics, and public policy trade-offs. The HPC environment is critical for scaling simulations to incorporate thousands of agents with real-time adaptive learning capabilities, enabling the study of how localized ethical decisions propagate through systems and influence collective outcomes. Computational outputs will be analyzed using network theory and game-theoretic frameworks to identify patterns in moral conflict resolution, consensus formation, and the stability of ethical norms under varying conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of modular, open-source ethical reasoning algorithms for interdisciplinary use, (2) quantitative insights into the resilience of specific ethical frameworks in large-scale social simulations, and (3) methodological innovations in applying computational modeling to normative theory validation. This work bridges philosophical rigor with computational social science, offering novel tools to test ethical theories’ practical implications while maintaining fidelity to their conceptual foundations. The requested resources will enable simulations at unprecedented scales, directly contributing to the emerging field of computational ethics and its applications to sociotechnical system design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the theory of moral good and its application to various theoretical and practical problems. Includes instruction in ethical theory, history of ethics, belief and value systems, ethical constructs, and applications to specific topics, issues and problems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern datasets in applied fields such as healthcare, economics, and environmental science necessitates advanced statistical methods that can handle high dimensionality, non-linear relationships, and heterogeneous data structures. Traditional approaches often face computational bottlenecks when scaling to these challenges, particularly for Bayesian hierarchical models and non-parametric techniques that require intensive simulation or iterative optimization. This project proposes the development and implementation of scalable computational workflows to fit such models efficiently using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Specifically, we will focus on enhancing Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for Bayesian spatiotemporal models via parallelized chains and preconditioned gradient-based methods, while also exploring distributed computing frameworks for large-scale Gaussian process regression. Computational tasks will include simulating synthetic datasets to evaluate methodological performance, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized grid search, and validating models on real-world datasets, such as multi-site clinical trial data and high-resolution ecological sensor networks. The project will produce open-source software tools to streamline the deployment of these methods on HPC systems, ensuring reproducibility and accessibility for applied researchers. Expected outcomes include improved inference accuracy for complex models, reduced runtime for iterative algorithms, and novel insights into computational-statistical trade-offs. By addressing scalability challenges, this work will empower statisticians and domain scientists to tackle previously intractable problems, advancing research in precision medicine, climate resilience, and policy evaluation. The requested computing resources are critical to managing memory-intensive workloads and achieving timely convergence for models with millions of parameters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of intercultural communication and identity negotiation in digitally mediated spaces, with a focus on mitigating polarization in multicultural urban environments. While prior studies have examined demographic or survey-based trends in diversity, this work addresses a critical gap: simulating how real-time, large-scale interactions between culturally diverse groups influence the emergence of inclusive or divisive social norms. The research integrates computational sociology, network science, and linguistic anthropology to analyze how micro-level communicative behaviors—such as code-switching, narrative framing, and symbolic gesture exchange—scale into macro-level patterns of social cohesion or fragmentation. Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate populations with heterogeneous cultural attributes (e.g., values, communication styles, identity salience) interacting within dynamic social networks, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will process multilingual corpora from social media and community forums to parameterize agent behaviors. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing thousands of stochastic simulations across diverse demographic and policy scenarios (e.g., varying levels of institutional support for multiculturalism, migration rates, or economic inequality). Expected outcomes include (1) identifying leverage points where targeted intercultural interventions (e.g., moderated dialogue platforms, algorithmic fairness adjustments) could reduce polarization, and (2) developing open-source tools for policymakers to visualize how systemic inequalities amplify cultural tensions in specific urban contexts. By bridging granular behavioral data with societal-scale dynamics, this project advances computational methods for diversity studies while providing actionable insights for fostering intercultural resilience in increasingly complex, digitally connected societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize collision repair processes and material performance in automotive body restoration, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current methods for evaluating structural integrity, paint adhesion, and composite material behavior in damaged vehicles rely heavily on empirical testing, which is time-intensive, costly, and limited in predicting complex interactions under dynamic conditions. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating predictive simulations to enhance repair accuracy, reduce material waste, and improve safety outcomes. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will model stress distribution in deformed auto body structures, curing dynamics of adhesives and coatings, and airflow patterns during spray-painting applications. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to analyze historical repair data and identify correlations between material properties, environmental factors, and long-term durability. These simulations require HPC resources due to the high-resolution meshing of multi-layered vehicle components, non-linear material behaviors, and the need for real-time parametric adjustments. Expected outcomes include a framework for virtual testing of repair techniques, optimized paint application parameters to minimize overspray, and predictive tools for assessing bond strength in modern lightweight composites. The results will be validated against physical experiments conducted in collaboration with industry partners, ensuring translational relevance. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches, this work aims to establish computational standards for collision repair training programs and inform the development of next-generation repair protocols. The project will also generate open-access datasets to support further innovation in automotive repair technologies, benefiting both technical education and industry practices.
cip_title: Autobody/ Collision and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, reconstruct and finish automobile bodies, fenders, and external features. Includes instruction in structure analysis, damage repair, non-structural analysis, mechanical and electrical components, plastics and adhesives, painting and refinishing techniques, and damage analysis and estimating.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the biomechanical and cultural dimensions of dance through computational modeling and large-scale motion data analysis. While dance is widely recognized as a medium of cultural expression, quantitatively mapping its embodied narratives—such as the relationship between movement patterns, emotional intent, and sociocultural context—remains a significant challenge. Current methodologies, limited by manual annotation and small-scale motion capture datasets, struggle to capture the complexity of dance as a dynamic, multimodal phenomenon. This research proposes a computational framework integrating motion capture data from diverse dance traditions (e.g., ballet, contemporary, and folk forms) with machine learning techniques to model choreographic structures, biomechanical efficiency, and cultural-semiotic meanings. HPC resources will enable processing of high-dimensional datasets (including 3D kinematic data, muscle activation simulations, and audiovisual records) and training of neural networks to identify latent patterns across dance genres. Key computational tasks include biomechanical optimization modeling to study injury prevention strategies, graph-based analysis of choreographic “vocabulary” within cultural contexts, and real-time simulation of Labanotation scores for archival applications. Outcomes will advance the scholarly understanding of dance as a culturally coded movement system while providing practical tools for choreographers, educators, and cultural archivists. The project’s computational workflows will also contribute interdisciplinary methods to the digital humanities, bridging embodied practice with data-driven inquiry. By allocating HPC resources, this work addresses critical gaps in dance research scalability, enabling analyses of movement complexity that are inaccessible to traditional laboratory setups. Anticipated deliverables include open-source tools for dance analytics and a publicly accessible database of annotated movement sequences, fostering new collaborations between performing arts and computational sciences.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to express ideas, feelings, and/or inner visions through the performance of one or more of the dance disciplines, including but not limited to ballet, modern, jazz, ethnic, and folk dance, and that focuses on the study and analysis of dance as a cultural phenomenon. Includes instruction in technique, choreography, Laban notation, dance history and criticism, and dance production.

abstract: Laboratory animal medicine research is critical for advancing translational biomedical sciences, yet the increasing complexity of multi-modal datasets in this field—spanning genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and clinical monitoring data—exceeds the analytical capacity of conventional computing infrastructure. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable advanced computational modeling of disease pathogenesis and treatment responses in laboratory animal models. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) developing machine learning frameworks to integrate heterogeneous datasets from murine and non-human primate studies of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and (2) creating agent-based simulations of host-microbiome interactions under varying therapeutic regimens. Current limitations in processing speed and memory allocation prevent simultaneous analysis of whole-genome sequencing data, high-frequency sensor-derived behavioral metrics, and longitudinal histopathology imaging—a bottleneck resolved through parallelized workflows on GPU-accelerated nodes. The computational pipeline will employ containerized bioinformatics tools (e.g., Qiime2, CellProfiler) coupled with custom Python scripts for neural network training, optimized via Slurm job arrays. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying microbiome signatures associated with treatment-resistant IBD subtypes and simulation-derived insights into optimal dosing schedules. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will establish novel methodologies for analyzing complex physiological interactions in controlled animal studies, directly enhancing the precision of veterinary clinical trials. The resource allocation will also support the development of open-source data management templates tailored to laboratory animal research facilities, addressing critical gaps in reproducible computational workflows for this domain. Results will be disseminated through the AniBench platform to strengthen cross-institutional collaboration in translational animal research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied veterinary research and related techniques, equipment, data systems and research design. May included related research in the management of veterinary and other animal research laboratories and health care facilities.

abstract: Urban forests are critical for mitigating climate change, enhancing biodiversity, and improving human well-being in cities, yet their management is challenged by dynamic stressors such as shifting climate patterns, invasive pests, and air pollution. Current models for predicting tree health and ecosystem service provision lack the spatial resolution and integration of multi-scale environmental data required to inform adaptive management in heterogeneous urban landscapes. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate urban forest dynamics under diverse environmental and management scenarios. Leveraging LiDAR-derived 3D cityscape data, hyperlocal climate projections, soil condition maps, and species-specific stress tolerance thresholds, we will parameterize an agent-based model to predict individual tree growth, mortality, and carbon sequestration potential across micro-environments. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify optimal species compositions and planting strategies that maximize resilience to heatwaves, drought, and pest outbreaks. The computational demands of processing city-scale geospatial datasets, running Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, and training deep neural networks on multi-modal environmental data necessitate access to HPC resources for parallelized workflows and large-memory computation. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool for urban foresters, validated against field data from six major U.S. cities, and novel insights into how hybrid natural-infrastructure systems can be optimized for climate adaptation. This research will directly inform municipal policies on tree canopy targets, species selection guidelines, and maintenance protocols, while advancing computational methodologies for ecological forecasting in built environments. By integrating urban forestry principles with cutting-edge computational analytics, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven stewardship of urban ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of forestry and related sciences to the development, care, and maintenance of individual trees and forested areas within or close to areas of dense human habitation. Includes instruction in urban environments; effects of pollution on tree species; environmental design and landscaping; urban pest infestation; urban forest management; and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders in pediatric populations present unique challenges due to the dynamic nature of growing bones and tissues, necessitating tailored diagnostic and treatment strategies. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized protocols derived from adult studies, which fail to account for developmental variability and the long-term biomechanical consequences of interventions. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific predictive models for surgical and non-surgical management of early-onset scoliosis (EOS) and developmental hip dysplasia (DDH). The research will integrate multimodal clinical data—including longitudinal imaging (MRI, CT), motion capture, and electronic health records—to analyze growth patterns, biomechanical stress distributions, and post-intervention outcomes across diverse pediatric cohorts. Computational workflows will employ finite element modeling (FEM) to simulate spinal and hip joint mechanics under varying treatment scenarios, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify predictive biomarkers of progression or complications. A key innovation involves coupling these models with population-level registry data to quantify the impact of socioeconomic factors on treatment accessibility and outcomes. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps for sensitivity analysis, Bayesian optimization of treatment parameters, and real-time visualization of complex biomechanical interactions. Expected outcomes include validated computational tools to guide implant selection in EOS, optimize bracing protocols for DDH, and stratify patients by risk of secondary complications. By establishing open-source datasets and modular simulation pipelines, this work will provide a scalable framework for precision orthopedics in pediatric populations, reducing the need for iterative invasive procedures. Resource requests include GPU nodes for deep learning tasks, high-memory nodes for FEM simulations, and secure storage for sensitive patient data, with all workflows adhering to HIPAA and institutional ethics standards.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, surgical and non-surgical treatment, and management of musculoskeletal diseases, abnormalities and trauma in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: The growing complexity of vendor-specific software ecosystems necessitates advanced methodologies to ensure reliable certification processes for installation, customization, and maintenance workflows. Current approaches to vendor product certification rely on manual testing and static validation frameworks, which struggle to scale with heterogeneous computing environments, evolving software dependencies, and emergent security threats. This project proposes the development of an automated, high-fidelity simulation platform to model and validate vendor-certified software deployments across diverse hardware-software configurations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will focus on creating scalable virtualized environments that replicate real-world deployment scenarios, including edge computing systems, hybrid cloud architectures, and legacy infrastructure integrations. Computational methods will combine parallelized dependency resolution algorithms, machine learning-driven anomaly detection, and stochastic fault injection testing to systematically evaluate certification criteria under dynamic conditions. Key objectives include optimizing resource allocation for concurrent certification workflows, reducing false positives in compatibility assessments, and identifying latent failure modes in vendor-recommended configurations. The project will utilize containerized workloads and GPU-accelerated simulation frameworks to achieve rapid iteration across thousands of parametric variations. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible benchmarking toolkit for vendor-agnostic certification analytics, a repository of performance-optimized deployment templates, and novel metrics for quantifying certification robustness in multi-vendor ecosystems. By addressing the computational bottlenecks in large-scale certification processes, this work aims to bridge gaps between vendor-specific training protocols and the operational realities of modern computing environments, ultimately enhancing the reliability and interoperability of certified software solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to fulfill the requirements set by vendors for professional qualification as certified installation, customization, and maintenance engineers for specific software products and/or processes. Includes training in specific vendor-supported software products and their installation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities investigation into the evolving cultural narratives of migration and identity within U.S. civilization from the 19th century to the present. By integrating large-scale textual and visual datasets—including digitized newspapers, oral histories, government records, and multimedia archives—the research addresses a critical gap in understanding how regional and transnational migration patterns have shaped collective memory and cultural discourse. Traditional qualitative methods in American Studies struggle to systematically analyze the scale and complexity of these interactions, particularly across underrepresented communities. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of historical texts, network modeling to trace the dissemination of cultural narratives, and machine learning-driven image recognition to examine visual representations of identity in public media. HPC resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets, training custom transformer models on historical language variants, and running iterative simulations to map cultural diffusion pathways. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas visualizing shifting narratives of belonging and exclusion, as well as new computational frameworks for interdisciplinary analysis of cultural change. This work will contribute methodological innovations to the digital humanities while offering empirically grounded insights into the contested construction of American identity, with implications for public history, education, and policy discussions on immigration and cultural heritage. The scale of data processing—particularly the parallelized analysis of temporally layered textual and visual corpora—requires the distributed computing capabilities and GPU acceleration uniquely available through HPC infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the United States and its Pre-Columbian and colonial predecessors, and including the flow of immigrants from other societies.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the development of adaptive decision architectures for next-generation combat systems through high-fidelity modeling of multi-domain operational scenarios. Modern combat systems face escalating complexity due to the integration of heterogeneous platforms, AI-driven threat environments, and contested communications networks. Traditional static architectures struggle to maintain operational coherence under dynamically shifting constraints, creating critical vulnerabilities in latency-sensitive kill chains. This work proposes a computational framework to simulate and optimize real-time resource allocation across distributed combat networks, with emphasis on resilience against adversarial machine learning attacks and electromagnetic spectrum degradation. The research employs agent-based modeling to represent platform-level decision nodes, coupled with multi-objective reinforcement learning to train adaptive coordination policies under uncertainty. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of large-scale engagement scenarios involving 100+ interacting agents, including blue-force assets, adversarial systems, and neutral entities. Computational experiments will evaluate system performance metrics across varied threat landscapes, quantifying tradeoffs between centralized control resilience and decentralized autonomy. Key innovations include a novel graph neural network architecture for cross-domain situational awareness fusion and a physics-informed digital twin framework that integrates combat system reliability models with real-time sensor degradation data. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for dynamic compute resource partitioning in edge-deployed combat modules and predictive maintenance algorithms optimized for contested logistics environments. The results will inform Department of Defense standards for trusted AI integration in mission-critical systems while advancing computational methods for analyzing emergent behaviors in human-machine combat teams. This work directly addresses priorities outlined in recent National Defense Authorization Acts regarding cyber-physical resilience and adaptive decision superiority.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of systems engineering and system architecture to the design and construction of modern combat systems and their integration with each other, with host platforms and with other forces into network-centric warfighting systems. Includes instruction in systems engineering, computer programming, chemical systems, biological systems, material systems, human factors, combat environments, sensor systems, threat and system risk assessment, conventional and unconventional weapons, combat simulation, reliability and maintenance, testing, engineering project management, strategic planning and applications to aerospace, ground, and naval combat systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the usability and effectiveness of multimodal technical communication materials, with a focus on optimizing complex documentation systems for diverse audiences. As technical communication increasingly relies on interactive digital platforms, traditional text-centric evaluation methods fail to account for dynamic user interactions, multivariate content delivery, and accessibility requirements across devices. The research problem centers on creating scalable models to simulate user engagement patterns, predict comprehension barriers, and test adaptive content strategies in high-dimensional scenarios. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement agent-based simulations of user interactions with technical documentation systems, incorporating natural language processing to analyze semantic coherence across multimedia components and machine learning models to identify patterns in large-scale usability datasets. Computational experiments will evaluate how variables such as information architecture, visual hierarchy, and adaptive content delivery impact user task success rates across different demographic and expertise groups. The project will also employ GPU-accelerated rendering to model real-time document accessibility adjustments for users with disabilities. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for optimizing technical communication products during the design phase, reducing iterative testing costs, and improving inclusivity metrics. By enabling large-scale simulation of user experiences that would be impractical to test empirically, this research aims to advance evidence-based practices in technical communication while developing computational methods transferable to emerging domains like augmented reality documentation systems. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the parallel processing demands of multivariate simulations and training deep learning models on interaction log datasets exceeding 10^6 events.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the communication of technical and scientific knowledge to a variety of audiences through print, video, and digital media; and that prepares individuals to function as technical writers and editors, documentation developers, web designers, and usability specialists. Includes instruction in scientific and technical writing and editing, graphic and information design, web design, audience analysis, document usability and field testing, publications management, and applications to specific technical fields.

abstract: Educational entrepreneurship faces dynamic challenges in scaling innovations effectively, particularly in balancing cost, accessibility, and learning outcomes under resource constraints. This project seeks to develop computational models that simulate the impact of entrepreneurial strategies—such as alternative funding mechanisms, technology integration, and operational scaling—on educational ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will build agent-based models (ABMs) to represent interactions among stakeholders (e.g., schools, investors, policymakers) and machine learning (ML) frameworks to analyze longitudinal datasets on educational ventures’ performance. The ABMs will incorporate variables such as regional economic conditions, policy environments, and resource allocation patterns, while ML pipelines will identify predictors of scalability and sustainability from historical data on charter schools, edtech startups, and philanthropic initiatives. A Monte Carlo approach will assess financial and operational risks under diverse scenarios. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to test thousands of strategy permutations, enabling robust sensitivity analyses and optimization of decision-making frameworks. Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide resource allocation for education entrepreneurs, such as optimal investment thresholds for technology adoption or evidence-based thresholds for student-to-instructor ratios in hybrid learning environments. These tools will address a critical gap in data-driven decision support for education ventures, which often rely on anecdotal or localized insights. The computational outputs will be disseminated as open-access tools for entrepreneurs and policymakers, with potential applications in curriculum design for entrepreneurship programs. This work advances the integration of computational social science methods into education leadership, offering scalable solutions to systemic challenges in equitable resource distribution and innovation sustainability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create, fund, and manage innovations in education. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, the design of learning environments, the economics of education, entrepreneurship, evaluation, finance, human-centered design, investing, resource management, project management, and marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance data-driven decision-making in college student counseling by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multi-source datasets on student behavior, academic performance, and mental health outcomes. Current counseling practices often rely on qualitative assessments and siloed data, limiting the ability to identify at-risk students proactively or tailor interventions effectively. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating institutional records, anonymized counseling session transcripts, and longitudinal student surveys to model factors influencing academic persistence and well-being. Machine learning techniques, including natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment analysis of counseling dialogues and graph neural networks to map student support networks, will be applied to uncover patterns in service utilization and intervention efficacy. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of unstructured text data, training multi-modal predictive models, and running agent-based simulations to test hypothetical counseling strategies under varied demographic and institutional conditions. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for identifying early warning signs of academic disengagement or mental health crises, (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing counselor-student ratios and service allocation, and (3) open-source tools to help institutions anonymize and analyze counseling data ethically. By enabling rapid analysis of heterogeneous datasets while preserving student privacy through federated learning architectures, this work aims to advance personalized counseling approaches and inform equity-focused resource distribution in higher education settings. The computational infrastructure will support replication studies across diverse institutions, contributing foundational knowledge to education research on student success ecosystems.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: Liver transplantation remains a complex intervention with variable outcomes influenced by donor-recipient compatibility, immunosuppression dynamics, and post-transplant complications. Current predictive models lack the resolution to integrate multi-dimensional clinical, genomic, and imaging data, limiting personalized risk stratification and therapeutic optimization. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model post-transplant outcomes by analyzing high-dimensional datasets from electronic health records, longitudinal allograft imaging, and multi-omics profiles (e.g., donor-recipient HLA sequencing, microbiome dynamics, and metabolomic trajectories). Leveraging machine learning algorithms, including ensemble neural networks and Bayesian hierarchical models, we will integrate heterogeneous data streams to predict graft rejection, metabolic complications, and immunosuppression-related morbidity. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further model vascular and biliary anastomotic patency using pre- and post-transplant imaging. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabytes of imaging data, training complex models on longitudinal patient cohorts (n > 2,000), and performing real-time sensitivity analyses across clinical scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early rejection detection, optimized immunosuppression dosing protocols, and mechanistic insights into alloimmune-microbiome interactions. These tools will be deployed as clinical decision support modules within transplant EHR systems, aiming to reduce re-transplantation rates and improve 5-year survival. By bridging computational innovation with transplant hepatology practice, this work aligns with national priorities to advance precision medicine in organ transplantation, offering scalable solutions to address critical gaps in post-transplant care. Resource allocation will directly support data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale simulation workloads, enabling translational insights that traditional clinical research infrastructure cannot feasibly achieve.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge and the skill required of a gastroenterologist to care for patients prior to and following hepatic transplantation that spans all phases of liver transplantation.

abstract: Healthcare systems face persistent challenges in optimizing resource allocation, predicting patient outcomes, and scaling innovative solutions due to the complexity of clinical, operational, and biological data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that address these challenges through systems-level innovation. The research focuses on two interrelated aims: (1) creating predictive models for hospital readmission risks and resource utilization by integrating multi-source data (electronic health records, wearable devices, and genomic profiles), and (2) simulating the impact of novel medical devices and care protocols within virtual healthcare environments. Machine learning algorithms, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on terabyte-scale datasets to identify patterns in patient outcomes, while agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation frameworks will evaluate proposed interventions under diverse operational scenarios. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration to manage data dimensionality, reduce training times for iterative model refinement, and enable real-time simulations of hospital-scale systems. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic resource allocation, risk-stratified care pathways, and virtual prototyping of medical devices, all designed to reduce costs and improve care delivery. By providing scalable, evidence-based frameworks, this work will empower healthcare leaders to test innovations in silico before implementation, mitigate financial risks, and accelerate the translation of research into practice. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the precision, speed, and complexity required to model emergent behaviors in healthcare systems, ultimately supporting data-driven decisions in policy, finance, and organizational change.
