cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to innovate solutions and lead change within a healthcare organization. Includes instruction in innovation management, medical device development, evidence-based practice, systems thinking, information technology, healthcare policy and finance, organizational change, and leadership.

abstract: The gut microbiome’s role in modulating host responses to personalized dietary interventions remains poorly understood, particularly in the context of metabolic disorders such as type 2 diabetes (T2D). While advances in multi-omics technologies have generated vast datasets linking microbial taxa, dietary patterns, and metabolic outcomes, integrating these heterogeneous data to predict individualized nutritional strategies remains a computational challenge. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution, mechanistic model of diet-microbiome-host interactions using genome-scale metabolic networks (GEMs) tailored to patient-specific metagenomic, metabolomic, and clinical data. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate microbial community dynamics under varying dietary inputs, predict metabolite exchange networks, and map these outputs to host metabolic pathways implicated in glucose regulation. A hybrid approach combining constraint-based modeling, machine learning (neural ordinary differential equations), and Bayesian inference will be implemented to reconcile population-scale omics data with individual-level predictions. The computational framework will be validated against longitudinal data from a cohort of 200 T2D patients undergoing controlled dietary interventions, with iterative model refinement based on observed glycemic outcomes. Successful implementation will yield a predictive tool for optimizing personalized dietary recommendations based on an individual’s microbiome composition, metabolic state, and genetic background. This work addresses a critical gap in clinical nutrition by moving beyond population-level dietary guidelines to precision approaches, potentially reducing trial-and-error in dietary management of metabolic diseases. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling simulations to accommodate the combinatorial complexity of dietary components, microbial taxa, and host interactions, enabling real-time parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses that are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure. Outcomes will advance both computational methodologies in microbiome research and translational applications in dietetics, fostering a new paradigm for data-driven clinical nutrition services.
cip_title: Dietetics and Clinical Nutrition Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dietetics and clinical nutrition services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial machinery and the demand for predictive maintenance solutions require advanced computational tools to optimize operational reliability and cost-efficiency. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for predictive maintenance of industrial systems, including pumps, conveyor systems, and steam propulsion equipment, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current predictive models often lack sufficient resolution to account for multi-physics interactions (e.g., thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamic stresses) or real-time sensor data integration, leading to suboptimal maintenance schedules and unplanned downtime. To address this, the proposed research will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) algorithms to model equipment degradation under operational conditions. Large-scale simulations will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including vibration, thermal imaging, and pressure sensor outputs—to train ML models for fault detection and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. HPC resources are critical to handle the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations, parallel processing of sensor datasets, and iterative optimization of neural networks. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of simulating failure modes with 85-90% accuracy, reducing maintenance costs by 15-20% in pilot industrial use cases. Additionally, the project will produce open-source tools for real-time anomaly detection, enabling broader adoption in small-to-medium enterprises. The work aligns with workforce development goals by incorporating HPC-driven methodologies into the Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance Technology curriculum, preparing technicians to utilize advanced computational tools in industrial settings. This research bridges a critical gap between theoretical predictive models and practical maintenance workflows, offering scalable solutions to enhance the resilience of industrial infrastructure.
cip_title: Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair and maintain industrial machinery and equipment such as cranes, pumps, engines and motors, pneumatic tools, conveyor systems, production machinery, marine deck machinery, and steam propulsion, refinery, and pipeline-distribution systems.

abstract: Construction projects are complex systems influenced by dynamic variables such as weather patterns, supply chain disruptions, labor availability, and regulatory constraints. Traditional project management tools often fail to account for the interdependencies and stochastic nature of these factors, leading to cost overruns, delays, and suboptimal resource allocation. This research proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to model construction project workflows under uncertainty, integrating real-time data streams with predictive analytics to optimize scheduling, risk mitigation, and sustainability outcomes. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute agent-based simulations of construction site operations, machine learning algorithms for delay prediction, and multi-objective optimization techniques to balance competing priorities across cost, time, and environmental impact. Key computational challenges include processing heterogeneous datasets from IoT sensors, historical project records, and climate models while maintaining the temporal granularity required for actionable insights. The research will implement parallelized Monte Carlo methods to quantify systemic risks and evaluate mitigation strategies across thousands of simulated project scenarios. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that dynamically updates resource allocation plans based on evolving site conditions, probabilistic completion timelines, and carbon footprint projections. By bridging computational science with construction management practices, this work aims to establish new methodologies for adaptive project governance in the context of climate change and global supply chain volatility. The HPC infrastructure is critical for achieving the necessary scale and speed to model multi-year projects with hourly resolution, enabling practitioners to test interventions in silico before implementation. This interdisciplinary approach advances both computational capabilities in business operations and the practical application of digital twin technologies in construction ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply project management knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques in the construction and facility management industries. Includes instruction in facilities operations and maintenance, construction estimating, OSHA standards, sustainability, drafting, construction plans, project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in correctional facility operations through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Correctional systems face challenges in balancing security, resource allocation, and rehabilitative outcomes, yet operational decision-making often relies on legacy frameworks ill-suited for dynamic, large-scale environments. The research problem centers on developing an agent-based simulation platform to model inmate movement, staff-inmate interactions, and facility-wide resource flows under varying policy scenarios. By integrating anonymized historical data on facility incidents, staffing patterns, and program participation, the model will simulate emergent behaviors and stress-test operational protocols (e.g., lockdown procedures, educational program scheduling) to identify failure points and optimization opportunities. Computational methods will combine discrete-event simulation with machine learning techniques to iteratively refine predictive accuracy, requiring parallel processing capabilities to manage stochastic simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of identifying trade-offs between security expenditures, rehabilitative programming access, and operational overhead. The project’s significance lies in its novel application of HPC to corrections management—a domain traditionally underserved by computational social science—while adhering to ethical constraints through synthetic data safeguards. Results will provide actionable insights for facility administrators and contribute methodological frameworks for complex system analysis in criminal justice contexts. This work bridges gaps between computational social science and applied corrections research, offering a template for evidence-based operational design without direct overlap with excluded disciplines such as public administration or social services. The requested resources will enable simulations at unprecedented granularity, capturing multi-scale interactions across 10,000+ agent populations in real-world facility geometries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in corrections and criminal justice, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of educational administration in K-7 schools necessitates data-driven strategies to optimize operational decision-making, yet school leaders often lack access to advanced computational tools to model dynamic systems at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and simulate agent-based models (ABMs) of school operations, focusing on three interconnected challenges: equitable resource allocation under fluctuating enrollment, multi-criteria scheduling for facilities and staff, and longitudinal policy impact analysis. The computational approach integrates anonymized district datasets (enrollment, staffing, budgets, facility use) with stochastic parameters reflecting community demographics and state-mandated requirements. ABMs will simulate scenarios such as redistricting adjustments, emergency budget cuts, or compliance with new safety protocols, incorporating feedback loops between administrative decisions, staff workload, and student outcomes. Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in outcomes, while machine learning pipelines will identify high-impact decision pathways. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for principals to test hypothetical interventions in silico, reducing trial-and-error risks in real-world implementation. The project will also generate policy-relevant insights into how compounding factors—such as concurrent enrollment growth and staffing shortages—affect the feasibility of equity-focused initiatives. By bridging computational modeling and K-7 administrative practice, this work aims to equip school leaders with evidence-based strategies to balance competing priorities in resource-constrained environments. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the parallelized simulation workloads (estimated 50,000+ core-hours) and analyzing high-dimensional output data, which exceeds the capacity of standard institutional computing infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through a web-based decision-support toolkit tailored for non-technical administrators and state-level policy briefs on computational approaches in educational leadership.
cip_title: Elementary and Middle School Administration/ Principalship
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the elementary and middle school (K-7) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of elementary and middle schools. Includes instruction in elementary and/or middle school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, childhood and pre-adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Forest ecosystems face intensifying threats from climate change, including altered disturbance regimes, habitat fragmentation, and shifting species distributions. Current forest management models lack the spatial resolution and computational capacity to simulate complex ecological processes across multi-decadal timescales while integrating real-world constraints such as economic viability and stakeholder priorities. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel framework for optimizing sustainable forest management strategies under uncertainty. We will develop parallelized simulations coupling process-based forest growth models, species dispersal algorithms, and climate projection ensembles at 1 km² resolution across regional landscapes. Machine learning techniques will be employed to parameterize ecological interactions from lidar-derived canopy structure data and multi-spectral satellite imagery, while Markov decision processes will evaluate management trade-offs between carbon sequestration, timber yield, and biodiversity metrics. The computational scale requires terabyte-scale memory handling and GPU acceleration to run millions of Monte Carlo iterations assessing climate scenario impacts on keystone species survival thresholds. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool capable of identifying robust adaptive management policies across variable time horizons, directly addressing the critical gap between ecological forecasting and operational planning. By quantifying resilience trade-offs in heterogeneous forest systems, this work will provide land managers with evidence-based strategies to balance conservation goals with socioeconomic needs—a pressing challenge as global demand for forest resources escalates. The HPC infrastructure is essential for achieving the temporal granularity and parametric sensitivity analyses required to inform policy in rapidly changing environments.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to manage and develop forest areas for economic, recreational, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in forest-related sciences, mapping, statistics, harvesting and production technology, natural resources management and economics, wildlife sciences, administration, and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study of cultural narratives and identity formation in Canadian Indigenous and immigrant communities. The research addresses a critical gap in interdisciplinary methodologies for analyzing large-scale, multilingual textual and oral history archives that reflect Canada’s complex cultural intersections. Current scholarship often relies on manual or siloed analyses of historical records, limiting the scope of comparative studies on how cultural narratives evolve across time, language, and geography. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, machine learning, and network modeling to systematically examine digitized archival materials—including Indigenous oral histories, colonial-era documents, and immigrant community records—in English, French, and Indigenous languages. Key computational tasks include training multilingual natural language processing (NLP) models to identify thematic patterns, sentiment shifts, and cross-cultural references, as well as constructing temporal networks to map the diffusion of narratives across regions and groups. The scale of data (over 500,000 digitized pages and 2,000 hours of transcribed oral histories) and the complexity of multilingual, non-linear textual relationships necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallel processing, large-scale data storage, and GPU-accelerated model training. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of open-access tools for culturally sensitive text analysis, visualizations of narrative networks, and a publicly accessible database linking historical texts to contemporary cultural practices. This work will provide new insights into the resilience and adaptation of cultural identities in Canada, particularly among underrepresented communities, while demonstrating how HPC can bridge computational and humanistic approaches in area studies. The results will inform educational curricula, cultural preservation initiatives, and policy frameworks addressing multiculturalism and reconciliation.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Canada and its Pre-Columbian, colonial, and pre-federation predecessors, including immigrant flows and related borderlands and island groups.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Korean linguistics through large-scale corpus analysis and computational modeling. The primary research problem centers on resolving gaps in understanding the historical evolution of Korean dialects and their sociolinguistic variation, particularly in understudied regional and informal speech contexts. Traditional methods in Korean language studies, reliant on manual text analysis or small datasets, struggle to capture nuanced linguistic patterns across time and geography. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques with machine learning models to analyze multi-terabyte corpora of historical texts, modern speech transcripts, and social media data. Key tasks include training transformer-based models for dialect classification, automating syntactic and semantic annotation of pre-modern Hangul manuscripts, and simulating phonetic shifts using acoustic datasets. These workflows demand parallelized processing, extensive memory allocation, and GPU acceleration to handle complex tasks such as graph-based dependency parsing of agglutinative Korean morphology and sequence alignment for diachronic comparisons. The project will utilize open-source tools like Stanza and PyTorch, adapted for Korean-specific linguistic features, and integrate domain-specific lexicons for historical and regional terms. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Korean dialect boundaries, a publicly accessible annotated corpus of 18th–20th century texts, and probabilistic models mapping language change trajectories. These resources will provide foundational data for sociolinguistic research, inform AI-driven language preservation efforts, and enhance pedagogical tools for advanced Korean language education. By bridging computational methods with philological expertise, this work aims to establish new interdisciplinary frameworks for analyzing non-standard and evolving language forms, with implications for cross-cultural NLP applications and heritage language documentation.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on personalized mental health counseling interventions through the analysis of large-scale, multi-modal datasets. While counseling efficacy is influenced by complex interactions between client demographics, psychosocial histories, and therapeutic techniques, existing studies often rely on small samples or simplified models that inadequately capture these dynamics. To address this gap, we propose developing machine learning models capable of identifying patterns in treatment outcomes using integrated datasets spanning electronic health records, therapist notes, behavioral assessments, and biometric data (e.g., wearable device metrics). Computational challenges include processing unstructured text from clinical narratives via natural language processing (NLP), harmonizing heterogeneous data formats, and training ensemble models to predict client progress across diverse populations. HPC resources are critical for managing the storage and computational demands of these tasks, particularly for parallelized hyperparameter optimization and validation across 10,000+ simulated client profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for ethically integrating sensitive counseling data into predictive analytics, (2) open-source tools to help clinicians identify clients at risk of treatment stagnation, and (3) preliminary evidence on how specific counseling strategies (e.g., cognitive-behavioral vs. person-centered techniques) interact with client characteristics in digital-era practice settings. By combining counseling psychology expertise with computational scalability, this work aims to bridge the gap between data-driven insights and human-centered care, ultimately supporting more responsive mental health services. All analyses will adhere to HIPAA standards and institutional review board protocols, with synthetic datasets generated for public dissemination.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide evaluations, referrals, and short-term counseling services to help people prevent or remediate personal problems, conflicts, and emotional crises. Includes instruction in human development, psychopathology, individual and group counseling, personality theory, career assessment, patient screening and referral, observation and testing techniques, interviewing skills, professional standards and ethics, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in somatic psychology, a discipline within counseling and applied psychology that emphasizes body-centered interventions for psychological well-being. The core research problem lies in the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to model the dynamic interplay between somatic practices (e.g., authentic movement, yoga, Tai Chi) and psychological outcomes. Current methodologies often rely on qualitative or small-scale quantitative analyses, limiting the ability to generalize findings or predict individualized therapeutic benefits. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating motion-capture data, biometric sensor inputs (heart rate variability, galvanic skin response), and psychometric assessments to create multimodal machine learning models. These models will analyze how specific somatic interventions modulate physiological and emotional states in real time, with a focus on identifying patterns of body-mind integration across diverse populations. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing high-frequency sensor data (sampled at 1000 Hz), training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to detect temporal relationships between movement sequences and stress reduction, and employing graph-based analytics to map bidirectional interactions between somatic engagement and self-reported psychological states. HPC resources are critical for handling the volume of multimodal data (estimated at 15 TB per cohort) and optimizing hyperparameters for deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include predictive models that quantify the efficacy of somatic techniques in reducing anxiety and enhancing emotional regulation, as well as open-source tools for clinicians to personalize body-based interventions. This work will establish a novel computational foundation for somatic psychology, bridging embodied therapeutic practices with data science—a significant advancement for both counseling research and applied mental health innovation. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary journals at the intersection of psychology, movement science, and computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on a holistic approach to solving interpersonal issues and psychological problems. Includes instruction in authentic movement, body-mind balance and integration, contact improvisation, dance, Pilates, Tai Chi, relaxation techniques, and Yoga.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in veterinary administrative systems through the development of a predictive framework for optimizing clinic workflow and resource allocation. Veterinary administrative services—spanning electronic health record management, client communication, inventory tracking, and regulatory compliance—increasingly generate complex, heterogeneous datasets that challenge conventional analytical tools. Current approaches lack the capacity to model dynamic interactions between administrative variables (e.g., appointment scheduling bottlenecks, staff-task mismatches, or supply chain delays) and clinical outcomes. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based simulations coupled with machine learning (ML) models trained on multi-year operational data from 14 regional veterinary clinics. The computational workflow will integrate anonymized records (1.2M+ patient visits), staff rostering patterns, and real-time inventory logs to simulate clinic operations under variable constraints. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess the impact of proposed interventions, such as dynamic staff reallocation algorithms or predictive inventory restocking triggers, while natural language processing submodels will analyze unstructured client communication data to identify patterns linked to service delays. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to process high-dimensional time-series data across nested spatial-temporal scales (clinic-level, regional, and seasonal variations) while maintaining low-latency feedback for iterative model refinement. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for veterinary administrators to simulate operational policies, predict resource gaps, and mitigate bottlenecks through scenario testing. By bridging computational modeling and veterinary management, this work aims to establish a methodological foundation for data-driven decision-making in a domain where administrative complexity increasingly impacts animal care quality and clinic sustainability.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary administrative services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The beauty and salon industry, a $190 billion global sector, faces unique operational challenges in customer flow optimization, service personalization, and inventory management that remain understudied in computational research. This project proposes developing an AI-driven simulation environment to model salon operations at unprecedented scale, integrating heterogeneous data streams including customer preference surveys (n=15,000+), real-time service duration logs from 200+ partner salons, and product supply chain datasets. The research problem centers on creating adaptive scheduling algorithms that balance stylist expertise, client retention patterns, and retail upsell opportunities while adhering to 43 distinct state/provincial licensing regulations encoded as constraint matrices. Computational methods will combine agent-based modeling of customer-stylist interactions with transformer neural networks trained on sequential service data to predict optimal service bundles. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: 1) Parallel processing of 10TB historical appointment records to identify latent demand patterns, 2) Multi-objective optimization across 14 competing operational parameters (e.g., stylist fatigue coefficients vs. peak pricing windows), and 3) Real-time simulation of 50,000+ possible daily scheduling configurations per salon location. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support framework that increases average salon profitability by 12-18% in pilot implementations while reducing no-show rates through personalized booking incentives. This interdisciplinary work bridges beauty industry praxis with computational social science methods, establishing new methodologies for service sector optimization that could extend to adjacent personal care fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares cosmetologists, hairstylists, and other personal grooming specialists to manage beauty parlors, shops, and full-service or specialized salons and to prepare for licensure as professional salon owners and operators.  Includes instruction in cosmetic services marketing and retailing; advertising and promotion; salon management; the cosmetic and salon supply industries; hiring, supervision, and labor relations; applicable business and professional laws and regulations; professional standards and image; and customer service.

abstract: Forest ecosystems face mounting pressures from climate change, invasive species, and shifting disturbance regimes, necessitating advanced tools to model dynamic forest responses at scale. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop spatially explicit, agent-based models simulating forest growth, pest outbreaks, and wildfire behavior across heterogeneous landscapes in the northeastern United States. Current management tools struggle to integrate real-time environmental data with long-term ecological processes, limiting predictive capacity for adaptive silviculture and conservation planning. Our computational approach will couple remote sensing datasets (LiDAR, multispectral imagery) with mechanistic tree growth algorithms and climate-driven disturbance models, calibrated using field data from long-term forest inventory plots. Parallelized simulations will quantify interactions between forest structure, harvest regimes, and disturbance probabilities under multiple climate scenarios, resolving processes at individual tree and stand scales across 10,000+ hectare landscapes. HPC resources are critical to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, optimize machine learning models for pest spread prediction, and run ensemble projections at temporal resolutions (daily steps over 50-year horizons) impractical on local clusters. Expected outcomes include open-source decision support tools to identify harvest schedules that balance timber yield with resilience to compound disturbances, as well as vulnerability maps prioritizing at-risk habitats for assisted migration or fuel reduction. By bridging gaps between empirical forestry data and computational scalability, this work will provide actionable frameworks for maintaining forest health and carbon sequestration capacity in managed landscapes. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with state forestry agencies and incorporated into Forest Technology curricula, training future technicians in computational resource management applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist foresters in the management and production of forest resources. Includes instruction in woods and field skills, tree identification, timber measurement, logging and timber harvesting, forest propagation and regeneration, forest fire-fighting, resource management, equipment operation and maintenance, record-keeping, sales and purchasing operations, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing plant health and landscape sustainability in managed green spaces through advanced computational modeling of dynamic plant-environment interactions. Current landscaping practices rely heavily on generalized guidelines for irrigation, nutrient application, and pest management, which often fail to account for micro-scale variations in soil composition, microclimate, and plant phenology. We propose to develop a high-resolution simulation framework integrating agent-based modeling of plant growth with real-time environmental data assimilation to predict outcomes under diverse management scenarios. The computational approach will couple process-based models of turfgrass and ornamental species physiology with machine learning algorithms trained on hyperspectral imaging data and IoT sensor feeds from experimental plots. High-performance computing resources are essential to parameterize species-specific responses across heterogeneous landscapes, simulate water-nutrient dynamics at sub-meter scales, and conduct Monte Carlo analyses of long-term management strategies under climate uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of prescribing spatially variable irrigation schedules, fertilizer application rates, and species selection matrices that minimize resource use while maintaining aesthetic and functional requirements. By enabling precision landscaping at scale, this research will provide commercial groundskeeping operations and urban planners with evidence-based tools to reduce water consumption by an estimated 15-25%, decrease chemical inputs, and enhance climate resilience in designed landscapes. The proposed work directly advances the agricultural sciences through novel applications of computational agroinformatics to ornamental horticulture, while maintaining strict exclusion of natural ecosystem conservation aspects to align with program scope.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the socio-cultural dynamics of 19th-century Protestant missionary networks in the Pacific Islands through the computational analysis of historical correspondence, ethnographic records, and mission society archives. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how missionary activities—shaped by localized interactions, language adaptation, and cross-cultural negotiation—contributed to long-term shifts in Indigenous social structures and regional connectivity. While traditional historiography has relied on qualitative close readings, this study employs high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze over 150,000 digitized pages of multilingual texts (letters, journals, reports) and relational metadata spanning 1820–1900. Natural language processing (NLP) models, adapted for historical dialects and non-Latin scripts, will identify patterns in missionary discourse related to resource allocation, conflict resolution, and knowledge transmission. Concurrently, network analysis will map the evolution of mission stations, supply routes, and interpersonal alliances, integrating GIS data on environmental constraints and preexisting Indigenous trade pathways. The computational workflow requires iterative training of custom transformer-based NLP architectures to handle code-switching in missionary texts (e.g., English-Tongan-Rarotongan mixes) and probabilistic graph modeling to reconstruct fragmented or anonymized correspondences. HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive tasks, including large-scale named entity recognition across heterogeneous documents and dynamic network visualizations of multi-decadal interactions. Expected outcomes include an open-access database linking missionary operations to demographic and ecological datasets, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural brokerage roles in colonial contact zones, and methodological innovations in computational humanities for under-resourced languages. By revealing how mission infrastructures both disrupted and catalyzed Indigenous transnational networks, this research aims to reframe scholarly debates on religious globalization while providing actionable models for heritage communities documenting complex colonial legacies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of religious outreach, social service and proselytization, and that prepares individuals for mission vocations. Includes instruction in theology, evangelism, preaching, medical and social mission work, missionary education, missionary aviation, emergency services, legal and political aspects of working in other countries, and preparation for ordination as missionaries.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in livestock populations present critical challenges to animal health, food security, and public health. Current surveillance and prediction methods for AMR dynamics are limited by the complexity of microbial communities, the diversity of resistance genes, and the nonlinear interactions between environmental, host, and management factors. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model AMR transmission pathways in livestock systems and predict hotspots of resistance gene proliferation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate metagenomic sequencing data from cattle gastrointestinal microbiomes, epidemiological records, and environmental metadata to train machine learning models identifying key drivers of resistance gene transfer. Agent-based simulations will then model the spatial and temporal spread of resistance under varying scenarios of antibiotic use, herd density, and management practices. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of large genomic datasets (>10 TB) and iterative simulation runs across parameter spaces, necessitating scalable GPU and CPU nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps of AMR risk in livestock populations, (2) actionable insights into optimizing antibiotic stewardship protocols, and (3) a publicly accessible toolkit for veterinarians and producers to evaluate farm-specific intervention strategies. By elucidating the systems-level dynamics of AMR, this work will directly support the development of precision veterinary technologies to mitigate resistance spread, enhance animal welfare, and reduce zoonotic transmission risks.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary or animal health technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance fire protection science by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model fire dynamics and suppression in complex urban and industrial environments. Current predictive models for fire spread, smoke transport, and suppression system effectiveness struggle to account for the interplay of multi-scale physics—such as turbulence, chemical kinetics, and heat transfer—in geometrically intricate settings like high-rise buildings, warehouses, or wildfire-urban interfaces. These limitations hinder the development of optimized fire safety protocols and real-time decision-support tools for emergency responders. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating large-eddy simulation (LES) with conjugate heat transfer modeling and machine learning-based parameterization of fuel sources. The simulations will resolve centimeter-scale flame structures while capturing room- or landscape-level fluid dynamics, enabled by adaptive mesh refinement and parallelized solvers. Validation will utilize experimental data from controlled burn tests and historical fire incident reports. A key innovation involves coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) outputs with reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively optimize suppression tactics, such as water mist deployment timing or ventilation strategies, under uncertain boundary conditions. The HPC resources will support ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainties in material flammability, weather variables, and human behavior factors. Expected outcomes include high-fidelity risk assessment templates for municipal fire codes, data-driven guidelines for retrofitting legacy structures, and open-source tools for simulating novel fire scenarios (e.g., lithium-ion battery fires in energy storage systems). By scaling these simulations to real-world complexity, this work aims to reduce preventable fire-related fatalities and economic losses while informing next-generation firefighting technologies and adaptive building design standards.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fire protection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex, dynamic interactions between biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors influencing end-of-life decision-making and bereavement outcomes. Thanatology, as a multidisciplinary field, lacks integrative computational frameworks capable of synthesizing heterogeneous datasets—ranging from physiological biomarkers of terminal illness to qualitative narratives of grief—to predict individualized trajectories of coping and care needs. Current approaches often silo these dimensions, limiting their utility in designing personalized interventions. The proposed research will develop a scalable agent-based model (ABM) simulating how variables such as cultural norms, access to palliative care, neurobiological stress responses, and social support networks co-evolve over time to shape outcomes for terminally ill patients and their families. The ABM will integrate anonymized electronic health records, longitudinal psychosocial surveys, and semi-structured interview data (processed via NLP techniques) to parameterize stochastic interactions across scales, from cellular senescence to community-level resource allocation. HPC resources are critical for optimizing the model’s parallelized architecture, enabling Monte Carlo simulations across diverse demographic and policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include identifying leverage points for improving equity in end-of-life care, predicting systemic bottlenecks in bereavement support systems, and generating hypotheses for targeted clinical trials. By bridging computational social science, biostatistics, and digital humanities methodologies, this work advances thanatology’s capacity to address emergent challenges such as global aging populations and culturally contested ethical frameworks for death. The resulting open-source tools will provide a foundation for interdisciplinary collaboration, fostering innovation in a field where computational rigor remains underdeveloped despite growing complexity in its research questions.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, philosophical, psychological, sociological, and theological aspects of death, dying, and bereavement. Includes instruction in counseling, ethics, grief, palliative and hospice care, philosophy, thanatology, and theology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for real-time, AI-driven music synthesis and spatial audio rendering, addressing the challenge of creating adaptive, immersive musical experiences that dynamically respond to performer input and environmental variables. Current tools for interactive music systems often lack the low-latency processing and computational scalability required for complex, multi-layered audio transformations in live performance contexts. The proposed research will implement machine learning models for timbre transfer and generative composition, coupled with wave-based acoustic simulations for 3D sound propagation. These methods demand high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on large datasets of spectral audio features, optimize real-time inference pipelines, and parallelize finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) calculations for spatial audio rendering in variable acoustic environments. The project will leverage GPU clusters for accelerated model training and distributed CPU resources for concurrent processing of audio streams across multiple spatial zones. Expected outcomes include an open-source software framework for adaptive music performance systems, validated through collaborations with ensemble musicians and electronic composers. This work will advance the technical foundations for next-generation interactive music technologies while contributing novel datasets of annotated performance interactions to the field. By enabling computationally intensive audio processing at sub-20ms latency thresholds, the proposed infrastructure will support new forms of technology-mediated artistic expression, bridging gaps between algorithmic composition, live performance, and immersive audience experiences. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome current bottlenecks in real-time audio network buffering, model parallelism, and large-scale acoustic simulation—challenges that exceed the capabilities of local workstations. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications in music technology conferences and public demonstrations at performing arts venues.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creative aspects of the blending of music and technology; and that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the composition, recording, synthesis, and performance of music; audio-visual production; scoring for film and multimedia; and software and multimedia development. Includes instruction in music theory, music history, composition, acoustics, recording technology, computer composition, electronic music synthesis, technology-based performance, 3D sound and spatial audio, and music business and law.

abstract: Abdominal radiology faces growing challenges in diagnosing complex disorders due to the heterogeneity of imaging data, variations in disease presentation, and the need for rapid, precise analysis in clinical workflows. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing advanced computational tools to automate and enhance the interpretation of abdominal and pelvic imaging studies, including CT, MRI, and ultrasound. A critical bottleneck in current research is the limited capacity to process large-scale, multi-modal datasets and integrate them with clinical and genomic data for predictive modeling. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models for lesion detection, organ segmentation, and disease classification, while enabling multi-institutional data harmonization. The computational approach will involve three phases: (1) curating and preprocessing a retrospective dataset of 50,000 anonymized abdominal imaging studies with linked clinical outcomes, (2) developing ensemble convolutional neural networks (CNNs) optimized for heterogeneous imaging protocols, and (3) implementing federated learning frameworks to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. HPC resources will be essential for managing GPU-accelerated model training, conducting hyperparameter optimization at scale, and running simulations to validate algorithm generalizability across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated quantitative analysis of abdominal pathologies—such as liver fibrosis staging, tumor response assessment, and inflammatory bowel disease tracking—that reduce inter-reader variability and diagnostic delays. Success will be measured by algorithm performance against expert radiologist consensus in validation studies, with benchmarks targeting ≥90% sensitivity and specificity for priority conditions. By enabling scalable analysis of imaging biomarkers, this work aims to accelerate translational research in abdominal radiology, support personalized treatment planning, and establish a computational infrastructure for future studies in oncologic, traumatic, and congenital disorders of the abdomen and pelvis.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the abdomen and pelvis in adults and children.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolutionary mechanisms underlying morphological and genomic adaptations in hominins through advanced computational modeling and large-scale data integration. A key challenge in physical and biological anthropology is disentangling the complex interplay of genetic, environmental, and selective pressures that shaped anatomical and physiological traits in early Homo and related taxa. Traditional analytical methods struggle to synthesize multidimensional datasets—including high-resolution 3D fossil morphology, ancient DNA fragments, paleoenvironmental proxies, and comparative primate genomics—while accounting for stochastic evolutionary processes. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based evolutionary simulations, Bayesian phylogenetic comparative models, and machine learning-driven morphometric analyses. The computational workflow will integrate fossil cranial and postcranial datasets from Pleistocene hominins with genomic data from modern and ancient populations to simulate adaptive scenarios under variable climatic and ecological conditions. Parallelized Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) algorithms will assess trait covariance and selection coefficients across simulated populations, while neural networks trained on geometric morphometric data will classify adaptive signatures in fragmentary fossil specimens. This approach requires significant memory allocation and GPU acceleration due to the iterative nature of simulations (10⁶+ agent generations) and the processing of terabyte-scale micro-CT scan repositories. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in environmental variability that precipitated locomotor and encephalization adaptations, reconstructing adaptive landscapes for key hominin lineages, and publishing open-source tools for fossil data integration. The project will advance methodological frameworks in evolutionary anthropology by enabling probabilistic reconciliation of morphological and genomic evidence at previously unfeasible scales, with implications for understanding human resilience to environmental stress.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and anthropology to the study of the adaptations, variability, and the evolution of human beings and their living and fossil relatives. Includes instructions in anthropology, human and mammalian anatomy, cell biology, paleontology, human culture and behavior, neuroscience, forensic anthropology, anatomical reconstruction, comparative anatomy, and laboratory science and methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for energy-efficient and high-performance computer hardware by optimizing thermal management and computational throughput in next-generation multi-core processors. As processor architectures scale in complexity—with increasing core counts, heterogeneous designs, and 3D integrated circuits (ICs)—traditional simulation tools struggle to model thermal-electronic interactions at sufficient fidelity. Current methods often oversimplify material properties, boundary conditions, and dynamic workloads, leading to suboptimal thermal solutions that limit device longevity and performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-physics computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for heat transfer modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for cooling system design, and machine learning (ML) to predict thermal behavior under variable operational scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute these simulations at scale, as the coupled models require parallel processing of fine-grained meshes (exceeding 10^8 elements) and iterative optimization across thousands of design parameters. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers (e.g., ANSYS Mechanical, OpenFOAM) and ML libraries (TensorFlow, PyTorch) to explore novel cooling topologies, adaptive voltage-frequency scaling policies, and material configurations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting thermal runaway thresholds in 3D ICs, a dataset of optimized cooling strategies for heterogeneous architectures, and open-source tools for co-simulating electronic and thermal performance. These results will directly inform the design of energy-efficient processors for data centers and edge computing devices, reducing cooling energy costs by an estimated 15–30% compared to conventional approaches. By integrating computational modeling with hardware prototyping, this work advances the broader goal of sustainable computing while providing students in Computer Hardware Technology with hands-on experience in cutting-edge simulation-driven design methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: The increasing complexity of student mental health needs in higher education requires data-driven approaches to optimize counseling interventions. Current research lacks scalable methods to analyze multifaceted datasets encompassing counseling interactions, academic performance, demographic variables, and longitudinal outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models that identify predictors of counseling efficacy and student well-being trajectories. The research will integrate anonymized records from university counseling centers, academic databases, and student surveys using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage and process heterogeneous data at scale. Machine learning techniques, including ensemble classifiers and neural networks, will be employed to model nonlinear relationships between intervention strategies and student outcomes. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze unstructured text from counselor notes to quantify therapeutic themes and their association with clinical improvements. Computational demands include training deep learning architectures on text corpora exceeding 10 million tokens, running Monte Carlo simulations to assess intervention scenarios, and optimizing hyperparameters across multimodal datasets. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for personalizing counseling approaches, evidence-based recommendations for resource allocation in student services, and open-source tools for educational researchers analyzing mixed-methods data. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance the precision and scalability of research in student counseling, ultimately supporting institutional efforts to enhance mental health support systems.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance cross-linguistic research on under-documented languages, focusing on computational analysis of syntactic diversity and dialectal variation. While linguistic theory has long relied on manual annotation and small-scale corpora, the increasing availability of digitized texts and speech data from diverse languages presents an opportunity to systematically investigate patterns in morphology, syntax, and semantic structures at scale. However, processing these datasets—which include non-standardized orthographies, code-switching phenomena, and sparse annotations—requires significant computational power and specialized NLP pipelines. Our team will develop parallelized workflows to analyze multilingual corpora spanning 15+ languages from geographically dispersed regions, including endangered and minority languages with limited digital resources. Key computational methods include transformer-based models adapted for low-resource language scenarios, graph-based algorithms for mapping syntactic dependencies across typologically distinct languages, and probabilistic clustering techniques to identify latent dialect boundaries. The HPC environment is critical for training cross-linguistic embeddings, running large-scale simulations of language contact scenarios, and processing high-resolution audio data for phonetic alignment. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated linguistic features, new metrics for quantifying syntactic complexity, and computational models that illuminate historical language convergence patterns. This work will directly support efforts to preserve linguistic diversity while advancing methodological frameworks for comparative analysis in multilingual contexts. By integrating computational rigor with theoretical linguistics, the project aims to address critical gaps in understanding how structural language features evolve and interact, with implications for both academic research and community-led language revitalization initiatives.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more modern foreign languages that is not specific as to the name of the language(s) studied; that is otherwise undifferentiated; or that introduces students to language studies at the basic/elementary level.

abstract: Endocrine disorders such as diabetes, obesity, and thyroid dysfunction arise from complex interactions between genetic susceptibility, environmental factors, and metabolic dysregulation. While advances in high-throughput technologies have enabled large-scale generation of multi-omics data, integrating these heterogeneous datasets to uncover disease mechanisms remains computationally prohibitive. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular drivers of polygenic endocrine disorders. We propose a computational framework combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS), deep learning-based analysis of epigenomic and transcriptomic data, and dynamic network modeling of metabolic pathways. These methods will be applied to a cohort of 10,000 patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity, integrating genomic variants, DNA methylation profiles, single-cell RNA sequencing, and longitudinal clinical data. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, training of multimodal neural networks for predictive phenotyping, and stochastic simulations of hormone-receptor interactions under varying metabolic states. The HPC environment is essential for enabling scalable data integration, reducing model training times from weeks to days, and performing millions of molecular dynamics simulations to identify allosteric binding sites. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel genetic-epigenetic interactions influencing insulin resistance, predictive models of diabetes progression, and candidate therapeutic targets for adrenal dysfunction. This research will provide a computational foundation for precision endocrinology, enabling data-driven stratification of patient subgroups and optimization of hormone-based therapies. The requested resources will directly support the development of open-source tools for endocrine research, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational domains.
cip_definition: Research on disorders of the internal (endocrine) glands such as the thyroid and adrenal glands, and to deal with disorders such as diabetes, metabolic and nutritional disorders, obesity, pituitary diseases, and menstrual and sexual problems. Requires prior completion of a residency program in internal medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the design, fabrication, and performance of custom wood components and cabinetry, addressing inefficiencies in traditional cabinetmaking workflows. While modern Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machinery has improved precision, challenges persist in predicting material behavior, minimizing waste, and ensuring structural durability across diverse environmental conditions. Current industry practices rely heavily on empirical testing and iterative physical prototyping, which are time-intensive and resource-consuming. This research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate and analyze wood composite mechanics, moisture-induced deformation, and stress distribution in complex joinery systems. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will model the anisotropic properties of hardwoods, engineered lumber, and adhesives under varying thermal and hygroscopic loads. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and experimental datasets to predict optimal toolpaths for CNC machinery, reducing material waste during cutting operations. Additionally, generative design frameworks will explore topology-optimized structures that balance weight, strength, and aesthetic requirements. The computational workflows will integrate parametric modeling tools to enable rapid prototyping of custom millwork designs. By leveraging HPC resources, this project aims to establish predictive models that accelerate design validation, mitigate production risks, and extend the functional lifespan of architectural woodwork. Outcomes will include open-access simulation templates tailored to cabinetmaking applications and a database of material performance profiles under environmental stressors. This work bridges gaps between manual craftsmanship and computational engineering, offering scalable solutions for sustainable manufacturing. The requested computing resources will support large-scale parallel simulations and data-intensive optimization tasks, which are infeasible on local workstations due to memory and processing constraints. Results will be disseminated through industry workshops and integrated into the academic program’s curriculum, equipping students with advanced digital fabrication skills.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate and repair industrial woodworking machinery, and to use such machinery to design and fabricate wooden components and complete articles.

abstract: This project addresses critical gaps in understanding the evolutionary relationships and biogeographic history of understudied plant clades in tropical montane ecosystems, where rapid diversification and complex biogeographic processes have generated persistent taxonomic discordance. Traditional systematic approaches, limited by insufficient computational power and restrictive modeling assumptions, struggle to resolve phylogenies for these lineages, hindering conservation prioritization and macroevolutionary studies. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a novel integrative framework combining genome-scale phylogenomic datasets, fossil-informed divergence time estimation, and probabilistic biogeographic reconstruction. Key computational challenges include Bayesian inference under complex multispecies coalescent models to account for incomplete lineage sorting, which requires millions of MCMC iterations across terabyte-scale genomic alignment matrices. Parallelized likelihood calculations will enable comparative analyses of diversification rates across heterogeneous environmental gradients, while machine learning approaches will identify traits associated with speciation pulses. The project will deploy containerized workflows on GPU-accelerated nodes to efficiently process phenotypic, geographic, and genomic data from 500+ species. Anticipated outcomes include (1) resolved phylogenetic hypotheses for three contentious angiosperm families, (2) spatially explicit models linking Andean orogeny to Neotropical diversification, and (3) open-access pipelines for scalable analysis of complex systematic datasets. By overcoming current computational barriers to synthesizing multidimensional biological data, this work will establish new best practices for testing evolutionary hypotheses in species-rich regions and provide critical baseline data for biodiversity monitoring initiatives. The requested resources directly address the prohibitive runtime and memory requirements that currently limit probabilistic analyses of large systematic datasets in non-model organisms.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model the dispersion and health impacts of airborne particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) in urban environments, with a focus on integrating traffic emissions, construction activity, and meteorological variables. Current models often oversimplify source interactions or rely on coarse spatial resolutions, limiting their utility for pinpointing exposure risks and designing targeted mitigation strategies. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling approach combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD), agent-based transportation simulations, and machine learning-driven source attribution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve micro-scale pollutant transport (1–10 m resolution) across entire city districts while incorporating real-time traffic flow data and time-varying emission profiles. The CFD simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers to model airflow turbulence and particle deposition, validated against sensor networks deployed in partnership with municipal agencies. Concurrently, graph neural networks will analyze spatial-temporal correlations between pollution hotspots and infrastructure dynamics, such as traffic congestion patterns or construction timelines. Expected outcomes include an open-source modeling platform capable of predicting acute exposure risks for vulnerable populations and testing the efficacy of interventions like green infrastructure placement or traffic rerouting. This work directly supports environmental health equity goals by providing urban planners and public health agencies with actionable, hyperlocal data. The computational demands of simultaneously running ensemble simulations, processing terabyte-scale sensor datasets, and training deep learning models necessitate access to HPC clusters with parallelized workflows and large-memory nodes. Results will advance predictive modeling in environmental engineering while addressing a critical gap in community-scale air quality management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: Personalized dietary planning for individuals with specific nutritional needs requires balancing complex variables, including medical requirements, cultural preferences, budget constraints, and sensory acceptability. Current manual approaches to meal optimization are labor-intensive, prone to suboptimal outcomes, and lack scalability. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to automate and enhance meal planning processes for dietitians, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges. The research will focus on integrating multi-objective optimization algorithms with machine learning models trained on diverse datasets, including nutritional databases, clinical guidelines, patient health records, and food preference surveys. Key computational tasks include large-scale combinatorial optimization to generate meal combinations that meet nutrient targets, predictive modeling of patient acceptance and adherence, and simulations of long-term health outcomes under varying dietary scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration across high-dimensional parameter spaces, real-time adaptation to dynamic constraints (e.g., ingredient availability), and validation through Monte Carlo simulations of population-level dietary impacts. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dietitian assistants that optimizes meal plans 50–100x faster than manual methods while improving adherence rates by quantitatively incorporating patient preferences. The project will further contribute novel datasets mapping regional food costs to nutritional density, supporting equity-focused meal planning. By computationally addressing the trade-offs between clinical efficacy, practicality, and patient satisfaction, this work aims to establish evidence-based protocols for scalable, personalized nutrition interventions. Successful implementation could reduce healthcare costs associated with diet-related chronic diseases while enhancing the operational capacity of dietetic professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address challenges in optimizing industrial-scale chemical processes through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial chemical production often involves complex multiphase reactions, heat and mass transfer phenomena, and fluid dynamics that are difficult to predict using conventional experimental methods or simplified simulations. Current limitations in modeling these systems at scale result in suboptimal reactor designs, energy inefficiencies, and safety risks during scale-up from laboratory to production environments. To overcome these barriers, this research will develop high-fidelity simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), reactive transport modeling, and machine learning-driven optimization. The project will focus on catalytic reactor systems for sustainable chemical manufacturing, incorporating heterogeneous catalysis and non-Newtonian fluid behavior. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of multiscale phenomena—from molecular-scale surface reactions to meter-scale reactor hydrodynamics—using open-source tools such as OpenFOAM and LAMMPS, coupled with custom code for reaction network analysis. Validation will utilize experimental datasets from collaborative industry partners, including temperature profiles and reaction yields. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing reactor geometry, operating conditions, and catalyst configurations to maximize product selectivity while minimizing energy consumption and waste generation. The computational framework will also assess process safety by simulating failure scenarios, such as thermal runaway or flow instabilities. By bridging the gap between laboratory research and industrial implementation, this work aims to advance sustainable chemical manufacturing practices, reduce environmental impacts, and provide a template for HPC-driven process intensification in the chemical engineering technology sector. Results will be disseminated through open-access datasets and workshops to support workforce training in computational process engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for analyzing narrative structures and audience engagement patterns in theatrical and cinematic scripts. While traditional scriptwriting pedagogy emphasizes craft and intuition, there remains a gap in quantitatively modeling how narrative choices—such as dialogue pacing, emotional arc dynamics, and character network evolution—affect perceived dramatic tension or viewer immersion. This research proposes a hybrid methodology combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML), and agent-based audience response simulations to systematically evaluate scripts at scale. Scripts will be parsed into structured data (e.g., sentiment trajectories, interaction frequencies, temporal scene shifts) using transformer-based NLP models, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively simulate hypothetical audience reactions to narrative variations. Agent-based models will further explore how demographic or cultural variables might modulate engagement. The computational intensity of training multi-modal ML architectures, coupled with the need for parallelized simulation of thousands of narrative permutations, necessitates HPC resources for viable runtime. Expected outcomes include: (1) a reproducible pipeline for quantifying narrative “efficacy” metrics correlated with historical box office or critical success, (2) an open-access toolset to help playwrights and screenwriters test structural edits against predictive engagement models, and (3) foundational datasets linking linguistic features in scripts to empirical audience response studies. By bridging computational analysis with dramatic theory, this work aims to advance both the academic study of narrative mechanics and the practical craft of script development, offering novel insights into how data-driven methods can coexist with artistic intuition in performing arts education and practice.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for communicating dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the composition of creative written works for the theatre, film, and/or television. Includes instruction in creative writing craft, scene writing, script development, stage and/or camera instructions, line and moment analysis, script reading, script editing, and the creation of full productions.

abstract: Turfgrass systems are critical components of agricultural and recreational landscapes, yet their sustainability is increasingly threatened by abiotic stressors such as drought, heat, and soil salinity, as well as biotic challenges like pathogen outbreaks. Traditional approaches to developing stress-resistant turfgrass varieties and optimizing management practices are limited by the complex interplay of genetic, environmental, and microbial factors influencing turf health. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance genomic and systems-level analyses of turfgrass resilience, enabling data-driven solutions for sustainable turf management. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic profiling, and soil microbiome metagenomics to identify genetic markers and microbial consortia associated with stress tolerance in key turfgrass species. Machine learning models will be trained on these multi-omics datasets to predict optimal genotype-environment-management combinations under projected climate scenarios. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model turfgrass growth dynamics and pest interactions at landscape scales. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallel processing for genome assembly, population genetics analyses, and iterative model optimization, necessitating HPC capabilities for handling terabytes of sequencing data and complex ecological simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of candidate genes for breeding programs targeting drought and disease resistance, (2) predictive frameworks for precision turf management, and (3) open-source tools for simulating turfgrass ecosystem responses to environmental change. By elucidating the genetic and ecological determinants of turfgrass resilience, this research will directly support the development of climate-adapted turf varieties and inform sustainable land-use practices in urban and agricultural settings, with translational benefits for the $40 billion global turf industry. The requested computing resources will enable transformative advances in bridging genomic discovery with applied agronomic solutions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
