cip_definition: A program that focuses on turfgrasses and related groundcover plants and prepares individuals to develop ornamental or recreational grasses and related products; plant, transplant, and manage grassed areas; and to produce and store turf used for transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable plant sciences, genetics of grasses, turf science, use analysis, turf management, and related economics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling and optimizing integrated electromechanical systems for advanced manufacturing applications. Electromechanical systems, particularly those involving real-time feedback control and multiphysics interactions, require high-fidelity simulations to capture nonlinear dynamics, thermal-electrical coupling, and mechanical wear—a task that exceeds the capabilities of standard computing resources. The research focuses on developing a scalable framework to simulate automated robotic assembly lines with embedded sensor networks, where electromechanical actuators, power electronics, and thermal management systems interact dynamically. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management and circuit simulation tools for power distribution stability. A key innovation involves the integration of machine learning algorithms to optimize control parameters in hybrid systems, reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy. The project will validate models against experimental data from a laboratory-scale electromechanical testbed, iterating between simulations and physical measurements to refine predictive capabilities. Expected outcomes include a validated multiphysics simulation toolkit for electromechanical system design, data-driven control strategies to minimize energy consumption in automated processes, and insights into failure modes under extreme operational conditions. These results will directly support the development of more reliable, energy-efficient manufacturing systems, advancing the industrial application of smart electromechanical integration. The requested HPC allocation is critical to handle the ∼10^6-degree-of-freedom models and the iterative optimization workflows, which demand parallel processing capabilities and large-memory nodes unavailable on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the problems associated with combining electrical and mechanical components with special emphasis on manufacturing and automated processes. Includes instruction in applied mechanics, instrumentation and monitoring, machine design, automated control techniques, fluid and thermal dynamics, circuit analysis, and solid state electronics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis and modeling of complex jazz improvisation patterns and ensemble interactions, a critical challenge in jazz studies. While traditional analytical methods in musicology rely on manual transcription and subjective interpretation, the nonlinear, real-time dynamics of jazz performance—particularly in collective improvisation—resist reduction to static scores or isolated parameters. This research addresses this gap by developing computational tools to process and analyze large-scale audio datasets of historic and contemporary jazz recordings, capturing temporal, harmonic, and timbral features at scale. Machine learning models, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer architectures, will be trained to identify stylistic signatures of improvisational vocabularies across eras (e.g., swing, bebop, avant-garde) and simulate interaction dynamics within ensembles. Additionally, agent-based models will be employed to study emergent behaviors in improvisational decision-making, incorporating harmonic rulesets derived from jazz theory and real performer data. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of high-resolution audio (10,000+ hours), GPU-accelerated model training, and large-memory nodes for real-time simulation of multi-agent musical interactions. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for computational jazz analysis, new insights into the evolution of improvisational practices, and predictive models to inform pedagogical frameworks for ensemble communication. By bridging data-driven methods and musicological expertise, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of jazz as a dynamic, collaborative art form while preserving its intangible cultural practices through quantitatively grounded research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study and master the performance and composition of Jazz. Includes instruction in the history of Jazz and related musical styles such as the Blues, Jazz composition and theory, improvisation, Jazz instrument and ensemble performance, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict health outcomes in family practice nursing, with a focus on optimizing personalized care strategies for diverse family units. Family practice nurses manage complex, multi-generational health data influenced by genetic, environmental, and socio-economic factors, yet existing tools often lack the capacity to integrate these variables dynamically. The research problem centers on the need for scalable, predictive models to identify at-risk populations and tailor interventions within family systems. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), demographic datasets, and real-time biometric data from wearable devices. Machine learning algorithms—including ensemble methods and graph neural networks—will be employed to model familial health trajectories, account for interdependencies among family members, and simulate the impact of targeted nursing interventions. Computational challenges include managing heterogeneous data formats, ensuring privacy-preserving data linkage, and running iterative simulations to test care scenarios. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing for training complex models, while agent-based simulations will replicate family health dynamics under varying clinical and social conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to stratify families by chronic disease risk (e.g., diabetes, hypertension) based on aggregated genetic and lifestyle factors, (2) a decision-support system for nurses to prioritize interventions, and (3) open-source code for replicable family health analytics. This work will advance nursing science by integrating computational precision into family-centric care, directly supporting the program’s emphasis on holistic practice and health assessment. The requested resources are critical to handling the project’s data volume (~50 TB of structured/unstructured EHRs) and computational demands, which exceed the capacity of local servers. Findings will inform clinical guidelines and policy recommendations for scalable family health monitoring in primary care settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for analyzing high-dimensional biomedical data with complex spatial and temporal dependencies, addressing critical gaps in current biostatistical models for public health applications. Traditional approaches often struggle with incomplete data, non-linear covariate interactions, and computational bottlenecks when modeling disease spread or treatment outcomes across large populations. We propose a novel integration of Bayesian hierarchical modeling with machine learning techniques, specifically focusing on spatially varying coefficient models and recurrent neural networks, to improve prediction of disease progression patterns while quantifying uncertainty. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources for three core tasks: (1) parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for spatial process parameter estimation across multi-terabyte electronic health record datasets, (2) distributed training of neural networks for temporal pattern recognition in streaming wearable device data, and (3) ensemble model validation through large-scale simulation studies comparing proposed methods to existing survival analysis frameworks. Key challenges include optimizing memory usage for sparse spatial covariance matrices and developing hybrid CPU-GPU architectures for mixed model types. The project will utilize open-source tools (R/TensorFlow, STAN, and PyTorch) within containerized environments to ensure reproducibility. Expected outcomes include an open-access software package for spatiotemporal health analytics and new methodology papers addressing computational efficiency in missing data scenarios. This work directly supports precision public health initiatives by enabling real-time analysis of heterogeneous data streams from municipal health systems, with immediate applications to COVID-19 sequelae monitoring and cardiovascular disease risk stratification. Successful implementation requires dedicated HPC allocation for sustained multi-node computations, as preliminary benchmarks indicate a minimum need for 64-core parallelization with 512GB RAM to handle metropolitan-scale epidemiological datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of descriptive and inferential statistics to biomedical research and clinical, public health, and industrial issues related to human populations. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, modeling, clinical trials methodology, disease and survival analysis, longitudinal analysis, missing data analysis, spatial analysis, computer tomography, biostatistics consulting, and applications to such topics as genetics, oncology, pharmacokinetics, physiology, neurobiology, and biophysics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing large-scale regulatory text corpora to identify latent patterns in compliance risk across evolving legal and policy environments. While compliance law is traditionally rooted in qualitative analysis, the increasing volume, velocity, and complexity of global regulations—coupled with the dynamic interplay between legal jurisdictions and industry-specific standards—necessitates advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on the inadequacy of manual or conventional digital tools to systematically map regulatory interdependencies, predict emergent compliance obligations, or model the cascading effects of policy changes in multi-jurisdictional contexts. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models on a curated dataset of 15 million regulatory documents, including statutes, case law, enforcement actions, and cross-border agreements from 2000–2023. The computational approach integrates three phases: 1) semantic clustering of obligations using fine-tuned BERT variants to detect conceptual overlaps and conflicts, 2) temporal network analysis of regulatory influence across jurisdictions via dynamic graph neural networks, and 3) agent-based simulations of compliance cascades under hypothetical policy scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for processing terabyte-scale text datasets, optimizing transformer architectures with domain-specific legal embeddings, and running parallelized simulations across 10,000+ parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated compliance horizon scanning, validated against historical enforcement patterns in financial services and healthcare compliance case studies. By quantifying previously opaque relationships between regulatory actors and obligations, this work aims to advance computational legal analytics as a distinct interdisciplinary field while providing practical frameworks for adaptive compliance strategy design. The resource-intensive nature of training legal language models and simulating multi-agent regulatory ecosystems fundamentally requires the memory bandwidth, parallel processing capabilities, and scalable storage solutions uniquely afforded by HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in compliance, ethics, internal monitoring, regulatory affairs, and related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making and operational planning for critical incident response scenarios, such as active threats, hostage negotiations, and coordinated terrorist attacks. Current protocols rely heavily on static playbooks and experiential knowledge, which may fail to account for dynamic variables such as shifting threat behaviors, environmental complexity, and real-time resource constraints. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate hyper-realistic incident scenarios, integrating multi-agent modeling, geospatial analytics, and behavioral psychology datasets. Agent-based models will simulate interactions between responders, suspects, bystanders, and infrastructure under varying conditions, while machine learning algorithms will identify patterns in historical incident data to predict escalation risks and intervention efficacy. Computational fluid dynamics modules will model crowd movements and hazardous material dispersion in enclosed spaces, and network analysis tools will evaluate communication bottlenecks during multi-agency operations. The simulations will be iteratively refined using anonymized case data from law enforcement partners, with sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of variables like response time, team composition, and environmental layout. Outcomes will include a decision-support toolkit for pre-incident planning, real-time resource allocation dashboards, and training modules for scenario-based preparedness drills. By bridging computational modeling and tactical response strategies, this work aims to enhance operational flexibility, reduce collateral risks, and improve cross-agency interoperability during high-stakes incidents. The scale and complexity of these simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure to manage parallelized scenario testing, large-scale data integration, and real-time visualization of multi-dimensional incident parameters.
cip_title: Critical Incident Response/ Special Police Operations
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for dealing with police emergencies such as hostage situations, bomb threats, barricades and terrorist incidents. Includes instruction in crisis management, command procedures, incident containment, information collection and debriefing, first responder negotiation, victim and criminal psychology, site survey and surveillance, special weapons and tactics, interagency communications and joint operations, pre-confrontation and contingency planning, assault and rescue operations, security and crowd control, media relations, and post-operation procedures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modeling subsurface geological processes at high resolution presents a critical computational challenge in understanding lithospheric dynamics and associated seismic hazards. This project seeks to advance the simulation of fault zone interactions and stress propagation within heterogeneous rock matrices through the development of a scalable, physics-informed numerical framework. The research problem centers on resolving the multiscale coupling between long-term tectonic strain accumulation and short-term seismic rupture events, which requires capturing nonlinear material behaviors across spatial scales from meters to kilometers and temporal scales spanning seconds to millennia. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining finite element discretization with adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) and parallelized iterative solvers. The model will integrate constitutive relationships derived from laboratory rock mechanics data, enabling explicit representation of friction laws, fracture propagation, and poroelastic effects. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the anticipated 10^8–10^9 degree-of-freedom simulations, leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes for matrix assembly and distributed memory architectures via MPI for domain decomposition. Validation against geodetic InSAR datasets and historical seismic catalogs will constrain model parameters through inverse optimization techniques. Expected outcomes include: (1) quantification of stress transfer thresholds between adjacent fault segments in active tectonic regions, (2) probabilistic forecasts of rupture cascades under varying fluid injection scenarios, and (3) open-source release of optimized solver routines for the geodynamics community. The computational infrastructure requested will enable unprecedented resolution of strain localization patterns near critical mineralogical phase boundaries, directly contributing to improved seismic hazard assessment frameworks. By elucidating how microscale rock properties influence macroscale tectonic behavior, this work bridges a fundamental gap in physics-based earthquake forecasting while providing generalizable methods for HPC-enabled geomechanical modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and relationships between the solids, liquids and gases comprising it.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of geochemical and petrological processes governing magma crystallization, metamorphic reactions, and hydrothermal mineralization through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations. Current models struggle to integrate the multi-scale complexity of these systems, which span atomic-scale mineral-fluid interactions to kilometer-scale fluid flow in evolving tectonic settings. We propose to develop a coupled computational framework combining quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT) calculations, reactive transport modeling, and machine learning (ML) to simulate geochemical reactions and their feedbacks with geological processes. The HPC resources will enable DFT simulations of silicate melt-crystal equilibria at mantle conditions, parameterize reactive transport models for hydrothermal systems, and train ML surrogates to accelerate equilibrium calculations across variable pressure-temperature-composition regimes. These components will be integrated into open-source geodynamic codes (e.g., ASPECT) to simulate magma chamber evolution and ore-forming systems at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. Key challenges include scaling hybrid DFT-continuum workflows across GPU/CPU architectures and managing petabyte-scale mineralogical datasets. Success will provide quantitative constraints on the role of volatile fluxes in porphyry copper formation, metamorphic decarbonation rates in orogenic systems, and the links between melt chemistry and volcanic eruption dynamics. The outcomes will directly support mineral exploration strategies and improve assessments of geothermal energy resources. By bridging atomic-to-regional scales, this work addresses fundamental gaps in predicting the behavior of Earth’s lithosphere under dynamic thermal and chemical forcings. The requested computing allocation is critical to achieving the necessary resolution and ensemble sizes to reduce uncertainties in model predictions, with broader impacts including publicly accessible datasets and optimized codes for the geosciences community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the igneous, metamorphic, and hydrothermal processes within the earth and the mineral, fluid, rock, and ore deposits resulting from them. Includes instruction in mineralogy, crystallography, petrology, volcanology, economic geology, meteoritics, geochemical reactions, deposition, compound transformation, core studies, theoretical geochemistry, computer applications, and laboratory studies.

abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events underscore the need for advanced predictive frameworks that capture multiscale interactions between atmospheric and oceanic processes. Current global climate models often inadequately represent stochastic variability in subgrid-scale phenomena, such as turbulent ocean eddies and convective cloud dynamics, which contribute to the onset and amplification of extreme events. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a novel mathematical framework that integrates stochastic parameterizations into a high-resolution Earth system model, enabling the explicit representation of uncertainty across spatiotemporal scales. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the proposed approach will implement a hierarchy of stochastic partial differential equations to model unresolved processes, coupled with ensemble-based data assimilation techniques to refine predictive accuracy. Key computational challenges include the parallelization of multiscale solvers, optimization of memory-intensive ensemble workflows, and real-time analysis of petabyte-scale output datasets. The research will focus on two case studies: extreme precipitation forecasting in tropical coastal regions and the dynamics of marine heatwave propagation in boundary current systems. By quantifying the interplay between deterministic forcings and stochastic perturbations, this work aims to advance the theoretical understanding of tipping points in coupled atmosphere-ocean dynamics while delivering actionable improvements in operational forecasting tools. Outcomes will include open-source software modules for stochastic climate modeling, a publicly accessible ensemble dataset for community-driven diagnostics, and foundational insights into the role of multiplicative noise in non-equilibrium geophysical systems. This interdisciplinary effort sits at the nexus of applied mathematics, physical oceanography, and climate science, addressing a critical vulnerability in current predictive capabilities through innovative numerical frameworks enabled by cutting-edge computational resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to atmospheric and oceanic problems. Includes instruction in chemistry, physics, atmospheric/ocean dynamics, climatology, weather simulation, climate modeling, mathematics, oceanography, and atmospheric science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Islamic theological and juridical discourse through computational text mining and network analysis of classical Arabic texts. The research problem centers on tracing doctrinal developments across time, regions, and schools of thought in Islam, as reflected in foundational works (e.g., Qur’anic exegeses, hadith commentaries, legal treatises) and later scholarly debates. Current scholarship relies heavily on manual close reading, limiting the scale at which patterns, influences, and conceptual shifts can be systematically identified, particularly across multilingual corpora spanning 14 centuries. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining optical character recognition (OCR) correction for digitized manuscripts, semantic embedding models tailored to classical Arabic, and graph-based network analyses to map intellectual lineages and thematic divergences. The HPC infrastructure is critical for training transformer-based language models on curated datasets of primary sources (∼10^7 words) and secondary literature, as well as for running large-scale simulations of textual transmission and influence networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) a searchable database linking key doctrinal concepts to their temporal, geographic, and sectarian contexts; (2) quantitative visualizations of epistemological shifts in Islamic philosophy; and (3) open-source tools for Arabic-script manuscript processing. By enabling systematic analysis at unprecedented scales, this work aims to reveal understudied connections between early Islamic thought and later scholastic traditions while providing a replicable computational framework for interdisciplinary religious studies. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multilingual text corpora, and parallelized network analysis workflows requiring ∼25,000 core-hours over 12 months.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Islam as preached by the Prophet Muhammad in 6th century Arabia and subsequently interpreted and elaborated by Islamic scholars and others; together with the cultural and social milieu related to the faith in various periods, localities, and branches. Includes instruction in Islamic scripture and related written authorities and commentaries

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing operational workflows in veterinary office management—a domain underexplored in computational research despite its growing complexity. Veterinary practices face unique challenges, including dynamic patient scheduling, inventory management for diverse medical supplies, and compliance with rapidly evolving healthcare regulations. Existing software tools often lack the capacity to integrate multi-source data (e.g., client demographics, seasonal disease trends, staff availability) or simulate scenarios at scale. The research problem centers on designing an adaptive decision-support system that balances efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and compliance in real-world veterinary administrative settings. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate clinic operations under variable constraints, such as emergency caseload surges or supply chain disruptions. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of hypothetical scenarios, training ML models on synthetic and anonymized historical data to identify patterns in resource bottlenecks or staff burnout risks. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) will be applied to automate analysis of regulatory documents (e.g., state veterinary board guidelines) and update compliance protocols dynamically. The expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for veterinary administrators to forecast operational challenges, allocate resources proactively, and reduce overhead costs by 15–20% in simulated environments. By integrating computational social science methods with veterinary management principles, this project fills a critical gap in non-STEM HPC applications, offering a scalable model for small-to-medium healthcare enterprises. Results will be validated through partnerships with regional veterinary clinics, ensuring practical relevance and fostering a new research niche at the intersection of computational optimization and animal healthcare administration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a veterinary office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, veterinary care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Otolaryngologic disorders, such as head and neck cancers, chronic sinusitis, and hearing loss, involve complex interactions between genetic, molecular, and structural factors. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to integrate multimodal data—including high-resolution imaging, genomic sequencing, and patient-specific clinical records—at scales necessary to uncover actionable insights. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that elucidate disease mechanisms and optimize therapeutic strategies. Using machine learning algorithms, we will analyze multi-omics datasets from tumor biopsies to identify biomarkers predictive of treatment response and metastasis in squamous cell carcinoma. Concurrently, computational fluid dynamics simulations will model sinonasal airflow in chronic rhinosinusitis patients, enabling personalized surgical planning to restore physiologic function. HPC infrastructure is critical to process terabytes of imaging data, perform real-time probabilistic network analyses on genomic interactions, and execute large-scale parameter sweeps in patient-specific anatomies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for oncology decision support, optimized surgical approaches for airway disorders, and open-source tools for integrating heterogeneous clinical data. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this research aims to accelerate translational discoveries in otolaryngology, bridging gaps between molecular insights and patient-centered care.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians to diagnose and provide medical and/or surgical therapy or prevention of diseases, allergies, neoplasms, deformities, disorders, and injuries of the ears, nose, sinuses, throat, respiratory and upper alimentary systems, face, jaws, and the other head and neck systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the cascading impacts of climate change on coupled human-natural systems in critical watershed regions. As climate variability intensifies, managing water resources sustainably requires resolving complex interactions between hydrological processes, land-use decisions, and policy frameworks. Current regional-scale models lack the resolution to capture feedback loops between localized ecosystem stressors (e.g., deforestation, urbanization) and basin-wide hydrological shifts, limiting predictive capacity for adaptive management. To address this gap, we propose a nested modeling framework integrating high-resolution climate projections (1 km² grid), agent-based land-use simulations, and hydrodynamic models of sediment transport and nutrient cycling. The computational workflow will parallelize ensemble runs across climate scenarios (CMIP6 datasets), parameterize stakeholder decision-making via machine learning-calibrated agents, and quantify uncertainties using Monte Carlo methods. HPC resources are essential to process multi-terabyte geospatial datasets, execute computationally intensive fluid dynamics solvers (e.g., ANUGA for flood modeling), and iteratively optimize policy interventions under stochastic climate forcings. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of watershed “tipping points” where current management strategies fail under projected drought-flood cycles, (2) spatially explicit risk maps to prioritize conservation investments, and (3) open-source policy simulation tools for evaluating trade-offs between agricultural runoff regulations, urban water allocations, and ecosystem health. By quantifying how localized decisions propagate through socio-hydrological networks, this work will provide actionable insights for reconciling water security goals with biodiversity conservation in governance frameworks. The scale and resolution of these analyses are computationally intractable without HPC infrastructure, necessitating allocations for GPU-accelerated model training and distributed memory processing of 4D environmental datasets.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Management and Policy, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental or natural resources management and policy, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the detection and interpretation of complex structural genomic variations underlying hematologic malignancies and congenital disorders. Current cytogenetic methods, including karyotyping and fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), face limitations in resolving cryptic rearrangements or low-frequency mosaicism, while emerging sequencing-based approaches struggle with accurate phasing and integration of cytogenetic data. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multimodal framework that synergizes whole-genome sequencing (WGS), high-resolution imaging, and deep learning to improve the characterization of clinically significant genomic aberrations. The computational pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets encompassing WGS reads, FISH image stacks, and spectral karyotyping data, employing graph-based genome assembly algorithms optimized for GPU-accelerated environments to resolve complex structural variants. Concurrently, a 3D convolutional neural network architecture will analyze multidimensional FISH image arrays to detect spatial patterns indicative of cryptic translocations. Resource-intensive tasks, including population-scale haplotype phasing and batch processing of high-throughput imaging data, will leverage parallelized workflows across HPC nodes. Validation will utilize retrospective cohorts from pediatric leukemia and rare chromosomal disorder cases with unresolved cytogenetic diagnoses. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source platform for integrated cytogenomic analysis, improved detection thresholds for mosaic structural variants (<5% allele frequency), and benchmarked protocols for correlating computational predictions with clinical phenotypes. This work will advance precision diagnostics by bridging molecular cytogenetics with scalable computational infrastructure, directly impacting patient stratification for targeted therapies and transplantation protocols.
cip_title: Cytogenetics/ Genetics/ Clinical Genetics Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform analyses of the human genome and chromosomes for the research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes instruction in chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between dynamic environmental cues in immersive virtual reality (VR) and collective decision-making processes, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model emergent group behaviors in digitally mediated spaces. While traditional environmental psychology focuses on physical settings, the proliferation of VR necessitates understanding how algorithmically generated sensory inputs—such as shifting lighting, spatial acoustics, or procedural landscapes—unconsciously bias collaborative outcomes. The research problem centers on identifying quantifiable relationships between real-time environmental manipulations in VR and measurable shifts in group consensus-building, conflict resolution, and risk assessment behaviors. Using a mixed-methods framework, we will collect multimodal behavioral data (eye tracking, vocal tone analysis, movement kinematics) from participants completing cooperative tasks in procedurally modulated VR environments. These datasets will feed into two computational pipelines: 1) a graph neural network architecture trained to predict decision trajectories based on environmental feature interactions, and 2) agent-based models simulating large-scale emergent behaviors under varied digital environmental conditions. HPC resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale VR telemetry, training models with temporally dense input sequences (100Hz sampling rates), and running parallelized simulations across parameter spaces encompassing 10^5+ agent permutations. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of digital environmental influencers on group cognition, validated predictive models of environment-behavior relationships, and open-source tools for ethical design of VR spaces in organizational and educational contexts. By bridging ecological psychology with computational social science, this work establishes foundational methods for studying human behavior in algorithmically constructed worlds, with implications for mitigating unintended behavioral manipulation in next-generation collaborative platforms.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of solvent-mediated reaction dynamics in complex chemical systems, with a focus on understanding how solvation environments influence reaction pathways and kinetics. Traditional quantum mechanical approaches struggle to capture the interplay between electronic structure, solvent reorganization, and rare event dynamics at experimentally relevant scales. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining density functional theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and enhanced sampling techniques, including metadynamics and variational free energy perturbation methods. The research will investigate prototypical nucleophilic substitution (SN2) and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) reactions in aqueous and mixed-solvent environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) large-scale DFT calculations to parameterize reactive force fields for solvated ions, (2) extended AIMD simulations with explicit solvent molecules to map free energy landscapes, and (3) Markov state modeling to quantify kinetic bottlenecks in multi-step mechanisms. Expected outcomes include new predictive models for solvent effects on activation barriers and transmission coefficients, validated against existing ultrafast spectroscopy data. These results will provide fundamental insights into designing solvent systems for selective catalysis and energy storage applications. The computational workflows developed will be generalized into an open-source toolkit for simulating solvent-dependent reaction dynamics, filling a critical gap between gas-phase quantum chemistry and continuum solvation models. This work requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for AIMD trajectory sampling, high-memory nodes for post-processing terabyte-scale simulation datasets, and parallel storage systems for managing millions of configuration snapshots. Successful implementation will enhance predictive capabilities in physical chemistry while establishing scalable protocols for simulating chemically accurate reaction networks in realistic condensed-phase environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of understanding and predicting the behavior of chemical systems ranging from nuclear particles to atoms, molecules, clusters, biological materials and macroscopic assemblies. Includes instruction in quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, reaction dynamics, group theory, collision theory, and polymer science.

abstract: Urban stormwater management systems are increasingly challenged by climate change-induced precipitation variability, leading to amplified risks of combined sewer overflows (CSOs) and contaminant mobilization in receiving waters. Current design standards, reliant on historical rainfall patterns, inadequately address the non-stationarity of hydrologic regimes, resulting in compromised water quality and public health hazards. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to optimize adaptive stormwater infrastructure under uncertain climate futures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will couple hydrodynamic models (EPA SWMM, HEC-RAS 2D) with contaminant transport algorithms to simulate fine-scale spatiotemporal dynamics of runoff, sediment-bound pollutants, and pathogen dispersal across urban watersheds. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate models using real-time sensor data from municipal networks and identify cost-effective green-gray infrastructure configurations under ensemble climate projections (CMIP6). Computational demands arise from the need to execute millions of scenario iterations across decadal horizons at meter-scale spatial resolution, requiring parallelized processing of large geospatial datasets and multi-objective optimization workflows. Anticipated outcomes include (1) risk-informed thresholds for infrastructure retrofitting in flood-vulnerable communities, (2) predictive tools for evaluating pathogen exposure hotspots during extreme wet weather events, and (3) open-source decision support frameworks enabling municipalities to prioritize interventions balancing hydraulic capacity, ecological preservation, and environmental justice considerations. The HPC resources will enable previously intractable analyses of distributed stormwater systems as complex adaptive systems, directly advancing the program’s mission to develop engineering solutions for pollution control and protective living environments amidst climatic uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the resilience of aquatic ecosystems under multifactorial environmental stressors, with a focus on the interplay between habitat fragmentation, nutrient cycling dynamics, and co-evolutionary predator-prey interactions. A critical gap persists in predicting how ecosystems reconcile abrupt anthropogenic disturbances with slower evolutionary and biogeochemical feedbacks, particularly in freshwater communities where microbial, invertebrate, and vertebrate trophic networks intersect. To address this, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of organismal interactions with spatially explicit biogeochemical reaction-diffusion systems. The ABM component will simulate adaptive behaviors and selection pressures across trophic levels, while reaction-diffusion models will quantify nutrient flux thresholds under varying oxygen and pH regimes derived from climate projection datasets. A novel feature involves coupling genetic algorithms to the ABM to simulate trait evolution in response to shifting resource landscapes. The computational scale necessitates HPC capabilities to resolve hourly dynamics across decadal timescales in 3D lattice representations of stratified lake systems, integrating over 10^6 individual agents with heterogeneous life history traits. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of nonlinear tipping points in community stability linked to phosphorus-nitrogen stoichiometry imbalances, (2) quantification of evolutionary rescue potential under pulsed vs. chronic disturbance regimes, and (3) high-resolution vulnerability maps for regional freshwater food webs. Results will directly inform watershed management strategies addressing synergistic threats from agricultural runoff and thermal stratification intensification. This work advances mechanistic theory in eco-evolutionary dynamics while providing actionable frameworks for biodiversity conservation in anthropogenically altered aquatic systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions of small-scale biological systems, such as organisms, to each other, to complex and whole systems, and to the physical and other non-biological aspects of their environments. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry; landscape and/or marine/aquatic dynamics; decomposition; global and regional elemental budgets; biotic and abiotic regulation of nutrient cycles; ecophysiology; ecosystem resilience, disturbance, and succession; community and habitat dynamics; organismal interactions (co-evolution, competition, predation); paleoecology; and evolutionary ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to evaluate the impact of pharmaceutical regulatory policies on drug pricing, accessibility, and health outcomes using advanced computational modeling. Current approaches often lack the capacity to integrate multi-dimensional data sources or simulate complex interactions between policy variables, market dynamics, and patient behaviors. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate stakeholder decision-making processes, machine learning algorithms to analyze longitudinal healthcare claims data, and Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic cost-effectiveness analyses. Key datasets include national drug expenditure records, insurance reimbursement patterns, and patient-level outcomes from electronic health records. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale of these datasets, executing parallelized policy scenario simulations, and optimizing model parameters through iterative learning processes. Expected outcomes include predictive models quantifying trade-offs between drug affordability and innovation incentives, policy scenario analyses to identify equitable reimbursement frameworks, and risk-assessment tools for formulary design. This work will provide actionable insights for regulators and healthcare organizations, advancing evidence-based pharmacy policy while demonstrating the transformative potential of computational methods in pharmaceutical administration research. By integrating real-world data with systems-level simulations, the project aims to establish a replicable methodology for evaluating emergent challenges in drug regulation and access.
cip_title: Pharmacy Administration and Pharmacy Policy and Regulatory Affairs
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial, social, and economic sciences to the study and management of the distribution and use of pharmaceutical products and the provision of pharmacy services. Includes instruction in research design and methods, statistics, social and organizational behavior, pharmacoeconomics, management of pharmacy services, outcomes research, product planning and reimbursement, cost-benefit analysis, drug marketing, pharmacy and pharmaceutics law and regulation, risk assessment, and organization of the health care system.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and installation of energy-efficient glazing systems in modern architectural applications. The research problem centers on the growing demand for sustainable building practices, which requires precise simulations of thermal performance, stress distribution, and material behavior in complex glass and transparent polymer assemblies. Current empirical methods for predicting energy efficiency and structural integrity in glazed systems lack the resolution to account for micro-scale material variations, dynamic environmental loads, and site-specific geometric constraints, leading to suboptimal installations and increased waste. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-physics simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven optimization. The computational workflow will model heat transfer, mechanical stress, and airflow interactions across diverse glazing configurations under real-world climatic conditions, including extreme temperature gradients and wind loads. Training datasets will incorporate material properties from industry-standard glass and polymer samples, structural data from historical installation failures, and LiDAR-derived site geometries. Parallelized simulations will enable rapid iteration of design parameters such as pane thickness, framing materials, and sealant properties, while reinforcement learning algorithms will identify configurations that maximize energy efficiency and durability. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for glaziers to preemptively assess failure risks, reduce material waste during installation, and comply with evolving energy codes. By quantifying the performance trade-offs of novel materials like electrochromic glass and aerogel-insulated panels, this work will directly inform curriculum updates in glazier training programs, bridging the gap between traditional craftsmanship and computational design. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary scale and resolution for these simulations, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations due to their high-dimensional parameter spaces and iterative optimization requirements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair fixtures, sheets, windows, and skylights made of glass, plexiglass, and other transparent materials. Includes instruction in site measurement, job analysis and estimation, material cutting and trimming, window and door installation, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of manual therapy interventions, specifically massage therapy, on soft tissue dynamics and pain modulation. Despite its widespread clinical use, the mechanistic underpinnings of massage therapy remain poorly quantified, particularly regarding how localized mechanical forces translate to cellular-level changes or systemic outcomes such as reduced inflammation or altered pain signaling. Current experimental models lack the resolution to capture multiscale interactions between tissue deformation, fluid dynamics in extracellular matrices, and neural feedback loops. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of soft tissue mechanics with agent-based simulations of inflammatory mediator diffusion and agent-based neural network responses. The FEM component will simulate real-time stress-strain distributions in multilayered tissue models (skin, fascia, muscle) under varying massage protocols (pressure, direction, duration), calibrated using MRI-derived viscoelastic parameters from human subjects. Concurrently, discrete element modeling will track cytokine dispersion and mechanotransduction pathways linked to macrophage activation. A machine learning layer, trained on existing proteomic and patient-reported outcome datasets, will predict dose-response relationships between intervention parameters and biomarkers of inflammation or pain thresholds. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space, iterative optimization of coupled models, and sensitivity analyses across physiological variables (e.g., tissue fibrosis, adiposity). Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for personalizing massage protocols based on individual biomechanical and immunological profiles, as well as mechanistic insights into how manual therapies interface with peripheral and central nervous system signaling. This work bridges gaps between manual therapy practice and computational biomedicine, offering a novel framework to advance evidence-based standardization in a field traditionally reliant on qualitative assessment.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being to clients through the application of manual techniques for manipulating skin, muscles, and connective tissues. Includes instruction in Western (Swedish) massage, sports massage, myotherapy/trigger point massage, myofascial release, deep tissue massage, cranio-sacral therapy, reflexology, massage safety and emergency management, client counseling, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interplay of sociocultural, psychological, and biological factors influencing end-of-life decision-making and bereavement outcomes—a critical gap in thanatology research. Traditional qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between individual grief trajectories, community-level cultural norms, and systemic healthcare variables. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), natural language processing (NLP), and multilevel network analysis. The ABM component will simulate decision-making processes in palliative care scenarios, incorporating individualized psychological profiles (e.g., coping styles, spiritual beliefs) derived from anonymized clinical datasets. Concurrently, NLP algorithms will analyze historical and contemporary textual corpora (medical records, social media, and religious texts) to quantify evolving cultural attitudes toward death across diverse populations. These layers will be coupled with hospital system data to model resource allocation impacts on bereavement outcomes. The computational intensity arises from simulating 10^5+ heterogeneous agents across parameterized cultural contexts while maintaining real-time interaction with high-dimensional NLP embeddings. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of critical leverage points for improving end-of-life care accessibility, (2) predictive models of grief complication risks based on sociocultural-environmental interactions, and (3) a novel open-source toolkit for thanatology research integrating temporal, spatial, and semantic analysis. By bridging computational social science with clinical thanatology, this work will establish a paradigm for simulating mortality-related phenomena at unprecedented scale, directly informing interventions in hospice care, community support systems, and public health policy. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive cultural language models and achieving sufficient stochastic simulation iterations to capture rare but consequential decision pathways.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, philosophical, psychological, sociological, and theological aspects of death, dying, and bereavement. Includes instruction in counseling, ethics, grief, palliative and hospice care, philosophy, thanatology, and theology.

abstract: This project investigates the emergence of decentralized, algorithmically mediated social trust networks in hybrid digital-physical communities, a phenomenon not yet systematically studied within traditional sociological or anthropological frameworks. As digital platforms increasingly facilitate resource-sharing economies (e.g., tool libraries, cooperative childcare networks), these systems develop unique governance protocols blending machine learning recommendations with culturally embedded reciprocity norms. The research employs large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate how trust metrics, algorithmic mediation, and historical inequities co-evolve in such systems, focusing on how marginalized groups navigate these sociotechnical hierarchies. Using anonymized transaction data from three partner organizations spanning urban and rural cooperatives (3.2M interactions), we will train graph neural networks to identify latent trust dynamics, then integrate these into adaptive ABM agents. High-performance computing resources are critical for running parallelized simulations across diverse demographic and policy scenarios (estimated 250,000 core-hours), enabling real-time sensitivity analyses of parameters like fairness-aware algorithm adjustments or shock events (e.g., resource scarcity). Methodological innovations include developing a cultural schema interpreter module that translates qualitative ethnographic data on local cooperation practices into agent decision trees through transformer-based NLP pipelines. Expected outcomes include 1) a framework for auditing equity impacts of algorithmic resource allocation in community networks, 2) empirically grounded models of how digital mediation alters traditional anthropological concepts of gift economies, and 3) open-source tools for cooperatives to simulate policy interventions. This work bridges computational social science with critical data studies, advancing interdisciplinary capacity to study post-platform sociotechnical systems while directly supporting community-led alternatives to extractive sharing economies.
cip_definition: A program that combines sociology and anthropology to study how society is organized, the origins and development of social institutions, social change, social organizations, race, class, gender and culture.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and rapidly evolving viral pathogens in animal populations presents critical challenges to veterinary medicine, with implications for animal welfare, food security, and zoonotic disease risks. Current gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms driving pathogen adaptation and host-microbe interactions limit the development of targeted therapies and diagnostic tools. This project seeks to address these challenges through a computational study of bacterial and viral pathogen dynamics in clinically relevant animal hosts. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets from pathogens such as methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus pseudintermedius* (MRSP) in companion animals and highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) viruses in poultry. Multi-omics integration will be performed to identify conserved virulence factors, resistance gene networks, and host immune evasion strategies. Machine learning models will predict AMR emergence patterns across bacterial lineages, while molecular dynamics simulations will characterize structural variations in viral surface proteins linked to cross-species transmission. Additionally, agent-based epidemiological models will simulate outbreak scenarios under varying intervention strategies. The computational workflows will utilize containerized pipelines for reproducibility, with parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for rapid diagnostics, predictive frameworks for resistance gene dissemination, and actionable insights into viral mutation hotspots affecting vaccine efficacy. By elucidating pathogen evolution in animal hosts, this research aims to directly inform clinical decision-making for antimicrobial stewardship, outbreak containment protocols, and prophylactic strategies in veterinary practice. The proposed work bridges computational biology and clinical microbiology, offering a scalable approach to address pressing One Health challenges at the animal-human-environment interface.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict the structural and material degradation of historic buildings under varying environmental and anthropogenic stressors, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in traditional architectural conservation practices. Architectural conservation faces challenges in quantitatively forecasting long-term material behavior, particularly for complex, multi-layered structures subjected to climate change, urban development, and tourism pressures. Current methods rely heavily on physical sampling and static simulations, which lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between environmental variables, material properties, and structural integrity over extended timescales. To address this, the project proposes a multi-scale computational approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate decay processes in historic masonry, timber, and mortars. High-resolution 3D scans of case-study buildings will inform geometric models, while material datasets from spectral analysis and mechanical testing will parameterize degradation algorithms. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of century-scale weathering cycles, thermal fluctuations, and visitor footfall impacts, iteratively refined via ML models trained on real-world conservation outcomes. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset to prioritize intervention strategies, optimize maintenance schedules, and assess risk scenarios for heritage sites. By bridging computational engineering and conservation theory, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for data-driven preservation planning, reducing reliance on reactive, trial-and-error approaches. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for large-scale fluid-structure interaction simulations and ML training on heterogeneous material datasets—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools and case studies on UNESCO World Heritage sites, offering scalable solutions for global conservation practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the architectural design principles and building techniques used in historic structures and environments, and the process of saving and restoring old buildings and districts for contemporary use and enjoyment. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation techniques, and material conservation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between distributed cognitive processes and environmental affordances in shaping collective decision-making within culturally diverse groups. While traditional cognitive science often focuses on individual cognition or homogeneous populations, this research addresses a critical gap by modeling how heterogeneous cultural frameworks, embedded in variable ecological contexts, co-evolve with group-level cognitive strategies. The core computational challenge lies in simulating multi-agent systems where agents operate under distinct, culturally inherited perceptual priors, dynamically adapting their problem-solving heuristics through both social learning and real-time environmental feedback. To achieve this, we will develop a high-performance agent-based modeling framework integrating (1) biophysically plausible neural network models of individual decision-making, (2) stochastic cultural transmission dynamics, and (3) ecological niche construction processes. The simulations will employ evolutionary algorithms to explore emergent coordination patterns across timescales, from rapid situational adaptation to intergenerational knowledge transmission. Computational demands arise from simultaneously tracking millions of neural activation states across diverse agent populations, modeling complex environment-agent couplings through spatially explicit landscapes, and performing sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces governing cultural-evolutionary dynamics. Expected outcomes include predictive models of how specific cultural-environmental configurations foster resilient collective cognition, with applications to designing inclusive decision-support systems and understanding cognitive diversity in ecological transition zones. This work establishes a novel methodological bridge between cultural neuroscience, ecological psychology, and complex systems theory, requiring HPC resources to manage the combinatorial complexity inherent in truly interdisciplinary cognitive science research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cognitive science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing volume and heterogeneity of signals intelligence (SIGINT) data from multi-domain sensors—including radar, acoustic arrays, and electro-optical systems—present significant challenges for real-time processing and actionable geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) extraction. Traditional computational architectures struggle with the latency and scalability demands of integrating disparate sensor streams, particularly in contested environments where rapid decision-making is critical. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework optimized for multi-modal SIGINT fusion and adaptive signal exploitation. Leveraging distributed memory parallelism and GPU-accelerated processing, the proposed framework will implement novel algorithms for real-time feature extraction, cross-domain correlation, and anomaly detection across terahertz-frequency radar returns, underwater acoustic signatures, and hyperspectral infrared datasets. The computational approach integrates graph-based signal representation with machine learning models trained on phenomenology-specific datasets to enable context-aware processing in dynamic operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for concurrent processing of petabyte-scale SIGINT collections, reducing analyst burden through automated pattern recognition and predictive threat modeling. The research will advance computational methodologies for next-generation intelligence architectures, directly supporting enhanced situational awareness and time-sensitive decision processes in joint military operations. By bridging the gap between raw sensor data and tactical intelligence products, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for processing efficiency and analytical fidelity in emerging multi-intelligence fusion environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational aspects of collecting, processing and exploiting remote-sensed, radar, acoustic and other forms of signals intelligence. Includes instruction in applied physics, wave propagation and capture, radar systems, acoustics and underwater systems, infrared systems, synthetic aperture systems, collection and processing systems, signal phenomenology, signal analysis and exploitation, and applications to specific intelligence problems.

abstract: Contemporary digital communication ecosystems generate vast, heterogeneous datasets that challenge traditional analytical methods. This project addresses the critical gap in understanding how multimedia content—spanning text, audio, and video—achieves virality and shapes public discourse across platforms. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-modal computational framework integrating natural language processing, computer vision, and network analysis to model content dissemination dynamics at scale. The research will process terabytes of timestamped social media data, streaming metadata, and user interaction logs, employing GPU-accelerated deep learning models to extract semantic, visual, and temporal features. Agent-based simulations will then reconstruct information cascades under varying platform algorithms and user behavior parameters. This approach enables the identification of cross-platform virality patterns while accounting for the temporal sensitivity of digital engagement metrics. Expected outcomes include: (1) a novel computational model of multimedia content propagation validated against real-world case studies, (2) quantitative frameworks for assessing platform-specific engagement drivers, and (3) open-source tools to assist content creators and journalists in optimizing ethical audience reach. By addressing computational bottlenecks in processing synchronized multimedia streams and large-scale network simulations, this research advances methodological capabilities in digital communication studies while providing practical insights for media professionals navigating evolving platform ecosystems.
cip_title: Radio, Television, and Digital Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in radio, television, and digital communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the understudied challenge of optimizing task allocation and ergonomic safety for health aides and attendants in dynamic care environments. Health aides perform physically demanding tasks—such as patient transfers, repositioning, and mobility assistance—that carry high risks of musculoskeletal injury. Current guidelines for safe practice rely on static, population-level ergonomic standards, which fail to account for individual variability in patient needs, aide biomechanics, and real-time environmental constraints. We propose a computational framework integrating biomechanical modeling, reinforcement learning, and real-time sensor data to generate personalized task strategies that minimize injury risk while maintaining care quality. The project will develop multi-body simulations of common patient care maneuvers, parameterized by anthropometric data from both aides and patients (collected via 3D scanning and motion capture). These simulations will train reinforcement learning agents to optimize kinetic load distribution across joints and muscle groups under varying constraints, such as patient weight, room layout, and aide fatigue states. A parallel agent-based modeling component will evaluate how optimized individual strategies scale to team-based care scenarios, incorporating stochastic variables like emergency interruptions or equipment failures. The computational workflow demands significant HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of the parameter space, the need for real-time parallel simulation, and the iterative training of deep reinforcement learning models. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for pre-shift task planning, a real-time decision-support system for mobile devices, and evidence-based recommendations for adaptive ergonomic protocols. By bridging biomechanics, occupational health, and AI, this work aims to reduce workplace injuries in a critical yet underserved healthcare workforce while establishing a computational paradigm for human-centric task optimization in care delivery.
cip_definition: Any other instructional program that prepares individuals to provide routine patient care and assistance.

abstract: Adult education programs face unique challenges in addressing the diverse needs of learners, including varying skill levels, prior knowledge gaps, and time constraints. Traditional pedagogical approaches often struggle to scale personalized instruction, particularly in hybrid or fully online environments where adult learners increasingly seek flexible opportunities. This project seeks to develop and validate computational models that optimize adaptive learning systems for adult education contexts through large-scale analysis of learner engagement patterns and instructional outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process multimodal datasets spanning anonymized learner interactions (e.g., forum participation, assignment submissions), demographic profiles, and longitudinal performance metrics from three statewide continuing education systems. Machine learning techniques, including transformer-based natural language processing and temporal graph neural networks, will be employed to model how adult learners develop competencies across heterogeneous cohorts. Computational experiments will simulate the impact of alternative instructional strategies, content sequencing approaches, and feedback mechanisms on predicted learning trajectories. The scale of data (anticipated 8TB structured/unstructured inputs) and complexity of modeling cross-domain skill transfer necessitate parallelized training pipelines and GPU-accelerated inference that only HPC infrastructure can provide. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated framework for predicting adult learners’ responsiveness to different pedagogical interventions, 2) open-source tools to help instructors design computationally informed adaptive curricula, and 3) novel insights into how workforce-relevant skill acquisition differs from traditional academic learning patterns. By bridging educational research with computational modeling at scale, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in adult teacher education while demonstrating how HPC resources can address critical scalability challenges in non-STEM disciplines. All models and anonymized datasets will be made available to the broader educational research community.
detailed_field: Adult, continuing, and workforce education and development
cip_title: Adult and Continuing Education and Teaching
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach adult students in various settings, including basic and remedial education programs, continuing education programs, and programs designed to develop or upgrade specific employment-related knowledge and skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a dynamic simulation framework for optimizing culturally responsive parent education programs. Parent education services face a critical challenge: designing curricula that adapt to the complex interplay of cultural, socioeconomic, and developmental variables influencing family outcomes. Traditional program evaluations rely on post-intervention surveys or small-scale observational studies, limiting the ability to model longitudinal impacts or test program variations across diverse populations. This project addresses this gap by constructing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate parent-child interactions, community dynamics, and program delivery mechanisms at scale. The computational approach integrates anonymized longitudinal datasets from regional parenting programs, developmental psychology frameworks, and generative AI tools to populate synthetic families reflecting demographic diversity. HPC resources will enable parallelized parameter sweeps to evaluate how variations in program content, delivery formats (e.g., virtual vs. in-person), and facilitator training protocols affect predicted outcomes across 10,000+ simulated family units. Machine learning techniques will identify nonlinear relationships between program features and key metrics such as parental self-efficacy scores and child emotional regulation trajectories. The resulting framework will provide a predictive tool for educators to customize interventions for specific cultural contexts while maintaining fidelity to evidence-based practices. By quantifying how micro-level interactions scale to population-level outcomes, this work aims to advance precision in parent education design while preserving cultural responsiveness—a previously intractable balance using conventional research methods. The computational infrastructure developed will be shared as an open-source toolkit, enabling replication studies and iterative refinement by the parent education research community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, coordinate, and teach parent education programs and services that address the cultural, emotional, intellectual, physical and social needs of children and parents. Includes instruction in child development, cultural diversity in schools, child behavior, family development, family-community partnerships, family dynamics, interpersonal relationships, parent-child relationships, and social services.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize greenhouse climate and resource management through advanced computational modeling to address inefficiencies in current systems, which often rely on static protocols that fail to adapt to dynamic environmental variables or plant physiological needs. Current approaches to managing temperature, humidity, irrigation, and nutrient delivery in controlled environments lack predictive precision, leading to energy waste, suboptimal crop yields, and unsustainable resource consumption. To resolve this, we propose developing a high-resolution, multi-scale simulation framework integrating real-time sensor data, plant growth models, and environmental control systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large datasets from IoT-enabled greenhouse sensors, genomic databases, and historical climate records, enabling the training of machine learning models to predict crop responses under variable conditions. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between plant cohorts, microbial communities, and environmental control systems, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model microclimate heterogeneity within greenhouse structures. The proposed models will dynamically adjust irrigation schedules, ventilation, and supplemental lighting to balance productivity with energy and water use. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for greenhouse operators, capable of reducing energy consumption by 15–25% and improving water-use efficiency by 20% compared to conventional systems. By elucidating genotype-environment interactions, the project will also inform the selection of crop varieties tailored to specific controlled environments. This work advances precision agriculture by bridging gaps between plant science, engineering, and data science, offering a replicable framework for sustainable food production amid climate variability. The requested HPC resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter optimization, and real-time simulation workflows critical to achieving these objectives.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce, store, and deliver plant species in controlled indoor environments for wholesale, commercial, research, or other purposes. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science; climate, irrigation, and nutrition control equipment operation and maintenance; facilities management; inventory control; safety procedures; and personnel supervision.
