Validated against full-scale experimental data and historical incident reconstructions, these simulations will yield predictive insights into failure thresholds of fire-resistant materials, optimal placement of detection apparatus, and efficacy of hybrid suppression systems combining water mist and chemical agents. The computational outcomes will directly inform revisions to fire protection engineering standards, enhance predictive maintenance strategies for critical infrastructure, and reduce lifecycle costs of fire safety systems. By overcoming current scalability limits through GPU-accelerated solvers and adaptive mesh refinement, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift in fire systems technology, bridging the gap between theoretical fire science and real-world emergency response challenges.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and practice of firefighting systems, building construction and related resources as applied to fire prevention, control, and mitigation. Includes instruction in fire hydraulics and dynamics, fire protection structures and systems design, fire behavior and combustion, fire protection hydraulics and water supply, fire protection equipment and systems, building construction for fire protection, and fire apparatus.

abstract: The increasing complexity of psychometric models and large-scale assessment datasets necessitates advanced computational infrastructure to support methodological innovation. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in estimating high-dimensional item response theory (IRT) models and conducting simulation studies to evaluate their statistical properties. Traditional estimation methods, such as marginal maximum likelihood, face scalability limitations when applied to models with thousands of parameters, hierarchical structures, or time-intensive Bayesian estimation workflows. The research aims to (1) develop optimized parallel computing algorithms for multidimensional IRT models with cross-classified data structures, (2) implement Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers with adaptive tuning for high-dimensional latent variable models, and (3) conduct large-scale Monte Carlo studies to assess estimator robustness under non-ignorable missing data and differential item functioning conditions. Computational workflows will leverage GPU acceleration for matrix operations and distributed computing frameworks to manage memory-intensive tasks. The project will extend open-source psychometric software (e.g., Stan and R packages) to incorporate these optimizations, enabling reproducible research workflows. Expected outcomes include new computational strategies for handling complex dependencies in modern assessment data, validated performance benchmarks for emerging IRT extensions, and publicly shared code templates for efficient psychometric simulation design. By addressing computational bottlenecks in model estimation and validation, this work will enhance the precision and applicability of quantitative methods for educational and psychological measurement, directly supporting the development of fairer, more reliable assessments. The requested HPC resources are essential given the projected need for 50,000+ CPU-core hours to complete parameter recovery studies across 1,000+ synthetic datasets per model configuration, alongside memory requirements (>1 TB RAM) for processing national-level assessment data with nested response patterns.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical procedures used in psychological test construction and validation; the general problems of the measurement of behavior; and the application of quantitative methods to research design and other methodological topics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of image-guided interventions in vascular and interventional radiology (VIR) necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize procedural planning, predict outcomes, and personalize therapies. Current limitations in modeling device-tissue interactions, hemodynamic changes post-intervention, and patient-specific anatomical variability hinder the development of precise, data-driven protocols. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address these challenges by integrating multimodal imaging data, biomechanical simulations, and machine learning. The research will focus on two interventional scenarios: stent-graft deployment in aortic aneurysms and transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for hepatocellular carcinoma. Patient-specific 3D anatomical models will be reconstructed from clinical CT, MRI, and fluoroscopy datasets. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model mechanical stresses during stent deployment and post-procedural hemodynamics, while agent-based modeling will simulate drug-particle transport during TACE. Deep learning architectures will be trained on retrospective clinical data to predict complications such as endoleaks or incomplete tumor targeting. HPC resources are critical due to the scale of imaging data (>10 TB across 500+ cases), the computational intensity of multiphysics simulations requiring iterative solvers, and the need for hyperparameter optimization in neural networks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for device failure and therapeutic efficacy, open-source simulation tools for procedural rehearsal, and AI-derived decision-support algorithms. This work aims to reduce intraoperative complications, improve long-term patient outcomes, and establish a computational pipeline adaptable to emerging VIR technologies. By bridging clinical practice with large-scale computational analysis, the project will advance precision medicine in minimally invasive therapies, directly addressing the growing demand for data-driven innovation in interventional radiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists with additional training in image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of multi-scale atmospheric wave interactions and their role in modulating severe weather events and upper atmospheric dynamics. A critical gap persists in resolving how mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) interact with gravity waves and larger-scale solar wind perturbations, particularly during geomagnetic storms. These coupled processes influence ionospheric variability and tropospheric storm intensity but remain poorly quantified due to computational limitations in simulating cross-scale feedbacks. To address this, we propose high-resolution numerical simulations using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model coupled with the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model with thermosphere-ionosphere extension (WACCM-X). The simulations will resolve turbulence and boundary layer dynamics at sub-kilometer horizontal grid spacing while incorporating real-time solar wind data to capture magnetosphere-ionosphere-atmosphere coupling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational demands of (1) nested domains spanning 10 km to 100 m resolution, (2) ensemble forecasting under varying geomagnetic conditions, and (3) assimilation of radar and satellite remote sensing data. The project will leverage GPU-optimized model configurations and parallelized workflows to process petabytes of 4D atmospheric state variables. Expected outcomes include improved parameterizations of gravity wave momentum transfer in weather-climate models and quantifiable linkages between solar wind variability and convective system intensification. Results will directly benefit the development of coupled space-weather-forecasting frameworks and inform climate resilience strategies reliant on accurate severe weather prediction. The scale of these multi-physics simulations—requiring 2.5 million core-hours and 400 TB of storage—exceeds institutional capabilities, necessitating allocation of national HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the processes governing the interactions, movement, and behavior of atmospheric phenomena and related terrestrial and solar phenomena. Includes instruction in cloud and precipitation physics, solar radiation transfer, active and passive remote sensing, atmospheric electricity and acoustics, atmospheric wave phenomena, turbulence and boundary layers, solar wind, geomagnetic storms, coupling, natural plasma, and energization.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing strategies for municipal green bonds, addressing inefficiencies in current public debt instruments that hinder climate-aligned infrastructure financing. Municipal bond markets face challenges in accurately pricing long-term environmental risks and returns, particularly as climate-related fiscal pressures and heterogeneous investor ESG (environmental, social, governance) preferences reshape public finance landscapes. Traditional valuation models struggle to incorporate real-time geospatial climate data, behavioral economic factors, and multi-agent market interactions at scale. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build an adaptive simulation environment integrating three computational layers: 1) machine learning models trained on historical bond issuance data and climate vulnerability indices, 2) agent-based market simulations capturing institutional investor decision-making under evolving ESG regulations, and 3) network analysis of fiscal contagion risks across interdependent municipal issuers. By processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning bond covenants, climate projections, and investor disclosures, the framework will identify optimal pricing mechanisms that balance municipal funding costs with sustainability targets. Expected outcomes include a novel risk-sharing algorithm for inter-municipal climate bonds and an open-source tool enabling public agencies to simulate pricing scenarios under varying decarbonization pathways. The computational intensity of running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of climate-economic trajectories necessitates GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. This work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for aligning public debt markets with climate resilience goals while maintaining fiscal stability—a critical gap in contemporary public finance research. Results will inform policy frameworks for green bond standardization and multi-jurisdictional risk pooling mechanisms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the financial assets and budgets of public sector organizations. Includes instruction in public trusts and investments; the laws and procedures used to plan, prepare and administer public agency budgets; and the preparation and analysis of public budget projections and policies.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive analytics framework for optimizing law enforcement resource allocation in dynamic urban environments. While traditional approaches to patrol distribution and incident response rely on historical crime statistics and heuristic decision-making, these methods often fail to adapt to real-time variables such as shifting population density, transient event-driven risks (e.g., protests, festivals), and multi-jurisdictional coordination challenges. The proposed computational model integrates heterogeneous datasets—including geospatial crime reports, traffic patterns, social media activity, and emergency service call logs—to simulate urban risk landscapes and test allocation strategies under diverse scenarios. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between law enforcement units, civilian populations, and environmental factors, while graph neural networks will analyze temporal-spatial dependencies in incident patterns. A key innovation involves coupling real-time data assimilation with ensemble forecasting to quantify uncertainty in resource deployment outcomes. The computational demands of this approach necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized scenario testing, hyperparameter optimization of machine learning models, and large-scale sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that identifies high-probability intervention points for crime prevention, reduces emergency response latency, and balances proactive community engagement with reactive enforcement needs. By addressing the computational gap between theoretical public administration frameworks and operational realities, this project aims to advance evidence-based policing strategies while maintaining ethical oversight through embedded fairness audits of algorithmic recommendations. The resulting open-source framework will provide law enforcement agencies with scalable, adaptable tools to improve public safety outcomes without expanding budgetary or personnel resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply theories and practices of organization management and criminal justice to the administration of public law enforcement agencies and operations. Includes instruction in law enforcement history and theory, operational command leadership, administration of public police organizations, labor relations, incident response strategies, legal and regulatory responsibilities, budgeting, public relations, and organizational leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing wastewater treatment systems and enhancing water recycling efficiency through advanced computational modeling. Current treatment methods often struggle to balance energy consumption, cost, and effectiveness, particularly when managing complex contaminants such as emerging organic pollutants and microplastics. Traditional experimental approaches to system design and process optimization are resource-intensive and fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale interactions within treatment systems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating high-fidelity simulations of fluid dynamics, reactive transport, and microbial community interactions in wastewater environments. The study will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-physics models that couple computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with biogeochemical reaction networks, enabling granular analysis of treatment processes across spatial and temporal scales. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter calibration, identify optimal operational conditions, and predict system performance under varying influent compositions. Key objectives include simulating membrane fouling dynamics in real-time, optimizing aeration strategies in biological reactors, and evaluating the feasibility of hybrid treatment-recycling systems for decentralized applications. The computational demands of these tasks—including large-scale matrix operations, parallelized CFD solvers, and ensemble modeling for uncertainty quantification—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing energy use in treatment plants, strategies to enhance contaminant removal efficiency by 20-30%, and scalable models for adaptive water recycling systems in water-stressed regions. By bridging gaps between process engineering and computational science, this work aims to advance sustainable water management practices, reduce operational costs, and support regulatory decision-making for next-generation wastewater infrastructure.
cip_title: Water Quality and Wastewater Treatment Management and Recycling Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using water storage, waterpower, and wastewater treatment systems. Includes instruction in water storage, power and/or treatment systems and equipment; testing and inspection procedures; system maintenance procedures; and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of personalized healthcare demands advanced computational tools to integrate multi-dimensional patient data and optimize treatment strategies. This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting individualized therapeutic responses for chronic diseases by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including genomic, metabolomic, and electronic health record (EHR) data. Current methods often fail to account for nonlinear interactions between genetic, environmental, and clinical variables, resulting in suboptimal treatment recommendations. To overcome this, we propose a machine learning framework that combines graph neural networks (GNNs) and ensemble methods to model patient-specific disease pathways and predict intervention outcomes. The GNN architecture will map biological networks (e.g., protein-protein interactions, metabolic pathways) to patient data, while ensemble techniques will integrate EHR-derived temporal patterns. HPC resources are critical for training these models at scale, given the high dimensionality of multi-omics data (>1 million features) and the need for hyperparameter optimization across thousands of parallelized trials. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model population-level treatment effects under varying clinical scenarios. The project will utilize existing datasets from three longitudinal cohorts (total n=45,000 patients) and validate findings through collaboration with a regional health network. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for treatment resistance, the development of an open-source predictive tool for clinicians, and scalable frameworks for real-time therapeutic decision support. This work will advance precision medicine by bridging computational innovation and clinical practice, ultimately reducing trial-and-error prescribing and improving patient outcomes in chronic disease management. The requested computing resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets and reduce model training times from weeks to days, accelerating translational impact.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The rapid evolution of computer hardware demands increasingly sophisticated design methodologies to address challenges in performance, energy efficiency, and scalability. Current approaches to optimizing circuit architectures and chip layouts often rely on iterative simulations that are computationally prohibitive, particularly for emerging technologies such as quantum-inspired computing elements or heterogeneous multi-core systems. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate novel computational frameworks for hardware design automation. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating scalable algorithms for real-time thermal and electromagnetic modeling of nanoscale circuits, and (2) implementing machine learning-driven optimization for energy-aware component placement in three-dimensional integrated systems. Computational methods will include finite-element analysis accelerated via GPU-parallelized solvers, Monte Carlo-based reliability testing, and graph neural networks trained on synthetic chip design datasets. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to reduce simulation times for complex hardware configurations by orders of magnitude compared to existing commercial tools. Anticipated outcomes include open-source software modules for hardware co-design, validated against physical prototypes fabricated through university-industry partnerships. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—particularly the need for multi-node GPU clusters to handle memory-intensive electromagnetic field solvers and large-scale parameter sweeps—necessitates access to advanced HPC infrastructure. Success in this work will directly address critical bottlenecks in designing next-generation processors for AI accelerators and edge computing devices, while establishing reproducible workflows for resource-efficient hardware development. The resulting methodologies will be disseminated through academic publications and integrated into graduate-level courses, bridging gaps between theoretical computer engineering principles and practical large-scale computational challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and evaluation of computer hardware and related peripheral equipment. Includes instruction in computer circuit and chip design, circuitry, computer systems design, computer equipment design, computer layout planning, testing procedures, and related computer theory and software topics.

abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone of non-invasive vascular diagnostics, yet challenges persist in achieving high-resolution, real-time imaging of dynamic vascular processes while minimizing artifacts caused by physiological motion. Current clinical protocols often compromise between spatial resolution, temporal resolution, and scan duration, limiting their ability to capture transient pathological changes in vascular structures. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing and validating a computational framework for accelerated, motion-robust vascular MRI using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) optimizing a physics-informed deep learning model for reconstructing undersampled MRI data with embedded motion correction, and (2) simulating complex blood flow dynamics through patient-specific vascular geometries to inform scan parameter selection. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated iterative reconstruction algorithms with 4D flow simulations derived from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models. HPC resources will enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization of neural networks trained on synthetic and clinical datasets (∼10 TB), as well as parallelized CFD simulations across diverse vascular anatomies. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline that reduces scan times by ≥50% while maintaining diagnostic accuracy, as demonstrated through phantom studies and retrospective clinical validation using existing coronary and cerebrovascular MRI datasets. The project will also generate open-source tools for simulating MRI artifacts under varying hemodynamic conditions. By bridging computational modeling with clinical MRI workflows, this work aims to advance the precision of vascular diagnostics, particularly for transient ischemic events and small-vessel pathologies, while providing a template for resource-efficient protocol development in MRI technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals who are AART-certified radiological technicians to utilize MRI technology to obtain still and moving images of various vascular structures in the human body that aid the physician in the diagnosis or treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in MRI imaging, sectional anatomy and pathology, MRI technology, MRI techniques and procedures, MRI physics, and clinical training.

abstract: Geriatric patients frequently present with complex, overlapping chronic conditions that require tailored pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. However, optimizing individualized care plans remains challenging due to the dynamic interplay of age-related physiological changes, polypharmacy risks, and heterogeneous treatment responses. This project seeks to develop predictive computational models to support nurse-led decision-making in geriatric care, with a focus on minimizing adverse drug events and enhancing therapeutic efficacy. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets spanning electronic health records, geriatric assessment metrics, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) parameters. Machine learning models, including ensemble algorithms and neural networks, will be trained to identify risk patterns in medication regimens, predict drug-drug and drug-disease interactions specific to aging populations, and simulate longitudinal outcomes under varying intervention scenarios. Computational fluid dynamics and physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling will further elucidate age-related changes in drug distribution and metabolism. By integrating these approaches at scale, the project aims to create a nurse-centered decision support platform that accounts for patient-specific factors such as renal/hepatic function decline, cognitive status, and comorbidity burden. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools to guide dose adjustments, deprescribing strategies, and non-pharmacological intervention timing in geriatric primary and acute care settings. This work will advance evidence-based geriatric nursing by enabling real-time analysis of high-dimensional clinical data, ultimately reducing trial-and-error approaches to complex care. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling computationally intensive simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts and ensuring robust model generalizability in this understudied population.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of creating immersive, interactive graphic design environments that integrate real-time user input, dynamic visual elements, and machine learning-driven generative processes. While contemporary graphic design increasingly relies on high-fidelity simulations, 3D modeling, and AI-augmented creativity, existing consumer-grade hardware struggles to handle the latency, rendering complexity, and data throughput required for experimental, large-scale digital installations. The research will develop a framework for optimizing generative adversarial networks (GANs) and physics-based rendering pipelines using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Key computational challenges include parallelizing neural style transfer algorithms across GPU nodes to enable multi-resolution texture synthesis, simulating light-material interactions in complex 3D scenes, and maintaining sub-50ms response times for user-driven parametric design systems. The project will utilize distributed computing architectures to train AI models on heterogeneous datasets of design patterns, material properties, and gestural input data, while implementing containerized workflows to manage version-controlled design iterations. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for real-time collaborative design prototyping, quantitative benchmarks for computational-aesthetic quality evaluation, and novel methods for balancing artistic intent with algorithmic stochasticity in HPC environments. By establishing performance-optimized pipelines for computationally intensive design tasks, this work aims to expand the creative possibilities of data-driven visual storytelling while providing empirical insights into resource allocation strategies for hybrid human-AI design systems. The results will directly inform curriculum development in computational design literacy and offer open-source reference implementations for the visual arts community.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic and computer techniques to the interpretation of technical and commercial concepts. Includes instruction in computer-assisted art and design, printmaking, concepts sketching, technical drawing, color theory, imaging, studio technique, still and life modeling, multimedia applications, communication skills and commercial art business operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive biohybrid systems, integrating synthetic biological components with engineered materials for dynamic environmental sensing and response. The central challenge lies in modeling the bidirectional feedback between living cells (e.g., engineered microbes) and abiotic systems (e.g., responsive polymers or microfluidics) under spatially heterogeneous and temporally variable conditions. Traditional reductionist approaches fail to capture the emergent behaviors arising from multi-scale interactions, necessitating a computational framework that bridges molecular-scale biochemical kinetics, mesoscale material deformation, and macroscale environmental dynamics. The project will employ hybrid simulation methods, combining agent-based modeling for cellular decision-making, finite element analysis for stress-strain relationships in deformable materials, and lattice Boltzmann methods for fluid-structure interactions in microfluidic environments. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate parameter space exploration and optimize system designs for target functions, such as pollutant degradation or pathogen detection. Expected outcomes include predictive models of biohybrid system stability, open-source simulation tools for interdisciplinary researchers, and validated design principles for scalable fabrication. By addressing the computational bottleneck in simulating these complex interfaces, this work aims to establish a foundation for next-generation adaptive technologies with applications in environmental remediation, precision agriculture, and biomedical diagnostics. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces, stochasticity inherent in biological components, and real-time coupling of disparate physical models across spatiotemporal scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of computing and its application for solving challenges in science and engineering fields, with a focus on principles from mathematics, science, engineering and computing.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to develop a computational framework for real-time, adaptive media generation driven by neurophysiological user feedback, bridging gaps between affective computing, generative algorithms, and neuroaesthetic theory. Current media generation tools lack systematic methods to dynamically optimize content based on implicit cognitive or emotional responses, particularly at the intersection of artistic intent and neuroscientific validity. This project addresses two core challenges: 1) designing biologically grounded metrics for aesthetic engagement using multimodal neuroimaging data (EEG, eye tracking, and galvanic skin response), and 2) creating resource-efficient generative architectures that iteratively refine outputs through closed-loop interaction with these metrics. The computational approach combines high-temporal-resolution analysis of neurophysiological streams via convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with latent space manipulation techniques for generative adversarial networks (GANs) and diffusion models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized training of hybrid encoder-generator systems across multiple aesthetic domains (visual, auditory, and cross-modal stimuli), as well as real-time inference optimization for low-latency feedback loops. Expected outcomes include an open-source software toolkit for neuroadaptive media synthesis, a validated dataset linking neurophysiological signatures to subjective aesthetic evaluations across diverse demographics, and new theoretical insights into computational models of dynamic creativity. The work advances emerging applications in personalized digital therapeutics, immersive education, and human-AI collaborative art, while establishing methodological foundations for resource-conscious deployment of neuroadaptive systems on heterogeneous computing architectures. By tightly coupling HPC-scale model development with edge-computing feasibility studies, this research aims to create transferable paradigms for next-generation interactive media that operate across the compute continuum.
cip_title: Computer Software and Media Applications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer software and media applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing additive manufacturing processes for high-performance, multi-material components through advanced computational modeling. Additive manufacturing enables unprecedented design flexibility but faces persistent issues such as defect formation, residual stress accumulation, and inconsistent microstructure development, particularly when combining dissimilar alloys or composite materials. Traditional experimental approaches to parameter optimization are time-intensive and cost-prohibitive, while existing simulations often oversimplify the multi-physics interactions governing these processes. We propose a high-fidelity, multi-scale computational framework to model laser-powder bed fusion (LPBF) processes, integrating thermal-fluid dynamics, phase transformations, and mechanical deformation across spatial and temporal scales. The framework will leverage coupled finite element and lattice Boltzmann methods, enhanced by machine learning surrogates to accelerate convergence in parameter space. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve micron-scale melt pool dynamics while maintaining system-level thermal histories over build volumes exceeding 100 mm³. Parallelized simulations will run on GPU-accelerated nodes, requiring 5,000+ core-hours per parameter set to capture the non-linear interactions between laser parameters, material properties, and cooling rates. Expected outcomes include predictive models for defect-free printing of steel-titanium hybrid structures, validated against synchrotron X-ray imaging data. The resulting open-source toolchain will enable rapid process optimization for industry partners in aerospace and energy sectors, reducing trial-and-error iterations by an estimated 60%. By elucidating fundamental relationships between process variables and microstructural outcomes, this work aims to advance the adoption of additive manufacturing for load-bearing applications while contributing scalable computational methods to the broader materials processing community. The requested resources will support parameter sensitivity studies, surrogate model training, and large-scale validation cases that are computationally intractable on local cluster infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Periodontal disease, a leading cause of tooth loss and systemic health complications, involves complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and environmental factors. Current clinical and laboratory methods struggle to resolve the dynamic, multiscale processes driving disease progression, limiting the development of targeted therapies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model microbial-host interactions, predict disease trajectories, and optimize treatment strategies. We propose an integrative computational framework combining multi-omics data analysis, agent-based modeling, and machine learning to investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of periodontal pathogenesis. Metagenomic sequencing data from subgingival plaque samples (n=1,200) will be analyzed to map microbial community shifts during disease transitions. Concurrently, single-cell RNA sequencing of gingival tissue will characterize host immune cell heterogeneity and inflammatory pathways. These datasets will inform a multiscale agent-based model simulating biofilm formation, immune cell recruitment, and bone resorption dynamics under varying clinical conditions. Machine learning algorithms will identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response using longitudinal clinical data paired with microbial and molecular profiles. The computational workflow requires HPC resources to manage large-scale data integration, parallelize simulations across parameter spaces, and train deep learning models on high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of keystone pathogens and host pathways driving irreversible tissue damage, (2) predictive models for personalized treatment planning, and (3) in silico testing of novel therapeutic interventions targeting biofilm-immune crosstalk. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of periodontitis while providing a scalable computational platform for translational research in oral immunobiology. By elucidating disease mechanisms at unprecedented resolution, the project aligns with clinical priorities in periodontology to reduce therapeutic variability and improve long-term patient outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: Understanding the impacts of climate change on watershed systems is critical for sustainable natural resource management, yet existing models often lack the resolution to capture complex interactions between hydrological processes, land-use changes, and extreme weather events. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate watershed dynamics under varying climate scenarios, with a focus on predicting water availability, sediment transport, and pollutant dispersion in the rapidly changing Pacific Northwest watersheds. The research will integrate multi-scale datasets, including satellite-derived land cover, regional climate projections, and in-situ hydrological measurements, to parameterize a coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical model. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine-scale spatial heterogeneities (≤100m resolution) and temporal variability across decadal scales, leveraging parallelized simulations to evaluate mitigation strategies such as riparian buffer restoration and adaptive reservoir management. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs associated with uncertainty quantification, enabling probabilistic assessments of intervention efficacy under ensemble climate pathways. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into watershed resilience thresholds, optimized conservation planning maps for regional stakeholders, and open-source tools for scalable hydrologic modeling. By advancing predictive capabilities at the intersection of climatology, geomorphology, and resource management, this work will directly inform state and tribal natural resource policies while contributing methodological innovations to environmental computational science. The requested allocation of 200,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster will support the iterative model calibration, large-ensemble climate simulations, and machine learning workflows required to address these interdisciplinary challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of the physical environment and the solution of environmental problems, including subjects such as abating or controlling environmental pollution and degradation; the interaction between human society and the natural environment; and natural resources management. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, physics, geosciences, climatology, statistics, and mathematical modeling.

abstract: Healthcare environments are complex systems where spatial design, human behavior, and environmental factors dynamically interact to influence health outcomes. While evidence-based design principles exist, current approaches often rely on static metrics or retrospective analyses, failing to capture real-time, multiscale interactions between architectural variables (e.g., layout, airflow, material use), occupant behavior, and biological responses. This project proposes a computational framework to model and optimize healthcare spaces by integrating behavioral dynamics, pathogen transmission risks, and neurophysiological stress signals. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop multi-agent simulation environments that couple 1) spatial network analyses of clinical workflows, 2) airborne contaminant dispersion modeling with dynamic occupancy patterns, and 3) machine learning-driven analysis of biometric data streams (e.g., wearable stress monitors, eye-tracking). The computational pipeline will iteratively test design modifications against emergent infection control risks, staff cognitive load patterns, and patient recovery metrics. Key innovations include the development of adaptive graph neural networks to model behavior-environment feedback loops and GPU-accelerated fluid dynamics simulations scaled to entire hospital units. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies how micron-scale material properties interact with meter-scale spatial configurations to impact population health metrics. This work directly addresses critical gaps in designing post-pandemic healthcare infrastructure while advancing computational methods for human-environment interaction modeling. The requested resources will enable processing of petabyte-scale datasets from partner hospitals, including 3D lidar scans, microbial samples, and continuous biometric recordings from 2,000+ participants. By bridging architectural analytics, microbiology, and behavioral neuroscience through large-scale simulation, this project establishes a new paradigm for preventive health design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the impact of design and architecture on the health of individuals and larger populations, and how to create settings that promote health, healing, and well-being. Includes instruction in architecture, interior design, human health services, communication studies, medical and clinical innovations, behavioral and engineering sciences, hospitals and health systems, and environmental conditions that influence health.

abstract: Clinical cytogenetics research is integral to diagnosing genetic disorders, informing cancer treatment strategies, and ensuring compatibility in organ transplantation. However, the increasing resolution of genomic technologies, including next-generation sequencing (NGS), fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and high-throughput photomicrography, has generated vast, multi-modal datasets that exceed the processing capabilities of conventional computational infrastructure. Current methods for analyzing chromosomal abnormalities, structural variants, and mosaic mutations lack the scalability to integrate heterogeneous data types while maintaining the precision required for clinical applications. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through the development of advanced computational workflows for large-scale cytogenetic data analysis. The research will focus on three aims: (1) optimizing machine learning algorithms to detect subtle chromosomal rearrangements and copy-number variations in whole-genome sequencing data, (2) implementing GPU-accelerated image analysis pipelines for high-resolution FISH and photomicrography datasets to quantify spatial genomic patterns in cancer samples, and (3) building predictive models to correlate cytogenetic profiles with transplant rejection risks and chemotherapy response. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized processing frameworks (e.g., Apache Spark) and containerized environments (e.g., Singularity) to ensure reproducibility and scalability. The HPC resources will enable rapid analysis of petabyte-scale datasets, reducing turnaround times for critical diagnostics from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for identifying low-frequency mosaic variants in leukemia patients, open-source tools for integrating cytogenetic and transcriptomic data, and clinically validated models to predict post-transplant complications. This work will directly enhance the precision of genetic diagnostics, support personalized treatment strategies for hematologic malignancies, and improve organ transplantation outcomes. By democratizing access to scalable computational methods, the project will empower clinical cytogenetics laboratories to harness complex datasets for evidence-based patient care.
cip_definition: The clinical research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize electrical system design and fault detection in residential, commercial, and industrial settings, addressing gaps in traditional manual estimation methods. The increasing complexity of modern electrical infrastructures—including hybrid AC/DC systems, renewable energy integrations, and smart grid components—demands high-fidelity simulations to ensure safety, efficiency, and compliance with evolving codes. Current approaches often rely on oversimplified assumptions or static datasets, leading to suboptimal designs and delayed fault identification. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale electrical networks, model transient behaviors, and automate code-compliance checks. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) for thermal and electromagnetic modeling of wiring systems, machine learning algorithms trained on synthetic and real-world fault data, and Monte Carlo simulations to assess failure probabilities under diverse load conditions. These models will integrate real-time sensor data from prototype systems to refine predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for optimizing wire gauge selection, circuit protection coordination, and energy loss minimization across heterogeneous environments. The project will also produce open-source tools for automated National Electrical Code (NEC) compliance validation, reducing installation errors. By enabling rapid, high-resolution analysis of complex scenarios—such as arc fault dynamics or grid-tied solar inverter interactions—this work aims to advance training protocols for electricians and improve safety standards in next-generation electrical installations. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the computational intensity of multi-physics simulations and large-scale dataset processing, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain, and repair electric apparatus and systems such as residential, commercial, and industrial electric-power wiring; and DC and AC motors, controls, and electrical distribution panels. Includes instruction in the principles of electronics and electrical systems, wiring, power transmission, safety, industrial and household appliances, job estimation, electrical testing and inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The study of dynamic macromolecular assemblies remains a critical challenge in structural biology, particularly for systems exhibiting transient conformational states or complex multimeric interactions. Traditional experimental techniques often lack the temporal resolution to capture these dynamic processes, while conventional computational approaches are hindered by system size and sampling limitations. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and integrative modeling of two high-priority systems: (1) the conformational switching mechanism of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters during substrate translocation, and (2) the assembly dynamics of voltage-gated ion channel complexes with regulatory subunits. All-atom and coarse-grained MD simulations will be combined with cryo-EM density maps and X-ray crystallographic data using adaptive sampling algorithms and Markov state modeling to resolve metastable states and transition pathways. The proposed work requires extensive GPU-accelerated simulations (cumulatively >2.5 million core-hours) to achieve microsecond-to-millisecond sampling of systems containing 150,000–500,000 atoms, alongside development of custom analysis pipelines for detecting allosteric networks and interfacial stability in multi-protein complexes. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into nucleotide-dependent conformational coupling in ABC transporters—a process relevant to multidrug resistance—and atomistic models of ion channel regulation with implications for neurological disorder therapeutics. By bridging gaps between static structural snapshots and functional dynamics, this research will establish computational frameworks for studying elusive biological assemblies, directly advancing the program’s focus on molecular organization in living systems. The requested resources will enable unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution in modeling critical biomedical targets, fostering collaborative experimental-computational workflows in structural biology.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of submolecular and molecular components and assemblies of living systems and how they are organized into functional units such as cells and anatomic tissues. Includes instruction in glycoprotein, carbohydrate, protein, and nucleic acid structures and chemistry; cytoskeletal structure; nuclear and intracellular structures; molecular recognition; molecular chaperones; transcription and folding; multicellular organization; microtubules and microfilaments; cell differentiation; immunophysics; and DNA sequencing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic, multi-channel merchandising strategies in fragmented retail ecosystems. As consumer touchpoints diversify across physical stores, augmented reality (AR) interfaces, and hyper-localized social commerce platforms, traditional demand forecasting and inventory allocation models fail to account for real-time behavioral shifts and cross-channel interference effects. The project focuses on developing a graph neural network (GNN) framework enhanced by multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate emergent purchasing patterns in hybrid digital-physical environments. Computational workflows will integrate tera-scale transactional datasets with spatial-temporal behavioral traces from IoT-enabled smart stores and computer vision analyses of in-aisle customer movement patterns. Key innovations include the development of attention mechanisms to weight influence across heterogeneous data streams and the implementation of distributed quantum-inspired optimization algorithms for inventory routing under uncertainty. The HPC environment is critical for training models across 50+ simulated retail configurations simultaneously while maintaining sub-second latency for sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of prescriptive merchandising adjustments at 15-minute intervals, validated against live A/B tests with partner retailers. By bridging computational scalability gaps in current marketing operations tools, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for adaptive resource allocation in next-generation retail ecosystems, particularly for businesses operating at the intersection of immersive technologies and micro-localized fulfillment networks.
cip_title: Specialized Merchandising, Sales, and Marketing Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sales, marketing, and distribution operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing adaptive learning platforms through computationally intensive modeling of learner interactions, a critical gap in scalable educational technology research. While adaptive systems are increasingly deployed in K-12 and higher education environments, their underlying algorithms often lack the capacity to process multimodal learner data (e.g., text responses, clickstream patterns, and voice inputs) in real time while maintaining pedagogical coherence. The research will develop and train deep learning architectures to model how students construct knowledge during technology-mediated problem-solving tasks, with a focus on STEM education contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to handle three computational demands: 1) parallel processing of longitudinal interaction datasets from 10,000+ learners across diverse demographic groups, 2) neural architecture search for multi-modal transformer models that align cognitive processing patterns with learning outcomes, and 3) reinforcement learning simulations to test personalized intervention strategies. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for training ensemble models that integrate natural language processing of open-response inputs with temporal analysis of problem-solving pathways. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for dynamic difficulty adjustment in educational software, validated through benchmark comparisons against existing adaptive systems. By enabling real-time analysis of complex learner behaviors at scale, this work aims to advance evidence-based designs for educational technologies that balance computational personalization with human-centered pedagogy. The requested resources directly support the computational workload necessary to bridge educational research with machine learning innovation, particularly in modeling how diverse learners engage with increasingly complex digital learning environments. Results will inform both the academic field of educational technology design and practical implementations aimed at reducing achievement gaps through responsive technological supports.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, computer applications, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual analysis of British and Commonwealth literary works from the 18th century to the mid-20th century, with a focus on tracing the evolution of stylistic and thematic patterns across genres, regions, and historical contexts. The research addresses a critical gap in computational literary studies: the limited application of scalable, data-driven methods to analyze how British imperial and postcolonial dynamics manifest in literary form, particularly in understudied genres such as travel writing, epistolary fiction, and regional periodicals. By processing a corpus of over 50,000 digitized texts—including novels, poetry, pamphlets, and archival materials—the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, machine learning classification, and network analysis to identify stylistic shifts, intertextual references, and thematic clusters that reflect changing socio-political ideologies. Key computational challenges include training custom word embedding models to capture archaic and region-specific dialects, parsing non-standardized OCR outputs from historical documents, and mapping citation networks across dispersed Commonwealth archives. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the scale of data, enabling parallel processing of text extraction, and running iterative semantic similarity algorithms across multilingual subcorpora (e.g., works incorporating South Asian or African vernacular languages). Expected outcomes include a public dataset of annotated texts, visualizations of genre evolution timelines, and quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric periodization models in literary history. This work will provide scholars with new methodologies to interrogate the relationship between literary form and colonial legacies, while demonstrating the transformative potential of computational resources for humanities research traditionally reliant on close reading. By integrating HPC-driven macroanalysis with qualitative literary criticism, the project aims to redefine canonical boundaries and amplify marginalized voices within British and Commonwealth literary studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literatures and literary developments of the English-speaking peoples of the British Isles and the British Commonwealth, from the origins of the English language to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, country and regional specializations, literary criticism, and the study of folkloric traditions.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding interindividual variability in susceptibility to environmental toxins, particularly those influencing pulmonary and hepatic toxicity. Despite advances in toxicology, the mechanisms linking genetic polymorphisms in xenobiotic-metabolizing enzymes (e.g., CYP450 isoforms) to differential toxic outcomes remain poorly resolved. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model toxin-biomolecule interactions and simulate metabolic pathways at scale, integrating structural biology data with population-level genomic datasets. Key objectives include (1) predicting toxin-enzyme binding affinities across genetic variants using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, (2) reconstructing metabolic networks perturbed by chronic low-dose toxin exposure via kinetic modeling, and (3) identifying gene-environment interactions that modulate oxidative stress responses in human cell systems. Computational workflows will leverage quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) hybrid methods to resolve electron transfer events in mutagenic toxin activation, coupled with machine learning models trained on toxicogenomics data from primary human hepatocytes and airway epithelia. These analyses require parallelized processing of large-scale simulation ensembles (>10,000 GPU hours) and genome-to-phenotype association testing across multi-omics datasets (>50 TB). Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into genetic risk factors for toxin-induced carcinogenesis, predictive models of metabolic susceptibility, and candidate therapeutic targets for countermeasure development. The resource allocation will directly enable hypothesis-driven investigations of molecular toxicant signaling that cannot be experimentally resolved due to technical limitations in capturing rare stochastic events or long-timescale protein conformational changes. By bridging molecular toxicology with computational pharmacology, this work aims to advance precision risk assessment frameworks and inform personalized interventions for populations disproportionately exposed to environmental toxicants.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetic determinants of susceptibility to external pollutants and poisons; the interaction of toxic agents with biological systems at the molecular and cellular levels; and the development of countermeasures and treatments. Includes instruction in pharmacogenetics, biomolecular structure, gene expression and regulation, transgenic modeling, toxic events signaling, transcriptional activation, mutagenesis and carcinogenesis, pulmonary toxicology, xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress, risk assessment, molecular dosimetry, and studies of specific toxins and treatment therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing therapeutic interventions in acquired motor speech disorders (MSDs), such as apraxia of speech and dysarthria. While speech-language pathology (SLP) relies on evidence-based protocols, current approaches to personalizing therapy for MSDs remain largely heuristic, with limited computational tools to model the complex interactions between neural impairment, speech motor control, and linguistic factors. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating a computational framework that simulates speech production under varying neuromotor constraints and predicts individualized therapy outcomes. The project will utilize high-resolution acoustic and kinematic datasets from clinical populations, including electromagnetic articulography (EMA) and formant trajectory data, to train neural network models that map impaired speech motor patterns to perceptual intelligibility metrics. Computational experiments will employ dynamical systems modeling to simulate the effects of neuromotor parameters (e.g., muscle stiffness, coordination latency) on speech output, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to identify optimal therapeutic targets. HPC resources will be critical for parallelizing large-scale parameter sweeps across simulated speech tasks and scaling generative models to account for speaker-specific variability. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-source tools for simulating speech motor learning trajectories and a decision-support system that recommends personalized therapy parameters based on computational biomarkers. This work aims to establish a novel paradigm for data-driven intervention design in SLP, with potential applications in telerehabilitation and adaptive therapeutic technologies. By integrating computational neuroscience with clinical SLP practice, the project addresses an emerging niche in health sciences that intersects communication disorders, motor control theory, and artificial intelligence.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance pharmacoeconomic modeling and regulatory decision-making frameworks for optimizing drug reimbursement policies. Current challenges in pharmacy administration include integrating large-scale real-world data (RWD)—such as electronic health records, insurance claims, and patient-reported outcomes—with dynamic cost-effectiveness models to evaluate therapeutic value under evolving regulatory and market conditions. Traditional computational methods struggle to manage the combinatorial complexity of variables influencing drug pricing, patient adherence, and population health outcomes, particularly when simulating longitudinal policy impacts across diverse subpopulations. To address this, we propose developing a scalable, agent-based simulation platform that integrates Bayesian hierarchical models, discrete-event simulations, and machine learning-driven sensitivity analyses. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte RWD datasets to parameterize synthetic patient cohorts, while Monte Carlo methods will assess uncertainty in cost-benefit projections under varying reimbursement scenarios. Key computational challenges include optimizing memory allocation for sparse, high-dimensional healthcare data and accelerating Markov chain convergence in pharmacoeconomic models through GPU-accelerated sampling. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for predicting the fiscal and clinical impacts of formulary design choices, prior authorization policies, and value-based contracting structures. This work directly supports evidence-based pharmacy policy by quantifying trade-offs between patient access, healthcare system costs, and manufacturer incentives. The requested computing resources will also facilitate reproducibility through containerized workflows and enable open-access publication of de-identified model outputs for regulatory stakeholders. By bridging computational scalability gaps in pharmacoeconomic research, this project aims to establish best practices for HPC-driven policy analytics in pharmaceutical services management.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Pharmacy Administration and Pharmacy Policy and Regulatory Affairs
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial, social, and economic sciences to the study and management of the distribution and use of pharmaceutical products and the provision of pharmacy services. Includes instruction in research design and methods, statistics, social and organizational behavior, pharmacoeconomics, management of pharmacy services, outcomes research, product planning and reimbursement, cost-benefit analysis, drug marketing, pharmacy and pharmaceutics law and regulation, risk assessment, and organization of the health care system.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in aviation operations management, particularly in optimizing dynamic decision-making for airport ground operations, air traffic flow, and resource allocation under uncertainty. Current models struggle to integrate real-time data streams—such as weather fluctuations, flight delays, and passenger demand variability—with the complex regulatory and safety constraints inherent to aviation systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation and optimization framework. The computational approach will combine agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods for stochastic scenario generation, and reinforcement learning algorithms to create adaptive decision-support tools. Agent-based models will simulate interactions between aircraft, ground crews, air traffic control systems, and terminal passengers, while reinforcement learning will train policies for real-time resource allocation (e.g., gate assignments, fuel trucks, security staffing). Large-scale historical data from FAA databases, airline operations, and IoT-enabled airport infrastructure will be processed in parallel to calibrate models and validate scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of multi-airport network simulations, enabling rapid evaluation of millions of operational scenarios with sub-minute decision cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for bottleneck reduction, robust strategies for irregular operations (e.g., weather disruptions), and a scalable digital twin prototype for aviation hubs. This work will provide aviation managers with evidence-based tools to balance efficiency, safety margins, and environmental impacts while advancing computational methodology in operations research. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to bridge gaps between theoretical optimization models and practical aviation management needs, directly supporting the FAA’s NextGen modernization goals and contributing to sustainable aviation business practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the management of aviation industry operations and services. Includes instruction in airport operations, ground traffic direction, ground support and flightline operations, passenger and cargo operations, flight safety and security operations, aviation industry regulation, and related business aspects of managing aviation enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the formation and evolution of singularities in geometric flows, with a focus on Ricci flow and mean curvature flow in high-dimensional Riemannian manifolds. These flows are central to understanding geometric and topological transformations, yet analytical solutions to their governing nonlinear partial differential equations remain limited, particularly in non-Euclidean settings or under degenerate initial conditions. The research will employ large-scale numerical simulations to resolve fine-scale behavior near singularities, which are critical to conjectures in geometric analysis, including the classification of compact manifolds admitting metrics with prescribed curvature properties. Key computational challenges include discretizing high-dimensional manifolds with adaptive mesh refinement, solving coupled tensor PDEs with stiff nonlinearities, and preserving geometric invariants under numerical evolution. The proposed methods combine spectral collocation techniques on structured meshes, implicit-explicit time-stepping schemes, and parallelized tensor algebra operations optimized for distributed-memory architectures. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the memory and processing demands of simulating 4- and 5-dimensional manifolds with sufficient resolution to capture singularity dynamics. Expected outcomes include new conjectures on the stability of singularity types under metric perturbations, quantitative bounds on curvature blow-up rates, and open-source software tools for geometric flow simulations. The results will advance foundational knowledge in differential geometry, with potential applications to theoretical physics, including the study of spacetime singularities in general relativity. By bridging analytical and computational approaches, this work aims to establish reproducible frameworks for probing geometric structures inaccessible to purely theoretical methods.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties, measurements, and relationships pertaining to points, lines, angles, surfaces, and solids. Includes instruction in global analysis, differential geometry, Euclidian and Non-Euclidian geometry, set theory, manifolds, integral geometry, and applications to algebra and other topics.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the modeling and optimization of resilient urban transportation networks under dynamic stressors, including population growth, climate variability, and evolving mobility technologies. Current simulation frameworks struggle to capture the interdependencies between infrastructure degradation, traffic flow patterns, and real-time decision-making at metropolitan scales, limiting their utility for adaptive planning. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining agent-based modeling, finite element analysis, and graph-theoretic network optimization. The computational workflow will integrate multi-resolution datasets—spanning traffic sensor feeds, material fatigue models, and socioeconomic mobility patterns—into a coupled simulation platform. Parallelized finite element solvers will assess pavement and bridge deterioration under probabilistic climate scenarios, while GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize traffic signal control and rerouting strategies in response to simulated disruptions. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these analyses to city-level networks with sub-meter spatial resolution and sub-minute temporal resolution, which exceeds the capacity of conventional workstations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for quantifying trade-offs between infrastructure maintenance investments, congestion mitigation, and equity in transportation access. Results will inform the development of digital twin tools for municipal planners, enabling proactive adaptation to systemic shocks. By leveraging distributed memory architectures and scalable optimization libraries, this work will also contribute methodological advances in computationally intensive civil systems analysis. The resource request supports 12 months of large-scale simulations on GPU- and CPU-based clusters, including parametric studies across 10+ metropolitan templates. This project aligns with national priorities for sustainable urban infrastructure and provides open-source computational tools to the civil engineering community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in civil engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Respiratory care protocols for mechanically ventilated patients rely on generalized guidelines that often fail to account for individual variability in lung biomechanics and disease progression, leading to suboptimal outcomes in critical care settings. This project seeks to develop patient-specific computational models of pulmonary mechanics to optimize ventilator settings in real time, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome the computational complexity of dynamic, multi-scale simulations. Current approaches use static compliance and resistance metrics, which inadequately capture the nonlinear viscoelastic behavior of damaged lung tissue or heterogeneous ventilation-perfusion mismatches. We propose a hybrid methodology integrating finite element modeling of regional lung deformation with computational fluid dynamics simulations of airflow, calibrated using high-resolution clinical data from electrical impedance tomography and ventilator waveform analyses. HPC resources are essential to solve these coupled partial differential equations at clinically relevant spatiotemporal resolutions, enabling iterative parameter optimization via machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective electronic health record data. The resulting framework will predict optimal positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), tidal volume, and inspiratory flow profiles tailored to individual patients’ evolving pathophysiology. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for generating real-time ventilator adjustment recommendations, reducing the incidence of ventilator-induced lung injury and accelerating weaning protocols. By bridging respiratory physiology, biomechanics, and computational engineering, this work establishes a paradigm for precision critical care that transcends traditional protocol-based approaches. The computational tools developed will be shared via an open-source platform, fostering collaboration in emerging interdisciplinary domains at the intersection of clinical respiratory therapy and predictive computational modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive resource management framework for heterogeneous computing systems, addressing the challenge of dynamically balancing performance, energy efficiency, and reliability in distributed edge computing environments. As edge devices and IoT systems grow in complexity, integrating diverse hardware accelerators (e.g., GPUs, FPGAs) with traditional CPUs, existing scheduling algorithms struggle to optimize workloads across mixed architectures under real-time constraints. The research will employ a hybrid computational approach combining discrete-event simulation, reinforcement learning (RL), and hardware-in-the-loop testing to model and predict system behavior. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train multi-agent RL models that coordinate task allocation, power management, and fault tolerance strategies across simulated edge nodes. Large-scale simulations will replicate variable network conditions, hardware failures, and workload spikes to evaluate resilience and efficiency trade-offs. Concurrently, prototype testing will validate models using containerized microservices on FPGA-CPU clusters. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive resource orchestration, reducing energy consumption by 15-25% in benchmark edge computing scenarios while maintaining sub-millisecond latency thresholds. The project will also generate datasets correlating hardware telemetry with optimization policies, supporting reproducibility in edge system design. By enhancing the program’s focus on applied computing systems, this work bridges gaps between theoretical resource allocation models and real-world deployment challenges, directly benefiting industries reliant on low-latency, energy-conscious edge infrastructure. The requested HPC access will enable iterative training of resource-intensive RL agents and parallelized simulation runs, which are infeasible on local laboratory hardware.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of professionals who use computer systems. Includes instruction in basic computer design and architecture, programming, problems of specific computer applications, component and system maintenance and inspection procedures, hardware and software problem diagnosis and repair, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize flight training scenarios through real-time simulation of complex aerodynamic, environmental, and operational variables.
