Current flight training tools often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the nonlinear interactions between aircraft performance, weather systems, and human decision-making under stress. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating high-resolution atmospheric modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of aircraft behavior, and adaptive machine learning algorithms to generate dynamic, scenario-based training environments. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize large-scale CFD simulations of fixed and rotary wing aircraft across diverse flight regimes, coupled with ensemble weather prediction models. These simulations will inform the development of a probabilistic risk assessment tool that quantifies trainee performance under variable turbulence, system failures, and airspace congestion scenarios. Additionally, reinforcement learning techniques will be applied to adapt training modules in real time based on instructor-defined learning objectives and trainee response patterns. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for CFD preprocessing and distributed CPU clusters for Monte Carlo analyses of scenario outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform compatible with existing flight training devices, a database of validated performance benchmarks for FAA-certified training scenarios, and predictive models of skill acquisition rates under optimized training sequences. This work aims to enhance the safety and efficiency of flight instruction by providing empirically grounded, computationally robust tools to assess trainee readiness while reducing the cost and environmental impact of live training flights. Results will directly inform updates to FAA advisory circulars on simulation-based training credits and support the development of standardized proficiency metrics for next-generation flight instructor curricula.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the training of pilots or navigators, to prepare them to fly and/or navigate commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue aircraft, and fixed or rotary wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications and navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to administer the FAA commercial air crew examinations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-modal health data in allied health diagnostics and treatment planning necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize clinical decision-making. This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating heterogeneous data streams—including high-resolution medical imaging, wearable sensor outputs, genomic biomarkers, and longitudinal electronic health records—to develop predictive models for personalized rehabilitation outcomes in patients with neuromusculoskeletal disorders. Current analytical approaches struggle with the volume, velocity, and dimensionality of these datasets, particularly when analyzing dynamic patient responses to multi-stage interventions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a federated learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on distributed datasets while maintaining patient privacy. The computational workflow will involve parallelized processing of 3D motion capture data (sampled at 200Hz), GPU-accelerated feature extraction from diffusion tensor imaging, and hybrid quantum-classical optimization of hyperparameters for ensemble models. Resource-intensive tasks include real-time simulation of biomechanical load distributions across 10^6+ voxel meshes and federated averaging across five institutional partners. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for identifying optimal intervention sequences in traumatic brain injury rehabilitation, (2) open-source tools for federated analysis of sensitive allied health data, and (3) quantitative benchmarks comparing HPC-enabled workflows to conventional clinical analytics pipelines. By enabling rapid integration of multi-scale data from diverse diagnostic modalities, this research will directly enhance evidence-based practice in prosthetics fitting, therapeutic exercise prescription, and neurorehabilitation monitoring. The requested computing resources are essential for achieving sub-24hr model retraining cycles required to adapt recommendations to evolving patient status, representing a 40x speed improvement over current institutional capabilities.
cip_title: Allied Health Diagnostic, Intervention, and Treatment Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health diagnostic, intervention, and treatment professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Interindividual variability in drug response poses a significant challenge in pharmacotherapy, often leading to suboptimal outcomes and adverse effects. Traditional approaches struggle to integrate the multifactorial determinants of drug efficacy and toxicity, including genetic, molecular, and clinical variables. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulate drug interactions at scale. We will employ molecular dynamics simulations to characterize drug-target binding affinities across diverse patient-derived genomic profiles, alongside machine learning algorithms trained on multi-omics datasets to identify biomarkers predictive of therapeutic outcomes. Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling will be integrated to quantify temporal drug behavior in heterogeneous populations. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of large-scale genomic data, intensive free energy calculations, and iterative optimization of neural networks, necessitating HPC infrastructure for feasible execution. Anticipated outcomes include patient-specific dosing guidelines, mechanistic insights into resistance mutations, and classifiers to stratify patients by toxicity risk. By elucidating the interplay between genomic variation and drug action, this research aims to advance precision pharmacotherapy, reduce empiric treatment strategies, and improve clinical outcomes across therapeutic areas such as cardiovascular diseases, oncology, and infectious diseases. The proposed computational framework will also provide a scalable platform for future investigations into emerging therapeutics and population-specific pharmacogenomic trends.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pharmacotherapy

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance neuroanatomical research on the structural organization of synaptic connectivity in the mammalian somatosensory cortex. A critical gap persists in understanding how microcircuit anatomy relates to functional signaling dynamics and how these relationships are disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder. Traditional histological and imaging methods lack the scalability to map synaptic-level connectivity across entire cortical columns, while existing computational models often oversimplify the 3D spatial complexity of neuronal arbors. To address this, we propose a dual computational approach. First, we will process ultra-high-resolution serial electron microscopy datasets (50+ TB) from mouse cortical tissue using automated segmentation pipelines enhanced by custom deep learning algorithms to reconstruct neuronal morphologies and synaptic contacts. Second, we will develop biologically constrained network models incorporating reconstructed morphologies, ion channel distributions, and synapse locations to simulate signal propagation in both healthy and neurodevelopmentally altered microcircuits. HPC resources are essential for managing large-scale image analysis, optimizing neural network training for segmentation tasks, and running physics-based simulations of extracellular electrical fields generated by morphologically detailed neurons. Expected outcomes include the first spatially explicit connectome of a cortical column with integrated electrophysiological parameters, novel insights into how dendritic geometry shapes population coding, and a publicly accessible computational framework linking neuroanatomical features to circuit dysfunction. This work will establish an infrastructure for testing anatomical hypotheses about neurological disorders that cannot be investigated experimentally, directly supporting the development of targeted neurotherapies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates or the nervous system of invertebrates. Includes instruction in cellular and circuit anatomy, mapping of neuronal pathways, anatomical distribution and mapping of neuronal signaling molecules and their receptors, and the anatomical basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the linguistic and structural evolution of rabbinic responsa literature (She’elot u-Teshuvot) across temporal, geographic, and cultural boundaries. While traditional scholarship in Rabbinical Studies has focused on manual close reading of these legal-ethical texts, the sheer volume of material—spanning over 1,500 years and tens of thousands of documents—presents a barrier to systemic analysis of patterns in halachic reasoning, rhetorical strategies, and cross-cultural influence. The project addresses this gap by developing a computational pipeline to process digitized responsa in Hebrew and Aramaic, integrating natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for rabbinic textual structures (e.g., citation chains, argument-counterargument frameworks) with geospatial-temporal network analysis. Custom algorithms will trace the diffusion of legal concepts through Jewish diaspora communities, identify syntactic markers of cultural adaptation in ritual guidance, and quantify shifts in ethical priorities relative to historical crises such as forced migrations or technological disruptions. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on non-standard orthography and abbreviations in manuscript sources, running large-scale graph analyses of citation networks, and simulating probabilistic models of decision-tree influences across rabbinic schools. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access annotated corpus of 10,000+ responsa enriched with computational metadata, 2) visualization tools mapping doctrinal development against external historical datasets, and 3) quantitative frameworks to contextualize contemporary rabbinic discourse within longitudinal patterns of legal-ethical reasoning. By bridging computational humanities and rabbinic textual tradition, this work aims to provide scholars and religious practitioners with new methodologies for understanding Judaism’s adaptive legal-ethical systems while preserving the interpretive nuance central to Rabbinical Studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as Rabbis. Includes instruction in Talmud, Halacha, Liturgy and Rituals, Rabbinical Thought, Jewish Ethics, Jewish Education, Pastoral Counseling and Homiletics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for adaptive typography systems capable of dynamically optimizing readability, aesthetic coherence, and cross-platform consistency in digital publishing. Current computational tools for typographic design often rely on static templates or manual adjustments, which struggle to accommodate the diverse screen resolutions, aspect ratios, and user accessibility needs of modern devices. The research problem centers on developing machine learning (ML)-driven frameworks to automate context-sensitive typographic composition while preserving design intent. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose training generative models on a curated dataset of 50,000+ professionally designed documents spanning genres such as editorial layouts, interactive eBooks, and responsive web interfaces. These models will learn hierarchical relationships between typographic variables (e.g., kerning, line spacing, font pairing) and contextual factors like device specifications, content type, and user preferences. Computational workflows will include parallelized rendering simulations to evaluate perceptual legibility under varying conditions and evolutionary algorithms to iteratively refine layout parameters. The project further plans to implement a real-time optimization pipeline using GPU-accelerated inference, enabling rapid prototyping of adaptive typography for A/B testing with human participants. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated typographic adaptation, validated through usability studies measuring reading efficiency and aesthetic satisfaction across diverse digital platforms. This work aims to advance the integration of computational design principles into communication workflows, reducing production costs while enhancing accessibility in journalism and digital media. By demonstrating scalable HPC applications in non-traditional computational domains, the project will also contribute methodological insights for resource-efficient ML deployment in graphic design education and practice.
cip_title: Computer Typography and Composition Equipment Operator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to design and execute page formats, layouts and text composition, and to make typographical selections using computer graphics and other computer-assisted design programs.

abstract: The safety and shelf-life of processed foods are critically influenced by microbial dynamics and physicochemical interactions during production and storage. Current experimental approaches to optimize processing parameters or predict spoilage risks are time-consuming and often fail to capture the complexity of multi-variable systems. This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to model microbial behavior, enzymatic activity, and nutrient degradation in heterogeneous food matrices under varying thermal, chemical, and storage conditions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, agent-based microbial growth models, and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive analytics. MD simulations will resolve atomic-level interactions between water, lipids, proteins, and preservatives in model food systems, while agent-based models will predict population-level microbial responses to environmental stressors. ML algorithms, trained on experimental and simulated datasets, will identify nonlinear relationships between processing variables (e.g., temperature gradients, pH, preservative concentrations) and quality outcomes. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from collaborator labs, including time-resolved spectroscopy and microbial viability assays. Successful implementation will yield predictive tools to optimize pasteurization protocols, reduce preservative use without compromising safety, and extend shelf-life through scenario-based simulations of novel packaging materials. This work addresses a critical gap in food science by enabling rapid, resource-efficient exploration of processing-design spaces that are infeasible to study experimentally. The outcomes will directly support industry efforts to minimize food waste, enhance sustainability, and meet evolving regulatory standards for food safety. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive multiscale simulations central to this interdisciplinary approach.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in food sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, real-time flight simulation environment to enhance the training of commercial flight instructors and their students in managing complex aerodynamic scenarios and emergency procedures. Current flight simulators used in training programs often lack the computational resolution to model fine-grained interactions between aircraft systems, environmental variables (e.g., turbulence, icing), and pilot decision-making under stress. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-physics interactions—including computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airflow over control surfaces, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural responses, and machine learning (ML) for predictive modeling of trainee behavior—within a unified, dynamically adaptive framework. The computational approach will involve parallelized simulations using GPU-accelerated solvers to resolve real-time aerodynamic forces and system failures, coupled with agent-based models to emulate air traffic and environmental stochasticity. Large-scale parameter sweeps will assess scenarios such as partial engine loss, rapid decompression, and crosswind landings across diverse aircraft types (fixed-wing and rotary). Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit optimized for HPC clusters, enabling instructors to design bespoke training modules with quantifiable risk profiles and adaptive difficulty. This resource will directly support FAA-certified programs in validating trainee readiness under rare but critical conditions, reducing reliance on costly physical prototypes. By integrating high-resolution simulations into pedagogical workflows, the project aims to elevate aviation safety standards and inform regulatory updates for flight crew competency assessments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the training of pilots or navigators, to prepare them to fly and/or navigate commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue aircraft, and fixed or rotary wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications and navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to administer the FAA commercial air crew examinations.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathological vascular remodeling—such as arterial stiffening and maladaptive hypertrophy—representing a critical yet poorly understood driver of disease progression. This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and molecular mechanisms underlying vascular remodeling in hypertension and diabetes, focusing on the interplay between hemodynamic stress, vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) plasticity, and extracellular matrix dysregulation. A key challenge lies in integrating multiscale physiological data—from cellular signaling pathways to tissue-level mechanical behavior—to predict disease trajectories and identify novel therapeutic targets. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining multiscale computational modeling with experimental validation. The computational approach includes (1) finite element analysis to simulate blood vessel wall mechanics under dynamic pressure loads, (2) agent-based modeling of VSMC phenotypic switching and migration, and (3) network modeling of calcium-dependent signaling pathways regulating contractility and matrix synthesis. These models will be parameterized using in vivo hemodynamic data from murine models of hypertension and human clinical imaging datasets. The integration of terabyte-scale multiphoton microscopy datasets of vascular microstructure with real-time hemodynamic simulations requires significant parallel processing capabilities, particularly for iterative optimization of model parameters and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive models of vascular remodeling progression, identification of mechanosensitive therapeutic targets, and validation of computational predictions through ex vivo vascular reactivity assays. This work will advance understanding of how localized mechanical forces drive systemic cardiovascular pathology while establishing a computational framework adaptable to studying other vascular disorders. The requested HPC resources are essential given the need for high-resolution 3D simulations, complex parameter space exploration, and rapid iteration between modeling and experimental validation cycles.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and functioning of the heart, vascular system, and blood in animals and human beings and the disorders and diseases associated with the cardiovascular system. Includes instruction in cardiovascular physiology, blood physiology, vasculature, vascular metabolism, neural control of cardiovascular function, microvascular permeability and membrane transport, cardiac contraction mechanisms, homeostasis, and applications to topics such as arteriosclerosis, heart disease, diabetes, vascular remodeling, transplantation, transfusion, and pacemakers and artificial organs.

abstract: The pulp and paper manufacturing industry faces critical challenges in optimizing energy-intensive processes, reducing environmental impact, and enhancing product performance while meeting growing demand for sustainable materials. Current limitations in understanding the multiscale interactions between lignocellulosic fibers, chemical additives, and process conditions hinder advancements in efficiency and material innovation. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model fiber behavior, chemical transport, and fluid-structure interactions during pulping, bleaching, and paper formation processes. The MD simulations will resolve nanoscale phenomena, such as fiber swelling and lignin dissolution kinetics, while CFD models will predict macroscale fluid flow and heat transfer in industrial-scale digesters and coating systems. ML algorithms will bridge these scales by identifying correlations between fiber morphology, process parameters, and final product properties. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, large datasets from experimental characterization, and real-time optimization of coupled simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive models for minimizing chemical usage in bleaching, optimizing coating uniformity, and designing energy-efficient drying protocols. This work will directly inform pilot-scale trials at collaborating mill facilities, with potential reductions in process energy consumption by 15–20% and improved mechanical properties of recycled paper products. By advancing computational capabilities in paper science, this project aims to accelerate the transition to circular economy practices in the pulp and paper sector while providing open-source simulation tools for the broader engineering community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and manufacturing of pulp and paper products. Includes instruction in pulp and paper science, pulping and bleaching processes, paper structure and processes, pulp and paper manufacturing, coating technology, surface and colloid science, and fibers.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of fire dynamics in complex, multi-use urban environments, with a focus on scenarios involving atypical structural materials and hybrid occupancy spaces (e.g., mixed residential-commercial-industrial zones). Current fire spread models, largely designed for homogeneous environments or standardized building codes, inadequately capture emergent risks posed by novel construction materials, retrofitted historical buildings, and ad-hoc urban densification. The computational limitations of existing tools restrict their ability to resolve fine-scale interactions between heterogeneous fuels, ventilation pathways, and human evacuation behaviors in real time. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-physics framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), discrete element modeling (DEM), and agent-based simulations (ABS) to model fire progression, structural degradation, and occupant egress simultaneously at city-block scales. The HPC implementation will prioritize parallelized solver algorithms to handle high-resolution 3D meshes for heat transfer and smoke dispersion, coupled with machine learning surrogates to accelerate DEM-ABS feedback loops. Validation will utilize historical fire incident data from municipalities with dense, mixed-use urban footprints, supplemented by controlled experimental benchmarks. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source simulation toolkit capable of informing fire code updates for evolving urban landscapes, optimizing emergency response protocols for atypical fire scenarios, and quantifying risk trade-offs associated with non-standard retrofitting practices. By bridging gaps between traditional fire science and computational engineering, this work aims to establish a foundational framework for next-generation fire protection strategies in understudied urban contexts.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fire protection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Hematologic malignancies and disorders, such as acute leukemias, myelodysplastic syndromes, and lymphomas, exhibit complex molecular heterogeneity that drives treatment resistance and disease progression. Current clinical strategies often rely on generalized protocols, leading to suboptimal outcomes for many patients. This project seeks to address this challenge by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omic datasets and predict patient-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities. We propose an integrative computational approach combining bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, and epigenetic profiling from a cohort of 500 patients with refractory hematologic diseases. These datasets will be processed using scalable bioinformatics pipelines to identify recurrent mutations, dysregulated signaling pathways, and clonal architecture patterns. Machine learning models—including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers—will be trained to associate molecular features with clinical outcomes, such as drug response and relapse risk. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize the structural consequences of high-priority mutations in hematopoietic transcription factors (e.g., RUNX1, CEBPA) to infer functional impacts. The HPC environment is critical for managing the scale of genomic data (>200 TB), parallelizing computationally intensive tasks (e.g., variant calling, phylogenetic tree reconstruction), and enabling real-time interactive visualization of 3D protein-ligand interactions. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early intervention, patient stratification algorithms for targeted therapies, and dynamic models of resistance mechanisms. This work will directly inform two ongoing clinical trials at our institution, optimizing trial design by pre-selecting patients likely to benefit from experimental agents. By bridging large-scale genomic analysis with clinical decision-making, this project aims to advance precision medicine paradigms in hematology, reducing ineffective treatments and improving survival for high-risk populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the mechanisms and therapy of diseases of the blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lymph, including patient management, diagnostic tests, biopsies, and other procedures.

abstract: Diabetes mellitus represents a complex metabolic disorder with multifaceted etiology, heterogeneous clinical manifestations, and variable treatment responses. Despite advances in clinical management, persistent gaps remain in understanding the dynamic interplay between genetic susceptibility, molecular pathways, and environmental factors that drive disease progression and complications. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models integrating genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical data from diverse diabetic cohorts. The primary research problem centers on identifying robust biomarkers predictive of glycemic deterioration and microvascular complications, while elucidating context-specific therapeutic targets. A hybrid machine learning framework will be implemented, combining unsupervised clustering for patient stratification, graph neural networks to model interacting biological pathways, and Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty in multi-omics integration. Parallelized workflows will process whole-genome sequencing data (>10,000 samples) and longitudinal electronic health records, requiring distributed memory architectures for genome-wide association studies and time-series analyses. Molecular dynamics simulations of insulin receptor variants will complement these analyses, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes to assess structural-functional relationships at atomic resolution. Anticipated outcomes include the discovery of novel genetic modifiers of β-cell dysfunction, a predictive model for diabetic kidney disease progression, and a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking molecular signatures to clinical phenotypes. By enabling large-scale data synthesis across biological scales, this HPC-driven approach aims to advance precision medicine strategies in diabetes care, ultimately informing targeted interventions tailored to individual pathophysiological profiles. The computational infrastructure will support reproducible workflows compliant with FAIR data principles, with all models and pipelines made available to the research community upon publication.
cip_definition: Research focused on Diabetes

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize safety and operational efficiency in commercial vehicle training programs through high-fidelity simulations of vehicle dynamics, driver behavior, and environmental conditions. Commercial vehicle operators face complex challenges, including variable cargo loads, diverse road conditions, and evolving vehicle technologies such as electric powertrains. Traditional training methods struggle to replicate these scenarios at scale, limiting opportunities for risk-free experiential learning. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-physics interactions between vehicles, cargo, and infrastructure under thousands of simulated scenarios. Agent-based models will simulate driver decision-making processes, while finite element analysis will evaluate stress distributions in cargo securing systems during emergency maneuvers. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify high-risk operational patterns from synthetic and real-world telemetry data. The computational workload requires parallelized simulations across multiple nodes to achieve the necessary resolution for capturing transient mechanical forces, aerodynamic effects, and human-machine interface responses. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for cargo securement failure modes, (2) optimized training modules addressing common accident precursors, and (3) digital twins of commercial vehicles adaptable to evolving powertrain technologies. By quantifying relationships between operator decisions, vehicle responses, and external conditions, this research will enable data-driven improvements to instructional curricula and certification standards. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will empower technical educators to create scenario libraries reflecting regional operational challenges, from mountain descents with heavy payloads to urban last-mile delivery constraints. This work directly supports the program's mission to advance commercial vehicle education through technological innovation while addressing critical workforce safety needs in transportation industries.
cip_title: Truck and Bus Driver/ Commercial Vehicle Operator and Instructor
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to drive trucks and buses, delivery vehicles, for-hire vehicles and other commercial vehicles, or to instruct commercial vehicle operators. Includes instruction in operating gas, diesel, or electrically-powered vehicles; loading and unloading cargo or passengers; reporting delays or accidents on the road; verifying load against shipping papers; arranging transportation for personnel; and keeping records of receipts and fares.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to analyze and optimize decision-making processes in music management, with a focus on predictive modeling for audience engagement, resource allocation in event promotion, and dynamic pricing strategies for music products. The research addresses the growing complexity of data-driven management in the music industry, where large-scale datasets from streaming platforms, social media, and ticket sales require advanced analytical methods. Traditional approaches often struggle to integrate multimodal data (e.g., audio metadata, consumer behavior metrics, geographic trends) in real time, limiting adaptive strategies for emerging artists and small-to-mid-sized music organizations. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC) framework leveraging machine learning and agent-based modeling. The computational pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets to train ensemble models predicting regional demand for live events, simulate the impact of marketing variables on merchandise sales, and identify optimal contract terms for artist-fan engagement platforms. GPU-accelerated clustering algorithms will classify audience segments based on streaming patterns and demographic cross-correlations, while Monte Carlo methods will assess financial risk in tour planning scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these analyses across heterogeneous datasets and enabling real-time parameter optimization via parallelized workflows. Outcomes will include open-source software modules for music management analytics, validated against case studies from independent record labels and music festivals. By integrating computational social science methods with industry-specific challenges, this work aims to democratize data-driven tools for non-profit music organizations and reduce operational uncertainties in artist promotion. The project will also contribute interdisciplinary insights into how computational resource allocation can support creative industries within academic programs focused on visual arts, media, and design.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage music organizations, operations, facilities, and personnel. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; music products merchandising; artist agency and promotion; music law; and applications to specific activities such as managing theaters, recording studios and companies, bands and other ensembles, individual artists, and music organizations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial machinery and the demand for rapid, cost-effective repair strategies necessitate advanced computational tools to optimize maintenance protocols. This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting mechanical failures in high-stakes environments—such as manufacturing systems and transportation infrastructure—where unplanned downtime leads to significant economic losses. Traditional diagnostic methods often rely on heuristic approaches or oversimplified models, which struggle to account for dynamic interactions between wear, environmental conditions, and material fatigue. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a hybrid computational framework integrating physics-based simulations with machine learning (ML) to predict failure modes and prioritize repair interventions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distribution, crack propagation, and thermal degradation across diverse mechanical systems. Concurrently, ML algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets—including vibrational spectra, thermal imaging, and maintenance logs—will identify patterns indicative of incipient failures. By coupling these approaches through surrogate modeling and real-time data assimilation, the framework will dynamically update risk assessments and recommend targeted maintenance actions. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from industrial partners, focusing on gearbox systems and hydraulic actuators as case studies. Outcomes include a scalable predictive maintenance toolkit capable of reducing equipment downtime by 20–30% in pilot applications, alongside open-source simulation templates for educational use in technician training programs. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary resolution in multi-physics simulations and managing the computational load of parallelized ML training. This work bridges the gap between theoretical mechanics and practical repair workflows, offering a paradigm shift in how maintenance resources are allocated across technology-driven industries.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of tools, equipment, and machines.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods in sustainable fashion design and textile innovation. Current practices in apparel design face challenges in balancing aesthetic creativity with material efficiency, particularly as the industry shifts toward circular economies and reduced waste. Traditional physical prototyping and manual pattern optimization are resource-intensive, limiting scalability and iterative experimentation. This research proposes a computational framework integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) and physics-based simulations to automate and optimize design processes. The project will develop machine learning models trained on diverse datasets of historical textile patterns, material properties, and consumer trend analytics to generate novel, sustainable design concepts. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) simulations will model stress, drape, and wearability of digitally fabricated textiles under varied environmental conditions, enabling rapid virtual prototyping. A key innovation lies in coupling these approaches to create a feedback loop: AI-generated designs will inform simulation parameters, while simulation outcomes will refine the generative models to prioritize material efficiency and structural integrity. The computational workload involves large-scale parallel processing for training multi-modal neural networks, iterative 3D simulations of fabric behavior, and real-time rendering of high-resolution virtual garments. By transitioning design workflows to HPC-enabled digital environments, this research aims to reduce physical prototyping cycles by 60-80%, minimize textile waste in early-stage design, and establish data-driven metrics for sustainability in apparel production. Outcomes will include open-source tools for parametric pattern generation and a public dataset linking material choices to environmental impact indices, fostering broader academic and industry collaboration. This work bridges gaps between artistic intuition and computational rigor, offering a transformative framework for eco-conscious fashion innovation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional design of commercial fashions, apparel, and accessories, and the management of fashion development projects. Includes instruction in apparel design; accessory design; the design of men's', women's', and children's' wear; flat pattern design; computer-assisted design and manufacturing; concept planning; designing in specific materials; labor and cost analysis; history of fashion; fabric art and printing; and the principles of management and operations in the fashion industry.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of quantum reaction dynamics in heterogeneous chemical systems, a critical challenge in chemical physics where traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve atomistic details of short-lived intermediates and transition states. We aim to computationally model nonadiabatic energy transfer processes at molecule-surface interfaces and solvated environments, systems central to catalytic and photochemical applications. Current limitations in simulating such processes stem from the high computational cost of accurately treating coupled electronic and nuclear motion across multiple scales while preserving quantum coherence effects. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT) with trajectory surface hopping dynamics, accelerated by machine-learned potential energy surfaces. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute massively parallel simulations of molecular ensembles under varying interfacial geometries and thermodynamic conditions. The allocation will enable large-scale ab initio calculations using software packages like Q-Chem and in-house modified versions of LAMMPS, which are optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures. Key deliverables include quantitative predictions of solvent-mediated charge transfer rates in metal-organic complexes and surface-alignment effects on reaction branching ratios in photocatalysis. These results will directly test recent theoretical predictions about the role of decoherence in suppressing unwanted recombination pathways at interfaces. The outcomes will provide foundational insights for designing energy-efficient catalytic systems and advance methodological standards for simulating quantum dynamics in spatially inhomogeneous environments. By integrating chemical physics principles with scalable computational workflows, this work bridges critical gaps between quantum mechanical accuracy and mesoscale phenomena relevant to next-generation chemical technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of structural phenomena combining the disciplines of physical chemistry and atomic/molecular physics. Includes instruction in heterogeneous structures, alignment and surface phenomena, quantum theory, mathematical physics, statistical and classical mechanics, chemical kinetics, and laser physics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, machine learning-driven geospatial intelligence framework to enhance real-time threat assessment and disaster response capabilities for homeland security applications. Traditional geospatial analysis methods struggle to integrate heterogeneous data streams—such as satellite imagery, social media feeds, sensor networks, and historical incident reports—at the scale and speed required for dynamic security scenarios. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing multi-modal geospatial data to identify emerging threats, predict vulnerability hotspots, and optimize resource deployment during crises. The proposed computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize geospatial data fusion, train deep learning models for anomaly detection, and simulate disaster propagation across urban landscapes. Key methods include (1) developing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze high-resolution aerial imagery for critical infrastructure monitoring, (2) implementing natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract location-specific threat indicators from unstructured text data, and (3) creating agent-based models to simulate crowd dynamics during emergency scenarios. Spatial programming libraries (e.g., GDAL, PostGIS) will be integrated with PyTorch and TensorFlow environments to enable GPU-accelerated geocomputation. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing petabyte-scale datasets, reducing model training times from weeks to days, and executing complex spatial-temporal analyses at meter-level precision across entire metropolitan regions. Expected outcomes include an open-source geospatial analytics toolkit capable of processing real-time data feeds with 95% latency reduction compared to existing systems, validated through case studies on flood risk prediction and critical infrastructure protection. This research will advance computational geospatial intelligence methodologies while directly supporting homeland security priorities in proactive risk mitigation and cross-agency coordination during multi-threat incidents. The resulting frameworks and benchmarks will be disseminated to government partners and the broader geospatial research community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to analyze security and intelligence problems using a geographic perspective by relating human actions to cultural, political, economic, social, and physical landscapes. Includes instruction in aerial photography analysis, cartography, geographic information systems (GIS), physical geography, remote sensing, spatial programming, and quantitative methods in geographic research.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time financial data reconciliation for small and midsize enterprises (SMEs) by developing an AI-driven framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. Current manual and semi-automated bookkeeping systems struggle with latency and accuracy when processing high-volume transactional data from heterogeneous sources (e.g., IoT-enabled POS systems, blockchain-based supply chain ledgers, and multi-platform e-commerce APIs). The research problem centers on creating a computational model capable of autonomously resolving temporal, semantic, and structural discrepancies in accounting data streams at scale, while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards. The proposed methodology combines graph neural networks (GNNs) to model transactional relationships across temporal dimensions with quantum-inspired optimization algorithms to reconcile conflicting entries in near real time. HPC resources will be critical for training domain-specific language models on proprietary accounting lexicons and simulating multi-agent systems that mimic cross-platform transaction flows. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of processing 10^6 transactions/hour with <0.1% reconciliation error rates, benchmarked against IFRS and GAAP compliance thresholds. The research will additionally yield novel metrics for quantifying temporal data coherence in accounting contexts and an open-source library for adaptive schema mapping between disparate financial reporting formats. By pushing the boundaries of computational bookkeeping infrastructure, this work aims to establish new paradigms for autonomous financial governance in distributed business ecosystems while reducing SME operational risks associated with manual accounting practices. The HPC-enabled scale of analysis will provide unprecedented insights into emergent financial data patterns within hybrid physical-digital transaction networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical administrative support to professional accountants and other financial management personnel. Includes instruction in posting transactions to accounts, record-keeping systems, accounting software operation, and general accounting principles and practices.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing next-generation energy storage systems through advanced computational modeling of multiphysics phenomena in solid-state battery interfaces. Despite the promise of solid-state batteries for high energy density and safety, interfacial instability between electrodes and solid electrolytes remains a key barrier to scalability and longevity. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve dynamic electrochemical and mechanical interactions at atomistic and mesoscopic scales, while existing simulations often oversimplify coupled thermal, stress, and ion transport effects. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), phase-field modeling, and continuum-scale finite element analysis (FEA). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform massively parallel DFT calculations of interfacial defect dynamics, coupled with GPU-accelerated phase-field simulations of dendrite growth mechanisms across experimentally relevant timescales. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-derived datasets to predict degradation pathways, enabling efficient parameter space exploration for novel electrolyte materials. The computational workflow will leverage distributed-memory architectures for cross-scale data integration and real-time visualization of evolving interface morphologies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models of interfacial failure modes, optimized material pairing recommendations, and open-source simulation tools for the energy storage community. By elucidating design rules for stable interfaces, this work aims to accelerate the development of durable solid-state batteries, directly supporting global efforts to transition toward renewable energy infrastructure. The requested resources will enable the execution of >10^6 core-hours of simulations across three key validation studies, each requiring petascale data handling capabilities to resolve multi-physics interactions at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance French language teacher training by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multilingual classroom interaction datasets and model language acquisition processes. Despite advances in pedagogical methods, teacher education programs often lack data-driven tools to systematically evaluate how instructional strategies affect learners’ proficiency in real-world settings. Current approaches rely on manual assessment or small-sample studies, limiting generalizability. This research addresses this gap by developing computational models to quantify relationships between teaching practices, learner engagement, and linguistic outcomes across diverse educational contexts. The project will process multimodal data—including transcribed classroom dialogues, written assignments, and longitudinal proficiency assessments—from French learners at secondary and postsecondary levels. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines, optimized for HPC environments, will extract syntactic, semantic, and discourse features to train neural networks that predict pedagogical effectiveness. Agent-based simulations will model classroom dynamics under varying instructional conditions, enabling virtual experimentation with teaching strategies. Resource requests include GPU nodes for deep learning workflows and parallelized processing of terabyte-scale linguistic corpora. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive frameworks identifying high-impact teaching behaviors, (2) interactive visualization tools for teacher trainees to explore scenario-based learning outcomes, and (3) open-access benchmarks for French language education research. By bridging computational linguistics with teacher training, this work aims to establish reproducible methods for optimizing curriculum design and clinical practice in language education programs, while advancing HPC applications in the humanities. Results will directly inform competency frameworks for accreditation bodies and provide empirical foundations for evidence-based teaching standards in francophone contexts worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach French language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing personalized language instruction for adult learners of English or French as a second language. A critical challenge in language education lies in efficiently analyzing large-scale, multimodal learner datasets—including speech recordings, writing samples, and interaction logs—to identify patterns in individual error trajectories, proficiency progression, and pedagogical intervention efficacy. Traditional methods struggle to process such heterogeneous data at scale, limiting the ability to model complex, dynamic interactions between instructional strategies and learner outcomes. This project proposes a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and agent-based modeling to simulate language acquisition processes and test pedagogical hypotheses. Neural networks will be trained on annotated learner corpora to classify error types and predict developmental stages, while reinforcement learning frameworks will model adaptive tutor-learner interactions. Large-scale simulations will evaluate how variations in instructional sequencing, feedback timing, and multimodal input (e.g., visual vs. auditory cues) affect long-term retention. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of speech and text data, parallelizing hyperparameter optimization for deep learning models, and running thousands of simulated teaching scenarios with diverse learner profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based frameworks for dynamically tailoring instruction to individual cognitive and linguistic needs, (2) open-source tools for automated error detection and progress monitoring, and (3) scalable models of second language acquisition that account for cross-linguistic transfer and socio-pragmatic competence. By bridging computational linguistics with language pedagogy, this work aims to empower educators with data-driven strategies to accelerate proficiency gains while reducing learner attrition in multilingual classrooms.
cip_title: Teaching English or French as a Second or Foreign Language, Other
cip_definition: Any program in teaching English or French as a second or foreign language, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social stratification and mobility in urban populations using large-scale demographic microdata and advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on understanding how macro-level social inequalities emerge from micro-level interactions, particularly in contexts of rapid demographic change and institutional policy shifts. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, multiscale interdependencies between individual behaviors (e.g., migration, education, employment) and structural factors (e.g., housing policies, labor market segmentation). To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) that simulate population-scale decision-making processes under varying social and economic constraints. These models will integrate longitudinal census data, geospatial information systems (GIS) layers, and social survey datasets to parameterize heterogeneous agent behaviors across diverse socioeconomic groups. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to run thousands of parallelized simulations exploring alternative policy scenarios and demographic trajectories, enabling robust sensitivity analyses and the identification of critical leverage points in social systems. The computational workflow will employ distributed memory architectures for scaling agent populations to metropolitan-region levels (10^6–10^7 agents) while maintaining fine-grained interaction rules. Expected outcomes include (1) new insights into how institutional discrimination and network homophily jointly reproduce inequality across generations, (2) empirically grounded projections of social mobility trends under policy interventions, and (3) open-source tools for scalable ABM development in sociological research. By bridging computational social science with classical stratification theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for reducing systemic inequities while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in population-focused sociological inquiry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human social institutions and social relationships. Includes instruction in social theory, sociological research methods, social organization and structure, social stratification and hierarchies, dynamics of social change, family structures, social deviance and control, and applications to the study of specific social groups, social institutions, and social problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to predict and mitigate workplace hazards in high-risk industrial environments, with a focus on optimizing occupational safety protocols. Current methods for assessing exposure to airborne contaminants, ergonomic risks, and equipment-related dangers often rely on reactive, post-incident analyses or simplified static models, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between workers, machinery, and environmental factors. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), agent-based modeling, and machine learning to simulate complex workplace scenarios in real time. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale sensor datasets, model particulate dispersion in three-dimensional spaces, and simulate worker movements under varying conditions. The CFD component will predict the spread of hazardous substances using multiphase flow simulations, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize evacuation routes and equipment placement. Agent-based models will evaluate how procedural changes affect collective risk profiles. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to proactively identify hazard hotspots, validate the efficacy of ventilation systems, and inform adaptive safety training protocols. By enabling granular, scenario-specific risk assessments, this work aims to reduce occupational injuries and long-term health impacts in manufacturing, construction, and chemical handling sectors. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source resources to support safety compliance benchmarking and foster collaboration between engineering technologists and industrial hygienists. This project directly aligns with the program’s mission to bridge technical skills with health protection, offering a scalable methodology to advance evidence-based safety engineering practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining job-related health and safety standards. Includes instruction in safety engineering principles, inspection and monitoring procedures, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, applications to specific work environments, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time business data processing in distributed, heterogeneous computing environments, with a focus on enhancing the scalability and security of dynamic resource allocation algorithms. As enterprises increasingly rely on cloud-edge hybrid architectures for mission-critical operations, traditional static resource management frameworks struggle to balance latency, cost, and data integrity requirements across fluctuating workloads. The research proposes developing adaptive quantum-inspired optimization models that leverage tensor network representations to simulate multi-objective resource allocation scenarios. Using historical infrastructure logs from financial transaction systems and IoT-enabled supply chain networks, we will train hybrid classical-quantum neural networks to predict optimal compute-storage distributions under constraints including regulatory compliance thresholds and cyberattack resilience parameters. The computational workload involves simulating 10,000+ node network topologies through discrete-event simulations accelerated via GPU-parallelized Monte Carlo methods, requiring access to high-performance computing clusters with multi-terabyte memory nodes and CUDA-enabled accelerators. Expected outcomes include 1) a benchmark comparison of quantum-enhanced optimization against classical metaheuristics in reducing service-level agreement violations, 2) an open-source framework for privacy-preserving resource negotiation in multi-tenant business ecosystems, and 3) quantitative insights into the energy efficiency trade-offs of proactive versus reactive scaling strategies. By bridging quantum computing principles with operational decision-making in distributed information systems, this work aims to establish foundational methodologies for next-generation business infrastructure that autonomously adapts to both market demands and emerging computational paradigms. The results will directly inform the design of adaptive middleware for blockchain-orchestrated Industry 4.0 platforms while advancing theoretical understanding of complex resource allocation in non-stationary business environments.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of inter-group conflict escalation and de-escalation in fragile sociopolitical ecosystems, integrating computational social science, network theory, and behavioral psychology. The research addresses a critical gap in peace studies: predicting tipping points in communal conflicts where traditional analytical methods fail to account for nonlinear interactions between socio-economic stressors, identity-based polarization, and third-party intervention efficacy. By developing an agent-based model (ABM) that simulates multi-scale interactions among individuals, community leaders, and external mediators, the project aims to identify latent variables influencing conflict trajectories. The computational framework will incorporate real-world datasets on historical conflicts (e.g., ACLED, UCDP) to parameterize agents’ decision-making heuristics, trust erosion mechanisms, and information diffusion patterns. HPC resources are essential to run ensemble simulations across diverse geopolitical contexts, varying parameters such as resource scarcity, external aid timing, and social media disinformation rates. Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to detect early-stage signatures of destabilization and test the resilience of proposed mediation strategies under stochastic shocks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for conflict analysts to simulate localized interventions and a novel metric for quantifying "escalation risk" in real-time monitoring systems. By bridging granular behavioral data with macro-level conflict theory, this work advances computational peacebuilding methodologies, offering policymakers data-driven insights into preemptive de-escalation. The scalability of the ABM, requiring parallel processing of up to 10^6 agent interactions across 500+ concurrent scenarios, necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure to achieve the resolution and statistical power required for actionable conclusions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of international and inter-group conflicts. Includes instruction in peace research methods and related social scientific and psychological knowledge bases.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing crop yield stability under increasing climate variability and resource constraints, with a focus on staple grain and vegetable systems. Current agronomic models often lack the resolution to account for dynamic interactions between genotype-specific traits, spatially heterogeneous soil conditions, and microclimate patterns at farm-relevant scales. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution computational framework integrating 3D root architecture modeling, hyperspectral canopy stress detection, and probabilistic weather anomaly projections. The core methodology involves parallelized execution of modified DSSAT crop models coupled with machine learning-based pest/disease risk classifiers trained on historical field trial data from regional agricultural stations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets from UAV-based field sensors, satellite phenology time series, and soil microbiome sequencing, enabling daily simulations across 10,000+ parameter combinations at 1m² resolution. Expected outcomes include identification of stress-resilient cultivar-soil-climate configurations and dynamic nutrient management schedules that reduce fertilizer inputs by 15-20% while maintaining yield targets. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental plots at three USDA-ARS research farms, with model outputs formatted for integration into existing precision agriculture platforms. By enabling subfield-scale optimization of planting strategies and input allocation, this work directly supports climate adaptation priorities in domestic crop production systems while advancing computational methods for spatial agronomy. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and large-memory instances for genomic-environmental association analyses.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cultivate grain, fiber, forage, oilseed, fruits and nuts, vegetables, and other domesticated plant products. Includes instruction in basic principles of plant science, health, and nutrition as applied to particular species and breeds; soil preparation and irrigation; pest management; planting and harvesting operations; product marketing; and applicable issues of safety, regulation, logistics, and supply.

abstract: Commercial fishing operations face complex challenges in balancing economic viability with sustainable resource management, particularly under dynamic environmental conditions and regulatory constraints. This project seeks to address critical gaps in real-time decision-making and operational efficiency by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model and predict optimal fishing strategies. The research problem centers on the inability of current empirical methods to integrate multi-scale data—such as vessel telemetry, catch records, oceanographic conditions, and regulatory boundaries—into actionable insights. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and hydrodynamic simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large spatiotemporal datasets from satellite remote sensing, in-situ sensors, and historical fisheries records, which collectively exceed 50 TB in scale. Agent-based models will simulate fleet behavior under varying environmental and policy scenarios, while ML algorithms will identify patterns in species distribution and gear performance. Concurrently, hydrodynamic models will resolve localized currents and temperature gradients at sub-kilometer resolutions to assess their impact on catch efficiency and fuel consumption. The integration of these components will enable probabilistic forecasts of high-yield fishing zones, bycatch risks, and compliance outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for commercial fishers to optimize routing and gear deployment, reducing fuel use by an estimated 15–20% and minimizing regulatory violations. Additionally, the models will provide policymakers with predictive metrics to evaluate spatial management strategies under climate change scenarios. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges technological innovation with practical applications in fisheries management, promoting both economic resilience and ecological stewardship in a rapidly evolving industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as commercial fishermen, fishing operations supervisors or in related fishing industry operations. Includes instruction in fishing vessel operation; fishing equipment operation and maintenance; equipment repair; catch identification, sorting, and storage; safety procedures; record keeping; and applicable legal regulations.

abstract: The controlled use of explosives in construction and demolition requires precise optimization of blast parameters to balance efficiency, safety, and environmental impact. Current empirical methods for designing blast patterns and charge distributions often lead to suboptimal outcomes, including excessive ground vibrations, irregular fragmentation, and unintended structural damage. This project proposes a computational framework to model explosive-induced rock fragmentation and stress propagation at unprecedented resolution, enabling data-driven optimization of blasting operations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop multi-physics simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for fracture mechanics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for detonation gas expansion, and discrete element methods (DEM) for granular flow of fragmented materials. These simulations will account for heterogeneous geological conditions, varying explosive properties, and dynamic interactions between shockwaves and subsurface structures. A machine learning pipeline will then analyze simulation outputs to identify correlations between blast parameters (e.g., hole spacing, burden, charge density) and outcomes such as fragmentation size distribution, vibration attenuation, and energy efficiency. Validation will occur through comparison with field data from active blasting sites, including LiDAR-scanned post-blast topography and seismic monitoring records. The computational intensity of modeling three-dimensional blast effects at engineering-relevant scales necessitates HPC capabilities, particularly for parallelized solvers handling billions of mesh elements and iterative parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive models for blast design under diverse geological constraints, reduced trial-and-error testing in hazardous environments, and quantitative guidelines to minimize collateral damage while maximizing material yield. This work will advance the scientific foundation of blasting engineering, with applications in infrastructure development, mining, and environmental remediation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in using a variety of explosive materials to aid in the construction process. Includes instruction in safety procedures for storing, handling, placement, charge power determination, drilling, pounding, building demolition, preparing rocky surfaces for building foundations and demolition of explosives.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in optimizing high-performance internal combustion engines by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex engine dynamics and component interactions. Traditional trial-and-error methods for engine tuning—particularly for custom powertrains, forced induction systems, and hybrid fuel configurations—are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to resolve multivariable trade-offs between power output, emissions, thermal management, and mechanical reliability. The research will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to analyze turbulent combustion processes, exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) efficiency, and heat dissipation in modified engine blocks. Parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) will evaluate stress distributions in custom components, such as turbocharger impellers and reinforced crankshafts, under extreme operating conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to iteratively optimize fuel injection timing, valve lift profiles, and ignition parameters based on multi-physics simulation outputs. By coupling these computational approaches, the project aims to develop predictive models that reduce prototyping iterations and enable data-driven design of high-efficiency engines. Anticipated outcomes include validated simulation workflows for performance tuning, open-source benchmarks for aftermarket component compatibility, and educational modules to train technicians in computational diagnostics. Access to HPC resources is critical to resolving the scale of meshing required for transient combustion simulations and the computational expense of multi-objective optimization. This work will advance both academic and industry practices by bridging empirical mechanical expertise with scalable computational methods, ultimately supporting sustainable innovation in high-performance automotive systems.
cip_title: High Performance and Custom Engine Technician/ Mechanic
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to increase the power of diesel and automotive engines; enhance the performance of automobiles; and repair, service, and maintain high performance vehicles. Includes instruction in adding performance accessories; modifying powertrains; tuning custom engines, suspension, and exhaust systems; and using dynamometers and other diagnostic equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze large-scale, multimodal second language acquisition (SLA) datasets, with the goal of identifying patterns in learner errors and adaptive instructional strategies for diverse ESL populations. A critical challenge in TESL research is the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to model the interplay between linguistic complexity, pedagogical interventions, and individual learner variability. Existing approaches often rely on small-sample studies or manual error coding, limiting generalizability and real-time applicability in classroom settings. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process spoken and written learner corpora—including audio recordings, written essays, and interactive dialogue logs from 10,000+ ESL learners across proficiency levels. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be optimized to automate error detection (e.g., syntactic inaccuracies, lexical misuse) and correlate these with instructional metadata (task design, feedback type, L1 background). Deep learning models will simulate longitudinal language development trajectories under varying pedagogical conditions, requiring distributed training across GPU nodes to handle the high dimensionality of multilingual, code-switched input. Computational experiments will benchmark the efficacy of adaptive error correction strategies and task sequencing algorithms derived from these analyses. Outcomes will include open-source tools for ESL instructors to generate proficiency-specific lesson materials, predictive diagnostics for common L1 transfer errors, and empirically grounded frameworks for personalizing grammar instruction in mixed-ability classrooms. By enabling large-scale modeling of SLA processes that account for both cognitive and sociolinguistic factors, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical linguistics, computational pedagogy, and classroom practice, while advancing infrastructure for data-intensive research in language teacher education.
cip_title: Teaching English as a Second or Foreign Language/ ESL Language Instructor
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching English to students who are not proficient in English or who do not speak, read or write English, and that may prepare individuals to function as teachers and administrators in such programs.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an AI-driven predictive model for optimizing administrative workflows in multi-specialty medical office environments. The central problem addressed is the inefficiency of current task prioritization and resource allocation systems in clinical administrative settings, which often lead to delays in patient processing, staff burnout, and financial losses due to suboptimal scheduling. Current approaches rely on static protocols that fail to adapt to dynamic variables such as fluctuating patient volumes, staff availability, and emergent priority cases. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating real-time data streams (e.g., electronic health records, appointment systems, and staff performance metrics) with machine learning algorithms to predict and dynamically adjust workflow patterns.
