Our research focuses on developing a multi-agent simulation framework that captures these interdependencies at a granular scale, incorporating real-time traffic data, demographic projections, environmental impact assessments, and policy scenarios. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, machine learning for pattern recognition in transportation networks, and geospatial analytics using high-resolution GIS datasets. These methods require parallel processing capabilities to simulate interactions across millions of agents (e.g., commuters, policymakers, businesses) and optimize infrastructure investments under uncertainty. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to assess resilience against extreme weather events, equity implications of transit expansions, and emissions trade-offs between transportation modes. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible modeling toolkit for urban planners, validated against case studies in three metropolitan regions, to evaluate policies such as congestion pricing, electric vehicle adoption incentives, and green infrastructure integration. By quantifying the cascading effects of transportation decisions on housing affordability, air quality, and economic productivity, this project aims to advance evidence-based infrastructure planning and support equitable climate adaptation strategies. The computational outputs will directly inform state and municipal policy briefs, prioritizing scalable solutions for reducing carbon footprints while maintaining mobility access for underserved communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the economic, social, spatial, and environmental aspects of transportation and infrastructure planning. Includes instruction in economics, environmental analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, risk analysis, transportation economics, transportation evaluation, transportation planning, transportation policy, and urban transportation planning.

abstract: Climate change and increasing anthropogenic pressures are driving unprecedented shifts in ecosystem dynamics, yet predicting the resilience of natural systems under these cumulative stressors remains a critical challenge in conservation science. This project seeks to develop a scalable, high-resolution modeling framework to assess the vulnerability of interconnected ecological networks—including boreal forests, wetland complexes, and watersheds—across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Current limitations in computational capacity restrict existing models to coarse resolutions or isolated system components, hindering our ability to capture cross-system feedbacks, dispersal dynamics, and threshold behaviors. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled modeling approach integrating agent-based species distribution models, hydrologic simulations, and climate anomaly projections at 1 km² resolution across a 50-year horizon. The workflow will utilize parallelized processing for Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses across 10⁴ parameter combinations, Bayesian network calibration against continental-scale biodiversity databases, and GPU-accelerated machine learning to identify nonlinear tipping points in ecosystem services. Expected outcomes include the first pan-regional assessment of cross-biome resilience synergies in North America’s northern latitudes, with specific deliverables identifying priority conservation corridors under multiple climate scenarios (RCP 4.5 and 8.5). The computational architecture developed will be released as open-source tools to enable community-driven scenario testing, reducing redundancy in conservation resource allocation. By quantifying how landscape-scale connectivity mediates climate adaptation capacity, this work directly addresses the urgent need for predictive frameworks in adaptive management policy, while advancing computational ecology methods for coupled human-natural systems. Successful implementation requires sustained access to HPC resources capable of handling petascale environmental datasets and concurrent multiphysics simulations.
cip_title: Natural Resources Conservation and Research, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources conservation and research, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing multi-venue sports facility operations through advanced computational modeling, a challenge exacerbated by the dynamic interplay of financial constraints, real-time resource allocation, and evolving safety standards. Traditional management approaches often rely on siloed data and heuristic decision-making, which struggle to balance competing objectives such as energy efficiency, crowd safety, and revenue generation during concurrent events. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates agent-based crowd simulations, facility-specific IoT sensor data, and multi-objective optimization algorithms. The computational model will simulate scenarios ranging from routine operations to high-density events, incorporating variables such as HVAC load balancing, emergency egress patterns, and concession demand forecasting. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical and real-time datasets to predict maintenance needs and staffing requirements, while parallelized optimization routines will dynamically adjust resource allocation across facilities. The expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of reducing operational costs by 15-20%, improving emergency response planning through probabilistic risk mapping, and enhancing patron experience metrics via congestion-aware spatial management. This work bridges gaps between sports management theory and computational systems engineering, offering a novel methodology for scalable, data-driven facility governance. By leveraging HPC resources, the project will demonstrate how emerging computational techniques can transform traditionally qualitative domains, setting a precedent for resource allocation models applicable to large-scale athletic complexes, community recreation centers, and adaptive reuse venues. The resulting open-source framework will provide actionable insights for administrators while contributing interdisciplinary methodologies to the evolving field of computational sport management.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business, coaching and physical education principles to the organization, administration and management of athletic programs and teams, fitness/rehabilitation facilities and health clubs, sport recreation services, and related services. Includes instruction in program planning and development; business and financial management principles; sales, marketing and recruitment; event promotion, scheduling and management; facilities management; public relations; legal aspects of sports; and applicable health and safety standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic treatment personalization for complex, multi-system disorders by integrating high-dimensional clinical, genomic, and metabolomic data. Current approaches to precision medicine often rely on static models that fail to account for temporal variations in patient physiology, heterogeneous data streams, and the nonlinear interactions between biomarkers. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning architecture leveraging time-series analysis, graph neural networks (GNNs), and federated learning to model patient trajectories and predict individualized therapeutic adjustments in real time. The research will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from 15,000 patients with autoimmune-inflammatory conditions, paired with longitudinal multi-omics datasets, to train models that identify critical inflection points in disease progression and recommend intervention strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing petabytes of raw EHR data, training GNNs on dynamically evolving patient graphs, and simulating virtual cohorts to validate model robustness under diverse clinical scenarios. Key computational challenges include managing sparse, irregularly sampled data streams, ensuring privacy-preserving federated learning across institutional partners, and scaling ensemble methods to accommodate thousands of concurrent simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive treatment optimization, validated against retrospective clinical outcomes, and a novel biomarker interaction network revealing previously unrecognized therapeutic targets. This work bridges translational gaps by enabling clinicians to operationalize complex, data-driven insights at the point of care, directly supporting the program’s focus on integrating computational innovation into clinical practice. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parallelized simulations, and secure data federation infrastructure, advancing both methodological rigor and practical applicability in next-generation clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares medical and health clinicians to combine knowledge from scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge, improve medical education, and bridge laboratory and clinical science into clinical practice. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, medical education and scientific writing.

abstract: This project addresses the critical need for advanced computational resources in art historical research and conservation, particularly in analyzing large-scale, high-resolution imaging datasets and simulating material degradation processes. Traditional methods of studying artistic techniques and conserving cultural heritage artifacts often face limitations in scalability, precision, and interdisciplinary integration. The research focuses on two interconnected objectives: first, the automated identification of underdrawings and material alterations in paintings using machine learning (ML) models trained on multispectral and hyperspectral imaging data; second, the simulation of environmental and temporal impacts on pigments and substrates through physics-based modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of high-fidelity imaging data from museum collections, train deep neural networks for pattern recognition, and run iterative simulations of degradation mechanics across diverse climatic scenarios. By leveraging GPU-accelerated processing and distributed computing frameworks, this project aims to map stylistic continuities in underdrawings across 15th-century European panel paintings—a task currently hindered by data fragmentation and manual analysis—and predict microfracture propagation in aging oil paintings. Outcomes will include open-access tools for computational connoisseurship, a predictive database for preventive conservation, and novel visualizations of artistic process. This work bridges computational science and art historical inquiry, offering scalable methodologies to analyze cultural materials at unprecedented resolution while advancing interdisciplinary paradigms in heritage science. The requested resources will directly support the development of reproducible workflows, enabling collaborative research across institutions and fostering new standards for data-driven scholarship in the visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical development of art as social and intellectual phenomenon, the analysis of works of art, and art conservation. Includes instruction in the theory of art, art history research methods, connoisseurship, the preservation and conservation of works of art, and the study of specific periods, cultures, styles, and themes.

abstract: Veterinary dermatology faces significant challenges in diagnosing and treating complex skin diseases in animals, which often involve multifactorial etiologies such as genetic predispositions, environmental triggers, and dysbiosis of the skin microbiome. Current diagnostic approaches and therapeutic strategies frequently yield suboptimal outcomes due to incomplete understanding of disease mechanisms and interindividual variability in treatment responses. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and metagenomic datasets from companion animals with chronic dermatologic conditions, including atopic dermatitis, autoimmune disorders, and recurrent pyoderma. Computational workflows will integrate whole-genome sequencing, host immune gene expression profiling, and longitudinal microbiome data to identify biomarkers of disease susceptibility, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Machine learning models will be developed to predict treatment outcomes based on multi-omics signatures and clinical metadata, while molecular dynamics simulations will characterize interactions between cutaneous microbiota-derived metabolites and host immune receptors. These analyses require substantial parallel processing capabilities for alignment of sequencing data, training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets, and simulation of molecular interactions at scale. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel therapeutic targets, stratification of patient subgroups for personalized treatment regimens, and optimization of probiotic interventions to restore skin barrier function. By elucidating the complex interplay between host genetics, microbial communities, and environmental factors in veterinary dermatologic diseases, this research will directly inform clinical decision-making and advance precision medicine approaches in veterinary care. The computational infrastructure will enable processing of petabyte-scale datasets, reduce time-to-insight for translational applications, and support open-access repositories for collaborative research in veterinary dermatology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between language policy implementation and real-time classroom discourse in multilingual educational contexts, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multimodal interaction data. While language-in-education policies increasingly emphasize inclusive pedagogies, their on-the-ground enactment remains understudied, particularly in classrooms where teachers and students navigate multiple languages. The research addresses this gap by examining how code-switching (alternating between languages) mediates equity in learning opportunities, focusing on under-resourced regions with linguistically diverse populations. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to process 10,000+ hours of classroom audio recordings, video transcripts, and written materials across three typologically distinct language pairs. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to identify code-switching patterns, pedagogical moves, and student participation metrics, while graph neural networks will map interactional networks to quantify access to learning moments. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate policy outcomes under varying resource constraints. HPC resources are critical for parallel processing of raw audio data, fine-tuning large language models on low-resource languages, and running iterative simulations. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for analyzing policy implementation at the micro-interactional level, 2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive teacher training modules, and 3) open-source tools for automating equity-focused discourse analysis in multilingual classrooms. By bridging computational linguistics and language policy research, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in applied linguistics while addressing pressing questions about educational justice in linguistically complex settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language-related concerns in the everyday world, including language education, acquisition of first and additional languages, discourse analysis, language assessment, literacy, and language policy and planning. Includes instruction in linguistic theory; language teaching and learning; discourse analysis; language and cognition; and language, culture, and identity.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize next-generation military radar systems operating in contested electromagnetic environments. The increasing density of adversarial electronic warfare (EW) threats and spectrum congestion has created critical challenges for legacy radar architectures, which struggle to maintain detection fidelity while simultaneously mitigating interference and avoiding spectral fratricide. Traditional analytical methods fail to account for the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between modern multifunction phased array radars, agile threat waveforms, and heterogeneous clutter environments. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-domain radar-EW interactions at unprecedented scale and resolution. The computational approach integrates finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) electromagnetic simulations with reinforcement learning algorithms to develop adaptive radar waveform and beamforming strategies. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated propagation modeling for complex terrain and urban environments, coupled with distributed machine learning workflows to train cognitive radar controllers under thousands of concurrent threat scenarios. The simulation environment will incorporate real-world data from field experiments to validate digital twins of operational military systems. Successful implementation will enable predictive analysis of emerging radar technologies, including meta-material apertures and quantum-enhanced detection schemes, while maintaining compliance with strict spectral coexistence requirements. Expected outcomes include quantifiable performance improvements in target detection range (+15-20%), false alarm reduction (>30%), and adaptive response times (<100μs) for tactical radar systems. This research directly supports modernization priorities for resilient sensor networks in joint all-domain operations, bridging critical gaps between electromagnetic theory, computational physics, and deployable military technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of air, sea and ground-based radar systems. Includes instruction in electronic principles and digital techniques, transistors and solid-state component theory, radar systems; maintenance technology, data processing systems, wiring and circuit schematics, maintenance management, safety procedures, and applications to specific systems and services.

abstract: The integration of precision medicine into oncology pharmacy remains limited by the complexity of predicting patient-specific responses to anticancer therapies, particularly in the context of polypharmacy and dynamic tumor evolution. Current approaches to optimizing drug selection, dosing, and combination strategies rely heavily on population-level evidence, which often fails to account for genomic heterogeneity, drug-drug interactions, and microenvironmental influences on pharmacokinetics. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multivariate predictors of therapeutic efficacy and toxicity in oncology patients. The research will integrate multi-omics data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) from institutional cohorts with drug pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) parameters, tumor microenvironment simulations, and real-world medication adherence patterns. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to predict patient-specific outcomes under varying treatment regimens, while molecular dynamics simulations will characterize drug-target binding affinities in the context of somatic mutations. The computational workflow will require parallelized processing of large-scale genomic datasets (≥10,000 patients) and iterative optimization of PK-PD models across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 variables. By establishing a scalable platform for simulating therapeutic scenarios, this work aims to identify candidate drug combinations with minimized off-target effects, propose adaptive dosing strategies for evolving tumors, and stratify patients based on resistance mechanisms. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for therapy personalization, validated against retrospective clinical data, and a predictive database linking somatic alterations to drug transport/metabolism pathways. This resource will address critical gaps in clinical decision support for oncology pharmacists, enabling data-driven management of polypharmacy, drug interactions, and interpatient variability in treatment response. Successful implementation will directly inform prospective trials on computational-guided therapy selection in hematologic and solid malignancies.
cip_definition: Research focused on oncology pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and optimize multimodal corporate communication strategies in multilingual, multicultural organizational environments. Traditional approaches to evaluating communication effectiveness—such as manual sentiment analysis or small-scale readability metrics—fail to capture the dynamic interplay of linguistic, visual, and contextual factors in global business interactions. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to model how textual, auditory, and visual elements in corporate communications (e.g., internal memos, stakeholder reports, crisis responses) interact across languages and cultural contexts to influence organizational outcomes. Using transformer-based language models, computer vision algorithms, and agent-based simulations, the project will process terabyte-scale datasets of corporate communications from multinational firms, including email archives, video presentations, and cross-platform social media engagement metrics. Computational workflows will integrate multilingual sentiment analysis, visual rhetoric mapping, and network-based diffusion models to identify patterns in communication efficacy, with a focus on scenarios involving information asymmetry or cross-cultural misinterpretation. HPC resources are critical for training ensemble models that simultaneously process heterogeneous data types while maintaining low-latency performance for real-time simulation of communication cascades in virtual organizational environments. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of high-impact communication strategies for crisis management, a predictive tool for assessing cross-cultural message alignment, and an open-source library for multimodal communication analytics. This work bridges computational linguistics, behavioral economics, and organizational psychology, offering actionable insights for designing adaptive communication systems in globally distributed enterprises.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: Periodontal disease progression and treatment outcomes are influenced by complex biomechanical interactions between microbial biofilms, host immune responses, and occlusal forces. However, current clinical models inadequately capture the multiscale dynamics of these interactions, particularly regarding strain propagation through heterogeneous periodontal tissues during functional loading. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution computational model integrating microbiological, immunological, and biomechanical data to simulate periodontal tissue responses under varying pathological and therapeutic conditions. Using patient-derived 3D cone-beam CT reconstructions and microbiomic profiles, we will implement finite element analysis coupled with agent-based modeling to study how localized mechanical stresses interact with site-specific microbial communities to drive bone resorption patterns. The computational framework will employ GPU-accelerated solvers to handle nonlinear tissue properties and stochastic microbial growth dynamics across spatial scales spanning four orders of magnitude (µm to cm). A second phase will simulate therapeutic interventions, including occlusal adjustment effects on biofilm mechanical disruption and immune cell recruitment patterns predicted through lattice Boltzmann methods for fluid-structure interactions. Validation will utilize longitudinal clinical datasets from digital periodontal charting and biomarker analyses. This resource-intensive modeling requires high-performance computing capabilities for 1) parallel processing of multiphysics simulations, 2) machine learning-assisted parameter optimization across 10^6+ variable combinations, and 3) visualization of 4D tissue remodeling patterns. Successful implementation will yield the first integrated platform capable of predicting individual patients' risk trajectories based on unique biofilm-tissue-loading triads, potentially revolutionizing personalized occlusal therapy planning. Outcomes will be disseminated through open-source model components and clinical decision support modules compatible with dental CAD/CAM systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical dynamics of connective tissue remodeling in chronic tendinopathy using multiscale computational modeling, a niche area intersecting computational biology, biophysics, and clinical medicine. Chronic tendon disorders affect millions globally, yet the mechanisms driving pathological tissue adaptation—particularly the interplay between cellular mechanotransduction, extracellular matrix degradation, and aberrant load distribution—remain poorly quantified. Current clinical interventions lack personalization due to gaps in understanding how microscale tissue properties influence macroscale mechanical failure. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations of collagen fibril deformation, agent-based models of fibroblast activity, and finite element analysis of tendon macrostructure. These models will be parameterized using multi-omics datasets (proteomics, transcriptomics) from patient-derived tendon samples and validated against biomechanical testing data. The computational workflow requires parallelized execution of coupled simulations across spatial and temporal scales, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure to handle terabytes of spatially resolved mechanical and biological data. Expected outcomes include predictive maps linking localized cellular responses to tissue-scale mechanical vulnerabilities, identification of novel biomarkers for early pathology detection, and optimization of load-modulation strategies for rehabilitation. By elucidating mechanobiological drivers of tendinopathy, this work aims to advance precision rehabilitation frameworks while demonstrating the utility of HPC in bridging molecular-scale biology to organ-level clinical phenomena. The developed models will be disseminated as open-source tools for the biomechanics community, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in understudied musculoskeletal pathologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale textual corpora in English literature, addressing gaps in understanding how genre conventions evolve across historical periods and cultural contexts. Traditional literary scholarship often relies on close reading of select texts, limiting the scope of analysis to small datasets and subjective interpretations. By contrast, this research employs computational methods to systematically examine thousands of literary works spanning the 16th to 21st centuries, with a focus on detecting patterns in narrative structure, stylistic features, and thematic content. The primary research problem centers on identifying quantifiable markers of genre transformation—such as shifts in diction, metaphor density, or syntactic complexity—and mapping their correlation with sociocultural trends documented in secondary historical sources. Using natural language processing (NLP) tools, custom Python scripts will parse and annotate texts from curated digital archives (e.g., Project Gutenberg, EEBO, and HathiTrust), while machine learning models (BERT-based classifiers, clustering algorithms) will categorize emergent subgenres and trace intertextual influences. Computational demands include parallel processing for training models on terabyte-scale datasets, GPU-accelerated sentiment analysis, and storage for intermediate outputs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking stylistic features to genre classifications, visualizations of literary influence networks, and statistical frameworks for testing hypotheses about periodization in literary history. This work aims to advance digital humanities scholarship by demonstrating how computational scalability can enrich traditional qualitative methods, offering new methodologies for interdisciplinary studies of cultural change. Results will inform ongoing debates about canon formation, the relationship between aesthetic innovation and reader reception, and the operationalization of “genre” as an analytical category.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on literature from one or more genres, cultures or traditions. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and studies of various types of literary text.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of non-textual symbolic communication in decentralized digital communities, focusing on the emergence and evolution of visual-iconographic systems within niche online platforms. As digital spaces increasingly prioritize multimodal interaction, communities are developing complex visual languages—such as emoji sequences, custom avatars, and procedural generative art—that transcend conventional linguistic frameworks. These systems raise fundamental questions about collective meaning-making, cultural transmission, and identity formation in post-textual environments, yet remain understudied due to the technical challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous multimedia datasets. The research will employ computational visual semiotics, combining computer vision techniques for pattern recognition in image corpora with graph-based network analysis of usage contexts across temporal and platform boundaries. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing petabytes of user-generated content from federated platforms (including ActivityPub networks and blockchain-based communities), requiring GPU-accelerated feature extraction, transformer-based multimodal embedding, and dynamic network modeling at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) a computational framework for identifying emergent visual grammars across decentralized networks, 2) quantitative models of cultural innovation diffusion in iconographic systems, and 3) ethical guidelines for preserving ephemeral digital vernaculars. By bridging humanities-focused cultural analysis with scalable computational methods, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying twenty-first-century cultural production while addressing preservation challenges posed by proprietary platform dependencies and digital obsolescence. The resource request supports both the development of custom vision-language models tailored to grassroots digital aesthetics and the creation of an open repository for analyzing at-risk community-generated visual cultures.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any single instructional program in liberal arts and sciences, general studies and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Laboratory animal models are essential for understanding human disease mechanisms and developing therapeutic interventions, yet current approaches often struggle to account for interspecies biological variability, limiting translational accuracy. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to predict species-specific molecular and physiological responses to experimental conditions, thereby refining the selection and interpretation of animal models. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omics datasets (genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) from murine, porcine, and non-human primate models with human clinical data. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to identify conserved and divergent pathways across species, while agent-based modeling will simulate systemic responses to perturbations such as drug administration or pathogen exposure. A key focus will be optimizing in silico models of immune-mediated diseases, which exhibit high interspecies heterogeneity. Computational outputs will be validated against in vivo experimental data from our laboratory’s ongoing studies on autoimmune disorders and sepsis. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabytes of raw sequencing data, running parallelized simulations, and iterating complex neural networks. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to guide model organism selection for specific disease contexts, (2) open-access databases of cross-species pathway annotations, and (3) computational protocols to reduce redundant animal trials by prioritizing high-probability experimental conditions. This work directly supports the program’s mission to advance ethical, efficient laboratory animal medicine through innovation in comparative systems biology. By elucidating species-specific adaptations at unprecedented resolution, the project will enhance the translational relevance of animal studies while aligning with the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) in biomedical research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: Understanding the relationship between polymer chain dynamics and macroscopic material properties remains a central challenge in polymer physics. While empirical models exist for specific regimes, a unified framework connecting molecular-scale entanglements, chain mobility, and emergent viscoelastic behavior across melt, solution, and solid-state systems is lacking. This project aims to address this gap through large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of coarse-grained polymer systems under varied thermodynamic conditions. The research will implement a modified Kremer-Grest bead-spring model with tunable persistence lengths and interaction potentials to systematically investigate how chain stiffness, entanglement density, and solvent quality influence stress relaxation spectra and nonlinear rheological responses. Parallelized simulations leveraging GPU-accelerated codes will enable access to experimentally relevant timescales (1–10^6 τ) while maintaining molecular resolution across systems of 10^3–10^5 chains. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify collective variables governing glass transition dynamics in amorphous polymers, with particular attention to the role of local packing heterogeneities. The computational workflow integrates LAMMPS for MD, PLUMED for enhanced sampling, and PyTorch-based neural networks for feature extraction. Expected outcomes include (1) validated scaling relationships between entanglement length and nonlinear modulus in melts, (2) predictive models for solvent-mediated dynamic asymmetry in polymer solutions, and (3) quantitative maps linking processing-induced orientation in solids to anisotropic thermal transport. By bridging molecular-level mechanisms to continuum-level properties, this work will advance fundamental theories of polymer dynamics while providing open-source simulation tools for the community. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential for achieving sufficient sampling across parameter space and resolving multiscale phenomena critical to developing first-principles design rules for polymeric systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanical, optical, and transport properties of polymers with respect to the underlying physics and physical chemistry of polymers in melt, solution, and solid state

abstract: Cancer treatment remains challenged by the heterogeneity of tumors and the dynamic mechanisms underlying therapy resistance, which demand advanced computational models to decipher complex biological systems. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multiscale, data-driven models that integrate genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical data to predict tumor behavior and optimize therapeutic strategies. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating predictive algorithms to identify molecular vulnerabilities in treatment-resistant cancers, and (2) simulating tumor-immune microenvironment interactions to evaluate combination therapies. Using machine learning frameworks, including ensemble methods and graph neural networks, we will analyze multi-omics datasets from institutional cohorts and public repositories (e.g., TCGA, ICGC) to map clonal evolution patterns and microenvironmental adaptations. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate spatial tumor dynamics under varying therapeutic conditions, requiring parallelized computation for stochastic simulations across parameter spaces. HPC resources will enable the processing of high-dimensional data (>100,000 features per patient) and reduce runtime for iterative model training from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for therapy response in pancreatic and triple-negative breast cancers, as well as in silico optimization of immunotherapy-radiotherapy sequencing. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to facilitate reproducibility in oncology research. By bridging translational hypotheses with large-scale computational validation, this work aims to accelerate the translation of mechanistic insights into personalized treatment strategies, directly addressing the National Cancer Institute’s priority of integrating computational oncology into clinical decision-making. The requested resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in single-institution computational capacity, ensuring robust statistical power, and enabling real-time adaptive modeling for precision oncology applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of all types of cancer and other benign and malignant tumors; this includes deciding on and administering therapy for these malignancies, as well as consulting with surgeons and radiotherapists on other treatments for cancer.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate advanced computational models to enhance the pedagogical strategies used in chemistry teacher education, addressing the challenge of effectively teaching dynamic chemical processes and molecular-level interactions. Traditional teaching methods often struggle to convey the complexity of real-time chemical phenomena, such as reaction mechanisms, equilibrium dynamics, or spectroscopic behavior, which are critical for student conceptual understanding. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and visualize these processes at unprecedented scales and resolutions. The research will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, quantum mechanical calculations (via density functional theory), and machine learning (ML)-driven analysis to generate interactive, adaptable teaching modules. These modules will model chemical systems under diverse conditions, enabling educators to demonstrate how variables like temperature, concentration, or catalyst design influence outcomes. Additionally, ML algorithms will process anonymized student interaction data from virtual labs to identify common misconceptions and optimize feedback mechanisms. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the computational load of parallelized MD trajectories, ab initio calculations across large molecular datasets, and training predictive ML models on heterogeneous educational data. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of validated, curriculum-aligned simulations; (2) quantitative frameworks linking simulation fidelity to learning gains in pre-service teacher assessments; and (3) AI-driven tools that help educators customize content based on learner needs. By integrating computational chemistry directly into teacher training, this work aims to establish scalable, evidence-based practices that empower chemistry educators to foster deeper conceptual mastery and engagement in their classrooms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach chemistry programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and evaluate adaptive, data-driven tools for improving instructional strategies in secondary special education. Students with disabilities in secondary grades face unique challenges, including heterogeneous learning needs, social-emotional barriers, and transitions to postsecondary life. While individualized education plans (IEPs) are central to addressing these needs, educators often lack efficient, evidence-based methods to design personalized curricula or predict intervention outcomes. This research addresses these gaps by combining educational datasets (e.g., student performance metrics, behavioral logs, IEP texts) with computational modeling to optimize instructional decision-making. Machine learning models, including transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) and reinforcement learning agents, will be trained to analyze IEP requirements, recommend subject-specific instructional modifications, and simulate student responses to interventions. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale datasets (spanning thousands of anonymized student records), running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and fine-tuning generative AI models that assist teachers in creating accessible, standards-aligned lesson content. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework that identifies patterns in effective accommodations for diverse disabilities (e.g., autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia) and a predictive tool to assess the viability of transition-focused vocational training plans. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with special education pedagogy, this work aims to reduce educators’ administrative burdens while enhancing the scalability of personalized, secondary-level instruction. Results will be validated through partnerships with special education classrooms, ensuring alignment with real-world teaching constraints and student needs. The project bridges computational innovation and inclusive education, offering a template for data-informed teaching practices in high-need educational settings.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Secondary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the secondary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for secondary grades special education; content, methods, and modifications in specific subject areas; issues in vocational education; and promoting successful transitions to postsecondary settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance applied psychological research on optimizing community-based mental health interventions. A critical challenge in counseling and applied psychology is designing scalable, adaptive interventions that account for dynamic interactions between individual psychological factors (e.g., resilience, coping strategies) and environmental stressors (e.g., socioeconomic disparities, access to care). Traditional statistical methods often struggle to model these multilevel, time-varying relationships in large, real-world datasets. To address this, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) that simulate population-level mental health outcomes under varying intervention scenarios. These models will integrate empirical data from longitudinal community mental health surveys (N ≈ 50,000 participants) and regional socioeconomic indicators. Computational workflows will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to test how different counseling frameworks—such as tiered support systems or mobile health outreach—interact with demographic variables and resource constraints. Machine learning pipelines will further analyze simulated and empirical data to identify nonlinear predictors of intervention success. The scale of these analyses—involving billions of agent interactions and high-dimensional optimization of intervention parameters—necessitates HPC capabilities for memory-intensive simulations and distributed computing. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational toolkit for predicting intervention efficacy across diverse community contexts, (2) evidence-based guidelines for allocating mental health resources in underserved populations, and (3) open-source software to support applied psychologists in designing adaptive interventions. By bridging computational modeling and applied psychological theory, this work aims to enhance the precision and equity of community mental health programs while establishing a methodological framework for HPC-driven research in counseling and applied psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychological theories and methods to real-world settings and problems, such as business and industry, government, education, military, and community settings. Includes instruction in applications of psychology, industrial/organizational psychology, developmental psychology, social psychology, cognitive psychology, counseling, human factors, research methods and statistics, and program evaluation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the integration of computational modeling and multi-physical simulation tools to optimize energy-efficient building systems in architectural design. Current approaches to evaluating building performance—particularly in balancing structural stability, thermal efficiency, and mechanical system integration—rely on fragmented analyses that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between subsystems. This limitation hinders the development of holistic, sustainable designs, especially for complex urban structures with variable environmental loads. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework coupling finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and parametric energy modeling. The research will develop scalable algorithms to simulate interdependent systems—such as HVAC airflow, solar gain distribution, and load-bearing component stress—under real-world climatic and operational scenarios. Large-scale parametric studies will assess design variations across building geometries, material properties, and mechanical configurations, leveraging GPU-accelerated solvers and parallelized workflows to manage computational costs. Validation will utilize sensor data from existing structures to calibrate models. Anticipated outcomes include a modular simulation toolkit for architects and engineering teams, enabling rapid prototyping of designs that minimize energy use while meeting safety and comfort standards. The resource request supports GPU nodes for CFD-FEA coupling, high-memory nodes for large urban-scale models, and storage for terabyte-scale datasets. By bridging architectural design with systems engineering through HPC, this work aims to establish best practices for computationally driven sustainable building innovation, reducing reliance on physical prototyping and accelerating the adoption of high-performance building technologies in industry practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Occupational therapy interventions often rely on subjective clinical assessments and generalized protocols to address functional deficits, limiting personalized and dynamically adaptive strategies. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific motor learning patterns during therapeutic activities, with the goal of optimizing task difficulty and intervention timing for individuals with neuromotor impairments. The research problem centers on the lack of quantitative, real-time tools to predict how patients adapt to skill-enhancing tasks—a critical gap in personalizing occupational therapy (OT) interventions. We will integrate motion capture data from wearable sensors, electromyography, and cognitive load metrics collected during simulated activities of daily living (ADLs) into a machine learning pipeline. This pipeline will train recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and reinforcement learning models to identify individualized performance thresholds, fatigue trajectories, and error-correction patterns. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (sampled at 100Hz across 20+ biomechanical and physiological channels) and iteratively refining models that account for intra- and inter-session variability. The computational workflow includes parallelized hyperparameter optimization for time-series prediction and GPU-accelerated simulations of proposed adaptive task sequences. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for patient responsiveness to graded motor challenges, (2) an open-source toolkit for generating patient-specific activity progressions, and (3) quantitative evidence linking computational adaptability metrics to functional recovery rates. By bridging computational motor control theory with OT practice, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven therapeutic activity design, enhancing the precision of assistive interventions while maintaining the human-centered ethos of occupational therapy. The results will directly inform clinical training protocols for OT assistants in monitoring and adjusting sensor-embedded therapeutic technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize radiation exposure risk assessments in complex environments, addressing critical gaps in real-time decision-making for radiation protection scenarios. Current predictive tools for radiation dispersion, shielding efficacy, and dose accumulation often rely on simplified assumptions that fail to capture dynamic variables such as heterogeneous material interactions, time-dependent source terms, and multi-pathway exposure routes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate Monte Carlo radiation transport modeling, computational fluid dynamics for airborne contaminant spread, and machine learning-driven uncertainty quantification. The computational workflow will utilize established codes (e.g., Geant4, OpenFOAM) alongside custom algorithms to model scenarios relevant to nuclear medicine facilities, industrial radiography, and environmental monitoring contexts. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated particle tracking for rapid scenario testing and graph neural networks to identify hidden correlations in historical radiation safety incident data. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the petascale datasets generated by coupled simulations of radiation-matter interactions across spatial scales (nanometer to kilometer) and temporal resolutions (microsecond to annual exposures). Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for 3D dose distribution mapping in irregular geometries, probabilistic risk assessment tools for emergency response planning, and optimized radiation shielding configurations adaptable to diverse workplace layouts. These resources will directly enhance the technical capabilities of radiation protection personnel by providing evidence-based protocols for contamination control and waste management while serving as a platform for training technicians in next-generation computational health physics applications. The project’s computational products will be disseminated through open-source plugins for radiation safety software suites, bridging the gap between academic research and operational health physics practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health physicists, occupational safety and health specialists, and public health officials, to monitor and control radiation exposure and implement preventive measures in health care, work, and natural environments. Includes instruction in radiation physics, environmental radioactivity, radiological instrumentation, electronics of radiation detection equipment, radioactive waste management and control, safety and handling procedures, decontamination procedures, radioactivity testing and analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance comparative analyses of cultural and group identity formation across marginalized communities, with a focus on intersectional dynamics in visual and literary media. The research problem centers on the computational challenges of analyzing large-scale, multimodal datasets—including digitized archives, visual art, and multilingual literature—to identify patterns in how racial, gender, and ethnic identities are constructed and contested in different sociocultural contexts. Traditional qualitative methods, while foundational to group studies, struggle to systematically map cross-regional or transhistorical trends across fragmented, heterogeneous sources. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, and network analysis. NLP pipelines will process multilingual textual corpora to trace semantic shifts in identity-related discourse, while vision-based algorithms will classify stylistic and thematic elements in visual media (e.g., protest art, film). Network models will then map how these elements coalesce into broader narratives of resistance or solidarity across groups. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses to handle terabyte-scale datasets, enabling parallel processing of high-resolution images and GPU-accelerated transformer models for low-resource languages. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated cultural artifacts, (2) computational workflows tailored for interdisciplinary group studies, and (3) empirical insights into how marginalized communities negotiate identity in response to globalization and displacement. By bridging computational scalability with humanistic rigor, this project aims to establish new methodologies for comparative cultural analysis while fostering collaborative infrastructure for scholars in critical race, gender, and urban studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the comparative study of the history, literature, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of different groups such as racial, gender, sexual, class, ethnic, geographical, and national. Includes instruction in comparative studies, comparative literature, critical race theory, cultural anthropology, cultural studies, religious studies, science studies, social and cultural theory, urban studies, and visual culture.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time decision-making for aircraft armament systems maintenance under dynamic operational conditions. Modern military platforms integrate complex weapon systems subject to mechanical wear, environmental degradation, and evolving mission requirements, yet existing predictive models lack the resolution to account for nonlinear interactions between corrosion kinetics, structural fatigue, and adaptive threat scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this research will develop a multi-scale simulation framework to model the interdependent effects of operational stressors on armament system reliability. Computational workflows will combine finite element analysis for micromechanical damage prediction, computational fluid dynamics for corrosion propagation under varying climatic conditions, and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate maintenance prioritization strategies across heterogeneous datasets. The framework will be validated against field data from legacy and next-generation systems, incorporating temporal sensor feeds and historical failure records. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing of maintenance protocols and material performance, this project aims to generate actionable insights for lifecycle management, reducing unplanned downtime while maintaining mission-critical readiness. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolchain for adaptive armament system health monitoring and a probabilistic risk assessment database to inform safety-critical updates to MIL-STD-3034 compliance guidelines. The computational demands—particularly the need for parallelized Monte Carlo simulations and terabyte-scale optimization of neural network architectures—necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory systems. This work bridges gaps between defense logistics, materials informatics, and operational analytics, advancing a data-driven paradigm for sustainment of advanced military technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of aircraft weapons systems and associated peripherals. Includes instruction in basic science and quantitative methods, computer science, electronics, engineering graphics, fluid power, heavy equipment operation, armament systems, weapon materials and processes, weapon safety, corrosion control, aircraft systems maintenance, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for modeling dynamic consumer decision-making under volatile economic conditions. Traditional microeconomic models of consumer behavior often rely on simplified assumptions about rationality, static preferences, and market equilibrium, limiting their ability to capture real-world complexities such as adaptive learning, social influence networks, and rapid shifts in purchasing power. Our research addresses this gap by developing an agent-based model (ABM) that integrates heterogeneous consumer profiles, real-time price and wage data streams, and social media sentiment analysis to simulate emergent consumption patterns at scale. The computational approach combines econometric calibration techniques with machine learning algorithms to process high-dimensional datasets spanning anonymized transaction records, employment trends, and digital engagement metrics. Key challenges include managing asynchronous data updates across regional economies, optimizing parallelized simulations of 10^6+ agent interactions, and validating model outputs against established consumer confidence indices. By deploying containerized workflows on HPC clusters, we aim to achieve the necessary scalability and computational throughput to analyze crisis-driven consumption scenarios, such as pandemic-induced supply chain disruptions or inflationary shocks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for policymakers to stress-test economic interventions and a methodological contribution to computational consumer economics through adaptive preference modeling. This work bridges gaps between behavioral economics, data science, and distributed systems, offering a replicable framework for studying consumption dynamics in an era of increasing macroeconomic instability. The requested resources will directly support parameter space exploration, sensitivity analyses, and the development of GPU-accelerated inference pipelines for real-time scenario forecasting.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of micro- and macro-economic theory to consumer behavior and individual and family consumption of goods and services. Includes instruction in modeling, economic forecasting, indexing, price theory, and analysis of individual commodities and services and/or groups of related commodities and services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze ethical decision-making processes in complex, real-world professional scenarios, with a focus on healthcare and technology sectors. Current applied ethics research often relies on qualitative case studies or simplified theoretical models, which struggle to account for the dynamic, multi-agent interactions and contextual variables present in modern organizational environments. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale ethical decision environments using agent-based modeling (ABM) and probabilistic reasoning systems. The research will construct parameterized agents representing stakeholders with competing ethical priorities (e.g., patient autonomy vs. resource allocation efficiency in hospital systems) and train them on de-identified case datasets from institutional ethics review boards. Computational experiments will systematically vary cultural, legal, and organizational constraints to identify critical thresholds where different ethical frameworks (utilitarian, deontological, care ethics) produce divergent outcomes. A novel component involves integrating transformer-based natural language processing to analyze how ethical reasoning patterns in simulated decisions correlate with real-world ethics committee deliberations. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing three core challenges: 1) parallel processing of >10,000 agent interactions per experimental condition, 2) Bayesian network calculations across high-dimensional ethical preference spaces, and 3) comparative analysis of emergent normative patterns across simulated institutions. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for ethics sensitivity analysis in organizational policies, predictive models of ethical conflict escalation pathways, and quantitative evidence about contextual factors influencing moral reasoning consistency. This computational approach aims to advance applied ethics research beyond anecdotal analysis while maintaining philosophical rigor, ultimately helping organizations design more robust ethical governance systems responsive to complex societal challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of ethical issues in the workplace and public life, and the application of ethical decision-making to the practical problems of society and the professions. Includes instruction in ethical theory; history of ethics; contemporary social dilemmas; methods in applied ethics; and applications including medical ethics, legal ethics, business ethics, environmental ethics, and criminal justice ethics.

abstract: The proposed research employs high-performance computing to analyze the transnational development of feminist cultural production through computational text and network analysis of digitized women's archives. Current scholarship lacks large-scale systematic investigations into how artistic and literary works by women have circulated outside dominant institutional frameworks, particularly across linguistic and geographical boundaries. This project will process approximately 250,000 digitized items—including zines, experimental films, oral history transcripts, and underground press publications from 1970-2010—using natural language processing and computer vision techniques. Custom transformer models will be developed to identify patterns in visual motifs, narrative structures, and material practices that facilitated cross-cultural feminist solidarity, with particular attention to queer and BIPOC creators often excluded from canonical histories. Graph neural networks will map dissemination pathways through alternative distribution networks, analyzing how grassroots feminist aesthetics adapted to local contexts while maintaining transnational dialogues. The computational demands require GPU-accelerated processing of multilingual texts, high-resolution image analysis, and dynamic network modeling across temporal scales. Expected outcomes include an interactive spatial-temporal visualization platform tracking the emergence of feminist artistic counterpublics, plus machine learning classifiers to assist future archival research on marginalized cultural producers. This interdisciplinary approach advances Women's Studies by revealing previously underexamined connections between artistic form and collective mobilization while developing computational methods sensitive to intersectional feminist epistemologies. The resource allocation will enable processing heterogeneous data types at necessary scale while maintaining ethical frameworks for handling sensitive community-produced materials.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of women, and the development of modern feminism in relation to the roles played by women in different periods and locations in North America and the world. Programs may focus on literature, philosophy, and the arts as much as on social studies and policy.

abstract: Chronic wounds represent a significant clinical challenge, with diabetic ulcers, pressure injuries, and vascular ulcers contributing to prolonged patient suffering, high healthcare costs, and increased mortality. Traditional approaches to wound care research face limitations in modeling the complex interplay of biological, biomechanical, and environmental factors that dictate healing outcomes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that integrate molecular, cellular, and tissue-level dynamics in chronic wound environments. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate cellular interactions (e.g., immune response, fibroblast proliferation) and finite element analysis to characterize mechanical stress distributions in wound beds. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to clinical datasets, including electronic health records and multimodal imaging, to identify predictive biomarkers of healing trajectories. Computational workflows will require parallel processing for parameter optimization across heterogeneous datasets (genomic, proteomic, and biomechanical) and stochastic simulations of wound microenvironment variability. The proposed framework will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 350 patients with diabetic foot ulcers. By elucidating mechanisms underlying healing stagnation and regression, this work aims to advance personalized treatment strategies, including optimized debridement protocols and mechanomodulatory interventions. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for clinical decision support, novel targets for bioengineered therapies, and computational tools for virtual clinical trial design. Access to HPC resources is critical to manage the scale of spatiotemporal simulations, enable real-time analytics of high-resolution imaging data, and support the integration of multiphysics models. This project bridges computational innovation with translational wound care research, offering a pathway to reduce healing times, prevent complications, and improve quality of life for patients globally.
cip_definition: Research focused on Wound Care

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance the development of adaptive, large-scale virtual environments capable of simulating complex human-object interactions in real time, with applications in disaster response training and infrastructure resilience planning. Current simulation frameworks struggle to balance high-fidelity physics-based modeling with dynamic agent behavior, particularly when scaling to scenarios involving thousands of interacting entities (e.g., crowds, vehicles, and collapsing structures). This limitation stems from computational bottlenecks in resolving bidirectional feedback between discrete event systems, continuum mechanics models, and psychologically grounded agent decision-making processes. To address this gap, we propose a heterogeneous computing architecture combining particle-based fluid dynamics solvers, graph neural networks for emergent group behavior prediction, and neuromorphic decision modules trained on human behavioral data. The computational approach leverages parallelized message-passing interfaces for multi-physics coupling and integrates stochastic optimization techniques to manage uncertainty propagation across temporal scales. High-performance computing resources will enable parameter-space exploration through massively parallel simulations comparing different crisis scenarios, material failure thresholds, and evacuation protocol efficiencies. Expected outcomes include a novel simulation framework that reduces latency in human-environment feedback loops by 40% compared to existing solutions while maintaining sub-second synchronization across distributed compute nodes. The research will produce open-source tools for real-time simulation fidelity assessment and a dataset correlating computational resource allocation patterns with measurable training outcomes in virtual emergency response exercises. By bridging gaps between distributed systems engineering, behavioral modeling, and computational mechanics, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for responsive virtual environments in safety-critical applications.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles of applied visual simulation technology and the application of quantitative analyses to human-computer interaction. Includes instruction in object-oriented programming, artificial intelligence, computer communications and networks, computer graphics, virtual worlds and simulation systems, probability, statistics, stochastic modeling, data analysis, human-performance evaluation, and human-behavior modeling.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing real-time multimedia content delivery in dynamic broadcasting environments. As streaming platforms and hybrid broadcast-internet systems grow in complexity, media producers face challenges in minimizing latency, ensuring signal integrity, and adapting content for heterogeneous viewer devices without compromising artistic intent. Traditional broadcast simulation tools struggle to model large-scale, multi-platform distribution scenarios or process high-resolution audiovisual data efficiently. This research will develop computational workflows to simulate and analyze signal propagation, compression artifacts, and adaptive bitrate streaming across urban-scale networks. Using GPU-accelerated rendering and parallelized finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations, we will model electromagnetic wave behavior for next-gen broadcast systems operating in the 3-24 GHz spectrum, incorporating real-world geographic and architectural data. Machine learning models trained on perceptual quality metrics will automate artifact detection in 4K/8K video streams, while Monte Carlo methods will assess failure probabilities in distributed content delivery networks. The computational intensity of processing terabyte-scale media datasets and running millions of parallel transmission scenarios necessitates HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for optimizing transmitter placement in 5G broadcast networks, adaptive encoding presets that balance technical constraints with creative priorities, and policy recommendations for spectrum allocation in dense media markets. By bridging media production practices with computational engineering, this work aims to empower content creators with evidence-based strategies for maintaining artistic vision amid evolving technological constraints, while providing regulators with tools to evaluate interference claims in licensing disputes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, methods, and techniques used to plan, produce, and distribute audio and video programs and messages, and that prepares individuals to function as staff, producers, directors, and managers of radio and television shows and media organizations. Includes instruction in media aesthetics; planning, scheduling, and production; writing and editing; performing and directing; personnel and facilities management; marketing and distribution; media regulations, law, and policy; and principles of broadcast technology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multimodal clinical data, including electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and genomic profiles, presents significant challenges in developing predictive models for precision medicine. Current approaches often struggle to integrate heterogeneous data types efficiently, limiting their ability to capture nuanced patient-specific patterns critical for clinical decision support. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize scalable machine learning frameworks capable of synthesizing diverse clinical datasets. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) designing a federated learning architecture to enable privacy-preserving analysis of distributed EHR data across healthcare institutions; (2) implementing deep learning models for multimodal fusion of imaging, temporal clinical data, and genomic features; and (3) creating an interpretable decision support system for predicting treatment responses in complex chronic diseases. Computational methods will include distributed tensor factorization for dimensionality reduction, graph neural networks to model patient similarity networks, and transformer-based architectures for temporal data analysis. The proposed work requires HPC resources to manage large-scale data processing (10+ TB of imaging and genomic data), parallelize hyperparameter optimization across thousands of model configurations, and simulate federated learning scenarios across virtualized clinical nodes. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for multimodal clinical data integration, validated through retrospective studies on oncology and cardiology cohorts, and a deployable framework for real-time decision support. This work will advance medical informatics by providing computational tools to overcome data siloing challenges while maintaining patient privacy, ultimately supporting more personalized therapeutic strategies. Successful implementation will provide open-source software packages to the research community and lay the foundation for prospective clinical validation studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to medical research and clinical information technology support, and the development of advanced imaging, database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in computer science, health information systems architecture, medical knowledge structures, medical language and image processing, quantitative medical decision modeling, imaging techniques, electronic medical records, medical research systems, clinical decision support, and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.
