abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze the structural and semantic evolution of Eucharistic liturgies across underrepresented Christian traditions, including Syriac, Coptic, and Nestorian rites, from antiquity to the early modern period. While liturgical studies remain central to divinity and ministry training, existing scholarship has disproportionately focused on Western traditions, leaving critical gaps in understanding how textual, theological, and cultural dynamics shaped non-European rites. The project addresses this imbalance by computationally examining a multilingual corpus of digitized liturgical manuscripts, rubrics, and patristic commentaries (4th–16th centuries) to identify patterns in theological emphasis, ritual innovation, and cross-traditional influence. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for ancient Syriac, Coptic, and Arabic texts—including transformer-based models fine-tuned for low-resource languages—the team will perform large-scale semantic role labeling, conceptual metaphor analysis, and network modeling of liturgical elements. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of over 20,000 manuscript pages, training of custom word embeddings for niche theological terminology, and simulation of textual transmission pathways across geographic and doctrinal boundaries. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative typology of Eastern liturgical development, a public database of annotated texts for ministerial pedagogy, and computational frameworks adaptable to other understudied religious corpora. By bridging computational linguistics, historical theology, and ministerial training, this work aims to equip divinity scholars and practitioners with tools to critically engage liturgical diversity while preserving endangered religious heritage.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as ministers or priests in any of the Christian religious traditions. Includes instruction in the theology and polity of a particular church, church law, liturgy and ritual, principles of pastoral ministry, homiletics, evangelism, church/parish organization and management, Christian ethics, church history, and related studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive analytics framework for optimizing the allocation of police patrol units in dynamic urban environments. Current approaches to patrol allocation rely heavily on historical crime data and static zoning models, which inadequately account for real-time variables such as shifting crowd densities, traffic patterns, and transient socio-economic events (e.g., festivals, protests). The computational limitations of existing tools restrict the granularity and temporal resolution of predictive models, resulting in suboptimal resource deployment and delayed response times. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including live traffic camera feeds, social media activity, emergency call logs, and weather reports—into a unified spatiotemporal forecasting system. The core computational challenge involves training deep reinforcement learning agents on multi-terabyte datasets to simulate patrol decision-making under complex, evolving constraints. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing the processing of high-dimensional time-series data, enabling rapid retraining of models as new information streams are incorporated. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source framework for real-time patrol optimization, validated against historical incident response data from three mid-sized U.S. cities. The project’s interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational criminology, urban informatics, and operations research, offering a novel tool for enhancing proactive policing strategies while minimizing operational costs. Successfully demonstrating this approach could redefine standards for data-driven law enforcement resource management, with potential applications in disaster response and critical infrastructure protection.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of police and public security officers, including patrol and investigative activities, traffic control, crowd control and public relations, witness interviewing, evidence collection and management, basic crime prevention methods, weapon and equipment operation and maintenance, report preparation and other routine law enforcement responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize personalized educational interventions for K–12 students with emotional disturbances (ED), leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex, multimodal datasets. Students with ED often exhibit heterogeneous behavioral and academic needs, yet educators face challenges in systematically predicting which instructional or socioemotional strategies will be most effective for individual learners. Current approaches rely heavily on manual observation and static intervention plans, which lack the scalability to address dynamic student needs. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning framework that integrates longitudinal student data—including academic performance metrics, behavioral incident reports, physiological sensor data (e.g., heart rate variability), and teacher feedback—to identify patterns associated with successful outcomes. HPC resources will enable the processing and synthesis of these large-scale, high-dimensional datasets, which include sensitive, time-series information from over 10,000 anonymized student records. Computational models will be trained to classify student responsiveness to specific interventions under varying contextual conditions (e.g., classroom size, time of day) and recommend adaptive strategies in near-real time. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom dynamics to evaluate how proposed interventions scale across diverse educational environments. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for educators to simulate and predict intervention efficacy, alongside evidence-based guidelines for embedding computational modeling into teacher training programs. This work directly supports the development of precision education strategies in special education, equipping teachers with data-driven tools to address the acute needs of students with ED while reducing trial-and-error approaches. By aligning computational advances with pedagogical expertise, the project aims to bridge a critical gap in teacher education, fostering scalable, individualized support for a historically underserved student population.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Emotional Disturbances
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with emotional conditions which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with emotional disturbances, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising individuals with emotional disturbances, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the cognitive and linguistic processes underlying second language acquisition (SLA) among adult learners in English as a Second Language (ESL) programs. While existing research emphasizes sociocultural and pedagogical factors, the computational modeling of real-time language processing—particularly the interplay between syntactic complexity, semantic retention, and cross-linguistic interference—remains underexplored. To bridge this gap, we propose a large-scale computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze longitudinal datasets of learner interactions, including written essays, spoken dialogue transcripts, and reading comprehension assessments. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to extract syntactic structures, lexical diversity metrics, and error patterns, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer-based models will simulate incremental language production and comprehension. Parallelized simulations will model the impact of母语 (L1) transfer on English morphosyntactic development across diverse language pairs (e.g., Mandarin-English, Spanish-English). The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of multimodal data (over 10,000 learner hours), the complexity of training multilingual models with attention mechanisms, and the need for real-time analysis in virtual ESL classroom simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for identifying at-risk learners based on computational biomarkers, (2) evidence-based strategies for personalized curriculum design targeting syntactic and semantic bottlenecks, and (3) open-source NLP tools optimized for SLA research. By integrating computational linguistics with applied ESL pedagogy, this work aims to advance both theoretical models of interlanguage development and practical interventions for postsecondary ESL programs.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: Gynecologic cancers, including ovarian, endometrial, and cervical malignancies, exhibit significant molecular heterogeneity, complicating treatment optimization and biomarker discovery. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized therapeutic strategies, which may inadequately address interpatient variability in tumor biology and treatment response. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-omics predictive models that integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data from patient cohorts, aiming to identify subtype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities and resistance mechanisms. The computational workflow will process raw sequencing data from tumor biopsies and liquid biopsies, harmonize disparate omics datasets, and apply machine learning algorithms to uncover patterns associated with clinical outcomes. Key challenges include managing large-scale data volumes (≥10 TB), executing parallelized bioinformatic pipelines for variant calling and pathway analysis, and training deep learning models to predict drug response across heterogeneous tumor subtypes. The HPC infrastructure will enable accelerated genome-wide association studies (GWAS), dynamic simulations of tumor-immune interactions, and validation of candidate biomarkers through in silico perturbation experiments. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for stratifying patients based on molecular profiles, (2) novel biomarkers predictive of platinum-based chemotherapy resistance in ovarian cancer, and (3) open-source tools for real-time integration of multi-omics data in clinical decision support systems. This work directly addresses the urgent need for precision medicine in gynecologic oncology by bridging computational innovation with clinical translation. Successful implementation will enhance therapeutic targeting, reduce ineffective treatment exposures, and provide a template for computational resource utilization in oncologic research. All models, code, and de-identified datasets will be shared via public repositories to foster collaborative advances in the field.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for consultation and comprehensive management of patients with gynecologic cancer, including those diagnostic and therapeutic procedures necessary for the total care of the patient with gynecologic cancer and resulting complications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the design and real-time operation of hybrid energy systems integrating distributed renewable generation, electrochemical storage, and hydrogen-based long-duration energy storage. As power grids transition toward decarbonization, the coupled dynamics between intermittent renewables, multi-scale storage technologies, and demand-side flexibility create complex operational challenges that exceed the capabilities of conventional single-timescale optimization models. The research problem centers on addressing temporal and spatial mismatches in renewable-dominant systems through a novel multi-layered optimization approach combining year-round capacity planning, day-ahead scheduling, and intra-hour model predictive control. The computational methodology leverages high-performance computing to resolve nested timescales across three key areas: (1) physics-informed machine learning surrogate models trained on electrochemical battery degradation datasets, (2) mixed-integer nonlinear programming for hydrogen storage dispatch optimization under equipment durability constraints, and (3) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations evaluating system reliability under 10,000+ weather-realistic scenarios. By implementing a heterogeneous computing architecture combining CPU clusters and GPU-accelerated tensor operations, the framework aims to reduce simulation wall times for annual operational analyses from weeks to hours while maintaining sub-minute temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source optimization toolkit capable of co-optimizing capital costs and operational expenditures for hybrid systems at unprecedented spatiotemporal granularity, validated against operational data from a 50 MW pilot site. The results will provide quantitative guidance for minimizing levelized storage costs in high-renewable penetration grids while maintaining grid-forming capabilities, directly supporting national priorities for clean energy resilience. This computational advance addresses a critical gap in energy systems engineering by enabling holistic analysis of storage technologies across their full operational lifespan and grid service value dimensions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of energy generation, storage, conversion, and distribution systems. Includes instruction in conventional and alternative/renewable energy systems, electrical power systems, and electrical system design.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of producing high-resolution, dynamic commercial art in an era where consumer engagement relies on increasingly complex, data-driven visual media. While advancements in generative AI and real-time rendering tools offer new creative possibilities, current consumer-grade hardware limits artists’ ability to efficiently iterate on large-scale projects, integrate multi-modal datasets, or simulate photorealistic outputs for diverse advertising platforms. This research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize computational workflows for generative design, 3D asset rendering, and adaptive media personalization. The study will employ parallelized neural networks to train custom generative models on heterogeneous datasets (including branded content, consumer behavior metrics, and stylistic precedents), enabling rapid prototyping of context-aware advertising visuals. Additionally, distributed rendering pipelines will be tested to reduce latency in producing 4K/8K outputs for augmented reality (AR) campaigns and interactive digital displays. By analyzing computational bottlenecks in existing design software through GPU-accelerated profiling, the project aims to create open-source tools that streamline resource allocation for common tasks like vector-raster conversion, texture synthesis, and cross-platform format optimization. Outcomes will include a framework for scalable, HPC-enhanced artistic workflows, reducing production timelines for high-fidelity commercial art by an estimated 30–50% while maintaining creative flexibility. This work will provide actionable insights into bridging computational efficiency with artistic intent, directly benefiting educators, digital artists, and advertising firms navigating the technical challenges of modern visual communication. The requested resources—including GPU nodes and high-memory processors—are critical for handling the terabyte-scale asset libraries and latent diffusion models central to this research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via illustrations and other forms of digital or printed media. Includes instruction in concept design, layout, paste-up, and techniques such as engraving, etching, silkscreen, lithography, offset, drawing and cartooning, painting, collage, and computer graphics.

abstract: Livestock production systems face increasing pressure to enhance productivity while addressing environmental and animal welfare concerns. A critical challenge lies in optimizing feed efficiency and methane mitigation strategies in ruminants, which require understanding complex interactions between host genetics, gut microbiomes, and dietary inputs. Current experimental approaches are limited in scalability and fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale biological processes involved. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating genomic, metabolomic, and microbiome data to model metabolic pathways and predict outcomes of dietary interventions. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ agent-based modeling to simulate microbial community dynamics in the rumen under varying nutritional regimes, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify genotype-by-environment interactions influencing methane production and nutrient utilization. The computational pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets from 16S rRNA sequencing, metagenomics, and livestock sensor networks (e.g., wearable devices monitoring real-time methane emissions). Parallelized simulations will assess thousands of hypothetical feed formulations and genetic selection scenarios, reducing reliance on costly longitudinal animal trials. Expected outcomes include predictive models for methane abatement strategies, optimized feed formulations tailored to regional agricultural byproducts, and genomic selection indices for low-emission breeding programs. This work will advance precision livestock management by providing actionable insights to reduce greenhouse gas intensity per unit of animal protein while maintaining economic viability. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of multi-omics integration, enable large-scale parameter space exploration, and deliver scalable solutions adaptable to diverse production systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of livestock animals and the production and handling of meat and other products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, range science, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: Protective services operations face increasingly complex challenges in mitigating dynamic physical threats across diverse environments, necessitating advanced computational approaches to optimize resource allocation and operational planning. Traditional methods for security protocol design often rely on static risk assessments and historical data, which may inadequately address real-time variables such as adaptive adversarial behavior, multi-threat interactions, and environmental unpredictability. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation framework to model threat scenarios, security responses, and contingency outcomes under variable conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate agent-based modeling, real-time geospatial analytics, and machine learning to simulate interactions between protective agents, threat actors, and environmental factors at scale. Key computational challenges include parallelizing thousands of concurrent agent decision trees, processing sensor-derived spatial data streams, and training reinforcement learning models on synthetic threat-response datasets. The framework will incorporate operational parameters from protective services domains, including surveillance system latency, personnel mobility constraints, and weapon engagement dynamics, validated through collaboration with active security professionals. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for vulnerability surfaces in hybrid physical-digital environments, adaptive deployment strategies for rapid threat containment, and probabilistic models of cascading failure points in multi-layered security systems. By enabling granular, data-driven scenario testing beyond the capacity of conventional simulations, this work aims to advance decision-support tools for protective operations in critical infrastructure, executive protection, and crowd management contexts. The requested HPC allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated deep reinforcement learning workflows and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to quantify emergent risks in understudied threat landscapes.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques of providing physical security protection to clients in various environments and situations. Includes instruction in security intelligence and information resources, operations planning and surveying, operations security, weapons and explosives, defense and offense techniques, security and surveillance systems, communications systems, perimeter and access control, weapons of mass destruction, contingency planning, crowd control, cover and evacuation, combat and vehicle techniques, and applicable legal and administrative responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and enhance the preservation of dynamic, born-digital cultural materials within library special collections. As libraries increasingly acquire complex digital artifacts—such as interactive media, ephemeral web content, and software-dependent artworks—existing metadata standards and preservation workflows struggle to capture their technical dependencies, contextual relationships, and behavioral integrity over time. Traditional approaches, designed for static physical materials, lack the capacity to model the mutable, interdependent components of these digital objects, risking long-term accessibility gaps. The research will employ graph neural networks (GNNs) and provenance-aware simulation techniques to map temporal dependencies between digital components, predict degradation pathways, and recommend adaptive preservation strategies. High-performance computing resources are required to process heterogeneous datasets (including code repositories, version histories, and hardware emulation logs) and train models that account for multi-scale interactions between software environments, file formats, and user engagement patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for libraries to simulate preservation scenarios, quantify risks to digital object functionality, and optimize archival storage decisions. This work bridges computational preservation science and information theory, advancing library practice by addressing gaps in contemporary digital stewardship frameworks. Results will be validated against real-world collections containing interactive narratives, virtual reality exhibits, and legacy hypermedia, with implications for ensuring persistent access to evolving forms of cultural memory. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with archival principles, the project establishes a methodological foundation for stewarding complex digital artifacts as living, interdependent systems rather than static files.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project addresses the growing need for advanced computational methods to analyze complex, large-scale educational assessment data, particularly in contexts where traditional statistical approaches are insufficient. The research focuses on developing and validating predictive models of student learning outcomes using multi-modal data, including longitudinal assessment results, digital learning platform interactions, and contextual socio-educational variables. A critical challenge lies in integrating these heterogeneous datasets—often comprising millions of observations with temporal, spatial, and hierarchical dependencies—while accounting for measurement error and missing data inherent in educational settings. The proposed computational approach combines multilevel Bayesian networks with deep learning architectures to model nonlinear relationships between assessment performance, instructional interventions, and student characteristics across diverse populations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models at scale, conducting Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate assessment instrument validity, and performing sensitivity analyses through massive parameter space exploration. The project will leverage parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling and distributed tensor computations to manage computational complexity, with iterative model refinement informed by real-world educational assessment data from partner institutions. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source framework for adaptive educational assessment analytics, (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing assessment design in technology-enhanced learning environments, and (3) novel metrics for detecting early warning patterns in student achievement trajectories. By enabling more precise analysis of assessment data at unprecedented scales, this work aims to advance equitable evaluation practices while providing methodological innovations for handling the computational demands of modern educational research. The requested HPC resources will directly support the intensive memory and processing requirements of simultaneously analyzing multiple assessment cohorts while maintaining strict privacy-preserving protocols through encrypted distributed computing.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_title: Educational Assessment, Evaluation, and Research, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in educational evaluation, research and statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the empirical understanding of dance movement therapy (DMT) as a rehabilitative and mental health intervention. While DMT has demonstrated clinical efficacy, the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain poorly characterized. Current limitations stem from the complexity of analyzing multidimensional movement data, dynamic interpersonal interactions in therapeutic settings, and the integration of heterogeneous datasets (e.g., motion capture, biometric sensors, neuroimaging, and psychological assessments). This research proposes a computational framework to model how structured dance interventions modulate motor behavior, emotional regulation, and neural plasticity. Motion capture data from clinical DMT sessions will be processed using machine learning algorithms to quantify movement patterns, synchrony between participants and therapists, and correlations with self-reported psychological outcomes. Concurrently, neuroimaging datasets will be analyzed to identify functional connectivity changes associated with specific therapeutic movement protocols. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further investigate how rhythmic movement influences autonomic nervous system responses, such as heart rate variability and respiratory patterns. HPC resources are critical for handling the scale of spatiotemporal movement data, training predictive models for therapeutic outcomes, and running computationally intensive simulations of neural and physiological processes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for multimodal DMT data analysis, (2) predictive models linking movement features to therapeutic efficacy across diverse populations, and (3) mechanistic insights into how dance modulates neurobehavioral pathways. By bridging computational methodologies with dance therapy practice, this work aims to establish robust, data-driven frameworks for optimizing clinical protocols, personalizing interventions, and strengthening the empirical foundation of DMT within integrative healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use the therapeutic application of creative dance movement to assist in promoting client rehabilitation and physical, emotional, and mental health. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, personality development, movement and motor behavior, psychology, dance, creative expression modalities, improvisation, group psychology and leadership, client evaluation and supervision, dance therapy practice, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of comedic storytelling and audience reception through computational analysis of large-scale performance datasets. While comedy’s cultural impact is well acknowledged, quantitative frameworks for analyzing its structural patterns, emotional dynamics, and audience engagement remain underdeveloped. Our research addresses this gap by developing computational models to examine how comedic techniques—such as timing, semantic incongruity, and callbacks—correlate with measurable audience responses (e.g., laughter frequency, sentiment shifts) across diverse demographics. The project will aggregate and process multimodal data from archival recordings of live comedy performances, annotated scripts, and audience biometric feedback (voluntarily provided), totaling approximately 10 TB of raw audio, video, and text. Machine learning pipelines will be trained to identify comedic devices in scripts and performances, while natural language processing (NLP) tools will map narrative arcs against audience reaction timelines. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate how variations in delivery (e.g., pacing, tonal emphasis) influence perceived humor under different cultural or contextual parameters. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-memory nodes to handle high-dimensional data and complex simulations. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database linking comedic techniques to audience engagement metrics, (2) predictive models to assist writers and performers in optimizing content for specific audiences, and (3) new methodologies for computational humor studies within the performing arts. By bridging data science and comedic theory, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of humor’s mechanics while providing practical tools for comedy creation and pedagogy. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the scale and complexity of this analysis, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical, cultural, and theoretical dimensions of comedy as an art form, and the writing, performance, and production of comedy. Includes instruction in comedic storytelling, comedy production, comedy writing, history of comedy, improvisation, and sketch writing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and operational efficiency of next-generation hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES) under dynamic environmental and load conditions. Current HRES models struggle to balance real-time energy generation, storage, and distribution across variable renewable sources (e.g., solar, wind) and demand profiles, leading to suboptimal performance in grid stability and energy yield. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for turbine and photovoltaic array modeling, machine learning (ML)-driven demand forecasting, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming for system optimization. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute parallelized CFD simulations resolving turbulent airflow around wind turbines at 1-meter resolution, coupled with transient solar irradiance datasets across annual cycles. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated ML models will train on terabyte-scale historical weather and grid demand data to predict short-term load fluctuations. These components will feed into a distributed optimization algorithm designed to minimize energy waste and infrastructure costs while maintaining grid reliability. The computational workload necessitates access to HPC clusters with 10,000+ CPU cores and multi-node GPU arrays due to the scale of parametric sweeps (10^6+ configurations) and the need for near-real-time optimization under dynamically changing constraints. Expected outcomes include validated models for HRES component interaction, open-source optimization tools for adaptive energy management, and design guidelines for resilient hybrid systems in urban and remote environments. This work will directly inform ongoing partnerships with regional energy providers aiming to achieve 80% renewable integration by 2030, bridging critical gaps between theoretical models and deployable clean energy solutions.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of under-resourced Southeast Asian languages, with a focus on syntactic diversity and contact-induced language change in the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian families. Despite their sociolinguistic importance, many languages in this region lack robust digital corpora and computational tools, hindering large-scale comparative studies. The project addresses this gap by developing automated methods to analyze syntactic structures and lexical borrowing patterns across 15+ languages, including Burmese, Tagalog, and Javanese, using digitized texts, oral narratives, and historical records. Key computational challenges include processing agglutinative morphology, modeling non-configurational syntax, and identifying cross-linguistic transfer in multilingual communities. Proposed methods integrate transformer-based language models fine-tuned on newly annotated datasets, Bayesian phylogenetic inference for contact networks, and graph-based algorithms to map syntactic typology. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale multilingual corpora, hyperparameter optimization for low-resource NLP models, and Monte Carlo simulations of language diversification timelines. Expected outcomes include: (1) open-source tools for syntactic annotation and borrowability prediction tailored to Southeast Asian languages, (2) quantitative evidence challenging existing assumptions about Sprachbund boundaries in mainland Southeast Asia, and (3) a computational framework to prioritize endangered language documentation efforts based on typological rarity. By combining linguistic theory with scalable computation, this work aims to reshape comparative methodologies in Southeast Asian linguistics while contributing novel datasets and algorithms to the digital humanities. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for collaborative corpus development, and reproducible workflow management for cross-institutional research teams.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the modern languages spoken in mainland Southeast Asia and the Indonesian and Philippines Archipelagoes, including, but not limited to, members of the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian language families.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of information diffusion and rhetorical strategy adaptation in large-scale digital media ecosystems, with a focus on understanding how sociocultural variables influence the spread and polarization of public discourse. The increasing complexity of communication networks, combined with the real-time, multimodal nature of digital interactions, presents challenges for traditional analytical frameworks in communication theory. Current models often oversimplify the interdependencies between message content, platform affordances, and audience behavior, particularly at the scale of millions of interactions. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-terabyte datasets of social media content, user engagement metrics, and cross-platform sharing patterns. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be deployed to classify rhetorical strategies and semantic frames in text and multimedia content, while temporal network analysis will model the co-evolution of discourse communities and information cascades. Agent-based simulations will test theoretical assumptions about attention economies and confirmation bias in networked environments. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling memory-intensive graph computations, training transformer-based NLP models on heterogeneous communication data, and running parallelized simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel framework for modeling communication processes as complex adaptive systems, (2) empirically grounded insights into how platform architectures amplify specific rhetorical tactics, and (3) open-source tools for scalable analysis of cross-cultural communication patterns. These contributions will advance theoretical understanding of digital persuasion mechanisms while providing practical methodologies for researchers studying misinformation, political communication, and online collective behavior. The project directly aligns with the program’s emphasis on media effects analysis and critical evaluation of communication systems in sociotechnical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on theories of communication. Includes instruction in theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural and intellectual networks of feminist movements across the 20th century, with a focus on understudied literary and artistic communities. While existing scholarship has mapped broad ideological shifts in feminist thought, granular analyses of regional and transnational exchanges—particularly those mediated through alternative publications, visual art, and performance archives—remain limited by the scale and complexity of multimodal data. This research addresses this gap by employing computational text analysis, image recognition, and network modeling to trace patterns of collaboration, dissent, and knowledge circulation among feminist creators. The proposed workflow will process digitized collections of zines, experimental theater scripts, and mixed-media artworks using NLP techniques adapted for historical vernacular and visual datasets. Network models will reconstruct influence pathways between individuals and collectives, while temporal analysis will track how intersectional frameworks emerged through material and aesthetic practices. HPC resources are critical for handling the heterogeneous datasets (spanning 50,000+ pages of text and 15,000+ images) and computationally intensive tasks, including training custom vision models to detect recurring symbolic motifs in scanned artworks. Expected outcomes include: 1) new empirical insights into how marginalized feminist groups negotiated cultural production under differing political conditions, 2) methodological innovations in computationally analyzing non-canonical artistic archives, and 3) public-facing interactive visualizations to support pedagogy in global gender studies. By centering computationally driven inquiry on material often excluded from institutional archives, this project aims to reshape scholarly understandings of feminist cultural labor while demonstrating the value of HPC infrastructure for humanistic research in gender and women’s studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of women, and the development of modern feminism in relation to the roles played by women in different periods and locations in North America and the world. Programs may focus on literature, philosophy, and the arts as much as on social studies and policy.

abstract: The increasing complexity of well drilling operations, driven by demands for deeper, more efficient extraction of water, oil, and gas resources, necessitates advanced computational modeling to optimize drilling parameters and mitigate risks such as wellbore instability, equipment failure, and fluid loss. Current industry practices often rely on generalized empirical models, which inadequately account for site-specific geological heterogeneity, dynamic stress regimes, and multiphase fluid interactions. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, physics-based simulation framework to model drilling processes in heterogeneous subsurface environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical processes during drilling. Key objectives include modeling drill bit-rock interaction under varying lithologies, predicting fracture propagation during hydraulic fracturing, and assessing the impact of drilling fluid properties on wellbore stability. The computational workflow will integrate machine learning algorithms to calibrate simulations with real-time sensor data from field operations, enabling adaptive parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce non-productive time (NPT) caused by unexpected formation behavior, guidelines for fluid selection and pressure management in complex geological settings, and risk-assessment protocols for environmentally sensitive areas. By enabling large-scale, high-resolution simulations of subsurface systems, HPC resources are critical to resolving the spatial and temporal scales required for actionable insights. This work will advance the academic program’s capacity to train students in computational geomechanics and data-driven drilling optimization, while providing industry partners with open-source tools to enhance operational safety and efficiency. The project’s significance lies in bridging the gap between theoretical models and field-scale challenges, fostering sustainable resource extraction practices through innovation in computational drilling science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, maintain, repair, and operate well drilling equipment; locate, drill, construct, and develop water, gas, and oil wells; and test and monitor wells to ensure adequate flow. Includes applications to home, business, and industrial uses.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance safety and efficiency in professional diving operations through high-fidelity computational modeling of dynamic underwater environments and physiological responses during decompression. Despite established protocols, diving-related injuries such as decompression sickness persist due to variability in diver physiology, equipment performance, and environmental conditions. Current predictive models lack the resolution to account for real-time interactions between these factors, particularly in complex scenarios involving mixed-gas diving, salvage operations, or extreme depths. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of gas exchange in tissues, machine learning-driven analysis of diver biometric data, and probabilistic risk assessment for equipment failure modes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve 3D simulations of gas bubble nucleation under varying pressure regimes, coupled with ensemble modeling of thousands of dive profiles to identify critical risk thresholds. The computational workflow will process sensor data from prototype dive computers, environmental monitoring systems, and historical incident reports to train neural networks for adaptive decompression scheduling. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for decompression stress that incorporate individual physiological variability, (2) optimized equipment design parameters for next-generation rebreather systems, and (3) AI-assisted decision support tools for dive planning in challenging conditions. By leveraging parallelized simulations across GPU clusters, this work will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling transient pressure changes and microbubble dynamics at biologically relevant scales. The resulting frameworks will directly benefit diving instructors and commercial diving operations through data-driven safety protocols while informing regulatory updates for decompression tables. This project establishes a computational foundation for precision diving medicine and adaptive underwater human performance monitoring.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as professional deep-water or scuba divers, diving instructors, or diving support personnel. Includes instruction in the use of diving equipment and related specialized gear; diving safety procedures; operation and maintenance of underwater life-support systems; underwater communication systems; decompression systems; underwater salvage; exploration, rescue, and photography; and installation and fitting of underwater mechanical systems and their maintenance, repair or demolition.

abstract: Healthcare environments significantly influence patient outcomes, staff efficiency, and operational costs, yet the design of these spaces often relies on generalized guidelines rather than evidence-based, hyper-localized insights. This project addresses the critical gap in understanding how dynamic, real-time interactions between environmental variables (e.g., spatial layout, airflow, lighting, noise) and human behaviors (e.g., patient movement, care workflows) impact healing outcomes. Traditional architectural simulations lack the computational power to model these multidimensional, nonlinear relationships at scale. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrated simulation framework combining agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to optimize healthcare environment design. Agent-based models will simulate patient and staff movement patterns, while CFD will analyze environmental factors such as airborne pathogen dispersion and thermal comfort. ML algorithms will iteratively refine design parameters by correlating simulated environments with real-world health outcome data from electronic medical records (EMRs) and sensor networks. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing large-scale spatial datasets, running parallelized simulations across diverse design scenarios, and training predictive models with high-dimensional inputs. Expected outcomes include actionable design principles for reducing hospital-acquired infections, minimizing patient stress through sensory-aware layouts, and improving care team efficiency. This work will establish a computational foundation for data-driven healthcare architecture, enabling rapid prototyping of adaptive environments tailored to evolving clinical needs. By bridging architecture, healthcare, and computational science, the project advances a novel paradigm for evidence-based design that prioritizes human health at the intersection of built and biological systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and performance of healthcare environments to optimize healing. Includes instruction in interior design, architecture, healing sciences, healthcare environments, human-centered design, and healthcare delivery.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, cross-channel consumer engagement in digital marketing environments. While businesses increasingly rely on omnichannel strategies to integrate customer interactions across platforms, the computational demands of modeling dynamic, high-dimensional consumer behavior—spanning social media, e-commerce, mobile apps, and IoT touchpoints—exceed the capabilities of conventional systems. Current approaches often rely on siloed analytics or simplified heuristics, limiting their ability to capture nonlinear interactions, temporal dependencies, and context-aware personalization at scale. The proposed work will develop a computational framework combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with large-scale graph neural networks (GNNs) to simulate multi-agent consumer journeys in real time. The model will ingest heterogeneous data streams—including clickstreams, sentiment analysis from natural language processing (NLP), geospatial patterns, and probabilistic attribution data—to predict and optimize micro-moments in customer decision pathways. HPC resources are critical for training ensemble models on terabyte-scale datasets, enabling parallelized hyperparameter optimization across thousands of simulated marketing scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel algorithm for adaptive budget allocation across digital channels, empirically validated against anonymized corporate partner datasets spanning 10M+ user profiles. The research will advance computational marketing by addressing latency and scalability barriers in dynamic campaign orchestration, with potential applications in churn prediction, hyper-personalized content delivery, and ethical AI-driven targeting. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for marketing analytics, reducing barriers to entry for SMEs lacking proprietary HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop a digital marketing plan and integrate marketing, advertising, sales, and logistics across physical and digital channels. Includes instruction in digital marketing, e-commerce, online consumer psychology, search engine optimization, social media marketing, and web analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze nonlinear dynamics in heterogeneous agent macroeconomic models with stochastic shocks, a problem intractable to closed-form solutions due to high-dimensional state spaces and path-dependent interactions. Traditional equilibrium analyses often rely on restrictive homogeneity assumptions or linear approximations that fail to capture emergent complexity in financial networks, labor market frictions, and climate-economic feedback loops. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to implement massively parallelized Monte Carlo simulations coupled with numerical continuation methods, enabling systematic exploration of bifurcation thresholds and resilience regimes in coupled economic-ecological systems. The computational architecture will combine agent-based modeling techniques with stochastic optimal control solvers, operating across multiple scales from microeconomic decision rules to macroeconomic stability metrics. Key challenges include adaptive meshing for value function iteration in 8+ dimensional state spaces and Bayesian estimation of nonlinear impulse responses using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of early-warning indicators for critical transitions in debt-climate cascades, (2) quantitative assessment of policy intervention efficacy under deep uncertainty, and (3) open-source modular code for heterodox economic system simulation. The HPC resources requested are essential for achieving statistical significance across parameter sweeps (>10^5 parallelized runs), maintaining numerical stability in stiff differential-algebraic systems, and storing petabyte-scale output for topological data analysis. This interdisciplinary synthesis of dynamical systems theory, computational statistics, and economic modeling aims to establish new standards for complexity-aware policy design while advancing numerical methods for high-dimensional economic systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical methods to the development of economic theory, models, and quantitative analysis. Includes instruction in data analysis, applied business economics, calculus, econometrics, linear algebra, microeconomic theory, probability, and statistical methods.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare administration demands innovative computational approaches to optimize medical office operations, yet existing tools often fail to address the dynamic interplay between patient flow, resource allocation, and regulatory constraints. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform to model and improve decision-making in medical office management. By integrating real-world data from electronic health records (EHRs), appointment scheduling systems, and staff productivity metrics, we aim to create a multi-agent simulation framework that captures the stochastic nature of patient arrivals, provider workflows, and administrative task prioritization. The research will employ parallelized discrete-event simulation techniques to analyze scenarios such as peak-hour patient bottlenecks, emergency visit disruptions, and compliance-driven documentation workflows. Machine learning components will be embedded to predict operational inefficiencies and recommend adaptive staffing models or resource reallocation strategies. Key challenges include scaling simulations to reflect multi-site medical practices and ensuring algorithmic fairness in resource distribution policies. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for medical office administrators, quantitative benchmarks for operational efficiency under varying constraints, and predictive models to mitigate revenue cycle disruptions caused by workflow delays. This work bridges computational systems engineering with healthcare administration, offering a novel methodology to enhance patient throughput, reduce administrative overhead, and maintain compliance in evolving regulatory environments. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling large-scale optimization runs and sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous datasets, which cannot feasibly be executed on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a medical or clinical office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, medical and health care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive analytics framework to optimize credentialing and privileging workflows in healthcare institutions, addressing inefficiencies in Medical Staff Services (MSS) operations. Traditional credentialing processes are labor-intensive, prone to delays, and vulnerable to human error, creating bottlenecks that impact healthcare workforce readiness and institutional compliance. To overcome these challenges, we propose a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to automate the extraction, validation, and risk assessment of practitioner credentials from heterogeneous data sources (e.g., licensure records, malpractice claims, peer references). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training large-scale language models on sensitive, unstructured text data (CVs, accreditation documents, legal transcripts) and constructing dynamic knowledge graphs mapping practitioner competencies, institutional requirements, and regulatory constraints. The pipeline will include federated learning to preserve data privacy across collaborating healthcare systems while enabling model refinement. Anticipated outcomes include a real-time decision support tool that reduces credentialing cycle times by ≥40%, identifies high-risk privileging scenarios with >90% precision, and dynamically aligns staffing resources with evolving care standards. By leveraging HPC to process multi-modal datasets at scale, this work bridges gaps between healthcare administration, regulatory informatics, and computational ethics—advancing a novel, technology-driven paradigm for MSS operations. The resulting open-source framework will be validated against retrospective data from three academic medical centers, with benchmarks shared publicly to inform standards for AI-augmented healthcare workforce management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform credentialing, privileging, personnel management, and accreditation compliance services for hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in medical staff organization and management, medical terminology, credentialing and re-credentialing, health care accreditation and regulatory standards, health care law, meeting and negotiation management, and office information systems management.

abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in urban environments has strained traditional spectrum allocation frameworks, which rely on static frequency assignments ill-suited to dynamic, high-density networks. This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing real-time spectrum utilization for IoT ecosystems in smart cities by developing a machine learning-driven dynamic spectrum access (DSA) system. Current approaches fail to account for the spatiotemporal variability of urban RF environments, leading to inefficient bandwidth use, increased interference, and latency. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for modeling device interactions with reinforcement learning (RL) agents trained to make decentralized spectrum allocation decisions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate city-scale IoT networks incorporating 50,000+ heterogeneous devices, urban topography data, and real-world spectrum occupancy patterns. Key computational challenges include parallelizing millions of concurrent channel state evaluations, optimizing GNN training across distributed GPU nodes, and validating system performance under realistic interference scenarios. The project will develop novel metrics for spectral efficiency in dense urban environments and establish an open-source simulation toolkit for next-generation DSA research. Successful implementation is expected to yield a 30-50% improvement in aggregate network throughput compared to existing contention-based protocols while maintaining sub-ms latency thresholds required for time-sensitive IoT applications. This work bridges gaps between wireless networking, machine learning, and urban informatics, offering a foundation for scalable spectrum management strategies as cities transition to 5G/6G infrastructures. Outcomes will directly inform smart city policymakers and telecommunications standards bodies seeking sustainable solutions for spectrum scarcity.
cip_title: Computer Systems Networking and Telecommunications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer systems networking and telecommunications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics and philological analysis of understudied East Asian languages, with a focus on syntactic variation in pre-modern Sino-Tibetan texts and dialectal divergence in regional forms of Japanese and Korean. A central challenge in analyzing these languages lies in processing large, heterogeneous corpora spanning centuries, including classical manuscripts, vernacular records, and oral tradition transcriptions, which require computationally intensive methods to model linguistic evolution and contact phenomena. The proposed work will employ neural language models trained on curated historical and contemporary datasets to identify morphosyntactic shifts, contact-induced changes, and sociolinguistic patterns. Key computational tasks include graph-based parsing of Classical Chinese texts with embedded vernacular annotations, transformer-driven dialect classification for Japanese Kyūshū variants, and probabilistic alignment of Middle Korean lexical borrowings. These methods demand parallelized processing of terabyte-scale textual data and GPU-accelerated model training, necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access database of annotated syntactic trees for 50+ pre-modern Sino-Tibetan texts, 2) dialect maps quantifying phonetic and lexical divergence across 20 Japanese and Korean regional varieties, and 3) comparative analyses of grammaticalization pathways in contact zones. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this project aims to address critical gaps in understanding language change dynamics while developing reusable pipelines for low-resource historical linguistics. The resource allocation will directly support scalable text processing, reduce training bottlenecks for deep learning architectures, and enable reproducible large-scale comparisons across time periods and geographic regions—advancing both theoretical frameworks in East Asian linguistics and applied tools for digital humanities scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: East Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the languages of East Asia, including, but not limited to, the Sino-Tibetan, Japanese, and Korean languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of digital platforms in shaping transnational cultural identities among diasporic communities, with a focus on understudied groups in South Asia and East Africa. The research problem centers on how geographically dispersed communities negotiate cultural preservation and adaptation in digitally mediated spaces, particularly amid globalization and shifting sociopolitical dynamics. Existing studies often rely on small-scale qualitative data, limiting insights into large-scale patterns of cultural exchange, hybridity, or conflict. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods computational approach combining multilingual natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and geospatial modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing terabytes of social media data, archival digital texts, and multimedia content across multiple languages (e.g., Swahili, Tamil, Gujarati) and platforms (e.g., community forums, encrypted messaging apps). Custom transformer models will be trained to detect cultural narratives, symbols, and identity markers while preserving contextual nuance. Dynamic network analysis will map evolving community structures and cross-group interactions over a 15-year span. The computational pipeline requires parallelized workflows for data ingestion, GPU-accelerated model training, and real-time visualization of multidimensional cultural dynamics. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for analyzing transnational identity formation at scale, with applications for policymakers and cultural organizations working to support marginalized communities. This work will advance methodological innovation in computational cultural studies by addressing challenges in multilingual, multimodal data integration while providing empirical evidence of how digital infrastructures both sustain and transform collective identities. The requested resources will enable processing speeds and data volumes unattainable with local computing infrastructure, ensuring robust statistical validity and temporal granularity.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of real-time, AI-driven animation systems for immersive storytelling in interactive media. The growing demand for hyperrealistic visual effects (VFX) and responsive virtual environments in entertainment, virtual production, and simulation-based training necessitates computational workflows that exceed the capabilities of standard desktop systems. Current bottlenecks include rendering latency in complex 3D scenes, training generative models for procedural animation, and simulating physics-based interactions at scale. To address these challenges, the research will utilize GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines via Unreal Engine 5 and Unity, coupled with distributed machine learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) to train neural networks for automated lip-syncing, character motion synthesis, and dynamic texture generation. Custom CUDA kernels will be developed to optimize particle-based simulations for fire, fluid, and debris effects, which are critical for disaster preparedness training modules being co-developed with journalism collaborators. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of multi-camera volumetric capture datasets (up to 16 synchronized 8K streams) for light-field reconstruction, reducing preprocessing time from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include: 1) an open-source toolkit for latency-critical animation tasks in extended reality (XR) environments, 2) novel methods for integrating AI-generated assets into real-time compositing workflows, and 3) benchmark data on energy-efficient rendering configurations for GPU clusters. This work directly supports the program’s mission to bridge technical innovation with communication arts, offering students and industry partners scalable solutions for next-generation media production while advancing scholarly understanding of computational creativity in non-stem domains.
cip_title: Animation, Interactive Technology, Video Graphics, and Special Effects
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use computer applications and related visual and sound imaging techniques to manipulate images and information originating as film, video, still photographs, digital copy, soundtracks, and physical objects in order to communicate messages simulating real-world content. Includes instruction in specialized camerawork and equipment operation and maintenance, image capture, computer programming, dubbing, CAD applications, and applications to specific commercial, industrial, and entertainment needs.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the relationship between digital writing environments and compositional practices using computational text analysis and visualization methods. While existing scholarship in rhetoric and composition has qualitatively examined how digital platforms shape writing processes, the scale of available digital writing artifacts—including multimodal drafts, revision histories, and peer feedback exchanges in online learning management systems—exceeds the analytical capacity of manual humanistic methods. Our interdisciplinary team proposes to apply natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to a corpus of 250,000 anonymized student writing artifacts (totaling ~75 million tokens) drawn from 15 years of first-year composition courses. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement a three-phase analysis: (1) cluster analysis of syntactic patterns and rhetorical moves across genres and assignment types, (2) network analysis of citation practices and intertextual connections in argumentative essays, and (3) longitudinal modeling of stylistic changes in student writing correlated with platform migration (from traditional word processors to collaborative web-based editors). The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated transformers for latent semantic analysis and distributed computing frameworks for processing heterogeneous file formats (text, HTML, Markdown). Expected outcomes include new models for understanding how digital writing infrastructures influence rhetorical development, visualizations of large-scale compositional trends, and open-source tools for corpus-based writing studies. This research directly addresses gaps in empirical approaches to digital writing pedagogy while demonstrating how computational humanities methods can advance core questions in rhetoric and composition studies. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impractical on standard academic computing infrastructure, particularly for training custom NLP models on mixed-genre composition corpora.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the humanistic and scientific study of rhetoric, composition, literacy, and language/linguistic theories and their practical and pedagogical applications. Includes instruction in historical and contemporary rhetoric/composition theories; composition and criticism of written, visual, and mixed-media texts; analysis of literacy practices in cultural and cross-cultural contexts; and writing program administration.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of high-fidelity 3-D modeling and simulation workflows in industrial design and advanced manufacturing. While 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), additive manufacturing, and 3-D scanning technologies have transformed prototyping and production, current workflows struggle to efficiently process large-scale, multi-physics models—particularly those involving complex geometries, material behaviors, or real-time optimization. The research aims to develop a scalable computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these limitations. Central to this effort is the implementation of parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters, enabling rapid simulation of stress distribution, thermal effects, and fluid-structure interactions in intricate 3-D models. Additionally, the project will integrate machine learning algorithms to automate topology optimization and defect detection in 3-D printed components, using HPC resources to train models on terabyte-scale datasets of scanned industrial parts. A key innovation involves developing hybrid CPU-GPU pipelines for real-time processing of high-resolution 3-D scan data into simulation-ready meshes, reducing preprocessing bottlenecks. The computational workflows will be validated through case studies in aerospace component design and architectural structural modeling, comparing HPC-accelerated results against physical prototype testing. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in simulation time for multi-phase design problems, enabling iterative optimization of manufacturable models with fewer physical trials. The resource request supports both algorithm development and large-scale benchmarking, with all tools to be released as open-source plugins for major CAD platforms. By democratizing access to HPC-driven 3-D modeling, this work aims to bridge gaps between academic research and industrial applications while establishing best practices for computational resource allocation in next-generation digital manufacturing curricula.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the use of three-dimensional (3-D) computer technology to create technical illustrations and models used in manufacturing, design, production, and construction. Includes instruction in 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), 3-D printing, 3-D model design and construction, and 3-D scanning.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a dynamic resource allocation framework for decentralized engineering systems operating under uncertainty, with applications in large-scale infrastructure resilience planning. Traditional resource allocation models often assume centralized decision-making or static environments, limiting their applicability to modern engineering systems characterized by distributed stakeholders, real-time data streams, and competing operational priorities. The proposed work integrates agent-based modeling, constrained optimization, and machine learning techniques to address the computational challenges of multi-objective resource coordination across interdependent subsystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be employed to simulate complex network interactions at urban scale, optimize allocation policies through evolutionary algorithms, and train surrogate models that balance technical requirements with organizational constraints. The computational methodology combines discrete-event simulation for infrastructure behavior, graph neural networks for dependency modeling, and multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive policy generation. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework capable of processing heterogeneous datasets (sensor networks, maintenance logs, economic indicators) to recommend resource distribution strategies that minimize systemic risk while satisfying budgetary and regulatory constraints. This research will advance engineering management practices by providing quantitative tools for scenario analysis in critical infrastructure sectors, particularly for regions facing compounded stressors from climate change and rapid urbanization. The HPC implementation will leverage parallel processing architectures to handle combinatorial optimization spaces inherent to systems with >10^4 decision variables, enabling runtime efficiencies unachievable through conventional computing resources. Results will be benchmarked against historical infrastructure failure cases, with potential applications in public-private partnership governance and adaptive capacity planning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of management and administration principles to engineering systems and applications. Includes instruction in resource allocation theory, control theory, statistical analysis, business management and administration, and applications to specific engineering research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of efficient geothermal energy systems by addressing critical challenges in modeling subsurface thermal-hydraulic-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes. Geothermal reservoirs are inherently complex, with heterogeneous geological properties and dynamic interactions between fluids, heat, and rock formations. Current simulation tools often simplify these multi-physics phenomena, leading to uncertainties in predicting long-term reservoir performance, optimal well placement, and heat extraction rates. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate coupled THMC processes at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales. The research will employ finite element methods with adaptive mesh refinement to resolve fine-scale fractures and permeability variations, integrated with machine learning algorithms to calibrate model parameters using field data from existing geothermal sites. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational demands of 3D multiphase simulations, which involve solving nonlinear partial differential equations across millions of grid cells and iterative optimization workflows. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation platform capable of optimizing geothermal system design, reducing drilling risks, and improving energy extraction efficiency by 20-30% compared to conventional methods. This work will directly support the development of enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) in low-permeability regions, contributing to scalable, renewable energy solutions. By providing predictive tools for reservoir management, the project aims to lower operational costs and accelerate the adoption of geothermal technology, aligning with global decarbonization goals. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sensitivity studies, uncertainty quantification, and large-scale scenario testing, which are infeasible with current institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and real-time environmental simulations in architectural design processes.
