The research addresses a critical gap in current computational design methodologies, which often prioritize formal or aesthetic outcomes over dynamic, context-sensitive performance metrics. By developing a novel framework that combines generative adversarial networks (GANs), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and agent-based pedestrian movement modeling, the project aims to create adaptive design systems capable of iteratively optimizing architectural proposals for energy efficiency, thermal comfort, and spatial circulation in dense urban contexts. The computational workflow will process multi-scale datasets, including high-resolution LiDAR scans of existing urban fabric, historical climate data, and real-time sensor inputs from IoT networks, to generate and evaluate thousands of design permutations. This requires parallel processing of complex 3D geometry operations, coupled with machine learning model training on heterogeneous urban datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for performance-driven architectural design, validated through case studies in three climatically distinct cities. The research contributes to emerging paradigms in computational architecture by bridging gaps between generative design, environmental simulation, and human behavior modeling—advancing both methodological innovation and practical applications for sustainable urban development. Successful implementation of this framework could significantly reduce the computational barriers currently limiting holistic performance-based design approaches in architectural practice and education.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of architecture, cities, landscapes, designed objects, ornament, architectural photography, and material culture in diverse places and time periods, and the social and aesthetic dimensions of contemporary architecture, landscapes, and cities, emphasizing issues of sustainable environments, new forms of urbanism, and the use of digital media for visualization and analysis. Includes instruction in the fundamentals of architecture, design, environmental and sustainability studies, historic preservation, landscape architecture, studio art, and urban affairs and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational frameworks to model emergent properties in complex biological networks, with a focus on systems-level interactions that cannot be adequately captured by reductionist experimental approaches. A critical challenge in computational biology is the integration of multi-omics datasets (e.g., transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic) into predictive models that account for nonlinear dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and stochasticity in cellular systems. Current tools struggle with scalability and parameter estimation for large-scale networks, limiting their utility in uncovering system-wide regulatory mechanisms. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining stochastic differential equation (SDE) modeling, agent-based simulations, and machine learning (ML)-driven parameter optimization. The SDE framework will model global biochemical reaction networks, while agent-based methods will simulate spatially resolved cellular microenvironments. ML algorithms, including variational autoencoders and Bayesian neural networks, will enable efficient parameter inference from noisy, high-dimensional datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational complexity: stochastic simulations across parameter spaces will require parallelized workflows on GPU-accelerated nodes, and ML training will leverage distributed computing for hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for scalable, multi-scale biological network modeling, (2) novel insights into feedback mechanisms driving metabolic adaptation in stress-response pathways, and (3) a publicly accessible database of pre-trained ML models for parameter estimation in diverse biological contexts. This work will advance computational methodologies for systems biology, providing a foundation for predicting emergent behaviors in synthetic biology applications and disease states. The requested HPC allocation will directly support large-scale simulations (>10^6 CPU core-hours), distributed data storage for petabyte-scale outputs, and real-time analytics pipelines to iteratively refine models against experimental data from collaborating labs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computational theoretical approaches to understanding biological systems, including computational models of biological processes, computational management of large-scale projects, database development and data-algorithm development, and high-performance computing, as well as statistical and mathematical analyses.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of novel ceramic materials and glazes through predictive modeling and simulation, addressing a critical gap in the empirical trial-and-error methods that dominate ceramic arts. Traditional approaches to formulating glazes and optimizing kiln firing conditions are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited by the physical constraints of material experimentation. By integrating computational chemistry, thermodynamics, and machine learning, this research aims to simulate the molecular behavior of clay bodies and glaze components under varying thermal and atmospheric conditions. Key objectives include modeling phase transitions in crystalline glazes, predicting crack propagation in clay substrates during drying and firing, and optimizing kiln temperature profiles for energy efficiency and artistic outcomes. Finite element analysis (FEA) will be employed to simulate thermal stress distributions in ceramic structures, while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will explore interactions between organic additives and inorganic glaze matrices. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on datasets of historical and contemporary ceramic artworks to propose innovative texture and color combinations. The computational workflows will be validated through parallel physical experiments, with iterative feedback loops refining model accuracy. Expected outcomes include open-access databases of simulated glaze properties, predictive tools for reducing material waste in studio practice, and new methods for replicating historical ceramic techniques with modern sustainability standards. By bridging computational science and ceramic arts, this project aims to establish a framework for data-driven artistic innovation while preserving craft traditions, ultimately expanding the technical and expressive possibilities of the medium.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by producing art works out of clay and similar materials. Includes instruction in handbuilt and wheel thrown techniques; molding; slips and glazes; trimming and decorating; firing and kiln operation; oxidation; mixed media; ceramic murals; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational models for optimizing next-generation wireless communication systems under energy efficiency constraints, a critical challenge in expanding IoT and 5G/6G networks. Current designs struggle to balance high data rates, low latency, and minimal power consumption, particularly in dense urban environments with dynamic interference patterns. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and analyze multi-antenna beamforming techniques, adaptive modulation schemes, and distributed network protocols at scale. Computational workflows will integrate finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for electromagnetic wave propagation, machine learning-driven optimization of antenna array configurations, and Monte Carlo-based reliability testing of error-correction algorithms under stochastic channel conditions. These tasks require parallelized processing of large parameter spaces, including terrain data, user mobility patterns, and real-time spectral occupancy—a computational burden exceeding the capacity of local workstations. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of hybrid analog-digital beamforming architectures and decentralized resource allocation strategies, targeting a 30-50% reduction in power consumption compared to conventional OFDM-based systems. Outcomes will include open-source simulation frameworks for energy-aware protocol design and empirically validated guidelines for deploying reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in heterogeneous networks. This work aligns with the program’s focus on applied engineering solutions, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-aided prototyping while advancing industrial capabilities for sustainable communication infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops and collaborations with regional telecom partners, bridging academic research and practical implementation challenges.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronic, and Communications Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of electrical, electronics and communication engineers. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, prototype development and testing, systems analysis and testing, systems maintenance, instrument calibration, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of computational aesthetics, generative design, and immersive media within the visual arts. The central challenge lies in developing and refining algorithms capable of simulating complex, dynamic visual systems while maintaining artistic intent and procedural nuance. Current limitations in processing power restrict the scale and fidelity of such simulations, particularly when integrating real-time interactivity, high-resolution 3D rendering, or machine learning-driven generative models. To address this, the research will employ parallelized rendering pipelines, neural network training on large-scale visual datasets, and agent-based modeling of emergent aesthetic patterns. Key computational tasks include optimizing physics-based simulations for material interactions in digital sculpture, accelerating frame generation for experimental animation sequences, and enabling iterative design processes through GPU-accelerated evolutionary algorithms. The project will utilize containerized workflows to manage dependencies across creative coding environments like TouchDesigner and Unity, alongside custom Python frameworks for parametric design exploration. Expected outcomes include new methods for artist-guided generative AI in procedural content creation, enhanced tools for real-time collaborative visualization in augmented reality environments, and scalable architectures for preserving computational reproducibility in digital art practices. By bridging the gap between artistic experimentation and advanced computing capabilities, this work aims to establish best practices for resource-intensive creative research while contributing open-source tools to the media arts community. The requested HPC allocation will directly support GPU-dependent processes that exceed local workstation capacities, including multi-node rendering tasks and distributed training of diffusion models on curated visual corpora spanning historical art movements and contemporary digital aesthetics.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the visual and performing arts and that may prepare individuals in any of the visual artistic media or performing disciplines.

abstract: Urban environments are complex systems where socio-economic dynamics, infrastructure networks, and land use policies intersect, yet traditional planning tools often struggle to model these interdependencies at scale. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate the long-term impacts of zoning reforms and transportation investments on neighborhood equity and environmental resilience. The research focuses on mid-sized cities undergoing rapid growth, where outdated master plans risk exacerbating displacement, congestion, and climate vulnerabilities. By integrating agent-based modeling, geospatial machine learning, and discrete event simulation, the computational approach will analyze terabyte-scale datasets spanning property records, transit patterns, climate projections, and community survey responses. Key innovations include adaptive algorithms to simulate resident decision-making under policy scenarios and network analysis tools to quantify cascading infrastructure stresses. The HPC environment is critical for running thousands of parallelized simulations that account for stochastic variables in population growth and resource constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model to assess trade-offs between infill development, green space preservation, and affordable housing mandates, with open-source code repositories for public-sector adaptation. This work fills a methodological gap in data-driven participatory planning by creating scalable tools to visualize policy impacts across decadal timescales—a capability absent in current commercial urban planning software. Results will directly inform three ongoing municipal corridor redevelopment initiatives, demonstrating how computational social science methods can bridge technical planning analyses and community-driven governance frameworks. The resource request prioritizes GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory instances to process 3D urban morphology datasets, enabling previously infeasible granularity in simulating built-environment transitions.
detailed_field: City/ urban, community, and regional planning
cip_title: City/ Urban, Community, and Regional Planning
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of planning, analysis, and architecture to the development and improvement of urban areas and surrounding regions, and to function as professional planners. Includes instruction in principles of architecture; master plan development; service, communications, and transportation systems design; community and commercial development; zoning; land use planning; applied economics; policy analysis; applicable laws and regulations; and professional responsibilities and managerial duties.

abstract: Forensic chemistry faces growing demands to analyze increasingly complex evidentiary materials, such as synthetic drugs, environmental toxins, and trace residues, where traditional methods encounter limitations in resolution, speed, and predictive capability. This project proposes the development of computational models to enhance the interpretation of chemical data from forensic casework, supported by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on two interconnected challenges: (1) elucidating degradation pathways of forensic analytes in variable environmental conditions and (2) improving the identification of novel psychoactive substances (NPS) in complex mixtures. Molecular dynamics simulations will model the stability and decomposition kinetics of target compounds, integrating solvent effects and temperature gradients observed in real-world evidence. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will be trained on multidimensional spectral datasets (e.g., GC-MS, LC-QTOF) to classify NPS analogs and resolve overlapping chromatographic peaks. Quantum chemical calculations will supplement these efforts by predicting NMR and IR spectra for emerging synthetic compounds lacking reference standards. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from controlled degradation studies and casework samples. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish predictive frameworks that reduce reliance on physical reference materials and accelerate the interpretation of challenging forensic evidence. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for spectral matching uncertainty quantification and a database of simulated degradation products for priority analytes. These resources will strengthen the scientific basis of forensic conclusions, particularly in cases involving rapidly evolving drug markets or environmentally degraded evidence, while addressing critical needs for reproducibility and efficiency in forensic laboratories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical techniques and instrumentation to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence to aid in criminal investigations. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; biochemistry; forensic toxicology; instrumental analysis; crime scene processing; criminal investigation; forensic laboratory technology; and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a data-driven framework for optimizing operational efficiency and customer experience in full-service dining environments. While food service management has historically relied on qualitative practices, emerging challenges—such as dynamic staffing needs, real-time inventory coordination, and personalized guest interactions—require computational approaches to model complex, interdependent variables. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, predictive tools to address inefficiencies in table turnover rates, staff-task allocation, and menu customization under fluctuating demand. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid computational architecture integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and discrete-event simulation (DES) to analyze multi-modal datasets from real-world dining operations. The ABM component will simulate guest behavior, server workflows, and kitchen processes, while ML algorithms trained on historical transaction data will predict peak demand intervals and ingredient usage patterns. DES will model spatial dynamics of dining room layouts to evaluate table configurations and traffic flow bottlenecks. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations across thousands of parametrized scenarios, including seasonal menu changes, staff skill variability, and unexpected disruptions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for restaurant managers to dynamically adjust staffing levels, reduce food waste through predictive inventory models, and personalize service pacing based on real-time guest analytics. By quantifying traditionally subjective aspects of hospitality—such as the relationship between server-guest interaction timing and perceived service quality—this work establishes a novel computational paradigm for the food service industry. The project’s interdisciplinary integration of operations research, behavioral analytics, and hospitality management fills a specialized niche in non-STEM computational applications, offering scalable solutions for an industry underrepresented in high-performance computing research.
cip_title: Food Service, Waiter/Waitress, and Dining Room Management/Manager.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve food to customers in formal or informal settings.  Includes instruction in the nutritional, sensory, and functional properties of food and its ingredients; food services principles; table and counter services; dining room operations and procedures; service personnel supervision and management; communication skills; business math; safety; and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance three-dimensional structural analyses of cellular and tissue dynamics in musculoskeletal systems, with a focus on age-related degenerative changes. A central challenge in anatomical research is resolving how spatial organization and mechanical interactions at cellular and subcellular scales influence tissue-scale function and pathology. Traditional imaging and biomechanical models often lack the resolution or computational capacity to integrate multiscale data, limiting insights into mechanisms driving conditions such as sarcopenia or osteoarthritis. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework combining large-scale electron microscopy datasets, agent-based modeling, and finite element simulations. High-resolution volumetric imaging of muscle and joint tissues from murine models will generate terabytes of structural data, capturing cellular architectures, extracellular matrix organization, and organelle distributions. These datasets will inform agent-based models simulating cellular responses to mechanical stress, while finite element analyses will predict tissue-level strain patterns under physiological loads. HPC resources are critical for managing data storage, parallel processing of multiscale simulations, and machine learning-driven segmentation of complex tissue features. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking subcellular alterations (e.g., mitochondrial displacement, cytoskeletal rearrangements) to tissue mechanical failure in aging, (2) identification of structural biomarkers preceding macroscopic degeneration, and (3) open-source tools for automated analysis of anatomical ultrastructure. By enabling integration of cellular-scale dynamics with organ-level biomechanics, this work will provide foundational insights into anatomical adaptations during aging while establishing computational workflows for hypothesis-driven exploration of tissue pathophysiology. The requested resources will directly support time-sensitive simulations requiring >10,000 core-hours and GPU-accelerated deep learning pipelines for image processing, advancing anatomical discovery through scalable, data-intensive computational approaches.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of organ systems, tissue structures, and whole bodies together with their cellular and structural components and dynamics. Includes instruction in cell biology and histology, structural biology, molecular mechanics, regional and gross anatomy, embryology, neuroanatomy, endocrinology and secretory dynamics, and applications to such topics as aging and disease conditions.

abstract: Agricultural machinery systems are increasingly complex, integrating mechanical, hydraulic, electrical, and digital components to meet demands for precision and efficiency. However, optimizing the performance and reliability of these systems under diverse field conditions remains a critical challenge. Current empirical testing approaches are resource-intensive, limited in scalability, and unable to fully capture dynamic interactions between subsystems or environmental variables. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and simulate multifactorial stressors on agricultural equipment, with a focus on sprayers, harvesters, and autonomous field robots. Multiphysics models will integrate structural mechanics, fluid dynamics (for hydraulic and pesticide delivery systems), and thermal-electrical coupling in powertrains, parameterized using field data from sensor-equipped machinery. Machine learning methods will be applied to identify failure-prone design features, predict wear patterns under varying soil and crop conditions, and optimize maintenance schedules. HPC resources are essential to resolve high-fidelity simulations of multi-component interactions at operational timescales, train predictive models on heterogeneous sensor datasets, and perform sensitivity analyses across thousands of operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) validated digital twins for key equipment categories, enabling virtual testing of design modifications, (2) predictive maintenance algorithms to reduce downtime, and (3) actionable insights for improving component durability and energy efficiency. By transitioning equipment optimization from trial-and-error to computational workflows, this research will directly support the development of robust, sustainable agricultural machinery tailored to evolving operational demands, benefiting equipment manufacturers, farm operators, and extension services.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural Mechanics and Equipment/ Machine Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to maintain and repair specialized farm, ranch, and agribusiness power equipment and vehicles. Includes instruction in the principles of diesel, combustion, electrical, steam, hydraulic, and mechanical systems and their application to the maintenance of terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying equipment; tractors and hauling equipment; planting and harvesting equipment; cutting equipment; power sources and systems for silos; irrigation and pumping equipment; dairy, feeding, and shearing operations; and processing systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance molecular-scale modeling of biopharmaceutical processes and biomolecular systems central to chemical and biomolecular engineering. A critical challenge in this field lies in predicting and optimizing the behavior of complex biological molecules (e.g., enzymes, engineered proteins, lipid nanoparticles) within industrially relevant environments, such as bioreactors or drug delivery systems. Traditional experimental approaches are often limited in resolving dynamic molecular interactions under process conditions, while existing computational models struggle to balance atomic-level fidelity with the timescales and system sizes required for practical insights. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enhanced sampling techniques, and machine learning-driven parameterization. Key focus areas include (1) elucidating solvent-mediated conformational changes in therapeutic proteins during downstream purification, (2) optimizing enzyme-substrate binding energetics for metabolic engineering applications, and (3) modeling self-assembly dynamics of lipid-based drug carriers under varying thermodynamic conditions. The HPC resources will enable simulations spanning microsecond timescales for systems exceeding 1 million atoms, coupled with high-throughput screening of bioprocess variables. Expected outcomes include predictive models for biocatalyst stability in industrial reactors, design principles for next-generation biomaterials with tailored release kinetics, and fundamental insights into molecular driving forces governing biopharmaceutical manufacturability. By bridging molecular-level phenomena with process-scale engineering requirements, this work aims to accelerate the development of sustainable biomanufacturing platforms and precision therapeutic delivery systems. The computational datasets and protocols generated will be disseminated as open-source tools to advance research capabilities at the intersection of molecular biotechnology and chemical process engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems at the interface of chemical engineering and biology, with an emphasis at the molecular level, such as biopharmaceutical processes, protein engineering, metabolic engineering, gene therapy, biomaterials, cell and tissue engineering, and drug delivery. Includes instruction in chemical engineering, thermodynamics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, momentum and heat transfer, cellular and molecular biotechnology, process design, and chemical reactor design.

abstract: The biological effects of ionizing radiation arise from complex molecular interactions that drive DNA damage, protein dysfunction, and cellular repair processes. Current gaps in understanding the precise biophysical mechanisms of radiation-induced damage at the atomic and molecular levels limit the development of targeted radioprotective strategies and precision radiotherapies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model radiation-induced perturbations in critical biomolecular systems, with a focus on DNA-protein interactions and repair enzyme dynamics. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating quantum mechanical (QM) simulations of radiation-induced ionization events, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of DNA damage recognition by repair proteins, and kinetic modeling of repair pathway activation. QM simulations will quantify ionization cross-sections and radical formation in DNA backbone components and associated water molecules, providing energetics for parametrizing coarse-grained MD models. Large-scale MD simulations will then track the structural dynamics of DNA repair complexes (e.g., base excision repair glycosylases) as they recognize and process radiation-induced lesions under varying ionization densities. Parallelized kinetic Monte Carlo methods will model the competition between lesion accumulation and repair kinetics in simulated chromatin environments. These simulations require HPC resources due to the femtosecond-scale resolution needed for QM accuracy, microsecond-scale MD trajectories for conformational sampling, and the combinatorial complexity of lesion-repairer interactions across biologically relevant timescales. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how radiation quality (e.g., linear energy transfer) influences lesion complexity and repair fidelity, as well as predictive models linking molecular-scale damage to cellular survival curves. This work will advance radiobiology by establishing a computational framework to dissect the biophysical determinants of radiation toxicity, with implications for optimizing therapeutic radiation regimens and mitigating off-target effects in healthy tissues.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the effects of radiation on organisms and biological systems. Includes instruction in particle physics, ionization, and biophysics of radiation perturbations, cellular and organismic repair systems, genetic and pathological effects of radiation, and the measurement of radiation dosages.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, culturally responsive pedagogical tools for K-12 multilingual classrooms. Despite growing linguistic and cultural diversity in schools, many digital learning platforms lack the capacity to dynamically address the intersectional needs of students from non-dominant cultural backgrounds. Current approaches to analyzing classroom interaction data or modeling personalized learning pathways remain limited by conventional computational tools, which struggle to process multimodal datasets (e.g., speech, text, gesture) while accounting for sociocultural variables. Our research employs natural language processing (NLP) and agent-based modeling to simulate and optimize culturally sustaining instructional strategies. Computational workflows will integrate multilingual student discourse data from ESL classrooms, demographic and performance metrics, and ethnographic observations to train deep learning models that predict engagement patterns across cultural subgroups. Concurrently, HPC-enabled simulations will test the efficacy of hypothetical interventions—such as code-switching supports or culturally contextualized problem scenarios—in virtual classroom environments. This dual approach addresses critical gaps in scaling qualitative insights about cultural dynamics into actionable, system-level pedagogical frameworks. The anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating adaptive lesson plans responsive to students’ cultural funds of knowledge and linguistic repertoires, as well as a validated simulation framework for pre-service teacher training. By enabling large-scale analysis of cross-cultural educational interactions, this work aims to reduce persistent disparities in learning outcomes while providing teacher education programs with evidence-based computational methods to design inclusive curricula. The requested resources are essential for processing terabytes of audiovisual classroom data and iterating complex, culturally parameterized models within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, and implementation of instructional and advising services for culturally diverse learning populations. Includes instruction in cultural diversity, at-risk populations, multilingual and ESL education, program and curriculum design, instructional technology, information resources, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling and communicating with multicultural populations, law and regulations, and applications to specific cultural groups, educational services, and research issues.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing next-generation telecommunications networks, particularly in dense urban environments where high user density and heterogeneous devices strain existing infrastructure. Current network management strategies struggle to balance real-time demand fluctuations, dynamic resource allocation, and energy efficiency while maintaining low latency for applications like augmented reality and IoT-enabled systems. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate scalable machine learning models for adaptive network slicing in 5G/6G environments. The computational workflow will involve large-scale simulations of multi-tenant network architectures using discrete-event modeling and parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess traffic patterns across varying spatial-temporal conditions. Additionally, we will train graph neural networks (GNNs) on synthetic and real-world datasets to predict optimal resource distribution across virtualized network slices, incorporating constraints from quality-of-service metrics and energy consumption profiles. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of digital signal processing pipelines for interference mitigation in millimeter-wave bands, utilizing GPU-accelerated Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) implementations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for dynamic spectrum sharing, optimized beamforming configurations, and energy-aware routing protocols that reduce baseline power consumption by 18-22% in simulated scenarios. These results will provide actionable insights for telecom operators deploying software-defined networks and contribute open-source tools for stochastic network modeling. By bridging algorithmic innovation with practical deployment constraints, this work aims to advance the scalability and sustainability of urban telecommunications infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to help design and implement telecommunications systems. Includes instruction in communications protocol, data networking, digital compression algorithms, digital signal processing, Internet access, object-oriented and relational databases, and programming languages.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing institutional decision-making in community college administration. Community colleges face dynamic challenges, including fluctuating enrollment patterns, funding constraints, and equity gaps in student outcomes. Traditional analytical approaches often fail to account for the complexity of these interrelated factors or the speed at which institutional conditions change. This research proposes a computational framework to simulate enrollment trends, resource allocation scenarios, and student success pathways under varying policy and financial conditions. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets from multiple institutions—including enrollment records, course completion rates, and budget allocations—we will train machine learning models to identify critical predictors of student retention and program viability. Agent-based modeling will simulate how administrative decisions (e.g., staffing adjustments, facility investments, or curriculum revisions) propagate through institutional systems. Monte Carlo methods will assess financial and operational risks under uncertainty, such as state funding volatility or demographic shifts. The scale of these analyses, involving millions of data points and thousands of concurrent simulations, necessitates HPC capabilities to reduce processing time from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for community college leaders to evaluate policy trade-offs, forecast enrollment impacts, and prioritize interventions that align with equity goals. This work will advance the application of computational social science in higher education administration, offering empirically grounded strategies to enhance institutional resilience. By integrating large-scale data analytics with organizational theory, the project aims to bridge a critical gap in community college research: the ability to rapidly model complex, real-world administrative dilemmas while centering student success and fiscal sustainability.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of administering community and junior colleges and related postsecondary systems, the study of community and junior colleges as objects of applied research, and that may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in community and junior college finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; student services; research on community and junior colleges; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: The administration of anesthetic agents is a complex process requiring precise titration to individual patient physiology to optimize efficacy and minimize adverse outcomes. Current protocols rely on population-based guidelines and iterative intraoperative adjustments, which may lead to suboptimal dosing, prolonged recovery times, or perioperative complications. This project proposes to develop a computational framework for personalized anesthesia delivery by integrating patient-specific pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling with machine learning (ML) to predict dynamic drug responses. The research problem centers on the high interpatient variability in drug metabolism and the lack of real-time adaptive systems to guide anesthesiologist assistants (AAs) in clinical decision-making. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the computational demands of this work, which involves large-scale simulations of drug distribution models, Bayesian parameter estimation for PK/PD model calibration, and training deep neural networks on multimodal perioperative datasets (e.g., electronic health records, intraoperative vital signs, and biomarker data). The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification in drug response predictions and to optimize hyperparameters for ensemble ML models. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive tool for real-time anesthetic dosing recommendations based on individual patient characteristics and surgical context, (2) generative models to simulate rare adverse event scenarios for AA training modules, and (3) open-source computational workflows to support clinical translation. This work has the potential to enhance the precision of anesthetic care, reduce postoperative complications, and improve resource utilization in surgical settings. By aligning computational advances with the operational needs of AAs, the project bridges a critical gap between theoretical models and bedside applications, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance evidence-based practices in anesthesia care delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in developing and implementing patient anesthesia care plans, including preoperative, surgical theater, recovery room, and postoperative/intensive care procedures. Includes instruction in patient data collection, catheter insertion, airway management and drug administration, assisting the administration and monitoring of regional and peripheral nerve blockades, support therapy, adjusting anesthetic levels during surgery, interoperative monitoring, postoperative procedures, pain clinics and patient education, and administrative tasks.

abstract: Cytotechnologists play a critical role in early cancer detection by identifying subtle cellular abnormalities in cytological specimens. However, manual microscopic analysis remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability, particularly in borderline or rare cases. This project proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging deep learning to augment cytotechnologists’ diagnostic accuracy and efficiency by automating the detection and classification of cellular anomalies in whole-slide images (WSIs) of gynecologic and non-gynecologic samples. The research addresses a critical gap in computational pathology tools tailored to cytotechnology workflows, which differ fundamentally from histopathology due to the absence of tissue architecture and reliance on dispersed cellular features. We will train convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) on a curated dataset of 25,000 annotated WSIs from diverse clinical sources, including low-prevalence malignancies and pre-malignant states. Computational challenges include managing gigapixel-scale images, class imbalance, and artifact mitigation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for distributed training of multi-resolution models, hyperparameter optimization, and inference pipeline testing. The proposed workflow integrates patch-based feature extraction with global attention mechanisms to prioritize diagnostically relevant regions, mimicking cytotechnologists’ scanning patterns. Success metrics include achieving ≥95% sensitivity for high-grade lesions and reducing false positives in benign reactive changes by 30% compared to existing algorithms. Outcomes will be validated against consensus reviews by certified cytotechnologists and molecular testing results. This project will yield an open-source model deployable in clinical cytology laboratories, directly addressing workforce shortages and diagnostic delays. By bridging computational innovation with cytotechnology practice, this work advances precision in early cancer diagnostics while providing a scalable framework for integrating machine learning into cytology education and quality assurance programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with pathologists to detect changes in body cells that may indicate, and permit diagnosis of, the early development of cancers and other diseases. Includes instruction in biochemistry, microbiology, applied mathematics, microscopy, slide preparation, identification of cellular structures and abnormalities, and laboratory procedures and safety.

abstract: Behavioral disorders in companion animals present complex challenges that often involve interactions between medical, environmental, and neurophysiological factors. Current approaches to diagnosing and treating these disorders rely heavily on observational assessments and generalized behavior modification protocols, which may not account for the heterogeneous biological underpinnings of maladaptive behaviors. This project seeks to advance precision veterinary behavioral medicine by integrating multimodal data—including electronic health records, video-based ethograms, wearable sensor outputs, and genomic biomarkers—to model individualized treatment pathways. The primary research problem centers on disentangling the contributions of medical comorbidities (e.g., chronic pain, endocrine dysfunction) to behavioral presentations while predicting optimal combinations of pharmacotherapy and behavior modification strategies. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework using machine learning architectures trained on longitudinal datasets from 15,000+ clinical cases. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (≥50 TB), including video analyses via convolutional neural networks to quantify subtle behavioral phenotypes and reinforcement learning models to simulate intervention outcomes across diverse virtual patient profiles. Parallelized workflows will enable in silico trials comparing >10,000 therapeutic permutations, while federated learning techniques will preserve data privacy across collaborating veterinary hospitals. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive algorithms to differentiate medically driven behavioral changes from primary psychological disorders, (2) optimized treatment protocols personalized to patient-specific risk factors and owner compliance patterns, and (3) mechanistic models linking neurochemical dynamics to behavior modification efficacy. This work will establish a computational foundation for evidence-based veterinary behavioral medicine, reducing trial-and-error approaches that prolong patient distress. By leveraging HPC capabilities to synthesize multi-scale biological and behavioral data, the project aims to transform clinical decision-making in a field where computational resources have historically been underutilized.
cip_definition: Research on how to understand and treat the behavioral problems of animals, primarily through the application of behavior modification techniques to companion animals; may also involve diagnosis of medical conditions that can affect a pet's behavior, and the use of medication in conjunction with behavior modification therapy.

abstract: The poultry industry faces critical challenges in optimizing production efficiency, disease resistance, and sustainability while meeting growing global protein demands. Current limitations in understanding the complex interactions between avian genetics, gut microbiota dynamics, and nutritional interventions hinder progress. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through advanced genomic and microbiomic modeling. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of poultry breeds with machine learning-driven analyses of gut microbial ecosystems. Using whole-genome sequencing data from broiler and layer populations, we will identify genetic markers linked to disease resilience and feed efficiency. Concurrently, metagenomic datasets from poultry gut microbiomes will be analyzed to model microbial community responses to dietary additives and environmental stressors. These datasets will inform agent-based simulations of host-microbiome interactions under varying nutritional regimes. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallel processing for alignment of terabase-scale sequencing data, Bayesian hierarchical modeling of genotype-phenotype associations, and dynamic flux balance analysis of microbial metabolic networks. By coupling these approaches, we aim to predict optimal genetic selection criteria and feed formulations that maximize growth performance while reducing antibiotic dependence. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the project's data volume (>500 TB raw sequencing data), complex model integration, and iterative simulations across biological scales. Expected outcomes include predictive models for precision poultry nutrition, candidate genes for selective breeding programs, and a computational toolkit for optimizing hatchery environments. This work will provide transformative insights into avian systems biology, directly supporting the development of sustainable poultry production strategies that align with global food security priorities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of poultry animals and the production and handling of poultry products. Includes instruction in avian sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, hatchery design, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in mortuary science by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize embalming processes, which currently rely on empirically derived techniques with limited systematic validation. Traditional embalming practices face challenges in adapting to diverse environmental conditions, variable tissue integrity in postmortem cases, and evolving requirements for culturally or religiously sensitive preparations. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive frameworks to account for dynamic interactions between embalming chemicals, biological tissues, and environmental variables, which can lead to suboptimal preservation outcomes or excessive chemical use. To address this, we propose a computational approach integrating fluid dynamics simulations, machine learning, and multi-scale biochemical modeling. HPC resources will enable the simulation of embalming fluid diffusion through heterogeneous tissue matrices under varying temperatures, humidity levels, and tissue degradation states, calibrated using histological and thanatochemical datasets. Concurrently, machine learning models will analyze historical case data to identify patterns linking embalming efficacy to demographic, pathological, and environmental factors. The integration of these methods aims to generate predictive tools for optimizing fluid formulations and injection protocols, reducing chemical waste, and tailoring approaches to specific religious or cultural requirements (e.g., rapid preparation for Jewish burial or eco-friendly alternatives for natural interment). Expected outcomes include open-access computational models to guide embalmer training and a decision-support system for atypical cases, such as advanced decomposition or mass fatality events. By bridging mortuary science with computational fluid dynamics and data science, this work advances a traditionally practice-driven field into an evidence-based discipline while addressing sustainability and equity in postmortem care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for licensure as embalmers and morticians.  Includes instruction in pathogenic microbiology, systematic pathology, thanatochemistry, gross anatomy, clinical mortuary science, embalming, restorative art, applicable laws and regulations, and special services such as cremation and preparations required by specific religious communities.

abstract: The assembly and functional dynamics of macromolecular complexes involved in cellular energy transduction remain poorly understood due to the transient nature of intermediate states and the complexity of multi-scale interactions. This project seeks to elucidate the structural dynamics and energy transfer mechanisms underlying the assembly of respiratory Complex I and its interaction with electron carriers, a system critical to oxidative phosphorylation. Experimental limitations in resolving real-time conformational changes at atomic resolution necessitate a computational approach. We propose large-scale, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enhanced with free energy calculations to map the conformational landscape of Complex I during electron transfer and proton translocation. These simulations will integrate cryo-EM structural data and experimental kinetic parameters to model transient states, including the formation of ubiquinone-binding intermediates and coupling between electron transport and proton motive force generation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve microsecond-scale sampling of the 1.2-million-atom system, employing hybrid GPU-CPU parallelization in AMBER for force field accuracy. Adaptive sampling and Markov state models will identify metastable states and transition pathways, while QM/MM simulations will characterize redox-driven protonation dynamics at Fe-S clusters. Expected outcomes include a mechanistic framework for how conformational rearrangements in Complex I optimize energy conversion efficiency, with implications for understanding mitochondrial disorders linked to mutations in assembly factors. The project will also establish protocols for simulating large, asymmetric membrane protein complexes, advancing methodological capabilities for studying supramolecular energy transduction systems. By bridging structural data with dynamic functional insights, this work addresses a critical gap in molecular biophysics, offering predictive models to guide targeted biochemical validations and therapeutic interventions.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the dynamics and interactions of macromolecules and other three-dimensional ultrastructures, the architecture of supramolecular structures, and energy transfer in biomolecular systems. Includes instruction in energy transduction, structural dynamics, mechanisms of electron and proton transfer in biological systems, bioinformatics, automated analysis, and specialized research techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in analyzing and simulating complex human movement patterns for choreographic innovation and dance pedagogy. While traditional dance research relies on qualitative observation and manual notation systems, the scale and precision required to model dynamic, multi-dancer interactions in three-dimensional space demand advanced computational resources. The core research problem centers on developing a framework to quantify improvisational dance processes, map biomechanical efficiency across diverse dance styles, and predict emergent group choreographic behaviors in real time. To achieve this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process motion-capture datasets from studio recordings, including high-frequency kinematic data (250 Hz) and synchronized multimedia feeds. Machine learning models—particularly graph neural networks and transformer architectures—will be trained to identify latent movement motifs and simulate their evolution under varying artistic constraints. The computational pipeline will integrate biomechanical simulation via rigid-body dynamics engines with cultural movement analysis parameters specific to underrepresented dance traditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for choreographers to visualize energy expenditure metrics during compositional processes, a probabilistic model of ensemble movement coordination, and a database linking kinematic patterns to ethnographic records of dance practices. By enabling large-scale analysis of movement creativity, this work aims to bridge computational and embodied knowledge in the performing arts while preserving kinetic heritage through digitally augmented methodologies. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive pose estimation tasks, parallelizing agent-based choreographic simulations, and reducing latency in interactive AI-assisted composition tools.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dance, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance precision in large animal surgical and medical interventions through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address high morbidity rates linked to postoperative complications in food animals and equines. Despite advancements in veterinary care, variability in patient outcomes persists due to complex interactions between species-specific anatomy, metabolic demands, and disease pathophysiology. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols, which inadequately account for individual biomechanical, physiological, and genomic factors. To bridge this gap, we propose developing species-specific multiscale models integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for biomechanical stress prediction during surgical procedures, machine learning (ML)-enabled risk stratification using retrospective electronic health records (n > 50,000 cases), and genomic variant analysis to identify biomarkers associated with recovery trajectories. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of high-resolution imaging data (CT/MRI), whole-genome sequencing datasets, and real-time sensor data from wearable monitoring devices deployed in perioperative care. Computational workflows will be optimized using GPU-accelerated frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) for ML model training and ANSYS for FEA simulations. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing surgical planning (e.g., orthopedic implant design in equines, cesarean section protocols in dairy cattle) and personalized analgesia/anesthesia regimens. This work will establish open-access computational pipelines tailored to veterinary applications, directly addressing critical gaps in food animal and equine medicine. By reducing complication rates through data-driven precision, the project aims to improve welfare in production and sport animals while mitigating economic losses linked to prolonged recovery. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the computational burden of multimodal data integration and deliver scalable, translatable solutions for clinical veterinary practice.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Large Animal/ Food Animal and Equine Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of herd, work, sport, and food animals. Includes instruction in equine medicine, swine and dairy medicine, food animal medicine, pathophysiology, large animal diseases, large animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: Ornamental horticulture faces pressing challenges in optimizing plant traits for aesthetic appeal, environmental resilience, and commercial viability under dynamic climatic conditions. This project seeks to advance genomic and phenotypic prediction models for ornamental species by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex datasets spanning genetic, transcriptomic, and environmental variables. The research problem centers on identifying genetic markers and environmental covariates associated with desirable traits—such as flower morphology, pigmentation, disease resistance, and drought tolerance—while overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional datasets. Current methods for trait prediction in ornamental plants rely on limited genomic resources and static statistical models, which fail to account for genotype-by-environment interactions at scale. To address this, we propose an integrative computational framework combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS), machine learning (ML)-based phenotypic prediction, and 3D growth simulations under varying climatic scenarios. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of whole-genome sequencing data from target species (e.g., Rhododendron, Rosa), integration with RNA-Seq datasets to identify expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), and training of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze time-series imagery of plant development. Environmental parameters, including temperature gradients and soil moisture dynamics, will be modeled using climate reanalysis data to simulate stress-response pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for multi-omics data integration in non-model horticultural species, (2) predictive models linking genetic variants to phenotypic plasticity in ornamental traits, and (3) climate-resilient cultivar recommendations tailored to regional growing conditions. This work will directly inform breeding programs to accelerate the development of ornamental varieties with enhanced marketability and reduced resource inputs, supporting sustainable practices in urban landscaping and nursery production. By bridging computational biology and applied horticulture, the project aims to establish a template for data-driven decision-making in specialty crop optimization.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on domesticated plants and plant materials used for decorative and recreational applications and prepares individuals to breed, grow, and utilize ornamental plant varieties for commercial and aesthetic purposes. Includes instruction in applicable plant science subjects, the environmental design and artistic aspects of horticultural product usage, and the management of horticultural operations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of clinical diagnostics, driven by advancements in multi-omics technologies and large-scale biomedical data, necessitates robust computational infrastructure to support research in clinical laboratory science. This project seeks to address critical bottlenecks in analyzing high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiles—to improve the accuracy and efficiency of disease diagnosis and monitoring. Current methods for integrating heterogeneous clinical data often lack scalability, leading to delays in identifying actionable biomarkers and validating laboratory-developed tests (LDTs). To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize machine learning (ML) models capable of processing multi-omics data in real time. Our computational approach will focus on ensemble learning techniques and neural networks to identify patterns across disparate datasets, while parallelized workflows will enable rapid validation of candidate biomarkers against clinical outcomes. Key tasks include the deployment of containerized pipelines for data harmonization, feature selection, and model training, utilizing frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch. Additionally, we will simulate large-scale virtual cohorts to assess the generalizability of diagnostic algorithms across diverse patient populations. The use of HPC will allow iterative refinement of models with minimal latency, ensuring compliance with clinical turnaround time requirements. Expected outcomes include the development of a scalable computational platform for biomarker discovery, validated ML models for early detection of sepsis and hematologic malignancies, and open-source tools to enhance reproducibility in clinical laboratory research. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation diagnostic protocols, reduce reliance on manual interpretation, and advance precision medicine initiatives. By bridging computational innovation with clinical laboratory practice, the project aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy, optimize laboratory workflows, and ultimately improve patient outcomes through data-driven decision-making.
cip_title: Clinical Laboratory Science/ Medical Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conduct and supervise complex medical tests, clinical trials, and research experiments; manage clinical laboratories; and consult with physicians and clinical researchers on diagnoses, disease causation and spread, and research outcomes. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, immunology, immunohematology, physiological relationships to test results, laboratory procedures and quality assurance controls, test and research design and implementation, analytic techniques, laboratory management, data development and reporting, medical informatics, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine and surgical outcomes in large animal species, including equids, food animals (e.g., bovids, swine), and sport animals. A critical challenge in clinical veterinary medicine is the lack of species-specific models to predict complex physiological responses to diseases, treatments, and surgical interventions. Existing datasets—spanning multi-omics, imaging, and herd-level health records—remain underutilized due to computational limitations in integrating heterogeneous data types and scaling analyses across populations. This work proposes a computational framework to model disease progression, optimize surgical planning, and predict therapeutic efficacy in diverse large animal cohorts. Machine learning methods, including graph neural networks and ensemble models, will be applied to integrate genomic, proteomic, and clinical data for conditions such as septic arthritis, bovine respiratory disease complex, and equine colic. High-fidelity finite element simulations will further assess biomechanical stress distributions in species-specific anatomies during orthopedic procedures. By deploying these workflows on HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve three outcomes: (1) identify biomarkers for early disease detection in herd and individual animal contexts, (2) generate predictive models for postoperative recovery risks tied to variables like breed, age, and comorbidities, and (3) optimize protocols for anesthesia and analgesia using pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations across metabolic and weight variations. The computational outputs will directly inform clinical trials and surgical training programs, bridging gaps between experimental data and applied veterinary care. This work will enhance the evidence base for precision treatment strategies in food animal and equine medicine, ultimately supporting agricultural productivity, animal welfare, and translational insights into comparative pathophysiology. Successful implementation requires scalable GPU-accelerated computing for deep learning tasks and parallelized CPU resources for large-scale genomic and biomechanical simulations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Large Animal/ Food Animal and Equine Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of herd, work, sport, and food animals. Includes instruction in equine medicine, swine and dairy medicine, food animal medicine, pathophysiology, large animal diseases, large animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the design and construction of load-bearing wooden structures, with a focus on improving efficiency, material sustainability, and structural reliability in carpentry practices. Traditional approaches to structural analysis and material selection in carpentry rely heavily on empirical guidelines and iterative physical testing, which can lead to material waste, extended timelines, and suboptimal load distribution in complex designs. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML) to simulate stress dynamics, predict material failure points, and recommend optimal joinery techniques under diverse environmental conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large datasets of wood grain variability, moisture content, and mechanical properties across species, as well as to run parallelized simulations of structural behavior at resolutions impractical for desktop systems. The first phase will involve validating FEA models against experimental data from standardized timber load tests. Subsequent phases will train ML algorithms on simulation outputs to generate predictive tools for rapid design iteration, reducing computational costs for end users. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for automated blueprint analysis, real-time stress visualization, and resource-efficient framing recommendations compatible with industry-standard building codes. This work bridges gaps between empirical carpentry knowledge and computational engineering, with potential applications in disaster-resistant housing, modular construction, and sustainable material reuse. By integrating HPC-driven insights into vocational training frameworks, the project aims to equip carpentry professionals with data-enhanced decision-making tools while maintaining alignment with hands-on technical workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to lay out, cut, fabricate, erect, install, and repair wooden structures and fixtures, using hand and power tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, framing, construction materials and selection, job estimating, blueprint reading, foundations and roughing-in, finish carpentry techniques, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets documenting trade networks, administrative records, and cultural exchanges across the medieval and early modern Middle East and Near East (ca. 600–1800 CE). The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how regional connectivity and institutional practices evolved amid shifting political regimes, such as the Abbasid-Umayyad transitions, the Mongol invasions, and Ottoman administrative reforms. Existing scholarship relies heavily on qualitative analyses of fragmentary textual sources, limiting systematic comparisons across time and space. To overcome this, the project will computationally process digitized corpora of Arabic, Persian, and Ottoman Turkish manuscripts, travelers’ accounts, tax registers, and archaeological records (totaling ~15 TB) using natural language processing (NLP) models tailored for historical languages. Custom algorithms will map trade routes, quantify fiscal data, and trace the diffusion of legal and bureaucratic terminology across dynastic boundaries. HPC resources are essential to train transformer-based NLP models on low-resource historical languages, run agent-based simulations of trade network resilience, and perform spatial-temporal analyses of administrative practices using GIS-integrated datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database linking economic, linguistic, and institutional patterns to political events; (2) visualizations of regional interdependencies previously undetectable through manual methods; and (3) statistical models testing hypotheses about centralized vs. decentralized governance in sustaining long-distance trade. By integrating computational methods with historiographical frameworks, this work will provide new insights into state formation, cross-cultural exchange, and the endurance of institutional legacies in the Middle East, while establishing scalable methodologies for computational historical analysis in understudied linguistic and regional contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the critical challenge of predicting and preventing early childhood caries (ECC) progression in pediatric populations through advanced computational modeling of oral microbiome dynamics and enamel demineralization processes. Despite established clinical protocols, ECC remains the most common chronic disease in children globally, with complex, multifactorial etiology involving microbial ecology, host immunology, and behavioral factors. Current diagnostic tools lack predictive precision for individual risk trajectories, particularly in patients with developmental disabilities who exhibit unique oral microbiome profiles. This project will develop a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling of biofilm formation, finite element analysis of enamel stress distribution, and machine learning analysis of longitudinal clinical-metagenomic datasets from a diverse pediatric cohort (n=1,200). High-performance computing resources are essential to simulate 3D tooth surface interactions across micron-scale spatial resolutions while concurrently processing terabyte-scale genomic data from saliva samples. The computational pipeline will parameterize microbial community networks (including *Streptococcus mutans*, *Candida albicans*, and aciduric symbioses) against pH cycling patterns and dietary variables, then validate predictions through parallel in vitro microfluidic tooth models. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a predictive risk stratification algorithm for ECC progression incorporating real-time sensor data from smart dental devices, 2) identification of keystone microbial taxa influencing caries acceleration in neurodiverse patients, and 3) optimized remineralization protocols personalized to salivary biochemistry. By bridging gaps between computational microbiology, materials science, and clinical pedodontics, this work will establish a novel paradigm for precision prevention in pediatric oral health, with particular significance for patients requiring special care dentistry. The resource-intensive simulations (requiring >200,000 core-hours) and integrative data analytics exceed current institutional computing capacities, necessitating access to large-scale GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of children from birth through adolescence, and the care of adults with physical, mental, and emotional disabilities. Includes instruction in developmental oral biology, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, patient management, pediatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and the treatment of handicapped patients.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize precision anesthesia protocols for diverse veterinary populations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome limitations in current empirical dosing strategies. In veterinary anesthesiology, inter-species physiological variability, compounded by intra-species factors such as breed, age, and comorbidities, complicates the prediction of drug responses. Traditional trial-and-error approaches risk underdosing (causing intraoperative awareness) or overdosing (leading to cardiopulmonary instability), particularly in high-risk patients. To address this, we propose developing species-specific pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models using machine learning algorithms trained on multi-modal datasets, including electronic health records (1,200+ canine, feline, and equine cases), physiological monitoring streams, and genomic biomarkers of drug metabolism. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to simulate drug behavior across virtual populations, accounting for anatomic, metabolic, and hemodynamic variables. A parallel computational workflow will integrate real-time sensor data from intraoperative monitoring devices (e.g., EEG-based depth-of-anesthesia metrics, continuous arterial pressure waveforms) with these models to generate dynamic dosing recommendations. Validation will occur through in silico trials comparing simulated outcomes against retrospective clinical data, followed by prospective testing in a controlled canine orthopedic surgery cohort (n=45). Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for personalized anesthesia induction and maintenance, reducing adverse event rates by an estimated 30-40% in modeled scenarios. The project will also produce open-access species-specific PK/PD libraries to support dose extrapolation in exotic animals. By enabling data-driven anesthesia tailored to individual patients, this work aims to improve perioperative safety in veterinary medicine while establishing computational methods adaptable to emerging analgesics and wearable monitoring technologies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical animal care and the care of pain problems. May included related research in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: Athletic injuries present complex biomechanical and physiological challenges, with recovery outcomes influenced by multifaceted interactions between tissue-level damage, rehabilitation protocols, and psychological factors. Current clinical models often oversimplify these dynamics, limiting their ability to predict injury risks or personalize interventions. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to simulate injury mechanisms, rehabilitation efficacy, and psychophysiological recovery trajectories using high-performance computing (HPC). The research integrates three methodological components: (1) multi-scale finite element modeling of musculoskeletal tissues under dynamic athletic loads to quantify stress distributions and failure thresholds, (2) agent-based simulations of cellular responses to therapeutic interventions, and (3) machine learning analysis of multimodal datasets combining biomechanical metrics, imaging data, and psychological assessments from collegiate athletes.
