The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution anatomical models derived from clinical MRI/CT scans, real-time coupling of tissue mechanics with inflammatory cascades, and probabilistic forecasting of recovery timelines. Anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms to identify athletes at high risk of reinjury, optimized rehabilitation protocols tailored to individual biomechanical profiles, and evidence-based insights into the bidirectional relationship between physical recovery and psychological resilience. By bridging computational biomechanics with clinical sports medicine, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven injury management, directly informing therapeutic strategies that address both physiological healing and mental health. The scale of simulations—involving 10^6–10^7 degrees of freedom per model and terabyte-scale datasets—necessitates dedicated HPC resources to achieve clinically relevant throughput and resolution, advancing translational outcomes for athlete care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the pathology and biomechanics of athletic injuries and the effects of injury on the athlete, including both physical and psychological manifestations. Includes instruction in acute and chronic patient supervision, therapy and rehabilitation, and diagnostic procedures.

abstract: Dental diseases remain a significant public health burden globally, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations due to systemic inequities in access to care. Traditional approaches to designing preventive interventions often rely on static epidemiological models, which inadequately capture the dynamic interactions between socioeconomic factors, behavioral patterns, and healthcare infrastructure. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate the long-term impacts of community-level dental public health interventions, enabling data-driven policy decisions. The primary research problem centers on identifying optimal, equitable strategies for deploying preventive services (e.g., fluoridation programs, mobile clinics) under resource constraints. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with machine learning (ML) to analyze multi-source data, including electronic health records, demographic surveys, and geospatial datasets. The ABM will simulate population-level oral health outcomes by modeling individual agents’ behaviors, environmental exposures, and care-seeking decisions across diverse socioeconomic strata. ML components will refine parameter estimation using real-world data and predict intervention scalability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the computational complexity of simulating millions of agents over decadal timeframes while incorporating stochastic variability and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for dental public health simulation, (2) quantitative comparisons of intervention cost-effectiveness across different regional contexts, and (3) policy recommendations for reducing disparities in caries and periodontal disease prevalence. This work will provide novel insights into the nonlinear effects of public health investments and empower policymakers to prioritize interventions with the highest equitable impact. The requested computing resources will enable iterative model calibration, large-scale parameter sweeps, and uncertainty quantification, which are infeasible with standard clinical research infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the formulation and delivery of public preventive and curative dental health services.

abstract: The horticultural industry faces mounting challenges from climate unpredictability, which disrupts growth cycles, increases pest pressures, and threatens yield stability in high-value crops. Current breeding and management strategies lack the predictive capacity to rapidly adapt to these dynamic stressors, particularly for perennial species with long breeding timelines. This project proposes a computational framework to model genotype-by-environment interactions (G×E) in horticultural crops, integrating genomic, phenotypic, and high-resolution environmental data to accelerate the development of climate-resilient cultivars. We will focus on citrus, berry crops, and ornamental species critical to regional economies. Using machine learning architectures optimized for high-performance computing (HPC), we will analyze terabyte-scale datasets encompassing multi-omics profiles, historical yield records, and microclimate sensor networks from experimental orchards. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will be coupled with agent-based models simulating pest population dynamics under future climate projections. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of genomic variants across 20+ crop genomes, real-time integration of distributed climate data streams, and iterative optimization of neural networks predicting flowering time and stress tolerance. HPC resources are essential for scaling these analyses beyond proof-of-concept trials to operationalize models across diverse production systems. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of genetic markers associated with drought resilience in citrus rootstocks, (2) predictive algorithms for optimizing protected cultivation schedules in ornamental nurseries, and (3) open-source tools for simulating pest dispersal under varying management scenarios. By reducing trial-and-error in field testing, this work will shorten breeding cycles for stress-tolerant varieties while providing actionable intelligence for adaptive crop management—critical steps in safeguarding horticultural productivity under climate change.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific principles related to the cultivation of garden and ornamental plants, including fruits, vegetables, flowers, and landscape and nursery crops. Includes instruction in specific types of plants, such as citrus; breeding horticultural varieties; physiology of horticultural species; and the scientific management of horticultural plant development and production through the life cycle.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in clinical decision support systems (CDSS) for sepsis management, a critical challenge in acute care settings where Clinical Nurse Specialists (CNSs) play a pivotal role. Sepsis, a life-threatening dysregulated immune response to infection, requires rapid, personalized interventions to reduce mortality. However, existing CDSS tools often lack the computational capacity to integrate real-time multimodal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), continuous vital sign monitoring, and biomarker trends—while accounting for patient-specific variables such as comorbidities, pharmacotherapeutic responses, and genomic predispositions. This gap limits the ability of CNSs to optimize dynamic treatment plans. To address this, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) framework capable of processing heterogeneous clinical data streams at scale. The framework will employ federated learning techniques to preserve patient privacy across institutions while training predictive models for sepsis progression and therapeutic outcomes. HPC resources will enable the parallelization of model training across thousands of patient cases, the simulation of treatment trajectories under diverse clinical scenarios, and the real-time validation of risk stratification algorithms. Key computational challenges include managing high-dimensional temporal data, optimizing hyperparameters for interpretable ML models, and integrating domain-specific knowledge from nursing practice guidelines. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source CDSS prototype that provides actionable, evidence-based recommendations to CNSs, reducing time-to-intervention and variability in care delivery. This work aligns with national priorities to reduce sepsis-related mortality through data-driven innovations and will inform future CNS-led initiatives in predictive analytics and holistic care integration. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the project’s scale, ensuring robust model generalizability across diverse patient populations and care environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver direct patient and client care in clinical settings. Includes instruction in clinical pharmacotherapeutics, advanced clinical practice, holistic nursing, nursing practice and health care policy, administration and consultation services, health assessment, patient stabilization and care, and patient education.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and inventory allocation strategies for automotive aftermarket supply chains using high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in demand forecasting and resource distribution. Traditional approaches in vehicle parts marketing struggle to adapt to real-time fluctuations in consumer behavior, supply chain disruptions, and evolving vehicular technology trends. The proposed computational framework integrates multi-source data streams—including IoT-enabled vehicle telematics, regional maintenance patterns, and social media sentiment—to model spatially and temporally heterogeneous demand. A hybrid machine learning architecture will be deployed, combining graph neural networks to capture supplier-retailer-customer network dependencies with transformer-based models for sequential decision-making under uncertainty. Agent-based simulations will emulate competitive market dynamics across 10,000+ virtual retail nodes, while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will quantify risk exposure under diverse macroeconomic and regulatory scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations, enabling near-real-time parameter optimization across high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of recommending adaptive pricing, inventory redistribution, and promotional campaigns at hyperlocal resolutions, reducing excess stock by an estimated 15-22% in test markets while maintaining service-level agreements. This work bridges gaps between operations research, computational marketing, and vehicular IoT analytics, offering novel methodologies for resource allocation in perishable-part industries. Results will be validated against historical sales data from three multinational automotive distributors, with open-source release of non-proprietary model components to advance interdisciplinary research in next-generation vehicle services optimization.
cip_title: Vehicle and Vehicle Parts and Accessories Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of replacement parts and other end-use supplies in the automotive, marine, and aviation industries. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, principles of vehicular technologies, storage and distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: School psychologists face the challenge of integrating complex, multidimensional datasets—including behavioral assessments, academic performance metrics, and socio-environmental factors—to design effective interventions for students with learning and behavioral difficulties. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to model the dynamic interactions between these variables, particularly across developmental stages and diverse populations. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that identify patterns in behavioral-academic linkages and predict intervention outcomes. Using anonymized longitudinal data from school districts (e.g., behavioral incident reports, individualized education program records, and socio-emotional screening tools), we will apply machine learning algorithms to classify risk profiles and simulate intervention efficacy under varying conditions. Computational methods will include multilevel modeling to account for nested data structures (e.g., students within schools), network analysis to map bidirectional relationships between behavioral traits and academic outcomes, and agent-based simulations to test how hypothetical interventions propagate through student networks. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (spanning thousands of students over 5–10 years) and running computationally intensive Bayesian optimization routines to refine model parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for identifying students at risk of behavioral escalation, (2) evidence-based guidelines for tailoring interventions to specific developmental and contextual profiles, and (3) open-source tools for school psychologists to simulate intervention impacts using localized data. By bridging gaps between data-driven decision-making and applied psychological practice, this work will enhance the precision and equity of school-based mental health supports while reducing reliance on reactive disciplinary measures. The project aligns with the School Psychology program’s focus on ethical, empirically grounded strategies for improving student well-being and academic success.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing radiation shielding materials and safety protocols in nuclear and industrial radiologic systems through advanced computational modeling. Current shielding materials and operational practices often rely on empirical data and conservative design principles, which can lead to inefficiencies in cost, weight, and radiation exposure management. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations, molecular dynamics modeling, and machine learning (ML) to systematically evaluate novel material compositions and operational configurations. The research will employ Geant4 for simulating gamma-ray and neutron interactions across heterogeneous shielding materials, coupled with LAMMPS for analyzing radiation-induced microstructural changes. ML algorithms will then be trained on the resulting datasets to predict optimal material properties and operational parameters under varying radiation environments. The computational intensity of these simulations—requiring millions of particle histories and terabyte-scale datasets—necessitates access to HPC resources with parallel processing capabilities. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-performance composite materials with superior radiation attenuation and durability, as well as data-driven recommendations for minimizing occupational exposure in industrial radiography and nuclear facility operations. This work will provide a foundational framework for accelerating the development of next-generation radiologic technologies while maintaining compliance with evolving safety standards. Results will be disseminated through open-access databases to support broader research and regulatory efforts in radiation protection.
cip_title: Nuclear and Industrial Radiologic Technologies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in nuclear and industrial radiologic technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in evaluating the long-term impacts of health policy interventions on systemic inequities in healthcare access and outcomes. Current policy analysis frameworks often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the dynamic interactions between multi-level factors, including institutional regulations, regional resource allocation patterns, and individual health-seeking behaviors. This project will develop and apply an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework enhanced with machine learning to simulate how proposed Medicaid expansion policies in four U.S. states might influence care utilization disparities among vulnerable populations over a 10-year horizon. The computational model will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), census-derived socioeconomic indicators, and state-level healthcare facility inventories, to parameterize approximately 2 million agent interactions across demographic and geographic strata. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the parallel processing demands of calibrating model parameters through iterative Bayesian optimization, validating outputs against historical policy outcomes, and conducting sensitivity analyses across 500+ simulated policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive health policy simulation, quantitative projections of how specific reimbursement structures and outreach programs could reduce racial disparities in preventive care uptake, and uncertainty-quantified estimates of policy cost-effectiveness under demographic change. By enabling granular, systems-level analysis of emergent policy effects, this work will provide actionable evidence for designing targeted interventions that account for complex feedback loops between policy implementation and community health dynamics. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter space exploration, and storage of multi-terabyte synthetic populations generated through statistical matching of federal survey microdata.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to domestic and international health and health care systems. Includes instruction in contemporary health issues and policies, politics and economics of health care delivery, epidemiology, public health, comparative and global health, medical law and ethics, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing large-scale, multi-objective manufacturing systems under uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in real-time decision-making for flexible production environments. Modern manufacturing networks face challenges in balancing competing objectives—such as cost minimization, energy efficiency, and throughput maximization—while managing stochastic variables like equipment failures, demand fluctuations, and material delays. Current analytical methods struggle with the combinatorial complexity of these systems, particularly when scaling to enterprise-level operations. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid approach integrating stochastic mixed-integer programming, discrete-event simulation, and reinforcement learning. The computational workflow will model interdependent production stages as networked queuing systems with probabilistic state transitions, using parallelizable decomposition algorithms to solve optimization subproblems. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to characterize robustness across uncertain scenarios, as well as training of deep reinforcement learning agents on synthetic datasets representing diverse factory configurations. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating and optimizing adaptive manufacturing systems, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational strategies under varying uncertainty levels, and (3) prescriptive guidelines for deploying HPC-enabled optimization in industrial settings with dynamic constraints. By enabling rapid evaluation of trade-offs in complex production environments, this work aims to advance data-driven manufacturing system design while providing a template for scalable industrial operations research. The requested computing resources will directly support parallel simulation runs, distributed optimization tasks, and machine learning model training, which are infeasible on local clusters due to memory and runtime constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, and implementation of manufacturing systems. Includes instruction in materials science and engineering, manufacturing processes, process engineering, assembly and product engineering, manufacturing systems design, and manufacturing competitiveness.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize decision-making processes in contested information environments critical to military Joint Information Operations (JIO). The research problem centers on the escalating complexity of adversarial information campaigns, where rapid, multi-domain data synthesis and scenario forecasting are constrained by legacy computational tools. Traditional models struggle to integrate real-time intelligence with probabilistic assessments of adversary behavior, social network dynamics, and the cascading effects of countermeasures across cyber, electromagnetic, and psychological domains. To address this gap, the project will develop a multi-agent simulation framework that combines game-theoretic adversarial modeling, network influence propagation algorithms, and uncertainty-aware machine learning. The computational approach will prioritize scalable parallelism to simulate thousands of concurrent decision threads across hybrid threat scenarios, with dynamic adaptation to evolving mission parameters and resource constraints. Key technical challenges include optimizing latency-sensitive event processing for time-critical operational recommendations and validating model outputs against classified historical JIO datasets. Expected outcomes include a prototype decision-support system capable of generating ranked courses of action (COAs) under asymmetric information conditions, quantifying risk trade-offs for integrated electronic warfare and narrative operations. The research will further contribute novel metrics for measuring "information resilience" in coalition networks, informed by emergent patterns in large-scale simulations. By enabling granular analysis of cross-domain second- and third-order effects, this work aims to advance the operationalization of information superiority as a measurable, computable component of joint force readiness. HPC resources are essential to achieve the required fidelity in modeling multi-echelon adversarial decision loops while maintaining security-compliant isolation of sensitive data layers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the strategic and operational use of information relative to the support of military and strategic policy and objectives. Includes instruction in information technology, decision theory and applications, military operations, command and control technology, network operations, network systems integration, computer network defense, space communications technology, and applications to specific military operational tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of computational biology and machine learning with Ayurvedic pharmacology, addressing a critical gap in the empirical validation of traditional Ayurvedic formulations. Despite centuries of documented clinical efficacy, the molecular mechanisms underlying polyherbal formulations and their systemic effects on human physiology remain poorly characterized. This limits their acceptance in evidence-based medical frameworks and hinders optimization for personalized treatment. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach combining molecular dynamics simulations, network pharmacology, and natural language processing (NLP) of classical Sanskrit texts. HPC resources will enable large-scale virtual screening of phytochemicals from Ayurvedic herb libraries against protein targets implicated in metabolic, inflammatory, and neurological disorders. Concurrently, NLP models will analyze structured treatment protocols from digitized Vedic manuscripts to identify patterns in historical therapeutic applications. Machine learning will integrate these data streams with contemporary clinical datasets to predict formulation efficacy, potential drug-herb interactions, and biomarker correlations. The computational workflow will be validated against in vitro assays of key formulations’ immunomodulatory and antioxidant properties. Expected outcomes include a curated database of Ayurvedic compound-target interactions, predictive models for personalized formulation design, and novel insights into the systems biology principles underlying Ayurveda’s holistic framework. This research will establish a bridge between traditional knowledge systems and modern computational biology, enhancing the scientific rigor of Ayurvedic practice while informing integrative medicine strategies for complex chronic diseases. The requested HPC allocation is essential for managing the terabyte-scale data generated by molecular simulations and text corpora, as well as for training deep learning models on heterogeneous biomedical datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to advance the precision and sustainability of footwear and leather goods repair practices. Traditional repair techniques rely heavily on empirical knowledge and manual skill, limiting scalability and adaptability to modern materials and design complexities. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model material behaviors, optimize repair workflows, and simulate long-term wear patterns. A key focus is on orthopedic footwear, where individualized adjustments require predictive biomechanical modeling to balance durability, comfort, and anatomical alignment. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distributions in repaired leather and synthetic materials under dynamic loading conditions. Machine learning models, trained on datasets of material degradation (e.g., creasing, dye fading, sole wear), will predict failure points and recommend reinforcement strategies. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will explore eco-friendly alternatives to traditional adhesives and dyes, targeting reduced environmental impact without compromising performance. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-resolution 3D scans of footwear components, multi-physics simulations of repair interfaces, and large-scale parameter optimization for material formulations. Expected outcomes include open-access predictive tools for artisans, a digital library of material response profiles, and validated computational protocols for custom orthopedic modifications. By bridging artisanal expertise with computational innovation, this work aims to modernize technical training in leather repair fields, reduce material waste through data-driven decision-making, and extend the functional lifespan of repaired goods. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated through partnerships with vocational training centers and industry collaborators, ensuring direct translational impact on sustainable practices in the footwear repair sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair all types of footwear, including replacement and mending of worn parts, repairing orthopedic footwear, refinishing and dyeing leather, and repairing other leather goods such as handbags, belts, and luggage.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze patterns in interfaith spiritual care delivery across crisis environments, a critical yet understudied aspect of chaplaincy studies. Chaplains operate in high-stakes, multi-faith contexts—such as disaster response, healthcare, and military settings—where effective communication requires nuanced adaptation to diverse cultural, religious, and emotional needs. However, systematic frameworks for evaluating the efficacy of chaplain interventions remain underdeveloped, hindered by the complexity of qualitative data and the ethical sensitivities of real-world case studies. This project addresses this gap by employing computational text analysis and agent-based modeling to simulate and evaluate chaplain decision-making processes in crisis scenarios. Using anonymized chaplain narratives, interview transcripts, and crisis response records (totaling ~2 TB of text data), we will train natural language processing (NLP) models to identify linguistic markers of effective spiritual care, such as empathy modulation, interfaith competency, and crisis-specific rhetoric. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model chaplain-crisis interactions under variable conditions (e.g., cultural diversity, trauma severity, resource constraints) to predict optimal intervention strategies. The HPC environment is essential for scaling transformer-based NLP architectures (e.g., BERT, GPT-3 fine-tuning) and parallelizing thousands of simulation iterations. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for assessing chaplain efficacy, an open-access corpus of de-identified training data for interdisciplinary research, and computational tools to enhance chaplain education programs. By integrating humanities-based ethical inquiry with machine learning, this project aims to advance evidence-based practices in chaplaincy while establishing methodological precedents for computational humanities in caregiving disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide caregiver, pastoral, and spiritual support in an institutional, hospice, military, or sports setting. Includes instruction in global, healthcare, prison, and sports chaplaincy; addiction, crisis, disaster, family, marriage, grief, and loss counseling; ethics; leadership; multi-cultural, multi-faith contexts; and worship.

abstract: Pediatric gastrointestinal (GI) disorders, such as inflammatory bowel disease, functional abdominal pain, and biliary atresia, present complex etiologies involving interactions between genetic predisposition, gut microbiome dynamics, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches often lack precision, leading to suboptimal outcomes in children. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omic datasets and simulate pathophysiological mechanisms underlying pediatric GI diseases. The primary research problem centers on identifying predictive biomarkers and mechanistic drivers of disease progression, which remain poorly characterized due to the computational limitations of processing large-scale clinical, genomic, and metagenomic data. We propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) models with mechanistic simulations to unravel disease heterogeneity. Whole-genome sequencing data from pediatric cohorts will be analyzed for rare variants and polygenic risk scores, while longitudinal metagenomic data will be processed to model gut microbiome-host interactions. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate mucosal immune responses and microbial community dynamics under varying clinical scenarios. These analyses demand substantial computational power due to the scale of data (terabytes of sequencing data) and the complexity of simulating stochastic biological systems. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of genomic datasets, training of deep neural networks for pattern recognition in endoscopic imaging, and large-scale parameter sweeps in mechanistic models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early disease detection, stratification of patients into molecular subtypes for personalized therapy, and optimization of therapeutic protocols via in silico trials. This work will provide a foundation for data-driven clinical decision-making, reducing invasive diagnostic procedures and improving outcomes for children with GI disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the digestive systems of infants, children, and adolescents; includes treatment of conditions such as abdominal pain, ulcers, diarrhea, cancer, and jaundice, and performance of complex diagnostic and therapeutic procedures using lighted scopes to see internal organs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic analysis of understudied Semitic languages and dialects, with a focus on identifying patterns of morphological and syntactic evolution across historical and modern textual corpora. The research addresses a critical gap in Middle/Near Eastern linguistics: the limited application of scalable computational methods to trace linguistic change in non-standardized or sparsely documented languages, such as Neo-Aramaic dialects, Classical Ethiopic (Ge’ez), and pre-Islamic epigraphic South Arabian. Traditional manual analysis struggles to process the scale and complexity of these datasets, which include digitized inscriptions, multilingual manuscripts, and contemporary spoken recordings. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for low-resource languages, to automate morphological tagging, syntactic parsing, and dialect classification. Computational phylogenetics will be applied to model language divergence, while distributed algorithms will map contact-induced changes across multilingual regions. HPC resources are essential for training custom neural models on heterogeneous data (e.g., tokenized ancient scripts, transliterated oral histories) and running large-scale simulations of language evolution scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source computational toolkit optimized for Semitic language structures, (2) empirically grounded reconstructions of under-resourced language varieties, and (3) new hypotheses about the diffusion of grammatical features across trade and migration networks in the Near East. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work will provide novel insights into linguistic resilience and shift in multilingual societies, while enhancing digital infrastructure for endangered language preservation. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, parallel corpus processing, and storage for terabyte-scale linguistic datasets, enabling methodologies previously inaccessible to traditional humanities scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Middle/ Near Eastern and Semitic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Middle/Near Eastern and Semitic languages of the ancient and modern Middle/Near East, Western Asia, North Africa, and Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of embodied cognition in actor training through computational modeling of performance dynamics. The research problem centers on understanding how actors internalize and reproduce complex emotional and physical states under varying theatrical constraints. Traditional pedagogical methods rely on subjective observation and iterative rehearsal, limiting systematic analysis of how physiological, linguistic, and environmental factors interact during performance. To address this, we propose developing a multimodal simulation framework that integrates motion capture data, vocal acoustics, and script semantic analysis to model adaptive actor behaviors in virtual performance environments. Computational workflows will process terabytes of biometric and textual data from laboratory-based actor ensembles, employing neural networks to correlate biomechanical patterns (e.g., posture shifts, breath control) with emotional valence metrics derived from speech and movement. Agent-based models will further simulate audience-performer dynamics under configurable parameters (e.g., stage size, acoustic properties). The HPC infrastructure is critical for running high-fidelity, real-time simulations of these multivariate interactions, which require parallelized processing of GPU-accelerated physics engines and large-language model inference for script analysis. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital toolkit for quantifying pedagogical efficacy across acting methodologies, with applications in curriculum design and accessibility-focused performance practices. By bridging computational analytics with performative embodiment theory, this work aims to establish new frameworks for evidence-based actor training while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in performing arts research.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to communicate dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the achievement of naturalistic and believable behavior in imaginary circumstances. Includes instruction in voice and acting speech, stage dialects, movement, improvisation, acting styles, theatre history, script interpretation, and actor coaching.

abstract: The increasing complexity of embedded systems in IoT and edge computing applications necessitates advanced methodologies for hardware-software co-design. Traditional approaches often struggle to balance performance, energy efficiency, and scalability, leading to suboptimal system configurations. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a novel framework for optimizing embedded system architectures. The research will employ large-scale simulations to model interactions between hardware components and software algorithms under varying workloads. Machine learning techniques, including neural networks and genetic algorithms, will be integrated to predict optimal resource allocation strategies and identify system bottlenecks. Additionally, FPGA-based prototyping emulated on HPC clusters will enable rapid iteration and testing of candidate designs. The computational demands of these tasks—such as parallelized circuit simulation, real-time data processing for adaptive algorithms, and multi-objective optimization—require access to HPC infrastructure with robust processing capabilities and distributed memory systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for co-design optimization, demonstrated through case studies on edge computing nodes and IoT sensor networks. The project aims to reduce development cycles by 30–40% while improving energy efficiency by 20% compared to existing methodologies. By providing insights into efficient hardware-software integration, this research will contribute to the development of next-generation embedded systems capable of supporting advanced applications in smart infrastructure and industrial automation. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the intensive computational workloads inherent in simulating complex electronic systems and training data-driven models at scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: Wooden boatbuilding integrates artisanal techniques with evolving material and hydrodynamic challenges, yet the field lacks robust computational tools to systematically optimize designs, predict structural failures, or model environmental impacts on traditional materials. This project seeks to address these gaps by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive models for wooden boat performance and longevity. The research will focus on two interconnected computational workflows: finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution in complex joinery and planking systems under dynamic loads, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to evaluate hull efficiency and stability across diverse hydrodynamic conditions. Machine learning algorithms will augment these simulations by training on historical datasets of wood degradation, moisture absorption, and failure modes specific to marine environments. Additionally, parametric modeling will explore trade-offs between traditional construction methods (e.g., carvel vs. clinker planking) and modern material hybrids. By leveraging HPC resources, the project will iteratively refine these models at scale, enabling sensitivity analyses across variables such as timber species, fastener corrosion rates, and sail rigging configurations. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools for boatbuilders to virtually prototype designs, predictive frameworks for maintenance scheduling, and evidence-based guidelines for sustainable material selection. This work aims to preserve maritime heritage by enhancing the precision of traditional practices while reducing trial-and-error waste, ultimately fostering safer, more durable wooden vessels. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as pedagogical resources, integrating digital literacy into technical curricula for future boatbuilding professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to construct and repair traditional and modern wooden boats. Includes instruction in budgeting, drafting, fairing, lofting, joinery, planking, spars and rigging, and woodworking.

abstract: The development of efficient catalytic systems for selective organic transformations remains a critical challenge in synthetic chemistry, particularly for reactions involving complex substrates or requiring precise stereochemical control. Current experimental approaches to catalyst design are often limited by the inability to probe transition states and reactive intermediates at atomic resolution, leading to time-consuming trial-and-error optimization. This project seeks to address these limitations through a computational study of reaction mechanisms and catalyst-substrate interactions in enantioselective organocatalytic processes. We propose to employ hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations combined with ab initio molecular dynamics to model asymmetric aldol and Mannich reactions mediated by chiral amine catalysts. These methods will enable explicit sampling of solvent effects, conformational dynamics, and non-covalent interactions governing stereoselectivity. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the system sizes (200-500 atoms) and timescales (10-100 ps) required for statistically meaningful sampling of reaction pathways. Additionally, we will develop machine learning models trained on computed activation barriers and stereochemical outcomes to predict optimal catalyst architectures for novel substrate classes. The computational workflow will integrate Gaussian 16 for QM calculations, AMBER for MD simulations, and PyTorch-based neural networks for predictive modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic insights into hydrogen-bonding networks and π-π interactions that direct stereochemistry, (2) a predictive framework for catalyst design, and (3) identification of three lead catalyst candidates for experimental validation. This work will directly advance sustainable synthesis methodologies by reducing reliance on empirical optimization, with potential applications in pharmaceutical development where stereocontrol is paramount. The requested resources will support 15,000 CPU-core hours and GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models across multiple reaction classes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of hydrocarbon compounds and their derivatives. Includes instruction in molecular conversion and synthesis, molecular synthesis and design, the molecular structure of living cells and systems, the mutual reactivity of organic and inorganic compounds in combination, the spectroscopic analysis of hydrocarbon compounds, and applications to specific problems in research, industry, and health.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of neurodevelopmental trajectories in children with behavioral and emotional disorders, with a focus on identifying early biomarkers of conditions such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Current diagnostic frameworks rely heavily on behavioral observations, which often delay intervention until symptoms become pronounced. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating longitudinal neuroimaging (fMRI, MRI), genetic, and behavioral datasets from a multi-site cohort of 1,200 children aged 3–12. The primary research problem involves modeling the dynamic interplay between neural circuit maturation, genetic risk factors, and emerging psychopathology, which requires processing high-dimensional, multimodal data at scale. Our computational approach will employ machine learning pipelines to identify predictive patterns of developmental divergence, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for structural MRI feature extraction, graph theory-based analyses of functional connectivity, and ensemble methods to integrate genetic polymorphisms with neurocognitive metrics. These analyses demand significant parallel processing capabilities and memory allocation due to the volume of imaging data (>500 TB) and the need for iterative model training across permutations of risk variables. HPC resources will also enable large-scale simulations of neurodevelopmental pathways under varying genetic and environmental conditions, using agent-based models to test hypotheses about resilience mechanisms. Expected outcomes include the identification of subtype-specific neural signatures associated with transition points in symptom severity, which could inform earlier, more precise interventions. By optimizing predictive algorithms on HPC infrastructure, this work aims to generate open-source tools for clinicians to stratify risk during critical developmental windows, ultimately improving outcomes for children with neurodevelopmental disorders. The project aligns with clinical child psychology’s emphasis on developmental neuropsychology and evidence-based practice while adhering to ethical standards for data privacy and equitable resource use.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the developmental processes of children and associated disorders and that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical child psychology. Includes instruction in developmental neuropsychology, child psychopathology, testing of children and adolescents, pediatric psychology, psychosocial variables in child development, clinical skills, family therapy, behavioral assessment and intervention, clinical skills, consultation, professional standards and ethics, and applications to topics such as infancy, childhood, and adolescence.

abstract: The motorsports industry demands continuous advancements in vehicle performance, safety, and efficiency, requiring high-fidelity simulations to address complex multi-physics challenges. Current computational limitations restrict the ability to model intricate interactions between aerodynamics, structural dynamics, and thermal systems in real-world racing conditions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize a coupled simulation framework for motorsports applications. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to analyze turbulent airflow around vehicle surfaces and underbody components, (2) finite element analysis (FEA) to assess structural integrity under dynamic loads, and (3) conjugate heat transfer modeling to evaluate thermal management in high-performance engines and braking systems. Leveraging open-source tools like OpenFOAM and Code_Aster, alongside GPU-accelerated machine learning algorithms for design optimization, the simulations will incorporate real-world data from wind tunnel experiments and on-track telemetry. The HPC environment will enable parametric studies at unprecedented scales, reducing reliance on physical prototyping while improving predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include novel design guidelines for aerodynamic components, weight-reduction strategies for chassis components without compromising safety, and optimized cooling solutions for hybrid powertrains. This work will directly support student and faculty research in vehicle dynamics and energy-efficient motorsports technologies, fostering industry partnerships through validated computational models. By integrating HPC into the curriculum, the project will also train the next generation of motorsports engineers in advanced simulation techniques, bridging gaps between academic research and professional motorsports engineering practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the design, construction, and repair of vehicles used in racing and motorsports. Includes instruction in aerodynamics, design, vehicle dynamics, performance engines, fluid mechanics, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical engineering, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models for analyzing the evolution of legal frameworks in response to decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) and blockchain-based smart contracts. As these technologies disrupt traditional notions of contractual enforcement, jurisdictional authority, and corporate governance, existing legal systems face challenges in reconciling rigid statutory frameworks with dynamic, code-driven agreements. The research problem centers on identifying patterns and gaps in current legal responses to DAO-related disputes, which require parsing large corpora of international case law, regulatory guidance, and smart contract codebases. Computational methods will combine natural language processing (NLP) techniques with network analysis to map relationships between legal precedents, contractual clauses, and blockchain transaction histories. Machine learning models will be trained to simulate dispute resolution scenarios across jurisdictions, accounting for variables such as cryptographic audit trails, tokenized governance mechanisms, and conflicting national regulations. The proposed work requires HPC resources to handle the scale of legal text datasets (spanning multiple languages and jurisdictions) and to run iterative simulations of cross-border contractual disputes under varying interpretive frameworks. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of emergent legal conflicts specific to autonomous digital organizations, predictive models for jurisdictional arbitrage risks, and a framework for computationally assisted legal analysis in this domain. By bridging gaps between computational logic and legal reasoning, this research aims to inform the development of adaptive regulatory models while advancing methodological innovations at the intersection of legal informatics and decentralized systems. The project’s findings will contribute to both academic discourse and practical tools for legal professionals navigating the governance challenges of next-generation digital infrastructures.
cip_title: Legal Research and Advanced Professional Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in legal research and advanced professional studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Cardiovascular interventions require precise characterization of coronary hemodynamics to optimize clinical outcomes, yet current methods for evaluating blood flow and pressure gradients in stenotic vessels remain limited by static anatomical assessments and simplified computational models. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing patient-specific, dynamic simulations of coronary blood flow and pressure under varying physiological and procedural conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate high-resolution intravascular imaging data (e.g., optical coherence tomography) with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models to simulate transient flow patterns, shear stress distributions, and pressure gradients across stenoses before and after percutaneous coronary interventions. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify predictive hemodynamic signatures associated with procedural complications, such as stent thrombosis or edge dissection. The computational workflow will require processing multi-terabyte imaging datasets, running parallelized CFD simulations with adaptive meshing for complex geometries, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data. HPC resources are essential to manage the iterative modeling demands, particularly for simulating time-resolved, three-dimensional flow dynamics in anatomically accurate coronary trees. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for post-interventional hemodynamic performance and a framework for real-time procedural decision support. This work aims to advance the personalization of interventional strategies by quantifying how anatomical and physiological variables interact to influence procedural success, potentially reducing adverse events and improving long-term patient outcomes. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source resources to foster collaboration in hemodynamics research, bridging gaps between imaging innovation, computational modeling, and clinical translation in interventional cardiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of specialized imaging and other diagnostic techniques to evaluate blood flow and pressure in the coronary arteries and chambers of the heart, and in the use of technical procedures and medications to treat abnormalities that impair the function of the cardiovascular system.

abstract: Reproductive system cancers, such as ovarian and prostate malignancies, exhibit complex interactions between hormonal regulation, tumor microenvironment dynamics, and therapeutic resistance mechanisms that remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address critical gaps in modeling the systemic physiological drivers of reproductive cancer progression and treatment response, with a focus on how endocrine-disergulation and stromal-epithelial crosstalk influence tumor evolution. We propose to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale simulation framework integrating patient-derived physiological data, including hormone fluctuation patterns, vascular remodeling dynamics, and spatially resolved cellular interaction networks. Agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate tumor growth under varying endocrine conditions, while finite element analysis will quantify mechanical stress distributions in evolving tumor microenvironments. The computational pipeline will process longitudinal clinical datasets encompassing serum hormone levels, histopathology imaging, and treatment outcomes from 450+ patients with reproductive cancers. By leveraging GPU-accelerated parallel processing, we aim to establish predictive models of therapeutic response that account for cyclical hormonal variations and stromal reprogramming events—factors frequently neglected in current oncology models. Expected outcomes include the identification of microenvironment-specific biomarkers for treatment resistance and the generation of in silico platforms for testing hormone modulation strategies in combination with standard therapies. This work will provide novel insights into the systemic physiology of reproductive malignancies while advancing computational methodologies for simulating hormonally regulated cancer progression. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the high-dimensional parameter space of coupled endocrine-tumor systems and achieving clinically relevant simulation timescales. Results will directly inform the design of adaptive therapeutic protocols tailored to individual hormonal profiles, addressing a critical need in reproductive cancer management.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of reproductive processes and biogenesis in animals and human beings. Includes instruction in reproductive ecology and behavior, reproductive system physiology, endocrinology, developmental biology, neuroendocrinology, evolution and types of reproductive systems, reproductive genetics, physiopathology of reproductive processes, and applications of molecular biology and biophysics to the study of reproductive physiology.

abstract: Traditional craft practices are integral to cultural heritage yet face challenges in material sustainability, structural innovation, and the preservation of intangible techniques. This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to investigate complex material interactions and generative design methodologies in artisanry. The research employs finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML) to simulate material behaviors under diverse environmental conditions and optimize craft design parameters. High-resolution 3D scans of historical artifacts will train ML models to identify correlations between traditional methods and material performance, while multi-scale simulations model stress distribution and degradation in craft objects. These computationally intensive tasks—processing large spectral datasets, iterative simulation workflows, and neural network training—require HPC infrastructure for efficient execution. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for sustainable material selection, a digital repository of craft techniques, and generative tools that assist artisans in creating structurally resilient works without compromising aesthetic integrity. By integrating computational science with craft practice, this project advances the preservation of cultural heritage and addresses contemporary challenges in artisanry, demonstrating how HPC resources can drive innovation in visual arts. The interdisciplinary approach underscores the potential of computational methods to enrich traditional practices, fostering new creative possibilities rooted in historical continuity while promoting ecological and structural resilience.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Crafts/ Craft Design, Folk Art and Artisanry
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the aesthetics, techniques, and creative processes for designing and fashioning objects in one or more of the handcraft or folk art traditions, and that prepares individuals to create in any of these media.

abstract: The increasing complexity of chemical systems in analytical applications—such as environmental monitoring, pharmaceutical analysis, and metabolomics—demands advanced computational tools to interpret high-dimensional spectroscopic and chromatographic data. Traditional analytical methods struggle to resolve overlapping spectral features or predict retention times for novel compounds in multi-component mixtures, particularly when experimental parameters are constrained by time, cost, or instrumental limitations. This project seeks to develop a scalable machine learning framework integrated with quantum mechanical simulations to enhance the resolution, identification, and quantification of analytes in complex matrices. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train deep neural networks on large datasets of simulated and experimental NMR, Raman, and mass spectra, coupled with chromatographic retention data. These models will be optimized to disentangle spectral overlaps, predict physicochemical properties, and infer molecular structures under varying experimental conditions. Quantum chemistry calculations (e.g., density functional theory for vibrational spectra and molecular dynamics for solvation effects) will supplement empirical data to improve model generalizability. The computational workflow will employ distributed computing for parallelized spectral simulation, hyperparameter optimization, and uncertainty quantification. Key outcomes include open-source software for automated spectral deconvolution, a predictive retention time database for untargeted metabolomics, and validated protocols for integrating simulation-driven insights into analytical workflows. By reducing reliance on resource-intensive trial-and-error experimentation, this work aims to accelerate method development in analytical chemistry while improving reproducibility and detection limits. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training, and computationally intensive quantum simulations required to achieve these objectives. Successful implementation will directly benefit interdisciplinary efforts in drug discovery, environmental toxicology, and clinical diagnostics by enabling more precise, data-driven analytical strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of techniques for analyzing and describing matter, including its precise composition and the interrelationships of constituent elements and compounds. Includes instruction in spectroscopy, chromatography, atomic absorption, photometry, chemical modeling, mathematical analysis, laboratory analysis procedures and equipment maintenance, and applications to specific research, industrial and health problems.

abstract: Current methodologies in computer hardware diagnostics predominantly rely on reactive measures, addressing failures post-occurrence, which leads to increased downtime and repair costs. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing predictive maintenance frameworks through advanced computational modeling and machine learning. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate stress conditions across critical hardware components, including power supplies, memory modules, and microprocessors, under varying operational loads and environmental factors. These simulations will generate large-scale datasets capturing failure precursors, such as voltage fluctuations, thermal thresholds, and signal integrity degradation. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will be trained on both simulated data and real-world repair logs to identify patterns predictive of impending hardware faults. The integration of distributed computing architectures will enable real-time analysis of diagnostic data streams from deployed systems, facilitating proactive intervention. Anticipated outcomes include optimized repair protocols, reduced operational downtime, and the development of open-source diagnostic tools tailored for technician training programs. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to transform hardware maintenance paradigms from reactive to predictive, enhancing both technical education curricula and industry practices in computer installation and repair. The scalability of this approach will be validated through benchmarking against traditional diagnostic workflows, with an emphasis on improving repair accuracy and resource efficiency in heterogeneous computing environments.
cip_title: Computer Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair computers and related instruments. Includes instruction in power supplies, number systems, memory structure, buffers and registers, microprocessor design, peripheral equipment, programming, and networking.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the efficacy of clinical pastoral counseling interventions in mitigating psychological distress among patients with chronic illnesses. While spiritual and emotional care is increasingly recognized as integral to holistic healthcare, quantifying its impact remains challenging due to the dynamic, context-dependent nature of patient-provider interactions and the multidimensional variables influencing outcomes. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in therapeutic effectiveness across diverse demographic and clinical cohorts, integrating linguistic, behavioral, and physiological data from counseling sessions, patient self-reports, and biometric monitoring. A computational pipeline will be developed to process unstructured textual data (e.g., session transcripts, patient journals) via natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including sentiment analysis and topic modeling, to map emotional trajectories and therapeutic themes. These outputs will be fused with structured datasets (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels, treatment adherence metrics) using machine learning models to predict intervention success and latent risk factors for emotional collapse or prolonged distress. Agent-based simulations will further model the cascading effects of tailored counseling strategies on long-term patient resilience. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across terabytes of multimodal data, training deep learning architectures, and running computationally intensive simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to optimize pastoral counseling protocols in acute and chronic care settings, actionable insights into the interplay of spiritual coping mechanisms and neurophysiological stress responses, and a publicly accessible toolkit for adaptive intervention design. By bridging computational analytics with pastoral care praxis, this work aims to establish an empirical foundation for integrating spiritual support into precision medicine paradigms, advancing a niche yet vital dimension of health sciences.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including but not limited to, ordained clergy and other counseling professionals to respond to the emotional and/or spiritual needs of patients and families in health care emergencies and other situations, and to consult with and counsel other health care professionals. Includes instruction in advanced interpersonal communication; individual and small group counseling; interdisciplinary teamwork; crisis management; extended care relationships; self-analysis; medical ethics; pastoral care art; spiritual dimensions of human growth and health; counseling psychology and therapy; and applications to grief, death, emotional collapse, injury, individual/family adjustment, and chronic illness situations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and semantic patterns within responsa literature—a corpus of rabbinic legal rulings spanning over a millennium—to uncover latent networks of influence and decision-making frameworks in Halacha (Jewish law). While traditional rabbinic scholarship relies on manual text analysis to trace legal precedents, the sheer volume and complexity of responsa (estimated at tens of thousands of documents in Hebrew and Aramaic) present a barrier to systematic, large-scale study. The research addresses this gap by applying computational methods to map the evolution of legal reasoning, identify underrepresented voices in halachic discourse, and model how cultural, geographic, and temporal factors shape rabbinic rulings. A hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and graph theory will be employed: transformer-based models fine-tuned on classical rabbinic texts will extract legal concepts and argumentative structures, while network analysis will visualize relationships between decisors, texts, and legal outcomes. Computational challenges include adapting NLP pipelines for non-standardized premodern Hebrew orthography, resolving referential ambiguity in citational practices, and handling multi-layered commentaries. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated workloads for model training and CPU-intensive simulations to test hypotheses about decision diffusion across historical Jewish communities. Outcomes will include an open-access annotated corpus of responsa, a toolset for computational rabbinics, and visualizations of legal influence networks. This work aims to advance both rabbinic scholarship and digital humanities methodologies, offering quantitative frameworks to complement qualitative textual analysis. By revealing macro-scale trends in Halacha, the project holds significance for understanding how religious legal systems balance continuity and adaptation—a question with implications for contemporary Jewish education and interfaith ethical discourse.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as Rabbis. Includes instruction in Talmud, Halacha, Liturgy and Rituals, Rabbinical Thought, Jewish Ethics, Jewish Education, Pastoral Counseling and Homiletics.

abstract: The increasing demand for precision in histologic diagnostics necessitates advancements in tissue processing workflows to improve reproducibility and reduce manual intervention. Current histologic techniques, while effective, exhibit variability in staining quality, tissue sectioning precision, and artifact identification, particularly when applied to diverse tissue types or degraded clinical samples. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model and optimize histotechnical processes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating machine learning (ML) models to predict optimal fixation, embedding, and staining protocols for specific tissue characteristics, and (2) simulating tissue sectioning dynamics under varying microtome parameters to minimize cutting artifacts. A hybrid approach will be employed, combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on digitized histology slides from public repositories (e.g., TCGA, HTAN) with finite element analysis simulations of tissue-mechanical interactions during sectioning. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of whole-slide images (WSIs) for feature extraction and the iterative refinement of 3D tissue deformation models. Computational outcomes will be validated against experimental data from controlled tissue processing trials conducted by histotechnician trainees. Anticipated deliverables include an open-access protocol optimization tool and a digital twin framework for virtual microtome calibration. This work addresses critical gaps in histotechnology education and practice by providing data-driven insights into process standardization while reducing reagent waste and diagnostic turnaround times. Successful implementation could transform how histologic technicians approach complex specimens, particularly in resource-constrained settings where trial-and-error methods remain prevalent. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the ∼50 TB of image data and ∼10⁶ core-hours required for model training and multiscale simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision and efficiency in machining processes by developing computational models for optimizing toolpath planning, material deformation prediction, and thermal management in metal fabrication. Traditional machining workflows often rely on iterative trial-and-error methods to address challenges such as tool wear, workpiece distortion, and heat-induced material degradation, leading to increased costs, material waste, and energy consumption. To overcome these limitations, this research will integrate physics-based simulations with machine learning (ML) to create predictive frameworks for machining parameter optimization. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution and thermal profiles during cutting operations, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate coolant flow and heat dissipation. These simulations will generate datasets to train ML models that correlate machining parameters (e.g., spindle speed, feed rate, tool geometry) with outcomes such as surface finish quality and tool longevity. HPC resources are critical to scaling these simulations across diverse materials (e.g., steel, aluminum, titanium) and machining configurations, enabling the exploration of complex parameter spaces impractical for physical testing. The resulting hybrid computational toolkit will be validated against experimental data from CNC milling and turning operations. Anticipated outcomes include open-access predictive models to guide toolpath programming, reduce scrap rates, and minimize energy use in industrial and educational machine shops. By bridging computational modeling with hands-on machining, this work aims to accelerate the adoption of data-driven practices in vocational training programs, equipping future technicians with skills to optimize digital and physical workflows. The project will also contribute benchmarks for integrating HPC-driven analytics into small-scale manufacturing, supporting sustainability goals in technology-driven trades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and modify metal parts in support of other manufacturing, repair or design activities, or as an independent business.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interactions between urban climate resilience policies, real estate valuation, and decentralized property investment patterns. The research addresses a critical gap in real estate analytics: current valuation models inadequately account for spatially heterogeneous climate risks (e.g., flood zones, heat islands) and their cascading effects on investor behavior in multi-jurisdictional markets. By integrating geospatial climate projections, granular property transaction data, and agent-based simulations of investor decision-making, we aim to quantify how localized adaptation policies influence cross-regional capital flows and long-term asset performance. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model interdependencies among municipal climate regulations with high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations of urban microclimates. These components will be coupled through a reinforcement learning system that simulates investor responses to evolving risk-return profiles across commercial and residential portfolios. The analysis will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to forecast valuation distributions under 12 climate policy scenarios at a 1km² resolution across three U.S. coastal metro regions. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing 50+ TB of LiDAR, satellite thermal imagery, and parcel-level transaction records while maintaining sub-hourly temporal resolution across decadal horizons. Expected outcomes include an open-source risk modeling platform capable of real-time policy impact assessments and a novel metric for climate-adjusted cap rates that incorporates spatial spillover effects. This work will provide actionable insights for municipalities balancing resilience investments with market stability and help institutional investors optimize climate-adaptive portfolio allocations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, buy, sell, appraise, and manage real estate. Includes instruction in land use development policy, real estate law, real estate marketing procedures, agency management, brokerage, property inspection and appraisal, real estate investing, leased and rental properties, commercial real estate, and property management.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize operational decision-making in multi-location restaurant enterprises through advanced computational modeling, addressing the challenge of dynamically balancing resource allocation, supply chain logistics, and labor management across geographically distributed operations. Traditional management approaches often struggle to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating consumer demand, perishable inventory constraints, and staff scheduling conflicts at scale. The project will develop a high-performance computing (HPC) framework integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to simulate complex operational scenarios. Agent-based models will represent individual restaurant units, suppliers, and customer behavior patterns, while discrete-event simulations will map cross-location interactions and resource flows.
