Machine learning components will analyze historical sales data, weather patterns, and local event calendars to predict demand surges and inventory requirements. The computational intensity of simultaneously modeling hundreds of interconnected agents and supply chain networks necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing food waste through just-in-time inventory systems, adaptive staffing algorithms that comply with labor regulations across jurisdictions, and scenario-testing capabilities for emergency preparedness (e.g., supply chain disruptions). The research will produce an open-source computational toolkit tailored for culinary management applications, bridging gaps between operations research and hospitality-specific constraints. By enabling data-driven decision-making at enterprise scale, this work aims to establish computational modeling as a transformative methodology in culinary management, with potential applications in sustainability initiatives and crisis response planning for the food service industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage food and beverage preparation and service operations, restaurant facilities, and catering services.  Includes instruction in food/beverage industry operations, cost control, purchasing and storage, business administration, logistics, personnel management, culinary arts, restaurant and menu planning, executive chef functions, event planning and management, health and safety, insurance, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of theological hermeneutics—the principles governing the interpretation of sacred texts—across decentralized religious communities from the 4th to 14th centuries. While doctrinal studies have traditionally relied on qualitative analysis of key texts, this research addresses a gap in systematic, large-scale comparative analysis of interpretive patterns and their socio-cultural drivers. The core challenge lies in processing a multilingual corpus of over 15,000 digitized theological manuscripts, sermons, and liturgical commentaries spanning Syriac, Coptic, Latin, and early Arabic traditions, which exhibit complex linguistic variations and non-standardized theological terminology. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for ancient Semitic and Afro-Asiatic languages, we will train transformer-based models to identify doctrinal motifs, trace their diffusion pathways, and map correlations between interpretive shifts and geopolitical events documented in parallel historical datasets. Computational workflows will integrate phylogenetic algorithms adapted from bioinformatics to model branching traditions of exegetical reasoning, while graph neural networks will reconstruct networks of influence among monastic centers and itinerant scholars. The scale of textual data and need for real-time alignment with archeological and climatological datasets necessitate HPC-grade parallel processing and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include 1) a quantitative framework for assessing theological innovation versus conservatism in premodern religious movements, 2) dynamic visualizations of doctrinal development across Eurasia and North Africa, and 3) open-source tools for diachronic analysis of theological semantics. By bridging computational linguistics and historical theology, this project aims to establish new methodologies for studying religious thought as a complex adaptive system, with implications for understanding contemporary hermeneutic conflicts in global faith communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the beliefs and doctrine of a particular religious faith from the intramural point of view of that faith. Includes instruction in systematic theology, historical theology, moral theology, doctrinal studies, dogmatics, apologetics, and applications to specific questions of ecclesiastical polity and religious life.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the rigorous analysis of nonlinear evolution equations arising in mathematical physics, particularly those governed by nonlocal operators and exhibiting multiscale dynamics. The primary research problem involves characterizing the well-posedness, long-time behavior, and stability of solutions to fractional dissipative systems in high-dimensional function spaces. Such equations, which model phenomena like anomalous diffusion and turbulence, present analytical challenges due to their intricate interplay of nonlinearity, nonlocality, and critical regularity thresholds. While recent theoretical advances have established existence results under certain constraints, the quantitative analysis of solution blow-up, pattern formation, and attractor dynamics remains underdeveloped. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining modern harmonic analysis tools with large-scale numerical simulations. The methodology integrates wavelet-based spectral decomposition for adaptive resolution of multiscale features, parallelized iterative schemes for solving high-dimensional integral equations, and GPU-accelerated time-stepping algorithms for long-horizon stability analysis. Key computational challenges include managing memory-intensive harmonic transforms in Sobolev spaces of fractional order and maintaining numerical fidelity across disparate temporal scales. High-performance computing resources are essential for executing parameter space explorations across varying fractional exponents and nonlinearity strengths, as well as for validating conjectures about energy transfer mechanisms in critical function spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative criteria for finite-time singularity formation in nonlocal reaction-diffusion systems, (2) classification of asymptotic stability regimes for weakly dissipative wave equations, and (3) optimized algorithms for functional-analytic computations in high-dimensional Besov spaces. The results will directly contribute to the mathematical foundations of nonlinear PDE theory while demonstrating novel synergies between abstract analysis and extreme-scale computation. By resolving persistent open problems about solution regularity in critical spaces, this work aims to establish new connections between harmonic analysis techniques and computational methods for infinite-dimensional dynamical systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and behavior of equations, multivariate solutions, functions, and dynamic systems. Includes instruction in differential equations, variation, approximations, complex variables, integrals, harmonic analysis and wavelet theory, dynamic systems, and applications to mathematical physics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and cognitive dynamics of emergent online communities in decentralized digital platforms, focusing on how ad hoc collectives negotiate shared norms and epistemic frameworks in the absence of centralized governance. As digital interactions increasingly supplant traditional physical communities, understanding the self-organizing mechanisms that underpin trust, conflict resolution, and knowledge validation in these spaces represents a critical social science challenge. The research employs a mixed-methods computational approach, combining large-scale network analysis of real-time interaction data from federated social platforms (e.g., Mastodon, Matrix) with agent-based modeling to simulate consensus-building processes under varying communication constraints. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets of timestamped user interactions, training graph neural networks to detect latent community boundaries, and running parallelized simulations of norm-formation scenarios across diverse synthetic populations. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of emergent governance patterns in decentralized digital spaces, (2) quantitative metrics for predicting community fragmentation or resilience based on early interaction networks, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing epistemic alignment processes in real-time collaboration environments. By bridging computational social science with network theory and cognitive modeling, this work addresses a critical gap in understanding how human social systems adapt to radically decentralized digital environments—a pressing concern as Web3 technologies and AI-mediated communication redefine collective human behavior. Results will inform both theoretical frameworks for studying post-institutional sociality and practical designs for next-generation collaborative platforms.
cip_definition: Any program in general social sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the identification and functional characterization of structural genetic variants (SVs) contributing to rare developmental disorders. While genome-wide association studies have identified numerous single-nucleotide variants linked to disease, SVs—including deletions, duplications, inversions, and translocations—remain understudied due to computational challenges in detection and interpretation. Current methods for SV analysis struggle with sensitivity and scalability when applied to large-scale whole-genome sequencing (WGS) datasets, limiting insights into their role in Mendelian conditions. We propose developing a novel computational pipeline integrating graph-based genome representations, machine learning–enhanced variant prioritization, and multi-omics functional annotation to resolve SVs at scale. The pipeline will process WGS data from 5,000 trios (affected probands and unaffected parents) from the NIH’s GREGoR Consortium, requiring parallelized alignment, variant calling, and population genetics analyses across petabytes of genomic data. Deep learning models trained on epigenomic profiles (ATAC-seq, Hi-C) will predict SV pathogenicity by assessing disruptions to 3D chromatin architecture and regulatory elements. Resource-intensive tasks include de novo assembly of complex genomic regions, haplotype phasing across diverse populations, and simulating SV effects on gene networks using systems biology models. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a validated, open-source SV detection framework optimized for HPC environments, 2) a catalog of high-confidence pathogenic SVs linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, and 3) mechanistic insights into how noncoding SVs dysregulate developmental pathways. This work will directly enhance clinical diagnostic yield for rare genetic diseases while providing a computational foundation for studying SVs in complex traits. Successful implementation requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning, high-memory nodes for genome graph traversal, and scalable storage for population-level genomic data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of human genetics from the standpoint of medical applications such as clinical diagnosis, genetic engineering and therapy, transplantation, and the study of genetic diseases and disabilities and their defense. Includes instruction in human molecular genetics; genetic factors causing disease; changes in gene expression during development, differentiation, and pathogenesis; recombinant DNA; gene therapy; clinical genetics; genetic epidemiology; immunogenetics; cytogenetics; and genetics of specific disorders and diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the structural evolution and logical coherence of epistemological arguments across diverse philosophical traditions, addressing the challenge of systematically evaluating large-scale textual corpora in philosophy. Traditional methods of close reading and manual comparison struggle to account for the complexity and volume of historical and cross-cultural philosophical works, limiting scholars’ ability to identify patterns, inconsistencies, or latent connections in epistemological discourse. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multilingual philosophical texts spanning ancient to contemporary sources, with a focus on theories of knowledge, justification, and belief. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be designed to extract argumentative structures, semantic relationships, and logical operators, while machine learning models will classify epistemological positions and trace conceptual shifts across temporal and cultural contexts. Network analysis will map the influence and divergence of ideas among philosophers, and automated logic validation tools will assess the formal consistency of reconstructed arguments. The scale of data—encompassing digitized primary texts, commentaries, and secondary literature—necessitates parallelized computation, large-memory nodes, and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access database of annotated epistemological arguments with metadata on their logical and historical relationships, (2) quantitative insights into understudied cross-traditional dialogues, and (3) a methodological toolkit for computational philosophy. This work will advance scholarly understanding of how epistemological frameworks develop, intersect, and diverge, while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC-driven approaches in philosophical research. By integrating computational rigor with philosophical inquiry, the project aims to bridge methodological gaps in the humanities and stimulate interdisciplinary innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on ideas and their logical structure, including arguments and investigations about abstract and real phenomena. Includes instruction in logic, ethics, aesthetics, epistemology, metaphysics, symbolism, and history of philosophy, and applications to the theoretical foundations and methods of other disciplines.

abstract: Forensic investigations increasingly rely on integrating complex, multi-modal datasets—including DNA sequences, digital evidence, bloodstain patterns, and crime scene imagery—to reconstruct events and identify suspects. However, the volume, heterogeneity, and latency of these data sources pose significant challenges to timely and accurate analysis, particularly when traditional computational tools struggle to scale. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to automate and enhance forensic evidence processing. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) optimizing parallelized workflows for rapid DNA profile matching and mixture deconvolution using probabilistic genotyping algorithms; (2) training deep learning models on GPU clusters to classify bloodstain patterns and fingerprint features from high-resolution crime scene images; and (3) simulating large-scale crime scene reconstructions via agent-based modeling to evaluate competing hypotheses under varying environmental parameters. By leveraging HPC resources, these methods will reduce processing times for forensic workflows from days to hours while improving analytical precision, especially for degraded or ambiguous evidence. The project will also pilot a cloud-accessible platform to enable collaboration between forensic laboratories and law enforcement agencies, adhering to chain-of-custody and data integrity standards. Outcomes will directly support homeland security priorities by accelerating investigative timelines, reducing backlogs, and strengthening evidentiary rigor in legal proceedings. This work bridges computational innovation with forensic practice, establishing scalable methodologies for next-generation crime scene analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the physical, biomedical, and social sciences to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence, human testimony and criminal suspects. Includes instruction in forensic medicine, forensic dentistry, anthropology, psychology, entomology, pathology, forensic laboratory technology and autopsy procedures, DNA and blood pattern analysis, crime scene analysis, crime scene photography, fingerprint technology, document analysis, witness and suspect examination procedures, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing school counseling interventions through large-scale analysis of student behavioral, academic, and psychosocial data. School counselors face growing demands to address complex student needs—including mental health crises, equity gaps, and college/career readiness—yet lack robust tools to systematically evaluate the longitudinal efficacy of interventions across diverse populations. Current studies rely on small-sample surveys or qualitative methods, limiting generalizability and real-time decision support. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating anonymized student records (e.g., grades, attendance, disciplinary actions), demographic data, and counselor-reported intervention logs from statewide K-12 datasets. Machine learning models, including transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for analyzing counselor case notes and graph neural networks (GNNs) to map intervention impact across student networks, will be developed to identify predictors of intervention success and equity disparities. HPC resources are critical for training these models on multi-terabyte datasets, conducting hyperparameter optimization at scale, and simulating intervention scenarios via agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive toolkit for personalizing counseling strategies based on student subpopulation characteristics, (2) actionable metrics to quantify equity in resource allocation, and (3) open-source dashboards enabling counselors to visualize intervention pathways and outcomes. By bridging computational social science and counselor education, this work aims to transform reactive practices into proactive, data-driven support systems while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for student privacy. The scalability of these methods will provide a template for replication in other educational contexts, advancing empirical foundations for equitable student support.
cip_title: Counselor Education/ School Counseling and Guidance Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the theory and principles of guidance and counseling to the provision of support for the personal, social, educational, and vocational development of students, and the organizing of guidance services within elementary, middle and secondary educational institutions. Includes instruction in legal and professional requirements, therapeutic counselor intervention, vocational counseling, and related sociological and psychological foundations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of multigenerational family systems under stress using advanced computational modeling, with a focus on understanding resilience patterns and systemic feedback loops. Family systems, as complex adaptive systems, exhibit nonlinear interactions influenced by cultural, psychological, and socioeconomic variables. Traditional qualitative or survey-based methods often struggle to capture these interdependencies at scale, particularly when analyzing longitudinal or cross-cultural data. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating family decision-making processes, emotional transmission, and resource-sharing behaviors across generations. The model will integrate empirical datasets from sociology and psychology, including trauma response metrics, household economic data, and intergenerational communication patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize thousands of family archetypes, run Monte Carlo simulations testing intervention scenarios (e.g., policy changes, therapeutic approaches), and perform sensitivity analyses on emergent system behaviors. Computational challenges include managing stochastic interactions among agents with heterogeneous belief systems, scaling network analyses for extended kinship structures, and processing high-dimensional time-series outputs. Expected outcomes include identifying critical leverage points for enhancing family resilience, quantifying the systemic impacts of socioeconomic policies on family cohesion, and generating predictive frameworks for risk stratification in social work contexts. This work bridges computational social science with family systems theory, offering a novel methodology for studying relational dynamics that could inform both clinical practice and policymaking. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will provide a foundation for interdisciplinary research into complex familial interactions that traditional disciplinary approaches cannot adequately model.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the family as a social unit in its developmental, dynamic, comparative, and structural aspects, and the significance of the family as a system that impacts individuals and society. Includes instruction in related principles of sociology, psychology, behavioral sciences, and the humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of integrating advanced computational modeling into vocational teacher education, specifically for trades such as advanced manufacturing, construction, and automotive systems. As industrial technologies evolve rapidly, educators require scalable, immersive training tools to simulate complex, real-world environments that are otherwise cost-prohibitive or unsafe to replicate in classroom settings. However, existing educational simulations often lack the fidelity and adaptability to mirror modern industrial systems, limiting their utility in preparing instructors to teach cutting-edge technical skills. To bridge this gap, we propose developing high-fidelity, interactive simulations of industrial workflows (e.g., automated production lines, structural engineering processes) using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. These simulations will employ agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation frameworks to replicate equipment behavior, material flows, and human-machine interactions at scale. By leveraging GPU-accelerated rendering and parallelized computational workflows, the models will support real-time adjustments to variables such as equipment failure rates, supply chain disruptions, and safety protocols, enabling instructors to design dynamic, scenario-based lessons. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to anonymized user interaction data to identify patterns in skill acquisition and optimize simulation difficulty for diverse learner cohorts. The outcomes will include an open-access repository of modular simulation templates, validated through partnerships with regional trade schools and industry stakeholders. This resource will empower vocational educators to deliver standardized, immersive training that aligns with industry 4.0 competencies while reducing reliance on physical infrastructure. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for large-scale parameter sweeps, real-time multi-user environments, and high-resolution physics modeling—necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to ensure feasibility and scalability across educational institutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational trades and industries programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project investigates the computational modeling of cross-linguistic semantic change driven by multilingual online communication, with a focus on under-resourced languages. As digital platforms accelerate language contact and hybridization, traditional frameworks for analyzing semantic shifts struggle to capture the dynamic, large-scale interactions between speakers of typologically diverse languages. The project addresses this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to model semantic networks across 50+ languages, prioritizing Indigenous and minority languages with limited digital corpora. Using transformer-based architectures adapted for low-resource settings, we will train multilingual embeddings on scraped web data (social media, forums, collaborative platforms) and historical texts, then quantify cross-linguistic convergence/divergence patterns through graph-based metrics. Key computational challenges include scaling dynamic time warping algorithms for diachronic comparisons across language pairs and implementing distributed training for morphologically complex languages. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of 15TB+ unstructured text data, iterative refinement of attention mechanisms for code-switched utterances, and agent-based simulations of semantic propagation in language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include: 1) a publicly accessible database tracking semantic shifts in under-documented languages, 2) novel metrics for quantifying language vitality based on digital interaction patterns, and 3) open-source tools enabling real-time monitoring of emergent semantic phenomena in multilingual online spaces. This work advances computational linguistics by bridging typological research with sociocultural language dynamics, offering methodological innovations for analyzing language change in the digital age while supporting efforts to document and preserve linguistic diversity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language, language development, and relationships among languages and language groups from a humanistic and/or scientific perspective. Includes instruction in subjects such as psycholinguistics, behavioral linguistics, language acquisition, sociolinguistics, mathematical and computational linguistics, grammatical theory and theoretical linguistics, philosophical linguistics, philology and historical linguistics, comparative linguistics, phonetics, phonemics, dialectology, semantics, functional grammar and linguistics, language typology, lexicography, morphology and syntax, orthography, stylistics, structuralism, rhetoric, and applications to artificial intelligence.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic infectious diseases present critical challenges to global public health and animal welfare. Current limitations in understanding the complex interactions between pathogens, hosts, and environmental factors hinder the development of targeted prevention and treatment strategies. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps through advanced computational modeling and large-scale genomic analyses. Specifically, we aim to investigate the evolutionary dynamics of high-consequence pathogens, including avian influenza viruses, antimicrobial-resistant bacterial strains, and vector-borne parasites, to identify drivers of cross-species transmission and adaptive mechanisms. Computational workflows will integrate multi-omics datasets (e.g., whole-genome sequencing, metagenomics, and host transcriptomics) with epidemiological and ecological data to construct predictive models of disease spread and host-pathogen interactions. Agent-based simulations will assess intervention strategies under varying ecological scenarios, while molecular dynamics modeling will probe structural determinants of viral entry and antibody evasion. These analyses demand significant memory and parallel processing capabilities due to the scale of genomic datasets (>100 TB), the complexity of spatiotemporal models, and the need for rapid iteration in machine learning frameworks. Expected outcomes include the identification of genetic markers associated with host specificity, predictive maps of outbreak risk under climate change scenarios, and mechanistic insights into pathogen resistance. By elucidating critical pathways in disease transmission and adaptation, this research will directly inform vaccine design, surveillance protocols, and targeted biosecurity measures. The proposed computational workflows will also establish scalable frameworks for real-time genomic epidemiology, enhancing preparedness for emerging zoonotic threats. This project aligns with broader efforts to mitigate the economic and health impacts of infectious diseases in animal populations and human communities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of zoonotic infectious diseases, disease mechanisms, and prevention and treatment strategies. Includes instruction in disease pathogenesis, vector biology, mycobacterial infection, blood parasites, retroviruses, food-borne diseases, new infectious agents, ecotoxicology, mechanisms of disease transfer, antibody resistance, comparative pathology, communicable diseases, and disease prevention and eradication.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in integrating and analyzing heterogeneous, large-scale disease registry datasets to improve public health surveillance and clinical decision-making. Disease registries aggregate complex demographic, diagnostic, treatment, and outcomes data across populations, but computational limitations hinder real-time analysis, particularly when linking registry data with external sources such as genomic databases, environmental exposure records, and socioeconomic datasets. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to harmonize multi-modal health data while preserving privacy, enabling high-dimensional analytics to identify disease patterns, risk factors, and disparities. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to deploy parallelized data pipelines for cleaning, transforming, and standardizing registry entries using natural language processing (NLP) for unstructured clinical text and federated learning techniques for secure cross-institutional analysis. Machine learning models will be trained on GPU clusters to predict disease progression, treatment responses, and population-level outcomes, with a focus on rare diseases where sparse data necessitates large-scale simulations. Statistical frameworks will be implemented to account for missing data biases and temporal confounders in longitudinal registry entries. The project will utilize containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility across HPC environments. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for registry data interoperability, validated predictive models for early intervention targeting, and novel metrics for registry data quality assessment. By enabling efficient processing of petabyte-scale registry datasets, this work will advance precision public health strategies, inform policy decisions, and enhance the operational capacity of disease registries to support rapid research responses during emerging health crises. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in current single-node systems, ensuring scalable, privacy-preserving analytics that align with modern regulatory requirements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to find, interpret, and record demographic and medical information on individuals for healthcare agencies and disease registries. Includes instruction in anatomy, data management, disease registry organization and operations, epidemiology, ethics, fundamentals of disease coding and staging, medical terminology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, physiology, quality management, and statistics.

abstract: Stellar atmospheric dynamics in magnetically active stars present unresolved challenges in reconciling multiwavelength observations with theoretical models, particularly regarding energy transport mechanisms and transient phenomena like flares. Current simulations often oversimplify the coupling between magnetic fields, radiative transfer, and plasma turbulence, limiting their predictive power for next-generation observatories. This project addresses these gaps by developing a novel computational framework for 3D radiation-magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) simulations of stellar atmospheres, incorporating non-gray radiative transfer, non-equilibrium ionization, and small-scale dynamo processes. The research leverages the open-source code COOLFluiD, modified with GPU-accelerated radiative solvers and adaptive mesh refinement to resolve critical scales from photospheric granulation (10–100 km) to chromospheric structures (1,000–10,000 km). Each simulation tracks the evolution of magnetic field topology and energy dissipation over stellar rotation timescales, requiring petascale computational resources to manage 10^4–10^5 core-hours per parameter set. Key deliverables include the first self-consistent models of magnetic reconnection events in partially ionized stellar atmospheres and synthetic spectral line profiles accounting for non-Local Thermal Equilibrium effects. These results will directly interpret high-cadence spectroscopic data from the European Solar Telescope and Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope, constraining mechanisms for coronal heating and stellar wind acceleration. By quantifying the role of magnetic intermittency in mass-loss rates across stellar spectral types, the project will refine evolutionary models of stars hosting exoplanetary systems. The computational tools developed will be disseminated to the astrophysics community via a public repository, enabling broader investigations into stellar activity cycles and their impact on galactic environments. This work aligns with the program’s focus on advancing observational astrophysics through cutting-edge numerical methods while training researchers in exascale-ready simulation techniques.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and observational study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena. Includes instruction in cosmology, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: Veterinary radiology faces significant challenges in processing and analyzing large-scale, multi-modal imaging datasets (e.g., CT, MRI, nuclear medicine) to diagnose complex diseases such as oncology or musculoskeletal disorders in animals. Current workflows lack the computational capacity to efficiently integrate high-resolution 3D imaging with dynamic functional data, limiting diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment planning. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable advanced quantitative analysis of veterinary radiological data. The research will focus on three objectives: (1) creating AI-driven segmentation models to automate the detection of tumors and anatomical anomalies in heterogeneous animal species; (2) implementing GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations to optimize radiation therapy dosing for irregular animal anatomies; and (3) establishing a federated learning platform to analyze distributed imaging datasets while preserving data privacy across veterinary institutions. The computational workflow will utilize containerized environments to ensure reproducibility and scale across HPC clusters, with iterative model training on multi-terabyte datasets comprising diverse species and pathologies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for lesion progression in canine osteosarcoma and feline oral squamous cell carcinoma, as well as open-source tools for species-specific radiation dose calculation. This work addresses critical gaps in veterinary precision medicine by enabling rapid, large-scale analysis of imaging biomarkers that are infeasible with conventional computing resources. The resulting infrastructure will directly support multi-institutional clinical trials and advance translational applications of radiomics in veterinary oncology, while establishing scalable computational methodologies for emerging hybrid imaging modalities in animal healthcare.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of radiologic imaging and therapies to diagnose and treat animal diseases and health problems. May included related research in the use and handling of equipment for radionuclides detection and application.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of dynamic, large-scale Bayesian hierarchical models for analyzing spatial-temporal business data in the context of climate-driven market volatility. Traditional business forecasting tools often struggle to integrate high-dimensional environmental datasets—such as satellite-derived climate metrics, regional regulatory shifts, and supply chain geolocation data—with real-time market performance indicators. The computational complexity of modeling nonlinear interactions across these variables, particularly under uncertainty, exceeds the capacity of standard statistical software and workstations. This project proposes a novel computational framework combining Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods with distributed tensor factorization to estimate latent relationships between climate stressors and sector-specific financial outcomes. The HPC environment will enable parallelized sampling for multi-level models spanning terabytes of heterogeneous data from public (NOAA, IPCC) and proprietary (global logistics sensors, equity trading APIs) sources. Key challenges include optimizing memory allocation for irregularly sampled time series and validating model stability across GPU-CPU hybrid architectures. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source library for scalable Bayesian inference on business-environment interdependencies, (2) predictive insights into climate-adaptive investment strategies for Fortune 500 partners, and (3) methodological advancements in uncertainty quantification for decision-making under cascading ecological and economic shocks. By bridging computational statistics, environmental science, and business analytics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven resilience planning in industries facing escalating climate-related financial disclosures. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated parameter estimation, hyperparameter tuning via evolutionary algorithms, and sensitivity analyses across 50+ sector-specific model variants.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data. Includes instruction in statistical theory and methods, computer applications, data analysis and display, long- and short-term forecasting methods, and market performance analysis.

abstract: Pediatric rheumatological disorders, including juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), pediatric lupus, and inherited connective tissue diseases, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their clinical heterogeneity, complex pathophysiology, and variable treatment responses. Current approaches to risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making rely on limited biomarkers and population-level data, which fail to account for the dynamic interplay of genetic, immunological, and environmental factors in individual patients. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a computational framework integrating multi-omics data, longitudinal clinical records, and advanced imaging to enable personalized prediction of disease trajectories and treatment outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, and proteomic datasets from a multi-center cohort of 1,200 patients, alongside biomechanical imaging of joint and muscle tissues. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and transformer-based architectures, will be trained to identify disease subphenotypes, predict flare risk, and optimize treatment recommendations. Agent-based modeling will simulate immune-stromal cell interactions and tissue remodeling processes to uncover mechanistic drivers of treatment resistance. The computational workflow will require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, iterative hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale in silico perturbation experiments, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for JIA remission and lupus nephritis risk, (2) novel digital biomarkers derived from multimodal data fusion, and (3) open-source tools for pediatric rheumatology biomarker discovery. By enabling real-time analysis of complex biological networks and patient-specific treatment simulations, this work aims to transform clinical decision-making in pediatric rheumatology, reducing diagnostic delays and improving targeted therapeutic strategies for children with chronic musculoskeletal diseases.
cip_definition: Research on how to diagnose and treat diseases of joints, muscle, bones, and tendons in children and young adults, including arthritis, back pain, muscle strains, common athletic injuries, and collagen diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of next-generation automotive systems, including electric and hybrid propulsion, energy storage, and aerodynamic efficiency, which demand high-fidelity modeling of complex multi-physics interactions. Current simulation tools and physical prototyping methods are constrained by computational limitations, restricting the exploration of design parameters under dynamic real-world conditions. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct large-scale simulations that integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization. The computational workflow will focus on optimizing thermal management systems for lithium-ion batteries, reducing aerodynamic drag through parametric vehicle shape studies, and predicting material fatigue in lightweight composite structures under varied load cycles. These simulations will employ parallelized solvers and scalable algorithms to handle millions of mesh elements and transient boundary conditions, enabling rapid iteration of designs while maintaining accuracy. The project also includes validation phases using experimental data from wind tunnel tests and battery cyclers to ensure model fidelity. Expected outcomes include the identification of design configurations that improve energy efficiency by 15–20%, extend battery lifespan, and reduce vehicle emissions. By integrating HPC-driven insights into the Automotive Engineering Technology curriculum, this work will enhance student proficiency in computational methods and foster industry partnerships through actionable data for prototyping. The requested resources will directly support the program’s mission to advance sustainable transportation technologies while reducing reliance on costly physical testing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Child development is shaped by dynamic interactions between individual cognitive processes, social environments, and evolving cultural contexts. However, existing models often oversimplify these interactions by treating them as static or unidirectional, limiting their capacity to predict long-term outcomes or inform interventions. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate and analyze the emergence of self-regulation skills in children aged 3–8 years, integrating neurocognitive, behavioral, and sociolinguistic data within a unified agent-based modeling (ABM) paradigm. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how nonlinear feedback loops between caregiver communication patterns, peer interactions, and neural maturation jointly influence developmental trajectories. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of these multiscale simulations, which will parameterize thousands of synthetic agents using real-world developmental datasets, including longitudinal eye-tracking records, naturalistic audio recordings of caregiver-child dyads, and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data. Bayesian optimization methods will be deployed to iteratively refine model parameters, while graph neural networks will identify latent interaction patterns predictive of self-regulation milestones. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating developmental cascades in diverse sociocultural contexts, (2) evidence-based criteria for identifying at-risk profiles through computational biomarkers, and (3) actionable insights for tailoring community programs that align with neurodevelopmental sensitive periods. By bridging developmental science with computational modeling, this work advances theoretical frameworks for understanding emergent complexity in child development while providing scalable tools to inform policy and practice. The requested HPC allocation will directly support parallelized simulation runs, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale sensitivity analyses that are computationally infeasible on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the intellectual, social, emotional, and biological development of children and the planning and design of related human services. Includes instruction in parent-child relations, parenting practices, special needs of children, parental and environmental influences on child development, external support services, and related public policy issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing artificial intelligence (AI) applications in clinical decision-making, with a focus on liability, algorithmic bias, and compliance risks. As AI tools become integral to diagnostics and treatment planning, gaps persist in understanding how existing health law doctrines—such as tort liability, informed consent, and anti-discrimination statutes—apply to opaque, adaptive algorithms. The research addresses this problem by constructing a computational legal analytics pipeline to model interactions between AI system behaviors, regulatory constraints, and litigation outcomes. Using natural language processing (NLP), we will process a corpus of U.S. case law, federal health regulations, and insurance claim records to identify latent patterns in legal disputes involving AI-driven care. Graph neural networks will map relationships between algorithmic design choices (e.g., interpretability thresholds, training data provenance) and statutory compliance metrics. Monte Carlo simulations will then project liability risk landscapes under hypothetical regulatory scenarios, such as stricter transparency mandates or shifts in burden-of-proof standards. The computational workload requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale legal texts and synthetic patient datasets, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale graph traversals. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to assess litigation risks associated with clinical AI deployments and evidence-based recommendations for updating liability doctrines in model governance policies. By quantifying how technical and legal variables co-evolve, this work aims to establish computational jurisprudence as a methodology for anticipatory health law research, bridging gaps between algorithmic accountability practices and regulatory enforcement mechanisms.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies and regulations affecting the health care industry, health professions, health services and insurance industries, and patients.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics (DBP), focusing on the integration of large-scale, multimodal datasets to identify biomarkers and mechanistic pathways underlying neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). A critical challenge in DBP research is the heterogeneous nature of developmental trajectories and behavioral outcomes, compounded by the complexity of integrating genetic, neuroimaging, electronic health record (EHR), and longitudinal behavioral data. Traditional computational tools are insufficient for handling the volume, dimensionality, and temporal resolution of these datasets, limiting the ability to model dynamic interactions between biological, environmental, and clinical factors. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining machine learning, network analysis, and multilevel modeling to analyze high-dimensional datasets. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of genomic data (e.g., whole-exome sequencing), voxel-based morphometry from MRI scans, and time-series behavioral assessments, while preserving data security for sensitive EHRs. Key objectives include (1) developing predictive models of developmental outcomes using federated learning approaches to harmonize multi-institutional data, (2) identifying gene-environment interactions through genome-wide association studies (GWAS) coupled with geospatial environmental exposure data, and (3) simulating neural network dynamics to test hypotheses about atypical neurodevelopment. Expected outcomes include novel biomarkers for early risk stratification, validated computational models of developmental trajectories, and open-source tools for scalable DBP data analysis. By elucidating mechanisms underlying variability in treatment response, this work will directly inform personalized intervention strategies. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome computational bottlenecks in processing petabyte-scale datasets and running iterative simulations, which are infeasible on local infrastructure. This project aligns with national priorities in precision medicine for neurodevelopmental disorders and has the potential to transform clinical practice in DBP through data-driven diagnostic and therapeutic advances.
cip_definition: Research focused on Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision horticulture through the development of predictive models for optimizing plant growth and stress resilience under dynamic environmental conditions. Current horticultural practices face challenges in balancing resource efficiency (e.g., water, fertilizers) with crop yield and quality, particularly as climate variability intensifies. Traditional experimental approaches to evaluate plant-environment interactions are limited by spatial and temporal scalability, hindering rapid adaptation to emerging stressors. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating hyperspectral imaging data, genomic datasets, and microclimate sensor networks to model physiological responses of high-value horticultural crops (e.g., greenhouse tomatoes, ornamental shrubs) across growth stages. Machine learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees, will be trained on multimodal datasets to predict nutrient uptake efficiency, drought tolerance, and disease susceptibility under simulated environmental scenarios. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization for these models, as well as parallelized simulations of genotype-by-environment interactions across 10,000+ virtual crop trials. Expected outcomes include actionable thresholds for irrigation scheduling, targeted genetic markers for stress-tolerant cultivars, and dynamic risk maps for pathogen outbreaks in controlled agricultural environments. By quantifying trade-offs between yield, resource use, and economic viability at unprecedented resolution, this work will provide growers with decision-support tools to implement climate-adaptive practices. The computational pipelines developed will be modularly designed for broader application to perennial and ornamental species, fostering innovation in sustainable horticulture operations. This project directly aligns with institutional priorities in agricultural technology while avoiding overlap with natural resources conservation domains, focusing exclusively on production-scale plant management challenges.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general production and processing of domesticated plants, shrubs, flowers, foliage, trees, groundcovers, and related plant materials; the management of technical and business operations connected with horticultural services; and the basic scientific principles needed to understand plants and their management and care.

abstract: Orthopedic disorders, including degenerative joint diseases, traumatic fractures, and musculoskeletal deformities, present significant clinical challenges due to their heterogeneity and complex biomechanical interactions. Traditional experimental approaches often fail to capture patient-specific variability or predict long-term outcomes of surgical interventions, limiting personalized treatment optimization. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale biomechanical processes in bone and soft tissue, integrating patient imaging, genomic data, and dynamic load simulations. The research will address two core problems: (1) predicting post-surgical bone remodeling patterns in joint replacement patients using finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning, and (2) optimizing implant design parameters through large-scale parametric simulations accounting for anatomical diversity. High-resolution CT/MRI datasets from a clinical cohort (n=1,200) will inform patient-specific models, while GPU-accelerated solvers will enable real-time simulation of mechanobiological responses across spatial scales. A novel deep learning architecture will be developed to reduce computational costs in uncertainty quantification, training on HPC-generated datasets to predict stress-shielding risks and osseointegration outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for preoperative planning, a database of biomechanically optimized implant configurations, and new biomarkers for early intervention in osteoporosis progression. By enabling rapid iteration through billions of potential physiological scenarios, HPC resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in static, population-averaged orthopedic models. This work directly aligns with clinical priorities to reduce revision surgeries, improve implant longevity, and advance precision orthopedics through computationally driven insights into bone adaptation mechanisms.
cip_definition: Research focused on Orthopedic

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in the design and installation of customized home furnishings through the development of a computational framework for optimizing spatial, aesthetic, and functional parameters in residential environments. Current practices in home furnishings installation rely heavily on manual measurements, static design templates, and trial-and-error approaches, leading to material waste, prolonged project timelines, and suboptimal ergonomic outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-modal simulation platform that integrates 3D spatial modeling, material stress analysis, and machine learning-driven consumer preference prediction. The computational workflow will process real-world data from LiDAR scans of client spaces, textile durability metrics, and historical client interaction patterns to generate adaptive installation plans. Key technical challenges include resolving conflicts between aesthetic recommendations (e.g., color harmony, stylistic coherence) and structural constraints (e.g., weight distribution, fabric tension) through parallelized optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support system capable of simulating over 10,000 design permutations per project while accounting for sustainability metrics such as material waste reduction and energy-efficient fabrication pathways. The research will specifically advance computational methods for non-rectangular space utilization—a critical gap in home furnishings software—by developing GPU-accelerated tessellation algorithms for irregular architectural features. Successful implementation could reduce average project planning time by 40% while improving client satisfaction through personalized, data-driven design proposals. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational geometry, behavioral analytics, and textile science within the understudied domain of residential space optimization, offering methodological innovations applicable to emerging smart home ecosystems and sustainable interior design practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in home furnishings and decorations. Includes instruction in selecting, purchasing, and designing home furnishings, decorations, and equipment; floral design; accessory construction; textiles; and upholstery.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in music management, specifically optimizing decision-making processes for music organizations and events in dynamic, data-rich environments. The research focuses on developing computational models to analyze large-scale datasets spanning music consumption patterns, marketing campaign efficacy, and logistical constraints in event management. A key problem lies in synthesizing heterogeneous data—streaming metrics, social media engagement, ticket sales, and artist contract terms—into actionable insights for stakeholders. Traditional methods struggle with the volume and velocity of these datasets, necessitating advanced computational approaches. The project will employ machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and reinforcement learning, to model audience behavior, simulate marketing scenarios, and predict revenue outcomes under varying constraints. Agent-based modeling will further test resource allocation strategies for concert logistics, venue operations, and artist-fan interaction networks. These simulations will integrate real-world variables such as regional copyright laws, labor agreements, and supply chain disruptions. By parallelizing computations across HPC clusters, the team aims to reduce model training times from weeks to days while scaling analyses to global music markets. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive budget allocation, risk-aware contract negotiation frameworks, and predictive systems for tour routing optimization. Results will be validated against historical case studies from partner music festivals and artist management firms. This work directly addresses gaps in data-driven decision support for an industry facing increasing complexity in audience fragmentation, digital platform dominance, and sustainability pressures. The computational infrastructure requested will enable transformative analyses at the intersection of arts administration, business analytics, and cultural policy, with implications for equitable resource distribution in music ecosystems.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage music organizations, operations, facilities, and personnel. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; music products merchandising; artist agency and promotion; music law; and applications to specific activities such as managing theaters, recording studios and companies, bands and other ensembles, individual artists, and music organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on the Albanian language, with a focus on its dialects, historical evolution, and modern applications. Despite Albanian’s unique linguistic heritage and status as an Indo-European isolate, computational tools for its analysis remain underdeveloped compared to those for major global languages. The research problem centers on the lack of large-scale, dialect-aware models capable of processing Albanian texts, particularly given the structural divergences between Gheg and Tosk dialects and the influence of historical language contact. To address this, the project will compile and digitize a corpus of Albanian texts spanning pre-modern to contemporary sources, including regional publications and oral narratives, with metadata tagging for dialect, genre, and period. Computational methods will involve training transformer-based language models optimized for code-switching between dialects, developing algorithms for diachronic phonetic analysis (e.g., tracking shifts in vowel systems), and simulating language change through agent-based modeling. These tasks require HPC resources due to the scale of data (estimated 10–15 TB), the complexity of parallelizing dialect-specific NLP pipelines, and the need for iterative hyperparameter tuning in deep learning workflows. Expected outcomes include the first open-source NLP toolkit for Albanian dialect processing, a publicly accessible digital corpus annotated for linguistic features, and quantitative models of dialectal divergence. The project will directly support pedagogical tools for Albanian language instruction, inform policy on language preservation, and enable applications in automated translation for regional technology sectors. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to position Albanian studies at the forefront of digital humanities while addressing critical gaps in resources for under-resourced languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Albanian language. Includes instruction in Albanian/Illyrian philology; Ghegg and Tosk dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and behavioral mechanisms underlying music therapy interventions for individuals with acquired communication disorders, such as aphasia and apraxia of speech, using advanced computational modeling. While music therapy has shown empirical promise in enhancing speech rehabilitation, the field lacks robust quantitative frameworks to characterize how specific auditory-motor entrainment protocols modulate neural plasticity or optimize therapeutic outcomes. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating high-resolution neuroimaging data, acoustic feature extraction, and patient-specific biophysical models to decode the dynamic interplay between rhythmic auditory stimuli, cortical reorganization, and functional recovery. The computational approach employs machine learning pipelines to analyze multimodal datasets (fMRI, EEG, and kinematic speech recordings) from 120 participants undergoing rhythm-based therapy, identifying patterns in neural oscillation coupling, sensorimotor synchronization, and speech production metrics. Concurrently, biologically constrained neural network models will simulate intervention effects on damaged language networks, incorporating individual lesion profiles and neurotransmitter dynamics. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing terabytes of temporally dense neuroimaging data, training deep learning architectures on heterogeneous feature sets, and running large-scale parameter sweeps in personalized neural simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking therapeutic music parameters (tempo, spectral complexity, pulse clarity) to neurobehavioral response profiles, enabling data-driven personalization of intervention protocols. The project aims to establish foundational computational tools for optimizing music therapy efficacy while advancing mechanistic understanding of auditory-motor integration in neurorehabilitation. By leveraging HPC capabilities to address the multidimensionality of music-based interventions, this work will foster translational innovation at the intersection of clinical neuroscience, computational psychiatry, and therapeutic arts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in association with a rehabilitation team or in private practice, to use music in therapeutic relationships to address the physical, psychological, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of clients. Includes instruction in music theory and performance, human growth and development, biomedical sciences, abnormal psychology, disabling conditions, patient assessment and diagnosis, treatment plan development and implementation, clinical evaluation, record-keeping, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Chiropractic care relies on precise spinal adjustments to address vertebral misalignments and their systemic effects, yet the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying optimal clinical outcomes remain incompletely understood. Current experimental and clinical methods lack the resolution to model the complex, dynamic interactions between spinal structures, neural pathways, and adjustment forces in patient-specific contexts. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models of spinal biomechanics and simulate the effects of chiropractic interventions. Using anonymized patient imaging data (MRI, CT) and clinical records, we will construct finite element models of spinal segments to analyze load distribution, tissue deformation, and joint kinematics during manual adjustments. These models will integrate neural network simulations to predict how biomechanical changes influence proprioceptive feedback and autonomic nervous system activity. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will process longitudinal clinical datasets to identify patterns linking adjustment techniques, patient demographics, and health outcomes. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated solvers for finite element analysis and distributed computing frameworks for large-scale data analytics. By coupling mechanistic simulations with data-driven inference, this research aims to establish predictive relationships between adjustment parameters, biomechanical responses, and therapeutic efficacy. Expected outcomes include optimized adjustment protocols for specific vertebral misalignment patterns, personalized treatment planning tools, and a foundational computational framework for hypothesis testing in chiropractic research. The project will enhance evidence-based practice by providing quantitative insights into adjustment mechanisms while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in advancing chiropractic science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of chiropractic, a health care and healing system based on the application of non-invasive treatments and spinal adjustments to alleviate health problems caused by vertebral misalignments affecting bodily function as derived from the philosophy of Daniel Palmer. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, chiropractic theory and science, postural and spinal analysis, diagnostic radiology and ultrasound, adjustment technique, patient counseling, professional standards and ethics, and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model language acquisition dynamics in multilingual K-12 classrooms, with the goal of optimizing instructional strategies for emergent bilingual students. Current approaches to designing bilingual education curricula often rely on static proficiency categorizations, failing to account for the nonlinear interactions between learners’ multiple languages, sociocultural contexts, and instructional interventions. To address this gap, we propose implementing a high-performance agent-based modeling (ABM) system that simulates classroom-scale second language development under variable teaching conditions. The computational model will integrate psycholinguistic theories of cross-linguistic transfer with empirical datasets from dual-language classrooms, including longitudinal proficiency scores, language use patterns, and demographic factors. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate agent behaviors using real-world classroom observations, while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will enable robust sensitivity analyses across diverse virtual student populations. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of simulating 30+ interactive agents across thousands of scenario iterations with millisecond-scale linguistic interactions. Expected outcomes include evidence-based guidelines for sequencing language instruction, dynamic grouping strategies, and personalized resource allocation in heterogeneous bilingual classrooms. By quantifying how specific teaching approaches propagate through multilingual social networks, this work aims to provide teacher educators with predictive tools for designing adaptive pedagogies that leverage students’ full linguistic repertoires. The resulting open-source simulation platform will serve as a training resource for pre-service bilingual educators, bridging theoretical knowledge and practical instructional decision-making through computational scenario testing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to bilingual/bicultural children or adults, and/or the design and implementation of educational programs having the goal of producing bilingual/bicultural individuals. Includes preparation to serve as teachers and administrators in bilingual/bicultural education programs.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare data ecosystems, driven by advances in interoperable health information exchange and artificial intelligence applications, has amplified vulnerabilities in patient privacy protection. Existing anonymization frameworks often fail to account for combinatorial re-identification risks arising from multimodal data integration across distributed networks. This project seeks to develop and validate a dynamic privacy-risk assessment platform capable of simulating large-scale healthcare data linkage attacks while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct a synthetic health data environment mirroring real-world patient demographics, clinical variables, and socio-geographic markers across 50 million simulated patient records. Computational workflows will integrate graph neural networks to model potential adversarial inference pathways and probabilistic re-identification surfaces across heterogeneous data types, including genomic markers, wearable device outputs, and longitudinal electronic health record data. The parallelized architecture will enable simultaneous evaluation of multiple attack vectors under varying threat models while preserving differential privacy constraints through GPU-accelerated cryptographic computations. Validation phases will benchmark performance against current de-identification standards using federated learning approaches across simulated healthcare institutions. Expected outcomes include a risk stratification framework that quantifies re-identification probabilities in emerging data-sharing contexts and an open-source toolkit for adaptive anonymization policy testing. This work addresses critical gaps in healthcare information security by providing computational tools to proactively identify privacy erosion points in next-generation health data infrastructures, ultimately supporting the development of more robust patient privacy preservation strategies in complex, interconnected care environments.
cip_title: Healthcare Information Privacy Assurance and Security
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers in designing, implementing, and administering comprehensive privacy and security protection programs in all types of healthcare organizations. Includes instruction in health information ethics, healthcare information privacy and security, healthcare compliance, healthcare information security and disaster recovery, and healthcare privacy law.

abstract: Clinical research trials generate vast multimodal datasets, yet current analytical workflows often fail to integrate real-time physiological, behavioral, and patient-reported outcomes at scale. This project proposes developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to analyze dynamic interactions between wearable device metrics, electronic health record (EHR) data, and adaptive patient feedback in decentralized clinical trials. The research addresses critical gaps in processing temporally dense biosensor data (e.g., continuous glucose monitoring, actigraphy) alongside irregularly sampled EHR entries and qualitative patient inputs—a computational challenge requiring parallelized architectures. Our approach combines graph neural networks to model temporal dependencies in heterogeneous data streams with federated learning techniques to preserve participant privacy across distributed trial sites. The HPC environment will enable simultaneous training of multiple predictive models examining (1) early warning signals for adverse event prediction using anomaly detection in high-frequency biosensor data, and (2) personalized intervention timing optimization through reinforcement learning simulations. A custom workflow manager will orchestrate containerized analyses across GPU nodes, integrating raw data from OpenClinica, Fitbit API, and REDCap platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for multimodal clinical trial analytics, validated against three ongoing neurology trials (n=420 participants) measuring intervention efficacy in epilepsy and migraine management. This resource will empower clinical research coordinators to identify subpopulation response patterns, optimize monitoring protocols, and reduce computational bottlenecks in complex trial designs. By enabling real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, the project advances precision medicine capabilities while maintaining regulatory compliance through auditable data provenance tracking—a critical requirement in therapeutic development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers as clinical research administrators or clinical research coordinators where they work under the supervision of a Principal Investigator to organize, coordinate and administer clinical research trials. Includes instruction in pharmacology, medical terminology, foundations of clinical research, project management, ethics, research design and data management, and legal and regulatory compliance .

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation for fine and studio arts organizations through data-driven computational modeling. Arts institutions such as galleries, museums, and community studios face complex operational demands—balancing financial constraints, spatial logistics, audience engagement, and community impact—yet lack robust predictive tools tailored to their unique needs. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a scalable computational framework that integrates historical institutional data, demographic trends, and real-time visitor analytics to model resource allocation scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large, heterogeneous datasets spanning attendance records, grant funding patterns, and facility usage metrics, as well as to run iterative simulations evaluating the efficacy of staffing, budgeting, and space management strategies. Machine learning algorithms will identify correlations between programming decisions and community engagement outcomes, while agent-based modeling will simulate the cascading effects of funding shifts or spatial reconfigurations. A key innovation involves adapting network analysis techniques to map relationships between arts organizations and their stakeholders, enabling predictive insights into collaborative opportunities or resource-sharing partnerships. Outcomes will include an open-source toolset for arts administrators to visualize trade-offs in allocation decisions, forecast the impact of programming changes, and advocate for data-informed policy adjustments. By translating computational methods into accessible strategies for arts management, this project aims to enhance the operational sustainability of visual arts institutions while advancing interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of arts administration, data science, and community design. The requested HPC resources will enable processing multi-terabyte datasets and running high-fidelity simulations that standard computing infrastructure cannot support, directly addressing scalability and reproducibility challenges in arts-focused computational research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage fine and studio art organizations, operations, and facilities. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; public relations and arts advocacy; arts law; and applications to specific arts activities such as galleries, museums, studios, foundations, and community organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interactions between urban crime patterns, law enforcement resource allocation, and community safety outcomes.
