Leveraging GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks, the pipeline will integrate convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for whole-slide image segmentation with graph-based algorithms to model cell-cell interaction networks and spatial gene expression gradients. Computational workflows will be optimized for scalability across multi-terabyte histology datasets, with containerized deployment to ensure reproducibility. Key challenges include mitigating batch effects in heterogeneous staining protocols, resolving subcellular feature ambiguity in low-resolution legacy datasets, and validating computational predictions against gold-standard manual annotations. Anticipated outcomes include a validated toolkit for quantifying spatial biomarkers in archival tissue samples, novel metrics for tumor microenvironment classification, and public datasets annotated with rare histological features. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in niche histopathology use cases—such as identifying early stromal remodeling in pre-malignant lesions—while providing the histotechnician community with scalable computational methods to bridge traditional morphology with emerging spatial biology paradigms. Access to HPC resources is critical for training high-parameter models, conducting hyperparameter optimization at scale, and enabling rapid iteration of spatial analytics workflows in a clinical research context.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid edge-cloud infrastructures demands adaptive resource management strategies that transcend traditional static allocation models. This project addresses the challenge of optimizing computational and network resource distribution in dynamic, heterogeneous environments where IoT devices, edge nodes, and cloud systems operate under fluctuating workloads and strict latency constraints. Current approaches in network and system administration often rely on reactive scaling or oversimplified predictive models, leading to suboptimal utilization rates and service degradation during demand spikes. We propose developing an autonomous resource orchestration framework that integrates graph-based network topology analysis with real-time telemetry from distributed systems. The computational methodology combines temporal graph neural networks to model evolving device dependencies with multi-agent reinforcement learning for decentralized decision-making. This approach requires high-performance computing resources to simulate large-scale network environments (10,000+ nodes) while training machine learning models on parallelized workflows. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing for neural network training and distributed memory systems for network emulation at operational scales. Expected outcomes include a novel resource allocation algorithm capable of maintaining sub-100ms decision latency in simulated smart city deployments, dynamic storage tiering strategies that reduce redundant data transfers by 30-40%, and failure prediction models that improve fault tolerance through proactive resource reservation. Success metrics will be validated against industrial IoT and emergency response communication scenarios, providing system administrators with concrete benchmarks for next-generation infrastructure management. The developed tools will be released as open-source modules for integration with existing network monitoring platforms, advancing capabilities in adaptive system administration while establishing performance baselines for AI-driven resource management in critical infrastructure applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the computer operations and control the system configurations emanating from a specific site or network hub. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software and applications; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) networking; principles of information systems security; disk space and traffic load monitoring; data backup; resource allocation; and setup and takedown procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the preparation of history educators by analyzing the representation of historical narratives in digital educational materials at scale—a challenge unaddressed by traditional manual methods. Despite the growing availability of digitized primary sources, textbooks, and lesson plans, there is limited understanding of how systemic biases, regional variations, or shifts in pedagogical priorities manifest across these resources. This gap hinders the development of teacher training programs that equip educators to critically evaluate and present inclusive, accurate historical content. To address this, we propose a computational analysis of multilingual and multinational educational datasets using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of terabytes of text and multimedia data, including historical documents, teacher-created lesson repositories, and government-mandated curricular standards. Methods will include transformer-based models for cross-lingual semantic analysis to track narrative consistency, graph neural networks to map the evolution of historical themes over time, and clustering algorithms to identify geographic or cultural disparities in content emphasis. The computational pipeline will also simulate the impact of specific curricular biases on student learning outcomes through agent-based modeling of classroom interactions. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying representational gaps in historical pedagogy and evidence-based guidelines for revising teacher education curricula. By revealing patterns in how historical causality, marginalized perspectives, and critical thinking prompts are currently framed, this work will empower teacher candidates to design instruction that fosters nuanced historical literacy. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential given the computational intensity of training multimodal models on heterogeneous educational datasets and iteratively refining analyses across diverse sociopolitical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach history programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze large-scale historical datasets for public history applications, addressing the challenge of efficiently synthesizing fragmented archival records into accessible narratives. Public history initiatives increasingly rely on digitized collections—such as municipal archives, oral histories, and cultural heritage datasets—but traditional historiographic methods struggle to process the volume, heterogeneity, and spatial-temporal complexity of these resources. Our research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to apply natural language processing (NLP), geospatial network modeling, and machine learning classification to three core datasets: 19th-century municipal records from industrializing U.S. cities, mid-20th-century community oral histories, and digitized artifacts from endangered historical sites. The computational workflow will identify patterns in labor migration, civic infrastructure development, and collective memory formation across these sources, while addressing biases inherent in archival preservation practices. By parallelizing resource-intensive tasks like entity recognition in handwritten text, dynamic mapping of demographic shifts, and semantic clustering of interview transcripts, HPC resources will enable analysis at scales previously unfeasible. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for historians to visualize multidimensional historical relationships, a methodological framework for ethically aligning computational methods with community-based historical practices, and case studies demonstrating how computational public history can inform contemporary policy debates on urban development and cultural preservation. This work advances applied history by bridging qualitative interpretation and data-driven inquiry while maintaining rigorous engagement with historical context, directly supporting the program’s mission to enhance public engagement with historical resources through innovative technical and administrative approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of history and administrative skills to the recording of public events and the management of related historical resources. Includes instruction in historical research methods, the planning and administration of public history projects, and applications to specific problems in public organizations, government agencies, foundations, and other facilities.

abstract: Medical staff credentialing and privileging processes are critical for ensuring healthcare quality and regulatory compliance, yet remain largely manual, time-intensive, and prone to human error. This project proposes the development of an AI-driven predictive analytics platform to optimize credential verification, privilege allocation, and compliance monitoring in hospital systems. The research addresses the inefficiencies of current workflows, which struggle to adapt to dynamic regulatory requirements and evolving clinician competency standards. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process multi-modal datasets—including training histories, licensure records, procedural outcomes, and real-time accreditation standards—to train deep learning models for automated document analysis and risk prediction. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will extract semantic features from unstructured credentialing documents, while graph neural networks will model practitioner competency networks across specialties. Computational validation will involve federated learning across synthetic and de-identified institutional datasets to preserve privacy while identifying patterns in credentialing delays or compliance gaps. The HPC environment will enable large-scale simulation of credentialing policy impacts through Monte Carlo methods, assessing how proposed workflow changes affect verification timelines and accreditation readiness. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of predicting privileging conflicts 6-12 months in advance, reducing manual verification workloads by ≥40%, and dynamically updating privilege criteria based on evolving healthcare regulations. This work bridges clinical operations management with computational social science, creating novel methodologies for workforce optimization in healthcare systems. The resulting framework will provide medical staff offices with actionable insights to preempt credentialing bottlenecks, align privileges with emerging care models, and maintain continuous regulatory compliance in an era of rapid technological and policy change.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform credentialing, privileging, personnel management, and accreditation compliance services for hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in medical staff organization and management, medical terminology, credentialing and re-credentialing, health care accreditation and regulatory standards, health care law, meeting and negotiation management, and office information systems management.

abstract: This project seeks to address a critical gap in psychology teacher education: understanding how pre-service teachers develop and refine pedagogical decision-making skills when designing instruction for complex psychological concepts. While existing research emphasizes curricular content and teaching strategies, the cognitive processes underlying effective lesson planning, adaptive assessment design, and real-time classroom decision-making remain poorly understood. To investigate these dynamics, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that simulate teacher cognition and classroom interactions at scale. The project will utilize agent-based modeling frameworks to represent diverse student learning trajectories, coupled with neural network architectures trained on classroom discourse datasets to emulate teacher responsiveness. These simulations will enable systematic testing of how variations in pedagogical training (e.g., scenario-based learning modules vs. traditional lecture formats) influence emergent teaching behaviors. By parallelizing thousands of simulated classroom scenarios across HPC nodes, we aim to identify cognitive load patterns, decision-making heuristics, and intervention thresholds that predict teaching effectiveness. Outcomes will inform the development of targeted training protocols for psychology educators, particularly in addressing common misconceptions in topics like cognitive development and social behavior. The computational infrastructure will also support the creation of an open-access repository of synthetic classroom interaction data, enabling further research without compromising student privacy. This work bridges educational psychology with computational social science, offering novel insights into the cognitive architectures that underpin effective psychology instruction while demonstrating how HPC resources can advance teacher preparation through large-scale behavioral modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general psychology at the secondary school level.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in business and economic journalism by addressing the challenges of analyzing large-scale, dynamic datasets in real time. Business journalists increasingly confront complex financial markets, global supply chain disruptions, and rapidly evolving economic indicators, yet traditional analytical tools often lack the capacity to process heterogeneous data streams—including structured financial records, unstructured corporate disclosures, and social media sentiment—at the speed and scale required for timely reporting. The research problem centers on developing computational workflows that integrate machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis to identify trends, anomalies, and narratives within these datasets. Proposed methods include training transformer-based models to extract semantic patterns from earnings calls and regulatory filings, applying graph algorithms to map interdependencies in global trade networks, and deploying ensemble forecasting techniques to predict market reactions to geopolitical events. These workflows will be optimized for parallel processing and GPU acceleration to handle terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools tailored for journalistic investigations, enabling faster identification of underreported economic stories (e.g., supply chain vulnerabilities, regulatory arbitrage) and democratizing access to advanced analytics for newsrooms with limited technical infrastructure. The project also aims to produce methodological frameworks for ethically integrating automated insights into reporting processes, addressing concerns around algorithmic bias and transparency. By enhancing the computational rigor of business journalism, this work will strengthen public understanding of economic systems while maintaining the discipline’s emphasis on accuracy, context, and accountability. Resource requests include GPU nodes for model training, high-memory nodes for large-scale NLP tasks, and scalable storage for curating annotated datasets spanning financial, corporate, and media sources.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares students to gather, analyze, and synthesize verbal and visual information to communicate stories related to business and economics across multiple media platforms. Includes instruction in accounting, business, business and economic reporting, business law, economics, finance, financial accounting and reporting, ethics, journalistic research methods and resources, and journalism skills and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a cross-linguistic analysis of narrative structures in understudied literary traditions, focusing on 20th-century speculative fiction across Arabic, Japanese, and Russian corpora. The research problem centers on identifying and quantifying transnational patterns in narrative temporality and focalization—features that resist manual annotation at scale due to the syntactic complexity and cultural specificity of the source texts. Current scholarship lacks systematic frameworks for comparing these elements across distantly related languages, particularly in non-Western contexts. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline integrating multilingual transformer models (fine-tuned on literary texts) with graph-based representations of narrative dynamics. The workflow includes: (1) automated parsing of tense, aspect, and perspective markers using custom-trained NLP tools adapted for each language; (2) network analysis of character focalization shifts via dynamic graph embeddings; and (3) comparative visualization of temporal narrative arcs through dimensionality reduction techniques. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models on our curated corpus of 15,000+ primary texts and annotations, as well as for running large-scale graph computations across narrative networks. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative typology of speculative fiction narrative strategies across these linguistic traditions, alongside open-source tools for multilingual literary analysis. The project will contribute methodological innovations to digital humanities by addressing challenges in cross-lingual transfer learning for low-resource literary languages, while advancing comparative literature scholarship through computational evidence for previously theorized—but empirically unverified—cultural convergences in global speculative fiction. Results will inform a monograph and a public dataset supporting future transnational literary studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on two or more literary traditions in the original languages or in translation. Includes instruction in comparative linguistics; applicable foreign languages; English/French language and literature; literary criticism; and applications to genre, period, national, and textual studies as well as literary forms such as poetry, prose, and drama.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing personalized professional development for K-12 educators in STEM disciplines through advanced computational modeling of classroom dynamics. Traditional teacher training often relies on generalized frameworks that fail to account for the complex interplay of instructional strategies, student engagement patterns, and subject-specific pedagogical content knowledge. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation environment leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning to analyze how varying teaching approaches impact learning outcomes in diverse classroom contexts. The research will utilize anonymized datasets from classroom observations, student performance metrics, and teacher feedback surveys to parameterize multi-agent systems representing student cohorts with heterogeneous learning profiles. High-performance computing resources are critical for scaling these simulations to model thousands of virtual classrooms simultaneously, enabling the identification of context-dependent teaching strategies that maximize conceptual understanding in mathematics and science. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about the relationship between real-time teacher decision-making, differentiated instruction techniques, and longitudinal student achievement. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework to guide the design of adaptive professional development programs, equipping educators with data-driven insights into tailoring instruction for specific curricular goals and student populations. This work will provide teacher education programs with a novel tool for scenario-based training, reducing the gap between theoretical pedagogical training and practical classroom effectiveness. The requested computing resources will directly support the parallel processing demands of large-scale ABM iterations and the training of neural networks for pattern recognition in instructional efficacy.
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Subject Areas, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education, specific academic and vocational programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational methods for solving inverse problems arising in the analysis of nonlinear wave propagation in heterogeneous media, with applications to seismic imaging and materials characterization. A key challenge lies in accurately reconstructing material properties from sparse, noisy observational data, which involves solving high-dimensional optimization problems governed by complex partial differential equations (PDEs). Traditional approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs and poor convergence when applied to realistic three-dimensional geometries. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining asymptotic waveform analysis, adjoint-based optimization, and parallelized iterative solvers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to implement large-scale finite element discretizations of the governing PDEs, accelerate matrix-free linear algebra operations, and enable ensemble-based uncertainty quantification across parameter spaces. The project will extend existing open-source PDE solvers using domain decomposition techniques optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures, with adaptive mesh refinement targeting regions of high solution gradients. Validation will focus on viscoelastic wave models relevant to subsurface imaging, where multi-scale material heterogeneities dominate wave attenuation patterns. Successful implementation is expected to yield a 40-60% reduction in computational time compared to conventional full-waveform inversion methods while improving parameter recovery accuracy. Outcomes will advance inverse problem methodologies in applied mathematics by bridging asymptotic approximation theory with data-driven optimization, with direct applications to geophysical sensing and nondestructive material testing. The developed software tools will be disseminated as modular extensions to the FEniCSx framework, promoting reproducibility in computational inverse problems. This work requires access to HPC systems capable of supporting distributed memory parallelism, large-scale eigenvalue computations, and GPU-accelerated linear algebra to manage memory demands exceeding 10 TB for high-resolution 3D simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as engineering and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in natural phenomena modeling continuum mechanics, reaction-diffusion, wave propagation, dynamic systems, numerical analysis, controlled theory, asymptotic methods, variation, optimization theory, inverse problems, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance real-time decision-making in multi-domain military operations through advanced simulation and predictive analytics. The research addresses the challenge of integrating heterogeneous data streams—including intelligence feeds, command protocols, and dynamic environmental factors—into cohesive operational models under time-sensitive conditions. Traditional approaches often struggle with scalability, latency, and the interdependencies inherent in joint all-domain command and control (JADC2) environments, particularly when accounting for adversarial information operations and contested communications. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational architecture combining agent-based modeling, graph-theoretic analysis, and federated machine learning techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale operational scenarios involving thousands of autonomous agents, probabilistic threat cascades, and adaptive adversarial strategies while maintaining sub-second decision cycles. The framework will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in intelligence fusion and optimize resource allocation across cyber, physical, and cognitive domains. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for stress-testing command protocols against emergent hybrid threats, a benchmark dataset for evaluating AI-driven decision aids in information-denied environments, and novel metrics for operational resilience in decentralized command structures. By enabling rapid iteration of "what-if" scenarios at unprecedented granularity, this work aims to advance adaptive decision architectures for future military operations while contributing methodological innovations to the computational social systems domain. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations, distributed memory processing for real-time adversarial gaming, and secure data federation across classified and unclassified research environments.
cip_title: Intelligence, Command Control and Information Operations, Other (MILITARY)
cip_definition: Any instructional program in intelligence, command control and information operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in chemistry education by developing interactive, computationally driven pedagogical tools to model complex chemical systems and processes for classroom instruction. A persistent issue in chemistry teacher education is the difficulty of conveying abstract molecular-level phenomena—such as reaction mechanisms, thermodynamics, and quantum interactions—using traditional teaching methods. Static diagrams and simplified analogies often fail to bridge the gap between theoretical concepts and student comprehension, leading to persistent misconceptions. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create dynamic, real-time simulations and visualizations that enable pre-service and in-service chemistry teachers to explore these systems with unprecedented fidelity. The computational approach will involve molecular dynamics simulations using packages like GROMACS and LAMMPS, quantum chemistry calculations via NWChem, and machine learning-driven adaptive modeling to tailor simulations to diverse learning contexts. These tools will be integrated into a web-based platform optimized for classroom use, allowing educators to manipulate variables (e.g., temperature, concentration) and visualize outcomes interactively. The project will also develop modular lesson plans aligned with secondary and postsecondary curricula, emphasizing active learning strategies. By utilizing HPC, we aim to overcome the limitations of consumer-grade hardware in rendering large-scale simulations or handling computationally intensive tasks such as ab initio calculations for multi-electron systems. Expected outcomes include measurable improvements in pre-service teachers’ conceptual mastery of challenging topics, as demonstrated by pre-/post-assessment metrics, and the creation of an open-access repository of simulations for broader educational use. This work will advance chemistry pedagogy by embedding computational science directly into teacher training, equipping educators to foster deeper student engagement with foundational chemical principles while aligning with modern STEM education standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach chemistry programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Nuclear radiology faces critical challenges in improving the spatial resolution, quantification accuracy, and diagnostic sensitivity of radionuclide-based imaging modalities such as single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET). Current reconstruction algorithms struggle with noise, limited photon counts, and motion artifacts, particularly in dynamic studies assessing biodistribution over time. This project proposes to develop and validate a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating advanced iterative reconstruction techniques, machine learning (ML)-based denoising, and patient-specific motion correction to address these limitations. The primary research problem centers on optimizing the trade-off between image quality and computational efficiency for clinical translation. We will employ Monte Carlo simulations of photon transport to model scanner-specific response functions, paired with patient-derived 4D CT data to simulate realistic anatomical and physiological variability. These datasets will train a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict noise distributions and compensate for respiratory/cardiac motion in list-mode PET/SPECT data. Reconstruction will leverage GPU-accelerated maximum likelihood expectation maximization (MLEM) with depth-dependent point spread function modeling, implemented via the open-source CASToR platform. The computational workflow requires HPC resources to manage large-scale parameter optimization across simulated and clinical datasets (n=200 retrospective/prospective oncology cases), including voxel-wise uncertainty quantification. Expected outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in reconstruction time compared to conventional ordered subset methods, improved lesion detectability (<4mm diameter), and more accurate time-activity curve measurements for pharmacokinetic modeling. Success would directly enhance diagnostic confidence in early cancer detection, therapy response assessment, and radiopharmaceutical dosimetry. This project aligns with national priorities in precision nuclear medicine by enabling faster, higher-quality imaging with lower radiotracer doses—critical for pediatric and serial imaging applications. The developed tools will be disseminated as open-source plugins to promote reproducibility in the field.
cip_definition: Research focused on the imaging by external detection of radionuclides and/or biodistribution by external detection of radionuclides for diagnosis of disease. Requires prior partial completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic resource allocation for heterogeneous computing systems, which are increasingly critical in enterprise and cloud environments where mixed hardware architectures (CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs) must adapt to fluctuating workloads. Current static allocation strategies often lead to resource underutilization, energy waste, and latency spikes during demand surges, particularly in systems supporting real-time data processing or distributed machine learning tasks. To overcome these limitations, we propose the development of an adaptive resource management framework that leverages machine learning (ML) and real-time telemetry to optimize hardware utilization. The framework will integrate predictive workload modeling with runtime decision-making algorithms to dynamically redistribute computational tasks across available hardware. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale heterogeneous environments, train ML models on diverse workload patterns, and validate the framework’s scalability under peak loads. Simulations will replicate scenarios such as edge computing clusters handling IoT data streams and hybrid cloud systems managing batch and interactive workloads. Metrics including task completion time, energy consumption, and hardware utilization rates will be benchmarked against conventional allocation methods. Expected outcomes include a publicly deployable toolkit for system administrators to automate resource optimization, reducing operational costs and energy use by an estimated 15–30% in target use cases. The project will also generate datasets and performance models to inform future research on adaptive computing architectures. By bridging gaps between theoretical resource allocation models and practical system administration challenges, this work aligns with the program’s focus on applied engineering solutions, directly supporting professionals tasked with maintaining complex, evolving computer systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of professionals who use computer systems. Includes instruction in basic computer design and architecture, programming, problems of specific computer applications, component and system maintenance and inspection procedures, hardware and software problem diagnosis and repair, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized treatment strategies for complex, multifactorial neurological disorders, such as functional movement disorders (FMDs), which lack clear biomarkers and exhibit heterogeneous symptom profiles. Current clinical decision-making relies on subjective assessments and trial-and-error approaches, leading to delayed or suboptimal outcomes. To address this, we propose integrating high-dimensional clinical data—including dynamic motion capture, neurophysiological signals (EEG, EMG), and patient-reported outcomes—with mechanistic computational models of sensorimotor network dysfunction. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train graph neural networks (GNNs) on federated multi-institutional datasets, capturing spatiotemporal relationships between symptom clusters and neurophysiological signatures. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate how perturbations in neural circuit dynamics manifest as observable motor behaviors, enabling in silico testing of therapeutic interventions. The computational pipeline will employ Bayesian optimization to iteratively refine treatment recommendations based on real-world patient responses, creating adaptive decision-support tools for clinicians. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform that identifies individualized neuromodulation targets and behavioral therapy regimens, reducing the average time to effective intervention by ≥40% in pilot validation cohorts. This work bridges gaps between systems neuroscience, dynamical systems theory, and clinical practice, directly aligning with translational research priorities in medical education by producing open-source simulation tools for training clinicians in precision neurology paradigms. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling petabyte-scale multimodal data streams, parallelizing computationally intensive simulations across GPU nodes, and maintaining data security compliance through containerized workflows. Successful implementation will establish a template for computational phenotyping in other poorly understood neuropsychiatric conditions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares medical and health clinicians to combine knowledge from scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge, improve medical education, and bridge laboratory and clinical science into clinical practice. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, medical education and scientific writing.

abstract: The proliferation of decentralized decision-making in global enterprises has intensified challenges in maintaining coherent organizational knowledge ecosystems, particularly as real-time data streams and siloed digital tools hinder cross-functional insights. This project addresses the critical gap in dynamic knowledge synthesis—the ability to integrate fragmented, transient information from distributed teams into actionable strategic intelligence. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), the research will develop a computational architecture to model knowledge flow across multimodal platforms (e.g., Slack, CRM systems, IoT sensors) while accounting for contextual biases and temporal decay. The methodology combines transformer-based neural networks to process unstructured text and speech data at scale, probabilistic knowledge graphs to map concept relationships, and reinforcement learning agents to simulate optimal knowledge-routing pathways under resource constraints. By deploying distributed training frameworks on HPC clusters, the team will optimize latency-sensitive inference for real-world applications, such as predicting critical knowledge gaps during rapid product launches or mergers. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a novel metric system for quantifying knowledge cohesion in multinational organizations, (2) open-source algorithms to prioritize high-impact knowledge interventions, and (3) empirical validation of computational methods through partnerships with three Fortune 500 firms undergoing digital transformation. This work advances the emerging field of computational organizational epistemology, bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and AI ethics. The requested resources will enable unprecedented analysis of petabyte-scale interaction datasets, directly informing scalable solutions to knowledge fragmentation—a $300B annual productivity loss driver per industry estimates—while establishing benchmarks for ethical AI deployment in human-centric knowledge systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of knowledge management in government agencies and corporations for the purpose of supporting stated organizational goals and objectives, and prepares individuals to function as information resource managers. Includes instruction in information technology, principles of computer and information systems, management information systems, applicable policy and regulations, and operations and personnel management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the adaptive behavioral dynamics of urban wildlife populations in response to anthropogenic noise pollution, a growing ecological stressor with poorly understood impacts on interspecies communication and survival strategies. Focusing on avian and mammalian species in metropolitan ecosystems, the research integrates bioacoustic field data, machine learning–driven behavioral analysis, and agent-based modeling to simulate long-term adaptive pathways under varying noise regimes. The central challenge lies in processing terabytes of high-resolution audio recordings to identify species-specific vocalization patterns, coupled with simulating complex feedback loops between behavioral plasticity, habitat fragmentation, and urban soundscape evolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for (1) training convolutional neural networks to classify and contextualize vocal modifications across 15+ species in noise-gradient environments, (2) running spatially explicit, individual-based models that incorporate real-world GIS layers of urban infrastructure and human activity patterns, and (3) conducting monte carlo simulations to quantify probabilistic outcomes for population viability under future noise scenarios. The computational framework will utilize parallelized workflows for bioacoustic signal processing (using Python-based Librosa and TensorFlow ecosystems) and NetLogo-ROS hybrid modeling for robotic validation of predicted behavioral responses in field conditions. Expected outcomes include a predictive atlas of noise-driven adaptive thresholds for urban wildlife, identification of acoustic refugia critical for conservation planning, and novel metrics for assessing cross-species resilience in soundscape-altered environments. By bridging computational ethology with urban ecosystem management, this work will provide municipal planners and wildlife agencies with empirically grounded tools to mitigate anthropogenic noise impacts while advancing methodological paradigms for studying animal behavior in complex, human-dominated landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological principles to the study of vertebrate wildlife, wildlife habitats, and related ecosystems in remote and urban areas. Includes instruction in animal ecology; adaptational biology; urban ecosystems; natural and artificial habitat management; limnology; wildlife pathology; and vertebrate zoological specializations such as mammalogy, herpetology, ichthyology, ornithology, and others.

abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic stressors, including nutrient pollution, climate change, and invasive species, yet predicting their ecological responses remains a critical challenge in limnology. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to simulate multi-trophic interactions and emergent ecosystem dynamics in temperate lakes under varying disturbance regimes. The research combines long-term limnological datasets (water chemistry, plankton communities, fish populations) with spatially explicit environmental data to parameterize agent-based models (ABMs) and hydrodynamic-biogeochemical models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve complex feedbacks among physical lake processes (e.g., stratification, nutrient mixing), species behavior (e.g., predator-prey dynamics, algal bloom formation), and stochastic disturbance events (e.g., heatwaves, pollutant pulses). Parallelized simulations will assess how biodiversity loss and shifting thermal regimes alter ecosystem stability across gradients of lake depth, trophic status, and connectivity. Machine learning workflows will further identify early warning signals of regime shifts from multidimensional output data. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into resilience thresholds for keystone aquatic species, spatially resolved projections of habitat suitability under climate scenarios, and scalable methods to prioritize lakes for conservation interventions. By bridging ecological theory with computational scalability, this work will advance predictive capacity for freshwater resource management while addressing fundamental questions in aquatic community ecology. The requested allocation supports iterative model calibration, large ensemble simulations (>10,000 core-hours), and high-dimensional data synthesis, enabling novel analyses of cross-scale interactions that cannot be feasibly studied through empirical approaches alone.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting inland fresh waters such as lakes, ponds, rivers, creeks, estuaries, and wetlands. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; aquatic ecosystems; microbiology; mycology; botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; population biology and biodiversity; studies of specific species, phyla, and habitats; and applications to fields such as natural resources conservation, fisheries science, and biotechnology.

abstract: The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens presents an urgent global health challenge, demanding advanced tools to elucidate resistance mechanisms and virulence pathways. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the genomic and metabolic adaptations of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, with a focus on Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii. These pathogens exhibit complex resistance profiles, often mediated by horizontal gene transfer, efflux pump overexpression, and biofilm formation, yet the interplay between these traits remains poorly understood at a systems level. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating bacterial whole-genome sequencing data, transcriptomic profiles, and dynamic metabolic models to identify conserved genetic and regulatory networks driving resistance and persistence in clinical isolates. Genome-scale metabolic reconstructions will be optimized using flux balance analysis to simulate nutrient utilization under antibiotic stress, while agent-based modeling will explore population-level heterogeneity in biofilm communities. Comparative phylogenomic analyses will trace the emergence of resistance genes across strains, correlating their dissemination with host microenvironmental factors. By coupling these datasets through machine learning pipelines, we aim to predict co-evolutionary pathways linking bacterial metabolism, stress response systems, and virulence factor expression. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities for large-scale genomic alignment (1000+ isolate genomes), stochastic simulations of bacterial population dynamics, and parallelized optimization of metabolic models. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-priority targets for combination therapies, such as vulnerabilities in redox homeostasis or cell envelope biogenesis pathways that could potentiate existing antibiotics. This work will provide a framework for decoding resistance evolution in nosocomial pathogens, directly informing translational efforts to combat multidrug-resistant infections.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of pathogenic bacteria that are significant factors in causing or facilitating human disease. Includes instruction in the pathogenesis of bacterial diseases, bacterial genetics and physiology, bacterial anatomy and structure, antigens, bacterial reproduction, bacterial adhesion, phagocytes, and the identification of new or mutated bacteria and bacterial agents.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to model and analyze individualized learning trajectories for students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), with the goal of informing adaptive teaching strategies. A critical challenge in special education is the design of personalized interventions that account for the heterogeneous cognitive, sensory, and behavioral profiles of autistic learners. Current approaches to creating individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual observation and qualitative assessment, limiting scalability and the ability to predict long-term outcomes. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including longitudinal academic performance records, behavioral logs from classroom technologies, and sensor-derived physiological data—to identify patterns and predictors of skill acquisition. Machine learning models (e.g., recurrent neural networks, clustering algorithms) will be trained to simulate student responses to specific teaching methods, enabling educators to test intervention scenarios in silico before implementation. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing large volumes of unstructured data (e.g., video recordings of classroom interactions), running parallelized simulations of learning pathways, and optimizing instructional variables via reinforcement learning. HPC resources are essential due to the high dimensionality of the data, the need for real-time feedback in model training, and the complexity of modeling dynamic interactions between pedagogical strategies and student behaviors. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating data-driven IEP recommendations and a repository of simulated teaching-interaction datasets. This work will provide educators with evidence-based insights into tailoring instructional pacing, content sequencing, and sensory supports, ultimately advancing the precision and efficacy of autism education practices.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Autism
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with autism, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with autism, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising autistic students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: The exponential growth of global air traffic has intensified congestion and inefficiencies in current air transportation systems, leading to increased delays, fuel consumption, and environmental impact. Traditional air traffic management (ATM) frameworks struggle to adapt to dynamic operational demands and the integration of emerging technologies such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and urban air mobility (UAM) platforms. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity computational model to simulate and optimize large-scale air traffic flow management (ATFM) under varying operational and environmental constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will implement a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically allocate airspace resources, predict traffic conflicts, and optimize routing strategies in real time. The computational framework will integrate heterogeneous data sources, including historical flight trajectories, weather patterns, and airspace configurations, to generate scalable solutions for congested and complex airspace environments. Key outcomes include actionable insights for reducing systemic delays, minimizing fuel burn through optimal flight path allocation, and enhancing the adaptability of ATM systems to accommodate future air transportation paradigms. The project’s significance lies in its potential to inform policy decisions, support the development of next-generation air traffic control systems, and contribute to the aviation industry’s sustainability goals. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the required computational throughput for simulating millions of flight trajectories and iteratively refining optimization models, tasks that are infeasible with conventional computing resources.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in aviation and air transportation services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance educational assessment methodologies by developing computationally intensive models capable of analyzing large-scale, hierarchically structured assessment data. Contemporary educational datasets, such as those from national and international assessments, often encompass millions of students nested within thousands of institutions, alongside longitudinal measures and contextual variables. Traditional analytical approaches, limited by computational scalability, struggle to efficiently estimate complex models that account for multilevel interactions, latent traits, and time-dependent covariates. To address this gap, we propose the development of a Bayesian multilevel multidimensional item response theory (IRT) framework, which integrates student performance data with institutional and socioeconomic covariates. This model requires high-dimensional parameter estimation through Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, a process that becomes computationally prohibitive as dataset size and model complexity increase. Access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources is critical to enable parallelized sampling algorithms, reduce runtime from weeks to hours, and facilitate robust convergence diagnostics across hyperparameters. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated libraries for matrix operations and distributed computing frameworks to manage memory-intensive tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source software package for scalable educational measurement, (2) validated insights into how institutional resources mediate equity in assessment outcomes, and (3) optimized MCMC implementations for future large-scale psychometric research. By enabling precise, context-aware evaluations of student learning, this work aims to inform equitable policy decisions and reduce biases in high-stakes educational assessments. The requested resources will directly support iterative model development, validation on real-world datasets (e.g., PISA, NAEP), and dissemination of reproducible computational workflows to the education research community.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_title: Educational Assessment, Evaluation, and Research, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in educational evaluation, research and statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of phonological and syntactic features across Iberian Romance languages (Spanish, Catalan, Galician, and Portuguese) from the medieval period to the modern era. The core challenge lies in processing and modeling large, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized historical texts, dialectal corpora, and spoken language recordings—to trace linguistic shifts and identify sociocultural drivers of language change. Traditional methods lack the scalability to handle the volume and complexity of these datasets, particularly when analyzing phonetic variations in regional dialects or syntactic innovations across centuries. The project will employ computational linguistics techniques, including neural language models fine-tuned for historical texts, dynamic phonetic alignment algorithms, and agent-based simulations of language contact scenarios. These methods will be applied to three interconnected tasks: (1) reconstructing proto-Romance phonological networks using comparative analysis of medieval manuscripts, (2) quantifying the impact of urbanization on dialect leveling in 20th-century Iberian speech communities, and (3) modeling the diffusion of grammatical innovations through multilingual social networks. By parallelizing corpus preprocessing, training language-specific transformer models, and running large-scale Monte Carlo simulations, HPC resources will enable the integration of previously disconnected linguistic timelines and geographic scales. Anticipated outcomes include a diachronic atlas of Iberian Romance linguistic features, open-source tools for historical corpus analysis, and evidence-based models of language change that account for both structural constraints and sociocultural dynamics. This work will advance methodological innovation in computational philology while providing empirical insights into language preservation challenges faced by minority Romance varieties.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Romance languages of Western, Central, and Southern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying synergistic interactions in botanical medicine formulations used within naturopathic clinical practice. A central challenge in naturopathy is optimizing complex herbal blends to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing adverse effects, a process complicated by the combinatorial complexity of phytochemical mixtures and their nonlinear interactions with human physiological systems. Current research lacks robust computational models capable of predicting how multi-herb formulations influence cellular signaling pathways, microbiome dynamics, and epigenetic regulation. To address this gap, we propose an integrative systems biology approach combining network pharmacology, molecular docking simulations, and machine learning to analyze 30 prioritized botanical combinations from historical and contemporary naturopathic protocols. The computational workflow will incorporate multi-omics data (transcriptomic, metabolomic, and proteomic profiles) from existing databases and novel in silico predictions of phytochemical-target interactions. HPC resources will enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to characterize binding affinities of plant secondary metabolites with immune-modulatory proteins (e.g., NLRP3 inflammasome components) and epigenetic regulators (e.g., HDAC enzymes). Concurrently, graph neural networks will model herb-herb-host interactions across biological scales, from molecular targets to tissue-level outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for identifying optimal botanical synergies, novel biomarkers for personalized naturopathic interventions in chronic inflammatory conditions, and mechanistic insights into the polypharmacological effects of whole-plant extracts. This work will establish a computational foundation for evidence-based formulation design in naturopathic medicine while advancing methodologies for studying complex natural product systems. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities for parallelized quantum chemistry calculations, terabyte-scale multi-modal data integration, and iterative training of deep learning models with over 10^8 parameters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of naturopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic approach combining medical knowledge with noninvasive natural, homeopathic, and non-Western therapies and emphasizing disease prevention, wellness, and self-healing. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, epidemiology, neuroscience, biostatistics, public and community health, laboratory and clinical diagnosis, pharmacognosy, botanical medicine, homeopathy, principles of Oriental medicine and Ayurveda, manipulative therapy, naturopathic therapeutics, therapeutic nutrition, case analysis and management, philosophy of naturopathy, patient counseling, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Aromatherapy’s therapeutic potential is increasingly recognized in integrative health practices, yet the biochemical mechanisms underlying its efficacy remain poorly characterized. This project addresses the critical gap in understanding how essential oil compounds interact with human physiological systems at the molecular level, particularly in modulating inflammatory and neurological pathways. Current limitations stem from the complexity of essential oil chemistry—each oil contains hundreds of volatile organic compounds—and the challenges of modeling their dynamic interactions with biological targets. To overcome these barriers, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate molecular interactions, predict bioactive constituents, and optimize therapeutic blends. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will be performed on GPU-accelerated nodes to model ligand-receptor binding kinetics between key essential oil components (e.g., terpenes, phenylpropanoids) and human proteins implicated in pain perception (TRPV1, opioid receptors) and inflammation (COX-2, NF-κB). Quantum mechanical calculations will supplement MD to assess electronic properties influencing bioavailability. Concurrently, machine learning models trained on existing phytochemical and clinical datasets will identify predictive patterns linking specific compound ratios to therapeutic outcomes. These computational workflows will be validated against in vitro assays measuring cytokine suppression and receptor activation. The HPC environment is essential for managing the scale of simulations (10,000+ ligand-protein pairs), iterative blend optimization, and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for designing evidence-based essential oil formulations, safety profiles for high-risk compounds, and mechanistic insights into aromatherapy’s bioactivity. This research will advance aromatherapy from anecdotal practice to a data-driven discipline, offering healthcare providers quantitative tools to personalize treatments while minimizing adverse effects. Results will be disseminated through open-access databases to support interdisciplinary innovation in botanical medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide therapeutic care through the preparation and application of extracted essential oils from plants, including flowers (botanicals), roots, berries, and bark. Includes instruction in aromatherapy history and theory, basic physiology of absorption, aromachemistry, organic chemistry, botanical taxonomy, carrier oils, essential oils, extraction methods, blending techniques, application methods, safety, client consultation and treatment planning, business management, professional standards and ethics, and applicable regulations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of psychometric models, combined with the growing scale of modern assessment datasets, demands advanced computational resources to ensure robust parameter estimation and model validation. Traditional methods for fitting high-dimensional item response theory (IRT) models and multidimensional factor analyses face significant limitations in processing speed and memory allocation, particularly when applied to datasets with millions of responses or models incorporating hierarchical structures, latent interactions, or dynamic response processes. This project proposes the development and evaluation of scalable Bayesian estimation algorithms for advanced psychometric models using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) implementing parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers for cross-classified IRT models that account for nested respondent-item dependencies in large-scale educational testing data; (2) optimizing variational inference procedures for confirmatory multidimensional factor analysis with non-linear latent interactions; and (3) conducting comprehensive simulation studies to evaluate the statistical properties of these estimators under varying sample sizes and missing data mechanisms. The computational workload requires distributed memory architectures for storing massive sparse matrices, GPU acceleration for tensor operations in gradient calculations, and multi-node parallelization to conduct simultaneous simulation conditions. Successful implementation will produce open-source software tools optimized for HPC environments, empirical benchmarks for computational efficiency gains in complex model estimation, and methodological advances in handling massive, clustered psychometric data. These outcomes will directly enhance the precision and scalability of measurement models in educational and psychological research while establishing computational best practices for quantitative psychology workflows. The requested resources will enable critical comparisons between approximation methods and exact inference approaches at unprecedented data scales, addressing fundamental questions about the trade-offs between computational feasibility and statistical accuracy in next-generation psychometrics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical procedures used in psychological test construction and validation; the general problems of the measurement of behavior; and the application of quantitative methods to research design and other methodological topics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dermatologic research, particularly in understanding the molecular mechanisms of inflammatory skin diseases and cutaneous malignancies, demands advanced computational tools to integrate multi-modal data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical datasets from patients with psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and melanoma. A critical barrier in current research is the inability to efficiently process and model interactions between genetic variants, immune cell dynamics, and environmental triggers, which collectively drive disease heterogeneity and treatment resistance. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining machine learning (ML) and network biology approaches. Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from skin biopsies will be analyzed using deep neural networks to identify disease-specific transcriptional signatures, while graph-based algorithms will map protein-protein interaction networks to pinpoint hub genes and pathways. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize structural changes in pathogenic proteins linked to genetic mutations. These analyses require substantial computational power due to the volume of sequencing data (>10 TB), the complexity of ML model training, and the need for parallelized simulations. The integration of HPC resources will enable the processing of these datasets at scale, reducing runtime for iterative model optimization from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early diagnosis, predictive models of therapeutic response, and candidate targets for biologic drug development. This work will directly inform clinical trial design and personalized treatment strategies, addressing unmet needs in managing chronic and life-threatening skin diseases. By elucidating the systems-level biology of cutaneous pathologies, this project aims to bridge translational gaps in dermatology, ultimately improving patient outcomes through data-driven innovation.
cip_definition: Research focused on diseases of the skin, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May also include research on dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, sexually transmitted diseases, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for modeling the dynamic interactions between corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures and real-time financial market reactions. While ESG metrics are increasingly critical to investor decision-making, current accounting practices struggle to quantify their nonlinear, time-dependent impacts on market volatility, liquidity, and firm valuation. The project addresses this gap by integrating heterogeneous datasets—including SEC filings, ESG rating databases, social media sentiment, and high-frequency trading data—to analyze how granular ESG factors propagate through global markets. Computational methods will combine natural language processing (NLP) for extracting latent ESG themes from unstructured disclosures, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map inter-firm ESG influence networks, and multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate investor behavior under evolving regulatory scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of petabyte-scale financial time series data and probabilistic uncertainty quantification across thousands of concurrent market simulations. Expected outcomes include a novel risk assessment tool that identifies ESG-driven financial tipping points and a publicly accessible dataset linking ESG disclosure patterns to market microstructure effects. This work bridges accounting theory with computational social science, offering practitioners a systematic approach to evaluate ESG strategies in volatile markets while advancing methodological integration of AI/ML techniques in fiduciary analytics. The resource-intensive nature of modeling cross-scale interactions—from firm-level disclosures to systemic market shocks—necessitates specialized computing capabilities beyond conventional cloud infrastructure.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and business administration/management that prepares individuals to function as accountants and business managers.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational efficiency and user-centric design of word processing systems through large-scale simulation and machine learning-driven optimization. While modern word processors enable complex document creation, the growing demand for real-time collaborative editing, automated formatting, and error detection in large documents (e.g., technical manuals, legal contracts) strains conventional algorithms. Current methods for dynamic text rendering, version synchronization, and semantic consistency checks exhibit latency and accuracy trade-offs, particularly when scaling to multi-user environments or documents exceeding 10,000 pages. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining parallelized workflow simulation and transformer-based language models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable: 1) Large-scale agent-based modeling of concurrent user interactions across distributed document sections, 2) GPU-accelerated training of domain-specific language models for context-aware formatting prediction, and 3) Distributed benchmarking of compression algorithms for version history storage. Our approach will leverage MPI-based parallelism for simulating 1000+ concurrent editing sessions, while fine-tuning BERT-style architectures on a curated corpus of technical documents (1TB+) to improve automated style guide enforcement. Expected outcomes include optimized algorithms for real-time conflict resolution in collaborative editing, reduced computational overhead for document integrity checks, and quantifiable performance benchmarks for resource allocation in cloud-based word processing services. This research directly supports educational and professional training objectives in the Word Processing discipline by providing open-source computational tools to enhance software responsiveness during high-stakes tasks like timed transcription exams or mission-critical technical documentation. Results will be disseminated through computational linguistics conferences and integrated into keyboarding pedagogy modules to bridge theoretical training with industry-scale system demands.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: The increasing demand for energy-efficient power electronic systems necessitates advanced optimization methodologies to address complex trade-offs between efficiency, thermal management, and electromagnetic compatibility. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multi-objective design optimization of next-generation switched-mode power converters. Current design processes rely on iterative prototyping and simplified analytical models, which fail to capture nonlinear interactions between semiconductor devices, passive components, and control algorithms under dynamic operating conditions. The proposed research will employ parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) for electromagnetic and thermal modeling, coupled with machine learning techniques to explore high-dimensional parameter spaces and identify Pareto-optimal configurations. Large-scale parametric sweeps will characterize component interactions across frequency domains, while transient simulations will assess stability margins and harmonic distortion profiles. The computational workflow will integrate SPICE-level circuit simulations with 3D multiphysics models to bridge system-level and component-level analyses. Successful implementation will reduce development cycles by predicting performance boundaries prior to physical prototyping, enabling rapid iteration of topologies such as LLC resonant converters and active rectification systems. Expected outcomes include validated design guidelines for high-density power converters targeting 95%+ efficiency across load ranges, with direct applications in renewable energy integration and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. This work requires HPC resources to manage the computational intensity of coupled simulations, particularly for GPU-accelerated FEA solvers and distributed training of neural networks on terascale datasets. Results will advance simulation-driven design methodologies in power electronics, aligning with industry needs for sustainable energy conversion technologies.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronic, and Communications Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of electrical, electronics and communication engineers. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, prototype development and testing, systems analysis and testing, systems maintenance, instrument calibration, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the emergent dynamics of microbial biofilm communities under fluctuating environmental stressors, integrating principles from biophysics, geochemistry, and systems biology. Microbial biofilms play critical roles in natural ecosystems, industrial processes, and human health, yet their resilience to dynamic stressors—such as pH shifts, nutrient oscillations, and temperature gradients—remains poorly understood at the intersection of physical interactions and biological adaptation. Current models often oversimplify either the physicochemical environment or the genetic-regulatory networks governing microbial behavior, limiting predictive power. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of individual microbial cells with lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations of fluid flow and solute transport. This approach will resolve microscale chemical gradients, hydrodynamic shear forces, and cell-cell signaling dynamics across spatially heterogeneous biofilm architectures. The ABM component will incorporate stochastic gene expression models to simulate phenotypic plasticity, while the LBM will capture advection-diffusion-reaction processes at the biofilm-environment interface. By parallelizing these coupled simulations on HPC clusters, we aim to explore how biofilm functional resilience emerges from the interplay of local environmental variability, metabolic trade-offs, and evolutionary constraints. Expected outcomes include novel insights into biofilm adaptation thresholds under climate-relevant stressor regimes, with applications to biofilm mitigation strategies and engineered biofilm optimization. The computational framework will also provide a template for integrating biological complexity with physicochemical realism in other interdisciplinary systems. Successful implementation requires sustained access to HGPU nodes for parameter space exploration and large-scale 3D simulations, as well as high-memory nodes for handling hybrid model datasets. This work will advance predictive modeling in environmental microbiology while fostering methodological synergies between traditionally siloed disciplines.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on one or more of the physical and biological sciences.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Catalan linguistic diversity and literary production across historical and contemporary contexts. The Catalan language, with its complex dialectal variations and rich textual traditions, presents unique challenges for large-scale linguistic analysis, particularly in parsing regional phonological, morphological, and syntactic features from heterogeneous sources, including medieval manuscripts, modern literature, and digital communication. Traditional methods struggle to efficiently process the growing corpus of digitized texts (spanning over 10 million words) and audio recordings, necessitating scalable computational approaches. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models and dialectometric algorithms, to map dialectal boundaries, track language evolution, and identify stylistic patterns in Catalan literature. Custom pipelines will be developed to handle non-standard orthography in historical texts and code-switching phenomena in modern media. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large datasets, training of language-specific models, and high-resolution visualization of linguistic trends. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Catalan texts, tools for automated dialect classification, and quantitative insights into the sociolinguistic factors shaping language use in educational and technological domains. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to strengthen resources for Catalan language preservation, pedagogy, and digital humanities research while setting a precedent for under-resourced language studies. The requested computing infrastructure is critical to managing memory-intensive tasks, such as aligning cross-dialectal corpora and simulating language change models, which are infeasible on standard academic workstations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Catalan language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The development of next-generation spacecraft for deep-space exploration and hypersonic atmospheric entry requires high-fidelity modeling of complex aerothermodynamic phenomena. Current computational tools struggle to resolve multi-scale, non-equilibrium gas dynamics in rarefied and transitional flow regimes, which are critical for optimizing thermal protection systems (TPS) and ensuring mission safety. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement advanced particle-continuum hybrid algorithms and machine learning-accelerated solvers. The research will focus on simulating coupled radiation-ablation processes during atmospheric entry and plasma interactions around spacecraft in low-Earth orbit. A multi-physics framework will integrate Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) methods for rarefied flows, Navier-Stokes solvers with finite-rate chemistry for continuum regions, and neural network surrogates to bridge spatiotemporal scales.
