Large-scale parametric studies will assess TPS material responses under extreme heating conditions and ionization effects on communication blackout phases. Validation will utilize experimental data from arc-jet facilities and flight tests from collaborative partnerships with NASA centers. The computational demands are substantial, requiring millions of core-hours to resolve microseconds of physical time across three-dimensional domains with adaptive mesh refinement. Anticipated outcomes include validated models for predicting heat flux distributions with <10% uncertainty relative to current industry standards, a publicly accessible database of ablation-radiation coupling coefficients, and reduced-order models deployable for real-time mission planning. This work directly supports the design of crewed Mars entry vehicles and reusable hypersonic platforms, addressing national priorities in space exploration and responsive launch capabilities. The requested HPC allocation will enable unprecedented resolution of gas-surface interaction physics, advancing fundamental knowledge in rarefied flow theory while delivering engineering tools to mitigate risks in high-speed flight operations.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any program in aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, or space engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing algorithmic decision-making in human resources (HR). As organizations increasingly deploy artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) tools for hiring, performance evaluation, and workforce management, disparities in compliance with anti-discrimination laws, data privacy regulations, and jurisdictional mandates have emerged as a critical challenge. Traditional legal analysis struggles to systematically evaluate the scale and interaction of these tools with heterogeneous legal requirements, particularly across multinational contexts. To address this gap, the project will develop a computational legal analytics framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and simulation modeling. Legal texts—including statutes, case law, administrative guidance, and enforcement actions from multiple jurisdictions—will be processed using transformer-based models to identify obligations, risks, and conflicts related to algorithmic HR systems. Agent-based simulations will then model organizational compliance behaviors under varying regulatory conditions, while graph neural networks will map cross-jurisdictional legal influences. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale legal corpora, iterative training of domain-specific ML models, and large-scale scenario testing—tasks requiring HPC infrastructure for distributed storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and high-throughput simulations. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of algorithmic HR compliance risks, predictive tools for assessing policy impacts on equitable workplace outcomes, and a public dataset linking legal provisions to technical system requirements. By bridging computational methods and HR law, this work aims to advance evidence-based regulatory design and provide organizations with scalable strategies for maintaining legal and ethical AI deployments in HR practices.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting human resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of maintaining modern building systems—including HVAC, electrical networks, plumbing, and integrated appliances—by developing a computational framework for predictive maintenance and energy optimization. The increasing reliance on IoT-enabled sensors and heterogeneous data streams in buildings generates vast datasets that traditional analytical tools struggle to process efficiently. Current maintenance practices often rely on reactive or fixed-interval strategies, which lead to unnecessary costs, energy waste, and system downtime. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to model building systems dynamically, predict failures, and optimize resource allocation for maintenance tasks. The research will integrate real-time sensor data, historical maintenance records, and environmental variables (e.g., weather patterns, occupancy rates) into a machine learning pipeline. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model HVAC performance under varying operational scenarios, while graph neural networks will analyze interdependencies between electrical, plumbing, and mechanical systems to identify failure cascades. HPC resources are critical to train these models at scale, process terabyte-scale datasets from diverse structures (commercial buildings, industrial facilities, and mobile homes), and run parallelized simulations to assess system resilience. Expected outcomes include a predictive maintenance toolkit that prioritizes high-risk failures, recommends energy-efficient system configurations, and adapts to the unique demands of different building types. This work will provide facility managers with actionable insights to reduce operational costs by an estimated 15–20%, extend equipment lifespans, and lower carbon footprints through optimized energy use. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to bridge the gap between traditional building maintenance practices and data-driven smart infrastructure management, fostering safer, more sustainable built environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to keep a building functioning, and to service a variety of structures including commercial and industrial buildings and mobile homes. Includes instruction in the basic maintenance and repair skills required to service building systems, such as air conditioning, heating, plumbing, electrical, major appliances, and other mechanical systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in traditional data entry workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable solutions for automating and optimizing microcomputer-based tasks. Conventional data entry processes often struggle with accuracy and speed when handling large datasets, particularly in applications such as spreadsheet management, database population, and audio-to-text transcription. The proposed research will implement parallelized data processing algorithms on HPC clusters to accelerate batch operations in common productivity software, while machine learning models trained on GPU-accelerated nodes will be deployed to automate error detection and correction in heterogeneous data streams. Additionally, computational simulations will evaluate the performance characteristics of distributed data entry systems under varying workloads, informing the design of adaptive resource allocation strategies. The expected outcomes include (1) open-source tools for enhancing legacy microcomputer applications with HPC capabilities, (2) benchmarks for error reduction in automated data pipelines, and (3) a framework for integrating voice recognition technologies with cluster-based text processing workflows. By bridging the gap between consumer-grade software and advanced computational infrastructure, this work aims to establish new paradigms for efficiency and reliability in data-driven technical fields, with potential applications in administrative support, digital archiving, and real-time transcription services. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the large-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations required to validate these methods, ensuring robust, generalizable results that advance both educational and industry practices in microcomputer applications.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform basic data and text entry using standard and customized software products. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, personal computer and work station operation, reading draft texts and raw data forms, audio and tape dictation, and various interactive software programs used for tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, databases, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational advertising, specifically addressing the challenge of optimizing real-time, cross-platform ad campaign performance in dynamic consumer environments. Modern advertising requires rapid analysis of vast datasets—including social media interactions, consumer behavior metrics, and real-time bidding logs—to deliver personalized content while balancing ethical, budgetary, and brand consistency constraints. Existing methods struggle to process these heterogeneous data streams at scale, limiting predictive accuracy and adaptability. The proposed research will develop machine learning models to simulate and predict consumer responses across diverse media channels, integrating natural language processing for ad copy analysis, computer vision for visual ad element optimization, and reinforcement learning for adaptive budget allocation. Agent-based modeling will simulate large-scale consumer networks to test campaign scenarios under varying market conditions. These computationally intensive tasks demand parallelized processing, GPU acceleration, and large-memory nodes to handle terabyte-scale datasets and complex model training workflows. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for real-time ad performance prediction, actionable insights into cross-platform audience engagement patterns, and open-source tools for ethical targeting parameter optimization. The project will directly support graduate-level coursework in data-driven advertising strategy and provide empirical foundations for three peer-reviewed studies on computational advertising efficiency. By enabling rapid iteration of campaign simulations that mirror real-world complexity, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical advertising models and practical industry needs while adhering to emerging privacy standards. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the required computational throughput for multi-objective optimization tasks, which would be infeasible on local infrastructure.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creation, execution, transmission, and evaluation of commercial messages in various media intended to promote and sell products, services, and brands; and that prepares individuals to function as advertising assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in advertising theory, marketing strategy, advertising design and production methods, campaign methods and techniques, media management, related principles of business management, and applicable technical and equipment skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to analyze the structural and cultural dynamics of 19th-century transnational missionary networks through computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multilingual archival materials and simulate interaction patterns. Missionary activities during this period involved complex exchanges between religious institutions, colonial infrastructures, and Indigenous communities, yet existing studies often focus on isolated case histories. The project addresses this gap by constructing a large-scale relational database from digitized correspondence, mission reports, and regional ethnographic records (spanning English, French, German, and Indigenous languages), then applying natural language processing (NLP) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to map how doctrinal adaptations, resource allocation decisions, and cross-cultural conflicts propagated across global networks. Key computational challenges include training multilingual NLP models to detect semantic shifts in missionary writings over time, geolocating unstructured historical data, and simulating decentralized decision-making processes within ABM frameworks at scale. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the volume of heterogeneous data (estimated at 15 TB), parallelizing language model fine-tuning, and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about network resilience and cultural hybridity. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated missionary records, a suite of computational tools tailored for historical network analysis in underrepresented linguistic contexts, and new interdisciplinary frameworks for understanding how ideological systems adapt in transnational contexts. By integrating methods from digital humanities, computational linguistics, and complexity science, this project aims to redefine scholarly approaches to missiology as a catalyst for both cultural preservation and conflict, with implications for contemporary studies of globalization and intercultural communication.
cip_title: Missions/ Missionary Studies and Missiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in missions, missionary studies, and missiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze cross-cultural literary patterns across multilingual corpora spanning French, Japanese, and Arabic modernist prose (1890–1950). While traditional comparative methods have focused on close readings of select texts, the scale and linguistic diversity of global literary production during this period—coupled with variations in syntax, semantic structures, and translation artifacts—pose significant barriers to systematic analysis. Current tools for multilingual text mining lack the capacity to process non-Latin scripts at scale or model stylistic convergences across divergent grammatical systems. Our research will employ transformer-based language models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, parallelized sentiment and metaphor detection algorithms, and graph-based network analysis to trace transnational thematic clusters. Computational workflows will integrate optical character recognition for digitized archival materials in Arabic and Japanese scripts, alignment of multilingual embeddings to reduce translation-induced bias, and GPU-accelerated topic modeling across 15,000+ texts. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized stylistic exchanges between Francophone and Arabic experimental movements, as well as quantitative frameworks for assessing non-Western modernisms’ role in shaping global literary aesthetics. The project’s computational demands—including large-scale distributed training of multilingual transformers, memory-intensive processing of high-resolution scanned texts, and real-time alignment of cross-lingual semantic networks—necessitate HPC infrastructure. Results will advance methodologies in computational comparative literature while challenging Eurocentric periodization models, with open-source tools released to support under-resourced language analysis in the humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on two or more literary traditions in the original languages or in translation. Includes instruction in comparative linguistics; applicable foreign languages; English/French language and literature; literary criticism; and applications to genre, period, national, and textual studies as well as literary forms such as poetry, prose, and drama.

abstract: Modern agricultural operations face increasing complexity due to the need to integrate heterogeneous data streams—such as weather patterns, soil health metrics, crop yields, livestock biometrics, and market fluctuations—into actionable management decisions. Current analytical tools often lack the capacity to process these multidimensional datasets at scale, limiting the ability to optimize operational efficiency, financial planning, and long-term sustainability. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision-support framework for farm and ranch management. The research will focus on creating agent-based models that simulate farm operations under variable environmental and economic conditions, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict outcomes of management strategies. These models will incorporate real-time data from IoT sensors, historical yield records, and regional market trends to evaluate resource allocation scenarios, including labor distribution, equipment use, capital investment, and risk mitigation. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle large-scale spatial-temporal datasets and stochastic simulations of climate variability, pest outbreaks, and commodity price shifts. By leveraging HPC resources, the project aims to generate predictive insights into optimal planting schedules, livestock rotation plans, and financial hedging strategies while accounting for regulatory constraints and estate planning considerations. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for adaptive farm management, validated against empirical data from partner agricultural enterprises. This work will advance precision agriculture by enabling dynamic, data-driven decision-making at the enterprise level, directly contributing to improved profitability and resilience in farm operations. The scalability of the proposed framework will also support policy analyses on the economic impacts of agricultural subsidies or climate adaptation programs, fostering broader interdisciplinary collaboration in agricultural sciences.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage farms, ranches, and similar enterprises. Includes instruction in applicable agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, taxation, capitalization, purchasing, government programs and regulations, operational planning and budgeting, contracts and negotiation, and estate planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the precision and innovation of baking and pastry arts through computational modeling of complex biochemical and physical processes inherent to artisanal and commercial baking. Traditional baking relies heavily on experiential knowledge and iterative experimentation, limiting the scalability of recipe optimization, consistency in product quality, and adaptation to novel dietary or sustainability constraints. To address these challenges, this research proposes the development of a multi-scale simulation framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) models of dough fermentation, heat and mass transfer simulations during baking, and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive analytics for texture and flavor outcomes. The MD component will simulate enzymatic activity and gas diffusion in dough matrices under varying ingredient ratios and environmental conditions, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will analyze heat distribution patterns in commercial ovens to minimize energy waste and optimize crust formation. Concurrently, ML algorithms will process experimental and simulated datasets to correlate ingredient combinations, processing parameters, and sensory outcomes, enabling predictive recipe design. HPC resources are critical to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize stochastic simulations, and train deep learning models on heterogeneous data (e.g., 3D crumb structure imaging, moisture gradients). Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for bakers to prototype recipes virtually, reduce trial-and-error resource costs, and customize products for dietary needs without compromising traditional quality. By bridging culinary arts with computational science, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven gastronomy, enhancing both the sustainability and creativity of professional baking practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares  individuals to serve as professional bakers and pastry specialists in restaurants or other commercial baking establishments.  Includes instruction in bread and pastry making, bread and pastry handling and storage, cake and pastry decorating, baking industry operations, product packaging and marketing operations, and counter display and service.

abstract: The increasing demand for durable, sustainable, and customized footwear and leather goods necessitates advancements in repair methodologies that integrate modern computational techniques. Traditional shoe, boot, and leather repair practices rely heavily on empirical knowledge and manual processes, which limit scalability, precision, and adaptability to new materials. This project proposes to address these challenges by developing computational models to optimize repair techniques, material interactions, and structural integrity assessments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to simulate the mechanical behavior of repaired footwear components under stress, model the chemical interactions of dyes and adhesives with aged or degraded materials, and predict the long-term performance of orthopedic modifications. A multi-scale computational approach will be employed, combining finite element analysis (FEA) for macro-scale stress distribution studies, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate leather-dye adhesion at the molecular level, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to correlate repair parameters with customer-reported durability metrics. The HPC environment is critical to handle the high-resolution simulations of heterogeneous materials (e.g., layered leather, synthetic composites) and the large datasets generated from 3D scans of repaired goods. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimal stitch patterns in high-wear areas, solvent selection frameworks for eco-friendly refinishing, and a digital toolset to guide the restoration of vintage leather items while preserving historical integrity. By bridging artisanal craftsmanship with computational engineering, this research will empower repair technicians with data-driven decision-making tools, reduce material waste through precision repair planning, and extend the functional lifespan of footwear and leather products—advancing sustainability in the leather goods lifecycle. The project will also establish a precedent for computational resource integration in technical trade education, fostering interdisciplinary innovation in vocational technology fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair all types of footwear, including replacement and mending of worn parts, repairing orthopedic footwear, refinishing and dyeing leather, and repairing other leather goods such as handbags, belts, and luggage.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolution of theological frameworks within the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS) through computational analysis of doctrinal discourse across historical and contemporary sources. The primary challenge lies in systematically identifying patterns of continuity and change in LDS theology, given the vast and heterogeneous corpus of texts—including sermons, official publications, and scholarly exegeses—spanning nearly two centuries. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to scale to this volume of data, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models, semantic network analysis, and dynamic topic modeling, to analyze doctrinal shifts in context. This will involve training custom models on a curated dataset of digitized LDS texts, historical records, and comparative religious writings to detect theological motifs, conceptual relationships, and rhetorical strategies. A secondary aim involves simulating the diffusion of doctrinal interpretations through agent-based modeling, incorporating sociological data on LDS community structures. The computational intensity of processing multilingual texts (e.g., early translations of foundational works) and generating high-dimensional semantic maps requires parallelized workflows and significant memory allocation, which HPC infrastructure uniquely provides. Expected outcomes include a temporally stratified ontology of Mormon theological concepts, quantitative frameworks for assessing religious discourse evolution, and openly accessible computational tools tailored for interdisciplinary religious studies. This project will advance methodological innovation in digital humanities while offering empirically grounded insights into how LDS theology negotiates modernity, authority, and cultural change—a contribution critical to philosophy of religion and sociological studies of religious institutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on beliefs, practices, culture, and history of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Mormon). Includes instruction in Mormon culture, history, literature, philosophy, sociology, and theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance three-dimensional (3D) multiscale modeling of musculoskeletal systems in large animal species, with a focus on equine and bovine anatomy. A critical challenge in veterinary anatomy is understanding how microstructural tissue properties, such as tendon fiber alignment or bone trabecular architecture, influence macroscale biomechanical function and susceptibility to injury. Current imaging and modeling approaches lack the computational capacity to integrate high-resolution histological, micro-CT, and MRI datasets into dynamic simulations spanning cellular to organ-level scales. To address this, we propose developing a computational pipeline that combines deep learning-based segmentation of multi-modal imaging data with finite element modeling (FEM) and agent-based simulations. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale volumetric datasets, automated reconstruction of tissue microenvironments, and simulation of mechanical stress propagation under physiological loading conditions. Key objectives include mapping strain distribution patterns in equine superficial digital flexor tendons during locomotion and modeling remodeling dynamics in bovine subchondral bone under osteoarthritis progression. The outcomes will provide unprecedented insights into species-specific biomechanical adaptations, identify early biomarkers of degenerative tissue changes, and inform targeted therapeutic strategies. By creating open-source tools for veterinary-specific computational anatomy, this work will establish a framework for predictive modeling of complex anatomical systems, directly addressing gaps in translational veterinary research. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated neural network training, large-scale parallelized FEM computations, and storage of annotated multi-species anatomical datasets, fostering collaboration across veterinary biomechanics and precision medicine communities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of small and large animal cellular, organ, tissue, and body systems and their relation to physiologic function, disease, and therapeutic treatment. Includes instruction in histology, ultrastructure, molecular biology, biochemistry, developmental biology, neuroscience, electrophysiology, electron microscopy, computer imaging, and applications to specific species.

abstract: Public sector resource allocation during crises remains a persistent challenge, with inefficiencies in disaster response and social service delivery disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize equitable resource distribution under dynamic, large-scale emergencies such as pandemics or climate-related disasters. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with geospatial analytics, we will simulate urban disaster scenarios to evaluate how institutional decision-making protocols, infrastructure limitations, and socioeconomic disparities interact to constrain effective responses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process real-time demographic datasets, model millions of agent interactions, and run iterative policy experiments under varying crisis conditions. The computational architecture will incorporate machine learning to adaptively refine resource prioritization rules based on simulated outcomes, including metrics for equity, cost efficiency, and service coverage. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated ABM toolkit for stress-testing public administration policies in silico, (2) evidence-based protocols to reduce spatial and demographic disparities in emergency resource access, and (3) scalable decision-support interfaces for municipal planners. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, this project will overcome current limitations in modeling granular urban systems at regional scales, enabling unprecedented analysis of how micro-level decisions aggregate to macro-level service gaps. Results will directly inform resilience planning in three partner cities, while the open-source framework will empower broader academic and governmental efforts to computationally evaluate equity-centered governance strategies. This work bridges computational social science with public administration practice, advancing both methodological capacity and applied policy knowledge in crisis management.
cip_definition: Any program in public administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the spatial and temporal dynamics of informal urban green spaces (IGS) as adaptive socio-ecological systems in rapidly urbanizing regions, with a focus on how marginalized communities repurpose residual land for climate resilience and cultural practices. While traditional urban geography emphasizes formal planning, this study addresses the gap in understanding self-organized, bottom-up adaptations to environmental stressors, particularly in contexts where governance structures are fragmented. The research employs a mixed-methods computational framework integrating high-resolution satellite imagery, agent-based modeling (ABM), and ethnographic data to analyze how informal green infrastructure emerges, evolves, and sustains under competing land-use pressures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-temporal geospatial datasets (10-30m resolution, 2000-2023) across six case study cities, running spatially explicit ABMs simulating household decision-making under climate scenarios (RCP 4.5/8.5), and applying machine learning classifiers to differentiate culturally significant vegetation patterns from random growth. The computational pipeline combines Python-based geospatial analytics (GDAL, rasterio), NetLogo for ABM parallelization, and PyTorch for training convolutional neural networks on historical land-use transitions. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable model linking micro-scale social practices to macro-scale landscape changes, (2) evidence-based thresholds for IGS viability under urbanization rates exceeding 3% annually, and (3) open-access tools for participatory mapping of culturally meaningful green infrastructure. By quantifying how informal systems buffer heat island effects and preserve biocultural diversity, this work aims to inform hybrid governance approaches that bridge formal environmental policy with grassroots ecological knowledge.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human cultures and their adaptation to physical environments. Includes instruction in archaeology, biogeography, climatology, cultural anthropology, cultural geography, economic development, environmental geography, geomorphology, global environmental change, historical geography, mapping sciences, physical anthropology, political ecology, Quaternary studies, and urban geography.

abstract: Audiovisual communication technologies face growing demands for processing high-resolution, multimodal data in real-time applications, yet existing computational infrastructures struggle to balance latency, quality, and scalability. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a novel framework for adaptive streaming and immersive audiovisual synthesis using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on optimizing dynamic resource allocation for parallelized encoding/decoding pipelines, leveraging machine learning models to predict and prioritize bandwidth-intensive visual and auditory elements in heterogeneous network environments. Computational workflows will integrate GPU-accelerated neural networks for real-time video super-resolution and spatial audio rendering, paired with distributed computing strategies to synchronize multi-channel data streams. The project will utilize HPC clusters to simulate large-scale user interactions in virtual environments, stress-testing latency thresholds under variable load conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for efficient bitrate adaptation in 4K/8K streaming, validated benchmarks for QoS (Quality of Service) in cloud-based audiovisual production, and a scalable architecture for low-latency telepresence systems. By advancing computational methods tailored to audiovisual workflows, this work aims to directly benefit remote collaboration tools, interactive media platforms, and accessibility technologies—domains critical to modern communication and journalism. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of video/audio datasets, training deep learning models on temporal-spatial features, and emulating global-scale user networks to ensure practical applicability. This research bridges a gap in non-STEM computational innovation, demonstrating how HPC can drive progress in understudied areas of audiovisual technology while adhering to ethical standards for data privacy and inclusive design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in audiovisual communications technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric musculoskeletal disorders present unique challenges due to the dynamic nature of skeletal growth and the heterogeneity of disease presentations. Current treatment strategies for conditions such as early-onset scoliosis, developmental dysplasia of the hip, and growth plate injuries often rely on generalized protocols that may not account for patient-specific anatomical variability or longitudinal growth patterns. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing computational models to optimize personalized treatment planning and predict long-term outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale simulations integrating biomechanical, imaging, and clinical data from a multicenter pediatric cohort. The research will employ finite element analysis to model bone remodeling under surgical or bracing interventions, machine learning algorithms to identify predictors of treatment response, and agent-based simulations to map growth trajectories in congenital deformities. Key computational challenges include managing high-resolution 3D imaging datasets, resolving multi-scale interactions between implants and developing bone, and executing iterative simulations across parameter spaces representing biological variability. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical for parallel processing of these resource-intensive tasks, enabling rapid prototyping of virtual treatment scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for postoperative complication risks, data-driven guidelines for implant selection in growing patients, and open-source tools for simulating growth-modulating interventions. By bridging computational innovation with clinical data, this work aims to reduce revision surgery rates, improve functional outcomes, and establish a framework for precision medicine in pediatric orthopedics. The proposed models will be shared via a cloud-based platform to facilitate collaborative research and clinical translation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, surgical and non-surgical treatment, and management of musculoskeletal diseases, abnormalities and trauma in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in mathematical logic by addressing open questions in model theory, recursion theory, and set theory through computationally intensive methods. The core problem involves analyzing the structural properties and decidability boundaries of formal systems, particularly in contexts where traditional proof-based methods encounter complexity barriers. A central focus is the classification of countable models for theories with non-standard arithmetic, where the interplay between automorphism groups and definability patterns remains poorly understood. To tackle this, we propose a hybrid approach combining symbolic computation with Monte Carlo methods to generate and test candidate models under varying axiomatic constraints. This requires enumerating possible structures while verifying their consistency with target properties, a process computationally infeasible without high-performance resources. A second thrust investigates the computational complexity of ordinal-invariant functions in admissible set theory, aiming to characterize their recursion-theoretic behavior through large-scale simulation of priority arguments. These simulations will map convergence patterns across ordinal notations, demanding parallelized processing of iterative trees with depths exceeding practical manual analysis. In set theory, the project will employ distributed computing to explore consistency bounds for combinatorial principles under large cardinal hypotheses, iterating forcing constructions to identify critical thresholds. The computational workload involves manipulating sparse matrices representing set-theoretic universes, with memory-intensive tasks scaling exponentially with cardinality parameters. Outcomes will include the first systematic taxonomy of automorphism-rich models in weak arithmetic systems, a complexity hierarchy for ordinal-driven functions, and refined consistency results for determinacy axioms. By integrating computational rigor with theoretical frameworks, this work aims to resolve conjectures in reverse mathematics and descriptive set theory while establishing scalable methodologies for future logic research. The requested resources—high-memory nodes, GPU-accelerated parallelism, and long-duration job scheduling—are essential to manage the combinatorial explosion inherent in these problems, enabling breakthroughs in understanding the limits of formal systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study foundations of mathematics, including model theory, recursion theory and set theory.

abstract: The increasing complexity of datasets in fields such as public health, environmental science, and urban planning demands visualization tools that transcend traditional static or low-dimensional representations. However, existing methods often fail to integrate real-time, multi-modal data streams (e.g., sensor networks, geospatial layers, and qualitative narratives) into cohesive visual frameworks that support decision-making under uncertainty. This project proposes the development of an adaptive, high-dimensional visualization platform to unify heterogeneous data types while preserving context-specific interpretability. The research problem centers on balancing computational scalability with perceptual accessibility: how can dynamic, large-scale datasets be rendered interactively without overwhelming users or obscuring critical patterns? The computational approach combines graph-based data structures for hierarchical relationships, GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines for real-time updates, and machine learning models trained on eye-tracking datasets to optimize visual saliency. High-performance computing resources are essential for simulating multi-agent interactions (e.g., crowd movement in disaster scenarios), training perception-aware ML models, and stress-testing visualization scalability across datasets exceeding 10^8 elements. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for context-aware visual analytics, validated through case studies in climate resilience planning and emergency response coordination. By embedding cognitive principles (e.g., gestalt grouping, color semiotics) into computational workflows, this work aims to reduce misinterpretation risks in high-stakes scenarios while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for data synthesis. The project’s significance lies in bridging gaps between technical scalability, human-centered design, and domain-specific storytelling—a triad often siloed in existing visualization research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and derive meaning from data by using visual presentation tools and techniques. Includes instruction in cognitive science, computer programming, data management, data visualization theory, graphic design, infographics, perceptual psychology, statistics, and visual design.

abstract: Pediatric infectious diseases present unique challenges due to evolving pathogens, complex host-pathogen interactions in developing immune systems, and the urgent need for precision in treating vulnerable populations. This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting treatment outcomes for severe pediatric infections, particularly in cases involving antimicrobial resistance, atypical presentations, or comorbidities. We aim to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating host genomic, pathogen genomic, and clinical data to model disease progression and optimize therapeutic strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets, including whole-genome sequencing of bacterial and viral isolates from pediatric patients, longitudinal electronic health records, and multi-omics profiles of host immune responses. Machine learning approaches will be employed to identify biomarkers of treatment failure, while mechanistic models will simulate pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationships in pediatric physiology. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of infection dynamics within hospital settings to evaluate targeted prevention strategies. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across 10,000+ patient records, Bayesian inference for treatment outcome prediction, and real-time simulations of outbreak scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for personalized antimicrobial selection, risk stratification tools for complicated infections, and optimized dosing guidelines for novel therapeutics. By elucidating interactions between pathogen virulence factors and developmental immunology, this work will directly inform clinical trial design and stewardship programs. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project's data volume (>500 TB), complex model architectures, and iterative analyses required to translate computational insights into actionable clinical protocols for pediatric infectious disease management.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases in children; and to effect a better outcome for pediatric infections with complicated courses, underlying diseases that predispose to unusual or severe infections, unclear diagnoses, uncommon diseases, and complex or investigational treatments.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in real-time auditing and risk assessment frameworks for decentralized financial ecosystems, specifically focusing on blockchain-based transactions and smart contracts. Traditional accounting and finance models struggle to adapt to the velocity, volume, and cryptographic complexity of decentralized ledgers, resulting in delayed anomaly detection and systemic risk exposure. The project proposes developing a computational framework that integrates machine learning (ML) with distributed ledger analytics to automate compliance checks, fraud detection, and liquidity risk forecasting in real time. Using parallelized processing on HPC clusters, the team will train deep neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets of historical blockchain transactions, synthetic smart contract interactions, and correlated market data. Agent-based modeling will simulate stress scenarios across hybrid financial systems (e.g., decentralized finance protocols interfacing with traditional banking), while graph algorithms will map interdependencies between transactional nodes to predict contagion risks. Key challenges include optimizing cryptographic verification workflows for GPU acceleration and reducing latency in cross-chain data aggregation. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dynamic audit trails in Web3 environments, predictive models for regulatory arbitrage detection, and benchmarks for computational resource allocation in decentralized accounting infrastructures. By bridging cryptographic finance, computational auditing, and high-frequency risk analytics, this work aims to establish scalable protocols for transparency and stability in emerging digital asset markets, with direct applications for financial institutions, regulatory bodies, and blockchain developers. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive graph traversals, hyperparameter tuning of ensemble ML models, and large-scale validation against real-world DeFi platforms.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and finance that prepares individuals to function as accountants and financial managers or analysts.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of non-classical logics by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze the computational complexity and proof-theoretic properties of paraconsistent and many-valued logical systems. While classical logic remains foundational, non-classical frameworks are increasingly critical in addressing inconsistencies in real-world reasoning, AI systems, and interdisciplinary applications. However, the meta-logical exploration of these systems—including questions of decidability, proof complexity, and automated theorem proving—is constrained by the exponential growth of search spaces in even modestly expressive formalisms. Traditional analytical methods struggle to scale, particularly when evaluating interactions between non-classical operators, adaptive proof strategies, or multi-agent reasoning dynamics. This project proposes a computational approach combining formal verification techniques with parallelized theorem-proving algorithms to systematically map the resource requirements of reasoning in these logics. Custom proof-search algorithms will be implemented using SAT modulo theories (SMT) frameworks and optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters to handle combinatorial explosions in possible derivation paths. Simulations will assess the tractability of paraconsistent inference under varying consistency constraints and quantify the impact of many-valued truth-value lattices on proof length. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a ranked taxonomy of non-classical logics by computational complexity, (2) optimized heuristics for automated reasoning in understudied systems like relevance and fuzzy logics, and (3) open-source tools enabling philosophers to test conjectures about logical properties at unprecedented scales. By bridging formal philosophy with computational methods, this work aims to resolve long-standing debates about the feasibility of applying non-classical logics in knowledge representation systems while providing a template for resource-intensive meta-logical analysis. The requested HPC resources are essential due to the parallel nature of proof-space exploration and the need for repeated large-scale experiments across parameterized logic families.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of valid inference, argument, and sound reasoning. Includes instruction in Classical logic, properties of argument, validity, proof, fallacies, formal and material logic, symbolic and mathematical logic, analysis, specific schools of logic, and applications to problems in other academic disciplines and professional fields.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the linguistic and cultural evolution of Balkan communities through digitized historical manuscripts, oral histories, and ethnographic records spanning the medieval to modern periods. The core research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural exchange, language contact, and identity formation across the Balkan Peninsula, particularly among minority and non-Slavic groups underrepresented in existing scholarship. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of multimodal data—including handwritten texts in obsolete scripts, audio recordings in regional dialects, and visual cultural artifacts—that document these interactions. To address this, the project will implement computational workflows integrating natural language processing (NLP) for historical languages (e.g., Ottoman Turkish, Church Slavonic, and Arvanitika), machine learning-based image analysis of manuscript marginalia, and network modeling of cultural influence across time and space. Key challenges include developing OCR models for under-resourced Balkan scripts, aligning multilingual corpora, and detecting subtle semantic shifts in vernacular sources. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, training transformer models on Balkan linguistic varieties, and simulating cultural diffusion patterns through agent-based modeling. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated primary sources, computational tools tailored to Balkan studies, and new frameworks for interpreting hybrid identities in borderland regions. By bridging computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to reshape scholarly understanding of cultural resilience and transnational connectivity in a historically contested region, while preserving endangered linguistic heritage through machine-readable archives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the Balkan Peninsula and associated island groups and borderlands, Southern Slavic and non-Slavic, during the medieval, Ottoman, and modern periods.

abstract: The diagnosis of complex pathologies in veterinary medicine relies heavily on the integration of histopathological, molecular, and clinical data. Current workflows for analyzing diseased animal tissues face challenges in scalability, reproducibility, and quantitative precision, particularly when handling large-scale datasets from digital histopathology, genomic sequencing, or multiplex imaging. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational pathology pipeline optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The research will focus on automating the detection and classification of histomorphometric features in veterinary cancers and inflammatory diseases using deep learning models trained on whole-slide imaging (WSI) datasets. A secondary aim involves integrating spatially resolved transcriptomic data with histopathology findings to identify microenvironmental biomarkers of disease progression. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated image analysis frameworks (e.g., MONAI, PyTorch) for WSI processing and graph neural networks to model tissue-omics interactions. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte slide repositories, hyperparameter optimization for complex neural architectures, and genome-scale variant analysis. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for standardized lesion quantification in common veterinary species, open-source tools for multimodal data integration, and predictive models linking tissue-level patterns to clinical outcomes. By enhancing analytical throughput and precision, this work will directly inform diagnostic protocol improvements, therapeutic target discovery, and comparative disease modeling across species. The requested computing infrastructure is critical to manage memory-intensive analyses that exceed the capacity of local workstations, ensuring statistically robust validation across diverse case cohorts. Results will advance computational pathology capabilities in veterinary medicine while contributing reusable frameworks for biomedical machine learning applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of diseased animal tissues and anatomic abnormalities. May included related research in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management and quality control.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the interplay between advanced performance techniques and acoustic phenomena in stringed instruments. While traditional pedagogical and analytical methods in performing arts have focused on subjective or low-dimensional assessments of sound production, this study addresses the critical gap in quantitatively modeling the complex, nonlinear dynamics of string vibration, bowing mechanics, and resonance behavior across diverse instruments (e.g., violin, cello, harp). The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to map multiphysics interactions between performer gestures, instrument materials, and acoustic output at microsecond temporal resolution. Concurrently, machine learning models will process high-resolution audio datasets of professional performances to identify patterns linking technical execution to perceptual qualities like timbre and expressiveness. These computational workflows require parallelized processing of terabytes of data, necessitating HPC infrastructure for both large-scale numerical simulations and training of deep neural networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) a physics-informed framework correlating biomechanical input variables (bow pressure, fingering position) with spectral features, (2) predictive models of tonal quality across historical instrument designs, and (3) an open-access database of annotated performance data for pedagogical applications. By bridging computational acoustics and artistic practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based performance pedagogy while providing luthiers with quantitative tools for material and design optimization. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ simulated performance scenarios and real-time analysis of ensemble synchronization patterns, tasks infeasible on standard workstations. Results will directly inform curriculum development in string performance programs and establish novel methodologies for computational musicology research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individual to master a stringed instrument and performing arts as solo, ensemble and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in optimizing equine athletic performance and welfare through advanced computational modeling of biomechanical and physiological interactions during equestrian activities. While traditional equine studies rely on observational or small-scale empirical data, the complexity of dynamic horse-rider systems—particularly in competitive disciplines such as dressage, show jumping, and eventing—remains understudied at scale. This project will develop high-fidelity simulations of equine locomotion, muscle activation patterns, and rider biomechanics to quantify how training techniques, equipment adjustments, and environmental factors influence performance outcomes and injury risks. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning-driven multibody dynamics models to process motion-capture data from wearable sensors, veterinary imaging, and historical competition records. These models will integrate heterogeneous datasets spanning gait kinematics, ground reaction forces, and metabolic expenditure, enabling predictive analyses of stress distribution across musculoskeletal structures under varying scenarios. The computational framework will also simulate long-term effects of repetitive training loads to identify thresholds for overuse injuries. Expected outcomes include evidence-based guidelines for personalized training regimens, equipment optimization (e.g., saddle fit, horseshoe design), and interventions to mitigate career-limiting pathologies. By bridging equestrian expertise with computational biomechanics, this work will establish a novel paradigm for data-driven decision-making in equine management, enhancing both competitive outcomes and animal welfare standards. The scale of data fusion and real-time simulation required for such analyses necessitates HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-level datasets and parallelize computationally intensive iterative modeling, tasks infeasible with conventional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the horse, horsemanship, and related subjects and prepares individuals to care for horses and horse equipment; ride and drive horses for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes; and manage the training of horses and riders. Includes instruction in horse breeding, nutrition, health, and safety; history of the horse and horsemanship; horse development and training; riding and equestrian technique; stable, paddock, and track management; and equipment maintenance and repair.

abstract: The diagnosis and management of oral and maxillofacial diseases are complicated by the heterogeneity of pathological presentations, overlapping clinical features, and the need for multi-modal data integration. Current approaches often lack the computational capacity to synthesize high-dimensional datasets—including clinical histories, radiographic imaging, histopathological slides, and genomic profiles—into actionable diagnostic or prognostic models. This project proposes to address these challenges by developing a machine learning (ML) framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to enable precision classification of oral pathologies. The research will focus on oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), where early and accurate diagnosis is critical to improving patient outcomes. Key computational tasks include training deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on whole-slide histopathology images, integrating 3D radiographic volumetric data via hybrid vision transformers, and building multimodal fusion architectures to cross-reference clinical metadata with molecular biomarkers. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of terabytes of imaging data, hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models, and survival analysis using Cox proportional hazards frameworks scaled across multi-node GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) validated ML models for automated risk stratification of OPMD progression, (2) a radiomic-pathomic-genomic correlation atlas for OSCC subtyping, and (3) open-source tools for granular feature extraction from intraoral scans and CBCT datasets. By leveraging distributed computing to manage computational bottlenecks in multimodal integration, this work aims to establish a scalable pipeline for translating complex oral pathology data into clinical decision support systems. The results will directly address critical gaps in diagnostic reproducibility and therapeutic personalization, with potential applications in biomarker discovery, digital pathology workflows, and AI-assisted biopsy guidance.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases affecting the oral and maxillofacial regions, using clinical, radiographic, microscopic, biochemical, or other examinations.

abstract: This research project investigates the spatial dynamics of informal knowledge networks in urban environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model how transient social interactions shape localized innovation ecosystems. While prior studies focus on formal institutions or economic frameworks, this work addresses a gap in understanding self-organizing, non-hierarchical networks that emerge through ephemeral human contacts in public spaces, transit hubs, and community events. The research combines geolocated social media data, anonymized mobility traces, and ethnographic field observations to construct a multilayer network model capturing temporal, spatial, and social dimensions of knowledge exchange. Agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations will be implemented using parallelized computing architectures to test hypotheses about threshold effects in network formation, scaling relationships between urban morphology and innovation diffusion, and resilience to spatial disruptions. Computational challenges include processing petabyte-scale streaming datasets, optimizing graph neural networks for dynamic spatial networks, and running ensemble simulations across parameter spaces characterizing diverse urban configurations. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying "serendipity potential" in urban design, predictive models of grassroots innovation spread under different zoning policies, and open-source tools for simulating socio-spatial networks at metropolitan scales. Results will contribute to interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of human geography, computational social science, and urban informatics, offering evidence-based insights for planners seeking to foster inclusive innovation ecosystems without centralized coordination. The project's computational demands necessitate dedicated HPC resources due to memory-intensive network analyses, real-time data integration requirements, and the need for comparative scenario testing across multiple city typologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in geography, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model urban air pollutant dispersion and assess associated public health risks, addressing critical gaps in current environmental exposure assessments. Traditional models often rely on simplified meteorological and topographical data, leading to inaccuracies in predicting localized pollution hotspots and population-level exposure dynamics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this study will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning, and real-time sensor data to simulate multiphase pollutant transport at unprecedented spatial (1–10 m) and temporal (minute-scale) resolutions. The computational framework will couple open-source CFD software (e.g., OpenFOAM) with deep learning architectures to assimilate heterogeneous datasets, including LiDAR-derived urban geometry, traffic emissions inventories, and atmospheric boundary layer profiles. Parallelized simulations will quantify interactions between built environments, transient wind fields, and particulate matter (PM2.5/PM10) distributions across a representative metropolitan area. Model outputs will be validated against ground-based air quality monitors and wearable exposure sensors deployed in collaboration with public health partners. The HPC scale enables sensitivity analyses to evaluate mitigation scenarios, such as green infrastructure placement or traffic rerouting, while reducing computational wall time from weeks to hours. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-access tool for municipal policymakers to prioritize interventions that reduce health disparities in pollution-burdened communities. This work directly advances environmental engineering’s capacity to resolve micro-scale exposure gradients, a prerequisite for achieving equity in urban sustainability planning. By aligning computational innovation with public health imperatives, the project supports the program’s mission to optimize engineered systems for environmental and human well-being.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: Veterinary toxicology faces a critical challenge in predicting and mitigating adverse health effects caused by synthetic and naturally occurring chemical exposures in animals. Current approaches to risk assessment rely heavily on time-consuming in vivo studies and limited mechanistic data, which fail to account for the vast chemical diversity and complex interactions affecting toxicity outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to model chemical interactions with biological targets and predict species-specific toxicological responses, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize toxin-receptor binding dynamics across veterinary-relevant species, including companion animals and livestock, with machine learning (ML) models trained on multi-omics datasets (transcriptomic, metabolomic) from clinical toxicology cases. Key objectives include mapping structural determinants of toxin affinity for neural, hepatic, and reproductive system targets; simulating dose-response relationships under varying physiological conditions; and identifying genetic susceptibility markers for adverse outcomes. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of MD simulations across diverse chemical classes (e.g., pesticides, mycotoxins, pharmaceuticals) and support the training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets encompassing 50,000+ historical exposure records. Expected outcomes include predictive models for acute and chronic toxicity thresholds, a computational biomarker panel for rapid clinical risk stratification, and mechanistic insights into interspecies variability in chemical sensitivity. This work will directly inform evidence-based treatment protocols, regulatory guidelines for veterinary drug residues, and targeted antidote development, addressing critical gaps in clinical veterinary toxicology while reducing reliance on animal testing. By bridging computational chemistry with clinical data science, the project establishes a scalable paradigm for precision toxicology in veterinary medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical application of research on the nature and extent of adverse effects of synthetic and naturally occurring chemical substances on animals. May included related research in chemical mechanisms and the specialties of reproductive, developmental, genetic, forensic, inhalation and neurobehavioral toxicology.

abstract: Emerging technologies increasingly demand interfaces that adapt to users’ dynamic cognitive and perceptual states, yet current design paradigms rely on static models of human behavior. This project addresses the challenge of creating real-time adaptive interfaces through computational modeling of individual neurocognitive processes during human-technology interaction. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to develop a framework that integrates multimodal data streams—including eye-tracking, electroencephalography (EEG), and interaction logs—to predict and respond to shifts in user attention, cognitive load, and decision-making strategies. The research problem centers on the computational latency and complexity of processing heterogeneous biosignals at scale, which existing consumer-grade systems cannot support. Our approach combines graph neural networks to model temporal dependencies in neurophysiological data with reinforcement learning agents that simulate interface adaptations. These models will be trained on a corpus of user studies involving diverse task environments, from healthcare decision-support systems to immersive educational platforms. HPC resources are critical for three components: (1) parallel processing of high-frequency biosignal data to achieve real-time inference, (2) large-scale hyperparameter optimization for personalized adaptation policies, and (3) agent-based simulations of population-level interface interactions under stochastic cognitive load scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dynamic interface personalization validated through controlled user experiments, with measurable improvements in task accuracy and cognitive ergonomics. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience and interaction design, offering a foundation for ethically aligned technologies that respect cognitive diversity. By prioritizing HPC-driven adaptability, the project advances human-centered design paradigms beyond reactive interfaces toward systems that co-evolve with users’ situated needs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on incorporating a human perspective into designing, researching, and creating technological interfaces. Includes instruction in design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

abstract: Palliative care patients often experience complex, dynamic pain profiles that require personalized treatment strategies. Current approaches to pain management rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for individual variability in drug metabolism, comorbidities, psychosocial factors, or genetic predispositions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing predictive computational models to optimize pain management regimens using high-dimensional clinical, genomic, and pharmacogenomic data. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze retrospective electronic health records (EHRs) from 15,000 palliative care patients, including pain scores, opioid dosing histories, adverse events, and polypharmacy interactions. Machine learning methods, such as recurrent neural networks and ensemble models, will be trained to predict individualized pain trajectories and opioid response patterns. Concurrently, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations will model interpatient variability in drug metabolism, incorporating genomic data from a subset of 2,000 patients with whole-exome sequencing. These simulations will utilize parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess dose-response relationships under diverse physiological scenarios. The integration of predictive ML outputs with PK/PD models aims to generate actionable treatment recommendations for clinical testing. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for identifying patient-specific risk factors for inadequate pain control or opioid toxicity, validated against prospective observational data. This work addresses a critical gap in palliative care by enabling data-driven personalization of pain management, with potential to reduce trial-and-error prescribing and improve quality of life for patients with serious illness. The scale of multimodal data integration and the complexity of concurrent ML and PK/PD modeling necessitate HPC resources for efficient computation, storage, and real-time analytics.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care/Pain Management

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance tactical decision-making frameworks in contested, multi-domain operational environments, a critical gap in contemporary military applied sciences. Current approaches to simulating hybrid threats—such as coordinated cyber-physical attacks, disinformation campaigns, and adaptive adversarial logistics—rely on compartmentalized models that inadequately capture the interdependencies between domains. The research problem centers on developing a unified computational architecture capable of simulating dynamic, multi-agent interactions across cyber, informational, and human terrain layers under resource-constrained conditions. The proposed methodology integrates agent-based modeling, game-theoretic adversarial reasoning, and real-time data assimilation to construct a scalable synthetic environment. This environment will test adaptive decision protocols for resource allocation, including prioritization of countermeasures under partial information and rapidly shifting threat landscapes. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, managing latency in iterative human-in-the-loop scenarios, and balancing fidelity with computational tractability in large-scale agent networks. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for evaluating trade-offs between preemptive resource investment and reactive flexibility, as well as novel metrics for resilience in hybrid conflict scenarios. The project will generate open-source tools for modular threat emulation, enabling military planners to stress-test contingency protocols against emergent asymmetric tactics. By addressing the computational barriers to holistic scenario generation, this work aims to inform doctrine for next-generation command-and-control systems, enhancing strategic adaptability in environments where traditional kinetic and non-kinetic boundaries are increasingly blurred.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dental restorative materials are critical for maintaining oral health, yet their long-term performance is limited by mechanical failure and biodegradation in the complex oral environment. This project addresses the need to predict and optimize the durability of resin-based composites (RBCs) used in dental restorations by modeling their interactions with mechanical stress, enzymatic activity, and microbial biofilms at multiscale resolutions. Current experimental approaches struggle to capture the dynamic interplay between physicochemical material properties and biological factors, leading to trial-and-error development cycles. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning to resolve these multiphysics interactions. Atomistic MD will characterize interfacial bonding between silica nanoparticles and polymer matrices under hydrolytic degradation, while coarse-grained models simulate biofilm adhesion mechanisms. FEA will map stress distribution in restored teeth during mastication, incorporating anisotropic material behavior derived from simulated microstructural defects. A neural network trained on simulation data will identify predictive relationships between filler morphology, monomer chemistry, and clinical failure modes. This computationally intensive workflow requires large-scale parallelization for parameter space exploration across 10^6+ configurations. Anticipated outcomes include a validated multiscale model of RBC degradation and failure, enabling inverse design of materials with enhanced fatigue resistance and biofilm-inhibiting surfaces. The resource allocation will directly support the development of open-source simulation tools tailored for dental biomaterials, bridging gaps between materials science, computational mechanics, and oral microbiology. By reducing reliance on physical prototyping, this work accelerates the translation of durable restorations to clinical practice while establishing a computational paradigm for studying interfacial phenomena in other bioactive material systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Lao language studies by developing scalable natural language processing (NLP) tools and analyzing historical and contemporary Lao texts. Despite Lao’s status as a linguistically and culturally significant language in Southeast Asia, it remains under-resourced in computational linguistics, with limited annotated corpora, dialectal dictionaries, or NLP models. This hinders scholarly analysis of Lao literature, philological research, and practical applications in technology. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to train transformer-based language models on a newly compiled corpus of Lao texts spanning classical literature, modern media, and regional dialects. Computational methods will include semi-supervised learning to overcome data sparsity, neural machine translation for cross-dialectal mapping, and graph-based algorithms for syntactic analysis of classical Lao poetry. Additionally, HPC resources will enable large-scale phonetic alignment to trace diachronic shifts in tonal systems and dialect variation. Outcomes will include the first open-source NLP toolkit for Lao, optimized for tasks such as tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and named entity recognition, as well as a dialect classification framework to inform sociolinguistic studies. The resource demands are substantial: preliminary experiments indicate that training a Lao-specific BERT model requires processing over 10 million tokens across diverse genres, with iterative hyperparameter tuning necessitating GPU-accelerated workflows. By enabling these analyses, the project aims to advance Lao literary scholarship, support language preservation efforts, and create infrastructure for applied uses in Lao-speaking communities, such as educational technology and low-resource machine translation.
