Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source platform for simulating surgical wound biomechanics, (2) predictive metrics for complication risks based on simulated stress-perfusion thresholds, and (3) optimization protocols for flap design in reconstruction. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process terabyte-scale datasets and perform parallelized multi-physics simulations, this work aims to advance precision surgery tools that reduce postoperative morbidity. The resource allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated computations, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the development of reduced-order models for clinical translation.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing Computer Numerically Controlled (CNC) machining processes through advanced computational modeling and simulation. CNC machining efficiency is hindered by complex variables such as toolpath optimization, material deformation, thermal dynamics, and real-time error correction, particularly when working with high-strength alloys or intricate geometries. Traditional trial-and-error methods and single-workstation simulations are insufficient for exploring the vast parameter space required to balance precision, speed, and tool longevity. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale simulation framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) models. The computational approach will involve parallelized simulations of cutting forces, heat generation, and material stress distributions across diverse machining scenarios, coupled with ML-driven predictive models trained on synthetic and experimental datasets. These models will identify optimal toolpaths, spindle speeds, and feed rates while predicting tool wear patterns and potential workpiece defects. The HPC environment will enable parameter sweeps across hundreds of concurrent machining configurations, significantly accelerating the discovery of robust operating parameters. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin system capable of reducing machining cycle times by 15-25%, decreasing material waste by up to 30%, and extending tool life through adaptive control strategies. The research will produce open-access datasets of simulated machining operations and a modular software toolkit compatible with industry-standard CAD/CAM platforms. By demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in CNC process optimization, this work aims to bridge the gap between academic CNC curricula and emerging Industry 4.0 practices while supporting advanced manufacturing sectors such as aerospace, automotive, and medical device production.
cip_title: Computer Numerically Controlled (CNC) Machinist Technology/ CNC Machinist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) machine tools, such as lathes, mills, precision measuring tools, and related attachments and accessories, to perform machining functions, such as cutting, drilling, shaping, and finishing products and component parts. Includes instruction in CNC terminology, setup, programming, operations, and troubleshooting; blueprint reading; machining; lathe and mill operations; technical mathematics; computer literacy; CAD/CAM systems; shop and safety practices; equipment capabilities; and regulations and laws.

abstract: Perioperative nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to optimize patient outcomes and surgical efficiency. However, variability in intraoperative workflows, patient responses, and surgical team dynamics presents challenges in standardizing care and predicting complications. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex perioperative environments and develop predictive tools for real-time clinical support. We will integrate multimodal data streams—including electronic health records, real-time vital signs, surgical instrument telemetry, and nurse documentation—to create dynamic simulations of surgical workflows. Machine learning models will be trained on retrospective datasets to identify patterns associated with adverse events (e.g., hypothermia, surgical site infections) and inefficiencies in instrument handling or team communication. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further analyze airflow patterns in operating rooms to optimize sterile field maintenance. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-frequency sensor data and iterative refinement of neural networks to account for rare but critical events. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for early complication detection, evidence-based recommendations for workflow redesign, and interactive training modules for perioperative nurses using synthetic surgical scenarios. By quantifying relationships between nursing interventions and surgical outcomes at scale, this work aims to advance precision in perioperative practice while maintaining focus on the human factors essential to patient-centered care. The requested computing resources will directly support the development of open-source tools adaptable to diverse surgical settings, ultimately contributing to safer, more efficient operating room environments through enhanced nursing decision-support systems.
cip_title: Perioperative/ Operating Room and Surgical Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care to patients before and during surgery, and provide tableside assistance to surgeons. Includes instruction in operating room safety and preparation, aseptic technique, anesthesia, patient preparation, surgical instruments and procedures, sterilization and disinfecting, surgical drugs and solutions, hemostasis, emergency procedures, and patient/family education.

abstract: Emerging viral pathogens in livestock populations present complex challenges to global animal health, driven by rapid genetic evolution and host adaptability. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale genomic datasets hinder the ability to predict virulence shifts and design targeted interventions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular dynamics of bovine respiratory syncytial virus (BRSV) evolution across bovine and porcine hosts, integrating multi-omic data from longitudinal field samples. Computational workflows will employ phylogenetic reconciliation algorithms to model strain divergence, machine learning classifiers to identify host-specific adaptation markers, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize fusion protein conformational changes associated with cross-species transmission. The scale of data—encompassing 15,000+ whole-genome sequences, metatranscriptomic profiles, and terascale molecular simulation outputs—necessitates distributed-memory parallelization and GPU-accelerated architectures. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking genetic variation to clinical outcomes, validated through in vitro infectivity assays. By elucidating evolutionary pathways governing interspecies transmission, this work will directly inform vaccine antigen selection and surveillance protocols for veterinary practitioners. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster will enable the completion of these analyses within an 18-month timeframe, addressing critical gaps in translational veterinary virology. Results will be disseminated through open-access genomic databases and predictive toolkits tailored for veterinary diagnostic laboratories, strengthening capacity to mitigate economically devastating livestock epidemics.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and development necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in predicting drug efficacy, toxicity, and resistance mechanisms. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the design of novel therapeutics targeting chemotherapy-resistant cancers, a critical problem in pharmaceutical sciences. Current experimental methods struggle to capture the dynamic interplay between drug molecules, cellular targets, and resistance-conferring mutations at atomic resolution. To overcome this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-enhanced virtual screening, and quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling. The MD simulations will model protein-ligand interactions for mutated oncogenic targets over microsecond timescales, while ML algorithms will predict binding affinities and off-target effects across large compound libraries. QSAR models will correlate structural features of lead compounds with pharmacokinetic properties to optimize bioavailability and minimize toxicity. The scale of these analyses—requiring petabytes of conformational sampling data and training on millions of molecular descriptors—demands HPC capabilities for parallel processing, GPU-accelerated simulations, and distributed data storage. Expected outcomes include the identification of 3-5 high-priority drug candidates with validated activity against resistant cancer cell lines, predictive models for drug-mutation compatibility, and a publicly accessible database of simulated protein-drug interaction trajectories. This work will advance personalized oncology by enabling rapid adaptation of therapies to evolving tumor genetics while reducing late-stage clinical attrition rates. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as a template for future studies on antimicrobial resistance and neurodegenerative diseases, directly supporting pharmaceutical science education through integration into graduate-level cheminformatics curricula. By bridging atomic-scale biophysics with population-level pharmacological trends, this project addresses a critical gap in modern drug development workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the basic sciences that underlie drugs and drug therapy and that prepares individuals for further study and/or careers in pharmaceutical science and research, pharmaceutical administration and sales, biotechnology, drug manufacturing, regulatory affairs, and related fields. Includes instruction in mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, statistics, pharmaceutics, pharmacology and toxicology, dosage formulation, manufacturing, quality assurance, and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the morphological and syntactic evolution of Hindi and its dialects, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to process large-scale textual corpora spanning pre-modern to contemporary sources. Despite Hindi’s status as a major global language, existing computational tools for its analysis remain limited, particularly in handling dialectal diversity, historical orthographic variations, and non-standardized grammatical structures. The research problem centers on creating scalable models to trace linguistic shifts, identify regional dialect boundaries, and map sociolinguistic influences across time. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques—including transformer-based architectures and probabilistic morphological parsers—with diachronic corpus linguistics. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of digitized texts (e.g., Braj Bhasha and Awadhi manuscripts, modern Hindi literature, and spoken dialect corpora), training neural models to detect phonological, lexical, and syntactic patterns across millions of tokens. Key tasks include automating grapheme-to-phoneme conversion for obsolete scripts, clustering dialect features using graph-based algorithms, and simulating language change through agent-based models. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for Hindi corpus analysis, a diachronic dataset annotating linguistic changes from 1500 CE to the present, and quantitative insights into the impact of urbanization and technology on contemporary Hindi usage. These resources will advance scholarly capacity to study Hindi’s historical development at unprecedented scale, support dialect preservation efforts, and inform NLP applications in under-resourced contexts such as automated transcription of archival materials. The project’s computational demands—including GPU-accelerated model training and large-memory processing of heterogeneous text sources—necessitate HPC infrastructure beyond the capacity of standard university computing systems.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hindi language, antecessors, and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Hindi; Hindustani; related dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Agricultural Teacher Education faces growing demands to integrate data-driven agricultural practices into vocational curricula, yet educators often lack accessible tools to model complex agroecosystems or analyze real-world agricultural datasets in classroom settings. This project seeks to develop a computational platform enabling instructors to simulate crop management scenarios, analyze precision agriculture data, and visualize outcomes for pedagogical use. The research problem centers on bridging the gap between rapidly evolving computational agricultural practices and the technical capacity of vocational educators to teach these concepts effectively. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to construct scalable models of crop growth, soil health dynamics, and climate interactions using machine learning algorithms and agent-based simulations. These models will process heterogeneous datasets—including satellite imagery, sensor networks, and historical yield records—to generate region-specific case studies for instructional design. Computational workflows will optimize parameter space exploration for diverse farming scenarios while maintaining interpretability for non-specialist educators. Expected outcomes include an open-access web interface that allows teachers to adjust simulation parameters, visualize multi-year agricultural outcomes, and export lesson-ready datasets. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform vocational agricultural education by equipping instructors with research-grade computational tools tailored to classroom needs, thereby enhancing student competencies in data-driven decision-making. Successful implementation requires HPC resources to handle concurrent simulations across multiple geographic contexts, high-resolution climate modeling, and training neural networks on agricultural time-series data. This work aligns with national priorities for modernizing agricultural education while explicitly avoiding administrative or general education research foci to maintain alignment with teacher training objectives in technical agriculture.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational agricultural programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the analysis of histopathological and autopsy-derived imaging data, addressing critical bottlenecks in diagnostic accuracy and workflow efficiency for pathology professionals. The increasing volume and complexity of whole-slide imaging (WSI) datasets, combined with the need to correlate morphological features with clinical outcomes, present challenges that exceed the capabilities of traditional manual or semi-automated methods. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep learning models capable of large-scale, high-throughput analysis of WSIs, autopsy records, and associated clinical metadata. The computational approach will involve three phases: (1) preprocessing and segmentation of terabyte-scale imaging data using GPU-accelerated pipelines to isolate regions of diagnostic interest; (2) development of ensemble convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify pathological features across diverse tissue types and staining protocols; and (3) integration of multi-modal data through graph-based neural networks to identify prognostic patterns linking histological findings with patient outcomes. The project will utilize distributed storage systems for managing sensitive clinical data and parallel computing architectures to optimize model training times. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated detection of subtle pathological features in surgical and autopsy specimens, validated against ground-truth annotations from board-certified pathologists. Successful implementation could significantly reduce diagnostic turnaround times, improve detection consistency for rare morphological patterns, and enable predictive modeling of disease progression using legacy case repositories. This work directly supports the educational mission of Pathology/Pathologist Assistant programs by creating scalable computational resources for training students in digital pathology and fostering research collaborations between clinical practitioners and quantitative scientists.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the performance and reliability of alternative fuel vehicle (AFV) systems, with a focus on hybrid-electric powertrains and compressed natural gas (CNG) storage solutions. A critical challenge in AFV technology is balancing energy efficiency, emissions reduction, and system durability under diverse operating conditions. Current diagnostic and design methods rely heavily on empirical testing, which is time-intensive and limited in exploring the full parameter space of multi-fuel systems. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex interactions between mechanical, thermal, and electrical components in AFVs. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model CNG tank stress profiles during rapid refueling cycles, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess hybrid battery pack thermal management under extreme climates. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to predict failure modes in retrofitted AFV electrical systems. The simulations will incorporate real-world driving patterns, fuel mixtures, and aging effects on materials. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to accelerate parameter optimization for conversion kits and generate predictive maintenance frameworks adaptable to varying vehicle platforms. Expected outcomes include validated digital twins of AFV subsystems, open-source simulation tools for technician training programs, and design guidelines for improving the safety of aftermarket conversions. This research will directly support the development of standardized protocols for AFV retrofitting while reducing reliance on physical prototyping. The computational resources will enable scaling to fleet-level analyses, providing actionable insights for policymakers and automotive technicians working toward sustainable transportation infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the maintenance of alternative fuel vehicles and the conversion of standard vehicles to AFV status. Includes instruction in electrical vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles, hybrid fuel technology, electrical and electronic systems, engine performance, diagnosis and repair, and conversion/installation.

abstract: The development of novel pharmaceutical compounds is hindered by the high costs and prolonged timelines associated with traditional drug discovery pipelines, particularly in predicting clinical efficacy, safety, and scalable manufacturability. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the integration of multi-omics data, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning (ML) models for rational drug design and process optimization. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) developing predictive models for drug-target interactions and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) relationships using large-scale genomic, proteomic, and clinical trial datasets, and (2) simulating industrial-scale bioprocess parameters to optimize yield, purity, and stability of candidate therapeutics. Computational workflows will employ molecular docking (AutoDock, GROMACS) and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) to screen compound libraries against disease-specific targets, prioritizing candidates with favorable binding affinities and ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity) profiles. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will model variability in bioreactor conditions, enabling predictive scaling from bench to production. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabytes of heterogeneous data—including electronic health records, high-content screening results, and structural biology databases—while executing computationally intensive tasks such as free-energy perturbation calculations and 3D-QSAR modeling. Expected outcomes include the identification of three lead compounds with enhanced target specificity for Phase I trials, predictive bioprocess templates for monoclonal antibody production, and open-source ML tools for real-time quality control analytics. By reducing late-stage attrition rates and manufacturing bottlenecks, this work aims to lower development costs by an estimated 20–30% for neurodegenerative and oncologic therapeutics while establishing a reproducible computational framework for data-driven drug development. The requested resources will directly support iterative model training, validation against experimental datasets, and virtual population studies to address inter-individual variability in drug response.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific application of pharmacology, pharmaceutics, and industrial management to the development, production, marketing, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. Includes instruction in industrial microbiology, plasmids, expression vectors, protein chemistry, assay and evaluation, drug synthesis and purification, quality control, industrial management, production security, patent procedures, intellectual property regulations and issues, patent enforcement and defense, and research design and testing.

abstract: Prosthodontic rehabilitation requires precise integration of biomechanical principles, material science, and patient-specific anatomies to optimize functional and aesthetic outcomes. However, current methods for designing and evaluating dental prostheses, implants, and occlusal devices rely heavily on static clinical metrics and trial-and-error adjustments, limiting their ability to predict long-term performance under dynamic physiological loads. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to simulate multiscale biomechanical interactions within the masticatory system, including bone-implant interfaces, stress distribution in prostheses, and soft tissue responses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model these complex systems at clinically relevant resolutions, incorporating patient-derived 3D imaging data, heterogeneous material properties, and time-dependent loading conditions representative of mastication, parafunction, and speech. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be employed to assess stress concentrations, fatigue resistance of restorative materials, and fluid flow patterns around implant surfaces. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze large datasets from clinical cohorts to identify predictors of prosthetic failure or complications. The proposed simulations will enable virtual prototyping of patient-specific prosthodontic solutions, reducing iterative physical adjustments and chairside time. Expected outcomes include validated computational models for predicting biomechanical risks in implant-supported prostheses, guidelines for material selection in geriatric and high-load cases, and open-source tools for optimizing occlusal device design in temporomandibular joint dysfunction. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance evidence-based prosthodontics, improve clinical decision-making, and enhance the longevity and patient satisfaction of restorative treatments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the restoration and maintenance of teeth, oral function, and aesthetic form through the use of single or compound materials, structures, and artificial devices. Includes instruction in implant dentistry, surgical procedures, denture design and fabrication, fixed and removable prosthodontics, restorative techniques, occlusion therapy and devices, geriatric dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in analyzing and interpreting complex, large-scale datasets related to theatrical performance dynamics and historical dramatic literature. While traditional theater scholarship has relied on qualitative methods, the growing availability of digitized scripts, performance recordings, and audience response data presents an opportunity to quantitatively investigate patterns in dramatic structure, actor movement, and audience engagement at unprecedented scales. The primary research problem centers on the computational limitations of existing tools, which struggle to process multimodal datasets—such as synchronized text, audio, and motion-tracking data from live performances—while maintaining the temporal and spatial precision required for meaningful analysis. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for script analysis, computer vision techniques for movement pattern recognition in performance videos, and machine learning models to correlate these inputs with audience biometric data (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate). HPC resources are essential for training multimodal neural networks, conducting parallelized simulations of audience sightline variations across virtual theater architectures, and processing high-resolution video archives spanning decades of productions. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for theater researchers to analyze historical performance trends, optimize staging configurations, and model how textual rhetoric intersects with physical choreography to shape viewer attention. By enabling systematic comparisons across cultural contexts and historical periods, this project aims to advance empirical understanding of theatrical efficacy while preserving the interpretive nuance central to the humanities. The requested computing infrastructure will support both the creation of novel methodologies for performance studies and the preservation of fragile digital theater artifacts through large-scale archival analysis.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Drama and Dramatics/ Theatre Arts, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of dramatic works and their performance. Includes instruction in major works of dramatic literature, dramatic styles and types, and the principles of organizing and producing full live or filmed productions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the complex challenge of modeling the interdependent factors influencing cultural heritage preservation, an issue that spans material degradation, environmental conditions, and socio-cultural dynamics. Current research often isolates these elements, limiting holistic insights into sustainable preservation strategies. To bridge this gap, we propose an interdisciplinary computational framework integrating material science datasets, environmental monitoring data, and sociocultural metadata from heritage sites. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-agent simulations that model interactions between environmental stressors (e.g., temperature fluctuations, pollution) and human-driven variables (e.g., community engagement, funding cycles). Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze historical preservation outcomes across diverse geographic and cultural contexts to identify patterns and predictors of success. The scale of these datasets—spanning tera bytes of high-resolution environmental readings, 3D scans of artifacts, and decades of ethnographic records—necessitates parallelized processing and large memory allocation, which are only feasible with HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models to prioritize at-risk sites, dynamic visualizations of preservation scenarios, and a publicly accessible database linking material decay rates to socio-environmental variables. This work will advance methodologies in digital humanities by demonstrating how computational scalability can address inherently interdisciplinary problems. Results will provide cultural institutions with evidence-based tools to allocate resources effectively while contributing to academic discourse on integrating computational rigor with qualitative cultural research. The project underscores the role of general studies in fostering innovation through the synthesis of arts, science, and technology.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated program that includes instruction in the general arts, general science, or unstructured studies.

abstract: Global food security is increasingly threatened by climate variability, population growth, and geopolitical disruptions, necessitating advanced predictive tools to optimize agricultural systems across diverse regions. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating climate, crop, and economic models to evaluate adaptive strategies for sustainable food production under dynamic global conditions. The research focuses on three staple crops—maize, rice, and wheat—which collectively account for over 40% of global caloric intake. Current limitations in existing models include coarse spatial resolution, inadequate representation of agroecological feedbacks, and insufficient scalability to assess multi-country trade dependencies. To address these gaps, we propose a multi-model ensemble approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate biophysical processes (e.g., crop phenology, soil-water dynamics) and socioeconomic factors (e.g., supply chain resilience, policy impacts) at 1-km resolution across 15 climate-vulnerable countries. Machine learning algorithms will assimilate satellite-derived vegetation indices, soil moisture datasets, and historical yield records to calibrate model parameters. Computational workflows will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in yield projections under IPCC climate scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5), while agent-based modeling will evaluate farmer decision-making in response to market and environmental shocks. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabyte-scale geospatial inputs, executing 10^4+ parallelized model runs, and reducing runtime from months to days. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision support tool for policymakers, identification of region-specific crop diversification strategies, and quantification of trade policy impacts on cross-border food availability. By bridging agronomic and computational sciences, this work aims to provide actionable insights for enhancing the resilience of international agricultural systems in the face of 21st-century challenges.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of agricultural management and scientific principles to the problems of global food production and distribution, and to the study of the agricultural systems of other countries. Includes instruction in agricultural economics; comparative agricultural systems; international agribusiness and law; third-world development studies and economic development; and global applications of climate, soil, water resources, ecological and environmental studies, and animal and plant sciences.

abstract: The growing complexity of long-term care (LTC) administration—driven by aging populations, evolving regulatory requirements, and heterogeneous patient needs—demands advanced computational tools to optimize operational decision-making and care delivery. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to support LTC facility administrators in balancing clinical, financial, and regulatory priorities. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven tools capable of integrating real-time patient health metrics, staffing patterns, reimbursement policies, and facility-level financial data to simulate outcomes under dynamic conditions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate machine learning models that forecast patient health trajectories, staffing shortages, and budget impacts across multi-year horizons. These models will synthesize anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), workforce scheduling datasets, and federal/state reimbursement policies into an agent-based simulation platform. Computational workflows will prioritize parallelized parameter optimization for scenario testing, including the effects of staffing ratios, occupancy rates, and intervention timing on care quality metrics (e.g., hospital readmissions, falls) and operational sustainability. Sensitivity analyses will quantify trade-offs between cost containment strategies and compliance risks. By enabling large-scale simulations of facility operations under diverse regulatory and demographic assumptions, this project aims to generate actionable insights for LTC administrators, policymakers, and accreditation bodies. Expected outcomes include open-source decision-support tools for resource allocation, evidence-based recommendations for staffing models, and a computational pipeline adaptable to emerging LTC challenges such as pandemic response planning or value-based payment transitions. The scalability of these methods—enabled by HPC infrastructure—will support broader applications in gerontological research and health systems management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of nursing homes, assisted living facilities, adult day care, home health services, and other long term care settings and agencies serving the elderly and disabled. Includes instruction in social and clinical aspects of aging, health care delivery systems, nursing home administration, assisted living administration, aging policy and government programs, ethics, business management, financial management, human resource management, marketing, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying somatic bodywork therapies using high-performance computing (HPC) to model tissue-level and systemic responses to manual therapeutic interventions. Despite widespread clinical use of modalities such as myofascial release, craniosacral therapy, and neuromuscular re-education, the biophysical basis for their therapeutic effects remains poorly quantified. Current research relies heavily on empirical observations, lacking robust computational frameworks to predict how specific techniques interact with complex tissue networks or influence proprioceptive feedback loops. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models integrating finite element analysis of soft tissue deformation, agent-based simulations of interstitial fluid dynamics, and machine learning-driven analysis of autonomic nervous system responses derived from wearable biosensor data. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of high-resolution MRI-derived anatomical datasets, real-time optimization of hyperelastic material properties in heterogeneous fascial networks, and training of neural networks to correlate therapeutic pressure parameters with physiological outcomes (e.g., heart rate variability, regional oxygenation). The computational pipeline will be validated against motion capture and ultrasound elastography data collected during controlled manual therapy sessions. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for optimizing force vectors and treatment durations in somatic interventions, identification of mechanotransduction pathways linking manual input to systemic relaxation responses, and a novel framework for personalizing bodywork protocols based on individual connective tissue topology. This work will establish a computational foundation for evidence-based practice in somatic therapies while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies at the intersection of biomechanics, systems biology, and manual medicine.
cip_title: Somatic Bodywork and Related Therapeutic Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in somatic bodywork and related therapeutic services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research addresses critical gaps in understanding the mechanisms by which environmental and synthetic toxins disrupt organ-specific physiological functions, particularly in the liver and kidney, which are central to toxin metabolism and excretion. Current experimental models struggle to integrate multi-scale data—from molecular interactions to tissue-level dysfunction—limiting predictive capabilities for toxin-induced pathologies. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-compartment, physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK) model that dynamically simulates toxin transport, metabolic activation, and cellular injury across heterogeneous tissue environments. The computational framework will integrate spatially resolved cellular automata models to simulate toxin diffusion and advection in hepatic and renal tissues, coupled with ordinary differential equation systems modeling intracellular metabolic networks (e.g., cytochrome P450-mediated bioactivation) and subsequent oxidative stress pathways. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of parenchymal and non-parenchymal cell populations to capture emergent tissue damage patterns, including necrosis, fibrosis, and inflammatory cascades. Model parameterization will utilize existing in vivo toxicity datasets and in vitro organ-on-a-chip experiments, with Bayesian inference methods applied via Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling to resolve parameter uncertainties. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize stochastic simulations, and achieve biologically relevant temporal resolutions (millisecond-scale events over hours of simulated time). Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify tissue-specific vulnerability to emerging toxins (e.g., per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) and identify molecular targets for antidote development. This work directly aligns with the Toxicology program’s focus on counteracting biohazards by enabling rapid, cost-effective prioritization of toxins for regulatory review and mechanistic hypothesis generation for experimental validation. The requested resources will support 20,000 core-hours per month for model calibration, sensitivity analyses, and large-scale virtual screening of toxin interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of poisons and other biohazards; their interactions with organisms and their food and respiratory systems; and their prevention, management, and counteraction. Includes instruction in toxicological biochemistry, toxic agents and transporters, toxin fate, toxicokinetics and metabolism, toxin classification, molecular toxic mechanisms, extracellular matrices and cell function, bacterial pathogenesis and mutagenesis, pathophysiology and apoptosis, cell stress and injury, studies of specific toxins, and studies of specific organ systems and physiological functions in relation to toxicological problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Romanian linguistics through large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary text corpora. The primary research problem centers on tracing the evolution of Romanian dialects and identifying understudied syntactic and morphological patterns that distinguish regional variations. Despite Romania’s rich linguistic diversity, comprehensive studies of dialectal divergence remain limited due to the manual effort required to process heterogeneous sources, including 19th-century manuscripts, regional periodicals, and modern digital texts. This project proposes an automated pipeline combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques, machine learning models, and philological annotation to analyze lexical, grammatical, and stylistic features across a curated corpus of over 100,000 text samples. Computational tasks include training transformer-based models for diachronic language modeling, clustering dialect-specific lexemes, and mapping syntactic shifts influenced by contact languages such as Hungarian and Slavic varieties. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution OCR outputs of historical documents, parallelizing feature extraction across multi-genre texts, and optimizing memory-intensive tasks like training custom embedding layers for low-resource dialectal data. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated Romanian texts spanning 1800–2020, (2) quantitative frameworks for dialect classification, and (3) insights into how technological and sociopolitical changes have shaped regional linguistic identities. By bridging computational methods with traditional philology, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying non-dominant languages in NLP contexts while preserving endangered dialectal features. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impossible on local infrastructure, reducing model training times by 80% and supporting the first large-scale comparative analysis of Romanian’s dialect continuum.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Romanian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the emerging field of computational consumer neuroscience, an interdisciplinary niche integrating marketing, cognitive science, and artificial intelligence. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how consumers process multimodal digital stimuli (e.g., augmented reality ads, dynamic pricing interfaces) at scale, particularly in real-world, high-velocity decision-making contexts. Traditional neuroimaging methods, such as fMRI or EEG, struggle to model the combinatorial effects of rapidly evolving visual, auditory, and contextual inputs in digital marketplaces. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining deep neural networks, agent-based modeling, and psychophysiological data assimilation. The project will process terabyte-scale datasets spanning fMRI recordings, eye-tracking metrics, and real-time consumer interaction logs from e-commerce platforms to train multimodal transformer architectures. These models will simulate neural and behavioral responses to dynamic marketing stimuli under varying cognitive load conditions. A key innovation involves parallelized reinforcement learning agents that emulate heterogeneous decision-making strategies observed across cultural and demographic cohorts. The HPC infrastructure is essential for three phases: (1) large-scale pretraining of vision-language models on marketing-relevant stimuli, (2) distributed hyperparameter optimization for personalized neuromorphic response prediction, and (3) real-time simulation of marketplace dynamics through GPU-accelerated agent swarms. Expected outcomes include a novel computational taxonomy of digital consumer engagement patterns and an open-source framework for ethical AI-driven neuromarketing design. This work will provide foundational insights into the neurocomputational principles governing 21st-century consumer behavior while establishing methodological benchmarks for responsible use of machine learning in market research. The resource-intensive nature of modeling brain-behavior-environment interactions at population scale necessitates the requested computing capabilities to achieve statistically robust and commercially actionable results.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general marketing and marketing research, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision in radiation dose optimization for computed tomography (CT) imaging through the development of patient-specific, anatomy-aware exposure protocols. While modern CT systems employ automated exposure control, these tools rely on generalized patient models and lack the resolution to account for fine-scale variations in tissue composition, organ geometry, or pathological anomalies. This gap poses risks of overexposure in vulnerable populations—particularly pediatric and oncologic patients—and undermines image quality in complex anatomical regions. We propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations with deep learning-based organ segmentation to generate dynamic, adaptive exposure parameters tailored to individual patient anatomy. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train 3D convolutional neural networks on a curated dataset of 15,000 anonymized pediatric and adult CT studies, with voxel-level annotations for 27 tissue types. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations (Geant4-based) will model photon interactions across 10^6 unique anatomical configurations, incorporating variable beam energies, collimation strategies, and iterative reconstruction algorithms. Computational outputs will be validated against physical phantom measurements and clinical image quality assessments conducted by certified radiographers. Anticipated outcomes include a deployable software module for real-time exposure adaptation and an open-access dataset correlating simulated dose distributions with patient-specific image noise metrics. This work bridges radiologic science, computational physics, and machine learning to address a critical need in medical imaging: minimizing ionizing radiation risks while preserving diagnostic fidelity. Successful implementation could reduce effective dose variability by 30-50% in heterogeneous patient populations, directly enhancing safety protocols in radiologic practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical imaging services to patients and attending health care professionals. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, patient positioning, radiographic technique, radiation biology, safety and emergency procedures, equipment operation and maintenance, quality assurance, patient education, and medical imaging/radiologic services management.

abstract: The increasing demand for scalable telemedicine solutions necessitates robust computational frameworks capable of integrating multi-modal clinical data, enabling real-time decision-making, and addressing disparities in healthcare access. Current telemedicine platforms often struggle to efficiently process large-scale datasets—including high-resolution medical imaging, continuous vital sign monitoring from wearables, and electronic health records (EHRs)—while maintaining clinical accuracy and low latency. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that enhance diagnostic precision, personalize treatment recommendations, and optimize resource allocation in telemedicine workflows. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating federated learning pipelines to train machine learning models on distributed, privacy-sensitive EHR and imaging datasets without centralized data aggregation; (2) implementing real-time predictive analytics for early detection of clinical deterioration in remote patient monitoring; and (3) simulating large-scale virtual patient cohorts to evaluate telemedicine protocols under diverse demographic and infrastructural constraints. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated deep learning for medical image analysis, parallelized agent-based modeling for care pathway simulations, and graph neural networks to model patient-provider interaction patterns. The HPC environment is critical for managing the project’s petabyte-scale datasets, reducing model training times from weeks to days, and enabling complex multi-institutional data governance structures. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithmic frameworks for privacy-preserving federated learning in clinical settings, validated prediction tools for remote patient triage, and evidence-based guidelines for telemedicine deployment in resource-limited regions. By addressing both technical and equity-focused challenges, this work aims to establish computational best practices for next-generation telemedicine systems, ultimately improving care quality while reducing geographic and socioeconomic barriers to medical access.
cip_definition: Research on how to bring together technology and clinical medicine to enhance the overall delivery of medical care.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the historical and cultural interconnectedness of Ural-Altaic and Central Asian societies through large-scale linguistic and textual analysis. The research problem centers on deciphering patterns of cultural exchange and linguistic evolution across the Silk Road and adjacent regions, where fragmented historical records and the diversity of languages (e.g., Turkic, Mongolic, Tungusic) pose significant challenges to manual analysis. Current scholarship lacks a systematic, data-driven approach to map the diffusion of oral traditions, religious texts, and administrative lexicons across these regions, particularly before the 15th century. To address this gap, the project will employ computational methods, including natural language processing (NLP) tailored for low-resource languages, phylogenetic modeling of language divergence, and network analysis of textual corpora drawn from digitized manuscripts, epigraphic materials, and ethnographic recordings. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual datasets (estimated at 50+ TB), training transformer-based models on historical language variants, and simulating contact scenarios across temporal and spatial scales. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access database of annotated texts and linguistic features, (2) dynamic visualizations of cultural-linguistic networks highlighting key hubs of exchange, and (3) probabilistic models identifying understudied pathways of influence between nomadic and sedentary communities. By integrating computational rigor with area studies expertise, this work aims to redefine narratives of cultural transmission in Inner Asia while providing methodological frameworks for analyzing non-Latin script historical sources. The requested resources will enable the processing of heterogeneous data types (OCR outputs, XML-TEI encoded texts, geospatial coordinates) at scales unachievable with standard workstations, directly supporting the program’s mission to illuminate Central Asia’s complex heritage through innovative interdisciplinary research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries of Inner/Central Asia, including the Turkic and Mongolian inhabitants of the Caspian, Amur, Tien Shan, Baikal, Gobi, Siberian, and Manchurian areas and the historical Silk Road, in terms of their past and present development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Chinese dialectology and historical linguistics, addressing critical gaps in the analysis of linguistic variation and evolution across time and space. The research problem centers on the computational modeling of phonological and syntactic shifts in understudied Sinitic languages, particularly Min and Wu dialects, which exhibit complex divergence from Middle Chinese. Existing studies rely on manual corpus analysis or limited computational tools, hindering scalable comparisons of lexical, phonetic, and grammatical patterns across centuries of textual and spoken records. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a hybrid computational workflow integrating dialectal corpus preprocessing, neural sequence modeling, and phylogenetic algorithms. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on annotated corpora of pre-modern and contemporary texts (e.g., vernacular literature, transcribed oral histories) to detect cross-dialectal correspondences, followed by Bayesian phylogenetic inference to reconstruct ancestral linguistic features. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of multi-terabyte text datasets, optimizing hyperparameters for dialect-specific language models, and running computationally intensive simulations of language diversification pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for diachronic dialect comparison, (2) open-access repositories of computationally tagged linguistic features for Min and Wu variants, and (3) quantitative evidence refining theories of language contact and divergence in eastern China. By enabling large-scale, data-driven analysis of non-standardized Sinitic varieties, this work will support interdisciplinary scholarship in digital humanities, language preservation, and sociolinguistics while providing methodological templates for computational research on other under-resourced languages. The requested resources will directly address current bottlenecks in processing efficiency, model training times, and simulation fidelity, ensuring robust results with implications for both academic research and community-driven language revitalization efforts.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of China and associated dialects and literature. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize the design of adaptive educational tools for students with visual impairments (VI). While individualized education plans (IEPs) are critical for this population, educators face challenges in efficiently integrating real-time student performance data with evidence-based strategies to adjust tactile, auditory, or multimodal learning interfaces. Current tools lack dynamic personalization at scale, relying on static heuristics that do not account for the diverse sensory, cognitive, and developmental profiles of learners with VI. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning framework that simulates learner interactions with assistive technologies and generates actionable recommendations for instructional adaptation. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning models on longitudinal datasets of student engagement metrics (e.g., haptic response times, audio interface usage patterns, and task accuracy) alongside teacher intervention logs. Computational experiments will simulate diverse VI learner profiles under varying educational scenarios to identify optimal intervention pathways. Key technical challenges include managing high-dimensional spatiotemporal data from sensory interfaces and ensuring low-latency model inference for real-world classroom deployment. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for generating IEP components informed by predictive analytics, as well as a novel VI learner simulation platform to enhance teacher training. By enabling data-driven personalization of sensory-rich learning environments, this work aims to reduce educators’ operational burdens while improving accessibility outcomes. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing multimodal datasets at scale, conducting parallelized hyperparameter optimization for domain-specific neural architectures, and validating models against synthetic cohorts representing the full spectrum of visual impairments and comorbidities.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Vision Impairments Including Blindness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with visual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with visual impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising blind or visually handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision skincare protocols by integrating computational modeling with dermatological and aesthetic practice. Despite advancements in cosmetic science, estheticians lack robust tools to predict individualized skin responses to multifactorial treatments—such as combined chemical exfoliants, light therapy, or topical biologics—in dynamic environmental conditions. Current protocols rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for genetic variability, microbiome interactions, or real-time shifts in skin barrier function. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates skin behavior at the microphysiological level, combining finite element analysis (FEA) for biomechanical stress modeling, agent-based simulations for microbial community dynamics, and machine learning (ML) to correlate treatment combinations with clinical outcomes. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of diverse skin phenotypes under thousands of treatment-environment scenarios, iteratively trained on a multimodal dataset comprising 3D facial scans, genomic data, and longitudinal client records from partnered spas. Key challenges include optimizing fluid-structure interaction models for epidermal hydration kinetics and resolving stochastic noise in microbiome datasets. Outcomes will include a validated predictive tool to recommend personalized treatment sequences, reducing adverse reactions and improving efficacy in acne, rosacea, and aging-related concerns. Additionally, the project will generate open-access benchmarks for computational esthetics, fostering collaboration between beauty professionals and quantitative researchers. By bridging empirical practice with computational rigor, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based skincare, with implications for licensing standards, product development, and client safety in the rapidly growing wellness industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cleanse, depilate, massage, and beautify the human body and to function as licensed estheticians and skin care specialists.  Includes instruction in skin anatomy, physiology, and health; principles of nutrition; decontamination and infection control; health and safety; facial and body massage; body wrapping and spa treatments; temporary hair removal including waxing and tweezing; color and skin analysis; client consultation and care; applicable laws and regulations; business practices; and sometimes related alternative healing regimens.

abstract: The development of investigational drugs requires rigorous evaluation of efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) profiles to advance candidates into clinical trials. A critical challenge lies in predicting patient-specific responses to novel therapeutics, particularly in heterogeneous populations with complex comorbidities or genetic variations. Traditional trial-and-error approaches remain resource-intensive and prone to high attrition rates, underscoring the need for advanced computational models to optimize drug selection and trial design. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale, patient-derived models that integrate genomic, proteomic, and clinical data to simulate drug behavior across virtual cohorts. The computational framework will employ molecular dynamics simulations to characterize drug-target binding affinities, machine learning algorithms to predict off-target effects and toxicity risks, and population PK/PD modeling to quantify inter-individual variability in drug exposure and response. Large-scale genomic datasets from public repositories (e.g., UK Biobank, TCGA) and proprietary clinical trial data will be processed to identify biomarkers of therapeutic response and adverse events. Parallelized workflows will enable the simultaneous evaluation of thousands of drug-candidate combinations under diverse physiological scenarios, while Bayesian optimization techniques will prioritize compounds with the highest likelihood of clinical success. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for dose optimization, patient stratification strategies, and mechanistic insights into drug resistance pathways. By reducing reliance on costly late-stage trial failures, this work aims to accelerate the translation of investigational drugs into clinically viable therapies. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational demands of iterative model training, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the integration of high-dimensional omics data. Successful implementation will provide a scalable platform for precision medicine applications, directly supporting the development of safer, more effective therapeutics for complex diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on Investigational Drugs and Research

abstract: The emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens underscores the urgent need to elucidate molecular mechanisms of immune evasion and microbial pathogenesis. This project seeks to investigate how surface-exposed virulence factors of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium tuberculosis interact with host immune components to subvert adaptive and innate defenses. A critical gap lies in understanding the structural dynamics of these interactions at atomic resolution, particularly under conditions mimicking host microenvironments. To address this, we propose large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the conformational behavior of microbial adhesins (e.g., S. aureus protein A, M. tuberculosis ESX-1 secretion system effectors) when bound to host targets such as immunoglobulin Fc regions, complement proteins, and T-cell receptors. Simulations will integrate cryo-EM and crystallographic data from collaborator labs to refine binding interfaces and predict allosteric regulatory sites. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve millisecond-scale sampling of these 500,000–1,000,000-atom systems under varying pH, ionic strength, and oxidative stress conditions. Parallel tempering and enhanced sampling algorithms will be employed to map free-energy landscapes of pathogen-host complexes, identifying transient states that may represent therapeutic intervention points. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into how post-translational modifications of microbial proteins alter immune receptor engagement and (2) predictive models of strain-specific adaptive mutations affecting host tropism. This work directly addresses NIH priorities on antimicrobial resistance by revealing novel targets for immunotherapeutics or vaccines. The requested resources will enable simulations across 50+ pathogen-host systems, generating >100 TB of trajectory data for comparative analysis. By bridging structural microbiology with computational biophysics, this project will advance our understanding of host-pathogen interface plasticity while developing scalable workflows for simulating complex immunological interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microorganisms that cause disease and the host immune response to them. Includes instruction in microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, pathogenic bacteriology, disease mechanisms, immunology, immunogenetics, autoimmunity, and bioinformatics.

abstract: Directed energy systems (DES) represent a transformative capability in modern defense infrastructure, yet their operational efficacy is constrained by complex, dynamic interactions between high-energy lasers, atmospheric conditions, and target materials. Current modeling frameworks lack the resolution to account for multi-physics phenomena—such as turbulence-induced beam degradation, thermal blooming, and nonlinear optical effects—in real-world operational environments. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, scalable computational model to simulate and optimize directed energy weapon (DEW) performance under diverse atmospheric and adversarial conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate adaptive optics, computational fluid dynamics, and quantum-mechanical photon-matter interaction models into a unified simulation framework. Key objectives include quantifying the impact of aerosol dispersion, humidity gradients, and countermeasure-induced scattering on beam coherence, as well as identifying material-specific vulnerabilities to pulsed laser irradiation. The computational approach employs a hybrid architecture, combining GPU-accelerated finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for electromagnetic simulations with machine learning-driven surrogate models to reduce computational costs in multi-parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for DEW system calibration in contested environments, validated against experimental data from military test ranges. This work will directly inform next-generation DES design, enabling rapid scenario analysis for mission planning and enhancing the reliability of energy deposition metrics. By addressing critical gaps in multi-scale, real-time DES modeling, the project advances the operational readiness of directed energy platforms while establishing a computational foundation for adaptive countermeasure development. The resulting frameworks will be disseminated through secure defense research channels, contributing to strategic technological superiority in high-stakes engagement scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of lasers and other directed energy phenomena and their application to the creation of energy beam weapons systems. Includes instruction in photonics, electro-optics, microwave phenomena, laser chemistry, spectroscopy, chemical lasers, fibre lasers, imaging and optics, laser propagation and control, laser communication, infrared remote sensing, modeling and simulation, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in mathematical logic by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address open problems in model theory and recursion theory. The core research problem involves analyzing the computational complexity of constructing and classifying models of axiomatic systems, particularly those with non-arithmetical properties or unconventional recursion-theoretic features. A key focus is on determining the resource thresholds—such as time, memory, and parallelism—required to algorithmically verify the consistency of theories with uncountable models or to resolve the decidability of index sets in the hyperarithmetical hierarchy. To achieve this, we propose a hybrid computational methodology combining symbolic computation, automated theorem-proving frameworks, and custom algorithms for exploring large solution spaces. This includes the implementation of parallelized satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solvers to test model existence under varying cardinality constraints, as well as Monte Carlo tree search techniques to identify critical patterns in recursively enumerable structures. The computational workload necessitates distributed-memory architectures due to the exponential scaling of combinatorial possibilities in model construction and the need to simulate non-well-founded set-theoretic universes. Expected outcomes include new insights into the limits of effective model theory, refined complexity classifications for recursion-theoretic problems, and publicly accessible datasets cataloging isomorphism types of minimal models. By bridging abstract logical frameworks with scalable computational tools, this work aims to resolve conjectures in reverse mathematics and illuminate the interplay between axiomatic independence and computational feasibility. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory bottlenecks in handling large-scale combinatorial objects and to enable the iterative refinement of proof strategies through high-throughput experimentation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study foundations of mathematics, including model theory, recursion theory and set theory.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized facial treatment protocols by integrating biometric data analysis, predictive modeling, and real-time simulation of skin response dynamics. The research addresses a critical gap in the esthetics industry: the lack of data-driven, reproducible methods to predict how individual skin characteristics interact with treatment variables such as product formulations, massage techniques, and environmental factors. Current practice relies heavily on subjective assessment and generalized protocols, which can lead to inconsistent outcomes and inefficiencies in client care. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets, including hyperspectral imaging of skin microtexture, longitudinal moisture retention metrics, and client-specific genetic predispositions to sensitivity or dehydration. A machine learning pipeline will be developed to classify skin types and predict treatment responses across diverse demographic cohorts. Concurrently, finite element modeling will simulate the biomechanical effects of manual manipulation techniques (e.g., lymphatic drainage, myofascial release) on subcutaneous tissue, while agent-based models will map the diffusion kinetics of topical compounds through stratum corneum layers under varying pH and humidity conditions. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies treatment efficacy probabilities, identifies risk thresholds for adverse reactions, and generates adaptive treatment sequences based on real-time sensor feedback. This work bridges computational biosystems modeling with practical esthetic practice, offering a novel paradigm for evidence-based personalization in facial therapies. The computational intensity of processing high-resolution 3D skin maps, running parallelized simulations of biochemical interactions, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory architectures. Successful implementation could establish new standards for precision in non-medical skincare interventions while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in vocational health-adjacent fields traditionally underserved by advanced computational research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and scalp with chemical and cosmetic preparations, and to function as licensed facial specialists in specialized and full service salons.  Includes instruction in facial surface anatomy; skin properties; skin decontamination and infection control; facial massage; facial makeup; facial wrapping; selection and application of creams, lotions, oils, and other chemicals and cosmetics; European and other facial techniques; client evaluation and care; applicable laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Thai linguistics, focusing on the analysis of syntactic and morphological patterns in historical and contemporary Thai texts. While Thai language studies have traditionally relied on manual textual analysis, the increasing availability of digitized corpora—spanning classical literature, legal documents, and modern social media—presents an opportunity to apply scalable computational methods. The primary challenge lies in processing these heterogeneous datasets, which include non-standardized orthography, dialectal variations, and code-switching, all of which complicate automated analysis. This research aims to develop and refine natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to Thai, utilizing transformer-based models and rule-based systems to classify syntactic structures, trace linguistic evolution, and map regional dialect features. Key tasks include training domain-specific language models on curated corpora, implementing parallelized algorithms for comparative analysis of text genres, and simulating language change via agent-based models. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the need for large-scale tokenization, distributed training of deep learning models, and probabilistic simulations—necessitates access to HPC resources for efficient processing. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of annotated Thai texts, computational tools for dialect classification, and quantitative insights into how sociohistorical factors have shaped grammatical norms in Thai. These resources will support interdisciplinary applications, from improving machine translation for low-resource Thai dialects to informing language preservation policies. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this project bridges a methodological gap in Thai linguistics and establishes a framework for data-driven humanities research in Southeast Asian studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Thai languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize clinical decision support for complex patient populations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets. Clinical Nurse Leaders (CNLs) require real-time, evidence-based tools to guide care coordination and risk stratification in dynamic healthcare environments. However, existing models often lack the computational capacity to integrate multi-modal data (e.g., vital signs, medication histories, genomic markers) or account for temporal patterns in patient trajectories. This limitation hinders personalized interventions for patients with comorbidities, chronic conditions, or acute decompensation risks. To address this, we propose a hybrid machine learning approach combining recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to model longitudinal EHR data and graph neural networks (GNNs) to map patient-provider interaction networks. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets from three regional health systems, spanning 250,000+ patient encounters. Computational workflows will include data preprocessing (imputation, normalization), feature extraction, and model training across multiple GPU nodes. Validation will assess predictive accuracy for 30-day readmission, sepsis onset, and medication adherence outcomes. Results will be compared to traditional regression-based tools used in current CNL workflows. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source predictive toolkit tailored to CNL priorities, such as identifying high-risk patients for proactive care escalation or simulating the impact of staffing ratios on care quality. This work directly supports the CNL role in translating data-driven insights into bedside practice while advancing computational nursing science. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive workloads, reducing model training times from weeks to days, and ensuring scalability to diverse healthcare settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses for careers as clinical nurse leaders in which they work as part of an interdisciplinary team that provides direct medical care for patients based on evidence-based practice and research. Includes instruction in pharmacology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, research in nursing methods, advanced health assessment, statistics, and clinical practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing the performance and longevity of modern diesel engines, which face increasing demands for efficiency, reduced emissions, and operational reliability. Current diagnostic and predictive modeling approaches in diesel mechanics often rely on simplified simulations or empirical data, limiting their ability to capture the complex, dynamic interactions within engine systems—particularly under extreme loads or variable fuel compositions.
