To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate combustion dynamics, exhaust aftertreatment systems, and mechanical wear in diesel engines. These models will integrate multiphysics frameworks, including computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion chamber analysis, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress prediction in engine components, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to correlate sensor data with failure modes. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate engine performance across diverse operating conditions, fuel blends, and emission control strategies. Key outcomes will include predictive tools for identifying optimal maintenance intervals, mitigating premature component failure, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions through real-time adaptive tuning. By bridging advanced computational methods with applied diesel technology, this work aims to provide actionable insights for industry partners while enhancing the precision of technician training programs. The project will also establish a scalable computational workflow adaptable to emerging engine technologies, such as hybrid diesel-electric systems and alternative fuel compatibility studies. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the necessary resolution in spatial and temporal simulations, which would otherwise be computationally infeasible on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain diesel engines in vehicles such as automobiles, buses, ships, trucks, railroad locomotives, and construction equipment; as well as stationary diesel engines in electrical generators and related equipment.

abstract: The study of dynamic crustal processes and their role in shaping geological hazards requires high-resolution modeling of complex, multi-physics interactions across spatial and temporal scales. This project seeks to advance understanding of fault zone evolution and seismic cycle dynamics through large-scale numerical simulations of lithospheric deformation. The research addresses a critical gap in current models, which often oversimplify the coupling between thermal, mechanical, and fluid-mediated processes in active fault systems. We propose to develop 3D finite element models integrating visco-elasto-plastic rheologies, heat transfer, and pore fluid pressure effects using the open-source code ASPECT, augmented with custom constitutive relationships for fault friction. These simulations will resolve meter- to kilometer-scale heterogeneities across domains spanning hundreds of kilometers, requiring petascale computing resources to manage the nonlinear system solutions and adaptive mesh refinement. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for matrix assembly and hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization for efficient memory distribution. Initial benchmarks on regional-scale models (10^8 degrees of freedom) demonstrate strong scaling up to 2048 cores, with proposed production runs targeting 5x larger domains. Outputs will be validated against geodetic strain rates, exhumed fault rock microstructures, and seismic catalogs from the San Andreas Fault System and Himalayan frontal thrusts. Expected outcomes include quantitative constraints on how transient fluid pressures influence earthquake nucleation patterns and long-term fault geometry development. The generated datasets will be made available through a community portal, enabling comparative studies across tectonic settings. By bridging computational geodynamics and field observations, this work will provide new frameworks for assessing seismic hazards in active continental margins while advancing parallel algorithms for geomechanical simulations. Successful implementation requires sustained access to high-performance computing infrastructure with large memory nodes and fast interconnects to achieve the necessary resolution for capturing multi-scale fault processes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and relationships between the solids, liquids and gases comprising it.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interactions between household financial decision-making, systemic economic stressors, and public resource accessibility—a critical gap in Family Resource Management Studies. Current approaches often rely on static survey data or simplified economic assumptions, limiting their capacity to simulate cascading effects of financial shocks (e.g., job loss, medical emergencies) across diverse household archetypes. We propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) system leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate 10,000+ heterogeneous household agents operating under adaptive budget allocation strategies. Each agent will integrate stochastic income streams, debt instruments, savings behaviors, and eligibility thresholds for public assistance programs, with parameters derived from anonymized national household economic surveys. The computational model will implement parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate how localized policy interventions (e.g., emergency savings matching programs) affect long-term financial resilience across demographic strata. A novel machine learning layer will iteratively calibrate agent decision trees using historical crisis recovery data, requiring GPU-accelerated training cycles. By simulating multi-year timelines across synthetic populations, this approach addresses the temporal and interactive complexities that traditional regression analyses cannot capture. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for simulating household financial ecosystems, quantitative evidence on policy designs that mitigate wealth stratification during economic disruptions, and behavioral insights into how information access inequalities compound financial fragility. This work establishes a computational foundation for evidence-based family resource management strategies while advancing methodological integration of HPC-scale simulations into consumer economics research.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and implementation of policies and processes contributing to successful individual and family resource management. Includes instruction in financial goal-setting and strategies; household income, assets, and debt management; preventing and resolving financial difficulties; and the use of relevant public resources.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced control frameworks for autonomous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments, a core challenge in mechatronics and automation engineering. Current limitations in real-time sensor fusion, adaptive decision-making, and multi-objective optimization hinder the deployment of robust robotic systems for applications such as precision manufacturing, agile logistics, and human-robot collaboration. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale simulations of complex electro-mechanical systems, coupled with machine learning-driven control strategies. Computational models will integrate multi-body dynamics, vision-based perception networks, and distributed sensor-actuator systems using parallelized finite element analysis and digital twin frameworks. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to optimize control policies for hybrid systems involving both discrete event-driven tasks and continuous motion planning. Key outcomes include validated control architectures for redundant manipulators and mobile robot fleets, with emphasis on fault tolerance and energy efficiency. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of system prototypes through hardware-in-the-loop testing, reducing development cycles for industrial partners. This work directly supports curriculum development in embedded robotics by generating case studies on computational constraints in real-time systems. By bridging simulation-to-deployment gaps in multi-agent automation, the project aims to advance scalable solutions for small-to-medium enterprises adopting Industry 4.0 technologies. Resource allocation will specifically target GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory nodes for virtual prototyping of complex mechatronic assemblies.
cip_title: Mechatronics, Robotics, and Automation Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in the support of engineers to the design, development, and operational evaluation of autonomous, computer-controlled, electro-mechanical systems. Includes instruction in computer and software engineering, control engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and robotics.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex foot pathologies, such as Charcot neuroarthropathy and progressive adult-acquired flatfoot deformity, presents significant challenges in predicting optimal surgical and orthotic interventions. Current biomechanical models lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between soft tissue remodeling, bone stress redistribution, and altered gait patterns in three dimensions. This project proposes to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with machine learning to simulate foot biomechanics at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallel processing of patient-specific MRI-derived anatomical models (0.1 mm isotropic voxels) coupled with real-world inertial measurement unit (IMU) gait data from 500 podiatric patients. The computational pipeline will employ GPU-accelerated solvers to model tissue deformation under varying load conditions while training neural networks to predict long-term morphological changes based on mechanical stress patterns. Validation will occur through comparison with intraoperative pressure sensor measurements and 12-month postoperative outcomes. This approach addresses critical gaps in understanding how microstructural adaptations in plantar fascia and tarsal ligaments influence macroscopic foot stability. Successful implementation could revolutionize preoperative planning by enabling virtual testing of surgical procedures and custom orthotic designs, potentially reducing revision rates by 30-40% in complex deformity cases. The resulting open-source biomechanics toolkit will provide the podiatric research community with the first scalable platform for simulating foot pathophysiology across multiple biological scales, fostering innovation in personalized lower extremity care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of podiatric medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and injuries to the foot and lower extremities. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, anatomy of the lower extremity, functional orthopedics, foot biomechanics, podiatric radiology, dermatology, podiatric surgery, podopediatrics, sports medicine, physical diagnosis, emergency medicine and traumatology, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of under-resourced modern languages and their literary traditions, focusing on cross-linguistic patterns that remain underexplored due to scalability constraints. A central challenge in foreign language studies is the lack of computational tools tailored to low-resource languages, which limits large-scale comparative analyses of syntactic structures, dialectal variations, and literary motifs across linguistic families. To address this, we propose developing a multilingual corpus-processing pipeline integrating transformer-based models and rule-based morphological analyzers to parse and annotate texts from 15+ languages, including regional and minority languages with limited digital representation. The pipeline will automate syntactic tagging, dialect classification, and sentiment analysis across heterogeneous literary and colloquial corpora. HPC resources are critical for training and fine-tuning language-specific models in parallel, managing memory-intensive tasks such as dynamic programming for alignment of parallel texts, and enabling large-scale simulations of language contact effects on semantic change. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated corpora, a comparative framework for identifying typological and stylistic convergences across languages, and computational evidence for hypotheses regarding dialect leveling in multilingual communities. This work will provide humanities researchers with scalable methods to analyze linguistic diversity beyond dominant global languages, while advancing interdisciplinary dialogue between computational linguistics and area studies. The requested resources will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for terabyte-scale text datasets, and high-throughput processing of non-Latin script encoding challenges.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more modern foreign languages that is not specific as to the name of the language(s) studied; that is otherwise undifferentiated; or that introduces students to language studies at the basic/elementary level.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the preservation, accessibility, and ethical stewardship of born-digital archival materials, which are increasingly at risk due to format obsolescence, data degradation, and scalability challenges. Traditional archival methods struggle to manage the volume and complexity of modern digital records, particularly those with dynamic or interactive elements (e.g., multimedia collections, software-dependent artifacts). The research addresses this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to automate and optimize workflows for large-scale archival processing, format migration, and integrity verification. Using machine learning models trained on heterogeneous datasets—including file formats, metadata schemas, and user interaction logs—the project will develop tools to predict preservation risks, prioritize resource allocation, and simulate long-term access scenarios. Computational methods will also enable the reconstruction of degraded or incomplete digital objects through probabilistic modeling and distributed checksum validation. A key innovation involves deploying containerized emulation environments on HPC clusters to test access pathways for obsolete software-dependent materials at scale, reducing the manual labor currently required for such tasks. Additionally, the project will explore ethical implications of AI-driven archival decisions by integrating computational accountability frameworks into resource allocation algorithms. Outcomes include open-source tools for automated archival processing, a benchmark dataset for evaluating digital preservation strategies, and a scalable model for prioritizing at-risk collections. By bridging archival theory and computational praxis, this work aims to transform how cultural heritage institutions manage digital assets, ensuring their longevity and equitable accessibility in an era of exponential data growth.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to identify, manage, preserve, and make available records with long-term value for documentation, legal, research, and other purposes. Includes instruction in appraisal and collection development, information and records management, archival preservation, access systems, management of electronic records, archival outreach, and legal and ethical issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of digital misinformation across decentralized communication networks, a critical challenge in contemporary journalism and media studies. The rapid proliferation of unverified information through social platforms, encrypted messaging apps, and AI-generated content has complicated efforts to track, contextualize, and counter false narratives at scale. Traditional computational tools are insufficient to process the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of multimodal data (text, images, video) involved in these ecosystems. The proposed research will develop and deploy machine learning models to map the diffusion pathways of misinformation, identify amplification patterns, and assess the interplay between algorithmic recommendation systems and user engagement behaviors. Computational tasks include large-scale network analysis of cross-platform content sharing, transformer-based NLP for semantic and sentiment analysis of multilingual datasets, and agent-based simulations to model audience responses under varying moderation policies. These methods require parallelized processing of terabytes of data, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed storage systems. Outcomes will include an open-source framework for real-time misinformation risk assessment, actionable insights into platform-specific intervention points, and evidence-based recommendations for improving media literacy campaigns. By advancing computational methods tailored to communication research, this project aims to strengthen the capacity of journalists, fact-checkers, and policymakers to address epistemic threats in digitally fragmented publics. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the project’s scale and reproducibility goals while maintaining ethical standards for data anonymization and bias mitigation.
cip_title: Communication, Journalism, and Related Programs, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication, journalism, and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural underpinnings of speech motor control deficits in acquired apraxia of speech (AOS) using high-performance computing (HPC) to model disrupted cortico-cerebellar networks. AOS, often resulting from stroke or traumatic brain injury, is characterized by inconsistent articulatory errors and prosodic abnormalities, yet the dynamic interactions between cortical speech planning regions and cerebellar timing circuits remain poorly understood. Current lesion-based models fail to explain the heterogeneity of symptom profiles, limiting personalized therapeutic approaches. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating functional neuroimaging, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and kinematic speech data to simulate network dysfunction. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of neural population dynamics using biologically constrained spiking neuron models, calibrated to individual patient data. Parallelized parameter optimization will map lesion effects on cerebellar-thalamo-cortical loop stability, while GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines will identify compensatory network configurations associated with recovery trajectories. The computational platform will process high-resolution fMRI time series (7T) and real-time electromagnetic articulography recordings, requiring petabyte-scale storage and distributed processing capabilities. Expected outcomes include a predictive model of AOS subtype classification based on network resilience thresholds and virtual stimulation targets for neuromodulation therapies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges communication sciences with computational neuroscience, offering a paradigm shift from symptom-focused rehabilitation to mechanism-driven interventions. The proposed HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of multi-modal neural datasets and advancing precision medicine applications for motor speech disorders.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biomedical, psychological, and physical principles to the study of the scientific bases, development, and treatment of speech, language, hearing, and cognitive communication problems caused by disease, injury, or disability. Includes instruction in language science, hearing science, speech and voice science, biology of communication, behavioral linguistics, psychology, and applications to the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative strategies and technologies.

abstract: This project proposes to develop an adaptive modeling framework to analyze the interplay between microplastic pollution dynamics and coastal socioecological systems, integrating hydrodynamic, ecological, and human behavioral data streams. While microplastics represent a growing environmental threat, their dispersion patterns and impacts on both marine food webs and adjacent human communities remain poorly quantified due to the complex feedback loops between physical transport processes, organismal interactions, and economic activities. The research will leverage high-performance computing to couple three-dimensional particle-tracking simulations of microplastic dispersal (using ROMS-WRF-HYCOM outputs) with agent-based models of fishing practices and machine learning analysis of community health surveys. By implementing graph neural networks to map connectivity between pollution hotspots and livelihood disruptions across temporal scales, the framework will address critical gaps in predicting threshold behaviors in coupled human-natural systems. Computational challenges include processing petascale oceanographic datasets, resolving multi-agent interactions through parallelized Monte Carlo sampling, and training physics-informed generative models to account for underrepresented regional dynamics. The hybrid architecture will require GPU-accelerated workloads for neural operator training alongside CPU-bound ensemble simulations of particle transport. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize remediation efforts based on ecological vulnerability and socioeconomic sensitivity indices, fostering interdisciplinary convergence between environmental fluid mechanics, marine policy, and anthropological statistics. This computational approach enables novel synthesis of disparate data modalities essential for addressing Anthropocene-era sustainability challenges that defy single-discipline paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to generate insights from data and identify and predict trends. Includes instruction in computer databases, computer programming, inference, machine learning, optimization, probability and stochastic models, statistics, strategy, uncertainty quantification, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to advance personalized learning strategies for students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) by analyzing multimodal behavioral and educational data. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) rely on manual observation and qualitative assessments, which are time-intensive and lack scalability. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large datasets of student interactions, including video recordings of classroom activities, sensor-based physiological data, and longitudinal academic performance metrics. The research will employ machine learning models to identify patterns in communication, sensory processing, and skill acquisition unique to learners with ASD. Computational experiments will simulate the efficacy of various intervention strategies under diverse classroom conditions using agent-based modeling, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will analyze teacher-student dialogue to optimize instructional scaffolding. Key challenges include handling high-dimensional, heterogeneous data and ensuring models generalize across the broad spectrum of ASD phenotypes. The use of HPC will enable rapid iteration of reinforcement learning algorithms to predict optimal teaching interventions and reduce latency in processing real-time sensor data during simulated training scenarios for educators. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for dynamically adjusting IEP targets based on computational evidence, (2) predictive models to guide educators in selecting evidence-based strategies for specific behavioral or learning profiles, and (3) open-source tools to help teacher training programs integrate data-driven decision-making into autism education curricula. By quantifying relationships between instructional methods and student outcomes at scale, this work aims to equip educators with empirically validated practices tailored to neurodiverse learners, ultimately improving the quality and accessibility of specialized autism education. All data will be anonymized and processed in compliance with FERPA and institutional review protocols.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Autism
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with autism, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with autism, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising autistic students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern manufacturing systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize production efficiency, resource utilization, and sustainability. This project seeks to address the challenge of dynamically balancing stochastic demand, multi-stage process interdependencies, and equipment constraints in large-scale discrete manufacturing environments. Traditional analytical methods struggle to model these systems at scale due to nonlinear interactions, high-dimensional parameter spaces, and real-time decision-making requirements. We propose developing a hybrid simulation-optimization framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable rapid scenario analysis and adaptive scheduling. The computational approach integrates discrete-event simulation for granular process modeling with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms for real-time decision optimization. Large-scale parameter sweeps will be conducted to train DRL agents across diverse production scenarios, while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty propagation through supply chain and assembly subsystems. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of training neural networks on high-dimensional state-action spaces and running thousands of concurrent simulation instances. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of recommending optimal resource allocation strategies under dynamic constraints, reducing idle time in production lines by an estimated 15-25%, and minimizing material waste through predictive buffer management. This work will advance the field of industrial engineering by demonstrating scalable computational methods for manufacturing system design, directly supporting the transition to Industry 4.0 capabilities. The resulting open-source framework will enable manufacturers to simulate complex trade-offs between energy consumption, throughput, and equipment longevity, fostering data-driven decision-making in resource-constrained environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, and implementation of manufacturing systems. Includes instruction in materials science and engineering, manufacturing processes, process engineering, assembly and product engineering, manufacturing systems design, and manufacturing competitiveness.

abstract: Developmental-behavioral disorders in children arise from complex interactions between genetic, neurobiological, and environmental factors, yet current diagnostic and intervention frameworks often lack precision due to heterogeneous data and limited integrative analysis. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to predict developmental-behavioral trajectories and optimize personalized intervention strategies. Leveraging multimodal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, genomic profiles, and longitudinal behavioral assessments—we aim to identify biomarkers and environmental modifiers associated with developmental delays, autism spectrum disorder, and family dysfunction. The scale and complexity of these datasets, which encompass millions of clinical variables and high-resolution neuroimaging data, necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources for efficient processing, integration, and analysis. We will employ ensemble machine learning methods to handle data heterogeneity, coupled with graph neural networks to model dynamic interactions between biological and psychosocial factors. Bayesian hierarchical models will further quantify uncertainty in predictive outcomes across diverse populations. Computational workflows will parallelize feature extraction from neuroimaging pipelines, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and natural language processing (NLP) of clinical notes. HPC infrastructure is critical to meet the memory and processing demands of these tasks, particularly for training deep learning architectures on clustered GPUs and conducting large-scale simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for early risk stratification, a computational framework for evaluating intervention efficacy, and open-source tools to assist clinicians in personalizing care plans. By integrating multidimensional data at unprecedented scale, this work will advance translational research in developmental-behavioral pediatrics, offering new pathways to mitigate disparities in diagnostic access and improve long-term developmental outcomes for children and families.
cip_definition: Research on how to assist in the prevention, diagnosis, and management of developmental difficulties and problematic behaviors in children, and in the family dysfunctions that compromise children's development; and to foster understanding and promotion of optimal development of children and families through research, education, clinical care, and advocacy efforts.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of next-generation composite materials for applications in aerospace, automotive, and renewable energy systems. Composite materials face critical challenges in optimizing their mechanical properties, durability, and manufacturability due to the complex interplay of fiber-matrix interactions, curing processes, and environmental factors. Traditional experimental approaches to design and test these materials are resource-intensive, time-consuming, and limited in their ability to predict multiscale behaviors. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to model composite performance across micro-, meso-, and macro-structural scales. FEA will simulate stress distribution and failure modes in component geometries under operational loads, while MD simulations will resolve atomic-scale interactions between polymer matrices and reinforcing fibers. ML algorithms, trained on these datasets, will identify optimal material configurations and processing parameters, such as resin viscosity gradients and fiber orientation patterns, to enhance mechanical strength and reduce defect formation. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of simulations, reducing computational bottlenecks in solving nonlinear, multiphysics problems. Expected outcomes include predictive models for composite fatigue life, damage tolerance, and thermal stability, validated against experimental data from partner industries. These tools will accelerate the design of lightweight, high-performance composites for wind turbine blades and medical prostheses, reducing reliance on physical prototyping. The project will also generate open-access datasets and workflows to support workforce training in computational materials science, aligning with the program’s mission to integrate advanced technical skills with industry needs. By bridging simulation-driven innovation with practical applications, this research aims to position composite materials technology at the forefront of sustainable engineering solutions.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development, manufacture, and use of composite materials in aircraft technology, automotive technology, boats, medical prostheses, and wind turbines. Includes instruction in computer-aided design and drafting, composite materials and processes, composite maintenance, composite manufacturing, composite repair, material science, and mold manufacturing and production.

abstract: Agricultural supply chains face significant challenges in balancing efficiency, sustainability, and profitability due to dynamic market conditions, variable production yields, and complex logistics. This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize decision-making in agricultural retail and wholesale operations, focusing on inventory management, demand forecasting, and distribution networks. Current analytical tools often lack the capacity to integrate real-time data from heterogeneous sources—including weather patterns, commodity pricing, IoT sensor networks, and historical sales—while accounting for stochastic variables such as crop failures or supply chain disruptions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build agent-based simulations and machine learning frameworks capable of modeling multi-scale interactions across agricultural supply chains. The computational workflow will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods for risk assessment, graph neural networks to model spatial distribution networks, and reinforcement learning to optimize restocking strategies under uncertainty. By simulating scenarios at regional and national scales, the project aims to identify resilient procurement policies, reduce waste from overstocking perishable goods, and improve profit margins for retailers and wholesalers. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive inventory management and data-driven recommendations for coordinating agricultural input suppliers with retail demand hotspots. This work will directly support agricultural businesses in mitigating operational risks, enhancing resource allocation, and fostering sustainable practices. The scale of data integration and the need for high-fidelity simulations of interdependent systems necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for efficient model training, large-scale parameter sweeps, and real-time analytics. Successful implementation will advance both academic understanding of agricultural supply chain dynamics and practical tools for industry stakeholders.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Farm Supplies Retailing and Wholesaling
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to sell agricultural products and supplies, provide support services to agricultural enterprises, and purchase and market agricultural products. Includes instruction in basic business management, marketing, retailing and wholesaling operations, and applicable principles of agriculture and agricultural operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the dynamics of information diffusion within family and consumer sciences (FCS) communication networks. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how complex, context-dependent human sciences content—such as financial literacy, nutrition education, or family resource management—is adopted, adapted, and shared across heterogeneous audiences. Current models of science communication often prioritize STEM-focused frameworks, neglecting the unique sociocultural and cognitive factors that shape decision-making in FCS domains. By integrating agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis, this study will simulate how multimodal FCS messaging propagates through diverse community structures while accounting for variables such as socioeconomic status, cultural values, and media literacy levels. The computational approach will process large-scale datasets from public health campaigns, social media interactions, and longitudinal household surveys to parameterize models that reflect real-world communication patterns. Key objectives include identifying critical thresholds for message saturation in target populations, optimizing content personalization strategies, and quantifying the impact of misinformation correction mechanisms. The requested HPC resources will enable iterative simulation of population-scale interaction networks (N ≈ 10^6 nodes) and parallel processing of multimedia content metadata. Expected outcomes include the development of an open-source framework for predictive FCS communication analytics, validated against empirical data from cooperative extension programs. This work holds significance for improving the efficacy of evidence-based consumer education while advancing computational social science methodologies tailored to human sciences contexts. By bridging gaps between communication theory, behavioral economics, and computational modeling, the project aims to establish new best practices for resource-constrained FCS outreach initiatives in an increasingly digital information ecosystem.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Communication
cip_definition: A program that focuses on communication of human sciences subject matter and related consumer information to a variety of audiences through print and non-print media.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolving dynamics of audience engagement and content dissemination across hybrid digital-media ecosystems, with a focus on the computational challenges inherent to analyzing large-scale, multimodal communication datasets. As media consumption shifts toward platform-agnostic behaviors—spanning streaming services, social media, and legacy broadcast systems—traditional analytical tools struggle to process the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of these data. The proposed work will develop and apply machine learning models to analyze temporal patterns in cross-platform media engagement, integrating natural language processing (NLP) for text/video metadata, graph-based methods for tracking content diffusion, and neural networks for audience sentiment analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train these models on terabyte-scale datasets, which include timestamped social media interactions, streaming platform logs, and broadcast archives from partner networks. A central objective is to simulate real-time content optimization scenarios, testing how algorithmic adjustments to scheduling or recommendation systems might affect audience retention in multi-platform environments. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for modeling cross-media engagement, insights into the resilience of local broadcast content in algorithmically driven ecosystems, and benchmarks for ethical AI applications in media strategy. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to address gaps in computational communication research, offering tools to help media producers, regulators, and scholars better navigate the infrastructural complexities of modern digital communication networks. The work aligns with the program’s focus on emergent media technologies while prioritizing scalable, reproducible methods for interdisciplinary collaboration.
cip_title: Radio, Television, and Digital Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in radio, television, and digital communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to address efficiency and scalability challenges in computer-aided design and drafting (CAD/CADD) for multidisciplinary engineering projects. Current CAD/CADD tools face limitations in processing complex, high-resolution models and simulating large-scale design iterations, particularly when integrating parametric constraints, material behavior datasets, and real-time collaboration features. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA) simulations, optimize topology generation algorithms, and enable cloud-based collaborative design environments. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) implementing GPU-accelerated solvers to reduce computational bottlenecks in stress-strain and thermal analysis for multi-component assemblies, and (2) developing machine learning-assisted workflows to automate design validation against industry standards (e.g., ASME Y14.5-2018). Computational methods will combine open-source CAD kernels with custom Python-based optimization scripts, containerized for reproducibility across HPC architectures. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for distributed processing of CADD tasks, demonstrating ≥40% reduction in simulation time for assemblies exceeding 10⁴ parts compared to single-node workstations. The results will directly benefit engineering technology education by enabling student teams to interact with industrial-scale design challenges while maintaining hardware accessibility. Furthermore, the project will produce open-access templates for integrating HPC workflows into CAD/CADD curricula, addressing a critical gap in training for next-generation digital twin technologies. By enhancing computational capacity for complex design scenarios, this work aims to bridge the gap between academic CADD instruction and evolving industry demands for high-throughput, data-driven engineering design.
cip_title: CAD/ CADD Drafting and/ or Design Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and advanced computer software and hardware to the creation of graphic representations and simulations in support of engineering projects. Includes instruction in engineering graphics, two-dimensional and three-dimensional engineering design, solids modeling, engineering animation, computer-aided drafting (CAD), computer-aided design (CADD), and auto-CAD techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying mind-body movement therapies (MBMTs), such as Feldenkrais Method and Body-Mind Centering, which lack rigorous computational frameworks to quantify their therapeutic efficacy. While clinical studies suggest benefits for chronic pain, mobility disorders, and cognitive function, the integration of real-time sensorimotor feedback, neural dynamics, and biomechanical adaptation in these practices remains poorly modeled. We propose a multiscale computational approach combining high-density electromyography (HD-EMG), motion capture, and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data from 120 participants engaged in structured MBMT protocols. The core computational challenge involves developing a coupled neural-biomechanical model using hierarchical Bayesian inference to map cortical hemodynamic patterns, muscle activation synergies, and joint kinematics during therapeutic movements. High-performance computing resources are essential for three key tasks: (1) Parallelized processing of multi-terabyte sensor datasets via GPU-accelerated signal decomposition, (2) Training deep neural networks to identify cross-modal biomarkers of therapeutic responsiveness, and (3) Running massively parallel simulations of neuromotor control circuits using spiking neural network models. Expected outcomes include the first open-source computational framework for MBMT analysis, validated against psychometric and physiological outcome measures. This work will establish quantitative bridges between subjective therapeutic experiences and objective neurobiomechanical states, addressing critical gaps in evidence-based validation for movement-based mind-body therapies. The requested resources will enable parameter sensitivity analyses across 10^6 possible neural-circuit configurations and real-time feedback system prototyping at millisecond resolution. By elucidating how intentional movement modulates central-peripheral nervous system communication, this research advances fundamental knowledge in embodied cognition while providing computational tools for personalized rehabilitation protocols in underserved clinical populations, including fibromyalgia and Parkinson’s disease.
cip_title: Movement and Mind-Body Therapies and Education, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in movement and mind-body therapies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to model and optimize personalized behavioral interventions for individuals with developmental disabilities and autism, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the complexity of behavioral data and intervention design. Applied behavior analysis (ABA) relies on iterative, data-driven adjustments to intervention strategies, but current methods often struggle with scalability when analyzing large, longitudinal datasets or dynamically adjusting multi-component interventions in real time. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional behavioral data—including frequency, duration, and contextual variables—to identify patterns and predict intervention outcomes efficiently. The proposed computational approach integrates reinforcement learning algorithms with multi-level Bayesian models to simulate intervention efficacy across diverse behavioral profiles. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of thousands of simulated intervention scenarios, training predictive models on historical ABA datasets (e.g., discrete trial training logs, functional behavior assessments), and validating results against real-world case studies. Key objectives include (1) optimizing parameters for individualized reinforcement schedules, (2) identifying critical thresholds for intervention adjustments, and (3) developing an open-source framework for clinicians to simulate intervention outcomes based on client-specific data. Expected outcomes include scalable models that reduce the trial-and-error period in ABA practice, predictive tools to guide clinician decision-making, and publicly accessible computational workflows for the ABA research community. By enabling rapid analysis of complex behavioral interactions, this work aims to enhance the precision of ABA interventions, reduce resource-intensive processes in clinical settings, and contribute to equitable access to data-driven behavioral support. The project aligns with the ethical priorities of ABA by emphasizing transparency in algorithmic recommendations and fostering collaboration between computational and applied psychology domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of principles of learning and behavior to enhance the development, abilities, and choices of children and adults; and that prepares individuals to address the behavioral needs of individuals, especially those with developmental disabilities and autism. Includes instruction in behavior analysis and learning, behavioral and functional assessment, developmental psychology, applied behavioral analysis in developmental disabilities and autism, applied behavioral analysis in mental health and aging, research methods, evaluation of interventions, and professional and ethical issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in obstetrics and gynecology by analyzing complex, multidimensional datasets to predict and mitigate adverse pregnancy outcomes. The research problem centers on the heterogeneity of conditions such as preeclampsia, preterm birth, and gestational diabetes, which remain leading causes of maternal and neonatal morbidity. Current risk stratification tools lack accuracy due to the interplay of genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, and environmental factors, necessitating computational approaches capable of modeling high-dimensional interactions. The proposed work integrates longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), placental transcriptomics, and dynamic biomarker profiles from a prospective cohort of 5,000 patients to develop predictive models. Machine learning algorithms, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, will be trained to identify early risk signatures and infer causal pathways. A key innovation involves coupling these models with mechanistic simulations of uteroplacental blood flow dynamics using finite element analysis, enabling the validation of predictive biomarkers against physiological outcomes. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale of omics data (≥50 TB), optimizing hyperparameters across thousands of parallel jobs, and running computationally intensive fluid dynamics simulations. Expected outcomes include clinically actionable risk scores for preeclampsia, validated via a blinded randomized trial assessing early intervention efficacy, and open-source tools for placental function modeling. By elucidating subtype-specific mechanisms, this work aims to shift obstetrical care from reactive to proactive strategies, reducing disparities in outcomes. The computational frameworks developed will also be adaptable to gynecologic oncology and reproductive health research, broadly advancing data-driven innovation in women’s health.
cip_definition: Research focused on Obstetrics and Gynecology

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolving legal and administrative frameworks governing transnational religious institutions through computational analysis of multi-jurisdictional regulatory documents and case law. As religious organizations increasingly operate across national boundaries, they face complex legal challenges arising from conflicting secular laws, digital governance requirements, and shifting cultural norms. Traditional legal scholarship struggles to systematically analyze the scale and complexity of these interactions, particularly across languages and jurisdictions. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques on a corpus of 250,000+ legal documents (including court decisions, institutional policies, and legislative texts from 15 countries) to model patterns in legal conflicts, regulatory compliance strategies, and administrative decision-making processes. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on multilingual legal texts, conducting network analysis of citation patterns between judicial systems, and simulating the cascading effects of policy changes through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of recurring conflict domains in cross-border religious administration; 2) development of predictive models for legal risk assessment in institutional operations; and 3) creation of an open-access visualization platform mapping relationships between religious governance structures and secular legal systems. This computational approach advances humanistic scholarship by revealing hidden systemic interactions in religious institutional law while providing practical tools for faith-based organizations navigating complex regulatory environments. The research bridges computational legal studies, digital humanities, and organizational theory within an understudied domain of religious institutional practice.
cip_title: Religious Institution Administration and Law, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious institution administration and law, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity and volume of legal documentation, combined with the need for rapid analysis in litigation and regulatory compliance, present significant challenges for legal support systems. Traditional methods of manual review and keyword-based searches are inefficient, error-prone, and unable to scale with the exponential growth of digitized legal texts. This project proposes the development of a high-throughput computational framework to automate the extraction of semantically meaningful patterns from unstructured legal documents, including court opinions, contracts, and regulatory filings. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research aims to create a scalable natural language processing (NLP) pipeline tailored to the syntactic and contextual nuances of legal language. The framework will integrate transformer-based models for entity recognition, clause classification, and precedent linkage, trained on a curated corpus of legal texts spanning multiple jurisdictions. Computational workflows will parallelize document processing across GPU nodes to enable real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, while privacy-preserving federated learning techniques will address confidentiality constraints inherent to legal data. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for legal document analysis, validated against ground-truth annotations from legal experts, and a benchmark dataset to support reproducibility. By automating labor-intensive tasks such as contract clause identification, case law summarization, and compliance auditing, this work has the potential to reduce costs, mitigate risks, and improve access to justice through enhanced efficiency in legal support services. The project bridges computational linguistics and legal informatics, establishing a foundation for AI-assisted legal workflows while maintaining rigorous adherence to ethical and procedural standards in legal practice.
cip_definition: Any program in legal support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the documentation and analysis of understudied languages in Southeast Asia and the Pacific, focusing on their morphosyntactic diversity, historical development, and sociolinguistic vitality. Many languages in these regions remain under-documented, with limited digital corpora, and are at risk of endangerment due to shifting linguistic ecologies. Traditional methods of manual analysis are insufficient for processing the growing volume of digitized recordings, texts, and metadata, necessitating scalable computational approaches. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply machine learning models for automated phonetic alignment, syntactic parsing, and cross-linguistic comparison. A key focus is the creation of language-specific NLP pipelines for Austronesian and Papuan languages, which present challenges such as complex clause chaining, tonal variation, and non-concatenative morphology. These pipelines will integrate transformer-based models fine-tuned on newly digitized field recordings and legacy texts, combined with phylogenetic algorithms to model language contact and divergence. Additionally, HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of language shift scenarios, informed by sociodemographic data, to assess preservation strategies. Expected outcomes include open-access corpora for 10+ endangered languages, a comparative database of grammatical structures, and methodological advancements in computational linguistics for low-resource contexts. The project will directly support collaborative revitalization efforts with Indigenous communities while advancing theoretical frameworks for understanding linguistic diversity in the region. By leveraging parallel processing and GPU-accelerated workflows, this work addresses computational bottlenecks in handling terabytes of multimodal data, enabling analyses previously infeasible on standard infrastructure. Results will inform both academic research and community-based language preservation initiatives, contributing to global efforts to safeguard intangible cultural heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian and Australasian/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for optimizing vehicle performance in motorsports necessitates advanced computational tools to address complex challenges in aerodynamic design, thermal management, and structural integrity. Current simulation workflows for race car development often rely on simplified models or commercial software with limited customization, which restricts the ability to explore novel design paradigms under realistic multi-physics racing conditions. This project proposes to develop and validate a high-fidelity computational framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable coupled aerodynamic, thermal, and structural simulations of motorsports vehicles. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) implementing large-eddy simulation (LES) models to resolve unsteady airflow interactions around vehicle surfaces and cooling systems, (2) integrating conjugate heat transfer analyses to evaluate engine bay thermal loads and brake system performance, and (3) employing topology optimization algorithms to iteratively improve chassis component designs under combined mechanical and thermal stresses. The computational approach will leverage open-source solvers (e.g., OpenFOAM, SU2) with GPU-accelerated workflows to manage the high-resolution meshes (>100 million cells) and transient simulations required for capturing turbulent flow features and thermal gradients. Parametric studies will assess design variables such as diffuser geometry, vortex generator placement, and material selection under diverse track conditions. Outcomes will include validated simulation protocols for motorsports applications, quantitative performance benchmarks for prototype components, and open-access datasets to support academic-industry collaborations. By providing scalable HPC workflows tailored to racing environments, this work aims to reduce physical prototyping costs while enabling data-driven innovations in vehicle dynamics and energy efficiency. The resource allocation will also directly enhance student training through hands-on experience with cutting-edge computational tools in motorsports-relevant courses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the design, construction, and repair of vehicles used in racing and motorsports. Includes instruction in aerodynamics, design, vehicle dynamics, performance engines, fluid mechanics, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical engineering, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational design of enzyme-inspired catalysts for sustainable chemical production by integrating molecular-scale simulations with machine learning optimization. Traditional catalyst development relies on empirical approaches, which are inefficient for tailoring biocatalysts to non-natural substrates. We propose a multi-scale computational framework combining quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulations, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD), and deep neural networks to predict mutation hotspots that enhance catalytic activity and stability under industrial conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable exhaustive sampling of enzyme conformations, free energy calculations via enhanced sampling algorithms, and training of predictive models on terabytes of structural and thermodynamic data. The proposed work focuses on engineering cytochrome P450 variants for selective C–H bond activation, a critical step in pharmaceutical and biofuel synthesis. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational pipeline for rational enzyme design, validated by experimental collaborators, and fundamental insights into protein dynamics-function relationships. By accelerating the development of biocatalysts for greener manufacturing processes, this research addresses urgent needs in biopharmaceutical and bio-based industries while reducing reliance on toxic reagents. The requested resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of protein sequences and reaction pathways, which exceeds the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems at the interface of chemical engineering and biology, with an emphasis at the molecular level, such as biopharmaceutical processes, protein engineering, metabolic engineering, gene therapy, biomaterials, cell and tissue engineering, and drug delivery. Includes instruction in chemical engineering, thermodynamics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, momentum and heat transfer, cellular and molecular biotechnology, process design, and chemical reactor design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biophysical and systemic mechanisms underlying Reiki therapy, with a focus on quantifying its effects on human biofield dynamics. Despite widespread use in holistic health practices, the energetic interactions and physiological correlates of Reiki remain poorly characterized, limiting integration into evidence-based care frameworks. The research will develop computational models to simulate biofield perturbations during Reiki interventions, analyze patterns in energy transfer efficiency, and correlate these with psychophysiological outcomes. A multi-scale modeling approach will be employed, integrating quantum biophysical representations of bioenergetic pathways with systemic models of neural, endocrine, and immune responses. Machine learning algorithms will process empirical data from biofeedback devices (e.g., EEG, HRV, and thermal imaging) collected during clinical Reiki sessions, cross-referenced with practitioner-reported techniques (e.g., symbol use, distance healing protocols). Agent-based simulations will model hypothesized entrainment effects between practitioner and recipient biofields, while Monte Carlo methods will assess variability in therapeutic outcomes across different Reiki lineages. The computational framework will require parallel processing capabilities to handle high-dimensional datasets spanning molecular, cellular, and organismal scales. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative models of Reiki's biofield modulation principles, identification of biomarkers predictive of therapeutic efficacy, and optimization parameters for attunement processes. Results will advance scientific understanding of energy medicine modalities, inform standardized training protocols, and provide mechanistic insights to support interdisciplinary dialogue with conventional healthcare systems. This work directly addresses critical gaps in complementary medicine research by applying rigorous computational methodologies to traditionally qualitative healing practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical, emotional, and spiritual balance and healing through the manipulation of the body's energy field to increase healing energy. Includes instruction in the history and philosophy of Usui Reiki, attunement, empowerment, self-treatment, direct and distance healing techniques, healing symbols, aura clearing, Reiki meditation, practice management, and related Reiki systems such as Lightarian, Urevia, and Magnified Healing.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze large-scale ethical reasoning patterns and their logical coherence across diverse cultural and historical contexts. Philosophical ethics grapples with systematizing moral principles, yet human ethical reasoning often involves context-dependent judgments that challenge universal models. Traditional philosophical methods struggle to evaluate the consistency of such reasoning at scale or to model the dynamic interplay between abstract principles and situated decisions. To address this, we will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-agent ethical decision-making scenarios, parameterized by historical ethical texts, anthropological data, and formal axiomatic systems. Agent-based modeling will be used to test the stability and emergent properties of hybrid ethical frameworks (e.g., consequentialist-deontological interactions) under variable social conditions. Natural language processing pipelines will parse and structurally map arguments from digitized philosophical corpora (e.g., cross-cultural treatises on justice), transforming them into computable logical networks. These networks will then be analyzed for topological patterns and paradoxes using graph-theoretic algorithms. The computational demands arise from the need to process terabytes of unstructured text, simulate millions of agent interactions with nested decision trees, and solve complex constraint satisfaction problems inherent in evaluating coherentist ethical systems. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database of formalized ethical arguments tagged with logical dependencies, 2) quantitative measures of framework consistency across simulated sociocultural environments, and 3) novel visualizations of philosophical argument structures to enhance human-computer collaborative analysis. This work bridges computational social science and moral philosophy, offering empirically grounded insights into the scalability of ethical theories while developing humanities-specific computational tools. The requested resources will enable previously intractable investigations into how abstract philosophical systems interact with real-world reasoning complexity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on ideas and their logical structure, including arguments and investigations about abstract and real phenomena. Includes instruction in logic, ethics, aesthetics, epistemology, metaphysics, symbolism, and history of philosophy, and applications to the theoretical foundations and methods of other disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and optimize donor engagement strategies for religious institutions, a critical challenge in the interdisciplinary field of Religious Institution Administration and Management. As these institutions increasingly rely on philanthropic support to sustain operations, traditional fundraising approaches often lack the granularity to address evolving donor behaviors, demographic shifts, and economic volatility. This research aims to develop a computational framework to model donor decision-making processes, simulate the impact of targeted outreach campaigns, and identify factors that maximize philanthropic contributions. Using anonymized donation records, demographic datasets, and socioeconomic indicators from over 200 religious organizations, the project will apply machine learning algorithms to classify donor segments and predict giving patterns. Agent-based modeling will simulate hypothetical fundraising scenarios, incorporating variables such as community demographics, institutional program offerings, and macroeconomic trends. These simulations, requiring parallel processing for large-scale parameter space exploration, will test the efficacy of personalized outreach strategies, event-based fundraising, and digital engagement tools. The computational outputs will be validated against historical campaign performance data to refine predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating donor behavior, evidence-based recommendations for campaign design, and a repository of anonymized models to support adaptive resource allocation. By integrating computational social science methods with institutional management theory, this research addresses a critical gap in data-driven decision-making for religious organizations, offering scalable solutions to enhance financial resilience while maintaining alignment with ethical and mission-driven priorities. The project’s findings will contribute to broader interdisciplinary dialogues on nonprofit management, behavioral economics, and the role of technology in sustaining community-centered institutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the business affairs and administration of religious institutions. Includes instruction in business management, principles of accounting and financial management, human resources management, taxation of religious institutions, and business law as applied to religious institutions.

abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain present complex clinical challenges due to their multifactorial etiology, spanning biomechanical, neurobiological, and psychosocial dimensions. Current diagnostic frameworks and treatment protocols lack precision, in part due to insufficient understanding of the dynamic interactions between joint biomechanics, pain pathway activation, and patient-specific anatomical variability. This project proposes a computational biomechanics and neuroimaging approach to model the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) under functional loads and correlate these dynamics with central nervous system pain processing patterns. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate finite element analysis (FEA) of patient-specific TMJ anatomy—derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)—with functional MRI (fMRI) data capturing pain-related neural activity. Multiscale simulations will map strain distributions within the joint capsule, disc, and surrounding musculature during mastication and parafunctional movements, while machine learning algorithms will identify associations between mechanical stress patterns, inflammatory biomarker profiles, and maladaptive neuroplasticity observed in chronic pain states. A key innovation lies in coupling biomechanical models with dynamic pain network analyses to predict individual progression from acute to chronic TMD. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of high-resolution imaging datasets (>10 TB), iterative optimization of nonlinear FEA solvers, and real-time visualization of coupled biomechanical-neural datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for identifying high-risk patients based on simulated joint loading patterns and neural signatures, (2) quantitative biomarkers to guide personalized occlusal appliance design, and (3) open-source tools for multimodal data integration in orofacial pain research. By bridging computational mechanics and systems neuroscience, this work aims to advance precision medicine approaches for TMD while establishing scalable methods for studying musculoskeletal disorders with complex pain comorbidities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to evaluate, diagnose, and treat of a wide variety of temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain disorders as well as the treatment of sleep apnea and snoring with intraoral appliances. Includes instruction in head and neck anatomy, physical diagnosis and evaluation, orofacial pain, neurobiology of pain and analgesia, and diagnostic radiography.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of designing advanced catalytic materials for sustainable chemical processes through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multi-scale modeling. Industrial catalysts used in petroleum refining and chemical synthesis often suffer from inefficiencies, such as low selectivity or rapid deactivation under harsh reaction conditions. Experimental optimization of these materials is time- and resource-intensive, motivating the need for predictive computational frameworks. We propose a hybrid approach integrating quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT), classical molecular dynamics (MD), and machine learning (ML) to model catalyst surfaces, reaction pathways, and structure-property relationships. The study focuses on transition metal oxides and supported metal clusters, targeting applications in hydrocarbon reforming and CO₂ conversion. DFT calculations will elucidate electronic structure effects on adsorption energies and activation barriers, while MD simulations will assess thermal stability and diffusion dynamics in nanoporous catalyst architectures. ML algorithms trained on these datasets will accelerate the exploration of compositional and morphological variables. The scale of these simulations—requiring thousands of core-hours for ab initio calculations of defect-rich surfaces and microsecond-scale MD trajectories—necessitates access to HPC resources with parallelized chemistry codes (e.g., VASP, LAMMPS) and GPU-accelerated ML workflows. Expected outcomes include identifying candidate materials with enhanced activity and durability for methane dry reforming, as well as a transferable protocol for screening hierarchical catalysts. This work aligns with Engineering Chemistry’s emphasis on materials innovation for energy applications, offering atomistic insights to bridge the gap between laboratory-scale synthesis and industrial reactor performance. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, the project aims to advance computational design paradigms for sustainable chemical engineering.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of chemical principles to the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems, such as development of electronic materials, solid-state science and technology, polymers, ceramics, and biomaterials. Includes instruction in physical chemistry, organic chemistry, materials science, chemical processes and systems, chemical reaction engineering, biochemical engineering, engineering mathematics, classical and modern physics, and computer science.

abstract: Phlebotomy procedures, while routine, involve complex interactions between anatomical variability, technique precision, and patient-specific factors that influence success rates and complication risks. This project seeks to optimize blood collection practices by developing computational models to simulate venipuncture dynamics, predict outcomes, and guide evidence-based protocol improvements. The primary research challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous biological data—including vascular anatomy, blood flow characteristics, and tissue biomechanics—into predictive frameworks that account for real-world clinical variability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to run multi-scale simulations coupling finite element analysis of needle-tissue interactions with machine learning models trained on anonymized phlebotomy outcome datasets (e.g., hematoma rates, sample hemolysis). These simulations will incorporate 3D vascular mapping derived from ultrasound imaging data and patient demographic variables to assess technique efficacy across diverse populations. A secondary aim involves creating virtual reality (VR)-compatible training modules that use real-time biomechanical feedback to accelerate skill acquisition among phlebotomy students. The computational workflow demands parallel processing for Monte Carlo simulations evaluating 10,000+ procedural scenarios, as well as GPU-accelerated neural networks to identify risk patterns in retrospective clinical data. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to guide needle insertion angle and depth based on individual patient characteristics, (2) quantitative safety thresholds for specimen handling variables like tube inversion frequency, and (3) validated VR training sequences that reduce skill competency time by ≥30% compared to traditional methods. By establishing computational phlebotomy benchmarks, this work addresses critical gaps in standardized practice guidelines while providing a scalable framework to analyze procedural outcomes across healthcare settings. The requested HPC allocation will enable the parameter space exploration necessary to account for biological diversity and operational constraints inherent in clinical phlebotomy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and other health care professionals, to draw blood samples from patients using a variety of intrusive procedures. Includes instruction in basic vascular anatomy and physiology, blood physiology, skin puncture techniques, venipuncture, venous specimen collection and handling, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and operational efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) systems under variable environmental and load conditions. A critical challenge in solar energy technology lies in mitigating efficiency losses caused by thermal fluctuations, material degradation, and suboptimal energy storage integration. Traditional experimental approaches to these issues are time-intensive and costly, while existing simulation tools often lack the resolution to capture complex, coupled phenomena in PV systems. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating multiphysics modeling, machine learning, and real-world sensor data. The computational workflow will simulate heat transfer, charge carrier dynamics, and mechanical stress across PV modules at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolutions, leveraging finite element analysis and Monte Carlo methods. Machine learning algorithms will then identify patterns in degradation rates and energy output under diverse climatic scenarios, enabling predictive maintenance strategies. Additionally, the models will evaluate hybrid energy storage configurations to balance grid demand and solar intermittency. The HPC resources will facilitate large-scale parameter sweeps to optimize panel orientation, material selection, and storage system sizing across geographic regions. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for PV system lifetime performance, open-source tools for solar array design, and a decision-support framework for integrating solar technologies into microgrids. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on applied engineering solutions by bridging theoretical solar principles with scalable computational methods.
