The results will provide actionable insights for reducing solar energy costs and improving adoption rates in underserved regions with harsh environmental conditions, advancing equitable access to renewable energy infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing solar-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in solar energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of stress transfer mechanisms within complex fault systems to improve earthquake hazard assessment. Current models of fault interactions often oversimplify the 3D geometry of fault networks and the viscoelastic properties of surrounding rock, limiting their predictive capability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled study integrating geomechanical modeling with geodetic and seismological data from the San Andreas Fault System (SAFS) and adjacent crustal faults. The research will develop parallelized finite element models to simulate stress evolution across multi-scale fault geometries, incorporating heterogeneous material properties derived from seismic tomography and laboratory rock mechanics data. A key innovation is the coupling of quasi-dynamic rupture simulations with long-term tectonic loading models to capture both coseismic and interseismic phases of the earthquake cycle. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to analyze terabyte-scale InSAR and GNSS datasets, identifying patterns of strain accumulation correlated with modeled stress perturbations. The computational demands are substantial, requiring millions of CPU-hours for ensemble simulations across parameter space and GPU-accelerated processing of high-resolution geodetic time series. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of stress transfer efficiency between geometrically irregular fault segments, (2) improved constraints on recurrence intervals for multi-fault rupture scenarios, and (3) open-source tools for community use in fault interaction analysis. Results will directly inform probabilistic seismic hazard models for California while advancing computational methods applicable to fault systems worldwide. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the spatial resolution (≤100 m grid spacing) and temporal duration (10^4 year simulations) needed to resolve both near-field stress concentrations and system-scale deformation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and relationships between the solids, liquids and gases comprising it.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to optimize operational efficiency and emissions control in fossil fuel and nuclear power plants, with a focus on addressing thermal stress dynamics in turbine systems and real-time pollutant mitigation. Power plant operations require precise balancing of energy output, equipment longevity, and regulatory compliance, yet existing models often oversimplify transient thermal gradients in turbine blades or rely on static assumptions about combustion byproduct dispersion. The research will employ multiphysics simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization to characterize heat transfer, material fatigue, and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system performance under variable load conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve 3D transient simulations of turbine blade erosion patterns, coupled with reactor core thermal-hydraulic interactions in nuclear systems, at timescales spanning milliseconds to operational cycles. A parallelized workflow will combine OpenFOAM for turbulent flow modeling, MOOSE Framework for thermomechanical stress analysis, and custom Python-based optimizers to identify operating thresholds that minimize NOx/SOx emissions while maintaining grid stability. Datasets from three operational power plants will validate model outputs. Anticipated outcomes include predictive maintenance algorithms for turbine assemblies, dynamic SCR control templates to reduce reagent waste by 15-20%, and generalized thermal stress mitigation protocols applicable to next-generation reactor designs. This work directly supports workforce training in power plant instrumentation and industrial controls by generating open-access simulation case studies for academic use. The requested computing allocation will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ core-hour simulations, which are infeasible on local clusters due to memory-intensive meshing requirements for rotating machinery geometries. Results will advance scalable computational tools for power generation infrastructure, aligning with national priorities for grid reliability and emissions reduction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational workflows in architectural design, with a focus on integrating generative design, machine learning (ML), and real-time environmental simulation into the iterative development of sustainable urban structures. Current architectural practices face limitations in efficiently modeling complex, large-scale geometries and optimizing designs for dynamic environmental factors such as microclimate variability, energy efficiency, and material circularity. Traditional software tools struggle to balance high-fidelity simulation with rapid iteration, particularly when addressing multi-objective design criteria across urban contexts. The proposed research will develop a computational framework that couples parametric modeling platforms with ML-driven optimization and physics-based simulation, enabling architects to explore design spaces at unprecedented scales. Key methods include (1) parallelized parametric generation of architectural forms using evolutionary algorithms to meet aesthetic, functional, and sustainability constraints; (2) training graph neural networks on urban morphology datasets to predict site-specific environmental performance; and (3) deploying finite element analysis and agent-based modeling to simulate building-fluid interactions and pedestrian flow patterns under varying climate scenarios. HPC resources will be critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of design variables, training large-scale ML models on 3D urban datasets, and running coupled simulations with reduced latency. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generative urban design, validated through case studies on adaptive reuse projects in coastal cities facing sea-level rise. This work aims to establish new methodologies for data-driven architectural practice while contributing to climate-resilient design frameworks that integrate computational efficiency with ecological sensitivity. By bridging gaps between architectural theory, computational design, and environmental science, the project demonstrates how HPC can catalyze innovation in non-STEM disciplines facing complex sociotechnical challenges.
cip_definition: An advanced program of study for architects and related professionals that focuses on theoretical and practical issues in architecture and integrates digital technologies into architectural design, fabrication, and construction. Includes instruction in architectural history and urban theory, 3-D digital technologies, construction, design and fabrication methods, and sustainable practices in architecture.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into fashion and apparel design presents a transformative opportunity to address complex challenges in sustainable design, material optimization, and consumer customization. Current industry practices rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is resource-intensive, time-consuming, and environmentally unsustainable. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for simulating textile behaviors, automating design processes, and optimizing material usage. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating physics-based models to predict the drape, stretch, and wearability of novel sustainable textiles under diverse conditions; (2) training machine learning algorithms to analyze historical and real-time consumer trend data for generative design applications; and (3) implementing multi-objective optimization to minimize waste in pattern cutting while maximizing aesthetic and functional outcomes. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating fabric mechanics, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for visual trend recognition, and genetic algorithms for evolving design solutions. The scale of these simulations—particularly the high-resolution textile models and large datasets of consumer preferences—requires parallel processing capabilities and significant memory allocation, necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of simulated textile properties, an open-source tool for AI-assisted design iteration, and a framework for quantifying environmental impact during the conceptual design phase. By reducing reliance on physical prototyping, this research aims to accelerate sustainable innovation in apparel production, lower material waste, and enable data-driven customization at scale. The project bridges gaps between computational science and creative practice, offering methodologies that could redefine resource efficiency in the fashion industry while maintaining artistic integrity.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional design of commercial fashions, apparel, and accessories, and the management of fashion development projects. Includes instruction in apparel design; accessory design; the design of men's', women's', and children's' wear; flat pattern design; computer-assisted design and manufacturing; concept planning; designing in specific materials; labor and cost analysis; history of fashion; fabric art and printing; and the principles of management and operations in the fashion industry.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid cloud environments has exposed critical gaps in adaptive resource orchestration frameworks, particularly in scenarios requiring real-time balancing of security, latency, and computational efficiency across distributed systems. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven resource allocation model optimized for multi-domain network architectures, where traditional static provisioning strategies fail to account for dynamic interdependencies between edge devices, private infrastructure, and public cloud services. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate heterogeneous network topologies under variable load conditions, including IoT data bursts and intermittent connectivity events. Computational methods will integrate graph neural networks (GNNs) to model infrastructure dependencies and reinforcement learning to optimize containerized workload placement while maintaining strict service-level agreements. Key challenges include developing lightweight anomaly detection modules for resource contention prediction and creating evolutionary algorithms capable of adapting allocation policies across dissimilar virtualization platforms. The simulations will utilize Kubernetes-based orchestration layers modified to interface with custom traffic generators and failure scenario emulators. Expected outcomes include a publicly available benchmarking toolkit for hybrid cloud resource management and novel metrics quantifying the trade-offs between energy efficiency, security overhead, and quality of service in ephemeral computing environments. This work directly addresses operational pain points in modern system administration by providing empirically validated strategies for maintaining performance parity during infrastructure scaling events, with potential applications in disaster response networks and federated learning deployments. The HPC environment is essential for training models on petabyte-scale synthetic datasets representing realistic multi-tenant workloads, enabling the identification of phase transition points in distributed system behavior that cannot be observed in smaller testbeds.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the computer operations and control the system configurations emanating from a specific site or network hub. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software and applications; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) networking; principles of information systems security; disk space and traffic load monitoring; data backup; resource allocation; and setup and takedown procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design of multifunctional nanoscale systems that integrate responsive nanomaterials with dynamic control mechanisms, addressing a critical gap in scalable nanoengineering. Current approaches to nanodevice design often treat material synthesis, structural configuration, and operational control as separate challenges, leading to suboptimal performance in applications requiring real-time adaptability. The research will focus on simulating hybrid nanosystems combining phase-change metamaterials with optically active quantum dots, where emergent behaviors arise from the interplay of thermal, electromagnetic, and quantum effects at the 1-100 nm scale. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve multi-physics interactions across spatial and temporal domains spanning 12 orders of magnitude. The computational approach employs hierarchical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations coupled with finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) electromagnetic modeling, enhanced by machine learning surrogates to accelerate parameter space exploration. GPU-optimized algorithms will handle the concurrent simulation of >10^6 nanoparticle ensembles while maintaining atomic-level fidelity in critical interfacial regions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for nonlinear response tuning in reconfigurable nanodevices and a publicly accessible database of optimized nanomaterial configurations. This work will advance the fundamental understanding of coupled nanoscale phenomena while providing practical design guidelines for next-generation applications in programmable nanophotonics and adaptive thermal management systems. The requested computing resources will enable unprecedented resolution of time-dependent nanoscale energy transfer processes, directly supporting the development of experimental protocols for controlled nanofabrication. By bridging simulation scales and physical domains, this research establishes a computational paradigm for engineering multifunctional nanotechnology systems that transcend conventional single-domain optimization strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical, scientific, and engineering principles and technical skills to manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) and to design, fabricate, and integrate nanoscale structures, devices, and systems. Includes instruction in materials science, thermodynamics, nanomaterials, nanoelectronics, and nano/micro device fabrication and testing.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of speech-language pathology (SLP) screenings and assessments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale speech datasets. Current clinical protocols for identifying communication disorders often rely on manual, time-intensive evaluations by speech-language pathologists (SLPs) and their assistants (SLPAs), which can limit scalability and introduce subjective variability. To address this, we propose developing computational models capable of automating the detection of speech and language anomalies in diverse populations. The research will utilize a corpus of de-identified speech samples from individuals with disorders such as aphasia, dysarthria, and childhood apraxia, alongside typical speakers, to train machine learning algorithms. These models will process acoustic features (e.g., pitch, articulation rates) and linguistic patterns (e.g., syntactic complexity, semantic coherence) using neural networks optimized via HPC clusters. The computational workflow will involve parallelized feature extraction, hyperparameter tuning, and validation against clinical diagnoses to ensure robustness. By integrating these tools into a user-friendly interface, SLPAs could conduct preliminary screenings with greater consistency, allowing SLPs to focus on nuanced diagnostic and therapeutic tasks. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for disorder classification, open-source tools for speech analysis, and benchmarks for computational efficiency in processing real-world clinical data. This work holds significance for reducing disparities in access to SLP services, particularly in underserved regions, while advancing research on the neurocomputational underpinnings of communication disorders. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive training processes, which exceed the capacity of standard institutional infrastructure. Successful implementation will bridge gaps between computational research and clinical practice, fostering innovation in health professions education and patient care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic impacts of trade policy uncertainty on global value chain (GVC) integration using large-scale computational modeling. Recent geopolitical shifts and trade conflicts have amplified uncertainty in international commercial relations, yet existing trade models inadequately capture the heterogeneous responses of multinational firms to stochastic policy environments. The research addresses this gap by developing a high-dimensional structural model that integrates firm-level production network data, tariff schedules, and real exchange rate volatility. The computational approach employs a parallelized dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) framework augmented with agent-based modeling techniques to simulate cross-border input-output linkages under varying policy scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the model’s scale, which requires solving systems of non-linear equations across 10,000+ firm agents interacting in 45 countries and 30 industrial sectors. Key tasks include Bayesian estimation of shock propagation parameters using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify welfare effects under alternative trade agreement designs. Expected outcomes include: (1) granular insights into how tariff uncertainty thresholds influence multinational firms’ reshoring decisions, (2) policy-relevant metrics on the resilience of GVCs to non-tariff trade barriers, and (3) open-source computational tools for trade elasticity estimation. Results will inform multilateral trade negotiations and supply chain risk management strategies. The requested computing resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from the World Input-Output Database, BEA, and customs transaction records, which are computationally prohibitive on standard workstations. This work advances methodological capabilities in trade policy analysis while addressing urgent questions about economic globalization in an era of increasing protectionism.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study and analysis of international commercial behavior and trade policy. Includes instruction in international trade theory, tariffs and quotas, commercial policy, trade factor flows, international finance and investment, currency regulation and trade exchange rates and markets, international trade negotiation, and international payments and accounting policy.

abstract: This research project investigates the dynamic interplay between social connectivity patterns and cognitive health trajectories in older adults, leveraging computational social science methods to model longitudinal aging processes. As global populations age, understanding how evolving social networks influence cognitive resilience—and vice versa—remains a critical gap. Traditional gerontological studies face limitations in capturing bidirectional feedback loops between multidimensional social variables (e.g., digital communication behaviors, intergenerational interactions) and neuropsychological outcomes at scale. We propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework enhanced by machine learning to simulate lifespan social-cognitive ecosystems, informed by multimodal data from the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) and real-time sensor-derived interaction metrics from a pilot cohort (n=420). High-performance computing resources are essential to manage three computational challenges: 1) Parallelized parameter space exploration for ABM validation against longitudinal observational data, 2) Training graph neural networks on temporal multiplex networks representing diverse relationship types and communication channels, and 3) Running counterfactual simulations of community-level interventions under demographic constraints. The computational architecture will integrate Python-based Mesa for ABM development, PyTorch Geometric for dynamic network analysis, and SLURM-managed workflows for large-scale sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation platform for testing "social prescription" strategies, quantitative evidence on network structure thresholds associated with cognitive risk mitigation, and methodological advances in modeling aging as a complex adaptive system. By bridging computational social science with gerontology, this work aims to inform personalized and population-level strategies for maintaining cognitive health through social infrastructure optimization.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences and psychology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the historical evolution of ethical frameworks in medical decision-making by analyzing large-scale, multilingual corpora of primary sources spanning religious texts, philosophical treatises, medical literature, and patient narratives from 1600–1950. While qualitative scholarship has explored localized case studies, there remains a critical gap in systematically mapping how cultural, spiritual, and scientific values intersected to shape care practices across temporal and geographic boundaries. The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to process over 10 million pages of digitized materials through natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical language variants and OCR imperfections. Custom transformer models will classify ethical themes (e.g., autonomy, beneficence, sanctity of life) while tracking semantic shifts in key terms like “healing,” “suffering,” and “duty” across epochs. Graph neural networks will model the diffusion of ideas between medical, religious, and literary communities. By integrating computational text analysis with hermeneutic frameworks from health humanities, this work aims to 1) identify previously unrecognized patterns in the prioritization of ethical principles during major medical paradigm shifts, 2) map how colonial exchanges and technological innovations reconfigured value systems, and 3) generate publicly accessible annotated datasets bridging historical context with modern AI/ML workflows. The scale and linguistic complexity of the corpus necessitate HPC resources for distributed training of domain-specific language models, large-scale sentiment and topic coherence analysis, and 3D visualization of concept networks across time. Outcomes will provide empirical foundations for contemporary debates on culturally responsive care while demonstrating methodological innovations for computational humanities. This interdisciplinary approach advances both health humanities scholarship and NLP techniques for historical texts, with implications for medical education, policy, and AI ethics.
cip_definition: A program that explores the ethical, historical, literary, philosophical, and religious dimensions of medicine or health. Includes instruction in art, cultural studies, economics, ethics, history, literature, medical anthropology, philosophy, religion and spiritual thought, science and technology, visual art, and writing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational networks and cultural impacts of 19th-century Protestant medical missions in colonial Southeast Asia, a topic situated at the intersection of missionary studies, colonial history, and digital humanities. While archival records—including correspondence, mission reports, and indigenous oral histories—document the role of medical missionaries in mediating cross-cultural encounters, these sources remain fragmented across repositories and languages, hindering systematic analysis of their social and ideological influence. The project addresses this gap by constructing a unified digital corpus of over 50,000 multilingual texts and ethnographic records, paired with geospatial data on mission stations and regional disease patterns. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) to track shifts in missionary rhetoric and indigenous responses over time, network analysis to map relationships between missions, colonial administrations, and local communities, and agent-based modeling to simulate the diffusion of medical practices and religious ideologies. HPC resources are critical for processing non-Latin script texts (e.g., Jawi, Hanunó'o), training custom transformer models for low-resource languages, and running large-scale simulations of cultural exchange dynamics. Expected outcomes include a public database of annotated missionary records, visualizations of mission networks’ adaptive strategies, and new frameworks for quantifying the interplay between humanitarian rhetoric and colonial power structures. By integrating computational tools with critical mission studies, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary scholarship on how religiously motivated aid infrastructures shaped—and were reshaped by—globalization processes, offering methodological precedents for analyzing complex historical systems through data-driven humanities research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of religious outreach, social service and proselytization, and that prepares individuals for mission vocations. Includes instruction in theology, evangelism, preaching, medical and social mission work, missionary education, missionary aviation, emergency services, legal and political aspects of working in other countries, and preparation for ordination as missionaries.

abstract: Dental pathologies such as caries, periodontitis, and oral cancer arise from complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and environmental factors. Despite advances in clinical dentistry, the mechanistic underpinnings of these interactions remain poorly understood, particularly at the spatial and temporal scales relevant to disease progression. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model oral microbiome dynamics, host-tissue interactions, and the efficacy of therapeutic interventions. We will integrate multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) from clinical cohorts with high-resolution imaging and longitudinal patient records to construct predictive computational models. Agent-based modeling and machine learning frameworks will be employed to simulate microbial community behaviors under varying conditions, including biofilm formation, pH fluctuations, and antimicrobial treatments. Additionally, finite element analysis will be used to evaluate biomechanical stress distributions in dental restorations and implants, optimizing designs for durability and biocompatibility. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallel processing for parameter optimization, sensitivity analyses, and 3D visualization of microbial-tissue interfaces. Expected outcomes include identifying critical biomarkers for early disease detection, predicting therapeutic failure risks, and informing personalized treatment plans. By elucidating the systems-level drivers of oral diseases, this research will advance translational dentistry, enabling data-driven clinical decisions and innovative preventive strategies. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the project’s data volume (>500 TB of multi-modal datasets) and computational complexity, particularly for real-time simulations of microbial evolution and host-pathogen cross-talk. This work aligns with the program’s focus on integrating biomedical sciences with clinical practice, directly contributing to improved diagnostic tools, restorative materials, and ethical patient care standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of dentistry/dental medicine, encompassing the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, and adjacent structures and their impact on the human body and health. Includes instruction in the basic biomedical sciences, occlusion, dental health and prevention, oral pathology, cariology, operative dentistry, oral radiology, principles of the various dental specialties, pain management, oral medicine, clinic and health care management, patient counseling, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural and gendered dynamics of Polish diaspora communities through the analysis of digitized archival materials, oral histories, and multimedia artifacts. While existing scholarship has mapped broad migration patterns, significant gaps remain in understanding how localized cultural practices, gender roles, and intergenerational memory have evolved within dispersed Polish communities since the mid-20th century. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and heterogeneity of available data, including multilingual texts, audio recordings, and visual media from institutional and community archives. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of textual records, computer vision techniques to identify visual motifs in photographs and folk art, and network modeling to trace transnational connections across diaspora nodes. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect gendered language patterns and cultural references in Polish, Ukrainian, and Yiddish sources, while graph algorithms will map shifting community structures against geopolitical events. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to process over 500,000 digitized items from 15 collections within a 12-month period—a task infeasible on standard computing systems. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing cultural transmission pathways, computational models for intersectional analysis in Slavic studies, and new methodologies for ethically engaging with fragmented or contested heritage materials. This work will provide the first large-scale computational framework for analyzing Polish diasporic identity formation, offering insights into how cultural preservation interacts with gender dynamics in displaced communities. Results will directly inform curricular development in digital Polish studies and support collaborative preservation initiatives with diaspora organizations.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Poland and the current and historical inhabitants of the Polish lands, including borderlands, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling the dynamics of consumer decision-making in fragmented, hyperconnected markets, where traditional marketing analytics struggle to capture nonlinear interactions between micro-influencers, algorithmic recommendation systems, and real-time sentiment shifts. The research problem centers on the inadequacy of static, survey-based models to predict emergent purchasing patterns in environments dominated by short-form video platforms, decentralized social networks, and AI-curated content ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose implementing large-scale agent-based simulations that integrate behavioral economics principles with deep learning architectures trained on multi-platform digital trace data. The computational model will simulate 10^6+ heterogeneous agents across parameterized cultural contexts, incorporating temporal network effects from social media APIs, psychographic segmentation clusters, and stochastic shock events mimicking viral content spread. Key methodological challenges include developing adaptive attention allocation algorithms that reflect neurocognitive limits in information processing and implementing GPU-accelerated causal inference techniques to isolate platform-specific effects on conversion pathways. Expected outcomes include a novel metric system for quantifying brand resilience to information cascade disruptions and predictive benchmarks for budget allocation across hybrid human-AI influencer networks. By enabling real-time simulation of competing marketing interventions at unprecedented scale, this research aims to establish computational decision theater capabilities for strategic planners—addressing a critical gap in marketing science’s capacity to navigate post-platform consumer environments. The resource request specifically supports parallelized model validation against terascale datasets from partnered e-commerce platforms and comparative analysis of emergent market structures under varying regulatory AI transparency scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to undertake and manage the process of developing consumer audiences and moving products from producers to consumers. Includes instruction in buyer behavior and dynamics, principle of marketing research, demand analysis, cost-volume and profit relationships, pricing theory, marketing campaign and strategic planning, market segments, advertising methods, sales operations and management, consumer relations, retailing, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the emergent challenge of algorithmic bias in decentralized financial (DeFi) ecosystems, a critical yet underexplored issue at the intersection of computational finance, ethics, and business operations. As DeFi platforms—which automate financial transactions via smart contracts—gain prominence, their reliance on opaque, self-executing algorithms raises concerns about systemic inequities in loan approvals, asset pricing, and liquidity distribution. Traditional fairness frameworks, designed for centralized institutions, fail to account for the dynamic, multi-agent interactions and incentive structures inherent to decentralized systems. This project proposes a novel computational approach to model, detect, and mitigate bias in DeFi protocols using large-scale simulations and machine learning. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate heterogeneous agent behaviors (e.g., liquidity providers, arbitrage bots, retail users) across blockchain networks, while training deep learning models on historical transaction data to identify latent bias patterns. Agent-based modeling will replicate market microstructures under varying governance rules, enabling causal analysis of how protocol design choices propagate discrimination. Expected outcomes include a fairness auditing toolkit for DeFi developers, a taxonomy of bias amplification mechanisms in decentralized settings, and policy recommendations for algorithmic transparency standards. By bridging computational techniques with business ethics in an emerging financial paradigm, this work aims to establish governance frameworks that balance innovation with equity, reducing regulatory risks for enterprises operating in Web3 economies. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale blockchain datasets and running millions of parallelized market scenarios necessitate access to advanced GPU clusters and distributed storage systems, positioning HPC infrastructure as critical to achieving statistically robust insights.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of business, including the processes of interchanging goods and services (buying, selling and producing), business organization, and accounting as used in profit-making and nonprofit public and private institutions and agencies. The programs may prepare individuals to apply business principles and techniques in various occupational settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and optimize the efficacy of corporate communication strategies in large multinational organizations. The core problem lies in the escalating complexity of communication ecosystems—spanning internal memos, stakeholder reports, crisis responses, and digital platforms—and the lack of scalable frameworks to evaluate their coherence, sentiment alignment, and risk exposure. Traditional qualitative methods are insufficient to process the volume, velocity, and linguistic nuance of modern business communications, particularly in multilingual and multicultural contexts. To address this gap, the project proposes a computational linguistics approach combined with network analysis to model communication flows, detect latent inconsistencies, and simulate the downstream impact of messaging strategies. Key methods include training transformer-based language models on proprietary corporate text corpora (e.g., earnings calls, internal policy documents, social media interactions) to identify patterns in tone, semantic drift, and rhetorical effectiveness. Graph neural networks will map how information propagates across organizational hierarchies and external stakeholders, while agent-based simulations will test how hypothetical communication interventions affect reputational risk and operational alignment. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale text datasets, real-time sentiment tracking across 20+ languages, and iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization—tasks requiring GPU-accelerated clusters and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for auditing communication coherence, predictive models to flag high-risk messaging before deployment, and evidence-based guidelines for adaptive communication strategies in volatile markets. By bridging computational linguistics and corporate communications, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven decision-making in business messaging, with implications for crisis management, brand resilience, and cross-cultural stakeholder engagement.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying horizontal gene transfer (HGT) dynamics in microbial-eukaryotic symbiotic systems, a critical driver of adaptation and evolutionary innovation in microbial communities. Despite advances in identifying HGT events, the regulatory networks and host-symbiont interactions that govern these processes remain poorly characterized, particularly in non-model eukaryotes. We propose to address this gap by analyzing large-scale genomic and epigenomic datasets from microbial communities associated with anaerobic protists, which exhibit high rates of HGT and unique organellar genome architectures. The research will employ comparative genomics to identify horizontally acquired regions, chromatin accessibility data to map epigenetic regulation, and machine learning models to predict HGT hotspots based on sequence features and host-symbiont metabolic dependencies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabase-scale metagenomic assemblies, performing phylogenetically aware alignment of 10,000+ microbial genomes, and simulating host-symbiont coevolutionary dynamics under varying environmental constraints. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved genetic elements facilitating cross-domain DNA integration, characterization of epigenetic barriers to foreign gene expression, and predictive models linking HGT frequency to symbiotic metabolic networks. These findings will advance fundamental understanding of genetic exchange at microbial-eukaryotic interfaces while providing insights into the evolution of organelle genomes and parasitic/symbiotic adaptation strategies. The requested computing allocation will enable genome-resolved analyses across unprecedented taxonomic breadth, overcoming current limitations in dataset size and complexity that restrict conventional computational workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of viruses, infectious agents, organelles, nuclear genomes, eubacteria, archaebacteria, and eukaryotic organisms. Includes instruction in molecular genetics and evolution, parasitic and symbiotic interaction at the genetic level, epigenetic phenomena, microbial interactions, and genomics.

abstract: Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) is critical for preventing neurological injury during high-risk surgeries, yet existing methods face challenges in real-time analysis of complex neurophysiological data streams, including electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and evoked potentials. Current systems often rely on threshold-based alerts or manual interpretation, introducing latency and variability in detecting early signs of neural compromise. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a machine learning-driven framework for real-time, multimodal data integration and predictive analytics. The primary research problem centers on the computational demands of processing high-resolution, time-sensitive neurophysiological signals while simultaneously training and deploying adaptive models to identify pathological patterns. To achieve this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized signal processing pipelines and deep neural networks capable of analyzing terabytes of intraoperative data with millisecond-level latency. Key computational steps include noise reduction via wavelet transforms, feature extraction across temporal and spectral domains, and ensemble modeling to predict adverse neurological events. The HPC environment will enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization of convolutional and recurrent neural networks using retrospective datasets from 2,000+ surgical cases, followed by validation in simulated real-time scenarios. Expected outcomes include a deployable model suite that reduces false-positive alerts by ≥30% compared to current standards while improving detection sensitivity for ischemic and mechanical insults. Success in this work would directly enhance surgical decision-making, minimize postoperative deficits, and establish a scalable infrastructure for integrating emerging neuromonitoring modalities. The requested computing resources are essential to manage the iterative training of resource-intensive models, real-time data throughput, and multi-institutional collaboration, ultimately advancing precision in neuromonitoring technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to become neuromonitoring technicians who analyze, monitor, and record nervous system function to promote the effective treatment of pathological conditions. Includes instruction in EEG technology, EMG technology, anatomy, and neuroanatomy.

abstract: Cardiovascular complications are a leading cause of morbidity in cancer patients, yet the mechanisms linking tumor progression to systemic vascular dysfunction remain poorly understood. This project seeks to elucidate how solid tumors mechanically impair vascular function, driving arterial remodeling and cardiac stress. We propose a multiscale computational framework integrating finite element modeling of tumor-induced vascular compression with computational fluid dynamics simulations of pulsatile blood flow in deformable arterial networks. High-performance computing resources are critical to resolve the coupled mechanical and hemodynamic stresses across spatially heterogeneous tumor microenvironments. The model will incorporate patient-derived imaging data to reconstruct tumor-vascular anatomies and validate against clinical measurements of arterial stiffness and cardiac output. By simulating the dynamic interplay between tumor growth kinetics and vascular adaptation, we aim to identify biomechanical thresholds that trigger heart failure in cancer patients. Expected outcomes include predictive biomarkers for early detection of cardiovascular decline and mechanistic insights into tumor-mediated vascular remodeling. This work bridges oncology and cardiovascular physiology, informing strategies to mitigate cardiac complications in cancer therapy.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and functioning of the heart, vascular system, and blood in animals and human beings and the disorders and diseases associated with the cardiovascular system. Includes instruction in cardiovascular physiology, blood physiology, vasculature, vascular metabolism, neural control of cardiovascular function, microvascular permeability and membrane transport, cardiac contraction mechanisms, homeostasis, and applications to topics such as arteriosclerosis, heart disease, diabetes, vascular remodeling, transplantation, transfusion, and pacemakers and artificial organs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel investigation into the psychological impacts of urban built environments on stress and social behavior—a critical yet underexplored area in environmental psychology. Traditional methods in this field often rely on small-scale surveys or observational studies, limiting the ability to model complex, dynamic interactions between environmental variables (e.g., noise levels, green space density, architectural layout) and human behavioral outcomes at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and geospatial analysis to simulate how diverse urban configurations influence stress responses and social connectivity. The ABM component will simulate population-level interactions within high-resolution 3D urban models, incorporating psychophysiological data (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels) to parameterize stress dynamics. ML algorithms will analyze large-scale datasets from wearable sensors, public health records, and environmental sensors to identify nonlinear relationships between environmental features and psychological outcomes. Geospatial tools will map these relationships across varying urban contexts. The computational intensity of simultaneously modeling millions of agent interactions, training predictive ML models on heterogeneous data, and processing high-dimensional geospatial layers necessitates HPC resources for parallelization and memory management. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying urban design features that mitigate stress and foster social cohesion, (2) open-source tools for simulating environment-behavior dynamics, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for urban planners and policymakers. By bridging computational scalability with psychological theory, this work aims to transform how environmental psychology informs equitable, health-promoting design—a priority in counseling and applied psychology. The requested resources will enable unprecedented resolution in analyzing how everyday environments shape mental well-being at population scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of behavioral interactions between human beings and the environment in individual and group contexts, and ways to improve them. Includes instruction in contextual theory; statistics; physiological, social, and psychological responses to natural and technological hazards and disease; environmental perception and cognition; loneliness and stress; and psychological aspects of environmental design and planning.

abstract: The increasing sophistication of adversarial artificial intelligence (AI) in cyber warfare necessitates advanced computational approaches to develop resilient defense mechanisms. Current military cyber defense systems, reliant on static rule-based methodologies, struggle to counter dynamically evolving AI-driven threats capable of adaptive attack vectors and obfuscated infiltration tactics. This project seeks to address this critical gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and mitigate adversarial AI strategies within contested electronic battlefields. The research will employ a multi-pronged computational methodology, combining generative adversarial networks (GANs) to emulate adversarial behavior, reinforcement learning algorithms to train adaptive defense agents, and large-scale network simulations replicating tactical military environments. Key objectives include the identification of latent vulnerabilities in existing cyber-physical infrastructure, the development of real-time threat detection frameworks optimized for low-latency operational constraints, and the validation of countermeasure efficacy against synthetic and historically modeled attack campaigns. By integrating domain-specific constraints—such as electromagnetic spectrum limitations, satellite communication interdependencies, and rules of engagement compliance—the project aims to produce operationally viable defense protocols. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated vulnerability assessment, benchmarks for AI-driven cyber warfare performance metrics, and policy recommendations for the ethical deployment of autonomous cyber defense systems. This work will directly enhance the resilience of military networks against next-generation threats while informing the doctrinal integration of AI capabilities in cyber-electronic operations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the technological and operation aspects of information warfare, including cyber attack and cyber defense. Includes instruction in computer and network security, cryptography, computer forensics, systems security engineering, software applications, threat and vulnerability assessment, wireless networks and satellite communications, tactical and strategic planning, legal and ethical issues, and cyber warfare systems development and acquisition.

abstract: This project seeks to address large-scale stochastic optimization challenges in dynamic operational systems, where resource allocation decisions must adapt to real-time uncertainties while integrating human expertise. Such problems arise in logistics, healthcare operations, and supply chain management, where traditional deterministic models fail to capture variability in demand, service times, or disruptions. The research will develop and validate computationally intensive models that combine multi-stage stochastic programming with human-in-the-loop decision rules, enabling adaptive resource allocation under partial observability. The core computational challenge involves solving high-dimensional optimization problems with nested recourse decisions and nonlinear constraints, which exceed the capabilities of standard solvers. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid decomposition framework leveraging parallelizable Benders decomposition and scenario reduction techniques, augmented by reinforcement learning to approximate human decision policies. The implementation will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources for distributed memory parallelism to manage scenario trees with >10^4 branches and real-time simulation of decision pathways. Validation will involve Monte Carlo simulations across synthetic and real-world datasets, including hospital bed allocation during demand surges and dynamic routing for last-mile delivery networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable methodology for embedding human expertise in stochastic optimization models, (2) open-source implementations of parallel decomposition algorithms, and (3) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational efficiency against commercial solvers. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling memory-intensive scenario ensembles and achieving wall-clock times compatible with operational decision cycles. This work will advance operations research capabilities in human-integrated systems while providing practical tools for organizations managing resources under uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems.

abstract: Urban transportation systems face complex challenges in balancing economic efficiency, social equity, environmental sustainability, and spatial accessibility. Traditional planning methods often struggle to integrate these multidimensional factors at scale, particularly in rapidly growing metropolitan regions where dynamic population shifts, climate risks, and infrastructure interdependencies compound decision-making complexity. This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework for evaluating equitable and sustainable transportation policies using high-performance computing (HPC). The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate travel demand patterns across diverse socioeconomic groups, coupled with geospatial optimization algorithms to assess infrastructure investment scenarios under environmental constraints. Large-scale datasets—including anonymized mobile device GPS traces, transit ridership records, emissions inventories, and climate projection data—will be processed using distributed computing techniques to parameterize models and quantify system-wide tradeoffs. Machine learning methods will enhance scenario forecasting by identifying nonlinear relationships between land-use policies, transportation behaviors, and equity outcomes. By leveraging parallelized computations, the project will enable real-time sensitivity analyses of policy interventions across multiple sustainability metrics, such as greenhouse gas reductions, accessibility disparities, and fiscal feasibility. The computational outputs will inform a decision-support tool for planners to visualize tradeoffs between competing priorities under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include novel methodologies for embedding equity considerations into infrastructure resilience planning and evidence-based recommendations for prioritizing transit investments in underserved communities. This work addresses critical gaps in public administration by advancing scalable, data-driven approaches to multicriteria transportation planning, with direct applications to regional climate action plans and federal infrastructure funding guidelines. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive simulations, training predictive models on heterogeneous datasets, and optimizing runtime for iterative scenario testing across hypothetical population growth and climate risk pathways.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the economic, social, spatial, and environmental aspects of transportation and infrastructure planning. Includes instruction in economics, environmental analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, risk analysis, transportation economics, transportation evaluation, transportation planning, transportation policy, and urban transportation planning.

abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed generation into power grids has introduced unprecedented operational complexity, particularly in hybrid power plants that combine traditional thermal generation with intermittent renewables. Current models for optimizing real-time dispatch and stability in such systems struggle to account for the dynamic coupling between electrical grid behavior, thermodynamic inertia in thermal units, and stochastic renewable outputs. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, multi-timescale simulation framework to address these interdependencies, enabling predictive optimization of hybrid plant operations under fluctuating grid conditions. The research will employ a coupled computational approach combining transient stability analysis, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of thermal unit responses, and machine learning-based forecasting of renewable generation patterns. High-performance computing resources are critical to resolve the temporal and spatial scales involved, from sub-second electrical transients to hour-ahead operational planning, while maintaining grid-code compliance and minimizing wear-and-tear costs. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers for differential-algebraic equations governing grid dynamics, GPU-accelerated CFD simulations of steam cycle thermal lag, and ensemble forecasting techniques for renewable uncertainty quantification. Expected outcomes include novel control strategies that exploit thermal inertia as grid-stabilizing energy storage, predictive maintenance schedules informed by transient-induced mechanical stresses, and operational protocols for maintaining frequency regulation during renewable ramping events. This work aims to establish a computational foundation for next-generation hybrid power plant design, directly supporting the transition to low-inertia power systems while preserving grid reliability. The resulting models and algorithms will be validated against operational data from a partner utility, with potential applications in retrofit planning for existing fossil-fuel plants and standardization of hybrid plant grid interconnection requirements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan electrical systems and modify existing electrical systems that generate and use large amounts of electricity required for distribution networks that are economical, safe, and functional. Includes instruction in alternative/renewable energy systems; calculus; circuit analysis; electrical power systems and industry practices; electrical system design; microprocessor architecture; motor control systems; power electronics operation, planning and protection; programmable logic controllers; and project management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing hybrid quantum-classical machine learning (ML) models for scalable deployment on emerging quantum computing architectures. While quantum ML algorithms promise advantages in areas such as pattern recognition and optimization, their integration with classical neural networks introduces complex parameter optimization landscapes and hardware-software co-design constraints. Current simulation frameworks struggle to efficiently model these systems at scale, particularly when accounting for real-world noise profiles and heterogeneous computing architectures. We propose developing a novel computational framework that combines tensor network simulations with gradient-based optimization techniques, accelerated through high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The methodology will implement parameterized quantum circuits as neural network layers using modified versions of PyTorch and TensorFlow, augmented with custom CUDA kernels for quantum state evolution simulations. Key innovations include a distributed optimization protocol that partitions parameter updates across CPU-GPU clusters and a noise-aware compiler that maps logical circuits to target hardware configurations. The computational demands necessitate large-scale parallelism for simultaneous training of multiple model variants (≥10^3 parameter sets) and real-time tomography of quantum state dynamics. Expected outcomes include: (1) quantitative benchmarks comparing hybrid quantum-classical architectures against classical baselines in image classification and molecular property prediction tasks, (2) open-source tools for resource-aware deployment of quantum ML models, and (3) fundamental insights into the memory-time tradeoffs inherent in distributed quantum circuit simulations. This work will advance the interdisciplinary integration of computer science principles (algorithm design, complexity analysis) and computer engineering priorities (hardware mapping, performance optimization), directly contributing to the development of practical quantum ML systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for overcoming current memory bottlenecks in full-scale simulations and enabling timely comparisons across different quantum processor topologies.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of computer science and computer engineering principles or a specialization which includes expertise in both computer engineering and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing instructional design and pedagogical decision-making in social science teacher education. A critical challenge in preparing educators to teach social science subjects—such as history, geography, and civics—is understanding how emerging technologies and data-driven approaches can enhance the scalability and personalization of teacher training. Current methods for analyzing classroom interactions, curriculum efficacy, and trainee performance often rely on small-scale qualitative studies or coarse quantitative metrics, limiting generalizability and real-time adaptability. To address this gap, we propose developing computational models that simulate diverse classroom environments and teacher-student dynamics. These agent-based models will integrate multimodal datasets, including video recordings of classroom instruction, longitudinal student assessment data, and demographic variables from partner K-12 schools. Machine learning techniques, such as natural language processing for analyzing discourse patterns and reinforcement learning for adaptive pedagogical strategies, will be applied to identify optimal teaching practices under varying socioeconomic and institutional constraints. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of data (terabytes of unstructured video and text) and the complexity of parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameterized scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for predicting the impact of specific instructional interventions on student engagement and critical thinking skills, (2) evidence-based recommendations for integrating computational tools into teacher training curricula, and (3) open-source software modules to help educators visualize and adapt model-derived strategies. By bridging social science education research with advanced computational methods, this project aims to generate scalable, equitable solutions for improving teacher preparedness in an era of rapidly evolving educational demands.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific social science subjects and programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of next-generation computational cinematography tools, addressing the growing demand for real-time, high-fidelity visual storytelling in film and multimedia production. Traditional workflows for rendering complex lighting environments, dynamic camera motion, and photorealistic virtual scenes remain computationally prohibitive, limiting creative experimentation and scalability in previsualization and post-production. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes a hybrid approach combining physics-based simulation, neural rendering, and distributed parallel processing. Using GPU-accelerated ray tracing and generative adversarial networks (GANs), the team will develop a framework for simulating adaptive lighting systems and camera behaviors that respond dynamically to scene context, optimizing resource allocation across multi-node clusters. Additionally, the project will implement machine learning models trained on high-resolution cinematic datasets to automate labor-intensive tasks such as depth-of-field synthesis and temporal coherence in compositing. By integrating these methods into an open-source pipeline compatible with industry-standard tools, the research aims to reduce rendering times for 4K/8K sequences by 40–60% while preserving artistic control. Outcomes will be validated through collaborative case studies with filmmakers, measuring gains in creative flexibility and workflow efficiency. The computational infrastructure requested will enable large-scale testing of multi-sensor data fusion (e.g., LiDAR and RGB-D captures) for immersive virtual production environments, directly contributing to pedagogical innovations in cinematography education. This work bridges gaps between artistic intent and technical feasibility, offering novel methodologies for resource-constrained productions while advancing scholarly understanding of computational aesthetics in visual media.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to communicate dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the making and producing of films and videos. Includes instruction in theory of film, film technology and equipment operation, film production, film directing, film editing, cinematographic art, film audio, techniques for making specific types of films and/or videos, media technologies, computer image making, multi-media production, and the planning and management of film/video operations.

abstract: Aging populations present complex challenges that intersect biological, psychological, and social domains, yet existing models often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between these factors. This project seeks to advance gerontological research by developing an agent-based computational framework to simulate how social connectivity, health behaviors, and cognitive decline co-evolve over the adult lifespan. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding nonlinear feedback mechanisms between social isolation and health deterioration—a phenomenon disproportionately affecting older adults but inadequately modeled using traditional longitudinal or compartmental approaches. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the simulation will integrate multimodal datasets including neuroimaging-derived cognitive trajectories, real-world social interaction metrics from wearable devices, and clinical health records from aging cohort studies. Computational challenges include scaling adaptive network algorithms to model time-varying social ties across 100,000+ synthetic agents, implementing neural network-based decision modules for health behavior choices, and conducting sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces exceeding 10^8 combinations. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical inflection points where declining social engagement accelerates health risks, (2) predictive validation of community-level intervention strategies, and (3) open-source tools for simulating aging populations under diverse policy scenarios. By bridging computational social science with gerontological health research, this work will provide novel insights into how macro-level aging trends emerge from micro-level social and biological interactions, ultimately informing targeted strategies to enhance healthspan in diverse aging populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the linguistic and cultural interconnectedness of Ural-Altaic and Central Asian communities through large-scale textual and artifact datasets. The research problem centers on tracing the evolution of shared cultural narratives and linguistic features across historically mobile populations in Inner Asia, particularly along the Silk Road corridor, where dynamic interactions between Turkic, Mongolian, and other groups remain understudied due to computational limitations. Current scholarship lacks integrative models that account for both temporal depth and spatial diffusion of cultural practices, a gap this project aims to address. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) for analyzing digitized historical manuscripts in Old Turkic, Classical Mongolian, and Chagatai with network analysis to map semantic and thematic parallels across oral traditions. A custom convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained to detect visual patterns in archaeological artifacts (textiles, epigraphy) that correlate with linguistic data, requiring parallelized processing of high-resolution imagery. Phylogenetic algorithms will model language divergence timelines, while geospatial clustering techniques will identify cultural contact zones. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10th–18th century sources, enabling comparative analysis at unprecedented scale. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing cultural-linguistic exchange networks and their relationship to historical trade routes, climatic shifts, and migration patterns. This work will provide new methodologies for synthesizing material culture and textual evidence in area studies, offering insights into how shared heritage elements persisted despite political fragmentation. Results will directly support endangered language revitalization initiatives and inform contemporary cross-cultural policy frameworks in Central Asia by clarifying historical precedents for intergroup collaboration.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries of Inner/Central Asia, including the Turkic and Mongolian inhabitants of the Caspian, Amur, Tien Shan, Baikal, Gobi, Siberian, and Manchurian areas and the historical Silk Road, in terms of their past and present development.

abstract: The increasing complexity of regulatory workflows for novel biomedical products—including gene therapies, personalized medicines, and AI-driven diagnostics—demands advanced computational tools to analyze high-dimensional datasets and simulate regulatory scenarios. Traditional methods for evaluating safety, efficacy, and compliance struggle to scale with the volume and heterogeneity of modern clinical, genomic, and post-market surveillance data, creating bottlenecks in product development and regulatory review. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and scalable analytics frameworks tailored to regulatory science. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) constructing machine learning models to predict adverse event risks and optimize clinical trial designs using multi-omic datasets, electronic health records (EHRs), and real-world evidence, and (2) simulating regulatory decision-making processes under varying compliance scenarios via agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will employ distributed data processing (Apache Spark), deep learning architectures (PyTorch), and large-scale parameter sweeps to assess the impact of manufacturing variances, patient subpopulations, and protocol deviations on regulatory outcomes. By parallelizing these tasks across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce simulation times for complex regulatory pathways from weeks to days while improving model accuracy through integration of high-resolution datasets. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for automated compliance gap analysis, dynamic risk prediction, and scenario-based FDA submission planning. These resources will enhance the capacity of regulatory professionals to navigate evolving requirements for emerging therapies, accelerating time-to-market without compromising safety. The work directly supports public health by enabling data-driven, proactive regulatory strategies for cutting-edge biomedical innovations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the regulatory process for companies innovating and developing cutting edge products in science, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medicine. Includes instruction in regulatory affairs, clinical documentation, human and animal subject protection, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, data management and analysis, good manufacturing practices, and quality management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in processing large-scale geospatial datasets for modern surveying engineering applications, including high-resolution terrain modeling, real-time deformation monitoring, and multi-sensor data fusion. The increasing resolution of satellite imagery, LiDAR point clouds, and drone-based photogrammetry has strained traditional computing infrastructures, limiting the spatial and temporal resolution achievable in critical applications such as infrastructure resilience assessment and land-use change detection. We propose to develop parallelized workflows for error-adjusted surface reconstruction, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize iterative least-squares adjustments and machine learning-based feature extraction algorithms. The computational approach will focus on three pillars: (1) GPU-accelerated processing of multi-temporal InSAR (Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar) data to detect sub-centimeter ground displacements, (2) distributed computing frameworks for fusing terrestrial laser scans with aerial photogrammetry in urban environments, and (3) uncertainty propagation modeling across heterogeneous geospatial datasets. These methods will be validated through case studies examining landslide-prone regions and urban utility corridor monitoring. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining the millimeter-level precision required for engineering-grade surveys. Expected outcomes include open-source computational tools for scalable geospatial data fusion, improved protocols for real-time monitoring of critical infrastructure, and enhanced predictive models for terrain stability analysis. By advancing computational methodologies in surveying engineering, this work will directly support evidence-based decision-making in civil infrastructure development, climate adaptation planning, and natural hazard mitigation, while training the next generation of surveying professionals in HPC-enabled geospatial analysis techniques.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the determination of the location, elevations, and alignment of natural and manmade topographic features. Includes instruction in property line location, surveying, surface measurement, aerial and terrestrial photogrammetry, remote sensing, satellite imagery, global positioning systems, computer applications, and photographic data processing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a real-time adaptive middleware framework for tactile-augmented reality (tAR) platforms, addressing the computational challenges of synchronizing dynamic tactile feedback with heterogeneous sensor arrays in resource-constrained environments. Current tAR systems struggle with latency and cross-platform compatibility due to the variable computational demands of multi-modal tactile inputs (e.g., pressure, temperature, vibration) and the need for deterministic response times under fluctuating workloads. The research will employ a hybrid computational architecture combining edge-based preprocessing clusters with cloud-hosted predictive models to optimize resource allocation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for simulating large-scale tAR environments, training physics-informed neural networks to predict tactile interaction patterns, and stress-testing dynamic load-balancing algorithms across GPU-accelerated nodes.
