Methods include the development of a platform-agnostic API for tactile data normalization, implementation of latency-aware task schedulers using reinforcement learning, and validation through biomechanical user interaction datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework capable of reducing perceptual latency by ≥40% in multi-user tAR scenarios while maintaining <5ms jitter across industrial and consumer-grade hardware. This work directly impacts emerging fields such as tactile teleoperation systems for hazardous environments and adaptive assistive technologies, bridging gaps between real-time systems design, human-computer interaction, and distributed computing paradigms. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale validation of fault-tolerant tactile data pipelines and energy-efficient scheduling strategies critical for next-generation embodied computing platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, develop, and implement software-based solutions for specific business and consumer platforms including industrial, game, mobile, tactile, and web platforms. Includes instruction in computer programming, computer hardware, data structures, database theory, maintenance, operating systems, project management, software development, and systems analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in French language pedagogy through the development of a computational framework for analyzing second language acquisition patterns in classroom settings. A critical challenge in French teacher education lies in identifying and addressing systematic gaps in learners’ grammatical, phonological, and sociolinguistic competencies, particularly in multilingual classrooms where interference from learners’ first languages complicates instructional strategies. Current manual analysis methods are time-intensive and lack scalability, limiting educators’ ability to derive actionable insights from large datasets of student interactions. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to analyze spoken and written French learner corpora. The project will process audio recordings, written assignments, and real-time classroom interaction data from diverse learner cohorts using transformer-based models fine-tuned for error detection in French. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multimodal data streams, training of domain-specific language models, and simulation of language acquisition trajectories under varied pedagogical conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable toolkit for diagnosing learner-specific and cohort-wide challenges in French proficiency, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive teaching strategies targeting common error patterns, and (3) open-access datasets annotated for grammatical, phonological, and pragmatic features. By bridging computational linguistics and teacher education, this work aims to empower French language educators with data-driven tools to personalize instruction and improve learning outcomes in K-12 and postsecondary contexts. The integration of HPC-driven analytics into teacher training programs has the potential to transform how future educators approach curriculum design, assessment, and intervention in French language classrooms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach French language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Improving the efficiency and precision of agricultural animal breeding programs requires advanced genomic selection strategies capable of integrating complex genetic, environmental, and phenotypic datasets. Current approaches often rely on simplified models that fail to fully capture non-additive genetic effects, gene-environment interactions, or the contributions of structural genomic variation, limiting their predictive accuracy. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-resolution computational framework to optimize breeding decisions for dairy cattle, leveraging whole-genome sequencing data, longitudinal productivity metrics, and environmental covariates. The research will employ Bayesian neural networks and ensemble machine learning models to predict breeding values, augmented by population-scale simulations to evaluate long-term genetic diversity outcomes under different selection scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational load, as the analyses involve iterative training on terabytes of genomic data, stochastic simulation of breeding populations across 20+ generations, and multi-objective optimization to balance traits such as milk yield, disease resistance, and climate adaptability. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for genotype-to-phenotype prediction, validated strategies to mitigate inbreeding depression in closed herds, and actionable insights into allele-specific responses to heat stress in subtropical regions. By enabling more accurate modeling of complex genetic architectures, this work will directly support breeders in accelerating genetic gain while maintaining population health—a critical step toward global food security amid shifting climate conditions and evolving agricultural demands. The proposed computational pipeline will also provide a template for integrating heterogeneous data types in livestock genomics, with potential applications across species and production systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural animal health, the development of new animal breeds, and the selective improvement of agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, animal health, animal husbandry, and biotechnology.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into traditional crafts such as leatherworking and upholstery remains underexplored, despite its potential to revolutionize material innovation, sustainability, and design precision. This project seeks to address critical gaps in the empirical understanding of leather biomechanics, adhesive interactions, and textile-layered composites through high-performance computing (HPC). Current manual and trial-and-error approaches to material selection, stress testing, and pattern optimization are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in scalability. To overcome these challenges, we propose a computational framework leveraging molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) models to predict material behavior under diverse environmental and mechanical conditions. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of collagen fiber networks in leather substrates, multi-physics modeling of adhesive curing processes, and topology optimization of upholstery structures for enhanced durability and ergonomics. Concurrently, ML algorithms will be trained on simulation-derived datasets to identify non-intuitive correlations between material treatments (e.g., tanning agents, stitching densities) and functional outcomes (e.g., tensile strength, moisture resistance). The project’s computational outputs will be validated through physical prototyping and mechanical testing, creating a closed-loop feedback system to refine predictive models. Anticipated outcomes include the development of open-access simulation tools tailored for artisanal industries, data-driven guidelines for sustainable material substitution, and novel composite designs that minimize waste while maximizing performance. By bridging computational science and traditional craftsmanship, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for resource-efficient, innovation-driven practices in leatherworking and upholstery, with implications for heritage preservation, circular economies, and adaptive manufacturing in small-scale technical fields.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in leatherworking and upholstering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing integration of variable renewable energy sources into modern power grids has introduced complex challenges in maintaining system stability, efficiency, and resilience. Existing simulation tools often lack the capability to model dynamic interactions between distributed energy resources, storage systems, and demand-side technologies at scale, particularly under real-world operational uncertainties. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize hybrid energy systems in scenarios involving high renewable penetration. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized, multi-timescale simulations that integrate machine learning-driven load forecasting, stochastic optimization for resource allocation, and physics-based modeling of thermal-electrochemical storage systems. Key computational challenges include resolving transient grid behaviors at sub-second resolutions, managing large parameter spaces in system configuration optimization, and quantifying propagation of uncertainties across cyber-physical grid components. The proposed framework will employ adaptive mesh refinement for partial differential equation solutions in storage system modeling, distributed computing for Monte Carlo-based reliability analyses, and graph neural networks to capture spatial-temporal dependencies in grid dynamics. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for real-time adaptive control of hybrid microgrids, validated against experimental data from partner testbeds, and open-source tools for risk-aware planning of renewable energy infrastructure. This work will provide critical insights into scalability constraints of decarbonized energy systems and directly inform the design of next-generation grid management protocols. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of rare but high-impact scenarios—such as multi-day renewable generation droughts or cascading failures in multi-carrier energy networks—the project aims to advance the operational feasibility of high-renewable power systems while maintaining cost and reliability targets. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current bottlenecks in simulation throughput and to achieve the granularity required for technology-agnostic system optimization.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Plant diseases pose significant threats to global food security, yet predicting pathogen dispersal in heterogeneous agricultural landscapes remains a critical challenge. Traditional epidemiological models often oversimplify interactions between environmental variables, host spatial arrangements, and pathogen life cycles, limiting their utility for real-world disease management. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based computational framework to simulate spatiotemporal dynamics of airborne fungal pathogen spread (e.g., *Puccinia* spp. in cereal crops) across diverse farming systems. The model will integrate multi-scale datasets including 3D canopy architecture from UAV LiDAR, microclimate sensor networks, soil moisture gradients, and regional wind patterns to quantify how localized physical barriers and planting configurations alter pathogen transmission. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize stochastic interactions across 10^6–10^7 agents representing individual spores, host plants, and environmental matrices at sub-meter resolution over growing seasons. Parallelized simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods to model turbulent spore transport and Markov chain Monte Carlo approaches to assess uncertainty in outbreak trajectories under climate variability. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of landscape design thresholds (e.g., intercropping density, windbreak porosity) that disrupt pathogen connectivity while maintaining yield, and (2) probabilistic risk maps linking early-season environmental signatures to late-season epidemic severity. By bridging gaps between phytopathology, fluid dynamics, and agricultural systems engineering, this work will provide actionable insights for spatially optimized disease intervention strategies, directly supporting resilient crop production. The computational framework will be open-sourced to enable adaptation to other pathosystems, fostering cross-disciplinary innovation in sustainable agriculture.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms from an agricultural perspective. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: Dental implant failure due to biomechanical incompatibility and microbial biofilm formation remains a critical challenge in restorative dentistry, with limited predictive tools to optimize patient-specific outcomes. This project proposes a computational biomechanics and machine learning approach to model the interplay between implant design, jawbone microarchitecture, and oral microbiome dynamics, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address this multiscale problem. Using anonymized clinical CT scans and intraoral microbiome sequencing data from a retrospective cohort of 450 patients, we will construct finite element models of mandibular bone stress distributions under varying occlusal loads and simulate bacterial adhesion patterns on titanium versus novel bioactive implant surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize atomic-scale interactions between oral pathogens (e.g., *Porphyromonas gingivalis*) and surface coatings containing antimicrobial peptides. A convolutional neural network trained on these multimodal datasets will predict long-term osseointegration success rates and infection risks based on individual anatomical features and microbial profiles. The HPC environment is essential for managing the 50+ TB dataset, running parallelized simulations across spatial scales (1 nm to 10 cm), and iterating deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for personalized implant selection, identification of optimal surface topographies to resist microbial colonization without compromising bone integration, and open-source simulation tools for educational use in pre-clinical dental training. This interdisciplinary integration of computational biomechanics, microbiology, and AI addresses an emerging niche in precision dental medicine, with potential applications in biomaterial development and adaptive treatment planning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in dentistry.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize adaptive sales strategies in dynamic, large-scale customer interaction environments. The core problem addressed is the inefficiency of traditional sales training frameworks, which rely on static, scenario-based models that fail to account for real-time behavioral variability, complex decision networks, and the nonlinear effects of psychological cues in buyer-seller interactions. Current approaches lack the computational power to simulate hyper-realistic, multi-agent environments where thousands of concurrent sales scenarios evolve through machine learning-driven customer avatars. The proposed computational methodology combines agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and reinforcement learning to create a sandbox environment simulating heterogeneous customer profiles, contextual market pressures, and multi-channel communication patterns. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of sales agent algorithms across diverse demographic and behavioral datasets, while preserving granular temporal resolution in interaction sequences. Key innovations include embedding psychometric trait inference within real-time dialogue simulations and quantifying the cascading impacts of micro-level sales tactics on macro-level pipeline performance. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting optimal persuasion pathways under constrained operational conditions (e.g., limited call time, quota pressures), as well as generative tools for scenario prototyping in sales training systems. The computational outputs will advance both academic understanding of cognitive-adaptive selling processes and practical applications in sales operations, particularly for industries requiring rapid response to volatile demand signals. By quantifying previously qualitative aspects of sales effectiveness—such as empathy modulation or urgency framing—this work establishes a foundation for data-driven sales skill optimization at previously unattainable scales.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to possess the skills associated with direct promotion of products and services to potential customers and to function as independent sales representatives and managers. Includes instruction in consumer psychology, image projection, public speaking and interpersonal communications, sales organization and operations, customer relations, professional standards and ethics, and applicable technical skills.

abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) face escalating challenges due to increasing patient volumes, resource constraints, and the critical need for rapid, data-driven decision-making. A key unmet need is the ability to predict patient outcomes and optimize care pathways in real time, particularly for high-acuity conditions such as sepsis, traumatic injury, and acute cardiovascular events. Existing predictive models often lack the granularity, scalability, or computational efficiency required for dynamic ED environments. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing and validating machine learning (ML) models to predict clinical deterioration, prioritize resource allocation, and personalize treatment strategies using multimodal data from electronic health records (EHRs), real-time vital sign streams, and imaging studies. The computational complexity of integrating heterogeneous data sources—spanning structured EHR entries, free-text clinical notes, and high-resolution physiological waveforms—necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose a hybrid deep learning framework combining transformer-based natural language processing for clinical text, convolutional networks for imaging analysis, and temporal models for continuous vital sign interpretation. These components will be integrated via ensemble methods to generate risk scores updated in real time. HPC infrastructure is critical for training these models on retrospective datasets (>500,000 ED encounters) and simulating operational workflows under varying patient influx scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include validated prediction tools for sepsis onset within 1–3 hours of triage, mortality risk stratification for trauma patients, and optimized bed assignment algorithms to reduce ED boarding times. Successful implementation will provide a scalable computational framework to enhance clinical decision-making, reduce preventable morbidity, and improve resource utilization in emergency care. The requested resources will enable processing of terabytes of multimodal data, parallelized hyperparameter optimization, and deployment of low-latency inference pipelines, which are infeasible with standard clinical computing systems. This work aligns with national priorities to integrate advanced analytics into emergency medicine, offering a template for data-driven acute care innovation.
cip_definition: Research focused on Emergency Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and optical mechanisms underlying age-related declines in dynamic visual processing, with a focus on how environmental factors such as low-contrast lighting and ocular aberrations exacerbate functional deficits. Current clinical models inadequately capture the interplay between corneal elasticity, lenticular opacity progression, and neural adaptation thresholds during motion perception. To address this, we propose developing a multiscale computational model integrating finite element simulations of anterior eye structures with psychophysically informed neural networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable iterative optimization of 1) ray-tracing algorithms that map age-dependent light scatter patterns onto retinal photoreceptor arrays, and 2) spatiotemporal models of cortical responses to degraded motion signals. The computational framework will be validated against longitudinal datasets of contrast sensitivity and eye-tracking metrics from ongoing clinical studies. Expected outcomes include predictive biomarkers for early-stage visuomotor decline and quantitative guidelines for adaptive lighting systems in age-related visual impairment. By leveraging parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for photon transport and GPU-accelerated neural population modeling, this work will establish the first unified platform correlating anterior eye biophysics with cortical compensation mechanisms under ecological viewing conditions. The requested resources will directly support parameter space exploration across 10^6+ simulated combinations of ocular parameters and environmental stressors, a computational load exceeding current institutional cluster capacities. Resultant datasets will inform targeted interventions to maintain functional vision in aging populations while advancing fundamental understanding of visuomotor resilience thresholds.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of vision, visual processes, and related phenomena and clinical research and treatment modalities. Includes instruction in ocular anatomy and physiology, microbiology of the eye, electrophysiology, neurophysiology, corneal physiology, photochemistry, psychophysics, visual biophysics and motor systems, sensory mechanisms and photoreception, eye circulation and metabolism, geometric and physical optics, ocular development across the life span, visual stimuli and perception, color vision, eye motility, biometrics and measurement techniques, visual pathology, and environmental issues.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a dynamic, agent-based simulation framework for optimizing consumer merchandising strategies in multi-channel retail environments. The research problem centers on the computational limitations of current retail management models, which struggle to integrate real-time consumer behavior data, supply chain variables, and competitive market dynamics at scale. Traditional approaches often rely on static or segmented datasets, leading to suboptimal inventory allocation, pricing decisions, and promotional campaign effectiveness. This project addresses these gaps by creating a unified computational model that simulates emergent consumer purchasing patterns across physical stores, e-commerce platforms, and mobile marketplaces. The proposed framework will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to process heterogeneous data streams—including IoT-enabled shelf sensors, social media sentiment analysis, and transactional histories—while incorporating stochastic elements of cultural trends and economic shocks. By utilizing GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines, the model will dynamically adjust merchandise mix recommendations and pricing tiers at hyperlocal levels, accounting for regional demographic shifts and sustainability preferences. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of reducing overstock waste by 15-25% in simulated retail networks while improving customer satisfaction metrics through personalized promotion timing. The computational demands of simulating millions of concurrent consumer agents across diverse market scenarios necessitate HPC resources for memory-intensive optimization tasks and validation against global retail datasets. This work bridges computational social science with retail operations management, establishing a novel methodology for data-driven consumer analytics that could redefine resource allocation paradigms in ethically conscious merchandising. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation modules tailored for non-technical retail strategists, advancing both academic research and industry practice in sustainable consumer engagement.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on product and service promotion from the perspective of individual and family consumers and that prepares individuals to function as consumer management and marketing consultants in for-profit and non-profit enterprises. Includes instruction in applied market research, consumer behavior, product sourcing and distribution, profitability, customer feedback and evaluation methods, promotion and retailing campaign development, and applications to specific domestic and international consumer markets.

abstract: The integration of multi-omics data, electronic health records (EHRs), and clinical trial datasets presents a critical challenge in translational research, where computational limitations hinder the ability to identify biomarkers, predict treatment responses, and personalize therapies for complex diseases. This project seeks to address these bottlenecks by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable frameworks for analyzing heterogeneous biomedical datasets. We propose a computational pipeline combining machine learning, network biology, and Bayesian hierarchical models to disentangle interactions between genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and clinical variables in patients with autoimmune disorders. Key components include federated learning architectures to preserve patient privacy during cross-institutional EHR analysis, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for imaging-derived phenotype classification, and agent-based simulations of immune cell signaling pathways. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of whole-genome sequencing data from 10,000+ participants, real-time integration of streaming sensor data from wearable devices in ongoing trials, and optimization of predictive models via hyperparameter tuning across GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of novel biomarker panels for early diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis and lupus, (2) predictive algorithms for treatment resistance in biologic therapies, and (3) an open-source platform for reproducible clinical-translational analysis workflows. By overcoming current limitations in data harmonization and computational scalability, this work will directly support precision medicine initiatives while establishing infrastructure for collaborative research across our clinical investigation network. The requested resources are essential given the project’s 800 TB multi-modal datasets, need for 24/7 job scheduling across 500+ concurrent nodes, and memory-intensive simulations of molecular interaction networks. Results will be disseminated through clinician-facing decision support tools, validation studies in prospective cohorts, and training modules for medical residents in computational research methods.
cip_definition: A program that prepares medical and health clinicians to combine knowledge from scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge, improve medical education, and bridge laboratory and clinical science into clinical practice. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, medical education and scientific writing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive analytics and machine learning models tailored to optimize children and youth library services. While libraries serving young populations collect vast amounts of data—including program attendance, material circulation, digital resource usage, and demographic information—existing tools for analyzing these datasets are often siloed, inefficient, or incapable of identifying nuanced patterns critical to service personalization. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating heterogeneous data streams to model engagement dynamics, predict program efficacy, and recommend culturally responsive resource allocation strategies. The computational approach will employ graph neural networks (GNNs) to map relationships between user behavior, program outcomes, and collection diversity, alongside natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze textual feedback from youth patrons and caregivers. These models will be trained on multi-year datasets from urban and rural library systems, incorporating privacy-preserving federated learning frameworks to address data sensitivity. The project will further utilize agent-based modeling to simulate the impact of proposed service changes on equitable access and long-term literacy outcomes. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time decision support, enabling librarians to dynamically adapt programming, collections, and outreach efforts. By quantifying the interplay between service design and community needs, this work aims to establish scalable, data-driven methodologies for enhancing equity in youth library services—a specialized niche intersecting information science, computational social research, and education technology. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets, iterating complex model architectures, and ensuring low-latency analysis in resource-constrained library environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide library and information services and programming for children and young adults. Includes instruction in information needs of children and young adults, resources and services for children and young adults, literature for youth, storytelling, multi-ethnic materials, library management, and information technology for librarians.

abstract: This project seeks to characterize the ecological and evolutionary drivers of zoonotic disease spillover in changing landscapes, with a focus on vector-borne pathogens in tropical regions. Rapid environmental shifts, including deforestation and climate variability, are altering host-vector-pathogen dynamics, yet the mechanisms underlying spillover risk remain poorly quantified. We propose to integrate spatially explicit ecological data, host movement patterns, and pathogen genomic variation into a unified modeling framework to identify high-risk interfaces for disease emergence. The research employs agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate multi-scale interactions between wildlife reservoirs, arthropod vectors, and human populations across heterogeneous landscapes. These models will incorporate satellite-derived land-use changes, climate projections, and field-collected data on host density and pathogen prevalence. A parallel component uses maximum entropy and machine learning approaches to map current and future habitat suitability for key vector species under multiple climate scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for parameterizing spatially resolved ABMs at ecologically relevant scales (1km² resolution across 100,000km² study regions), conducting ensemble simulations to capture uncertainty in climate and land-use trajectories, and analyzing pathogen phylogenies to infer transmission networks. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of landscape features amplifying cross-species transmission, 2) projections of emerging risk hotspots under coupled environmental and demographic change, and 3) evolutionary risk assessments of pathogen adaptation to novel hosts. The computational workflow requires large-memory nodes for genomic analyses and GPU acceleration for real-time visualization of spatiotemporal transmission patterns. By bridging ecological scaling principles with epidemiological theory, this work will advance predictive frameworks for preemptive surveillance and targeted intervention in resource-limited settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of disease, disability, and trauma patterns within and across populations and the development of health management mechanisms to prevent and control disease outbreaks and injurious behaviors. Includes instruction in biostatistics, biochemistry, molecular biology, immunology, disease and injury determinants, genetic disease and disability factors, behavioral studies, health services research, environmental disease and injury factors, and population studies.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the performance and sustainability of advanced textile composites through computational modeling of fiber-matrix interactions at multiple scales. Despite the growing demand for high-strength, lightweight materials in applications such as protective gear and flexible electronics, the structural efficiency of fiber-reinforced composites remains limited by poor interfacial adhesion between synthetic fibers and polymer matrices. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve the dynamic chemical and mechanical processes at these interfaces, hindering the rational design of next-generation textiles. To overcome this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, coarse-grained modeling, and finite element analysis (FE) to systematically investigate interface formation mechanisms, stress transfer efficiency, and failure modes in hybrid fiber systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of simulating polymer crystallization kinetics at fiber surfaces (requiring >1 million atom MD systems), mesoscale fiber network deformation under cyclic loading, and parametric studies of bio-inspired interfacial architectures. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated simulations and machine learning-based surrogate models to predict optimal surface functionalization strategies for carbon and aramid fibers, reducing iterative experimental trials. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for textile composite design and evidence-based guidelines for engineering hierarchical interfaces that enhance toughness by 30-50% compared to conventional treatments. By establishing computational workflows tailored to textile systems, this work will accelerate the development of energy-efficient manufacturing processes and recyclable composite materials, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance sustainable fiber technologies. The requested allocation of 200,000 node-hours on parallel computing clusters will enable these large-scale simulations, which cannot feasibly run on local laboratory resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to test and manufacture fibers and fiber products, both synthetic and natural; to develop new and improved fibers, textiles and their uses; and to the analysis of related engineering problems such as structural factors, molecular synthesis, chemical manufacturing, weaves, strength and stress, useful life, dyes, and applications to composite systems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between socio-cultural practices and health disparities in underserved urban populations, with a focus on how traditional healing systems coexist with biomedical healthcare frameworks. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable methodologies to analyze complex, multi-layered datasets—including ethnographic interviews, clinical records, and community health surveys—that capture the dynamic relationships between cultural norms, healthcare decision-making, and health outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational anthropology approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate qualitative and quantitative data at unprecedented scale. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to analyze ethnographic narratives from 500+ interview transcripts, identifying patterns in health-seeking behaviors and perceptions of illness. Concurrently, agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate community-level interactions between healthcare providers, patients, and traditional healers, incorporating spatial data on resource access and epidemiological variables. These computational methods require HPC capabilities to manage iterative simulations across diverse demographic scenarios and process unstructured linguistic data through transformer-based models. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for modeling cultural determinants of health inequities, predictive insights into barriers to care integration, and visualizations of how socio-cultural networks mediate disease vulnerability. The project will advance medical anthropology’s methodological repertoire by demonstrating how computational social science can bridge micro-level cultural analyses with population health patterns, ultimately informing culturally responsive public health strategies. By allocating resources for parallelized processing and large-scale data storage, this work will enable the first longitudinal study of its kind, tracking health behavior evolution in rapidly urbanizing regions over a simulated 10-year period.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological, socio-cultural, psychological, and behavioral factors as they relate to health, illness, medical practices, and access to health care services. Includes instruction in ethno-medicine, urban health, international health, psychiatric and psychological anthropology, aging, and health and identity.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of multi-omics data with clinical electrophysiology for personalized management of chronic neurological disorders, focusing on epilepsy and Parkinson’s disease. Current approaches to optimizing neuromodulation therapies (e.g., deep brain stimulation) rely on static anatomical or phenomenological biomarkers, often overlooking dynamic interactions between genetic, molecular, and real-time neural circuit activity. The research addresses this gap by developing computational models that unify patient-specific genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiles with high-density intracranial EEG (iEEG) and wearable sensor data. A hybrid machine learning framework will be implemented, combining graph neural networks to model brain network dynamics and variational autoencoders to identify latent multi-omics signatures predictive of therapeutic response. Computational workflows will require parallel processing of terabyte-scale neurophysiological datasets, GPU-accelerated training of deep learning architectures, and large-scale simulations of biologically constrained neural networks. Key challenges include scaling Bayesian inference for probabilistic integration of heterogeneous data streams and mitigating computational bottlenecks in real-time closed-loop stimulation modeling. Anticipated outcomes include a novel open-source pipeline for biomarker discovery, validated against retrospective clinical trial data, and predictive models to guide adaptive neuromodulation parameter tuning. This work bridges computational neuroscience, systems biology, and clinical neuroengineering, directly supporting translational objectives by enabling data-driven personalization of neuromodulation therapies. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive omics analyses, iterative model optimization, and validation against multi-site electrophysiology repositories, ultimately accelerating the translation of multi-scale biological insights into clinically actionable tools.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares clinicians to direct a broad range of scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge into clinical practice, and bridge clinical science with laboratory investigations. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, and scientific writing.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize real-time, adaptive data entry workflows for distributed microcomputer networks by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and train resource-efficient neural architectures. Traditional data entry systems—particularly in legacy industrial or archival contexts—rely on rigid, manual processes prone to latency and human error. While recent advances in edge computing and lightweight machine learning offer potential improvements, existing frameworks lack the capacity to dynamically adapt to heterogeneous microcomputer hardware (e.g., 8-bit microcontrollers, low-memory IoT devices) without excessive retraining or centralized compute dependencies. The proposed research addresses this gap by developing a novel computational pipeline that combines federated learning with hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS). Using HPC resources, we will simulate thousands of parallelized microcomputer nodes to iteratively train and validate adaptive models under constrained memory, power, and processing scenarios. Key innovations include a hybrid optimization algorithm that balances task accuracy against hardware limitations and a synthetic data generation toolkit replicating real-world data entry heterogeneity (e.g., sensor inputs, manual form digitization). Outcomes will include open-source frameworks for deploying adaptive models on legacy microcomputer systems, reducing manual correction efforts by an estimated 40–60% in pilot archival digitization workflows. This work bridges gaps between embedded systems, human-computer interaction, and decentralized AI, offering scalable solutions for understudied yet critical data entry applications in resource-limited environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data entry/microcomputer applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in medical insurance coding, a critical yet understudied nexus of healthcare administration, data science, and clinical documentation. Medical coding errors—arising from complex code interdependencies, evolving regulatory guidelines, and ambiguities in clinical narratives—result in billions of dollars in delayed reimbursements, claim denials, and compliance penalties annually. Current approaches to error detection rely on retrospective audits, which are resource-intensive and lack predictive capacity. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) framework trained on multimodal healthcare data, including de-identified insurance claims, electronic health records (EHRs), and coder workflow logs. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets spanning diverse medical specialties, geographies, and payer systems, which is infeasible with standard computing infrastructure. Natural language processing (NLP) models will analyze unstructured clinical notes to identify documentation patterns correlated with coding inaccuracies, while graph neural networks will map hierarchical relationships between ICD-11, CPT, and HCPCS codes to detect semantic mismatches. Parallelized optimization algorithms will simulate coding pathways under varying regulatory constraints to recommend context-aware code selections. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source predictive analytics toolkit capable of flagging high-risk claims in real time, reducing error rates by automating code-validation workflows. This research bridges health informatics and computational linguistics, offering novel insights into the cognitive load and decision-making patterns of medical coders. By integrating these tools into coder training platforms, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for precision in revenue cycle management, directly enhancing healthcare operational efficiency while maintaining compliance with evolving billing policies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized data entry, classification, and record-keeping procedures related to medical diagnostic, treatment, billing, and insurance documentation. Includes instruction in medical records and insurance software applications, basic anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, fundamentals of medical science and treatment procedures, data classification and coding, data entry skills, and regulations relating to Medicare and insurance documentation.

abstract: Emerging zoonotic diseases at the human-wildlife interface present complex challenges shaped by ecological dynamics, host-pathogen evolution, and anthropogenic environmental change. This project seeks to quantify how landscape fragmentation and wildlife community composition interact to drive cross-species transmission risk for priority pathogens in tropical biodiversity hotspots. We propose developing an integrative computational framework combining high-resolution spatial datasets of land-use change, wildlife movement ecology, and longitudinal pathogen surveillance data from bat reservoirs in Southeast Asia. Agent-based models will simulate host foraging behavior under varying habitat connectivity scenarios, while Bayesian phylodynamic models will reconstruct viral evolutionary trajectories from genomic data. A novel spatial metapopulation component will incorporate host immune landscape heterogeneity derived from eco-immunological field sampling. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage iterative parameterization of stochastic transmission models across 10⁶ simulated landscapes, parallelized phylogenetic inference for 15,000+ viral sequences, and real-time integration of satellite-derived forest cover data at 30m resolution. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical habitat thresholds amplifying spillover risk through host crowding and immune depletion, (2) predictive maps of evolutionarily vulnerable viral lineages based on host shifting potential, and (3) open-source tools for coupling ecological metacommunity dynamics with pathogen genomic surveillance. This work addresses a fundamental gap in spatial epidemiology by unifying ecological scaling principles with evolutionary predictors of cross-species transmission, directly informing planetary health strategies at the nexus of conservation and pandemic prevention. The requested GPU nodes and distributed memory architecture will enable processing of petabyte-scale remote sensing inputs while maintaining phylogenetic likelihood calculations for complex evolutionary models.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of epidemiology and biostatistics or a specialization which draws from epidemiology and biostatistics. Includes instruction in biostatistics, disease and injury determinants, epidemiology, health services research, pathology, spatial analysis, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges of modeling orbital debris mitigation strategies for sustainable space operations, a critical concern as near-Earth orbits become increasingly congested. Current simulations struggle to resolve the multi-physics interactions between debris clouds, active satellites, and mitigation systems at scale, limiting predictive accuracy. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework coupling orbital mechanics, hypervelocity impact dynamics, and machine learning to simulate debris evolution under various removal scenarios. The computational approach integrates direct numerical simulations of plasma-fluid interactions during directed-energy debris deorbiting, adaptive mesh refinement for high-resolution collision modeling, and graph neural networks to predict debris cloud propagation. These methods will leverage distributed-memory parallelism and GPU-accelerated solvers to scale simulations to realistic debris densities across multi-year orbital timelines. Validation will utilize historical tracking data from the US Space Surveillance Network and experimental hypervelocity impact datasets. The outcomes will produce predictive models for assessing debris removal efficacy, optimizing spacecraft shielding configurations, and informing policy frameworks for traffic management in low Earth orbit. By enabling high-fidelity, large-scale simulations of debris interactions, this work aims to reduce collision risks for operational satellites and crewed missions while advancing spacecraft design paradigms. The resulting open-source codebase will provide the astronautical engineering community with tools to evaluate mitigation technologies, from laser ablation systems to reusable orbital servicers, supporting the long-term viability of space exploration activities.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and operational evaluation of aircraft and space vehicles. Includes instruction in control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of genetic susceptibility to environmental toxicants by investigating molecular mechanisms underlying toxin-receptor interactions and metabolic dysregulation. A critical challenge in molecular toxicology lies in predicting how individual genetic variability influences adverse outcomes following exposure to pollutants, particularly in complex biological systems where dynamic interactions between xenobiotics and cellular pathways remain poorly resolved. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning-driven analysis of toxicogenomic datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of toxin interactions with metabolic enzymes (e.g., cytochrome P450 isoforms) and stress-response proteins under varied genetic backgrounds, including polymorphisms identified in human population studies. Machine learning models will be trained on multi-omics data to identify gene regulatory networks associated with susceptibility to pulmonary toxicants, leveraging existing transcriptomic and epigenomic datasets from in vivo exposure studies. The computational pipeline will further simulate dose-response relationships for priority chemicals flagged by regulatory agencies, incorporating transgenic modeling data to assess tissue-specific toxicokinetics. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-risk genetic variants impacting xenobiotic metabolism, predictive maps of toxin-induced signaling perturbations in susceptible populations, and optimized in silico biomarkers for early toxicity detection. This work directly supports the development of precision risk assessment tools and targeted countermeasures against environmental toxicants, aligning with the program’s focus on molecular-scale interventions. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the iterative simulations, complex model parameterization, and high-dimensional data integration required to resolve toxicity mechanisms at biologically relevant scales. By bridging genetic susceptibility with molecular toxicodynamic processes, this project aims to inform therapeutic strategies that mitigate health disparities in toxin-exposed communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetic determinants of susceptibility to external pollutants and poisons; the interaction of toxic agents with biological systems at the molecular and cellular levels; and the development of countermeasures and treatments. Includes instruction in pharmacogenetics, biomolecular structure, gene expression and regulation, transgenic modeling, toxic events signaling, transcriptional activation, mutagenesis and carcinogenesis, pulmonary toxicology, xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress, risk assessment, molecular dosimetry, and studies of specific toxins and treatment therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy efficiency and guest experience in smart hotel environments, addressing the hospitality industry’s urgent need to balance sustainability goals with service quality. While energy management systems in hospitality settings are increasingly data-driven, existing approaches lack the capacity to integrate real-time sensor data, weather forecasts, and dynamic occupancy patterns at scale. The research problem centers on designing adaptive algorithms that minimize energy consumption in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems without compromising guest comfort—a challenge requiring high-resolution simulations of thermal dynamics, occupant behavior, and operational constraints. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on multi-modal datasets (including IoT sensor streams, reservation logs, and environmental reports) and run parallelized simulations of energy use scenarios across diverse hotel layouts and climatic conditions. Methods include reinforcement learning to optimize HVAC control policies, agent-based modeling to predict guest movement patterns, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in demand forecasts. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that recommends real-time energy adjustments while maintaining predefined comfort thresholds, validated against historical data from partner hotels. This work aims to reduce hospitality sector carbon footprints by an estimated 15–20% in simulated environments, with broader implications for resource allocation in service industries where operational efficiency intersects with customer satisfaction. The computational intensity of modeling fine-grained spatial-temporal interactions necessitates HPC capabilities, particularly for GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale parameter optimization. By bridging hospitality management, building science, and computational sustainability, this project advances an emerging niche in data-driven service operations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in hospitality service management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of engineering design requirements demands advanced computational tools to enable efficient, high-fidelity modeling and simulation within CAD/CADD workflows. Current software frameworks often struggle with scalability when handling intricate geometries, multi-physics simulations, or real-time collaborative design processes, leading to computational bottlenecks that delay project timelines. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize parallelized algorithms for next-generation CAD/CADD applications. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) implementing distributed-memory parallelization strategies to accelerate finite element analysis (FEA) integration within CAD environments, (2) developing GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines for interactive visualization of large-scale assembly models, and (3) prototyping machine learning models to predict and mitigate design conflicts in multi-user collaborative platforms. Using HPC clusters, we will benchmark these approaches against conventional single-node workflows, quantifying improvements in simulation resolution, rendering frame rates, and conflict detection accuracy. The computational workflows will utilize open-source CAD kernels coupled with MPI and CUDA frameworks to ensure scalability across heterogeneous architectures. Anticipated outcomes include a validated toolkit for HPC-enhanced CAD workflows, reducing simulation times by 40–60% for models exceeding 10^6 elements and enabling real-time collaboration on complex designs. This work will provide a methodological foundation for integrating HPC capabilities into CAD/CADD education, equipping students with skills to tackle industry challenges in advanced manufacturing and smart infrastructure. By demonstrating the transformative potential of scalable computing in design technology, the project aims to bridge the gap between traditional drafting pedagogy and emerging computational engineering demands.
cip_title: CAD/ CADD Drafting and/ or Design Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and advanced computer software and hardware to the creation of graphic representations and simulations in support of engineering projects. Includes instruction in engineering graphics, two-dimensional and three-dimensional engineering design, solids modeling, engineering animation, computer-aided drafting (CAD), computer-aided design (CADD), and auto-CAD techniques.

abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing processes, such as deposition, etching, and lithography, involve complex interactions between materials, equipment, and environmental conditions. These processes are critical to producing high-yield, reliable microchips, but optimizing them experimentally is time-intensive and costly. This project seeks to address the challenge of improving process efficiency and defect reduction in semiconductor fabrication by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-physics phenomena at scale. Specifically, we aim to develop predictive simulations that capture the interplay of plasma dynamics, chemical reactions, and thermal effects during key manufacturing steps, such as reactive ion etching and chemical vapor deposition. Current computational limitations restrict the resolution and parameter space of such models, hindering their utility for real-time process control. By utilizing HPC resources, we will implement large-scale, three-dimensional simulations using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and molecular dynamics (MD) frameworks. These simulations will integrate experimental data from in-situ sensors and metrology tools to validate and refine predictive models. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify correlations between process parameters (e.g., gas flow rates, RF power, pressure) and defect formation, enabling inverse design of optimal operating conditions. The outcomes of this research will provide actionable insights into minimizing process variability, reducing material waste, and extending equipment longevity. The resulting computational tools will be disseminated as open-source modules to support academic and industrial research in semiconductor manufacturing. This work aligns with national priorities to strengthen domestic semiconductor production capabilities and will directly enhance the training of students in advanced computational methods applied to manufacturing challenges. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required scale and speed for these simulations, which involve millions of degrees of freedom and require parallelized computation across thousands of cores.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to operate and monitor equipment for the fabrication of semiconductors or microchips from silicon wafers, and to troubleshoot, maintain, and repair the specialized equipment used in this process. Includes instruction in AC and DC circuits, digital fundamentals, solid state devices, manufacturing processes, vacuum principles and technology, industrial electronics, quality assurance, and semiconductor manufacturing technology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the socio-technical evolution of 19th-century hospital design and its relationship to shifting medical theories of contagion, leveraging computational modeling to analyze spatial, archival, and epidemiological datasets. While historical scholarship has examined hospital architecture or disease concepts in isolation, the dynamic interplay between evolving germ theory paradigms, urbanization pressures, and institutional care infrastructures remains underexplored. The research addresses this gap by reconstructing longitudinal networks of hospital construction patterns, patient outcomes, and municipal public health debates across three European cities (London, Paris, Vienna) from 1820–1900. High-performance computing resources are required to process heterogeneous data streams, including digitized blueprints, mortality registers, city sanitation records, and medical society proceedings, which collectively exceed 15TB. Computational methods will integrate geospatial machine learning to map architectural feature diffusion, natural language processing to track semantic shifts in "contagion" discourse within medical journals, and agent-based modeling to simulate disease transmission risks in historically accurate virtual hospital environments. The simulations will test hypotheses about how specific design elements (ventilation systems, ward segmentation) mediated mortality rates during cholera outbreaks. Expected outcomes include a novel open-access platform for diachronic analysis of medical infrastructure, quantitative evidence linking epistemic changes to material practices in clinical environments, and methodological frameworks for interdisciplinary history of medicine research. By computationally bridging archival sources with epidemiological models, this work aims to reveal previously inaccessible patterns in how emerging biomedical knowledge became spatially embedded—a process with implications for understanding contemporary challenges in healthcare facility design during disease crises.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution and socio-economic context of medical theories, education, practices, and technologies; and on the history of diseases, therapeutics, patients, and healers. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of the historiography of medicine; the history of science, medicine, and technology; and of research methods in the history of medicine.

abstract: Maternal morbidity and adverse pregnancy outcomes remain significant challenges in women’s health, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations. Current approaches to risk stratification and intervention planning often rely on generalized guidelines that inadequately account for the complex interplay of physiological, pharmacological, and sociodemographic factors unique to individual patients. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a predictive computational framework to optimize personalized care strategies for obstetric and gynecological patients. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-modal datasets—including electronic health records, longitudinal biomarker profiles, pharmacogenomic data, and patient-reported outcomes—to construct machine learning models capable of forecasting individualized risks for conditions such as preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, and postpartum hemorrhage. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian hierarchical modeling to address data sparsity in underrepresented groups and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate tailored intervention pathways. The models will further incorporate pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations to evaluate drug efficacy and safety across pregnancy stages, accounting for dynamic physiological changes. By enabling real-time analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, HPC resources are critical to achieving the resolution and speed required for these simulations. The anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools to guide nurse-led interventions, reducing preventable complications and advancing equity in women’s health care. This work aligns with nursing science priorities by translating computational insights into actionable clinical practices, ultimately strengthening evidence-based, patient-centered care models in obstetrics and gynecology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of high-power laser systems through advanced computational modeling of nonlinear optical interactions and thermal-wavefront coupling. High-power lasers are limited by thermally induced phase distortions and nonlinear effects such as self-focusing, which degrade beam quality and system efficiency. Current analytical models fail to capture the full spatiotemporal complexity of these phenomena, particularly in novel photonic architectures involving multi-core fibers or ultrafast pulse shaping. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-physics computational framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations of electromagnetic wave propagation with coupled thermal-fluid dynamics models. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized 3D simulations tracking femtosecond-scale optical dynamics alongside millisecond-scale thermal diffusion processes across meter-scale optical paths. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate parameter space exploration for adaptive optics control systems. Key deliverables include validated models of cascaded Raman scattering in crystalline waveguides, predictive tools for thermal lensing mitigation in kW-class fiber lasers, and optimization strategies for broadband optical parametric amplifiers. The computational outcomes will directly inform the fabrication of prototype systems with enhanced brightness and stability, advancing applications in laser machining, free-space communications, and medical device development. By enabling unprecedented resolution of coupled nonlinear processes in complex optical systems, this work will establish new paradigms for photonic device design while providing open-source simulation tools to the laser engineering community. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the petascale datasets generated by our high-resolution, multi-domain simulations, which cannot be executed on local computing infrastructure within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of optical systems, lasers and related electronic devices. Includes instruction in wave theory and mechanics, electromagnetic applications, linear and non-linear optics, photon detecting, laser beam properties, directed energy, harmonic generation, optical systems, shielding and the design and implementation of related systems and equipment.

abstract: Pediatric patients exhibit significant variability in treatment responses due to interactions between developmental, genetic, and environmental factors, complicating the delivery of optimized care. Traditional clinical approaches often rely on generalized protocols, which may inadequately address individual patient needs, potentially leading to suboptimal outcomes or adverse effects. This project proposes to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that integrate multi-dimensional data, enabling personalized, predictive strategies for pediatric nursing. The research will focus on common pediatric conditions such as asthma, congenital heart defects, and type 1 diabetes, where dynamic treatment adjustments are critical. Using machine learning algorithms, we will analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and socio-environmental datasets to identify patterns influencing disease progression and therapeutic efficacy. Agent-based simulations will model patient-specific responses to interventions, while real-time optimization frameworks will test hypothetical treatment adjustments to minimize risks. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data, training complex neural networks, and executing parallelized simulations at scale—tasks infeasible with standard clinical computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to stratify patients by risk of complications, decision-support systems for nurses to tailor medication dosages and monitoring schedules, and evidence-based insights into modifiable factors affecting recovery. By translating computational findings into clinical workflows, this work aims to reduce hospital readmissions, mitigate treatment side effects, and improve long-term health outcomes for pediatric populations. The project underscores the transformative potential of computational science in advancing precision nursing, offering a scalable framework to bridge data-driven research and bedside care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care for children from infancy through adolescence. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting physicians, patient examination and referral, and planning and delivering health maintenance and health education programs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize precision meat-cutting workflows in commercial settings through advanced simulation and predictive modeling. The research addresses inefficiencies in traditional meat processing, which relies heavily on manual expertise and static guidelines, leading to variable yield rates, energy waste, and suboptimal equipment utilization. By integrating high-fidelity physics-based simulations with machine learning, we aim to model the biomechanical properties of diverse meat products (e.g., beef, pork, poultry) under varying blade geometries, cutting speeds, and refrigeration conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate tissue deformation and stress distribution during cutting, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to map thermal gradients in storage environments. Parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine cutting protocols to maximize yield while minimizing energy consumption and tool wear. Additionally, genomic and proteomic datasets from livestock sources will be analyzed to predict muscle fiber orientation and fat marbling patterns, informing adaptive cutting strategies. The computational pipeline will be validated against empirical data from sensor-equipped cutting stations, tracking outcomes such as waste reduction, ergonomic safety metrics, and shelf-life extension. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision support toolkit for butchers, dynamically optimized cutting templates for automated machinery, and predictive models for regulatory compliance in meat handling. By bridging gaps between computational mechanics, materials science, and food technology, this work establishes a novel interdisciplinary paradigm for advancing precision in meat processing—a critical yet underexplored domain in non-STEM vocational research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, cut, and package animal meat products in commercial establishments and to function as licensed meat cutters/butchers.  Includes instruction in product recognition for beef, veal, lamb, pork, poultry, and fancy and smoked meats; retail and wholesale cutting and specialty cuts; packaging and counter display; shop safety; meat sanitation, storage and rotation; quality control; meat handling laws and regulations; and customer service.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing the structural integrity and safety of aging munitions storage facilities under dynamic environmental conditions. The degradation of such facilities—often exposed to temperature fluctuations, humidity, and chemical interactions from stored ordnance—poses significant risks, including corrosion-induced failures and hazardous material leaks. Traditional empirical models struggle to account for the complex, multi-physics interactions driving degradation, particularly in facilities housing diverse ordnance types with varying chemical and thermal footprints. To address this gap, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate coupled thermo-chemo-mechanical processes across heterogeneous materials and environmental scenarios. A hybrid computational approach will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-corrosion cracking, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for ventilation efficiency and contaminant dispersion, and machine learning (ML) to identify degradation patterns from historical maintenance data. Custom code will couple open-source solvers (e.g., OpenFOAM, FEniCS) with ML libraries (TensorFlow, PyTorch) to enable real-time parameter optimization. The simulations will account for site-specific variables, including localized climate data, munitions composition, and facility geometry, to generate risk-prediction maps and maintenance prioritization schedules. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin prototype for proactive infrastructure management, reducing unplanned downtime and enhancing safety compliance. This work aligns with military priorities to modernize legacy systems through computational resilience modeling, offering a scalable template for analogous critical infrastructure challenges. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the high-resolution 3D meshing, parallelized multi-physics solvers, and large-scale ML training required for robust, actionable predictions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of ground or sea-based weapons systems, ordinance and munitions. Includes instruction in basic sciences, electronics, systems technology, fluid power, computer science, conventional weapons systems, nuclear weapons systems, munitions systems, storage and safety, equipment operation, guidance and control systems, hazardous materials, corrosion control, nondestructive testing and quality control, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic neural mechanisms underlying real-time language comprehension through computational modeling, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current models of syntactic and semantic integration lack the scalability to simulate brain-scale networks or process naturalistic linguistic input efficiently. We propose developing a parallelized neural network architecture that mimics cortical and subcortical interactions during speech processing. The model will integrate psycholinguistic datasets, including eye-tracking and EEG data, to constrain real-time processing dynamics. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization via gradient-free search algorithms and Bayesian inference techniques, which are computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure. Simulations will generate testable predictions about context-driven lexical access and ambiguity resolution, addressing theoretical debates on modular versus interactive language processing. Additionally, the project will create open-source tools for cognitive modeling, facilitating reproducibility in computational psycholinguistics. Anticipated outcomes include a mechanistic understanding of how prediction and memory systems coordinate during comprehension, with implications for developmental disorders affecting language. By leveraging distributed computing to overcome current limitations in model complexity, this research bridges gaps between cognitive theory and neurocomputational implementation, advancing both psychological science and artificial language systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the mechanisms and processes of learning and thinking, and associated information encoding, decoding, processing and transmitting systems. Includes instruction in theories of cognition and intelligence; studies of cognitive processes such as memory, sensation, perception, pattern recognition, problem solving, and conceptual thinking; cybernetics; psycholinguistics; and the study of biological and social communications mechanisms and processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of team cohesion in collegiate athletics, with a focus on the interplay between athlete identity, institutional policies, and historical legacies of exclusion. While existing studies in sports psychology and sociology have explored these themes qualitatively, this research adopts a novel computational approach to model longitudinal interactions among athletes, coaches, and administrative systems. The central problem lies in understanding how systemic biases—rooted in race, gender, and socioeconomic factors—persist or dissolve within team environments over time, particularly in institutions undergoing policy reforms. To address this, the project will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating decision-making processes and social networks within athletic programs, informed by historical datasets spanning 30 years of collegiate sports records, demographic archives, and institutional policy documents. These models will incorporate machine learning techniques to identify latent patterns in athlete retention rates, conflict resolution outcomes, and leadership dynamics. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to reflect the complexity of real-world systems, enabling parallel processing of millions of agent interactions across variable policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting the efficacy of equity-driven interventions in sports organizations, as well as the creation of open-access computational tools tailored for sports studies researchers.
