abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing clinical workflows and patient outcomes through advanced computational modeling of multi-modal health data. Despite the growing availability of electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and genomic datasets, healthcare systems struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data sources for real-time decision support. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to improve resource allocation in clinical settings, reduce diagnostic delays, and personalize care pathways for patients with complex chronic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, machine learning techniques—including graph neural networks and transformer architectures—will be applied to de-identified EHR data from [Institution/Partner Network] to identify patterns in care delivery bottlenecks and comorbidities. Second, discrete-event simulation models will be developed to test interventions for clinic scheduling, staff deployment, and equipment utilization under varying patient volumes. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including time-series vital sign data, radiology reports, and administrative operation logs. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for simulating clinic operations under different resource constraints, predictive models for early identification of high-risk patients, and evidence-based recommendations for balancing clinical efficiency with care quality. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on medical management and clinical specialization by creating scalable tools to enhance both administrative decision-making and patient-facing care coordination. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of complex models that cannot run efficiently on local clinical systems, particularly for Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of operational scenarios. Results will be disseminated through healthcare informatics conferences and adapted into training modules for clinical assistant education programs.
cip_title: Medical/ Health Management and Clinical Assistant/ Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, nurses, or other health care professionals, to perform medical office or facilities management services and perform one or more clinical allied health specialties. Includes instruction in health care management; medical office administration; medical law and regulations; training in one or more diagnostic, treatment, therapy, or laboratory specialties at the assistant level or above; and applicable professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the accuracy and efficiency of real-time court interpretation through computational modeling of linguistic and procedural dynamics in multilingual legal settings. Court interpreters face unique challenges, including the need to preserve semantic precision, manage rapid code-switching between languages, and adhere to strict legal protocols under time-sensitive conditions. Existing training tools and simulation platforms lack the capacity to model the full complexity of courtroom interactions, particularly for low-resource languages or specialized legal terminology. The proposed research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework that integrates natural language processing (NLP), acoustic modeling, and real-time latency optimization to simulate and analyze interpreter performance in virtual courtroom environments. Using anonymized multilingual court transcripts, audio recordings, and procedural metadata, the project will train transformer-based models to recognize context-dependent legal terminology and generate probabilistic assessments of interpretation accuracy under varying conditions (e.g., overlapping speech, regional dialects, or ambiguous phrasing). HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of training workflows, hyperparameter optimization for low-latency inference models, and the synthesis of multimodal training datasets incorporating gesture recognition and prosodic features. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for interpreter training, quantitative benchmarks for error reduction in high-stakes legal scenarios, and a cross-linguistic repository of annotated legal interpretation corpora. By bridging computational linguistics and legal procedural analysis, this work aims to establish scalable, evidence-based standards for interpreter competency while addressing equity gaps in access to justice for non-dominant language speakers. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—situated at the intersection of language technology, cognitive science, and legal practice—exemplifies an emerging niche in computational humanities that transcends traditional disciplinary boundaries.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to provide accurate translation and interpretation between two or more languages for parties involved in a legal proceeding. Includes instruction in courtroom standards and procedures, court interpreting, legal terminology, consecutive interpretation, simultaneous interpretation, and sight translation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of neuromuscular control during human movement, with applications to exercise optimization and post-injury rehabilitation. A critical challenge in biomechanics and motor control research lies in understanding how neural, muscular, and skeletal systems interact dynamically across spatiotemporal scales. Existing experimental methods often lack the resolution to isolate individual neuromuscular contributions during complex, real-world tasks, while simplified models fail to capture the nonlinear interactions governing movement adaptability. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale, patient-specific simulations integrating musculoskeletal dynamics, neural excitation patterns, and metabolic cost functions. The computational framework will utilize OpenSim for inverse kinematics/dynamics, coupled with finite element modeling of muscle-tendon mechanics and reinforcement learning algorithms to predict adaptive motor strategies under varying physiological constraints (e.g., muscle fatigue, joint instability). HPC resources are essential to parameterize models using high-resolution MRI/EMG datasets from ongoing studies (n=120 participants, including athletes and post-stroke patients), perform sensitivity analyses across 10^4+ parameter combinations, and simulate movement trajectories in virtual environments mimicking rehabilitation protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of neuromuscular biomarkers predictive of rehabilitation outcomes, (2) optimization of task-specific exercise prescriptions through in silico testing of loading strategies, and (3) open-source tools for simulating impaired gait patterns. By enabling real-time feedback loops between computational predictions and clinical assessments, this work will establish a paradigm for personalized therapeutic interventions while advancing the scalability of neuromusculoskeletal models in kinesiology research. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated training of neural controllers and parallelized execution of multibody dynamics simulations, reducing per-simulation runtime from weeks to hours.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, with diagnostic and therapeutic advancements constrained by the complexity of hemodynamic interactions and limitations in current clinical imaging analysis. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced computational models of cardiovascular physiology, focusing on patient-specific simulations of blood flow dynamics and tissue remodeling. The research problem centers on the need for high-resolution, multi-scale modeling that integrates heterogeneous clinical data—including echocardiograms, angiograms, and electrophysiological measurements—to predict disease progression and optimize treatment strategies for conditions such as aortic stenosis, coronary artery disease, and heart failure. Current methods lack the computational power to process these datasets in tandem while accounting for real-world variability in anatomy, hemodynamics, and device-tissue interactions. The proposed computational approach combines finite element analysis, machine learning-based image segmentation, and fluid-structure interaction simulations to create patient-specific predictive models. HPC resources are essential to manage the high dimensionality of 4D imaging data, perform parallelized simulations across diverse physiological scenarios, and enable parameter optimization through iterative learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting post-interventional outcomes (e.g., stent deployment or valve replacement), open-source tools for automated hemodynamic analysis, and a framework for integrating simulation results into clinical decision-support systems. This work aligns with the Cardiovascular Technology program’s emphasis on advancing diagnostic and therapeutic precision through technology, with potential impacts on reducing procedural complications, personalizing treatment plans, and improving long-term patient outcomes. The requested computing resources will directly support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale data storage for multicenter collaborations, and the development of cloud-based interfaces for clinician-researcher partnerships.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform invasive, noninvasive, and peripheral examinations of the cardiovascular system at the request of physicians to aid in diagnoses and therapeutic treatments. Includes instruction in reviewing and recording patient histories and clinical data, patient care, investigative and examination procedures, diagnostic procedures, data analysis and documentation, physician consultation, equipment operation and monitoring, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The proposed research project addresses the critical need for advanced computational tools in the analysis of Hungarian literary texts and their linguistic evolution, particularly in tracing morphological and syntactic shifts across historical periods. While Hungarian philology has a rich tradition of manual textual analysis, the increasing availability of digitized archives—including 19th-century manuscripts, early print materials, and contemporary literature—demands scalable methods to identify patterns in lexical usage, grammatical structures, and stylistic innovations. Current challenges include processing large corpora with diacritic-rich orthography, managing archaic vocabulary, and modeling dialectal variations in pre-standardization texts. This project will deploy high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-stage computational pipeline: first, training transformer-based models on domain-specific Hungarian texts to improve tokenization and morphological disambiguation; second, applying graph-based algorithms to map semantic networks in literary works; and third, conducting comparative analyses of syntactic complexity across genres using parallelized dependency parsing. The workflow will integrate existing NLP tools adapted for Hungarian’s agglutinative structure with custom scripts for frequency distribution analysis and stylometric profiling. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of 10,000+ historical and modern Hungarian texts, quantitative frameworks for assessing linguistic change, and visualizations of intertextual relationships in canonical works. By enabling large-scale pattern recognition across centuries of Magyar literature, this research will advance scholarly understanding of language standardization processes, authorial influence networks, and the interplay between linguistic innovation and cultural identity. The computational resources requested are essential to handle memory-intensive tasks such as training specialized language models and processing multi-gigabyte text collections, which exceed the capacity of standard academic computing infrastructure. This project bridges computational linguistics with traditional literary studies, offering a replicable methodology for Uralic language research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hungarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance K-12 environmental education by developing interactive, computationally driven tools that model complex ecological systems, enabling educators to teach dynamic environmental concepts with greater fidelity. Current pedagogical approaches often rely on static or simplified representations of ecosystems, climate processes, and human-environment interactions, which fail to convey the interconnected, nonlinear behaviors inherent to these systems. To address this gap, the research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct high-resolution simulations of ecological and climatic phenomena tailored for classroom use. Agent-based models will simulate species interactions, nutrient cycles, and climate feedbacks under varying scenarios, while machine learning algorithms will process real-time environmental data from public datasets to personalize simulations based on regional or local contexts. These tools will be integrated into an open-access platform designed for educators, allowing them to adjust parameters (e.g., precipitation patterns, land-use changes) and visualize outcomes through intuitive interfaces. The computational demands of running parallelized simulations across diverse scenarios, training predictive models on large geospatial datasets, and supporting concurrent user access in classrooms necessitate scalable HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a suite of modular, standards-aligned computational tools that demonstrate cause-effect relationships in environmental systems, (2) quantitative evaluation of student learning gains in systems thinking and data literacy when using dynamic versus static models, and (3) a framework for embedding computational modeling into teacher professional development programs. By bridging environmental science, education research, and high-performance computing, this work aims to empower educators with resources that foster deeper engagement with environmental complexity, preparing students to critically analyze real-world sustainability challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach environmental education at various educational levels as a K-12 classroom educator. Includes instruction in foundations of environmental education, instructional methods, and related content knowledge.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling large-scale, interactive music and dance performances. While the study of live artistic collaboration offers critical insights into improvisation, cultural expression, and human creativity, existing analytical tools struggle to process the temporal, spatial, and multimodal complexity of synchronized audio, movement, and physiological data generated during performances. The research will develop computational frameworks to analyze real-time interactions between musicians and dancers, integrating motion-capture data, high-fidelity audio streams, and biometric signals (e.g., heart rate variability) captured during experimental performances. Machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures and graph neural networks, will be trained to identify patterns in improvisational decision-making and corporeal-auditory synchronization across diverse cultural traditions, such as jazz, West African drumming, and contemporary dance. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing the processing of terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters for ensemble models, and simulating agent-based environments to test hypotheses about collective creativity. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time performance analysis, a public repository of annotated performance data, and novel theoretical frameworks for understanding how emergent artistic behaviors arise from nonlinear interactions. This work will advance interdisciplinary methodologies in musicology and dance studies while providing infrastructure for future studies on computational ethnomusicology, embodied cognition, and augmented performance technologies. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of live art, the project aims to bridge artistic practice and computational research, fostering new pedagogical and creative applications in the performing arts.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of music and the performing arts. Includes instruction in music, dance, and other performing arts media.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in osteopathic medicine by modeling the biomechanical and systemic effects of osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT). Despite the widespread clinical use of OMT to address musculoskeletal dysfunction and promote holistic health, the precise mechanisms linking manual interventions to physiological outcomes—such as altered tissue mechanics, inflammatory modulation, or autonomic nervous system responses—remain poorly quantified. This gap limits the development of evidence-based protocols for optimizing therapeutic efficacy. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multiscale biomechanical modeling, systems biology, and machine learning. Patient-specific anatomical datasets, including MRI-derived musculoskeletal geometry and motion capture kinematics, will inform finite element models of tissue strain during OMT. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate cellular responses to mechanical stimuli, incorporating pathways related to cytokine signaling, nociception, and vascular adaptation. Machine learning algorithms will analyze paired clinical datasets (e.g., pre/post-treatment biomarker profiles, patient-reported outcomes) to identify predictive signatures of therapeutic success. These computational layers will be dynamically coupled to explore emergent interactions between manual interventions and systemic health outcomes. HPC resources are critical for managing the high dimensionality of multiscale simulations, iterative parameter optimization, and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include predictive models of OMT efficacy, validated against prospective clinical studies, which can guide personalized treatment strategies. This work will provide a mechanistic foundation for osteopathic principles, bridging traditional practice with computational innovation. By quantifying the relationships between manual therapy, tissue remodeling, and systemic physiology, the project aims to enhance clinical training tools, refine OMT techniques, and strengthen osteopathic medicine’s role in integrative healthcare. The resulting computational infrastructure will also serve as a platform for future studies on musculoskeletal health, mechanotransduction, and non-pharmacologic interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of osteopathic medicine, involving a combination of medical principles and procedures and osteopathic principles of holistic medicine and the relationship of the musculoskeletal system to general health. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, preventive medicine, family and community medicine, medical informatics, disease systems, organ and physiologic systems, osteopathic principles and practice, osteopathic manipulative treatment, musculoskeletal and skin systems, clinical specialty rotations, medical ethics, and professional standards and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets central to understanding the development of Canadian social and political institutions in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The research problem centers on tracing the interconnected evolution of federal policies, regional identities, and public discourse during a period of rapid industrialization and demographic change. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to systematically process the vast quantity of digitized primary sources now available, including parliamentary debates, regional newspapers, census records, and correspondence networks. To address this, the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques and network analysis algorithms to map patterns in policy language, track the dissemination of political ideas, and quantify shifts in regional representation within federal institutions. Computational workflows will be designed to handle multilingual texts (English and French), temporal-spatial metadata, and heterogeneous data formats, with iterative validation against established historical interpretations. Key objectives include identifying previously undocumented correlations between resource allocation decisions and regional voting patterns, as well as visualizing the long-term impacts of immigration policies on urban-rural divides. The scale of data—spanning over 10 million pages of text and 150,000 archival records—necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory operations, and efficient storage of intermediate analytical outputs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated historical texts, novel computational methods tailored to Canadian historiography, and peer-reviewed findings challenging existing narratives about federal-provincial power dynamics during Confederation-era reforms. By enabling systematic analysis across previously siloed sources, this project aims to advance methodological innovation in historical research while generating new insights into the structural foundations of modern Canadian governance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the society, culture, and institutions of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in Canadian historiography, sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and evaluate adaptive, data-driven instructional models for students with specific learning disabilities (SLDs), such as dyslexia, dyscalculia, and dysgraphia. Students with SLDs often require highly individualized educational strategies to address their unique cognitive and academic profiles. However, designing effective, personalized interventions remains a significant challenge due to the heterogeneity of learning needs and the dynamic interplay of cognitive, behavioral, and environmental factors. Current approaches to creating individualized education plans (IEPs) rely on static assessments and manual adjustments, limiting their responsiveness and scalability. This project proposes a computational framework to model learning trajectories, predict intervention efficacy, and optimize instructional sequences in real time. Using machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning and neural networks, we will analyze multimodal datasets (e.g., student performance metrics, eye-tracking data, and behavioral logs) to identify patterns in skill acquisition and barriers to learning. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments to test the scalability of personalized strategies under varying conditions. HPC resources are critical to processing large-scale datasets, training complex models, and running computationally intensive simulations that account for high-dimensional variables (e.g., attention span, memory load, and socioemotional factors). Expected outcomes include the development of an open-source toolkit for generating dynamic IEP recommendations, validated against empirical classroom data, and a predictive model to guide educators in adapting lesson plans for students with SLDs. By integrating computational precision with pedagogical expertise, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in special education, reduce administrative burdens on teachers, and improve academic outcomes for learners with SLDs. The scalability of these tools will be tested across virtual classroom environments, enabling broader dissemination of equitable, data-informed teaching strategies.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Specific Learning Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with specific learning disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with specific learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with specific learning disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation strategies for hybrid hospitality operations—businesses integrating accommodation, dining, and experiential services under one ecosystem—using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, real-time decision-making. Traditional revenue management systems in hotels and restaurants often treat lodging, food service, and ancillary offerings as siloed entities, leading to suboptimal pricing and capacity decisions when demand patterns intersect across services. Our work addresses this gap by developing an adaptive computational framework that simulates multi-dimensional consumer behavior, supply chain volatility, and operational constraints unique to integrated hospitality environments. Leveraging agent-based modeling and deep reinforcement learning, the project will process heterogeneous datasets—including historical booking patterns, real-time IoT sensor data from facility usage, and local event-driven demand surges—to generate responsive pricing and staffing policies. HPC resources are critical to scaling simulations across thousands of concurrent agents representing guests, employees, and suppliers while maintaining granular temporal resolution (15-minute intervals) over extended planning horizons (180-day cycles). Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that increases cross-service revenue capture by 12–18% in pilot tests with partner resorts, alongside actionable insights into demand spillover effects between lodging and restaurant operations during peak seasons. The computational models will also quantify sustainability trade-offs, such as energy use versus service quality, enabling operators to balance profit margins with environmental targets. By bridging hospitality management, behavioral economics, and computational optimization, this work advances a niche but growing domain where traditional business analytics fail to address the interdependencies of modern, experience-driven travel ecosystems.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide food and/or lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage, and control; hotel and restaurant facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; facilities management; marketing and sale promotion strategies; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotel, motel, and/or restaurant operations. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 52.0902.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how large-scale digital communication patterns within organizations influence decision-making, conflict resolution, and the cultivation of shared values. As organizations increasingly rely on platforms like Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email for internal communication, the volume, velocity, and complexity of interaction data pose significant challenges for traditional analytical methods. The research problem centers on identifying how emergent communication dynamics—such as asymmetries in information flow, sentiment polarization, and the role of symbolic language in shaping organizational identity—affect collaborative outcomes and institutional resilience. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, network modeling, and agent-based simulations to analyze anonymized, organization-wide communication datasets spanning multiple years and comprising terabytes of text. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models to detect nuanced semantic patterns (e.g., metaphors, power-laden terminology) and for running parallelized network analyses to map real-time information diffusion across hierarchical structures. Agent-based models will simulate how policy changes or leadership interventions might alter communication efficiency under crisis scenarios. Outcomes will include (1) a framework for diagnosing communication bottlenecks in large organizations, (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing digital platforms to mitigate conflict and align messaging with organizational values, and (3) open-source tools tailored for non-technical researchers in organizational communication to analyze interaction data. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances theoretical understanding of technology-mediated organizational dynamics while providing actionable insights for improving equity in participation, responsiveness to employee needs, and strategic coherence in mission-driven institutions.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on general communication processes and dynamics within organizations. Includes instruction in the development and maintenance of interpersonal group relations within organizations; decision-making and conflict management; the use of symbols to create and maintain organizational images, missions, and values; power and politics within organizations; human interaction with computer technology; and how communications socializes and supports employees and team members.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a machine learning framework to optimize the design of individualized education plans (IEPs) for elementary students with disabilities, addressing the challenge of efficiently integrating heterogeneous data to personalize instruction. Current IEP development relies heavily on manual analysis of student performance, behavioral observations, and diagnostic assessments—a process that strains educator capacity and may overlook subtle patterns in multisource data. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning models on structured and unstructured data from 5,000+ anonymized IEPs, longitudinal academic records, and sensor-based engagement metrics (e.g., eye-tracking, response latency) collected across 15 special education classrooms. Computational workflows will process natural language notes, time-series behavioral logs, and curriculum-aligned assessment scores to identify cross-modal predictors of skill acquisition rates. A transformer-based architecture will then recommend targeted accommodations, scaffolded objectives, and intervention strategies tailored to individual learner profiles. Validation will involve simulating IEP efficacy across synthetic cohorts representing diverse disabilities, socioeconomic factors, and classroom contexts. By automating data synthesis and pattern detection, this approach aims to reduce IEP preparation time by 30–50% while improving the granularity of skill progression targets, as measured by post-implementation student growth metrics. The resulting open-source toolkit will provide educators with real-time decision support, dynamically adjusting recommendations based on ongoing student data. This work directly addresses critical gaps in special education practice by enhancing the scalability of evidence-based personalization, ultimately fostering more equitable outcomes for neurodiverse learners. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets, training complex models with cross-validation, and running large-scale simulations to ensure robustness across educational settings.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Elementary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the elementary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for elementary special education; and teaching elementary education subject matter.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in computational philology and dialectology for Hindi and its related language varieties. While Hindi is among the most widely spoken languages globally, computational tools for analyzing its historical evolution, dialectal diversity, and sociolinguistic applications remain underdeveloped compared to Indo-European counterparts like English. The primary research problem centers on modeling linguistic variation across Hindi dialects—including Braj, Awadhi, and Hindustani—using large-scale textual and speech corpora, which requires processing non-standardized orthographies, phonetic variations, and morphosyntactic shifts. The project will employ computational methods such as neural machine translation for cross-dialect alignment, transformer-based language models for diachronic analysis of pre-modern to contemporary Hindi texts, and graph-based algorithms to map dialect continua. These methods demand significant parallel processing capabilities to handle terabytes of unstructured data, including digitized manuscripts, oral histories, and modern social media content. Additionally, phonetic analysis of under-documented regional variants will utilize GPU-accelerated speech recognition pipelines. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access computational models for dialect classification, a diachronic corpus annotated for linguistic features, and tools for automating the analysis of Hindi’s historical texts. These resources will advance scholarly understanding of language change in the Hindi context while supporting practical applications in NLP for low-resource dialects, educational technology, and cross-dialect communication systems. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to establish a scalable framework for preserving linguistic diversity and enhancing interdisciplinary research capabilities in Hindi studies. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to overcome current bottlenecks in processing speed, model training complexity, and large-data interoperability, thereby enabling novel insights into Hindi’s linguistic ecology.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hindi language, antecessors, and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Hindi; Hindustani; related dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the interplay between infectious disease dynamics, health system capacity, and socio-economic disparities in low-resource settings through advanced computational modeling. Maternal and child health outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia remain disproportionately affected by infectious diseases such as malaria, cholera, and HIV, yet existing intervention strategies often fail to account for the complex, multi-scale interactions between pathogen transmission, healthcare access, and community behavior. To bridge this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling framework integrating epidemiological, geospatial, and behavioral data to simulate disease spread under varying public health policies and resource allocation scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize models using region-specific demographic data, climate patterns, and health infrastructure metrics; execute large-scale sensitivity analyses; and optimize real-time scenario testing for emerging outbreaks. Computational workflows will leverage machine learning to identify high-risk population clusters from heterogeneous datasets (e.g., DHS surveys, satellite-derived mobility patterns, and electronic health records) and reinforcement learning to iteratively improve intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include the identification of cost-effective, equity-focused allocation policies for vaccines, diagnostics, and community health workers, as well as open-source tools for adaptive decision-making in resource-constrained health systems. By quantifying trade-offs between vertical disease programs and horizontal health system strengthening, this work will directly inform national health ministries and global partners participating in the Sustainable Development Goals agenda. The requested computing resources will enable simulations at unprecedented granularity (1 km² resolution across 10+ countries) and temporal scales (decadal projections under climate change scenarios), advancing both methodological innovation and actionable policy insights for reducing preventable mortality in marginalized populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, the social and behavioral sciences, and policy and communications methods to the study of health problems in low- and middle-income countries and regions, and prepares individuals to function as professional international health specialists. Includes instruction in health education and promotion, research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, public nutrition and food security, information systems, program evaluation, medical anthropology, international communication, behavioral sciences, maternal and child health, demography and population policy, and health care finance and economics.

abstract: The management of acute medical conditions in aging populations presents complex challenges due to heterogeneous patient responses, comorbidities, and polypharmacy. Current clinical decision-making tools often lack the granularity to predict individualized outcomes or optimize interventions in real time. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating multi-modal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), biomarker trajectories, and imaging data—to model dynamic treatment responses in critically ill older adults. A key barrier is the computational demand of processing high-dimensional, temporally resolved datasets while accounting for interactions between clinical variables, which existing statistical methods cannot efficiently resolve. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble machine learning models that identify patterns in treatment efficacy and adverse event risks across diverse geriatric cohorts. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing and harmonizing EHR data (structured and unstructured) using natural language processing, followed by feature selection and time-series analysis to extract predictive signatures. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models and recurrent neural networks, will be optimized to simulate patient trajectories under varying intervention strategies. Validation will employ synthetic datasets generated via agent-based modeling to test clinical scenarios while adhering to privacy constraints. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms capable of stratifying patients by likelihood of clinical deterioration, renal/cardiac complications, or delirium during acute care episodes. These tools aim to enable proactive, personalized intervention adjustments, reducing ICU lengths of stay and iatrogenic risks. The scalability of this approach relies on parallelized computing for model training and hyperparameter optimization, which necessitates access to GPU clusters and large-memory nodes. By integrating computational precision with geriatric acute care principles, this work has the potential to redefine clinical benchmarks for aging populations in critical settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Acute Care

abstract: Orthopedic interventions, particularly those involving complex joint mechanics and tissue remodeling, remain challenged by interpatient variability and incomplete understanding of biomechanical load distributions in pathological states. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing patient-specific computational models of musculoskeletal dynamics to optimize surgical planning and predict postoperative outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML)-driven simulations integrating multimodal clinical data, including preoperative imaging, gait analysis, and longitudinal patient outcomes. A key focus is modeling the biomechanical behavior of osteoarthritic joints under varying loading conditions and simulating the effects of surgical interventions such as total knee arthroplasty or spinal fusion. The computational pipeline will process high-resolution CT/MRI datasets to construct 3D anatomical models, simulate tissue stress-strain patterns, and train ML algorithms to correlate biomechanical parameters with clinical endpoints (e.g., implant longevity, pain reduction). HPC resources are critical due to the need for parallelized solving of nonlinear partial differential equations in FEA and the iterative optimization required for neural network training on heterogeneous clinical datasets. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for identifying optimal surgical approaches based on patient-specific anatomy and activity profiles, potentially reducing revision rates and improving functional recovery. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—requiring terabytes of memory allocation and GPU-accelerated computation for real-time parameter sensitivity studies—necessitates scalable HPC infrastructure. This work aims to establish an open-source computational toolkit for orthopedic research, bridging biomechanical theory with clinical decision-making while advancing precision medicine in musculoskeletal care.
cip_definition: Research focused on Orthopedic

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of personalizing mental health interventions for university students by leveraging computational modeling to analyze complex, multi-dimensional datasets. Student counseling services increasingly face diverse needs, including rising rates of anxiety, depression, and academic stress, yet resource constraints limit the scalability of individualized support. Current approaches often rely on generalized interventions, which may overlook nuanced interactions between demographic factors, behavioral patterns, and intervention efficacy. To bridge this gap, we propose developing machine learning models trained on anonymized student records, longitudinal counseling session data, and campus climate surveys to identify predictors of intervention success across subpopulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets (N > 50,000 student profiles) with high dimensionality, including text analytics of counselor notes, temporal patterns in service utilization, and cross-institutional comparisons. Computational workflows will integrate clustering algorithms to detect underserved subgroups, natural language processing to quantify qualitative session themes, and reinforcement learning simulations to optimize resource allocation strategies under varying demand scenarios. The project will produce open-source tools for adaptive intervention design and a framework for ethically deploying predictive analytics in counseling contexts. Expected outcomes include empirically validated guidelines for tailoring services to intersectional identities (e.g., first-generation students with comorbid anxiety) and dynamic prioritization protocols during high-stress academic periods. By enhancing the precision of counseling resource deployment, this work aims to improve equity in mental health support while advancing methodological innovation in education research.
cip_title: Student Counseling and Personnel Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in student counseling and personnel services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop novel computational methods for analyzing the long-time behavior of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in mathematical physics, with a focus on systems exhibiting multiscale dynamics and energy-critical nonlinearities. The central challenge lies in resolving the intricate interplay between dissipative and conservative mechanisms over extended temporal domains, where traditional numerical schemes suffer from prohibitive computational costs or loss of fidelity. We propose an adaptive spectral-Galerkin framework incorporating dynamically refined wavelet bases and exponential time-differencing techniques to maintain accuracy while mitigating stiffness. The methodology will integrate rigorous a posteriori error estimates with machine learning-driven mesh adaptation to optimize basis selection in high-dimensional phase spaces. Implementation will leverage parallelized tensor-contraction algorithms on distributed-memory architectures to handle the curse of dimensionality, with particular emphasis on memory-efficient representations of nonlinear coupling terms. Key deliverables include open-source software for simulating energy-critical PDE systems, quantitative bounds on pattern formation thresholds in turbulent regimes, and classification criteria for asymptotic stability of solitary wave solutions. The computational demands necessitate sustained access to high-performance computing resources due to (1) the need for petascale spatial resolution in three-dimensional turbulence studies, (2) massively parallel eigenvalue analyses of linearized operators over O(10^6)-dimensional Krylov subspaces, and (3) ensemble simulations spanning parameter spaces with 10^4+ configurations for statistical characterization of attractor basins. Successful completion will advance fundamental understanding of nonlinear wave phenomena while establishing scalable computational paradigms for rigorous analysis of infinite-dimensional dynamical systems. Results will directly inform ongoing mathematical investigations into singularity formation in fluid dynamics and nonlinear optics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of theoretical and applied mathematics to the solution of functional problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, numerical statistics, optimization, operational research, signal analysis, wavelets, image processing, fuzzy sets, spline, stochastic analysis, integral equations, differential equations, and partial differential equations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the diffusion of political and cultural ideologies across early modern Europe (1500–1800 CE), a period marked by transformative events such as the Reformation, Enlightenment, and revolutions. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to systematically trace the transmission of ideas across fragmented multilingual sources, including pamphlets, correspondence, and institutional records, which exist in vast but underutilized digital archives. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in how ideologies spread between urban centers, adapted to local contexts, and influenced institutional changes—questions critical to understanding Europe’s transition to modernity. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, network modeling, and geospatial mapping. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to extract semantic and thematic content from digitized texts in six languages, using transformer-based models fine-tuned on historical corpora. Network analysis will map connections between individuals, institutions, and regions based on shared terminology and referenced events, while geospatial tools will visualize temporal and spatial diffusion pathways. HPC resources are essential for training multilingual NLP models, processing terabytes of unstructured text, and simulating large-scale networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking ideological shifts to sociopolitical events, visualizations of transnational knowledge networks, and quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural exchange. This work will advance historiographical debates about European identity formation, the role of print culture in societal change, and the interplay between local and transnational forces. By integrating computational methods with archival research, the project aims to establish a replicable model for data-driven historical inquiry, bridging qualitative and quantitative approaches in the humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of European society, culture, and institutions from the origins to the present. Includes instruction in European historiography, European history sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making for the preservation of at-risk cultural heritage sites, addressing the challenge of balancing conservation priorities with socioeconomic and environmental pressures. Current approaches often rely on fragmented datasets and qualitative assessments, limiting the ability to model dynamic interactions between site degradation factors, policy interventions, and community impacts. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate heterogeneous data streams—including multispectral imaging of artifact decay, regional climate projections, tourism foot traffic patterns, and demographic shifts—into a unified simulation platform. Agent-based modeling will simulate stakeholder behaviors (e.g., local governments, tourism operators, conservation groups) under varying policy scenarios, while machine learning algorithms trained on global case studies will predict site vulnerability thresholds. Geospatial analytics will map risk exposure across multiple heritage corridors, prioritizing interventions based on projected cultural value loss and community equity outcomes. The computational intensity of processing petabyte-scale archival records, high-resolution environmental sensor data, and 3D site reconstructions necessitates parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated neural networks achievable only through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for heritage managers, validated through partnerships with three UNESCO National Committees, that quantifies trade-offs between preservation strategies and regional development goals. By enabling real-time scenario testing at scale, this work aims to advance evidence-based cultural policy while establishing computational social science methodologies for interdisciplinary heritage studies. The resource request directly supports the program’s mandate to bridge technical preservation practices with systemic policy analysis through innovative computational applications.
cip_title: Cultural Resource Management and Policy Analysis
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of cultural studies, public policy analysis, and management skills to planning, promoting, and implementing programs to preserve and protect cultural heritage sites and artifacts. Includes instruction in historical preservation and conservation, business management, policy analysis, applied economics, public relations, applied history, historical archaeology, and environmental impact studies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model complex, multiparty dispute resolution scenarios and predict optimal mediation strategies across diverse contexts. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, evidence-based tools to simulate high-stakes negotiations involving dynamic human behaviors, cultural variables, and institutional constraints. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to account for the combinatorial complexity of interactions in business, legal, and labor disputes, particularly when analyzing how shifting power dynamics or communication patterns influence outcomes. To address this, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating game-theoretic models, agent-based simulations, and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train machine learning models on large datasets of historical arbitration cases and simulated negotiation dialogues, while enabling real-time analysis of hypothetical dispute trajectories under varying parameters. Agent-based models will represent parties with divergent priorities, ethical frameworks, and behavioral biases, simulating thousands of conflict scenarios to identify intervention points that maximize cooperative outcomes. Concurrently, NLP pipelines will process textual records from mediated settlements to extract latent patterns in successful resolution strategies. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible computational toolkit for evaluating dispute resolution tactics in configurable scenarios, (2) evidence-based guidelines for tailoring mediation approaches to specific cultural or institutional contexts, and (3) predictive metrics assessing the stability of proposed agreements under socioeconomic uncertainty. By bridging computational social science with conflict resolution theory, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in mediation training programs while providing empirical insights into the scalability of negotiation frameworks across globalized systems. The project’s computational demands necessitate GPU-accelerated workloads for deep reinforcement learning components and parallelized scenario testing across multi-node clusters.
cip_definition: A program that provides individuals with skills in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration, that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to improve the predictive accuracy of high-impact weather events in a changing climate by advancing the resolution and parameterization of atmospheric models. Current numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems struggle to resolve mesoscale processes—such as convective initiation, aerosol-cloud interactions, and boundary layer turbulence—that govern extreme precipitation, heatwaves, and tropical cyclone intensification. These limitations hinder reliable forecasts at lead times critical for disaster preparedness. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to dynamically couple a global climate model (MPAS-Atmosphere) with a convection-permitting regional model (WRF) at an unprecedented 3 km horizontal resolution over North America and adjacent ocean basins. The computational workflow will integrate ensemble-based data assimilation, machine learning-augmented parameterization of subgrid-scale processes, and probabilistic quantification of climate-driven changes in extreme event frequency. Simulations will span historical (2000–2020) and future (SSP5-8.5, 2040–2060) periods, utilizing CMIP6 boundary conditions. The HPC resources will enable petascale computations across 10,000+ CPU cores to manage memory-intensive tasks, including real-time coupling of ocean-atmosphere fluxes and hyper-resolution cloud microphysics. Expected outcomes include (1) improved representation of precipitation extremes in NWP systems, (2) quantification of model sensitivity to aerosol forcing and sea surface temperature gradients, and (3) open-source parameterization modules for community use. By resolving scale interactions between synoptic systems and convective processes, this work will directly inform climate adaptation strategies while advancing the computational infrastructure required for next-generation Earth system modeling. Resource allocation will support 18 months of simulations, generating over 2 PB of data for public archiving and collaborative analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the prediction of atmospheric motion and climate change. Includes instruction in general circulation patterns, weather phenomena, atmospheric predictability, parameterization, numerical and statistical analysis, large- and mesoscale phenomena, kinematic structures, precipitation processes, and forecasting techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of preparing educators to teach effectively across multiple educational levels (e.g., elementary/middle school) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze complex, multi-level pedagogical interactions. Teacher education programs often lack granular insights into how instructional strategies must adapt to developmental, curricular, and classroom management demands across distinct grade bands. Current research is limited by small-scale datasets and an inability to simulate the dynamic interplay of variables influencing cross-level teaching efficacy. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study integrating heterogeneous datasets—including longitudinal student performance metrics, classroom observation videos, and teacher reflection journals—from a network of partner K-12 schools. Machine learning models will be trained on these multimodal datasets to identify patterns in effective instructional adaptations across grade levels. Agent-based simulations will further model hypothetical classroom scenarios, testing how variations in teacher decision-making (e.g., differentiation strategies, behavior interventions) impact student engagement and learning outcomes in mixed-level contexts. HPC resources are critical due to the scale of video and text data (∼50 TB), the computational demands of training transformer-based models on pedagogical interactions, and the parallelized execution of thousands of simulated classroom environments. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks linking specific teaching practices to contextually appropriate outcomes across levels and (2) interactive training modules for pre-service teachers, informed by simulation results. This work will directly inform the design of competency-based curricula in multi-level teacher education programs, equipping educators with evidence-based strategies to navigate the complexities of teaching across developmental stages.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at more than one educational level, such as a combined program in elementary/secondary, early childhood/elementary, elementary/middle school, or junior high/high school teacher education.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative coalition formation in multiparty systems using advanced computational modeling, with a focus on understanding how institutional rules and interest group networks shape policy outcomes. Despite extensive theoretical work on legislative behavior, existing models struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions between formal procedural constraints, informal lobbying networks, and ideological bargaining in large, heterogeneous legislatures—a gap particularly relevant to contemporary challenges in fragmented democracies. The research employs a multi-method computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM), network analysis, and machine learning-driven text analysis of legislative records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) large-scale ABM simulations parameterized with ideological positions of 5,000+ legislators across 30 countries, (2) dynamic network analysis tracking interest group influence through temporal graph neural networks, and (3) transformer-based NLP analysis of parliamentary speech data to detect coalition signaling patterns. The computational architecture will utilize parallelized Monte Carlo methods for sensitivity testing across institutional scenarios and GPU-accelerated graph processing for real-time network visualization. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for predicting coalition stability under different electoral rules, quantitative measures of procedural vs. network-based influence on legislation, and open-source tools for legislative analytics. Results will advance formal theories of institutional design while providing practical insights for constitutional reformers and international governance organizations. The project’s scale—requiring simultaneous processing of 10TB+ structured voting records, 50 million parliamentary speech tokens, and 100,000 simulated legislative sessions—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation beyond standard campus computing capacities. By integrating political theory with computational social science methods, this work aims to establish new standards for data-intensive legislative studies while directly addressing core questions in comparative political institutions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in political science and government, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the interplay between individualized metabolic heterogeneity and dietary response variability, with a focus on optimizing clinical nutrition strategies for chronic disease management. Current dietary recommendations often adopt generalized approaches, which fail to account for inter-individual differences in metabolic pathways, gut microbiome composition, and epigenetic regulation. This gap limits the efficacy of nutrition interventions for conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disorders. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (metabolomic, metagenomic, and epigenomic profiles) with dynamic systems modeling to predict patient-specific responses to macronutrient manipulation. The project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate metabolic flux variations across virtual patient cohorts, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal clinical datasets to identify biomarkers of dietary responsiveness. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses to account for the combinatorial complexity of nutrient interactions, high-dimensional data integration, and stochastic variability in physiological systems. Expected outcomes include the development of a predictive tool to guide personalized dietary prescriptions and the identification of novel metabolic targets for precision nutrition therapies. This work bridges computational biology, systems nutrition, and clinical dietetics, offering a transformative approach to evidence-based nutrition care that aligns with emerging paradigms in precision medicine. The computational pipelines and models generated will be made publicly available to support future research in niche areas of clinical nutrition science.
cip_title: Dietetics and Clinical Nutrition Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dietetics and clinical nutrition services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize digital pre-press workflows and dynamic color management systems for high-volume graphic and printing production environments. The research addresses critical inefficiencies in current industry practices, where manual calibration, inconsistent color reproduction across substrates, and suboptimal resource allocation during raster image processing (RIP) lead to material waste and production delays. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to simulate multi-variable printing environments at scale, analyzing interactions between digital file parameters, inkjet hardware behavior, and substrate properties. Computational methods will include finite element analysis for droplet dispersion modeling, machine learning algorithms trained on spectral reflectance data from diverse media types, and Monte Carlo simulations to predict optimal ink coverage thresholds. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated rendering frameworks to parallelize complex RIP tasks and reduce computational bottlenecks in halftoning operations. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive toolset for automated device profiling, capable of reducing substrate waste by 15-20% in test environments, and a dynamic color adjustment protocol adaptable to hybrid printing systems. These advancements will directly enhance curriculum development for digital press operation courses while providing industry-relevant benchmarks for sustainable production practices. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the 10+ terabyte datasets generated by high-resolution inline inspection systems and for achieving the millisecond-scale processing times required to model real-world production scenarios. By bridging computational analytics with graphic arts workflows, this research aims to establish new standards for precision and efficiency in next-generation printing operations.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Modern Greek linguistics and literary analysis through large-scale computational methods. The primary research problem centers on analyzing the evolution of Modern Greek dialects and literary styles from the late 15th century to the present, particularly their syntactic, morphological, and semantic shifts in response to sociohistorical changes. Traditional philological approaches face limitations in processing vast textual corpora spanning five centuries, including digitized manuscripts, printed texts, and contemporary digital media. To address this, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines and machine learning models to automate the identification of linguistic patterns, dialectal variations, and stylistic innovations across genres and periods. Computational tasks include training transformer-based models on curated datasets of annotated texts to classify regional dialects, detect diachronic grammatical changes, and map lexical borrowing from contact languages. Additionally, sentiment analysis and topic modeling will be applied to modern Greek literary works to quantify stylistic trends and thematic shifts in 20th- and 21st-century prose and poetry. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling memory-intensive tasks such as parallel processing of multi-gigabyte text corpora, optimizing neural network training on GPU clusters, and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about language change. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access datasets of annotated Modern Greek texts, (2) computational models for dialect classification and literary analysis, and (3) new insights into the relationship between linguistic innovation and cultural identity in post-Ottoman Greece. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological scholarship, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for studying under-resourced languages while advancing interdisciplinary research in Modern Greek studies. The requested resources will directly support graduate student training in digital humanities and strengthen institutional capacity for computationally driven literary-linguistic research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and use of the Greek language in the period dating from the late 15th century to the present. Includes instruction in modern Greek literature, current Greek dialects, and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling and optimization of microbial community dynamics in engineered biosystems for sustainable environmental applications. Microbial consortia play critical roles in bioremediation, bioenergy production, and agricultural biosensing, but their complex interactions—shaped by metabolic cross-feeding, spatial heterogeneity, and environmental stressors—remain poorly understood. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve these multiscale, nonlinear relationships, limiting the design of robust bioengineered systems. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), genome-scale metabolic networks (GSMNs), and machine learning (ML) to predict community stability and function under dynamic conditions. The ABM component will simulate spatial and temporal interactions at the microscale using individual cell behaviors and metabolite diffusion, while GSMNs derived from annotated genomes (e.g., KBase, ModelSEED) will constrain metabolic exchanges. ML algorithms will then identify emergent patterns linking community composition to system-level outputs, such as pollutant degradation rates or biogas yields. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational load of parallelized ABM-GSMN simulations across diverse parameter spaces (e.g., pH, substrate gradients, species ratios) and to train deep neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models of microbial consortia performance in wastewater treatment prototypes and optimized synthetic communities for field-deployable biosensors. By bridging gaps between systems biology and biosystems engineering, this work will provide actionable insights for scaling bio-based technologies, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches in environmental biotechnology. The resulting open-source tools and datasets will be disseminated to accelerate research in bioresource engineering and microbial ecology.
detailed_field: Biological/ biosystems engineering and biomedical technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and management of biological systems; and includes applications to biology, biochemistry, ecology, and microbiology. Includes instruction in organic chemistry; microbiology; biochemistry; chemical, biological, biochemical, and process engineering; thermodynamics; process control; kinetics and reactor design; electric circuits; biosystem modeling; and bioelectronics and instrumentation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern computing systems necessitates advanced resource allocation strategies to optimize performance, energy efficiency, and scalability in heterogeneous architectures. This project seeks to address the challenge of dynamically balancing computational workloads across hybrid CPU-GPU-FPGA platforms, which are critical for applications in machine learning, real-time signal processing, and autonomous systems. Current static allocation methods fail to adapt to variable task demands, leading to suboptimal utilization and energy overhead. To overcome this, we propose a machine learning-driven framework that leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to autonomously distribute tasks based on real-time system telemetry and workload characteristics. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale heterogeneous environments, train deep RL models, and validate allocation policies under diverse scenarios. Key computational tasks include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for policy exploration, GPU-accelerated neural network training, and FPGA-emulated hardware-in-the-loop testing. The project will also develop a lightweight runtime scheduler to deploy optimized policies on physical testbeds. Expected outcomes include a generalizable resource allocation framework that reduces energy consumption by 15-20% while maintaining latency targets, compared to state-of-the-art heuristic approaches. This work will advance the design of adaptive systems for edge-to-cloud computing infrastructures, directly contributing to sustainable computing initiatives. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated to the research community, fostering collaboration in computer engineering and accelerating innovation in energy-aware system design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding how dynamic soil-microbial-plant interactions influence nutrient cycling under varying agricultural management practices. Current models of soil biogeochemistry lack the resolution to simulate spatially heterogeneous processes at microbial scales, limiting predictive accuracy for nutrient availability and crop productivity. To overcome this, we propose developing a high-resolution, mechanistic model integrating soil hydrology, organic matter decomposition, and microbial metabolic networks. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute spatially explicit simulations at micrometer-to-meter scales across realistic agricultural field domains. Parallelized numerical solvers will couple finite element methods for water and solute transport with agent-based microbial community dynamics, while machine learning surrogates will accelerate parameterization of enzymatic kinetics derived from multi-omics datasets. Computational demands are substantial, requiring >10,000 core-hours per scenario to resolve 3D soil pore networks across seasonal timescales. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of management practices that optimize nitrogen retention in root zones, (2) quantitative maps of microbial hotspots controlling carbon sequestration, and (3) open-source simulation tools for predicting soil health responses to crop rotations and tillage regimes. By elucidating microscale drivers of macroscale soil functions, this work will provide a computational framework to advance precision soil management—directly supporting agricultural sustainability goals through reduced fertilizer inputs and enhanced climate resilience. The requested HPC allocation is essential for overcoming current limitations in temporal scaling and spatial representation that hinder conventional soil models.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the soil sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in advancing jewelry design innovation and material optimization. Traditional jewelry arts rely on labor-intensive experimentation to balance aesthetic intent with material constraints, such as metal fatigue, gemstone structural integrity, and thermal behavior during casting or enameling. However, the complex interplay of physical forces, microstructural evolution, and geometric variables in these processes limits the scalability of empirical methods. This project proposes a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics simulations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to model material responses, predict fabrication outcomes, and explore design spaces. HPC resources will enable multi-physics simulations of metalforming techniques (e.g., electroforming current distribution, stress gradients in lapidary work) at micron-scale resolutions, coupled with machine learning-driven optimization of stone-cutting angles for light refraction efficiency. A parallel focus involves training GANs on historical and contemporary jewelry corpora to generate culturally informed, structurally feasible design variants while minimizing material waste. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating process parameters (e.g., alloy composition, annealing schedules) with mechanical and aesthetic properties, reducing trial-and-error cycles in studio practice. The integration of computational materials science with generative design aims to establish a new paradigm for sustainable jewelry production, preserving craft traditions while expanding creative possibilities through digital innovation. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for jewelry educators and workshops demonstrating computational workflows, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between artisanal practices and computational research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by fashioning jewelry from gems, other stones, and precious metals.
