Includes instruction in design concepts, electroforming, enameling, gemology, lapidary technique and art, metal and non-metal casting and molding, metal coloring, metalsmithing and finishing, personal style development, photo etching, and stone cutting and polishing.

abstract: The safe storage and long-term reliability of conventional munitions systems are critical challenges in military logistics, with aging stockpiles and evolving environmental conditions posing risks of accidental ignition, corrosion, and material degradation. Traditional empirical models for predicting munitions stability under variable storage conditions lack the resolution to account for complex interactions between environmental factors (e.g., humidity cycles, thermal gradients) and heterogeneous material compositions in ordnance casings, propellants, and fuzing systems. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate multi-physics aging processes in munitions storage environments at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop coupled finite element models integrating hygrothermal transport, chemical kinetics of propellant decomposition, and mechanochemical corrosion mechanisms across composite materials. Machine learning surrogate models will be trained on simulation outputs to predict critical failure thresholds under stochastic climate scenarios. A parallelized workflow will enable probabilistic risk assessments for diverse global storage sites, incorporating geospatial climate data and real-time sensor inputs. The computational approach addresses gaps in existing military standards by quantifying emergent risks from synergistic degradation pathways, such as stress-corrosion cracking exacerbated by cyclic thermal loading. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for optimizing storage protocols, informing depot maintenance schedules, and guiding material substitutions to extend munitions service life. This work bridges gaps between materials science, environmental engineering, and military logistics, offering a template for data-driven lifecycle management of high-consequence systems where physical testing is prohibitively hazardous or costly.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of ground or sea-based weapons systems, ordinance and munitions. Includes instruction in basic sciences, electronics, systems technology, fluid power, computer science, conventional weapons systems, nuclear weapons systems, munitions systems, storage and safety, equipment operation, guidance and control systems, hazardous materials, corrosion control, nondestructive testing and quality control, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing persuasive communication strategies in dynamic digital environments. Public relations and advertising campaigns increasingly rely on real-time analysis of multi-modal datasets—including social media interactions, consumer behavior metrics, and sentiment trends—to tailor messages for diverse audiences. However, traditional computational tools struggle to process these datasets at scale, limiting the ability to model complex audience responses or predict the cascading effects of messaging across platforms. This research addresses this gap by developing machine learning models to analyze how message framing, visual rhetoric, and platform-specific dynamics collectively influence engagement and persuasion outcomes. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for text-based content, computer vision techniques for image/video analysis, and graph-based algorithms to map information diffusion networks. These methods require parallelized processing of terabytes of heterogeneous data, including historical campaign archives and real-time social media streams, to train deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models) for predictive and prescriptive analytics. By simulating audience segmentation scenarios and A/B testing message variants in virtual environments, the project aims to identify optimal strategies for maximizing reach and impact while minimizing unintended consequences, such as misinformation amplification. Outcomes will provide actionable frameworks for adaptive communication design, enabling practitioners to dynamically adjust campaigns based on computational insights. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive workloads, reducing model training times, and scaling analyses to global audience datasets. This work bridges computational innovation with communication theory, offering novel methodologies for data-driven persuasion research in non-technical academic domains.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on organizational communication, public relations, and advertising; and that prepares individuals to function in a wide range of public and private sector positions requiring the skills of persuasive communication. Includes instruction in communications, public relations, and advertising theory; principles and techniques of persuasion; message/image design; marketing strategy; professional writing; public speaking and multi-media presentation skills; digital communications; and applied research.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that optimize executive coaching strategies for driving organizational change in complex, dynamic environments. While executive coaching is widely used to enhance leadership effectiveness, current methodologies rely heavily on qualitative assessments and static frameworks, limiting scalability and predictive accuracy in rapidly evolving business contexts. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by quantifying the nonlinear relationships between coaching interventions, leader communication patterns, and organizational outcomes. Using a combination of agent-based modeling (ABM) and natural language processing (NLP), the project will simulate multilevel organizational systems where coached executives interact with teams, stakeholders, and external market variables. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large-scale behavioral datasets—drawn from anonymized coaching session transcripts, employee engagement metrics, and real-time performance indicators—to train deep learning architectures that identify patterns in successful change initiatives. A key innovation involves developing adaptive network models that account for cultural, cognitive, and emotional variables influencing coaching efficacy across diverse industries. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics framework that recommends personalized coaching approaches based on system-wide simulations, validated against empirical case studies of Fortune 500 leadership transitions. By integrating psycholinguistic metrics with organizational complexity theory, this computational approach aims to establish evidence-based standards for measuring coaching ROI while advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of behavioral science, computational linguistics, and strategic human capital development. The resulting tools will provide coaches and organizations with dynamically updated strategies to navigate volatility, aligning leadership development with real-time business needs.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on assisting individuals achieve career goals or assisting business leaders achieve organizational change. Includes instruction in executive coaching, group dynamics, leadership, management, organizational behavior, organizational communication, and team building.

abstract: Understanding the dynamics of magnetized stellar atmospheres remains a critical challenge in interpreting high-resolution spectroscopic observations. Current one-dimensional models fail to capture the complex interplay between magnetic fields, radiation transfer, and plasma kinetics, leading to systematic uncertainties in derived stellar parameters and chemical abundances. This project aims to develop three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations coupled with non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) radiation transfer calculations to model stellar atmospheres with unprecedented fidelity. The computational approach leverages GPU-accelerated solvers for the MHD equations and a novel sparse matrix formulation for non-LTE line transfer, enabling simultaneous resolution of small-scale magnetic structures and global atmospheric dynamics. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the 10^8–10^9 degree-of-freedom problem sizes required for converged solutions across parameter spaces encompassing different spectral types, metallicities, and magnetic field configurations. The resulting synthetic spectra will be validated against multi-epoch observations from instruments like ESPRESSO and upcoming datasets from the Extremely Large Telescope. By establishing physically consistent models of magnetized atmospheres, this work will directly impact the interpretation of galactic archaeology surveys, exoplanet host star characterization, and precision tests of stellar evolution theories. The developed computational framework will be made available to the community through open-source platforms, enhancing the capability of astrophysical simulations to leverage next-generation exascale computing architectures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and observational study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena. Includes instruction in cosmology, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the drivers of phylogenetic discordance and biogeographic patterns in a hyper-diverse clade of tropical angiosperms, integrating large-scale molecular, morphological, and ecological datasets to resolve longstanding uncertainties in evolutionary relationships and diversification processes. A major challenge in systematic biology is reconciling conflicting phylogenetic signals arising from incomplete lineage sorting, hybridization, and convergent trait evolution, particularly in lineages with rapid radiations. To address this, we will employ a computational pipeline combining Bayesian species-tree inference, divergence-time estimation, and comparative methods to analyze genome-scale sequence data (targeted enrichment sequencing), fossil-calibrated trait matrices, and historical biogeographic reconstructions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the project’s scope: datasets include ~2,000 loci across 500+ species, 10,000+ morphological character states, and probabilistic biogeographic models requiring iterative likelihood calculations across millions of tree topologies. Key computational steps include parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for multilocus coalescent models, machine learning-assisted morphological homology assessments, and likelihood-based tests for trait-dependent diversification. The requested resources will enable efficient processing of these analyses, which are otherwise computationally intractable on standard laboratory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a robust, time-calibrated phylogeny resolving contentious nodes in the focal clade, (2) identification of ecological and biogeographic factors correlated with diversification rate shifts, and (3) novel protocols for integrating high-dimensional morphological data into phylogenomic frameworks. This work will advance systematic theory by clarifying how heterogeneous evolutionary processes shape taxonomic diversity in tropical hotspots, while providing open-access computational workflows and a curated database of phenotypic characters to support future studies. Results will directly inform conservation prioritization by identifying evolutionarily distinct lineages in threatened ecosystems.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical inefficiencies in construction project management and finishing processes through advanced computational modeling and data-driven decision-making. Construction projects often face delays, cost overruns, and quality discrepancies due to fragmented workflows, unpredictable material behavior, and insufficient real-time inspection capabilities. To mitigate these challenges, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale simulation frameworks integrating agent-based modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) techniques. The computational models will simulate dynamic interactions between construction workflows, material performance under environmental stressors, and automated inspection protocols. Key objectives include optimizing resource allocation for finishing tasks, predicting material degradation in diverse climatic conditions, and training ML models to detect defects in real-time via sensor and image data from construction sites. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data—including LiDAR scans, thermal imaging, and IoT sensor streams—and to run parallelized simulations evaluating thousands of scenario permutations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for project timeline adjustment, risk-aware resource scheduling algorithms, and a cloud-enabled inspection platform for automated quality assurance. These innovations aim to reduce construction waste by up to 20%, improve adherence to project deadlines, and enhance the durability of finished structures. By advancing computational methods tailored to construction management, this work will contribute novel methodologies to the field while supporting sustainable practices through data-driven optimization. The resulting open-source tools and datasets will be disseminated to industry and academic partners, fostering collaboration in smart construction technologies.
cip_title: Building/ Construction Finishing, Management, and Inspection, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in building/construction finishing, management, and inspection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives across Western Europe from the medieval period to the early modern era, with a focus on underrepresented regional identities. Traditional scholarship in Western European Studies has often relied on manual analysis of localized textual and visual sources, limiting the scale at which transregional cultural dynamics can be examined. To address this gap, the research will employ computational text and image analysis methods on a curated corpus of digitized manuscripts, regional chronicles, and artistic works from Britain, Iberia, and the Western Mediterranean. The primary research problem centers on identifying and mapping patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance that shaped collective identities in borderland regions, particularly where Christian, Islamic, and Jewish traditions intersected. A hybrid computational approach will be implemented, combining transformer-based natural language processing models for multilingual text analysis (Latin, Old French, Medieval Arabic, and regional vernaculars) with graph neural networks to model cultural transmission networks across time and space. Image recognition algorithms will supplement textual analysis by detecting stylistic motifs in illuminated manuscripts and architectural illustrations. The scale of data—over 15TB of digitized primary sources from seven archival partners—necessitates distributed computing for parallelized feature extraction and dimensionality reduction. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas of cultural influence trajectories and a methodological framework for computationally assisted humanities research that bridges regional specificity with macro-scale analysis. This work will provide new insights into how decentralized cultural production in premodern Western Europe contributed to pluralistic identities, challenging homogenized narratives of regional heritage. By integrating HPC capabilities with humanistic inquiry, the project aims to establish scalable protocols for analyzing fragmented historical sources while advancing interdisciplinary dialogue in area studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of historical Western Europe, defined as including Britain, Ireland, France, the Low Countries, the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Western Mediterranean, and related island groups and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the diagnosis and monitoring of hematologic disorders through advanced computational analysis of blood-related data. Current diagnostic methods in hematology rely heavily on manual interpretation of laboratory tests, which can be time-consuming and prone to variability, particularly for complex conditions such as myelodysplastic syndromes, thrombotic disorders, and hemoglobinopathies. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing machine learning models to identify multidimensional patterns in blood cell morphology, coagulation dynamics, and genomic biomarkers. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale datasets, including high-resolution microscopy images of blood smears, flow cytometry outputs, and whole-exome sequencing data from patient cohorts. Computational workflows will integrate convolutional neural networks for image analysis, graph-based algorithms for mapping protein interaction networks in coagulation pathways, and Bayesian statistical models to correlate genetic variants with clinical outcomes. A key innovation involves simulating blood cell deformation and shear stress dynamics under pathological conditions using molecular dynamics frameworks optimized for GPU-accelerated systems. These simulations will inform the development of predictive models for thrombotic risk assessment. The project’s outcomes are expected to yield (1) automated tools for standardized classification of blood cell abnormalities, (2) novel biomarkers for early detection of hematologic malignancies, and (3) computational frameworks to personalize anticoagulation therapies. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge gaps between experimental hematology data and clinical decision-making, ultimately enhancing diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic strategies for blood disorders. The resource request supports the training of next-generation hematology technologists in computational methodologies, aligning with the program’s mission to integrate technology-driven solutions into modern laboratory practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists and health care professionals, to perform tests and analyses of blood samples. Includes instruction in clinical laboratory procedures; blood anatomy and physiology; cellular and molecular biology; blood pathology and disease indicators; quantitative, qualitative, and coagulation testing methodologies; equipment operation and maintenance; and record-keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical mechanisms underlying biofield therapies—such as Qi Gong and Therapeutic Touch—which purportedly modulate physiological states through non-invasive energy interactions. Despite anecdotal and clinical evidence of their effects on pain, inflammation, and stress, the fundamental principles of energy transfer, field dynamics, and cellular response remain poorly characterized. A critical barrier is the lack of multiscale computational models capable of simulating low-energy bioelectromagnetic interactions within biologically relevant systems. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven study integrating quantum mechanical, molecular dynamics, and continuum-level electromagnetic simulations. These models will map how externally applied energy fields (e.g., low-frequency electromagnetic waves or simulated "healing" waveforms) interact with ion channels, cell membranes, and tissue networks, focusing on mitochondrial voltage gradients, ATP production, and redox signaling pathways. Simulations will be parameterized using experimental data from in vitro bioelectric assays and validated against high-resolution biosensor measurements. The HPC framework will enable parallelized optimization of field parameters (frequency, amplitude, spatial distribution) and probabilistic analysis of emergent tissue-scale effects. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of plausible biophysical pathways for biofield-induced cellular modulation, (2) predictive models linking therapeutic parameters to specific physiological responses, and (3) a scalable computational platform for designing targeted energy-based interventions. By elucidating mechanisms at the intersection of biophysics and alternative medicine, this work aims to establish a quantitative foundation for optimizing biofield therapies, addressing skepticism about their scientific plausibility while advancing computational tools for studying subtle energy interactions in biological systems. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics (Amber, GROMACS), finite element electromagnetic modeling (COMSOL), and custom Python-based multiscale integration workflows requiring ~500,000 core-hours and large-memory nodes for terascale datasets.
cip_title: Energy and Biologically Based Therapies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative, complementary, and somatic health and therapeutic services not elsewhere classified (bioenergetics, cranio-sacral therapy, Therapeutic Touch, Qi Gong, and others).

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for the study of under-documented African languages by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze linguistic structures, dialectal variations, and oral literatures. Many African languages lack robust digital corpora and tools, hindering large-scale comparative studies and the preservation of endangered linguistic traditions. The research focuses on four language families (Niger-Congo, Nilo-Saharan, Khoisan, and Chadic) to investigate patterns in phonology, morphology, and syntax, as well as the transcription and semantic analysis of oral narratives. Computational challenges include processing sparse, heterogeneous data—such as audio recordings of oral traditions, annotated texts, and dialect maps—and training machine learning models to detect cross-linguistic features. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multimodal datasets, dynamic simulation of language evolution, and the deployment of transformer-based models for low-resource language tasks. Key methodologies include developing pipelines for automated phonetic alignment, dialect classification using graph-based algorithms, and semantic network analysis of oral literature. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access digital repositories, computational models for typological comparisons, and tools to support community-led language preservation. This work will advance linguistic theory by uncovering structural convergences and divergences across African languages, while directly contributing to global efforts to sustain linguistic diversity. The project’s computational outputs will be integrated into collaborative platforms for Africanist researchers, fostering interdisciplinary partnerships in digital humanities and language technology. By scaling analyses that are infeasible on local computing infrastructure, this research bridges a critical gap between traditional linguistic scholarship and data-driven methodologies, ensuring African languages are equitably represented in computational linguistics research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the African continent, including, but not limited to, Bantu languages, Nilo-Saharan languages, Niger-Congo languages, Khoisan languages, and the Chadic and Ethiopic languages of the Hamito-Semitic language family. Includes instruction in philology, dialects, and oral and written literatures.

abstract: This research project addresses the challenge of optimizing digital content distribution and audience engagement strategies for visual arts institutions in an increasingly data-saturated media landscape. While arts organizations generate vast quantities of digital engagement data—including user interactions with virtual exhibitions, social media metrics, and streaming patterns for digital artworks—many lack the computational capacity to analyze these datasets in ways that inform responsive, equitable resource allocation. This project proposes the development of a machine learning framework to model audience behavior, forecast engagement trends, and simulate the impact of curatorial and promotional decisions on institutional sustainability. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will process multi-modal datasets (image, video, text, and transactional records) from partner museums and digital art platforms using convolutional neural networks for visual pattern recognition and transformer-based models for temporal behavioral analysis. Computational experiments will simulate resource allocation scenarios under varying constraints, including budget fluctuations, shifting audience demographics, and emerging platform algorithms. The outcomes will yield a dynamic decision-support tool that enables arts managers to balance artistic missions with operational viability, particularly for underrepresented visual media forms. By quantifying relationships between digital curation practices, audience retention, and financial outcomes at scale, this work aims to advance evidence-based management frameworks for the visual arts sector while preserving creative autonomy. The requested computing resources are critical to handling the dimensionality of cultural consumption data and iterating complex simulations that account for heterogeneous variables in global media ecosystems.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Arts, Entertainment, and Media Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage various aspects of the visual arts, performing arts, and entertainment media industries. Includes instruction in business and financial management, marketing and fund-raising, labor relations for the arts, event promotion and management, product and artist management, and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision soil management by developing high-resolution computational models of soil-plant-water dynamics under variable agricultural conditions. Current models often lack the spatial granularity and scalability to predict nutrient cycling, moisture retention, and root-soil interactions across heterogeneous landscapes, limiting their utility for optimizing crop yields and soil health. To address this, we propose a coupled modeling framework integrating process-based agrohydrological simulations with machine learning (ML) to capture multiscale soil behavior. The research will parameterize soil properties using regional datasets spanning texture, organic matter, and microbial activity, then simulate interactions between crop growth, irrigation, and soil biogeochemistry at meter-scale resolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to run ensemble simulations of the HYDRUS-1D and DSSAT models across thousands of soil-crop-climate combinations, with ML applied to generalize results into predictive tools for underrepresented soil types. Expected outcomes include (1) improved forecasts of nitrogen leaching and water-use efficiency under drought scenarios, (2) identification of soil management thresholds to maintain productivity in degraded systems, and (3) open-source decision support tools for site-specific amendment and irrigation planning. The computational workload requires parallelized execution across 500+ CPU cores to handle stochastic parameter sampling and 3D soil profile analyses, with total memory demands exceeding 8 TB for transient simulation outputs. By bridging gaps between empirical soil science and computational agronomy, this work will provide scalable frameworks to address soil-specific constraints in sustainable intensification, directly benefiting agricultural practitioners and policymakers.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that generally focuses on the scientific classification of soils, soil properties, and their relationship to agricultural crops. Includes instruction in soil chemistry, soil physics, soil biology, soil fertility, morphogenesis, mineralogy, hydrology, agronomy, and soil conservation and management.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation aims to optimize functional outcomes for children with disabilities, but clinical decision-making remains constrained by heterogeneous data sources and complex interactions between biological, biomechanical, and environmental factors. Current analytical approaches struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, neuroimaging, wearable sensor data, and electronic health records—while accounting for individual variability in treatment response. This project proposes a computational framework to model patient-specific recovery trajectories and predict optimal rehabilitation strategies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will develop machine learning pipelines to harmonize multimodal datasets from a retrospective cohort of 2,500 children with cerebral palsy, traumatic brain injury, and spinal cord injuries. Predictive models will identify biomarkers of motor and cognitive recovery, while biomechanical simulations of musculoskeletal dynamics will evaluate the efficacy of assistive devices and therapeutic exercises under varying physiological constraints. HPC resources are critical for training deep learning architectures on large-scale neuroimaging data, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in treatment outcomes, and optimizing hyperparameters across diverse patient subgroups. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for personalizing rehabilitation protocols, validated against a prospective cohort of 200 patients. This work will advance precision medicine in pediatric rehabilitation by linking computational phenotyping to evidence-based interventions, ultimately reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice. The tools and datasets generated will be shared openly to accelerate innovation in rehabilitation science, with direct implications for improving functional independence and quality of life in children with disabilities.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Rehabilitation

abstract: Improving nutrient utilization efficiency in livestock is critical for enhancing animal health, reducing production costs, and minimizing environmental impacts. However, optimizing feed formulations to meet dynamic physiological and metabolic demands remains a challenge due to the complex interactions between dietary components, gut microbiota, and host metabolism. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model nutrient metabolism in ruminants, with a focus on identifying synergistic relationships between feed additives, microbial communities, and host enzymatic pathways. We will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic profiles) from cattle trials with mechanistic models of rumen fermentation and nutrient absorption. Machine learning approaches will be applied to predict microbial community responses to varying dietary ratios of proteins, lipids, and carbohydrate fractions, while agent-based simulations will explore emergent metabolic behaviors at cellular and tissue scales. The computational pipeline will also incorporate breed-specific genomic variations affecting nutrient uptake efficiency. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for designing precision feed regimens that maximize nitrogen retention, minimize methane emissions, and reduce undigested nutrient waste. By elucidating the systems-level dynamics of nutrient utilization, this work will advance foundational knowledge in animal biochemistry while providing actionable strategies for sustainable livestock production. The scale of metagenomic data analysis, coupled with the need for real-time parameter optimization in complex metabolic networks, necessitates access to HPC resources for parallelized computation and large-scale data integration. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for feed formulation optimization, benefiting both academic research and agricultural stakeholders.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biology and chemistry of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, water, vitamins, and feed additives as related to animal health and the production of improved animal products. Includes instruction in nutrition science, animal health and physiology, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, animal husbandry, and food science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize facility-wide operational decision-making in correctional environments through high-fidelity simulation of dynamic inmate behavior and resource allocation patterns. Corrections systems face complex challenges in balancing security, rehabilitation outcomes, and operational efficiency, yet lack robust predictive tools to model how facility policies interact with human behavioral factors at scale. Current approaches rely on static risk assessments and historical data analysis, which fail to capture emergent phenomena in overcrowded facilities or account for real-time behavioral cascades. We propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) system leveraging high-performance computing to simulate multi-scale interactions between inmates, staff protocols, and environmental constraints across temporal horizons. The computational architecture will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including anonymized movement logs, incident reports, and program participation records—to parameterize autonomous agents with empirically grounded behavioral profiles. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will enable exploration of "what-if" scenarios for policy adjustments, staffing patterns, and intervention timing. Machine learning components will identify latent patterns in historical disturbance events to improve model fidelity. Expected outcomes include a decision-support toolkit capable of predicting facility hot spots, evaluating procedural changes before implementation, and quantifying trade-offs between security protocols and rehabilitative programming access. By bridging computational social science with correctional operations research, this work aims to establish new methodologies for evidence-based corrections management while maintaining strict ethical safeguards for data anonymization and bias mitigation. The resource-intensive nature of simulating thousands of interacting agents across extended time horizons necessitates dedicated HPC allocations to achieve sufficient statistical power and operational realism.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study the theories and principles, of correctional science and to function as professional corrections officers and other workers in public and/or private incarceration facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the discovery and mechanistic analysis of bioactive natural products with therapeutic potential. Despite the rich diversity of compounds in plants, microbes, and marine organisms, identifying those with medicinal value remains labor-intensive and constrained by limitations in traditional experimental screening. Computational approaches can accelerate this process, but the scale of chemical space in natural product libraries and the complexity of modeling interactions between compounds and biological targets demand significant computational power. This project aims to address these challenges through two integrated computational workflows. First, molecular docking and virtual screening will be performed on a curated library of 500,000+ natural product structures to predict binding affinities for disease-relevant targets, including inflammatory enzymes and antimicrobial resistance proteins. Second, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will characterize the stability and conformational dynamics of top candidate complexes at atomic resolution, with simulations extending to the microsecond scale. These workflows will be complemented by machine learning models trained on existing bioactivity data to predict ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity) properties, prioritizing compounds with viable pharmacokinetic profiles. The HPC environment is critical for managing the parallelized processing of large ligand/target datasets, long-timescale MD simulations requiring GPU acceleration, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel lead compounds for experimental validation, structural insights into target engagement mechanisms, and predictive frameworks to guide future bioprospecting efforts. By integrating computational chemistry with ethnobotanical knowledge and experimental data from collaborators (e.g., mass spectrometry, bioassay results), this work will enhance the efficiency of natural product drug discovery and contribute to the understanding of structure-activity relationships in medicinal chemistry. The requested resources will directly support these computationally intensive tasks, enabling workflows that are infeasible on standard laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for educators serving students with speech or language impairments. A critical challenge in this field is the dynamic, individualized nature of language development and intervention efficacy. Traditional methods for designing and adjusting individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual observation and static assessment data, limiting educators’ ability to predict student progress or optimize interventions in real time. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale linguistic datasets, longitudinal student performance records, and machine learning (ML) models to simulate and predict language acquisition patterns under varying intervention strategies. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze speech samples from students with diverse impairments (e.g., phonological disorders, aphasia) and generate synthetically augmented training data to account for low-resource scenarios. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models, will be trained to identify subtle patterns in language development trajectories and correlate them with intervention outcomes. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments to test the scalability of personalized strategies under resource constraints. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of audio and textual data, train complex ML models with hyperparameter optimization, and run high-fidelity simulations iteratively. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access toolset for educators to dynamically adjust IEP targets based on predictive analytics, (2) a repository of anonymized speech datasets with synthetic augmentations, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for deploying computational tools in special education settings. By bridging gaps between special education practice and computational innovation, this work aims to reduce IEP design latency, improve intervention personalization, and empower educators with scalable, equity-focused resources.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Speech or Language Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study and design of educational services for children or adults with speech and language impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with speech and language impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with speech disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of automated medical transcription systems, addressing critical gaps in processing complex medical terminology, speaker variability, and real-time dictation. While human medical transcriptionists remain essential for verifying context and nuance, growing demand for rapid, error-free documentation in healthcare settings necessitates scalable computational tools. Current speech-to-text models often struggle with domain-specific jargon, multilingual accents, and overlapping dialogue in clinical recordings, leading to delays and inaccuracies that risk patient safety. To overcome these challenges, we propose training a suite of deep learning models on a curated corpus of annotated medical dictations, including multispeaker clinical conferences, patient histories, and procedural reports. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize transformer-based architectures for context-aware speech recognition, integrating domain-adapted language models fine-tuned on medical lexicons (e.g., ICD-10 codes, pharmacological terms). Parallelized workflows will be implemented to preprocess and augment audio data, anonymize protected health information, and validate outputs against gold-standard human transcripts. Key innovations include dynamic acoustic modeling for diverse recording environments and a hybrid system that flags low-confidence segments for human review. Expected outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in post-editing time for transcriptionists and improved model robustness across dialects and noise conditions. By providing open-access tools and benchmarks, this work will directly support healthcare documentation workflows, reduce administrative burdens on clinical staff, and establish reproducible methods for ethical AI-assisted transcription in regulated medical contexts. The computational demands of training large-vocabulary models on terabytes of sensitive audio data necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to ensure timely iteration and scalability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to execute verbatim medical conference minutes, medical reports, and medical orders. Includes instruction in dictation and simultaneous recording, analysis of notes and visual evidence, medical terminology, data processing applications and skills, formal medical report and correspondence formats, professional standards, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize diagnostic workflows and enhance predictive modeling for waived laboratory testing, a critical component of clinical laboratory operations. Medical laboratory assistants (MLAs) routinely perform high-volume, repetitive testing under CLIA-waived protocols, yet inefficiencies persist in error detection, quality control analytics, and integration of multi-source data (e.g., phlebotomy logs, instrument outputs, and patient demographics). The research problem centers on developing computational tools to address these gaps, enabling MLAs to focus on higher-value tasks while improving diagnostic reliability. We propose a two-phase approach: First, we will train machine learning models on historical laboratory datasets to identify patterns linked to pre-analytical errors (e.g., mislabeled specimens, hemolyzed samples) and instrument calibration drift. Second, we will simulate real-time workflows using agent-based modeling to evaluate the impact of predictive alerts on laboratory throughput and error rates. These models will integrate heterogeneous data streams, including time-stamped instrument logs, technician performance metrics, and environmental sensor data from laboratory equipment. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of structured and unstructured data, run parallelized simulations across diverse operational scenarios, and iteratively refine deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based anomaly detection). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for error prediction, validated workflow optimizations for CLIA-waived settings, and a benchmarking framework to quantify resource savings. The project aligns with the growing emphasis on data-driven quality improvement in laboratory medicine, offering scalable solutions to reduce diagnostic delays and enhance MLA training through synthetic data generation. By bridging computational innovation with practical laboratory workflows, this work aims to strengthen the role of MLAs in delivering precision diagnostics while advancing educational competencies in laboratory informatics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians or laboratory scientists or technologists, to perform waived testing procedures (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988), phlebotomy, and other duties in support of laboratory teams. Includes instruction in clinical procedures, various laboratory tests, laboratory mathematics, computer technology, equipment operation and maintenance, sterilization and safety, communications skills, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize public transportation network design and operations under dynamic demand and environmental constraints, aligning with the goals of equitable access, cost efficiency, and emissions reduction. Urban transportation systems face escalating challenges due to population growth, climate policies, and fluctuating mobility patterns, yet existing static optimization models fail to account for real-time behavioral data or multi-objective trade-offs at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a two-stage approach integrating agent-based simulation with reinforcement learning to model passenger decision-making and system-wide outcomes. The first stage employs granular, GIS-enabled traffic and ridership datasets to simulate multimodal travel patterns across a metropolitan case study region. The second stage trains deep reinforcement learning models on these simulations to iteratively optimize route frequencies, vehicle allocations, and pricing strategies while balancing equity metrics, operator costs, and emissions targets. Computational demands are substantial, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of scenarios, neural network training on high-dimensional spatial-temporal data, and sensitivity analyses of policy interventions. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive transit planning, validated against real-world data from partner agencies, and policy insights on incentivizing sustainable mode shifts. By enabling rapid analysis of complex interactions between infrastructure investments, pricing mechanisms, and traveler behavior, this work aims to advance evidence-based transportation management practices while reducing computational barriers for public-sector planners. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the project’s scale, as conventional cloud infrastructure cannot support the memory and processing requirements of billion-agent simulations or the concurrent training of multiple optimization models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, policy, law, and practices required to administrate and operate public transportation facilities, networks, services, and systems. Includes instruction in demand analysis and forecasting, environmental planning, facilities design and construction, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, multi- and intermodal transportation systems, project management, public administration, public policy, transportation economics, transportation law, transportation operations, transportation systems, and transportation technologies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug development pipelines necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in optimizing therapeutic efficacy, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory compliance. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate computational workflows central to preclinical drug design and industrial process optimization. A key focus is the integration of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML) models to predict drug-target binding affinities, stability under industrial-scale production conditions, and potential metabolic degradation pathways. Current in silico methods for these tasks are limited by the computational expense of simulating large protein-ligand systems or microbial expression vectors over biologically relevant timescales. By parallelizing MD simulations across GPU nodes, we aim to model conformational dynamics of plasmid-derived biologics and small-molecule drug candidates at unprecedented resolution. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on existing pharmacokinetic datasets to predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties, with model validation performed using molecular docking results. A second component focuses on optimizing microbial strain engineering for industrial drug synthesis through genome-scale metabolic modeling. Constraint-based reconstruction and analysis (COBRA) of bacterial and fungal systems will be scaled using distributed computing to identify gene knockout targets that maximize yield while minimizing byproduct formation. These computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from partner pharmaceutical labs. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of virtual screening pipelines, reducing reliance on costly trial-and-error experimentation. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for candidate drug prioritization, strain design blueprints for scalable synthesis, and quality control protocols informed by stability simulations. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on bridging pharmacological science and industrial management by providing computational tools to de-risk translational processes, streamline intellectual property strategy through early patentability assessments, and enhance regulatory compliance via in silico quality assurance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific application of pharmacology, pharmaceutics, and industrial management to the development, production, marketing, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. Includes instruction in industrial microbiology, plasmids, expression vectors, protein chemistry, assay and evaluation, drug synthesis and purification, quality control, industrial management, production security, patent procedures, intellectual property regulations and issues, patent enforcement and defense, and research design and testing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel framework for visualizing complex, multidimensional environmental data to enhance interpretability and decision-making across scientific and public stakeholders. Despite advances in data collection, critical challenges remain in effectively communicating intricate ecological interactions and climate feedback loops to diverse audiences, hindering collaborative mitigation efforts. Traditional visualization tools often oversimplify multidimensional relationships or fail to adapt to user-specific cognitive and perceptual needs. To address this, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating ecological modeling, perceptual psychology, and high-performance computing (HPC) to create dynamic, user-responsive visualization systems. The research will utilize HPC resources to process large-scale environmental datasets—including satellite-derived biogeochemical cycles, biodiversity surveys, and climate model outputs—through parallelized dimensionality reduction algorithms and generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained to identify latent patterns. These computational outputs will drive an adaptive visualization engine that dynamically adjusts data representation based on real-time eye-tracking metrics and user expertise levels, informed by cognitive load theory. The project will validate visualization efficacy through controlled experiments measuring policy-makers’ and scientists’ decision accuracy and response times across interface iterations. Expected outcomes include open-source visualization tools optimized for cross-disciplinary environmental communication, a cognitive benchmarking database for visualization design, and novel methods for integrating machine learning with perceptual adaptation in HPC workflows. By bridging ecological complexity with human-centered design, this work aims to establish new standards for data-driven environmental governance while advancing computational techniques at the intersection of cognitive science and scalable data analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and derive meaning from data by using visual presentation tools and techniques. Includes instruction in cognitive science, computer programming, data management, data visualization theory, graphic design, infographics, perceptual psychology, statistics, and visual design.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of atmospheric dynamics and cloud formation mechanisms in gas giant planets, with a focus on Neptune’s turbulent storm systems, using high-resolution numerical simulations. Despite advances in telescopic and spacecraft observations, the processes driving the evolution, stability, and energy transfer of Neptune’s dark vortices and transient cloud systems remain poorly constrained. Current models, limited by coarse resolution and simplified parameterizations, fail to capture the multi-scale interactions between planetary-scale waves, convective turbulence, and condensable species (e.g., CH4, H2S) in the upper troposphere. To address this gap, we propose a series of three-dimensional atmospheric simulations using the Explicit Planetary Isentropic-Coordinate (EPIC) model, optimized for HPC environments. The simulations will resolve dynamical features down to 10 km scales—critical for capturing moist convective processes—while incorporating radiative transfer and microphysical schemes for methane cloud formation. The computational workflow will leverage adaptive time-stepping and hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization to manage the high computational cost of multi-annual simulations across Neptune’s 16-hour rotational cycle. We request 1.2 million core-hours on a GPU-accelerated cluster to conduct parameter sweeps testing the roles of wind shear, latent heating, and background methane humidity in vortex longevity. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of mechanisms sustaining Neptune’s cyclonic storms against planetary-scale dissipation, (2) improved cloud microphysics parameterizations for future ice giant climate models, and (3) datasets to support observational campaigns by the James Webb Space Telescope and ground-based observatories. By bridging mesoscale dynamics to planetary-scale circulation, this work will inform comparative studies of extreme weather across solar system planets and exoplanetary analogues, while advancing computational methods for next-generation planetary atmospheric models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of planets and their planetary systems, small objects, and related gravitational systems. Includes instruction in the structure and composition of planetary surfaces and interiors, planetary atmospheres, moons, ring systems, gas clouds, magnetospheres, satellites, orbital mechanics, asteroids and comets, solar system evolution and dynamics, planetary evolution, gravitational physics, and radiation physics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the role of tumor microenvironmental stressors in driving metabolic plasticity and metastatic progression in epithelial cancers. A critical gap in cancer biology lies in understanding how dynamic interactions between hypoxic gradients, nutrient availability, and mechanical forces collectively reprogram cellular decision-making in heterogeneous tumors. Current experimental models struggle to capture the spatiotemporal complexity of these systems-level physiological interactions. To address this, we will develop a 3D multiscale computational platform integrating discrete cell-scale agent-based models with continuum tissue-scale biophysical simulations. The framework will parameterize cancer cell responses to microenvironmental variables—including oxygen diffusion, extracellular matrix stiffness, and glucose distribution—using empirical data from our lab’s prior organoid studies and in vivo imaging. HPC resources will enable iterative simulations of tumor growth under varying metabolic constraints, with parallelized solving of coupled differential equations governing nutrient transport, cellular energetics, and phenotype switching. Key outcomes will include predictive maps of metastatic propensity based on microenvironmental stressor combinations and identification of nodal points in metabolic decision-making networks that could be targeted to disrupt adaptation. This work will provide the first systems-level computational model of cancer cell functional dynamics that explicitly links subcellular metabolic pathways to tissue-scale physiological forces. By clarifying how tumors exploit physiological plasticity to overcome microenvironmental limitations, the results will advance translational strategies to impair metastatic fitness while avoiding the pitfalls of targeting static molecular vulnerabilities. The computational framework will also serve as a community resource for simulating therapeutic interventions within realistic, evolving tumor ecosystems.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the functional dynamics, morphology, and biochemical and biophysical communications within organisms and between living systems at all levels of complexity and integration. Includes instruction in reproduction, growth, hormonal action, vascular function, respiration, digestion, sensory perception and processing, sensorimotor integration, signal encoding and conveyance, homeostasis, physical function and malfunction, evolutionary physiology, and disease processes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to optimize parametric Computer-Aided Design (CAD) workflows for complex mechanical systems, addressing inefficiencies in current drafting processes that hinder rapid prototyping and precision in manufacturing. Traditional CAD tools often struggle with iterative design optimization under multi-physics constraints (e.g., thermal, structural, fluid dynamics), particularly when handling high-dimensional parameter spaces or non-linear material behaviors. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize generative design algorithms and automate finite element analysis (FEA) simulations integrated with CAD software APIs. The research will focus on two core objectives: (1) developing scalable algorithms to distribute parametric design tasks across HPC nodes, enabling real-time exploration of design alternatives, and (2) creating machine learning surrogates trained on HPC-accelerated simulation data to predict mechanical performance metrics directly within CAD environments. The computational workflow will be validated using case studies involving additive manufacturing toolpath optimization and CNC machining tolerance analysis, with emphasis on geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) compliance. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in iterative design cycle times for complex assemblies, improved simulation accuracy through high-resolution meshing enabled by HPC-scale memory, and open-source CAD plugin tools to democratize access to advanced optimization capabilities. By bridging gaps between mechanical drafting practices and computational engineering, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for CAD/CADD efficiency in small-to-medium manufacturing enterprises while providing pedagogical resources for integrating HPC methodologies into mechanical drafting curricula. The requested computing resources will directly support GPU-accelerated simulation batches, large-scale parameter sweeps, and data storage for benchmarking datasets.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision anesthesiology through the development of predictive models for perioperative risk stratification and personalized anesthesia protocols. A critical challenge in clinical anesthesiology is the optimization of dynamic, patient-specific variables—such as drug responses, hemodynamic stability, and pain modulation—amidst the complexity of surgical and critical care environments. Current approaches to anesthesia management rely on population-based guidelines, which inadequately address interindividual variability in comorbidities, genetic factors, and real-time physiological data. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) with multiscale physiological modeling to predict patient-specific outcomes under diverse anesthesia regimens. High-resolution electronic health records (EHRs), intraoperative monitoring streams, and biomarker data from 15,000+ surgical cases will be processed to train ensemble ML models for forecasting hemodynamic instability, opioid sensitivity, and postoperative pain trajectories. Concurrently, finite element modeling of drug diffusion and physiological system dynamics will simulate patient responses to anesthesia under varying clinical scenarios. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of training deep neural networks on multimodal datasets, parallelizing stochastic simulations of pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic interactions, and optimizing hyperparameters for model generalizability. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools to guide individualized fluid management, analgesic dosing, and hemodynamic support, reducing postoperative complications in high-risk cohorts. By enabling real-time analysis of large-scale heterogeneous data, this work will advance the translation of computational insights into clinical decision support systems, ultimately improving patient safety and outcomes in perioperative care. The scalability of these models will also provide a foundation for future studies on rare phenotypes and adaptive anesthesia protocols in critical care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical patient care, and the care of pain problems. Includes instruction in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: Agricultural business management faces growing complexity due to dynamic interactions between market volatility, climate variability, and global supply chain disruptions. Traditional analytical tools often lack the capacity to model these multidimensional, nonlinear relationships at scale, limiting the ability to optimize decisions such as crop planning, resource allocation, and risk mitigation. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework that integrates agent-based modeling, machine learning, and stochastic optimization to simulate agricultural enterprise decision-making under uncertainty. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize models using high-dimensional datasets, including historical commodity prices, regional climate projections, soil health metrics, and farm-level operational records. Agent-based simulations will capture heterogeneous decision behaviors across stakeholders (e.g., producers, distributors), while reinforcement learning algorithms will identify adaptive strategies that maximize profitability under fluctuating input costs and yield risks. A key innovation involves coupling geospatial data with market access models to evaluate the economic viability of alternative crop portfolios under localized climate scenarios. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing for Monte Carlo simulations spanning thousands of stochastic futures, as well as training deep learning architectures on multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to quantify trade-offs between short-term profitability and long-term resilience, (2) scalable decision-support systems for agricultural enterprises, and (3) open-source code repositories to enable reproducibility in agribusiness analytics. By advancing computational methods tailored to agricultural management, this work will provide actionable insights for stakeholders navigating interconnected economic and environmental pressures, ultimately contributing to more sustainable and data-driven operational frameworks. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the project’s computational demands, particularly for memory-intensive simulations and iterative model training cycles.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on modern business and economic principles involved in the organization, operation, and management of agricultural enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing digital content distribution and audience engagement strategies for visual arts and media organizations through advanced computational modeling. As the volume and complexity of digital visual media—including interactive installations, generative art, and augmented/virtual reality experiences—grow, arts managers require data-driven tools to predict audience behavior, allocate resources efficiently, and personalize content delivery. Current approaches often rely on limited datasets or static analytics, failing to account for the dynamic interplay between artistic content, platform algorithms, and user interaction patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework trained on multi-modal datasets encompassing user engagement metrics (e.g., dwell times, interaction logs), visual feature extraction data from digital artworks, and platform-specific performance indicators. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, train deep neural networks for predictive modeling, and simulate distribution scenarios across varying network architectures. Key computational challenges include real-time processing of high-resolution visual inputs, graph-based analysis of cross-platform content diffusion, and ensemble modeling to account for the subjective nature of artistic reception. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for arts organizations to forecast engagement patterns, optimize exhibition scheduling, and test virtual gallery configurations through digital twins. This work will contribute novel methodologies at the intersection of computational aesthetics and cultural analytics, while directly supporting evidence-based decision-making in visual arts management. The scale of data processing and iterative model training necessitates GPU-accelerated clusters and parallelized workflows, which form the core of this resource request.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Arts, Entertainment, and Media Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in arts, entertainment, and media management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the cultural dynamics of collaborative digital storytelling in decentralized online communities, focusing on emergent narrative practices within non-hierarchical, peer-produced platforms. While traditional humanities scholarship has examined storytelling through textual or historical lenses, this study addresses the computational analysis of real-time, multimodal narratives created through distributed authorship—a phenomenon underexplored in established humanities disciplines. The research problem centers on how decentralized collaboration shapes narrative coherence, thematic evolution, and cultural meaning-making in ephemeral digital spaces. Using high-performance computing resources, the project will analyze terabyte-scale datasets comprising timestamped text contributions, multimedia elements, and user interaction patterns from three distinct storytelling platforms operating under different governance models. Computational methods will combine transformer-based natural language processing for semantic analysis, graph neural networks to model contributor networks and narrative branching, and agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about emergent coordination patterns. The workflow requires parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams and iterative training of custom machine learning models to detect cultural motifs across linguistic, visual, and temporal dimensions. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for understanding collective narrative construction in digital environments, quantitative metrics for assessing decentralized cultural production, and open-source tools enabling humanities scholars to study large-scale collaborative creativity. By bridging computational social science with digital cultural studies, this work aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing post-disciplinary humanistic practices that transcend traditional categories of artistic and literary production. The requested resources are critical for handling the project's spatial-temporal data complexity and achieving sufficient model granularity to capture nuanced cultural interactions at web-scale.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any single instructional program in liberal arts and sciences, general studies and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of dental treatments, driven by patient-specific anatomical variability and the integration of advanced materials, demands computational approaches to optimize clinical outcomes. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating biomechanical interactions in dental restorations and implants, with a focus on predicting long-term functional performance. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, patient-specific models to evaluate stress distribution, material fatigue, and osseointegration dynamics under physiological loading conditions. Traditional experimental methods are limited in capturing the multi-scale, time-dependent behavior of dental systems, particularly when accounting for heterogeneous bone density, occlusal forces, and temperature fluctuations in the oral environment. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining finite element analysis (FEA), agent-based modeling, and machine learning to simulate biomechanical processes across spatial and temporal scales. HPC resources will enable parametric studies of 10,000+ virtual patient scenarios, incorporating CBCT-derived 3D geometries, material property databases, and stochastic loading profiles. Parallelized solvers will optimize simulation runtime for multi-physics models integrating thermal, mechanical, and biological domains. Machine learning components will train predictive models on simulation outputs to identify failure-risk biomarkers and optimal prosthesis design parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational platform for pre-treatment biomechanical evaluation of complex restorative cases, (2) evidence-based protocols for material selection and implant positioning in at-risk populations, and (3) open-access datasets correlating simulation predictions with 5-year clinical follow-up data from participating dental clinics. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to reduce iterative physical prototyping, minimize postoperative complications, and advance personalized treatment planning in advanced general dentistry. The resulting tools will directly inform curriculum development in digital dentistry and provide a foundation for studying emerging technologies like bioactive scaffolds and AI-assisted treatment workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of dental clinical techniques and dental practice issues. Includes instruction in subjects such as the history of dentistry, advanced dental practice management, dental ethics and jurisprudence, social and behavioral science studies of dentistry, advanced restorative dentistry, oral medicine, oral radiology, advanced clinical procedures and technology, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing wildfire evacuation strategies in urban-adjacent communities, integrating fire behavior modeling, human mobility dynamics, and real-time infrastructure vulnerability assessment. Wildfire evacuations present complex challenges due to rapidly evolving fire fronts, road network limitations, and heterogeneous population densities, yet existing evacuation models often rely on simplified fire spread assumptions or static infrastructure data. Our research addresses this gap by coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of fire propagation—incorporating localized fuel loads, microclimate variability, and ember dispersal—with agent-based models (ABMs) of pedestrian and vehicular movement. The HPC environment is critical for resolving fine-scale interactions between fire dynamics (via FireFOAM or WFDS solvers) and high-fidelity traffic simulations (using MATSim or SUMO) across large spatial domains. A novel component involves integrating LiDAR-derived building resilience metrics and real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled fire detection systems to dynamically update evacuation route viability. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated scenarios to enable rapid risk assessment during active incidents. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for municipal planners, enabling scenario testing of evacuation policies, infrastructure hardening priorities, and community education strategies. The computational framework will advance fire safety research by bridging gaps between physical fire science, transportation engineering, and emergency management, with direct applications to regional wildfire preparedness plans. By open-sourcing model components and publishing scenario libraries, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for adaptive evacuation planning in fire-prone regions globally.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science and technology to problems of reducing fire risk, limiting loss, supervising substance removal, conducting safety inspections and investigations, and advising on matters of safety procedures and fire prevention policy. Includes instruction in fire behavior, fire simulation, structural risk assessment, materials analysis, detection and suppression systems, smoke management, supply and evacuation, public education, legal aspects of fire prevention, and related research and communications methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of deploying deep neural networks (DNNs) on resource-constrained edge devices by developing a co-design framework that optimizes both algorithmic efficiency and hardware execution. While advances in deep learning have enabled state-of-the-art performance across domains, the computational and energy costs of modern DNNs remain prohibitive for real-time edge applications, such as autonomous systems and IoT devices. Existing approaches often treat model architecture design and hardware optimization as isolated tasks, leading to suboptimal trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and power consumption.
