This work proposes an interdisciplinary computational methodology integrating neural architecture search (NAS), hardware-aware quantization, and energy-efficient accelerator design. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale parallel simulations of candidate architectures across heterogeneous computing platforms, iteratively refining models using multi-objective optimization techniques. Key computational steps include distributed training of surrogate models for rapid architecture evaluation, hardware-in-the-loop simulations to assess latency and energy profiles, and reinforcement learning-driven exploration of the joint design space. The project’s outcomes will include (1) energy-optimized DNN architectures tailored for edge deployment, (2) an open-source framework for hardware-algorithm co-design, and (3) empirical benchmarks quantifying trade-offs across accuracy, latency, and power for emerging edge devices. By bridging computer science (algorithmic innovation) and computer engineering (hardware optimization), this work aims to advance the development of sustainable, scalable intelligent systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the computational complexity of multi-fidelity simulations and enabling rapid iteration across design parameters, which would be infeasible on local infrastructure. Results will directly benefit applications in smart healthcare, robotics, and distributed sensor networks, while contributing methodological advances to interdisciplinary computing research.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of computer science and computer engineering principles or a specialization which includes expertise in both computer engineering and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a spatially explicit modeling framework to assess the impacts of climate change and land-use dynamics on freshwater availability and aquatic biodiversity in critical watershed regions. Rapid environmental change threatens the sustainability of water resources and ecosystems, yet predicting these impacts remains challenging due to the complex interplay of hydrological, ecological, and anthropogenic factors. We propose to integrate high-resolution climate projections, land-cover data, and species habitat models within a coupled hydrological-ecological simulation platform. The computational workflow will employ machine learning algorithms to downscale global climate models to regional scales, paired with agent-based models to simulate human water use patterns. Hydrological processes will be modeled using a parallelized implementation of the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT), while biodiversity responses will be assessed through ensemble species distribution models. The scale of analysis—encompassing 10^6 km² of watershed areas at 100m spatial resolution—and the need for multi-decadal, multi-scenario simulations necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Key outcomes will include probabilistic maps of future water stress, identification of aquatic species at heightened risk of habitat loss, and evaluation of conservation strategies under varying climate pathways. These results will directly inform regional water management policies and prioritization of protected area expansions. The project requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning components and large-memory nodes for processing high-dimensional ecological datasets. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance predictive capacity in natural resource management while establishing a transferable framework for climate resilience planning in freshwater systems globally.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the studies and activities relating to the natural environment and its conservation, use, and improvement. Includes instruction in subjects such as climate, air, soil, water, land, fish and wildlife, and plant resources; in the basic principles of environmental science and natural resources management; and the recreational and economic uses of renewable and nonrenewable natural resources.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the longitudinal efficacy of spiritual care interventions in mitigating psychological distress among patients with chronic illnesses. Despite growing recognition of spiritual care as a component of holistic healthcare, empirical models to quantify its impact on patient outcomes—particularly in dynamic, real-world clinical settings—remain underdeveloped. This research addresses this gap by integrating computational linguistics, psychometric analysis, and machine learning to evaluate unstructured data from chaplain-patient interactions (e.g., session transcripts, self-reported narratives) alongside clinical biomarkers of stress (e.g., cortisol levels, heart rate variability). The primary computational challenge lies in processing high-dimensional, temporally sensitive datasets to identify latent patterns linking pastoral counseling techniques to measurable health improvements. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines, we will extract semantic and emotional features from counseling dialogues, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will model temporal relationships between intervention timing, linguistic markers of coping, and physiological stress indicators. Parallelized Bayesian inference methods will be employed to account for heterogeneity in patient demographics, spiritual backgrounds, and disease trajectories. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive framework to optimize spiritual care delivery by identifying intervention characteristics most strongly associated with reduced anxiety, improved emotional resilience, and enhanced treatment adherence. This work will establish a novel computational paradigm for evaluating non-pharmacological psychosocial interventions, with implications for personalized care planning and interdisciplinary collaboration in clinical settings. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of patient-provider interactions, the project advances methodological innovation at the intersection of pastoral theology, healthcare psychology, and data science.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including but not limited to, ordained clergy and other counseling professionals to respond to the emotional and/or spiritual needs of patients and families in health care emergencies and other situations, and to consult with and counsel other health care professionals. Includes instruction in advanced interpersonal communication; individual and small group counseling; interdisciplinary teamwork; crisis management; extended care relationships; self-analysis; medical ethics; pastoral care art; spiritual dimensions of human growth and health; counseling psychology and therapy; and applications to grief, death, emotional collapse, injury, individual/family adjustment, and chronic illness situations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale digital communication patterns in professional and technical contexts, addressing a critical gap in understanding how multimodal documents—integrating text, visuals, and interactive elements—impact user comprehension and decision-making. While prior studies have examined discrete aspects of technical writing, such as readability or usability, the dynamic interplay between evolving digital formats (e.g., AI-generated content, augmented reality manuals, and adaptive web interfaces) and audience engagement remains underexplored. This research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) models to process and classify terabytes of multimodal documents from industries such as healthcare, engineering, and public policy. Computational methods will include semantic analysis of technical jargon, sentiment detection in user feedback datasets, and neural network-driven simulations of document usability across diverse demographic groups. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve real-time analysis of complex document interactions at scale—a task infeasible with standard computing infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible corpus of annotated technical documents, predictive models for optimizing document design, and frameworks for assessing the ethical implications of AI-assisted writing tools. These results will directly inform curriculum development in professional writing programs and provide evidence-based guidelines for organizations managing large-scale documentation systems. The project thus bridges computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, advancing both the theory and practice of effective communication in technical and scientific domains.
cip_title: Professional, Technical, Business, and Scientific Writing
cip_definition: A program that focuses on professional, technical, business, and scientific writing; and that prepares individuals for academic positions or for professional careers as writers, editors, researchers, and related careers in business, government, non-profits, and the professions. Includes instruction in theories of rhetoric, writing, and digital literacy; document design, production, and management; visual rhetoric and multimedia composition; documentation development; usability testing; web writing; and publishing in print and electronic media.

abstract: The rapid evolution of next-generation wireless communication systems necessitates advanced computational tools to address the escalating complexity of channel modeling, signal processing, and network optimization. This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for simulating and optimizing ultra-massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) systems operating in high-frequency bands (e.g., millimeter-wave and sub-THz), which are critical for 6G networks. Current methods struggle to balance computational efficiency with the accuracy required to model dynamic, spatially diverse channels and interference patterns in dense urban environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining parallelized finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) electromagnetic simulations with machine learning-driven surrogate models. The FDTD simulations will capture fine-grained wave propagation effects, while neural networks trained on this data will accelerate real-time optimization of antenna array configurations and beamforming parameters. The project requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the multi-scale nature of the problem: large-scale parameter sweeps for training datasets, distributed training of deep reinforcement learning models, and validation via full-wave simulations across heterogeneous computing nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source tools for efficient MIMO system design, (2) novel beamforming algorithms adaptive to non-stationary channel conditions, and (3) quantitative guidelines for balancing energy efficiency and spectral capacity in THz-band networks. This work will directly address the computational bottlenecks hindering the practical deployment of ultra-dense communication architectures, providing a foundation for energy-aware 6G infrastructure. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce simulation times by two orders of magnitude compared to conventional single-node approaches, enabling rapid prototyping of systems that meet emerging latency and throughput standards.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronics, and Communications Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical, electronics, and communications engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for scalable, adaptive online teaching frameworks necessitates advanced computational tools to model and optimize virtual learning environments. Current approaches to online instructional design often rely on static, one-size-fits-all methodologies, which fail to account for the dynamic interplay between learner diversity, real-time engagement patterns, and pedagogical effectiveness. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform to test and refine adaptive instructional strategies for heterogeneous student populations. Leveraging anonymized datasets from existing online courses—including temporal interaction logs, assessment outcomes, and multimodal engagement metrics (e.g., video attention tracking, forum participation)—we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate learner behaviors under varying pedagogical conditions. These models will integrate reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively optimize instructional content delivery, pacing, and feedback mechanisms in response to simulated learner trajectories. The computational workload involves large-scale parallel simulations across thousands of virtual student agents, necessitating HPC resources for efficient execution. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for predicting the efficacy of specific instructional designs across learner subgroups, (2) actionable guidelines for dynamically personalizing content sequencing and intervention timing, and (3) open-source tools to help educators prototype and evaluate adaptive strategies in virtual environments. By bridging computational modeling and pedagogical theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in online teacher education, directly equipping instructors with data-driven methods to enhance equity and outcomes in digitally mediated classrooms.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various academic levels through online instructional technologies. Includes instruction in andragogy, pedagogy, assessment, instructional design and technology, and learning science.

abstract: Insect populations are increasingly threatened by synergistic stressors, including climate variability, habitat fragmentation, and agrochemical exposure, yet predicting their resilience requires models that integrate individual behavior, population dynamics, and environmental heterogeneity at biologically relevant scales. This project addresses the computational limitations of current entomological models, which often oversimplify spatial-temporal interactions or fail to capture adaptive behaviors in response to dynamic stressors. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate multi-generational insect population responses across realistic landscapes, incorporating agent-based modeling (ABM) for individual movement and decision-making, coupled with environmental data assimilation from remote sensing and field sensors. The ABM will integrate ethological data on species-specific foraging, mating, and oviposition behaviors, parameterized through meta-analysis of empirical studies, while geospatial layers will represent shifting microclimates and resource distributions. A novel machine learning module will iteratively refine behavioral rules based on fitness outcomes, enabling adaptive plasticity within simulations. Computational challenges include scaling spatially explicit simulations over decadal timeframes, managing high-dimensional parameter spaces for sensitivity analyses, and optimizing runtime for ensemble projections under IPCC climate scenarios. The project requests GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized ABM execution and large-memory nodes for real-time environmental data integration. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of population viability for key pollinator and pest species under mitigation scenarios, identification of critical stressor thresholds, and open-source tools for adaptive entomological modeling. This work bridges ecology, computer science, and environmental science to advance predictive capacity in insect conservation and integrated pest management, addressing a gap in biologically detailed, landscape-scale computational models. Results will inform policy frameworks for agricultural land use and pesticide regulation, with direct applications to food security and biodiversity preservation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of insect species and populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: Veterinary anesthesiology faces unique challenges in optimizing species-specific anesthetic protocols, particularly given the physiological variability across companion animals, livestock, and exotic species. Current protocols often rely on generalized guidelines that may not account for individual patient factors such as comorbidities, drug interactions, or breed-specific vulnerabilities, leading to increased perioperative risks. This project seeks to develop predictive computational models to personalize anesthetic dosing and monitoring strategies, thereby improving safety and outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-modal data, including electronic health records, intraoperative vital sign streams, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) parameters, and species-specific anatomical/physiological datasets. A hybrid approach combining mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling and machine learning will be employed. PBPK models will simulate drug distribution across tissue compartments in diverse species, while neural networks will identify nonlinear relationships between patient variables (e.g., age, weight, metabolic rate) and outcomes such as hemodynamic stability or recovery times. Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in dose-response predictions under varying clinical scenarios. The computational pipeline will be validated against retrospective data from 15,000+ anesthetic cases across three veterinary hospitals, with iterative refinement using Bayesian calibration. Expected outcomes include (1) species- and condition-specific anesthetic dosing algorithms, (2) real-time risk prediction tools for intraoperative hypotension or hypoxemia, and (3) open-access simulation frameworks for protocol optimization in rare or underrepresented species. By enabling large-scale integration of heterogeneous clinical data, HPC resources are critical to overcoming memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in high-dimensional PK/PD models. This work will directly address gaps in evidence-based veterinary anesthesia, reducing adverse events by an estimated 20-30% in target populations while providing a template for computational resource utilization in clinical veterinary research. Resultant models will be deployed via a cloud-based interface for collaborative validation through the American College of Veterinary Anesthesia and Analgesia.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical animal care and the care of pain problems. May included related research in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: Neonatal morbidity and mortality in high-risk pregnancies remain significant challenges due to the complex interplay of maternal, placental, and neonatal factors. Current clinical models lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale physiological data, limiting predictive accuracy and mechanistic understanding. This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to model maternal-fetal physiology and predict neonatal outcomes in high-risk pregnancies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate electronic health records, placental histomorphometry, and real-time neonatal vital signs to construct a dynamic model of maternal-fetal interactions. Machine learning algorithms will identify critical biomarkers and physiological thresholds associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, such as hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and preterm birth complications. The computational framework will utilize agent-based modeling to simulate placental nutrient transport and hemodynamic changes, coupled with finite element analysis of neonatal cardiovascular adaptation. By analyzing terabyte-scale datasets from a retrospective cohort of 10,000 high-risk pregnancies, the HPC environment will enable parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams and validation of model predictions against clinical outcomes. The expected outcomes include a predictive tool for neonatal resuscitation readiness and individualized risk stratification for obstetricians and neonatologists. This research will advance our understanding of transitional physiology in high-risk neonates and provide a computational platform for optimizing perinatal care strategies. The proposed HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of multi-modal data integration, real-time simulation, and large-scale parameter optimization, which are infeasible with standard clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physiology of the normal neonate, the pathophysiology of the sick infant, and the diagnosis and management of problems of the newborn infant, including consulting with obstetricians to plan for the care of women with high-risk pregnancies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of personalized myopia progression modeling by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate complex interactions between ocular biomechanics, optical aberrations, and environmental factors. Myopia, a leading cause of preventable vision impairment, exhibits heterogeneous progression patterns that remain poorly predicted by current clinical metrics. Traditional approaches rely on population-averaged trends, but emerging evidence suggests that individual variations in scleral stiffness, corneal topography, and habitual visual behaviors drive differential outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of posterior eye biomechanics, ray-tracing simulations of retinal defocus patterns, and machine learning analysis of longitudinal electronic health records from optometric practice networks. The HPC environment will enable parallel execution of patient-specific FEM meshes simulating scleral creep under intraocular pressure, coupled with Monte Carlo sampling of daily near-work cycles and outdoor exposure scenarios derived from wearable light sensors. A neural operator will be trained on synthetic data generated through these physics-informed models to establish real-time predictors of axial elongation rates. This computationally intensive workflow demands large-scale parameter sweeps across ocular geometries and material properties, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for the ray-tracing submodules and high-memory CPUs for the biomechanical simulations. Successful implementation will yield two key outcomes: 1) a validated digital twin pipeline for simulating patient-specific myopia trajectories, and 2) an open-source risk stratification tool that integrates seamlessly with standard optometric imaging systems. By elucidating mechano-optical drivers of progression, this work aims to transform the personalization of myopia control strategies, particularly optical interventions like specialty contact lenses and low-dose atropine protocols. The computational infrastructure will additionally create a template for addressing other optometric challenges requiring multiscale tissue modeling, such as keratoconus progression and post-LASIK ectasia risk prediction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of optometry and that focuses on the principles and techniques for examining, diagnosing and treating conditions of the visual system. Includes instruction in prescribing glasses and contact lenses, other optical aids, corrective therapies, patient counseling, physician referral, practice management, and ethics and professional standards.

abstract: Chemical processes involving heterogeneous catalysis are central to the production of fuels, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals. However, the empirical development of catalysts and reaction conditions remains time-intensive and costly. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multiscale modeling of catalytic systems, integrating quantum mechanical simulations of active sites with reactor-scale transport phenomena. Density functional theory (DFT) will be employed to elucidate reaction mechanisms and activation barriers on candidate catalyst surfaces, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) frameworks will model mass and heat transfer in industrial reactor geometries. The integration of these scales requires iterative data exchange between software packages, necessitating large-scale parallelization and significant memory allocation. HPC resources will also facilitate machine learning-assisted optimization of catalyst compositions and operating parameters by training on terabyte-scale datasets generated from combinatorial simulations. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel catalyst formulations with improved selectivity for target products, reduced energy demands for hydrocarbon processing, and validated multiscale workflows adaptable to other reactive systems. This work addresses critical gaps in accelerating sustainable process engineering by replacing trial-and-error experimentation with predictive computational frameworks, directly benefiting industries reliant on catalytic technologies while minimizing environmental impacts through optimized resource utilization.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable and high-performance materials in leatherworking and upholstery necessitates advanced computational approaches to overcome limitations in traditional experimental methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the mechanical and chemical behavior of novel composite materials, including bio-based leather alternatives and reinforced upholstery textiles, under diverse environmental and stress conditions. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive frameworks for optimizing material durability, flexibility, and eco-efficiency during the design phase, which currently leads to resource-intensive prototyping cycles. Using multiscale computational modeling, we will simulate molecular interactions, tensile dynamics, and degradation pathways of these materials through finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics (MD), and machine learning-driven predictive analytics. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of composite formulations and processing variables, enabling rapid iteration of virtual prototypes. Expected outcomes include a validated computational pipeline for predicting material performance metrics (e.g., abrasion resistance, moisture retention, lifecycle emissions) and generating optimized design guidelines for sustainable manufacturing. This work will directly address gaps in technology-driven leatherworking education by providing open-source simulation tools tailored for vocational training programs. The integration of computational materials science into upholstery and leatherworking workflows has broader implications for reducing waste in artisanal and industrial production, aligning with circular economy objectives. By establishing a scalable digital prototyping framework, this project aims to position computational resource utilization as a cornerstone of innovation in a traditionally craft-based field.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in leatherworking and upholstering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in keyboard performance practice through computational analysis of large-scale performance datasets. The research problem centers on understanding the relationship between technical execution, expressive interpretation, and pedagogical outcomes in keyboard performance. While traditional analysis methods rely on manual observation or small-sample studies, this project will develop machine learning models to analyze multi-modal performance data—including audio recordings, MIDI kinematics, and motion-capture gestures—across diverse repertoire and skill levels. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) processing and synchronizing heterogeneous performance data using signal processing and time-series alignment algorithms; (2) training neural networks to detect patterns linking technical parameters (e.g., keystroke velocity, pedal timing) to expressive outcomes (e.g., phrasing, dynamic shaping); and (3) creating simulation environments to model the biomechanical demands of advanced keyboard works. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling terabyte-scale datasets from international performance archives, enabling parallel processing of high-dimensional feature spaces, and supporting iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include new analytical frameworks for quantifying performance excellence, data-driven insights into technical development pathways, and generative models that assist pedagogues in creating personalized training regimens. By bridging computational musicology and performance pedagogy, this research aims to establish evidence-based benchmarks for keyboard education while preserving artistic individuality. The resource request supports both proposed work in model development and ongoing analysis of historical performance corpora, with potential applications in adaptive learning systems and augmented practice technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the piano, organ, or related keyboard instruments and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in piano and keyboard pedagogy, ensemble playing, accompanying, service playing, repertoire, keyboard and pedal skills, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying therapy resistance in solid tumors, with a focus on pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Despite advances in targeted therapies, PDAC remains highly lethal due to its complex tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by dynamic interactions between neoplastic cells, stromal components, and immune populations that drive evasion of treatment. Current experimental models struggle to capture the spatial and temporal heterogeneity of these interactions, limiting mechanistic insights. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multiplex immunohistochemistry data from patient biopsies, single-cell proteomic profiles, and dynamic cytokine signaling measurements to build a spatially resolved, multiscale model of PDAC-TME crosstalk. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular behaviors (e.g., proliferation, apoptosis, immune cell recruitment) under varying stromal stiffness and hypoxic conditions, while partial differential equations will model nutrient and cytokine diffusion. The HPC environment is critical for parameter optimization across thousands of simulated TME permutations and for analyzing high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include identifying dominant stromal-immune signaling axes that promote therapy resistance, predicting combinatorial therapeutic vulnerabilities, and validating candidate targets in vitro using 3D organoid co-cultures. This work will advance experimental pathology by bridging tissue-scale pathophysiological observations with subcellular mechanistic data, offering a platform to dissect context-specific drivers of tumor progression. Findings will inform biomarker discovery and the design of stroma-modulating adjuvant therapies, directly addressing unmet needs in oncology and cancer biology.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the expression, initiation, maintenance and progression of tissue injury and disease, including death, and the relationship of pathogenesis to fundamental molecular and cellular mechanisms. Includes instruction in immunology, microbiology, gene expression, inflammation, cell injury, apoptosis, immunopathology, molecular markers of disease and toxins, neoplasia, growth regulation, and organ- and system-specific investigations.

abstract: Inverse problems in wave propagation present significant challenges due to their inherent ill-posedness and the computational complexity of high-dimensional parameter spaces. This project seeks to develop robust computational methods for reconstructing spatially heterogeneous material properties from partial and noisy wave measurements, with applications in non-destructive testing and geophysical imaging. The proposed approach integrates asymptotic model reduction techniques with adjoint-based optimization algorithms, aiming to mitigate the curse of dimensionality while maintaining physical fidelity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the computational demands of solving large-scale finite element discretizations of the governing partial differential equations and iteratively refining parameter estimates through parallelized gradient descent. The work involves distributed-memory architectures to manage multi-physics simulations and stochastic optimization steps, which require tera-scale linear algebra operations and adaptive mesh refinement. Anticipated outcomes include scalable algorithms that enhance reconstruction accuracy under data constraints, validated through synthetic and experimental benchmarks. By advancing the computational efficiency of inverse solvers, this research will enable real-time material characterization in industrial settings, such as detecting subsurface fractures in energy infrastructure or imaging biological tissues. The project will also contribute open-source tools for the applied mathematics community, fostering interdisciplinary collaborations in computational science and engineering. The resulting framework will be extensible to other inverse problems governed by wave phenomena, including seismic inversion and photonic device design, bridging theoretical advances with practical implementation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as engineering and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in natural phenomena modeling continuum mechanics, reaction-diffusion, wave propagation, dynamic systems, numerical analysis, controlled theory, asymptotic methods, variation, optimization theory, inverse problems, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the resilience of ecological communities to climate-driven disturbances by integrating field-derived interaction networks with spatially explicit, dynamic simulations. A critical challenge in evolutionary ecology lies in predicting how interspecific relationships—such as competition, mutualism, and trophic dependencies—mediate ecosystem responses to environmental stressors. Traditional models often oversimplify biotic interactions or fail to capture nonlinear feedbacks across scales, limiting their utility for conservation planning. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling framework that simulates community dynamics under varying climate scenarios, parameterized using empirical data from long-term monitoring of temperate forest and freshwater ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to run ensembles of these computationally intensive simulations, which track individual species’ traits, interaction strengths, and dispersal constraints at fine spatial resolutions (1 km² grids) across decadal timescales. The models will incorporate paleoecological data to calibrate historical baselines and test hypotheses about co-evolutionary buffers to disturbance. Parallelized sensitivity analyses will identify key thresholds in habitat connectivity and functional diversity that govern ecosystem collapse or recovery. Outcomes will advance mechanistic understanding of how biotic networks mediate resilience, enabling predictions of community restructuring under projected warming scenarios. Results will directly inform regional habitat corridor designs and species-specific management plans. By leveraging HPC capabilities to scale from organismal physiology to landscape-level processes, this work bridges a critical gap between ecological theory and climate adaptation practice. The computational workflows and open-source tools generated will provide a template for integrating complex interaction networks into predictive ecology, with applications in conservation biology and ecosystem services planning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions of small-scale biological systems, such as organisms, to each other, to complex and whole systems, and to the physical and other non-biological aspects of their environments. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry; landscape and/or marine/aquatic dynamics; decomposition; global and regional elemental budgets; biotic and abiotic regulation of nutrient cycles; ecophysiology; ecosystem resilience, disturbance, and succession; community and habitat dynamics; organismal interactions (co-evolution, competition, predation); paleoecology; and evolutionary ecology.

abstract: Agricultural biometry frequently involves analyzing datasets characterized by sparse observations, unbalanced designs, and heterogeneous variance structures, complicating the development of robust predictive models. Traditional statistical approaches often fail to account for these complexities, leading to biased estimates and unreliable inferences. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a scalable computational framework for fitting high-dimensional hierarchical models to unbalanced agricultural data, integrating spatially explicit environmental covariates and longitudinal measurements. Leveraging Bayesian inference with Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods and machine learning techniques, the proposed approach will employ adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo samplers and stochastic variational inference algorithms to handle complex error structures and missing data mechanisms. The computational intensity of these methods necessitates high-performance computing resources, particularly for large-scale matrix operations, parallel chain sampling, and cross-validation across multiple environmental scenarios. By utilizing GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory systems, this project aims to reduce computation time from weeks to days while maintaining statistical precision. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for agricultural biometry, improved prediction of crop yield variability under climate uncertainty, and methodological advances in handling sparse temporal-spatial biological data. The results will directly support precision agriculture initiatives and contribute to sustainable natural resource management strategies by enhancing decision-making capabilities in heterogeneous agricultural systems.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics and other computational methods to the study of problems in the biological sciences and related fields in agriculture and natural resources. Includes instruction in computational biology, mathematical statistics, matrix algebra, applied calculus, experimental design, linear modeling, sampling theory, stochastic processes, spatial and temporal analysis, longitudinal analysis, sparse/unbalanced data and complex error, and applications to such topics as population genetics, animal breeding, forest genetics, population dynamics, wildlife biometry, ecology, and agricultural and natural resource management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of consumer decision-making processes in omnichannel retail environments, where dynamic interactions between digital platforms, physical stores, and supply chains create complex, data-rich challenges. Traditional consumer behavior models struggle to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating inventory levels, personalized promotions, and cross-channel browsing patterns, which require granular temporal and spatial analysis at scale. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to simulate hyper-personalized consumer journeys while integrating heterogeneous data streams—including transaction histories, mobile app interactions, and social media sentiment—to optimize merchandising strategies. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) paired with machine learning (ML), the project will simulate millions of synthetic consumers with adaptive preferences, enabling probabilistic forecasting of purchasing behaviors under varying retail scenarios. HPC resources are critical for deploying parallelized simulations that capture regional market differences, seasonal demand shifts, and supply chain disruptions, tasks infeasible with conventional computing due to the non-linear interactions between agents and high-dimensional data inputs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for retailers to test merchandising campaigns in silico, reducing reliance on costly A/B testing while improving campaign ROI. Additionally, the project aims to identify latent variables influencing cross-channel loyalty and price sensitivity, offering novel insights into micro-segmentation strategies. By bridging computational scalability gaps in consumer analytics, this work will empower retailers to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency in increasingly fragmented retail ecosystems, establishing a methodological precedent for HPC applications in non-STEM consumer research domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on product and service promotion from the perspective of individual and family consumers and that prepares individuals to function as consumer management and marketing consultants in for-profit and non-profit enterprises. Includes instruction in applied market research, consumer behavior, product sourcing and distribution, profitability, customer feedback and evaluation methods, promotion and retailing campaign development, and applications to specific domestic and international consumer markets.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design of energy-efficient and resilient building systems through high-fidelity computational modeling of coupled structural, thermal, and environmental interactions. Current architectural engineering practices often rely on simplified analytical models or siloed simulations, which inadequately capture the dynamic interdependencies between a building’s structural integrity, HVAC performance, and environmental impacts. Such limitations hinder the optimization of sustainable designs, particularly as climate change exacerbates demands for adaptive infrastructure. To address this gap, we propose a multi-physics computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and data-driven optimization to holistically simulate building behavior under diverse operational and environmental conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these interactions, which involve large-scale parametric studies of material properties, airflow dynamics, and heat transfer across building envelopes. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to identify Pareto-optimal designs balancing energy use, thermal comfort, and lifecycle carbon emissions. The proposed work will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and parallel computing architectures to reduce computational costs associated with high-resolution, city-scale microclimate modeling. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for architectural engineers, validated against experimental data from sensor-equipped test buildings, and generalized design guidelines for climate-resilient structures. By enabling rapid prototyping of adaptive building systems, this research aims to reduce energy consumption in the built environment by 15–30% in modeled scenarios, directly supporting decarbonization targets in urban infrastructure planning. The requested HPC allocation will empower resource-intensive workflows, including ensemble simulations of extreme weather events and uncertainty quantification for novel bio-based construction materials, ensuring robust, scalable solutions for sustainable architectural practice.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials, systems, and methods used to construct and equip buildings intended for human habitation or other purposes.

abstract: Optimizing plant nursery operations requires precise management of environmental variables, genetic selection, and resource allocation to maximize propagation success and minimize losses. Current practices rely heavily on generalized protocols, leading to suboptimal growth rates, elevated disease susceptibility, and inefficient resource use. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating high-resolution environmental sensing, genomic data, and growth performance metrics to generate nursery-specific optimization models. We propose using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize multi-scale simulations of plant-environment interactions under varying nursery configurations. These simulations will couple 3D fluid dynamics models of irrigation systems with spatially explicit microclimate data, soil moisture sensors, and species-specific physiological thresholds. Machine learning models will then identify genotype-by-environment (GxE) interactions predictive of successful transplantation outcomes using whole-genome sequencing data from 15 commercially important woody species. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of terabyte-scale environmental datasets from IoT sensors deployed across six partner nurseries, paired with genomic variant analysis pipelines. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for custom irrigation and fertilization schedules that reduce water and nutrient waste by ≥25%, (2) a decision-support tool for matching plant genotypes to nursery microclimates to improve post-transplantation survival rates, and (3) open-source algorithms for real-time disease risk forecasting based on hyperspectral imaging and pathogen dispersal simulations. By scaling these analyses across heterogeneous nursery environments, this work will establish a paradigm for data-driven precision nursery management, directly addressing workforce training needs in operational efficiency and sustainable practices. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the computational intensity of coupled physical-biological models and enabling rapid iteration of management scenarios.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage outdoor plant farms, tree and shrub nurseries, and related facilities that develop domesticated plant products for propagation, harvesting, and transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science, farm and business management, nursery operations, equipment operation and maintenance, safety procedures, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic in-store customer traffic patterns using high-resolution behavioral simulations to enhance retail operational efficiency and customer experience. Traditional retail space planning relies on static models or historical sales data, which fail to account for real-time variables such as shifting crowd densities, seasonal promotions, or emergent in-store bottlenecks. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate and predict customer movement, inventory interaction, and staff responsiveness in hyper-realistic retail environments. The research leverages anonymized video analytics data from partner retailers, processed via convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract spatiotemporal movement patterns, which inform the ABM’s decision rules. A parallelized RL pipeline will then iteratively optimize layout configurations, staff allocation, and inventory placement by minimizing simulated congestion and maximizing product engagement metrics. The scale of this analysis—requiring millions of parallel simulations across diverse store formats and customer demographics—necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources for GPU-accelerated deep learning, distributed ABM execution, and multi-objective optimization. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for real-time retail space adaptation, validated against empirical data from pilot implementations. This work bridges computational social science and retail operations, offering a novel paradigm for responsive store design while advancing methodologies for large-scale behavioral simulation in constrained physical environments. Successful implementation could reduce operational costs by 12–18% in test cases and inform adaptive retail systems for rapidly changing consumer landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations associated with retail sales in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in over-the-counter and other direct sales operations in business settings, basic bookkeeping principles, customer service, team/staff leadership and supervision, floor management, and applicable technical skills.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the optimization of decentralized wastewater treatment systems through high-fidelity computational modeling and machine learning, addressing the challenge of scalable, energy-efficient water recycling in resource-constrained settings. Current systems often struggle to balance treatment efficacy, operational costs, and adaptability to variable contaminant loads, particularly in emerging contaminants such as microplastics and pharmaceutical residues. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating hydrodynamic simulations (via OpenFOAM), reactive transport modeling, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to predict system performance under dynamic real-world conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 3D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of hybrid biofilm-membrane reactors at pore-to-tank scales, coupled with Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification for influent variability. Concurrently, we will train GNNs on synthetic and experimental datasets to identify optimal operational parameters (e.g., aeration rates, biofilm thickness) across diverse wastewater matrices. The computational workflow will be validated against pilot-scale systems operated by municipal partners, incorporating real-time sensor data through a digital twin interface. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for designing modular treatment units, predictive models for emerging contaminant removal, and AI-driven optimization frameworks to reduce energy consumption by 25-40% compared to conventional systems. This work will directly support the development of adaptive wastewater infrastructure capable of meeting stringent reuse standards while minimizing resource inputs, with particular relevance to arid regions and rapidly urbanizing areas. The requested HPC allocations are critical for managing the computational intensity of coupled physicochemical-biological simulations and large-scale parameter space exploration required for robust system generalization.
cip_title: Water Quality and Wastewater Treatment Management and Recycling Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using water storage, waterpower, and wastewater treatment systems. Includes instruction in water storage, power and/or treatment systems and equipment; testing and inspection procedures; system maintenance procedures; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the detection and classification capabilities of undersea acoustic signals in contested environments through the development of high-fidelity computational models optimized for antisubmarine warfare (ASW) applications. Traditional signal processing methods struggle to distinguish low-signature submarines from complex background noise in shallow-water littoral zones, which are characterized by dynamic bathymetry, temperature gradients, and anthropogenic interference. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining physics-based acoustic propagation modeling with machine learning techniques to enhance target discrimination. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of underwater soundscapes under varying operational conditions, including multi-static sonar configurations and clutter scenarios induced by marine life or civilian vessel traffic. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods will model broadband signal interactions with seabed structures, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on synthetic aperture sonar data will be deployed for real-time feature extraction. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated wave equation solvers with distributed training of deep learning architectures, requiring access to parallelized processing and high-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive sonar signal processing and quantitative metrics quantifying detection probability improvements in cluttered environments compared to legacy systems. By bridging physics-based simulation and data-driven analytics, this research aims to deliver actionable insights for next-generation ASW decision support systems while establishing scalable computational methodologies for undersea acoustic challenges at the intersection of defense technology and environmental complexity. The requested resources will directly support parametric studies across 10+ operational variables, reducing reliance on costly at-sea testing while accelerating algorithmic readiness for deployment on naval platforms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of acoustics and signals processing to undersea and antisubmarine warfare. Includes instruction in acoustics; electrical engineering; the generation, propagation and reception of underwater sound waves; military applications of underwater sound; and acoustic signal processing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex challenges in insurance law, specifically focusing on the computational modeling of regulatory compliance risks and litigation outcomes in multi-jurisdictional insurance markets. Insurance law, while rooted in legal frameworks, increasingly intersects with data-driven decision-making as insurers and regulators contend with dynamic risks, evolving case law, and heterogeneous regulatory environments. Traditional legal analysis struggles to systematically analyze the vast volume of case rulings, regulatory texts, and transactional data required to identify patterns in coverage disputes or predict systemic vulnerabilities. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), graph-based network analysis, and agent-based modeling to map interactions between legal precedents, regulatory policies, and market behaviors. NLP pipelines will process unstructured legal texts (court opinions, regulatory filings) to extract semantic relationships and classify argumentation patterns. Network models will represent the influence of judicial decisions across jurisdictions, while agent-based simulations will test how hypothetical regulatory changes propagate through insurance ecosystems. The computational scale of these tasks—processing terabyte-scale legal corpora, training deep learning models on low-resource legal language, and simulating multi-actor systems with thousands of interdependent variables—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include: (1) a predictive framework for assessing compliance risks under emerging regulations (e.g., climate-related liability frameworks), (2) quantitative insights into judicial decision-making biases in coverage disputes, and (3) open-source tools for scenario-testing regulatory impacts. By integrating computational social science methods with doctrinal legal analysis, this work aims to advance evidence-based policy design while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-STEM legal research domains.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting insurance.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in analyzing and generating complex polyphonic music structures. Traditional methods for modeling advanced harmonic progressions, counterpoint interactions, and timbral evolution in large-scale compositions face limitations in scalability and precision, particularly when working with high-dimensional musical datasets or real-time algorithmic composition systems. The proposed work integrates parametric music representations with machine learning frameworks to enable granular analysis of stylistic patterns across historical corpora while simulating novel compositional outputs. Key computational objectives include parallelized acoustic rendering of orchestral textures, GPU-accelerated training of generative models on spectral and symbolic music data, and dynamic optimization of rule-based composition systems through evolutionary algorithms. By utilizing HPC infrastructure, the project aims to overcome latency barriers in real-time interactive systems for computer-aided composition while enabling large-scale comparative studies of harmonic complexity across genres. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for spectral analysis of microtonal structures, a database of parametrically annotated orchestration patterns, and a framework for hybrid human-AI collaborative composition. This work will advance computational musicology by establishing scalable methods to quantify and manipulate high-level musical features, with applications in pedagogy, archival analysis, and the creation of algorithmically informed contemporary works. The requested resources will directly support simulations requiring teraflop-scale processing for waveform synthesis, distributed memory architectures for corpus analysis, and high-throughput workflows for benchmarking generative models against music-theoretical constraints.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the principles of sound manipulation as applied to the creation of music, and the techniques of creating and arranging music. Includes instruction in aural theory, melody, counterpoint, complex harmony, modulation, chromatics, improvisation, progressions, musical writing, instrumentation, orchestration, electronic and computer applications, studies of specific musical styles, and development of original creative ability.

abstract: Congenital anomalies of the genitourinary tract represent a significant source of morbidity in pediatric populations, with surgical outcomes influenced by complex anatomical variations, tissue biomechanics, and postoperative healing dynamics. Current clinical decision-making relies on static imaging and population-level data, limiting the ability to predict patient-specific surgical outcomes or optimize procedural planning. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific computational models of genitourinary anatomy and simulate surgical interventions. The research will integrate clinical imaging data (MRI/CT), biomechanical tissue properties, and fluid dynamics to create multi-scale models of congenital defects such as bladder exstrophy, hypospadias, and ureteropelvic junction obstruction. Finite element analysis and machine learning algorithms will be employed to predict postoperative tissue stress distributions, urinary flow dynamics, and long-term functional outcomes under varying surgical approaches. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution imaging datasets, iterative optimization of surgical parameters, and validation against retrospective clinical outcomes from a multicenter cohort of 500+ patients. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for identifying optimal surgical strategies tailored to individual anatomical and biomechanical profiles, reducing revision rates and complications. This work will also generate open-source computational tools for simulating pediatric urologic surgeries, fostering collaborative innovation in the field. By bridging clinical expertise with advanced computational modeling, this project aims to establish a paradigm shift toward data-driven, personalized surgical planning in pediatric urology, ultimately improving quality of life for children with congenital genitourinary anomalies.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals in the study, prevention, and management of congenital, childhood-acquired, and overlapping adolescent anomalies of the genitourinary tract, including problems, diseases, tumors, and traumas.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of diagnosing and optimizing modern motorcycle systems—including hybrid and electric drivetrains—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive maintenance frameworks and multiphysics simulations. Current maintenance practices rely heavily on manual inspections and static schedules, which struggle to account for dynamic operational stresses, environmental variability, and emerging technologies. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational approach integrating large-scale simulations of mechanical wear, fluid dynamics in lubrication and cooling systems, and electrochemical processes in battery and ignition systems. HPC resources will enable finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distribution in moving components under diverse loads, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to optimize fuel injection and carburetion, and machine learning algorithms trained on synthetic and real-world sensor data to predict component degradation. By simulating thousands of operational scenarios, we aim to identify failure thresholds, refine diagnostic criteria, and generate adaptive maintenance protocols. Expected outcomes include data-driven models to prioritize part replacements, reduce unplanned downtime, and extend vehicle lifespan. These tools will empower technicians with actionable insights, lower repair costs, and support the sustainable adoption of advanced motorcycle technologies. The project bridges hands-on technical training with computational innovation, fostering a new paradigm in vehicular maintenance education and practice.
cip_title: Motorcycle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain motorcycles and other similar powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication and cooling systems, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuel systems and adjustments of moving parts.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize marine vessel repair and maintenance processes, with a focus on improving the durability, safety, and efficiency of ship components in corrosive and high-stress marine environments. A critical challenge in marine maintenance is predicting the degradation of materials such as steel, fiberglass, and composite hulls under dynamic operational conditions, as well as optimizing repair workflows for complex systems like propulsion shafts and steering mechanisms. Traditional trial-and-error approaches are time-intensive and costly, necessitating data-driven solutions. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale mechanical, chemical, and hydrodynamic interactions affecting vessel integrity. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model stress distribution in hulls and propulsion systems under varying loads, while machine learning algorithms trained on historical failure data will identify corrosion patterns and predict component lifespans. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate repair workflows in virtual drydock environments to optimize technician task allocation and resource use. By integrating these computational approaches, the project aims to generate predictive maintenance frameworks tailored to specific vessel types and operational profiles. Anticipated outcomes include validated models for material failure prediction, adaptive repair protocols to extend component service life, and decision-support tools for prioritizing maintenance interventions. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in marine repair technician training programs, bridging gaps between empirical practices and computational methodologies. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling large-scale simulations of heterogeneous materials and complex fluid-structure interactions, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. This work aligns with broader industry goals to reduce downtime, lower repair costs, and enhance safety in global maritime operations.
cip_title: Marine Maintenance/ Fitter and Ship Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair outboard and inboard engines; test, maintain, and repair steering devices and electrical systems; repair metal, wood, and fiberglass hulls and vessel components; fabricate and maintain sails; and repair and balance propellers and drive shafts.

abstract: This project seeks to advance research in immersive audio production by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the computational challenges of real-time spatial sound processing and machine learning-driven audio enhancement. Current workflows in spatial audio rendering, such as ambisonics and object-based mixing, require intensive processing to simulate dynamic acoustic environments, especially for virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) applications. Existing consumer-grade hardware struggles to handle low-latency, high-channel-count processing, limiting the fidelity and scalability of immersive audio experiences. This research will develop and optimize parallelized algorithms for real-time soundfield synthesis, binaural rendering, and adaptive noise reduction using GPU-accelerated computing. A secondary focus involves training deep learning models on large datasets of multichannel audio recordings to automate tasks like dialogue isolation and acoustic signature matching, which are critical for post-production efficiency. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of room acoustics, GPU-based model training on thousands of hours of audio data, and benchmarking of latency-sensitive processing chains. Outcomes will include open-source tools for spatial audio production, publishable frameworks for computational sound design, and educational modules integrating these methods into Recording Arts Technology curricula. By bridging the gap between artistic intent and technical feasibility, this work aims to democratize high-end immersive audio production while providing empirical insights into computational demands for next-generation media workflows. The results will directly benefit collaborative projects with local VR studios and inform industry standards for real-time audio processing in emerging media platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the production of sound recordings as finished products or as components of film/video, broadcast, live, or mixed media productions. Includes instruction in sound equipment operation and maintenance; music, dialogue, and sound effects recording; soundtrack editing; dubbing and mixing; sound engineering; tape, disk, and CD production; digital recording and transmission; amplification and modulation; and working with producers, editors, directors, artists, and production managers.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in hydroelectric energy system efficiency and longevity by developing advanced computational models to optimize turbine design, maintenance protocols, and environmental impact mitigation. Hydroelectric systems face operational inefficiencies due to factors such as sediment erosion, mechanical wear, and dynamic environmental conditions, which existing models struggle to predict accurately at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct high-fidelity simulations of turbine-fluid interactions, sediment transport dynamics, and structural fatigue under variable load conditions. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model complex flow patterns and sediment accumulation in turbines, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess stress distribution and material degradation in turbine components. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to correlate simulation data with real-world sensor inputs, enabling predictive maintenance frameworks and adaptive control strategies. The computational demands of these multi-physics simulations—requiring parallel processing for large-scale meshing, transient solvers, and probabilistic risk assessments—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include optimized turbine geometries to reduce energy losses, predictive maintenance schedules to minimize downtime, and sediment management strategies to mitigate ecological disruption. These advancements will directly inform technician training programs by providing data-driven insights into installation best practices and failure mitigation. By enhancing the precision of hydroelectric system modeling, this research aims to reduce operational costs, extend infrastructure lifespans, and support the transition to sustainable energy systems. The proposed computational framework will also serve as a template for future applied research in hydroelectric technology, fostering innovation in a critical renewable energy sector.
cip_title: Hydroelectric Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: Urban educational systems face complex, multidimensional challenges shaped by dynamic socioeconomic factors, resource inequities, and diverse student needs. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the interconnected variables influencing educational outcomes in metropolitan contexts, limiting leaders’ capacity to design adaptive policies. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating urban demographic datasets, school performance metrics, and community resource maps to model systemic inequities and simulate intervention strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze longitudinal data from 15 urban school districts (2010–2023), including enrollment patterns, funding allocations, multilingual learner support systems, and neighborhood health indicators. Agent-based modeling will simulate how policy decisions propagate through educational ecosystems, while machine learning techniques will identify high-impact leverage points for reducing achievement gaps. Computational demands include processing terabyte-scale geospatial datasets, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess policy uncertainty, and training neural networks on heterogeneous data streams (sociodemographic, academic, and municipal records). Expected outcomes include 1) a predictive dashboard for evaluating equity-focused resource distribution strategies, 2) evidence-based thresholds for multilingual support staffing in high-need zones, and 3) optimized safety-net service allocation models responsive to housing instability patterns. By quantifying cascading impacts of leadership decisions across urban educational networks, this work will provide administrators with scalable tools to address systemic barriers. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling computationally intensive spatial-temporal analyses and maintaining data security protocols for sensitive student information. Results will advance computational social science applications in educational leadership while directly informing equity audits and strategic planning processes mandated for Title I districts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on issues and problems specific to the educational needs of populations and communities located in metropolitan, inner city, and related areas and prepares individuals to provide educational services and administrative leadership in urban contexts. Includes instruction in multicultural education, at-risk studies, urban sociology, multilingual education, urban studies and planning, human services, health services and nutrition, cross-cultural communication, diversity studies, safety and security, and urban educational administration and leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the evidence-based understanding of therapeutic massage mechanisms and optimize clinical protocols through biomechanical modeling and large-scale data analysis. Despite the widespread use of massage therapy for pain management, rehabilitation, and wellness, the physiological effects of specific manual techniques—such as myofascial release or deep tissue manipulation—remain poorly quantified. Current research relies heavily on qualitative or small-scale clinical studies, limiting the ability to predict individualized outcomes or establish standardized guidelines. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) of soft tissue mechanics with machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of clinical outcome datasets. Three-dimensional biomechanical models will simulate tissue deformation, fluid dynamics, and stress distribution under varying massage parameters (e.g., pressure magnitude, duration, directionality), calibrated using anonymized patient data from partner clinics. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify patterns in treatment efficacy across diverse demographic and physiological profiles. HPC resources are critical to resolve the multiscale complexity of these simulations, which require parallel processing to handle high-resolution meshes, nonlinear material properties of muscle and connective tissues, and transient interactions across anatomical regions. The computational pipeline will be validated against motion-capture and pressure-sensor data from in vitro experiments. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific techniques to quantifiable changes in tissue perfusion, inflammation markers, and pain modulation pathways. These results will inform the development of personalized treatment algorithms and safety thresholds, reducing trial-and-error approaches in practice. By establishing a publicly accessible repository of simulation templates and clinical correlations, this work aims to bridge the gap between manual therapy traditions and computational biomedicine, fostering innovation in massage therapy education and evidence-based practice standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being to clients through the application of manual techniques for manipulating skin, muscles, and connective tissues. Includes instruction in Western (Swedish) massage, sports massage, myotherapy/trigger point massage, myofascial release, deep tissue massage, cranio-sacral therapy, reflexology, massage safety and emergency management, client counseling, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between organismal form and function across diverse taxa using high-performance computing (HPC) to model biomechanical and physiological constraints in evolutionary processes. The research problem centers on understanding how physical and energetic limitations shape the adaptive trajectories of multicellular organisms in variable environments, a question that remains unresolved due to the computational complexity of integrating multi-scale biological data. Current models often oversimplify interactions between anatomical structures, metabolic demands, and environmental pressures, limiting their predictive power. To address this, we propose developing a novel computational framework that combines 3D biomechanical simulations with agent-based modeling to analyze how resource allocation strategies influence survival and reproductive success across simulated ecosystems. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large parameter spaces encompassing morphological variation, energy budgets, and stochastic environmental factors. By leveraging GPU-accelerated finite element analysis and machine learning-based optimization, the project aims to identify universal principles governing trade-offs between structural investment and functional performance. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational platform for predicting adaptive responses to environmental change and quantitative benchmarks for comparing real-world biological systems.
