This work will provide foundational insights into the limits of phenotypic plasticity while establishing computational methods applicable to broad questions in organismal biology. The requested resources are critical for handling the terabytes of simulation data and enabling real-time visualization of complex system interactions, capabilities unattainable with existing institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A general program of biology at the introductory, basic level or a program in biology or the biological sciences that is undifferentiated as to title or content. Includes instruction in general biology and programs covering a variety of biological specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-linguistic grammatical convergence in multilingual contact scenarios through large-scale computational simulations, addressing a critical gap in understanding how social interaction patterns shape structural language change. While prior research has focused on lexical borrowing or phonological shifts, systematic analysis of syntactic and morphological adaptation under diverse sociocommunicative conditions remains understudied due to methodological constraints. We propose developing an agent-based modeling framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate language contact phenomena across 50+ typologically diverse language pairs, incorporating parameters for social network density, prestige asymmetries, and interaction frequency drawn from ethnographic and psycholinguistic data. The computational architecture will integrate neural language models trained on grammatically annotated corpora to simulate production and comprehension behaviors, coupled with evolutionary algorithms modeling intergenerational transmission. Simulations will be deployed across multiple HPC nodes to systematically vary population-scale parameters (10,000+ agents) over 500+ generations, generating longitudinal datasets tracking grammatical alignment. Expected outcomes include identifying threshold conditions for structural convergence, quantifying the relative impact of social versus cognitive factors in contact-induced change, and validating predictions against documented cases of language mixing. Results will advance theoretical models of language evolution while providing methodological innovations in scaling cognitive simulations. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, parallelized simulation runs, and large-scale output analysis, enabling unprecedented resolution in modeling the interplay between individual communicative behaviors and emergent linguistic patterns. This work bridges computational linguistics with language contact theory, offering insights applicable to minority language preservation and AI systems operating in multilingual contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language, language development, and relationships among languages and language groups from a humanistic and/or scientific perspective. Includes instruction in subjects such as psycholinguistics, behavioral linguistics, language acquisition, sociolinguistics, mathematical and computational linguistics, grammatical theory and theoretical linguistics, philosophical linguistics, philology and historical linguistics, comparative linguistics, phonetics, phonemics, dialectology, semantics, functional grammar and linguistics, language typology, lexicography, morphology and syntax, orthography, stylistics, structuralism, rhetoric, and applications to artificial intelligence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to identify college students at risk of academic disengagement or mental health crises by analyzing multimodal datasets from counseling services, academic records, and anonymized student interaction logs. Despite growing demands on student support systems, current approaches often rely on self-referrals or late-stage interventions, leaving gaps in proactive care. The research will integrate structured data (e.g., GPA trends, service utilization) with unstructured data from counseling session transcripts and advising notes using natural language processing (NLP) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process these large-scale datasets (anticipated at 50+ TB), train deep learning models for longitudinal risk prediction, and simulate intervention outcomes across diverse student subpopulations. Computational workflows will employ transformer-based architectures for text analysis, graph neural networks to model social support networks, and ensemble methods to account for temporal academic patterns. The project will validate models against historical student outcomes from three partner institutions, ensuring generalizability through federated learning approaches. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for higher education institutions to prioritize counseling outreach, optimize resource allocation, and personalize support strategies. By enabling real-time analysis of complex student data, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in student affairs, reduce equity gaps in service access, and establish computational social science methodologies within college counseling research. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and secure data processing compliant with FERPA regulations.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: Cancer-related muscle wasting and dysfunction present significant challenges to patient quality of life and treatment efficacy, yet the systemic and molecular mechanisms linking exercise adaptation to cancer pathophysiology remain poorly understood. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational model of skeletal muscle response to exercise in the context of cancer, integrating cellular energetics, systemic inflammation, and tumor-derived metabolic perturbations. Current experimental models struggle to isolate the dynamic interactions between exercise-induced anabolic signaling, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and tumor microenvironment factors that drive cachexia. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework coupling finite element models of muscle fiber force production with agent-based simulations of intercellular signaling networks. The model will incorporate clinical data from oncology-exercise trials, including cytokine profiles, muscle biopsy transcriptomics, and real-time wearable sensor outputs from patients undergoing prescribed exercise regimens. Computational workloads will focus on parameter optimization across heterogeneous datasets and stochastic simulations of metabolic crosstalk between tumor, immune, and muscle cells. Resource allocation is critical for parallelized solving of ordinary differential equation systems characterizing proteostasis and mitochondrial bioenergetics at scale. Expected outcomes include identification of exercise intensity thresholds that maximize myocyte survival signaling while minimizing tumor-promoting systemic stress, as well as predictive biomarkers of exercise responsiveness in cachexia-prone patients. This work will establish a first-in-class computational platform to personalize exercise prescriptions in oncology, directly addressing the NIH’s prioritization of mechanistic frameworks for exercise as adjuvant cancer therapy. By bridging exercise physiology with tumor-host dynamics, the project advances fundamental knowledge of how physical activity modulates pathological physiology while delivering translatable tools for clinical kinesiology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physiological processes involved in physical or motor activity, including sensorimotor interactions, response mechanisms, and the effects of injury, disease, and disability. Includes instruction in muscular and skeletal anatomy; molecular and cellular basis of muscle contraction; fuel utilization; neurophysiology of motor mechanics; systemic physiological responses (respiration, blood flow, endocrine secretions, and others); fatigue and exhaustion; muscle and body training; physiology of specific exercises and activities; physiology of injury; and the effects of disabilities and disease.

abstract: The increasing complexity of radionuclide-based in vitro analyses in clinical pathology demands advanced computational tools to optimize diagnostic accuracy, laboratory efficiency, and safety protocols. Current methods for quantifying radioisotopes in biological samples (e.g., blood, urine, biopsied tissues) rely on static calibration models that inadequately account for temporal decay variations, matrix interference effects, and non-linear detector responses. This project proposes to develop dynamic, high-resolution simulation frameworks to address these limitations, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-physics interactions at scale. We will implement Monte Carlo simulations to track radiation transport through heterogeneous sample matrices and detector systems, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on experimental datasets to predict isotope-specific decay corrections and quenching effects. Parallelized workflows will process high-throughput spectral data from gamma counters and liquid scintillation systems, integrating time-resolved decay constants and environmental variables (e.g., temperature, pH) to improve quantification accuracy. A secondary aim involves simulating isotope storage conditions to optimize containment geometries and shielding configurations, reducing occupational exposure risks. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time parameter optimization during live experiments, enabled by HPC-scale containerization to maintain reproducibility across clinical laboratories. Expected outcomes include validated models for 10 commonly used diagnostic radionuclides (e.g., Tc-99m, I-131), an open-source analysis toolkit for automated quality control, and evidence-based guidelines for safe isotope handling. By enabling precision-adjusted in vitro radioassays, this work aims to reduce diagnostic errors in conditions such as thyroid dysfunction and metastatic cancer monitoring while advancing computational pathology infrastructure for radiopharmaceutical development. The requested HPC allocation is critical to manage the petabyte-scale datasets and iterative training processes required for robust, generalizable models in this high-dimensional parameter space.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of radionuclides in the study of body fluids, excreta, or tissues quantified outside the body. May included related research in laboratory management and safety, quality control, instrumentation, isotope storage and in vitro analyses.

abstract: Healthcare organizations face escalating challenges in safeguarding sensitive patient data against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats, necessitating advanced computational approaches to model, analyze, and secure complex health information systems. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a multi-layered privacy-preserving framework for large-scale healthcare datasets. The research problem centers on the inadequacy of existing cryptographic and anonymization techniques to balance data utility with privacy compliance in distributed healthcare environments, particularly as datasets grow in volume and heterogeneity. Computational methods will include parallelized simulations of adversarial attacks on synthetic health datasets to stress-test privacy mechanisms, optimization of federated learning architectures for secure multi-institutional data collaboration, and scalable implementations of homomorphic encryption for real-time analytics. Machine learning models will be trained on HPC clusters to detect emergent threat patterns in network traffic logs, while graph-based algorithms will map vulnerabilities in interoperable health information exchange (HIE) systems. Expected outcomes include quantifiable benchmarks for privacy-utility tradeoffs in terabyte-scale health datasets, open-source tools for automated compliance auditing under HIPAA and GDPR, and novel protocols for secure genomic data sharing. The computational intensity of simulating healthcare cyber-physical systems—modeling millions of patient records across distributed nodes—requires dedicated HPC resources for memory-intensive encryption trials and parallel vulnerability assessments. This work will directly address critical gaps in healthcare information security infrastructure, providing evidence-based strategies to prevent data breaches while maintaining clinical usability. Results will be disseminated through healthcare IT conferences and collaborative partnerships with regional hospital networks, potentially influencing national standards for health data protection in cloud-based environments.
cip_title: Healthcare Information Privacy Assurance and Security
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers in designing, implementing, and administering comprehensive privacy and security protection programs in all types of healthcare organizations. Includes instruction in health information ethics, healthcare information privacy and security, healthcare compliance, healthcare information security and disaster recovery, and healthcare privacy law.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the critical challenge of scalable, high-fidelity multi-physics integration in computational engineering, a domain not confined to traditional disciplinary boundaries but essential for advancing next-generation engineering systems. Current approaches to coupling disparate physical models—such as thermal, fluid, structural, and electromagnetic phenomena—often rely on static, manually tuned interfaces that introduce inefficiencies, inaccuracies, and scalability bottlenecks in high-performance computing (HPC) environments. This project aims to develop a novel, adaptive computational framework that dynamically optimizes multi-physics coupling through a hybrid approach combining domain decomposition, machine learning (ML)-driven parameterization, and asynchronous parallelization. The framework will leverage graph-based representations to model interactions between physical domains, enabling automated load balancing and adaptive resolution scaling across heterogeneous HPC architectures. Key computational innovations include the integration of reinforcement learning to predict optimal coupling intervals and error tolerance thresholds, reducing synchronization overhead while maintaining numerical stability. The research will validate the framework using benchmark problems from emerging engineering applications such as plasma-assisted manufacturing and hypersonic material degradation, where tightly coupled multi-physics interactions defy conventional single-domain simulation tools. Anticipated outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in wall-clock time for coupled simulations compared to existing monolithic solvers, demonstrated on petascale systems via weak and strong scaling studies. By providing an open-source, modular toolkit for adaptive multi-physics integration, this work will empower interdisciplinary engineering research in areas requiring complex system-level simulations, from energy-material interfaces to bioelectronic device design, without dependence on domain-specific solvers. The results will advance computational engineering methodologies by bridging gaps between algorithmic innovation, HPC resource utilization, and cross-domain model interoperability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to engineering practice and research. Includes instruction in engineering and science fundamentals, advanced mathematics, algorithms, computer languages, and software engineering design.

abstract: This project addresses the critical need for advanced computational resources to analyze the linguistic complexity and dialectal diversity of Indonesian and Malay languages, which remain understudied in computational humanities due to the lack of scalable infrastructure. The research focuses on two interrelated challenges: (1) mapping phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variations across 300+ regional Malay dialects using heterogeneous data sources (historical manuscripts, modern social media, transcribed oral narratives), and (2) modeling diachronic language shifts in Indonesian through automated analysis of century-spanning textual corpora. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-stage computational workflow utilizing natural language processing (NLP) and deep learning architectures. Transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variations) will be trained on distributed GPU clusters to handle code-switching patterns and non-standard orthographies, while phylogenetic algorithms will reconstruct dialect relationships using MPI-parallelized comparative analysis. The workflow requires processing 12TB of text and audio data (converted to spectrogram representations via parallel Fourier transforms), necessitating large-memory nodes and high-throughput storage systems. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Malay dialects, a temporally annotated Indonesian language corpus (1600CE-present), and open-source NLP tools optimized for low-resource Austronesian languages. These resources will directly support endangered language preservation efforts and enhance machine translation systems for regional development initiatives. By establishing computational methods tailored to Indonesian/Malay philological characteristics, this project aims to redefine research paradigms in Southeast Asian linguistics while demonstrating how HPC capabilities can bridge gaps between traditional humanistic scholarship and cutting-edge language technologies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Malay and Indonesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize irrigation scheduling and system design in water-scarce agricultural regions. Current irrigation management practices often rely on static crop water requirement models, which fail to dynamically account for real-time soil moisture variability, localized weather patterns, and heterogeneous field conditions. This limitation leads to inefficient water use, energy overconsumption by pumping systems, and reduced crop yields. To address this gap, we propose integrating sensor network data, satellite-derived evapotranspiration estimates, and machine learning (ML) models within a distributed computing architecture. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run parallelized simulations of soil-water dynamics across diverse agricultural landscapes, using physically based hydrologic models coupled with ML-driven predictive analytics. Key computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale datasets from IoT soil sensors, resolving fine-scale spatial gradients in soil properties, and iteratively training ensemble models to forecast irrigation demand under climate uncertainty. The project will validate simulations against field experiments conducted in partnership with regional farming cooperatives, comparing traditional irrigation schedules against model-prescribed variable-rate systems. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolset for adaptive irrigation management, reducing water use by 15–30% in testbed systems while maintaining crop productivity. By enabling precision control of pumping infrastructure and drainage networks, this work aims to advance scalable solutions for sustainable agriculture, particularly in arid regions facing heightened water stress. The requested HPC resources are critical to support the multi-node GPU-accelerated workloads required for near-real-time decision-making at farm-to-watershed scales.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in the field of agricultural technology and irrigation. Includes instruction in irrigation and drainage methodologies, pumping and delivery systems, system design and evaluation, and principles of installation and repair of irrigation systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in motorcycle engine performance optimization and predictive maintenance through advanced computational modeling. Modern motorcycles integrate complex mechanical, electrical, and fuel systems, where small inefficiencies in components such as carburetors, ignition timing, or cooling systems can lead to significant performance degradation or failure. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to diagnostics and tuning are time-intensive and often fail to account for dynamic interactions between subsystems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of high-fidelity simulations leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multiphysics interactions within motorcycle engines and drivetrains. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be employed to analyze fuel-air mixture dynamics in carburetion systems under varying operational conditions, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess thermal stress distributions in engine components. Machine learning models trained on synthetic and experimental datasets will predict wear patterns in moving parts and optimize maintenance schedules. The scale of these simulations—particularly the resolution required for micron-level fuel droplet behavior in carburetors and real-time thermal profiling—necessitates parallelized computing architectures. By integrating these computational tools, the project aims to generate actionable insights for (1) optimizing fuel efficiency and emissions in legacy and modern engines, (2) developing predictive maintenance algorithms to reduce mechanical failures, and (3) informing the design of next-generation lubrication and cooling systems. Outcomes will be validated against dynamometer tests and field data from industry partners. Successful implementation will provide a template for data-driven motorcycle maintenance protocols, reduce environmental impact through emission minimization, and enhance the technical toolkit available to motorcycle repair technicians. This work directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance repair technologies through innovative technical methodologies.
cip_title: Motorcycle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain motorcycles and other similar powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication and cooling systems, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuel systems and adjustments of moving parts.

abstract: The development of sustainable wood-based materials and efficient pulp processing technologies is hindered by the complex, hierarchical structure of wood and the energy-intensive nature of industrial manufacturing. Current experimental approaches struggle to predict the multiscale interactions between wood components (cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin) during processing or to optimize equipment design for emerging biorefinery applications. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable physics-based simulations and machine learning workflows that bridge molecular-scale material behavior with macroscopic process engineering. We will employ molecular dynamics to model lignin depolymerization mechanisms during kraft pulping, finite element analysis to predict stress distributions in engineered wood composites under hygrothermal loads, and computational fluid dynamics to simulate fiber suspension flows in paper-forming systems. Machine learning models trained on these simulations and experimental datasets will identify correlations between raw material properties, processing parameters, and final product performance. The HPC environment is critical for executing these computationally intensive models, particularly for parametric studies exploring diverse wood feedstocks and large-scale reactor designs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing pulp yield while reducing chemical inputs, virtual prototyping frameworks for defect-resistant wood composites, and operational guidelines for energy-efficient paper machine operations. This computational approach will reduce reliance on physical trials, accelerate the development of circular production strategies, and support the transition to climate-smart forest product manufacturing. By integrating HPC-driven insights with traditional wood science methodologies, the project aims to advance fundamental knowledge of wood-water interactions, fibrillation dynamics, and process scalability while delivering actionable solutions for industry partners.
cip_title: Wood Science and Wood Products/ Pulp and Paper Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the analysis of the properties and behavior of wood and wood products and the development of processes for converting wood into paper and other products. Includes instruction in wood classification and testing, product development, manufacturing and processing technologies, and the design and development of related equipment and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary study examining the evolution of cultural narratives across digitized historical archives. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how large-scale sociocultural shifts—such as migration, technological adoption, or ideological conflicts—are reflected and reinforced through textual artifacts spanning diverse geographies and time periods. Traditional humanities methodologies struggle to systematically analyze the scale and complexity of such datasets, which include multilingual manuscripts, periodicals, and public records from the 18th to 20th centuries. By integrating computational linguistics, network analysis, and machine learning, this project aims to identify latent patterns in narrative propagation, semantic adaptation, and cross-cultural influence. The computational approach involves developing a pipeline to preprocess heterogeneous text corpora (OCR corrections, language translation, and entity recognition), followed by transformer-based models to map thematic evolution and graph-based algorithms to model narrative diffusion. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative training of deep learning architectures, necessitating HPC infrastructure for efficient GPU utilization and distributed storage. Expected outcomes include (1) a reusable framework for interdisciplinary analysis of historical texts, (2) empirical insights into how regional narratives coalesced into global discourses during pivotal historical transitions, and (3) publicly accessible visualizations of narrative networks to support pedagogy and policy discussions on cultural memory. The project bridges computational scalability with humanistic inquiry, offering a model for resource-intensive interdisciplinary research that transcends conventional disciplinary boundaries. By elucidating mechanisms of cultural persistence and change, the findings will inform contemporary efforts to address polarization and identity-based conflicts, demonstrating the broader societal relevance of integrating HPC-driven methods into non-STEM disciplines.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The optimization of multi-phase chemical reactors is a critical challenge in industrial processes such as petroleum refining and pharmaceutical synthesis, where inefficiencies in heat and mass transfer lead to significant energy waste and operational costs. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve the complex, dynamic interactions between gas, liquid, and solid phases at varying scales, limiting the ability to predict and mitigate localized hotspots, incomplete mixing, or catalyst deactivation. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model multi-phase reactive flows in industrial reactors, enabling the design of energy-efficient and scalable systems. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a multi-scale approach combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with discrete element method (DEM) simulations to capture particle-scale interactions and reactor-scale hydrodynamics. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate parameter optimization and uncertainty quantification, reducing computational costs associated with traditional trial-and-error methods. The simulations will leverage open-source tools (OpenFOAM, LIGGGHTS) and custom code to model industrially relevant geometries, validated against experimental data from collaborating partners in chemical manufacturing. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for reactor performance under diverse operating conditions, identification of optimal flow regimes to minimize energy consumption, and guidelines for scaling laboratory-scale processes to industrial production. By addressing these computational bottlenecks, the project aims to advance the sustainable intensification of chemical processes, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and raw material waste. The resulting open-access datasets and workflows will provide a foundation for future research in reactor design and operator training, directly supporting the chemical industry’s transition toward net-zero operations. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the high memory demands of DEM-CFD coupling and the parallel processing requirements of ensemble simulations across thousands of cores.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of chemical processing equipment in industries such as chemical manufacturing, petroleum refining, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and waste water treatment. Includes instruction in mathematics, chemistry, and physics; computer applications; chemical and refinery plant operations, processes, and equipment; safety, health, and environment; instrumentation; troubleshooting; and applications to specific industries.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models for optimizing operational and rehabilitative strategies within correctional facilities. Correctional systems face complex challenges, including overcrowding, resource allocation inefficiencies, and dynamic interactions between incarcerated populations and staff, all of which impact rehabilitation outcomes and facility safety. Traditional approaches to these problems are often reactive, relying on historical data or generalized protocols that fail to account for the nonlinear, adaptive behaviors of individuals within carceral environments. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent simulation framework that models facility operations, inmate behavior, and staff decision-making under varying policy conditions. The framework integrates real-world data—such as demographic trends, incident reports, and program participation rates—with behavioral theory to simulate scenarios ranging from routine daily operations to crisis events (e.g., conflicts, medical emergencies). Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze simulation outputs, identify high-risk patterns, and generate predictive insights for proactive interventions. Computational demands are significant due to the need for fine-grained, parallelized simulations across diverse facility types and policy regimes, necessitating HPC capabilities for scalable processing and storage. Expected outcomes include actionable recommendations for staffing ratios, program scheduling, and crisis response protocols, as well as a publicly accessible toolkit for correctional administrators to test policy changes in silico. By bridging computational social science with correctional practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in a historically under-resourced field while adhering to ethical imperatives of fairness and transparency. The project’s computational outputs will undergo rigorous validation against empirical datasets, with collaboration from state correctional agencies to ensure practical relevance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study the theories and principles, of correctional science and to function as professional corrections officers and other workers in public and/or private incarceration facilities.

abstract: The increasing complexity of health system pharmacy operations, driven by evolving patient needs, medication shortages, and cost constraints, demands advanced computational tools to optimize decision-making. Current approaches to medication utilization analysis, inventory management, and clinical outcome prediction often rely on simplified models that fail to account for the dynamic interplay of patient-specific factors, institutional workflows, and real-world data granularity. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model large-scale pharmacy operations and clinical outcomes across diverse healthcare settings. Using anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), medication dispensing data, and supply chain logs from multiple health systems, we will implement parallelized machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in medication-related adverse events, predict critical drug shortages, and simulate the impact of alternative staffing and inventory policies. Computational workflows will integrate time-series forecasting, natural language processing of clinical notes, and agent-based modeling to capture multi-level interactions between pharmacists, patients, and institutional resources. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of petabyte-scale datasets while maintaining the temporal resolution required for operational decision support. Expected outcomes include predictive models for adverse drug event risk stratification, optimized medication distribution protocols under resource constraints, and evidence-based recommendations for pharmacy workflow redesign. By leveraging distributed computing architectures, this work will provide health systems with scalable tools to improve medication safety, reduce waste, and enhance care coordination. The resulting open-source computational framework will advance research capabilities in pharmacy administration by enabling reproducible analysis of system-level interventions across heterogeneous care environments.
cip_definition: Research focused on Health System Pharmacy Administration

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and validation of computational models for optimizing personalized counseling interventions in diverse populations. Counseling psychology faces a critical challenge in tailoring therapeutic strategies to individual clients’ dynamic needs, particularly when addressing complex, overlapping distress symptoms (e.g., anxiety, relational conflicts, identity-related stressors) that vary across cultural and socioeconomic contexts. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between client characteristics, intervention techniques, and longitudinal outcomes. To address this, we propose building machine learning (ML) frameworks trained on multimodal datasets, including anonymized clinical session transcripts, client self-report metrics, and demographic data from supervised counseling practice archives. These models will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to analyze therapeutic dialogue patterns, graph neural networks to map symptom interdependencies, and reinforcement learning to simulate intervention adaptation over time. The scale of data (projected at 50,000+ session records) and complexity of modeling temporal, textual, and relational variables necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized training and large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to identify client subgroups most likely to benefit from specific counseling modalities, (2) a computational framework for simulating the longitudinal impacts of culturally adapted interventions, and (3) open-source algorithms to help practitioners refine case conceptualizations. By bridging counseling psychology’s human-centered ethos with computational rigor, this work aims to enhance equitable access to effective mental health support while maintaining ethical alignment with client autonomy and therapeutic relationship principles. The requested resources will enable iterative model development, including sensitivity analyses to mitigate algorithmic bias and ensure interpretability for clinical utility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of psychological counseling, involving the rendering of therapeutic services to individuals and groups experiencing psychological problems and exhibiting distress symptoms. Includes instruction in counseling theory, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient/counselor relationships, testing and assessment methods and procedures, group therapy, marital and family therapy, child and adolescent therapy, supervised counseling practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of personality dynamics by integrating multi-level data on trait-behavior interactions, neurophysiological correlates, and environmental feedback loops. Personality psychology has long grappled with the challenge of modeling the temporal stability and context-dependent variability of traits, particularly when accounting for biological mechanisms (e.g., neurotransmitter systems) and social reinforcement patterns. Traditional statistical approaches struggle to handle the non-linear interactions, high-dimensional longitudinal data, and recursive individual-environment transactions central to these phenomena. We propose developing agent-based models and dynamical systems frameworks to simulate how enduring personality characteristics emerge from and adapt to intra-individual neurocognitive processes (e.g., dopaminergic reward sensitivity) and inter-individual social evaluations. The computational pipeline will implement hierarchical Bayesian inference to estimate latent trait-state networks from multimodal datasets, including experience-sampling surveys, functional neuroimaging meta-analyses, and behavioral task performance metrics. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across 50,000+ simulated agents with individualized neural architectures, processing decade-spanning longitudinal data from three established cohort studies (total N > 15,000), and conducting parameter space explorations of trait development under varying environmental contingencies. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating personality-environment co-evolution, (2) novel insights into mechanistic boundaries between major theoretical frameworks (e.g., reinforcement sensitivity theory vs. socioanalytic models), and (3) empirically grounded hypotheses about neurocomputational moderators of trait malleability. By enabling simultaneous modeling of biological, cognitive, and social timescales, this work aims to bridge gaps between dispositional, process-oriented, and interpersonal approaches in personality psychology while establishing computational best practices for the field.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the unique organization of fairly permanent characteristics that set the individual apart from other individuals and, at the same time, determine how others respond to that individual. Includes instruction in Freudian, Skinnerian, Rogerian, and Ellisonian psychology; neo-Freudian psychology; psychological systems, neurophysiology, and psychopharmacology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing personalized therapeutic recreation (TR) interventions targeting neurodevelopmental and chronic pain conditions. TR utilizes structured leisure activities to improve physical, cognitive, and psychosocial outcomes, yet current protocols rely on generalized guidelines with limited predictive power for individual response variability. The research problem centers on the lack of computational tools to analyze complex, multimodal datasets—including biometric wearables, patient-reported outcomes, and neurobehavioral assessments—that could dynamically tailor TR interventions. We propose a machine learning pipeline integrating temporal convolutional networks and graph neural networks to model nonlinear interactions between intervention parameters (activity type, duration, social context) and multidimensional health outcomes (motor function, emotional regulation, pain biomarkers). The computational approach will process high-dimensional datasets from a longitudinal cohort (n=450) undergoing TR protocols, incorporating federated learning techniques to preserve patient privacy across collaborating clinical sites. HPC resources are critical for training ensemble models on heterogeneous data streams (sampled at 10-100Hz) and simulating intervention efficacy through agent-based modeling of virtual patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source platform for adaptive TR prescription, identification of latent biomarkers predictive of intervention success, and quantitative frameworks to personalize activity sequencing based on real-time physiological feedback. This work bridges health sciences and computational modeling to advance precision therapeutic recreation, offering novel methodologies for non-pharmacological intervention design while addressing scalability challenges in allied health research. Results will directly inform clinical guidelines for TR in underserved populations with complex comorbidities, enhancing accessibility to evidence-based, data-driven rehabilitation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, organize, and direct recreational activities designed to promote health and well-being for patients who are physically, mentally, or emotionally disabled. Includes instruction in the foundations of therapeutic recreation, leisure education and counseling, program planning, therapeutic recreational modalities, basic anatomy and physiology, psychology, medical terminology, human growth and development, patient observation and evaluation, special needs populations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize clinical training scenarios for nursing educators using high-fidelity simulations, addressing a critical gap in scalable, evidence-based pedagogical strategies. Nursing education faces challenges in balancing resource-intensive clinical training with growing student cohorts and variable clinical site availability. Existing approaches to simulation design often rely on generalized templates, which may not adequately adapt to diverse learner needs or evolving clinical competencies. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven approach to dynamically model student performance data, clinical competency metrics, and patient scenario variables. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process multimodal datasets from electronic health records, sensor-based simulation equipment, and longitudinal assessment tools. Using cluster computing capabilities, we will train neural networks to identify patterns in skill acquisition rates, error thresholds, and scenario complexity. A parallelized Monte Carlo method will then simulate thousands of training pathway variations to determine optimal scenario sequences for different learner profiles. The computational workflow will integrate natural language processing of nursing narratives, time-series analysis of simulation performance logs, and topological data analysis of competency networks. Expected outcomes include a predictive model for personalized simulation sequencing and an open-source toolkit for adaptive scenario generation. This work will directly inform curriculum development in advanced nursing practice programs while establishing quantitative benchmarks for clinical competency assessment. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to transform how nursing educators design clinical simulations, ultimately improving the efficiency of skill transfer and patient safety outcomes in real-world healthcare settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to teach in academic and clinical settings, including staff development. Includes instruction in advanced nursing practice, nursing role development, curriculum and instruction, program and course design, clinical instruction, and evaluation of learning.

abstract: The increasing complexity of gastrointestinal and hepatic diseases, such as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), necessitates advanced computational approaches to integrate multi-dimensional data for personalized treatment strategies. Current clinical models often fail to account for the interplay between genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and longitudinal clinical data, limiting their predictive accuracy. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning algorithms capable of synthesizing heterogeneous datasets. We will aggregate and preprocess multi-omics data from cohorts of patients with NAFLD, HCV-related cirrhosis, and IBD, alongside electronic health records encompassing imaging, histopathology, and treatment outcomes. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models and graph neural networks, will be trained to identify predictive biomarkers, stratify disease subtypes, and forecast progression to complications such as hepatocellular carcinoma or treatment-resistant flares. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing on HPC clusters to handle the scale of data (>100 TB) and the complexity of models requiring millions of parameters. The anticipated outcomes include the creation of open-source predictive tools validated against prospective clinical data, novel insights into molecular drivers of disease heterogeneity, and a framework for real-time decision support in clinical workflows. By enabling the analysis of previously intractable datasets, this research aims to advance precision medicine in gastroenterology and hepatology, ultimately improving risk stratification and therapeutic targeting for complex digestive diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on Gastroenterology and Hepatology

abstract: Regulatory science faces a critical challenge in evaluating complex, rapidly evolving medical technologies—such as AI-driven diagnostics or gene-edited therapies—where traditional approval frameworks struggle to balance safety, efficacy, and innovation. This project proposes a computational approach to model and simulate regulatory decision pathways for emerging technologies, enabling data-driven policy optimization. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate interactions between regulators, developers, and clinical trial data streams under varying regulatory scenarios. These ABMs will integrate real-world FDA submission datasets, synthetic clinical trial data generated via generative adversarial networks (GANs), and dynamic risk-benefit algorithms that account for evolving post-market evidence. A parallelized computational workflow will assess thousands of regulatory parameter combinations (e.g., evidence thresholds, adaptive trial designs, real-world evidence integration protocols) to identify optimal pathways that minimize time-to-decision while maintaining safety standards. Validation will involve retrospective analysis of historical device/drug approvals and forward-looking case studies on AI-based medical imaging systems. The HPC environment is essential for scaling Monte Carlo simulations across multidimensional parameter spaces and managing petabytes of structured/unstructured regulatory document data. Outcomes will include an open-source computational toolkit for predictive regulatory analytics, quantitative benchmarks for evidence requirements in novel technology domains, and policy recommendations for adaptive licensing frameworks. This work aims to transform regulatory science into a proactive, simulation-informed discipline capable of accelerating patient access to breakthrough technologies without compromising scientific rigor.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the regulatory process for companies innovating and developing cutting edge products in science, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medicine. Includes instruction in regulatory affairs, clinical documentation, human and animal subject protection, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, data management and analysis, good manufacturing practices, and quality management.

abstract: This research project seeks to integrate advanced computational modeling with traditional sculpture practices to address material and structural challenges in large-scale three-dimensional art. While sculptors have long relied on empirical methods to predict material behavior, the increasing complexity of contemporary works—incorporating dynamic forms, hybrid materials, and interactive elements—demands precise simulations of stress distribution, environmental interactions, and fabrication feasibility. Current tools lack the resolution and scalability to model irregular geometries or heterogeneous media such as metal-resin composites, limiting artists’ capacity to prototype ambitious projects without physical trial-and-error. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics simulation framework tailored to sculptural workflows. Computational fluid dynamics will model casting processes for molten metals and bio-based polymers, while finite element analysis will predict structural integrity under gravitational and dynamic loads for free-standing installations. Machine learning models trained on material datasets will correlate tensile strength, thermal expansion, and weathering resistance with artistic intent, enabling predictive guidance for material selection. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will assist in optimizing relief patterns and surface textures under spatial constraints. The simulations will be validated against physical tests conducted in the university’s sculpture studio, including strain measurements from embedded sensors in clay prototypes and 3D-scanned deformation profiles of welded steel assemblies. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for computational sculptural design, reducing material waste and enabling safer, more efficient fabrication of structurally innovative works. By bridging computational engineering and artistic practice, this research aims to expand the expressive possibilities of sculpture while establishing new interdisciplinary methodologies for integrating HPC-driven analytics into visual arts pedagogy and creation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by creating three-dimensional art works. Includes instruction in the analysis of form in space; round and relief concepts; sculptural composition; modern and experimental methods; different media such as clay, plaster, wood, stone, and metal; techniques such as carving, molding, welding, casting, and modeling; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in diver safety and operational efficiency through advanced computational modeling of underwater physiological responses and equipment dynamics. Professional diving involves complex interactions between human physiology, environmental variables, and equipment performance, particularly under extreme pressure conditions. Current decompression models and equipment design protocols rely on generalized assumptions that fail to account for individual variability, dynamic environmental factors, or real-time equipment feedback, contributing to preventable risks such as decompression sickness (DCS) and equipment failure. To resolve this, we propose developing high-fidelity simulations of gas exchange dynamics, tissue saturation profiles, and equipment-environment interactions using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. These simulations will integrate multi-scale physiological data, including cardiovascular function, tissue permeability, and gas solubility, with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of rebreather systems and underwater tools. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to optimize decompression schedules and predict failure modes in diving gear under varying conditions. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the high dimensionality of coupled biological-physical systems, requiring parallelized solvers for partial differential equations and large-scale parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include personalized decompression protocols, improved safety margins for mixed-gas diving operations, and data-driven designs for next-generation diving equipment. This work will directly enhance training simulations for diving professionals, reduce occupational hazards, and inform regulatory frameworks. By bridging gaps in hyperbaric medicine and marine engineering, the project will establish a computational foundation for adaptive, real-time decision support systems in commercial, scientific, and military diving contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as professional deep-water or scuba divers, diving instructors, or diving support personnel. Includes instruction in the use of diving equipment and related specialized gear; diving safety procedures; operation and maintenance of underwater life-support systems; underwater communication systems; decompression systems; underwater salvage; exploration, rescue, and photography; and installation and fitting of underwater mechanical systems and their maintenance, repair or demolition.

abstract: Veterinary anesthesiology faces critical challenges in optimizing drug dosing and pain management protocols due to the vast physiological variability across species, body weights, and comorbidities. Current anesthetic regimens, often extrapolated from human or limited veterinary studies, may inadequately address these complexities, leading to suboptimal outcomes such as intraoperative instability, prolonged recovery, or undertreated pain. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to predict individualized anesthetic and analgesic requirements for diverse animal patients, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the multidimensional nature of this problem. The research will integrate species-specific pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models, dynamic physiological simulations, and machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on retrospective clinical data, including electronic health records, intraoperative monitoring streams, and post-operative recovery metrics. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing to simulate drug interactions, fluid dynamics during hemodilution, and nociceptive pathways under varying physiological states. Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes of dosing strategies across virtual patient populations, while finite element analysis will model localized drug diffusion in epidural and regional nerve block procedures. Additionally, reinforcement learning frameworks will iteratively optimize protocols based on simulated clinical scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide dose titration, reduce adverse events, and enhance perioperative safety in species ranging from small companion animals to large livestock. The models will also inform real-time decision support systems for critical care settings and improve protocols for pain management in chronic conditions. By bridging translational gaps in veterinary anesthesiology, this work aims to establish a computational foundation for precision medicine in animal healthcare, directly impacting clinical outcomes, operational efficiency, and safety standards in veterinary surgical and critical care environments.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical animal care and the care of pain problems. May included related research in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: Surgical wound healing and tissue reconstruction outcomes are critically influenced by complex biomechanical, biochemical, and patient-specific factors, yet current clinical approaches lack predictive tools to optimize individualized surgical planning. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to simulate wound biomechanics, predict healing trajectories, and evaluate reconstructive surgical strategies under diverse physiological conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement multi-scale finite element models integrating tissue-level stress-strain dynamics, cellular-scale mechanobiological responses, and patient-derived imaging data (e.g., CT, MRI) to quantify how surgical techniques, material properties of grafts or sutures, and comorbidities (e.g., diabetes, obesity) interact to affect healing. Machine learning pipelines will be trained on retrospective clinical datasets to identify predictive signatures of complications such as dehiscence or infection. The computational framework will also simulate blood flow and oxygen diffusion in reconstructed tissues to assess perfusion adequacy. By parallelizing these resource-intensive simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to achieve submillimeter spatial resolution and real-time parameter optimization for surgical variables. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for wound failure risk, a decision-support tool for personalized flap/graft design, and mechanistic insights into how mechanical forces modulate cellular healing pathways. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs for novel surgical protocols and provide open-source computational tools to advance precision surgery. The scale of 3D tissue modeling, integration of multi-omics data, and iterative machine learning workflows necessitate HPC capabilities beyond institutional computing infrastructure, particularly for GPU-accelerated simulations and large-memory data processing. Successful implementation will bridge a critical gap between computational biomechanics and translational surgical research.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive computational framework to analyze complex, spatiotemporal environmental datasets for predicting ecosystem responses to extreme climate events—a challenge requiring integration of heterogeneous data streams, nonlinear pattern detection, and predictive uncertainty quantification. Current approaches in climate-impact modeling often treat physical, biological, and anthropogenic factors as isolated systems, limiting their ability to capture cascading failures in interdependent ecological networks. Our work addresses this gap by combining graph-based data mining of multisource observational records (remote sensing, species tracking, soil sensors) with novel hybrid machine learning architectures. The computational approach leverages transformer-based models to process irregularly sampled temporal data, coupled with geometric deep learning to analyze spatial dependencies across varying scales. A key innovation involves training adversarial networks to synthesize rare-event scenarios, enabling robust prediction of low-probability, high-impact climatic tipping points. The framework will be tested on a globally distributed dataset spanning 40 years of marine-terrestrial interface records, including hyperspectral imagery, microbial metagenomics, and human land-use histories. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: (1) parallelized processing of petabyte-scale geospatial arrays using distributed tensor decomposition, (2) optimization of memory-intensive graph neural networks modeling species interaction networks, and (3) Bayesian uncertainty propagation across chained models via Monte Carlo simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for coupled human-natural system forecasting, validated through case studies on coastal forest collapse and phytoplankton regime shifts. The resource demands stem from the need to simultaneously maintain high-resolution environmental representations while capturing decade-scale temporal dynamics—a computational challenge exceeding conventional cluster capabilities. Successful implementation will provide both methodological advances in handling ecological "big data" heterogeneity and practical insights for climate resilience planning, bridging gaps between computational science, environmental physics, and conservation policy.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of data mining and machine learning. Includes instruction in naive Bayes rule, artificial neural networks, genetic algorithms, decision tree learning, neural nets, network science, optimization, statistical computing, and graphical models and methods.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-border disinformation ecosystems and their impact on national security decision-making, leveraging advanced computational methods to analyze multilingual, multimedia data streams. As digital platforms enable rapid dissemination of manipulated narratives across geopolitical boundaries, traditional qualitative approaches struggle to scale to the volume, velocity, and complexity of these information operations. Our research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to identify coordinated influence campaigns, trace their transnational diffusion pathways, and model their potential effects on public perception and policy outcomes. Using a combination of natural language processing (NLP), temporal network analysis, and agent-based modeling, we will process terabyte-scale datasets spanning social media platforms, state-aligned news outlets, and leaked strategic communications. High-performance computing resources are critical for training transformer-based models on low-resource languages prevalent in understudied regions, conducting real-time sentiment and semantic analysis across 10+ languages, and simulating multi-actor scenarios in evolving geopolitical contexts. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel taxonomy of cross-platform disinfection tactics tailored to asymmetric conflict zones, (2) predictive models of narrative escalation patterns during diplomatic crises, and (3) an open-source toolkit for security analysts to assess information vulnerabilities in multilateral engagements. By integrating computational social science with intelligence studies, this work advances methodological innovation in tracking emergent hybrid threats while providing actionable insights for international security institutions navigating algorithmically amplified information warfare. The proposed computational infrastructure will enable processing of 2.5 billion text and image samples over 18 months, supporting both retrospective analysis and near-real-time monitoring capabilities.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_title: International Relations and National Security Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in international relations and national security studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance psychology teacher education by developing and validating computational models to simulate student learning processes in secondary-level psychology classrooms. A critical challenge in training future psychology educators is the limited availability of scalable, data-driven methods to predict how pedagogical strategies interact with individual differences in student cognition and motivation. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build agent-based models (ABMs) that emulate classroom dynamics under varied instructional conditions. These models will integrate empirical datasets from psychology education research, including student performance metrics, self-reported engagement, and demographic variables, to parameterize virtual student agents with psychologically plausible learning behaviors. Simulations will test hypotheses about how interventions such as active learning modules, personalized feedback systems, or metacognitive scaffolding affect aggregate classroom outcomes. Additionally, machine learning pipelines will analyze multi-terabyte teaching practicum video datasets to identify nonverbal behavioral signatures of effective instructional practices. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of complex temporal data and Monte Carlo sampling across parameter spaces to ensure model robustness. Outcomes will include (1) a validated simulation framework for optimizing evidence-based teacher training protocols and (2) predictive analytics tools to help novice instructors anticipate student needs. By quantifying relationships between teaching methods and learning outcomes at scale, this work aims to transform how psychology educators are prepared to address diverse classrooms. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive simulations and real-time analysis of high-dimensional educational data, which exceed the capabilities of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general psychology at the secondary school level.

abstract: The increasing complexity of autonomous systems in mechatronics and robotics demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in real-time control, dynamic simulation, and multi-objective optimization. Current computational resources often limit the fidelity and scalability of simulations for robotic systems operating in dynamic environments, particularly when integrating sensor fusion, machine learning, and physics-based modeling. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, parallelized simulations and optimizations for autonomous robotic systems, focusing on applications such as collaborative robotic swarms, adaptive manufacturing processes, and autonomous vehicle navigation. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in modeling nonlinear interactions between mechanical, electrical, and software subsystems under real-world constraints, including latency, uncertainty, and energy efficiency. The proposed computational approach leverages distributed computing frameworks to execute high-fidelity simulations of electro-mechanical systems using multi-body dynamics software (e.g., ROS, Gazebo) coupled with AI-driven control algorithms. Finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics will be employed to optimize sensor placements and energy consumption in robotic platforms, while reinforcement learning pipelines will be parallelized to accelerate training of adaptive controllers. The HPC environment will also facilitate Monte Carlo studies to evaluate system robustness across stochastic operating conditions. Expected outcomes include the development of scalable control architectures for heterogeneous robotic teams, validated optimization frameworks for energy-aware automation, and open-source tools for real-time simulation of cyber-physical systems. This work will directly advance the design of resilient autonomous systems for industrial and environmental applications, reducing reliance on costly physical prototyping. By integrating HPC capabilities into the program’s research infrastructure, the project will also enhance interdisciplinary training opportunities in computational robotics and smart manufacturing, bridging gaps between theoretical models and deployable technological solutions.
cip_title: Mechatronics, Robotics, and Automation Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in the support of engineers to the design, development, and operational evaluation of autonomous, computer-controlled, electro-mechanical systems. Includes instruction in computer and software engineering, control engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and robotics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision agriculture through the development of large-scale predictive models for crop stress resilience. Agricultural systems face mounting challenges from climate variability, pathogen evolution, and soil degradation, necessitating data-driven tools to optimize crop management. Current approaches to modeling plant-environment interactions are limited by the computational complexity of integrating heterogeneous datasets—including genomic, phenomic, and geospatial data—at biologically relevant scales. We propose a computational framework to analyze terabyte-scale agricultural datasets using machine learning and agent-based modeling. The first phase focuses on training deep neural networks to predict drought and disease susceptibility across diverse crop genotypes, utilizing genomic sequences and historical field trial data. The second phase employs distributed-memory simulations to model spatiotemporal pest dispersal dynamics under varying climate scenarios, incorporating high-resolution satellite imagery and soil sensor data. These computational workflows demand parallel processing capabilities, extensive memory allocation, and GPU acceleration to handle iterative parameter optimization and large-scale spatial analyses. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for identifying stress-resistant crop varieties and region-specific mitigation strategies. By enabling rapid analysis of complex agricultural systems, this research will directly support extension services in disseminating adaptive practices to farming communities. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current bottlenecks in dataset integration and model scalability, thereby accelerating innovation in agricultural public services. Results will be disseminated through cooperative extension networks and integrated into decision-support platforms for stakeholders, enhancing food security and sustainable production systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general agricultural sciences and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical laboratory testing generates vast, heterogeneous datasets spanning hematology, microbiology, immunology, and clinical chemistry, yet integrating these multimodal results to predict patient-specific outcomes remains a critical challenge. Current laboratory information systems (LIS) prioritize data storage and workflow management over advanced analytics, limiting the ability to identify subtle, cross-disciplinary patterns indicative of emerging pathologies or treatment responses. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to unify disparate laboratory data streams—including time-series chemistry results, cellular morphology images, microbial culture data, and immunological markers—into predictive models for early detection of sepsis in hospitalized patients. Using graph neural networks (GNNs) to map temporal and relational dependencies between laboratory parameters, combined with convolutional networks for automated analysis of peripheral blood smear images, the system will identify pre-symptomatic sepsis signatures obscured across multiple testing domains. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated training on retrospective datasets (n > 50,000 patient episodes) from partner hospital laboratories, followed by real-time inference integration within existing LIS architectures. Validation will focus on model interpretability for clinical laboratory technicians, emphasizing actionable alert thresholds and uncertainty quantification aligned with diagnostic operational standards. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC resources can transform routine laboratory data into proactive clinical decision-support tools while maintaining regulatory compliance. This interdisciplinary approach bridges diagnostic laboratory science with computational pathology, advancing precision diagnostics without requiring novel instrumentation—a critical innovation for resource-constrained healthcare settings. Anticipated outcomes include a 15-20% improvement in sepsis prediction sensitivity over current electronic health record-based systems, directly impacting morbidity and antimicrobial stewardship.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists/medical technologists, to perform routine medical laboratory procedures and tests and to apply preset strategies to record and analyze data. Includes instruction in general laboratory procedures and skills; laboratory mathematics; medical computer applications; interpersonal and communications skills; and the basic principles of hematology, medical microbiology, immunohematology, immunology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis.

abstract: The rapid evolution of dynamic web ecosystems demands adaptive frameworks to optimize resource allocation for content delivery, particularly as user expectations for real-time interactivity and personalized multimedia experiences intensify. Traditional server management strategies often rely on static heuristics or reactive scaling, which struggle to balance computational efficiency with the nonlinear, context-dependent behaviors of modern web traffic. This project proposes a novel approach to predictive resource allocation by integrating fine-grained user interaction analytics, semantic content complexity metrics, and adaptive machine learning models. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will develop a simulation environment that models multi-layered web architectures under variable demand patterns, incorporating temporal, geographic, and device-specific usage data from heterogeneous sources. The computational methodology combines graph neural networks to capture dependency structures in content delivery pipelines with reinforcement learning agents trained to optimize server configuration parameters in response to simulated stress scenarios. Key innovations include the development of a hybrid scoring system that quantifies both technical performance metrics (e.g., latency, throughput) and user-centric quality indicators (e.g., engagement decay rates, accessibility compliance) across dynamically generated content types. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for proactive resource budgeting in web management systems, validated against real-world traffic datasets spanning educational, e-commerce, and collaborative web applications. By enabling context-aware allocation strategies that anticipate usage spikes while minimizing energy consumption and infrastructure costs, this research aims to establish new paradigms for sustainable web operations in data-intensive environments. The requested computing resources will facilitate large-scale parallelism for training multi-objective optimization models and simulating edge-case failure modes across distributed server topologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and maintain web servers and the hosted web pages at one or a group of web sites, and to function as designated webmasters. Includes instruction in computer systems and networks, server installation and maintenance, web page design and editing, information resources management, web policy and procedures, Internet applications of information systems security, user interfacing and usability research, and relevant management and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address a foundational challenge in moral philosophy: the dynamic resolution of ethical conflicts in multi-agent systems under conditions of uncertainty and incomplete information. Traditional philosophical methods, which rely on analytical reasoning and thought experiments, struggle to model the emergent complexities of real-world ethical decision-making involving diverse actors, competing value frameworks, and evolving sociotechnical contexts. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational approach that combines agent-based modeling (ABM), game-theoretic simulations, and machine learning to systematically analyze how deontological, utilitarian, and virtue ethics frameworks interact in large-scale decision environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating populations of 10,000+ autonomous agents with heterogeneous ethical priorities, processing iterative decision trees across parametrized scenarios, and training neural networks to identify patterns in cross-framework moral tradeoffs. The simulations will incorporate formal logic systems to represent axiomatic ethical principles while using evolutionary algorithms to model adaptive reasoning processes.
