cip_definition: A program that focuses on the symbolic inference, representation, and simulation by computers and software of human learning and reasoning processes and capabilities, and the computer modeling of human motor control and motion. Includes instruction in computing theory, cybernetics, human factors, natural language processing, and applicable aspects of engineering, technology, and specific end-use applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling and personalized intervention strategies in hospice and palliative care, where patient outcomes are shaped by multifaceted physical, psychosocial, and ethical variables. Current approaches to prognosis and care planning often rely on fragmented data and static models, limiting their ability to account for dynamic interactions between symptoms, treatment responses, and patient/family preferences. To address this gap, we propose developing an integrative computational framework that synthesizes electronic health records (EHRs), longitudinal symptom assessments, caregiver-reported data, and genomic markers to model trajectories of advanced illness. Machine learning methods, including ensemble classifiers and recurrent neural networks, will be applied to identify patterns in symptom clusters, treatment efficacy, and quality-of-life metrics. A key innovation involves simulating patient-specific decision pathways using agent-based modeling to evaluate how psychosocial interventions (e.g., spiritual counseling, family support protocols) interact with biomedical treatments under diverse ethical scenarios. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (spanning >50,000 patient histories), training multi-modal deep learning architectures, and running large-scale sensitivity analyses to optimize care recommendations. Expected outcomes include validated prognostic tools for 6- and 12-month survival probabilities, dynamic algorithms to prioritize patient-centered interventions, and a publicly accessible simulation platform for testing palliative care policies. By elucidating how computational integration of biopsychosocial data can reduce care disparities, this work aims to establish a paradigm for evidence-based hospice practice while addressing computational challenges unique to ethically sensitive healthcare domains. The project will directly support 3-5 graduate trainees in health data science, fostering interdisciplinary skills at the intersection of clinical palliative care and advanced analytics.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to work with patients in hospice and palliative care and focuses on the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social needs of patients and families affected by advanced illness. Includes instruction in aging, thanatology, pharmacology, complementary and integrative therapies, pathophysiology, and ethics.

abstract: The widespread use of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and environmental contaminants poses significant risks to animal health, yet predicting species-specific toxicological responses remains a critical challenge in veterinary medicine. Current experimental models struggle to account for interspecies variations in xenobiotic metabolism, tissue-specific pharmacokinetics, and complex exposure scenarios involving multiple chemical interactions. This project seeks to develop predictive computational toxicology frameworks through advanced machine learning and multiscale modeling, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose to integrate molecular dynamics simulations of drug-receptor interactions with physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models across six veterinary species (canine, feline, equine, bovine, avian, and rodent), incorporating genomic data on cytochrome P450 polymorphisms and membrane transporter expression. A parallelized computational workflow will evaluate 120+ veterinary-relevant compounds, including antimicrobials, antiparasitics, and common environmental toxicants like organophosphates and mycotoxins. Neural architecture search techniques will optimize deep learning models for predicting species-specific adverse outcome pathways using a curated database of 50,000+ historical toxicity records. The HPC environment is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of cross-species extrapolations, running millions of parameter combinations in Monte Carlo risk assessments, and processing high-dimensional toxicogenomics datasets. Expected outcomes include open-source models for precision dosing in veterinary pharmacology, predictive tools for chemical risk assessment in food animals, and mechanistic insights into neurotoxicant bioactivation pathways. This computational infrastructure will directly support veterinary toxicology research by enabling rapid evaluation of emerging contaminants, reducing reliance on animal testing through in silico toxicology approaches, and informing species-specific antidote development. The generated models and datasets will be disseminated through a cloud-based platform for veterinary researchers and regulatory toxicologists.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of specific environmental and food hazards affecting domestic and wild animals and the development and action of chemical antidotes and treatments. Includes instruction in small and large animal toxicology and pharmacology, neurotoxicology, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, neuropharmacology, xenobiotics, drug resistance, pesticides, toxicological pathology, genetic and molecular toxicology, environmental toxicology, drug and toxicant analysis and evaluation, and environmental radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize personalized care plans for diverse family units, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex, multi-generational health datasets. Family practice nurses face significant challenges in synthesizing dynamic health, behavioral, and socio-environmental data across family systems, particularly when managing chronic conditions with genetic, epigenetic, and lifestyle components. Current decision-support tools lack the computational capacity to model longitudinal family health trajectories while accounting for interdependencies between members. Our research will employ machine learning architectures, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to identify risk propagation patterns within family structures using electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and social determinants of health from regional health networks. Agent-based modeling will simulate intervention outcomes under varying care coordination scenarios. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to 1) the scale of multimodal data (projected 50+ TB across 15,000+ family clusters), 2) the combinatorial complexity of modeling bidirectional caregiver-patient relationships, and 3) the need for real-time parameter optimization in simulated care pathways. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive system for anticipating care coordination breakdowns, a ranked inventory of intervention priorities for multi-morbidity families, and genomic-environmental risk interaction maps specific to family nursing contexts. This work will directly inform the development of clinical decision protocols for family health preservation strategies while advancing computational nursing methodology. The requested resources will enable crucial benchmarking against traditional statistical approaches, ensuring translational relevance for nurse educators and policymakers working to reduce care fragmentation in family practice settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the diachronic evolution of syntactic structures across major Romance languages (French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese) through computational analysis of historical textual corpora. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how grammatical complexity and sentence-level patterns diverged from Vulgar Latin, shaped by sociolinguistic and geographic factors. Current methodologies rely on manual comparative analysis, limiting scalability and the ability to detect subtle, large-scale trends. To overcome these constraints, this study employs natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including dependency parsing and transformer-based models, to automatically annotate and analyze syntactic features in a multilingual corpus spanning the 9th to 19th centuries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing over 10 million tokens of digitized texts, training language-specific models, and running parallelized comparative simulations. The computational workflow integrates phylogenetic algorithms to model evolutionary pathways, enabling quantitative assessment of hypotheses regarding contact-induced change and internal structural drift. Expected outcomes include a detailed typological map of syntactic evolution, open-source tools for diachronic Romance linguistics, and a replicable framework for computational historical linguistics. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance empirical foundations in Romance language studies while demonstrating the transformative potential of large-scale computational methods in under-resourced linguistic domains.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Romance languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for optimizing large-scale, stochastic industrial systems, with applications to supply chain resilience and production scheduling under uncertainty. Industrial systems increasingly face disruptions from geopolitical, environmental, and market volatility, necessitating real-time adaptive decision-making. However, existing optimization frameworks struggle with combinatorial complexity when modeling multi-echelon networks or high-dimensional uncertainty spaces, limiting their practical utility. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational architecture integrating distributed stochastic optimization, parallelized Monte Carlo simulation, and graph-based machine learning. The methodology leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to decompose problems across temporal and spatial dimensions while maintaining coordination through asynchronous consensus algorithms. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated scenario generation for non-stationary disruption risks and memory-efficient graph neural networks to predict cascading failures in interconnected production networks. Computational experiments will evaluate system performance under synthetic and real-world datasets spanning semiconductor manufacturing logistics and hospital resource allocation networks. The project requires HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale optimization models, parallelize millions of scenario evaluations, and train deep reinforcement learning agents on GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source algorithmic frameworks for stochastic industrial system optimization, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational scalability against commercial solvers, and (3) case studies demonstrating 15-30% improvements in recovery time and resource utilization under disruption scenarios. By enabling rapid analysis of complex trade-offs between efficiency, cost, and risk, this work will provide foundational tools for next-generation resilient systems engineering. Results will be disseminated through the INFORMS Journal on Computing and collaborations with industry partners in advanced manufacturing and healthcare operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Includes instruction in applied mathematics, physical sciences, the social sciences, engineering analysis, systems design, computer applications, and forecasting and evaluation methodology.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the emergent field of neuromarketing-driven adaptive pricing optimization, integrating consumer neuroscience, behavioral economics, and machine learning to address critical gaps in dynamic pricing models. Traditional price elasticity models fail to account for implicit neural responses to pricing stimuli, particularly in hybrid digital-physical retail environments where consumer decision-making involves complex cognitive-emotional interactions. The central challenge lies in processing multi-modal data streams – including functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) neuroimaging, eye-tracking metrics, and real-time transaction records – to model subconscious price perception mechanisms at population scale. The proposed computational approach leverages high-performance computing resources to train temporal graph neural networks that simulate the dynamic interplay between neural engagement patterns, contextual marketing stimuli, and purchase decisions across diverse consumer segments. By implementing distributed deep learning architectures optimized for heterogeneous data fusion, the project aims to overcome current limitations in processing latency and model scalability that constrain real-time price adaptation systems. Expected outcomes include a novel neural predictive framework capable of identifying non-linear price thresholds and optimal discount phasing strategies that maximize both conversion rates and customer lifetime value. This research will advance theoretical understanding of neurocognitive biases in price perception while delivering practical tools for ethical personalized pricing in omnichannel retail ecosystems. The computational demands of processing petabyte-scale consumer neurobehavioral datasets and training complex multi-agent reinforcement learning models necessitate specialized GPU-accelerated infrastructure to achieve the required throughput for commercial deployment scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to undertake and manage the process of developing consumer audiences and moving products from producers to consumers. Includes instruction in buyer behavior and dynamics, principle of marketing research, demand analysis, cost-volume and profit relationships, pricing theory, marketing campaign and strategic planning, market segments, advertising methods, sales operations and management, consumer relations, retailing, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the integration of real-time motion analytics and predictive biomechanical modeling to optimize personalized rehabilitation protocols for individuals recovering from musculoskeletal injuries. Current rehabilitation strategies often rely on generalized guidelines, which fail to account for patient-specific biomechanical variability, leading to suboptimal recovery trajectories and prolonged care. This project addresses the critical gap in adaptive, data-driven decision-making tools for allied health professionals specializing in physical rehabilitation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to develop a computational framework that processes multimodal data—including wearable sensor outputs, electromyography, and 3D motion capture—to simulate patient-specific musculoskeletal dynamics under varying therapeutic conditions. The core computational challenge lies in scaling finite element models and machine learning algorithms to handle high-resolution, time-series datasets while maintaining real-time feedback capabilities. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of tissue stress distributions, joint loading patterns, and neuromuscular activation states across diverse rehabilitation scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform that predicts optimal intervention parameters (e.g., exercise intensity, assistive device configurations) based on individualized risk-benefit analyses. This tool will undergo validation through retrospective clinical datasets and prospective pilot studies with collaborating rehabilitation clinics. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform post-injury care by merging computational biomechanics with clinical practice, reducing trial-and-error approaches in therapy design. Successful implementation could decrease rehabilitation durations by 15-20% in pilot populations while minimizing secondary injury risks, directly aligning with allied health priorities in precision intervention. This work establishes a template for integrating HPC-driven modeling into routine clinical decision-making within niche rehabilitation specializations.
cip_title: Allied Health Diagnostic, Intervention, and Treatment Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health diagnostic, intervention, and treatment professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for analyzing the complex linguistic structures of American Sign Language (ASL), which integrates visual, spatial, and gestural modalities distinct from spoken languages. Despite advances in natural language processing (NLP), existing tools are ill-suited for modeling ASL’s nonlinear morphology, classifier predicates, and spatial grammar, limiting progress in both linguistic research and technologies like automated translation systems. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to process and analyze large-scale ASL video corpora, combining computer vision techniques with linguistically informed machine learning models. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated 3D pose estimation and motion tracking to extract articulatory features (handshape, movement trajectories, facial expressions) from video data, followed by transformer-based architectures trained to map these features to syntactic and semantic annotations. A key innovation involves integrating linguistic constraints from ASL theoretical frameworks directly into model architectures to improve interpretability and accuracy. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of terabyte-scale video datasets and iterative training of deep neural networks, necessitating HPC resources for storage, distributed computing, and multi-node GPU support. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for ASL computational analysis, a richly annotated ASL linguistic corpus, and benchmarks for evaluating sign language processing systems. This work will advance understanding of ASL’s typological uniqueness while supporting downstream applications in education (e.g., AI-driven ASL tutoring tools) and accessibility (real-time translation services). By centering computational rigor and collaboration with Deaf researchers, the project aims to set new standards for ethically grounded, linguistically robust sign language technologies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on American Sign Language as a communication medium or language skill that is, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Allergic, asthmatic, and immunologic diseases exhibit complex heterogeneity in clinical presentation, treatment response, and underlying molecular mechanisms, posing challenges for personalized therapeutic strategies. Current approaches to biomarker discovery and treatment optimization rely on limited phenotypic or genomic datasets, often failing to capture the dynamic interplay between immune pathways, environmental triggers, and patient-specific factors. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-modal clinical data—including longitudinal electronic health records, single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomic profiles, and geospatial environmental exposures—from a cohort of 2,500 patients with severe asthma and comorbid immune dysregulation. Using a federated learning framework, we will train ensemble machine learning models to identify predictive signatures of treatment response to biologics (e.g., anti-IL5, anti-IgE monoclonal antibodies) while preserving data privacy across four academic medical centers. Concurrently, agent-based computational models will simulate immune cell interactions in airway microenvironments under varying cytokine milieus, parameterized by patient-derived data. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallelization of these simulations across 10,000+ parameter combinations to map mechanistic drivers of treatment resistance. Validation will involve in silico perturbation experiments and prospective comparison with clinical outcomes from a 12-month observational sub-study. This computational approach addresses critical gaps in translating complex biological data into actionable clinical insights, with particular emphasis on predicting corticosteroid resistance and optimizing biologic therapy selection. Successful completion will yield (1) a validated predictive algorithm for real-time treatment personalization, integrated into our institutional clinical decision support system, and (2) open-source computational models of type 2 inflammation pathways. The requested resources are essential for managing petabyte-scale datasets, executing computationally intensive simulations, and maintaining secure data federation across sites. Findings will advance precision medicine in allergy/immunology by bridging systems immunology with clinical decision-making, potentially reducing trial-and-error prescribing and associated healthcare costs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of skilled medical care to patients suffering from allergic, asthmatic, and immunologic diseases. Requires completion of a prior residency program in internal medicine or pediatrics.

abstract: Geothermal energy systems offer a sustainable pathway for decarbonizing energy production, yet optimizing their efficiency requires resolving complex, multiscale interactions between subsurface geology, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer. Current computational models often oversimplify fracture networks in geothermal reservoirs or neglect dynamic feedback between operational parameters and long-term reservoir performance, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing high-fidelity, coupled simulations of enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate multiphysics modeling approaches to capture thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes across temporal and spatial scales, with a focus on predicting fracture propagation, fluid flow churn, and heat extraction efficiency under varying operational scenarios. Computational workflows will leverage finite element methods (FEM) and discrete fracture network (DFN) models, validated against experimental data from lab-scale rock mechanics tests and field-scale EGS pilot sites. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs associated with uncertainty quantification, enabling probabilistic assessments of reservoir longevity and energy output. The HPC resources will support large-scale parallel simulations to resolve meter-scale reservoir features across kilometer-scale domains, a capability unfeasible with existing institutional computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include optimized well placement strategies, improved understanding of induced seismicity risks, and data-driven guidelines for sustaining reservoir permeability over decadal timescales. By advancing predictive modeling tools for EGS design, this work aims to reduce development risks and costs, directly supporting the scalability of geothermal energy as a baseload renewable resource. The resulting open-source simulation frameworks will be shared with the geothermal research community to accelerate collaborative innovation in subsurface energy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex sociocultural and logistical dynamics influencing the success of church planting initiatives in diverse urban contexts. While church planting is traditionally guided by theological frameworks, its practical implementation intersects with spatial demographics, migration patterns, community network formation, and intercultural communication—areas underexplored in computational humanities. The primary research problem centers on identifying scalable, data-driven models to optimize site selection, resource allocation, and contextual adaptation strategies for new congregations, particularly in hyper-diverse cities experiencing rapid demographic shifts. Using anonymized global census data, geospatial analytics, and ethnographic records from 15 transnational church planting networks, the project will apply agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate community engagement outcomes under varying theological, ethical, and operational parameters. Machine learning algorithms will further classify historical success/failure patterns across 500+ documented cases, correlating theological approaches with sociodemographic variables. Computational challenges include processing high-resolution geotemporal datasets, managing stochastic elements in ABM simulations, and integrating qualitative ethnographic data into quantitative predictive frameworks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support toolkit for religious organizations, prioritizing ethical considerations in algorithmic recommendations. The project advances interdisciplinary humanities scholarship by formalizing computational methodologies for missiological studies while addressing gaps in how emerging technologies engage with faith-based community development. Results will be disseminated through open-access repositories and a peer-reviewed paper analyzing the epistemic tensions between computational modeling and theological agency in mission contexts. This work underscores the role of HPC in bridging applied humanities research with complex real-world challenges in pluralistic societies.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to establish congregations of Christians in new locations. Includes instruction in models of church planting, church multiplication strategies, church leadership, evangelism, missiology, Christian ethics, and mission-oriented theology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of forensic evidence analysis, particularly in cases involving complex biological mixtures, degraded samples, or ambiguous crime scene patterns. A critical challenge in forensic science is the reliable interpretation of trace evidence—such as multi-contributor DNA profiles, bloodstain patterns in dynamic environments, or chemically altered materials—where traditional analytical methods often struggle to resolve uncertainties or integrate multi-modal datasets. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement probabilistic modeling, machine learning, and large-scale simulations tailored to forensic applications. Key computational tasks include the development of Bayesian networks for DNA mixture deconvolution, agent-based simulations of blood spatter dynamics under variable environmental conditions, and deep learning models for automated comparison of toolmarks or fracture patterns. These methods require iterative parameter sampling, high-dimensional data integration, and validation against empirical datasets, all of which demand substantial parallel processing capabilities. By utilizing GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, we aim to reduce analysis times from weeks to hours while improving statistical confidence in evidence interpretation. The outcomes will directly support forensic practitioners in generating reproducible, court-admissible results, particularly in high-stakes cases involving terrorism, mass disasters, or cold case reinvestigations. Additionally, this work will establish open-source computational frameworks that adhere to forensic ethics standards, enabling transparent peer validation and reducing risks of algorithmic bias. The requested HPC resources will enable scaling to real-world forensic datasets, including 3D crime scene reconstructions and multi-omics forensic biomarkers, thereby bridging gaps between laboratory research and operational forensic workflows in homeland security contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the physical, biomedical, and social sciences to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence, human testimony and criminal suspects. Includes instruction in forensic medicine, forensic dentistry, anthropology, psychology, entomology, pathology, forensic laboratory technology and autopsy procedures, DNA and blood pattern analysis, crime scene analysis, crime scene photography, fingerprint technology, document analysis, witness and suspect examination procedures, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic research on Slovak dialectal variation and its historical evolution. Despite Slovakia’s rich linguistic diversity, comprehensive studies of regional dialects remain limited due to the complexity of analyzing large, unstructured datasets spanning centuries of textual and oral records. The primary research problem involves modeling phonetic, syntactic, and lexical shifts across dialects while accounting for sociocultural influences, a task requiring systematic analysis of digitized historical texts, modern speech corpora, and ethnographic records. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to automate the identification of dialect boundaries, trace linguistic change trajectories, and simulate contact-induced variations. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on annotated corpora of Slovak dialects, employing graph-based algorithms to map dialect networks, and running phylogenetic analyses to reconstruct proto-forms. HPC resources are critical for handling the scale of data (20+ TB of text and audio) and the computational intensity of deep learning workflows, which involve parallelized training of multilingual models and large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible digital atlas of Slovak dialects with dynamic visualization tools, (2) novel NLP pipelines optimized for low-resource Slavic languages, and (3) quantitative insights into how migration and language policy shaped regional linguistic identities. This work will directly support philological research, language preservation initiatives, and pedagogical tools for Slovak studies while establishing scalable methodologies for minority language analysis. By bridging computational linguistics with traditional dialectology, the project aims to redefine scholarly approaches to Slavic language heritage in the digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Slovak language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of scalable, evidence-driven analysis of student writing development in English/Language Arts (ELA) teacher education. While ELA instructors routinely assess student writing to tailor pedagogical strategies, manual evaluation of large, longitudinal writing datasets remains labor-intensive and limits opportunities to identify nuanced patterns in language acquisition, rhetorical development, or grammar mastery. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that analyze writing samples from diverse K-12 classrooms, enabling data-driven insights for teacher training programs. The research will utilize natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based architectures, to automate syntactic, semantic, and discourse-level analyses of student writing corpora. These models will process multi-year datasets spanning narrative, expository, and argumentative genres, tracking features such as lexical diversity, coherence, and grammatical complexity across developmental stages. Computational outputs will be triangulated with human-coded assessments by experienced ELA educators to validate pedagogical relevance. The project will also simulate classroom scenarios through agent-based modeling to test how varying instructional approaches—informed by computational findings—affect projected student outcomes. By integrating HPC capabilities, this work aims to (1) identify previously undetected correlations between instructional strategies and writing proficiency growth, (2) generate actionable frameworks for training teachers in data-informed writing pedagogy, and (3) prototype open-source tools that help educators visualize developmental trajectories in student writing. Outcomes will directly inform ELA teacher education curricula by grounding instructional methods in large-scale empirical analysis while maintaining humanistic engagement with language arts. This interdisciplinary approach advances the integration of computational analytics in teacher preparation, offering scalable solutions to enhance writing instruction without compromising the interpretive rigor central to ELA disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach English grammar, composition and literature programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of a computational framework for simulating and optimizing multisensory urban environments, with a focus on understudied auditory and haptic interactions in public spaces. While environmental design traditionally prioritizes visual and spatial factors, emerging evidence suggests that non-visual sensory inputs—such as soundscapes, vibrational feedback, and microclimatic textures—profoundly influence human well-being, social cohesion, and place identity. Current tools lack the capacity to model these dynamic, interdependent phenomena at neighborhood scales, particularly in real-world conditions with transient populations and variable environmental parameters. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating a GPU-accelerated simulation platform that integrates agent-based behavioral modeling, finite element analysis for acoustic propagation, and machine learning-driven sensory preference prediction. Computational workflows will process LiDAR-derived 3D urban morphology data, anonymized pedestrian movement patterns, and empirical sensory perception datasets to iteratively test design interventions. Key challenges include resolving time-domain wave equations across heterogeneous materials at city-block scales and coupling these physical simulations with stochastic models of human-environment interaction. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for multisensory design validation, predictive metrics for auditory-haptic comfort in public spaces, and evidence-based guidelines for mitigating sensory inequities in urban planning. By enabling previously intractable analyses of how non-visual sensory layers shape human experiences, this work aims to establish computational environmental design as a distinct interdisciplinary domain, advancing both methodological innovation and equitable placemaking practices. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive simulations across parameterized scenarios, reducing wall-clock time for iterative design testing from weeks to days.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental design, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives in Ukrainian literary and media sources from the late 20th century to the present. Despite rich archival resources, large-scale computational analysis of these texts remains underexplored, limiting insights into how collective identity and cultural memory have been shaped during periods of socio-political transformation. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, this study will apply natural language processing techniques—including multilingual transformer models, dynamic topic modeling, and semantic network analysis—to analyze a corpus of over 500,000 digitized documents, spanning novels, periodicals, and community-authored texts. The computational approach addresses challenges in processing historical Ukrainian language variants, code-switching with Russian, and regionally specific dialects, requiring distributed training of custom language models and GPU-accelerated inference. Expected outcomes include the identification of thematic shifts in cultural discourse following key events such as independence (1991) and the Euromaidan protests (2013–2014), as well as spatial-temporal patterns in regional narrative development. The project will produce an open-access annotated corpus and computational workflows tailored to Ukrainian linguistic contexts, enhancing both digital humanities infrastructure and scholarly understanding of cultural resilience in post-colonial societies. By bridging area studies with advanced computational methods, this research aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing cultural production in multilingual, historically contested regions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Ukraine and its inhabitants, and related border regions, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the socio-political and economic networks of the Abbasid Caliphate (8th–10th centuries CE) through large-scale integration of fragmented textual, archaeological, and climatological data. The Abbasid era witnessed transformative shifts in trade, governance, and cultural exchange across the Near East and North Africa, yet existing studies remain constrained by the limited synthesis of dispersed sources and the computational challenges of modeling complex, multi-regional systems. Our research addresses this gap by developing a geospatial-temporal database integrating Arabic chronicles, Geniza documents, archaeological site reports, and paleoclimate proxies. Using natural language processing (NLP), we will extract and disambiguate references to settlements, trade goods, and administrative actors from heterogeneous texts, while agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate interactions between environmental stressors, economic flows, and institutional responses. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual OCR outputs, training transformer-based models for entity recognition in classical Arabic sources, and running parallelized ABM iterations to explore counterfactual scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas of Abbasid resource networks, quantitative assessments of climate-induced disruptions to agrarian economies, and visualizations of administrative decentralization patterns preceding regional fragmentation. This work will provide historians with a scalable framework to test hypotheses about state resilience and cross-cultural connectivity, while advancing computational methods applicable to under-resourced historical languages. By clarifying how environmental, economic, and political dynamics intersected in a pivotal era, the project aims to reshape scholarly debates on premodern state formation and the long-term impacts of resource allocation in arid-zone empires.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize AI-driven models for enhancing decision-support systems in executive assistance, a specialized niche within Business that intersects computational linguistics, workflow automation, and behavioral analytics. The increasing complexity of executive support tasks—such as dynamic scheduling, cross-departmental communication triage, and real-time prioritization of stakeholder requests—has outpaced traditional productivity tools. Current solutions lack adaptive learning capabilities to handle unstructured data (e.g., email semantics, meeting context) or model the cascading impacts of scheduling perturbations in large organizations. This project addresses these gaps by constructing a framework that integrates natural language processing (NLP) to interpret executive communication patterns, reinforcement learning to optimize calendar management, and agent-based modeling to simulate workflow interdependencies. Computational challenges include training transformer-based models on proprietary corporate communication datasets (≥10 TB), running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to stress-test scheduling scenarios, and deploying graph neural networks to map decision hierarchies within organizational structures. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of ensemble models combining supervised and unsupervised learning approaches, critical for handling the stochastic nature of executive workflows. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool for identifying high-priority tasks from multimodal inputs (voice, text, calendar metadata), (2) a risk-aware rescheduling algorithm that minimizes operational disruption, and (3) quantifiable metrics for evaluating executive assistant effectiveness in complex environments. By bridging computational scalability challenges with human-centric workflow design, this research aims to establish new standards for data-driven executive support systems while contributing methodological innovations at the intersection of business operations and adaptive machine learning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and/or personal secretaries for business executives and top management. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, public relations, scheduling and travel management, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, conference and meeting recording, report preparation, office equipment and procedures, office supervisory skills, and professional standards and legal requirements.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural and linguistic identities across the Balkan Peninsula from the late medieval period to the early 20th century. The research addresses a critical gap in interdisciplinary scholarship: the lack of systematic, large-scale computational analysis of vernacular texts, oral histories, and material culture artifacts that reflect the region’s pluralistic heritage. By integrating digitized manuscripts, ethnographic recordings, and archival records from diverse Balkan communities, the study aims to trace patterns of cultural hybridity, language contact, and identity negotiation in contexts shaped by shifting political and religious boundaries. The computational approach employs natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical South Slavic dialects and non-Slavic languages (e.g., Albanian, Vlach), alongside network analysis to map cross-regional transmission of narratives and symbols. A key innovation involves training custom transformer models to detect semantic shifts in religious and ethnic terminology within Ottoman tax registers, liturgical texts, and folkloric corpora. Image processing workflows will also be applied to analyze stylistic variations in ecclesiastical art and domestic material culture, correlating visual motifs with textual evidence of communal self-representation. The scale of data—over 10 million text tokens and 50,000 high-resolution artifact images—necessitates parallelized computing for dimensionality reduction, temporal-spatial modeling, and interactive visualization of results. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas of Balkan cultural interfaces, methodological frameworks for computationally tracing identity formation in multi-ethnic regions, and new datasets challenging nationalist historiographies that dominate the field. By enabling granular analysis of understudied vernacular sources, this project will advance transdisciplinary dialogue in Balkan Studies while demonstrating how HPC can reshape research on cultural memory in contested borderlands.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the Balkan Peninsula and associated island groups and borderlands, Southern Slavic and non-Slavic, during the medieval, Ottoman, and modern periods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize adaptive workplace design in hybrid work environments through high-fidelity simulations of spatial utilization, occupant behavior, and environmental feedback loops. As organizations increasingly adopt flexible work models, facility managers face complex challenges in balancing real estate efficiency, employee well-being, and operational costs. Traditional space planning tools lack the capacity to model dynamic interactions between workplace configurations, occupancy patterns, and organizational outcomes at scale. Our research addresses this gap by integrating agent-based modeling, graph neural networks, and real-time sensor data streams to simulate how physical and digital infrastructure co-evolve with workforce dynamics. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing resources to process multimodal datasets spanning building information models (BIM), IoT sensor networks, and human mobility tracking across 12 prototype sites. Key innovations include a reinforcement learning system that predicts optimal space reconfiguration thresholds and a generative design module that proposes layout adaptations in response to changing collaboration patterns. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform capable of recommending context-aware facility adjustments with quantified impacts on productivity metrics, energy consumption, and space utilization rates. By advancing computational methods for adaptive workplace planning, this project aims to establish new benchmarks for data-driven facility management in post-pandemic organizational ecosystems. The resource allocation will enable large-scale parallel processing of spatial-temporal datasets and training of multi-objective optimization models that exceed the capabilities of current commercial workplace analytics tools.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on strategic workplace and facility planning and that prepares individuals to function as facility and event managers and workplace consultants. Includes instruction in the principles of aesthetic and functional design, environmental psychology and organizational behavior, real estate planning, principles of occupational health and safety, event planning and management, operations management, and applicable regulatory and policy issues.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the complex biomechanical and biochemical interactions underlying periodontal disease progression, with a focus on optimizing personalized treatment strategies. Despite advances in dental diagnostics, the multifactorial etiology of periodontitis—involving host-microbial interactions, inflammatory cascades, and biomechanical stress—remains inadequately characterized. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to model these dynamic, multiscale processes efficiently. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, finite element analysis, and machine learning. Agent-based models will simulate microbial community dynamics and host immune responses at the cellular level, while finite element models will map mechanical stress distributions in periodontal tissues under varying occlusal loads. Machine learning algorithms, trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, proteomic, and clinical data), will identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response. The computational pipeline will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 500 patients with stage III/IV periodontitis. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to achieve real-time analysis of tissue-level biomechanics and microbial ecology interactions, which is infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into synergistic effects of microbial dysbiosis and biomechanical stress on periodontal breakdown, (2) predictive models for individualized risk stratification, and (3) in silico optimization of occlusal adjustment protocols to mitigate inflammation. This work will establish a novel computational platform for accelerating translational research in periodontology, with potential applications to implantology and oral rehabilitation. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project's computational demands, including processing 40+ TB of multimodal data and executing >10,000 concurrent simulations to capture biological variability.
cip_title: Dental Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dental services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Parasitic infections remain a critical global health challenge, with complex host-parasite interactions driving pathogenicity and treatment resistance. This project seeks to address the urgent need for advanced computational models to unravel molecular mechanisms underlying parasite evasion of host immune responses, with a focus on *Schistosoma mansoni* and *Leishmania donovani*. Current experimental approaches struggle to capture dynamic, multi-scale interactions between parasitic virulence factors and host immunological pathways, particularly in resource-limited settings where these infections are endemic. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop spatially resolved, multi-agent models simulating host-parasite interfaces at cellular and molecular scales. These models will integrate structural data of parasite-derived immunomodulatory proteins (e.g., tegumental antigens in schistosomes, lipophosphoglycans in *Leishmania*) with real-time immune cell signaling dynamics. Molecular dynamics simulations will explore conformational changes in key parasite proteins during host cell membrane interactions, while lattice-based Monte Carlo methods will model population-level immune response patterns across tissue microenvironments. The computational framework will be validated against experimental datasets from collaborator labs, including proteomic profiles of infected host cells and cytokine activation kinetics. Expected outcomes include identification of conserved parasite strategies for immune evasion, prediction of high-value targets for disruption via small-molecule inhibitors, and generation of testable hypotheses about synergistic therapeutic approaches. By elucidating spatiotemporal features of parasitical adaptation, this work will directly inform development of novel chemotherapeutics and vaccine candidates, addressing critical gaps in neglected tropical disease control. The requested HPC allocation will enable simulations spanning biologically relevant timescales (microseconds to hours) and spatial resolutions (Ångström to micrometer), which are computationally intractable on local cluster resources. This project bridges parasitology, immunology, and computational biology while remaining firmly grounded in microbiological mechanisms, avoiding overlap with excluded fields such as bioinformatics or genomics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biological organisms living in ecologically exploitative and competitive relationships with host organisms, and the role of parasites in causing injury, disease, and environmental damage. Includes instruction in vector biology, immunoparasitology, medical parasitology, molecular biology of parasitical associations, veterinary and comparative parasitology, chemotherapeutics, and ecological and systematic parasitology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize grooming protocols for domestic animals by modeling the biomechanical and physiological interactions between grooming tools, animal anatomy, and coat characteristics. Current grooming practices rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for individual variations in species, breed-specific skin elasticity, fur density, or stress responses. The lack of data-driven, personalized protocols can lead to suboptimal outcomes, including skin irritation, incomplete coat maintenance, or undue animal stress. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate grooming processes across a diverse array of biological and tool-based parameters. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model tool-skin interactions under varying pressure, motion, and temperature conditions, while agent-based simulations will predict stress responses in animals based on physiological metrics such as heart rate variability and thermal regulation. Machine learning algorithms will integrate empirical data from veterinary studies, groomer-reported outcomes, and sensor-derived biometrics (collected via wearable devices during grooming sessions) to generate adaptive, breed-specific grooming recommendations. The computational pipeline will also evaluate the efficacy of novel grooming tool designs through virtual prototyping, reducing reliance on iterative physical testing. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of simulated grooming scenarios, predictive models for stress-minimized workflows, and evidence-based guidelines for tool selection and maintenance. By bridging computational biomechanics, ethology, and cosmetology, this work aims to advance animal welfare standards while supporting innovation in a historically practice-driven industry. The scale of multi-parametric simulations and real-time data assimilation necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve the resolution required for actionable insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of decentralized, AI-mediated labor negotiation systems in gig economy platforms—a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of labor relations, computational economics, and algorithmic decision-making. Traditional collective bargaining frameworks struggle to adapt to the fluid, real-time nature of gig work, where labor conditions and compensation are dynamically determined by opaque platform algorithms. The research problem centers on simulating how AI-driven negotiation agents, representing workers and platforms, could autonomously resolve conflicts over pay, task allocation, and benefit structures while balancing efficiency, equity, and regulatory compliance. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) combined with reinforcement learning techniques, the project will construct a computational testbed simulating millions of worker-platform interactions under varying economic conditions, labor laws, and algorithmic incentive structures. The HPC environment is essential for scaling simulations to capture network effects in platform labor markets, training negotiation agents through multi-objective optimization, and performing sensitivity analyses across diverse jurisdictional frameworks (e.g., differing minimum wage laws or collective bargaining rights). Key computational challenges include parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations of contract outcomes, optimizing neural architectures for multi-party negotiation strategies, and analyzing emergent patterns in labor market stability. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for evaluating algorithmic labor negotiation systems, quantitative insights into policy interventions that prevent exploitative equilibria, and novel metrics for assessing fairness in decentralized bargaining processes. This work will provide empirical foundations for regulators and platforms navigating the legal and operational complexities of AI-mediated labor relations, advancing both computational social science and practical strategies for equitable algorithmic management.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on employee-management interactions and the management of issues and disputes regarding working conditions and worker benefit packages, and that may prepare individuals to function as labor or personnel relations specialists. Includes instruction in labor history, policies and strategies of the labor movement, union organization, labor-management negotiation, labor law and contract interpretation, labor economics, welfare and benefit packages, grievance procedures, and labor policy studies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance strategies for heavy equipment by integrating sensor data analytics, physics-based simulations, and machine learning. Heavy equipment in sectors like construction, mining, and agriculture faces complex operational stresses, yet traditional maintenance practices remain reactive, leading to costly downtime and safety risks. The research problem centers on the lack of robust, real-time tools to predict component failures in heterogeneous environments, particularly for systems with interdependent mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical subsystems. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining multi-physics simulations of critical components (e.g., hydraulic pumps, drivetrains) with anomaly detection algorithms trained on historical telemetry data. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distributions in high-wear components under variable loads, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will assess fluid behavior in hydraulic systems. These simulations will generate synthetic failure datasets to augment sparse real-world data, enabling the training of ensemble machine learning models to predict residual component life. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across thousands of parameter combinations and iteratively refining predictive models. Expected outcomes include a digital twin framework for real-time equipment health monitoring and a decision-support tool recommending maintenance interventions based on probabilistic failure forecasts. The project will validate models using field data from collaborating industry partners, targeting a 15–30% reduction in unplanned downtime for benchmark equipment classes. By bridging gaps between empirical maintenance practices and computational engineering, this work aims to advance technician training programs with data-driven diagnostics protocols while providing a scalable template for predictive maintenance in heavy equipment applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the field maintenance and repair of heavy equipment, and in the general maintenance and overhaul of such equipment. Includes instruction in inspection, maintenance, and repair of tracks, wheels, brakes, operating controls, pneumatic and hydraulic systems, electrical circuitry, engines and in techniques of welding and brazing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for youth services programs, addressing systemic inefficiencies in delivering social services to children, adolescents, and families. Current approaches to distributing limited resources—such as funding, staff, and facilities—often rely on static models that fail to account for dynamic factors like fluctuating community needs, geographic disparities, and intersecting vulnerabilities (e.g., poverty, mental health, or legal challenges). The research problem centers on creating adaptive, data-driven decision-making tools to improve service accessibility and equity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate service delivery networks across diverse demographic and socioeconomic scenarios. The ABM framework will integrate real-world datasets, including regional child welfare statistics, program utilization rates, and longitudinal outcomes, to model interactions between service providers, clients, and policymakers. Machine learning techniques, such as clustering algorithms and reinforcement learning, will be applied to identify optimal resource distribution patterns under constraints. Computational workloads will focus on parallelized simulations to evaluate thousands of allocation scenarios, requiring significant memory and processing power to handle large-scale geographic and temporal data. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between funding priorities, predicts service gaps, and evaluates policy impacts. This work will directly inform administrative practices in public youth services by providing evidence-based strategies to reduce service delays, mitigate burnout among social workers, and improve outcomes for high-risk populations. By aligning computational social science with public administration, the project aims to advance ethical, equitable resource allocation frameworks that adapt to evolving community needs while adhering to professional standards in youth services.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and implement social services for children, youth, and families. Includes instruction in child development and psychology, adolescence, family studies, social work, social services administration, juvenile and family law, program and facilities planning, youth leadership, counseling, probation, casework, applicable procedures and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of computationally intensive workflows for optimizing 3-D modeling processes in industrial design and precision manufacturing applications. While 3-D computer-aided design (CAD) and additive manufacturing technologies have transformed prototyping and production, challenges persist in efficiently simulating multi-material interactions, resolving fine geometric details in large-scale assemblies, and predicting structural performance under dynamic loads. Current software tools struggle with these tasks due to memory limitations and insufficient processing power for iterative design optimization. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven topology optimization. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers to simulate thermal-mechanical stresses in metal-polymer composite 3-D printed components, while parallelized algorithms will enable voxel-based refinement of complex geometries derived from 3-D scan data. A key innovation involves developing hybrid meshing techniques to handle heterogeneous material distributions inherent in multi-nozzle printing systems. The HPC resources will facilitate parameter sweeps across material properties, layer resolutions, and support structure configurations, reducing physical trial cycles by 40-60% in industrial test cases. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for warpage minimization in high-tolerance applications and open-source tools for adaptive mesh generation optimized for additive manufacturing constraints. By enabling rapid virtual testing of functionally graded components, this research will directly benefit small-to-medium manufacturers adopting 3-D printing for customized production. The computational infrastructure will also support educational modules integrating distributed computing concepts into 3-D design curricula, strengthening workforce training in advanced manufacturing technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the use of three-dimensional (3-D) computer technology to create technical illustrations and models used in manufacturing, design, production, and construction. Includes instruction in 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), 3-D printing, 3-D model design and construction, and 3-D scanning.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize blockchain-based accounting ecosystems, a novel interdisciplinary niche integrating distributed ledger technologies, cryptographic verification, and real-time financial transparency frameworks. Traditional accounting systems struggle to scale efficiently in decentralized business environments, particularly when reconciling multi-stakeholder transactions with auditability and compliance requirements. The project addresses this gap by simulating hybrid blockchain architectures that balance computational efficiency, data integrity, and regulatory adherence in cross-organizational accounting workflows. Using agent-based modeling and cryptographic game theory, we will quantify trade-offs between consensus mechanisms (e.g., proof-of-work vs. proof-of-stake) and their impacts on transaction finality, energy consumption, and audit trail reliability. HPC resources are critical for running Monte Carlo simulations across millions of synthetic transactions while varying network parameters, node behaviors, and threat models. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for dynamically adjusting blockchain protocols based on real-time accounting demands, reducing computational overhead by 30–50% compared to static systems. The project further explores machine learning techniques to detect anomalous transaction patterns within encrypted ledger data, requiring GPU-accelerated training on terabyte-scale datasets. Results will advance the integration of adaptive blockchain systems into accounting practice, offering businesses scalable tools for maintaining audit readiness in decentralized finance environments. This work bridges computational complexity theory with applied accounting innovation, directly supporting the program’s mission to develop professionals capable of navigating emergent technologies at the accounting-business interface.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and business administration/management that prepares individuals to function as accountants and business managers.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in predictive modeling of occupational hazards by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate complex workplace safety scenarios. Current approaches to risk assessment in occupational safety and health often rely on static datasets or simplified analytical models, limiting their ability to anticipate emerging risks in dynamic environments such as construction sites, manufacturing facilities, or emergency response scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose the development of a multi-scale computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model real-time interactions between environmental factors, equipment, and human workers. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of airborne contaminant dispersion, structural failure mechanisms under stress, and ergonomic strain patterns across diverse populations. Additionally, ML algorithms will be trained on synthetic and historical injury datasets to identify latent risk factors and predict accident probabilities under varying operational conditions. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from sensor networks deployed in industrial settings. Expected outcomes include optimized safety protocols for mitigating exposure to chemical, physical, and biomechanical hazards, as well as an open-source toolkit for probabilistic risk assessment adaptable to small- and medium-sized enterprises. By providing unprecedented resolution in simulating high-consequence, low-probability events—such as equipment malfunctions coupled with human error—this research will directly enhance the evidence base for proactive safety interventions. The project aligns with the Occupational Safety and Health Technology program’s mission to bridge engineering principles and practical safety solutions, while advancing technical capacity in hazard modeling for workforce training and regulatory compliance applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining job-related health and safety standards. Includes instruction in safety engineering principles, inspection and monitoring procedures, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, applications to specific work environments, and report preparation.

abstract: Occupational medicine research requires the integration of complex, multidimensional datasets—including workplace environmental exposures, biometric monitoring, and longitudinal health outcomes—to identify risk factors and design interventions that protect worker health. Current analytical approaches struggle to model the dynamic interactions between occupational hazards, individual susceptibility, and health impacts at scale, particularly when incorporating high-resolution sensor data, genomic information, or spatially explicit workplace layouts. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through advanced computational methods. We propose a two-phase approach: first, developing machine learning models to predict acute and chronic health outcomes using linked datasets from occupational health registries, wearable devices, and environmental monitoring systems; second, implementing agent-based simulations to model pathogen transmission and chemical exposure dynamics in diverse workplace settings. The machine learning workflow will employ ensemble methods and deep neural networks to handle heterogeneous data types (e.g., time-series sensor inputs, unstructured clinical notes) while accounting for confounding variables such as shift work patterns. The simulation phase will leverage parallel computing to run thousands of parameterized scenarios, assessing how ventilation systems, workforce density, and safety protocols influence exposure risks. By utilizing GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and high-memory nodes for large-scale simulations, this work will overcome current computational bottlenecks in analyzing terabyte-scale occupational datasets. Expected outcomes include identifying modifiable risk factors for musculoskeletal disorders, optimizing workplace outbreak containment strategies, and generating evidence-based thresholds for chemical exposures. These results will directly inform the development of adaptive occupational health policies and personalized prevention programs, ultimately reducing work-related morbidity in high-risk industries. The project will also establish reproducible computational workflows for occupational medicine research, enabling future studies to scale analyses across broader worker populations and emerging hazards.
cip_definition: Research focused on the maintenance of the health of workers, the ability to perform work, the arrangements of work, and the physical and chemical environments of the workplace. Includes instruction in data collection and management and the administration and regulation of occupational medical services. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: Agricultural business and management faces increasing complexity due to the integration of multi-scale data—from field-level sensor inputs to global market trends—that drive operational and strategic decisions. Current analytical tools often lack the computational power to synthesize these heterogeneous datasets in real time, limiting the ability to optimize supply chains, forecast pricing volatility, or evaluate risk under climate variability. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model decision-making processes in agribusiness systems, with a focus on enhancing resilience and profitability. Leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML), we will simulate interactions between producers, distributors, and markets under dynamic environmental and economic conditions. The ABM component will integrate geospatial data, IoT-derived crop performance metrics, and historical market records to represent stakeholder behavior, while ML algorithms will predict short- and long-term outcomes of management strategies, such as crop diversification or contract pricing adjustments. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these simulations to regional and global contexts, enabling parallel processing of millions of agent interactions and high-resolution scenario testing. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision support tool that quantifies trade-offs between profitability, sustainability, and risk mitigation for agricultural enterprises. This work will advance computational methodologies in agricultural business by bridging gaps between precision agriculture data and macroeconomic modeling, providing stakeholders with actionable insights to navigate volatile markets and resource constraints. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for ML training and large-memory nodes for ABM ensemble runs, which are infeasible on local computing clusters. By enhancing computational capacity, this project aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven agricultural business optimization, contributing to both academic research and industry practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural business and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of sustainable wood-based materials and optimize pulp processing through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled modeling of complex lignocellulosic systems. The research addresses critical gaps in understanding the nanoscale interactions between wood polymers (cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin) during chemical pulping and composite material synthesis—processes that remain energy-intensive and empirically optimized. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve dynamic molecular-scale phenomena governing fiber separation, lignin redistribution, and interfacial bonding in engineered wood products. We propose multiscale computational workflows integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model: (1) solvent-lignin interactions during kraft pulping under varied temperature/pH conditions, (2) stress distribution in cellulose-reinforced biocomposites, and (3) process parameter optimization for reduced chemical consumption. The MD simulations will employ validated force fields (CHARMM36, GLYCAM06) to simulate polymer-solvent systems exceeding 1 million atoms, requiring GPU-accelerated computing for adequate sampling timescales. Concurrently, ML models trained on simulation outputs and experimental datasets will identify predictive relationships between processing conditions, fiber morphology, and composite mechanical properties. Expected outcomes include atomistic insights into delignification kinetics, validated predictive models for fiber strength retention, and processing guidelines to minimize carbon footprint in pulp production. By coupling HPC with targeted material characterization, this work will establish a computational framework to accelerate the design of circular bioeconomy-compliant wood technologies, directly supporting industrial transitions toward greener manufacturing protocols. Resource allocation is requested for 200,000 GPU-hours to handle the iterative sampling demands of free energy calculations and parametric studies across multiple length scales.
cip_title: Wood Science and Wood Products/ Pulp and Paper Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the analysis of the properties and behavior of wood and wood products and the development of processes for converting wood into paper and other products. Includes instruction in wood classification and testing, product development, manufacturing and processing technologies, and the design and development of related equipment and systems.
