This work directly advances the translation of computational bioengineering into clinical practice by enabling data-driven implant personalization, with potential applications in craniofacial reconstruction and orthopedic surgery. The requested HPC allocation will support large-scale parameter sweeps, parallelized ABM-FEA workflows, and ML training on heterogeneous datasets (imaging, genomic, and biomechanical), which are infeasible on local clusters due to memory and runtime constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of biomedical and health systems and products such as integrated biomedical systems, instrumentation, medical information systems, artificial organs and prostheses, and health management and care delivery systems.

abstract: Blood transfusion safety and efficacy depend on optimizing blood component storage, minimizing adverse reactions, and personalizing transfusion protocols. However, variability in donor biology, storage-induced degradation of cellular components, and complex immune interactions between donors and recipients present unresolved challenges. This project seeks to develop predictive models of red blood cell (RBC) and platelet storage stability, transfusion outcomes, and alloimmunization risks using multi-omics data integration and mechanistic simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets—including genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and clinical data from blood donors and recipients—and to simulate dynamic cellular changes during storage. Machine learning models will identify biomarkers predictive of component shelf life and adverse events, while agent-based simulations will map immune cell interactions driving platelet clearance or RBC alloimmunization. A parallelized computational pipeline will analyze donor-recipient HLA/KIR compatibility matrices to guide stratified blood product matching for high-risk patients. The project leverages existing clinical datasets from 15,000+ transfusions and prospectively collected multi-omics profiles from 2,000 blood donors. HPC infrastructure is required to manage the ∼450 TB of genomic and imaging data, run iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization, and execute large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of membrane degradation in stored RBCs. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for blood component quality, decision-support tools for inventory management, and a framework for precision transfusion matching. These results will directly inform blood bank operational guidelines, reduce transfusion-related complications, and extend the utility of scarce blood products. By integrating heterogeneous datasets at scale, this work advances translational goals in transfusion medicine while establishing computational methods adaptable to other cellular therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for the maintenance of an adequate blood supply, blood donor and patient-recipient safety, and appropriate blood utilization. Includes directing the preparation and safe use of specially prepared blood components, including red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and plasma constituents, and marrow or stem cells for transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of terrestrial ecosystem resilience to climate-driven disturbances by integrating high-resolution hydrological modeling, biogeochemical cycling, and satellite remote sensing data. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting how dynamic interactions between soil moisture regimes, vegetation productivity, and carbon-nutrient fluxes influence landscape-scale recovery from droughts and extreme precipitation events. Current models often treat these processes in isolation or at coarse spatial resolutions, limiting their utility for regional adaptation planning. We propose developing a novel computational framework that couples a parallelized hydrological model (HYDRUS-3D) with a biogeochemical reaction network solver (CLM-CN) at unprecedented 100-meter resolution across five major U.S. ecoregions. The integration of daily MODIS and Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, SMAP soil moisture products, and PRISM climate data will enable data assimilation at scales relevant to ecosystem management decisions. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve fine-scale heterogeneity in soil texture, topography, and land cover while simulating decadal timeseries under multiple climate scenarios (CMIP6). Each ensemble member will require 48 hours on 256 cores to complete the coupled surface-subsurface hydrology calculations, followed by iterative biogeochemical simulations using GPU-accelerated matrix solvers. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold behaviors in soil carbon storage following hydroclimatic extremes, (2) quantification of landscape connectivity impacts on nutrient transport, and (3) open-source tools for optimizing groundwater recharge interventions in agricultural watersheds. The 10TB of generated outputs will be synthesized into a public knowledge portal supporting USDA and USGS land stewardship initiatives. By elucidating cross-scale feedbacks between physical and biogeochemical processes, this work will provide actionable insights for maintaining critical zone services under increasing climate variability.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction of the Earth's oceanographic, atmospheric, and terrestrial systems. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic stressors are increasingly disrupting watershed dynamics, threatening biodiversity, water security, and ecosystem services. Current predictive models for watershed resilience often lack the spatial resolution and integration of cross-scale feedbacks between hydrologic, ecological, and socio-economic systems, limiting their utility for regional conservation planning. This project seeks to advance high-resolution, integrative modeling of watershed resilience under climate change scenarios to inform adaptive management strategies for natural resource conservation. The research employs a coupled modeling framework combining a process-based hydrologic model (SWAT+) with an agent-based land-use decision model, calibrated using regional climate projections, remote sensing data, and stakeholder-derived socio-economic parameters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to resolve fine-grained spatial interactions (1 km² resolution across 50,000 km² of critical watersheds), simulate decadal-scale hydrological-ecological feedbacks under multiple Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios, and perform Monte Carlo uncertainty analyses across 10,000+ parameter permutations. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized model runs and machine learning-based sensitivity analysis to identify thresholds of ecosystem collapse and prioritize intervention zones. Expected outcomes include (1) spatially explicit projections of water availability and habitat suitability for keystone species under 2050/2080 climate scenarios, (2) a decision-support toolkit quantifying trade-offs between conservation targets and human water use, and (3) open-source code for coupled socio-hydrological modeling adaptable to other regions. This work directly addresses the urgent need for computational tools that bridge biophysical and social dynamics in environmental management, providing actionable insights for agencies managing protected areas and water resources. The requested HPC allocation will enable the scaling of analyses currently constrained by single-node computational limits, reducing wall-clock time for ensemble simulations from months to days while improving statistical robustness. Project outputs will be disseminated through partnerships with regional conservation authorities and the U.S. Geological Survey to guide climate-resilient resource allocation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on environment-related issues using scientific, social scientific, or humanistic approaches or a combination. Includes instruction in the basic principles of ecology and environmental science and related subjects such as policy, politics, law, economics, social aspects, planning, pollution control, natural resources, and the interactions of human beings and nature.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cross-regional cultural narratives in East Asia, with a focus on the interplay between textual production, gender representation, and diasporic identity in premodern and early modern Chinese, Japanese, and Korean literary collections. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural transmission and adaptation across linguistic and geopolitical boundaries, using digitized corpora of classical texts, personal correspondences, and vernacular publications from the 12th to 19th centuries. Current methodologies in area studies lack the capacity to systematically process over 150,000 multilingual primary-source documents (spanning 8 TB of OCR-scanned manuscripts and annotated translations) while accounting for dialectal variations, non-standard orthographies, and intertextual references. The proposed computational approach integrates transformer-based language models fine-tuned on classical Sinographic texts, network analysis of recurring narrative motifs, and geospatial visualization of textual circulation routes. Custom pipelines will be developed to handle mixed-script materials (e.g., Hanja-Hangul hybrid texts, Man'yōgana annotations) and mitigate historical OCR errors through ensemble correction models. By parallelizing semantic role labeling and entity recognition tasks across GPU nodes, the project aims to reconstruct how gendered archetypes and diasporic experiences were reconfigured through transregional literary exchanges. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access knowledge graph linking 50,000+ textual entities with cultural provenance metadata, plus computational models adaptable to understudied vernacular collections. This work will provide the first large-scale quantitative framework for analyzing East Asia's interconnected literary heritage while advancing computational methods for non-Latin script historical documents in area studies. The requested HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific NLP models and processing heterogeneous textual datasets at scales unachievable through traditional close-reading approaches.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of East Asia, defined as including China, Korea, Japan, Mongolia, Taiwan, Tibet, related borderlands and island groups, and including the study of the East Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: The development of efficient catalytic processes is critical for sustainable chemical manufacturing, yet the molecular-level understanding of reaction mechanisms in heterogeneous systems remains a significant challenge. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic behavior of transition metal catalysts under industrial biofuel production conditions. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve atomic-scale interactions and transient intermediates, limiting the rational design of catalysts optimized for low-temperature operation. The research will employ multiscale computational models, integrating density functional theory (DFT) for electronic structure analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to track reaction pathways, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict structure-activity relationships. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of these tasks, including large-scale parallel calculations for high-throughput screening of bimetallic catalyst compositions and long-timescale MD simulations to capture rare catalytic events. Data from collaborative experimental studies on catalyst performance will validate the computational models. Expected outcomes include identifying catalyst formulations with improved activity and selectivity at reduced energy inputs, directly addressing industrial needs for decarbonized processes. The project will also generate an open-access database of catalytic properties, enabling broader innovation in chemical technology. By bridging molecular insights with industrial applicability, this work aims to advance sustainable manufacturing practices while training students in cutting-edge computational methodologies. The requested HPC allocation will support intensive simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, ensuring robust sampling of chemical space and statistically significant results. This research aligns with global priorities in energy efficiency and underscores the transformative role of computational science in chemical technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of chemical and biochemical research and industrial operations. Includes instruction in principles of chemistry and biochemistry, technical mathematics, computer applications, radiochemistry, industrial biochemistry, chemical instrumentation, physical chemistry, laboratory research methods, industrial processing methods and equipment, and test equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: The corrections system faces persistent challenges in balancing security, rehabilitation, and operational efficiency, yet data-driven strategies to optimize these priorities remain underdeveloped. This project proposes the creation of a computational framework to model inmate behavior dynamics, facility resource allocation, and the long-term impacts of rehabilitation programs. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including historical inmate records, real-time sensor data from correctional facilities, and psychosocial intervention outcomes—to simulate complex interactions within carceral environments. Agent-based modeling will capture individual and group behaviors, while network analysis will map communication patterns and risk factors for conflict. A machine learning layer will identify predictive markers of recidivism and program efficacy, enabling scenario testing for policy decisions. Key computational challenges include scaling simulations to reflect population-level dynamics across multi-facility systems, managing high-dimensional temporal data, and ensuring ethical AI practices to mitigate bias. The outcomes will yield actionable insights into optimal staffing ratios, crisis intervention protocols, and programmatic investments aligned with reduced reoffending rates. By bridging computational social science with corrections administration, this project aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in a traditionally under-resourced field, offering scalable tools to improve safety, rehabilitation outcomes, and systemic cost-effectiveness. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the iterative, resource-intensive nature of these models, which require parallel processing capabilities to explore vast parameter spaces and generate statistically robust recommendations for diverse correctional contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage institutional facilities and programs for housing and rehabilitating prisoners in the public and/or private sectors. Includes instruction in the principles and practice of correction, facilities planning and management, safety and security, social and health services, staff and inmate management, budgeting, communication skills, correctional psychology, and applications to specific types of correctional facilities approaches.

abstract: Marine transportation systems are critical to global trade and economic stability, yet they face increasing pressure to optimize operational efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and enhance navigational safety amid growing maritime traffic and climate variability. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to model and simulate vessel dynamics, route optimization, and environmental interactions in complex marine environments. A key research problem lies in the integration of real-time hydrodynamic, meteorological, and logistical data to predict vessel performance and optimize routing strategies under dynamic conditions. Existing methods often rely on simplified assumptions or static datasets, limiting their applicability to rapidly changing maritime scenarios. To overcome these limitations, this project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale, multi-physics simulations combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML)-driven predictive analytics, and geospatial optimization algorithms. These simulations will process high-resolution bathymetric, weather, and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data to generate adaptive routing recommendations, assess hydrodynamic stresses on vessel structures, and quantify emissions under varying operational parameters. The computational demands of this work—including parallelized CFD solvers, iterative ML model training, and Monte Carlo-based uncertainty analyses—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure capable of handling terabytes of input data and millions of core-hours. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for maritime operators to minimize fuel consumption, mitigate collision risks, and comply with emissions regulations, as well as new insights into the interplay between vessel design, operational practices, and environmental factors. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance the sustainability and resilience of marine transportation systems while providing a scalable computational methodology for future maritime research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in water transportation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to analyze the ethical implications of algorithmic bias in large-scale digital archival systems, a critical yet underexplored challenge in library and information science (LIS). As cultural heritage institutions increasingly rely on machine learning (ML) to process digitized collections, biases embedded in classification models—such as skewed representation of marginalized voices or mislabeling of historically contextual materials—risk perpetuating systemic inequities in access and discoverability. Current tools for auditing these systems lack the capacity to process heterogeneous data types (text, images, metadata) across distributed repositories, limiting proactive mitigation of harm. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal neural networks on curated datasets spanning digitized manuscripts, oral histories, and visual archives from underrepresented communities. The computational workflow will integrate transformer-based NLP models for textual analysis, convolutional networks for image recognition, and graph-based algorithms to map metadata relationships, enabling systemic identification of bias patterns across scales. By parallelizing model training and validation across diverse archival corpora, this approach will quantify disparities in classification accuracy and recommendation fairness while simulating the longitudinal impacts of biased algorithms on user engagement. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for ethical ML auditing in digital libraries, benchmark datasets annotated with bias indicators, and scalable protocols for equitable metadata generation. This research directly supports the LIS mission of democratizing access to knowledge by ensuring computational infrastructure aligns with principles of justice and inclusivity, offering a model for interdisciplinary collaboration between information professionals, ethicists, and AI researchers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the knowledge and skills required to develop, organize, store, retrieve, administer, and facilitate the use of local, remote, and networked collections of information in print, audiovisual, and electronic formats and that prepares individuals for professional service as librarians and information consultants.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of silicate mineral formation and stability under varying geochemical and tectonic conditions using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex physicochemical interactions at unprecedented scales. Silicates dominate Earth’s crust and mantle, yet their formation pathways, phase transitions, and long-term stability in dynamic systems remain poorly resolved, particularly in settings involving multi-component fluid-rock interactions, extreme pressures, or rapid tectonic forcing. Current experimental and analytical methods struggle to capture the coupled spatial and temporal scales governing these processes, necessitating computational approaches. We propose to develop and apply a suite of 3D reactive transport models integrating molecular-scale silicate-fluid interfacial reactions with continuum-scale geomechanical simulations. These models will leverage existing thermodynamic databases and machine learning-optimized force fields to simulate silicate crystallization, dissolution, and recrystallization across hydrothermal, metamorphic, and magmatic environments. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of systems spanning micrometers to kilometers, with time steps from nanoseconds to millennia, to resolve how micro-scale chemical processes propagate to macro-scale geological features. Key objectives include quantifying the role of stress gradients in silicate phase stability, predicting fluid-mediated mineral redistribution in fault zones, and identifying kinetic barriers to equilibrium in metamorphic reactions. Outcomes will provide mechanistic insights into silicate-driven geochemical cycles, ore formation processes, and rock rheology, with applications to natural hazard assessment and subsurface resource management. The computational framework developed here will be open-sourced to support broader community research on reactive transport in geological systems, fostering collaboration across geosciences and computational geochemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the silicates and other substances formed by chemical and physical geomorphological processes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the real-time decision-making algorithms of autonomous ground vehicles (AGVs) operating in complex urban environments. Current AGV systems face challenges in balancing computational efficiency with safety-critical responsiveness, particularly in scenarios involving unpredictable pedestrian behavior, mixed traffic flows, and adverse weather conditions. We propose to address these limitations through large-scale simulations of vehicle-pedestrian interaction models, multi-agent reinforcement learning for cooperative navigation, and probabilistic risk assessment under sensor uncertainty. The research will employ high-fidelity traffic simulations incorporating 3D LiDAR point cloud processing, camera vision transformer models, and dynamic route optimization algorithms. A key innovation involves parallelized training of machine learning models across diverse operational domains (e.g., construction zones, school areas, emergency vehicle corridors) while maintaining real-time performance constraints. The computational demands require access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep neural network training, distributed memory clusters for city-scale traffic simulations, and high-throughput storage systems for processing petabytes of sensor data from existing AGV fleets. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated framework for AGV decision latency reduction by 40-60% in edge cases, (2) open-source simulation tools for vehicle-pedestrian interaction modeling, and (3) quantitative safety benchmarks for autonomous systems operating in mixed-use transportation corridors. This work directly supports national priorities in intelligent transportation infrastructure while addressing critical gaps in AGV deployment scalability. The requested computing resources will enable parameter-space explorations that are computationally prohibitive on local clusters, particularly for ensemble uncertainty quantification across 10^4+ scenario variations and real-world validation against 15+ TB of operational telemetry data from industry partners.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle and equipment operation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of next-generation spacecraft thermal protection systems (TPS) for high-speed atmospheric entries, a critical challenge in planetary exploration and crewed spaceflight. Current TPS materials and configurations face extreme aerothermal loads during hypersonic deceleration, but existing predictive models lack the resolution to capture coupled thermochemical ablation, turbulent boundary layer transitions, and microscale material responses under real flight conditions. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining direct numerical simulation (DNS) of reactive hypersonic flows with finite element modeling of anisotropic carbon composite degradation. The approach leverages high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFS3D-HyCAP) and material response (CHAR) codes, coupled through a novel implicit boundary data transfer algorithm to resolve bidirectional fluid-structure interactions. Simulations will utilize adaptive mesh refinement to track ablation fronts and localized heating spikes while maintaining computational tractability. The research requires access to high-performance computing resources for three primary workloads: 1) petascale DNS of turbulent reacting boundary layers (10^8-10^9 grid points), 2) ensemble-based parameter optimization of TPS layup configurations using Monte Carlo methods, and 3) machine learning surrogate model training on multi-terabyte simulation datasets. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for TPS performance under Venusian and Martian entry profiles, identification of optimal porous material architectures for heat flux mitigation, and open-source release of optimized coupling libraries for the aerospace community. This work directly supports NASA’s Moon-to-Mars objectives by enabling lighter, more reliable thermal protection systems, with potential performance improvements of 15-20% in mass-specific heat rejection capacity compared to current Artemis-era designs.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any program in aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, or space engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Slavic linguistic evolution and dialectal variation. Slavic languages, characterized by complex morphological systems and historical diversification, present significant challenges in tracing diachronic developments and synchronic variation across regions. Traditional methods, limited by manual analysis and small datasets, struggle to address the scale and intricacy of these linguistic phenomena. This research aims to develop a corpus-driven computational framework to model phonological, morphological, and syntactic shifts in key Slavic languages—including Old Church Slavonic, Russian, and Ukrainian—over time, while mapping dialectal boundaries in contemporary usage. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) tools adapted for historical and non-standardized texts, combined with machine learning algorithms to detect patterns in language change. Large-scale parallel processing will enable the alignment and analysis of digitized historical manuscripts, regional speech corpora, and sociolinguistic metadata. Additionally, phylogenetic algorithms will reconstruct probabilistic models of language divergence, accounting for contact-induced changes and areal features. The computational demands of training transformer-based models on low-resource historical languages, coupled with the need to process terabytes of heterogeneous textual and audio data, necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Slavic linguistic variants, predictive models of language change, and visualizations of dialect continua across Eastern Europe. These resources will provide novel insights into the dynamics of Slavic language evolution, support comparative literary studies, and inform language preservation efforts for endangered dialects. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this project bridges gaps in Slavic linguistics and demonstrates the transformative potential of HPC in humanities research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Slavic languages of Central and Eastern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational models for simulating and optimizing complex printmaking processes. Traditional printmaking techniques, such as lithography, intaglio, and relief printing, rely on nuanced interactions between ink viscosity, substrate porosity, pressure application, and environmental conditions. These variables are challenging to isolate experimentally, leading to iterative physical trials that consume time, materials, and artistic labor. This project addresses the gap in predictive tools for printmakers by creating physics-based simulations of ink transfer dynamics, material deformation, and color layering under diverse technical configurations. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate non-Newtonian ink behavior across substrates, while finite element analysis (FEA) will map mechanical stresses during plate pressing. Machine learning frameworks will then iteratively refine these models using experimental data from collaborator print studios, correlating simulated outcomes with physical results. HPC resources are critical due to the high resolution required for microscale surface-texture modeling, the need for parallelized parameter sweeps across artistic variables (e.g., ink dilution, humidity), and the real-time rendering of multi-layered color interactions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset enabling artists to virtually test print configurations, predict material outcomes, and explore novel hybrid techniques (e.g., combining digital and analog processes). By reducing reliance on physical trial-and-error, this work aims to lower barriers to technical innovation in printmaking, support sustainable material practices, and expand creative possibilities for complex, large-scale artworks. The project bridges computational science and traditional art practice, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue while preserving the tactile heritage of printmaking through enhanced digital stewardship.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by rendering art concepts onto surfaces and transferring images, via ink or dyes, onto paper or fabric. Includes instruction in monochrome and color printing; tonality; chemistry; equipment set-up and maintenance; techniques such as serigraphy, lithography, intaglio, woodcut, block, stencil, relief, etching, and composite; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making in multi-site restaurant operations, integrating real-time data from supply chains, customer behavior, and staff logistics. The culinary management industry faces growing complexity due to fluctuating demand patterns, perishable inventory constraints, and labor scheduling challenges, yet existing operational models rely heavily on static heuristics ill-suited for rapid environmental changes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose an agent-based simulation environment that models restaurant networks as interacting systems of suppliers, kitchens, service staff, and customers. The platform will incorporate machine learning algorithms trained on historical sales data, weather patterns, and event calendars to predict demand surges, while constraint optimization modules will simultaneously address food safety protocols, labor laws, and waste reduction targets. By parallelizing scenario testing across thousands of parameter combinations—including menu engineering strategies, staff cross-training configurations, and just-in-time delivery schedules—the HPC infrastructure will identify robust operational policies adaptable to regional market variations. Expected outcomes include predictive models for ingredient yield optimization under seasonal variability, AI-driven staffing templates that balance service speed with employee retention metrics, and a decision-support system for catering event portfolio management. This work aims to establish computational gastronomy operations research as a distinct analytical discipline, providing evidence-based tools to reduce food costs by an estimated 12-18% in simulated environments while maintaining service quality standards. The resource-intensive nature of simultaneously modeling molecular-level food preparation processes and enterprise-level financial outcomes necessitates GPU-accelerated computing clusters capable of handling heterogeneous data streams at restaurant-industry scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage food and beverage preparation and service operations, restaurant facilities, and catering services.  Includes instruction in food/beverage industry operations, cost control, purchasing and storage, business administration, logistics, personnel management, culinary arts, restaurant and menu planning, executive chef functions, event planning and management, health and safety, insurance, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive maintenance and energy efficiency optimization in residential and commercial appliances, including refrigeration systems, laundry units, and cooking appliances. A critical challenge in appliance repair and installation is the lack of data-driven frameworks to anticipate mechanical failures or energy inefficiencies in aging or complex systems. Traditional diagnostics rely on static guidelines or reactive troubleshooting, which can lead to increased downtime, resource waste, and consumer costs. To address this gap, we propose developing physics-informed machine learning models that simulate appliance performance under diverse operational conditions, material stresses, and environmental factors. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution modeling in components like compressor valves or heating elements, coupled with time-series forecasting to predict wear patterns. High-resolution sensor data from field deployments (e.g., temperature, vibration, power draw) will train neural networks to correlate real-world usage patterns with failure risks. HPC resources are essential to parallelize simulations across thousands of appliance configurations and rapidly iterate multi-physics models that account for thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamics interactions. Expected outcomes include a predictive maintenance toolkit that enables technicians to prioritize repairs, reduce energy waste by up to 20% in malfunctioning units, and extend appliance lifespans. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular simulation templates tailored to common appliance architectures, fostering innovation in technician training programs and sustainable appliance design. By bridging computational modeling with applied repair technologies, this work aims to elevate technical standards in the field while supporting global energy conservation goals.
cip_title: Appliance Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, install, and service major gas, electric, and microwave consumer appliances such as stoves, refrigerators, dryers, water heaters, washers, dishwashers, and commercial units such as ice makers and coffee makers.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of linguistic evolution and dialectal diversity in Hindi and its related languages. Despite Hindi’s status as a major global language with over 600 million speakers, computational studies of its historical development, regional variations, and syntactic structures remain limited, particularly for non-standardized dialects and older textual forms. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable tools to process large corpora of Hindi texts—spanning classical literature, modern media, and oral narratives—while accounting for dialectal shifts, phonetic variability, and orthographic inconsistencies. Current methods, often constrained by single-threaded processing and memory limitations, struggle to handle the volume and complexity of such datasets. This project proposes a multi-stage computational approach: (1) developing parallelized NLP pipelines to preprocess and annotate diverse Hindi texts, including rare manuscripts and transcribed speech; (2) training transformer-based models to detect and classify dialectal features across temporal and geographic axes; and (3) implementing distributed simulations to model language change dynamics using agent-based frameworks. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration on neural architectures (e.g., fine-tuning BERT-like models for Hindi) and large-scale phonetic alignment of speech samples. Anticipated outcomes include the first open-source toolkit for pan-dialectal Hindi analysis, a publicly accessible corpus of annotated historical and contemporary texts, and quantitative insights into the sociolinguistic drivers of language divergence in North India. These resources will directly support pedagogical tools, policy-relevant dialect preservation efforts, and cross-disciplinary applications in NLP for low-resource languages. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to redefine methodologies in Hindi studies while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in humanities research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hindi language, antecessors, and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Hindi; Hindustani; related dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical and energetic mechanisms underlying Polarity Therapy, an integrative health approach centered on the Human Energy Field (HEF) theory, using advanced computational modeling. Despite its clinical application in energy-based healing, the quantitative dynamics of HEF interactions with physiological systems remain poorly characterized, limiting evidence-based validation and protocol optimization. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models integrating principles of polarity theory with empirical biomechanical, bioelectrical, and biochemical datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable finite element simulations of energy flow patterns across anatomical regions, molecular dynamics analyses of hypothesized biofield-cellular interactions, and machine learning-driven correlations between therapeutic interventions (e.g., polarity bodywork, yoga postures) and physiological outcomes (e.g., autonomic nervous system responses, cytokine profiles). The computational framework will incorporate clinical data from electromyography, heart rate variability monitoring, and patient-reported outcomes to parameterize energy field dynamics. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of therapist-client energy exchanges during polarity processing sessions, simulating charge distribution and resonance effects theorized in HEF theory. The project will also employ neural networks to identify predictive signatures linking specific energetic interventions to therapeutic outcomes across diverse demographic cohorts. Expected outcomes include validated models of energy field modulation mechanisms, optimized treatment parameters for common health conditions, and open-source tools for simulating polarity-based interventions. By elucidating quantifiable connections between energy medicine principles and measurable biological effects, this work aims to advance Polarity Therapy’s scientific foundation, enhance clinical training protocols, and inform personalized treatment strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling complex simulations of nonlinear energy systems, large-scale data integration, and iterative model refinement, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote health and well-being through application of the integrative therapeutic system based on the Human Energy Field theory developed by Randolph Stone. Includes instruction in polarity theory and principles, energy-based and orthodox anatomy and physiology, polarity processing, polarity bodywork, polarity yoga, energetic nutrition, energetic evaluation and assessment, client communication, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the complex challenge of optimizing interdisciplinary synchronization in musical theatre productions. While the integration of live vocal performance, choreography, and technical staging is central to the art form, the dynamic interplay between these elements remains poorly quantified, limiting data-driven approaches to rehearsal planning, creative iteration, and pedagogical refinement. Our research will develop computational models to analyze and simulate multi-modal performance data, including synchronized motion capture (mocap) from choreography, high-resolution acoustic profiles of vocal performances, and real-time stage technical cues. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of mocap and audio-visual data, training machine learning models to identify patterns in performer coordination, and simulating audience sightline-acoustic interactions across virtual venue geometries. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of ensemble kinematic data, GPU-accelerated acoustic propagation modeling, and large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate staging configurations. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive tools for identifying synchronization bottlenecks in complex choreography-vocal sequences, (2) a framework for simulating audience perceptual experiences under different staging conditions, and (3) open-source datasets linking biomechanical, acoustic, and technical theatre parameters. This work will provide the first quantitative methodology for evaluating integrative musical theatre performance at scale, with applications to curriculum development, virtual rehearsal systems, and accessibility-focused staging adaptations. By bridging computational analysis with performing arts praxis, the project aims to establish new standards for evidence-based creative decision-making in musical theatre production and education.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for integrating theatre, music, and dance into a unified production. Includes instruction in acting, dance, voice, technical theater, musical genres, piano, and history of musical theater.

abstract: The safe and efficient management of hazardous materials requires advanced predictive tools to address the complex interactions between contaminants, environmental systems, and engineered disposal solutions. Current methods for evaluating hazardous waste behavior—such as chemical degradation rates, transport in heterogeneous environments, or long-term containment stability—rely heavily on physical experiments and simplified analytical models. These approaches are resource-intensive, time-consuming, and often fail to capture multi-scale, dynamic processes critical to risk assessment. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate hazardous material interactions at molecular, geochemical, and ecosystem scales. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ reactive transport modeling coupled with machine learning to predict contaminant fate in disposal scenarios, optimize remediation strategies, and assess failure risks in containment systems. Molecular dynamics simulations will elucidate degradation pathways of priority pollutants, while finite element models will evaluate engineered barrier performance under extreme environmental stressors. Machine learning algorithms, trained on experimental and field data, will accelerate parameterization and uncertainty quantification. The computational intensity of these multi-physics simulations—requiring parallelized solvers, large-scale optimization, and 3D visualization of terabyte-scale datasets—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will include predictive tools to guide waste classification, site-specific disposal protocols, and real-time monitoring system design. By integrating computational advances with hazardous materials management, this work aims to reduce environmental exposure risks, lower remediation costs, and inform policy updates for emerging contaminants. The resulting open-source models will provide the waste technology community with scalable, adaptable resources to address evolving regulatory and environmental challenges.
cip_title: Hazardous Materials Management and Waste Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in identifying and disposing of hazardous materials. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, biohazard identification, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, hazardous waste disposal procedures and systems, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the personalization of mental health counseling interventions through the integration of multimodal data analytics and dynamical systems modeling. Current frameworks for short-term counseling often rely on generalized protocols, which may inadequately address the heterogeneous and time-sensitive nature of client needs. To address this, we propose developing a computational platform that analyzes real-world counseling session data—including linguistic patterns, vocal prosody, and physiological signals (e.g., heart rate variability collected via wearable devices)—to identify latent biomarkers of therapeutic progress and predict optimal intervention pathways. The core challenge lies in processing high-dimensional, temporally sensitive datasets while preserving the contextual nuances critical to mental health interactions. Our approach combines natural language processing (NLP) transformers for semantic and sentiment analysis, graph neural networks to model evolving client-counselor relational dynamics, and differential equation systems to simulate intervention outcomes under varying scenarios. HPC resources are essential for training ensemble models on anonymized datasets spanning >10,000 historical counseling sessions (audio, text, and biometrics) and conducting parallelized simulations of intervention efficacy across diverse demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for matching clients to evidence-based counseling strategies within 3–5 sessions, reducing trial-and-error approaches that delay recovery. This work bridges computational psychiatry and counseling practice, offering a novel methodology to operationalize the "stepped care" model in mental health while maintaining ethical rigor through embedded bias-detection algorithms. The resulting tools will empower counselors with real-time decision support, potentially transforming accessibility and precision in short-term mental health care delivery.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide evaluations, referrals, and short-term counseling services to help people prevent or remediate personal problems, conflicts, and emotional crises. Includes instruction in human development, psychopathology, individual and group counseling, personality theory, career assessment, patient screening and referral, observation and testing techniques, interviewing skills, professional standards and ethics, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive analytics in dynamic pricing optimization, a specialized niche within business statistics that intersects econometrics, behavioral economics, and real-time data processing. Traditional pricing models struggle to account for high-dimensional, non-stationary data streams from digital marketplaces, including competitor price fluctuations, granular consumer sentiment metrics, and supply chain volatility. The computational limitations of conventional statistical software further restrict model complexity, leading to suboptimal pricing strategies under rapidly evolving market conditions. This project proposes the development of a hybrid ensemble framework combining Bayesian hierarchical models with transformer-based neural architectures to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies and latent demand signals. The computational approach will involve distributed training of deep learning components across GPU nodes, Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) parallelization for Bayesian parameter estimation, and real-time simulation of pricing scenarios using agent-based modeling techniques. Key challenges include optimizing memory allocation for sparse high-frequency datasets and reducing latency in multi-agent reinforcement learning systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for adaptive pricing决策, validated against terabyte-scale historical retail datasets encompassing 10+ global markets. The research aims to demonstrate statistically significant improvements in profit margin forecasting accuracy (targeting 15-20% reduction in MAPE versus existing methods) while establishing computational benchmarks for real-time pricing systems. Results will provide actionable insights for businesses operating in hypercompetitive e-commerce environments and contribute methodological innovations to the emerging field of computational pricing analytics. HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s  iterative model training demands, which preliminary estimates suggest will require 8,000+ GPU-hours for hyperparameter optimization alone.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data. Includes instruction in statistical theory and methods, computer applications, data analysis and display, long- and short-term forecasting methods, and market performance analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model ethical decision-making processes in critical care settings, with a focus on equitable resource allocation during public health crises. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to evaluate how implicit biases, institutional policies, and cultural variables influence life-saving interventions such as ventilator allocation, ICU triage, or experimental treatment access. Current bioethics paradigms often rely on qualitative case analyses or small-sample surveys, limiting their capacity to generalize findings across diverse populations or rapidly evolving scenarios. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-agent healthcare systems incorporating patient demographics, clinician decision patterns, and dynamic resource constraints. Agent-based modeling will be used to test competing ethical frameworks (e.g., utilitarianism vs. prioritarianism) under crisis conditions, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will analyze historical triage guidelines and ethics committee reports from 50+ institutions. Machine learning algorithms will identify latent biases in triage outcomes using de-identified patient datasets spanning 10 million records. Computational experiments will quantify how variations in policy parameters—such as prioritization of frontline workers or disability-adjusted life year (DALY) thresholds—affect survival disparities across racial, economic, and geographic groups. The HPC environment is essential for running large-scale sensitivity analyses, parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across ethical decision trees, and processing high-dimensional clinical ethics datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for bioethicists, empirically derived thresholds for equitable resource distribution protocols, and policy recommendations for balancing autonomy, justice, and beneficence in emergency medicine. This work will provide the first quantitative evidence base for comparing the population-level consequences of bioethical principles under resource scarcity, directly informing clinical guidelines and crisis preparedness frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational pathology platform to enhance the analysis of high-resolution histopathological imaging data, addressing the growing demand for precision in diagnostic workflows. The increasing use of digital whole-slide imaging (WSI) in pathology generates terabytes of complex data per case, creating bottlenecks in manual annotation, quantitative analysis, and integration with clinical metadata. Current methods for tissue segmentation, anomaly detection, and predictive modeling lack scalability, limiting their utility in time-sensitive diagnostic environments and large-scale research studies. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models capable of automating WSI analysis while maintaining diagnostic rigor. Our approach combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for multi-scale feature extraction with graph-based algorithms to model spatial relationships between tissue structures. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of thousands of WSIs, iterative optimization of 3D reconstruction pipelines for autopsy specimens, and validation of models against curated datasets spanning diverse pathological conditions. Key deliverables include an open-source framework for GPU-accelerated tissue segmentation, predictive models correlating histological patterns with clinical outcomes, and computational tools to standardize autopsy report generation. The successful implementation of this platform will reduce inter-observer variability in specimen analysis, accelerate turnaround times for complex cases, and enable population-scale studies of histopathological biomarkers. By integrating these tools into pathology workflows, we aim to enhance diagnostic accuracy for malignancies, inflammatory disorders, and forensic investigations while providing Pathologist Assistant trainees with advanced computational skills. This work will establish a scalable infrastructure for digital pathology research, directly supporting precision medicine initiatives and fostering collaborations between computational scientists and clinical diagnosticians.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in intellectual property (IP) law, specifically focusing on the computational analysis of patent litigation dynamics and their implications for innovation policy. The exponential growth of global patent filings, coupled with the increasing complexity of patent disputes involving emerging technologies (e.g., AI-generated inventions, CRISPR-based biotech innovations), has created a pressing need for advanced computational tools to model litigation risks, predict case outcomes, and assess systemic biases within IP adjudication systems. Traditional legal research methods struggle to process the scale and interdependencies of multi-jurisdictional patent data, including millions of litigation records, patent office decisions, and technology-specific claim language. This project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze patent claim construction trends across U.S., European, and Asian jurisdictions, combined with graph-based network analysis to map relationships between litigants, expert witnesses, and technical subject matter. Machine learning models will be trained on historical litigation datasets to identify predictors of case outcomes, while agent-based simulations will evaluate how proposed policy reforms might impact innovation ecosystems. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for NLP corpus analysis (patent texts, court opinions), high-memory nodes for graph database operations linking 10M+ legal entities, and GPU-accelerated training of deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible computational framework for assessing patent litigation risks in emerging technology sectors, (2) evidence-based policy recommendations for balancing patent enforcement with open innovation principles, and (3) novel methodologies for applying HPC resources to complex legal system analysis. By bridging computational science and IP law, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven legal research while informing critical debates about how intellectual property regimes can adapt to 21st-century technological realities.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations related to copyrights, patents, trademarks, trade secrets, and related issues. Includes instruction in patent law, copyright law, trademark law, intellectual property licensing and litigation, and applications such as art and entertainment law, communications law, information technology law, sports law, and chemical and biotech patent law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize predictive models for evaluating the long-term efficacy of community-based intervention programs aimed at enhancing family resilience and social equity. Despite the critical role of family and community services in mitigating systemic inequities, existing evaluation frameworks often rely on static, survey-based methodologies that fail to capture the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between socioeconomic factors, policy implementation, and individual behavioral adaptation. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning (ML) to simulate multiscale socioecological systems. The ABM framework will parameterize household decision-making processes, resource allocation dynamics, and community network interactions using longitudinal datasets from public health agencies, nonprofit organizations, and anonymized service utilization records. ML algorithms will then iteratively refine model accuracy by calibrating simulated outcomes against real-world data on program effectiveness, such as housing stability, intergenerational educational attainment, and mental health trends. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of parallelized simulations across high-dimensional parameter spaces, enabling sensitivity analyses to identify leverage points for policy optimization. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolkit for simulating intervention scenarios under varying economic and demographic conditions, as well as evidence-based recommendations for adaptive resource distribution strategies. By bridging computational social science with community praxis, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in family services research while providing actionable insights to stakeholders operating in resource-constrained environments. The project aligns with national priorities to reduce disparities through data-driven policy design, offering a novel paradigm for understanding how micro-level service interactions propagate to macro-level societal outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and implementation of public, private, and voluntary support services for individuals, families, and localities and that prepares individuals to function in a variety of occupations promoting family life, and family/community development. Includes instruction in family systems, human development, social services, community social and economic development, social policy, voluntary sector activities, and outreach and community education.

abstract: Glacial landscapes are dynamic systems shaped by the interplay of ice dynamics, erosion, and climate, yet the mechanisms controlling their evolution—particularly under rapid climate warming—remain poorly resolved. This project seeks to advance understanding of glacial landscape response to climatic and tectonic forcing by developing high-resolution, process-based numerical models of ice flow, subglacial erosion, and sediment transport. A critical challenge lies in simulating coupled ice-bedrock interactions across spatial scales (meters to kilometers) and timescales (years to millennia), necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve nonlinear feedbacks between glacial hydrology, basal sliding, and erosional efficiency. We propose to implement a three-dimensional finite element model integrating higher-order ice dynamics with a granular sediment transport module, calibrated against field data from modern glaciers and paleo-glacial landforms. The model will leverage parallelized solvers to simulate multi-century glacial retreat scenarios under projected warming, with parameter spaces exploring variations in meltwater availability, bedrock lithology, and subglacial sediment saturation. Key computational challenges include managing high-resolution meshes for complex topography, coupling ice-flow and sediment advection equations, and optimizing runtime for ensemble simulations. Outcomes will quantify rates of glacial erosion and deposition during deglaciation, identify thresholds in sediment-flux-driven ice dynamics, and improve predictions of landscape resilience to climate-driven ice loss. This work will directly inform interpretations of glacial landform records, support hazard assessments in rapidly deglaciating regions, and provide open-source modeling tools for the geomorphology community. The requested HPC allocation is essential to achieve the necessary spatial-temporal resolution and computational throughput, as local cluster resources are insufficient for the proposed multi-node, memory-intensive simulations. By bridging glacial process models with landscape evolution theory, this project addresses a critical gap in predicting Earth surface responses to anthropogenic climate change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origin and evolution of topographic features created by physical, chemical or biological processes operating at or near the Earth's surface, including glaciers.

abstract: Rangelands, covering over 40% of Earth’s terrestrial surface, face escalating degradation due to climate variability, invasive species encroachment, and unsustainable grazing practices. Effective management of these ecosystems requires predictive tools to balance livestock productivity, biodiversity conservation, and soil-water resource sustainability. However, current models lack the resolution to capture fine-scale interactions between vegetation dynamics, herbivore behavior, and hydrological processes across heterogeneous landscapes. This project seeks advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a spatially explicit, multi-agent simulation framework that integrates plant growth models, livestock foraging algorithms, and surface hydrology across temporal and spatial scales relevant to management decisions. The computational approach will couple process-based biogeochemical models (using DayCent-CA) with agent-based livestock movement simulations, parameterized by field data from GPS-collared cattle and drone-derived vegetation maps. High-resolution climate projections (CMIP6) and soil moisture datasets will drive dynamic feedbacks between grazing patterns, plant community shifts, and erosion risks. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations to assess uncertainty in management outcomes under 50-year climate scenarios, as well as for machine learning optimization of grazing rotation strategies. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold conditions for irreversible shrub encroachment in arid grasslands, (2) quantification of trade-offs between stocking rates and water retention capacity under drought regimes, and (3) spatially mapped guidelines for adaptive management practices. By enabling 10-meter resolution simulations across 10,000+ hectare domains, this work will provide ranchers and policymakers with decision-support tools to enhance rangeland resilience while maintaining agricultural livelihoods. The computational framework will be modularly designed to support future integration of wildlife movement ecology and carbon sequestration dynamics, advancing interdisciplinary research capabilities in range science.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of rangelands, arid regions, grasslands, and other areas of low productivity, as well as the principles of managing such resources for maximum benefit and environmental balance. Includes instruction in livestock management, wildlife biology, plant sciences, ecology, soil science, and hydrology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the complex sociocultural dynamics influencing the success of church planting initiatives in diverse urban environments. While traditional theological and ethnographic methods dominate the field, there remains a critical gap in understanding how large-scale demographic, economic, and cultural variables interact to shape congregational viability. The project addresses this by integrating computational social science with missiological frameworks, utilizing geospatial data, census records, and historical church growth datasets to construct agent-based models (ABMs) simulating community engagement and congregational development. These models will incorporate variables such as population density, mobility patterns, socioeconomic disparities, and interfaith dynamics to test hypotheses about optimal strategies for resource allocation, leadership training, and community integration. A key innovation lies in applying natural language processing (NLP) to analyze unstructured textual data from missionary reports, social media, and local governance documents, identifying latent cultural barriers and opportunities. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of multivariate simulations (10,000+ agent interactions per trial) and the processing of terabyte-scale multilingual corpora. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for evaluating site-specific risks, dynamic visualization platforms for stakeholder training, and evidence-based frameworks for adaptive mission planning. By bridging computational analytics with practical theology, this project aims to establish a replicable methodology for data-driven decision-making in religious community formation, offering insights applicable to interfaith dialogue and cultural sustainability studies. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, high-memory nodes for geospatial analysis, and secure storage for sensitive ethnographic data, ensuring both academic rigor and ethical compliance.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to establish congregations of Christians in new locations. Includes instruction in models of church planting, church multiplication strategies, church leadership, evangelism, missiology, Christian ethics, and mission-oriented theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies and safety risks in commercial kitchen operations through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Commercial kitchens face persistent challenges in balancing workflow optimization, energy consumption, and compliance with food safety protocols, yet these systems remain understudied in computational research. By integrating real-world data from kitchen sensors, equipment performance metrics, and staff movement patterns, we propose developing a multi-agent simulation framework to model dynamic kitchen environments. The computational model will simulate scenarios such as peak-hour workflow bottlenecks, cross-contamination risks during high-volume food preparation, and energy inefficiencies in equipment use. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize task scheduling, predict equipment maintenance needs, and identify latent sanitation risks based on historical and simulated data. The project further aims to create a predictive analytics tool for real-time decision support, enabling kitchen managers to adjust workflows, staffing, and equipment use dynamically. By employing parallelized computing to handle the high dimensionality of spatial, temporal, and operational variables, this work will generate actionable insights into kitchen system resilience. Outcomes will include open-source simulation tools tailored to culinary training programs, evidence-based protocols for reducing foodborne illness risks, and optimization templates for sustainable kitchen design. This interdisciplinary effort bridges computational systems analysis with vocational culinary education, offering novel methodologies to enhance training outcomes for kitchen assistants while advancing operational standards in the food service industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve under the supervision of chefs and other food service professionals as kitchen support staff and commercial food preparation workers.  Includes instruction in kitchen organization and operations, sanitation and quality control, basic food preparation and cooking skills, kitchen and kitchen equipment maintenance, and quantity food measurement and monitoring.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the computational challenges of simulating multiscale fluid-structure interaction (FSI) phenomena in biomechanical systems, such as cardiovascular devices and soft robotic actuators. These systems involve tightly coupled nonlinear dynamics across disparate spatial and temporal scales, leading to prohibitive computational costs when using conventional monolithic solvers. Current approaches often rely on simplified models or weak coupling schemes, sacrificing accuracy for tractability. This project seeks to develop a scalable, adaptive parallel algorithm that combines implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, domain decomposition, and reduced-order modeling to enable high-fidelity simulations of FSI systems. The core innovation lies in a hybrid framework that decouples fluid and solid subsystems using asynchronous time integration while preserving strong coupling through iterative substructuring. HPC resources will be critical for implementing distributed-memory parallelism using the PETSc library, optimizing load balancing across fluid (Navier-Stokes) and solid (hyperelasticity) solvers, and validating the method against experimental particle image velocimetry data. The algorithm will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve boundary layers near moving interfaces and employ proper orthogonal decomposition to accelerate repetitive subproblems. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in time-to-solution compared to existing partitioned methods while maintaining energy conservation properties, as quantified by dimensionless error metrics. Successful implementation will advance computational capabilities for designing patient-specific medical devices and bioinspired robotics, where accurate prediction of unsteady flow-structure interactions is essential. The developed software toolkit will be made open-source to support broader research in applied mechanics, with particular relevance to NSF’s Harnessing the Data Revolution initiatives. Resource requests include 200,000 node-hours on GPU-accelerated clusters to benchmark weak scaling performance up to 8,192 cores and test multi-physics convergence criteria across prototype applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of a broad range of mathematical and computational methods to modeling, analysis, algorithm development, and simulation for the solution of complex scientific and engineering problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, discrete mathematics, operations research, optimization, differential equations, statistics, scientific computation, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biomedical data and the need for personalized therapeutic strategies in oncology demand advanced computational approaches to model tumor heterogeneity and treatment responses. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale computational framework for simulating tumor evolution, immune interactions, and drug resistance mechanisms. The research addresses a critical gap in predictive oncology: the inability to integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data with dynamic tumor microenvironment (TME) interactions to forecast patient-specific treatment outcomes. Current models lack the resolution to capture spatial and temporal heterogeneity in metastatic cancers, particularly in understudied populations. The proposed framework employs agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate individual cell behaviors within the TME, coupled with deep learning algorithms trained on multi-omics datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and institutional biobanks. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will further characterize protein-ligand interactions for candidate therapeutic compounds. Key computational challenges include scaling ABM to simulate 10^6–10^7 cells across biologically relevant timeframes, optimizing neural network architectures for multimodal data fusion, and parallelizing MD simulations across diverse drug-target pairs. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across tumor growth rates, immune cell infiltration profiles, and drug pharmacokinetics to identify high-risk resistance trajectories. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking genomic variants to TME-driven resistance mechanisms, (2) optimized in silico screening pipelines for combination therapies, and (3) open-source tools for simulating patient-derived tumor-immune ecosystems. This work will directly inform two ongoing clinical trials investigating adaptive therapy regimens in metastatic breast cancer. By bridging computational and translational oncology, the project aims to establish a scalable platform for precision treatment optimization, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches in late-stage cancer care. The requested resources are essential for handling the project’s data volume (>500 TB), real-time model calibration, and achieving the millisecond-scale resolution required for mechanistic insights into emergent resistance phenotypes.
cip_definition: Any program in medicine, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in automated document formatting and structural optimization within modern word processing systems, particularly when handling large-scale, complex documents common in technical fields. Current algorithms for dynamic layout adjustment, table auto-formatting, and multi-element document rendering often struggle with latency and consistency when processing documents exceeding 500 pages or containing embedded technical schematics, mathematical notation, and heterogeneous media.
