We propose developing a parallelized formatting engine that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable real-time optimization of document workflows. The computational approach combines discrete event simulations of user editing patterns with GPU-accelerated constraint satisfaction algorithms to model optimal text flow, image placement, and cross-reference maintenance across distributed document components. A corpus of 10,000 technical documents from engineering reports and academic publications will be used to train transformer-based models for predicting formatting conflicts and stylistic inconsistencies. By implementing distributed memory parallelization across document subsections, we aim to reduce layout computation times by 85% compared to single-threaded processing while maintaining WYSIWYG accuracy. The project will validate results through A/B testing with professional technical writers and benchmark performance against industry-standard word processors under load conditions simulating collaborative editing of 100+ GB documents. Successful implementation could enable new capabilities in automated technical documentation systems, particularly for aerospace manuals and biomedical research publications requiring frequent large-scale updates. This work will also produce open-source optimizations for paragraph-level load balancing in text rendering engines, with direct applications to accessibility tools for visually impaired users navigating complex document structures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: Healthcare-associated adverse events remain a significant challenge, with existing approaches often limited by reactive, siloed analyses that fail to leverage emerging computational tools. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to identify systemic risks and optimize interventions for preventable patient harm. The research integrates multimodal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic biomarkers, and socio-demographic factors—to model interactions between clinical workflows, human factors, and patient-specific vulnerabilities. Computational methods will employ ensemble machine learning algorithms to analyze structured and unstructured EHR data at scale, coupled with agent-based simulations to test hypothetical interventions in virtual care environments. Key challenges include processing terabyte-scale datasets with temporal dependencies (e.g., longitudinal patient trajectories), applying natural language processing to clinician notes for latent risk patterns, and simulating hospital-wide cascades of human error under varying staffing and protocol conditions. HPC resources will enable parallelized model training across thousands of hyperparameter combinations, real-time sensitivity analyses for risk mitigation strategies, and probabilistic forecasts of adverse event trajectories at the population level. Expected outcomes include: (1) validated predictive tools for sepsis progression, medication errors, and hospital-acquired infections with ≥85% precision-recall performance, (2) scalable simulation environments to stress-test patient safety protocols under rare-event scenarios, and (3) actionable risk stratification dashboards for clinical deployment. By unifying systems thinking with computational scalability, this work aims to advance proactive, personalized approaches to harm reduction while addressing critical gaps in healthcare quality research infrastructure. The requested computing resources are essential for managing memory-intensive genomic-phenotypic association studies and achieving subhourly model retraining cycles across multi-site healthcare networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of transformative mechanisms and evidence-based protocols to reduce preventable patient harm and improve clinical outcomes. Includes instruction in healthcare quality, patient safety, research methods, program evaluation, epidemiology, legal and regulatory compliance, systems thinking, human factors engineering, and risk management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable algorithms for real-time analysis of dynamic, large-scale networks, addressing critical limitations in existing computational methods that struggle with evolving connectivity patterns in applications such as social networks, IoT systems, and distributed sensor arrays. Current graph processing frameworks exhibit inefficiencies when handling frequent edge/node updates, leading to suboptimal resource utilization and prohibitive latency for time-sensitive tasks. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid parallel computing approach combining shared-memory (OpenMP) and distributed-memory (MPI) paradigms, augmented by GPU-accelerated preprocessing for dynamic data streams. The research will implement adaptive load-balancing strategies to address workload skew in heterogeneous clusters and integrate incremental computation techniques to minimize redundant processing during graph updates. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for evaluating scalability across billion-edge graphs using real-world datasets from collaborative filtering and autonomous vehicle networks, with comparative benchmarks against state-of-the-art frameworks like GraphX and CuGraph. Expected outcomes include a 40-50% reduction in synchronization overhead for streaming graph operations and validated performance thresholds for subsecond response times in anomaly detection tasks. The resulting open-source framework will directly benefit research in distributed machine learning and real-time decision systems, while novel metrics for dynamic graph complexity will advance theoretical foundations in computational scalability. By enabling efficient processing of continuously evolving networks, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in deploying large-scale adaptive systems for cybersecurity and intelligent infrastructure applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer theory, computing problems and solutions, and the design of computer systems and user interfaces from a scientific perspective. Includes instruction in the principles of computational science, computer development and programming, and applications to a variety of end-use situations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for modeling the linguistic complexity of American Sign Language (ASL), focusing on its multimodal and spatial-grammatical structures. While ASL is a fully realized natural language, computational tools for analyzing its non-linear syntax, simultaneous articulation of manual and non-manual markers, and three-dimensional signing space remain underdeveloped compared to spoken language technologies. The research problem centers on the inability of existing software to process high-resolution motion capture data and video corpora at scale, limiting progress in ASL linguistics, machine translation, and educational tool development. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural network architectures on a curated corpus of 4D signing data (3D joint trajectories + time) captured via inertial motion sensors and stereoscopic video. Computational methods will include the development of hybrid graph convolutional networks to model signer-specific kinematics and recurrent spatial transformers to parse syntactic dependencies across signing space. The pipeline will integrate GPU-accelerated preprocessing of 20TB of raw motion data and distributed training of multi-modal transformer models. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for analyzing ASL’s unique morphosyntactic features at unprecedented temporal resolution (<5ms frame analysis), with applications to improving sign language recognition systems and linguistic theory. Results will advance computational sign language linguistics by providing the first HPC-optimized toolkit for modeling ASL’s simultaneous articulation patterns, directly supporting deaf-led research initiatives. Resource allocation will enable processing of the largest available ASL motion corpus, benefiting interdisciplinary work in sign language preservation, AI accessibility, and neurolinguistic studies of visual-spatial grammar.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on American Sign Language as a communication medium or language skill that is, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of advanced computational tools into technical theatre production presents a critical opportunity to address complex design challenges while optimizing resource efficiency. Current workflows in theatre design—spanning set construction, dynamic lighting, spatial acoustics, and interactive soundscapes—often rely on iterative physical prototyping and disjointed software tools, leading to material waste, prolonged development timelines, and suboptimal audience experiences. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a unified simulation framework capable of modeling multi-sensory theatre environments in real time. By combining physics-based rendering, acoustic wave propagation algorithms, and parametric design optimization, the proposed system will simulate interactions between set geometries, variable lighting conditions, and audience-perceived sound quality under dynamic performance parameters. Key computational challenges include large-scale finite element analysis for structural integrity of kinetic set pieces, GPU-accelerated ray tracing for real-time light and shadow accuracy, and machine learning models to predict audience sensory responses across diverse seating configurations. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized testing of design alternatives, reducing reliance on physical mock-ups and enabling data-driven decisions during pre-production. Anticipated outcomes include a modular software toolkit for theatre designers, validated through case studies on proscenium, thrust, and immersive stage configurations. This work will directly enhance the precision and sustainability of technical theatre workflows while establishing a methodological foundation for computational creativity in live performance design. By bridging gaps between artistic vision and technical feasibility, the project aims to expand access to high-quality theatrical experiences and inform pedagogical advancements in theatre technology education.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Technical Theatre/ Theatre Design and Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic, technical and dramatic principles and techniques to the communication of dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through technical theatre methods. Includes instruction in set design, lighting design, sound effects, theatre acoustics, scene painting, property management, costume design, and technical direction and production and use of computer applications to support these functions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize speech education interventions for diverse learner populations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in personalized teacher training. While speech educators are trained to address variations in students’ linguistic development, existing methods for designing tailored instructional strategies lack scalability and real-time adaptability. The research problem centers on integrating large-scale speech datasets (e.g., student recordings, demographic factors, and longitudinal performance metrics) with dynamic models of pedagogical effectiveness, which traditional computing infrastructure cannot process efficiently. The proposed computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques for analyzing phonetic, prosodic, and syntactic features in student speech samples with machine learning algorithms to simulate learning trajectories under varied teaching strategies. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multimodal data (audio, text, and behavioral annotations) across thousands of simulated classroom scenarios, using agent-based modeling to test hypotheses about intervention efficacy. Key methods include training neural networks to classify speech development patterns, clustering learners by intervention-responsive profiles, and optimizing instructional decision trees via reinforcement learning. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a predictive model linking specific teaching techniques to speech skill acquisition rates in heterogeneous student groups and (2) an open-access toolkit for generating adaptive lesson plans based on real-time diagnostic data. This work will directly enhance speech teacher education by providing evidence-based, computationally derived frameworks for individualized instruction, thereby bridging the gap between theoretical pedagogy and data-driven classroom practices. The scalability of the models, made feasible through HPC, ensures applicability across K–12 and special education contexts, ultimately supporting equitable outcomes in speech and language arts proficiency.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach speech and language arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular and systemic drivers of chronic inflammatory diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease. These conditions, which affect millions globally, arise from complex interactions between genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors. Current analytical approaches struggle to integrate multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) with clinical and demographic data at scale, limiting the identification of predictive biomarkers and personalized therapeutic targets. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in analyzing these high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets to uncover disease-subtype-specific pathways and modifiable risk factors. The proposed computational approach combines federated learning frameworks with graph neural networks (GNNs) to model biological networks and patient-level data across distributed repositories while preserving privacy. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of whole-genome sequencing data from 50,000+ participants in the NIH All of Us cohort, coupled with longitudinal electronic health records, to train interpretable machine learning models. Key tasks include optimizing containerized workflows for GPU-accelerated feature extraction, simulating immune cell signaling dynamics via ordinary differential equation systems, and validating models against in vitro cytokine response assays. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for multi-omics integration in population health studies, (2) prioritized candidate genes and environmental triggers for experimental validation, and (3) open-source tools for reproducible analysis of immune-mediated diseases. By enabling rapid iteration of systems biology models at unprecedented resolution, this work will advance precision medicine strategies for chronic inflammation while establishing computational frameworks adaptable to other complex health conditions. The requested resources directly address memory-intensive genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and latency challenges in real-time model inference across distributed clinical datasets.
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health sciences.

abstract: The increasing complexity of clinical workflows and patient data management in ambulatory care settings presents challenges for medical assistants (MAs) in balancing administrative and clinical responsibilities. This project seeks to develop an AI-driven decision-support framework to optimize real-time task prioritization for MAs during patient encounters, reducing cognitive overload and improving adherence to clinical protocols. Leveraging anonymized electronic health record (EHR) data from outpatient clinics, we will train multimodal machine learning models to predict context-sensitive task sequences (e.g., vital sign acquisition timing, medication reconciliation prompts, or documentation requirements) based on patient-specific clinical histories, presenting complaints, and workflow state. The computational approach integrates natural language processing for clinical note analysis, temporal convolutional networks for longitudinal EHR pattern recognition, and reinforcement learning to adapt recommendations to dynamic clinic environments. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning 50,000+ patient encounters, enabling parallelized hyperparameter optimization of ensemble models, and simulating clinic workflows through discrete-event modeling. Expected outcomes include an open-source inference engine capable of subsecond latency recommendations deployable on clinic workstations, validated against gold-standard workflow analyses from video-recorded MA-patient interactions. This research addresses a critical gap in human-factors engineering for clinical support roles, with potential to reduce procedural errors by 15-20% in pilot studies while maintaining patient-centered communication standards. By focusing on the specialized interface between administrative logistics and protocol-driven clinical tasks, the project advances health sciences through computational innovation tailored to underexplored allied health professions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical office administrative services and perform clinical duties including patient intake and care, routine diagnostic and recording procedures, pre-examination and examination assistance, and the administration of medications and first aid. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology; medical terminology; medical law and ethics; patient psychology and communications; medical office procedures; and clinical diagnostic, examination, testing, and treatment procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of next-generation hypersonic re-entry vehicles through high-fidelity computational modeling of aerothermal-structural interactions during atmospheric entry. Current models struggle to resolve multiscale turbulence, chemically reactive boundary layers, and transient material ablation phenomena simultaneously, limiting predictive accuracy for thermal protection system (TPS) performance. To address this, we propose a tightly coupled computational framework integrating large-eddy simulation (LES) for compressible turbulent flows, finite-rate chemistry models for air dissociation, and nonlinear thermostructural solvers for anisotropic composite materials. The workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform 3D implicit simulations at unprecedented resolutions, capturing sub-mm boundary layer features across meter-scale vehicle geometries. Adaptive mesh refinement will dynamically resolve shock interactions and localized ablation zones, while asynchronous parallelization strategies will enable efficient scaling across thousands of cores. Validation will utilize legacy wind tunnel data from arcjet tests and flight measurements from past missions. Successful implementation will produce the first open-source toolchain capable of full-cone hypersonic TPS analysis with coupled fluid-structure-chemistry effects at mission-relevant scales. Outcomes will directly inform material selection and cooling system designs for the NSF-sponsored HYPERSAT spacecraft program, reducing reliance on conservative safety margins that currently limit payload capacity. By enabling predictive modeling of extreme aerothermal environments, this work aims to accelerate the development of reusable hypersonic platforms while mitigating risks in crewed lunar return missions and Mars entry systems. The requested computing allocations will support parametric studies across Mach 8–20 regimes, requiring petascale storage for high-dimensional output datasets and dedicated GPU nodes for machine learning-assisted turbulence closure model training.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematic principles to the design, technology, and development of systems and equipment used in aerospace and astronautical operations. Includes instruction in basic and applied sciences related to astronomy and astronautics, control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: Dental diseases remain a significant global public health burden, disproportionately affecting underserved populations due to systemic inequities in access to care. Current approaches to optimizing preventive service delivery—such as community fluoride programs or school-based dental screenings—often rely on static epidemiological data, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between population demographics, behavioral factors, and resource constraints. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model the cost-effectiveness and equity impacts of alternative public health strategies for dental disease prevention. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale, spatially explicit simulations integrating multi-source data, including census tract demographics, disease prevalence maps, and healthcare utilization patterns. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be used to simulate individual and community-level decision-making under varying policy scenarios, such as mobile clinic deployments or targeted oral health education campaigns. Machine learning algorithms will further refine parameter estimation for disease progression and intervention efficacy using longitudinal electronic health record data from public health clinics. Computational demands arise from the need to simultaneously model millions of agents across diverse geographies, incorporate stochastic variability in outcomes, and perform sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimized resource allocation strategies that maximize population-level caries reduction while minimizing disparities in access. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will enable local health departments to tailor preventive programs to community-specific needs. By quantifying trade-offs between cost, equity, and clinical impact, this work aims to provide policymakers with evidence-based tools to transform dental public health planning from reactive to proactive, data-driven decision-making.
cip_definition: Research focused on the formulation and delivery of public preventive and curative dental health services.

abstract: Agricultural systems face mounting challenges in optimizing crop productivity and resilience under increasingly variable climatic conditions. Traditional plant breeding and agronomic approaches struggle to efficiently address the complex interactions between genotype, environment, and management practices that govern crop performance. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for identifying optimal crop varieties and cultivation strategies tailored to specific regional conditions. The research will integrate large-scale genomic datasets, historical yield records, and high-resolution environmental models to simulate crop responses across diverse agroecological zones. Machine learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks and ensemble methods, will be employed to analyze genotype-by-environment interactions and predict phenotypic outcomes under projected climate scenarios. Key computational challenges include processing multi-terabyte datasets spanning 20+ crop species, running iterative simulations to assess trait stability, and optimizing hyperparameters for spatially explicit models. Access to HPC resources will enable parallelized workflows for genomic prediction, reduce runtime for complex optimization tasks from weeks to days, and facilitate the analysis of high-dimensional data that exceeds the capacity of local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of genetic markers associated with drought and heat tolerance in staple crops, (2) predictive maps of variety performance under future climate conditions, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic yield forecasting at subregional scales. These results will directly inform breeding programs and precision agriculture initiatives while providing a computational foundation for accelerating crop improvement cycles. The project addresses critical gaps in plant sciences by enabling data-driven decision-making for sustainable agricultural intensification, with particular relevance to food security in climate-vulnerable regions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding, cultivation, and production of agricultural plants, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural plant products. Includes instruction in the plant sciences, crop cultivation and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Chinese linguistic diversity and classical literary texts. The research problem centers on the vast scale and structural complexity of Chinese dialects and premodern texts, which hinder systematic analysis using conventional methods. While dialectology and textual studies have long relied on manual annotation or small-scale computational tools, the volume of data—including digitized historical texts, spoken dialect corpora, and cross-regional linguistic datasets—demands advanced computational infrastructure to enable large-scale pattern recognition, phonetic modeling, and semantic mapping. The project will employ neural language models optimized for classical Chinese and dialectal speech, alongside graph-based algorithms to trace lexical and syntactic evolution across literary periods. Key tasks include training transformer architectures on Ming-Qing vernacular literature to detect stylistic shifts, applying contrastive phonemic analysis to understudied Mandarin and Wu dialect recordings, and simulating language contact effects in pidgin varieties. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of terabyte-scale text corpora, hyperparameter tuning of deep learning models, and real-time acoustic feature extraction from oral archives. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialectal features, predictive models of literary genre evolution, and tools for automated glossing of rare characters in medieval manuscripts. By integrating computational linguistics with Sinological scholarship, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in Chinese philology, support endangered dialect preservation, and provide scalable frameworks for analyzing non-standard linguistic phenomena. The results will directly contribute to interdisciplinary digital humanities initiatives while addressing gaps in language technologies tailored to Chinese’s unique morphological and tonal properties.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of China and associated dialects and literature. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing demand for portable power equipment with enhanced efficiency and reduced emissions necessitates advanced research into optimizing small internal-combustion engines. Current experimental methods for improving engine performance and durability are time-consuming and limited in their ability to model complex, real-world operating conditions. This project proposes a computational approach to simulate and analyze small engine systems under diverse environmental and mechanical stressors, enabling rapid iteration of design and repair strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to develop multi-physics models integrating combustion dynamics, thermal stress analysis, and material wear prediction. These models will simulate engine behavior across parameter spaces that are impractical to test experimentally, such as extreme temperature gradients, fuel mixtures, and mechanical load cycles. A key focus will be validating computational predictions against empirical data from engine test benches to ensure model accuracy. Machine learning techniques will then be applied to identify optimal maintenance protocols and component redesigns that maximize engine lifespan while minimizing emissions. The computational workflow will require parallel processing capabilities to handle coupled fluid-structure interaction simulations and large-scale parameter optimization. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for diagnosing common failure modes in small engines, data-driven guidelines for sustainable repair practices, and novel insights into combustion efficiency improvements for alternative fuels. By bridging computational engineering with applied small engine mechanics, this research will provide technical educators and repair technicians with evidence-based strategies to address evolving industry challenges. The project will also establish a framework for integrating HPC-based simulations into vocational training programs, fostering innovation in a field traditionally reliant on manual troubleshooting methods.
cip_title: Small Engine Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain small internal-combustion engines used on portable power equipment such as lawnmowers, chain saws, rotary tillers, and snowmobiles.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) and co-occurring psychiatric conditions represent a critical public health challenge, with heterogeneity in etiology, progression, and treatment response complicating clinical management. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of treatment outcomes and neurobiological mechanisms in addiction psychiatry. Current approaches often rely on simplified clinical variables or small neuroimaging datasets, limiting their ability to capture multidimensional interactions between genetic, neurocircuitry, and psychosocial factors. We propose to integrate large-scale multimodal data—including longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), functional MRI (fMRI) from patients with opioid and stimulant use disorders, and polygenic risk scores—to develop computational models of relapse risk and treatment responsiveness. A hybrid machine learning framework will be implemented, combining graph neural networks to model brain connectivity dynamics with transformer-based architectures for temporal EHR analysis. Computational psychiatry methods will be extended to simulate reward pathway dysregulation in dual-diagnosis patients, using biophysically informed models of dopaminergic signaling under varying stress and pharmacotherapy conditions. HPC resources are essential for training these models on clustered neuroimaging data (>10 TB), optimizing hyperparameters across distributed nodes, and running Monte Carlo simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of neurocognitive biomarkers predictive of abstinence durability, (2) a decision-support tool for personalizing medication-assisted therapy based on computational phenotypes, and (3) mechanistic insights into how comorbid depression alters addiction-related neural plasticity. By enabling analysis of previously intractable datasets and complex system dynamics, this work aims to bridge computational neuroscience with clinical addiction research, ultimately informing more precise stratification strategies and accelerating the translation of neurocomputational findings into targeted therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation and treatment of individuals with alcohol, drug, or other substance-related disorders, and of individuals with the dual diagnosis of substance-related and other psychiatric disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay of family relational patterns and mental health outcomes in systemic therapy contexts. Despite growing evidence that family interactions significantly influence individual well-being, computational tools capable of capturing the non-linear, time-dependent complexities of relational behaviors remain underdeveloped. Traditional statistical methods often fail to account for the high-dimensional, interdependent variables inherent in family systems, such as communication styles, emotional reciprocity, and cultural or generational influences. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to simulate and predict how micro-level relational shifts—identified in therapy sessions—propagate through family networks to affect mental health trajectories. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with natural language processing (NLP) to analyze longitudinal therapy session transcripts, behavioral surveys, and biometric data (e.g., wearable device outputs). Machine learning algorithms will be trained on anonymized datasets from diverse family structures to identify critical inflection points in therapeutic progress, while graph neural networks will map relational dependencies. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing simulations of large family networks (n > 1,000 synthetic cohorts) and optimizing hyperparameters in real-time feedback loops. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for identifying families at risk of poor therapeutic outcomes due to entrenched relational patterns, (2) a generative AI tool to assist clinicians in tailoring interventions based on simulated system-wide responses, and (3) open-source code for replicating the framework in other systemic therapy contexts. By bridging computational science and relational health, this work aims to advance precision approaches in marriage and family therapy while establishing scalable methodologies for studying complex interpersonal systems in mental health care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of marriage and family therapy, involving the diagnosis of cognitive, affective, and behavioral domain disorders, both mental and emotional, within the context of marriage and family systems and the application of short- and long-term therapeutic strategies in family group contexts. Includes instruction in psychotherapy, family systems and studies, small group intervention and therapy, marital problems, depression, identification of psychopathologies and behavioral disorders, holistic health care, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding and treatment of complex ophthalmic diseases, such as age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and glaucoma, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multimodal clinical datasets. Current diagnostic and prognostic models for these conditions lack precision due to the heterogeneity of disease phenotypes, limited integration of imaging, genetic, and electronic health record (EHR) data, and computational constraints in processing high-dimensional datasets. The research aims to develop scalable machine learning frameworks to integrate optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, genomic sequencing data, and longitudinal EHRs, enabling the identification of novel biomarkers and patient-specific risk trajectories. A key computational challenge lies in processing terabyte-scale OCT datasets, which require GPU-accelerated deep learning models for segmentation and feature extraction, alongside parallelized pipelines for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and multi-omics integration. The project will deploy federated learning architectures to collaborate across institutional datasets while preserving patient privacy. Expected outcomes include predictive models for disease progression in AMD, optimized treatment stratification protocols for glaucoma, and open-source computational tools tailored for ophthalmic data. These resources will address critical gaps in clinical decision-making, particularly in early intervention and personalized therapeutic strategies. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the computational load of training 3D convolutional neural networks on volumetric eye scans, conducting real-time simulations of surgical outcomes (e.g., trabeculectomy dynamics), and performing large-scale permutation testing for genetic associations. By unifying disparate data modalities at scale, this work will provide translational insights into ocular pathology mechanisms and establish a computational foundation for future innovation in vision science.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention treatment of ophthalmic diseases and disorders, and ocular pathology procedures. May included related research in eye surgery.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into clinical dental research has the potential to revolutionize precision treatment planning and outcomes analysis. However, existing approaches for modeling complex dental datasets—including 3D radiographic imaging, intraoral scans, electronic health records (EHRs), and genomic data—are limited by the computational demands of processing multi-modal data at scale. This project proposes to develop a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze heterogeneous dental datasets and predict treatment efficacy for complex restorative and prosthodontic cases. The primary research challenge lies in harmonizing high-resolution cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) volumes, dynamic occlusal force measurements, and longitudinal EHRs while accounting for patient-specific variables such as bone density, immune markers, and genetic predispositions. Our computational approach will employ deep learning architectures optimized for parallel processing to identify latent patterns across imaging, biomechanical, and clinical data. Finite element analysis (FEA) simulations of masticatory forces on digitally reconstructed dentition will be accelerated using GPU clusters, enabling probabilistic modeling of long-term restoration outcomes under diverse physiological conditions. A federated learning component will facilitate multi-institutional collaboration while maintaining data privacy compliance. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model for optimal material selection in crown/bridge cases based on biomechanical stress distributions, (2) an automated risk stratification system for peri-implantitis using genomic-clinical data fusion, and (3) open-source tools for real-time rendering of treatment simulations in clinical education settings. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven decision support in advanced general dentistry, reducing trial-and-error approaches in complex cases while providing quantitative frameworks for evaluating emerging dental technologies. The computational infrastructure will enable processing of petabyte-scale datasets from participating dental clinics, supporting both retrospective analysis and prospective clinical validation studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of dental clinical techniques and dental practice issues. Includes instruction in subjects such as the history of dentistry, advanced dental practice management, dental ethics and jurisprudence, social and behavioral science studies of dentistry, advanced restorative dentistry, oral medicine, oral radiology, advanced clinical procedures and technology, and others.

abstract: Oral and maxillofacial diseases exhibit significant heterogeneity in clinical presentation, molecular drivers, and treatment responses, complicating accurate diagnosis and personalized management. Current approaches often rely on histopathological analysis or isolated molecular biomarkers, which lack the resolution to fully capture disease complexity. This project proposes an integrative computational framework to analyze multi-modal datasets—including whole-slide histopathology images, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and clinical metadata—to identify predictive signatures of disease progression and therapeutic resistance in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of high-resolution imaging data, perform GPU-accelerated deep learning for feature extraction, and run large-scale simulations of molecular interaction networks. Computational pipelines will employ convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect micro-anatomic patterns in histopathology slides, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model cell-cell communication dynamics, and Bayesian hierarchical models to integrate multi-omics data with clinical outcomes. The project will leverage distributed computing frameworks to parallelize analysis across 500+ patient samples from international collaborator networks. Expected outcomes include: 1) validated computational biomarkers for early detection of high-risk OSCC subtypes, 2) mechanistic insights into medication-related ONJ pathogenesis through simulated bone remodeling pathways, and 3) open-source tools for multimodal data fusion in oral pathology. Results will address critical gaps in prognostic stratification and inform targeted therapeutic strategies. The scale of data processing—requiring >2 PB storage, >50,000 GPU hours, and multi-node memory allocation—necessitates dedicated HPC infrastructure beyond institutional cluster capabilities. This work establishes a paradigm for computational pathology in oral health research, with translational potential for clinical decision-support systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases affecting the oral and maxillofacial regions, using clinical, radiographic, microscopic, biochemical, or other examinations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing energy consumption and operational efficiency in mid-scale hotel facilities through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled dynamic simulations. Current energy management systems in hospitality often rely on static models that fail to account for real-time fluctuations in occupancy, weather, guest behavior, and equipment performance, leading to suboptimal resource allocation. This study proposes the development of a multi-agent simulation framework integrating IoT-derived sensor data, historical occupancy patterns, and predictive weather analytics to model energy use across HVAC, lighting, and water systems at a granular, room-by-room level. Leveraging HPC resources, the framework will simulate millions of scenario permutations to identify adaptive control strategies that balance sustainability goals with guest comfort metrics. Computational methods will combine discrete-event simulation for operational workflows with recurrent neural networks to predict short-term demand surges and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize equipment scheduling. The project will utilize anonymized operational data from a network of 12 hotels spanning three climate zones, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle 8TB of structured and unstructured data inputs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of reducing energy waste by 15-22% in test environments while maintaining guest satisfaction scores, along with generalized predictive models for equipment maintenance cycles. This work bridges computational engineering and hospitality management by creating scalable solutions for resource allocation in transient occupancy environments, offering methodological innovations in real-time adaptive systems for the lodging industry. Results will provide actionable insights for reducing operational costs and carbon footprints in hotel operations, contributing to the emerging field of computational sustainability in service-sector businesses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage and control; hotel facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; marketing and sales promotion; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotels and motel operations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and operational efficiency of complex mechanical systems, such as multi-phase fluid dynamics in heat exchangers, thermo-mechanical stress distributions in additive manufacturing components, and dynamic responses of composite materials under extreme loading. Traditional experimental and analytical methods for these systems face limitations in scalability, cost, and resolution, particularly when analyzing multi-physics interactions or transient behaviors. To address these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and coupled multi-physics simulations. These models will integrate machine learning algorithms to iteratively refine material property predictions and system performance under variable boundary conditions. The computational workflow will employ open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM, FEniCS) alongside GPU-accelerated commercial software (ANSYS, COMSOL) to resolve high-fidelity meshes and reduce simulation times. Key objectives include validating models against experimental data from partner industrial labs, identifying failure thresholds in turbine blade coatings under thermal cycling, and optimizing fluid-structure interaction in next-generation hydraulic actuators. The outcomes will directly inform prototype development guidelines, reducing iterative testing costs by an estimated 30–40% for small- and medium-sized manufacturers. Additionally, the project will generate publicly accessible datasets and modular simulation templates to support workforce training in computational mechanical design. By enabling rapid, high-resolution analysis of non-linear phenomena, this work aims to advance predictive maintenance strategies and accelerate the adoption of sustainable materials in energy and transportation systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations, which require parallel processing capabilities for tasks exceeding 10,000 CPU-core hours per parametric study.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the design and development phases of a wide variety of projects involving mechanical systems. Includes instruction in principles of mechanics, applications to specific engineering systems, design testing procedures, prototype and operational testing and inspection procedures, manufacturing system-testing procedures, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing wastewater treatment systems to enhance contaminant removal efficiency while reducing energy consumption and operational costs. Current treatment processes, particularly for emerging contaminants such as pharmaceuticals and microplastics, rely on empirical trial-and-error approaches that are time-intensive and fail to account for dynamic system interactions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity fluid dynamics modeling, machine learning (ML), and molecular-scale simulations to predict and optimize treatment performance under variable wastewater compositions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multi-physics interactions in bioreactors, membrane filtration units, and advanced oxidation processes at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolutions. Large-scale simulations will model hydrodynamic behavior, microbial community dynamics, and reactive transport processes using open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM, PHREEQC) coupled with custom ML models trained on experimental datasets. Molecular dynamics simulations will further elucidate degradation pathways of refractory contaminants in electrochemical treatment systems. The computational workflow will iteratively inform pilot-scale experiments, reducing the need for physical prototyping. Expected outcomes include the identification of energy-efficient operational parameters, predictive models for contaminant removal under climate-induced inflow variability, and design guidelines for modular treatment systems tailored to decentralized reuse applications. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to accelerate the development of adaptive, data-driven wastewater management strategies that support water recycling goals while mitigating environmental and public health risks. The resulting open-access datasets and scalable computational tools will provide a foundation for future innovation in sustainable water infrastructure.
cip_title: Water Quality and Wastewater Treatment Management and Recycling Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using water storage, waterpower, and wastewater treatment systems. Includes instruction in water storage, power and/or treatment systems and equipment; testing and inspection procedures; system maintenance procedures; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural and linguistic identities in the Iberian Peninsula through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in Iberian Studies: the lack of systematic, data-driven methodologies to trace how regional, gender, and ethnic identities were negotiated and represented across premodern and early modern Iberian societies. Current scholarship often relies on fragmented archival samples, limiting the ability to identify macro-level patterns in cultural production. To overcome this, the project will compile and process a multilingual corpus of digitized manuscripts, printed texts, and iconographic materials (8th–17th centuries) from Spanish, Portuguese, Catalan, and Arabic sources. Computational challenges include handling non-Latin scripts, variant orthographies, and degraded visual materials. A hybrid pipeline will be developed, combining optical character recognition (OCR) fine-tuning for historical Iberian languages, transformer-based NLP models for semantic and sentiment analysis, and graph neural networks to map socio-cultural networks across regions and time periods. HPC resources are essential to train these models on terabytes of unstructured data, enable parallel processing of heterogeneous file types, and run iterative simulations testing hypotheses about cultural transmission pathways. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated texts and images, novel computational workflows tailored to Iberian Studies, and quantitative insights into how intersecting identities (e.g., gender, religion, linguistic affiliation) shaped artistic and literary production. By bridging computational methods and humanistic inquiry, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of Iberian cultural hybridity while establishing scalable frameworks for interdisciplinary analysis of underrepresented historical narratives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of the Iberian Peninsula and related island groups and border regions from earliest times to the present, with particular emphasis on the development of Spain and Portugal but including other historical and current cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving role of digital media platforms in shaping cultural narratives and public opinion during sociopolitical crises, with a focus on large-scale, cross-platform content analysis. While existing scholarship has explored media effects through qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods, the scale, diversity, and real-time nature of contemporary digital media necessitate computational approaches to analyze patterns across billions of texts, images, and videos. The research problem centers on how algorithmic content prioritization and user engagement dynamics interact with cultural context to amplify or suppress specific narratives, particularly in multilingual and transnational contexts. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for multilingual sentiment analysis and topic modeling, alongside computer vision tools for meme and visual rhetoric analysis. Network analysis will map cross-platform information diffusion, while high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets from social media APIs, broadcast archives, and web scraping initiatives. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of platform-specific amplification patterns for crisis-related content, 2) a computational framework for assessing cultural bias in algorithmic content curation, and 3) longitudinal models of narrative evolution across media types and geopolitical contexts. The scale of data processing—requiring parallelized ingestion of streaming media, GPU-accelerated deep learning for multimodal analysis, and distributed storage for petascale datasets—necessitates HPC infrastructure beyond conventional departmental resources. Results will advance media ecology theory while providing actionable insights for policymakers addressing platform governance and crisis communication strategies. This computationally intensive approach bridges critical media studies with data science, establishing new methodologies for analyzing digital culture at societal-scale resolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis and criticism of media institutions and media texts, how people experience and understand media content, and the roles of media in producing and transforming culture. Includes instruction in communications regulation, law, and policy; media history; media aesthetics, interpretation, and criticism; the social and cultural effects of mass media; cultural studies; the economics of media industries; visual and media literacy; and the psychology and behavioral aspects of media messages, interpretation, and utilization.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop and evaluate scalable machine learning models to optimize personalized learning pathways in adaptive educational technologies, addressing the challenge of efficiently tailoring content to diverse learner needs in real time. While adaptive learning systems show promise for improving educational outcomes, current approaches often rely on simplified heuristics or small-scale datasets, limiting their responsiveness to complex, dynamic learner behaviors. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework that integrates multimodal learner data (interaction logs, assessment performance, and eye-tracking metrics) with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents to dynamically adjust instructional sequences. The project requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate these models on large-scale datasets spanning 50,000+ learners across three open online course platforms. Key computational tasks include parallelized hyperparameter optimization for DRL policies, real-time simulation of alternative instructional scenarios using agent-based modeling, and NLP-driven analysis of learner feedback at scale. The HPC environment will enable comparative studies of model architectures (e.g., transformer-based vs. recurrent networks) under varying conditions of data sparsity and temporal granularity. Expected outcomes include 1) open-source algorithms for resource-efficient personalization in learning management systems, 2) evidence-based design principles for temporal sequencing of multimedia content, and 3) benchmark datasets documenting model performance across demographic subgroups to mitigate algorithmic bias. By establishing computational methods to balance personalization with scalability, this work aims to advance the design of equitable, data-driven educational technologies while contributing new methodologies for HPC applications in learning analytics.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on designing and integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, design, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, computer applications, human-computer interaction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: Pediatric musculoskeletal disorders present unique challenges due to the dynamic nature of growing bones and tissues, where treatment outcomes depend on complex interactions between surgical interventions, rehabilitation protocols, and biological development. Current clinical decision-making tools often lack the capacity to model these multidimensional, time-dependent processes at patient-specific resolution, leading to suboptimal risk stratification and intervention planning. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to predict long-term outcomes of orthopedic treatments in children, with a focus on congenital deformities, growth plate injuries, and early-onset scoliosis. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate longitudinal clinical imaging, biomechanical loading data, and mechanistic bone growth models into multiscale simulations. Patient-specific finite element models will be constructed from 3D radiographs and motion capture data to simulate skeletal stress distributions under varying treatment scenarios, while agent-based modeling will capture cellular-scale growth plate activity. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on retrospective clinical datasets to identify predictors of complications such as limb-length discrepancies or asymmetric growth. The computational pipeline will require iterative optimization of coupled models, necessitating parallel processing capabilities for parameter sweeps across thousands of simulated growth trajectories. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for estimating postoperative growth patterns and optimizing surgical timing in epiphysiodesis procedures, as well as biomechanical risk scores for guided bracing in scoliosis management. By enabling real-time analysis of terabyte-scale imaging datasets and computationally intensive multiphysics simulations, the requested HPC resources will directly support the translation of mechanistic insights into clinical decision aids. This work aims to reduce revision surgery rates in pediatric orthopedic populations by 15-20% through personalized intervention planning, while establishing an open-source computational toolkit for growth-aware surgical simulation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, surgical and non-surgical treatment, and management of musculoskeletal diseases, abnormalities and trauma in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance precision medicine in otolaryngology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex multi-modal datasets from patients with head and neck cancers (HNCs). Despite advances in genomic and imaging technologies, integrating heterogeneous data types—such as bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, radiomics, and clinical outcomes—remains a critical challenge. Current analytical pipelines lack the computational scalability to identify robust biomarkers or model tumor-immune microenvironment interactions at the resolution required for personalized therapeutic strategies. This project will develop and deploy machine learning frameworks optimized for HPC environments to unify these datasets, enabling the identification of molecular signatures predictive of treatment response and metastasis. Computational workflows will include graph neural networks to model spatial tumor-immune cell interactions from multiplex immunohistochemistry data, Bayesian hierarchical models to resolve subtype heterogeneity in multi-omics cohorts, and fluid dynamics simulations to assess upper airway functional outcomes post-surgery. Anticipated outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for immunotherapy response in HNCs, (2) open-source tools for integrative analysis of otolaryngologic imaging and genomic data, and (3) patient-specific biomechanical simulations to optimize surgical planning. The scale of these analyses—requiring parallel processing of >10 TB of imaging data, >100,000-cell single-cell datasets, and finite element modeling with 10^6-node meshes—necessitates dedicated HPC resources for memory-intensive tasks and GPU-accelerated model training. By bridging computational innovation with clinical translation, this work aims to establish a pipeline for data-driven decision-making in otolaryngology, ultimately improving survival and quality of life for patients with complex head and neck disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians to diagnose and provide medical and/or surgical therapy or prevention of diseases, allergies, neoplasms, deformities, disorders, and injuries of the ears, nose, sinuses, throat, respiratory and upper alimentary systems, face, jaws, and the other head and neck systems.

abstract: Pediatric radiology faces unique challenges in diagnostic imaging due to the dynamic anatomical and physiological changes across developmental stages, as well as the need to minimize radiation exposure while maximizing diagnostic accuracy. Current imaging protocols, often adapted from adult practices, may not optimize resolution, artifact reduction, or safety for pediatric populations. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing computational models to enhance image quality, automate anomaly detection, and simulate low-dose imaging protocols tailored to pediatric patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large datasets of pediatric imaging studies (MRI, CT, and ultrasound) and integrate multi-modal data, including patient-specific clinical variables. Advanced machine learning techniques, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs) for artifact correction and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for lesion detection, will be trained on curated datasets representing diverse age groups and pathologies. Monte Carlo simulations will model radiation dose distribution to identify protocols that reduce exposure without compromising diagnostic value. Computational demands include high-throughput processing of 3D/4D imaging data, iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale statistical validation. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for pediatric image enhancement, validated predictive models for early diagnosis of conditions like congenital anomalies and pediatric cancers, and evidence-based guidelines for dose reduction. By combining clinical expertise with computational innovation, this work aims to establish safer, more precise imaging standards for children while providing a scalable framework for pediatric radiomics research. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the project’s data-intensive workflows and achieving statistically robust results within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on all forms of diagnostic imaging as it pertains to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases in the newborn, infant, child, and adolescent.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating heterogeneous, high-dimensional health data—including structured electronic health records (EHRs), unstructured clinical notes, medical imaging metadata, and genomic datasets—into unified predictive models for clinical decision support. Current systems struggle to harmonize these disparate data types efficiently, limiting their utility in real-time clinical settings. The research proposes the development of a scalable, high-performance computing (HPC) framework to enable dynamic data fusion and multimodal machine learning (ML) for predicting patient-specific treatment risks and outcomes. Leveraging GPU-accelerated clusters, the project will optimize parallel processing pipelines for natural language processing (NLP) of clinical narratives, dimensionality reduction of imaging metadata, and federated learning across partitioned genomic datasets while maintaining compliance with HIPAA and GDPR standards. Key computational innovations include adaptive graph neural networks to model relationships between data modalities and a containerized workflow orchestrator to manage resource allocation across preprocessing, model training, and validation phases. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for federated multimodal health data integration and validated ML models demonstrating improved predictive accuracy (targeting ≥15% increase over single-modality baselines) in two clinical use cases: chemotherapy toxicity risk stratification and postoperative complication forecasting. By addressing computational bottlenecks in multimodal health data synthesis, this work aims to advance precision medicine applications while providing a template for HPC-driven innovation in health information systems infrastructure. The resource request emphasizes GPU node hours and distributed storage solutions to accommodate petabyte-scale datasets from three partner health networks.
cip_title: Health Information/ Medical Records Administration/ Administrator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage systems, processes, and facilities used to collect, store, secure, retrieve, analyze, and transmit medical records and other health information used by clinical professionals and health care organizations. Includes instruction in the principles and basic content of the biomedical and clinical sciences, information technology and applications, data and database management, clinical research methodologies, health information resources and systems, office management, legal requirements, and professional standards.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation and risk mitigation strategies in private security services, an area that remains underexplored in high-performance computing (HPC) applications despite its growing complexity. Private security operations must balance personnel deployment, technology integration, and threat response in rapidly evolving environments, yet existing decision-making models often rely on static heuristics or oversimplified risk assessments. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling, real-time data assimilation, and multi-objective optimization to simulate security scenarios at scale. The agent-based component will model interactions between security personnel, clients, and potential threats using behavioral parameters derived from anonymized industry data. Concurrently, live inputs from IoT-enabled security systems (e.g., surveillance feeds, access logs) will be processed through adaptive machine learning classifiers to detect emerging risk patterns. These components will feed into a parallelized optimization engine that evaluates millions of potential resource configurations against evolving constraints, including client service-level agreements, labor regulations, and cost parameters. The HPC infrastructure is critical for maintaining sub-minute decision latency while managing the combinatorial complexity of urban-scale security networks. Expected outcomes include a novel benchmarking toolkit for security service efficacy and an open-source optimization library tailored to the unique temporal and spatial demands of protective operations. By establishing quantitative metrics for security resource performance, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in an industry traditionally governed by qualitative standards, while demonstrating how computational social science methodologies can address operational challenges in non-STEM professional services.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and supervise services providing private security protection for people and property and related investigative and consulting functions. Includes instruction in security and loss prevention services, private security and investigation techniques, security technologies, personnel management, business operations, marketing, applicable law and regulations, and client relations.

abstract: Printing press operations are central to the dissemination of physical media in communication and journalism, yet optimizing press performance remains a persistent challenge. Current industry practices rely heavily on operator expertise and iterative trial-and-error adjustments to manage variables such as ink viscosity, roller pressure, substrate alignment, and drying times. These methods are time-intensive, resource-wasteful, and often fail to account for dynamic interactions between parameters. This project proposes a computational approach to model and simulate the nonlinear relationships governing print quality and operational efficiency in offset lithography, the most widely used commercial printing method. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to develop a multiphysics simulation framework integrating fluid dynamics (ink transfer), mechanical stress (plate-roller interactions), and thermal processes (drying stages). The model will be validated against empirical data from laboratory-scale press trials, with sensor measurements capturing real-time performance metrics. Machine learning techniques will then be applied to identify optimal parameter combinations under diverse material and environmental conditions. The computational intensity of coupling finite element analysis with iterative optimization algorithms necessitates parallelized computing architectures to achieve practical runtime scales. Expected outcomes include predictive models for defect minimization (e.g., mottling, misregistration), data-driven guidelines for press configuration, and a decision-support tool prototype for operators. By reducing setup waste and unplanned downtime, this research directly addresses sustainability and cost-efficiency priorities in print media industries. Furthermore, the project will generate open-access training modules integrating simulation workflows into printing press operator education, bridging computational literacy with traditional technical skills. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC-enabled modeling can advance non-STEM technical fields through targeted digital transformation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate, and maintain printing presses.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance our understanding of the formation and evolution of galaxy clusters and their role in cosmological structure formation. The research addresses critical gaps in modeling the interplay between dark matter, baryonic matter, and feedback mechanisms (e.g., active galactic nuclei, supernovae) that govern the thermodynamic and kinematic properties of the intracluster medium (ICM). Current simulations often oversimplify these multiscale processes, leading to discrepancies with observational data from missions like Chandra, XMM-Newton, and upcoming surveys. To resolve this, we propose a suite of high-resolution, cosmological hydrodynamical simulations using adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) to capture turbulence, shock dynamics, and non-equilibrium plasma effects in the ICM. The simulations will incorporate subgrid models for star formation, radiative cooling, and relativistic jet feedback, coupled with a novel radiation transfer module to self-consistently model the Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (SZ) effect and X-ray emission. These models require solving coupled equations of magnetohydrodynamics, gravity, and non-local radiation transport across spatial scales spanning six orders of magnitude. The computational demand is substantial: each simulation will utilize ~10,000 CPU cores for months, generating petabytes of data for statistical analysis of cluster scaling relations, turbulence spectra, and synthetic observables. Expected outcomes include resolving the “cooling flow” problem, quantifying biases in cluster mass estimates for cosmological surveys, and providing publicly accessible synthetic datasets to interpret next-generation CMB experiments (e.g., Simons Observatory, CMB-S4). By bridging numerical predictions and multiwavelength observations, this work will refine constraints on dark energy, neutrino masses, and primordial non-Gaussianity, directly supporting the cosmological objectives of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and Athena missions. The requested HPC allocation is critical to achieving the resolution and physical fidelity required for these transformative results.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical, observational, and numerical study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena of the universe on a large scale. Includes instruction in clusters of galaxies, the cosmic microwave background, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic and transboundary animal diseases pose significant threats to global food security, animal health, and public health systems. Current epidemiological models often lack the resolution to account for complex interactions between dynamic variables such as host-pathogen evolution, environmental drivers, and heterogeneous livestock production practices. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing high-resolution, multi-scale computational models to predict disease transmission risks and optimize intervention strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate geospatial data, genomic surveillance datasets, and animal movement networks to simulate disease spread across regional livestock populations. Agent-based models will capture individual animal interactions, while machine learning approaches will identify high-risk transmission pathways and forecast outbreak trajectories under varying climate and management scenarios. A key focus will be validating models against historical outbreak data for pathogens such as avian influenza and African swine fever, with additional applications to antimicrobial resistance patterns in foodborne pathogens. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for large-scale parameter sweeps, real-time data assimilation, and sensitivity analyses across billions of simulated interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for prioritizing surveillance efforts, evaluating vaccine deployment strategies, and informing livestock biosecurity policies. By quantifying the economic and public health impacts of preventive measures, this work will directly support evidence-based decision-making for veterinary public health practitioners. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling petabyte-scale datasets and achieving the spatiotemporal resolution required to model complex agro-ecological systems. This project aligns with national priorities for One Health preparedness while advancing computational methodologies in veterinary epidemiology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology, and Public Health
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the prevention and control of communicable animal diseases, diseases affecting humans, and prepares veterinarians to function as public health specialists. Includes instruction in animal epidemiology, biostatistics, food safety and quality assurance, food toxicology, zoonotic and infectious diseases, disease vectors and transference, production medicine, animal health, veterinary public health practice, and inspection and evaluation methods.

abstract: The management of acutely life-threatening conditions in veterinary patients, such as sepsis, trauma, or polytrauma-induced multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), remains a critical challenge due to the dynamic interplay of physiological, pathological, and treatment-related variables. Current clinical decision-making relies on static protocols, which often fail to account for individual patient heterogeneity, time-sensitive pathophysiological cascades, and complex drug interactions. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model disease progression, predict treatment responses, and optimize emergency interventions in critically ill animals.
