Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-scale data—including electronic health records, real-time vital sign streams, biomarker kinetics, and species-specific pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) parameters—into dynamic Bayesian networks and agent-based simulations. These models will simulate organ-level interactions under varying treatment scenarios, such as fluid resuscitation strategies, vasopressor dosing, and anticoagulant therapies, while accounting for interspecies physiological differences (e.g., canine vs. feline metabolic rates). Machine learning pipelines will analyze historical ICU datasets to identify early predictors of decompensation and train adaptive algorithms for personalized therapeutic recommendations. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing of high-dimensional datasets (>10 TB) and real-time Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic outcome forecasting. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for MODS mortality risk, optimized species-specific emergency protocols, and an open-source decision support tool for veterinary critical care units. By enabling rapid, data-driven adjustments to life-support interventions, this work aims to reduce preventable deaths in veterinary emergency medicine and establish a translational framework for computational critical care research. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the iterative model training, large-scale parameter sweeps, and real-time simulation demands inherent to this complex, systems-based approach.
cip_title: Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Medicine
cip_definition: Research focused on the emergency treatment and management of care for animals with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. May included related research in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures, and long-term care of critically diseased animals.

abstract: The craft brewing industry faces increasing challenges in optimizing resource allocation across complex, dynamic supply chains while maintaining sustainability and profitability. Traditional operational models often fail to account for the interplay of variables such as fluctuating ingredient quality, energy consumption patterns, real-time market demand shifts, and regulatory constraints. This project proposes to develop a computational decision-support system for brewery operations through the integration of multi-agent simulation, machine learning, and life cycle assessment methodologies. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to model entire production ecosystems at unprecedented resolution, incorporating real-time data streams from agricultural suppliers, production facilities, distribution networks, and retail endpoints. A hybrid architecture combining discrete event simulation with deep reinforcement learning will be implemented to identify optimal resource allocation strategies under uncertainty, while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess risk profiles across different operational scenarios. The computational framework will specifically address the unique constraints of small-to-medium breweries, including batch production variability, cold chain logistics, and circular economy opportunities for spent grain valorization. Expected outcomes include a novel optimization engine capable of recommending real-time adjustments to production schedules, inventory management, and energy utilization patterns while simultaneously calculating environmental impact metrics. This research aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven brewery operations management that balances economic viability with sustainability objectives, potentially reducing resource waste by 15-20% in modeled scenarios. The project will generate open-source tools for supply chain resilience analysis in craft beverage production and contribute methodological advances in computational sustainability for small-scale manufacturing systems. Results will be validated through partnerships with regional breweries, ensuring practical relevance while maintaining computational rigor.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market breweries and brewpubs. Includes instruction in brewing science, food services management, logistics and distribution, business networking, personnel management, business planning and capitalization, brewing industry operations, marketing, alcohol and liquor law and regulations, finance, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address a critical gap in the application of computational modeling to optimize environmentally sustainable practices in the funeral service industry, with a focus on reducing the carbon footprint of mortuary operations. While traditional mortuary science emphasizes chemical embalming and energy-intensive preservation techniques, emerging ecological concerns demand innovative approaches to balance cultural expectations, regulatory compliance, and environmental impact. The research problem centers on simulating decomposition dynamics under varying non-invasive preservation methods (e.g., organic biocides, cryogenic cooling) and their interactions with soil microbiomes in green burial contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model complex biochemical pathways, microbial community shifts, and heat transfer processes across multi-scale temporal and spatial dimensions. Agent-based models will simulate microbial activity in decomposition, coupled with finite element analysis of thermal gradients in shallow grave environments. Machine learning pipelines will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including historical burial records, soil chemistry profiles, and climate data, to predict optimal preservation protocols under region-specific ecological constraints. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to guide morticians in selecting methods that minimize formaldehyde use, reduce energy consumption, and align with conservation goals without compromising ethical or cultural standards. The computational tools developed will also inform policy discussions on sustainable cemetery management and provide open-access datasets for interdisciplinary collaboration between funeral service professionals, ecologists, and public health researchers. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project pioneers a data-driven paradigm shift in mortuary science, addressing 21st-century challenges at the intersection of tradition, technology, and environmental stewardship.
cip_title: Funeral Service and Mortuary Science, General.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals for careers in the funeral service industry and for licensure as funeral service directors or morticians.  Includes instruction in the basic elements of mortuary science and the business, counseling, and operational aspects of funeral service.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-accuracy geospatial data in land management, infrastructure development, and environmental monitoring necessitates advanced computational methods to process large-scale surveying datasets efficiently. Current workflows for analyzing terrestrial LiDAR, photogrammetric, and satellite-derived geospatial data face limitations in scalability and precision when handling complex terrain models, high-resolution point clouds, and real-time deformation monitoring. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize algorithms for automated error correction, 3D feature extraction, and geodetic network adjustment. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) parallel processing of multi-sensor LiDAR datasets to reduce registration and classification time while maintaining sub-centimeter accuracy; (2) GPU-accelerated least-squares adjustment of large geodetic networks with >10^6 observation equations; and (3) machine learning-driven simulation of terrain deformation patterns using finite element analysis integrated with real-time GNSS data streams. By implementing distributed computing frameworks such as Apache Spark for point cloud processing and CUDA-optimized solvers for matrix computations, the project aims to achieve a 10-20x speedup compared to conventional desktop-based workflows. Validation will involve benchmarking against ground truth data from established surveying projects and comparison with existing commercial software packages. The outcomes will advance the precision and scalability of geospatial data processing in surveying applications, directly benefiting infrastructure resilience planning and natural hazard mitigation efforts. Additionally, the developed open-source computational workflows will be disseminated to the surveying community, fostering collaboration and enabling resource-constrained organizations to leverage HPC capabilities. This work will also serve as a foundation for training surveying technology students in computational geomatics, bridging the gap between traditional surveying practices and modern high-performance computational methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the delineation, determination, planning and positioning of land tracts, land and water boundaries, land contours and features; and the preparation of related maps, charts and reports. Includes instruction in applied geodesy, computer graphics, photointerpretation, plane and geodetic surveying, mensuration, traversing, survey equipment operation and maintenance, instrument calibration, and basic cartography.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing real-time, multi-platform advertising campaigns in dynamic consumer environments. As digital advertising ecosystems become increasingly data-intensive—with high-dimensional user interaction data, cross-channel performance metrics, and real-time bidding systems—traditional analytical tools struggle to model the non-linear relationships between creative content, audience segmentation, and platform-specific engagement patterns. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and train machine learning models capable of simulating large-scale consumer response scenarios across social media, streaming services, and programmatic ad exchanges. Specifically, we will implement agent-based modeling frameworks to replicate heterogeneous audience behaviors, coupled with deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models) to predict cross-platform engagement cascades. The computational workflow will integrate real-world datasets spanning 50M+ anonymized user interactions, requiring distributed memory parallelism for feature engineering and GPU-accelerated training of multimodal neural networks. Key challenges include managing sparse, high-velocity data streams from programmatic auctions and resolving temporal synchronization issues in cross-channel attribution modeling. Outcomes will include an open-source framework for simulating advertising campaign performance under varying budget allocations and media mix scenarios, validated against industry partner datasets from connected TV and mobile advertising platforms. This work will advance academic understanding of computational advertising systems by quantifying latent synergies between creative elements and platform algorithms while providing practitioners with scalable tools for adaptive campaign optimization. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s memory-intensive consumer behavior simulations and enabling hyperparameter optimization across competing attribution models at industry-relevant scales.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creation, execution, transmission, and evaluation of commercial messages in various media intended to promote and sell products, services, and brands; and that prepares individuals to function as advertising assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in advertising theory, marketing strategy, advertising design and production methods, campaign methods and techniques, media management, related principles of business management, and applicable technical and equipment skills.

abstract: The dynamic interplay between macromolecular structure and energy transduction mechanisms underpins critical biological processes, yet the atomic-scale determinants of efficiency in these systems remain poorly understood. This project seeks to elucidate the structural dynamics and energy transfer pathways in multi-protein complexes central to biological electron transport, with a focus on oxidoreductase systems and photosynthetic assemblies. Current experimental techniques face limitations in resolving transient conformational states and ultrafast energy redistribution events, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose a multi-scale simulation strategy integrating all-atom molecular dynamics (MD), hybrid quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods, and free energy landscape sampling to characterize (1) the coupling between protein conformational fluctuations and electron/proton transfer kinetics, (2) the role of solvation dynamics and interfacial water networks in modulating redox potentials, and (3) the emergence of collective vibrational modes that facilitate long-range energy transduction. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve the necessary spatial and temporal resolution, particularly for systems exceeding 500,000 atoms and microsecond-scale simulations. The workflow leverages enhanced sampling techniques (metadynamics, replica exchange) to map rare-event transitions and machine learning-accelerated potential energy surfaces to bridge quantum and classical regimes. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how supramolecular architecture optimizes energy conversion efficiency, predictive models of mutagenic effects on redox cofactor energetics, and identification of key structural motifs governing charge transport fidelity. These results will advance fundamental understanding of biological energy transduction while informing the design of biohybrid catalytic systems and engineered enzymes for renewable energy applications. The computational framework developed will be disseminated as modular tools for simulating multi-scale biophysical processes, filling a critical gap in resources for studying emergent properties in supramolecular biomolecular systems.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the dynamics and interactions of macromolecules and other three-dimensional ultrastructures, the architecture of supramolecular structures, and energy transfer in biomolecular systems. Includes instruction in energy transduction, structural dynamics, mechanisms of electron and proton transfer in biological systems, bioinformatics, automated analysis, and specialized research techniques.

abstract: Hemodialysis treatment efficacy is critically dependent on the precise optimization of dialyzer performance, yet current clinical protocols rely on static, population-averaged parameters that inadequately account for patient-specific vascular dynamics and solute transport heterogeneity. This project proposes to develop a computational framework for real-time, personalized hemodialysis optimization by modeling the complex interplay between blood flow patterns, membrane permeability, and uremic toxin clearance at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement multiscale fluid-structure interaction models integrating patient-derived vascular geometry (from anonymized CT angiography datasets) with molecular dynamics simulations of middle-molecule transport across novel nanoporous dialyzer membranes. A machine learning pipeline will be trained on simulated and clinical data to identify dynamic parameter adjustments that maximize toxin clearance while minimizing albumin loss and hemodynamic instability risks. The computational workflow will employ finite element analysis via FEniCS for continuum-scale blood flow modeling, LAMMPS for nanoscale membrane interactions, and TensorFlow-based neural networks for adaptive treatment prediction. Expected outcomes include 1) predictive models correlating patient-specific vascular tortuosity with regional flow stagnation risks, 2) quantitative design criteria for next-generation dialyzers balancing hydraulic permeability with molecular selectivity, and 3) an open-source simulation toolkit enabling dialysis technicians to visualize treatment parameters in 3D and predict solute clearance efficiency. This interdisciplinary approach bridges clinical nephrology with computational engineering, addressing critical gaps in renal replacement therapy personalization while establishing novel quantitative methods for dialysis technology development. Successful implementation could reduce average treatment duration by 15-20% while improving middle-molecule clearance rates, directly impacting the 2.5 million patients globally dependent on hemodialysis for survival.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer hemodialysis treatments to patients with renal failure under the supervision of a nurse or physician. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, dialysis prescription interpretation, dialysate preparation, extracorporeal circuit and dialyzer set-up and maintenance, equipment monitoring, patient preparation, taking vital signs, documentation and communication, venipuncture and local anesthesia administration, emergency intervention, safety and sanitation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance pedagogical strategies for Teaching French as a Second or Foreign Language (TFSL) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze large-scale, multimodal learner interaction data. Current TFSL methods often rely on static curricula or generalized proficiency assessments, which inadequately address the dynamic, individualized challenges learners face in acquiring phonetics, syntax, and sociolinguistic competence. To address this gap, we propose computational modeling of longitudinal learner data—including speech recordings, written assignments, and real-time classroom interactions—to identify patterns in error propagation, fluency development, and cross-linguistic interference. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for HPC environments to transcribe and tag learner outputs, coupled with machine learning frameworks to simulate adaptive feedback mechanisms. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of terabyte-scale audio-visual datasets, training transformer-based models for error detection in learner French, and agent-based simulations of classroom discourse dynamics. Outcomes will include (1) predictive models correlating instructional interventions with proficiency gains, (2) an open-source toolkit for generating personalized pronunciation exercises based on learners’ first-language profiles, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for sequencing grammatical concepts in curricula. By quantifying previously qualitative aspects of language acquisition, this work aims to equip TFSL educators with data-driven frameworks to optimize lesson planning and feedback delivery. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the computational intensity of acoustic feature extraction, large-language model fine-tuning, and multivariate analysis across diverse learner populations. Results will directly inform teacher training programs and digital resource development, advancing precision in French language education while maintaining pedagogical responsiveness to individual learner needs.
cip_title: Teaching French as a Second or Foreign Language
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching French to students who are not proficient in French or who do not speak, read, or write French, and prepares individuals to serve as teachers and administrators.

abstract: The increasing complexity of decentralized information ecosystems—such as those in distributed sensor networks, community-driven data repositories, and hybrid human-AI decision-making frameworks—presents critical challenges in scalability, resilience, and adaptive resource allocation. Traditional centralized models fail to address the dynamic, heterogeneous interactions inherent in these systems, particularly when balancing real-time responsiveness with long-term data integrity. This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework to model and optimize emergent behaviors in such ecosystems, with a focus on scenarios where human and algorithmic agents co-evolve information-sharing protocols under resource constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement large-scale, multi-agent simulations that integrate stochastic network modeling, game-theoretic negotiation strategies, and lightweight machine learning architectures tailored for edge computing environments. These simulations will capture nonlinear feedback between localized decision-making and global system stability, incorporating real-world data from participatory sensing platforms and adaptive IoT networks. Key computational challenges include parallelizing asynchronous agent interactions, optimizing memory usage for sparse, evolving graph structures, and validating models against empirical cases of information cascade failures. The outcomes will yield (1) a scalable toolkit for simulating hybrid human-AI information ecosystems, (2) empirically grounded principles for designing fault-tolerant resource negotiation protocols, and (3) benchmarks for evaluating trade-offs between computational overhead and systemic resilience. This work bridges informatics, complexity science, and human-computer interaction, offering methodological advances for managing next-generation sociotechnical systems where adaptive resource allocation is critical to functionality. By prioritizing HPC-enabled exploration of emergent phenomena, the project addresses a gap in current informatics research, which often neglects the co-adaptive dynamics between heterogeneous agents in decentralized environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.

abstract: Motorsports engineering demands rapid iteration of high-performance vehicle designs to optimize speed, safety, and reliability under extreme conditions. Current physical prototyping and wind tunnel testing methods are resource-intensive, limiting the exploration of innovative geometries and materials. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling capabilities for aerodynamics, structural integrity, and thermal management in race vehicle components. The research will focus on developing multiphysics simulation frameworks integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and transient thermal modeling to analyze interactions between airflow, mechanical stress, and heat dissipation in real-world racing scenarios. Key challenges include resolving turbulent flow features around complex geometries at high Reynolds numbers, modeling composite material behavior under dynamic loads, and predicting thermal gradients in engine and braking systems. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parametric studies of wing configurations, underbody designs, and cooling solutions using high-fidelity meshes with adaptive refinement. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate design optimization by training surrogate models on simulation datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for drag reduction, downforce maximization, and fatigue life extension in critical components, with direct applications to electric motorsport platforms requiring novel thermal strategies. By reducing reliance on physical testing, this work aims to shorten design cycles by 30–40% while identifying performance gains equivalent to 2–3% lap time improvements in circuit racing conditions. The resource allocation will also support educational integration, providing Motorsports Engineering Technology students with hands-on experience in HPC-driven engineering workflows. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and open-source simulation templates to benefit smaller racing teams with limited computational infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the design, construction, and repair of vehicles used in racing and motorsports. Includes instruction in aerodynamics, design, vehicle dynamics, performance engines, fluid mechanics, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical engineering, and welding.

abstract: The increasing complexity of predicting drug toxicity and therapeutic potential demands advanced computational tools to integrate heterogeneous biological data and simulate dynamic interactions between xenobiotics and biological systems. Current approaches in pharmacological and toxicological research often lack the scalability to evaluate high-throughput chemical libraries or model multi-scale phenomena, such as tissue-specific biotransformation pathways and their systemic effects. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply computational models that bridge molecular-scale interactions (e.g., enzyme-substrate binding, reactive metabolite formation) with organ-level toxicity outcomes. Leveraging molecular dynamics simulations, we will characterize the binding dynamics of neurotoxicants and chemotherapeutic agents to targets such as ion channels and cytochrome P450 isoforms, incorporating solvent effects and membrane lipid interactions. Concurrently, machine learning models trained on toxicogenomics datasets will predict off-target effects and species-specific metabolic vulnerabilities. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale virtual screening of chemical libraries to identify compounds with optimal pharmacodynamic profiles and minimal hepatotoxic or immunotoxic risk. Key innovations include the integration of quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods to resolve electron transfer events in bioactivation pathways and the use of graph neural networks to map structure-toxicity relationships across diverse chemical classes. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for identifying high-risk xenobiotics during early drug development, (2) mechanistic insights into enzyme-mediated detoxification failures linked to genetic polymorphisms, and (3) open-access toxicity prediction tools validated against in vitro and clinical data. This work addresses critical gaps in computational toxicology by enabling high-resolution simulations of toxicokinetic processes and data-driven prioritization of safer therapeutic candidates, directly supporting translational goals in precision medicine and environmental health risk assessment.
cip_definition: A program with an integrated, combined approach to the study of pharmacological and toxicological issues in biology and the biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in topics such as solvents, xenobiotic metabolism, chemical toxicity, neurotoxicology, immunopharmacology, biotransformation, tissue culture and in vitro studies, biomolecular analysis, bioactivation and inactivation, enzyme regulation, chemoprevention and chemotherapy, industrial and chemical studies, radiation health, and bioinformatics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized biomechanical models for cartilage degeneration, a critical yet understudied factor in early-onset osteoarthritis. Current clinical models lack the resolution to map microstructural tissue changes influenced by genetic, metabolic, and mechanical factors, limiting early intervention strategies. To address this, we propose an interdisciplinary computational framework integrating multiscale finite element analysis (FEA) with machine learning (ML)-driven biomarker discovery. The project will process high-resolution MRI and proteomic datasets from a longitudinal cohort to simulate tissue-level stress distributions and degradation pathways under dynamic loading conditions. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulation of patient-specific joint geometries (10,000+ degrees of freedom per model) and iterative training of neural networks to identify predictive signatures of cartilage failure. Key innovations include coupling lattice Boltzmann methods for fluid-solid interactions in synovial environments with graph neural networks to model collagen fibril remodeling. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source platform for simulating cartilage aging and a validated set of computational biomarkers for preclinical osteoarthritis risk stratification. This work bridges biomechanics, computational biology, and precision medicine, offering a paradigm shift from reactive to predictive management of joint degeneration. Successful implementation could reduce diagnostic delays by 3-5 years in high-risk populations while informing targeted tissue-engineering solutions. The scale of data integration (15 TB multimodal inputs) and real-time parameter optimization required for clinical relevance necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve biologically feasible simulation timescales.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing large-scale supply chain networks under uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in strategic decision-making tools for business management. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the dynamic complexity of global supply chains, particularly when accounting for stochastic elements such as demand fluctuations, geopolitical disruptions, and supplier reliability. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrated approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning techniques to simulate multi-echelon supply chain interactions across diverse risk scenarios. HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of millions of simulation iterations, incorporating real-world data from industry partners on logistics costs, production capacities, and inventory policies. The computational framework will identify optimal resource allocation strategies that balance cost efficiency with operational resilience, while machine learning components will predict emergent vulnerabilities and recommend adaptive mitigation measures. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for evaluating trade-offs between lean operational practices and redundancy investments, validated through case studies in manufacturing and retail sectors. This research will advance strategic management theory by quantifying resilience trade-offs in network design and provide practitioners with evidence-based guidelines for building agile supply chains. The proposed work directly aligns with contemporary priorities in business administration, addressing critical gaps in computational methods for large-scale organizational decision-making under uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on developing and expanding the theory and research in regards to the planning, organizing, directing , and controlling the functions and processes of a firm or organization.

abstract: The increasing complexity of xenobiotic interactions in biological systems presents a critical challenge in predicting adverse drug reactions and environmental toxin effects. Traditional experimental approaches in pharmacology and toxicology are often limited by the cost, time, and ethical constraints of in vivo studies, while in vitro models fail to capture systemic metabolic dynamics. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models that simulate xenobiotic biotransformation pathways and their tissue-specific toxicological outcomes. The research will focus on cytochrome P450-mediated metabolism of novel therapeutics and industrial solvents, integrating enzyme kinetics, competitive inhibition dynamics, and organ-level compartmentalization. Molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to resolve atomic-scale interactions between xenobiotics and metabolic enzymes, while systems pharmacology models will predict metabolite accumulation and toxicity thresholds in hepatic, renal, and neuronal tissues. A key innovation involves machine learning-driven parameterization of these models using existing toxicity databases and novel in vitro biomarker data. The computational framework will be validated against clinical case studies of drug-induced hepatotoxicity and neurotoxicity. Successful implementation will enable predictive screening of drug candidates and chemical agents for off-target toxic effects, directly addressing the FDA's Critical Path Initiative for reducing late-stage clinical trial failures. The HPC resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of metabolic networks, enabling parallelized simulation of multiple xenobiotic exposure scenarios, and processing high-dimensional toxicogenomic datasets. Outcomes will include open-access predictive toxicity modules for rare metabolic phenotypes and a computational platform for evaluating chemical mixtures—a growing concern in environmental toxicology. This work bridges critical gaps between pharmacological efficacy assessments and toxicological risk prediction, advancing precision medicine while reducing reliance on animal testing.
cip_definition: A program with an integrated, combined approach to the study of pharmacological and toxicological issues in biology and the biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in topics such as solvents, xenobiotic metabolism, chemical toxicity, neurotoxicology, immunopharmacology, biotransformation, tissue culture and in vitro studies, biomolecular analysis, bioactivation and inactivation, enzyme regulation, chemoprevention and chemotherapy, industrial and chemical studies, radiation health, and bioinformatics.

abstract: Understanding the mechanisms underlying ecosystem resilience to environmental disturbances is a critical challenge in ecological research, particularly as anthropogenic pressures alter disturbance regimes globally. This project seeks to model how interactions between biotic communities and abiotic factors mediate ecosystem recovery following disturbances such as wildfires, invasive species colonization, and extreme climate events. We propose an agent-based modeling framework to simulate multi-species dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes, integrating empirical data on species traits, nutrient cycling, and environmental gradients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and execute spatially explicit simulations at ecologically relevant scales, capturing feedbacks between organismal behavior, resource availability, and landscape-level processes. The computational approach will leverage parallel processing to run ensemble simulations exploring how variation in disturbance intensity, species functional diversity, and historical legacies (e.g., prior adaptation to disturbance) influence recovery trajectories. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify thresholds in system states and predictors of irreversible regime shifts. Expected outcomes include (1) a mechanistic understanding of how co-evolved species interactions enhance or constrain resilience, (2) quantification of the role of dispersal limitation and habitat connectivity in post-disturbance succession, and (3) predictive frameworks for prioritizing conservation interventions in vulnerable ecosystems. By bridging theoretical ecology and applied resource management, this work will advance fundamental knowledge of complex system dynamics while providing actionable insights for biodiversity preservation under accelerating environmental change. The requested computing resources will enable iterative model refinement, sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces, and the synthesis of multi-terabyte outputs into generalized ecological principles.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions of small-scale biological systems, such as organisms, to each other, to complex and whole systems, and to the physical and other non-biological aspects of their environments. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry; landscape and/or marine/aquatic dynamics; decomposition; global and regional elemental budgets; biotic and abiotic regulation of nutrient cycles; ecophysiology; ecosystem resilience, disturbance, and succession; community and habitat dynamics; organismal interactions (co-evolution, competition, predation); paleoecology; and evolutionary ecology.

abstract: The increasing demand for safe and effective blood products, coupled with the complexity of donor-recipient immunological compatibility, presents critical challenges in transfusion medicine. Current blood bank protocols rely on serological testing and antigen matching, but these methods struggle to predict rare alloimmunization events or fully account for the dynamic biochemical changes in stored blood products. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating multi-omics data from stored red blood cell (RBC) units with immunological compatibility modeling to optimize transfusion outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets encompassing metabolomic profiles, RBC membrane proteomics, and donor-recipient human leukocyte antigen (HLA)/KIR genotype pairs, which collectively influence post-transfusion hemolysis and adverse immune responses. Machine learning models will be trained on retrospective clinical data to identify biomarkers of RBC storage lesion severity and predict alloimmunization risks in diverse patient populations. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model antigen-antibody interactions under varying storage conditions to refine compatibility assessments. The computational pipeline will also incorporate real-time sensor data from smart blood storage devices to dynamically adjust shelf-life predictions. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for personalized blood product selection, validated against prospective clinical cohorts, and a novel risk stratification system for transfusion-related complications. This work bridges gaps in hematology, immunology, and computational biology, offering a data-driven approach to enhance blood bank operations while addressing unmet needs in precision transfusion medicine. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce discard rates of expired units, mitigate adverse transfusion reactions, and establish scalable protocols for emerging cellular therapy products requiring similar storage and compatibility frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Nursing science faces growing demands to integrate large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, genomic profiles, and continuous physiological monitoring—to advance evidence-based practice and healthcare innovation. However, conventional computational tools are insufficient for analyzing these complex datasets in ways that address critical challenges in clinical decision-making, care optimization, and nursing administration. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these barriers through three synergistic objectives: (1) developing machine learning models to predict patient-specific risks of hospital-acquired infections using multi-modal clinical data, (2) simulating the impact of nursing staffing models on patient outcomes and workforce well-being under varying care scenarios, and (3) analyzing longitudinal genomic and symptom data to identify biomarkers associated with treatment responsiveness in chronic conditions. HPC capabilities will enable the processing of terabytes of structured and unstructured data, the deployment of deep neural networks for temporal pattern recognition in vital sign streams, and agent-based simulations of hospital workflows at unprecedented resolution. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for proactive clinical interventions, empirically grounded staffing recommendations to balance care quality and nurse retention, and mechanistic insights into patient subgroups benefiting from tailored interventions. By providing scalable infrastructure for data-intensive methodologies, this project will establish a foundation for precision nursing science, directly informing policy, education, and bedside practice. The results will be disseminated through open-source tools for nursing researchers, clinical decision support prototypes, and policy briefs aimed at healthcare administrators. This work underscores the transformative potential of HPC in addressing systemic challenges in nursing research, from molecular discovery to organizational dynamics, while fostering a computational paradigm shift in the field.
cip_definition: A research program that focuses on the study of advanced clinical practices, research methodologies, the administration of complex nursing services, and that prepares nurses to further the progress of nursing research through experimentation and clinical applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of consumer behavior in sustainable apparel markets, a niche interdisciplinary domain intersecting computational social science, behavioral economics, and textile lifecycle analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in marketing strategies for circular fashion systems, where traditional consumer segmentation models fail to account for dynamic, nonlinear interactions between cultural trends, environmental awareness, and supply chain transparency. Current approaches rely on static survey data and linear regression techniques, inadequately capturing the real-time feedback loops inherent in social media-driven purchasing decisions and post-purchase garment reuse behaviors. The proposed computational framework integrates agent-based modeling with transformer-based natural language processing to simulate emergent consumption patterns across heterogeneous demographic clusters. A custom multi-modal architecture will process structured transactional data (purchase histories, product returns) alongside unstructured data from resale platforms and sustainability-focused social media communities. High-throughput parameter sweeps will optimize model fidelity across global markets, requiring parallelized execution across GPU clusters to manage the combinatorial complexity of cultural, economic, and environmental variables. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support tool for adaptive marketing campaigns that dynamically align with regional textile waste reduction targets and evolving consumer ethics. This work will establish computational benchmarks for ethical consumption modeling while providing the apparel industry with scalable methods to evaluate marketing interventions in simulated circular economies. The resource-intensive nature of training domain-specific language models on fashion-related discourse and synchronizing them with behavioral simulation kernels necessitates HPC capabilities beyond typical consumer analytics infrastructure, positioning this project at the forefront of computational marketing innovation for sustainable textile systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on marketing research and management as applied to the products and services of the apparel and textile industries. Includes instruction in applicable principles of textile and apparel design and manufacturing, sales and distribution systems, domestic and international market research, profitability, consumer research, and the design and implementation of marketing campaigns.

abstract: Advancing nanostructured materials for energy technologies requires precise control over atomic-scale properties, but traditional experimental approaches are hindered by high costs and slow iteration cycles. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a multiscale computational framework integrating quantum mechanical simulations, molecular dynamics, and machine learning to predict and optimize materials for catalytic and energy storage applications. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale density functional theory (DFT) calculations, enabling the exploration of electronic structures and reaction pathways across diverse material compositions. Concurrently, coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations will model mesoscale phenomena, such as phase segregation and defect propagation, under operational conditions. Machine learning models, trained on simulation datasets, will accelerate property prediction and guide iterative design. The proposed computational workflow will generate actionable insights into structure-property relationships, reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel high-efficiency catalyst candidates and electrode materials, alongside the development of open-source tools for automated materials screening. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish a scalable paradigm for accelerating materials discovery, with potential applications in renewable energy systems and sustainable manufacturing. The requested computing resources will support the execution of parallelized simulations, management of multi-terabyte datasets, and validation of hybrid algorithms, ensuring robust statistical sampling across parameter spaces. Success in this endeavor will advance both applied materials science and computational methodology, bridging gaps between atomistic modeling and industrial-scale engineering challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical science technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Preventable patient harm remains a significant challenge in healthcare systems despite widespread adoption of safety protocols. Current approaches often lack the granularity to model complex, dynamic interactions between clinical workflows, human factors, and organizational systems that contribute to adverse events. This project proposes to develop a computational framework for simulating healthcare delivery processes and predicting safety risks using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate heterogeneous data sources—including electronic health records, sensor-derived staff movement patterns, and incident reporting systems—to construct multi-scale models of hospital operations. Agent-based modeling techniques will simulate clinician decision-making under varying workload conditions, while discrete-event simulations will map system-level bottlenecks that increase error likelihood. Machine learning approaches, particularly transformer-based architectures, will be applied to unstructured clinical notes for real-time identification of near-miss events that traditional reporting systems miss. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (10+ TB of longitudinal patient safety records), complexity of parallelized simulations across diverse clinical scenarios, and need for rapid retraining of predictive models as new protocols are implemented. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated risk prediction tool identifying high-probability failure points in medication administration pathways, (2) quantitative evidence for optimal staffing ratios in critical care units based on error propagation modeling, and (3) an open-source framework enabling hospitals to simulate proposed safety interventions before implementation. By combining systems thinking with computational precision, this work aims to advance proactive risk mitigation strategies that adapt to evolving healthcare environments, ultimately reducing preventable harm through data-driven resource allocation and protocol design. The requested HPC resources are essential for maintaining model fidelity across multi-institution datasets while ensuring practical computation times for iterative simulation-optimization cycles.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of transformative mechanisms and evidence-based protocols to reduce preventable patient harm and improve clinical outcomes. Includes instruction in healthcare quality, patient safety, research methods, program evaluation, epidemiology, legal and regulatory compliance, systems thinking, human factors engineering, and risk management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic data in clinical diagnostics poses significant challenges in identifying and interpreting pathogenic variants, particularly structural variants, non-coding mutations, and epigenetic modifications linked to genetic diseases. While advances in sequencing technologies have expanded the scope of detectable variants, existing computational pipelines lack the scalability and sensitivity required to analyze large, multi-modal datasets, resulting in unresolved cases of variant pathogenicity and missed diagnoses. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to integrate whole-genome sequencing, chromatin conformation capture (Hi-C), and methylation profiling data for improved variant prioritization and functional annotation. The computational approach will leverage graph-based genome representations to model structural variations and their spatial genomic context, combined with deep learning models trained on population-scale genomic datasets to predict variant impact. Custom algorithms will be designed to parallelize read alignment, variant calling, and epigenetic feature extraction across multi-terabyte datasets, optimized for GPU-accelerated nodes. The HPC infrastructure will also support the deployment of federated learning workflows to collaboratively train models on distributed clinical datasets while maintaining patient privacy. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for resolving variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in rare developmental disorders and cancer predisposition syndromes, with preliminary applications focused on reanalyzing unresolved cases from institutional cohorts. The project will further generate open-access tools for visualizing multi-omics interactions in structural variant hotspots, aiding clinical reporting. By enhancing the resolution of complex genomic rearrangements and their regulatory consequences, this work aims to increase diagnostic yield in clinical genetics and provide mechanistic insights into genotype-phenotype correlations, directly informing patient management and therapeutic targeting.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of geometric flows on Riemannian manifolds with singular metrics, a central topic in geometric analysis with implications for understanding the structure and evolution of complex geometric spaces. The research focuses on analyzing the long-time behavior of Ricci-DeTurck flows in settings where the initial metric admits controlled singularities or incomplete regions—a regime critical to conjectures in global analysis and manifold topology. While foundational work has established short-time existence results, the convergence properties and stability of such flows under perturbations remain unresolved, particularly in dimensions ≥4. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining adaptive finite element methods on simplicial complexes with spectral techniques to discretize and evolve the flow equations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multiscale curvature dynamics and manage the high-dimensional parameter spaces inherent to these problems. Simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated tensor operations for parallelized metric updates and employ scalable solvers for nonlinear parabolic PDE systems. Key challenges include maintaining numerical stability near singularities and preserving geometric invariants during discretization. The project will validate conjectures related to singularity formation in non-compact settings and test criteria for flow convergence proposed in recent theoretical work. Outcomes will provide quantitative insights into the regularity of geometric flows, inform analytic approaches to open problems in differential geometry, and yield open-source software tools for large-scale geometric PDE computation. Successful results may also clarify connections between flow-driven metrics and topological obstructions in manifold classification. This work requires sustained access to HPC clusters due to the O(10^5) core-hour demands of 3D/4D simulations and the need for iterative parameter sweeps to characterize flow dependence on initial data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties, measurements, and relationships pertaining to points, lines, angles, surfaces, and solids. Includes instruction in global analysis, differential geometry, Euclidian and Non-Euclidian geometry, set theory, manifolds, integral geometry, and applications to algebra and other topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation and operational efficiency in veterinary office management, a domain that combines administrative logistics with specialized healthcare delivery. Veterinary practices face unique challenges, including dynamic patient scheduling, inventory management for medical supplies, compliance with evolving regulatory requirements, and balancing client communication with clinical workflows. Traditional management tools often fail to account for the high variability and interdependencies inherent in these tasks, leading to inefficiencies that impact both cost and care quality. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to design agent-based simulations and predictive models that integrate real-world data streams—such as appointment patterns, staff availability, supply chain lead times, and seasonal demand fluctuations—into a unified decision-support system. Computational experiments will test adaptive scheduling algorithms, inventory optimization strategies under uncertainty, and scenario-based policy evaluations for regulatory compliance. By modeling clinic operations at scale, the project aims to identify systemic bottlenecks and generate actionable insights for improving throughput, reducing overhead, and enhancing service consistency. Outcomes will include open-source tools tailored for veterinary administration, validated against anonymized operational data from partner clinics. This work bridges a critical gap in non-science computational research by applying advanced modeling techniques to a specialized niche where administrative complexity intersects with animal healthcare priorities, ultimately supporting scalable solutions for an understudied yet vital sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a veterinary office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, veterinary care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic decision-making in complex supply chain networks under uncertainty, a critical problem in business operations management. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the interdependencies and real-time variability inherent in global supply chains, particularly when accounting for disruptions such as demand fluctuations, supplier delays, or geopolitical events. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), Monte Carlo simulations, and reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-echelon supply networks with 10,000+ node configurations, incorporating stochastic demand patterns and adaptive supplier behaviors. By parallelizing scenario testing across HPC clusters, we aim to reduce simulation time for enterprise-scale networks from weeks to hours while maintaining granular temporal resolution. The computational architecture will enable real-time sensitivity analyses to identify resilience thresholds and evaluate mitigation strategies for cascading failures. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel hybrid ABM-RL model for prescriptive supply chain optimization, (2) quantitative benchmarks for operational resilience metrics under various risk profiles, and (3) open-source tools enabling managers to simulate custom network configurations. This work will advance strategic decision-support systems in operations management by providing empirically grounded, computationally robust frameworks for balancing efficiency and risk mitigation. The requested HPC resources are essential given the combinatorial complexity of modeling concurrent adaptive agents, the need for massive parallelization in scenario testing, and the memory-intensive nature of training RL policies on high-dimensional state spaces. Results will directly inform curriculum development in supply chain analytics and quantitative risk management courses while providing transferable computational methods for adjacent challenges in resource allocation and organizational design.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, organize, direct, and control the functions and processes of a firm or organization. Includes instruction in management theory, human resources management and behavior, accounting and other quantitative methods, purchasing and logistics, organization and production, marketing, and business decision-making.

abstract: The increasing reliance on digital infrastructure in clinical environments has exposed critical vulnerabilities in the operational continuity of medical offices, particularly in managing hardware-software integration for diagnostic and administrative systems. Frequent system failures, often due to unanticipated incompatibilities between legacy medical devices and modern software updates, disrupt patient care workflows and introduce risks to data integrity. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing an adaptive compatibility framework (ACF) powered by machine learning to predict and mitigate interoperability failures in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze heterogeneous datasets spanning device performance logs, software version histories, and error reports from diverse clinical settings. Computational workflows will integrate graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex dependencies between hardware components and software dependencies, while reinforcement learning agents will simulate update scenarios to identify failure-prone configurations. The ACF will be validated against a multi-institutional corpus of de-identified medical office system data, with performance benchmarks comparing failure prediction accuracy and mitigation success rates against existing rule-based compatibility tools. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for proactive system maintenance, reducing unplanned downtime by an estimated 40–60% in test environments. By focusing on the intersection of clinical operations and computational systems engineering, this research bridges a gap in health sciences informatics, offering a specialized solution to infrastructure resilience that enhances both patient care delivery and operational efficiency. The project’s HPC requirements—including GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale simulation of device networks—are essential to address the temporal and structural complexity of real-world medical office ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply computer programming, troubleshooting, and information technology skills to the installation, maintenance, and upgrade of standard, customized, or proprietary medical software and associated hardware. Includes instruction in computer programming, systems analysis, networking, telecommunications, medical records and informatics software applications, information technology, systems administration, computer security, and applicable regulations and certifications or licenses.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of enforcing environmental regulations across vast and ecologically sensitive regions through the development of advanced computational models. Current methods for monitoring illegal activities such as poaching, illegal logging, and hazardous waste dumping often rely on reactive, resource-intensive patrols, which are insufficient for real-time intervention. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes an integrated approach combining high-resolution satellite imagery, IoT sensor networks, and historical enforcement data to predict environmental crime hotspots and optimize emergency response strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte geospatial datasets, training machine learning algorithms to recognize patterns of illicit activity, and simulating dynamic scenarios such as wildfire spread or pollutant dispersion in near-real time. Agent-based modeling will further assess the efficacy of various patrol routes and resource allocation strategies under different environmental conditions. The expected outcomes include predictive risk maps for proactive enforcement, optimized deployment algorithms for field personnel, and decision-support tools for rapid crisis management. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to transform environmental law enforcement from a reactive to a predictive paradigm, significantly enhancing the capacity to prevent ecological damage, protect public safety, and ensure compliance with natural resource legislation. The tools developed will provide agencies with scalable, data-driven solutions to safeguard ecosystems while efficiently utilizing limited personnel and logistical resources.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Law Enforcement and Protective Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to enforce natural resource and environmental protection regulations and laws; and to perform emergency duties to protect human life, property and natural resources, including fire prevention and control measures, and emergency and rescue procedures. Includes instruction in natural and physical sciences, natural resource management, outdoor field skills, firearms and outdoor equipment and vehicle operation, evidence collection and environmental sampling and monitoring, natural resource legislation, environmental compliance techniques, patrol procedures, investigation and report writing, interpersonal skills and crisis intervention, community liaison, public safety, public education, and public relations. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 03.0203.

abstract: Understanding the dynamic interactions within neural networks underlying complex behaviors remains a critical challenge in neuroscience. Current experimental techniques provide limited temporal or spatial resolution when capturing multi-scale neural activity, particularly in vivo during behaviorally relevant tasks. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model large-scale neural circuits and simulate their emergent dynamics under varying behavioral conditions. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement biologically realistic spiking neural network models that integrate experimental data from electrophysiology, calcium imaging, and behavioral assays. The models will incorporate region-specific connectivity patterns from rodent prefrontal-hippocampal circuits, which are implicated in spatial navigation and decision-making. Simulations will span multiple temporal scales, from millisecond-level synaptic events to minute-long behavioral epochs, requiring parallelized computation and optimized memory allocation. A key innovation involves coupling network simulations with machine learning pipelines to identify activity motifs predictive of behavioral outcomes. By systematically perturbing synaptic weights, neuromodulatory inputs, and network topology, we aim to uncover principles governing robustness and plasticity in memory-related circuits. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the computational load of parameter space exploration, which involves >10,000 iterations of network configurations per experimental condition. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how disruptions in long-range connectivity contribute to cognitive deficits observed in neuropsychiatric disorders. All models and analysis pipelines will be made publicly available to advance reproducibility in computational neuroscience. This work directly addresses the NIH’s emphasis on bridging cellular-level mechanisms with systems-level behavior, while providing a scalable computational resource for the broader neurobiology community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in neurobiology and neurosciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling multi-sectoral policy interventions in urban systems, where interdependencies between transportation, housing, and environmental policies generate nonlinear outcomes that are difficult to predict using conventional analytical tools. Traditional approaches often fail to capture the dynamic feedback loops between policy decisions, resource allocation, and population behavior at scale, limiting policymakers’ ability to design resilient, equitable interventions. To overcome this, we propose developing a high-resolution computational framework that integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with real-time urban data streams, enabling the simulation of heterogeneous population responses to policy combinations under varying socioeconomic and environmental conditions. The ABM will simulate decision-making processes of over 10 million agents—representing residents, businesses, and municipal entities—across a 10-year horizon, incorporating granular datasets on mobility patterns, housing affordability, and energy consumption. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parallelize simulations across hundreds of policy scenarios, optimize parameters via Bayesian calibration, and validate models against historical outcomes using spatially explicit difference-in-differences techniques. The computational workflow will leverage distributed memory architectures to manage memory-intensive tasks, such as processing terabyte-scale satellite imagery and IoT sensor data for real-time model initialization. Expected outcomes include a scalable policy testing platform capable of quantifying trade-offs between equity, fiscal sustainability, and environmental goals in urban planning. This tool will empower policymakers to identify intervention sequences that maximize synergies and mitigate unintended consequences, advancing evidence-based decision-making in complex governance contexts. The project will also generate open-source modules for simulating cross-sectoral policy impacts, filling a critical gap in public policy analysis methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues and decision processes. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, microeconomic analysis of policy issues, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dissemination of political and religious ideas across 17th-century Europe through the analysis of historical correspondence networks. Traditional historiography has often relied on fragmentary evidence to reconstruct intellectual exchanges, leading to gaps in understanding the mechanisms and scale of ideological diffusion. To address this, we propose a large-scale computational study leveraging network science and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The research will utilize digitized collections of letters, diaries, and pamphlets from archival repositories, comprising over 100,000 documents in multiple languages. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct dynamic network models to map communication pathways and apply community detection algorithms to identify influential nodes and clusters. NLP pipelines will be developed to extract thematic content and trace semantic shifts in key concepts over time. The computational demands of processing multilingual texts, coupled with the iterative simulation of network dynamics, necessitate parallelized data processing, large-scale storage, and rapid execution of complex algorithms. Expected outcomes include a granular reconstruction of transnational intellectual networks, quantitative assessments of cultural transmission rates, and methodological frameworks for integrating computational analysis with historical interpretation. By bridging archival research with data-driven approaches, this project aims to advance scholarly debates on early modern public spheres while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources in humanities research. The results will provide a model for scalable, interdisciplinary historical inquiry, offering insights into how ideas shaped sociopolitical transformations and enabling future studies to expand upon this computational infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in history, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Cardiovascular interventions require precise characterization of coronary hemodynamics to optimize clinical outcomes, yet current methods for predicting post-procedural blood flow dynamics remain limited by empirical models and static anatomical assessments. This project seeks to develop patient-specific computational models of coronary artery hemodynamics to guide percutaneous interventions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in resolution and clinical applicability. The research will integrate invasive angiography, intravascular imaging, and pressure-wire data from 150 patients undergoing coronary interventions into multiscale fluid-structure interaction models. These models will simulate transient blood flow, vessel wall mechanics, and stent deployment effects under physiologic and pathologic conditions. Key computational challenges include resolving turbulent flow in stenotic arteries, modeling viscoelastic arterial responses to balloon angioplasty, and predicting microvascular resistance changes after stent placement. HPC resources are essential to perform ensemble simulations across diverse anatomic geometries and boundary conditions, enabling probabilistic assessments of post-intervention fractional flow reserve (FFR) and wall shear stress gradients. Machine learning workflows will be deployed on HPC clusters to identify imaging-derived biomarkers predictive of computational FFR discordance with invasive measurements. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for real-time intervention planning, with simulations completing within clinically feasible timeframes (<2 hours). This work aims to reduce rates of stent failure and ischemia-driven revascularization by 15-20% compared to current angiography-guided practices. By bridging high-fidelity modeling with clinical interventional workflows, the project will establish a paradigm for computationally driven personalization of coronary revascularization strategies, directly addressing variability in patient responses to stent placement and pharmacotherapy. All models and datasets will be made available to the cardiovascular research community through an open-access portal, fostering broader innovation in interventional simulation technologies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of specialized imaging and other diagnostic techniques to evaluate blood flow and pressure in the coronary arteries and chambers of the heart, and in the use of technical procedures and medications to treat abnormalities that impair the function of the cardiovascular system.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across the British Commonwealth through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of shared and divergent cultural expression in postcolonial literature, media, and public archives from Commonwealth nations, which remain underexplored due to the scale and heterogeneity of materials. By integrating computational methods from the digital humanities, the project will process multilingual texts, digitized colonial records, and visual media (e.g., political cartoons, propaganda posters) to map transnational cultural flows and localized adaptations. Key computational approaches include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for semantic topic modeling across languages, computer vision techniques to classify visual motifs, and network analysis to trace the dissemination of narratives. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train machine learning models on multimodal data, and run parallelized analyses across temporal (19th–21st centuries) and geographic (Africa, South Asia, Caribbean) dimensions. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking cultural artifacts to sociopolitical contexts, quantitative frameworks for assessing hybrid identities in postcolonial societies, and visualizations of narrative resilience or erasure in decolonization movements. The project addresses a critical gap in Commonwealth Studies by systematizing cross-regional cultural analysis, offering methodological innovations for computational area studies. Results will inform policy dialogues on cultural heritage preservation and provide scalable tools for scholars working with multilingual, multimodal archives. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in processing speed, model complexity, and data integration, enabling interdisciplinary inquiry at unprecedented scope.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries comprising components of the historical British Empire and modern British Commonwealth, including migration patterns, shared sociocultural and political features and problems, and contemporary relations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize fairness-aware algorithmic decision-making in decentralized financial networks, addressing the tension between regulatory compliance, ethical AI principles, and operational efficiency in peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platforms. The core problem lies in the lack of scalable methods to simultaneously mitigate algorithmic bias across interconnected micro-lending decisions while preserving market liquidity and lender profitability—a challenge exacerbated by heterogeneous regulatory environments and evolving consumer protection standards. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture coupled with constrained Bayesian optimization to model dynamic interactions between borrowers, lenders, and regulatory agents across synthetic financial ecosystems. The computational approach will involve large-scale simulations of alternative fairness constraints (demographic parity, equal opportunity) under varying market conditions, processed through parallelized Monte Carlo tree search for equilibrium analysis. Key innovations include the integration of privacy-preserving federated learning techniques with explainable AI modules to audit decision pathways across decentralized ledgers. Expected outcomes include a novel metric space for quantifying fairness-efficiency tradeoffs in distributed financial systems, benchmark datasets for ethical AI validation in P2P markets, and adaptive policy templates for cross-jurisdictional compliance. The research directly contributes to emerging quantitative methods in ethical fintech governance, providing computational tools to align decentralized financial innovation with societal equity goals while maintaining market stability. Resource requirements focus on GPU-accelerated optimization workflows and distributed hyperparameter tuning at scale, necessitating dedicated HPC allocations for the iterative simulation of complex adaptive systems with >10^6 agent interactions per experimental condition.
cip_title: Management Sciences and Quantitative Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business quantitative methods and management science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational frameworks to optimize the security and reliability of distributed software systems in resource-constrained environments.
