Modern software applications increasingly rely on distributed architectures, such as edge computing and IoT networks, where traditional encryption protocols and quality assurance methods struggle to balance performance with security and accuracy. Existing tools for software testing and vulnerability detection often fail to account for the dynamic, heterogeneous nature of these environments, leading to inefficiencies and undetected risks. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate large-scale distributed systems, evaluate adaptive encryption strategies, and automate stress-testing workflows. The project will leverage parallel computing architectures to model diverse network topologies, simulate real-time data flows, and iteratively test cryptographic algorithms under variable load conditions. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify latent vulnerabilities in simulated software interactions and predict failure points. Key outcomes include an open-source toolkit for performance-optimized encryption in low-latency environments and a generative adversarial network (GAN)-based framework for automated, high-coverage software testing. By harnessing HPC resources, this work will enable rapid prototyping of security solutions tailored to emerging software paradigms while reducing computational overhead during testing phases. The resulting methodologies aim to advance best practices in secure software development for industries reliant on distributed systems, including healthcare, logistics, and smart infrastructure. This project directly aligns with the Computer Software Technology program’s focus on engineering principles for software evaluation, security, and customization, while excluding hardware-centric or non-software engineering domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in developing, implementing, and evaluating computer software and program applications. Includes instruction in computer programming, programming languages, databases, user interfaces, networking and warehousing, encryption and security, software testing and evaluation, and customization.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling the evolution of legal language within non-binding public policy frameworks, such as municipal guidelines, community-led governance charters, and open-access educational resources. While legal informatics has traditionally focused on statutory or case law, non-professional legal documents—created and iterated outside formal legislative processes—remain understudied despite their growing influence on civic engagement and grassroots policy development. The research employs computational text analysis and network modeling to trace semantic shifts, cross-document influence, and stakeholder interaction patterns within a corpus of 15,000+ non-professional legal texts collected from digital civic platforms, open-source repositories, and community archives. High-performance computing resources are critical to process the heterogeneous dataset, which includes unstructured text, revision histories, and metadata spanning 20 years. Natural language processing pipelines will be optimized to identify latent normative frameworks, while graph-based algorithms will map temporal and contextual dependencies between documents. A key innovation involves simulating decentralized policy adaptation using agent-based models to evaluate how informal legal systems respond to sociotechnical disruptions, such as digital platform migration or demographic change. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for quantifying the resilience and accessibility of non-professional legal ecosystems, as well as open-source tools to assist communities in drafting participatory governance documents. By bridging computational social science and legal studies, this work aims to advance scholarly understanding of bottom-up legal innovation while providing practical resources for civic organizations and educators focused on democratizing legal knowledge. The project’s computational demands—particularly in training transformer-based models on low-resource legal dialects and parallelizing large-scale network simulations—necessitate dedicated GPU nodes and high-memory infrastructure to achieve feasible runtime for iterative experimentation.
cip_definition: Any program in non-professional legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing crop resilience under climate variability. Agricultural productivity is increasingly threatened by shifting environmental conditions, including unpredictable droughts, heatwaves, and pathogen outbreaks. Traditional field-based breeding and phenotyping methods are slow and resource-intensive, limiting the pace of adaptation. To overcome this, we propose a computational approach integrating large-scale genomic datasets, climate projections, and machine learning to model genotype-environment interactions in staple crops such as maize and wheat. By analyzing terabyte-scale genomic sequences and historical yield data, we aim to identify genetic markers and regulatory pathways associated with stress tolerance. Parallelized genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and deep learning architectures will be deployed to predict phenotypic outcomes under simulated future climate scenarios. These models will enable rapid in silico testing of hypothetical breeding strategies, reducing reliance on physical trials. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the computational complexity of multi-layered neural networks, processing high-resolution climate datasets, and running iterative simulations across diverse genetic and environmental parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate genes for drought resistance, predictive frameworks for crop performance under biotic and abiotic stresses, and open-access tools for optimizing breeding programs. This work directly supports the development of climate-resilient agricultural systems, with implications for global food security and sustainable farming practices. By bridging computational genomics and agronomy, the project aligns with the program’s goal of solving practical agricultural problems through innovative research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and practice of agricultural research and production and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of practical agricultural problems. Includes instruction in basic animal, plant, and soil science; animal husbandry and plant cultivation; soil conservation; and agricultural operations such as farming, ranching, and agricultural business.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and molecular drivers of temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA), a debilitating condition affecting jaw function with poorly understood etiology. Current diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks for TMJ-OA remain limited due to gaps in modeling the complex interplay between mechanical stress, inflammatory signaling, and cartilage degradation in this highly specialized joint. We propose an integrative computational approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) of mandibular dynamics with agent-based modeling (ABM) of chondrocyte responses to simulated biomechanical and biochemical stimuli. High-resolution clinical imaging data (CBCT, MRI) from a retrospective cohort of 150 TMJ-OA patients will inform anatomically accurate FEA models to map strain distribution during mastication. Concurrently, single-cell RNA sequencing data from synovial fluid samples will parameterize ABMs simulating cytokine-mediated chondrocyte apoptosis and extracellular matrix remodeling. Multiscale integration of these models will be achieved through dynamic data coupling algorithms, enabling identification of critical stress thresholds and molecular pathways driving OA progression. HPC resources are essential for executing parallelized simulations across diverse biomechanical scenarios and scaling ABM populations to biologically relevant cell counts (10^6–10^7 agents). Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific occlusal loading patterns to molecular degradation signatures, potentially enabling early risk stratification and mechanistically targeted interventions. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational biomechanics, systems biology, and clinical dentistry, establishing a novel paradigm for investigating etiologically complex craniofacial disorders. Results will be disseminated through open-source model repositories and validation studies in collaborative in vitro mechanobiology platforms.
cip_title: Advanced/ Graduate Dentistry and Oral Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in advanced/graduate dentistry and oral sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Advances in oncology pharmacy require precise integration of pharmacogenomic, clinical, and molecular data to optimize therapeutic strategies for cancer patients. A critical barrier in this field is the computational complexity of modeling multi-omics datasets to predict patient-specific drug responses, particularly in heterogeneous malignancies. This project proposes the development of a scalable machine learning framework to analyze high-dimensional genomic, transcriptomic, and pharmacokinetic data, coupled with real-world clinical outcomes, to identify predictive biomarkers and personalize treatment regimens. The research will employ ensemble learning algorithms, neural networks, and Bayesian inference models to integrate sparse, multi-modal datasets while accounting for tumor evolution and drug resistance mechanisms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the iterative training of models on terabyte-scale datasets, perform parallelized molecular dynamics simulations of drug-target interactions, and conduct sensitivity analyses across diverse patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for chemotherapy and targeted therapy response in solid tumors, (2) identification of novel combinatorial drug targets to overcome resistance pathways, and (3) an open-source computational pipeline for adaptive therapy optimization. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid processing of whole-exome sequencing data from 2,000+ patients (retrospective cohort) and real-time analysis of prospective data from ongoing clinical trials. By leveraging distributed computing for large-scale parameter optimization and cross-validation, this work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks that currently limit clinical translation. The results will directly inform precision dosing protocols, enhance therapeutic efficacy, and minimize adverse drug events in oncology practice. This project bridges computational innovation with clinical pharmacy by providing a template for resource-efficient, data-driven decision support in cancer care.
cip_definition: Research focused on oncology pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize radiation dose efficiency and diagnostic image quality in radiologic imaging through advanced computational modeling, addressing a critical challenge in radiologic technology. While modern imaging systems prioritize patient safety, balancing minimal radiation exposure with clinically usable image quality remains complex, particularly for pediatric, geriatric, and high-body-mass-index patients. Current protocols rely on generalized exposure parameters, which may lead to unnecessary radiation or suboptimal diagnostic outcomes. To address this, we propose developing patient-specific imaging protocols using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate radiation-tissue interactions and image formation processes. Monte Carlo simulations will model X-ray photon transport across anatomically variable digital phantoms, incorporating tissue density, thickness, and metabolic variations derived from clinical CT datasets. Concurrently, deep learning architectures (3D convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks) will be trained on paired low-dose and diagnostic-quality images to predict noise reduction and artifact correction strategies. The HPC environment is essential for managing the computational intensity of Monte Carlo methods, which require ~10^8 particle histories per simulation, and for processing multi-terabyte imaging datasets during neural network training. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to customize tube voltage, current, and filtration settings based on patient anatomy and clinical indication, potentially reducing average radiation doses by 20-40% while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Validated models will be deployed as open-source tools for protocol optimization in clinical radiography systems. This work bridges computational physics and clinical practice, offering data-driven strategies to enhance radiation safety and imaging efficacy—key priorities for radiologic technologists and healthcare systems. Resource allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale image analysis, and the development of educational modules for training radiographers in protocol personalization techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical imaging services to patients and attending health care professionals. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, patient positioning, radiographic technique, radiation biology, safety and emergency procedures, equipment operation and maintenance, quality assurance, patient education, and medical imaging/radiologic services management.

abstract: The increasing demand for portable power equipment with enhanced efficiency, reduced emissions, and extended operational lifespans necessitates advanced research into small internal-combustion engine (ICE) systems. Current challenges in Small Engine Mechanics and Repair Technology stem from the inherent trade-offs between power output, fuel efficiency, and emissions in compact engine designs, compounded by the lack of high-resolution computational tools tailored to small-scale ICE dynamics. This project proposes a computational investigation to optimize combustion efficiency, thermal management, and mechanical wear in small engines using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will employ multi-physics simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion and airflow analysis, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress and thermal deformation modeling, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to identify design and operational optimizations. High-fidelity models will be validated against experimental data from engine test benches, focusing on common small-engine platforms such as those used in handheld landscaping equipment. The HPC environment is critical for resolving the transient, three-dimensional phenomena governing small-engine performance, which require parallel processing capabilities to handle large meshes, turbulent flow simulations, and iterative optimization workflows. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for combustion chamber geometry, fuel injection timing, and material selection to minimize carbon deposits and component fatigue. These results will directly inform repair protocols and retrofit solutions to extend engine service life while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. By bridging computational engineering with practical technician training, this project aims to advance sustainable small-engine technologies and provide a framework for integrating simulation-driven design into vocational education curricula, fostering innovation in a critical sector of the technical workforce.
cip_title: Small Engine Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain small internal-combustion engines used on portable power equipment such as lawnmowers, chain saws, rotary tillers, and snowmobiles.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical need for advanced computational resources in the documentation and analysis of Uralic languages, many of which are endangered or under-resourced. The research focuses on developing scalable methods for morphological parsing, syntactic annotation, and cross-dialectal comparison across languages such as Karelian, Sami, and their variants. Current approaches are hindered by the agglutinative nature of these languages and the scarcity of digitized corpora, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to train deep learning models on fragmented data and perform large-scale simulations of language evolution. The computational workflow involves the deployment of transformer-based architectures for unsupervised morphological segmentation, coupled with phylogenetic algorithms to model historical relationships. Additionally, phonetic analysis of archival recordings will leverage parallel processing to automate the alignment of acoustic features with linguistic annotations. The utilization of HPC resources will enable the processing of terabytes of text and audio data, significantly reducing the time required for corpus construction and model training. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access annotated corpora, machine learning tools tailored for Uralic languages, and empirical insights into dialectal variation and language contact phenomena. These resources will directly support revitalization efforts and provide foundational infrastructure for computational linguistics research in Uralic studies. By integrating philological expertise with advanced computational techniques, this project aims to bridge methodological gaps in minority language analysis while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in humanities scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Uralic languages, including, but not limited to, Finnish, Estonian, Karelian, and Sami. Includes instruction in philology; oral and written literatures; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The management of fine and studio arts organizations faces growing challenges in balancing operational sustainability with equitable access to cultural resources. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model complex variables, such as fluctuating community needs, dynamic funding landscapes, and evolving digital engagement metrics. This project proposes the development of a computational modeling platform to optimize resource allocation strategies for galleries, museums, and arts nonprofits. By integrating high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to analyze multi-source datasets—including visitor analytics, donor behavior patterns, and spatial utilization metrics—to simulate the long-term impacts of financial, curatorial, and outreach decisions. Computational methods will combine network analysis to map stakeholder relationships, Monte Carlo simulations to forecast budget scenarios under uncertainty, and computer vision algorithms to assess the relationship between exhibition design and audience retention. The scale of these datasets, which encompass geospatial, temporal, and visual information, necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated machine learning workflows only feasible through HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that enables arts administrators to visualize trade-offs between fiscal responsibility, programmatic scope, and community impact. This research advances the integration of computational social science methodologies into arts management, offering empirically grounded strategies to address systemic inequities in cultural resource distribution. Results will be disseminated through interactive workshops for arts professionals and a pilot implementation with three regional galleries, establishing a replicable model for data-informed stewardship in the visual arts sector.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage fine and studio art organizations, operations, and facilities. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; public relations and arts advocacy; arts law; and applications to specific arts activities such as galleries, museums, studios, foundations, and community organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for computationally intensive workflows in digital illustration, particularly in simulating complex material interactions and generating high-resolution, dynamic visual content. Current digital tools often lack the capacity to authentically replicate traditional media behaviors—such as pigment dispersion in watercolor, ink bleeding on textured surfaces, or the interplay of light in layered mixed-media compositions—at scales required for professional applications. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize physics-based simulation models that capture these phenomena with unprecedented fidelity. The research will employ a hybrid computational approach, integrating fluid dynamics solvers, discrete particle systems, and machine learning models trained on high-resolution scans of physical artworks. These simulations will account for variables such as substrate porosity, pigment viscosity, and environmental conditions, enabling real-time adjustments in virtual rendering pipelines. By parallelizing these processes across HPC clusters, we aim to reduce computation times for multi-layered, large-format illustrations (e.g., mural-sized digital works or interactive installations) from days to hours while maintaining 8K+ resolution standards. The outcomes will directly benefit illustration practice by preserving traditional artistic nuance in digital workflows and enabling novel hybrid techniques. Anticipated applications include customizable tools for fashion illustration textiles, dynamic map visualization systems, and adaptive exhibit design platforms. This work will also produce open-source simulation frameworks, fostering collaboration across visual arts and computational science communities. The requested resources are critical to handling the petascale datasets generated during model training and validation, ensuring that artistic intent remains central to technologically advanced illustration workflows.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decompression schedules and risk mitigation strategies for professional and technical divers operating in complex underwater environments. Current dive planning tools rely on simplified models of gas diffusion and tissue saturation, which inadequately account for dynamic variables such as water temperature shifts, exertion levels during salvage operations, or equipment failure scenarios. These limitations increase risks of decompression sickness and operational inefficiencies during extended or deep dives. To address this, we propose a high-fidelity simulation approach using parallelized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning to model gas exchange across heterogeneous tissue types under real-world diving conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps simulating nitrogen/helium absorption across 3D tissue meshes derived from medical imaging data, while integrating real-time sensor inputs from prototype dive computers. A reinforcement learning pipeline will train adaptive dive profile generators on these simulations, coupled with historical incident datasets from diver certification agencies. The resulting models will quantify tissue-specific microbubble formation risks under diverse operational constraints, enabling probabilistic safety thresholds for mixed-gas diving. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for generating personalized decompression schedules, a risk prediction dashboard for dive instructors, and optimized gas mixture recommendations for specialized tasks like underwater welding or archaeological recovery. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process multi-physics simulations and terabyte-scale sensor datasets, this work aims to establish a new standard for data-driven dive safety protocols while reducing computational barriers for resource-limited training programs. The project directly supports the program’s mission to advance technical diving education through evidence-based infrastructure, with potential applications in commercial, military, and research diving operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as professional deep-water or scuba divers, diving instructors, or diving support personnel. Includes instruction in the use of diving equipment and related specialized gear; diving safety procedures; operation and maintenance of underwater life-support systems; underwater communication systems; decompression systems; underwater salvage; exploration, rescue, and photography; and installation and fitting of underwater mechanical systems and their maintenance, repair or demolition.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized skin treatment protocols for clients undergoing advanced esthetic medical procedures, with a focus on post-operative care and chronic skin condition management. Current protocols rely on generalized guidelines that do not account for the complex interplay of individual skin biomechanics, biochemical responses to treatments, and environmental variables. The lack of predictive models for treatment efficacy and adverse reaction risks limits the ability of master estheticians to tailor interventions effectively. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-layered skin interactions under diverse therapeutic regimens, integrating heterogeneous datasets including hyperspectral skin imaging, longitudinal biometric sensor data, and molecular profiles of cosmetic formulations. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular responses to treatments such as chemical peels and lymphatic drainage, while finite element analysis will map stress distributions in healing tissues. Machine learning pipelines will identify predictive biomarkers for treatment outcomes using federated learning approaches to preserve client privacy across collaborating clinics. The computational platform will be validated against clinical outcomes from 200 anonymized case studies of post-operative patients. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies probabilistic treatment success rates for individual clients and generates adaptive treatment timelines. This project represents the first systematic effort to apply computational modeling at the intersection of dermatophysiology, cosmetic chemistry, and clinical esthetics, with potential to reduce trial-and-error practices, minimize adverse events, and establish data-driven standards in an emerging computational esthetics paradigm. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter sweeps, and secure data aggregation infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and body with advanced chemical and cosmetic preparations and esthetic medical treatments, and to function as licensed master or medical estheticians in dermatologists' and plastic surgeons' offices as well as in salons and spas. Includes instruction in advanced anatomy and physiology, skin properties and disorders, sanitation and infection control, advanced facial treatments, spa body treatments, advanced extractions, corrective makeup, chemical peels, microdermabrasion, lymphatic drainage and advanced massage techniques, pre- and post-operative esthetic skin care, client/patient evaluation and care, applicable laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems operate under extreme thermal, mechanical, and aerodynamic conditions, necessitating precise maintenance and performance optimization to ensure safety, efficiency, and regulatory compliance. Traditional empirical approaches to diagnosing engine wear, predicting component failure, and optimizing fuel systems are limited in scalability and resolution, particularly for next-generation hybrid-electric propulsion architectures and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) compatibility. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate multiphysics interactions within aircraft powerplants, enabling predictive maintenance and performance enhancements. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct large-scale simulations of turbine blade thermal stress, combustion dynamics in SAF-adapted engines, and fluid-structure interactions in variable-pitch propeller systems. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) will be coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on historical engine telemetry and maintenance records to identify failure precursors and optimize inspection intervals. Key challenges include resolving turbulent combustion phenomena at microscales, modeling cyclic fatigue in composite materials, and validating simulations against experimental data from engine testbeds. The outcomes will include predictive maintenance frameworks to reduce unplanned downtime, computational tools for evaluating novel fuel injector designs, and datasets correlating operational parameters with component degradation rates. By integrating HPC-driven insights into technician training protocols, this work aims to bridge the gap between advanced computational research and practical aircraft maintenance workflows, directly supporting the aviation industry’s transition toward safer, more efficient, and environmentally adaptive propulsion systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of ballet through computational modeling of complex movement patterns and choreographic innovation. Ballet training and performance involve intricate biomechanical interactions and artistic decisions that are challenging to analyze at scale using traditional methods. The research problem centers on quantifying the relationship between biomechanical efficiency, stylistic fidelity, and creative expression in classical and contemporary ballet. To address this, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to simulate dancer kinematics, ensemble synchronization, and choreographic evolution. Motion capture data from professional ballet performances will inform model parameters, while Laban Movement Analysis (LNA) frameworks will be encoded into the simulations to evaluate stylistic adherence. The HPC environment is critical for processing terabytes of motion data, running high-fidelity biomechanical simulations, and training deep learning models that predict optimal movement sequences under artistic constraints. Expected outcomes include a computational toolkit for choreographers to prototype ensemble configurations in virtual environments, reducing rehearsal trial-and-error. Additionally, the models will identify movement patterns that minimize injury risk without compromising artistic intent, offering evidence-based insights for ballet pedagogy. This interdisciplinary work bridges performing arts and computational science, establishing a framework to preserve choreographic heritage while enabling data-driven innovation in ballet. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with dance scholarship, the project aims to transform how ballet techniques are taught, performed, and creatively expanded.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to express ideals and feelings through interpretation of classical dance choreography. Includes instruction in ballet exercise, solo and ensemble dance, history of ballet, ballet choreography, Laban notation, ballet technique, and interpretations of specific styles and schools.

abstract: This research investigates the dynamic interplay between language contact, digital communication practices, and emergent cultural identities in multilingual online communities—a phenomenon underexplored in traditional sociolinguistics. The project addresses a critical gap in understanding how rapid, algorithm-mediated language mixing in digital spaces (e.g., social media platforms, gaming environments) influences the formation of hybrid linguistic norms and their role in shaping transnational identity networks. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose a mixed-methods framework combining computational discourse analysis, agent-based modeling, and network theory to analyze large-scale multilingual corpora spanning 10+ digital platforms. The computational approach involves training transformer-based models on code-switched text to identify syntactic and semantic innovation patterns, paired with graph-based simulations of language diffusion across user interaction networks. Key challenges include processing low-resource language varieties and modeling non-linear feedback loops between platform algorithms and user linguistic behavior. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel typology of digitally emergent contact languages, (2) quantitative frameworks for predicting identity-driven language shift in algorithmically structured environments, and (3) open-source tools for ethical multilingual data stewardship in community-driven research. By integrating linguistic anthropology with computational social science methods, this work advances theoretical models of language as a distributed cultural system while providing practical insights for developers and policymakers navigating the intersection of AI, cultural preservation, and digital community governance. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale text datasets, running parallelized natural language processing pipelines, and executing complex network simulations with >1 million agent nodes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the anthropological, historical, and sociological context of language with a particular emphasis on language use and its role in shaping cultural and social diversity. Includes instruction in applied linguistics, data management, field methods, language heritage, socialization, structure, linguistic analysis, linguistic theory, and multilingualism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven decision-making in sport and fitness administration through the development of a predictive analytics framework for optimizing talent identification, team performance, and injury risk mitigation. Current approaches to athlete evaluation and program management often rely on fragmented datasets, subjective assessments, or simplified statistical models that fail to integrate multi-modal inputs—such as biometric sensor data, psychometric profiles, environmental conditions, and historical performance metrics—into a unified computational architecture. The proposed research addresses this gap by constructing a machine learning pipeline capable of synthesizing heterogeneous data streams from wearable devices, video analytics platforms, and organizational databases to generate actionable insights for coaches, administrators, and facility managers. Computational workflows will employ ensemble learning techniques, agent-based modeling of team dynamics, and time-series analysis of physiological adaptations under varying training loads. A critical innovation involves simulating facility usage patterns and resource allocation scenarios through discrete-event modeling to balance athlete development objectives with operational constraints such as equipment availability, staff scheduling, and budgetary limitations. By deploying these models on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to achieve three outcomes: (1) real-time processing of athlete monitoring data streams during training cycles, (2) scalable optimization of facility resource distribution across competing user groups, and (3) probabilistic forecasting of injury risks based on biomechanical stressors and recovery interventions. The anticipated significance lies in establishing a replicable computational framework that bridges sport management theory with applied operational analytics, offering athletic organizations evidence-based strategies to enhance performance outcomes while maintaining duty-of-care standards. This work will contribute methodological advances to the emerging domain of computational sport administration, where large-scale data integration and predictive modeling remain underutilized relative to their potential impact on program sustainability and athlete welfare.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business, coaching and physical education principles to the organization, administration and management of athletic programs and teams, fitness/rehabilitation facilities and health clubs, sport recreation services, and related services. Includes instruction in program planning and development; business and financial management principles; sales, marketing and recruitment; event promotion, scheduling and management; facilities management; public relations; legal aspects of sports; and applicable health and safety standards.

abstract: The increasing complexity of histologic data, driven by high-resolution whole-slide imaging and multi-modal tissue analyses, presents challenges in efficiently correlating structural biomarkers with molecular and functional phenotypes. Current manual and semi-automated approaches in histotechnologic workflows struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including multiplex immunohistochemistry, spatial transcriptomics, and 3D electron microscopy reconstructions—limiting diagnostic precision and discovery of novel tissue-based disease signatures. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging deep learning and topological data analysis (TDA) to automate the identification of multiscale histologic patterns and their contextual relationships to subcellular omics data. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process petabytes of whole-slide images from neurodegenerative disease cohorts, paired with single-cell resolution proteomic and metabolic profiles. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will be trained to segment tissue regions of interest, while graph-based TDA methods will model spatial interactions between cellular clusters and extracellular matrix components. Parallelized workflows will align these outputs with mass spectrometry imaging datasets to construct probabilistic maps of disease progression biomarkers. The computational pipeline will incorporate quality control modules simulating histotechnologist decision-making patterns, ensuring clinical interpretability. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for integrative histologic-omics analysis, validated against gold-standard manual annotations, and novel insights into tissue-level heterogeneity in early-stage neurodegeneration. This work bridges gaps between traditional histotechnologic expertise and emerging computational pathology paradigms, offering scalable solutions for precision diagnostics while maintaining alignment with ethical standards for automated tissue analysis. Successful implementation will enhance the role of histotechnologists in data-driven biomarker discovery and provide a template for resource allocation in specialized health science computation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, at the request of physicians, researchers, and laboratory scientists, to identify tissue structures and cell components and relate these findings to physiological functions and to the detection and diagnosis of diseases and other abnormalities. Includes instruction in medical chemistry, histochemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, medical informatics, applied mathematics, electron microscopy, instrumentation, quality control procedures, data recording and analysis, laboratory administration, medical terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of legal reasoning in U.S. appellate court decisions, with a focus on identifying latent patterns in judicial argumentation that correlate with shifts in jurisprudential philosophy. The research addresses a critical gap in traditional legal scholarship, which often relies on manual case review or small-scale qualitative analysis, limiting the ability to systematically trace doctrinal developments across large temporal and jurisdictional scales. By applying natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to a corpus of over 10 million judicial opinions spanning 150 years, we aim to quantify how legal concepts such as "due process," "equal protection," and "original intent" have been semantically reinterpreted in response to sociopolitical changes. Computational methods will include transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned on legal text) for semantic similarity analysis, dynamic topic modeling to track concept migration across legal domains, and graph neural networks to map citation networks that reveal influential precedent shifts. The scale and complexity of the dataset—requiring parsing of non-standardized legal language, temporal alignment of concept trajectories, and cross-referential analysis across circuits—necessitate HPC infrastructure for distributed training, large-scale parallelism, and high-memory data processing. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for computational legal analysis, quantitative models of doctrinal evolution, and visualizations of pivotal inflection points in legal reasoning. This work will provide novel insights into the relationship between judicial language and legal change, with implications for legal education, appellate strategy, and interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of computational linguistics and jurisprudence. By establishing scalable methodologies for legal text analysis, the project aims to advance preparative training for law students in data-driven legal research while preserving interpretive rigor characteristic of traditional scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional study of law at the post-baccalaureate level.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and generating immersive, multidimensional soundscapes, addressing the challenge of real-time spatial audio manipulation in large-scale artistic installations. Current tools for spatial sound design struggle to integrate dynamic acoustic simulations with live performance inputs, limiting the complexity and adaptability of site-specific works. The proposed research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to model intricate sound diffusion patterns across variable physical environments while processing live sensor data from performers and audiences. Using a hybrid approach combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) acoustic simulations, machine learning-driven gesture recognition, and GPU-accelerated spatialization algorithms, the system will enable real-time interaction between computational sound synthesis and embodied human input. The project will leverage parallelized computing architectures to handle latency-critical tasks, including multichannel convolution reverberation for site-specific impulse responses and adaptive granular synthesis for stochastic sound textures. Outcomes will include an open-source software toolkit for artistic research, quantitative evaluations of computational efficiency in live spatial audio contexts, and two public installations demonstrating HPC-enabled sound art. By bridging the gap between physical acoustics, interactive systems, and computational creativity, this work aims to expand methodologies for sound as a cultural practice while establishing performance benchmarks for resource-intensive audio processing in artistic contexts. The requested computing resources are essential for scaling simulations beyond single-workstation capabilities, particularly when modeling large architectural spaces or processing high-density microphone/transducer arrays in real time.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on sound as a form of cultural expression, and its relationship to other disciplines such as computer programming, performance, and video. Includes instruction in acoustics; arranging, composing, and editing music; music theory; musicology; orchestration and scoring; and sound design.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum vortex networks in turbulent superfluid systems using advanced computational modeling. While classical turbulence is well-studied, the quantum regime—governed by discrete vortices in superfluids such as helium-4—remains poorly understood, particularly regarding energy transfer mechanisms and vortex entanglement at near-zero temperatures. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting how quantum turbulence evolves under varying boundary conditions and external perturbations, which has implications for fundamental physics and technologies leveraging quantum fluid dynamics. The computational approach involves solving the three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation using high-resolution spectral methods on adaptive meshes, enabling direct simulation of vortex interactions across multiple length scales. Large-scale parallelization via MPI will manage the high memory and processing demands of tracking thousands of vortices in realistic geometries. Statistical analyses of vortex reconnection rates, energy spectra, and topological entropy will quantify turbulence decay pathways. The simulations will integrate finite-temperature effects through stochastic extensions of the governing equations, a novel aspect requiring validation against experimental data. Successful execution of this work demands access to high-performance computing resources capable of sustaining petascale calculations over extended durations. Expected outcomes include predictive models of quantum turbulence dissipation, which could inform the design of ultra-sensitive rotation sensors and cryogenic systems. Additionally, the numerical frameworks developed will provide open-source tools for simulating complex quantum fluids, fostering interdisciplinary collaborations in low-temperature physics and nonlinear wave dynamics. This work bridges microscopic quantum behavior and macroscopic hydrodynamic phenomena, advancing foundational knowledge while addressing scalability challenges in quantum fluid simulations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing leadership decision-making processes in complex organizational environments. The research problem centers on the challenge of modeling dynamic, multi-level interactions within organizations—such as communication networks, resource allocation conflicts, and team coordination under uncertainty—where traditional analytical methods lack the scalability to capture nonlinear relationships and real-time feedback loops. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques, this study will simulate large-scale organizational ecosystems to identify patterns in leadership effectiveness, team resilience, and conflict escalation. Computational models will integrate empirical data from case studies, stakeholder surveys, and historical organizational performance metrics to parameterize agents representing employees, managers, and external partners. HPC resources are critical to iteratively run thousands of simulations across diverse scenarios, varying parameters such as decision-making hierarchies, communication latency, and stress-testing crisis response protocols. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to quantify how specific leadership styles—e.g., transformational versus transactional approaches—affect organizational adaptability and operational efficiency under resource constraints. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) methods will be applied to analyze internal communication datasets, enabling the identification of linguistic markers correlated with successful conflict mediation or collaboration breakdowns. The scalability of HPC will allow for unprecedented granularity in modeling organization-wide cascades of leadership decisions, providing actionable insights for designing training programs and policy guidelines. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this project aims to deliver tools for proactive organizational planning, ultimately enhancing the capacity of leaders to navigate volatility in business, non-profit, and cross-sector environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leadership skills that can be applied to a business, government, non-profit, or educational setting. Includes instruction in organizational planning, dynamics of leadership, finance, team building, conflict resolution and mediation, communication and other management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing spinal adjustment protocols in chiropractic care, focusing on biomechanical variability among patients. Chiropractic interventions rely heavily on manual techniques, where outcomes depend on practitioner skill and subjective patient feedback. However, the lack of personalized, data-driven models to predict spinal segment response to adjustment forces limits reproducibility and efficacy. This research aims to address this gap by integrating patient-specific biomechanical simulations with machine learning (ML) to model spinal dynamics under varying adjustment parameters. Using anonymized clinical data—including radiographic imaging, pre- and post-adjustment motion capture, and patient outcome records—we will construct finite element models (FEMs) of lumbar and cervical spinal segments. These FEMs will simulate tissue deformation, stress distribution, and joint kinematics during adjustments, calibrated against empirical data. Concurrently, an ML pipeline will analyze historical treatment datasets to identify correlations between adjustment parameters (e.g., force vector, velocity) and clinical outcomes. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across diverse anatomical geometries and for training ML models on high-dimensional datasets. The resulting framework will generate predictive insights into optimal adjustment strategies for specific patient subgroups, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches. Outcomes include open-source tools for simulating spinal adjustments and a recommendation system to assist chiropractic technicians in tailoring treatment plans. By bridging biomechanics, data science, and clinical practice, this work aims to enhance the precision of chiropractic care, improve patient outcomes, and elevate the technical capacity of chiropractic assistants in diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a chiropractor, to provide patient management, examination, and treatment services. Includes instruction in the principles and procedures of chiropractic, radiographic X-Ray procedures and techniques, X-Ray film analysis and media studies, orthopedic and neurological testing, clinical laboratory procedures, patient management and education, office administrative skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex optimization challenges in large-scale meeting and event planning, with a focus on dynamic resource allocation under uncertainty. The central problem lies in balancing real-time logistical demands—such as spatial layouts, attendee flow, vendor coordination, and emergency contingencies—with constraints like budget volatility, sustainability targets, and heterogeneous stakeholder preferences. Traditional event planning tools rely on static models ill-suited for scenarios requiring rapid recalibration, such as last-minute venue changes or crowd behavior anomalies. The project proposes a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, multi-objective optimization, and machine learning to simulate hyper-realistic event environments. By parameterizing variables including attendee demographics, vendor service times, and environmental factors (e.g., weather, acoustics), the models will generate adaptive resource allocation strategies under thousands of simulated scenarios. HPC resources are critical for running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risk propagation across interconnected systems (e.g., cascading delays in catering due to AV setup failures) and for training neural networks to predict optimal vendor negotiation thresholds. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit capable of real-time scenario testing, alongside novel metrics for quantifying resilience in event ecosystems. This work bridges computational social science, operations research, and hospitality management, offering methodological advances for transient, high-stakes organizational environments. Results will inform best practices for scalable event architectures in contexts ranging from hybrid conferences to disaster-response coordination hubs, with implications for reducing resource waste and improving attendee safety in crowded venues.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, budget, and implement conferences, meetings, and other special events in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in principles of meeting and event planning; special event management; budgets and finance; site selection; contracts, vendors, and negotiations; marketing and promotions; food and beverage management; audio-visual basics and meeting technology; and hospitality law.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the dynamic mechanisms underlying the structural regulation of a macromolecular enzyme complex central to cellular energy metabolism, with a focus on ATP synthase conformational transitions and their coupling to proton gradients. Despite extensive structural data, the real-time dynamics of subunit rearrangements and their kinetic coordination with proton flux remain poorly resolved, limiting our understanding of how mechanical energy is precisely converted to chemical synthesis. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational approach integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with Markov state modeling to map free energy landscapes governing rotary catalysis. All-atom MD simulations (using NAMD and CHARMM36) will model the F₀ motor domain embedded in a lipid bilayer, capturing proton-driven rotation at microsecond timescales. Enhanced sampling techniques will probe rare transitions in the F₁ catalytic head, while coarse-grained simulations will bridge local conformational changes with global complex rearrangements. These data will parameterize kinetic network models to predict rate-limiting steps under varying electrochemical conditions. The simulations demand high-performance computing resources due to system size (>500,000 atoms), explicit solvent requirements, and the need for extensive replica sampling to achieve statistical rigor. Expected outcomes include resolving protonation-dependent rotation intermediates, identifying critical residues driving mechanochemical coupling, and predicting mutation-induced dysregulation scenarios. This work will establish a computational framework for analyzing energy-transducing assemblies, with broader implications for understanding pathological mutations in mitochondrial disorders. By linking supramolecular mechanics to biochemical function, the project advances foundational knowledge in molecular enzymology while providing actionable insights for manipulating bioenergetic systems.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific relationship of physiological function to the structure and actions of macromolecules and supramolecular assemblies such as multienzyme complexes, membranes, and viruses. Includes instruction in the chemical mechanisms of regulation and catalysis, protein synthesis and other syntheses, and biomolecular chemical reactions.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of next-generation electromechanical systems through high-fidelity computational modeling and simulation. Electromechanical technologies increasingly rely on tightly integrated hardware-software interactions, particularly in applications such as smart manufacturing, autonomous robotics, and energy-efficient industrial systems. However, the multiphysics nature of these systems—spanning mechanical, electrical, thermal, and control domains—poses significant challenges in predicting dynamic behaviors, failure modes, and energy efficiency at scale. Traditional experimental approaches are cost-prohibitive and limited in resolving coupled phenomena, while existing computational tools struggle with the required spatiotemporal resolution for system-level optimization. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining finite element analysis, circuit simulation, and data-driven control algorithms. The research will focus on three interconnected thrusts: (1) developing multiscale models of electromechanical actuators under variable load and thermal conditions, (2) simulating real-time embedded control systems interfaced with physical component models, and (3) optimizing system performance through machine learning-enhanced parameter space exploration. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations across thousands of cores, leveraging GPU acceleration for matrix-intensive operations and adaptive meshing algorithms for dynamic resolution scaling. Expected outcomes include predictive models for wear reduction in servo-mechanical systems, validated control strategies for energy-constrained environments, and open-source tools for coupled electromechanical simulation. These results will directly inform the development of more reliable, efficient industrial automation systems while establishing a computational foundation for future research in adaptive electromechanical architectures. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the tera-scale datasets and complex solver interactions inherent to this multidisciplinary work.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electromechanical technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for real-time, high-fidelity visualization of atmospheric phenomena in climate science applications presents a critical computational challenge. Current rendering techniques struggle to balance physical accuracy with interactive performance when simulating dynamic, large-scale atmospheric processes such as cloud formation, aerosol scattering, and radiative transfer. This project proposes the development of a hybrid ray-tracing and lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) systems to address this gap. By integrating spectral radiative transfer models with GPU-accelerated fluid dynamics simulations, the framework aims to enable interactive exploration of multi-scale atmospheric interactions while maintaining physically grounded light transport calculations. The research will focus on parallelization strategies for irregular workloads inherent in adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) grids, leveraging distributed GPU memory architectures to manage data-intensive scattering computations. Key innovations include a wavelet-based compression scheme for heterogeneous participating media and a dynamic load-balancing algorithm tailored for hybrid CPU-GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include an open-source software toolkit for climate visualization, validated against satellite observational data and high-resolution climate models. This work will directly support interdisciplinary efforts in climate communication and education by providing scientists and policymakers with an intuitive platform to visualize complex feedback loops in atmospheric systems. The computational resource request targets 200,000 node-hours on a GPU-equipped cluster to benchmark scaling performance and simulate global-scale phenomena at sub-kilometer resolutions. Successful implementation will advance the state of the art in scientific visualization while establishing new methodologies for coupling physical simulations with real-time rendering in HPC environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the software, hardware, and mathematical tools used to represent, display, and manipulate topological, two-, and three-dimensional objects on a computer screen and that prepares individuals to function as computer graphics specialists. Includes instruction in graphics software and systems; digital multimedia; graphic design; graphics devices, processors, and standards; attributes and transformations; projections; surface identification and rendering; color theory and application; and applicable geometry and algorithms.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dynamic, multimodal information systems in healthcare necessitates novel approaches to optimize data integration and decision-making processes. This project addresses the challenge of modeling and simulating large-scale, heterogeneous clinical data flows to improve the responsiveness and accuracy of real-time clinical decision support systems (CDSS). Current systems struggle with latency and fragmentation due to siloed electronic medical records (EMRs), wearable device streams, and imaging databases, leading to suboptimal patient outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate information pathways across distributed healthcare networks, incorporating temporal, spatial, and semantic variability in data exchange. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling of institutional data-sharing behaviors with graph-theoretic analysis of information flow bottlenecks. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess millions of potential routing configurations under diverse clinical scenarios, while machine learning models—trained on synthetic and de-identified patient data—will predict optimal data aggregation strategies. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration over hyperparameters governing network topology, privacy constraints, and emergency prioritization protocols. Expected outcomes include a scalable informatics architecture that reduces CDSS latency by 40–60% in simulated trauma care workflows and identifies critical interoperability gaps in multi-hospital systems. This work will provide a foundation for designing adaptive, context-aware healthcare information systems that balance speed, accuracy, and regulatory requirements. The computational tools developed will be generalized to other high-stakes domains requiring real-time integration of distributed, sensitive data streams, such as disaster response coordination or precision public health initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.

abstract: Secondary school administrators face complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation, operational efficiency, and student outcomes amidst dynamic enrollment patterns, budgetary constraints, and evolving policy requirements. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model multi-variable scenarios or simulate long-term impacts of administrative strategies. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze district- and school-level administrative data, enabling evidence-based policy design for secondary school leadership. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will build agent-based models simulating student population dynamics, staff deployment patterns, and facility utilization across diverse urban and rural school systems. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical datasets—including enrollment trends, academic performance metrics, and community demographic shifts—to identify predictive relationships between resource allocation decisions and educational outcomes. Computational experiments will evaluate hypothetical interventions such as redistricting, extracurricular program expansion, and crisis response protocols under varying socioeconomic conditions. The scale of analysis requires parallel processing to manage high-dimensional data from 10+ partner school districts, encompassing 500,000+ student records and longitudinal operational metrics. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking specific administrative actions to graduation rates and equity indicators, (2) optimized decision-support tools for principals facing budget reallocation or infrastructure planning challenges, and (3) policy recommendations for scalable interventions that balance academic priorities with fiscal responsibility. By quantifying the systemic impacts of leadership decisions, this work advances computational approaches in education administration while directly addressing the National Educational Leadership Preparation (NELP) standards for data-driven school improvement. The requested HPC resources will enable previously infeasible large-scale simulations critical for generalizing findings across institutional contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the junior high, secondary, or senior high school (7-12) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of secondary schools. Includes instruction in secondary school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in optimizing healthcare delivery systems through advanced computational modeling of multi-institutional resource allocation strategies under dynamic public health conditions. A central challenge in health services administration is balancing cost-efficiency, equitable access, and operational resilience when coordinating resources across hospitals, clinics, and community care networks—particularly during demand surges such as infectious disease outbreaks or demographic shifts. Current decision-support tools often lack the granularity to model complex interdependencies between facility-level capacity constraints, workforce availability, supply chain logistics, and patient flow patterns at regional scales. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an agent-based simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model healthcare networks as adaptive systems. The computational approach will integrate real-world data from electronic health records, staffing databases, and supply inventories to create synthetic populations of patients and providers, with parameterized interactions informed by discrete-event simulation and machine learning techniques. Key innovations include parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate millions of scenario permutations for emergency preparedness planning and graph neural networks to predict cascading resource shortages. By simulating metropolitan-scale healthcare ecosystems under varying policy interventions (e.g., tiered referral protocols, mobile clinic deployments, predictive staffing models), this research will generate evidence-based strategies for mitigating systemic bottlenecks while maintaining care quality benchmarks. The anticipated outcomes include open-source optimization algorithms for bed allocation, predictive analytics dashboards for regional health administrators, and policy briefs on computational modeling standards for healthcare resource planning. This work directly advances the Health Services Administration field by enabling data-driven governance of complex health systems while adhering to public health priorities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of policy analysis, public administration, business management, and communications to the planning and management of health services delivery systems in the public and private sectors, and prepares individuals to function as health services administrators and managers. Includes instruction in health systems planning, public health organization and management, pubic health policy formulation and analysis, finance, business and operations management, economics of health care, organizational and health communications, marketing, human resources management, and public health law and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an adaptive decision-support framework for next-generation military Command and Control (C2) systems using high-performance computing (HPC) to address the challenge of real-time resource allocation in contested, data-dense operational environments. Modern C2 systems must integrate heterogeneous data streams—including sensor feeds, intelligence reports, and logistics updates—amidst adversarial cyber-physical disruptions, yet existing architectures struggle with latency, scalability, and uncertainty quantification. The proposed work combines computational game theory, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), and probabilistic graph analytics to model dynamic threat landscapes and optimize resource distribution across distributed C2 nodes. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of multi-domain operational scenarios (e.g., electronic warfare, unmanned system coordination) through parallelized Monte Carlo methods and ensemble machine learning pipelines. Key innovations include a hybrid quantum-inspired optimization layer for rapid contingency planning and a federated learning framework to preserve data security across coalition networks. Expected outcomes include a prototype software toolkit validated against synthetically generated combat scenarios mirroring peer-state capabilities, with performance benchmarks targeting a 40% reduction in decision latency and 30% improvement in resource utilization efficiency under degraded communications. This work directly supports the development of resilient, AI-augmented C2 systems capable of maintaining decision superiority in denied environments, with broader implications for adaptive logistics planning and autonomous system integration. By leveraging HPC to stress-test emergent behaviors in complex adversarial interactions, the project aims to establish computational best practices for balancing human oversight with machine autonomy in mission-critical applications.
cip_title: Command & Control (C3, C4I) Systems and Operations (MILITARY)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational use of information and decision systems in support of battlefield, theatre, and global strategic operations. Includes instruction in applied mathematics and statistics, computer systems, real-time analysis and decision systems, surveillance and navigation systems, information and communications technology, information security, situational awareness, system integration, joint operations and applications to specific command problems and services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of under-documented and typologically diverse languages, focusing on syntactic and morphological patterns in non-Indo-European language families. The research addresses a critical gap in linguistic scholarship: the limited computational infrastructure available for processing low-resource languages with complex agglutinative or polysynthetic structures, which are often excluded from mainstream natural language processing (NLP) tools due to data scarcity and morphological complexity. The study will utilize parallelized algorithms to analyze multilingual corpora from archival field recordings and written texts of three endangered languages from the Caucasus and Amazonian regions, each representing distinct typological features. Computational methods will include finite-state transducers for morphological segmentation, transformer-based models for cross-linguistic syntactic alignment, and graph-based clustering to identify diachronic shifts in dialectal variation. By deploying these workflows on HPC clusters, the project will overcome memory-intensive bottlenecks in training models on sparse data while enabling large-scale comparative analyses. Anticipated outcomes include the development of open-source tools for morphosyntactic annotation tailored to agglutinative systems, a diachronic dataset tracking phonetic erosion in vowel harmony systems, and probabilistic models quantifying the relationship between syntactic complexity and language contact. These results will provide novel insights into linguistic typology while directly supporting community-driven language preservation initiatives. The computational frameworks produced will be scalable to other underrepresented languages, bridging methodological disparities in linguistic research and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational linguistics and documentary fieldwork.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Foreign Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Gynecologic cancers exhibit significant molecular heterogeneity, contributing to variable treatment responses and the development of therapy resistance. Current clinical strategies often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for tumor evolution or patient-specific biomarkers. This project seeks to address these limitations by integrating multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics) with clinical outcomes to identify predictive signatures of therapeutic resistance and metastasis. The primary computational challenge lies in analyzing high-dimensional datasets spanning tumor sequencing, longitudinal imaging, and electronic health records from a cohort of 1,200 patients with ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process these data at scale, employing machine learning frameworks to model tumor dynamics and simulate treatment responses. Key computational steps include unsupervised clustering of molecular subtypes, Bayesian network inference of signaling pathways associated with resistance, and reinforcement learning to optimize personalized treatment sequences. The analysis will leverage containerized workflows for reproducibility, with GPU-accelerated nodes enabling rapid training of deep neural networks on whole-slide histopathology images. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model stratifying patients by risk of platinum-resistant recurrence in ovarian cancer, (2) dynamic biomarkers for early detection of endometrial cancer metastasis, and (3) an open-source computational pipeline for adaptive therapy design. By elucidating mechanisms of treatment failure, this work aims to shift clinical practice toward precision interventions, potentially improving progression-free survival rates. The requested HPC allocation will directly support data harmonization across 45 TB of multi-modal inputs, reduce model training times from weeks to days, and facilitate large-scale validation through synthetic cohort generation. This project bridges computational innovation with translational needs in gynecologic oncology, offering a template for resource-efficient, data-driven cancer care.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for consultation and comprehensive management of patients with gynecologic cancer, including those diagnostic and therapeutic procedures necessary for the total care of the patient with gynecologic cancer and resulting complications.

abstract: Pediatric cardiovascular diseases, particularly congenital heart defects (CHDs) and cardiomyopathies, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to anatomical variability, developmental dynamics, and limited predictive models for long-term outcomes. Current approaches often rely on generalized clinical criteria, which may inadequately address individual patient complexity. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific predictive models for postoperative outcomes and disease progression in pediatric cardiology.
