abstract: This project seeks to characterize how intratumoral metabolic stress in solid malignancies drives cellular adaptation and therapeutic resistance, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic tumor microenvironment interactions. A critical barrier in oncology lies in understanding how spatially heterogeneous nutrient gradients, hypoxia, and acidosis in tumors reprogram cancer cell physiology to promote survival despite chemotherapy, radiation, or targeted therapies. Current experimental models struggle to resolve the multiscale feedback between tissue-scale resource distribution and single-cell metabolic decision-making. To address this, we propose a spatially explicit computational framework integrating physiological data on tumor metabolism, ion transport, and stress-response pathways. Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate 3D tumor regions with varying glucose, oxygen, and proton concentrations, tracking individual cell states (proliferation, quiescence, apoptosis) influenced by local conditions and intercellular signaling. Differential equations will couple microenvironmental dynamics (e.g., lactate diffusion, pH buffering) to intracellular processes such as autophagy, mitochondrial plasticity, and proton pump activity. The HPC environment is essential for scaling simulations to biologically relevant tumor volumes (>10^6 cells) while resolving subcellular mechanisms. Models will be parameterized using in vitro data from nutrient-deprived cancer cell cultures and validated against murine xenograft histology. Expected outcomes include identifying metabolic dependencies that emerge under sustained stress, predicting microenvironmental niches most likely to harbor resistant cells, and testing computational interventions such as spatially fractionated radiation or pH-modulating drugs. This work will advance physiological oncology by mapping adaptive thresholds in cancer cell behavior, directly informing translational studies on microenvironment-targeted therapy combinations. The requested resources—parallelized simulations across 200+ cores and high-memory nodes for large-scale parameter optimization—are critical to achieving these aims.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of carcinogens; the onset of malignancy in cells, tissues, blood, and organs; the genetics of cancer; the anatomy and physiology of cancer cells; and the study of cancer behaviors and treatments. Includes instruction in gene expression; oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes; viral genes and cancer proliferation; regulation of signal transduction; cancer proteins; hormonal and growth factors in cancer cells; tumor promotion, progression, and metastasis; carcinogen receptors and metabolism; carcinogen ecology; immunological targeting; and studies of genetic, chemical, radiologic and other treatment therapies.

abstract: The development of advanced polymers with tailored functionalities requires precise control over molecular architecture and dynamic interactions, yet predicting how structural variations influence bulk properties remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to establish a multi-scale computational framework to model polymerization kinetics, chain conformation dynamics, and emergent material behaviors in stimuli-responsive polymer systems. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations coupled with kinetic Monte Carlo methods, we will investigate the self-assembly of zwitterionic block copolymers designed for pH-dependent micellization in aqueous environments. These simulations will parameterize bond formation/cleavage rates and segmental mobility using atomistic quantum mechanical calculations of transition states and non-covalent interactions. The proposed work requires high-performance computing resources to address three key challenges: (1) simulating polymerization processes across experimentally relevant timescales (µs–ms), (2) resolving mesoscale phase separation in multicomponent systems with >1 million particles, and (3) integrating machine learning potentials to accelerate free energy calculations for solvated ions near charged polymer interfaces. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking monomer sequence distributions to stimuli-responsive swelling ratios and ion transport selectivity. These insights will directly inform the synthesis of next-generation polymer membranes for electrochemical applications, with preliminary data guiding experimental collaborators in optimizing monomer feed ratios for targeted glass transition temperatures. The computational workflows developed will be shared as open-source tools to enable systematic design of functional polymers, reducing trial-and-error experimentation in industrial formulations. By leveraging GPU-accelerated MD codes and scalable optimization algorithms, this project aims to advance fundamental understanding of polymerization-structure-property relationships while addressing scalability bottlenecks in computational polymer chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of synthesized macromolecules and their interactions with other substances. Includes instruction in molecular bonding theory, polymerization, properties and behavior of unstable compounds, the development of tailored polymers, transition phenomena, and applications to specific industrial problems and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on early identification of reading difficulties through computational modeling of language and literacy development in young learners. The research problem centers on the challenge of analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets—including speech recordings, eye-tracking metrics, and written responses—to detect subtle patterns predictive of atypical reading trajectories. Traditional statistical methods are insufficient for modeling the dynamic interactions between phonological, syntactic, and semantic development at scale, particularly when integrating longitudinal data from diverse learner populations. To address this, the project will employ machine learning techniques, including transformer-based neural networks and graph analytics, to process multimodal datasets from 5,000+ K-3 students. These models will simulate language acquisition pathways and identify critical inflection points where targeted interventions could mitigate reading challenges. Computational demands include training deep learning architectures on longitudinal speech-text paired data, clustering atypical vs. typical literacy profiles using unsupervised methods, and validating models against clinical diagnostic benchmarks. HPC resources are essential for managing distributed training across GPU nodes, processing terabytes of audio-visual data, and running iterative simulations to test hypothetical intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source tools for automated analysis of literacy behaviors, (2) evidence-based thresholds for early risk detection, and (3) a framework for personalizing phonics-based instruction based on computational profiles. By scaling the analysis of micro-level language interactions, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical models of reading development and classroom practices, ultimately equipping educators with data-driven strategies to address literacy disparities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach language and literacy subject matter areas, at various educational levels. Includes instruction in language development, typical and atypical reading development, and diagnosing reading difficulties.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how socio-cognitive, instructional, and socio-cultural factors interact to shape learning outcomes in technology-enhanced collaborative learning environments. A key challenge in learning sciences is modeling the dynamic, multilevel nature of these interactions—ranging from individual cognitive processes and peer discourse patterns to broader classroom-level cultural dynamics—using traditional analytical methods. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), natural language processing (NLP), and multilevel statistical analyses to simulate and analyze how micro-level cognitive and social behaviors propagate into macro-level learning outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing large-scale multimodal datasets (including discourse logs, eye-tracking, and assessment metrics from 15,000+ learners) and running parallelized simulations of virtual learning environments. The ABM component will parameterize agents with empirically derived cognitive profiles and interaction rules, enabling simulations of diverse pedagogical scenarios. NLP pipelines will extract linguistic and socio-metacognitive features from student discourse, while hierarchical Bayesian models will quantify cross-level effects. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, we aim to overcome scalability barriers in modeling complex educational systems. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying critical leverage points where instructional interventions amplify equitable learning outcomes, (2) generating evidence-based principles for culturally responsive adaptive learning systems, and (3) advancing methodological infrastructure for computationally intensive learning analytics. This work will provide novel insights into the emergence of collective efficacy in STEM learning communities, with implications for designing inclusive, data-informed pedagogical practices. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source resources to support reproducibility in education research.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the multiple aspects of learning in different environments, including specific aspects of the content to be mastered, cognitive aspects of the student, the instructional environment and materials, the preparation and activities of the instructor, socio-cultural and linguistic components, and assessment outcomes. Includes instruction in the social, organizational, and cultural dynamics of learning; learning and cognition; learning strategies; educational psychology; educational testing and measurement; instructional design and technology; and statistical design of educational research.

abstract: Molecular genetic diagnostics face growing challenges in integrating multi-omics data, resolving complex structural variants, and detecting low-frequency pathogenic variants in heterogeneous samples. Current clinical pipelines often lack the computational scalability to process large genomic datasets efficiently, hindering diagnostic accuracy for Mendelian disorders, malignancies, and infections. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational frameworks for identifying clinically actionable variants, elucidating disease mechanisms, and improving diagnostic workflows. The research will leverage whole-genome sequencing, RNA-seq, and methylation data from patients with unresolved diagnoses, focusing on three aims: (1) optimizing deep learning models for variant prioritization in non-coding regions and repetitive sequences, (2) implementing graph-based genome algorithms to resolve structural rearrangements in developmental disorders, and (3) simulating host-pathogen genomic interactions to improve detection of low-abundance pathogens in immunocompromised patients. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of these tasks, including comparative analyses across 50,000+ clinical genomes, iterative training of neural networks on GPU clusters, and real-time hybrid assembly of metagenomic sequencing data. Expected outcomes include validated computational pipelines for detecting mosaic variants below 5% allele frequency, a novel classifier for pathogenic non-coding variants in developmental disorders, and a cloud-compatible platform for rapid pathogen identification. These tools will address critical bottlenecks in molecular diagnostics, reduce turnaround times for complex cases, and provide insights into genotype-phenotype correlations across diverse populations. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with clinical validation, this work will advance precision diagnostics for rare genetic diseases and inform therapeutic strategies for malignancies with molecular heterogeneity. All pipelines and models will be made open-source to foster collaboration in clinical genomics research.
cip_definition: Research on how to make or confirm diagnoses of Mendelian genetic disorders, disorders of human development, infectious diseases and malignancies, and to assess the natural history of those disorders, using the principles, theory, and technologies of molecular biology and molecular genetics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for optimizing urban microclimates through architectural design. Urban heat islands, exacerbated by climate change and inefficient built environments, pose significant risks to public health, energy sustainability, and urban livability. Traditional design approaches lack the capacity to model complex interactions between architectural forms, material properties, and atmospheric dynamics at city scales, limiting the efficacy of microclimate mitigation strategies. This project addresses this gap by developing a scalable computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning, and parametric design optimization. High-resolution simulations will model airflow, solar radiation, and thermal exchange across diverse urban typologies, while machine learning algorithms will identify patterns and predict outcomes of design interventions. The HPC environment is critical for processing large geospatial datasets, running parallelized simulations, and iterating multi-objective optimization workflows that balance thermal comfort, energy efficiency, and spatial functionality. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating climate-responsive architectural configurations and urban layouts, validated through case studies in cities with varying climatic conditions. By enabling data-driven design of low-impact urban environments, this research aims to establish new methodologies at the intersection of architectural science, environmental modeling, and high-performance computing, with potential applications in municipal planning, building codes, and climate adaptation frameworks. The project’s computational demands necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes, large-memory systems, and distributed storage to manage terabyte-scale simulation outputs and iterative model training processes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and linguistic mechanisms underlying variability in second language (L2) developmental trajectories using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral data analysis. Despite advances in second language acquisition (SLA) research, significant gaps persist in understanding how individual differences in cognitive control, linguistic exposure, and instructional interventions interact to shape learning outcomes. Traditional methods, constrained by small datasets and limited computational capacity, struggle to capture the dynamic, nonlinear relationships between these factors. To address this, we propose a multidisciplinary approach integrating psycholinguistic theory, longitudinal learner corpora, and high-performance computing (HPC) to model L2 acquisition processes. The research will develop and train neural network models to simulate language learning under varying conditions of input quality, cognitive load, and pedagogical strategies. Parallelized processing will enable the analysis of multi-terabyte datasets comprising longitudinal speech, writing, and eye-tracking data from diverse L2 learners. Key computational tasks include natural language processing (NLP) for feature extraction from learner corpora, Bayesian hierarchical modeling to quantify individual differences, and reinforcement learning frameworks to optimize simulated instructional scenarios. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale and complexity of these analyses, particularly for training transformer-based models on unstructured linguistic data and running millions of parameter permutations in cognitive simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for predicting L2 proficiency trajectories based on learner profiles, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive language teaching methodologies, and (3) open-access tools for analyzing learner interactions in real-world educational contexts. By elucidating the computational principles of language acquisition, this work aims to advance SLA theory while providing practical insights for personalized language instruction. The project underscores the growing role of HPC in addressing non-uniform, high-dimensional research problems in the humanities and interdisciplinary social sciences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, and maintenance of second languages. Includes instruction in language pedagogy, use, analysis and processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of cultural discourse in digital media ecosystems, with a focus on identifying patterns in arts criticism and public engagement across visual, performing, and literary arts. Cultural journalism faces a critical challenge in contextualizing the rapid proliferation of digital content—from social media commentary to multimedia reviews—and its impact on cultural narratives. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of this data, limiting journalists’ ability to trace emergent trends, biases, or shifts in public perception. Our research addresses this gap by developing computational frameworks to analyze multimodal datasets (text, images, audio, and video) spanning platforms such as arts-focused blogs, streaming service reviews, and archival performance recordings. Using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision models, we will classify thematic clusters in arts criticism, map sentiment trajectories around specific cultural works, and detect correlations between media coverage and audience engagement metrics. The scale of data—terabytes of unstructured content across decades—requires distributed computing for parallelized model training, feature extraction, and network analysis. HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of transformer-based models fine-tuned on domain-specific corpora (e.g., theater reviews, music journalism) and GPU-accelerated processing of audiovisual materials. Outcomes will include open-access tools for automated cultural metadata generation, visualizations of discourse networks, and a public dashboard tracking real-time cultural trends. These resources aim to empower journalists and critics with data-driven insights, enhancing their capacity to interrogate cultural power dynamics and democratize access to nuanced arts analysis. By bridging computational methods and humanistic inquiry, this project redefines the tools available for critical cultural reporting in the digital age.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to be journalists who critically examine current culture as expressed through the visual and performing arts, design, film, music, radio, television, dance, theater, and written text. Includes instruction in arts criticism, art and entertainment reporting, cultural critique, investigative reporting, newspaper reporting, photojournalism, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic mechanisms of multi-domain enzymatic systems, with a focus on resolving atomic-level conformational changes that govern catalytic efficiency and allosteric regulation. A critical challenge in biochemistry is elucidating how large, multi-domain enzymes couple structural rearrangements to substrate binding and product release—processes occurring on micro- to millisecond timescales that are inaccessible to conventional experimental techniques. To address this, we propose an integrated computational approach combining classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enhanced sampling algorithms, and free energy calculations. These methods will model enzymatic systems comprising >200,000 atoms, including solvent and ion interactions, to capture functionally relevant transitions. HPC resources are essential to achieve the required sampling (multi-µs trajectories) and parallelize replica-exchange simulations across temperature or collective variable spaces. The study will focus on two undercharacterized ATP-dependent enzymes implicated in nucleotide metabolism, chosen for their structural complexity and unresolved mechanistic questions. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying key residues driving allosteric communication between domains, (2) quantifying energy landscapes for substrate binding and transition-state stabilization, and (3) generating testable hypotheses for collaborative experimental validation via mutagenesis and kinetic assays. By bridging gaps between static crystal structures and dynamic catalytic behavior, this work will advance fundamental understanding of enzyme design principles, with potential applications in rational protein engineering. The computational framework developed will also serve as a template for studying other large molecular machines in the BMB domain, fostering broader community capability in biomolecular simulation.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_title: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Molecular Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biochemistry, biophysics and molecular biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical pharmacogenomics aims to optimize drug therapies by integrating genomic variability with patient-specific factors, yet challenges persist in predicting multifactorial drug response due to the polygenic nature of traits, population diversity, and environmental interactions. Current models often lack scalability to handle high-dimensional genomic data alongside clinical variables, limiting their utility in real-world settings. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze large-scale pharmacogenomic datasets, including whole-genome sequences, electronic health records (EHRs), and longitudinal drug outcome data, to identify genetic and non-genetic predictors of drug efficacy and toxicity. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to model complex gene-drug-environment interactions. These models will be trained on multi-ethnic cohorts to address population biases and improve generalizability. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will be conducted to explore functional mechanisms of prioritized genetic variants affecting drug metabolism pathways (e.g., CYP450 isoforms). The computational pipeline will integrate genome-wide association studies (GWAS), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling, and real-world evidence from EHRs to enable patient stratification. HPC resources are critical for managing the terabytes of genomic data, parallelizing computationally intensive simulations, and optimizing hyperparameters for deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include predictive models for dose optimization, risk stratification tools for adverse drug reactions, and novel biomarkers for targeted therapies. These results will be validated through collaboration with clinical partners using retrospective EHR data and prospective pilot studies. By enhancing the precision of pharmacogenomic guidance, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error prescribing, mitigate adverse events, and advance equitable implementation of personalized medicine across diverse populations. The scalability of the framework will also provide a template for future studies integrating multi-omics data into clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Pharmacogenomics

abstract: This project seeks to characterize the role of mechanical stress in tumor microenvironments and its influence on cancer progression, with a focus on biomechanical interactions in epithelial tissues. While biochemical pathways in oncology are well studied, the mechanical forces exerted by extracellular matrix remodeling, interstitial fluid pressure, and cellular contractility remain poorly quantified in the context of tumorigenesis. We propose to develop multiscale computational models integrating tissue-level biomechanics with cellular responses to identify critical mechanical thresholds that trigger metastatic behavior. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate dynamic, three-dimensional environments using finite element analysis coupled with agent-based cellular models. These simulations will incorporate patient-derived data from breast and pancreatic cancer histology, including spatially resolved collagen fiber alignment and cellular strain measurements obtained via digital image correlation. The computational framework will parameterize variables such as shear stress, pressure gradients, and viscoelastic tissue properties, enabling predictive analyses of how localized mechanical perturbations alter tumor cell migration and proliferation. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into mechanically driven cancer invasion patterns and the identification of potential biomechanical biomarkers for clinical prognostication. By leveraging HPC capabilities to manage large-scale parameter sweeps and optimize model fidelity, this work will bridge gaps between biomechanical theory and oncological practice. Results will be disseminated through open-source model repositories and collaborations with experimentalists validating predictions in vitro. This resource allocation will directly support 4-6 graduate researchers in physiology and biomechanics while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies to decode mechanical contributors to cancer biology.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, anatomical, and mechanical structure and function of the mechanical aspects of biological systems. Includes courses in anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, mechanics, measurement and instrumentation, and research methods.

abstract: The study of non-equilibrium quantum systems presents fundamental challenges in understanding emergent phenomena under time-dependent perturbations. Current analytical methods struggle to resolve the complex interplay of entanglement growth, thermalization dynamics, and symmetry-breaking processes in driven many-body systems. This project seeks to address these challenges through large-scale numerical simulations of quantum spin chains and bosonic lattices subject to periodic driving and quenched disorder. The research will employ tensor network methods, specifically time-dependent variational principles with matrix product states, to simulate systems beyond the reach of exact diagonalization. A parallelized implementation of time-evolving block decimation (TEBD) algorithms will be optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters to handle entanglement entropy scaling and long-time evolution. Key objectives include characterizing the stability of many-body localized phases under high-frequency drives, quantifying the role of conservation laws in suppressing heating, and identifying metastable states in symmetry-protected topological systems. These simulations will directly inform ongoing experiments with ultracold atomic platforms and trapped ion quantum simulators. The requested high-performance computing resources are critical for achieving system sizes (>100 sites) and simulation timescales (>10^4 driving periods) necessary to extract robust thermodynamic-limit predictions. Expected outcomes include new phase diagrams for driven-disordered systems, universal scaling relations for prethermalization timescales, and optimized protocols for mitigating decoherence in near-term quantum devices. By bridging gaps between condensed matter theory and quantum simulation technologies, this work aims to advance predictive control over non-equilibrium quantum matter while developing open-source tools for the broader computational physics community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Diseases of the ear and temporal bone, such as Meniere’s disease, vestibular schwannomas, and otosclerosis, present significant clinical challenges due to the complex anatomy and physiological variability of the inner ear. Current treatment strategies often rely on generalized approaches, which may fail to account for patient-specific biomechanical, hydrodynamic, or neurophysiological factors that influence disease progression and therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific computational models of the inner ear and temporal bone, enabling precision medicine approaches for neurotological disorders. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating high-resolution finite element models of the cochlea, vestibular system, and surrounding structures to simulate biomechanical responses to surgical interventions or implantable devices, and (2) integrating fluid-structure interaction simulations with clinical imaging and electrophysiological data to predict functional outcomes of therapies for hearing and balance disorders. Computational workflows will utilize patient-derived CT/MRI data to construct anatomically accurate models, while machine learning algorithms will analyze multimodal datasets to identify biomarkers of disease progression. The scale and resolution required for these simulations—particularly the need to resolve micron-scale structures and millisecond-level dynamic processes—demand significant parallel processing capabilities and large-scale memory allocation, necessitating HPC resources. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive frameworks to optimize cochlear implant placement, improve vestibular prosthesis design, and personalize surgical planning for tumor resection. By bridging computational biomechanics with clinical neurotology, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven treatment personalization, reducing trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice. The resulting models and tools will be disseminated to the broader research community, fostering collaboration in computational otology and accelerating translational innovations for hearing and balance disorders.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat diseases of the ear and temporal bone, including disorders of hearing and balance.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling in credit risk assessment by integrating dynamic behavioral data and network analysis—a novel interdisciplinary approach at the intersection of computational finance, behavioral economics, and graph theory. Traditional credit scoring models rely heavily on static financial indicators and historical repayment data, often failing to capture real-time shifts in borrower behavior or systemic risks arising from interconnected financial networks. This limitation becomes acute in volatile markets, where cascading defaults or emergent fraud patterns can propagate through credit systems. The proposed work will develop a computational framework to process large-scale transactional datasets, social network interactions, and macroeconomic signals, employing graph neural networks (GNNs) and agent-based simulations to model credit ecosystems in high resolution. Key challenges include scaling graph-based algorithms to handle billions of transactional edges, optimizing temporal embeddings for irregular financial event sequences, and simulating stress scenarios across heterogeneous borrower clusters. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of deep learning architectures on multi-terabyte datasets spanning anonymized global credit card transactions, peer-to-peer lending platforms, and synthetic fraud scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a dynamic risk scoring system that updates in near real-time using streaming data, (2) identification of latent network-driven risk factors (e.g., default contagion pathways), and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating regulatory interventions in synthetic credit markets. By bridging computational scalability gaps in existing credit management systems, this research aims to provide financial institutions with adaptive tools for preemptive risk mitigation while informing ethical AI governance frameworks for credit decision systems. The computational intensity of modeling evolving financial networks at scale necessitates distributed memory architectures and GPU-accelerated graph processing capabilities unavailable in conventional enterprise environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and/or manage operations concerning personal and corporate credit, collateral, loan processing, and related financial agency communications. Includes instruction in general finance and banking principles, insurance, real estate, taxation, business law and regulations, quantitative methods, financial computer systems applications, database management, communications skills, business and office management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in cosmetic formulation design and safety assessment, addressing a critical gap in cosmetology education and practice. Current methods for testing hair and skincare products rely heavily on iterative laboratory experiments and clinical trials, which are time-consuming, resource-intensive, and limited in their ability to predict complex biochemical interactions across diverse hair and skin types. We propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML), and multi-scale modeling to analyze the behavior of cosmetic compounds (e.g., dyes, keratin treatments, surfactants) at the molecular level. The research will focus on simulating interactions between common cosmetic chemicals and structural proteins in hair (e.g., keratin) or skin components (e.g., collagen, lipids), accounting for variations in porosity, elasticity, and ethnic hair morphology. Large-scale MD simulations will map diffusion kinetics, binding affinities, and degradation pathways of active ingredients under varied environmental conditions (humidity, UV exposure). Concurrent ML models, trained on experimental data and simulation outputs, will predict allergenicity risks and optimize formulation stability. By coupling these approaches, the project aims to establish predictive guidelines for reducing adverse reactions and improving product performance across demographics. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of simulated cosmetic compound interactions, a toolkit for educators to visualize molecular-scale cosmetic effects in training environments, and evidence-based strategies for formulating inclusive, sustainable products. This interdisciplinary work bridges cosmetology, computational chemistry, and materials informatics, offering a novel paradigm for evidence-driven practice in a field traditionally dominated by empirical methods. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the high-throughput simulations and neural network training required for robust, generalizable models.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to cut, trim, and style scalp, facial, and body hair; apply cosmetic preparations; perform manicures and pedicures; massage the head and extremities; and prepare for practice as licensed cosmetologists in specialized or full-service salons.  Includes instruction in hair cutting and styling, manicuring, pedicuring, facial treatments, shampooing, chemical applications, esthetics, shop management, sanitation and safety, customer service, and applicable professional and labor laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation strategies for decentralized hospitality ecosystems, with a focus on integrating fragmented service providers (e.g., boutique hotels, independent tour operators, and niche experience vendors) into adaptive, AI-driven networks. The hospitality industry increasingly relies on real-time demand forecasting and hyper-localized pricing, but existing models fail to account for the complex interdependencies between small-scale operators, seasonal environmental factors, and multi-platform traveler behavior. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) system that simulates competitive and cooperative decision-making across thousands of heterogeneous entities under stochastic demand conditions. The model will ingest real-world datasets spanning 12 global tourism markets, including Airbnb occupancy patterns, localized event impacts, and climate-driven travel disruptions, processed through graph neural networks to map latent spatial-temporal dependencies. Computational experiments will benchmark novel coalitional game-theoretic algorithms against traditional revenue management systems, evaluating their resilience to supply chain shocks and ability to maximize collective profitability while preserving operator autonomy. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for decentralized hospitality coordination, empirically validated strategies to reduce over-tourism in saturated markets, and dynamic pricing templates that align micro-provider incentives with regional sustainability goals. This work addresses a critical gap in scalable computational solutions for non-corporatized hospitality networks, offering a paradigm shift from monolithic pricing engines to adaptive, community-aware resource allocation systems. The HPC environment is essential for training high-dimensional MARL agents and conducting billion-scale Monte Carlo simulations of cross-market ripple effects, tasks infeasible on standard cloud infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as general managers and directors of hospitality operations on a system-wide basis, including both travel arrangements and promotion and the provision of traveler facilities. Includes instruction in principles of operations in the travel and tourism, hotel and lodging facilities, food services, and recreation facilities industries; hospitality marketing strategies; hospitality planning; management and coordination of franchise and unit operations; business management; accounting and financial management; hospitality transportation and logistics; and hospitality industry policies and regulations.

abstract: This project investigates how institutional configurations in democratic systems shape the responsiveness of economic policies to societal preferences and external shocks. Traditional studies in political economy often rely on cross-national regression analyses or case studies, which struggle to capture dynamic interactions between political actors, institutional constraints, and economic variables. To address this gap, we propose developing a large-scale agent-based model (ABM) simulating legislative decision-making processes under varying electoral rules, party systems, and economic conditions. The ABM will incorporate heterogeneous actors—including legislators, interest groups, and voters—whose strategic interactions are informed by empirical data from 30 democracies over a 20-year period. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations across diverse institutional scenarios, calibrate model parameters using Bayesian optimization, and analyze emergent policy outcomes through machine learning techniques. The computational demands arise from the model’s granularity (10,000+ agents per simulation), stochastic elements, and the need for robustness checks across 10,000+ iterations. Expected outcomes include identifying institutional designs that enhance policy adaptability during economic crises and quantifying trade-offs between democratic accountability and economic stability. By integrating political science theory with computational social science methods, this project will generate novel insights into the microfoundations of policy formation and provide a scalable toolkit for simulating institutional reforms. The requested resources will enable parameter sensitivity analyses, real-world validation against historical policy shifts, and the production of open-access datasets for replication studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction between politics and economics in the formation of public policy. Includes instruction in microeconomics; macroeconomics; political theory; American, comparative, and international political economy; and quantitative methods.

abstract: This research seeks to investigate the molecular dynamics of plant cell wall remodeling under oscillatory mechanical stress, a process critical to growth and environmental adaptation but poorly understood at mechanistic scales. While plant cell walls are structurally complex composites of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin, their real-time reorganization during responses to physical forces—such as wind, turgor pressure, or root penetration—remains a computational challenge due to the multi-scale, nonlinear interactions between polymers and stress-responsive proteins. We propose to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale model integrating atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) of polysaccharide-protein interactions with coarse-grained continuum mechanics simulations of wall network deformation. This hybrid approach will parameterize MD-derived binding affinities and conformational shifts of expansins and cellulases under load, feeding into mesoscale models of wall plasticity during stress cycles. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated architectures to resolve time-dependent polymer reconfigurations across microseconds (atomistic) and minutes (continuum) while incorporating experimental data from live-cell imaging of wall strain in Arabidopsis hypocotyls. Key outcomes include a predictive framework linking nanoscale protein activity to tissue-level mechanical behavior, identification of critical thresholds for wall failure or reinforcement, and candidate regulatory motifs for engineering stress-resilient crops. By bridging molecular biophysics with plant biomechanics, this work addresses a gap in mechanobiological models of plant development and establishes computational tools to study dynamic structural adaptations in plant extracellular matrices.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of molecular biology, biochemistry, and biophysics to the study of biomolecular structures, functions, and processes specific to plants and plant substances. Includes instruction in the biochemistry of plant cells, nuclear-cytoplasmic interactions, molecular cytostructures, photosynthesis, plant molecular genetics, and the molecular biology of plant diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the impact of quantum computing-driven market microstructure dynamics on financial decision-making under uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model emergent trading behaviors in decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems. Traditional financial models struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between algorithmic trading agents, liquidity fragmentation across blockchain-based platforms, and real-time risk propagation in markets dominated by quantum-inspired optimization strategies. The research addresses this gap by developing an agent-based simulation framework that integrates quantum annealing techniques with game-theoretic liquidity provision models, calibrated to multi-chain DeFi transaction data. Using HPC clusters, we will simulate order book evolution across synthetic markets under varying quantum computing adoption scenarios, analyzing cascading effects on price discovery, arbitrage opportunities, and systemic stability. Computational experiments will employ hybrid quantum-classical optimization algorithms to resolve high-dimensional portfolio allocation problems in environments with nanosecond latency constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) quantitative benchmarks for quantum advantage in dark pool routing efficiency, 2) topology-aware risk metrics for cross-protocol liquidity shocks, and 3) adaptive hedging strategies resilient to quantum-accelerated front-running attacks. By mapping the computational complexity frontier where classical HPC infrastructure intersects with emerging quantum financial technologies, this work aims to establish foundational frameworks for next-generation market surveillance systems while informing regulatory approaches to quantum-ready financial infrastructure. The requested resources will enable large-scale parallelism of market scenario simulations, storage of petabyte-scale limit order book reconstructions, and real-time analysis of quantum circuit optimization patterns across heterogeneous compute architectures.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, manage, and analyze the financial and monetary aspects and performance of business enterprises, banking institutions, or other organizations. Includes instruction in principles of accounting, financial instruments, capital planning, funds acquisition, asset and debt management, budgeting, financial analysis, and investments and portfolio management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods to address high-dimensional, non-convex optimization problems arising in machine learning and data science. A key challenge in training modern neural networks or solving large-scale inverse problems is navigating complex, noisy optimization landscapes with numerous local minima. Traditional gradient-based methods often stagnate in these settings, while stochastic or metaheuristic approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs when applied to high-dimensional systems. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid framework integrating stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics with parallel tempering techniques, enhanced by algebraic topology tools to characterize landscape connectivity. The research will implement and test these algorithms on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, leveraging distributed memory architectures for parallel sampling and ensemble-based exploration of parameter spaces. Key innovations include adaptive temperature scheduling via reinforcement learning and the application of persistent homology to map metastable regions in optimization trajectories. The computational workload involves large-scale matrix computations, Monte Carlo simulations, and topological data analysis, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and high-throughput interconnects. Expected outcomes include robust optimization algorithms with demonstrably faster convergence rates on benchmark tasks such as training transformer-based models and solving ill-posed imaging problems. By unifying probabilistic sampling, geometric analysis, and parallel computing, this work aims to advance both theoretical understanding of non-convex optimization and practical tools for data-intensive applications. The resulting software will be released as an open-source library optimized for HPC environments, with potential impacts in autonomous systems, computational biology, and climate modeling. Successful implementation requires allocation of 200,000 node-hours to evaluate scalability on problems exceeding 10^6 dimensions, alongside storage for terabyte-scale optimization trajectory datasets.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and computer science or a specialization which draws from mathematics and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in drywall installation workflows through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize material usage, labor allocation, and structural performance. Despite the ubiquity of drywall in modern construction, current practices rely heavily on manual estimation and static guidelines, leading to material waste, inconsistent quality, and safety risks. Our research aims to bridge this gap by developing dynamic, data-driven models that simulate installation scenarios under variable constraints. Key computational approaches include finite element analysis (FEA) to predict stress distribution in drywall assemblies under diverse environmental and load conditions, machine learning algorithms trained on construction datasets to optimize cutting patterns and minimize material waste, and agent-based modeling to evaluate ergonomic risks and workflow efficiency. These models will integrate real-world variables such as humidity, tool performance, and crew size, requiring parallelized simulations to process large parameter spaces. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of scenarios, including rare but critical edge cases (e.g., seismic stresses, extreme temperature fluctuations). Expected outcomes include predictive tools for drywall failure thresholds, generative algorithms for layout optimization, and evidence-based guidelines for training programs to reduce musculoskeletal injuries. By quantifying relationships between installation techniques and long-term structural integrity, this work will provide a foundation for revising industry standards and certification criteria. The computational frameworks developed will be adaptable to emerging materials like fire-resistant or moisture-reactive drywall, ensuring scalability. This project represents a novel intersection of construction trades and computational engineering, with potential to reduce construction waste by an estimated 15–20% in modeled scenarios while improving installer safety and project timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, tape, and plaster drywall installations in interior and exterior construction jobs. Includes instruction in drywall handling and transport, cutting and mounting, taping and spackling, finishing, job analysis and estimation, site safety, tool operation and maintenance, blueprint and specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the complex interplay of biopsychosocial factors influencing patient outcomes in palliative care nursing. Despite the growing emphasis on personalized, evidence-based approaches, clinicians lack robust tools to predict symptom trajectories, optimize pain management, or tailor interventions for patients with life-limiting illnesses. Current methods for analyzing multidimensional data—including electronic health records, patient-reported outcomes, and biomarkers—are constrained by computational limitations, hindering the integration of dynamic variables such as fluctuating symptoms, treatment responses, and psychosocial stressors. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model longitudinal palliative care datasets. Machine learning algorithms, including recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods, will be deployed to identify patterns in symptom progression, treatment efficacy, and quality-of-life metrics across diverse patient populations. The project will also employ natural language processing to analyze unstructured clinical notes and caregiver narratives, extracting latent themes related to grief, communication preferences, and cultural factors. By simulating patient trajectories under varying care scenarios, the models will enable probabilistic forecasting of outcomes such as pain crises, hospital readmissions, and psychosocial distress. The computational demands of training these models on terabyte-scale datasets—spanning genomic, clinical, and behavioral variables—necessitate parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated analytics. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide clinical decision-making, risk stratification protocols for proactive interventions, and a publicly accessible palliative care simulation environment. This work will advance the scientific rigor of palliative nursing by bridging qualitative care paradigms with quantitative computational methods, ultimately fostering more equitable, patient-centered approaches to end-of-life care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide a combination of active and compassionate therapies intended to comfort and support patients and their families who are living with life-threatening illness. Includes instruction in pathophysiology, palliative care processes, pain management, pharmacology, loss, grief, death, and bereavement.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze the morphosyntactic and sociolinguistic evolution of Punjabi dialects, with a focus on bridging gaps in digital resources for this under-resourced language. Despite Punjabi’s status as a major global language with over 100 million speakers, computational tools for its dialects remain sparse, hindering scholarly analysis and practical applications in technology-driven contexts. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process large-scale corpora of written and spoken Punjabi, including historical texts, modern literature, and transcribed oral narratives, to model dialectal variations and their sociocultural drivers. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for dialect classification, automating syntactic parsing of non-standardized grammatical structures, and simulating diachronic linguistic shifts using probabilistic graphical models. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization of deep learning architectures, necessitating GPU-accelerated HPC resources. Expected outcomes include the first open-access, computationally annotated Punjabi dialect corpus, a suite of NLP tools tailored for regional variants (e.g., Majhi, Malwai), and quantitative insights into how migration and technology adoption have influenced linguistic change. The project will directly support Punjabi language preservation efforts, enable downstream applications in education and localized AI systems, and establish methodological frameworks adaptable to other low-resource languages. By integrating computational linguistics with philological scholarship, this work advances interdisciplinary humanities research while addressing tangible needs in speech recognition, machine translation, and digital archiving for Punjabi communities worldwide.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Punjabi language (Punjabi) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize patient-specific surgical planning for complex maxillofacial reconstructions, addressing the challenge of biomechanical unpredictability in heterogeneous bone and soft tissue environments. Current approaches rely on static anatomical models and generalized biomechanical assumptions, which fail to account for dynamic intraoperative forces, tissue variability, and postoperative healing responses. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create multi-scale finite element models integrating patient-specific CT/MRI data, real-time intraoperative sensor metrics, and mechanobiological healing simulations. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on retrospective surgical outcomes to predict optimal osteotomy patterns, fixation hardware configurations, and load distribution thresholds. A hybrid computational pipeline will combine lattice Boltzmann methods for simulating fluid-structure interactions in vascularized bone grafts with agent-based modeling of osteoblast-osteoclast dynamics during healing. The HPC environment is critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space, including stochastic variations in bone density, graft viability, and masticatory force profiles. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for minimizing postoperative complications such as plate failure, non-union fractures, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction, while enabling dynamic intraoperative adaptation through real-time data assimilation. This work bridges computational biomechanics, precision surgery, and regenerative medicine, offering a paradigm shift from static preoperative plans to adaptive, physiology-informed surgical strategies. Successful implementation could reduce revision surgery rates by an estimated 30-40% in complex cases, with broader implications for personalized surgical interventions across musculoskeletal disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the diagnosis and intrusive and adjunctive treatment of diseases, injuries, and defects of the oral and maxillofacial regions, including functional and aesthetic aspects. Includes instruction in pharmacology, analgesia, anesthesia, anxiety control, surgical procedures and techniques, surgical instrumentation, exodontia, oral diseases and malfunctions, soft and hard tissue pathology, dentoalveolar surgery, infection management, and prosthetic implantation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate dynamic audience-performer interactions in immersive theatre environments, addressing a critical gap in the quantitative analysis of live performance dynamics. While traditional theatrical design relies on iterative physical prototyping and qualitative feedback, this approach lacks the capacity to predict how spatial configurations, acoustic conditions, or movement patterns influence collective audience engagement. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets—including motion-captured performer trajectories, directional audio recordings, and real-time audience biometric responses (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate variability)—collected from experimental performances. Agent-based modeling will simulate audience sightline obstructions and acoustic propagation variances across hypothetical venue geometries, while recurrent neural networks will identify patterns linking technical parameters (lighting transitions, sound spatialization) to physiological markers of engagement. The computational pipeline will integrate Unity3D for real-time visualization of stage configurations and audience sightline analyses, paired with lattice Boltzmann methods to model airborne sound diffusion in complex, adaptable stage architectures. By optimizing these models on HPC clusters, we aim to generate predictive tools for designers to virtually test scenographic concepts at unprecedented scales, reducing reliance on physical mock-ups. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of simulated theatre environments and evidence-based guidelines for enhancing emotional resonance through computational scenography. This work bridges performing arts practice with computational engineering, offering new methodologies to quantify ephemeral aspects of theatrical experience while preserving artistic intentionality. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of virtual venue configurations, which would be computationally infeasible on local hardware.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Dramatic/ Theatre Arts and Stagecraft, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dramatic/theatre arts and stagecraft, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing iterative writing instruction in secondary education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale student writing datasets. While iterative drafting and feedback are central to developing argumentative writing skills, educators lack granular insights into how specific revision patterns correlate with improved outcomes. Current manual assessment methods are time-intensive and fail to capture longitudinal trends across diverse student populations. To bridge this gap, this study will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to evaluate 50,000+ argumentative essay drafts and revisions from a multi-district corpus, tracking syntactic complexity, rhetorical moves, and argumentation coherence across iterations. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of text data to train transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants) for automated feedback quality classification and revision impact prediction. Network analysis will map structural changes in argumentation frameworks between drafts, while hierarchical clustering will identify common revision pathways tied to proficiency gains. The computational workflow will integrate Python-based NLP pipelines (spaCy, Transformers) with distributed training on GPU clusters to handle embedding generation and model optimization at scale. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of high-impact revision strategies linked to writing growth, (2) predictive models to prioritize actionable feedback, and (3) interactive visualization tools for teacher professional development. By revealing how iterative writing processes develop in authentic classrooms, this research will directly inform the design of training modules for pre-service teachers in the Communication Arts and Literature program, equipping them with evidence-based strategies to scaffold argumentative writing. The requested computing resources are essential for processing the dataset’s volume and complexity, enabling real-time analytics that traditional methods cannot provide.
cip_title: Communication Arts and Literature Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to teach oral expression, literature, and writing to students at various education levels. Includes instruction in interpersonal communication, intercultural communication, language learning, listening instructional techniques, public speaking, reading instructional techniques, writing instructional techniques, and practical teaching experience.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of oral biofilm-mediated diseases, such as peri-implantitis and dental caries, underscores a critical gap in understanding the biomechanical and biochemical dynamics of polymicrobial communities under clinically relevant conditions. Traditional in vitro models fail to capture the complex spatiotemporal interactions between microbial species, host-derived factors, and mechanical stressors like occlusal forces or orthodontic device micro-movements. This project proposes an interdisciplinary computational framework to model oral biofilm resilience and adaptive behaviors in response to multifactorial perturbations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop a hybrid agent-based model (ABM) coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate biofilm growth, metabolite diffusion, and mechanical strain across 3D-reconstructed dental and mucosal surfaces derived from clinical imaging data. The ABM will integrate strain-specific genomic and metabolomic datasets to parameterize microbial interactions, while finite element analysis (FEA) will map stress distributions affecting biofilm detachment and virulence gene expression. Machine learning techniques will optimize model calibration against experimental biofilm assays conducted under microfluidic shear conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of biofilm vulnerability zones, identification of keystone species driving treatment resistance, and in silico testing of novel antimicrobial surface topographies. By bridging microbial ecology, biomechanics, and computational modeling, this work aims to establish a paradigm for personalized biofilm intervention strategies in restorative dentistry and orthodontics, ultimately reducing device failure rates and antibiotic overuse. The requested HPC allocation will enable simulations at unprecedented spatial resolutions (sub-µm scale) across clinically relevant timeframes (days to weeks), addressing a critical bottleneck in translational oral health research.
cip_title: Dental Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dental services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop data-driven tools to optimize individualized education plans (IEPs) for students with orthopedic and other physical health impairments through advanced computational modeling. Current IEP design faces challenges in systematically addressing the heterogeneous needs of students, including mobility limitations, assistive technology dependencies, and variable health-related absences. Existing approaches often rely on qualitative assessments, which can lead to delays in identifying effective interventions. To address this, we propose a computational framework leveraging machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate student outcomes under diverse educational strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal datasets—including academic performance metrics, assistive technology usage logs, and physical accessibility assessments—while training ensemble ML models to predict intervention efficacy. ABM simulations will replicate classroom dynamics, testing how environmental adaptations (e.g., desk configurations, digital tool integration) and instructional methods impact student engagement and learning. The project will utilize federated learning techniques to preserve privacy across distributed educational records from partner institutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform that recommends IEP adjustments based on real-time data, prioritized accessibility features for classroom environments, and evidence-based guidelines for educators. By quantifying relationships between instructional strategies, assistive technologies, and student success, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error in special education practices and improve resource allocation for students with physical impairments. The scalability of these models, enabled by HPC, will support future research on equitable AI applications in special education, ensuring tools remain adaptable to evolving policies and diverse student needs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Orthopedic and Other Physical Health Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with orthopedic and other health impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying physically disabled students, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with orthopedic and other health impairments, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing strategies in live auctioneering environments through advanced computational modeling of bidder behavior and real-time decision-making algorithms. Auctioneering involves complex, high-stakes interactions where traditional static pricing models fail to account for rapidly shifting participant psychology, inventory heterogeneity, and market signals. The research problem centers on developing a predictive framework that integrates bid-calling patterns, temporal auction dynamics, and commodity-specific valuation factors to maximize both seller returns and bidder engagement. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating thousands of concurrent auction scenarios across diverse specialty markets (e.g., agricultural equipment, rare collectibles) while modeling adaptive strategies under latency constraints mirroring real-world events. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling with deep reinforcement learning, training bidder agents on synthetic and historical auction datasets to capture behavioral nuances such as competitive escalation, risk aversion, and social signaling. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will test auction format variations, including hybrid sealed-bid/live-bidding systems and AI-assisted reserve price adjustments. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for optimizing auctioneer pacing, lot sequencing, and incentive structures across specialized markets, validated against transactional data from partner auction houses. The project addresses a gap in business research by formalizing computational auctioneering as a distinct interdisciplinary domain intersecting behavioral economics, operations research, and real-time systems optimization. Results will provide actionable insights for licensing programs seeking to modernize bid-calling pedagogy and for auction platforms requiring adaptive tools to manage volatility in emerging markets like decarbonization equipment or AI-generated art. By leveraging HPC capabilities to model hyper-dynamic auction ecologies, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for a profession undergoing rapid technological transformation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional careers as auctioneers and auction managers, and for meeting applicable state licensing requirements. Includes instruction in bid calling, public speaking, ringworking, auction techniques, salesmanship skills, auction clerking and cashiering, auction advertising, working independently or with auction houses, contracts and agency, applicable sales law, and managing both general auctions and auctions specializing in commodities such as antiques, consignments, farm equipment, industrial equipment, real estate, livestock, and automobiles.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociocultural dynamics of Italian identity formation through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The research focuses on tracing the evolution of regional and national narratives in modern Italy (post-1861 unification) by examining digitized archives of literature, periodicals, and public discourse. A key challenge lies in processing heterogeneous, multilingual materials—including vernacular texts, state-sponsored publications, and migrant correspondence—to identify patterns of cultural hybridity, gendered representations, and contested historical memory. Traditional humanities methods struggle to manage the scale and complexity of these datasets, which span over 15 million pages of digitized material from Italian libraries and diaspora collections. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical Italian dialects, network analysis to map ideological diffusion across regions, and computer vision tools to detect visual motifs in propaganda art and photography. Custom transformer models will be trained to classify rhetorical strategies in political and literary texts, while graph-based algorithms will reconstruct transnational intellectual networks linking Italy to its global diasporas. By deploying these methods on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to quantify previously opaque cultural processes, such as the role of non-elite actors in shaping national identity or the impact of emigration on regional linguistic practices. Expected outcomes include an open-access corpus of annotated texts, visualizations of discourse networks across critical historical junctures (e.g., Fascist era, post-war reconstruction), and methodological frameworks for computational cultural analysis. This work will advance interdisciplinary scholarship in Italian Studies by bridging qualitative interpretation with scalable data-driven inquiry, while providing actionable insights for preserving intangible cultural heritage in digitized archives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of modern Italy and its predecessors on the Italian Peninsula, including the overseas migrations of Italian peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent turbulence phenomena in quantum fluid systems through large-scale numerical simulations, addressing critical gaps in understanding how turbulent behavior manifests in superfluids at ultra-low temperatures. While classical turbulence is well-studied, the quantum regime—where fluid dynamics are governed by quantized vortices and macroscopic quantum coherence—remains poorly characterized due to the absence of analytical solutions and experimental resolution limits. We propose to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate the dynamics of vortex networks in two- and three-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates using the nonlinear Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Our numerical approach leverages adaptive spectral methods and parallelized time-integration algorithms to resolve vortex nucleation, reconnection events, and energy cascades across multiple scales. These simulations will quantify how quantum turbulence deviates from classical Kolmogorov scaling laws, particularly in the decay of kinetic energy and the role of vortex filament interactions. By systematically varying system parameters (e.g., temperature, trapping potentials, and initial vortex configurations), we aim to identify universal statistical features of quantum turbulence and their dependence on microscopic physics. The computational demands are substantial: resolving sub-healing-length vortex core structures while tracking system-scale evolution requires petascale capabilities for meshes exceeding 10^8 grid points and long simulation timescales. Outcomes will provide predictive benchmarks for ongoing experimental efforts in ultracold atomic gases and helium superfluids, advancing fundamental knowledge of non-equilibrium quantum systems. This work will also develop open-source GPU-optimized simulation tools for the broader quantum fluids community. Successful completion of these objectives will establish a computational framework to probe quantum turbulence regimes inaccessible to current laboratory techniques, with implications for understanding dissipation mechanisms in topological quantum matter.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The development of targeted therapeutics requires precise understanding of drug-receptor interactions at atomistic resolution, yet current approaches struggle to predict pharmacodynamic outcomes in complex signaling environments. This project seeks to address the critical gap in quantifying how conformational dynamics of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) influence drug efficacy and off-target toxicity, a challenge exacerbated by the transient nature of allosteric binding states and the limitations of experimental structural biology. We propose an integrative computational strategy leveraging enhanced sampling molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to map free-energy landscapes of 12 therapeutically relevant GPCR-ligand complexes. Multi-replica Gaussian accelerated MD (GaMD) protocols will be deployed across 2,000+ concurrent nodes to achieve microsecond-scale sampling of metastable states, coupled with Markov state model analysis to identify cryptic binding pockets. These data will inform structure-based virtual screening of a curated library of 1.2 million drug-like molecules using ensemble docking approaches that account for receptor flexibility. The computational workflow requires petascale storage for trajectory analysis and GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning-based prediction of binding kinetics. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic models of how ligand-specific receptor dynamics modulate downstream signaling bias, (2) identification of lead compounds with improved selectivity profiles for three understudied receptors linked to metabolic disorders, and (3) open-access protocols for incorporating conformational ensemble data into rational drug design pipelines. By elucidating molecular determinants of signaling bias, this work will advance therapeutic strategies that optimize drug efficacy while minimizing adverse effects—a critical need in precision pharmacology. The requested HPC resources are essential for overcoming current sampling limitations in MD simulations and enabling large-scale comparative analyses across receptor subtypes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biochemical and biophysical characteristics of drugs at the molecular level and their interaction with, and effects on, biological macromolecules and cellular structures and processes. Includes instruction in molecular biology and biophysics; pharmacology of signal transduction, transmitters, and protein synthesis and release; receptors, protein interaction and binding; drug discovery and recognition; molecular toxicology; drug design; pharmacodynamics; developmental genetics; and studies of therapeutic strategies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of urban fire spread dynamics in complex built environments, with a focus on integrating real-time human behavior data into fire safety simulations. Current fire propagation models often rely on static structural and environmental inputs, neglecting the dynamic interplay between occupant decision-making, evacuation patterns, and evolving fire conditions. This limitation hinders the accuracy of risk assessments for high-occupancy structures and urban centers, where human factors significantly influence outcomes. Our research will develop a hybrid computational framework combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of fire and smoke spread with agent-based modeling (ABM) of crowd movement. The CFD component will utilize FireFOAM, an open-source solver for turbulent reactive flows, to model multi-scale fire phenomena, while the ABM module will incorporate machine learning-derived behavioral profiles trained on evacuation case studies and sensor data from smart building systems.
