The integration of these components demands HPC capabilities to resolve sub-meter spatial scales across city-block-sized domains while maintaining real-time simulation speeds for time-sensitive scenario testing. Key challenges include optimizing parallelization strategies for coupled simulations and validating models against both controlled fire experiments and historical urban fire incident datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for fire departments and urban planners, enabling scenario-based testing of evacuation protocols, infrastructure hardening strategies, and emergency response coordination. The project will also generate novel insights into feedback loops between fire progression and crowd behavior, informing revisions to international building codes and public safety guidelines. By bridging gaps between fire physics, behavioral science, and computational engineering, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive fire risk management in increasingly dense urban landscapes.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science and technology to problems of reducing fire risk, limiting loss, supervising substance removal, conducting safety inspections and investigations, and advising on matters of safety procedures and fire prevention policy. Includes instruction in fire behavior, fire simulation, structural risk assessment, materials analysis, detection and suppression systems, smoke management, supply and evacuation, public education, legal aspects of fire prevention, and related research and communications methods.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of dynamic, large-scale visual communication systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in real-time rendering, adaptive graphic optimization, and audience engagement analytics. Contemporary graphic communications workflows—particularly in immersive media, interactive design, and multi-platform publishing—struggle to balance computational efficiency with aesthetic and functional demands. Current tools often lack the capacity to simulate complex visual environments or process audience interaction data at scale, limiting innovation in personalized and responsive design. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes a computational framework combining GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines, machine learning models for adaptive asset generation, and distributed data processing to analyze real-time user engagement metrics. The project will utilize HPC clusters to parallelize tasks such as (1) simulating photorealistic environments under variable display conditions (e.g., AR/VR, mobile, print), (2) training generative adversarial networks (GANs) to automate context-aware design adjustments, and (3) processing terabyte-scale datasets of user interaction logs to identify behavioral patterns. By integrating these methods, the study aims to develop a prototype system capable of dynamically optimizing graphic outputs across media platforms while reducing computational latency by an estimated 40-60% compared to existing workflows. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for resource-efficient rendering, validated models for audience-centric design adaptation, and benchmarks for HPC-driven scalability in graphic communication pipelines. This work will directly benefit educators and practitioners in communication design by providing actionable insights into computationally sustainable creative practices, while expanding the methodological toolkit for data-driven visual storytelling in non-STEM disciplines.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in graphic communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems operate under extreme thermal, mechanical, and aerodynamic stresses, leading to complex degradation patterns that challenge traditional inspection and maintenance protocols. This project seeks to address the critical need for predictive modeling of turbine engine component failures, specifically focusing on high-cycle fatigue in compressor blades and thermal degradation in combustion chambers. Current empirical methods for assessing wear and predicting failures are limited by their reliance on post-service inspections and generalized operational data, which often fail to capture localized stress dynamics or transient thermal gradients. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating high-fidelity fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations, machine learning (ML)-enabled anomaly detection, and probabilistic lifetime prediction models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multiphysics phenomena—including turbulent combustion dynamics, conjugate heat transfer, and cyclic elastoplastic deformation—at scales relevant to microstructural material behavior. Large-eddy simulations (LES) will model combustion instability effects on chamber walls, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict stress accumulation in blade root geometries under variable rotor speeds. A recurrent neural network (RNN) trained on simulation-derived datasets will correlate real-time sensor data with early failure signatures. Outcomes will include a validated digital twin framework for powerplant subsystems, enabling proactive maintenance scheduling and reducing unplanned downtime. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated failure scenarios to support curriculum advancements in powerplant diagnostics, equipping technicians with data-driven decision-making tools. By bridging computational mechanics with applied aircraft maintenance practices, this work aims to extend service intervals safely and inform next-generation engine design priorities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: This project seeks to advance theoretical understanding in nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) and their solutions within function spaces, with applications to problems in mathematical physics. The research focuses on analyzing the existence, regularity, and stability of solutions to high-dimensional PDEs arising in wave propagation and dissipative dynamical systems. Traditional analytical methods face limitations in addressing these problems due to the complexity of nonlinear interactions, geometric constraints, and the need for high-dimensional function space approximations. To overcome these barriers, we propose a computational framework combining modern harmonic analysis techniques with adaptive spectral methods. The core challenges involve resolving multiscale phenomena in Sobolev and Besov spaces, characterizing energy transfer in weak solutions, and verifying conjectured blow-up behaviors in critical norms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to implement large-scale Galerkin approximations, compute invariant measures for stochastic PDEs via Monte Carlo parallelization, and perform precision-intensive wavelet decompositions for singularity analysis. Key algorithms will leverage GPU-accelerated iterative solvers for sparse linear systems arising from spectral discretizations, while distributed memory architectures will enable parameter space exploration across functional geometries. Expected outcomes include new criteria for solution uniqueness in non-convex energy landscapes, quantitative bounds on approximation errors in high-dimensional Sobolev embeddings, and classification of attractors in infinite-dimensional dynamical systems. These results will provide foundational insights into the structure of PDE solutions under minimal regularity assumptions, with implications for modern analysis in mathematical physics. The computational infrastructure will also yield open-source software tools for functional analysis in high dimensions, bridging theoretical advances with reproducible numerical experimentation. This work directly aligns with the program’s emphasis on rigorous analysis of dynamic systems and complex function spaces while avoiding applied or statistical methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and behavior of equations, multivariate solutions, functions, and dynamic systems. Includes instruction in differential equations, variation, approximations, complex variables, integrals, harmonic analysis and wavelet theory, dynamic systems, and applications to mathematical physics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative gridlock and bipartisan coalition formation in the U.S. Congress using advanced computational modeling. Despite extensive scholarship on partisan polarization, the conditions under which cross-party collaboration emerges—or fails to emerge—remain poorly understood, particularly in complex policy environments with overlapping issue dimensions. To address this gap, we propose developing a large-scale agent-based model (ABM) simulating legislative behavior, incorporating data on historical voting patterns, constituency demographics, interest group networks, and intra-party factionalism. The ABM will integrate machine learning techniques to calibrate legislator agents’ decision rules using 30 years of roll-call vote data (1993-2023), then test how institutional rules (e.g., filibuster thresholds) and exogenous shocks (e.g., economic crises) affect coalition viability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized parameter space exploration across 50+ ideological and strategic dimensions, (2) network analysis of co-sponsorship and committee membership graphs (>100,000 edges), and (3) NLP processing of 200,000+ congressional speech transcripts to refine preference metrics. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational framework for testing institutional reform proposals, novel quantitative measures of “coalition plasticity” across policy domains, and dynamic visualizations of threshold effects in majority-building. Results will advance theoretical understanding of legislative bargaining under constraints of multidimensional polarization while providing empirically grounded insights about procedural designs that incentivize cross-partisan cooperation. The scale of behavioral data integration and the need for real-time sensitivity analyses across billions of agent interactions necessitate cluster computing capabilities exceeding local workstation limits, particularly for GPU-accelerated neural networks training on speech corpora and memory-intensive Monte Carlo simulations of alternative legislative histories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of United States political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in American political theory, political parties and interest groups, state and local governments, Constitutional law, federalism and national institutions, executive and legislative politics, judicial politics, popular attitudes and media influences, political research methods, and applications to the study of specific issues and institutions.

abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of healthcare data present significant challenges in efficiently managing, analyzing, and securing medical records while adhering to regulatory standards. This project seeks to address critical gaps in real-time health information systems by developing scalable computational models for integrating heterogeneous clinical data sources, enhancing predictive analytics for patient outcomes, and optimizing privacy-preserving data sharing protocols. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-phase approach to process large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic datasets, and real-time wearable device data. First, distributed machine learning frameworks will be implemented to train predictive models for early detection of adverse clinical events, such as hospital-acquired infections or medication errors, using temporal and multimodal data fusion techniques. Second, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be optimized to extract structured insights from unstructured clinical notes and imaging reports at scale, enabling automated quality metric reporting. Third, federated learning architectures will be tested to facilitate cross-institutional collaboration without compromising data sovereignty, incorporating differential privacy mechanisms to meet HIPAA and GDPR requirements. The computational demands of these tasks—including parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and cryptographic simulations for secure multi-party computation—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with high-memory nodes, scalable storage, and specialized accelerators. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for interoperable health data analytics, open-source tools for privacy-aware federated learning in clinical settings, and benchmarks for computational efficiency in EHR processing workflows. By advancing the technical capabilities of health information systems, this research aims to empower healthcare organizations to derive actionable insights from complex data while maintaining rigorous compliance, ultimately improving patient safety, operational decision-making, and resource allocation in clinical environments.
cip_title: Health Information/ Medical Records Administration/ Administrator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage systems, processes, and facilities used to collect, store, secure, retrieve, analyze, and transmit medical records and other health information used by clinical professionals and health care organizations. Includes instruction in the principles and basic content of the biomedical and clinical sciences, information technology and applications, data and database management, clinical research methodologies, health information resources and systems, office management, legal requirements, and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling frameworks for strategic intelligence prioritization in dynamic, multi-domain military environments. The research addresses the challenge of synthesizing heterogeneous data streams—including sociocultural indicators, geopolitical event patterns, and real-time sensor networks—into actionable intelligence assessments. Traditional analytical methods struggle to reconcile the scale, velocity, and ambiguity of modern intelligence data, particularly in contested information environments where adversarial deception tactics and rapid situational shifts are prevalent. To address this gap, the project proposes a computational architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for relational inference across entity interactions, transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for multilingual open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis, and adaptive ensemble learning systems to quantify uncertainty in threat forecasts. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale simulations of conflict scenarios, training of multi-modal AI models on classified and unclassified data repositories, and real-time testing of decision-support prototypes through digital twin environments mirroring theater-level command structures. Anticipated outcomes include a novel metrics framework for evaluating intelligence confidence under partial observability, optimized algorithms for resource allocation in joint operational planning, and deployable tools to enhance situational awareness of emergent hybrid threats. By integrating computational social science methodologies with defense-specific operational requirements, this work aims to establish a paradigm for next-generation intelligence systems capable of anticipating strategic shocks while maintaining rigorous audit trails for model interpretability. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, secure data federation across sensitivity levels, and validation exercises using historical crisis datasets to benchmark performance against human-analyst baselines.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the management, analysis and use of national-level, theatre-level, and international intelligence and related policy issues. Includes instruction in intelligence organization and management, strategic uses of intelligence, management of intelligence systems and assets, command and control, joint intelligence operations, electronic and signals intelligence, threat assessment and estimation, intelligence analysis and reporting, counterintelligence, and studies of specific regions and situations.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance, sustainable polymers in industrial applications necessitates advanced computational tools to overcome the limitations of traditional trial-and-error material development. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize the synthesis, processing, and performance of novel polymer systems, with a focus on biodegradability and recyclability. The primary challenge lies in predicting macromolecular behavior under dynamic manufacturing conditions, including polymerization kinetics, thermal stability, and stress-response properties, which are experimentally time-intensive and cost-prohibitive to characterize. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) algorithms. MD simulations will model molecular interactions during polymerization and degradation, while FEA will assess mechanical performance under industrial processing parameters. ML models trained on experimental and simulated datasets will identify correlations between polymer architectures, processing variables, and end-use properties, enabling inverse design of materials with tailored characteristics. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of these tasks, particularly for simulating large-scale polymer networks (>100,000 atoms) and iterative optimization workflows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for designing biodegradable polymers with equivalent or superior mechanical properties to conventional plastics, as well as energy-efficient processing protocols to reduce manufacturing carbon footprints. This work will directly support ongoing industry partnerships aimed at commercializing circular-economy-compliant materials, while providing a computational resource framework for future research in polymer engineering education and applied R&D. The requested allocation will enable simulations at experimentally relevant timescales and system sizes, which are unfeasible with current institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using industrial polymers. Includes instruction in the principles of macromolecular chemistry, polymerization and plastic manufacturing processes and equipment, design and operational testing procedures, equipment maintenance and repair procedures, safety procedures, applications to specific products, and report preparation.

abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders, encompassing injuries and degenerative conditions of joints, bones, and soft tissues, are a leading cause of chronic pain and disability worldwide. Despite advances in imaging modalities such as MRI and CT, significant challenges remain in early detection, quantitative assessment of disease progression, and personalized treatment planning. Current clinical workflows often rely on qualitative interpretations of imaging data, which lack the precision needed to capture subtle pathological changes or predict biomechanical outcomes. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing and validating advanced computational tools to analyze multidimensional musculoskeletal imaging data, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The primary research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution MRI, dynamic CT, and biomechanical measurements—to create predictive models of musculoskeletal pathology and therapeutic response. Computational methods will focus on three areas: (1) deep learning-based segmentation of anatomical structures using 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) optimized for GPU-accelerated processing, (2) finite element modeling to simulate load distribution in osteoarthritic joints and post-surgical bone implants, and (3) federated learning frameworks to aggregate imaging data across institutions while preserving patient privacy. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale training of models on multi-terabyte imaging datasets, parallelized biomechanical simulations, and real-time processing of dynamic joint motion studies. Expected outcomes include the development of automated tools for quantifying cartilage thickness, bone density, and ligament integrity with submillimeter precision, as well as patient-specific biomechanical risk profiles for fractures or implant failure. These tools aim to reduce diagnostic variability, enable earlier intervention in degenerative diseases, and optimize surgical planning. By providing open-source algorithms and validation pipelines, this work will establish a foundation for data-driven musculoskeletal radiology, directly impacting clinical decision-making and translational research in orthopedic and rheumatologic care.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders or injuries of the joints, bones, muscles, and spine in adults and children.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to address the computational challenges of processing and analyzing large-scale geospatial datasets in modern surveying applications. Traditional surveying workflows struggle to efficiently manage the increasing volume and complexity of data from advanced technologies such as LiDAR, UAV photogrammetry, and real-time kinematic (RTK) GNSS systems, particularly when modeling subsidence, deformation, or boundary disputes across extensive geographic regions. The research will implement parallelized algorithms to accelerate geodetic computations—including least-squares adjustments, error propagation modeling, and 3D point cloud registration—while integrating machine learning methods to automate feature extraction and anomaly detection in topographic data. HPC resources will be critical for optimizing iterative simulations of land movement patterns, leveraging historical survey records and sensor data to predict subsidence risks in urban or geologically active areas. The computational pipeline will also support the generation of high-resolution digital elevation models (DEMs) and cadastral maps with reduced processing times compared to conventional software. Expected outcomes include scalable workflows for real-time data assimilation, improved accuracy in deformation forecasting, and open-source tools tailored for surveying applications. This work will directly benefit infrastructure monitoring, land-use planning, and disaster resilience efforts by enabling surveyors and geoscientists to process terabyte-scale datasets with higher precision and temporal resolution. The requested computing resources will facilitate benchmarking across heterogeneous architectures to ensure compatibility with field-deployable devices, bridging the gap between computational geoscience and practical surveying operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the delineation, determination, planning and positioning of land tracts, land and water boundaries, land contours and features; and the preparation of related maps, charts and reports. Includes instruction in applied geodesy, computer graphics, photointerpretation, plane and geodetic surveying, mensuration, traversing, survey equipment operation and maintenance, instrument calibration, and basic cartography.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay between insurance law frameworks and emergent systemic risks in decentralized financial systems. Traditional legal scholarship has struggled to model the dynamic, nonlinear relationships between regulatory policies, contractual language in insurance products, and evolving risk landscapes—particularly in contexts such as parametric insurance for blockchain-based assets or AI-driven underwriting systems. The computational demands of parsing large-scale legal corpora (e.g., cross-jurisdictional statutes, case law, and insurance contracts) while simulating risk propagation in heterogeneous digital markets exceed the capabilities of conventional analytical tools. This project will employ natural language processing (NLP) transformers to classify latent ambiguities in policy wording across 10 million+ insurance contracts, paired with agent-based modeling to simulate how these ambiguities interact with automated claims adjudication systems under stress scenarios. Graph neural networks will map citation networks within insurance case law to identify regulatory arbitrage patterns, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify the systemic impacts of proposed legislative reforms. By integrating these approaches on an HPC cluster, the research aims to 1) identify critical vulnerabilities in current insurance law frameworks exposed by decentralized finance technologies, 2) develop a predictive model for litigation hotspots arising from generative AI in claims processing, and 3) propose adaptive regulatory metrics capable of responding to computational insurance products. Outcomes will provide policymakers and legal practitioners with empirically grounded tools to address gaps in traditional insurance law paradigms, while advancing methodological frameworks for computational legal analysis in non-binary regulatory environments. The scale of required legal text analysis, parallel scenario simulations, and real-time sensitivity testing necessitates dedicated HPC resources to achieve sublinear time complexity in model training and validation phases.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting insurance.

abstract: The safe and efficient management of traffic through construction zones remains a critical challenge in infrastructure development, requiring dynamic solutions to mitigate risks to workers, drivers, and pedestrians. Current traffic control strategies often rely on static protocols that inadequately account for real-world variables such as fluctuating traffic volumes, weather conditions, or unexpected disruptions. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework to model traffic flow and flagging operations in diverse construction scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate real-world traffic datasets, driver behavior models, and environmental factors to simulate interactions between vehicles, pedestrians, and flaggers at scale. Computational methods will include Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate probabilistic outcomes, machine learning algorithms to predict emergent traffic patterns, and optimization techniques to test adaptive flagging protocols. The framework will also incorporate LiDAR and camera data from field studies to validate virtual models against observed behaviors. By enabling the parallel simulation of thousands of scenario variations—including night operations, freeway work zones, and emergency response contexts—this project aims to identify optimal traffic control configurations that minimize congestion, reduce collision risks, and improve compliance with safety standards. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for training flaggers, evidence-based recommendations for revising national traffic control guidelines, and predictive models to assist in real-time decision support systems. The scale and complexity of these simulations necessitate HPC capabilities to manage large parameter spaces, process high-resolution sensor data, and execute computationally intensive optimizations within practical timeframes. This work will advance the integration of computational modeling into infrastructure safety planning, offering a transformative approach to protecting lives and optimizing traffic management in dynamic work zones.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to control the movement of traffic through construction and maintenance zones and to protect the safety of work crews, drivers, and pedestrians. Includes instruction in flagging duties and responsibilities, the traffic control zone, flagging signals, pavement markers, freeway flagging, utility flagging, emergency response flagging, and night traffic control.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic and cytogenetic datasets presents a critical challenge in diagnosing and managing human genetic diseases. Current clinical workflows struggle to integrate high-resolution molecular data (e.g., whole-genome sequencing, methylation arrays) with cytogenetic findings (e.g., karyotypes, FISH, chromosomal microarray) efficiently, particularly for rare or structural variants. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to unify multimodal genetic data, improve variant interpretation, and identify novel genotype-phenotype associations. A key barrier is the scale and heterogeneity of these datasets, which demand high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized analysis, machine learning model training, and large-scale genomic simulations. We propose leveraging HPC clusters to deploy a hybrid pipeline combining deep learning architectures for cytogenetic image analysis (e.g., automated aneuploidy detection in karyograms) with graph-based algorithms for integrating sparse clinical data and population-scale genomic databases. This pipeline will process raw sequencing data, structural variant calls, and cytogenetic image inputs to generate unified pathogenicity scores for variants of uncertain significance (VUS), prioritizing candidates for functional validation. Additionally, we will simulate population-level genomic landscapes under varying mutation rate models to benchmark the clinical sensitivity of current diagnostic assays. The computational workload involves terabytes of multi-omics data, millions of parallelized variant effect predictions, and iterative training of attention-based neural networks—tasks requiring GPU-accelerated nodes, large-memory environments, and distributed storage systems. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolset for multimodal genetic data integration, (2) validated classifiers to reduce VUS interpretation bottlenecks, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for assay selection in complex cases. By enhancing the resolution and reproducibility of clinical genomic analyses, this work directly aligns with the Laboratory Genetics and Genomics program’s mission to advance diagnostic precision in human genetic disease.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize parametric design workflows in mechanical drafting and CAD/CADD applications, with a focus on addressing inefficiencies in simulating large-scale assemblies under dynamic manufacturing constraints. Current CAD tools struggle to resolve multi-physics interactions (e.g., thermal-structural deformation in welded components) in complex mechanical systems without oversimplifying geometry or material properties, leading to costly prototyping iterations. Our research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) solvers capable of handling high-resolution meshes for assemblies exceeding 10^6 degrees of freedom. The computational approach integrates topology optimization algorithms with GPU-accelerated rendering to iteratively refine designs based on simultaneous stress, thermal, and tolerance analyses. A novel aspect involves developing machine learning surrogate models trained on HPC-generated datasets to predict deformation patterns in sheet metal forming processes, reducing simulation overhead for common drafting scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source plugin for commercial CAD platforms that enables real-time design validation against ASME Y14.5 geometric dimensioning and tolerancing standards, validated through case studies involving multi-axis machined components. By bridging the gap between traditional drafting practices and compute-intensive simulation, this work aims to reduce design cycle times by 30-50% for small-to-medium manufacturing enterprises while providing Mechanical Drafting students with cloud-accessible tools to study complex system behaviors beyond desktop software limitations. The requested computing resources will specifically support the distributed memory architecture required for large eigenvalue analyses in vibration studies and the storage needs for training dataset generation.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural communication patterns in decentralized digital communities, focusing on how emergent norms and conflict-resolution strategies develop in large-scale, non-hierarchical online networks. While prior research has examined social behavior in established platforms (e.g., Twitter, Reddit), less attention has been paid to rapidly evolving, blockchain-based forums and peer-to-peer networks where governance structures are algorithmically mediated. The study addresses a critical gap in understanding how trust, cooperation, and cultural negotiation emerge in environments lacking centralized moderation, with implications for designing equitable digital social spaces. Leveraging a multi-modal computational approach, we will analyze 12TB of anonymized interaction data (text, transaction logs, and network graphs) from three decentralized platforms using natural language processing, temporal network analysis, and agent-based modeling. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing graph-structured data with >10^8 edges, training transformer-based models on multilingual corpora, and running parallelized simulations of norm-formation processes across parameter spaces. The computational pipeline includes (1) clustering semantically similar conflict episodes using contrastive learning, (2) identifying phase transitions in community cohesion through dynamic network embedding, and (3) simulating long-term cultural convergence/divergence patterns via evolutionary game theory frameworks adapted to digital contexts. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of self-organizing governance mechanisms in decentralized societies, predictive models of cultural friction points in mixed-origin communities, and open-source tools for analyzing large-scale digital ethnography datasets. Results will contribute to theoretical frameworks at the intersection of computational social science, digital humanities, and human-computer interaction while informing practical strategies for fostering resilience in emerging online social ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of human social behavior and social institutions using any of the methodologies common to the social sciences and/or history, or an undifferentiated program of study in the social sciences.

abstract: Rural populations face disproportionate health disparities due to geographic isolation, limited healthcare infrastructure, and socioeconomic barriers. While clinical and public health datasets from these regions hold critical insights, their scale and complexity—encompassing electronic health records, genomic data, and environmental variables—exceed the processing capabilities of conventional computing systems. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets from rural communities, aiming to identify modifiable risk factors, predict disease trajectories, and optimize intervention strategies. Using machine learning models, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, we will integrate heterogeneous data sources to uncover spatial-temporal patterns in chronic disease prevalence, such as diabetes and cardiovascular conditions. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model the impact of telehealth interventions and resource allocation scenarios on health outcomes. HPC infrastructure is essential to manage petabytes of distributed health data, execute parallelized algorithms for real-time analytics, and train computationally intensive predictive models. Expected outcomes include the development of scalable frameworks for rural health surveillance, validated predictive tools for early disease detection, and evidence-based recommendations for policymakers. By enabling large-scale, data-driven insights, this research will address critical gaps in rural clinical practice and contribute to reducing health inequities for underserved populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rural Health

abstract: The oral cavity represents a complex ecosystem where microbial communities interact dynamically with host tissues, influencing health and disease states. Emerging evidence suggests that dysbiotic shifts in the oral microbiome are linked to oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), yet the mechanistic pathways and predictive biomarkers remain poorly characterized. This project seeks to integrate high-resolution metagenomic sequencing, host transcriptomic data, and spatially resolved proteomic imaging to model microbiome-host interactions in OSCC progression. A critical barrier to advancing this research is the computational demand of analyzing multi-omic datasets at scale, particularly when resolving spatial and temporal heterogeneity across tumor microenvironments. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid computational pipeline combining neural network architectures for feature extraction, Bayesian probabilistic modeling to infer causal microbial-host networks, and agent-based simulations to predict dysbiosis-driven carcinogenic pathways. The pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets from 150 OSCC patient samples, including matched tumor, adjacent normal, and distant mucosal tissues. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive spatial transcriptomic alignments and optimizing parallelized simulations of microbial community dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved microbial taxa and metabolic pathways associated with malignant transformation, (2) predictive models linking spatial microbiome patterns to immune evasion mechanisms, and (3) open-source tools for integrative analysis of multi-omic oral cancer datasets. This work will establish a computational framework to decode microbiome contributions to OSCC, offering novel targets for early detection and microbiome-modulating therapies. By addressing the unique computational demands of spatially resolved multi-omics in oral oncology, this project fills a critical niche at the intersection of microbial ecology, cancer systems biology, and clinical dentistry.
cip_title: Advanced/ Graduate Dentistry and Oral Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in advanced/graduate dentistry and oral sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The global decline in honey bee populations presents a critical challenge to agricultural productivity and ecosystem stability, with colony collapse disorder (CCD) linked to multifactorial stressors including pathogens, pesticides, and habitat fragmentation. While field studies and experimental apiaries provide foundational insights, the complex interplay of these factors across spatial, temporal, and biological scales remains poorly characterized, limiting the development of predictive models for colony resilience. This project proposes an integrated computational approach to model honey bee colony dynamics, health, and environmental interactions using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate individual and collective bee behaviors, integrating real-world data on Varroa mite infestations, pesticide exposure, and floral resource availability. Machine learning algorithms will analyze multi-year datasets from hive monitoring systems (e.g., temperature, acoustics, and weight sensors) alongside geospatial climate and land-use data to identify early warning signatures of colony stress. Parallelized simulations will explore colony-scale responses to hypothetical mitigation strategies, such as optimized forage planting or novel pest management protocols. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need to process terabyte-scale sensor datasets and run millions of parameterized ABM iterations—require GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to assess colony viability under regional climate scenarios, decision-support frameworks for beekeepers adapting management practices, and policy-relevant metrics on landscape-scale habitat requirements. By bridging behavioral ecology, epidemiology, and computational analytics, this work aims to advance precision apiculture practices, reduce overwintering mortality, and stabilize pollination services for agricultural systems dependent on honey bees.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on improving the beekeeping industry, promoting pollination of fruits and vegetables, and bee colony expansion and maintenance. Includes instruction in apiary behavior, apiary equipment and supplies, beekeeping, bee pests and parasites, handling bees, hive set up and care, queen rearing, and seasonal management practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of a computational framework for analyzing transnational policy coherence in climate adaptation strategies across developing nations. While global agreements like the Paris Accord provide high-level targets, fragmented implementation persists due to mismatches between national policies, local governance practices, and non-state actor interventions. Traditional policy analysis methods struggle to model these multiscale, dynamic interactions at the granularity required for actionable insights. Our research addresses this gap by integrating geospatial data on climate vulnerabilities, textual analysis of policy documents from 50+ countries, and agent-based simulations of institutional decision-making under resource constraints. The computational pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets spanning satellite imagery, multilingual policy texts, and longitudinal socioeconomic indicators to identify patterns in policy alignment and implementation bottlenecks. Agent-based models will simulate scenarios testing how funding mechanisms, information-sharing networks, and governance structures influence policy outcomes. Machine learning classifiers will assess semantic coherence between national adaptation plans and subnational priorities, while graph analytics will map transnational policy influence networks. HPC resources are critical due to the iterative nature of training transformer models on multilingual policy corpora, running parallelized climate impact simulations at 1km resolution, and conducting sensitivity analyses across thousands of agent-based model permutations. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for quantifying policy alignment metrics and predictive models of implementation success under varying climate scenarios. This work directly supports SDG 13 (Climate Action) by providing policymakers with evidence-based strategies to harmonize cross-border adaptation efforts while addressing the program’s focus on systemic analysis of governance challenges in global policy frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to relationships among nations and among governments and non-governmental entities. Includes instruction in international politics, governance, financial policy, and security affairs; globalization; economic and social policies of developing nations; and applications to specific public policy topics such as labor and employment, immigration, and human rights.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate cross-linguistic patterns of morphosyntactic variation in under-documented languages using computational methods, with a focus on non-Indo-European language families. The research problem centers on the scarcity of scalable frameworks for analyzing complex morphological systems and syntactic structures in languages with limited digital corpora, which hinders comparative studies and typological classification. Current methodologies in linguistic analysis often rely on manual annotation or small-scale computational tools, which are impractical for processing large, heterogeneous datasets spanning multiple language groups. To address this, the project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline integrating neural transformer models, rule-based morphological parsers, and probabilistic syntactic alignment algorithms. This pipeline will process raw text and audio-to-text corpora from 15+ low-resource languages—including Austronesian, Niger-Congo, and Trans-New Guinea families—leveraging parallel GPU-accelerated processing for feature extraction, morphological segmentation, and dependency parsing. Key challenges include managing irregular orthographies, dialectal variations, and sparse data while ensuring computational reproducibility across diverse linguistic systems. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-batch training of multilingual transformer models (e.g., XLM-RoBERTa) on distributed clusters, reducing training times for low-resource language tasks from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database of annotated morphosyntactic features for under-studied languages, 2) quantitative typological profiles revealing previously unobserved structural correlations, and 3) open-source tools optimized for cross-linguistic computational analysis. This work will advance theoretical linguistics by enabling data-driven hypotheses about language universals while providing practical resources for NLP applications in minority language contexts. The requested computing resources are critical due to the memory-intensive nature of processing agglutinative/polysynthetic languages and the need for iterative model fine-tuning across multiple GPUs.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Foreign Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address fundamental challenges in understanding reaction mechanisms and quantum dynamics at heterogeneous interfaces, which play a critical role in catalytic processes and energy conversion systems. Current experimental techniques struggle to resolve the ultrafast electronic and nuclear motions governing these processes at atomic resolution, while traditional computational models lack the accuracy or scale to capture multi-configurational quantum effects in realistic interfacial environments. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study integrating ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) with time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) and multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) methods. These simulations will model photoinduced charge transfer and bond-breaking/forming events at metal-oxide interfaces and solvated molecular systems, with explicit treatment of solvent and surface interactions. The high-performance computing (HPC) resources requested will enable large-scale parallelization for electronic structure calculations on systems exceeding 500 atoms, including long-timescale dynamics (≥100 ps) and statistically robust sampling of rare events. Key objectives include elucidating the role of solvent polarization in modulating proton-coupled electron transfer kinetics and identifying surface defects that enhance catalytic selectivity in CO2 reduction. The computational framework will leverage GPU-accelerated quantum chemistry codes (e.g., CP2K, Q-Chem) coupled with machine learning potentials to extend sampling efficiency. Expected outcomes include predictive models for interfacial charge transport and reaction branching ratios, directly informing the design of next-generation photocatalysts and energy storage materials. This work will advance molecular-level understanding of nonadiabatic phenomena at complex interfaces while developing transferable methodologies for simulating quantum dynamics in condensed-phase systems. The requested resources are essential to overcome current limitations in system size and simulation timescales, enabling unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution of coupled electronic-nuclear processes central to chemical physics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of structural phenomena combining the disciplines of physical chemistry and atomic/molecular physics. Includes instruction in heterogeneous structures, alignment and surface phenomena, quantum theory, mathematical physics, statistical and classical mechanics, chemical kinetics, and laser physics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in forensic social work, a field requiring the integration of large-scale, heterogeneous datasets to address systemic challenges in criminal justice, mental health, and social service delivery. The research problem centers on the limitations of current analytical methods in modeling complex interactions among individuals, interventions, and institutional policies. For example, predicting long-term outcomes of substance abuse treatment programs or understanding the cascading effects of trauma on recidivism involves multivariate, longitudinal datasets that exceed the capacity of conventional statistical tools. This project proposes a computational approach combining machine learning, network analysis, and agent-based modeling to analyze anonymized administrative records (e.g., criminal justice histories, mental health service usage, and program participation data) alongside unstructured data from clinical notes and victim advocacy reports. HPC resources will enable the training of deep learning models to identify risk and resilience patterns across populations, simulate the impact of policy changes on service accessibility, and optimize resource allocation strategies for underserved groups. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive tools to support early intervention for high-risk individuals, evidence-based frameworks for evaluating restorative justice programs, and scalable models for assessing equity in service delivery. By integrating computational social science methods with domain-specific expertise, this work aims to generate actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers, ultimately improving outcomes for individuals navigating overlapping legal, mental health, and social service systems. The requested computing resources are critical to managing the project’s data volume, computational complexity, and need for rapid iteration in model development, ensuring rigorous and reproducible results aligned with ethical standards for sensitive data.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as social workers in correctional facilities, mental health hospitals, the justice system, substance abuse treatment programs, and victim assistance. Includes instruction in forensic social work, criminal justice administration, domestic violence, ethics, juvenile justice systems, mental illness and crime, program evaluation, and research methods.

abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of data generated through law enforcement intelligence operations present significant challenges to traditional analytical methods, which often lack the computational capacity to efficiently integrate heterogeneous data streams or identify nuanced patterns in real time. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational frameworks for processing, analyzing, and visualizing large-scale intelligence datasets. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) optimizing the integration of structured and unstructured data from surveillance systems, financial records, social media, and geographic information systems (GIS); (2) deploying machine learning models to detect hidden relationships in criminal networks through dynamic link analysis; and (3) simulating operational scenarios to evaluate resource allocation strategies and operational security risks. Computational workflows will employ distributed computing architectures to parallelize data ingestion and model training, while graph-based algorithms and natural language processing (NLP) techniques will enhance the granularity of entity resolution and temporal pattern recognition. A key innovation involves the development of a modular analytics pipeline that aligns with legal and regulatory constraints to ensure evidentiary integrity. Anticipated outcomes include scalable tools for real-time threat assessment, improved predictive accuracy in identifying high-risk entities, and empirically validated protocols for operational planning. By enhancing the speed and precision of intelligence analysis, this project aims to strengthen law enforcement decision-making in critical areas such as organized crime interdiction, counterterrorism, and cross-jurisdictional investigations. The resulting frameworks will be disseminated as open-source resources to support training and operational use within the law enforcement community, directly contributing to the advancement of homeland security capabilities.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the preparation of law enforcement personnel to perform intelligence and surveillance operations and to analyze and use data collected via such operations. Includes instruction in the intelligence cycle, information sources, data retrieval, digital investigation, financial investigations, document analysis, external sources, geographic information systems, link analysis, operation planning and security, case management, applicable law and regulations, and case preparation.

abstract: The development of next-generation nuclear fusion reactors demands high-fidelity computational tools to address the complex multiphysics phenomena governing plasma stability, neutron transport, and materials performance under extreme conditions. Current simulations often rely on decoupled or reduced-order models due to computational limitations, leading to gaps in understanding the nonlinear interactions between magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities, neutron-induced material damage, and heat transfer in plasma-facing components. This project seeks to advance integrated, high-resolution simulations of fusion reactor systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve coupled plasma-material dynamics at unprecedented scales. The research will employ a hybrid computational framework combining finite-element MHD solvers, Monte Carlo neutron transport codes, and molecular dynamics models to capture cross-scale interactions—from macroscopic plasma behavior to atomic-scale defect evolution in tungsten-based divertors. Key challenges include optimizing parallel scalability for heterogeneous architectures, managing data-intensive workflows between physics modules, and validating simulations against experimental datasets from tokamak facilities. The HPC resources requested will enable parametric studies of reactor configurations under varying magnetic confinement scenarios, neutron flux intensities, and transient thermal loads. Expected outcomes include predictive insights into plasma edge-localized mode (ELM) suppression mechanisms, quantitative estimates of structural degradation in irradiated materials, and optimized divertor geometries to mitigate heat flux asymmetries. By bridging gaps between plasma physics and materials engineering, this work aims to accelerate the design of robust fusion systems with enhanced operational lifetimes, directly supporting global efforts to achieve sustainable fusion energy. The developed computational workflows will also be disseminated as open-source tools to foster collaboration within the fusion research community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling and manipulating nuclear energy, including nuclear power plant design, fission reactor design, fusion reactor design, reactor control and safety systems design, power transfer systems, containment vessels and structures design; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as fission and fusion processes, human and environmental factors, construction, and operational considerations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociolinguistic dynamics of understudied sign languages in digitally mediated environments, focusing on how emerging technologies shape language evolution and accessibility for Deaf communities. While sign languages are critical to cultural identity and communication, many remain under-documented, particularly in regions with limited institutional support. The research addresses two interrelated gaps: (1) the absence of large-scale computational models capable of analyzing visual-spatial linguistic features in real-time interactions, and (2) the need to quantify how digital platforms influence sign language vitality and intergenerational transmission. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will process multimodal datasets—including video recordings of naturalistic sign language use, motion-capture data, and user-generated content from Deaf-led online communities—to identify patterns in lexical innovation, grammatical variation, and cross-sign language contact. Computational methods will integrate 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial-temporal feature extraction, graph-based algorithms to model community interaction networks, and agent-based simulations to project language shift scenarios under varying technological adoption rates. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for sign language corpus analysis, predictive models of lexical convergence in digital contexts, and empirically grounded recommendations for inclusive platform design. By centering computational rigor on marginalized linguistic systems, this work advances interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of language preservation, human-computer interaction, and social equity, offering methodological innovations applicable to other embodied communication modalities. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the project’s terabyte-scale visual data and computationally intensive simulations, which exceed the capacity of standard university computing clusters.
cip_title: Linguistic, Comparative, and Related Language Studies and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in linguistic, comparative, and related language studies and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Medical insurance coding accuracy is critical for healthcare reimbursement, compliance, and operational efficiency, yet persistent challenges in coding errors and workflow delays impose significant financial and administrative burdens on healthcare systems. This project proposes the development of a machine learning (ML)-driven computational framework to analyze patterns in medical coding practices, identify systemic error sources, and optimize code assignment processes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process large-scale, de-identified datasets encompassing clinical documentation, billing records, and insurance claims from diverse healthcare settings. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to extract semantic features from unstructured clinical notes, while graph-based algorithms will map relationships between diagnostic codes, procedural terms, and insurance policy constraints. Computational workflows will integrate ensemble ML models to predict coding discrepancies, audit code-to-documentation alignment, and simulate the impact of regulatory changes (e.g., ICD updates) on coding workflows. The analysis will prioritize Medicare and commercial insurance use cases, with model validation against expert-coded datasets and compliance benchmarks. By parallelizing data preprocessing and model training across HPC nodes, we aim to overcome scalability limitations inherent in traditional coding audit tools, enabling real-time analysis of multimillion-record datasets. Anticipated outcomes include (1) identification of high-risk coding patterns contributing to claim denials, (2) predictive tools to flag documentation ambiguities during code assignment, and (3) open-source software prototypes to assist coders in code selection and compliance checks. This research directly aligns with workforce development goals in medical coding education by generating evidence-based insights into computational best practices, ultimately supporting curriculum updates focused on data-driven decision-making in health information management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized data entry, classification, and record-keeping procedures related to medical diagnostic, treatment, billing, and insurance documentation. Includes instruction in medical records and insurance software applications, basic anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, fundamentals of medical science and treatment procedures, data classification and coding, data entry skills, and regulations relating to Medicare and insurance documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the preservation of culturally significant historic structures through the development of a computational framework to model material degradation and structural vulnerabilities in aging architectural heritage. Many historic buildings feature unique, non-standardized construction materials and methods, making their conservation challenging. Current approaches rely heavily on physical inspections and localized testing, which are time-intensive and fail to capture system-wide interactions between environmental stressors, material fatigue, and structural integrity. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning, and environmental sensor data to predict long-term degradation patterns in historic masonry, timber, and composite structures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating complex, nonlinear interactions across spatial and temporal scales—from micro-crack propagation in aged mortar to macro-scale load redistribution in vaulted ceilings. The computational workflow will leverage historical climate data, material property databases, and 3D laser scans of case-study buildings to parameterize models. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and empirical datasets to identify high-risk degradation pathways and prioritize intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolset for predicting site-specific preservation needs, reducing reliance on invasive sampling, and informing climate-resilient restoration practices. By enabling dynamic, data-driven conservation planning, this research aims to extend the lifespan of heritage structures while maintaining their historical authenticity. The project bridges computational engineering, materials science, and preservation ethics, aligning with interdisciplinary priorities in historic conservation. Successful implementation will provide preservationists with evidence-based frameworks to allocate resources efficiently, particularly for underrepresented or at-risk sites with limited prior study.
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on architectural design and building techniques for historic and restored structures, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and acoustic interactions underlying advanced performance techniques in stringed instruments. While traditional pedagogical methods for instruments such as the violin, cello, or guitar rely heavily on qualitative feedback, the complex dynamics of bow-string contact, fingerboard kinematics, and resonant body behavior remain insufficiently quantified. Current computational models lack the resolution to capture micro-variations in force, motion, and sound production critical to virtuosic playing. This gap limits the development of data-driven tools for performance optimization, injury prevention, and instrument design. To address this, we propose a multimodal computational framework integrating motion capture, acoustic signal processing, and finite element modeling. High-frequency sensor data from instrument-mounted accelerometers and wearable motion trackers will be synchronized with audio recordings to correlate physical gestures with spectral outputs. Machine learning models will then analyze these datasets to identify patterns in bowing techniques, finger placement precision, and vibrato modulation. Concurrently, HPC-enabled finite element simulations will model the transient vibrational modes of instrument bodies under varying performance conditions, providing insights into how material properties and construction influence timbre and projection. By parallelizing these simulations across GPU clusters, we aim to achieve the temporal resolution necessary to resolve sub-millisecond acoustic events. The expected outcomes include predictive models linking biomechanical inputs to acoustic outputs, a publicly accessible database of annotated performance data, and real-time feedback tools for performers and educators. This research will advance the scientific understanding of stringed instrument performance while establishing scalable computational methodologies for interdisciplinary arts research. By bridging performing arts pedagogy with engineering-grade analytics, the project aims to elevate technical mastery and artistic innovation in string performance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individual to master a stringed instrument and performing arts as solo, ensemble and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: The proposed research explores the development of quantum-enhanced topological metamaterials for adaptive infrastructure systems, an emerging interdisciplinary domain bridging quantum engineering, photonics, and advanced computational mechanics. Traditional metamaterial design faces limitations in real-time adaptability and resilience under dynamic environmental stressors, such as seismic activity or thermal fluctuations. This project addresses these challenges by integrating quantum-inspired optimization algorithms with multi-physics simulations to design metamaterials with tunable topological properties. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to model the non-linear interactions between electromagnetic, mechanical, and thermal fields at multiple scales, enabling the discovery of metastructures that autonomously reconfigure their geometry and material response. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning-driven topology optimization to iteratively refine designs under stochastic loading scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for synthesizing adaptive metamaterials with applications in next-generation civil infrastructure, energy-efficient photonic devices, and deployable disaster-response systems. By advancing computational methods at the intersection of quantum engineering and materials science, this work will provide foundational insights into the dynamic control of topological states in engineered systems, while offering Pre-Engineering students hands-on experience with cutting-edge HPC tools for interdisciplinary problem-solving. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will facilitate broader academic and industrial collaboration in this nascent field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission or transfer to a baccalaureate-level program in any of the fields of engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the systemic physiological mechanisms underlying exercise intolerance in cancer survivors, with a focus on the interplay between neuromuscular efficiency, metabolic fuel utilization, and cardiovascular dynamics during graded exercise. Cancer treatments often induce persistent deficits in physical capacity, but the integrative physiological pathways driving these impairments remain poorly characterized. Current experimental models struggle to capture the real-time, multi-system interactions governing fatigue development, limiting the personalization of exercise rehabilitation protocols. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity computational model integrating neuromuscular activation patterns, substrate metabolism, and hemodynamic responses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallelized simulation of dynamic, multi-scale physiological data from 200 cancer survivors undergoing cardiopulmonary exercise testing, including breath-by-breath gas exchange, electromyography, and continuous hemodynamic monitoring. Machine learning approaches will identify critical inflection points in fatigue-related parameters across cancer types and treatment histories. The model will be validated against empirical data from a longitudinal exercise intervention trial, with iterative refinement of its predictive capacity. This computational framework will elucidate how cancer-specific physiological disruptions—such as chemotherapy-induced mitochondrial dysfunction or radiation-impaired cardiac output—constrain exercise adaptability. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for optimizing exercise prescriptions to counteract treatment-related deconditioning and a publicly accessible simulation platform for testing hypotheses about dose-response relationships in exercise oncology. By leveraging HPC capabilities to synthesize complex, time-dependent physiological data, this work advances translational kinesiology research while directly addressing the urgent need for evidence-based rehabilitation strategies in cancer survivorship care.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physiological processes involved in physical or motor activity, including sensorimotor interactions, response mechanisms, and the effects of injury, disease, and disability. Includes instruction in muscular and skeletal anatomy; molecular and cellular basis of muscle contraction; fuel utilization; neurophysiology of motor mechanics; systemic physiological responses (respiration, blood flow, endocrine secretions, and others); fatigue and exhaustion; muscle and body training; physiology of specific exercises and activities; physiology of injury; and the effects of disabilities and disease.

abstract: Pediatric dermatological disorders, such as atopic dermatitis, acne vulgaris, and congenital ichthyoses, present unique therapeutic challenges due to developmental differences in skin biology, immune responses, and pharmacokinetics in young populations. Current treatment paradigms often extrapolate from adult studies, resulting in suboptimal efficacy and safety profiles. This project aims to address this gap by developing computational models to identify pediatric-specific therapeutic targets and predict personalized treatment outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omic data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) from pediatric cohorts with clinical datasets, including electronic health records and longitudinal treatment responses. Machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to map disease subtypes to molecular pathways and drug mechanisms, accounting for age-stratified variations in skin physiology. Molecular dynamics simulations will further model drug interactions with pediatric-specific skin barrier proteins and immune receptors to optimize dosing and formulation. Key challenges include scaling these analyses across heterogeneous datasets (>50 TB) and achieving real-time predictions for clinical decision support. The HPC infrastructure is critical for parallel processing of large-scale simulations, hyperparameter optimization of predictive models, and federated learning across multi-institutional data repositories. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for treatment stratification, predictive models for adverse event risk, and a computational framework for repurposing existing therapies for pediatric populations. This work will directly inform ongoing clinical trials in pediatric dermatology and provide a scalable platform for precision medicine in understudied populations. By integrating computational and clinical research, the project seeks to improve therapeutic precision, reduce trial-and-error prescribing, and address disparities in pediatric dermatologic care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the treatment of specific skin disease categories, with emphasis on those diseases which predominate in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing technology-driven entrepreneurship, with a focus on algorithmic accountability, decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), and cross-jurisdictional compliance challenges. The rapid proliferation of emerging technologies such as blockchain, generative AI, and decentralized finance has created novel legal ambiguities that traditional statutory interpretation methods struggle to address systematically. This study proposes a computational legal analytics approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis to map precedent patterns across 10 million pages of case law, administrative rulings, and international regulatory guidance. Custom transformer models will be trained to identify latent policy priorities in judicial decisions affecting startup liability, while graph neural networks will model the cascading effects of regulatory changes on innovation ecosystems. The computational workload requires parallelized processing of heterogeneous legal texts across multiple jurisdictions, necessitating GPU-accelerated clusters for transformer model training and high-memory nodes for large-scale network simulations. Expected outcomes include a dynamic visualization platform tracking regulatory risk exposure for entrepreneurial ventures and a predictive framework quantifying how hypothetical policy interventions might influence innovation rates in specific technology sectors. By bridging legal hermeneutics with computational social science methods, this project aims to establish an evidence-based paradigm for evaluating entrepreneurship law's impact on economic ecosystems while maintaining compliance with ethical AI governance standards. The resulting tools could inform legislative reforms and help startups navigate complex compliance landscapes without stifling technological experimentation.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting entrepreneurship and innovation.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical inefficiencies in culinary operations management, specifically targeting dynamic optimization challenges in multi-venue catering enterprises. The culinary industry faces persistent issues in resource allocation, including real-time menu adaptation to ingredient availability, energy-efficient kitchen workflow scheduling, and predictive logistics for perishable goods across distributed event sites. Traditional heuristic methods fail to account for the high-dimensional variables—such as fluctuating supplier costs, staff mobility constraints, and real-time guest dietary preference tracking—that define modern large-scale catering ecosystems. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, mixed-integer linear programming, and transformer-based neural networks to simulate and optimize decision-making processes across catering operations. The HPC environment will enable parallelized scenario testing of kitchen staff routing algorithms under stochastic demand patterns, multi-objective optimization of seasonal menu portfolios considering regional ingredient carbon footprints, and ensemble forecasting of equipment maintenance needs using sensor data from commercial kitchen IoT networks. By scaling these analyses to enterprise-level datasets encompassing over 500 historical events and 3M+ ingredient transactions, the computational approach aims to derive adaptive management policies that reduce food waste by an estimated 15-22%, improve staff utilization rates by 20%, and decrease fuel consumption in catering logistics by 12-18%. The resulting open-source optimization toolkit will provide the hospitality industry with actionable insights for sustainable operations while advancing computational methodology in culinary systems engineering—an emerging interdisciplinary domain combining gastronomic sciences, operations research, and sustainability analytics.
