cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage food and beverage preparation and service operations, restaurant facilities, and catering services.  Includes instruction in food/beverage industry operations, cost control, purchasing and storage, business administration, logistics, personnel management, culinary arts, restaurant and menu planning, executive chef functions, event planning and management, health and safety, insurance, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: The increasing burden of infectious diseases in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) demands innovative approaches to model complex disease dynamics and evaluate intervention strategies. Current limitations in computational power restrict the ability to simulate large-scale, spatially explicit models that integrate demographic, environmental, and behavioral data—critical factors influencing disease transmission in resource-constrained settings. This project proposes the development of an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to analyze the spread of malaria in sub-Saharan Africa, incorporating high-resolution climate data, population mobility patterns, and heterogeneous healthcare access. The model will simulate transmission dynamics under varying scenarios, including climate change projections, insecticide resistance trends, and intervention strategies such as targeted vaccine distribution and bed-net campaigns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the scale of these simulations, which involve millions of agents, stochastic parameter sampling, and iterative optimization of intervention parameters. Parallel computing will enable sensitivity analyses to quantify uncertainty in model outputs, while machine learning techniques will identify key predictors of intervention success from simulated and real-world surveillance data. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into cost-effective intervention combinations tailored to regional disparities in healthcare infrastructure and environmental risk factors. The computational framework will be designed for adaptability, allowing future application to other vector-borne or infectious diseases in LMICs. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance evidence-based policymaking in international health, directly supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to health equity and epidemic preparedness. The project will also produce open-source tools to empower local researchers and health agencies in LMICs to conduct similar analyses, fostering long-term capacity in data-driven public health decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, the social and behavioral sciences, and policy and communications methods to the study of health problems in low- and middle-income countries and regions, and prepares individuals to function as professional international health specialists. Includes instruction in health education and promotion, research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, public nutrition and food security, information systems, program evaluation, medical anthropology, international communication, behavioral sciences, maternal and child health, demography and population policy, and health care finance and economics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in autonomous ground vehicle (AGV) fleet coordination for mixed-traffic urban environments through advanced computational modeling. Current AGV control systems struggle to optimize routing, energy use, and collision avoidance at scale when interacting with human-operated vehicles, particularly during peak congestion scenarios. The proposed work will develop a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging agent-based modeling and reinforcement learning (RL) to analyze multi-vehicle interactions across diverse urban layouts and traffic patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training deep RL policies on millions of simulated agent-hours while maintaining real-world physics constraints through parallelized Unity3D and SUMO traffic simulations. The computational workflow will integrate vehicle sensor data streams, traffic light control systems, and pedestrian movement predictors in a distributed computing environment, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and CPU clusters for large-scale scenario testing. Expected outcomes include optimized AGV coordination algorithms that reduce average urban commute times by 12-18% in simulated environments while maintaining ASIL-D safety standards. The resulting open-source framework will provide municipal planners and automotive manufacturers with validated tools for deploying mixed fleets in smart city networks. By resolving computational bottlenecks in multi-agent trajectory prediction, this work advances the operational limits of ground transportation systems while establishing benchmarks for HPC-enabled mobility research. Resource allocation will directly support critical path operations including hyperparameter optimization across 10,000+ concurrent simulations and validation against real-world traffic datasets from 15 metropolitan regions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle and equipment operation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across Latin America and the Caribbean through large-scale textual and visual analysis. The research problem centers on the fragmented preservation of regionally significant, non-institutionalized cultural outputs—including community-produced zines, oral history transcripts, and grassroots visual media—which are often dispersed across physical archives or digitized in unstructured formats. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to systematically analyze these materials at scale, limiting interdisciplinary insights into how marginalized communities negotiate cultural memory and identity in postcolonial contexts. The project will employ computational text mining, multimodal neural networks, and geospatial network analysis to process multilingual corpora (Spanish, Portuguese, Creole, and indigenous languages) and image datasets from 15 countries, spanning 1945–2020. Custom transformer models will be fine-tuned to recognize vernacular linguistic patterns and cross-modal semantic relationships, while graph-based algorithms will map the diffusion of narrative themes across diasporic networks. Computational workflows will integrate privacy-preserving federated learning techniques to accommodate ethically sensitive materials. Anticipated outcomes include the first open-access repository of computationally enriched cultural metadata for the region, revealing understudied transnational connections in grassroots cultural production. The work will directly support emerging scholarship in decolonial digital humanities while providing a template for ethically grounded HPC applications in area studies. Resource requests emphasize GPU nodes for model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous data types, and scalable memory for cross-regional network simulations.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in the preservation, accessibility, and semantic enrichment of culturally significant but computationally intensive archival materials, such as digitized historical manuscripts, multimedia collections, and born-digital records. Current library and archival workflows struggle to efficiently process, analyze, and contextualize large-scale heterogeneous datasets due to limitations in existing tools, which are often siloed, resource-constrained, or designed for narrowly defined formats. The research problem centers on developing scalable computational methods to automate metadata generation, enhance searchability, and predict degradation risks for fragile or obsolete digital assets. Planned approaches include deploying machine learning models to identify latent patterns in unstructured text and image corpora, simulating decay processes in aging digital formats via probabilistic modeling, and optimizing graph-based frameworks for cross-repository knowledge linkage. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of terabyte-scale collections, training of domain-adapted vision-language models for context-aware annotation, and iterative testing of preservation strategies under varied environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic prioritization of at-risk materials, semantically enriched discovery interfaces, and adaptive workflows that reduce manual intervention in archival curation. By integrating computational resilience planning with user-centered access design, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for sustainable digital stewardship while addressing critical gaps in library and archival training programs, particularly in computational literacy and emergent technology integration. The project’s interdisciplinary focus bridges archival science, data ethics, and computational linguistics, advancing both the theoretical and practical foundations of digital cultural heritage management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist professional librarians and archivists. Includes instruction in principles, systems, processes, and procedures of library and archive operation; library resources and services; processes of acquisition, cataloging, storage, and display systems; discovery and retrieval of requested materials; and management of books, periodicals, and other documents and records.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in agricultural business decision-making caused by fragmented and heterogeneous data streams. Modern agricultural operations generate vast datasets from precision farming sensors, supply chain logistics, market price fluctuations, and climate models, yet integrating these datasets for actionable insights remains computationally prohibitive for small-to-medium agribusinesses. Our research focuses on developing a scalable computational framework to unify these disparate data sources, enabling real-time analytics for crop yield optimization, cost forecasting, and risk mitigation. The proposed work combines machine learning (ML) models—including transformer-based architectures for time-series market data and convolutional neural networks for satellite imagery analysis—with agent-based simulations of agricultural supply chains. Key computational challenges include processing high-resolution geospatial datasets (10-100 TB scale), training multi-modal ML models with asynchronous data inputs, and simulating stochastic market-climate interactions across parametric scenarios. HPC resources are critical to parallelize model training, optimize hyperparameter searches, and run ensemble simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include an open-source analytics platform tailored for agricultural cooperatives, validated against case studies in Midwestern U.S. soybean and livestock operations. This work will provide empirically grounded tools to improve resource allocation decisions, reduce operational waste, and enhance profitability for agribusinesses operating in climate-volatile regions. By quantifying the economic value of integrated data systems, the project also aims to inform policy incentives for technology adoption in underserved agricultural communities. The computational workflows developed will be documented for reuse in similar agricultural technology applications, fostering broader innovation in the sector.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized support functions related to agricultural business offices and operations and to operate agricultural office equipment, software, and information systems. Includes instruction in basic agricultural business principles, office management, equipment operation, standard software, and database management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biochemical and environmental interactions influencing tissue preservation efficacy in embalming processes, a critical yet understudied area in mortuary science. Current embalming practices rely on empirically derived protocols, which may not account for dynamic variables such as microbial resistance, tissue heterogeneity, or environmental stressors post-embalming. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive tools to optimize embalming fluid formulations and application methods for diverse biological and cultural scenarios, including cases of advanced decomposition or specific religious requirements. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Agent-based modeling will simulate microbial colonization dynamics in human tissues under varying embalming chemical concentrations, while finite element analysis will map fluid diffusion rates in tissues with distinct structural integrity (e.g., trauma vs. natural decay). Machine learning models, trained on spectral data from thanatochemistry experiments, will predict oxidative degradation patterns of embalming agents in different climatic conditions. The computational pipeline will integrate these components to generate adaptive preservation strategies tailored to individual cases. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for virtual testing of embalming protocols, reducing reliance on trial-and-error in sensitive scenarios. This work will directly contribute to enhancing restorative outcomes, addressing public health concerns in delayed interments, and supporting culturally specific preservation requirements. By bridging computational science and mortuary practice, the project establishes a foundation for data-driven innovation in a field where technological integration remains nascent. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the high parametric variability in tissue-microbe-chemical systems and to achieve the spatial-temporal resolution required for clinically actionable results.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for licensure as embalmers and morticians.  Includes instruction in pathogenic microbiology, systematic pathology, thanatochemistry, gross anatomy, clinical mortuary science, embalming, restorative art, applicable laws and regulations, and special services such as cremation and preparations required by specific religious communities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing large-scale music performance datasets to enhance pedagogical strategies in music teacher education. A critical challenge in training music educators is the lack of data-driven tools to systematically evaluate how novice instructors adapt to diverse student needs, particularly in real-time classroom settings. Current methods rely on subjective assessments or small-scale observational studies, limiting generalizable insights. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model multimodal data—including audio recordings of student performances, video analyses of teaching techniques, and longitudinal learning outcomes—from a network of partnered K–12 music programs. The computational approach will integrate signal processing for audio feature extraction (e.g., pitch accuracy, rhythmic precision), computer vision for evaluating teacher-student interactions, and machine learning to identify patterns linking instructional methods to student progress. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU nodes, we aim to analyze terabyte-scale datasets spanning 5,000+ hours of classroom interactions, enabling the detection of subtle, actionable correlations imperceptible through manual review. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model to recommend personalized teaching interventions based on student performance metrics and (2) an open-access repository of annotated pedagogical scenarios for use in music education curricula. This work will provide empirical foundations for evidence-based training frameworks, directly addressing the program’s mission to advance adaptive, equitable music instruction. The scale of data processing and real-time simulation requirements—particularly for training neural networks on temporal pedagogical sequences—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust results within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach music and music appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural dynamics of social inequality through large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis. The research problem centers on understanding how micro-level interactions—such as those influenced by institutional policies, economic shocks, or demographic shifts—propagate systemic inequalities across social networks over time. Traditional sociological methods face limitations in simulating complex, nonlinear feedback loops inherent in such systems, particularly when scaling to population-level analyses. To address this, the project will develop computational models that integrate granular demographic microdata, longitudinal survey data, and policy records to simulate multi-generational social mobility patterns under varying conditions. Key methodological challenges include optimizing parallelized simulations for heterogeneous agent behaviors, managing memory-intensive network datasets (e.g., kinship or professional ties across synthetic populations), and validating models against historical inequality trajectories using Bayesian calibration techniques. The HPC infrastructure will enable iterative scenario testing at unprecedented scales, such as simulating the cascading effects of educational access policies across 10 million+ agent populations with dynamic attribute updates. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying critical leverage points in social systems where targeted interventions could disrupt path-dependent inequality, (2) generating open-source simulation frameworks for reproducibility in sociological computational research, and (3) producing policy-relevant insights into the long-term impacts of algorithmic bias in resource allocation systems. By bridging computational scalability with sociological theory, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in demography and stratification research while contributing empirical evidence to debates on equity in institutional decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human social institutions and social relationships. Includes instruction in social theory, sociological research methods, social organization and structure, social stratification and hierarchies, dynamics of social change, family structures, social deviance and control, and applications to the study of specific social groups, social institutions, and social problems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between human movement, choreographic structures, and computational modeling in contemporary dance practice. While traditional dance research relies on qualitative analysis and manual notation systems, the scale and dimensionality of movement data in ensemble choreography present challenges that exceed conventional methods. The research problem centers on developing a framework to analyze and simulate emergent patterns in group choreography, with a focus on how individual dancers’ kinematic decisions propagate through ensembles to create collective aesthetic outcomes. The computational approach integrates motion capture data from live performances with agent-based modeling to simulate choreographic dynamics under varying parameters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabytes of high-frequency motion capture data, training recurrent neural networks to identify movement motifs, and running large-scale simulations of dancer interactions in virtual environments. Machine learning pipelines will classify movement signatures across cultural dance traditions, while parallelized physics simulations will model the biomechanical constraints of multi-dancer systems. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dance movement sequences, tools for generative choreography assisted by AI, and quantitative metrics for assessing collective coordination in performance. This work bridges computational science and artistic practice, offering new methods to preserve intangible cultural heritage in dance and enabling choreographers to explore complex spatial-temporal relationships at scales impractical for human-led experimentation. The requested resources will directly support the first systematic study of self-organization principles in dance ensembles, with implications for both performing arts pedagogy and interdisciplinary research in complex systems.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dance, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing sustainable urban design through the integration of multi-agent behavioral modeling, generative design algorithms, and life-cycle environmental impact analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in current urban planning paradigms, which often fail to reconcile dynamic human behavior patterns with long-term ecological sustainability at neighborhood-scale resolutions. Using high-performance computing resources, the team will simulate complex interactions between pedestrian movement patterns, microclimate conditions, and material performance across temporal scales ranging from diurnal cycles to decadal weathering processes. The computational approach combines discrete element modeling for structural stress analysis with reinforcement learning agents trained on historical urban heat island data and real-time energy consumption patterns from smart city networks. A novel aspect of the methodology involves developing graph neural networks to predict emergent spatial configurations that minimize embodied carbon while maintaining cultural heritage preservation parameters extracted from architectural archives. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of generating Pareto-optimal urban layouts under climate uncertainty constraints, validated against sensor data from three pilot cities undergoing sustainable retrofitting. The computational intensity stems from coupling 4D finite element analysis (simulating material degradation under projected climate scenarios) with agent-based crowd dynamics operating at city-block resolution. This work advances the emerging field of computational urban ecology by creating decision-support tools that bridge architectural design principles with complex systems science, ultimately enabling data-driven policies for equitable climate resilience in heterogeneous urban landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, physical, and social science in the design of sustainable cities and metropolitan regions. Includes instruction in community revitalization, community economic development, construction technology, design innovation, environmental economics, ethics, justice and politics, sustainable materials, sustainability theory, structural materials, and urbanism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the complex, multifactorial interactions underlying patient outcomes in integrative medicine, with a focus on personalized treatment optimization. Integrative medicine emphasizes holistic care, combining conventional therapies with evidence-based complementary approaches, yet the lack of predictive tools to evaluate how biological, behavioral, and environmental variables interact limits the scalability of personalized interventions. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, multi-omics profiles, patient-reported lifestyle data, and clinical trial outcomes—to identify dynamic predictors of treatment response. We propose using high-performance computing (HPC) to implement ensemble machine learning models capable of handling high-dimensional, longitudinal data while preserving interpretability for clinical use. Computational workflows will include federated learning to address data privacy concerns across institutions, network analysis to map bidirectional relationships between physiological systems and therapeutic modalities, and agent-based modeling to simulate patient-practitioner decision-making processes in diverse care scenarios. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale combinatorial optimization of treatment protocols. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational platform to (1) predict individual responses to integrative care plans, (2) identify novel biomarkers of treatment synergy or antagonism between therapies, and (3) generate actionable clinical decision support tools that balance quantitative evidence with patient preferences. By enabling real-time analysis of complex health trajectories, this resource will advance rigorous, data-driven methods in integrative medicine while preserving its humanistic focus, ultimately supporting research into precision care models that unify biomedical, psychosocial, and lifestyle dimensions of healing.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine in a way that reaffirms the importance of the relationship between practitioner and patient; focuses on the whole person; is informed by evidence; and makes use of all appropriate therapeutic approaches, healthcare professionals, and disciplines to achieve optimal health and healing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision agriculture strategies for optimizing crop yield resilience under dynamic environmental stressors. A critical challenge in modern crop production is predicting how genotype-environment-management (G×E×M) interactions influence phenotypic outcomes across diverse agroecosystems. Traditional field trials and simplified statistical models lack the resolution to account for the nonlinear interactions between genetic traits, soil heterogeneity, microclimate variability, and pest pressures. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating mechanistic crop growth models, machine learning, and spatially explicit environmental datasets. The research will parameterize process-based models (e.g., APSIM, DSSAT) with high-resolution soil moisture data, drone-derived canopy imagery, and genomic markers linked to stress tolerance in staple crops. Bayesian optimization algorithms will identify management interventions that maximize yield stability under simulated drought, heat, and pest infestation scenarios. A key innovation involves coupling agent-based pest dispersal models with crop physiology simulations to evaluate integrated pest management strategies at landscape scales. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the iterative nature of ensemble climate simulations (CMIP6 downscaled projections), parameter calibration across millions of genotype-environment combinations, and real-time sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include open-source decision support tools for farmers, optimized cultivar recommendations tailored to regional climate forecasts, and dynamically updated risk maps for pest outbreaks. By elucidating G×E×M trade-offs, this work will directly inform breeding programs and sustainable intensification practices, enhancing food security while minimizing input waste. The requested HPC resources will enable the scaling of simulations to cover major U.S. agricultural regions, with methodology transferable to global cropping systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cultivate grain, fiber, forage, oilseed, fruits and nuts, vegetables, and other domesticated plant products. Includes instruction in basic principles of plant science, health, and nutrition as applied to particular species and breeds; soil preparation and irrigation; pest management; planting and harvesting operations; product marketing; and applicable issues of safety, regulation, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and analyze complex flight training scenarios, addressing critical gaps in current flight instructor methodologies. Traditional pilot training relies heavily on static scenarios and generalized protocols, which often fail to account for the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between human decision-making, environmental variables, and aircraft performance. The research problem centers on optimizing scenario-based training for flight instructors by modeling rare but high-risk events—such as extreme weather recovery, multi-system failures, and airspace congestion—under physiologically realistic pilot stress conditions. To achieve this, the project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run large-scale Monte Carlo simulations integrating aerodynamic models, human performance data, and real-time atmospheric datasets. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict aircraft behavior under degraded systems, while agent-based modeling will simulate air traffic interactions and trainee responses. The simulations will incorporate FAA regulatory parameters, enabling scenario validation against certification standards. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source training module that quantifies risk mitigation strategies, personalized trainee performance benchmarks, and data-driven recommendations for updating flight crew operational guidelines. By enabling instructors to dynamically adjust scenarios based on probabilistic outcomes, this work aims to reduce skill decay in commercial pilots and enhance adaptive training for emerging technologies, such as electric propulsion systems and advanced avionics. The HPC infrastructure is essential to process terabytes of spatially resolved meteorological data, resolve microsecond-scale control inputs, and parallelize thousands of training iterations. Results will be disseminated through FAA-sponsored workshops and integrated into accredited flight instructor curricula, directly supporting the program’s mission to align technical education with evolving aviation safety demands.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the training of pilots or navigators, to prepare them to fly and/or navigate commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue aircraft, and fixed or rotary wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications and navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to administer the FAA commercial air crew examinations.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model the neurocognitive and behavioral effects of drama therapy interventions, with a focus on optimizing therapeutic protocols for individuals with trauma-related dissociation. Drama therapy employs embodied, narrative-based techniques to address fragmented self-perception and emotional dysregulation, but the neural and cognitive mechanisms underlying its efficacy remain poorly understood. The research problem centers on identifying how specific drama therapy methods (e.g., role reversal, sociodramatic metaphor) dynamically engage distributed brain networks involved in autobiographical memory, emotional processing, and self-referential thought. To address this, we will integrate multimodal data from wearable biosensors (EEG, electrodermal activity), motion capture systems, and therapist-client interaction logs collected during structured drama therapy sessions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to implement a multilayer network analysis pipeline that combines dynamic functional connectivity modeling with natural language processing of session transcripts and kinematic feature extraction. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) creating personalized brain-body interaction graphs using time-locked neural and physiological data, (2) training transformer-based models to detect linguistic markers of therapeutic breakthroughs in session narratives, and (3) developing agent-based simulations of therapist-client co-regulation dynamics. Expected outcomes include a predictive model correlating specific dramatic intervention sequences with normalized connectivity patterns in the default mode and salience networks, validated against longitudinal clinical outcomes. This work will establish the first quantitative framework for optimizing drama therapy protocols in trauma care while preserving the art-based integrity of interventions. The computational tools developed will enable real-time adaptive therapy design and provide foundational insights into how performative embodiment influences neurocognitive integration—advancing both therapeutic practice and interdisciplinary understanding of arts-based healing mechanisms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in association with a rehabilitation team or in private practice, to use dramatic play, theater, role play, psychodrama, and dramatic ritual in therapeutic relationships to address the physical, psychological, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of clients. Includes instruction in drama theory and performance, human growth and development, biomedical sciences, abnormal psychology, disabling conditions, patient assessment and diagnosis, treatment plan development and implementation, clinical evaluation, record-keeping, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern platemaking and digital imaging workflows, which face growing demands for precision, speed, and sustainability in the communication and journalism sectors. Traditional plate production methods and direct-to-press workflows often struggle with material waste, inconsistent quality in high-resolution outputs, and computational bottlenecks when processing complex graphic datasets. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes the development of a scalable computational framework to optimize image rendering, plate surface simulation, and color calibration processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to support large-scale image analysis, including the training of machine learning models to predict plate degradation patterns under varying press conditions, as well as GPU-accelerated simulations of ink dispersion dynamics on novel substrate materials. The project will integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as 3D surface scans, spectral color profiles, and press performance metrics—into a unified optimization pipeline, leveraging parallelized algorithms to reduce computational overhead in preprocessing workflows. Expected outcomes include a reduction in material waste by 20–30% through predictive modeling of plate longevity, improved color fidelity in high-speed printing environments, and a 40–50% acceleration in digital prepress workflows for complex graphic designs. By bridging gaps between traditional platemaking techniques and data-driven computational methods, this work will enhance the sustainability and technical capacity of imaging workflows critical to publishing, packaging, and digital media production. The requested HPC resources will enable iterative testing of hybrid (physical-digital) workflow models at scales unachievable with local computing infrastructure, directly benefiting academic training programs in platemaking and industry partners seeking to adopt next-generation imaging systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare film, digital data, and surfaces to reproduce printed or graphic images. Includes instruction in platemaking, stripping, camerawork, imposition, digital imaging, computer direct-to-plate and direct-to-press, and related processes.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of regulatory compliance frameworks by developing a computational model to simulate and predict the cascading impacts of multi-jurisdictional legal changes on organizational compliance strategies. The research problem centers on the dynamic, interdependent nature of modern compliance obligations, where updates to financial regulations, data privacy laws, and industry-specific mandates create compound effects that traditional legal analysis struggles to anticipate. Using high-performance computing resources, the project will process and analyze 1.2+ terabytes of structured and unstructured regulatory data spanning 15 jurisdictions, including legislative texts, enforcement actions, and case law from 2010–2024. Computational methods will combine natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of legal amendments with graph-based network modeling to map dependencies between regulatory clauses. A machine learning layer will train on historical compliance violation patterns to identify high-risk intersections between evolving requirements. The proposed simulations will model hypothetical regulatory change scenarios, quantifying their potential operational impacts through probabilistic risk scoring. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for compliance officers to visualize regulatory exposure hotspots and test mitigation strategies under varying conditions. By bridging computational social science methods with legal informatics, this work aims to advance predictive capabilities in compliance risk management while establishing scalable methodologies for analyzing large-scale legal systems. The requested computing resources are critical for maintaining low-latency processing of real-time regulatory updates and enabling complex network analyses that exceed the capacity of standard legal research platforms.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in compliance, ethics, internal monitoring, regulatory affairs, and related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing multiphysics simulations for advanced engineering systems. A core research problem in engineering technologies lies in accurately modeling interactions between mechanical, thermal, and fluid dynamics phenomena in complex systems such as energy-efficient HVAC components, additive manufacturing processes, and composite material structures. Traditional computational methods often fail to resolve these coupled processes at relevant scales due to prohibitive computational costs, limiting predictive accuracy and design innovation. To overcome this barrier, the proposed work will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) within a modular simulation framework, enabling high-resolution modeling of transient multiphysics behavior. The computational approach will integrate adaptive mesh refinement algorithms to dynamically allocate resources to regions of high gradients or interfacial activity, coupled with GPU-accelerated solvers for efficient large-scale matrix operations. Validation cases will focus on turbulent heat transfer in microchannel heat exchangers and residual stress evolution during metal 3D printing, using experimental data from collaborating industry partners. The requested HPC resources will support parametric studies across diverse operating conditions, material properties, and geometric configurations, with simulations targeting 10⁶–10⁷ degrees of freedom. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing energy efficiency in thermal systems, reducing material waste in manufacturing, and accelerating the development of lightweight structural composites. By providing open-source simulation templates and performance benchmarks, this work will directly enhance the capabilities of engineering technology researchers and practitioners to address real-world design challenges through computationally informed decision-making. The resource allocation will also facilitate training opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students in HPC-driven engineering analysis, bridging critical gaps between theoretical principles and industrial applications.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in a wide variety of projects. Includes instruction in various engineering support functions for research, production, and operations, and applications to specific engineering specialties.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives within Asian-American communities using large-scale textual and multimedia archives. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in how intergenerational memory, diasporic identity, and community solidarity are represented across time and regional contexts, with a focus on understudied groups such as Hmong-American and Filipino-American populations. Current scholarship lacks systematic methods to process heterogeneous, multilingual primary sources—including oral history transcripts, community newspapers, digital media, and literary works—at the scale required to detect nuanced cultural shifts. To address this gap, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for code-switched text (e.g., Tagalog-English) and transformer-based architectures fine-tuned on Asian-American literary corpora. Computational workflows will integrate temporal network analysis to map conceptual relationships in community discourse and multimodal neural networks to analyze visual motifs in self-published zines and protest art. High-performance computing resources are critical for training custom embedding models on our curated dataset of 750,000+ documents spanning 1945–2020 and for running iterative simulations of cultural diffusion patterns across migration waves. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access repository of annotated Asian-American narrative datasets, 2) computational models that account for intersectional identity factors in cultural analytics, and 3) visualizations tracing the impact of historical events like the 1965 Immigration Act on community storytelling practices. By enabling large-scale analysis of cultural production beyond traditional close-reading methods, this work will provide new empirical foundations for understanding how marginalized communities negotiate identity in transnational contexts. The requested resources directly support algorithmic development requiring GPU-accelerated processing of non-standard linguistic data and storage for petascale multimedia collections.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of Asian population groups who have immigrated to the United States and Canada, or sought refugee asylum, from the colonial period to the present, and including Chinese-Americans, Japanese-Americans, Korean-Americans, Vietnamese-Americans, Cambodian-Americans, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of enhancing pedagogical strategies in drama and dance teacher education through advanced computational analysis of movement and instructional dynamics. Traditional methods for training educators in these disciplines often rely on subjective evaluations of teaching efficacy and student performance, limiting opportunities for scalable, data-driven refinement of classroom practices. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets from simulated and real-world teaching environments. Motion capture technology and audiovisual recordings will generate high-resolution kinematic and behavioral data from student-teachers and learners during practice sessions. These datasets will be processed using machine learning models to quantify relationships between pedagogical techniques—such as verbal feedback, demonstration quality, and spatial positioning—and learner engagement or skill acquisition. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, training of deep neural networks to classify effective teaching behaviors, and agent-based simulations of classroom interactions under varying instructional scenarios. Expected outcomes include the development of a computational framework to identify optimal teaching practices tailored to diverse learning styles, as well as interactive tools for student-teachers to visualize and iteratively refine their methods. This work will provide the first large-scale empirical analysis of drama and dance pedagogy, offering transformative insights into how computational approaches can democratize access to high-quality arts education training. Results will be disseminated through open-source pedagogical modules integrated into teacher education curricula, fostering evidence-based advancements in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach drama and/or dance programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of large-scale, algorithmically driven multimedia installations that integrate real-time data processing, generative visual systems, and interactive audience engagement. A central challenge in contemporary intermedia practice lies in scaling complex, dynamic artworks that synthesize heterogeneous inputs—such as environmental sensors, biometric feedback, or crowdsourced digital content—into cohesive, responsive visual environments. Traditional single-node systems struggle to manage the latency, parallel computation, and data throughput required for seamless integration of these components, particularly when operating at architectural or public-space scales. The proposed work will utilize GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines and distributed computing frameworks to process multi-modal data streams, train lightweight machine learning models for adaptive audience interaction, and simulate emergent behavior in particle-based visual systems. Key computational methods include the deployment of containerized microservices for modular input/output handling, neural style transfer optimized for real-time video synthesis, and agent-based modeling to govern generative aesthetics. By enabling the creation of artworks that dynamically reconfigure themselves in response to live inputs at unprecedented scales, this project aims to expand the technical and expressive possibilities of computational intermedia. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly exhibited installation demonstrating these capabilities, alongside open-source toolkits for scalable multimedia workflows. The research bridges gaps between data-driven art, human-computer interaction, and high-performance computing, offering new methodologies for resource-intensive creative practice while contributing to interdisciplinary discourse on computational aesthetics and participatory media systems.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions in either two or three dimensions, through simultaneous use of a variety of materials and media.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research at the intersection of vocal performance, physiology, and computational modeling. The human voice is a complex instrument shaped by biomechanical, aerodynamic, and neuromuscular interactions, yet traditional pedagogical methods in opera and voice training often rely on subjective feedback and qualitative assessments. This research addresses the critical gap in quantitatively analyzing vocal production dynamics and their relationship to performance efficacy, vocal health, and stylistic expression. By integrating computational models of vocal fold vibration, respiratory kinematics, and articulatory motion, we aim to simulate and optimize performance techniques across diverse repertoires and physiological profiles. The computational approach employs finite element modeling to simulate vocal fold dynamics under varying subglottal pressures and muscle activation patterns, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on multimodal performance data (audio, electromyography, and motion capture). These models will be validated against empirical datasets collected from professional singers performing standardized exercises and operatic excerpts. The scale of these simulations—requiring real-time processing of high-resolution biomechanical data and iterative parameter optimization—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallelized computation and large-scale data storage. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to identify vocal strain risks, personalized feedback systems for technical refinement, and evidence-based frameworks for repertoire selection tailored to individual physiological constraints. This work will not only advance pedagogical practices in voice training but also establish a novel computational paradigm for studying artistic performance, with implications for injury prevention and interdisciplinary collaborations between performing arts and computational science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the human voice and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers in concert, choir, opera, or other forms of singing. Includes instruction in voice pedagogy, diction, vocal physiology and exercise, expressive movement, repertoire, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating and mitigating privacy breaches in large-scale healthcare data ecosystems. As healthcare organizations increasingly adopt distributed cloud platforms and interoperable systems, the attack surface for sensitive health data expands, creating vulnerabilities that existing threat models and compliance tools often fail to anticipate. The research problem centers on the insufficiency of conventional risk assessment methods to model multi-step adversarial attacks that exploit interactions between legacy systems, third-party applications, and emerging data-sharing architectures. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining graph-based anomaly detection, adversarial machine learning simulations, and cryptographic protocol stress-testing. Computational workflows will model hospital networks as dynamic heterogeneous graphs (5-10 million nodes) to identify latent vulnerabilities in access control hierarchies. Parallel Monte Carlo simulations will assess probabilistic risks of re-identification attacks on partially de-identified datasets under varying compliance regimes. Cryptographic penetration testing will employ GPU-accelerated brute-force and side-channel attacks to evaluate post-quantum encryption candidates for health data at rest. The HPC environment is critical for maintaining requisite scale in simulating hospital network topologies (OpenMPI), training graph neural networks on anonymized insurance claim datasets (200+ TB, PyTorch Distributed), and optimizing lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes (CUDA). Expected outcomes include an open-source risk quantification toolkit that predicts breach likelihoods 12-18 months ahead of current compliance audit cycles, plus evidence-based recommendations for hardening hybrid cloud architectures. By enabling real-world simulation of coordinated cyber-physical attacks on health data infrastructures, this work aims to advance proactive privacy preservation strategies while maintaining computational feasibility for resource-constrained healthcare providers.
cip_title: Healthcare Information Privacy Assurance and Security
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers in designing, implementing, and administering comprehensive privacy and security protection programs in all types of healthcare organizations. Includes instruction in health information ethics, healthcare information privacy and security, healthcare compliance, healthcare information security and disaster recovery, and healthcare privacy law.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying stress adaptation in agriculturally significant plant species. Climate change and environmental degradation increasingly threaten global crop productivity, necessitating rapid identification of genetic loci associated with drought tolerance, pathogen resistance, and nutrient-use efficiency. While advances in plant genomics have generated vast datasets—including whole-genome sequences, chromatin accessibility profiles, and methylation states for diverse cultivars—integrating these multi-omics layers to pinpoint functional regulatory elements remains computationally prohibitive using conventional resources. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze terabyte-scale genomic datasets from maize (Zea mays) and rice (Oryza sativa), focusing on structural variations and epigenetic modifications correlated with stress-responsive phenotypes. A hybrid pipeline combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with deep learning models will identify candidate cis-regulatory regions and quantify their pleiotropic effects across environments. Population genomic analyses will further reconstruct evolutionary trajectories of these loci under selective pressures. Computational demands include large-memory nodes for de novo genome assembly of non-reference cultivars, GPU-accelerated training of convolutional neural networks to predict enhancer-promoter interactions, and parallelized population genetics simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a prioritized list of haplotype-specific regulatory elements driving phenotypic variation, (2) predictive models linking epigenetic states to gene expression under stress, and (3) evolutionary inference frameworks to distinguish adaptive mutations from drift. These results will directly inform marker-assisted breeding programs and provide foundational insights into how chromatin architecture shapes plant adaptation. The scale of data (≥50 TB) and need for real-time iterative model tuning necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve biologically relevant throughput, as local clusters cannot support the concurrent genomic alignments, graph-based pangenome analyses, and population-level Bayesian computations required. This work bridges functional genomics with evolutionary theory, offering translational strategies to enhance crop resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of multicellular plants and fungi as related to botanical research as well as to applications in comparative genetics, ecology and evolutionary studies, clinical studies, and industrial research. Includes instruction in molecular genetics, gene expression, gene regulation, genomics, epigenetic phenomena, DNA recombination and repair, genetic interactions at the microbial and higher levels, and molecular evolution.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolution and transmission of pre-modern liturgical chant traditions across Eurasia using computational methods, with a focus on identifying patterns of melodic adaptation in sacred music repertoires that emerged at cultural crossroads. The study centers on digitized manuscripts and field recordings of lesser-studied Christian, Jewish, and Islamic monophonic chant traditions from 800–1600 CE, particularly those demonstrating syncretic features between Byzantine, Syriac, and Central Asian musical practices. A key challenge lies in analyzing complex melodic structures across fragmented archival sources while accounting for notation variances, oral transmission drift, and contextual performance factors. To address this, we propose deploying machine learning models on high-performance computing (HPC) resources to 1) process optical music recognition outputs from heterogeneous manuscript sources into standardized symbolic representations, 2) perform comparative melodic contour analysis across traditions using graph-based similarity metrics, and 3) simulate acoustic environments of historical worship spaces through waveguide synthesis to model chant propagation characteristics. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of ~15 TB of manuscript images and audio data, including 3D impulse responses from archaeological site models. Expected outcomes include the first large-scale melodic typology of cross-cultural chant diffusion patterns and an open-source toolkit for sacred music analysis. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational musicology, historical acoustics, and digital humanities, offering new methodologies for preserving endangered sacred music heritage while advancing understanding of how sonic practices mediated interreligious cultural exchange. The project’s scale necessitates HPC resources to manage memory-intensive tasks in spectral feature extraction and wave equation modeling, which would be computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, theory, composition, and performance of music for religious or sacred purposes, and that prepares individuals for religious musical vocations such as choir directors, cantors, organists, and chanters.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interactions between legal frameworks, urban development patterns, and socio-economic outcomes in the context of Real Estate and Land Development Law. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, dynamic tools to simulate how evolving legal and regulatory environments—such as zoning amendments, environmental compliance mandates, or affordable housing policies—impact land use decisions, market behavior, and community equity over time. Traditional legal analyses often rely on static case studies or qualitative assessments, which struggle to account for nonlinear feedback loops, multi-stakeholder decision-making, or long-term systemic effects. To address this gap, the project will develop computational models integrating agent-based simulations, geospatial analytics, and network theory to map how legal constraints propagate through real estate ecosystems. Key components include parsing large-scale legal text corpora (e.g., municipal codes, court rulings) using natural language processing (NLP) to identify policy patterns, training machine learning algorithms to predict developer responses to regulatory changes, and simulating urban growth scenarios under varying legal regimes. The computational workload demands parallel processing for Monte Carlo simulations of stochastic market behaviors and GPU-accelerated deep learning for spatial-temporal pattern recognition in land use datasets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible modeling framework to quantify the cascading effects of legal interventions, enabling policymakers to anticipate unintended consequences—such as displacement risks or infrastructure strain—before enacting reforms. By bridging computational social science with legal scholarship, this project aims to establish a methodological precedent for data-driven policy design in land development law, while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional, interdisciplinary domains.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: Theatrical productions involve complex, dynamic interactions between spatial design, performer movement, and audience perception that remain challenging to optimize through traditional rehearsal methods alone. This project seeks to develop computational models for simulating and analyzing multidimensional production elements through high-performance computing (HPC). The research problem centers on the lack of integrated tools to quantitatively evaluate how staging decisions—such as actor blocking, set configurations, and lighting designs—collectively impact audience engagement and narrative clarity across diverse performance spaces. To address this, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, motion-capture data from rehearsals and historical productions will be used to train agent-based models that simulate performer trajectories and audience sightline obstructions in parametrized virtual venues. Second, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will iteratively propose staging adjustments that balance artistic intent with spatial efficiency, using reinforcement learning to optimize for metrics derived from dramaturgical principles and crowd-sourced viewer feedback. These simulations will require parallelized rendering of 3D environments and real-time physics calculations to model acoustics, lighting propagation, and multi-view spectator perspectives at scale. By leveraging GPU clusters and distributed memory systems, the project aims to produce adaptive tools that assist directors in prototyping productions computationally before physical rehearsals begin. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying directorial choices, a repository of annotated performance simulations for pedagogical use, and evidence-based guidelines for staging in non-traditional venues. This work bridges performing arts practice with computational analytics, offering methods to preserve artistic nuance while reducing resource-intensive trial-and-error in theatrical workflows. Successful implementation could transform how productions are planned in an era of increasingly constrained budgets and hybrid digital-live performance formats.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the planning, design, preparation, and production of plays and other theatrical entertainment programs. Includes instruction in theatrical design, program management, dramatic production, rehearsal management, personnel management and casting, actor coaching, directing concepts and techniques, theater history, scene work, script interpretation, business management, marketing, public relations, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal analytics, an emerging interdisciplinary domain intersecting legal theory, natural language processing (NLP), and network science. The research focuses on analyzing the structural evolution of legal argumentation frameworks within appellate court decisions, particularly in understudied areas of administrative law where precedent networks exhibit high complexity and rapid change. Traditional legal research methods struggle to map dynamic interactions between rulings, dissents, and legislative updates at scale, limiting predictive insights into judicial decision-making patterns. The project will develop a novel computational pipeline combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with transformer-based NLP models to process over 1.2 million digitized legal documents from federal and state courts. Key technical challenges include resolving referential ambiguity in legal citations, modeling temporal dependencies in precedent hierarchies, and quantifying the influence of non-binding persuasive authorities across jurisdictions. HPC resources are essential for training multi-modal architectures on heterogeneous legal texts (opinions, statutes, regulatory filings) while maintaining chain-of-custody data provenance requirements critical for legal informatics. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for temporal legal network analysis, quantitative metrics measuring doctrinal stability, and predictive models identifying latent factors in judicial reasoning. This work will provide empirical foundations for improving access to justice through AI-assisted legal research tools while establishing methodological benchmarks for computational legal studies—a field presently underserved by conventional science-focused HPC allocations. Results will be validated against expert-annotated test cases in environmental law and digital privacy regulation, with potential applications in legal education, policy analysis, and court resource optimization.
cip_definition: Any program in law, legal services, and legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of efficiently managing and securing large-scale medical data systems in clinical environments, which are increasingly strained by high-volume electronic health records (EHRs), diagnostic imaging, and real-time telemedicine applications. Medical offices face critical bottlenecks in processing speed, data interoperability, and compliance with evolving regulatory standards (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR), compounded by the need to integrate legacy systems with modern cloud-based platforms. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a scalable, AI-driven framework for optimizing medical software performance and cybersecurity. Computational workflows will include parallelized simulations of multi-site EHR networks to model data traffic patterns, machine learning algorithms to detect vulnerabilities in proprietary medical software, and GPU-accelerated testing of encryption protocols for patient data transmission. Additionally, we will benchmark the interoperability of open-source and commercial health informatics tools under simulated high-load scenarios, assessing latency and error rates. The project will utilize containerized environments to replicate diverse clinical IT infrastructures, enabling rapid iteration of system configurations. Outcomes will include predictive models for hardware resource allocation in medical offices, a validated toolkit for auditing compliance-ready software deployments, and open-access benchmarks for telemedicine platform scalability. By addressing computational bottlenecks in medical office IT systems, this work aims to reduce operational downtime, enhance data security, and support the cost-effective adoption of emerging technologies in healthcare settings. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of synthetic and anonymized clinical datasets, train deep learning models for anomaly detection, and execute large-scale network simulations that mirror real-world medical office environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply computer programming, troubleshooting, and information technology skills to the installation, maintenance, and upgrade of standard, customized, or proprietary medical software and associated hardware. Includes instruction in computer programming, systems analysis, networking, telecommunications, medical records and informatics software applications, information technology, systems administration, computer security, and applicable regulations and certifications or licenses.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of leadership decision-making and its impact on organizational resilience in educational institutions. Educational leaders face complex challenges in adapting to rapidly evolving demands, such as workforce skill gaps, technological disruptions, and shifting policy environments. However, existing studies often rely on small-scale qualitative data or simplified statistical models, limiting their capacity to simulate nonlinear interactions between leadership behaviors, organizational policies, and systemic outcomes. The proposed research will develop agent-based computational models (ABMs) to simulate how different leadership strategies—such as distributed decision-making, crisis response protocols, and professional development investments—propagate through multi-tiered educational organizations. These models will integrate empirical data from longitudinal HR records, institutional surveys, and policy documents to parameterize agent behaviors and environmental constraints. By scaling simulations to thousands of parallel scenarios using HPC clusters, the project will identify critical leverage points for sustaining organizational adaptability under resource constraints. Additional computational workloads will apply natural language processing (NLP) to analyze leadership communication patterns in meeting transcripts and policy drafts, correlating semantic features with measurable outcomes like staff retention and program efficacy. Outcomes will advance evidence-based frameworks for leadership development programs, particularly in under-resourced educational settings. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces of ABMs, the computational linguistics workloads, and the sensitivity analyses required to validate model robustness. Results will be disseminated through open-access simulation toolkits tailored for education administrators, enabling data-driven strategies to enhance organizational learning and systemic resilience in the face of 21st-century educational challenges.
cip_title: Education and Human Resource Studies/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: Pediatric endocrine disorders, such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia, early-onset diabetes, and growth hormone deficiencies, arise from complex interactions between genetic susceptibility, hormonal dysregulation, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies often lack personalization due to limited tools for integrating multi-omics data (genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic) with dynamic hormone profiling and clinical outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model endocrine system dynamics and predict disease trajectories in pediatric populations. The primary research problem centers on identifying biomarkers and mechanistic pathways that differentiate transient hormonal variations from pathological states, which is critical for timely intervention. We propose a multi-scale approach combining longitudinal clinical data from electronic health records, high-resolution hormone time-series data, and whole-genome sequencing from a cohort of 1,200 patients. Machine learning models will be trained to classify disease subtypes and predict treatment responses, while mechanistic network models will simulate hypothalamic-pituitary-end organ axes under genetic and pharmacological perturbations. These analyses demand high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the dimensionality of multi-omics integration, the iterative optimization of patient-specific models, and the need for real-time simulations of endocrine feedback loops. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive algorithm for distinguishing benign pubertal variations from endocrine pathologies, (2) in silico identification of candidate therapeutic targets for rare endocrine disorders, and (3) open-source computational tools for hormone time-series analysis. The requested HPC allocation will enable parallel processing of genomic data, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and large-scale parameter sweeps in biological network simulations. This work will directly enhance clinical decision-making in pediatric endocrinology by providing quantitative frameworks to interpret complex hormonal data, reduce diagnostic delays, and personalize treatment regimens. The computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other hormone-mediated conditions, extending the project’s impact across developmental medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of endocrine diseases and the regulation of hormone balance in childhood and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and performance of implantable biomedical devices, such as neural interfaces and bioelectronic pacemakers, which require precise integration with dynamic biological systems. Current challenges in device development stem from the complex, multiscale interactions between engineered components and physiological environments, including time-varying electrical, mechanical, and biochemical factors. Traditional experimental approaches to iteratively test device designs are resource-intensive and fail to capture the full spectrum of in vivo variability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline combining multiphysics modeling, machine learning (ML), and sensitivity analysis. The computational workflow will integrate finite element simulations of device-tissue interfaces (e.g., electrode-electrolyte charge transfer, mechanical stress distributions) with ML-based surrogate models trained on heterogeneous datasets spanning material properties, anatomical variability, and physiological signaling. By leveraging GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed memory parallelism, the framework will enable parameter sweeps across millions of design configurations while accounting for real-world biological noise and uncertainty. Key outcomes include predictive models linking device geometries, material choices, and placement strategies to long-term performance metrics such as signal fidelity, inflammatory response, and energy efficiency. The HPC resources will specifically support large-scale simulations of cardiac electrophysiology models coupled to bioelectronic implants, as well as neural network training on simulated and experimental histology data. This work will advance personalized biomedical device design by reducing reliance on trial-and-error prototyping, accelerating translation to clinical applications. The resulting open-source tools will be disseminated to the research community, fostering collaboration in computational bioengineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing biological or medical systems and products. Includes instruction in instrument calibration, design and installation testing, system safety and maintenance procedures, procurement and installation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of scopist workflows in legal transcription through advanced error detection and contextual analysis of machine shorthand outputs. Court reporters rely on scopists to edit real-time stenographic transcripts, a process complicated by phonetic ambiguities, speaker overlap, and domain-specific legal terminology. Existing tools lack the contextual awareness to resolve semantic inconsistencies at scale, leading to time-intensive manual corrections. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and domain-adapted neural networks to automate error identification, disambiguate homophones in machine-generated text, and flag contextually implausible phrases in real time. The computational approach will involve training transformer-based models on curated datasets of legal transcripts annotated for common scopist interventions, including misheard terminology, punctuation errors, and speaker attribution mismatches. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process the high-dimensional linguistic patterns inherent in stenographic data, which combines abbreviated phonetic encodings with dense legal jargon. By parallelizing model training across GPU nodes, we aim to optimize hyperparameters for low-latency inference while maintaining the precision required for legal-admissible transcripts. A secondary focus involves developing an open-source API to integrate these models with computer-aided transcription (CAT) software, enabling dynamic suggestions during editing. The expected outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in manual correction time per transcript, validated through partnerships with certified court reporting schools, and a publicly available benchmark dataset for stenographic NLP tasks. This work bridges computational linguistics and legal documentation practices, offering a novel application of HPC to a specialized domain that supports equitable access to accurate judicial records.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to perform editing and word processing on a court reporter transcript to ensure the accuracy of the transcripts. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcriptioning, machine shorthand, and computer-aided transcription software.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between human perception of environmental risk and geospatial decision-making patterns in coastal communities facing accelerated sea-level rise. While existing research in geography often prioritizes physical vulnerability modeling, this study focuses on the sociocultural and cognitive factors that mediate how communities interpret spatial data, prioritize adaptive actions, and negotiate conflicting risk narratives.
