By bridging computational physics with clinical imaging practices, this project aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven, personalized diagnostic radiology that prioritizes both accuracy and patient safety.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnostic applications of x-rays, gamma rays from sealed sources, ultrasonic radiation, and magnetic resonance; and in the use of equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: Dental prostheses, such as crowns and bridges, require precise biomechanical compatibility to ensure long-term functionality and patient comfort. However, current design workflows in dental laboratory technology rely heavily on manual iteration and generic material assumptions, leading to suboptimal performance in complex anatomical scenarios. This project proposes a computational framework to optimize prosthesis design by integrating patient-specific biomechanical simulations, advanced material modeling, and machine learning-driven topology optimization. The central challenge lies in modeling the multiscale interactions between heterogeneous oral tissues, dynamic occlusal forces, and bioactive ceramic materials—a task requiring high-resolution finite element analysis (FEA) and molecular dynamics simulations that exceed conventional computing capabilities. We will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to 1) develop a multiscale model of masticatory biomechanics using clinical CT scans and intraoral force mapping data, 2) simulate stress distribution patterns in novel zirconia-titanium composite materials under physiological loading conditions, and 3) train generative adversarial networks (GANs) to propose topology-optimized designs that minimize peak stress concentrations. The computational pipeline will be validated against physical compression tests and digital image correlation measurements from 3D-printed prototypes. By establishing predictive relationships between microstructure, design geometry, and clinical performance metrics, this research aims to reduce prosthesis failure rates by ≥40% in edge-case occlusal scenarios while decreasing manual design time by 60%. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will enable dental technicians to personalize prostheses based on predictive biomechanical outcomes rather than static templates, fundamentally advancing digital dentistry workflows. This interdisciplinary approach bridges materials science, biomechanics, and artificial intelligence to address critical gaps in dental laboratory technology, with potential applications in craniofacial reconstruction and implantology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of dentists, to design and construct dental prostheses such as caps, crowns, bridges, dentures, splints, and orthodontic appliances. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, dental materials, ceramics technology, impressions, complete dentures, partial dentures, orthodontics, crowns and bridges, sculpture, bonding and assembly techniques, and equipment operation.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing the diagnostic accuracy of ophthalmic technicians in detecting early-stage glaucoma through advanced analysis of optical coherence tomography (OCT) and visual field data. Glaucoma progression is characterized by subtle, heterogeneous changes in retinal structure and function, which are challenging to interpret consistently across diverse patient populations using current clinical protocols. The research problem centers on the lack of standardized, data-driven tools to integrate multimodal ophthalmic measurements into actionable diagnostic models that account for anatomical variability, confounding pathologies, and technician-level decision-making workflows. The computational approach combines three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D CNNs) trained on OCT volumetric scans with graph-based algorithms to model spatial relationships between optic nerve head topography and visual field loss patterns. These models will be augmented by generative adversarial networks (GANs) to simulate rare or edge-case presentations, addressing data scarcity in underrepresented demographic groups. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-resolution ophthalmic datasets (≥10 TB) from multi-institutional registries, enabling parallelized training of ensemble models while maintaining temporal resolution required for clinical usability. Expected outcomes include an open-source diagnostic decision support system that quantifies technician-interpreted findings against computational predictions, flagging discordant cases for secondary review. The project will establish novel biomarkers for pre-perimetric glaucoma detection and generate evidence-based protocols for technician-led monitoring of disease progression. By bridging ophthalmic imaging, computational biomechanics, and clinical workflow design, this work aims to redefine the technical scope of ophthalmic allied health practice while maintaining alignment with physician-supervised care standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist ophthalmologists and optometrists in examining and treating patients with vision problems, vision disorders, and eye diseases. Includes instruction in taking patient histories, administering directed treatments and topical medications, diagnostic test procedures and equipment operation, anatomical and functional ocular measurements, patient care and instruction, ophthalmic and surgical equipment maintenance, safety and sterilization procedures, and office administrative procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a dynamic simulation framework for optimizing micro-targeting strategies in small e-commerce businesses operating in volatile markets. Small businesses face unique challenges in allocating limited marketing budgets effectively, particularly when competing against data-rich enterprises. Traditional approaches rely on aggregated demographic data or static customer segmentation, which fail to capture real-time behavioral shifts, hyperlocal demand fluctuations, or emergent competition patterns in digital marketplaces. The proposed computational model integrates heterogeneous agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning to simulate complex interactions between small business decision-making, competitor actions, and consumer behavior across multiple digital platforms. The ABM component will represent diverse consumer agents with adaptive preference structures, while a parallelized Monte Carlo tree search algorithm will optimize budget allocation across channels under uncertainty. Key innovations include the development of a multi-scale temporal framework accommodating platform-specific algorithm updates (e.g., social media feed prioritization changes) and a novel entropy-based metric for quantifying market unpredictability. By processing petabytes of synthetic yet realistic transaction and engagement data, the HPC implementation enables simultaneous testing of intervention strategies across thousands of simulated market conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for small businesses to predict optimal marketing mix adjustments during demand shocks, identify underutilized niche audiences through computational ethnography techniques, and quantify the resilience of different targeting approaches to platform policy changes. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational social science, operations research, and digital marketing analytics, providing small businesses with evidence-based strategies to improve customer acquisition costs and lifetime value predictions in rapidly evolving e-commerce ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage independent small businesses. Includes instruction in business administration; enterprise planning and entrepreneurship; start-up; small business operations and problems; personnel supervision; capitalization and investment; taxation; business law and regulations; e-commerce; home business operations; and applications to specific sectors, products, and services.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize real-time, multi-channel customer engagement strategies in tourism and travel service operations using advanced computational modeling. The hospitality industry faces growing complexity in managing dynamic customer interactions across digital platforms (e.g., chatbots, personalized booking systems, and mobile apps) while balancing operational costs and revenue goals. Current marketing operations often rely on siloed data streams and heuristic decision-making, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and missed opportunities for hyper-personalized service delivery. To address this gap, we propose developing an adaptive machine learning framework that integrates heterogeneous data—including real-time customer behavior, seasonal demand patterns, and operational constraints—to simulate and optimize marketing workflows. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep reinforcement learning models on large-scale historical transaction datasets (10+ TB) from partner hotel chains, coupled with agent-based simulations of customer decision pathways. Computational challenges include parallelizing Monte Carlo tree search algorithms to evaluate billions of potential interaction sequences and optimizing neural architecture search for context-aware recommendation systems. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for customer lifetime value under dynamic pricing scenarios and a decision support tool capable of prescribing optimal resource allocations across marketing channels with millisecond latency. This work will advance the operational efficiency of travel service providers by enabling data-driven micro-targeting at unprecedented scales while maintaining compliance with evolving privacy regulations. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of multi-objective optimization across temporal, spatial, and service-type dimensions inherent in tourism ecosystems.
cip_title: Tourism and Travel Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide direct retail services to hotel and motel clients and customers in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in the principles of hotel/motel operations, customer sales and assistance operations and techniques, telephone operations, and basic office management.

abstract: Osteopathic medicine emphasizes the integration of holistic care with the biomechanical relationships of the musculoskeletal system, yet the systemic effects of osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) remain incompletely understood at molecular and tissue levels. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the multiscale biomechanical and neurophysiological responses to OMT. We aim to develop computational frameworks that simulate how manual interventions alter tissue mechanics, cellular signaling, and autonomic nervous system activity, with a focus on chronic pain and inflammatory conditions. A key challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets—including clinical motion capture, MRI-derived tissue properties, and omics-scale molecular profiles—into predictive models. The computational approach will combine finite element analysis for musculoskeletal stress-strain dynamics, agent-based modeling of inflammatory cascades, and machine learning to identify biomarkers of treatment efficacy. These models will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 200 patients receiving OMT for low back pain. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the iterative parameter optimization required for multiscale simulations and the analysis of high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into how OMT modulates systemic health through musculoskeletal pathways, (2) predictive algorithms to personalize treatment protocols based on patient-specific biomechanical and molecular profiles, and (3) openly accessible simulation tools for the osteopathic research community. By bridging clinical practice with computational systems biology, this work will advance evidence-based applications of osteopathic principles and provide a foundation for future studies exploring OMT’s role in preventive care and complex disease management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of osteopathic medicine, involving a combination of medical principles and procedures and osteopathic principles of holistic medicine and the relationship of the musculoskeletal system to general health. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, preventive medicine, family and community medicine, medical informatics, disease systems, organ and physiologic systems, osteopathic principles and practice, osteopathic manipulative treatment, musculoskeletal and skin systems, clinical specialty rotations, medical ethics, and professional standards and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of transregional cultural identities across Latin America and the Caribbean through large-scale textual and visual data. The research addresses a critical gap in interdisciplinary area studies: the lack of computational frameworks capable of tracing how shared cultural narratives—expressed in literature, folklore, and digital media—have developed across linguistically and politically fragmented contexts. While existing scholarship often relies on localized case studies, this work proposes a comparative, data-driven approach to identify patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance spanning the 20th and 21st centuries. The computational methodology integrates multilingual natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned for regional dialects and creoles, network analysis of narrative motifs across digitized archives (including newspapers, oral histories, and social media corpora), and machine learning-driven image classification for symbolic visual elements in public art and protest ephemera. Key challenges include processing non-standardized orthographies in historical texts, managing heterogeneous data formats from partner institutions in 15 countries, and scaling graph-based analyses to map cultural connectivity across millions of nodes. Access to HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, training domain-specific transformer models, and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about cultural transmission pathways. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of transregional cultural linkages, a methodological framework for computational humanities research in underrepresented linguistic contexts, and actionable insights for heritage preservation initiatives. By bridging computational scalability with area studies expertise, this project aims to redefine how cultural dynamics in Latin America and the Caribbean are studied, emphasizing interconnectedness over traditional nation-state boundaries.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an AI-driven computational framework to optimize credentialing and privileging workflows for medical staff in healthcare facilities, addressing systemic inefficiencies that delay provider onboarding and compliance. Manual review processes for verifying practitioner qualifications, licensure, and disciplinary histories are time-intensive and prone to human error, creating risks for regulatory noncompliance and operational bottlenecks. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on multi-modal datasets, including historical credentialing records, licensure databases, and accreditation guidelines, to automate document verification, risk prediction, and decision support. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will parse unstructured text from medical licenses, malpractice claims, and peer references, while graph-based algorithms will map practitioner networks to identify undisclosed affiliations or conflicts. Computational simulations will model credentialing workflow scenarios under varying staffing and regulatory constraints to identify optimal resource allocation strategies. The project requires HPC capabilities to manage large-scale parallel processing of sensitive healthcare data, train deep learning models with millions of parameters, and run iterative Monte Carlo simulations for system optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive toolset to reduce average credentialing cycle times by 30-50%, improve detection of incomplete or anomalous applications by 25%, and generate actionable metrics for compliance risk mitigation. This work will provide healthcare administrators with a scalable computational infrastructure to meet evolving accreditation standards while maintaining rigorous practitioner qualification oversight. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and interdisciplinary collaborations with health informatics researchers to advance data-driven innovations in medical staff services technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform credentialing, privileging, personnel management, and accreditation compliance services for hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in medical staff organization and management, medical terminology, credentialing and re-credentialing, health care accreditation and regulatory standards, health care law, meeting and negotiation management, and office information systems management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to investigate the evolutionary dynamics of host-pathogen interactions, with a focus on understanding how molecular-scale mutations in viral proteins influence population-level transmission and immune evasion. A critical challenge in predicting pathogen evolution lies in bridging scales—from atomic-level structural changes in proteins to shifts in epidemiological dynamics. Current models often treat these scales independently, limiting their ability to predict emergent virulence or resistance. To address this gap, we propose an integrated approach combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of viral spike protein variants with agent-based models (ABMs) of host population infection dynamics. MD simulations will quantify the biophysical effects of mutations on protein stability and host receptor binding, while ABMs will simulate transmission chains and selection pressures across heterogeneous host populations. The computational workflow will employ iterative parameterization: MD-derived binding affinities and fitness estimates will inform ABM rules, while ABM outcomes will guide the sampling of mutation space in subsequent MD cycles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the scale of this work, which involves thousands of parallel MD simulations (using GROMACS) and stochastic ABMs tracking millions of agents over epidemiologically relevant timescales. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of mutation hotspots that disproportionately impact transmission and immune escape, (2) predictive metrics for strain emergence based on early molecular surveillance data, and (3) an open-source software package for coupled multiscale modeling in evolutionary biology. This work will provide novel insights into the feedback between molecular adaptability and population-level resilience, with direct applications in vaccine design and outbreak preparedness. The requested resources will enable the first systematic integration of structural biology data into real-time epidemiological forecasting, advancing mathematical biology’s capacity to address urgent public health challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to genomics, molecular modeling, structural biology, ecology, evolutionary biology and systems of analysis of neurobiology, physiology, and metabolism. Includes instruction in computational mathematics, chaos and nonlinear systems, perturbation methods, evolutionary biology, molecular biology, bioinformatics, and neurobiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Hebrew linguistics, focusing on the diachronic analysis of morphological and syntactic evolution from Biblical to Modern Hebrew. A central challenge in Hebrew philology lies in systematically tracking linguistic shifts across millennia, given the fragmented nature of historical texts, dialectal variations, and the scarcity of large-scale digital tools tailored to Semitic languages. Current manual methods limit the scope and granularity of analysis, particularly in identifying patterns of language change and their sociolinguistic drivers. This project proposes to develop and apply computational workflows to analyze digitized corpora spanning pre-exilic Biblical Hebrew texts, Rabbinic Hebrew, and Modern Hebrew, including regional dialects. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for automated morphological parsing of unvocalized texts, implementing probabilistic algorithms to detect syntactic innovations, and simulating language contact effects using agent-based models. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte text datasets, fine-tuning multilingual large language models for Hebrew-specific tasks, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to test hypotheses about historical language change. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access annotated corpora with diachronic linguistic annotations, a computational framework for comparative Semitic linguistics, and novel insights into the mechanisms of Hebrew’s transition from a liturgical to a revitalized vernacular. The results will directly benefit scholars in Hebrew studies by providing scalable tools for text analysis while contributing methodological advances to computational linguistics, particularly in modeling fusional morphology and non-concatenative word formation. This work aligns with institutional priorities in digital humanities and strengthens interdisciplinary collaborations between linguistics and HPC research communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hebrew language. Includes instruction in philology; Biblical Hebrew (including Pre- and Post-Exilic scripts); Modern Hebrew; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of autonomous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments necessitates high-fidelity simulations to ensure robustness and adaptability. Current computational limitations hinder the ability to model multi-robot coordination, real-time sensor fusion, and nonlinear control strategies at scales required for practical deployment. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a framework for simulating heterogeneous robotic networks with embedded AI-driven decision-making. The research focuses on optimizing distributed control algorithms for swarms of mobile robots operating under communication constraints and environmental uncertainties, such as variable terrain and partial sensor data. Computational methods will include parallelized multi-body dynamics simulations, Monte Carlo-based robustness testing, and machine learning models trained on synthetic datasets generated via physics-informed neural networks. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify optimal control policies, as well as real-time emulation of sensor-actuator feedback loops across thousands of simulated agents. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for fault-tolerant coordination in resource-constrained scenarios and validated models of energy-efficient locomotion strategies for wheeled-legged hybrid robots. The computational results will directly inform the design of physical prototypes for search-and-rescue applications and industrial automation systems, bridging the gap between theoretical control engineering and deployable mechatronic solutions. By enabling previously intractable simulations of complex electro-mechanical interactions, this work aims to advance the development of adaptive robotic systems capable of operating in environments where traditional automation approaches fail. The resource allocation will support critical benchmarking against experimental data, ensuring computational models accurately capture nonlinearities in actuator responses and sensor noise characteristics inherent to real-world systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer controlled electro-mechanical systems and products with embedded electronics, sensors, and actuators; and which includes, but is not limited to, automata, robots and automation systems. Includes instruction in mechanical engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, computer and software engineering, and control engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model neuromuscular activation patterns during therapeutic movement sequences, with the goal of optimizing personalized movement therapy interventions for individuals with psychosomatic dysfunction. Current movement therapy practices rely heavily on qualitative observational assessments and generalized protocols, limiting the ability to predict patient-specific responses or dynamically adjust interventions. To address this gap, we propose integrating high-density electromyography (HD-EMG), inertial motion capture data, and patient-reported somatic feedback into a machine learning pipeline that maps neuromuscular coordination strategies to therapeutic outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to process multimodal time-series datasets from 200 participants undergoing structured movement education protocols, including individuals with chronic pain and stress-related movement inhibition. Computational methods will include 1) GPU-accelerated signal decomposition of HD-EMG arrays to identify latent muscle synergies, 2) recurrent neural network modeling of temporal relationships between kinematic variables and self-reported psychophysical states, and 3) reinforcement learning simulations to predict optimal movement parameter adjustments. The resulting models will enable quantitative characterization of how specific movement qualities (e.g., force gradation, joint coupling sequences) influence autonomic regulation and somatic awareness. This work represents the first systematic attempt to establish computational biomarkers for movement therapy efficacy, with potential applications in clinical decision support systems for somatically-oriented rehabilitation. By bridging movement neuroscience, affective computing, and rehabilitation engineering, the project aims to advance evidence-based practices in therapeutic movement education while developing novel computational tools for analyzing embodied cognition processes. Successful implementation could transform current phenomenological approaches into precision interventions tailored to individual neurobiomechanical profiles.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use functional and expressive integration strategies to help promote somatic awareness and optimal psychophysical functioning. Includes instruction in skilled touch techniques, kinesthetic awareness processes, movement observation, patterning, client assessment and guidance, verbal and nonverbal communication, practice management, professional standards and ethics, and specific therapeutic and educational modalities

abstract: Cybersecurity defense strategies require dynamic, evidence-based policy frameworks capable of adapting to rapidly evolving adversarial tactics and systemic vulnerabilities. Traditional policy evaluation methods often lack the granularity to model complex, large-scale interactions between cyber adversaries, defenders, and infrastructure, particularly under scenarios involving cascading failures or multi-actor coordination. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational model to simulate cyber conflict dynamics and evaluate the resilience of policy interventions in real-world, heterogeneous network environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning-driven threat behavior prediction to analyze how strategic policy decisions—such as incident reporting mandates, public-private threat intelligence sharing protocols, and cross-border regulatory harmonization—impact systemic risk reduction and attack surface management. The computational framework will ingest real-world datasets, including historical cyber incident reports, geopolitical event timelines, and critical infrastructure metadata, to generate probabilistic scenarios for stress-testing policy efficacy under varying adversarial capabilities and societal dependencies. Key outcomes will include a policy optimization toolkit for identifying context-specific resilience thresholds, a taxonomy of high-impact cyber deterrence failure modes linked to regulatory gaps, and predictive metrics for quantifying the societal cost-benefit tradeoffs of emerging defense paradigms. By bridging computational scalability with policy analytics, this work aims to advance the operationalization of adaptive governance frameworks in cybersecurity, offering stakeholders actionable insights into long-term strategic planning and resource allocation for cyber defense ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, heterogeneous engineering systems operating under stochastic constraints. Traditional optimization methods struggle to address the real-time interplay between discrete-event decision-making (e.g., task prioritization) and continuous-state physical processes (e.g., energy transfer, material flows) in complex applied engineering environments such as adaptive manufacturing networks or decentralized infrastructure systems. Leveraging advances in hybrid digital twin architectures and transfer learning, the research will implement a multi-paradigm simulation approach combining agent-based modeling, non-convex optimization solvers, and physics-informed neural networks to resolve interdependencies across temporal and spatial scales. The computational workflow will integrate real-time sensor data streams with predictive system models to enable adaptive reconfiguration of resources under uncertainty, with validation targeting a case study in resilient modular production systems. High-performance computing resources are critical to support parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for robustness testing, training of graph neural networks on system topology variants, and solving mixed-integer linear programs with >10^6 variables arising from multi-objective scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for optimizing resource elasticity in systems where operational flexibility coexists with rigid physical constraints, directly addressing gaps in applied engineering methodologies for cyber-physical infrastructure. The results will provide quantitative insights into trade-offs between system-wide efficiency and local resilience, with applications ranging from distributed additive manufacturing clusters to hybrid renewable energy microgrids. This work bridges control theory, industrial systems engineering, and computational mathematics, advancing decision-support capabilities for next-generation adaptive engineering systems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles inherent to engineering to the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance our understanding of non-perturbative phenomena in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) through large-scale numerical simulations, addressing critical gaps in predicting hadronic interactions and quark confinement dynamics. Despite the success of the Standard Model, first-principles calculations of low-energy QCD remain computationally intractable with conventional methods, limiting progress in interpreting experimental results from high-energy colliders and rare decay studies. We propose to employ lattice QCD techniques on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to compute key observables such as hadron mass spectra, decay constants, and nucleon structure functions. These simulations will utilize improved gauge and fermionic actions to reduce discretization errors, coupled with multi-level Monte Carlo sampling to mitigate signal-to-noise challenges in correlation functions. A novel algorithmic component involves leveraging machine learning-assisted hybrid Monte Carlo updates to accelerate convergence in large-volume ensembles with near-physical quark masses. The requested resources will enable the generation of gauge field configurations across multiple lattice spacings (0.04–0.12 fm) and volumes (up to 96⁴), systematically controlling finite-size effects while approaching the physical pion mass. Expected outcomes include precision determinations of light and strange quark masses, charmed hadron properties relevant to flavor physics anomalies, and improved parton distribution functions for proton structure studies. These results will directly inform ongoing experiments at CERN and Fermilab while providing benchmark data for beyond-Standard-Model scenarios. The computational strategy developed here will establish scalable workflows for future exascale QCD investigations, enhancing the broader particle physics community’s capacity to interface theoretical predictions with next-generation experimental facilities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the basic constituents of sub-atomic matter and energy, and the forces governing fundamental processes. Includes instruction in quantum theory, field theory, single-particle systems, perturbation and scattering theory, matter-radiation interaction, symmetry, quarks, capture, Schroedinger mechanics, methods for detecting particle emission and absorption, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a novel computational framework to model and analyze adversarial decision-making processes in contested cyber environments, with a focus on enhancing defensive agility in military cyber operations. The increasing complexity of modern cyber warfare—characterized by adaptive adversaries, ephemeral attack surfaces, and the convergence of AI-driven tactics with legacy infrastructure—creates critical gaps in existing simulation tools. Current methods often fail to capture the recursive interplay between offensive cyber maneuvers, defensive countermeasures, and the strategic misdirection inherent in multi-domain operations. To address this, we propose an agent-based hybrid simulation architecture combining game-theoretic adversarial modeling, probabilistic attack graph analysis, and neural-symbolic reinforcement learning. The framework will integrate real-world cyber terrain data with synthetically generated threat behavior profiles to simulate multi-echelon cyber conflicts across tactical edge networks and enterprise-scale systems. High-performance computing resources are essential for maintaining fidelity in three key areas: 1) Parallel execution of Monte Carlo simulations exploring decision trees under partial observability constraints, 2) Training ensemble ML models on petabyte-scale network telemetry datasets augmented with adversarial perturbations, and 3) Real-time emulation of software-defined radio environments for assessing wireless attack vectors in spectrum-contested battlespaces. Expected outcomes include a validated capability to predict adversary courses of action with temporal precision 40% greater than current state-of-the-art tools, as well as actionable metrics for quantifying the resilience of zero-trust architectures against coordinated cyber-electronic warfare campaigns. This work directly supports next-generation cyber mission force readiness by providing validated computational testbeds for doctrine development and capability gap analysis, while maintaining ethical AI governance through embedded interpretability modules and human-in-the-loop validation protocols.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the technological and operation aspects of information warfare, including cyber attack and cyber defense. Includes instruction in computer and network security, cryptography, computer forensics, systems security engineering, software applications, threat and vulnerability assessment, wireless networks and satellite communications, tactical and strategic planning, legal and ethical issues, and cyber warfare systems development and acquisition.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to enhance pedagogical strategies in drama and dance education by analyzing the biomechanical and expressive qualities of student performance. While traditional teacher training emphasizes qualitative assessment of movement and expression, current methods lack scalable frameworks for quantifying progress or personalizing feedback. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale motion-capture datasets and simulate dynamic teaching environments. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) creating machine learning models to classify movement patterns and correlate them with skill development stages in dance, and (2) generating 3D simulations of classroom scenarios to model how varying instructional approaches impact student engagement in drama exercises. Motion data will be collected from student teachers and their pupils during rehearsals, using inertial measurement units (IMUs) and optical tracking systems. These datasets will train convolutional neural networks to identify technical proficiency and expressive nuance, while agent-based modeling will simulate peer interactions during improvisational theater activities. The computational demands of processing high-frequency kinematic data (sampled at 200Hz) and rendering real-time, multi-agent virtual environments necessitate parallelized GPU computing and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for drama and dance educators to visualize student progress metrics, predict learning bottlenecks, and test instructional interventions in silico. By bridging performing arts pedagogy with computational analytics, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for training teachers in embodied art forms, ultimately improving how movement-based creativity is taught across K-12 and higher education settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach drama and/or dance programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous corpora of student writing to identify patterns in rhetorical strategies and compositional decision-making across diverse genres and contexts. While existing scholarship in rhetoric and composition has relied on manual close reading or small-sample qualitative analysis, the scale and complexity of contemporary digital writing ecologies—including multimodal artifacts, revision histories, and peer feedback interactions—demand computational methods capable of processing unstructured text, metadata, and embedded contextual signals. The research team proposes to leverage high-performance computing resources to develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for rhetorical analysis, including transformer-based models fine-tuned to classify argumentative structures, discourse moves, and audience adaptation strategies in student writing datasets exceeding 10 million tokens. Parallelized workflows will enable comparative analysis across institutional contexts, demographic variables, and assignment types while preserving the situated nature of writing as a social practice. Key computational challenges include balancing model interpretability with scalability, integrating multi-modal data (e.g., comments, drafts), and developing ethical frameworks for algorithmic analysis of learner-generated texts. Expected outcomes include 1) new methodologies for computational rhetoric applicable to longitudinal studies of writing development, 2) empirically grounded insights into how emerging genres influence rhetorical choices, and 3) open-source tools to support corpus-based pedagogy research. By bridging humanistic inquiry with scalable text analysis, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in writing instruction while contributing to interdisciplinary dialogues about computational humanities infrastructure. The scale of data processing and model training required for robust, generalizable results necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed storage systems beyond typical departmental computing capacities.
cip_title: Rhetoric and Composition/ Writing Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rhetoric and composition/writing studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Mental health disorders in elderly populations, such as late-life depression, dementia-related neuropsychiatric symptoms, and treatment-resistant geriatric schizophrenia, present complex etiological pathways involving genetic, neurobiological, and environmental interactions. Current diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks often lack precision due to the heterogeneity of aging-related comorbidities and the limited integration of multimodal data. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, neuroimaging, and electronic health record (EHR) datasets. The primary research objective is to identify biomarkers and computational phenotypes that predict disease progression and treatment response in geriatric psychiatric disorders. A multi-omics approach will integrate whole-genome sequencing, epigenetic profiles, and structural/functional MRI data from a longitudinal cohort of 2,500 patients aged 65+. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to detect cross-modal associations between genetic risk variants, neuroanatomical changes, and clinical outcomes. Computational workflows will parallelize image processing via containerized pipelines to analyze terabytes of diffusion tensor imaging data, while federated learning frameworks will enable privacy-preserving analysis of distributed EHRs across collaborating institutions. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with age-stratified covariates, and for reducing runtime during hyperparameter optimization of deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive models for personalized intervention strategies, the identification of novel therapeutic targets linked to neuroinflammation pathways in aging, and open-source tools for scalable geriatric psychiatry analytics. This research aims to advance precision medicine in geriatric mental health by elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment variability and informing clinical guidelines for data-driven, patient-specific care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of mental and emotional disorders in the elderly, and to improve the psychiatric care of the elderly both in health and in disease.

abstract: The development of advanced drug formulations requires precise understanding of molecular interactions, pharmacokinetics, and dynamic behaviors of drug-delivery systems, yet empirical approaches remain labor-intensive and limited in resolving multi-scale complexities. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing drug formulations and predicting therapeutic outcomes through computational modeling. The research focuses on three interconnected aims: (1) simulating drug-host interactions at atomic resolution using molecular dynamics (MD) to elucidate binding affinities and conformational changes in target proteins; (2) integrating physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models with machine learning algorithms to predict drug absorption, distribution, and clearance across diverse patient populations; and (3) applying finite element analysis to model drug release kinetics from novel polymeric nano-carriers under varying physiological conditions. These computational workflows demand significant parallel processing capabilities due to the need for large-scale parameter optimization, long-timescale MD simulations (exceeding microsecond durations), and high-throughput screening of formulation variables. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of multi-physics models, ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainty, and training of neural networks on heterogeneous datasets spanning in vitro and clinical data. Expected outcomes include the identification of formulation parameters that maximize bioavailability while minimizing toxicity, predictive models for patient-specific dosing, and mechanistic insights into carrier-mediated drug delivery. By bridging molecular-scale phenomena with system-level pharmacokinetics, this work aims to accelerate the design of safer, more efficacious therapeutics and establish a computational framework for rational formulation development. The requested resources are essential to overcoming current bottlenecks in processing speed and data volume, ultimately advancing translational research in pharmaceutics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the formulation of medicinal substances into product vehicles capable of being stored, transported, and then introduced into the patient and behaving in ways optimal to therapeutic interaction. Includes instruction in statistics, biopharmaceutics, drug metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, physical pharmacy, pharmacological analysis, drug design and development, pharmacological biotechnology, chemical separations, spectroscopy, drug-host interactions, immunology, quantitative drug measurement, enzymatic transformations, and metabolic excretion.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing clinical decision support systems (CDSS) for allied health professionals through advanced computational modeling of heterogeneous patient data. Current CDSS tools in allied health settings often lack precision due to limited integration of multimodal data—including electronic health records, real-time biometric sensor outputs, and socioenvironmental factors—which creates barriers to personalized care planning. To overcome this, we propose developing a machine learning framework capable of synthesizing high-dimensional datasets to predict patient-specific intervention outcomes. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate ensemble models combining convolutional neural networks for imaging analysis (e.g., rehabilitation progress tracking), transformer architectures for longitudinal EHR interpretation, and graph neural networks to model patient-environment interactions. A novel aspect of this work involves simulating virtual patient cohorts to stress-test model generalizability across diverse demographic groups—a computationally intensive process requiring parallelized workflows. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source predictive toolkit for allied health teams and evidence-based thresholds for intervention adjustments in chronic care management. The computational demands of processing 50+ TB of de-identified clinical data, coupled with the need for rapid iteration during model optimization cycles, necessitate dedicated HPC allocation. Successful implementation will provide a template for resource-efficient CDSS development in understudied allied health domains, directly supporting the program's mission to bridge technological innovation with frontline clinical workflows. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary collaborations with rehabilitation science departments and community health partners to ensure translational impact.
cip_title: Allied Health and Medical Assisting Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health and medical assisting services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational analysis of doctrinal and philosophical evolution within Hindu theological texts. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of conceptual continuity and divergence across key Sanskrit works—including the Vedas, Upanishads, and later commentarial traditions—to trace how core ideas such as dharma, karma, and moksha were reinterpreted across historical periods and sectarian lineages. Manual analysis of these voluminous and linguistically complex texts poses significant challenges, limiting systematic cross-textual comparisons. To address this, the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including semantic role labeling, entity recognition, and topic modeling, tailored to classical Sanskrit corpora. Computational workflows will be designed to map conceptual networks, detect shifts in terminological usage, and quantify intertextual influences. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on niche Sanskrit datasets, running large-scale parallelized analyses across multilingual commentaries, and visualizing high-dimensional philosophical relationships. Expected outcomes include (1) a dataset of annotated philosophical correlations across major Hindu schools, (2) dynamic models of doctrinal development linked to socioreligious contexts, and (3) open-access tools for cross-referencing theological arguments in digital editions of primary texts. By bridging computational methods and Indological scholarship, this work aims to deepen understanding of Hinduism’s intellectual diversity while establishing scalable frameworks for analyzing non-Western religious canons. The results will support interdisciplinary dialogues in global philosophy and digital humanities, offering scholars new pathways to interrogate the adaptive resilience of Hindu thought.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the group of South Asian theologies and philosophies collectively known as Hinduism; together with the religious history and cultural and social manifestations of the faith. Includes instruction in Hindu theology and philosophy (dharma); literature (Vedas, Upanishads, Epics, and commentaries); the Hindu Pantheon, sects, and movements; schools and disciplines; and related arts and sciences.

abstract: Medical toxicology faces critical challenges in predicting and mitigating complex toxic exposures, which often involve dynamic interactions between multiple drugs, environmental toxins, and patient-specific factors. Current clinical tools lack the capacity to model these multidimensional interactions at scale, particularly for emerging synthetic drugs, chemical mixtures, or novel toxicants where human data are sparse. This project seeks to develop computational models to predict toxicity mechanisms, optimize treatment protocols, and identify risk biomarkers by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, toxicogenomics databases, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) parameters, and molecular dynamics simulations of toxin-receptor interactions. Machine learning frameworks will be trained to identify patterns in drug-drug-environment interactions linked to adverse outcomes, while parallelized molecular simulations will characterize binding affinities of understudied synthetic opioids and environmental neurotoxicants. A key focus is simulating large-scale virtual populations to assess how genetic polymorphisms, comorbidities, and polypharmacy influence toxicity thresholds—a task requiring HPC due to the combinatorial complexity of variables. Expected outcomes include predictive models for acute multi-substance overdose management, a toxicity risk stratification tool for clinical use, and mechanistic insights into novel toxicant actions. These resources will address urgent gaps in medical toxicology, such as improving antidote development for emerging synthetic drugs and personalizing treatments for chemically exposed populations. The computational infrastructure will also support real-time toxicity surveillance by analyzing regional poison control center data streams, enhancing preparedness for mass exposure events. By bridging clinical data with molecular-scale simulations, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in overdose response, chemical threat mitigation, and precision toxicology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians who specialize in the prevention, evaluation, treatment, and monitoring of injury and illness from exposures to drugs and chemicals, as well as exposures to biological and radiological agents. Important areas include acute drug poisoning; adverse drug events; drug abuse, addiction, and withdrawal; chemicals and hazardous materials; terrorism preparedness; venomous bites and stings; and environmental and workplace exposures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the design and optimization of energy-efficient heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVAC-R) systems. A critical challenge in HVAC-R engineering is balancing energy consumption, thermal comfort, and environmental impact, particularly as regulations phase out high-global-warming-potential refrigerants and demand stricter efficiency standards. Current simulation tools struggle to model complex, transient interactions between refrigerant thermodynamics, airflow dynamics, and heat exchanger performance at the resolution required for next-generation systems. To address this, we propose developing multi-physics computational models that integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-based optimization. These models will simulate refrigerant phase changes, turbulent airflow in ductwork, and heat transfer across variable-speed compressor cycles under diverse operating conditions. HPC resources are essential to resolve these multi-scale phenomena, which involve millions of mesh elements and require iterative parameter sweeps to optimize system configurations. The project will validate simulations against experimental data from lab-scale HVAC-R test rigs, ensuring predictive accuracy for real-world applications. Expected outcomes include novel design frameworks for low-emission, high-efficiency heat pumps and air-handling units, as well as open-source tools to accelerate industry adoption of sustainable HVAC-R technologies. By enabling rapid prototyping of systems tailored to evolving refrigerants and climate-specific loads, this work will directly support decarbonization goals in building infrastructure and cold-chain logistics. The requested computing resources will also facilitate training programs for students in advanced HVAC-R computational methods, bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical system diagnostics.
cip_title: Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using air conditioning, refrigeration, ventilation, and heating systems. Includes instruction in principles of heating and cooling technology, design and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, installation and operation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Surgical wound complications, including infection, dehiscence, and delayed healing, remain a significant challenge in reconstructive procedures, contributing to prolonged recovery, increased healthcare costs, and patient morbidity. Current risk prediction models lack precision due to the multifactorial nature of tissue repair, which involves dynamic interactions between patient-specific biological factors, surgical technique, and postoperative care. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating multi-omics data, biomechanical simulations, and machine learning to model wound healing trajectories and optimize reconstruction strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic datasets, and 3D medical imaging from 2,500 patients undergoing abdominal wall reconstruction and breast flap procedures. Deep neural networks will be trained to identify biomarkers predictive of impaired healing, while finite element analysis will simulate tissue stress distributions under varying surgical closure protocols. Agent-based models will map cellular responses to inflammatory mediators and mechanical strain across spatiotemporal scales. By coupling these approaches, the framework will generate patient-specific risk profiles and propose tailored interventions, such as suture pattern optimization or targeted adjuvant therapies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for wound failure risk (target AUC >0.85), biomechanical guidelines for tension redistribution in complex closures, and a cloud-based decision support tool for surgeons. The computational demands—including parallel processing of 10TB imaging datasets, Monte Carlo simulations of stochastic healing processes, and hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models—necessitate dedicated HPC allocations. This work aims to advance precision surgery by bridging molecular, biomechanical, and clinical predictors of wound outcomes, directly addressing the National Academy of Medicine’s priority to reduce surgical complications through data-driven innovation. Results will be disseminated through open-source model repositories and clinical validation trials at three academic medical centers.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: This research seeks to address the growing complexity of hybrid threat environments in modern military operations, where adversarial tactics increasingly blend conventional and non-conventional domains, such as cyber operations, disinformation campaigns, and decentralized logistics networks. Traditional modeling frameworks struggle to capture the dynamic interactions between these domains, limiting the ability to simulate realistic scenarios for training, strategic planning, and decision support. The project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, multi-domain simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model hybrid threat ecosystems at scale. Computational methods will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate adversarial and civilian actors, graph neural networks (GNNs) to analyze interdependencies between physical and digital infrastructure, and discrete-event simulations to replicate time-sensitive operational workflows. The platform will incorporate real-world geospatial data, anonymized network traffic patterns, and stochastic event generators to create adaptive threat scenarios. By parallelizing these components across HPC clusters, the research aims to achieve near-real-time simulation of theater-scale engagements with granular subsystem interactions, enabling the identification of emergent vulnerabilities and cascading failure points. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for assessing the resilience of joint command structures under hybrid warfare conditions, as well as open-source tools for scenario generation optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures. This work will directly support advanced training programs and contingency planning initiatives, while contributing methodological innovations to the nascent field of computational hybrid threat analysis. The resource request focuses on GPU node allocation for GNN training, large-memory nodes for ABM concurrency, and scalable storage solutions for scenario databases.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for analyzing the morphological complexity and syntactic diversity of under-documented African languages, with a focus on Bantu, Niger-Congo, and Chadic language families. Despite their rich linguistic structures, many African languages lack digitized corpora and tools for large-scale analysis, hindering efforts to model language evolution, document oral literatures, and support pedagogical resources. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process multilingual datasets spanning written texts, transcribed oral narratives, and annotated speech recordings, leveraging parallelized workflows to train neural models for morphological segmentation, syntactic parsing, and cross-linguistic feature comparison. Computational methods will include transformer-based architectures adapted for low-resource settings, graph-based algorithms for dialect mapping, and probabilistic models to infer historical language contacts. Key challenges include scaling analyses across languages with agglutinative morphologies and non-Latin scripts, which require significant memory allocation and GPU acceleration. Outcomes will include open-access tools for automated glossing of oral literature, a pan-African language feature database, and comparative studies on grammaticalization patterns in Niger-Congo verb systems. These resources will advance computational linguistics methodologies for non-Indo-European languages while supporting community-driven preservation initiatives. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage terabyte-scale datasets, reduce model training times for iterative experimentation, and enable reproducible workflows across distributed research teams. By integrating computational rigor with linguistic fieldwork, this project aims to redefine scholarly engagement with African languages and establish scalable frameworks for analyzing their structural and literary diversity.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the African continent, including, but not limited to, Bantu languages, Nilo-Saharan languages, Niger-Congo languages, Khoisan languages, and the Chadic and Ethiopic languages of the Hamito-Semitic language family. Includes instruction in philology, dialects, and oral and written literatures.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in personalized mental health intervention strategies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multi-dimensional datasets. Current approaches to predicting treatment outcomes in mental health often rely on isolated data sources—such as clinical assessments, electronic health records, or social determinants—limiting their ability to capture the interplay of biological, psychological, and environmental factors. To overcome this, we propose an integrative computational framework that combines machine learning, network analysis, and high-dimensional data fusion techniques. The research will utilize large-scale datasets, including longitudinal clinical records, genomic data, and real-time social-behavioral metrics from wearable devices, to model dynamic predictors of treatment response in individuals with major depressive disorder. HPC resources are essential for processing these heterogeneous datasets, which encompass terabytes of structured and unstructured data, and for training ensemble models that require parallelized workflows. Key computational challenges include optimizing natural language processing pipelines for clinical notes, integrating sparse genomic data with time-varying behavioral signals, and scaling graph-based algorithms to map social support networks. Expected outcomes include the identification of multi-modal biomarkers associated with resilience or relapse, the development of an open-source predictive tool for clinicians to stratify patients by likely intervention outcomes, and a public dataset to support reproducibility. By enabling real-time analysis of complex interactions across data layers, this project aims to advance precision mental health care, reduce trial-and-error treatment approaches, and provide a scalable computational model for future studies in underserved populations. The requested HPC allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory simulations, and secure storage of sensitive health data.
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in play therapy by developing computational models to analyze therapeutic play interactions and predict behavioral outcomes in children. Play therapy relies on nuanced, non-verbal communication and symbolic play behaviors, which are challenging to quantify systematically. Current methods for evaluating play therapy sessions depend heavily on manual observation and qualitative interpretation, limiting scalability and reproducibility. This research addresses the critical need for data-driven tools to identify patterns in play behavior, correlate them with clinical diagnoses (e.g., anxiety, trauma), and optimize therapeutic strategies. The project will utilize video recordings of play therapy sessions from clinical and school settings, anonymized and annotated by registered play therapists. Computational workflows will be developed to process multimodal data, including visual cues (e.g., toy selection, play sequences), auditory signals (e.g., tone, verbal interactions), and annotated therapist notes. Machine learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for video analysis and transformer-based architectures for language processing, will be trained to detect behavioral markers associated with specific emotional or developmental challenges. Agent-based modeling will simulate child-therapist interactions to test hypotheses about intervention efficacy under varying conditions. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale of video data (terabytes of high-resolution footage), parallelizing model training across thousands of sessions, and running complex simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for automating play session analysis, validated predictive models linking play behaviors to clinical profiles, and a virtual training platform for play therapists. By integrating computational psychiatry with play therapy practice, this work aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy, personalize treatment plans, and expand access to evidence-based training tools. The results will directly support the development of scalable, standardized assessment protocols in child mental health while preserving the creative, child-centered ethos of play therapy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of hierarchical fiber architectures to optimize performance in high-strength, multifunctional textiles. A critical challenge in textile engineering lies in predicting how molecular-scale interactions in synthetic and natural fibers propagate to influence macroscale mechanical, thermal, and interfacial properties. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve these multiscale relationships efficiently, particularly for novel fiber blends or bio-inspired composite designs. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning to model fiber systems across atomic to mesoscopic scales. The computational workflow will simulate stress-strain behavior under varying thermal and chemical conditions, interfacial adhesion in hybrid fiber-matrix systems, and dye-polymer interactions at the molecular level. Key targets include optimizing processing parameters for aramid-polyolefin composite fibers and designing bio-derived flame-retardant coatings. The HPC environment is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of fiber orientations, polymer chain conformations, and multiphysics interactions, with simulations requiring parallelized execution across thousands of cores. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking fiber chemistry to bulk textile performance, validated against experimental tensile testing and microscopy data. These tools will enable rapid virtual prototyping of textiles for extreme environments, reducing reliance on iterative physical trials. By elucidating structure-property relationships in cellulose-nanocrystal-reinforced fibers and recyclable polymer blends, this work directly supports sustainable materials innovation—a priority for the textile engineering field. The requested resources will also facilitate the development of open-source simulation modules tailored for textile applications, fostering collaboration across materials science and manufacturing domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to test and manufacture fibers and fiber products, both synthetic and natural; to develop new and improved fibers, textiles and their uses; and to the analysis of related engineering problems such as structural factors, molecular synthesis, chemical manufacturing, weaves, strength and stress, useful life, dyes, and applications to composite systems.

abstract: The widespread adoption of alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs) hinges on improving the reliability and efficiency of hybrid, electric, and gaseous fuel systems, yet optimizing these technologies remains challenging due to the complex interplay of electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical processes. This project seeks to advance AFV performance analysis and conversion protocol development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-physics interactions in AFV systems at unprecedented resolution. Current diagnostic methods for AFV components—such as battery degradation in electric vehicles or combustion dynamics in compressed natural gas (CNG) engines—rely heavily on empirical testing, which is time-intensive and limited in predictive capability. We propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural-thermal simulations of power electronics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion and gas flow modeling in retrofit CNG/LPG systems, and machine learning (ML) to predict battery lifecycle under diverse operating conditions. These models will be validated against experimental data from partner automotive workshops, creating a feedback loop to refine predictive accuracy. The HPC environment is critical for handling the scale of these simulations, particularly for hybrid systems where coupled electrochemical-thermal models require millions of mesh elements and sub-millisecond temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include optimized charge/discharge protocols for extended battery longevity, improved combustion chamber designs for retrofit CNG engines, and data-driven guidelines for hybrid powertrain maintenance. By bridging computational engineering with hands-on AFV technician training, this work will directly inform curriculum updates in diagnostic techniques and conversion best practices, while providing a scalable toolkit for industry stakeholders to evaluate emerging AFV technologies. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for ML training and high-memory nodes for multi-domain simulations, enabling a 10-15x reduction in model iteration times compared to existing departmental computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the maintenance of alternative fuel vehicles and the conversion of standard vehicles to AFV status. Includes instruction in electrical vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles, hybrid fuel technology, electrical and electronic systems, engine performance, diagnosis and repair, and conversion/installation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational textual analysis in Talmudic Studies, a field characterized by complex intertextual relationships, layered commentaries, and evolving legal-ethical discourse. Traditional methods of Talmudic analysis rely on manual close reading, which limits scalability when tracing conceptual networks across vast corpora spanning centuries. The research problem centers on developing scalable computational frameworks to model semantic, logical, and jurisprudential patterns in Talmudic literature and its reception history. Using natural language processing (NLP) adapted to rabbinic Aramaic and Hebrew, combined with graph-based network analysis, the project will map argumentative structures, cross-referential dependencies, and conceptual shifts within and across key texts. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on digitized manuscripts and critical editions, enabling semantic similarity detection and automated source linkage at scale. Further computational work will involve agent-based modeling to simulate historical debates documented in the Talmud, testing hypotheses about dialogic reasoning norms. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated textual networks, visualization tools for interdisciplinary scholarship, and methodological frameworks bridging computational humanities with Jewish legal philosophy. This work aims to transform the study of Talmudic reasoning processes, offering new pathways to analyze how ethical principles are dynamically constructed through multilayered discourse. By integrating advanced computing with traditional hermeneutics, the project will enhance scholarly capacity to trace the evolution of Jewish legal thought while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations in digital religious studies.
cip_definition: A program focused on intense study of the Talmud that fosters values, critical thinking, and scholarship skills; prepares students for entry into a broad spectrum of graduate and professional schools; and prepares students for entry into a variety of careers including the Rabbinate. Includes instruction in Jewish law, Jewish jurisprudence, ethics, philosophy, and related disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the complex dynamics of real-time coordination in musical ensemble performances through computational modeling and analysis. Despite extensive study of individual musicianship, the mechanisms underlying precise temporal and expressive synchronization in ensembles—particularly in improvisational or non-notated contexts—remain poorly understood. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the high-dimensional, nonlinear interactions between performers, especially in live settings with variable acoustics and human-responsive adaptability. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate ensemble interactions at scale. Multi-channel audio recordings of live performances (e.g., jazz combos, chamber groups) will be processed using machine learning techniques to extract temporal, timbral, and dynamic features. These data will inform agent-based models where virtual performers, parameterized by individual expressive tendencies and real-time responsiveness, interact under variable conditions. The simulations will run iteratively on HPC clusters to explore how micro-level decisions (e.g., rhythmic adjustments, dynamic balancing) propagate across ensembles, enabling statistical analysis of emergent coherence or instability. Additionally, high-resolution acoustic simulations will model how venue-specific factors (e.g., reverberation, spatial arrangement) mediate collective performance. Outcomes will include predictive tools to identify critical thresholds of ensemble adaptability, a publicly accessible dataset of annotated performances, and pedagogical frameworks to train musicians in collaborative improvisation. This work bridges computational musicology and performance practice, offering empirically grounded insights into the interplay of individual agency and collective artistry. By quantifying traditionally subjective aspects of musical interaction, the project aims to advance both academic understanding and practical training in ensemble musicianship, with implications for AI-driven performance systems and adaptive human-machine collaboration in the arts.
