cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to master musical instruments and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers. Includes instruction on one or more specific instruments from various instrumental groupings.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of climate-driven shifts in vector-pathogen coevolution dynamics in understudied tropical arboviruses, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex biological and environmental interactions. Emerging arboviral diseases in tropical regions—such as Oropouche virus and Mayaro virus—are increasingly linked to climate variability, yet the mechanisms driving pathogen adaptation within mosquito vectors under changing thermal and hydrological conditions remain poorly characterized. Current models lack granularity in integrating genomic, entomological, and microclimatic data at spatiotemporal scales relevant to transmission hotspots. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining agent-based modeling of vector population dynamics with machine learning-driven phylogenetic prediction. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 10^6+ mosquito cohorts under projected climate scenarios, incorporating high-resolution temperature and precipitation data from regional Earth system models. Concurrently, we will apply Bayesian inference and neural networks to analyze time-series viral genomic datasets (∼50 TB) from field isolates, identifying signatures of thermal adaptation in structural proteins and untranslated regions. This dual approach will quantify how temperature fluctuations alter viral mutation rates in vectors and modulate transmission efficiency. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of arboviral emergence risks under IPCC climate pathways and mechanistic insights into thermal tolerance thresholds for viral replication in *Culicidae* vectors. The work directly supports targeted surveillance and the design of thermostable vaccines, addressing critical gaps in tropical disease resilience. By bridging computational genomics, ecological modeling, and climate science, this project establishes a template for interdisciplinary research on climate-sensitive zoonoses, with deliverables aligned with global health priorities for neglected tropical diseases.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to prevent and control vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases. Includes instruction in microbiology, parasitology, mycology, virology, vector biology, vaccinology, laboratory diagnosis, travelers' health, epidemiology, and disease management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized, data-driven protocols in aesthetic skincare, a field traditionally reliant on manual techniques and qualitative assessment. Current methodologies for designing facial and body treatments—such as selecting products, predicting skin responses, or optimizing regimens—lack robust computational frameworks to account for the complex interplay of variables like skin biomechanics, transient environmental factors, and individual client health histories. This gap limits both the precision of treatment outcomes and the scalability of evidence-based practices in esthetics. The proposed research will address this challenge by constructing computational models to simulate skin behavior under diverse treatment conditions and external stressors. Using anonymized client data (e.g., hyperspectral imaging, elasticity metrics, pH levels, and microbiome profiles), coupled with environmental datasets (humidity, UV exposure, pollution indices), we will develop machine learning algorithms to predict treatment efficacy and adverse reaction risks. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to map interactions between skincare modalities and skin subtypes, as well as Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in treatment outcomes. Additionally, finite element modeling will be employed to simulate the biomechanical effects of massage and topical product application across skin layers. The resulting predictive tools aim to establish a novel decision-support system for estheticians, reducing trial-and-error practices while enhancing client-specific treatment design. Outcomes will include open-access computational workflows tailored to esthetic practice needs, validated against clinical trial data from partner spas. By integrating computational science into a discipline historically dominated by manual artistry, this work bridges emerging technologies with skincare expertise, offering a template for data-driven innovation in non-traditional HPC domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cleanse, depilate, massage, and beautify the human body and to function as licensed estheticians and skin care specialists.  Includes instruction in skin anatomy, physiology, and health; principles of nutrition; decontamination and infection control; health and safety; facial and body massage; body wrapping and spa treatments; temporary hair removal including waxing and tweezing; color and skin analysis; client consultation and care; applicable laws and regulations; business practices; and sometimes related alternative healing regimens.

abstract: Rural populations experience disproportionately higher morbidity and mortality rates for chronic and infectious diseases compared to urban counterparts, compounded by systemic barriers such as fragmented healthcare access, environmental exposures, and socioeconomic disparities. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the multifactorial drivers of rural health outcomes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets spanning electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, environmental sensor outputs, and community-level social determinants of health. Current clinical research in rural settings is limited by insufficient computational capacity to integrate these data streams at scale, hindering the identification of actionable patterns and predictive biomarkers. We propose a computational framework combining machine learning (ML) models, geospatial analytics, and agent-based simulations to investigate (1) longitudinal disease progression pathways in rural cohorts, (2) environmental and genetic risk interactions for conditions such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes, and (3) the impact of hypothetical interventions on reducing care inequities. HPC resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets, train deep learning architectures on spatially resolved EHRs, and run parallelized simulations modeling healthcare delivery scenarios across diverse rural landscapes. Anticipated outcomes include the development of predictive tools to stratify high-risk populations, optimize screening protocols, and inform targeted policy interventions. By elucidating context-specific disease mechanisms and resource allocation strategies, this work aims to advance clinical decision-making for rural providers and reduce disparities in preventable adverse outcomes. The scalability of the computational pipeline will also provide a template for future studies in underrepresented rural regions globally.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rural Health

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance mechanistic modeling of drug-induced organ toxicity, a critical challenge in pharmacological and toxicological research. Traditional in vitro and animal models often fail to predict human-specific toxicities, leading to costly late-stage drug failures and safety-related withdrawals. Our research focuses on developing multiscale computational models to simulate drug interactions with hepatic cellular systems, integrating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) parameters, metabolic pathway dynamics, and tissue-level response networks. The core computational challenge lies in simulating nonlinear interactions between xenobiotics, metabolic enzymes (e.g., CYP450 isoforms), and cellular stress pathways at physiologically relevant timescales. We propose to implement hybrid modeling approaches combining ordinary differential equation systems for metabolic flux analysis with agent-based models of hepatocyte population responses. These simulations will incorporate human toxicogenomic datasets from primary hepatocytes and post-market surveillance reports to parameterize species-specific toxicity thresholds. The HPC environment is essential for parallel processing of stochastic model iterations across diverse drug candidates and genetic subpopulations, requiring terabytes of memory allocation and GPU-accelerated computation for molecular docking simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for identifying hepatotoxic liabilities in drug candidates prior to clinical trials, validated against historical toxicity data from withdrawn pharmaceuticals. This resource will enable rational prioritization of safer lead compounds and guide structure-activity relationship refinements to mitigate toxicity risks. By bridging gaps between cellular-scale mechanisms and organ-level toxicity phenotypes, this work addresses a fundamental need in pharmacological safety assessment while reducing reliance on animal testing.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pharmacology and toxicology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative coalition formation and stability in multiparty democracies using advanced computational modeling. While existing scholarship has explored coalition behavior through game-theoretic frameworks, these models often oversimplify the role of ideologically driven negotiation processes, institutional constraints, and exogenous shocks. The research problem centers on developing a more robust understanding of how heterogeneous political actors adapt strategies under evolving electoral incentives and procedural rules. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach that simulates strategic interactions among political parties, incorporating multidimensional policy preferences, historical voting data, and time-varying network structures. The computational framework will integrate machine learning techniques to calibrate agent decision rules using real-world coalition datasets from 25 parliamentary systems (1990–2020), followed by counterfactual scenario testing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of multi-parameter simulations, which involve over 10^6 autonomous agents operating across dynamically evolving institutional environments. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will enable systematic variation of key variables, including electoral thresholds, party discipline mechanisms, and external crisis events, while Bayesian inference techniques will quantify uncertainty in parameter estimates. Expected outcomes include novel insights into the conditions that promote durable versus fragile coalitions, with particular attention to institutional design trade-offs in newer democracies. The project will produce an open-source computational toolkit for political coalition analysis, enabling replication and extension of findings. By bridging formal theory with data-driven simulation at unprecedented scale, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in comparative politics while informing practical debates about constitutional engineering and democratic governance.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in political science and government, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing complex, interdependent systems in industrial and operational contexts, where traditional optimization methods fail due to nonlinear dynamics, high-dimensional constraints, and real-time decision-making requirements. The research addresses the challenge of balancing competing objectives—such as cost, throughput, resilience, and sustainability—in systems ranging from manufacturing supply chains to service delivery networks. Current approaches struggle with combinatorial complexity and stochastic variability, particularly when integrating human-in-the-loop factors or dynamic environmental inputs. To overcome these limitations, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized mixed-integer programming, agent-based simulations, and deep reinforcement learning algorithms. These methods will be co-designed to exploit distributed computing architectures, enabling iterative scenario testing, sensitivity analysis, and multi-objective Pareto frontier exploration at unprecedented scales. Key innovations include hybrid models that bridge discrete-event simulation with continuous optimization, adaptive metaheuristics for dynamic constraint handling, and GPU-accelerated neural networks for predictive system diagnostics. The computational workflows will be validated against industrial case studies involving facility layout optimization, maintenance scheduling under uncertainty, and multi-echelon inventory management. Expected outcomes include generalized decision support tools capable of handling systems with >10^5 variables, reduced solution times for NP-hard problems through heuristic decomposition strategies, and quantitative insights into resilience-sustainability tradeoffs. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will advance systems engineering methodologies for managing 21st-century sociotechnical systems while providing open-source optimization libraries to bridge academic research and industrial practice. The requested resources will directly enable large-scale experiments requiring terabytes of memory, thousands of CPU cores for parallel task farming, and GPU nodes for machine learning workloads.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems solutions to a wide variety of engineering problems, including the integration of human, physical, energy, communications, management, and information requirements as needed, and the application of requisite analytical methods to specific situations.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the critical challenge of optimizing nanoscale interfacial systems for next-generation energy conversion devices, focusing on quantum-confined fluidic transport phenomena that transcend classical continuum models. While advancements in nanofluidic systems hold promise for revolutionizing sustainable energy technologies, existing frameworks inadequately capture the interplay between quantum electronic effects, ion solvation dynamics, and sub-10 nm confinement geometries. This project employs ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) coupled with density functional theory (DFT) to model charge transfer mechanisms at solid-liquid interfaces under extreme spatial confinement, where surface polarization and electron correlation effects dominate transport behavior. Multiscale simulations will bridge quantum mechanical precision at electrode-electrolyte boundaries with mesoscale Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Stokes solvers, enabling the first unified computational framework for predicting emergent electrokinetic phenomena in angstrom-scale channels. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of variable confinement geometries (0.5-5 nm), electrolyte compositions, and surface functionalizations across relevant thermodynamic ensembles. Expected outcomes include fundamentally new design principles for voltage-gated nanofluidic membranes capable of exceeding classical permselectivity limits, with direct applications in osmotic energy harvesting and electrochemical carbon capture. The developed computational toolkit will establish protocols for simulating quantum-hydrodynamic coupling in non-equilibrium nanoscale systems, filling a critical gap between condensed matter physics and nanoengineering. By elucidating how subnanometer interfacial structuring modulates both ionic and electronic transport pathways, this work aims to enable predictive design of energy conversion architectures that leverage atomic-scale confinement effects beyond existing paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, growth, properties, and fundamental interactions of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across scientific disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate non-perturbative phenomena in quantum field theories (QFTs) with non-linear topological interactions, focusing on resolving divergences in path integral formulations of gauge theories in 3+1 dimensions. Current analytical methods struggle to address the strong coupling regimes of such systems, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic vacuum transitions or emergent solitonic structures. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining lattice field theory simulations with adaptive spectral methods to discretize and solve high-dimensional functional integrals. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized Monte Carlo sampling across distributed GPU nodes, enabling statistically robust evaluations of partition functions and correlation dynamics at unprecedented lattice sizes (≥128^4) and fine coupling resolutions. Key challenges include mitigating sign problems in complex action spaces through reweighting algorithms and optimizing memory-efficient tensor contractions for non-Abelian gauge groups. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative predictions for vacuum decay rates in metastable Yang-Mills configurations, (2) characterization of instanton density scaling laws near critical couplings, and (3) development of open-source numerical libraries for topological sector analysis in QFTs. These results will advance foundational understanding of non-perturbative effects in quantum chromodynamics analogs while providing methodological benchmarks for emergent spacetime geometries in quantum gravity models. The requested computing allocation—supporting 12 months of sustained simulations on GPU-accelerated nodes with high inter-node bandwidth—is critical for achieving the necessary statistical precision and parameter space coverage. Success will establish computational pathways to address long-standing mathematical physics questions inaccessible to perturbative or continuum-limit approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and mathematical formulation and evaluation of the physical laws governing, and models describing, matter-energy phenomena, and the analysis of related experimental designs and results. Includes instruction in classical and quantum theory, relativity theory, field theory, mathematics of infinite series, vector and coordinate analysis, wave and particle theory, advanced applied calculus and geometry, analyses of continuum, cosmology, and statistical theory and analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of consumer behavior in the digital apparel and textile marketplace, an emerging interdisciplinary niche integrating computational social science, marketing analytics, and sustainable design principles. The research addresses the critical challenge of forecasting rapidly evolving fashion consumption patterns amid climate-conscious purchasing trends, where traditional linear regression models fail to capture complex interactions between social media influence, product sustainability metrics, and real-time economic indicators. By employing agent-based modeling (ABM) frameworks scaled across HPC architectures, we will simulate decision-making processes of heterogeneous consumer agents interacting with dynamic environmental and marketing variables. The computational workflow integrates natural language processing (NLP) of user-generated content from fashion platforms, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) analyzing visual trend data, and multi-objective optimization algorithms balancing profitability against ecological impact metrics. Key technical hurdles include managing sparse, high-dimensional datasets from augmented reality fitting tools and scaling graph-based analyses of influencer network effects across distributed memory systems. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time adaptive marketing strategy optimization, capable of processing terabyte-scale streams from IoT-enabled retail environments. This work fills a critical gap in non-STEM computational research by developing domain-specific methodologies for ethical AI applications in fashion marketing, while providing novel insights into the relationship between digital consumer engagement and sustainable textile consumption patterns. The requested resources will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling emergent market behaviors, directly supporting industry transitions toward data-driven circular economy practices.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on marketing research and management as applied to the products and services of the apparel and textile industries. Includes instruction in applicable principles of textile and apparel design and manufacturing, sales and distribution systems, domestic and international market research, profitability, consumer research, and the design and implementation of marketing campaigns.

abstract: The increasing complexity of business data ecosystems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize office automation workflows, particularly in data entry and transformation processes. This project addresses inefficiencies in legacy systems that struggle with real-time processing of heterogeneous data streams—including unstructured text, tabular reports, and IoT sensor outputs—common in modern administrative environments. Traditional rule-based automation frameworks exhibit latency and error propagation when handling dynamic data schemas or scaling across distributed teams. We propose developing an adaptive processing architecture leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallelized data ingestion, context-aware validation, and self-optimizing workflow orchestration. The computational approach combines graph-based dependency modeling with transformer neural networks trained on synthetic office operation datasets to predict processing bottlenecks and resource conflicts. Agent-based simulations will model interactions between automated systems and human operators across scaled organizational topologies, requiring distributed memory computing for real-time scenario testing. Expected outcomes include a framework for energy-efficient allocation of computational resources during peak administrative loads, dynamic error-correction protocols that reduce manual reconciliation efforts by an estimated 40%, and predictive models for infrastructure scaling in hybrid office environments. The research will provide novel metrics for quantifying automation ROI through computational resource utilization patterns, addressing a critical gap in business technology evaluation practices. By implementing containerized workflows on HPC clusters, we aim to demonstrate throughput improvements of 15-25x over conventional cloud-based solutions for mass data normalization tasks, while maintaining sub-second latency for mission-critical operations like financial transaction logging and compliance reporting. This work establishes methodological foundations for next-generation office automation systems capable of supporting exponential data growth in business environments without proportional increases in operational overhead.
cip_title: Business/ Office Automation/ Technology/ Data Entry
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to support business information operations by using computer equipment to enter, process, and retrieve data for a wide variety of administrative purposes. Includes instruction in using basic business software and hardware, business computer networking, principles of desktop publishing, preparing mass mailings, compiling and editing spreadsheets, list maintenance, preparing tables and graphs, receipt control, and preparing business performance reports.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive computational models for complex chemical reaction mechanisms, with a focus on systems where experimental characterization remains challenging. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding solvent-mediated reaction pathways and dynamic conformational changes in organic and organometallic compounds, particularly in non-equilibrium environments. Current density functional theory (DFT) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) methods struggle to efficiently model these phenomena due to the computational cost of simulating explicit solvent interactions over biologically or catalytically relevant timescales. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) framework coupled with enhanced sampling techniques, including metadynamics and variational free energy profiling. These methods will be optimized for parallelization on GPU-accelerated HPC architectures to enable microsecond-scale simulations of solvated systems. Key targets include acid-base equilibria in non-aqueous solvents, stereochemical outcomes in asymmetric catalysis, and transient intermediate states in enzyme-like complexes. The computational workflow will integrate machine learning force fields trained on high-level QM data to reduce sampling bottlenecks while maintaining accuracy. Outcomes will provide atomistic insights into solvent effects on reaction thermodynamics and kinetics, directly informing experimental design in catalysis and synthetic chemistry. By bridging gaps between static quantum chemical models and dynamic experimental observations, this work aims to establish scalable protocols for simulating reactive systems in realistic environments. Successful implementation will advance predictive modeling capabilities in computational chemistry, with potential applications in drug discovery and sustainable catalyst design. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the iterative sampling demands and large dataset generation inherent to this approach.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of principals of mathematical algorithms, statistics, and large databases to integrate chemical theory and modeling with experimental observations. Includes instruction in chemistry or a related scientific field, computer training, a familiarity with chemical principles, including conformational analysis, acid–base equilibria, physical organic chemistry, molecular structure, thermodynamics, and stereochemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of recidivism patterns through an interdisciplinary computational criminology framework. Traditional recidivism risk assessment tools rely on static, demographic-heavy datasets and linear statistical methods, which often fail to capture dynamic, context-dependent factors such as evolving social networks, spatial-temporal behavioral patterns, and unstructured textual data from rehabilitation program interactions. The research problem centers on developing a machine learning architecture capable of integrating high-dimensional, heterogeneous data streams—including anonymized criminal histories, geospatial mobility traces, and natural language processing (NLP)-analyzed caseworker notes—to generate dynamic risk forecasts. The computational approach combines graph neural networks (GNNs) to model offender social ties, transformer-based NLP for semantic analysis of counseling transcripts, and reinforcement learning to simulate intervention scenarios. HPC resources are critical for training multi-modal models on sensitive, federated datasets (simulated via synthetic data generation) while maintaining computational efficiency and scalability. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for ethically aligned recidivism analytics, validated against historical correctional outcomes in partnership with state agencies. The project’s significance lies in its potential to inform resource allocation for targeted rehabilitative programs, reduce algorithmic bias in risk assessment, and establish computational workflows adaptable to emerging challenges in community-based corrections. By bridging criminological theory with scalable AI/ML techniques, this work aims to create a paradigm shift in evidence-based correctional policy while adhering to strict ethical guidelines for justice-related data usage.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general study of criminal justice and corrections. Includes instruction in criminology, criminal justice, correctional science, forensic science, law enforcement, psychology, and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in warehouse operations and maintenance by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex logistical workflows, predict equipment failures, and optimize inventory management. Modern warehousing faces dynamic challenges, including fluctuating demand, equipment downtime, and the need for real-time decision-making, which traditional analytical methods struggle to address due to computational limitations. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate warehouse operations under varying demand scenarios, integrating real-world data on inventory turnover, equipment performance, and labor allocation. Concurrently, machine learning (ML) algorithms will be trained on historical maintenance records and sensor data from forklifts, conveyor systems, and automated storage/retrieval systems to predict equipment failures and recommend preemptive maintenance schedules. A parallel computational framework will optimize inventory routing and storage allocation using mixed-integer linear programming (MILP), balancing spatial constraints, energy consumption, and labor costs. These computational tasks demand HPC resources due to their scale: ABM simulations will model thousands of concurrent agents (e.g., workers, robots, inventory units), while ML training and MILP solvers require distributed computing to handle high-dimensional datasets and complex constraint matrices. Outcomes will include predictive maintenance benchmarks, adaptive inventory routing algorithms, and open-source simulation tools tailored for warehouse technicians. By integrating computational modeling with operational data, this project aims to advance decision-support systems for warehouse personnel, reduce unplanned downtime by up to 30%, and lower storage costs through dynamic spatial optimization. The results will directly inform curriculum updates in warehousing technology programs, bridging gaps between traditional maintenance practices and data-driven operational strategies.
cip_title: Parts and Warehousing Operations and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain inventory control, care for inventory, and make minor repairs to warehouse equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Italian dialectology and historical linguistics, with a focus on analyzing regional language variation and its evolution across time. Despite Italy’s rich linguistic diversity, many regional dialects remain underdocumented, and their dynamic interactions with standardized Italian are poorly understood. Traditional methods in philology and dialectology struggle to process the scale of textual, audio, and sociolinguistic data required to model these complex systems. This project will develop and apply computational workflows to digitized historical texts, modern dialect corpora, and oral archives to trace phonetic, morphological, and lexical shifts across space and time. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for automated dialect classification, employing graph-based algorithms to map dialect contact networks, and conducting large-scale comparative analyses using phylogenetic methods adapted from evolutionary biology. The workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) tools optimized for low-resource languages and dialect-specific orthographies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialect features, quantitative models of language change in post-unification Italy, and open-source tools for interdisciplinary researchers working with multilingual historical corpora. These resources will address critical gaps in Italian linguistic scholarship while demonstrating how HPC can enable novel methodologies in humanities research. The project requires significant parallel processing capabilities for training deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets, as well as high-memory nodes for phylogenetic inference and network analysis. By bridging computational linguistics with traditional philological expertise, this work aims to reshape the study of Italian language diversity and inform broader debates about language preservation, standardization, and digital heritage.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Italian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing customer service operations in dynamic, high-volume environments through advanced computational modeling. While customer service management research has traditionally relied on qualitative frameworks or small-scale simulations, the increasing complexity of omnichannel customer interactions, real-time demand fluctuations, and workforce variability necessitates a more rigorous, data-driven approach. The research problem centers on developing predictive models that can account for multidimensional factors—including customer behavior patterns, service agent skill distributions, and operational constraints—to improve decision-making in resource allocation and service protocol design. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale historical customer interaction datasets (e.g., call center logs, live chat transcripts, and customer satisfaction surveys) from three industry partners. Machine learning techniques, including natural language processing for sentiment analysis of customer feedback and deep reinforcement learning for dynamic staffing optimization, will be implemented alongside discrete-event simulations modeling service workflows. Agent-based modeling will test the resilience of proposed strategies under scenarios of demand surges or system disruptions. Computational outcomes will identify optimal thresholds for service-level agreements, predict customer attrition risks based on interaction patterns, and generate adaptive staffing schedules that balance operational costs with service quality targets. By enabling simultaneous analysis of terabyte-scale datasets and complex parameter spaces, HPC resources are critical for capturing the nonlinear relationships inherent in customer service ecosystems. The expected significance lies in providing organizations with evidence-based tools to reduce customer wait times, improve agent utilization, and mitigate service failures through scenario-aware planning. This work will advance academic understanding of computational applications in service operations while addressing a persistent industry need for scalable, responsive customer management systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and monitor customer service performance and manage frontline customer support services, call centers/help desks, and customer relations. Includes instruction in customer behavior, specialized information technology and systems management, developing and using customer service databases, user surveys and other feedback mechanisms, strategic and performance planning and analysis, operations management, personnel supervision, and communications and marketing skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving intersections of Tribal/Indigenous legal systems, federal jurisprudence, and Indigenous rights advocacy through advanced computational legal analytics. The research problem centers on the fragmented and often inaccessible nature of legal data pertaining to Tribal sovereignty, treaty obligations, and intergovernmental litigation, which limits comprehensive analysis of systemic trends, biases, and cultural impacts. Traditional legal scholarship relies on manual case review, but the scale of digitized court opinions, treaties, tribal codes, and oral histories—spanning centuries and multiple languages—demands scalable computational methods. This project will develop machine learning models to identify patterns in judicial reasoning, temporal shifts in federal-tribal power dynamics, and the influence of cultural narratives in legal texts. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be tailored to handle Indigenous language corpora, treaty documents, and intertextual references across tribal, federal, and international legal frameworks. Network analysis will map citation practices and policy diffusion among tribal legal systems, while geospatial tools will visualize jurisdictional conflicts and land restitution outcomes. The computational workflows will integrate ethical AI protocols to address cultural sensitivity, data sovereignty, and the risks of algorithmic bias when analyzing Indigenous legal materials. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of annotated legal datasets, predictive models to assess the impacts of proposed legislation on Tribal sovereignty, and frameworks for computationally tracing the preservation of Indigenous legal principles in contemporary jurisprudence. By applying HPC to Tribal/Indigenous law, this project aims to advance scholarly and community-engaged tools for decolonizing legal analytics, empowering Tribal governments in policy design, and strengthening interdisciplinary bridges between computational social science and Indigenous methodologies.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting federal Indian law, tribal law and policy, and Indigenous peoples' human rights.

abstract: The increasing complexity of delivering equitable special education services, compounded by evolving legal mandates and heterogeneous student needs, necessitates data-driven strategies to optimize resource allocation and program administration. Current approaches to managing individualized education programs (IEPs), staffing, and budgetary decisions often rely on fragmented datasets and heuristic methods, limiting scalability and adaptability across diverse districts. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate resource allocation scenarios in special education administration, enabling evidence-based decision-making under constraints. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets from K-12 districts (including IEP records, staffing patterns, budget allocations, and student outcome metrics), we will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between administrators, educators, students, and resources. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to run large-scale parameter sweeps analyzing how variables such as disability type prevalence, staff-to-student ratios, and funding fluctuations impact service delivery efficacy. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive patterns in historical data, while optimization algorithms will propose resource distribution strategies that balance compliance, cost-effectiveness, and student outcomes. The computational pipeline will integrate geospatial analysis to account for regional disparities in resource availability. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating policy impacts, actionable metrics for benchmarking district performance, and adaptive models to project resource needs under demographic or regulatory changes. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process multi-terabyte datasets and computationally intensive simulations, this work aims to advance administrative practices in special education, ultimately supporting more equitable and efficient systems for over 7 million students with disabilities in U.S. public schools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage programs for exceptional students and their parents. Includes instruction in special education theory and practice, special education program development, evaluation and assessment in special education, state and federal law and regulations, managing individual education plans, problems of low- and high- disability students, mainstreaming, special education curricula, staff management, parent education, communications and community relations, budgeting, and professional standards and ethics.
